title: The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to guardian and ward.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to minors and their guardians concerning the person and/or property.

key_definitions.minor: A person who, under the provisions of the Indian Majority Act, 1875, is to be deemed not to have attained his majority.
key_definitions.guardian: A person having the care of the person of a minor or of his property, or of both person and property.
key_definitions.ward: A minor for whose person or property, or both, there is a guardian.
key_definitions.District Court: Has the meaning assigned to that expression in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1882, and includes a High Court in the exercise of its ordinary original civil jurisdiction.
key_definitions.the Court: The District Court having jurisdiction to entertain an application under this Act for appointing or declaring a guardian; or where a guardian has been appointed or declared, the court which appointed/declared them, or the District Court where the ward resides, or the court to which proceedings have been transferred.
key_definitions.Collector: The chief officer in charge of the revenue-administration of a district, and includes any officer whom the State Government may appoint to be a Collector for all or any of the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date it came into force (July 1, 1890).

main_sections.section_title: Saving of jurisdiction of Courts of Wards and Chartered High Courts
main_sections.description: States that the Act is subject to enactments relating to Courts of Wards and does not affect the jurisdiction or authority of any Court of Wards or any High Court.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'minor', 'guardian', 'ward', 'District Court', 'the Court', and 'Collector'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to confer jurisdiction on subordinate judicial officers and to transfer proceedings to such officers
main_sections.description: Empowers High Courts to allow subordinate judicial officers to dispose of proceedings under the Act and allows District Court Judges to transfer proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Court to make order as to guardianship
main_sections.description: Grants the Court the power to make an order appointing or declaring a guardian for the person or property of a minor if it is satisfied that it is for the welfare of the minor. It also implies removal of existing guardians not appointed by will or the Court.

main_sections.section_title: Persons entitled to apply for order
main_sections.description: Specifies who can apply for an order of guardianship, including the person wishing to be guardian, a relative or friend of the minor, or the Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Court having jurisdiction to entertain application
main_sections.description: Determines which District Court has jurisdiction to entertain applications, based on the minor's ordinary residence for guardianship of the person, and either residence or property location for guardianship of the property.
Outlines the required format and content of an application for guardianship, including details about the minor, property, existing guardians, and proposed guardian.

main_sections.section_title: Matters to be considered by the Court in appointing guardian
main_sections.description: Details the factors the Court must consider when appointing a guardian, with the primary consideration being the welfare of the minor.

main_sections.section_title: Fiduciary relation of guardian to ward
main_sections.description: Establishes that a guardian is in a fiduciary relationship with the ward.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of guardian of the person
main_sections.description: Specifies the duties of a guardian of the minor's person.
Specifies the duties of a guardian of the minor's property.

main_sections.section_title: Limitation of powers of guardian of property appointed or declared by the Court
main_sections.description: Limits the powers of a guardian of property appointed or declared by the Court, requiring court permission for certain transactions.

main_sections.section_title: Voidability of transfers made in contravention of section 28 or section 29
main_sections.description: Declares transfers of property made in contravention of specific sections voidable.
Outlines the grounds on which the Court can remove a guardian.

main_sections.section_title: Orders for regulating conduct or proceedings of guardians, and enforcement of those orders
main_sections.description: Grants the Court power to issue orders regulating the conduct of guardians and to enforce these orders.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for removal of ward from jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for removing a ward from the jurisdiction of the Court.
Provides for penalties for contumacy (disobedience or resistance) in proceedings under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of High Court to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: The Court must be satisfied that an order for guardianship is for the welfare of the minor (Section 7(1)).
Guardianship applications must be made by specific persons like the desirous guardian, a relative/friend, or the Collector (Section 8).
The primary consideration for the Court in appointing a guardian is the welfare of the minor (Section 17).
A guardian of property appointed or declared by the Court cannot transfer the property without the Court's permission (Section 29).
Transfers made in contravention of limitations on guardian's powers are voidable (Section 30).
Guardians are generally held to the same liabilities as trustees (Section 37).

penalties: Penalty for removal of ward from jurisdiction (Section 44).
Penalty for contumacy (disobedience) (Section 45).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Courts, primarily the District Courts, with powers conferred upon subordinate judicial officers and oversight by High Courts. Collectors also play a role in initiating proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders, directives, and the imposition of penalties for non-compliance. High Courts can make rules to govern procedures and enforcement.

rights: Right of a proposed guardian to apply for appointment or declaration.
Right of a relative or friend of the minor to apply for guardianship.
Right of the ward to have a guardian appointed for their welfare.
Right of a guardian to apply to the Court for opinion in management of property (Section 33).
duties: Duty of the Court to ensure the welfare of the minor when making orders.
Duty of a guardian to have care of the person or property of the minor.
Duty of a guardian of the person to provide for the minor's upbringing and maintenance.
Duty of a guardian of property to manage the property prudently and for the benefit of the ward.
obligations: Obligations on a guardian of property appointed or declared by the Court, including rendering accounts (Section 34).

key_procedures: Application for guardianship: Filed by eligible persons, stating specific details about the minor, property, and proposed guardian (Section 10).
Admission of application and hearing: Court fixes a date, serves notice to parents and persons in custody of the minor, and hears evidence (Section 11, 13).
Interlocutory orders: Power to make interim orders for the production of the minor and interim protection of person and property (Section 12).
Transfer of proceedings: High Courts can empower subordinate officers, and District Court Judges can transfer proceedings (Section 4A).
Appointment or declaration: Court makes an order if satisfied it's for the minor's welfare (Section 7).
administration: The Act is administered by the Courts, primarily District Courts and High Courts, with the involvement of Collectors in certain capacities.
important_notes: The Act does not affect the jurisdiction of Courts of Wards or High Courts (Section 3).
The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration for the Court in appointing a guardian (Section 17).
Certain transfers of property by a guardian without court permission are voidable (Section 30).

title: An Act to extend the Indian Easements Act, 1882, to certain areas in which that Act is not in force.
purpose: To extend the provisions of the Indian Easements Act, 1882 (Act V of 1882) to specific territories where it was not previously in force.
scope: This Act applies to the territories administered by the Governor of Bombay in Council and the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh. It also notes an extension to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of Act V, 1882, to Bombay and the North-Western Provinces and Oudh.
main_sections.description: This section formally extends the Indian Easements Act, 1882 (Act V of 1882) to the territories administered by the Governor of Bombay in Council and the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh.

important_rules: The Indian Easements Act, 1882 (Act V of 1882) is extended to the territories administered by the Governor of Bombay in Council.
The Indian Easements Act, 1882 (Act V of 1882) is extended to the territories administered by the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the respective administrations of Bombay, North-Western Provinces, and Oudh.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Indian Easements Act, 1882.

administration: The administration of the extended Act falls under the respective governmental authorities of Bombay, North-Western Provinces, and Oudh.
important_notes: The North-Western Provinces is now Uttar Pradesh.
The Act has been extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh by Act 34 of 2019, effective from 31-10-2019.

title: The Partition Act, 1893
purpose: To amend the law relating to partition of property.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Excludes local laws for partition of immoveable property paying revenue to Government. Applies to suits instituted before its commencement where no partition scheme has been finally approved.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Partition Act, 1893, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India), and includes a saving clause for local laws concerning revenue-paying immoveable property.

main_sections.section_title: Power to court to order sale instead of division in partition suits.
main_sections.description: Empowers the court to order the sale of property and distribution of proceeds in partition suits if division is not reasonably or conveniently possible due to the nature of the property, number of shareholders, or other special circumstances, provided a moiety or upwards of shareholders request it.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when sharer undertakes to buy.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure when a shareholder requests to buy the share(s) of a party seeking a sale. The court orders a valuation and offers the share to the applicant. If multiple shareholders apply, the highest bidder gets the share. Applicants unwilling to buy at the ascertained price are liable for costs.

main_sections.section_title: Partition suit by transferee of share in dwelling-house.
main_sections.description: Deals with partition suits by a non-family member transferee of a share in a dwelling-house of an undivided family. The court shall direct a sale of the transferee's share to a family member if they undertake to buy it, following a valuation. Similar procedure to Section 3 applies if multiple family members offer to buy.

Allows for requests, undertakings, or applications on behalf of parties under disability by their authorized representatives in partition suits. However, the court's compliance is conditional on it being of the opinion that the sale or purchase benefits the party under disability.

main_sections.section_title: Reserved bidding and bidding by shareholders.
main_sections.description: States that all sales under Section 2 are subject to a reserved bidding fixed by the court. Shareholders are allowed to bid with flexible terms regarding deposit and set-off. If two or more bidders advance the same sum, with one being a shareholder, it's considered the shareholder's bid.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed in case of sales.
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for sales directed under the Act. For High Courts of Calcutta, Madras, or Bombay, their original jurisdiction sale procedure applies. For other courts, High Court rules or, in their absence, the Code of Civil Procedure for sales in execution of decrees shall be followed.

main_sections.section_title: Orders for sale to be deemed decrees.
main_sections.description: Declares that any order for sale made by the court under Sections 2, 3, or 4 is to be considered a decree within the meaning of Section 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1882.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of power to order partly partition and partly sale.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the court can, at its discretion, pass a decree for the partition of a part of the property and a sale of the remainder under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to pending suits.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Act applies to suits filed before its commencement, provided that no scheme for partition has been finally approved by the court.

important_rules: If a property cannot be reasonably or conveniently divided in a partition suit, the court can order a sale and distribution of proceeds if beneficial to shareholders (Section 2).
In a partition suit where sale is requested, a shareholder can apply to buy the share(s) of the party asking for sale at a court-assessed valuation (Section 3).
If a dwelling-house share is transferred to a non-family member, the court can direct its sale to a family member shareholder at a valuation if they undertake to buy it (Section 4).
Sales under Section 2 are subject to a reserved bidding fixed by the court (Section 6).
Shareholders can bid at sales with terms like non-payment of deposit or setting off purchase money (Section 6).
Orders for sale under Sections 2, 3, or 4 are legally considered decrees (Section 8).

penalties: Applicants unwilling to buy a share at the ascertained price are liable to pay all costs of or incident to their application (Section 3(3)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts (Civil Courts dealing with partition suits)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial orders and decrees issued by the courts. Procedures for sales are outlined in Section 7.

rights: Shareholders have the right to request a sale of the property if division is not feasible or beneficial (Section 2).
Shareholders have the right to apply to buy the share of a party requesting a sale (Section 3).
Shareholders have the right to bid at sales of the property (Section 6).
Family members who are shareholders have the right to buy the share of a non-family transferee in a dwelling-house (Section 4).
duties: Parties seeking a sale must ensure it is requested by shareholders representing at least a moiety or upwards (Section 2).
Shareholders who apply to buy a share but do not proceed at the ascertained price are liable for costs (Section 3(3)).
Authorized representatives of parties under disability must act in the best interest of the party (Section 5).
obligations: The court has an obligation to consider the benefit of parties under disability when approving sales or purchases on their behalf (Section 5).

key_procedures: Initiating a partition suit and, if division is not feasible, requesting a sale by shareholders representing a moiety or upwards.
Application by a shareholder to buy the share of a party requesting sale, followed by court valuation and offer.
Procedure for multiple shareholders applying to buy, leading to a highest bidder selection.
Sale of a dwelling-house share to a family member transferee by a court-directed valuation and sale to an undertaking family member shareholder.
Application of established court procedures for sales by High Courts or, if not prescribed, by the Code of Civil Procedure.
administration: Civil Courts (though the High Courts prescribe rules for sales in some cases).
important_notes: The Act was extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Pondicherry, and Sikkim.
The exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir was omitted via Act 34 of 2019.
Sub-section (3) of Section 1, relating to territorial extent, was repealed.
The original jurisdiction of the Court of the Recorder of Rangoon was omitted from Section 7(a).

title: The Anand Marriage Act, 1909
purpose: To remove doubts as to the validity of the marriage ceremony common among the Sikhs called Anand.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Specifically concerns marriages solemnized according to the Sikh marriage ceremony called Anand (Anand Karaj).

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the 'Anand Marriage Act, 1909' and specifies its extent to the whole of India.
Declares all marriages duly solemnized according to the Sikh marriage ceremony called Anand (commonly known as Anand Karaj) as good and valid in law, retrospectively from the date of solemnization.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption of certain marriages from Act
main_sections.description: Excludes marriages between persons not professing the Sikh religion and marriages already judicially declared null and void from the purview of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of marriages solemnized according to other ceremonies
main_sections.description: States that the Act does not affect the validity of marriages solemnized according to any other customary Sikh marriage ceremonies.

main_sections.section_title: Non-validation of marriages within prohibited degrees
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not validate marriages between persons who are related within prohibited degrees of consanguinity or affinity according to the customary law of the Sikhs.

Provides for the registration of Anand marriages by State Governments to facilitate proof. It allows for the entry of marriage particulars in a Marriage Register, makes the register open for inspection, and certified extracts admissible as evidence. The validity of a marriage is not affected by the omission of registration. Rules made by the State Government under this section are to be laid before the State Legislature.

important_rules: Marriages duly solemnized according to the Sikh marriage ceremony called Anand (Anand Karaj) are valid in law (Section 2).
Marriages between non-Sikhs or those judicially declared void are exempt (Section 3).
The Act does not affect marriages solemnized by other customary Sikh ceremonies (Section 4).
The Act does not validate marriages within prohibited degrees as per Sikh customary law (Section 5).
State Governments shall make rules for the registration of Anand marriages to facilitate proof, without prejudice to other marriage laws (Section 6(1)).
Marriage Registers will be open for inspection, and certified extracts are admissible as evidence (Section 6(2)).
Omission to register a marriage does not affect its validity (Section 6(3)).
Parties whose marriages are registered under this Act are not required to register under any other law (Section 6(5)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (for making rules regarding registration).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the framework of rules established by the State Government for marriage registration and enforcement of the Act's provisions concerning validity and exemptions.

rights: Right to have an Anand marriage declared valid in law.
Right to have marriage particulars entered in a Marriage Register.
Right to obtain certified extracts from the Marriage Register as evidence.
Right not to be required to register marriage under other laws if registered under this Act.
duties: Duty to solemnize marriages according to the Sikh marriage ceremony called Anand for the Act to apply.
Duty of the State Government to make rules for the registration of marriages.

key_procedures: Solemnization of marriage according to the Sikh marriage ceremony called Anand.
Application to the State Government for rules regarding marriage registration.
Entry of marriage particulars in a Marriage Register.
Inspection of the Marriage Register.
Application for certified extracts from the Marriage Register.
administration: State Government (for making rules and managing the Marriage Register).
important_notes: The Act was extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted.
Section 6 regarding registration of marriages was inserted by an amendment in 2012, effective from 2013.

title: THE HINDU DISPOSITION OF PROPERTY ACT, 1916
purpose: To remove certain existing disabilities in respect of the power of disposition of property by Hindus for the benefit of persons not in existence at the date of such disposition.
scope: Applies to Hindus throughout India. It can be extended to the Khoja community by notification by the State Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its territorial extent. It originally extended to the whole of India, with subsequent amendments specifying exclusions and extensions to specific territories.

main_sections.section_title: Dispositions for the benefit of persons not in existence.
main_sections.description: States that no disposition of property by a Hindu, whether by inter vivos transfer or by will, shall be invalid solely because the beneficiary was not in existence at the time of the disposition, provided it adheres to the limitations and provisions of the Act.

Specifies the limitations and provisions referred to in section 2. For inter vivos transfers, these are found in Chapter II of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. For dispositions by will, these are found in sections 113, 114, 115, and 116 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925.
This section was repealed by the Transfer of Property (Amendment) Supplementary Act, 1929.

main_sections.section_title: Application of this Act to the Khoja community.
main_sections.description: Allows the State Government, if it believes the Khoja community desires it, to extend the provisions of this Act to that community by official gazette notification, substituting 'Khojas' or 'Khoja' for 'Hindus' or 'Hindu'.

important_rules: A disposition of property by a Hindu for the benefit of a person not in existence at the date of disposition is not invalid solely on that ground.

Such dispositions must comply with the limitations and provisions outlined in Chapter II of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (for inter vivos transfers) and sections 113, 114, 115, and 116 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 (for wills).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the courts and relevant legal authorities responsible for property law.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and interpretation of the Act's provisions by courts.

rights: Right of Hindus to dispose of property for the benefit of unborn persons, subject to specified limitations.
Right of the Khoja community to have the Act extended to them.
duties: Duty of Hindus making dispositions to adhere to the limitations and provisions of the Transfer of Property Act and Indian Succession Act as specified.
Duty of the State Government to consider the desire of the Khoja community for the Act's extension.

key_procedures: Procedure for extending the Act to the Khoja community: The State Government, upon being of the opinion that the Khoja community desires it, may by notification in the Official Gazette declare that the Act shall apply to that community with necessary substitutions.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be under the purview of the Ministry of Law and Justice and relevant State Governments.
important_notes: Section 4 of the Act has been repealed.
The Act's application has been subject to various amendments regarding its territorial extent and specific communities (e.g., Renoncants of Pondicherry are excluded).

title: THE SALE OF GOODS ACT, 1930
purpose: To define and amend the law relating to the sale of goods.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to contracts for the sale of goods.

key_definitions.buyer: A person who buys or agrees to buy goods.
key_definitions.delivery: Voluntary transfer of possession from one person to another.
key_definitions.deliverable state: Goods are in such a state that the buyer would under the contract be bound to take delivery of them.
key_definitions.document of title to goods: Includes a bill of lading, dock warrant, warehouse keeper’s certificate, wharfinger’s certificate, railway receipt, multimodal transport document, warrant or order for the delivery of goods and any other document used in the ordinary course of business as proof of the possession or control of goods, or authorizing or purporting to authorize, either by endorsement or by delivery, the possessor of the document to transfer or receive goods thereby represented.
key_definitions.future goods: Goods to be manufactured or produced or acquired by the seller after the making of the contract of sale.
key_definitions.goods: Every kind of moveable property other than actionable claims and money; and includes stock and shares, growing crops, grass, and things attached to or forming part of the land which are agreed to be severed before sale or under the contract of sale.
key_definitions.insolvent: A person who has ceased to pay his debts in the ordinary course of business, or cannot pay his debts as they become due, whether he has committed an act of insolvency or not.
key_definitions.mercantile agent: A mercantile agent having in the customary course of business as such agent authority either to sell goods, or to consign goods for the purposes of sale, or to buy goods, or to raise money on the security of goods.
key_definitions.price: The money consideration for a sale of goods.
key_definitions.property: The general property in goods, and not merely a special property.
key_definitions.seller: A person who sells or agrees to sell goods.
key_definitions.specific goods: Goods identified and agreed upon at the time a contract of sale is made.
key_definitions.Indian Contract Act, 1872: Expressions used but not defined in this Act and defined in the Indian Contract Act, 1872, have the meaning assigned to them in that Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date it came into force (July 1, 1930).
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as buyer, delivery, goods, price, seller, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Application of provisions of Act 9 of 1872
main_sections.description: States that unrepealed provisions of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, continue to apply to contracts for the sale of goods, unless inconsistent with this Act.
Distinguishes between a 'sale' (where property in goods is transferred) and an 'agreement to sell' (where transfer is to take place in the future or subject to conditions).
Explains that a contract of sale is made by offer and acceptance and can be written, oral, partly written and partly oral, or implied from conduct. It also covers provisions for delivery and payment.
Deals with the subject matter of a contract of sale, allowing for existing or future goods, or goods whose acquisition depends on a contingency.

main_sections.section_title: Goods perishing before making of contract
main_sections.description: Makes a contract void if specific goods perish or are damaged without the seller's knowledge at the time of contract formation.

main_sections.section_title: Goods perishing before sale but after agreement to sell
main_sections.description: Avoids an agreement to sell specific goods if they perish or are damaged without fault of either party before the risk passes to the buyer.
Provides for how the price in a contract of sale can be fixed or determined, including the concept of a reasonable price.
Addresses agreements where the price is to be fixed by a third-party valuation and what happens if the valuation cannot be made.
States that time of payment is generally not of the essence of a contract of sale, unless a different intention appears from the terms.
Defines 'condition' (essential to the main purpose) and 'warranty' (collateral to the main purpose) and their respective consequences upon breach.

main_sections.section_title: When condition to be treated as warranty
main_sections.description: Explains how a buyer may waive a condition or treat its breach as a breach of warranty, especially after accepting goods.

main_sections.section_title: Implied undertaking as to title, etc.
main_sections.description: Implies that the seller has a right to sell goods and that the buyer will have quiet possession, free from encumbrances not known to the buyer.
Implies a condition that goods sold by description shall correspond with the description.

main_sections.section_title: Implied conditions as to quality or fitness
main_sections.description: Implies conditions as to quality or fitness for a particular purpose when the buyer makes known the purpose and relies on the seller's skill or judgment.
Establishes conditions in a sale by sample: correspondence with sample, reasonable opportunity to compare, and freedom from defects not apparent on reasonable examination.
Property in goods cannot pass until the goods are ascertained.

main_sections.section_title: Property passes when intended to pass
main_sections.description: Property passes when the parties intend it to pass, which is determined by the terms of the contract and the conduct of the parties.

main_sections.section_title: Specific goods in a deliverable state
main_sections.description: Property in specific goods in a deliverable state passes to the buyer when the contract is made.

main_sections.section_title: Specific goods to be put into a deliverable state
main_sections.description: Property in specific goods passes when they are put into a deliverable state.

main_sections.section_title: Specific goods in a deliverable state, when the seller has to do anything thereto in order to ascertain price
main_sections.description: Property in specific goods passes when they are in a deliverable state and the seller has done something to ascertain the price.

main_sections.section_title: Sale of unascertained goods and appropriation
main_sections.description: Deals with the sale of unascertained goods and the appropriation of goods to the contract.

main_sections.section_title: Goods sent on approval or “on sale or return”
main_sections.description: Specifies the conditions under which property passes when goods are sent on approval or 'on sale or return'.
Allows the seller to reserve the right of disposal of goods until certain conditions are fulfilled.

main_sections.section_title: Risk prima facie passes with property
main_sections.description: States that, as a general rule, risk passes with the property in the goods.

main_sections.section_title: Sale by person not the owner
main_sections.description: Defines when a buyer of goods acquires good title, even if the seller is not the owner.

main_sections.section_title: Sale by one of joint owners
main_sections.description: Conditions under which a buyer can gain good title from a joint owner in possession.

main_sections.section_title: Sale by person in possession under voidable contract
main_sections.description: Deals with the title acquired by a buyer from a seller in possession of goods under a voidable contract.

main_sections.section_title: Seller or buyer in possession after sale
main_sections.description: Governs the title acquired by a buyer from a seller or buyer who continues in possession of goods after a sale or agreement to sell.
Outlines the mutual duties of the seller to deliver goods and the buyer to accept and pay for them.

main_sections.section_title: Payment and delivery are concurrent conditions
main_sections.description: Payment and delivery of goods are generally concurrent conditions, meaning they should happen at the same time unless otherwise agreed.
Delivery is deemed to be effectual by voluntary transfer of possession.
Part delivery of goods can indicate delivery of the whole, depending on the circumstances.
The buyer needs to apply for delivery of the goods unless the contract specifies otherwise.
Specifies various rules regarding the place, time, and manner of delivery.
Outlines the buyer's rights and remedies when the seller delivers a smaller or larger quantity of goods than contracted for, or when goods of a different description are included.
Governs delivery of goods by instalments and the consequences of defective instalments.
Explains the implications of delivering goods to a carrier or wharfinger for transmission to the buyer.

main_sections.section_title: Risk where goods are delivered at distant place
main_sections.description: Addresses risk when goods are delivered at a distant place, potentially involving the seller bearing the risk of deterioration during transit.

main_sections.section_title: Buyer’s right of examining the goods
main_sections.description: Grants the buyer a reasonable opportunity to examine the goods to ascertain their conformity with the contract.
Defines when a buyer is deemed to have accepted the goods.

main_sections.section_title: Buyer not bound to return rejected goods
main_sections.description: States that a buyer who has the right to reject goods is not bound to return them to the seller.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of buyer for neglecting or refusing delivery of goods
main_sections.description: Covers the buyer's liability for damages if they neglect or refuse to take delivery of goods.
Defines an 'unpaid seller' as one who has not received the whole price or for whom the bill of exchange or other negotiable instrument has been dishonoured.
Lists the rights of an unpaid seller, including the right of lien, right of stoppage in transit, and right of resale.
Details the seller's right to retain possession of goods until the price is paid or tendered, under certain conditions.
Explains that part delivery of goods does not necessarily terminate the seller's lien over the remaining goods.
Specifies the circumstances under which the seller's lien is terminated.
Grants the unpaid seller the right to stop goods in transit if the buyer becomes insolvent.
Defines the period during which goods are considered to be in transit.

main_sections.section_title: How stoppage in transit is effected
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure by which a seller can exercise the right of stoppage in transit.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of sub-sale or pledge by buyer
main_sections.description: Explains how a sub-sale or pledge of goods by the buyer affects the seller's right of lien or stoppage in transit.

main_sections.section_title: Sale not generally rescinded by lien or stoppage in transit
main_sections.description: Clarifies that exercising a lien or stoppage in transit does not generally rescind the contract of sale.
Allows the seller to sue for the price of goods when the property has passed to the buyer and the buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay.
Enables the seller to sue for damages if the buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to accept and pay for the goods.
Allows the buyer to sue for damages if the seller wrongfully neglects or refuses to deliver the goods.
Grants the buyer the right to sue for specific performance of the contract in cases of breach, where damages are not an adequate remedy.
Provides the buyer with a remedy for breach of warranty, typically a claim for damages.

main_sections.section_title: Repudiation of contract before due date
main_sections.description: Deals with the consequences of a party repudiating a contract of sale before the due date of performance.

main_sections.section_title: Interest by way of damages and special damages
main_sections.description: Allows for the recovery of interest by way of damages and special damages in cases of breach of contract.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of implied terms and conditions
main_sections.description: States that implied terms and conditions can be excluded or varied by express agreement, or by the course of dealing between the parties, or by usage which is not contrary to law.

main_sections.section_title: Reasonable time a question of fact
main_sections.description: Declares that what constitutes a 'reasonable time' for any purpose under the Act is a question of fact.
Provides specific rules for auction sales, including conditions relating to bidding and the completion of sale.

main_sections.section_title: In contracts of sale, amount of increased or decreased taxes to be added or deducted
main_sections.description: Mandates that in contracts of sale, any increase or decrease in taxes applicable to the goods between the time of sale and delivery shall be added to or deducted from the price.
Ensures that certain existing laws or customs are not affected by the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: A contract of sale involves the transfer or agreement to transfer property in goods for a price.
Goods are either 'existing' or 'future'.
Specific goods perishing before contract makes the contract void.
Price can be fixed, agreed upon, determined by course of dealing, or a reasonable price.
Stipulations as to time of payment are generally not of the essence of a contract.
A 'condition' is essential to the main purpose; breach allows repudiation. A 'warranty' is collateral; breach leads to damages only.
Implied condition of title: seller has right to sell.
Implied condition of fitness for purpose: buyer makes known the purpose and relies on seller's skill/judgment.
Implied condition of merchantable quality: goods must be of merchantable quality.
Sale by sample implies goods match sample, have opportunity to compare, and are free from defects not apparent on examination.
Property in goods passes when parties intend it to pass, generally when goods are ascertained and in a deliverable state.
Risk prima facie passes with property.
Sale by a non-owner can pass good title in certain circumstances (e.g., under a voidable contract, mercantile agent).
Seller's duties include delivering conforming goods; buyer's duties include accepting and paying.
Payment and delivery are concurrent conditions unless otherwise agreed.
Buyer has the right to examine goods.
Unpaid seller has rights of lien, stoppage in transit, and resale.
Damages are available for non-acceptance, non-delivery, and breach of warranty.
Specific performance may be available for breach.
Implied terms can be excluded by express agreement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but generally enforced through the civil courts for breach of contract and civil remedies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through civil suits for damages, specific performance, or other remedies for breach of contract. Penalties for specific offenses are not detailed in the provided sections.

rights: Buyer's right to receive goods corresponding to description and sample.
Buyer's right to examine goods.
Buyer's right to reject goods for breach of condition.
Buyer's right to claim damages for breach of warranty.
Seller's right to receive price and acceptances.
Seller's right to lien on goods for unpaid price.
Seller's right to stop goods in transit.
Seller's right to resell goods under certain conditions.
duties: Seller's duty to deliver goods.
Buyer's duty to accept and pay for goods.
Seller's duty to pass good title.
Seller's duty to ensure goods are of merchantable quality and fit for purpose (where implied).
obligations: Obligation to enter into contract of sale as per its formation rules.
Obligation to adhere to terms regarding delivery and payment.
Obligation to fulfill implied conditions and warranties unless excluded.
Obligation to perform contract as per its terms or face consequences of breach.

key_procedures: Formation of a contract of sale through offer and acceptance.
Ascertainment of goods and price.
Transfer of property in goods based on intent and circumstances.
Delivery of goods at agreed time and place.
Buyer's examination and acceptance or rejection of goods.
Exercise of unpaid seller's rights (lien, stoppage in transit) upon buyer's default or insolvency.
Initiation of legal proceedings (suits) for breach of contract.
administration: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text. Typically, laws related to contract and sale of goods are administered through the judicial system.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India.
It came into force on July 1, 1930.
Provisions of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, remain applicable unless inconsistent.
Certain goods like actionable claims and money are excluded from the definition of 'goods'.
Implied terms regarding quality and fitness can be excluded by express agreement or course of dealing.
Section 64A mandates adjustment of taxes in the sale price.

title: The Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939
purpose: To consolidate and clarify the provisions of Muslim law relating to suits for dissolution of marriage by women married under Muslim law and to remove doubts as to the effect of the renunciation of Islam by a married Muslim woman on her marriage tie.
scope: Applies to women married under Muslim law throughout India, with specific provisions for Pondicherry and extensions to Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Excludes Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its territorial extent, which is the whole of India (excluding Jammu and Kashmir as per subsequent amendments, and with specific provisions for Pondicherry).

main_sections.section_title: Grounds for decree for dissolution of marriage
main_sections.description: Lists the specific grounds on which a woman married under Muslim law can obtain a decree for the dissolution of her marriage. These include husband's absence, neglect, imprisonment, failure to perform marital obligations, impotence, insanity or venereal disease, repudiation of marriage before age of eighteen (if married before fifteen and not consummated), cruelty, and other grounds recognized under Muslim law.

main_sections.section_title: Notice to be served on heirs of the husband when the husband’s whereabouts are not known
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for serving notice on the husband's potential heirs in cases where the husband's whereabouts are unknown, ensuring they have the right to be heard.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of conversion to another faith
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the renunciation of Islam or conversion to another faith by a married Muslim woman does not automatically dissolve her marriage, but she can seek dissolution on the grounds specified in Section 2. It also provides a proviso for women converted to Islam from another faith who re-embrace their former faith.

main_sections.section_title: Rights to dower not to be affected
main_sections.description: States that the Act does not affect a married woman's right to her dower or any part thereof upon the dissolution of her marriage under Muslim law.
This section relating to the repeal of Section 5 of Act 26 of 1937 has been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1942.

important_rules: A woman married under Muslim law can obtain a decree for divorce on various grounds specified in Section 2.
No decree shall be passed on the ground of the husband's imprisonment until the sentence has become final.
A decree based on the husband's absence for four years will not take effect for six months, and can be set aside if the husband appears and is prepared to fulfill his marital duties.
Before passing a decree on the ground of impotence, the court must provide the husband a year to satisfy it that he has ceased to be impotent.
Renunciation of Islam or conversion to another faith by a wife does not automatically dissolve the marriage, but she can seek divorce on other grounds.
A woman married before the age of fifteen can repudiate the marriage before eighteen, provided the marriage has not been consummated.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of law.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial proceedings and decrees for dissolution of marriage based on the grounds provided in the Act.

rights: Right to seek dissolution of marriage on specified grounds.
Right to dower or any part thereof on dissolution of marriage.
Right to be heard for the heirs of the husband in suits where the husband's whereabouts are unknown.
Right to repudiate marriage before attaining eighteen if married before fifteen and not consummated.
duties: Husband's duty to perform marital obligations.
Husband's duty to provide maintenance.
Husband's duty to treat wives equitably if he has more than one.
obligations: Husband's obligation to perform conjugal duties.
Husband's obligation to satisfy the court regarding cessation of impotence.
Husband's obligation to satisfy the court of his preparedness to perform conjugal duties if his whereabouts were unknown.

key_procedures: Filing a suit for dissolution of marriage by the wife, stating the grounds as per Section 2.
If the ground is husband's absence, stating heirs' names and addresses in the plaint and serving notice on them, allowing them to be heard.
Court making an order for the husband to satisfy the court regarding cessation of impotence within one year before passing a decree on that ground.
Setting aside a decree for dissolution if the husband appears within six months and shows preparedness to perform conjugal duties after being absent for four years.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be administered by the civil courts of India.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India (with specific exclusions and inclusions mentioned in footnotes).
The provisions of this section shall not apply to a woman converted to Islam from some other faith who re-embraces her former faith.
A decree passed on the ground of the husband's absence for four years will not take effect for a period of six months.

title: The Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947
purpose: To constitute an Indian Nursing Council in order to establish a uniform standard of training for nurses, midwives, and health visitors.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the regulation of nursing, midwifery, and health visitor training and qualifications.

key_definitions.the Council: The Council constituted under this Act (Indian Nursing Council).
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under section 16.
key_definitions.[State] Council: A council constituted under the law of a State to regulate the registration of nurses, midwives or health visitors in that State.
key_definitions.[State] register: A register of nurses, midwives or health visitors maintained under the law of a State.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and that it comes into force at once.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'the Council', 'prescribed', '[State] Council', and '[State] register'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of the Council
main_sections.description: Details the composition of the Indian Nursing Council, specifying various categories of members to be elected or nominated, including nurses, heads of institutions, medical bodies, and representatives from Parliament. It also outlines the election of the President and provides for continuity of the Council's acts despite vacancies.
Declares the Council as a body corporate named the Indian Nursing Council, with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of acquiring property and suing/being sued.

Specifies how elections are to be conducted, differentiating between elections by State Councils (governed by State Government rules) and other elections (conducted in the prescribed manner). It also outlines the procedure for resolving election disputes.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and casual vacancies
main_sections.description: Defines the term of office for elected or nominated members (five years), provisions for resignation, deemed vacation of seats due to absence, and procedures for filling casual vacancies.
Outlines the procedure for holding Council meetings, including the first meeting and subsequent meetings, and specifies the quorum (ten members) and decision-making process (majority vote).

main_sections.section_title: Officers, committees and servants of the Council
main_sections.description: Details the appointment of the Secretary (initially by the Central Government), election of a Vice-President, constitution of an Executive Committee and other committees, appointment of other officers and servants, requirements for security, and the fixing of fees and allowances with Central Government sanction.
Describes the composition of the Executive Committee (nine members, including ex-officio President and Vice-President) and its powers and duties as conferred by the Act or Council regulations.

Defines recognized qualifications (Part I of the Schedule) and recognized higher qualifications (Part II of the Schedule). It outlines the process for recognizing qualifications not listed in the Schedule, negotiations with foreign authorities for reciprocity, and conditions for such recognition, including reciprocal access to practice.

important_rules: Members of the Council shall hold office for a term of five years from the date of election or nomination.
An elected or nominated member may resign by writing to the President, causing their seat to become vacant.
A member is deemed to have vacated their seat if absent from three consecutive meetings without sufficient excuse, where the interval between the first and third meeting exceeds six months.
Casual vacancies must be filled by fresh election or nomination for the remainder of the term.
Members are eligible for re-election or re-nomination.
The Council shall hold its first meeting at a time and place appointed by the President, and thereafter as appointed by the Council.
Ten members constitute a quorum for Council meetings, and decisions are made by a majority vote.
The Secretary of the Council is appointed for three years by the Central Government and holds office during the pleasure of the Central Government.

rights: Right to practice the nursing profession if holding recognized qualifications.
Right to have qualifications recognized by the Council, either directly or through reciprocity.
duties: Duty to establish and maintain uniform standards of training for nurses, midwives, and health visitors.
Duty to regulate and recognize nursing qualifications.
Duty to maintain the Indian Nurses Register.
Duty to conduct inspections to ensure standards.
obligations: Institutions granting nursing qualifications must apply for recognition if not listed in the Schedule.
Authorities in foreign countries must permit persons holding recognized Indian qualifications to practice nursing in their country for reciprocity.

key_procedures: Application for recognition of nursing qualifications not included in the Schedule: An authority must apply to the Council, which may declare it a recognized qualification.

Negotiations for reciprocity: The Council can negotiate with foreign authorities for reciprocal recognition of qualifications, provided Indian certificate holders are permitted to practice in that country.
Filling casual vacancies: A casual vacancy in the Council shall be filled by fresh election or nomination, with the new member serving for the remainder of the predecessor's term.
Conducting meetings: The Council must hold its first meeting as appointed by the President and subsequent meetings as decided by the Council, with a quorum of ten members.
administration: The Central Government plays a role in appointing the initial Secretary and fixing salaries, and the Council itself, with its Executive Committee, is responsible for administration.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Pondicherry, and Goa, Daman and Diu.
The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted by Act 34 of 2019.
Substantial amendments were made by Act 45 of 1957, affecting the extent, composition of the Council, and recognition of qualifications.

The provisions for recognition of qualifications require that for foreign qualifications, persons domiciled or originating in India holding recognized Indian qualifications must be permitted to practice in that foreign country.

title: THE DAMODAR VALLEY CORPORATION ACT, 1948
purpose: To provide for the establishment and regulation of a Corporation for the development of the Damodar Valley in the Provinces of Bihar and West Bengal.
scope: The Act extends to the States of Bihar and West Bengal. The Damodar Valley includes the basin of the Damodar river and its tributaries. The area of operation can be extended by the Central Government through notification.

key_definitions.Damodar Valley: Includes the basin of the Damodar river and its tributaries.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Corporation and includes the Chairman.
key_definitions.participating Governments: The Central Government, the State Government of Bihar and the State Government of West Bengal.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under section 59.
key_definitions.State Government: The Government of Bihar or West Bengal, and collectively the Governments of Bihar and West Bengal.

main_sections.description: Names the Act, specifies its territorial extent (Bihar and West Bengal), and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Corporation', 'Damodar Valley', 'member', and 'participating Governments'.
Establishes the Damodar Valley Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of suing and being sued.

Details the composition of the Corporation, including the Chairman, members (technical, finance, representatives from Central and State Governments, independent experts), and a Member-Secretary. It also outlines appointment procedures, disqualifications for membership, and provisions for vacancies.

main_sections.section_title: Limits of Damodar Valley and area of operations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to specify the limits of the Damodar Valley and potentially extend the Corporation's area of operation.

Outlines the primary functions of the Corporation, including promotion and operation of schemes for irrigation, water-supply, drainage, generation/transmission/distribution of electrical energy, flood control, navigation, afforestation, soil erosion control, and overall well-being in the Damodar Valley.

main_sections.section_title: Supply and generation of electrical energy
main_sections.description: Regulates the sale, transmission, and generation of electrical energy in the Damodar Valley, overriding certain provisions of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, and specifying conditions and exceptions.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.

important_rules: Construction, operation, or maintenance of any dam or water extraction installation in the Damodar Valley requires the consent of the Corporation (Section 17).
Sale, transmission, or generation of electrical energy above specified thresholds in the Damodar Valley requires permission from the Corporation (Section 18).
The Corporation may appoint Advisory Committees to ensure efficient discharge of its functions (Section 10).

penalties: Section 53 outlines penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Damodar Valley Corporation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for penalties, prosecution procedures, powers of entry, and general control by the Central Government.

rights: Right to sue and be sued (Section 3).
Right to construct, maintain, and operate canals and distributaries (Section 13).
Right to determine and levy rates for water supply (Sections 14, 15).
Right to sell electrical energy (Section 18).
Power to close roads and open spaces (Section 23).
Compulsory acquisition of land for the Corporation (Section 50).
duties: Promoting and operating schemes for various developmental activities (Section 12).
Co-operating with other authorities to minimize inconvenience caused by submersion (Section 25).
Avoiding submersion of coal mines (Section 26).
Arranging water supply on the same terms if supply has been stopped or reduced to persons with prescriptive rights (Section 16).
obligations: Participating Governments have liabilities to provide capital to the Corporation (Section 30).
The Corporation is liable to pay Central taxes (Section 43).

key_procedures: Appointment of Corporation members and officers (Sections 4, 6, 7).
Notification process for defining the Damodar Valley and area of operation (Section 11).
Determination and levy of rates for water supply (Sections 14, 15).
Obtaining permission for selling, transmitting, or generating electrical energy (Section 18).
Budget preparation and submission (Section 44).
Preparation of annual reports and financial statements (Sections 45, 46).
Auditing of accounts (Section 47).
Procedure for prosecution (Section 54).
administration: The Damodar Valley Corporation, with overall control and direction from the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act has been amended in the State of West Bengal by West Bengal Act 3 of 1956.
Sub-clause (c) of Section 18, regarding generation of electrical energy, has specific provisos for existing installations and the fertilizer factory at Sindri.
Members, officers, and servants of the Corporation are deemed to be public servants (Section 56).

title: The Delhi and Ajmer-Merwara Land Development Act, 1948
purpose: To provide for the preparation and execution of land development schemes, the reclamation of waste-land, and the control of private forests and grass-land in the Provinces of Delhi and Ajmer-Merwara.
scope: The Act extends to the States of Delhi and Ajmer. It applies to land development schemes, reclamation of waste-land, and control of private forests and grass-land within these territories. It affects owners of land, tenants, and government authorities involved in land development.

key_definitions.Board: The Land Development Board constituted for the State under section 3.
key_definitions.owner: A person having a proprietary right in the land, including a usufructuary mortgagee, and in the State of Ajmer, an istimrardar, a jagirdar, a muafidar, and a bhumia. It also includes a tenant of the land.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.reclamation: Includes cultivation, afforestation, and any other improvement of land.
key_definitions.tenant: Includes a usufructuary mortgagee of the rights of a tenant.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Delhi and Ajmer), and how its commencement date will be notified by the Chief Commissioner.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'reclamation', and 'tenant'.

Details the establishment of Land Development Boards, including the appointment of a Land Development Commissioner as Chairman, and the composition of official and non-official members. It also outlines procedures for resignation, removal, decision-making, and the appointment of a Secretary. The Chief Commissioner can also invest the Land Development Commissioner with powers of a Deputy Commissioner or Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Matters for which land development schemes may provide
main_sections.description: Outlines the various matters that land development schemes can cover, including soil preservation, erosion prevention, water supply improvement, agricultural methods, introduction of dry farming, supply of agricultural inputs, horticulture development, reclamation of waste-land, cultivation of uncultivated land, regulation of grazing, control of tree-growth, afforestation, protection from pests, and any other prescribed matter. It also specifies the particulars that every scheme must contain, such as its objects, area, works, implementing agency, cost, financing, and the duties/obligations of the Government and owners.

main_sections.section_title: Inquiry into, and sanctioning of, schemes
main_sections.description: Describes the process for sanctioning schemes. After a scheme is prepared, an Inquiry Officer is appointed, and the scheme is published for suggestions from affected persons. The Chief Commissioner then considers the inquiry report and consults the Board before submitting the scheme to the Central Government for sanction or rejection.
States that sanctioned schemes will be published by the Land Development Commissioner in the prescribed manner and will come into force on a specified date.
Grants the Board the power to make regulations for carrying out the objects of the scheme, which must also be published.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make grant or advance loan
main_sections.description: Empowers the Land Development Commissioner, with Board approval, to make grants or advance loans for carrying out works under a scheme, subject to prescribed terms and conditions. Unpaid loans can be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

Allows the Board to specify that contravention of certain provisions of a scheme or regulations is punishable with simple imprisonment up to one month, a fine up to fifty rupees, or both. Prosecutions require a written complaint from the Land Development Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Works to be carried out by Government at owner’s expense
main_sections.description: Details the process when work is to be carried out on land at the owner's expense. If the owner is willing, they can notify the Land Development Commissioner and undertake the work within a fixed timeframe. If the owner fails or informs inability, the Commissioner can get the work done and recover expenses as arrears of land revenue. Other owners benefiting from work done by one owner must contribute.

main_sections.section_title: Contribution by owners of other land benefiting by work
main_sections.description: Establishes that owners of land benefiting from work carried out under a scheme, even if not directly responsible for the work, shall contribute to its expenses as determined by the Board. The Chief Commissioner can remit contributions for Government land.

Specifies that determined contributions under sections 10(4) and 11 are to be paid within a time specified by the Board, and in default, recovered as arrears of land revenue and paid to those entitled.

main_sections.section_title: Power to carry out works and recover expenses from owners
main_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to direct the Land Development Commissioner to carry out any work not yet completed or to be carried out, and to recover the expenses (in whole or part) from owners as arrears of land revenue, based on proportions, times, and instalments fixed by the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Statement and map showing details of work
main_sections.description: Requires the Land Development Commissioner to prepare a statement and map showing details of completed work under a scheme. These, upon Board approval, become part of the settlement record or record-of-rights and necessitate corrections to the record.

If a person liable for maintenance and repairs fails to do so within the specified time, the Land Development Commissioner can get the work done by an agency and recover the expenses as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Enhancement of rent on account of improvement effected by work
main_sections.description: Allows for the enhancement of rent payable by a tenant if their land benefits from work carried out under a scheme at the owner's expense, provided the tenant did not contribute to the expenses. This is done by the Revenue Officer upon application by the owner.

Grants members, officers, workmen of the Board, or authorized persons the right to enter, survey, and carry out work on land after giving prescribed notice, for the purpose of preparing, inquiring into, or executing land development schemes. Such persons are deemed public servants.

important_rules: Land development schemes can provide for a wide range of activities including soil improvement, water management, agricultural modernization, reclamation of waste-land, afforestation, and pest control.
Schemes must detail their objects, area, works, implementing agency, cost, financing, and the duties of the Government and owners.
Works to be carried out at the owner's expense can be undertaken by the Government if the owner fails to do so, with expenses recovered as arrears of land revenue.
Owners of land benefiting from scheme works, even if not directly involved in execution, must contribute to the expenses.
Tenants whose land benefits from owner-funded scheme works can have their rent enhanced.
Persons authorized under the Act have the right of entry onto land for scheme-related purposes.

penalties: Contravention of specified provisions of a scheme or regulations can be punishable with simple imprisonment up to one month, a fine up to fifty rupees, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Land Development Commissioner (for initiating prosecution) and the Board (for specifying punishable contraventions). The Chief Commissioner has control and can invest powers in the Land Development Commissioner.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Expenses incurred by the Government for works not carried out by owners are recovered as arrears of land revenue. Contributions and loans are also recoverable as arrears of land revenue. Prosecutions are initiated based on written complaints by the Land Development Commissioner.

rights: Right of owners to carry out works at their own expense after notification.
Right of owners to apply for enhancement of rent if tenants benefit from scheme works without contribution.
Right of authorized persons to enter and survey land for scheme purposes.
Right to appeal against certain decisions (mentioned in section 18 and 28).
duties: Duty of owners to carry out works if directed or to notify inability.
Duty of owners to contribute to expenses of works benefiting their land.
Duty of persons liable to maintain and repair works.
Duty of tenants not to obstruct land development activities.
Duty of the Board to prepare and implement schemes.
Duty of the Land Development Commissioner to manage schemes and recover expenses.
obligations: Financial or other obligations of the Government and owners as detailed in the schemes.
Obligation to pay contributions determined by the Board.
Obligation to repay loans and interest as per terms and conditions.

key_procedures: Scheme preparation by the Board, including specifying objects, area, works, agency, cost, financing, and duties of stakeholders.
Scheme inquiry process involving an Inquiry Officer and inviting suggestions from affected persons.
Sanctioning of schemes by the Central Government after review by the Chief Commissioner and the Board.
Publication of sanctioned schemes and their coming into force.
Notification by owners to undertake works at their expense, with deadlines set by the Land Development Commissioner.
Recovery of expenses and contributions as arrears of land revenue.
Preparation of statements and maps of completed works and their integration into land records.
administration: The Act is administered by the Land Development Commissioner, who heads the Land Development Board. The Chief Commissioner plays a significant role in appointing officers, sanctioning schemes, and exercising control. The Central Government is involved in the final sanctioning of schemes.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to address land development in the specific regions of Delhi and Ajmer-Merwara, which were then considered Provinces.
The definition of 'owner' includes various forms of landholders and tenants, reflecting the land tenure systems in the region at the time.
The Act allows for the recovery of expenses and contributions as arrears of land revenue, indicating a strong enforcement mechanism.
Actions taken under the Act are protected from legal challenges, provided they were done in good faith (implied by Section 33).

title: The Scheduled Areas (Assimilation of Laws) Act, 1951
purpose: To assimilate certain laws in force in the scheduled areas to the laws in force in the districts of Darrang and Lakhimpur of the State of Assam, by repealing special laws and making applicable the laws in force in the specified districts.
scope: This Act applies to the scheduled areas specified in the Schedule, which are defined as parts of Balipara Frontier Tract, Abor Hills and Mishmi Hills districts (Sadiya Frontier Tract), and Tirap Frontier Tract. It assimilates laws from these scheduled areas to those in the Darrang and Lakhimpur districts of Assam.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed by the Central Government for the Act to come into force.
key_definitions.law: So much of any Act, Ordinance, Regulation, rule, order or bye-law as relates to any of the matters enumerated in List I and III in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.
key_definitions.scheduled areas: The areas specified in the Schedule to the Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'law', and 'scheduled areas'.

Specifies that laws in force in scheduled areas cease to be in force after the appointed day, and that laws in force in Darrang and Lakhimpur districts will extend to or come into force in the scheduled areas.

Empowers the Central Government or the State of Assam to direct, by order, that certain laws in the scheduled areas shall be deemed to have continued in force for a period not exceeding twelve months from the appointed day.

Provides for the continuation of certain legal proceedings related to Scheduled Tribes in the specified areas under the Assam Frontier (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1945, as if this Act had not been passed.
Authorizes the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties arising in the transition from one law or group of laws to another.

important_rules: All laws that were in force in the scheduled areas immediately before the appointed day will cease to be in force on that day, except for things done or omitted before that date.
Laws in force in the Darrang district of Assam will extend to or come into force in the areas specified in paragraph 1 of the Schedule from the appointed day.
Laws in force in the Lakhimpur district of Assam will extend to or come into force in the areas specified in paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Schedule from the appointed day.

The Central Government or the State of Assam can issue orders for a period not exceeding twelve months from the appointed day to continue the force of certain laws in the scheduled areas or to prevent others from coming into force.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the State of Assam have powers to issue orders and notifications for the implementation and administration of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette for appointing dates, making provisions for removal of difficulties, and issuing orders for transitional provisions.

rights: Proceedings related to Scheduled Tribes can continue under the Assam Frontier (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1945, despite the passing of this Act.
duties: The Central Government has the duty to appoint a date for the commencement of the Act.
The Central Government has the duty to make provisions for the removal of difficulties.

key_procedures: The Central Government appoints the 'appointed day' by notification in the Official Gazette, upon which the Act comes into force.
The Central Government or the State of Assam can issue orders specifying periods for the continuation or suspension of laws in scheduled areas.
The Central Government can issue orders, notified in the Official Gazette, to remove difficulties arising from the transition of laws.
administration: The Central Government and the State of Assam.
important_notes: The Act clarifies that section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, applies to the cessation of laws in scheduled areas.

The Act is enacted to address the assimilation of laws in areas declared by the Governor of Assam as not included in the Tribal areas specified in Part B of the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, incorporating them into adjoining districts and administering them under normal laws.
The Statement of Objects and Reasons indicates that the Assam legislature had already passed a bill for State List subjects, and this Bill addresses subjects in the Union and Concurrent Lists.

title: THE DRUGS AND MAGIC REMEDIES (OBJECTIONABLE ADVERTISEMENTS) ACT, 1954
purpose: To control the advertisement of drugs in certain cases, to prohibit the advertisement for certain purposes of remedies alleged to possess magic qualities and to provide for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies also to persons domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who are outside the said territories. It applies to advertisements relating to drugs and magic remedies.

key_definitions.advertisement: Includes any notice, circular, label, wrapper or other document, and any announcement made orally or by any means of producing or transmitting light, sound or smoke.
key_definitions.drug: Includes a medicine for the internal or external use of human beings or animals; any substance intended to be used for or in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of disease in human beings or animals; any article, other than food, intended to affect or influence in any way the structure or any organic function of the body of human beings or animals; any article intended for use as a component of any medicine, substance or article.
key_definitions.magic_remedy: Includes a talisman, mantra, kavacha, and any other charm of any kind which is alleged to possess miraculous powers for or in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of any disease in human beings or animals or for affecting or influencing in any way the structure or any organic function of the body of human beings or animals.
key_definitions.registered_medical_practitioner: Means any person who holds a qualification granted by an authority specified in, or notified under section 3 of the Indian Medical Degrees Act, 1916 (7 of 1916) specified in the Schedules to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (102 of 1956); or who is entitled to be registered as a medical practitioner under any law for the time being in force in any State to which this Act extends relating to the registration of medical practitioner.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the procedure for its commencement through notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'advertisement', 'drug', 'magic remedy', and 'registered medical practitioner'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of advertisement of certain drugs for treatment of certain diseases and disorders
main_sections.description: Prohibits the advertisement of drugs for purposes such as procurement of miscarriage, prevention of conception, improvement of sexual pleasure, correction of menstrual disorders, and diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of diseases specified in the Schedule or rules.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of misleading advertisements relating to drugs
main_sections.description: Prohibits advertisements that directly or indirectly give a false impression, make false claims, or are otherwise false or misleading regarding the true character of a drug.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of advertisement of magic remedies for treatment of certain diseases and disorders
main_sections.description: Prohibits the advertisement of magic remedies that claim to be efficacious for any of the purposes specified in section 3.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of import into, and export from, India of certain advertisements
main_sections.description: Prohibits the import into or export from India of documents containing advertisements referred to in sections 3, 4, or 5. Such documents are deemed to be goods whose import or export is prohibited.

Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder. First conviction may result in imprisonment up to six months or fine, or both. Subsequent convictions may result in imprisonment up to one year or fine, or both.

Empowers authorized Gazetted Officers to enter and search any place where an offense is believed to have been committed, seize offending advertisements or documents, and examine and seize records that may furnish evidence of an offense. Provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure apply to search and seizure.

Holds companies guilty of contravening the Act, with individuals in charge being liable. Exemption is provided if the offense was committed without knowledge or with due diligence. Directors, managers, or officers are also liable if the offense was committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect.
Declares offenses punishable under this Act to be cognizable, notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Specifies that only Presidency Magistrates or Magistrates of the first class have the jurisdiction to try offenses punishable under this Act.
Allows the court to direct forfeiture to the Government of any document, article, or thing in respect of which a contravention of the Act or rules has been made.

main_sections.section_title: Officers to be deemed to be public servants
main_sections.description: States that every person authorized under section 8 shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
Provides indemnity against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act.
Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, the provisions of any other law for the time being in force.
