Specifies exceptions to the Act's applicability, including signboards by registered medical practitioners, bona fide scientific or social treatises, advertisements sent confidentially to registered medical practitioners, government-published advertisements, and advertisements published with prior government sanction.

main_sections.section_title: Power to exempt from application of Act
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to exempt any specified drug or class of drugs, or any specified class of advertisements relating to drugs, from the provisions of sections 3, 4, 5, and 6, or to apply them subject to conditions, by notification in the Official Gazette, if public interest requires.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including specifying diseases, disorders, or conditions to which section 3 applies.

important_rules: No person shall publish any advertisement referring to any drug for the procurement of miscarriage in women or prevention of conception in women (Section 3(a)).
No person shall publish any advertisement referring to any drug for the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure (Section 3(b)).
No person shall publish any advertisement referring to any drug for the correction of menstrual disorder in women (Section 3(c)).

No person shall publish any advertisement for drugs for the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of diseases specified in the Schedule or rules, without timely consultation with a registered medical practitioner or where accepted remedies exist (Section 3(d)).
No advertisement relating to a drug shall contain any matter that directly or indirectly gives a false impression, makes a false claim, or is otherwise false or misleading (Section 4).
No person carrying on the profession of administering magic remedies shall advertise them as being efficacious for the purposes specified in section 3 (Section 5).
No person shall import into or export from India any documents containing advertisements prohibited by sections 3, 4, or 5 (Section 6).

penalties: First conviction: Imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
Subsequent conviction: Imprisonment which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Gazetted Officers authorized by the State Government (for entry, search, and seizure under Section 8).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, search, and seizure by authorized officers. Offences are cognizable. Jurisdiction lies with Presidency Magistrates or Magistrates of the first class. Forfeiture of offending materials is also possible.

rights: Right to advertise drugs for bonafide scientific or social purposes (under certain conditions, Section 14(b)).
Right to send advertisements confidentially to registered medical practitioners (Section 14(c)).
Right to publish advertisements with previous government sanction (Section 14(e)).
Right to be indemnified for actions taken in good faith under the Act (Section 12).
duties: Duty not to take part in the publication of objectionable advertisements as defined in Sections 3, 4, and 5.
Duty not to import or export prohibited advertisements (Section 6).
Duty of companies to ensure compliance, with individuals responsible being liable (Section 9).
obligations: Obligation for advertisements of certain drugs to comply with Section 3.
Obligation for all drug advertisements to be truthful and not misleading (Section 4).
Obligation for magic remedy advertisements to be truthful and not claim efficacy for prohibited purposes (Section 5).
Obligation to comply with rules made under the Act (Section 16).

key_procedures: Publication of an advertisement related to drugs or magic remedies.
Enforcement by authorized Gazetted Officers: entering and searching premises, seizing offending materials, and examining records.
Trial of offenses by Presidency Magistrates or Magistrates of the first class.
Forfeiture of offending materials by the court.
Making of rules by the Central Government for carrying out the Act's purposes.
administration: Central Government (for making rules, issuing notifications, and granting exemptions) and State Governments (for authorizing officers for enforcement).
important_notes: The Act is not intended to affect other laws in force (Section 13).

The Act provides exemptions for certain types of advertisements, such as those by registered medical practitioners, bona fide scientific treatises, advertisements sent confidentially to medical practitioners, and government-published advertisements (Section 14).
The Central Government has the power to exempt specific drugs or classes of advertisements from the Act's provisions if it's in the public interest (Section 15).

title: THE MANIPUR (COURTS) ACT, 1955
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Judicial Commissioner’s Court and other Courts in Manipur.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Manipur. Covers the establishment, appointment, jurisdiction, and administration of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner and subordinate civil courts.

key_definitions.civil suit: Includes every suit of a civil nature not expressly or impliedly classed otherwise by any law for the time being in force.
key_definitions.district court: Means the court of the district judge and includes the court of the additional district judge.
key_definitions.hill areas: Means such areas in the hill tracts of the Union territory of Manipur as the Chief Commissioner may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare to be hill areas.
key_definitions.small cause suit: Means a suit of the nature cognizable by a court of small causes under the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887.
key_definitions.value: In relation to a suit means the amount or value of the subject-matter of the suit.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of the Union territory of Manipur, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Chief Commissioner.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including Chief Commissioner, civil suit, district court, hill areas, small cause suit, and value.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner
main_sections.description: Establishes the Court of the Judicial Commissioner for the Union territory of Manipur, to be composed of the Judicial Commissioner and any Additional Judicial Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Judicial Commissioner and Additional Judicial Commissioner
main_sections.description: Details the appointment of the Judicial Commissioner and Additional Judicial Commissioner by the President, who hold office during the President's pleasure. Outlines qualifications for appointment.

main_sections.section_title: Civil and criminal jurisdiction of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner
main_sections.description: Declares the Court of the Judicial Commissioner as the highest court of appeal, revision, or reference for civil and criminal proceedings in the Union territory of Manipur, unless otherwise provided.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence and control of subordinate courts
main_sections.description: Grants general superintendence and control of all subordinate courts in the Union territory of Manipur to the Court of the Judicial Commissioner. Lists powers such as calling for returns, directing transfers, and making rules for practice and procedure.

Specifies the classes of subordinate civil courts in the Union territory of Manipur as the district court, the court of a subordinate judge, and the court of a munsiff, in addition to other existing courts.

main_sections.section_title: District court to be principal civil court of original jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Declares the district court as the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in the district.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Court of the Judicial Commissioner is a court of record and possesses all powers of such a court, including the power to punish for contempt of itself (Section 14).

Rule 2: The Court of the Judicial Commissioner shall keep necessary registers, books, and accounts and forward them to the Chief Commissioner as required. It shall also comply with requisitions for certified copies or extracts (Section 11).
Rule 3: The Court of the Judicial Commissioner may admit persons as advocates, vakils, and pleaders and may remove or suspend them from practice (Section 13).

Rule 4: No person other than an admitted advocate, vakil, or pleader shall be allowed to plead or act for parties and accused persons, except that a party may appear on their own behalf or on behalf of another if authorized (Section 13(2)).

penalties: Punishment for contempt of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner (Section 14).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Court of the Judicial Commissioner and subordinate courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the judicial process, including appeals, revisions, and the general superintendence and control exercised by the Court of the Judicial Commissioner over subordinate courts.

rights: Right to appeal or seek revision in the Court of the Judicial Commissioner (Section 8).
Right of a party to appear and act on their own behalf or on behalf of another if authorized (Section 13(2)).
duties: Duty of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner to keep registers, books, and accounts and to comply with requisitions for certified copies (Section 11).
Duty of subordinate courts to be under the general superintendence and control of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner (Section 10).
obligations: Obligation for the Judicial Commissioner to be responsible for the administration and distribution of business in the Court of the Judicial Commissioner (Section 6).
Obligation for the Chief Commissioner to consult the Judicial Commissioner when appointing district judges, additional district judges, and fixing the number of subordinate judges and munsiffs.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointment and qualification of Judicial Commissioner and Additional Judicial Commissioner (Section 4).
Procedure for the exercise of jurisdiction by the Judicial Commissioner and Additional Judicial Commissioner (Section 7).
Procedure for the administration and control of subordinate courts, including calling for returns and directing transfers (Section 10).
Procedure for the establishment and jurisdiction of subordinate civil courts (Sections 16-25).
Procedure for appeals from original and appellate decrees (Sections 32-33).
administration: Chief Commissioner of Manipur and the Court of the Judicial Commissioner.
important_notes: The Act specifies that the Court of the Judicial Commissioner can be constituted with or without an Additional Judicial Commissioner.
The Act provides for the delegation of powers by the Judicial Commissioner to the Registrar.
The Act makes provisions for the establishment of subordinate judges' courts only when notified by the Chief Commissioner.
Certain decisions are to be made according to custom or personal law (Section 42).
The Act declares the Court of the Judicial Commissioner as a High Court for certain purposes (Section 46).

title: The University Grants Commission Act, 1956
purpose: To make provision for the co-ordination and determination of standards in Universities and for that purpose, to establish a University Grants Commission.
scope: The Act applies to Universities established or incorporated by or under a Central Act, a Provincial Act or a State Act, and institutions recognized by the Commission as equivalent to a University. It also applies to institutions declared by the Central Government, on the advice of the Commission, to be deemed as Universities for the purposes of this Act. The geographical scope is India.

key_definitions.commission: The University Grants Commission established under section 4.
key_definitions.executive_authority: In relation to a University, the chief executive authority of the University (by whatever name called) in which the general administration of the University is vested.
key_definitions.fund: The Fund of the University Grants Commission constituted under section 16.
key_definitions.member: A member of the University Grants Commission and includes the Chairman and Vice-Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.university: A University established or incorporated by or under a Central Act, a Provincial Act or a State Act, and includes any such institution as may, in consultation with the University concerned, be recognised by the Commission in accordance with the regulations made in this behalf under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The University Grants Commission Act, 1956' and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Commission', 'executive authority', 'Fund', 'member', 'prescribed', and 'University'.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to institutions for higher studies other than Universities
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government, on the advice of the Commission, to declare any institution for higher education (other than a University) as a University for the purposes of the Act, making all provisions of the Act applicable to it.
Establishes the University Grants Commission as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, to be established on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Details the composition of the Commission, which includes a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman, and ten other members, all appointed by the Central Government. It specifies the criteria for selecting these members, with a focus on educators and individuals with relevant experience.

main_sections.section_title: Terms and conditions of service of members
main_sections.description: Outlines the terms of office for the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and other members. It specifies their tenure, eligibility for reappointment, and conditions for resignation and filling of casual vacancies.

Defines the general duty of the Commission to promote and coordinate university education, and to determine and maintain standards of teaching, examination, and research. It lists specific powers including inquiring into financial needs, allocating grants, recommending improvements to universities, advising governments and universities on various matters, collecting information, and requiring information from universities.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of fees and prohibition of donations in certain cases
main_sections.description: Empowers the Commission to regulate fees and prohibit donations in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition regarding giving of any grant to a University not declared by the Commission fit to receive such grant
main_sections.description: Prohibits the granting of any financial aid to a University that has not been declared by the Commission as fit to receive such a grant.
Deals with the right of Universities to confer degrees.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of the use of the word „University‟ in certain cases
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of the word 'University' in certain specified circumstances.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Commission the power to make regulations for carrying out its functions.

important_rules: The Commission has the general duty to promote and coordinate university education and to determine and maintain standards of teaching, examination, and research in Universities.
The Commission can allocate and disburse grants to Universities (including institutions deemed to be Universities) from its Fund for maintenance, development, or other specified purposes.
Universities are required to furnish information to the Commission regarding their financial position and studies.
No institution can use the word 'University' without proper authorization.
The Central Government can make rules, and the Commission can make regulations, to implement the Act.

penalties: Section 24 specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions. (Specific details of penalties are not provided in the excerpt but are indicated to exist).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University Grants Commission and the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Commission to inquire, recommend, advise, and disburse grants. The Central Government enforces the Act through its rule-making powers and by appointing and overseeing the Commission. Failure to comply with recommendations can lead to consequences as outlined in Section 14.

rights: Universities have the right to be considered for grants from the Commission.
The Commission has the right to collect information from Universities.
Persons associated with the Commission for specific purposes have the right to participate in discussions but not to vote.
duties: The Commission has the duty to promote and coordinate university education and maintain standards.
Universities have a duty to furnish information to the Commission as required.
Members of the Commission have duties related to their service terms and conditions.
obligations: Universities must adhere to recommendations made by the Commission.
Institutions must not use the word 'University' improperly.

key_procedures: Establishment of the University Grants Commission: Central Government appoints a date via notification.
Composition and Appointment of Members: Central Government appoints Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and other members based on specified criteria.
Grant Allocation and Disbursement: Commission allocates and disburses grants from its Fund to Universities based on their needs and development.
Making Rules and Regulations: Central Government makes rules, and the Commission makes regulations for the implementation of the Act.
administration: The University Grants Commission, established by the Act, and the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force on November 5, 1956.
Amendments were made in 1972 and 1985, particularly regarding the composition and terms of service of Commission members.
The Act aims to ensure that only recognized and fit institutions can use the title 'University' and receive grants.

title: THE HINDU MINORITY AND GUARDIANSHIP ACT, 1956
purpose: To amend and codify certain parts of the law relating to minority and guardianship among Hindus.
scope: Applies to the whole of India (excluding Jammu and Kashmir prior to Oct 31, 2019) and to Hindus domiciled in those territories who are outside them. It applies to Hindus by religion (including Virashaiva, Lingayat, follower of Brahmo, Prarthana or Arya Samaj), Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs, and other persons domiciled in the Act's territories who are not Muslim, Christian, Parsi, or Jew by religion, unless proven otherwise. It also applies to legitimate or illegitimate children whose parents are Hindu, Buddhist, Jain or Sikh, or one parent is such and the child is brought up in that community, or any convert/re-convert. However, it does not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes unless notified by the Central Government, nor to Renoncants of the Union Territory of Pondicherry. The term 'Hindu' is to be construed broadly to include persons to whom the Act applies by virtue of its provisions.

key_definitions.minor: A person who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.guardian: A person having the care of the person of a minor or of his property or of both his person and property. This includes a natural guardian, a guardian appointed by will, a guardian appointed or declared by a court, and a person empowered by a Court of Wards enactment.
key_definitions.natural guardian: Any of the guardians mentioned in section 6.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent and application to domiciled Hindus outside the territory.

main_sections.section_title: Act to be supplemental to Act 8 of 1890
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890.
Defines who the Act applies to based on religion and domicile, and provides exceptions for Scheduled Tribes and Renoncants of Pondicherry.
Defines 'minor', 'guardian', and 'natural guardian'.

Declares that any existing Hindu Law, custom, or usage that is inconsistent with this Act will cease to have effect, and any other law in force will cease to have effect if it is inconsistent with this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Natural guardians of a Hindu minor
main_sections.description: Specifies who the natural guardians are for a Hindu minor's person and property (excluding undivided interest in joint family property), differentiating between legitimate and illegitimate children, and boys and girls. It also outlines disqualifications for acting as a natural guardian.
States that the natural guardianship of an adopted son passes to the adoptive father and then the adoptive mother.

Details the powers of a natural guardian to act for the benefit of the minor, with specific restrictions on dealing with immovable property, requiring court permission for certain transactions like mortgage, sale, gift, or lease beyond a certain duration. It also outlines the procedure for obtaining court permission and the applicability of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890.

Enables a father, widow, or mother entitled to act as a natural guardian to appoint a guardian by will for the minor's person or property. It specifies conditions for the revival and cessation of such appointments.

main_sections.section_title: Incapacity of minor to act as guardian of property
main_sections.description: Prohibits a minor from acting as a guardian of any minor's property.

main_sections.section_title: De facto guardian not to deal with minor’s property
main_sections.description: Prohibits persons from dealing with a Hindu minor's property solely on the basis of being a de facto guardian after the Act's commencement.

main_sections.section_title: Guardian not to be appointed for minor’s undivided interest in joint family property
main_sections.description: States that no guardian shall be appointed for a minor's undivided interest in joint family property if it is under the management of an adult family member, with a proviso for the High Court's jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Welfare of minor to be paramount consideration
main_sections.description: Emphasizes that the welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in any appointment or declaration of a guardian by a court, and no person will be entitled to guardianship if their guardianship is not for the welfare of the minor.

important_rules: Rule 1: Natural guardians for legitimate boys and unmarried girls are the father, and then the mother. Custody of minors under five years is ordinarily with the mother.
Rule 2: Natural guardians for illegitimate boys and unmarried girls are the mother, and then the father.
Rule 3: The natural guardian for a married girl is the husband.
Rule 4: A natural guardian cannot bind the minor by a personal covenant.

Rule 5: A natural guardian requires previous court permission to mortgage, charge, sell, gift, exchange, or lease immovable property of the minor for a term exceeding five years or more than one year beyond the minor's majority.
Rule 6: Any disposal of minor's immovable property by a natural guardian in contravention of powers is voidable at the minor's instance.
Rule 7: Court permission for transactions involving minor's immovable property will only be granted in cases of necessity or evident advantage to the minor.
Rule 8: A minor is incompetent to act as a guardian of the property of another minor.
Rule 9: De facto guardians cannot dispose of or deal with a Hindu minor's property.
Rule 10: The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration in appointing a guardian by the court.

penalties: Any disposal of immovable property by a natural guardian in contravention of sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of Section 8 is voidable at the instance of the minor or any person claiming under him.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, specifically city civil courts or district courts, or courts empowered under section 4A of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through applications made to the court for permission to deal with a minor's property, and through legal proceedings to challenge voidable transactions. The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, governs the procedure for obtaining court permissions.

rights: Natural guardians have the power to do all acts necessary or reasonable for the benefit of the minor or their estate.
Testamentary guardians have the right to act as minor's guardian after the death of the father or mother and exercise rights of a natural guardian, subject to restrictions.
Minors have the right to challenge voidable transactions concerning their property made by natural guardians in contravention of the Act.
duties: Natural guardians have a duty to act for the realization, protection, or benefit of the minor's estate.
Natural guardians have a duty to obtain court permission before mortgaging, charging, selling, gifting, exchanging, or leasing minor's immovable property under specific conditions.
Courts have a duty to consider the welfare of the minor as the paramount consideration when appointing or declaring a guardian.
obligations: Natural guardians are obligated to not bind the minor by a personal covenant.
Natural guardians are obligated to seek court permission for specific transactions involving the minor's immovable property.
Any person appointed as a guardian by will is obligated to act within the scope and restrictions specified in the Act and the will.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining court permission to deal with minor's immovable property: Application to the court (city civil court, district court, or empowered court) as per the procedure and powers specified in sections 31(2), (3), and (4) of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. Appeals lie from refusal of permission.

Procedure for challenging voidable transactions: A minor or a person claiming under them can initiate proceedings to void a disposal of immovable property made by a natural guardian in contravention of Section 8 of the Act.
administration: The administration of this Act is primarily through the courts, particularly in matters requiring permission for property transactions and guardianship appointments. The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, also plays a significant role in procedural aspects.
important_notes: The custody of a minor who has not completed the age of five years shall ordinarily be with the mother.
The expressions “father” and “mother” in Section 6 do not include a step-father and a step-mother.
The right of a guardian appointed by will ceases on the marriage of a minor girl.
A minor's undivided interest in joint family property under the management of an adult member generally does not allow for the appointment of a guardian, except for the High Court's jurisdiction.

title: THE BIHAR AND WEST BENGAL (TRANSFER OF TERRITORIES) ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the transfer of certain territories from Bihar to West Bengal and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the States of Bihar and West Bengal. Specifically, it details the transfer of specific territories from Bihar to West Bengal and makes consequential provisions for representation in legislatures, high courts, financial matters, and apportionment of assets and liabilities.

key_definitions.appointed day: The 1st day of November, 1956.
key_definitions.transferred territories: The territories transferred from the State of Bihar to the State of West Bengal by section 3.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or in any part of Bihar or West Bengal.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1956.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'transferred territories', 'law', 'population ratio', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of territories from Bihar to West Bengal.
main_sections.description: Specifies the territories to be transferred from Bihar to West Bengal as from the appointed day, including portions of Kishanganj sub-division and Purulia sub-division. It also defines the boundary demarcation and how these territories will be incorporated into West Bengal.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the revised territories of Bihar and West Bengal after the transfer.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Fourth Schedule to the Constitution.
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution regarding the allocation of seats in the Council of States for Bihar and West Bengal.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seats in the House of the People and assignment of seats to State Legislative Assemblies.
main_sections.description: Modifies the number of seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of Bihar and West Bengal.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, Calcutta High Court.
main_sections.description: Concerns the extension of the jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court and the transfer of proceedings to it.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in transferred territories.
main_sections.description: Deals with the appropriation of moneys for expenditure in the transferred territories, referencing Appropriation Acts.
Addresses the distribution of revenues between the states of Bihar and West Bengal.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of assets and liabilities: Land and goods.
main_sections.description: Details the apportionment of assets and liabilities, starting with land and goods.
Makes provisions relating to services affected by the transfer of territories.
Specifies the territorial extent of laws in light of the territorial adjustments.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule concerning the demarcation of the boundary line for the transferred territories to ensure it does not cut across villages or towns.
Rules for the allocation of sitting members of the Legislative Assembly of Bihar to either the Bihar or West Bengal Legislative Assembly based on their constituency.
Rules for the modification of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, to reflect the territorial changes.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and state governments of Bihar and West Bengal are responsible for implementing the Act's provisions.

title: THE RIVER BOARDS ACT, 1956

title: THE MANIPUR (VILLAGE AUTHORITIES IN HILL AREAS) ACT, 1956
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the constitution and functions of Village Authorities in the hill areas of the Union territory of Manipur.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the hill areas of the Union territory of Manipur. It applies to villages having twenty or more tax-paying houses for the constitution of Village Authorities and village courts.

key_definitions.Deputy Commissioner: The Deputy Commissioner of Manipur and includes the Additional Deputy Commissioner thereof.
key_definitions.heinous offence: Includes specific offenses under the Indian Penal Code (Chapter VI, rioting, Chapter XII, murder, culpable homicide not amounting to murder, grievous hurt, kidnapping or abducting to subject a person to slavery, buying or disposing of any person as a slave, habitual dealing in slaves, rape, robbery, dacoity, mischief by fire or explosive substance, and house breaking) and offenses under the Indian Arms Act, 1878, including attempts, preparations, conspiracies, and abetments of these offenses.
key_definitions.hill areas: Such areas in the Hill tracts of the Union territory of Manipur as the Chief Commissioner may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare to be hill areas.
key_definitions.legal practitioner: Includes a pleader, mukhtar or revenue-agent.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent to the hill areas of Manipur, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including Chief Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, heinous offence, hill areas, legal practitioner, and prescribed.

Outlines the criteria for the constitution of a Village Authority based on the number of tax-paying houses. It also provides for elected or nominated Village Authorities and the appointment of a chairman.

Provides for the constitution of village courts.

Village Authorities must report unnatural, suspicious, or sudden deaths to the sub-divisional magistrate.

Decisions of village courts are generally final, but a retrial may be ordered.
Fees and fines collected by village courts are to be realized in a prescribed manner.
Members of Village Authorities are to be elected or nominated based on criteria like age and residency.

title: THE FARIDABAD DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the establishment and regulation of a trading corporation for the purpose of carrying on and promoting trade and industry in the town of Faridabad, assisting in the rehabilitation of displaced persons settled therein and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the town of Faridabad in the district of Gurgaon, State of Haryana (as per the Schedule mentioned, though not provided in full). It covers the establishment, powers, functions, and financial management of the Faridabad Development Corporation.

key_definitions.Corporation: The Faridabad Development Corporation established under section 3.
key_definitions.displaced person: Any person who, on account of the setting up of the Dominions of India and Pakistan or on account of civil disturbances or the fear of such disturbances in any area now forming part of Pakistan, has, after the 1st day of March, 1947, left, or been displaced from, his place of residence in such area and who has been subsequently residing in India.
key_definitions.Faridabad: The new township at Faridabad in the district of Gurgaon in the State of Haryana, the area of which is described in the Schedule.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Faridabad Development Corporation and includes its Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

Establishes the Faridabad Development Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of suing and being sued.
Specifies that the Corporation shall consist of a Chairman and other members, appointed by the Central Government, with a specified minimum and maximum number.

Outlines the primary responsibilities of the Corporation: to carry on and promote trade, business, and industry in Faridabad, assist in the rehabilitation of displaced persons, and manage and develop Union property vested in it.

Mandates the Corporation to maintain books of account and have its accounts audited as prescribed.

Rule: The Corporation shall have a Chairman and other members appointed by the Central Government.
Rule: The Corporation's general duty includes promoting trade and industry, assisting displaced persons, and managing Union property.
Rule: The Corporation has powers to acquire property, carry on business, provide financial aid, construct buildings, and advance loans.
Rule: The Corporation must prepare and submit an annual budget and an annual report to the Central Government.
Rule: The Corporation's accounts are subject to audit.
Rule: Members and officers of the Corporation are considered public servants.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette, appointment of members and Administrator, making rules, and directing financial provisions and audits.

title: THE SLUM AREAS (IMPROVEMENT AND CLEARANCE) ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the improvement and clearance of slum areas in certain Union territories and for the protection of tenants in such areas from eviction.
scope: Applies to all Union territories except the Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands. The Act's application can be initiated on different dates for different Union territories via official gazette notification.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator of a Union territory.
key_definitions.building: Includes any structure or erection or any part of a building, but does not include plant or machinery comprised in a building.
key_definitions.competent authority: An officer or authority appointed by the Administrator, by notification in the Official Gazette, for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.erection: In relation to a building, includes extension, alteration or re-erection.
key_definitions.land: Includes benefits to arise out of land, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.
key_definitions.occupier: Includes persons paying or liable to pay rent, owners in occupation, rent-free tenants, licensees, and persons liable to pay damages for use and occupation.
key_definitions.owner: Includes any person receiving or entitled to receive rent of any building or land, whether on their own account, on behalf of others, or as agent or trustee.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.slum clearance: The clearance of any slum area by the demolition and removal of buildings therefrom.
key_definitions.work of improvement: Includes necessary repairs, structural alterations, provision of light points, water taps, bathing places, construction of drains, provision of latrines, provision of additional or improved fixtures or fittings, opening up or paving of courtyards, removal of rubbish, and any other necessary work including demolition for improvement.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Union territories excluding Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands), and the commencement of the Act via Central Government notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, building, competent authority, occupier, owner, etc.

Empowers the competent authority to declare an area as a slum area if the buildings are unfit for human habitation or detrimental to safety, health, or morals due to dilapidation, overcrowding, faulty design, narrow streets, or lack of ventilation, light, or sanitation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of competent authority to require improvement of buildings unfit for human habitation
main_sections.description: Allows the competent authority to serve a notice on the owner requiring them to execute works of improvement to render a building fit for human habitation, provided it can be done at a reasonable expense.

main_sections.section_title: Power of competent authority to order demolition of buildings unfit for human habitation
main_sections.description: Authorizes the competent authority to order the demolition of a building if it is unfit for human habitation and cannot be rendered fit at a reasonable expense. It also allows for an undertaking from the owner to carry out improvements.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare any slum area to be a clearance area
main_sections.description: Grants the power to declare a slum area as a 'clearance area' for the purpose of slum clearance.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to acquire land
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to acquire land needed for the improvement or clearance of slum areas.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings for eviction of tenants not to be taken without permission of the competent authority
main_sections.description: Prohibits the eviction of tenants from slum areas without the prior permission of the competent authority.
Outlines the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law.
Confers the power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: A competent authority can declare an area as a slum area if buildings are unfit for human habitation or detrimental to health, safety, or morals.
Rule: Owners of unfit buildings can be required to carry out 'works of improvement' if it can be done at reasonable expense.
Rule: If owners fail to comply with improvement notices, the competent authority can carry out the works and recover expenses.
Rule: Expenses for maintenance of improvement works are recoverable from occupiers.
Rule: No person can erect a building in a slum area without the previous written permission of the competent authority (with exceptions for improvement works or areas under slum clearance orders).
Rule: Buildings unfit for habitation and not capable of being improved at reasonable expense can be ordered for demolition.
Rule: Tenants cannot be evicted from slum areas without permission from the competent authority.
Rule: The Central Government has the power to acquire land for slum improvement and clearance.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contravention of the Act's provisions (detailed in Section 32).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority, appointed by the Administrator.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notices requiring improvements, orders for demolition, acquisition of land, permission for new construction, and prohibition of eviction without permission. Penalties are enforced for non-compliance.

rights: Right of owners to be given notice and an opportunity to rectify unfit buildings.
Right to appeal against certain orders.
Right to receive compensation for acquired land.
Right of tenants to protection from eviction without competent authority's permission.
duties: Duty of owners to improve or demolish unfit buildings as required by the competent authority.
Duty of occupiers to pay for maintenance of improvement works.
Duty of persons to obtain permission for new construction in slum areas.
Duty of tenants to comply with legal procedures regarding their tenancy.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to make acquired land available to the competent authority.
Obligation of the competent authority to follow prescribed procedures for declarations, notices, and orders.

key_procedures: Procedure for declaring a slum area: Competent authority receives reports/information, is satisfied about unfit conditions, and issues a notification in the Official Gazette.

Procedure for building improvement: Competent authority serves a notice on the owner requiring works of improvement within a specified time. If not complied with, the authority can execute the works and recover costs.

Procedure for demolition: If a building is unfit and cannot be improved at reasonable expense, the competent authority serves a notice to show cause why demolition should not occur. An undertaking to improve can prevent demolition.
Procedure for slum clearance: Declaration of a slum area as a clearance area, followed by a slum clearance order, and subsequent re-development by the competent authority.
Procedure for eviction of tenants: Requires prior permission from the competent authority.
Procedure for acquisition of land: Initiated by the Central Government.
administration: Competent authority appointed by the Administrator of the Union territory. The Central Government plays a role in land acquisition and rule-making.
important_notes: The Act allows for different commencement dates for different Union territories.
The definition of 'work of improvement' is extensive, covering various aspects of building repair and amenity provision.
The Act aims to balance slum improvement and clearance with the protection of existing tenants.
There are provisions for appeals against orders made under the Act.
The Act overrides other laws in case of inconsistency.

title: The Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1959
purpose: To provide for the alteration of boundaries of the States of Andhra Pradesh and Madras and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the States of Andhra Pradesh and Madras, specifically concerning the transfer of territories between them and the consequential changes in their administrative divisions, representation in legislatures, high courts, and the apportionment of assets and liabilities.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed for the coming into force of this Act, notified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.assembly constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.council constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.parliamentary constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or in any part of Andhra Pradesh or Madras.
key_definitions.notified order: An order published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.sitting member: A person who, immediately before the appointed day, is a member of the Council of States, House of the People, or the Legislature of a State.
key_definitions.transferred territories: Refers to territories transferred between Andhra Pradesh and Madras as specified in the Schedules of the Act.
key_definitions.territorial division: References to districts, taluks, firkas, villages, or other territorial divisions are construed as referring to the area comprised within that division on July 1, 1957.

main_sections.description: Covers the extension of jurisdiction and transfer of proceedings related to the Andhra Pradesh High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, Madras High Court
main_sections.description: Covers the extension of jurisdiction and transfer of proceedings related to the Madras High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in transferred territories under existing appropriation Acts
main_sections.description: Deals with the appropriation of funds for expenditure in the transferred territories under existing appropriation Acts.
Specifies the distribution of revenues between the two states following the boundary alteration.
Addresses the apportionment of land and goods between the states.
Covers the apportionment of Provident Funds.
Deals with the apportionment of pensions.
Addresses the apportionment of contractual liabilities and benefits.
Contains provisions concerning the services of personnel affected by the boundary changes.
Defines the territorial extent of existing laws after the alteration of boundaries.
Grants the power to adapt existing laws to the new territorial arrangements.
Empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove any difficulties arising from the provisions of this Act.
Grants the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: As from the appointed day, territories specified in the First Schedule are transferred from Madras to Andhra Pradesh, and territories specified in the Second Schedule are transferred from Andhra Pradesh to Madras.
The Act provides for detailed changes in territorial divisions (districts, taluks, firkas) within both Andhra Pradesh and Madras to accommodate the transferred territories.
The Act makes consequential amendments to the Constitution of India (First and Fourth Schedules) to reflect the altered state boundaries and representation in the Council of States.
Provisions are made for the continuation of sitting members in the House of the People and Legislative Assemblies, even if their constituencies' extents are altered.

The Act details the apportionment of assets and liabilities, including land, goods, taxes, loans, deposits, provident funds, pensions, contracts, and liabilities in respect of actionable wrongs, between the two states.
The jurisdiction of High Courts and transfer of pending proceedings are addressed.
The Act includes provisions for the adaptation and construction of laws applicable to the transferred territories.

rights: Right to appear or act in any proceedings transferred under section 18 or section 19.
Right to recover loans and advances (Section 27).
duties: Duty to adhere to the apportionment of assets and liabilities as outlined in Part VI.
Duty to comply with provisions relating to services (Section 43).
obligations: Obligation to ensure that transferred territories and their populations are properly integrated into the new states.
Obligation to manage pension liabilities and provident funds of employees affected by the boundary changes.

key_procedures: Notification by the Central Government to appoint the 'appointed day' for the Act to come into force.
Transfer of territories as specified in the Schedules on the appointed day.
Reconstitution and reallocation of territorial divisions (districts, taluks, firkas) within both states.
Amendment of legislative schedules (Constitution, Delimitation Orders) to reflect new boundaries and representation.
Apportionment of assets and liabilities between the states as per the Act's provisions.
Transfer of pending proceedings in High Courts.
Adaptation of laws to the new territorial configuration.
administration: Central Government (for appointment of commencement date and removal of difficulties), State Governments of Andhra Pradesh and Madras (for administrative changes and financial matters).
important_notes: The Act specifies that nothing in Part I (Preliminary) or Part II (Transfer of Territories) affects the power of the State Governments to alter the name, extent, or boundaries of any district, taluk, firka, or village after the appointed day.
The Act includes provisions for sitting members of the legislature to be deemed elected to their respective altered constituencies.
The Act empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove any difficulties arising from its provisions.

title: The Manipur Land Revenue and Land Reforms Act, 1960
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to land revenue in the Union territory of Manipur and to provide for certain measures of land reform.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Manipur, except the hill areas thereof. The Act's provisions may come into force on different dates for different areas and different sections as appointed by the Administrator.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator of the Union territory of Manipur.
key_definitions.agriculture: Includes horticulture, raising of annual or periodical crops or garden produce, dairy farming, poultry farming, stock breeding and grazing and pisciculture.
key_definitions.basic_holding: Land used for agricultural purposes equal to 2.5 acres in area.
key_definitions.family_holding: Land used for agricultural purposes equal to 7.5 acres in area.
key_definitions.improvement: Any work that materially adds to the value of land, is suitable to the land, and consistent with its character. This includes construction of water storage/distribution works, drainage/flood protection works, land preparation for irrigation, conversion to two-crop land, reclaiming/clearing/enclosing/levelling/terracing land, erection of buildings for tenant's use or agricultural purposes, and renewal or reconstruction of such works.
key_definitions.landowner: A person who acquires rights of ownership under section 99, including their successors-in-interest.
key_definitions.personal_cultivation: Cultivation by a person on their own account by their own labor, by a family member's labor, or by servants/hired labor under their or a family member's personal supervision. Residence in the village or a nearby village during the agricultural season is required for personal supervision.
key_definitions.rent: Whatever is lawfully payable in cash or kind for the use or occupation of land or any right in land, but excludes land revenue.
key_definitions.tenant: A person who cultivates or holds land of another person under an agreement, paying rent in cash or kind or a share of the produce. This also includes those paying 'lousal' or under systems like 'bhag', 'adhi', or 'barga'.

main_sections.description: States the short title as 'The Manipur Land Revenue and Land Reforms Act, 1960', its extent to the Union territory of Manipur (excluding hill areas), and its commencement date to be notified by the Administrator.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, agriculture, basic holding, family holding, improvement, landowner, personal cultivation, rent, tenant, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Power to create, alter or abolish districts, sub-divisions, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the Administrator the power, with the concurrence of the Government, to divide the territories into districts and sub-divisions by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Definitions of “revenue survey”, “settlement” and “term of settlement”
main_sections.description: Defines key terms related to the survey and settlement of land revenue.
Deals with the preparation of the record of rights pertaining to landholdings.
Outlines the process for determining village boundaries.

main_sections.section_title: Land revenue to be first charge
main_sections.description: Establishes land revenue as a first charge on the land.
Specifies procedures for the recovery of arrears of land revenue.
Declares revenue officers to be courts for certain purposes.
Provides for the mechanism of appeals against orders passed under the Act.
Details how rights of landowners accrue under the Act.
Defines the rights and interests of tenants.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of ownership of land to tenant
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of ownership of land to tenants.
Imposes a ceiling on land holdings.
Imposes restrictions on the transfer of land to prevent fragmentation.
Contains special provisions applicable to Scheduled Tribes.
Provides for the repeal of previous laws and savings.

important_rules: Land revenue is a first charge on the land (Section 59).
Arrears of land revenue are recoverable through various means including distraint and sale of movable/immovable property (Sections 62-65).
Revenue officers are vested with court-like powers for certain proceedings (Section 81).
Appeals against orders can be filed within a specified limitation period (Sections 93-94).
Landowners have specific rights, including the right to lease and reservation of land for personal cultivation (Sections 100-101).
Tenants have rights to improvements, fair rent, and protection against eviction, with provisions for transfer of ownership to tenants under certain conditions (Sections 109-132).
There is a ceiling on land holdings to ensure equitable distribution (Chapter XI).
Fragmentation of land holdings is restricted (Chapter XII).
Special provisions are made for Scheduled Tribes (Section 158).
The Act overrides contracts and other laws to the extent of inconsistency (Section 160).

penalties: Penalty for neglect to furnish information (Section 47).
Penalty for injuring boundary marks (Section 58).
Penalties for offences under Chapter XI (Ceiling on Land Holdings) (Section 148).
Penalty for contravention of Chapter XII (Prevention of Fragmentation) (Section 155).
General provisions as to penalties (Section 164).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various revenue officers, including the Deputy Commissioner and officers appointed by the Administrator as competent authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of powers by revenue officers, including surveys, inquiries, issuing notices, distraint and sale of property for recovery of dues, and legal proceedings for offences.

rights: Right to own land (Section 99).
Right to lease land (Section 106).
Right of tenants to improvements (Section 111).
Right of tenants to fair rent (Section 114).
Right of tenants to restoration of possession (Section 120, 124).
Right of tenants to compensation for improvements (Section 122).
Right of tenants to transfer of ownership (Section 127).
Right to first option to purchase land (Section 132).
duties: Duty to pay land revenue (Section 22).
Duty to provide assistance in surveys (Section 27).
Duty to furnish information for land records (Section 47).
Duty to maintain boundary marks (Section 56).
Duty to pay rent (Section 113).
Duty to submit returns regarding holdings (Section 137).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to land revenue assessments.
Obligation to comply with survey and settlement procedures.
Obligation to adhere to the ceiling on land holdings.
Obligation to comply with restrictions on land transfers to prevent fragmentation.

key_procedures: Procedure for creation, alteration, or abolition of districts/sub-divisions (Section 3).
Procedure for survey and settlement of land revenue, including determination of rates and preparation of records (Chapters IV & V).
Procedure for realization of land revenue and other public demands, including recovery of arrears through distraint and sale (Chapter VII).
Procedure for appeals and revisions against orders of revenue officers (Chapter VIII).
Procedure for reservation of land for personal cultivation by landowners (Sections 102-104).
Procedure for transfer of ownership of land to tenants (Sections 129-131).
Procedure for determination of excess land under the ceiling provisions (Section 139).
Procedure for taking possession of excess land by the Deputy Commissioner (Section 147).
administration: The Administrator of the Union territory of Manipur, with powers delegated to various revenue officers.
important_notes: The Act excludes the hill areas of Manipur from its purview.
Different dates can be appointed for the commencement of different provisions in different areas.
The Act overrides existing contracts and other laws.
Civil courts' jurisdiction is excluded in certain matters (Section 44, 159).
Special provisions exist for Scheduled Tribes.

title: The Delhi Primary Education Act, 1960
purpose: To provide for free and compulsory primary education for children in the Union territory of Delhi.
scope: The Act extends to the Union territory of Delhi and applies to children within specified age groups and up to a certain standard for whom primary education is declared compulsory by local authorities.

key_definitions.academic_year: The year beginning on a date specified by a local authority for any area, approved schools, or classes of approved schools within its jurisdiction.
key_definitions.approved_school: Any school within a local authority's jurisdiction imparting primary education, managed by the State Government or local authority, or recognized by the local authority if under other management.
key_definitions.attendance_authority: A person appointed to be an attendance authority under section 7.
key_definitions.child: A boy or girl within an age group, not less than six or more than fourteen, as specified in a declaration under section 4.
key_definitions.local_authority: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi, the New Delhi Municipal Committee, and the Delhi Cantonment Board.
key_definitions.parent: Includes a guardian and every person who has the actual custody of the child.
key_definitions.primary_education: Education up to a prescribed class or standard, not beyond the eighth class or standard.
key_definitions.specified_area: Any area within a local authority's jurisdiction where primary education is declared compulsory under section 4.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Union territory of Delhi), and the date it comes into force, which is appointed by the State Government.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'academic year', 'approved school', 'child', 'local authority', 'parent', 'primary education', and 'specified area'.

Outlines the duty of local authorities to provide for compulsory primary education by submitting schemes to the State Government. It also details the required particulars for such schemes and the State Government's power to sanction them.

main_sections.section_title: Primary education to be compulsory in areas covered by schemes
main_sections.description: Describes how a local authority shall give effect to a sanctioned scheme by declaring primary education compulsory in specified areas for children of certain ages and standards, with specific publication and notice requirements.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of local authority to prepare lists of children
main_sections.description: Mandates the local authority to prepare and revise lists of children in specified areas after a declaration of compulsory primary education.
Empowers local authorities to appoint attendance authorities and assistants, and outlines their powers to question parents and gather information about children.

main_sections.section_title: Attendance authority to notify parent of his obligation towards his child
main_sections.description: Requires the attendance authority to notify parents about their obligation to send their children to an approved school.

main_sections.section_title: Responsibility of parent to cause his child to attend school
main_sections.description: Establishes the parent's duty to ensure their child attends an approved school, unless there is a reasonable excuse.

Lists circumstances that constitute a reasonable excuse for a child's non-attendance, such as lack of an approved school nearby, satisfactory alternative instruction, completion of primary education, or physical/mental defects.

main_sections.section_title: Special schools for physically or mentally deficient children
main_sections.description: Details provisions for children with physical or mental defects, allowing attendance authorities to direct them to special schools if deemed necessary and satisfactory instruction is not being received elsewhere.

Describes the process for issuing attendance orders against parents who fail to cause their child to attend school without reasonable excuse, including inquiry, order issuance, and provisions for custody transfer and cancellation.

main_sections.section_title: Children not to be employed so as to prevent them from attending school
main_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of children in ways that would prevent them from attending an approved school.

Ensures that primary education is free in approved schools managed by the State Government or local authorities, and outlines steps for ensuring free education in privately managed schools under specific circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Failure of local authority to prepare or implement scheme
main_sections.description: Addresses consequences when a local authority fails to submit or implement a scheme for compulsory primary education.
Specifies penalties for contravening attendance orders issued under section 13.
Specifies penalties for contravening the prohibition on employing children in a manner that prevents school attendance (section 14).
Designates the courts competent to try offenses under the Act.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Punjab Primary Education Act
main_sections.description: Repeals the Punjab Primary Education Act in its application to the Union territory of Delhi.

important_rules: Local authorities must submit schemes for compulsory primary education to the State Government.
Once a scheme is sanctioned, primary education becomes compulsory in specified areas for defined age groups and standards.
Parents are obligated to ensure their children attend an approved school unless a reasonable excuse exists.
Employment of children that prevents school attendance is prohibited.
Primary education must be free in government and local authority-managed schools, and steps must be taken to ensure it's free in some private schools where attendance is mandated.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of section 13 (attendance orders).
Penalty for contravention of section 14 (prohibition on employment preventing school attendance).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Attendance authorities appointed by local authorities, with oversight from the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of attendance orders, inquiries into non-attendance, and prosecution for violations.

rights: Children have the right to free primary education in specified schools.
Parents have the right to present reasonable excuses for non-attendance.
duties: Duty of local authorities to provide for compulsory primary education and prepare lists of children.
Duty of attendance authorities to notify parents of their obligations.
Duty of parents to cause their children to attend an approved school.
Duty of parents to inform the attendance authority of child custody transfers if an attendance order is in force.
obligations: Obligation of parents to ensure child's attendance at an approved school.
Obligation of parents to answer questions and furnish information to attendance authorities regarding their child.

key_procedures: Submission and sanctioning of schemes for primary education by local authorities and the State Government.
Declaration of compulsory primary education in specified areas.
Preparation and revision of lists of children by local authorities.
Appointment and function of attendance authorities.
Notification of parents regarding their obligations.
Inquiry process by attendance authorities for non-attendance and issuance of attendance orders.
Application for cancellation or modification of attendance orders.
Procedure for dealing with children with physical or mental deficiencies.
Procedure for special provision for part-time education.
administration: Local authorities (Municipal Corporation of Delhi, New Delhi Municipal Committee, Delhi Cantonment Board) are responsible for the implementation of schemes, with the State Government overseeing and sanctioning these schemes and having the power to make rules.
important_notes: The Act came into force on October 2, 1960.
The definition of 'child' is tied to an age group specified in a declaration under section 4, with a minimum of six and a maximum of fourteen years.
The State Government may delegate its powers under the Act.
Certain persons performing duties under the Act are considered public servants.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

title: THE SALAR JUNG MUSEUM ACT, 1961
purpose: To declare the Salar Jung Museum together with the Salar Jung Library at Hyderabad as an institution of national importance and to provide for its administration and certain other connected matters.
scope: This Act applies to the Salar Jung Museum and Salar Jung Library located in Hyderabad, Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana). It establishes a Board for its administration and defines its functions and powers.

key_definitions.Board: The Board established under section 4, known as the Salar Jung Museum Board.
key_definitions.Fund: The fund referred to in section 19, maintained by the Board.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board, including the Chairman.
key_definitions.museum: The Salar Jung Museum together with the Salar Jung Library, declared an institution of national importance.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Salar Jung Museum together with Salar Jung Library as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Salar Jung Museum and Salar Jung Library at Hyderabad as an institution of national importance.
Defines terms used in the Act, including Board, Chairman, Fund, member, museum, prescribed, and State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the Board
main_sections.description: Establishes the Salar Jung Museum Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession, common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract, subject to the Act's provisions. It also specifies restrictions on the disposal of certain articles without Central Government approval.

Details the composition of the Board, including ex officio members (Governor of Andhra Pradesh, Secretary to Government of India in the concerned Ministry, Mayor of Hyderabad, Vice-Chancellor of Osmania University, Accountant-General of Andhra Pradesh) and nominated members (one from the family of late Nawab Salar Jung Bahadur, three with museum/library experience, and two by the State Government).

Outlines the general duty of the Board to manage the museum efficiently, plan and promote its development, and perform other functions assigned by the Central Government. It also includes specific duties for instruction, research, advancement of learning, and dissemination of knowledge related to museums and libraries.

Grants the Board powers necessary to carry out its duties, subject to Central Government conditions. These include acquiring, exchanging, selling, destroying, or lending articles and things worthy of preservation in the museum.
States that properties specified in the Schedule, which vested in the Central Government by a High Court decree, will vest in the Board from the date of its establishment.

main_sections.section_title: Grants by Central Government to the Board
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to provide financial assistance in the form of grants, loans, or otherwise to the Board for efficient discharge of its functions.

Details the sources of the Board's Fund (Central Government grants, fees, donations, etc.) and its expenditure. It also specifies provisions for maintaining a current account and depositing/investing excess funds.
Requires the Board to submit a budget for the next financial year to the Central Government for approval, showing estimated receipts and expenditure.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make regulations for its meetings, association of persons, recruitment and conditions of service of staff, and other matters not inconsistent with the Act or rules made by the Central Government.

important_rules: The Salar Jung Museum and Library in Hyderabad are declared institutions of national importance.
A Salar Jung Museum Board is established with corporate status for the administration of the museum.
The Board's composition includes ex officio members and nominated members with specific expertise and representation.
The Board has the general duty to manage the museum efficiently and promote its development.
The Board has the power to acquire, sell, and lend museum articles, subject to Central Government approval for certain items.
Properties vesting in the Central Government by decree are transferred to the Board.
The Central Government may provide grants to the Board for its functioning.
The Board must maintain a Fund and operate a budget approved by the Central Government.
Officers and employees of the Board are considered public servants.
The Central Government can issue directions to the Board.
The Central Government can make rules, and the Board can make regulations for the Act's implementation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and the Salar Jung Museum Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of a Board with specific powers and duties, the ability for the Central Government to issue directions, make rules, and oversee the Board's budget and operations. Enforcement also occurs through the provisions regarding public servants and protection of actions taken under the Act.

rights: Right of the Board to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right of the Board to contract and sue/be sued.
Right of nominated members to be eligible for renomination.
Right of associated persons to take part in discussions (but not vote).
Right of existing employees to hold their office/service on the same terms unless altered to their disadvantage with Central Government approval.
duties: Duty of the Central Government/State Government to satisfy themselves about the lack of prejudicial interest of nominated members.
Duty of nominated members to disclose interest in contracts.
General duty of the Board to manage the museum efficiently and plan its development.
Duty of the Board to provide instruction and research in museum/library matters.
Duty of the Board to submit a budget for approval.
Duty of the Board to maintain accounts and undergo audit.
obligations: Obligation of the Board to obtain prior approval of the Central Government for selling or disposing of certain specified articles.
Obligation of nominated members to furnish information regarding their interests when requested by the government.
Obligation of the Board to get its budget approved by the Central Government.
Obligation for tenure, remuneration, and terms and conditions of service of existing employees not to be altered to their disadvantage without Central Government approval.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Salar Jung Museum Board by notification from the Central Government.
Nomination of Board members by the Central Government and State Government according to specified criteria.
Conduct of Board meetings according to regulations, including quorum and voting procedures.
Submission of an annual budget by the Board to the Central Government for approval.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules and the Board to make regulations.
Procedure for the transfer of existing employees' services to the Board.
administration: The Salar Jung Museum Board, under the overall supervision and direction of the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act distinguishes between 'rules' made by the Central Government and 'regulations' made by the Board.
Certain articles of historical significance (specified in the Schedule) require Central Government approval for disposal by the Board.
The Act ensures protection for actions taken in good faith under its provisions.
Officers and employees of the Board are deemed public servants, implying certain legal responsibilities and protections.

title: THE INSTITUTES OF TECHNOLOGY ACT, 1961
purpose: To declare certain institutions of technology to be institutions of national importance and to provide for certain matters connected with such institutions and the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur.
scope: The Act applies to institutions declared as institutions of national importance, including the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, and other specified Indian Institutes of Technology across India. It also covers the establishment and functioning of the Indian Institutes of Technology Council.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of an Institute.
key_definitions.Chairman: The Chairman of the Board of Governors.
key_definitions.Institute: Any of the institutions mentioned in section 2, including the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur.
key_definitions.society: Refers to various registered societies, including Indian Institutes of Technology, Bombay, Delhi, Guwahati, Kanpur, Madras, and others listed.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: Statutes and Ordinances of an Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares various Indian Institutes of Technology as institutions of national importance.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as Board, Chairman, Council, Director, Institute, Registrar, Senate, society, Statutes, Ordinances, University of Roorkee, and zone.
Establishes each of the declared Institutes as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Details the consequences of incorporation, including transfer of property, rights, liabilities, and employment conditions from societies to the corresponding Institutes.
Provides for the establishment of the Council.
Outlines the functions of the Council.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: Institutes are declared as institutions of national importance (Section 2).
Each Institute shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (Section 4(1)).

On incorporation, references to societies shall be deemed references to the corresponding Institute; property, rights, and liabilities of societies shall vest in the Institutes; and employees shall continue under similar terms and conditions (Section 5).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and authorities established under the Act (e.g., Council, Board, Senate).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, appointment of dates, establishment of the Council, and by the powers vested in the Institutes and their authorities as defined in the Act and subsequent Statutes and Ordinances.

rights: Right of employees to retain tenure, remuneration, and terms/conditions of service, with provisions for termination and compensation (Section 5(d)).
duties: Institutes are to be open to all races, creeds, and classes (Section 7).
obligations: Institutes have obligations related to their incorporation, transfer of assets and liabilities, and employee conditions.
The Central Government has the obligation to appoint commencement dates and potentially specify zones.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act on a date appointed by the Central Government (Section 1(2)).
Declaration of institutions as national importance (Section 2).
