Incorporation of institutes as bodies corporate (Section 4).
Transfer of property, rights, and liabilities upon incorporation (Section 5).
Establishment and functioning of the Council (Sections 31-35).
Making of Statutes and Ordinances (Sections 26-29).
administration: The Central Government plays a significant role in the commencement and oversight, while specific administration of each Institute is managed by its Board of Governors and Senate, overseen by the Indian Institutes of Technology Council.
important_notes: The Act has undergone several amendments to include new IITs and institutions.
Different commencement dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The Act includes provisions for removing difficulties and transitional arrangements.

title: The State of Nagaland Act, 1962
purpose: To provide for the formation of the State of Nagaland and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the formation of the State of Nagaland, its representation in legislatures, the establishment of a common High Court, and financial and miscellaneous provisions related to the new state. Geographically, it pertains to the territories that were comprised in the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area.

key_definitions.appointed day: The day which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument or custom or usage having the force of law.
key_definitions.Naga Hills-Tuensang Area: The Naga Hills-Tuensang Area specified in Part B of the Table appended to paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution, comprising the areas which at the commencement of the Constitution were known as the Naga-Hills District and the Naga Tribal Area.
key_definitions.regional council: The regional council referred to in article 371A.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the State of Nagaland Act, 1962.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'article', 'assembly constituency', 'parliamentary constituency', 'law', 'Naga Hills-Tuensang Area', and 'regional council'.

Establishes the State of Nagaland as a new state comprising the territories of the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area, effective from the appointed day. It also specifies the initial three districts of the new state: Kohima, Mokokchung, and Tuensang.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to include the State of Nagaland and its territories.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Sixth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution by omitting certain provisions related to the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area.
Allots one seat to the State of Nagaland in the Council of States and makes consequential amendments to the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in House of the People
main_sections.description: Allots one seat to the State of Nagaland in the House of the People and makes consequential amendments to the Representation of the People Act, 1950. It also defines the parliamentary constituency for Nagaland.

Specifies the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland (initially 60, with a temporary provision for 52 seats for a period related to article 371A). It details seat allocation to Tuensang district and other areas, and outlines procedures for delimitation of constituencies.

main_sections.section_title: Common High Court for Assam and Nagaland
main_sections.description: Establishes a common High Court for the States of Assam and Nagaland, to be known as the High Court of Assam and Nagaland. It also addresses the allocation of expenditure for the Judges' salaries and allowances.

important_rules: The State of Nagaland shall be formed on the appointed day, comprising the territories previously in the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area, which will then cease to be part of Assam.
The State of Nagaland shall initially consist of three districts: Kohima, Mokokchung, and Tuensang.
The State of Nagaland shall be allotted one seat in the Council of States and one seat in the House of the People.
The Legislative Assembly of Nagaland shall have 60 seats, with specific provisions for a temporary reduction in seats and allocation to the Tuensang district.
A common High Court, the High Court of Assam and Nagaland, shall be established for both states.

rights: Right of advocates practicing in the High Court of Assam to practice in the common High Court.
Right of audience in the common High Court regulated by principles in force for the High Court of Assam.
duties: Preparation and revision of electoral rolls for the parliamentary constituency of Nagaland, with a separate roll for the Tuensang district part.
obligations: The Central Government's role in appointing the 'appointed day' through notification.
The President's role in determining the proportion of expenditure for the common High Court judges between Assam and Nagaland.

key_procedures: Procedure for the formation of the State of Nagaland on the 'appointed day'.
Procedure for amending the First and Sixth Schedules of the Constitution.
Procedure for the election of representatives to the Council of States and the House of the People.
Procedure for the delimitation of assembly constituencies in Nagaland by the Election Commission, including inviting objections and suggestions, holding public sittings, and publishing final orders.
Procedure for making rules of procedure for the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland, initially adopting rules from Assam's Legislative Assembly.
administration: The Act implies administration by the Central Government for appointments (appointed day) and potentially for defining district boundaries. The Election Commission is responsible for delimitation of constituencies. The High Court of Assam and Nagaland will administer judicial matters. The Governor will specify the manner of choosing members from the regional council for the Legislative Assembly.
important_notes: The provisions regarding the strength of the Legislative Assembly and seat allocation to Tuensang district are subject to a specific period referred to in clause (2) of article 371A.
The term of office for the first member elected to the Council of States from Nagaland will expire on April 2, 1968.
The sitting member representing the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area in the House of the People will continue to represent Nagaland until a new election is held.

title: THE EXTRADITION ACT, 1962
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the extradition of fugitive criminals and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to foreign states with which extradition arrangements exist and can be extended to other foreign states by notified order. It deals with the apprehension and return of fugitive criminals to foreign states.

key_definitions.composite_offence: An act or conduct of a person occurred, wholly or in part, in a foreign State or in India but its effects or intended effects, taken as a whole, would constitute an extradition offence in India or in a foreign State, as the case may be.
key_definitions.conviction: Does not include or refer to a conviction which under foreign law is a conviction for contumacy, but the term 'person accused' includes a person so convicted for contumacy.
key_definitions.extradition_offence: In relation to a foreign State being a treaty State, an offence provided for in the extradition treaty with that State; in relation to a foreign State other than a treaty State, an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year under the laws of India or of a foreign State and includes a composite offence.
key_definitions.extradition_treaty: A treaty, agreement or arrangement made by India with a foreign State relating to the extradition of fugitive criminals, and includes any treaty, agreement or arrangement relating to the extradition of fugitive criminals made before the 15th day of August, 1947, which extends to, and is binding on, India.
key_definitions.foreign_state: Means any State outside India and includes every constituent part, colony or dependency of such State.
key_definitions.fugitive_criminal: A person who is accused or convicted of an extradition offence within the jurisdiction of a foreign State and includes a person who, while in India, conspires, attempts to commit or incites or participates as an accomplice in the commission of an extradition offence in a foreign State.
key_definitions.magistrate: A magistrate of the first class or a presidency magistrate.
key_definitions.notified_order: An order notified in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.treaty_state: A foreign State with which an extradition treaty is in operation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as the Extradition Act, 1962, states its extent to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'composite offence', 'conviction', 'extradition offence', 'extradition treaty', 'foreign State', 'fugitive criminal', 'magistrate', 'notified order', 'prescribed', and 'treaty State'.

Details how the Act (other than Chapter III) can be applied to foreign states by notified order, with provisions for restricting application to certain parts of India and for implementing treaties with modifications.
Outlines the procedure for making a requisition for the surrender of a fugitive criminal of a foreign state to the Central Government, typically through its diplomatic representative.
Empowers the Central Government to issue an order to a magistrate to inquire into the case of a fugitive criminal if a requisition for surrender is made.
Mandates the magistrate to issue a warrant for the arrest of the fugitive criminal upon receiving an order from the Central Government.

Specifies the procedure before the magistrate, including inquiry into the case, taking evidence, discharging the fugitive if a prima facie case is not made out, or committing the fugitive to prison to await Central Government orders if a prima facie case is established.
Allows the Central Government to issue a warrant for the custody, removal, and delivery of a fugitive criminal to a foreign state if it is of the opinion that the fugitive ought to be surrendered.
States that Chapter III applies only to those foreign states to which the Central Government, by notified order, deems it expedient to apply it due to an extradition arrangement.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of fugitive criminals from foreign States to be apprehended and returned
main_sections.description: Declares that a fugitive criminal of a foreign State to which Chapter III applies, found in India, is liable to be apprehended and returned to that State.
States that a fugitive criminal can be apprehended in India under an endorsed warrant or a provisional warrant.

important_rules: Rule 1: A requisition for the surrender of a fugitive criminal of a foreign state must be made to the Central Government, typically by its diplomatic representative.
Rule 2: Upon a requisition, the Central Government may order a magistrate to inquire into the case.
Rule 3: The magistrate, upon receiving the Central Government's order, shall issue a warrant for the arrest of the fugitive criminal.
Rule 4: During the magisterial inquiry, evidence in support of the requisition and on behalf of the fugitive criminal shall be taken.
Rule 5: If a prima facie case is not made out, the fugitive criminal shall be discharged.
Rule 6: If a prima facie case is made out, the fugitive criminal may be committed to prison to await the orders of the Central Government.
Rule 7: The Central Government may issue a warrant for the surrender of the fugitive criminal if it is of the opinion that surrender is warranted.
Rule 8: Documents, depositions, and certificates from foreign states relating to extradition offences must be duly authenticated to be received as evidence.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and Magistrates
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of warrants, magisterial inquiries, and Central Government orders for surrender.

rights: Right of a fugitive criminal to present evidence on their behalf during magisterial inquiry.
Right of a fugitive criminal to be discharged if a prima facie case is not made out.
Right of a fugitive criminal to be released on bail in certain cases (Section 25, not fully detailed in excerpt).
Protection from trial for certain offences for surrendered or returned accused or convicted persons (Section 21).
duties: Duty of the Central Government to consider the case of a fugitive criminal before ordering surrender.
Duty of the magistrate to report the issue of arrest warrants to the Central Government.
Duty of the magistrate to commit a fugitive criminal to prison to await Central Government orders if a prima facie case is made out.

key_procedures: Requisition for surrender of a fugitive criminal by a foreign state to the Central Government.
Central Government ordering a magisterial inquiry.
Magistrate issuing an arrest warrant for the fugitive criminal.
Magisterial inquiry into the case, including taking evidence.
Magistrate committing the fugitive criminal to prison to await Central Government orders if a prima facie case is established.
Central Government reviewing the magistrate's report and issuing a surrender warrant if deemed appropriate.
Apprehension of a fugitive criminal using an endorsed or provisional warrant.
Authentication of foreign documents for evidentiary purposes.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: Chapter III applies only to foreign states with which extradition arrangements exist, as determined by the Central Government through notified orders.
The Act can be applied to foreign states with modifications, exceptions, conditions, and qualifications for implementing extradition arrangements.
The Act does not apply to fugitive criminals to which Chapter III applies when considering Chapter II.
A person arrested on a provisional warrant may not be detained for more than three months unless an order from the Central Government is received within that period.

title: THE MANIPUR (SALES OF MOTOR SPIRIT AND LUBRICANTS) TAXATION ACT, 1962
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the levy of a tax on sales of motor spirit and lubricants in the Union territory of Manipur.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Manipur. It covers the sale of motor spirit and lubricants by dealers.

key_definitions.dealer: Any person who sells taxable goods manufactured, made or processed by him in, or brought by him into, the Union territory from any place outside that territory for the purpose of sale in that territory. Includes managers or agents of dealers residing outside the Union territory.
key_definitions.lubricant: Any form of oil or other lubricating substance primarily used for lubricating machinery or parts of motor vehicles and other machinery, including greases, spindle oils, cutting oils, and hydraulic brake fluids.
key_definitions.motor_spirit: Any substance ordinarily used as fuel for automotive or stationary internal combustion engines, including petrol and diesel oil, but excluding kerosene, furnace oil, coal, or charcoal.
key_definitions.person: Includes a Department of Government and a Hindu Joint Family.
key_definitions.petrol: Dangerous petroleum as defined in the Petroleum Act, 1934.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.sale: Any transfer of property in goods by one person to another for cash or deferred payment or any other valuable consideration.
key_definitions.taxable_goods: Goods specified in sub-section (1) of section 3.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of the Union territory of Manipur), and the commencement date to be notified by the Chief Commissioner.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Chief Commissioner', 'Commissioner', 'dealer', 'lubricant', 'motor spirit', 'sale', and 'taxable goods'.

Details the levy and collection of tax on sales of specified goods (motor spirit, lubricants, diesel oil, internal combustion oils other than petrol, crude oil) at rates fixed by the Central Government. It also specifies exemptions for sales outside the Union territory, in the course of import/export, or inter-State trade. It also includes a provision for taxing shortages in motor spirit received into stock.
Empowers the Chief Commissioner to appoint a Commissioner of Taxes and other assisting persons to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Mandates dealers to apply for registration, obtain separate certificates for each place of business, and prohibits carrying on business in taxable goods without a valid registration certificate.

Outlines the grounds for cancellation of a registration certificate by the Commissioner, including cessation of business, non-payment of tax, breach of provisions, or conviction. It also specifies procedures for cancellation and clarifies that cancellation does not absolve the dealer from liabilities.
Requires every registered person to submit prescribed returns at prescribed intervals to the prescribed authority.
Describes the process of assessment of tax payable by a dealer, either based on a furnished return or through best judgment assessment if the return is unsatisfactory or a return is not filed.

Provides for the cancellation of an assessment made under best judgment if the dealer satisfies the Commissioner within a month that they were prevented by sufficient cause from filing the return or complying with notices.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment and penalty in case of evasion by unregistered persons
main_sections.description: Details the process of assessment and imposition of penalty for persons liable to tax but who failed to register and pay tax. The penalty can be up to the amount of tax assessed.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment and penalty in case of evasion by registered persons
main_sections.description: States that registered persons who have not paid the full tax due can be proceeded against in a similar manner as unregistered persons evading tax.

main_sections.section_title: Power to grant exemption from tax
main_sections.description: Grants the Chief Commissioner the power to exempt, by notification, any class of dealers or any specific dealer from payment of tax, in the public interest or under exceptional circumstances.

Specifies penalties for various offenses, including failure to furnish returns, non-compliance with notices, concealment of sales particulars, and evasion of tax liability. Penalties can be up to one and a half times the tax payable or the tax sought to be evaded.

Establishes the right of a dealer to appeal against an order of assessment or penalty within thirty days. It also requires the deposit of tax or penalty pending appeal, with provisions for dispensing with the deposit in cases of undue hardship.
Grants the Commissioner powers of revision over orders passed by subordinate officers.
Grants the Chief Commissioner powers of revision over orders passed by the Commissioner or other authorities.
Deals with the payment of tax, penalties, and other dues under the Act.
Outlines the procedures for the recovery of tax, penalties, and other amounts due under the Act.
Provides for the refund of tax paid in excess or otherwise erroneously paid.
Requires dealers to maintain proper accounts of their business transactions.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to order production of accounts, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers taxing authorities to order the production of accounts, documents, or other evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Power for entry, inspection, search and seizure
main_sections.description: Grants powers to authorized officers to enter, inspect, search, and seize goods or documents.
Defines offenses under the Act and prescribes penalties for them.
Prescribes penalties for making false statements in declarations required under the Act.
Specifies the procedure for conducting searches and seizures.
Grants powers of investigation to authorized officers.
Provides punishment for officers conducting vexatious searches or seizures.
Specifies goods or things that are liable to confiscation under the Act.
Empowers authorities to compound offenses under the Act.
Deals with the cognizance of offenses by courts.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting in good faith and limitation of suits and proceedings
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith under the Act and imposes limitations on suits and proceedings.
Allows the Commissioner to delegate his powers to subordinate officers.

main_sections.section_title: Computation of the period of limitation
main_sections.description: Specifies how the period of limitation is to be computed for various actions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Information to be furnished regarding change of business
main_sections.description: Requires dealers to furnish information regarding any change in their business.
Lays down the procedure for serving orders and notices under the Act.
Empowers the Chief Commissioner to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Assam Act 4 of 1939 as extended to Manipur
main_sections.description: Repeals the Assam Sales Tax Act, 1939, as extended to Manipur, indicating this Act is the superseding legislation for Manipur.

important_rules: Dealers must apply for registration within a prescribed time and obtain a separate certificate for each place of business (Section 5).
No dealer shall carry on business in taxable goods without a valid registration certificate (Section 5(5)).
Registered persons must submit prescribed returns at prescribed intervals (Section 7).
Shortages in motor spirit exceeding one percent of received quantities are presumed to be due to sale and subject to tax (Section 3(4)).
Dealers must deposit tax demanded or penalty levied pending appeal, unless it causes undue hardship (Section 14(2)).
Dealers must maintain proper accounts of their business (Section 20).

penalties: Penalty for failure to furnish returns or comply with notices: up to 1.5 times the tax (Section 13(1)(a) & (b)).
Penalty for concealing sales particulars or furnishing incorrect particulars: up to 1.5 times the tax that would have been avoided (Section 13(1)(c)).
Penalty for evading tax liability: up to 1.5 times the tax sought to be evaded (Section 13(1)(d)).
Penalty for evasion by unregistered persons: up to the amount of tax assessed (Section 10).
Penalties for false statements in declarations (Section 24).
Punishment for vexatious search, etc. (Section 27).
Confiscation of things liable to confiscation (Section 28).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner of Taxes, assisted by other appointed persons, under the overall direction of the Chief Commissioner.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, imposition of penalties, search and seizure powers, investigation, compounding of offenses, and recovery procedures. Appeals and revisions provide for review of decisions.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment or penalty orders (Section 14).
Right to be heard before penalty is imposed or assessment is made based on best judgment (Sections 6, 8, 10, 11, 13).
Right to apply for cancellation of registration if business has ceased (Section 6).
Right to seek cancellation of assessment under certain circumstances (Section 9).
Right to apply for exemption from tax under exceptional circumstances (Section 12(2)).
duties: Duty to apply for registration and obtain a certificate (Section 5).
Duty to furnish returns as prescribed (Section 7).
Duty to pay tax assessed and any penalties imposed (Sections 3, 10, 11, 13).
Duty to maintain accounts (Section 20).
Duty to furnish information regarding change of business (Section 34).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation to cooperate with taxing authorities during assessments, inspections, and investigations.

key_procedures: Registration of dealers: Application for registration, issuance of certificate, and amendment/cancellation of certificate (Sections 5 & 6).

Assessment of tax: Filing of returns, assessment based on returns, or best judgment assessment if returns are unsatisfactory or not filed, with provisions for cancellation of assessment (Sections 7, 8, 9).
Evasion assessment and penalty: Procedures for assessing tax and imposing penalties on persons evading tax, whether registered or unregistered (Sections 10 & 11).
Appeals: Filing an appeal against assessment or penalty orders, with provisions for deposit of tax/penalty pending appeal (Section 14).
Search, seizure, and investigation: Powers of officers to conduct searches, seizures, and investigations, with procedures outlined (Sections 22, 25, 26).
Service of notices: Procedures for serving orders and notices on dealers (Section 35).
administration: The Chief Commissioner of Manipur, through the Commissioner of Taxes and other appointed taxing authorities.
important_notes: The Act specifically applies to 'motor spirit' and 'lubricants' and defines these terms with exclusions.
The rates of tax are to be fixed by the Central Government by notification, not exceeding specified rates.
Exemptions from tax can be granted by the Chief Commissioner in the public interest.
Provisions exist for compounding offenses, suggesting a mechanism for resolving minor violations outside of court proceedings.
The Act repeals an earlier Assam Act extended to Manipur, consolidating the law on sales tax for these specific commodities in the Union territory.

title: THE DELHI MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION ACT, 1962
purpose: To impose a tax on motor vehicles in the Union territory of Delhi and for other matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to all motor vehicles used or kept for use in the Union territory of Delhi.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator of Delhi appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.quarter: A period of three months commencing on the first day of April, the first day of July, the first day of October or the first day of January in each year.
key_definitions.registered owner: The person in whose name a motor vehicle is registered under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (4 of 1939).
key_definitions.tax: The tax levied under this Act.
key_definitions.taxation authority: Any person or authority appointed by the Administrator by notification in the Official Gazette to exercise the powers and perform the duties conferred or imposed upon a taxation authority by or under this Act.
key_definitions.token: A ticket to be displayed on a motor vehicle as an indication that the tax has been duly paid or that no tax is payable.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of the Union territory of Delhi), and the commencement date to be appointed by the Administrator.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Administrator, Delhi, prescribed, quarter, registered owner, tax, taxation authority, token, and year. It also states that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, shall have their respective meanings.

Specifies the levy and collection of tax on motor vehicles used or kept for use in Delhi. It details taxes for vehicles in Part A of Schedule I (annual or quarterly rates) and Part B of Schedule I (one-time tax upon registration or re-registration). It also allows for an increase in tax rates by the Administrator, with limitations, and excludes certain vehicles from increased rates.

Requires every registered owner or person in possession/control of a motor vehicle to fill and sign a declaration and pay the applicable tax, either annually, quarterly, or a one-time tax as per Schedule I. Tax calculation for periods less than a year is also detailed.

Mandates the taxation authority to issue a token upon payment of tax or proof of no tax liability. It also requires an endorsement on the certificate of registration. No motor vehicle liable to tax can be used or kept for use without a valid, displayed token.

Requires an additional declaration and payment of additional tax if a motor vehicle is altered or its use changes in a way that incurs higher tax liability. A fresh token is issued upon receipt of the additional tax.

Outlines the liability for additional tax when a motor vehicle is altered or its use changes during a period for which tax has been paid, making it subject to a higher tax rate. The additional tax is for the unexpired portion of the period.
Requires the production of a valid certificate of insurance complying with Chapter VIII of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, at the time of tax payment.

main_sections.section_title: Liability to pay arrears of tax of person succeeding to the ownership, possession or control of motor vehicles
main_sections.description: States that if tax remains unpaid by a person who then transfers ownership or ceases possession/control, the successor in ownership or possession/control becomes liable for the arrears, without affecting the original defaulter's liability.

Details the conditions and entitlement for a refund of tax paid when a vehicle's tax token and registration certificate are surrendered, or when a vehicle is removed outside Delhi or its registration is cancelled before the tax period expires. It also allows for corresponding increases in refund rates when tax rates are increased.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty payable when tax not paid
main_sections.description: Empowers the taxation authority to impose a penalty, not exceeding the annual tax, in addition to arrears, when tax payment is in default. Requires a directive before imposing the penalty.

main_sections.section_title: Arrears of tax and penalty recoverable as arrears of land revenue
main_sections.description: States that arrears of tax and penalty are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
Provides for exemptions from tax.

main_sections.section_title: Reduction of tax in cases of certain motor vehicles
main_sections.description: Allows for a reduction of tax in specific cases for certain motor vehicles.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of payment of tax in other States with respect to motor vehicles brought into Delhi
main_sections.description: Deals with the effect of paying tax in other States for motor vehicles brought into Delhi.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders made under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of police officers and other officers
main_sections.description: Confers powers upon police officers and other designated officers.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for incomplete and untrue declaration, etc.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for making incomplete or untrue declarations.
Enacts other penalties for contraventions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Utilization of the proceeds of tax
main_sections.description: Specifies how the proceeds from the tax are to be utilized.
Details the procedure for the trial of offences under the Act.
Provides protection for acts done in good faith under the Act.
Grants the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Annuls previous legislation.
Amends a specific section of another Act.

important_rules: Every registered owner or person in possession/control of a motor vehicle must submit a declaration and pay the applicable tax within the prescribed time (Section 4).
No motor vehicle liable to tax can be used or kept for use in Delhi unless a valid token is obtained and displayed (Section 5(2)).
When a vehicle's use or alteration leads to a higher tax liability, an additional declaration and tax payment are required for the unexpired period (Section 6 & 7).
A valid certificate of insurance must be produced at the time of tax payment (Section 8).
Arrears of tax are recoverable as arrears of land revenue (Section 12).

penalties: Penalty not exceeding the annual tax payable, in addition to arrears, for default in tax payment (Section 11).
Penalties for incomplete and untrue declarations (Section 18).
Other penalties for contraventions of the Act (Section 19).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Taxation authority, police officers, and other officers appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment and collection of tax, imposition of penalties, recovery of arrears as land revenue, and trial of offences. Police and other officers may have specific powers for enforcement.

rights: Right to receive a token upon payment of tax or proof of no liability (Section 5(1)(a)).
Right to have the certificate of registration endorsed regarding tax payment (Section 5(1)(b)).
Right to appeal against orders made under the Act (Section 16).
Right to a refund of tax under specific conditions (Section 10).
duties: Duty to pay the levied tax on motor vehicles (Section 3 & 4).
Duty to submit a declaration and pay tax within prescribed time (Section 4).
Duty to display the tax token on the vehicle (Section 5(2)).
Duty to submit an additional declaration and pay additional tax when applicable (Section 6).
Duty to produce a certificate of insurance at the time of tax payment (Section 8).
obligations: Obligation to ensure tax is paid for any motor vehicle used or kept for use in Delhi.
Obligation to comply with all rules and regulations prescribed under the Act.

key_procedures: Declaration and Payment of Tax: Registered owner/person in control fills a prescribed form, declares particulars, and pays tax to the taxation authority within the prescribed time. Tax can be paid annually, quarterly, or for shorter periods as per rates in Schedule I (Section 4).

Issue of Token: Upon tax payment or proof of no liability, the taxation authority issues a token and makes an endorsement on the registration certificate. The token must be displayed on the vehicle (Section 5).
Refund Application: A person seeking a refund must apply to the taxation authority with required certificates (e.g., from registering authority) and fulfill prescribed conditions (Section 10).
Appeal Process: An aggrieved person can file an appeal against an order passed under the Act as per the prescribed procedure (Section 16).
administration: The Administrator of Delhi and the taxation authority appointed by the Administrator.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1989, with certain provisions coming into force in 1990, indicating significant changes to the original legislation.
Motor vehicles more than ten years old from their first registration may not attract tax under certain conditions, requiring endorsement on their registration certificates (Section 3(1) proviso).
Fractions of a rupee are counted as a whole rupee for tax calculation (Section 4(4)).
Broken periods in a month are considered a full month for calculating unexpired portions for additional tax (Section 7, Explanation).

title: THE COMPANIES (PROFITS) SURTAX ACT, 1964
purpose: To impose a special tax on the profits of certain companies.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to companies. The tax is on chargeable profits that exceed the statutory deduction.

key_definitions.assessee: A person by whom surtax or any other sum of money is payable under this Act and includes every person in respect of whom any proceeding under this Act has been taken for the assessment of his chargeable profits or of the amount of refund due to him or of the chargeable profits of any other person in respect of which he is assessable or of the amount of refund due to such other person.
key_definitions.assessment year: The period of twelve months commencing on the 1st day of April, every year.
key_definitions.chargeable profits: The total income of an assessee computed under the Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961) for any previous year or years, as the case may be, and adjusted in accordance with the provisions of the First Schedule.
key_definitions.statutory deduction: An amount equal to fifteen per cent. of the capital of the company as computed in accordance with the provisions of the Second Schedule, or an amount of two hundred thousand rupees, whichever is greater. This amount is adjusted proportionately if the previous year is longer or shorter than twelve months.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Companies (Profits) Surtax Act, 1964 and specifies its territorial extent as the whole of India.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including advance surtax, assessee, assessment year, chargeable profits, and statutory deduction. It also clarifies that undefined terms with definitions in the Income-tax Act will have the meanings assigned to them in that Act.

Specifies that income-tax authorities under the Income-tax Act are also authorities for this Act. It outlines their jurisdiction and the power of the Board (Central Board of Direct Taxes) to issue orders, instructions, and directions for administration, with certain restrictions to avoid interference with judicial discretion.

Imposes a surtax on every company for assessment years commencing on or after April 1, 1964, but before April 1, 1988. The tax is levied on the chargeable profits of the previous year or years that exceed the statutory deduction, at rates specified in the Third Schedule.

Mandates companies whose chargeable profits exceed the statutory deduction to furnish a return of chargeable profits by September 30th of the assessment year. It also allows the Assessing Officer to issue a notice for a return and permits assessees to file revised returns before assessment.

Empowers the Assessing Officer to require assessees to produce accounts, documents, or evidence for assessment. After considering the obtained material, the Assessing Officer will issue an order assessing the chargeable profits and the surtax payable.

Allows the Assessing Officer to make a summary provisional assessment of chargeable profits and surtax before a regular assessment. The assessee is notified and has an opportunity to raise objections. No appeal lies against a provisional assessment, and amounts paid towards it are adjusted against the regular assessment.

Introduces provisions for the advance payment of surtax during the financial year. It defines 'chargeable amount' and 'current chargeable amount' and outlines how the advance surtax is to be computed and paid in instalments.

important_rules: Companies whose chargeable profits exceed the statutory deduction must furnish a return of their chargeable profits by September 30th of the assessment year.
The Assessing Officer can issue a notice to any company to furnish a return of chargeable profits within thirty days.
An assessee can file a revised return at any time before assessment if they discover any omission or wrong statement in their original return.
The Assessing Officer may require an assessee to produce accounts, documents, or evidence for the purpose of assessment.
Provisional assessment can be made by the Assessing Officer before regular assessment, with notice and an opportunity for the assessee to object.
Advance surtax is payable in instalments during the financial year.
The rate of surtax is specified in the Third Schedule.

penalties: Section 9: Penalties for various offenses related to the Act.
Section 9A: Penalty for false estimate of, or failure to pay, advance surtax.
Section 20: Penalty for failure to deliver returns, etc.
Section 21: Penalty for false statements.
Section 22: Penalty for abetment of false returns, etc.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Income-tax authorities specified in section 116 of the Income-tax Act, and the Central Board of Direct Taxes (Board).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, provisional assessment, imposition of penalties for non-compliance or false statements, and other provisions outlined in the Act, largely leveraging the framework of the Income-tax Act.

rights: Right to object to a proposed provisional assessment.
Right to appeal against certain orders (as specified in sections 11 and 12).
Right to have mistakes rectified (Section 13).
Right to be heard (Section 10).
duties: Duty to furnish a return of chargeable profits.
Duty to produce accounts, documents, or evidence when required by the Assessing Officer.
Duty to pay surtax as per the assessment.
Duty to pay advance surtax in instalments.
Duty to follow orders, instructions, and directions issued by the Board (unless they interfere with appellate discretion).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act, including timely filing of returns and payment of taxes.
Obligation to provide accurate information in returns and statements.

key_procedures: Furnishing a return of chargeable profits by companies whose profits exceed the statutory deduction.
Issuance of notice by the Assessing Officer to a company to furnish a return.
Filing of revised returns before assessment.
Assessment process by the Assessing Officer, including obtaining evidence and issuing an order.
Provisional assessment process, including notice, objections, and finalization.
Advance surtax payment process with specific instalment dates.
Appeals process to the Commissioner (Appeals) and the Appellate Tribunal.
Rectification of mistakes in orders.
administration: The administration of the Act is carried out by the income-tax authorities as specified in section 116 of the Income-tax Act, under the overall supervision and direction of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (Board).
important_notes: The Act was in force for assessment years commencing on or after April 1, 1964, but before April 1, 1988.
The Act relies heavily on the definitions, procedures, and authorities established by the Income-tax Act, 1961.
There is no right of appeal against a provisional assessment made under section 7.

title: THE SEAMEN’S PROVIDENT FUND ACT, 1966
purpose: To provide for the institution of a provident fund for seamen.
scope: Applies to every seaman and their employer, as defined by the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, with specific exclusions for welfare officers, nurses, musicians, pilots, and deck barbers. The geographical scope is India, implied by the reference to the Republic of India and the Central Government.

key_definitions.agreement_with_the_crew: The agreement referred to in section 100 or section 114 of the Merchant Shipping Act.
key_definitions.board: The Board of Trustees of the Seamen’s Provident Fund constituted under section 5.
key_definitions.continuous_discharge_certificate: The certificate referred to in section 99 of the Merchant Shipping Act.
key_definitions.contribution: A contribution payable in respect of a member under the Scheme.
key_definitions.employer: In relation to a seaman, means the owner of the ship on which the seaman is employed or engaged, or the agent of such owner or the master of the ship.
key_definitions.fund: The Seamen’s Provident Fund established under the Scheme.
key_definitions.master: Has the meaning assigned in the Merchant Shipping Act.
key_definitions.ship: Has the meaning assigned in the Merchant Shipping Act.
key_definitions.member: A seaman who is in possession of a continuous discharge certificate and who is admitted as a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.scheme: The Seamen’s Provident Fund Scheme framed under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.seaman: A person employed or engaged as a member of the crew of a ship under the Merchant Shipping Act, excluding welfare officers, nurses, musicians, pilots, or deck barbers.
key_definitions.service: The period of employment of a seaman under the agreement with the crew, including any period in respect of which wages are paid or are payable.
key_definitions.wages: The basic wages for the time being payable to a seaman under the agreement with the crew, including remuneration for holidays or leave periods and any increase in wages, but excluding overtime allowance.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act and specifies its application to every seaman and their employer, unless otherwise expressly provided.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'agreement with the crew', 'Board', 'contribution', 'employer', 'Fund', 'member', 'Scheme', 'seaman', 'service', and 'wages'.

This section empowers the Government to frame a Seamen’s Provident Fund Scheme, establish a Fund, and outlines the provisions that the Scheme may cover, including prospective or retrospective effect and its precedence over other laws.

This section states that the Fund vests in and is administered by the Board of Trustees. It also specifies that the moneys in the Fund are to be applied for meeting the expenses of the Board and for carrying out the purposes of the Act. Moneys are to be deposited in an approved bank or invested in approved securities.

This section details the constitution of the Board of Trustees, including its corporate status, head office, composition (Chairman, government officials, employer representatives, seaman representatives), and how its terms and administration of the Fund will be managed.

This section outlines the mandatory contributions to the Fund by both employers and seamen, specifying the rates applicable for different periods and the method of recovery of employee contributions by the employer. It also includes provisions for sums towards administration costs and rounding of fractional amounts.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of moneys due from employers
main_sections.description: This section details how amounts due from employers, including contributions and damages, can be recovered by the Government in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue.

This section protects the amount standing to the credit of a member in the Fund from assignment, charge, or attachment by any court decree or order for debts or liabilities incurred by the member. It also specifies that amounts payable to a nominee upon the member's death are free from the deceased's or nominee's prior debts.
This section lists the penalties for various offenses under the Act, such as failure to deduct or pay contributions, or contravening provisions of the Scheme.

important_rules: Every employer must contribute to the Fund for each seaman employed by them, at specified rates (currently 10% or higher as per Scheme).
Every seaman must also contribute an amount equal to the employer's contribution.
The employer is responsible for paying both contributions and is entitled to recover the employee's contribution by deduction from wages.
Employers must pay sums towards the cost of administering the Fund as specified in the Scheme.
Contributions must be paid on or before a date specified by the Government, which cannot be earlier than sixty days after the commencement of the Scheme.

penalties: Failure to deduct or pay contributions: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
Failure to pay contributions within the stipulated time: Forfeiture of damages recoverable under section 18.
Contravention of the Scheme: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Seamen's Provident Fund Commissioner or any Deputy Seamen's Provident Fund Commissioner, and the Government for recovery of arrears.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through determination of amounts due by the Commissioner, recovery by the Government as arrears of land revenue, and prosecution for penalties.

rights: Seamen have the right to a provident fund benefit under the Scheme.
Seamen's contributions are protected against attachment and are free from prior debts upon death if payable to a nominee.
duties: Employers have a duty to contribute to the Fund for each seaman employed.
Employers have a duty to deduct and remit employee contributions.
Employers have a duty to pay sums towards the cost of administering the Fund.
Seamen have a duty to contribute to the Fund.
obligations: Employers are obligated to ensure that contributions are paid on time.
The Board of Trustees has an obligation to administer the Fund and carry out the purposes of the Act.

key_procedures: Framing of the Seamen's Provident Fund Scheme by the Government via notification.
Constitution of the Board of Trustees by the Government via notification.
Determination of amounts due from employers by the Seamen's Provident Fund Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner, involving inquiry and a fair opportunity for the employer to be heard.
Recovery of arrears due from employers as land revenue.
Appointment of the Seamen's Provident Fund Commissioner and Deputy Commissioners, with consultation of the Union Public Service Commission for certain appointments.
administration: The Board of Trustees of the Seamen's Provident Fund administers the Fund, with the Seamen's Provident Fund Commissioner as its chief executive officer. The Government also plays a role in framing the scheme, appointing the Board, and recovering dues.
important_notes: The Scheme can have retrospective effect.
The Fund is deemed to be a recognized Provident Fund under the Income-tax Act, 1961.
The Act includes provisions for delegation of powers by the Government and the Board.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Any amount due to the Fund in respect of contributions shall have priority over other debts if the employer is insolvent or being wound up.

title: The Delhi High Court Act, 1966
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a High Court for the Union territory of Delhi, for the extension of the jurisdiction of that High Court to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the Union territory of Delhi and, with extended jurisdiction, to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh. It governs the establishment, jurisdiction, powers, and procedures of the High Court of Delhi.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date appointed under section 3 for the establishment of the High Court of Delhi.
key_definitions.notified_order: An order notified in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for different provisions, with Section 17 coming into force on a date appointed by the Central Government and other provisions coming into force at once.
Defines 'appointed day' and 'notified order' for the purposes of the Act.

Provides for the establishment of the High Court of Delhi from a date appointed by the Central Government, specifies its principal seat, and allows for sittings at other places with Presidential approval.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries and allowances of Judges to be expenditure charged on Consolidated Fund of India
main_sections.description: States that the salaries and allowances of the Judges of the High Court of Delhi are an expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

main_sections.section_title: Exceptions and modifications subject to which the provisions of Chapter V of Part VI of the Constitution apply to the High Court of Delhi
main_sections.description: Outlines specific exceptions and modifications to Chapter V of Part VI of the Constitution as they apply to the High Court of Delhi, particularly concerning appointments, references to the Governor, and certain articles relating to administrative costs and jurisdiction over Union territories.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of High Court of Delhi
main_sections.description: Confers upon the High Court of Delhi all original, appellate, and other jurisdiction exercisable by the High Court of Punjab in respect of the Union territory of Delhi, and also grants it ordinary original civil jurisdiction in suits exceeding a specified value.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of proceedings from the High Court of Punjab to the High Court of Delhi
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of proceedings from the High Court of Punjab to the High Court of Delhi, specifying which proceedings are to be transferred and retaining jurisdiction for certain matters with the High Court of Punjab.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the jurisdiction of the High Court of Delhi
main_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court of Delhi to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh from a prescribed date, and abolishes the Court of the Judicial Commissioner for Himachal Pradesh.

important_rules: The High Court of Delhi shall have all such original, appellate, and other jurisdiction as was exercisable by the High Court of Punjab in respect of the Union territory of Delhi immediately before the appointed day.
The High Court of Delhi shall have ordinary original civil jurisdiction in every suit whose value exceeds rupees two crore.
Legal practitioners enrolled in the High Court of Punjab immediately before the appointed day shall be recognised as advocates or attorneys in the High Court of Delhi.
Proceedings pending in the High Court of Punjab that ought to be heard and decided by the High Court of Delhi shall be transferred.

The High Court of Punjab shall retain jurisdiction to entertain, hear, or dispose of appeals, applications for leave to appeal, applications for review, and other proceedings concerning orders passed by it before the appointed day, unless transferred.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the High Court of Delhi itself, through its powers to make rules and orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of existing laws with necessary modifications, appointment of Judges, and the High Court's own rule-making powers regarding practice and procedure.

rights: Right to appear or act in proceedings transferred to the High Court of Delhi for persons who were advocates or attorneys in the High Court of Punjab and authorized for those proceedings.
The High Court of Delhi has the right to approve, admit, enrol, remove, and suspend legal practitioners.
duties: Legal practitioners have a duty to adhere to the rules and orders made by the High Court of Delhi regarding their practice.
The High Court of Delhi has a duty to ensure that its jurisdiction and procedures are exercised in accordance with the Act and applicable constitutional provisions.
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to appoint dates for commencement of certain provisions and to issue notifications.
The President has the obligation to appoint the Chief Justice and other Judges of the High Court of Delhi.

key_procedures: Appointment of the Chief Justice and Judges of the High Court of Delhi by the President after consultation.
Transfer of pending proceedings from the High Court of Punjab to the High Court of Delhi, certified by the Chief Justice of the Punjab High Court.
Application of existing laws related to practice and procedure of the High Court of Punjab to the High Court of Delhi, with necessary modifications.
Transfer of pending proceedings in subordinate courts in Delhi related to civil suits under section 5(2) to the High Court of Delhi.
administration: The Central Government, the President, and the High Court of Delhi (through its Chief Justice and Judges).
important_notes: Section 19 has been repealed.
The Schedule has been repealed.
Substitutions and insertions have been made by later Acts, e.g., Act 37 of 1969 and Act 23 of 2015.

title: THE PUNJAB REORGANISATION ACT, 1966
purpose: To provide for the reorganisation of the existing State of Punjab and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the reorganization of the State of Punjab, forming new states and Union territories, and matters related to representation in legislatures, High Court, finances, assets and liabilities, corporations, projects, services, and legal provisions.

key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator of a Union territory appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.appointed day: The 1st day of November, 1966.
key_definitions.assembly constituency, council constitue: Have the same meanings as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950).
key_definitions.Delimitation Commission: The Delimitation Commission constituted under section 3 of the Delimitation Commission Act, 1962 (61 of 1962).
key_definitions.existing State of Punjab: The State of Punjab as existing immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having, immediately before the appointed day, the force of law in the whole or in any part of the existing State of Punjab.
key_definitions.notified order: An order published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.population ratio: In relation to the States of Haryana and Punjab and the Union, means the ratio of 37.38 to 54.84 to 7.78.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.sitting member: In relation to either House of Parliament or of the Legislature of the existing State of Punjab, means a person who immediately before the appointed day is a member of that House.
key_definitions.State of Punjab: The State with the same name, comprising the territories referred to in sub-section (1) of section 6.
key_definitions.successor State: In relation to the existing State of Punjab, means the State of Punjab or Haryana, and includes also the Union in relation to the Union territory of Chandigarh and the transferred territory.
key_definitions.transferred territory: The territory which on the appointed day is transferred from the existing State of Punjab to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh.
key_definitions.territorial division reference: Any reference to a district, tahsil or other territorial division of the existing State of Punjab shall be construed as a reference to the area comprised within that territorial division on the 1st day of July, 1966.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, appointed day, article, constituencies, Delimitation Commission, existing State of Punjab, law, notified order, population ratio, prescribed, sitting member, State of Punjab, successor State, transferred territory, treasury, and territorial divisions.

Establishes the formation of a new State named Haryana comprising specific districts and tahsils of the existing State of Punjab, effective from the appointed day. It also specifies the formation of Jind and Ambala districts within Haryana.

main_sections.section_title: Formation of Union territory of Chandigarh
main_sections.description: Provides for the formation of a new Union territory named Chandigarh, comprising specified territories from the Kharar tahsil of Ambala district, effective from the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of territory from Punjab to Himachal Pradesh
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of specific territories from the existing State of Punjab to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, including districts, tahsils, and kanungo circles, effective from the appointed day. It also specifies how these territories will be included in existing districts and tahsils of Himachal Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: State of Punjab and territorial divisions thereof
main_sections.description: Defines the territories that will constitute the new State of Punjab after the reorganisation, excluding those transferred to Haryana, Chandigarh, and Himachal Pradesh. It also describes the formation of Rupar district, Mullanpur kanungo circle, and Anandpur Sahib tahsil within the new State of Punjab.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution to include the new State of Haryana and the Union territory of Chandigarh, and to modify the description of the State of Punjab and the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh.

States that the provisions of Part II do not affect the power of the Government of Punjab or Haryana, or the Administrator of Himachal Pradesh, to alter the name, area, or boundaries of any district or territorial division after the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution, likely concerning the allocation of seats in the Council of States.
Deals with the allocation of sitting members of the Council of States.
Concerns the process of filling up vacancies in the Council of States.
Makes provisions regarding the existing House of the People.
Deals with provisions related to the Legislative Assemblies of the newly formed states.
Provides for the amendment of Delimitation Orders.
Concerns the allocation of sitting members to the Legislative Assemblies.

main_sections.section_title: Duration of Legislative Assembly of Haryana
main_sections.description: Specifies the duration of the Legislative Assembly of Haryana.

main_sections.section_title: Duration of Legislative Assemblies of Punjab and Himachal Pradesh
main_sections.description: Specifies the duration of the Legislative Assemblies of Punjab and Himachal Pradesh.
Deals with the Speakers and Deputy Speakers of the Legislative Assemblies.
Concerns the rules of procedure for the Legislative Assemblies.
Makes provisions regarding the Legislative Council of Punjab.
Deals with council constituencies.

main_sections.section_title: Provision as to certain sitting members
main_sections.description: Makes provisions concerning certain sitting members of the Legislative Council.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seats in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Concerns the allocation of seats in the House of the People.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seats in the Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Deals with the allocation of seats in the Legislative Assembly.
Provides for the delimitation of constituencies.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of article 371 of the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends article 371 of the Constitution.
Amends orders pertaining to Scheduled Castes.
Amends orders pertaining to Scheduled Tribes.

main_sections.section_title: Common High Court for Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh
main_sections.description: Establishes a common High Court for Punjab, Haryana, and Chandigarh.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of the common High Court
main_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction of the common High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision relating to Bar Council and Advocates
main_sections.description: Makes special provisions related to the Bar Council and Advocates.

main_sections.section_title: Practice and procedure in common High Court
main_sections.description: Specifies the practice and procedure to be followed in the common High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Custody of seal of common High Court
main_sections.description: Concerns the custody of the seal of the common High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Form of writs and other processes
main_sections.description: Prescribes the form of writs and other processes issued by the common High Court.
Defines the powers of the Judges of the common High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Principal seat and other places of sitting of the common High Court
main_sections.description: Specifies the principal seat and other places where the common High Court may sit.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure as to appeals to Supreme Court
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for appeals to the Supreme Court from the common High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of the Court of Judicial Commissioner for Himachal Pradesh
main_sections.description: Provides for the extension of jurisdiction of the Court of Judicial Commissioner for Himachal Pradesh.
Deals with the transfer of pending proceedings before the reorganisation.
Provides for the interpretation of the Act.
Contains saving clauses for the provisions of Part IV.

main_sections.section_title: Authorisation of expenditure of the State of Haryana
main_sections.description: Authorises expenditure for the State of Haryana.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in transferred territory
main_sections.description: Concerns the appropriation of moneys for expenditure in territories transferred to Himachal Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Reports relating to the accounts of the existing State of Punjab
main_sections.description: Deals with reports related to the accounts of the existing State of Punjab.

main_sections.section_title: Allowances and privileges of Governor of Haryana
main_sections.description: Specifies the allowances and privileges of the Governor of Haryana.
Provides for the distribution of revenues between the successor states and the Union.
Specifies the application of Part VI concerning the apportionment of assets and liabilities.
Deals with the apportionment of land and goods.
Concerns the apportionment of treasury and bank balances.
Provides for the apportionment of arrears of taxes.

main_sections.section_title: Right to recover loans and advances
main_sections.description: Deals with the right to recover loans and advances.

main_sections.section_title: Investments and credits in certain funds
main_sections.description: Concerns the apportionment of investments and credits in certain funds.

main_sections.section_title: Assets and liabilities of State undertakings
main_sections.description: Provides for the apportionment of assets and liabilities of State undertakings.
Deals with the apportionment of public debt.

main_sections.section_title: Refund of taxes collected in excess
main_sections.description: Concerns the refund of taxes collected in excess.
Provides for the apportionment of deposits and other similar items.
Deals with the apportionment of provident fund.
Concerns the apportionment of pensions.
Provides for the apportionment of liabilities arising from contracts.

main_sections.section_title: Liability in respect of actionable wrong
main_sections.description: Deals with liability in respect of actionable wrongs.
Concerns liability as a guarantor.
Provides for the apportionment of items in suspense.
Includes a residuary provision for apportionment of assets and liabilities.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of assets or liabilities by agreement
main_sections.description: Allows for the apportionment of assets or liabilities by mutual agreement.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to order allocation or adjustment in certain cases
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to order allocation or adjustment of assets and liabilities in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Certain expenditure to be charged on the Consolidated Fund
main_sections.description: Specifies certain expenditures that are to be charged on the Consolidated Fund.
Makes provisions concerning certain corporations.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of arrangements in regard to generation and supply of electric power and supply of water
main_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of arrangements for the generation and supply of electric power and water.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions as to Punjab State Financial Corporation
main_sections.description: Deals with provisions related to the Punjab State Financial Corporation.
Amends Act 6 of 1942.
Makes provisions concerning co-operative banks.

main_sections.section_title: General provisions as to statutory corporations
main_sections.description: Provides general provisions applicable to statutory corporations.
Deals with provisions concerning certain companies.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary provisions as to continuance of certain existing road transport permits
main_sections.description: Includes temporary provisions for the continuance of certain existing road transport permits.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision relating to retrenchment compensation in certain cases
main_sections.description: Makes special provisions regarding retrenchment compensation in specific cases.
Provides a special provision concerning income-tax.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of facilities in certain State institutions
main_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of facilities in certain State institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Rights and liabilities in regard to Bhakra-Nangal and Beas Projects
main_sections.description: Addresses the rights and liabilities related to the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas Projects.
Makes provisions concerning the Bhakra Management Board.
Deals with the construction of the Beas Project.
Makes provisions regarding All-India Services.
Concerns provisions related to other services.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions as to continuance of officers in the same post
main_sections.description: Specifies provisions for the continuance of officers in their existing posts.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions as to State Public Service Commissions
main_sections.description: Deals with provisions concerning State Public Service Commissions.
Amends Act 37 of 1956.

main_sections.section_title: Power to extend enactments to Chandigarh
main_sections.description: Grants the power to extend enactments to Chandigarh.
Defines the territorial extent of laws after reorganisation.
Grants the power to adapt existing laws.
Provides the power to construe laws in light of the reorganisation.

main_sections.section_title: Power to name authorities, etc., for exercising statutory functions
main_sections.description: Grants the power to name authorities for exercising statutory functions.
Deals with legal proceedings that may arise from the reorganisation.
Concerns the transfer of pending legal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Right of pleaders to practise in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies the right of pleaders to practise in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of provisions of the Act inconsistent with other laws
main_sections.description: Clarifies the effect of the Act's provisions if they are inconsistent with other laws.
Grants the power to remove difficulties encountered in giving effect to the Act.
Empowers the government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text for general enforcement, but various authorities are implied through sections on High Court, Government powers, and Central Government directions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied through legal proceedings, High Court jurisdiction, and powers of various governmental bodies.

rights: Right of pleaders to practise in certain cases (Section 94).
obligations: Obligation for successor states and the Union to take over assets and liabilities (Part VI).

key_procedures: Formation of new states and Union territories (Sections 3, 4, 5).
Amendment of Constitutional Schedules (Section 7).
Allocation of seats in legislatures and delimitation of constituencies (Part III).
Establishment and functioning of a common High Court (Part IV).
Authorisation and distribution of expenditure and revenues (Part V).
Apportionment of assets and liabilities (Part VI).
Continuance and adjustment of provisions for corporations and projects (Part VII, Part VIII).
Provisions concerning services and public service commissions (Part IX).
Adaptation and construction of laws (Part X).
administration: The Central Government plays a significant role in directing and ordering matters related to reorganisation, and various state governments and the administrator of Union territories are involved in their respective jurisdictions. The rules made under the Act would be prescribed.
important_notes: The 'appointed day' is crucial for the effective date of reorganisation: November 1, 1966.
The Act provides for the transfer of territories, formation of new states (Haryana), a new Union territory (Chandigarh), and addition of territories to Himachal Pradesh.
Detailed provisions cover representation in Parliament and State Legislatures, the functioning of a common High Court, financial arrangements, and the division of assets and liabilities.
Special provisions are made for projects like Bhakra-Nangal and Beas, services, and legal matters arising from the reorganisation.
The Act includes powers for the Central Government to remove difficulties and issue directions to facilitate the reorganisation process.
Laws can be adapted and construed to give effect to the Act's provisions.

title: THE POST-GRADUATE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH, CHANDIGARH ACT, 1966
purpose: To declare the institution known as the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, and its operations. Geographically, it is centered in the Union territory of Chandigarh. The subject matter scope covers the establishment, governance, functions, and academic activities of the institute.

key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Institute referred to in section 16.
key_definitions.Governing Body: The Governing Body of the Institute.
key_definitions.Institute: The institution known as the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, incorporated under this Act.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Institute.
key_definitions.regulation: A regulation made by the Institute.
key_definitions.rule: A rule made by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, as an institution of national importance due to its objectives.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Fund', 'Governing Body', 'Institute', 'member', 'regulation', and 'rule'.

Constitutes the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract.

Specifies the members of the Institute, including ex-officio members (Vice-Chancellor of Punjab University, Director-General of Health Services, Director of the Institute), representatives from the Central Government (Finance, Education, Health), a non-medical scientist, representatives of medical faculties, and members of Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of, and vacancies among, members
main_sections.description: Details the tenure of office for members (typically five years), conditions for termination of office for elected members, continuity of ex-officio members, filling of casual vacancies, continuation in office until successors are appointed, eligibility for re-nomination/re-election, resignation process, and the procedure for filling vacancies.
Establishes the office of the President of the Institute, who is nominated by the Central Government from among the members (excluding the Director), and outlines their powers and functions.
States that the President and other members shall receive allowances from the Institute as prescribed by rules.
Specifies rules for the first meeting of the Institute (time, place, procedure appointed by Central Government) and subsequent meetings (time, place, procedure as prescribed by regulations).

main_sections.section_title: Governing Body and other Committees of Institute
main_sections.description: Establishes a Governing Body as the executive committee of the Institute, its constitution as per regulations, the President of the Institute as its Chairman, and outlines its powers, functions, and procedures. It also allows for the constitution of standing and ad hoc committees for specific purposes.

Details the appointment and designation of the chief executive officer as the Director, their term of office, and their role as Secretary. It also covers the appointment of other officers and employees and their salaries, allowances, and conditions of service as determined by the Central Government and regulations.

Outlines the primary objectives of the Institute: developing high standards of undergraduate and post-graduate medical education, bringing together advanced educational facilities, and achieving self-sufficiency in post-graduate medical education for specialists and teachers.

Details the functions the Institute may perform to achieve its objectives, including providing teaching in modern medicine and allied sciences, facilitating research, teaching humanities, conducting experiments in medical education methods, prescribing courses, establishing and maintaining medical colleges, hospitals, dental colleges, nursing colleges, health organizations, and other training institutions, training teachers, granting degrees, holding examinations, appointing staff, receiving grants and donations, managing property, demanding fees, constructing staff quarters, and borrowing money.
Deals with the vesting of the properties of the Institute.

important_rules: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.
Members of the Institute generally have a term of five years, with specific provisions for ex-officio members and those filling casual vacancies.
The President of the Institute is nominated by the Central Government.
The Governing Body acts as the executive committee of the Institute.
The Director is the chief executive officer of the Institute and acts as Secretary to the Institute and the Governing Body.
The Institute may receive grants from the Government and gifts, donations, benefactions, bequests, and transfers of property.
The Institute may borrow money with the prior approval of the Central Government.
The Institute shall have a fund from which all its expenses shall be met.
