The Institute shall prepare an annual budget and maintain accounts which are subject to audit.

rights: The Institute has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The Institute has the right to contract and sue and be sued in its corporate name.
Members have the right to receive allowances as prescribed by rules.
The Institute has the right to demand and receive fees and other charges.
The Institute has the right to borrow money with Central Government approval.
The Director has the right to exercise powers and functions delegated by the Institute, President, or Governing Body.
Existing employees have their services transferred to the Institute.
Members elected to the Institute may have their term end upon assuming certain high public offices.
duties: The Institute has the duty to develop patterns of teaching in medical education to demonstrate high standards.
The Institute has the duty to provide facilities for training personnel in health activities.
The Institute has the duty to attain self-sufficiency in post-graduate medical education.
The Institute has the duty to provide for undergraduate and post-graduate teaching in medicine and allied sciences.
The Institute has the duty to provide facilities for research.
The Institute has the duty to train teachers for medical colleges in India.
The Institute has the duty to hold examinations and grant degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.
The Institute has the duty to institute professorships, readerships, lectureships, and other posts.
The Institute has the duty to construct and allot quarters for its staff.
The Institute has the duty to manage its fund and prepare budgets.
The Institute has the duty to maintain accounts and submit an annual report.
The Institute is subject to the control of the Central Government.
The Institute must comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
obligations: The Institute is obligated to act in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
The Institute is obligated to comply with the directions of the Central Government.
The Institute is obligated to ensure that the number of non-members on the Governing Body does not exceed one-third of its total membership.
The Institute must obtain prior approval of the Central Government for borrowing money.

key_procedures: Appointment of the first Director by the Central Government.
The Institute's first meeting is convened by the Central Government, with subsequent meetings governed by regulations.
The Governing Body is constituted by the Institute as per regulations.
Filling of vacancies among members is done as prescribed by rules.
The Institute appoints staff subject to Central Government rules and regulations.
The Institute establishes and maintains various medical and health-related institutions as specified.
The Institute receives grants, gifts, and donations and manages them.
The Institute prepares its budget and accounts, which are subject to audit.
administration: Central Government (overall control, rule-making, appointments, approval of borrowing)
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2001 (Act 18 of 2001) and 2007 (Act 42 of 2007) affecting provisions like the Director's term of office.
The commencement date of the Act was April 1, 1967.

title: The Seeds Act, 1966
purpose: To provide for regulating the quality of certain seeds for sale, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It regulates the sale of seeds of notified kinds or varieties, setting standards for germination, purity, and labeling. It also covers the import and export of seeds.

key_definitions.certification agency: Means the certification agency established under section 8 or recognised under section 18.
key_definitions.container: Means a box, bottle, g asket, tin, barrel, case, receptacle, sack, bag, wrapper or other thing in which any article or thing is placed or packed.
key_definitions.export: Means taking out of India to a place outside India.
key_definitions.import: Means bringing into India from a place outside India.
key_definitions.kind: Means one or more related species or sub-species of crop plants each individually or collectively known by one common name such as cabbage, maize, paddy and wheat.
key_definitions.notified kind or variety: In relation to any seed, means any kind or variety thereof notified under section 5.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.seed: Means any of the following classes of seeds used for sowing or planting: seed of food crops including edible oil seeds and seeds of fruits and vegetables; cotton seeds; seeds of cattle fodder; jute seeds. It includes seedlings, and tubers, bulbs, rhizomes, roots, cuttings, all types of grafts and other vegetatively propagated material, of food crops or cattle fodder.
key_definitions.variety: Means a sub-division of a kind identifiable by growth, yield, plant, fruit, seed, or other characteristic.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Seeds Act, 1966, its extent to the whole of India, and the provisions for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including agriculture, certification agency, container, export, import, kind, notified kind or variety, prescribed, seed, variety, Central Seed Laboratory, State Seed Laboratory, Seed Analyst, Seed Inspector, and State Government.

Establishes the Central Seed Committee to advise the Central and State Governments on matters arising from the administration of the Act. It details the composition, tenure of members, and the committee's power to make bye-laws and appoint sub-committees.

main_sections.section_title: Central Seed Laboratory and State Seed Laboratory
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish or declare a Central Seed Laboratory and the State Government to establish or declare State Seed Laboratories for carrying out functions related to seed analysis.

main_sections.section_title: Power to notify kinds or varieties of seeds
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power, after consulting the Committee, to notify specific kinds or varieties of seeds by notification in the Official Gazette, making them subject to regulation under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to specify minimum limits of germination and purity, etc.
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to specify minimum germination and purity limits for notified seeds, and to prescribe the mark or label that such seeds should bear.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation or sale of seeds of notified kinds or varieties
main_sections.description: Prohibits the business of selling, keeping for sale, or supplying seeds of notified kinds or varieties unless they are identifiable by kind/variety, conform to specified germination and purity limits, bear the correct mark or label, and meet other prescribed requirements.
Allows the State or Central Government (in consultation with the State Government) to establish a certification agency for a State to carry out functions under the Act.

Establishes the Central Seed Certification Board to advise the Central and State Governments on certification matters and to coordinate certification agencies. It details the Board's composition and tenure.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of certificate by certification agency
main_sections.description: Details the process for applying for and obtaining a certificate from a certification agency for seeds of notified kinds or varieties, subject to prescribed standards.
Outlines the grounds and procedure for revoking a certificate granted by a certification agency, including obtaining it by misrepresentation or failing to comply with conditions.
Provides a mechanism for appeal against a decision of a certification agency regarding the grant or revocation of a certificate.
Empowers the State Government to appoint Seed Analysts with prescribed qualifications and defines their jurisdiction.
Empowers the State Government to appoint Seed Inspectors with prescribed qualifications.
Details the powers vested in a Seed Inspector, such as inspecting seeds, taking samples, and seizing them.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on export and import of seeds of notified kinds or varieties
main_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on the export and import of seeds of notified kinds or varieties.
Specifies the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall sell, keep for sale, offer to sell, barter, or otherwise supply any seed of a notified kind or variety unless it is identifiable, conforms to prescribed germination and purity standards, and its container bears the correct mark or label.
Seeds of notified kinds or varieties must meet the minimum germination and purity limits specified by the Central Government.
Containers of seeds of notified kinds or varieties must bear a prescribed mark or label with correct particulars.

penalties: Penalty for contravening provisions of the Act (Section 19). Specific details of penalties are not fully provided in the excerpt, but they are mentioned.
Forfeiture of property (Section 20).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Seed Inspectors (appointed by the State Government) have powers to inspect, sample, and seize seeds. Certification agencies are responsible for granting and revoking certificates. The Central and State Governments are involved in establishing committees and laboratories.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection and sampling by Seed Inspectors, analysis by Seed Analysts, certification by certification agencies, and enforcement of penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to appeal against a decision of a certification agency (Section 11).
Right to an opportunity of being heard before a certificate is revoked (Section 10).
duties: Duty to comply with prescribed standards for germination and purity.
Duty to ensure seeds are identifiable by kind or variety.
Duty to correctly mark and label seed containers as prescribed.
Duty to comply with other requirements prescribed under the Act.
Duty of persons selling seeds to apply for certification if they desire it.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a seed certificate: An application is made to the certification agency, which may conduct an inquiry and grant a certificate if the seed conforms to prescribed standards (Section 9).
Procedure for appeal against a certification agency's decision: An aggrieved person can prefer an appeal within thirty days to a specified authority (Section 11).

Procedure for revoking a certificate: The certification agency must provide the holder an opportunity to show cause before revoking a certificate obtained by misrepresentation or for non-compliance (Section 10).
administration: The Central Government and State Governments are involved in the administration. The Central Seed Committee advises the governments. The Central Seed Certification Board coordinates agencies. Seed Analysts and Seed Inspectors are appointed by the State Government.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act and for different States or areas thereof (Section 1(3)).
The Board or any Committee's proceedings are not invalid due to a vacancy or defect in constitution (Section 8C).

title: THE PASSPORTS ACT, 1967
purpose: To provide for the issue of passports and travel documents, to regulate the departure from India of citizens of India and other persons and for matters incidental or ancillary thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies also to citizens of India who are outside India. It governs the issuance and regulation of passports and travel documents for departure from India.

key_definitions.departure: Departure from India by water, land or air.
key_definitions.passport: A passport issued or deemed to have been issued under this Act.
key_definitions.passport authority: An officer or authority empowered under rules made under this Act to issue passports or travel documents and includes the Central Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.travel document: A travel document issued or deemed to have been issued under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Passports Act, 1967, and specifies its territorial and personal extent.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'departure', 'passport', 'passport authority', 'prescribed', and 'travel document'.

main_sections.section_title: Passport or travel document for departure from India
main_sections.description: Mandates that no person shall depart or attempt to depart from India without a valid passport or travel document. It also includes an explanation for what constitutes a 'passport' and 'travel document' in this context, including those issued by foreign governments under certain conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Classes of passports and travel documents
main_sections.description: Specifies the classes of passports (ordinary, official, diplomatic) and travel documents (emergency certificate, certificate of identity, etc.) that may be issued. It also grants the Central Government the power to prescribe classes of persons to whom these documents may be issued.

main_sections.section_title: Applications for passports, travel documents, etc, and orders thereon
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for applying for passports and travel documents, including fees and required particulars. It details the passport authority's powers to issue, endorse, or refuse applications, and requires written reasons for refusal unless against public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Refusal of passports, travel documents, etc
main_sections.description: Specifies the grounds on which a passport authority shall refuse to make an endorsement for visiting a foreign country or to issue a passport or travel document. These grounds relate to activities prejudicial to India's sovereignty, security, friendly relations, or public interest, as well as criminal convictions and pending proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Duration of passports and travel documents
main_sections.description: States that passports and travel documents have a prescribed duration unless revoked earlier, with provisions for different periods for different classes or categories. It also allows for issuance for shorter periods if desired by the applicant or deemed necessary by the passport authority.
Deals with the extension of passports issued for a shorter period than the prescribed duration, subject to certain conditions and passport authority's determination.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions and forms of passports and travel documents
main_sections.description: Prescribes the conditions and forms for issuing or renewing passports and travel documents, allowing for different conditions and forms for different classes or categories. The passport authority can also impose additional conditions with Central Government approval.

main_sections.section_title: Variation, impounding and revocation of passports and travel documents
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the passport authority to vary or cancel endorsements or conditions of passports/travel documents, and to impound or revoke them under various circumstances, including wrongful possession, suppression of information, interests of India, conviction for certain offenses, pending proceedings, contravention of conditions, failure to comply with notices, and court orders.

important_rules: No person shall depart or attempt to depart from India without a valid passport or travel document (Section 3).
Applications for passports and travel documents must be made to the passport authority with prescribed fees and particulars (Section 5).
Passport authority shall refuse applications on specific grounds related to national interest, security, and public order (Section 6).
Passports and travel documents have a prescribed duration but can be issued for shorter periods and extended (Sections 7 & 8).
The passport authority can vary, impound, or revoke passports and travel documents under specified conditions (Section 10).

penalties: Section 12 details offences and penalties related to contravention of the Act or rules made thereunder.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Passport authority and the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of arrest, search, seizure, refusal, variation, impounding, and revocation of passports and travel documents, as well as through rules and penalties prescribed under the Act.

rights: Right to apply for a passport or travel document.
Right to receive reasons for refusal of passport or travel document, unless against public interest (Section 5(3)).
Right to appeal against orders of the passport authority (Section 11).
duties: Duty to possess a valid passport or travel document for departure from India (Section 3).
Duty to comply with notices from the passport authority regarding delivery of passports or travel documents (Section 10(1)).
Duty to comply with prescribed conditions and forms of passports and travel documents (Section 9).
obligations: Obligation to pay prescribed fees for passport and travel document applications (Section 5).
Obligation to provide truthful information in applications (Section 10(3)(b)).

key_procedures: Application for a passport or travel document, including specified foreign countries and payment of fees.
Inquiry by the passport authority regarding the application.
Order by the passport authority to issue, endorse, or refuse the passport/travel document.
Notification of reasons for refusal if applicable.
Appeal process against passport authority's orders.
Procedure for variation, impounding, or revocation of passports/travel documents.
administration: Central Government and Passport Authority (empowered officers/authorities).
important_notes: The Act is in addition to certain other enactments (Section 23).
The Central Government has the power to make rules and exempt certain persons or documents from the provisions of the Act (Sections 22 & 24).

title: THE BIHAR AND UTTAR PRADESH (ALTERATION OF BOUNDARIES) ACT, 1968
purpose: To provide for the alteration of boundaries of the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, specifically concerning the alteration of their boundaries and related matters. It defines 'transferred territories' in relation to both states. The Act has territorial scope concerning specific districts and rivers (Ganga and Ghaghra).

key_definitions.appointed day: The day which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
key_definitions.assembly constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.council constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.parliamentary constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.deep stream: In relation to the river Ganga or the river Ghaghra, it means the deep stream thereof as verified and agreed upon by the State Governments of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, or as determined by an authority specified by the Central Government in default of agreement.
key_definitions.fixed boundary: The boundary line demarcated under the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 3 in relation to the river Ganga or the river Ghaghra.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or in any part of the State of Bihar or Uttar Pradesh.
key_definitions.notified order: An order published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.sitting member: In relation to either House of Parliament or of the Legislature of a State, means a person who immediately before the appointed day is a member of that House.
key_definitions.transferred territories: Refers to the territories transferred by this Act from one state to the other (either from Bihar to Uttar Pradesh or vice versa).

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1968.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', constituencies, 'deep stream', 'fixed boundary', 'law', 'notified order', 'prescribed', 'sitting member', and 'transferred territories'.

Details the transfer of territories between Bihar and Uttar Pradesh as from the appointed day. It specifies which parts of Ballia and Shahabad districts are transferred to Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, respectively, based on the fixed boundary and deep stream of the rivers Ganga and Ghaghra. It also outlines the process for demarcating the fixed boundary, the powers of the demarcating authority, and the preparation of maps.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Specifies the amendments to be made to the First Schedule of the Constitution concerning the territories of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh following the boundary alteration.
Provides for the construction of references in delimitation orders to states and administrative units, ensuring they include or exclude the transferred territories as appropriate.
Deals with sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures whose constituencies' extent has been altered by the Act, deeming them elected to the altered constituencies.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, High Court at Patna
main_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court at Patna to territories transferred from Uttar Pradesh to Bihar and restricts the jurisdiction of the High Court at Allahabad in those territories. It also provides for the transfer of pending proceedings from Allahabad to Patna and specifies jurisdiction for appeals and reviews related to orders passed before the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, High Court at Allahabad
main_sections.description: This section is analogous to Section 7 but deals with the extension of jurisdiction of the High Court at Allahabad to territories transferred from Bihar to Uttar Pradesh and the transfer of relevant proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Right to appear in any proceedings transferred under section 7 or section 8
main_sections.description: Ensures the right of pleaders to appear in proceedings transferred under sections 7 and 8.
Provides for the interpretation of any law in relation to the transferred territories.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in transferred territories under existing appropriation Acts
main_sections.description: Deals with the appropriation of moneys for expenditure in the transferred territories under existing appropriation Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Reports relating to accounts of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
main_sections.description: Concerns reports relating to the accounts of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh after the boundary alteration.
Provides for the apportionment of land and goods between the two states.
Deals with the apportionment of arrears of taxes.

main_sections.section_title: Right to recover loans and advances
main_sections.description: Concerns the right to recover loans and advances.

main_sections.section_title: Refund of taxes collected in excess
main_sections.description: Provides for the refund of taxes collected in excess.
Deals with the apportionment of deposits.
Provides for the apportionment of contracts.

main_sections.section_title: Liability in respect of actionable wrong
main_sections.description: Concerns liability in respect of actionable wrongs.

main_sections.section_title: Liability as guarantor of co-operative societies
main_sections.description: Deals with liability as a guarantor of co-operative societies.
Addresses items in suspense and their apportionment.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of assets or liabilities by agreement
main_sections.description: Allows for the apportionment of assets or liabilities by agreement between the state governments.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to order allocation or adjustment in certain cases
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to order allocation or adjustment of assets and liabilities in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Expenditure to be charged on the Consolidated Fund
main_sections.description: Specifies that certain expenditures are to be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

main_sections.section_title: State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards
main_sections.description: Deals with the status of State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards in relation to the transferred territories.
Determines the territorial extent of laws in the transferred territories.
Grants power to adapt existing laws to the altered boundaries.
Provides power to construe laws in the context of the altered state boundaries.
Covers legal proceedings that may be affected by the alteration of boundaries.
Provides for the transfer of pending proceedings in courts and tribunals.

main_sections.section_title: Right of pleaders to practise in certain courts
main_sections.description: Ensures the right of pleaders to practise in courts after the transfer of territories.
Deals with the construction of boundary pillars and other related infrastructure.

main_sections.section_title: Validity of demarcation done before commencement of Act
main_sections.description: Confirms the validity of any demarcation done before the commencement of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of provisions inconsistent with other laws
main_sections.description: States the effect of provisions of this Act that may be inconsistent with other laws.
Grants the Central Government power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: As from the appointed day, territories from Ballia district (UP) lying between the fixed boundary and the deep stream of Ghaghra/Ganga are added to Bihar, ceasing to be part of UP. Similarly, territories from Saran district (Bihar) lying between the fixed boundary and the deep stream of Ghaghra/Ganga are added to Uttar Pradesh, ceasing to be part of Bihar.

Rule 2: The fixed boundary in relation to the Ganga and Ghaghra rivers shall be demarcated by an authority appointed by the Central Government, generally in conformity with the Schedule, with powers to rationalize the alignment, ensure stability of pillars, and avoid splitting existing abadis.
Rule 3: The demarcating authority's decision on interpretation of boundary descriptions and determination of pillar locations and responsibilities for construction/maintenance shall be final.
Rule 4: The demarcating authority shall prepare a map of transferred territories showing the deep stream, fixed boundary, and village details, to be published by the Central Government.
Rule 5: State Governments shall provide for the administration of transferred territories by including them in appropriate administrative units via official gazette order.
Rule 6: Delimitation orders shall be construed to include or exclude transferred territories and administrative units within them.
Rule 7: Sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures in altered constituencies shall be deemed elected to the altered constituencies.

Rule 8: The jurisdiction of the High Court at Patna extends to territories transferred from UP to Bihar, and the High Court at Allahabad loses jurisdiction in those territories. Proceedings can be transferred based on cause of action.
Rule 9: The High Court at Allahabad retains jurisdiction for appeals and reviews of its own orders passed before the appointed day, unless transferred to Patna.
Rule 10: Provisions for apportionment of assets and liabilities, including land, goods, taxes, loans, deposits, contracts, and liabilities, are established.
Rule 11: Existing laws are to be adapted and construed to apply to the altered territories.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, demarcating authority appointed by Central Government, Chief Justices of High Courts, State Governments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders, demarcations, transfers of proceedings, adaptation of laws, and administrative orders. Powers are vested in the Central Government and designated authorities.

rights: Right to appear in proceedings transferred under sections 7 or 8 for pleaders.
Right to recover loans and advances.
Right of pleaders to practise in certain courts.
duties: Duty of State Governments to be responsible for construction and maintenance of boundary pillars as decided by the demarcating authority.
Duty of State Governments to provide for the administration of transferred territories.
obligations: Obligation to ensure provisions for the administration of transferred territories.
Obligation to comply with orders issued by the Central Government for allocation or adjustment of assets/liabilities.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Demarcation of the fixed boundary by an appointed authority, involving surveying and marking the line between high banks of rivers, with final decisions on interpretation and pillar placement.
Procedure 2: Preparation and publication of maps of transferred territories by the demarcating authority and Central Government.
Procedure 3: Issuance of orders by State Governments for the administration of transferred territories.
Procedure 4: Transfer of proceedings from one High Court to another as certified by the Chief Justice.
Procedure 5: Adaptation and construction of existing laws to apply to the new territorial arrangements.
administration: Central Government (for appointments, notifications, rules, and orders), State Governments of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (for administration of transferred territories and boundary pillar maintenance).
important_notes: The 'appointed day' is to be notified by the Central Government.
The demarcation of the fixed boundary allows for rationalization and considerations for stability and avoiding splitting of existing settlements ('abadis').
The Act provides for continuity of representation in legislatures despite boundary changes.
Specific provisions are made for the continuation and transfer of legal and High Court proceedings.

title: THE ENEMY PROPERTY ACT, 1968
purpose: To provide for the continued vesting of enemy property vested in the Custodian of Enemy Property for India under the Defence of India Rules, 1962 and the Defence of India Rules, 1971, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Extends to the whole of India and applies to all citizens of India outside India and to branches and agencies outside India of companies or bodies corporate registered or incorporated in India.

key_definitions.custodian: The Custodian of Enemy Property for India appointed or deemed to have been appointed under section 3, including Deputy Custodian and Assistant Custodian.
key_definitions.enemy_enemy_subject_enemy_firm: A person or country who or which was an enemy, an enemy subject (including legal heirs and successors, irrespective of nationality or changes in nationality), or an enemy firm (including succeeding firms, irrespective of partners' nationality or changes in nationality), as defined under the Defence of India Act, 1962, or the Defence of India Act, 1971. It excludes citizens of India, except for those who are legal heirs and successors of an 'enemy', 'enemy subject', or 'enemy firm' that has ceased to be an enemy due to death, extinction, winding up of business, or change of nationality, or where the successor is a citizen of India or a non-enemy country. Explanation 1 clarifies that 'does not include a citizen of India' excludes citizens who are legal heirs and successors under specific conditions. Explanation 2 clarifies that rights of such legal heirs and successors under other laws are not affected, provided they are not inconsistent with this Act.
key_definitions.enemy_property: Any property belonging to or held or managed on behalf of an enemy, an enemy subject, or an enemy firm. It continues to be regarded as enemy property even if an individual enemy subject dies within or outside India, or if the enemy, enemy subject, or enemy firm has ceased to be an enemy due to death, extinction, winding up of business, or change of nationality, or if the legal heir and successor is a citizen of India or a citizen of a country which is not an enemy. It includes all rights, titles, interests, and benefits arising out of such property.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent and application, and the date of commencement.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Custodian', 'enemy', 'enemy subject', 'enemy firm', 'enemy property', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Custodian of Enemy Property for India and Deputy Custodian, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Custodian of Enemy Property for India, and Deputy and Assistant Custodians for specified local areas. Persons appointed under the Defence of India Rules, 1962 or 1971, are deemed to have been appointed under this section.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Inspectors of Enemy Property.
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to appoint Inspectors of Enemy Property for ensuring compliance with the Act. Inspectors appointed under the Defence of India Rules, 1962 or 1971, are deemed appointed under this section.

main_sections.section_title: Property vested in the Custodian of Enemy Property for India under the Defence of India Rules, 1962, and the Defence of India Rules, 1971 to continue to vest in Custodian.
main_sections.description: States that enemy property vested in the Custodian under the Defence of India Rules, 1962, and the Defence of India Rules, 1971, will continue to vest in the Custodian under this Act, even after the expiration of those Rules. It also specifies that enemy property vested in the Custodian continues to vest even if the enemy, enemy subject, or enemy firm ceases to be an enemy due to various reasons, or if legal heirs are Indian citizens or citizens of non-enemy countries.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition to transfer any property vested in Custodian by an enemy, enemy subject or enemy firm.
main_sections.description: Prohibits any enemy, enemy subject, or enemy firm from transferring property vested in the Custodian. Any such transfer is void. It also addresses the voiding of previous transfers of enemy property that were declared void by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Payment to Custodian of money otherwise payable to an enemy, enemy subject or enemy firm.
main_sections.description: Mandates that any sums payable to an enemy, enemy subject, or enemy firm (e.g., dividends, interest, profits) must be paid to the Custodian, unless otherwise directed by the Central Government. Provisions are made for payments in foreign currency to be made in Indian rupees at the official exchange rate.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Custodian in respect of enemy property vested in him.
main_sections.description: Grants the Custodian powers to take necessary measures to preserve enemy property vested in him until it is disposed of according to the Act.

important_rules: Enemy property vested in the Custodian continues to remain vested, even if the original owner ceases to be an enemy due to death, extinction, winding up of business, or change of nationality, or if the legal heir is an Indian citizen or a citizen of a non-enemy country.
No enemy, enemy subject, or enemy firm has any right to transfer property vested in the Custodian; any such transfer is void.
Any sums payable to an enemy, enemy subject, or enemy firm must be paid to the Custodian.
The Custodian may take necessary measures to preserve enemy property vested in him.

penalties: Section 20 specifies penalties for contravention of the Act or rules made thereunder.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Custodian of Enemy Property for India, Deputy Custodians, Assistant Custodians, and Inspectors of Enemy Property, appointed by the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appointment of Custodian, Deputy Custodians, Assistant Custodians, and Inspectors; vesting of enemy property; prohibition of transfers; mandatory payments to Custodian; power to summon persons and call for documents; protection for compliance with orders; and penalties for offenses.

rights: Legal heirs and successors (not inconsistent with the Act) of an 'enemy' or 'enemy subject' or 'enemy firm' may have rights conferred upon them under other laws.
Citizens of India are generally excluded from the definition of 'enemy', 'enemy subject', or 'enemy firm', except where they are legal heirs and successors under specific circumstances.
Protection for complying with orders of the Custodian.
duties: Persons by whom sums would have been payable to an enemy, enemy subject or enemy firm are obligated to pay such sums to the Custodian.
The Custodian has a duty to preserve enemy property vested in him.
obligations: Any property vested in the Custodian by an enemy, enemy subject, or enemy firm cannot be transferred by them.
Sums payable to an enemy, enemy subject, or enemy firm must be paid to the Custodian.
The Custodian must deal with money and property in such manner as the Central Government may direct.

key_procedures: Appointment of Custodian, Deputy Custodians, and Assistant Custodians by the Central Government.
Appointment of Inspectors of Enemy Property by the Central Government.
Vesting of enemy property in the Custodian.
Transfer of property vested in the Custodian is prohibited and void.
Payment of sums otherwise payable to an enemy to the Custodian.
Power of the Custodian to take measures for preserving enemy property.
Power of the Custodian to summon persons and call for documents.
Returns as to enemy property are to be made to the Custodian.
Appeals to the High Court against certain orders.
Making of rules by the Central Government.
administration: Central Government, through the Custodian of Enemy Property for India, Deputy Custodians, Assistant Custodians, and Inspectors of Enemy Property.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment and validation of previous provisions related to enemy property.
The Act aims to ensure that enemy property remains vested in the Custodian.
The law of succession or any custom or usage does not apply to enemy property under this Act.
Jurisdiction of civil courts is excluded in certain matters.

title: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971
purpose: To provide for the termination of certain pregnancies by registered medical practitioners and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, recognizing the importance of safe, affordable, and accessible abortion services.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It governs the circumstances under which pregnancies can be terminated by registered medical practitioners.

key_definitions.guardian: A person having the care of the person of a minor or a mentally ill person.
key_definitions.medical_board: A Medical Board constituted under sub-section (2C) of section 3 of the Act, consisting of a Gynaecologist, a Paediatrician, a Radiologist or Sonologist, and other members as notified.
key_definitions.mentally_ill_person: A person who is in need of treatment by reason of any mental disorder other than mental retardation.
key_definitions.minor: A person who, under the provisions of the Indian Majority Act, 1875, is to be deemed not to have attained his majority.
key_definitions.registered_medical_practitioner: A medical practitioner with a recognized medical qualification, whose name is entered in a State Medical Register, and who has prescribed experience or training in gynaecology and obstetrics.
key_definitions.termination_of_pregnancy: A procedure to terminate a pregnancy by using medical or surgical methods.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and its commencement date as appointed by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including guardian, Medical Board, mentally ill person, minor, registered medical practitioner, and termination of pregnancy.

main_sections.section_title: When pregnancies may be terminated by registered medical practitioners
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a registered medical practitioner can terminate a pregnancy, subject to certain gestational limits (up to 20 weeks generally, and up to 24 weeks for specific categories of women). It also addresses risks to the woman's life or health, or substantial risk of serious fetal abnormality, and the role of Medical Boards for certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Place where pregnancy may be terminated
main_sections.description: Specifies that pregnancy termination can only be performed in a government hospital or a place approved by the Government or a District Level Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Sections 3 and 4 when not to apply
main_sections.description: Details exceptions, such as when immediate termination is necessary to save the life of the pregnant woman. It also specifies penalties for performing or facilitating abortions at unapproved places or by unregistered practitioners.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of privacy of a woman
main_sections.description: Ensures the privacy of a woman whose pregnancy has been terminated, prohibiting disclosure of her particulars except to authorized persons.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, including rules regarding the experience/training of registered medical practitioners, categories of women, norms for medical practitioners, and powers/functions of the Medical Board.
Empowers the State Government to make regulations regarding the certification of opinions for termination, intimation of terminations, and prohibition of disclosure of information.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits or legal proceedings for any damage caused or likely to be caused by anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act by a registered medical practitioner.

important_rules: Rule: Pregnancies up to 20 weeks can be terminated by a registered medical practitioner if they are of the opinion, formed in good faith, that the continuance of the pregnancy would involve a risk to the life of the pregnant woman or of grave injury to her physical or mental health, or if there is a substantial risk of serious physical or mental abnormality in the child.

Rule: Pregnancies exceeding 20 weeks but not exceeding 24 weeks can be terminated for specific categories of women as prescribed by rules, and requires the opinion of at least two registered medical practitioners.
Rule: Termination of pregnancy must be performed in a hospital established or maintained by Government, or a place approved by Government or a District Level Committee.

Rule: The termination of pregnancy for a minor or a mentally ill person requires the written consent of her guardian, in addition to the consent of the pregnant woman if she is above 18 years and not mentally ill.
Rule: The privacy of a woman whose pregnancy has been terminated must be protected, with disclosure of her particulars restricted to authorized persons.

penalties: Termination of pregnancy by a person who is not a registered medical practitioner: rigorous imprisonment of not less than two years but may extend to seven years.
Terminating any pregnancy in a place other than that mentioned in section 4: rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than two years but may extend to seven years.
Owner of a place not approved under section 4: rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than two years but may extend to seven years.
Contravention of privacy provisions (section 5A): imprisonment which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
Wilful contravention or failure to comply with regulations made under sub-section (1) of section 7: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act is enforced through the legal framework of India, involving registered medical practitioners, government authorities, and the judiciary. State Governments are responsible for constituting Medical Boards and District Level Committees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves adherence to the conditions for termination, proper venue for procedures, consent requirements, and reporting mechanisms established by rules and regulations. Penalties are prescribed for violations.

rights: Right of a pregnant woman to seek termination of pregnancy under specified conditions.
Right to privacy regarding termination of pregnancy.
Right to safe and legal abortion services.
duties: Duty of registered medical practitioners to act in accordance with the provisions of the Act and to form opinions in good faith.
Duty of the Central and State Governments to make rules and regulations to facilitate the implementation of the Act.
Duty of owners of approved places to maintain them according to the Act's requirements.
obligations: Obligation to obtain consent for termination (from the woman or her guardian if applicable).
Obligation to perform termination at an approved place.
Obligation to maintain privacy of the woman's information.

key_procedures: Procedure for Termination up to 20 Weeks: A registered medical practitioner, in good faith, forms an opinion that continuance of pregnancy poses a risk to the woman's life/health or a substantial risk of fetal abnormality. Consent of the pregnant woman (or guardian if applicable) is required.

Procedure for Termination between 20-24 Weeks: For specific categories of women, at least two registered medical practitioners must form the opinion (as above). Consent of the pregnant woman (or guardian if applicable) is required.

Procedure for Substantial Foetal Abnormalities: Termination may be necessitated by diagnosis of substantial foetal abnormalities by a Medical Board, where gestational limits may not apply. Medical Boards are constituted by State Governments.
Procedure for Approval of Places: Government or District Level Committees approve places for pregnancy termination, ensuring they meet specified standards.
Procedure for Privacy Protection: Registered medical practitioners must not reveal patient particulars except to authorized persons.
Procedure for Rule Making: Central Government frames rules through notification, subject to parliamentary approval.
Procedure for Regulation Making: State Governments frame regulations, which are laid before the State Legislature.
administration: The Act is administered by the Central Government and State Governments. The Central Government makes rules, and State Governments are responsible for constituting Medical Boards and District Level Committees, and making regulations.
important_notes: The Act supersedes provisions of the Indian Penal Code regarding termination of pregnancy, making it legal under specific conditions.
Explanations to Section 3 clarify that anguish caused by pregnancy due to failure of contraception or rape is presumed to constitute grave injury to mental health.
The Act was amended in 2002 and 2021 to increase gestational limits and introduce Medical Boards for certain conditions.
The Act explicitly provides protection to registered medical practitioners acting in good faith.

title: THE DELHI SCHOOL EDUCATION ACT, 1973
purpose: To provide for better organization and development of school education in the Union territory of Delhi and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi. Covers establishment, recognition, management, aid, property, service conditions of employees, admissions, fees, and taking over management of schools. It distinguishes between recognised schools, aided schools, and unaided minority schools.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator of the Union territory of Delhi appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.Advisory Board: The Board referred to in section 22 of the Act.
key_definitions.aid: Any aid granted to a recognised school by the Central Government, Administrator, a local authority or any other authority designated by the Central Government, Administrator or a local authority.
key_definitions.aided school: A recognised private school which is receiving aid in the form of maintenance grant from the Central Government, Administrator or a local authority or any other designated authority.
key_definitions.appropriate authority: Depends on the type of school, referring to the Central Government, Administrator, Delhi Administration, Municipal Corporation of Delhi, or any other authorized officer.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of Education, Delhi, and includes any other officer authorized by him.
key_definitions.employee: A teacher and includes every other employee working in a recognised school.
key_definitions.existing employee: An employee of an existing school employed immediately before the commencement of the Act, or for at least twelve months preceding September 2, 1972.
key_definitions.existing school: A recognised private school in existence at the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Head of school: The principal academic officer of a recognised school.
key_definitions.local authority: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi, New Delhi Municipal Committee, or Delhi Cantonment Board.
key_definitions.manager: The person entrusted with the management of a school's affairs.
key_definitions.managing committee: The body of individuals entrusted with the management of a recognised private school.
key_definitions.minority school: A school established and administered by a minority having the right to do so under article 30(1) of the Constitution.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.private school: A school not run by the Central Government, Administrator, a local authority or any other designated or sponsored authority.
key_definitions.public examination: An examination conducted by recognized Boards like CBSE, CISCE, or newly established boards recognized by the Administrator.
key_definitions.recognised school: A school recognized by the appropriate authority.
key_definitions.school: Includes pre-primary, primary, middle, and higher secondary schools, and institutions imparting education or training below degree level, but excludes technical education institutions.
key_definitions.school property: All movable and immovable property belonging to or in possession of the school, including land, buildings, playgrounds, hostels, furniture, books, equipment, cash, investments, and bank balances.
key_definitions.teacher: Includes the Head of a school.
key_definitions.unaided minority school: A recognised minority school that does not receive any aid.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Delhi School Education Act, 1973, its extent to the Union territory of Delhi, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Administrator.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, aid, aided school, appropriate authority, Delhi, Director, employee, school, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Administrator to regulate education in schools
main_sections.description: Empowers the Administrator to regulate education in all schools in Delhi, establish/maintain schools, and states that new schools or classes must comply with the Act for recognition.

Details the process for recognition of private schools by the appropriate authority, including conditions for recognition (financial stability, scheme of management, accommodation, courses, qualified teachers, facilities), appeal against refusal, withdrawal of recognition, and deems existing schools as recognized.

Requires the managing committee of every recognised school to make a scheme of management with the approval of the appropriate authority, with variations for unaided private schools. Excludes minority schools from prior approval requirements.

Describes the provision of aid to recognised private schools by the Central Government through the Administrator, subject to prescribed conditions. It also covers conditions for continuance of aid, stopping/reducing aid, use of aid funds, and ineligibility for aid for schools whose management is taken over or for unrecognised schools.
Mandates aided schools to furnish property statements to the appropriate authority.

main_sections.section_title: Terms and conditions of service of employees of recognised private schools
main_sections.description: This chapter (Chapter IV) deals with the terms and conditions of service for employees in recognised private schools, subject to a Code of Conduct and prescribed salaries. It also establishes a Tribunal for disputes.

main_sections.section_title: Chapter not to apply to unaided minority school
main_sections.description: Specifies that Chapter IV (Terms and Conditions of Service of Employees) does not apply to unaided minority schools.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prescribe minimum qualifications for recruitment
main_sections.description: This chapter (Chapter V) pertains to unaided minority schools, allowing for the prescription of minimum qualifications for recruitment.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prescribe Code of Conduct
main_sections.description: This chapter (Chapter V) allows for the prescription of a Code of Conduct for unaided minority schools.
This chapter (Chapter V) deals with the contract of service for unaided minority schools.
This chapter (Chapter VI) concerns admission to recognised schools.
This chapter (Chapter VI) addresses fees and other charges in schools.
This chapter (Chapter VI) deals with the establishment and management of a School Fund.
This chapter (Chapter VI) pertains to affiliations of schools.

main_sections.section_title: Taking over the management of schools
main_sections.description: This chapter (Chapter VII) provides for the taking over of the management of schools under certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Section 20 not to apply to minority schools
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the power to take over management under Section 20 does not apply to minority schools.
This chapter (Chapter VIII) provides for the establishment and functions of the Delhi Schools Education Advisory Board.
This chapter (Chapter VIII) allows for the delegation of powers conferred by the Act.
This chapter (Chapter VIII) provides for the inspection of schools.
This chapter (Chapter VIII) bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in certain matters.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: This chapter (Chapter VIII) provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
This chapter (Chapter VIII) deals with the liability of a manager to punishment.
This chapter (Chapter VIII) empowers the appropriate authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
This chapter (Chapter VIII) grants the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: A new school or higher class cannot be established or opened without complying with the provisions of the Act and its rules. Such schools will not be recognized (Section 3(3)).
Recognition for a private school requires adequate funds, a duly approved scheme of management, suitable accommodation, approved courses, qualified teachers, and prescribed facilities (Section 4(1)).
Decisions on recognition applications must be communicated within four months. Appeals against refusal are possible within thirty days to a prescribed authority (Section 4(2), 4(3)).
Recognition can be withdrawn if obtained by fraud or misrepresentation, or if the school fails to comply with conditions after recognition (Section 4(4)).
Every recognised school must have a scheme of management approved by the appropriate authority, unless it's an unaided minority school (Section 5(1)).
Aid to recognised private schools is subject to prescribed conditions. Aid can be stopped or reduced for violations. Aid meant for salaries cannot be used for other purposes (Section 6).
No aid shall be given to a school whose management has been taken over (Section 6(5)).
Employees of recognised private schools are to be governed by a Code of Conduct and receive prescribed salaries (Section 9, 10).
A Tribunal is established to adjudicate disputes concerning employees of recognised private schools (Section 11).

penalties: Liability of manager to punishment for contravention of provisions or rules (Section 27).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Administrator, appropriate authority, Director, and prescribed authorities appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers of the Administrator to regulate education, grant or withdraw recognition, prescribe schemes of management, provide aid, and appoint authorities for appeals and dispute resolution. Enforcement also includes rules made under the Act and provisions for inspection and penalties.

rights: Minority groups have the right to establish and administer schools under Article 30(1) of the Constitution, with some provisions of the Act not applying to them (Section 5(1) proviso, Section 21).
Aggrieved persons have the right to appeal against the refusal of recognition (Section 4(3)).
Schools have the right to be heard before recognition is withdrawn (Section 4(4)).
Employees have rights regarding terms and conditions of service, salaries, and may have recourse to a Tribunal (Chapter IV, Section 11).
duties: Schools must comply with the Act and rules to be recognized and to receive aid.
Managing committees must make a scheme of management for recognised schools.
Aided schools must furnish property statements to the appropriate authority.
Schools must provide prescribed facilities for physical education, library, laboratory, etc.
Schools must ensure adequate funds for financial stability and employee salaries.
obligations: The Administrator has the obligation to regulate education in schools and can establish or permit the establishment of schools.
The appropriate authority has the obligation to entertain and consider recognition applications within a specified period.
The management of aided schools has an obligation to furnish financial and property statements.
Employees must adhere to a Code of Conduct.
Funds provided as aid for salaries, allowances, and provident fund must not be used for any other purpose.

key_procedures: Procedure for recognition of a private school, including application, scrutiny by the appropriate authority, decision communication, and appeal process (Section 4).
Procedure for making, varying, or modifying a scheme of management for a recognised school (Section 5).
Procedure for the grant, continuance, stoppage, or reduction of aid to recognised schools (Section 6).
Procedure for taking over the management of a school (Section 20).
Procedure for the establishment of the Delhi Schools Education Advisory Board (Section 22).
Procedure for inspection of schools (Section 24).
administration: The Administrator of the Union territory of Delhi, with the support of the appropriate authorities, Director of Education, and the Delhi Schools Education Advisory Board.
important_notes: Different commencement dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act (Section 1(3)).
The provisions of Chapter IV (Terms and Conditions of Service of Employees) do not apply to unaided minority schools (Section 12).
The power to take over management under Section 20 does not apply to minority schools (Section 21).
Jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in certain matters related to the Act (Section 25).

title: THE NORTH-EASTERN HILL UNIVERSITY ACT, 1973
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University for the hill areas of the North-Eastern region, to develop the intellectual, academic, and cultural background of the people of these areas, and to improve their social and economic conditions and welfare.
scope: The Act extends to the State of Meghalaya and the State of Arunachal Pradesh. The University's jurisdiction is also limited to these geographical areas. It applies to educational institutions, students, academic staff, employees, and the administration of the North-Eastern Hill University.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.University: The North-Eastern Hill University.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent (State of Meghalaya and State of Arunachal Pradesh), and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'University', 'College', 'Court', 'Department', 'employee', 'Executive Council', 'Hall', 'Institution', 'North-Eastern region', 'Principal', 'recognised teachers', 'School', 'Statutes', 'Ordinances', 'Regulations', and 'teachers of the University'.

Establishes the North-Eastern Hill University, specifies its headquarters at Shillong and the possibility of campuses in Meghalaya and other places within its jurisdiction. It also constitutes the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objectives of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, and paying special attention to the improvement of social and economic conditions, welfare, and intellectual, academic, and cultural advancement of the people in the hill areas of the North-Eastern region.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, improving economic conditions in the region, granting diplomas/degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, conferring honorary degrees, establishing teaching posts, recognizing teachers, creating administrative posts, collaborating with other universities, establishing campuses and centers, awarding fellowships/scholarships, establishing and maintaining colleges/institutions/halls, admitting other institutions to its privileges, declaring autonomous institutions, determining admission standards, levying fees, supervising student residences, making provisions for women students, regulating discipline, promoting employee welfare, acquiring and disposing of property, and borrowing money with government approval.

Defines the geographical jurisdiction of the University as extending to the State of Meghalaya and the State of Arunachal Pradesh. It also specifies conditions for affiliation of colleges and institutions, ensuring they do not associate with other universities without proper approval.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Declares that the University is open to all individuals regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, and prohibits any religious test for admission or holding office. It allows for special provisions for weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University. The Visitor has the right to inspect and inquire into the University's administration, finances, examinations, teaching, and other work, with provisions for notice and representation from the University or management.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University, through its authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council) and officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, etc.). The Visitor (President of India) also has oversight and inquiry powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations made under the Act. Enforcement of discipline among students and employees is also a key mechanism. The Visitor's inspection and inquiry powers serve as a form of external enforcement.

rights: Right to education and advancement of knowledge.
Right of students and employees to welfare and proper conditions of service.
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases.
Right of the University to grant degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.
Right of the Visitor to inspect and inquire.
duties: Duty of the University to disseminate and advance knowledge.
Duty to pay special attention to the improvement of social and economic conditions and welfare of the people of the North-Eastern region.
Duty to provide instructional and research facilities.
Duty to uphold openness to all classes, castes, and creeds, with provisions for weaker sections.
Duty of the University and management to cooperate with the Visitor during inspections and inquiries.
obligations: Obligation for affiliated colleges/institutions to accept the Statutes and Ordinances.
Obligation for institutions admitted to privileges to cease association with other Universities.
Obligation for the University to maintain its corporate status and common seal.
Obligation to act in accordance with the provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.

key_procedures: Procedure for the establishment of the University and its corporate body.
Procedures for the making of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Procedures for the appointment of University officers and members of authorities.
Procedures for conducting inspections and inquiries by the Visitor, including notice and representation.
Procedures for the grant and withdrawal of degrees, diplomas, and certificates.
Procedures for admitting and withdrawing privileges of colleges and institutions.
Procedures for regulating discipline among students and employees.
administration: The administration of the Act is primarily carried out by the North-Eastern Hill University through its various authorities and officers. The Central Government appoints the commencement date and can be involved in approving borrowing powers. The President of India acts as the Visitor, providing oversight.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1989 and 2000 to reflect changes in the territorial composition of the North-Eastern region (e.g., inclusion/exclusion of states/union territories).
The University is mandated to pay special attention to the welfare and advancement of the people of the hill areas of the North-Eastern region.
Provisions are made for special admission of students from weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The Visitor has significant powers to inspect and inquire into the functioning of the University and its affiliated institutions.

title: THE UNIVERSITY OF HYDERABAD ACT, 1974
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching University in the State of Andhra Pradesh and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the University of Hyderabad, established in the State of Andhra Pradesh. Its jurisdiction extends to the whole of the State of Andhra Pradesh. The University is open to all persons regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, with special provisions for weaker sections, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes. It also covers institutions affiliated with or associated with other universities in Andhra Pradesh, requiring prior approval for recognition.

key_definitions.academic_council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic_staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the University of Hyderabad Act, 1974 and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including academic council, academic staff, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, College, Court, Department, employee, Executive Council, Hall, Institution, Principal, recognised institution, recognised teachers, School, Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, teachers of the University, and University.

Establishes the University of Hyderabad in Andhra Pradesh with headquarters at Hyderabad and the power to establish campuses elsewhere. Constitutes a body corporate by the name 'University of Hyderabad' and grants it perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objects of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, making special provisions for integrated courses in humanities and science, and promoting inter-disciplinary studies and research.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction, research, granting degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, conferring honorary degrees, establishing and appointing academic and administrative posts, recognizing institutions, cooperating with other bodies, establishing campuses, instituting scholarships, managing property, and borrowing money with government approval.

Defines the geographical jurisdiction of the University as the entire State of Andhra Pradesh and restricts the recognition of institutions affiliated with other universities in the state without prior government and university approval.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Ensures the University is open to all sexes, races, creeds, castes, and classes, prohibiting any religious tests for admission or holding office. It allows for special provisions for weaker sections, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor, granting powers to inspect and inquire into the University's affairs, including buildings, equipment, examinations, teaching, administration, and finances. The Visitor can issue directions based on these inspections, with provisions for the University to make representations and for annulment of non-conforming proceedings.
Appoints the Governor of the State of Andhra Pradesh as the Chief Rector.
Lists the officers of the University: Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Deans of Schools, Registrar, Finance Officer, and other officers as declared by the Statutes.
Specifies that the Chancellor is appointed by the Visitor, is the Head of the University, and presides at degree-conferring convocations.

States that the Vice-Chancellor is appointed by the Visitor, is the principal executive and academic officer, exercises general supervision and control, and gives effect to decisions of University authorities. Grants emergency powers to the Vice-Chancellor with reporting and appeal provisions.
Mentions Pro-Vice-Chancellors, implying their role in assisting the Vice-Chancellor or holding specific responsibilities as defined by Statutes.
Refers to the Deans of Schools, indicating their administrative and academic roles within their respective Schools.
Identifies the Registrar as an officer of the University, whose specific duties would be detailed in Statutes or Ordinances.
Identifies the Finance Officer as an officer of the University, responsible for financial matters.
Allows for the creation of other officers as declared by the Statutes.
Introduces the concept of University authorities, which are further detailed in subsequent sections.
Refers to 'The Court' as an authority of the University, likely a deliberative or advisory body.
Identifies 'The Executive Council' as a key authority, likely responsible for the day-to-day administration and implementation of University policies.
Identifies 'The Academic Council' as an authority, responsible for academic matters such as curriculum, teaching, and examinations.
Allows for the establishment of other authorities as needed.
Establishes a Planning Board, likely responsible for strategic development and future planning of the University.
Introduces Statutes as the primary rule-making instrument of the University, which govern its constitution and powers.
Details the process by which Statutes are made, likely involving the Executive Council and the Court, and requiring Visitor's assent.
Defines Ordinances as rules made under the Statutes, dealing with more detailed administrative and academic matters.
Defines Regulations as rules made under the Ordinances, typically concerning day-to-day academic and student-related matters.
Requires the University to prepare an annual report on its activities, to be submitted to the Visitor and the Central Government.
Mandates the preparation of annual accounts, which are to be audited and presented to the Visitor and the Central Government.
Governs the conditions of service for University employees, likely detailed further in Statutes or Ordinances.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students
main_sections.description: Establishes procedures for appeals and arbitration in disciplinary matters involving students.
Confirms the right to appeal for individuals within the University, possibly related to disciplinary actions or administrative decisions.
Deals with the establishment and management of provident and pension funds for employees.

main_sections.section_title: Disputes as to constitution of University authorities and bodies
main_sections.description: Provides a mechanism for resolving disputes concerning the constitution of University authorities and bodies.
Allows for the formation of committees by University authorities for specific purposes.
Lays down procedures for filling casual vacancies in University authorities and bodies.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings of University authorities or bodies not invalidated by vacancies
main_sections.description: States that the validity of proceedings of University authorities or bodies is not affected by vacancies within them.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to individuals acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of proof of University record
main_sections.description: Specifies how University records can be proven in legal or administrative proceedings.
Grants the Central Government the power to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Includes provisions to manage the transition from the pre-Act situation to the functioning of the established University.

important_rules: The University shall be open to persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste, or class, and shall not impose any test of religious belief or profession for admission, office, graduation, or privilege, except for special provisions for weaker sections, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes.
The University must provide instructional and research facilities and promote inter-disciplinary studies.
The University can only recognize institutions affiliated with other universities in Andhra Pradesh with prior approval from the State Government and the concerned University.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Visitor (President of India) has significant oversight and enforcement powers, including the ability to annul proceedings and issue directions. The Vice-Chancellor exercises executive control. The Central Government has powers to remove difficulties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, issuing directions by the Visitor, and by the executive and administrative functions of the Vice-Chancellor and other officers, guided by Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.

rights: Right to education and research opportunities at the University.
Right to be free from religious tests for admission or holding office.
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases (for students) and potentially for employees.
Right to representation during inspections/inquiries by the Visitor.
duties: Duty of the University to disseminate and advance knowledge.
Duty of the University to provide instructional and research facilities.
Duty of the University to be open to all classes, castes, and creeds.
Duty of the Vice-Chancellor to exercise supervision and control and give effect to decisions of authorities.
Duty of the Executive Council to comply with directions from the Visitor.
obligations: Obligation of the University to prepare and submit annual reports and audited accounts.
Obligation of the University to follow procedures for making Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Obligation to obtain prior approval for recognition of certain affiliated institutions.

key_procedures: Establishment of the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and common seal.
Appointment of the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor by the Visitor.
Process of making Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Procedure for inspections and inquiries by the Visitor, including the University's right to make representations.
Procedure for preparing and submitting annual reports and accounts.
administration: The University is administered by its Officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, etc.) and Authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, etc.), with oversight from the Visitor and the Chief Rector. The Central Government has powers related to commencement and removing difficulties.
important_notes: The Act allows for special provisions for the admission of students from weaker sections, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes.
The Visitor's powers are extensive, including the ability to annul proceedings not conforming to the Act, Statutes, or Ordinances, after providing an opportunity for the University to show cause.
The Act outlines the structure and functioning of a university, covering academic, administrative, and financial aspects.

title: THE INTEREST-TAX ACT, 1974
purpose: To impose a special tax on interest in certain cases.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to credit institutions and scheduled banks.

key_definitions.assessee: A person by whom interest-tax or any other sum of money is payable under this Act, and includes persons subject to assessment proceedings or deemed to be in default.
