key_definitions.assessment year: The period of twelve months commencing on the 1st day of April, every year.
key_definitions.board: The Central Board of Direct Taxes constituted under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963 (54 of 1963).
key_definitions.chargeable interest: The total amount of interest referred to in section 5, computed in the manner laid down in section 6.
key_definitions.credit institution: Includes banking companies, public financial institutions, State financial corporations, and other financial companies.
key_definitions.financial company: A company, other than specified institutions, whose principal business is hire-purchase finance, investment, housing finance, loan provision, mutual benefit finance, residuary non-banking, or miscellaneous finance.
key_definitions.interest: Interest on loans and advances made in India, including commitment charges on unutilised credit and discount on promissory notes/bills of exchange drawn/made in India, but excludes certain RBI Act interest and discount on treasury bills.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'assessee', 'assessment', 'chargeable interest', 'credit institution', 'interest', etc.
Specifies that income-tax authorities under the Income-tax Act are also the interest-tax authorities for this Act and outlines their jurisdiction and powers.
Details the imposition of interest-tax on scheduled banks and credit institutions for specified assessment years, at prescribed rates.
Defines what constitutes chargeable interest for a credit institution, excluding interest on loans/advances to other credit institutions or cooperative banks.
Outlines the rules for computing chargeable interest, including deductions for bad debts and specifying periods for which interest is not to be taken into account.
Mandates the furnishing of returns of chargeable interest by credit institutions and empowers the Assessing Officer to require such returns.

important_rules: Interest-tax is charged on chargeable interest of scheduled banks and credit institutions for specified assessment years.
Chargeable interest for credit institutions excludes interest on loans and advances to other credit institutions or cooperative banks.
Deduction for bad debts is allowed in computing chargeable interest.
Interest accruing or arising before April 1, 1974, or between April 1, 1985, and September 30, 1991, is not taken into account for computation.
Credit institutions must furnish a return of their chargeable interest by December 31st of the assessment year.

penalties: Penalty for concealment of chargeable interest (Section 13).
Interest for default in furnishing return of chargeable interest (Section 12).
Interest for default in payment of interest-tax in advance (Section 12A).
Interest for deferment of interest-tax payable in advance (Section 12B).
Penalties for false statements and wilful attempts to evade tax (Sections 24, 25).
Penalties for abetment of false returns (Section 26).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Interest-tax authorities, which are the income-tax authorities specified in Section 116 of the Income-tax Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, re-assessment, appeals, revision of orders, and imposition of penalties and interest for defaults.

rights: Right to appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals) and the Appellate Tribunal.
Right to rectification of mistakes.
Right to be heard before any adverse order is passed.
duties: Duty to furnish a return of chargeable interest.
Duty to pay interest-tax in advance.
Duty to comply with notices issued by tax authorities.
obligations: Obligation to pay interest-tax as per the Act.
Obligation to maintain records and provide information as required.

key_procedures: Filing of returns of chargeable interest by credit institutions.
Assessment and self-assessment of chargeable interest by tax authorities.
Appeals process to the Commissioner (Appeals) and the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal.
Rectification of mistakes by tax authorities.
Procedure for dealing with interest escaping assessment.
administration: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) oversees the administration of the Act through the designated interest-tax authorities.
important_notes: The Act was significantly amended in 1991, broadening its scope to include 'credit institutions' beyond scheduled banks and modifying definitions and chargeability.
Interest-tax was subject to varying rates over the years and was ultimately removed for chargeable interest accruing or arising after March 31, 2000.
Provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, are generally applied to this Act where not specifically provided otherwise, ensuring consistency in procedures and definitions.

title: THE SICK TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1974
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of sick textile undertakings and the rights of their owners, with the objective of reorganizing and rehabilitating them to serve public interest through increased production and distribution of cloth and yarn at fair prices.
scope: The Act applies to specific sick textile undertakings listed in the First Schedule, along with the rights, title, and interests of their owners. It covers the geographical location of these undertakings within India, as well as their operational and financial aspects. The scope extends to employees, liabilities, and the management of these undertakings.

key_definitions.appointed day: The 1st day of April, 1974.
key_definitions.bank: Includes the State Bank of India, subsidiary banks, corresponding new banks, and other scheduled banks.
key_definitions.Commissioner: A Commissioner of Payments appointed under section 17.
key_definitions.Custodian: A Custodian appointed under the Sick Textile Undertakings (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1972, or a person authorized to take over management under other relevant acts.
key_definitions.National Textile Corporation: The National Textile Corporation Limited, registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.owner: The proprietor, lessee, or occupier of a sick textile undertaking immediately before the appointed day, including liquidators or receivers of textile companies, but excluding persons authorized to take over management under specific acts.
key_definitions.sick textile undertaking: A textile undertaking specified in the First Schedule whose management was taken over by the Central Government prior to the appointed day under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, or vested in the Central Government under the Sick Textile Undertakings (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1972.
key_definitions.textile undertaking: An undertaking engaged in textile manufacturing to which the Factories Act, 1948, applies.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974. Sections 32 and 33 came into force immediately, while other provisions are deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1974.

Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, including 'appointed day', 'bank', 'Commissioner', 'Custodian', 'National Textile Corporation', 'owner', 'sick textile undertaking', and 'textile undertaking'.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of rights of owners in respect of sick textile undertakings
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, every sick textile undertaking and the owner's rights shall vest in the Central Government and then immediately in the National Textile Corporation. It also clarifies the status of leasehold rights and the jurisdiction of courts.

Details what is included in the vested sick textile undertaking (assets, rights, liabilities), and clarifies that vested property is freed from trusts, mortgages, and other incumbrances. It also covers the substitution of the National Textile Corporation in licenses and instruments, and the procedure for mortgages and other interested parties.

main_sections.section_title: Owner to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: Specifies that liabilities of a sick textile undertaking prior to the appointed day are the responsibility of the owner, not the Central Government or the National Textile Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Management, etc., of sick textile undertakings
main_sections.description: Deals with the management of sick textile undertakings after vesting.
Outlines the penalties for contravening provisions of the Act.
Addresses the repeal of any previous enactments and savings provisions.

important_rules: Rule: Sick textile undertakings and their owners' rights vest in the Central Government and then in the National Textile Corporation on the appointed day (April 1, 1974).
Rule: All assets, rights, and properties of the sick textile undertaking are transferred, freed from encumbrances.
Rule: The National Textile Corporation is to be substituted in any existing licenses or instruments related to the undertaking.
Rule: Owners remain liable for liabilities incurred before the appointed day.
Rule: Employees of sick textile undertakings are to be employed by the National Textile Corporation.
Rule: A Commissioner of Payments is appointed to manage claims and disbursement of amounts to owners and creditors.

penalties: Section 32 outlines penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Section 33 addresses offences by companies.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the National Textile Corporation, with specific roles for the Commissioner of Payments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the vesting of undertakings, transfer of rights, appointment of authorities (like Commissioners of Payments), and imposition of penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Owners have the right to receive payment for their undertakings as specified in the Act.
Creditors and mortgagees have rights to claim payment from the specified amount.
Employees have the right to continued employment.
The National Textile Corporation has rights over the vested undertakings, including managing them and entering into contracts.
The Central Government retains leasehold rights under certain conditions.
duties: Owners have a duty to transfer their undertakings and related rights.
Persons in charge of management have a duty to deliver all assets, records, etc., to the new authorities.
The National Textile Corporation has a duty to manage and rehabilitate the undertakings.
The Commissioner of Payments has a duty to receive claims and disburse payments.
Mortgagees and others with interests have a duty to intimate their claims to the Commissioner.
obligations: The Central Government has obligations related to leasehold rents and potentially for further amounts to owners.
The National Textile Corporation has obligations to manage the undertakings, provide employment, and pay dues.
Owners have obligations related to prior liabilities.

key_procedures: Acquisition and Vesting: Sick textile undertakings and owner rights are transferred to the Central Government and then to the National Textile Corporation on the appointed day.
Payment to Owners: A process is established for determining and paying the amount due to owners of sick textile undertakings, involving a Commissioner of Payments.
Claim Resolution: Creditors and others with interests in the undertakings can make claims to the Commissioner of Payments, who will examine and admit or reject them.
Disbursement: The Commissioner of Payments disburses money to claimants and owners.
Employee Transfer: Provisions are made for the employment of existing employees of the sick textile undertakings.
administration: The National Textile Corporation is the primary administrative body, with the Central Government having oversight and the Commissioner of Payments playing a crucial role in financial matters.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have retrospective effect for most provisions, starting from April 1, 1974.
The Act overrides all other enactments in case of conflict.
Contracts related to the undertaking may cease to have effect unless ratified by the National Textile Corporation.
Textile companies cannot be wound up by a court without the consent of the Central Government.
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

title: THE TOBACCO BOARD ACT, 1975
purpose: To provide for the development, under the control of the Union, of the tobacco industry.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It specifically regulates the production and disposal of Virginia tobacco, and impacts growers, curers, processors, manufacturers, exporters, packers, auctioneers, and dealers of tobacco and tobacco products.

key_definitions.Board: The Tobacco Board established under section 4.
key_definitions.curing: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 (1 of 1944).
key_definitions.Executive Director: The Executive Director appointed under section 6.
key_definitions.export and import: Respectively, taking out of, or bringing into, India, by land, sea or air.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board and includes the Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered: Except in the expression 'registered grower', registered under Chapter III of this Act and the rules made thereunder.
key_definitions.registered grower: A person who has obtained a certificate of registration under section 10 for growing Virginia tobacco.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as the Tobacco Board Act, 1975, states its extent to the whole of India, and mentions its commencement upon notification by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to take under its control the tobacco industry.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairman', 'curing', 'dealer', 'Executive Director', 'export', 'import', 'member', 'prescribed', 'registered', and 'registered grower'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and constitution of the Board
main_sections.description: Establishes the Tobacco Board, a body corporate, with a specified composition including a Chairman, members of Parliament, representatives from Central Government ministries and State Governments, and representatives from the tobacco industry and experts. It also specifies the location of the head office.

Outlines the primary duty of the Board to promote the development of the tobacco industry. It details specific measures including regulating production and curing of Virginia tobacco, monitoring the market, maintaining and developing markets, recommending minimum export prices, regulating marketing and export, propagating information, purchasing tobacco to protect growers' interests, promoting grading, and sponsoring research.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of growers of virginia tobacco
main_sections.description: Mandates the registration of growers of Virginia tobacco.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of curers of virginia tobacco
main_sections.description: Mandates the registration of curers of Virginia tobacco.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of exporters, packers, auctioneers and dealers
main_sections.description: Requires registration for exporters, packers, auctioneers, and dealers.

main_sections.section_title: Virginia tobacco to be sold at registered auction platforms
main_sections.description: Specifies that Virginia tobacco must be sold at registered auction platforms.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit or control import and export of tobacco and tobacco products
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to prohibit or control the import and export of tobacco and tobacco products.
Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the Board.
Addresses penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the Board the power to make regulations, with the approval of the Central Government, to carry out its functions.

important_rules: Virginia tobacco must be sold at registered auction platforms (Section 13).
Registered dealers and exporters have a duty to purchase Virginia tobacco at auction platforms (Section 13A).
Buyers of Virginia tobacco at places other than auction platforms must refrain from certain unfair practices (Section 13B).
The Board is responsible for promoting the development of the tobacco industry through various measures (Section 8(1)).
The Board may purchase Virginia tobacco from growers when necessary to protect their interests (Section 8(2)(g)).
The Central Government has the power to prohibit or control import and export of tobacco and tobacco products (Section 20).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 23).
Penalties for obstructing Board members/officers and for failure to produce books/records (Section 24).
Other penalties are also specified (Section 25).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Tobacco Board, with oversight and direction from the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of penalties, powers of inspection, and the ability of the Central Government to issue directions and make rules.

rights: Registered growers have the right to have their tobacco purchased by the Board when necessary to protect their interests.
Persons associated with the Board for specific purposes have the right to participate in discussions.
Officers deputed by the Central Government have the right to attend Board meetings and participate in proceedings, but not to vote.
duties: The Board has the duty to promote the development of the tobacco industry.
Registered dealers and exporters have a duty to purchase Virginia tobacco at auction platforms.
Buyers at places other than auction platforms have a duty to refrain from unfair practices.
obligations: Growers, curers, exporters, packers, auctioneers, and dealers are obligated to obtain registration as required by the Act.
The Board is obligated to operate under the control of the Central Government.

key_procedures: Registration of growers, curers, exporters, packers, auctioneers, and dealers (Sections 10, 11, 12, 14).
Application, cancellation, and fee payment related to registration (Section 14).
Establishment and functioning of auction platforms (Section 8(2)(cc)).
Reporting and submission of returns to the Central Government (Section 22).
Making of rules by the Central Government (Section 32) and regulations by the Board (Section 33).
administration: The Tobacco Board, with the ultimate control and rule-making authority resting with the Central Government.
important_notes: Different commencement dates may be appointed for different provisions and different areas (Section 1(3)).
The Act has been extended to specific states for certain sections (footnote on page 3).

No act or proceeding of the Board or its committees is invalidated by reason of vacancy, defect in constitution, defect in appointment, or procedural irregularity not affecting the merits of the case (Section 4(9)).
The office of a member of the Board does not disqualify them from being a member of Parliament (Section 4(4A)).
Actions taken in good faith in the execution of duties under the Act are protected (Section 29).

title: THE RAMPUR RAZA LIBRARY ACT, 1975
purpose: To declare the Rampur Raza Library to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its administration and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the Rampur Raza Library located in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh. It establishes a Board for its administration and management. The scope includes the management of the library, development of its collections, promotion of research, and financial and administrative matters related to the library.

key_definitions.Board: The Board established under section 4 of the Act, known as the "Rampur Raza Library Board".
key_definitions.deed of trust: The deed of trust executed by the late Nawab Sir Syed Raza Ali Khan Bahadur of Rampur on August 6, 1951.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund referred to in section 19.
key_definitions.library: The Rampur Raza Library, declared as an institution of national importance by this Act.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board, including the Chairman and Vice-Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Rampur: The headquarters of the District of Rampur in the State of Uttar Pradesh.
key_definitions.State Government: The Government of the State of Uttar Pradesh.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Rampur Raza Library Act, 1975, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Rampur Raza Library as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: This section declares the Rampur Raza Library, located at Rampur, as an institution of national importance.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairman', 'deed of trust', 'Fund', 'library', 'member', 'prescribed', 'Rampur', and 'State Government'.

This section provides for the establishment of a Board, to be known as the 'Rampur Raza Library Board', on a date appointed by the Central Government. The Board is established as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and enter into contracts.

This section details the composition of the Board, which includes ex officio members like the Governor of Uttar Pradesh (Chairman) and the Collector and District Magistrate of Rampur, as well as nominated members with expertise in library matters, historical scholarship, government officials, and scholars nominated by the State Government. The Director of the Library is the ex officio Member-Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and fresh nomination in certain cases
main_sections.description: This section outlines the term of office for nominated members, provisions for resignation, filling of vacancies by fresh nominations, eligibility for re-nomination, and the nomination of acting members in case of temporary incapacity or absence.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate acts
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that any act of the Board will not be invalidated due to vacancies, defects in the Board's constitution, defects in nomination, or procedural irregularities that do not affect the merits of the case.

This section imposes a duty on the nominating governments (Central or State) to ensure that nominated members have no prejudicial financial or other interests. Nominated members are also required to disclose any such interests in contracts or arrangements involving the Board.

This section outlines the procedures for Board meetings, including timing, location, quorum, and decision-making by majority vote. It also specifies who presides over meetings and provisions for authorized attendees and casting votes.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary association of persons with Board for particular purposes
main_sections.description: This section allows the Board to associate with any person for their assistance or advice in performing its functions, with such persons having the right to participate in discussions but not to vote.

main_sections.section_title: Authentication of orders and other instruments of Board
main_sections.description: This section details how orders and decisions of the Board are authenticated (by the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, or authorized member) and other instruments (by an authorized officer). Authenticated documents are admissible as evidence.
This section empowers the Board to appoint officers and employees for the efficient performance of its functions, with recruitment and service conditions to be governed by regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of service of existing employees to Board
main_sections.description: This section ensures that employees of the library before the Board's establishment become employees of the Board with the same terms and conditions, unless altered to their disadvantage with the Central Government's approval.
This section mandates that the library and its collections shall continue to be located at Rampur.

This section stipulates that upon the Board's establishment, properties, funds, and dues vested in the trustees shall vest in the Board, and liabilities enforceable against the trustees shall be enforceable against the Board. Any future acquisitions by the library or Board also vest in the Board.

This section outlines the general duty of the Board to manage the library, plan for its development on modern scientific lines, including preservation and photo-duplication of rare manuscripts, and perform other functions assigned by the Central Government. It also specifies particular duties such as providing for instruction and research, protecting and improving collections, and promoting study and research.

important_rules: The Rampur Raza Library is declared an institution of national importance.
A Rampur Raza Library Board is established for the administration of the library.
The Board is a corporate body with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Board's composition includes ex officio members (Governor of UP, Collector of Rampur) and nominated members with specific expertise or representation.
Nominated members' terms of office are to be prescribed.
No act of the Board is invalid due to vacancies, constitutional defects, or procedural irregularities not affecting merits.
Nominated members must disclose any conflicts of interest related to contracts or arrangements with the Board.
Board meetings require a quorum and decisions are made by majority vote, with the Chairman having a casting vote.
The Board can associate external persons for advice but they do not have voting rights.
All orders and decisions of the Board must be authenticated and are admissible as evidence.
The Board can appoint its own staff, with recruitment and service conditions governed by regulations.
Existing library employees are transferred to the Board with their existing terms and conditions, unless altered to their disadvantage with Central Government approval.
The library and its collections must remain located in Rampur.
Properties, funds, and liabilities of the library's trustees are transferred to the Board.
The Board's primary duty is to manage and develop the library, including preservation of rare manuscripts and promotion of research. It must also perform functions assigned by the Central Government.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (for the Board).
Right to contract (for the Board).
Right to sue and be sued (for the Board).
Right to take part in discussions of the Board for associated persons (non-voting).
Right to obtain copies of authenticated orders, decisions, or instruments from the library upon payment of fees (for members, officers, employees, or interested persons).
Existing employees have the right to retain their original terms and conditions of service unless altered to their disadvantage with Central Government approval.
duties: Duty of Central/State Government to ensure nominated members have no prejudicial interests.
Duty of nominated members to disclose financial or other interests in contracts/arrangements.
Duty of the Board to manage the library and plan for its development.
Duty of the Board to protect, enlarge, and improve library collections.
Duty of the Board to promote study and research and provide facilities to scholars.
Duty of the Board to perform functions assigned by the Central Government.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the deed of trust in managing the library.
Obligation to adhere to regulations for recruitment and service conditions of staff.
Obligation for any nominated member to disclose their interest in a contract or arrangement at a Board meeting.
Obligation for the Board to manage the library on modern scientific lines.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Rampur Raza Library Board upon notification by the Central Government.
Nomination of Board members by the Central and State Governments, with notification in the Official Gazette.
Resignation of nominated members through written notice.
Filling of vacancies by fresh nomination.
Conduct of Board meetings according to regulations, including quorum, presiding officer, and voting procedures.
Authentication of Board orders, decisions, and instruments.
Appointment of Board staff and determination of their recruitment and service conditions by regulations.
Transfer of existing library employees to the Board with specified conditions.
Management and development of the library by the Board as per its duties and assigned functions.
administration: The Rampur Raza Library Board is responsible for the administration of the library. The Central Government has oversight powers, including issuing directions and making rules, and the State Government has nomination powers for certain members.
important_notes: The Act aims to elevate the Rampur Raza Library to a status of national importance.
The Act intends to provide a framework for the administration and management of the library.
The library and its collections must remain in Rampur.
The Board's powers and duties are subject to the existing deed of trust and the provisions of this Act.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Board and make rules, while the Board can make regulations.
The Act overrides other enactments and instruments where there is an inconsistency.

title: THE DELHI SALES TAX ACT, 1975
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the levy of tax on sale of goods in the Union territory of Delhi.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi. It governs dealers engaged in the business of selling goods within Delhi.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator of Delhi appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: The Appellate Tribunal constituted under section 13.
key_definitions.business: Includes any trade, commerce, or manufacture, or any adventure or concern in the nature of trade, commerce, or manufacture, whether or not carried on with a motive to make gain or profit, and any transaction incidental or ancillary to such business.
key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of Sales Tax appointed under sub-section (1) of section 9.
key_definitions.dealer: Any person who carries on business of selling goods in Delhi, including the Central or State Government, incorporated societies, clubs or associations selling goods to members, managers, factors, brokers, commission agents, del credere agents, or any mercantile agent selling goods for a principal, and auctioneers selling goods for a principal.
key_definitions.goods: Includes all materials, articles, commodities, and all other kinds of moveable property, but excludes newspapers, actionable claims, stocks, shares, securities, or money.
key_definitions.manufacture: Producing, making, extracting, altering, ornamenting, finishing, or otherwise processing, treating, or adapting any goods, but does not include prescribed processes.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.sale: Any transfer of property in goods by one person to another for cash, deferred payment, or other valuable consideration. Includes hire-purchase, payment by instalments, supply of goods by certain entities to their members, and transfer of goods by an auctioneer.
key_definitions.sale price: The amount payable to a dealer as consideration for the sale of any goods, less cash discount, but inclusive of sums charged for anything done by the dealer in respect of goods at the time of or before delivery, excluding freight, delivery, or installation costs if separately charged.
key_definitions.tax: Sales tax payable under this Act.
key_definitions.turnover: The aggregate of the amounts of sale price receivable, or actually received, by the dealer in respect of any sale of goods during any prescribed period in any year, after deducting refunded amounts for returned goods. An election to receive or receivable can be altered only with the Commissioner's permission.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Administrator.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, dealer, goods, sale, sale price, and turnover.

Specifies who is liable to pay tax under the Act, based on turnover, existing registration under the Central Sales Tax Act, and the timing of exceeding the taxable quantum or becoming registered under the Central Sales Tax Act.
Lays down the rates of tax applicable to different categories of goods specified in the Schedules or otherwise, including special rates for food/drink served with entertainment.
Empowers the appointment of sales tax authorities.
Provides for the constitution of an Appellate Tribunal.
Deals with the requirement for dealers to register under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Periodical payment of tax and filing of returns
main_sections.description: Mandates periodical payment of tax and the filing of returns by dealers.
Covers the process of assessment of tax liability by the authorities.
Outlines the procedures for payment and recovery of tax.

main_sections.section_title: Liability in case of transfer of business
main_sections.description: Addresses the tax liability in situations where a business is transferred.
Specifies the requirement for dealers to maintain accounts.

main_sections.section_title: Production and inspection of accounts and documents and search of premises
main_sections.description: Grants powers to sales tax authorities for the production and inspection of accounts and documents, and for searching premises.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders passed under the Act.
Defines various offences under the Act.
Details the provisions for the imposition of penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Empowers the granting of exemptions from tax.
Grants the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Dealers whose turnover exceeds the taxable quantum are liable to pay tax on sales.
Tax is levied at specified rates on taxable turnover based on goods specified in schedules or otherwise.
Registered dealers are responsible for collecting tax and issuing tax invoices.
Dealers must file periodical returns and pay tax within the prescribed time.
Accounts must be maintained by dealers, and these can be inspected by sales tax authorities.
Penalties are imposed for offences like concealment of sales, furnishing inaccurate particulars, or contravening tax collection provisions.

penalties: Penalty for concealment of sales or furnishing inaccurate particulars or making false representations.
Penalty for contravening provisions regarding collection of tax by dealers.
Penalties for various offences as defined in Chapter IX.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Sales tax authorities appointed under the Act, including the Commissioner and the Appellate Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, recovery of tax, imposition of penalties, prosecution for offences, appeals, references, and revisions.

rights: Right to appeal against orders passed by sales tax authorities.
Right to apply for cancellation of registration if liability ceases.
Right to claim refund of excess tax paid.
duties: Duty to pay tax on sales.
Duty to register as a dealer if liable.
Duty to file periodical returns and pay tax on time.
Duty to maintain accounts and produce them for inspection.
Duty to collect tax from purchasers and pay it to the government.
Duty to report changes in business.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation to pay tax on turnover exceeding the taxable quantum.
Obligation to cooperate with sales tax authorities during assessments, inspections, and investigations.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of dealers (Sections 14-17).
Procedure for filing periodical returns and payment of tax (Section 21).
Procedure for assessment of tax (Sections 23-24).
Procedure for recovery of tax (Section 25).
Procedure for appeals (Section 43).
Procedure for revision of orders (Sections 46-47).
Procedure for rectification of mistakes (Section 48).
Procedure for compounding of offences (Section 54).
administration: The Act is administered by the Sales Tax authorities appointed under it, headed by the Commissioner of Sales Tax, and ultimately overseen by the Administrator of Delhi.
important_notes: Goods specified in the Third Schedule are not liable to tax.
Sales and purchases of certain nature are not liable to tax (Section 8).
Specific provisions exist for liability in case of transfer of business, company liquidation, and other special cases (Chapter VI).
The Act clarifies that certain actions, like mortgages or hypothecations, are not considered sales.
The power to make rules rests with the Administrator, with rules to be laid before Parliament.

title: THE BONDED LABOUR SYSTEM (ABOLITION) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the abolition of the bonded labour system with a view to preventing the economic and physical exploitation of the weaker sections of the people and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to any person who is or has been a bonded labourer, any agreement or custom that enforces bonded labour, and any bonded debt.

key_definitions.advance: An advance, whether in cash or in kind, made by a creditor to a debtor.
key_definitions.agreement: An agreement, written or oral, between a debtor and creditor, including those providing for forced labour presumed under social custom.
key_definitions.bonded debt: An advance obtained or presumed to have been obtained by a bonded labourer under the bonded labour system.
key_definitions.bonded labour: Any labour or service rendered under the bonded labour system.
key_definitions.bonded labourer: A labourer who incurs, has, or is presumed to have incurred a bonded debt.
key_definitions.bonded labour system: A system of forced or partly forced labour where a debtor agrees to render labour or service to a creditor in consideration of an advance, interest, customary obligation, succession obligation, economic consideration, or birth in a particular caste or community. This includes forfeiting freedom of employment, right to move freely, or right to appropriate or sell property or products of labour. It also includes a surety rendering bonded labour on behalf of a debtor who fails to repay a debt.
key_definitions.nominal wages: Wages less than the minimum wages fixed by the Government, or in their absence, wages normally paid for similar labor in the same locality.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date it came into force (deemed to have come into force on October 25, 1975).

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including advance, agreement, bonded debt, bonded labour, bonded labourer, bonded labour system, ascendant, descendant, family, and nominal wages.
Declares that the provisions of this Act will prevail over any other inconsistent enactment or instrument.

Abolishes the bonded labour system upon the commencement of the Act and declares all bonded labourers freed and discharged from any obligation to render bonded labour. It also prohibits making advances or compelling persons to render bonded labour or other forms of forced labour.

main_sections.section_title: Agreement, custom, etc., to be void
main_sections.description: States that any custom, tradition, contract, agreement, or instrument enforcing bonded labour shall be void and inoperative upon commencement of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Liability to repay bonded debt to stand extinguished
main_sections.description: Extinguishes all obligations of bonded labourers to repay bonded debts. Prohibits suits for recovery of bonded debts, deems decrees/orders for recovery as satisfied, vacates attachments, and restores seized movable property. It also mandates restoration of property forcibly taken for debt recovery and outlines a procedure for aggrieved persons to apply for restoration. Sales of attached property before commencement are not affected unless a bonded labourer applies within five years to set aside the sale. Pending suits for enforcement of bonded labour obligations are dismissed, and bonded labourers detained in civil prison are to be released.

main_sections.section_title: Property of bonded labourer to be freed from mortgage, etc.
main_sections.description: Frees all property vested in a bonded labourer from mortgages, charges, liens, or other encumbrances connected to bonded debts and mandates restoration of such property to the bonded labourer. It also provides for recovery of mesne profits if restoration is delayed.

main_sections.section_title: Freed bonded labourer not to be evicted from homestead, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the eviction of freed bonded labourers from their homesteads or residential premises occupied before the commencement of the Act as part of bonded labour consideration. Empowers Executive Magistrates to restore possession if eviction occurs.

main_sections.section_title: Creditor not to accept payment against extinguished debt
main_sections.description: Prohibits creditors from accepting payment against extinguished bonded debts and prescribes punishment (imprisonment and fine) for contravention. Convicted persons may be ordered to deposit the accepted amount for refund to the bonded labourer.

main_sections.section_title: Authorities who may be specified for implementing the provisions of this Act
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to specify authorities for implementing the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of District Magistrate and other officers to ensure credit
main_sections.description: Assigns the duty to the District Magistrate and other officers to ensure credit facilities for freed bonded labourers.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of District Magistrate and officers authorised by him
main_sections.description: Outlines the duties of the District Magistrate and officers authorized by him in implementing the Act.
Provides for the constitution of Vigilance Committees.
Details the functions and responsibilities of Vigilance Committees.
Specifies the burden of proof in cases related to bonded labour.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for enforcement of bonded labour
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for enforcing bonded labour.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for advancement of bonded debt
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for advancing bonded debt.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for extracting bonded labour under the bonded labour system
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for extracting bonded labour under the bonded labour system.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for omission or failure to restore possession of property to bonded labourers
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for failing to restore possession of property to bonded labourers.
Makes abetment of offences under the Act an offence.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be tried by Executive Magistrates
main_sections.description: Specifies that offences under the Act are to be tried by Executive Magistrates.
Details the procedure for taking cognizance of offences under the Act.
Deals with offences committed by companies.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters covered by the Act.
Confers the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Repeals previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: On commencement of the Act, the bonded labour system is abolished, and all bonded labourers are freed from their obligations (Section 4(1)).
No person shall make advances under or in pursuance of the bonded labour system, or compel any person to render bonded labour or other forced labour (Section 4(2)).
Any agreement, custom, or instrument enforcing bonded labour is void and inoperative (Section 5).
All obligations to repay bonded debt are extinguished. No suits or proceedings for recovery of bonded debts are maintainable (Section 6(1), 6(2)).
Property of bonded labourers under mortgage or charge for bonded debt stands freed and discharged, and possession shall be restored to the bonded labourer (Section 7(1)).
Freed bonded labourers cannot be evicted from their homesteads or residential premises occupied before the Act's commencement (Section 8(1)).
Creditors shall not accept payment against extinguished bonded debts (Section 9(1)).

penalties: Punishment for enforcement of bonded labour (Section 16).
Punishment for advancement of bonded debt (Section 17).
Punishment for extracting bonded labour under the bonded labour system (Section 18).
Punishment for omission or failure to restore possession of property to bonded labourers (Section 19).

Punishment for contravention of Section 9(1) (accepting payment against extinguished debt) can include imprisonment up to three years and fine. The court may also order the deposit of the accepted amount for refund (Section 9(2), 9(3)).
Abetment of offences is also punishable (Section 20).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Magistrate, other officers authorized by the State Government, and Executive Magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the prosecution of offenders, restoration of property and possession to bonded labourers, and by the actions of specified implementing authorities and Vigilance Committees.

rights: Right to be freed and discharged from bonded labour obligations (Section 4(1)).
Right to have bonded debts extinguished (Section 6(1)).
Right to have property freed from mortgages/charges related to bonded debts and restored to possession (Section 7(1)).
Right not to be evicted from homesteads or residential premises (Section 8(1)).
Right to have possession of property restored if taken forcibly for debt recovery (Section 6(5)).
Right to apply for restoration of property if not restored within thirty days (Section 6(6)).
Right to be released from civil prison if detained for bonded debt (Section 6(10)).
duties: Duty of the State Government to specify authorities for implementation (Section 10).
Duty of the District Magistrate and other officers to ensure credit for freed bonded labourers (Section 11).
Duty of the District Magistrate and authorized officers to implement the Act (Section 12).
Duty of Vigilance Committees to perform their functions (Section 14).
Duty of creditors not to accept payment against extinguished debts (Section 9(1)).
obligations: Obligation to not compel persons to render bonded labour or other forced labour (Section 4(2)).
Obligation for creditors not to accept payment against extinguished debts (Section 9(1)).
Obligation for specified authorities to implement the Act's provisions.

key_procedures: Application for restoration of property: An aggrieved person can apply to the prescribed authority for restoration of property if it is not restored within thirty days of the Act's commencement (Section 6(6)).
Trial of offences: Offences under the Act are to be tried by Executive Magistrates (Section 21).
Making rules: The State Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 26).
administration: The State Government is responsible for specifying authorities for implementation, and the District Magistrate, along with other officers and Vigilance Committees, plays a key role in administration and enforcement.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on any inconsistent laws (Section 3).
The Act is deemed to have come into force from October 25, 1975 (Section 1(3)).

Sales of attached property in execution of a decree for bonded debt before the Act's commencement are not affected unless the bonded labourer applies to set aside the sale within five years by depositing the specified amount (Section 6(8)).
The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in matters covered by the Act (Section 25).

title: The Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976
purpose: To provide for the incorporation, regulation, and winding up of Regional Rural Banks to develop the rural economy by providing credit and other facilities, particularly to small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans, and small entrepreneurs.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to Regional Rural Banks established under it. It also applies to Sponsor Banks and State Governments in relation to Regional Rural Banks.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of directors of a Regional Rural Bank.
key_definitions.Chairman: The individual appointed or re-appointed as the Chairman of a Regional Rural Bank.
key_definitions.director: A member of the Board of a Regional Rural Bank.
key_definitions.National Bank: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development established under the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981.
key_definitions.notified area: The local limits within which a Regional Rural Bank shall operate, as specified by notification.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Regional Rural Bank: A Regional Rural Bank established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Sponsor Bank: A bank by which a Regional Rural Bank has been sponsored.
key_definitions.State Government: In relation to a Regional Rural Bank established in a Union territory, the Central Government; in relation to a Regional Rural Bank established in a State, the Government of that State.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its extent (whole of India), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on September 26, 1975).

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Board, Chairman, director, National Bank, notified area, prescribed, Regional Rural Bank, Sponsor Bank, and State Government. It also refers to definitions in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Regional Rural Banks
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish Regional Rural Banks upon request from a Sponsor Bank, specifying their name and operational area. It states that each Regional Rural Bank shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire property, contract, sue, and be sued. It also outlines the duty of the Sponsor Bank to aid and assist the sponsored Regional Rural Bank.

Specifies that the head office of a Regional Rural Bank shall be in its notified area, as determined by the Central Government in consultation with the National Bank and the Sponsor Bank. It also allows Regional Rural Banks to establish branches or agencies within their notified area.

Defines the authorised capital of each Regional Rural Bank and empowers the Central Government, in consultation with the National Bank and the Sponsor Bank, to increase or reduce it, with a minimum limit.

Specifies the initial issued capital of a Regional Rural Bank and the proportion of subscription by the Central Government, the concerned State Government, and the Sponsor Bank. It also allows for raising capital from other sources and provides for consultation with the State Government regarding shareholding limits.

Declares that the shares of a Regional Rural Bank are deemed to be included among the securities enumerated in section 20 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and are approved securities for the purposes of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

States that the general superintendence, direction, and management of a Regional Rural Bank vest in its Board of directors, who can exercise all powers and discharge all functions. The Board is required to act on business principles and give due regard to public interest.

Details the composition of the Board of directors, including the Chairman, nominated directors from the Central Government, State Government, Reserve Bank, National Bank, and Sponsor Bank, and elected directors by shareholders. It also allows the Central Government to increase the Board's strength and appoint a government officer.

Specifies the term of office for directors nominated by the Central Government, stating they hold office at the pleasure of the Central Government and are eligible for renomination, with a maximum continuous or intermittent holding period.

Outlines the appointment of the Chairman by the Sponsor Bank, specifying their term of office and the conditions for appointment, including consultation with the National Bank or prior approval of the Central Government in certain cases. It also grants the Sponsor Bank the right to terminate the Chairman's term.

important_rules: Regional Rural Banks must operate within their notified area.
The Board of directors must act on business principles and consider public interest.
The Sponsor Bank has a duty to aid and assist the sponsored Regional Rural Bank by subscribing to share capital, training personnel, and providing managerial and financial assistance.
The shares of a Regional Rural Bank are considered approved securities under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, National Bank, Sponsor Bank, State Government (depending on the specific provision).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, rules, regulations, consultations, and the powers vested in the Central Government, National Bank, Sponsor Bank, and State Government.

rights: Regional Rural Banks have the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract, sue, and be sued in their name.
The Sponsor Bank has the right to appoint the Chairman of a Regional Rural Bank and to terminate their term.
Shareholders have the right to elect directors under certain conditions.
duties: Regional Rural Banks have a duty to operate on business principles and consider public interest.
Sponsor Banks have a duty to aid and assist the Regional Rural Banks they sponsor.
The Central Government, State Government, Reserve Bank, National Bank, and Sponsor Bank have duties related to nominations and approvals for the Board of directors and Chairman.
obligations: Sponsor Banks are obligated to subscribe to the share capital, train personnel, and provide managerial and financial assistance to sponsored Regional Rural Banks.
Regional Rural Banks are subject to regulation and winding up procedures as outlined in the Act.
The Central Government has an obligation to consult the concerned State Government before reducing the State Government's shareholding below fifteen percent.

key_procedures: Establishment of a Regional Rural Bank: Central Government, upon request by a Sponsor Bank, establishes the bank via notification, specifying its name and operational area.
Appointment of Chairman: Sponsor Bank appoints a Chairman, specifying the term, with conditions regarding consultation or approval.
Nomination of Directors: Central Government, Reserve Bank, National Bank, Sponsor Bank, and State Government nominate directors to the Board.
Election of Directors: Shareholders elect directors based on their equity share capital percentage.
administration: The Central Government, in conjunction with the National Bank, Sponsor Banks, and State Governments, plays a significant role in the administration of Regional Rural Banks.
important_notes: The Act was deemed to have come into force on September 26, 1975.
The Act allows for amendments to the authorised and issued capital of Regional Rural Banks.
Provisions for the amalgamation and liquidation of Regional Rural Banks are included (Chapter VA).

title: The Public Sector Iron and Steel Companies (Restructuring) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1978
purpose: To provide for the restructuring of iron and steel companies in the public sector to ensure better management and increased efficiency, and to deal with related or incidental matters.
scope: The act applies to specific public sector iron and steel companies, their undertakings, shares, officers, and employees, as detailed in the schedules and definitions. It covers the geographical scope implied by the registered offices of the companies and the locations of the undertakings, primarily within India.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which the Act comes into force, notified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.dissolved company: A company specified in the First Schedule of the Act.
key_definitions.transferee company: A company to which undertakings of a dissolved company or a transferred unit are transferred by this Act.
key_definitions.transferred company: Includes Metallurgical and Engineering Consultants (India) Limited, National Mineral Development Corporation Limited, Hindustan Steelworks Construction Limited, Bharat Refractories Limited, and India Firebricks and Insulation Company Limited.
key_definitions.transferred unit: Includes Kiriburu Iron Ore Mines, Meghahatuburu Iron Ore Project, Ramgarh Refractory Plant, Refractory Project (Bhilai), and Sillimanite Mines, as units of specific corporations.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via official gazette notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Companies Act', 'corresponding unit', 'dissolved company', 'Integral Company', 'transferee company', 'transferred company', and 'transferred unit'.
Defines 'undertaking' for the purpose of the Act to include all assets, rights, leaseholds, licences, properties (movable and immovable), and liabilities of a dissolved company or transferred unit.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution, transfer and vesting of undertakings of certain companies in Integral Company
main_sections.description: States that companies listed in the First Schedule stand dissolved on the appointed day, and their undertakings are transferred to and vest in the Integral Company.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting of Kiriburu Iron Ore Mines, etc., in Integral Company
main_sections.description: Specifies the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of Kiriburu Iron Ore Mines and Meghahatuburu Iron Ore Project in the Integral Company.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting of Refractory Plant, etc., in the Bharat Refractories Limited
main_sections.description: Details the transfer and vesting of the Ramgarh Refractory Plant, Sillimanite Mines, and Refractory Project (Bhilai) in Bharat Refractories Limited. It also allows for the registered office of Bharat Refractories Limited to remain at Bokaro Steel City or be transferred to Ranchi.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of immovable properties of Hindustan Steel Limited to Metallurgical and Engineering Consultants (India) Limited
main_sections.description: Covers the transfer of Hindustan Steel Limited's immovable properties in Ranchi District, Bihar, along with related liabilities and obligations, to Metallurgical and Engineering Consultants (India) Limited.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of shares held by Bokaro Steel Limited to Central Government
main_sections.description: States that shares held by Bokaro Steel Limited in Bharat Refractories Limited are transferred to and vest in the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of shares held by Integral Company to Central Government
main_sections.description: Specifies the transfer of shares held by Integral Company in companies listed in the Second Schedule to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of shares held by Integral Company to Bharat Refractories Limited
main_sections.description: Covers the transfer of shares held by Integral Company in India Firebricks and Insulation Company Limited to Bharat Refractories Limited.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of shares held by Central Government to Integral Company
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of shares held by the Central Government in Indian Iron and Steel Company Limited to the Integral Company.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government, etc., deemed to be registered in the register of members of companies
main_sections.description: Provides that the Central Government, Bharat Refractories Limited, or Integral Company, as the case may be, are deemed to be registered members in the respective companies' registers of members for shares transferred to them.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to modify amount of paid-up share capital of Integral Company, etc., and issue of shares
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to modify the paid-up share capital of Integral Company, Bharat Refractories Limited, Metallurgical and Engineering Consultants (India) Limited, and National Mineral Development Corporation Limited, taking into account factors like book value of shares, net value of undertakings, and book value of properties. It also allows for the issue or cancellation of shares.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions relating to officers and other employees of dissolved companies
main_sections.description: Deals with the continuation of service for officers and employees of dissolved companies (excluding directors and those in units under section 6) in the corresponding units of the Integral Company, with existing terms and conditions, unless altered.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions relating to officers and employees of transferred units
main_sections.description: Ensures that officers and employees of transferred units continue in service in the corresponding units of the transferee company with their existing terms and conditions of service, unless altered.
Deals with the provisions concerning directors.
Addresses provisions related to auditors.
States that compensation for transfer under this Act is not payable.
Covers provisions related to Provident Fund.
Addresses provisions for Gratuity, welfare, and other funds.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions with respect to income-tax and surtax
main_sections.description: Deals with provisions concerning income-tax and surtax.

main_sections.section_title: Taxes, fees and other charges not payable
main_sections.description: States that certain taxes, fees, and other charges are not payable.
Provides for the saving of existing contracts.
Ensures the saving of legal proceedings.
Grants the Central Government power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act to override the provisions of other laws
main_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in other laws.

main_sections.section_title: Power to amend memorandum and articles of association
main_sections.description: Confers power to amend the memorandum and articles of association of companies.

important_rules: Companies listed in the First Schedule are dissolved on the appointed day, and their undertakings are transferred to the Integral Company.
Specific units like Kiriburu Iron Ore Mines and Meghahatuburu Iron Ore Project are transferred to the Integral Company.
Certain refractory plants and mines are transferred to Bharat Refractories Limited.
Immovable properties of Hindustan Steel Limited in Ranchi District are transferred to Metallurgical and Engineering Consultants (India) Limited.
Shares of various companies are transferred between Bokaro Steel Limited, Integral Company, Bharat Refractories Limited, and the Central Government as specified.
Officers and employees of dissolved companies and transferred units continue in service with their existing terms and conditions unless altered.
Compensation for transfer of undertakings or shares under this Act is not payable.
Certain taxes, fees, and charges are not payable under this Act.
The Act overrides the provisions of other laws where there is inconsistency.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders, and the application of the Act's provisions regarding transfer, vesting, and management of companies and their assets. Section 25 allows the Central Government to remove difficulties in implementation.

rights: Officers and employees retain their tenure, terms and conditions of service, and retirement benefits.
The Central Government has the right to issue orders to modify share capital and resolve implementation difficulties.
Companies' legal proceedings and contracts are generally saved.
duties: The Central Government has the duty to notify the commencement date and issue orders for share capital adjustments.
Transferee companies have a duty to continue employing officers and employees from dissolved companies and transferred units under existing conditions.
Companies must comply with the Act's provisions regarding the transfer and vesting of undertakings and shares.
obligations: Companies and their transferred units have obligations related to their assets, liabilities, and operations as transferred.
The Central Government has obligations related to ensuring the effective restructuring and management of the public sector iron and steel companies.

key_procedures: Notification of the appointed day by the Central Government.
Automatic dissolution and transfer/vesting of undertakings and shares on the appointed day as per specified sections.
Issuance of orders by the Central Government to adjust share capital and direct the issue or cancellation of shares.
Continuation of employment for affected officers and employees under existing terms and conditions.
Application of Section 25 for removing any difficulties encountered during the Act's implementation, by order of the Central Government.
administration: The Central Government, with specific references to departments or bodies like the Steel Authority of India Limited (Integral Company), Bharat Refractories Limited, Metallurgical and Engineering Consultants (India) Limited, and National Mineral Development Corporation Limited.
important_notes: The Act aims to improve management and efficiency in public sector iron and steel companies.
The Act may have retrospective effect from the appointed day for orders made under section 13(3).
Section 26 explicitly states that this Act overrides other laws.

title: The Coast Guard Act, 1978
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an Armed Force of the Union for ensuring the security of the maritime zones of India with a view to the protection of maritime and other national interests in such zones and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the Coast Guard, its members, and the maritime zones of India (territorial waters, contiguous zone, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, or any other maritime zone). It covers the security and protection of national interests within these zones.

key_definitions.Chief Law Officer and Law Officer: Appointed under section 115 of the Act.
key_definitions.civil offence: An offence triable by a criminal court.
key_definitions.civil prison: Any jail or place used for detention of criminal prisoners under the Prisons Act, 1894, or any other law.
key_definitions.Coast Guard: The armed force constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.Coast Guard custody: Arrest or confinement of a member of the Coast Guard according to rules.
key_definitions.Commanding Officer: The officer responsible for the functions of a Commanding Officer for a unit or ship.
key_definitions.criminal court: A court of ordinary criminal justice in any part of India.
key_definitions.Deputy Inspector-General: A Deputy Inspector-General of the Coast Guard appointed under section 5.
key_definitions.Director-General: The Director-General of the Coast Guard appointed under section 5.
key_definitions.enrolled person: A subordinate officer, sailor, or other person enrolled under this Act.
key_definitions.Inspector-General: An Inspector-General of the Coast Guard appointed under section 5.
key_definitions.maritime zones of India: Includes territorial waters, contiguous zone, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, or any other maritime zone of India.
key_definitions.member of the Coast Guard: An officer, subordinate officer, sailor, or other enrolled person.
key_definitions.notification: Published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.offence: Any act or omission punishable under this Act, including a civil offence.
key_definitions.officer: A person appointed or in pay as an officer of the Coast Guard, excluding subordinate officers, sailors, or enrolled persons.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.rule: A rule made under this Act.
key_definitions.sailor: A member of the Coast Guard other than an officer, subordinate officer, or other enrolled person.
key_definitions.ship: A Coast Guard vessel, including any establishment or station belonging to or under the control of the Coast Guard, whether within or without India (except in the expression 'on board a ship').
key_definitions.skipper: A subordinate officer in command of a ship.
key_definitions.subordinate officer: A person appointed or in pay as a Pradhan Adhikari, Pradhan Sahayak Engineer, Uttam Adhikari, Uttam Sahayak Engineer, Adhikari, Sahayak Engineer, or Pradhan Yantrik of the Coast Guard.
key_definitions.superior officer: An officer or subordinate officer senior to a person subject to the Act or entitled to give a command to that person.
key_definitions.territorial waters, contiguous zone, con: Have meanings assigned in the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Coast Guard Act, 1978, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Coast Guard', 'member of the Coast Guard', 'maritime zones of India', 'offence', and 'officer'.
Specifies who is subject to the Act, including officers, enrolled persons, persons serving on Coast Guard ships by order, and passengers on Coast Guard ships or aircraft.

Establishes the Coast Guard as an armed force of the Union for ensuring the security of India's maritime zones and protecting maritime and national interests within them. It also outlines the manner of constitution and conditions of service.
vests general superintendence, direction, and control of the Coast Guard in the Central Government, with the Director-General exercising command and supervision.

main_sections.section_title: Duties and functions of Coast Guard
main_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities and operational roles of the Coast Guard.
Details various offences that members of the Coast Guard or persons subject to the Act can commit, including desertion, disobedience, mutiny, and offences related to property and discipline.
Specifies the types of punishments that can be awarded by Coast Guard Courts and otherwise, including imprisonment, detention, and minor punishments.
Covers procedures for the arrest and custody of offenders before their trial.
Details the convening, composition, powers, and jurisdiction of Coast Guard Courts, including choices between criminal courts and Coast Guard Courts.
Lays down the procedural rules for Coast Guard Courts, including evidence, witness examination, and handling of lunacy cases.
Covers the execution, suspension, commutation, and remission of sentences awarded by Coast Guard Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Chief Law Officer and Law Officers
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment and functions of the Chief Law Officer and Law Officers.

main_sections.section_title: Judicial review of proceedings of Coast Guard Courts
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for judicial review of proceedings by the Chief Law Officer and consideration by the Director-General.

main_sections.section_title: Modification of findings and sentences, pardons, commutation and remission of sentences
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the Central Government and Director-General regarding petitions, modifications of findings and sentences, and granting of pardons, commutations, and remissions.
Includes provisions on powers and duties conferrable on members, protection for acts of members, and rule-making powers.

important_rules: Members of the Coast Guard are liable for service both within and outside India.
Every member must take an oath or affirmation of allegiance.
No member can resign or withdraw from duties without the prescribed authority's permission.
Members hold office during the pleasure of the President.
Specific authorities (Central Government, Director-General, etc.) have power to dismiss or remove members from service.
Offences detailed in Chapters IV are punishable under the Act.
Punishments are awarded by Coast Guard Courts or otherwise, as specified in Chapter V.
Arrest and custody procedures for offenders are outlined in Chapter VI.
Coast Guard Courts have defined powers and procedures for trials as detailed in Chapters VII and VIII.
Sentences awarded can be executed, suspended, commuted, or remitted as per Chapter IX.
Judicial review of Coast Guard Court proceedings is a process involving the Chief Law Officer and Director-General.
The Central Government and Director-General have powers to modify findings and sentences.
Rules can be made by the Central Government to prescribe various aspects of the Act's implementation.

penalties: Punishments awardable by Coast Guard Courts, which can include death, imprisonment, detention, dismissal, reduction in rank, forfeiture of pay, and fines.
Minor punishments for less serious offences.
Punishments for officers below the rank of Commandant.
Provisions for civil offences committed by Coast Guard personnel.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Coast Guard itself, through its command structure (Director-General, Inspector-Generals, Commanding Officers), and Coast Guard Courts. Civil authorities may also be involved in arrest.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through arrest, custody, trial by Coast Guard Courts or criminal courts, and execution of sentences. The Act also provides for judicial review and administrative modification of findings and sentences.

rights: Right to receive pay and benefits as per service conditions.
Right to hold office during the pleasure of the President (implies protection from arbitrary dismissal without cause defined by the Act).
Right to appeal or petition against findings and sentences to the Central Government or Director-General.
Protection for acts done in good faith in the execution of duty (section 122).
Freedom from double jeopardy (prohibition of second trial for the same offence, section 68).
duties: To perform duties and functions as assigned by the Act.
To be subject to the Act and its provisions.
To maintain good order and discipline.
To obey lawful commands of superior officers.
To serve in any part of India as well as outside India.
To make and subscribe an oath or affirmation of allegiance.
To not resign or withdraw from duties without permission.
obligations: Obligation to be enrolled and follow prescribed procedures.
Obligation to cooperate with investigations and trials.
Obligation to adhere to the rules and orders made under the Act.

key_procedures: Enrolment: Persons to be enrolled, mode, and procedure are prescribed by rules (Section 6).
Arrest and Custody: Procedures for arresting and detaining offenders before trial (Chapter VI).
Convening a Coast Guard Court: Process and composition of Coast Guard Courts (Chapter VII).
Trial Procedure: Rules governing evidence, challenges, witness examination, and voting in Coast Guard Courts (Chapter VIII).
Execution of Sentences: Procedures for carrying out death sentences, imprisonment, detention, and fines (Chapter IX).
Judicial Review: Process for reviewing proceedings of Coast Guard Courts by the Chief Law Officer and Director-General (Chapter XI).
Petitions against findings/sentences: Procedure for submitting petitions to the Central Government or Director-General (Chapter XII).
administration: The Central Government exercises general superintendence, direction, and control. The Director-General of the Coast Guard is responsible for command and supervision, assisted by other officers appointed by the Central Government. Rule-making power rests with the Central Government (Section 123).
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date to be notified by the Central Government.
The specific 'prescribed' procedures, rules, and conditions are detailed in separate rules made under the Act, which are not fully provided in this excerpt.
Section 2(y) refers to the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976, for definitions of maritime zones.
Section 2(z) refers to the Indian Penal Code, 1860, for the meaning of words and expressions not defined in this Act.

title: THE METRO RAILWAYS (CONSTRUCTION OF WORKS) ACT, 1978
purpose: To provide for the construction of works relating to metro railways in metropolitan cities and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act initially applies to the metropolitan city of Calcutta. The Central Government can extend its application to other metropolitan cities, metropolitan areas, and the National Capital Region through notification, after consultation with the respective State Governments. The Act covers the acquisition of land, buildings, streets, roads, passages, and rights of user or easements for metro railway construction and related works. It also governs the construction of works, inspection of metro railways, and addresses various miscellaneous provisions related to metro railways.

key_definitions.advisory_board: The Advisory Board constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.appellate_authority: The appellate authority appointed under section 16.
