key_definitions.building: A house, outhouse, stable, latrine, urinal, shed, hut or wall or any other structure or erection, whether of masonry bricks, wood, mud, metal or any other material or any part of a building, but does not include plant or machinery installed in a building or any part thereof or any portable shelter.
key_definitions.commissioner: A commissioner of metro railway appointed under section 27.
key_definitions.competent_authority: The competent authority appointed under section 16.
key_definitions.development: The carrying out of building, engineering, mining or other operations in, on, over or under land or the making of any material change in any building or land or planting of any tree on land and includes redevelopment.
key_definitions.land: Includes any right or interest in land.
key_definitions.metro_alignment: In relation to any metropolitan city, metropolitan area and the National Capital Region, means such alignment of the metro railway as is specified in the Schedule under that city and includes the metro railway.
key_definitions.metropolitan_area: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in clause (c) of article 243P of the Constitution.
key_definitions.metro_railway: A metro railway or any portion thereof for the public carriage of passengers, animals or goods and includes all land within the boundary marks indicating the limits of the land appurtenant to a metro railway, all lines of rails, sidings, yards or branches worked over for the purposes of, or in connection with, a metro railway, and all stations, offices, ventilation shafts and ducts, warehouses, workshops, manufactories, fixed plants and machineries, sheds, depots and other works constructed for the purpose of, or in connection with, a metro railway.
key_definitions.metro_railway_administration: In relation to any metro railway, means the General Manager of that metro railway.
key_definitions.metropolitan_city: Means the metropolitan city of Bombay, Calcutta, Delhi or Madras.
key_definitions.rolling_stock: Includes locomotives, engines, carriages (whether powered or not), wagons, trollies and vehicles of all kinds moving or intended to move on rails.
key_definitions.to_erect: In relation to any building, includes any material alteration or enlargement of such building; conversion, by structural alteration, into a place for human habitation of such building not originally constructed for human habitation; conversion into more than one place for human habitation of such building originally constructed as one such place; conversion of two or more places of human habitation in such building into a greater number of such places; such alteration of such building as would alter the drainage or sanitary arrangements therein or would materially affect its security; and the addition of any rooms in such building.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, and details its initial application to Calcutta, with provisions for extension to other metropolitan areas.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Advisory Board', 'building', 'commissioner', 'competent authority', 'land', 'metro alignment', 'metro railway', 'metropolitan city', and 'rolling stock'.
Empowers the Central Government to appoint a General Manager for every metro railway.

Allows the Central Government to constitute an Advisory Board for each metro railway to assist and advise on matters related to its development, financing, execution, and coordination, ensuring due regard to local circumstances and requirements.
Grants the Advisory Board the power to constitute committees for specific purposes, consisting of its members or other persons.

Empowers the metro railway administration to apply to the Central Government for the acquisition of land, buildings, streets, roads, passages, or rights of user/easement necessary for metro railway construction.

Details the process of issuing a notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government declaring its intention to acquire specified property after being satisfied of the public purpose. It also outlines the publication requirements for the notification.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter for survey, etc.
main_sections.description: Authorizes the metro railway administration or its employees to enter, survey, take levels, dig, bore, set out works, mark boundaries, and perform other necessary acts on the notified land to ascertain suitability for the metro railway, with a mandate to cause minimal damage.

Provides a mechanism for persons interested in the property to object to the construction within twenty-one days of the notification. The competent authority must provide a hearing to the objector and can allow or disallow objections, with the order being final.
Stipulates that if no objections are raised or if objections are disallowed, the competent authority shall submit a report for the declaration of acquisition.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take possession of acquired land, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the competent authority the power to take possession of land, buildings, etc., after the declaration of acquisition.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of amount payable for acquisition
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for determining the compensation amount payable for acquired property.

main_sections.section_title: Land Acquisition Act 1 of 1894 not to apply
main_sections.description: States that the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, will not apply to acquisitions made under this Act.
Defines the general functions of the metro railway administration.
Details the powers vested in the metro railway administration for the construction and operation of metro railways.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit or regulate construction of buildings and excavation
main_sections.description: Grants the metro railway administration the power to prohibit or regulate the construction of buildings and excavation within specified areas to ensure the safety and integrity of metro railway works.
Provides for the appointment and defines the duties of a commissioner for metro railways.
Specifies the powers that commissioners of metro railways can exercise.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to comply with directions issued under section 21
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for non-compliance with directions issued under section 21 concerning building construction and excavation.

main_sections.section_title: General provision for punishment of offences
main_sections.description: Lays down general provisions for the punishment of offences committed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of Act and rules, etc., inconsistent with other enactments
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act and its rules will have an overriding effect where they are inconsistent with other laws.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any person interested in a property intended for acquisition can object to the metro railway construction within twenty-one days of the notification's publication.
Rule 2: Objections must be made in writing to the competent authority, stating the grounds, and the objector has a right to be heard.
Rule 3: The metro railway administration or its employees have the right to enter and survey land notified for acquisition, causing minimal damage.
Rule 4: The metro railway administration can prohibit or regulate building construction and excavation in areas impacting metro railway works.
Rule 5: Penalties are prescribed for failure to comply with directions issued under section 21 (prohibition/regulation of construction and excavation).

penalties: Penalty for failure to comply with directions issued under section 21.
General provision for punishment of offences under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent Authority, Appellate Authority, Commissioners of Metro Railway, and Central Government (for making rules and notifications).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, orders by competent and appellate authorities, and general penal provisions for offences. Enforcement of orders of competent and appellate authorities is also specified.

rights: Right of persons interested in property to object to acquisition.
Right to be heard by the competent authority.
Right to claim for damages for loss or injury caused by metro railway construction.
Right to enter into the land where right of user, etc., is vested in the Central Government.
Right to receive compensation for acquired land, building, etc.
Right to access information published by the Central Government.
duties: Duty of metro railway administration to cause as little damage or injury as possible during survey.
Duty to give objectors an opportunity of being heard.
Duty of local authorities to assist.
Duty to afford facilities to commissioners.
obligations: Obligation to comply with directions issued under section 21.
Obligation to report accidents.
Obligation to not obstruct metro railway works.
Obligation to not remove marks placed for survey.

key_procedures: Procedure for acquisition of land: Application by metro railway administration, Central Government notification, publication of notification, hearing of objections, declaration of acquisition, taking possession, and determination/deposit of compensation.

Procedure for construction of works: Functions and powers of the metro railway administration, including power to prohibit or regulate construction and excavation, underpin buildings, and enter property.
Procedure for inspection: Appointment and duties of commissioners, their powers, and facilities to be afforded to them.
Procedure for dealing with surplus land: Sale or other disposal of surplus land.
Procedure for accident reporting: Notice of accidents and enquiries.
Procedure for making rules: Power of the Central Government to make rules.
administration: Central Government, Metro Railway Administration (headed by the General Manager), Advisory Board, Competent Authority, Appellate Authority, and Commissioners of Metro Railway.
important_notes: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894, does not apply to acquisitions under this Act.
The Act allows for the extension of its application to other metropolitan areas beyond Calcutta.
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws inconsistent with its provisions.

title: THE DELHI POLICE ACT, 1978
purpose: To amend and consolidate the law relating to the regulation of the police in the Union territory of Delhi.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi. It applies to the police force and various aspects of public order, security, and conduct within Delhi.

key_definitions.administrator: The Administrator of Delhi appointed under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.cattle: Includes elephants, camels, horses, asses, mules, sheep, goats and swine.
key_definitions.competent_authority: When used with reference to the exercise of any power or discharge of any duty, means the Commissioner of Police or any other police officer specially empowered in that behalf by the Central Government.
key_definitions.constable: A police officer of the lowest grade.
key_definitions.corporation: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi constituted under the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957.
key_definitions.delhi_police_or_police_force: The police force referred to in section 3 and includes all persons appointed as special police officers or additional police officers, and all other persons who exercise any police function in any part of Delhi.
key_definitions.eating_house: Any place to which the public are admitted and where any kind of food or drink is supplied for consumption on the premises, including refreshment rooms, boarding houses, coffee houses, or shops where food/drink is supplied for consumption on or near the premises. Excludes places of public entertainment.
key_definitions.municipality: The New Delhi Municipal Committee, the Cantonment Board, or any other municipal body (other than the Corporation) established by law in Delhi.
key_definitions.place: Includes any building, tent, booth, or other erection, whether permanent or temporary, and any area, whether enclosed or open.
key_definitions.place_of_public_amusement: Any place where music, singing, dancing, games, or any other amusement, diversion, or recreation is provided, to which the public is admitted either on payment or with the intention that money may be collected. Includes race courses, circuses, theatres, music halls, etc.
key_definitions.place_of_public_entertainment: A lodging house, boarding and lodging house, or residential hostel, and includes any eating house or other place in which liquor or intoxicating drug is supplied for consumption in or near such place (e.g., taverns, shops selling liquor/drugs).
key_definitions.police_officer: Any member of the Delhi police.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules.
key_definitions.public_place: Any place to which the public have access.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Delhi Police Act, 1978, specifies its territorial extent to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi, and states its commencement date as July 1, 1978.

Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'cattle', 'competent authority', 'constable', 'Corporation', 'Delhi', 'Delhi police', 'eating house', 'municipality', 'place', 'place of public amusement', 'place of public entertainment', 'police officer', 'prescribed', and 'public place'.

main_sections.section_title: One police force for the whole of Delhi
main_sections.description: Establishes a single police force for the entire Union territory of Delhi.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence of police force to vest in the Administrator
main_sections.description: Confers the overall superintendence of the Delhi police force upon the Administrator.
Outlines the structure and constitution of the Delhi police force.
Provides for the appointment and role of the Commissioner of Police.
Details the disciplinary powers of superior officers to impose punishments on police personnel.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make regulations for regulating traffic and for preservation of order in public places, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the police the authority to make regulations for traffic management and maintaining order in public spaces.

main_sections.section_title: Employment of additional police to keep peace
main_sections.description: Allows for the deployment of additional police force to maintain peace.

main_sections.section_title: Dispersal of gangs and bodies of persons
main_sections.description: Empowers the police to disperse unlawful gangs and bodies of persons.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of police officer to enforce provisions of the Act
main_sections.description: Mandates that every police officer is responsible for enforcing the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Police to take charge of unclaimed property
main_sections.description: Specifies the duty of the police to take charge of any property that is unclaimed.

main_sections.section_title: Disregarding the rules of the road
main_sections.description: Defines an offense related to disregarding traffic rules.

main_sections.section_title: Penalties for offences under sections 80 to 96
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various offenses related to public order and nuisance detailed in preceding sections.
Grants the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings provisions.

important_rules: Police officers are deemed to be always on duty and liable for employment anywhere in Delhi (Section 24).
Police have the power to make regulations for regulating traffic and preserving order in public places (Section 28).
Police can prohibit certain acts for the prevention of disorder (Section 30).
Police must provide against disorder at places of public amusement or assembly (Section 31).
Police have powers to take special measures to prevent the outbreak of epidemic diseases at fairs (Section 35).
Police officers have the duty to enforce the provisions of the Act (Section 59).
Police officers are required to comply with the reasonable directions of superior police officers (Section 65).
Police must take charge of unclaimed property (Section 66).
Offenses like disregarding rules of the road, causing obstruction, and behaving indecently in public are penalized (Sections 80-96).
Police officers are not liable for acts done in good faith in pursuance of duty (Section 138).

penalties: Penalties for various offenses including disregarding rules of the road, causing obstruction, public nuisance, indecent behavior, and contravention of police orders and regulations (Sections 97-126). Specific penalties are detailed within these sections and chapter X.
Penalty for failure to deliver up certificate of appointment or other articles upon ceasing to be a police officer (Section 123).
Penalty for vexatious entry, search, arrest, etc., by a police officer (Section 124).
Penalty for vexatious delay in forwarding a person arrested (Section 125).
Penalty for unauthorized use of police uniforms (Section 126).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Delhi Police, under the superintendence of the Administrator. Specific powers are vested in the Commissioner of Police and other superior police officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through police investigation, apprehension of offenders, imposition of penalties, and implementation of regulations and orders issued under the Act. Enforcement includes powers of search, arrest, and taking charge of property. The Act also outlines procedures for appeals and the finality of certain orders.

rights: Right to appeal from orders of punishment (Section 23).
Right to be heard before certain orders (e.g., removal of persons) are passed (Section 50).
Right to appeal against orders of removal (Section 51).
Right to seek to annul, reverse, or alter any rule or order (Section 145).
Police officers are protected from liability for acts done in good faith in pursuance of duty (Section 138).
Public servants are protected for giving effect in good faith to rules, regulations, orders, or directions issued with apparent authority (Section 139).
duties: Duty of police officers to enforce the provisions of the Act (Section 59).
Other duties of a police officer as prescribed or implied by the Act (Section 60).
Duty to comply with reasonable directions of police officers (Section 65).
Duty of police to take charge of unclaimed property (Section 66).
Duty to deliver certificates, arms, etc., upon ceasing to be a police officer (Section 26).
obligations: Obligation to vacate premises provided for police officers when no longer entitled (Section 27).
Obligation to comply with orders and directions issued by the police under the Act, including orders for dispersal, removal, or prohibition of acts (Sections 30, 33, 46, 47, 48, 65).
Obligation to provide satisfactory account of possession of property (Section 103).
Obligation to report to police possession or tender of property suspected to be stolen (Section 104).

key_procedures: Procedure for awarding punishments to police officers (Section 22).
Procedure for disposal of unclaimed property (Section 67).
Procedure on failure of a person to leave an area or re-entry after removal (Section 53).
Procedure for taking measurements and photographs of persons against whom certain orders are made (Section 55).
Summary disposal of certain cases (Section 129).
Method of proving orders and notifications (Section 133).
administration: The Act is administered by the Delhi Police, with overall superintendence vested in the Administrator of Delhi. The Commissioner of Police plays a significant role in its implementation.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on July 1, 1978 (Section 1(3)).
Special police officers and additional police officers are included within the definition of 'Delhi police' or 'police force' (Section 2(g)).
The Act aims to consolidate and amend existing laws relating to the Delhi Police.
Certain sections provide for the exercise of powers under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, by Delhi Police officers (Chapter VIII).
The Act includes provisions for the use of police powers in relation to offenses under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 (Chapter IX).
The police force functioning in Delhi immediately before the commencement of this Act is deemed to be the police force constituted under this Act (Section 150).
The Act includes repeal and saving provisions, indicating that previous laws on the subject are superseded, with certain savings (Section 152).

title: The Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978
purpose: To ban the promotion or conduct of prize chits and money circulation schemes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Covers prize chits and money circulation schemes that are not conventional chits, with specific exceptions for certain government-backed or regulated financial institutions.

key_definitions.conventional_chit: A transaction where a person responsible for its conduct agrees with specified individuals to subscribe a sum of money or grain by installments, with each subscriber entitled to a prize amount determined by lot, auction, or tender. The 'prize amount' is what remains after deducting commission and sums foregone by a subscriber.
key_definitions.money: Includes cheques, postal orders, demand drafts, telegraphic transfers, or money orders.
key_definitions.money_circulation_scheme: Any scheme, regardless of its name, designed for making quick or easy money, or for receiving money or valuable things in exchange for a promise to pay money, contingent on the enrolment of members. The money or thing received may originate from member entrance fees or periodical subscriptions.
key_definitions.prescribed: As defined by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prize_chit: Includes any transaction or arrangement where a person collects money, in lump sum or installments, as contributions, subscriptions, membership/admission fees, or service charges for savings, mutual benefit, thrift, or similar schemes. The collected money is then used to give prizes or gifts to subscribers, or to refund subscriptions to non-winners. It specifically excludes conventional chits.
key_definitions.reserve_bank: The Reserve Bank of India constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent (whole of India).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'conventional chit', 'money', 'money circulation scheme', 'prescribed', 'prize chit', and 'Reserve Bank'.

main_sections.section_title: Banning of prize chits and money circulation schemes or enrolment as members or participation therein
main_sections.description: Prohibits the promotion or conduct of any prize chit or money circulation scheme, as well as enrolling as a member, participating in, or receiving or remitting money in pursuance of such schemes.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravening the provisions of section 3
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravening Section 3, including imprisonment and fines, with minimum terms and amounts specified.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for other offences in connection with prize chits or money circulation schemes
main_sections.description: Details penalties for various actions related to promoting or conducting prize chits or money circulation schemes in contravention of the Act, such as printing/publishing tickets, selling/distributing documents, advertising schemes, or using premises for such purposes.

Establishes liability for offences committed by companies, holding individuals in charge responsible, and also holding directors or officers liable if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter, search and seize
main_sections.description: Grants police officers and authorized government officers the power to enter, search, seize, and take custody of persons and things connected with prize chits or money circulation schemes that contravene the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Forfeiture of newspaper and publication containing prize chit or money circulation scheme
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to declare forfeited any newspaper or publication containing material related to illegal prize chits or money circulation schemes.
Specifies that only Chief Metropolitan Magistrates or Chief Judicial Magistrates can try offences under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Offences under this Act to be cognizable
main_sections.description: Declares all offences punishable under this Act as cognizable.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain prize chits or money circulation schemes
main_sections.description: Lists exceptions to the Act's application, including schemes promoted by State Governments, state-owned companies, certain banking institutions, and notified charitable or educational institutions.

Allows existing prize chit or money circulation schemes to continue for a winding-up period (not exceeding two years) under certain conditions, including reporting and submitting a winding-up plan. It also allows for extensions with consultation from the Reserve Bank.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules under this Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: No person shall promote or conduct any prize chit or money circulation scheme.
No person shall enroll as a member to any such chit or scheme, or participate in it otherwise.
No person shall receive or remit any money in pursuance of such a chit or scheme.
Actions such as printing, publishing, selling, distributing, or advertising prize chits or money circulation schemes are prohibited and punishable.
Companies committing offences are liable, and individuals in charge or consenting to the offence are also held responsible.
Certain entities like State Governments, state-owned companies, specified banking institutions, and notified charitable/educational institutions are exempt from the Act's provisions.

penalties: Contravention of Section 3: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. Minimum imprisonment of one year and fine of one thousand rupees, unless special reasons are recorded.

Other offences under Section 5: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to three thousand rupees, or both. Minimum imprisonment of one year and fine of one thousand rupees, unless special reasons are recorded.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers (not below the rank of officer in charge of a police station) and officers authorized by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers to enter, search, seize, and take custody of persons and evidence. Searches are conducted according to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. State Governments can also declare forfeited newspapers and publications containing illegal scheme information. Offences are cognizable and tried by Chief Metropolitan or Judicial Magistrates.

rights: Right to conduct conventional chits (not covered by this Act).
Right for certain financial institutions and government bodies to conduct specific schemes as per Section 11.
Right for persons conducting existing schemes at commencement to wind them up within a specified period (Section 12).
duties: Duty not to promote or conduct prize chits or money circulation schemes.
Duty not to enroll as a member or participate in such schemes.
Duty not to receive or remit money in pursuance of such schemes.
Duty for companies and their officers to ensure compliance and prevent offences.
obligations: Obligation for those conducting existing schemes to report and submit a winding-up plan within the transitional period.
Obligation for police and authorized officers to enforce the Act, including searching and seizing illegal materials and apprehending offenders.

key_procedures: Investigation and enforcement by police and authorized officers, including entering premises, searching persons and places, seizing items, and taking persons into custody.
Forfeiture of publications containing illegal scheme information by the State Government.
Trial of offences by designated Magistrates (Chief Metropolitan/Judicial Magistrate).
Winding up of existing schemes within a specified transitional period, including reporting and plan submission to the State Government and Reserve Bank.
Application to the State Government for extension of the winding-up period, with consultation from the Reserve Bank.
administration: State Governments and authorized officers, with oversight and consultation from the Reserve Bank in certain matters (e.g., transitional provisions).
important_notes: The Act explicitly excludes 'conventional chits' from its definition of 'prize chit'.
The Act was extended to the whole of India, with the exception of Jammu and Kashmir being omitted by a later amendment.
Transitional provisions allow for the orderly winding up of existing schemes, with potential extensions under specific conditions.

title: The Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979
purpose: To provide for the alteration of boundaries of the States of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the States of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, specifically concerning the alteration of their boundaries. It also covers the representation in legislatures, High Courts, authorization of expenditure, apportionment of assets and liabilities, and legal and miscellaneous provisions related to these boundary changes.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The day appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.assembly_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.council_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.fixed_boundaries: The boundaries demarcated under the provisions of section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, Ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or in any part of the State of Haryana or Uttar Pradesh.
key_definitions.notified_order: An order published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.present_deep_stream_line: The deep stream line of the river Yamuna as verified and determined by the Survey of India during November, December 1974, January 1975, and February 1975.
key_definitions.sitting_member: A person who immediately before the appointed day is a member of either House of Parliament or of the Legislature of a State.
key_definitions.transferred_territories: In relation to Haryana, territories transferred from Haryana to Uttar Pradesh; in relation to Uttar Pradesh, territories transferred from Uttar Pradesh to Haryana.
key_definitions.district: Shall be construed as a reference to the area physically comprised within that district immediately before the appointed day.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'law', 'transferred territories', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Replacement of fluctuating boundaries by fixed boundaries
main_sections.description: Provides for the alteration and replacement of the fluctuating boundaries of the Yamuna river between specific districts of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh with fixed boundaries, to be demarcated by an authority appointed by the Central Government. It also details the process of demarcation, including the finality of the authority's decisions and the preparation of maps.

Specifies that as from the appointed day, territories lying on the Haryana side of the fixed boundaries will be added to Haryana, and territories lying on the Uttar Pradesh side of the fixed boundaries will be added to Uttar Pradesh. It also mandates State Governments to provide for the administration of these transferred territories.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution by substituting the entries for Uttar Pradesh and Haryana to reflect the territorial changes brought about by this Act.

Deals with the construction of delimitation orders for parliamentary, assembly, and council constituencies, ensuring they are construed to include or exclude territories based on the boundary alterations effected by this Act.

Ensures that sitting members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies/Councils representing constituencies whose extent has been altered by this Act are deemed to have been elected by those constituencies as altered.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, High Court of Punjab and Haryana
main_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court of Punjab and Haryana to territories transferred from Uttar Pradesh to Haryana and provides for the transfer of pending proceedings from the High Court at Allahabad to the High Court of Punjab and Haryana. It also outlines provisions for advocates and orders made by the Allahabad High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, High Court at Allahabad
main_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court at Allahabad to territories transferred from Haryana to Uttar Pradesh and provides for the transfer of pending proceedings from the High Court of Punjab and Haryana to the High Court at Allahabad. It also contains provisions for advocates and orders made by the Punjab and Haryana High Court.
Provides for the interpretation of any doubt or difficulty arising in the application of Part IV (High Courts).

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in transferred territories under existing appropriation Acts
main_sections.description: Concerns the appropriation of moneys for expenditure in the transferred territories under existing appropriation Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Reports relating to accounts of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh
main_sections.description: Relates to reports concerning the accounts of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.
Deals with the apportionment of land and goods between the two states.
Addresses the apportionment of arrears of taxes.

main_sections.section_title: Right to recover loans and advances
main_sections.description: Concerns the right to recover loans and advances.

main_sections.section_title: Refund of taxes collected in excess
main_sections.description: Deals with the refund of taxes collected in excess.
Concerns the apportionment of deposits.
Deals with the apportionment of contracts.

main_sections.section_title: Liability in respect of actionable wrong
main_sections.description: Addresses liability in respect of actionable wrongs.

main_sections.section_title: Liability as guarantor of co-operative societies
main_sections.description: Concerns liability as a guarantor of co-operative societies.
Deals with the apportionment of items in suspense.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of assets or liabilities by agreement
main_sections.description: Provides for the apportionment of assets or liabilities by agreement between the states.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to order allocation or adjustment in certain cases
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to order allocation or adjustment of assets and liabilities in certain specified cases.

main_sections.section_title: Expenditure to be charged on the Consolidated Fund
main_sections.description: Specifies that certain expenditures shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

main_sections.section_title: State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards
main_sections.description: Deals with provisions related to State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards in the context of altered boundaries.
Determines the territorial extent of laws applicable to the states after the boundary alteration.
Grants the power to adapt existing laws to give effect to the provisions of this Act.
Provides the power to construe laws in a manner consistent with the provisions of this Act.
Makes provisions for legal proceedings that are pending or may arise as a result of the boundary alterations.
Provides for the transfer of pending proceedings consequent upon the alteration of boundaries.
Deals with the construction of boundary pillars and other related infrastructure.

main_sections.section_title: Validity of demarcation done before commencement of Act
main_sections.description: Addresses the validity of any demarcation done before the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of provisions inconsistent with other laws
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law.
Empowers the Central Government to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

important_rules: The boundary between specific districts of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, currently defined by the deep stream of the Yamuna river, shall be replaced by fixed boundaries as described in the Schedule (Section 3(1)).

The fixed boundaries shall be demarcated by an authority appointed by the Central Government, generally in conformity with the Schedule, with the authority's decisions being final on interpretation and location of boundary pillars (Section 3(2), 3(3)).
As from the appointed day, territories transferred to a state shall be included in its respective constituencies, districts, sub-divisions, or police stations (Section 6).

Sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures representing constituencies affected by the boundary alteration shall continue to be deemed elected by those constituencies as altered (Section 7).
Proceedings pending in one High Court due to boundary changes may be transferred to the other High Court based on specific criteria and certification (Sections 8(2), 9(2)).

Assets and liabilities of the erstwhile states shall be apportioned between Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, with the Central Government having the power to order allocation or adjustment in certain cases (Part VI, Section 24).
The Central Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 36).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, and specifically appointed demarcation authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the demarcation of fixed boundaries, transfer of territories, amendments to constitutional schedules, adjustments in legislative representation, transfer of High Court proceedings, and apportionment of assets and liabilities. The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties and make rules for enforcement.

rights: Right of advocates to practice in the respective High Courts after transfer of jurisdiction (Sections 8(5), 9(5)).
Right to recover loans and advances (Section 16).
Right to claim refund of taxes collected in excess (Section 17).
duties: Duty of State Governments to provide for the administration of transferred territories (Section 4(2)).
Duty of State Governments to be responsible for the construction and maintenance of boundary pillars (Section 3(3)(b)).
Duty to follow the provisions of the Act notwithstanding inconsistencies with other laws (Section 34).
obligations: Obligation to accept the fixed boundaries as demarcated (Section 3(3)(a)).
Obligation to ensure that constituencies are construed to include or exclude territories as per the Act (Section 6).
Obligation to apportion assets and liabilities as per the Act or agreements (Part VI).

key_procedures: Demarcation of fixed boundaries by a Central Government-appointed authority, including preparation of maps and specifying responsibilities for boundary pillars (Section 3).
Transfer of territories from one state to another based on the fixed boundaries (Section 4(1)).
State Governments issuing orders for the administration of transferred territories (Section 4(2)).
Transfer of pending proceedings in High Courts based on certification and cause of action (Sections 8(2), 9(2)).
Apportionment of assets and liabilities, with the Central Government having the power to order allocation or adjustment (Sections 14-24, Section 24).
Removal of difficulties by the Central Government (Section 35).
Making of rules by the Central Government (Section 36).
administration: Central Government and State Governments of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.
important_notes: The Act significantly alters the geographical boundaries of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, impacting their constitutional status, legislative representation, judicial jurisdiction, and the distribution of assets and liabilities.
The 'appointed day' is crucial, as most of the Act's provisions come into effect from that date, which is to be notified by the Central Government.
The Schedule, which describes the fixed boundaries, is an integral part of the Act, though its content is not provided in the given text.

title: The Prevention of Blackmarketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Act, 1980
purpose: To provide for detention in certain cases for the purpose of preventing black marketing and maintaining supplies of commodities essential to the community, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It concerns actions prejudicial to the maintenance of supplies of essential commodities, including offenses under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, or similar laws, and dealing in essential commodities with a view to making unlawful gains.

key_definitions.appropriate Government: As respects a detention order made by the Central Government or its officer, it's the Central Government. As respects a detention order made by a State Government or its officer, it's the State Government. For Union territories, the administrator is the appropriate Government.
key_definitions.detention order: An order made under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.State Government: In relation to a Union territory, it means the administrator thereof.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on October 15, 1979).
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'detention order', and 'State Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons
main_sections.description: Grants the Central or State Government, or their empowered officers, the power to issue detention orders for persons acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of essential supplies. Defines 'acting in any manner prejudicial' to include instigating offenses under the Essential Commodities Act or dealing in essential commodities for gain that defeats the law. Also empowers District Magistrates and Commissioners of Police to make such orders.
Specifies that detention orders can be executed anywhere in India as per the procedures for executing arrest warrants under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate place and conditions of detention
main_sections.description: Outlines the authority of the appropriate Government to specify the place and conditions of detention, and to transfer detained persons between places of detention, with a proviso for inter-State transfers requiring consent.

main_sections.section_title: Detention orders not to be invalid or inoperative on certain grounds
main_sections.description: States that a detention order will not be invalid or inoperative if the person to be detained or the place of detention is outside the territorial jurisdiction of the issuing authority.

main_sections.section_title: Powers in relation to absconding persons
main_sections.description: Details measures for dealing with persons against whom detention orders have been made but who have absconded or are concealing themselves. This includes reporting to magistrates and directing appearance, with penalties for non-compliance.

main_sections.section_title: Grounds of order of detention to be disclosed to person affected by the order
main_sections.description: Mandates that the grounds for detention must be communicated to the detained person as soon as possible (ordinarily within five days, exceptionally within ten days) and an opportunity for representation must be provided. However, facts against public interest need not be disclosed.

Requires the Central and State Governments to constitute Advisory Boards comprising persons qualified as High Court Judges. One member, who is or has been a High Court Judge, is appointed as Chairman.
Specifies that detention orders must be referred to the Advisory Board within three weeks of detention, along with grounds and any representation made by the detainee.

Outlines the procedure for Advisory Boards, including considering materials, seeking further information, hearing the concerned person if necessary, and submitting a report within seven weeks. The report must state whether there is sufficient cause for detention. Legal practitioners are not permitted, and proceedings are confidential except for the opinion part.

main_sections.section_title: Action upon the report of Advisory Board
main_sections.description: Describes the actions the appropriate Government must take based on the Advisory Board's report: confirm detention if sufficient cause is found, or revoke the order and release the person if no sufficient cause is found.
Sets the maximum period of detention at six months from the date of detention, for orders confirmed under section 12, without prejudice to the government's power to revoke or modify earlier.

Allows for the revocation or modification of detention orders at any time by the respective governments. It also clarifies that revocation or expiry does not prevent a fresh detention order if new facts arise.

Empowers the appropriate Government to grant temporary release to detained persons for a specified period, with or without conditions, and to cancel such release. It also allows for requiring a bond for observance of conditions.

important_rules: A detention order can be made if the appropriate government is satisfied that it is necessary to prevent a person from acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of essential supplies.
Detained persons must be informed of the grounds for their detention and given an opportunity to make a representation against the order.
Detention orders must be referred to an Advisory Board for review within three weeks of detention.
Detention orders are subject to a maximum period of six months if confirmed by the Advisory Board.
Detained persons can be temporarily released under specified conditions.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine or with both for failing to comply with a direction to appear before an officer as notified in the Official Gazette (under section 7(1)(b)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, empowered officers of Central and State Governments, District Magistrates, Commissioners of Police.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through detention orders, execution of these orders, regulation of detention conditions, actions against absconding persons, and review by Advisory Boards.

rights: Right to be informed of the grounds of detention.
Right to make a representation against the detention order.
Right to be heard by the Advisory Board if the person concerned desires it (subject to confidentiality).
duties: Duty to comply with detention orders.
Duty to appear before specified officers if directed.
Duty to comply with conditions of temporary release and surrender at the required time and place.
obligations: Obligation on the government to provide grounds for detention and opportunity for representation.
Obligation on the government to refer cases to the Advisory Board.
Obligation on the Advisory Board to report on the sufficiency of cause for detention.

key_procedures: Issuance of a detention order by authorized authorities based on satisfaction of prejudicial activity.
Execution of the detention order.
Communication of grounds of detention to the detainee and providing an opportunity for representation within specified timelines.
Reference of the detention order, grounds, and representation to an Advisory Board within three weeks.
Advisory Board's review of the case, potentially including hearing the detainee, and submission of a report within seven weeks.
Government's action on the Advisory Board's report (confirmation or revocation of detention).
Detention for a maximum period of six months if confirmed.
Temporary release of detained persons with or without conditions.
administration: Central Government and State Governments (and Administrators of Union Territories).
important_notes: The Act was extended to the whole of India, with an omission regarding the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now UT of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh) effective from October 31, 2019.
Disclosure of facts against public interest is not required when communicating grounds of detention.
Detained persons cannot appear through a legal practitioner before the Advisory Board.
Proceedings of the Advisory Board are confidential, except for its opinion.

title: The National Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of Messrs. National Company Limited to ensure their proper management for the benefit of the general public by continuing the manufacture, production, and distribution of jute-based articles essential to the Indian economy.
scope: This act applies to the undertakings of Messrs. National Company Limited and their associated assets, rights, and liabilities. It also covers employees and financial matters related to these undertakings. The geographical scope extends to undertakings within and outside India, as indicated in Section 4(1).

key_definitions.appointed day: The 27th day of April, 1980.
key_definitions.Company: Messrs. National Company Limited, registered at 18A-Brabourne Road, Calcutta-700001, West Bengal.
key_definitions.existing Government company: A Government company carrying on business on the appointed day.
key_definitions.new Government company: A Government company formed and registered on or after the appointed day.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and the dates on which its provisions come into force. Sections 29 and 30 are effective immediately, while other provisions are deemed to have come into force on April 27, 1980.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'Company', 'existing Government company', 'new Government company', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'specified date', and references to definitions in the Companies Act, 1956.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the Company
main_sections.description: Declares that on the appointed day, the undertakings of the Company and the Company's right, title, and interest in them are transferred to and vested in the Central Government.

Details the comprehensive nature of the vesting, including all assets, rights, powers, and privileges. It also addresses the discharge of properties from trusts, mortgages, and other incumbrances, the continuation of existing licenses and instruments, and the non-abatement of pending suits or proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the Company in an existing Government company
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct, by notification, that the undertakings vested in it shall instead vest in an existing Government company on a specified date.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of undertakings of the Company from an existing Government company to a new Government company
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to declare the transfer of undertakings from an existing Government company to a newly formed Government company.

main_sections.section_title: Company to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: States that liabilities of the Company for the period prior to the appointed day remain the liability of the Company and are not enforceable against the Central Government or any vested Government company, unless expressly provided otherwise.
Specifies that an amount of ten crores and four lakhs of rupees shall be paid by the Central Government to the Company in cash for the transfer and vesting of its undertakings.
This section likely outlines the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act.
This section likely deals with offenses committed by companies in relation to the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Authorizes the Central Government to make provisions to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws and includes provisions for saving certain actions or proceedings.

important_rules: Rule: All assets, rights, powers, and privileges of the Company's undertakings vest in the Central Government on the appointed day (Section 3 & 4).
Rule: Properties vested in the Central Government are discharged from any trusts, mortgages, charges, liens, and incumbrances (Section 4(2)).
Rule: Existing licenses and instruments remain in force and are deemed to be granted to the succeeding Government company (Section 4(5)).
Rule: Pending suits, appeals, or other proceedings do not abate and can be continued by or against the Central Government or the relevant Government company (Section 4(6)).
Rule: The Company remains liable for its prior liabilities up to the appointed day, not the Central Government or any acquiring Government company (Section 7).
Rule: An amount of rupees ten crores and four lakhs is to be paid by the Central Government to the Company for the transfer of its undertakings (Section 8(1)).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 29).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and potentially appointed authorities like the Commissioner of Payments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal provisions outlined in the Act, including penalties for offenses and the management of financial claims and disbursements.

rights: Right of the Central Government to acquire and transfer undertakings.
Right of mortgagees and lien holders to claim payment from specified amounts (Section 4(4)).
Right of employees to continue in service under the acquiring Government company (implied by Chapter V).
duties: Duty of persons in charge of management to deliver all assets, etc., to the acquiring entity (Section 11).
Duty of persons to account for assets in their possession (Section 12).
Duty of mortgagees and lien holders to intimate their interest to the Commissioner of Payments (Section 4(3)).
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to pay the specified amount for the undertakings.
Obligations of Government companies to comply with terms and conditions set by the Central Government.
Obligations related to the provident fund and other funds of employees (Section 14).

key_procedures: Procedure for the transfer and vesting of undertakings of the Company to the Central Government on the appointed day (Section 3).
Procedure for the Central Government to direct the vesting of these undertakings in an existing Government company via notification (Section 5).
Procedure for the transfer of undertakings from an existing Government company to a new Government company via declaration by the Central Government (Section 6).
Procedure for the appointment and functioning of the Commissioner of Payments for managing claims and disbursements (Sections 15-24).
Procedure for submitting claims to the Commissioner, examination, admission, rejection, and disbursement of amounts (Sections 18-23).
administration: Central Government, and potentially a Commissioner of Payments appointed under the Act.
important_notes: Note: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions supersede any conflicting laws (Section 25).
Note: Contracts entered into by the Company may cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or the Government company (Section 28).
Note: The management of undertakings vests in the Custodian until alternative arrangements are made (Section 27).

title: The Brahmaputra Board Act, 1980
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Board for the planning and integrated implementation of measures for the control of floods and bank erosion in the Brahmaputra Valley and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the Brahmaputra Valley, an inter-State river valley. The Central Government can demarcate the limits of this valley and specify areas within it where the Board performs its functions. It concerns the regulation and development of this river valley for public interest, specifically flood control, bank erosion, and drainage improvement.

key_definitions.Board: The Brahmaputra Board established under section 4.
key_definitions.Brahmaputra Valley: The inter-State Brahmaputra river valley as demarcated under section 11.
key_definitions.Fund: The Brahmaputra Board Fund constituted under section 19.
key_definitions.Master Plan: The Master Plan for the control of floods, bank erosion and improvement of drainage in the Brahmaputra Valley prepared under section 12.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Board under this Act.
key_definitions.rules: Rules made by the Central Government under this Act.
key_definitions.State Government: In relation to a Union territory, means the administrator thereof appointed under article 239 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Brahmaputra Board Act, 1980, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union
main_sections.description: Declares that it is in the public interest for the Central Government to control the regulation and development of the inter-State Brahmaputra river valley.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'Brahmaputra Valley', 'Fund', 'Master Plan', 'member', 'prescribed', 'regulations', 'rules', and 'State Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the Brahmaputra Board
main_sections.description: Establishes the Brahmaputra Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract. It also outlines the composition of the Board, including the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, General Manager, Financial Adviser, representatives from State Governments and Union Territories, and representatives from relevant Central Government Ministries and organizations.

Empowers the Central Government to demarcate the limits of the Brahmaputra Valley through notification and to specify areas within the valley where the Board shall perform its functions, after consulting the concerned State Governments.

main_sections.section_title: Master Plan for the control of floods, etc., in the Brahmaputra Valley
main_sections.description: Mandates the Board to carry out surveys and investigations to prepare a Master Plan for flood control, bank erosion, and drainage improvement in the Brahmaputra Valley. The plan can be prepared in parts and revised. It also requires consideration of water resource development for irrigation, hydro power, navigation, and other beneficial purposes. The Master Plan is submitted to the Central Government for approval, with modifications after consulting State Governments.

Details additional functions of the Board, including preparing detailed reports and estimates for projects in the Master Plan, drawing up standards for construction and operation, constructing and operating multi-purpose dams and works with Central Government approval, and preparing phased construction programs for State Governments for other projects. It can also perform prescribed or supplemental functions.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions subject to which the Board may perform its functions
main_sections.description: Specifies conditions for the Board's functions, including State Governments making land available for construction, undertaking maintenance of projects, agreeing to provide assistance for construction, operation, and maintenance, and sharing costs and benefits as specified by the Central Government. If agreement on cost and benefit sharing cannot be reached, the matter is referred to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Directions and instructions by Central Government
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to give directions and instructions to the Board, which the Board is bound to follow.
Requires the Board to maintain proper accounts and that these accounts, along with the annual audit report, be presented to the Central Government and laid before Parliament.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Board to make regulations for carrying out its functions, subject to rules and the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that all rules and regulations made under the Act be laid before Parliament.

important_rules: The Central Government may appoint a date for the commencement of the Act.
The Central Government can declare the expediency of Union control over the Brahmaputra river valley.
The Brahmaputra Board is established as a corporate body with specific composition and appointment procedures.
The Board must prepare a Master Plan for flood control and bank erosion in the Brahmaputra Valley.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Board.
The Board must maintain accounts and its annual report is subject to audit and parliamentary review.
Rules made by the Central Government and regulations made by the Board must be laid before Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (via directions and oversight), Brahmaputra Board (for its functions and operations).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the Central Government's power to issue directions, approve plans and projects, and by the Board's mandate to implement the Master Plan and perform its functions as prescribed and regulated. Enforcement of conditions for State Government cooperation is also a mechanism.

rights: The Board has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The Board has the power to contract.
The Board can sue and be sued in its own name.
Officers deputed by the Central Government have the right to attend Board meetings and participate in proceedings (without voting rights).
Persons associated with the Board for assistance or advice have the right to participate in relevant discussions (without voting rights).
duties: The Board has the duty to prepare a Master Plan for flood control, bank erosion, and drainage improvement.
The Board has the duty to prepare detailed reports and estimates for projects.
The Board has the duty to draw up standards and specifications for construction, operation, and maintenance.
The Board has the duty to construct, maintain, and operate dams and works as approved.
The Board has the duty to consult State Governments where required.
The Board must abide by directions and instructions from the Central Government.
The Board must maintain proper accounts and prepare an annual report.
obligations: The Board is obligated to obtain approval from the Central Government for certain construction and operational activities.

The Board is obligated to adhere to conditions set by the Central Government for performing its functions, including those related to land acquisition, cost sharing, and maintenance by State Governments.
The Board is obligated to submit its Master Plan for approval by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Board: The Central Government appoints a date for the Board's establishment via notification.
Demarcation of Brahmaputra Valley: The Central Government, by notification, demarcates the limits of the Brahmaputra Valley.

Preparation and approval of Master Plan: The Board surveys and investigates, prepares a Master Plan (possibly in parts), submits it to the Central Government, which approves it after consulting State Governments.

Construction of projects: The Board constructs multi-purpose dams and works with Central Government approval. For other projects, it prepares a phased program for State Governments, but can undertake construction with prior Central Government approval if satisfied.

Consultation with State Governments: The Central Government must consult State Governments before specifying areas for the Board's functions and before approving the Master Plan. The Board also consults State Governments for phased programs and conditions related to project execution.
Dispute resolution: Disputes between the Board and State Governments are referred to the Central Government if they cannot agree on cost and benefit sharing of projects.
administration: Central Government (overall control, rule-making, approval), Brahmaputra Board (implementation, planning, regulation-making).
important_notes: The Act came into force on December 1, 1981.
The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Board's functions are subject to conditions, including cooperation and financial/land contributions from State Governments.
The Central Government can override State Government agreements on cost and benefit sharing by referring the matter to itself if no agreement is reached.
Members and employees of the Board are considered public servants.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

title: The Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Trivandrum Act, 1980
purpose: To declare the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society for Advanced Studies in Specialities, Trivandrum, as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the institution known as the Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Trivandrum, located in the State of Kerala. It governs the incorporation, composition, functions, and administration of the institute.

key_definitions.Chairman: The Chairman of the Governing Body.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Institute.
key_definitions.Governing Body: The Governing Body of the Institute.
key_definitions.Institute: The institution known as the Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Trivandrum, incorporated under this Act.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Institute.
key_definitions.regulation: A regulation made by the Institute.
key_definitions.rule: A rule made by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and the procedure for its commencement, which is upon notification by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society for Advanced Studies in Specialities, Trivandrum, as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society for Advanced Studies in Specialities, Trivandrum, as an institution of national importance due to its objectives.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as Chairman, Director, Fund, Governing Body, Institute, member, President, regulation, and rule.

Constitutes the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society as a body corporate named Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Trivandrum, granting it perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire property and contract.
Details the composition of the Institute, listing ex officio members, nominated members by the Central and State Governments, scientists, and Members of Parliament.
Outlines the primary objectives of the Institute, including promoting biomedical engineering and technology, providing high standards of patient care, and developing post-graduate training programs.

Specifies the functions the Institute may undertake to achieve its objects, such as providing post-graduate teaching and research facilities, establishing hospitals and research centers, conducting examinations, and receiving grants.
Establishes a Fund for the Institute, detailing its sources of income (government funds, fees, grants, donations) and its application towards the Institute's expenses.
Requires the Institute to maintain proper accounts and records and prepare an annual statement of accounts, which is subject to audit.
Indicates that the Central Government exercises control over the Institute.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the Institute the power to make regulations for its internal administration and functioning.

important_rules: The Central Government may, by notification, appoint the date of commencement of the Act.
The Central Government nominates members to represent various departments and scientific fields.
The Central Government may pay sums of money to the Institute for its functioning.
The Institute shall prepare an annual budget showing estimated receipts and expenditure.
The Central Government exercises control over the Institute and can resolve disputes.
Rules made by the Central Government and regulations made by the Institute are to be laid before Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Institute, Governing Body
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules and regulations, government oversight, and provisions for dispute resolution.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right to contract.
Right to sue and be sued.
Right to receive grants and donations.
Right to demand and receive fees and charges.
Right to hold examinations and grant degrees, diplomas, and distinctions.
Right to institute and appoint persons to academic posts.
Right to establish and maintain hospitals and research centers.
duties: Duty to promote biomedical engineering and technology.
Duty to provide high standards of patient care.
Duty to develop post-graduate training programs.
Duty to provide post-graduate teaching and facilities for research.
Duty to prepare and present an annual budget and report.
Duty to maintain proper accounts and undergo audit.
obligations: Obligation to act in accordance with the Act, rules, and regulations.
Obligation to adhere to the prescribed procedure for meetings and business transactions.
Obligation to ensure that the Governing Body's membership does not exceed one-third non-members of the Institute.
Obligation to manage the Institute's Fund for its expenses.

key_procedures: Procedure for the incorporation of the Institute under the name Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Trivandrum.
Procedure for the composition of the Institute, including nomination and election of members.
Procedure for the term of office and filling of vacancies among members.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Governing Body and other committees.
Procedure for the appointment of the Director and other officers and employees.
Procedure for the preparation and submission of the Institute's budget.
Procedure for maintaining accounts and undergoing audit.
Procedure for the preparation and submission of the Institute's annual report.
administration: The Central Government exercises overall control and makes rules, while the Institute, through its Governing Body and Director, manages its day-to-day operations.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act is to be notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette.
Existing employees' services are subject to transfer as per the Act.
Facilities at the Institute are to be continued.
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

title: THE HOTEL-RECEIPTS TAX ACT, 1980
purpose: To impose a special tax on gross receipts of certain hotels.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Specifically targets hotels where room charges for residential accommodation are seventy-five rupees or more per day per individual. Also applies to entities closely connected to hotels if arrangements are made to avoid tax liability.

key_definitions.assessee: A person by whom hotel-receipts tax or any other sum of money is payable under this Act, and includes any person whose assessment or refund proceedings are underway or who is deemed to be an assessee in default.
key_definitions.assessment_year: The period of twelve months commencing on the 1st day of April every year.
key_definitions.chargeable_receipts: The total amount of all charges referred to in section 6, computed in the manner laid down in section 7.
key_definitions.hotel: Includes a building or part of a building where residential accommodation is, by way of business, provided for a monetary consideration.
key_definitions.hotel-receipts_tax: The tax chargeable under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.room_charges: Charges for residential accommodation in a hotel, including furniture, air-conditioner, etc., but excluding charges for food, drink, and other services not normally included in room rent.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Hotel-Receipts Tax Act, 1980, and states that it extends to the whole of India.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'assessee', 'assessment', 'assessment year', 'chargeable receipts', 'hotel', 'hotel-receipts tax', 'room charges', and 'Income-tax Act'.

Specifies that the Act applies to hotels where room charges are seventy-five rupees or more per day per individual. It also outlines how to determine room charges when composite charges are levied or when charges are understated.

Grants Income-tax Act authorities (Directors of Inspection, Commissioners, Income-tax Officers, etc.) the same powers and functions under this Act as they have under the Income-tax Act. It also outlines their adherence to Board orders.

Imposes a tax of fifteen per cent on the chargeable receipts of hotels for every assessment year commencing on or after April 1, 1981. It also provides a rebate for charges received in foreign exchange and addresses arrangements made to avoid tax liability.

Defines chargeable receipts as the total amount received or accrued in connection with residential accommodation, food, drink, and other services in a hotel, including taxes collected. It excludes receipts from persons covered by Vienna Conventions.
Outlines deductions allowed in computing chargeable receipts, such as bad debts, sales tax, entertainment tax, tax on luxuries, and the hotel-receipts tax itself. It prohibits any other deductions.

Mandates the furnishing of a return of chargeable receipts by hotel operators within a specified period. It also allows for notices to be issued by the Income-tax Officer for furnishing returns and for the submission of revised returns.
Requires assessees to pay the hotel-receipts tax before furnishing the return, with proof of payment accompanying the return.

important_rules: Rule 1: Hotels where room charges are Rs. 75 or more per day per individual are subject to this Act.
Rule 2: Composite charges for accommodation and food require room charges to be determined in a prescribed manner.
Rule 3: Income-tax Officers can determine room charges on a reasonable basis if they appear to be understated, especially in cases involving composite charges or perceived understatements.
Rule 4: The tax rate is 15% of chargeable receipts, with a reduction for charges received in foreign exchange.
Rule 5: Chargeable receipts include all charges for accommodation, food, drink, and services, as well as taxes collected by the hotel.
Rule 6: Deductions for computing chargeable receipts are limited to bad debts, sales tax, entertainment tax, luxury tax, and the hotel-receipts tax itself.
Rule 7: Returns of chargeable receipts must be filed within four months of the end of the previous year or by June 30th of the assessment year, whichever is later.
Rule 8: Assessees must pay the calculated hotel-receipts tax before filing their return.

penalties: Penalty for failure to furnish returns, comply with notices, or concealment of receipts (Section 15).
Penalty for false estimate of or failure to pay hotel-receipts tax payable in advance (Section 16).
Penalty for wilful attempt to evade tax (Section 26).
Penalty for failure to furnish returns of chargeable receipts (Section 27).
Penalty for failure to produce accounts and documents (Section 28).
Penalty for false statement in verification (Section 29).
Penalty for abetment of false return (Section 30).
Punishment for second and subsequent offences (Section 31).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tax authorities as defined under the Income-tax Act, including Directors of Inspection, Commissioners of Income-Tax, Inspecting Assistant Commissioners of Income-tax, Income-tax Officers, and Inspectors of Income-tax.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, reassessment, best judgment assessment, and specific penalties and punishments for non-compliance, evasion, and offences. Appeals processes are also established.

rights: Right to an opportunity of being heard before adverse orders (Section 17).
Right to appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals) (Section 18).
Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal (Section 19).
Right to apply for rectification of mistakes (Section 20).
