Right to claim hotel-receipts tax as a deduction in computing total income under the Income-tax Act (Section 21).
Right to seek revision of orders by the Commissioner (Section 23).
duties: Duty to furnish returns of chargeable receipts within the prescribed time (Section 8).
Duty to pay hotel-receipts tax before furnishing returns (Section 9).
Duty to comply with notices and requirements from tax authorities.
Duty to maintain accounts and produce them when required.
obligations: Obligation to pay hotel-receipts tax at the prescribed rate.
Obligation to ensure that arrangements are not made to avoid or reduce tax liability.
Obligation to cooperate with tax authorities during assessments and investigations.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment: Includes self-assessment, regular assessment, best judgment assessment, and reassessment.
Procedure for appeals: Assessees can appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals) and then to the Appellate Tribunal.
Procedure for rectification of mistakes: Assessees can apply for the correction of errors in orders.
Procedure for revision: Commissioners can revise orders prejudicial to the revenue or of an assessee.
Procedure for filing returns: Outlines the form, verification, and timelines for submitting returns of chargeable receipts.
administration: Central Board of Direct Taxes (Board) and various Income-tax authorities.
important_notes: The Act uses provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, where not specifically defined or contradicted.
Charges received in foreign exchange are subject to a reduction in tax payable.
Arrangements to avoid or reduce tax liability involving closely connected persons are covered.
Certain offences are non-cognizable.

title: THE JUTE COMPANIES (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1980
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of specified jute companies with the objective of ensuring their proper management to serve public interests by continuing the manufacture, production, and distribution of jute articles, which are essential for the national economy, and for related matters.
scope: This act applies to the undertakings of jute companies specified in the First Schedule. It covers the acquisition, transfer, management, and payment related to these undertakings and their employees. Geographically, it applies within India for the specified jute companies.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of Payments appointed under section 14.
key_definitions.jute companies: Companies defined in the Companies Act, 1956, and specified in the First Schedule.
key_definitions.Jute Manufactures Corporation: The National Jute Manufactures Corporation Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.specified date: A date that the Central Government may specify by notification for the purposes of a particular provision, with different dates allowed for different provisions.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Jute Companies (Nationalisation) Act, 1980.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'jute companies', 'Jute Manufactures Corporation', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'specified date'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the jute companies
main_sections.description: On the appointed day, the undertakings of every jute company and their associated rights, titles, and interests vest in the Central Government by virtue of this Act.

Details what the undertakings include (all assets, rights, properties, documents, etc.), clarifies that vested properties are freed from trusts and incumbrances, requires mortgagees and lien holders to inform the Commissioner, and clarifies their right to claim payment from the amounts to be given to the jute company, but not against the vested property. It also deals with the continuation of licenses and instruments and the continuation of pending suits or proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Jute companies to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: Specifies that liabilities of jute companies for periods prior to the appointed day are generally the company's own liability, except for loans advanced by Central or State Governments after management was taken over, which become the liability of the Central Government or the Jute Manufactures Corporation. It also clarifies that no other prior liabilities or post-appointed day awards related to pre-appointed day disputes are enforceable against the Central Government or the Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the jute companies in Jute Manufactures Corporation
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct, by notification, that the undertakings and specified liabilities, after vesting in the Central Government, shall instead vest in the Jute Manufactures Corporation, either on the notification date or another specified date not earlier than the appointed day. On such vesting, the Corporation becomes the owner, and the Central Government's rights and liabilities become those of the Corporation.
States that each jute company will be given a specific amount by the Central Government for the transfer and vesting of its undertakings, to be paid in cash as specified in Chapter VI.

Requires the Central Government to pay each jute company an additional amount of Rs. 10,000 per annum for the period from when its management was taken over until the appointed day. It also specifies that all amounts will carry simple interest at 4% per annum from the appointed day until payment. These additional amounts are paid on top of the amounts specified in the First Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Management, etc., of the undertakings of the jute companies
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government general superintendence, direction, control, and management of the affairs and business of the undertakings of jute companies whose rights, titles, and interests have vested in the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of persons in charge of management of the undertakings to deliver all assets, etc.
main_sections.description: Obligates all persons in charge of the management of the undertakings to deliver all assets, books of account, registers, and other documents to the Central Government or the Jute Manufactures Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of persons to account for assets, etc., in their possession
main_sections.description: Requires persons in possession of assets, books of account, registers, or other documents belonging to the undertakings to account for them to the Central Government or the Jute Manufactures Corporation.
Ensures that employees of the jute companies continue in service on the same terms and conditions of service as immediately before the appointed day, with continuity of service.
Deals with the transfer and continuation of provident fund and other funds for the employees of the jute companies.
Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner of Payments to disburse the amounts to the jute companies.

main_sections.section_title: Payment by Central Government to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Central Government shall pay the amounts to the Commissioner of Payments for disbursement.

main_sections.section_title: Certain powers of Central Government or Jute Manufactures Corporation
main_sections.description: Outlines certain powers that the Central Government or the Jute Manufactures Corporation may exercise in relation to the undertakings.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Requires all persons entitled to any claim against the jute companies or their undertakings to make such claims to the Commissioner of Payments.
Establishes the order of priority for the payment of claims by the Commissioner.
Details the process by which the Commissioner will examine the claims received.
Defines the procedure for the Commissioner to admit or reject claims.

main_sections.section_title: Disbursement of money by the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Commissioner to disburse money to the claimants.

main_sections.section_title: Disbursement of amounts to the jute companies
main_sections.description: Specifies how the remaining amounts are to be disbursed to the jute companies.

main_sections.section_title: Undisbursed or unclaimed amounts to be deposited with the general revenue account
main_sections.description: States that any amounts that remain undisbursed or unclaimed after a certain period shall be deposited into the general revenue account.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict.
Clarifies the assumption of liabilities by the Central Government or the Jute Manufactures Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Management to continue to vest in certain persons until alternative arrangements have been made
main_sections.description: Allows management to continue with certain persons until alternative arrangements are made.

main_sections.section_title: Contracts to cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or Jute Manufactures Corporation
main_sections.description: States that contracts entered into by jute companies will cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or the Jute Manufactures Corporation.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Deals with offenses committed by companies under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides the Central Government with the power to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: All undertakings of specified jute companies, along with their rights, titles, and interests, vest in the Central Government on the appointed day (Section 3).
Vested undertakings are freed from all trusts, obligations, mortgages, charges, liens, and incumbrances (Section 4(2)).
Mortgagees or persons with liens have the right to claim payment from the amounts given to the jute company, but not against the vested property (Section 4(4)).
Employees of jute companies continue in service on their existing terms and conditions of employment (Section 12).
All claims against jute companies must be made to the Commissioner of Payments (Section 17).
The Act has overriding effect over other laws in case of inconsistency (Section 24).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions are specified in Section 28.
Offences by companies are covered, with penalties applicable to the company and its officers (Section 29).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Jute Manufactures Corporation are the primary authorities for the enforcement of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the vesting of undertakings, the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments for claims and disbursements, the continuation of management under government control, and the application of penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Jute companies have the right to receive specified amounts and further amounts as compensation for the acquisition of their undertakings (Sections 7 and 8).
Employees have the right to continued employment on existing terms and conditions (Section 12).
Mortgagees and lien holders have the right to claim payment from the compensation amounts (Section 4(4)).
duties: Persons in charge of management have the duty to deliver all assets, books, and documents to the Central Government or the Corporation (Section 10).
Persons possessing assets or documents have the duty to account for them (Section 11).
obligations: Jute companies are liable for their prior liabilities, except for government loans taken after management takeover (Section 5).
Companies and individuals must comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Acquisition and Vesting: Undertakings of jute companies are transferred to and vest in the Central Government on the appointed day, and can subsequently be vested in the Jute Manufactures Corporation (Sections 3 and 6).

Payment of Compensation: Amounts due to jute companies are determined based on the First Schedule and further calculations, then paid through a Commissioner of Payments after claims are processed (Chapters III, VI).
Claims Management: All claims against the undertakings are submitted to the Commissioner, who examines, admits, or rejects them and disburses funds according to priority (Sections 14-23).
administration: The Central Government and the Jute Manufactures Corporation are responsible for the administration of this Act.
important_notes: The Act explicitly states that it has an overriding effect on other laws (Section 24).
Contracts entered into by jute companies may cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or the Jute Manufactures Corporation (Section 27).
The Central Government has powers to make rules and remove difficulties to ensure the effective implementation of the Act (Sections 32 and 33).

title: The National Security Act, 1980
purpose: To provide for preventive detention in certain cases and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to any person, including foreigners, whose detention is deemed necessary for national security, public order, or essential supplies and services.

key_definitions.appropriate Government: As respects a detention order made by the Central Government or a person detained under such order, the Central Government, and as respects a detention order made by a State Government or by an officer subordinate to a State Government or as respects a person detained under such order, the State Government.
key_definitions.foreigner: Has the same meaning as in the Foreigners Act, 1946 (31 of 1946).
key_definitions.State Government: In relation to a Union territory, means the administrator thereof.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'detention order', 'foreigner', 'person', and 'State Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government or the State Government the power to order the detention of individuals under specific circumstances related to national security, foreign relations, security of the State, public order, and essential supplies and services. It also empowers District Magistrates or Commissioners of Police to issue detention orders under delegated authority.
Specifies that detention orders can be executed at any place in India in the manner provided for the execution of warrants of arrest under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate place and conditions of detention
main_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to specify the place and conditions of detention, including provisions for maintenance, discipline, and removal from one detention place to another.

States that if a detention order is made on multiple grounds, it will not be deemed invalid if one or more grounds are found to be vague, non-existent, irrelevant, or otherwise invalid, provided there are remaining valid grounds.

main_sections.section_title: Detention orders not to be invalid or inoperative on certain grounds
main_sections.description: Clarifies that detention orders are not invalidated by the fact that the person to be detained or the place of detention is outside the territorial jurisdiction of the issuing authority.

main_sections.section_title: Powers in relation to absconding persons
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers of the government to deal with persons in respect of whom a detention order has been made but who have absconded or are concealing themselves. This includes reporting to magistrates and directing appearance, with penalties for non-compliance.

main_sections.section_title: Grounds of order of detention to be disclosed to persons affected by the order
main_sections.description: Mandates that the grounds for detention must be communicated to the detained person as soon as possible (ordinarily within five days, or exceptionally within fifteen days) and that they must be afforded an opportunity to make a representation, unless disclosure is against public interest.
Requires the Central and State Governments to constitute Advisory Boards consisting of persons qualified to be High Court judges for the purposes of the Act.

Specifies that detention orders must be referred to the constituted Advisory Board within three weeks of the detention, along with the grounds for detention and any representation made by the detainee.

Details the procedure of the Advisory Boards, including the consideration of materials, calling for information, hearing the person concerned, and submitting a report within seven weeks, specifying whether there is sufficient cause for detention.

main_sections.section_title: Action upon the report of the Advisory Board
main_sections.description: Dictates the action to be taken by the appropriate Government based on the Advisory Board's report: confirming detention if there is sufficient cause, or revoking the detention order and releasing the person if there is no sufficient cause.
Specifies the maximum period for which a person can be detained after a detention order has been confirmed.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any person in respect of whom a detention order has been made can be detained in such place and under such conditions as specified by the appropriate government.

Rule 2: A person detained under a detention order can be removed from one detention place to another by order of the appropriate government, with the consent of the other State Government if it involves inter-State transfer.

Rule 3: Grounds of detention must be communicated to the detained person as soon as possible (ordinarily within five days, or exceptionally within fifteen days) and the person must be given an opportunity to make a representation.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, for failing to comply with an order to appear if a person has absconded or is concealing themselves.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, and officers mentioned in sub-section (3) of section 3 (District Magistrates or Commissioners of Police).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of detention orders, execution of these orders, regulation of detention conditions, and actions against absconding persons. Advisory Boards review detention orders.

rights: Right to be informed of the grounds of detention (within a specified time frame).
Right to make a representation against the detention order.
Right to be heard by the Advisory Board if the Board considers it essential or if the person concerned desires it.
duties: Duty of the detaining authority to communicate the grounds of detention.
Duty of the detaining authority to afford an opportunity to make a representation.
Duty of the appropriate government to refer the detention order and representation to the Advisory Board.
Duty of the detainee to comply with lawful orders, including appearance orders if they have absconded.
obligations: Obligation of the appropriate Government to act upon the report of the Advisory Board.
Obligation to comply with the detention order and the conditions of detention.

key_procedures: Issuance of a detention order by the Central Government, State Government, or delegated officer if satisfied about the necessity of detention.
Execution of the detention order as per the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Communication of grounds of detention and an opportunity for representation to the detained person.
Reference of the detention order, grounds, and representation to an Advisory Board within three weeks.
Advisory Board's review of the case, including calling for information and potentially hearing the detainee.
Submission of the Advisory Board's report on whether sufficient cause exists for detention.
Action by the appropriate Government to confirm detention or revoke the order based on the Advisory Board's report.
administration: Central Government and State Governments.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1984 to introduce Section 5A regarding severability of grounds of detention and to modify time limits for communication of grounds.
The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted by Act 34 of 2019, indicating the Act now extends to the entire territory of India.

title: THE HIND CYCLES LIMITED AND SEN-RALEIGH LIMITED (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1980
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of the undertakings of Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited to ensure their proper management and continued manufacture, production, and distribution of bicycles, their component parts, and accessories, which are essential for the economy.
scope: Applies to the undertakings of Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited. It has national implications due to the essential nature of the manufactured goods for the country's economy.

key_definitions.appointed day: The 15th day of October, 1980.
key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of Payments appointed under section 15.
key_definitions.Custodian: The Custodian appointed to take over or carry on the management of the undertakings.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Sen-Raleigh Limited: Includes Sen and Pandit Industries Limited, Ancillary Industries (Lugs) Private Limited, Ancillary Industries (Forgings) Private Limited, Ancillary Industries (Cranks) Private Limited and Naokhali Machine Tools Limited.
key_definitions.specified date: Such date as the Central Government may, by notification, specify for the purposes of a particular provision.
key_definitions.two companies: Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on October 15, 1980.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'Custodian', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'Sen-Raleigh Limited', 'specified date', and 'two companies'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the two companies
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the undertakings of Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited, along with their rights and interests, shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government.

Details the implications of the vesting, including the inclusion of all assets, rights, properties (movable and immovable), and liabilities. It also clarifies that vested properties are freed from encumbrances and that existing legal proceedings will continue.

main_sections.section_title: Owners of the two Companies to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: Specifies that liabilities of the two companies prior to the appointed day (except for those arising from materials supplied after the government took over management) remain with the respective companies and are not transferred to the Central Government or any Government Company.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the two Companies in two Government Companies
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to direct, by notification, that the undertakings vested in it shall instead vest in two Government Companies, specifying the date of such vesting and the liabilities to be transferred.
States that an amount, as specified in the First Schedule, will be paid by the Central Government to each of the two companies for the transfer and vesting of their undertakings.
Provides for the payment of further amounts to each company, calculated at a rate specified in the Second Schedule, for the deprivation of their management.

main_sections.section_title: Management, etc., of the undertakings of the two companies
main_sections.description: Deals with the management of the undertakings after they vest in the Central Government or Government companies.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of persons in charge of management of the undertakings of the two companies to deliver all assets, etc.
main_sections.description: Obligates persons in charge of the management to deliver all assets and documents related to the undertakings.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of persons to account for assets, etc., in their possession
main_sections.description: Requires individuals to account for any assets or documents in their possession.
Mandates the maintenance of accounts and the conducting of audits for the undertakings.
Ensures the continuity of employment for the employees of the two companies.
Addresses the treatment of provident funds and other employee funds.
Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments.

main_sections.section_title: Payment by Central Government to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Details the process of payment from the Central Government to the Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Certain powers of Central Government or Government companies
main_sections.description: Outlines specific powers exercisable by the Central Government or Government companies.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Instructs that all claims against the undertakings must be made to the Commissioner.
Establishes the order of priority for settling claims.
Describes the process of examining claims submitted to the Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Admission or rejection of the claims
main_sections.description: Covers the decision-making process for admitting or rejecting claims.

main_sections.section_title: Disbursement of money by the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Details how the Commissioner will disburse the collected money.

main_sections.section_title: Disbursement of amounts to the two companies
main_sections.description: Specifies the disbursement of amounts to the respective companies.

main_sections.section_title: Undisbursed or unclaimed amount to be deposited with the general revenue account
main_sections.description: States that any amounts that remain undisbursed or unclaimed shall be deposited into the general revenue account.
Declares that this Act shall have an overriding effect over other laws.

main_sections.section_title: Contracts to cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or Government companies
main_sections.description: Contracts entered into by the companies will cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or Government companies.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Deals with offenses committed by companies under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Enables the Central Government to make orders to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any inconsistent provisions and saving of certain actions.

important_rules: On the appointed day (October 15, 1980), the undertakings of Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited, including all their assets, rights, and interests, vest in the Central Government.
The Central Government may direct that these undertakings shall vest in two Government Companies instead of continuing to vest in the Central Government.
Liabilities incurred by the companies prior to the appointed day (with specific exceptions) remain with the companies and are not transferable to the Central Government or Government companies.
Liabilities arising from materials supplied after the management was taken over by the Central Government are the responsibility of the Central Government or the concerned Government company.
All claims against the undertakings must be submitted to the Commissioner of Payments.
Contracts entered into by the companies will cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or Government companies.

penalties: Section 27 specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Government Companies, and the Commissioner of Payments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the vesting of undertakings, appointment of Custodians and Commissioner of Payments, examination and disbursement of claims, and imposition of penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to receive payment for nationalized undertakings.
Right for employees to continue in service.
Right of mortgagees/lien holders to claim payment from the specified amounts.
Right to enforce certain prior liabilities against the original companies.
Right for Government companies to possess licenses and instruments previously granted to the original companies.
duties: Duty of persons in charge of management to deliver assets and account for them.
Duty to make claims to the Commissioner of Payments.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Duty of Central Government or Government companies to pay amounts and manage undertakings.
Duty to continue manufacturing and production of essential goods.
obligations: The Central Government is obligated to pay amounts to the companies.
Government companies are obligated to manage the undertakings and fulfill liabilities as specified.
The Commissioner of Payments has the obligation to receive, examine, and disburse claims.
The Act places an obligation on the Central Government to ensure the continued manufacture and distribution of essential goods.

key_procedures: Vesting of undertakings in the Central Government or subsequently in Government Companies.
Appointment of a Commissioner of Payments to manage financial claims.
Submission, examination, admission/rejection, and disbursement of claims by the Commissioner.
Payment of amounts to the companies as per the Schedules.
Ratification of existing contracts by the Central Government or Government companies.
Power of the Central Government to make rules and remove difficulties.
administration: Central Government, and subsequently two Government Companies to which the undertakings are vested.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions take precedence over any other law.
Actions taken in good faith under this Act are protected.
Specific liabilities of the companies before the appointed day remain with the companies.
The management of the undertakings was initially taken over by the Central Government under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, prior to this nationalization act.

title: THE EXPORT-IMPORT BANK OF INDIA ACT, 1981
purpose: To establish a corporation known as the Export-Import Bank of India for providing financial assistance to exporters and importers, and for functioning as the principal financial institution for coordinating the working of institutions engaged in financing export and import of goods and services to promote the country’s international trade.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank) and its operations related to the financing of exports and imports of goods and services.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of Directors of the Exim Bank.
key_definitions.Development Bank: The Industrial Development Bank of India.
key_definitions.export: Export from or import into India or any other country of goods or services, or both.
key_definitions.import: Export from or import into India or any other country of goods or services, or both.
key_definitions.goods: Includes all materials, commodities and articles in a solid, liquid or gaseous state and all forms of energy.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.scheduled bank: A bank for the time being included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
key_definitions.services: Includes providing personnel, transferring technology, furnishing information, blueprints, plans, or advice, and making available any other resources.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'Development Bank', 'Exim Bank', 'export', 'import', 'goods', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'Reserve Bank', 'scheduled bank', and 'services'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Export-Import Bank of India
main_sections.description: Establishes the Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank) as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire property and contract. It also specifies the location of the head office and the possibility of establishing offices, branches, or agencies.
Specifies the authorized capital of the Exim Bank and allows the Central Government to increase it. It also states that the issued capital is wholly subscribed by the Central Government.

Vests the general superintendence, direction, and management of Exim Bank's affairs in the Board. It outlines the powers of the Chairman and/or Managing Director and emphasizes that the Board shall act on business principles with due regard to public interest and be guided by Central Government policy directions.

Details the composition of the Board of Directors, including the Chairman, Managing Director, whole-time directors, and nominated directors from the Reserve Bank, Development Bank, Export Credit and Guarantee Corporation Limited, and scheduled banks, as well as persons with expertise in export/import.
Specifies that the Exim Bank may grant loans and advances in or outside India, alone or in participation with other banks or financial institutions, for the purposes of export or import.

important_rules: The general superintendence, direction, and management of the Exim Bank's affairs and business vest in the Board of Directors.
The Exim Bank shall act on business principles with due regard to public interest.
The Exim Bank shall be guided by directions from the Central Government in matters of policy involving public interest.
The Exim Bank may grant loans and advances for the purposes of export or import, either by itself or in participation with other institutions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Board of Directors of the Exim Bank.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Board for management, the Central Government's policy directives and appointment/removal powers, and by specifying regulations for its operations.

rights: The Exim Bank has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract.
The Exim Bank has the right to sue or be sued in its name.
duties: The Exim Bank has a duty to act on business principles with due regard to public interest.
The Exim Bank has a duty to be guided by Central Government policy directions in matters of public interest.
obligations: The Exim Bank has an obligation to facilitate international trade by providing financial assistance to exporters and importers.

key_procedures: Appointment and removal of Chairman, Managing Director, and Directors of the Board.
Convening of Board meetings and decision-making by majority vote.
Establishment and functioning of Committees by the Board.
Granting of loans and advances for export/import purposes.
administration: The Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank), managed by its Board of Directors under the overall guidance and policy direction of the Central Government.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force.
The Central Government may increase the authorized capital of the Exim Bank.
The Central Government has the right to terminate the term of office of the Chairman or Managing Director with notice or payment in lieu.

title: The Maritime Zones of India (Regulation of Fishing by Foreign Vessels) Act, 1981
purpose: To provide for the regulation of fishing by foreign vessels in certain maritime zones of India and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to foreign vessels fishing within the maritime zones of India, which include the territorial waters of India and the exclusive economic zone of India. It also covers the activities of Indian citizens and certain other individuals/entities using foreign vessels for fishing in these zones.

key_definitions.exclusive_economic_zone_of_india: The exclusive economic zone of India as defined under the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976.
key_definitions.fish: Includes any aquatic animal, whether piscine or not, and encompasses shellfish, crustaceans, molluscs, turtles, aquatic mammals, holothurians, coelenterates, seaweed, coral, and other aquatic life, including their young, fry, eggs, and spawn.
key_definitions.fishing: Encompasses catching, taking, killing, attracting, or pursuing fish by any method, and includes the processing, preserving, transferring, receiving, and transporting of fish.
key_definitions.foreign_vessel: Any vessel that is not an Indian vessel.
key_definitions.indian_vessel: A vessel owned by the Government or a corporation established by a Central or State Act, or a vessel owned wholly by Indian citizens or specified entities and registered under relevant maritime laws.
key_definitions.maritime_zones_of_india: The territorial waters of India or the exclusive economic zone of India.
key_definitions.territorial_waters_of_india: The territorial waters of India as defined under the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Maritime Zones of India (Regulation of Fishing by Foreign Vessels) Act, 1981' and outlines the commencement provisions, allowing the Central Government to appoint different dates for different provisions.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'exclusive economic zone of India', 'fish', 'fishing', 'foreign vessel', 'Indian vessel', 'licence', 'maritime zones of India', 'master', 'owner', 'permit', 'prescribed', 'processing', 'specified ports', 'territorial waters of India', and 'vessel'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of fishing in maritime zones of India by foreign vessels
main_sections.description: Prohibits foreign vessels from fishing in the maritime zones of India, except under a valid licence granted under section 4 or a permit granted under section 5.

Details the process for applying for and granting licences to foreign vessels for fishing in India's maritime zones. It specifies application procedures, conditions for grant, validity, renewal, and adherence to prescribed conditions and restrictions.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of fishing by Indian citizens, etc., using foreign vessels
main_sections.description: Regulates fishing by Indian citizens and certain other specified entities using foreign vessels within India's maritime zones, requiring them to obtain a permit. It also addresses existing permissions granted before the Act's commencement.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation or suspension of licence or permit
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to suspend or cancel a licence or permit if the holder makes false statements or contravenes the Act's provisions, rules, or conditions of the licence/permit.

main_sections.section_title: Foreign vessel entering maritime zones of India without licence or permit to stow gear
main_sections.description: Mandates that any foreign vessel entering India's maritime zones without a valid licence or permit must keep its fishing gear stowed in the prescribed manner.

main_sections.section_title: Fishing for scientific research, investigation, etc.
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to grant written permission for foreign vessels to fish in India's maritime zones for scientific research, investigation, or experimental fishing under prescribed terms and conditions.

Empowers authorized officers (Coast Guard or other government officers) to stop, board, search foreign vessels, examine documents, seize vessels and equipment, and arrest individuals suspected of committing offences under the Act.
Specifies the penalty for contravening section 3, which prohibits unauthorized fishing by foreign vessels in India's maritime zones.
Defines the penalty for violating the conditions of a licence granted under the Act.
Defines the penalty for violating the conditions of a permit granted under the Act.
Details the provisions for the confiscation of vessels and other items seized under the Act.
Specifies the penalty for contravening section 7, which requires foreign vessels entering without a licence to stow their gear.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for obstruction of authorised officers
main_sections.description: Prescribes the penalty for obstructing authorised officers in the performance of their duties.
Outlines the powers of the court regarding orders to be passed in relation to offences under the Act.
Addresses the liability for offences committed by companies under the Act.
Declares that offences under this Act are cognizable.
Specifies the procedure for the cognizance and trial of offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Magistrate’s power to impose enhanced penalties
main_sections.description: Grants Magistrates the power to impose enhanced penalties for certain offences.
Defines the jurisdiction for the trial of offences under the Act.
Outlines certain presumptions that can be made in proceedings under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to individuals acting in good faith under the provisions of the Act.
States that this Act is in addition to and not in derogation of any other laws for the time being in force.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: Foreign vessels require a licence or permit from the Central Government to fish in India's maritime zones (Section 3).
Indian citizens and certain specified entities using foreign vessels for fishing in India's maritime zones must obtain a permit (Section 5).
Foreign vessels entering India's maritime zones without a licence/permit must stow their fishing gear (Section 7).
Fishing for scientific research, investigation, or experimental fishing by foreign vessels requires specific written permission from the Central Government (Section 8).
Authorised officers have the power to search vessels, seize equipment and catches, and arrest persons for suspected offences (Section 9).

penalties: Penalty for contravention of section 3 (unauthorized fishing).
Penalty for contravention of licence conditions.
Penalty for contravention of permit conditions.
Confiscation of vessels, fishing gear, equipment, stores, or cargo.
Penalty for contravention of section 7 (failure to stow gear).
Penalty for obstruction of authorized officers.
Enhanced penalties may be imposed by magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through authorized officers (including Coast Guard officers) and courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of search, seizure, detention, arrest, and prosecution of offenders. Courts are empowered to try offences and pass orders including confiscation. Rules made under the Act also specify enforcement mechanisms.

rights: Right to apply for a licence or permit to fish.
Right to operate within the terms of a granted licence or permit.
Right to be protected from arbitrary actions, with provisions for good faith actions.
Right to have a licence or permit considered for renewal.
duties: Duty of foreign vessel owners/operators to obtain necessary licences or permits.
Duty of Indian citizens/entities using foreign vessels to obtain necessary permits.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act, rules, orders, and conditions of licences/permits.
Duty to stow fishing gear if entering maritime zones without a licence/permit.
Duty to surrender suspended or cancelled licences/permits.
Duty to cooperate with authorised officers during searches and investigations.
Duty of licence/permit holders to ensure their employees comply with the Act.
obligations: Obligation to adhere strictly to the area, period, method of fishing, and purposes specified in the licence or permit.
Obligation to facilitate inspection and inquiry by authorised officers.
Obligation to surrender a vessel or items if seized under the Act.
Obligation to cease fishing activities upon suspension or cancellation of a licence or permit.

key_procedures: Application for a licence by foreign vessel owners or specified persons.
Application for a permit by Indian citizens or specified persons using foreign vessels.
Granting or rejection of licences/permits by the Central Government after inquiry.
Suspension or cancellation of licences/permits upon contravention or false statements.
Search and seizure of foreign vessels and related items by authorized officers.
Arrest of individuals committing offences under the Act.
Production of seized items and arrested persons before a competent Magistrate.
Trial of offences by designated courts.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for the administration of this Act, including granting licences and permits, making rules, and authorizing officers.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, which can differ for various provisions.
Existing permissions granted to Indian citizens before the Act's commencement are deemed permits if their terms are not inconsistent with the Act.
The Act is intended to supplement other maritime laws, not replace them.

title: The Emigration Act, 1983
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the emigration of citizens of India.
scope: Extends to the whole of India and applies also to citizens of India outside India. It covers the emigration of Indian citizens for employment outside India.

key_definitions.certificate: A certificate of registration issued under section 11.
key_definitions.conveyance: Includes a vessel, vehicle, country-craft and an aircraft.
key_definitions.dependent: Any person who is related to an emigrant and is dependent on that emigrant.
key_definitions.emigrant: Any citizen of India who intends to emigrate, or emigrates, or has emigrated, but does not include a dependent of an emigrant or certain persons who have resided outside India for a significant period.
key_definitions.emigrate/emigration: The departure out of India of any person with a view to taking up any employment in any country or place outside India.
key_definitions.employer: Any person providing or offering to provide employment in any country or place outside India.
key_definitions.employment: Any service, occupation or engagement (not under Central or State Government) for wages or reward, excluding work in specific capacities.
key_definitions.recruiting agent: A person engaged in India in the business of recruitment for an employer and representing that employer.
key_definitions.work: Includes various categories of unskilled, domestic, service, skilled, professional, and other types of labour as specified, with provisions for the Central Government to add or exclude categories.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Emigration Act, 1983, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India and citizens outside India), and outlines the commencement procedure by notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as emigrant, emigration, employer, recruiting agent, work, and others.
Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Protector General of Emigrants and Protectors of Emigrants, defining their areas of authority and distribution of work.

main_sections.section_title: General duties of Protectors of Emigrants
main_sections.description: Outlines the general duties of Protectors, including protecting and advising intending emigrants and emigrants, ensuring compliance with the Act, inspecting conveyances, inquiring into emigrants' treatment, and aiding returned emigrants.
Specifies the Central Government's power to appoint the Protector General of Emigrants or another officer of higher rank as the registering authority for recruiting agents.

main_sections.section_title: No person to function as recruiting agent without a valid certificate
main_sections.description: Mandates that no recruiting agent can operate without a valid certificate issued by the registering authority, with a transitional provision for existing agents.
Deals with the offenses and penalties stipulated under the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall function as a recruiting agent without a valid certificate issued by the registering authority, except under specific transitional provisions.
Recruitment by employers must be through a registered recruiting agent or under a permit obtained by the employer.
Emigration clearance is a requirement for emigration.
The Central Government has the power to prohibit emigration to any country in the interests of the general public, due to epidemics, civil disturbances, or for any class or category of persons.

penalties: Offences and penalties are detailed in Chapter VII, including provisions for offenses by companies and ensuring penalties are without prejudice to other actions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Protectors of Emigrants, Protector General of Emigrants, emigration officers, and officers in charge of emigration check-posts, all appointed under the Act. The Central Government also plays a key role in setting up structures and making rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of authorities, registration of recruiting agents, issuance of permits, emigration clearance, inspection of conveyances, and the imposition of penalties for contraventions of the Act.

rights: Intending emigrants and emigrants have the right to be protected and aided with advice by Protectors of Emigrants.
Emigrants who have returned to India have the right to be aided and advised by Protectors.
duties: Protectors of Emigrants have the duty to protect and aid emigrants, ensure compliance with the Act, inspect conveyances, and inquire into the treatment of emigrants.
Recruiting agents have duties related to their registration and adherence to terms and conditions.
Employers have duties regarding recruitment through authorized channels.
obligations: Individuals intending to emigrate or emigrating have an obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act, including obtaining emigration clearance.
Recruiting agents have an obligation to operate only with a valid certificate.
Employers have an obligation to recruit through registered agents or obtain permits.

key_procedures: Application for registration as a recruiting agent involves submitting an application with prescribed particulars, financial soundness information, premises details, and an undertaking, followed by the registering authority's assessment and potential security furnishing.
Procedure for obtaining permits for recruitment by employers involves specific application processes to the competent authority.
Emigration clearance requires adherence to specified procedures before departure.
Appeals against orders under the Act are provided for in Chapter VI.
administration: The Central Government, through the Protector General of Emigrants, Protectors of Emigrants, and other appointed emigration officers and staff.
important_notes: The Act explicitly excludes certain categories of persons from the definition of 'emigrant', such as dependents and individuals with significant prior residence abroad.
The Central Government has broad powers to exempt certain conveyances from being classified as 'emigrant conveyances' and to exempt specific categories of work from the definition of 'work'.
The Act repeals the Indian Emigration Act, 1922 (Act 7 of 1922).

title: THE PREVENTION OF DAMAGE TO PUBLIC PROPERTY ACT, 1984
purpose: To provide for the prevention of damage to public property and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It pertains to acts of mischief causing damage to public property.

key_definitions.mischief: Shall have the same meaning as in section 425 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
key_definitions.public property: Means any property, whether immovable or movable (including any machinery) which is owned by, or in the possession of, or under the control of the Central Government, any State Government, any local authority, any corporation established by or under a Central, Provincial or State Act, any company as defined in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956, or any institution, concern or undertaking specified by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette (provided such entity is financed wholly or substantially by government funds).

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984', states that it extends to the whole of India, and deems it to have come into force on January 28, 1984.
Defines key terms used in the Act, notably 'mischief' and 'public property'.

main_sections.section_title: Mischief causing damage to public property
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for committing mischief causing damage to public property. Sub-section (1) covers general public property with a penalty of imprisonment up to five years and fine. Sub-section (2) specifies more severe penalties (rigorous imprisonment of at least six months, up to five years, and fine) for damage to specific critical public properties like water/power installations, oil installations, sewage works, mines, factories, and public transportation/telecommunication facilities.

main_sections.section_title: Mischief causing damage to public property by fire or explosive substance
main_sections.description: Prescribes enhanced penalties for committing mischief causing damage to public property using fire or explosive substances, with rigorous imprisonment of at least one year, up to ten years, and fine.

Stipulates that an accused or convicted person under sections 3 or 4, if in custody, cannot be released on bail or their own bond without the prosecution being given an opportunity to oppose the bail application.
States that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and do not derogate from, any other existing law, and do not exempt any person from proceedings under other laws.

Repeals the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Ordinance, 1984. It also provides that anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Any person who commits mischief causing damage to any public property (other than those specified in sub-section (2) of Section 3) shall be punished with imprisonment up to five years and fine.

Any person who commits mischief causing damage to specific public properties like those related to water, light, power, energy, oil installations, sewage works, mines, factories, or public transportation/telecommunications, shall face rigorous imprisonment of at least six months, up to five years, and fine.
Committing mischief causing damage to public property using fire or explosive substance will result in rigorous imprisonment of at least one year, up to ten years, and fine.
An accused or convicted person under this Act, if in custody, shall not be released on bail or their own bond unless the prosecution has had an opportunity to oppose the release.
Actions taken under this Act are in addition to, and do not replace, provisions of any other law.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine (for general mischief causing damage to public property).
Rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months, but which may extend to five years and with fine (for mischief causing damage to specific critical public properties).
Rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year, but which may extend to ten years and with fine (for mischief causing damage by fire or explosive substance).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be law enforcement agencies and courts of law.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution and imposition of penalties as prescribed in the Act by courts. Bail is subject to specific procedural requirements.

rights: Right to oppose bail applications by the prosecution.
duties: Duty to refrain from committing mischief causing damage to public property.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of this Act and other applicable laws.
Obligation for individuals accused or convicted to adhere to bail restrictions.

key_procedures: Procedure for prosecution of individuals accused of damaging public property, involving arrest, trial, and sentencing.
Procedure for granting bail to individuals accused or convicted under the Act, requiring the prosecution to be given an opportunity to oppose the application.
administration: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but likely overseen by the Ministry of Home Affairs or relevant law enforcement and judicial bodies.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to the whole of India.
The Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law.
The Act was enacted following a repealed Ordinance (Ord. 3 of 1984), and actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed valid.
Courts have discretion to award sentences of imprisonment less than the minimum prescribed in specific circumstances, provided reasons are recorded.

title: The Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited (Nationalisation) Act, 1984
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited, ensuring their proper management for the benefit of the general public by continuing the manufacture, production, and distribution of essential tyres, tubes, and other rubber goods.
scope: This Act applies to the undertakings of Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited, including all their assets, rights, and liabilities. It extends to the entire country, as the companies' registered offices are in Calcutta, and the goods produced are essential to the national economy. The Act's provisions cover employees, payments, and the general management of these undertakings.

key_definitions.appointed day: February 14, 1984, the date from which the Act is deemed to have come into force.
key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of Payments appointed under section 15 of the Act.
key_definitions.existing Government company: A Government company actively engaged in business on the appointed day.
key_definitions.new Government company: A Government company formed and registered on or after the appointed day.
key_definitions.two companies: Refers to Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited, as defined under the Companies Act, 1956, with registered offices in Calcutta.

main_sections.description: Names the Act and specifies its commencement date as February 14, 1984.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'existing Government company', 'new Government company', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'specified date', and 'two companies'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the two companies
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the undertakings of both Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited, along with their rights and interests, are transferred to and vested in the Central Government.

Details what the vesting of undertakings includes (all assets, rights, properties, etc.) and clarifies that vested properties are freed from trusts, mortgages, and other encumbrances. It also outlines procedures for former mortgagees and the continuation of existing licenses and legal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Companies to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: Establishes that liabilities of the two companies incurred before the appointed day are the responsibility of the respective companies, not the Central Government or any Government company. However, liabilities for materials supplied after the management takeover are the responsibility of the Central Government or the acquiring Government company.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the two companies in an existing Government Company
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct, via notification, that the undertakings vested in it under section 3 shall instead vest in an existing Government company, specifying the date of vesting.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of the undertakings of the two companies from an existing Government company to a new Government company
main_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to declare, by notification, that undertakings vested in an existing Government company under section 6 shall be transferred to a newly formed Government company.
Ensures that employees of the two companies continue their employment under the new management.
Authorizes the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner of Payments.
Outlines the order in which claims against the acquired undertakings will be prioritized for payment.
States that this Act supersedes any other law in case of conflict.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any prior inconsistent provisions and savings.

important_rules: Rule: On the 'appointed day' (February 14, 1984), the undertakings of Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited are automatically transferred to and vested in the Central Government.

Rule: All assets, rights, leaseholds, powers, authorities, privileges, and properties (movable and immovable) of the companies, including machinery, cash, reserves, investments, and book debts, immediately prior to the appointed day, are included in the vested undertakings.
Rule: Vested properties are discharged from all trusts, obligations, mortgages, charges, liens, and other encumbrances.

Rule: Liabilities of the two companies incurred before the appointed day remain their responsibility and are not transferable to the Central Government or any acquiring Government company, except for liabilities related to materials supplied after management takeover.
Rule: The Central Government can direct the vesting of undertakings from itself to an existing Government company.
Rule: The Central Government can then direct the transfer of these undertakings from an existing Government company to a new Government company.
Rule: Employees of the acquired companies continue in their service.
Rule: A Commissioner of Payments is appointed to manage claims and disbursements.
Rule: Claims against the undertakings must be made to the Commissioner, who will examine and disburse them according to a priority order.
Rule: Unclaimed amounts are to be deposited with the general revenue account.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contraventions of the Act's provisions (Section 27).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government is the primary authority for enforcement, with powers to issue notifications, direct vesting, appoint officials (like the Commissioner of Payments), and make rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the statutory transfer of undertakings, appointment of a Commissioner of Payments to manage claims and liabilities, continuation of employees, and the application of penalties for non-compliance. The Act also has an over-riding effect, ensuring its provisions take precedence.

rights: The Central Government has the right to acquire and transfer the undertakings.
The Central Government has the power to direct vesting and transfer to Government companies.
Former mortgagees and lien holders have the right to claim payment out of the specified amounts (First Schedule and section 9) for their interests, but not against the vested property itself.
Employees have the right to continued employment.
Creditors and others with claims have the right to present their claims to the Commissioner of Payments.
duties: The Central Government has the duty to ensure the proper management of the acquired undertakings for the public good.
Persons in charge of the management of the undertakings have a duty to deliver all assets, etc., to the appropriate authority.
Individuals possessing assets of the companies have a duty to account for them.
The Commissioner of Payments has the duty to examine claims and disburse payments.
Existing and new Government companies have the duty to manage the undertakings as directed and comply with terms and conditions.
Mortgagees and other interested parties have a duty to provide intimation of their interests to the Commissioner within a prescribed time.
obligations: Government companies (existing or new) are obligated to accept the vested undertakings under specified terms and conditions.
Individuals or entities holding encumbrances on the vested property are obligated to notify the Commissioner of Payments.
The Central Government and acquiring Government companies are obligated to discharge liabilities arising from materials supplied after management takeover.

key_procedures: Procedure: Acquisition and Transfer - On the appointed day, the undertakings of the two companies vest in the Central Government. This vesting can subsequently be directed to an existing Government company or a new Government company via notification.

Procedure: Payment of Amounts - The Central Government makes payment for the acquired undertakings. A Commissioner of Payments is appointed to receive claims from creditors and other parties, examine them, and disburse the available funds according to a specified priority.
Procedure: Management of Undertakings - The Act provides for the management of the acquired undertakings, ensuring continuity of operations and employment for existing staff.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for the overall administration of the Act, including making rules, issuing notifications, directing vesting, and appointing the Commissioner of Payments. The acquired undertakings will be managed by either an existing or a new Government company as directed by the Central Government.
important_notes: Note: The Act has an over-riding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over any other law that may be inconsistent with it.
Note: Contracts in existence before the appointed day cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or the relevant Government company.
Note: Any difficulties in the operation of the Act can be removed by the Central Government.

Note: The Act specifies that certain liabilities of the companies prior to the appointed day are not enforceable against the Central Government or the acquiring Government company, with a specific exception for liabilities arising from materials supplied after management takeover.

title: The National Capital Region Planning Board Act, 1985
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Planning Board for the preparation of a plan for the development of the National Capital Region, for coordinating and monitoring the implementation of such plan, and for evolving harmonized policies for the control of land-uses and development of infrastructure in the National Capital Region to avoid haphazard development.
scope: Applies to the National Capital Region (NCR) as specified in the Schedule, which includes the Union territory of Delhi and parts of Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. The Act covers the planning, development, and coordinated implementation of various plans (Regional, Functional, Sub-Regional, Project) within the NCR.

key_definitions.Board: The National Capital Region Planning Board constituted under the Act.
key_definitions.Committee: The Planning Committee constituted under the Act to assist the Board.
key_definitions.counter-magnet area: An urban area selected by the Board for development to achieve the objectives of the Regional Plan.
key_definitions.Functional Plan: A plan prepared to elaborate one or more elements of the Regional Plan.
key_definitions.land: Includes benefits arising from land and things permanently attached to the earth.
key_definitions.National Capital Region: The areas specified in the Schedule, which can be amended by the Central Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Project Plan: A detailed plan prepared to implement elements of the Regional, Sub-Regional, or Functional Plan.
key_definitions.Regional Plan: The plan prepared for the development of the NCR, including control of land-uses and infrastructure development.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Board under this Act.
key_definitions.sub-region: A part of the NCR falling within a participating State or Union territory.
key_definitions.Sub-Regional Plan: A plan prepared for a sub-region.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is deemed to be October 19, 1984.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including Board, Committee, Regional Plan, and National Capital Region.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the constitution of the National Capital Region Planning Board by the Central Government, its corporate status, and its composition, including the Chairman and other members.
Describes the constitution and composition of the Planning Committee, established to assist the Board.
Outlines the primary functions of the Board, including preparing plans, coordinating implementation, and overseeing financing of development projects.
Specifies the powers of the Board, such as calling for reports, ensuring conformity with the Regional Plan, reviewing implementation, and selecting areas for development.
Details the elements that must be included in the Regional Plan, such as land-use policy, urban settlement patterns, economic base proposals, transport, water supply, and priority areas.
States that this Act has an overriding effect on other laws concerning the matters dealt with by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to give directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Board.
Deals with the consequences of violating the Regional Plan.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Board to make regulations.
Provides for the repeal of any existing law and savings provisions.

important_rules: The Regional Plan shall indicate the manner in which land in the NCR shall be used and include proposals for land-use allocation, urban settlement patterns, economic base, transport, water supply, drainage, and priority development areas.
The Board shall coordinate the enforcement and implementation of various plans through the participating States and the Union territory.
The Central Government has the power to give directions to the Board regarding the implementation of the Act.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over other laws on similar matters.
The Board may co-opt members for specific periods, who will have powers but no voting rights.

penalties: Section 29 outlines provisions related to the violation of the Regional Plan, though specific penalties are not detailed in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Capital Region Planning Board (the Board) and the participating States and Union territory.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the coordination and monitoring of plan implementation by the Board, and by the participating States and Union territory adhering to the Regional Plan and other plans prepared under the Act.

rights: The Board has the right to call for reports and information from participating States and the Union territory.
The Board has the power to select and approve projects, call for priority development, and provide assistance.
The Central Government has the right to give directions to the Board.
duties: The Board has a duty to prepare the Regional Plan and Functional Plans.
The Board has a duty to coordinate the enforcement and implementation of all prepared plans.
The Board has a duty to ensure proper programming and phasing of development.
Participating States and the Union territory have a duty to prepare Sub-Regional and Project Plans as arranged by the Board and to coordinate the enforcement and implementation of plans.
obligations: Participating States and the Union territory are obligated to comply with the Regional Plan and other plans developed under the Act.
Members of the Board and Committee are obligated to act in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Preparation of the Regional Plan: Involves preparing a draft plan with assistance from the Committee, publishing it for public inspection, and inviting objections.
Constitution of the Board: The Central Government notifies its constitution.
Constitution of the Planning Committee: The Board constitutes the Committee to assist it.
administration: The Central Government and the National Capital Region Planning Board.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 19, 1984.
Amendments to the composition of the Board require the consent of all participating States and the Union territory.
Co-opted members of the Board or Committee do not have voting rights.
Acts or proceedings of the Board or Committee are not invalidated by vacancies or defects in constitution, provided they do not affect the merits of the case.
The Central Government may, with the consent of the concerned State Government and in consultation with the Board, add or exclude areas from the National Capital Region through notification.

title: THE PONDICHERRY UNIVERSITY ACT, 1985
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the Union territory of Pondicherry and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the Union territory of Pondicherry. It can be extended to Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep with Central Government approval. It governs the establishment, functioning, and administration of the Pondicherry University, including its campuses, colleges, institutions, and academic activities.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by Ordinances.
key_definitions.University: The Pondicherry University.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, academic staff, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, College, Court, Department, Director, employee, Executive Council, Hall, Institution, Principal, recognised institution, recognised teachers, School, Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, teachers of the University, and University.
Establishes the Pondicherry University, defines its headquarters, and constitutes it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objectives of the University, including disseminating and advancing knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, making special provisions for studies in French and integrated courses, and promoting inter-disciplinary studies and research.

Enumerate the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research facilities, organizing studies in French, granting degrees, conferring honorary degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, recognizing institutions, creating posts, collaborating with other institutions, establishing campuses, awarding fellowships, maintaining colleges and institutions, making provision for research and advisory services, admitting colleges and institutions to its privileges, declaring autonomous colleges/institutions, determining admission standards, receiving fees, supervising student residences, making special arrangements for women students, regulating discipline, promoting employee welfare, receiving donations, and borrowing money with government approval.

Defines the territorial jurisdiction of the University to the Union territory of Pondicherry and allows for extension to Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep. It also specifies conditions for affiliation of colleges and institutions.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: States that the University shall be open to all individuals irrespective of sex, race, creed, caste, or class and prohibits religious tests for admission or employment. It also allows for special provisions for weaker sections and eligibility for French nationals of Indian origin.
