Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and grants the Visitor rights to conduct inspections and inquiries into the University's administration, finances, and academic activities.

important_rules: University must be open to all persons regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, with no religious tests for admission or employment.
French nationals of Indian origin permitted long-term residence in Pondicherry are eligible for admission.
Colleges seeking affiliation must agree to accept the University's Statutes and Ordinances.
Any college or institution admitted to the University's privileges must cease association with any other university.

rights: Right to representation to the Visitor during inspections/inquiries.
Right to appoint a representative to be present and heard during inspections/inquiries.
Right to appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
duties: University has a duty to provide instructional and research facilities.
University has a duty to disseminate and advance knowledge.
Colleges/Institutions admitted to privileges must cease association with other universities.
obligations: Obligation to uphold the principle of openness to all classes, castes, and creeds.
Obligation to follow Statutes and Ordinances for affiliation.
Obligation to comply with directives from the Visitor after inspections/inquiries.

key_procedures: Procedure for the Visitor to cause inspections and inquiries, including providing notice and allowing for representations.
Procedure for appointing representatives during inspections/inquiries.
Procedure for making Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations (though detailed procedures are not fully elaborated in the provided text).
administration: The Central Government appoints the date of commencement. The President of India is the Visitor. The Vice-Chancellor, Chancellor, Executive Council, and Academic Council are key administrative bodies.
important_notes: The commencement date is to be notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette.
The University has the power to withdraw degrees, diplomas, certificates, or academic distinctions for good and sufficient cause.
The Act provides for the establishment of specific Schools: 'Sri Aurobindo School of Eastern and Western Thought' and 'Subramania Bharati School of Tamil Language and Literature'.

title: THE JUDGES (PROTECTION) ACT, 1985
purpose: To secure additional protection for Judges and others acting judicially and for matters connected therewith.

scope.geographical: The whole of India (with an exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir which was omitted in 2019).
scope.subject_matter: Protection for Judges acting in discharge of their official or judicial duty or function from civil or criminal proceedings.

key_definitions.Judge: Means not only every person who is officially designated as a Judge, but also every person who is empowered by law to give in any legal proceeding a definitive judgment, or a judgment which, if not appealed against, would be definitive, or a judgment which, if confirmed by some other authority, would be definitive; or who is one of a body of persons which body of persons is empowered by law to give such a judgment.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial application.
Defines the term 'Judge' for the purposes of the Act.
Provides that no court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceeding against a Judge for acts done in the discharge of official or judicial duty, with a proviso for government action.
Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws providing protection to Judges.

important_rules: No court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceeding against a person who is or was a Judge for any act, thing or word committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of, acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official or judicial duty or function.

The power of the Central Government, State Government, Supreme Court of India, High Court, or any other authority under any law to take action against a Judge (civil, criminal, departmental, or otherwise) is not affected by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly defined for penalties, but the protection is enforced by the courts refusing to entertain proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Courts are barred from entertaining or continuing civil or criminal proceedings against a Judge for acts done in official capacity.

rights: Judges have the right to protection from civil and criminal proceedings for acts done in the discharge of their official or judicial duty.
The Central Government, State Governments, Supreme Court, High Courts, and other authorities have the right to take action against Judges under existing laws.

key_procedures: Courts must dismiss or refuse to entertain civil or criminal proceedings against a Judge for actions taken in their official or judicial capacity, unless an exception under sub-section (2) of Section 3 applies.

The Central Government, State Governments, Supreme Court, High Courts, or other authorities can initiate civil, criminal, or departmental proceedings against a Judge, notwithstanding the protection provided by this Act.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but likely falls under the Ministry of Law and Justice or the Department of Justice.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2019 to omit the exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir, extending its application to the entire country.
The protection provided by this Act is in addition to any other legal protections available to Judges.

title: THE MUSLIM WOMEN (PROTECTION OF RIGHTS ON DIVORCE) ACT, 1986
purpose: To protect the rights of Muslim women who have been divorced by, or have obtained divorce from, their husbands and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It specifically addresses the rights of divorced Muslim women and their former husbands, and in certain cases, their relatives and the Wakf Board.

key_definitions.divorced woman: A Muslim woman who was married according to Muslim law, and has been divorced by, or has obtained divorce from, her husband in accordance with Muslim law.
key_definitions.iddat period: The period following divorce, defined as three menstrual courses, three lunar months, or the period until the termination of pregnancy if the woman is enceinte at the time of divorce.
key_definitions.Magistrate: A Magistrate of the First Class exercising jurisdiction under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in the area where the divorced woman resides.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial extent.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'divorced woman', 'iddat period', 'Magistrate', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Mahr or other properties of Muslim woman to be given to her at the time of divorce
main_sections.description: Ensures that a divorced woman is entitled to reasonable and fair provision and maintenance within the iddat period, maintenance for children for two years, her mahr or dower, and all properties given to her.
Provides for the payment of maintenance to a divorced woman who has not remarried and cannot maintain herself after the iddat period, by her relatives or, if necessary, the State Wakf Board.

main_sections.section_title: Option to be governed by the provisions of sections 125 to 128 of Act 2 of 1974
main_sections.description: Allows a divorced woman and her former husband to opt to be governed by the provisions of sections 125 to 128 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including the form of declarations, procedure for Magistrates, and other prescribed matters.
Deals with applications pending before a Magistrate under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, at the commencement of this Act, ensuring they are disposed of according to this Act's provisions.

important_rules: Rule 1: Within the iddat period, a divorced woman is entitled to reasonable and fair provision and maintenance from her former husband.
Rule 2: A divorced woman is entitled to the full amount of mahr or dower agreed upon at the time of marriage or thereafter.
Rule 3: A divorced woman is entitled to all properties given to her by relatives or the husband's side before, at, or after the marriage.
Rule 4: If a divorced woman maintains children, her former husband must provide reasonable maintenance for a period of two years from the birth of each child.

Rule 5: If a divorced woman cannot maintain herself after the iddat period and has not remarried, her relatives are liable to pay maintenance, and if they cannot, the State Wakf Board will be directed to pay.

penalties: If a person fails to comply with a Magistrate's order for payment of maintenance or mahr/dower, a warrant may be issued to recover the amount.
Failure to comply with the order after warrant execution can lead to imprisonment for up to one year or until payment is made.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate of the First Class.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders and warrants for recovery of amounts, and potential imprisonment in case of non-compliance.

rights: Right to reasonable and fair provision and maintenance within the iddat period.
Right to maintenance for children for two years from their respective birth dates.
Right to the full amount of mahr or dower.
Right to all properties gifted to her.
Right to maintenance after the iddat period if unable to maintain herself and not remarried.
Option to be governed by sections 125-128 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
duties: Duty of former husband to provide reasonable and fair provision and maintenance within the iddat period.
Duty of former husband to provide maintenance for children for two years.
Duty of former husband to pay mahr or dower.
Duty of former husband or his relatives to deliver properties gifted to the woman.
Duty of relatives (if applicable) to pay maintenance to the divorced woman.
Duty of the State Wakf Board to pay maintenance if relatives are unable to do so.
obligations: Obligation of the former husband to meet the financial needs of the divorced woman and children.
Obligation of entitled relatives to contribute to the maintenance of the divorced woman.
Obligation of the State Wakf Board to provide maintenance when other avenues are exhausted.

key_procedures: A divorced woman can apply to a Magistrate for an order for payment of provision, maintenance, mahr/dower, or delivery of properties if not provided by the former husband.
The Magistrate, upon satisfaction of the husband's failure or neglect, must make an order within one month of the application filing.
In cases where a divorced woman cannot maintain herself after the iddat period, the Magistrate can order relatives to pay maintenance.
If relatives cannot pay, the Magistrate can order the State Wakf Board to pay maintenance.
Divorced women and their former husbands can opt to be governed by sections 125-128 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, by filing a joint or separate declaration.
administration: Central Government (for making rules), Magistrates (for enforcement and orders), and State Wakf Boards (for payment of maintenance as directed).
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2019 to omit the exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The Act overrides any other law for the time being in force regarding the rights of divorced Muslim women.

title: THE SWADESHI COTTON MILLS COMPANY LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1986
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of certain textile undertakings of the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited, with a view to securing their proper management for the continued manufacture, production, and distribution of cloth and yarn, serving public interest and giving effect to the State's policy as per Article 39(b) and (c) of the Constitution.
scope: This Act applies to the six textile undertakings of the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited, Kanpur, including those located in Kanpur, Pondicherry, Naini, Maunath Bhanjan, Udaipur, and Rae Bareli. It also covers related assets, rights, liabilities, and employees associated with these undertakings.

key_definitions.appointed day: The 1st day of April, 1985.
key_definitions.Company: The Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited, Kanpur.
key_definitions.National Textile Corporation: The National Textile Corporation Limited, a company formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.textile undertakings: The six specific textile undertakings of the Company located in Kanpur, Pondicherry, Naini, Maunath Bhanjan, Udaipur, and Rae Bareli.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies the dates when different provisions come into force. Sections 27 and 28 are effective immediately, while other provisions are deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1985.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'Company', 'date of taking over', 'National Textile Corporation', 'notification', 'Ordinance', 'prescribed', 'specified date', 'Subsidiary Textile Corporation', and 'textile undertakings'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting of the textile undertakings
main_sections.description: Declares that on the appointed day, all textile undertakings of the Company and the Company's right, title, and interest therein shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government, and immediately thereafter, in the National Textile Corporation.

Details the comprehensive nature of the vesting, including all associated assets, rights, powers, privileges, property (movable and immovable), and documents. It also clarifies that vested property is freed from encumbrances and that pending legal proceedings will continue by or against the National Textile Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Company to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: Establishes that all liabilities of the Company relating to the textile undertakings for the period prior to the appointed day remain the liability of the Company and are not enforceable against the Central Government or the National Textile Corporation.
Specifies that an amount of twenty-four crores and thirty-two lakhs of rupees shall be paid by the Central Government to the Company in cash for the transfer and vesting of the textile undertakings.
Outlines the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: On the appointed day (April 1, 1985), the textile undertakings of the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited and all related rights, titles, and interests vest in the Central Government, and subsequently in the National Textile Corporation.
The vesting includes all assets, property, rights, and documents pertaining to the textile undertakings, irrespective of their location.

All liabilities of the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited concerning the textile undertakings prior to the appointed day remain with the Company and are not transferred to the Central Government or the National Textile Corporation.
The Central Government shall pay a specified amount (Rs. 24.32 crores) to the Company for the acquisition of the textile undertakings.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 27).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the National Textile Corporation are central to the enforcement and administration of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes the transfer and vesting of undertakings, the payment of amounts, the management of undertakings, provisions for employees, the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments for claims, and penalties for offenses.

rights: The Central Government has the right to acquire the textile undertakings.
The National Textile Corporation has the right to manage and operate the acquired undertakings.
Employees of the textile undertakings have rights concerning their continuance in service and benefits (Section 12, 13).
duties: The Central Government has the duty to pay the specified amount for the acquisition.
The National Textile Corporation has the duty to manage the acquired undertakings for the benefit of the public.
Persons in charge of the management of the textile undertakings have a duty to deliver all assets, etc., to the National Textile Corporation (Section 11).
obligations: The Company is obligated to transfer its textile undertakings and related rights and interests.
The Company remains obligated for its prior liabilities related to the undertakings.

Mortgagees or persons holding charges/liens on vested property must intimate the Commissioner and are entitled to claim payment from specified amounts, not from the vested property itself (Section 4(5)).

key_procedures: Transfer and vesting of textile undertakings in the Central Government and then the National Textile Corporation on the appointed day.
Payment of a specified amount by the Central Government to the Company.
Appointment of a Commissioner of Payments to receive and disburse claims against the Company related to the acquired undertakings.
Examination, admission, or rejection of claims by the Commissioner.
Disbursement of money by the Commissioner to claimants and deposit of undisbursed amounts.
administration: The Central Government and the National Textile Corporation.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over any other law, agreement, or instrument to the contrary (Section 24).
Contracts existing before the appointed day cease to have effect unless ratified by the National Textile Corporation (Section 26).
The Central Government has the power to make rules and remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act (Sections 31, 32).

title: THE STATE OF MIZORAM ACT, 1986
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the State of Mizoram and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the territories that comprised the existing Union territory of Mizoram, establishing it as the new State of Mizoram. It covers representation in the legislatures, establishment of a common High Court, authorization of expenditure, distribution of revenues, assets and liabilities, provisions as to services, and legal and miscellaneous provisions related to the formation of the State of Mizoram.

key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator appointed by the President under Article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.appointed day: The day which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
key_definitions.Election Commission: The Election Commission appointed by the President under Article 324.
key_definitions.existing Union territory of Mizoram: The Union territory of Mizoram as existing immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having, immediately before the appointed day, the force of law in the whole or any part of the existing Union territory of Mizoram.
key_definitions.sitting member: In relation to either House of Parliament or of the Legislative Assembly of the existing Union territory of Mizoram, means a person who, immediately before the appointed day, is a member of that House or that Assembly.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the State of Mizoram Act, 1986.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, appointed day, article, Election Commission, existing Union territory of Mizoram, law, sitting member, and treasury.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of the State of Mizoram
main_sections.description: Declares that on and from the appointed day, a new State to be known as the State of Mizoram shall be established, comprising the territories that were part of the existing Union territory of Mizoram.

States that on and from the appointed day, the sitting member of the Council of States representing the existing Union territory of Mizoram shall be deemed to have been duly elected to fill the seat allotted to the State of Mizoram. The term of office of this member remains unaltered.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seat in the existing House of the People
main_sections.description: Specifies that on and from the appointed day, the allocation of seats to the State of Mizoram in the House of the People shall be one, and this seat shall be reserved for the Scheduled Tribes. It also states that the parliamentary constituency of the existing Union territory of Mizoram shall be deemed to be the parliamentary constituency of the State of Mizoram.
On and from the appointed day, the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Mizoram to be filled by persons chosen by direct election shall be forty.

Mandates the Election Commission to, before the appointed day, distribute the seats assigned to the Legislative Assembly into single-member territorial constituencies. It outlines the criteria for delimitation, including geographical compactness, consideration of physical features, administrative boundaries, communication facilities, public convenience, and location of constituencies for Scheduled Tribes.

main_sections.section_title: Common High Court for Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura and Mizoram
main_sections.description: Establishes a common High Court for the States of Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, and Mizoram, to be known as the Gauhati High Court. Judges of the previous High Court will become Judges of the common High Court. It also details the allocation of expenditure for the Judges' salaries and allowances.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of existing laws and their adaptations
main_sections.description: Provides for the continuance of existing laws and their adaptation to the new State of Mizoram.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule: On and from the appointed day, the State of Mizoram shall be established, comprising the territories of the existing Union territory of Mizoram.
Rule: The sitting member of the Council of States representing the existing Union territory of Mizoram shall be deemed to have been elected to the seat allotted to Mizoram.
Rule: The State of Mizoram shall have one seat in the House of the People, reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
Rule: The Legislative Assembly of Mizoram shall have forty seats filled by direct election.
Rule: The Election Commission shall delimit constituencies for the Legislative Assembly before the appointed day, following specific guidelines.
Rule: A common High Court, the Gauhati High Court, shall be established for Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, and Mizoram.
Rule: Existing laws shall continue to be in force in Mizoram and may be adapted as necessary.
Rule: The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the State for the purposes of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities as implied by the nature of the act, including the Election Commission for delimitation and the Central Government for general administration and direction.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, notifications, orders, and potentially by the courts for interpretation and enforcement of legal provisions.

rights: Right of the sitting member of the Council of States to continue in office.
Right of the sitting member of the House of the People to be deemed elected.
Right of advocates to practice in the common High Court.
Right to appear or to act in proceedings transferred to the common High Court.
duties: Duty of the Election Commission to delimit constituencies before the appointed day.
Duty of the Central Government to appoint the 'appointed day' by notification.
Duty of the Central Government to issue directions as necessary.
obligations: Obligation to establish the State of Mizoram on the appointed day.
Obligation to adhere to the delimitation of constituencies as published by the Election Commission.
Obligation to respect the jurisdiction and functioning of the common High Court.

key_procedures: Procedure for delimitation of constituencies by the Election Commission: This involves publishing proposals, inviting objections and suggestions, considering them, and publishing the final order, which then has the force of law.
Procedure for the establishment of the State of Mizoram: This occurs on the 'appointed day' as notified by the Central Government.
Procedure for the allocation of sitting members to legislative bodies: Existing members are deemed to have been elected to the new State's representation.
Procedure for the functioning of the common High Court: The law regarding practice and procedure of the previous High Court is applied with necessary modifications.
Procedure for removing difficulties: The Central Government can make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for appointing the 'appointed day', issuing directions, and removing difficulties. The Election Commission is responsible for the delimitation of constituencies. The High Court functions under this Act.
important_notes: Several sections of the Act (4, 5, 7, 13, 14) have been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2001.
The 'appointed day' for the establishment of the State of Mizoram was 20th February, 1987, as per notification No. S.O. 72(E).
The common High Court serves multiple states beyond Mizoram, including Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Manipur, and Tripura.
Associate members assisting the Election Commission in delimitation do not have voting rights.

title: THE NATIONAL SECURITY GUARD ACT, 1986
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for combating terrorist activities with a view to protecting States against internal disturbances and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to all members of the National Security Guard, including officers, Assistant Commanders, Rangers, and combatised tradesmen. It covers their service, duties, offences, punishments, and legal proceedings. The Act is applicable within India and potentially outside India as per section 6.

key_definitions.active duty: Any duty as a member of the Security Guard during the period in which such person is attached to, or forms part of, a unit of the Security Guard which is engaged in operations against terrorists or any person in arms against the Union, or which is operating at a picket or engaged on patrol or any other duty, in relation to combating terrorist activity.
key_definitions.civil offence: An offence which is triable by a Criminal Court or by a special Judge appointed under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1952.
key_definitions.member of the Security Guard: An officer, an Assistant Commander, a Ranger or a combatised tradesman.
key_definitions.terrorist: Any person who, with intent to over-awe the Government as by law established or to strike terror in the people or any section of the people or to alienate any section of the people or to adversely affect the harmony amongst different sections of the people, does any act or thing by using bombs, dynamite or other explosive substances or inflammable substances or firearms or other lethal weapons or poisons or noxious gases or other chemicals or any other substances (whether biological or otherwise) of a hazardous nature, in such a manner as to cause, or as is likely to cause, death of, or injuries to, any person or persons or damage to, or destruction of, property or disruption of any supplies or services essential to the life of the community.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used throughout the Act, including 'active duty', 'civil offence', 'member of the Security Guard', 'terrorist', and other designations within the Security Guard.

Specifies that officers, Assistant Commanders, Rangers, and combatised tradesmen appointed to the Security Guard are subject to this Act, wherever they may be, and remain subject until repatriated, retired, released, discharged, removed, or dismissed.

Establishes the National Security Guard as an armed force of the Union for combating terrorist activities and states that its constitution and the conditions of service of its members shall be as prescribed.

Vests the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Security Guard in the Central Government, and places the command and supervision under the Director-General, who is assisted by other appointed officers.
States that every member of the Security Guard is liable to serve in any part of India as well as outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation and withdrawal from the post
main_sections.description: Prohibits members of the Security Guard from resigning or withdrawing from their duties except with the prior written permission of the prescribed authority.

main_sections.section_title: Tenure of service under the Act
main_sections.description: States that every person subject to this Act holds office during the pleasure of the Central Government.

important_rules: Members of the Security Guard are liable to serve anywhere in India and abroad (Section 6).
Members cannot resign or withdraw from duty without prior written permission from the prescribed authority (Section 7).
Members hold office during the pleasure of the Central Government (Section 8).
The Act outlines numerous offences related to military discipline, desertion, disobedience, and conduct unbecoming of a member (Chapter III, Sections 15-46).
The Act provides for punishments for these offences, awardable by Security Guard Courts or other officers (Chapter IV, Sections 47-54).

penalties: Punishments awardable by Security Guard Courts, including death, imprisonment, dismissal, reduction in rank, forfeiture of pay, etc. (Sections 47-54).
Specific penalties are outlined for various offences such as mutiny, desertion, disobedience, and disgraceful conduct.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Director-General of the Security Guard and other appointed officers, as well as Security Guard Courts, are responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of Security Guard Courts (General, Petty, and Summary), investigation of offences, trial of offenders, and execution of sentences.

rights: Right to remedy for aggrieved persons other than officers (Section 13).
Right to remedy for aggrieved officers (Section 14).
Protection for acts of members of the Security Guard (Section 138).
duties: Duty of Commander in regard to detention of offenders (Section 56).
Duty to remain subject to the Act until properly released or dismissed (Section 3(2)).
Members have duties related to their appointment and service as outlined throughout the Act and prescribed rules.
obligations: Members are obligated to combat terrorist activities and protect states against internal disturbances.
Members are obligated to adhere to the rules and regulations governing the Security Guard.
Members are obligated to face trial and punishment for offences committed under the Act.

key_procedures: Arrest and custody of offenders (Sections 55-59).
Proceedings before trial, including inquiry into absence without leave (Sections 55-60).
Establishment and procedure of Security Guard Courts (General, Petty, Summary) (Chapters VI and VII, Sections 61-103).
Confirmation and revision of findings and sentences (Chapter VIII, Sections 104-114).
Execution of sentences, pardons, remissions, etc. (Chapter IX, Sections 115-134).
Rules regarding evidence, witnesses, and judicial notice in Security Guard Courts (Sections 82-95).
administration: The Central Government and the Director-General of the Security Guard.
important_notes: The Act establishes a specialized armed force to combat terrorism, indicating its critical role in national security.
The Act distinguishes between 'civil offences' and offences under the Act, providing for potential trial in either Criminal Courts or Security Guard Courts (Section 77).
The Act details extensive disciplinary measures and court-martial-like procedures for its members, reflecting the nature of an armed force.
The definition of 'terrorist' is broad and covers various acts aimed at disrupting society or government functioning.
The Central Government has the power to make rules under the Act (Section 139).

title: THE DELHI APARTMENT OWNERSHIP ACT, 1986
purpose: To provide for the ownership of an individual apartment in a multi-storeyed building and of an undivided interest in the common areas and facilities appurtenant to such apartment, and to make such apartment and interest heritable and transferable, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to every apartment in a multi-storeyed building constructed for residential, commercial, or other prescribed purposes by any group housing co-operative society or any other person or authority. It extends to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi. The provisions also apply to buildings with two or three apartments if the owner declares his intention to make the Act applicable and registers a Deed of Apartment.

key_definitions.administrator: The Administrator of the Union territory of Delhi appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.allottee: In relation to an apartment, the person to whom such apartment has been allotted, sold, or otherwise transferred by the promoter.
key_definitions.apartment: A part of any property intended for independent use, including one or more rooms or enclosed spaces on one or more floors in a multi-storeyed building, used for residence, office, profession, occupation, trade, or business, with direct exit to a public street or common area. It includes any garage or room provided by the promoter for parking or domestic aide.
key_definitions.apartment_owner: The person or persons owning an apartment and an undivided interest in the common areas and facilities appurtenant to such apartment in the percentage specified in the Deed of Apartment.
key_definitions.association_of_apartment_owners: All the owners of apartments in a multi-storeyed building, or in designated blocks/pockets, acting as a group according to bye-laws.
key_definitions.common_areas_and_facilities: Includes the land on which the building is located, foundations, walls, roofs, common passages, staircases, entrances/exits, basements, yards, gardens, parking areas, central services (power, light, water, heating, etc.), elevators, tanks, pumps, and other parts necessary for the existence, maintenance, safety, or common use of the property.
key_definitions.common_expenses: Sums lawfully assessed by the Association of Apartment Owners for administration, maintenance, repair, or replacement of common areas and facilities, or expenses declared as such by the Act, bye-laws, or agreed upon by the Association.
key_definitions.deed_of_apartment: The Deed of Apartment referred to in section 13.
key_definitions.multi_storeyed_building: A building with four or more apartments, or two or more buildings with a total of four or more apartments, including buildings with two or three apartments where the Act is declared applicable. The lease for the land must be for thirty years or more.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Delhi Apartment Ownership Act, 1986, specifies its extent to the Union territory of Delhi, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Administrator.

Defines the types of multi-storeyed buildings to which the Act applies, including those constructed by group housing co-operative societies or other persons/authorities on freehold or leasehold land (lease of 30+ years). It also includes a provision for buildings with two or three apartments if the owner makes a declaration.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, apartment, apartment owner, common areas and facilities, common expenses, Deed of Apartment, multi-storeyed building, promoter, etc.

Establishes exclusive ownership and possession of an apartment for the allottee/transferee. It also states that each apartment owner is entitled to a percentage of undivided interest in common areas and facilities, which is permanent and cannot be altered without consent. It prohibits partition of common areas and facilities and outlines the use of common areas.

main_sections.section_title: Apartment to be heritable and transferable
main_sections.description: Declares that each apartment, along with its undivided interest in common areas, constitutes heritable and transferable immovable property. It can be transferred by sale, mortgage, lease, gift, exchange, or bequest, subject to applicable laws. Transfers by group housing co-operative societies are regulated by their specific laws.

main_sections.section_title: Ownership of apartment subject to conditions
main_sections.description: States that ownership is subject to conditions, particularly where allotment, sale, or transfer is made in pursuance of payment or part payment of consideration.

important_rules: Exclusive ownership and possession of an apartment is granted to the allottee or transferee.
Each apartment owner is entitled to a permanent, undivided interest in common areas and facilities, which cannot be altered without unanimous consent.
Common areas and facilities remain undivided and cannot be partitioned.
Apartment owners must use common areas and facilities without hindering others.
Maintenance, repair, replacement, and additions to common areas must be done according to the Act and bye-laws.
The Association of Apartment Owners has the right to access apartments for maintenance, repairs, or emergency repairs to common areas or other apartments.
Apartments, along with their undivided interest in common areas, are heritable and transferable like other immovable property.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Administrator has the power to appoint a 'competent authority' (Secretary in Delhi Administration, Vice-Chairman of DDA, or Land and Development Officer) to perform functions under the Act. The Association of Apartment Owners, through its Board or Manager, exercises enforcement rights regarding access to apartments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement appears to be through the 'competent authority' for certain functions, and by the Association of Apartment Owners for managing common areas and ensuring compliance with bye-laws. Specific penalties are not detailed in the provided extract.

rights: Right to exclusive ownership and possession of one's apartment.
Right to an undivided interest in common areas and facilities.
Right to use common areas and facilities for their intended purposes.
Right to transfer one's apartment and interest in common areas.
Right to inherit and bequeath one's apartment and interest.
The Association of Apartment Owners has the right of access to apartments for maintenance and repairs.
duties: To comply with the covenants and bye-laws of the Association of Apartment Owners.
To pay common expenses assessed by the Association.
To not hinder or encroach upon the lawful rights of other apartment owners when using common areas.
To comply with provisions of the Act and bye-laws for maintenance, repair, and replacement of common areas.
Purchasers or lessees of apartments must execute an undertaking (as per section 9, though details are not in the extract).
obligations: Obligation to contribute to common expenses.
Obligation to adhere to the terms specified in the Deed of Apartment.
Obligation to ensure that the percentage of undivided interest in common areas is not separated from the apartment.
Joint and several liability for unpaid common expenses (as per section 23, though details are not in the extract).

key_procedures: Declaration of applicability for buildings with two or three apartments, followed by registration of a Deed of Apartment.
Execution and registration of a Deed of Apartment by the promoter.
Formation of an Association of Apartment Owners and making of bye-laws.
Assessment of common expenses by the Association of Apartment Owners.
Transfer of apartments and undivided interest in common areas through sale, mortgage, lease, gift, exchange, or bequest.
administration: The Administrator of the Union territory of Delhi, and potentially a 'competent authority' designated by the Administrator (Secretary in Delhi Administration, Vice-Chairman of DDA, or Land and Development Officer). The Association of Apartment Owners, through its Board or Manager, also plays an administrative role.
important_notes: The transferability of apartments by group housing co-operative societies is regulated by the law applicable to such societies.
The percentage of undivided interest in common areas and facilities has a permanent character and cannot be altered without the written consent of all apartment owners.
Any covenant contrary to the prohibition of partition of common areas and facilities shall be void.
The Act is binding on apartment owners, tenants, etc.

title: THE INDECENT REPRESENTATION OF WOMEN (PROHIBITION) ACT, 1986
purpose: To prohibit indecent representation of women through advertisements or in publications, writings, paintings, figures or in any other manner and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Prohibits indecent representation of women in advertisements, publications, writings, paintings, figures, and other forms. Specific exceptions are made for scientific, literary, artistic, or learning purposes, religious purposes, ancient monuments, temples, and films certified under the Cinematograph Act, 1952.

key_definitions.advertisement: Includes any notice, circular, label, wrapper or other document and also includes any visible representation made by means of any light, sound, smoke or gas.
key_definitions.distribution: Includes distribution by way of samples whether free or otherwise.
key_definitions.indecent_representation_of_women: Means the depiction in any manner of the figure of a woman, her form or body or any part thereof in such a way as to have the effect of being indecent, or derogatory to, or denigrating, women, or is likely to deprave, corrupt or injure the public morality or morals.
key_definitions.label: Means any written, marked, stamped, printed or graphic matter, affixed to, or appearing upon, any package.
key_definitions.package: Includes a box, carton, tin or other container.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'advertisement', 'distribution', 'indecent representation of women', 'label', 'package', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of advertisements containing indecent representation of women
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from publishing, arranging, or taking part in the publication or exhibition of any advertisement containing indecent representation of women.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of publication or sending by post of books, pamphlets, etc., containing indecent representation of women
main_sections.description: Prohibits the production, sale, hire, distribution, circulation, or posting of any book, pamphlet, paper, slide, film, writing, drawing, painting, photograph, representation, or figure containing indecent representation of women. Includes provisos for exceptions.

Grants powers to a Gazetted Officer authorized by the State Government to enter and search premises, seize offending materials, and examine records if there is reason to believe an offence under the Act has been committed. Private dwelling houses require a warrant for entry.
Specifies penalties for contravening sections 3 or 4, including imprisonment and fines, with enhanced penalties for second or subsequent convictions.
Holds companies and persons in charge responsible for offences committed by the company, with provisions for demonstrating lack of knowledge or due diligence.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable and bailable
main_sections.description: Declares offences under the Act to be bailable and cognizable.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act by the Central or State Governments or their officers.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including rules for seizure and seizure lists. Rules are subject to parliamentary approval.

important_rules: No person shall publish, arrange, or take part in the publication or exhibition of any advertisement that contains indecent representation of women (Section 3).

No person shall produce, sell, let to hire, distribute, circulate, or send by post any book, pamphlet, paper, slide, film, writing, drawing, painting, photograph, representation, or figure which contains indecent representation of women (Section 4).

Exceptions to Section 4 include publications justified for public good (science, literature, art, learning), religious purposes, ancient monuments, temples, and films certified under the Cinematograph Act, 1952 (Section 4 proviso).
A Gazetted Officer can enter and search premises suspected of containing offences, seize materials, and examine records. Entry into private dwellings requires a warrant (Section 5).
Offences are punishable with imprisonment and fines, with increased penalties for repeat offenders (Section 6).
If an offence is committed by a company, those in charge and responsible for the business are liable, unless they prove it was without their knowledge or they exercised due diligence (Section 7).

penalties: First conviction: Imprisonment up to two years and/or fine up to two thousand rupees.
Second or subsequent conviction: Imprisonment of not less than six months but up to five years and fine not less than ten thousand rupees but up to one lakh rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Gazetted Officers authorized by the State Government (for search and seizure).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through search and seizure powers granted to authorized officers, and prosecution for contraventions of the Act. The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, applies to search and seizure procedures.

rights: Right to protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith by government entities (Section 9).
Right to present a defense if accused of an offence by a company, by proving lack of knowledge or due diligence (Section 7).
duties: Duty of all persons not to publish or distribute materials containing indecent representation of women.
Duty of companies and their responsible personnel to ensure compliance with the Act.
Duty of officers to inform the nearest Magistrate about seizures and take their orders for custody (Section 5(3)).
obligations: Obligation to comply with rules made under the Act.
Obligation for companies to prevent offences and for individuals in charge to be responsible.
Obligation to adhere to the exceptions provided for certain publications and representations.

key_procedures: Entry and search of premises by authorized Gazetted Officers, with provisions for warrant for private dwelling houses.
Seizure of advertisements, books, pamphlets, and other materials believed to contravene the Act.
Examination of records and seizure of documents that may furnish evidence of an offence.
Reporting of seizures to the nearest Magistrate for custody orders.
Procedure for making and laying of rules before Parliament for approval or modification.
administration: Central Government (for making rules and appointing commencement date), State Government (for authorizing Gazetted Officers).
important_notes: The Act was extended to the whole of India, omitting the exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir (effective from 31-10-2019).
The Act came into force on 2nd October, 1987.
The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, apply to search and seizure under this Act.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a total of thirty days and are subject to modification or annulment.

title: THE GOA, DAMAN AND DIU REORGANISATION ACT, 1987
purpose: To provide for the reorganisation of the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu, and its reorganisation into the State of Goa and the Union territory of Daman and Diu. It covers representation in legislatures, the High Court, distribution of revenues, assets and liabilities, arrangements and corporations, inter-state agreements, services, and legal and miscellaneous provisions.

key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator appointed by the President under article 239.
key_definitions.appointed day: The day which the Central Government may, by notification, appoint.
key_definitions.existing Union territory: The Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu as existing immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having immediately before the appointed day, the force of law in the whole or any part of the existing Union territory.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'appointed day', 'article', 'assembly constituency', 'parliamentary constituency', 'Election Commission', 'existing Union territory', 'law', 'notification', 'population ratio', 'sitting member', and 'treasury'.
Establishes the State of Goa on and from the appointed day, comprising the territories of the Goa district of the existing Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Formation of Union territory of Daman and Diu
main_sections.description: Establishes the Union territory of Daman and Diu on and from the appointed day, comprising the territories of the Daman and Diu districts of the existing Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seats in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Allocates two seats to the State of Goa and one seat to the Union territory of Daman and Diu in the House of the People, amending the First Schedule to the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

main_sections.section_title: Common High Court for Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
main_sections.description: Provides for a common High Court for Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
Deals with the distribution of revenues between the newly formed State of Goa and the Union.
Addresses the transfer and continuance of contracts.
Specifies the territorial extent of laws applicable to the new State and Union territory.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: On and from the appointed day, a new State to be known as the State of Goa shall be formed, comprising the territories of the Goa district of the existing Union territory.

On and from the appointed day, a new Union territory to be known as the Union territory of Daman and Diu shall be formed, comprising the territories of the Daman and Diu districts of the existing Union territory.
On and from the appointed day, two seats shall be allotted to the State of Goa, and one seat to the Union territory of Daman and Diu in the House of the People.
The whole of the Union territory of Daman and Diu shall form one parliamentary constituency.

The Election Commission shall, in a prescribed manner, distribute the seats assigned to the Legislative Assembly of the State of Goa to single-member territorial constituencies and delimit them, having regard to constitutional provisions and specified factors.

The rules of procedure and conduct of business of the Legislative Assembly of the existing Union territory, as in force immediately before the appointed day, shall apply to the provisional Legislative Assembly until new rules are made.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Election Commission are key authorities for enforcement and administration of specific provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the provisions of the Act, including the delimitation of constituencies, allocation of seats, and the establishment of a common High Court. The Central Government has powers to issue directions and remove difficulties.

rights: Right to representation in the Council of States and the House of the People for the new State of Goa and Union territory of Daman and Diu.
Right to have a Legislative Assembly for the State of Goa.
Rights of sitting members of Parliament and the Legislative Assembly.
duties: Duty of the Election Commission to delimit constituencies.
Duty to maintain and adapt laws.
Duty to ensure the continuity of courts and services.
obligations: Obligation to form the new State of Goa and Union territory of Daman and Diu.
Obligation to conduct elections to fill allocated seats.
Obligation to arrange for the functioning of the common High Court.
Obligation to distribute revenues and apportion assets and liabilities.

key_procedures: Delimitation of constituencies for the Legislative Assembly of the State of Goa, involving the Election Commission, associate members, publication of proposals, and consideration of objections.
Conduct of elections to fill seats in the Council of States and the House of the People.
Procedure for the formation and functioning of the provisional Legislative Assembly of the State of Goa.
Procedure for the transfer of proceedings to the common High Court.
Procedure for the apportionment of assets or liabilities by agreement or order of the Central Government.
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative body, with the Election Commission playing a crucial role in electoral matters. The common High Court is established for judicial administration.
important_notes: Sections 5, 6, 14, and the First and Second Schedules were repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2001.
The 'appointed day' for the reorganisation was May 30, 1987, as notified by the Central Government.
Provisions for provisional legislative assembly are in place until the regular assembly is constituted.
The Act includes provisions for the continuity of existing arrangements, corporations, and inter-state agreements.

title: THE NATIONAL DAIRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 1987
purpose: To declare the institution known as the National Dairy Development Board in the State of Gujarat as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and for the vesting in that body corporate of the undertakings of the Indian Dairy Corporation with a view to provide for the administration and the carrying on of the functions to be performed by the body corporate more effectively throughout the country and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the National Dairy Development Board and the Indian Dairy Corporation. It aims to establish a more effective administration and functioning of the National Dairy Development Board throughout the country. The act declares the National Dairy Development Board, located in Gujarat, as an institution of national importance.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date of commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Directors of the National Dairy Development Board.
key_definitions.Chairman: The Chairman of the National Dairy Development Board.
key_definitions.director: A director of the National Dairy Development Board, and includes the Chairman.
key_definitions.foodstuffs: Such of the foodstuffs as are included in the definition of essential commodities as contained in clause (a) of section 2 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955).
key_definitions.Indian Dairy Corporation: The Indian Dairy Corporation, a company formed and registered under the Companies Act, and having its registered office at Baroda in the State of Gujarat.
key_definitions.milk_product: Includes sterilized, standardized, recombined, toned, double-toned, skimmed, flavoured or acidified milk, ice-cream, cream, cheese, butter, milk powders, weaning foods with milk and infant milk foods, malted milk foods with or without cocoa powder, ghee, anhydrous milk fat and butter oil, casein, and any other product containing milk or all or any of the milk products specified above which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify.
key_definitions.National Dairy Development Board: The National Dairy Development Board incorporated under section 4.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.restructuring_and_streamlining: In relation to the organisational and functional set-up of the National Dairy Development Board, includes opening or closing of units or offices; revision of the organisational and functional set-up; declaration of staff required; integration of posts, fixation of seniority and pay scales; integration of required personnel in the revised set-up and issuance of appointment orders; declaration or demarcation of duties and responsibilities attendant to posts; declaration of posts equivalent to one another; and any other matter that may be necessary or incidental to meet the organisational or functional needs of the National Dairy Development Board.
key_definitions.society: The National Dairy Development Board, a society formed and registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860) and functioning as such immediately before the appointed day.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of National Dairy Development Board as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Hereby declares the National Dairy Development Board in Gujarat as an institution of national importance.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Chairman', 'Companies Act', 'director', 'foodstuffs', 'Indian Dairy Corporation', 'milk product', 'National Dairy Development Board', 'prescribed', 'restructuring and streamlining', and 'society'.

main_sections.section_title: Incorporation of National Dairy Development Board
main_sections.description: Constitutes the National Dairy Development Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract. It also specifies the head office location and the power to establish units or offices elsewhere.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting of undertakings of Indian Dairy Corporation in National Dairy Development Board and dissolution of Indian Dairy Corporation
main_sections.description: States that all undertakings of the Indian Dairy Corporation will be transferred to and vest in the National Dairy Development Board on the appointed day, and the Indian Dairy Corporation will stand dissolved.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of incorporation of National Dairy Development Board
main_sections.description: Details the consequences of the incorporation, including the vesting of all properties and assets, transfer of rights, debts, liabilities, interests, privileges, and obligations, continuation of contracts and business, due sums, subsidiary status of existing subsidiaries, management of organizations, continuation of assistance, and the capital of the dissolved company forming part of the Board's funds. It also covers references to the society or dissolved company in other laws and instruments.

Ensures that pending legal proceedings by or against the society or the dissolved company will not abate or be affected by the incorporation or dissolution and may be continued by or against the National Dairy Development Board.

main_sections.section_title: Management of National Dairy Development Board and composition of its Board of Directors
main_sections.description: Vests the general superintendence, direction, control, and management of the Board in a Board of Directors. It outlines the composition of the Board, including a Chairman, a director from Central Government officials, two directors from State Co-operative Dairy Federations Chairmen, up to three whole-time directors from executives, and one external expert director. It also specifies the nomination process by the Central Government.

rights: The National Dairy Development Board has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract (Section 4(1)).
The National Dairy Development Board may establish units, offices, branches, or agencies in or outside India (Section 4(3)).
All rights, liabilities, interests, privileges, and obligations of the society and the Indian Dairy Corporation are transferred to the National Dairy Development Board (Section 6(b)).
Sums of money due to the society and the dissolved company become due to the National Dairy Development Board (Section 6(d)).
Every subsidiary of the society and the dissolved company becomes a subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board (Section 6(e)).
The National Dairy Development Board may continue to provide financial, managerial, or technical assistance to organizations (Section 6(g)).
The Board of Directors has the power to exercise all powers and do all acts and things that may be exercised or done by the National Dairy Development Board (Section 8(1)).
duties: The National Dairy Development Board is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, control, and management of its affairs and business (Section 8(1)).
obligations: The National Dairy Development Board is subject to the provisions of the Act (Section 4(1)).
The National Dairy Development Board must administer and carry on the functions to be performed more effectively throughout the country (Preamble).

All debts, liabilities, and obligations incurred, contracts entered into, and matters and things engaged to be done by, with, or for the society or the dissolved company are deemed to have been incurred, entered into, or engaged to be done by, with, or for, the National Dairy Development Board (Section 6(c)).

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).
Vesting of undertakings: On the appointed day, all undertakings of the Indian Dairy Corporation stand transferred to and vest in the National Dairy Development Board (Section 5(1)).
Dissolution of Indian Dairy Corporation: On the appointed day, the Indian Dairy Corporation stands dissolved (Section 5(2)).

Transfer of rights, liabilities, etc.: On the appointed day, all rights, debts, liabilities, interests, privileges, and obligations of the society and the Indian Dairy Corporation stand transferred to the National Dairy Development Board (Section 6(b)).

Continuation of legal proceedings: Pending legal proceedings by or against the society or the dissolved company may be continued, prosecuted, and enforced by or against the National Dairy Development Board (Section 7).

Composition and nomination of the Board of Directors: The Board of Directors is composed of specific members, and the Chairman and certain directors are nominated by the Central Government, with consultations for others (Section 8(2) & 8(3)).
administration: The Central Government, through its notifications and nominations, plays a significant role in the administration and oversight of the National Dairy Development Board.
important_notes: The National Dairy Development Board was previously a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
The Indian Dairy Corporation was a company formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
The functions of the Indian Dairy Corporation and the National Dairy Development Board were complementary.
The Act aims to ensure the continued freedom and flexibility of operation for the National Dairy Development Board to perform its functions more effectively.

title: THE LEGAL SERVICES AUTHORITIES ACT, 1987
purpose: To constitute legal services authorities to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of the society to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities, and to organize Lok Adalats to secure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice on a basis of equal opportunity.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It establishes various legal services authorities at the national, state, district, and taluk levels. It also covers the organization and functioning of Lok Adalats and Permanent Lok Adalats.

key_definitions.case: Includes a suit or any proceeding before a court.
key_definitions.Central Authority: The National Legal Services Authority constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.court: Means a civil, criminal or revenue court and includes any tribunal or any other authority constituted under any law for the time being in force, to exercise judicial or quasi-judicial functions.
key_definitions.District Authority: A District Legal Services Authority constituted under section 9.
key_definitions.High Court Legal Services Committee: A High Court Legal Services Committee constituted under section 8A.
key_definitions.legal service: Includes the rendering of any service in the conduct of any case or other legal proceeding before any court or other authority or tribunal and the giving of advice on any legal matter.
key_definitions.Lok Adalat: A Lok Adalat organised under Chapter VI.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.scheme: Any scheme framed by the Central Authority, a State Authority or a District Authority for the purpose of giving effect to any of the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.State Authority: A State Legal Services Authority constituted under section 6.
key_definitions.State Government: Includes the administrator of a Union territory appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.Supreme Court Legal Services Committee: The Supreme Court Legal Services Committee constituted under section 3A.
key_definitions.Taluk Legal Services Committee: A Taluk Legal Services Committee constituted under section 11A.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date, which can be appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'case', 'Central Authority', 'court', 'District Authority', 'legal service', 'Lok Adalat', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'scheme', 'State Authority', 'State Government', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the National Legal Services Authority.
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Legal Services Authority (Central Authority) with the Chief Justice of India as Patron-in-Chief, a Supreme Court Judge as Executive Chairman, and other nominated members. It also details the appointment of the Member-Secretary and other staff, terms of office, and administrative expenses.
Provides for the constitution of a Supreme Court Legal Services Committee to exercise powers and perform functions determined by regulations, headed by a sitting Supreme Court Judge.

Outlines the functions of the Central Authority, including laying down policies, framing schemes for legal services, allocating funds, taking social justice litigation steps, organizing legal aid camps, encouraging dispute settlement, promoting research, ensuring commitment to fundamental duties, monitoring programs, providing grants-in-aid, developing legal education, spreading legal literacy, enlisting support of voluntary institutions, and coordinating the functioning of various legal service bodies.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of State Legal Services Authority.
main_sections.description: Details the constitution of a State Legal Services Authority for each State, with the Chief Justice of the High Court as Patron-in-Chief, a High Court Judge as Executive Chairman, and other nominated members.
Provides for the constitution of a District Legal Services Authority for each district.
Specifies the criteria that determine eligibility for receiving legal services under the Act.
Defines who is entitled to receive legal services.
Describes how Lok Adalats are to be organized.

main_sections.section_title: Cognizance of cases by Lok Adalats.
main_sections.description: Explains which cases can be taken up by Lok Adalats.
Details the nature and effect of an award made by a Lok Adalat.
Provides definitions specific to Chapter VIA concerning pre-litigation conciliation and settlement.
Deals with the establishment of Permanent Lok Adalats.

main_sections.section_title: Cognizance of cases by Permanent Lok Adalat.
main_sections.description: Specifies the types of cases that can be brought before a Permanent Lok Adalat.

main_sections.section_title: Award of Permanent Lok Adalat to be final.
main_sections.description: States that the award of a Permanent Lok Adalat is final.
States that this Act has an overriding effect on other laws where inconsistent.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Authority to make regulations.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Authority to make regulations for the efficient discharge of its functions.

important_rules: The Central Government shall constitute the National Legal Services Authority (Central Authority).
The Central Authority shall consist of the Chief Justice of India (Patron-in-Chief), a Supreme Court Judge (Executive Chairman), and other nominated members.
Every State Government shall constitute a State Legal Services Authority.
A State Authority shall consist of the Chief Justice of the High Court (Patron-in-Chief), a High Court Judge (Executive Chairman), and other nominated members.
Criteria for giving legal services are specified in Section 12.
Entitlement to legal services is outlined in Section 13.
Lok Adalats are to be organized as per Chapter VI.
Permanent Lok Adalats can be established as per Chapter VIA.
Members and staff of Authorities, Committees, and Lok Adalats are deemed to be public servants (Section 23).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities established under the Act, including the National Legal Services Authority, State Legal Services Authorities, District Legal Services Authorities, High Court Legal Services Committees, Supreme Court Legal Services Committee, and Taluk Legal Services Committees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provision of legal services, organization of Lok Adalats and Permanent Lok Adalats for dispute resolution, and the enforcement of awards and decisions made by these bodies. Specific enforcement mechanisms for penalties are not detailed in the provided text but would likely be through standard legal proceedings.

rights: Right to free and competent legal services for weaker sections of society.
Opportunity to secure justice should not be denied due to economic or other disabilities.
Access to justice through the operation of the legal system on a basis of equal opportunity.
duties: Duty of the Central Authority to lay down policies, frame schemes, and allocate funds for legal services.
Duty of State and District Authorities to implement legal services programs.
Duty to organize Lok Adalats to promote justice.
Duty to spread legal literacy and legal awareness amongst the people.

key_procedures: Constitution of National, State, District, and Taluk Legal Services Authorities and Committees.
Application for and provision of legal services based on defined criteria and entitlement.
Organization and functioning of Lok Adalats for dispute settlement.
Establishment and operation of Permanent Lok Adalats for pre-litigation conciliation and settlement.
Making rules and regulations by the Central and State Governments and the Central and State Authorities.
Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament or State Legislatures.
administration: The National Legal Services Authority (Central Authority) and State Legal Services Authorities are responsible for the administration of the Act. The Central Government and State Governments also play a significant role in making rules and providing oversight.
important_notes: The Act was amended to remove the exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Different commencement dates can be appointed for different provisions and different States.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning it prevails over other laws in case of inconsistency.

title: The All India Council for Technical Education Act, 1987
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an All India Council for Technical Education for the proper planning and co-ordinated development of the technical education system throughout the country, promoting qualitative improvement in relation to planned quantitative growth, and regulating and maintaining norms and standards in the technical education system.
scope: Applies to technical education and technical institutions throughout India. This includes programs in engineering, technology, architecture, town planning, management, pharmacy, applied arts and crafts, and other areas declared by the Central Government. Universities are included when imparting technical education.

key_definitions.Commission: The University Grants Commission established under section 4 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.
key_definitions.Council: The All India Council for Technical Education established under section 3.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Council constituted under section 16.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Council, including the Chairman and Vice-Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.technical education: Programs of education, research, and training in engineering, technology, architecture, town planning, management, pharmacy, applied arts and crafts, and other areas as declared by the Central Government in consultation with the Council.
key_definitions.technical institution: An institution, not being a University, that offers courses or programs of technical education, including those declared as such by the Central Government in consultation with the Council.
key_definitions.University: A University defined under clause (f) of section 2 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, and includes an institution deemed to be a University under section 3 of that Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and provides for its commencement on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Commission', 'Council', 'Fund', 'member', 'prescribed', 'regulations', 'technical education', 'technical institution', and 'University'.

Provides for the establishment of the All India Council for Technical Education as a body corporate. It outlines the composition of the Council, including ex officio members and appointed members representing various government ministries, Parliament, states and union territories, industry, commerce, educational bodies, and professional organizations. It also details the appointment of the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and Member-Secretary, and provisions for the first appointments.

Specifies the term of office for members (five years for the first constitution, then three years for non-ex officio members). It also details procedures for filling casual vacancies in the office of the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, or other members.

Outlines the procedures for Council meetings, including time, place, quorum, and rules of procedure as provided by regulations. It mandates at least one meeting per year and details the presiding officer and voting procedures.

Details the duties and powers of the Council, including undertaking surveys, collecting data, forecasting needs, coordinating technical education development, disbursing grants, promoting innovations, formulating schemes for various sections of society, linking education with industry, evolving appraisal systems, formulating teacher training schemes, laying down norms and standards for courses, curricula, facilities, staff, fees, granting approvals for new institutions and courses, and advising the Central Government on granting charters to professional bodies.

important_rules: The Council shall have a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and a Member-Secretary, appointed by the Central Government.
The Council shall have a defined composition with representation from various government bodies, Parliament, states, industry, and educational institutions.
Non-ex officio members have a term of office of three years (after the initial five-year term for the first constitution).
The Council shall meet at least once every year.
All questions before the Council shall be decided by a majority vote, with the Chairman having a casting vote.
The Council may associate persons for assistance or advice, who can participate in discussions but not vote.
The Council shall take steps for the co-ordinated and integrated development of technical education and maintenance of standards.
The Council can grant approval for starting new technical institutions and introducing new courses/programmes.
The Council shall lay down norms and standards for courses, curricula, facilities, staff, and examinations.
The Council can advise the Central Government regarding the grant of charters to professional bodies.
