penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Council are implicitly responsible for enforcement through their powers and functions outlined in the Act. Specific penalties are not detailed in the provided text, but Section 21 grants the Central Government the power to supersede the Council.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the Council's functions such as setting norms and standards, granting approvals, advising the government, and through the Central Government's power to make rules, regulations, and supersede the Council.

rights: Right of the Council to undertake surveys, collect data, and forecast needs in technical education.
Right of the Council to coordinate technical education development.
Right of the Council to allocate and disburse grants to technical institutions and Universities.
Right of the Council to promote innovations and research.
Right of the Council to formulate schemes for various societal sections.
Right of the Council to evolve performance appraisal systems and enforce accountability.
Right of the Council to lay down norms and standards.
Right of the Council to grant approval for new institutions and courses.
Right of the Council to advise the Central Government.
duties: Duty of the Council to ensure coordinated and integrated development of technical education.
Duty of the Council to maintain standards in technical education.
Duty of the Council to promote qualitative improvement and planned quantitative growth.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Council by the Central Government notification.
Appointment of Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and Member-Secretary.
Conduct of Council meetings according to regulations, including quorum and voting.
Filling of casual vacancies in the Council.
Temporary association of persons with the Council for specific purposes.
Appointment of officers and employees of the Council, subject to Central Government approval for certain categories.
Authentication of Council orders and instruments.
Submission of an annual report by the Council to the Central Government.
Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament.
Removal of difficulties by the Central Government.
administration: The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 28th March, 1988.
The first Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and Member-Secretary were the Minister of Human Resource Development, Minister of State for Education, and Educational Adviser (Technical) respectively.
The Central Government has the power to supersede the Council in certain circumstances (Section 21).
The Central Government has the power to make rules and the Council has the power to make regulations, both of which must be laid before Parliament (Sections 22, 23, 24).

title: The Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Board to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote the development of, and to regulate, the securities market and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the securities market, investors, and entities involved in the issuance and trading of securities.

key_definitions.Board: The Securities and Exchange Board of India established under section 3.
key_definitions.collective investment scheme: Any scheme or arrangement which satisfies the conditions specified in section 11AA.
key_definitions.existing Securities and Exchange Board: The Securities and Exchange Board of India constituted under the Resolution of the Government of India in the Department of Economic Affairs No. 1(44)SE/86, dated the 12th day of April, 1988.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund constituted under section 14.
key_definitions.securities: Has the meaning assigned to it in section 2 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title as the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, its territorial extent (whole of India), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on January 30, 1992).

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairman', 'Fund', 'securities', and others. It also states that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 or the Depositories Act, 1996 shall have their respective meanings.

Establishes the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of acquiring, holding, and disposing of property, and suing or being sued. The head office is in Bombay, and other offices can be established in India.

Outlines the composition of the Board, consisting of a Chairman, members from the Central Government (dealing with Finance and Companies Act administration), a member from the Reserve Bank, and five other members (at least three whole-time). It vests general superintendence, direction, and management in the Board of members, with the Chairman having powers of general superintendence and direction.
Details the various functions of the Board, which include protecting investors, promoting the development of and regulating the securities market.

main_sections.section_title: Board to regulate or prohibit issue of prospectus, offer document or advertisement soliciting money for issue of securities
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to regulate or prohibit the issue of prospectus, offer documents, or advertisements soliciting money for the issue of securities.

main_sections.section_title: Power to issue directions and levy penalty
main_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to issue directions to intermediaries and other persons associated with the securities market and to levy penalties for violations.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of stock-brokers, sub-brokers, share transfer agents, etc.
main_sections.description: Mandates the registration of stock-brokers, sub-brokers, share transfer agents, and other intermediaries with the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to furnish information, return, etc.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for the failure to furnish information, returns, or documents to the Board.
Defines penalties for engaging in insider trading.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal
main_sections.description: Provides for the right to appeal against orders passed by the Board to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the Board.
Grants the Board the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules made thereunder.
Provides for the repeal of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Ordinance, 1992, and savings.

important_rules: The Board is empowered to regulate the securities market, protect investor interests, and promote market development (Section 11).
The Board has the authority to issue directions and levy penalties for violations (Section 11B).
Entities like stock-brokers, sub-brokers, and share transfer agents must be registered with the Board (Section 12).
Insider trading is prohibited and attracts penalties (Section 15G).
Appeals against the Board's orders can be made to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (Section 15T).

penalties: Penalty for failure to furnish information, return, etc. (Section 15A)
Penalty for failure by any person to enter into agreement with clients (Section 15B)
Penalty for failure to redress investors’ grievances (Section 15C)
Penalty for certain defaults in case of mutual funds (Section 15D)
Penalty for failure to observe rules and regulations by an asset management company (Section 15E)
Penalty for default in case of alternative investment funds, infrastructure investment trusts and real estate investment trusts (Section 15EA)
Penalty for default in case of investment adviser and research analyst (Section 15EB)
Penalty for default in case of stock brokers (Section 15F)
Penalty for insider trading (Section 15G)
Penalty for non-disclosure of acquisition of shares and takeovers (Section 15H)
Penalty for fraudulent and unfair trade practices (Section 15HA)
Penalty for alteration, destruction, etc., of records and failure to protect the electronic database of Board (Section 15HAA)
Penalty for contravention where no separate penalty has been provided (Section 15HB)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation (Section 11C), adjudication (Section 15-I), imposition of penalties, issuance of directions, and the establishment of a Securities Appellate Tribunal for appeals (Chapter VIB).

rights: Investors have the right to have their interests protected.
Entities involved in the securities market have the right to appeal against SEBI's orders to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (Section 15T).
The Board has the right to issue directions and levy penalties (Section 11B).
The Board has the right to investigate matters related to the securities market (Section 11C).
duties: The Board has a duty to protect the interests of investors.
The Board has a duty to promote the development of the securities market.
The Board has a duty to regulate the securities market.
Entities are duty-bound to comply with the rules and regulations framed by SEBI.
Persons associated with the securities market have a duty to avoid insider trading and manipulative practices.
obligations: Obligation to register with SEBI for stock-brokers, sub-brokers, etc. (Section 12).
Obligation to furnish information and returns as required by SEBI.
Obligation to comply with directions issued by SEBI (Section 11B).
Obligation to prevent insider trading and manipulative devices (Chapter VA).

key_procedures: Establishment of SEBI: Appointment of a Board by the Central Government with specific composition and management structure (Sections 3 & 4).

Regulation of Securities Market: SEBI functions include investor protection, market development, and regulation, including prohibiting manipulative devices and insider trading (Sections 11, 11A, 12A).
Registration of Intermediaries: Stock-brokers, sub-brokers, etc., must obtain registration from SEBI (Section 12).
Investigation and Adjudication: SEBI can investigate offenses and has the power to adjudicate penalties (Sections 11C & 15-I).
Appeals: Appeals against SEBI's orders lie with the Securities Appellate Tribunal (Section 15T), and further appeals to the Supreme Court (Section 15Z).
administration: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
important_notes: The Act was originally an Ordinance and was subsequently enacted as an Act. It was deemed to have come into force on January 30, 1992 (Section 1(3)).
The Act has been amended multiple times by various amending Acts listed at the beginning of the document.
The Board is vested with broad powers to ensure the integrity and functioning of the securities market.

title: The Tezpur University Act, 1993
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and residential University in the State of Assam at Tezpur and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Geographical scope is the State of Assam. Subject matter scope includes the establishment, incorporation, powers, administration, and functioning of Tezpur University as a teaching and residential institution.

key_definitions.University: The Tezpur University established under this Act.
key_definitions.academic_staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University, including teachers and other staff.
key_definitions.teachers_of_the_University: Professors, Readers, Lecturers and other persons appointed for instruction or research, designated as teachers by the Ordinances.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'Board of Management', 'College', 'employee', 'Statutes', 'Ordinances', and 'University'.
Establishes the Tezpur University, defines its headquarters at Tezpur, allows for campuses at other places, and constitutes it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objectives of the University, including disseminating and advancing knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, promoting integrated courses, innovations in teaching-learning, educating and training manpower for Assam, and improving social, economic, intellectual, academic, and cultural development of the people of Assam.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting diplomas and degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, conferring honorary degrees, providing distance education, establishing teaching positions, recognizing institutions, creating posts, collaborating with other institutions, establishing campuses, awarding fellowships, maintaining colleges and halls, providing research services, organizing refresher courses, making special arrangements for women students, appointing visiting professors, conferring autonomous status, determining admission standards, demanding fees, supervising student residence, laying down conditions of service for employees, regulating discipline, promoting employee welfare, receiving benefactions, acquiring and disposing of property, and borrowing money.
Specifies that the jurisdiction of the University extends to the whole of the State of Assam.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: States that the University is open to all sexes, castes, creeds, races, or classes and prohibits any tests of religious belief for appointment, admission, or graduation. It allows for special provisions for women, physically handicapped, and weaker sections including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Mandates that all students (except those in distance education) must reside in a Hall or hostel or under conditions prescribed by Ordinances.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and outlines the Visitor's powers to review work and progress, appoint inspectors, cause inquiries, take action based on reports, and issue directions to the University.

important_rules: Students (other than distance education) must reside in university-provided accommodation (Section 8).
The University must be open to all individuals regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, without religious tests (Section 7).
The Visitor (President of India) has the power to inspect and inquire into the University's functioning and issue directions (Section 9).
The University's jurisdiction is limited to the State of Assam (Section 6).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act does not explicitly detail penalties for violations by individuals. Enforcement of the University's regulations and disciplinary measures is within the University's powers (Section 5(xxiv)). The Visitor has significant oversight and can issue directions that the University must comply with (Section 9).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the University's internal disciplinary mechanisms, and by the Visitor's powers of inspection, inquiry, and direction.

rights: Right to admission to the University for all individuals regardless of background (subject to special provisions for certain groups) (Section 7).
Right of the University to have perpetual succession and a common seal, and to sue and be sued (Section 3(4)).
Right of the University to determine admission standards (Section 5(xx)).
Right of representation to the Visitor during inspections or inquiries (Section 9(4)).
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases against students (Section 33).
duties: Duty of the University to be open to all without discrimination (Section 7).
Duty of the University to comply with directions issued by the Visitor (Section 9(2)).
Duty to make provisions for integrated courses, research, and to promote innovations (Section 4).
obligations: Obligation of students to reside in prescribed accommodation (Section 8).
Obligation of the University to provide instructional and research facilities (Section 4).
Obligation of the University to promote the social, economic, intellectual, academic, and cultural development of the people of Assam (Section 4).

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Upon notification by the Central Government (Section 1(2)).
Making Statutes: As prescribed by Section 27.
Making Ordinances: As prescribed by Section 28.
Making Regulations: As prescribed by Section 29.

Visitor's inspection/inquiry: Notice to University, University's representation, Visitor's decision on inspection/inquiry, University's right to representation during proceedings, Visitor's address to Vice-Chancellor, communication to Board of Management (Section 9).
Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students (Section 33).
administration: The Tezpur University itself, with its various authorities (Board of Management, Academic Council, etc.) and officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer), as established and empowered by the Act.
important_notes: The Act was to come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, which was January 15, 1994 (as per footnote).
Special provisions can be made for employment or admission of women, physically handicapped, or persons from weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 7 proviso).

title: THE EMPLOYMENT OF MANUAL SCAVENGERS AND CONSTRUCTION OF DRY LATRINES (PROHIBITION) ACT, 1993
purpose: To provide for the prohibition of employment of manual scavengers as well as construction or continuance of dry latrines and for the regulation of construction and maintenance of water-seal latrines and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The Act aims to abolish manual scavenging and ban further proliferation of dry latrines, thereby protecting and improving the human environment and ensuring the dignity of individuals.
scope: Applies to the States of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tripura, and West Bengal, and to all Union territories. It can also be adopted by other states through a resolution under Article 252(1) of the Constitution. The Act's provisions apply to specified areas within these states and Union territories, as notified by the State Government.

key_definitions.area: Such area as the State Government may, having regard to the requirements of that provision, specify by notification.
key_definitions.building: A house, out-house, stable, latrine, urinal, sheet house, hut, wall (other than a boundary wall) or any other structure whether made of masonry, bricks, wood, mud, metal or other material.
key_definitions.dry_latrine: A latrine other than a water-seal latrine.
key_definitions.environment: Includes water, air and land and the inter-relationship which exists among and between water, air and land and human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organism and property.
key_definitions.environmental_pollutant: Any solid, liquid or gaseous substance present in such concentration as may be, or tend to be, injurious to environment.
key_definitions.environmental_pollution: The presence in the environment of any environmental pollutant.
key_definitions.Executive_Authority: An Executive Authority appointed under sub-section (1) of section 5.
key_definitions.HUDCO: The Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited.
key_definitions.latrine: A place set apart for defecation together with the structure comprising such place, the receptacle therein for collection of human excreta and the fittings and apparatus, if any, connected therewith.
key_definitions.manual_scavenger: A person engaged in or employed for manually carrying human excreta.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.State_Government: In relation to a Union territory, means the Administrator thereof appointed under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.water_seal_latrine: A pour-flush latrine, water flush latrine or a sanitary latrine with a minimum water-seal of 20 millimetres diameter in which human excreta is pushed in or flushed by water.

main_sections.description: This section specifies the short title of the Act as the Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993. It details the geographical application of the Act, initially to specific states and Union territories, and outlines the commencement of the Act, which is to be appointed by the Central Government through notification.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'area', 'building', 'dry latrine', 'environment', 'environmental pollutant', 'environmental pollution', 'Executive Authority', 'HUDCO', 'latrine', 'manual scavenger', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'State Government', and 'water-seal latrine'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of employment of manual scavengers, etc.
main_sections.description: This section prohibits the engagement or employment of any person for manually carrying human excreta and prohibits the construction or maintenance of dry latrines. The prohibition takes effect from a date and in an area specified by the State Government through notification, provided that adequate notice is given, water-seal latrines are available, and it is necessary for environmental or public health protection.

This section grants the State Government the power to exempt any area, category of buildings, or class of persons from any provision of the Act or any requirement contained in the Act, rules, orders, notifications, or schemes, if it deems fit and upon such conditions as it may impose.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Executive Authorities and their powers and functions
main_sections.description: The State Government may appoint a District Magistrate or Sub-Divisional Magistrate as an Executive Authority to exercise jurisdiction within a specified area. This authority is empowered to ensure the Act's provisions are carried out and can delegate powers and duties to subordinate officers. The Executive Authority is also tasked with rehabilitating and promoting the welfare of persons who were engaged as manual scavengers.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make schemes
main_sections.description: The State Government can make schemes for regulating the conversion of dry latrines to water-seal latrines, their construction and maintenance, and the rehabilitation of former manual scavengers. Schemes may include time-bound programs, provision of technical/financial assistance, community latrines, shared latrines in slum areas, registration and rehabilitation of manual scavengers, and specification of latrine standards.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: The State Government can issue written directions to any person, officer, or authority to ensure compliance with the Act, and such directions are binding.

main_sections.section_title: Executive Authorities, inspectors, officers and other employees of such authorities to be public servants
main_sections.description: All Executive Authorities, inspectors, officers, and employees involved in executing the Act or its schemes are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of inspectors and their powers of entry and inspection
main_sections.description: The State Government can appoint inspectors with defined local limits of jurisdiction. Inspectors are subordinate to the Executive Authority and have powers to enter any place at reasonable times to perform their functions, ascertain compliance with the Act, and inspect buildings where an offence may have been committed or to prevent environmental pollution.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Executive Authority to prevent environmental pollution in certain cases
main_sections.description: If there's information about contravention of Section 3, the Executive Authority must direct the owner/occupier to take remedial measures. If the owner/occupier fails to comply, the Executive Authority can cause such measures to be taken at the owner's/occupier's cost to prevent or mitigate environmental pollution.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act and rules, orders, directions and schemes.
main_sections.description: This section outlines penalties for violating the Act's provisions, rules, orders, directions, and schemes.
This section addresses how offences committed by companies are to be handled under the Act.
This section states that offences under the Act are cognizable.
This section deals with the jurisdiction of courts in relation to offences under the Act.
This section specifies the time limit for initiating prosecution for offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: This section grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: This section grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act, consistent with the rules made by the Central Government.
This section provides the Central Government with the power to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: No person shall engage in or employ another person for manually carrying human excreta.
No person shall construct or maintain a dry latrine.

State Governments must provide at least ninety days' notice before prohibiting manual scavenging or dry latrines, ensure adequate water-seal latrine facilities exist, and deem it necessary for environmental or public health protection.
State Governments shall, as far as practicable, try to rehabilitate and promote the welfare of persons previously engaged as manual scavengers by securing and protecting their economic interests.

Schemes may provide for time-bound conversion of dry latrines, financial assistance for sanitation, construction and use of community or shared latrines, registration and rehabilitation of manual scavengers, and specification of water-seal latrine standards.
All Executive Authorities, inspectors, officers, and employees acting under the Act are deemed public servants.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act and rules, orders, directions and schemes (detailed in Section 14).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Executive Authorities (appointed by the State Government, typically District or Sub-Divisional Magistrates) and Inspectors (appointed by the State Government).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment and powers of Executive Authorities and Inspectors, who can direct remedial measures, conduct inspections, and ensure compliance with the Act, rules, orders, and schemes. Offences are cognizable.

rights: Right to dignity assured by the Preamble to the Constitution, which the Act aims to uphold by eliminating manual scavenging.
Right to a protected and improved human environment.
Right to adequate sanitation facilities (water-seal latrines).
duties: Duty of the State to regard raising the standard of living and improvement of public health as primary duties.
Duty of persons, officers, and local/other authorities to comply with directions issued by the State Government under the Act.
Duty of Executive Authorities and officers to try to rehabilitate and promote the welfare of former manual scavengers.
obligations: Obligation not to engage in or employ for manual scavenging.
Obligation not to construct or maintain dry latrines.
Obligation of owners/occupiers to take remedial measures to prevent or mitigate environmental pollution when directed by the Executive Authority.
Obligation to convert dry latrines to water-seal latrines as per schemes.

key_procedures: Notification by State Government of its intention to prohibit manual scavenging or dry latrines with at least 90 days' notice, ensuring availability of water-seal latrines and necessity for environmental/public health.
Appointment of Executive Authorities and Inspectors by the State Government.
Inspection of premises by Inspectors to ascertain compliance or commission of offences.
Issuance of directions by Executive Authority to owners/occupiers to take remedial measures to prevent environmental pollution, with provision for execution at their cost if they fail to comply.
Development and implementation of schemes by the State Government for conversion of latrines and rehabilitation of manual scavengers.
Prosecution for offences under the Act, subject to limitations on prosecution.
administration: State Governments and their appointed Executive Authorities and Inspectors. The Central Government has powers to make rules and remove difficulties.
important_notes: The Act was enacted based on resolutions passed by the Legislatures of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tripura, and West Bengal under Article 252(1) of the Constitution.
The Act emphasizes the dignity of the individual and the State's duty to improve public health and living standards.
Exemptions from the Act's provisions can be granted by the State Government under certain conditions.
HUDCO has a role in providing financial assistance for schemes.
The Act aims for uniform legislation across India for the specified matters.
The Act extends to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh from October 31, 2019.

title: THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR SAFAI KARAMCHARIS ACT, 1993
purpose: To constitute a National Commission for Safai Karamcharis and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to Safai Karamcharis, defined as persons engaged in or employed for manually carrying human excreta or any sanitation work.

key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Commission.
key_definitions.Commission: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Safai Karamchari: A person engaged in, or employed for, manually carrying human excreta or any sanitation work.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application, commencement, duration and savings.
main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), commencement date, duration (until February 29, 2004, with savings for past actions), and provisions for savings.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including Chairperson, Commission, Member, prescribed, Safai Karamchari, and Vice-Chairperson.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis.
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis, to be constituted by the Central Government. It outlines the composition of the Commission, including a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, and five Members nominated by the Central Government, with at least one woman Member.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and Members.
main_sections.description: Details the term of office for the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and Members, their conditions of service, resignation provisions, grounds for removal from office (insolvency, conviction, unsound mind, inability to act, absence from meetings, abuse of position), and the process for filling vacancies.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and other employees of the Commission.
main_sections.description: States that the Central Government shall provide the Commission with necessary officers and employees and that their terms and conditions of service will be as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancy, etc., not to invalidate the proceedings of the Commission.
main_sections.description: Ensures that the existence of any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Commission does not invalidate its acts or proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be regulated by the Commission.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Commission to regulate its own procedure, including meeting times and places, and mandates that its orders and decisions be authenticated.

main_sections.section_title: Functions and powers of the Commission.
main_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the Commission, including recommending action plans for the elimination of inequalities for Safai Karamcharis, studying and evaluating rehabilitation programs, investigating grievances, taking suo moto notice of non-implementation of relevant schemes or laws, making reports to governments, and undertaking other matters referred by the Central Government. It also grants the Commission the power to call for information from any government or authority.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and Members and staff of the Commission to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares that the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Members, officers, and employees of the Commission are deemed to be public servants under the Indian Penal Code.
Mandates that the Central Government shall consult the Commission on all major policy matters affecting Safai Karamcharis.
Requires the Commission to prepare an annual report detailing its activities during the previous financial year and submit it to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report to be laid before Parliament or the Legislative Assembly.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Central Government shall lay the annual report before Parliament, along with a memorandum on actions taken or proposed regarding the recommendations. If the report relates to a State Government, a copy is to be forwarded to the Governor to be laid before the State Legislature with a similar memorandum.
Allows the Commission to delegate its powers and duties to the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, any Member, or any officer of the Commission, subject to specified conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act by the Central Government, Commission, or its personnel.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including rules for salaries and allowances, terms and conditions of service, the format and timing of annual reports, and other prescribed matters. It also outlines the procedure for laying such rules before Parliament.

important_rules: Rule to be prescribed by the Central Government for salaries, allowances, and terms and conditions of service for the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Members, and staff.
Rule to be prescribed for the form and time for preparation of the annual report.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days and are subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis, with the Central Government and State Governments involved in policy matters and legislative actions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through recommendations to the Central and State Governments, investigation of grievances, taking suo moto notice of non-implementation of laws and schemes, and periodic reporting. The Central Government is responsible for making rules and laying reports before Parliament.

rights: Right to have grievances investigated by the Commission.
Right to benefit from programs and schemes for social and economic rehabilitation.
Right to have the Commission recommend action plans for elimination of inequalities.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to consult the Commission on major policy matters affecting Safai Karamcharis.
Duty of the Central Government to provide officers and employees to the Commission.
Duty of the Commission to prepare and submit an annual report.
Duty of the Central Government to lay the annual report before Parliament.
Duty of State Governments to address recommendations related to them.
obligations: Obligation on the Central Government to constitute the Commission.
Obligation on the Commission to perform its functions and exercise its powers.
Obligation on government and local authorities to provide information to the Commission when called upon.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Commission: Central Government issues notification.
Nomination of Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and Members: Central Government nominates persons of eminence.
Term of Office: Specified period not exceeding three years, subject to various conditions and amendments.
Removal of office bearers: Grounds specified and a reasonable opportunity of being heard must be given.
Filling of vacancies: By fresh nomination for the unexpired term.
Commission Meetings: As necessary, at a time and place determined by the Chairperson; procedure regulated by the Commission.
Investigation of grievances: Commission investigates specific grievances and takes suo moto notice of matters relating to non-implementation of programs or laws.
Reporting: Commission makes periodical reports to Central and State Governments; prepares an annual report.
Laying of Annual Report: Central Government lays the report before Parliament; State Governments lay it before their Legislatures.
Rule-making: Central Government makes rules via notification, subject to parliamentary approval.
administration: The Central Government, with the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis acting as the primary administrative and advisory body.
important_notes: The Act was initially set to cease to have effect on February 29, 2004, but this duration might have been subject to further extension or amendment.
The Act originally excluded the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but this exclusion was omitted later.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith by the Central Government, Commission, and its personnel.
The Commission's proceedings are not invalidated by vacancies or defects in its constitution.

title: THE KALAKSHETRA FOUNDATION ACT, 1993
purpose: To declare Kalakshetra of Madras as an institution of national importance, to provide for the establishment and incorporation of a Foundation for its administration, and to make provisions for further development of Kalakshetra in accordance with its founding aims and objects.
scope: The Act applies to the institution known as Kalakshetra situated at Adyar, Madras, and its constituent units. It covers the acquisition and transfer of its assets and properties, the establishment and functioning of the Kalakshetra Foundation, and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The Act is enacted by the Parliament of India and has come into force on September 29, 1993.

key_definitions.Academic Committee: The Academic Committee constituted under section 15.
key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which the Foundation is established under sub-section (1) of section 8.
key_definitions.Board of Trustees: The Board of Trustees managing the affairs of Kalakshetra under the 'scheme writ' approved by the Madras High Court in petition No. 716 of 1985.
key_definitions.constituent units: The units of Kalakshetra specified in the First Schedule.
key_definitions.Director: The Director appointed under sub-section (1) of section 19.
key_definitions.Finance Committee: The Finance Committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 17.
key_definitions.Foundation: The Kalakshetra Foundation established under sub-section (1) of section 8.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Foundation referred to in section 22.
key_definitions.Governing Board: The Governing Board constituted under section 11.
key_definitions.Kalakshetra: The institution known as Kalakshetra founded by the late Thirumathi Rukmini Devi Arundale, situated at Adyar, Madras, and includes its constituent units.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Governing Board and includes the Chairperson thereof.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made under section 32.
key_definitions.Schedule: A Schedule annexed to this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the 'Kalakshetra Foundation Act, 1993' and states that it is deemed to have come into force on September 29, 1993.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Kalakshetra as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the institution known as Kalakshetra at Adyar, Madras, founded by late Thirumathi Rukmini Devi Arundale, as an institution of national importance due to its objects.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Academic Committee, appointed day, Board of Trustees, constituent units, Director, Finance Committee, Foundation, Fund, Governing Board, Kalakshetra, notification, Member, prescribed, regulations, Schedule, and State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the assets and properties of Kalakshetra
main_sections.description: States that upon commencement of the Act, the right, title, and interest in the assets and properties of Kalakshetra, vested in the Board of Trustees or any other body, shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government.

Details the general effect of vesting, including the inclusion of all assets, rights, leaseholds, powers, properties, instruments, and documents. It also specifies that vested assets are freed from trusts, mortgages, charges, liens, and encumbrances, and any pending proceedings shall not abate but may be continued by the Central Government or the Foundation.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government to direct vesting of assets and properties in the Foundation
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct, by notification, that the assets and properties vested in it shall vest in the Foundation on a specified date. Upon such vesting, the Foundation becomes the owner and assumes the rights and liabilities of the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of persons to deliver and to account for assets, properties, etc.
main_sections.description: Mandates persons in charge of Kalakshetra's assets and properties to deliver them, along with books of account and documents, to the Central Government or the Foundation. It also makes such persons liable to account for these assets and properties.

Provides for the establishment of the Kalakshetra Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property. Its office is to be located at Thiruvanmiyur, Madras.

Outlines the objects of the Foundation, including emphasizing the unity of arts, promoting arts for individual and national growth, maintaining artistic traditions, facilitating training and research in arts, and adhering to principles of 'education without fear' and 'art without vulgarity'.
Specifies the authorities of the Foundation: the Governing Board, the Academic Committee, and the Finance Committee. These authorities are to be guided by the objects of the Foundation.

Details the composition of the Governing Board, including a Chairperson appointed by the Central Government, Members nominated by the Central and State Governments, and ex officio officers representing relevant Ministries and Departments.

Defines the term of office for Members of the Governing Board as five years, provisions for filling casual vacancies, eligibility for re-nomination, resignation procedures, and entitlement to allowances.
States that the Governing Board shall meet at least twice a year at Madras at times fixed by the Chairperson.

main_sections.section_title: Grants by Central Government to the Foundation
main_sections.description: Concerns grants provided by the Central Government to the Foundation.
Relates to the establishment and management of the Fund of the Foundation.
Pertains to the budget of the Foundation.

main_sections.section_title: Accounts and audit of the Foundation
main_sections.description: Covers the accounts and audit procedures for the Foundation.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to furnish returns, annual reports, etc.
main_sections.description: Obligates the Foundation to furnish returns, annual reports, and other necessary information.

main_sections.section_title: Prior approval of the Central Government for alienation of property
main_sections.description: Requires prior approval from the Central Government for the alienation of property by the Foundation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions to the Foundation
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Foundation.
Provides for the dissolution of the Foundation.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Offers protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Addresses matters of indemnity.
Grants the power to make rules under the Act.
Grants the power to make regulations under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that rules and regulations made under the Act be laid before Parliament.
Empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: Rule: On commencement of the Act, assets and properties of Kalakshetra vest in the Central Government (Section 4).
Rule: The Central Government shall direct the vesting of these assets and properties in the Kalakshetra Foundation (Section 6).
Rule: Persons in possession of Kalakshetra's assets and properties must deliver them and account for them to the Central Government or the Foundation (Section 7).
Rule: The Kalakshetra Foundation is established as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (Section 8).
Rule: The Governing Board, Academic Committee, and Finance Committee are the authorities of the Foundation, guided by its objects (Section 10).
Rule: The Governing Board shall meet at least twice a year (Section 13).
Rule: The Central Government may provide grants to the Foundation (Section 21).
Rule: The Foundation shall maintain a Fund, prepare a budget, and its accounts are subject to audit (Sections 22, 23, 24).
Rule: The Foundation must furnish returns and annual reports (Section 25).
Rule: Prior approval of the Central Government is required for alienation of Foundation property (Section 26).
Rule: The Central Government can give directions to the Foundation (Section 27).
Rule: Rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament (Section 33).

penalties: While specific penalties for violations are not detailed in the provided text, Section 7(2) states that any person in possession or control of Kalakshetra's assets, properties, books, documents or other papers who fails to account for or deliver them shall be liable to the Central Government or the Foundation.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Kalakshetra Foundation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directions issued by the Central Government (Section 27), the power to remove difficulties (Section 34), and the requirement for persons to deliver and account for assets (Section 7). Enforcement also involves the administrative and financial oversight by the Governing Board, Academic Committee, and Finance Committee, and the audit of accounts.

rights: The Foundation has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (Section 8).
The Foundation has the right to sue and be sued (Section 8).
The Foundation holds licenses, permissions, authorities, concessions, facilities, privileges, affiliations, etc., granted to the previous body, for the remainder of their period (Section 5(3)).
Members of the Governing Board (nominated under clauses (b) and (c) of section 11) are entitled to such allowances as may be prescribed (Section 12(5)).
duties: Persons in charge of Kalakshetra's assets and properties must deliver them and account for them to the Central Government or the Foundation (Section 7).
The Foundation is to be guided by its objects specified in Section 9 in discharging its functions and exercising powers (Section 10(2)).
The Foundation must adhere to the principles of 'education without fear' and 'art without vulgarity' (Section 9(v)).
The Foundation must prepare a budget (Section 23).
The Foundation must maintain accounts and undergo audit (Section 24).
The Foundation must furnish returns and annual reports (Section 25).
obligations: The Foundation is obligated to fulfill the objects of Kalakshetra (Section 9).
The Foundation is obligated to use assets and properties as per its objectives and legal provisions.
The Foundation is obligated to comply with directions from the Central Government (Section 27).

key_procedures: Transfer and Vesting of Assets: Assets and properties of Kalakshetra are transferred to and vest in the Central Government, then directed to vest in the Kalakshetra Foundation through notifications (Sections 4, 6).
Establishment of the Foundation: The Central Government establishes the Kalakshetra Foundation by notification, which becomes a body corporate (Section 8).
Constitution of Governing Board: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson and nominates Members, along with nominations from the State Government and ex officio officers (Section 11).
Meetings of the Governing Board: The Governing Board must meet at least twice a year, with decisions taken at these meetings (Section 13).
Budgeting and Financial Management: The Foundation prepares an annual budget and manages its funds, with accounts subject to audit (Sections 22, 23, 24).
Reporting: The Foundation must submit returns and annual reports (Section 25).
administration: The Kalakshetra Foundation, with oversight and direction from the Central Government. The Governing Board is the supreme authority of the Foundation.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on September 29, 1993, before its official enactment date (Section 1(2)).
Kalakshetra is declared an institution of national importance (Section 2).
The Act aims to ensure the development of Kalakshetra in accordance with its founding ideals, emphasizing 'education without fear' and 'art without vulgarity' (Section 9).
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act (Section 34).
Existing employees' services are transferred (Section 20).

title: The Manipur Panchayati Raj Act, 1994
purpose: To provide for the constitution and organisation of Panchayats as units of local self-Government in the rural areas of Manipur, establishing a two-tier Panchayati Raj system with elected bodies at the Gram and District levels for greater people's participation and effective implementation of rural development programmes.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Manipur, excluding areas covered by the Manipur (Hill Areas) District Council Act, 1971, the Manipur (Village Authorities in Hill Areas) Act, 1956, areas declared or included in a municipality, or areas declared or included in a cantonment under the Cantonment Act, 1924.

key_definitions.Adhyaksha and Up-Adhyaksha: Adhyaksha and Up-Adhyaksha of a Zilla Parishad elected under section 54.
key_definitions.Chairperson: Chairperson of a Standing Committee of a Zilla Parishad or a Gram Panchayat.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: Chief Executive Officer of a Zilla Parishad appointed under section 75.
key_definitions.Commissioner: Commissioner of the Government in the Development and Panchayati Raj or any other person appointed by the State Government to exercise the powers of a Commissioner.
key_definitions.Gram Sabha: A body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the Panchayat area at the village level.
key_definitions.Gram Panchayat: A Gram Panchayat constituted under the Act.
key_definitions.Panchayat: A Gram Panchayat and a Zilla Parishad constituted under the Act.
key_definitions.Pradhan: Pradhan of a Gram Panchayat elected under section 21.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under the Act.
key_definitions.Secretary: Secretary of a Gram Panchayat appointed under this Act.
key_definitions.Standing Committee: A Standing Committee constituted by a Zilla Parishad or a Gram Panchayat.
key_definitions.Up-Pradhan: Up-Pradhan of a Gram Panchayat elected under section 24.
key_definitions.village: A village specified by the Governor by public notification, including a group of villages so specified.
key_definitions.Zilla Parishad: A Zilla Parishad of a district constituted under section 48.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent within Manipur, and the process for its commencement, allowing for different dates for different provisions.
Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, including various roles within Panchayats and Zilla Parishads, and administrative entities.

main_sections.section_title: Membership of Gram Sabha and disqualification
main_sections.description: Defines the membership of a Gram Sabha as persons registered in electoral rolls for the village area and outlines disqualifications for membership, including not being a citizen of India, being of unsound mind, or being disqualified from voting in State Legislature elections due to corrupt practices.

Establishes the constitution of a Gram Panchayat for every Gram Sabha, its notification in the Official Gazette, and the eligibility criteria for inclusion in the Gram Panchayat's list of electors, including age and ordinary residence.
Provides for the establishment of a Zilla Parishad for a district.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and provisions for saving existing matters.

important_rules: Rule for Gram Sabha Meetings: Meetings must be held from time to time, with no more than six months between any two meetings.
Quorum for Gram Sabha Meetings: A quorum of one-tenth of the total membership is required for a Gram Sabha meeting. If no quorum is present, the meeting is adjourned to the following week.

Eligibility for Gram Panchayat Electors: Individuals must be at least eighteen years of age, ordinarily resident within the Gram Panchayat area, and not be listed in more than one Gram Panchayat's electoral roll.

rights: Right of persons registered in electoral rolls to be members of the Gram Sabha.
Right for individuals to be included in the list of electors of a Gram Panchayat if they meet the age and residency criteria.
duties: Gram Sabha's duty to render assistance in implementing development schemes and identify beneficiaries.
Gram Panchayat's duty to prepare the agenda for Gram Sabha meetings, including annual accounts, budget, and development programmes.
obligations: Obligation for members of a Gram Sabha to cease membership if they cease to be ordinarily resident within the Gram Sabha area.
Obligation for persons to be ordinarily resident within the area of a Gram Panchayat to be included in its electoral roll.

key_procedures: Procedure for convening Gram Sabha meetings: Meetings are to be held in accordance with prescribed procedures.
Procedure for election of Pradhan and members of Gram Panchayat (detailed in Section 21, not fully provided in excerpt).
Procedure for election of Up-Pradhan on the establishment of Gram Panchayat (detailed in Section 26, not fully provided in excerpt).
administration: The State Government of Manipur (referred to as 'Government') is responsible for various administrative functions, including making notifications, appointing officials, and exercising powers to revise or modify decisions.
important_notes: Exclusions from the Act's extent: The Act does not apply to areas under the Manipur (Hill Areas) District Council Act, 1971, the Manipur (Village Authorities in Hill Areas) Act, 1956, areas declared as municipalities, or areas declared as cantonments.
Commencement: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through notification in the Official Gazette, with provisions for different commencement dates for different sections.

title: The Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994
purpose: To provide for the regulation of removal, storage, and transplantation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes, and to prevent commercial dealings in human organs and tissues.
scope: Applies to the States of Goa, Himachal Pradesh, and Maharashtra, and all Union territories. It also applies to any other state that adopts the Act by resolution. The Act covers the regulation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes and the prevention of commercial dealings.

key_definitions.advertisement: Any form of advertising, whether to the public generally, to any section of the public, or individually to selected persons.
key_definitions.appropriate_authority: The Appropriate Authority appointed under section 13.
key_definitions.authorisation_committee: The committee constituted under clause (a) or clause (b) of sub-section (4) of section 9.
key_definitions.brain_stem_death: The stage at which all functions of the brain-stem have permanently and irreversibly ceased and is so certified under sub-section (6) of section 3.
key_definitions.deceased_person: A person in whom permanent disappearance of all evidence of life occurs, by reason of brain-stem death or in a cardio-pulmonary sense, at any time after live birth has taken place.
key_definitions.donor: Any person, not less than eighteen years of age, who voluntarily authorises the removal of any of his human organs for therapeutic purposes under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 3.
key_definitions.hospital: Includes a nursing home, clinic, medical centre, medical or teaching institution for therapeutic purposes and other like institutions.
key_definitions.human_organ: Any part of a human body consisting of a structured arrangement of tissues which, if wholly removed, cannot be replicated by the body.
key_definitions.human_organ_retrieval_centre: A hospital which has adequate facilities for treating seriously ill patients who can be potential donors of organs in the event of death, and which is registered under sub-section (1) of section 14 for retrieval of human organs.
key_definitions.minor: A person who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.near_relative: Spouse, son, daughter, father, mother, brother, sister, grandfather, grandmother, grandson, or granddaughter.
key_definitions.payment: Payment in money or money's worth, but does not include any payment for defraying or reimbursing the cost of removing, transporting, or preserving the human organ or tissue or both to be supplied, or any expenses or loss of earnings incurred by a person so far as reasonably and directly attributable to his supplying any human organ from his body.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.recipient: A person into whom any human organ or tissue or both is, or is proposed to be, transplanted.
key_definitions.registered_medical_practitioner: A medical practitioner who possesses a recognised medical qualification and is enrolled on a State Medical Register.
key_definitions.therapeutic_purposes: Systematic treatment of any disease or measures to improve health according to any particular method or modality.
key_definitions.tissue: A group of cells, except blood, performing a particular function in the human body.
key_definitions.tissue_bank: A facility registered under section 14A for carrying out any activity relating to the recovery, screening, testing, processing, storage, and distribution of tissues, but does not include a Blood Bank.
key_definitions.transplantation: The grafting of any human organ from any living person or deceased person to some other living person for therapeutic purposes.
key_definitions.transplant_co_ordinator: A person appointed by the hospital for co-ordinating all matters relating to removal or transplantation of human organs or tissues or both and for assisting the authority for removal of human organs in accordance with the provisions of sections 3.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994', outlines its initial application to specific states and Union territories, and details how it comes into force.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'advertisement', 'Appropriate Authority', 'brain-stem death', 'donor', 'hospital', 'human organ', 'minor', 'near relative', 'payment', 'therapeutic purposes', 'tissue', and 'transplantation'.

main_sections.section_title: Authority for removal of human organs or tissues or both
main_sections.description: Specifies the conditions and manner under which a donor can authorize the removal of their organs or tissues before death, and outlines the duties of registered medical practitioners in obtaining consent or informing about donation options. It also details the process for removal from deceased persons, including the certification of brain-stem death.
Establishes the appointment of an 'Appropriate Authority' responsible for overseeing the implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of hospitals engaged in removal, storage or transplantation of human organs or tissues or both
main_sections.description: Mandates the registration of hospitals that are involved in the removal, storage, or transplantation of human organs or tissues.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for removal of human organ without authority
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for the unauthorized removal of human organs.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for commercial dealings in human organs
main_sections.description: Outlines the punishment for engaging in commercial transactions involving human organs.

important_rules: A donor, if not a minor, can authorize the removal of their organs or tissues before death for therapeutic purposes.
If a donor has previously authorized organ removal in writing and witnessed by two or more people (one being a near relative), this authorization is generally valid after death, unless revoked.

If no prior authorization or objection was expressed by the deceased, and no objection is raised by a near relative, the person in lawful possession of the body may authorize removal of organs or tissues.
Removal of organs or tissues from a deceased person requires the registered medical practitioner to confirm the extinction of life or certified brain-stem death.
Brain-stem death must be certified by a Board of medical experts, including the in-charge registered medical practitioner, an independent specialist, and a neurologist or neurosurgeon.

penalties: Punishment for removal of human organ without authority.
Punishment for commercial dealings in human organs.
Punishment for illegal dealings in human tissues.
Punishment for contravention of any other provision of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Appropriate Authority appointed under section 13, and potentially other authorities as prescribed by the Act and rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings for offenses committed under the Act, including imprisonment and fines. Registration of hospitals and Tissue Banks are also mechanisms for control and enforcement.

rights: The right of a donor to authorize the removal of their organs for therapeutic purposes.
The right of a deceased person's near relative to object to the removal of organs, even if no explicit objection was made by the deceased.
The right to receive organ transplantation for therapeutic purposes.
duties: Duty of registered medical practitioners to ascertain donor authorization and inform about donation options.
Duty to comply with the prescribed procedures for removal, storage, and transplantation of organs and tissues.
Duty of hospitals to be registered for organ retrieval and transplantation activities.
obligations: Obligation to obtain authorization for organ removal.
Obligation to prevent commercial dealings in human organs and tissues.
Obligation for hospitals to maintain records and comply with registration requirements.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining donor authorization (pre-mortem and post-mortem).
Procedure for certifying brain-stem death by a medical expert board.
Procedure for registration of hospitals and Tissue Banks.
Procedure for reporting offenses and taking cognizance of them.
administration: The Act is administered through the 'Appropriate Authority' appointed under Section 13, and potentially other government departments or agencies designated by the Central Government for making rules.
important_notes: The Act prohibits the removal or transplantation of human organs or tissues for any purpose other than therapeutic purposes.
Commercial dealings in human organs are strictly prohibited and punishable.
The definition of 'payment' excludes reimbursement of costs related to removal, transport, preservation, or loss of earnings directly attributable to organ donation.

title: The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994
purpose: To provide for the prohibition of sex selection before or after conception and to regulate pre-natal diagnostic techniques for the purpose of detecting genetic abnormalities or metabolic disorders or chromosomal abnormalities or certain congenital malformations or sex-linked disorders, and to prevent their misuse for sex determination leading to female foeticide.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to Genetic Counselling Centres, Genetic Laboratories, Genetic Clinics, and any person involved in conducting pre-conception or pre-natal diagnostic techniques.

key_definitions.appropriate_authority: The Appropriate Authority appointed under section 17.
key_definitions.board: The Central Supervisory Board constituted under section 7.
key_definitions.conceptus: Any product of conception at any stage of development from fertilization until birth including extra embryonic membranes as well as the embryo or foetus.
key_definitions.embryo: A developing human organism after fertilization till the end of eight weeks (fifty-six days).
key_definitions.foetus: A human organism during the period of its development beginning on the fifty-seventh day following fertilization or creation and ending at birth.
key_definitions.genetic_counselling_centre: An institute, hospital, nursing home or any place which provides for genetic counselling to patients.
key_definitions.genetic_clinic: A clinic, institute, hospital, nursing home or any place which is used for conducting pre-natal diagnostic procedures. This includes a vehicle where ultrasound or imaging equipment capable of determining sex of the foetus is used.
key_definitions.genetic_laboratory: A laboratory and includes a place where facilities are provided for conducting analysis or tests of samples received from Genetic Clinic for pre-natal diagnostic test. This includes a place where ultrasound or imaging equipment capable of determining sex of the foetus is used.
key_definitions.medical_geneticist: A person who possesses a degree or diploma in genetic science in the fields of sex selection and pre-natal diagnostic techniques or has experience of not less than two years in any of these fields after obtaining a recognized medical qualification or a post-graduate degree in biological sciences.
key_definitions.pre_natal_diagnostic_procedures: All gynecological or obstetrical or medical procedures such as ultrasonography, foetoscopy, taking or removing samples of amniotic fluid, chorionic villi, embryo, blood or any other tissue or fluid of a man, or of a woman before or after conception, for being sent to a Genetic Laboratory or Genetic Clinic for conducting any type of analysis or pre-natal diagnostic tests for selection of sex before or after conception.
key_definitions.pre_natal_diagnostic_tests: Ultrasonography or any test or analysis of amniotic fluid, chorionic villi, blood or any tissue or fluid of a pregnant woman or conceptus conducted to detect genetic or metabolic disorders or chromosomal abnormalities or congenital anomalies or haemoglobinopathies or sex-linked diseases.
key_definitions.sex_selection: Includes any procedure, technique, test or administration or prescription or provision of anything for the purpose of ensuring or increasing the probability that an embryo will be of a particular sex.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date from which it comes into force.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Appropriate Authority', 'Board', 'conceptus', 'embryo', 'foetus', 'Genetic Counselling Centre', 'Genetic Clinic', 'Genetic Laboratory', 'medical geneticist', 'pre-natal diagnostic procedures', 'pre-natal diagnostic tests', and 'sex selection'.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of Genetic Counselling Centres, Genetic Laboratories and Genetic Clinics
main_sections.description: States that no such center, laboratory, or clinic can conduct activities related to pre-natal diagnostic techniques unless registered under the Act. It also prohibits employing unqualified persons and conducting pre-natal diagnostic techniques at unregistered places.
Prohibits any person, including specialists in infertility, from conducting or aiding in conducting sex selection on a woman or man, or any related tissue, embryo, conceptus, fluid, or gametes.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on sale of ultrasound machine, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the sale of ultrasound machines or other sex-detection equipment to entities not registered under the Act.

Regulates the use of pre-natal diagnostic techniques for specific purposes only (detection of chromosomal abnormalities, genetic metabolic diseases, haemoglobinopathies, sex-linked genetic diseases, congenital anomalies, etc.). It also specifies conditions under which these techniques can be used, such as maternal age above 35, history of abortions, exposure to teratogenic agents, or family history of genetic diseases. It prohibits seeking or encouraging conduct of pre-natal diagnostic techniques for sex selection.

main_sections.section_title: Written consent of pregnant woman and prohibition of communicating the sex of foetus
main_sections.description: Mandates obtaining written informed consent from the pregnant woman before conducting pre-natal diagnostic procedures and prohibits communicating the sex of the foetus to the woman or any other person.
Prohibits Genetic Counselling Centres, Laboratories, or Clinics from conducting pre-natal diagnostic techniques for the purpose of determining the sex of a foetus.
Provides for the constitution of a Central Supervisory Board.
Provides for the appointment of an Appropriate Authority and an Advisory Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of Genetic Counselling Centres, Genetic Laboratories or Genetic Clinics
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for registration of Genetic Counselling Centres, Genetic Laboratories, or Genetic Clinics.
Details the grounds and process for cancellation or suspension of registration.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders of cancellation or suspension of registration.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of advertisement relating to pre-conception and pre-natal determination of sex and punishment for contravention
main_sections.description: Prohibits advertisements related to pre-conception and pre-natal determination of sex and specifies punishment for contravention.
Specifies the offences under the Act and the corresponding penalties.

main_sections.section_title: Offence to be cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable
main_sections.description: Declares offences under the Act as cognizable, non-bailable, and non-compoundable.

main_sections.section_title: Power to search and seize records, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants powers to search and seize records, equipment, etc.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

important_rules: No Genetic Counselling Centre, Genetic Laboratory or Genetic Clinic shall conduct or associate with activities relating to pre-natal diagnostic techniques unless registered under the Act.
No person shall conduct or aid in conducting sex selection on a woman or a man or on any tissue, embryo, conceptus, fluid or gametes.

Pre-natal diagnostic techniques shall be conducted only for the detection of specific abnormalities (chromosomal, genetic metabolic, haemoglobinopathies, sex-linked, congenital, etc.) and not for sex determination.

Pre-natal diagnostic techniques can be used only if certain conditions are met, such as maternal age above 35, history of abortions, exposure to teratogenic agents, or family history of genetic diseases.
Written informed consent of the pregnant woman is mandatory before conducting pre-natal diagnostic procedures.
Communication of the sex of the foetus to the pregnant woman or her relatives is prohibited.
Sale of ultrasound machines or other sex-detection equipment is prohibited to unregistered entities.

penalties: Punishment for prohibition of advertisement relating to pre-conception and pre-natal determination of sex.
Punishment for offences related to conducting pre-natal diagnostic techniques for sex determination or sex selection.
Penalty for contravention of provisions for which no specific punishment is provided.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Appropriate Authorities appointed under section 17, Central Supervisory Board, and State Supervisory Boards.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration requirements, inspections, search and seizure of records and equipment, prosecution for offences, and imposition of penalties.

rights: Right of a pregnant woman to informed consent before pre-natal diagnostic procedures.
Right of a pregnant woman to not have the sex of her foetus communicated to her or her relatives.
duties: Duty of registered centres, laboratories, and clinics to conduct activities related to pre-natal diagnostic techniques ethically and as per regulations.
Duty of medical professionals not to conduct or aid in conducting sex selection.
Duty of persons not to seek or encourage sex selection techniques.
Duty of persons to obtain written consent from pregnant women before conducting pre-natal diagnostic procedures.
Duty to maintain records as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation to register Genetic Counselling Centres, Genetic Laboratories, and Genetic Clinics.
Obligation to adhere to the specified purposes and conditions for conducting pre-natal diagnostic techniques.
Obligation to prohibit the determination of sex of a foetus.
Obligation to prohibit the communication of the sex of a foetus.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of Genetic Counselling Centres, Genetic Laboratories, and Genetic Clinics.
Procedure for obtaining written consent of the pregnant woman before conducting pre-natal diagnostic procedures.
Procedure for conducting pre-natal diagnostic techniques for specified medical reasons only.
Procedure for appealing against cancellation or suspension of registration.
Procedure for search and seizure of records and equipment by authorized personnel.
administration: The Central Government, through the Central Supervisory Board and Appropriate Authorities, is responsible for the administration and implementation of the Act. State Governments also play a role through State Supervisory Boards.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2003 to include definitions of 'conceptus', 'embryo', 'foetus', and to expand the definitions of 'Genetic Clinic' and 'Genetic Laboratory' to include vehicles with imaging equipment. It also strengthened provisions related to sex selection.
The Act aims to curb female foeticide, which is a significant social issue in India.

title: THE BABASAHEB BHIMRAO AMBEDKAR UNIVERSITY ACT, 1994
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and residential University in the State of Uttar Pradesh and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

scope.geographical: The jurisdiction of the University shall extend to the whole of the State of Uttar Pradesh.
scope.subject_matter: Establishment, incorporation, powers, authorities, administration, and functioning of the Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.Board of Management: The Board of Management of the University.
key_definitions.University: The Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University established under this Act.
key_definitions.distance education system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more such means.
key_definitions.teachers of the University: Professors, Readers, Lecturers and such other persons as may be appointed for imparting instruction or conducting research in the University or in any College or Institution maintained by the University and are designated as teachers by the Ordinances.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and the procedure for its commencement through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'Board of Management', 'University', 'distance education system', and 'teachers of the University'.
Establishes the Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, specifies its headquarters in Lucknow, and declares it a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
