Outlines the objectives of the University, including promoting advanced knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, offering courses for socially and economically depressed sections, promoting national integration, social justice, and democratic way of life, and paying special attention to the welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, conferring honorary degrees, establishing campuses and centers, creating posts, cooperating with other institutions, and managing property.
Specifies that the University's jurisdiction extends to the entire State of Uttar Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all individuals regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, class, or domicile, prohibiting any test of religious belief for admission or employment, with a proviso for special provisions for women, the physically handicapped, and weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Mandates that students, except those in distance education, must normally reside in a Hall or hostel or under prescribed conditions.
Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and outlines the Visitor's powers to review work, conduct inspections and inquiries, and issue directions to the University.

important_rules: Rule 1: The University shall be open to all persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race, class, place of domicile and no religious test shall be imposed for admission or employment (Section 7).
Rule 2: Every student, other than distance education students, shall normally reside in a Hall or hostel or under prescribed conditions (Section 8).
Rule 3: The President of India, as the Visitor, has the right to review the University's work, conduct inspections, and issue binding directions for necessary actions (Section 9).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University itself, through its authorities, and the Visitor (President of India) for oversight and direction.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of University authorities, the promulgation of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations, and through the Visitor's power to direct action based on inspections and inquiries.

rights: Right to educational and research facilities (Section 4, 5).
Right to be admitted and employed without discrimination based on religion, caste, creed, etc. (Section 7).
Right to appeal disciplinary cases (Section 33).
Right to be heard during inspections/inquiries by the Visitor (Section 9(6)).
duties: Duty to provide instructional and research facilities (Section 4, 5(i)).
Duty to make provisions for integrated courses and relevant courses for societal development (Section 4).
Duty to promote study of principles like national integration and social justice (Section 4).
Duty to admit students and employ staff without religious or creedal tests (Section 7).
Duty to comply with directions issued by the Visitor (Section 9(2)).
Duty to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees (Section 5(xxv)).
obligations: Obligation to establish and maintain colleges, institutions, and halls (Section 5(xiv)).
Obligation to supervise student residences and promote their health and welfare (Section 5(xxiii)).
Obligation to make provisions for the health and general welfare of employees (Section 5(xxvi)).

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).

Visitor's Review and Inspection: The Visitor can appoint persons to review the University's work, conduct inspections, and make inquiries, after giving notice to the University and considering its representations (Section 9).
Making Statutes: The Board of Management has the power to make Statutes, which are then to be made in the manner prescribed (Sections 25, 26).
Making Ordinances: The Board of Management has the power to make Ordinances (Section 27).
administration: The University itself, through its various authorities like the Board of Management, Academic Council, Planning Board, and Finance Committee, and overseen by the Visitor (President of India).
important_notes: The Act provides for special provisions for the employment or promotion of educational interests of women, the physically handicapped, and persons belonging to weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 7 proviso).
The Act lists specific powers of the University in 29 sub-sections, covering academic, administrative, financial, and welfare aspects.
The First and Second Schedules are mentioned but not detailed in the provided text excerpt, likely containing further details on objects or statutes.

title: THE MAULANA AZAD NATIONAL URDU UNIVERSITY ACT, 1996
purpose: To establish and incorporate a University at the national level mainly to promote and develop Urdu language and to import vocational and technical education in Urdu medium through conventional teaching and distance education system, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The jurisdiction of the University extends to the whole of India. The Act applies to the establishment, incorporation, objects, powers, and administration of the Maulana Azad National Urdu University.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.Board of Studies: The Board of Studies of the University.
key_definitions.Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor and Pro-Vice: Mean, respectively, the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor and Pro-Vice Chancellor of the University.
key_definitions.Department: A Department of Studies; and includes a Centre of Studies.
key_definitions.distance education system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication such as broadcasting, telecasting, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more of such means.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.Executive Council: The Executive Council of the University.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Maulana Azad National Urdu University Act, 1996, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'University', 'academic staff', 'distance education system', 'employee', and others.
Establishes the Maulana Azad National Urdu University with its headquarters at Hyderabad, constituting it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objectives of the University, which include promoting Urdu language, imparting vocational and technical education in Urdu medium, providing wider access to higher education in Urdu medium through campus and distance learning, and focusing on women's education.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, conferring honorary degrees, instituting academic positions, creating posts, collaborating with other institutions, establishing centres and laboratories, awarding fellowships, establishing and maintaining institutions, providing research and advisory services, organizing refresher courses, making special arrangements for women students, appointing visiting professors, determining admission standards, levying fees, supervising student residences, laying down conditions of service for employees, regulating discipline, promoting employee welfare, receiving donations, acquiring and managing property, borrowing money with government approval, organizing distance education programmes, establishing study centres, preparing instructional materials, devising schemes for Urdu promotion and dissemination, and performing all other acts necessary for its objects.
Specifies that the jurisdiction of the University extends to the whole of India.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creeds
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all sexes, castes, creeds, races, or classes, prohibiting any religious tests for appointment, admission, or privileges. It also allows for special provisions for women, the physically handicapped, and weaker sections of society, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University. It details the Visitor's powers to review work and progress, conduct inspections and inquiries, issue directions, and annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act, Statutes, or Ordinances.
Lists the officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Pro-Vice-Chancellor.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Visitor (President of India) has significant oversight and enforcement powers, including annulling proceedings and issuing directions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, issuing directions, and annulling proceedings that are not in conformity with the Act, Statutes, or Ordinances.

rights: Right to be open to all classes, castes, and creeds.
Right to make special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped, or persons from weaker sections.
Right of the University to make representations to the Visitor during inspections or inquiries.
Right of a representative of the University to be present and heard during inspections or inquiries.
duties: Duty to promote and develop Urdu language.
Duty to impart vocational and technical education in Urdu medium.
Duty to provide wider access to higher education in Urdu medium.
Duty to focus on women's education.
Duty to comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
Duty to allow the Visitor to cause inspections and inquiries.
obligations: The University shall be bound to comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
The University shall give notice of the Visitor's intention to conduct an inspection or inquiry.
The University shall consider representations made by the Executive Council before the Visitor issues directions.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Procedure for Visitor's inspection/inquiry: The Visitor must give notice of intention to inspect/inquire, the University has the right to make representations, a University representative can be present and heard, the Visitor communicates results to the Vice-Chancellor, and the Executive Council communicates its proposed action. If unsatisfied, the Visitor can issue directions.
Procedure for annulling proceedings: The Visitor must call upon the Registrar to show cause why an order of annulment should not be made.
administration: The administration of the University involves various officers like the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, and Librarian, and authorities such as the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council. The Visitor (President of India) also plays a significant administrative oversight role.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the 47th Year of the Republic of India.
The commencement date of the Act was 9th January, 1998.
The University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal.
The University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of India.
Special provisions can be made for women, the physically handicapped, and weaker sections.

title: THE MAHATMA GANDHI ANTARRASHTRIYA HINDI VISHWAVIDYALAYA ACT, 1996
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching University for the promotion and development of Hindi language and literature, through teaching and research, with a view to enabling Hindi to achieve greater functional efficiency and recognition as a major international language and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The jurisdiction of the University extends to the whole of India. The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya.

key_definitions.academic_staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.board_of_studies: The Board of Studies of the University.

key_definitions.department: A Department of Studies and includes a Centre of Studies.
key_definitions.distance_education_system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more such means.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University, and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.executive_council: The Executive Council of the University.

key_definitions.university: The Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya established and incorporated as a University under this Act.

Establishes the University by the name 'Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya', specifies its headquarters at Wardha, and constitutes it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objectives of the University, which include promoting and developing Hindi language and literature through teaching, research, comparative studies, dissemination of information, translation, interpretation, linguistics, and popularization through distance education.

title: THE MIZORAM UNIVERSITY ACT, 2000
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Mizoram and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Mizoram. It establishes the Mizoram University, which takes over the jurisdiction and assets of the North-Eastern Hill University within Mizoram. The University is open to all classes, castes, and creeds, with provisions for special consideration for women, the physically handicapped, and weaker sections including Scheduled Castes and Tribes.

key_definitions.University: The Mizoram University established and incorporated as a University under this Act.
key_definitions.College: A College maintained by, or admitted to the privileges of, the University.
key_definitions.Institution: An academic institution, not being a College, maintained by, or admitted to the privileges of, the University.
key_definitions.Teachers of the University: Professors, Readers, Lecturers and such other persons as may be appointed for imparting instruction or conducting research in the University or in any College or Institution maintained by the University and are designated as teachers by the Ordinances.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Mizoram University Act, 2000, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, academic staff, Board of Studies, College, Court, Department, distance education system, employee, Executive Council, Hall, Institution, North-Eastern Hill University, Principal, recognised Institution, recognised teachers, Regulations, School, Statutes, Ordinances, Teachers of the University, University, Vice-Chancellor, and Pro-Vice-Chancellor.

Establishes the Mizoram University, defines its headquarters as Aizawl, and constitutes the first Vice-Chancellor and members of various authorities as a body corporate. It grants the University perpetual succession and a common seal, allowing it to sue and be sued by its name.

Outlines the objectives of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge through instructional and research facilities, promoting integrated courses in various disciplines, fostering innovation in teaching and research, educating and training manpower for Mizoram's development, and improving the social, economic, and intellectual well-being of the state's people.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting diplomas and degrees, organizing extramural studies, conferring honorary degrees, providing distance education, establishing teaching positions, recognizing institutions and teachers, creating posts, collaborating with other institutions, establishing research centers, awarding scholarships, establishing and maintaining colleges, providing research and advisory services, organizing refresher courses, admitting colleges and institutions to its privileges, appointing visiting professors, conferring autonomous status, determining admission standards, levying fees, supervising student residence and welfare, laying down conditions of service for employees, enforcing discipline, promoting employee welfare, receiving donations, and acquiring and disposing of property. It also includes the power to borrow money with Central Government approval and to perform all other acts conducive to its objects.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of properties of North-Eastern Hill University
main_sections.description: States that all properties of the North-Eastern Hill University located in the State of Mizoram shall be transferred to and vest in the Mizoram University upon commencement of the Act, and shall be applied to the University's objects.

Defines the University's jurisdiction to extend to the whole State of Mizoram. It also stipulates that all Colleges, Institutions, Schools, and Departments affiliated with, or admitted to the privileges of, or maintained by the North-Eastern Hill University in Mizoram shall stand affiliated to, or admitted to the privileges of, or maintained by the Mizoram University. Furthermore, the North-Eastern Hill University shall cease to exercise its jurisdiction in Mizoram upon the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Declares the University to be open to all persons regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, or class. It prohibits the University from imposing any test of religious belief or profession for appointment, admission, graduation, or enjoyment of privileges. However, it allows for special provisions for the employment or admission of women, the physically handicapped, and persons from weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University. The Visitor has the power to review the University's work and progress, appoint inspectors for inspection and inquiry into the University's administration and finances, and issue directions based on such reviews or inquiries, which the University is bound to comply with. The Visitor must provide notice of intention to inspect or inquire.

important_rules: Rule 1: The University shall be open to persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class, without any religious or belief tests for appointment, admission, graduation or enjoyment of privileges, with specific provisions for women, physically handicapped, and Scheduled Castes/Tribes.
Rule 2: The Visitor (President of India) can review the University's work, order inspections, conduct inquiries, and issue binding directions.
Rule 3: Properties of the North-Eastern Hill University within Mizoram are transferred to the Mizoram University upon commencement of the Act.

rights: Right to open admission for all regardless of class, caste, or creed (with provisions for special categories).
duties: Duty to disseminate and advance knowledge.
Duty to provide instructional and research facilities.
Duty to educate and train manpower for Mizoram's development.
Duty to improve social and economic conditions and welfare of the people of Mizoram.
Duty to comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
Duty to apply transferred properties to the University's objects.
obligations: Obligation to be open to all classes, castes, and creeds.
Obligation to comply with directions from the Visitor.
Obligation to transfer and utilize properties from North-Eastern Hill University.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishment of the University: Based on the Act, the University is established with a name, headquarters, and constitutes its first officers and members as a corporate body.
Procedure for commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Procedure for Visitor's review and inspection: The Visitor can appoint persons to review work and progress, and conduct inspections or inquiries after giving notice to the University. The University must comply with the Visitor's directions.
Procedure for transfer of properties: Properties of North-Eastern Hill University in Mizoram are automatically transferred to Mizoram University upon commencement.
administration: The Act establishes the Mizoram University, with various authorities like the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council to manage its affairs. The President of India is the Visitor.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
The North-Eastern Hill University ceases its jurisdiction in Mizoram upon the commencement of this Act.
Special provisions may be made for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped, or persons belonging to weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

title: The Designs Act, 2000
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the protection of designs.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to articles of manufacture and substances, artificial or partly artificial and partly natural, including parts thereof that can be sold separately. It also covers new or original designs that are not contrary to public order or morality. The scope also includes international arrangements with the United Kingdom and other convention countries or groups of countries of inter-governmental organizations.

key_definitions.article: Any article of manufacture and any substance, artificial, or partly artificial and partly natural; and includes any part of an article capable of being made and sold separately.
key_definitions.controller: The Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks.
key_definitions.copyright: The exclusive right to apply a design to any article in any class in which the design is registered.
key_definitions.design: Only the features of shape, configuration, pattern, ornament or composition of lines or colours applied to any article whether in two dimensional or three dimensional or in both forms, by any industrial process or means, whether manual, mechanical or chemical, separate or combined, which in the finished article appeal to and are judged solely by the eye; but does not include any mode or principle of construction or anything which is in substance a mere mechanical device, and does not include any trade mark, property mark, or artistic work.
key_definitions.original: In relation to a design, means originating from the author of such design and includes the cases which though old in themselves yet are new in their application.
key_definitions.proprietor of a new or original design: The person for whom the design is executed if done for good consideration; the person who acquires the design or the right to apply it; or the author in any other case. It also includes subsequent persons upon whom the property or right has devolved.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'article', 'Controller', 'copyright', 'design', 'High Court', 'legal representative', 'original', 'Patent Office', 'prescribed', and 'proprietor of a new or original design'.

Establishes the Controller of Designs (who is the Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks) and empowers the Central Government to appoint examiners and other officers. It also details the delegation of powers by the Controller to these officers.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of registration of certain designs
main_sections.description: Lists the types of designs that cannot be registered, including those that are not new or original, have been disclosed to the public prior to the application date, are not significantly distinguishable from known designs, or contain scandalous or obscene matter.

Outlines the process for applying for the registration of a design, including requirements for the design to be new, original, and not contrary to public order or morality. It also mandates examination of the design and details the procedure for application, fees, classes of registration, and abandonment of applications.
Grants copyright to the registered proprietor of a design upon its registration.
Defines piracy of a registered design and likely outlines the consequences or remedies for such an act.
Specifies the right to appeal to the High Court against decisions made by the Controller.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous legislation and provisions for savings.

important_rules: A design must be new or original to be registered.

A design must not have been disclosed to the public anywhere in India or in any other country by publication in tangible form or by use or in any other way prior to the filing date or priority date of the application.
A design must not be significantly distinguishable from known designs or combinations of known designs.
A design must not comprise or contain scandalous or obscene matter.
An application for registration must be filed in the prescribed form, in the prescribed manner, and accompanied by the prescribed fee.
A design may be registered in not more than one class.

penalties: The document outlines 'Piracy of registered design' (Section 22), implying that penalties exist for infringement, although the specific penalties are not detailed in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Controller (Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks) and other officers appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the registration process, examination of designs, and legal proceedings for piracy. The Controller has powers to make orders regarding applications, correct errors, and rectify the register. Appeals against Controller's decisions lie with the High Court.

rights: The right to apply for registration of a new or original design.
The exclusive right (copyright) to apply a registered design to any article in a registered class.
The right to appeal to the High Court against the Controller's refusal to register a design.
The right of the proprietor of a lapsed design that has been restored.
duties: Applicants have a duty to provide complete and accurate information in their applications.
Applicants have a duty to ensure their designs meet the criteria for registration (new, original, not scandalous, etc.).
Proprietors have a duty to pay prescribed fees.
Proprietors have a duty to ensure that requirements before delivery on sales are met (implied).
obligations: The obligation not to register designs that are not new or original, have been previously disclosed, are not significantly distinguishable from known designs, or contain scandalous matter.
The obligation to comply with the prescribed procedures for application and registration.
The obligation to avoid infringement (piracy) of registered designs.

key_procedures: Application for registration of a design: Filing the prescribed form with the Patent Office, accompanied by the prescribed fee. The application is then referred to an examiner for assessment.
Examination of Design Application: An examiner appointed by the Central Government assesses whether the design is capable of being registered.

Registration and Publication: Upon successful examination and approval by the Controller, the design is registered as of the date of application. Particulars of the registered design are then published, making the design open to public inspection.
Appeals to the High Court: Any person aggrieved by the Controller's refusal to register a design may appeal to the High Court.
Rectification of Register: The Controller has the power to rectify the register in certain circumstances.
administration: The Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (referred to as the Controller) and other officers appointed by the Central Government. The Central Government also has powers to make rules and take directions.
important_notes: Designs registered in one class can be applied to other articles within that class without invalidating the registration, provided the period of copyright is not extended beyond the initial registration.
The Act allows for reciprocal arrangements with the United Kingdom and other convention countries or groups of countries of inter-governmental organizations.
The Central Government can make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
The Act consolidates and amends the law relating to the protection of designs, indicating it replaces previous legislation in this area.

title: THE UTTAR PRADESH REORGANISATION ACT, 2000
purpose: To provide for the reorganisation of the existing State of Uttar Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the existing State of Uttar Pradesh and provides for the formation of a new State named Uttaranchal comprising specific districts. It also covers representation in legislatures, the High Court, distribution of revenues, apportionment of assets and liabilities, provisions concerning corporations and services, management of water resources, and legal and miscellaneous provisions.

key_definitions.appointed day: The day appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.existing State of Uttar Pradesh: The State of Uttar Pradesh as it existed immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having, immediately before the appointed day, the force of law in the whole or in any part of the existing State of Uttar Pradesh.
key_definitions.successor State: In relation to the existing State of Uttar Pradesh, means the State of Uttar Pradesh or Uttaranchal.
key_definitions.transferred territory: The territory which on the appointed day is transferred from the existing State of Uttar Pradesh to the State of Uttaranchal.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'article', 'assembly constituency', 'Election Commission', 'existing State of Uttar Pradesh', 'law', 'notified order', 'population ratio', 'sitting member', 'successor State', 'transferred territory', 'treasury', and references to territorial divisions.

Establishes the formation of a new State named Uttaranchal from the appointed day, comprising specific districts from the existing State of Uttar Pradesh, and states that these territories will cease to be part of the existing State of Uttar Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: State of Uttar Pradesh and territorial divisions thereof
main_sections.description: Defines the territories of the State of Uttar Pradesh on and from the appointed day, comprising the territories of the existing State of Uttar Pradesh other than those specified for Uttaranchal.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Details amendments to the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution regarding the allocation of seats in the Council of States for the new States of Uttar Pradesh and Uttaranchal.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Specifies the allocation of seats in the House of the People for the successor State of Uttar Pradesh (80 seats) and Uttaranchal (5 seats) on and from the appointed day, and deems the Representation of the People Act, 1950, to be amended accordingly.

States the number of seats in the Legislative Assemblies of Uttar Pradesh (403) and Uttaranchal (70) on the appointed day and makes consequential amendments to the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

Details the allocation of sitting members of the Legislative Assembly of the existing State of Uttar Pradesh to the new State of Uttaranchal and specifies that other sitting members continue to be members of the Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh. It also deems the Legislative Assemblies of Uttar Pradesh and Uttaranchal to be duly constituted.
Provides for the establishment of a High Court for the State of Uttaranchal on and from the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of proceedings from Allahabad High Court to Uttaranchal High Court
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of pending proceedings from the Allahabad High Court to the Uttaranchal High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Authorisation of expenditure of Uttaranchal State
main_sections.description: Provides for the authorisation of expenditure of the Uttaranchal State.
Specifies the application of Part VI, which deals with the apportionment of assets and liabilities.
Addresses the apportionment of land and goods between the successor states.
Deals with the apportionment of public debt.
Covers provisions related to pensions.
Addresses the apportionment and continuance of contracts.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions for Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited, etc.
main_sections.description: Makes provisions for specific corporations like the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited.
Outlines provisions concerning All-India Services in relation to the reorganisation.
Deals with provisions related to other services.

main_sections.section_title: Water Resources Development and its Management
main_sections.description: Introduces provisions for the management and development of water resources.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and functions of the Ganga Management Board
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution and functions of the Ganga Management Board.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of the water resources of the River Yamuna
main_sections.description: Addresses the allocation of water resources of the River Yamuna.
Specifies the territorial extent of laws.
Grants the power to adapt existing laws to the reorganisation.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of provisions of the Act inconsistent with other laws
main_sections.description: Clarifies the effect of the Act's provisions when they are inconsistent with other laws.
Confers power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: On and from the appointed day, a new State named Uttaranchal shall be formed comprising specific districts of the existing State of Uttar Pradesh.
Rule 2: On and from the appointed day, the State of Uttar Pradesh shall comprise the territories of the existing State of Uttar Pradesh other than those specified for Uttaranchal.
Rule 3: On and from the appointed day, the Constitution's First Schedule shall be amended to include Uttaranchal as a State and to reflect the updated territories of Uttar Pradesh.
Rule 4: On and from the appointed day, the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution will be amended to reallocate seats in the Council of States for Uttar Pradesh and Uttaranchal.
Rule 5: On and from the appointed day, 80 seats in the House of the People will be allocated to Uttar Pradesh and 5 to Uttaranchal.
Rule 6: On the appointed day, the Legislative Assemblies of Uttar Pradesh will have 403 seats and Uttaranchal will have 70 seats.

Rule 7: Sitting members of the Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh elected from constituencies now part of Uttaranchal will cease to be members of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly and will be deemed elected to the provisional Legislative Assembly of Uttaranchal.
Rule 8: A High Court for Uttaranchal shall be established on and from the appointed day.

Rule 9: Provisions are made for the apportionment of assets and liabilities, including land, goods, treasury balances, taxes, loans, investments, public debt, and pensions between the successor states.

Rule 10: Provisions are made for the continuance and functioning of certain corporations and companies, including the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited and Uttar Pradesh State Financial Corporation.
Rule 11: Provisions are made for the continuation of All-India Services and other services in the context of the reorganisation.

Rule 12: The Act provides for the management and development of water resources, including the constitution and functions of the Ganga Management Board and the allocation of water resources of the River Yamuna.

rights: Right to continue in office for sitting members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies (with unaltered terms of office where applicable).
Right to appear or act in proceedings transferred to Uttaranchal High Court.
Right to recover loans and advances as per the apportionment of assets and liabilities.
duties: The Central Government has the duty to appoint the 'appointed day' by notification in the Official Gazette.
The Ganga Management Board has duties related to water resources development and management.
The Uttaranchal High Court has duties related to its jurisdiction and the transfer of proceedings.
obligations: Obligation to apportion assets and liabilities between Uttar Pradesh and Uttaranchal.
Obligation to ensure the continued functioning of essential services and corporations.
Obligation for the Central Government to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Appointment of the 'appointed day' by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette, triggering the reorganisation.
Procedure 2: Allocation of sitting members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies to the successor states based on constituency changes.
Procedure 3: Transfer of pending proceedings from the Allahabad High Court to the Uttaranchal High Court.
Procedure 4: Apportionment of assets and liabilities between Uttar Pradesh and Uttaranchal, with provisions for agreement or Central Government intervention.
Procedure 5: Establishment and functioning of the Ganga Management Board and allocation of river water resources.
Procedure 6: Adaptation of existing laws to suit the reorganisation and the new states.
administration: The Central Government plays a significant role in appointing the 'appointed day', issuing notifications, and having the power to give directions regarding services and to remove difficulties. The Election Commission is also involved in delimitation of constituencies. The Ganga Management Board is constituted for water resource management.
important_notes: The 'appointed day' is crucial for the commencement of the reorganisation and is to be notified by the Central Government.
The Act includes provisions for saving the powers of State Governments to alter district boundaries after the appointed day.
The Act addresses the continuity of arrangements for essential services like electric power and water supply.
Special provisions are made for income-tax and retrenchment compensation in certain cases.
The Act clarifies that its provisions, if inconsistent with other laws, will prevail to the extent of inconsistency, unless otherwise specified.

title: THE BIHAR REORGANISATION ACT, 2000
purpose: To provide for the reorganisation of the existing State of Bihar and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the State of Bihar and the newly formed State of Jharkhand, including their legislatures, high courts, finances, assets, liabilities, and services.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The day appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette, which is November 15, 2000.
key_definitions.existing_state_of_bihar: The State of Bihar as it existed immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having, immediately before the appointed day, the force of law in the whole or in any part of the existing State of Bihar.
key_definitions.successor_state: In relation to the existing State of Bihar, means the State of Bihar or Jharkhand.
key_definitions.transferred_territory: The territory which on the appointed day is transferred from the existing State of Bihar to the State of Jharkhand.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Bihar Reorganisation Act, 2000.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'existing State of Bihar', 'law', 'successor State', and 'transferred territory'.
Establishes the new State of Jharkhand comprising specific districts of the existing State of Bihar from the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: State of Bihar and territorial divisions thereof
main_sections.description: Defines the State of Bihar as comprising the territories of the existing State of Bihar other than those specified for Jharkhand.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution to allocate seats in the Council of States for the new State of Jharkhand.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Allocates seats in the House of the People to the successor States of Bihar and Jharkhand and amends the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Specifies the number of seats in the Legislative Assemblies of Bihar and Jharkhand and amends the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Provides for the establishment of a High Court for Jharkhand.
Specifies that Part VI deals with the apportionment of assets and liabilities.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions as to Bihar State Electricity Board, State Warehousing Corporation and State Road Transport Corporation
main_sections.description: Addresses the provisions related to specific corporations during the reorganisation.
Covers the provisions related to All-India Services in the context of the reorganisation.
Amends the Andhra Pradesh and Madras Alteration of Boundaries Act, 1956 (though the provided text doesn't detail this specific amendment, it's listed).
Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove any difficulties arising from the provisions of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and relevant state authorities are implicitly responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, amendments to existing laws, and notifications issued by the Central Government.

rights: Right to appear or to act in proceedings transferred to High Court of Jharkhand (Section 35).

key_procedures: Formation of Jharkhand State by the appointed day (Section 3).
Allocation of sitting members to the Council of States and House of the People for the successor states (Sections 8, 11).
Allocation of sitting members to the Legislative Assemblies of Bihar and Jharkhand (Section 13).
Apportionment of assets and liabilities between Bihar and Jharkhand (Part VI, Sections 41-61).
Provisions for the continuance of arrangements in regard to generation and supply of electric power and supply of water (Section 63).
Provisions for the continuance of facilities in certain State institutions (Section 70).
Transfer of pending proceedings in courts and other authorities (Section 89).
administration: The Central Government plays a significant role in administering the Act, particularly through the power to appoint the 'appointed day' and issue notifications and orders to remove difficulties.
important_notes: The Act provides for the creation of a new state, Jharkhand, from the existing state of Bihar.
It details the reorganisation of legislative representation, including the allocation of seats in Parliament and State Assemblies.
The Act addresses the establishment and jurisdiction of the High Court for Jharkhand.
It outlines the complex process of apportioning assets and liabilities between the two successor states.
Special provisions are made for various corporations, services, and the management of water resources.

title: THE SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED CIRCUITS LAYOUT-DESIGN ACT, 2000
purpose: To provide for the protection of semiconductor integrated circuits layout-designs and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, in accordance with India's commitments under the Agreement on Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to semiconductor integrated circuits layout-designs.

key_definitions.Appellate Board: The Appellate Board established under section 32.
key_definitions.assignment: An assignment in writing by act of the parties concerned.
key_definitions.layout-design: A layout of transistors and other circuitry elements and includes lead wires connecting such elements and expressed in any manner in a semiconductor integrated circuit.
key_definitions.registered layout-design: A layout-design which is actually on the register.
key_definitions.semiconductor integrated circuit: A product having transistors and other circuitry elements which are inseparably formed on a semiconductor material or an insulating material or inside the semiconductor material and designed to perform an electronic circuitry function.
key_definitions.transmission: Transmission by operation of law, devolution on the personal representation of a deceased person or any other mode of transfer not being assignment.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date to be appointed by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Appellate Board, assignment, layout-design, registered layout-design, semiconductor integrated circuit, and transmission.

main_sections.section_title: Registrar of Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Registrar and other officers for the purposes of the Act.
Establishes a Register of Layout-Designs to be kept at the Registry, containing details of all registered layout-designs.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of registration of certain layout-designs
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a layout-design cannot be registered, including if it's not original, has been commercially exploited, is not inherently distinctive, or is not distinguishable from other registered designs.
Details the procedure for any person claiming to be the creator of a layout-design to apply for its registration.

main_sections.section_title: No action of infringement of unregistered layout-design
main_sections.description: States that no legal action can be taken for the infringement of an unregistered layout-design.
Specifies the exclusive rights granted to the proprietor of a registered layout-design.
Defines what constitutes infringement of a registered layout-design.
Provides for the establishment of a Layout-Design Appellate Board to hear appeals and other related matters.
Prescribes penalties for the infringement of a layout-design.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: A layout-design must be original, not commercially exploited (with exceptions for recent exploitation), inherently distinctive, and distinguishable from other registered designs to be registrable.
A layout-design created under commission or employment belongs to the commissioner or employer, unless otherwise contractually agreed.
Registration of a layout-design confers exclusive rights on the proprietor, preventing others from performing certain acts without permission.
Infringement occurs when a person performs certain unauthorized acts related to a registered layout-design.

penalties: Penalty for infringement of layout-design (Section 56)
Penalty for falsely representing a layout-design as registered (Section 57)
Penalty for improperly describing a place of business as connected with the Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry (Section 58)
Penalty for falsification of entries in the register (Section 59)
Forfeiture of goods (Section 60)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design, and the Layout-Design Appellate Board for appeals and certain powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, penalties, forfeiture of goods, and appeals to the Appellate Board.

rights: Exclusive rights conferred by registration to prevent unauthorized acts (e.g., reproduction, sale, distribution of the layout-design or semiconductor integrated circuit containing it).
Right to assign and transmit the registered layout-design.
Right of a registered user to take proceedings against infringement.
duties: Duty to adhere to the conditions for registration.
Duty to comply with provisions regarding assignment and transmission.
Duty to follow procedures for registration, renewal, and any other processes outlined in the Act.
Duty to avoid infringing registered layout-designs.
obligations: Obligation to register the layout-design to gain protection.
Obligation to pay prescribed fees and surcharges.
Obligation for registered users to adhere to the terms of their registration.
Obligation to provide accurate information to the Registrar and the Appellate Board.

key_procedures: Application for registration of a layout-design.
Examination of the application, advertisement, and opposition to registration.
Correction and amendment of applications and specifications.
Registration of the layout-design and issuance of a certificate.
Assignment and transmission of registered layout-designs.
Registration of registered users.
Rectification and correction of the register.
Appeals to the Layout-Design Appellate Board.
Proceedings related to offenses, penalties, and forfeiture of goods.
administration: The Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry, administered by the Registrar of Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design. The Central Government oversees the registry and may establish branch offices. The Layout-Design Appellate Board handles disputes and appeals.
important_notes: The Act is enacted to give effect to international agreements on Intellectual Property Rights.
Different provisions of the Act can come into force on different dates.
The Act provides for a two-year grace period for commercial exploitation before an application is barred.
A layout-design created as a work for commission or employment belongs to the commissioner or employer, unless agreed otherwise.

title: THE METRO RAILWAYS (OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE) ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide for the operation and maintenance and to regulate the working of the metro railway in the National Capital Region, metropolitan city and metropolitan area, and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to metro railways within the National Capital Region and other metropolitan areas/cities notified by the Central Government, excluding trams. Covers operation, maintenance, safety, and related aspects.

key_definitions.metro_railway: A rail-guided mass rapid transit system having dedicated right-of-way, with steel wheel or rubber-tyred wheel coaches, but excluding tramways, for the carriage of passengers. Includes associated land, tracks, stations, and works.
key_definitions.metro_railway_administration: In relation to a Government metro railway, it's the General Manager. For a non-Government metro railway, it's the owner, lessee, or person operating it under an arrangement.
key_definitions.commissioner: The Commissioner of the Metro Railway Safety appointed under section 7.
key_definitions.fare: The charge levied for the carriage of passengers.
key_definitions.government_metro_railway: A metro railway owned by the Central Government.
key_definitions.non_government_metro_railway: A metro railway other than a Government metro railway.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent (initially National Capital Region, extendable to other metropolitan areas), and its commencement date (deemed to be 29th October, 2002).

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Central Government, Claims Commissioner, Commissioner, development, electric supply-line, fare, Government metro railway, land, metropolitan area, metropolitan city, metro railway, metro railway administration, metro railway official, National Capital Region, non-Government metro railway, notification, pass, prescribed, railway, regulations, rolling stock, and telegraph line.

Empowers the Central Government to constitute Government metro railways for efficient administration in specified areas and allows the metro railway administration to appoint necessary officers and employees.
Mandates the Central Government to appoint a General Manager for a Government metro railway, in whom the general superintendence and control of the railway vests.

Outlines the primary functions of a metro railway administration, which include maintaining and operating the metro railway for public passenger carriage and engaging in other necessary activities for its operation and maintenance.

Grants broad powers to the metro railway administration for carrying out its functions, including acquiring/disposing of property, developing land for commercial use, providing integrated transport services, removing obstructions, executing leases, entering contracts, employing agents, obtaining licenses for telegraph lines and electric supply, and levying penalties.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety
main_sections.description: Deals with the appointment of the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety.
Requires notification of metro railway accidents.
Provides for the appointment of Claims Commissioners.
Defines the extent of liability of the metro railway administration due to accidents.

main_sections.section_title: Drunkenness or nuisance on metro railway
main_sections.description: Specifies offenses and penalties related to public order on metro railways.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the metro railway administration.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of metro railway administration to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the metro railway administration to make regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of Act inconsistent with other enactments
main_sections.description: Clarifies the overriding effect of this Act in case of inconsistency with other laws.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: Passengers are prohibited from travelling without a valid pass or ticket (Section 25).
Carriage of dangerous or offensive material on the metro railway is regulated (Sections 30, 60, 61).
Prohibition against travelling by persons suffering from infectious or contagious diseases and powers to remove them (Section 27).
Metro railway administration has the right to display commercial advertisements (Section 29).
Fare fixation for passengers is governed by specific provisions (Chapter VII).
Notice of metro railway accidents must be given, followed by inquiries (Chapter VIII).
Liability of metro railway administration for accidents is defined (Chapter X).

penalties: Penalties for drunkenness or nuisance (Section 59).
Penalties for taking offensive or dangerous material (Sections 60, 61).

Penalties for travelling on the roof, unlawfully entering tracks, obstructing trains or officials, interfering with communication, altering tickets, defacing notices, unauthorized sale of tickets (Sections 63-77).
Penalties for damaging or destroying metro railway property, making false claims, and malicious acts (Sections 74, 78, 80).
Offences by companies are also addressed (Section 81).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Metro railway officials, police, and potentially the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety and Claims Commissioner depending on the offense.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for arrest without warrant (Sections 82, 83), designation of magistrates with jurisdiction (Section 84), and specified places of trial (Section 85).

rights: Passengers have the right to travel upon payment of fare and possession of a valid pass or ticket.
Passengers have the right to communication with metro railway officials in charge of trains (Section 28).
Metro railway administration has the right to display commercial advertisements (Section 29).
Passengers have rights related to compensation in case of accidents (Chapter IX and X).
duties: Duty to travel with a valid pass or ticket.
Duty to not carry dangerous or offensive materials.
Duty to refrain from causing nuisance or drunkenness.
Duty to surrender passes/tickets upon demand (Section 24).
Duty to comply with directions of metro railway officials.
obligations: Obligation of the metro railway administration to maintain and operate the railway safely and efficiently.
Obligation to provide fare tables at stations and supply tickets (Section 23).
Obligation to provide facilities to the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (Section 11).
Obligation to provide compensation for accidents under certain conditions (Chapter X).

key_procedures: Procedure for sanctioning the opening of a metro railway, including compliance with formalities (Sections 14, 15).
Procedure for fare fixation by a committee and binding recommendations (Chapter VII).
Procedure for reporting and inquiring into metro railway accidents, including powers of the Commissioner (Chapter VIII).
Procedure for Claims Commissioners to handle compensation claims (Chapter IX).
Procedures for arrest and trial of offenders (Sections 82-85).
Procedure for the delivery of property detained by metro railway officials (Section 91).
Procedures for service of notices by and on the metro railway administration (Sections 93-95).
administration: Central Government (Ministry of Railways for technical planning and safety), and the respective Metro Railway Administration (General Manager for Government metro railways, owner/lessee/operator for non-Government metro railways).
important_notes: The Act can be extended to other metropolitan areas by notification by the Central Government.
Certain definitions are based on other Acts like the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, Railways Act, 1989, and the Constitution of India.
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act (Section 99).
Rules and regulations made under the Act are to be laid before Parliament (Section 102).

title: The Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005
purpose: To provide for the regulation of private security agencies and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to persons and bodies engaged in the business of providing private security services, including training of private security guards and supervisors.

key_definitions.armoured car_service: Service provided by deployment of armed guards along with armored cars and related services as notified by the Central or State Government.
key_definitions.controlling_authority: An officer designated by the State Government, not below the rank of Joint Secretary in the Home Department or equivalent, responsible for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.licence: A license granted under sub-section (5) of section 7.
key_definitions.private_security: Security provided by a person, other than a public servant, to protect or guard any person or property, including armored car service.
key_definitions.private_security_agency: A person or body of persons, other than a government agency, engaged in providing private security services, including training to private security guards or supervisors, or providing private security guards to any industrial or business undertaking, company, or any other person or property.
key_definitions.private_security_guard: A person providing private security with or without arms to another person or property, and includes a supervisor.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'armoured car service', 'Controlling Authority', 'licence', 'private security', 'private security agency', and 'private security guard'.

The State Government shall designate an officer, not below the rank of Joint Secretary in the Home Department or equivalent, as the Controlling Authority. The State Government may also provide additional staff for efficient functioning.

main_sections.section_title: Persons or Private Security Agency not to engage or provide private security guard without licence
main_sections.description: No person can carry on or commence the business of a private security agency without a license. Existing agencies have one year to obtain a license. Agencies cannot provide private security abroad without permission from the Controlling Authority, which must consult the Central Government.
An application for a license will only be considered after a due verification of the applicant's antecedents.

This section outlines conditions under which a person or a company is not eligible for a license, including past convictions for fraud, offenses with imprisonment of not less than two years, links with banned organizations, dismissal from government service for misconduct, or if a company is not registered in India or has non-citizen proprietors/majority shareholders.

Details the process for applying for a license, including the form, required affidavit, training availability, conditions, pending cases, application fees based on operational area, and the timeframe for the Controlling Authority to grant or refuse the license within sixty days after inquiry and obtaining no-objection certificates.
Specifies the process for license renewal, requiring application at least 45 days before expiry, with requisite fees and documents. The Controlling Authority must pass an order within thirty days.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions for commencement of operation and engagement of supervisors
main_sections.description: Requires private security agencies to commence activities within six months of obtaining a license. They must ensure training for guards and supervisors and employ a prescribed number of supervisors within sixty days of license issuance. Preference is given to ex-servicemen or former police personnel for supervisor roles.

main_sections.section_title: Eligibility to be a private security guard
main_sections.description: Outlines the criteria for employing a private security guard, including citizenship, age limits, character and antecedent verification, successful completion of prescribed training, physical standards, and not having been convicted or dismissed for misconduct from armed forces or government service. Preference is given to ex-servicemen and former police personnel.

The State Government may frame rules prescribing license conditions, including training requirements, details of the agency's personnel, and obligations to inform the Controlling Authority about changes in address, management, or any criminal charges.
Every private security agency must exhibit its license or a copy thereof in a conspicuous place at its business premises.

The Controlling Authority can cancel a license on various grounds, including obtaining it through misrepresentation, using false documents, violating the Act or license conditions, misusing information, impersonating government agencies, failure to commence activities or employ supervisors within specified times, wilful failure to render agreed services, violation of court orders, or repeated instances of guards failing to provide security or being negligent.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders of the Controlling Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Register to be maintained by a private security agency
main_sections.description: Requires private security agencies to maintain a register.
Allows for inspection of licenses and other relevant documents.
Mandates the issue of photo identity cards to private security guards.

main_sections.section_title: Disclosure of information to unauthorised person
main_sections.description: Prohibits the disclosure of information obtained during duty to unauthorized persons.
Empowers the delegation of powers by the Controlling Authority or State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for contravention of certain provisions
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening certain provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for unauthorised use of certain uniforms
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties for the unauthorized use of uniforms associated with private security agencies.
Deals with offenses committed by companies.
Provides for indemnity to officers acting in good faith.

main_sections.section_title: Framing of model rules for adoption by States
main_sections.description: The Central Government may frame model rules for adoption by the States.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall carry on or commence the business of private security agency without a license.
Private security agencies must ensure training for their guards and supervisors as prescribed.
Private security guards must meet eligibility criteria including age, character, training, and physical standards.
Private security agencies must exhibit their license in a conspicuous place.
Licenses can be cancelled for obtaining them through misrepresentation, violating the Act, misusing information, or failing to provide agreed services.

penalties: Punishment for contravention of certain provisions (Section 20).
Penalty for unauthorized use of certain uniforms (Section 21).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Controlling Authority appointed by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance, renewal, suspension, and cancellation of licenses, inspection of records, and imposition of penalties for contraventions. State Governments are empowered to make rules for enforcement.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of the Controlling Authority (Section 14).
Right to be heard before a license is refused or cancelled.
duties: Duty to obtain and display a license.
Duty to impart prescribed training to private security guards and supervisors.
Duty to employ eligible persons as private security guards and supervisors.
Duty to report changes in address, management, or criminal charges to the Controlling Authority.
Duty not to disclose information to unauthorized persons.
Duty to maintain a register.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation to adhere to the conditions of the license.
Obligation to ensure that private security guards and supervisors meet eligibility criteria and have received necessary training.

key_procedures: Application for a license: Submit an application with an affidavit, details of training, conditions met, and any pending cases to the Controlling Authority. Pay prescribed fee based on operational area.
Grant or refusal of license: Controlling Authority conducts inquiries, obtains no-objection certificate, and grants or refuses the license within 60 days, providing reasons for refusal.
Renewal of license: Apply for renewal at least 45 days before expiry with requisite fee and documents. Controlling Authority passes an order within 30 days.
Cancellation of license: Controlling Authority may cancel a license on various grounds after giving the holder an opportunity to be heard.
administration: The State Government, through the designated Controlling Authority (an officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary in the Home Department or equivalent), administers the Act.
important_notes: The Act was extended to the whole of India, omitting the exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The Act came into force on March 14, 2006.
Existing private security agencies had one year from the commencement of the Act to obtain a license, with provisions for ongoing applications.
Preference for employing supervisors and private security guards is given to persons with experience in the Army, Navy, Air Force, State Police, or Home Guards.

title: THE MANIPUR UNIVERSITY ACT, 2005
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Manipur and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The jurisdiction of the University extends to the whole of the State of Manipur. The Act applies to the Manipur University, its employees, students, and affiliated institutions within Manipur.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.Affiliated College: A college admitted to the privileges of the University.
key_definitions.University: The Manipur University established and incorporated as a University under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on October 13, 2005.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'Affiliated College', 'University', among others.

Establishes the Manipur University as a body corporate under this Act, continuing the existence of the university established under the Manipur University Act, 1980. It outlines the composition of the University and its perpetual succession, common seal, and headquarters at Imphal.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of establishment of the University
main_sections.description: Details the consequences of the Act's commencement, including the transfer of references, properties, rights, and liabilities from the old Manipur University to the new University. It also covers the continuation of employment for existing staff with provisions for termination and compensation, and the deemed appointment of the Vice-Chancellor.

Outlines the primary objectives of the University, such as disseminating knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, promoting integrated courses, fostering innovations, training manpower for the State's development, and improving social and economic conditions and welfare.

Enumerates the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting diplomas and degrees, organizing extramural studies, conferring honorary degrees, establishing distance education, instituting teaching positions, recognizing institutions, appointing teachers, creating posts, collaborating with other bodies, establishing specialized units, awarding fellowships, establishing and maintaining colleges, providing research and advisory services, organizing refresher courses, admitting affiliated colleges, appointing visiting professors, conferring autonomous status, determining admission standards, collecting fees, supervising student residences, laying down conditions of service for employees, regulating discipline, promoting employee welfare, receiving donations, and acquiring and disposing of property. It also includes the power to borrow money with Central Government approval and to perform all acts conducive to its objects.
Specifies that the University's jurisdiction extends to the entire State of Manipur.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all individuals regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, prohibiting any religious tests for admission, employment, or privileges. It includes a proviso for making special provisions for women, the physically handicapped, and weaker sections like Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and grants the Visitor the power to appoint persons to review the work and progress of the University.

duties: The University has a duty to disseminate and advance knowledge.
The University must provide instructional and research facilities.
The University must promote innovations in teaching-learning and research.
The University must educate and train manpower for the development of Manipur.
The University must pay special attention to improving the social and economic conditions and welfare of the people of Manipur.

The University is open to all, but special provisions can be made for employment or admission of women, physically handicapped, and weaker sections.
