title: The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a National Commission and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights and Children's Courts for providing speedy trial of offences against children or of violation of child rights and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. It aims to give effect to policies adopted by the Government regarding children, standards prescribed in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC), and other relevant international instruments.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It establishes a National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights, and defines Children's Courts. It applies to all matters concerning the protection of child rights in India.

key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Commission or of the State Commission, as the case may be.
key_definitions.child rights: Includes the children's rights adopted in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child on the 20th November, 1989 and ratified by the Government of India on the 11th December, 1992.
key_definitions.Commission: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Commission or the State Commission, as the case may be, and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.State Commission: A State Commission for Protection of Child Rights constituted under section 17.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement as notified by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including Chairperson, child rights, Commission, Member, notification, prescribed, and State Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights by the Central Government. Details its composition, consisting of a Chairperson and six Members with specific qualifications and representation.
Outlines the process for appointing the Chairperson and other Members of the National Commission by the Central Government, including the role of a Selection Committee for the Chairperson.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office (three years) for the Chairperson and Members, limits on the number of terms (two), and the age of retirement (sixty-five for Chairperson, sixty for Members). It also allows for resignation.

main_sections.section_title: Salary and allowances of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: States that the salary, allowances, and other service conditions of the Chairperson and Members will be prescribed by the Central Government, and these shall not be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.

Details the grounds on which the Chairperson or a Member can be removed from office by the Central Government, including misbehaviour, incapacity, insolvency, engaging in paid employment outside duties, unsound mind, abuse of office, conviction for certain offences, and absence from meetings. A hearing opportunity must be given.

main_sections.section_title: Vacation of office by Chairperson or Members
main_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which a seat becomes vacant (disqualifications under section 7 or resignation). It also provides for filling casual vacancies within ninety days by a fresh appointment for the remainder of the term.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of Commission
main_sections.description: Ensures that the proceedings of the Commission are not invalidated due to vacancies, defects in its constitution, or procedural irregularities that do not affect the merits of a case.
Lays down the rules for the Commission's meetings, including frequency, decision-making by majority (with casting vote for Chairperson), quorum, and authentication of orders and decisions.

main_sections.section_title: Member-Secretary, officers and other employees of Commission
main_sections.description: Describes the appointment of a Member-Secretary and other necessary officers and employees by the Central Government. It outlines the responsibilities of the Member-Secretary for administration and management.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries and allowances to be paid out of grants
main_sections.description: States that the salaries and allowances of the Chairperson, Members, Member-Secretary, and other employees, as well as administrative expenses, are to be paid out of the grants referred to in section 27.

Enumerate the extensive functions of the National Commission, including examining safeguards for child rights, inquiring into violations, examining factors affecting children, looking into children in need of special care, studying international instruments, promoting research, and spreading child rights literacy.

Grants powers to the Commission to conduct inquiries, which include summoning persons, examining witnesses, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, and requisitioning public records.
Specifies the actions the Commission can take after an inquiry, such as passing orders or recommendations, and forwarding them to the concerned authorities or governments.

main_sections.section_title: Annual and special reports of Commission
main_sections.description: Requires the Commission to present annual and special reports to the Central Government on its working, which are then to be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of State Commission for Protection of Child Rights
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights by the respective State Governments.
Designates Courts of Session as Children's Courts for speedy trial of offences against children or violations of child rights.
Details the provisions for grants made by the Central Government to the National Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Governments to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act within their respective States.

important_rules: Rule: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights shall be constituted by the Central Government.
Rule: The Commission shall consist of a Chairperson and six Members, with at least two women members.
Rule: The Chairperson and Members shall hold office for a term of three years, with a maximum of two terms, and subject to age limits.
Rule: The Commission shall meet regularly, with no more than three months between meetings.
Rule: Decisions at Commission meetings shall be taken by majority, with the Chairperson having a casting vote.
Rule: The functions of the Commission include examining safeguards for child rights, inquiring into violations, and recommending remedial measures.
Rule: State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights are to be constituted by State Governments.
Rule: Courts of Session are designated as Children's Courts for speedy trials related to children.
Rule: The Central Government can make rules to implement the Act, and State Governments can make rules for their respective states.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights, and Children's Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries conducted by the Commissions, recommendations made by the Commissions, and speedy trials of offences against children by Children's Courts. The Central and State Governments are responsible for implementing the Act and making rules.

rights: Children's rights as adopted in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.
The right to have their rights protected by safeguards provided under law.
The right to have violations of their rights inquired into.
The right to special care and protection for children in distress, marginalized children, children in conflict with law, etc.
The right to have their enjoyment of rights promoted and protected against various inhibiting factors.
duties: Duty to provide for the constitution of a National Commission and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights.
Duty to constitute Children's Courts for speedy trials.
Duty to ensure the effective implementation of safeguards for child rights.
Duty to examine and address factors that inhibit the enjoyment of child rights.
Duty to undertake and promote research in child rights.
Duty to spread child rights literacy and awareness.
obligations: Obligation to take all necessary steps to protect children's rights as per international treaties.
Obligation to give effect to national policies and international instruments concerning children.
Obligation for the National Commission to present reports on the working of safeguards to the Central Government.
Obligation for the Central Government to consider recommendations from the Commission.
Obligation for the Central Government and State Governments to frame rules as prescribed by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: Constitution of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights by the Central Government through notification.
Procedure: Appointment of Chairperson and Members of the National Commission by the Central Government on the recommendation of a Selection Committee.
Procedure: Conducting meetings of the Commission with specific rules regarding frequency, quorum, and decision-making.
Procedure: Inquiring into violations of child rights by the Commission, including summoning witnesses and examining evidence.
Procedure: Presenting annual and special reports by the Commission to the Central Government.
Procedure: Constitution of State Commissions by State Governments.
Procedure: Designation of Children's Courts by the State Government.
Procedure: Making rules by the Central Government and State Governments to carry out the Act's purposes.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments are responsible for administering the Act, with the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights carrying out specific functions.
important_notes: Note: The extent of the Act was formerly "except the State of Jammu and Kashmir" but this was omitted by Act 34 of 2019.
Note: The Act came into force on 5th February, 2007, vide notification No. S.O. 229(E).
Note: Provisions related to the removal of Chairperson or Member require an opportunity of being heard.
Note: Any casual vacancy in the office of the Chairperson or Member must be filled within ninety days.
Note: The salaries and allowances of the Chairperson and Members shall not be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
Note: The Act aligns with India's participation in the UN General Assembly Summit, accession to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, and adoption of the National Charter for Children, 2003.

title: THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FASHION TECHNOLOGY ACT, 2006
purpose: To establish and incorporate the National Institute of Fashion Technology for the promotion and development of education and research in fashion technology and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), its campuses (initially in New Delhi, Gandhinagar, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, Kolkata, and potentially others in India or abroad), and its operations related to fashion technology education, research, and development. It covers all persons associated with the Institute, including students, faculty, staff, and governing bodies.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of establishment of the National Institute of Fashion Technology under section 3(1).
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of the Institute constituted under section 3(3).
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Institute nominated under section 3(3)(a).
key_definitions.Director-General: The Director-General of the Institute appointed under section 15.
key_definitions.fashion: Includes a popular trend or a lifestyle, especially in styles of dress and ornament or manners of behaviour or the business of creating, promoting or studying styles in vogue or the designing, production and marketing of new styles of goods such as clothing, accessories, craft and cosmetics.
key_definitions.fashion technology: Includes grammatical variations and cognate expressions of 'fashion'.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Institute to be maintained under section 19.
key_definitions.Institute: The National Institute of Fashion Technology established under section 3(1).
key_definitions.Institute Campus: An Institute Campus located at New Delhi, Gandhinagar, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, Kolkata or any other place in India or abroad as may be decided by the Board of Governors.
key_definitions.Senate: The Senate of the Institute referred to in section 12.
key_definitions.Society: The National Institute of Fashion Technology, New Delhi registered as a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860).
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: The Statutes and the Ordinances of the Institute made under this Act, respectively.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the National Institute of Fashion Technology Act, 2006 and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette, allowing for different dates for different provisions.

Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Director-General', 'fashion', 'fashion technology', 'Fund', 'Institute', 'Institute Campus', 'Senate', 'Society', and 'Statutes and Ordinances'.

Establishes the National Institute of Fashion Technology as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It outlines the composition of the Board of Governors, including the Chairperson, Members of Parliament, ex-officio members, and nominated representatives, and defines their terms of office and meeting procedures.
States that on and from the appointed day, all properties vested in the Society shall vest in the Institute.

Details the consequences of the Institute's incorporation, including the transfer of rights and liabilities from the Society to the Institute, and the continuation of employment for existing employees under similar terms and conditions, with provisions for termination or alteration of terms.

Enumerate the broad functions of the Institute, which include promoting education and research in fashion technology, laying down courses, granting degrees, cooperating with other institutions, conducting courses for professionals, undertaking research, developing information centers, creating a faculty resource, experimenting and innovating, developing an international center, fostering a multi-disciplinary approach, organizing symposia, catering to developing countries' needs, acting as a liaison between academia and industry, providing technical assistance, and carrying out other related activities.

Outlines the powers of the Board of Governors, which include overall superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs. Specific powers include making policy decisions, establishing new campuses, fixing fees, managing student residences, instituting academic posts, framing Statutes and Ordinances, awarding fellowships, considering reports and accounts, and receiving gifts. It also details the Central Government's power to review the Institute's work and issue directions, and the Visitor's/Central Government's power to remove Board members.

main_sections.section_title: Institute be open to all races, creeds and classes
main_sections.description: Mandates that the Institute shall be open to all persons regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, without imposing religious tests or conditions for admission or appointment. It also states that the Institute shall not accept bequests or donations that involve conditions opposed to this principle.
Specifies that all teaching at the Institute's campuses shall be conducted in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances.
Mentions the establishment of a Tribunal of Arbitration, although its specific functions and composition are not detailed in the provided text.

main_sections.section_title: Acts and proceedings not to be invalidated by vacancies, etc.
main_sections.description: States that the acts and proceedings of the Institute shall not be invalidated by reason of any vacancy or defect in the constitution of any of its authorities or by reason of any defect or irregularity in the appointment of any member thereof.
Refers to sponsored schemes, indicating the Institute may undertake projects funded by external entities.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Institute to grant degrees, etc.
main_sections.description: Confers upon the Institute the power to grant degrees, diplomas, certificates and other academic distinctions in fashion technology.
Empowers the Central Government to make such orders as may be necessary for removing any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.
Allows for provisions to be made for the transition from the existing arrangements to the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Statutes and Ordinances to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires that all Statutes and Ordinances made under this Act shall be published in the Official Gazette and laid before each House of Parliament.

important_rules: The Institute shall be open to all persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class, without religious tests or conditions for admission or appointment.
No bequest or donation shall be accepted if it involves conditions opposed to the spirit of non-discrimination.
Teaching at the Institute campuses must be conducted in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances.
The Board of Governors is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs.
The Board shall meet at least four times a year.
The Board shall not dispose of any immovable property without prior approval from the Central Government.
The Central Government has the power to review the work and progress of the Institute and issue directions, which the Institute must comply with.
Members of the Board (Chairperson and others nominated by the Visitor) can be removed by the Visitor on the recommendations of the Central Government.
Other members of the Board can be removed by the Central Government if deemed appropriate.
No Chairperson or member shall be removed without being given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Visitor, and the Institute's Board of Governors and other authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Board of Governors, the Visitor, and the Central Government to issue directions, review operations, remove members, and make rules through Statutes and Ordinances. The Central Government can also make orders to remove difficulties.

rights: Right to education and research in fashion technology.
Right to be considered for admission without discrimination based on race, creed, caste, or class.

Employees have rights to their existing tenure, remuneration, terms, and conditions, including pension, leave, gratuity, and provident fund, unless duly altered with compensation for unaccepted alterations.
duties: Duty of the Institute to promote quality and excellence in fashion technology education and research.
Duty of the Board to ensure the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs.
Duty of the Institute to comply with directions issued by the Central Government.
Duty to provide an opportunity of being heard before removal of any member.
Duty to conduct teaching in accordance with Statutes and Ordinances.
obligations: Obligation of the Institute to be open to all races, creeds, and classes.
Obligation of the Institute to not accept donations with discriminatory conditions.
Obligation of the Institute to maintain its Fund.
Obligation to publish Statutes and Ordinances in the Official Gazette and lay them before Parliament.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Institute by the Central Government notification.
Constitution of the Board of Governors with specified members and terms.
Meeting procedures for the Board of Governors.
Process for making Statutes and Ordinances by the Board.
Process for the Central Government to appoint persons to review the Institute's work and issue directions.
Procedure for removal of Board members, including the requirement for a hearing.
Publication of Statutes and Ordinances in the Official Gazette and laying them before Parliament.
administration: The Act establishes the National Institute of Fashion Technology. The overall administration and control lie with the Board of Governors, under the overall control of the Central Government. The Central Government also has significant oversight and directive powers. The Visitor (likely the President of India, though not explicitly stated in the excerpt) has powers related to appointing the Chairperson and removing certain Board members.
important_notes: The Act came into force on April 1, 2007, for all provisions, as notified by the Central Government.
The Institute has a common seal and can acquire property and contract.
The Institute is a body corporate with perpetual succession.
The Institute is open to all, irrespective of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, and no religious tests are imposed.
The Central Government can appoint persons to review the Institute's work and issue directions.
Statutes and Ordinances are subject to parliamentary review.
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

title: The Actuaries Act, 2006
purpose: To provide for regulating and developing the profession of Actuaries and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to individuals engaged in the actuarial profession, including those involved in determining the present effects of future contingent events, finance modelling, risk analysis, insurance, annuities, pensions, and related financial and investment matters. It also governs the Institute of Actuaries of India and the dissolution of the Actuarial Society of India.

key_definitions.actuary: A person skilled in determining the present effects of future contingent events or in finance modelling and risk analysis in different areas of insurance, or calculating the value of life interests and insurance risks, or designing and pricing of policies, working out benefits, recommending rates relating to insurance business, annuities, insurance and pension rates on the basis of empirically based tables, and includes a statistician engaged in such technology, taxation, employees' benefits and such other risk management and investments, who is a fellow member of the Institute.
key_definitions.institute: The Institute of Actuaries of India constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.member: An individual whose name appears in the register of members maintained by the Institute.
key_definitions.register: The register of members maintained by the Institute under this Act.
key_definitions.actuarial_society: The Actuarial Society of India registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 and the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950.
key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which the Institute is constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act (The Actuaries Act, 2006), its extent (whole of India), and commencement date, which can be appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Actuary', 'Institute of Actuaries of India', 'member', 'register', 'Actuarial Society', 'appointed day', 'Authority', 'Board', 'Council', 'fellow', 'prescribed', 'President', 'specified', 'Tribunal', 'Vice-President', and 'year'.

Constitutes the Institute of Actuaries of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowering it to acquire and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued. The head office location is to be decided by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets, liabilities, etc., of Actuarial Society
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of all assets and liabilities of the Actuarial Society to the Institute on the appointed day, including rights, properties, debts, obligations, contracts, and legal proceedings.

Outlines the objectives of the Institute, which include promoting and developing the standards of professional education, training, knowledge, practice, and conduct of Actuaries; promoting the status of the actuarial profession; regulating its practice; promoting knowledge and research in actuarial science; and performing incidental activities.

Specifies the categories of persons entitled to have their names entered in the register, including former members of the Actuarial Society, those who passed its examinations and training, and those who pass examinations and complete training specified for the Institute's membership. It also includes provisions for honorary fellowship and conditions for non-resident individuals.

Divides members into two classes: associates and fellows. Entry into the register generally makes a person an associate (entitled to use 'AIAI'). Former fellows of the Actuarial Society entered under section 6(1)(a) become fellows (entitled to use 'FIAI').

Allows the Council to appoint honorary members, admit affiliate members from similar institutions, and admit student members who enroll for Institute examinations and possess specified academic qualifications. These members do not have voting rights.
Stipulates that no member can practice unless they fulfill specified qualifications and obtain a certificate of practice from the Council. An annual fee is payable for this certificate.

main_sections.section_title: Members to be known as Actuaries
main_sections.description: States that members of the Institute shall be known as Actuaries.
Likely to detail conditions under which a person may be disqualified from being a member or practicing as an actuary (content not fully provided in excerpt).

Deals with the establishment and functions of a Disciplinary Committee (content not fully provided in excerpt).

main_sections.description: Outlines the actions the Council must take based on the reports of the Disciplinary Committee (content not fully provided in excerpt).
Defines what constitutes professional or other misconduct for members of the Institute (content not fully provided in excerpt).
Concerns the formation of an Appellate Authority (content not fully provided in excerpt).
Specifies the process for appealing to the Appellate Authority (content not fully provided in excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, etc.
main_sections.description: Introduces penalties for individuals falsely claiming to be a member of the Institute (content not fully provided in excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Companies not to engage in actuarial practice
main_sections.description: Prohibits companies from engaging in actuarial practice (content not fully provided in excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Unqualified person not to sign documents
main_sections.description: Prevents unqualified individuals from signing documents related to actuarial practice (content not fully provided in excerpt).
Covers the establishment of a Quality Review Board (content not fully provided in excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of Actuarial Society of India
main_sections.description: Provides for the dissolution of the Actuarial Society of India (content not fully provided in excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Institute (content not fully provided in excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules under the Act (content not fully provided in excerpt).
Empowers the Institute's Council to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules (content not fully provided in excerpt).

important_rules: Members in practice must obtain a certificate of practice from the Council.
An annual fee is payable for the certificate of practice on or before the first day of April each year.
The Actuarial Society of India is dissolved and its assets and liabilities are transferred to the Institute of Actuaries of India.
The Institute is established as a body corporate responsible for regulating and developing the actuarial profession.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions, make rules, and appoint commencement dates for different provisions of the Act.

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, etc. (Section 37)
Penalty for using the name of the Institution, awarding degrees of actuarial science, etc. (Section 38)
Penalties for unqualified persons signing documents (Section 40)
Offences by companies (Section 41)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Institute of Actuaries of India, its Council, Disciplinary Committee, and potentially the Central Government or an Appellate Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary proceedings, imposition of penalties for violations, and potentially legal action for offences. The Quality Review Board likely plays a role in ensuring quality standards.

rights: Members whose names are entered in the register have rights, subject to provisions of the Act.
Fellows are entitled to use the letters 'FIAI', and associates 'AIAI'.
Members in practice have the right to practice upon obtaining a certificate of practice.
Members have the right to be afforded an opportunity of being heard in disciplinary proceedings.
duties: Members have a duty to uphold and develop the standards of professional education, training, knowledge, practice, and conduct.
Members have a duty to regulate their practice in accordance with the Act and Council regulations.
Members must comply with the requirements for obtaining and maintaining a certificate of practice.
Members must not engage in professional or other misconduct.
obligations: Members must ensure their names are entered in the register as per the Act's provisions.
Members must pay specified fees for membership and certificates of practice.
Members must adhere to the disciplinary procedures and decisions made by the Council and Disciplinary Committee.

key_procedures: Entry of names into the register of members (Section 6).
Application for and obtaining a certificate of practice (Section 9).
Disciplinary proceedings initiated by the Disciplinary Committee and action by the Council (Sections 26-30).
Appeals to the Appellate Authority (Sections 32-36).
Establishment and functioning of the Quality Review Board (Sections 43-47).
administration: The Institute of Actuaries of India, governed by its Council, is the primary administrative body. The Central Government also plays a significant role in rule-making, direction issuance, and appointment of commencement dates.
important_notes: Different commencement dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
Non-permanent residents of India may have additional conditions imposed by the Central Government or the Council for membership.
Honorary, affiliate, and student members do not have voting rights.
Companies are generally not permitted to engage in actuarial practice; the practice is for individual actuaries or firms of actuaries.
The Act aims to regulate and develop the actuarial profession, implying a focus on quality, ethics, and professional standards.

title: THE ASSAM RIFLES ACT, 2006
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the governance of the Assam Rifles, an Armed Force of the Union for ensuring the security of the borders of India, to carry out Counter Insurgency Operations in the specified areas and to act in aid of civil authorities for the maintenance of law and order and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the Assam Rifles, an armed force of the Union, for ensuring border security, conducting counter-insurgency operations, and assisting civil authorities in maintaining law and order. It governs persons subject to the Act.

key_definitions.active duty: Means any duty as a member of the Force during operations against an enemy, insurgent, terrorist, person in arms, or engaged on border guard duty. It also includes periods declared by the Central Government as active duty.
key_definitions.Assam Rifles Court: A Court referred to in section 86.
key_definitions.civil offence: An offence that is triable by a criminal court.
key_definitions.enemy: Includes armed mutineers, rebels, rioters, pirates, terrorists, and any person in arms against whom it is the duty of a person subject to this Act to take action.
key_definitions.enrolled person: An under-officer or other person enrolled under this Act.
key_definitions.member of the Force: Means an officer, subordinate officer, under-officer, other enrolled person, and includes persons on deputation.
key_definitions.offence: Means any act or omission punishable under this Act and includes a civil offence.
key_definitions.officer: A person appointed or in pay as an officer of the Force, excluding subordinate officers or under-officers.
key_definitions.terrorist: A person who, with intent to overawe the Government or strike terror, causes or is likely to cause death or injury to persons or damage/destruction to property through various means including explosives, firearms, or hazardous substances.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'active duty', 'civil offence', 'enemy', 'Force', 'member of the Force', 'offence', and 'terrorist'.
Specifies who are the persons subject to the provisions of this Act.
Details the constitution of the Assam Rifles Force.

main_sections.section_title: Offences in relation to the enemy and punishable with death
main_sections.description: Outlines offences committed in relation to the enemy that carry the death penalty.
Enumerates the different types of Assam Rifles Courts that can be convened.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings provisions.

important_rules: Only authorized deductions can be made from pay (Section 14).
Remedies are available for aggrieved persons, including officers (Sections 15, 16).
Persons subject to the Act have immunity from attachment and arrest for debt (Sections 17, 18).
The Act defines a comprehensive list of offences related to military discipline, duty, and conduct (Chapters IV, V).
Procedures for arrest, trial, and punishment are established, including the convening and powers of Assam Rifles Courts (Chapters VII, VIII, IX, X, XI).

penalties: Death penalty for certain offences in relation to the enemy (Section 21).
Various punishments for different offences including imprisonment, reduction in rank, forfeiture of pay, and dismissal (Chapter V).
Collective fines can be imposed (Section 67).
Penal deductions from pay and allowances for various offences and periods of absence/custody (Chapter VI).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Assam Rifles, under the control and direction of the Central Government and the Director-General.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the internal disciplinary mechanisms of the Assam Rifles, including Assam Rifles Courts, summary punishments, and through general criminal courts for civil offences. Enforcement involves investigation, arrest, trial by courts, and execution of sentences.

rights: Right to remedy if aggrieved (Sections 15, 16).
Immunity from attachment and arrest for debt (Sections 17, 18).
Rights and privileges under other laws are saved (Section 20).
Right to fair trial by Assam Rifles Courts as per laid down procedures.
Right to pardon, remission, or commutation of sentences (Section 150).
duties: Duty to obey orders from superior officers (Section 28).
Duty to maintain good order and discipline (Section 49).
Duty to report for service and adhere to the terms of enrolment.
Duty to uphold the security of India's borders and participate in counter-insurgency operations.
obligations: Obligation to be subject to the Act and its provisions.
Obligation to perform duties diligently and without becoming unbecoming of a member of the Force.
Obligation to surrender for arrest or custody when required.

key_procedures: Enrolment procedures for new members (Section 6).
Procedures for resignation and withdrawal from service (Section 8).
Procedures for arrest and custody of offenders (Chapter VII).
Procedures for convening and conducting trials by Assam Rifles Courts (Chapters VIII, IX).
Procedures for confirmation and revision of findings and sentences (Chapter X).
Procedures for execution of sentences, including imprisonment and fines (Chapter XI).
Procedures for dealing with lunatic accused (Sections 121-125).
administration: The Central Government, with the Director-General and other appointed officers of the Assam Rifles overseeing its administration.
important_notes: The Act distinguishes between 'officers', 'subordinate officers', and 'enrolled persons' with varying service conditions and disciplinary powers.
The Act specifies limitations on the right to form associations and freedom of speech for members of the Force (Section 13).
The Act allows for the application of the Indian Penal Code and other civil laws for 'civil offences' (Sections 55, 56).

title: THE PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS REGULATORY BOARD ACT, 2006
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board to regulate the refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing, and sale of petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas (excluding production of crude oil and natural gas). The act aims to protect the interests of consumers and entities engaged in specified activities, ensure uninterrupted and adequate supply across the country, and promote competitive markets.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing, and sale of petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas, excluding the production of crude oil and natural gas.

key_definitions.Board: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Authorised entity: An entity registered by the Board to market notified petroleum, petroleum products, or natural gas, or to establish and operate liquefied natural gas terminals; or an entity authorised by the Board to lay, build, operate, or expand a common carrier or contract carrier, or to lay, build, operate, or expand a city or local natural gas distribution network.
key_definitions.City or local natural gas distribution n: An interconnected network of gas pipelines and associated equipment used for transporting natural gas from a bulk supply high-pressure transmission main to the medium-pressure distribution grid and subsequently to service pipes supplying natural gas to domestic, industrial, or commercial premises and CNG stations within a specified geographical area.
key_definitions.Common carrier: Pipelines for the transportation of petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas by more than one entity, declared or authorised by the Board on a non-discriminatory open access basis, excluding pipelines to supply a specific consumer or crude oil. A contract carrier is treated as a common carrier if it has surplus capacity or its firm contract period has expired.
key_definitions.Contract carrier: Pipelines for the transportation of petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas by more than one entity pursuant to firm contracts for at least one year, as declared or authorised by the Board.
key_definitions.Entity: A person, association of persons, firm, company, or co-operative society, other than a dealer or distributor, engaged or intending to be engaged in refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing, import, and export of petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas, including laying of pipelines, city or local natural gas distribution networks, or establishing and operating a liquefied natural gas terminal.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act as the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act, 2006. It states that the Act extends to the whole of India, comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, and applies to the specified activities related to petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas (excluding production).

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'authorised entity', 'city or local natural gas distribution network', 'common carrier', 'contract carrier', 'entity', and many others crucial for understanding the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the establishment of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract.

Outlines the primary functions of the Board, which include regulating the refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing, and sale of petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas to protect consumer interests, ensure adequate supply, and promote competition.
Requires the Board to maintain a register of all entities registered or authorised under the Act.
Deals with the process of granting authorisation to entities for laying, building, operating, or expanding a common carrier or contract carrier, or a city or local natural gas distribution network.

main_sections.section_title: Declaring, laying, building, etc., of common carrier or contract carrier and city or local natural gas distribution network
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for declaring and authorising common carriers, contract carriers, and city or local natural gas distribution networks.
Empowers the Board to determine transportation tariffs for common carriers and contract carriers.
Establishes the Board's role in settling disputes related to the petroleum and natural gas sector.

main_sections.section_title: Civil penalty for contravention of directions given by the Board
main_sections.description: Provides for the imposition of civil penalties on entities that contravene directions issued by the Board.
Provides for the establishment of an Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals against orders passed by the Board.
Allows for an appeal to the Supreme Court against an order passed by the Appellate Tribunal.
Details the creation and management of the Fund of the Board, which will be used for its functions.
Mandates that the accounts of the Board be maintained and audited in the prescribed manner.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Board on policy matters.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for contravention of directions of the Board
main_sections.description: Specifies punishments for entities that contravene directions issued by the Board.
Prescribes punishments for carrying out activities related to petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas without the necessary authorisation or registration.
Outlines the obligations that entities engaged in the petroleum and natural gas sector must adhere to.

main_sections.section_title: Civil courts not to have jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Stipulates that civil courts shall not have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which the Board or the Appellate Tribunal is empowered to determine.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules made by the Central Government.

important_rules: Entities involved in refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing, and sale of petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas must comply with the regulations set by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board.
Any entity intending to lay, build, operate, or expand a common carrier or contract carrier, or a city or local natural gas distribution network must obtain authorisation from the Board.
Entities must adhere to the transportation tariffs determined by the Board for common carriers and contract carriers.
Entities must not contravene directions or orders issued by the Board or the Appellate Tribunal.
Entities have obligations to supply natural gas to consumers as a local distribution entity and to maintain minimum stock of notified petroleum and petroleum products.
Civil courts are barred from entertaining suits or proceedings concerning matters that the Board or Appellate Tribunal is empowered to decide.

penalties: Civil penalty for contravention of directions given by the Board (Section 28).
Punishment for contravention of directions of the Board (Section 44).
Penalty for wilful failure to comply with orders of Appellate Tribunal (Section 45).
Punishment for unauthorised activities (Section 46).
Punishment for establishing or operating a liquefied natural gas terminal without registration (Section 47).
Punishment for laying, building, operating, or expanding a common carrier or contract carrier without authorisation (Section 48).
Punishment for wilful damages to common carrier or contract carrier (Section 49).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) and the Appellate Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation of complaints, issuance of directions and orders, imposition of civil penalties and punishments, and through the appellate process up to the Supreme Court.

rights: Consumers have a right to protection of their interests.
Entities have a right to seek authorisation for specified activities.
Entities have a right to appeal against orders of the Board to the Appellate Tribunal.
Entities have a right to fair and non-discriminatory access to common carriers and contract carriers.
Entities have a right to operate under a regulatory framework that promotes competitive markets.
duties: Entities have a duty to comply with the Act, rules, regulations, and directions issued by the Board.
Entities have a duty to ensure the safety and integrity of pipelines and infrastructure.
Entities have a duty to provide data and information to the Board and Central Government as required.
Entities have a duty to maintain minimum stock of notified petroleum and petroleum products.
Local distribution entities have a duty to supply natural gas to consumers.
obligations: Marketing service obligations, which include setting up marketing infrastructure and retail outlets in remote areas, maintaining minimum stock, and supplying natural gas to consumers.
Obligation to register or obtain authorisation from the Board for specific activities.

key_procedures: Registration of entities: Entities engaged in marketing notified petroleum, petroleum products, or natural gas, or in establishing and operating liquefied natural gas terminals must register with the Board (Section 15).

Authorisation for infrastructure: Entities seeking to lay, build, operate, or expand a common carrier, contract carrier, or city or local natural gas distribution network must apply for and obtain authorisation from the Board (Sections 16, 17, 19).
Complaint and dispute resolution: Filing of complaints with the Board and the Board's procedure for investigating and settling disputes (Sections 12, 13, 25).
Appeals: Filing appeals against orders of the Board before the Appellate Tribunal (Section 33) and subsequently to the Supreme Court (Section 37).
Rule-making and Regulation-making: Process for the Central Government to make rules (Section 60) and the Board to make regulations (Section 61).
administration: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is established to administer this Act. The Central Government also holds significant powers, including issuing directions and making rules.
important_notes: The Act excludes the production of crude oil and natural gas from its scope.
Different commencement dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The Board is required to maintain a data bank and information system relevant to the sector.
The Chairperson, members, and officers of the Board are considered public servants for the purposes of the Indian Penal Code.
Actions taken in good faith in execution of the Act are protected.

title: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006
purpose: To recognise and vest forest rights and occupation in forest land in forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers who have been residing in such forests for generations but whose rights could not be recorded; to provide for a framework for recording the forest rights so vested and the nature of evidence required for such recognition and vesting in respect of forest land. It aims to address historical injustice and insecurity of tenurial and access rights of these communities.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers who reside in and depend on forests for their livelihood.

key_definitions.community_forest_resource: Customary common forest land within the traditional or customary boundaries of the village or seasonal use of landscape, including reserved forests, protected forests, Sanctuaries and National Parks to which the community had traditional access.
key_definitions.critical_wildlife_habitat: Areas of National Parks and Sanctuaries required to be kept inviolate for wildlife conservation, determined by the Central Government after consultation with an Expert Committee.
key_definitions.forest_dwelling_scheduled_tribes: Members or community of Scheduled Tribes who primarily reside in and depend on forests or forest lands for bona fide livelihood needs, including Scheduled Tribe pastoralist communities.
key_definitions.forest_land: Land of any description falling within any forest area, including unclassified forests, undemarcated forests, existing or deemed forests, protected forests, reserved forests, Sanctuaries and National Parks.
key_definitions.forest_rights: Refers to the rights specified in section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.forest_villages: Settlements inside forests by forest departments for forestry operations or converted through forest reservation, including forest settlement villages, fixed demand holdings, and taungya settlements.
key_definitions.gram_sabha: A village assembly of all adult members, including women, with full and unrestricted participation. In states without Panchayats, it includes Padas, Tolas, and other traditional village institutions.
key_definitions.habitat: Includes customary habitat and other habitats in reserved and protected forests of primitive tribal groups, pre-agricultural communities, and other forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes.
key_definitions.minor_forest_produce: Non-timber forest produce of plant origin including bamboo, brush wood, stumps, cane, tussar, cocoons, honey, wax, lac, tendu or kendu leaves, medicinal plants and herbs, roots, tubers, and the like.
key_definitions.other_traditional_forest_dweller: Any member or community who has for at least three generations prior to December 13, 2005, primarily resided in and depended on forest or forest land for bona fide livelihood needs. 'Generation' means a period of twenty-five years.
key_definitions.village: As defined in the Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, or any State law relating to Panchayats, forest villages, old habitations, unsurveyed villages, or traditional villages where no Panchayats exist.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'community forest resource', 'critical wildlife habitat', 'forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes', 'forest land', 'forest rights', 'forest villages', 'Gram Sabha', 'habitat', 'minor forest produce', 'nodal agency', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'Scheduled Areas', 'sustainable use', 'other traditional forest dweller', 'village', and 'wild animal'.

main_sections.section_title: Forest rights of Forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers
main_sections.description: Specifies the forest rights that secure individual or community tenure on forest lands for forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers. These include rights to live and cultivate forest land, community rights like nistar, ownership and access to minor forest produce, grazing rights, rights for primitive tribal groups, rights in disputed lands, conversion of leases to titles, settlement of forest villages, right to protect and manage community forest resources, rights recognised under State or customary laws, access to biodiversity and traditional knowledge, and rights for rehabilitation of illegally evicted persons.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of, and vesting of, forest rights in forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers
main_sections.description: Recognises and vests forest rights in forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers. It also provides conditions under which forest rights in critical wildlife habitats may be modified or resettled, requiring specific conditions like completion of rights recognition, establishment of irreversible damage to wildlife, lack of co-existence options, provision of secure livelihood, free informed consent of Gram Sabhas, and completion of resettlement facilities before relocation.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of holders of forest rights
main_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of those holding forest rights, including the protection, regeneration, and conservation of the forest and biodiversity.

main_sections.section_title: Authorities to vest forest rights in forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers and procedure thereof
main_sections.description: Establishes the authorities responsible for vesting forest rights and the procedures to be followed for recognition and vesting.

main_sections.section_title: Offences by members or officers of authorities and Committees under this Act
main_sections.description: Deals with offences committed by members or officers of authorities and Committees constituted under the Act.
Specifies the procedure for taking cognizance of offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Members of authorities, etc., to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members of authorities and other persons performing duties under the Act as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act.
Designates a nodal agency for the implementation and coordination of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions for the implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not in derogation of any other law
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not affect the operation of any other law that provides for more favourable rights or protections to forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes or other traditional forest dwellers.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Recognition and vesting of forest rights in forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers on forest lands (Section 3 & 4).
Rule 2: Rights include individual or community tenure for habitation, cultivation, collection of minor forest produce, grazing, access to water bodies, and rights in habitat.
Rule 3: Forest rights holders have duties to protect, regenerate, and conserve forest resources (Section 5).
Rule 4: Specific procedures and authorities are established for the recognition and vesting of forest rights (Section 6).
Rule 5: Conditions for modification or resettlement of forest rights in critical wildlife habitats are outlined, requiring stringent safeguards and Gram Sabha consent (Section 4(2)).
Rule 6: Diversion of forest land for certain government-managed facilities is allowed under specific conditions, including Gram Sabha recommendation and limited land area (Section 3(2)).
Rule 7: The Act is not in derogation of any other law providing more favourable rights (Section 13).

penalties: Offences by members or officers of authorities and Committees under this Act are subject to penalties (Section 7).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act is enforced through authorities established for vesting forest rights, Gram Sabhas, State Governments, and the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the recognition and vesting of rights, adherence to procedures for claims, and penal action for offences. The Central Government can issue directions, and rules can be made for implementation.

rights: Right to hold and live in forest land for habitation or self-cultivation.
Community rights such as nistar.
Right of ownership, access to collect, use, and dispose of minor forest produce.
Other community rights such as fishing and grazing.
Rights for primitive tribal groups and pre-agricultural communities.
Rights in or over disputed lands.
Rights for conversion of leases/grants on forest lands to titles.
Rights of settlement and conversion of forest villages into revenue villages.
Right to protect, regenerate, conserve, or manage community forest resources.
Rights recognised under State law or customary law.
Right of access to biodiversity and community right to intellectual property and traditional knowledge.
Right to in situ rehabilitation for illegally evicted persons.
duties: To protect, regenerate, or conserve or manage any community forest resource which they have been traditionally protecting and conserving for sustainable use (Section 3(1)(i)).
obligations: Holders of forest rights are obligated to ensure sustainable use, conservation of biodiversity, and maintenance of ecological balance as per the preamble.
Diversion of forest land for developmental projects requires recommendation from the Gram Sabha (Section 3(2) proviso).

key_procedures: Procedure for recognition and vesting of forest rights by designated authorities (Section 6).
Procedure for modification or resettlement of forest rights in critical wildlife habitats, involving assessment of impact, alternatives, resettlement packages, and Gram Sabha consent (Section 4(2)).
Procedure for seeking diversion of forest land for specified facilities, requiring Gram Sabha recommendation (Section 3(2)).
Procedure for taking cognizance of offences (Section 8).
administration: The Central Government, through the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and Ministry of Environment and Forests, plays a significant role in issuing directions, making rules, and notifying critical wildlife habitats. State Governments and designated authorities are also involved in the administration and implementation of forest rights.
important_notes: The Act came into force on December 31, 2007.
The provisions of this Act were extended to the whole of India, including the omission of the exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir from October 31, 2019.

Forest rights recognized in critical wildlife habitats can be modified or resettled only under stringent conditions to protect wildlife conservation, ensuring no forest rights holder is affected except under specified circumstances.
Diversion of forest land for specified facilities requires Gram Sabha recommendation and the diverted land area must be less than one hectare per case.

title: The Rajiv Gandhi University Act, 2006
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Arunachal Pradesh and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the Rajiv Gandhi University, which is established in the State of Arunachal Pradesh. It covers its establishment, objectives, powers, structure of authorities, and the terms and conditions of its officers and employees.

key_definitions.academic_council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic_staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.affiliated_college: A college admitted to the privileges of the University.
key_definitions.constituent_college: A college maintained by the University.
key_definitions.distance_education_system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more such means.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.university: The Rajiv Gandhi University established and incorporated as a University under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Rajiv Gandhi University Act, 2006, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'Affiliated College', 'Constituent College', 'distance education system', 'employee', and 'University', among others.
Declares the establishment of the Rajiv Gandhi University as a body corporate under this Act, with its headquarters at Itanagar. It also outlines the initial constitution of the University.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of establishment of the University
main_sections.description: Details the legal implications of the establishment of the University under this Act, including the transfer of property, rights, and liabilities, and the continuation of employment for existing staff.

Outlines the primary objectives of the University, which include disseminating knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, promoting integrated courses, fostering innovation, training manpower for Arunachal Pradesh, and contributing to the social and economic welfare of its people.

Enumerate the extensive powers vested in the University, such as providing instruction, granting degrees, organizing extramural studies, conferring honorary degrees, establishing colleges and institutions, appointing staff, and receiving donations.

important_rules: The University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal and shall sue and be sued by its name.
The headquarters of the University shall be at Itanagar.
All property, rights, and liabilities of the former Rajiv Gandhi University shall be transferred to the new University.
Employees of the former University shall continue their service under the new University with similar terms and conditions, unless altered by Statutes.
The University has the power to grant diplomas, certificates, and confer degrees based on examinations or other evaluation methods.
The University can establish and maintain colleges, institutions, and halls, and can also admit to its privileges other colleges and institutions within Arunachal Pradesh.
The University can receive benefactions, donations, and gifts, and manage property with the approval of the Central Government.
The University can borrow money on the security of its property with the approval of the Central Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement through the University's own administrative and disciplinary mechanisms, and potentially by the Central Government through notifications and approvals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of various authorities within the University (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council), the making of Statutes and Ordinances, and the power to regulate and enforce discipline.

rights: Right to provide instruction and research facilities.
Right to grant diplomas, certificates, and confer degrees.
Right to admit students and employees.
Right to hold and manage property.
Right to borrow money.
Employees have rights to their existing tenure, remuneration, and benefits unless duly altered.
duties: Duty to disseminate and advance knowledge.
Duty to provide instructional and research facilities.
Duty to educate and train manpower for the development of Arunachal Pradesh.
Duty to improve the social and economic conditions and welfare of the people of Arunachal Pradesh.
Duty to maintain discipline among students and employees.
Duty to provide for the health and general welfare of students and employees.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Obligation to obtain prior approval of the Central Government for certain actions, such as establishing specialized laboratories or disposing of property.
Obligation to make annual reports and accounts available.

key_procedures: Making of Statutes: Section 29 outlines the power to make Statutes, and Section 30 details how they are to be made.
Making of Ordinances: Section 31 details the power to make Ordinances.
Making of Regulations: Section 32 deals with Regulations.
Procedure for appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students: Section 37.
Procedure for filling casual vacancies: Section 41.
Procedure for handling proceedings of authorities or bodies when vacancies exist: Section 42.
Procedure for removing difficulties: Section 45.
administration: The overall administration of the University falls under its own authorities like the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council, with oversight and certain approval powers vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Arunachal Pradesh Act 1 of 1984.
The Act includes an amendment to Act 24 of 1973.
Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations made under the Act are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
The Act provides for transitional provisions to ensure a smooth transition from the previous Act.
Section 43 provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

title: THE TRIPURA UNIVERSITY ACT, 2006
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Tripura and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of Tripura University within the State of Tripura. Its jurisdiction extends to the whole of the State of Tripura. No educational institution within Tripura can be associated with any other university incorporated by law in India.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.Affiliated College: A college admitted to the privileges of the University.
key_definitions.University: The Tripura University established and incorporated as a University under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'Affiliated College', 'University', and others.

States that the Tripura University, previously established under the Tripura University Act, 1987, shall be established as a body corporate under this Act. It also outlines the composition of the University and its perpetual succession, common seal, and the ability to sue and be sued. The headquarters are to be in Agartala.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of establishment of the University
main_sections.description: Details the consequences of the Act's commencement, including how references to the old Tripura University should be treated, the transfer of property, rights, and liabilities, and the continuation of service for existing employees with provisions for altered terms.

Outlines the objectives of the University, which include disseminating knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, making provisions for integrated courses, promoting studies in tribal life and culture, fostering innovation, educating and training manpower for the development of Tripura, and improving the social and economic conditions of its people.

Enumerates the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting diplomas and degrees, organizing extramural studies, conferring honorary degrees, establishing and maintaining colleges and institutions, appointing staff, collaborating with other institutions, and managing property.
Specifies that the University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of the State of Tripura and prohibits any educational institution within Tripura from associating with any other university.

important_rules: The University is established as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The University's jurisdiction is limited to the entire State of Tripura.
No educational institution within Tripura can be affiliated with any other university in India.
The University has broad powers related to education, research, administration, and property management.
The University must adhere to the objectives outlined in Section 5.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act does not explicitly detail penalties for violations. Enforcement is implied through the powers granted to the University and the general legal framework.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is carried out through the University's own statutes, ordinances, and regulations, as well as by the relevant government authorities overseeing educational institutions.

rights: Employees retain their terms of service and remuneration unless altered by Statutes.
Students have rights to education and welfare as provided by the University.
The University has the right to confer degrees, diplomas, and academic distinctions.
The University has the right to manage its property and finances.
The University has the right to regulate discipline among students and employees.
duties: The University has a duty to disseminate and advance knowledge.
The University has a duty to provide instructional and research facilities.
The University has a duty to promote the social, economic, intellectual, academic, and cultural development of the people of Tripura.
The University has a duty to ensure the health and general welfare of its employees and students.
obligations: The University must comply with the provisions of this Act and any statutes or ordinances made thereunder.
The University must ensure that its jurisdiction is respected by other educational institutions in Tripura.
Employees retained their service conditions unless legally altered.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act upon notification by the Central Government.
Establishment of the University as a body corporate.
Transfer of all assets, rights, and liabilities from the previous Tripura University to the new University.
Continuation of employment for existing staff under specified conditions.
Granting of academic privileges and affiliations to colleges and institutions within Tripura.
administration: The Act establishes the Tripura University, which will be administered by its various authorities including the Visitor, Chief Rector, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Executive Council, and Academic Council. The Central Government has a role in appointing the commencement date and approving certain financial transactions.
important_notes: The headquarters of the University is located at Agartala.
The Act repeals the Tripura Act 11 of 1987, which previously governed the Tripura University.
Provisions for the transfer of employees and their service conditions are detailed.
The Central Government's approval is required for establishing certain research centers and for disposing of property and borrowing money.

title: THE SIKKIM UNIVERSITY ACT, 2006
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Sikkim and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The jurisdiction of the University extends to the whole of the State of Sikkim. It applies to educational institutions within Sikkim and aims to provide higher education and research facilities.

key_definitions.University: The Sikkim University established and incorporated as a University under this Act.
key_definitions.academic_staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.affiliated_college: A college admitted to the privileges of the University.
key_definitions.statutes: The Statutes of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.ordinances: The Ordinances of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.teachers_of_the_university: Professors, Readers, Lecturers and such other persons as may be appointed for imparting instruction or conducting research in the University or in any College or Institution maintained by the University and are designated as teachers by the Ordinances.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'University', 'academic staff', 'affiliated college', 'Statutes', 'Ordinances', and 'teachers of the University'.
Establishes the Sikkim University, specifies its headquarters at Gangtok, and constitutes it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objects of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, promoting innovations, educating and training manpower for Sikkim's development, and improving the social, economic, and intellectual welfare of its people.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting diplomas and degrees, organizing extramural studies, conferring honorary degrees, establishing colleges and institutions, recognizing other institutions, appointing staff, collaborating with other bodies, and managing finances and property.

Specifies that the University's jurisdiction extends to the entire State of Sikkim and prevents educational institutions within Sikkim from associating with other Indian Universities without Central Government approval.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Mandates that the University is open to all irrespective of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, and prohibits any religious tests for admission or employment. It allows for special provisions for women, persons with disabilities, and weaker sections.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and outlines the Visitor's powers to review university work, conduct inspections and inquiries, and issue directives for improvement.

important_rules: The University shall be open to all persons irrespective of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, without imposing religious tests.
The University is empowered to establish and maintain Colleges, Institutions, and Halls.
The University shall have the power to confer honorary degrees or other distinctions.
The University shall have the power to provide facilities through the distance education system.
The University shall be bound to comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
No educational institution within Sikkim shall be associated with any other University in India without Central Government direction.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University itself and the Visitor (President of India) have enforcement roles.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the University's authorities and through directives from the Visitor following inspections and inquiries.

rights: Right to provide instruction and research facilities.
Right to grant diplomas, certificates, and degrees.
Right to confer honorary degrees.
Right to admit students and appoint employees.
Right to withdraw privileges from affiliated colleges.
Right to manage its own property and finances.
Right to appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
Right to appeal.
duties: Duty to disseminate and advance knowledge.
Duty to educate and train manpower for Sikkim's development.
Duty to improve the social and economic conditions of the people of Sikkim.
Duty to be open to all classes, castes, and creeds without discrimination.
Duty to comply with Visitor's directions.
Duty to make provision for integrated courses in various disciplines.
obligations: The University shall be bound to comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
Educational institutions in Sikkim shall not be associated with other Universities in India without specific orders from the Central Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for making Statutes (Section 29): Statutes are made by the Court based on proposals from the Executive Council, with final approval from the Visitor. They must be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
