Procedure for making Ordinances (Section 30): Ordinances are made by the Executive Council subject to the provisions of the Statutes and the Act.
Procedure for making Regulations (Section 31): Regulations are made by the Academic Council subject to the Statutes and Ordinances.

Procedure for Visitor's Inspection/Inquiry (Section 8(2) & 8(3)): The Visitor can appoint persons to review work and progress or conduct inspections/inquiries. The University or concerned management must be given notice and the right to make representations. The University is bound to comply with the Visitor's directions.
administration: The administration of the University is carried out through its various Officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, etc.) and Authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, etc.). The Central Government oversees certain aspects, particularly regarding property disposal and borrowing, and the Visitor has overarching inspection and directive powers.
important_notes: The Act specifies a commencement date to be notified by the Central Government (Section 1(2)). The footnote indicates this was July 2, 2007.

The Act provides for the establishment of a University open to all, but allows for special provisions for employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, and weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 7 proviso).
The Act outlines transitional provisions to ensure a smooth transition (Section 46).

title: THE INDIRA GANDHI NATIONAL TRIBAL UNIVERSITY ACT, 2007
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University at Amarkantak in the State of Madhya Pradesh to facilitate and promote avenues of higher education and research facilities for the tribal population in India and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Geographical scope extends to the whole of India. Subject matter scope includes higher education, research facilities, tribal art, culture, tradition, language, medicinal systems, customs, forest-based economic activities, flora, fauna, advancement in technologies related to natural resources of tribal areas, and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.University: The Indira Gandhi National Tribal University as incorporated under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheduled Population: Scheduled Tribes as well as Scheduled Castes, as defined in the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.Tribal areas: Areas that are predominantly inhabited by tribal populations, as prescribed in the Statutes.
key_definitions.Distance education system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, webcasting, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or a combination of any two or more such means.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'University', 'Scheduled Population', 'Academic Board', 'Academic Council', 'employee', 'Statutes', and 'Ordinances'.

Establishes the Indira Gandhi National Tribal University in Madhya Pradesh with its headquarters at Amarkantak. It also outlines the body corporate nature of the University and its perpetual succession.

Outlines the primary objectives of the University, focusing on providing higher education and research for the tribal population, advancing knowledge in tribal-specific areas, collaborating with national and international organizations, formulating tribal-centric development models, and promoting the social, educational, and economic welfare of Scheduled Tribes.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, conferring honorary degrees, establishing regional centers and campuses, creating posts, entering into collaborations, establishing and maintaining colleges, and making special provisions for the promotion of the welfare of Scheduled Tribes.
States that the jurisdiction of the University extends to the whole of India.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all individuals regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class.

important_rules: The University must be open to all classes, castes, and creeds, without imposing any tests.
The University shall provide instruction and research facilities primarily for the tribal population of India.
The University has the power to establish and maintain regional centers and campuses in tribal areas.

The University has the power to make special provisions for the promotion of educational, economic interests, and welfare of members belonging to Scheduled Tribes, including reservation in admission and employment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the University authorities are responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of the University, its governance structure, and the powers vested in its authorities to make Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.

rights: Right to access higher education and research facilities for the tribal population.
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases against students.
Right to sue and be sued by the University's name.
duties: The University has a duty to promote the intellectual, academic, and cultural development of Scheduled Tribes.
The University has a duty to provide adequate percentage of seats in admissions and posts in employment to members of Scheduled Tribes.
The University has a duty to make provisions for the health and general welfare of its students and employees.
obligations: Obligation to disseminate and advance knowledge in tribal art, culture, tradition, language, medicinal systems, etc.
Obligation to collaborate with national and international organizations for cultural studies and research on tribal populations.
Obligation to formulate tribal-centric development models and provide policy inputs.

key_procedures: Establishment of the University with specific headquarters and regional centers.
Formation of University authorities such as the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.
Making of Statutes and Ordinances to govern the University's functioning.
Procedure for the appointment of officers like the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, etc.
Procedure for granting degrees, diplomas, and certificates.
Procedure for admission to the University, which may include examinations, evaluation, or other testing methods.
administration: The Indira Gandhi National Tribal University
important_notes: The University shall be open to persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class.
The Act provides for the establishment of Regional Centres in more tribal dominated areas, as prescribed in the Statutes.
The University can withdraw diplomas, certificates, degrees, or academic distinctions for good and sufficient cause.
Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.

title: THE MAINTENANCE AND WELFARE OF PARENTS AND SENIOR CITIZENS ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for more effective provisions for the maintenance and welfare of parents and senior citizens guaranteed and recognised under the Constitution and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies also to citizens of India outside India. It primarily concerns the maintenance, welfare, medical care, and protection of life and property of parents and senior citizens.

key_definitions.children: Includes son, daughter, grandson and grand-daughter but does not include a minor.
key_definitions.maintenance: Includes provision for food, clothing, residence and medical attendance and treatment.
key_definitions.minor: A person who is deemed not to have attained the age of majority under the Majority Act, 1875.
key_definitions.parent: Father or mother, whether biological, adoptive or step-father or step-mother, irrespective of whether they are senior citizens.
key_definitions.property: Property of any kind, whether movable or immovable, ancestral or self-acquired, tangible or intangible, including rights or interests in such property.
key_definitions.relative: Any legal heir of a childless senior citizen who is not a minor and is in possession of or would inherit their property after their death.
key_definitions.senior citizen: Any citizen of India who has attained the age of sixty years or above.
key_definitions.welfare: Provision for food, health care, recreation centres and other amenities necessary for senior citizens.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: This section names the Act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India, including citizens abroad), and outlines how it comes into force in a State.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'children', 'maintenance', 'parent', 'senior citizen', and 'welfare'.
This section states that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any other enactment or instrument that is inconsistent with it.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance of parents and senior citizens
main_sections.description: This section establishes the right of a senior citizen or parent, unable to maintain themselves, to seek maintenance from their children or specified relatives, outlining the extent of this obligation.
This section details how an application for maintenance can be made, who can make it, the possibility of interim maintenance orders, and the procedure for disposal of applications.
This section defines the jurisdiction for proceedings under Section 5 and outlines the procedural powers of the Tribunal, including summoning, evidence, and the role of a Conciliation Officer.
This section provides for the constitution of Maintenance Tribunals by the State Government and specifies the rank of the presiding officer.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of property to be void in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: This section addresses the protection of property of senior citizens by making certain transfers of property void.

main_sections.section_title: Exposure and abandonment of senior citizen
main_sections.description: This section deals with the offense of exposing and abandoning a senior citizen.

important_rules: Children or specified relatives have a legal obligation to maintain parents and senior citizens who are unable to maintain themselves, ensuring they can lead a normal life.
Maintenance includes provision for food, clothing, residence, and medical attendance and treatment.
Applications for maintenance must be disposed of within ninety days, with a possible extension of thirty days in exceptional circumstances.
The maximum maintenance allowance that can be ordered shall not exceed ten thousand rupees per month.
A senior citizen's property transfer that is intended to defeat maintenance claims may be declared void.
Exposure and abandonment of a senior citizen is an offense punishable under the Act.

penalties: Failure to comply with a maintenance order can lead to a warrant for levying the due amount, and imprisonment for up to one month or until payment is made.
Exposure and abandonment of a senior citizen is an offense (Section 24).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Maintenance Tribunals, constituted by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through summary procedures, issuance of warrants for levying amounts, and potentially imprisonment. The Act also allows for the enforcement of maintenance orders in any place where the person against whom it is made resides.

rights: Right to maintenance and welfare for parents and senior citizens.
Right to apply for maintenance if unable to maintain oneself.
Right to legal representation before the Tribunal (Section 17).
Right to appeal against orders of the Maintenance Tribunal.
Right to protection of life and property.
duties: Duty of children or relatives to provide maintenance to parents and senior citizens.
Duty to ensure senior citizens receive medical support.
Duty of the State Government to establish and maintain old age homes and take measures for publicity and awareness for the welfare of senior citizens.
obligations: Children's obligation to maintain their parents and senior citizens extends to meeting their needs for a normal life.
Relatives in possession of or inheriting property of a childless senior citizen have an obligation to maintain them.

key_procedures: Application for maintenance can be made by the senior citizen/parent, an authorized person, or suo motu by the Tribunal.
Upon receiving an application, the Tribunal issues a process to the respondent, hears both parties, and holds an inquiry.
The Tribunal may order interim maintenance during the pendency of proceedings.
Applications are to be disposed of within ninety days.
Evidence is taken in the presence of the respondent, with provisions for ex parte proceedings if the respondent willfully avoids service.
Referral to a Conciliation Officer for amicable settlement is possible.
Appeals against orders of the Maintenance Tribunal lie with the Appellate Tribunal.
administration: State Governments are responsible for constituting Tribunals, establishing old age homes, and making rules. The Central Government has powers to give directions and review the Act.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on other inconsistent laws.
The State Government is empowered to make rules for the implementation of the Act.
Specific provisions exist for the establishment of old age homes and for medical support for senior citizens.
Transfer of property by senior citizens to defeat maintenance claims can be deemed void.
The Act provides for the offence of exposure and abandonment of senior citizens.

title: The Indian Maritime University Act, 2008
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University at the national level to facilitate and promote maritime studies and research and to achieve excellence in areas of marine science and technology, marine environment and other related fields, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Indian Maritime University, which is a national-level university. Its jurisdiction extends to maritime studies, research, and related fields across India and potentially offshore campuses. It covers students, academic staff, employees, and institutions related to maritime education.

key_definitions.University: The Indian Maritime University established under this Act.
key_definitions.Maritime Studies: Implied through objects and powers, encompassing oceanography, maritime history, maritime laws, maritime security, search and rescue, transportation of dangerous cargo, environmental studies, and other related fields.
key_definitions.Certificate of Competency: A certificate issued by the competent authority under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958.
key_definitions.Director-General: The Director-General of Shipping appointed by the Government of India under section 7 of the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, academic staff, Campus, Certificate of Competency, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, College, Court, Department, Director-General, Distance Education System, Employee, Executive Council, Finance Committee, Governing Body, Hall, Institution, Notification, Off-shore Campus, Planning Board, Principal, Recognised Institution, Recognised teachers, School, Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations, University, teachers of the University, and University Grants Commission.

Establishes the Indian Maritime University, defines its headquarters and campuses, constitutes the initial University body, and declares its perpetual succession, common seal, and capacity to sue and be sued. It also specifies that the University will be both a teaching and an affiliating University.

Outlines the primary objectives of the University, including promoting maritime studies, training, research, and extension work in emerging areas, achieving excellence in marine science and technology, providing advanced knowledge and research facilities, promoting innovations, promoting educational and economic interests of India, and fostering national development values.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, establishing and maintaining campuses, colleges, departments, libraries, laboratories, etc., granting diplomas and degrees (excluding Certificates of Competency for seafarers), organizing extra-mural studies, instituting teaching positions, appointing staff, recognizing institutions, coordinating work, setting up central facilities, and prescribing fees.

important_rules: The University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal and shall sue and be sued by its name.
The University shall be both a teaching and an affiliating University.
Certificates of Competency for seafarers shall continue to be issued by the Director-General of Shipping until the Central Government decides otherwise.
Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations made under this Act are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
administration: The Central Government plays a role in appointing the commencement date and potentially deciding on the issuance of Certificates of Competency. The Director-General of Shipping is also a key figure in maritime education and certification.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act was notified on 14th November, 2008.
Substitutions and amendments may occur as indicated by the footnotes, e.g., by Act 19 of 2015.

title: THE SOUTH ASIAN UNIVERSITY ACT, 2008
purpose: To give effect to the Agreement for the establishment of South Asian University and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The Act establishes the South Asian University with its main campus located in India as per the SAARC agreement.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and to campuses and centres established outside India in the SAARC region. The University is open to all persons irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, ethnicity or socio-economic background.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Statutes.
key_definitions.Agreement: The Agreement for the establishment of the South Asian University.
key_definitions.University: The South Asian University incorporated under section 4.
key_definitions.Member States: The Member States of the SAARC.
key_definitions.SAARC region: The region comprising the territories of the Member States.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India and SAARC region campuses outside India), and the commencement date which is to be notified by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'Agreement', 'University', 'Member States', 'SAARC region', 'President', 'Governing Board', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of Agreement to have force of law
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding any other law, the provisions of the Agreement set out in the Schedule shall have the force of law in India.

Provides for the establishment of the South Asian University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It states its headquarters will be in Delhi and allows for campuses and centres in other places within India and the SAARC region.
Defines the jurisdiction of the University to extend to the whole of India and to campuses and centres established outside India in the SAARC region, subject to the Agreement and local laws.

Establishes a Governing Board for the University consisting of members from each SAARC Member State and the President. It outlines the interim arrangement, leadership, selection of members, and responsibilities of the Governing Board.

Details the objectives of the University, including disseminating knowledge, promoting innovation, providing higher education, fostering civic sense, building a South Asian community of learning, and harmonizing academic standards.

Enumerate the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, establishing centres, planning courses, granting degrees, conferring honorary degrees, organizing open learning, instituting academic positions, creating administrative posts, laying down service conditions, establishing campuses, collaborating with other institutions, determining admission standards, receiving fees, managing property, borrowing money, and entering into agreements.

Ensures that the University is open to all persons irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, ethnicity or socio-economic background, prohibiting any tests of religious belief for admission, appointment, or privilege.
Designates the Foreign Minister of the current Chair of SAARC as the Visitor of the University and states that the Visitor shall have powers as prescribed by Statutes.
Establishes the position of a President of the University and other officers, whose appointment and functions will be prescribed.

important_rules: The provisions of the Agreement for the establishment of the South Asian University, as set out in the Schedule, have the force of law in India.
The University shall be open to all persons irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, ethnicity or socio-economic background.
No person shall be subjected to any test of religious belief or profession to be appointed as a teacher, hold office, be admitted as a student, graduate, or enjoy any privilege of the University.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act does not explicitly detail penalties for violations or an enforcement authority in the provided text, beyond the general powers of the University for regulation and discipline.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act provides the University with powers to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees, and to take disciplinary measures.

rights: Right to education without discrimination based on gender, caste, creed, disability, ethnicity or socio-economic background.
Right to access all privileges of the University without religious tests.
duties: Duty to disseminate and advance knowledge, wisdom, and understanding.
Duty to promote innovations in teaching-learning process and application of knowledge for social advancement and regional peace.
Duty to impart liberal and humane education for capacity building of South Asian nations.
Duty to foster sound civic sense and train students to become useful citizens.
Duty to build a South Asian community of learning and strengthen regional consciousness.
Duty to harmonize academic standards and accreditation norms acceptable to all Member States.
obligations: Obligation to implement the provisions of the Agreement for the establishment of the South Asian University.
Obligation to operate within the framework of its jurisdiction and subject to SAARC agreements and member state laws where campuses are located outside India.

key_procedures: Appointment of University officers, including the President, as prescribed.
Formation of the Governing Board, including selection of members and election of a Chairperson.
Establishment of various academic and administrative authorities as per the Statutes.
Processes for planning courses of study, granting degrees/diplomas, and conferring academic distinctions.
Procedures for the creation and appointment to administrative and other posts.
Regulation and enforcement of discipline among students and employees.
Receiving benefactions, donations, and gifts, and managing University property.
Borrowing money on the security of University property.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for appointing the commencement date of the Act. The Governing Board is responsible for the policies, directions, and management of the University's affairs. The President is an officer of the University. The Foreign Minister of the current Chair of SAARC is the Visitor.
important_notes: The Act is based on an Agreement signed by SAARC Member States, and its provisions have the force of law in India.
The main campus of the University is located in India as per the Agreement.
The jurisdiction extends to campuses and centres outside India in the SAARC region, subject to those countries' laws.

title: The Land Ports Authority of India Act, 2010
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the Land Ports Authority of India to put in place systems that address security imperatives, and for the development and management of facilities for cross-border movement of passengers and goods at designated points along India's international borders.
scope: The Act applies to designated points along the international borders of India where cross-border movement of passengers and goods occurs. It covers the development, management, and provision of facilities at integrated check posts, including aspects related to security, customs, immigration, and other ancillary services.

key_definitions.Authority: The Land Ports Authority of India constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Authority appointed under clause (a) of sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.immigration check post: Any port or place of departure on the land as notified under the Foreigners' Act, 1946.
key_definitions.integrated check post: Any land port, as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify.
key_definitions.land customs station: Any place notified as such by the Central Government under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Customs Act, 1962, for the clearance of goods imported or to be exported by land or inland water.
key_definitions.land port: An area on the international borders of India including portions of national highways, State highways and other roads, notified as land customs station or immigration check post under the Customs Act, 1962 or the Foreigners' Act, 1946, and includes railways, with facilities for clearance and transport of passengers and goods across the borders of India.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Authority under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette, allowing for different dates for different provisions.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Authority', 'Chairperson', 'integrated check post', 'land port', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'regulations'.

Establishes the Land Ports Authority of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It details the composition of the Authority, including the Chairperson, whole-time members, ex-officio members representing various government ministries, state government representatives, and other co-opted representatives.

Outlines the primary functions of the Authority, which include developing, sanitizing, and managing facilities for cross-border movement of passengers and goods. It lists specific powers such as implementing security systems, constructing and maintaining infrastructure, procuring equipment, providing various services (immigration, customs, banking, etc.), and establishing hotels and warehouses. It also allows the Authority to form companies and undertake operations abroad.
Mandates the Authority to maintain proper accounts and conduct audits, although specific details are likely to be prescribed by rules.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede Authority
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to supersede the Authority in certain circumstances, likely due to persistent default or mismanagement.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Authority to make regulations for carrying out its functions.

important_rules: The Authority shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract.

The Authority shall consist of a Chairperson, two whole-time Members (Planning & Development and Finance), ex-officio members from relevant government ministries, state government representatives, and worker/trader representatives.
Members of the Authority are subject to disqualifications, including conviction for offenses involving moral turpitude, insolvency, unsound mind, or prejudicial financial interests.
Whole-time members hold office for five years or until they attain the age of sixty, whichever is earlier, and their appointment can be terminated under specific conditions.

The Authority's functions include developing, sanitizing, and managing facilities at integrated check posts, including security systems, infrastructure, equipment, and various services for passengers and goods.
Sovereign functions of the Authority cannot be assigned to any private entity.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Authority and to supersede it in case of persistent default.
The Central Government can make rules, and the Authority can make regulations, for the effective implementation of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Land Ports Authority of India and the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers granted to the Authority for development and management of land ports, through rules and regulations made under the Act, and through the Central Government's oversight powers, including directions and supersession of the Authority.

rights: The right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The right to contract and sue and be sued.
The right to develop, manage, and provide services at integrated check posts.
The right to form companies for efficient discharge of functions.
The right to undertake operations in India and abroad in relation to integrated check posts.
duties: To develop, sanitize, and manage facilities for cross-border movement of passengers and goods.
To put in place systems that address security imperatives at integrated check posts.
To ensure prevention and control of fire and other hazards.
To co-ordinate and facilitate the working of agencies at integrated check posts.
To discharge functions with due regard to efficiency, economy, and safety.
To comply with laws for the time being in force.
obligations: To maintain proper accounts and undergo audit.
To submit annual reports to the Central Government.
To ensure that sovereign functions are not assigned to private entities.

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairperson and Members: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson and Members of the Authority.
Conduct of Meetings: The Authority meets at specified times and places with rules of procedure for transacting business, including quorum and voting procedures.
Making Rules and Regulations: The Central Government makes rules, and the Authority makes regulations, which are subject to laying before Parliament.
Supervision and Direction by Central Government: The Central Government can issue directions to the Authority and, in case of default, can supersede the Authority.
administration: The Land Ports Authority of India, under the overall supervision and direction of the Central Government.
important_notes: Different commencement dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
Sovereign functions of the Authority cannot be assigned to any private entity.
Rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

title: The Nalanda University Act, 2010
purpose: To establish the Nalanda University in the State of Bihar as an international institution for the pursuit of intellectual, philosophical, historical, and spiritual studies, implementing decisions from the Second and Fourth East Asia Summits for regional educational cooperation and revival of Nalanda University.
scope: The Act applies to the Nalanda University, established in the State of Bihar. Its jurisdiction extends to the whole of India and to centers established within or outside India. It also concerns Member States of the East Asia Summit.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Staff designated as academic staff by the Statutes.
key_definitions.Centre: A center established or maintained by the University in India or the East Asia region for coordinating and supervising work and performing functions assigned by the Governing Board.
key_definitions.East Asia region: The region comprising the territories of the Member States of the East Asia Summit.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University, including teachers and other staff.
key_definitions.Finance Officer: The Finance Officer of the University appointed under section 17.
key_definitions.Governing Board: The Governing Board of the University constituted under section 7.
key_definitions.Hall: A unit of residence for students, provided, maintained, or recognized by the University.
key_definitions.Member States: The Member States of the East Asia Summit.
key_definitions.Nalanda Mentor Group: A group constituted by the Government of India to examine the framework and structure of international cooperation for establishing the University.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by Statutes, Ordinances, or Regulations.
key_definitions.recognised institution: An institution of higher learning maintained or recognized by, or associated with, the University.
key_definitions.Registrar: The Registrar of the University appointed under section 16.
key_definitions.School: A school of studies of the University.
key_definitions.teacher: Professor, associate professor, assistant professor, and research staff appointed or recognized by the University for instruction, research, or student guidance.
key_definitions.University: The Nalanda University established and incorporated under section 4.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Nalanda University Act, 2010 and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Nalanda University as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares Nalanda University as an institution of national importance.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, academic staff, Centre, East Asia region, employee, Faculty, Finance Officer, Governing Board, Hall, Member States, Nalanda Mentor Group, Ordinances, prescribed, recognised institution, Registrar, Regulations, School, Statutes, teacher, and University.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Nalanda University
main_sections.description: Establishes the University of Nalanda, previously under a Bihar Act, as a body corporate named 'Nalanda University'. It outlines the composition of the University, its perpetual succession, common seal, and establishes its headquarters in Nalanda, Bihar. It also allows for the establishment of centers in India and study centers outside India.

Details the consequences of the Act's commencement, including how references to the previous University of Nalanda will be treated, the vesting of property, transfer of rights and liabilities, continuation of employment for existing staff, and the continuation of appointed Visitor, Chancellor, and Vice-Chancellor.
Specifies that the University's jurisdiction extends throughout India and to centers established within or outside India.

Establishes the Governing Board of the University, outlining its composition including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, members from Member States, representatives from the Ministry of External Affairs and Human Resource Development, representatives from the State Government of Bihar, and renowned academicians. It also specifies the term of office for members and the Chairperson and Member-Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Governing Board
main_sections.description: States that the Governing Board is responsible for all policies, directions, and management of the University. It also mentions that the Nalanda Mentor Group will exercise the powers of the Governing Board for a specified period until the nominated members are in place.

Outlines the objectives of the University, including capacity building in ancient science, philosophy, language, and history for Member States, promoting regional peace, harmonizing academic standards, creating partnerships, understanding Buddha's teachings in a contemporary context, enhancing research and interaction between Asian countries, fostering accommodation and understanding among students, and improving educational systems of Member States.

important_rules: Section 1(2): The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette, with different dates possible for different provisions.
Section 4(4): The Headquarters of the University shall be in the district of Nalanda in the State of Bihar.
Section 4(5): The University may establish or maintain centers at other places in India and, with Governing Board approval, study centers outside India.

Section 7(1): The Governing Board shall consist of the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, nominated members from Member States, representatives from relevant Ministries, and representatives from the State Government of Bihar.
Section 7(2): Members of the Governing Board (excluding Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor) hold office for a fixed term of three years.
Section 8(1): The Governing Board is responsible for all policies and directions of the University and management of its affairs.

Section 9(1): The University's objectives include imparting education and research for capacity building in ancient science, philosophy, language, and history; promoting regional peace; harmonizing academic standards; creating partnerships; understanding spiritual teachings; enhancing Asian interaction; fostering exemplary citizens; and improving Member States' educational systems.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the University's governing bodies (Governing Board, Visitor, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor) are responsible for enforcement through their respective powers and functions as defined in the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the application of the Act's provisions, including the powers and functions of its various bodies, the making of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations, and the declaration of the University as an institution of national importance. Specific enforcement mechanisms are not detailed in the provided text but would be governed by the rules and regulations established under the Act.

rights: Right to hold office or service in the University under the same tenure, remuneration, and terms and conditions as before the Act, unless altered by Statutes, with provisions for termination and compensation if alterations are not acceptable (Section 5(d)).
Right to appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students (Section 34).
duties: Duty to impart education and enable research (Section 9(a)).
Duty to contribute to the promotion of regional peace and vision (Section 9(b)).
Duty to harmonize academic standards and accreditation norms (Section 9(c)).
Duty to create a unique partnership between scholars and interested persons (Section 9(d)).
Duty to understand Buddha's teachings in the contemporary context (Section 9(e)).
Duty to enhance research for greater interaction between Asian countries (Section 9(f)).
Duty to foster the spirit of accommodation and understanding in students and scholars (Section 9(g)).
Duty to contribute to the improvement of the educational system of Member States (Section 9(h)).
obligations: Obligation for the University to have perpetual succession and a common seal (Section 4(3)).
Obligation for the University to sue and be sued by its corporate name (Section 4(3)).
Obligation to ensure the University is open to all persons (Section 11).

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).
Nomination of Governing Board members: Members from Member States, Ministries, and academicians are to be nominated as per the provisions of Section 7.

Regulation of Governing Board procedure: The Governing Board may regulate its own procedure, including quorum, for the conduct of its meetings, subject to the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances (Section 7(5)).
Making of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations: These are prescribed by the Act and are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament (Section 42).
administration: The Central Government is involved in appointing the commencement date, nominating members to the Governing Board, and overseeing the establishment and functioning of the University. The Nalanda University itself, through its Governing Board, Visitor, Chancellor, and Vice-Chancellor, administers its affairs.
important_notes: The Nalanda Mentor Group exercised powers of the Governing Board for a period of one year or until members are nominated, whichever is earlier (Section 8(2)).
Any reference to the University of Nalanda in any contract or instrument shall be deemed a reference to Nalanda University (Section 5(a)).
All property, rights, and liabilities of the University of Nalanda shall be transferred to Nalanda University (Section 5(b), 5(c)).
Employees of the University of Nalanda continue their service under Nalanda University with existing terms and conditions, subject to potential alterations (Section 5(d)).
The Visitor, Chancellor, and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Nalanda are deemed to have been appointed under the Nalanda University Act, 2010 for specified durations (Section 5(e), 5(f), 5(g)).
Colleges, Institutions, Faculties, and Departments affiliated with the University of Nalanda stand affiliated with Nalanda University (Section 5(h)).
The Nalanda University Act, 2010, repeals the University of Nalanda Act (Bihar Act 18 of 2007) (Section 44).

title: THE COINAGE ACT, 2011
purpose: To consolidate the laws relating to coinage and the Mints, the protection of coinage and to provide for the prohibition of melting or destruction of coins and prohibit the making or the possession thereof for issue and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to all coins, denominations, dimensions, designs, and composition of coins, as well as the establishment and abolition of Mints. It also covers offences and penalties related to coins and pieces of metal intended for use as money.

key_definitions.coin: Any coin made of any metal or other material stamped by the Government or an empowered authority, which is a legal tender, including commemorative coins and Government of India one rupee notes. It explicitly excludes credit cards, debit cards, postal orders, and e-money.
key_definitions.commemorative_coin: Any coin stamped by the Government or an empowered authority to commemorate a specific occasion or event and expressed in Indian currency.
key_definitions.deface: Any clipping, filing, stamping, or other alteration of the surface or shape of a coin that is readily distinguishable from the effects of reasonable wear.
key_definitions.issue: To put a coin into circulation for use as money.
key_definitions.metal: Any metal, base metal, alloy, gold, silver, or any other material that may be prescribed by the Government for the purpose of any coin.
key_definitions.Mint: The Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Limited or any other organization established by or under the authority of the Government to make a coin by stamping metal.
key_definitions.remedy: Variation from the standard weight and fineness.
key_definitions.standard_weight: The weight prescribed for any coin.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title as the Coinage Act, 2011, its extent to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'coin', 'commemorative coin', 'deface', 'Government', 'issue', 'metal', 'Mint', 'notification', 'per cent.', 'prescribed', 'remedy', and 'standard weight'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to establish and abolish Mints.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to establish and abolish Mints, and to authorize the minting of coins by foreign organizations or governments. Existing Mints are deemed to have been established under this section.

main_sections.section_title: Denominations, dimensions, designs and composition of coins.
main_sections.description: Details that coins can be minted at Mints or authorized places with denominations not higher than one thousand rupees, and of specified dimensions, designs, and metal composition as prescribed by the Government.
States that the standard weight of a coin and the allowed remedy (variation from standard weight and fineness) shall be as prescribed by the Government.

Defines the conditions under which coins are legal tender for various sums, depending on their denomination, and also continues the legal tender status of older naya paisa series coins under specific conditions.

Establishes the decimal system where the rupee is divided into one hundred units. It also provides for the conversion of references to older currency units (annas, paisa, pies, naya paisa) to the new unit system.
Grants the Government the power to withdraw any coin from circulation by notification, after which it ceases to be legal tender except to the extent specified.

main_sections.section_title: Power to certain persons to cut, diminished or defaced coins.
main_sections.description: Authorizes certain persons to cut or break diminished or defaced coins. It specifies how to handle such coins based on whether the defacement is fraudulent or not.

main_sections.section_title: Power to certain persons to cut counterfeit coins.
main_sections.description: Empowers authorized persons to cut or break counterfeit coins that are tendered, with the tenderer bearing the loss.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Mint to delegate its functions.
main_sections.description: Allows a Mint to delegate its functions, such as melting withdrawn coins, to other government organizations or public sector undertakings.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of making or melting or destruction of coins.
main_sections.description: Prohibits using metal pieces as coins without government authority, melting or destroying coins, using coins other than as a medium of exchange, and possessing melted, destroyed, or mutilated coins beyond reasonable requirements for disposal other than as a medium of exchange. It also creates a presumption of contravention for possessing metal with the same alloy proportions as coins.
Prescribes a penalty of imprisonment up to seven years and a fine for contravening Section 12.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition and penalty for unlawful making, issue or possession of pieces of metal to be used as money.
main_sections.description: Prohibits making, issuing, or possessing metal pieces with the intent to use them as money, other than as authorized for coins. Penalties include imprisonment up to one year or fine, with increased penalties for repeat offenders.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition and penalty for bringing metal piece for use as coin.
main_sections.description: Prohibits bringing any piece of metal into India for use as coin without government authority. Penalties include imprisonment up to seven years and a fine.

Makes every person in charge of a company responsible for offences committed by the company. It also holds directors, managers, or other officers liable if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or due to their neglect.
Deals with forfeiture related to offences under the Act (details not fully provided in the excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 not to apply to offences under this Act.
main_sections.description: Excludes the application of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, to offences committed under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable, bailable and non-compoundable.
main_sections.description: Classifies offences under this Act as cognizable, bailable, and non-compoundable.
Indicates an amendment to Act 2 of 1934 (likely the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934) in relation to this Act (details not fully provided in the excerpt).
Allows for offences under this Act to be tried summarily.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to remove difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be laid before Parliament.
main_sections.description: Requires rules made under the Act to be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of making other coins at Mints.
main_sections.description: Saves the provision for making other coins at Mints as per government authority, which might not be covered by the general provisions of this Act.
Deals with the repeal of existing laws and savings to ensure continuity and prevent unintended consequences.
Ensures that coins existing at the commencement of the Act continue to be valid, subject to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall melt or destroy any coin (Section 12(1)(ii)).
No person shall use coin other than as a medium of exchange (Section 12(1)(iii)).
No person shall possess melted or destroyed coins substantially in excess of reasonable requirements for purposes other than as a medium of exchange (Section 12(1)(iv)).
No person shall make or issue any metal piece for use as coin except by government authority (Section 14(1)(a)).
No person shall bring any piece of metal into India to be used as coin without government authority (Section 15(1)).
Diminished or defaced coins can be cut or broken by authorized persons, with specific procedures for fraudulent defacement (Section 9).
Counterfeit coins can be cut or broken by authorized persons, with the tenderer bearing the loss (Section 10).

penalties: Contravention of Section 12 (prohibitions on melting, destruction, etc.): Imprisonment up to seven years and fine.

Contravention of Section 14 (unlawful making, issue, or possession of metal pieces for money): Imprisonment up to one year or fine, or both. Repeat offenders face imprisonment up to three years or fine, or both.
Contravention of Section 15 (bringing metal pieces for use as coin into India): Imprisonment up to seven years and fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, authorized persons for cutting coins, and potentially police and judicial authorities for enforcing penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution for offences, seizure of prohibited items, and application of penalties as prescribed in the Act. Offences are cognizable, bailable, and non-compoundable, and can be tried summarily.

rights: Right to use legal tender coins as a medium of exchange within the limits specified in Section 6.
Right to receive face value for a coin cut due to diminution in weight if not fraudulently diminished (Section 9(2)).
Right to receive face value for a coin cut due to non-fraudulent defacement (Section 9(3)(b)).
duties: Duty to not melt or destroy coins (Section 12(1)(ii)).
Duty to use coins only as a medium of exchange (Section 12(1)(iii)).
Duty to not possess excessive amounts of melted or destroyed coins (Section 12(1)(iv)).
Duty to not unlawfully make, issue, or possess metal pieces for use as money (Section 14(1)).
Duty to not bring unauthorized metal pieces for use as coin into India (Section 15(1)).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the prescribed denominations, dimensions, designs, and composition of coins (Section 4).
Obligation to adhere to standard weight and remedy for coins (Section 5).
Obligation for companies to ensure their officers and employees comply with the Act, with provisions for individual liability (Section 16).
Obligation for tenderers of diminished or defaced coins to bear loss if fraudulently diminished or defaced (Section 9(2), 9(3)(a)).
Obligation for tenderers of counterfeit coins to bear the loss (Section 10).

key_procedures: Procedure for establishing and abolishing Mints (Section 3).
Procedure for minting coins with specified denominations, dimensions, designs, and composition (Section 4).
Procedure for a coin to be considered legal tender, including conditions on weight and defacement (Section 6).
Procedure for authorized persons to cut or break diminished, defaced, or counterfeit coins, including provisions for payment or loss bearing (Sections 9 and 10).
Procedure for the Government to call in any coin, ceasing its legal tender status (Section 8).
Procedure for companies to be held liable for offences committed by them (Section 16).
administration: The Central Government, through relevant departments and empowered authorities, including Mints and other authorized organizations.
important_notes: The Act consolidates and modernizes coinage laws in India.
It explicitly excludes credit cards, debit cards, postal orders, and e-money from the definition of 'coin'.
The Act establishes a clear framework for the prohibition and penalty of activities detrimental to the coinage system, such as melting, destruction, and counterfeiting.
Provisions for companies committing offences ensure accountability at the corporate level.

title: The Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development Act, 2012
purpose: To declare the institution known as the Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development, an institution of national importance. Its headquarters are in the district of Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu, and it may establish centers at other places in India. The Act governs its incorporation, functioning, authorities, officers, finance, accounts, and miscellaneous provisions.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the Institute.
key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed for the coming into force of this Act.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Executive Council.
key_definitions.Executive Council: The Executive Council of the Institute established under section 12.
key_definitions.existing Institute: The Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development, Sriperumbudur, established under the Society Registration Act, 1860, and declared as deemed to be a University under the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, in existence immediately before the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Fund: The fund of the Institute to be maintained under section 26.
key_definitions.Institute: The Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development incorporated under section 4.
key_definitions.notification: The notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: The Statutes and Ordinances of the Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares that the Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development is an institution of national importance due to its objectives.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, appointed day, Chairperson, Director, Executive Council, existing Institute, Fund, Institute, notification, prescribed, Registrar, Statutes and Ordinances.

Establishes the Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and contract. It also specifies the headquarters and the possibility of establishing centers elsewhere in India.

Details the consequences of the Institute's establishment, including the transfer of references in contracts, vesting of property, transfer of rights and liabilities, and continuation of employment for existing staff under the same terms and conditions, with provisions for termination or alteration of terms.

Outlines the objectives of the Institute, which include evolving an integrated approach to youth development, setting up a National Youth Resource Centre, providing research and development, acting as a nodal agency for capacity building, empowering youth, evolving as an institute of advanced study in youth development, and providing higher education in youth development.

Specifies the functions of the Institute, such as developing a 'think tank' for policy research, acting as a repository of youth data, developing documentation and publication services, providing technical advice, building professional capacity of youth organizations, designing training programs, conducting seminars, setting up learning centers, collaborating with national and international bodies, awarding degrees, conferring honorary distinctions, receiving fees, conducting sponsored projects, creating posts, regulating affairs, supervising discipline, acquiring property, and establishing hostels.

main_sections.section_title: Institute to be open to all races, creeds, gender and classes
main_sections.description: States that the Institute shall be open to all persons regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, class, or physical ability, and that no test or condition shall be imposed based on religious belief. It also prohibits accepting bequests or donations with conditions opposed to this spirit.
Mandates that all teaching and academic activities shall be conducted by or in the name of the Institute in accordance with its Statutes and Ordinances.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the Institute, with the power to nominate someone to act as Visitor and to appoint persons to review the Institute's work and hold inquiries. The Institute is bound to comply with the Visitor's directions.
Lists the authorities of the Institute: the Executive Council, the Academic Council, and other authorities as declared by the Statutes.

Provides for the establishment of the Executive Council as a central body, to be constituted by a Chairperson nominated by the Visitor and other members including the Secretary of the Department of Youth Affairs.

important_rules: The Institute shall be open to persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class, physical ability, and no test or condition shall be imposed as to religious belief or profession in admitting students, appointing teachers or employees or in any other connection whatsoever.

No bequest, donation or transfer of any property shall be accepted by the Institute which in the opinion of the Executive Council involves conditions or obligations opposed to the spirit and object of this section.
All teaching and other academic activities at the Institute shall be conducted by or in the name of the Institute in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances made in this behalf.
The Institute shall be bound to comply with directions issued by the Visitor within a reasonable time.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Visitor have powers to issue directions and enforce compliance. The Institute itself is responsible for regulating its affairs and supervising discipline.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directions from the Visitor, by ensuring compliance with Statutes and Ordinances, and through the powers vested in the Executive Council and other authorities.

rights: Employees of the existing Institute retain their tenure, remuneration, terms, conditions, and privileges related to pension, leave, gratuity, and provident fund.
The Institute has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, contract, sue and be sued.
The Institute has the right to award degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions.
The Institute has the right to determine, demand, and receive fees and other charges.
The Institute can establish and maintain centers, collaborate with other institutions, and enter into agreements.
duties: To evolve and achieve an integrated approach to youth development.
To set up an advanced National Youth Resource Centre.
To provide for research and development and dissemination of knowledge.
To act as a nodal agency for capacity building of stakeholders.
To empower youth for inclusive development and nation building.
To evolve as an institute of advanced study in youth development.
To provide higher education in youth development.
To comply with directions from the Visitor.
obligations: To ensure its facilities are open to all without discrimination.
To not accept bequests or donations with conditions contrary to its open nature.
To ensure all employees continue under existing terms unless altered by Statutes, with specific provisions for employee consent or compensation if altered.

key_procedures: Appointment of the first Chairperson, Director, and members of the Executive Council and Academic Council.
Coming into force of the Act upon notification by the Central Government.
Establishment of the Executive Council on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Review of work and progress of the Institute and inquiries into its affairs by persons appointed by the Visitor.
Action and directions by the Visitor based on inquiry reports.
Making of Statutes and Ordinances by the Institute.
Conduct of business by authorities of the Institute.
Grant of degrees, diplomas, certificates, or other academic distinctions by the Institute.
Publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and notifications in the Official Gazette and laying them before Parliament.
administration: The Central Government, the Visitor (President of India), the Executive Council, and the Academic Council are key administrative bodies. The day-to-day administration will likely involve officers like the Director and Registrar.
important_notes: The Act came into force on November 19, 2012, vide notification No. S.O. 2747(E).
The existing Institute was a body established under the Society Registration Act, 1860, and declared as deemed to be a University under the UGC Act, 1956.
The President may nominate a person to act as Visitor for a term not exceeding five years.
If alterations to employment terms for existing employees are not acceptable, their employment may be terminated with compensation.

title: The National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bangalore Act, 2012
purpose: To declare the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bangalore as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and related matters.
scope: The Act applies to the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bangalore. It covers its incorporation, powers, functions, composition, administration, and the granting of medical degrees and diplomas.

key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Institute referred to in section 17.
key_definitions.Governing Body: The Governing Body of the Institute.
key_definitions.Institute: The institution known as the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bangalore, incorporated under this Act.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Institute.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.specified: Specified by regulations made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bangalore, as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bangalore, as an institution of national importance due to its objects.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Fund', 'Governing Body', 'Institute', 'member', 'prescribed', and 'specified'.

Constitutes the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, Bangalore, as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, granting it powers to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract.

Outlines the composition of the Institute, including ex officio members (Ministers, Secretaries, Director of the Institute, Director-General of Health Services, Vice-Chancellor) and nominated/elected members (scientists, medical faculty representatives, Members of Parliament).

Specifies the objectives of the Institute, including developing teaching patterns in mental health and neuro-sciences, providing high-order educational facilities, achieving self-sufficiency in postgraduate medical education, evolving innovative diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and conducting research.

Details the functions of the Institute, such as providing undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, facilities for research, teaching of humanities, conducting experiments in medical education, specifying courses, establishing medical institutions, hospitals, nursing colleges, health centres, and training health workers. It also covers granting degrees and appointing staff.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the Institute the power to make regulations for the transaction of its business and for other matters as specified in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires that all rules and regulations made under the Act be laid before each House of Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and by extension, the Institute and its Governing Body through its administrative and regulatory functions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers granted to the Central Government to make rules, notifications, and oversight, and the Institute's ability to make regulations, establish institutions, and grant academic distinctions. Enforcement of academic standards and institutional operations is implied through these powers.

rights: Right to be declared an institution of national importance.
Right to have perpetual succession and a common seal.
Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right to contract and sue and be sued.
Right to receive grants from the Government and gifts/donations.
Right to demand and receive fees with prior approval of the Central Government.
Right to grant medical degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.
duties: Duty to develop high standards of medical education.
Duty to bring together educational facilities.
Duty to attain self-sufficiency in postgraduate medical education.
Duty to offer diagnostic and comprehensive therapeutic services.
Duty to conduct in-depth study and research.
Duty to provide undergraduate and postgraduate teaching and research facilities.
Duty to establish and maintain medical institutions, hospitals, and training centres.
Duty to conduct examinations and grant qualifications.
Duty to adhere to rules and regulations prescribed by the Central Government and the Institute.
obligations: Obligation to follow procedures for meetings and business transactions.
Obligation for staff and members to adhere to prescribed conditions of service and allowances.
Obligation for rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament.

key_procedures: Appointment of the President and Vice-President of the Institute by the Central Government.
Constitution of the Governing Body by the Institute, with a majority of Institute members.
Appointment of the Director of the Institute by the Institute (first Director by Central Government).
Appointment of other officers and employees by the Institute.
Granting of medical degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions by the Institute based on regulations.
Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament for review.
administration: The Act is administered by the Central Government, which has powers to make rules and notifications. The Institute, with its Governing Body and Director, is responsible for the day-to-day operations and management.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Members elected from Parliament will cease to be members of the Institute if they become Ministers or hold certain parliamentary positions.
The Director holds office for a term of five years or until attaining the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.
The Institute can establish various medical and training institutions, including hospitals, nursing colleges, and health centres.
All rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

title: The National Food Security Act, 2013
purpose: To provide for food and nutritional security in a human life cycle approach, by ensuring access to adequate quantity of quality food at affordable prices to people to live a life with dignity and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to all persons belonging to eligible households under the Targeted Public Distribution System, pregnant women, lactating mothers, and children up to the age of fourteen years, and impacts the Central Government, State Governments, and local authorities in their respective roles concerning food security.

key_definitions.anganwadi: A child care and development center set up under the Integrated Child Development Services Scheme of the Central Government to render services covered under sections 4, 5(1)(a), and 6.
key_definitions.central_pool: The stock of food grains procured by the Central Government and State Governments through minimum support price operations, maintained for allocations under the Targeted Public Distribution System, other welfare schemes, including calamity relief, and kept as reserves.
key_definitions.eligible_households: Households covered under the priority households and the Antyodaya Anna Yojana referred to in sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.fair_price_shop: A shop licensed to distribute essential commodities by an order issued under section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, to ration card holders under the Targeted Public Distribution System.
key_definitions.foodgrains: Rice, wheat or coarse grains or any combination thereof conforming to such quality norms as may be determined by the Central Government.
key_definitions.food_security: The supply of the entitled quantity of foodgrains and meal specified under Chapter II.
key_definitions.food_security_allowance: The amount of money to be paid by the concerned State Government to the entitled persons under section 8.
key_definitions.local_authority: Includes Panchayat, municipality, district board, cantonment board, town planning authority, and in certain North-Eastern States, village council or committee or any other body authorised for self-governance or civic services management.
key_definitions.meal: Hot cooked or pre-cooked and heated before its service meal or take home ration, as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
key_definitions.minimum_support_price: The assured price announced by the Central Government at which foodgrains are procured from farmers for the central pool.
key_definitions.priority_households: Households identified as such under section 10.
key_definitions.Targeted_Public_Distribution_System: The system for distribution of essential commodities to ration card holders through fair price shops.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the National Food Security Act, 2013, declares its extent to the whole of India, and specifies its commencement date as July 5, 2013.

Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, including 'anganwadi', 'central pool', 'eligible households', 'fair price shop', 'foodgrains', 'food security', 'food security allowance', 'local authority', 'meal', 'minimum support price', 'priority households', and 'Targeted Public Distribution System'.

main_sections.section_title: Right to receive foodgrains at subsidised prices by persons belonging to eligible households under Targeted Public Distribution System
main_sections.description: Entitles persons in priority households to receive 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month at subsidized prices. Households under Antyodaya Anna Yojana are entitled to 35 kg per household per month. It also specifies coverage percentages for rural and urban populations.

main_sections.section_title: Nutritional support to pregnant women and lactating mothers
main_sections.description: Entitles pregnant women and lactating mothers to free meals through local anganwadis and a maternity benefit of not less than Rs. 6,000, excluding those in regular government or PSU employment receiving similar benefits.

Provides for age-appropriate meals free of charge for children aged six months to six years through anganwadis, and one mid-day meal free of charge daily for children up to Class VIII or aged six to fourteen years in government, local body, and government-aided schools. It also mandates cooking, drinking water, and sanitation facilities.
Provides for the constitution of a State Food Commission by the State Government to perform functions assigned under the Act.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over any other law inconsistent with its provisions.

important_rules: Persons belonging to priority households are entitled to receive 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month at subsidized prices under the Targeted Public Distribution System.
Households covered under Antyodaya Anna Yojana are entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month at subsidized prices.
Pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to a free meal during pregnancy and six months post-childbirth, and a maternity benefit of at least Rs. 6,000.
Children up to the age of fourteen years are entitled to age-appropriate meals through anganwadis (six months to six years) and mid-day meals in schools (up to Class VIII or six to fourteen years).
State Governments shall implement schemes to identify and provide meals, free of charge, to children suffering from malnutrition.
In case of non-supply of entitled foodgrains or meals, affected persons are entitled to receive food security allowance from the concerned State Government.
Women of eighteen years of age or above are to be considered the head of the household for the purpose of issuing ration cards.

penalties: Contravention of provisions of the Act can lead to penalties as specified in Section 33.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and State Governments, with the involvement of local authorities and the State Food Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of schemes, identification of eligible households, grievance redressal mechanisms, monitoring, social audits, and vigilance committees. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions.

rights: Right to receive foodgrains at subsidized prices by persons belonging to eligible households.
Right to receive nutritional support (meals and maternity benefit) for pregnant women and lactating mothers.
Right to receive nutritional support (meals) for children.
Right to receive food security allowance in cases of non-supply of entitled foodgrains or meals.
Right to access records of the Targeted Public Distribution System for transparency.
Right to participate in social audits.
duties: Duty of Central Government to allocate required quantity of foodgrains and provide funds.
Duty of State Governments to implement and monitor schemes, and identify eligible households.
Duty of local authorities to implement the Targeted Public Distribution System in their areas.
Duty to ensure transparency and accountability in the implementation of schemes.
Duty to prevent and manage child malnutrition.
Duty to provide facilities for cooking meals, drinking water, and sanitation in schools and anganwadis.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government for food security, including allocations and funds.
Obligation of the State Government for food security, including scheme implementation and monitoring.
Obligation of local authorities in implementing the Targeted Public Distribution System and their civic service management.

key_procedures: Identification of eligible households: State Governments shall prepare guidelines and identify households for Antyodaya Anna Yojana and priority households.
Publication and display of list of eligible households.
Grievance Redressal: Establishment of internal grievance redressal mechanisms, appointment of District Grievance Redressal Officers, and constitution of State Food Commissions.
Social Audit: Conduct of social audits to monitor and evaluate the planning and implementation of programs and schemes.
Setting up of Vigilance Committees: To supervise the implementation of all schemes under the Act.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments administer the Act. Specific departments or agencies within these governments would be responsible for various aspects like food procurement, distribution, scheme implementation, and monitoring. The State Food Commissions are also key administrative bodies.
important_notes: The Act provides for food security through a human life cycle approach, ensuring nutritional needs from pregnancy to childhood.
The Act aims to promote dignity by ensuring access to adequate quantity of quality food at affordable prices.
