The provisions of the Act have an overriding effect over any other law inconsistent with them.
Force Majeure clause (Section 44) addresses situations beyond control.

title: The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013
purpose: To provide for the prohibition of employment as manual scavengers, rehabilitation of manual scavengers and their families, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, aiming to correct historical injustice and indignity suffered by manual scavengers and to rehabilitate them to a life of dignity.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to individuals, local authorities, and agencies involved in sanitation and the employment of individuals for cleaning human excreta.

key_definitions.agency: Any agency, other than a local authority, which may undertake sanitation facilities in an area, including a contractor, firm, or company involved in real estate development and maintenance.
key_definitions.appropriate_government: In relation to Cantonment Boards, railway lands, and lands/buildings owned by the Central Government, a Central Public Sector Undertaking, or an autonomous body substantially funded by the Central Government, it's the Central Government. In all other cases, it's the State Government.
key_definitions.hazardous_cleaning: Manual cleaning of a sewer or septic tank by an employee without the employer providing protective gear, cleaning devices, and ensuring safety precautions.
key_definitions.insanitary_latrine: A latrine that requires manual cleaning or handling of human excreta, either in situ, in an open drain or pit, before it fully decomposes. (Excludes specific railway coach latrines cleaned with prescribed devices and protective gear).
key_definitions.local_authority: A Municipality or Panchayat responsible for sanitation, a Cantonment Board, or a railway authority.
key_definitions.manual_scavenger: A person engaged or employed to manually clean, carry, dispose of, or handle human excreta in an insanitary latrine, open drain or pit, or on a railway track, before it fully decomposes. (Excludes those cleaning with prescribed devices and protective gear).

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the process for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'agency', 'appropriate government', 'hazardous cleaning', 'insanitary latrine', 'local authority', 'manual scavenger', 'sanitary latrine', 'septic tank', and 'sewer'.

Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in the Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993, or any other law.

main_sections.section_title: Local authorities to survey insanitary latrines and provide sanitary community latrines
main_sections.description: Mandates local authorities to survey insanitary latrines, publish a list, notify occupiers for demolition or conversion, and construct sanitary community latrines within specified periods.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of insanitary latrines and employment and engagement of manual scavenger
main_sections.description: Prohibits the construction of insanitary latrines and the employment or engagement of manual scavengers. It also mandates the demolition or conversion of existing insanitary latrines.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of persons from engagement or employment for hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks
main_sections.description: Prohibits the engagement or employment of any person for hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks.

main_sections.section_title: Survey of manual scavengers in urban areas by Municipalities
main_sections.description: Requires Municipalities to conduct a survey of manual scavengers in urban areas.

main_sections.section_title: Rehabilitation of persons identified as manual scavengers by a Municipality
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the rehabilitation of individuals identified as manual scavengers by a Municipality.

main_sections.section_title: Survey of manual scavengers in rural areas by Panchayats
main_sections.description: Requires Panchayats to conduct a survey of manual scavengers in rural areas.

main_sections.section_title: Rehabilitation of persons identified as manual scavengers by a Panchayat
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the rehabilitation of individuals identified as manual scavengers by a Panchayat.
Provides for the constitution of Vigilance Committees.
Details the functions and responsibilities of the Vigilance Committees.
Provides for the constitution of a Central Monitoring Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Central Monitoring Committee
main_sections.description: Details the functions and responsibilities of the Central Monitoring Committee.
Grants the appropriate Government the power to exempt any person or class of persons from any provision of the Act.

important_rules: No person, local authority, or agency shall construct an insanitary latrine after the commencement of the Act.
No person, local authority, or agency shall engage or employ a manual scavenger, directly or indirectly.
Every insanitary latrine existing at the commencement of the Act must be demolished or converted into a sanitary latrine by the occupier at their own cost within the specified period.
No person shall be engaged or employed for hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks.
Local authorities must conduct surveys of insanitary latrines and provide sanitary community latrines.
Municipalities and Panchayats must survey manual scavengers and implement their rehabilitation.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of section 5 or section 6 (prohibition of insanitary latrines and employment of manual scavengers, and void contracts) is imprisonment and fine.
Penalty for contravention of section 7 (prohibition of hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks) is imprisonment and fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authorities, Executive Magistrates, Vigilance Committees, State Monitoring Committees, Central Monitoring Committee, and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis play roles in enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through surveys, prohibition notices, prosecution of offenders by Executive Magistrates, and monitoring by various committees and commissions. Offences are cognizable and non-bailable.

rights: Right to live with dignity (Preamble).
Right to be protected from social injustice and exploitation (Preamble).
Right to rehabilitation for identified manual scavengers and their families.
duties: Duty of local authorities to survey insanitary latrines and provide sanitary community latrines.
Duty of occupiers to demolish or convert insanitary latrines.
Duty of Municipalities and Panchayats to survey and identify manual scavengers.
Duty of State Governments or Union territories to send periodic reports to the Central Government.
Duty of local authorities and other agencies to use modern technology for cleaning sewers, etc.
obligations: Obligation of employers to provide protective gear and ensure safety precautions during cleaning of sewers and septic tanks (implied by definition of hazardous cleaning).
Obligation of local authorities to ensure hygienic upkeep of community sanitary latrines.

key_procedures: Survey and identification of insanitary latrines by local authorities, followed by notices for demolition or conversion, and construction of community latrines.
Survey and identification of manual scavengers in urban and rural areas by Municipalities and Panchayats, respectively.
Application process for urban and rural manual scavengers for identification.
Rehabilitation process for identified manual scavengers.
Establishment and functioning of Vigilance Committees and State/Central Monitoring Committees for oversight and implementation.
Trial of offences by Executive Magistrates.
Powers of inspectors appointed under the Act.
administration: The Act is administered by various authorities including the Central Government, State Governments, local authorities (Municipalities, Panchayats, Cantonment Boards, railway authorities), and designated officers.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on certain previous laws.
Water flush latrines in railway passenger coaches, when cleaned with specified devices and protective gear, are not considered insanitary latrines.
A person engaged or employed to clean excreta with the help of specified devices and protective gear is not deemed a manual scavenger.
Jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in certain matters.
The Central Government has the power to make model rules and remove difficulties.

title: The Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University Act, 2013
purpose: To establish and incorporate a national aviation University to facilitate and promote aviation studies and research, achieve excellence in aviation management, policy, science, technology, environment, safety, and security, and produce quality human resources for the aviation sector.
scope: The Act applies to the Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University, its campuses, colleges, institutions, and recognized institutions across India, and also has provisions for off-shore campuses. It covers the establishment, objectives, powers, authorities, and administration of the University.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.Campus: A unit established or constituted by the University for instruction, research, education, and training.
key_definitions.College: A college maintained by or admitted to the privileges of the University for imparting education and training in aviation studies or its associated disciplines.
key_definitions.Director General: The Director General of Civil Aviation.
key_definitions.Distance Education System: The system of imparting education through various communication means like broadcasting, telecasting, internet, correspondence, etc.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University, including teachers and other staff.
key_definitions.Institution: An institution, school, college, or centre of studies maintained by or admitted to the privileges of the University for imparting education, training, and research in aviation studies or its associated disciplines.
key_definitions.recognised Institution: An institution admitted to the privileges of the University for imparting education in aviation studies or its associated disciplines.
key_definitions.teachers of the University: Professors, Associate Professors, Assistant Professors, Readers, Senior Lecturers, Lecturers, and other persons appointed or recognized for imparting instruction or conducting research in the University or its affiliated colleges/institutions.
key_definitions.University: The National Aviation University established under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University Act, 2013' and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'Academic Council', 'Campus', 'College', 'Director General', 'Institution', 'recognised Institution', 'teachers of the University', and 'University'.

Establishes the University by the name 'Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University', specifies its headquarters at Fursatganj, Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh, and allows for the establishment of other campuses and centres. It also states that the University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objectives of the University, including facilitating and promoting aviation studies, teaching, training, research, and extension work in various emerging areas, promoting advanced knowledge, creating an ambience for learning, ensuring quality of aviation education, developing international academic standards, and developing skilled aviation manpower.

Details the powers of the University, including providing instruction and research in aviation-related fields, recognizing aviation training colleges and institutes, establishing and maintaining campuses, departments, laboratories, libraries, hostels, and other facilities, collaborating with other institutions, preparing educational programs leading to degrees and diplomas, conferring honorary degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, instituting academic positions, and appointing staff.

important_rules: The Act shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may appoint by notification in the Official Gazette.
The University shall be a teaching, research, and affiliating Aviation University.
The University shall facilitate and promote aviation studies, teaching, training, research, and extension work with a focus on emerging areas.
The University shall have the power to provide for instruction in aviation-related natural sciences, social sciences, humanities, engineering, technology, and medicine.
The University shall have the power to recognize aviation training colleges and institutes and maintain standards.
The University shall have the power to prepare educational programs leading to degrees and diplomas in civil aviation.

The University shall have the power to grant degrees (including doctoral degrees), diplomas, or certificates other than Certificates of Competencies of licensed aviation personnel, which are issued by the Director General of Civil Aviation.
The University shall have the power to recognize and withdraw recognition of institutions of higher learning.

rights: The University has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The University has the right to sue and be sued in its name.
The University has the right to grant degrees and other academic distinctions.
The University has the right to confer honorary degrees.
duties: The University has a duty to facilitate and promote aviation studies, teaching, training, research, and extension work.
The University has a duty to ensure and regulate the quality of aviation education programs.
The University has a duty to develop academic standards of an international level.
The University has a duty to develop various programs for aviation sector staff.
The University has a duty to undertake inter-disciplinary studies and research.
The University has a duty to provide for instruction in aviation-related fields and make provision for research.
The University has a duty to establish and maintain facilities necessary for its objects.
The University has a duty to ensure proper standards of instruction, teaching, and training in recognized institutions.
obligations: The University must operate in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
The University must adhere to the Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations made under the Act.

administration: The University shall be administered by its various authorities, including the Court, the Executive Council, and the Academic Council, as constituted under the Act.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act.
Certificates of Competencies of licensed aviation personnel shall continue to be issued by the Director General of Civil Aviation, Government of India, until the Central Government otherwise decides.
The Act provides for the establishment of a Tribunal of Arbitration for certain disputes.
The Act outlines procedures for appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.

title: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a body of Lokpal for the Union and Lokayukta for States to inquire into allegations of corruption against certain public functionaries and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, implementing the United Nations Convention Against Corruption and ensuring prompt and fair investigation and prosecution in cases of corruption.
scope: Applies to public servants in and outside India. Extends to the whole of India.

key_definitions.competent_authority: Defined in relation to the Prime Minister, Ministers, Members of Parliament, officers of the Central Government, and chairpersons or members/officers of various bodies, boards, corporations, authorities, companies, societies, or autonomous bodies established or financed by the Central Government.
key_definitions.complaint: A complaint, made in such form as may be prescribed, alleging that a public servant has committed an offence punishable under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
key_definitions.investigation: An investigation as defined under clause (h) of section 2 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
key_definitions.member: A Member of the Lokpal.
key_definitions.public_servant: A person referred to in clauses (a) to (h) of sub-section (1) of section 14, excluding those under the purview of the Army Act, Air Force Act, Navy Act, and Coast Guard Act.
key_definitions.special_court: The court of a Special Judge appointed under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act, its territorial extent, application to public servants, and commencement date.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'bench', 'Chairperson', 'competent authority', 'complaint', 'investigation', 'Lokpal', 'Member', 'public servant', and 'Special Court'.
Establishes the Lokpal body, detailing its composition, eligibility criteria for the Chairperson and Members, and restrictions on their appointment and holding other offices.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chairperson and Members on recommendations of Selection Committee
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for appointing the Chairperson and Members of the Lokpal through a Selection Committee comprising the Prime Minister, Speaker of the House of the People, Leader of Opposition, Chief Justice of India (or nominee), and an eminent jurist. Also establishes a Search Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of Lokpal to include Prime Minister, Ministers, members of Parliament, Groups A, B, C and D officers and officials of Central Government
main_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction of the Lokpal in relation to various public functionaries, including the Prime Minister, Ministers, Members of Parliament, and officers of the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions relating to complaints and preliminary inquiry and investigation
main_sections.description: Details the procedures for receiving complaints, conducting preliminary inquiries, and carrying out investigations.
Grants supervisory powers to the Lokpal.
Empowers the Lokpal with the power of search and seizure.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Lokpal to recommend transfer or suspension of public servant connected with allegation of corruption
main_sections.description: Allows the Lokpal to recommend the transfer or suspension of public servants involved in corruption allegations.
Mandates the declaration of assets by public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Prosecution for false complaint and payment of compensation, etc., to public servant
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for making false complaints and provisions for compensation to public servants.
Provides for the establishment of Lokayukta for States.

important_rules: Complaints must allege that a public servant has committed an offence punishable under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Persons likely to be prejudicially affected by an inquiry must be given an opportunity to be heard.
The Lokpal can require any public servant or any other person to furnish information.
The Lokpal can grant sanction for initiating prosecution.
The Lokpal has supervisory powers, including search and seizure.
The Lokpal can recommend the transfer or suspension of public servants linked to corruption allegations.
Public servants are required to declare their assets.
False complaints can lead to prosecution and compensation to the public servant.
The Act has an overriding effect over other laws in certain circumstances.

penalties: Prosecution for false complaints.
Payment of compensation to public servants for false complaints.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Lokpal, assisted by its Inquiry Wing and Prosecution Wing. Special Courts are constituted for speedy trial.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through preliminary inquiries, investigations, prosecution by the Prosecution Wing, and trial by Special Courts. The Lokpal also has powers of search, seizure, provisional attachment and confiscation of assets. Recommendations for transfer or suspension of public servants can be made.

rights: Right of persons likely to be prejudicially affected to be heard.
Right to legal assistance in certain cases.
Protection of action taken in good faith by public servants and others.
duties: Duty of public servants to declare assets.
Duty of public servants and other persons to furnish information when required by the Lokpal.
Duty of the Lokpal to inquire into allegations of corruption against specified public functionaries.
obligations: Obligation to establish Lokpal for the Union and Lokayuktas for States.
Obligation to comply with directions from the Lokpal.
Obligation to ensure prompt and fair investigation and prosecution in corruption cases.

key_procedures: Receiving and processing complaints alleging corruption by public servants.
Conducting preliminary inquiries to ascertain the veracity of allegations.
Carrying out investigations, including search and seizure, if necessary.
Granting sanction for prosecution.
Referring cases to Special Courts for trial.
Provisional attachment and confiscation of assets derived from corruption.
Recommending transfer or suspension of public servants involved in corruption.
Declaration of assets by public servants.
administration: The Lokpal, with its Chairperson and Members, along with its Inquiry Wing and Prosecution Wing, is responsible for the administration of this Act concerning the Union. The Act also provides for the establishment of Lokayuktas for States, implying State-level administration for those bodies.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to public servants both within and outside India.
It aims to implement the United Nations Convention Against Corruption.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws.
Provisions of this Act are in addition to other laws, meaning it supplements existing legal frameworks for combating corruption.
The Lokpal also functions as an appellate authority for appeals arising out of any other law for the time being in force.

title: THE SCHOOL OF PLANNING AND ARCHITECTURE ACT, 2014
purpose: To establish and declare Schools of Planning and Architecture as Institutions of national importance in order to promote education and research in architectural studies including planning of human settlements.
scope: Applies to the Schools of Planning and Architecture mentioned in the Schedule and any other Schools established under this Act. It applies to the field of architectural studies, including planning of human settlements, education, and research. The Act declares these Schools as Institutions of national importance.

key_definitions.Board: In relation to any School, means the Board of Governors thereof.
key_definitions.Chairperson: Means the Chairperson of the Board.
key_definitions.Council: Means the Council established under sub-section (1) of section 33.
key_definitions.Director: In relation to any School, means the Director thereof.
key_definitions.existing School: Means the School mentioned under column (3) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.Member: Means a Member of the Board and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Registrar: In relation to any School, means the Registrar thereof.
key_definitions.School: Means any of the Schools mentioned in column (5) of the Schedule and such other Schools established under this Act.
key_definitions.Senate: In relation to any School, means the Senate thereof.
key_definitions.Society: Means any of the societies registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860) or under the societies of respective State Governments and mentioned in column (3) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: In relation to any School, means the Statutes and Ordinances of that School made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette. Different dates can be appointed for different provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain Schools as Institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Schools mentioned in the Schedule as Institutions of national importance due to their objects.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Council', 'Director', 'existing School', 'Member', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'Registrar', 'School', 'Senate', 'Society', and 'Statutes and Ordinances'.

States that the Schools specified in the Schedule, from the commencement of the Act, shall be body corporates with perpetual succession and a common seal, having the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, contract, and sue or be sued in their respective names.

Outlines the objects of each School, which include supporting the establishment and development of Schools of Planning and Architecture and providing global leadership in architecture, planning, and allied fields.

Details the consequences of incorporation, including the re-reference of existing Schools to corresponding Schools, vesting of properties, transfer of rights, debts, and liabilities, continuation of employment terms for existing staff, migration of students, and continuation of legal proceedings.

Specifies the powers and duties of each School, such as organizing research, granting degrees, instituting fellowships, fixing fees, managing hostels, appointing staff (excluding Director), framing Statutes and Ordinances, establishing infrastructure, managing funds, and co-operating with other institutions. It also states that no immovable property can be disposed of without prior Central Government approval.

main_sections.section_title: Schools to be open to all races, creeds and classes
main_sections.description: Mandates that every School shall be open to all persons regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, class, religion, disability, domicile, ethnicity, social, or economic background. It also states that no bequest or donation with conditions opposed to this spirit shall be accepted.
States that all teaching shall be conducted in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances.

main_sections.section_title: School to be a distinct legal entity not-for-profit
main_sections.description: Establishes each School as a not-for-profit legal entity, with any surplus revenue to be used for the growth and development of the School or research.
Designates the President of India as the Visitor of every School, with the power to appoint persons to review work, conduct inquiries, and issue directions to the School.
Lists the authorities of a School: Board of Governors, Senate, and other authorities declared by Statutes.

Defines the Board of Governors as the principal executive body of the School and specifies its composition, including the Chairperson appointed by the Visitor, representatives from State Government, professional bodies (Institute of Town Planners, India, Council of Architecture), AICTE, UGC, experts, Senate representatives, Central Government nominees, Ministry of Urban Development nominee, Director, and Registrar.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of vacancies among, and allowances payable to, Members of Board
main_sections.description: Specifies that the term of office for the Chairperson and other Members of the Board is five years from the date of nomination, and for ex-officio Members, it continues as long as they hold their respective offices.
Provides for the establishment of a Council for Schools.

main_sections.section_title: Returns and information to be provided to Central Government
main_sections.description: Requires Schools to provide returns and information to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: School to be public authority under Right to Information, Act, 2005
main_sections.description: Declares that a School shall be a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
Makes provisions for transitional matters.

important_rules: Schools shall be open to all individuals irrespective of sex, race, creed, caste, class, religion, disability, domicile, ethnicity, social or economic background (Section 8(1)).
No bequest or donation shall be accepted if it imposes conditions or obligations contrary to the spirit of Section 8 (Section 8(2)).
All teaching must be conducted in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances (Section 9).
Schools must operate as not-for-profit entities, with any surplus reinvested for growth, development, or research (Section 10).
Schools cannot dispose of immovable property without prior approval from the Central Government (Section 7(2)).
The President of India, as Visitor, can review School activities and issue binding directions (Section 11).
The Board of Governors is the principal executive body of each School and its composition is detailed (Section 13).
Schools must provide returns and information to the Central Government (Section 39).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Visitor (President of India), Council, Board of Governors, Senate
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directions issued by the Visitor, framing of Statutes and Ordinances, oversight by the Central Government, and the functioning of the Board of Governors and Senate.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right to contract and sue or be sued.
Right to organize research and innovations.
Right to grant degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions.
Right to fix, demand, and receive fees.
Right to establish and manage hostels.
Right to appoint adjunct, guest, or visiting teachers.
Right to frame Statutes and Ordinances.
Right to manage the fund and receive gifts, grants, donations, bequests, and transfers of property.
Right to co-operate with other institutions globally.
Right to undertake consultancy services.
Right to have its staff continue under same tenure, remuneration, and terms unless altered by Statutes (with provisions for termination compensation).
duties: To promote education and research in architectural studies and planning of human settlements.
To support the establishment and development of Schools of Planning and Architecture.
To provide global leadership in architecture, planning, and allied fields.
To be open to all races, creeds, and classes.
To conduct teaching in accordance with Statutes and Ordinances.
To use surplus revenue for growth, development, or research.
To comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
To provide returns and information to the Central Government.
To supervise and control student residence, discipline, health, welfare, and culture.
To establish and maintain necessary infrastructure.
obligations: To ensure Schools are open to all and do not accept bequests with discriminatory conditions.
To comply with directions from the Visitor.
To provide required information and returns to the Central Government.
To seek prior approval of the Central Government for disposal of immovable property.

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairperson: Visitor appoints Chairperson from a panel recommended by the Central Government (Section 13(2)(a)).
Establishment and Incorporation: Schools mentioned in the Schedule are incorporated as body corporates upon commencement of the Act (Section 4).
Review by Visitor: Visitor may appoint persons to review School work and progress, conduct inquiries, and issue directions based on reports (Section 11).

Framing Statutes and Ordinances: Schools have the power to frame, alter, modify, or rescind Statutes and Ordinances (Section 7(1)(i)). The process for making Statutes is detailed in Section 29, and for Ordinances in Section 31.
Reporting to Central Government: Schools must provide returns and information to the Central Government as required (Section 39).
administration: Central Government (overall oversight, approval for immovable property, appointments, rules), Visitor (President of India) (highest oversight, review, directions), Council (establishment and functions detailed in Chapter V), Board of Governors (principal executive body), Director (head of the School's operations), Registrar (secretary to the Board, administrative officer).
important_notes: Different dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act's commencement (Section 1(2)).
Schools are declared as 'Institutions of national importance' (Section 2).
Existing Schools' properties, liabilities, and employee terms are transferred to corresponding new Schools (Section 6).
Schools are designated as public authorities under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (Section 41).
The Act includes transitional provisions to manage the shift from existing societies/schools to the incorporated bodies (Section 42).

title: THE REGIONAL CENTRE FOR BIOTECHNOLOGY ACT, 2016
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an institution of national importance to be known as Regional Centre for Biotechnology and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. It aims to strengthen the Regional Centre for Biotechnology for imparting education, training, and conducting research in the areas of Biotechnology and related multi-disciplinary areas.
scope: The Act applies to the Regional Centre for Biotechnology, which has its headquarters in Faridabad, Haryana. Its jurisdiction extends to the whole of India and to such centers and specialized laboratories or other units for research, development, and instruction, established by the Regional Centre within or outside India. The region of operation is also defined to include territories of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC) States and generally the Asia region.

key_definitions.academic_staff: Includes Assistant Professors, Associate Professors, Professors, Deans, Sub-Deans, Executive Director, and other persons appointed or engaged for imparting education, training, or conducting research.
key_definitions.Board: Refers to the Board of Governors constituted under section 14.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the Regional Centre, including officers, academic, and other staff.
key_definitions.institution: Includes autonomous organizations within or outside India for imparting education, training, and conducting research in Biotechnology, supported by the Government of India, industry, universities, or other organizations.
key_definitions.region: The region comprising the territories of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC) States and generally the Asia region.
key_definitions.Regional_Centre: The Regional Centre for Biotechnology established under section 3.
key_definitions.UNESCO: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'academic staff', 'Board', 'employee', 'institution', 'region', 'Regional Centre', and 'UNESCO'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Regional Centre for Biotechnology
main_sections.description: Establishes the Regional Centre for Biotechnology as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, headquartered in Faridabad, Haryana. It also states that the Regional Centre shall consist of a Board of Governors and other specified authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Regional Centre for Biotechnology as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Regional Centre for Biotechnology as an institution of national importance.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of establishment of Regional Centre
main_sections.description: Outlines the consequences of the Act's commencement, including the transfer of properties, assets, rights, liabilities, contracts, and legal proceedings from the existing Regional Centre to the newly established Regional Centre. It also addresses the service conditions of existing employees.

Specifies that the jurisdiction of the Regional Centre extends to the whole of India and to any centers, specialized laboratories, or other units established by the Regional Centre within or outside India.

Details the objectives of the Regional Centre, including disseminating and advancing knowledge in biotechnology, capacity-building, facilitating knowledge and technology transfer, creating a hub of expertise, promoting international cooperation, and establishing a network of satellite centers.

Enumerate the functions of the Regional Centre, such as establishing infrastructure, conducting educational and training activities, producing human resources, undertaking research and development, holding scientific symposia, collecting and disseminating information, developing intellectual property rights policies, and promoting collaborative research.

main_sections.section_title: Regional Centre to work in collaboration with other institutions of UNESCO
main_sections.description: Mandates that the Regional Centre shall pursue its objects and discharge its functions in close collaboration with other national, regional, and international institutions of UNESCO.

Lists the powers of the Regional Centre, including providing degrees and diplomas, organizing training courses, conferring honorary degrees, instituting and appointing academic staff, recognizing higher learning institutions, and creating administrative and technical posts.

important_rules: The Regional Centre for Biotechnology is established as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. (Section 3(1))
The Regional Centre is declared an institution of national importance. (Section 4)
Upon commencement of the Act, all properties, assets, rights, and liabilities of the existing Regional Centre are transferred to the new Regional Centre. (Section 5)
The jurisdiction of the Regional Centre extends to the whole of India and its units established within or outside India. (Section 6)
The Regional Centre shall pursue its objects and discharge its functions in collaboration with other UNESCO institutions. (Section 9)
The Regional Centre has the power to provide degrees, diplomas, organize training, institute academic positions, and recognize institutions of higher learning. (Section 10)

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but implied to be through the authorities of the Regional Centre and potentially government oversight.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

rights: The Regional Centre has the right to sue or be sued in its own name. (Section 3(1))
Employees of the existing Regional Centre retain their tenure and terms and conditions of service upon absorption into the Regional Centre. (Section 5(1)(g))
The Regional Centre has the power to provide educational programs, conduct research, and confer degrees and diplomas. (Section 10)
duties: The Regional Centre has a duty to disseminate and advance knowledge in biotechnology and related fields. (Section 7(a))
The Regional Centre has a duty to provide capacity-building through education, training, research, and development. (Section 7(b))
The Regional Centre has a duty to facilitate the transfer of knowledge and technology related to biotechnology at the regional level. (Section 7(c))
The Regional Centre has a duty to promote and strengthen international cooperation. (Section 7(e))
The Regional Centre must work in collaboration with other UNESCO institutions. (Section 9)
obligations: The Regional Centre has an obligation to work in collaboration with other institutions of UNESCO. (Section 9)
The Regional Centre must develop and implement a policy for intellectual property rights that is equitable and just to stakeholders. (Section 8(h))
The Regional Centre must ensure protection of intellectual property rights of local stakeholder communities when collecting and disseminating local knowledge. (Section 8(g))

key_procedures: Establishment of the Regional Centre as a body corporate with a Board of Governors and other authorities. (Section 3)
Transfer of assets, liabilities, and employees from the existing Regional Centre to the new Regional Centre upon commencement of the Act. (Section 5)
Dissemination of knowledge, capacity building, technology transfer, and promotion of international cooperation as per the objectives. (Section 7)
Conducting research, training, symposia, and disseminating research outcomes. (Section 8)
Providing degree programs, training courses, and academic appointments as specified by Statutes. (Section 10)
administration: The Regional Centre for Biotechnology functions under the Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India. The Act also establishes various authorities for its administration, including the Board of Governors, Programme Advisory Committee, Executive Committee, and Finance Committee.
important_notes: The absorption of any employee by the Regional Centre shall not entitle such employee to any compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or any other law. (Section 5(2))
The Regional Centre is to work in close collaboration with other national, regional, and international institutions of UNESCO. (Section 9)

title: The National Sports Governance Act, 2025
purpose: To provide for the development and promotion of sports, welfare measures for sportspersons, ethical practices based on basic universal principles of good governance, ethics and fair play of the Olympic and sports movement, the Olympic Charter, the Paralympic Charter, international best practices and established legal standards and to provide for the resolution of sports grievances and sports disputes in a unified, equitable and effective manner and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to sports governance in India, aiming to align national sports governing bodies with global standards, ensure transparency, and provide effective mechanisms for grievance and dispute resolution in sports. It specifically addresses national sports governing bodies, national sports boards, recognized sports organizations, ethical conduct, safe sports policies, and dispute resolution.

key_definitions.ad_hoc_administrative_body: A body constituted for ad hoc administration under section 11.
key_definitions.affiliate_unit: The State, district or other units of the National Olympic Committee, National Paralympic Committee, National Sports Federation, and the Regional Sports Federation.
key_definitions.board: The National Sports Board established under sub-section (1) of section 5.
key_definitions.board_recognition: Recognition of a sports organisation by the Board under this Act.
key_definitions.bye_laws: The memorandum of association or articles of association, by whatever name called, of a sports organisation.
key_definitions.designated_sport: Any sport discipline as may be specified by the Central Government, by notification, to be a designated sport for a specific region or State or for the whole of India.
key_definitions.international_charters_and_statutes: The Olympic Charter and other Charters and Statutes of the international sports governing bodies and include any bye-laws, rules, regulations or constitution, by whatever name called, as may be adopted, amended or issued by such bodies from time to time.
key_definitions.international_federation: A federation recognised as such by the International Olympic Committee in respect of an Olympic sport; or a federation recognised as such by the International Paralympic Committee in respect of a Paralympic sport; or a federation which regulates the sport at international level in respect of non-Olympic or non-Paralympic sports.
key_definitions.national_sports_body: A national sports governing body such as the National Olympic Committee or the National Paralympic Committee or the National Sports Federation or the Regional Sports Federation, established under section 3.
key_definitions.recognized_sports_organisation: A sports organisation recognised by the Board as a National Sports Body under sub-section (1) of section 8.
key_definitions.tribunal: The National Sports Tribunal constituted under sub-section (1) of section 17.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and provides for its commencement, allowing for different dates for different provisions.
Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, crucial for understanding its provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of national sports governing bodies
main_sections.description: Details the establishment of national sports governing bodies, including the National Olympic Committee, National Paralympic Committee, National Sports Federations, and Regional Sports Federations.

main_sections.section_title: Compliance with certain requirements by National Sports Bodies
main_sections.description: Outlines the requirements that National Sports Bodies must comply with, including their organizational structure such as General Body, Executive Committee, Ethics Committee, Dispute Resolution Committee, and Athletes Committee, as well as roles of President, Secretary General, and Treasurer.
Provides for the establishment of the National Sports Board.
Details the powers and functions of the National Sports Board.
Governs the process of recognition and registration of sports organizations by the Board.
Mandates the implementation of a Safe Sports Policy.
Specifies the privileges that recognized sports organizations are entitled to.
Outlines the duties that recognized sports organizations must fulfill.
Details the constitution of the National Sports Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Use of national names and insignia
main_sections.description: Regulates the use of national names and insignia in sports.

main_sections.section_title: Measures for promotion and development of sports
main_sections.description: Addresses measures for the promotion and development of sports.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.
Grants the Board the power to make regulations under the Act.

important_rules: Every National Sports Body shall have a General Body, an Executive Committee (with specific representation requirements for sportspersons of outstanding merit, Athletes Committee members, women, and age limits), an Ethics Committee, a Dispute Resolution Committee, and an Athletes Committee.

A person is disqualified from contesting for election or seeking nomination to the Executive Committee if they are not a citizen of India aged at least twenty-five, or if their nomination is not duly proposed and seconded, or if they are declared of unsound mind, or if they do not comply with age and term limits stipulated by International Charters and bye-laws (with specific provisions for those aged 70-75).
National Sports Bodies must comply with International Charters and Statutes and their own bye-laws regarding the structure and functioning of their committees and elections.
The National Sports Tribunal is constituted to resolve sports grievances and disputes.
The Act provides for measures for the promotion and development of sports.

penalties: While specific penalties for violations are not detailed in the provided text, the Act establishes a National Sports Tribunal (Section 17) for dispute resolution, implying that non-compliance with its provisions or those of the National Sports Board would be subject to its jurisdiction and potentially lead to sanctions.
Suspension or cancellation of Board recognition or registration is a power of the Board (Section 10), acting as an enforcement mechanism.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Sports Board and the National Sports Tribunal are the primary authorities for enforcement and dispute resolution.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the Board's powers of recognition, registration, inquiry, and suspension/cancellation (Sections 9 and 10). The National Sports Tribunal (Section 17 onwards) handles the resolution of grievances and disputes, with its orders executable as a decree (Section 26).

rights: Privileges of recognised sports organisations (Section 14).
duties: Duties of recognised sports organisations (Section 15).
National Sports Bodies must ensure compliance with requirements regarding their organizational structure, including representation and committee composition (Section 4).
obligations: National Sports Bodies have obligations to align with international governance standards, ethical behaviour, and transparency.
Recognized sports organizations have duties as outlined in Section 15.

key_procedures: Establishment of National Sports Governing Bodies (Section 3).
Compliance procedures for National Sports Bodies regarding their internal structure and governance (Section 4).
Process for Board recognition and registration of sports organizations (Section 8).
Procedure for the National Sports Board to conduct inquiries (Section 9).
Procedure for the National Sports Board to suspend or cancel recognition/registration (Section 10).
Constitution and functioning of the National Sports Tribunal for dispute resolution (Sections 17-26).
Procedure for appeals to the Supreme Court from decisions of the National Sports Tribunal (Section 25).
administration: The Central Government has powers to make rules (Section 31) and issue notifications, and the National Sports Board (established under Section 5) administers the Act's provisions related to recognition and governance of sports organizations.
important_notes: Different provisions of the Act can come into force on different dates as appointed by the Central Government via notification (Section 1(2)).
The Act emphasizes adherence to International Charters and Statutes, including the Olympic Charter and Paralympic Charter, and international best practices.
The Act allows the Central Government to exempt in special cases (Section 34) and to issue directions and impose restrictions in the national interest (Section 35).
The National Sports Tribunal's jurisdiction excludes civil courts (Section 23).

title: THE POLICE, AGRA ACT, 1854
purpose: To amend Regulation XI. of 1831 of the Bengal Code, by repealing certain inconvenient provisions and extending the amended regulation to the Province of Benares.
scope: This act applies to the Province of Benares and potentially other areas within the North-Western Provinces. It deals with the administration and subordination of Police Darogahs to Tehseeldars.

key_definitions.Darogah of Police: A police officer appointed within the local limits of a Tehseeldar's police jurisdiction.
key_definitions.Tehseeldar: An official who may have police jurisdiction under Regulation XI. of 1831.
key_definitions.Chief Police Thannadar: The capacity in which a Tehseeldar exercises control over a Police Darogah.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Sections III. and VII., Regulation XI. 1831
main_sections.description: This section explicitly repeals Sections III. and VII. of Regulation XI. of 1831 of the Bengal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Subordination of Darogahs of Police to Tehseeldars
main_sections.description: This section establishes that any Police Darogah appointed within the police jurisdiction of a Tehseeldar shall be subordinate to and under the control of that Tehseeldar, in his role as Chief Police Thannadar.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of Regulation XI. 1831, as amended, to Benares
main_sections.description: This section extends Regulation XI. of 1831, as amended by this Act, to the entire Province of Benares. It also states that powers vested in the Governor General in Council under the said Regulation can be exercised by the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces.

important_rules: Section III. and VII. of Regulation XI. 1831 are repealed.
Police Darogahs appointed within a Tehseeldar's police jurisdiction are subordinate to and controlled by that Tehseeldar as Chief Police Thannadar.
Regulation XI. 1831, as amended by this Act, is extended to the Province of Benares.
The Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces can exercise powers vested in the Governor General in Council under Regulation XI. 1831.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces, and potentially Tehseeldars in their capacity as Chief Police Thannadars.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the established legal and administrative framework for police and revenue officials within the specified provinces.

rights: The right of the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces to exercise certain powers.
duties: Darogahs of Police have a duty to be subordinate to and controlled by the Tehseeldar.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the amended Regulation XI. 1831 within the Province of Benares.

key_procedures: Appointment of Darogahs of Police within a Tehseeldar's jurisdiction.
Exercise of control by Tehseeldars over subordinate Darogahs.
Application of Regulation XI. 1831, as amended, to the Province of Benares.
administration: Likely administered by the Police Department and revenue authorities under the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces.
important_notes: The original Regulation XI. of 1831 is being amended.
The extension to Benares signifies a geographical expansion of the amended regulation's applicability.

title: The Fatal Accidents Act, 1855
purpose: To provide compensation to families for loss occasioned by the death of a person caused by an actionable wrong.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It covers cases where death is caused by a wrongful act, neglect, or default.

key_definitions.person: Applies to bodies politic and corporate.
key_definitions.parent: Includes father, mother, grandfather, and grandmother.
key_definitions.child: Includes son, daughter, grandson, granddaughter, step-son, and step-daughter.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855, and states its extent to the whole of India.

main_sections.section_title: Suit for compensation to the family of a person for loss occasioned to it by his death by actionable wrong
main_sections.description: Establishes that if a person's death is caused by a wrongful act, neglect, or default, the liable party can be sued for damages, even if death has occurred and the act was a felony. The suit is for the benefit of the wife, husband, parent, and child of the deceased, brought by their executor, administrator, or representative. The Court can award damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the beneficiaries.

main_sections.section_title: Not more than one suit to be brought. Claim for loss to estate may be added.
main_sections.description: Specifies that only one suit can be brought for the same subject-matter. It also allows the executor, administrator, or representative to include a claim for any pecuniary loss to the deceased's estate caused by the wrongful act, which recovered sum will be part of the estate's assets.
Requires the plaint in any such action to provide full particulars of the beneficiaries for whom the action is brought and the nature of the claim for which damages are sought.
Defines terms such as 'person', 'parent', and 'child' for the purpose of the Act.

important_rules: A suit for compensation can be brought if a person's death is caused by a wrongful act, neglect, or default.
The suit must be for the benefit of the wife, husband, parent, and child of the deceased.
The suit must be brought by the executor, administrator, or representative of the deceased.
Only one suit can be brought for the same cause of action.
A claim for pecuniary loss to the deceased's estate can be added to the suit.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of law
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through civil actions or suits for damages brought by the representatives of the deceased.

rights: Right of the family (wife, husband, parent, child) to receive compensation for loss occasioned by a death due to actionable wrong.
Right of the executor, administrator, or representative to bring a suit for compensation.
Right to add a claim for pecuniary loss to the deceased's estate.
duties: Duty of the liable party to be answerable in damages for causing death by wrongful act, neglect, or default.
Duty of the plaintiff to deliver full particulars of beneficiaries and the claim in the plaint.

key_procedures: Initiation of a suit by the executor, administrator, or representative of the deceased.
Inclusion of particulars of beneficiaries and the nature of the claim in the plaint.
Determination of damages by the Court proportionate to the loss suffered by the beneficiaries.
Division of recovered damages amongst beneficiaries as directed by the Court.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be administered by the judicial system through civil courts.
important_notes: The Act was amended to extend to the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands and the Union territory of Pondicherry.
The exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir from the extent of the Act has been omitted.
The original Section 1 was re-numbered as Section 1A.
The requirement to bring the action within twelve calendar months after the death of the deceased person has been omitted and now falls under the Indian Limitation Act, 1963.

title: THE CALCUTTA LAND – REVENUE ACT, 1856
purpose: To modify existing regulations concerning the collection of Stamp Duty in Calcutta, placing this responsibility primarily with the Collector of Calcutta, and to empower the Collector to delegate any of his duties to a subordinate Deputy Collector.
scope: This Act applies to the Town of Calcutta and concerns the administration of public revenues, specifically the collection of Stamp Duty. It modifies previous regulations and acts relating to the office of the Collector and Deputy Collector within this geographical area.

key_definitions.Collector of Calcutta: The designated officer responsible for revenue collection in Calcutta.
key_definitions.Deputy Collector: An officer subordinate to the Collector who can be tasked with performing parts of the Collector's duties.

main_sections.description: Declares that specific parts of Section VI, Regulation XII, 1826 of the Bengal Code, and Section VI of a Rule, Ordinance, and Regulation for the Town of Calcutta (dated June 14, 1827) are modified. These modified parts previously required a specially appointed Civil Servant by the Governor General in Council to manage Stamp Duty collection in Calcutta.

main_sections.section_title: Collection of Stamp Duty in Calcutta to be ordinarily in charge of the Collector
main_sections.description: Establishes that the collection of Stamp Duty within the Town of Calcutta will, by default, be under the charge of the Collector of Calcutta. This arrangement can be altered only if the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal directs otherwise.

main_sections.section_title: Collector may entrust any part of his duties to his Deputy
main_sections.description: Grants the Collector of Calcutta the legal authority to assign any portion of his official duties to a subordinate Deputy Collector. This delegation applies to duties under the specified Regulation, Act XI of 1849, or Act XXIII of 1850. It also confirms that existing rules, regulations, and acts pertaining to the Deputy Collector's office are equally effective within Calcutta as in other territories under the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.

important_rules: The Collector of Calcutta is to be ordinarily in charge of the collection of Stamp Duty within the Town of Calcutta, unless the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal decides otherwise.
The Collector of Calcutta is empowered to delegate any of his duties to a subordinate Deputy Collector.
Rules and regulations concerning Deputy Collectors are to be applied within Calcutta in the same manner as they are in other territories under the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector of Calcutta, Deputy Collectors subordinate to him, and potentially the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the delegation of duties by the Collector to his Deputies and the application of existing rules and regulations governing the office of Deputy Collector.

rights: The right of the Collector of Calcutta to be ordinarily in charge of Stamp Duty collection.
The right of the Collector of Calcutta to delegate duties to his Deputy Collector.
The right of Deputy Collectors to perform duties delegated by the Collector.
duties: Duty to collect Stamp Duty in Calcutta ordinarily by the Collector.
Duty of the Collector to manage and oversee the collection of Stamp Duty.
Duty of the Deputy Collector to perform duties as entrusted by the Collector.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to modified regulations regarding Stamp Duty collection.
Obligation to follow any directions issued by the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal regarding Stamp Duty collection.

key_procedures: Delegation of duties by the Collector of Calcutta to a subordinate Deputy Collector, which then allows the Deputy Collector to perform those duties.
The Lieutenant Governor of Bengal can direct otherwise, altering the ordinary procedure of the Collector being in charge of Stamp Duty collection.
administration: The administration of this Act falls under the purview of the Collector of Calcutta and his subordinate Deputy Collectors, with the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal having oversight and the power to issue directives.
important_notes: This Act modifies pre-existing regulations, specifically Regulation XII of 1826 and a Rule, Ordinance, and Regulation from 1827, to centralize Stamp Duty collection with the Collector of Calcutta.
The power to delegate duties to Deputy Collectors is a significant aspect, ensuring flexibility in revenue administration within Calcutta.

title: THE TOBACCO DUTY (TOWN OF BOMBAY) ACT, 1857
purpose: To amend the law relating to the duties payable on Tobacco, and the retail sale and warehousing thereof in the Town of Bombay.
scope: This act applies to Tobacco intended for consumption within the Town of Bombay. The 'Town of Bombay' is defined to include all places within the Islands of Bombay and Colaba.

key_definitions.municipal_duty: A duty of seven Rupees and eight annas per maund of forty seers of eighty tolas to the seer, levied on Tobacco imported into the Town of Bombay for consumption therein. This is in addition to any Customs Duty.
key_definitions.retail_sale: Any sale of Tobacco not exceeding in weight fourteen seers of eighty tolas to the seer.

main_sections.description: Repeals Chapters V, VI, VII, and VIII of Regulation XXI of 1827 of the Bombay Code, and Act XXIV of 1850. It clarifies that this repeal does not revive any other previously repealed Regulation or Act.

main_sections.section_title: Municipal Duty on Tobacco intended for consumption in Bombay
main_sections.description: Imposes a 'Municipal Duty' on all Tobacco imported into the Town of Bombay for consumption therein, except for small quantities for private consumption. The duty rate is specified as seven Rupees and eight annas per maund.
States that the Municipal Duty can be paid either upon the importation of the Tobacco or after it has been warehoused.

main_sections.section_title: Duty if not paid on importation, to be paid on removal from warehouse for consumption. Remission of Municipal Duty on re-exportation.
main_sections.description: If the Municipal Duty is not paid on importation, the Tobacco must be warehoused. The duty is then payable upon its removal from the warehouse for consumption in Bombay. The duty is remitted if the warehoused Tobacco is re-exported outside the Town.

main_sections.section_title: Bombay a warehousing port for Tobacco
main_sections.description: Declares the Port of Bombay as a warehousing port for Tobacco under Act XXV of 1836. The provisions of that Act are to be applied to the warehousing of Tobacco in Bombay, with the Import Duty in that Act including the Municipal Duty.

main_sections.section_title: Powers for collection and enforcing payment of the Municipal Duty
main_sections.description: Grants the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, and Officers of Customs, powers for collecting and enforcing the Municipal Duty, in addition to existing powers for Customs duties.

main_sections.section_title: Tobacco not to be imported otherwise than by Sea. Landing places to be prescribed
main_sections.description: Prohibits the importation of Tobacco into Bombay by means other than sea, without permission from the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium or other authorized officer. It also mandates landing only at places prescribed by the Government of Bombay.
Exempts small quantities of Tobacco (not exceeding four seers in weight) intended for the private consumption of the importer from the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Permit necessary for removal of Tobacco. Proviso.
main_sections.description: Requires a permit from the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium for the removal of Tobacco within the Town, for carrying it on thoroughfares, or for transporting it in small vessels on adjacent waters. Permits are valid only between sunrise and sunset. Exempts lawful importation and small quantities for personal use from the permit requirement.

main_sections.section_title: No Permit for removal from warehouse of less than a bale. Proviso.
main_sections.description: States that no permit will be granted for removing less than a whole bale or package from a warehouse. However, if Tobacco is to be removed for consumption, the Commissioner may allow opening bales to set aside refuse or waste, which can be re-exported or destroyed.

main_sections.section_title: License for retail sale of Tobacco
main_sections.description: Mandates obtaining a license from the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, or another authorized officer, for the retail sale of Tobacco in Bombay. The license is valid for twelve months and costs one Rupee. Licenses can be revoked under the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: What to be deemed retail sale
main_sections.description: Defines a 'retail sale' as any sale of Tobacco not exceeding fourteen seers in weight.

main_sections.section_title: Retail sale to be only at the place mentioned in the license. Name of licensed dealer to be affixed to shop.
main_sections.description: Requires retail sales and storage of Tobacco to occur only at the premises specified in the license. The name and license number of the dealer must be displayed prominently in English, Guzerati, and Maharatti on the shop.

main_sections.section_title: Monthly returns of stock to be made by retail dealers
main_sections.description: Obligates retail dealers to submit monthly returns to the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, detailing stock at the beginning of the month, quantities received (with source and date), and remaining stock at the end of the month. Failure to comply or making false returns can lead to license revocation and a fine not exceeding two hundred Rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Retail dealer to make entry in a book, of weight, &c., of all Tobacco received. Inspection of book.
main_sections.description: Requires retail dealers to record the weight, date of receipt, and source of all Tobacco received into their shops on the same day. This book must be open for inspection by authorized officers, who can make notes or extracts. Non-compliance is punishable by license revocation and a fine not exceeding two hundred Rupees.

Empowers the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, or other authorized officer, to issue a search warrant to a public officer for entering and searching any building or place where Tobacco is suspected to be illegally deposited or stored. Such a warrant allows for the seizure of illicit Tobacco and other confiscable articles.

main_sections.section_title: Power to arrest and detain. To search vehicles, &c.
main_sections.description: Grants the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, or authorized officers, the power to arrest and detain individuals in possession of Tobacco liable to confiscation, and to search any vessel, package, boat, or vehicle suspected of carrying such Tobacco.

main_sections.section_title: Confiscation of Tobacco illegally imported, removed, &c. Mitigation of penalty.
main_sections.description: All Tobacco illegally imported, removed, possessed, or sold contrary to the Act, along with the vessels, vehicles, or animals used in its transport (with owner's knowledge), are liable to confiscation. The adjudicating officer can commute confiscation to a fine up to the value of the goods, which can be enforced by sale of the goods.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for illegal importation, removal, sale, or possession. Revocation of license.
main_sections.description: Imposes a penalty of a fine not exceeding ten times the value of the Tobacco for illegal importation, removal, sale, or knowing possession of confiscable Tobacco. If the offender is a licensed retail dealer, their license can be revoked.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of fines and adjudication and sale of confiscations.
main_sections.description: All confiscations and fines under this Act are to be adjudicated and levied by a Magistrate of Police for the Town of Bombay. Confiscated goods will be sold under a warrant from the Magistrate.
Defines 'Town of Bombay' to include the Islands of Bombay and Colaba. It also provides standard interpretations for singular/plural and masculine/feminine gender in the Act.

important_rules: All Tobacco imported into the Town of Bombay for consumption is liable to a Municipal Duty of seven Rupees and eight annas per maund.
Municipal Duty can be paid upon importation or after warehousing.
Tobacco not intended for consumption in Bombay and re-exported is exempt from Municipal Duty.
Importation of Tobacco is restricted to by sea, and landing at prescribed places only.
Small quantities of Tobacco (up to four seers) for private consumption are exempt from duty.
Removal of Tobacco within the Town, or transport on thoroughfares or small vessels, requires a permit.
A license is mandatory for the retail sale of Tobacco in Bombay.
Retail sales can only occur at licensed premises, and the dealer's name and license number must be displayed.
Retail dealers must submit monthly stock returns and maintain a book of all Tobacco received.
Illegal importation, removal, sale, or possession of Tobacco is subject to confiscation and/or fines.

penalties: Confiscation of Tobacco illegally imported, removed, or possessed.
A fine not exceeding ten times the value of the illegally dealt with Tobacco.
Revocation of license for retail dealers who commit offenses.
Fine not exceeding two hundred Rupees for failing to make monthly returns or making false returns.
Fine not exceeding two hundred Rupees for neglecting or refusing to comply with record-keeping provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, Officers of Customs, and Magistrates of Police for the Town of Bombay.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of collection and enforcement of duties, issuance of search warrants, arrest and detention of persons, search of vehicles, confiscation of goods, and levy of fines by Magistrates.

rights: Right to import Tobacco (subject to duty and regulations).
Right to warehouse Tobacco.
Right to re-export warehoused Tobacco for remission of duty.
Right to obtain a license for retail sale of Tobacco.
Right to remit confiscation penalty to a fine (at the discretion of the adjudicating officer).
Exemption for small quantities of Tobacco for private consumption.
duties: Duty to pay Municipal Duty on imported Tobacco for consumption.
Duty to warehouse Tobacco if Municipal Duty is not paid on importation.
Duty to obtain permits for removal of Tobacco within the Town.
Duty to obtain a license for retail sale of Tobacco.
Duty to display the dealer's name and license number on the shop.
Duty to make monthly stock returns.
Duty to maintain a book of all Tobacco received and allow its inspection.
Duty to comply with search warrants and cooperate with enforcement officers.
obligations: Importers have an obligation to pay Municipal Duty or warehouse Tobacco.
Retail dealers have obligations regarding licensing, premises, record-keeping, and reporting.
All individuals dealing with Tobacco must adhere to import, removal, sale, and possession regulations.

key_procedures: Importation of Tobacco: Tobacco must be imported by sea and landed at prescribed places. Duty is payable upon importation or after warehousing. Warehousing is required if duty is not paid on import. Bombay is designated as a warehousing port.

Removal of Tobacco: A permit from the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium is generally required for removing Tobacco within the Town, for carrying it on thoroughfares, or for transport in small vessels. Exemptions apply for lawful importation and small personal use quantities.

Retail Sale of Tobacco: A license from the Commissioner or authorized officer is required. Sales must occur at the licensed premises, and the dealer's details must be displayed. Retail dealers must maintain stock records and submit monthly returns.

Enforcement Actions: The Commissioner or authorized officers can issue search warrants, arrest individuals, detain vehicles, and seize Tobacco. Confiscation and fines are adjudicated by Police Magistrates.
Adjudication of Confiscations and Fines: Confiscations and fines are handled by the Police Magistrate of Bombay. Goods adjudged liable to confiscation are sold under the Magistrate's warrant.
administration: Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, Officers of Customs, and Magistrates of Police for the Town of Bombay.
important_notes: The 'Town of Bombay' includes the Islands of Bombay and Colaba.
Small quantities of Tobacco not exceeding four seers for personal consumption are exempt from duty and permit requirements for removal.
Permits for Tobacco removal are only valid between sunrise and sunset.
The Act does not revive any previously repealed regulations or acts.

title: THE PARTITION OF REVENUE-PAYING ESTATES ACT, 1863
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the partition of estates paying revenue to Government in the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.
scope: Applies to all partitions of estates ordered to be made by Government officers after the passing of this Act, irrespective of the tenure of the estate. It specifically concerns revenue-paying estates in the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal. Parties entitled to partition are every recorded proprietor of a joint undivided estate paying revenue to Government, or any portion thereof.

main_sections.section_title: Future partitions to be made under provisions of Act
main_sections.description: Mandates that all future partitions of estates ordered by government officers must adhere to the provisions of this Act.
Establishes that every recorded proprietor of a joint undivided estate paying Government revenue, or any part thereof, is eligible to claim partition.

main_sections.section_title: Parties desirous of partition to apply to Collector in writing
main_sections.description: Details the process for proprietors seeking to separate their shares, requiring a written application to the Collector of the District. It also allows for multiple proprietors to apply for separation to hold their shares as a joint estate.

main_sections.section_title: Application to be signed, and certain particulars specified
main_sections.description: Specifies that the partition application must be signed by the applicant(s), state the tenure of the estate, the names and shares of co-sharers, and the desired mode of partition. Applications lacking these particulars may be rejected.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure of Collector on receipt of application
main_sections.description: Outlines the Collector's procedure upon receiving a partition application, including publishing a notification, inviting objections from non-joining proprietors, and serving notice to them. It also provides for proclamation if notice service is impracticable.

main_sections.section_title: In case of valid objection being made within time allowed, application may be refused
main_sections.description: Allows the Collector to refuse a partition application if a valid objection is raised within the prescribed time, and if there are good and sufficient reasons for refusal.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure if question of title, or of proprietary right, be raised
main_sections.description: Details the Collector's actions when a question of title or proprietary right is raised. The Collector can either decline to proceed until a competent court determines the issue, or inquire into the objection, record declarations of interests, and may refer questions to arbitration.

main_sections.section_title: Decision of Collector equivalent to decision of civil Court, and open to appeal
main_sections.description: Declares that decisions by the Collector on proprietary rights are equivalent to decisions of a civil court of first instance and are appealable. The appellate court can stay partition pending appeal.
Allows for a special appeal to the Sadr Court from decisions made by a District Court under the previous section.

main_sections.section_title: Civil Court to entertain suits only on appeal from decision of Collector
main_sections.description: Prohibits civil courts from entertaining partition suits or applications except on appeal from a Collector's decision, notwithstanding contrary provisions in other acts.
Requires the Collector to publish a notification indicating the intention to proceed with a partition after thirty days, once objections are resolved and partition is ordered.
