Improvements like wasteland reclamation or irrigation of unirrigated land may be subject to land revenue assessment after a specified period.
The Act repealed earlier legislation on land improvement loans.

title: THE EXPLOSIVES ACT, 1884
purpose: To regulate the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import and export of explosives.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import, and export of explosives. It also covers related aspects like licensing, prohibition of certain explosives, and safety measures.

key_definitions.aircraft: Any machine deriving support in the atmosphere from air reactions, including balloons, airships, kites, gliders, and flying machines.
key_definitions.carriage: Includes any means of conveying goods or passengers by land, propelled in any manner.
key_definitions.District Magistrate: In areas with a Commissioner of Police, refers to the Commissioner of Police. Includes Deputy Commissioners of Police and Additional District Magistrates.
key_definitions.explosive: Encompasses gunpowder, nitroglycerine, gun-cotton, and a wide range of other chemical compounds and mixtures, including fireworks, fuses, rockets, percussion caps, detonators, cartridges, and ammunition, used or manufactured to produce an explosion or pyrotechnic effect.
key_definitions.export: Taking explosives out of India to a place outside India by land, sea, or air.
key_definitions.import: Bringing explosives into India from a place outside India by land, sea, or air.
key_definitions.master: In relation to a vessel or aircraft, it's the person in charge or control, excluding pilots and specific port officers. For a ship's boat, it's the ship's master.
key_definitions.manufacture: Includes dividing explosives into component parts, breaking them up, unmaking them, making damaged explosives fit for use, and remaking, altering, or repairing explosives.
key_definitions.prescribed: As prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes any ship, boat, sailing vessel, or other navigation vessel, and anything made for conveyance by water.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.
Specifies the date on which the Act comes into force, to be appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules as to licensing of the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import and export of explosives.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for regulating or prohibiting the handling of explosives, requiring licenses.

main_sections.section_title: Power for Central Government to prohibit the manufacture, possession or importation of specially dangerous explosives.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to prohibit the manufacture, possession, or importation of explosives deemed too dangerous for public safety.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of manufacture, possession, sale or transport of explosives by young persons and certain other persons.
main_sections.description: Prohibits individuals under eighteen, those with past violent/moral turpitude convictions, those under peace bonds, and those whose licences were cancelled from handling explosives.

Outlines the process for granting licences for explosives, requiring the licensing authority to conduct inquiries and be satisfied about the applicant's technical know-how and experience for manufacture, or other relevant criteria for different purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules conferring powers of inspection, search, seizure, detention and removal.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to create rules for inspection, search, seizure, detention, and removal related to explosives.
Mandates reporting of accidents involving explosives.
Provides for the inquiry into accidents.
Specifies provisions for the forfeiture of explosives.

main_sections.section_title: Power to arrest without warrant persons committing dangerous offences.
main_sections.description: Authorizes arrest without a warrant for persons committing dangerous offences related to explosives.

important_rules: Manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import, and export of explosives are generally prohibited except under and in accordance with a licence granted as provided by rules (Section 5(1)).
Rules may specify the authority for granting licences, fees, application procedures, licence forms and conditions, duration of licences, appeal procedures, and exemptions (Section 5(2)).
The Central Government can prohibit the manufacture, possession, or importation of explosives deemed too dangerous for public safety (Section 6(1)).
Individuals under eighteen, those with specific criminal records, those under peace bonds, and those whose licences have been cancelled are prohibited from handling explosives (Section 6A(a)).
No person shall sell, deliver, or despatch explosives to someone they know or have reason to believe is prohibited or of unsound mind (Section 6A(b)).
Licences for manufacture require satisfaction of technical know-how and experience (Section 6B(2)(a)).
Accidents involving explosives must be notified (Section 8).
Explosives can be forfeited under certain circumstances (Section 10).

penalties: Punishment for certain offences (Section 9B).
Offences by companies are covered (Section 9C).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Central Government and designated authorities through rules made under the Act, including licensing authorities and enforcement agencies responsible for search, seizure, and detention.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through licensing, inspection, search, seizure, detention, forfeiture of explosives, and legal prosecution for offences. The Customs Act, 1962 is referenced for import prohibitions (Section 6(2)). Arrest without a warrant is possible for dangerous offences (Section 13).

rights: Right to carry on business without a licence for a certain period if already in business before the 1978 amendment, with conditions (Section 5A).
Right to appeal against refusal or revocation of a licence (implied by Section 6F).
duties: Duty to obtain a licence for the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import, or export of explosives.
Duty to comply with conditions specified in the licence.
Duty to report accidents.
Duty not to sell, deliver, or despatch explosives to prohibited individuals or those of unsound mind.
obligations: Obligation to possess technical know-how or employ persons with it for manufacturing licences (Section 6B(2)(a)).
Obligation to follow procedures prescribed by rules for applications and operations.
Obligation for masters of vessels or aircraft to comply with regulations concerning explosives on board.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for and obtaining a licence for explosives, involving an inquiry by the licensing authority (Section 6B).
Procedure for the Central Government to prohibit specific explosives through notification (Section 6).
Procedure for making, publication, and confirmation of rules (Section 18).
Procedure for inquiry into accidents (Sections 9 and 9A).
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative body, with powers to make rules, issue notifications, and appoint authorities. Licensing authorities and other designated officials administer specific provisions.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various regions of India with modifications.
Section 3, which dealt with repeals, has been removed.
The definition of 'explosive' is broad and includes various chemical substances and devices.
The Act is a precursor to or works in conjunction with other relevant legislation like the Arms Act, 1959 (Section 15) and the Explosive Substances Act, 1908.

title: THE AGRICULTURISTS' LOANS ACT, 1884
purpose: To amend and provide for the extension of the Northern India Takkavi Act, 1879, for making loans to agriculturists for relief of distress, purchase of seed or cattle, or other agricultural objects.
scope: The Act, in its entirety, extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before November 1, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. Initially, the rest of the Act extended to Uttar Pradesh, Central Provinces, Assam, Delhi, and the territories comprised in the States of Bombay, Punjab, and Ajmer. State Governments can extend the Act to other territories under their administration.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1884, and specifies its commencement date as August 1, 1884.
Defines the geographical application of the Act, initially specifying which areas it covers and allowing for extension by State Governments.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Act X of 1879, and sections 4 and 5 of Act XV of 1880
main_sections.description: This section related to the repeal of previous acts or parts thereof, but has been repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938.

main_sections.section_title: Power for State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government (or Board of Revenue/Financial Commissioner in certain states) to make rules regarding loans for agricultural purposes, such as relief of distress, purchase of seed or cattle, or other purposes connected with agriculture not covered by the Land Improvement Loans Act, 1883. Rules are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before the State Legislature.
Stipulates that loans made under the Act, along with any interest and costs, are recoverable as arrears of land-revenue from the borrower or their surety.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of joint-borrowers as among themselves
main_sections.description: Deals with situations where loans are made to multiple individuals who are jointly and severally bound. It outlines how the proportion of contribution among them is determined and evidenced by a signed statement entered upon the loan order.

important_rules: Rules can be made by the State Government or designated authorities for loans to owners and occupiers of arable land.
Loans can be granted for relief of distress, purchase of seed or cattle, or other agricultural objects not specified in the Land Improvement Loans Act, 1883.
All rules made under the Act must be published in the Official Gazette.
Every rule made by the State Government or a Board of Revenue or a Financial Commissioner under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the State Legislature.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and authorities empowered by rules made under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Loans, interest, and costs are recoverable as if they were arrears of land-revenue.

rights: Eligibility for loans for agricultural purposes under specified conditions.
duties: Repayment of loans, interest, and costs by borrowers and sureties.
obligations: Joint and several liability for repayment of the whole loan amount for joint-borrowers, with specific contributions as agreed among themselves.

key_procedures: State Government (or Board of Revenue/Financial Commissioner) makes rules regarding loans for agricultural purposes.
Loans are granted based on these rules.
If a loan is granted to joint-borrowers, a statement specifying their individual contributions is entered and signed on the loan order.
Loans, interest, and costs become due and are recoverable as arrears of land-revenue.
administration: State Government (and in some cases, Board of Revenue or Financial Commissioner).
important_notes: The Act has been subject to numerous amendments and extensions across various states and union territories over time.
Section 3, which dealt with the repeal of prior acts, has itself been repealed.
The initial scope of the Act has been significantly expanded through subsequent adaptations and notifications.

title: The Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act, 1886
purpose: To provide for the voluntary registration of certain births and deaths, for the establishment of General Registry Offices for keeping registers of certain births, deaths and marriages, and for certain other purposes. It also aims to provide for the authentication and custody of certain existing registers and to declare that copies of entries in those registers shall be admissible in evidence.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. Chapter III applies to members of races, sects or tribes to which the Indian Succession Act, 1865 applies, and to all persons professing the Christian religion. State Governments may extend Chapter III to other classes of persons.

key_definitions.sign: Includes mark, when the person making the mark is unable to write his name.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by a rule made under this Act.
key_definitions.Registrar of Births and Deaths: Means a Registrar of Births and Deaths appointed under this Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act, 1886, and states that it comes into force on a day specified by the Central Government notification.
Specifies the geographical applicability of the Act to the whole of India, excluding former Part B States.
Defines terms such as 'sign', 'prescribed', and 'Registrar of Births and Deaths'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of general registry offices and appointment of Registrars General
main_sections.description: Mandates State Governments to establish general registry offices for certified copies of registers and allows for the appointment of a Registrar General for their territories.

main_sections.section_title: Persons whose births and deaths are registrable
main_sections.description: Outlines the initial categories of individuals whose births and deaths are registrable under Chapter III, primarily those covered by the Indian Succession Act, 1865, and Christians. It also allows State Governments to extend this to other classes.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Registrar to register births and deaths of which notice is given
main_sections.description: Obligates Registrars to register births and deaths upon receiving timely and proper notice from authorized persons, with provisions for refusal if the notice is suspected to be false and specific rules for naming the father of an illegitimate child.

important_rules: Rule 1: State Governments are required to establish general registry offices and may appoint a Registrar General for their territories.
Rule 2: Registrars General must maintain indexes of all certified copies of registers sent to their office and these indexes must be open for public inspection upon payment of prescribed fees.
Rule 3: Births and deaths of members of specific races, sects, or tribes to which the Indian Succession Act, 1865 applies, and of all Christian persons, are initially registrable.
Rule 4: State Governments have the power to appoint Registrars of Births and Deaths for defined local areas or classes of persons.
Rule 5: Registrars are deemed public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.
Rule 6: Registrars must maintain an office in their designated area and attend for registration purposes as directed by the Registrar General.
Rule 7: In the absence or temporary vacancy of a Registrar, a substitute is appointed by the Registrar General or a designated judge/officer.
Rule 8: State Governments shall provide Registrars with register books and make provisions for the preservation of records.
Rule 9: Registrars must register births and deaths upon receiving notice from authorized persons within the prescribed time and manner, unless they have reason to believe the information is false.

Rule 10: Specific individuals, including parents, persons present at birth/death, household occupants, medical attendants, and those in charge of the child or who saw the deceased's body, are authorized to give notice of birth or death.

penalties: Penalty for willfully giving false information (Section 27).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Governments, Registrar Generals, and Registrars of Births and Deaths.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of Registrars, establishment of registry offices, maintenance of indexes, and potential refusal to register if information is suspected to be false.

rights: Right to inspect indexes of registered births, deaths, and marriages.
Right to obtain copies of entries in the registers upon application and payment of fees.
duties: Duty of Registrars General to establish and maintain registry offices and keep indexes.
Duty of Registrars to register births and deaths upon receiving proper notice.
Duty of State Governments to supply register books and ensure record preservation.
obligations: Obligation of authorized persons to give notice of births and deaths.
Obligation for certain classes of persons to have their births and deaths registered.

key_procedures: Procedure for registering a birth or death: An authorized person gives notice to the Registrar within the prescribed time and manner. The Registrar, if satisfied, makes an entry in the register book. If the information is suspected to be false, the Registrar may refuse to register until an order from the District Court is obtained.

Procedure for obtaining copies of entries: Interested persons can inspect indexes of registers (subject to fees) and apply for certified copies of entries from the Registrar General's office, which are admissible in evidence.
administration: State Governments and Registrar Generals of Births, Deaths and Marriages.
important_notes: This Act is intended to supplement, not replace, local laws providing for birth and death registration within particular local areas.
Copies of entries certified by the Registrar General or an authorized officer are admissible in evidence.
The Act has been extended to various territories and has seen some sections repealed or omitted over time due to subsequent legislation.

title: The Suits Valuation Act, 1887
purpose: To prescribe the mode of valuing certain suits for the purpose of determining the jurisdiction of Courts with respect thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. Part I extends to such local areas as the State Government directs. Part II came into force on July 1, 1887.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Extent and commencement of Part I
main_sections.description: Specifies that Part I shall extend to such local areas and come into force on such dates as the State Government directs.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules determining value of land for jurisdictional purposes
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for determining the value of land for jurisdictional purposes in suits mentioned in the Court-fees Act, 1870. These rules can determine the value of any class of land or interest in land and may prescribe different values for different places.

main_sections.section_title: Valuation of relief in certain suits relating to land not to exceed the value of the land
main_sections.description: Stipulates that in suits relating to land where the value has been determined by rules under section 3, the valuation for jurisdiction shall not exceed the value of the land or interest as determined by those rules.
Requires the State Government to consult the High Court before making rules under section 3, and states that a rule will take effect one month after its publication in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of section 14 of the Madras Civil Courts Act, 1873
main_sections.description: Provides for the repeal of section 14 of the Madras Civil Courts Act, 1873, in areas where rules under section 3 take effect.

main_sections.section_title: Extent and commencement of Part II
main_sections.description: States that Part II came into force on the first day of July, 1887.

main_sections.section_title: Court-fee value and jurisdictional value to be the same in certain suits
main_sections.description: Mandates that in certain suits (other than those specified in the Court-fees Act, 1870) where court-fees are payable ad valorem, the value for court-fees and jurisdiction shall be the same.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of value of certain suits by High Court
main_sections.description: Allows the High Court, with the sanction of the State Government, to direct how suits of certain classes, which cannot be satisfactorily valued, shall be treated for the purposes of court-fees and this Act.
This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1891.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where objection is taken on appeal or revision that a suit or appeal was not properly valued for jurisdictional purposes
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for entertaining objections regarding over-valuation or under-valuation of suits or appeals in appellate or revisional courts, with specific conditions and limitations to prevent undue delays and ensure merits are considered.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings pending at commencement of Part I or Part II
main_sections.description: Ensures that the Act does not affect the jurisdiction of any Court with respect to suits or appeals instituted before the commencement of Part I or Part II.

important_rules: Rule 1 (Section 3): State Governments can make rules to determine the value of land for jurisdictional purposes in specific suits related to land. These rules can define values for different classes of land or interests within a local area.
Rule 2 (Section 4): In certain suits related to land, the jurisdictional value of the relief sought cannot exceed the determined value of the land or interest.
Rule 3 (Section 5): State Governments must consult the High Court before making rules under Section 3, and such rules become effective one month after publication in the Official Gazette.

Rule 4 (Section 8): For suits where court-fees are payable ad valorem, the value for court-fees and jurisdiction must be the same, with some exceptions related to specific sections of the Court-fees Act.

Rule 5 (Section 11(1)(a)): Objections regarding improper valuation for jurisdiction will not be entertained by an Appellate Court unless taken in the Court of first instance or in the memorandum of appeal to the lower Appellate Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Governments (for making rules), High Courts (for determining value in certain cases), Appellate Courts and Courts exercising revisional jurisdiction (for handling objections on valuation).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the rules made by State Governments, the directions issued by High Courts, and the procedural provisions for appeals and revisions concerning valuation objections.

rights: Right to have suits valued according to prescribed rules for determining court jurisdiction.
Right to have objections regarding valuation handled in appellate and revisional proceedings under specific conditions.
duties: Duty of State Government to consult High Court before making valuation rules.
Duty of State Government to publish rules in Official Gazette.
Duty of parties to raise objections regarding valuation at appropriate stages of the legal proceedings.

key_procedures: Procedure for making and enforcing valuation rules: consultation with High Court, publication in Official Gazette, and a one-month waiting period before effect.

Procedure for handling valuation objections in appeals and revisions: objections must be raised at specific stages, and appellate/revisional courts must be satisfied about prejudice caused by the incorrect valuation.
administration: State Governments, with consultation from High Courts.
important_notes: The Act has been amended and extended to various territories over time, with some parts being repealed in specific regions.
Section 10 was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1891.
Section 11 significantly modifies the general rule in the Code of Civil Procedure regarding the entertainment of objections as to jurisdiction based on valuation in appeal or revision.

title: The Punjab Land-Revenue Act, 1887
purpose: To amend and declare the law in force in the Punjab with respect to the making and maintenance of records-of-rights in land, the assessment and collection of land-revenue, and other matters relating to land and the liabilities incident thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the territories for the time being administered by the Lieutenant-Governor of the Punjab, including the Pargana of Spiti. It does not affect any Regulation in force under the provisions of Statute 33 Victoria, chapter 3, section 1, in any portion of those territories, unless expressly provided by this Act.

key_definitions.estate: An area for which a separate record-of-right has been made, or which has been separately assessed to land-revenue (or would have been so assessed if the land-revenue had not been released, compounded for or redeemed), or which the Local Government may, by general rule or special order, declare to be an estate.
key_definitions.landowner: Does not include a tenant or an assignee of land-revenue, but includes a person to whom a holding has been transferred, or an estate or holding has been let in farm, under this Act for the recovery of an arrear of land-revenue or of a sum recoverable as such an arrear, under every other person not hereinbefore in this clause mentioned who is in possession of an estate or any share or portion thereof, or in the enjoyment of any part of the profits of an estate.
key_definitions.holding: A share or portion of an estate held by one landowner or jointly by two or more landowners.
key_definitions.rent: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887.
key_definitions.tenant: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887.
key_definitions.landlord: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887.
key_definitions.tenancy: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887.
key_definitions.pay: Includes, when used with reference to rent, 'deliver' and 'render'.
key_definitions.land-revenue: Includes assigned land-revenue and any sum payable in respect of land, by way of quit-rent or of commutation for service, to the Government or to a person to whom the Government has assigned the right to receive the payment.
key_definitions.arrear of land-revenue: Land-revenue which remains unpaid after the date on which it becomes payable.
key_definitions.defaulter: A person liable for an arrear of land-revenue, and includes a person who is responsible as surety for the payment of the arrear.
key_definitions.rates and cesses: Rates and cesses which are primarily payable by landowners, and includes the local rate (if any) under the Punjab Local Rates Act, 1878, the local rate (if any) under the Punjab District Boards Act, 1883 (and any fee leviable under section 33 of that Act from landowners for the use of or benefits derived from such works as are referred to in section 20, clauses (i) and (j), of that Act), any annual rate chargeable on owners of lands under section 59 of the Northern India Canal and Drainage Act, 1873, the zaildari and village-officers’ cesses, and sums payable on account of village-expenses.
key_definitions.village-cess: Includes any cess, contribution or due which is customarily leviable within an estate and is neither a payment for the use of private property or for personal services.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Punjab, including Spiti), and the provisions for its commencement through a notification by the Local Government. It also allows for the exercise of rule-making powers before the commencement date.

Repeals specified enactments mentioned in the schedule. It clarifies that rules, appointments, assessments, transfers, notifications, proclamations, conferred authorities and powers, granted farms and leases, framed or revised records-of-rights and other records, acquired rights, incurred liabilities, appointed times and places, and other things done under the repealed enactments are deemed to have been done under this Act. It also states that any reference to a repealed enactment in any enactment or document shall be construed as a reference to this Act.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'estate', 'landowner', 'holding', 'rent', 'tenant', 'landlord', 'tenancy', 'pay', 'land-revenue', 'arrear of land-revenue', 'defaulter', 'rates and cesses', and 'village-cess'.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of certain land from operation of Act
main_sections.description: Empowers the exclusion of certain land from the operation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to vary limits and alter number of tahsils, districts and divisions
main_sections.description: Grants power to the Local Government to vary limits and alter the number of tahsils, districts, and divisions.
Specifies the different classes of Revenue-officers.
Designates the Financial Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Commissioners, and Deputy, Assistant and Extra Assistant Commissioners
main_sections.description: Details the appointment of Commissioners, Deputy Commissioners, Assistant Commissioners, and Extra Assistant Commissioners.
Outlines the appointment of Tahsildars and Naib-tahsildars.
Defines the powers vested in Revenue-officers.
Establishes the superintendence and control of Revenue-officers.

main_sections.section_title: Power to distribute business and withdraw and transfer cases
main_sections.description: Grants power to distribute business and withdraw and transfer cases among Revenue-officers.
Lays down the provisions for appeals against orders made by Revenue-officers.
Specifies the time limits for filing appeals.
Allows for the review of decisions by Revenue-officers.

main_sections.section_title: Power to call for, examine and revise proceedings of Revenue-officers
main_sections.description: Grants the power to call for, examine, and revise proceedings of Revenue-officers.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules as to procedure
main_sections.description: Empowers the making of rules regarding procedure for Revenue-officers.

main_sections.section_title: Persons by whom appearances and applications may be made before and to Revenue-officers
main_sections.description: Specifies who can make appearances and applications before and to Revenue-officers.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Revenue-officer to summon persons
main_sections.description: Grants Revenue-officers the power to summon persons.
Details the procedure for serving summons.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of service of notice, order or proclamation or copy thereof
main_sections.description: Specifies the mode of service for notices, orders, proclamations, or their copies.
Describes the method of making proclamations.
Addresses the place where Revenue-officers will sit.
Deals with holidays in relation to the Act's operations.

main_sections.section_title: Discharge of duties of Collector dying or being disabled
main_sections.description: Provides for the discharge of duties when a Collector dies or becomes disabled.

main_sections.section_title: Retention of powers by Revenue-officers on transfer
main_sections.description: Allows Revenue-officers to retain their powers upon transfer.
Details the conferment of powers of Revenue-officers.

main_sections.section_title: Rules respecting kanungos, zaildars, inamdars and village-officers
main_sections.description: Empowers the making of rules concerning kanungos, zaildars, inamdars, and village-officers.
Addresses the cess levied for village officers.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on attachment or assignment of remuneration of kanungos, Zaildars, Inamdar’s and village-officers
main_sections.description: Restricts the attachment or assignment of remuneration for kanungos, zaildars, inamdars, and village-officers.
Defines the record-of-rights and the documents to be included in it.

main_sections.section_title: Making or special revision of record-of-rights
main_sections.description: Provides for the making or special revision of the record-of-rights.
Deals with the preparation and maintenance of the annual record.

main_sections.section_title: Making of that part of the annual record which relates to land-owners, assignees of revenue and occupancy tenants
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for preparing the part of the annual record concerning landowners, assignees of revenue, and occupancy tenants.

main_sections.section_title: Making of that part of the annual record which relates to other persons
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for preparing the part of the annual record concerning other persons.
Provides for the determination of disputes related to record entries.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on variation of entries in records
main_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on varying entries in records.
Deals with fees payable for mutation of records.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for neglect to report acquisition of any right referred to in section 34
main_sections.description: Specifies the penalty for failing to report the acquisition of rights mentioned in section 34.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation to furnish information necessary for the preparation of records
main_sections.description: Establishes the obligation to furnish information required for record preparation.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of the Government in mines and minerals
main_sections.description: Defines the rights of the Government in mines and minerals.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption as to ownership of forests, quarries and waste-lands
main_sections.description: Establishes presumptions regarding the ownership of forests, quarries, and waste-lands.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for infringement of rights of third parties in exercise of a right of the Government
main_sections.description: Provides for compensation for the infringement of third-party rights when the Government exercises its rights.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption in favour of entries in records-of-rights and annual records
main_sections.description: Creates a presumption in favour of the correctness of entries in records-of-rights and annual records.

main_sections.section_title: Suit for declaratory decree by person aggrieved by an entry in a record
main_sections.description: Allows a person aggrieved by an entry in a record to file a suit for a declaratory decree.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules respecting records and other matters connected therewith
main_sections.description: Grants power to make rules concerning records and related matters.

main_sections.section_title: Record-of-rights and annual records for groups of estates
main_sections.description: Deals with the preparation of records-of-rights and annual records for groups of estates.
Outlines the process of assessing land-revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Notification of intended re-assessment and instructions, as to principles of assessment
main_sections.description: Requires notification of intended re-assessment and provides instructions on assessment principles.
Specifies the method for determining the assessment of land-revenue.
Details the announcement of the determined assessment.
Provides for applications for the reconsideration of an assessment.
Covers the confirmation and duration of the land-revenue assessment.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment to remain in force till new assessment takes effect
main_sections.description: States that the current assessment remains in force until a new assessment takes effect.

main_sections.section_title: Refusal to be liable for assessment and consequence thereof
main_sections.description: Deals with the consequences of refusing to be liable for assessment.

main_sections.section_title: Distribution of the assessment of an estate over the holdings comprised therein
main_sections.description: Provides for the distribution of the assessment of an estate among the holdings within it.

main_sections.section_title: Application for amendment of the distribution of an assessment
main_sections.description: Allows for applications to amend the distribution of an assessment.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals from orders under sections 52 and 57
main_sections.description: Specifies appeals against orders made under sections 52 and 57.
Covers provisions for special assessments of land-revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Formation of waste-land into separate estates
main_sections.description: Deals with the formation of waste-land into separate estates.
Outlines measures for securing the payment of land-revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Further security for payment of land-revenue
main_sections.description: Provides for additional security for land-revenue payments.

main_sections.section_title: Orders to regulate payment of land-revenue
main_sections.description: Empowers the issuance of orders to regulate land-revenue payments.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to regulate collection, remission and suspension of land-revenue
main_sections.description: Allows for rules to regulate the collection, remission, and suspension of land-revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Costs recoverable as part of arrear
main_sections.description: States that costs incurred are recoverable as part of an arrear of land-revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Certified account to be evidence as to arrear
main_sections.description: Provides that a certified account serves as evidence of an arrear.
Details the processes for recovering arrears of land-revenue.
Introduces the concept of a writ of demand for arrears.
Allows for the arrest and detention of defaulters.

main_sections.section_title: Distress and sale of moveable property and crops
main_sections.description: Provides for the distress and sale of moveable property and crops to recover arrears.

Empowers the attachment of an estate or holding for recovery of arrears.

main_sections.section_title: Annulment of assessment of estate or holding
main_sections.description: Provides for the annulment of the assessment of an estate or holding in case of default.

main_sections.section_title: Proclamation of attachment or annulment of assessment, and consequences of the proclamation

main_sections.description: Permits proceedings against other immoveable property of a defaulter.

main_sections.section_title: Remedies open to person denying his liability for an arrear
main_sections.description: Outlines the remedies available to a person who denies liability for an arrear.

main_sections.description: Provides indemnity to Revenue-officers regarding the contents of sale proclamations.

main_sections.description: Requires the highest bidder to pay a deposit.

main_sections.description: Details the order for confirming or setting aside a sale.

main_sections.description: Identifies other sums that are recoverable as arrears of land-revenue.

main_sections.description: Extends the application of Chapter VI to sums recoverable under this Chapter.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Financial Commissioner to make rules for demarcation of boundaries and erection of survey-marks
main_sections.description: Grants the Financial Commissioner power to make rules for boundary demarcation and survey-mark erection.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Revenue-officers to define boundaries
main_sections.description: Empowers Revenue-officers to define boundaries.

main_sections.description: Addresses the cost of erecting and repairing survey-marks.

main_sections.description: Details the recovery of costs incurred by the Government for surveys and marks.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Revenue-offices to enter on land for purposes of survey and demarcation
main_sections.description: Grants Revenue-officers the power to enter land for survey and demarcation purposes.

main_sections.description: Covers surveys conducted for the preparation of records.

main_sections.section_title: Provision of flag holders and chainmen for those surveys
main_sections.description: Arranges for flag holders and chainmen for surveys.
Deals with professional surveys.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for destruction, injury or removal of survey-marks
main_sections.description: Specifies the penalty for damaging, injuring, or removing survey-marks.

main_sections.section_title: Report of destruction or removal of or injury to survey-marks
main_sections.description: Requires reporting of the destruction, removal, or injury of survey-marks.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of partitions of estates and tenancies on joint liability for revenue and rent
main_sections.description: Explains the effect of partitions on joint liability for revenue and rent.
Provides for making applications for partition.
Sets out restrictions and limitations on partitions.
Requires notice to be given of partition applications.
Allows for the addition of parties to a partition application.
Enables the absolute disallowance of a partition.
Outlines the procedure when a partition application is admitted.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of questions as to title in property to be divided
main_sections.description: Deals with the disposal of questions concerning title in property to be divided.
Covers the disposal of other questions arising during partition.

main_sections.section_title: Administration of property excluded from partition
main_sections.description: Provides for the administration of property excluded from partition.

main_sections.section_title: Distribution of revenue and rent after partition
main_sections.description: Specifies the distribution of revenue and rent after a partition.
Deals with the formal instrument of partition.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of possessions of property allotted on partition
main_sections.description: Covers the delivery of possession of property allotted through partition.
Allows for the affirmation of partitions that have been privately effected.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules as to costs of partition
main_sections.description: Empowers the making of rules regarding the costs of partition.

main_sections.section_title: Re-distribution of land according to custom
main_sections.description: Allows for the re-distribution of land according to custom.

main_sections.section_title: Officer who may be empowered to act under this Chapter
main_sections.description: Specifies the officers who can be empowered to act under the Partition Chapter.
Grants the power to refer disputes to arbitration.

main_sections.section_title: Order of reference and contents thereof
main_sections.description: Details the order of reference to arbitration and its contents.
Covers the nomination of arbitrators.
Allows parties to substitute arbitrators.

main_sections.section_title: Nomination and substitution of arbitrators by Revenue-officers
main_sections.description: Empowers Revenue-officers to nominate and substitute arbitrators.
Describes the process for appearance before arbitrators.

main_sections.section_title: Award of arbitrators and presentation thereof
main_sections.description: Deals with the award of arbitrators and its presentation.
Outlines the procedure upon the presentation of an award.
Specifies the legal effect of an arbitration award.

main_sections.section_title: Power to invest officers making records-of-rights or general re-assessments with powers of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: Allows for the investment of officers involved in record-of-rights or re-assessments with Civil Court powers.

main_sections.section_title: Control over such officers and appeals from and revision of their decrees and orders
main_sections.description: Establishes control over officers invested with Civil Court powers and procedures for appeals and revisions of their decisions.

main_sections.section_title: Power to deposit certain sums other than rent
main_sections.description: Grants the power to deposit certain sums of money, other than rent.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure in case of deposit on account of a payment due to Government
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for deposits made on account of payments due to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure in case of other deposits
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for other types of deposits.

main_sections.section_title: Orders of Civil and Criminal Courts for execution of processes against land or the produce thereof to be addressed to a Revenue-officer
main_sections.description: Specifies that orders from Civil and Criminal Courts for processes against land or its produce are to be addressed to a Revenue-officer.
Covers the attachment of assigned land-revenue.
Deals with the preservation of produce that has been attached.
Outlines the procedure for the division of produce.
Addresses village cesses.
Deals with dues payable to superior landowners.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of service for payment of land-revenue
main_sections.description: Allows for the substitution of service in lieu of land-revenue payment.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of cost of assessing assigned land-revenue
main_sections.description: Provides for the recovery of costs incurred in assessing assigned land-revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to attend within limits of estate in obedience to order of Revenue-officers
main_sections.description: Specifies the penalty for failing to attend within an estate's limits when ordered by a Revenue-officer.

main_sections.section_title: Prevention of encroachment on common lands
main_sections.description: Deals with measures to prevent encroachment on common lands.

main_sections.section_title: Papers kept by village-officers to be deemed public documents
main_sections.description: Declares that papers kept by village-officers are considered public documents.
Addresses the recovery of costs in legal proceedings under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Computation of periods limited for appeals and applications for review
main_sections.description: Specifies how periods for appeals and review applications are to be computed.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on Revenue-officers bidding at auctions or trading
main_sections.description: Prohibits Revenue-officers from bidding at auctions or engaging in trade.
Grants power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be made after previous publication
main_sections.description: Requires that rules are made only after previous publication.

main_sections.section_title: Powers exerciseable by the Financial Commissioner from time to time
main_sections.description: Specifies powers exercisable by the Financial Commissioner from time to time.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of Civil Courts, in matters within the jurisdiction of Revenue-officers
main_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters that fall within the purview of Revenue-officers.

important_rules: Rules for the making and maintenance of records-of-rights in land are to be established.
Rules for the assessment and collection of land-revenue are to be established.
Rules regarding the appointment, powers, and administrative control of Revenue-officers are to be made.
Rules governing appeals, reviews, and revisions of proceedings by Revenue-officers are to be formulated.
Rules concerning Kanungos, Zaildars, Inamdars, and Village-officers are to be made.
Rules for the demarcation of boundaries and erection of survey-marks are to be made by the Financial Commissioner.
Rules for the partition of estates and tenancies are to be established.
Rules for arbitration in land-related disputes are to be enacted.
Rules to regulate the collection, remission, and suspension of land-revenue are to be formulated.
Rules for the recovery of arrears of land-revenue are to be made.
Rules concerning the costs of partition are to be established.
Rules for the deposit of certain sums other than rent are to be made.
Rules for the preparation and maintenance of the annual record are to be established.
Rules for the prevention of encroachment on common lands are to be made.

penalties: Penalty for neglect to report acquisition of any right referred to in section 34.
Penalty for destruction, injury or removal of survey-marks.
Penalty for failure to attend within limits of estate in obedience to order of Revenue-officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue-officers, including the Financial Commissioner, Commissioners, Deputy Commissioners, Assistant Commissioners, Extra Assistant Commissioners, Tahsildars, and Naib-tahsildars.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through processes for recovery of arrears, including writ of demand, arrest and detention of defaulters, distress and sale of moveable property and crops, transfer of holding, attachment of estate or holding, annulment of assessment, sale of estate or holding, and legal proceedings as prescribed.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of Revenue-officers.
Right to apply for review of decisions by Revenue-officers.
Right to sue for a declaratory decree if aggrieved by an entry in a record.
Right of pre-emption in sales.
Remedies for persons denying liability for an arrear.
Right to deposit certain sums other than rent.
duties: Duty to report acquisition of rights as specified in section 34.
Duty to furnish information necessary for the preparation of records.
Duty to pay land-revenue by the specified date.
Duty to appear before Revenue-officers when summoned.
Duty to comply with orders of Revenue-officers, including attending within estate limits.
Duty to cooperate with surveys and demarcation activities.
obligations: Obligation to prepare and maintain records-of-rights and annual records.
Obligation to assess and collect land-revenue.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for revenue collection and recovery.
Obligation to ensure the proper demarcation of boundaries and maintenance of survey-marks.
Obligation to administer property excluded from partition.
Obligation for landowners to pay rates and cesses.

key_procedures: Procedure for making and revising records-of-rights and annual records, including determination of disputes and mutation of entries.
Procedure for assessment of land-revenue, including notification, determination, announcement, and confirmation of assessment.
Procedure for the collection of land-revenue, including processes for recovery of arrears like writ of demand, attachment, sale of property, and annulment of assessment.
Procedure for survey and demarcation of boundaries, including the erection and maintenance of survey-marks.
Procedure for partition of estates and tenancies, including application, notice, disposal of disputes, and distribution of revenue.
Procedure for arbitration of disputes, including reference, nomination of arbitrators, award, and effect thereof.
Procedure for the deposit of sums other than rent and for the execution of Civil and Criminal Court orders by Revenue-officers.
Procedure for setting aside sales of estates or holdings.
administration: The Act is administered by Revenue-officers, under the superintendence and control of the Financial Commissioner and the Local Government (Lieutenant-Governor of the Punjab).
important_notes: The Act explicitly repeals and consolidates existing land-revenue laws in the Punjab.
The Act distinguishes between 'land-revenue' and 'rates and cesses', with specific provisions for each.
The Act provides for the exclusion of Civil Court jurisdiction in matters falling under the purview of Revenue-officers.
The Act allows for the conferment of Civil Court powers on officers involved in record-making and re-assessment processes.
The commencement of the Act is subject to a notification by the Local Government with the previous sanction of the Governor General in Council.

title: THE PROVINCIAL SMALL CAUSE COURTS ACT, 1887
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to Courts of Small Causes established beyond the Presidency-towns.
scope: Applies to the whole of India except territories which were comprised in Part B States before November 1, 1956. It establishes and defines the jurisdiction, constitution, practice, procedure, and supplemental provisions for Provincial Courts of Small Causes.

key_definitions.Court of Small Causes: A Court of Small Causes constituted under this Act, and includes any person exercising jurisdiction under this Act in any such Court.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date it came into force.

Specifies what the Act does not affect, including pre-commencement proceedings, the jurisdiction of Magistrates, village-munsifs or village-panchayats, and local or special laws other than the Code of Civil Procedure.
Defines 'Court of Small Causes'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to establish Courts of Small Causes and define their local limits and place of sitting.
Provides for the appointment of a Judge to a Court of Small Causes, with the possibility of one Judge presiding over multiple courts.
Allows for the appointment of Additional Judges to Courts of Small Causes, outlining their functions and powers.

main_sections.section_title: Cognizance of suits by Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Defines the pecuniary jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes, excluding suits listed in the second schedule, and allows for enhancement by State Government order.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusive jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: States that Courts of Small Causes have exclusive jurisdiction over suits of a civil nature cognizable by them, with certain exceptions.

important_rules: Suits of a civil nature with a value not exceeding five hundred rupees are generally cognizable by a Court of Small Causes, subject to schedule exceptions.
The State Government can direct that suits up to one thousand rupees are cognizable by a specified Court of Small Causes.
Judges of multiple Courts of Small Causes can fix sitting times with the sanction of the District Court, with notice published as directed by the High Court.
If two Judges or a Judge and an Additional Judge sitting together differ on a question of law or construction affecting merits, they must refer the case to the High Court.
If they differ on other matters, the senior Judge's opinion prevails.
Registrars can be conferred jurisdiction to try suits valued up to twenty rupees.

rights: Right to institute suits of a civil nature within the specified pecuniary limits and not falling under scheduled exceptions.
duties: Ministerial officers have duties as prescribed by the Act, other enactments, and directions from the Judge.
Ministerial officers' powers and duties are regulated by rules made by the High Court.

key_procedures: Application of the Code of Civil Procedure for practice and procedure, with modifications as specified.
Trial of suits by a Registrar for suits within his conferred jurisdiction.
Admission, return, and rejection of plaints by the Registrar.
Passing of decrees by the Registrar on confession.
Execution of decrees by the Registrar.
Adjournment of cases by the chief ministerial officer.
Return of plaints in suits involving questions of title.
Appeals from certain orders of Courts of Small Causes.
Revision of decrees and orders of Courts of Small Causes.
Referral of cases to the High Court when Judges sitting together differ on questions of law or construction affecting merits.
administration: State Government (for establishment and jurisdiction limits), High Court (for rules for ministerial officers and direction on sitting times), District Court (for sanctioning sitting times for judges of multiple courts).
important_notes: The Act has been subject to numerous state amendments, particularly in Uttar Pradesh, altering pecuniary limits and provisions related to eviction suits.
The Act has been repealed in its application to specific districts and cities.
The Act has been extended to Union Territories.
The Act has been amended in its application to various states.
Certain sections have been repealed or substituted over time.

title: The Indian Reserve Forces Act, 1888
purpose: To provide for the Government, discipline and regulation of the Indian Reserve Forces.
scope: Applies to the Indian Reserve Forces, which can serve both within and beyond the limits of India. The Act also addresses the rights and duties of employers regarding persons belonging to the Reserve Forces called up for training or service.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Indian Reserve Forces Act, 1888, and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Division of Reserve Forces into Regular and Supplementary Reserves
main_sections.description: Divides the Indian Reserve Forces into two categories: the Regular Reserve and the Supplementary Reserve.
States that persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces are liable to serve both within and beyond the limits of India.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules for regulation of Reserve Forces
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules and orders for the government, discipline, and regulation of the Indian Reserve Forces. These rules are subject to parliamentary review.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of Reserve Forces to military law
main_sections.description: Makes persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces subject to military law to the same extent as persons belonging to the Regular Army, subject to any rules and orders made under section 4.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment of certain offences by persons belonging to Reserve Forces
main_sections.description: Outlines punishments for specific offenses by persons in the Reserve Forces, including failure to attend when required, failure to comply with rules, or fraudulently obtaining pay. Punishments can be awarded by court-martial or a Magistrate.

main_sections.section_title: Reinstatement in civil employ of persons belonging to Reserve Forces on termination of periods of training, muster or Army service
main_sections.description: Mandates employers to reinstate persons belonging to the Reserve Forces after their training, muster, or army service, under conditions not less favorable than before. It also provides for dispute resolution and penalties for non-compliance.

main_sections.section_title: Preservation of certain rights of persons belonging to Reserve Forces when called up for training, muster or army service
main_sections.description: Ensures that persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces called up for training, muster, or army service retain their rights under provident funds, superannuation funds, or other employee benefit schemes connected to their employment.

important_rules: Rule 1: Persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces are liable to serve both within and beyond the limits of India.
Rule 2: The Central Government can make rules for the government, discipline, and regulation of the Indian Reserve Forces. These rules must be laid before Parliament for review.
Rule 3: Persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces are subject to military law.
Rule 4: Failure to attend when required, failure to comply with rules, or fraudulently obtaining pay by members of the Reserve Forces are punishable offenses.
Rule 5: Employers must reinstate members of the Reserve Forces in their civil employment after their service, under favorable conditions.
Rule 6: Members of the Reserve Forces retain their rights to provident funds and other benefit schemes during their service.

penalties: On conviction by a court-martial: Punishment other than death, transportation, or imprisonment exceeding one year.
On conviction by a Presidency Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class: Imprisonment up to six months for a first offense, and up to one year for a subsequent offense.
Employer failure to obey reinstatement orders: Punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees, and an order to pay compensation equivalent to six months' remuneration.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts-martial, Presidency Magistrates, Magistrates of the first class, and authorities prescribed by rules made under the Act for reinstatement disputes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings and adherence to rules and orders made under the Act, including parliamentary oversight of rules and orders.

rights: Right to be reinstated in civil employment under favorable conditions after service.
Right to retain rights under provident funds and other employee benefit schemes.
Right to have reinstatement disputes resolved by a prescribed authority.
duties: Duty of persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces to attend when required, comply with rules, and serve when called upon.
Duty of employers to reinstate persons belonging to the Reserve Forces in their employment.
Duty of the Central Government to make rules for the regulation and discipline of the Reserve Forces.
obligations: Obligation for employers to reinstate personnel under conditions not less favorable than before their service.
Obligation for employers to comply with orders from the prescribed authority regarding reinstatement or compensation.
Obligation for persons in the Reserve Forces to be subject to military law.

key_procedures: Procedure for calling up members of the Indian Reserve Forces for training, muster, or army service.
Procedure for reinstatement of Reserve Forces members in civil employment, including referral to a prescribed authority in case of dispute or employer refusal.
Procedure for seeking reinstatement within two months of service termination.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules and orders for the regulation of the Reserve Forces, which are then laid before Parliament.
administration: Central Government, through powers to make rules and orders.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Lakshadweep, and Pondicherry.
Substitutions and omissions of certain words and sections have occurred due to subsequent amendments (e.g., A.O. 1950, Act 12 of 1931, Act 20 of 1983).

title: THE CHARITABLE ENDOWMENTS ACT, 1890
purpose: To provide for the vesting and administration of property held in trust for charitable purposes.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to property held or to be applied in trust for charitable purposes. The 'appropriate government' (Central or State) has jurisdiction depending on the scope of the charitable endowment.

key_definitions.charitable purpose: Includes relief of the poor, education, medical relief, and the advancement of any other object of general public utility, but does not include a purpose which relates exclusively to religious teaching or worship.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and its commencement date (October 1, 1890).
Defines 'charitable purpose' for the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and incorporation of treasurer of Charitable Endowments
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Treasurer of Charitable Endowments for India and State Governments to appoint Treasurers for their respective States. These treasurers are to be corporation soles for holding and transferring property.

Defines 'appropriate Government' as the State Government for endowments within a single State and not extending to the Central Government's executive authority, and the Central Government for all other endowments.

Allows the 'appropriate Government' to vest property held in trust for a charitable purpose in the Treasurer of Charitable Endowments, subject to agreement on the application of the property. The treasurer is entitled to title documents but not obligated to administer the property.

main_sections.section_title: Schemes for administration of property vested in the treasurer
main_sections.description: Enables the 'appropriate Government' to settle, modify, or substitute schemes for the administration of property vested in the treasurer. Such schemes supersede conflicting court decrees and are not subject to judicial questioning, provided the 'appropriate Government' was correctly identified. The wishes of the trust author are to be considered.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of applying for vesting orders and schemes
main_sections.description: Specifies who can apply for vesting orders and schemes: the persons administering an existing trust or those proposing to create one. Executors or administrators of deceased trustees are also included.

Clarifies that the treasurer acts as a bare trustee and does not administer the trust directly. They keep separate accounts for securities and apply property or income as per vesting orders or schemes. For other property, possession and management remain with the persons administering the trust.

main_sections.section_title: Annual publication of list of properties vested in treasurer
main_sections.description: Requires the treasurer to publish an annual list of vested properties and an abstract of accounts in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Limitation of functions and powers of treasurer
main_sections.description: Defines the treasurer as a sole trustee with limited powers. They can only hold or transfer property as per the Act, or in obedience to a decree or direction from the authority that vested the property. Directions can include selling or investing property.

main_sections.section_title: Provision for continuance of office of treasurer in certain contingencies
main_sections.description: Allows the 'appropriate Government' to appoint a successor treasurer if the office of the incumbent is abolished or renamed.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of property from one treasurer to another
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to direct the transfer of property vested in one treasurer to another, due to alterations in areas or appointment of new treasurers.

important_rules: The treasurer of Charitable Endowments shall act as a sole trustee and not engage in the direct administration of any trust whose property is vested in them (Section 8(1)).
The treasurer must maintain separate accounts for securities and apply property or income as per vesting orders or schemes (Section 8(2)).
For non-securities property, the treasurer must permit the administering persons to retain possession, management, and control as if the property were vested in them (Section 8(3)).
The treasurer can only transfer property vested in them under the Act, or as directed by a decree or the vesting authority (Section 10(1)).
Directions from the vesting authority can include selling or disposing of property and investing proceeds (Section 10(2)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The 'appropriate Government' (Central or State) is the primary authority for vesting orders, schemes, and directions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through vesting orders and schemes settled by the 'appropriate Government'. The Uttar Pradesh amendment (Section 6-A) provides for the State Government to modify or substitute schemes if property is wasted or mal-administered.

rights: The Treasurer of Charitable Endowments has the right to hold and transfer movable or immovable property under the Act.
The Treasurer is entitled to all documents of title relating to property vested in them (Section 4(2)).
Persons administering a trust have the right to possession, management, and control of property not consisting of securities, as if it were vested in them (Section 8(3)).
duties: The treasurer must apply property or income according to vesting orders or schemes (Section 8(2)).
The treasurer must cause an annual publication of a list of vested properties and accounts in the Official Gazette (Section 9).
The treasurer must act only as a sole trustee and not administer trusts directly (Section 8(1)).
obligations: The treasurer must transfer property only as per the Act, a decree, or a direction from the vesting authority (Section 10(1)).
When divested of property, the treasurer must ensure it vests in the persons administering the trust on the same trusts (Section 10(3)).

key_procedures: Application for vesting orders and schemes: Made by the persons administering an existing trust or those intending to create one (Section 6).

Settlement of administration schemes: The 'appropriate Government' can settle a scheme for property administration on application and with concurrence, potentially appointing administrators other than the treasurer (Section 5).
Modification or substitution of schemes: The 'appropriate Government' can modify or substitute existing schemes (Section 5(2)).
Publication of vested property lists: The treasurer must publish annual lists and account abstracts (Section 9).
Directions for property transfer/disposal: The vesting authority can direct the treasurer to sell, dispose of, or invest property (Section 10(2)).
administration: The administration of property vested under this Act is managed through schemes settled by the 'appropriate Government' and administered by persons appointed in those schemes, with the treasurer acting as a bare trustee.
important_notes: The Act has been amended and extended to various regions and states over time.
Certain provisions have been omitted or superseded.
The Act does not apply to any wakf to which the Wakf Act, 1954 applies.
The Uttar Pradesh amendment (Section 6-A) allows the State Government to intervene if property is being wasted or mal-administered.

title: The Moorshedabad Act, 1891
purpose: To confirm and give effect to an Indenture made between the Secretary of State for India in Council and the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, concerning the maintenance of his position, dignity, and property.
scope: This Act applies to the Secretary of State for India in Council and the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, and his successors, within British India. It specifically deals with immoveable property associated with the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad and the financial arrangements for his maintenance and dignity.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Moorshedabad Act, 1891, and that it shall come into force immediately upon its enactment.
This section confirms the indenture made on March 12, 1891, between the Secretary of State and the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad.

This section empowers the Governor General in Council to add immoveable property to the schedules annexed to the indenture, upon the written request of the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, for the purpose of maintaining his position and dignity. It also outlines the procedure for making such additions, including notification and publication requirements.

main_sections.section_title: Limitation for claims to scheduled immoveable property
main_sections.description: This section sets a limitation of sixty years for acquiring rights to scheduled immoveable property by adverse possession or assertion of title, if such right has not accrued before the passing of the Act.

This section states that all property, moveable and immoveable, mentioned in the indenture or its schedules, shall descend and be enjoyed perpetually by the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad for the time being, subject to the provisions of the indenture.

main_sections.section_title: Relief from stamp and registration laws
main_sections.description: This section provides that the indenture shall be admissible in evidence and have the same effect as if it had been duly stamped and registered, irrespective of stamp and registration laws.

important_rules: The indenture between the Secretary of State and the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, dated March 12, 1891, is confirmed and given effect by this Act.
The Governor General in Council may, on the request of the Nawab Bahadoor, add immoveable property to the schedules of the indenture for the maintenance of the Nawab's position and dignity.
Claims to scheduled immoveable property by adverse possession or assertion of title require at least sixty years of existence if the right has not accrued before the Act's enactment.
All property covered by the indenture or its schedules will descend and be enjoyed perpetually by the current Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad.
The indenture is deemed to be duly stamped and registered for all legal purposes, providing relief from relevant laws.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Governor General in Council (for additions to schedules), and impliedly the Courts for general enforcement of the Act and the indenture.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through confirmation of the indenture, provisions for its amendment, and establishing legal standing and limitations regarding property claims.

rights: The Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad for the time being has the right to possess and enjoy the property mentioned in the indenture and its schedules perpetually.
The Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad for the time being has the right to request additions to the scheduled immoveable property for the maintenance of his position and dignity.
duties: The Nawab Bahadoor, his heirs, and successors are bound by the provisions of the indenture.
The Nawab Bahadoor has a duty to maintain his position and dignity as stipulated in the indenture.
obligations: The Secretary of State has an obligation to uphold the confirmed indenture.
The Governor General in Council has an obligation to follow the procedures outlined for adding property to the schedules.

key_procedures: Procedure for adding immoveable property to the indenture schedules: 1. Written request from the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad. 2. Discretionary decision by the Governor General in Council. 3. Notification published in the Gazette of India. 4. Prior publication as required by Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1887.
Procedure for resolving claims to scheduled immoveable property: Claims must have accrued before the Act's passage, or adverse possession/assertion of title must have existed for sixty years.
administration: The Governor General in Council (for administrative decisions related to schedule additions) and the Secretary of State for India in Council (as a party to the indenture).
important_notes: The Act confirms an indenture made on March 12, 1891, between the Secretary of State and the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, resolving historical claims and establishing future arrangements.
The historical context involves complex financial matters, debts of previous Nawabs, and the devolution of titles and property.
The Act effectively transfers the rights and responsibilities associated with the Nawab Nazim of Bengal, Behar, and Orissa to the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, with a revised scope and provisions.
The Act ensures that the indenture is legally binding and effective by overriding standard stamp and registration laws.

title: The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891
purpose: To amend the Law of Evidence with respect to Bankers’ books, allowing for their use as evidence in legal proceedings.
scope: Extends to the whole of India, with provisions applicable to companies, corporations, partnerships, individuals carrying on banking business, and post office savings banks or money order offices. It covers legal proceedings where evidence is or may be given, including arbitrations and investigations under the Code of Criminal Procedure or other laws for evidence collection.

key_definitions.company: As defined in section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, including foreign companies.
key_definitions.corporation: Any body corporate established by law in India, including the Reserve Bank of India, State Bank of India, and subsidiary banks.
key_definitions.bank and banker: Includes companies or corporations carrying on banking, partnerships or individuals to whose books the Act's provisions are extended, and any post office savings bank or money order office.
key_definitions.bankers' books: Ledgers, day-books, cash-books, account books, and all other records used in the ordinary business of the bank, whether in written form, micro film, magnetic tape, or any other mechanical or electronic data retrieval mechanism, onsite or offsite.
key_definitions.legal proceeding: Any proceeding or inquiry where evidence is or may be given, an arbitration, or an investigation/inquiry for evidence collection by a police officer or authorized person.
key_definitions.the Court: The person or persons before whom a legal proceeding is held or taken.
key_definitions.Judge: A Judge of a High Court Division.
key_definitions.trial: Any hearing before the Court at which evidence is taken.
key_definitions.certified copy: A true copy of an entry in a bank's books, with specific certificates, including those for electronic records and printouts.

main_sections.description: Names the Act and specifies its territorial application.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'company', 'corporation', 'bank', 'banker', 'bankers' books', 'legal proceeding', 'Court', 'Judge', 'trial', and 'certified copy'.
Details the specific conditions and certificates required for printouts of electronic data to be considered valid evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Power to extend provisions of Act
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to extend the Act's provisions to the books of partnerships or individuals carrying on banking business.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of proof of entries in bankers’ books
main_sections.description: Specifies that certified copies of entries in bankers' books are prima facie evidence in legal proceedings, admissible to the same extent as the original entry.

main_sections.section_title: Case in which officer of bank not compellable to produce books
main_sections.description: States that bank officers are not compellable to produce bank books or appear as witnesses in legal proceedings to which the bank is not a party, unless ordered by the Court or Judge for special cause.

main_sections.section_title: Inspection of books by order of Court or Judge
main_sections.description: Empowers the Court or Judge to order inspection and copying of entries in bankers' books or direct the bank to produce certified copies.
Deals with the discretion of the Court or Judge regarding costs of applications and actions taken under the Act, including payment by the bank in case of fault or delay.

main_sections.section_title: Order of court to be construed to be order made by specified officer
