administration: Central Government (through various departments and authorized officers, including the Collector and Commissioner).
important_notes: The Act has ceased to have effect in relation to ancient and historical monuments and archaeological sites and remains declared to be of national importance by or under Act 24 of 1958.
The Act has been repealed in its application to certain regions (e.g., Bellary District, Maharashtra) and amended in others (e.g., Mysore, Rajasthan).
The Act now applies to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
Compulsory purchase under Section 10 is restricted for monuments forming part of a dwelling-house, unless the owner is willing or the monument is in danger of destruction, injury, or neglect.

title: THE INDIAN PORTS ACT, 1908
purpose: To consolidate the enactments relating to ports and port-charges.
scope: The Act extends to ports mentioned in the first schedule and parts of navigable rivers and channels leading to them, and to other ports or parts of navigable rivers or channels to which the Government extends it. Specific sections may have a more limited application. It applies to vessels and aircraft making use of ports, and to port officials.

key_definitions.Magistrate: A person exercising powers under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
key_definitions.master: In relation to any vessel or aircraft, the person having charge or control of it (excluding a pilot or harbour-master).
key_definitions.pilot: A person authorized by the Government to pilot vessels.
key_definitions.port: Includes any part of a river or channel where the Act is in force.
key_definitions.ton: As determined by rules under section 74 of the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, for measuring gross tonnage.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes anything made for conveyance mainly by water.
key_definitions.major port: A port declared as such by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Government: For major ports, and for specific purposes in other ports (making rules under section 6(1)(p), appointing and controlling port health officers), it means the Central Government; otherwise, it means the State Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial and subject matter extent, including how it can be extended to other ports.

Specifies exemptions from the Act, including vessels of the Central or State Government, foreign princes or states, and not affecting customs laws or private property rights unless expressly provided.
Defines key terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to extend or withdraw the Act or certain portions thereof
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to extend or withdraw the Act, or specific sections, from any port or part of a navigable river or channel through notification. It also details how limits of such areas are defined.
Empowers the Government to alter the limits of any port where the Act is in force, with notification and clear description of the new limits.

Authorizes the Government to make rules for various purposes related to the safe and efficient operation of ports, including vessel movement, berthing, ballast discharge, and fees for services and moorings.
Provides for the appointment of a conservator for a port.

main_sections.section_title: Raising or removal of wreck impeding navigation within limits of port
main_sections.description: Deals with the removal of wrecks that obstruct navigation within a port.
Empowers the levy of port-dues.

main_sections.section_title: Distraint and sale on refusal to pay port-charges
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for distraint and sale of property if port-charges are not paid.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for disobedience to rules and orders of the Government
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for violating rules and orders made under the Act.
Relates to maritime security provisions.

important_rules: Rules can be made by the Government for regulating vessel entry, exit, and movement speed and manner within ports (Section 6(1)(a)).
Rules can be made for regulating berths, stations, and anchorages for vessels (Section 6(1)(b)).
Rules can be made for the proper rigging and placement of vessel equipment like anchors and spars (Section 6(1)(c), (d)).
Rules for regulating vessels while taking in or discharging passengers, ballast, or cargo (Section 6(1)(e)).
Rules for keeping passages free within ports and marking out such spaces (Section 6(1)(f)).
Rules for regulating anchoring, fastening, mooring, and unmooring of vessels (Section 6(1)(g)).
Rules for regulating the use of mooring buoys, chains, and other moorings (Section 6(1)(i)).
Port-dues are to be levied (Section 33).
Masters must report arrival of vessels (Section 39).

penalties: Penalty for disobedience to rules and orders of the Government (Section 54).
Penalties for evading payment of port-charges (Section 45).
Penalties for specific offenses like injuring buoys, beacons, moorings, improperly discharging ballast, etc., as detailed in various sections.
Penalties for pilots disobeying provisions related to hoisting vessel numbers (Section 53).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (Central and State, depending on the context) and port officials like the conservator and health officer are empowered to enforce the Act and its rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes imposing penalties, recovering expenses and damages, distraint and sale of property for unpaid charges, and prosecution for offenses as outlined in Chapter VII (Provisions with respect to Penalties).

rights: Right of property and other private rights are generally preserved unless expressly provided otherwise (Section 2(ii)).
duties: Masters have a duty to report vessel arrivals (Section 39).
Masters have a duty to hoist the number of their vessel (Section 51).
Masters have a duty to take orders to extinguish fire (Section 28).
Port officials have duties related to port safety, navigation, and health (e.g., Sections 7, 8, 17).
Authorities exercising jurisdiction in ports have duties to cooperate in defence manoeuvres and act in emergencies (Sections 68A, 68B).
obligations: Obligations to pay port-dues and other charges (Chapter V).
Obligations to comply with rules and orders made under the Act (Chapter IV and Section 54).
Obligations regarding the prevention and extinguishing of fire on vessels (Section 16, 28).

key_procedures: Procedure for extending or withdrawing the Act to ports through notification (Section 4).
Procedure for the Government to alter port limits (Section 5).
Procedure for making port-rules by the Government (Section 6).
Procedure for removal of obstructions within port limits and recovery of expenses (Sections 10, 11).
Procedure for raising or removal of wreck impeding navigation (Section 14).
Procedure for levy and collection of port-dues and other charges, including distraint and sale for non-payment (Chapter V, Sections 33-48).
Procedure for trial of offenses and recovery of penalties (Chapter VII, Sections 55-61).
administration: The administration of the Act involves the Central Government and State Governments, depending on the specific provisions and type of port (major or other). Port officials like conservators and health officers also play a significant administrative role.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to vessels of the Central Government, State Government, or foreign war vessels, nor does it affect customs laws or private property rights beyond what is expressly stated (Section 2).
Sections 31 and 32 have a more limited application and are only effective in ports to which they have been specifically extended by the Government (Section 1(3)).
The definition of 'Government' distinguishes between Central and State Government depending on the context and the type of port (Section 3(9)).
The Act has been amended by various state and central acts over time.
Specific provisions apply to aircraft making use of ports (Section 3(2)).

title: THE INDIAN MUSEUM ACT, 1910
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the Indian Museum.
scope: The Act applies to the Indian Museum and its collections. It establishes the Trustees of the Indian Museum, defines their powers and duties, and outlines procedures for managing the museum's property, collections, and staff. It also grants the Central Government oversight and rule-making authority.

key_definitions.The Trustees: Refers to the Trustees of the Indian Museum, a body corporate established by the Act.
key_definitions.public servants: Officers and servants appointed under this Act are deemed to be public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Indian Museum Act, 1910, and states that it comes into force on a date to be notified by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of the Trustees of the Indian Museum
main_sections.description: Establishes the Trustees of the Indian Museum as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It lists the ex-officio and nominated members of the Trustees and specifies their term of office and provision for authorized representatives.

main_sections.section_title: Minimum number of Trustees and quorum
main_sections.description: Specifies that the powers of the Trustees can only be exercised when there are at least six members, and the quorum for meetings is not less than four members.
Details the circumstances under which a nominated Trustee's office may become vacant and the authority's power to nominate a replacement.

main_sections.section_title: Property vested in or placed under the control of the Trustees
main_sections.description: States that all property held by the previous Trustees vests in the new Trustees and outlines their power to expend capital on the maintenance, improvement, and enlargement of the museum's collections. It also grants them exclusive possession and control of the scheduled land and buildings, except for areas designated for the Geological Survey of India.

main_sections.section_title: Power to Trustees to exchange, sell and destroy articles in collections
main_sections.description: Grants the Trustees the power to loan, exchange, sell duplicates, present duplicates to other museums in India, and remove/destroy articles from the collections, subject to bye-laws.

main_sections.section_title: Power to Trustees to make bye-laws
main_sections.description: Empowers the Trustees to make bye-laws with the previous sanction of the Central Government for the execution of their trust. It lists specific areas for which bye-laws can be made, including meetings, minute-books, catalogues, lending, exchange, sale, presentation, removal, destruction of articles, and general management. It also mandates that bye-laws are laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Trustees to appoint officers and servants
main_sections.description: Allows the Trustees to appoint necessary officers and servants and determine their functions, with their recruitment and conditions of service regulated by rules made under the Act.
Requires the Trustees to submit their budget for the next financial year to the Central Government for approval by a specified date.
Mandates the Trustees to submit an annual report on their activities and audited accounts to the Central Government and to publish them for general information.

main_sections.section_title: Collections of Asiatic Society to be kept distinguished in the Museum
main_sections.description: Requires the Trustees to mark and preserve articles from the former collections of the Asiatic Society of Bengal and any additions thereto, with provisions for inventories and mutual delivery of signed copies.

main_sections.section_title: Articles received in exchange or purchased and moneys realised from sale to be held on trust
main_sections.description: Specifies that articles acquired through exchange or purchase, and moneys from sales, are to be held on trust with powers and declarations corresponding to those in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions to Trustees
main_sections.description: States that the Trustees shall be bound by directions on questions of policy issued by the Central Government, with an opportunity for the Trustees to express their views beforehand. The Central Government's decision on whether a question is of policy is final.

main_sections.section_title: Officers under Act to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares that all officers and servants appointed under the Act are to be considered public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Power to Trustees to keep collections not belonging to them
main_sections.description: Allows the Trustees, with the Central Government's sanction, to assume custody and administration of collections not belonging to them, subject to approved conditions and prescribed rules. Such collections do not become Government property if the trust is determined.

main_sections.section_title: Power to Trustees to part with certain property in their possession
main_sections.description: Permits the Trustees, subject to Central Government approval, to deliver possession of property described in the schedule to a person appointed by the Government.

Grants the Central Government the power to make rules, in consultation with the Trustees, to carry out the Act's purposes. These rules can cover recruitment and service conditions of staff, maintenance and audit of accounts, custody and administration of collections, and conditions for parting with property. Rules are to be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Property in collections on determination of trust
main_sections.description: Deals with the disposition of property in the collections if the trust is determined.

important_rules: The Trustees must manage the museum's property, including collections, for the purposes of the museum. (Section 6)
The Trustees have the power to loan, exchange, sell duplicates, present duplicates to other museums in India, and remove/destroy articles from the collections, subject to bye-laws. (Section 7)
Bye-laws made by the Trustees require the previous sanction of the Central Government and must be consistent with the Act. (Section 8)
Officers and servants appointed under the Act are considered public servants. (Section 13)
The Trustees must submit an annual budget for approval by the Central Government. (Section 10)
The Trustees must submit an annual report of activities and audited accounts to the Central Government and publish them. (Section 10A)
The Trustees must keep collections formerly belonging to the Asiatic Society of Bengal distinctly marked and preserved. (Section 11)
Articles received in exchange or purchased, and proceeds from sales, are held on trust. (Section 12)
The Trustees must follow directions on questions of policy issued by the Central Government. (Section 12A)
The Central Government can make rules to carry out the Act's purposes, covering aspects like staff, accounts, and property management. (Section 15A)

penalties: The Act does not explicitly detail penalties for violations. However, as officers and servants are deemed public servants (Section 13), they would be subject to the provisions of the Indian Penal Code for misconduct.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and the Trustees of the Indian Museum.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Central Government enforces the Act through its power to approve bye-laws and rules, issue directions on policy, and appoint auditors. The Trustees enforce the Act through their management of the museum, appointment of staff, and adherence to bye-laws and rules.

rights: The Trustees have the right to acquire and hold property, enter into contracts, and perform acts necessary for the museum's purposes. (Section 2(2))
The Trustees have the power to manage and control the museum's property and collections. (Sections 6, 7, 8)
The Trustees have the power to appoint officers and servants. (Section 9)
The Trustees have the right to receive directions on policy from the Central Government. (Section 12A)
duties: The Trustees have a duty to manage the museum's property and collections for the stated purposes. (Section 6)
The Trustees have a duty to submit an annual budget for approval. (Section 10)
The Trustees have a duty to submit an annual report and accounts and to publish them. (Section 10A)
The Trustees have a duty to keep collections of the Asiatic Society distinguished. (Section 11)
The Trustees must be bound by directions on questions of policy from the Central Government. (Section 12A)
obligations: The Trustees are obligated to operate as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. (Section 2(2))
The Trustees are obligated to ensure a minimum number of members and quorum for meetings. (Section 3)
The Trustees are obligated to have their bye-laws sanctioned by the Central Government. (Section 8(1))
The Trustees are obligated to ensure that officers and servants' recruitment and service conditions are regulated by rules. (Section 9(2))

key_procedures: Appointment of Trustees: Ex-officio and nominated members are constituted as the Trustees. Vacancies in nominated positions are filled by the nominating authority. (Section 2, 4)
Making Bye-laws: Trustees can make bye-laws with Central Government sanction, which are then published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament. (Section 8)
Appointment of Staff: Trustees appoint officers and servants as necessary, with recruitment and service conditions governed by rules. (Section 9)
Budget Submission: Trustees submit the annual budget to the Central Government for approval by a specified date. (Section 10)
Annual Reporting: Trustees submit an annual report and accounts to the Central Government and publish them. (Section 10A)
Issuing Policy Directions: The Central Government can issue directions on policy to the Trustees, after providing them an opportunity to express views. (Section 12A)
Making Rules: The Central Government can make rules to carry out the Act's purposes, with rules to be laid before Parliament. (Section 15A)
administration: The Trustees of the Indian Museum, overseen by the Central Government.
important_notes: Certain ex-officio Trustees can authorize a person to attend meetings with the Chairman's approval if they are unable to attend. (Section 2(1) proviso)
The Central Government has the power to make rules that can modify or annul bye-laws. (Section 8(3))
Collections kept by the Trustees under Section 14 (not belonging to them) do not become Government property if the trust is determined. (Section 14 proviso)
The Act was amended in 1960 and 1983, affecting provisions related to the constitution of Trustees, quorum, appointment of officers, and bye-law making process.

title: THE OFFICIAL TRUSTEES ACT, 1913
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law constituting the office of Official Trustee.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The act governs the appointment, powers, duties, and liabilities of the Official Trustee and Deputy Official Trustees.

key_definitions.Government: In relation to a State, the State Government and, in relation to a Union territory, the Central Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of commencement.
Defines terms used in the Act, such as 'Government' and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Extent of jurisdiction of High Court
main_sections.description: Specifies the extent of the High Court's jurisdiction concerning proceedings under this Act or the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, while also preserving the jurisdiction of district courts.
Establishes the appointment of an Official Trustee for each State and outlines the qualifications required for such an appointment.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and powers of Deputy Official Trustee
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to appoint Deputy Official Trustees to assist the Official Trustee and defines their powers, duties, and qualifications.

main_sections.section_title: Official Trustee to be corporation sole to have perpetual succession and official seal, and to sue and be sued in his corporate name
main_sections.description: Declares the Official Trustee as a corporation sole with perpetual succession, an official seal, and the ability to sue and be sued in his corporate name.

main_sections.section_title: General powers and duties of Official Trustee
main_sections.description: Outlines the general powers and duties of the Official Trustee, including acting as an ordinary trustee, accepting appointments by the court, and the conditions under which a trust may be declined.

main_sections.section_title: Official Trustee may with consent be appointed trustee of settlement by grantor
main_sections.description: Allows the Official Trustee to be appointed as a trustee of a settlement by the grantor, provided the Official Trustee consents and the instrument is duly executed.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Official Trustee as trustee by will
main_sections.description: Details the process for appointing the Official Trustee as a trustee under a will, including notification to the Official Trustee and the execution of an instrument of transfer.

main_sections.section_title: Power of High Court to appoint Official Trustee to be trustee of property
main_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power to appoint the Official Trustee as a trustee of property upon application, subject to certain conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of private trustees to appoint Official Trustee to be trustee of property
main_sections.description: Enables private trustees, beneficiaries, or surviving trustees to appoint the Official Trustee in their place, with the Official Trustee's consent.

main_sections.section_title: Executor or administrator may pay to Official Trustee legacy, share, etc., of minor or lunatic
main_sections.description: Permits executors or administrators to transfer gifts, legacies, or shares of assets belonging to a minor or lunatic to the Official Trustee.

main_sections.section_title: Official Trustee not to be required to give bond or security
main_sections.description: Exempts the Official Trustee from the requirement of providing any bond or security upon appointment and from verifying petitions beyond their signature.

main_sections.section_title: Entry of Official Trustee not to constitute notice of a trust
main_sections.description: States that the Official Trustee's name appearing in company books does not constitute notice of a trust, and companies cannot object to registering the Official Trustee's name.
Establishes the Government's liability to make good sums required to discharge liabilities that a private trustee would be personally liable for, with certain exceptions.
Deals with the imposition and collection of fees for the services rendered by the Official Trustee.
Specifies how the collected fees are to be utilized.

main_sections.section_title: Auditors to be appointed to examine Official Trustee's accounts, etc., and to report to Government
main_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of auditors to examine the Official Trustee's accounts and report to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Auditor's power to summon witnesses and to call for documents
main_sections.description: Grants auditors the power to summon witnesses and demand the production of documents during their examination of accounts.

main_sections.section_title: Costs of audit, etc., how paid
main_sections.description: Defines the procedure for paying the costs associated with the audit and related processes.

main_sections.section_title: Right of beneficiary to inspection and copies of accounts
main_sections.description: Confers upon beneficiaries the right to inspect and obtain copies of the accounts maintained by the Official Trustee.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to Government of accumulations in the hands of Official Trustee
main_sections.description: Allows for the transfer of any accumulations in the hands of the Official Trustee to the Government under specific circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of proceeding by claimant to recover money so transferred
main_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for claimants to recover money that has been transferred to the Government under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of High Court to make orders in respect of property vested in Official Trustee
main_sections.description: Grants the High Court the authority to make orders concerning property that has vested in the Official Trustee.

main_sections.section_title: Who may apply for order under Act
main_sections.description: Specifies the individuals or entities who are eligible to apply for orders under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Order of Court to have effect of a decree
main_sections.description: States that any order passed by a Court under this Act shall have the force of a decree.
Confers general administrative powers upon the Official Trustee.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of trust property by Official Trustee to original trustee or any other trustee
main_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of trust property by the Official Trustee back to the original trustee or any other appointed trustee.
Grants the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Contains provisions that save certain existing laws or situations from the purview of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision regarding certain Official Trustees affected by States’ reorganisation
main_sections.description: Addresses special provisions concerning Official Trustees whose roles are affected by the reorganisation of States.

important_rules: The Official Trustee can decline to accept any trust, either absolutely or on specific conditions.
The Official Trustee shall not accept any trust under a composition or scheme of arrangement for creditors, or any estate known or believed to be insolvent.
The Official Trustee shall not accept any trust for a religious purpose or any trust involving the management or carrying on of any business, except as provided by rules.
The Official Trustee shall not administer the estate of a deceased person unless expressly appointed sole executor and sole trustee under the will.
The Official Trustee shall always be the sole trustee and cannot be appointed as a trustee along with any other person.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: High Court, District Courts, Government, and appointed auditors.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders, audits, and the statutory powers vested in the Official Trustee and other authorities.

rights: Right to sue and be sued in the corporate name.
Right to have perpetual succession and an official seal.
Right to the same powers, duties, and liabilities as any other trustee, subject to the Act.
Right to be exempt from giving bond or security.
Right for beneficiaries to inspect and obtain copies of accounts.
duties: To act as an ordinary trustee or be appointed by a competent court.
To discharge duties and exercise powers subject to the Act and rules.
To manage trust property upon appointment.
To maintain accounts and be subject to audit.
To be accountable to the Court and beneficiaries.
obligations: To act with reasonable diligence and care.
To adhere to the terms of the trust instrument and the provisions of the Act.
To provide accounts and allow inspection by beneficiaries.
To be subject to the control and orders of the Court.

key_procedures: Appointment of Official Trustee by the Government for each State, with specific qualifications required (e.g., seven years as an advocate or attorney, or ten years in judicial service, or five years as Deputy Official Trustee).
Appointment of Deputy Official Trustees with specified qualifications (e.g., three years as an advocate, attorney, or member of the judicial service).
Appointment of Official Trustee by grantors in settlement instruments, requiring the Official Trustee's consent and due execution of the instrument.
Appointment of Official Trustee by will, requiring executors or administrators to notify the Official Trustee and execute an instrument of transfer upon consent.
Appointment of Official Trustee by the High Court upon application if there is no willing or capable trustee, requiring the Official Trustee's consent.
Appointment of Official Trustee by private trustees and beneficiaries through a written instrument, with the Official Trustee's consent.
Transfer of legacies, shares, or gifts of minors or lunatics to the Official Trustee by executors, administrators, or existing trustees, with the Official Trustee's consent.
Procedure for claimants to recover money transferred to the Government from the Official Trustee's accumulations.
administration: The Government (State Government or Central Government depending on the context of a State or Union Territory) and the Official Trustee's office.
important_notes: The Act has been amended in its application to specific regions like Bengal and extended to areas like Berar and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
Certain sections have been repealed or omitted over time.
The provisions of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, are saved.

title: THE WHITE PHOSPHORUS MATCHES PROHIBITION ACT, 1913
purpose: To prohibit the importation, manufacture, and sale of matches made with white phosphorus.
scope: Applies to the whole of India, excluding territories that were formerly Part B States before November 1, 1956. It prohibits the use, manufacture, and sale of matches containing white phosphorus.

key_definitions.white phosphorus: The substance commonly known as white or yellow phosphorus.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and its commencement date. Section 6 has a delayed commencement.
Defines 'white phosphorus'.
This section was repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of use of white phosphorus in manufacture of matches
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of white phosphorus in the manufacture of matches and specifies penalties for contravention.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Inspector of Factories to take samples of material used in manufacture
main_sections.description: Empowers Inspectors of Factories to take samples of materials used in match manufacturing for analysis and penalizes refusal to allow such sampling.
Prohibits the sale, offering for sale, or possession for sale of matches made with white phosphorus. Specifies penalties for contravention, including forfeiture of such matches.

important_rules: Rule 1: No person shall use white phosphorus in the manufacture of matches.
Rule 2: No person shall sell, offer for sale, or have in possession for sale any matches made with white phosphorus.
Rule 3: Manufacturers of matches must allow Inspectors of Factories to take samples of materials used in manufacture for analysis.
Rule 4: If a sample is taken, the manufacturer may require the inspector to divide it into two parts and hand one part over to them.
Rule 5: Refusing an Inspector of Factories access to materials for sampling is punishable.

penalties: Fine up to two hundred rupees for using or permitting the use of white phosphorus in match manufacturing (Section 4(2)).
Fine up to two hundred rupees for refusing an Inspector of Factories to take samples (Section 5(2)).
Forfeiture of matches made with white phosphorus, to be destroyed or dealt with as directed by a Magistrate, for contravention of sale prohibition (Section 6(2)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspector of Factories (for sampling and enforcement of manufacturing rules), Presidency Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate, or Magistrate of the first class (for contraventions of sale prohibition and forfeiture).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, taking samples for analysis, and legal proceedings leading to fines or forfeiture of prohibited goods.

rights: Manufacturers have the right to have a sample divided and one part delivered to them (Section 5(1) Proviso).
duties: Every person who manufactures matches has a duty to allow Inspectors of Factories to take samples of materials used in manufacture (Section 5(1)).
obligations: Obligation not to use white phosphorus in the manufacture of matches (Section 4(1)).
Obligation not to sell, offer for sale, or possess for sale matches made with white phosphorus (Section 6(1)).

key_procedures: Sampling Procedure: An Inspector of Factories may take samples of materials used in match manufacture. The manufacturer can request the sample to be divided into two parts, with one part being handed over to them (Section 5).
Enforcement of Sale Prohibition: For contraventions of the sale prohibition, a complaint can be made to a Magistrate who may order forfeiture of the matches (Section 6(2)).
administration: The Act is administered through the enforcement of its prohibitions by factory inspectors and judicial magistrates.
important_notes: Section 3 was repealed and no longer applies.
The scope of the Act was amended regarding Part B States.
Section 6 (Prohibition of sale) came into force one year after the commencement of the Act (July 1, 1914).

title: The Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914
purpose: To prevent the introduction into India and the transport from one province to another of any insect, fungus or other pest which is or may be destructive to crops.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the import and transport of insects and articles likely to cause infection to crops, as well as to crops themselves. It also covers actions by the Central Government and State Governments in relation to these matters.

key_definitions.crops: Includes all agricultural or horticultural crops and all trees, bushes or plants.
key_definitions.import: Means the bringing or taking by sea, land or air across any customs frontier as defined by the Central Government.
key_definitions.infection: Means infection by any insect, fungus or other pest injurious to a crop.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914' and states its extent across the whole of India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'crops', 'import', and 'infection'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to regulate or prohibit the import of articles likely to infect
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prohibit or regulate the import into India, or any part thereof, of any article or class of articles, or of insects generally or any class of insects, that are likely to cause infection to crops. It also allows for the levy of fees for permits and inspections.

States that notifications issued under section 3 operate as if issued under section 19 of the Sea Customs Act, 1878, granting customs officers powers similar to those for regulated or prohibited imports.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to regulate or prohibit transport from State to State of insects or articles likely to infect
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to prohibit or regulate the export from a State or transport from one State to another of any article or class of articles likely to cause infection to crops, or of insects.

main_sections.section_title: Refusal to carry article of which transport is prohibited
main_sections.description: Mandates railway and inland steam vessel station personnel to refuse carriage of prohibited articles or to ensure compliance with conditions for transport, as specified by a notification under section 4A.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules prescribing the nature of documents required for export or transport subject to conditions under section 4A, including their issuance and usage. It also includes provisions for laying rules before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to make rules for the detention, inspection, disinfection or destruction of insects or articles specified in notifications under section 3 or 4A, and for regulating the powers and duties of appointed officers. It allows for fines for breaches and requires rules to be laid before the State Legislature.
Specifies penalties for contravention of notifications under section 4A or provisions of section 4B, including fines for initial and subsequent convictions.

main_sections.section_title: Protection to persons acting under Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection to any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act, preventing suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings.

important_rules: Rule 1: Central Government can prohibit or regulate the import of articles or insects likely to cause crop infection, with specific conditions and potential fees (Section 3).
Rule 2: Notifications under Section 3 have the force of Sea Customs Act provisions for customs officers (Section 4).
Rule 3: Central Government can prohibit or regulate the transport of infected articles or insects between States (Section 4A).
Rule 4: Transport operators must refuse to carry prohibited items or ensure compliance with transport conditions (Section 4B).
Rule 5: State Governments can make rules for inspection, disinfection, or destruction of infected items and appoint officers for this purpose. Breaches can be fined (Section 5).
Rule 6: Penalties include fines for illegally exporting or transporting articles/insects between states, or for non-compliance with transport regulations (Section 5A).

penalties: Fines for knowingly exporting or transporting articles or insects in contravention of a notification under section 4A, or attempting to do so.
Fines for persons responsible for booking of goods or parcels who knowingly contravene the provisions of section 4B.
Subsequent convictions may result in higher fines.
State Governments can direct that breaches of their rules under section 5 shall be punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, and customs officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, rules, prohibition/regulation of import and transport, refusal of carriage by transport operators, inspection, disinfection, and destruction of articles/insects.

rights: Right of customs officers to exercise powers related to prohibited imports.
Right of persons to protection from legal proceedings for acts done in good faith under the Act.
duties: Duty of transport operators to refuse carriage of prohibited items or ensure compliance with transport conditions.
Duty of persons to comply with notifications and rules made under the Act.
Duty of the Central Government to lay rules before Parliament.
Duty of State Governments to lay rules before the State Legislature.
obligations: Obligation to comply with regulations on import and transport of potentially infectious articles and insects.
Obligation to adhere to prescribed documents and procedures for inter-state transport.

key_procedures: Issuance of notification by the Central Government to prohibit or regulate import (Section 3).
Issuance of notification by the Central Government to prohibit or regulate inter-state transport (Section 4A).
Refusal of carriage by transport operators if conditions are not met (Section 4B).
Making of rules by the Central Government for documentation of inter-state transport (Section 4D).
Making of rules by State Governments for detention, inspection, disinfection, or destruction (Section 5).
administration: Central Government and State Governments.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Pondicherry.
The Act was amended to include 'and the transport from one province to another' and to define 'crops' more broadly.
Provisions related to Jammu and Kashmir have been omitted or modified by subsequent amendments.
Rules made by the Central Government must be laid before Parliament and are subject to modification or annulment.
Rules made by State Governments must be laid before the State Legislature.

title: THE SIR JAMSETJEE JEJEEBHOY BARONETCY ACT, 1915
purpose: To repeal Act No. 20 of 1860 and to resettle Government Promissory Notes, Mazagon Castle, and other hereditaments to support the title and dignity of the Baronetcy conferred on Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy and the heirs male of his body, and for other purposes connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the Baronetcy established by Letters Patent of Her late Majesty Queen Victoria, the associated property including Government Promissory Notes and Mazagon Castle, and the Trustees appointed to manage these assets. It specifically pertains to the Presidency of Bombay.

key_definitions.Baronetcy: A hereditary title of honor, established by Letters Patent, to be held by Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy and the heirs male of his body.
key_definitions.Trustees: The Commissioner for the Northern Division of the Presidency of Bombay, the Accountant-General of Bombay, and the Collector of Bombay, acting as a Corporation for the execution of the Trusts of the Act.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act and its commencement date.
Repeals the previous Act No. 20 of 1860.

main_sections.section_title: The Commissioner for the Northern Division, the Accountant-General, and the Collector of Bombay to be a Corporation for execution of the Trusts of this Act.
main_sections.description: Constitutes the specified officials as a Corporation to execute the Trusts of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Present Baronet to continue to bear, and all future Baronet to take, names of First Baronet.
main_sections.description: Mandates that the current and future Baronets must adopt the names 'Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy'.

main_sections.section_title: Government Promissory Notes of a certain nominal value vested in Trustees.
main_sections.description: Vests Government Promissory Notes in the Trustees, outlines reinvestment provisions if paid off, and specifies the payment of income to the current and future Baronets for their lives, with ultimate trust for the Second Baronet.

main_sections.section_title: Power to Baronet for the time being to purchase land to erect a Mansion House thereon.
main_sections.description: Grants the current Baronet the power to purchase land and erect a Mansion House, or purchase land with an existing house and alter or rebuild it.

main_sections.section_title: Power to Baronet for the time being to sell Mazagon Castle.
main_sections.description: Grants the current Baronet the power to sell Mazagon Castle.

main_sections.section_title: Settlement of Mansion House, etc., in support of Baronetcy.
main_sections.description: Details the settlement of the Mansion House and related hereditaments to support the Baronetcy.

main_sections.section_title: Provision in case of refusal or discontinuance of names of First Baronet.
main_sections.description: Addresses the situation where a Baronet refuses or discontinues using the required names.
Prohibits the alienation of property associated with the Baronetcy during its subsistence.
Provides an indemnity to the Trustees.

important_rules: Rule: The current and all future Baronets must adopt and bear the names 'Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy'.
Rule: Government Promissory Notes vested in the Trustees are to be managed, reinvested if paid off, and their income paid to the Baronet for the time being.
Rule: Investments made by the Trustees cannot be varied without the consent of the person entitled to the income.
Rule: The total sum raised from selling securities for land purchase shall not exceed Rs. 2,25,000.
Rule: The proceeds from the sale of Mazagon Castle, not exceeding Rs. 2,75,000, may be applied towards purchasing land and erecting a Mansion House.
Rule: The total amount of funds subject to the Settlement shall not exceed fifty lakh rupees.
Rule: The Mansion House and hereditaments are not to be subject to jointure.
Rule: Alienation of property is prohibited during the Baronetcy.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Corporation constituted by the Commissioner for the Northern Division of the Presidency of Bombay, the Accountant-General of Bombay, and the Collector of Bombay.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers and duties vested in the Trustees (the Corporation) by the Act, including management of assets, investment, sale, and ensuring compliance with the terms of the settlement.

rights: Right of the current and future Baronets to receive income from the Trust Fund.
Right of the current Baronet to purchase land and erect a Mansion House.
Right of the current Baronet to sell Mazagon Castle.
Right of the Baronet to enter into arrangements with the Government regarding land revenue.
duties: Duty of the Trustees to manage the Government Promissory Notes and other Trust properties.
Duty of the Trustees to invest and reinvest funds according to the Act.
Duty of the Trustees to apply proceeds from sales for designated purposes.
Duty of the Trustees to ensure the Mansion House and other buildings are kept in repair.
Duty of the Trustees to apply surplus income and interest during the minority of any Baronet.
obligations: Obligation of the current and future Baronets to bear the names 'Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy'.
Obligation to keep Mazagon Castle and substitute buildings in repair.
Obligation not to alienate property during the Baronetcy.

key_procedures: Procedure: To establish the Baronetcy and appoint Trustees, Act No. 20 of 1860 was passed, and this Act repeals and re-enacts provisions for resettlement.
Procedure: The Trustees are to manage and invest Government Promissory Notes, reinvesting if paid off.
Procedure: The Baronet can purchase land, erect a Mansion House, or purchase and alter existing houses.
Procedure: The Baronet can sell Mazagon Castle, with proceeds used for purchasing land and erecting a Mansion House, up to a specified limit.
Procedure: Surplus proceeds from the sale of Mazagon Castle above Rs. 2,75,000 are subject to specific trusts.
Procedure: Trustees can invest surplus income during the minority of a Baronet.
Procedure: Baronets may grant jointures, with limits on aggregate payable amounts.
Procedure: Trustees can sell land subject to the Settlement, with directions on how sales and investments of proceeds should be made.
administration: The Corporation comprising the Commissioner for the Northern Division of the Presidency of Bombay, the Accountant-General of Bombay, and the Collector of Bombay.
important_notes: Note: The Act acknowledges the unhealthiness of the Mazagon Castle locality and allows for its sale and the purchase of a new residence in a healthier area.
Note: All possible beneficiaries of the Trust, with the exception of two, have agreed to the proposals concerning the sale of Mazagon Castle.
Note: Objections from the two dissenting beneficiaries regarding the sale of Mazagon Castle have been overruled by the Governor General in Council.
Note: The total amount of funds subject to the Settlement is capped at fifty lakh rupees.
Note: Jointures are not to be levied on the Mansion House and hereditaments.
Note: Alienation of property is prohibited during the Baronetcy.

title: THE BANARAS HINDU UNIVERSITY ACT, 1915
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and residential Hindu University at Banaras, and to dissolve the Hindu University Society and transfer its property and rights to the University.
scope: Applies to the Banaras Hindu University, its students, teachers, officers, and all its property and affairs. Geographically, it pertains to the university established in Banaras.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.college: A college or teaching institution (other than a secondary, primary or infant school or pathasala) maintained by, or admitted to the privileges of, the University.
key_definitions.Ordinances: The Ordinances of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.Regulations: The Regulations of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.Statutes: The Statutes of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.teacher: A salaried professor, reader, lecturer or tutor who imparts instruction in a Faculty of, or in a college maintained by, the University and includes any other person who is declared to be a teacher by the Academic Council.
key_definitions.University: The Banaras Hindu University.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Banaras Hindu University Act, 1915, and specifies that it comes into force on a date to be notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, college, Court, Executive Council, Faculty, Ordinances, Regulations, Statutes, teacher, and University.

States that the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and members of the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council shall form a body corporate by the name of the Banaras Hindu University. The University is granted perpetual succession and a common seal, and the power to sue and be sued.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creeds
main_sections.description: Mandates that the University shall be open to all individuals regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class. It prohibits the University from imposing any religious test for admission, holding office, graduating, or enjoying privileges, except for specific benefactions with a stipulated condition.

Outlines the various powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, promoting study of various civilizations and cultures, holding examinations, granting degrees and diplomas, conferring honorary degrees, cooperating with other universities, instituting teaching posts, awarding fellowships and scholarships, maintaining hostels, creating administrative posts, and acquiring/managing property.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University. The Visitor has the right to inspect the University and its institutions, and to inquire into any matter connected with the University. The Visitor can annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act, Statutes, or Ordinances after providing an opportunity for the University to show cause.

Lists the officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Rector, Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans of Faculties, Dean of Students, Librarian, Chief Proctor, and other officers declared by the Statutes.

States that the Chancellor is elected by the Court for a term of three years and continues in office until a successor is elected. If the office becomes vacant, the Vice-Chancellor performs its functions.
Defines the Chancellor as the Head of the University and states that they shall preside at university convocations and meetings of the Court.

Specifies that the Vice-Chancellor is appointed by the Visitor on the recommendation of a Selection Committee. The Vice-Chancellor is a whole-time salaried officer, holds office for three years (eligible for reappointment for a second term), and continues until a successor is appointed. Their emoluments and terms of service are prescribed by Statutes. If the office becomes vacant, the Rector or Registrar performs its functions.

Designates the Vice-Chancellor as the principal executive and academic officer, responsible for general supervision and control of the University's affairs and giving effect to decisions of its authorities. They are the ex-officio Chairman of the Executive Council, Academic Council, and Finance Committee, and preside at convocations and Court meetings in the Chancellor's absence. They have the right to be present at and address meetings of any authority or committee but cannot vote unless a member.

important_rules: The University shall be open to all regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, without any religious tests for admission or holding office, except for specific benefactions.
Religious instruction can be provided with the consent of those receiving it or their guardians.
The University has the power to provide instruction, conduct research, promote various studies, hold examinations, grant degrees, and confer honorary degrees.
The President of India, as Visitor, has the power to inspect and inquire into the University's affairs and can annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act, Statutes, or Ordinances.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act's provisions are enforced through the powers vested in the University's authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council), the Visitor (President of India), and implicitly through adherence to the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the Visitor's inspection and annulment powers, the Vice-Chancellor's executive and academic oversight, and the statutory functions of other University authorities. Non-compliance with directions from the Visitor can be binding on the Executive Council.

rights: Right of persons of all classes, castes, and creeds to be admitted to the University.
Right of the Visitor to cause inspections and inquiries.
Right of the University to be represented and heard during inspections/inquiries.
Right of the Vice-Chancellor to general supervision and control over University affairs.
Right of the Vice-Chancellor to be present at and address meetings of University authorities.
Right of the Visitor to annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act.
duties: Duty of the University to be open to all classes, castes, and creeds.
Duty of the Visitor to give notice of intention to inspect/inquire.
Duty of the Vice-Chancellor to communicate the Visitor's views and advice to the Executive Council.
Duty of the Executive Council to communicate proposed or taken action to the Visitor.
Duty of the Executive Council to comply with the Visitor's directions.
Duty of the Vice-Chancellor to see that provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations are duly observed.
obligations: The Executive Council is bound to comply with the Visitor's directions if they do not take satisfactory action.
The University must show cause why proceedings should not be annulled by the Visitor.

key_procedures: Appointment of Vice-Chancellor: Visitor appoints on recommendation of a Selection Committee, with provision for fresh recommendations if not approved.

Inspection and Inquiry by Visitor: Visitor gives notice, University can appoint a representative, Visitor communicates views to Executive Council, Executive Council communicates action, Visitor can issue directions if action is unsatisfactory.
Annulment of Proceedings by Visitor: Visitor can annul proceedings not in conformity with Act/Statutes/Ordinances after calling upon the University to show cause.
administration: The administration of the University is overseen by its various authorities: the Visitor (President of India), Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council, as further detailed in the Statutes and Ordinances.
important_notes: The Act was modified as of 3rd December 2018.
The commencement date of the Act was 1st April, 1916.
Certain sections and sub-sections have been omitted or substituted by subsequent amendments (e.g., Act 55 of 1951, Act 52 of 1966, Act 34 of 1969).

title: THE USURIOUS LOANS ACT, 1918
purpose: To provide additional powers to Courts to deal with usurious loans of money or in kind.
scope: Extends to the whole of India, except for territories formerly comprised in Part B States. The State Government may, by notification, exclude specific areas, classes of persons, or classes of transactions.

key_definitions.interest: Rate of interest and includes any return above what was actually lent, whether specifically charged or otherwise.
key_definitions.loan: A loan whether of money or in kind, and includes any transaction that the Court deems to be substantially a loan.
key_definitions.suit_to_which_this_act_applies: Any suit for the recovery of a loan made after the Act's commencement, or for enforcing any security or agreement related to a loan (made before or after commencement), or for the redemption of any security given after commencement in respect of a loan.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act and defines its territorial and administrative extent, including provisions for exclusion by State Government notification.
Provides definitions for 'Interest', 'Loan', and 'Suit to which this Act applies'.
Empowers Courts to re-open usurious loan transactions if interest is excessive and the transaction is substantially unfair, outlining specific powers and limitations.
Extends the powers granted under Section 3 to Courts dealing with insolvency proceedings concerning the admission or amount of a loan proof.

important_rules: Rule 1: If a Court believes interest is excessive and the transaction substantially unfair in a suit to which this Act applies, it can re-open the transaction, take accounts, and relieve the debtor of excessive interest liability.
Rule 2: The Court can re-open accounts even if an agreement purports to close previous dealings and create a new obligation, and order the creditor to repay any sum found to be repayable.
Rule 3: The Court can set aside, revise, or alter any security or agreement, and if the creditor has parted with security, order indemnity to the debtor.
Rule 4: The Court shall not re-open an agreement closing previous dealings and creating a new obligation entered into more than twelve years before the transaction date.
Rule 5: The Court shall not affect any decree of a Court.
Rule 6: 'Excessive' interest is defined as that exceeding a reasonable rate considering the creditor's perceived risk at the time of the loan.
Rule 7: When considering if interest is excessive, the Court must consider all charges, compound interest periods, and total expected advantages from the transaction.
Rule 8: When considering risk, the Court must consider the presence and value of security, the debtor's financial condition, and past loan transaction results known to the creditor.

Rule 9: When considering if a transaction was substantially unfair, the Court must consider all circumstances affecting the parties' relationship, including the debtor's necessities known to the creditor.
Rule 10: Excessive interest itself can be sufficient evidence of a substantially unfair transaction.
Rule 11: This section applies to any suit that is substantially for loan recovery, enforcement of security/agreement, or redemption of security.
Rule 12: The provisions of this section do not affect bona fide transferees for value who had no notice of facts entitling the debtor to relief.
Rule 13: Nothing in this section derogates from existing Court powers or jurisdiction.
Rule 14: Courts dealing with insolvency proceedings can exercise the same powers as under Section 3 regarding loan proofs.

penalties: The Act empowers Courts to relieve debtors of excessive interest liability, order repayment of sums found repayable, and order creditors to indemnify debtors. Specific monetary penalties are not detailed in the provided text, but the Court's powers imply financial redress.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of Law.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of powers granted to Courts in suits for loan recovery, enforcement of securities, and insolvency proceedings, including re-opening transactions, taking accounts, revising agreements, and ordering repayment or indemnity.

rights: Right of a debtor to be relieved of excessive interest.
Right of a debtor to have unfair transactions re-opened.
Right of a debtor to have security or agreements revised or set aside.
Right of a debtor to receive indemnity from a creditor if security has been parted with.
Right of a debtor to relief in insolvency proceedings concerning loan proofs.
obligations: Obligation of a creditor to accept reasonable interest only.
Obligation of a creditor to repay amounts found to be repayable by the Court.
Obligation of a creditor to indemnify a debtor if security has been parted with.
Obligation of a creditor to act bona fide in transactions and not exploit debtor's necessities.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Filing a suit for recovery of a loan, enforcement of security, or redemption of security.

Procedure 2: The Court, upon having reason to believe that interest is excessive and the transaction substantially unfair, exercises powers to re-open the transaction, take accounts, relieve the debtor, revise agreements/securities, or order repayment/indemnity.
Procedure 3: In insolvency proceedings, an application relating to the admission or amount of a loan proof triggers the Court's power to apply similar relief as in suits.
administration: The Act is administered by the Courts of Law, and specific State Governments have the power to issue notifications regarding its application.
important_notes: The Act has been amended in various states and extended to new territories over time.
The Act has been repealed in its application to the Bellary District by Mysore Act 14 of 1955.
Transferees for value are protected if they acted bona fide and had no notice of facts entitling the debtor to relief.
The powers granted under this Act do not derogate from existing powers or jurisdiction of any Court.

title: The Calcutta High Court (Jurisdictional Limits) Act, 1919
purpose: To declare and prescribe the limits of the ordinary original civil jurisdiction of the High Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal.
scope: Applies to the High Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal and defines the geographical limits within which its ordinary original civil jurisdiction is to be exercised. The scope is primarily geographical, defining specific boundaries around Calcutta.

key_definitions.water-line: All pucca ghats and other objects permanently attached to the bank and in contact with the water are deemed to appertain to the area to which the land on that bank pertains. The water in contact with such objects is deemed to appertain to the other side of the boundary. In places where the boundary is described this way, the boundary line is the moving edge of the water. For bridges, supporting piles in contact with the bank are deemed permanently attached, and the boundary line across the bridge is immediately above the described water-line.
key_definitions.solid side or solid corner: Means the line or spot marked out by solid objects, such as a pucca wall or the face of a house, the wayside lands.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Calcutta High Court (Jurisdictional Limits) Act, 1919.

main_sections.section_title: Limits of ordinary original civil jurisdiction.
main_sections.description: Declares that the ordinary original civil jurisdiction of the High Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal shall be exercised within the limits set out in the Schedule. It also includes a proviso that the Act does not affect pending suits or legal proceedings.

important_rules: The ordinary original civil jurisdiction of the High Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal shall be exercised within the specific geographical limits detailed in the Schedule.
Nothing in this Act shall affect any suit or other legal proceeding that was pending in any Court at the date of the commencement of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implicitly, the High Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal is the authority whose jurisdiction is defined by this act, and its enforcement would be through the judicial system.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By defining the jurisdictional boundaries within which the High Court can exercise its ordinary original civil jurisdiction.

rights: The right of the High Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal to exercise ordinary original civil jurisdiction within defined limits.
duties: The duty of the High Court to exercise its jurisdiction within the prescribed limits.

key_procedures: The Act itself prescribes the procedure of defining jurisdictional limits through a detailed schedule, which involves identifying specific geographical boundaries based on landmarks, roads, and waterlines.
The Schedule outlines a method for defining boundaries by tracing lines (straight or along specific features) and referencing boundary pillars and reference points.
administration: The High Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal.
important_notes: The Act was modified as on 3rd December, 2018, indicating that it has undergone amendments or updates over time.
The Schedule provides a very detailed and specific description of the geographical limits, involving numerous reference points and directional descriptions.

title: THE ALIGARH MUSLIM UNIVERSITY ACT, 1920
purpose: To incorporate a teaching and residential Muslim University at Aligarh, dissolving existing societies and transferring their assets and liabilities to the new University.
scope: The act establishes and governs the Aligarh Muslim University, a teaching and residential institution in Aligarh. It applies to all persons associated with the University, including students, teachers, and staff.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.Board of Studies: The Board of Studies of the University.
key_definitions.Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor and Vice-Chan: The respective officers of the University.
key_definitions.Department: A Department of Studies and includes a Centre of Studies established by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.Executive Council: The Executive Council of the University.
key_definitions.Hall: A unit of residence or of corporate life maintained by the University for its students.
key_definitions.non-teaching staff: Employees of the University other than teachers.
key_definitions.Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations: The Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.Teachers: Professors, Readers, Lectures and such other persons as may be appointed for imparting instruction in the University or a hall and are designated as Teachers by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.University: The educational institution of their choice established by the Muslims of India, which originated as the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, and which was subsequently incorporated as the Aligarh Muslim University.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Aligarh Muslim University Act, 1920, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act and its associated Statutes.
Establishes the Aligarh Muslim University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, and the Muslim University Association, and transfer of all property to the University
main_sections.description: Dissolves the named societies and transfers all their property, rights, liabilities, and obligations to the University. It also provides for the interpretation of existing documents and employment conditions.

Outlines the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction, conducting research, promoting various studies (Oriental, Islamic, Indian culture, Muslim advancement), holding examinations, conferring degrees, cooperating with other institutions, instituting posts, managing property, and maintaining discipline.
States that degrees, diplomas, and distinctions granted by the University shall be recognized by the Central and State Governments, equivalent to those from other incorporated Universities.
Mandates the University to maintain a permanent endowment fund of thirty lakhs of rupees for recurring charges, with provisions for its calculation and investment.
Declares that the University is open to all persons irrespective of sex, race, religion, creed, caste, or class, with a proviso for religious instruction to consenting individuals.
Requires all students to reside in a Hall or hostel, or under conditions prescribed by Ordinances.

Specifies that all recognized teaching for University degrees, diplomas, and certificates shall be conducted under the supervision of the Academic Council and in accordance with Statutes and Ordinances.

important_rules: Rule: All students must reside in a Hall, hostel, or under prescribed conditions.
Rule: Teaching for University degrees, diplomas, and certificates must be supervised by the Academic Council and adhere to Statutes and Ordinances.
Rule: The University shall maintain a reserve fund of thirty lakhs of rupees for recurring charges.
Rule: The University shall be open to all persons, regardless of sex, race, religion, creed, caste, or class.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for commencement notification) and University authorities (for internal matters).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the University, its authorities, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations. Enforcement of the Act's commencement is via notification.

rights: Right for all persons to access the University irrespective of their background.
Right to receive degrees, diplomas, and certificates recognized by the government.
Right to employment under similar terms and conditions for existing staff of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College.
Right to appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
duties: Duty to provide instruction and conduct research.
Duty to promote Oriental and Islamic studies, Muslim theology and religion, and moral/physical training.
Duty to promote the study of India's religions, civilization, and culture.
Duty to promote the educational and cultural advancement of Muslims in India.
Duty to maintain a reserve fund.
Duty to supervise and control student residence, discipline, and health.
Duty to regulate and enforce discipline among employees.
obligations: Obligation to dissolve existing societies and transfer assets and liabilities.
Obligation to apply transferred property to the University's objects.
Obligation to discharge debts and liabilities of dissolved societies and committees.
Obligation to meet recurring charges from the reserve fund.
Obligation to ensure student residence and discipline.
Obligation to appoint staff and determine their service conditions as per Statutes.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement of the Act: The Central Government shall issue a notification in the Official Gazette.

Procedure for transfer of property and dissolution of societies: Upon commencement of the Act, the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College and Muslim University Association are dissolved, and their assets are transferred to the University.
Procedure for maintaining reserve fund: The University must invest and keep invested a sum of thirty lakhs of rupees as a permanent endowment.
Procedure for recognition of degrees: Degrees conferred by the University are recognized by Central and State Governments.
Procedure for student residence: Students must reside in a Hall, hostel, or under prescribed conditions.
Procedure for teaching: All recognized teaching must be conducted under the Academic Council's supervision and in accordance with Statutes and Ordinances.
administration: The Central Government (for commencement), and the University's various authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor) for day-to-day administration and governance.
important_notes: Note: Certain sections (9 and 14) have been omitted or repealed by subsequent amendments.
Note: The Act was amended in 1972 and 1981, affecting definitions and university powers.
Note: The commencement date of the Act was December 1, 1920.
Note: The Act allows for religious instruction to be given if students consent, without preventing it.
Note: The Act specifies conditions for the recognition of degrees and the management of the reserve fund.

title: The Official Secrets Act, 1923
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to official secrets.
scope: Extends to the whole of India and applies to servants of the Government and citizens of India outside India.

key_definitions.place_belonging_to_government: Includes any place occupied by any department of the Government, whether vested in the Government or not.
key_definitions.communicating_or_receiving: Includes any communicating or receiving, whether in whole or in part, and whether the sketch, plan, model, article, note, document, or information itself or its substance, effect, or description only is communicated or received.
key_definitions.obtaining_or_retaining: Includes the copying or causing to be copied of the whole or any part of any sketch, plan, model, article, note, or document.
key_definitions.communication_of_document: Includes the transfer or transmission of the sketch, plan, model, article, note, or document.
key_definitions.munitions_of_war: Includes any ship, submarine, aircraft, tank or similar engine, arms and ammunition, torpedo, or mine intended or adapted for use in war, and any other article, material, or device, whether actual or proposed, intended for such use.
key_definitions.office_under_government: Includes any office or employment in or under any department of the Government.
key_definitions.photograph: Includes an undeveloped film or plate.
key_definitions.prohibited_place: Includes defense works, arsenals, military/air force establishments, minefields, camps, ships, aircraft, military telegraphs/telephones, wireless/signal stations/offices, factories, dockyards used for making/storing munitions of war or related documents, places used under contract for government munitions, places declared prohibited by the Central Government for security reasons, and public utility works or places where munitions are made/repaired/stored otherwise than for government, if declared prohibited.
key_definitions.sketch: Includes any photograph or other mode of representing any place or thing.
key_definitions.superintendent_of_police: Includes any police officer of a like or superior rank, and any person conferred powers of a Superintendent of Police by the Central Government for the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India), and its application to government servants and Indian citizens outside India.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'prohibited place', 'munitions of war', 'document', 'sketch', and others.

Outlines penalties for engaging in activities prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State, such as approaching prohibited places, making useful sketches for enemies, or obtaining/collecting/publishing secret information.

main_sections.section_title: Communications with foreign agents to be evidence of commission of certain offences
main_sections.description: Establishes that communication with a foreign agent can be used as evidence to prove an attempt to obtain information useful to an enemy.
Deals with the wrongful communication, use, retention, or endangerment of secret official information, codes, pass words, or documents.

main_sections.section_title: Unauthorised use of uniforms; falsification of reports, forgery, personation, and false documents
main_sections.description: Addresses offenses related to unauthorized use of uniforms, falsification of reports, forgery, personation, and the use of false documents.

main_sections.section_title: Interfering with officers of the police or members of the Armed Forces of the Union
main_sections.description: Penalizes interference with police officers or members of the Armed Forces of the Union.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of giving information as to commission of offences
main_sections.description: Imposes a duty on individuals to provide information regarding the commission of offenses under this Act.
Covers attempts, incitements, and conspiracies to commit offenses under the Act.
Specifies the penalty for harboring spies.
Provides for the issuance of search-warrants in relation to offenses under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of section 337 of Act 5 of 1898 to apply to offences under sections 3, 5 and 7
main_sections.description: States that certain provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1898, apply to offenses under sections 3, 5, and 7 of this Act.
Imposes restrictions on the trial of offenses under this Act.
Allows for the exclusion of the public from court proceedings related to offenses under this Act.
Deals with offenses committed by companies under the Act.
This section has been repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: No person shall approach, inspect, pass over, be in the vicinity of, or enter any prohibited place for any purpose prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State.
Rule 2: No person shall make any sketch, plan, model, or note calculated to be or intended to be, directly or indirectly, useful to an enemy.

Rule 3: No person shall obtain, collect, record, publish, or communicate to any other person any secret official code or pass word, or any sketch, plan, model, article, note, document, or information which is likely to affect the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the State, or friendly relations with foreign States, or is useful to an enemy.

Rule 4: Any person found in possession or control of secret official information, documents, or codes must not wilfully communicate them to unauthorized persons or use them for the benefit of any foreign power or in a manner prejudicial to the safety of the State.
Rule 5: Individuals must take reasonable care of, and not endanger the safety of, any sketch, plan, model, article, note, document, secret official code, pass word, or information.
Rule 6: Anyone voluntarily receiving secret information knowing or having reasonable grounds to believe it was communicated in contravention of this Act is guilty of an offense.
Rule 7: It is an offense to communicate information relating to munitions of war to any foreign power or in a manner prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State.
Rule 8: Individuals must not make, falsify, or use false documents or personate others in relation to official secrets.
Rule 9: It is an offense to interfere with police officers or members of the Armed Forces of the Union.
Rule 10: Individuals have a duty to give information regarding the commission of offenses under this Act.

penalties: Spying (Section 3): Imprisonment up to fourteen years (if in relation to defense works, military affairs, etc., or secret codes) or up to three years in other cases.
