Procedure for recognizing title to a Government security of a deceased sole holder, including provisions for Hindu undivided families (Section 7).
Summary procedure on the death of a holder of Government securities not exceeding five thousand rupees face value (Section 9).
Procedure for making nominations by holders of Government securities (Section 9B).
Procedure for obtaining duplicate or new securities on conversion, consolidation, sub-division or renewal (Section 11).
Procedure for summary determination by the Bank of title to a Government security in case of dispute (Section 12).
administration: The Reserve Bank of India (referred to as 'the Bank') plays a central role in the administration of this Act, particularly concerning the management of public debt and the handling of Government securities. The Central Government also has powers related to notifications and rule-making.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various Union territories, including Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.
Specific dates are provided for the validity of transfers of securities issued by different governments.
The Act provides for exceptions and special considerations for Hindu undivided families and joint holders.
The Act may override provisions of other laws, such as the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and the Indian Contract Act, 1872, in specific contexts.

title: THE DELHI SPECIAL POLICE ESTABLISHMENT ACT, 1946
purpose: To make provision for the constitution of a special police force in Delhi for the investigation of certain offences in the Union territories, for the superintendence and administration of the said force, and for the extension to other areas of the powers and jurisdiction of members of the said force in regard to the investigation of the said offences.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. The Delhi Special Police Establishment is constituted for the investigation of certain offences in any Union territory. Its powers and jurisdiction can be extended to any area in a State (including Railway areas) with the consent of the State Government.

key_definitions.Director: An officer appointed by the Central Government to administer the Delhi Special Police Establishment.
key_definitions.Director of Prosecution: An officer heading the Directorate of Prosecution, responsible for conducting prosecutions under this Act, appointed on the recommendation of the Central Vigilance Commission.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, and states its extent to the whole of India.
Specifies that words and expressions used in the Act but not defined shall have the meanings assigned to them in the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and powers of special police establishment
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute the Delhi Special Police Establishment for investigating notified offences in Union territories. Members of this establishment have the powers, duties, privileges, and liabilities of local police officers in relation to such investigations and arrests. Members of or above the rank of Sub-Inspector can exercise the powers of an officer in charge of a police station.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be investigated by special police establishment
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to specify, by notification in the Official Gazette, the offences or classes of offences to be investigated by the Delhi Special Police Establishment.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence and administration of Special Police Establishment
main_sections.description: States that superintendence of the Delhi Special Police Establishment concerning investigations of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, vests in the Commission. In all other matters, superintendence vests in the Central Government. Administration vests in a Director appointed by the Central Government.

Establishes a committee comprising the Prime Minister (Chairperson), Leader of Opposition or Leader of the single largest Opposition Party, and the Chief Justice of India or a nominated Judge for recommending the appointment of the Director. The committee recommends a panel of officers based on seniority, integrity, and experience.

main_sections.section_title: Terms and conditions of service of Director
main_sections.description: Mandates a minimum tenure of two years for the Director, with possibilities for extension up to one year at a time, not exceeding five years in total, on recommendation and for reasons to be recorded. The Director cannot be transferred without the consent of the appointment committee.

Provides for a Directorate of Prosecution headed by a Director, who is an officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary to the Government of India. The Director of Prosecution functions under the overall supervision of the Director and is appointed on the recommendation of the Central Vigilance Commission. They have a minimum tenure of two years.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment for posts of Superintendent of Police and above, extension and curtailment of their tenure, etc.
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for appointing officers to posts of Superintendent of Police and above (excluding the Director), and for recommending tenure extensions or curtailments. This is done by a committee consisting of the Central Vigilance Commissioner (Chairperson), Vigilance Commissioners, and Secretaries from the Ministry of Home and Department of Personnel. The committee must consult the Director before submitting recommendations to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of powers and jurisdiction of special police establishment to other areas
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to extend the powers and jurisdiction of the Delhi Special Police Establishment to any area (including Railway areas) in a State (not being a Union territory) for investigating specified offences. Members exercising powers in such areas are deemed to be members of the local police force and possess corresponding powers, functions, and liabilities. Members of or above the rank of Sub-Inspector can exercise powers of an officer in charge of a police station.

main_sections.section_title: Consent of State Government to exercise of powers and jurisdiction
main_sections.description: States that the powers and jurisdiction of the Delhi Special Police Establishment cannot be exercised in any area in a State (not being a Union territory or railway area) without the consent of the Government of that State.

main_sections.section_title: Approval of Central Government to conduct, inquiry or investigation
main_sections.description: Requires the prior approval of the Central Government to conduct any inquiry or investigation into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, if the allegations relate to employees of the Central Government of the level of Joint Secretary and above, or officers appointed by the Central Government in government-owned or controlled entities. An exception is made for arrests on the spot for accepting or attempting to accept gratification.
This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1950.

important_rules: Rule: Members of the Delhi Special Police Establishment shall have throughout any Union territory, in relation to the investigation of notified offences and arrest of persons concerned, all the powers, duties, privileges, and liabilities which police officers of that Union territory have in connection with the investigation of offences committed therein.

Rule: Any member of the Delhi Special Police Establishment of or above the rank of Sub-Inspector may, subject to Central Government orders, exercise in any Union territory any of the powers of the officer in charge of a police station and shall be deemed to be such an officer within the limits of his station.
Rule: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify the offences or classes of offences to be investigated by the Delhi Special Police Establishment.
Rule: The Director shall hold office for a period of not less than two years from the date of assumption of office.
Rule: The Director shall not be transferred except with the previous consent of the Committee for appointment of Director.

Rule: The Delhi Special Police Establishment shall not conduct any inquiry or investigation into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, concerning employees of the Central Government of the level of Joint Secretary and above, or officers in Central Government controlled entities, without the previous approval of the Central Government (unless it involves an on-the-spot arrest for gratification).
Rule: The Delhi Special Police Establishment cannot exercise powers and jurisdiction in any State area without the consent of that State's Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Delhi Special Police Establishment, State Governments (for consent to jurisdiction extension).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation of notified offences, exercise of police powers by its members, requiring State Government consent for jurisdiction in State areas, requiring Central Government approval for certain investigations under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

rights: Members of the Delhi Special Police Establishment have the powers, privileges, and liabilities of local police officers in Union territories for investigating notified offences.
Members of or above the rank of Sub-Inspector can exercise powers of an officer in charge of a police station.
duties: To investigate specified offences as notified by the Central Government.
To uphold the powers, duties, privileges, and liabilities of police officers in relation to investigations and arrests in Union territories.
To conduct investigations and inquiries with prior approval of the Central Government in specific cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
obligations: The Director must hold office for a minimum period and cannot be transferred without committee consent.
The Delhi Special Police Establishment must obtain State Government consent to exercise powers in State areas.
The Delhi Special Police Establishment must obtain Central Government approval for certain investigations under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

key_procedures: Appointment of the Director: Recommended by a committee (Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition, Chief Justice of India) based on a panel of officers chosen for seniority, integrity, and experience.
Extension of jurisdiction to States: Central Government may extend powers to any area in a State via order, but requires the consent of the State Government.

Investigation of certain offences: Central Government can specify offences for investigation by notification. For offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, concerning senior officials or employees in government entities, prior Central Government approval is needed, except in cases of on-the-spot arrests for gratification.
administration: Central Government (for superintendence and appointment of Director and administration), Central Vigilance Commission (for superintendence in certain cases and recommendation of Director of Prosecution).
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various Union Territories and other regions through various notifications and regulations.
The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted from the extent clause.

The Act has undergone several amendments, including the insertion of interpretation, appointment, and tenure provisions for the Director and Director of Prosecution, and provisions for Central Government approval for certain investigations.

title: THE RUBBER ACT, 1947
purpose: To provide for the development of the rubber industry under the control of the Union.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India (excluding the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh as of 2019). It governs the rubber industry, including production, marketing, import, and export. It applies to owners of estates, dealers, manufacturers, processors, and growers of rubber plants.

key_definitions.Board: The Rubber Board constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.dealer: Any person who deals in rubber, whether wholesale or retail, or holds stocks of rubber, and includes their representative or agent.
key_definitions.estate: Any area administered as one unit which contains land planted with rubber plants.
key_definitions.export: Taking out of India by sea, land or air.
key_definitions.import: Bringing into India by sea, land or air.
key_definitions.manufacturer: Any person engaged in the manufacture of any article in the making of which rubber is used.
key_definitions.owner: Includes any agent of an owner, a mortgagee in possession, and a lessee of an estate.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.processor: A person who undertakes the processing of rubber.
key_definitions.rubber: Includes crude rubber (prepared from leaves, bark or latex of any rubber plant), latex in any stage of treatment, and scrap rubber, sheet rubber, rubber in powder, and all forms of crepe rubber. It does not include rubber contained in any manufactured article.
key_definitions.rubber plant: Includes Hevea Braziliensis (Para Rubber), Manihot Glaziovii (Ceara Rubber), Castillio elastica, Ficus elastica (Rambong), and any other plant declared as such by the Board.
key_definitions.small grower: An owner whose estate does not exceed fifty acres in area.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial extent.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of Union control
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to control the rubber industry.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act.
Details the composition of the Rubber Board, including appointment of Chairman and members representing different states, interests, and Parliament.

Outlines the duties and functions of the Rubber Board, including promoting the development of the rubber industry through research, training, technical advice, improving marketing, collecting statistics, securing better working conditions for workers, and advising the Central Government on matters related to the industry.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit or control imports and exports of rubber
main_sections.description: Grants power to prohibit or control the import and export of rubber.
Empowers the imposition of a new rubber cess.

main_sections.section_title: Power to fix maximum and minimum prices for sale of rubber
main_sections.description: Grants power to fix maximum and minimum prices for the sale of rubber.
Provides for the licensing of transactions in rubber.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Prohibition or control of imports and exports of rubber (Section 11).
Fixing of maximum and minimum prices for the sale of rubber (Section 13).
Licensing of transactions in rubber (Section 14).
Restriction on possession of rubber (Section 16).
Licences for planting or replanting rubber (Section 17).
Submission of returns and maintenance of accounts by licencees (Section 20).
Inspection of land and premises by authorized officers (Section 21).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act or rules made thereunder, as specified in Section 26.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Rubber Board and the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of penalties, compounding of offences, adjudication of penalties, and court prosecutions. The Central Government also has the power to issue directions to the Board and make rules.

rights: Right to attend meetings of the Board and participate in proceedings for deputed Central Government officers (though without voting rights).
Right to appeal against orders of the Board.
duties: Duty of the Board to promote the development of the rubber industry (Section 8(1)).
Duty of licencees to submit reports and maintain accounts (Section 18, 20).
Duty to advise the Central Government on matters related to the rubber industry (Section 8(3)(a)).
Duty to submit reports on activities and working of the Act (Section 8(3)(c)).
obligations: Obligation to obtain licences for planting, replanting, and certain transactions in rubber.
Obligation to comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
Obligation to provide accurate returns and maintain accounts.
Obligation to allow inspection of land and premises.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Rubber Board by the Central Government through notification.
Appointment of Chairman, Executive Director, Rubber Production Commissioner, and Secretary.
Granting of licences for planting, replanting, and transactions in rubber.
Submission of returns and maintenance of accounts by licencees.
Inspection of land and premises.
Appeals against orders of the Board.
Rule-making and regulation-making procedures by the Central Government and the Board, respectively.
administration: The Central Government and the Rubber Board.
important_notes: The Act was amended to include the State of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh within its scope.
The Act has been extended to Pondicherry and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
Specific sections like 22A (Power of Central Government to issue directions to Board) and 25A (Power to make regulations) indicate further administrative and regulatory mechanisms.

title: THE UNITED NATIONS (SECURITY COUNCIL) ACT, 1947
purpose: To enable effect to be given to certain provisions of the Charter of the United Nations.
scope: This act applies to the Central Government of India and its ability to implement decisions of the UN Security Council, particularly those under Article 41 of the UN Charter. It can have extra-territorial operation.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1947.

main_sections.section_title: Measures under Art 41 of the Charter of the United Nations.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to apply measures, not involving the use of armed force, as called for by the UN Security Council under Article 41 of the UN Charter. The Central Government can issue orders in the Official Gazette to effectively apply these measures, including provisions for the punishment of offenders.

important_rules: If the UN Security Council calls upon the Central Government to apply measures under Article 41 (not involving armed force) to give effect to a decision, the Central Government is empowered to act.
The Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make necessary or expedient provisions to effectively apply these measures.
Such provisions may have extra-territorial operation.
Orders made by the Central Government can include provisions for the punishment of persons offending against the order.

penalties: Punishment of persons offending against orders made by the Central Government under Section 2.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government of India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders published in the Official Gazette, which can include provisions for punishment.

rights: The Central Government has the right to make orders to implement UN Security Council decisions under Article 41.
duties: The Central Government has a duty to implement UN Security Council decisions when called upon to do so under Article 41.

key_procedures: 1. UN Security Council calls upon the Central Government to apply measures under Article 41 (not involving armed force).
2. Central Government decides on necessary or expedient provisions to effectively apply these measures.
3. Central Government publishes an order in the Official Gazette containing these provisions.
4. Provisions may include punishment for offenders.
administration: The Central Government of India.
important_notes: The measures to be applied are those not involving the use of armed force, as per Article 41 of the UN Charter.
The provisions made by the Central Government can have extra-territorial operation.

title: The United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947
purpose: To give effect to the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations and to enable similar privileges and immunities to be enjoyed by other international organisations and their representatives and officials.
scope: Applies to the United Nations, its representatives, officers, and other international organizations, their representatives, and officers within India. It also extends to the Union territory of Pondicherry and the State of Sikkim.

key_definitions.Convention on the Privileges and Immunit: An international agreement adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations on February 13, 1946, the provisions of which are incorporated into Indian law by this Act.
key_definitions.representatives: In the context of Article IV, includes all delegates, deputy delegates, advisers, technical experts, and secretaries of delegations.
key_definitions.officials: Categories of officials specified by the Secretary-General of the UN, as communicated to Member Governments.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment on United Nations and its representatives and officers and certain privileges and immunities
main_sections.description: Gives the force of law in India to the provisions of the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations, as set out in the Schedule. It also empowers the Central Government to amend the Schedule in conformity with amendments to the Convention.

main_sections.section_title: Power to confer certain privileges and immunities on other international organisations and their representatives and officers
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare, through notification, that the provisions in the Schedule shall apply, with necessary modifications, to other international organizations and their representatives and officers if required by an international agreement.
Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. It also includes provisions for laying such rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.

important_rules: The provisions of the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations, as detailed in the Schedule, have the force of law in India.
The Central Government can amend the Schedule to align with any amendments made to the Convention.
The Central Government can extend similar privileges and immunities to other international organizations through official notifications.
Rules made under this Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period before they become effective.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and appropriate authorities of Member States.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Convention's provisions, which are given the force of law in India. The Act empowers the Central Government to make rules and notifications to facilitate enforcement. The United Nations is obligated to cooperate with authorities to facilitate justice and prevent abuse of privileges.

rights: The United Nations has the right to possess juridical personality, contract, acquire property, and institute legal proceedings.
The United Nations has the right to transfer funds, gold, and currency, and convert currencies.
The United Nations has the right to receive communications treatment not less than diplomatic missions, and no censorship shall be applied to its official correspondence.
Representatives of Members, officials, and experts on missions for the UN have rights to various immunities and privileges necessary for their functions.
duties: The United Nations, in exercising its rights concerning fund transfers, must pay due regard to representations made by Member Governments.
Members have a duty to waive the immunity of their representatives if it would impede the course of justice and can be waived without prejudice to the purpose of the immunity.
The Secretary-General of the UN has the duty to waive the immunity of an official when it impedes the course of justice.
The United Nations shall cooperate with appropriate authorities of Members to facilitate the proper administration of justice and prevent abuse of privileges.
obligations: Officials are subject to national service obligations only if they are nationals of the State concerned.
Representatives are not subject to immigration restrictions, alien registration, or national service obligations in the state they are visiting or passing through.
Representatives and officials enjoy exemptions from direct taxes, customs duties, and other charges, subject to specific conditions and limitations.

key_procedures: The Central Government, by notification, can extend privileges and immunities to other international organizations and their personnel by declaring the Schedule's provisions applicable.
The Secretary-General of the UN designates categories of officials to whom Article V and VII apply, communicating these to Member Governments.
The Central Government makes rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, which are then presented to Parliament.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act has been extended to the Union territory of Pondicherry and the State of Sikkim.
Immunities and privileges granted are for the independent exercise of functions, not personal benefit.
Waiver of immunity is possible if it impedes justice and can be done without prejudice to the purpose of the immunity.
Immunities and privileges do not apply as between a representative and the authorities of their own country.
Certain articles imported under exemption will not be sold except under conditions agreed with the Government of that country.
The United Nations will not claim exemption from taxes that are in fact charges for public utility services.

title: THE PHARMACY ACT, 1948
purpose: To regulate the profession of pharmacy and for that purpose to constitute Pharmacy Councils.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. Chapters III, IV, and V apply to a particular State from a date appointed by the State Government. It covers the regulation of pharmacy practice, the establishment and functioning of Pharmacy Councils, and the registration of pharmacists.

key_definitions.agreement: An agreement entered into under section 20.
key_definitions.approved: Approved by the Central Council under section 12 or section 14.
key_definitions.central_council: The Pharmacy Council of India constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.central_register: The register of pharmacists maintained by the Central Council under section 15A.
key_definitions.executive_committee: The Executive Committee of the Central Council or of the State Council, as the context may require.
key_definitions.indian_university: A University within the meaning of section 3 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, and includes such other institutions, established by or under a Central Act, as the Central Government may specify.
key_definitions.medical_practitioner: A person holding a specified qualification or registered/eligible for registration in a medical register of a State, or declared by the State Government as a practitioner of modern scientific medicine, or registered/eligible for registration in the register of dentists, or engaged in veterinary medicine with approved qualifications.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under section 18 (for Chapter II) and by rules made under section 46 (elsewhere).
key_definitions.register: A register of pharmacists prepared and maintained under Chapter IV.
key_definitions.registered_pharmacist: A person whose name is for the time being entered in the register of the State in which he is for the time being residing or carrying on his profession or business of pharmacy.
key_definitions.state_council: A State Council of Pharmacy constituted under section 19, including a Joint State Council of Pharmacy constituted by agreement under section 20.
key_definitions.university_grants_commission: The University Grants Commission established under section 4 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and commencement provisions, noting that Chapters III, IV, and V come into effect in a State on a date appointed by the State Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'agreement', 'approved', 'Central Council', 'Central Register', 'Executive Committee', 'Indian University', 'medical practitioner', 'prescribed', 'register', 'registered pharmacist', 'State Council', and 'University Grants Commission'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of Central Council
main_sections.description: Details the constitution and composition of the Pharmacy Council of India (Central Council), including elected and nominated members from various bodies like universities, medical practitioners, and State Councils, along with ex-officio members.
Establishes the Pharmacy Council of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire property and sue and be sued.

main_sections.section_title: President and Vice-President of Central Council
main_sections.description: Outlines the election of the President and Vice-President of the Central Council from among its members and their term of office.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of State Councils
main_sections.description: Details the constitution and composition of State Pharmacy Councils, including members elected and nominated by State Governments and State Councils.
Governs the preparation and maintenance of registers of pharmacists by the State Councils.
Specifies the process for preparing the first register of pharmacists.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications for entry on first register
main_sections.description: Lays down the qualifications required for a person's name to be entered in the first register.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who falsely claim to be registered pharmacists.
Addresses the issue of dispensing medicines by persons who are not registered pharmacists.

important_rules: A member of the Central Council elected under clause (a), (c) or (g) of section 3 is deemed to have vacated their seat if they cease to be a member of the teaching staff, Medical Council of India, or a registered pharmacist, respectively.
Members of the Central Council are eligible for re-nomination or re-election.
The Central Council shall appoint a Registrar, who shall also act as the Secretary and potentially Treasurer.
The Central Council shall have an Executive Committee consisting of the President (Chairman), Vice-President, and five other elected members.
State Councils are responsible for the preparation and maintenance of registers of pharmacists.
Specific qualifications are required for entry onto the first register of pharmacists.
Penalties are prescribed for falsely claiming to be a registered pharmacist.
Dispensing of medicines by unregistered persons is an offense.

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered (Section 41).
Penalty for dispensing by unregistered persons (Section 42).
Penalty for failure to surrender a certificate of registration (Section 43).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Governments and the Pharmacy Councils (Central and State) are involved in the enforcement of the Act. Section 43A mentions adjudication of penalties, implying a mechanism for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for registration, maintenance of registers, inspection, and penal consequences for violations. State Governments appoint dates for certain chapters to come into force. The Central Government decides disputes related to elections. Adjudication of penalties is also a mechanism.

rights: Right to be registered as a pharmacist if one meets the prescribed qualifications.
Right to practice pharmacy if registered under the Act.
Right to receive remuneration and allowances as determined for the President, Vice-President, members, officers, and servants of the Central Council.
duties: Duty to prepare and maintain registers of pharmacists.
Duty to conduct elections in the prescribed manner.
Duty to ensure that only registered pharmacists dispense medicines.
Duty to surrender a certificate of registration when required.
obligations: Obligation for the Central Government to constitute the Central Council.
Obligation for the Central Council to make regulations for educational standards and other matters.
Obligation for State Governments to appoint dates for Chapters III, IV, and V to take effect.
Obligation for members of the Central Council to vacate their seats under certain conditions.
Obligation to pay renewal fees for registration.
Obligation to appoint staff and provide them with remuneration and allowances.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Central Council: The Central Government constitutes the Council with specific elected and nominated members.
Constitution of State Councils: State Councils are constituted with elected and nominated members.
Registration of Pharmacists: Involves the preparation and maintenance of registers, scrutiny of applications, and entry of qualifications.
Election Procedures: Elections for President, Vice-President, and members of the Councils are conducted in a prescribed manner, with disputes referred to the Central Government.
Appointment of Staff: The Central Council appoints a Registrar and other officers and servants.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments, along with the Pharmacy Council of India (Central Council) and State Pharmacy Councils, administer the Act.
important_notes: The Act was extended to various Union Territories and had modifications in its application to certain States.
The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted with effect from 31-10-2019.
Provisions for the Pharmacy (Amendment) Act, 1976, allowed Union territories to nominate members eligible for registration.
The Act clarifies that no act done by the Central Council shall be questioned solely due to a vacancy or defect in its constitution.

title: THE NATIONAL CADET CORPS ACT, 1948
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a National Cadet Corps.
scope: Extends to the whole of India and applies to all persons enrolled or appointed under this Act, wherever they may be. Recruitment is primarily from students of universities and schools.

key_definitions.corps: The National Cadet Corps constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.enrolled: Enrolled in the Corps under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.school: Includes any institution recognised in this behalf by the Central Government or the State Government.
key_definitions.university: Means any university established by law in India and includes colleges affiliated to universities, intermediate colleges and such technical institutions of collegiate status, as are recognised in this behalf by the Central Government or the State Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and to whom it applies (all persons enrolled or appointed under the Act).
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'corps', 'enrolled', 'prescribed', 'school', and 'university'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the National Cadet Corps.
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Cadet Corps and empowers the Central Government to establish its units as necessary.
Empowers the Central Government to constitute, disband, or reconstitute units of the Corps in any State, recruiting members from university or school students.

main_sections.section_title: Division of the Corps into Divisions.
main_sections.description: Details the three Divisions of the Corps: Senior Division (male university students), Junior Division (male school students), and Junior Division (female students of universities or schools).

Outlines the eligibility and process for male students of universities and schools to enroll in the Senior and Junior Divisions respectively, and for female students to enroll in the Girls Division, provided they meet the prescribed age.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government may raise other units.
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to constitute other units of the Corps in any place and prescribe eligibility criteria for enrolment.

Specifies the grounds for discharge from the Corps, including expiration of the enrollment period or ceasing to be a student of the affiliated institution. Also allows for discharge at any time by a prescribed authority.
Grants the Central Government the power to appoint officers for the Corps units, from university/school staff or otherwise, and to prescribe their duties, powers, and functions.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of persons subject to this Act.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that members are not liable for active military service but are liable to perform prescribed duties and obligations.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for offences under this Act.
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for contravention of rules made under the Act, with a fine up to fifty rupees.

Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Central Advisory Committee (listing its members including Ministers, Secretaries, Chiefs of Staff, and nominated non-officials and MPs) and State Advisory Committees.

Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the objects of the Act, covering various aspects of the Corps' operation, enrolment, training, discipline, and administration. Rules are subject to parliamentary approval.

important_rules: Enrolment is primarily for students of universities and schools (Section 6).
Members are not liable for active military service but must perform prescribed duties (Section 10).
Contravention of rules can lead to a fine of up to fifty rupees (Section 11).
The Central Government can make rules for the effective administration of the Act, which are subject to parliamentary review (Section 13).

penalties: Fine which may extend to fifty rupees for contravention of any rule made under this Act (Section 11).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed authority (implied, as detailed in rules made under the Act, e.g., for recovery of fines).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prescribed procedures for recovery of fines and potential disciplinary actions as detailed in rules made under the Act.

rights: Entitlement to discharge from the Corps upon expiration of the enrollment period or cessation of student status (Section 8).
duties: Perform such duties and discharge such obligations as may be prescribed (Section 10).
Undergo preliminary and periodical military training as prescribed (Section 13(2)(e)).
Liable to military or other obligations when undergoing military training and maintain discipline (Section 13(2)(f)).
obligations: To perform duties and discharge obligations as prescribed (Section 10).
To undergo prescribed military or other training (Section 13(2)(e), (f)).
To maintain discipline as prescribed (Section 13(2)(f)).

key_procedures: Enrolment of students in Senior and Junior Divisions based on gender, educational institution type, and age (Section 6).
Discharge of enrolled persons upon completion of service period or ceasing to be a student (Section 8).
Appointment of officers for Corps units (Section 9).
Constitution and disbandment of Corps units by the Central Government (Section 4).
Establishment of Central and State Advisory Committees (Section 12).
Making of rules by the Central Government to carry out the Act's objects, subject to parliamentary approval (Section 13).
administration: Central Government, Ministry of Defence (implied through Advisory Committee composition and rule-making powers).
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various territories including Goa, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Lakshadweep, and Arunachal Pradesh (footnotes).
The words 'except the State of Hyderabad' were omitted from Section 1(2) by Act 3 of 1951.
The words 'or Acceding State' were omitted from Section 4 by A.O. 1950.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before Parliament for a specified period and can be modified or annulled by Parliament (Section 13(3)).

title: THE CALCUTTA PORT (PILOTAGE) ACT, 1948
purpose: To provide for the transfer of control over pilotage on the River Hooghly to the Commissioners for the Port of Calcutta and for other matters incidental thereto, and to make certain consequential amendments in the Calcutta Pilots Act 12 of 1859.
scope: Applies to the Hooghly area, which extends from the Port of Calcutta to the sea, concerning pilotage services. The act primarily concerns the Commissioners for the Port of Calcutta and persons involved in pilotage.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.commissioners: The Commissioners for the Port of Calcutta incorporated under the Calcutta Port Act, 1890.
key_definitions.hooghly_area: The part of the Hooghly River extending from the Port of Calcutta to the sea to which section 31 of the Indian Ports Act, 1908, has been extended.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Calcutta Port (Pilotage) Act, 1948, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.
Provides definitions for 'Appointed day', 'Commissioners', and 'Hooghly area'.
Mandates the Commissioners to maintain pilots for the safe navigation of vessels in the Hooghly area and to ensure a sufficient number of pilots as prescribed by the Central Government.
Stipulates that only persons authorized by the Central Government under the Indian Ports Act, 1908, can be appointed as pilots by the Commissioners.

Empowers the Commissioners to make rules for fixing salaries, wages, allowances, and regulating the behavior and conduct of pilots. Observance can be enforced through pecuniary penalties, suspension, or deprivation. Rules require Central Government approval and publication.
Grants the Commissioners the right to levy fees for pilotage of vessels in the Hooghly area at rates fixed under the Indian Ports Act, 1908.

main_sections.section_title: Pilotage fees and fines and penalties levied under the Act
main_sections.description: Specifies that all pilotage fees, fines, and penalties levied under this Act (except those imposed by a Court) shall be accounted for and expended by the Commissioners according to section 36 of the Indian Ports Act, 1908.

main_sections.section_title: Power to transfer moneys from the general account to pilotage account and vice versa
main_sections.description: Allows the Commissioners, with Central Government sanction, to use funds from the general account to cover deficits in the pilotage account and transfer surplus pilotage funds to the general account.

main_sections.section_title: Application of certain provisions of Bengal Act 3 of 1890
main_sections.description: Incorporates specific sections of the Calcutta Port Act, 1890, into this Act with modifications, primarily concerning references to the Calcutta Port Act, pilotage fees, and procedural details.

important_rules: The Commissioners must maintain a sufficient number of pilots as prescribed by the Central Government for safe navigation in the Hooghly area.
Only individuals authorized by the Central Government under the Indian Ports Act, 1908, can be appointed as pilots.
Rules made by the Commissioners for regulating pilots require approval from the Central Government and publication in the Official Gazette before taking effect.
Pilotage fees, fines, and penalties levied under the Act are to be accounted for and expended by the Commissioners as per section 36 of the Indian Ports Act, 1908.
The Commissioners can transfer funds between their general account and the pilotage account with the Central Government's sanction.

penalties: Pecuniary penalties not exceeding two hundred rupees for every breach of rules regulating pilots.
Suspension or deprivation of appointment for pilots.
Fines and penalties levied under the Act (excluding those imposed by a Court).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioners for the Port of Calcutta and the Central Government (for approvals and oversight).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of pecuniary penalties, suspension, deprivation of appointment for pilots, and through accounting and expenditure of fees and fines as per the Indian Ports Act, 1908.

rights: The Commissioners are entitled to levy fees for pilotage.
The Commissioners have the power to make rules for regulating pilots.
The Commissioners have the power to transfer moneys between general and pilotage accounts.
duties: The Commissioners have a duty to maintain pilots for the safe navigation of vessels in the Hooghly area.
The Commissioners are bound to maintain a sufficient number of pilots as prescribed by the Central Government.
obligations: The Commissioners must ensure pilotage fees, fines, and penalties are accounted for and expended according to the Indian Ports Act, 1908.

key_procedures: Appointment of pilots by the Commissioners, requiring Central Government authorization.
Making and enforcing rules for pilots by the Commissioners, subject to Central Government approval and publication.
Levying pilotage fees at rates fixed under the Indian Ports Act, 1908.
Accounting for and expending pilotage fees, fines, and penalties according to the Indian Ports Act, 1908.
Transferring funds between the general and pilotage accounts with Central Government sanction.
administration: Commissioners for the Port of Calcutta, with oversight and approval from the Central Government.
important_notes: Sections 8 and 11 of the Act have been repealed.
The Act makes consequential amendments to the Calcutta Pilots Act, 1859.
The Act incorporates certain provisions of the Calcutta Port Act, 1890, with modifications.

title: The Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948
purpose: To provide for the administration of oaths by diplomatic and consular officers and to prescribe the fees leviable in respect of certain of their official duties.
scope: The Act applies to diplomatic and consular officers exercising their functions in any foreign country or place. It also applies to any State within India for matters related to oaths, affidavits, and notarial acts, as well as the trial of offenses committed under the Act. The scope is global for the officers' actions abroad and national for the legal framework and enforcement within India.

key_definitions.consular_officer: Includes consul-general, consul, vice-consul, consular agent, pro-consul, and any other person authorized to perform the duties of these roles.
key_definitions.diplomatic_officer: Means any ambassador, envoy, minister, charge d'affaires, or secretary of embassy or legation.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948'.
Defines 'consular officer', 'diplomatic officer', and 'prescribed' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers as to oaths and notarial acts abroad
main_sections.description: Grants diplomatic and consular officers the power to administer oaths, take affidavits, and perform notarial acts abroad that a notary public can do within a State. Documents authenticated by their seal and signature are admissible as evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for offences under this Act
main_sections.description: Specifies punishments for swearing falsely in an oath or affidavit administered under the Act, and for forging or fraudulently altering seals or signatures of authorized officers or using such forged documents.
Allows offences under the Act to be tried in any State where the accused person is apprehended or in custody, as if the offence occurred there.

Empowers the Central Government to prescribe fees for services rendered by diplomatic or consular officers in their official capacity, and outlines how these fees should be levied, accounted for, applied, and remitted.

main_sections.section_title: Publication and issue of tables of fees
main_sections.description: Mandates the publication of tables of fees and their free distribution. Diplomatic and consular officers must keep a copy of the fee table exhibited in their office for public inspection.

Authorizes the Central Government to make rules to carry out the Act's purposes, including prescribing fee scales, remuneration for officers, registers to be kept, and the manner of publishing fee tables. Rules made are subject to parliamentary approval.

important_rules: Any oath, affidavit, or notarial act administered, sworn, or done by a diplomatic or consular officer abroad shall be as effective as if done by lawful authority within a State.
Documents bearing the seal and signature of an authorized officer are admissible as evidence without proof of the seal, signature, or official character.
False swearing in an oath or affidavit under the Act is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and a fine.
Forging or fraudulently altering seals/signatures of authorized officers, or tendering/using forged documents, is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and a fine.
Diplomatic or consular officers shall not, unless permitted by rules, ask for or take any fee or reward for their official acts or services.
Tables of fees leviable under the Act must be published and made available for inspection by interested persons.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period and are subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and liability to fine for swearing falsely in an oath or affidavit.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and liability to fine for forging or fraudulently altering seals or signatures, or using forged documents.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government has the power to prescribe fees and make rules. The trial of offenses can occur in any State where the accused is apprehended or in custody.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the legal framework for administering oaths and notarial acts abroad, the penalties for offenses, and the process for trying these offenses within designated States. The Central Government also enforces rules related to fees and their collection.

rights: The right for individuals abroad to have oaths administered, affidavits taken, and notarial acts performed by diplomatic and consular officers.
The right to have documents authenticated by these officers admitted as evidence without further proof of authenticity.
The right to inspect tables of fees in the offices of diplomatic and consular officers.
duties: Diplomatic and consular officers have the duty to administer oaths, take affidavits, and perform notarial acts as authorized.
They have a duty to keep a copy of the table of fees exhibited in their office and allow inspection.
They have a duty not to ask for or take fees or rewards beyond what is prescribed by rules.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the punishments prescribed for offenses under the Act.
Obligation for the Central Government to prescribe rules and fees in a manner that facilitates the Act's purpose.
Obligation for rules to be laid before Parliament for approval.

key_procedures: Administering oaths, taking affidavits, and performing notarial acts abroad by diplomatic or consular officers.
Admission of authenticated documents as evidence without proof of seal or signature.
Inquiry, dealing, trial, and punishment of offenses in any State where the accused is apprehended or in custody.
Prescribing, levying, accounting for, and remitting fees as per Central Government rules.
Publication and display of tables of fees for public inspection.
Making and laying of rules by the Central Government before Parliament.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for prescribing fees and making rules for the administration of this Act. Diplomatic and consular officers administer oaths and perform notarial acts abroad.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to the Union territory of Pondicherry.
Certain provisions (marked with '*') have been omitted or substituted by later amendments.

title: THE COAL MINES PROVIDENT FUND AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ACT, 1948
purpose: To make provisions for the framing of a Provident Fund Scheme, a Pension Scheme, a Deposit linked Insurance Scheme and a Bonus Scheme for persons employed in Coal Mines.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to persons employed in Coal Mines. The definition of 'coal mine' is extensive and includes various excavations, shafts, levels, open cast workings, conveyors, machinery, workshops, offices, power stations, premises for refuse disposal, hospitals, canteens, coke ovens, and ancillary plants. 'Employee' includes any person employed for wages in any kind of work, manual or otherwise, in or in connection with a coal mine, including those employed through contractors and certain other categories like sanitary workers, mális, teachers, domestic servants, apprentices, and trainees who receive remuneration directly from the employer.

key_definitions.bonus: Any sum of money payable to an employee under the Coal Mines Bonus Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.coal_mine: Means any excavation where any operation for the purpose of searching for or obtaining coal has been or is being carried on, and includes various associated structures, machinery, and premises. It also includes any open cast working or quarry not being a shaft or excavation extending below superjacent ground, and coke ovens or plants.
key_definitions.contribution: Means the contribution payable in respect of a member under the Coal Mines Provident Fund Scheme or the contribution payable in respect of an employee to whom the Insurance Scheme applies.
key_definitions.employee: Means any person who is employed for wages in any kind of work, manual or otherwise, in or in connection with a coal mine, and who gets his wages directly or indirectly from the employer. This definition is broad and includes persons employed through contractors and certain other categories.
key_definitions.employer: Means the immediate proprietor, lessee, or occupier of a coal mine. It also includes liquidators, receivers, and managing agents. However, it does not include a person who merely receives royalty, rent, or fine, or is merely the proprietor subject to a lease, grant, or licence, or is merely the owner of the soil. Contractors for working a coal mine are subject to the Act as if they were employers.
key_definitions.fund: Means the provident fund established under the Coal Mines Provident Fund Scheme.
key_definitions.insurance_fund: Means the Deposit-linked Insurance Fund established under sub-section (2) of section 3G.
key_definitions.insurance_scheme: Means the Coal Mines Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme framed under sub-section (1) of section G.
key_definitions.managing_agent: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.member: Means a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.pension_fund: Means the Pension Fund established under sub-section (2) of section 3E.
key_definitions.pension_scheme: Means the Coal Mines Pension Scheme framed under sub-section (1) of section 3E.
key_definitions.superannuation: In relation to an employee who is a member of the Pension Scheme, means the attainment by the employee of such age as is fixed in the contract or conditions of service as the age on the attainment of which such employee shall vacate the employment.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent, which is the whole of India.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'bonus', 'coal', 'coal mine', 'contribution', 'employee', 'employer', 'Fund', 'Insurance Fund', 'Insurance Scheme', 'managing agent', 'member', 'Pension Fund', 'Pension Scheme', and 'superannuation'.

Empowers the Central Government to frame a scheme for the establishment of a provident fund for employees and to specify the coal mines to which the scheme shall apply. It also states that the Fund shall vest in and be administered by the Board of Trustees and that the scheme may provide for matters specified in the First Schedule.

Details the constitution of a Board of Trustees for administering the Fund. The Board consists of a Chairman, the Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner (ex officio), representatives of the Central Government, State Governments, employers, and employees. It also outlines the terms and conditions for board members and the administration of the Fund by the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Board of Trustee to be a body corporate
main_sections.description: Declares the Board of Trustees as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, enabling it to sue and be sued in its corporate name.

Provides for the appointment of a Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner as the chief executive officer of the Board, and other officers to assist him. The Board also has the power to appoint other officers and employees for efficient administration. It specifies the conditions of service, salary, and allowances for these officers.

Governs the transfer of provident fund accumulations when an employee becomes a member of the Coal Mines Provident Fund Scheme or when a member leaves employment in a coal mine and gets re-employed in another establishment with a provident fund.
This section title is listed in the Arrangement of Sections, indicating the Act makes provisions for Coal Mines Bonus Schemes.
This section title indicates that the Act includes provisions for penalties.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of money due from an employer
main_sections.description: This section title indicates provisions related to the recovery of money owed by employers.

main_sections.section_title: Priority of payment of contributions and bonus over other debts
main_sections.description: This section title suggests that contributions and bonus payments have priority over other debts.
This section title indicates the Act provides powers to address and resolve difficulties.
This section title suggests the Act grants powers to exempt certain entities or situations.

important_rules: The Central Government may frame a Coal Mines Provident Fund Scheme for the establishment of a provident fund for employees in coal mines (Section 3(1)).
The Fund shall be vested in and administered by a Board of Trustees constituted by the Central Government (Section 3(1A) and 3A).
The Board of Trustees is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (Section 3B).
The Central Government appoints a Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner as the chief executive officer of the Board (Section 3C(1)).

Provident fund accumulations of employees are transferable when they become members of the Coal Mines Provident Fund Scheme or when they leave a coal mine and join another establishment with a provident fund, subject to scheme provisions (Section 3D).
Schemes framed under the Act are subject to modification (Section 7).
Schemes must be laid before Parliament (Section 7A).

penalties: Section 9 lists 'Penalty', indicating that penalties are defined within the Act, though specifics are not detailed in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board of Trustees, overseen by the Central Government, is responsible for administering the Fund and schemes. The Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner is the chief executive officer. Inspectors are also appointed (Section 10).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act provides for the mode of recovery of money due from an employer (Section 10A). Contributions are to be made by employers and recovered from members (Section 10D). Powers to recover damages are also included (Section 10F).

rights: Employees have the right to a provident fund, pension, and deposit-linked insurance under the respective schemes.
Members have the right to have their provident fund accumulations transferred under specific circumstances (Section 3D).
Employees may have the right to receive bonus payments under the Coal Mines Bonus Schemes.
duties: Employers have a duty to contribute to the provident fund, pension scheme, and insurance scheme for their employees.
Employers have a duty to comply with the provisions of the Coal Mines Bonus Schemes.
Members have a duty to abide by the rules and regulations of the schemes framed under the Act.
obligations: Employers are obligated to pay contributions and bonuses as stipulated by the schemes (Section 10D).
The Board of Trustees has an obligation to administer the Fund and schemes efficiently (Section 3A(3)).
Employers are subject to penalties for non-compliance with the Act and its schemes (Section 9).

key_procedures: Framing of schemes by the Central Government (Section 3(1)).
Constitution of the Board of Trustees by notification (Section 3A(1)).
Transfer of provident fund accounts upon change of employment (Section 3D).
Appointment of officers by the Central Government and the Board (Section 3C).
Determination of moneys due from employers (Section 7B).
Recovery of money due from an employer (Section 10A).
administration: The Central Government, through the Board of Trustees and the Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner, administers the Act and the schemes framed under it. Inspectors are also appointed for enforcement.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective operation for schemes, as indicated by Section 6.
Schemes can be modified (Section 7).
Schemes must be laid before Parliament (Section 7A).
There is a provision for the power to remove difficulties (Section 11B) and the power to exempt (Section 11C).

The Act is to have effect notwithstanding anything contained in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Act 14 of 1947) (though the PDF text mentions Act 31 of 1956, which might be an older reference or a typo in the document itself, Section 11D refers to Act 31 of 1956).
The Act repeals Ordinance 7 of 1948 (Section 12).

title: The Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948
purpose: To provide for the regulation of oilfields and for the development of mineral oil resources in the public interest.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to operations related to prospecting, exploration, development, production, and disposal of mineral oils and the management of oilfields.

key_definitions.mineral_oils: Naturally occurring hydrocarbons in various forms, including crude oil, natural gas, petroleum, condensate, coal bed methane, oil shale, shale gas, shale oil, tight gas, tight oil, and gas hydrate. It excludes coal, lignite, and helium associated with petroleum or shale.
key_definitions.mining_lease: A lease for searching, winning, working, getting, making merchantable, carrying away, or disposing of mineral oils or related purposes. Includes exploring or prospecting licenses granted before the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025.
key_definitions.oilfield: Any area where operations for obtaining mineral oils, refined oil, partially refined oil, or petroleum products are being or are to be carried out.
key_definitions.petroleum_lease: A lease granted on or after the commencement of the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025, for prospecting, exploration, development, production, making merchantable, carrying away, or disposing of mineral oils, or related purposes. Includes a mining lease granted before the commencement of the said Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its extent to the whole of India, and outlines the procedure for its commencement through a Central Government notification.
This section, concerning the declaration of expediency of control by the Central Government, has been omitted.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including lessor, lessee, mineral oils, mining lease, and oilfield.

main_sections.section_title: No petroleum lease to be valid unless it is in accordance with this Act
main_sections.description: Stipulates that petroleum leases granted after the commencement of the Act must comply with the rules made under the Act. Leases granted contrary to this provision are void.

Prohibits any person from undertaking operations for prospecting, exploration, development, or production of mineral oils without a valid lease granted under this Act and its rules, except for operations under licenses or leases granted before the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules as respects petroleum leases
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for regulating the grant, extension, or renewal of petroleum leases, or for prohibiting them in certain areas or for certain mineral oils. It also specifies matters that can be included in these rules, such as application procedures, terms and conditions, area limits, rent fixation, and dispute resolution mechanisms.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules as respects mineral oils development
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for the exploration, development, production, and conservation of mineral oils. This includes regulations on equipment use, drilling operations, production methods, notification of new borings, sampling, storage, royalty collection, submission of returns, sharing of facilities, safety, environmental protection, unitization of leases, and promoting low-carbon operations.

main_sections.section_title: Royalties in respect of mineral oils
main_sections.description: Deals with the payment of royalties by holders of mining leases granted before a certain date, irrespective of the lease instrument or existing laws.
Provides for penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Grants powers of inspection to authorized officials to ensure compliance with the Act and rules.

main_sections.section_title: Relaxation of rules in special cases
main_sections.description: Allows for the relaxation of rules in special cases by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Act to be binding on the Government
main_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of the Act are binding on the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules.

important_rules: No petroleum lease shall be granted after the commencement of this Act otherwise than in accordance with the rules made under this Act. Any lease granted contrary to this provision shall be void (Section 4).
No person shall undertake any operation for prospecting, exploration, development, or production of mineral oils without a valid lease granted under this Act and its rules (Section 4A).
The Central Government has the power to make rules for regulating the grant, extension, or renewal of petroleum leases, including terms, conditions, and fees (Section 5).
The Central Government can make rules for the exploration, development, production, and conservation of mineral oils, covering various aspects of operations and resource management (Section 6).
Royalties are payable in respect of mineral oils produced or collected from leased areas (Section 6A).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act or rules made thereunder are specified in Section 9.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the making and enforcement of rules, inspections, and adjudication/appeal processes as outlined in Sections 9A and 9B.

rights: Right to obtain petroleum leases subject to compliance with Act and rules.
Right to benefit from provisions for dispute resolution through alternative methods.
Right to protection of action taken in good faith.
duties: Duty to obtain valid leases for mineral oil operations.
Duty to comply with the rules made under the Act.
Duty to pay royalties in respect of mineral oils.
Duty to submit special or periodical returns and reports as required.
Obligations towards environmental protection during operations and decommissioning.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the terms and conditions of petroleum leases.
Obligation to follow safety standards and protocols in oilfields.
Obligation to report carbon and greenhouse gas emissions related to mineral oil operations.

key_procedures: Procedure for granting petroleum leases: Applications must be made in accordance with rules, and leases are granted or extended/renewed based on specified terms and conditions (Section 5).
Procedure for development of mineral oils: Rules can prescribe methods for exploration, development, production, conservation, drilling, sampling, storage, and facility sharing (Section 6).
Adjudication and Appeal: Mechanisms for adjudicating disputes and filing appeals are provided (Sections 9A, 9B).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act has undergone several amendments, notably the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025, which introduced significant changes to definitions and provisions.
The terms and conditions of a petroleum lease shall remain stable during its period for efficient development and shall not be altered to the disadvantage of the lessee (Section 5(3)).
Operations undertaken in accordance with licenses or leases granted before the commencement of the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025, are not affected by Section 4A.

title: The Territorial Army Act, 1948
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Territorial Army.
scope: Extends to the whole of India and applies to all classes of persons in the Territorial Army, wherever they may be.

key_definitions.enrolled: Enrolled in the Territorial Army under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.officer: An officer of any of the two classes specified in section 5.
key_definitions.non-commissioned officer: A person holding a non-commissioned rank in the Territorial Army, and includes an acting non-commissioned officer.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public utility service: An undertaking supplying power, light, gas or water to the public, or carrying on public transport, or maintaining public conservancy or sanitation, declared as such by the Central Government by notification.
key_definitions.Regular Army: Officers and other ranks liable to render continuously for a term military service under the Army Act, 1950.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and its application to all classes of persons in the Territorial Army.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'enrolled', 'officer', 'non-commissioned officer', 'prescribed', 'public utility service', and 'Regular Army'.
Establishes the Territorial Army and empowers the Central Government to constitute, disband, or reconstitute its units.
Specifies the classes of persons in the Territorial Army: officers and enrolled persons.

Details the two classes of officers in the Territorial Army: those holding commissions granted by the President with designations corresponding to Regular Army officers, and junior commissioned officers.
States that any citizen of India may offer for enrolment if they satisfy prescribed conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of certain persons for compulsory service in the Territorial Army
main_sections.description: Makes persons employed under the Government or in public utility services, between the ages of 20 and 40, liable for compulsory service in the Territorial Army, subject to prescribed conditions and the authority's call.

Outlines the liability of officers and enrolled persons for military service, including restrictions on service beyond India without Central Government order, service in any unit to which attached, and conditions for being called out for support of civil power, essential guards, training, supplementing regular forces, or attachment to regular forces.

main_sections.section_title: Reinstatement in civil employ of persons required to perform military service
main_sections.description: Imposes a duty on employers to reinstate persons who performed military service in their former employment under not less favourable conditions. It also provides procedures for resolving disputes and penalties for non-compliance.

main_sections.section_title: Preservation of certain rights of persons required to perform military service
main_sections.description: Ensures that persons performing military service retain their rights under provident funds, superannuation funds, or other employee benefit schemes related to their relinquished employment.

States that enrolled persons are entitled to discharge upon expiration of their enrolment period and can be discharged earlier by prescribed authority, provided they are not engaged in military service.

Makes officers and enrolled persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, when doing duty or embodied, with adaptations and modifications made by the Central Government. It also covers the trial and punishment of offences committed under the Army Act.
Allows for summary trial and punishment of enrolled persons in addition to or substitution for punishments under the Army Act, 1950.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for failure to lodge forms duly filled up, etc.
main_sections.description: Deals with punishment for failing to lodge forms duly filled up, etc.
Concerns the jurisdiction to try offences under the Act.
Relates to the presumption of validity for certain documents.

main_sections.section_title: Persons subject to this Act to be deemed part of regular forces for certain purposes
main_sections.description: States that persons subject to this Act are deemed part of the regular forces for certain purposes.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.
This section has been repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: Enrolled persons are subject to military service conditions as prescribed, including being attached to units, called out for civil power support, essential guards, training, supplementing regular forces, or attachment to regular forces.

Rule 2: Employers must reinstate persons who performed military service in their previous employment under favorable conditions, with provisions for dispute resolution and penalties for non-compliance.
Rule 3: Persons performing military service retain rights in their provident and superannuation funds.
Rule 4: Officers and enrolled persons performing military service are subject to the Army Act, 1950, with specified adaptations and modifications.

penalties: Failure by an employer to obey an order regarding reinstatement may result in a fine up to one thousand rupees, and the court may order compensation to the person not re-employed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed authority for reinstatement matters, and criminal courts for other offences. The Army Act, 1950, also applies for military offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, summary trials, and application of the Army Act, 1950.

rights: Right to receive discharge upon completion of enrolment period.
Right to retain rights in provident/superannuation funds during military service.
Right to reinstatement in civil employment after military service.
Rights and privileges as an officer or enrolled person when compelled to join the Territorial Army.
duties: Duty to perform military service when called out or embodied.
Duty to fill up and lodge prescribed forms when required by the prescribed authority.
Duty of employers to reinstate persons after military service.
obligations: Obligation to serve in any unit of the Territorial Army to which attached.
Obligation to be subject to the rules made under the Act.
Obligation to perform military service under prescribed conditions.
Obligation to join the Territorial Army as an officer or enrolled person if services are requisitioned.

key_procedures: Procedure for calling upon persons for compulsory service in the Territorial Army by the prescribed authority, considering age, fitness, qualifications, and experience.
Procedure for employers to reinstate persons after military service, including referral to a prescribed authority for dispute resolution.
Procedure for obtaining discharge from the Territorial Army upon completion of the enrolment period.
administration: Central Government (through relevant departments/agencies, though not explicitly named in the provided text).
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various Union Territories with modifications.
The term 'public utility service' requires a Central Government notification to be declared as such.

Certain categories of persons are excluded from compulsory service under section 6A, including women, members of the Regular Army/Navy/Air Force, persons not citizens of India, and persons employed outside India.
No officer or enrolled person shall be required to perform military service beyond the limits of India except under a general or special order of the Central Government.

title: THE CENTRAL SILK BOARD ACT, 1948
purpose: To provide for the development under Central control of the silk industry and for that purpose to establish a Central Silk Board.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to the silk industry, including aspects like silk-worm seed, production, supply, distribution, trade, and commerce.

key_definitions.Board: The Central Silk Board constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.charkha raw silk: Raw silk reeled from silk worm cocoons with the help of any instrument not worked by power.
key_definitions.filature raw silk: Raw silk reeled from silk worm cocoons with the help of any instrument worked by power.
key_definitions.power: Any form of energy which is mechanically transmitted and is not generated by human or animal agency, and includes electrical energy.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
