key_definitions.spun silk: Silk yarn spun from pierced or spoilt cocoons, fluff from cocoons, pieces of silk, coils, or other silk waste.
key_definitions.Standing Committee: The Standing Committee of the Board constituted under sub-section (2) of section 6.
key_definitions.silk-worm seed or seed: All kinds of silk-worm seeds produced from the pure silk-worm races including the hybrids produced from two or more pure races, silk-worm seed cocoons of all kinds and moths thereof intended to be used or reared for the purpose of production or for commercial exploitation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Central Silk Board Act, 1948' and specifies its territorial extent.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of Union control
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to take control of the silk industry.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'charkha raw silk', 'filature raw silk', 'power', 'prescribed', 'spun silk', 'Standing Committee', and 'silk-worm seed'.

Details the constitution of the Central Silk Board, including the appointment of the Chairperson, nominated officials, elected members from Parliament, and nominated members from state governments and various industry representations.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification for being nominated or appointed as a member of Board
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a person is disqualified from being nominated, appointed, or continuing as a member of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government in default of nominations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make nominations if a state government fails to do so within the prescribed time, and to fill vacancies if the nominating authority fails.
Describes the roles of the Vice-Chairperson and the powers and constitution of a Standing Committee that the Board may form.
Defines the role of the Secretary of the Board, who acts under the control and direction of the Board and Chairperson.

Specifies the primary duty of the Board to promote the development of the silk industry and lists various measures it can undertake, including research, improving cultivation and reeling, marketing, and collecting statistics. It also includes advising the Central Government on silk-related matters and furnishing reports.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Central Silk-worm Seed Committee
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute a Central Silk-worm Seed Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Imposition of cess on certain kinds of silk
main_sections.description: Grants the power to impose a cess on certain kinds of silk.
States that the Central Government has control over the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the power to make regulations.
Provides for penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of sections 8C and 8E
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening sections related to silk-worm seed notification and registration.
Restricts legal proceedings against persons acting in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of Act and rules, etc., inconsistent with other enactments
main_sections.description: Clarifies the effect of the Act and its rules or regulations when they are inconsistent with other enactments.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contravention of the Act's provisions, including specific penalties for contravening sections 8C and 8E related to silk-worm seed notification and registration.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and authorities established or appointed under the Act (e.g., Silk-worm Seed Officers, Seed Certification Agency, Seed Testing Laboratories) are responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is carried out through penalties for contraventions, the establishment of regulatory bodies for silk-worm seed, and the Central Government's oversight and rule-making powers.

rights: Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property (for the Board).
Right to sue and be sued (for the Board).
Right to receive travelling and other allowances (for Board members).
duties: Duty of the Board to promote the development of the silk industry.
Duty of the Board to advise the Central Government on matters related to the silk industry.
Duty of the Board to prepare and furnish reports to the Central Government.
obligations: Obligation to comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
Obligation for silk-worm seed producers to make statements as required.
Obligation to ensure that raw silk is tested and graded if made compulsory by the Board.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Board: The Central Government notifies and constitutes the Board.
Nomination of Members: Members are appointed or elected as per the provisions in Section 4(3).
Filling Vacancies: Procedures for filling vacancies in the Board.

Constitution of Committees: The Central Government can constitute specialized committees like the Central Silk-worm Seed Committee, Hybrid Authorisation Committee, Registration Committee, Seed Certification Agency, and Central Seed Testing Laboratories.
Rule Making: The Central Government can make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Regulation Making: The Board or Committee can make regulations.
administration: The Central Government and the Central Silk Board.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Pondicherry.
The word 'raw' was omitted from 'raw silk industry' by Act 31 of 1953.
Certain parts of the Act concerning Jammu and Kashmir were omitted.
Amendments have been made over time, particularly by Act 42 of 2006, which introduced significant definitions and provisions related to silk-worm seed.
The term of office for Board members is generally not exceeding three years, but the Central Government can terminate the Chairperson's appointment or the Chairperson can resign with notice.

title: The Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948
purpose: To bring the share capital of the Reserve Bank of India into public ownership and to make consequential amendments in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
scope: This act applies to the Reserve Bank of India and its shareholders. Geographically, it applies within India where the Reserve Bank of India operates.

key_definitions.appointed day: Such day as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
key_definitions.Bank: The Reserve Bank of India as constituted by the principal Act.
key_definitions.principal Act: The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Bank', and 'principal Act'.

Details the transfer of Reserve Bank of India shares to the Central Government on the appointed day and the compensation to be paid to shareholders. It also outlines dividends payable to shareholders.

main_sections.section_title: Vacation of office by existing office bearers.
main_sections.description: States that existing Directors (other than Governor or Deputy Governor) and members of Local Boards shall vacate their office on the appointed day. It mentions the reconstitution of the Central and Local Boards as per the principal Act.
Empowers the Governor or a nominated Deputy Governor to exercise all powers of the Bank, subject to restrictions, pending the constitution of the Central Board.

Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to give effect to the objects of the Act, including rules for compensation payment and determination of recipients. It also includes a provision for laying rules before Parliament.
This section, pertaining to amendments to Act 2 of 1934, has been repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: On the appointed day, all shares in the capital of the Bank shall be transferred free of all trusts, liabilities, and encumbrances to the Central Government.

Rule 2: As compensation, the Central Government shall issue promissory notes bearing 3% per annum interest to shareholders, calculated at Rs. 118.10 per share, with provisions for amounts not being multiples of one hundred rupees and special rates for shares obtained at par by Directors.

Rule 3: Shareholders entitled to unpaid dividends before the appointed day shall receive them. Dividends for the period July 1, 1948, to the appointed day shall be calculated at Rs. 4 per annum per share.
Rule 4: Existing Directors (other than Governor/Deputy Governor) and Local Board members shall vacate office on the appointed day.
Rule 5: The Central Government can make rules for compensation payment and recipient determination.
Rule 6: Rules made by the Central Government under this Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specific period, allowing for modifications or annulment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Central Government under Section 6 and the provisions of the principal Act.

rights: Shareholders are entitled to receive compensation in the form of government promissory notes.
Shareholders are entitled to receive accrued and unpaid dividends.
Shareholders are entitled to dividends for the period from July 1, 1948, to the appointed day.
duties: The Central Government has a duty to issue compensation to shareholders.
The Reserve Bank of India has a duty to pay accrued and current dividends to entitled shareholders.
obligations: The Central Government is obligated to facilitate the transfer of shares and provide compensation.
The Reserve Bank of India is obligated to make payments to shareholders as stipulated.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Appointment of 'appointed day' by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.
Procedure 2: Transfer of Reserve Bank of India shares to the Central Government on the appointed day.
Procedure 3: Issuance of government promissory notes as compensation by the Central Government to registered shareholders.
Procedure 4: Payment of dividends to shareholders by the Reserve Bank of India.
Procedure 5: Vacation of office by existing Directors and Local Board members on the appointed day.
Procedure 6: Exercise of powers by the Governor or Deputy Governor during interim arrangements.
Procedure 7: Making and laying of rules by the Central Government before Parliament.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: Section 7 and the Schedule were repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1950.
The provision regarding laying of rules before Parliament was added by Act 4 of 2005.

title: THE POLICE ACT, 1949
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a general police-district embracing two or more Union territories and for the establishment of a police force therefor.
scope: The Act extends to all the Union territories. It applies to the police force constituted for a general police-district, which is defined as a district embracing two or more Union territories. Members of this police force have powers, duties, and privileges throughout the general police-district as if they were police officers under a single State Government.

key_definitions.general_police_district: The general police-district constituted under section 3, which embraces two or more Union territories.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Police Act, 1949. It specifies that the Act extends to all Union territories and will come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government for each Union territory.
Defines 'general police-district' as the area constituted under section 3.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of general police-district embracing two or more Union territories
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute a general police-district comprising two or more Union territories, notwithstanding anything in the Police Act, 1861.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of one police force for general police-district
main_sections.description: States that the entire police establishment within a general police-district shall form a single police force, constituted with a number of officers and men as directed by the Central Government.

Vests the superintendence of the police in a general police-district in the Central Government. The administration is vested in an officer appointed by the Central Government, who will exercise powers similar to an Inspector-General of Police under the Police Act, 1861, as specified by the Central Government.

Provides that, except where expressly stated otherwise in this Act, the provisions of the Police Act, 1861, shall apply to the police force constituted for the general police-district as if it were a police force for a State. Members of this force will have the same powers, duties, privileges, and liabilities as police officers under a State Government throughout the general police-district.
Clarifies that the Act does not affect the provisions of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.

important_rules: Rule 1: The entire police establishment in a general police-district shall constitute a single police force. (Section 4)
Rule 2: The superintendence of the police throughout a general police-district vests in the Central Government. (Section 5(1))
Rule 3: The administration of the police force vests in an officer appointed by the Central Government. (Section 5(2))

Rule 4: The Police Act, 1861, applies to the police force constituted for the general police-district, with members having the same powers, duties, and privileges as police officers under a State Government. (Section 6)

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Police Act, 1861, and the powers vested in the Central Government and its appointed officers.

rights: Members of the police force have the same powers and privileges as police officers under a State Government. (Section 6)
duties: Members of the police force have the same duties as police officers under a State Government. (Section 6)
obligations: Members of the police force are subject to the same liabilities as police officers under a State Government. (Section 6)

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Constitution of a general police-district by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette, comprising two or more Union territories. (Section 3)
Procedure 2: Establishment and constitution of a single police force for the general police-district, with the number of officers and men determined by the Central Government's order. (Section 4)
Procedure 3: Appointment of an officer by the Central Government to administer the police force and exercise specified powers. (Section 5(2))
Procedure 4: Commencement of the Act in a Union territory upon notification by the Central Government in the Official Gazette. (Section 1(3))
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications, and has come into force in Pondicherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Lakshadweep with specified modifications and dates.

References to 'Chief Commissioners' Provinces' and 'Part C States' have been substituted with 'Union territories' and 'Part C State' respectively, indicating amendments made by the Adaptation of Laws (No. 3) Order, 1956.
The Act explicitly saves the provisions of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946. (Section 7)

title: The Central Reserve Police Force Act, 1949
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed Central Reserve Police Force.
scope: Applies to the whole of India and to all members of the Central Reserve Police Force, wherever they may be.

key_definitions.active duty: The duty to restore and preserve order in any local area in the event of any disturbance therein.
key_definitions.close arrest: Confinement within the Force or a detachment of the Force or a post quarter-guard building or tent under charge of a guard.
key_definitions.member of the Force: A person appointed to the Force by the Commandant, or by the Central Government. In specific sections, it also includes persons appointed before or after the Act's commencement by the Central Government.
key_definitions.open arrest: Confinement within the precincts of any barracks, lines or camp for the time being occupied by any part of the Force.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.subordinate officer: A member of the Force of the rank of subedar-major, subedar, jemadar or sub-inspector.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Central Reserve Police Force Act, 1949 and specifies its applicability to the whole of India and its members.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'active duty', 'close arrest', 'the Force', 'member of the Force', 'open arrest', 'prescribed', 'subordinate officer', and refers to meanings of certain terms in the Indian Penal Code.

Establishes the existence of the Central Reserve Police Force as an armed force maintained by the Central Government and outlines that its constitution, pay, pension, and remuneration will be as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and powers of superior officers
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Commandant and other officers (assistant commandants and company officers) and states that these officers shall have powers and authority as provided by the Act.

Details the enrolment process, requiring prospective members to have the recruiting roll read and explained to them and to sign it. It also includes a provision for those who have served for six months.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation and withdrawal from the Force
main_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which members cannot resign (during the term of engagement, except within the first three months) and cannot withdraw from duties without written permission from an authorized officer.

main_sections.section_title: General duties of members of the Force
main_sections.description: Outlines the general duties of members, including obeying lawful orders and warrants, detecting offenders, apprehending individuals, and serving within and beyond India.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence, control and administration of the Force
main_sections.description: Vests superintendence and control of the Force in the Central Government, administered through appointed officers. It also specifies the headquarters and conditions for control while on active duty outside headquarters.
Lists severe offences that members of the Force can commit, such as mutiny, assaulting superior officers, desertion, and acts of cowardice, with corresponding severe punishments.
Details less severe offences, including intoxication on duty, insubordination, losing equipment, malingering, and absence without leave, with prescribed punishments.

Specifies minor punishments that can be awarded for disobedience, neglect of duty, or misconduct, including reduction in rank, fines, confinement, and removal from special positions. It also outlines punishments for petty offences against discipline.

main_sections.section_title: Place of imprisonment and liability to dismissal on imprisonment
main_sections.description: States that members sentenced to imprisonment may be dismissed from the Force and are liable for forfeiture of pay and allowances. It also specifies where imprisonment can occur.
Outlines penal deductions that can be made from a member's pay and allowances for absence, imprisonment, being in custody, and other specified reasons.

important_rules: Members must promptly obey and execute all lawful orders and warrants from competent authorities.
Members are liable to serve within and beyond the territory of India.
Members cannot resign during their engagement term, except within the first three months.
Members cannot withdraw from duties without written permission from an authorized officer.
Recruits must have the recruiting roll read and explained to them and sign it.
Members must report mutinies or conspiracies against the State without delay.
Members must not use criminal force or assault their superior officers.
Members must not shamefully abandon or deliver up posts or guards.
Members must not hold correspondence with or assist those in arms against the State.
Members on active duty must not disobey lawful commands of their superior officers.
Members must not desert the Force.
Sentries must not sleep on duty or leave their post without relief or leave.
Members must not leave their command post or party to go in search of plunder.
Members must not use criminal force or assault persons bringing provisions, force safeguards, break into houses for plunder, or plunder property.
Members must not intentionally cause or spread false alarms.
Members must not display cowardice in the execution of their duty.
Members must not be in a state of intoxication when on duty or warned for duty.
Members must not strike or attempt to force any sentry.
Commanding officers of guards, picquets, or patrols must receive prisoners and not release them or negligently suffer them to escape.
Members under arrest must not leave confinement before lawful authority.
Members must not be grossly insubordinate or insolvent to their superior officers.
Members must not refuse to superintend or assist in making ordered field-work.
Members must not strike or ill-use subordinate members.
Members must not injure, lose, or fraudulently dispose of their arms, clothes, or equipment.
Members must not malinger, feign disease, or intentionally delay their cure.
Members must not voluntarily cause hurt to themselves or others to become unfit for service.
Members must deliver up or account for all issued arms, ammunition, stores, and other property upon ceasing to be a member.
Members must not knowingly furnish false returns or reports, or omit to make required reports.
Members must not absent themselves without leave or overstay granted leave without sufficient cause.
Members must not commit acts prejudicial to good order and discipline not otherwise specified.
Members must not contravene provisions of the Act for which no punishment is expressly provided.

penalties: More heinous offences (Section 9): Punishable with transportation for life or for a term of not less than seven years, or imprisonment up to fourteen years, or fine up to three months' pay, or fine in addition to transportation or imprisonment.
Less heinous offences (Section 10): Punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to three months' pay, or both.

Minor punishments (Section 11): Include reduction in rank, fine not exceeding one month's pay and allowances, confinement to quarters/lines/camp for up to one month, confinement in quarter-guard for up to twenty-eight days, and removal from office of distinction or special emolument.
Penal deductions from pay and allowances (Section 13): Applicable for absence, imprisonment, being in custody, etc.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through its appointed officers (Commandant, assistant commandants, company officers, gazetted officers, subordinate officers).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the awarding of punishments as prescribed for various offences, including imprisonment, fines, and disciplinary actions. Enforcement is carried out by superior officers as defined in the Act and guided by rules made under the Act.

rights: Members have the right to be read and explained the recruiting roll before appointment.
Members have the right to resignation under specific conditions (first three months of service).
Members have the right to be lawfully apprehended and not otherwise.
Members have the right to be protected for acts done in good faith under the Act (Section 17).
duties: Duty to obey and execute all lawful orders and warrants.
Duty to detect and bring offenders to justice.
Duty to apprehend persons legally authorized to be apprehended.
Duty to serve without and beyond as well as within India.
Duty to give immediate information of mutinies or conspiracies to superior officers.
Duty to defend posts and guards committed to their charge.
Duty to not hold correspondence with, assist, or relieve persons in arms against the State.
Duty to not disobey lawful commands of superior officers.
Duty to not desert the Force.
Duty to not sleep on post or quit it without relief or leave.
Duty to not leave post or party to go in search of plunder.
Duty to not use criminal force or assault persons bringing provisions or other necessaries.
Duty to not force a safeguard or break into places for plunder.
Duty to not plunder, destroy, or damage property.
Duty to not intentionally cause or spread false alarms.
Duty to not display cowardice in the execution of duty.
Duty to not be intoxicated on duty.
Duty to not strike or attempt to force a sentry.
Duty of commanding officers to receive prisoners and prevent escapes.
Duty to not leave arrest or confinement before lawful authority.
Duty to not be grossly insubordinate or insolvent to superior officers.
Duty to superintend or assist in making ordered field-work.
Duty to not strike or ill-use subordinate members.
Duty to not injure, lose, or fraudulently dispose of arms, clothes, or equipment.
Duty to not malinger or feign disease.
Duty to not cause hurt to self or others to become unfit for service.
Duty to deliver up or account for all issued property upon ceasing to be a member.
Duty to furnish accurate returns and reports.
Duty to not absent themselves without leave or overstay leave.
Duty to not commit acts prejudicial to good order and discipline.
Duty to not contravene any provision of the Act for which no punishment is expressly provided.
obligations: Members are obligated to enroll by having the recruiting roll read and explained and signing it.
Members are obligated to serve as directed by the Central Government and their superior officers.
Members are obligated to accept punishments awarded under the Act for offences.
Members are obligated to forfeit pay and allowances under certain circumstances as outlined in the Act.

key_procedures: Enrolment Procedure (Section 5): Prospective members must have the recruiting roll read and explained to them and sign it in acknowledgement.

Resignation and Withdrawal Procedure (Section 6): Members must resign during the term of engagement only within the first three months. Withdrawal from duties requires prior written permission from an authorized officer.

Procedure for awarding Minor Punishments (Section 11): The Commandant or prescribed authority can award punishments for misconduct. Specific punishments for petty offences can be awarded by commanding officers of detachments or outposts without formal trial.
Procedure for Imprisonment (Section 12): Persons sentenced to imprisonment may be dismissed and imprisoned in a prescribed prison, or confined in the quarter-guard if not dismissed.
administration: The Central Government, through officers appointed by it, administers the Force. The Headquarters of the Force is at Neemuch or another place specified by the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act was amended to remove 'except the State of Hyderabad' in 1951, indicating its application was broadened.
Definitions of 'assault', 'criminal force', 'fraudulently', 'reason to believe', and 'voluntarily causing hurt' are adopted from the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
The powers and duties of members of the Force can be conferred and imposed by the Central Government.
Acts done before the commencement of the Act may be validated.
The Act provides for the constitution and regulation of an 'armed' Central Reserve Police Force.

title: THE MANGROL AND MANAVADAR (ADMINISTRATION OF PROPERTY) ACT, 1949
purpose: To provide for the vesting of certain properties belonging to the States of Mangrol and Manavadar in Kathiawar in the Managers of the said States, appointed by or on behalf of the Central Government, and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to certain properties belonging to the States of Mangrol and Manavadar. These properties are specified in the Schedule to the Act. The Act's scope is primarily financial and administrative concerning these specific states.

key_definitions.Manager: The Manager for the time being of the State of Mangrol or the State of Manavadar, as the case may be, appointed by, or on behalf of, the Central Government.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Mangrol and Manavadar (Administration of Property) Act, 1949.
Defines the term 'Manager' as the person appointed by or on behalf of the Central Government to manage the State of Mangrol or Manavadar.

Mandates the vesting of properties listed in the Schedule, standing in the name of the Sheikh of Mangrol, Khan of Manavadar, or other specified officials, in the respective Managers of Mangrol and Manavadar, retroactively from November 1, 1947.

Grants the Manager full owner's rights, powers, and authority over properties vested in him, with the caveat that if the property was subject to a lawful trust, the Manager must adhere to the trust's terms.

main_sections.section_title: Payment to Manager to be a discharge of obligations
main_sections.description: States that any payment made to the Manager in discharge of obligations related to the scheduled properties will fully discharge the payer from all liability.

Empowers the Manager to apply to the Reserve Bank of India for duplicate securities if original government securities vested in him are lost or not in his custody. The Reserve Bank is mandated to issue duplicates.

main_sections.section_title: Transfers otherwise than by Manager void
main_sections.description: Declares all transfers or dispositions of scheduled properties made on or after November 1, 1947, by any person other than the Manager, or without the Manager's consent, as void.
Allows the Central Government to require any person possessing property believed to belong to Mangrol or Manavadar to furnish information. Failure to comply is punishable by imprisonment or fine.

Prevents civil or criminal proceedings concerning scheduled properties from being entertained by any court, except at the instance of the Manager. Claims against the Central Government regarding these properties can be submitted directly to the Central Government, whose decision is final.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to add to the Schedule
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to amend or alter the Schedule by notification, including adding new items of property belonging to Mangrol or Manavadar.

Protects the Central Government, Reserve Bank of India, banks, companies mentioned in the Schedule, the Manager, and other persons from legal proceedings for any action taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Repeals the Mangrol and Manavadar (Administration of Property) Ordinance, 1948, and validates actions taken under it as if they were taken under the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Properties described in the Schedule, standing in the names of specified individuals or officials of Mangrol or Manavadar, are deemed vested in the respective Managers from November 1, 1947.
Rule 2: The Manager has all the rights and powers of a full owner over vested properties, subject to any existing lawful trusts.
Rule 3: Payments made to the Manager concerning scheduled properties discharge the payer from all liability.
Rule 4: The Reserve Bank of India shall issue duplicate securities upon application from the Manager if original securities are lost or not in custody.
Rule 5: Any transfer or disposition of scheduled property made after November 1, 1947, by anyone other than the Manager or without his consent is void.
Rule 6: Persons in possession of property belonging to Mangrol or Manavadar must furnish information when requested by the Central Government, or face penalties.
Rule 7: No court can entertain proceedings regarding scheduled properties unless initiated by the Manager.
Rule 8: The Central Government can add to the Schedule of properties via notification.
Rule 9: No legal proceedings lie against the Central Government, RBI, banks, companies, Manager, or others for good faith actions under the Act.

penalties: Imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, for failing to comply with a notice to furnish information regarding property belonging to the State of Mangrol or Manavadar (Section 8(2)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Manager.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Manager regarding property management and disposition, through the Central Government's power to call for information and amend the Schedule, and through the legal framework that bars court jurisdiction except at the Manager's instance.

rights: The Manager has the right to exercise all powers of a full owner over vested properties.
The Central Government has the right to call for information and to add to the Schedule of properties.
Persons making payments to the Manager have the right to a full discharge of liability.
Any person can submit claims regarding scheduled property to the Central Government, whose decision is final.
The Central Government, RBI, banks, companies, Manager, and others have the right to be protected from legal proceedings for good faith actions.
duties: The Manager has a duty to act in accordance with any lawful trusts affecting the properties.
Persons in possession of state property have a duty to furnish information when required by the Central Government.
The Reserve Bank of India has a duty to issue duplicate securities upon application.
obligations: The Manager is obligated to manage the vested properties.
The Manager is obligated to adhere to the terms of any lawful trust associated with the property.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: For obtaining duplicate securities: Manager applies to Reserve Bank of India if original security is lost or not in custody. RBI issues duplicate.
Procedure 2: For verifying property ownership: Central Government issues notice to suspected possessor for information. Failure to comply leads to penalties.
Procedure 3: For claiming property rights: Any person can submit claims to the Central Government. The Central Government's decision is final and not subject to court review.
administration: The Central Government (for appointing Managers, calling for information, adding to Schedule) and the appointed Manager (for administering the properties).
important_notes: The vesting of property is retroactive to November 1, 1947.
Any transfer of scheduled property not made by the Manager or without his consent is void.
Court jurisdiction is barred for matters concerning scheduled properties, except at the instance of the Manager.

title: The High Courts (Seals) Act, 1950
purpose: To provide for the use of seals of common form and design by the High Courts in the States.
scope: Applies to High Courts in States and Courts of the Judicial Commissioner for Union territories. Supersedes any contrary provisions in Letters Patent, Orders, directions, or other laws relating to the use of seals by High Courts.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the High Courts (Seals) Act, 1950.

Details the design and inscriptions for the seals of High Courts in States and Judicial Commissioner's Courts in Union territories. It specifies the use of the Asoka capital, the inscription "THE SEAL OF THE HIGH COURT AT (or OF) .............." followed by the name of the High Court or State, and "Satyameva Jayate" in Devanagari script. For Judicial Commissioner's Courts, the inscription is "THE SEAL OF THE JUDICIAL COMMISSIONER'S COURT FOR ......................." followed by the name of the Union territory.
This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1957.

important_rules: Every High Court in a State shall have and use a seal bearing a device and impression of the Asoka capital with specific inscriptions.
Every Court of the Judicial Commissioner for a Union territory shall have and use a similar seal with a modified inscription.
The provisions of this Act supersede any contrary or inconsistent provisions in any Letters Patent, Order, direction, or other law regarding the use of seals by High Courts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the High Courts and Judicial Commissioner's Courts themselves adhering to the prescribed seals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the mandatory use of the specified seals by the respective courts.

duties: Every High Court in a State has the duty to have and use a seal with the specified design and inscriptions.
Every Court of the Judicial Commissioner for a Union territory has the duty to have and use a seal with the specified design and inscriptions.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely overseen by the Ministry of Law and Justice or equivalent governmental bodies responsible for judicial administration.
important_notes: Section 3 of the Act has been repealed.
The Act supersedes any prior provisions related to High Court seals that are contrary or inconsistent.

title: The Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950
purpose: To prevent the improper use of certain emblems and names for professional and commercial purposes.
scope: Extends to the whole of India and applies to citizens of India outside India. It prohibits the use of specified emblems and names in trade, business, calling, profession, patents, trademarks, or designs without prior permission from the Central Government.

key_definitions.emblem: Any emblem, seal, flag, insignia, coat-of-arms or pictorial representation specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.competent_authority: Any authority competent under any law for the time being in force to register any company, firm, or other body of persons or any trade mark or design or to grant a patent.
key_definitions.name: Includes any abbreviation of a name.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India and citizens outside India), and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines 'emblem', 'competent authority', and 'name' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of improper use of certain emblems and names
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of any name or emblem specified in the Schedule, or any colourable imitation thereof, for any trade, business, calling, profession, in the title of a patent, or in any trademark or design, without the previous permission of the Central Government or an authorized officer.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of registration of certain companies, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the registration of any company, firm, or other body of persons, trademark, design, or patent if its name or emblem contravenes Section 3. It also specifies that the Central Government's decision on whether an emblem is a colourable imitation is final.
Prescribes a penalty of a fine up to five hundred rupees for contravention of the provisions of Section 3.
Mandates that no prosecution for an offense under the Act can be instituted without the previous sanction of the Central Government or an authorized officer.
Clarifies that the Act does not exempt any person from any suit or other proceedings that could be brought against them apart from this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to amend the Schedule
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to add to or alter the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act and requires such rules to be laid before Parliament for approval.

important_rules: No person shall use or continue to use any name or emblem specified in the Schedule, or any imitation thereof, for trade, business, profession, in patent titles, trademarks, or designs without prior permission from the Central Government or an authorized officer.
Competent authorities are prohibited from registering companies, firms, trademarks, designs, or granting patents if their names or emblems contravene Section 3.
Any use of names or emblems must be in accordance with the cases and conditions prescribed by the Central Government.

penalties: Fine up to five hundred rupees for contravening Section 3.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government or an officer authorized by the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution which requires previous sanction from the Central Government or an authorized officer. Registration authorities are also prohibited from registering items that contravene the Act.

rights: Right to use specified emblems and names with prior permission from the Central Government or authorized officer.
duties: Duty not to use prohibited emblems and names in trade, business, profession, patents, trademarks, or designs without permission.
Duty for competent authorities to ensure compliance before registration.
obligations: Obligation to obtain previous sanction for prosecution for any offence under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission to use specified emblems and names, as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
Procedure for registration of companies, trademarks, designs, and patents, requiring verification that names and emblems do not contravene Section 3.
Procedure for referring questions about an emblem to the Central Government for a final decision.
administration: The Central Government (through notifications and rule-making powers).
important_notes: The Schedule lists numerous specific names and emblems, including those of international organizations, government seals, national flags, and names of prominent personalities, that are protected under this Act.
The Act also prohibits names that suggest patronage of the government or connection with government-constituted bodies.
Amendments and additions to the Schedule can be made by the Central Government via notification.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for approval or modification.

title: The Special Criminal Courts (Jurisdiction) Act, 1950
purpose: To confer upon special criminal courts, constituted by or under certain State laws, jurisdiction to try offences against laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the Union List.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. It applies to offences against laws related to matters enumerated in the Union List (List I in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution).

key_definitions.special_criminal_court: Any special court of criminal jurisdiction constituted by or under any law included in the Schedule.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial application.
Defines the term 'special criminal court' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of special criminal courts to try offences with respect to matters in the Union List
main_sections.description: Confers jurisdiction on special criminal courts to try offences against laws related to Union List matters, notwithstanding any other existing law, provided the court is otherwise competent.
Grants the Central Government the power to add other State laws providing for the trial of offences by special criminal courts to the Schedule via notification in the Official Gazette.
Repeals the Special Criminal Courts (Jurisdiction) Ordinance, 1950. It also includes a saving clause for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule 1: Special criminal courts can try offences against laws relating to matters in the Union List, provided they are otherwise competent under their constituting law.
Rule 2: The Central Government can add State laws to the Schedule through a notification, thereby extending the Act's applicability to those laws.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implies the respective special criminal courts and potentially the Central Government for adding to the schedule.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By enabling special criminal courts to try specific offences.

rights: The right of special criminal courts to try offences related to Union List matters.
The right of the Central Government to add State laws to the Schedule.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: For a special criminal court to try an offence, it must be constituted under a law in the Schedule and be competent to try such an offence under that law.
Procedure 2: For the Central Government to add a State law to the Schedule, it must issue a notification in the Official Gazette.
administration: The Central Government is involved in administering the addition to the Schedule.
important_notes: The Act replaced the Special Criminal Courts (Jurisdiction) Ordinance, 1950.

The inclusion of West Bengal Criminal Law Amendment (Special Courts) Act, 1949 and Tribunals of Criminal Jurisdiction Ordinance, 1952 (West Bengal Ordinance) in the Schedule as per notifications indicates amendments and additions over time.

title: The Transfer of Prisoners Act, 1950
purpose: To provide for the removal from one State to another of persons confined in a prison.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to persons confined in prisons for various reasons including sentence of death, imprisonment, transportation, default of payment of fine, or default of giving security for keeping the peace or maintaining good behaviour.

key_definitions.court: Includes any officer lawfully exercising civil, criminal or revenue jurisdiction.
key_definitions.government_or_state_government: In relation to a Part C State, means the administrator thereof.
key_definitions.prison: Includes any place which has been declared by the State Government, by general or special order, to be a subsidiary jail.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its territorial extent, which is the whole of India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'court', 'Government' or 'State Government', and 'prison'.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of prisoners from one State to another
main_sections.description: Outlines the process and conditions for removing a prisoner from a prison in one State to a prison in another State, with the consent of the receiving State's Government. It also specifies that the receiving prison official must detain the prisoner according to the original commitment.
This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1957.

important_rules: Rule: A prisoner confined in a prison in one State can be removed to a prison in another State if the Governments of both States consent.

Rule: The removal is permissible if the prisoner is under sentence of death, or under or in lieu of a sentence of imprisonment or transportation, or in default of payment of a fine, or in default of giving security for keeping the peace or for maintaining good behaviour.
Rule: The officer in charge of the receiving prison must detain the prisoner as per the original writ, warrant, or order of commitment, until discharged or removed according to law.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Governments
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the State Government providing for the removal of the prisoner.

duties: Duty of the officer in charge of the receiving prison to receive and detain the prisoner according to the exigency of the original commitment.

key_procedures: Procedure: For removal of a prisoner from one State to another: 1. A prisoner is confined in a prison in State A. 2. The Government of State A seeks consent from the Government of State B for removal. 3. Upon obtaining consent, the Government of State A issues an order for the prisoner's removal to a prison in State B. 4. The officer in charge of the prison in State B receives and detains the prisoner as per the original court order.
administration: State Governments
important_notes: Note: The Act was extended to various territories including Kohima and Mokakchung Districts, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Goa, Daman and Diu.
Note: The extension of the Act to the State of Jammu and Kashmir was omitted.

Note: The original Act aimed to fill a lacuna in the Prisoners’ Act, 1900, which did not provide for inter-State transfer of prisoners between Part A, C, and D States and Part B States and vice-versa.

title: The Union Territories (Laws) Act, 1950
purpose: To provide for the extension of laws to certain Union territories, particularly Part C States (which later became Union territories), and to empower the Central Government to extend existing enactments to these territories with necessary restrictions and modifications.
scope: Geographical scope includes Union territories (initially referred to as Part C States) such as Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, and Vindhya Pradesh. Subject matter scope involves the extension of various enactments (Acts and Ordinances) from other States to these Union territories.

key_definitions.Union territory: Refers to former Part C States as defined in the Constitution.
key_definitions.State: Refers to Part A States as defined in the Constitution.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Union Territories (Laws) Act, 1950' and specifies its commencement date as April 16, 1950.

main_sections.section_title: Power to extend enactments to certain Union territories
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to extend any enactment in force in a State to specific Union territories (Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, or Tripura) by notification in the Official Gazette, with any necessary restrictions and modifications.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of laws to Tripura, Vindhya Pradesh and Manipur
main_sections.description: Extends specific Acts and Ordinances, as listed in the Schedule to the Merged States (Laws) Act, 1949, to Tripura and Vindhya Pradesh. It also extends these to Manipur, with specific modifications to the Indian Penal Code concerning age limits for certain offenses. It also outlines conditions for the extension of certain Acts to Manipur based on the Union Territories (Laws) Amendment Act, 1956.

Repeals Section 7 of the Delhi Laws Act, 1912, and the Ajmer Merwara (Extension of Laws) Act, 1947, along with any corresponding laws in force in Manipur, Tripura, and Vindhya Pradesh before the extension of the Acts by this Act. It includes savings provisions to ensure the previous operation of repealed laws, penalties, and legal proceedings are not affected, and actions taken under repealed laws are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

important_rules: The Central Government can extend any existing State law to specified Union territories via a gazetted notification.
The extension can be subject to restrictions and modifications deemed necessary by the Central Government.
Specific Acts and Ordinances were extended to Tripura and Vindhya Pradesh.
The Indian Penal Code was to be applied to Manipur with specific age modifications for offenses related to the age of consent and marriage.

penalties: Penalties incurred under previous laws that are repealed and superseded by this Act are preserved.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, and by extension, the relevant authorities in the Union territories to which the laws are extended.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the Central Government to extend enactments, and through the existing legal and judicial machinery in the Union territories.

rights: Citizens residing in the extended Union territories gain the benefit of laws that were previously only in force in other States.
The right of the Central Government to legislate for these territories by extending existing laws.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to issue necessary notifications for the extension of laws.
Duty of the courts and authorities in the Union territories to apply the extended laws, with necessary adaptations.
obligations: Obligation to adapt the applied laws for facilitating their application in the new territories.

key_procedures: Central Government issues a notification in the Official Gazette to extend an enactment to a Union territory.
The notification can include restrictions and modifications to the enactment.
For Tripura, Vindhya Pradesh, and Manipur, specific Acts and Ordinances were extended either directly or with modifications as outlined in Section 3 and the Schedule.
administration: The Central Government (Ministry of Home Affairs, historically, for matters concerning Union Territories).
important_notes: The Act was enacted to address the legislative needs of 'Part C States' which were later organized as Union territories.
Specific amendments were made to the Indian Penal Code for its application in Manipur due to local customs.
The Schedule to the Act specifies certain Acts that were not extended to Manipur initially or were extended later with amendments, highlighting a phased approach to legislative integration.
An explanation clarifies that references to Manipur and Tripura after October 31, 1956, should be construed as references to the Union territories of Manipur and Tripura respectively.

title: The Army and Air Force (Disposal of Private Property) Act, 1950
purpose: To provide for the disposal of the private property of persons subject to the Army Act, 1950 or the Air Force Act, 1950, who die or desert or are ascertained to be of unsound mind or while on active service are officially reported to be missing.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Applies to citizens of India and persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, or the Air Force Act, 1950, wherever they may be.

key_definitions.Committee: The Committee of Adjustment constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regimental and other debts in camp or qu: Includes moneys due as military debts (Army Act) or air force debts (Air Force Act) for quarters, mess, band and other accounts, and military/air force clothing, appointments and equipment not exceeding three months' pay and due within eighteen months before death.
key_definitions.representation: Includes probate, letters of administration (with or without will annexed) and a succession certificate.
key_definitions.representative: Any person who has taken out representation, but does not include an Administrator General.

main_sections.description: States the short title, the geographical and personal extent of the Act, and the date of its commencement.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Committee', 'prescribed', 'regimental and other debts in camp or quarters', 'representation', and 'representative'. It also clarifies that words and expressions defined in the Army Act, 1950 or the Air Force Act, 1950, shall have their respective meanings if not defined in this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Property of deceased persons and deserters other than officers
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for commanding officers to secure, inventory, and draw pay and allowances for the property of deceased or deserted persons (not officers). It details the payment of regimental and other debts, funeral expenses, and the collection and disposition of remaining money. It also specifies the process for delivering property to a representative or selling it if no representative is available.

main_sections.section_title: Property of officers who die or desert
main_sections.description: Extends the provisions of section 3 to officers, with the modification that the functions of the commanding officer are performed by a Committee of Adjustment.

main_sections.section_title: Decision of questions as to regimental and other debts in camp or quarters
main_sections.description: Establishes that the decision of the prescribed person shall be final and binding on all persons regarding any doubt or difference concerning regimental and other debts in camp or quarters.

main_sections.section_title: Representative powers of commanding officer or Committee
main_sections.description: Grants the commanding officer or Committee the same rights and powers as if they had taken out representation to the estate of the deceased, for the purpose of exercising their duties under sections 3 or 4. Receipts given by them are deemed valid.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to hand over estate of deceased person to the Administrator General
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct that the estate of a deceased person be handed over to the Administrator General for administration, with specific provisions for priority of regimental debts and fees charged by the Administrator General.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of surplus by prescribed persons
main_sections.description: Details the process for the 'prescribed person' to dispose of surplus funds received from the estate. This includes paying the representative if known, publishing notices if no representative is known, and eventually depositing the unclaimed surplus to the credit of the Central Government.
Covers the procedure for disposing of movable property that is not money, belonging to a deceased person.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of certain property without production of probate, etc.
main_sections.description: Permits the disposal of certain property without the production of probate or letters of administration, under specified conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Discharge of commanding officer, Committee, prescribed person and the Central Government
main_sections.description: Provides for the discharge of the commanding officer, Committee, prescribed person, and the Central Government from any liability concerning the estate after its proper disposal.

main_sections.section_title: Property in the hands of commanding officer, Committee or prescribed person not to be assets where commanding officer, Committee or prescribed person is stationed
main_sections.description: Clarifies that property held by these authorities is not considered assets at their stationed location for the purpose of legal proceedings against them.
Reserves the rights of the legal representative of a deceased person.

main_sections.section_title: Application of sections 3 to 13 to persons of unsound mind or to persons reported missing on active service
main_sections.description: Extends the provisions of sections 3 to 13 to individuals of unsound mind or those officially reported missing on active service.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of standing Committee of Adjustment in certain cases
main_sections.description: Empowers the appointment of a standing Committee of Adjustment in specific circumstances.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
This section has been repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: On the death or desertion of a person subject to Army or Air Force Acts (excluding officers), the commanding officer must secure movable property, make an inventory, draw pay/allowances, and provide for regimental and other debts.
Rule 2: If necessary, the commanding officer can collect money from banks or other institutions by requisition for the payment of debts, funeral expenses, and administrative costs.

Rule 3: Where the representative of a deceased person has provided security for debts and expenses, the commanding officer shall deliver the property to that representative, ceasing his responsibility.
Rule 4: If no representative provides security or for deserters, the commanding officer may sell or convert movable property into money to cover debts and expenses.

Rule 5: Surplus money after paying debts and expenses goes to the deceased's representative. If no claim is made within 12 months, it goes to the prescribed person. For deserters, surplus is paid to the prescribed person and forfeited to the Central Government after three years, unless the deserter surrenders or is apprehended. The prescribed person can pay the surplus to the deserter's wife, children, or dependants during this period.
Rule 6: For officers who die or desert, a Committee of Adjustment handles the property disposal under section 3's provisions.
Rule 7: The Central Government can direct the handover of an estate to the Administrator General for administration, with regimental debts having priority.
Rule 8: The Administrator General shall not charge more than three percent of the gross amount for his duties under this section.

Rule 9: The prescribed person receiving surplus funds must pay it to the representative if known. If not known and not disposed of under section 10, notices are published annually for six years. If no claim is made within six months of the last notice, the surplus is deposited to the Central Government.
Rule 10: Specific property can be disposed of without full probate or letters of administration, as detailed in section 10.

rights: Right of the representative of a deceased person to receive any surplus property after debts and expenses are paid.
Right of a deserter's wife, children, or dependants to receive all or part of the surplus if the deserter is not apprehended.
Right of any person to claim surplus funds deposited with the Central Government, if they are otherwise entitled.
duties: Duty of commanding officers to secure and manage the property of deceased or deserted persons.
Duty of banks and other institutions to comply with requisitions for money from commanding officers.
Duty of the prescribed person to publish notices for unclaimed surplus funds.
Duty of the Administrator General to administer estates according to law and pay surplus to heirs or prescribed person.
obligations: Obligation of the commanding officer to make provision for regimental and other debts, funeral expenses, and administrative costs.
Obligation of the Central Government to ensure the proper administration of estates handed over to the Administrator General.
Obligation of the Administrator General to prioritize regimental and other debts in camp or quarters.

key_procedures: Procedure for securing and inventorying the movable property of deceased or deserted persons (non-officers) by the commanding officer.
Procedure for drawing pay and allowances due to deceased or deserted persons.
Procedure for the commanding officer to collect money from banking companies or other institutions upon requisition.
Procedure for the commanding officer to deliver property to a representative upon security being provided.
Procedure for selling or converting movable property into money if no representative provides security or for deserters.
Procedure for the commanding officer to pay debts, expenses, and funeral costs from the realized money.
Procedure for the disbursement of surplus money to the representative or prescribed person, and the forfeiture of surplus for deserters.
Procedure for the disposal of property of officers, involving a Committee of Adjustment.
Procedure for the Central Government to hand over estates to the Administrator General.
Procedure for the Administrator General to administer estates and pay surplus to heirs or the prescribed person.
Procedure for the prescribed person to handle unclaimed surplus funds, including publication of notices and deposit with the Central Government.
administration: Central Government, with roles for commanding officers, Committees of Adjustment, prescribed persons, and Administrator Generals.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Pondicherry, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli with modifications.
The Act came into force on 22nd July, 1950.
The definition of 'officer' for persons subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, includes a warrant officer who has died or deserted.
The Administrator General's fees are capped at three percent of the gross amount handled.

title: The Representation of the People Act, 1950
purpose: To provide for the allocation of seats in, and the delimitation of constituencies for the purpose of election to, the House of the People and the Legislatures of States, the qualifications of voters at such elections, the preparation of electoral rolls, the manner of filling seats in the Council of States to be filled by representatives of Union territories, and matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the House of the People (Lok Sabha), the Legislatures of States (State Legislative Assemblies and Legislative Councils), and Union territories in India. It covers the allocation of seats, delimitation of constituencies, qualifications of voters, preparation of electoral rolls, and related matters.

key_definitions.assembly_constituency: A constituency provided by law for the purpose of elections to the Legislative Assembly of a State.
key_definitions.council_constituency: A constituency provided by law for the purpose of elections to the Legislative Council of a State.
key_definitions.election_commission: The Election Commission appointed by the President under article 324 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.order: An order published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.parliamentary_constituency: A constituency provided by law for the purpose of elections to the House of the People.
key_definitions.person: Does not include a body of persons.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.state_government: In relation to a Union territory, means the administrator thereof.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called 'The Representation of the People Act, 1950'.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'article', 'Assembly constituency', 'Council constituency', 'Election Commission', 'order', 'Parliamentary constituency', 'person', 'prescribed', 'State', and 'State Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seats in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Specifies the allocation of seats to the States in the House of the People and the number of seats to be reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in each State, as detailed in the First Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Filling of seats in the House of the People and parliamentary constituencies
main_sections.description: Deals with how seats in the House of the People are filled, stating that all seats allotted to States are to be filled by direct election from parliamentary constituencies. It also defines parliamentary constituencies as single-member constituencies and outlines how States with only one allotted seat form a single constituency. It refers to the Delimitation Commission's orders for determining the extent of constituencies.

main_sections.section_title: Total number of seats in Legislative Assemblies and Assembly Constituencies
main_sections.description: Specifies the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State, to be filled by direct election from Assembly Constituencies, and the number of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, as per the Second Schedule. It includes a proviso for the State of Nagaland regarding seats allocated to the Tuensang district.
Provides for the appointment of Chief Electoral Officers.
Provides for the appointment of Electoral Registration Officers.
Provides definitions for Part III, which deals with electoral rolls for Assembly constituencies.
Mandates the preparation of an electoral roll for every constituency.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualifications for registration in an electoral roll
main_sections.description: Outlines the grounds on which a person may be disqualified from being registered in an electoral roll.

main_sections.section_title: Preparation and revision of electoral rolls
main_sections.description: Details the process for the preparation and revision of electoral rolls.
Deals with the consequences of making false declarations in connection with electoral matters.

main_sections.section_title: Breach of official duty in connection with the preparation, etc., of electoral rolls
main_sections.description: Addresses breaches of official duty related to the preparation and maintenance of electoral rolls.

important_rules: All seats in the House of the People allotted to States are filled by direct election from parliamentary constituencies.
Every parliamentary constituency is a single-member constituency.
An electoral roll must be prepared for every constituency.
Certain disqualifications prevent a person from being registered in an electoral roll.
False declarations made in connection with electoral matters are prohibited.
Breaches of official duty related to electoral rolls are addressed.

penalties: Section 31: Making false declarations can lead to penalties.
Section 32: Breach of official duty in connection with electoral rolls can lead to penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Election Commission of India and relevant state authorities are responsible for the enforcement of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes the preparation and revision of electoral rolls, delimitation of constituencies, and legal action against those who violate provisions such as making false declarations or breaching official duties.

rights: The right to be registered as an elector in a constituency if eligible.
The right to vote in elections from designated constituencies.
duties: Duty to ensure the accuracy and integrity of electoral rolls.
Duty of officials to perform their duties without breach.
Duty to not make false declarations.
obligations: Obligation to follow the prescribed procedures for electoral roll preparation and revision.
Obligation to adhere to the allocation of seats and delimitation of constituencies as defined by the Act and related orders.

key_procedures: Preparation and revision of electoral rolls: This involves identifying eligible voters, registering them, and keeping the rolls up-to-date.
Delimitation of constituencies: The process of defining the geographical boundaries of parliamentary and assembly constituencies.
Allocation of seats: Determining the number of seats for each State in the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies, including reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
administration: The administration of this Act primarily falls under the purview of the Election Commission of India, along with State Governments and their designated officials.
important_notes: The Act has undergone numerous amendments over the years, as indicated by the 'LIST OF AMENDING ACTS'.
Certain sections (e.g., 3A, 5, 6, 9A, 9B, 26) have been repealed or omitted.
The Act defines 'State' to include a 'Union territory' for its purposes.
Specific provisions exist for the State of Sikkim and Union territories regarding electoral colleges and representation in the Council of States.

title: THE VISVA-BHARATI ACT, 1951
purpose: To declare the institution known as “Visva-Bharati” to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its functioning as a unitary teaching and residential university.
scope: The Act applies to the institution known as Visva-Bharati, declared as a university of national importance. It governs its academic activities, administration, officers, authorities, and general functioning. Its territorial jurisdiction is the subject of Section 7, with provisions for maintenance of examination centers outside these limits (Section 7A). The university is to be open to all races, creeds, and classes (Section 8).

key_definitions.academic_staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the statutes.
key_definitions.adhyapaka: Includes Professor, Reader, Lecturer, and any other person engaged in imparting instruction in relation to any learning process and designated as an adhyapaka by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.University: Means the institution known as Visva-Bharati and incorporated as a University under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Visva-Bharati as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares Visva-Bharati, founded by Rabindranath Tagore, as an institution of national importance and constitutes it as a University.

Defines various terms used in the Act and Statutes, including academic staff, Acharya (Chancellor), Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor), adhyapaka, Alumni Association, approved institution, Bhavana, campus, Chatravasa, Department, employee of the University, Institute Board, Institution, Karma-Samiti (Executive Council), Patha-Samiti (Board of Studies), prescribed, Samsad (Court), Siksha-Samiti (Academic Council), Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and University.

Constitutes the first Acharya, Upacharya, and members of the Samsad as a body corporate named Visva-Bharati, a unitary, teaching, and residential University, with perpetual succession and a common seal.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of incorporation of the University in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies the effects of incorporation, including construing references to the Society of Visva-Bharati as references to the University, transferring property, assets, rights, and liabilities of the Society to the University, and ensuring that existing employees continue with the same terms and conditions of service.

Outlines the primary objects of the University, which are to disseminate and advance knowledge and understanding through instructional, extension, and research facilities, and to harmonize cultures of India, the East, and the West. It also references Rabindranath Tagore's expressed objects for Visva-Bharati.

main_sections.section_title: Principles to be followed in organising activities of the University
main_sections.description: States that the University should have due regard to the pattern of education envisaged by Rabindranath Tagore in its activities and academic programmes.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing facilities for studies, research, socially useful productive work, community service, undertaking educational experiments, making provision for research and advisory services, co-operating with other institutions, establishing and maintaining various academic and residential units, organizing application of learning to village problems, promoting adult education and nation-building activities, establishing examination centers, granting diplomas and degrees, conferring honorary degrees, determining admission standards, supervising student residences, regulating student conduct, creating teaching and academic posts, and appointing various academic personnel.

important_rules: University must provide facilities for studies, instruction, socially useful productive work, community service, and research (Section 6(1)).
University shall have due regard to the objects for which Visva-Bharati was founded by Rabindranath Tagore (Section 5A(1)).
University activities and academic programmes should adhere to the pattern of education envisaged by Rabindranath Tagore (Section 5B).
University must be open to all races, creeds, and classes (Section 8).
Adhyapakas of the University are to be appointed under a written contract (Section 37).
Provisions for Pension and provident funds are to be made (Section 39).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for commencement notification, Section 1(2)) and University authorities (for various powers and regulations).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the University authorities as detailed in the Act, and through adherence to the provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.

rights: Employees retain rights to pension and gratuity as they would have held under the Society (Section 5(iii)).
Right to sue and be sued by the name of Visva-Bharati (Section 4).
Right to grant diplomas, certificates, and confer degrees (Section 6(11)).
Right to confer honorary degrees (Section 6(12)).
duties: Duty to disseminate and advance knowledge and understanding (Section 5A(1)).
Duty to harmonize cultures of India, the East, and the West (Section 5A(2)).
Duty to have due regard to Rabindranath Tagore's educational vision (Section 5B).
Duty to provide facilities for studies, instruction, work, and research (Section 6(1)).
Duty to supervise student residences and promote their health and welfare (Section 6(14)).
Duty to regulate student conduct and take disciplinary measures (Section 6(16)).

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement of the Act: Central Government notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).
Procedure for incorporation of the University: Appointment of Acharya, Upacharya, and members of the Samsad by the Central Government (Section 4).
Procedure for transferring property, assets, rights, and liabilities from the Society to the University (Section 5(ii)).
Procedure for modifying terms and conditions of service for existing employees: Execution of a fresh contract, with termination options if the employee is not agreeable (Section 5(iii)).
Procedures for making Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations are detailed in Sections 28, 30, and 31 respectively, with specific matters to be provided for in Ordinances listed in Section 29.
administration: Visva-Bharati University, administered by its various authorities including the Acharya (Chancellor), Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor), Samsad (Court), Karma-Samiti (Executive Council), and Siksha-Samiti (Academic Council).
important_notes: The Act was amended significantly by Act 31 of 1984, particularly regarding definitions, objects, and powers of the University.
Section 15, pertaining to 'The Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor)', was omitted.
The First Schedule was repealed.
The Act emphasizes the historical founding principles and educational philosophy of Rabindranath Tagore.

title: The President’s Emoluments and Pension Act, 1951
purpose: To provide for the emoluments of the President and for pensions to retiring Presidents.
scope: This Act applies to the President of India and their spouse. It outlines provisions for emoluments, pensions, and related benefits. The scope is national, pertaining to the highest office in the country.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The President’s Emoluments and Pension Act, 1951'.
