key_definitions.ready_delivery_contract: A contract which provides for the delivery of goods and the payment of a price therefor, either immediately or within such period not exceeding eleven days after the date of the contract and subject to such conditions as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify in respect of any goods.
key_definitions.option_in_goods: An agreement, by whatever name called, for the purchase or sale of a right to buy or sell, or a right to buy and sell, goods in future, and includes a teji, a mandi, a teji-mandi, a galli, a put, a call or a put and call in goods.
key_definitions.recognised_association: An association to which recognition for the time being has been granted by the Central Government under section 6 in respect of goods or classes of goods specified in such recognition.
key_definitions.registered_association: An association to which for the time being a certificate of registration has been granted by the Commission under section 14B.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and commencement dates for its provisions.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'association', 'commission', 'forward contract', 'goods', 'ready delivery contract', 'option in goods', 'recognised association', and 'registered association'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and constitution of the Forward Markets Commission
main_sections.description: Details the establishment of the Forward Markets Commission by the Central Government, its composition (number of members, appointment of Chairman), qualifications for members, term of office, and conditions of service.

Outlines the functions of the Forward Markets Commission, including advising the Central Government on recognition of associations, keeping forward markets under observation, collecting and publishing information on trading conditions, submitting reports, making recommendations for improving forward markets, and inspecting accounts of associations.

Grants the Commission powers similar to a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning persons, enforcing attendance, examining on oath, requiring production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, and requisitioning public records.

main_sections.section_title: Forward contracts in notified goods illegal or void in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare forward contracts in notified goods as illegal or void under specific circumstances.
Provides for the prohibition of options in goods.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Forward contracts in notified goods may be declared illegal or void by the Central Government.
The Central Government has the power to prohibit forward contracts in certain cases.
Options in goods are prohibited.
Members of recognized associations or registered associations may be suspended or prohibited from trading by the Commission.
The Commission has powers of a civil court for summoning, examining, and requiring production of documents.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 20).
Penalty for owning or keeping a place used for entering into forward contracts in goods (Section 21).
Power of the court to order forfeiture of property (Section 21A).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Forward Markets Commission, Central Government, and Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties, power to search and seize, presumptions in certain cases, and by conferring civil court powers on the Commission. Offences can be cognizable and tried by specific courts.

rights: Members of recognized associations have rights related to their trading activities as governed by the association's rules and bye-laws.
The Commission has the right to inspect accounts and documents of associations and their members.
duties: Associations have duties to regulate and control the business of sale or purchase of goods.
Members of associations have duties to comply with the rules and bye-laws of their respective associations.
Associations are required to furnish annual reports to the Central Government.
Members of the Commission have a duty to avoid conflicts of interest.
obligations: Associations must obtain a certificate of registration from the Commission to operate.
Parties entering into forward contracts must adhere to the regulations stipulated by the Act.

key_procedures: Application for recognition of an association by the Central Government (Section 5).
Grant or refusal of recognition to an association (Section 6).
Withdrawal of recognition (Section 7).
Procedure for making rules by recognized associations (Section 10, 11).
Procedure for suspension of trading or members by the Commission (Section 12B).
Procedure for superseding the governing body of a recognized association (Section 13).
Procedure for obtaining a certificate of registration by associations (Section 14A).
Procedure for searching and seizing books of account or documents (Section 22A).
administration: The Central Government and the Forward Markets Commission.
important_notes: The Act has been amended over the years by various amending Acts.
The Act was extended to Pondicherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications.
The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted from the extent clause.

The definition of 'ready delivery contract' includes a proviso detailing conditions under which a contract will not be deemed as such, especially concerning tendering of documents or realization of differences.
The definition of 'forward contract' was amended to omit 'at a future date'.

title: The Inflammable Substances Act, 1952
purpose: To declare certain substances to be dangerously inflammable and to provide for the regulation of their import, transport, storage, and production by applying thereto the Petroleum Act, 1934, and the rules thereunder, and for certain matters connected with such regulation.
scope: This Act applies to substances declared dangerously inflammable, and the regulation of their import, transport, storage, and production. The Petroleum Act, 1934, is applied to these substances. The Act is enacted by the Parliament of India and its application extends to the territories of India, with specific extensions noted for Pondicherry, Goa, Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

key_definitions.dangerously inflammable substance: Any liquid or other substance declared to be dangerously inflammable by this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Inflammable Substances Act, 1952.
Defines 'dangerously inflammable substance' and 'Petroleum Act'.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain substances to be dangerously inflammable
main_sections.description: Declares specific liquids and substances, including acetone, calcium phosphide, carbide of calcium, cinematograph films with a nitro-cellulose base, ethyl alcohol, methyl alcohol, and wood naphtha, as dangerously inflammable.

main_sections.section_title: Power to apply Petroleum Act to dangerously inflammable substances
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to apply any or all provisions of the Petroleum Act and its rules to any dangerously inflammable substance via notification. It also allows the Central Government to make rules for testing such substances.

main_sections.section_title: Operation of certain notifications and rules
main_sections.description: Deems notifications or rules issued under section 30 of the Petroleum Act between April 1, 1937, and the commencement of this Act as issued or made under this Act and continues their force.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain acts and indemnity in respect thereof
main_sections.description: Validates acts of executive authority, proceedings, and sentences done concerning inflammable substances between April 1, 1937, and the commencement of this Act, if done under the belief that they were under the Petroleum Act. It also indemnifies persons from legal proceedings on the ground that such acts were not in accordance with the law.
This section, which dealt with the repeal of section 30 of the Petroleum Act, 1934, was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1957.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Central Government may declare any liquid or other substance to be dangerously inflammable (Section 3 lists specific substances).
Rule 2: The Central Government can apply provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1934, to dangerously inflammable substances (Section 4(1)).
Rule 3: Special rules can be made for testing dangerously inflammable substances (Section 4(2)).
Rule 4: Notifications and rules issued under Section 30 of the Petroleum Act prior to this Act's commencement are deemed valid and continue in force (Section 5).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (through notifications and rules)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By applying provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1934, and making specific rules for testing.

rights: The right of the Central Government to declare substances as dangerously inflammable and regulate their handling.
Indemnity for individuals acting in good faith under the Petroleum Act concerning inflammable substances before this Act's commencement.
duties: Duty to comply with regulations regarding the import, transport, storage, and production of dangerously inflammable substances as per the applied provisions of the Petroleum Act.
obligations: Obligation for the Central Government to issue notifications and potentially rules for the regulation of dangerously inflammable substances.
Obligation for individuals to adhere to the regulations established through the application of the Petroleum Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Declaration of Substances: The Central Government declares specific liquids and substances to be dangerously inflammable (Section 3).
Procedure 2: Application of Petroleum Act: The Central Government issues a notification to apply provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1934, to dangerously inflammable substances (Section 4(1)).
Procedure 3: Rule Making for Testing: The Central Government can create specific rules for testing dangerously inflammable substances (Section 4(2)).
Procedure 4: Validation of Past Actions: Acts performed under the Petroleum Act concerning inflammable substances prior to this Act's commencement are validated (Section 6).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act serves to provide a legal basis for regulating inflammable substances, particularly addressing potential issues arising from the Government of India Act, 1935, and the new Constitution.
Section 7 of the Act, which concerned the repeal of section 30 of the Petroleum Act, 1934, has itself been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1957.

title: The Salaries and Allowances of Officers of Parliament Act, 1953
purpose: To provide for the salaries and allowances of certain officers of Parliament, specifically the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People.
scope: This Act applies to the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People in India. It governs their salaries, allowances, residences, medical facilities, and other benefits during their term of office and in certain cases, after their term or in case of death.

key_definitions.officer of Parliament: Means any of the following officers: the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, and the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The Salaries and Allowances of Officers of Parliament Act, 1953' and states that it is deemed to have come into force on May 1, 1953.
Defines 'officer of Parliament' to include the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries, etc., of officers of Parliament
main_sections.description: Details the salaries payable to the Chairman of the Council of States, and the salaries and constituency allowances for other officers of Parliament, referencing rates specified in the Salaries, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954.

Entitles officers of Parliament to the use of a furnished residence free of rent during their term of office and for one month thereafter. It also provides for the continued use of residence for their families in case of death.
Provides for a sumptuary allowance to be paid to the Speaker of the House of the People, Deputy Chairman, and Deputy Speaker, with rates adjusted based on other related Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Travelling and daily allowances to officers of Parliament
main_sections.description: Entitles officers of Parliament to travelling allowances for themselves and their families for journeys to assume or relinquish office, and for tours undertaken in the discharge of official duties. It also covers daily allowances and specifies rates equivalent to those for Ministers.

main_sections.section_title: Medical facilities to officers of Parliament
main_sections.description: Grants entitlement to free medical treatment and accommodation in Government-maintained hospitals for officers of Parliament and their families.

main_sections.section_title: Family pension, etc., to spouse of Speaker dying in office
main_sections.description: Introduces provisions for a family pension to the spouse of a Speaker who dies in office, along with continued use of residence and medical facilities.

main_sections.section_title: Advances to officers of Parliament for purchase of motor-cars
main_sections.description: Allows for repayable advances to officers of Parliament for the purchase of motor-cars to facilitate the discharge of their duties.

main_sections.section_title: Officers of Parliament not to draw salary or allowances as Members of Parliament
main_sections.description: Prohibits officers of Parliament from drawing salary or allowances as Members of Parliament if they are already receiving benefits under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Notification respecting appointment, etc., of officers of Parliament to be conclusive evidence thereof
main_sections.description: States that notifications in the Official Gazette regarding the appointment or cessation of an officer of Parliament are conclusive evidence of such events.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption from liability to pay income-tax on daily allowance received by the Chairman and certain perquisites received by an officer of Parliament
main_sections.description: Exempts the daily allowance received by the Chairman and the value of rent-free furnished residence provided to an officer of Parliament from income-tax, notwithstanding the Income-tax Act, 1961.

Empowers the Central Government, in consultation with the Chairman and Speaker, to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. It also outlines the procedure for laying rules before Parliament.

important_rules: Officers of Parliament are entitled to a salary and allowances as specified in the Act, with some rates aligned to those for Members of Parliament and Ministers.
Officers of Parliament are entitled to rent-free furnished residences during their term of office and for a period thereafter.
Provision is made for travelling and daily allowances for official duties and journeys related to assuming or relinquishing office.
Free medical facilities are provided to officers of Parliament and their families.
A family pension and continued residence benefits are provided to the spouse of a Speaker who dies in office.
Advance payments can be made for the purchase of motor-cars.
Officers of Parliament cannot claim both benefits under this Act and as Members of Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for making rules), Parliament (for approving rules)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, and rules made thereunder. Notifications in the Official Gazette serve as conclusive evidence. Rules made by the Central Government are subject to parliamentary scrutiny and approval.

rights: Right to receive salary and allowances as prescribed.
Right to use furnished residence free of rent.
Right to travelling and daily allowances for official duties and journeys.
Right to free medical treatment and accommodation in Government hospitals.
Right to advances for motor-car purchase.
Spouse of a deceased Speaker has rights to family pension, continued residence, and medical facilities.
duties: To discharge official duties efficiently and conveniently, potentially facilitated by motor-car advances.
To adhere to the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.
To not draw salary or allowances as a Member of Parliament while receiving benefits under this Act.

key_procedures: Determination of salaries and allowances based on rates specified in other Acts (e.g., Salaries, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954, Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952).
Notification of appointment and cessation of officers of Parliament in the Official Gazette, which serves as conclusive evidence.
Making of rules by the Central Government in consultation with the Chairman and Speaker, subject to parliamentary review and modification.
administration: Central Government (specifically, the power to make rules rests with the Central Government, in consultation with the Chairman and the Speaker).
important_notes: The Act refers to other Acts for determining specific rates of salaries, allowances, and benefits, indicating an interconnected legislative framework.
Substantial amendments have been made to the Act over time, as evidenced by the list of amending Acts.
Section 10A provides an income-tax exemption for specific allowances and perquisites received by officers of Parliament, highlighting the financial implications and benefits.

title: The Andhra State Act, 1953
purpose: To provide for the formation of the State of Andhra, the increase of the area of the State of Mysore, and the decrease of the area of the State of Madras, and for other connected matters.
scope: The Act applies to the territories that formed the State of Andhra, the State of Mysore, and the State of Madras. It covers provisions related to the formation of new states, representation in legislatures, High Courts, financial matters, legal provisions, and administrative arrangements.

key_definitions.appointed day: The 1st day of October, 1953.
key_definitions.Assembly constituency, Council constitue: Have the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950).
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or in any part of the State of Madras or Mysore as constituted immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.Order: An Order published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.sitting member: A person who immediately before the appointed day is a member of either House of Parliament or of the Legislature of a State.
key_definitions.transferred territory: The territory added to the State of Mysore by sub-section (1) of section 4.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and outlines the commencement dates for different parts and sections of the Act. Part I and certain other sections come into force immediately, while the rest come into force on October 1, 1953.
Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'article', 'law', 'sitting member', and 'transferred territory'.

Declares the formation of the State of Andhra as a Part A State from the appointed day, comprising specific districts and taluks previously belonging to the State of Madras. It also details the inclusion of certain taluks within specific districts of the new Andhra State.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of territory from Madras to Mysore
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of specified taluks from the Bellary district of Madras to the State of Mysore, which will then form a separate district named Bellary district in Mysore.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to include Andhra as a new Part A State, adjust the descriptions of territories for Andhra, Madras, and Mysore, and renumber existing entries.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in the Council of States
main_sections.description: Reduces the number of seats for Madras in the Council of States and allots seats to the new State of Andhra.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the changes in the allocation of seats in the Council of States for Andhra, Madras, and the total number of seats.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Adjusts the number of seats for Madras and Mysore in the House of the People and allots seats to the State of Andhra. It also makes consequential amendments to the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Determines the total number of seats for direct elections in the Legislative Assemblies of Andhra, Madras, and Mysore, making necessary adjustments to the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Provides for the establishment of a High Court for the new State of Andhra.
Deals with the apportionment of assets and liabilities between the newly formed states.
Specifies the territorial extent of laws in relation to the newly formed states.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of provisions of the Act inconsistent with other laws
main_sections.description: Clarifies that provisions of this Act that are inconsistent with other laws will prevail.
Grants the President the power to make orders to remove difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule (Section 1(2)): Certain parts of the Act (Part I and sections 43, 54, 58, 61, 62, 63, 64, 66, 69) come into force immediately, while the remaining provisions come into force on October 1, 1953.
Rule (Section 3(1)): The State of Andhra is formed on the appointed day, comprising specific territories from the State of Madras.
Rule (Section 4(1)): Territory from the Bellary district of Madras is transferred to the State of Mysore on the appointed day.
Rule (Section 6): The number of seats for Madras in the Council of States is reduced, and seats are allotted to Andhra.
Rule (Section 11(1)): The number of seats for Madras in the House of the People is reduced, Mysore's seats are increased, and seats are allotted to Andhra.
Rule (Section 15(1)): The strength of the Legislative Assemblies of Andhra, Madras, and Mysore are determined and adjusted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act does not explicitly detail specific penalties for violations. Enforcement would likely be through the relevant government departments and judicial processes as governed by existing laws and the provisions of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would involve the administration and application of the Act's provisions by the respective state governments and central authorities, including the judiciary, to ensure the formation of states, representation, and other administrative and financial arrangements are carried out as stipulated.

rights: Right to representation in the Council of States and the House of the People for the new State of Andhra.
Right to representation in the Legislative Assemblies for the new State of Andhra.
duties: Duty of the Parliament to enact legislation for the formation and reorganisation of states.
Duty of the respective state governments to implement the provisions related to territory transfer, representation, and administrative arrangements.
obligations: Obligation to amend the Constitution (First and Fourth Schedules) to reflect the changes in state boundaries and representation.
Obligation to adjust electoral rolls and constituencies according to the new state configurations.
Obligation to apportion assets and liabilities between the states.

key_procedures: Procedure for the formation of the State of Andhra and transfer of territories (Sections 3 & 4).
Procedure for amending the Constitution (First and Fourth Schedules) regarding state territories and representation (Sections 5 & 7).
Procedure for allocating sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures to the new and reorganised states (Sections 8, 13, 16).
Procedure for bye-elections to fill vacancies (Section 9).
Procedure for determining the terms of office of members of the Council of States (Section 10).
Procedure for adapting laws and removing difficulties (Sections 54 & 69).
administration: Various government departments and authorities at both the central and state levels would be responsible for administering different aspects of this Act, including the Ministry of Home Affairs for state formation and reorganization, and the Election Commission for representation matters. The President of India also has significant powers to issue directions and remove difficulties.
important_notes: The Act makes extensive amendments to the Constitution of India, specifically the First and Fourth Schedules.
The Act requires consequential amendments to other laws, such as the Representation of the People Acts.
The Act provides for transitional provisions to ensure a smooth transition during the formation of the new state and reorganisation of existing ones.

title: The Calcutta High Court (Extension of Jurisdiction) Act, 1953
purpose: To extend the jurisdiction of the High Court at Calcutta to Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands for all purposes.
scope: The Act applies to Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It extends the jurisdiction of the High Court at Calcutta to these territories.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Calcutta High Court (Extension of Jurisdiction) Act, 1953.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of Calcutta High Court to Chandernagore and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
main_sections.description: Declares that the jurisdiction of the High Court at Calcutta shall extend to Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It also specifies that this extension is deemed to have been effective from May 2, 1950, and that the High Court at Calcutta shall be deemed to be the High Court for Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands for all purposes.

States that any order made by the highest court of appeal in relation to Chandernagore before May 2, 1950, or in any pending proceeding on that day, or by the Chief Commissioner of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands before the commencement of the Act in his capacity as the High Court for those Islands, shall have effect as if it were an order made by the High Court at Calcutta.

Empowers the High Court at Calcutta to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act and for effectively exercising its jurisdiction in or in relation to Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, subject to any other law in force.

important_rules: The jurisdiction of the High Court at Calcutta is extended to Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
This extension is deemed to have been effective from May 2, 1950, for Chandernagore.
The High Court at Calcutta is considered the High Court for Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands for all purposes.

Orders made by previous highest appellate courts in Chandernagore or by the Chief Commissioner of Andaman and Nicobar Islands (acting as High Court) are to be treated as orders of the Calcutta High Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: High Court at Calcutta
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of its extended jurisdiction and the making of rules under section 4.

rights: The right of the people in Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to have their legal matters adjudicated by the High Court at Calcutta.
The High Court at Calcutta's right to exercise jurisdiction over these territories.
duties: The High Court at Calcutta's duty to exercise its jurisdiction effectively in relation to Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
The duty to ensure that orders made by previous authorities are recognized and have effect as if made by the High Court at Calcutta.

key_procedures: Legal matters from Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are to be brought before and decided by the High Court at Calcutta.
The High Court at Calcutta can make rules to facilitate the exercise of its jurisdiction in these areas.
administration: High Court at Calcutta
important_notes: The extension of jurisdiction to Chandernagore is effective from May 2, 1950.
The Act aims to consolidate the High Court's jurisdiction for all purposes, as previous jurisdiction was limited to specific laws.
The Act is enacted under the framework envisioned by Article 230 of the Constitution of India.

title: THE LUSHAI HILLS DISTRICT (CHANGE OF NAME) ACT, 1954
purpose: To change the name of the Lushai Hills District to Mizo District.
scope: This Act applies to the tribal area in Assam previously known as the Lushai Hills District. It also amends the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution to reflect this change in name for constitutional references.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Lushai Hills District (Change of Name) Act, 1954, and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Lushai Hills District to be known as Mizo District
main_sections.description: Declares that the tribal area in Assam known as the Lushai Hills District shall, from the commencement of the Act, be called the Mizo District.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution to: insert a new sub-paragraph (2A) stating that the Mizo District comprises the area that was known as the Lushai Hills District at the commencement of the Constitution; insert 'and the Mizo District' after 'United Khasi Jaintia Hills District' in sub-paragraph (3); and substitute 'The Mizo District' for 'The Lushai Hills District' in Part A of the table.

main_sections.section_title: Reference to Lushai Hills District to be construed as reference to Mizo District
main_sections.description: Stipulates that any reference to the Lushai Hills District in any law, instrument, or other document shall, unless the context dictates otherwise, be interpreted as a reference to the Mizo District.

important_rules: The tribal area in Assam known as Lushai Hills District will henceforth be known as Mizo District.
All references to Lushai Hills District in existing laws, instruments, or documents will be understood as Mizo District, unless the context requires otherwise.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for commencement date notification)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Official Gazette for commencement and by the legal framework governing the interpretation of laws and documents.

obligations: To change the name of the Lushai Hills District to Mizo District.
To amend the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the name change.

key_procedures: The Central Government may appoint a date for the commencement of the Act through a notification in the Official Gazette.
The Sixth Schedule to the Constitution is amended by inserting new provisions and modifying existing ones to reflect the name change.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be overseen by the Central Government and relevant constitutional bodies for amendment.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 1st September, 1954, as notified by the Central Government.
The Mizo District comprises the area that was known as the Lushai Hills District at the commencement of the Constitution.

title: The Shillong (Rifle Range and Umlong) Cantonments Assimilation of Laws Act, 1954
purpose: To assimilate certain laws in force in the scheduled areas (Shillong Rifle Range and Umlong Cantonments) to the laws in force in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills District.
scope: Applies to the 'scheduled areas' which are defined as the Shillong (Rifle Range) Cantonment and the Shillong (Umlong) Cantonment. The act aims to replace existing laws in these areas with those applicable in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills District.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed by the Central Government for the commencement of the Act.
key_definitions.law: So much of any Act, Ordinance, Regulation, rule, order, or bye-law as relates to any of the matters enumerated in Lists I and III in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.
key_definitions.scheduled areas: The areas specified in the Schedule, which are the Shillong (Rifle Range) Cantonment and the Shillong (Umlong) Cantonment.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and stipulates that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'law', and 'scheduled areas'.

States that laws in force in the scheduled areas immediately before the appointed day will cease to be in force, except for past actions. It also declares that laws in force in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills District will extend to and be in force in the scheduled areas from the appointed day. Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, is applicable to such cessations.

Empowers the Central Government to make necessary provisions by order, notified in the Official Gazette, to remove any difficulties arising in relation to the transition from one law or group of laws to another under section 3.

important_rules: All laws in force in the scheduled areas immediately before the appointed day will cease to be in force from that day, except for things done or omitted to be done before that day.
All laws in force in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills District immediately before the appointed day will extend to and be in force in the scheduled areas from that day.
The Central Government can issue orders to resolve difficulties during the transition of laws.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government has the authority to remove difficulties through orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Central Government enforces the removal of difficulties by issuing orders notified in the Official Gazette. The assimilation of laws is a direct legislative action.

key_procedures: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint a date for the commencement of the Act.
The Central Government may, by order notified in the Official Gazette, make provisions to remove difficulties arising from the transition of laws.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Schedule provides detailed descriptions and boundary measurements for the Shillong (Rifle Range) Cantonment and the Shillong (Umlong) Cantonment.
The commencement date was August 16, 1954, as per the Gazette of India 1954, Part II, s. 3.

title: The Special Marriage Act, 1954
purpose: To provide a special form of marriage in certain cases, for the registration of such and certain other marriages and for divorce.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies also to citizens of India domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends. It also applies to citizens of India domiciled in the State of Jammu and Kashmir (though this part has been subject to amendments).

key_definitions.degrees_of_prohibited_relationship: A man and any of the persons mentioned in Part I of the First Schedule, and a woman and any of the persons mentioned in Part II of the First Schedule, are considered to be within the degrees of prohibited relationship. This definition includes relationships by half or uterine blood, illegitimate blood, and adoption.
key_definitions.district: In relation to a Marriage Officer, it means the area for which he is appointed.
key_definitions.district_court: In areas with a city civil court, it refers to that court. In other areas, it means the principal civil court of original jurisdiction and any other civil court specified by the State Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.state_government: In relation to a Union territory, it means the administrator thereof.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and when it comes into force.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'degrees of prohibited relationship', 'district', 'district court', 'prescribed', and 'State Government'.
This section outlines the appointment of Marriage Officers by the State Government for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions relating to solemnization of special marriages
main_sections.description: This section specifies the conditions that must be fulfilled for a marriage to be solemnized under this Act, such as neither party having a spouse living, age requirements, and not being within prohibited degrees of relationship.
This section details the requirement for parties intending to marry under this Act to give written notice to the Marriage Officer.
This section allows any person to object to an intended marriage on the grounds that it contravenes the conditions specified in section 4.
This section outlines the requirement for the parties and witnesses to make a declaration before the Marriage Officer.
This section deals with the location and manner in which a special marriage is solemnized.
This section describes the issuance of a certificate of marriage by the Marriage Officer.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of marriages celebrated in other forms
main_sections.description: This section provides for the registration of marriages that were celebrated in other forms but meet certain criteria.
This section defines marriages that are considered void under the Act.
This section defines marriages that are considered voidable under the Act.
This section lists the grounds on which a petition for divorce can be presented.
This section provides for divorce by mutual consent of both parties.

main_sections.section_title: Court to which petition should be made
main_sections.description: This section specifies the court to which petitions under the Act should be presented.
This section deals with provisions for permanent alimony and maintenance for either party to a marriage.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on married person marrying again under this Act
main_sections.description: This section specifies the penalty for a married person who marries again under this Act.
This section addresses the punishment for bigamy.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for signing false declaration or certificate
main_sections.description: This section outlines the penalty for making false declarations or certificates.
This section grants the government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
This section details the repeal of previous enactments and savings provisions.

important_rules: A marriage can be solemnized under this Act only if neither party has a living spouse.
Neither party should be incapable of giving valid consent due to unsoundness of mind or mental disorder rendering them unfit for marriage and procreation.
The male party must have completed 21 years of age and the female party must have completed 18 years of age.
The parties must not be within the degrees of prohibited relationship, unless a custom permits such a marriage.
Parties intending to marry must give written notice to the Marriage Officer of the district where at least one party has resided for at least 30 days.
A Marriage Officer shall keep all notices in a Marriage Notice Book, which shall be open for inspection.
Any person can object to a marriage within 30 days of notice publication if it contravenes the conditions of section 4.
If an objection is upheld, the Marriage Officer cannot solemnize the marriage until the objection is resolved or withdrawn, with a maximum inquiry period of 30 days.
Appeals against the Marriage Officer's decision to refuse solemnization can be made to the district court, whose decision is final.
Marriage Officers have powers similar to civil courts in summoning witnesses, compelling production of documents, etc., for inquiries.
Marriage Officers can impose costs on persons making unreasonable objections in bad faith.
The Act provides for restitution of conjugal rights and judicial separation.
Grounds for divorce are specified, including adultery, cruelty, desertion, conversion, incurable unsoundness of mind, etc.
Divorce by mutual consent is permissible under certain conditions.
Petitions for divorce are generally restricted during the first year of marriage.
The Act makes provisions for alimony, maintenance, and custody of children.
Registration of marriages celebrated in other forms is allowed under specific procedures.
Penalties are prescribed for bigamy, making false declarations, and wrongful actions by Marriage Officers.

penalties: Penalty on a married person marrying again under this Act.
Punishment for bigamy.
Penalty for signing a false declaration or certificate.
Penalty for wrongful action of a Marriage Officer.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Marriage Officers and the District Courts are the primary authorities for enforcement and adjudication.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the process of notice, objection, inquiry, appeals to the district court, and by applying the penal provisions for violations. The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Indian Penal Code, 1860, are referenced for procedural powers and penalties for offenses related to judicial proceedings.

rights: Right to marry a person of choice, subject to the conditions of the Act.
Right to register marriages celebrated in other forms.
Right to seek restitution of conjugal rights.
Right to seek judicial separation.
Right to seek divorce on specified grounds.
Right to seek divorce by mutual consent.
Right to claim alimony and maintenance.
Right to seek custody of children.
Right to appeal against decisions of Marriage Officers.
Right to inspect the Marriage Notice Book and Marriage Certificate Book.
duties: Duty of parties to provide true notice of intended marriage.
Duty of Marriage Officer to publish notices and inquire into objections.
Duty of parties and witnesses to make a true declaration.
Duty of Marriage Officer to solemnize marriage and issue certificate if conditions are met.
Duty of parties to adhere to the conditions of the Act post-marriage.
Duty of the court to pass appropriate decrees and orders.
obligations: Obligation not to enter into a marriage if already married.
Obligation to adhere to age and mental capacity requirements for marriage.
Obligation to comply with the notice and objection procedures.
Obligation to follow the prescribed procedures for divorce, alimony, and custody.
Obligation to refrain from making false declarations or signing false certificates.

key_procedures: Notice of intended marriage: Parties give written notice to the Marriage Officer; the notice is recorded, published, and entered in the Marriage Notice Book.
Objection to marriage: Any person can object within 30 days; the Marriage Officer must inquire into the objection.

Solemnization of marriage: If no objection or if objection is resolved, and all conditions are met, the marriage is solemnized after parties and witnesses make a declaration, and a certificate is issued.
Registration of marriages in other forms: Procedure for applying for and registering marriages celebrated under other customary or religious forms.
Divorce proceedings: Filing a petition in the district court on grounds specified in section 27, or by mutual consent under section 28.
Alimony and maintenance: Application to the court for interim or permanent alimony and maintenance.
Custody of children: Application to the court for custody of children of the marriage.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Governments through appointed Marriage Officers. The Central Government has a role in appointing Marriage Officers for citizens of India domiciled in the State of Jammu and Kashmir, and in issuing notifications. The District Courts play a crucial role in hearing appeals and adjudicating divorce and related matters.
important_notes: The Act has undergone amendments, including changes related to the extension of its application to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Customary marriages that fall within prohibited degrees of relationship may still be solemnized if a custom governing at least one of the parties permits it.
The Act's provisions regarding mental disorder have been updated, with the omission of 'epilepsy' as a disqualifying condition.
The Act emphasizes that proceedings concerning divorce and judicial separation are to be held in camera and may not be printed or published.
The Act aims to provide a secular framework for marriage and divorce, independent of religious affiliations.

title: THE SALARY, ALLOWANCES AND PENSION OF MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT ACT, 1954
purpose: To provide for the salary, allowances, and pension of Members of Parliament.
scope: This Act applies to all Members of either House of Parliament in India, with specific exclusions for Ministers, Leaders of the Opposition, and Officers of Parliament. It also outlines provisions for former Members and their families.

key_definitions.committee: A Committee of either House of Parliament, including a Joint Committee of both Houses.
key_definitions.dependent: Relatives of a deceased member including minor children, unmarried daughters, widowed mother, infirm adult children wholly dependent, parents, minor brothers, unmarried sisters, widowed daughters-in-law, minor children of pre-deceased sons or daughters, paternal grandparents if no parent is alive, and other persons specified by rules.
key_definitions.member: A member of either House of Parliament, excluding Ministers, Leaders of the Opposition, and Officers of Parliament.
key_definitions.new_member: A member who takes their seat in either House after the Act's commencement, including re-elected or re-nominated members.
key_definitions.period_of_residence_on_duty: The period a member resides at a place for attending a session, committee sitting, or other parliamentary business, including a grace period before and after the event.
key_definitions.term_of_office: The duration of a member's tenure, starting from commencement or election/nomination date and ending when their seat becomes vacant.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954, and specifies its commencement date as June 1, 1954.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'committee', 'dependent', 'member', 'new member', 'period of residence on duty', and 'term of office'.

Specifies the monthly salary and daily allowance for members during their term of office and periods of residence on duty. Includes provisions for salary reduction during the COVID-19 pandemic and automatic increases based on inflation.

Details the travelling allowances admissible to members for journeys within India for attending sessions, committee meetings, or other official business. Covers air, steamer, and road travel with specific rates and conditions.
Covers allowances for journeys made between different places during the course of official duties.
Outlines the provisions for pension entitlement for former Members of Parliament.
Grants the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: A member is entitled to a monthly salary and a daily allowance for periods of residence on duty.
Members are eligible for travelling allowances for official journeys within India by air, steamer, or road.
Provisions exist for free transit by railway and steamer for members.
Special travel facilities are provided to members from Ladakh, and for blind and physically incapacitated members.
Pension and family pension provisions are outlined for former members.
Advances can be provided to members for the purchase of conveyances.
The salary payable to Members of Parliament was reduced by 30% for a period to meet exigencies arising out of the Corona Virus (COVID-19) pandemic.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Secretariat of the House of the People or Council of States (for signing registers) and potentially other authorities as implied by rule-making powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the entitlement to salary and allowances based on adherence to the Act's provisions and rules. Enforcement of penalties would likely be through specific rules made under Section 9.

rights: Right to receive salary during the term of office.
Right to receive daily allowances for periods of residence on duty.
Right to travelling allowances for official journeys.
Right to free transit by rail and steamer.
Right to pension and family pension (for ex-members and dependents).
Right to advances for purchase of conveyance.
Right to special travel facilities (e.g., for members from Ladakh, blind/incapacitated members).
duties: To attend sessions and committee meetings.
To sign attendance registers for claiming daily allowances.
To conduct official business in discharge of duties.
To adhere to the conditions specified for claiming allowances and facilities.
obligations: Obligation to use allowances and facilities for their intended purpose.
Obligation to comply with rules made under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for claiming daily allowance: Signing the attendance register maintained by the Secretariat of the House of the People or Council of States on all days of the session (except intervening holidays).
Procedure for claiming travelling allowance: Performing official journeys and submitting claims as per prescribed rates and conditions, including signing of registers where applicable.
Procedure for applying for advances for conveyance purchase as per rules.
administration: The administration of the Act would typically fall under the purview of the Parliament's secretariats (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha Secretariats) for matters related to allowances, travel, and pension, and the Ministry of Finance or relevant administrative ministry for financial oversight and rule-making.
important_notes: Salaries were reduced by 30% for a year starting April 1, 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The rates of salary specified in section 3 are applicable from May 18, 2009.
Salary and daily allowances are subject to increase after every five years based on the Cost Inflation Index.
Members must sign attendance registers to be eligible for daily allowances.
Specific conditions and limitations apply to various travelling allowances, including journey types and destinations.
The Act excludes Ministers, Leaders of the Opposition, and Officers of Parliament from its definition of 'member' for certain provisions.

title: The State Bank of India Act, 1955
purpose: To constitute a State Bank for India, transfer to it the undertaking of the Imperial Bank of India, and provide for other connected or incidental matters, with the aim of extending banking facilities on a large scale, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas, and for diverse other public purposes.
scope: This Act applies to the State Bank of India, the Reserve Bank of India, and the Imperial Bank of India. It covers the establishment, share capital, management, business, funds, accounts, and audit of the State Bank of India, as well as the transfer of the undertaking of the Imperial Bank of India.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.Central Board: The Central Board of Directors of the State Bank.
key_definitions.chairman: The chairman of the Central Board.
key_definitions.Imperial Bank: The Imperial Bank of India constituted under the Imperial Bank of India Act, 1920.
key_definitions.Local Board: A Local Board constituted under section 21.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.Reserve Bank: The Reserve Bank of India constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
key_definitions.State Bank: The State Bank of India constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.workman: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Central Board', 'Imperial Bank', 'Reserve Bank', and 'State Bank'.

Establishes the State Bank of India to carry on the business of banking and other business, and to take over the undertaking of the Imperial Bank. It also outlines the corporate status and powers of the State Bank.
Specifies the authorised capital of the State Bank, its division into shares, and the power of the Central Board and Central Government to alter it, with the approval of the Reserve Bank.

Details the initial issued capital of the State Bank on the appointed day, its allotment to the Reserve Bank, and provisions for future increases in issued capital through equity or preference shares, with specific conditions regarding Central Government's holding and approval.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the Imperial Bank to the State Bank
main_sections.description: Effectuates the transfer of the Imperial Bank's undertaking, including all its rights, powers, property, debts, liabilities, and obligations, to the State Bank on the appointed day. It also ensures the continuity of existing contracts, deeds, and legal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of service of existing officers and employees of the Imperial Bank to the State Bank
main_sections.description: Transfers officers and employees of the Imperial Bank (excluding certain management personnel) to the State Bank on the appointed day, maintaining their existing tenure and service conditions.

important_rules: The State Bank of India shall be constituted to carry on the business of banking and other business in accordance with the provisions of this Act and for the purpose of taking over the undertaking of the Imperial Bank.
All shares in the capital of the Imperial Bank shall be transferred to, and shall vest in, the Reserve Bank, free of all trusts, liabilities and encumbrances, on the appointed day.
The undertaking of the Imperial Bank shall be transferred to, and shall vest in, the State Bank on the appointed day.
Existing contracts, deeds, bonds, agreements, etc., of the Imperial Bank shall be enforceable by or against the State Bank.
Pending suits, appeals, or legal proceedings by or against the Imperial Bank shall continue by or against the State Bank.

Officers and employees of the Imperial Bank (excluding certain management) shall become officers and employees of the State Bank on the appointed day, holding their office by the same tenure and at the same remuneration.

rights: The State Bank has the power to acquire and hold property and dispose of it for its constituted purposes.
Shareholders have rights related to their shares, including the right to nominate (Section 10A) and voting rights (subject to restrictions in Section 11).
Existing officers and employees transferred to the State Bank retain their service rights and tenure.
duties: The State Bank has a duty to carry on the business of banking and other business in accordance with the Act.
The State Bank is established to extend banking facilities on a large scale, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas.
obligations: The State Bank is obligated to take over the undertaking of the Imperial Bank of India.
The State Bank is to be guided by the directions of the Central Government (Section 18).

key_procedures: Establishment of the State Bank of India.
Transfer of the Imperial Bank of India's undertaking, assets, liabilities, and employees to the State Bank.
Determining the authorised and issued capital of the State Bank.
Allotment of shares to the Reserve Bank in lieu of the Imperial Bank shares.
administration: The Central Government and the Central Board of Directors of the State Bank, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, administer various aspects of the Act.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various Union Territories.
The Act was initially notified to come into force on July 1, 1955.
Several sections have been omitted or repealed by subsequent amending acts.
The Act includes a list of amending acts up to 2025, indicating its continuous evolution.

title: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
purpose: To amend and codify the law relating to marriage among Hindus.
scope: Applies to the whole of India and to Hindus domiciled in India who are outside the said territories. It applies to persons who are Hindu by religion (including followers of Brahmo, Prarthana, Arya Samaj, Virashaiva, Lingayat), Buddhist, Jaina, or Sikh by religion. It also applies to other persons domiciled in India who are not Muslim, Christian, Parsi, or Jew, unless proven otherwise. It does not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes unless the Central Government directs otherwise.

key_definitions.custom_and_usage: Signify any rule which, having been continuously and uniformly observed for a long time, has obtained the force of law among Hindus in any local area, tribe, community, group or family, provided the rule is certain, not unreasonable or opposed to public policy, and in the case of a rule applicable only to a family, has not been discontinued by the family.
key_definitions.district_court: In any area for which there is a city civil court, that court, and in any other area the principal civil court of original jurisdiction, and includes any other civil court which the State Government may specify.
key_definitions.full_blood_and_half_blood: Two persons are related by full blood when descended from a common ancestor by the same wife, and by half blood when descended from a common ancestor by different wives.
key_definitions.uterine_blood: Two persons are related by uterine blood when they are descended from a common ancestress but by different husbands.
key_definitions.sapinda_relationship: Extends as far as the third generation (inclusive) in the line of ascent through the mother, and the fifth (inclusive) in the line of ascent through the father, with the person concerned counted as the first generation. Two persons are sapindas if one is a lineal ascendant of the other within these limits or if they have a common lineal ascendant within these limits.
key_definitions.degrees_of_prohibited_relationship: Includes lineal ascendants/descendants, a person being the wife/husband of a lineal ascendant/descendant, a person being the wife of a brother or father's/mother's brother or grandfather's/grandmother's brother of the other, or if the two are brother and sister, uncle and niece, aunt and nephew, or children of brother and sister or of two brothers or of two sisters. Relationship includes full blood, half blood, uterine blood, illegitimate blood, and adoption.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and defines its geographical and personal extent.

Specifies the categories of people to whom the Act applies, including Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs, and certain other individuals not following Islam, Christianity, Parsi, or Judaism. It also includes provisions for children of mixed religious parentage and converts/re-converts.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'custom', 'usage', 'district court', 'full blood', 'half blood', 'uterine blood', 'sapinda relationship', and 'degrees of prohibited relationship'.
States that any existing Hindu law, text, rule, interpretation, custom, or usage, or any other law in force, shall cease to have effect if it is inconsistent with the provisions of this Act.

Outlines the essential conditions that must be fulfilled for a valid Hindu marriage, including monogamy, mental capacity, age requirements (21 for groom, 18 for bride), and not being within the degrees of prohibited relationship or sapinda relationship unless permitted by custom.

Specifies that a Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party. If the rites include Saptapadi (seven steps before the sacred fire), the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.

Allows State Governments to make rules for the registration of Hindu marriages to facilitate proof. It can be made compulsory in certain areas or cases, with a penalty for contravention. The register is open for inspection and admissible as evidence. Omission to register does not affect the validity of the marriage.
Provides that if one spouse withdraws from the society of the other without reasonable excuse, the aggrieved party can petition the district court for restitution of conjugal rights.

Allows either party to present a petition for a decree of judicial separation on grounds specified for divorce. If a decree is passed, cohabitation is no longer obligatory, but the decree can be rescinded.
Declares marriages solemnised after the commencement of the Act to be null and void if they contravene specific conditions of Section 5 (i.e., bigamy, prohibited degrees, sapinda relationship).

Lists grounds on which a marriage can be annulled by a decree of nullity, including non-consummation due to impotence, contravention of certain conditions in Section 5, consent obtained by force or fraud, or respondent's pregnancy by another person at the time of marriage.
Enables either party to obtain a divorce on grounds such as adultery, desertion, cruelty, presumption of death, or conversion to another religion. Specific grounds are also provided for wives.
Allows for divorce by mutual consent if the parties have been living separately for one year or more, have not been able to live together, and mutually agree that the marriage should be dissolved.

main_sections.section_title: No petition for divorce to be presented within one year of marriage
main_sections.description: Prohibits the presentation of a petition for divorce within one year of the solemnization of the marriage, except in cases of special hardship.
Prescribes punishment for solemnizing a marriage in contravention of the conditions specified in section 5 (i.e., bigamy).

main_sections.section_title: Court to which petition shall be presented
main_sections.description: Specifies that petitions under the Act shall be presented to the district court within the local limits of whose ordinary jurisdiction the respondent resides or at whose instance the marriage was solemnized.
Lays down the conditions under which a court may pass a decree for restitution of conjugal rights, judicial separation, nullity of marriage, or divorce.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings
main_sections.description: Empowers the court to order the respondent to pay maintenance pendente lite (during the pendency of proceedings) and litigation expenses to the applicant, if the court is satisfied that the applicant has no independent income sufficient for the same.
Allows the court to pass an order for permanent alimony and maintenance in favour of the applicant, either in lump sum or from time to time, if it is deemed just and proper.
Provides for the custody, maintenance, and education of minor children during the pendency of any proceeding under the Act and also after the passing of a decree.
Saves any marriage solemnized before the commencement of the Act and any proceeding or cause of action arising before such commencement.

important_rules: A Hindu marriage can be solemnized if neither party has a living spouse, both are capable of giving valid consent and are fit for marriage and procreation, the bridegroom is 21 and the bride is 18, and they are not within prohibited degrees of relationship or sapinda relationship unless custom permits.
A Hindu marriage is complete and binding when the Saptapadi ceremony is completed.
Marriages solemnized in contravention of certain conditions (e.g., bigamy, prohibited degrees, sapinda relationship) are void.
Marriages can be voidable on grounds of impotence, unsoundness of mind, fraud, or pregnancy by another person at the time of marriage.
Divorce can be granted on various grounds including adultery, desertion, cruelty, and mutual consent after one year of separation.
The court can grant restitution of conjugal rights if one party has withdrawn from society without reasonable excuse.
Judicial separation can be granted on grounds similar to divorce, and it relieves parties from the obligation to cohabit.
Provisions exist for maintenance pendente lite, permanent alimony, and custody of children.
Bigamy is punishable under the Act.

penalties: Punishment for bigamy: Imprisonment which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both.
Punishment for contravention of certain other conditions for a Hindu marriage: Imprisonment which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both.
Penalty for contravening rules for compulsory registration: Fine which may extend to twenty-five rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Courts, other specified civil courts, and police (for criminal offenses like bigamy).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial proceedings initiated by petitions in courts for divorce, nullity, restitution of conjugal rights, judicial separation, and maintenance. Criminal prosecution for offenses like bigamy.

rights: Right to seek restitution of conjugal rights.
Right to petition for judicial separation.
Right to petition for divorce.
Right to petition for a decree of nullity for void or voidable marriages.
Right to claim maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings.
Right to claim permanent alimony and maintenance.
Right to seek custody, maintenance, and education of minor children.
Right to remarry after obtaining a decree of divorce.
Right to have one's marriage registered.
duties: Duty to solemnize marriage only if conditions in Section 5 are met.
Duty to adhere to customary rites and ceremonies.
Duty to cohabit with spouse unless judicial separation or divorce is granted.
Duty to maintain spouse and children as per court orders.
obligations: Obligation to ensure one's spouse is not already married before solemnizing a Hindu marriage.
Obligation to ensure parties are not within prohibited degrees or sapinda relationship unless custom permits.
Obligation to adhere to age requirements for marriage.
Obligation to comply with court orders regarding maintenance, custody, and restitution of conjugal rights.

key_procedures: Petition for restitution of conjugal rights: Aggrieved party applies to the district court. Court satisfied with truth of statements and no legal ground to refuse may decree restitution.
Petition for judicial separation: Either party petitions for a decree based on specified grounds. If granted, cohabitation is not obligatory.
Petition for divorce: Either party petitions for divorce on specified grounds (e.g., adultery, desertion, cruelty).

Petition for divorce by mutual consent: Both parties jointly present a petition stating they have been living separately for one year or more and cannot live together, and mutually agree to dissolve the marriage.
Petition for nullity of void or voidable marriage: Either party presents a petition to declare the marriage null and void or to annul it based on specific grounds.
Application for maintenance pendente lite and expenses: A party can apply during proceedings for financial support and costs.
Application for permanent alimony and maintenance: A party can apply for ongoing financial support after a decree.
Application for custody of children: A party can apply for the custody, maintenance, and education of minor children.
Appeals from decrees and orders: Appeals can be filed against decrees and orders passed under the Act.
administration: The administration of this Act is generally carried out by the judiciary, specifically the District Courts and other civil courts empowered to hear matters under the Act. State Governments are responsible for making rules related to registration of marriages and for specifying courts with jurisdiction.
important_notes: The Act overrides existing Hindu law, customs, and usages, and any other law that is inconsistent with its provisions.
The provisions of this Act do not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes unless specifically directed by the Central Government.
The legitimacy of children born from void and voidable marriages is protected under Section 16.
Divorce by mutual consent requires parties to have lived separately for at least one year and to have failed to reconcile.

title: The Durgah Khawaja Saheb Act, 1955
purpose: To make provision for the proper administration of the Durgah and the Endowment of the Durgah of Khawaja Moin-ud-din Chishti, generally known as Durgah Khawaja Saheb, Ajmer.
scope: This Act applies to the Durgah Khawaja Saheb, Ajmer, and its endowment, which includes land, buildings, movable property, and all income dedicated to the Durgah or placed for religious, pious, or charitable purposes under its administration. It overrides the Religious Endowments Act, 1863 (XX of 1863).

key_definitions.Chief Commissioner: The Chief Commissioner of Ajmer, acting in his individual capacity.
key_definitions.Committee: The Committee constituted under section 4 of the Act.
key_definitions.Durgah: The institution known as the Durgah Khawaja Saheb, Ajmer, including its premises and all associated buildings and alterations.
key_definitions.Durgah Endowment: Includes the Durgah itself, all buildings and movable property within its boundaries, Durgah Jagir (land, houses, shops), other property and income dedicated to the Durgah, and nazars/offerings received on behalf of the Durgah.
key_definitions.Nazim: The Nazim appointed under section 9 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Durgah Khawaja Saheb Act, 1955, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including Chief Commissioner, Committee, Durgah, Durgah Endowment, and Nazim.

main_sections.section_title: Act to override Act XX of 1863
main_sections.description: States that this Act will have effect notwithstanding any inconsistency with the Religious Endowments Act, 1863.
Vests the administration, control, and management of the Durgah Endowment in a Committee named 'The Durgah Committee, Ajmer', which is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Specifies that the Committee shall consist of not less than five and not more than nine members, all of whom must be Hanafi Muslims, appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and resignation and removal of members and casual vacancies
main_sections.description: Outlines the tenure of Committee members (five years), conditions for resignation and removal (unsound mind, insolvency, moral turpitude conviction, absence, prejudice to Durgah interests), and procedures for filling casual vacancies.
Details the election of a President and Vice-President from among Committee members, and their respective roles and responsibilities in meetings.

Empowers the Central Government to supersede the Committee if it is found guilty of gross mismanagement or neglect, and to appoint a person to exercise the Committee's powers until a new Committee is formed.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to appoint Nazim
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to appoint a Nazim in consultation with the Committee, who will also serve as the Secretary. It also details the Nazim's salary, allowances, and the Committee's exercise of powers through the Nazim.
Allows the Central Government to constitute an Advisory Committee, consisting of up to seven Hanafi Muslims from Ajmer or neighbouring states, to advise the Nazim.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Committee
main_sections.description: Enumerate the Committee's responsibilities, including administering the Durgah Endowment, maintaining its buildings, receiving income, ensuring proper spending of funds, paying salaries, regulating Khadims' presence, defining the Advisory Committee's role, determining Sajjadanashin's powers, appointing Durgah servants, providing for descendants and Khadims, delegating powers to the Nazim, and performing incidental administrative tasks.
Specifies that the Sajjadanashin shall receive a monthly remuneration of two hundred rupees from the Durgah Endowment revenues.

main_sections.section_title: Succession to the office of Sajjadanashin
main_sections.description: Details the process for filling a vacancy in the Sajjadanashin's office, including interim arrangements, inviting applications, verifying claims, referring disputes to the Judicial Commissioner, and the finality of the Committee's order with the Chief Commissioner's approval.

main_sections.section_title: Power to solicit or receive offerings on behalf of the Durgah
main_sections.description: Grants the Nazim or authorized persons the exclusive right to solicit and receive offerings on behalf of the Durgah. It also specifies penalties for contravention and deems these individuals as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Committee to observe Muslim Law and tenets of the Chishti Saint
main_sections.description: Mandates that the Committee, in its functions, must follow Hanafi Muslim Law and conduct rites according to the tenets of the Chishti Saint.

Establishes a Board of Arbitration for disputes between the Committee and the Sajjadanashin, Khadims, or hereditary servants, if not related to religious usage or custom. The award of the Board is final and not subject to court challenge.

main_sections.section_title: Defect in the constitution of, or vacancy in, the Committee not to invalidate acts and proceedings
main_sections.description: Ensures that any vacancy or defect in the Committee's constitution will not invalidate its acts or proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Enforcement of final orders of Committee
main_sections.description: States that final orders of the Committee must be complied with, and non-compliance can be enforced by any civil court as if it were its own decree.

main_sections.section_title: Audit of accounts and annual report
main_sections.description: Requires annual audit of the Durgah's accounts by persons directed by the Central Government and the annual publication of an administration report along with audited accounts.
Empowers the Committee to make bye-laws to carry out the Act's purposes, including the division of duties among office bearers.
Covers provisions for the transition to the new Act.
Concerns the repeal of any previous enactments.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Committee shall administer, control, and manage the Durgah Endowment (Section 11(a)).
Rule 2: The Committee must keep Durgah buildings and properties in good repair (Section 11(b)).
Rule 3: All income of the Durgah Endowment must be received by the Committee (Section 11(c)).
Rule 4: Endowment funds must be spent according to the donors' intentions (Section 11(d)).
Rule 5: The Nazim or authorized persons are exclusively empowered to solicit and receive offerings on behalf of the Durgah (Section 14(1)).
Rule 6: The Committee must follow Hanafi Muslim Law and the tenets of the Chishti Saint in its functions and duties (Section 15).

penalties: Fine up to one thousand rupees for soliciting or receiving nazars or offerings in contravention of Section 14(1) (Section 14(2)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, the Committee, the Nazim, and civil courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By the Committee's orders, which can be executed by civil courts as if they were decrees. The Central Government can supersede the Committee and appoint individuals with its full powers. The Nazim is responsible for enforcing rules regarding offerings.

rights: Right to receive remuneration for the Sajjadanashin (Section 12).
Right of the Nazim or authorized persons to solicit and receive offerings (Section 14(1)).
Right of Khadims to have their privileges determined by the Committee (Section 11(f)).
duties: Duty of the Committee to administer, control, and manage the Durgah Endowment (Section 4(1)).
Duty of the Committee to maintain Durgah buildings and properties (Section 11(b)).
Duty of the Committee to ensure endowment funds are spent as per donors' wishes (Section 11(d)).
Duty of the Committee to follow Muslim Law and Chishti Saint's tenets (Section 15).
Duty of the Nazim to manage affairs as per the Committee's direction (Section 9(3)).
obligations: Obligation to comply with final orders passed by the Committee (Section 18).
Obligation for members of the Committee to act in the interests of the Durgah.
Obligation for claimants to Sajjadanashin office to follow the prescribed succession procedure (Section 13).

key_procedures: Procedure for Appointment and Removal of Committee Members: The Central Government appoints members, who serve for five years. Members can resign, and the Government can remove them under specific grounds. Casual vacancies are filled by appointment in consultation with remaining members (Section 6).

Procedure for Succession to Sajjadanashin Office: Upon vacancy, interim arrangements are made. Applications are invited, claims are verified. If multiple claimants, the dispute is referred to the Judicial Commissioner. The Committee, with Chief Commissioner's approval, declares the successor based on the decision (Section 13).

Procedure for Dispute Resolution: Disputes not related to religious usage or custom are referred to a Board of Arbitration comprising a nominee from each party and a District Judge appointed by the Central Government (Section 16(1)).

Procedure for Enforcement of Committee Orders: Civil courts can execute final orders of the Committee against any person if they are not complied with, using the same procedure as for its own decrees (Section 18).
