administration: The Committee, named 'The Durgah Committee, Ajmer', is responsible for the administration, control, and management of the Durgah Endowment, operating through the Nazim. The Central Government has oversight and powers of appointment, supersession, and direction.
important_notes: The Act specifically overrides the Religious Endowments Act, 1863 (Section 3).
The Committee must consist exclusively of Hanafi Muslims (Section 5).
Decisions regarding succession to the Sajjadanashin office are final and cannot be questioned in any court (Section 13(5)).
The Nazim, Sajjadanashin, and other authorized persons are considered public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 14(3)).

title: THE ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES ACT, 1955
purpose: To provide, in the interest of the general public, for the control of the production, supply and distribution of, and trade and commerce, in certain commodities.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to commodities declared as 'essential commodities' and is subject to Central Government regulations concerning their production, supply, distribution, and trade.

key_definitions.collector: Includes an Additional Collector and such other officer, not below the rank of Sub-Divisional Officer, as may be authorized by the Collector to perform the functions and exercise the powers of the Collector under this Act. (Note: Definitions vary by State Amendment, e.g., Maharashtra includes Controller of Rationing).
key_definitions.notified_order: Means an order notified in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.state_government: In relation to a Union territory, means the administrator thereof.
key_definitions.sugar: Means any form of sugar containing more than ninety per cent of sucrose, including sugar candy; khandsari sugar or bura sugar or crushed sugar or any sugar in crystalline or powdered form; or sugar in process in vacuum pan sugar factory or raw sugar produced therein.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Collector', 'food-crops', 'notified order', 'order', 'State Government', and 'sugar'. This section is subject to state amendments.

Defines 'essential commodity' as a commodity specified in the Schedule and empowers the Central Government to amend the Schedule by adding or removing commodities, subject to consultation with State Governments and parliamentary approval. It also allows for temporary declarations of essential commodities.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to control production, supply, distribution, etc., of essential commodities
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to regulate or prohibit the production, supply, distribution, and trade of essential commodities if it's deemed necessary for maintaining or increasing supplies, securing equitable distribution and availability at fair prices, or for defense purposes. This section outlines various types of orders that can be made, including licensing, price control, storage regulations, and prohibitions on withholding from sale.
Deals with the confiscation of essential commodities.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of orders made under the Act.

important_rules: Orders can be made to regulate production, supply, distribution, and trade of essential commodities.
Orders can mandate selling specified quantities of essential commodities to government or designated entities.
Orders can regulate prices at which essential commodities are bought or sold.
Orders can require persons to maintain and produce books, accounts, and records related to their business.
Orders can be made for entry, search, and seizure of premises, vehicles, and items related to contraventions.
The Central Government can declare a commodity as essential by amending the Schedule.
Temporary declarations of essential commodities can be made for a period not exceeding six months, with possible extensions.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of orders made under the Act (detailed in Section 7).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, and officers authorized by them.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued under the Act, which can include licensing, permits, price control, seizure of goods, and imposition of penalties. Enforcement also involves search, entry, and confiscation.

rights: Right to receive payment for essential commodities sold under order (Section 3(3)).
Right to make copies or take extracts of seized books of accounts and documents (Section 3(2)(j)(iii)).
duties: Duty to comply with orders regulating production, supply, distribution, and trade of essential commodities.
Duty to sell specified quantities of essential commodities when required by order.
Duty to maintain and produce books, accounts, and records for inspection.
Duty to facilitate entry, search, and seizure by authorized persons.
obligations: Obligation to comply with any order made by the Central Government under Section 3.
Obligation to adhere to specified prices or market rates for sales mandated by orders.

key_procedures: Declaration of essential commodities: Central Government may amend the Schedule to add or remove commodities.
Issuance of control orders: Central Government may issue orders to regulate production, supply, distribution, etc., of essential commodities.
Sale of essential commodities under order: Procedures for determining the price of commodities sold as per government orders.
Confiscation of essential commodity: Procedures involving show cause notices and appeal processes before confiscation (Sections 6A-6E).
Cognizance of offences: Rules regarding how courts take cognizance of offences under the Act (Section 11).
administration: Central Government and State Governments.
important_notes: The Act has been subject to various amendments by State Legislatures (e.g., Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh).
The extent of the Act was initially the whole of India, excluding the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but this exclusion was later omitted.
The Act has been extended to various Union Territories with modifications.

title: THE LIFE INSURANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the nationalisation of life insurance business in India by transferring all such business to a Corporation established for the purpose and to provide for the regulation and control of the business of the Corporation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the nationalisation, regulation, and control of life insurance business in India. It establishes the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) and defines its functions, management, and financial operations. It also covers the transfer of existing life insurance business to the LIC, the employment of existing insurance employees, and penalties for non-compliance. Certain exceptions are noted for insurance business concerning persons residing outside India.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which the Corporation is established under section 3.
key_definitions.Corporation: The Life Insurance Corporation of India established under section 3.
key_definitions.controlled business: Refers to the life insurance business of an insurer as defined in the Insurance Act, with specific conditions outlined for different types of insurers and their business in India.
key_definitions.insurer: An insurer as defined in the Insurance Act who carries on life insurance business in India, including the Government and a provident society.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Corporation', 'controlled business', 'insurer', 'Insurance Act', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Life Insurance Corporation of India
main_sections.description: Establishes the Life Insurance Corporation of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowering it to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue and be sued in its name.

Outlines the establishment of a Board of Directors for the general superintendence and direction of the Corporation's affairs and business. It specifies the composition of the Board, including the Chairperson, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, other Managing Directors, a government official, individuals with special knowledge, and representatives of members.
Details the functions that the Corporation is empowered to perform, related to carrying on life insurance business.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of existing insurers carrying on controlled business
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of assets and liabilities of existing insurers who were carrying on controlled business to the Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Corporation to have the exclusive privilege of carrying on life insurance business
main_sections.description: Grants the Corporation the exclusive privilege of carrying on life insurance business in India.

important_rules: All life insurance business in India is transferred to the Life Insurance Corporation of India upon its establishment.
The Corporation shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The general superintendence and direction of the Corporation's affairs vest in its Board of Directors.
The Corporation has the exclusive privilege of carrying on life insurance business in India.
Policies issued by the Corporation are guaranteed by the Central Government.

penalties: Penalty for withholding property, etc. (Section 40)
Penalties related to finance, accounts and audit (Section 24D)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and authorities appointed or designated under the Act, including Tribunals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of the Corporation, the Board of Directors, the enforcement of its functions, the application of penalties, and the jurisdiction of Tribunals for specific matters.

rights: Right of registered members to nominate (Section 5E)
Right of Corporation to seek relief in respect of certain transactions of the insurer (Section 15)
Rights of policyholders as guaranteed by the Central Government (Section 37)
duties: Duty to deliver possession of property and documents relating thereto (Section 13)
Corporation to be guided by the directions of the Central Government (Section 21)
obligations: Obligation to comply with foreign laws in certain cases (Section 33)
Obligations related to the management and financial reporting of the Corporation.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Corporation by the Central Government via notification.
Appointment and nomination of directors to the Board of Directors.
Transfer of assets and liabilities of existing insurers to the Corporation.
Conduct of annual general meetings and other general meetings.
Auditing of accounts by appointed auditors.
Actuarial valuations of the Corporation's business.
Submission of annual reports to Parliament.
administration: The Life Insurance Corporation of India, under the superintendence of its Board of Directors and guided by the Central Government.
important_notes: Exceptions exist for insurance business in respect of persons residing outside India (Section 31).
The Act does not apply in certain cases as specified (Section 44).
Defects in the constitution of the Corporation or Committees or in appointments do not invalidate acts or proceedings (Section 46).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 47).

title: THE INTER-STATE RIVER WATER DISPUTES ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers and river valleys.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to disputes between two or more State Governments concerning the use, distribution, or control of waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys, or the interpretation or implementation of agreements related to such waters.

key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Tribunal: A Water Disputes Tribunal constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.water_dispute: Any dispute or difference between two or more State Governments with respect to: (i) the use, distribution or control of the waters of, or in, any inter-State river or river valley; or (ii) the interpretation of the terms of any agreement relating to the use, distribution or control of such waters or the implementation of such agreement; or (iii) the levy of any water rate in contravention of the prohibition contained in section 7.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it extends to the whole of India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'prescribed', 'Tribunal', and 'water dispute'.

main_sections.section_title: Complaints by State Governments as to water disputes
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for a State Government to complain to the Central Government about a water dispute with another State Government, where its interests or those of its inhabitants are or are likely to be affected prejudicially.

Details the procedure for the Central Government to constitute a Water Disputes Tribunal if a dispute cannot be settled by negotiations. It specifies the composition of the Tribunal (Chairman and two other members nominated by the Chief Justice of India) and the possibility of appointing assessors.

Describes the process of referring water disputes to the Tribunal, the Tribunal's investigation, reporting within three years (with possible extensions), and the handling of differing opinions among members. It also allows for further consideration or clarification of the Tribunal's decision.
Mandates the Central Government to publish the Tribunal's decision in the Official Gazette, making it final and binding. The decision has the same force as an order or decree of the Supreme Court.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make schemes to implement decision of Tribunal
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame schemes for all matters necessary to give effect to the Tribunal's decision, including establishing authorities for implementation, specifying their powers and functions, and managing funds.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of levy of seigniorage, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits any State Government from imposing seigniorage or additional rates/fees for the use of water from an inter-State river just because works for its conservation or utilization are within its limits. Disputes regarding such levies are deemed water disputes.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of reference of certain disputes to Tribunal
main_sections.description: Excludes disputes that can be referred to arbitration under the River Boards Act, 1956, from being referred to a Tribunal.

Grants the Tribunal the same powers as a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning persons, requiring discovery of documents, issuing commissions, and other prescribed matters. It can also require State Governments to carry out surveys and investigations and can direct which Government shall bear the expenses and costs.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance of data bank and information
main_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to maintain a national-level data bank and information system for each river basin, with State Governments obligated to supply data. The Central Government has powers to verify this data.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Supreme Court and other courts
main_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts in relation to any water dispute, except for proceedings under this Act.
Provides for the dissolution of the Tribunal after it has completed its functions.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Ravi and Beas Waters Tribunal
main_sections.description: A specific provision related to the constitution of a Tribunal for the Ravi and Beas waters.

important_rules: Rule: State Governments must request the Central Government to refer a water dispute to a Tribunal if it cannot be settled by negotiations. (Section 3 & 4)
Rule: Decisions of the Tribunal are final and binding on the parties and must be published in the Official Gazette. (Section 6(1))
Rule: Decisions of the Tribunal have the same force as an order or decree of the Supreme Court. (Section 6(2))
Rule: No State Government shall impose seigniorage or additional water rates based solely on the construction of water resource works within its territory. (Section 7(1))
Rule: The Tribunal has the powers of a civil court in matters like summoning witnesses and requiring discovery of documents. (Section 9(1))
Rule: The Central Government shall maintain a national data bank for river basins, and State Governments must supply data. (Section 9A(1))

penalties: Any violation of the Act or the schemes framed under it could lead to penalties as prescribed by rules or implied by the enforcement of Tribunal decisions as Supreme Court orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and the Tribunal itself to some extent regarding its decisions and directives.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Publication of Tribunal decisions in the Official Gazette, making them binding and enforceable as Supreme Court orders. Central Government can frame schemes for implementation and direct State Governments. Powers of civil courts vested in the Tribunal for investigation and evidence gathering.

rights: Right of a State Government to request adjudication of a water dispute by a Tribunal if negotiations fail. (Section 3)
Right to have water disputes adjudicated by an independent Tribunal. (Section 4 & 5)
Right to have Tribunal decisions published and enforced. (Section 6)
duties: Duty of State Governments to negotiate to settle water disputes before approaching the Central Government. (Section 4(1))
Duty of State Governments to comply with the decisions of the Tribunal. (Section 6(1))
Duty of State Governments to supply data to the Central Government for the national data bank. (Section 9A(1))
Duty of State Governments to carry out or permit surveys and investigations required by the Tribunal. (Section 9(2))
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to constitute a Tribunal when a dispute cannot be settled by negotiations. (Section 4(1))
Obligation of the Central Government to publish the Tribunal's decision. (Section 6(1))
Obligation of the Central Government to frame schemes for implementing Tribunal decisions if necessary. (Section 6A(1))

key_procedures: Procedure for initiating a water dispute: A State Government believes a water dispute exists with another State, impacting its interests. It formally requests the Central Government to refer the dispute to a Tribunal. (Section 3)
Procedure for Tribunal Constitution: If the Central Government deems the dispute unresolvable by negotiation, it constitutes a Tribunal within one year. (Section 4(1))
Procedure for Adjudication: The Central Government refers the dispute to the Tribunal. The Tribunal investigates and reports its decision within three years (extendable). (Section 5(2))
Procedure for Implementing Decisions: The Central Government publishes the decision, making it binding. It may also frame schemes to ensure effective implementation. (Section 6 & 6A)
administration: Central Government (primarily through the Ministry of Water Resources, though not explicitly named in the provided text).
important_notes: The Act was extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Pondicherry.
The Act has been amended to include provisions for filling vacancies in the Tribunal and for the Central Government to make schemes for implementing Tribunal decisions.
The Act explicitly prohibits the levy of seigniorage or additional water rates by a State based solely on works within its territory for inter-State rivers.
Disputes settled by a Tribunal before the commencement of the Inter-State Water Disputes (Amendment) Act, 2002, are not to be reopened.

title: The Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956
purpose: To prevent undesirable transactions in securities by regulating the business of dealing therein and by providing for certain other matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It primarily applies to transactions in securities, stock exchanges, dealers in securities, and related matters. It also covers commodity derivatives and pooled investment vehicles as defined within the Act.

key_definitions.contract: A contract for or relating to the purchase or sale of securities.
key_definitions.corporatisation: The succession of a recognized stock exchange by another stock exchange which is a company incorporated for the purpose of assisting, regulating or controlling the business of buying, selling or dealing in securities.
key_definitions.demutualisation: The segregation of ownership and management from the trading rights of the members of a recognised stock exchange in accordance with a scheme approved by the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
key_definitions.derivative: Includes a security derived from a debt instrument, share, loan, risk instrument or contract for differences; a contract which derives its value from the prices, or index of prices, of underlying securities; commodity derivatives; and such other instruments as may be declared by the Central Government to be derivatives.
key_definitions.securities: Includes shares, scrips stocks, bonds, debentures, debenture stock or other marketable securities of the like nature in or of any incorporated company or a pooled investment vehicle or other body corporate; derivative; units or any other instrument issued by any collective investment scheme to the investors in such schemes; security receipt; units or any other such instrument issued to the investors under any mutual fund scheme; units or any other instrument issued by any pooled investment vehicle.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including contract, corporatisation, demutualisation, derivative, government security, goods, commodity derivative, member, non-transferable specific delivery contract, option in securities, pooled investment vehicle, prescribed, ready delivery contract, recognised stock exchange, rules, scheme, Securities Appellate Tribunal, and securities.

main_sections.section_title: Application for recognition of stock exchanges
main_sections.description: Details the process for stock exchanges to apply for recognition from the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of recognition to stock exchanges
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions and procedures for the Central Government to grant recognition to stock exchanges.

main_sections.section_title: Corporatisation and demutualisation of stock exchanges
main_sections.description: Provides for the corporatisation and demutualisation of recognized stock exchanges.

main_sections.section_title: Contracts in notified areas illegal in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Prohibits certain types of contracts in securities in notified areas under specific circumstances.
Covers general penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules/bye-laws made thereunder.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Securities and Exchange Board of India to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to make regulations for the Act.

important_rules: Rule: Contracts in notified areas are illegal under certain circumstances (Section 13).
Rule: Contracts in notified areas are void under certain circumstances (Section 14).
Rule: Members of a stock exchange may not act as principals in certain circumstances (Section 15).
Rule: The Central Government has the power to prohibit contracts in certain cases (Section 16).
Rule: Dealers in securities in certain areas require a license (Section 17).
Rule: Spot delivery contracts are excluded from certain prohibitions (Section 18).
Rule: Contracts in derivatives are regulated (Section 18A).

penalties: Penalty for failure to furnish information, return, etc. (Section 23A).
Penalty for failure by any person to enter into an agreement with clients (Section 23B).
Penalty for failure to redress investors' grievances (Section 23C).
Penalty for failure to segregate securities or moneys of clients (Section 23D).
Penalty for failure to comply with listing conditions or delisting conditions or grounds (Section 23E).
Penalty for excess dematerialisation or delivery of unlisted securities (Section 23F).
Penalty for failure to furnish periodical returns, etc. (Section 23G).
Penalty for failure to conduct business in accordance with rules, etc. (Section 23GA).
Penalty for contravention where no separate penalty has been provided (Section 23H).
Contravention by companies can lead to penalties (Section 24).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and Special Courts established under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves adjudication of penalties, prosecution for offences, and establishment of Special Courts for trial of offences. SEBI also has powers to issue directions and settle administrative and civil proceedings.

rights: Right of appeal to Securities Appellate Tribunal against refusal by stock exchanges to list securities of public companies (Section 22A).
Right to legal representation before the Securities Appellate Tribunal (Section 22C).
Right to appeal to the Supreme Court from orders of the Securities Appellate Tribunal (Section 22F).
duties: Recognised stock exchanges have duties to furnish annual reports to the Central Government (Section 7).
Members of stock exchanges have duties related to their dealings in securities as prescribed by rules and bye-laws.
obligations: Persons dealing in securities are obligated to comply with the regulations set forth in the Act, rules, and bye-laws.
Companies issuing securities are obligated to comply with listing conditions.

key_procedures: Procedure for application for and grant of recognition to stock exchanges (Sections 3 and 4).
Procedure for corporatisation and demutualisation of stock exchanges (Sections 4A and 4B).
Procedure for adjudication of penalties (Sections 23-I to 23JB).
Procedure for establishment and functioning of Special Courts for trial of offences (Sections 26A to 26E).
Appeals to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and Supreme Court (Sections 22A, 22F, 23L, 26C).
administration: The Central Government and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) administer the Act.
important_notes: The Act does not apply in certain cases as specified in Section 28.
Protection of action taken in good faith is provided under Section 29.
Powers of SEBI do not apply to International Financial Services Centres as per Section 29B.
Special provisions exist for commodity derivatives (Section 30A) and pooled investment vehicles (Section 30B).

title: The Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957
purpose: To provide for the extension to cantonments of laws relating to the control of rent and regulation of house accommodation.
scope: Applies to cantonments in India. Specifically, it empowers the Central Government to extend state laws concerning rent control and house accommodation regulation to cantonments. Section 4 details the extension of the Madhya Bharat Accommodation Control Act, 1955, to the cantonment of Mhow.

key_definitions.cantonment: Any place declared to be a cantonment under section 3 of the Cantonments Act, 1924 (2 of 1924).

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states its deemed commencement date as January 26, 1950.
Defines the term 'cantonment'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to extend to cantonments laws relating to control of rents and regulation of house accommodation
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to extend state laws related to rent control and house accommodation to any cantonment, with possible restrictions and modifications. It outlines exceptions for government-owned premises, tenancies created by government grants, and houses appropriated by the Central Government. It also specifies rules regarding the effective date of extension and how previously made decrees or orders under state laws will be treated after the extension.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the Madhya Bharat Accommodation Control Act, 1955 to the cantonment of Mhow
main_sections.description: Details the extension of the Madhya Bharat Accommodation Control Act, 1955, to the cantonment of Mhow. It specifies modifications to the extended Act, including substitutions for certain phrases, adjustments to its applicability and duration, and omissions of certain sections. It also clarifies the status of existing laws and decrees in Mhow cantonment before and after the extension.

important_rules: The Central Government can extend state rent control laws to cantonments by notification.
Extensions can be made with restrictions and modifications.
Government-owned premises, tenancies created by government grants, and government-appropriated houses are exempt from extended laws.

The extension of a state law cannot be made effective from a date earlier than the commencement of that state law, the establishment of the cantonment, or the commencement of the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957, whichever is later.
Decrees or orders made under state rent control laws before the extension to a cantonment are deemed to have been made under the corresponding provisions of the extended law.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, and presumably the authorities responsible for enforcing the extended state laws within the cantonment.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications by the Central Government extending specific state laws, and subsequent enforcement of those extended laws by designated authorities within the cantonment.

rights: Tenants in cantonments may gain the rights provided by the extended rent control laws.
Government has certain rights regarding its property in cantonments as specified in the exemptions.
duties: Landlords and tenants are subject to the duties and obligations prescribed by the extended rent control laws.
The Central Government has a duty to act through notifications for extensions.
obligations: Landlords and tenants must comply with the provisions of the extended rent control laws.
The Central Government has an obligation to follow the procedural requirements for extension.

key_procedures: Central Government issues a notification to extend a state rent control law to a specific cantonment.
The notification may include restrictions and modifications to the extended law.
The Central Government determines the effective date of the extension, subject to certain limitations.
Existing decrees or orders are deemed to be made under the extended law.
administration: Central Government (specifically, the department or ministry responsible for cantonment administration and housing).
important_notes: The Act is designed to address potential gaps in rent control legislation within cantonments.
Specific modifications are detailed for the extension of the Madhya Bharat Accommodation Control Act, 1955, to Mhow cantonment, including its duration.
The amendment by Act 22 of 1972 introduced changes related to the commencement date and extended the scope of application retroactively.

title: The Delhi Development Act, 1957
purpose: To provide for the planned development of Delhi and for matters ancillary thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. It applies to the development of land and buildings in Delhi according to a master plan and zonal development plans.

key_definitions.amenity: Includes road, water supply, street lighting, drainage, sewerage, public works and other conveniences specified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.building: Includes any structure or erection intended for residential, industrial, commercial, or other purposes, whether in actual use or not.
key_definitions.building operations: Includes rebuilding, structural alterations or additions to buildings, and operations normally undertaken in connection with construction.
key_definitions.development: Carrying out building, engineering, mining, or other operations on land, or making any material change in any building or land, including redevelopment.
key_definitions.development area: Any area declared as such under sub-section (1) of section 12.
key_definitions.engineering operations: Includes forming or laying out means of access to a road or laying out means of water supply.
key_definitions.means of access: Includes any private or public means of access for vehicles or foot passengers, and includes a road.
key_definitions.regulation: A regulation made by the Delhi Development Authority.
key_definitions.rule: A rule made by the Central Government.
key_definitions.to erect: In relation to a building, includes material alteration or enlargement, conversion to a place for human habitation, conversion into more than one place of habitation, alterations affecting drainage or security, addition of rooms/structures, and construction of a door opening onto an adjoining street or land.
key_definitions.zone: A division of Delhi for the purposes of development under this Act.
key_definitions.land: As defined in section 3 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (National Capital Territory of Delhi), and the commencement date to be appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as amenity, building, development, development area, regulation, rule, etc.

Establishes the Delhi Development Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, outlining its composition and the qualifications/appointment of its members (Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Finance and Accounts Member, Engineer Member, representatives of Municipal Corporation and Legislative Assembly, nominated members, Commissioner of Municipal Corporation).

Outlines the main objectives of the Delhi Development Authority, which include preparing and executing a master plan and zonal development plans for Delhi, developing and redeveloping land, and providing amenities.

main_sections.section_title: Civic survey of, and master plan for, Delhi
main_sections.description: Mandates the Authority to carry out a civic survey of Delhi and to prepare a master plan for the development of Delhi.
Requires the Authority to prepare zonal development plans for different zones within Delhi, based on the master plan.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of development areas and development of land in those and other areas
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare any area as a development area and outlines provisions for the development of land in development areas and other areas.
Grants the Authority power to acquire land compulsorily for the purpose of development.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of land by the Authority or the local authority concerned
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for the disposal of land by the Authority or the concerned local authority.
Specifies the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act, including the plans prepared under it.
Gives the Authority power to order the demolition of any building that contravenes the Act or the plans.
Empowers the Authority to stop any development work that is being carried out in contravention of the Act or the plans.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Authority to levy betterment charges
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to levy betterment charges on properties that have increased in value due to development carried out by the Authority.
States that the Central Government shall have overall control of the Authority and may give directions to it.
Confers power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Confers power on the Delhi Development Authority to make regulations for carrying out its functions under the Act.
Deals with the repeal of certain previous laws and savings in respect of actions taken under them.

important_rules: Development of land must be in accordance with the Master Plan and Zonal Development Plans.
Application for permission is required for development of land.
User of land and buildings must conform to the plans.
Development carried out in contravention of plans can be stopped or demolished.
Betterment charges can be levied on properties benefiting from development.

penalties: Penalties for contravening the Act's provisions, including fines and imprisonment.
Order of demolition of buildings that contravene the Act or plans.
Power to seal unauthorised development.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Delhi Development Authority, with oversight from the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, issuing stop orders, demolition orders, sealing unauthorized development, and prosecution for offenses.

rights: Right to develop land in accordance with approved plans.
Right to appeal against certain orders of the Authority.
Right to receive amenities provided by the Authority.
duties: Duty to prepare and execute Master Plan and Zonal Development Plans.
Duty to ensure development is in accordance with plans.
Duty to provide amenities.
Duty to enforce the provisions of the Act.
obligations: Obligation to obtain permission for development.
Obligation to comply with the Master Plan and Zonal Development Plans.
Obligation to pay betterment charges where applicable.
Obligation to allow entry and inspection by Authority officials.

key_procedures: Preparation and approval of Master Plan and Zonal Development Plans: Includes civic survey, plan preparation, submission to Central Government, public notice, objections and suggestions, and final approval.
Application for permission to develop land: Involves submission of plans, scrutiny, and grant or refusal of permission.
Levy and assessment of betterment charges: Involves determination of increased value due to development and settlement of charges.
Appeals against orders: Procedures for filing appeals before the Appellate Tribunal and further appeals.
administration: The Delhi Development Authority, with overall control and rule-making power vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1996 to substitute 'National Capital Territory of Delhi' for 'Union territory of Delhi'.
The Act provides for an Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals against orders passed by the Authority.
Courts' jurisdiction is barred in certain matters, with appeals to the Appellate Tribunal being the designated remedy.

title: The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958
purpose: To provide for the preservation of ancient and historical monuments and archaeological sites and remains of national importance, for the regulation of archaeological excavations, and for the protection of sculptures, carvings, and other like objects.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to ancient monuments, archaeological sites and remains, and antiquities that are declared to be of national importance. It also establishes regulations for prohibited and regulated areas around protected monuments.

key_definitions.ancient_monument: Any structure, erection or monument, or any tumulus or place of interment, or any cave, rock sculpture, inscription or monolith, which is of historical, archaeological or artistic interest and which has been in existence for not less than one hundred years, and includes its remains, site, adjoining land for preservation, and means of access.
key_definitions.antiquity: Includes coins, sculptures, manuscripts, epigraphs, works of art or craftsmanship, articles detached from buildings or caves, articles illustrative of past cultures, and articles of historical interest, all existing for at least one hundred years, and anything declared as such by the Central Government.
key_definitions.archaeological_site_and_remains: Any area containing or believed to contain ruins or relics of historical or archaeological importance existing for at least one hundred years, including adjoining land for preservation and means of access.
key_definitions.protected_monument: An ancient monument declared to be of national importance.
key_definitions.protected_area: An archaeological site and remains declared to be of national importance.
key_definitions.prohibited_area: Any area specified or declared as a prohibited area under section 20A.
key_definitions.regulated_area: Any area specified or declared under section 20B.
key_definitions.construction: Any erection of a structure or building, including additions or extensions, but excludes reconstruction, repair and renovation of existing structures, drainage works, public latrines, water supply works, and electricity supply infrastructure for public use.
key_definitions.re_construction: Erection of a structure or building to its pre-existing structure, having the same horizontal and vertical limits.
key_definitions.repair_and_renovation: Alterations to a pre-existing structure or building, not including construction or re-construction.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'ancient monument', 'antiquity', 'archaeological site and remains', 'protected monument', 'protected area', 'prohibited area', 'regulated area', 'construction', 're-construction', and 'repair and renovation'.

main_sections.section_title: Certain ancient monuments, etc., deemed to be of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares that all ancient and historical monuments and archaeological sites and remains declared as of national importance under previous Acts (1951 and 1956) are deemed to be of national importance for the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to declare ancient monuments, etc., to be of national importance
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to declare ancient monuments or archaeological sites and remains not already covered as being of national importance, following a notification and objection period.

main_sections.section_title: Categorisation and classification in respect of ancient monuments or archaeological sites and remains declared as of national importance
main_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government, on the recommendation of the National Monuments Authority, to prescribe categories and classify monuments and sites based on their historical, archaeological, and architectural value, making this information publicly available.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of rights in a protected monument
main_sections.description: Empowers the Director-General, with Central Government sanction, to purchase, lease, or accept gifts or bequests of protected monuments. It also allows the Director-General to assume guardianship of monuments without owners or accept guardianship constituted by the owner.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on enjoyment of property rights in protected areas
main_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on the enjoyment of property rights within protected areas to ensure their preservation.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of prohibited area and carrying out public work or other works in prohibited area
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to declare a prohibited area around a protected monument and specifies conditions for carrying out public works or other works within it.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of regulated area in respect of every protected monument
main_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to declare a regulated area around every protected monument.

main_sections.section_title: Application for repair or renovation in prohibited area, or construction or re-construction or repair or renovation in regulated area
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for applying for permissions for repair or renovation in prohibited areas, and construction, re-construction, repair, or renovation in regulated areas.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of permission by competent authority within regulated area
main_sections.description: Details the process by which a competent authority grants permission for activities within a regulated area.
Provides for the establishment of the National Monuments Authority.
Outlines the various functions and powers vested in the National Monuments Authority.
Specifies penalties for contravening provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for construction, etc., in prohibited area
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for undertaking construction or similar activities in a prohibited area.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for construction, etc., in regulated area
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for undertaking construction or similar activities in a regulated area.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous legislation and savings provisions.

important_rules: Any ancient monument or archaeological site and remains declared of national importance by the Central Government is protected under this Act.
Construction, re-construction, repair, or renovation in prohibited or regulated areas around protected monuments requires permission from the competent authority.
The National Monuments Authority plays a key role in categorizing and classifying national monuments and archaeological sites and remains.
The Director-General, with Central Government sanction, can acquire rights in protected monuments.
Activities that damage or misuse protected monuments, archaeological sites, or remains are subject to penalties.

penalties: Punishment for construction, etc., in prohibited area (Section 30A).
Punishment for construction, etc., in regulated area (Section 30B).
General penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 30).
Special provision regarding fine (Section 33).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Director-General of Archaeology, Archaeological Officer, Competent Authority, National Monuments Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, declarations of national importance, acquisition of rights, prohibition of activities in regulated/prohibited areas, grant of permissions, imposition of penalties, and by enabling the Director-General to assume guardianship and enforce agreements.

rights: Right of access to protected monuments (Section 18).
Right to object to the declaration of a monument or site as being of national importance (Section 4(2)).
duties: Duty to preserve ancient monuments and archaeological sites and remains of national importance.
Duty to obtain necessary permissions before undertaking construction or renovation in regulated and prohibited areas.
Duty to cooperate with authorities for the preservation and management of protected monuments and areas.
obligations: Owners of protected monuments have obligations related to their preservation.
Individuals and entities must adhere to the restrictions and regulations imposed in protected, prohibited, and regulated areas.
Obligation to survey protected, prohibited, and regulated areas and identify unauthorized constructions (Section 35A, 35B).

key_procedures: Declaration of ancient monuments, archaeological sites, and remains as being of national importance, involving notification and a period for objections (Section 4).
Application and grant of permission for construction, re-construction, repair, or renovation in regulated and prohibited areas (Sections 20C, 20D).
Constitution and functioning of the National Monuments Authority (Sections 20F to 20N).
Acquisition of rights in a protected monument by purchase, lease, gift, or bequest (Section 5).
Assuming guardianship of a protected monument by the Director-General (Section 5(2)).
administration: Central Government, with administrative roles for the Director-General of Archaeology, Archaeological Officers, the National Monuments Authority, and competent authorities specified by the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act was extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Pondicherry with modifications.
Section 2A regarding references to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir was omitted.
The Act is now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
The definition of 'construction' specifically excludes reconstruction, repair, and renovation of existing structures, as well as essential public utility works.

title: The Sugar Export Promotion Act, 1958
purpose: To provide for the export of sugar in the public interest and for the levy and collection in certain circumstances of an additional duty of excise on sugar produced in India, with the objective of earning foreign exchange.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to sugar production by factories using the vacuum pan process. It specifically addresses the export of sugar and the associated financial and regulatory mechanisms.

key_definitions.export: Taking out of India by sea, land or air.
key_definitions.export agency: Any company or body of persons specified by the Central Government for this purpose, or the Central Government itself if no agency is specified.
key_definitions.export quota: The quantity of sugar apportioned to a factory owner for export as determined under section 5.
key_definitions.factory: Any premises, including precincts, where sugar is produced by the vacuum pan process.
key_definitions.owner: Refers to the current possessor or authorized agent of a factory, including transferees under lease or mortgage, agents of owners, or persons/bodies managing the factory under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.
key_definitions.sugar: Any form of sugar containing more than ninety per cent of sucrose.
key_definitions.year: The period beginning on the first day of May.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Sugar Export Promotion Act, 1958, and states its applicability to the whole of India.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'export', 'export agency', 'export quota', 'factory', 'owner', 'sugar', and 'year'.
Empowers the Central Government to specify a company or body corporate as an export agency for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Fixation of quantity of sugar for purposes of export
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to fix the quantity of sugar for export, considering availability in India, domestic consumption needs, and the necessity of earning foreign exchange. The export quantity is limited to twenty percent of the sugar produced in a season.
Details the process by which the Central Government will apportion the fixed export quantity among factory owners based on their production.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of owner to deliver export quota to export agency
main_sections.description: Mandates owners to deliver their export quota to the export agency as demanded, and states that the owner relinquishes rights to the delivered sugar except for payment.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of additional excise duty on sugar
main_sections.description: Specifies the levy and collection of an additional excise duty on sugar dispatched for domestic consumption when it falls short of the export quota. It also outlines penalties for non-payment and refers to the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 for procedural aspects.

main_sections.section_title: Sale by export agency of sugar delivered
main_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of the export agency to export delivered sugar, with provisions for selling sugar in India if deemed expedient, or allowing owners to sell under specific conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Payments to owners in respect of sugar delivered
main_sections.description: Describes how payments will be made to owners for sugar delivered, involving deductions for expenses and apportionment of the balance based on delivered quantities and grade adjustments.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions
main_sections.description: States that the export agency must follow directions given in writing by the Central Government.
Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act to subordinate officers or authorities through notification.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder by the export agency or the Central Government.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, including provisions for returns, accounts, inspection, payments, and penalties for breaches. Rules are subject to parliamentary modification.
This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1960.

important_rules: Owners must deliver their allocated export quota of sugar to the designated export agency upon demand.
An additional excise duty will be levied on sugar dispatched for domestic consumption if it falls short of the export quota.
The export agency is responsible for taking practical measures to export the delivered sugar, with the option to sell it domestically if necessary.
Payments to owners will be based on the total sale proceeds of exported sugar, after deducting expenses, and adjusted for grade differences.

penalties: Penalty for non-payment of the additional excise duty: up to ten percent of the outstanding duty for every thirty days or part thereof of default.
Breach of rules made under the Act may be punishable with a fine extending to five thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The export agency, acting under the directions of the Central Government. The Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 also plays a role in the levy and collection of duties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through demand for delivery of export quotas, levy and collection of excise duties, penalties for defaults, and enforcement of rules made under the Act. The Central Government can also issue directions and delegate powers for enforcement.

rights: Owners have the right to receive payment for the sugar delivered to the export agency.
Owners have the right to receive payments determined in accordance with the Act's provisions, including deductions for expenses and adjustments for grade.
duties: Owners have a duty to deliver their export quota to the export agency.
Owners have a duty to pay any additional excise duty levied on sugar not delivered for export.
Owners have a duty to submit returns or reports related to sugar production, sale, dispatch, stocks, and prices as may be required by rules.
obligations: The export agency has an obligation to take all practical measures to export sugar delivered to it.
The Central Government has the obligation to provide directions to the export agency and make rules to carry out the Act's purposes.

key_procedures: Fixation of total export quantity by the Central Government, considering availability, domestic needs, and foreign exchange requirements.
Apportionment of the export quantity among factory owners as export quotas, based on their production.
Delivery of the export quota by owners to the export agency as demanded.
Levy and collection of additional excise duty on sugar not delivered for export.
Export or sale of sugar by the export agency.
Payment to owners based on sale proceeds, expenses, and grade adjustments.
Submission of returns and information by owners as prescribed by rules.
administration: The Central Government, with the specified export agency acting under its directions. Rules and procedures may involve authorities specified by the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act was repealed by Ordinance 4 of 1997, with effect from January 15, 1997.
The Central Excise (Conversion to Metric Units) Act, 1960 and The Repealing and Amending Act, 1960 are listed as amending acts.
Section 7(1) mentions the duty rate as 'forty-five rupees and fifty five naye paise per quintal', which was substituted for 'seventeen rupees per mound'.

title: THE SUPREME COURT JUDGES (SALARIES AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) ACT, 1958
purpose: To regulate salaries and certain conditions of service of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
scope: Applies to the Judges of the Supreme Court of India, including the Chief Justice and Acting Chief Justice. It also covers service as a Judge in India, which includes service in the Supreme Court and High Courts.

key_definitions.acting Chief Justice: A Judge appointed under article 126 of the Constitution to perform the duties of the Chief Justice of India.
key_definitions.actual service: Includes time spent by a Judge on duty as a Judge, or in the performance of such other functions as he may, at the request of the President, undertake to discharge, and vacations.
key_definitions.Chief Justice: The Chief Justice of India, but does not include an acting Chief Justice.
key_definitions.High Court: The High Court for a State.
key_definitions.Judge: A Judge of the Supreme Court and includes the Chief Justice and an acting Chief Justice.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.service as a Judge in India: Service rendered in the Supreme Court and in one or more of the High Courts.
key_definitions.service for pension: Includes actual service; time spent by a Judge of a High Court in attending the sittings of the Supreme Court as an ad hoc Judge under article 127 of the Constitution, if he is subsequently appointed as a Judge; the amount, actually taken, of each period of leave on full allowances at a rate equal to the monthly rate of the salary; and vacation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1958.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'acting Chief Justice', 'actual service', 'Chief Justice', 'High Court', 'Judge', 'prescribed', 'service as a Judge in India', and 'service for pension'.

main_sections.section_title: Kinds of leave admissible to a Judge
main_sections.description: Specifies that leave granted to a Judge may be at his option either on full allowances, half allowances, or partly on full and partly on half allowances. It also states that leave on full allowances is reckoned as double that period of leave on half allowances and that casual leave may be admissible.

main_sections.section_title: Leave account showing the amount of leave due
main_sections.description: Details the maintenance of a leave account for each Judge, outlining what is credited (e.g., one-fourth of actual service, compensation for un-enjoyed vacation, leave earned as a High Court Judge) and debited (leave taken).
Entitles a Judge to claim the cash equivalent of leave salary on retirement in respect of the period of leave at his credit, calculated on full allowances basis.

main_sections.section_title: Aggregate amount of leave which may be granted
main_sections.description: Sets the maximum aggregate amount of leave that can be granted to a Judge during their entire service in terms of leave on half allowances and leave on full allowances.

main_sections.section_title: Commutation of leave on half allowances into leave on full allowances
main_sections.description: Allows a Judge to commute leave on half allowances into leave on full allowances on medical certificate up to a maximum of three months.
Permits grant of leave on half allowances in excess of the amount at credit, on medical certificate or otherwise, provided the Judge is expected to return to duty.
States that special disability leave may be granted under prescribed circumstances, on specified allowances and for specified periods.
Allows for extraordinary leave for a period not exceeding six months, during which no salary or allowances are payable.
Specifies that the monthly rate of leave salary payable to a Judge shall be in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 3.
Allows a Judge to combine vacation with leave under certain conditions related to the timing and continuity of the vacation and leave.

main_sections.section_title: Consequences of over staying leave or vacation
main_sections.description: States that a Judge overstaying leave or vacation shall receive no salary for the period of absence, unless the absence is due to circumstances beyond control and treated as leave.
Designates the President as the authority competent to grant, refuse, revoke, or curtail leave, after consultation with the Chief Justice.
Specifies the monthly salaries payable to the Chief Justice of India and other Judges of the Supreme Court.

Outlines the conditions under which a pension is payable to a Judge of the Supreme Court upon retirement, including reaching the age of sixty-five years or medical certification of ill-health. An explanation clarifies the definition of 'Judge' for this section.

main_sections.section_title: Benefit of added years of service
main_sections.description: Grants a period of ten years to be added to the service of a Judge for pension purposes, if they qualified for appointment under a specific constitutional provision.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions for pension in respect of Judges who are members of service
main_sections.description: Addresses pension for Judges who have held other pensionable posts under the Union or a State, requiring them to elect between pension under Part I or Part III of the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Power of President to add to the service for pension
main_sections.description: Empowers the President to add to the service for pension under specific circumstances.
Mentions provisions for extraordinary pension.
Provides for family pension and gratuity for Judges.

main_sections.section_title: Additional quantum of pension or family pension
main_sections.description: Allows for an additional quantum of pension or family pension.

main_sections.section_title: Pension payable to a Judge who was in receipt of pension at the time of appointment as such
main_sections.description: Deals with the pension payable to a Judge who was already receiving a pension at the time of their appointment as a Judge.
This section has been omitted from the Act.
Provides for the commutation of pension.
Addresses the provident fund for Judges.
Introduces a Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme.
Specifies the authority competent to grant pension.
Deals with the travelling allowance admissible to a Judge.

main_sections.section_title: Facilities for rent-free houses and other conditions of service
main_sections.description: Covers facilities for rent-free houses and other conditions of service for Judges.
Provides for conveyance facilities for Judges.
Grants sumptuary allowance to Judges.
Ensures medical facilities for retired Judges.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption from liability to pay Income-tax on certain perquisites received by a Judge
main_sections.description: Exempts Judges from paying Income-tax on certain perquisites received by them.
Empowers the appropriate authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Contains provisions for savings, ensuring that the Act does not affect certain pre-existing rights or liabilities.

important_rules: Leave on full allowances is reckoned as double the period of leave on half allowances.
A Judge is entitled to claim the cash equivalent of leave salary on retirement for the period of leave at their credit.
The aggregate amount of leave granted cannot exceed specific limits based on leave on half and full allowances.
Leave on half allowances can be granted in excess of the credit on medical certificate or otherwise, if the Judge is expected to return to duty.
Judges overstaying leave or vacation will not receive salary for the period of absence unless it's due to circumstances beyond their control and treated as leave.
The President, in consultation with the Chief Justice, is the authority competent to grant or refuse leave.
Specific monthly salaries are prescribed for the Chief Justice of India and other Judges.
Pension is payable upon retirement if the Judge has attained the age of sixty-five years or their retirement is medically certified due to ill-health.
A Judge can elect to receive pension under Part I or Part III of the Schedule if they have held other pensionable posts.
The President has the power to add to the service for pension under certain conditions.

penalties: If a Judge overstays leave or vacation, they shall receive no salary in respect of the period of absence in excess of the leave granted or beyond the end of the vacation, unless the absence is due to circumstances beyond their control and treated as leave.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The President, in consultation with the Chief Justice of India, is the authority competent to grant leave and likely involved in overall administration and enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act itself, including regulations on salaries, leave, pension, and other conditions of service. Rules made under the Act also play a role in enforcement. The President exercises powers related to leave and pension.

rights: Right to receive specified salaries.
Right to various kinds of leave (full allowances, half allowances, special disability leave, extraordinary leave).
Right to combine leave with vacation.
Right to leave encashment on retirement.
Right to pension upon retirement under specified conditions.
Right to a period of ten years added to service for pension calculation in certain cases.
Right to receive conveyance facilities.
Right to sumptuary allowance.
Right to medical facilities for retired Judges.
Right to exemption from Income-tax on certain perquisites.
duties: Duty to perform functions as a Judge.
Duty to undertake other functions at the request of the President.
Duty to return to duty at the end of leave or vacation, unless otherwise permitted or due to circumstances beyond control.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the terms and conditions of service as laid down in the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation to retire at the age of sixty-five years for pension entitlement, or retire due to medically certified ill-health.
Obligation to elect pension benefits if previously holding other pensionable posts.

key_procedures: Grant of leave: A Judge can request leave, and the President, in consultation with the Chief Justice, is the competent authority to grant or refuse it.

Calculation of leave due: A leave account is maintained for each Judge, crediting periods of actual service, compensation for un-enjoyed vacation, and leave earned as a High Court Judge, and debiting leave taken.
Leave encashment: Upon retirement, a Judge can claim cash equivalent of leave salary for credited leave.

Pension calculation: Pension is calculated based on service, age of retirement, or medical certification of ill-health, with provisions for added years of service and options for Judges with prior pensionable service.
Rule making: The Act empowers the President to make rules for its implementation.
administration: The Act is administered through the provisions laid out for salaries, leave, pensions, and other conditions of service. The President and the Chief Justice play key roles in its administration, particularly concerning leave and rule-making. The Ministry of Law and Justice in India is generally responsible for legislation related to the judiciary.
important_notes: Subsequent amendments have updated salary figures for Judges.
The Act was significantly amended in 1998 to revise conditions of service.
Provisions for family pension, gratuity, and additional pension have been introduced through amendments.
The definition of 'service for pension' includes specific inclusions like time spent as an ad hoc Supreme Court Judge and periods of leave on full allowances.

title: The International Finance Corporation (Status, Immunities and Privileges) Act, 1958
purpose: To implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the International Finance Corporation by conferring upon it and its officers and employees the necessary status, immunities, and privileges in India, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the International Finance Corporation (the 'Corporation') and its officers and employees, as well as to the provisions of the international agreement related to the Corporation's status, immunities, and privileges.

key_definitions.agreement: The Agreement for the establishment and operation of the international body known as the International Finance Corporation.
key_definitions.corporation: The International Finance Corporation established under the Agreement.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent, which is the whole of India. It also notes an extension to the Union territory of Pondicherry.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, specifically 'Agreement' and 'Corporation'.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of status and certain immunities and privileges on the Corporation and conferment of certain immunities and privileges on its officers and employees
main_sections.description: This section gives the provisions of the Agreement set out in the Schedule the force of law in India. It includes a proviso clarifying limitations on the Corporation's ability to import goods free of customs duty and exemptions from certain taxes. It also grants the Central Government the power to amend the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette, subject to parliamentary approval.

This section empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act by notification in the Official Gazette. It also outlines the procedure for laying such rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.

important_rules: The provisions of the Agreement set out in the Schedule shall have the force of law in India.
The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, amend the Schedule in conformity with amendments to the Agreement.
Every rule made under this Act shall be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period for potential modification or annulment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government is empowered to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, and the Act itself grants specific immunities and privileges which, by implication, would be enforced through appropriate legal and administrative channels.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would likely involve the application of the provisions of the Schedule (which are given force of law) and any rules made by the Central Government under Section 4 of the Act. The immunities and privileges conferred would be recognized and upheld by Indian courts and administrative bodies.

rights: The Corporation is granted juridical personality, capacity to contract, acquire/dispose of property, and institute legal proceedings.
The Corporation, its assets, property, income, operations, and transactions are immune from all taxation and customs duties.
The Corporation is immune from liability for the collection or payment of any tax or duty.
No tax shall be levied on salaries and emoluments paid to non-local Directors, Alternates, officials, or employees.
No tax shall be levied on obligations or securities issued or guaranteed by the Corporation, under certain conditions.
Officers and employees of the Corporation are immune from legal process for acts performed in their official capacity.
Non-local officers and employees are accorded immunities from immigration restrictions, alien registration, national service obligations, and certain exchange restrictions.
Officers and employees are granted specific travelling facilities.
The Corporation's archives are inviolable.
The Corporation's official communications are to be treated with the same treatment as those of other members.
duties: The Corporation must adhere to generally applicable foreign exchange restrictions in member territories for funds received or payable in respect of investments.
The Corporation must adhere to the provisions of Article III, Section 5, and other provisions of the Agreement when carrying out operations.

key_procedures: Amendment of the Schedule: The Central Government can amend the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette to conform with amendments to the Agreement. Such notifications must be laid before Parliament for at least thirty days and are subject to parliamentary modification.

Rule-making by Central Government: The Central Government can make rules to carry out the Act's purposes. These rules must be laid before Parliament for thirty days, during which they can be modified or annulled by mutual agreement of both Houses.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for making rules and potentially amending the Schedule to the Act.
important_notes: Proviso to Section 3(1) clarifies that the Corporation is not entitled to import goods free of customs duty without restriction on subsequent sale, nor is it exempt from taxes that are charges for services rendered.
The Act's extension to Pondicherry by Act 26 of 1968.
Sub-section (2) of Section 4 was substituted by Act 20 of 1983.

The Schedule details specific provisions of the Agreement that have the force of law in India, including details on financing operations, applicability of foreign exchange restrictions, the Corporation's status, immunities from judicial process, immunity of assets and archives, freedom of assets from restrictions, privilege for communications, immunities and privileges of officers/employees, and immunities from taxation. Section 10 of the Schedule allows the Corporation to waive its privileges and immunities.

title: The Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959
purpose: To declare the Indian Statistical Institute as an institution of national importance and to provide for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the Indian Statistical Institute, which is registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, and has its registered office in Calcutta. It grants the Central Government powers to oversee and direct the Institute's activities, including its educational and research programs.

key_definitions.institute: The Indian Statistical Institute registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.memorandum: The memorandum of association of the Institute filed with the Registrar of Joint-Stock Companies under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.rules and regulations: Includes any rule or regulation (by whatever name called) which the Institute is competent to make under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, but excludes bye-laws or standing orders for day-to-day administration.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Defines 'Institute', 'memorandum', and 'rules and regulations' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of the Indian Statistical Institute as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Indian Statistical Institute as an institution of national importance.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of degrees and diplomas by Institute
main_sections.description: Empowers the Institute to hold examinations and grant degrees and diplomas in statistics, mathematics, quantitative economics, computer science, and related subjects, notwithstanding other laws.

main_sections.section_title: Grants, loans, etc., by Central Government to the Institute
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to provide grants, loans, or other financial assistance to the Institute for its functions, including research, education, training, and project activities.

main_sections.section_title: Audit of accounts of the Institute
main_sections.description: Mandates the audit of the Institute's accounts by auditors qualified under the Companies Act, 1956, selected by the Central Government in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor-General. The Central Government can issue directions to auditors, who must have access to the Institute's records and submit reports to both the Institute and the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Prior approval of Central Government necessary for certain action by Institute
main_sections.description: Requires the Central Government's prior approval for actions such as altering the Institute's purposes, amalgamating with other institutions, altering its memorandum or rules, selling property acquired with government funds, or dissolution.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Committees by Central Government for preparing programme of work by the Institute, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to constitute committees to prepare and submit work programs and financial estimates for the Institute, and to settle the broad lines of such work programs. If the Institute disagrees with a suggested work, it must provide reasons.

main_sections.section_title: Review of work done, Inspection of assets, etc.
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to constitute committees to review the Institute's work, inspect its assets, evaluate its performance, and advise the Government. The Institute must be notified of reviews and has the right to appoint a representative. The Central Government can issue directions based on committee reports if the Institute does not take satisfactory action.

main_sections.section_title: Institute to afford facilities to Committees
main_sections.description: Obligates the Institute to provide all necessary facilities to committees constituted under sections 8 and 9.
