main_sections.section_title: Power to issue directions to Institute
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the Institute in the public interest, including directions to amend its memorandum or rules, or to prioritize certain work. These directions override any other laws or the Institute's own rules.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to assume functions of control
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to take over control of the Institute or parts of it if it defaults on directions, or if its Council exceeds or abuses its powers. The Central Government can appoint persons to manage the Institute for a specified period, during which the existing Council members vacate their offices.

important_rules: The Indian Statistical Institute is declared an institution of national importance.
The Institute may grant degrees and diplomas in specific subjects.
The Central Government can provide financial grants and loans to the Institute.
The Institute's accounts are subject to audit by government-selected auditors.
Significant actions by the Institute require prior approval from the Central Government.
The Central Government can form committees to oversee the Institute's work programs and performance.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Institute.
In cases of default or abuse of power, the Central Government can assume control of the Institute.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directives, committees for review and inspection, and the ultimate power to assume control of the Institute's functions.

rights: The Institute has the right to grant degrees and diplomas in specified fields.
The Institute has the right to appoint a representative to be present and heard during reviews or inspections.
duties: The Institute has a duty to afford all necessary facilities to committees constituted by the Central Government.
The Institute must provide reasons to the Central Government if it disagrees with proposed work.
The Institute must comply with directions issued by the Central Government.
If the Central Government assumes control, existing Council members must vacate their offices.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Upon notification by the Central Government.
Audit of Accounts: Appointment of auditors by the Central Government, access to records, and submission of reports.
Seeking Prior Approval: The Institute must obtain Central Government approval before altering its purposes, memorandum, rules, disposing of government-funded property, or dissolving.
Work Program and Estimates: Committees prepare programs and estimates, which the Institute can disagree with by providing reasons.
Reviews and Inspections: Central Government convenes committees; Institute is notified and can appoint a representative.
Issuing Directions: Central Government issues written directions with recorded reasons.
Assuming Control: If the Institute defaults on directions or its Council abuses powers, the Central Government can order it to show cause, and then appoint individuals to take charge.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act overrides provisions of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, and the Societies Registration Act, 1860, where they conflict with this Act.
The powers granted to the Central Government are extensive, allowing for significant oversight and intervention in the Institute's operations.
Amendments to the Institute's purposes, memorandum, or rules require Central Government approval.
The Central Government can specify movable property that does not require prior approval for disposal.
The period for which the Central Government can assume control of the Institute is limited to a maximum of two years.

title: THE ARMS ACT, 1959
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to Arms and Ammunition.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It regulates the acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, import, export, and transport of arms and ammunition.

key_definitions.acquisition: Includes hiring, borrowing, or accepting as a gift.
key_definitions.ammunition: Means ammunition for any firearm, and includes rockets, bombs, grenades, shells, articles designed for torpedo service and submarine mining, articles containing explosive material, charges for firearms, fuses, friction tubes, and parts or machinery for manufacturing ammunition.
key_definitions.arms: Articles of any description designed or adapted as weapons for offence or defence, including firearms, sharp-edged and other deadly weapons, and parts or machinery for manufacturing arms. It excludes articles designed solely for domestic or agricultural uses and weapons incapable of being used otherwise than as toys or of being converted into serviceable weapons.
key_definitions.firearms: Arms designed or adapted to discharge a projectile by the action of an explosive or other forms of energy. It includes artillery, hand-grenades, riot-pistols, weapons for discharging noxious substances, accessories to reduce noise or flash, parts or machinery for manufacturing firearms, and appliances for mounting artillery.
key_definitions.prohibited_arms: Includes firearms that discharge continuously when the trigger is pressed and weapons designed to discharge noxious substances. It also includes artillery, anti-aircraft and anti-tank firearms, and other arms specified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.prohibited_ammunition: Includes ammunition containing noxious substances, rockets, bombs, grenades, shells, articles designed for torpedo service, and other articles specified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.transfer: Includes letting on hire, lending, giving, and parting with possession.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its territorial extent (whole of India), and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'acquisition', 'ammunition', 'arms', 'firearms', 'prohibited arms', 'prohibited ammunition', and 'transfer'. It also includes provisions for interpreting measurements of firearm barrels and references to laws in areas where they might not be in force.

main_sections.section_title: Licence for acquisition and possession of firearms and ammunition
main_sections.description: Prohibits the acquisition, possession, or carrying of any firearm or ammunition without a valid licence. It also specifies a limit of two firearms per person, with provisions for existing holders and exceptions for dealers and rifle club members. It outlines procedures for depositing excess firearms.

main_sections.section_title: Licence for acquisition and possession of arms of specified description in certain cases
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to regulate the acquisition, possession, or carrying of arms other than firearms in specific areas if deemed necessary in the public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Licence for manufacture, sale, etc., of arms and ammunition
main_sections.description: Prohibits the manufacture, sale, transfer, repair, testing, or possession for sale of firearms or certain other arms and ammunition without a licence. It allows lawful possession for private use to be sold or transferred to eligible persons, provided prior notification to the authorities is given.

main_sections.section_title: Licence for the shortening of guns or conversion of imitation firearms into firearms
main_sections.description: Prohibits the shortening of the barrel of a firearm or the conversion of imitation firearms into serviceable firearms without a licence.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of acquisition or possession, or of manufacture or sale of prohibited arms or prohibited ammunition
main_sections.description: Prohibits the acquisition, possession, manufacture, or sale of prohibited arms or prohibited ammunition.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of sale or transfer of firearms not bearing identification marks
main_sections.description: Prohibits the sale or transfer of firearms that do not bear prescribed identification marks.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of acquisition or possession by, or of sale or transfer to, young persons and certain other persons of firearms, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the acquisition, possession, sale, or transfer of firearms or ammunition to young persons and certain other disqualified individuals.

main_sections.section_title: Licence for import and export of arms, etc.
main_sections.description: Requires a licence for the import and export of arms, ammunition, and certain other specified articles.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit import or export of arms, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to prohibit the import or export of specified arms or ammunition.

main_sections.section_title: Power to restrict or prohibit transport of arms
main_sections.description: Gives the Central Government the power to restrict or prohibit the transport of arms.
Deals with the procedure and conditions for the grant of licences.
Outlines the grounds on which a licence may be refused.
Specifies the duration for which licences are valid and the procedure for their renewal.
Covers the fees payable for licences and other related charges.

main_sections.section_title: Variation, suspension and revocation of licences
main_sections.description: Details the powers of licensing authorities to vary, suspend, or revoke licences.
Provides for the right of appeal against orders passed by licensing authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to demand production of licence, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants authorities the power to demand the production of a licence or arms and ammunition.

main_sections.section_title: Arrest of persons conveying arms, etc., under suspicious circumstances
main_sections.description: Allows for the arrest of individuals found conveying arms or ammunition under suspicious circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Deposit of arms, etc., on possession ceasing to be lawful
main_sections.description: Requires the deposit of arms or ammunition when lawful possession ceases.
Confers powers upon a magistrate to search for and seize arms and ammunition.

main_sections.section_title: Search of vessels, vehicles for arms, etc.
main_sections.description: Authorises the search of vessels and vehicles for arms and ammunition.

main_sections.section_title: Seizure and detention under orders of the Central Government
main_sections.description: Allows for the seizure and detention of arms or ammunition under the orders of the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition as to possession of notified arms in disturbed areas, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the possession of notified arms in disturbed areas.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition as to carrying of notified arms in or through public places in disturbed areas etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the carrying of notified arms in or through public places in disturbed areas.
Specifies punishments for various offences under the Act.
Deals with penalties for secret contraventions of the Act.
Prescribes punishment for the unlawful use of arms.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for use and possession of firearms or imitation firearms in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies punishments for the use and possession of firearms or imitation firearms in particular circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for knowingly purchasing arms, etc., from unlicensed person or for delivering arms, etc., to person not entitled to possess the same
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for knowingly purchasing arms from an unlicensed person or delivering them to an unauthorised person.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for contravention of licence or rule
main_sections.description: Provides punishment for violating the terms of a licence or any rule made under the Act.
Specifies enhanced punishments for repeat offenders.
Grants power to confiscate arms, ammunition, or vehicles used in the commission of an offence.
Deals with the criminal responsibility of companies for offences committed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Sanction of Central Government for warehousing of arms
main_sections.description: Requires the sanction of the Central Government for the warehousing of arms.

main_sections.section_title: Criminal responsibility of persons in occupation of premises in certain cases
main_sections.description: Addresses the criminal responsibility of individuals in occupation of premises where offences related to arms are committed.

main_sections.section_title: Information to be given regarding certain offences
main_sections.description: Mandates the reporting of certain offences to the authorities.
Consolidates provisions related to arrest and search powers under the Act.
Declares that offences under this Act are cognizable, meaning police can arrest without a warrant.

main_sections.section_title: Previous sanction of the district magistrate necessary in certain cases
main_sections.description: Requires the previous sanction of the District Magistrate for prosecution in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to exempt certain persons or arms from the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take census of firearms
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to conduct a census of firearms.
Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act.
Authorises the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies circumstances or cases where the Act may not apply.
Repeals the Indian Arms Act, 1878.

important_rules: No person shall acquire, possess, or carry any firearm or ammunition without a licence (Section 3(1)).
Generally, a person cannot possess more than two firearms at any time, with exceptions for dealers and rifle club members (Section 3(2)).

Firearms lawfully possessed for private use can be sold or transferred to eligible persons, provided written notice is given to the district magistrate or nearest police station at least 45 days prior to the transfer (Section 5(2) and proviso).
Prohibited arms and ammunition cannot be acquired, possessed, manufactured, or sold (Section 7).
Firearms sold or transferred must bear identification marks (Section 8).
Persons younger than a certain age or otherwise disqualified cannot acquire, possess, sell, or transfer firearms (Section 9).

penalties: Punishment for various offences including illegal acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, import, export, and transport of arms and ammunition.
Secret contraventions.
Using arms unlawfully.
Use and possession of firearms or imitation firearms in certain cases.
Knowingly purchasing from unlicensed persons or delivering to unauthorised persons.
Contravention of licence terms or rules.
Subsequent offences leading to enhanced penalties.
Confiscation of arms, ammunition, or vehicles.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Law enforcement agencies, including the police, and specified authorities empowered by the Central Government or State Governments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of search, seizure, arrest, demand for production of licences, and prosecution for offences. The Central Government has powers to prohibit import/export and restrict transport, and to order seizure and detention.

rights: Right to appeal against certain orders related to licences (Section 18).
Right to retain a limited number of firearms as per specified conditions, even if exceeding the new limits upon amendment acts (Section 3(2)).
duties: Duty to obtain a licence for acquiring, possessing, or carrying firearms and ammunition (Section 3(1)).
Duty to inform authorities before selling or transferring lawfully possessed firearms (Section 5(2) proviso).
Duty to deposit excess firearms with designated authorities or licensed dealers within specified timelines (Section 3(2) proviso).
Duty to report certain offences to the authorities (Section 36).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the terms and conditions of any issued licence.
Obligation to surrender or deposit arms when lawful possession ceases (Section 21).

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining, renewing, varying, suspending, and revoking licences (Chapters III).
Procedure for search and seizure of arms and ammunition by magistrates and other authorities (Sections 22, 23).
Procedure for arrest of persons conveying arms under suspicious circumstances (Section 20).
Procedure for depositing excess firearms (Section 3(2) proviso).
Procedure for sale or transfer of lawfully possessed firearms, including prior notification to authorities (Section 5(2) proviso).
administration: The Central Government and State Governments, through their respective authorities and officers, administer this Act. The Central Government issues notifications, makes rules, and has overarching powers related to prohibition, delegation, and exemption. Licensing authorities, magistrates, and police officials are key administrative bodies at the ground level.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Pondicherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Sikkim with modifications or effective from specific dates.
The definition of 'ammunition' includes a wide range of items beyond traditional bullets, encompassing missiles and ingredients specified by the Central Government.
The definition of 'arms' is broad and includes firearms, deadly weapons, and parts/machinery, but excludes domestic/agricultural tools and toy weapons.
Recent amendments (2019) have reduced the limit of firearms a person can possess from three to two, with specific transition periods and conditions for inheritance/heirloom licences.
The Act includes provisions for 'prohibited arms' and 'prohibited ammunition', which are subject to stricter regulations.

title: THE ORPHANAGES AND OTHER CHARITABLE HOMES (SUPERVISION AND CONTROL) ACT, 1960
purpose: To provide for the supervision and control of orphanages, homes for neglected women or children and other like institutions and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh). It applies to institutions maintained or intended to be maintained for the reception, care, protection and welfare of women or children, referred to as 'homes'. Certain institutions are exempted.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of Control established under section 5.
key_definitions.certificate: The certificate of recognition granted under section 15.
key_definitions.child: A boy or girl who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.home: An institution, whether called an orphanage, a home for neglected women or children, a widows' home, or by any other name, maintained or intended to be maintained for the reception, care, protection and welfare of women or children.
key_definitions.manager: A member of the managing committee appointed as such by the committee under section 20.
key_definitions.managing committee: The committee of management referred to in section 20.
key_definitions.recognised home: A home in respect of which a certificate has been granted.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.woman: A female who has completed the age of eighteen years.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the commencement date (which is to be appointed by the State Government).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'certificate', 'child', 'home', 'manager', 'managing committee', 'recognised home', 'prescribed', and 'woman'.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain institutions
main_sections.description: Exempts specific institutions from the purview of the Act, such as hostels attached to educational institutions, protective homes under the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956, and reformatories or workhouses governed by other enactments.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of Act on instruments governing recognised homes
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in any instrument governing a recognised home.

main_sections.section_title: Board of Control, its constitution, etc.
main_sections.description: Outlines the establishment and composition of the Board of Control by the State Government. It specifies the members to be elected from the State Legislature and managing committees, nominated members including the officer in charge of social welfare work, and nominated women. It also provides for the election of the Chairman.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and casual vacancies
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for members of the Board (five years), conditions for termination of office, procedures for resignation and filling casual vacancies, and eligibility for re-election or re-nomination. It also states that the Board's proceedings are not invalidated by vacancies or defects in its constitution.

Defines the primary duty of the Board as supervising and controlling all matters related to the management of homes in accordance with the Act. It also states that the Board shall be bound by directions from the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Board to give directions to manager of a recognised home
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to issue general or special directions to the manager of a recognised home for its efficient management, subject to the State Government's directions.

Grants power to any member of the Board or authorized officer to enter any home for inspection, examine documents, and seek information. A proviso specifies that entry into parts of a home where females are present must be in the presence of two respectable women.
Details the sources of the Board's funds, including contributions, donations, bequests, and grants from the State Government or other public bodies.
Allows the Board to appoint officers and employees for efficient functioning, subject to rules made by the State Government.
Permits the Board to delegate its powers and functions to the Chairman, other members, or officers, subject to the State Government's control and specified conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Homes not to be run without certificate
main_sections.description: Mandates that no home can be maintained or conducted without a certificate of recognition granted under the Act.
Prescribes the procedure for applying for a certificate of recognition, including the form and particulars required. It provides a grace period of three months for existing homes to apply.

Details the Board's power to grant or refuse a certificate after inquiry. It mandates providing an opportunity for the applicant to be heard and communicating the grounds for refusal. No fee is charged for the certificate, and it is non-transferable.

Specifies the details to be included in the certificate, such as the home's name and location, manager's name, nature of the home, number of inmates, minimum standards for boarding, lodging, clothing, sanitation, health, hygiene, and education/training. It includes a provision that the person in charge of a home for females shall ordinarily be a woman. It also restricts admitting persons of different sexes without Board consent and prohibits changes to name, location, or purpose without prior written consent.

Outlines the grounds on which the Board may revoke a certificate, including non-compliance with the Act or rules, conditions of the certificate, or if the home is found to be inefficiently managed or detrimental to the welfare of inmates.

important_rules: No person shall maintain or conduct a home without a valid certificate of recognition (Section 13).
Applications for certificates must be made in the prescribed form and contain prescribed particulars (Section 14).
A certificate of recognition cannot be transferred (Section 15(4)).
The person in charge of a home for females shall ordinarily be a woman (Section 16(1) proviso).
Homes for females and males should not ordinarily admit inmates of different sexes unless permitted by the Board for reasons recorded and subject to conditions (Section 16(2)).
No recognised home shall change its name or location or alter its purpose without the prior written consent of the Board (Section 16(3)).
Inmates of a recognised home can be discharged by the manager under certain conditions (Section 22).
Reports regarding the deaths of inmates must be submitted to the Board (Section 23).
Anyone maintaining or conducting a home without a certificate or in contravention of its conditions is liable to penalties (Section 24).

penalties: Fine up to two hundred rupees for maintaining or conducting a home without a certificate or in contravention of its conditions (Section 24).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board of Control, authorized members, and officers of the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection powers (Section 9), power to give directions (Section 8), and by imposing penalties for violations (Section 24). Prosecutions require sanction from the State Government or a prescribed authority (Section 25).

rights: Right to apply for a certificate of recognition to run a home (Section 14).
Right to be heard before a certificate is refused (Section 15(2)).
Right to appeal against decisions of the Board (Section 18).
Right to have acts done in good faith protected (Section 27).
duties: Duty of the Board to supervise and control all matters relating to the management of homes (Section 7(1)).
Duty of the manager to comply with directions from the Board (Section 8).
Duty of the manager to discharge inmates of a home under prescribed conditions (Section 22).
Duty to report deaths of inmates to the Board (Section 23).
Duty to obtain a certificate of recognition to run a home (Section 13).
obligations: Institutions must comply with minimum standards regarding boarding, lodging, clothing, sanitation, health, and hygiene (Section 16(1)(e)).
Institutions must provide a standard of education or training if undertaken for inmates (Section 16(1)(f)).
Persons running recognized homes must not change name, location, or purpose without prior Board consent (Section 16(3)).

key_procedures: Application for Certificate: A person desiring to run a home must apply to the Board in the prescribed form with prescribed particulars. Existing homes have three months from commencement to apply. (Section 14)

Grant or Refusal of Certificate: The Board conducts an inquiry and may grant or refuse the certificate by written order. If refused, grounds must be communicated after hearing the applicant. (Section 15)

Revocation of Certificate: The Board may revoke a certificate if the home is not managed efficiently, fails to comply with standards, or is detrimental to inmates' welfare, after providing notice and an opportunity to be heard. (Section 17)
Appeals: An appeal against the Board's order of refusal or revocation of a certificate can be filed with the prescribed authority. (Section 18)
Inspection: Authorized personnel can inspect homes, examine records, and ask for information. Special provisions apply for inspecting areas with females. (Section 9)
Sanction for Prosecution: Prosecution for offenses under the Act requires sanction from the State Government or a prescribed authority. (Section 25)
administration: The State Government establishes and oversees the Board of Control. The Board is responsible for the overall supervision and control of homes. The State Government also has the power to make rules for the Act.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but this has been amended to include the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
The commencement date of the Act varies by State, appointed by the respective State Government via notification.
The Maharashtra amendment modifies the nomination process for members of the State Legislative Assembly and Council on the Board of Control.
The Maharashtra amendment to Section 6 alters the conditions under which certain members' terms of office end.
Any member or officer entering a home where females are present must do so in the presence of two respectable women of the locality.
The State Government has the power to exempt certain homes from the provisions of the Act.
The State Government can make rules, and the Board can make regulations, for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

title: THE DELHI LAND HOLDINGS (CEILING) ACT, 1960
purpose: To provide for the imposition of a ceiling on land holdings in the Union territory of Delhi and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi, with specific exemptions for certain areas like municipalities, notified areas, cantonments, areas owned by government or local authorities, corporations owned by the central government, areas acquired for public purposes, areas used for goshala or horse breeding/feeding, and areas owned by agricultural cooperative land mortgage banks, state/central cooperative banks, or other banks. The act's provisions came into force on a date appointed by the Chief Commissioner via notification.

key_definitions.appointed day: 24th day of January, 1971
key_definitions.competent authority: Any person or authority authorized by the Chief Commissioner to perform functions under this Act for a specified area.
key_definitions.family: The person, their spouse, and their minor sons and unmarried minor daughters.
key_definitions.minor: A person not having attained majority under the Indian Majority Act, 1875.
key_definitions.orchard: A compact area of land with fruit-bearing trees that prevent or would prevent substantial use for agricultural purposes, excluding banana/guava gardens or vineyards.
key_definitions.person: Includes a company, family, association, or other body of individuals, incorporated or not, and any institution capable of holding property.
key_definitions.person under disability: Includes a widow, a minor, an unmarried woman or a divorced/separated woman or whose husband is in armed forces or incapable of cultivation, a member of the armed forces, or a person incapable of cultivating land due to physical/mental disability.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Asami: Defined in the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.
key_definitions.Bhumidhar: Defined in the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.
key_definitions.Deputy Commissioner: Defined in the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.
key_definitions.Gaon Panchayat: Defined in the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.
key_definitions.improvement: Defined in the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.
key_definitions.land: Defined in the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.
key_definitions.village: Defined in the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its extent to the Union territory of Delhi (with exemptions), and outlines the commencement provision (by notification).

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'ceiling limit', 'Chief Commissioner', 'competent authority', 'family', 'minor', 'orchard', 'person', 'person under disability', 'prescribed', and refers to definitions from the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954 for certain terms.

Sets the ceiling limits for land holdings based on irrigation sources and crop yield, with provisions for converting land between categories and for families exceeding five members. It also addresses land held by major sons and clarifies the calculation for married individuals.

Requires every person holding land in excess of the ceiling limit to submit a return to the competent authority, indicating the land they wish to retain. Provisions are made for joint holdings and for persons under disability.

main_sections.section_title: Collection of information through other agency
main_sections.description: Empowers the competent authority to collect necessary information from other agencies if a person fails to submit a return as required.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for determination of excess land
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the competent authority to determine the total land held, land to be retained, excess land, and whether the excess land is held as Bhumidhar or Asami. It also specifies which excess land vests in the government. It includes provisions for dealing with transfers made after the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Selection of excess land in cases of certain transfers
main_sections.description: Deals with the selection of excess land when transfers (other than bona fide sales for valuable consideration) occur after the appointed day. The excess land is selected from the remaining land, and if insufficient, the balance or entire excess land is considered.
Concerns the abatement of certain suits.

main_sections.section_title: Excess land to vest in Government
main_sections.description: States that excess land determined under the Act shall vest in the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of the final list and consequences thereof
main_sections.description: Deals with the publication of the final list of excess land and its consequences.
Addresses the compensation to be paid for excess land.
Specifies the manner in which any amount due under the Act is to be paid.

main_sections.section_title: Limit of future acquisition of land
main_sections.description: Imposes a limit on future acquisition of land.

main_sections.section_title: Excess land not to be surrendered in certain cases
main_sections.description: Provides for circumstances where excess land is not to be surrendered.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Deputy Commissioner to take possession of excess land
main_sections.description: Grants the Deputy Commissioner the power to take possession of excess land.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of land for certain purposes
main_sections.description: Allows for the reservation of land for specific purposes.
Details the process for the allotment of excess land.

main_sections.section_title: Act to override contract and other laws
main_sections.description: States that this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any contract or other law.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of any amount due under the Act
main_sections.description: Prescribes the method for recovering any amount due under the Act.
Provides for an appeal against orders made under the Act.
Grants power of revision against orders.

main_sections.section_title: Power of officers while holding inquiries, etc., under the Act
main_sections.description: Defines the powers of officers conducting inquiries or other proceedings under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Entry upon land for purposes of survey, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants authority for entry upon land for survey and other related purposes.
Specifies the offences under the Act and the penalties associated with them.

main_sections.section_title: Finality of orders and bar of jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Deals with the finality of orders passed under the Act and bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in certain matters.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under the Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
This section has been omitted.
Grants the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
This section has been repealed.

important_rules: No person, individually or with their family, shall hold land exceeding specified hectares based on irrigation and crop yield categories (Section 3(1)).
Land held by a person is converted to category (c) for calculation purposes when it falls under multiple categories, with specific conversion rates (Section 3(2)).
If a family exceeds five members, the ceiling limit can be extended by one-fifth for each member over five, up to twice the aggregate ceiling limit (Section 3(5)).
Land held by a person and their family members is aggregated for ceiling limit determination (Section 3(6)).
A person representing a family can hold additional land for each major son, considering the son's own land holdings (Section 3(7)).
Every person holding land in excess of the ceiling limit must submit a return to the competent authority, indicating the land they wish to retain (Section 4).
Transfers of land (except bona fide sales for valuable consideration) made after the appointed day are deemed to be held by the transferor for the purpose of determining excess land (Section 6(2)).
Excess land determined under the Act shall vest in the Government (Section 8).

penalties: Offences and penalties are detailed in Section 23.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority and Deputy Commissioner, as authorized by the Chief Commissioner.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, determination of excess land, taking possession of excess land, and potentially through other means specified in the Act and rules.

rights: Right to hold land up to the prescribed ceiling limit.
Right to select parcels of land to retain (within the ceiling limit).
Right to compensation for excess land vested in the Government (Section 10).
Right to appeal against orders (Section 19).
Right to revision against orders (Section 20).
duties: Duty to submit returns if holding land in excess of the ceiling limit (Section 4).
Duty to cooperate with information collection by the competent authority (Section 5).
Duty to surrender excess land that vests in the Government.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the ceiling limits on land holdings.
Obligation to provide accurate information in returns.
Obligation to allow entry for survey and inspection.
Obligation to comply with orders passed under the Act.

key_procedures: Submission of returns by persons holding excess land (Section 4).
Collection of information by competent authority if returns are not filed (Section 5).
Inquiry and determination of excess land by the competent authority (Section 6).
Selection of excess land, especially in cases of transfers (Section 7).
Vesting of excess land in the Government (Section 8).
Publication of the final list of excess land (Section 9).
Taking possession of excess land by the Deputy Commissioner (Section 14).
Allotment of excess land (Section 16).
Filing of appeals against orders (Section 19).
administration: The Chief Commissioner of Delhi, and the 'competent authority' appointed by them.
important_notes: Certain areas are exempted from the purview of the Act, including areas within municipalities, notified areas, cantonments, areas owned by government or local authorities, and specific types of land like those acquired for public purposes or used for goshala/horse breeding (Section 1(2)).
The Act overrides contracts and other laws in case of conflict (Section 17).
Orders passed under the Act are generally final, and civil court jurisdiction is barred in certain matters (Section 24).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 25).

title: The International Development Association (Status, Immunities and Privileges) Act, 1960
purpose: To implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the International Development Association in so far as it relates to the status, immunities and privileges of that Association, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the International Development Association (IDA), its officers, and employees, granting them certain immunities and privileges within India as outlined in the agreement.

key_definitions.Agreement: The Agreement for the establishment and operation of the international body known as the International Development Association.
key_definitions.Association: The International Development Association established under the Agreement.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines 'Agreement' and 'Association' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of status and certain immunities and privileges on the Association and conferment of certain immunities and privileges on its officers and employees
main_sections.description: Gives the force of law in India to Article VIII of the Agreement (regarding status, immunities, and privileges). It includes provisos that restrict certain immunities related to customs duties and taxes on goods sold or services rendered. It also allows the Central Government to amend the Schedule (containing Article VIII) via notification to conform with amendments to the Agreement.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Notifications under section 3 and rules under section 4 to be placed before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that every notification issued under section 3(2) and every rule made under section 4 must be laid before each House of Parliament. Parliament has the power to modify or annul these notifications or rules.

important_rules: Article VIII, Section 2 of the Agreement, incorporated into Indian law by Section 3(1) of the Act, grants the Association full juridical personality, including the capacity to contract, acquire/dispose of property, and institute legal proceedings.

Article VIII, Section 3 states that actions against the Association can only be brought in competent courts where it has an office, an agent for service, or has issued securities. The Association's property and assets are immune from seizure before final judgment.

Article VIII, Section 4 grants immunity of the Association's property and assets from search, requisition, confiscation, expropriation, or any other form of seizure by executive or legislative action.
Article VIII, Section 5 declares the archives of the Association to be inviolable.
Article VIII, Section 6 states that the Association's property and assets are free from restrictions, regulations, controls, and moratoria of any nature to the extent necessary for its operations.
Article VIII, Section 7 accords the same treatment to the official communications of the Association as members accord to the official communications of other members.

Article VIII, Section 8 grants immunities to Governors, Executive Directors, Alternates, Officers, and employees of the Association from legal process for acts in their official capacity (unless waived by the Association). Non-local nationals are accorded certain immigration and exchange facilities, and all are granted similar travel facilities as comparable officials of other members.
Article VIII, Section 9(a) grants the Association immunity from all taxation and customs duties, and from liability for collection or payment of taxes/duties.
Article VIII, Section 9(b) exempts salaries and emoluments paid by the Association to non-local citizen officials/employees from taxation.

Article VIII, Sections 9(c) and 9(d) prevent discriminatory taxation on obligations or securities issued or guaranteed by the Association solely based on their origin or the Association's involvement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (through notifications and rules). The Act itself enables the enforcement of the immunities and privileges by giving the Agreement's provisions the force of law in India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder. Courts would uphold the immunities and privileges of the Association and its personnel as specified in the Act.

rights: The Association has the right to possess full juridical personality.
The Association has the right to contract, acquire and dispose of property, and institute legal proceedings.
The Association's property and assets are immune from seizure, search, requisition, confiscation, expropriation, and execution before final judgment.
The Association's archives are inviolable.
The Association's assets are free from governmental restrictions and controls necessary for its operations.
Official communications of the Association are to be treated like those of other member countries.
Officers and employees of the Association have immunity from legal process for official acts.
Certain immigration, alien registration, national service, and exchange facilities are accorded to non-local national officers and employees.
Similar travel facilities are accorded to representatives, officials, and employees.
The Association and its transactions are immune from all taxation and customs duties.
Salaries and emoluments of non-local employees are exempt from tax.
Obligations and securities issued or guaranteed by the Association are protected from discriminatory taxation.
duties: The Association must operate within the framework of the Agreement.
The Central Government has a duty to lay notifications and rules before Parliament.
The Association has a duty to adhere to any restrictions on import of goods free of customs duty, as specified in the proviso to Section 3(1).
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to bring the Act into force via notification.
The Central Government has an obligation to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.
Parliament has an obligation to consider notifications and rules laid before it.

key_procedures: Enactment of the Act by Parliament.
Central Government appointing a commencement date via notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(3)).
Central Government making rules for the Act's purpose via notification (Section 4).
Central Government amending the Schedule (containing Article VIII) via notification to align with Agreement amendments (Section 3(2)).
Laying of notifications and rules before Parliament for review and potential modification or annulment (Section 5).
administration: Central Government (through its relevant ministries/departments responsible for international agreements and finance).
important_notes: Section 3(1) Proviso: The immunities granted to the Association do not permit duty-free import of goods without restriction on subsequent sale, nor do they confer exemption from taxes that are charges for services rendered.

The Act specifically incorporates Article VIII of the Agreement. Any modifications to this Article in the Agreement, if duly made and adopted, can be reflected in the Act by the Central Government amending the Schedule via notification (Section 3(2)).
Section 5 outlines a parliamentary oversight mechanism where notifications and rules can be modified or annulled by Parliament, ensuring legislative control over the implementation of the Act.

title: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
purpose: To prevent the infliction of unnecessary pain or suffering on animals and for that purpose to amend the law relating to the prevention of cruelty to animals.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It covers the prevention of cruelty to animals, including general cruelty, experimentation on animals, and performing animals.

key_definitions.animal: Any living creature other than a human being.
key_definitions.board: The Animal Welfare Board of India, established under section 4 and reconstituted from time to time under section 5A.
key_definitions.captive_animal: Any animal (not being a domestic animal) which is in captivity or confinement, whether permanent or temporary, or which is subjected to any appliance or contrivance for the purpose of hindering or preventing its escape from captivity or confinement or which is pinioned or which is or appears to be maimed.
key_definitions.domestic_animal: Any animal which is tamed or which has been or is being sufficiently tamed to serve some purpose for the use of man or which, although it neither has been nor is being nor is intended to be so tamed, is or has become in fact wholly or partly tamed.
key_definitions.local_authority: A municipal committee, district board or other authority for the time being invested by law with the control and administration of any matters within a specified local area.
key_definitions.owner: Used with reference to an animal, includes not only the owner but also any other person for the time being in possession or custody of the animal, whether with or without the consent of the owner.
key_definitions.phooka_or_doom_dev: Includes any process of introducing air or any substance into the female organ of a milch animal with the object of drawing off from the animal any secretion of milk.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.street: Includes any way, road, lane, square, court, alley, passage or open space, whether a thoroughfare or not, to which the public have access.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement through a notification by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'animal', 'Board', 'captive animal', 'domestic animal', 'local authority', 'owner', 'phooka or doom dev', 'prescribed', and 'street'.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of persons having charge of animals
main_sections.description: Mandates that every person having the care or charge of any animal must take all reasonable measures to ensure the animal's well-being and prevent unnecessary pain or suffering.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Animal Welfare Board of India
main_sections.description: Establishes the Animal Welfare Board of India for the promotion of animal welfare and protection of animals from unnecessary pain or suffering. The Board is a body corporate.
Defines what constitutes cruelty to animals, including beating, kicking, torturing, overloading, starving, abandoning, and causing unnecessary pain or suffering.
Regulates experiments on animals, requiring permission and adherence to prescribed conditions to minimize pain and suffering.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on exhibition and training of performing animals
main_sections.description: Prohibits the exhibition and training of performing animals unless registered and conducted in accordance with prescribed conditions.

important_rules: Every person in charge of an animal must ensure its well-being and prevent unnecessary pain or suffering (Section 3).
Experiments on animals are permitted only under strict conditions to minimize pain and suffering, and require proper authorization (Chapter IV).
Performing animals must be registered and trained/exhibited according to prescribed regulations (Chapter V).
No animal shall be subjected to unnecessary pain or suffering, including by abandonment, overworking, or insufficient sustenance (Section 11).

penalties: Penalties for various offences related to cruelty to animals are outlined in different chapters, including fines and imprisonment. For example, contravention of Section 11 can lead to fines and imprisonment (Section 11(1)).
Specific penalties exist for practicing 'phooka' or 'doom dev' (Section 12) and for the destruction of suffering animals (Section 13).
Penalties are also prescribed for offences related to experimentation on animals (Section 20) and performing animals (Section 26).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities, including the Animal Welfare Board of India, police officers, and other persons authorized by the Central Government or State Governments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of search, seizure, inspection, prohibition of experiments, and prosecution of offenders in courts. The Act also outlines procedures for the treatment and care of animals. State amendments may introduce specific enforcement mechanisms and penalties, such as those in Maharashtra for bullock cart races.

rights: The right of animals to be free from unnecessary pain or suffering.
The right of the public to report instances of cruelty to animals.
duties: The duty of every person having charge of an animal to ensure its well-being (Section 3).
The duty of the Animal Welfare Board to promote animal welfare.
Duties of the Committee for control and supervision of experiments on animals.
obligations: Obligations to obtain necessary permissions for animal experiments.
Obligations to register and adhere to regulations for performing animals.
Obligations for owners or custodians to provide proper care and prevent cruelty.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishing and reconstituting the Animal Welfare Board of India.
Procedure for obtaining permissions and adhering to regulations for animal experimentation.
Procedure for registration of performing animals and their exhibition/training.
Procedure for search and seizure of animals or related items by authorized persons.
Procedure for the destruction of suffering animals.
State amendments may outline specific procedures for events like bullock cart races or Kambala, including obtaining prior permission and adhering to conditions.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for establishing the Animal Welfare Board and making rules. Various State Governments and local authorities also play a role in the administration and enforcement of the Act within their jurisdictions. The Animal Welfare Board of India (established under Section 4) is a key administrative body.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2019 to remove the exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
State governments have the power to appoint different commencement dates for different provisions and states.

State amendments (e.g., Karnataka and Maharashtra) have introduced specific provisions and definitions for traditional sports involving animals, such as 'Bulls race or Bullock cart race' and 'Kambala', along with associated conditions and penalties.
Section 28 provides a saving as respects the manner of killing prescribed by religion, indicating a potential exemption under certain religious practices.

title: The Acquired Territories (Merger) Act, 1960
purpose: To provide for the merger into the States of Assam, Punjab and West Bengal of certain territories acquired in pursuance of agreements entered into between the Governments of India and Pakistan and for matters connected therewith.

scope.geographical: Acquired territories in relation to India and Pakistan border areas, specifically mentioned in relation to Assam, Punjab, and West Bengal.
scope.subject_matter: Merger of territories, amendment of constitutional schedules, construction of references to constituencies, provisions for sitting members of legislatures, transfer of property and assets, appropriation of moneys, extension of laws, naming of authorities, and removal of difficulties.

key_definitions.acquired_territories: Territories comprised in the Indo-Pakistan agreements and referred to in the First Schedule, demarcated for acquisition by India.
key_definitions.appointed_day: The date notified by the Central Government for the merger of acquired territories, which can differ for different states.
key_definitions.Indo-Pakistan_agreements: Agreements dated September 10, 1958, October 23, 1959, and January 11, 1960, between the Governments of India and Pakistan.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification, or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or in any part of the acquired territory.
key_definitions.sitting_member: A person who, immediately before the appointed day, is a member of the House of the People or the Legislature of a State.
key_definitions.State_concerned: Refers to Assam, Punjab, or West Bengal depending on the part of the First Schedule where the acquired territories are mentioned.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Acquired Territories (Merger) Act, 1960.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'acquired territories', 'appointed day', 'Indo-Pakistan agreements', 'law', 'sitting member', 'State concerned', and 'Union purposes'.

States that as from the appointed day, acquired territories mentioned in the First Schedule shall be included in and form part of Assam, Punjab, and West Bengal respectively. It also empowers the State Government to provide for the administration of these territories.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Details the amendments to be made to the First Schedule of the Constitution to include the acquired territories within the respective states of Assam, Punjab, and West Bengal.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to existing constituencies
main_sections.description: Specifies how references to states, districts, and other administrative units in various Delimitation Orders shall be construed to include the acquired territories.

Ensures that sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures whose constituencies have been altered by the Act are deemed to have been elected to their respective houses from the altered constituencies.

Deals with the vesting of property and assets within the acquired territories. Property related to Union purposes vests in the Union, and other property vests in the State concerned. A certificate from the Central Government is conclusive proof of Union purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in acquired territories
main_sections.description: Allows appropriation Acts passed before the appointed day to have effect in the acquired territories. The Governor can also authorize necessary expenditure for a limited period pending legislative sanction.

States that laws in force in acquired territories before the appointed day shall cease to be in force, and laws in force in the State concerned shall extend to those territories. Actions taken under previous laws are deemed to be taken under the corresponding new laws.

main_sections.section_title: Power to name authorities for exercising statutory functions
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to specify authorities or persons who will exercise statutory functions in the acquired territories after the appointed day.

Grants the Central Government and the State Government powers to make orders to remove difficulties arising from the transition to new laws or in the administration of the acquired territories, with a time limit of three years from the appointed day.

important_rules: Rule 1: As from the appointed day, the acquired territories referred to in the First Schedule shall be included in and form part of Assam, Punjab, and West Bengal as specified.
Rule 2: The State Government concerned shall provide for the administration of acquired territories by including them in appropriate administrative units.
Rule 3: Laws in force in the acquired territories before the appointed day shall cease to be in force, and laws of the State concerned shall extend to those territories.
Rule 4: Property and assets in acquired territories shall vest in the Union for Union purposes or in the State concerned otherwise.
Rule 5: References to states and administrative units in Delimitation Orders shall be construed to include the acquired territories.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (for administration of territories and removal of difficulties), Central Government (for removal of difficulties and determining Union purposes).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing notifications and orders to specify administrative units, authorities, and to remove difficulties. Enforcement of extended laws would be through the normal legal framework of the respective states.

rights: Nationals of both governments have the facility of navigation on the Piyain and Surma rivers.
Sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures are deemed elected to their altered constituencies.
duties: State Governments have a duty to provide for the administration of acquired territories.
Governors have a duty to authorize necessary expenditure pending legislative sanction.
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to appoint the 'appointed day' for merger.
The Central Government has the power to issue orders to remove difficulties, which implies an obligation to ensure smooth transition.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Central Government may, by notification, appoint a date (the 'appointed day') for the merger of acquired territories. Different dates can be appointed for different states.

Procedure 2: The State Government concerned shall, by order in the Official Gazette, provide for the administration of acquired territories by including them in specific districts, sub-divisions, etc.
Procedure 3: The Central Government or State Government may issue orders to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act within three years of the appointed day.
administration: The administration of acquired territories is primarily handled by the respective State Governments (Assam, Punjab, West Bengal) concerned, with oversight and powers to remove difficulties vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act requires the demarcation of territories as per Indo-Pakistan agreements before the appointed day can be set.
The power to remove difficulties under Section 11 is limited to three years from the appointed day.
Orders made to remove difficulties can be retrospective but not earlier than the appointed day.

title: THE ADVOCATES ACT, 1961
purpose: To amend and consolidate the law relating to legal practitioners and to provide for the constitution of Bar Councils and an All-India Bar.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to legal practitioners and advocates, and establishes Bar Councils at the State and national levels.

key_definitions.advocate: An advocate entered in any roll under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.bar_council: A Bar Council constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.bar_council_of_india: The Bar Council constituted under section 4 for the territories to which this Act extends.
key_definitions.high_court: Generally refers to the High Court for a State, but excludes a court of the Judicial Commissioner in most contexts. Specific inclusions and exclusions are detailed in the act.
key_definitions.law_graduate: A person who has obtained a bachelor's degree in law from any University established by law in India.
key_definitions.legal_practitioner: An advocate or vakil of any High Court, a pleader, mukhtar or revenue agent.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.roll: A roll of advocates prepared and maintained under this Act.
key_definitions.state: Does not include a Union territory.
key_definitions.state_bar_council: A Bar Council constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.state_roll: A roll of advocates prepared and maintained by a State Bar Council under section 17.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and provisions for its commencement, allowing for different dates for different provisions.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'advocate', 'Bar Council', 'High Court', 'legal practitioner', 'roll', and 'State Bar Council'.

Establishes the constitution of State Bar Councils for various states and union territories, and outlines the composition of these councils, including ex officio members (Advocate-General) and elected members.
Provides for the establishment of the Bar Council of India.

main_sections.section_title: Advocates to be the only recognised class of persons entitled to practise law
main_sections.description: Declares that advocates are the only recognized class of persons entitled to practice law.
Grants advocates the right to practice, subject to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the disciplinary proceedings and punishments for advocates found guilty of misconduct.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for persons illegally practising in courts and before other authorities
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who illegally practice law in courts or before other authorities.

main_sections.section_title: General power of the Bar Council of India to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Bar Council of India to make rules for various aspects of the Act.
Repeals specific prior enactments related to legal practitioners.

important_rules: Advocates are the sole recognized class entitled to practice law.
Advocates have the right to practice, subject to the Act's provisions.
State Bar Councils maintain rolls of advocates.
The Bar Council of India has disciplinary powers over advocates.
Penalties are prescribed for illegal practice of law.
The Bar Council of India has the general power to make rules to carry out the Act's provisions.

penalties: Penalty for persons illegally practising in courts and before other authorities (Section 45).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Bar Councils (State and National) and Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary proceedings, imposition of penalties for illegal practice, and the power of courts to permit appearances in particular cases.

rights: Right of advocates to practice law.
Right of pre-audience for advocates.
Right to be enrolled as an advocate for eligible persons.
duties: Duty to maintain professional standards and conduct.
Duty to uphold the law and the administration of justice.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the rules and regulations set by the Bar Councils.
Obligation to maintain the roll of advocates.

key_procedures: Admission and enrolment of advocates as per Chapter III.
Disposal of applications for admission as an advocate.
Disciplinary proceedings against advocates for misconduct.
Appeals to the Bar Council of India and the Supreme Court against disciplinary committee orders.
Maintenance of State rolls of advocates.
Transfer of names between State rolls.
administration: The Act is administered through State Bar Councils and the Bar Council of India. The Central Government also has rule-making powers.
important_notes: Specific provisions for the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Goa, Daman and Diu regarding commencement dates.
Transitional and temporary provisions are addressed in Chapter VII to handle the transition from existing legal practitioner systems to the new framework.
Certain existing legal practitioners' rights are not affected (Section 55).
The Act repeals certain enactments, consolidating the law.
The Central Government has the power to make rules for various aspects of the Act.

title: The Delhi (Urban Areas) Tenants’ Relief Act, 1961
purpose: To provide relief to the tenants of land in the urban areas of the Union territory of Delhi.
scope: Extends to areas in the Union territory of Delhi that were included in a municipality, notified area, or cantonment before November 1, 1956. Excludes areas owned by the Central Government, Delhi Development Authority, or any local authority.

key_definitions.family: Includes members of a joint Hindu family, or for any other person, includes the person, their spouse, and dependent children and grandchildren.
key_definitions.land_holder: A person under whom a tenant holds land and to whom rent is payable.
key_definitions.person_under_disability: Includes widows, minors whose father has died, unmarried or divorced/separated women whose husbands are also under disability, members of the Armed Forces, individuals incapable of cultivation due to physical/mental disability, students not exceeding 25 years of age, and persons under detention or imprisonment.
key_definitions.tenant_and_tenancy: Includes a sub-tenant and sub-tenancy respectively.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, defines its territorial and subject matter extent, and outlines the commencement provisions through notification by the Chief Commissioner.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Chief Commissioner', 'family', 'land-holder', 'person under disability', 'tenant', and 'tenancy'. It also clarifies that undefined terms used in this Act will take their meanings from the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, or the Agra Tenancy Act, 1901, as applicable.

Specifies the grounds on which a tenant can be ejected. These include unsatisfied decrees for rent arrears, failure to cultivate land when rent is payable in kind, subletting or unauthorized transfer, and using land in a way that renders it unfit for its purpose. It also allows for ejectment by religious/charitable institutions for their objects and by landholders who were persons under disability for their bona fide use or building purposes, with specific conditions and explanations for the cessation of disability.

Stipulates that no tenant shall be ejected except as provided in Section 3. It also states that any pending ejectment proceedings initiated before the Act's commencement, which could not have been instituted had the Act been in force, shall abate.

main_sections.section_title: Restoration of land to tenant in certain cases
main_sections.description: Provides for the restoration of land to tenants in specific circumstances. This includes cases where a person under disability or an institution takes possession but fails to use the land for the stated purpose within a year. It also allows for the restoration of tenants ejected before the Act's commencement if the ejectment would not have been permissible under the Act, with a provision that a tenant cannot be restored if the land is cultivated by the owner under disability or has ceased to be used for agricultural purposes before March 28, 1961.
Prescribes that the rent payable by a tenant shall not exceed one-fifth of the produce of the land or its money equivalent, or the agreed rent if it is lower.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any other law, custom, usage, agreement, decree, or court order, unless expressly provided otherwise.
Grants the Chief Commissioner the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, which must be laid before Parliament for approval or modification.

Repeals inconsistent provisions of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, the Agra Tenancy Act, 1901, and the Punjab Tenants (Security of Tenure) Act, 1950, as applicable to the Act's extent. It also includes a saving clause for actions taken under the repealed provisions that are not inconsistent with this Act.

important_rules: No tenant can be ejected except on specified grounds (arrears of rent, non-cultivation, subletting, misuse of land).
Ejectment is permissible for religious/charitable institutions for their bona fide non-agricultural use.
Ejectment is permissible for landholders who were persons under disability, for their bona fide cultivation or building needs, under certain conditions.
The rent payable by a tenant shall not exceed one-fifth of the produce or its equivalent, or a lower agreed rent.
The Act overrides other laws, customs, agreements, and court orders.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Chief Commissioner and officers specified by the Chief Commissioner.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders for ejectment, restoration of possession, and abatement of proceedings. Rules may be made by the Chief Commissioner for enforcement.

rights: Right to be protected from ejectment except on specific grounds.
Right to restoration of land if certain conditions are not met by the landholder after ejectment.
Right to pay rent not exceeding one-fifth of the produce or a lower agreed rent.
duties: Duty to pay rent as per the Act's provisions.
Duty to cultivate land appropriately when rent is payable in kind.
Duty not to sublet or transfer tenancy in contravention of law or contract.
Duty not to use land in a manner that renders it unfit for its purpose.

key_procedures: Ejectment proceedings must adhere to the grounds specified in Section 3.
Restoration of land to tenants can be initiated by the Chief Commissioner's specified officer, either suo motu or upon application.
Abatement of pending ejectment proceedings that could not have been instituted under this Act.
Making of rules by the Chief Commissioner for the Act's purpose, subject to parliamentary approval.
administration: Chief Commissioner of Delhi
important_notes: The Act specifically excludes areas owned by the Central Government, Delhi Development Authority, and local authorities from its scope.
The cessation of 'disability' for a person is clearly defined with specific dates for different categories.
The Act's provisions have overriding effect over other agreements, laws, and customs.
The Act aims to provide relief, suggesting a protective stance towards tenants in urban areas of Delhi.
The repeal of certain Acts signifies that this Act is intended to be the primary legislation for tenant relief in the specified urban areas of Delhi.

title: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli Act, 1961
purpose: To make provision for the representation of the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in Parliament and for the administration of that Union territory and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli. It covers representation in Parliament, administration, and continuity of existing laws, taxes, and authorities.

key_definitions.administrator: The Administrator of the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.appointed_day: The eleventh day of August, 1961.
key_definitions.dadra_and_nagar_haveli: The Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
key_definitions.varishta_panchayat: The Varishta Panchayat as in existence immediately before the appointed day.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title as 'The Dadra and Nagar Haveli Act, 1961', specifies its extent to the whole Union territory, and deems it to have come into force on August 11, 1961.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'appointed day', 'Dadra and Nagar Haveli', and 'Varishta Panchayat'.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Allots one seat to Dadra and Nagar Haveli in the House of the People and makes consequential amendments to the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and 1951 to include Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

Defines the advisory role of the Varishta Panchayat until other provision is made by law, focusing on matters of administration, general policy, and development schemes. It also outlines oath requirements for its members.
Ensures that judges, magistrates, and other officers and authorities exercising lawful functions before the appointed day continue to do so in Dadra and Nagar Haveli until other provision is made.
Declares that all property and assets vested in the Varishta Panchayat or the Administrator of Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli before the appointed day shall vest in the Union.

States that all rights, liabilities, and obligations of the Varishta Panchayat or the Administrator of Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli in relation to Dadra and Nagar Haveli shall, as from the appointed day, be those of the Central Government.
Provides for the continuation of all laws in force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli immediately before the appointed day, unless repealed or amended by Parliament or other competent authority.
Ensures that all taxes, duties, cesses, or fees lawfully levied before the appointed day continue to be levied and applied to the same purposes until other provisions are made.

main_sections.section_title: Power to extend enactments to Dadra and Nagar Haveli
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to extend any enactment in force in a State to Dadra and Nagar Haveli, with restrictions or modifications as deemed fit.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the jurisdiction of Bombay High Court to Dadra and Nagar Haveli
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to extend the jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of courts and other authorities for purposes of facilitating the application of laws
main_sections.description: Allows courts and authorities to construe laws with necessary alterations to adapt them for the administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act or in administering Dadra and Nagar Haveli, including retrospective orders from the appointed day.
Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including specific provisions for Varishta Panchayat vacancies, meetings, and conduct of business.

important_rules: The Varishta Panchayat has an advisory role on matters of administration, general policy, and development schemes until other provision is made by law.
Members of the Varishta Panchayat must take an oath or affirmation of allegiance to the Constitution and to faithfully discharge their duties.
Existing laws and taxes in force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli before the appointed day shall continue unless repealed or amended.
The Central Government can extend enactments from other states to Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
The jurisdiction of the Bombay High Court can be extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by the Central Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Administrator, Courts, and other authorities as established by law.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the continuation of existing legal frameworks, powers of the Central Government to extend laws, make rules, and remove difficulties, and the functioning of judicial and administrative bodies.

rights: Right of Dadra and Nagar Haveli to have one seat in the House of the People.
Right of the Varishta Panchayat to discuss and make recommendations to the Administrator on specified matters.
Continuation of existing rights in relation to the Union territory.
duties: Duty of the Administrator to give due regard to the advice of the Varishta Panchayat.
Duty of members of the Varishta Panchayat to take an oath or affirmation.
Duty of courts and authorities to facilitate the application of laws.
Duty of the Central Government to make provisions for the administration and representation.
