obligations: Continuance of existing obligations of the Varishta Panchayat or the Administrator of Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli, which become obligations of the Central Government.

key_procedures: Representation in the House of the People is established by amending the Representation of the People Acts.
The Varishta Panchayat operates with advisory functions, with the Administrator giving due consideration to its recommendations.
The Central Government can extend laws and establish the jurisdiction of the Bombay High Court through notifications.
The Central Government can make orders to remove difficulties, potentially with retrospective effect.
The Central Government can make rules for the implementation of the Act, subject to parliamentary review.
administration: Central Government (specifically through the Administrator appointed by the President and powers to make rules and notifications).
important_notes: The Act is effective from August 11, 1961, retrospectively.
The Varishta Panchayat's functions are advisory only, but its advice must be given due regard.
The Central Government has broad powers to extend laws, make rules, and remove difficulties to ensure the effective administration of the Union territory.

title: THE VOLUNTARY SURRENDER OF SALARIES (EXEMPTION FROM TAXATION) ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for exempting from taxes on income a portion of the salary or allowances payable to any person who has, in the public interest, volunteered to forego it.
scope: Applies to salaries and allowances paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India or of a State, or surrendered in favor of the Central Government, for any period after March 31, 1961. It exempts income tax and super-tax on such surrendered portions.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Voluntary Surrender of Salaries (Exemption from Taxation) Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption from taxes on income in respect of salaries surrendered in favour of Government.
main_sections.description: Provides exemption from income-tax and super-tax on salaries surrendered voluntarily in the public interest, either paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India or a State, or surrendered and paid to the Central Government in accordance with rules. Such surrendered salary will not be included in total income for tax purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of section 2 to apply to allowances.
main_sections.description: Extends the provisions of section 2, regarding exemption from taxes on surrendered salary, to also apply to allowances due to such persons for any period after March 31, 1961.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules by notification in the Official Gazette to carry out the purposes of the Act. It also outlines the procedure for laying these rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.
Repeals the Voluntary Surrender of Salaries (Exemption from Taxation) Act, 1950. Declarations made under the repealed Act are deemed to be declarations made for the purposes of this Act.

important_rules: Rule to be made by the Central Government: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act. (Section 4(1))

Parliamentary Scrutiny of Rules: Every rule made under section 4(1) must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days, and modifications or annulments can be made by Parliament. (Section 4(2))
Declaration in writing for surrender: A person must make a declaration in writing to voluntarily forego a portion of their salary in the public interest. (Section 2(a))

Surrender in favor of Central Government: In cases not covered by section 2(a), the surrendered salary must be paid to the Central Government in accordance with the rules made in this behalf. (Section 2(b))
Effective Date: The exemption applies to salary and allowances due for any period after March 31, 1961. (Section 2(a), 2(b), 3)

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (through rule-making power and by receiving surrendered salaries)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Central Government and by ensuring compliance with the provisions of the Act regarding voluntary surrender of salaries and allowances for tax exemption.

rights: Right to claim exemption from income-tax and super-tax on voluntarily surrendered salary and allowances.
Right to have surrendered salary excluded from total income for tax purposes.
duties: Duty to declare in writing the voluntary surrender of salary in the public interest (for salaries paid out of Consolidated Fund).
Duty to surrender salary in favor of and pay it to the Central Government in accordance with rules (for other cases).
obligations: Obligation to comply with rules made by the Central Government regarding the surrender of salaries.
Obligation for the payer of salary to correctly account for the surrendered portion.

key_procedures: Procedure for claiming exemption: A person must make a declaration in writing to voluntarily forego a part of their salary in the public interest if it is paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India or of a State. For other cases, the surrendered portion of salary must be paid to the Central Government in accordance with the rules made by the Government.

Procedure for making and laying rules: The Central Government makes rules by notification in the Official Gazette. These rules are then laid before both Houses of Parliament for a total period of thirty days, during which they can be modified or annulled by Parliament.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act does not apply to salary or allowances due before March 31, 1961.
Any declaration made under the repealed Act of 1950 is deemed valid under this Act.
The rules made by the Central Government are subject to parliamentary scrutiny and modification.

title: THE GOA, DAMAN AND DIU (ADMINISTRATION) ACT, 1962
purpose: To provide for the administration of the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu. Covers administration, representation, existing laws, and related matters.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator of Goa, Daman and Diu appointed by the President under Article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.appointed_day: The twentieth day of December, 1961.
key_definitions.Goa,_Daman_and_Diu: The Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its deemed commencement date.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'appointed day', and 'Goa, Daman and Diu'.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Allots seats to Goa, Daman and Diu in the House of the People and makes consequential amendments to the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and functionaries in relation to Goa, Daman and Diu
main_sections.description: Ensures that judges, magistrates, and other officers exercising lawful functions in Goa, Daman and Diu before the Act's commencement continue to do so, subject to Central Government directions.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of existing laws and their adaptation
main_sections.description: States that laws in force before the appointed day will continue until amended or repealed, and empowers the Central Government to adapt these laws.

main_sections.section_title: Power to extend enactments to Goa, Daman and Diu
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to extend any enactment in force in a State to Goa, Daman and Diu.
Allows courts or other authorities to construe laws in a manner necessary to adapt them to the context of Goa, Daman and Diu, without affecting their substance.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain action and indemnity of officers for certain acts
main_sections.description: Validates actions taken in good faith for the peace and good government of Goa, Daman and Diu between the appointed day and the Act's commencement, and provides indemnity to officers for such actions.
Empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act or in the administration of Goa, Daman and Diu.
Repeals the Goa, Daman and Diu (Administration) Ordinance, 1962, and provides that anything done under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done under the Act.

important_rules: Existing laws in force in Goa, Daman and Diu before the appointed day shall continue to be in force until amended or repealed (Section 5(1)).
Actions taken in good faith for the peace and good government of Goa, Daman and Diu between the appointed day and the commencement of the Act are validated (Section 9(1)).

No legal proceedings shall lie against the Administrator or any officer for actions taken in good faith for the peace and good government of Goa, Daman and Diu during the specified period (Section 9(2)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Administrator, and other appointed officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the continuation of existing functions of officers, extension of enactments, adaptation of laws, and orders to remove difficulties.

rights: Right to representation in the House of the People for Goa, Daman and Diu (Section 3).
obligations: Officers and functionaries are obligated to continue exercising their functions in connection with the administration of Goa, Daman and Diu (Section 4).

key_procedures: Adaptation of existing laws: The Central Government may, within two years of the appointed day, make adaptations and modifications to existing laws to facilitate their application to Goa, Daman and Diu as a Union territory and to bring them in accord with the Constitution (Section 5(2)).

Removal of difficulties: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of the Act or in connection with the administration of Goa, Daman and Diu, the Central Government may issue orders to remove the difficulty (Section 10).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: Section 7, concerning the extension of the jurisdiction of the Bombay High Court, was repealed by the Goa, Daman and Diu Judicial Commissioner's Court (Declaration as High Court) Act, 1964.
Orders made by the Central Government to remove difficulties can be retrospective to a date not earlier than the appointed day (Section 10(2)).

title: The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan Act, 1962
purpose: To declare the institution known as the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, having its head office at Allahabad, as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, which has its head office in Allahabad. It declares the institution as one of national importance and provides for its incorporation. The Act's provisions govern the Sammelan's functions, management, and affairs.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Sammelan: The institution known as the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, incorporated under this Act.
key_definitions.Society: The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan which has its head office at Allahabad and is registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, with its head office in Allahabad, as an institution of national importance due to its objects.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'prescribed', 'Sammelan', and 'Society'.

Constitutes the first members and future members of the Sammelan as a body corporate named the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan. It grants the Sammelan perpetual succession, a common seal, power to acquire/hold/dispose of property, and the ability to sue and be sued. The head office is fixed at Allahabad. It also specifies who constitutes the first members.

Details the consequences of incorporation, including references to the Society being deemed references to the Sammelan, the transfer of all property from the Society to the Sammelan, the transfer of rights and liabilities, and the continuation of employment for existing employees under similar terms.

Outlines the various functions of the Sammelan, including promoting the spread and development of Hindi language and literature, promoting the Devanagari script, arranging examinations, conferring academic distinctions, establishing institutions, affiliating institutions, awarding prizes, promoting research, cooperating with similar institutions, receiving grants and donations, managing property, and borrowing money with Central Government approval.

States that the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Sammelan's affairs shall vest in a Governing Body. It specifies the maximum number of members (not exceeding fifty-five), the number nominated by the Central Government, and how the remaining members are chosen. It also mentions that the powers, functions, term of office, allowances, procedure, quorum, and filling of casual vacancies shall be as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: First Governing Body and its duties
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to constitute the first Governing Body, consisting of a Chairman, Secretary, and thirteen other members. It details how these thirteen members are to be chosen, including representation from relevant Ministries and from former Presidents or eminent individuals in Hindi language/literature. The duties of the first Governing Body include performing Sammelan functions until a regular Governing Body is constituted, making rules with Central Government approval, determining the first members, and preparing for the constitution of the Governing Body.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and procedure of first Governing Body and allowances payable to members thereof
main_sections.description: Specifies that members of the first Governing Body hold office at the pleasure of the Central Government. It details decision-making by majority vote with a casting vote for the presiding officer, the quorum (five members), and the payment of salary or allowances to members, which are to be prescribed or specified by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: First Governing Body to take over management of properties of Sammelan
main_sections.description: Mandates that the first Governing Body shall take over the management, control, and administration of all properties vested in the Sammelan, notwithstanding any other law or court order.

Requires the first Governing Body to prepare a list of all persons who are to be considered first members of the Sammelan. This list is to be published as directed by the Central Government, and amendments can be made for wrongly omitted or entered names after providing an opportunity to be heard. Only persons on this list are considered first members.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be made by the first Governing Body
main_sections.description: Details the matters for which the first Governing Body shall make rules, including membership qualifications, powers and functions of the Governing Body, conduct of elections, appointment of committees, maintenance of accounts, conditions of service for employees, conduct of correspondence and suits, affiliation of institutions, award of degrees and prizes, amendment of rules, and other necessary matters. Draft rules require Central Government approval and must be published as directed.

important_rules: The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan is declared an institution of national importance.
The Sammelan is incorporated as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
All property, rights, and liabilities of the original Society are transferred to the incorporated Sammelan.
Employees of the Society continue their employment with the Sammelan under the same terms and conditions.
The Governing Body is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Sammelan's affairs.
The first Governing Body is tasked with crucial initial responsibilities, including making rules and determining the first members.
Rules made by the first Governing Body require approval from the Central Government before they come into effect.
The Sammelan is empowered to promote the spread and development of Hindi language and literature in various ways, including education, publications, and research.
The Sammelan can award honorary degrees and prizes to recognize contributions to Hindi.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for appointments, approval of rules, and oversight)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette, approval of rules, and by the Governing Body's management and administration of the Sammelan's affairs.

rights: The Sammelan has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The Sammelan has the right to contract.
The Sammelan can sue and be sued.
Employees retain their rights and privileges regarding pension, leave, gratuity, provident fund, etc.
duties: To promote the spread of Hindi language and its enrichment as per Article 351 of the Constitution.
To work for the promotion, development, and advancement of Hindi literature.
To promote the Devanagari script.
To arrange for examinations and confer academic distinctions.
To establish and maintain educational institutions.
To cooperate with similar institutions.
To manage its affairs through the Governing Body.
obligations: To comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder.
The first Governing Body has the obligation to perform all functions of the Sammelan and carry on its administration until a regular Governing Body is constituted.
The first Governing Body must make rules with the approval of the Central Government.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Upon notification by the Central Government in the Official Gazette.
Incorporation of the Sammelan: The first members and future members are constituted as a body corporate.
Management by the First Governing Body: The first Governing Body takes over the management and administration of the Sammelan's properties.
Determination and publication of first members: The first Governing Body prepares and publishes a list of first members.
Rule making: The first Governing Body makes rules subject to Central Government approval and publication.
Constitution of the Governing Body: The Central Government determines the size, and the Governing Body is constituted with a mix of nominated and elected members according to prescribed rules.
Transaction of business by the Governing Body: Decisions are made by majority vote, with a specified quorum.
Payment of allowances: Members of the first Governing Body are paid out of the Sammelan Fund as prescribed or specified.
administration: The Central Government has oversight and approval powers, especially regarding the first Governing Body and the rules. The Governing Body of the Sammelan is responsible for its day-to-day administration and management.
important_notes: The Act was brought into force on June 28, 1962.
Sub-section (4) of Section 4 was substituted by Act 1 of 1963, specifying the categories of individuals constituting the first members.
Clause (b) of Section 5 was substituted by Act 1 of 1963, clarifying the transfer of property.
The words 'be transferred to, and' were omitted from clause (c) of Section 5 by Act 1 of 1963.
The quorum for meetings of the first Governing Body was changed from 'three' to 'five' members by Act 1 of 1963.
The term 'allowances' in Section 9 was substituted with 'salary or allowances or both' by Act 1 of 1963.

title: The Atomic Energy Act, 1962
purpose: To provide for the development, control and use of atomic energy for the welfare of the people of India and for other peaceful purposes and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to individuals, companies, and the Central Government concerning atomic energy, prescribed substances, minerals, plants, and related activities.

key_definitions.atomic_energy: Energy released from atomic nuclei as a result of any process, including fission and fusion processes.
key_definitions.fissile_material: Uranium 233, Uranium 235, plutonium or any material containing these substances or any other material declared as such by the Central Government.
key_definitions.government_company: A company where not less than fifty-one per cent. of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, or the whole paid-up share capital is held by such companies and the Central Government can constitute and reconstitute its Board of Directors.
key_definitions.minerals: Includes all substances obtained or obtainable from the soil (including alluvium or rocks) by underground or surface working.
key_definitions.notification: Notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.plant: Includes machinery, equipment or appliance, whether affixed to land or not.
key_definitions.prescribed_equipment: Property specially designed or adapted or used for the production or utilisation of any prescribed substance, or for the production or utilisation of atomic energy, radioactive substances, or radiation, excluding mining, milling, laboratory and other equipment not so specially designed or adapted and not incorporated.
key_definitions.prescribed_substance: Any substance including any mineral that the Central Government may prescribe, which is or may be used for the production or use of atomic energy or research, and includes uranium, plutonium, thorium, beryllium, deuterium or their derivatives/compounds or materials containing them.
key_definitions.radiation: Gamma rays, X-rays, and rays consisting of alpha particles, beta particles, neutrons, protons and other nuclear and sub-atomic particles; but not sound or radio waves, or visible, infrared or ultraviolet light.
key_definitions.radioactive_substance_or_radioactive_mat: Any substance or material which spontaneously emits radiation in excess of the levels prescribed by notification by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement (to be notified by the Central Government).

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'atomic energy', 'fissile material', 'minerals', 'prescribed substance', 'radiation', etc., and provides rules for interpretation of references to working of minerals and production or use of atomic energy.

main_sections.section_title: General powers of the Central Government
main_sections.description: Outlines the broad powers of the Central Government concerning atomic energy, including production, development, use, disposal, research, manufacturing of related substances and articles, acquiring and storing substances, declaring restricted information and prohibited areas, controlling radioactive substances and radiation, producing electricity from atomic energy, and undertaking incidental works.

main_sections.section_title: Notification of discovery of uranium or thorium
main_sections.description: Mandates reporting the discovery of uranium or thorium to the Central Government within three months of discovery or commencement of the Act, whichever is later. Also requires reporting any belief that uranium or thorium occurs at a place.

main_sections.section_title: Control over mining or concentration of substances containing uranium
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to impose terms and conditions or prohibit mining or concentration of substances from which uranium can be isolated or extracted. Specifies compensation provisions in case of prohibition or imposition of terms.

Regulates the disposal of minerals, concentrates, and other materials containing uranium above a prescribed proportion, requiring previous permission from the Central Government. Allows for compulsory acquisition of such materials with compensation based on production cost, excluding the value of uranium.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to obtain information regarding materials, plant or processes
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to require any person to submit returns or statements regarding prescribed substances, plants, contracts, licenses, or any other relevant information related to prospecting, mining, or atomic energy production/use.
Authorizes persons authorized by the Central Government to enter mines, premises, or land where work related to atomic energy production is believed to be carried out for inspection.

important_rules: All persons discovering uranium or thorium must report the discovery to the Central Government within three months. (Section 4(1))
Any person believing uranium or thorium exists at a place must report it to the Central Government without delay. (Section 4(2))
Disposal of minerals/materials containing uranium above a prescribed proportion requires prior written permission from the Central Government. (Section 6(1))

Information related to the location, quality, quantity, transactions, processing of prescribed substances, design/operation of plants and reactors, and related research can be declared as 'restricted information' by the Central Government. (Section 3(c))
Areas where work related to atomic energy or prescribed substances is carried out can be declared as 'prohibited areas'. (Section 3(d))

penalties: Offences under the Act are punishable as prescribed in Section 24.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through various powers including issuing notifications, notices, requiring returns, prohibiting certain activities, compulsory acquisition, and delegation of powers. Enforcement also involves penal provisions for offences.

rights: Right to compensation in case of compulsory acquisition or prohibition of mining/treatment of substances containing uranium (Sections 5, 6, 12, 21).
duties: Duty to report discovery of uranium or thorium (Section 4).
Duty to comply with terms and conditions imposed by the Central Government for mining or concentration of substances containing uranium (Section 5).
Duty to obtain prior permission for disposal of materials containing uranium (Section 6).
Duty to submit returns and provide information as required by the Central Government (Section 7).
Duty to comply with safety provisions related to radioactive substances and radiation (Section 17).
obligations: Individuals and companies are obligated to adhere to the regulations set forth by the Central Government concerning atomic energy, prescribed substances, and radioactive materials.

key_procedures: Reporting the discovery of uranium or thorium: Discoverer must report in writing to the Central Government or authorized person within three months of discovery or commencement of the Act. (Section 4(1))

Obtaining information: Central Government may issue written notice to any person requiring periodical and other returns or statements with specific particulars relating to prescribed substances, plants, contracts, etc. (Section 7)
Compulsory acquisition of materials containing uranium: Central Government may serve notice to compulsorily acquire minerals, concentrates, or other materials containing uranium. (Section 6(2))
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act allows for the delegation of powers by the Central Government to any person or authority. (Section 27)
The Act is binding on the Government. (Section 31)
The Central Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act. (Section 30)

title: THE PONDICHERRY (ADMINISTRATION) ACT, 1962
purpose: To provide for the administration of Pondicherry and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of Pondicherry, which comprises the territories of the former French Establishments (Pondicherry, Karikal, Mahe, and Yanam). It primarily deals with the transition and administration following the cession of these territories from France to India.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator of Pondicherry appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.appointed_day: The 16th day of August, 1962, being the date of entry into force of the Treaty of Cession.
key_definitions.former_French_Establishments: The territories which immediately before the appointed day were comprised in the French Establishments in India known as Pondicherry, Karikal, Mahe and Yanam.
key_definitions.law: Any Act, Ordinance, Regulation, rule, order, bye-law, decree or other provision (by whatever name called) having the force of law.
key_definitions.Pondicherry: The Union territory comprising the territories of the former French Establishments.
key_definitions.Treaty_of_Cession: The treaty concluded between France and India on the 28th day of May, 1956, establishing the cession of the French Establishments by France to India in full sovereignty.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Pondicherry (Administration) Act, 1962, its extent to the whole of Pondicherry, and its deemed commencement from August 16, 1962.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'appointed day', 'former French Establishments', 'High Court', 'law', 'Pondicherry', and 'Treaty of Cession'.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and functionaries in relation to Pondicherry
main_sections.description: Ensures that existing courts, tribunals, authorities, and officers exercising lawful functions in the former French Establishments before the appointed day shall continue to do so in Pondicherry, unless otherwise directed or until new provisions are made.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of existing laws and their adaptation
main_sections.description: States that all laws in force in the former French Establishments before the appointed day shall continue in Pondicherry until amended or repealed. It also empowers the Central Government to adapt these laws within three years to align them with the Constitution.

Declares that all property and assets within Pondicherry that vested in the Government of the French Republic before the appointed day shall vest in the Union, except as otherwise provided in the Treaty of Cession.

Specifies that all rights, liabilities, and obligations of the Government of the French Republic related to the administration of the former French Establishments shall become those of the Central Government from the appointed day, subject to the Treaty of Cession.

States that all taxes, duties, cesses, and fees lawfully levied in the former French Establishments before the appointed day shall continue to be levied in Pondicherry for the same purposes until otherwise provided by law.

main_sections.section_title: Power to extend enactments to Pondicherry
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to extend any enactment in force in a State to Pondicherry, with necessary restrictions and modifications.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the jurisdiction of Madras High Court to Pondicherry
main_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court at Madras to Pondicherry from November 6, 1962.

Confers upon the High Court all such jurisdiction in respect of Pondicherry as was previously exercisable by French courts (Cour de Cassation, Cour Superieur d’ Arbitrage, Counseil d’ Etat). It also transfers pending proceedings from these French courts to the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Advocates entitled to practise before High Court
main_sections.description: Recognizes advocates entitled to practice before the Tribunal Superieur d’ Appeal at Pondicherry as eligible to practice before the High Court in cases originating from Pondicherry, subject to High Court rules.

main_sections.section_title: Power of High Court to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the High Court to make rules regarding translation of papers, court fees, procedure, and the approval, admission, enrolment, removal, and suspension of advocates from Pondicherry.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain orders and decrees
main_sections.description: Validates orders and decrees made by French courts between November 1, 1954, and the appointed day. It also addresses decisions made by French courts where the respondent was not properly served, deeming them never rendered and transferring them to the appropriate court in Pondicherry.

Sets out the periods of limitation for various types of appeals to the High Court from Pondicherry, including provisions for exclusion of time for obtaining certified copies and for appeals filed by incarcerated accused persons. It also allows for condonation of delay for sufficient cause.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of limitation in certain cases
main_sections.description: Provides for the exclusion of periods during which appeals or proceedings could not be filed due to the non-extension of the High Court's jurisdiction to Pondicherry, for the purpose of computing limitation periods.
Mandates that references in Pondicherry laws to French courts (Cour de Cassation, Court Superieur d’ Arbitrage, Counsel d’ Etat) shall be construed as references to the High Court.
Allows any court or authority to construe laws in Pondicherry in a manner necessary to adapt them to the local context without affecting their substance.
States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in any other law in force in Pondicherry.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act, with such orders potentially being retrospective.
Repeals the Pondicherry (Administration) Ordinance, 1962, but saves anything done or any action taken under that Ordinance, deeming them to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Existing laws in former French Establishments shall continue in Pondicherry until amended or repealed (Section 4(1)).
Rule: References to French authorities in existing laws shall be construed as references to Indian authorities (Section 4(1) proviso).
Rule: The Central Government can adapt existing laws for Pondicherry within three years of the appointed day (Section 4(2)).
Rule: All property and assets vesting in the French Republic in Pondicherry shall vest in the Union (Section 5).
Rule: Rights, liabilities, and obligations of the French Republic in Pondicherry shall become those of the Central Government (Section 6).
Rule: Existing taxes, duties, cesses, and fees in Pondicherry shall continue to be levied (Section 7).
Rule: The High Court at Madras's jurisdiction extends to Pondicherry (Section 9).
Rule: The High Court shall have the jurisdiction of former French superior courts (Section 10(1)).
Rule: Pending proceedings in French superior courts shall be transferred to the High Court (Section 10(2)).
Rule: Advocates practicing in the Tribunal Superieur d’ Appeal at Pondicherry are eligible to practice before the High Court in Pondicherry cases (Section 11).
Rule: Specific periods of limitation are prescribed for appeals to the High Court from Pondicherry (Section 14(1)).
Rule: Time taken to obtain certified copies for appeals is excluded from limitation (Section 14(2)).
Rule: Appeals by convicted and imprisoned persons are considered presented on the date lodged with the Jail Superintendent (Section 14(3)).
Rule: Appeals can be admitted after the limitation period if sufficient cause is shown (Section 14(4)).
Rule: Periods when High Court jurisdiction was not extended to Pondicherry shall be excluded for limitation calculation (Section 15).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and the Administrator of Pondicherry, and the High Court of Madras for judicial matters.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the continuation of existing judicial and administrative structures, the extension of the High Court's jurisdiction, and the Central Government's power to make adaptations and remove difficulties.

rights: Right to continued exercise of lawful functions by existing officers and authorities (Section 3).
Right to the continuation of existing laws (Section 4).
Right to property and assets vesting in the Union (Section 5).
Right to the Central Government assuming liabilities and obligations of the French Republic (Section 6).
Right to continuation of existing taxes, duties, etc. (Section 7).
Right for advocates of the Tribunal Superieur d’ Appeal to practice before the High Court (Section 11).
duties: Duty to continue exercising powers and performing duties as before the appointed day (Section 3).
Duty to comply with adapted laws (Section 4).
Duty to adhere to the Treaty of Cession regarding property, rights, and obligations (Sections 5, 6).
Duty to pay lawfully levied taxes, duties, etc. (Section 7).
obligations: Obligations arising from the administration of the former French Establishments are assumed by the Central Government (Section 6).

key_procedures: Procedure for Adaptation of Laws: The Central Government may, within three years of the appointed day, by order, make adaptations and modifications to existing laws to facilitate their application in Pondicherry and bring them into accord with the Constitution (Section 4(2)).

Procedure for Extension of Enactments: The Central Government may extend any enactment in force in a State to Pondicherry by notification in the Official Gazette, with restrictions and modifications as deemed fit (Section 8).

Procedure for Handling Pending Cases: Appeals and proceedings pending before French superior courts before the appointed day are transferred to the High Court and disposed of as if filed there (Section 10(2)).

Procedure for Validation of French Court Decisions: Certain orders and decrees of French courts made within a specified period are deemed valid and effective as if made by the High Court. Specific procedures are outlined for dealing with French court decisions where respondents were not properly served (Section 13).

Procedure for Filing Appeals: Appeals to the High Court must be filed within prescribed limitation periods, with provisions for exclusion of time for obtaining certified copies and condonation of delay (Section 14).
administration: Central Government, and the Administrator of Pondicherry. The High Court of Madras has extended jurisdiction.
important_notes: Note: The Act is deemed to have come into force on August 16, 1962, retroactively (Section 1(3)).
Note: The Act's provisions override any inconsistent laws (Section 18).
Note: The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties, and such orders can be retrospective to the appointed day (Section 19).
Note: Madras High Court jurisdiction was extended on November 6, 1962 (Section 9).

title: The State-Associated Banks (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1962
purpose: To further amend the State Bank of India Act, 1955, the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959, and the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891, and to provide for the winding up of certain minor State-associated banks and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to amendments of specific Acts and provisions related to the winding up of the Dholpur bank. Geographically, it concerns operations within India. Subject matter scope includes banking regulations, winding up procedures, and legal proceedings related to state-associated banks.

key_definitions.Dholpur bank: The bank known as the Dholpur State Bank and governed at the commencement of section 5 by the State Bank, Dholpur Act, 1915.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for different parts of the Act. Section 3, with specific exceptions, comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, while the rest of the Act comes into force immediately.
This section related to amendments to the State Bank of India Act, 1955, but was repealed.
This section related to amendments to the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959, but was repealed.
This section related to amendments to the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891, but was repealed.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions in respect of the State Bank Dholpur
main_sections.description: Details the provisions for taking over the management or winding up of the Dholpur bank. It outlines the exclusive jurisdiction of the principal civil court, applicability of banking company winding-up laws, a specific limitation period for claims, and the utilization of remaining assets.
This section related to amendments to the State Bank of Kurundwad (Junior) Act, 1933, but was repealed.

important_rules: Rule: The Central Government may appoint officers to manage or wind up the Dholpur bank and its assets.
Rule: The principal civil court has exclusive jurisdiction over all claims and questions related to the winding up of the Dholpur bank.
Rule: Laws relating to the winding up of banking companies apply to the Dholpur bank as if it were a banking company.
Rule: The period of limitation for claims due to the Dholpur bank is twelve years from accrual or five years from the appointment of the winding-up officer, whichever is later.
Rule: Remaining assets of the Dholpur bank, after liabilities are met, shall be used for purposes specified in the State Bank, Dholpur Act, 1915.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and Principal Civil Court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appointment of officers for management/winding up, court jurisdiction for claims, and application of banking company winding-up laws.

rights: Right to appoint officers to manage or wind up the Dholpur bank.
Right to distribute assets of the Dholpur bank.
duties: Duty to adhere to the exclusive jurisdiction of the principal civil court for Dholpur bank related matters.
Duty to follow the laws relating to the winding up of banking companies for the Dholpur bank.
Duty to repay all deposit liabilities and other amounts due by the bank, including those to the Government of Rajasthan.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that expenditure incurred in winding up or management is payable by the Dholpur bank.
Obligation to utilize remaining assets of the Dholpur bank for specified purposes after liabilities are cleared.

key_procedures: Procedure: Appointment of officers by the Central Government to manage or wind up the Dholpur bank and distribute its assets.

Procedure: Claims and questions relating to the Dholpur bank's winding up are to be heard and decided exclusively by the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in the district of its head office.

Procedure: Admissibility of entries in account books, settlement of debtors, payment orders, execution of decrees, priority of claims, preferential payments, and discharge of liabilities for the Dholpur bank follow the law applicable to banking companies.
administration: Central Government, in conjunction with the principal civil court for specific jurisdiction.
important_notes: Section 3, except for specific clauses, had a delayed commencement as appointed by the Central Government.
Several sections (2, 3, 4, and 6) of the Act have been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1974.

title: THE NATIONAL CO-OPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION ACT, 1962
purpose: To provide for the incorporation and regulation of a corporation for the purpose of planning and promoting programmes for the production, processing, marketing, storage, export and import of agricultural produce, foodstuffs, industrial goods, livestock, certain other commodities and services on co-operative principles and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Covers planning and promoting programs related to agricultural produce, foodstuffs, industrial goods, livestock, certain other commodities, and services on co-operative principles.

key_definitions.agricultural_produce: Includes edible and non-edible oil seeds; cattle feed, including oilcakes and other ingredients; produce of horticulture and animal husbandry; produce of forestry; produce of poultry farming; produce of pisciculture; and produce of other allied activities, whether or not undertaken jointly with agriculture.
key_definitions.bank: Means a nationalised bank and includes a scheduled bank.
key_definitions.board: Means the Board of Management of the Corporation constituted under section 10.
key_definitions.central_financing_institution: Means Industrial Development Bank of India established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964 (18 of 1964) or the Industrial Finance Corporation of India Limited, a company formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956 (1 of 1956), or the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Limited, a Company formed and registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1913 (7 of 1913).
key_definitions.central_warehousing_corporation: Means the Central Warehousing Corporation established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962 (58 of 1962).
key_definitions.cooperative_society: Means a society registered or deemed to be registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912 (2 of 1912) or under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 1984 (51 of 1984) or under any other law with respect to co operative societies for the time being in force in any State, which is engaged in any of the activities specified in sub-section (1) of section 9 and includes a Co-operative Land Development Bank, by whatever name called.
key_definitions.corporation: Means the National Co-operative Development Corporation established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.foodstuffs: Include coconuts and areca-nuts; eggs and egg products; fish, whether fresh, frozen, dried or preserved; fruits, whether fresh, dried or dehydrated; honey; meat, whether fresh, frozen, dried or preserved; milk and milk products; vegetables.
key_definitions.general_council: Means the General Council of the Corporation constituted under sub-section (4) of section 3.
key_definitions.industrial_goods: Means the products of industrial co-operatives or cottage and village industries or products of allied industries in the rural area and includes any handicrafts or rural crafts.
key_definitions.livestock: Includes all animals to be raised for milk, meat, fleece, skin, wool and other by-products.
key_definitions.managing_director: Means the managing director of the Corporation.
key_definitions.nationalised_bank: Means a corresponding new bank constituted under section 3 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970) or under section 3 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 (40 of 1980).
key_definitions.notified_commodity: Means any commodity (other than agricultural produce and foodstuffs) which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare to be a notified commodity for the purposes of this Act, being a commodity with respect to which Parliament has power to make laws by virtue of entry 33 in List III in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.
key_definitions.notified_services: Means any service which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare to be notified services for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.reserve_bank: Means the Reserve Bank of India constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934).
key_definitions.scheduled_bank: Means a bank for the time being included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934).
key_definitions.state_bank: Means the State Bank of India constituted under the State Bank of India Act, 1955 (23 of 1955) or any of the subsidiary banks of the State Bank of India.
key_definitions.state_cooperative_bank: Has the same meaning as in the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981 (61 of 1981).

title: The Marine Insurance Act, 1963
purpose: To codify the law relating to marine insurance.
scope: Applies to contracts of marine insurance, including those related to ships, goods, freight, and other maritime adventures. It also extends to certain inland waters and land risks incidental to sea voyages, and adventures analogous to marine adventures.

key_definitions.contract of marine insurance: A contract of marine insurance as defined by section 3.
key_definitions.freight: Includes profit derivable by a ship-owner from employing his ship to carry his own goods or other movables, as well as freight payable by a third party, but excludes passage money.
key_definitions.insurable property: Any ship, goods or other movables which are exposed to maritime perils.
key_definitions.marine adventure: Includes any adventure where insurable property is exposed to maritime perils; earnings or acquisition of freight, passage money, commission, profit or other pecuniary benefit, or security for advances, loans, or disbursements is endangered; or any liability to a third party may be incurred by the owner of, or other person interested in, insurable property by reason of maritime perils.
key_definitions.maritime perils: Perils consequent on, or incidental to, the navigation of the sea, including perils of the seas, fire, war perils, pirates, rovers, thieves, captures, seizures, restraints and detainments of princes and peoples, jettisons, barratry, and similar perils.
key_definitions.movables: Any movable tangible property, other than the ship, including money, valuable securities and other documents.
key_definitions.ship: Includes every description of vessel used in navigation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as contract of marine insurance, freight, insurable property, marine adventure, maritime perils, movables, policy, ship, and suit.
Defines a contract of marine insurance as an agreement where the insurer undertakes to indemnify the assured against marine losses.
States that every contract of marine insurance by way of wagering is void and defines conditions under which a contract is deemed to be a wagering contract.

Defines insurable interest as being interested in a marine adventure, which includes legal or equitable relation to the adventure or property at risk, where one may benefit by its safety or be prejudiced by its loss.
Establishes that a contract of marine insurance is based on the utmost good faith, and failure to observe it by either party can lead to the contract being avoided by the other.
Mandates the assured to disclose every material circumstance known to them to the insurer before the contract is concluded. Defines material circumstances and lists those that need not be disclosed.

main_sections.section_title: Contract must be embodied in policy
main_sections.description: Requires that the contract of marine insurance must be embodied in a policy.
Specifies what losses are covered and what losses are excluded under a marine insurance policy.
Defines what constitutes a constructive total loss.
Grants the insurer the right of subrogation upon payment of a loss.
Establishes the insurer's right of contribution.

important_rules: Rule 1: Every contract of marine insurance by way of wagering is void.
Rule 2: The assured must disclose to the insurer every material circumstance before the contract is concluded.
Rule 3: A contract of marine insurance must be embodied in a policy.
Rule 4: The assured must be interested in the subject-matter insured at the time of the loss, though not necessarily when the insurance is effected.
Rule 5: Upon payment of a loss, the insurer is subrogated to all rights of the assured in relation to the subject-matter insured to the extent of the sum paid.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be through the legal system for contract disputes and general enforcement of laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through civil courts for contractual disputes and the application of legal remedies. Specific enforcement mechanisms for breaches of duty or misrepresentation are not detailed in the provided text.

rights: Right of the assured to be indemnified against marine losses.
Right of the insurer to avoid the contract if utmost good faith is not observed.
Right of the insurer to subrogation upon payment of a loss.
Right of the insurer to contribution from other insurers in case of double insurance.
duties: Duty of the assured to observe utmost good faith.
Duty of the assured to disclose material circumstances to the insurer.
Duty of the insurer to indemnify the assured against agreed marine losses.
obligations: Obligation to embody the contract in a policy.
Obligation to pay premium for insurance cover.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Establishing an insurable interest before or at the time of loss for valid insurance claims.
Procedure 2: Disclosure of material facts by the assured to the insurer before the contract is concluded.
Procedure 3: Notifying the insurer of abandonment in case of a total loss.
Procedure 4: The process of subrogation where the insurer takes over the rights of the assured after paying a claim.
administration: Central Government (for commencement notification); other departments would likely be involved in overseeing insurance practices and resolving disputes, though not explicitly named in this excerpt.
important_notes: The Act can be applied with modifications in certain cases as per Section 89.
Certain provisions of this Act override the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Section 90).
A contract of marine insurance can be extended to cover inland waters or land risks incidental to a sea voyage.
The Act applies to adventures analogous to marine adventures, including those exposed to perils incidental to local or inland transit.

title: THE GOVERNMENT OF UNION TERRITORIES ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for Legislative Assemblies and Councils of Ministers for certain Union territories and for certain other matters.
scope: This act applies to certain Union territories of India, providing for their legislative assemblies, councils of ministers, and related administrative provisions. The specific Union territories are subject to amendments and notifications.

key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator of the Union territory appointed by the President under article 239.
key_definitions.assembly constituency: A constituency provided under this Act for the purpose of elections to the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory.
key_definitions.Election Commission: The Election Commission appointed by the President under article 324.
key_definitions.scheduled castes: Such castes, races or tribes or parts of or groups within such castes, races or tribes as are deemed under article 341 to be scheduled castes in relation to that Union territory.
key_definitions.scheduled tribes: Such tribes or tribal communities or parts of or groups within such tribes or tribal communities as are deemed under article 342 to be scheduled tribes in relation to that Union territory.
key_definitions.Union territory: The Union territory of Puducherry (as per amendment).

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette. Different dates can be appointed for different provisions and Union territories.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Administrator, article, assembly constituency, Election Commission, Judicial Commissioner, scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, and Union territory. It also clarifies references to laws made by Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Legislative Assemblies for Union territories and their composition
main_sections.description: Establishes a Legislative Assembly for each Union territory, specifies the total number of directly elected seats, allows for nominated members, and provides for reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes based on population proportion. It also includes provisions for the cessation of reservation based on parliamentary seats.

main_sections.section_title: Qualification for membership of Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Outlines the qualifications for a person to be chosen as a member of the Legislative Assembly, including Indian citizenship, taking an oath or affirmation, being at least twenty-five years of age, and possessing other prescribed qualifications.

States that the Legislative Assembly, unless sooner dissolved, continues for five years from its first meeting. This period can be extended during a Proclamation of Emergency, but not beyond six months after the Proclamation ceases to operate.

main_sections.section_title: Sessions of Legislative Assembly, prorogation and dissolution
main_sections.description: Empowers the Administrator to summon the Assembly, ensuring a maximum gap of six months between sessions. The Administrator can also prorogue or dissolve the Assembly.

main_sections.section_title: Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Requires the Legislative Assembly to elect a Speaker and Deputy Speaker. It also states that they vacate their office if they cease to be members of the Assembly.

important_rules: A Legislative Assembly must be established for each Union territory.
Members of the Legislative Assembly must be citizens of India, at least twenty-five years old, and have taken an oath or affirmation.
The Legislative Assembly's duration is five years, with provisions for extension during emergencies.
The Administrator summons, prorogues, and dissolves the Legislative Assembly.
The Legislative Assembly elects a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker.
Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assembly based on population proportion.

penalties: Penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation or when not qualified or when disqualified (Section 15).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, the President, the Administrator, and the Election Commission are involved in the enforcement and administration of various aspects of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, appointments, presidential orders, and the functioning of legislative bodies and administrative authorities within the Union territories.

rights: Right of Administrator to address and send messages to Legislative Assembly.
Rights of Ministers as respects Legislative Assembly.
Rights and privileges of members of the Legislative Assembly.
duties: Duty to adhere to qualifications for membership.
Duty to make oath or affirmation before sitting and voting.
Duty to conduct business according to established procedures.
obligations: Obligation to follow the duration and session rules of the Legislative Assembly.
Obligation to reserve seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as per law.
Obligation to adhere to restrictions on legislative power and financial bills.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act through Central Government notification.
Election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker by the Legislative Assembly.
Procedure for summoning, prorogation, and dissolution of the Legislative Assembly by the Administrator.
Procedure for delimitation of constituencies.
Procedure for financial bills and appropriation bills.
administration: The Central Government and the Administrator of the respective Union territories are responsible for the administration of this Act.
important_notes: The Act's commencement dates can vary for different provisions and Union territories.
The definition of 'Union territory' has been amended to specifically refer to Puducherry.
Provisions related to the duration of the Legislative Assembly can be extended during a Proclamation of Emergency.
Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is subject to census figures and constitutional provisions (e.g., Article 334).

title: THE EXPORT (QUALITY CONTROL AND INSPECTION) ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for the sound development of the export trade of India through quality control and inspection and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to commodities intended for export, specifically 'notified commodities' which are subject to quality control or inspection prior to export.

key_definitions.adjudicating_authority: The authority specified in, or under, section 10K.
key_definitions.appellate_authority: The appellate authority referred to in section 10M.
key_definitions.Council: The Export Inspection Council established under section 3.
key_definitions.export: Taking out of India to a place outside India.
key_definitions.inspection: The process of determining whether a batch of goods complies with standard specifications or contract specifications, by inspecting the whole batch or a sample.
key_definitions.notified_commodity: Any commodity notified under clause (a) of section 6.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.quality_control: Any activity aimed at determining the quality of a commodity (during manufacture, production, or subsequently) to ascertain if it satisfies applicable standard specifications or contract specifications for export.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its geographical extent (whole of India), and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'adjudicating authority', 'Appellate authority', 'Council', 'export', 'inspection', 'notified commodity', 'prescribed', and 'quality control'.

Details the establishment of the Export Inspection Council by the Central Government, its composition (Chairman, ex-officio members, nominated members), its corporate status, and provisions for term of office, vacancies, allowances, and appointment of staff.

main_sections.section_title: Director of Inspection and Quality Control
main_sections.description: States that the Central Government shall appoint a Director of Inspection and Quality Control to exercise prescribed powers and perform prescribed duties.

Outlines the Council's functions, including advising the Central Government on quality control and inspection measures for exports, drawing up programs, making grants to agencies, and performing other assigned functions. It also allows co-opting members and constituting specialist committees.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the Central Government in regard to quality control and inspection
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government powers to notify commodities for quality control/inspection, specify the type of control/inspection, establish/adopt/recognize standard specifications, and prohibit export of notified commodities unless they meet specified conditions or bear a recognized mark.

main_sections.section_title: Machinery for quality control and inspection
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish or recognize agencies for quality control and inspection. These agencies can hold examinations, issue certificates of compliance, and amend, suspend, or cancel certificates under certain conditions. It also provides for appeals against agency decisions and Central Government review.

main_sections.section_title: Power to recognise or establish marks to denote conformity with standard specifications
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to recognize or establish marks or seals for notified commodities to indicate conformity with standard specifications. Affixing such a mark is deemed evidence of conformity, but customs officers can still examine consignments if they suspect fraud or for other legal purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Power to obtain information from exporters, etc.
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government or authorized officers to require persons manufacturing, dealing in, or exporting notified commodities, and other prescribed persons, to furnish necessary information, returns, or reports.

Covers the finances of the Council, including grants, loans, and donations from the Central Government and approved bodies. It details the Council's fund, its application, preparation of program and financial estimates, maintenance of accounts, and auditing by the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
Grants the Director of Inspection and Quality Control or authorized officers the power to enter and inspect.
Grants the power to conduct searches.
Grants the power to seize commodities and other related items.

main_sections.section_title: Power to stop and seize conveyances
main_sections.description: Grants the power to stop and seize vehicles or other conveyances used in connection with offenses under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Search and seizure to be made in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
main_sections.description: Specifies that search and seizure operations must be conducted in accordance with the procedures laid down in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Details the provisions related to the confiscation of goods or commodities involved in offenses.
Allows for the confiscation of conveyances used in the commission of offenses under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Option to pay fine in lieu of confiscation
main_sections.description: Provides an option for the owner of goods or conveyances to pay a fine instead of facing confiscation.
Establishes liability for penalties in cases of contravention of the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Confiscation or penalty not to interfere with other punishments
main_sections.description: Clarifies that confiscation or imposition of a penalty does not prevent prosecution or punishment under any other law.
Outlines the process of adjudication by an appointed authority.

main_sections.section_title: Giving of opportunity to the owner of goods etc.
main_sections.description: Ensures that the owner of goods, conveyances, or other seized items is given an opportunity to be heard before any confiscation or penalty is imposed.
Provides for the right to appeal against decisions made by the adjudicating authority.
Grants powers of revision to higher authorities over orders passed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of adjudicating and other authorities
main_sections.description: Details the powers vested in the adjudicating and other authorities appointed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of proceedings in the event of death or insolvency
main_sections.description: Ensures that legal proceedings under the Act can continue even in cases of death or insolvency of the parties involved.
Specifies the general penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act or any rules or orders made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of order made by adjudicating authority or Appellate authority
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for failing to comply with orders issued by the adjudicating or appellate authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Offences by officers and employees of agency, etc.
main_sections.description: Addresses offenses committed by officers and employees of agencies established or recognized under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes
main_sections.description: Allows for the correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes in any order passed under the Act.
Lays down provisions for offenses committed by companies, making directors, managers, and other responsible individuals liable.
Empowers the Central Government to delegate its powers and functions under the Act to other officers or authorities.
Specifies the procedure to be followed for initiating prosecutions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and employees of agency to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares that officers and employees of any agency established or recognized under the Act are to be considered public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act or any rules or orders made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension, etc., of operation of the provisions of the Act
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to suspend the operation of certain provisions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Stipulates that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force.

important_rules: Rule: Export of notified commodities is prohibited unless accompanied by a certificate of quality control/inspection or a recognized mark (Section 6(d)).
Rule: Agencies established or recognized under the Act must examine commodities and issue certificates if they meet standards (Section 7(3)).
Rule: Affixing a recognized mark or seal to a notified commodity is deemed evidence of conformity to standard specifications (Section 8(2)).
Rule: Persons manufacturing, dealing in, or exporting notified commodities may be required to furnish information to the Central Government (Section 9).

penalties: General penalty for contravention of the Act, rules, or orders (Section 11).
Penalty for contravention of orders made by adjudicating or appellate authorities (Section 11A).
Specific penalties related to confiscation of goods and conveyances (Sections 10F, 10G).
Liability to pay fine in lieu of confiscation (Section 10H).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, the Director of Inspection and Quality Control, authorized officers, and agencies established or recognized under Section 7.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, search, seizure of commodities and conveyances, adjudication of offenses, imposition of penalties and confiscation, and prosecution. Enforcement also relies on the export certificate system and recognized marks.

rights: Right to appeal against decisions of an agency to an appellate authority (Section 7(4)).
Right to be given an opportunity to be heard before confiscation or penalty (Section 10L).
Right to demand correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes in orders (Section 11C).
duties: Duty of exporters to ensure commodities meet quality standards for export.
Duty of manufacturers, dealers, and exporters to furnish information as required by the Central Government (Section 9).
Duty of officers and employees of agencies to act as public servants (Section 15).
obligations: Obligation to comply with quality control and inspection requirements for notified commodities.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for obtaining export certificates.
Obligation to cooperate with inspection and enforcement authorities.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishing the Export Inspection Council: Central Government notification, appointment of Chairman, ex-officio and nominated members (Section 3).

Procedure for quality control and inspection of notified commodities: Notification of commodities by Central Government, specification of control/inspection type, establishment of standards, requirement of certificate or mark for export (Section 6).
Procedure for obtaining an export certificate: Examination by recognized agencies, issuance of certificate upon satisfaction of standards (Section 7).
Procedure for amendment, suspension, or cancellation of certificates: Agency's belief of fraud or deterioration, opportunity to be heard, prescribed manner and procedure (Section 7(3A)).
Procedure for appeal against agency decisions: Aggrieved person appeals to the constituted appellate authority within a prescribed time (Section 7(4)).
Procedure for adjudication: Adjudicating authority determines liability for penalties and confiscation (Section 10K).
Procedure for prosecution: As prescribed by the Central Government (Section 14).
administration: The Central Government, through various departments and appointed authorities like the Director of Inspection and Quality Control and the Export Inspection Council.
important_notes: The Act's provisions are to override other enactments where there is inconsistency (Section 18).
Actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act are protected (Section 16).
The Central Government can suspend the operation of certain provisions (Section 16A).

title: The Limitation Act, 1963
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law for the limitation of suits and other proceedings and for purposes connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to suits, appeals, and applications.

key_definitions.applicant: Includes a petitioner, any person from or through whom an applicant derives their right to apply, and any person whose estate is represented by the applicant.
key_definitions.bill of exchange: Includes a hundi and a cheque.
key_definitions.bond: Includes any instrument obliging a person to pay money to another, conditional on a specified act being performed or not performed.
key_definitions.defendant: Includes any person from or through whom a defendant derives their liability to be sued, and any person whose estate is represented by the defendant.
key_definitions.easement: Includes a right, not arising from contract, allowing one person to remove and appropriate part of another's soil or things growing on or attached to their land for their own profit.
key_definitions.good faith: Nothing done without due care and attention is deemed to be in good faith.
key_definitions.plaintiff: Includes any person from or through whom a plaintiff derives their right to sue, and any person whose estate is represented by the plaintiff.
key_definitions.period of limitation: The period of limitation prescribed for any suit, appeal, or application by the Schedule.
key_definitions.prescribed period: The period of limitation computed in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.promissory note: Any instrument where the maker engages absolutely to pay a specified sum of money to another at a limited time, on demand, or at sight.
key_definitions.suit: Does not include an appeal or an application.
key_definitions.tort: A civil wrong that is not exclusively a breach of contract or trust.
key_definitions.trustee: Does not include a benamidar, a mortgagee in possession after satisfaction of the mortgage, or a person in wrongful possession without title.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and commencement (to be appointed by the Central Government).
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as applicant, application, defendant, plaintiff, suit, and tort.

Mandates that every suit instituted, appeal preferred, and application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, even if limitation is not set up as a defence. Defines when a suit is instituted and how set-offs and counter-claims are treated.

main_sections.section_title: Expiry of prescribed period when court is closed
main_sections.description: Allows suits, appeals, or applications to be instituted, preferred, or made on the day the court re-opens if the prescribed period expires on a day when the court is closed.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of prescribed period in certain cases
main_sections.description: Allows appeals or applications (other than under Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908) to be admitted after the prescribed period if the appellant or applicant shows sufficient cause.

Deals with the extension of the limitation period for persons who are minors, insane, or idiots at the time the period is to be reckoned, allowing them to sue or apply after the disability ceases. It also covers cases of multiple disabilities and disability continuing until death.

main_sections.section_title: Disability of one of several persons
main_sections.description: Addresses situations where one of several jointly entitled persons has a legal disability. Time may run against all if a discharge can be given without the concurrence of the disabled person, otherwise, time does not run until one becomes capable of giving such discharge or the disability ceases.

Excludes suits to enforce rights of pre-emption from the provisions of sections 6 and 7, and limits the extension for other suits or applications to three years from the cessation of disability or death.
States that once time begins to run, no subsequent disability or inability stops it, with an exception for when letters of administration to a creditor's estate are granted to their debtor.

main_sections.section_title: Suits against trustees and their representatives
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit against a trustee for the purpose of following property vested in trust for a specific purpose, or for an account thereof, shall be barred by any length of time. This includes charitable and religious endowments.

main_sections.section_title: Suits on contracts entered into outside the territories to which the Act extends
main_sections.description: Governs suits on contracts made in Jammu and Kashmir or foreign countries. It stipulates that such suits are subject to this Act, and foreign rules of limitation are not a defence unless they have extinguished the contract and parties were domiciled there.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of time in legal proceedings
main_sections.description: Specifies time to be excluded when computing the period of limitation, including the day from which the period is to be reckoned, time taken to obtain a copy of a decree, judgment, or order for appeal or review, and time to obtain a copy of an award.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of time in cases where leave to sue or appeal as a pauper is applied for
main_sections.description: Allows exclusion of time spent prosecuting an application for leave to sue or appeal as a pauper, even if rejected, provided it was done in good faith.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of time of proceeding bona fide in court without jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Permits exclusion of time spent prosecuting another civil proceeding in good faith in a court lacking jurisdiction, if it relates to the same matter in issue.

important_rules: Every suit, appeal, and application must be filed within the prescribed period; otherwise, it will be dismissed, even if the defence of limitation is not raised.
