If the prescribed period for a suit, appeal, or application expires on a day the court is closed, it can be filed on the day the court reopens.
Appeals or applications may be admitted after the prescribed period if sufficient cause is shown.
For persons under legal disability (minor, insane, idiot), the period of limitation can be extended after the disability ceases.
If time has begun to run, it generally continues to run without stopping due to subsequent disability or inability.
Suits against trustees for specific purposes are not barred by time.
When computing limitation periods for appeals, revisions, or reviews, time taken to obtain copies of judgments or orders is excluded.
Time spent in good faith prosecuting a civil proceeding in a court without jurisdiction can be excluded from the limitation period for a subsequent suit on the same matter.
Acknowledgement of a debt in writing or part payment of a debt or legacy can revive or extend the period of limitation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of law enforce the provisions of this Act by dismissing suits, appeals, or applications filed after the prescribed period.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By judicial application of the time limits set forth in the Act to bar claims that are brought too late.

rights: Right to institute a suit, prefer an appeal, or make an application within the prescribed period.
Right to have the period of limitation extended under certain conditions (e.g., legal disability, sufficient cause for delay, prosecution in a wrong court).
Right to have time excluded in legal proceedings for obtaining copies, etc.
Right to pursue claims against trustees for specific purposes without time bar.
duties: Duty to institute suits, prefer appeals, and make applications within the prescribed periods.
Duty to exercise due diligence in prosecuting legal proceedings.
Duty to act in good faith and with due care and attention.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the time limits set by the Act.
Obligation to present claims within the statutory periods.

key_procedures: Institution of a suit: Generally, when the plaint is presented to the proper officer.
Filing an appeal or application: Must be within the prescribed period, with provisions for extension upon showing sufficient cause.
Computation of limitation period: Involves excluding specific periods as provided in sections 12-17, and considering acknowledgments or payments as per sections 18-20.
Application for leave to sue as a pauper: Time spent prosecuting this application, if rejected, can be excluded.
administration: The Act is administered by the judicial system of India, with courts determining the applicability of limitation periods.
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure that stale claims are not entertained by courts.
It provides a balance between the right of a party to seek justice and the need for legal certainty and finality.
Certain provisions were amended to remove references to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

title: The Administrators-General Act, 1963
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the office and duties of Administrators-General.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. It applies to the administration of estates of deceased persons by the Administrator-General.

key_definitions.assets: All the property, movable and immovable, of a deceased person, which is chargeable with and applicable to the payment of his debts and legacies, or available for distribution among his heirs and next-of-kin.
key_definitions.letters_of_administration: Includes any letters of administration whether general or with a copy of the will annexed or limited in time or otherwise.
key_definitions.next_of_kin: Includes a widower or widow of a deceased person, or any other person who by law would be entitled to letters of administration in preference to a creditor or legatee of the deceased.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement by notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'assets', 'letters of administration', 'next-of-kin', and 'prescribed'.

Outlines the process for the State Government to appoint an Administrator-General, specifying qualifications such as being an advocate, attorney, member of the judicial service, or Deputy Administrator-General for a certain number of years.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and powers of Deputy Administrator-General
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint Deputy Administrators-General to assist the Administrator-General, detailing their powers and qualifications.
Establishes the Administrator-General as a corporation sole with perpetual succession and an official seal, enabling him to sue and be sued in his corporate name.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of High Court for the whole State
main_sections.description: Declares the High Court as a court of competent jurisdiction for granting probate or letters of administration for estates situate anywhere within the State, without prejudice to the jurisdiction of district courts.

main_sections.section_title: Administrator-General entitled to letters of administration, unless granted to next-of-kin
main_sections.description: States that letters of administration shall be granted to the Administrator-General unless they are granted to the next-of-kin of the deceased.

main_sections.section_title: Administrator-General, entitled to letters of administration in preference to creditors, certain legatees or friends
main_sections.description: Grants the Administrator-General the right to letters of administration in preference to creditors, certain legatees, or friends.

main_sections.section_title: Right of Administrator-General to apply for administration of estates
main_sections.description: Allows the Administrator-General to apply for letters of administration for estates exceeding a specified value (currently ten lakhs) if no one has applied within one month of death and other protective measures are not taken, provided there's an apprehension of misappropriation, deterioration, or waste.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Administrator-General to collect and hold assets where immediate action is required
main_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power to direct the Administrator-General to collect and manage assets exceeding a specified value if there's imminent danger of misappropriation, deterioration, or waste, requiring immediate action.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of probate or letters of administration to person appearing in the course of proceedings taken by Administrator-General
main_sections.description: Details how the High Court shall proceed if a person establishes a claim to probate or letters of administration, or shows diligent action for estate protection, during proceedings initiated by the Administrator-General.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of administration to Administrator-General in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies that if no one appears to claim probate or letters of administration, or to demonstrate diligent protection of the estate, within a reasonable period during proceedings initiated by the Administrator-General, the High Court shall grant administration to the Administrator-General.

main_sections.section_title: Recall of Administrator-General’s administration and grant of probate, etc., to executor or next-of-kin
main_sections.description: Allows for the recall of administration granted to the Administrator-General and the subsequent grant of probate or letters of administration to an executor or next-of-kin.
Covers the distribution of assets of an estate under the administration of the Administrator-General.

main_sections.section_title: No security to be required from Administrator-General
main_sections.description: States that no security is required from the Administrator-General for obtaining letters of administration.

main_sections.section_title: In what cases Administrator-General may grant certificate
main_sections.description: Specifies the circumstances under which the Administrator-General can grant a certificate.
Addresses the liability of the Government in relation to the acts of the Administrator-General.
Deals with the fees that may be charged by the Administrator-General.
Mandates the audit of the Administrator-General's accounts.

main_sections.section_title: Assets unclaimed for twelve years to be transferred to Government
main_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of assets that remain unclaimed for twelve years to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules under the Act.
Contains provisions for the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: Rule for appointment of Administrator-General: Must have at least seven years as an advocate or attorney, or ten years in judicial service, or five years as a Deputy Administrator-General.
Rule for appointment of Deputy Administrator-General: Must have at least three years as an advocate, attorney, or member of the judicial service.
Administrator-General is entitled to letters of administration in preference to creditors, certain legatees, or friends.

Administrator-General can apply for administration of estates exceeding ten lakhs if no one else has applied within one month, provided there is an apprehension of misappropriation, deterioration, or waste.
High Court can direct Administrator-General to collect and hold assets if there is imminent danger of misappropriation, deterioration, or waste.
No security is required from the Administrator-General for obtaining letters of administration.
Assets unclaimed for twelve years are to be transferred to the Government.

penalties: Section 50: Punishment for giving false evidence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Administrator-General, High Court, State Government, Central Government (for rules).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings, applications for letters of administration and probate, High Court directions, and enforcement of rules and regulations.

rights: Right to letters of administration in preference to creditors, certain legatees, or friends.
Right to apply for administration of estates in specific circumstances.
Right to collect and hold assets where immediate action is required.
Right to reimbursement for payments made in respect of assets.
Right to retain fees chargeable under rules.
Right to inspect accounts and take copies of the Administrator-General's records for persons beneficially interested.
duties: To administer estates of deceased persons.
To collect and hold assets where immediate action is required.
To obtain letters of administration or probate when necessary.
To distribute assets according to law.
To maintain suits for recovery of assets.
To act under the directions of the High Court when specified.
To have accounts audited.
obligations: Obligation to act diligently for the protection of the estate.
Obligation to comply with High Court directions.
Obligation to surrender revoked certificates.
Obligation to ensure proper accounting and audit of all transactions.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining letters of administration: If no one else applies within one month, and there's an apprehension of misappropriation, deterioration, or waste, the Administrator-General can apply to the High Court for letters of administration.
Procedure for immediate action on assets: In cases of imminent danger to assets, the High Court can direct the Administrator-General to collect, hold, realize, sell, or invest them.
Procedure for recall of administration: An executor or next-of-kin can apply for recall of administration granted to the Administrator-General.
Procedure for granting certificates: Specific cases where the Administrator-General may grant a certificate to creditors and take charge of certain estates.
Procedure for recovering unclaimed assets: Claimants can recover principal money transferred to the Government after it has been unclaimed for twelve years.
administration: The Administrator-General of the respective State, under the supervision of the State Government and the Central Government for rule-making powers. Audit is conducted by auditors appointed to examine accounts and report to the Government.
important_notes: The Act was amended to remove the exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The monetary value for the threshold of assets requiring administration has been revised (e.g., from two lakhs to ten lakhs).
The Act does not affect the provisions of the Army and Air Force (Disposal of Private Property) Act, 1950, or the Navy Act, 1957.
Provisions of the Police Acts for presidency-towns are saved.
Letters of administration may not be necessary for small estates administered by the Administrator-General in accordance with certain other Acts.

title: The Specific Relief Act, 1963
purpose: To define and amend the law relating to certain kinds of specific relief.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and governs the provision of specific relief, focusing on enforcing individual civil rights rather than penal laws. It covers various aspects of contract enforcement, property recovery, and injunctions.

key_definitions.obligation: Includes every duty enforceable by law.
key_definitions.settlement: An instrument (other than a will or codicil) whereby the destination or devolution of successive interests in movable or immovable property is disposed of or agreed to be disposed of.
key_definitions.trust: Has the same meaning as in section 3 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and includes an obligation in the nature of a trust.
key_definitions.trustee: Includes every person holding property in trust.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of commencement.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'obligation', 'settlement', 'trust', and 'trustee'.
States that the Act does not deprive any person of other reliefs available under any contract or affect the operation of the Indian Registration Act, 1908.

main_sections.section_title: Specific relief to be granted only for enforcing individual civil rights and not for enforcing penal laws
main_sections.description: Clarifies that specific relief is granted to enforce individual civil rights and not for enforcing penal laws.
Provides for the recovery of specific immovable property by a person entitled to its possession, as per the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

main_sections.section_title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property
main_sections.description: Allows a person dispossessed of immovable property without consent and not in due course of law to recover possession. It outlines limitations and bars to such suits.

Enables recovery of specific movable property by a person entitled to its possession, as per the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Includes explanations regarding trustees and temporary rights to possession.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of person in possession, not as owner, to deliver to persons entitled to immediate possession
main_sections.description: Details circumstances under which a person in possession of movable property, who is not the owner, can be compelled to deliver it to the rightful possessor.

main_sections.section_title: Specific performance in respect of contracts
main_sections.description: States that specific performance of a contract shall be enforced subject to certain provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Cases in which specific performance of contracts connected with trusts enforceable
main_sections.description: Specifies that specific performance can be enforced when the act is in performance wholly or partly of a trust, but not if it's in excess of a trustee's powers or in breach of trust.

main_sections.section_title: Specific performance of part of contract
main_sections.description: Outlines conditions under which specific performance of only a part of a contract can be directed, including compensation for the deficiency.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of purchaser or lessee against person with no title or imperfect title
main_sections.description: Defines the rights of a purchaser or lessee when the vendor or lessor has no title or an imperfect title.
Lists categories of contracts that cannot be specifically enforced, such as those involving substituted performance or continuous duties that the court cannot supervise.
Deals with the circumstances under which an instrument can be rectified.

main_sections.section_title: When rescission may be adjudged or refused
main_sections.description: Explains when rescission of a contract may be granted or denied.
Specifies the conditions under which cancellation of an instrument may be ordered.

main_sections.section_title: Discretion of court as to declaration of status or right
main_sections.description: Grants discretion to the court regarding declarations of status or right.
Distinguishes between temporary and perpetual injunctions.
Outlines the conditions under which a perpetual injunction may be granted.
Deals with the issuance of mandatory injunctions.
Lists the circumstances under which an injunction will be refused.

important_rules: Specific relief is to be granted only for enforcing individual civil rights and not for enforcing penal laws.
Specific performance of a contract shall be enforced subject to certain provisions of the Act.
Specific performance of a contract can be enforced when the act agreed to be done is in performance wholly or partly of a trust, unless it's in excess of trustee's powers or in breach of trust.
Generally, the court shall not direct specific performance of only a part of a contract, but exceptions exist with compensation.
If a vendor or lessor lacks title or has an imperfect title, the purchaser or lessee has specific rights, including compelling the vendor to acquire title or get necessary concurrence from others.

penalties: The provided text does not explicitly detail specific monetary penalties or imprisonment for violations of this Act. Enforcement relies on the court's power to grant specific relief, injunctions, and compensation as outlined in the various sections.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of law in India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial orders for specific performance of contracts, recovery of property, rectification, rescission, cancellation of instruments, and granting injunctions. Enforcement is facilitated by adherence to procedures laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

rights: Right to recover specific immovable property.
Right to recover possession of immovable property if dispossessed without consent and not in due course of law.
Right to recover specific movable property.
Rights of a purchaser or lessee against a vendor or lessor with no title or imperfect title.
Right to specific performance of a contract.
Right to seek rectification, rescission, cancellation of instruments.
Right to seek declaratory decrees.
Right to preventive relief through injunctions.
duties: Duty to perform contracts as agreed.
Duty of a trustee to act in accordance with trust provisions.
Duty to deliver movable property if held as agent or trustee or when compensation is inadequate.
Duty to restore benefits or make compensation when an instrument is cancelled or resisted as void/voidable.
obligations: Every duty enforceable by law is considered an 'obligation' under this Act.

key_procedures: Filing a suit for recovery of specific immovable or movable property.
Filing a suit for specific performance of a contract, with defenses available to the defendant.
Seeking rectification of instruments based on fraud or mutual mistake.
Applying for rescission of contracts under specific circumstances.
Seeking cancellation of instruments that are void or voidable.
Applying for declaratory decrees regarding status or right.
Seeking temporary and perpetual injunctions to prevent breaches of obligations.
administration: The administration of this Act is primarily handled by the judicial system of India, with courts of law empowered to grant the specific reliefs provided.
important_notes: The Act specifies that specific relief is granted to enforce individual civil rights, not penal laws.
The extent of the Act was originally the whole of India, with specific omission of the State of Jammu and Kashmir through an amendment in 2019.
The Act came into force on March 1, 1964.
Sections 43 and 44 have been repealed.

title: The Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963
purpose: To provide for the constitution of separate Boards of Revenue for Direct Taxes and for Indirect Taxes and Customs, and to amend certain enactments for the purpose of conferring powers and imposing duties on the said Boards.
scope: This Act applies to the Central Government and establishes two new Boards: the Central Board of Direct Taxes and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs. It supersedes the previous Central Board of Revenue. The scope covers matters related to direct taxes, indirect taxes, and customs.

key_definitions.Board: Means the Central Board of Direct Taxes or the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Central Board of Revenue: Means the Central Board of Revenue constituted under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1924 (4 of 1924).
key_definitions.direct tax: Includes duties or taxes leviable under various specific acts such as the Estate Duty Act, 1953; Wealth-tax Act, 1957; Expenditure-tax Act, 1957; Gift-tax Act, 1958; Income-tax Act, 1961; Super Profits Tax Act, 1963; Interest-tax Act, 1974; Hotel-Receipts Tax Act, 1980; Expenditure-tax Act, 1987; and Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015. It also includes any other duty or tax declared as direct tax by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963' and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Central Board of Revenue', and 'direct tax'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of separate Central Boards for Direct Taxes and for Indirect Taxes and Customs
main_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute two separate Boards of Revenue, the Central Board of Direct Taxes and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, in place of the previous Central Board of Revenue. Each Board will exercise powers and perform duties entrusted to them by the Central Government or by law. Each Board can consist of up to seven members.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for regulating the transaction of business by each Board. Any order or act done according to these rules will be considered the order or act of the Board. Rules made under this section must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specific period, allowing for modification or annulment.

Amends various tax-related enactments to substitute references to the 'Central Board of Revenue' with the 'Central Board of Direct Taxes' or 'the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs'. It also clarifies the transfer of functions related to direct taxes and other matters to the respective Boards.

Specifies the transfer of proceedings pending before the Central Board of Revenue at the commencement of the Act to either the Central Board of Direct Taxes or the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, depending on whether the proceeding relates to direct taxes or other matters. It also provides a mechanism for resolving disputes regarding such transfers and deals with the substitution of Boards in pending legal proceedings.

Grants the Central Government the power to issue orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act's purposes. These orders can have retrospective effect.

Repeals the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1924. It also includes a saving clause to ensure that all appointments, assessments, orders, rules, exemptions, notices, penalties, etc., made by the previous Central Board of Revenue are deemed to have been made by the newly constituted Boards and continue in force until revised or superseded.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (through the newly constituted Boards of Revenue)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers and duties conferred upon the Central Boards of Direct Taxes and Indirect Taxes and Customs by this Act and other amended enactments. The Central Government can also issue orders to remove difficulties.

duties: The Central Government has the duty to constitute the Central Board of Direct Taxes and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs.
Each Board has the duty to exercise such powers and perform such duties as may be entrusted to it by the Central Government or by or under any law.
The Central Government has the duty to make rules for regulating the transaction of business by each Board.
Both Houses of Parliament have the right to discuss and modify rules made by the Central Government regarding the procedure of the Boards.

key_procedures: Constitution of Boards: The Central Government constitutes the Central Board of Direct Taxes and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs in place of the Central Board of Revenue.
Regulation of Business: The Central Government may make rules for regulating the transaction of business by each Board. These rules are subject to parliamentary review.
Transfer of Proceedings: Pending proceedings before the old Central Board of Revenue are transferred to the appropriate new Board (Direct Taxes or Indirect Taxes and Customs).
Substitution in Legal Proceedings: In legal proceedings where the Central Board of Revenue was a party, the new respective Board is substituted.
Removal of Difficulties: The Central Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.
administration: Central Government (specifically through the Ministry of Finance and the newly constituted Central Boards of Direct Taxes and Indirect Taxes and Customs)
important_notes: The Act came into force on January 1, 1964.
The Central Board of Revenue Act, 1924, has been repealed.
Amendments made by the Act are effective from dates specified in the amending acts, e.g., Act 13 of 2018 has amendments effective from 29-3-2018.

title: The Official Languages Act, 1963
purpose: To provide for the languages which may be used for the official purposes of the Union, for the transaction of business in Parliament, for Central and State Acts and for certain purposes in High Courts.
scope: This Act applies to the official purposes of the Union, the transaction of business in Parliament, Central and State Acts, and certain matters in High Courts. It also covers communication between the Union and States, and between different government entities and corporations controlled by the Union.

key_definitions.appointed day: In relation to section 3, it means the 26th day of January, 1965. In relation to any other provision, it means the day on which that provision comes into force.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for its provisions, with Section 3 coming into force on January 26, 1965, and other provisions on dates appointed by the Central Government.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day' and 'Hindi'.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of English language for official purposes of the Union and for use in Parliament
main_sections.description: Allows the continued use of English for official purposes of the Union and in Parliament, in addition to Hindi, even after the initial fifteen-year period from the Constitution's commencement. It outlines conditions for communication between the Union and States based on their adoption of Hindi and specifies rules for communication within the Central Government and related entities. It also details the use of both Hindi and English for various official documents and communications, and provides for the Central Government to make rules regarding language use, ensuring efficient disposal of business and effective functioning of personnel proficient in either Hindi or English.

Mandates the constitution of a Committee on Official Language after ten years from the commencement of Section 3 to review the progress of Hindi's use for official purposes of the Union, submit a report with recommendations to the President, who will lay it before Parliament and send it to State Governments. The President may issue directions based on the report and State Governments' views, provided they are consistent with Section 3.

main_sections.section_title: Authorised Hindi translations of Central Acts, etc.
main_sections.description: Declares that Hindi translations published under the President's authority in the Official Gazette on or after the appointed day of Central Acts, Ordinances, orders, rules, regulations, or bye-laws will be the authoritative Hindi texts. It also requires that all Bills introduced in Parliament and amendments thereto be accompanied by an authorized Hindi translation.

main_sections.section_title: Authorised Hindi translation of State Acts in certain cases
main_sections.description: Provides for the publication of authorized Hindi translations of State Acts and Ordinances, in addition to English translations, where the State Legislature has prescribed a language other than Hindi. These Hindi translations will be considered authoritative.

main_sections.section_title: Optional use of Hindi or other official language in judgments, etc., of High Courts
main_sections.description: Empowers the Governor of a State, with the President's consent, to authorize the use of Hindi or the State's official language, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees, or orders of the High Court. Such judgments in a language other than English must be accompanied by an English translation.

Grants the Central Government the power to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, for carrying out the purposes of the Act. These rules are subject to parliamentary approval and modification.

main_sections.section_title: [Certain provisions not to apply to Jammu and Kashmir .]
main_sections.description: This section has been omitted.

important_rules: Rule 1: Section 3(1) states that English can continue to be used for official purposes of the Union and for the transaction of business in Parliament, in addition to Hindi, from the appointed day.
Rule 2: Communication between the Union and a State that has not adopted Hindi as its official language must use English.
Rule 3: Communication in Hindi between states that have adopted Hindi and those that haven't, must be accompanied by an English translation.

Rule 4: Section 3(3) mandates that both Hindi and English shall be used for resolutions, general orders, rules, notifications, administrative reports, press communiques, reports and official papers laid before Parliament, and contracts, agreements, licenses, permits, notices, and tender forms.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for making rules and appointing commencement dates), President (for issuing directions based on the Committee's report), Governors of States (with President's consent for High Court judgments).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette, parliamentary resolutions, and presidential directions. Rules made by the Central Government are subject to parliamentary scrutiny.

rights: Right to use English for official purposes of the Union and in Parliament (in addition to Hindi).
Right of states not adopting Hindi to use Hindi for communication with the Union or with states that have adopted Hindi, or by agreement with other states, without obligation to use English.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to appoint commencement dates for provisions of the Act.
Duty of the Central Government to give due consideration to quick and efficient disposal of official business and the interests of the general public when making rules under Section 3(4).

Duty of the Central Government to ensure that persons serving in connection with the affairs of the Union are not placed at a disadvantage due to proficiency in only one of the languages (Hindi or English).
obligations: Obligation for communication between Union and non-Hindi adopting states to be in English.
Obligation to accompany Hindi communications between states with an English translation if one state has not adopted Hindi.
Obligation to use both Hindi and English for specified official documents and communications (Section 3(3)).
Obligation to provide an English translation for communications within the Central Government and its entities if one party lacks working knowledge of Hindi.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Committee on Official Language: Moved by a resolution in either House of Parliament with Presidential sanction and passed by both Houses, after ten years from the commencement of Section 3.

Review and Reporting by the Committee on Official Language: Review progress of Hindi use, submit a report with recommendations to the President, who lays it before Parliament and sends it to State Governments.
Issuance of Directions by the President: Based on the Committee's report and State Governments' views.
Rule-making by the Central Government: By notification in the Official Gazette, with rules subject to parliamentary modification or annulment.
Authorization of Hindi Translations: By the President for Central Acts and subordinate legislation, and by Governors for State Acts (with provisions for High Court judgments).
administration: Central Government (for overall administration, rule-making, and appointing dates), President (for issuing directions based on the Committee's report), Governors of States (with Presidential consent for High Court matters).
important_notes: The provisions of Section 3(1)(a), Section 3(2), Section 3(3), and Section 3(4) will remain in force until resolutions for the discontinuance of English are passed by the Legislatures of all non-Hindi adopting States and subsequently by both Houses of Parliament.
Section 9, concerning the application to Jammu and Kashmir, has been omitted.

title: THE TEXTILES COMMITTEE ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Committee for ensuring the quality of textiles and textile machinery and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to textiles, textile machinery, and related industries.

key_definitions.Committee: The Textiles Committee established under section 3.
key_definitions.fiber: Man-made fiber including regenerated cellulose rayon, nylon and the like.
key_definitions.handloom industries: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Khadi and Other Handloom Industries Development (Additional Excise, Duty on Cloth) Act, 1953 (12 of 1953).
key_definitions.powerloom: A loom which is worked by power and is used or capable of being used only for weaving cloth wholly or partly out of cotton yarn or woollen yarn, or fiber, or any kind of mixed yarn.
key_definitions.powerloom industry: An industry in which a manufacturer of textiles has, at any time during the period fixed by the Committee under clause (a) of sub-section (5) of section 5A, not more than fifty power looms (without any spinning plants) in the factory or factories owned, controlled or managed by him.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.textile machinery: The equipment employed directly or indirectly for the processing of textile fiber into yarn and for the manufacture of fabric therefrom by weaving or knitting and includes equipment used either wholly or partly for the finishing, folding, or packing of textiles.
key_definitions.textiles: Any fabric or cloth or yarn or garment or any other article made wholly or in part of cotton, wool, silk, artificial silk or other fiber, and includes fiber.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and when it comes into force.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act.
Details the establishment of the Textiles Committee as a body corporate, its headquarters, and its composition.
Outlines the general and specific functions of the Committee, including research, promotion, standard setting, quality control, inspection, testing, and data collection.
Grants the Committee the necessary powers to carry out its functions.

main_sections.section_title: Imposition of cess on textiles and textile machinery manufactured in India
main_sections.description: Provides for the levy and collection of a duty of excise (cess) on textiles and textile machinery manufactured in India for the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to constitute a Tribunal to hear appeals against assessments of the cess.
Specifies the procedure for hearing appeals by the Tribunal, including time limits, fees, and the powers of the Tribunal.
Details the procedure for recovering the duty of excise if not paid by the manufacturer.
Grants the Central Government the power to exempt certain textiles or textile machinery from the duty of excise.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of proceeds of cess to the Committee
main_sections.description: Describes how the proceeds of the duty of excise are credited and disbursed to the Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Grants by Central Government to the Committee
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to provide grants to the Committee for its functions.
Provides for the constitution of a Fund for the Committee.
Empowers the Committee to conduct inspections.
Deals with the accounts and audit of the Committee.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous enactments and saving provisions.

important_rules: Manufacturers of textiles and textile machinery are required to pay a duty of excise (cess) at a rate fixed by the Central Government, not exceeding one percent ad valorem, for the purposes of the Act.
The duty of excise levied under Section 5A is in addition to any other cess or duty leviable under any other law.
Manufacturers must furnish returns to the Committee regarding the quantity of textiles or textile machinery manufactured.
Manufacturers have the right to appeal to the Tribunal against any assessment made by the Committee.
The Tribunal's orders are final and are to be sent to the appellant and the Committee.

penalties: Failure to pay the duty of excise within the specified period or after the disposal of an appeal results in the duty being recoverable as an arrear of land revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Textiles Committee, supported by the Central Government and the Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy and collection of cess, inspections, audits, and legal recovery of dues. The Tribunal handles appeals against assessments. The Central Government has powers to make rules and notifications for enforcement.

rights: Manufacturers aggrieved by an assessment have the right to appeal to the Tribunal.
Manufacturers have the right to be heard by the Tribunal in appeal proceedings.
duties: Manufacturers have a duty to pay the levied duty of excise.
Manufacturers have a duty to furnish returns regarding their production.
obligations: The Central Government has the obligation to establish the Textiles Committee and provide grants.
The Committee has an obligation to ensure standard qualities of textiles and textile machinery.
The Tribunal has an obligation to hear and decide appeals fairly.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Textiles Committee by the Central Government through notification.
Levy and collection of cess on textiles and textile machinery by the Committee.
Submission of returns by manufacturers to the Committee for assessment.
Appeals against assessment by manufacturers to a Tribunal constituted by the Central Government.
Hearing of appeals by the Tribunal, with provisions for opportunity to be heard and final orders.
Recovery of unpaid duty of excise as an arrear of land revenue.
administration: The Central Government establishes and oversees the Textiles Committee. The Committee is responsible for its day-to-day functions and administration.
important_notes: The Act was amended to include the State of Jammu and Kashmir within its extent.
The cess levied is for the purposes of the Act, and its proceeds are to be paid to the Committee after deduction of collection costs.
The Central Government can exempt certain varieties of textiles or textile machinery from the duty of excise in the interest of trade or public interest.

title: The Taxation Laws (Continuation and Validation of Recovery Proceedings) Act, 1964
purpose: To provide for the continuation and validation of proceedings in relation to Government dues and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to any 'scheduled Act' which are Central Acts providing for the imposition or levy of any tax or duty. It covers proceedings related to Government dues, including taxes, duties, penalties, fines, and interest payable to the Government by an assessee under these scheduled Acts. The Act has retrospective effect, applying to notices of demand served before or after its commencement.

key_definitions.assessee: A person liable to pay tax or any other sum under a scheduled Act. For specific Acts like the Excess Profits Tax Act or Business Profits Tax Act, it refers to the person by whom the tax is payable. For the Estate Duty Act, it means an accountable person. For other scheduled Acts, it means an assessee as defined in that Act.
key_definitions.government_dues: Any tax, duty, penalty, fine, interest, annuity deposit, or any other sum payable to the Government by an assessee under a scheduled Act.
key_definitions.scheduled_act: An Act specified in the Schedule of this Act. The Schedule lists various taxation laws.
key_definitions.taxing_authority: An officer empowered to serve a notice of demand for Government dues under a scheduled Act.
key_definitions.tax_recovery_officer: A Tax Recovery Officer as defined in a scheduled Act, or if not defined, an officer to whom a certificate for the recovery of arrears of Government dues may be issued.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Taxation Laws (Continuation and Validation of Recovery Proceedings) Act, 1964'.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'assessee', 'Government dues', 'scheduled Act', 'Taxing Authority', and 'Tax Recovery Officer'.

main_sections.section_title: Continuation and validation of certain proceedings
main_sections.description: Deals with the continuation and validation of proceedings for Government dues when appeals or other proceedings are filed. It specifies how proceedings should continue if dues are enhanced or reduced, and clarifies that no fresh notice of demand is necessary in certain cases. It also states that these provisions have effect notwithstanding any court judgment.
Grants the Central Government the power to amend the Schedule by adding names of Central Acts providing for the imposition or levy of any tax or duty.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall apply and be deemed always to have applied to notices of demand served before or after the commencement of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. It also outlines the procedure for laying rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.

important_rules: Rule: If Government dues are enhanced after an appeal, the Taxing Authority must serve a fresh demand notice only for the enhanced amount. Proceedings can continue from the stage before disposal of the appeal without a fresh notice for the original amount.

Rule: If Government dues are reduced after an appeal, no fresh notice of demand is necessary. The Taxing Authority must inform the assessee and the Tax Recovery Officer (if a certificate was issued) of the reduction. Proceedings can continue for the reduced amount from the stage before disposal of the appeal.

Rule: Proceedings related to Government dues, including penalties and interest, will not be invalid solely due to the absence of a fresh demand notice after an appeal, or due to enhancement or reduction of dues in an appeal.

Rule: If, as a result of a final order, Government dues are reduced and the penalty exceeds the reduced amount, the excess penalty will not be recovered and will be refunded if already recovered, upon application.

Rule: If the penalty for failure to make an annuity deposit exceeds half the required annuity deposit amount, the excess penalty will not be recovered and will be refunded if already recovered, upon application.
Rule: Refunds of Government dues reduced by an appeal or proceeding must be made according to the provisions of the respective scheduled Act.

penalties: Excess penalty not to be recovered or to be refunded if already recovered, if Government dues are reduced and the penalty exceeds the reduced amount (other than annuity deposit).
Excess penalty for failure to make annuity deposit not to be recovered or to be refunded if already recovered, if it exceeds one-half of the required annuity deposit amount.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Taxing Authority and Tax Recovery Officer, as defined under the respective scheduled Acts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the continuation and validation of recovery proceedings for Government dues. Enforcement involves serving notices of demand, continuing existing proceedings, and making refunds where applicable. The Act overrides existing court orders to ensure its provisions are effective.

rights: Right to receive a refund of excess penalty if Government dues are reduced and the penalty exceeds the reduced amount.
Right to receive a refund of excess penalty for annuity deposit failure if it exceeds half the required deposit amount.
Right to receive a refund of any reduced Government dues in accordance with the provisions of the relevant scheduled Act.
duties: Duty of the Taxing Authority to serve a fresh notice of demand only for the enhanced amount of Government dues if they are increased after an appeal or proceeding.
Duty of the Taxing Authority to intimate the reduction of Government dues to the assessee and the Tax Recovery Officer (if applicable) when dues are reduced after an appeal or proceeding.
Duty to comply with rules made by the Central Government under the Act.
Duty to apply to the Taxing Authority for refund of excess penalty or Government dues within the prescribed time and manner.
obligations: Obligation to pay Government dues as determined under the scheduled Acts.
Obligation to comply with the provisions of this Act, which validates and continues recovery proceedings.

key_procedures: Procedure for continuation of proceedings after appeal/other proceeding: If Government dues are enhanced, a fresh demand notice for the enhanced amount is issued, and proceedings continue from the previous stage. If reduced, no fresh notice is needed, but intimation is given, and proceedings continue for the reduced amount.

Procedure for recovery of excess penalty or Government dues: An assessee must apply to the Taxing Authority within a prescribed time and manner for refunds of excess penalty or Government dues resulting from a final order.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for administering the Act, including amending the Schedule, removing difficulties, and making rules.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect and applies to notices of demand served before or after its commencement.
The provisions of Section 3 have effect notwithstanding any judgment, decree, or order of any court, tribunal, or other authority.
The Central Government can add new Acts to the Schedule, thereby bringing them under the purview of this Act.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.

title: THE DAKSHINA BHARAT HINDI PRACHAR SABHA ACT, 1964
purpose: To declare the institution known as the Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha as an institution of national importance and to provide for certain matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha, an institution with its registered office at Madras. Its scope is national importance concerning the promotion of Hindi.

key_definitions.memorandum: The memorandum of association of the Sabha filed with the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies, Madras, under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.rules and regulations: Includes any rule or regulation, by whatever name called, which the Sabha is competent to make under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, but excludes bye-laws or standing orders made for the conduct of its work.
key_definitions.Sabha: The Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha Act, 1964, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Defines 'memorandum', 'rules and regulations', and 'Sabha' as used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of the Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha as an institution of national importance.
main_sections.description: Declares the Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha as an institution of national importance.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of degrees, diplomas and certificates by the Sabha.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Sabha to hold examinations and grant degrees, diplomas, and certificates for proficiency in Hindi or the teaching of Hindi, notwithstanding provisions in the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, or other laws.

Mandates the Sabha to maintain proper accounts, prepare annual statements of accounts, and have its accounts audited annually by a chartered accountant. It also outlines auditor access to records and the submission of audit reports to the Sabha and the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Prior approval of the Central Government necessary for certain action by the Sabha.
main_sections.description: Requires the previous approval of the Central Government for the Sabha to alter its purposes, amalgamate, alter its memorandum or rules and regulations, or be dissolved, notwithstanding the Societies Registration Act, 1860, or its own memorandum or rules.

Allows the Central Government to constitute committees to review and evaluate the Sabha's work. It outlines the Sabha's obligation to cooperate, the process for submitting reports, the Sabha's right to appoint a representative, the procedure for addressing findings to the Sabha's President, and the Central Government's power to issue directions if satisfactory action is not taken. It also details the payment of allowances and expenses from the Sabha's funds.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha is declared an institution of national importance (Section 3).
Rule 2: The Sabha may grant degrees, diplomas, and certificates in Hindi proficiency and teaching, irrespective of other laws (Section 4).
Rule 3: The Sabha must maintain proper accounts and have them audited annually by a chartered accountant, with reports submitted to the Central Government (Section 5).
Rule 4: Certain actions by the Sabha, including altering its purpose, amalgamating, amending its constitution, or dissolution, require prior approval from the Central Government (Section 6).
Rule 5: The Central Government can review and evaluate the Sabha's work and issue directions if necessary, which the Sabha must comply with (Section 7).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directives issued by the Central Government if the Sabha fails to take satisfactory action after a review, and by requiring compliance with these directions.

rights: The Sabha has the right to hold examinations and grant degrees, diplomas, and certificates in Hindi proficiency and teaching (Section 4).
The Sabha is entitled to appoint a representative who has the right to be present and heard at reviews or evaluations conducted by committees (Section 7(4)).
duties: The Sabha must maintain proper accounts and have them audited annually (Section 5(1) & (2)).
The Sabha must afford all necessary facilities to committees constituted for reviewing its work (Section 7(2)).
The Sabha shall comply with directions issued by the Central Government under Section 7(6).
The Sabha shall pay the allowances and expenses of committees constituted by the Central Government for reviewing its work out of its own funds (Section 7(7)).
obligations: To obtain prior approval from the Central Government for significant actions like altering purposes, amalgamation, amending its memorandum or rules, or dissolution (Section 6).
To comply with any directions issued by the Central Government following a review of its work, even if it conflicts with existing laws or its own rules (Section 7(6)).

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Commencement of the Act: The Central Government appoints a date for the Act to come into force via notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).
Procedure 2: Audit and Reporting: The Sabha's accounts are audited annually by a chartered accountant. The auditors submit a report to the Sabha and a copy to the Central Government (Section 5).

Procedure 3: Review and Evaluation: The Central Government may form committees to review and evaluate the Sabha's work. The Sabha must cooperate and can appoint a representative. If the Sabha doesn't take satisfactory action on review findings, the Central Government can issue directions that the Sabha must comply with (Section 7).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act overrides the Societies Registration Act, 1860, and the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, in specific areas concerning the Sabha's functioning and powers (Sections 4 and 6).
The financial implications of the review committees, including allowances and expenses, are to be borne by the Sabha's funds, with prior approval from the Central Government (Section 7(7)).
The Act grants significant oversight and directive powers to the Central Government over the functioning of the Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha.

title: THE LEGAL TENDER (INSCRIBED NOTES) ACT, 1964
purpose: To restrict the negotiability of currency and other notes inscribed with messages of a political character.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to currency notes of the Government of India, bank notes issued by the Reserve Bank of India, and Government of India one-rupee notes that bear extrinsic words or visible representations intended to convey or capable of conveying a message of a political character.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the 'Legal Tender (Inscribed Notes) Act, 1964' and states that it extends to the whole of India.

main_sections.section_title: Notes bearing messages of a political character not to be legal tender.
main_sections.description: This section declares that currency notes or bank notes bearing written words or visible representations of a political character are not to be considered legal tender. It also clarifies that the Reserve Bank of India has no legal obligation to accept such notes or exchange them for other currency, although it may refund their value as an act of grace.

This section repeals the 'Legal Tender (Inscribed Notes) Ordinance, 1942' and includes a savings clause stating that any actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the current Act.

important_rules: Currency notes or bank notes bearing messages of a political character are not to be considered legal tender.
The Reserve Bank of India is not legally obligated to accept notes with political messages or to exchange them for other currency.
The Reserve Bank of India may, at its discretion (as of grace), refund the whole or part of the value of such inscribed notes.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Reserve Bank of India
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By refusing to accept notes with political inscriptions as legal tender and not being obligated to exchange them.

rights: Holders of currency notes that do not bear political messages have the right to their legal tender status.
duties: Citizens have a duty not to inscribe political messages on currency notes.
obligations: The Reserve Bank of India has no legal obligation to accept notes with political messages.
The Reserve Bank of India has no legal obligation to exchange notes with political messages for other currency or to refund their value, except as an act of grace.

key_procedures: When a currency note or bank note is presented with inscribed political messages, it is to be deemed non-legal tender.
The Reserve Bank of India is to refuse acceptance and exchange of such notes, unless it chooses to refund the value as an act of grace.
administration: The Reserve Bank of India is the primary body concerned with the implementation of this act.
important_notes: The Act overrides provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and the Currency Ordinance, 1940, in relation to inscribed notes.
Actions taken under the repealed Legal Tender (Inscribed Notes) Ordinance, 1942, are considered valid under this Act.

title: THE FOOD CORPORATIONS ACT, 1964
purpose: To provide for the establishment of Food Corporations for the purpose of trading in foodgrains and other foodstuffs and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It establishes the Food Corporation of India and provides for the establishment of State Food Corporations. Its subject matter scope covers trading in foodgrains and other foodstuffs.

key_definitions.Corporation: The Food Corporation of India established under section 3.
key_definitions.Food Corporation: The Food Corporation of India established under section 3 or a State Food Corporation established under section 17.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.scheduled bank: A bank for the time being included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934).
key_definitions.State Food Corporation: A State Food Corporation established under section 17.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Food Corporations Act, 1964, its extent to the whole of India, and the provision for its commencement by notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Corporation', 'Food Corporation', 'foodstuffs', 'prescribed', 'scheduled bank', 'State Food Corporation', and 'year'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Food Corporation of India
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish the Food Corporation of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract. It can sue and be sued in its name.

Specifies that the head office of the Corporation shall be at Madras or such other place as the Central Government may specify. It also allows the Corporation to establish offices or agencies at other places in or outside India with prior Central Government approval for locations outside India.

Details the capital structure of the Corporation, stating the original capital is a sum not exceeding one hundred crores of rupees fixed by the Central Government, which can be increased by the Central Government from time to time. Capital is provided by the Central Government via parliamentary appropriation.

States that the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Corporation's affairs vest in a board of directors. The board acts on business principles, considers producer and consumer interests, and is guided by instructions from the Central Government on policy matters. The Central Government's decision on policy questions is final.

Outlines the composition of the board of directors, including a Chairman, directors representing relevant Central Government ministries, the managing director of the Central Warehousing Corporation, a managing director of the Food Corporation, and six other directors. Most directors are appointed by the Central Government.
This section title indicates it defines the core functions of the Corporation. Specific details of these functions are not provided in the excerpt.
This section title indicates the provision for establishing State Food Corporations.

main_sections.section_title: Submission of programme of activities and financial estimates
main_sections.description: This section title indicates the requirement for submitting work plans and financial projections.
This section title indicates provisions related to the maintenance of accounts and their auditing.
This section title indicates the power of the Central Government to make rules under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Food Corporation to make regulations
main_sections.description: This section title indicates the power of the Food Corporation to make its own regulations.

important_rules: Directors are disqualified if they are adjudicated insolvent, of unsound mind, convicted of an offense involving moral turpitude (in the opinion of the Central Government), removed/dismissed from government service, or are salaried officials of a Food Corporation (except Chairman/MD).
The Central Government can remove the managing director after giving an opportunity to show cause.
The board of directors can remove a director if they become disqualified or are absent from three consecutive meetings without sufficient cause.
Directors can resign by giving written notice to the Central Government.
Board meetings require a quorum and decisions are made by majority vote, with the Chairman having a casting vote.
The Central Government may constitute Advisory Committees to advise it or the Corporation on matters related to the Act's purposes.

Government employees performing functions now assigned to the Corporation can be transferred to the Corporation under specific conditions, allowing them to opt for either government or corporation service terms.
The Central Government can make rules under the Act.
The Food Corporation can make regulations for its own governance and operations.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Board of Directors of the Food Corporation of India, and potentially State Governments for State Food Corporations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appointment of directors, issuance of notifications, making rules, and oversight of the Corporation's functioning. The Act also mentions provisions for winding up the Corporation, implying enforcement of its dissolution.

rights: Right of the Corporation to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right of the Corporation to contract.
Right of the Corporation to sue and be sued.
Right of directors to resign.
Right of transferred government employees to exercise an option regarding their service conditions.
Right of the Corporation to appoint its officers and employees.
duties: Duty of the board of directors to act on business principles, considering producer and consumer interests.
Duty of Advisory Committees to advise the Central Government or the Corporation.
Duty of transferred government employees to make an option regarding their service conditions.
Duty of the Corporation to maintain accounts and get them audited.
Duty to prepare and submit annual reports on the working of the Food Corporations.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to establish the Food Corporation of India.
Obligation of the Central Government to appoint the Secretary of the Corporation.
Obligation of the Corporation to meet expenses of Advisory Committees.
Obligation to submit programme of activities and financial estimates.
Obligation to adhere to rules and regulations made under the Act.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Food Corporation of India by the Central Government via notification.
Appointment of directors to the Board of Directors by the Central Government.
Removal of directors by the Central Government or the Board of Directors, with a process of showing cause for the managing director.
Conducting meetings of the Board of Directors according to prescribed procedures.
Transfer of Government employees to the Corporation, requiring notification and allowing employees to opt out.
Transferred employees exercising an option for pay scales and terminal benefits within a specified timeframe.
Submission of programmes of activities and financial estimates by the Corporation.
Auditing of accounts of the Corporation.
Preparation and submission of annual reports.
Winding up of the Corporation as per the Act's provisions.
Making of rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Corporation.
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative body, responsible for establishing the Corporation, appointing its key personnel, and making rules. The Board of Directors manages the Corporation's day-to-day affairs, guided by the Central Government on policy.
important_notes: The Act was initially not extended to the State of Jammu and Kashmir but this omission was later removed.

The Act allows for the transfer of Government employees to the Corporation, with provisions for them to choose between government and corporation service conditions. This includes options for pay scales and terminal benefits.
The Act includes a section on the 'Validation' of certain acts or proceedings, suggesting that there might have been past issues that needed legislative rectification.

title: THE WAREHOUSING CORPORATIONS (SUPPLEMENTARY) ACT, 1965
purpose: To supplement the provisions of the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962, by allowing for the regulation of storage of commodities, other than those already covered by the principal Act, in warehouses run by the corporations, in States where the respective Legislatures have passed resolutions empowering Parliament to legislate on the matter.
scope: Geographical scope includes the States specified in the Schedule. The Central Government can add other States to the Schedule via notification. Subject matter scope pertains to the storage of commodities in warehouses run by the Warehousing Corporations, specifically those not covered by the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its application to the States listed in the Schedule (with provisions for adding other States), and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the Act with respect to notified commodities.
main_sections.description: Modifies the application of the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962, in the scheduled States. It effectively omits the condition that the commodity must be one with respect to which Parliament has the power to legislate under entry 33 of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, thereby broadening the scope of commodities that can be stored.

important_rules: The Act applies to the States listed in the Schedule.
The Central Government can add new States to the Schedule through a notification if their Legislatures adopt the Act for regulating storage of specific commodities.
The Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962, is to be read with an amendment in scheduled States, allowing for storage of a wider range of commodities.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and by extension, the Warehousing Corporations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the Central Government to bring States under the Act's purview and to appoint commencement dates. The Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962, would be enforced in accordance with its own provisions as modified by this Supplementary Act.

rights: Right of States to have their Legislatures pass resolutions to bring them under the purview of this Act.
Right of the Central Government to extend the Act's application to new States.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to issue notifications for commencement and for adding States.
Duty of the Legislatures of States to pass resolutions for their adoption of the Act.
obligations: Obligation on Warehousing Corporations to regulate storage of commodities as per the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962, as amended by this Act, in the applicable States.

key_procedures: Procedure for a State to be included in the Schedule: The Legislature of a State must pass a resolution empowering Parliament to legislate on the storage of commodities other than those covered by the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962. Subsequently, the Central Government may issue a notification adding that State to the Schedule.
Procedure for commencement of the Act: The Central Government appoints a date for the Act to come into force by issuing a notification in the Official Gazette.
administration: Central Government, and the Warehousing Corporations established under the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962.
important_notes: The Act is intended to supplement existing legislation, not replace it.
The primary mechanism for a State's inclusion is through legislative action by that State and subsequent notification by the Central Government.
The schedule of states is subject to amendments and adaptations as evidenced by the footnotes indicating insertions and substitutions.

title: THE GOA, DAMAN AND DIU (EXTENSION OF THE CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE AND THE ARBITRATION ACT) ACT, 1965
purpose: To provide for the extension of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Arbitration Act, 1940, to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu and for certain other matters.

scope.subject_matter: Extension of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Arbitration Act, 1940.

key_definitions.Goa, Daman and Diu: The Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu.
key_definitions.Lieutenant-Governor: The administrator of Goa, Daman and Diu appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines terms used in the Act, specifically 'Goa, Daman and Diu' and 'Lieutenant-Governor'.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of Code of Civil Procedure and Arbitration Act, 1940, to Goa, Daman and Diu
main_sections.description: Extends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Arbitration Act, 1940, to Goa, Daman and Diu.
Repeals any existing laws in Goa, Daman and Diu that correspond to the extended Acts, with provisions for saving previous operations, rights, liabilities, and proceedings.

Provides rules for interpreting the extended Code of Civil Procedure and Arbitration Act in relation to Goa, Daman and Diu, including how to handle references to non-existent laws or functionaries, and construing references to the State Government.
Grants the Central Government the power to issue orders or directions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the extended provisions.
Makes consequential amendments to the Goa, Daman and Diu (Judicial Commissioner’s Court) Regulation, 1963.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Arbitration Act, 1940, are extended to Goa, Daman and Diu.
Rule 2: Existing laws in Goa, Daman and Diu that correspond to the extended Acts are repealed, subject to specific savings.

Rule 3: References in the extended Acts to provisions or functionaries not in force or existence in Goa, Daman and Diu shall be construed as references to corresponding provisions or functionaries in that Union territory, with the Lieutenant-Governor deciding in case of ambiguity or absence of a corresponding functionary.
Rule 4: References to the State Government in the extended Acts shall be construed as references to the Central Government and also to the Lieutenant-Governor.
Rule 5: Courts or authorities may construe the extended Acts in a manner necessary to adapt them to local circumstances without affecting their substance.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Lieutenant-Governor, and relevant courts/authorities as per the extended Code of Civil Procedure and Arbitration Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Arbitration Act, 1940, within Goa, Daman and Diu.

rights: Right to legal proceedings and remedies under the extended Code of Civil Procedure and Arbitration Act.
Rights, privileges, obligations, or liabilities acquired or incurred under repealed laws, which are saved.
duties: To comply with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, as extended to Goa, Daman and Diu.
To comply with the provisions of the Arbitration Act, 1940, as extended to Goa, Daman and Diu.
obligations: Obligations incurred under any law repealed by this Act, which are saved.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint the date on which the Act shall come into force.

Procedure 2: The Central Government may, by order in the Official Gazette, make provisions or give directions to remove any difficulties arising in the application of the extended Code of Civil Procedure and Arbitration Act.
administration: Central Government and the Lieutenant-Governor of Goa, Daman and Diu.
important_notes: The repeal of existing laws does not affect the previous operation of those laws or anything done thereunder, nor does it affect any right, privilege, obligation, or liability acquired or incurred under those laws.
Notifications, declarations, rules, appointments, etc., made under repealed laws will have force if consistent with the extended Code or Act.
References in other laws to repealed provisions shall be construed as references to the corresponding provisions of the extended Code or Act.
The Lieutenant-Governor's decision is final on questions regarding corresponding functionaries or when no corresponding functionary exists.

title: THE RAILWAYS (EMPLOYMENT OF MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES) ACT, 1965
purpose: To make certain provisions relating to the employment of members of the Armed Forces of the Union in the working and management of railways.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to the employment of members of the Armed Forces of the Union in connection with the service, working, use, management, and maintenance of railways.

key_definitions.railway servant: Defined in the Indian Railways Act, 1890, and its meaning is carried over to this Act.
key_definitions.railway administration: Implied to be the entity responsible for the operation of railways, as defined by the Indian Railways Act, 1890.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial application (whole of India).
Defines that words and expressions used in this Act and also defined in the Indian Railways Act, 1890, shall have the meanings assigned to them in that Act.

main_sections.section_title: Employment of members of Armed Forces of the Union to assist a railway administration in connection with the service of a railway
main_sections.description: Specifies the legal status and liabilities of members of the Armed Forces when employed to assist a railway administration. It extends provisions of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, relating to railway servants to these members and clarifies that their employment does not affect the liability of the railway administration. It also clarifies that Chapter VIA of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, does not apply to them and does not derogate from the laws governing the Armed Forces.

main_sections.section_title: Employment of members of Armed Forces of the Union to replace railway administration in working a railway
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to notify in the Official Gazette the assumption of the whole or a portion of a railway's working, management, and maintenance by the Armed Forces. During such assumption, the Indian Railways Act, 1890, ceases to be applicable to the affected railway.

Repeals the Railways (Employment of Members of the Armed Forces) Ordinance, 1965. It also provides that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, with retrospective effect from September 29, 1965.

important_rules: Rule 1: When members of the Armed Forces of the Union are employed to assist a railway administration, they shall have the same powers, status, immunities, duties, and liabilities as a railway servant under the Indian Railways Act, 1890.
Rule 2: The employment of Armed Forces members to assist or replace railway servants does not alter the liabilities of the railway administration.
Rule 3: If the Armed Forces assume the entire working, management, and maintenance of a railway, the Indian Railways Act, 1890, will not apply to that railway during the period of assumption.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for notification under Section 4)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of provisions of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, to members of the Armed Forces when assisting railway administrations. The cessation of applicability of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, under Section 4 also constitutes a form of regulatory change.

rights: Members of the Armed Forces employed to assist a railway administration gain the powers, status, and immunities conferred upon a railway servant under the Indian Railways Act, 1890.
duties: Members of the Armed Forces employed to assist a railway administration have the same duties and liabilities imposed upon a railway servant under the Indian Railways Act, 1890.
obligations: Railway administrations have obligations to ensure that the employment of Armed Forces members does not affect the liabilities that would otherwise attach to them.
The governance, control, and discipline of members of the Armed Forces remain subject to laws regulating the Armed Forces, even when employed by railway administrations.
