key_procedures: Procedure 1: When members of the Armed Forces are employed to assist a railway administration, the provisions of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, conferring powers, status, immunity, or imposing duties/liabilities on railway servants are automatically applied to these members.

Procedure 2: If the Central Government decides that the Armed Forces will assume the working, management, and maintenance of a railway (or a portion thereof), it must notify this in the Official Gazette. Upon such notification, the Indian Railways Act, 1890, becomes inapplicable to the affected railway.
administration: Central Government (specifically for the provisions of Section 4 and impliedly for the overarching regulation of railway services)
important_notes: The Act ensures that members of the Armed Forces retain their existing legal framework for governance, control, and discipline, meaning they are not subject to all the provisions of railway law.

The Act is designed to operate alongside existing railway legislation, primarily the Indian Railways Act, 1890, by extending certain provisions or modifying its applicability in specific circumstances.

title: The Union Territories (Direct Election to the House of the People) Act, 1965
purpose: To provide for direct election in certain Union territories for filling the seats allotted to them in the House of the People and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to direct elections in specific Union territories for seats in the House of the People. The identified Union territories are Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

key_definitions.parliamentary constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.sitting member: A person who immediately before the commencement of this Act is a member of the House of the People.
key_definitions.Union territory: Means any of the Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Union Territories (Direct Election to the House of the People) Act, 1965.
Provides definitions for 'parliamentary constituency', 'sitting member', and 'Union territory' as used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Direct election to fill the seats in the House of the People allotted to certain Union territories
main_sections.description: Establishes that seats allotted to the specified Union territories in the House of the People shall be filled by direct election, with each Union territory forming one parliamentary constituency.
This section, related to an amendment of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, has been repealed.
This section, related to an amendment of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, has been repealed.

States that a sitting member representing a Union territory will continue to do so until the dissolution of the present House of the People. If a seat becomes vacant before dissolution, it will be filled by a presidential nominee who will represent the Union territory until the House's dissolution.

important_rules: Seats allotted to specified Union territories in the House of the People will be filled by direct election.
Each specified Union territory will constitute a single parliamentary constituency.
Sitting members representing Union territories will continue their term until the dissolution of the current House of the People.
Vacancies in Union territory seats before the dissolution of the House will be filled by presidential nomination.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text. Likely falls under general election laws and authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text. Likely through the Election Commission of India and relevant electoral laws.

rights: Right of citizens in specified Union territories to elect their representatives in the House of the People through direct election.
obligations: Obligation for Union territories to hold direct elections for their House of the People seats.
Obligation to fill vacancies with presidential nominees if they occur before the dissolution of the current House.

key_procedures: Direct election process for filling House of the People seats in specified Union territories.
Nomination procedure for filling vacant seats by the President if such vacancies occur before the dissolution of the current House of the People.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text. Administration would likely involve the Election Commission of India and the respective Union territory administrations.
important_notes: Sections 4 and 5 of the Act have been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1974.
The name 'Lakshadweep' replaced 'Laccadive, Minicoy and Aminidivi Islands' through an Adaptation of Laws Order in 1974.

title: THE ASIAN DEVELOPMENT BANK ACT, 1966
purpose: To implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the Asian Development Bank and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the Asian Development Bank, its officers, employees, and operations within India.

key_definitions.Agreement: The Agreement for the establishment and operation of the international body known as the Asian Development Bank.
key_definitions.Bank: The Asian Development Bank established under the Agreement.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, namely 'Agreement' and 'Bank'.

Details the financial obligations of the Central Government towards the Bank, including payments for subscriptions, commission, fees, charges, and other sums as per the Agreement. It also allows the Central Government to issue non-interest bearing and non-negotiable notes to the Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Reserve Bank to be depository for Bank
main_sections.description: Designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of status and certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on Bank and conferment of certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on its officers and employees
main_sections.description: States that certain provisions of the Agreement, as set out in the Schedule, have the force of law in India. It also includes provisos to Article 56 of the Agreement regarding customs duties and taxes, and empowers the Central Government to amend the Schedule based on amendments to the Agreement.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Notifications issued under section 5 and rules made under section 6 to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that every notification issued under section 5(2) and every rule made under section 6 must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period for modification or annulment.

important_rules: Payments for subscriptions, commissions, fees, and other charges to the Asian Development Bank must be made from the Consolidated Fund of India, following parliamentary appropriation (Section 3(1)).
The Central Government can issue non-interest bearing and non-negotiable notes to the Bank as per the Agreement (Section 3(2)).
The Reserve Bank of India will act as the depository for the Bank's Indian currency holdings (Section 4).
Specific provisions of the Agreement concerning the status, immunities, exemptions, and privileges of the Bank and its personnel have the force of law in India (Section 5(1)).
Notifications and rules made under the Act must be presented to Parliament for review (Section 7).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (implied through rule-making power and notification)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the force of law given to the Agreement's provisions, and through rules made by the Central Government. Enforcement of the immunities and privileges granted to the Bank and its personnel would likely be based on the provisions of the Agreement itself and the interpretation of Indian law.

rights: The Bank has legal personality and capacity to contract, acquire/dispose of property, and institute legal proceedings (Article 49).
The Bank enjoys immunity from judicial proceedings, except in specific cases related to borrowing and securities (Article 50).
The Bank's property and assets are immune from search, requisition, confiscation, expropriation, etc. (Article 51).
The Bank's archives and documents are inviolable (Article 52).
The Bank's assets are free from restrictions necessary for its functioning (Article 53).
Official communications of the Bank shall be accorded favourable treatment (Article 54).
Bank personnel have immunity for acts performed in their official capacity, and certain immunities and facilities (Article 55).
The Bank, its assets, income, operations, and transactions are exempt from all taxation and customs duties (Article 56(1)).
Salaries and emoluments paid by the Bank are exempt from taxation, with exceptions for citizens/nationals of countries that retain the right to tax (Article 56(2)).
Bank obligations or securities are exempt from discriminatory taxation (Article 56(3)).
Bank-guaranteed obligations or securities are exempt from discriminatory taxation (Article 56(4)).
The Bank can waive its immunities, exemptions, and privileges (Article 58).
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to make payments to the Bank as required by the Agreement (Section 3(1)).
The Central Government may have obligations related to issuing notes to the Bank (Section 3(2)).
The Central Government must ensure that the provisions of the Agreement scheduled have the force of law in India (Section 5(1)).
The Central Government must present notifications and rules to Parliament for review (Section 7).

key_procedures: Appointment of the commencement date of the Act through a notification by the Central Government (Section 1(3)).
Payment of sums to the Bank from the Consolidated Fund of India upon parliamentary appropriation (Section 3(1)).
Issuance of non-interest bearing notes by the Central Government to the Bank, if deemed fit (Section 3(2)).
Amendment of the Schedule by the Central Government via notification, to conform with amendments to the Agreement (Section 5(2)).
Making of rules by the Central Government via notification (Section 6).
Laying of notifications and rules before Parliament for a period of thirty days for potential modification or annulment (Section 7).
administration: Central Government (specifically through the power to make rules and issue notifications). The Reserve Bank of India acts as the depository.
important_notes: The exemption from customs duties for goods imported by the Bank does not permit unrestricted sale of such goods in India (Section 5(1) proviso (a)).
The Bank is not exempt from duties or taxes that form part of the price of goods sold (Section 5(1) proviso (b)).
The Bank is not exempt from duties or taxes that are merely charges for services rendered (Section 5(1) proviso (c)).
Countries can retain the right to tax salaries and emoluments paid by the Bank to their citizens or nationals, by depositing a declaration (Section 56(2)).
Special procedures for settlement of controversies between the Bank and its members are to be followed, rather than direct legal action (Article 50(2)).

title: THE POLICE-FORCES (RESTRICTION OF RIGHTS) ACT, 1966
purpose: To provide for the restriction of certain rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution in their application to the members of the Forces charged with the maintenance of public order so as to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline among them.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It specifically applies to 'members of a police-force' as defined in the act, which includes any person appointed or enrolled under the enactments specified in the Schedule. The act targets forces charged with the maintenance of public order.

key_definitions.member_of_a_police_force: Any person appointed or enrolled under any enactment specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.police_force: Includes any force charged with the maintenance of public order.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and details the commencement provisions which can be appointed by notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government for Union territories and by the State Government for States, with different dates possible for different Union territories.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'member of a police-force', 'police-force', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions respecting right to form association, freedom of speech, etc.
main_sections.description: Outlines restrictions on members of a police-force regarding their right to form associations, freedom of speech, and participation in political activities without express sanction from the Central Government or prescribed authority. It prohibits association with trade unions, political associations, or other unrecognized organizations, and restricts communication with the press or publication of documents except in bona fide discharge of duties or for purely literary, artistic, or scientific purposes. It also prohibits participation in meetings or demonstrations for political purposes.

Specifies the penalty for contravening the provisions of Section 3, which can include imprisonment up to two years, a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both, in addition to any other action taken against the person.

Grants the Central Government the power to amend the Schedule by including or omitting enactments relating to forces charged with the maintenance of public order. Amendments are made through notification in the Official Gazette and a copy of the notification must be laid before each House of Parliament.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act by notification in the Official Gazette. Such rules are subject to parliamentary scrutiny and modification or annulment.

important_rules: Rule 1: No member of a police-force shall, without express sanction, be a member of, or be associated with, any trade union, labour union, political association, or any other unrecognized society or organization, unless it is purely social, recreational, or religious.

Rule 2: Members of a police-force are prohibited from communicating with the press or publishing documents except when it's in the bona fide discharge of their duties or of a purely literary, artistic, or scientific character, or of a prescribed nature.
Rule 3: Members of a police-force are not allowed to participate in or address any meeting or demonstration organized for political purposes or other prescribed purposes.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years
Fine which may extend to two thousand rupees
Both imprisonment and fine
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the authorities within the police-forces themselves, under the oversight of the Central Government and State Governments as per commencement provisions. The specific enforcement body is not explicitly named, but Section 3(1) mentions 'prescribed authority' for sanctions, and Section 4 states penalties are 'without prejudice to any other action that may be taken against him'.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through penal provisions (Section 4) for contravention of Section 3. The Central Government has the power to make rules (Section 6) to carry out the Act's purposes, which would likely detail enforcement mechanisms. Sanctions for certain actions are required from the Central Government or prescribed authority.

rights: The Act restricts certain rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution, implying that these rights (e.g., freedom of speech, right to form associations) are generally available but are specifically limited for members of police forces under this Act.
duties: To ensure the proper discharge of their duties.
To maintain discipline among themselves.
obligations: To refrain from joining trade unions, political associations, or other unauthorized organizations without sanction.
To refrain from communicating with the press or publishing unauthorized material.
To refrain from participating in political meetings or demonstrations.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement: The Act comes into force on dates appointed by notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government (for Union territories) or State Government (for States). Different dates can be appointed for different Union territories.

Procedure for amendment of the Schedule: The Central Government may amend the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette. A copy of every notification must be laid before each House of Parliament.
Procedure for making rules: The Central Government may make rules by notification in the Official Gazette. These rules are subject to parliamentary review and modification.
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative authority, responsible for making rules, sanctioning certain actions (Section 3), and amending the Schedule (Section 5). State Governments are involved in the commencement of the Act within their respective territories.
important_notes: The definition of 'police-force' is broad and includes any force charged with the maintenance of public order, not just traditional police forces.
The decision of the Central Government is final on whether any society, institution, association, or organization is of a purely social, recreational, or religious nature under Section 3(1)(b).
The Schedule lists specific enactments under which members are considered 'members of a police-force'. This schedule can be amended by the Central Government.

title: The Jawaharlal Nehru University Act, 1966
purpose: To establish and incorporate a university in Delhi, named Jawaharlal Nehru University, with the object of disseminating and advancing knowledge, wisdom, and understanding through teaching and research, and by the example and influence of its corporate life.
scope: The Act applies to the Union territory of Delhi for the establishment and functioning of the Jawaharlal Nehru University. The University's jurisdiction extends to all Colleges and recognized institutions. Powers and jurisdiction can also extend to institutions or bodies outside the Union territory of Delhi, subject to the laws of that State and the rules of the local University.

key_definitions.College: A college maintained by the University.
key_definitions.Hall: A unit of residence for students, provided, maintained, or recognized by the University.
key_definitions.Recognised institution: An institution of higher learning maintained or recognized by, or associated with, the University.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by Statutes, Ordinances, or Regulations.
key_definitions.Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations: Respectively, the Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations of the University made under this Act.
key_definitions.University: The Jawaharlal Nehru University.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Jawaharlal Nehru University Act, 1966, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'College', 'Hall', 'recognised institution', 'prescribed', 'Statutes', 'Ordinances', 'Regulations', and 'University'.

This section establishes the Jawaharlal Nehru University in the Union territory of Delhi. It constitutes the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to sue and be sued.

This section outlines the primary objects of the University, which are to disseminate and advance knowledge, wisdom, and understanding through teaching and research, and to foster its corporate life. It also refers to specific objects detailed in the First Schedule.

This section lists the various powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, establishing special centres and laboratories, organizing extra-mural teaching, conducting examinations, conferring degrees, creating posts, appointing staff, establishing and maintaining colleges and halls, regulating discipline, promoting student and employee welfare, recognizing institutions, cooperating with other bodies, entering into agreements, demanding fees, receiving donations, acquiring and disposing of property, providing research and advisory services, printing and publishing research, and borrowing money with Central Government approval.

This section defines the jurisdiction of the University to extend to all Colleges and recognized institutions. It also includes a provision that the University shall not recognize an institution already recognized by the University of Delhi without Central Government authorization and consultation with the University of Delhi. Upon such recognition, the University of Delhi's jurisdiction over that institution ceases.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and Jurisdiction in respect of institution or body outside the Union territory of Delhi
main_sections.description: This section details the powers and jurisdiction of the University concerning institutions or bodies established outside the Union territory of Delhi, whether seeking recognition or being established by the University. This is subject to the laws in force in the respective State and the rules of the local University.

This section designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University. It outlines the Visitor's powers, including appointing persons to review the University's work, taking action based on reports, causing inspections and inquiries, annulling proceedings not in conformity with the Act, and other powers prescribed by the Statutes.

This section lists the officers of the University: Chancellor (Head of the University), Vice-Chancellor (principal executive and Academic Officer), Rectors, Deans for each School of Study, Registrar (Secretary of Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council), Finance Officer (Secretary of Finance Committee), and other officers as provided by the Statutes.

This section enumerates the authorities of the University, which include the Court, the Executive Council, the Academic Council, the Schools of Studies, the Finance Committee, and any other authorities declared by the Statutes.

This section establishes the Court as the supreme authority of the University, defining its constitution and the terms of office of its members by the Statutes. It has the power to review acts of the Executive Council and Academic Council and exercise all powers not otherwise provided for, subject to specific majority requirements for review.

This section defines the Executive Council as the executive body of the University, responsible for the general management and administration, including revenue and property. Its constitution and member terms are prescribed by the Statutes.

This section establishes the Academic Council as the academic body of the University, responsible for the control, general regulation, and maintenance of standards of instruction, education, and examination. Its constitution and member terms are prescribed by the Statutes.

This section outlines the constitution and purpose of the Academic Advisory Committee, which advises on the planning and development of the University and reviews educational and research standards. It consists of persons of high academic standing appointed by the Statutes and the Vice-Chancellor. The Visitor can dissolve this committee.
This section states that Statutes are made subject to the provisions of the Act.
This section details how Statutes are made, though the specific details are not fully provided in the extract.
This section refers to Ordinances, which are made under the Act. Specific details are not provided in the extract.
This section refers to Regulations, which are made under the Act. Specific details are not provided in the extract.
This section likely pertains to the preparation and submission of an annual report by the University.
This section likely pertains to the audit of the University's accounts.

main_sections.section_title: Disputes as to constitution of the University authorities and bodies
main_sections.description: This section addresses how disputes concerning the constitution of University authorities and bodies are to be resolved.
This section likely outlines the process for constituting committees within the University.
This section deals with the procedure for filling casual vacancies in the University's officers or authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings of the University authorities and bodies not invalidated by vacancies
main_sections.description: This section ensures that the proceedings of University authorities and bodies are not invalidated solely due to vacancies within them.
This section likely provides a mechanism for addressing and resolving any difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the Act.
This section contains provisions for the transition from the pre-establishment phase to the functioning of the University.
This section indicates that the Act makes amendments to the Indian Universities Act, 1904 (Act 8 of 1904).

important_rules: The University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal, and shall sue and be sued by the name 'Jawaharlal Nehru University'.
The Visitor (President of India) has the power to review the University's work, cause inspections and inquiries, and issue directions which the University must comply with.
The Executive Council is responsible for the general management and administration of the University, including its revenue and property.
The Academic Council is responsible for the control and general regulation of standards of instruction, education, and examination within the University.
The University shall not grant recognition to any institution already recognized by the University of Delhi without Central Government authorization and consultation with the University of Delhi.
Powers and jurisdiction of the University over institutions outside Delhi are subject to the laws of the State and the rules of the local University.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Visitor (President of India) has significant oversight and enforcement powers, including the ability to annul proceedings and issue directions. The Central Government is involved in appointing the commencement date and authorizing recognition of institutions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directives issued by the Visitor, review of University work and progress, inspections, inquiries, and the potential annulment of proceedings. The Central Government's approval is required for borrowing and for recognizing certain institutions.

rights: Right to provide instruction and conduct research.
Right to establish and maintain institutions.
Right to grant degrees, diplomas, and certificates.
Right to confer honorary degrees.
Right to create and appoint staff.
Right to establish and maintain Colleges and Halls.
Right to determine admission examinations.
Right to recognize and withdraw recognition of institutions.
Right to cooperate with other bodies.
Right to enter into agreements.
Right to demand and receive fees and charges.
Right to receive donations and manage property.
Right to provide research and advisory services.
Right to borrow money with Central Government approval.
Right to sue and be sued.
duties: Duty to disseminate and advance knowledge, wisdom, and understanding.
Duty to comply with directions from the Visitor.
Duty to maintain standards of instruction, education, and examination.
Duty to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees.
Duty to make arrangements for promoting health and general welfare of students and employees.
obligations: The University shall be bound to comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
Recognition of certain institutions is conditional upon consultation and authorization by the Central Government and the University of Delhi.

key_procedures: Appointment of University officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Rectors, Deans, Registrar, Finance Officer) as prescribed by Statutes.
Constitution and functioning of University authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Finance Committee) as prescribed by Statutes and the Act.
Process for making Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations (details not fully extracted).
Procedure for the Visitor to review University work, conduct inspections/inquiries, and issue directions.
Procedure for the Executive Council to manage University affairs and the Academic Council to regulate academic standards.
Process for the Court to review the acts of the Executive Council and Academic Council.
Process for granting recognition to institutions and withdrawal thereof.
Procedure for filling casual vacancies in University offices and authorities.
Process for the University to borrow money, requiring Central Government approval.
administration: The Central Government plays a role in appointing the commencement date of the Act and in authorizing recognition of certain institutions. The President of India is the Visitor. The day-to-day administration is managed by the University's officers and authorities, primarily the Vice-Chancellor and the Executive Council, under the oversight of the Visitor.
important_notes: The Act came into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
The Jawaharlal Nehru University is established in the Union territory of Delhi.
The First Schedule contains specific objects of the University, which are not fully detailed in the provided extract.
The Second Schedule is also referenced but not detailed in the extract.

title: THE RAILWAY PROPERTY (UNLAWFUL POSSESSION) ACT, 1966
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to unlawful possession of railway property.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It concerns railway property, which includes goods, money, valuable security, or animals belonging to, or in the charge or possession of, a railway administration.

key_definitions.Force: The Railway Protection Force constituted under section 3 of the Railway Protection Force Act, 1957 (23 of 1957).
key_definitions.member_of_the_Force: A person appointed to the Force, other than a superior officer.
key_definitions.officer_of_the_Force: An officer of and above the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector appointed to the Force and includes a superior officer.
key_definitions.railway_property: Includes any goods, money or valuable security or animal, belonging to, or in the charge or possession of, a railway administration.
key_definitions.superior_officer: Any of the officers appointed under section 4 of the Railway Protection Force Act, 1957 (23 of 1957), and includes any other officer appointed by the Central Government as a superior officer of the force.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Force', 'member of the Force', 'officer of the Force', 'railway property', and 'superior officer'. It also specifies that undefined terms will take their meanings from the Indian Railways Act, 1890.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for theft, dishonest misappropriation or unlawful possession of railway property
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for theft, dishonest misappropriation, or unlawful possession of railway property reasonably suspected of being stolen or unlawfully obtained, unless lawful possession can be proven. It outlines specific minimum imprisonment and fine amounts for first and subsequent offenses.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for abetment, conspiracy or connivance at offences
main_sections.description: Specifies punishment for abetting or conspiring in offenses under the Act, or for owners/occupiers of land/buildings who wilfully connive at such offenses.

main_sections.section_title: Offences under the Act not to be cognizable
main_sections.description: States that offenses under this Act are not cognizable, notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

Grants superior officers or members of the Force the power to arrest any person involved in an offense punishable under the Act, or against whom there is a reasonable suspicion of involvement, without a magistrate's order or a warrant.
Mandates that persons arrested for offenses under this Act, if arrested by someone other than an officer of the Force, must be forwarded without delay to the nearest officer of the Force.

Outlines the procedure for officers of the Force when they receive information about an offense or when a person is arrested. It empowers them to inquire into the charge and exercise powers similar to a police station in-charge investigating a cognizable case, including admitting to bail or forwarding to a Magistrate, or releasing on bond if no sufficient evidence exists.

main_sections.section_title: Power to summon persons to give evidence and produce documents
main_sections.description: Grants officers of the Force the power to summon individuals to give evidence or produce documents/things during inquiries. It states that summoned persons are bound to attend and state the truth, and that such inquiries are deemed judicial proceedings.

Details the process for obtaining a search warrant. If an officer of the Force has reason to believe a place is used for depositing or selling stolen or unlawfully obtained railway property, they can apply to a Magistrate for a warrant to search the premises and seize such property.

main_sections.section_title: Searches and arrests how to be made
main_sections.description: Specifies that searches and arrests under this Act must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
Empowers and requires all Government officers and village officers to assist superior officers and members of the Force in enforcing the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of courts to order forfeiture of vehicles, etc.
main_sections.description: Gives courts trying offenses under the Act the power to order the forfeiture of property in respect of which an offense was committed, as well as any receptacles, packages, coverings, animals, vehicles, or conveyances used in carrying such property.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir
main_sections.description: This section was omitted by adaptation orders related to the reorganization of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

Repeals the Railway Stores (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1955, and provides savings for offenses committed under the repealed Act, which can still be investigated and tried as if the new Act had not been passed. It also references the General Clauses Act, 1897, regarding the effect of repeals.

important_rules: Whoever commits theft, dishonestly misappropriates, or is found in unlawful possession of railway property reasonably suspected of being stolen or unlawfully obtained, shall be punishable unless they prove lawful possession.
Abetting, conspiring in, or wilfully conniving at offenses under the Act is punishable.
Offenses under this Act are not cognizable.
Officers of the Force can arrest without a warrant if there is a reasonable suspicion of involvement in an offense.
Persons arrested must be forwarded to the nearest officer of the Force if not arrested by one.
Inquiries into offenses by officers of the Force are to be conducted with powers similar to police investigations, with provisions for bail, custody, or release on bond.
Officers of the Force can summon individuals for evidence or production of documents, and such inquiries are judicial proceedings.
A Magistrate can issue a search warrant to an officer of the Force to search premises suspected of storing or selling stolen/unlawfully obtained railway property.
Searches and arrests must follow the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
Government and village officers are required to assist in the enforcement of the Act.
Courts can order forfeiture of property, receptacles, and vehicles used in committing offenses under the Act.
The Act overrides any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

penalties: For theft, dishonest misappropriation, or unlawful possession of railway property:
First offense: Imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both. Minimum one year imprisonment and one thousand rupees fine, unless special reasons exist.
Second or subsequent offense: Imprisonment up to five years and fine. Minimum two years imprisonment and two thousand rupees fine, unless special reasons exist.
For abetment, conspiracy, or connivance: Imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officers of the Railway Protection Force (superior officers and members of the Force).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of arrest without warrant, conducting inquiries, summoning persons for evidence, issuing search warrants (via Magistrate), and requiring assistance from government and village officers. Courts can order forfeiture of property and vehicles.

rights: Right to be informed of the charge and to appear before a Magistrate.
Right to bail or release on bond if there is insufficient evidence.
Exemptions under sections 132 and 133 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, are applicable to requisitions for attendance.
duties: Duty to prove lawful possession of railway property if suspected of being stolen or unlawfully obtained.
Duty to attend when summoned by an officer of the Force and to state the truth.
Duty to produce documents and things as required by a summons.
Duty of Government and village officers to assist in enforcing the Act.
obligations: Obligation for arrested persons to be forwarded to the nearest officer of the Force.
Obligation for owners/occupiers of land/buildings to not wilfully connive at offenses against the Act.

key_procedures: Arrest of a person reasonably suspected of being concerned in an offense under the Act, without a warrant.
Forwarding of arrested persons to the nearest officer of the Force (if not arrested by one).
Inquiry by an officer of the Force into the charge against an arrested person, similar to a police investigation.
Decision by the officer of the Force to admit to bail, forward to a Magistrate, or release on bond based on evidence.
Summoning persons to give evidence or produce documents for an inquiry.
Application to a Magistrate for a search warrant if a place is suspected of being used for storing/selling stolen railway property.
Execution of search warrants to enter, search, and seize railway property.
Forfeiture of property, receptacles, and vehicles involved in an offense by a court trying the case.
administration: The Act is administered by the Railway Protection Force and relevant judicial magistrates for search warrants and court proceedings. The Central Government appoints the date of commencement.
important_notes: The Act overrides other laws in case of inconsistency.
The Act was amended in 2012, notably to clarify definitions and penalties.
Section 15 regarding Jammu and Kashmir was omitted due to reorganization.

title: THE LAND ACQUISITION (AMENDMENT AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1967
purpose: To further amend the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and to validate certain acquisitions of land under the said Act.
scope: This act applies to land acquisitions in India that were made or purported to be made under the principal Land Acquisition Act, 1894. It specifically addresses acquisitions made before the commencement of the Land Acquisition (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1967 (1 of 1967).

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Land Acquisition (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1967.
This section has been omitted by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1974.
This section has been omitted by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1974.

This section validates certain land acquisitions made under the principal Act, even if multiple Collectors, reports under section 5A, or declarations under section 6 were involved. It also addresses the timing of declarations and the payment of interest on compensation for delayed acquisitions.

This section repeals the Land Acquisition (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1967, and provides that anything done or action taken under the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: No acquisition of land made or purported to be made under the principal Act before the commencement of the Land Acquisition (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1967, shall be deemed invalid merely because one or more Collectors performed functions, one or more reports were made under section 5A, or one or more declarations were made under section 6 for different parcels of land covered by the same section 4 notification.
Rule 2: Acquisitions in pursuance of a section 4 notification published before the commencement of the Ordinance may be made after such commencement and shall not be deemed invalid.

Rule 3: No declaration under section 6 of the principal Act shall be made after the expiry of two years from the commencement of the Ordinance for land notified under section 4 before the Ordinance's commencement.

Rule 4: Where land acquisition was made under a section 6 declaration issued after the expiry of three years from the date of section 4 notification publication (for notifications before the Ordinance's commencement), simple interest at six percent per annum shall be paid on the market value from the expiry of the three-year period to the tender of payment of compensation, unless the proceedings were stayed by a court or compensation was already paid before this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the authorities responsible for administering the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (e.g., Collectors, revenue authorities).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the procedures outlined in the principal Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended and validated by this Act.

rights: Right to receive fair compensation for acquired land.
Right to receive interest on compensation if acquisition is delayed beyond specified periods.
duties: Duty to follow the procedures outlined in the principal Act and this amendment for land acquisition.
Duty to pay compensation and, where applicable, interest to persons interested.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that land acquisitions, even with procedural variations, are validated if they meet the criteria specified in section 4.
Obligation to adhere to the time limits for making declarations under section 6.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Validation of acquisitions made under the principal Act before the commencement of the Ordinance, addressing issues with multiple Collectors, section 5A reports, and section 6 declarations.
Procedure 2: Allowing acquisitions initiated by section 4 notifications before the Ordinance to be completed after its commencement without being deemed invalid.
Procedure 3: Stipulating a two-year time limit from the Ordinance's commencement for making section 6 declarations for land notified under section 4 before the Ordinance.

Procedure 4: Calculation and payment of simple interest at six percent per annum on the market value of land acquired under delayed section 6 declarations (exceeding three years from section 4 notification publication) for notifications published before the Ordinance.
administration: The administration of this act would fall under the purview of the authorities responsible for implementing the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, likely the revenue departments and district administration at the state and central levels.
important_notes: This Act serves to rectify certain procedural irregularities in land acquisition processes that might have rendered them invalid.
The validation provided by this Act is retrospective, applying to actions taken before its commencement.
Exceptions to interest payment apply if proceedings were stayed by court order or if compensation was already paid before the Act came into force.
The repeal of the Ordinance (1 of 1967) is confirmed, with continuity of actions taken under it.

title: THE UNLAWFUL ACTIVITIES (PREVENTION) ACT, 1967
purpose: To provide for the more effective prevention of certain unlawful activities of individuals and associations, and for dealing with terrorist activities, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to every person for acts or omissions contrary to its provisions committed in India. It also applies to acts committed beyond India if punishable under the Act, as if committed in India. Specifically, it applies to citizens of India outside India, persons in the service of the Government (wherever they may be), and persons on ships and aircraft registered in India (wherever they may be).

key_definitions.association: Any combination or body of individuals.
key_definitions.cession_of_a_part_of_the_territory_of_In: Includes admission of the claim of any foreign country to any such part.
key_definitions.code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.court: A criminal court having jurisdiction, under the Code, to try offences under this Act, and includes a Special Court constituted under section 11 or under section 22 of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.
key_definitions.designated_authority: Such officer of the Central Government not below the rank of Joint Secretary to that Government, or such officer of the State Government not below the rank of Secretary to that Government, as the case may be, as may be specified by the Central Government or the State Government, by notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.economic_security: Includes financial, monetary and fiscal stability, security of means of production and distribution, food security, livelihood security, energy security, ecological and environmental security.
key_definitions.order: The Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism (Implementation of Security Council Resolutions) Order, 2007, as may be amended from time to time.
key_definitions.person: Includes an individual, a company, a firm, an organisation or an association of persons or a body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, every artificial juridical person, not falling within any of the preceding sub-clauses, and any agency, office or branch owned or controlled by any person falling within any of the preceding sub-clauses.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.proceeds_of_terrorism: Includes all kinds of properties derived or obtained from the commission of any terrorist act or acquired through funds traceable to a terrorist act, irrespective of who owns them or where they are found. It also includes any property being used, or intended to be used, for a terrorist act or for the purpose of an individual terrorist or a terrorist gang or a terrorist organisation. It is declared that this expression includes any property intended to be used for terrorism.
key_definitions.property: Property and assets of every description whether corporeal or incorporeal, movable or immovable, tangible or intangible and legal documents, deeds and instruments in any form including but not limited to electronic or digital, evidencing title to, or interest in, such property or assets by means of bank credits, travellers’ cheques, bank cheques, money orders, shares, securities, bonds, drafts, letters of credit, cash and bank account including fund, however acquired.
key_definitions.secession_of_a_part_of_the_territory_of_: Includes the assertion of any claim to determine whether such part will remain a part of the territory of India.
key_definitions.state_government: In relation to a Union territory, means the Administrator thereof.
key_definitions.terrorist_act: Has the meaning assigned to it in section 15, and the expressions "terrorism" and "terrorist" shall be construed accordingly.
key_definitions.terrorist_gang: Any association, other than a terrorist organisation, whether systematic or otherwise, which is concerned with, or involved in, a terrorist act.
key_definitions.terrorist_organisation: An organisation listed in the First Schedule or an organisation operating under the same name as an organisation so listed.
key_definitions.unlawful_activity: In relation to an individual or association, means any action taken by such individual or association (whether by committing an act or by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representation or otherwise), which is intended, or supports any claim, to bring about, on any ground whatsoever, the cession of a part of the territory of India or the secession of a part of the territory of India from the Union, or which incites any individual or group of individuals to bring about such cession or secession; or which disclaims, questions, disrupts or is intended to disrupt the sovereignty and territorial integrity of India; or which causes or is intended to cause disaffection against India.
key_definitions.unlawful_association: Any association which has for its object any unlawful activity, or which encourages or aids persons to undertake any unlawful activity, or of which the members undertake such activity; or which has for its object any activity which is punishable under section 153A (45 of 1860) or section 153B of the Indian Penal Code, or which encourages or aids persons to undertake any such activity, or of which the members undertake any such activity. (Proviso: Nothing contained in sub-clause (ii) shall apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir).

main_sections.description: This section defines the short title as 'The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967'. It specifies that the Act extends to the whole of India. It outlines the liability of persons for acts or omissions contrary to the Act committed in India and extraterritorially. It also details the applicability to citizens of India outside India, government servants, and persons on registered Indian ships and aircraft.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'association', 'cession of a part of the territory of India', 'Code', 'court', 'Designated Authority', 'economic security', 'Order', 'person', 'prescribed', 'proceeds of terrorism', 'property', 'Schedule', 'secession of a part of the territory of India from the Union', 'State Government', 'terrorist act', 'terrorist gang', 'terrorist organisation', 'Tribunal', 'unlawful activity', and 'unlawful association'. It also addresses how references to enactments not in force in certain areas should be construed.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of an association as unlawful
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Central Government to declare an association unlawful by notification in the Official Gazette if it is of the opinion that the association is, or has become, unlawful. The notification must specify the grounds and particulars. The declaration takes effect only after confirmation by the Tribunal, unless immediate effect is necessary due to circumstances. The notification must also be published in a newspaper and served on the association.

important_rules: Rule: If the Central Government is of the opinion that an association is unlawful, it can declare it so by notification in the Official Gazette.
Rule: Such a notification must specify the grounds and other necessary particulars.
Rule: The notification does not take effect until confirmed by the Tribunal, unless immediate effect is deemed necessary.

Rule: The notification must be published in the Official Gazette, in at least one daily newspaper circulating in the State where the association's principal office is located, and served on the association.

penalties: Penalty for being a member of an unlawful association, etc. (Section 10)
Penalty for dealing with funds of an unlawful association (Section 11)
Penalty for contravention of an order made in respect of a notified place (Section 12)
Punishment for unlawful activities (Section 13)
Punishment for terrorist act (Section 16)
Punishment for raising funds for terrorist act (Section 17)
Punishment for conspiracy, etc. (Section 18)
Punishment for organising of terrorist camps (Section 18A)
Punishment for recruiting of any person or persons for terrorist act (Section 18B)
Punishment for harbouring, etc. (Section 19)
Punishment for being member of terrorist gang or organisation (Section 20)
Punishment for holding proceeds of terrorism (Section 21)
Punishment for threatening witness (Section 22)
Enhanced penalties (Section 23)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, and designated authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through declarations of unlawful associations, notification of places used for unlawful activities, investigation of offences, prosecution of offenders, and forfeiture of proceeds of terrorism. The Act also provides for special courts and modified procedures for certain investigations and trials.

rights: Right to appeal against the order of the Designated Authority (Section 25, 28).
duties: Duty to furnish information related to unlawful or terrorist activities (Section 43F).
obligations: Obligation to not be a member of an unlawful association or terrorist gang/organisation.
Obligation to not deal with funds of unlawful associations or proceeds of terrorism.
Obligation to comply with orders regarding notified places.
Obligation to not engage in unlawful activities or terrorist acts.
Obligation to not support terrorist organisations.
Obligation to not harbour individuals involved in terrorist acts.

key_procedures: Procedure for declaring an association as unlawful: Central Government issues a notification, which is published in the Official Gazette and a newspaper, and served on the association. This declaration requires confirmation from a Tribunal.
Procedure for confirmation of declaration of unlawful association: The Tribunal hears the case and makes an order to confirm or reject the declaration. (Section 4, 5)
Procedure for prohibiting the use of funds of an unlawful association: Based on a notification of unlawful association, the government can prohibit the use of funds. (Section 7)
Procedure for notifying places used for unlawful association: Power to notify places used for unlawful activities, with procedures for contravention. (Section 8)

Procedure for forfeiture of proceeds of terrorism: This involves investigation by an officer or Designated Authority, issuance of a show cause notice, and an order of forfeiture by the Court or Designated Authority. Appeals are possible. (Chapter V, Sections 24A-34)
Procedure for investigation of offences: Officers competent to investigate offences under Chapters IV and VI are specified. (Section 43)
Procedure of arrest, seizure, etc.: Procedures are outlined for arrest, search, and seizure. (Section 43A, 43B)
Procedure for taking cognizance of offences: How courts take cognizance of offences under the Act. (Section 45)
administration: Central Government and State Governments. Specific functions may be carried out by 'Designated Authorities'. The Act also establishes a 'Tribunal'.
important_notes: The Act has been significantly amended, notably by the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Amendment Act, 2004, and subsequent amendments to include provisions for dealing with terrorist activities.
The Act includes provisions for enhanced penalties for certain offences. (Section 23)
The Act specifies that offences under Chapters IV and VI are cognizable. (Section 14)
The Act allows for the impounding of passports and arms licenses of persons charge-sheeted under the Act. (Section 51)
The Act deals with the admissibility of evidence collected through the interception of communications. (Section 46)
The Act outlines presumptions regarding offences under Section 15 (Terrorist Act). (Section 43E)
The Act includes provisions for the protection of witnesses. (Section 44)
The Act provides for the closure of jurisdiction of civil courts in matters under the Act. (Section 47)

title: The Central Laws (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 1968
purpose: To provide for the extension of certain Central Laws to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh) and extends certain specified Central Laws to this region. The scope also includes amendments to these extended laws as detailed in the Schedule.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Central Laws (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 1968, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

main_sections.section_title: Extension and amendment of certain laws
main_sections.description: Declares that the Acts mentioned in the Schedule, along with their rules, orders, and regulations, are extended to and shall be in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It also states that these Acts shall be amended as specified in the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir
main_sections.description: Requires references in the scheduled Acts to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir to be construed as references to corresponding laws in force in that State.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to authorities where new Authorities have been constituted
main_sections.description: Ensures that references in existing laws of Jammu and Kashmir to authorities competent at the time of enactment are treated as references to newly constituted corresponding authorities under the extended Central Laws.

Provides for the repeal of any existing Jammu and Kashmir law corresponding to an extended Central Law. It includes savings for previous operations, acquired rights, liabilities, penalties, and legal proceedings under the repealed laws. It also deems actions taken under repealed laws as valid under the corresponding extended Act.

Empowers the Central Government to make orders or give directions, by notification, to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the extended Acts. This includes specifying corresponding authorities, transferring pending matters, and recognizing actions taken under repealed laws.

important_rules: Any Act mentioned in the Schedule is extended to Jammu and Kashmir, along with its associated rules, orders, and regulations.
The Acts mentioned in the Schedule are amended as specified in the Schedule.
References to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir in the scheduled Acts shall be construed as references to corresponding laws in force in that State.
References to authorities in Jammu and Kashmir shall be construed as references to new, corresponding authorities established by or under the extended laws.
Existing Jammu and Kashmir laws corresponding to the extended Central Laws stand repealed, with provisions for saving past actions, rights, and liabilities.
The Central Government has the power to issue orders to remove difficulties in the implementation of the extended Acts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders to remove difficulties, and the general application of the extended Central Laws.

rights: Previous rights, privileges, obligations, or liabilities acquired, accrued, or incurred under repealed laws are saved.

Investigations, legal proceedings, or remedies in respect of rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, forfeitures, or punishments incurred under repealed laws may be continued or enforced.
duties: Obligations acquired or incurred under any law so repealed are saved.
obligations: Obligations acquired or incurred under any law so repealed are saved.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act by Central Government notification.
Extension of specified Central Laws to Jammu and Kashmir.
Amendment of extended laws as per the Schedule.
Construction of references to laws and authorities within Jammu and Kashmir.
Repeal of corresponding local laws with savings.
Removal of difficulties by Central Government orders.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act came into force on August 15, 1968.
As of October 30, 2019, the Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

The Schedule details specific amendments to various Central Acts, including the Official Trustees Act, 1913; Motor Vehicles Act, 1939; Chartered Accountants Act, 1949; Transfer of Prisoners Act, 1950; Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950; Mines Act, 1952; Notaries Act, 1952; Essential Commodities Act, 1955; Companies Act, 1956; Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959; Apprentices Act, 1961; and Administrators-General Act, 1963.

title: The Pondicherry (Extension of Laws) Act, 1968
purpose: To extend certain Central Acts to the Union territory of Pondicherry.
scope: Applies to the Union territory of Pondicherry. The act extends various Central Acts to Pondicherry, some with modifications.

key_definitions.Act: An Act or Ordinance specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator of Pondicherry appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Pondicherry (Extension of Laws) Act, 1968.
Defines 'Act', 'Administrator', and 'Pondicherry' for the purpose of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Extension with amendments of certain laws to Pondicherry and their commencement therein
main_sections.description: Specifies the extension of Acts listed in the Schedule to Pondicherry, subject to modifications. It also outlines the commencement of these Acts through notification by the Administrator.

Repeals existing laws in Pondicherry that correspond to the extended Acts, with provisions for saving previous operations, rights, liabilities, penalties, and legal proceedings. It also clarifies that actions taken under repealed laws are deemed to have been taken under the extended Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of rules, orders, etc., under certain laws
main_sections.description: Extends rules, notifications, orders, regulations, and bye-laws made by the Central Government under the extended Acts to Pondicherry.

Provides rules for interpreting references to laws and functionaries not in existence or in force in Pondicherry, allowing for adaptation to the local context and defining the role of the Administrator in case of ambiguity. It also specifies that references to 'State Government' should be construed as 'Central Government' and include the 'Administrator'.

Empowers the Central Government to make orders or give directions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the extended Acts in Pondicherry. This power is limited to two years from the commencement of the Act.

important_rules: Rules of construction (Section 6) are crucial for adapting existing laws to the Pondicherry context, including interpreting references to functionaries and the State Government.
The Administrator has the power to appoint commencement dates for extended Acts and provisions (Section 3(2)).
The Central Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in the implementation of extended Acts (Section 7).

penalties: Penalties incurred under laws repealed by this Act are preserved and can be imposed as if the Act had not been passed (Section 4(2)(c)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Administrator and other relevant authorities as per the extended Acts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and enforcement of the extended Central Acts and their associated rules, notifications, orders, regulations, and bye-laws in Pondicherry.

rights: Rights acquired under any law repealed by this Act are saved and continue to be enforceable (Section 4(2)(b)).
duties: Obligations incurred under any law repealed by this Act are saved and continue to be enforceable (Section 4(2)(b)).
obligations: Obligations incurred under any law repealed by this Act are saved and continue to be enforceable (Section 4(2)(b)).

key_procedures: Extension of Acts: Specific Central Acts are extended to Pondicherry as listed in the Schedule, with potential modifications.
Commencement Notification: The Administrator notifies the commencement dates for the extended Acts or their provisions in the Official Gazette.
Removal of Difficulties: The Central Government can issue orders to resolve any difficulties encountered in the implementation of the extended Acts.
administration: The Central Government and the Administrator of Pondicherry.
important_notes: Certain Acts listed in the Schedule have specific modifications, such as exemptions for 'Renoncants' (e.g., Converts' Marriage Dissolution Act, 1866; Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872; Guardians and Wards Act, 1890; Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956).
The power to remove difficulties under Section 7 is time-bound, lasting for two years from the commencement of the respective Act or its provisions in Pondicherry.

title: THE CIVIL DEFENCE ACT, 1968
purpose: To make provision for civil defence and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The act's provisions for civil defence apply to measures for protecting persons, property, places, or things in India against hostile attacks, and measures for disaster management.

key_definitions.civil defence: Includes any measures, not amounting to actual combat, for affording protection to any person, property, place, or thing in India or any part of the territory thereof against any hostile attack, whether from air, land, sea or other places, or, for depriving any such attack of the whole or part of its effect, whether such measures are taken before, during, at or after the time of such attack, or any measure taken for the purpose of disaster management, before, during, at, or after any disaster.
key_definitions.Civil Defence Corps: Means the Corps formed wholly or mainly to meet the needs of civil defence and includes an organisation deemed to be a Corps under the proviso to sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.hostile attack: Means any attack by any person or body of persons, whether during any war, external aggression, internal disturbance or otherwise which endangers the security of any life, property, place or thing in India or any part of the territory thereof.
key_definitions.disaster: Means a disaster as defined in clause (d) of section 2 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
key_definitions.disaster management: Means the disaster management as defined in clause (e) of section 2 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005.

main_sections.description: Defines the short title of the Act as the Civil Defence Act, 1968. It states that the Act extends to the whole of India and specifies the conditions for its commencement in different States or parts thereof.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'civil defence', 'Civil Defence Corps', 'hostile attack', 'notification', 'personal service injury', 'State Government', 'disaster', and 'disaster management'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules for civil defence.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for securing civil defence, covering a wide range of measures such as preventing prejudicial work, instructing the public, storing commodities, regulating traffic and lights, protecting life and property, controlling explosives, evacuation, accommodation of evacuated persons, salvage, and ensuring the safety of critical infrastructure and facilities.

Allows the State Government to constitute a Civil Defence Corps for any area and appoint a 'Controller' to command it. It also allows for existing organizations to be deemed as the Corps and for the appointment of a Director of Civil Defence for coordinating activities.

Details the appointment of members to the Corps by the State Government and the appointment of members to offices or commands within the Corps by the Controller. It also specifies that members will be given a certificate of membership.

main_sections.section_title: Dismissal of members of Civil Defence Corps.
main_sections.description: Outlines the grounds and procedures for dismissing members of the Civil Defence Corps. Dismissal can occur for unsatisfactory performance or misconduct after an inquiry, or summarily if the member's continued presence is deemed undesirable.

Provides a right of appeal to members dismissed from the Corps under section 6. Appeals are to be made to the State Government within thirty days, which can confirm, modify, or reverse the dismissal order.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of members of Civil Defence Corps.
main_sections.description: Specifies that members of the Corps shall perform functions related to civil defence as assigned by rules or other laws. The State Government or Controller can call out members for training or specific functions. Members may also be required to discharge functions in other States.

Grants the Central Government the power to make regulations for carrying out the purposes of Chapter III (Civil Defence Corps). These regulations can cover the functions of members, their service conditions, discipline, accoutrement, clothing, and membership certificates.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of the Personal Injuries (Emergency Provisions) Act to apply to injuries sustained by the members of the Corps.
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Personal Injuries (Emergency Provisions) Act apply to injuries sustained by members of the Civil Defence Corps.
Specifies penalties for contravention of rules made under the Act. As amended, contravention can be punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of Act and rules, etc., inconsistent with other enactments.
main_sections.description: Clarifies the effect of this Act and rules made under it if they are inconsistent with other enactments.

main_sections.section_title: Ordinary avocations of life to be interfered with as little as possible.
main_sections.description: States that ordinary avocations of life should be interfered with as little as possible when implementing the provisions of the Act.
Provides savings for orders made under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to measures taken for the protection of the Armed Forces.
main_sections.description: Exempts measures taken for the protection of the Armed Forces from the purview of this Act.
Deals with the limitation period for legal prosecutions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to delegate.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to delegate its functions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of order made by the Central Government, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies the effect of orders made by the Central Government or other authorities.
Grants the power to delegate functions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Authorised persons and members of the Corps to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares authorized persons and members of the Civil Defence Corps as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament.
main_sections.description: Requires rules and regulations made under the Act to be laid before Parliament.

important_rules: Rules made by the Central Government for civil defence can cover a wide array of preventive and protective measures, including public instruction, resource management, traffic and communication control, and securing critical infrastructure (Section 3).
Contravention of rules made under Section 3 can lead to penalties, including fines and imprisonment (Section 3(3) as amended).
The State Government may constitute a Civil Defence Corps, appoint a Controller, and potentially designate existing organizations for civil defence functions (Section 4).
Members of the Civil Defence Corps can be called out for training or specific civil defence functions by the State Government or Controller (Section 8(2)).
Members of the Corps can be required to discharge civil defence functions in other States and will be deemed members of that State's Corps with corresponding powers and liabilities (Section 8(3)).
Regulations can be made by the Central Government regarding the organization, service conditions, discipline, and functions of Civil Defence Corps members (Section 9).

penalties: Contravention of rules made under sub-section (1) of Section 3 or any order made thereunder can be punishable with fine up to five hundred rupees, and a further fine of fifty rupees per day for continuing contravention (original provision).

As amended by Act 42 of 1971 (during emergency and six months thereafter), contravention of rules made under sub-section (1) or any order made or direction given thereunder shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and State Governments are empowered to make rules and regulations. The Controller has powers related to the dismissal of members of the Civil Defence Corps. Enforcement would likely involve relevant government departments and authorities responsible for civil defence and disaster management.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the promulgation of rules and regulations by the Central Government, the constitution and command of Civil Defence Corps by State Governments, and the potential for legal prosecution in case of contravention of these rules and regulations.

rights: Members of the Civil Defence Corps have the right to appeal against dismissal to the State Government (Section 7).
Members of the Civil Defence Corps are protected by the provisions of the Personal Injuries (Emergency Provisions) Act in case of injuries sustained during service (Section 10).
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act (Section 18).
duties: Members of the Civil Defence Corps have a duty to perform functions assigned to them in relation to civil defence (Section 8(1)).
Members of the Civil Defence Corps must comply with directions given by the Director of Civil Defence (Section 4(2)).
Owners or occupiers of buildings, structures, or premises may be required to make arrangements for fire detection and prevention (Section 3(t)).
obligations: Members of the Civil Defence Corps are obligated to discharge their duties satisfactorily and are subject to disciplinary action for misconduct (Section 6(1)).
Members of the Civil Defence Corps can be called out for training or specific civil defence functions and must comply (Section 8(2)).
Persons may be required to comply with any scheme of civil defence (Section 3(y)).
Persons in specified areas may be required to remain indoors except under a written permit (Section 3(v)).

key_procedures: Constitution of Civil Defence Corps: State Government constitutes the Corps, appoints a Controller, and may designate existing organizations (Section 4).
Appointment of Members: State Government appoints fit and willing persons as members; Controller appoints members to offices or commands (Section 5).
Dismissal of Members: Controller may dismiss a member for unsatisfactory duties or misconduct after inquiry, or summarily if presence is undesirable (Section 6).
Appeal against Dismissal: A dismissed member can appeal to the State Government within 30 days (Section 7).
Making of Rules: Central Government makes rules for civil defence by notification, covering various aspects of preparedness and response (Section 3).
Making of Regulations: Central Government makes regulations for carrying out the purposes of the Civil Defence Corps chapter (Section 9).
administration: The Central Government and State Governments are the primary administrative bodies. The Central Government makes rules and regulations, while State Governments constitute and manage Civil Defence Corps. The Controller leads the Corps in a specific area, and a Director of Civil Defence may be appointed for coordination within a State.
important_notes: The Act's commencement in a State was tied to the expiry of the Defence of India Act, 1962, and different dates could be appointed for different areas (Section 1(3)).
The Act was amended by Act 3 of 2010 to include disaster management within the definition of 'civil defence' (Section 2(a)).
The penalty provisions for contravention of rules were significantly enhanced by Act 42 of 1971, introducing imprisonment up to three years.
Ordinary avocations of life are to be interfered with as little as possible (Section 13).
Measures taken for the protection of the Armed Forces are not covered by this Act (Section 15).

title: THE ANDHRA PRADESH AND MYSORE (TRANSFER OF TERRITORY) ACT, 1968
purpose: To provide for the transfer of certain territory from the State of Mysore to the State of Andhra Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.

scope.geographical: The Act applies to the territory specified in the Schedule, which is transferred from the State of Mysore to the State of Andhra Pradesh. Specifically, it becomes part of the Hindupur taluk of Anantapur district in Andhra Pradesh.
scope.subject_matter: The Act covers the legal, administrative, and political adjustments required for the transfer of territory, including amendments to constitutional schedules, constituencies, jurisdiction of High Courts, appropriation of funds, assets and liabilities, and the extension of laws.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The 1st day of October, 1968.
key_definitions.assembly_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.council_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.parliamentary_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
