key_definitions.sitting_member: A person who, immediately before the appointed day, is a member of either House of Parliament or of the Legislature of a State.
key_definitions.transferred_territory: The territory specified in the Schedule and transferred from the State of Mysore to the State of Andhra Pradesh by section 3.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Andhra Pradesh and Mysore (Transfer of Territory) Act, 1968.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'assembly constituency', 'council constituency', 'parliamentary constituency', 'sitting member', and 'transferred territory'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of territory from Mysore to Andhra Pradesh.
main_sections.description: Provides for the addition of the specified territory to Andhra Pradesh, its cessation from Mysore, and its inclusion in the Hindupur taluk of Anantapur district. It also reserves the State Government's power to alter district or taluk boundaries.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the changes in the territories of Andhra Pradesh and Mysore due to the transfer.

main_sections.section_title: Extent of parliamentary and assembly Constituencies.
main_sections.description: Details how the transferred territory will cease to be part of existing constituencies in Mysore and form part of new constituencies in Andhra Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Provision as to sitting members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies.
main_sections.description: Ensures that sitting members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies continue to be members despite the alteration in constituency boundaries.
Addresses how references to districts in existing Delimitation of Council Constituencies Orders will be construed in light of the territorial transfer.
States that sitting members of Legislative Councils whose constituencies are altered will be deemed to have been elected to the altered constituency.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of Andhra Pradesh High Court.
main_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the Andhra Pradesh High Court to the transferred territory and clarifies that the Mysore High Court will have no jurisdiction, with provisions for pending proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in transferred territory under existing Appropriation Acts.
main_sections.description: Ensures that existing Appropriation Acts of Andhra Pradesh will apply to the transferred territory for expenditure during the financial year 1968-69.
Governs the transfer of all land, stores, articles, goods, rights, liabilities, and obligations of the State of Mysore in relation to the transferred territory to the State of Andhra Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards.
main_sections.description: Deems State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards to have been constituted for the altered areas of Mysore and Andhra Pradesh.

Specifies that laws in force in Hindupur taluk of Andhra Pradesh will extend to the transferred territory, and laws in force in the transferred territory will cease to be in force unless they were in force in Hindupur taluk, except for past actions.
Grants courts, tribunals, and authorities the power to construe laws applied to the transferred territory for easier application, without altering the substance.
Provides for the substitution or addition of the State of Andhra Pradesh as a party in legal proceedings where the State of Mysore was a party concerning transferred property, rights, or liabilities.
Deals with the transfer of pending proceedings (excluding High Court cases) from areas that become part of Mysore to the corresponding authorities in Andhra Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of provisions inconsistent with other laws.
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act will prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.
Empowers the President to issue orders to remove any difficulties arising in the implementation of the Act.
Authorizes the Central Government to make rules to give effect to the provisions of the Act, subject to parliamentary approval.

important_rules: Rule: As from the appointed day (October 1, 1968), the specified territory shall be added to Andhra Pradesh and cease to form part of Mysore.
Rule: The transferred territory shall be included in and form part of the Hindupur taluk of Anantapur district in Andhra Pradesh.

Rule: Laws in force in Hindupur taluk of Andhra Pradesh shall extend to the transferred territory, and laws only in force in the transferred territory shall cease to have effect, except for past actions.
Rule: All land, stores, articles, goods, rights, liabilities, and obligations of Mysore in relation to the transferred territory shall pass to Andhra Pradesh.
Rule: The jurisdiction of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh shall extend to the transferred territory, and the Mysore High Court shall have no jurisdiction, subject to provisions for pending cases.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act itself provides the framework for transfer and adjustments. Enforcement of specific laws extended to the transferred territory would be by the respective authorities in Andhra Pradesh. The President has the power to remove difficulties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legal and administrative mechanisms of the State of Andhra Pradesh, and through orders issued by the President to remove difficulties.

rights: The right of the State of Andhra Pradesh to receive the transferred territory and its associated assets and liabilities.
The right of sitting members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies to continue in their positions despite constituency changes.
duties: The duty of the State of Mysore to transfer the specified territory.
The duty of the State of Andhra Pradesh to accept the transferred territory and assume its rights, liabilities, and obligations.
The duty of relevant authorities to ensure the smooth transition of laws and legal proceedings.
obligations: Obligations of the State of Mysore in relation to the transferred territory are transferred to the State of Andhra Pradesh.
The obligation to ensure that existing appropriation acts continue to apply to the transferred territory for the specified financial year.

key_procedures: Procedure: The transfer of territory from Mysore to Andhra Pradesh occurs on the appointed day (October 1, 1968).
Procedure: Amendments to the Constitution's First Schedule are made to reflect the territorial changes.
Procedure: Constituencies are redefined to include the transferred territory within Andhra Pradesh's framework.
Procedure: Pending legal proceedings relating to the transferred territory are either transferred to Andhra Pradesh or handled by the Mysore High Court under specific conditions.
Procedure: The Central Government can make rules, subject to parliamentary review, to facilitate the implementation of the Act.
administration: The primary administration of the transferred territory will fall under the Government of Andhra Pradesh. The Central Government has the power to make rules and remove difficulties. The President can issue orders for removing difficulties.
important_notes: Note: The State Government of Andhra Pradesh retains the power to alter the name, extent, or boundaries of any district or taluk in the State after the appointed day.

Note: Any proceedings pending in the Mysore High Court relatable to the transferred territory shall be heard and disposed of by that High Court, and its orders will have effect as if made by the Andhra Pradesh High Court.
Note: The provisions of this Act have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law.

title: The Insecticides Act, 1968
purpose: To regulate the import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution and use of insecticides with a view to prevent risk to human beings or animals, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to all activities related to insecticides, including their import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution, and use. It also covers substances which may be declared as insecticides by the Central Government.

key_definitions.animals: Animals useful to human beings and includes fish and fowl, and such kinds of wild life as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify, being kinds which, in its opinions, it is desirable to protect or preserve.
key_definitions.board: The Central Insecticides Board constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.central_insecticides_laboratory: The Central Insecticides Laboratory established or, as the case may be, the Institution specified, under section 16.
key_definitions.import: Bringing into any place within the territories to which this Act extends from a place outside those territories.
key_definitions.insecticide: Any substance specified in the Schedule; or such other substances (including fungicides and weedicides) as the Central Government may, after consultation with the Board, by notification in the Official Gazette, include in the Schedule from time to time; or any preparation containing any one or more of such substances.
key_definitions.manufacture: In relation to any insecticide, includes any process or part of a process for making, altering, finishing, packing, labelling, breaking up or otherwise treating or adopting any insecticide with a view to its sale, distribution or use but does not include the packing or breaking up of any insecticide in the ordinary course of retail business; and any process by which a preparation containing an insecticide is formulated.
key_definitions.misbranded: An insecticide is deemed misbranded if its label contains false or misleading statements, is deceptive, lacks necessary warnings, doesn't display required information conspicuously, is not packed or labelled as required, refers to registration improperly, or has toxicity higher than prescribed or is mixed with substances altering its nature or quality.
key_definitions.package: A box, bottle, casket, tin, barrel, case, receptacle, sack, bag, wrapper, or other thing in which an insecticide is placed or packed.
key_definitions.premises: Any land, shop, stall or place where any insecticide is sold or manufactured or stored or used, and includes any vehicle carrying insecticide.
key_definitions.sale: The sale of any insecticide, whether for cash or on credit and whether by wholesale or retail, and includes an agreement for sale, an offer for sale, the exposing for sale or having in possession for sale of any insecticide and includes also an attempt to sell any such insecticide.
key_definitions.state_government: In relation to a Union territory, means the administrator thereof.
key_definitions.worker: A person employed under a contract of service or apprenticeship.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Insecticides Act, 1968, specifies its territorial extent to the whole of India, and outlines the commencement provisions, allowing the Central Government to appoint different dates for different provisions and states.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act are in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'animals', 'Board', 'Central Insecticides Laboratory', 'import', 'insecticide', 'Insecticide Analyst', 'Insecticide Inspector', 'label', 'licensing officer', 'manufacture', 'misbranded', 'package', 'premises', 'prescribed', 'registered', 'sale', 'State Government', and 'worker'.

Establishes the Central Insecticides Board to advise the Central and State Governments on technical matters arising from the administration of the Act. It details the composition of the Board, including ex officio members and nominated experts, and its functions concerning risks, safety measures, and the regulation of insecticides.

Constitutes a Registration Committee to register insecticides after scrutinizing their formulae and verifying claims regarding efficacy and safety. It outlines the composition of the committee, its functions, and procedures.

Requires any person desiring to import or manufacture an insecticide to apply for its registration to the Registration Committee. It also specifies a period for existing manufacturers/importers to apply for registration and provides for penalties for late applications.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any person intending to import or manufacture an insecticide must apply to the Registration Committee for its registration.
Rule 2: Existing importers or manufacturers must apply for registration within seventeen months of the commencement of the section, with penalties for delays.
Rule 3: Insecticides are considered misbranded if their labels are false or misleading, deceptive, lack necessary warnings, or do not comply with the Act's labeling requirements.

penalties: Penalties for late application for registration of insecticides (Rs. 100 per month or part thereof).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Insecticide Inspectors are appointed to enforce the Act. The Central Government also has powers to issue directions and make rules, and State Governments can make rules for their respective states. Special Courts may be established for the trial of offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves inspection of premises, seizure of insecticides, analysis of samples by Insecticide Analysts, and prosecution of offenders. The Central and State Governments can make rules to prescribe procedures and standards. The Act also outlines powers of Insecticide Inspectors, including search, seizure, and taking samples.

rights: Right to appeal against the decision of a licensing officer.
Right to appeal against non-registration or cancellation of registration.
duties: Manufacturers and importers have a duty to register their insecticides.
Persons are bound to disclose places where insecticides are manufactured or kept.
Compliance with labeling and packaging requirements is mandatory.
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to constitute the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee.
Manufacturers and importers have an obligation to ensure the safety of insecticides to human beings and animals.
Those involved in the trade of insecticides have an obligation to comply with all provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of insecticides: Application to the Registration Committee, scrutiny of formulae and claims, verification of efficacy and safety.
Procedure for obtaining a license: Application to a licensing officer, grant of license, and subsequent procedures for revocation, suspension, and amendment of licenses.
Procedure for analysis of insecticides: Taking of samples by Insecticide Inspectors, submission to Insecticide Analyst, and reporting of the analysis results.
Procedure for appeals: Appeals against decisions of licensing officers or the Registration Committee can be made to designated authorities or the Central Government.
administration: The Central Government, through the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee, administers the Act. State Governments also play a role in making rules and appointing licensing officers and inspectors.
important_notes: The Act commenced on different dates for different provisions and states, as notified by the Central Government.
The provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other existing law.
The Board and Registration Committee function even if there are vacancies or defects in their constitution.
Exemptions from certain provisions of the Act can be granted by the Central Government.

title: The Central Industrial Security Force Act, 1968
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for the better protection and security of industrial undertakings owned by the Central Government, certain other industrial undertakings, employees of all such undertakings and to provide technical consultancy services to industrial establishments in the private sector and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to industrial undertakings owned by the Central Government, joint ventures, private industrial undertakings, and employees of these undertakings. It also provides for technical consultancy services to industrial establishments in the private sector.

key_definitions.Director-General: The Director-General of the Force appointed under section 4.
key_definitions.enrolled_member_of_the_Force: Any subordinate officer, under officer, or any other member of the Force of a rank lower than that of an under officer.
key_definitions.Force: The Central Industrial Security Force constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Force custody: The arrest or confinement of a member of the Force in accordance with rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.industrial_undertaking: Any undertaking pertaining to a scheduled industry and includes an undertaking engaged in any other industry, or in any trade, business or service which may be regulated by Parliament by law.
key_definitions.industrial_undertaking_in_public_sector: An industrial undertaking owned, controlled or managed by a Government company, or a corporation established by or under a Central, Provincial or State Act, which is controlled or managed by the Government.
key_definitions.industrial_establishment: An industrial undertaking or a company as defined under section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956, or a firm registered under section 59 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, which is engaged in any industry, or in any trade, business or service.
key_definitions.joint_venture: A venture jointly undertaken by the Central Government or State Government with private industrial undertaking.
key_definitions.private_industrial_undertaking: An industry owned, controlled or managed by a person other than the Central or State Government or any industrial undertaking in public sector.
key_definitions.scheduled_industry: Any industry engaged in the manufacture or production of the articles mentioned in the First Schedule to the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.
key_definitions.subordinate_officer: A person appointed to the Force as an Inspector, a Sub-Inspector or an Assistant Sub-Inspector.
key_definitions.supervisory_officer: Any of the officers appointed under section 4 and includes any other officer appointed by the Central Government as a supervisory officer of the Force.
key_definitions.under_officer: A person appointed to the Force as a Head Constable, Naik or Lance Naik.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Central Industrial Security Force Act, 1968, its extent to the whole of India, and that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Director-General, enrolled member of the Force, Force, Force custody, industrial undertaking, industrial undertaking in public sector, industrial establishment, joint venture, private industrial undertaking, scheduled industry, subordinate officer, supervisory officer, and under officer.

Establishes and maintains the Central Industrial Security Force by the Central Government for the protection and security of industrial undertakings (owned by Central Government, joint venture, private) and to perform other entrusted duties. It also details the composition and remuneration of the Force members.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and powers of supervisory officers
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Director-General and other supervisory officers, who shall exercise powers and authority as provided by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of enrolled members of the Force
main_sections.description: States that the appointment of enrolled members of the Force rests with the Director-General, in accordance with prescribed rules. This power can also be exercised by other specified supervisory officers.

main_sections.section_title: Certificates of enrolled members of the Force
main_sections.description: Mandates that every enrolled member receives a certificate upon appointment, vesting them with the powers of an enrolled member. This certificate ceases to be effective when the person ceases to be an enrolled member.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence and administration of the Force
main_sections.description: Vests the superintendence of the Force in the Central Government. The command, supervision, and administration vest in the Director-General. The administration within local limits is carried out by other supervisory officers, who, in relation to industrial undertakings, function under the general supervision of the Managing Director.

main_sections.section_title: Dismissal, removal, etc., of members of the Force
main_sections.description: Allows supervisory officers to dismiss, remove, order compulsory retirement, or reduce in rank any enrolled member found remiss, negligent, or unfit. It also specifies punishments that can be awarded for careless or negligent discharge of duty, including fines, extra duties, removal from office, withholding of increments, and censure.

Provides a mechanism for enrolled members aggrieved by orders under section 8 to prefer an appeal within thirty days. It also outlines provisions for revision petitions and the power of the Central Government to call for and examine records of proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of members of the Force
main_sections.description: Details the duties of every member of the Force, including promptly obeying orders, protecting and safeguarding industrial undertakings (Central Government owned, joint venture, private), installations, and employees. It also includes performing other acts conducive to better protection and security.

important_rules: Members must promptly obey and execute all lawful orders from superior authority.

Members are responsible for protecting and safeguarding Central Government industrial undertakings, specified vital installations, joint ventures, private industrial undertakings, and their employees.
Supervisory officers can dismiss, remove, or reduce in rank enrolled members found negligent or unfit for duty.
Various punishments like fines, extra duties, and withholding of increments can be awarded for careless or negligent duty.
Aggrieved members have the right to appeal disciplinary orders and, in certain cases, file for revision.
Members are to be considered always on duty and liable for employment anywhere in India.

penalties: Fine to any amount not exceeding seven days' pay or reduction in pay scale.
Drill, extra guard, fatigue, or other duty.
Removal from any office of distinction or deprivation of any special emolument.
Withholding of increment of pay with or without cumulative effect.
Withholding of promotion.
Censure.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Supervisory officers (including the Director-General) are responsible for enforcing discipline and administering punishments. The Central Government has overarching authority for superintendence and can call for records of proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary actions such as dismissal, removal, reduction in rank, fines, extra duties, and other specified punishments. Appeals and revision processes are also part of the enforcement mechanism.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of dismissal, removal, etc.
Right to prefer a revision petition against an appellate order.
Right to be heard before an enhanced penalty is imposed.
duties: Promptly obey and execute all lawful orders from superior authority.
Protect and safeguard Central Government industrial undertakings and specified installations.
Protect and safeguard joint ventures, private industrial undertakings, and their employees.
Perform any other act conducive to the better protection and security of these undertakings and installations and their employees.
obligations: Enrolled members must possess a certificate issued by an authorized officer.
Members must surrender their certificates, arms, etc., upon ceasing to be members of the Force.
Members are liable to be employed anywhere in India.

key_procedures: Appointment of enrolled members of the Force by the Director-General (or as specified).
Issuance of certificates to enrolled members upon appointment.
Procedures for dismissal, removal, compulsory retirement, or reduction in rank of enrolled members by supervisory officers.
Procedure for filing an appeal against an order under section 8 within thirty days.
Procedure for filing a revision petition against an appellate order within six months.
Procedure for the Central Government or prescribed authority to call for and examine records of proceedings.
administration: The Central Government, through the Director-General and other supervisory officers.
important_notes: The Act was amended significantly in 1999 and 2009, expanding its scope to include joint ventures and private industrial undertakings, and introducing technical consultancy services.
The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) is an armed force of the Union.

title: THE JUDGES (INQUIRY) ACT, 1968
purpose: To regulate the procedure for the investigation and proof of the misbehaviour or incapacity of a judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court and for the presentation of an address by Parliament to the President and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts in India. The geographical scope is India.

key_definitions.Chairman: The Chairman of the Council of States.
key_definitions.Committee: A Committee constituted under section 3 for the purpose of investigating the misbehaviour or incapacity of a Judge.
key_definitions.Judge: A Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court, including the Chief Justice of India and the Chief Justice of a High Court.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Speaker: The Speaker of the House of the People.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Chairman', 'Committee', 'Judge', 'prescribed', and 'Speaker'.

main_sections.section_title: Investigation into misbehaviour or incapacity of Judge by Committee
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for initiating an investigation into a Judge's misbehaviour or incapacity. This includes notice of a motion for removal, admission of the motion, constitution of a three-member committee, framing of charges, communication of charges to the Judge, opportunity for defence, and medical examination in cases of alleged incapacity.

Details the procedure for the Committee to conduct its investigation, including the right of the Judge to cross-examine witnesses, adduce evidence, and be heard. The Committee submits its report to the Speaker or Chairman, which is then laid before the respective Houses of Parliament.

Grants the Committee the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning persons, enforcing attendance, examining on oath, requiring production of documents, receiving evidence, and issuing commissions.

main_sections.section_title: Consideration of report and procedure for presentation of an address for removal of Judge
main_sections.description: Describes the parliamentary procedure following the Committee's report. If the Judge is found not guilty, no further steps are taken. If found guilty, the report and motion are considered by Parliament, and if adopted by both Houses, an address is presented to the President for the Judge's removal.

Establishes a Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes. The Joint Committee consists of fifteen members and has the power to regulate its procedure. It can make rules concerning the transmission of motions between Houses, presentation of addresses, allowances, facilities for defence, and other necessary matters.

important_rules: Rule 1: The process for initiating an investigation into a Judge's misbehaviour or incapacity begins with a notice of a motion for removal signed by a specified number of members in the House of the People or Council of States.
Rule 2: Upon admission of the motion, a Committee of three members (one from Supreme Court Judges, one from High Court Chief Justices, and one distinguished jurist) is constituted to investigate.
Rule 3: The Committee frames definite charges against the Judge, communicates them, and provides a reasonable opportunity for the Judge to present a written defence.
Rule 4: In cases of alleged physical or mental incapacity, a Medical Board may be appointed to examine the Judge, and its report is submitted to the Committee.
Rule 5: The Committee has the powers of a civil court for conducting its investigation.
Rule 6: If the Committee's report finds the Judge guilty of misbehaviour or incapacity, and the motion is adopted by both Houses of Parliament, an address for removal is presented to the President.

Rule 7: A Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament is constituted to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, which require approval by the Speaker and Chairman and publication in the Official Gazette to take effect.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Speaker of the House of the People and the Chairman of the Council of States have the authority to initiate and oversee the process. Parliament as a whole is responsible for the final decision and presentation of the address for removal. The Central Government may appoint an advocate to conduct the case against the Judge.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves parliamentary procedures, including the admission and consideration of motions, constitution of committees, investigation, reporting, and adoption of resolutions by both Houses of Parliament. The ultimate enforcement of removal is through an address presented to the President.

rights: The Judge has the right to be informed of the charges against them.
The Judge has the right to a reasonable opportunity of presenting a written statement of defence.
The Judge has the right to cross-examine witnesses.
The Judge has the right to adduce evidence.
The Judge has the right to be heard in their defence.
The Judge has the right to a medical examination by a Medical Board in cases of alleged incapacity.
The Judge has the right to present a fresh written statement of defence if charges are amended.
duties: The Judge has a duty to submit to medical examination if required by the Committee for alleged incapacity.
The Judge has a duty to cooperate with the investigation process.

key_procedures: Initiation of Investigation: A motion for the removal of a Judge is given notice in either the House of the People (by 100 members) or the Council of States (by 50 members).
Admission of Motion: The Speaker or Chairman, after consultation, may admit or refuse the motion.
Committee Constitution: If admitted, a Committee of three members is constituted.
Framing Charges: The Committee frames definite charges against the Judge.
Defence Opportunity: Charges and grounds are communicated to the Judge, who is given an opportunity to submit a written defence.
Medical Examination (if applicable): In cases of alleged incapacity, a Medical Board may examine the Judge.
Committee Investigation: The Committee conducts the investigation, allowing the Judge to cross-examine, present evidence, and be heard.
Committee Report: The Committee submits its findings on each charge and observations to the Speaker/Chairman.
Parliamentary Consideration: The report is laid before Parliament. If the Judge is found guilty, the motion is considered by both Houses.
Address for Removal: If the motion is adopted by both Houses in accordance with constitutional provisions, an address is presented to the President for the Judge's removal.
administration: The administration of this Act involves the Speaker of the House of the People, the Chairman of the Council of States, the Committee constituted under Section 3, the Medical Board (if appointed), and the Joint Committee for making rules. The Central Government has a role in appointing the commencement date and potentially an advocate.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

If notices of a motion are given on the same day in both Houses, the Committee is constituted jointly only if the motion is admitted in both. If given on different dates, the later notice stands rejected.
The rules made under the Act by the Joint Committee must be approved and confirmed by both the Speaker and the Chairman and published in the Official Gazette to take effect.

title: The Legislative Assembly of Nagaland (Change in Representation) Act, 1968
purpose: To provide for a change in representation in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland and to make consequential amendments in the State of Nagaland Act, 1962 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
scope: This Act applies to the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland. It specifically addresses changes in the number of seats and their allocation, particularly concerning the Tuensang district and the rest of the State of Nagaland. The provisions are applicable for the period referred to in clause (2) of article 371A of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland (Change in Representation) Act, 1968.

main_sections.section_title: Change in representation in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland
main_sections.description: This section specifies that for the period referred to in clause (2) of article 371A of the Constitution, the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland shall be increased from forty-six to fifty-two. It further details the allocation of these seats: twelve seats for the Tuensang district, filled by persons chosen by the members of the regional council, and forty seats for the rest of the State of Nagaland, filled by direct elections from assembly constituencies.
This section, which dealt with the amendment of the State of Nagaland Act, 1962, has been repealed.
This section, which dealt with the amendment of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, has been repealed.

main_sections.section_title: Saving as to present Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: This section states that nothing in the Act shall affect any representation in the present Legislative Assembly of Nagaland until its dissolution.

important_rules: For the period specified in Article 371A(2) of the Constitution, the total seats in the Nagaland Legislative Assembly will increase from 46 to 52.
Out of the 52 seats, 12 will be for the Tuensang district, filled by members of the regional council chosen from amongst themselves, in a manner specified by the Governor.
The remaining 40 seats will be filled by direct elections from assembly constituencies in the rest of Nagaland.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but likely the Election Commission of India and the Governor of Nagaland for specific aspects.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of elections and notifications by the Governor as specified.

key_procedures: The Governor of Nagaland, after consulting the regional council for the Tuensang district, will specify by notification in the Official Gazette the manner in which the 12 seats for the Tuensang district will be filled by persons chosen from amongst themselves by the members of the regional council.
Direct elections will be held for the 40 assembly constituencies in the rest of Nagaland.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but likely involves the State Election Commission and the Governor's office for matters related to the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland.
important_notes: Sections 3 and 4 of the Act have been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1974.
The changes in representation are applicable until the dissolution of the present Legislative Assembly, after which the new representation will take effect.

title: The President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969
purpose: To provide for the discharge of the functions of the President of India in certain contingencies not covered by the Constitution, specifically when both the President and Vice-President are unable to perform their duties.
scope: This Act applies to the discharge of the functions of the President of India in India. It specifically addresses contingencies related to the office of the President and the Vice-President.

key_definitions.Second Schedule: The Second Schedule to the Constitution of India.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969.
Defines 'President', 'Vice-President', and 'Second Schedule' for the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Discharge of President’s functions in certain contingencies
main_sections.description: Details the circumstances under which the Chief Justice of India or the seniormost Judge of the Supreme Court will discharge the functions of the President. This includes situations where both the President and Vice-President are absent, deceased, resigned, or removed, or when the Vice-President is acting as President and becomes unable to discharge those functions.

important_rules: In the event of vacancies in the offices of both the President and the Vice-President, the Chief Justice of India (or the seniormost available Supreme Court Judge in his absence) shall discharge the President's functions until a new President or Vice-President enters office.

If the Vice-President, while discharging the President's functions, ceases to hold office, the Chief Justice of India (or the seniormost available Supreme Court Judge) shall discharge the President's functions until the President resumes duties or a new Vice-President is elected.

If the Vice-President is unable to discharge the President's functions (whether acting as President or discharging the President's functions) due to absence, illness, or any other cause, the Chief Justice of India (or the seniormost available Supreme Court Judge) shall discharge the President's functions until the President or Vice-President resumes duties, as applicable.

The person discharging the President's functions under this section will have all the powers and immunities of the President and will be entitled to emoluments, allowances, and privileges determined by Parliament, or as specified in the Second Schedule until such a law is made.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Chief Justice of India or the seniormost Judge of the Supreme Court of India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By the designated judicial officer stepping in to perform the duties of the President as stipulated in the Act.

rights: The right to hold and exercise all the powers and immunities of the President during the period of discharging Presidential functions.
The right to receive emoluments, allowances, and privileges as determined by Parliament or specified in the Second Schedule.
duties: Duty to discharge the functions of the President in specified contingencies.
Duty to act impartially and in accordance with the Constitution and laws while discharging Presidential functions.
obligations: Obligation to act when a contingency arises as defined in the Act.
Obligation to perform the duties until the rightful President or Vice-President resumes office or is elected.

key_procedures: Assessment of the occurrence of vacancies or inability to discharge functions in the offices of the President and Vice-President.
Designation of the Chief Justice of India or the seniormost available Supreme Court Judge to discharge Presidential functions.
Continuation of discharge of functions until a permanent or acting President/Vice-President is in place.
administration: The Act is implemented through the judicial branch, specifically the Chief Justice of India and the Supreme Court of India.
important_notes: This Act addresses contingencies not provided for in Chapter I of Part V of the Constitution.
The provisions of this Act are applicable until a new President or Vice-President is elected and assumes office, or the original incumbent resumes duties.

title: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
purpose: To provide for the regulation of registration of births and deaths and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the registration of births and deaths occurring within designated local areas, with specific provisions for registration of births and deaths of citizens outside India.

key_definitions.live-birth: Means the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of pregnancy, which, after such expulsion or extraction, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, and each product of such birth is considered live-born.
key_definitions.still-birth: Means foetal death where a product of conception has attained at least the prescribed period of gestation.
key_definitions.foetal_death: Means absence of all evidence of life prior to the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception irrespective of the duration of pregnancy.
key_definitions.death: Means the permanent disappearance of all evidence of life at any time after live-birth has taken place.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.State_Government: In relation to a Union territory, means the Administrator thereof.
key_definitions.Aadhaar_number: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (a) of section 2 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 (18 of 2016).
key_definitions.adoption: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (2) of section 2 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (2 of 2016).
key_definitions.database: Means the organised collection of data, generally stored and accessed in electronic form from a computer network.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the procedure for its commencement in different states and union territories through notification by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as birth, death, live-birth, still-birth, foetal death, prescribed, State Government, and also clarifies interpretation of references to laws not in force.

Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Registrar General of India, other officers for discharging functions under the Act, and outlines their duties in coordinating registration activities, maintaining a national database of registered births and deaths, and submitting annual reports.

Empowers the State Government to appoint a Chief Registrar for the State and other officers. It defines the Chief Registrar's role as the chief executive authority for implementing the Act within the state and their responsibility for coordinating and supervising registration work and submitting reports.

Allows for the appointment of a District Registrar and Additional District Registrars for each revenue district. The District Registrar is responsible for superintending the registration of births and deaths within the district and ensuring the implementation of the Act.

Authorizes the appointment of a Registrar for each local area (municipality, panchayat, etc.). Registrars are tasked with entering information about births and deaths into registers and informing themselves of such events within their jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Persons required to register births and deaths
main_sections.description: Specifies the individuals who are obligated to report births and deaths to the Registrar.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of certain persons to notify births and deaths and to certify cause of death
main_sections.description: Details the duty of specific individuals (e.g., medical practitioners) to notify births and deaths and to certify the cause of death.

main_sections.section_title: Delayed registration of births and deaths
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for registering births and deaths that occur after the prescribed period.

main_sections.section_title: Correction or cancellation of entry in the register of births and deaths
main_sections.description: Provides the mechanism for correcting or cancelling entries in the birth and death registers.

main_sections.section_title: Registrars to keep registers in the prescribed form
main_sections.description: Mandates that Registrars maintain registers in the form prescribed by the rules.

main_sections.section_title: Registrars to send periodical returns to the Chief Registrar for compilation
main_sections.description: Requires Registrars to submit periodic returns to the Chief Registrar for the purpose of compiling statistics.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision as to registration of births and deaths of citizens outside India
main_sections.description: Addresses the registration of births and deaths of Indian citizens occurring outside India.
Defines the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act.
Confers the power upon the Central Government and State Governments to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous enactment on the subject and provides for savings.

important_rules: Reporting births and deaths must be done by specific persons (e.g., head of household, medical attendant) within a prescribed time frame to the Registrar of the area where the event occurred.
Delayed registration of births and deaths requires specific procedures and may involve an affidavit or inquiry.
Registrars must maintain registers in the prescribed form and enter all information given to them accurately.
Registrars are required to send periodical returns to the Chief Registrar for compilation of vital statistics.
Registration of births and deaths of citizens outside India can be done through diplomatic or consular officers.
The Registrar General of India is responsible for maintaining a national database of registered births and deaths and making it available to specified authorities.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contravening the provisions of the Act, including failure to comply with reporting requirements or providing false information. Section 23 outlines these penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforcement is primarily carried out by the Registrar General of India, Chief Registrars, District Registrars, and Registrars appointed under the Act. State Governments and the Central Government also have oversight and rule-making powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the appointment of officials to register births and deaths, maintenance of accurate records, periodic reporting, and the imposition of penalties for non-compliance. The establishment of a national and state-level database also facilitates enforcement and data utilization.

rights: Right to obtain a certificate of registration of a birth or death.
Right to search the births and deaths register.
Citizens have the right to have their births and deaths registered.
duties: Duty of certain persons (e.g., heads of households, medical practitioners) to report births and deaths.
Duty of Registrars to accurately record information in the registers.
Duty of Registrars to send periodical returns to the Chief Registrar.
Duty of Chief Registrars to coordinate and supervise registration work in the state.
Duty of Registrar General of India to coordinate activities of Chief Registrars and maintain a national database.
obligations: Obligation to register births and deaths within the prescribed time frame.
Obligation to provide correct information for registration.
Obligation to comply with rules and directions issued under the Act.
Chief Registrars and Registrars have an obligation to share data for the unified state-level and national-level databases.

key_procedures: Registration of birth or death by the Registrar for the local area.
Notification of birth or death by designated individuals.
Procedure for delayed registration of births and deaths.
Procedure for correction or cancellation of entries in the register.
Issuance of a certificate of registration of birth or death.
Submission of periodical returns by Registrars to the Chief Registrar.
Maintenance of national and state-level databases of registered births and deaths.
administration: The administration of the Act involves the Registrar General of India at the national level and Chief Registrars at the state level, supported by District Registrars and Registrars at the local level. The Central Government and State Governments are responsible for appointing these officials and making rules.
important_notes: The Act can come into force in different parts of a state on different dates appointed by the Central Government.
The Act is not in derogation of the Indian Aircraft Act, 1934 (32 of 1934), or the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908), but provides for registration of births and deaths.

The database of registered births and deaths maintained at the national and state levels can be made available to authorities dealing with population registers, electoral rolls, Aadhaar numbers, ration cards, passports, driving licenses, property registration, and other specified national-level databases.

title: The Union Territories (Separation of Judicial and Executive Functions) Act, 1969
purpose: To provide for the separation of judicial and executive functions in Union territories.
scope: Applies to all Union territories except the Union territory of Chandigarh. The Act comes into force on dates appointed by the Central Government via notification. The definition of 'Union territory' in sections 3 to 9 excludes Chandigarh.

key_definitions.Union territory: Means any Union territory other than the Union territory of Chandigarh (for sections 3 to 9).

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the procedure for its commencement.
Defines 'Union territory' for the purposes of sections 3 to 9 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendments to Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, shall be amended in the manner and to the extent detailed in the Schedule for the purpose of separating judicial and executive functions in Union territories.

main_sections.section_title: Amendments not to render invalid notifications, etc., before commencement of Act
main_sections.description: Ensures that amendments made by this Act do not invalidate any notifications, orders, or actions taken before the Act's commencement, provided they were duly made or issued.

main_sections.section_title: Functions exercisable by Judicial and Executive Magistrates
main_sections.description: Distinguishes functions based on their nature: functions involving appreciation or sifting of evidence, or leading to punishment, penalty, or detention, shall be exercised by a Judicial Magistrate. Administrative or executive functions, such as granting licenses or sanctioning prosecutions, shall be exercised by an Executive Magistrate.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of laws in transferred areas in Himachal Pradesh
main_sections.description: Provides for the repeal of the Punjab Separation of Judicial and Executive Functions Act, 1964, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in specific transferred areas of Himachal Pradesh upon the commencement of this Act, with exceptions for things done or omitted before repeal.

Saves certain things from the operation of the Act, including actions taken before commencement, accrued rights, liabilities, penalties, and legal proceedings. It also addresses the transfer of pending legal proceedings to the appropriate Magistrate or Court.

Empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions by order, in consultation with the High Court, for a period of three years from commencement. Orders must be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Legislative Assembly of Union territory to amend this Act
main_sections.description: Grants the Legislative Assembly of a Union territory the power to amend this Act in its application to that territory, notwithstanding anything in the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963.

important_rules: Functions involving evidence appreciation, formulation of decisions leading to punishment, penalty, or detention shall be exercised by a Judicial Magistrate.
Administrative or executive functions (e.g., granting licenses, sanctioning prosecutions) shall be exercised by an Executive Magistrate.
The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, is amended by this Act to facilitate the separation of judicial and executive functions.
Amendments made by this Act do not invalidate pre-commencement actions, rights, or liabilities.
Pending legal proceedings will be transferred to the appropriate Magistrate or Court if jurisdiction changes due to the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for removal of difficulties), and relevant judicial and executive authorities as per the amended Code of Criminal Procedure.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and specific orders issued by the Central Government for removing difficulties.

rights: The right to have judicial functions performed by Judicial Magistrates and executive functions by Executive Magistrates.
Continuance of legal proceedings and remedies in respect of rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, forfeitures, or punishments incurred before the commencement of the Act.
duties: Duty to exercise functions by the appropriate class of Magistrate (Judicial or Executive) as defined by the Act.
Duty to adhere to the amended Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
obligations: The obligation to consult with the High Court when altering limits or numbers of divisions and districts (Section 7 of Schedule).
The obligation to consult with the High Court when appointing Magistrates or defining their powers.
Obligation to lay orders made for removing difficulties before each House of Parliament.

key_procedures: Appointment of Judicial and Executive Magistrates with defined classes and powers.
Alteration of limits or numbers of sessions divisions and districts in consultation with the High Court.
Procedure for the Central Government to remove difficulties by order, subject to parliamentary oversight.
administration: Central Government (for appointing commencement dates and removing difficulties), State Governments and High Courts (for appointment and defining powers of Magistrates, and for administrative matters related to courts).
important_notes: The Act explicitly excludes the Union territory of Chandigarh.
The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, has been superseded by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Act 2 of 1974), as noted in footnotes.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to three years from the commencement of the Act.

title: The Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Act, 1969
purpose: To declare the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library at Patna as an institution of national importance and to provide for its administration and certain other connected matters.
scope: The Act applies to the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library located at Patna, Bihar, and its administration. It establishes a Board for the management and development of the library.

key_definitions.Board: The Board established under section 4 of the Act, known as the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Board.
key_definitions.deed_of_trust: Deed of trust No. 217 executed on January 14, 1891, by Maulvi Khuda Bakhsh Khan Bahadur of Muradpur.
key_definitions.Fund: The fund referred to in section 19, maintained by the Board.
key_definitions.library: The Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library declared as an institution of national importance under this Act.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board, including the Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library at Patna as an institution of national importance.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairman', 'deed of trust', 'Fund', 'library', 'member', 'prescribed', and 'State Government'.

Establishes a Board, to be known as the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Board, for the purposes of the Act from a date appointed by the Central Government. The Board is constituted as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Details the composition of the Board, including ex-officio members (Governor of Bihar, Accountant General, Bihar, Director of the Library) and nominated members by the Central and State Governments.

Outlines the general duty of the Board to manage the library, plan and implement development programs (including microfilming rare manuscripts), and perform other functions assigned by the Central Government. It also specifies steps for promoting instruction and research related to libraries and for the advancement of learning and dissemination of knowledge.

Grants the Board powers necessary or expedient for carrying out its duties, subject to conditions imposed by the Central Government. It also allows the Board to acquire manuscripts, books, and other articles for preservation in the library.

main_sections.section_title: Grants by Central Government to Board
main_sections.description: States that the Central Government may provide sums of money to the Board as grants, loans, or otherwise for efficient discharge of its functions, subject to appropriation by Parliament.

Establishes a Fund for the Board, to which moneys from the Central Government, State Government, fees, grants, gifts, donations, bequests, subscriptions, contributions, transfers, and other sources are credited. The Board can expend sums from this Fund for its functions.

important_rules: The Board shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and enter into contracts.

Members of the Board must disclose any direct or indirect interest in a contract made or proposed to be made by the Board, and shall not participate in deliberations or decisions regarding that contract after disclosure.
The Central Government may issue directions to the Board.
The Board must manage the library and plan, promote, organize, and implement programs for its development on modern scientific lines.
The Board can acquire manuscripts, books, and articles worthy of preservation in the library.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Board, with appointed officers and employees, are responsible for the administration and enforcement of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the establishment and functioning of the Board, the management of the library, the collection and utilization of funds, and adherence to rules and regulations made under the Act. Section 26 provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

rights: The right to manage and develop the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library.
The right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The right to enter into contracts.
The right to sue and be sued in the name of the Board.
The right to acquire manuscripts, books, and articles for preservation.
The right to receive grants and funds for its operations.
duties: To manage the library efficiently.
To plan, promote, organize, and implement programs for the library's development.
To provide for instruction and research in library matters and for the advancement of learning and dissemination of knowledge.
To maintain accounts and submit reports.
To comply with directions issued by the Central Government.
To ensure that nominated members do not have prejudicial financial or other interests.
obligations: The Board has an obligation to manage the library in accordance with the deed of trust and the provisions of the Act.
Existing employees of the library become employees of the Board with their existing terms and conditions, which cannot be altered to their disadvantage without Central Government approval.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Board: The Central Government appoints a date for the establishment of the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Board.
Nomination of Board Members: The Central and State Governments nominate members to the Board based on specific criteria.
Meetings of the Board: The Board meets at prescribed times and places, with rules of procedure for transacting business, including quorum and voting.
Authentication of Orders: Orders and decisions of the Board are authenticated by the Chairman or an authorized member, and other instruments by an authorized officer.
Appointment of Staff: The Board appoints its officers and employees, with recruitment and service conditions governed by regulations.
Financial Management: The Board maintains a Fund, receives grants and other income, and expends money for its functions. Accounts are audited, and reports are submitted.
Rule Making: The Central Government has the power to make rules, and the Board has the power to make regulations, to carry out the provisions of the Act.
administration: The Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Board is responsible for the administration of the Act and the library. The Central Government oversees the Board and can issue directions.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act is determined by a notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government.

The tenure, remuneration, and terms and conditions of service of existing employees transferred to the Board shall not be altered to their disadvantage without the previous approval of the Central Government.

title: The Oaths Act, 1969
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to judicial oaths and for certain other purposes.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to courts, persons having authority to receive evidence, members of the Armed Forces (with certain exceptions), witnesses, interpreters, jurors, and affidavit preparation. It does not apply to proceedings before courts martial or oaths, affirmations or declarations prescribed by the Central Government for members of the Armed Forces.

key_definitions.witnesses: All persons who may lawfully be examined, or give, or be required to give, evidence by or before any court or person having by law or consent of parties authority to examine such persons or to receive evidence.
key_definitions.interpreters: Persons who interpret questions put to, and evidence given by, witnesses.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Oaths Act, 1969' and specifies its territorial extent.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of certain oaths and affirmations
main_sections.description: Exempts proceedings before courts martial and oaths/affirmations for members of the Armed Forces prescribed by the Central Government from the Act's provisions.

Details which courts and persons have the power to administer oaths and affirmations, including those with authority to receive evidence and commanding officers of Armed Forces stations or ships. It also covers the administration of oaths and affirmations for affidavits.

main_sections.section_title: Oaths or affirmations to be made by witnesses, interpreters and jurors
main_sections.description: Mandates oaths or affirmations for witnesses, interpreters, and jurors. It includes a proviso for children under twelve years of age and specifies that an accused person in a criminal proceeding is not generally required to take an oath unless examined as a witness for the defence.

main_sections.section_title: Affirmation by persons desiring to affirm
main_sections.description: Allows witnesses, interpreters, or jurors to make an affirmation instead of an oath.

Prescribes that oaths and affirmations should be administered according to the forms given in the Schedule. It also allows for other forms if they are common amongst a person's class and not repugnant to justice or decency.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings and evidence not invalidated by omission of oath or irregularity
main_sections.description: States that any omission, substitution, or irregularity in administering an oath or affirmation will not invalidate proceedings or render evidence inadmissible, nor will it affect the witness's obligation to state the truth.

main_sections.section_title: Persons giving evidence bound to state the truth
main_sections.description: Obligates every person giving evidence before an authorized court or person to state the truth.
Repeals the Indian Oaths Act, 1873, and provides for savings regarding agreements made under the repealed Act.

important_rules: Witnesses, interpreters, and jurors must take an oath or make an affirmation before giving evidence or performing their duties.
A witness, interpreter, or juror has the right to make an affirmation instead of an oath.
Oaths and affirmations are to be administered using the forms specified in the Schedule, unless specific conditions for alternative forms are met.
All persons giving evidence are bound to state the truth.

penalties: The Act primarily focuses on the administration of oaths and affirmations and the obligation to tell the truth. While section 8 states persons giving evidence are 'bound to state the truth,' specific penalties for lying (perjury) are typically covered under separate provisions of the Indian Penal Code, not explicitly detailed in this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts and persons empowered by law or consent of parties to receive evidence; commanding officers of the Armed Forces; High Courts and State Governments in relation to affidavits.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the judicial process and the power of courts and authorized individuals to administer oaths and affirmations. The consequence of not adhering to the truth is implied by the legal framework governing evidence and testimony.

rights: The right to make an affirmation instead of an oath.
The right to make an oath or affirmation in a form common to one's class, if not repugnant to justice or decency.
duties: Duty to take an oath or make an affirmation when required as a witness, interpreter, or juror.
Duty to state the truth when giving evidence.
obligations: Obligation to be truthful in all evidence provided.
Obligation to faithfully discharge duties as an interpreter or juror.

key_procedures: Administration of oaths and affirmations by authorized courts and persons to witnesses, interpreters, and jurors.
Acceptance of an affirmation in lieu of an oath by a witness, interpreter, or juror.
Use of prescribed forms for oaths and affirmations, with provisions for alternative forms under certain conditions.
The procedure for a child witness under twelve years of age, where the understanding of the duty to speak the truth is assessed rather than the understanding of an oath's nature.
administration: The Act is administered through the judicial system and empowered authorities within various branches of government, including the High Courts and State Governments for affidavit purposes.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to proceedings before courts martial.
The Act does not apply to oaths, affirmations, or declarations prescribed by the Central Government for members of the Armed Forces.
The omission or irregularity in the administration of an oath or affirmation does not invalidate proceedings or evidence, but the obligation to state the truth remains.
The Act repealed the Indian Oaths Act, 1873.

title: The Assam Reorganisation (Meghalaya) Act, 1969
purpose: To provide for the formation within the State of Assam of an autonomous State to be known as Meghalaya and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the formation of the autonomous State of Meghalaya within the State of Assam. It covers the executive powers, legislature, financial provisions, assets and liabilities, administrative relations, and transitional provisions related to Meghalaya. Geographically, it pertains to the United Khasi-Jaintia Hills District and the Garo Hills District, with provisions for the inclusion of North Cachar Hills or Mikir Hills districts if desired. Its subject matter scope includes governance, legislation, finance, and administration.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed by the Central Government for the formation of the autonomous State.
key_definitions.autonomous State: The autonomous State of Meghalaya formed under section 3.
key_definitions.Meghalaya: The autonomous State referred to in section 3.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, Ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument, having immediately before the appointed day, the force of law in the whole or in any part of the autonomous State.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette, with the possibility of different dates for different provisions.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'appointed day', 'article', 'autonomous State', 'constituency', 'Election Commission', 'Governor', 'law', 'Legislative Assembly', 'Meghalaya', 'member', 'Official Gazette', and 'prescribed'.

Establishes the autonomous State of Meghalaya within the State of Assam from the appointed day. It specifies the initial tribal areas comprising Meghalaya and includes a provision for the potential inclusion of North Cachar Hills or Mikir Hills districts based on a resolution by their respective District Councils and a President's order.

States that the executive power of Meghalaya vests in the Governor and is exercised by him directly or through subordinate officers, subject to the Act. It clarifies that this does not transfer functions conferred by existing law on other authorities or prevent Parliament or State Legislatures from conferring functions on subordinate authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Extent of executive power of Meghalaya
main_sections.description: Defines the extent of Meghalaya's executive power, which generally extends to matters on which its Legislature can make laws. It outlines limitations where Parliament or the Assam Legislature have concurrent powers and specifies that Assam's executive power does not extend to Meghalaya in matters where Meghalaya has exclusive legislative power. It also clarifies that Assam's executive power continues to extend to matters where Meghalaya's Legislature has no power to make laws, unless otherwise provided.

Provides for a Council of Ministers headed by a Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor in exercising his functions in relation to Meghalaya. It also states that the question of advice tendered to the Governor by Ministers cannot be inquired into by any court.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Legislature of Meghalaya
main_sections.description: Deals with the establishment and composition of the Legislative Assembly of Meghalaya.
Addresses the division of assets and liabilities between Meghalaya and the State of Assam.

important_rules: Rule 1: The executive power of Meghalaya is vested in the Governor and exercised by him directly or through subordinate officers, in accordance with the Act.
Rule 2: The Council of Ministers in Meghalaya is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
Rule 3: Ministers who are not members of the Legislative Assembly for six consecutive months shall cease to be Ministers.
Rule 4: All executive actions of the Government of Meghalaya must be expressed in the name of the Governor.
Rule 5: The Governor shall make rules for the convenient transaction of business of the Government of Meghalaya and for the allocation of business among Ministers.

Rule 6: It is the duty of the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of Meghalaya and proposals for legislation, and to furnish information as the Governor may require.

penalties: Penalty for sitting and voting before making an oath or affirmation or when not qualified or when disqualified (Section 30).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, the Governor of Assam (in relation to Meghalaya), and potentially the Legislature of Meghalaya and its authorities, depending on the specific provision.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders, appointment of officials, legislative measures, and judicial scrutiny where applicable.

rights: Right to vote in elections to the Legislative Assembly (Section 15).
Right to be a member of the Legislative Assembly (subject to qualifications) (Section 16).
Rights of Ministers as respects the Legislative Assembly (Section 22).
Powers, privileges, etc., of members of the Legislative Assembly (Section 31).
Right to receive salaries and allowances for members (Section 32).
duties: Duty of the Advocate-General to advise the Government of Meghalaya and perform other legal duties (Section 8).
Duty of the Chief Minister to communicate decisions and proposals to the Governor and furnish information (Section 10).
Obligation of Meghalaya, the State of Assam, and the Union to cooperate (Section 59).
obligations: Obligation of Meghalaya, the State of Assam and the Union to cooperate (Section 59).

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act on a date appointed by the Central Government (Section 1(2)).
Formation of Meghalaya on the 'appointed day' (Section 3(1)).
Appointment of Chief Minister and other Ministers by the Governor (Section 7(1)).
Making of rules by the Governor for transaction of business and allocation of work (Section 9(3)).
Delimitation of constituencies for elections (Section 12).
Procedure for election to the Legislative Assembly (Section 17).
Procedure in financial matters, including Annual Financial Statement, estimates, appropriation bills, and supplementary grants (Sections 42-46).
Procedure for Bills, including assent to Bills and Bills reserved for consideration (Sections 39-40).
Procedure for Governor to promulgate Ordinances during recess of the Legislative Assembly (Section 50).
administration: The Central Government has a role in appointing the 'appointed day' and making notifications. The Governor of Assam exercises functions in relation to Meghalaya as per this Act. The Government of Meghalaya, with its Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister, is responsible for the administration.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The executive power of Meghalaya is subject to the executive power expressly conferred by the Act or by any law made by Parliament upon the Union or the State of Assam.
The Act provides for the amendment of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution and other specified Acts.
The Act contains provisions for the adaptation of existing laws and the removal of difficulties.

title: The Haryana and Punjab Agricultural Universities Act, 1970
purpose: To provide for the establishment of two independent Agricultural Universities in place of the Punjab Agricultural University, and for matters consequential on, or connected with the establishment of these independent Agricultural Universities.
scope: This Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Haryana Agricultural University and the Punjab Agricultural University. The Haryana Agricultural University functions within the territories of the State of Haryana, while the Punjab Agricultural University functions within territories not including the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, with provisions for a future university in Himachal Pradesh.

key_definitions.agriculture: Includes the basic and applied science of soil and water management, crop and live-stock production and management, home sciences and the betterment of rural people.
key_definitions.corresponding_university: Refers to the Haryana Agricultural University or the Punjab Agricultural University, depending on the territories to which their functions extend.
key_definitions.existing_university: The Punjab Agricultural University constituted by section 3 of the Punjab Agricultural University Act, 1961.
key_definitions.appropriate_government: The Government of the State of Haryana for Haryana Agricultural University, and the Government of the State of Punjab for Punjab Agricultural University.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Haryana and Punjab Agricultural Universities Act, 1970' and states it came into force on February 2, 1970.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'agriculture', 'corresponding University', 'existing University', 'appropriate Government', 'Board', 'college', 'Statutes', and 'Regulations'.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of the existing University and establishment of Haryana and Punjab Agricultural Universities
main_sections.description: States that the existing Punjab Agricultural University shall stand dissolved and be replaced by two independent universities: the Haryana Agricultural University and the Punjab Agricultural University.
Declares each new university as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and to sue and be sued.

Defines the territorial jurisdiction of the Haryana Agricultural University (State of Haryana) and the Punjab Agricultural University. It also includes provisions for a future university in Himachal Pradesh and the transfer of assets and liabilities related to its agricultural college.

Specifies the headquarters of the Haryana Agricultural University at Hissar and the Punjab Agricultural University at Ludhiana, with the power for the appropriate government to direct other locations and requiring each to establish an office at the seat of the appropriate government.
