Outlines the objects for which each university is established, including imparting education in agriculture and allied sciences, furthering research, undertaking extension services to rural people, and other purposes directed by the appropriate government.

States that universities are open to all persons, subject to the Act and Statutes, with provisions for reserving seats for women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, or backward classes as directed by the appropriate government, provided admission standards are met.

Enumerate the powers of each university, including providing instructions in various fields, conducting research and extension programs, instituting degrees, holding examinations, conferring honorary degrees, cooperating with other institutions, creating posts, and establishing residential accommodation.

Grants the Chancellor the power to inspect universities and inquire into their administration and finances, with provisions for the university to appoint a representative and for the Chancellor to issue directions to the Board if satisfactory action is not taken.

main_sections.section_title: Authorities and officers of a corresponding University
main_sections.description: Lists the authorities (Board, Academic Council, Board of Studies, etc.) and officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Comptroller, etc.) of each university.
Details the role and powers of the Chancellor.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution, powers and duties of the Board of a corresponding University
main_sections.description: Defines the composition, powers, and responsibilities of the Board of Management.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Board
main_sections.description: Further elaborates on the specific powers and duties vested in the Board.
Introduces the office of the Vice-Chancellor.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Vice-Chancellor
main_sections.description: Specifies the powers and responsibilities of the Vice-Chancellor.
Details the role of the Registrar.
Outlines the responsibilities of the Comptroller.
Describes the duties of the Estate Officer.
Defines the role of the Director of Student Welfare.
Specifies the role of the Deans of colleges.
Outlines the responsibilities of the Librarian.
Details the structure and functions of the Academic Council.
Refers to the constituent colleges of the universities.
Covers the establishment and purpose of research experiment stations.
Deals with the provisions for agricultural extension education programs.

main_sections.section_title: Retirement and other conditions of services
main_sections.description: Specifies the retirement and service conditions for university employees.
Addresses the establishment and management of provident funds.
Governs the appointment of officers who receive a salary.
Allows for temporary arrangements within the university structure.
Refers to the Statutes as the governing rules of the universities.
Describes the process by which Statutes are created.
Refers to Regulations as rules made under the Statutes.
Deals with the financial accounts and auditing procedures of the universities.
Outlines the process for dividing the assets and liabilities of the dissolved existing University.
Addresses how legal proceedings involving the universities are handled.
Specifies the procedures for the transfer of employees from the existing University to the new universities.
Governs the membership of various bodies within the universities.
Requires the universities to prepare and submit an annual report.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to existing University in any document, etc.
main_sections.description: Provides guidance on how references to the former Punjab Agricultural University in existing documents should be interpreted.

main_sections.section_title: Obligations to be discharged by the Punjab Agricultural University
main_sections.description: Specifies certain obligations that the Punjab Agricultural University must fulfill.

main_sections.section_title: Proportion of cost to be borne by the Government of Himachal Pradesh
main_sections.description: Details the financial contribution expected from the Government of Himachal Pradesh.
Provides a mechanism for resolving disputes that remain unsettled.
Grants the appropriate government the power to issue orders to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Repeals the Punjab Agricultural University Act, 1961, and includes saving provisions.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Haryana Agricultural University shall function within the State of Haryana, and the Punjab Agricultural University shall function in other territories, with provisions for a future university in Himachal Pradesh.
Rule 2: Each university is established to provide education, conduct research, and undertake extension services in agriculture and allied sciences.
Rule 3: Universities are open to all, but may reserve seats for specific categories as directed by the appropriate government.
Rule 4: Universities have the power to institute degrees, hold examinations, and confer distinctions.
Rule 5: The Act establishes a clear governance structure with a Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Board, and Academic Council.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The appropriate Governments (Government of Haryana and Government of Punjab) and the Chancellors of the respective Universities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Chancellors for visitations and inquiries, the power of the appropriate governments to issue directions and notifications, and the overall management and regulatory framework established by the Act, Statutes, and Regulations.

rights: Right to education in agriculture and allied sciences.
Right to admission to universities, subject to standards and reservations.
Right to hold degrees and diplomas.
Right to participate in research and extension activities.
Right to be represented during inspections and inquiries.
duties: Duty of universities to provide education and conduct research.
Duty to undertake extension services to rural people.
Duty to adhere to the Act, Statutes, and Regulations.
Duty of the Board to comply with directions from the Chancellor.
Duty to maintain accounts and undergo audit.
obligations: Obligations to facilitate the establishment of two independent universities.
Obligations of the Punjab Agricultural University to discharge specific duties.
Obligations of the Government of Himachal Pradesh to bear a proportion of the cost.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Establishment of Haryana and Punjab Agricultural Universities, including the dissolution of the existing university.
Procedure 2: The process of visitation and inquiry by the Chancellor, including notice, representation, and potential issuance of directions.
Procedure 3: Making of Statutes and Regulations by the respective universities.
Procedure 4: Division of assets and liabilities upon the dissolution of the existing university.
Procedure 5: Settlement of unresolved disputes through designated mechanisms.
administration: The Act establishes two independent universities, the Haryana Agricultural University and the Punjab Agricultural University, each administered by their respective authorities (Board, Academic Council, etc.) under the overall purview of the appropriate State Governments and the Chancellors.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on February 2, 1970.
Specific provisions are made for the establishment of a university in the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh and the transfer of related assets and liabilities.
The Act allows for the appropriate government to direct the reservation of seats for various categories of citizens.
The power to remove difficulties is vested with the appropriate government.

title: The Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970
purpose: To enlarge the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in regard to criminal matters, specifically to provide an absolute right of appeal in certain cases where a High Court has reversed an acquittal or convicted an accused after withdrawing a case for trial.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970' and specifies its territorial application to the whole of India.

main_sections.section_title: Enlarged appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in regard to criminal matters
main_sections.description: Grants an appeal to the Supreme Court from any judgment, final order, or sentence in a criminal proceeding of a High Court if the High Court has either (a) reversed an order of acquittal and sentenced the accused to life imprisonment or imprisonment of not less than ten years, or (b) withdrawn a case from a subordinate court, tried it, and convicted the accused to life imprisonment or imprisonment of not less than ten years.

important_rules: An appeal shall lie to the Supreme Court from a High Court's judgment, final order, or sentence in a criminal proceeding under specific conditions.
These conditions include the High Court reversing an acquittal and sentencing the accused to life imprisonment or imprisonment for at least ten years.

Alternatively, if the High Court withdraws a case from a subordinate court for trial and convicts the accused to life imprisonment or imprisonment for at least ten years, an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Supreme Court of India
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of hearing appeals as provided by the Act.

rights: An accused person has a right of appeal to the Supreme Court against certain judgments of a High Court.

key_procedures: An appeal from a High Court's criminal judgment to the Supreme Court is initiated under the conditions specified in Section 2 of the Act. These conditions pertain to the High Court's actions regarding acquittals, reversals, or trials after withdrawal of cases, and the severity of the sentence imposed.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be under the purview of the Supreme Court of India.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1972 to omit the exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, thereby extending its application to the whole of India.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons highlights the disparity between appeal rights in civil and criminal matters and the intent to provide an absolute right of appeal in specific severe criminal cases decided by High Courts, aligning with Article 134(2) of the Constitution.

title: The Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of certain banking companies, with the objective of controlling the heights of the economy and to meet, progressively and serve better, the needs of development of the economy in conformity with national policy and objectives.
scope: Applies to certain banking companies specified in the First Schedule, whose deposits were not less than rupees fifty crores as of the last Friday of June 1969. It establishes corresponding new banks to take over these undertakings.

key_definitions.appointed day: February 14, 1970, the date of promulgation of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1970.
key_definitions.banking company: Does not include a foreign company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.corresponding new bank: The body corporate specified in the First Schedule in relation to an existing bank.
key_definitions.Custodian: The person appointed as Custodian under section 7.
key_definitions.existing bank: A banking company specified in the First Schedule with deposits of not less than fifty crores of rupees as of the last Friday of June 1969.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement dates. Most provisions came into force on July 19, 1969, with Section 21 coming into force on the appointed day.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'banking company', 'commencement of this Act', 'corresponding new bank', 'Custodian', and 'existing bank'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of corresponding new banks and business thereof
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of corresponding new banks on the commencement of the Act. It also details their paid-up capital and provisions for its increase or reduction, including scenarios for public issues and government holdings.

main_sections.section_title: Undertaking of existing banks to vest in corresponding new banks
main_sections.description: States that the undertaking of every existing bank shall be transferred to and vested in the corresponding new bank.
Outlines the general consequences of the vesting of an undertaking, including the transfer of assets and liabilities.
Deals with the payment of compensation to the shareholders of the existing banks for the acquisition of their undertakings.
Concerns the establishment of the head office and the management of the corresponding new banks.

main_sections.section_title: Corresponding new banks to be guided by the directions of the Central Government
main_sections.description: Mandates that corresponding new banks shall be guided by the directions issued by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make scheme
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make a scheme for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any existing law and savings provisions related to the commencement of the Act.

important_rules: On the commencement of the Act, corresponding new banks are to be constituted as specified in the First Schedule.
The undertaking of every existing bank shall stand transferred to and vested in the corresponding new bank.
Corresponding new banks are to be guided by the directions of the Central Government.
The Central Government has the power to make a scheme for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

rights: Shareholders of corresponding new banks (other than the Central Government) have certain voting rights, capped at ten percent of the total voting rights.
duties: Corresponding new banks are to be guided by the directions of the Central Government.
Corresponding new banks must maintain a register of shareholders.
Obligations as to fidelity and secrecy are imposed.
obligations: To maintain fidelity and secrecy.

key_procedures: Establishment of corresponding new banks.
Transfer of undertakings of existing banks to corresponding new banks.
Payment of compensation.
Management of corresponding new banks under Central Government guidance.
Central Government making schemes for the Act's implementation.
Reduction of paid-up capital of corresponding new banks under specified conditions.
Restrictions on shareholding by entities outside India.
Limitations on voting rights for shareholders.
administration: The Central Government, with consultation and guidance from the Reserve Bank, plays a significant role in the administration and direction of the corresponding new banks.
important_notes: The Act specifies that the 'appointed day' for certain provisions is February 14, 1970.
The Act distinguishes between 'existing banks' and 'corresponding new banks'.
The Central Government must hold at least fifty-one percent of the paid-up capital consisting of equity shares of each corresponding new bank.
Restrictions apply to the holding of shares by individuals or companies resident outside India.

title: The State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the State of Himachal Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the territories that comprised the existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, establishing it as a new state. It also makes provisions for representation in the legislatures, the High Court, authorization of expenditure, distribution of revenues, assets and liabilities, provisions relating to services, and legal and miscellaneous matters concerning the newly formed State of Himachal Pradesh.

key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.appointed day: The day which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
key_definitions.Election Commission: The Election Commission appointed by the President under article 324.
key_definitions.existing Union territory of Himachal Pra: The Union territory of Himachal Pradesh as existing immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having, immediately before the appointed day, the force of law in the whole or any part of the existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh.
key_definitions.sitting member: In relation to either House of Parliament or of the Legislative Assembly of the existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, means a person who, immediately before the appointed day, is a member of that House or that Assembly.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, appointed day, article, Election Commission, existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, law, sitting member, and treasury.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of State of Himachal Pradesh
main_sections.description: Declares the establishment of a new State, to be known as the State of Himachal Pradesh, comprising the territories that were part of the existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh from the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution to include Himachal Pradesh as a State and omits its entry as a Union Territory.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution to re-number an entry and insert a new entry for Himachal Pradesh, related to the allocation of seats in the Council of States.

Deems the three sitting members of the Council of States representing the existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh as duly elected to fill the seats allotted to the State of Himachal Pradesh, with their term of office remaining unaltered.

main_sections.section_title: Provision as to Legislative Assembly as constituted on the appointed day
main_sections.description: Specifies the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of Himachal Pradesh, including reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and deems existing constituencies as those of the new State's Legislative Assembly. It also states that the Legislative Assembly shall be deemed duly constituted on the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seats in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Allocates four seats to the State of Himachal Pradesh in the House of the People, with one seat reserved for the Scheduled Castes.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seats in the Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Specifies that the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of Himachal Pradesh shall be sixty-eight, with sixteen seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and three for Scheduled Tribes.

Empowers the Election Commission to distribute and delimit seats in the House of the People and the Legislative Assembly into single-member territorial constituencies based on the latest census figures, considering geographical compactness, administrative units, communication, public convenience, and population proportions for reserved seats.
Establishes a High Court for Himachal Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Authorisation of expenditure pending its sanction by the Legislature
main_sections.description: Authorizes expenditure pending its sanction by the Legislature.
Deals with the distribution of revenues.

main_sections.section_title: Property, assets, rights, liabilities, obligations, etc.
main_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of property, assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations.
Makes provisions relating to All-India Services.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of existing laws and their adaptation
main_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of existing laws and provides for their adaptation.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Confers the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State of Himachal Pradesh is established on the appointed day, comprising the territories of the existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh.
Rule 2: The Constitution's First Schedule is amended to include Himachal Pradesh as a State, and its entry as a Union Territory is removed.
Rule 3: Sitting members of the Council of States representing the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh are deemed elected to the newly formed State's seats, with their terms unchanged.
Rule 4: The Legislative Assembly of Himachal Pradesh will have sixty seats to be filled by direct election, with fourteen reserved for Scheduled Castes and three for Scheduled Tribes.
Rule 5: The Legislative Assembly of Himachal Pradesh will have a total of sixty-eight seats, with sixteen reserved for Scheduled Castes and three for Scheduled Tribes.

Rule 6: The Election Commission is responsible for delimiting constituencies for the House of the People and the Legislative Assembly, ensuring they are geographically compact and consider population distribution for reserved seats.
Rule 7: A High Court is established for Himachal Pradesh.
Rule 8: Expenditure pending sanction by the Legislature is authorized.
Rule 9: Existing laws continue to be in force and can be adapted.
Rule 10: The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: While not explicitly detailed for all provisions, the establishment and administration of the new state, legislative representation, and High Court functions imply enforcement by the Central Government, the State Government of Himachal Pradesh, and the judiciary.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through constitutional amendments, legislative actions, judicial pronouncements, and administrative directives. The Election Commission's role in delimitation is a key enforcement mechanism for representation.

rights: The right to representation in the Council of States and the House of the People for the State of Himachal Pradesh.
The right to have a Legislative Assembly constituted for the State of Himachal Pradesh.
The right to have a High Court for the State of Himachal Pradesh.
Continuance of rights associated with existing laws.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to appoint the 'appointed day' by notification.
Duty of the Election Commission to delimit constituencies.
Duty to ensure the functioning of the High Court and the Legislative Assembly.
obligations: Obligations regarding the transfer of property, assets, rights, and liabilities.
Obligations related to All-India Services and other services.

key_procedures: Procedure for the establishment of the State of Himachal Pradesh on the appointed day.
Procedure for amending the Constitution's First and Fourth Schedules.
Procedure for allocating sitting members to the Council of States.
Procedure for constituting the Legislative Assembly and delimiting its constituencies.
Procedure for allocating seats in the House of the People and delimiting constituencies.
Procedure for establishing and functioning of the High Court.
Procedure for authorising expenditure and distribution of revenues.
Procedure for adapting and continuing existing laws.
Procedure for removal of difficulties by the Central Government.
Procedure for making rules by the Central Government.
administration: The Central Government, and subsequently the newly formed State of Himachal Pradesh government and its institutions (Legislative Assembly, High Court).
important_notes: The 'appointed day' is crucial for the commencement of many provisions, and it is to be notified by the Central Government.
Amendments to the Representation of the People Act, 1950, are made to reflect the new state structure.
The Act makes specific provisions for the continuation of officers in their existing posts.
The Act empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties arising in the implementation of its provisions.

title: The Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971
purpose: To provide for the eviction of unauthorised occupants from public premises and for certain incidental matters.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to 'public premises', which are broadly defined to include premises belonging to or leased by the Central Government, certain government-controlled companies and corporations, universities, institutes, port trusts, government entities in Delhi, Cantonment Boards, and enemy property. It also covers premises of the Delhi Development Authority and specific state government or union territory premises in Delhi and other union territories.

key_definitions.estate officer: An officer appointed by the Central Government to carry out the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.premises: Any land or any building or part of a building, including gardens, grounds, outhouses, and fittings for beneficial enjoyment.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public premises: Includes premises belonging to or taken on lease/requisition by the Central Government, certain government-controlled companies and corporations, universities, institutes, port trusts, government entities in Delhi, Cantonment Boards, enemy property, and premises of the Delhi Development Authority, among others.
key_definitions.rent: The periodic consideration for authorized occupation of public premises, including charges for electricity, water, or taxes payable by the Central Government or a statutory authority.
key_definitions.residential accommodation occupation: Occupation by a person granted a license to occupy public premises based on an allotment order for a fixed tenure or while holding office, as per government rules.
key_definitions.statutory authority: Refers to specific entities such as the Secretariat of either House of Parliament, companies, corporations, universities, institutes, boards, Councils, and Corporations in Delhi, as defined in relation to the public premises they control.
key_definitions.temporary occupation: Occupation of public premises for a total period of less than thirty days, including any extended period, based on an order of allotment.
key_definitions.unauthorised occupation: Occupation of public premises without authority, or continuing to occupy them after the authority has expired or been determined.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on September 16, 1958, except for sections 11, 19, and 20 which came into force at once).

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'estate officer', 'premises', 'prescribed', 'public premises', 'rent', 'residential accommodation occupation', 'statutory authority', 'temporary occupation', and 'unauthorised occupation'.

Empowers the Central Government to appoint gazetted officers or equivalent rank officers of statutory authorities as estate officers and define their local limits or categories of public premises they will manage. Special provisions exist for officers of the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha secretariats and for officers managing enemy property.

Allows the estate officer to order immediate eviction of persons in unauthorized occupation of public premises under temporary occupation, after an inquiry, and to use necessary force to take possession.
Mandates the estate officer to issue a show-cause notice within three working days to persons in unauthorized occupation of residential accommodation, following which an eviction order can be made.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of notice to show cause against order of eviction
main_sections.description: Requires the estate officer to issue a notice to the unauthorised occupant to show cause against an order of eviction.
Details the process for the eviction of unauthorised occupants after the show-cause notice period has expired or no cause has been shown.
Defines offences under the Act and specifies the penalties for such offences.
Ousts the jurisdiction of civil courts in respect of certain matters dealt with under this Act.

important_rules: Unauthorised occupants must be issued a notice to show cause against eviction.
Eviction orders can be made against unauthorised occupants after the show-cause period expires or no valid cause is shown.
The estate officer has the power to remove unauthorised constructions and may order demolition or sealing of such constructions.
Property left behind by unauthorised occupants can be disposed of by the estate officer.
Rent or damages can be recovered from unauthorised occupants.
The Act defines specific procedures for eviction from temporary occupation and residential accommodation.

penalties: Specific penalties are defined for offences under Section 11 of the Act, though the detailed description of these penalties is not fully provided in the extracted text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Estate officers appointed by the Central Government, who can use necessary force to evict unauthorised occupants and take possession of premises.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issue of notices, eviction orders, and by using force if necessary for eviction and taking possession. Offences under Section 11 are cognizable.

rights: The right of the government/statutory authority to regain possession of public premises from unauthorised occupants.
The right of an unauthorised occupant to show cause against an eviction order.
duties: Duty of unauthorised occupants to vacate public premises upon order.
Duty of the Central Government to appoint estate officers.
Duty of estate officers to follow prescribed procedures for eviction.
obligations: Obligation to pay rent or damages for unauthorised occupation.
Obligation to comply with eviction orders.

key_procedures: Appointment of Estate Officers by the Central Government.
Issuance of a show-cause notice to an unauthorised occupant.
Making of an eviction order if no cause is shown or if the cause is not satisfactory.
Forthwith eviction of persons in temporary occupation of public premises.
Eviction from residential accommodation involves a three-day show-cause period.
Disposal of property left by unauthorised occupants.
Appeals against orders of estate officers.
Recovery of rent, etc., as arrears of land revenue.
Power to obtain information relevant to the Act.
Procedures for removal, demolition, or sealing of unauthorised constructions.
administration: The Central Government, through the appointment of Estate Officers and the power to make rules.
important_notes: Sections 11, 19, and 20 came into force at once, while the rest of the Act was deemed to have come into force on September 16, 1958.
The definition of 'public premises' is extensive and has been amended multiple times.
Specific conditions apply to the appointment of estate officers for Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha secretariats, and for enemy property.
The Act aims to expedite the eviction process from public premises.

title: The Naval and Aircraft Prize Act, 1971
purpose: To provide for the establishment and procedure of Prize Courts and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to naval and aircraft prizes, including ships, aircraft, and goods captured or seized during a war, as a measure of reprisal during an armed conflict, or in the exercise of the right of self-defence. It covers prizes brought into or seized within the territory of India, or in localities occupied by the Armed Forces of the Union, or appropriated for the use of the Central Government. It also applies to lost or destroyed prize property that cannot be brought in for adjudication.

key_definitions.aircraft: Has the meaning assigned to it in clause (ii) of section 4 of the Air Force Act, 1950.
key_definitions.aircraft papers: Includes all books, passes, charter parties, bills of lading, customs receipts, manifests, certificates, licenses, lists, tickets, notes, letters and other documents and writings delivered up or found on board a captured aircraft.
key_definitions.Armed Forces: Means the Army, Navy and Air Force or any part of any one or more of them and includes any other armed force in the service of, or employed with, the Army, Navy or Air Force during hostilities.
key_definitions.goods: Includes all such things as may be subject to adjudication as prize, but in the case of a naval prize does not include any aircraft or boat unless the aircraft or boat is a part of the cargo of a ship.
key_definitions.Prize Court: Means a prize court established under section 3.
key_definitions.Indian citizen: Includes a company registered in India and having its principal place of business in India.
key_definitions.military aircraft: Means any aircraft belonging to the Armed Forces and includes any armed aircraft in the service of the Armed Forces and any other aircraft used as a transport or auxiliary or in any other way for the purpose of prosecuting or aiding hostilities.
key_definitions.prize: Means anything which, subject to this Act and the rules made thereunder, may be subjected to adjudication and includes a ship or an aircraft and goods carried therein, irrespective of whether the ship is captured at sea or seized in port or whether the aircraft is on or over land or sea at the time of capture or seizure.
key_definitions.ship: Includes a vessel and a boat with the tackle, furniture and apparel of the ship, vessel or boat.
key_definitions.ship-of-war: Means any ship belonging to the Armed Forces and includes any armed ship in the service of the Armed Forces and any other ship used as transport or auxiliary or in any other way for the purpose of prosecuting or aiding hostilities.
key_definitions.ship papers: Includes all books, passes, sea briefs, charter parties, bills of lading, customs receipts, manifests, certificates, licenses, lists, tickets, notes, letters and other documents and writings delivered up or found on board a ship captured at sea or seized in port.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Naval and Aircraft Prize Act, 1971.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'aircraft', 'aircraft papers', 'Armed Forces', 'goods', 'Prize Court', 'Indian citizen', 'military aircraft', 'prize', 'ship', 'ship-of-war', and 'ship papers'.
Empowers the Central Government to establish Prize Courts by notification, specifying their jurisdiction and composition. Members must be Indian citizens qualified to be High Court Judges.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of Prize Courts in prize cases
main_sections.description: Grants exclusive jurisdiction to Prize Courts in prize cases, covering prizes brought into or seized within India, occupied territories, or appropriated for the Central Government. It also covers lost or destroyed prize property and allows application of International Law where provisions are insufficient.
Allows Prize Courts to transfer proceedings to another Prize Court if it's deemed more convenient, ensuring the receiving court has full jurisdiction.
Permits appeals to the Central Government against orders or decrees of a Prize Court within ninety days, with application of Limitation Act provisions for computation of period.

Confers powers similar to Civil Courts under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning witnesses, enforcing attendance, requiring document production, receiving affidavits, requisitioning records, issuing commissions, and enforcing orders of other Prize Courts or the Central Government.
Mandates that captured ships and aircraft be delivered to the Marshal of the Court or a government-appointed person, remaining in their custody subject to court orders.

main_sections.section_title: Ship and aircraft papers to be brought in Registry
main_sections.description: Requires captors to promptly bring ship or aircraft papers to the Registry of the Prize Court, with an oath to be made regarding their condition, or an explanation for any alteration or absence.
Extends the provisions for ships and aircraft to goods taken as prize, allowing the Prize Court to direct their unlading, inventory, and warehousing.
Allows the Central Government to purchase military or victualling stores intended for an enemy from a foreign ship or aircraft if deemed expedient, without prior condemnation by a Prize Court.

main_sections.section_title: Prize proceedings not to apply to enemy warships and military aircraft
main_sections.description: Exempts enemy warships, military aircraft, and any other enemy-owned ships or aircraft, along with their cargo, from prize proceedings and condemnation requirements.

main_sections.section_title: Capture to belong to Central Government
main_sections.description: Declares all condemned prizes captured by the Armed Forces as exclusive property of the Central Government, which may grant sums from proceeds to benevolent funds of the Armed Forces.

Specifies that Indian citizens' property retaken from the enemy will be restored upon payment of one-eighth of its value as prize salvage to the Central Government. A larger portion, up to one-fourth, may be awarded in cases of special difficulty or danger. If the retaken property is used by the enemy as a warship or military aircraft, restitution provisions do not apply, and ownership vests in the Central Government.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for the purposes of the Act.
Repeals the Indian Navy (Piracy) Act, 1926, and the Indian Air Force Act, 1950, in so far as they relate to prize.
Provides that anything done or any action taken under the repealed enactments shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Prize Courts have exclusive jurisdiction over prize cases under specific conditions (Section 4).
Captured ships and aircraft must be delivered to the Marshal or an appointed person (Section 8).
Ship and aircraft papers must be promptly submitted to the Registry of the Prize Court with an oath regarding their condition (Section 9).
Enemy warships and military aircraft are exempt from prize proceedings (Section 12).
Captured prizes become the exclusive property of the Central Government (Section 13).
Prize salvage is payable for retaken property belonging to Indian citizens (Section 14).

penalties: Offences in respect of prize are covered under Section 15, which implies penalties will be imposed for violations, though specific penalties are not detailed in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and Prize Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment and functioning of Prize Courts, adherence to established procedures for capture and adjudication, and enforcement of their orders and decrees.

rights: Right of owners to have their property restored upon payment of prize salvage if retaken from the enemy (Section 14).
Right to appeal to the Central Government against Prize Court orders (Section 6).
duties: Duty of captors to deliver captured ships/aircraft to the Marshal or appointed person (Section 8).
Duty of captors to submit ship/aircraft papers to the Registry of the Prize Court (Section 9).
Duty of owners to pay prize salvage for retaken property (Section 14).
obligations: Obligation for Prize Courts to adjudicate prize cases according to the Act and international law principles where applicable (Section 4).
Obligation for the Central Government to establish and constitute Prize Courts (Section 3).

key_procedures: Establishment of Prize Courts by the Central Government via notification (Section 3).
Jurisdiction of Prize Courts in prize cases, including adjudication and condemnation (Section 4).
Transfer of cases between Prize Courts if deemed more convenient (Section 5).
Appeals against Prize Court orders to the Central Government (Section 6).
Procedure for delivery of captured prize to the Marshal and custody (Section 8).
Submission of ship and aircraft papers to the Prize Court Registry with an oath (Section 9).
Condemnation of prizes by Prize Courts, after which they become property of the Central Government (Section 13).
administration: The Central Government is responsible for establishing Prize Courts, appointing members, determining conditions of service, making rules, and hearing appeals.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to enemy warships and military aircraft (Section 12).
The Central Government may purchase certain stores without condemnation in a Prize Court (Section 11).
Prize salvage is subject to specific conditions and limitations, with potential for higher salvage in cases of special difficulty or danger (Section 14).
The Act repeals certain provisions of other Acts related to prize, with savings for actions taken under the repealed laws (Sections 19, 20).

title: The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971
purpose: To define and limit the powers of certain courts in punishing contempts of courts and to regulate their procedure in relation thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to civil and criminal contempt of courts.

key_definitions.contempt_of_court: Means civil contempt or criminal contempt.
key_definitions.civil_contempt: Means wilful disobedience to any judgment, decree, direction, order, writ or other process of a court or wilful breach of an undertaking given to a court.
key_definitions.criminal_contempt: Means the publication (whether by words, spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representations, or otherwise) of any matter or the doing of any other act whatsoever which scandalises or tends to scandalise, or lowers or tends to lower the authority of, any court; or prejudices, or interferes or tends to interfere with, the due course of any judicial proceeding; or interferes or tends to interfere with, or obstructs or tends to obstruct, the administration of justice in any other manner.
key_definitions.High_Court: Means the High Court for a State or a Union territory, and includes the court of the Judicial Commissioner in any Union territory.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its territorial extent.
Defines key terms such as 'contempt of court', 'civil contempt', 'criminal contempt', and 'High Court'.

main_sections.section_title: Innocent publication and distribution of matter not contempt
main_sections.description: Specifies circumstances under which innocent publication and distribution of matter related to judicial proceedings do not constitute contempt of court, particularly if the person had no reasonable grounds to believe the proceeding was pending or contained contemptuous matter.

main_sections.section_title: Fair and accurate report of judicial proceeding not contempt
main_sections.description: States that publishing a fair and accurate report of a judicial proceeding or any stage thereof is not contempt of court, subject to provisions in Section 7.

main_sections.section_title: Fair criticism of judicial act not contempt
main_sections.description: Clarifies that publishing fair comment on the merits of a case that has been heard and finally decided is not contempt of court.

main_sections.section_title: Power of High Court to punish contempts of subordinate courts
main_sections.description: Grants High Courts the jurisdiction to punish contempts of courts subordinate to them, with a proviso that such contempts are not offenses punishable under the Indian Penal Code.

Outlines the punishments for contempt of court, which may include simple imprisonment, fine, or both. It also specifies provisions for civil contempt, companies found guilty, and the remission of punishment on apology.

main_sections.section_title: Contempts not punishable in certain cases
main_sections.description: Establishes that courts shall not impose a sentence for contempt unless it substantially interferes with the due course of justice, and permits justification by truth as a valid defense if it's in the public interest and bona fide.
Deals with the right to appeal against orders made by courts in contempt proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Supreme Court and High Courts to make rules
main_sections.description: Confers the power on the Supreme Court and High Courts to frame rules for their respective contempt jurisdiction and procedure.

important_rules: A person is not guilty of contempt for publishing matter if they had no reasonable grounds for believing a proceeding was pending at the time of publication (Section 3(1)).
Publication of matter related to a non-pending proceeding is not contempt (Section 3(2)).
A person is not guilty of contempt for distributing a publication if they had no reasonable grounds for believing it contained contemptuous matter (Section 3(3)).
Publishing a fair and accurate report of a judicial proceeding is not contempt, subject to Section 7 (Section 4).
Publishing fair comment on the merits of a decided case is not contempt (Section 5).
Statements made in good faith concerning presiding officers of subordinate courts to higher courts or other subordinate courts are not contempt (Section 6).
Publishing fair and accurate reports of proceedings in chambers or in camera is generally not contempt, except in specific cases outlined in Section 7.
No contempt shall be punished unless it substantially interferes, or tends to substantially interfere, with the due course of justice (Section 13(a)).
Justification by truth may be a valid defence in contempt proceedings if it is in the public interest and the request is bona fide (Section 13(b)).

penalties: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both (Section 12(1)).
For civil contempt, detention in a civil prison for a period not exceeding six months if a fine is insufficient (Section 12(3)).
For companies, punishment can be enforced by detention in civil prison of responsible persons (Section 12(4) & (5)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, including the Supreme Court and High Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial proceedings, issuance of summons or warrants, detention in custody or civil prison, imposition of fines, and other procedures as prescribed by the Act and applicable rules.

rights: Right to make an apology which may lead to discharge or remission of punishment (Section 12(1) Explanation).
Right to justification by truth as a defense in contempt proceedings under certain conditions (Section 13(b)).

Right to be informed in writing of the contempt charge and afforded an opportunity to make a defense when contempt is committed in the face of the Supreme Court or High Court (Section 14(1)(a) & (b)).
duties: Duty not to wilfully disobey court orders or breach undertakings given to a court (implied by definition of civil contempt).
Duty not to publish matters or do acts that scandalize, lower the authority of, prejudice, interfere with, or obstruct the administration of justice (implied by definition of criminal contempt).
Duty to exercise due diligence to prevent contempt by a company (Section 12(4) proviso).
obligations: Obligation to comply with judgments, decrees, directions, orders, writs, and undertakings of courts.
Obligation to avoid actions or publications that constitute criminal contempt.

key_procedures: When contempt is committed in the face of the Supreme Court or High Court: Court may detain the person, inform them in writing of the charge, afford an opportunity to make a defense, take evidence, and then proceed (Section 14).

For criminal contempt in other cases: Cognizance can be taken on a motion by the Advocate-General or any other person with the Attorney-General or Advocate-General's consent, or by the court itself (Section 15).
Hearings of criminal contempt cases are to be by Benches (Section 18).
Appeals against orders of a High Court in contempt proceedings lie to the Supreme Court (Section 19).
administration: The administration of this Act primarily falls under the purview of the judiciary, specifically the Supreme Court and High Courts, and subordinate courts.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India (Section 1(2)).
The Act does not affect other defenses that were valid before its enactment (Section 8).
The Act does not enlarge the scope of contempt beyond what was punishable before its enactment (Section 9).
The Act does not apply to Nyaya Panchayats or other village courts (Section 21).
The Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws relating to contempt (Section 22).
The proviso to Section 1, concerning the extent of the Act, has been omitted due to the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).

title: The Manipur (Hill Areas) District Councils Act, 1971
purpose: To provide for the establishment of District Councils in the Hill Areas in the Union territory of Manipur.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the Union territory of Manipur and applies to the Hill Areas within this territory. It establishes District Councils for autonomous districts within these Hill Areas.

key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator of the Union territory of Manipur appointed under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.autonomous district: An autonomous district referred to in sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.building: Includes a house, out-house, stable, latrine, urinal, shed, hut, wall (other than boundary wall) and any other structure (whether of masonry, bricks, wood, mud or other material) but does not include any portable or temporary shelter.
key_definitions.constituency: A District Council constituency provided by order made under section 5 for the purpose of elections to the District Council.
key_definitions.Deputy Commissioner: In relation to any District Council, the officer appointed as such by the Administrator to perform the functions of the Deputy Commissioner under this Act in the autonomous district.
key_definitions.Hill Areas: The Hill Areas determined by the President by any notification issued under sub-section (2) of section 52 of the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Hill Areas Committee: The Standing Committee referred to in section 52 of the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963.
key_definitions.market: Includes any place where persons assemble for the sale of, or for the purpose of exposing for sale of, meat, fish, fruit, vegetables, animals intended for human food or any other articles of human food whatsoever with or without the consent of the owner of such place, notwithstanding that there may be no common regulation for the concourse of buyers and sellers and whether or not any control is exercised over the business of, or the persons frequenting, the market by the owner of the place or by any other persons.
key_definitions.member: A member of a District Council constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.Official Gazette: The Gazette of the Union territory of Manipur.
key_definitions.person: Does not include a body of persons.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheduled Tribes: Has the same meaning assigned to it in clause (25) of article 366 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.vehicle: Includes a carriage, cart, hand-cart, bicycle, tricycle and every wheeled conveyance which is used or is capable of being used on a street but does not include a mechanically propelled vehicle.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Manipur (Hill Areas) District Councils Act, 1971, and specifies that it extends to the whole of the Union territory of Manipur.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Administrator, autonomous district, building, constituency, Deputy Commissioner, Hill Areas, Hill Areas Committee, market, member, Official Gazette, person, prescribed, Scheduled Tribes, and vehicle.

main_sections.section_title: Division of Hill Areas into autonomous districts
main_sections.description: Empowers the Administrator to divide the Hill Areas into not more than six autonomous districts and outlines the powers to declare areas part of or cease to be part of autonomous districts, increase or diminish areas, unite districts, define boundaries, and alter names, subject to consultation with the Hill Areas Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of District Councils and their composition
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a District Council for each autonomous district and specifies the composition, including a maximum of eighteen members chosen by direct election and a provision for nominating up to two members who are not in government service.
Mandates the Administrator to determine single-member constituencies within an autonomous district for elections to the District Council and define the extent of each constituency.

main_sections.section_title: Power to alter or amend delimitation orders
main_sections.description: Grants the Administrator the power to alter or amend orders made under section 5 regarding the delimitation of constituencies.
States that a person must be an elector for a District Council constituency within an autonomous district to be qualified for membership.

Lists disqualifications for membership, including being disqualified for membership of either House of Parliament or holding any office of profit under a District Council, with an exception for members themselves not being considered as holding an office of profit solely by virtue of their membership.

Specifies that persons entitled to vote are those eligible to be registered voters for elections to the House of the People, and that the electoral roll for a parliamentary constituency relating to the area of a District Council constituency will serve as its electoral roll.
Confirms the right to vote for every person whose name is on the electoral roll of a constituency and stipulates that each person has one vote.

Outlines that elections will be held according to rules made under section 21, on dates directed by the Administrator. It also addresses filling casual vacancies, with a proviso against holding elections for vacancies occurring within four months of a general election.
Requires the Administrator to publish the names of all elected or nominated members of a District Council in the Official Gazette.

Defines the term of office for a member as five years, commencing from the date of notification of election or nomination, or from the date the vacancy occurred, whichever is later. It also allows the Administrator to extend the term by up to one year and specifies the term for members filling casual vacancies.

Establishes the procedure for challenging elections, which must be done through an election petition presented to the District Judge within thirty days of the result notification. It outlines who can present a petition, the required respondents, and the format of the petition.

main_sections.section_title: Relief that may be claimed by petitioner
main_sections.description: Details the relief a petitioner can claim, which includes a declaration that the election of a returned candidate is void, and potentially a declaration that the petitioner or another candidate has been duly elected.

main_sections.section_title: Grounds on which an election may be called in question
main_sections.description: Lists the grounds for challenging an election, including the returned candidate being unqualified or disqualified, improper rejection of a nomination paper, or material effect on the result due to improper acceptance of a nomination or votes.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed by the District Judge
main_sections.description: States that the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, regarding suits shall be followed by the District Judge in the trial and disposal of election petitions.
Specifies the orders the District Judge can make at the conclusion of an election petition trial, including dismissing the petition, declaring an election void, or declaring a candidate duly elected.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure in case of equality of votes
main_sections.description: Initiates the procedure for handling a situation of equal votes during an election trial, though the full details are cut off in the provided text.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules regulating the election of members
main_sections.description: Grants the power to make rules regulating the election of members. (This section is mentioned in Section 11 but its full content is not provided in the excerpt.)
Deals with the legal incorporation of District Councils. (Section content not provided.)
Relates to the appointment or election of the Chairman and Vice-Chairman of District Councils. (Section content not provided.)
Concerns the oath or affirmation that members must take. (Section content not provided.)
Specifies the circumstances under which members must vacate their seats. (Section content not provided.)
Deals with the allowances payable to members. (Section content not provided.)
Outlines the liabilities of members. (Section content not provided.)

main_sections.section_title: Members to be deemed to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members of District Councils as public servants. (Section content not provided.)
Details the various functions that District Councils are empowered to perform. (Section content not provided.)
Prescribes the rules for the conduct of business by District Councils. (Section content not provided.)
Deals with the formation and functions of committees of District Councils. (Section content not provided.)
Concerns the appointment and management of officers and staff for District Councils. (Section content not provided.)
Grants District Councils the power to levy taxes. (Section content not provided.)
Empowers District Councils to levy fees. (Section content not provided.)
Outlines the procedure to be followed for imposing taxes. (Section content not provided.)
Deals with the power to abolish or reduce taxes. (Section content not provided.)
Specifies the methods for the recovery of taxes and fees. (Section content not provided.)

main_sections.section_title: Assessment and collection of taxes and fees
main_sections.description: Details the process for assessment and collection of taxes and fees. (Section content not provided.)
Provides for the mechanism of appeals related to taxes and fees. (Section content not provided.)
Concerns the payment of taxes and fees in instalments. (Section content not provided.)
Grants power to exempt certain entities or individuals from taxation. (Section content not provided.)

main_sections.section_title: Recoveries of moneys claimable by the Council
main_sections.description: Deals with the recovery of monies that are claimable by the Council. (Section content not provided.)
Specifies the establishment and management of the Council Fund. (Section content not provided.)
Defines the property that vests in a District Council. (Section content not provided.)
Concerns the preparation and approval of the annual budget for District Councils. (Section content not provided.)
Outlines the provisions for the control of District Councils. (Section content not provided.)
Provides for the supersession of a District Council under certain circumstances. (Section content not provided.)

main_sections.section_title: Effect of certain provisions during the period when the Hill Areas Committee is not functioning
main_sections.description: Addresses the implications of certain provisions when the Hill Areas Committee is not functional. (Section content not provided.)
Prescribes penalties for obstruction. (Section content not provided.)

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for entering into any contract with the Council
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties related to entering into contracts with the Council. (Section content not provided.)

main_sections.section_title: Power of Administrator to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Administrator the power to make rules. (Section content not provided.)
Empowers District Councils to make bye-laws. (Section content not provided.)

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for infringement of rules or bye-laws
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for the infringement of rules or bye-laws. (Section content not provided.)

important_rules: Election petitions must be presented to the District Judge within thirty days of the election result notification.
Election petitions must be supported by concise statements of material facts and sufficient particulars.
The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, applies to the trial and disposal of election petitions by the District Judge.
Electoral rolls for parliamentary constituencies will serve as the electoral rolls for District Council constituencies.
Each elector has one vote in the election of a member.
The Administrator may extend the term of office of all members by a period not exceeding one year.
Casual vacancies must be filled as soon as possible, unless occurring within four months of a general election.

penalties: Penalty for obstruction (Section 49)
Penalty for entering into any contract with the Council (Section 50)
Penalty for infringement of rules or bye-laws (Section 53)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Administrator, Deputy Commissioner, and District Judge (for election disputes).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal procedures, including election petitions adjudicated by the District Judge, and the imposition of penalties for offenses related to obstruction, contracts, and infringement of rules/bye-laws. Enforcement also involves the Administrator's powers regarding delimitation, elections, and rule-making.

rights: Right to vote for registered electors.
Right to present an election petition.
Right to claim specific reliefs in an election petition (declaration of election void, or another candidate being duly elected).
Right to have a District Council established in autonomous districts.
Right of members to receive allowances (details not provided).
duties: Duty of the Administrator to divide Hill Areas into autonomous districts and oversee elections.
Duty of members to take oath or affirmation.
Duty to follow procedures for conduct of business, taxation, and fee levying.
Duty to adhere to rules and bye-laws.
Duty of the District Judge to try election petitions.
obligations: Obligation for persons to be electors to be qualified for membership.
Obligation for candidates to comply with election rules.
Obligation for the Administrator to consult the Hill Areas Committee before making certain orders.
Obligation to pay taxes and fees levied by the Council.
Obligation for members to be deemed public servants.

key_procedures: Procedure for election of members (Section 11, governed by rules made under Section 21).
Procedure for challenging elections via election petition to the District Judge (Sections 14-18).
Procedure for delimitation of constituencies by the Administrator (Section 5).
Procedure for imposing taxes (Section 35).
Procedure for recovery of taxes and fees (Section 37).
Procedure for budget preparation and approval (Section 45).
administration: The Administrator of the Union territory of Manipur, with the Deputy Commissioner playing a role in specific districts.
important_notes: The Act makes provisions for the establishment of autonomous districts within the Hill Areas of Manipur, reflecting a decentralized administrative structure for these regions.
The Act draws upon existing constitutional provisions and other Acts, such as the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
The definition of 'market' is broad and inclusive.
The Act contains provisions for the financial autonomy of District Councils through powers of taxation and fee levying.
The Act outlines a clear process for resolving election disputes through judicial review by the District Judge.

title: The Delhi Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1971
purpose: To provide for the proper management of the Sikh Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property in Delhi and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi and applies to Sikh Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property situated within Delhi.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which this Act shall come into force.
key_definitions.board: The Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Board constituted under section 3 of the Delhi Sikh Gurdwaras (Management) Act, 1971 (24 of 1971).
key_definitions.committee: The Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee established under section 3.
key_definitions.director_gurdwara_elections: The Director Gurdwara Elections appointed by the Central Government under section 13.
key_definitions.gurdwaras: Sikh Gurdwaras situated in Delhi as were, immediately before the appointed day, being managed by or affiliated to the Board and includes such other local Gurdwaras as may, after the appointed day, be affiliated to or managed by the Committee.
key_definitions.gurdwara_property: Includes all movable and immovable property, offerings, and acquisitions related to Gurdwaras or the Committee.
key_definitions.local_gurdwara: A Gurdwara in Delhi, other than a Gurdwara under the control or management of the Board immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.ordinarily_resident: A person is not deemed to be ordinarily resident in a ward solely for owning a dwelling-house therein, and temporary absence does not cease ordinary residence.
key_definitions.patit: A Sikh who trims or shaves his beard or hair (keshas) or who after taking Amrit commits any of the four Kurahitis.
key_definitions.registered_singh_sabha: A Singh Sabha registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, managing or controlling a local Gurdwara in Delhi.
key_definitions.regulation: A regulation made under this Act by the Committee.
key_definitions.rule: A rule made under this Act by the Central Government.
key_definitions.sikh: A person who professes the Sikh religion, believes and follows the teachings of Sri Guru Granth Sahib and the ten Gurus only, and keeps unshorn hair (Keshas). A declaration is prescribed for determining Sikh identity.
key_definitions.amritdhari_sikh: A Sikh who has taken Khande ka Amrit or Khanda Pahul according to Sikh tenets.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Union territory of Delhi), and the provision for its commencement through a Central Government notification.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Committee', 'Delhi', 'Director Gurdwara Elections', 'Gurdwaras', 'Gurdwara property', 'local Gurdwara', 'ordinarily resident', 'patit', 'registered Singh Sabha', 'regulation', 'rule', 'Sikh', and 'Amritdhari Sikh'.

Establishes the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, for the management and control of Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property in Delhi. Its head office will be in Delhi.

Details the composition of the Committee, consisting of 46 elected members from wards and 9 co-opted members representing registered Singh Sabhas, head priests of Takhats, the Shromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, and the Sikh community of Delhi.

Specifies that the term of office for a member of the Committee is four years, commencing from the date of the first meeting. It also outlines procedures for filling vacancies and the continuation of outgoing members until their successors are notified.

Empowers the Director Gurdwara Elections to determine the number and extent of single-member wards for the election of Committee members, with the possibility of alteration in consultation with the Committee.
Mandates the preparation of an electoral roll for each ward, listing eligible voters. It prohibits multiple registrations for the same person in any ward or across different wards.

Defines the qualifications for an elector, requiring ordinary residence in a ward for a specified period and being a Sikh of at least 21 years of age. It also lists disqualifications, including trimming/shaving beard/hair, smoking, and consuming alcoholic drinks.
Grants the right to vote to every person registered on the electoral roll of a ward for the election of a Committee member, with the restriction that no person can vote in more than one ward.

Outlines the qualifications required to be a member of the Committee, including age (25 years), Indian citizenship, being an Amritdhari Sikh, adherence to Sikh practices (no beard/hair trimming, no smoking, no alcohol, not patit), mental soundness, solvency, and good conduct. It also requires the ability to read and write Gurmukhi and specifies a penalty for unqualified persons sitting or voting as members.

States that elections for members of the Committee will be conducted by the Director Gurdwara Elections according to prescribed rules. It also specifies that casual vacancies occurring within four months of a general election will not be filled until the general election.
Requires the Director Gurdwara Elections to publish the names of elected and co-opted members of the Committee in the prescribed manner.
Authorizes the Central Government to appoint a Director Gurdwara Elections who will have superintendence, direction, and control over the preparation of electoral rolls and elections.

important_rules: Electors must be ordinarily resident in a ward for at least 180 days during the qualifying period and be a Sikh of at least 21 years of age, and must not trim or shave their beard or hair, smoke, or take alcoholic drinks.

Members of the Committee must be at least 25 years old, a citizen of India, an Amritdhari Sikh who adheres to Sikh practices (no beard/hair trimming, no smoking, no alcohol, not patit), of sound mind, solvent, of good conduct, not a paid servant of a Gurdwara, and able to read and write Gurmukhi.
No person shall be registered on the electoral roll for any ward more than once or in more than one ward.
No person shall be entitled to vote at an election in more than one ward.

penalties: A penalty of three hundred rupees is imposed on any person who sits or votes as a member of the Committee knowing they are not qualified. This penalty is recoverable as an arrear of land revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Director Gurdwara Elections is responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls and conducting elections. The Central Government appoints the Director and can make rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the prescribed procedures for election conduct, preparation of electoral rolls, and recovery of penalties as arrears of land revenue. The Central Government has the power to make rules, and the Committee has the power to make regulations.

rights: Right to vote for registered electors in their respective wards.
Right to be elected or co-opted as a member of the Committee if qualifications are met.
Right to manage and control Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property through the Committee.
The Act shall not affect the rites and practices of the Sikh religion.
duties: Duty to adhere to the prescribed qualifications and disqualifications for electors and members.
Duty to participate in the management and control of Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property as per the Act.
Duty to ensure proper functioning of the Committee, Executive Board, and sub-committees.
Members, officers, and employees are deemed to be public servants.
obligations: Obligation for eligible Sikhs to register on electoral rolls for their wards.
Obligation to adhere to the definition of a Sikh and Amritdhari Sikh as specified.
Obligation to maintain accounts and ensure audit of the Gurdwara Fund.
Prohibition of making contributions from the Gurdwara Fund for political purposes.

key_procedures: Preparation and publication of electoral rolls for each ward.
Conduct of elections by the Director Gurdwara Elections.
Publication of election and co-option results.
Establishment and functioning of the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee, including the election of office-bearers and formation of an Executive Board and sub-committees.
Preparation and approval of the budget and maintenance of accounts.
Audit of accounts by auditors appointed by the Committee.
Procedure for affiliation of local Gurdwaras.
Settlement of election disputes and other disputes by the competent authorities.
administration: The Central Government appoints the Director Gurdwara Elections and makes rules. The Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee administers the Act and makes regulations. The Act also mentions the Shromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, Amritsar.
important_notes: The Act commenced on April 7, 1972, as notified by the Central Government.

The head priests of the four Takhats (Sri Akal Takhat Sahib, Sri Takhat Kesgarh Sahib, Sri Takhat Patna Sahib, and Sri Takhat Hazur Sahib) have no right to vote for the election of office-bearers and other members of the Executive Board.
Members, officers, and other employees of the Committee are considered public servants.
The salary, etc., of the Director Gurdwara Elections is defrayed out of the Consolidated Fund of India in the first instance.

title: The Departmental Inquiries (Enforcement of Attendance of Witnesses and Production of Documents) Act, 1972
purpose: To provide for the enforcement of attendance of witnesses and production of documents in certain departmental inquiries and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to every departmental inquiry in relation to persons appointed to public services or posts in connection with the affairs of the Union, and persons in the service or pay of local authorities in Union territories, corporations established by or under a Central Act and owned or controlled by the Central Government, government companies where the Central Government holds at least fifty-one percent of paid-up share capital, and societies registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, that are subject to the control of the Central Government. It extends to the whole of India, including the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

key_definitions.departmental inquiry: An inquiry held under or in accordance with any law made by Parliament or any rule made thereunder, or any rule made under the proviso to article 309, or continued under article 313, of the Constitution of India, into any allegation of lack of integrity against any person to whom this Act applies.
key_definitions.inquiring authority: An officer or authority appointed by the Central Government or by any officer or authority subordinate to that Government to hold a departmental inquiry, and includes any officer or authority empowered by or under any law or rule to hold such inquiry.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.

main_sections.section_title: Departmental inquiries to which the Act shall apply
main_sections.description: Defines the scope of departmental inquiries to which the provisions of this Act are applicable.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'departmental inquiry', 'inquiring authority', and 'lack of integrity'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to authorise the exercise of powers specified in section 5
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to authorize inquiring authorities to exercise powers specified in section 5, by notification, for the purposes of any departmental inquiry.

main_sections.section_title: Power of authorised inquiring authority to enforce attendance of witnesses and production of documents
main_sections.description: Confers powers on authorized inquiring authorities to enforce the attendance of witnesses and the production of documents, similar to those vested in a civil court.

main_sections.section_title: Territorial limits in which powers specified in section 5 may be exercised
main_sections.description: Specifies that the territorial jurisdiction of an authorised inquiring authority for exercising powers under section 5 extends to the limits of the territory to which the Act extends.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for giving effect to the provisions of the Act, with a provision for laying such rules before Parliament.

important_rules: Authorized inquiring authorities have the same powers as a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to summon and enforce the attendance of witnesses, examine them on oath, and require the discovery and production of documents or other material evidence.
Authorized inquiring authorities can requisition public records from any court or office.

Processes issued by an authorized inquiring authority for attendance or production of documents are served and executed through the District Judge within whose jurisdiction the person resides or works.
Authorized inquiring authorities are deemed to be civil courts for the purposes of sections 480 and 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in relation to disobedience of processes.

penalties: Disobedience of a process issued by an authorized inquiring authority is treated as disobedience of a process issued by the District Judge, implying potential penalties under relevant civil or criminal procedures.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, through authorized inquiring authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing processes for summoning witnesses and requiring production of documents, which are then enforced through the District Judge.

rights: Right to have attendance of witnesses enforced in departmental inquiries.
Right to have production of documents enforced in departmental inquiries.
duties: Duty to attend departmental inquiries when summoned as a witness.
Duty to produce documents or other material when required in departmental inquiries.
obligations: Obligation to comply with processes issued by authorized inquiring authorities for attendance and production of documents.

key_procedures: The Central Government, by notification, authorizes an inquiring authority to exercise powers under section 5 in relation to a specific class or category of persons for a departmental inquiry.
The authorized inquiring authority issues processes for summoning witnesses and producing documents.
These processes are served and executed through the District Judge.
