Disobedience of such processes is dealt with as if it were disobedience of a process issued by the District Judge.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Reserve Bank of India, the State Bank of India, subsidiary banks, and corresponding new banks are not compelled to produce books of account or other documents claimed to be confidential, nor to make them part of the record or allow inspection, if claimed as confidential.
The Act was extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh via Notifn No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.

title: The Architects Act, 1972
purpose: To provide for the registration of architects and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to architects and matters related to their professional practice and registration.

key_definitions.architect: A person whose name is for the time being entered in the register.
key_definitions.Council: The Council of Architecture constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.recognised qualification: Any qualification in architecture for the time being included in the Schedule or notified under section 15.
key_definitions.register: The register of architects maintained under section 23.
key_definitions.regulation: A regulation made under this Act by the Council.
key_definitions.rule: A rule made under this Act by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Architects Act, 1972', specifies its extent to the whole of India, and outlines the provision for its commencement through a notification by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'architect', 'Council', 'Indian Institute of Architects', 'recognised qualification', 'register', 'regulation', and 'rule'.

Details the constitution of the Council of Architecture, which is a body corporate. It specifies the composition of the Council, including elected architects, nominated persons from educational bodies and government departments, ex-officio members, and state-nominated architects.
Concerns the preparation and ongoing maintenance of a register of architects.
Outlines the qualifications required for an architect to be entered into the register.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for individuals who falsely claim to be registered architects.
Prohibits the unauthorized use of the title 'architect'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Council to make regulations
main_sections.description: Grants the Council of Architecture the power to make regulations under the Act.

important_rules: Rule: Architects must be registered to practice.
Rule: The Council of Architecture is responsible for maintaining the register of architects and setting standards for architectural education.
Rule: False claims of being a registered architect are punishable by penalty.
Rule: The use of the title 'architect' is prohibited for unregistered individuals.

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered (Section 36).
Penalty for failure to surrender a certificate of registration (Section 38).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Council of Architecture and potentially other authorities as designated by the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the maintenance of a register, inquiry proceedings for misconduct, and legal penalties for violations.

rights: Right to be registered as an architect upon meeting prescribed qualifications.
Right to practice architecture after registration.
duties: Duty to maintain professional conduct as prescribed by the Council.
Duty to adhere to the provisions of the Act and regulations made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that architectural education meets minimum standards.
Obligation to cooperate with the Council in matters of registration and professional conduct.

key_procedures: Procedure for Registration: Application for registration, verification of qualifications, and entry into the register (Sections 25, 26).
Procedure for Inquiries: Handling of inquiries relating to misconduct of registered architects, including the process for removal from the register (Section 30).
Procedure for Elections: Conducting elections for the Council members and their officers, including dispute resolution mechanisms (Sections 5, 4).
administration: The Council of Architecture, with the overarching authority and rule-making power vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force on April 2, 1973, vide notification No. G.S.R. 400(E), dated March 16, 1973.
The Council of Architecture is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Members of the Council and its officers are considered public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

title: The Taxation Laws (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 1972
purpose: To provide for the extension of certain taxation laws to the State of Jammu and Kashmir, facilitating the mobilization of additional resources and meeting expenditures for relief of Bangla Desh refugees.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It extends specific provisions of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 1971, the Tax on Postal Articles Act, 1971, and the Inland Air Travel Tax Act, 1971, along with their associated rules and notifications.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on the 1st day of July, 1972.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of certain taxation laws to Jammu and Kashmir and amendments thereto
main_sections.description: Extends Chapter VII of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 1971, and associated rules and notifications to Jammu and Kashmir. It also extends the Tax on Postal Articles Act, 1971, and the Inland Air Travel Tax Act, 1971, along with their rules and notifications to the state.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of references to Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
main_sections.description: Specifies that references to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, within Chapter VII of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 1971, and section 8 of the Inland Air Travel Tax Act, 1971, shall be construed as references to the corresponding law in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

Empowers the Central Government to make orders or give directions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the extended Chapter VII of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 1971, or the Tax on Postal Articles Act, 1971, or the Inland Air Travel Tax Act, 1971, in Jammu and Kashmir. Such orders must be notified in the Official Gazette and made within two years of the Act's commencement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the extension of existing taxation laws, rules, and notifications, and by the Central Government's power to issue orders to remove difficulties.

key_procedures: Extension of specific taxation laws and their associated rules and notifications to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: Section 3 and the Schedule were repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1978.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to orders made within two years from the commencement of this Act.

title: The National Service Act, 1972
purpose: To provide for the registration of qualified persons and for the rendering of national service by such persons and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to qualified citizens of India who are ordinarily resident in India. Qualified persons are those who hold recognized medical qualifications or degrees in engineering or technology, and are under the age of thirty years when they become qualified or at the commencement of the Act.

key_definitions.employer: Any person who employs any qualified person for doing any work in any establishment, including those entrusted with supervision and control.
key_definitions.establishment: Any office, or any place where any industry, trade, business or occupation is carried on, including any technical institution or training centre.
key_definitions.national service: Any service likely to assist the defence of India and civil defence or the efficient conduct of military operations, and includes social service specified by the Central Government for public purposes.
key_definitions.qualified person: A citizen of India ordinarily resident in India who holds a recognized medical qualification or a university degree (or equivalent) in engineering or technology. Special provisions exist to define 'ordinarily resident'.

main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act as the National Service Act, 1972, states that it extends to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'employer', 'establishment', 'national service', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'qualified person'.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of persons to be called up for national service
main_sections.description: Establishes the liability of qualified persons (under 30 years of age) to be called up for national service for a period of not more than four years, commencing from the date of the enlistment notice.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct a person to render service with the Armed Forces of Union or other national service
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to order a qualified person to render service in the Armed Forces of the Union or other specified national service for a specified period and place.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to require any employer to release qualified persons
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to order employers to release qualified persons for national service. It also outlines provisions regarding employer liability for wages, enforceability of contracts, and computation of service periods.

Mandates that qualified persons liable for national service must apply for registration within specified timeframes (90 days from commencement for existing qualified persons, 30 days from becoming liable for new qualified persons).

Details the process of registration, including the Central Government's power to issue general orders for qualified persons to furnish particulars and apply for registration. It also includes penalties for non-compliance.
Addresses offenses related to making false statements or forging documents in connection with the Act.

important_rules: Qualified persons under 30 years old are liable for national service for up to four years (Section 3).
Service in the Armed Forces or other declared equivalent services can be in lieu of national service (Section 4).
Employers must release qualified persons for national service when ordered by the Central Government (Section 8).
Qualified persons must register under the Act within specified timeframes (Section 11).
Leaving national service or employment after being served with a notice, without permission, is an offense punishable by imprisonment and fine (Section 10).

penalties: Imprisonment up to three years and fine up to one thousand rupees for failing to comply with registration orders (Section 12(3)).
Imprisonment up to three years and fine up to one thousand rupees for an employer failing to release a qualified person (Section 8(5)).

Imprisonment up to five years and fine up to two thousand rupees for a qualified person leaving employment or being discharged therefrom otherwise than in accordance with the Act after receiving a notice (Section 10(3)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders, notifications, general orders for registration, and by prescribing penalties for non-compliance. The Act also outlines provisions for summary trial of offenses and jurisdiction for trying offenses.

rights: Right to perform service in the Armed Forces or equivalent services in lieu of national service (Section 4).
Right to preservation of certain rights while rendering national service (Section 24).
duties: Duty to register under the Act if qualified and liable (Section 11).
Duty to render national service when called up (Section 3).
Duty to serve in the appointed branch or position and be subject to relevant laws and rules (Section 7).
Duty not to leave national service or employment without permission (Section 10).
obligations: Qualified persons are obligated to serve for a specified period.
Employers have an obligation to release qualified persons when directed by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Registration of qualified persons: Furnishing particulars and making an application for registration as directed by the Central Government (Section 12).
Calling up for national service: Issuance of an enlistment notice requiring the qualified person to present themselves to a specified authority (Section 3(2)).
Reinstatement of qualified persons: Procedures related to their return to previous employment (Chapter V).
administration: The Central Government, with provisions for delegation of powers (Section 35) and the making of rules and regulations (Sections 36, 37).
important_notes: The Act allows for voluntary service in lieu of national service under certain conditions (Section 4).
Postponement of national service is possible on grounds of hardship, with provisions for a committee and appeals (Chapter IV).
The Act includes provisions for the protection of actions taken in good faith (Section 33) and for the removal of difficulties (Section 34).

title: The Delhi Lands (Restrictions on Transfer) Act, 1972
purpose: To impose restrictions on the transfer of lands that have been acquired by the Central Government or for which acquisition proceedings have been initiated, with the aim of preventing large-scale fraudulent transfers and protecting the public from unknowingly purchasing such lands.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi. It applies to lands acquired by the Central Government or lands in relation to which acquisition proceedings have been initiated by the Central Government for the planned development of Delhi, including any scheme, project, or work implemented under the Delhi Master Plan.

key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator of the Union territory of Delhi appointed by the President.
key_definitions.competent authority: Any person or authority authorized by the Administrator to perform the functions of the competent authority under the Act for specified areas.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheme: The scheme of acquisition of land for the planned development of Delhi and includes any scheme, project, or work to be implemented in pursuance of the Delhi Master Plan.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Union territory of Delhi), and states that it comes into force at once.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'competent authority', 'Development Act', 'prescribed', and 'Scheme'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on transfer of lands acquired by Central Government
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from transferring, by sale, mortgage, gift, lease, or otherwise, any land situated in Delhi that has already been acquired by the Central Government under the Land Acquisition Act or any other law for a public purpose.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation on transfer of lands in relation to which acquisition proceedings have been initiated
main_sections.description: Prohibits the transfer of land situated in Delhi, which is proposed for acquisition in connection with a Scheme, unless the previous written permission of the competent authority is obtained. This applies after a declaration under section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act has been made and not withdrawn.

main_sections.section_title: Application for grant of permission for transfer under section 4
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for applying for permission to transfer land under section 4. It details the application process, the grounds for refusal, the requirement to record reasons for refusal, and the deemed grant of permission if no refusal is communicated within thirty days.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals against orders of competent authority
main_sections.description: Provides for appeals against orders of the competent authority under section 5. It specifies the timeframe for filing an appeal, the authority to whom the appeal is filed, and that the appellate authority's order is final.

main_sections.section_title: Period of operation of orders of refusal to grant permission to transfer land
main_sections.description: States that an order refusing permission to transfer land is effective only for three years from the date of the order, after which the land can be transferred subject to section 3. It also specifies that periods of court-stayed acquisition proceedings are excluded from this three-year period.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on registration of transfers of land
main_sections.description: Mandates that registering officers shall not register documents purporting to transfer land referred to in section 4 unless a written permission from the competent authority is produced.
Specifies the penalty for contravening the provisions of section 3 or section 4, which is imprisonment up to three years, fine, or both.

Deals with offences committed by companies, making those in charge of the company's business liable, and also holding directors, managers, or other officers liable if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect.

Grants the Administrator the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including matters related to applications for permission, appeals, and other prescribed matters. It also outlines the procedure for laying rules before Parliament.

important_rules: No person shall transfer any land acquired by the Central Government in Delhi (Section 3).
No person shall transfer land proposed for acquisition by the Central Government in Delhi without the written permission of the competent authority (Section 4).
Permission to transfer land can be refused if the land is needed for the Scheme, the objectives of the Delhi Development Authority, or for various development purposes (Section 5(3)).
If the competent authority does not refuse permission within 30 days of receiving an application, the permission is deemed to have been granted (Section 5(5)).
Orders of refusal to grant permission are only valid for three years (Section 7).
Registering officers must not register transfer documents for land under section 4 unless competent authority permission is shown (Section 8).

penalties: Contravention of sections 3 or 4 is punishable with imprisonment for up to three years, or with fine, or with both (Section 9).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The 'competent authority' is authorized to grant or refuse permission for transfers, and the 'Administrator' has the power to make rules and appoint the competent authority. Registering officers are also involved in enforcement by restricting registration of documents.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the requirement for prior written permission for transfers of proposed acquisition lands, restrictions on registration of such transfers, penalties for contravention, and the appellate process. The 'competent authority' investigates applications and makes decisions. The 'Administrator' has the power to make rules to ensure the Act's purposes are met.

rights: Right to apply for permission to transfer land proposed for acquisition (Section 5).
Right to appeal against an order of refusal by the competent authority (Section 6).
Right to transfer land after a refusal order expires, subject to Section 3 (Section 7).
duties: Duty not to transfer lands already acquired by the Central Government (Section 3).
Duty to obtain prior written permission from the competent authority before transferring lands proposed for acquisition (Section 4).
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation to provide prescribed particulars in an application for transfer permission (Section 5(1)).
Obligation for the competent authority to record reasons for refusal of permission (Section 5(4)).
Obligation for registering officers to verify permission before registering transfer documents for specific lands (Section 8).

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for permission to transfer land under Section 4: A written application with prescribed particulars is made to the competent authority, which then makes inquiries, grants or refuses permission, and communicates the decision with reasons if refused. If no refusal is communicated within 30 days, permission is deemed granted (Section 5).

Procedure for appeal against an order of the competent authority: An aggrieved person can file an appeal within 30 days to the prescribed authority in the prescribed form. The appellate authority hears the appellant and disposes of the appeal expeditiously (Section 6).
administration: The Administrator of the Union territory of Delhi, who appoints the competent authority. The Central Government is involved in the acquisition of land and framing of policies.
important_notes: The Act aims to curb unauthorized sale of plots by private colonizers, which leads to illegal colonies and vitiates urban planning efforts (Statement of Objects and Reasons).
The Act is intended to protect the general public from losing their savings by purchasing invalid titles to land (Statement of Objects and Reasons).
The definition of 'Scheme' is crucial as it encompasses land acquisition for planned development of Delhi, including projects under the Delhi Master Plan (Section 2(e)).
The period during which acquisition proceedings are stayed by a court is excluded from the three-year period for the operation of refusal orders (Section 7 Explanation).

title: The Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972
purpose: To regulate the export trade in antiquities and art treasures, prevent smuggling and fraudulent dealings in antiquities, provide for compulsory acquisition of antiquities and art treasures for preservation in public places, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental or ancillary thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to antiquities and art treasures, regulating their export, sale, and registration. It also covers provisions related to their compulsory acquisition and the enforcement of the Act.

key_definitions.antiquity: Includes coins, sculptures, paintings, epigraphs, works of art or craftsmanship, articles detached from buildings or caves, articles illustrative of science, art, crafts, literature, religion, customs, morals, or politics in bygone ages, articles of historical interest, and anything declared an antiquity by the Central Government, provided it has existed for at least one hundred years. It also includes manuscripts, records, or documents of scientific, historical, literary, or aesthetic value that have existed for at least seventy-five years.
key_definitions.art treasure: Any human work of art, not being an antiquity, declared by the Central Government to be an art treasure due to its artistic or aesthetic value. No declaration can be made if the author is alive.
key_definitions.export: Taking out of India to a place outside India.
key_definitions.licensing officer: An officer appointed as such under section 6.
key_definitions.registering officer: An officer appointed as such under section 15.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date, which can be appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'antiquity', 'art treasure', 'export', 'licensing officer', 'registering officer', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of export trade in antiquities and art treasures
main_sections.description: Prohibits the export of antiquities and art treasures by any person other than the Central Government or an authorized authority/agency, unless under a permit issued by a prescribed authority.

main_sections.section_title: Antiquities to be sold only under a licence
main_sections.description: Mandates that no person shall carry on the business of selling or offering to sell any antiquity except under a licence granted under section 8, after a specified period from the commencement of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to specify which antiquities shall be registered under the Act, considering factors like conservation necessity.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to compulsorily acquire antiquities and art treasures
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to compulsorily acquire antiquities and art treasures for preservation in public places.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: No person other than the Central Government or its authorized agency can export antiquities or art treasures, and such export must be with a permit.
Rule 2: The business of selling or offering to sell antiquities requires a licence.
Rule 3: Certain antiquities must be registered under the Act.
Rule 4: The Central Government has the power to compulsorily acquire antiquities and art treasures.
Rule 5: Licensees must maintain prescribed records, photographs, and registers, which are subject to inspection.

penalties: Penalty for contravening provisions of the Act (detailed in Section 25).
Magistrate's power to impose enhanced penalties (Section 27).
Provisions for offences by companies (Section 28).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and appointed licensing and registering officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through licensing, registration, inspection of records, search and seizure powers, penalties for contravention, and compulsory acquisition provisions. The Customs Act, 1962, is also applied in relation to export prohibition.

rights: Right to apply for a licence to sell antiquities (subject to conditions).
Right to appeal against decisions of licensing and registering officers.
Right to receive compensation for compulsorily acquired antiquities.
Right to sell licensed antiquities to other licensees upon revocation of a licence (under specific conditions).
duties: Duty to obtain a licence to sell antiquities.
Duty to comply with the conditions of a licence.
Duty to maintain records, photographs, and registers.
Duty to intimate transfer of ownership of registered antiquities.
Duty to comply with provisions regarding export permits and registration.
Duty to declare antiquities in possession upon revocation of licence or cessation of licence due to government takeover of business.
obligations: Obligation to not export antiquities or art treasures without authorization.
Obligation to adhere to the prescribed manner of selling, recording, and reporting.
Obligation to cooperate with licensing and registering officers during inspections and searches.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a licence to sell antiquities: application to the licensing officer, inquiry, and grant based on specified factors.
Procedure for renewal of a licence: application to the licensing officer.
Procedure for registration of antiquities: Central Government specifies antiquities, application for registration, and grant of a certificate.
Procedure for compulsory acquisition: Central Government's power to acquire, with provisions for compensation.
Procedure for appeals: against decisions of licensing and registering officers, and against awards of arbitrators.
Procedure for export: requiring a permit from a prescribed authority.
Procedure for search, seizure, and entry by authorized officers.
administration: The Central Government, and appointed licensing and registering officers.
important_notes: The definition of 'antiquity' excludes ancient and historical records that are not declared by or under law made by Parliament to be of national importance, for the purposes of sale under sections 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 17, and 18.
The Act can be applied to the State of Sikkim with specific provisions coming into force on designated dates.
The Customs Act, 1962, is applied to the export of antiquities and art treasures, with modifications concerning confiscation.
The Central Government can compulsorily acquire antiquities and art treasures for preservation in public places.
The Central Government can, by notification, decide to exclusively carry on the business of selling antiquities, ceasing the licensing provisions for private persons.
No licence shall be granted if the applicant has been convicted of an offence under the Antiquities (Export Control) Act, 1947, unless ten years have passed since conviction.

title: The General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of shares of Indian insurance companies and undertakings of other existing insurers to serve the economy by developing general insurance business in the best interests of the community, to prevent concentration of wealth to the common detriment, and to regulate and control such business.
scope: Applies to general insurance business in India. It nationalizes existing Indian insurance companies and the undertakings of other existing insurers, including foreign insurers and the general insurance business of the Life Insurance Corporation.

key_definitions.acquiring company: Any Indian insurance company, or an Indian insurance company formed by merger or amalgamation of other Indian insurance companies.
key_definitions.appointed day: A day not later than January 2, 1973, as notified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.existing insurer: Every insurer whose undertaking management vested in the Central Government under the General Insurance (Emergency Provisions) Act, 1971, and includes the general insurance business of the Life Insurance Corporation.
key_definitions.foreign insurer: An existing insurer incorporated outside India.
key_definitions.general insurance business: As defined in the Insurance Act, 1938.
key_definitions.Indian insurance company: An existing insurer with share capital, which is a company under the Companies Act.
key_definitions.Corporation: The General Insurance Corporation of India formed under section 9.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to the policy of the State
main_sections.description: Declares the Act's purpose is to give effect to the State's policy towards securing principles specified in Article 39(c) of the Constitution (economic system not resulting in concentration of wealth to common detriment).
Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of shares of Indian insurance companies
main_sections.description: Vests all shares of Indian insurance companies in the Central Government on the appointed day. The Central Government then transfers at least ten shares to specified persons to enable functioning as a Government company.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of undertakings of other existing insurers
main_sections.description: Transfers the undertaking of every existing insurer (not an Indian insurance company) to the Central Government and then to a specified Indian insurance company.

Specifies that the transferred undertaking includes all assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations. Existing contracts and legal proceedings continue to be valid and enforceable against the acquiring Indian insurance company.

main_sections.section_title: Formation of General Insurance Corporation of India
main_sections.description: Provides for the formation of the General Insurance Corporation of India.
Details the functions of the General Insurance Corporation of India.

main_sections.section_title: Acquiring companies to have the exclusive privilege of carrying on general insurance business
main_sections.description: Grants exclusive privilege to acquiring companies to conduct general insurance business.

important_rules: Rule 1: On the appointed day, all shares of Indian insurance companies are transferred to and vested in the Central Government.
Rule 2: The Central Government shall then transfer a minimum of ten shares of each such company to specified persons to facilitate its functioning as a Government company.

Rule 3: The undertaking of every existing insurer (not an Indian insurance company) is transferred to and vested in the Central Government and subsequently transferred to a specified Indian insurance company.
Rule 4: All assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations of the transferred undertakings are vested in the acquiring Indian insurance company.
Rule 5: Existing deeds, agreements, and legal proceedings remain in force and are enforceable by or against the acquiring Indian insurance company.

penalties: Penalty for withholding property, etc. (Section 30): Imposes penalties for withholding property or documents related to the transferred undertaking.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and authorities appointed or designated under the Act. Enforcement is also implied through the provisions of the Insurance Act and Companies Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, rectification of company registers, transfer of assets and liabilities, and legal proceedings as outlined in the Act. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance.

rights: Right of acquiring company to seek relief in respect of certain transactions (Section 28).
duties: Duty to deliver possession of property and documents relating thereto (Section 29).
obligations: Existing liabilities and obligations of the acquired undertakings are transferred to the acquiring companies.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Notification by the Central Government to appoint the 'appointed day' for the transfer of shares and undertakings.
Procedure 2: Notification by the Central Government to specify the Indian insurance company to which the undertaking of an existing insurer will be transferred.
Procedure 3: Rectification of the register of members of Indian insurance companies by including the names of persons to whom shares are transferred by the Central Government.
Procedure 4: Framing of schemes for reorganization of general insurance business, including mergers (Section 16).
administration: The Central Government is primarily responsible for the administration of this Act, including issuing notifications, making rules, and overseeing the transfer and management of general insurance business. The General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC) also plays a significant administrative role.
important_notes: The Act provides for the nationalization of general insurance business in India.
The Act aims to ensure that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth to the common detriment.
Provisions related to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India do not apply to International Financial Services Centres (Section 38A).
The Act has been amended multiple times, including significant amendments in 1985, 1989, 2002, 2015, 2019, and 2021.

title: The Former Secretary of State Service Officers (Conditions of Service) Act, 1972
purpose: To provide for the variation or revocation of the conditions of service of former Secretary of State Service officers in respect of certain matters and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to former Secretary of State Service officers, specifically members of the Indian Civil Service (ICS) who are now part of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and members of the Indian Police (IP) who are now part of the Indian Police Service (IPS). It also covers matters related to their remuneration, leave, pension, and disciplinary rights. The scope is national, covering officers in India.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.former Secretary of State Service office: A person referred to in sub-clause (a) or sub-clause (b) of clause (1) of article 312A of the Constitution.
key_definitions.I.C.S. member of the Indian Administrati: A person who was appointed to the Civil Service of the Crown in India known as the Indian Civil Service and who on the appointed day is a member of the Indian Administrative Service.
key_definitions.I.P. member of the Indian Police Service: A person who was appointed to the Police Service of the Crown in India known as the Indian Police and who on the appointed day is a member of the Indian Police Service.
key_definitions.pension: Has the meaning assigned to it in clause (17) of article 366 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'former Secretary of State Service officer', 'I.C.S. member of the Indian Administrative Service', 'I.P. member of the Indian Police Service', and 'pension'.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions of service of I.C.S. members of the Indian Administrative Service
main_sections.description: Specifies that from the appointed day, the conditions of service (remuneration, leave, pension, disciplinary matters, and other rights) for I.C.S. members of the IAS shall be the same as other members of that Service, applying the All-India Services Act, 1951 and its rules/regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions of service of I.P. members of the Indian Police Service
main_sections.description: Similar to Section 3, this section states that from the appointed day, the conditions of service (remuneration, leave, pension, disciplinary matters, and other rights) for I.P. members of the IPS shall be the same as other members of that Service, applying the All-India Services Act, 1951 and its rules/regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Pay of I.C.S. members of Indian Administrative Service and I.P. members of Indian Police Service
main_sections.description: Overriding Sections 3 and 4, this section states that I.C.S. or I.P. members holding specific posts listed in the Schedule or equivalent posts shall be entitled to draw pay as indicated against those posts.

main_sections.section_title: Retirement of I.C.S. members of Indian Administrative Service and I.P. members of Indian Police Service
main_sections.description: Outlines compulsory retirement conditions (age 58, or earlier if rules permit), the Central Government's power to retire officers in public interest (after 30 years of service or reaching 50 years of age, with notice), and voluntary retirement options for officers (after 30 years of service or reaching 50 years of age, with notice). 'Qualifying service' is defined as service qualifying for pension.

main_sections.section_title: Pension of I.C.S. members of Indian Administrative Service
main_sections.description: Details pension entitlement for I.C.S. members, including an annuity of Rs. 13,333.33. It also specifies conditions for death-cum-retirement gratuity, family pension benefits, and Provident Fund accounts, contingent on options exercised before the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Pension payable to former Secretary of State Service officers in Indian currency only
main_sections.description: Prohibits entitlement to claim pension in sterling, payment outside India, or computation at an exchange rate exceeding Rs. 13.33 to a pound sterling. It includes provisos for specific cases (domiciled in India on 1st Feb 1921, foreigners residing outside India) and requires refunds for overpayments based on higher exchange rates. It also clarifies applicability to judges, constitutional office holders, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to adapt certain rules, regulations and orders
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to adapt and modify existing rules, regulations, and orders applicable to former Secretary of State Service officers to align them with the Act, within two years of the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Power to construe rules, regulations and orders
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to interpret and apply existing rules, regulations, and orders in a manner consistent with the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make orders in certain cases to ensure parity
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue orders to ensure parity in certain situations.
Confers power upon the Central Government to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Declares that this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of orders in respect of disciplinary matters
main_sections.description: Saves any orders made concerning disciplinary matters before the commencement of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: From the appointed day, the conditions of service for I.C.S. members of the IAS and I.P. members of the IPS, including remuneration, leave, pension, and disciplinary matters, shall be the same as those of other members of their respective services (Sections 3 & 4).
Rule 2: I.C.S. or I.P. members holding specific scheduled posts or equivalent posts shall draw pay as per the schedule for as long as they hold such posts (Section 5).

Rule 3: I.C.S. and I.P. members will be subject to compulsory retirement at age 58, or earlier if applicable rules dictate. The Central Government can also require retirement in public interest after 30 years of service or upon reaching 50 years of age, with due notice (Section 6).

Rule 4: Pensions for former Secretary of State Service officers are payable only in Indian currency and are subject to specific exchange rate limitations. Certain exceptions exist for officers domiciled in India or residing permanently outside India, with specific conditions for converting annuities (Section 8).

penalties: Refund of excess pension amounts paid due to incorrect exchange rate calculations (Section 8(2)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette to set the commencement date (Section 1), by issuing orders to adapt rules and regulations (Section 9), by making orders to ensure parity (Section 10A), by issuing orders to remove difficulties (Section 11), and by enforcing the refund of excess pension payments (Section 8(2)).

rights: Right to have conditions of service (remuneration, leave, pension, disciplinary matters) aligned with other members of IAS/IPS (Sections 3 & 4).
Right to draw pay as per the schedule for specific posts (Section 5).
Right to voluntary retirement after fulfilling specified service or age criteria (Section 6(c)).
Right to receive pension as per Section 7 for I.C.S. members.
Right for certain officers to convert annuities into pound sterling under specific conditions (Section 8(1) proviso).
duties: Duty to retire compulsorily at the specified age or as required in public interest (Section 6).
Duty to provide notice for voluntary retirement (Section 6(c)).
Duty to refund any excess pension amounts paid based on incorrect exchange rates (Section 8(2)).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the conditions of service as laid down in the Act and applicable rules and regulations.
Obligation to comply with the Central Government's power to require retirement in public interest.
Obligation to comply with the exchange rate limitations for pension payments, unless specific provisos apply.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Commencement of the Act: The Central Government issues a notification in the Official Gazette to appoint the date on which the Act comes into force (Section 1(2)).

Procedure 2: Adaptation of Rules: The Central Government, within two years of the appointed day, publishes orders in the Official Gazette to adapt or modify existing rules and regulations to align with the Act (Section 9(1)).

Procedure 3: Retirement Process: For compulsory retirement in public interest, the Central Government consults with the State Government and gives the officer at least three months' written notice (Section 6(b)). For voluntary retirement, the officer must give at least three months' written notice to the State Government (Section 6(c)).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning it prevails over any other law that is inconsistent with its provisions (Section 12).
Orders made in respect of disciplinary matters before the Act came into force are saved (Section 13).

Special conditions apply to certain former Secretary of State Service officers regarding pension calculation and payment, particularly those domiciled in India or residing permanently outside India (Section 8).

title: The Richardson and Cruddas Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertaking) Act, 1972
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertaking of Richardson and Cruddas Limited, for the reconstruction of the register of its members, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, ensuring continuity of production and supply of goods by the company in the public interest.
scope: This act applies to the undertaking of Richardson and Cruddas Limited, a company registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1913, with its registered office in West Bengal. It also covers its assets, liabilities, employees, and members.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date appointed by the Central Government by notification for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking.
key_definitions.custodian: The person appointed as the Custodian of the old company under section 10.
key_definitions.nationalised_bank: A corresponding new bank as defined in the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970.
key_definitions.new_company: The Government company formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956, in pursuance of section 9.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.old_company: Richardson and Cruddas Limited, a company formed and registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1913, with its registered office in West Bengal.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.scheduled_bank: As defined in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and includes a Nationalised Bank.
key_definitions.share: A share in the capital of the old company.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as The Richardson and Cruddas Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertaking) Act, 1972.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Custodian', 'Nationalised Bank', 'new company', 'notification', 'old company', 'prescribed', 'scheduled bank', 'share', and 'Tribunal'.

main_sections.section_title: Undertaking of the old company to vest in the Central Government
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the undertaking of the old company shall transfer to and vest in the Central Government, which will then notify the transfer to the new company.

Details the comprehensive nature of the vesting, including all assets, rights, powers, liabilities, and obligations of the old company related to its undertaking. It also covers the continuation of existing contracts, deeds, and legal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to deliver possession of property acquired and documents relating thereto
main_sections.description: Requires any person in possession of vested property or documents relating to the undertaking to deliver them to the Central Government or the new company.
Obligates the old company to furnish a complete inventory of its properties, assets, liabilities, and agreements to the Central Government and the new company.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to employees of the old company
main_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of officers and employees of the old company to the Central Government and then to the new company, with continuity of service terms, unless they opt out or their terms are altered and not accepted.
Specifies a payment of thirty lakh rupees by the Central Government to the Custodian for the transfer of the undertaking, to be held in trust for the old company.

main_sections.section_title: Formation and registration of a new company
main_sections.description: Deals with the formation and registration of a new Government company for the efficient management and administration of the undertaking.
Provides for the establishment of a Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Tribunal to call upon persons to make claims
main_sections.description: Empowers the Tribunal to invite persons to submit claims.
Outlines the Tribunal's role in determining the authenticity of shares.

main_sections.section_title: No compensation for cancellation of spurious shares
main_sections.description: States that no compensation will be paid for the cancellation of spurious shares.
Deals with offences and their penalties.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: On the appointed day, the undertaking of Richardson and Cruddas Limited vests in the Central Government and is subsequently transferred to a newly formed Government company.
All assets, rights, powers, privileges, property, cash balances, reserve funds, investments, borrowings, liabilities, and obligations of the old company related to its undertaking are transferred.
Existing contracts, deeds, bonds, and agreements related to the undertaking remain in force and are enforceable by the Central Government or the new company.
Legal proceedings initiated by or against the old company concerning its undertaking can be continued by or against the Central Government or the new company.
Persons possessing property or documents belonging to the undertaking must deliver them to the Central Government or the new company.
The old company must provide a comprehensive inventory of its assets, liabilities, and agreements to the Central Government and the new company.

Employees of the old company (except directors or specified managerial personnel) become employees of the Central Government and then the new company on the same terms and conditions, with provisions for termination if alterations are not accepted.
A payment of thirty lakh rupees is made by the Central Government to the Custodian for the undertaking, to be held in trust for the old company.
A Tribunal is constituted to handle claims, determine genuine shares, and deal with matters related to the rectification of the register of members.
No compensation is payable for the cancellation of spurious shares.
The Central Government has the power to make rules to implement the Act.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed in Part III of the Act (Section 24). Specific details of these penalties are not yet provided in the text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the newly constituted Tribunal are the primary authorities for enforcement and adjudication.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the vesting of the undertaking, the transfer of liabilities and obligations, the continuation of legal proceedings, the powers of the Tribunal, and the imposition of penalties for offences.

rights: Employees of the old company have the right to hold office on the same terms and conditions with rights to pension, gratuity, etc., unless their employment is duly terminated.
Shareholders with genuine shares have rights related to the reconstruction of the register of members and potential reimbursement as determined by the Tribunal.
The Central Government and the new company have rights to the undertaking, its assets, and all related instruments and proceedings.
The Tribunal has the power to entertain and dispose of claims for reimbursement.
duties: Every person in possession of vested property or documents must deliver them to the Central Government or the new company.
The old company has a duty to furnish particulars and inventories.
The Custodian has a duty to open an account and hold the payment amount in trust.
The Custodian has a duty to reconstruct the register of members and issue fresh share certificates.
obligations: The Central Government is obligated to pay an amount for the acquisition of the undertaking.
The Central Government and the new company have obligations to continue existing contracts and legal proceedings related to the undertaking.
The Central Government and the new company have obligations to ensure continuity of employment and terms for transferred employees.

key_procedures: Acquisition and Transfer: On the appointed day, the undertaking vests in the Central Government, which then transfers it to a new company.
Delivery of Property and Documents: Persons in possession must deliver vested property and related documents.
Furnishing Particulars: The old company must provide a detailed inventory of assets, liabilities, and agreements.
Employee Transfer: Employees are transferred to the new company with continuity of service, with options for termination if terms are not acceptable.
Payment for Undertaking: The Central Government makes a payment to the Custodian for the acquisition.
Tribunal Proceedings: Claims are made to the Tribunal, which determines genuine shares and handles reimbursement claims.
Reconstruction of Register of Members: The Custodian reconstructs the register of members and issues new share certificates.
administration: The Central Government, the newly formed 'new company' (a Government company), and a constituted 'Tribunal' are involved in the administration of this Act.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the context of alleged mismanagement of Richardson and Cruddas Limited and the existence of a large number of duplicate shares, which made proper management by a constituted Board of Directors impossible.
The purpose is to ensure continuity of production and supply of goods by the company in the public interest.
The appointed day for the transfer was notified as March 31, 1973.
The Act overrides other laws such as the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, regarding compensation for employee transfers.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act (Section 27).

title: THE AUTHORITATIVE TEXTS (CENTRAL LAWS) ACT, 1973
purpose: To provide for authoritative texts of Central laws in certain languages.
scope: This Act applies to Central Acts, Ordinances promulgated by the President, and any order, rule, regulation, or bye-law issued under the Constitution or under any Central Act. The scope is for translations in languages specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, other than Hindi.

key_definitions.authoritative_text: A translation in a language specified in the Eighth Schedule (other than Hindi) of any Central Act or Ordinance, or any order, rule, regulation, or bye-law, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the '[Authoritative Texts] (Central Laws) Act, 1973' and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Authoritative texts of Central laws in certain languages
main_sections.description: This section defines what constitutes an authoritative text. It states that a translation in a language (other than Hindi) from the Eighth Schedule, published under the President's authority in the Official Gazette, of any Central Act, Ordinance, or any subordinate legislation issued under the Constitution or a Central Act, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in that language.

This section empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act by notification in the Official Gazette. It also includes a provision for laying these rules before both Houses of Parliament for a total of thirty days during a session or successive sessions, and for modifications or annulments by Parliament.

important_rules: Any translation of a Central Act, Ordinance, or subordinate legislation in a language specified in the Eighth Schedule (other than Hindi), published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be considered the authoritative text in that language.
The Central Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, which must be notified in the Official Gazette.
Rules made by the Central Government must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and are subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette and by laying rules before Parliament for approval or modification.

rights: Right to have authoritative texts of Central laws in specified languages.
duties: The Central Government has the duty to appoint a commencement date via notification.
The Central Government has the duty to make rules for the Act's purposes.
Parliament has the duty to review and potentially modify or annul rules made by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement: The Central Government issues a notification in the Official Gazette to appoint the date on which the Act comes into force.

Procedure for making rules: The Central Government makes rules by notification in the Official Gazette. These rules are then laid before both Houses of Parliament for a period of thirty days, after which they can be modified or annulled by Parliament. Any modification or annulment does not affect the validity of actions previously taken under the rule.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1988 (Act 18 of 1988) to substitute 'authorised translations' with 'authoritative texts'.
The commencement date for the Act was 1st July, 1981, as per notification S.O. 482(E) dated 15th June, 1981.

title: The Delhi Urban Art Commission Act, 1973
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the Delhi Urban Art Commission with a view to preserving, developing and maintaining the aesthetic quality of urban and environmental design within Delhi.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi. Covers urban and environmental design, including building operations, engineering operations, and development proposals that affect the skyline, aesthetic quality, or public amenities.

key_definitions.building: Includes any structure or erection or part of a structure or erection intended for residential, industrial, commercial, or other purposes, whether in actual use or not.
key_definitions.building operations: Includes rebuilding operations, structural alterations of, or additions to, buildings and other operations normally undertaken in connection with the construction of buildings.
key_definitions.commission: The Delhi Urban Art Commission established under section 3.
key_definitions.development: Includes carrying out of building, engineering, mining or other operations in, on, over or under, land or the making of any material change in any building or land and includes re-development.
key_definitions.local body: Includes the Delhi Municipal Corporation, the New Delhi Municipal Committee, the Delhi Development Authority, or any other local authority concerned with urban development of Delhi.
key_definitions.public amenity: Includes road, water supply, street lighting, drainage, sewerage, public works and such other convenience as the Central Government may specify.

main_sections.description: Defines the short title as 'The Delhi Urban Art Commission Act, 1973', specifies its extent to the Union territory of Delhi, and outlines the commencement procedure via notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'building', 'development', 'local body', and 'public amenity'.
Provides for the establishment of the Delhi Urban Art Commission as a body corporate with perpetual succession and power to acquire property and contract.

Details the composition of the Commission, consisting of a Chairman and other members appointed by the Central Government based on their sensibility and interest in arts and urban environment, or relevant knowledge/experience.

Outlines the general duty of the Commission to advise the Central Government on preserving, developing, and maintaining the aesthetic quality of urban and environmental design in Delhi. It also details the Commission's duty to scrutinize, approve, reject, or modify proposals related to various development aspects including district centres, re-development of specific areas, architectural expressions, conservation of historical sites, public amenities, and other beautification projects.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of local bodies to refer development proposals, etc., to the Commission
main_sections.description: Mandates local bodies to refer building operations, engineering operations, or development proposals relevant to Section 11 to the Commission for scrutiny, with the Commission's decision being binding.

Grants the Commission powers similar to a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning persons, examining them, requiring production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, and requisitioning public records.
Establishes a fund for the Commission, to which sums paid by the Central Government will be credited, and from which all payments by the Commission will be made.

important_rules: Local bodies must refer development proposals affecting aesthetic quality or public amenities to the Commission for scrutiny before approval.
The Commission's decisions on referred proposals are binding on local bodies.
The Central Government can revise decisions made by the Commission if deemed necessary in the public interest, after providing an opportunity for representation.
Members of the Commission are appointed for a term of three years and are eligible for re-appointment only once.
The Commission shall meet at times and places and follow procedures as prescribed by regulations.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Delhi Urban Art Commission and the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the Commission's power to scrutinize, approve, reject, or modify proposals, and by the Central Government's appellate and revisory powers. Local bodies are mandated to comply with the Commission's decisions.

rights: Local bodies have the right to appeal to the Central Government against decisions of the Commission.
Persons affected by Central Government revisory orders have the right to make a representation.
duties: It is the general duty of the Commission to advise the Central Government and local bodies on aesthetic quality of urban design.
Local bodies have a duty to refer development proposals to the Commission.
The Commission has a duty to scrutinize, approve, reject, or modify development proposals.
obligations: Local bodies are obligated to abide by the decisions of the Commission.
The Central Government has an obligation to consider appeals from local bodies and may review Commission decisions in the public interest.

key_procedures: Referral of development proposals by local bodies to the Commission for scrutiny.
Scrutiny, approval, rejection, or modification of proposals by the Commission.
Appeal by a local body to the Central Government against a Commission decision.
Central Government's power to suo motu examine and revise Commission decisions.
administration: The Central Government, through its notifications and by appointing members and the Secretary. The Commission itself administers its functions.
important_notes: The Act came into force on May 1, 1974, as per notification No. G.S.R. 189(E).
The Commission shall have its own fund, and all payments to it by the Central Government shall be carried to this fund.
Members of the Commission and its officers are considered public servants.

title: THE ECONOMIC OFFENCES (IN APPLICABILITY OF LIMITATION) ACT, 1974
purpose: To provide for the inapplicability of the provisions of Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to certain economic offences.
scope: The act extends to the territories to which the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 applies. It applies to offences punishable under enactments specified in the Schedule, and any other offence that may be tried along with such offences. It specifically excludes the application of Chapter XXXVI (limitation) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to these offences.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (coinciding with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973), and its commencement date (April 1, 1974).

main_sections.section_title: Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 not to apply to certain offences
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, which deals with the limitation period for filing certain cases, shall not apply to offences listed in the Schedule or offences triable along with them. It states that courts can take cognizance of such offences as if the limitation provisions were not enacted.

important_rules: Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, shall not apply to offences listed in the Schedule.
Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, shall not apply to any offence which, under the provisions of that Code, may be tried along with the scheduled offences.
Courts having jurisdiction can take cognizance of the specified economic offences as if the limitation provisions of Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, were not enacted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts having jurisdiction as per the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By allowing courts to take cognizance of scheduled economic offences without being bound by the limitation periods stipulated in Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

rights: The right for courts to take cognizance of specified economic offences without limitation periods.

key_procedures: The procedure for taking cognizance of offences specified in Section 2 of this Act will not be subject to the time limits prescribed in Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
administration: This Act primarily modifies the procedural aspect of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, concerning limitation periods. The administration of the underlying economic offences falls under the respective Acts listed in the Schedule.
important_notes: The Schedule lists various economic and financial acts, indicating the types of offences this Act is concerned with.
The Act was amended in 1984, 1974, 1980, 1987, 1994, and 1981, indicating the addition of new enactments to the Schedule over time.

title: THE OIL INDUSTRY (DEVELOPMENT) ACT, 1974
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Board for the development of the oil industry and for that purpose to levy a duty of excise on crude oil and natural gas and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to any company, corporation, or co-operative society engaged in activities related to the oil industry, including prospecting, exploration, production, refining, processing, transportation, storage, handling, marketing of mineral oil and its products, and the production of fertilizers and petro-chemicals.

key_definitions.board: The Oil Industry Development Board established under section 3.
key_definitions.court: The High Court or the Court of Judicial Commissioner within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the defendant or respondent carries on business, or any empowered civil court.
key_definitions.crude_oil: Petroleum in its natural state before refinement, with water and foreign substances extracted.
key_definitions.fertilisers: Oil-based chemical compounds used in agriculture that provide nitrogen, phosphorus, and potash.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board, including the Chairman.
key_definitions.natural_gas: Gas primarily consisting of hydrocarbons from oil or gas wells.
key_definitions.oil_industrial_concern: A company, corporation, or co-operative society engaged in oil industry activities.
key_definitions.oil_industry: Includes prospecting, exploration, production of mineral oil, refining, processing, transportation, storage, handling, marketing, production of all downstream products, fertilizers, petro-chemicals, and directly or indirectly connected activities.
key_definitions.petro_chemicals: Organic or inorganic chemicals derived from petroleum and natural gas.
key_definitions.petroleum_product: Any commodity made from petroleum or natural gas, including refined crude oil, processed crude petroleum, various fuel oils, gasoline, kerosene, bitumen, asphalt, tar, lubricating oil, and mixtures.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial applicability.
Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and constitution of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the establishment, corporate status, and composition of the Oil Industry Development Board, including appointment of members by the Central Government.

Outlines the primary functions of the Board, which include rendering financial and other assistance for the development of the oil industry, specifying various forms of assistance like grants, loans, guarantees, and underwriting.

Specifies the principles and conditions that the Board must adhere to before and during the rendering of assistance, including alignment with Central Government directions and prioritizing development interests.
Mentions the imposition of duties of excise, though the specifics are not detailed in the provided text.
Refers to the establishment and management of an Oil Industry Development Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require persons engaged in oil industry to maintain and produce books, accounts and records relating to business and inspection thereof
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to require oil industry personnel to maintain and produce business records and allows for inspection of these records.
Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the Board or entities in the oil industry.
Details the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
States that this Act shall have an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict.
Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Board shall render financial and other assistance for measures conducive to the development of the oil industry.
Rule 2: Assistance can be provided through grants, loans, guarantees for loans or deferred payments, underwriting issues, and subscriptions to stocks/shares/debentures of oil industrial concerns.
Rule 3: Before rendering assistance, the Board must ensure it aligns with Central Government directions and is a priority for oil industry development.
Rule 4: The Central Government has the power to require oil industry entities to maintain and produce business records for inspection.
Rule 5: The Central Government can issue directions to the Board or any person engaged in the oil industry.
Rule 6: The Act has an overriding effect on other laws.

penalties: Section 23 outlines penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions. Section 24 mentions 'other penalties', implying further penal provisions not detailed in the excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, and by implication, the Oil Industry Development Board established under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of penalties, powers of inspection of records, and by the Board's functions of providing assistance and overseeing development. The Central Government's power to issue directions also plays a role in enforcement.

rights: Right to establish the Oil Industry Development Board.
Right to levy a duty of excise on crude oil and natural gas.
Right of the Board to provide various forms of financial and other assistance.
Right of the Central Government to issue directions and require record production.
Right to protection of action taken in good faith (Section 28).
duties: Duty of the Board to promote the development of the oil industry.
Duty of persons engaged in the oil industry to maintain and produce records when required.
Duty to comply with directions issued by the Central Government.
Duty to adhere to the principles and conditions for receiving assistance.
obligations: Obligation to pay duties of excise (implied by section 15).
Obligation to comply with prescribed rules and conditions set by the Board and the Central Government.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Oil Industry Development Board by notification of the Central Government.
Appointment of Board members and Chairman by the Central Government.
Application for and rendering of assistance by the Board to oil industrial concerns, subject to prescribed conditions and Central Government directions.
Inspection of books, accounts, and records by the Central Government.
Making of rules by the Central Government for carrying out the Act's provisions.
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative body, responsible for establishing the Board, appointing its members, issuing directions, and making rules. The Oil Industry Development Board is responsible for executing the Act's provisions related to development and assistance.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on other laws (Section 30).
A specific section (22A) has been omitted.
The Act makes provisions for the dissolution of the Board (Section 29).

title: The Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974
purpose: To provide for preventive detention in certain cases for the purposes of conservation and augmentation of Foreign Exchange and prevention of smuggling activities.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It addresses activities prejudicial to the conservation or augmentation of foreign exchange, and smuggling of goods, abetting smuggling, transporting or concealing smuggled goods, dealing in smuggled goods, and harbouring persons engaged in smuggling.

key_definitions.appropriate government: As respects a detention order made by the Central Government or its officer, it's the Central Government. As respects a detention order made by a State Government or its officer, it's the State Government.
key_definitions.detention order: An order made under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.foreigner: Has the same meaning as in the Foreigners Act, 1946.
key_definitions.indian customs waters: Has the same meaning as in clause (28) of section 2 of the Customs Act, 1962.
key_definitions.smuggling: Has the same meaning as in clause (39) of section 2 of the Customs Act, 1962, with all its grammatical variations and cognate expressions construed accordingly.
key_definitions.state government: In relation to a Union territory, means the administrator thereof.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appropriate Government', 'detention order', 'foreigner', 'Indian customs waters', 'smuggling', and 'State Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons.
main_sections.description: Grants the power to the Central Government, State Government, or specially empowered officers to make detention orders if satisfied that detention is necessary to prevent a person from acting in a manner prejudicial to the conservation or augmentation of foreign exchange, or from engaging in smuggling activities or related offenses.
Specifies that a detention order can be executed anywhere in India in the manner provided for the execution of arrest warrants under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate place and conditions of detention.
main_sections.description: Lays down that a person in respect of whom a detention order has been made can be detained in a specified place under specified conditions and can be moved from one place of detention to another.

States that if a detention order is made on multiple grounds, it shall not be invalid if one or some of the grounds are found to be vague, non-existent, irrelevant, or otherwise invalid, provided the order could have been made based on the remaining valid grounds.

main_sections.section_title: Detention orders not to be invalid or inoperative on certain grounds.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that a detention order will not be invalid or inoperative simply because the person to be detained or the place of detention is outside the territorial jurisdiction of the issuing authority.

main_sections.section_title: Powers in relation to absconding persons.
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the appropriate government regarding persons against whom a detention order has been made who have absconded or are concealing themselves, including reporting to a Magistrate and directing appearance, with penalties for non-compliance.

Outlines the constitution and functions of Advisory Boards, including the process of referring cases for their opinion on the sufficiency of cause for detention, and the powers of the government based on the Board's report.

main_sections.section_title: Cases in which and circumstances under which persons may be detained for periods longer than three months without obtaining the opinion of Advisory Board.
main_sections.description: Provides for exceptions to the requirement of obtaining the Advisory Board's opinion for detention periods exceeding three months but not exceeding six months, under specific conditions related to smuggling in vulnerable areas.
Specifies the maximum period for which a person can be detained under this Act.
Empowers the appropriate government to revoke a detention order.
