Allows for the temporary release of persons detained under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous laws.

important_rules: Rule 1: A detention order can be made if the appropriate government is satisfied that it's necessary to prevent a person from acting prejudicially to the conservation or augmentation of foreign exchange, or from engaging in or abetting smuggling of goods, or dealing with smuggled goods.

Rule 2: Grounds for detention must be communicated to the detenu as soon as may be, ordinarily not later than five days, and in exceptional circumstances, not later than fifteen days from the date of detention.
Rule 3: A person detained under this Act cannot be represented by a legal practitioner before the Advisory Board.

Rule 4: If the Advisory Board reports sufficient cause for detention, the government may confirm the detention. If it reports insufficient cause, the government shall revoke the detention order and release the person.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine or with both for failure to comply with directions to appear before an officer as per section 7(1)(b).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and State Governments, and their specially empowered officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance and execution of detention orders, regulation of detention conditions, powers related to absconding persons, and referral to Advisory Boards. Offences under section 7(1)(b) are cognizable.

rights: Right to be informed of the grounds of detention (as per Article 22 of the Constitution).
Right to appeal to the Advisory Board (indirectly, by providing materials and potentially being heard).
Right to temporary release.
Right to be released if the Advisory Board reports insufficient cause for detention.
duties: Duty of the appropriate government to communicate grounds of detention.
Duty of the appropriate government to make references to the Advisory Board within five weeks (unless extended by section 9).
Duty of the Advisory Board to submit its report within eleven weeks.
Duty of the appropriate government to revoke the detention order if the Advisory Board finds no sufficient cause.
Duty of the detenu to comply with directions to appear if absconding, unless it's impossible and the reason is communicated.
obligations: Obligation on the Central Government to receive reports from State Governments within ten days for detention orders made by them.
Obligation on a State Government not to move a person to another State without the consent of that other State's government.

key_procedures: Making a detention order by the Central/State Government or empowered officer if satisfied about preventive necessity.
Communicating the grounds of detention to the detenu within a specified period.
Forwarding reports to the Central Government by State Governments within ten days of making a detention order.
Making a reference to the Advisory Board within five weeks of detention (unless section 9 applies).
Advisory Board considering materials, possibly calling for further information, and hearing the person, then submitting a report within eleven weeks.
Government acting on the Advisory Board's report – confirming detention or revoking the order and releasing the person.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments, with specific roles for their empowered officers and the Administrator for Union Territories.
important_notes: A proviso to Section 3(1) states that no order of detention shall be made on grounds for which an order could be made under the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1988.

Section 9 allows for detention periods longer than three months (up to six months) without the Advisory Board's opinion under specific circumstances related to smuggling in areas highly vulnerable to smuggling, subject to a Central Government declaration.

title: THE EAST PUNJAB URBAN RENT RESTRICTION ACT (EXTENSION TO CHANDIGARH) ACT, 1974
purpose: To extend the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, to the Union territory of Chandigarh.
scope: The Act applies to all urban areas in the Union territory of Chandigarh. It extends the provisions of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, to this territory.

key_definitions.the Act: The East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949 (East Punjab Act III of 1949) as it extended to, and was in force in, certain areas in the pre-reorganisation State of Punjab immediately before the 1st day of November, 1966.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.urban area: The area comprised in Chandigarh as defined in clause (d) of section 2 of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952 (Punjab Act XXVII of 1952) and includes such other area comprised in the Union territory of Chandigarh as the Central Government may, by notification, declare to be urban for the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act (Extension to Chandigarh) Act, 1974.

Defines 'the Act' as the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, and clarifies its scope prior to reorganisation of Punjab. It also defines 'notification' and 'urban area' with specific reference to Chandigarh.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of East Punjab Act III of 1949 to Chandigarh
main_sections.description: Extends the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, to the Union territory of Chandigarh, subject to modifications specified in the Schedule. It is deemed to have been in force from November 4, 1972, and overrides any conflicting court judgments.

(1) Validates and confirms anything done or action taken under the Act as if the provisions of this Act had been in force at all material times. (2) States that this Act does not render any person guilty of any offense for contraventions that occurred before the commencement of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Throughout the Act, 'State Government' is to be substituted with 'Central Government'.
Rule 2: The Act extends to all urban areas in the Union territory of Chandigarh.
Rule 3: The definition of 'urban area' is clarified for Chandigarh, allowing the Central Government to declare other areas as urban by notification.
Rule 4: The Central Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act by notification, and these rules are subject to parliamentary approval.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (as the State Government is substituted with Central Government for the purpose of the Act and making rules).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Central Government under Section 20 and through the provisions of the extended East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949.

rights: Right to have rent controlled under the provisions of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, in Chandigarh.
Protection from certain offenses that occurred before the commencement of this Act.
duties: To comply with rules made by the Central Government.
To adhere to the provisions of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, as extended to Chandigarh.

key_procedures: Procedure for declaring areas as 'urban areas': The Central Government may declare any area in the Union territory of Chandigarh as an 'urban area' by notification, considering population density, accommodation availability, and other relevant factors.

Procedure for making rules: The Central Government may make rules by notification for the purpose of carrying out the Act's provisions. These rules are subject to a 30-day review period by both Houses of Parliament.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The extension of the Act to Chandigarh is effective from November 4, 1972.
Any action taken or thing done under the Act before its enactment is deemed valid and effective.
No person shall be held guilty of an offense for contraventions that occurred before the commencement of this Act.

title: THE TOKYO CONVENTION ACT, 1975
purpose: To give effect to the Convention on offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It covers offences and other acts committed on board aircraft, including both Indian registered and other aircraft when in flight.

key_definitions.aircraft: Any aircraft, whether or not registered in India, excluding military aircraft or aircraft belonging to or exclusively employed in the service of the State.
key_definitions.appropriate_authority: In relation to India, a police officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector or an Immigration Officer. In relation to other Convention countries, an officer with corresponding functions.
key_definitions.commander: The crew member designated as commander by the operator, or the pilot in command.
key_definitions.convention_country: A country where the Tokyo Convention is in force.
key_definitions.indian_registered_aircraft: An aircraft registered in India, or an unregistered aircraft where the operator or owner meets specific India-based requirements, or an aircraft registered elsewhere but chartered to a person meeting those India-based requirements.
key_definitions.military_aircraft: An aircraft of the naval, military, or air force of any country, including those commanded by a person in such service.
key_definitions.operator: The person managing the aircraft at any given time.
key_definitions.pilot_in_command: The person in charge of piloting the aircraft, responsible for its operation and safety during flight time.
key_definitions.tokyo_convention: The Convention on offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft signed at Tokyo on September 14, 1963.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its extent to the whole of India, and outlines the process for its commencement through a Central Government notification.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'aircraft', 'appropriate authority', 'commander', 'Convention country', 'Indian registered aircraft', 'military aircraft', 'operator', 'pilot in command', and 'Tokyo Convention'. It also clarifies the period during which an aircraft is considered 'in flight'.

main_sections.section_title: Application of criminal law to aircraft
main_sections.description: States that acts or omissions on board an Indian registered aircraft in flight outside India, which would be an offence in India, constitute that offence. It includes a proviso for acts authorized by foreign law and requires Central Government consent for instituting proceedings for certain offences.
Deems any aircraft registered in a Convention country, while in flight, to be within the jurisdiction of that country for the purpose of the Extradition Act, 1962.

Outlines the powers of an aircraft commander to take measures, including restraint, against persons on board if they jeopardize safety, good order, or commit an offence under the law of the country of registration. It details conditions for continuing restraint, disembarkation, delivery to authorities, and reporting requirements.

Declares that courts in India have jurisdiction over offences committed on board aircraft, similar to jurisdiction over piracy on the high seas. It also deems offences committed on an aircraft in flight to have been committed in any place in India where the offender is present.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions as to evidence in connection with aircraft
main_sections.description: Provides for the admissibility of depositions made on oath outside India in proceedings before Indian courts, under certain conditions regarding the presence of the accused and authentication. It also allows consular officers to inquire into offences committed on Indian registered aircraft.

Details the admissibility of certain documentary evidence published by the Central Government's Ministry of Civil Aviation, such as the 'Aeronautical Information Publication', 'Notam', and 'Aeronautical Information Circular'.

important_rules: Any act or omission on board an Indian registered aircraft in flight outside India that would be an offence in India, shall constitute that offence, unless expressly or impliedly authorized by foreign law.
Proceedings for certain offences committed on aircraft in flight outside India cannot be instituted without the Central Government's consent.

An aircraft commander can take reasonable measures, including restraint, against a person on board if their actions jeopardize safety, good order, or constitute an offence under the law of the aircraft's country of registration.

Restraint of a person on board an aircraft cannot continue after the aircraft ceases to be in flight unless notification is sent to the appropriate authority of the country where it lands, or the person agrees to continue under restraint.

The commander may disembark a person in any country if necessary for safety, good order, or discipline, or deliver the person to the appropriate authority if an offence under the country of registration law has been committed.
The commander must report disembarkation or delivery of a person to the relevant authorities and diplomatic/consular officers.

penalties: A commander who fails without reasonable cause to comply with reporting requirements under section 5(6) is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding one thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, appropriate authorities (police officers, immigration officers), and consular officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, powers of arrest, rendition, and judicial jurisdiction. The commander's powers to restrain, disembark, and deliver individuals also form a part of enforcement.

rights: Right of the commander to take measures to ensure safety and maintain order.
Right of passengers and crew members to take reasonable preventive measures in emergencies.
Right of accused persons to be remanded in custody or on bail.
Right to have depositions admissible as evidence under specific conditions.
Right to be informed of the reasons for restraint or disembarkation.
duties: Duty of the commander to report disembarkation or delivery of persons.
Duty of the commander to notify authorities and diplomatic/consular officers.
Duty of the Central Government to appoint commencement date and potentially consent to proceedings.
Duty of appropriate authorities to receive reports and take over responsibility for persons and property.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the Convention on offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft.
Obligation for any person on board to refrain from acts that jeopardize safety or good order.
Obligation to comply with measures taken by the commander for safety and discipline.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Central Government notifies the date of commencement in the Official Gazette.

Definition of 'in flight': Includes the period from engine power application for takeoff until landing run completion, and specific additional periods in case of door closure for embarkation/disembarkation or forced landings.
Commander's actions: If reasonable grounds exist for belief of jeopardizing safety, order, or commission of an offence, the commander can take measures, including restraint.

Disembarkation/Delivery: The commander can disembark a person in any country for safety/order or deliver them to the appropriate authority if an offence under the country of registration law is believed to have occurred.
Reporting: The commander must report disembarkation or delivery to relevant authorities and diplomatic/consular officers.

Evidence admissibility: Deposition made on oath outside India can be admissible if certain conditions are met, including the accused's presence and authentication by a judge, magistrate, or consular officer.
administration: The Central Government (specifically, the Ministry dealing with Civil Aviation for documentary evidence).
important_notes: The definition of 'aircraft' excludes military and state-service aircraft.
The definition of 'in flight' is expanded to cover periods on the ground before takeoff and after landing, as well as during forced landings.

Section 3(2) requires consent of the Central Government for instituting proceedings for offences committed on aircraft in flight elsewhere than in or over India, except for offences under the Aircraft Act, 1934.
The Extradition Act, 1962, is applied to crimes on aircraft, deeming Convention country registered aircraft in flight to be within that country's jurisdiction.
The powers of the commander are subject to conditions and reporting requirements to prevent abuse.

title: THE ELECTION LAWS (EXTENSION TO SIKKIM) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the extension of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to the State of Sikkim.
scope: This act applies to the State of Sikkim. It extends the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951 to Sikkim, and makes specific amendments to these acts as they pertain to Sikkim.

key_definitions.assembly constituency: A constituency for direct election to the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim.
key_definitions.Sangha constituency: A specific constituency in Sikkim for Sanghas belonging to recognized monasteries.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the 'Election Laws (Extension to Sikkim) Act, 1976' and states that it is deemed to have come into force on September 9, 1975.

main_sections.section_title: Extension and amendment of election laws
main_sections.description: Extends the Acts mentioned in the Schedule to Sikkim and makes amendments to these Acts as specified in the Schedule. It also provides for construing references in the extended Acts to laws or functionaries not in existence in Sikkim.
Repeals the Election Laws (Extension to Sikkim) Ordinance, 1975, but saves any actions taken under that ordinance, deeming them to have been done under this Act.

important_rules: Rule for Sikkim Legislative Assembly Seats: The total number of seats to be filled by direct election in the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim is 32, with each constituency being single-member. The extent of each constituency and reservation of seats are as provided immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975.

Rule for Sangha Constituency Registration: Only Sanghas belonging to monasteries recognized for the purpose of the April 1974 elections in Sikkim are entitled to be registered in the electoral roll for the Sangha constituency. The electoral roll is to be prepared or revised as directed by the Election Commission in consultation with the Government of Sikkim.

Qualifications for Sikkim Legislative Assembly Membership: Specific qualifications are outlined for membership of the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim, including requirements for seats reserved for Sikkimese of Bhutia-Lepcha origin, Sikkimese of Nepali origin, Scheduled Castes, and Sanghas, linked to being an elector in the state.

Nomination Paper Requirements for Sikkim Legislative Assembly Elections: For elections to the Sikkim Legislative Assembly, nomination papers must be subscribed by the candidate and, for seats reserved for Sikkimese of Bhutia-Lepcha origin and Sanghas, must be proposed and seconded by at least twenty electors. For seats reserved for Sikkimese of Nepali origin, it needs one proposer. Nomination papers cannot be delivered on a public holiday.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government has the authority to decide on corresponding functionaries in Sikkim if questions arise regarding their existence or identity.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the extension and amendment of existing election laws, and specific provisions for Sikkim's electoral process.

rights: Right to be registered as an elector for the Sangha constituency if a Sangha belonging to a recognized monastery.
Right to be a candidate for reserved seats in the Sikkim Legislative Assembly if fulfilling the specific origin and elector requirements.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the extended Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951, within Sikkim.
Obligation for candidates to meet specific nomination and qualification criteria for Sikkim Legislative Assembly seats.

key_procedures: Procedure for preparing/revising the Sangha constituency electoral roll: To be directed by the Election Commission in consultation with the Government of Sikkim.

Procedure for filling the seat allotted to Sikkim in the Council of States: The President will issue a notification, on the Election Commission's recommendation, calling upon the elected members of the Sikkim Legislative Assembly to elect a member.

Procedure for electing Sikkim's representative to the House of the People: The Election Commission will call upon the members of the Sikkim Legislative Assembly to elect the representative, following applicable provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

Procedure for nomination to the Sikkim Legislative Assembly: Nomination papers must be in the prescribed form and manner, subscribed by the candidate and supported by proposers and seconders as per the seat reservation.
administration: The Central Government is involved in deciding on functionaries. The Election Commission plays a significant role in directing electoral processes and issuing notifications for elections.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively on September 9, 1975.

References in the extended Acts to laws or functionaries not in force or existence in Sikkim shall be construed as references to corresponding ones, with the Central Government having the final decision if there's ambiguity.
The provisions for the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim are made with reference to its constitution under the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975.

title: THE HIGH COURT AT PATNA (ESTABLISHMENT OF A PERMANENT BENCH AT RANCHI) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a permanent bench of the High Court at Patna at Ranchi.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment of a permanent bench of the High Court at Patna at Ranchi. The jurisdiction of this bench covers cases arising in the districts of Hazaribagh, Giridih, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Palamau, and Singhbhum. However, the Chief Justice has the discretion to order that any case or class of cases arising in these districts be heard at Patna.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the High Court at Patna (Establishment of a Permanent Bench at Ranchi) Act, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of a permanent bench of High Court at Patna at Ranchi
main_sections.description: This section provides for the establishment of a permanent bench of the High Court at Patna at Ranchi. It stipulates that at least three judges nominated by the Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna shall sit at Ranchi to exercise the jurisdiction and power vested in the High Court concerning cases originating from Hazaribagh, Giridih, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Palamau, and Singhbhum districts. A proviso allows the Chief Justice to order the hearing of any case or class of cases from these districts at Patna.

important_rules: At least three judges nominated by the Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna shall sit at Ranchi to exercise jurisdiction for cases arising in specific districts.
The Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna can, at his discretion, order any case or class of cases arising in the designated districts to be heard at Patna.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By nominating judges to sit at the Ranchi bench and by exercising discretion in ordering where cases are heard.

rights: Right to have cases arising in Hazaribagh, Giridih, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Palamau, and Singhbhum districts heard at the permanent bench in Ranchi.
duties: The Chief Justice has the duty to establish and oversee the functioning of the permanent bench at Ranchi.
Nominated judges have a duty to sit at Ranchi and exercise jurisdiction for specified cases.
obligations: The obligation to provide for the establishment of a permanent bench of the High Court at Patna at Ranchi.

key_procedures: Nomination of judges: The Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna nominates not less than three judges to sit at Ranchi.
Jurisdiction exercise: Nominated judges exercise the jurisdiction and power of the High Court at Patna for cases arising in the specified districts.
Discretionary hearing at Patna: The Chief Justice may, at his discretion, order cases or classes of cases from these districts to be heard at Patna.
administration: High Court at Patna
important_notes: The Act establishes a permanent bench, implying ongoing operation.
The Chief Justice retains significant discretionary power regarding case assignment.

title: The Departmentalisation of Union Accounts (Transfer of Personnel) Act, 1976
purpose: To provide for the transfer of officers serving in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department to any Ministry, Department or office of the Central Government for facilitating the efficient discharge by such Ministry, Department or office of the responsibility in connection with compiling the accounts thereof.
scope: Applies to officers and employees serving in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, and their transfer to any Ministry, Department or office of the Central Government. Geographically, it applies to the Union Government of India.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on March 1, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of officers and employees of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department
main_sections.description: Details the process and conditions for transferring officers and employees from the Indian Audit and Accounts Department to other Central Government ministries or departments. It outlines the role of the President, the Central Government's power to transfer, the establishment of Advisory Committees, and the terms of service for transferred personnel, including pay and designation.

Repeals the Departmentalisation of Union Accounts (Transfer of Personnel) Ordinance, 1976, and states that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Officers and employees of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department can be transferred to other Central Government ministries/departments if the President has relieved the Comptroller and Auditor-General from compiling certain accounts.
Transfers are subject to the advice of an Advisory Committee established by the Central Government.

Transferred officers and employees will cease to be part of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and will hold office in their new ministry/department with a designation specified by the Central Government.
Transferred personnel are entitled to a post with a pay scale not less favorable than their previous post.
If an officer/employee was officiating in a higher post, their pay will be protected for the unexpired period of the vacancy upon transfer.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the Central Government, possibly advised by Advisory Committees.

rights: Right to be appointed to a post with a pay scale not less favorable than the post held before transfer.
Protection of pay for the unexpired period of a higher officiating vacancy upon transfer.
Right to resign or retire from service in accordance with applicable rules.
duties: To serve in the new ministry or department to which they are transferred.
To facilitate the efficient discharge of responsibilities by the new ministry, department, or office in compiling accounts.
obligations: An officer or employee transferred must accept the new posting and designation.
An officer or employee can be transferred even if they have expressed unwillingness, if the Central Government deems it necessary in the public interest.

key_procedures: 1. President issues an order relieving the Comptroller and Auditor-General from compiling specified accounts.
2. Central Government establishes an Advisory Committee.
3. Advisory Committee advises the Central Government on transfers.
4. Central Government issues an order to transfer officers/employees from the Indian Audit and Accounts Department to other ministries/departments, specifying dates and designations.
5. Transferred personnel cease to be part of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and assume duties in their new roles, subject to pay and service conditions.
administration: Central Government (specifically regarding orders for transfer and establishment of Advisory Committees). The Act facilitates the departmentalization of Union Accounts, implying various ministries/departments will be involved in managing these accounts post-transfer.
important_notes: An officer or employee can be transferred even if they express unwillingness, provided the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary in the public interest.
The Act does not affect the right of an officer or employee to resign or retire from service according to applicable rules.

title: The Betwa River Board Act, 1976
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Board for the creation of a reservoir at Rajghat by construction of a dam on the Betwa river at Rajghat, and for the regulation of such reservoir, on behalf of the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
scope: Applies to the inter-State Betwa River and River Valley, specifically concerning the regulation and development of the Rajghat Dam and the Rani Laxmibai Sagar reservoir. It involves the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

key_definitions.Board: The Betwa River Board established under section 4.
key_definitions.Executive Committee: The Executive Committee constituted under section 5.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board and includes the Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made by the Central Government under section 22.
key_definitions.Rajghat Dam: The Dam described in the Schedule.
key_definitions.Rani Laxmibai Sagar: The reservoir created by the construction of the Rajghat Dam.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Board under section 23.
key_definitions.rules: Rules made by the Central Government under section 22.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Betwa River Board Act, 1976' and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government in consultation with the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Central Government to control the regulation and development of the inter-State Betwa River and River Valley to the extent provided in the Act.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairman', 'Executive Committee', 'member', 'prescribed', 'Rajghat Dam', 'Rani Laxmibai Sagar', 'regulations', and 'rules'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the Betwa River Board
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Betwa River Board with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract. It also specifies the composition of the Board, with the Union Minister in charge of Irrigation as Chairman, Chief Ministers of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, and their respective Ministers for Finance, Irrigation, and Power.

Allows for the constitution of an Executive Committee by the Central Government, responsible for the management of the Board's affairs, subject to the Board's superintendence and control. It specifies that an officer of the Central Government shall be the Chairman and that Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh shall have equal representation.

Outlines the functions of the Board, including carrying out surveys and investigations, preparing project reports for the Rajghat Dam and power generation, finalizing reports after consulting State Governments, preparing detailed reports and estimates, allocating costs, drawing up standards and specifications, constructing the dam and power house, laying down operation and management rules, and performing any supplemental, incidental, or consequential functions.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions subject to which the Board may exercise its functions
main_sections.description: Specifies conditions for the Board's functions, including that State Governments must provide money, land, and power, that expenditure on the dam and power house shall be shared by the State Governments in proportions determined by the Board, and that State Governments must cooperate and make land and power available expeditiously. It also addresses expenditure incurred by Uttar Pradesh before the Board's establishment.

Establishes the Betwa River Board Fund, into which sums paid by State Governments and other received sums will be credited. The fund is to be applied for salaries, administrative expenses, surveys and investigations, construction costs of the dam and power house, and other expenses related to the Board's functions.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Board's functions are subject to the condition that the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh make suitable provisions for moneys, land facilities, and electrical power for construction and other requirements.

Rule 2: The liability for the entire expenditure on the Rajghat Dam, Rajghat Power House, and associated works, including power generation, shall be shared by the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh in proportions specified by the Board, which may vary based on benefits and other factors.

Rule 3: The Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh shall extend full cooperation to the Board and make available required land and electric power for construction purposes as expeditiously as possible.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, the Betwa River Board, and potentially the State Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh through their cooperation and provision of resources.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the Board's powers, directions from the Central Government, and the cooperation and resource provision by the State Governments.

rights: Right to be represented in Board meetings for associated persons (without voting rights).
Right of associated persons to take part in discussions relevant to their association.
Right of the Board to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right of the Board to sue and be sued.
Right of the Board to require information from State Governments.
Right of the Chief Engineer to exercise powers and duties as prescribed or delegated.
Right of the Financial Adviser to act as the Chief Accounts Officer.
duties: Duty of the Board to carry out surveys, investigations, and project reports.
Duty of the Board to prepare detailed reports and estimates and allocate costs.
Duty of the Board to draw up standards and specifications.
Duty of the Board to construct the Rajghat Dam and Power House.
Duty of the Board to lay down rules of operation and management.
Duty of State Governments to provide necessary resources (money, land, power) to the Board.
Duty of State Governments to cooperate with the Board.
Duty of the Board to apply its Fund for specified purposes.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to appoint the Chief Engineer, Financial Adviser, and Secretary.
Obligation of the Board to utilize services of officers and employees from Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh with equal representation.
Obligation to adhere to rules and regulations made under the Act.
Obligation to ensure that the expenditure on the dam and power house is shared by the State Governments.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Appointment of the Betwa River Board by the Central Government through notification.
Procedure 2: Constitution of an Executive Committee by the Central Government through notification.
Procedure 3: Preparation of the Board's budget and annual report.
Procedure 4: Auditing of the Board's accounts.
Procedure 5: Making of rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Board, which are then laid before Parliament.
administration: The Central Government, in conjunction with the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, and the Betwa River Board itself.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act allows for the Central Government to appoint representatives for a State if a proclamation under Article 356 of the Constitution is in force in that State.
Note 2: The Board can permit officers of the Central or State Governments to attend meetings and participate in proceedings but without voting rights.
Note 3: The Board can associate individuals for assistance or advice, granting them participation in discussions relevant to their association but without voting rights.
Note 4: Acts or proceedings of the Board or Executive Committee are not invalidated by vacancies, defects in composition, or procedural irregularities that do not affect the merits of the case.

title: THE LIFE INSURANCE CORPORATION (MODIFICATION OF SETTLEMENTS) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the modification of the settlements arrived at between the Life Insurance Corporation of India and their workmen.
scope: This Act applies to the Life Insurance Corporation of India and its workmen, specifically concerning settlements related to payment of annual cash bonus.

key_definitions.Corporation: The Life Insurance Corporation of India established under section 3 of the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 (31 of 1956).
key_definitions.salary: Basic pay and includes special pay, dearness allowance, and additional dearness allowance.
key_definitions.settlements: Refers to two specific settlements: (i) arrived at between the Corporation and their workmen on January 24, 1974, under section 18 read with clause (p) of section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947; and (ii) arrived at between the Corporation and their workmen on February 6, 1974, under section 18 read with clause (p) of the said Act, in respect of terms for which there was no approval as provided in sub-clause (2) of clause 12 thereof.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Life Insurance Corporation (Modification of Settlements) Act, 1976.
Provides definitions for 'Corporation', 'salary', and 'settlements' as used in the Act.

Modifies the settlements by stating that their provisions relating to the payment of an annual cash bonus to every Class III and Class IV employee of the Corporation at the rate of fifteen per cent. of their annual salary shall have no force or effect from April 1, 1975.

important_rules: Rule 1: The provisions of the settlements, specifically those relating to the payment of an annual cash bonus to every Class III and Class IV employee of the Corporation at the rate of fifteen percent of their annual salary, shall have no force or effect and shall be deemed to have had no force or effect from April 1, 1975.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the Life Insurance Corporation of India and potentially labor authorities under the Industrial Disputes Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By nullifying the force and effect of specific settlement provisions regarding annual cash bonus payments.

rights: Employees have a right to receive salary (basic pay including special pay, dearness allowance, and additional dearness allowance).
duties: The Corporation has a duty to adhere to the modifications of settlements as stipulated by this Act.
obligations: The Corporation is obligated to cease the payment of annual cash bonus at the rate of fifteen percent of annual salary to Class III and Class IV employees from April 1, 1975, as per the modification of settlements.

administration: The Life Insurance Corporation of India is the entity whose settlements are being modified. The administration of the Act itself is overseen by the Parliament that enacted it and likely the Ministry of Labour.
important_notes: This Act overrides anything contained in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, concerning the specific settlements being modified.
The modification of the settlement regarding the annual cash bonus is effective from April 1, 1975.

title: The Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976
purpose: To provide for certain matters relating to the territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and other maritime zones of India.
scope: The Act applies to the territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and other maritime zones of India. It defines India's sovereignty, rights, and jurisdiction within these zones. It also addresses the passage of foreign ships and aircraft, and the exploration and exploitation of resources within these maritime areas.

key_definitions.limit: In relation to the territorial waters, the continental shelf, the exclusive economic zone or any other maritime zone of India, means the limit of such waters, shelf or zone with reference to the mainland of India as well as the individual or composite group or groups of islands constituting part of the territory of India.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date. Sections 5 and 7 come into force on dates appointed by the Central Government, while other provisions come into force immediately.
Defines the term 'limit' in relation to India's maritime zones.

main_sections.section_title: Sovereignty over, and limits of, territorial waters
main_sections.description: Asserts India's sovereignty over its territorial waters, including the seabed, subsoil, and air space. It defines the limit of territorial waters as twelve nautical miles from the nearest point of the baseline and allows for alteration of this limit by the Central Government with parliamentary approval.

main_sections.section_title: Use of territorial waters by foreign ships
main_sections.description: Grants foreign ships (excluding warships) the right of innocent passage through territorial waters. Foreign warships require prior notice. The Central Government can suspend entry of foreign ships in certain areas for security reasons.

Defines the contiguous zone as an area beyond and adjacent to territorial waters, extending up to twenty-four nautical miles from the baseline. The Central Government can exercise powers related to security, immigration, sanitation, customs, and fiscal matters within this zone and can extend Indian enactments to it.

Defines the continental shelf as the seabed and subsoil extending beyond territorial waters. India has full sovereign rights over its continental shelf for exploration, exploitation, conservation, and management of resources, and for construction of installations. Foreign exploration or exploitation requires a license from the Central Government. Designated areas within the continental shelf can be established for specific purposes, and Indian laws can be extended to it. The Central Government may not impede laying of submarine cables or pipelines with its consent.

Defines the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) as an area beyond and adjacent to territorial waters, extending up to two hundred nautical miles from the baseline. India has sovereign rights for exploration, exploitation, conservation, and management of natural resources, and for energy production from tides, winds, and currents. It also has exclusive rights for artificial islands, installations, and jurisdiction over scientific research and marine environment protection. Foreign activities require agreement or license. Freedom of navigation and overflight is granted to ships and aircraft, subject to India's rights. Indian laws can be extended to the EEZ.
Empowers the Central Government to specify the limits of historic waters adjacent to its land territory. India's sovereignty extends to these historic waters.

main_sections.section_title: Maritime boundaries between India and States having coasts opposite or adjacent to those of India
main_sections.description: This section is incomplete in the provided text.

important_rules: Foreign ships (other than warships) enjoy the right of innocent passage through India's territorial waters, provided the passage is not prejudicial to the peace, good order, or security of India.

Foreign warships, submarines, and underwater vehicles may enter or pass through territorial waters only after giving prior notice to the Central Government. Submarines and underwater vehicles must navigate on the surface and show their flag.

No person or foreign government can explore the continental shelf or exploit its resources, conduct research, or construct installations without a license or letter of authority from the Central Government.

No person or foreign government can explore or exploit resources in the EEZ, conduct research, or construct installations without an agreement or license from the Central Government, except for fishing by Indian citizens.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government is the primary enforcement authority, with powers to make rules, issue notifications, grant licenses, and extend enactments to maritime zones.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the exercise of sovereign rights and jurisdiction within the maritime zones, granting licenses, extending existing Indian laws, and establishing regulations for designated areas.

rights: Sovereignty over territorial waters, seabed, subsoil, and air space.
Full and exclusive sovereign rights in respect of the continental shelf for exploration, exploitation, conservation, and management of resources.
Exclusive rights and jurisdiction for construction, maintenance, or operation of artificial islands, installations, etc., in the continental shelf and EEZ.
Exclusive jurisdiction to authorize, regulate, and control scientific research in the continental shelf and EEZ.
Exclusive jurisdiction to preserve and protect the marine environment and prevent marine pollution in the continental shelf and EEZ.
Sovereign rights for exploration, exploitation, conservation, and management of natural resources in the EEZ, including energy from tides, winds, and currents.
Freedom of navigation and overflight in the EEZ and the air space over it, subject to India's rights.
duties: Foreign ships must have innocent passage through territorial waters.
Foreign warships must give prior notice before entering territorial waters.
Submarines and underwater vehicles must navigate on the surface and show their flag.
Persons (including foreign governments) require licenses for activities in the continental shelf and EEZ.
Obtaining consent from the Central Government is necessary for delineating the course for laying submarine cables or pipelines on the continental shelf and EEZ.

key_procedures: Central Government appointing dates for commencement of specific sections (Sections 5 and 7) via notification in the Official Gazette.
Central Government altering the limit of territorial waters or contiguous zone by notification in the Official Gazette, subject to resolutions passed by both Houses of Parliament.
Central Government issuing notifications to declare areas of the continental shelf or EEZ as designated areas and make provisions for their management, safety, and protection.
Central Government extending existing Indian enactments to the continental shelf, EEZ, or contiguous zone with modifications and making provisions for their enforcement.
administration: The Central Government
important_notes: The Central Government has the power to suspend the entry of foreign ships into specified areas of territorial waters if deemed necessary for the peace, good order, or security of India.
Notifications for altering the limits of territorial waters and the contiguous zone can only be issued after resolutions approving such notifications are passed by both Houses of Parliament.
Fishing by citizens of India in the exclusive economic zone is exempt from certain licensing requirements mentioned in Section 7(5).

title: The Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977
purpose: To provide for the salary and allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament.
scope: Applies to Leaders of Opposition in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha) in India. The Act covers financial entitlements, residence, travel, medical treatment, and other amenities for these individuals.

key_definitions.Leader of the Opposition: In relation to either House of Parliament, it means that member of the Council of States or the House of the People who is, for the time being, the Leader in that House of the party in opposition to the Government having the greatest numerical strength and recognised as such by the Chairman of the Council of States or the Speaker of the House of the People. Where there are two or more parties with the same numerical strength, the Chairman or Speaker, having regard to the status of the parties, shall recognize one of the Leaders as the Leader of the Opposition, and this recognition is final and conclusive.

main_sections.description: Names the act as 'The Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977' and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines who qualifies as the 'Leader of the Opposition' in either House of Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Salary, and daily, constituency and sumptuary allowances
main_sections.description: Specifies the salary, daily, constituency, and sumptuary allowances to which a Leader of the Opposition is entitled. These are generally at the same rates as provided to Members of Parliament. The sumptuary allowance rate was updated in 2002 to match that of Cabinet Ministers.

Grants Leaders of Opposition the use of a furnished residence without rent, including maintenance, for the period they hold office and for one month thereafter. Their families are entitled to use the residence for one month after their death without rent and for a further month with rent and charges for utilities.

main_sections.section_title: Travelling and daily allowances to Leaders of Opposition
main_sections.description: Entitles Leaders of Opposition to travelling allowances for themselves and their families, including transport of effects, for journeys to Delhi to assume office and from Delhi upon relinquishing office. It also covers travelling and daily allowances for tours undertaken in discharge of their duties. The rates and number of return journeys were updated in 2002 to align with those of Ministers.

main_sections.section_title: Medical treatment, etc., to Leaders of Opposition
main_sections.description: Provides Leaders of Opposition and their families with free accommodation in Government-maintained hospitals and free medical treatment, subject to rules made by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Leaders of Opposition not to draw salary or allowances as Members of Parliament
main_sections.description: Prohibits Leaders of Opposition receiving salary or allowances under this Act from also drawing any salary or allowance for their membership of Parliament.

Entitles Leaders of Opposition to telephone and secretarial facilities, and a conveyance allowance of three thousand rupees per month. The allowance is not payable if a conveyance facility with a driver is provided for security or other purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Advance to Leader of Opposition for purchase of motor car
main_sections.description: Allows for a repayable advance to be paid to a Leader of the Opposition for the purchase of a motor car, as prescribed by rules, to facilitate the efficient discharge of their duties.

main_sections.section_title: Notification respecting the date on which persons became or ceased to be Leaders of Opposition to be conclusive evidence thereof
main_sections.description: Mandates that the date on which a person becomes or ceases to be a Leader of the Opposition, when published in the Official Gazette, serves as conclusive evidence for all purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption from liability to pay income-tax on certain perquisites received by a Leader of the Opposition
main_sections.description: Exempts the value of rent-free furnished residence (including maintenance) provided to a Leader of the Opposition under section 4 from being included in the computation of their income chargeable under the 'Salaries' heading of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, including specific provisions for rent for family use of residence, travelling and daily allowances, medical treatment, telephone, secretarial, and conveyance facilities, and advances for motor cars. Rules must be laid before Parliament for approval.
This section, related to amendments, has been repealed.
This section, related to amendments, has been repealed.

important_rules: A Leader of the Opposition is entitled to a salary and daily, constituency, and sumptuary allowances, generally at rates similar to those for Members of Parliament.
Leaders of Opposition are provided with rent-free furnished residences, including maintenance, for their official term and for a period thereafter.
Traveling and daily allowances are provided for official journeys and tours.
Free medical treatment and hospital accommodation are provided to Leaders of Opposition and their families.
Leaders of Opposition cannot draw salary or allowances as Members of Parliament while receiving benefits under this Act.
Telephone, secretarial, and conveyance facilities (or allowance) are provided.
An advance may be provided for the purchase of a motor car.
Official gazette notifications regarding a person's status as Leader of Opposition are conclusive.
Rent-free furnished accommodation is exempt from income tax.
The Central Government can make rules to carry out the Act's provisions, subject to parliamentary approval.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and Parliament (through rule-making and oversight).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act itself, implementation of rules made by the Central Government, and official gazette notifications.

rights: Right to receive salary and allowances.
Right to use a furnished residence.
Right to travelling and daily allowances for official duties and relocation.
Right to free medical treatment and hospital accommodation.
Right to telephone and secretarial facilities.
Right to a conveyance allowance or facility.
Right to a repayable advance for a motor car purchase.
duties: To discharge duties as Leader of the Opposition.
To adhere to rules made by the Central Government regarding allowances and facilities.
To repay any advance taken for a motor car purchase.
obligations: Not to draw salary/allowances as a Member of Parliament while receiving benefits under this Act.
To abide by the conditions for receiving conveyance allowance (e.g., if a driver-provided facility is given).
To comply with the terms of any advance taken for a motor car.

key_procedures: Appointment of Leader of the Opposition: The Chairman of the Council of States or Speaker of the House of the People recognizes the leader of the majority opposition party. This recognition is final.
Notification of status: Dates of becoming or ceasing to be Leader of the Opposition are published in the Official Gazette and are conclusive evidence.
Rule-making by Central Government: The Central Government makes rules for the Act's implementation, which are then presented to both Houses of Parliament for modification or annulment.
Claiming allowances and benefits: Leaders of Opposition claim entitled allowances and facilities as per the Act and rules.
administration: The Central Government, likely through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs or a similar body responsible for legislative entitlements.
important_notes: The Act was amended to update various rates and provisions, notably by Act 78 of 1985, Act 7 of 1991, and Act 56 of 2002.
Sections 11 and 12 have been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1988.

title: THE PRESS COUNCIL ACT, 1978
purpose: To establish a Press Council for the purpose of preserving the freedom of the Press and of maintaining and improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to newspapers, news agencies, editors, working journalists, and persons who own or carry on the business of management of newspapers. It also covers persons managing news agencies and individuals with special knowledge or practical experience in education, science, law, literature, and culture. Members of Parliament are also included in the Council's composition.

key_definitions.Council: The Press Council of India established under section 4.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Council and includes its Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.editor: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867.
key_definitions.newspaper: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867.
key_definitions.working journalist: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Working Journalists and other Newspaper Employees (Conditions of Service) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1955.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Press Council Act, 1978, and states that it extends to the whole of India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including Chairman, Council, member, prescribed, editor, newspaper, and working journalist.

main_sections.section_title: Rule of construction respecting enactments not extending to the State of Jammu and Kashmir or Sikkim
main_sections.description: Specifies how references to laws not in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir or Sikkim should be construed in relation to those states. This section has been amended to omit references to Jammu and Kashmir and Sikkim.
Establishes the Press Council of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to sue and be sued.

Details the composition of the Council, consisting of a Chairman and twenty-eight other members, with specific nominations from working journalists, newspaper owners/managers, news agencies, educational/scientific/legal/cultural experts, and Members of Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and retirement of members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for the Chairman and other members, conditions for ceasing to be a member (e.g., censure, ceasing to be an MP), vacation of seats, resignation, and filling of vacancies. Retiring members are eligible for re-nomination for one additional term.

Outlines the conditions of service for members, including salary for the Chairman and allowances/fees for other members. It also clarifies that holding office in the Council does not disqualify a person from being a Member of Parliament.
Empowers the Council to constitute committees for general or special purposes and allows co-option of non-members to these committees, who can participate in discussions but not vote.

main_sections.section_title: Meetings of the Council and committees
main_sections.description: States that meetings of the Council and its committees will be held at such times and places and follow such procedures as may be provided by regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies among members or defect in the constitution not to invalidate acts and proceedings of the Council
main_sections.description: Ensures that any vacancy or defect in the Council's constitution does not invalidate its acts or proceedings.

Allows the Council to appoint a Secretary and other employees as necessary for its functions, subject to rules made by the Central Government, with their terms and conditions determined by regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Authentication of orders and other instruments of the Council
main_sections.description: Specifies that orders and decisions of the Council shall be authenticated by the Chairman or an authorized member, and other instruments by the Secretary or an authorized officer.

main_sections.section_title: Objects and functions of the Council
main_sections.description: Outlines the primary objects of the Council as preserving press freedom and maintaining/improving standards of newspapers and news agencies. It also details functions like helping newspapers maintain independence, building a code of conduct, ensuring high standards of public taste, fostering responsibility, reviewing news dissemination restrictions, and studying foreign newspapers.
Grants the Council the power to censure newspapers, news agencies, or journalists.
Grants the Council general powers necessary for the discharge of its functions.
Empowers the Council to levy fees.
Deals with payments to the Council.
Establishes a fund for the Council.
Relates to the Council's budget.
Requires the Council to submit an annual report.
Allows for the submission of interim reports.
Covers the accounts and audit of the Council.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Members, etc., to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members and staff of the Council as public servants.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules.
Grants the Council the power to make regulations.
Provides for the amendment of the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867.

important_rules: Rule of construction for laws not extending to Jammu and Kashmir or Sikkim: References to laws not in force in these states are to be construed as references to corresponding laws in force there.
The Chairman shall be a whole-time officer and shall be paid a salary determined by the Central Government. Other members receive allowances/fees for attending meetings.

Members are nominated based on specific criteria: working journalists (editors and non-editors), newspaper owners/managers (categorized by size), news agency managers, and individuals with expertise in education, science, law, literature, and culture. Members of Parliament are also included.
Nominations for working journalists and newspaper owners/managers require panels of names invited from relevant associations or news agencies.
No working journalist who owns or manages a newspaper is eligible for nomination as a working journalist.
Nominations must ensure no more than one person is interested in any single newspaper or group under the same control.
The Central Government categorizes newspapers as big, medium, or small based on circulation.

penalties: Section 14 provides the power for the Council to 'censure' newspapers, news agencies, or journalists. Specific penalties are not detailed in this excerpt but would be elaborated in the full text or associated rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Press Council of India is the primary enforcement authority for its own rules and standards.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Council enforces its mandate through its powers to review, inquire, and censure. The framing of a code of conduct (Section 13(2)(b)) is a mechanism for enforcing standards. Decisions of the Council are authenticated and would have legal weight.

rights: Freedom of the Press (as an objective of the Council).
Right to maintain independence (supported by the Council).
Right to engage in journalism with a sense of responsibility and public service.
Right to receive assistance from foreign sources, subject to review.
Right to participate in discussions for co-opted members of committees (though without voting rights).
duties: To preserve the freedom of the Press.
To maintain and improve the standards of newspapers and news agencies.
To adhere to a code of conduct for newspapers, news agencies, and journalists.
To maintain high standards of public taste.
To foster a sense of responsibility and public service among journalists.
To review developments restricting news dissemination.
To keep under review assistance received from foreign sources.
To appear before the Council if summoned or required.
To fulfill obligations as public servants for members and staff of the Council.
obligations: Members of the Council have obligations related to their term of office, attendance at meetings, and adherence to Council decisions.
Newspapers and news agencies have obligations to maintain professional standards and adhere to the code of conduct.
Members and staff of the Council are considered public servants.

key_procedures: Nomination of Chairman: A committee comprising the Chairman of Rajya Sabha, Speaker of Lok Sabha, and a person elected by Council members nominates the Chairman.

Nomination of other members: Specific procedures for inviting panels of names from associations of working journalists, newspaper owners/managers, and news agencies for nomination by the Central Government or the Council.
Election of a committee member: Members of the Council elect a person from among themselves to be a member of the committee for Chairman's nomination.
Meeting procedures: The Council and its committees meet at times and places and follow rules of procedure as provided by regulations.
Authentication of Council decisions: Orders and decisions of the Council are authenticated by the Chairman or an authorized member, and other instruments by the Secretary or an authorized officer.
Filling of vacancies: Vacancies are filled by nomination in the same manner as the original member.
Submission of reports: The Council is required to submit an annual report and may submit interim reports.
administration: The Central Government plays a role in establishing the Council, making rules, and overseeing certain nominations. The Press Council of India itself administers its functions, with a Chairman and staff. Departments or agencies involved in specific nominations include the University Grants Commission, Bar Council of India, and Sahitya Academy, and the Speaker of the House of the People and Chairman of the Council of States for Parliament members.
important_notes: The Act has been amended to remove references to the State of Jammu and Kashmir and Sikkim.
A member censured under Section 14 ceases to be a member of the Council.
Members nominated from Parliament cease to be Council members upon ceasing to be members of their respective Houses.
A member vacates their seat if absent from three consecutive meetings without sufficient excuse.
Retiring members are eligible for re-nomination for only one additional term.
The provisions of Section 13(2)(f) regarding foreign assistance do not preclude the Central Government from dealing with such cases in any other manner it deems fit.

title: THE UNION DUTIES OF EXCISE (DISTRIBUTION) ACT, 1979
purpose: To provide for the payment to States of sums equivalent to a part of the net proceeds of certain Union duties of excise, and for the distribution of these sums among the States based on the recommendations of the Finance Commission.
scope: Applies to the States of India that are covered by the laws imposing Union duties of excise. The distribution of funds is specifically for financial years commencing from April 1, 1995, and the four succeeding financial years, as per the Finance Commission's report dated November 25, 1994. It specifies distribution percentages for various states under two different tables, indicating a phased approach to distribution.

key_definitions.distributable Union duties of excise: Forty-seven and a half per cent. of the net proceeds of Union duties of excise, levied and collected under the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 (1 of 1944) and any other law for the levy and collection of such duty, unless the law earmarks the proceeds for any special purpose.
key_definitions.net proceeds: Has the same meaning as in clause (1) of article 279 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1979, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1979.
Defines the term 'distributable Union duties of excise' and clarifies the meaning of 'net proceeds'.

main_sections.section_title: Payment to States of sums equivalent to a part of the net proceeds of Union duties of excise and distribution of sums among them
main_sections.description: Details the payment of sums equivalent to 'distributable Union duties of excise' to States for the financial years 1995-96 to 1999-2000. It specifies that sixteen-nineteenths of the payable sums are distributed according to Table I and three-nineteenths according to Table II, with percentages provided for each state in different financial years.

main_sections.section_title: Payment to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
main_sections.description: States that the expenditure incurred for payments under section 3 is to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, regarding the timing and manner of payments, adjustments between financial years, and other incidental matters. It also includes a provision for laying these rules before Parliament for approval or modification.
Repeals the Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1962 (3 of 1962), effective from April 1, 1979.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules for the timing and manner of payments under the Act, adjustments between financial years, and other incidental matters. These rules are subject to parliamentary scrutiny and modification.
Rule 2: Payments to States under Section 3 are to be made out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
Rule 3: The distribution of sums among States is to be in accordance with the percentages specified in Table I and Table II for the financial years 1995-96 to 1999-2000.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for making rules and facilitating payments), Parliament (for scrutinizing rules)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions outlined in the Act regarding payments, distribution, and rule-making. Payments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

rights: States have the right to receive a share of the net proceeds of Union duties of excise as per the distribution mechanism outlined in the Act.
duties: The Central Government has a duty to ensure that sums equivalent to a part of the net proceeds of Union duties of excise are paid to the States.
The Central Government has the duty to make rules for the proper implementation of the Act.
Parliament has the duty to scrutinize and approve or modify rules made by the Central Government.
obligations: The Act obligates the payment of specific percentages of distributable Union duties of excise to the States during specified financial years.

key_procedures: Payment to States: Sums equivalent to distributable Union duties of excise are paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India.

Distribution to States: These sums are distributed among States based on the percentages provided in Table I (sixteen-nineteenths) and Table II (three-nineteenths) for the financial years 1995-96 to 1999-2000.
Rule Making and Approval: The Central Government makes rules, which are then laid before Parliament for a period of thirty days for potential modification or annulment.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act was amended significantly in 1995 (Act 31 of 1995) and 1989 (Act 17 of 1989) concerning definitions and section content, indicating updates to the distribution percentages and scope.
The distribution mechanism detailed in Section 3 is specifically for the financial years 1995-96 to 1999-2000, referencing the 1994 Finance Commission report.
The repeal of the 1962 Act indicates this 1979 Act supersedes or updates the previous distribution arrangements for Union duties of excise.

title: The Essential Services Maintenance (Assam) Act, 1980
purpose: To provide for the maintenance of certain essential services and the normal life of the community in Assam.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Assam and applies to services declared as essential services by the State Government.

key_definitions.essential_service: Includes transport services for passengers or goods (land or water), services related to production, storage, supply, or distribution of gas or water, services related to public health and sanitation (including hospitals and dispensaries), public services and posts connected with the affairs of the State, secretarial staff of the Legislative Assembly of Assam, and any other service or employment that the State Government declares as essential if strikes therein would prejudicially affect public utility, public safety, or supplies and services necessary for community life, or would cause grave hardship to the community.
key_definitions.state_government: Means the State Government of Assam.
key_definitions.strike: Means the cessation of work by a body of persons employed in any essential service acting in combination or a concerted refusal or a refusal under a common understanding to continue to work or to accept employment. It also includes refusal to work overtime when necessary for maintenance of an essential service, and any other conduct likely to result in cessation or substantial retardation of work in an essential service.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Essential Services Maintenance (Assam) Act, 1980' and specifies its extent to the whole of the State of Assam.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'essential service', 'State Government', and 'strike'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit strikes in certain employments
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to prohibit strikes in any essential service by issuing a general or special order if it is satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest. Such orders are in force for six months and can be extended. Upon issuance of such an order, strikes in the specified essential service become illegal.

main_sections.section_title: Dismissal of employees participating in illegal strikes
main_sections.description: States that any person participating in an illegal strike is liable to disciplinary action, including dismissal, according to their terms and conditions of service.
Prescribes penalties for commencing, continuing, or participating in an illegal strike, which may include imprisonment up to six months, a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
Specifies penalties for instigating, inciting, or acting in furtherance of an illegal strike, which may include imprisonment up to one year, a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for giving financial aid to illegal strikes
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for knowingly expending or supplying money in furtherance or support of an illegal strike, which may include imprisonment up to one year, a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.
Grants police officers the power to arrest without a warrant any person reasonably suspected of committing an offense under this Act.
Mandates that all offenses under this Act shall be tried summarily by a Judicial Magistrate of the first class specially empowered, following provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Declares that the provisions of this Act and any orders issued under it shall prevail over anything inconsistent contained in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or any other law for the time being in force.

Repeals the Essential Services Maintenance (Assam) Ordinance, 1980, and provides that anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: No person employed in an essential service specified in a prohibitory order shall go or remain on strike.
Rule 2: Any strike declared or commenced in an essential service after the issuance of a prohibitory order is illegal.
Rule 3: Refusal to work overtime when necessary for the maintenance of an essential service is considered a strike.
Rule 4: Any conduct likely to result in, or resulting in, cessation or substantial retardation of work in an essential service is considered a strike.

penalties: Illegal strikes: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
Instigation/furtherance of illegal strikes: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.
Financial aid to illegal strikes: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers (for arrest), Judicial Magistrates of the first class (for trial and sentencing). The State Government issues orders and empowers magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Arrests can be made without warrant for suspected offenses. Offences are tried summarily by specially empowered Judicial Magistrates. The Act's provisions override other inconsistent laws, ensuring its enforcement priority.

rights: Right to engage in employment under normal conditions.
Right to benefit from disciplinary actions being taken according to applicable provisions.
duties: Duty of employees in essential services to not participate in illegal strikes.
Duty to comply with prohibitory orders issued by the State Government.
Duty of individuals not to instigate or provide financial aid to illegal strikes.
obligations: Employees in essential services are obligated to continue working and not cease work in a manner that constitutes an illegal strike.
Individuals are obligated to refrain from actions that disrupt essential services.
The State Government has an obligation to publish prohibitory orders in a manner best calculated to inform affected persons.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Issuance of a prohibitory order by the State Government prohibiting strikes in specified essential services due to public interest.
Procedure 2: Publication of the prohibitory order in a manner deemed best by the State Government to reach affected persons.
Procedure 3: Trial of offenses under the Act summarily by a specially empowered Judicial Magistrate of the first class, applying Sections 262 to 265 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
