Procedure 4: Arrest without warrant by police officers for reasonable suspicion of committing an offense under the Act.
administration: The State Government (of Assam) is responsible for issuing orders, empowering officials, and overseeing the administration of the Act.
important_notes: Notifications issued under sub-clause (v) of clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 2 must be laid before Parliament and cease to operate after 40 days unless approved by both Houses.
The Act overrides the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and other inconsistent laws.
Actions taken under the repealed Essential Services Maintenance (Assam) Ordinance, 1980, are deemed valid under this Act.

title: THE BIRD AND COMPANY LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS AND OTHER PROPERTIES) ACT, 1980
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the Bird and Company Limited to ensure continuity of production of vital goods, and for the acquisition of shares held by the company in specified companies to secure facilities, advantages, and control over their operations to prevent mismanagement. It aims to enable the Central Government to make necessary investments for maintenance and development of production, and to ensure public interest is served by the continued manufacture, production, and distribution of essential goods.
scope: The act applies to the undertakings of The Bird and Company Limited and its shares held in specified companies. Geographically, it seems to cover properties within and outside India. The subject matter scope includes the acquisition of undertakings, shares, management, employee provisions, payment of amounts, and related miscellaneous provisions.

key_definitions.appointed day: The 25th day of October, 1980.
key_definitions.share: A share, whether equity or preference, held by the Company in the capital of a specified company, including pledged shares.
key_definitions.specified company: A company specified in Schedule I of the Act.

main_sections.description: Names the act and specifies its commencement date.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the Company
main_sections.description: States that the undertakings of the Company and related rights vest in the Central Government on the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting of shares held by the Company in the specified companies
main_sections.description: Transfers and vests all shares held by the Company in specified companies to the Central Government on the appointed day, and clarifies the Central Government's registration as the shareholder.

Details what the vested undertaking includes, clarifies that vested properties are freed from encumbrances, and outlines procedures for mortgagees and other interest holders, and the continuation of licenses and pending proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government or the Government company not to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: States that liabilities of the Company for periods prior to the appointed day are the Company's liability and not enforceable against the Central Government or a Government company.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the Company in a Government company
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to direct the vesting of the Company's undertakings in a Government company under specified terms and conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of amounts to the Company and specified companies
main_sections.description: Concerns the payment of amounts to the Company and specified companies.
Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect.
Specifies penalties for contraventions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.
Provides for the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing provisions and saving clauses.

important_rules: On the appointed day (October 25, 1980), the undertakings of The Bird and Company Limited and its rights shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government.
All shares held by The Bird and Company Limited in specified companies shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government on the appointed day.
Vested properties, whether undertakings or shares, are freed from any trusts, obligations, mortgages, charges, liens, and other incumbrances.
Liabilities of The Bird and Company Limited for periods prior to the appointed day are to be borne by the Company and are not enforceable against the Central Government or a Government company.
The Central Government can direct the vesting of the Company's undertakings in a Government company.
Contracts of the Company will cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or a Government company.

penalties: Penalties are specified in Section 25 for contraventions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments, and the powers vested in the Central Government and Government companies. Enforcement of penalties for contraventions is also described.

rights: Rights of specified companies against the Company to recover sums owed or payments due are preserved (Section 4(3)).
Mortgagees and holders of other interests are entitled to claim payment from specified amounts (Section 5(4)).
Pending suits, appeals, or other proceedings by or against the Company shall continue by or against the Central Government or the designated Government company (Section 5(6)).
duties: Persons in charge of the management of the Company's undertakings have a duty to deliver all assets, etc. (Section 10).
obligations: Every mortgagee or person holding a charge, lien, or other interest in a vested property must intimate this to the Commissioner within a prescribed time and manner (Section 5(3)).

key_procedures: Acquisition and Transfer: Undertakings and shares are transferred to and vest in the Central Government on the appointed day.
Direction of Vesting in Government Company: The Central Government may, by notification, direct the vesting of undertakings in a Government company.
Payment of Amounts: Procedures for the payment of amounts to the Company and specified companies are outlined.
Claims to Commissioner: Claims against the Company's undertakings or shares must be made to the Commissioner of Payments.
Examination and Disbursement of Claims: The Commissioner examines claims, admits or rejects them, and disburses money to claimants.
Overriding Effect: The Act has an overriding effect over other laws.
Contract Ratification: Contracts of the Company require ratification by the Central Government or Government company to remain effective.
Rule Making: The Central Government has the power to make rules under the Act.
administration: The Central Government, and potentially Government companies as directed by the Central Government. The Commissioner of Payments also plays a role in administration related to claims.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning it prevails over other inconsistent laws (Section 23).
Certain liabilities of the Company prior to the appointed day are not enforceable against the Central Government or a Government company (Section 6).
Specific companies are listed in Schedule I, defining 'specified company'.

title: The High Court at Bombay (Extension of Jurisdiction to Goa, Daman and Diu) Act, 1981
purpose: To provide for the extension of the jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu, for the establishment of a permanent bench of that High Court at Panaji and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu. Its subject matter scope includes the extension of jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay, the establishment of a permanent bench, and related procedural and administrative matters.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.court_of_the_judicial_commissioner: The Court of the Judicial Commissioner for Goa, Daman and Diu.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day' and 'Court of the Judicial Commissioner'.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of Bombay High Court to Goa, Daman and Diu
main_sections.description: States that the jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay is extended to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu from the appointed day, and that the Court of the Judicial Commissioner is abolished.
Specifies that the High Court at Bombay will have all jurisdiction, powers, and authority in respect of Goa, Daman and Diu that were previously exercised by the Court of the Judicial Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution to apply to the Bombay High Court exercising jurisdiction over the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu
main_sections.description: Details how Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution will apply to the Bombay High Court when exercising jurisdiction over Goa, Daman and Diu, including specific modifications for references to 'State' and 'Governor'.
Entitles advocates practicing in the Court of the Judicial Commissioner before the appointed day to practice in the High Court at Bombay, subject to any rules or directions from the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of pending proceedings from the Court of the Judicial Commissioner to the Bombay High Court
main_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of all pending proceedings from the Court of the Judicial Commissioner to the High Court at Bombay and states that such transferred proceedings will be disposed of as if they were originally entertained by the Bombay High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Right to appear or act in proceedings transferred to the Bombay High Court
main_sections.description: Grants advocates entitled to practice in the Court of the Judicial Commissioner the right to appear or act in the High Court at Bombay in relation to transferred proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of a permanent bench of Bombay High Court at Panaji
main_sections.description: Establishes a permanent bench of the High Court at Bombay at Panaji from the appointed day, with a minimum number of judges nominated by the Chief Justice to exercise jurisdiction over cases arising in Goa, Daman and Diu.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of expenditure of the Bombay High Court
main_sections.description: Specifies that the expenditure of the High Court at Bombay, including judges' salaries and allowances, will be allocated between the State of Maharashtra and the Union by order of the President.
States that references in any law in force in Goa, Daman and Diu to the Court of the Judicial Commissioner shall be construed as references to the High Court at Bombay.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, for a period of two years from the appointed day.

Authorizes the Central Government to adapt and modify existing laws for the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu to facilitate the application of this Act, for a period of two years from the appointed day.

important_rules: From the appointed day, the jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay extends to Goa, Daman and Diu.
The Court of the Judicial Commissioner for Goa, Daman and Diu is abolished from the appointed day.
All pending proceedings before the Court of the Judicial Commissioner are transferred to the High Court at Bombay and will be disposed of by it.

A permanent bench of the High Court at Bombay is established at Panaji to exercise jurisdiction over cases arising in Goa, Daman and Diu, with a provision for cases to be heard at Bombay at the Chief Justice's discretion.
Advocates practicing in the erstwhile Court of the Judicial Commissioner are entitled to practice in the High Court at Bombay for transferred proceedings.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the High Court at Bombay.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the extension of jurisdiction, transfer of proceedings, establishment of a bench, and the Central Government's power to remove difficulties and adapt laws.

rights: Right of advocates to practice in the High Court at Bombay for transferred proceedings.
Right to appear or act in proceedings transferred to the Bombay High Court.
duties: The High Court at Bombay has the duty to exercise its extended jurisdiction over Goa, Daman and Diu.
The Chief Justice of the High Court at Bombay has the duty to nominate judges for the Panaji bench.
The Central Government has the duty to appoint the 'appointed day' and has powers to remove difficulties and adapt laws.
obligations: Advocates are obligated to practice in the High Court at Bombay subject to its rules and directions.
The Central Government is obligated to lay orders made under the power to remove difficulties before Parliament.

key_procedures: The Central Government notifies the 'appointed day' in the Official Gazette for the Act to come into force.
Pending proceedings are automatically transferred from the Court of the Judicial Commissioner to the High Court at Bombay.
Judges are nominated by the Chief Justice of the High Court at Bombay to sit at the Panaji bench.
The Central Government can issue orders to remove difficulties and adapt laws, which are then laid before Parliament.
administration: The Central Government, in conjunction with the High Court at Bombay.
important_notes: The Act specifies modifications to the application of Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution, particularly regarding references to 'State' and 'Governor'.
Article 233A of the Constitution is excluded from application.
The power to remove difficulties and adapt laws by the Central Government is limited to a period of two years from the appointed day.
Section 12 was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1988.

title: THE BRITISH INDIA CORPORATION LIMITED (ACQUISITION OF SHARES) ACT, 1981
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of certain shares of the British India Corporation Limited to ensure proper management, continuity, and development of production vital to the country's needs, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This act applies to the acquisition of shares of the British India Corporation Limited, a company registered in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. It covers all shares of the company except those held by the Central Government, State Governments, State Bank of India and its subsidiaries, Life Insurance Corporation of India, Unit Trust of India, corresponding new banks, and nationalized general insurance companies.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The 11th day of June, 1981.
key_definitions.bank: A banking company as defined by the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
key_definitions.commissioner: The Commissioner of Payments appointed under section 6.
key_definitions.company: British India Corporation Limited, registered in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.share: Any ordinary or preference share in the capital of the Company, including pledged shares, but excluding shares held by specified government entities and financial institutions.
key_definitions.shareholder: A person registered as a shareholder, or who has lodged a proper instrument of transfer, or who claims under a proper instrument of transfer lodged by a specified date.
key_definitions.specified_date: A date specified by the Central Government through notification, which can vary for different provisions.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it is deemed to have come into force on June 11, 1981.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'bank', 'Commissioner', 'Company', 'notification', 'share', 'shareholder', and 'specified date'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting of shares of the Company in the Central Government
main_sections.description: Declares that all shares of the Company stand transferred to and vest in the Central Government on the appointed day. It also states that the Central Government will be deemed registered as the holder of these shares and that the vested shares will be free from all trusts, liabilities, and encumbrances. It clarifies that this transfer does not affect certain rights of the Company against shareholders or rights of shareholders against the Company.

Empowers the Central Government to make provisions, by notification, for the management of the Company as a Government company, including changes in the Board of Directors and amendments to the memorandum and articles of association.

Specifies that an amount of rupees twenty-two lakhs and sixty thousand shall be paid by the Central Government to the shareholders for the acquisition of shares. This amount will carry simple interest at 4% per annum from the appointed day until payment.

Mandates the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner of Payments for disbursing amounts to shareholders. It also allows for the appointment of other persons to assist the Commissioner and outlines their powers. The salaries and allowances of the Commissioner and staff are to be defrayed from the Consolidated Fund of India.

main_sections.section_title: Payment by the Central Government to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to pay the total amount for share acquisition and interest to the Commissioner within thirty days from the specified date. A deposit account will be opened for these funds, operated by the Commissioner, and any interest accrued will benefit the shareholders.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Instructs shareholders to prefer claims related to acquired shares before the Commissioner within thirty days of the specified date, with a provision for a further thirty days in exceptional cases. It also states that preference shareholders have a preferential claim on the amounts paid to the Commissioner.
Directs the Commissioner to examine claims separately for preference and ordinary shares.

Outlines the process for the Commissioner to admit or reject claims, including fixing a date for proof of claim, providing public notice, and giving claimants an opportunity to be heard. The Commissioner is vested with powers similar to a civil court for investigations and proceedings are deemed judicial.

main_sections.section_title: Disbursement of money by the Commissioner to claimants
main_sections.description: Specifies the rate of payment per preference share (Rupees 10) and ordinary share (50 paise) by the Commissioner. It also details the apportionment of interest received by the Commissioner among shareholders.

main_sections.section_title: Undisbursed or unclaimed amount to be deposited to the general revenue account
main_sections.description: States that any undisbursed or unclaimed amounts are to be deposited into the general revenue account.
Grants the Central Government the power to inspect the affairs of the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Commissioner to inquire into disputes as to amount
main_sections.description: Empowers the Commissioner to inquire into disputes regarding the amount payable to any shareholder.
Allows for the deposit of amounts in court under certain circumstances.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws to the extent of any inconsistency.
Prescribes penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Deals with offences committed by companies under the Act.
Specifies the limitations on taking cognizance of offences under the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any existing provisions and savings thereof.

important_rules: All shares of the British India Corporation Limited are to be transferred to and vested in the Central Government on the appointed day (June 11, 1981).
The Central Government will be deemed the registered holder of these acquired shares.
The acquired shares will be free from all trusts, liabilities, and encumbrances.
The Central Government shall pay a specified amount (Rs. 22,60,000) plus interest to the shareholders.
A Commissioner of Payments is to be appointed to disburse the amounts to shareholders.
Shareholders must prefer their claims to the Commissioner within a specified period.
The Commissioner will examine and admit or reject claims after due process.
Disbursements to shareholders will be at a rate of Rs. 10 per preference share and 50 paise per ordinary share.
Undisbursed or unclaimed amounts are to be deposited into the general revenue account.

penalties: Section 17 specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the appointed Commissioner of Payments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments to manage the disbursement of funds, the power of inspection, and the imposition of penalties for non-compliance as outlined in the Act.

rights: Shareholders have the right to receive payment for their acquired shares.
Shareholders have the right to appeal against the Commissioner's decision to the principal civil court.
The Central Government has the right to acquire shares and manage the Company.
The Company has the right to recover sums from shareholders who have not paid for their shares.
Shareholders have the right to receive any dividend or payment due from the Company that subsisted before the appointed day.
duties: Shareholders have a duty to prefer claims before the Commissioner within the stipulated time.
Shareholders have a duty to file proof of their claim with the Commissioner.
The Central Government has a duty to make payments for the acquired shares.
The Commissioner has a duty to disburse amounts to shareholders and examine claims.
obligations: The Central Government is obligated to pay the acquisition amount and interest.
The Commissioner is obligated to follow the procedures for claim examination and disbursement.

key_procedures: Acquisition of shares by the Central Government on the appointed day.
Appointment of a Commissioner of Payments.
Payment by the Central Government to the Commissioner.
Submission of claims by shareholders to the Commissioner.
Examination, admission, or rejection of claims by the Commissioner.
Disbursement of acquired amounts by the Commissioner to shareholders.
Appeals against the Commissioner's decision.
administration: The Central Government, with the assistance of the Commissioner of Payments.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on other laws where there is inconsistency.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on June 11, 1981.
Certain entities' shares are excluded from the acquisition.
The Commissioner's investigations are deemed judicial proceedings.

title: THE DALMIA DADRI CEMENT LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1981
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the Dalmia Dadri Cement Limited to ensure their proper management for the benefit of the general public by continuing the manufacture, production, and distribution of cement, which is essential for the economy. It also addresses matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This act applies to the undertakings of Dalmia Dadri Cement Limited and their operations. Geographically, it pertains to the company's registered office located in Charkhi Dadri (Haryana) and its assets, whether within or outside India, as they vested in the Central Government.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The 23rd day of June, 1981.
key_definitions.cement_corporation: The Cement Corporation of India, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.commissioner: The Commissioner of Payments appointed under section 14.
key_definitions.company: Dalmia Dadri Cement Limited, a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956, with its registered office at Charkhi Dadri (Haryana).
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.specified_date: A date that the Central Government may specify by notification for the purposes of a particular provision of the Act, with different dates possible for different provisions.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is deemed to be June 23, 1981.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Cement Corporation', 'Commissioner', 'Company', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'specified date'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the Company
main_sections.description: Declares that on the appointed day, the undertakings of the Company and all related rights, title, and interest shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government.

Details what the vesting of undertakings includes (assets, rights, property, etc.), clarifies that vested properties are discharged from encumbrances, outlines the duty for mortgagees and other interest holders to intimate their claims to the Commissioner, and states that these claims can be satisfied from the payment amounts specified in sections 7 and 8, but not against the vested property itself. It also addresses the continuation of existing licenses and instruments and the continuation of pending legal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government or Cement Corporation not to be liable for prior liabilities
main_sections.description: Establishes that any liability of the Company for the period prior to the appointed day is solely the Company's responsibility and not that of the Central Government or the Cement Corporation. It also clarifies that awards, decrees, or orders passed after the appointed day concerning pre-appointed day matters, and liabilities incurred for contravention of laws before the appointed day, are not enforceable against the Central Government or the Cement Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the Company in Cement Corporation
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to direct, by notification, that the undertakings vesting in the Central Government shall instead vest in the Cement Corporation, either on the date of notification or another specified date. Upon such vesting, the Cement Corporation assumes all rights and liabilities of the Central Government in relation to the undertakings.

Specifies that for the transfer and vesting of the Company's undertakings, the Central Government shall pay an amount of eighty-four lakhs and eighty-seven thousand rupees to the Company, in cash, as per Chapter VI.

States that the amount specified in section 7 will carry simple interest at 4% per annum from the appointed day until payment. This additional amount will be paid by the Central Government to the Company. It also clarifies that liabilities of the Company will be discharged from the amounts specified in section 7 and this further amount, according to creditors' rights.

main_sections.section_title: Management, etc., of the undertakings of the Company
main_sections.description: Outlines that the general superintendence, direction, control, and management of the undertakings vest in the Cement Corporation if the Central Government has directed so under section 6(1). The Cement Corporation is then empowered to exercise all powers and do all things that the Company was authorized to do, including the disposal of assets if deemed necessary for legal or financial reasons.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to deliver possession of the undertakings of the Company and documents relating thereto
main_sections.description: Mandates that the Official Liquidator or any other person in possession or custody of the Company's undertakings or any part thereof shall forthwith deliver possession to the Central Government, or the Cement Corporation if vested under section 6.
The Central Government is empowered to appoint a Commissioner of Payments to manage the disbursement of amounts to claimants.
Declares that this Act shall have an effect overriding any other law for the time being in force, in case of inconsistency.
Specifies penalties for contravening any provision of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing law and provides savings provisions.

important_rules: On the appointed day (June 23, 1981), the undertakings of Dalmia Dadri Cement Limited, including all assets, rights, and interests, vest in the Central Government.
The Central Government can, by notification, direct that these undertakings shall vest in the Cement Corporation.
The Central Government shall pay an amount of eighty-four lakhs and eighty-seven thousand rupees to the Company for the acquisition, with simple interest at 4% per annum.
Liabilities of the Company prior to the appointed day are not enforceable against the Central Government or the Cement Corporation.
Employees of the Company may continue their employment under the new management.
The Official Liquidator or any other person in possession of the Company's undertakings must deliver possession to the Central Government or Cement Corporation.
Contracts entered into by the Company will cease to have effect unless ratified by the Central Government or Cement Corporation.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of any provision of the Act or rules made thereunder (as per Section 28).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Cement Corporation, Commissioner of Payments (for claims).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through vesting of undertakings, appointment of a Commissioner of Payments, powers to direct vesting, making rules, and imposing penalties for violations.

rights: The Central Government has the right to acquire the undertakings of the Company.
The Cement Corporation, if directed, has the right to own and manage the undertakings.
Creditors of the Company have the right to claim payment out of the compensation amount.
Existing licenses and instruments related to the undertakings continue to be in force.
Pending legal proceedings related to the undertakings continue and can be prosecuted by or against the Central Government or Cement Corporation.
duties: The Official Liquidator or any other person in possession must deliver possession of the undertakings and related documents.
Mortgagees and persons with other interests must provide intimation of their claims to the Commissioner.
The Cement Corporation has the duty to manage the undertakings if directed to do so.
The Commissioner of Payments has the duty to receive, examine, and disburse claims.
obligations: The Central Government has the obligation to pay the specified amounts to the Company.
The Cement Corporation has obligations derived from the rights and liabilities of the Central Government upon vesting.
The Company's liabilities prior to the appointed day are to be discharged from the acquisition amounts.
Contracts require ratification to remain effective.

key_procedures: Acquisition and Vesting: Undertakings of the Company vest in the Central Government on the appointed day, and can subsequently be vested in the Cement Corporation by government notification.
Payment of Compensation: The Central Government pays a fixed amount plus interest to the Company for the acquisition.
Claims Processing: A Commissioner of Payments is appointed to receive, examine, admit or reject, and disburse claims from creditors and other interested parties against the compensation amount.
Delivery of Possession: The Official Liquidator or any other holder must deliver possession of the undertakings and documents to the new owner.
Ratification of Contracts: Existing contracts need to be ratified by the Central Government or Cement Corporation to remain in effect.
administration: Central Government, Cement Corporation of India.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on other laws in case of inconsistency.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
The Act includes provisions for repeal and saving, indicating that previous laws on the matter might be superseded.

title: THE ANTI-APARTHEID (UNITED NATIONS CONVENTION) ACT, 1981
purpose: To give effect to the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to the provisions of the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid as set out in the Schedule. It addresses actions and individuals related to the crime of apartheid.

key_definitions.crime_of_apartheid: Inhuman acts committed for the purpose of establishing and maintaining domination by one racial group of persons over any other racial group of persons and systematically oppressing them, including similar policies and practices of racial segregation and discrimination as practiced in southern Africa. Specific acts include denial of the right to life and liberty, inflicting serious bodily or mental harm, arbitrary arrest and illegal imprisonment, imposing living conditions calculated to cause physical destruction, and exploitation of labor, particularly forced labor, and persecution of organizations and persons opposing apartheid.
key_definitions.company: Any body corporate and includes a firm or other association of individuals.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and states that it extends to the whole of India.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid
main_sections.description: Declares that specified provisions of the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid shall have the force of law in India. It also allows the Central Government to amend the Schedule in conformity with amendments to the Convention and requires such notifications to be laid before Parliament.

Prescribes punishment for persons to whom international criminal responsibility applies under Article III of the Convention, including death, life imprisonment, imprisonment up to ten years, and liability to fine.

main_sections.section_title: Offences by companies, organisations or institutions
main_sections.description: Holds individuals in charge of and responsible for the business or affairs of a company, organisation, or institution liable for offences committed by them, unless they prove the offence was without their knowledge or they exercised due diligence.
Allows for the trial of an offence under section 3 in any place where the person may be found or in such other place as directed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Previous sanction of the Central Government for arrest or prosecution
main_sections.description: Requires the previous sanction of the Central Government or an authorized officer for the arrest or prosecution of any person for an offence under section 3.
States that for the purposes of the Extradition Act, 1962, the offence under section 3 shall not be considered to be an offence of a political character.

important_rules: Rule: The crime of apartheid includes specific inhuman acts committed to establish and maintain racial domination and oppression, as detailed in Article II of the Convention.

Rule: International criminal responsibility applies to individuals, members of organizations and institutions, and state representatives who commit, participate in, incite, conspire, abet, encourage, or co-operate in the commission of the acts mentioned in Article II.
Rule: Offences committed by companies, organizations, or institutions render those in charge and responsible liable, unless they demonstrate lack of knowledge or due diligence.
Rule: Offences under section 3 are not considered political offences for the purposes of the Extradition Act, 1962.

penalties: Death penalty
Imprisonment for life
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years
Liability to fine
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, or such officer or authority as may be authorized by the Central Government in writing.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution and trial of offenders, with previous sanction from the Central Government for arrest or prosecution. The Act also allows for trials in various locations and specifies that offences are not political for extradition purposes.

rights: Right to life and liberty of person (denied by the crime of apartheid).
Freedom from serious bodily or mental harm, infringement of freedom or dignity, torture, or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment (denied by the crime of apartheid).
Right to freedom from arbitrary arrest and illegal imprisonment (denied by the crime of apartheid).
Freedom from deliberate imposition of living conditions calculated to cause physical destruction.
Right to freedom from exploitation of labor, including forced labor.
Right to fundamental rights and freedoms, particularly for those opposing apartheid.

key_procedures: Procedure: Any person committing an offence under section 3 may be tried for the offence in any place in which he may be found or in such other place as the Central Government may direct.

Procedure: No person shall be arrested or prosecuted in respect of any offence under section 3 except with the previous sanction of the Central Government or such officer or authority as may be authorized by that Government by order in writing.
administration: The Central Government
important_notes: Note: The Schedule contains specific articles of the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid that have the force of law in India.
Note: The Central Government can amend the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette to conform with amendments to the Convention, and these notifications must be laid before Parliament.
Note: For the purposes of this Act, references in Article III of the Convention to 'Article II' are construed as references to Article II as set out in the Schedule.

title: THE NATIONAL BANK FOR AGRICULTURE AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT ACT, 1981
purpose: To establish a development bank to be known as the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development for providing and regulating credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture, micro-enterprises, small enterprises and medium enterprises, cottage and village industries, handlooms, handicrafts and other rural crafts and other allied economic activities in rural areas with a view to promoting integrated rural development and securing prosperity of rural areas.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Its subject matter scope covers agriculture, micro-enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, cottage and village industries, handlooms, handicrafts, and other rural crafts and allied economic activities in rural areas.

key_definitions.agriculture: Includes horticulture, animal husbandry, forestry, dairy and poultry farming, pisciculture, and other allied activities. Pisciculture includes development of fisheries (inland and marine), fish catching, and related activities.
key_definitions.co-operative society: A society registered or deemed to be registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, or any other relevant State law.
key_definitions.rural development: Development of rural areas through any activities conducive to such development, including production of goods or provision of services in rural areas, and promotion of cottage and village industries, micro-enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, handicrafts, and handlooms.
key_definitions.rural area: The area comprised in any village and includes the area comprised in any town with a population not exceeding ten thousand or such other figure as specified by the Reserve Bank.
key_definitions.National Bank: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development established under section 3 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its geographical extent (whole of India), and commencement date as notified by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including agriculture, co-operative society, rural development, rural area, and National Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire property and contract. It also specifies the head office location and the possibility of establishing offices/branches in India and abroad.

Specifies the initial capital of the National Bank and empowers the Central Government to increase it. It also details the transfer of subscribed capital from the Reserve Bank to the Central Government and provisions for future capital issuance.
Details the composition and appointment of the Board of Directors.
Covers the provision of credit for production and marketing of agricultural produce.
Outlines the additional functions of the National Bank beyond its credit functions.

main_sections.section_title: National Rural Credit (Long Term Operations) Fund
main_sections.description: Establishes a fund for long-term credit operations in rural areas.
Specifies the audit procedures for the accounts of the National Bank.
Deals with the penalties for offenses committed under the Act.

important_rules: The National Bank is established as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The initial capital of the National Bank is one hundred crores of rupees, with the provision for the Central Government to increase it.
The Reserve Bank's subscribed capital in the National Bank is transferred to the Central Government.
The National Bank is empowered to provide and regulate credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture and allied economic activities in rural areas.
The National Bank has various credit functions including production and marketing credit, conversion loans, investment credit, and direct loans.
The Act establishes various funds such as the National Rural Credit (Long Term Operations) Fund, National Rural Credit (Stabilisation) Fund, and Research and Development Fund.
The Act outlines penalties for offenses committed under its provisions.

penalties: Section 56 provides for penalties for offenses committed under the Act, with specific details likely found within the section itself.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development itself, and potentially other governmental or regulatory bodies as specified in the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, imposition of penalties, and the regulatory powers vested in the National Bank as defined by the Act.

rights: The right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The right to contract.
The right to sue and be sued.
Access to records for credit assessment (Section 35).
duties: To provide and regulate credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture and rural economic activities.
To maintain fidelity and secrecy in its dealings (Section 51).
To prepare balance sheets and accounts (Section 46).
obligations: To operate within the framework of the Act and regulations made thereunder.
To comply with audit requirements.
To adhere to conditions for accommodation and repayment before agreed periods when necessary (Section 33, 34).

key_procedures: Establishment of the National Bank with corporate status.
Appointment of the Board of Directors and management structure.
Procedure for obtaining credit and loans from the National Bank.
Procedure for the management of funds, accounts, and audit.
Procedure for making regulations by the Board of Directors.
administration: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development itself is established to administer this Act, under the overall purview of the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act provides for the transfer of business and assets/liabilities from the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation.
The Act repealed the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation Act, 1963 (Act 10 of 1963).
Different commencement dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The Act defines 'micro enterprise', 'small enterprise', and 'medium enterprise' with reference to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006.

title: THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT FUND ACT, 1982
purpose: To implement the African Development Fund Agreement and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the African Development Fund (Fund) established under the African Development Fund Agreement, its officers, and employees, and governs payments, depository arrangements, and the conferment of status, immunities, exemptions, and privileges in India as per the Agreement.

key_definitions.Fund: The African Development Fund established under the Agreement.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the African Development Fund Act, 1982, specifies its territorial extent to the whole of India, and designates the Central Government's power to bring it into force via notification.
Defines 'Agreement' as the African Development Fund Agreement and 'Fund' as the African Development Fund established under the Agreement.

Mandates payments from the Consolidated Fund of India, subject to parliamentary appropriation, for subscriptions, sums payable, and charges to the Fund as per specified Articles of the Agreement. It also allows the Central Government to issue non-interest bearing, non-negotiable notes or obligations to the Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Reserve Bank to be depository for Fund.
main_sections.description: Designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of status and certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on Fund and conferment of certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on its officers and employees.
main_sections.description: Gives the force of law in India to the provisions of the African Development Fund Agreement as set out in the Schedule, notwithstanding any other law. It includes provisos to clarify limitations on customs duty exemptions and sales tax exemptions for the Fund. It also empowers the Central Government to amend the Schedule to conform with amendments to the Agreement.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Notifications issued under section 5 and rules made under section 6 to be laid before Parliament.
main_sections.description: Requires that every notification issued under section 5(2) and every rule made under section 6 be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulment by Parliament.

important_rules: Payments to the Fund, including subscriptions, sums payable, and charges, must be made out of the Consolidated Fund of India after parliamentary appropriation (Section 3(1)).
The Central Government can issue non-interest bearing, non-negotiable notes or obligations to the Fund (Section 3(2)).
The Reserve Bank of India shall act as the depository for the Fund's Indian currency holdings (Section 4).
The provisions of the African Development Fund Agreement as set out in the Schedule have the force of law in India (Section 5(1)).
Notifications issued under Section 5(2) and rules made under Section 6 must be laid before Parliament for approval or modification (Section 7).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for making rules and notifications), Reserve Bank of India (as depository). The Agreement's provisions, when having the force of law, will dictate enforcement mechanisms related to immunities and privileges.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications and rules issued by the Central Government, and through the application of the African Development Fund Agreement's provisions within India.

rights: Right of the Fund to be accorded status, immunities, exemptions, and privileges as per the Agreement (Section 5).
Right of the Fund to have its currency holdings deposited by the Reserve Bank of India (Section 4).
Right of the Central Government to issue non-interest bearing, non-negotiable notes or obligations (Section 3(2)).
duties: Duty of the Central Government to make payments to the Fund out of the Consolidated Fund of India as required (Section 3(1)).
Duty of the Central Government to lay notifications and rules before Parliament (Section 7).
Duty of the Fund to adhere to conditions agreed with a participating state regarding the sale of imported goods under exemption (Article 49(3) in Schedule).
Duty of the Fund's President to waive immunity of personnel when it impedes justice, without prejudice to the Fund's interests (Article 50(2) in Schedule).
obligations: Obligations of the Central Government to ensure the provisions of the Agreement have the force of law in India (Section 5(1)).
Obligations related to the purpose and functions of the Fund as detailed in the Agreement (e.g., Article 41 in Schedule).

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement of the Act: The Central Government appoints a date by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(3)).
Procedure for payments to the Fund: Payments are made out of the Consolidated Fund of India after due appropriation by Parliament (Section 3(1)).
Procedure for amendment of the Schedule: The Central Government may amend the Schedule by notification to conform with amendments to the Agreement (Section 5(2)).

Procedure for laying notifications and rules before Parliament: Notifications and rules are laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modification or annulment (Section 7).
administration: Central Government (for rule-making, notifications, and payments). The African Development Fund itself administers its operations as per the Agreement.
important_notes: The immunities and privileges granted to the Fund are subject to specific limitations, particularly concerning customs duty exemptions on imports without restrictions, sales taxes embedded in goods, and charges for services rendered (Section 5(1) proviso and Article 49(2)).
The provisions of Chapter VIII of the Agreement, detailing status, immunities, exemptions, and privileges, are incorporated into Indian law via the Schedule (Section 5(1)).
The Fund's Board of Directors or the President may waive certain immunities, exemptions, and privileges in specific circumstances (Article 50 in Schedule).

title: The Sugar Development Fund Act, 1982
purpose: To provide for the financing of activities for the development of the sugar industry and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to the sugar industry, including sugar factories, units thereof, and sugarcane development.

key_definitions.Fund: The Sugar Development Fund formed under section 3.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Sugar Cess Act, 1982: Other words and expressions used in this Act and not defined, but defined in the Sugar Cess Act, 1982 (3 of 1982), shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in that Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India), and outlines the commencement date to be appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Committee', 'Fund', and 'prescribed'. It also refers to definitions in the Sugar Cess Act, 1982.

Establishes the Sugar Development Fund. It details that the Fund shall consist of proceeds from the duty of excise levied under the Sugar Cess Act, 1982 (reduced by collection costs), any moneys received for the Act's purposes, and income from investment of these amounts.

Specifies how the Fund shall be applied, including making loans for rehabilitation and modernization of sugar factories, development of sugarcane, bagasse-based co-generation power projects, production of anhydrous alcohol/ethanol, grants for research, defraying expenditure for buffer stocks of sugar, internal transport and freight charges for export shipments, financial assistance for interest on loans, and any other expenditure for the Act's purposes. It also states that the manner and terms of loans/grants will be prescribed.
Outlines that applications for loans or grants under section 4 must be made to the Committee in a prescribed manner and form.

Details the constitution of a committee by the Central Government to ensure speedy consideration of applications and address administrative problems. The composition and procedure of the Committee are to be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report of activities financed under the Act
main_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to publish an annual report in the Official Gazette, detailing activities financed under the Act and a statement of accounts for the financial year.

main_sections.section_title: Power to call for reports and returns
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to require sugar factory occupiers to furnish statistical and other information in a prescribed form and within a prescribed period for the Act's purposes.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions, including specific rules for loans/grants, applications, Committee composition and procedure, information furnishing, and any other prescribed matter. It also includes a parliamentary approval process for these rules.

important_rules: Loans or grants made under Section 4 are subject to prescribed terms and conditions.
Applications for loans or grants must be submitted to the Committee in the prescribed format and manner.
Sugar factory occupiers may be required to furnish specific statistical and other information to the Central Government.
Rules made under the Act require laying before both Houses of Parliament for a total of thirty days, with provisions for modification or annulment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made under the Act, requiring information submission, and by managing the Sugar Development Fund and its applications.

rights: Sugar factories and units have the right to apply for loans or grants for specified development purposes.
The sugar industry has the right to benefit from activities financed by the Sugar Development Fund.
duties: Occupiers of sugar factories have a duty to furnish information as required by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Application for loans or grants: An application must be made to the Committee in the prescribed manner and form (Section 5).
Rule-making process: The Central Government can make rules, which must be laid before Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulments (Section 9).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act came into force on 1st June, 1982.
Certain provisions were inserted or amended by later Acts, such as Act 30 of 2002, Act 64 of 1982, and Act 4 of 2008.

title: The Chit Funds Act, 1982
purpose: To provide for the regulation of chit funds and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The Act regulates chit funds, which involve a group of people subscribing to a sum of money periodically, with each subscriber taking turns to receive the net chit amount determined by lot, auction, or tender.

key_definitions.approved_bank: State Bank of India, a subsidiary bank, a corresponding new bank, a Regional Rural Bank, a banking company as defined under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, or a banking institution notified by the Central Government or approved by the State Government in consultation with the Reserve Bank.
key_definitions.chit: A transaction by or under which a person enters into an agreement with a specified number of persons to subscribe a certain sum of money or quantity of grain by periodical instalments over a definite period, and each subscriber in turn receives the net chit amount as determined by lot, auction, or tender, or in another specified manner.
key_definitions.chit_agreement: The document containing the articles of agreement between the foreman and the subscribers relating to the chit.
key_definitions.chit_business: The business of conducting a chit.
key_definitions.defaulting_subscriber: A subscriber who has failed to pay subscriptions due according to the chit agreement terms.
key_definitions.discount: The sum of money or quantity of grain a prized subscriber foregoes as per the chit agreement, set aside for running expenses, distribution among subscribers, or both.
key_definitions.draw: The method specified in the chit agreement for identifying the prized subscriber at any installment.
key_definitions.foreman: The person responsible for conducting the chit under the chit agreement, including any person performing the foreman's functions under section 39.
key_definitions.gross_chit_amount: The total of subscriptions payable by all subscribers for any installment of a chit, without any deduction.
key_definitions.net_chit_amount: The difference between the gross chit amount and the discount. For fractional tickets, it's the proportionate difference. If not in cash, its value is determined at the time it becomes payable.
key_definitions.non_prized_subscriber: Does not include a defaulting subscriber.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prized_subscriber: A subscriber who has received or is entitled to receive the net chit amount.
key_definitions.Registrar: The Registrar of Chits appointed under section 61, including Additional, Joint, Deputy, or Assistant Registrars appointed under that section.
key_definitions.share_of_discount: The subscriber's share in the discount amount available for distribution among subscribers at each installment.
key_definitions.State_Government: In relation to a Union territory, means the administrator of that Union territory.
key_definitions.subscriber: Includes a person holding a fraction of a ticket and a transferee of a ticket or fraction thereof by assignment or operation of law.
key_definitions.ticket: The subscriber's share in a chit.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title as the Chit Funds Act, 1982, its extent to the whole of India, and the provision for its commencement by notification in the Official Gazette, allowing for different dates for different States.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'approved bank', 'chit', 'chit agreement', 'chit business', 'defaulting subscriber', 'discount', 'draw', 'foreman', 'gross chit amount', 'net chit amount', 'non-prized subscriber', 'prized subscriber', 'Registrar', 'Reserve Bank', 'share of discount', 'State Government', 'subscriber', and 'ticket'.

main_sections.section_title: Act to override other laws, memorandum, articles, etc.
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any other law, memorandum, articles of association, bye-laws, agreement, or resolution, regardless of when they were registered, executed, or passed.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of chits not sanctioned or registered under the Act
main_sections.description: Prohibits the conduct of chit funds that are not sanctioned or registered in accordance with the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Security to be given by foreman
main_sections.description: Specifies the requirements for security to be provided by the foreman.
Mandates that a prized subscriber must furnish security.

main_sections.section_title: Circumstances under which chits may be wound up
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions or circumstances under which a chit fund can be wound up.
Details the penalties that may be imposed for violations of the Act.

important_rules: No chit shall be conducted unless it is sanctioned or registered under the Act (Section 4).
No invitation for subscriptions to a chit shall be made except under specified conditions (Section 5).
A chit agreement must be filed with the Registrar (Section 7).
Companies conducting chits must meet minimum capital requirements and create a reserve fund (Section 8).
Subscribers must be provided with copies of the chit agreement (Section 10).
The foreman must provide security as prescribed (Section 20).
Prized subscribers must furnish security (Section 31) and pay subscriptions regularly (Section 32).
Non-prized subscribers must pay subscriptions and obtain receipts (Section 27).

penalties: Penalties for offenses under the Act (Section 76).
Penalties for second and subsequent convictions (Section 77).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Chits and other appointed officers, as well as potentially the Reserve Bank and State Governments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection of books and records, imposition of penalties, compounding of offenses, and legal proceedings. The Registrar has powers to give extension of time for filing documents, delegate powers, and compound offenses.

rights: Right of a subscriber to receive the net chit amount as per the chit agreement (Section 2(b)).
Right of foreman to conduct the chit and demand future subscriptions by written notice (Section 21, 33).
Right of certain subscribers to inspect chit records (Section 44).
Right to appeal against decisions of the Registrar or nominee (Section 59, 70).
Right to claim compensation to foreman under certain circumstances (Section 58).
duties: Duty of foreman to conduct the chit responsibly, provide security, keep proper books, and furnish a balance sheet (Sections 22, 20, 23, 24).
Duty of subscribers to pay subscriptions regularly and obtain receipts (Section 27).
Duty of prized subscribers to furnish security and pay subscriptions regularly (Sections 31, 32).
Duty of foreman to give copies of chit agreements to subscribers (Section 10).
Duty of foreman to allow certain subscribers to inspect chit records (Section 44).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the terms of the chit agreement.
Obligation to pay future subscriptions for prized subscribers.
Obligation to provide security by the foreman and prized subscribers.

key_procedures: Registration of chits and filing of chit agreements with the Registrar (Sections 4, 7).
Conducting chits with proper documentation of proceedings and filing minutes with the Registrar (Sections 16, 17, 18).
Procedure for furnishing security by the foreman and prized subscribers (Sections 20, 31).
Procedure for the removal of defaulting subscribers (Section 28).
Procedure for the transfer of subscriber rights and recognition by the foreman (Sections 35, 36).
Procedure for the termination of chits (Section 40).
Procedure for the winding up of chits, including applications, orders, and vesting of assets (Sections 49, 51, 54).
Procedure for the settlement of disputes and arbitration (Sections 66, 67).
administration: The Act is administered by the Registrar of Chits appointed under section 61, and the Reserve Bank of India plays an advisory role.
important_notes: The Act is intended to override other laws and agreements related to chit funds (Section 3).
Certain chits may be exempted from the provisions of this Act by the Central Government (Section 85, 87).
Banks are generally prohibited from conducting chit business (Section 86).

title: The Governors (Emoluments, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1982
purpose: To determine the emoluments, allowances, and privileges of Governors.
scope: Applies to Governors of States in India. The Act extends to the whole of India. 'State' does not include a Union territory.

key_definitions.ex-Governor: A person who has been the Governor of a State or two or more States.
key_definitions.Governor: The Governor, or any person discharging the functions of the Governor, of any State or of two or more States.
key_definitions.maintenance: In relation to official residences, includes the provision of electricity, gas and water; in relation to motor vehicles, includes the pay and allowances of chauffeurs and the provision of oil and petrol or other fuel.
key_definitions.members of the family: In relation to a Governor, means the spouse, dependent children and the dependent parents of the Governor.
key_definitions.official residences: Residences specified by the President, by notification in the Official Gazette, as the official residences of the Governor and includes the staff quarters and other buildings appurtenant thereto and the gardens thereof.
key_definitions.State: Does not include a Union territory.

main_sections.description: Names the Act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India, with historical exclusion of Jammu and Kashmir), and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'ex-Governor', 'Governor', 'maintenance', 'members of the family', 'official residences', 'rules', and 'State'.
Specifies the monthly emoluments payable to every Governor. It also includes provisions for reducing emoluments if a Governor is in receipt of a pension or certain other benefits.

Deals with leave granted to a Governor by the President and the payment of leave allowance during such leave. The allowance is subject to reduction if the Governor's emoluments are reduced under Section 3.

main_sections.section_title: Use and maintenance of official residences
main_sections.description: Entitles a Governor to the use of official residences without payment of rent and absolves the Governor from personal charges for furnishing or maintenance.
States that no charge falls on a Governor personally for the pay, allowances, pension, or emoluments of the household establishment provided to them, subject to rules.
Grants entitlement to a Governor and their family for free medical attendance, accommodation, and treatment in government hospitals, both during and after their term of office.
Entitles a Governor to the use of a specified number of motor vehicles without rent or hire and without personal charge for maintenance. Rules regulate the use by family members.

main_sections.section_title: Traveling allowance on assumption or vacation of office
main_sections.description: Entitles a Governor to traveling allowance for themselves, family, and effects for journeys related to assuming or relinquishing office.

main_sections.section_title: Allowances for renewing furnishings and for maintenance of official residences
main_sections.description: Entitles a Governor to allowances for renewing furnishings and maintaining official residences as determined by the President.

Outlines additional privileges and payments to Governors for discharging their duties with convenience and dignity, including entertainment allowance, hospitality grant, household establishment expenses, office expenses, contract allowance, tour expenses, and others as prescribed by rules.
Empowers the President to increase authorized allowances or sanction expenses for matters not covered by rules, with the possibility of retrospective effect. Orders must be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Entitlement of ex-Governor to secretarial assistance
main_sections.description: Grants ex-Governors entitlement to secretarial assistance of one Personal Assistant on reimbursement basis for life, with exceptions if re-appointed or holding other public office.

Grants the President the power to make rules to give effect to the Act's provisions, covering various aspects like leave, household establishment, medical treatment, conveyance use, traveling allowances, furnishings, and privileges. Rules must be laid before Parliament for modification or annulment.

Validates special orders issued by the President regarding allowances, expenses, or privileges of Governors (with a specific provision for the Governor of Nagaland) before the Act's commencement, even if made retrospectively or inconsistent with general orders.
Ensures that the Act and its rules do not diminish the emoluments and allowances of any Governor during their term of office.

important_rules: Governors are entitled to emoluments at the rate of three lakh fifty thousand rupees per month.
Emoluments of a Governor shall be reduced if they are in receipt of a pension or certain other benefits from previous government service.
Governors are entitled to the use of official residences without payment of rent and without personal charge for furnishing or maintenance.
Governors and their families are entitled to free medical attendance, accommodation, and treatment in government hospitals.
Governors are entitled to the use of a specified number of motor vehicles without personal charge for maintenance.
Ex-Governors are entitled to secretarial assistance of one Personal Assistant on reimbursement basis for life, with exceptions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through the President who has the power to make rules and issue orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders issued by the President, and rules made under the Act. Orders and rules are subject to parliamentary oversight.

rights: Right to emoluments.
Right to leave allowance.
Right to use and maintenance of official residences.
Right to household establishment.
Right to free medical treatment for self and family.
Right to use of motor vehicles.
Right to traveling allowance on assumption or vacation of office.
Right to allowances for renewing furnishings and maintaining official residences.
Right to other privileges and allowances for discharging duties.
Right to secretarial assistance for ex-Governors.
obligations: Governors whose emoluments are reduced due to pension or other benefits must accept this reduction.
Rules made under the Act must be followed.
Orders and rules laid before Parliament are subject to modification or annulment.

key_procedures: Appointment of the Act's commencement date by the Central Government via notification.
Specification of official residences by the President via notification.
Granting of leave and determination of leave allowance rates by the President.
Determination of the number of motor vehicles for Governor's use by the President.
Issuance of special orders by the President to increase allowances or sanction expenses.
Laying of all orders and rules before both Houses of Parliament for review and potential modification/annulment.
administration: The President, with the Central Government facilitating through notifications and orders. Rules are made by the President.
important_notes: The Act was amended significantly in 1993, 2008, 2014, 2018, and 2019.
The exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir was omitted in 2019.
The emoluments have been revised multiple times, with the current rate of three lakh fifty thousand per month being a result of amendments.
Orders made under Section 12 can have retrospective effect.
The validation section (Section 14) retrospectively legitimizes past presidential orders regarding Governor's entitlements.

title: The State Bank of Sikkim (Acquisition of Shares) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1982
purpose: To provide, in the public interest, for the acquisition of certain shares of the State Bank of Sikkim for the purpose of better consolidation and extension of banking facilities in the State of Sikkim and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the State Bank of Sikkim (referred to as 'Sikkim Bank'), its shares, undertakings, employees, and related financial matters within the State of Sikkim. It also involves the Central Government and the State Government of Sikkim.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.co-operative_bank: The Sikkim State Co-operative Bank Limited, a society registered under the Sikkim Co-operative Societies Act, 1978.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.sikkim_bank: The State Bank of Sikkim constituted under the State Bank of Sikkim Proclamation, 1968.
key_definitions.united_commercial_bank: The United Commercial Bank constituted under section 3 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'co-operative bank', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'Sikkim Bank', 'State Government', and 'United Commercial Bank'.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting in the Central Government of certain shares of Sikkim Bank
main_sections.description: Declares that on the appointed day, all shares of the State Bank of Sikkim, except those held by the State Government, shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government. These shares are freed from all trusts, liabilities, and encumbrances. Shareholders are entitled to certain dividends.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting of undertaking of Sikkim Bank
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the undertakings of the Sikkim Bank shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government.
Details the scope of the 'undertakings' vesting, including all assets, rights, liabilities, contracts, and pending legal proceedings, which will be transferred to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting of the shares and undertakings of Sikkim Bank in the State Government
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct, by notification, that the shares and undertakings of Sikkim Bank, having vested in the Central Government, shall instead vest in the State Government of Sikkim.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of Sikkim Bank in the Sikkim Co-operative bank
main_sections.description: Allows the State Government to direct, by notification, that the undertakings of Sikkim Bank, after vesting in the State Government, shall vest in the Sikkim Co-operative Bank, subject to certain terms and conditions.
Specifies the amount payable by the Central Government to the holders of Sikkim Bank shares and the interest applicable on this amount.

main_sections.section_title: Management, etc., of the undertakings of Sikkim Bank
main_sections.description: Outlines the management of the vested undertakings. If vested in the State Government, it exercises powers. If directed to vest in the co-operative bank, that bank assumes management.

main_sections.section_title: Date of delivery, possession of property acquired and documents relating thereto
main_sections.description: Mandates the delivery of all property, books, documents, and papers relating to the vested undertakings to the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of service of existing officers and employees of the Sikkim Bank to the co-operative bank
main_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of service of officers and employees of Sikkim Bank to the State Government and subsequently to the co-operative bank, ensuring continuity of their rights and privileges regarding pension, gratuity, etc.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of inconsistency.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Protects persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act from legal proceedings.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Deals with offenses committed by companies under this Act.
Empowers the Central or State Government to delegate their powers under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: References to Sikkim Bank in other laws
main_sections.description: Provides for the substitution of references to 'Sikkim Bank' in other laws with appropriate references after its dissolution.
Provides for the dissolution of the Sikkim Bank.

important_rules: Shares of Sikkim Bank (excluding State Government's) vest in the Central Government on the appointed day.
The undertakings of Sikkim Bank also vest in the Central Government on the appointed day.
The Central Government can direct the vesting of these shares and undertakings in the State Government.
The State Government can further direct the vesting of the undertakings in the Sikkim Co-operative Bank.
Employees of Sikkim Bank are transferred to the State Government and then potentially to the co-operative bank, retaining their service rights.
Certain appointments, promotions, or benefits granted after November 16, 1976, to employees may not be valid unless approved by the State Government.

penalties: Specific penalties for contravention of the Act are outlined in Section 14.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, the State Government of Sikkim, and potentially the Sikkim Co-operative Bank, depending on the stage of vesting and management.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, directions, rules, and legal proceedings as empowered by the Act. Enforcement of possession of property and documents is also a key aspect.

rights: Shareholders are entitled to receive specified dividends.
Employees retain rights and privileges related to pension, gratuity, etc.
The Central Government, State Government, and Co-operative Bank acquire rights and assets of Sikkim Bank.
The Central Government has the right to make rules and remove difficulties.
