duties: Persons in possession of Sikkim Bank property must deliver it to the State Government.
Individuals possessing books, documents, or papers related to Sikkim Bank must account for and deliver them to the State Government.
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to make payments for acquired shares.
The Co-operative Bank, if it takes over the undertakings, assumes all rights and liabilities of the Central/State Government.

key_procedures: Appointment of an 'appointed day' by the Central Government via notification to bring the Act into force.
Vesting of shares and undertakings of Sikkim Bank first in the Central Government, then potentially in the State Government, and finally in the Sikkim Co-operative Bank via government notifications.
Transfer of employees' service to the new entities with protection of their service conditions.
Delivery of all acquired property and documentation to the relevant government entity.
The Central Government may issue rules and orders to remove difficulties in implementation.
administration: The Central Government, the State Government of Sikkim, and the Sikkim Co-operative Bank.
important_notes: The Act overrides other laws in case of conflict (Section 12).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 13).

Specific conditions apply to employee appointments and benefits made after November 16, 1976, before the appointed day, potentially requiring State Government approval for their validity (Section 11(3)).

title: The Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against Safety of Civil Aviation Act, 1982
purpose: To give effect to the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to offences committed outside India by any person under section 3. Specific clauses in section 5 detail jurisdiction for offences committed outside India.

key_definitions.aircraft: Any aircraft, whether or not registered in India, other than a military aircraft or an aircraft used in customs or police service.
key_definitions.aircraft registered in India: An aircraft which is for the time being registered in India.
key_definitions.airport: An aerodrome as defined in clause (2) of section 2 of the Aircraft Act, 1934 (22 of 1934).
key_definitions.Convention country: A country in which the Montreal Convention is for the time being in force.
key_definitions.military aircraft: An aircraft of the naval, military, air force or any other armed forces of any country and includes every aircraft commanded for the time being by a person in such force detailed for the purpose.
key_definitions.Montreal Convention: The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation signed at Montreal on the 23rd day of September, 1971.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), applicability to offences outside India, and the provision for commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'aircraft', 'aircraft registered in India', 'airport', 'Convention country', 'military aircraft', and 'Montreal Convention'. It also includes deemed definitions for an aircraft in flight and in service.

main_sections.section_title: Offence of committing violence on board an aircraft in flight, etc.
main_sections.description: Defines offences such as committing acts of violence, destroying or damaging aircraft, placing dangerous devices on aircraft, and communicating false information that endangers an aircraft in flight. It also covers attempts and abetment.

Defines offences committed at an airport, including acts of violence, destruction or damage to aircraft or airport facilities, or disruption of services, that endanger safety at the airport. It also covers attempts and abetment.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction of, or damage to, air navigation facilities
main_sections.description: Criminalizes the unlawful and intentional destruction, damage, or interference with air navigation facilities if it endangers the safety of aircraft in flight. It also covers attempts and abetment.

Outlines the jurisdiction for offences committed outside India, specifying conditions under which a person can be dealt with as if the offence were committed in India. It also sets conditions for courts to take cognizance of such offences.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of powers of investigation, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution on its officers, exercisable by police officers under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Provides for the specification of Courts of Session as Designated Courts for speedy trials, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court. It mandates day-to-day trials as far as practicable.
Specifies that all offences under this Act are triable only by Designated Courts. It also details procedures for forwarding persons to Designated Courts and for taking cognizance of offences.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the Code to proceedings before a Designated Court
main_sections.description: States that the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, shall apply to proceedings before a Designated Court, and the prosecutor will be deemed a Public Prosecutor.

Deems offences under sections 3 and 4 as extraditable offences in treaties with Convention countries. It also clarifies the application of the Extradition Act, 1962, to offences under this Act concerning aircraft in flight.

Imposes restrictions on granting bail for offences under this Act, requiring the Public Prosecutor to be given an opportunity to oppose and the court to be satisfied of reasonable grounds for release.
Authorizes the Central Government to notify contracting parties to the Montreal Convention, which serves as conclusive evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Power to treat certain aircraft to be registered in Convention countries
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct, by notification, that certain aircraft be treated as registered in a Convention country if they satisfy the requirements of Article 9 of the Montreal Convention.
Mandates that no prosecution for an offence under this Act can be instituted without the previous sanction of the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Presumptions as to offences under sections 3, 3A and 4
main_sections.description: Establishes presumptions in a prosecution for offences under sections 3, 3A, and 4, where the presence of arms, ammunition, or explosives, or evidence of violence by the accused, leads to a presumption of guilt unless proved otherwise.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act's provisions.

important_rules: Rule 1: Unlawfully and intentionally committing acts of violence against persons on board an aircraft in flight that are likely to endanger the aircraft's safety.
Rule 2: Unlawfully and intentionally destroying an aircraft in service or causing damage that renders it incapable of flight or endangers its safety.
Rule 3: Unlawfully and intentionally placing devices or substances on an aircraft in service that are likely to destroy it, render it incapable of flight, or endanger its safety.
Rule 4: Unlawfully and intentionally communicating false information that endangers the safety of an aircraft in flight.

Rule 5: At an airport, unlawfully and intentionally using any device, substance, or weapon to commit acts of violence likely to cause grievous hurt or death, or to destroy or seriously damage any aircraft or facility, or disrupt services, thereby endangering or threatening to endanger safety at the airport.
Rule 6: Unlawfully and intentionally destroying, damaging, or interfering with air navigation facilities in a manner likely to endanger the safety of aircraft in flight.

Rule 7: No person accused of an offence under this Act shall be released on bail or their own bond if in custody, unless the Public Prosecutor has had an opportunity to oppose the application, and the court is satisfied there are reasonable grounds that the accused is not guilty and not likely to commit an offence while on bail.

penalties: Imprisonment for life and liability to fine for committing offences under sections 3, 3A, and 4.
Imprisonment for life and liability to fine for attempts to commit, or abetting, offences under sections 3, 3A, and 4.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for sanctioning prosecution, conferring investigation powers), State Government (for specifying Designated Courts), Designated Courts (for trial), Police Officers and Government Officers (for assisting Central Government officers).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation and prosecution by designated officers and courts, with specific procedures for speedy trials and bail restrictions. Extradition provisions are also in place for international cooperation.

rights: Right to protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
duties: Duty to assist officers of the Central Government in executing the provisions of the Act (for police and other Government officers).
Duty to provide opportunity to Public Prosecutor to oppose bail applications.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation.
Obligation to adhere to the procedures established for Designated Courts and trials.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencing the Act: The Central Government appoints a commencement date by notification.
Procedure for investigation and prosecution: The Central Government can confer powers of investigation and prosecution on its officers.
Procedure for speedy trial: State Governments specify Courts of Session as Designated Courts for speedy trials.
Procedure for trial: Designated Courts are to hold trials on a day-to-day basis as far as practicable.
Procedure for cognizance of offences: Designated Courts can take cognizance of offences upon a complaint by an authorized officer, without the accused being committed for trial.

Procedure for bail: Strict conditions apply to granting bail, including opposition by the Public Prosecutor and satisfaction of the court regarding the accused's innocence and low risk of re-offending.
Procedure for prosecution: Previous sanction of the Central Government is mandatory for instituting prosecution.
administration: Central Government and State Governments (for designating courts). Specific officers of the Central Government are empowered for investigation and prosecution.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act gives effect to the Montreal Convention, 1971.
Note 2: Offences under this Act are considered extraditable offences.
Note 3: Special provisions exist for bail, with limitations beyond those in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, though High Courts retain special powers under Section 439 CrPC.
Note 4: Presumptions can be made regarding offences under sections 3, 3A, and 4 if certain conditions related to recovered arms/explosives or evidence of violence are met.

title: The African Development Bank Act, 1983
purpose: To implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the African Development Bank and for matters concerned therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It confers certain statuses, immunities, exemptions, and privileges on the African Development Bank and its officers and employees.

key_definitions.Agreement: The agreement for the establishment of the African Development Bank.
key_definitions.Bank: The African Development Bank established under the Agreement.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the African Development Bank Act, 1983, specifies that it extends to the whole of India, and outlines that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Defines 'Agreement' and 'Bank' for the purposes of the Act.

Specifies that sums required for paying subscriptions and other payments by the Central Government to the Bank under the Agreement shall be paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India. It also allows the Central Government to issue non-interest bearing and non-negotiable notes or obligations to the Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Reserve Bank to be depository for Bank
main_sections.description: Designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of status and certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on Bank and conferment of certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on its officers and employees
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Agreement set out in the Schedule have the force of law in India. It includes provisos to clarify the extent of exemptions, particularly regarding customs duties and taxes. It also empowers the Central Government to amend the Schedule based on amendments to the Agreement.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Notifications issued under section 5 and rules made under section 6 to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that every notification issued under section 5(2) and every rule made under section 6 must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period. It outlines the procedure for modifications or annulment of such notifications or rules by Parliament.

important_rules: Payments to the African Development Bank, including subscriptions and other sums payable by the Central Government under the Agreement, shall be made from the Consolidated Fund of India after parliamentary appropriation.
The Central Government may issue non-interest bearing and non-negotiable notes or obligations to the Bank.
The Reserve Bank of India shall act as the depository for the Bank's Indian currency holdings.
Provisions of the African Development Bank Agreement set out in the Schedule have the force of law in India, with specific limitations on exemptions from customs duties and taxes.
The Central Government can amend the Schedule to align with amendments in the Agreement.
The Central Government is empowered to make rules for the Act's implementation.
Notifications and rules under the Act must be presented to Parliament for review and potential modification or annulment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and Parliament (for oversight of rules and notifications). Enforcement of specific immunities and privileges would likely involve the Bank itself and potentially judicial interpretation in case of disputes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act and the incorporated Agreement. Section 5 makes the Agreement's provisions (as per the Schedule) have the force of law. Rules made under Section 6 provide further mechanisms for implementation.

rights: The African Development Bank has the right to receive payments from the Central Government of India.
The African Development Bank has the right to be held by the Reserve Bank of India as its depository.
The African Development Bank and its officers/employees are granted specific immunities, exemptions, and privileges as detailed in the Schedule (derived from the Agreement).
duties: The Central Government has a duty to pay subscriptions and other sums to the Bank.
The Central Government has a duty to comply with the provisions of the Agreement as implemented by this Act.
The Central Government has a duty to lay notifications and rules before Parliament.
Parliament has a duty to review and potentially modify or annul notifications and rules.
The Board of Directors of the Bank has the right and duty to waive immunities/exemptions in certain circumstances.
The President of the Bank has the right and duty to waive immunity of officials when it impedes justice.
obligations: India is obligated to implement the provisions of the African Development Bank Agreement.
The Central Government has an obligation to make payments to the Bank as required by the Agreement.

key_procedures: Notification of Commencement: The Central Government notifies the date on which the Act comes into force.
Payment Procedures: Payments to the Bank are made out of the Consolidated Fund of India, requiring parliamentary appropriation.
Rule Making and Notification: The Central Government may issue rules and notifications through the Official Gazette.
Parliamentary Laying: Notifications and rules are presented to Parliament for review.
Modification/Annulment of Rules/Notifications: Parliament can modify or annul notifications and rules.
administration: The Central Government (specifically, likely the Ministry of Finance or a related ministry responsible for international financial institutions).
important_notes: The immunities and privileges granted to the Bank, its property, assets, income, operations, and transactions are subject to certain limitations outlined in the proviso to Section 5(1), particularly concerning exemptions from customs duties and taxes on goods, and taxes that are charges for services rendered.

The Schedule contains specific articles from the Agreement Establishing the African Development Bank that have the force of law in India. These articles detail the Bank's status, immunities, exemptions, and privileges.

Waiver of immunities, exemptions, and privileges is possible under specific conditions and at the discretion of the Bank's Board of Directors or President, provided it serves the Bank's interests or facilitates the course of justice.

title: THE PUNJAB DISTURBED AREAS ACT, 1983
purpose: To make better provision for the suppression of disorder and for the restoration and maintenance of public order in disturbed areas in Punjab.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Punjab. It applies to areas declared as 'disturbed areas' by the State Government.

key_definitions.disturbed_area: An area which is for the time being declared by notification under section 3 to be a disturbed area.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Punjab), and commencement date (deemed to have come into force on October 7, 1983).
Defines the term 'disturbed area'.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to declare areas to be disturbed areas
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to declare any part or the whole of a district in Punjab as a disturbed area through official gazette notification.

main_sections.section_title: Power to fire upon persons contravening certain orders
main_sections.description: Grants authority to Magistrates or Police Officers (Sub-Inspector rank or above in Armed Branch) to use force, including firing, causing death, after due warning, against persons contravening laws or orders in a disturbed area that prohibit assemblies of five or more persons or the carrying of weapons, ammunition, or explosives.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to destroy arms dump, fortified positions, etc.
main_sections.description: Authorizes Magistrates or Police Officers (Sub-Inspector rank or above) to destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, shelters used for armed attacks, training camps for armed volunteers, or hide-outs used by armed gangs or absconders.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting under sections 4 and 5
main_sections.description: Provides protection from suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under sections 4 and 5, requiring previous sanction from the Central Government for such proceedings.
Repeals the Punjab Disturbed Areas Ordinance, 1983 (5 of 1983) and states that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any Magistrate or Police Officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector may, after giving due warning, fire upon or use force (even to the causing of death) against persons contravening orders prohibiting assemblies of five or more persons or the carrying of weapons, ammunition, or explosives in a disturbed area for the maintenance of public order.

Rule 2: Any Magistrate or Police Officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector may destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, shelters used for armed attacks, training camps for armed volunteers, or hide-outs used by armed gangs or absconders, if deemed necessary.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrates and Police Officers (specifically those not below the rank of Sub-Inspector, or Havildar in the Armed Branch for section 4).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of powers to use force, including lethal force, and to destroy property as outlined in sections 4 and 5.

rights: Right of individuals to be subject to lawful orders in disturbed areas.
Right of law enforcement to use necessary force to maintain public order.
duties: Duty of individuals to comply with orders prohibiting assembly of five or more persons in disturbed areas.
Duty of individuals to not carry prohibited weapons, ammunition, or explosives in disturbed areas.
Duty of State Government to maintain public order.
obligations: Obligation to obtain previous sanction from the Central Government for legal proceedings against persons acting under sections 4 and 5.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Declaration of a 'disturbed area' by the State Government through notification in the Official Gazette.
Procedure 2: Use of force, including lethal force, by authorized officers after due warning against persons contravening specific orders in a disturbed area.
Procedure 3: Destruction of specified structures and caches by authorized officers if deemed necessary.
Procedure 4: Requirement of Central Government sanction before initiating legal proceedings against individuals for actions taken under sections 4 and 5.
administration: State Government (for declaring disturbed areas) and Central Government (for sanctioning legal proceedings).
important_notes: The Act retroactively came into force on October 7, 1983.
Protection is afforded to persons acting under sections 4 and 5, requiring prior Central Government sanction for any legal proceedings against them.
The Act repeals and replaces the Punjab Disturbed Areas Ordinance, 1983.

title: The Chandigarh Disturbed Areas Act, 1983
purpose: To make better provision for the suppression of disorder and for the restoration and maintenance of public order in disturbed areas in Chandigarh.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Chandigarh. Specifically deals with areas declared as 'disturbed areas'.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh appointed under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.disturbed_area: An area which is for the time being declared by notification under section 3 to be a disturbed area.

main_sections.description: States the name of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Union territory of Chandigarh), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on October 7, 1983).
Defines key terms used in the Act, namely 'Administrator' and 'disturbed area'.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to declare areas to be disturbed areas
main_sections.description: Grants the Administrator the power to declare any part or the whole of the Union territory of Chandigarh as a disturbed area through a notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Power to fire upon persons contravening certain orders
main_sections.description: Empowers a Magistrate or a Police Officer (not below Sub-Inspector or Havildar in the Armed Branch) to use force, including firing which may cause death, after giving due warning, against persons contravening laws or orders in a disturbed area that prohibit assemblies of five or more persons or the carrying of weapons.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to destroy arms dump, fortified positions, etc.
main_sections.description: Authorizes a Magistrate or Police Officer (not below Sub-Inspector) to destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, shelters from which armed attacks are made, or structures used as training camps for armed volunteers or hide-outs by armed gangs or absconders.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting under sections 4 and 5
main_sections.description: Provides protection to individuals acting under the powers granted in sections 4 and 5. No legal proceedings can be instituted against them without the previous sanction of the Central Government.

Repeals the Chandigarh Disturbed Areas Ordinance, 1983, and states that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: In a disturbed area, a Magistrate or Police Officer can fire upon persons contravening laws or orders prohibiting assemblies of five or more persons or carrying weapons, after giving due warning. Such force can extend to causing death.
Rule 2: A Magistrate or Police Officer can destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, shelters used for armed attacks, training camps for armed volunteers, or hide-outs of armed gangs or absconders.

penalties: While specific penalties for contravening orders are not detailed in the provided text, section 4 implies that actions leading to the use of force, including causing death, can result from contraventions.
No explicit mention of fines or imprisonment for specific offenses under this Act is present in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrates and Police Officers (not below the rank of Sub-Inspector, or Havildar in the Armed Branch for section 4).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the use of force, including firing, to suppress disorder and maintain public order. Destruction of illicit arms dumps and fortified positions.

rights: Right to be warned before force is used (as per section 4).
Protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under sections 4 and 5 (requiring Central Government sanction).
duties: Duty of law enforcement to maintain public order.
Duty to comply with orders prohibiting assemblies and carrying of weapons in disturbed areas.
obligations: Obligation of the Administrator to declare disturbed areas.
Obligation to obtain Central Government sanction before instituting legal proceedings against persons acting under sections 4 and 5.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Declaration of a disturbed area - The Administrator issues a notification in the Official Gazette declaring a specific area as disturbed.

Procedure 2: Use of force - A Magistrate or Police Officer assesses the necessity for public order, gives warning if feasible, and then fires upon or uses force against persons contravening specific orders.
Procedure 3: Destruction of illegal assets - A Magistrate or Police Officer assesses the necessity and proceeds to destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, etc.
Procedure 4: Legal Protection - To institute legal proceedings against individuals acting under sections 4 and 5, prior sanction from the Central Government must be obtained.
administration: The Administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh, with oversight and sanctioning power from the Central Government for legal proceedings.
important_notes: The Act is retrospective, having come into force on October 7, 1983.
The Act repeals the Chandigarh Disturbed Areas Ordinance, 1983, but actions taken under the ordinance are saved.
Protection for those acting under sections 4 and 5 is granted by the Central Government, not solely by the Administrator or local authorities, indicating a higher level of review for such actions.

title: THE ILLEGAL MIGRANTS (DETERMINATION BY TRIBUNALS) ACT, 1983
purpose: To provide for the establishment of Tribunals for the determination, in a fair manner, of the question whether a person is an illegal migrant to enable the Central Government to expel illegal migrants from India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Specifically addresses illegal migrants who entered India on or after March 25, 1971, without valid travel documents or authority. The Act was initially focused on Assam and could be extended to other states.

key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: An Appellate Tribunal established by the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 15.
key_definitions.foreigner: Has the same meaning as in the Foreigners Act, 1946 (31 of 1946).
key_definitions.illegal migrant: A person who entered India on or after March 25, 1971, is a foreigner, and entered without a valid passport, travel document, or other lawful authority.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Tribunal: A Tribunal established by the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 5.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and commencement dates (deemed to be October 15, 1983, in Assam, and other dates for other states as notified).

Excludes certain categories of persons from the Act's purview, including those expelled before the Act's commencement, those detected as foreigners at entry, and those who overstayed their valid visa.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act and specifies how references to laws in force in certain areas should be construed.

States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything contained in other related Acts such as the Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920, the Foreigners Act, 1946, the Immigrants (Expulsion from Assam) Act, 1950, or the Passports Act, 1967.

Empowers the Central Government to establish Tribunals, specifies qualification for members (must be or have been a District Judge or Additional District Judge), and states that each Tribunal shall consist of two members, one of whom is the Chairman.
Details the process for referring questions of illegal migration to Tribunals. The Central Government can refer such questions, and individuals can also make applications to the Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of the question as to whether a person is an illegal migrant
main_sections.description: Outlines the process by which the Tribunal determines if a person is an illegal migrant.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders made by a Tribunal.
Deals with the expulsion of persons determined to be illegal migrants.
Specifies the penalties for offenses under the Act.

important_rules: A person is considered an illegal migrant if they entered India on or after March 25, 1971, are a foreigner, and entered without a valid passport, travel document, or lawful authority.
Tribunals are to be established by the Central Government, and their members must be qualified as District Judges or Additional District Judges.
The Act overrides provisions of other existing laws related to foreigners and passports.
References or applications to Tribunals must be made to the Tribunal within whose jurisdiction the person in question resides or is found.
Tribunals have the same powers as civil courts in matters of summoning witnesses, discovery of documents, and evidence reception.

penalties: Section 25 outlines penalties for offenses under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Tribunals established under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of Tribunals to determine the status of illegal migrants, and subsequent orders for expulsion. The Act also grants Tribunals powers similar to civil courts for evidence gathering and witness examination.

rights: Right to have one's status as an illegal migrant determined by a Tribunal.
Right to appeal against the decision of a Tribunal.
Right to present a defense and evidence before a Tribunal.
duties: Individuals suspected of being illegal migrants have a duty to cooperate with Tribunal proceedings.
Individuals making applications to the Tribunal have a duty to provide truthful information and corroborating affidavits.
The Central Government has a duty to establish and support Tribunals.
obligations: Persons determined to be illegal migrants are obligated to be expelled from India.
Applicants to the Central Government for references under Section 8A are limited to making ten applications or declarations.

key_procedures: Reference of a question regarding illegal migration by the Central Government to a Tribunal.
Application to a Tribunal by an individual for a decision on another person's illegal migrant status.
Issuance of notice by the Tribunal to the person in question, accompanied by a copy of the reference or application.
Submission of representation and evidence by the person in question within a specified period.
Determination of the question by the Tribunal based on evidence and representations.
Appeal against a Tribunal's order to an Appellate Tribunal.
Expulsion of persons confirmed as illegal migrants.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for establishing and overseeing the Tribunals and implementing the Act's provisions. The Act also mentions the possibility of rule-making powers under Section 28.
important_notes: The Act was struck down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarbananda Sonowal vs Union of India in December 2006.
The Act initially came into force in Assam on October 15, 1983, and could be extended to other states via notification.
Specific limitations apply to the number of applications or declarations a person can make under Section 8A.

title: THE PUBLIC FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS (OBLIGATION AS TO FIDELITY AND SECRECY) ACT, 1983
purpose: To provide for the obligation of public financial institutions as to fidelity and secrecy.
scope: Applies to public financial institutions as defined in the Act, their directors, members of committees, auditors, officers, and other employees. It also covers the information and affairs of their constituents.

key_definitions.public financial institution: Includes the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Limited, the Industrial Reconstruction Corporation of India Limited, and any other institution specified by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette, provided it is a company as defined in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956, or to which the provisions of section 619 of that Act apply. This definition is subject to modifications by subsequent legislation (e.g., Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005).
key_definitions.credit information: Has the same meaning as in clause (c) of section 45A of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, with the modification that 'banking company' refers to a bank listed in clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 3 of this Act or a public financial institution.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Public Financial Institutions (Obligation as to Fidelity and Secrecy) Act, 1983.

Defines 'public financial institution' and outlines the process for issuing and laying before Parliament notifications to specify such institutions. It also explains the meaning of 'credit information' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation as to fidelity and secrecy
main_sections.description: Stipulates that public financial institutions shall not divulge information relating to their constituents' affairs, except when legally permitted or customary among bankers. It also allows for the collection and furnishing of credit information and other useful information to the Central Government, specified banks, or other public financial institutions for efficient discharge of functions. This section is subject to exceptions under other laws, including the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005.

Requires every director, committee member, auditor, officer, or other employee of a public financial institution to make a declaration of fidelity and secrecy in the form prescribed in the Schedule, either before entering upon duties or within thirty days of the Act's applicability to the institution.
This section, relating to amendments to Act 15 of 1948, has been repealed.
This section, relating to amendments to Act 63 of 1951, has been repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: Public financial institutions must not divulge information about their constituents' affairs unless legally required, customary among bankers, or for specific purposes outlined in the Act.

Rule 2: Public financial institutions may exchange credit and other relevant information with the Central Government, specified banks, and other public financial institutions for efficient functioning.

Rule 3: All personnel (directors, officers, employees, etc.) of a public financial institution must make a declaration of fidelity and secrecy before assuming duties or within a specified period after the Act becomes applicable.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but implied to be related to the governance and oversight of public financial institutions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied through the requirement of declarations and the general legal framework governing financial institutions.

rights: Right of public financial institutions to collect and furnish credit and other information to specified entities for efficient discharge of functions.
duties: Duty of public financial institutions to maintain fidelity and secrecy regarding constituent affairs.
Duty of personnel to make declarations of fidelity and secrecy.
obligations: Obligation of public financial institutions to adhere to the fidelity and secrecy provisions, except where legally exempted or customary.
Obligation of personnel to make the prescribed declaration.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Specification of a public financial institution: The Central Government may notify an institution as a public financial institution by publishing in the Official Gazette. Such notifications must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

Procedure 2: Declaration of fidelity and secrecy: Relevant personnel must make this declaration in the specified format, either before starting work or within 30 days of the Act's application to their institution.
administration: The Central Government is involved in specifying public financial institutions and receiving information, and Parliament is involved in reviewing notifications.
important_notes: Note 1: Section 3(3) explicitly states that the provisions of section 3 do not apply to credit information disclosed under the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005.
Note 2: Sections 5 and 6, which dealt with amendments to other Acts, have been repealed.

title: The Asiatic Society Act, 1984
purpose: To declare the institution known as the Asiatic Society as an institution of national importance and to provide for certain matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the Asiatic Society, with its registered office in Calcutta, and its administration, functions, and financial matters.

key_definitions.memorandum: The memorandum of association of the Society.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Includes any rule or regulation (by whatever name called) which the Society is competent to make under the West Bengal Societies Registration Act, 1961, but excludes bye-laws or standing orders for day-to-day administration.
key_definitions.Society: The Asiatic Society, a society within the meaning of the West Bengal Societies Registration Act, 1961, and having its registered office in Calcutta.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and the date of commencement, which is to be appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Asiatic Society as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Asiatic Society, founded by William Jones on January 15, 1784, as an institution of national importance.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'memorandum', 'prescribed', 'regulations', and 'Society'.

main_sections.section_title: Grants, loans, etc., by Central Government to Society
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to provide grants, loans, or other financial assistance to the Society to enable it to discharge its functions efficiently, particularly in areas of research, literary, library, scientific, museological activities, collection of manuscripts, coins, art objects, and publication.

Mandates the Society to maintain proper accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts approved by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG). The accounts are to be audited by the CAG, who has similar rights and authorities as in the audit of Government accounts. The certified accounts and audit report are to be laid before Parliament.
Requires the Society to furnish an annual report on its activities, policies, and programmes to the Central Government, which shall be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Prior approval of Central Government necessary for certain action by Society
main_sections.description: Stipulates that the Society requires prior approval from the Central Government for actions such as altering its purposes, amalgamating, altering its memorandum or regulations, selling property acquired with specific Central Government funds (with exceptions for movable property), or dissolution.

Allows the Central Government to establish a Planning Board for the Society to advise on developmental programmes and other related matters. The Board consists of a Chairman and other members appointed by the Central Government and can regulate its own procedure.

Empowers the Central Government to constitute committees to prepare and submit programmes of work and financial estimates for the Society, and to settle broad lines of programmes. The Society must provide reasons if it disagrees with suggested work. Committees' procedures and member allowances are to be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Review of work done, inspection of assets, etc.
main_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to constitute a committee to review the Society's work, inspect assets, evaluate performance, and advise the Government. The Society must be given notice of such reviews and has the right to appoint a representative. If the Society fails to take satisfactory action based on reports, the Central Government may issue directions.

main_sections.section_title: Society to afford facilities to Committees
main_sections.description: Obligates the Society to provide all necessary facilities to the Planning Board and any committees constituted under sections 9 and 10.

main_sections.section_title: Power to issue directions to Society
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Society, including directions to amend its memorandum or regulations, or to prioritize its work. These directions have overriding effect.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to assume functions of control
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to take over the management of the Society or its activities for a period not exceeding two years if the Society defaults in giving effect to directions, or if its Council exceeds or abuses its powers. This involves appointing persons to manage the Society and vacating offices of existing Council members.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in the Society's memorandum, regulations, the West Bengal Societies Registration Act, 1961, or any other law.
Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, including rules regarding procedures for the Planning Board, committees, and other related matters.

important_rules: The Society shall maintain proper accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts in a form approved by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (Section 5(1)).
The accounts of the Society shall be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (Section 5(2)).
The Society shall furnish its annual report to the Central Government (Section 6).
The Society shall not alter its purposes, amalgamate, alter its memorandum or regulations, sell specified property, or be dissolved without the prior approval of the Central Government (Section 7).
The Society must afford all necessary facilities to the Planning Board and committees constituted under the Act (Section 11).
The Society must comply with directions issued by the Central Government, which may include amendments to its memorandum or regulations (Section 12).
The Society must show cause against the assumption of control by the Central Government if it defaults on directions or if its Council exceeds its powers (Section 13(1)).

penalties: If the Society defaults in giving effect to directions or if its Council exceeds its powers, the Central Government may assume control of the Society's management or activities (Section 13). This would result in the vacation of offices of Council members and the appointment of persons to manage the Society.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders, directions, appointment of committees and boards, and assumption of control of the Society's management or activities.

rights: The Society has the right to appoint a representative who shall have the right to be present and be heard during reviews, inspections, or evaluations conducted by committees (Section 10(4)).
The Society has the right to present explanations or make representations before the Central Government when the Government considers taking action based on review reports (Section 10(6)).
duties: The Society is duty-bound to maintain proper accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts (Section 5(1)).
The Society must furnish an annual report to the Central Government (Section 6).

The Society must obtain prior approval from the Central Government for significant actions like altering its purposes, amalgamating, altering its memorandum or regulations, or disposing of certain properties (Section 7).
The Society must afford all necessary facilities to the Planning Board and committees (Section 11).
The Society must comply with directions issued by the Central Government (Section 12).
obligations: The Society is obligated to be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (Section 5(2)).
The Society is obligated to provide reasons to the Central Government if it disagrees with undertaking work suggested by a committee (Section 9(3)).
The Society is obligated to respond to show cause notices issued by the Central Government before control is assumed (Section 13(1)).

key_procedures: Establishment of a Planning Board by the Central Government through notification, with appointment of Chairman and members (Section 8).
Constitution of committees by the Central Government through notification for specific duties like preparing work programs and financial estimates (Section 9).
Conduct of reviews, inspections, and evaluations by committees appointed by the Central Government, with notice to the Society and the right of representation for the Society (Section 10).
Issuance of directions by the Central Government to the Society, with reasons to be recorded and communicated (Section 12).

Process for the Central Government to assume control of the Society: issuing a show cause notice, and if not satisfied, publishing an order in the Official Gazette appointing persons to manage the Society or its activities (Section 13).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions will prevail over any inconsistent provisions in the Society's memorandum, regulations, the West Bengal Societies Registration Act, 1961, or any other law (Section 14).
The commencement date of the Act is to be notified by the Central Government (Section 1(2)).
Certain movable property or classes of movable property may be exempted from the requirement of Central Government approval for sale or disposal (Section 7 proviso).

title: THE FAMILY COURTS ACT, 1984
purpose: To provide for the establishment of Family Courts with a view to promote conciliation in, and secure speedy settlement of, disputes relating to marriage and family affairs and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India (excluding Jammu and Kashmir prior to its reorganization, and now applicable to the Union Territory of Ladakh as well). It establishes Family Courts for areas with a population exceeding one million and potentially for other areas deemed necessary by the State Government. It covers suits and proceedings related to marriage, matrimonial status, family property, marital relationships, legitimacy, maintenance, and child custody.

key_definitions.Judge: Means the Judge or, as the case may be, the Principal Judge, Additional Principal Judge or other Judge of a Family Court.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Family Court: Means a Family Court established under section 3.
key_definitions.Code of Civil Procedure, 1908: Other words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, shall have their meanings as assigned in that Code.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date which can be appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Judge', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'Family Court'.

Mandates the establishment of Family Courts for areas with a population exceeding one million and allows for their establishment in other areas. It also specifies the State Government's role in defining the local limits of jurisdiction after consulting the High Court.

Details the process for appointing Judges to Family Courts, including qualifications, the appointment of Principal and Additional Principal Judges, and provisions for distribution of business. It emphasizes selecting individuals committed to marriage and child welfare, with a preference for women. It also sets an age limit for Judges.

Outlines the jurisdiction of Family Courts, including civil jurisdiction over marriage-related disputes (nullity, restitution, separation, dissolution, matrimonial property, injunctions, legitimacy, custody, access) and the jurisdiction of a First Class Magistrate under the CrPC for maintenance. It also allows for conferring other jurisdictions.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Family Court to make efforts for settlement
main_sections.description: Mandates that Family Courts, in the first instance, endeavor to assist parties in reaching a settlement through conciliation and persuasion. It allows for adjournment of proceedings to facilitate settlement attempts.

States that the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other applicable laws will govern suits and proceedings before Family Courts, treating them as civil courts. For proceedings under Chapter IX of the CrPC, the provisions of that Code apply.
Provides for the right to appeal against judgments and orders of the Family Court.
Declares that this Act will have an overriding effect over other laws in force regarding matters covered by this Act.

important_rules: Family Courts must first attempt to assist parties in reaching a settlement in any suit or proceeding.
If there's a possibility of settlement, the court may adjourn proceedings to enable such attempts.
The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other relevant laws apply to proceedings before Family Courts, which are deemed civil courts.
Family Courts exercise jurisdiction equivalent to District Courts and subordinate civil courts for specified family law matters.
Family Courts also exercise the jurisdiction of a First Class Magistrate regarding maintenance orders under the CrPC.
Judges of Family Courts must have at least seven years of judicial office experience or be advocates of a High Court.
Preference in selecting Judges shall be given to women.
Individuals appointed as Judges must not have attained the age of sixty-two years.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Governments, in consultation with the High Courts, are responsible for establishing Family Courts, appointing Judges, and making necessary rules for their functioning.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of Family Courts, appointment of qualified Judges, and adherence to the procedures outlined in the Act and applicable civil and criminal codes. The Act's overriding effect ensures its provisions are prioritized.

rights: Right to seek remedies through Family Courts for marriage and family disputes.
Right to appeal judgments and orders of the Family Court.
Right to legal representation (implied by the procedures and nature of the courts).
duties: Duty of the Family Court to endeavor to promote settlement and conciliation.
Duty of the State Government to establish Family Courts and appoint Judges.
Duty of the Central Government to make rules for the Act.

key_procedures: Establishment of Family Courts in areas with significant population, after consultation with the High Court.
Appointment of Judges based on specific qualifications and experience, with emphasis on conciliation skills and preference for women.
Initial efforts by the Family Court to facilitate settlement and conciliation between parties.
Adjournment of proceedings if there's a reasonable possibility of settlement.
Application of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other relevant laws to Family Court proceedings.
Transfer of pending suits and proceedings to the established Family Court upon its constitution.
administration: State Governments (for establishment and appointment), High Courts (for consultation and rules), Central Government (for rules and prescribing qualifications).
important_notes: The Act was amended to omit references to the State of Jammu and Kashmir and to include the Union Territory of Ladakh.
Different dates can be appointed for the commencement of the Act in different States.
The Act aims to promote conciliation and speedy settlement, indicating a focus on non-adversarial dispute resolution within family matters.

title: The Calcutta Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Temporary Provisions Act, 1985
purpose: To make temporary provisions for the operation and maintenance of the Calcutta metro railway and for matters connected therewith, pending the making of regular arrangements for such operation and maintenance.
scope: Applies to the metropolitan city of Calcutta. Covers the operation and maintenance of the Calcutta metro railway, including passenger carriage, safety, and offenses. It also incorporates provisions from the Indian Railways Act, 1890, and the Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978.

key_definitions.calcutta_metro_railway_administration: The General Manager of the metro railway appointed under section 3 of the Construction Act.
key_definitions.commissioner: A commissioner of the metro railway appointed under section 27 of the Construction Act.
key_definitions.construction_act: The Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978 (33 of 1978).
key_definitions.metro_railway: Such portion of the metro railway constructed in the metropolitan city of Calcutta under the provisions of the Construction Act as may, for the time being, be available for public carriage of passengers. This definition also includes associated land, rails, stations, offices, and other infrastructure.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it is deemed to have come into force on October 22, 1984, and specifies that it applies to the metropolitan city of Calcutta.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Calcutta metro railway administration', 'commissioner', 'Construction Act', 'metro railway', and 'prescribed'. It also states that undefined terms shall have meanings assigned in the Indian Railways Act, 1890, or the Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978.

main_sections.section_title: Calcutta metro railway administration to be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the metro railway
main_sections.description: Establishes that the Calcutta metro railway administration is responsible for the operation and maintenance of the metro railway. It also allows the administration to appoint necessary officers and employees.

main_sections.section_title: Previous sanction of the Central Government required for the opening of metro railway
main_sections.description: Requires previous sanction from the Central Government before the metro railway can be opened for public carriage of passengers. The Central Government must be satisfied about public safety after considering the commissioner's report and other factors. Sanction can be absolute or conditional.
Prohibits passengers from carrying goods other than personal belongings within a prescribed volume and weight. Those contravening this can be removed from the train.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of compartments for females not necessary
main_sections.description: States that it is not necessary for the metro railway administration to reserve compartments for the exclusive use of females.

Prohibits the taking or causing to be taken of dangerous or offensive goods upon the metro railway. Metro railway officials may open packages to ascertain contents if they have reason to believe such goods are present.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for taking or causing to take offensive or dangerous goods upon the metro railway
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for carrying offensive goods (fine up to 500 rupees) and dangerous goods (imprisonment up to 4 years and fine up to 5000 rupees). It also makes the offender responsible for any loss, injury, or damage caused by such goods.
Prohibits smoking in compartments, carriages, or underground stations. Penalties include a fine up to 250 rupees, and persistent offenders can be removed.

main_sections.section_title: Drunkenness or nuisance upon the metro railway
main_sections.description: Punishes intoxication, nuisance, indecency, or abusive language on the metro railway with a fine up to 250 rupees, forfeiture of fare/ticket, or removal. Intoxicated metro railway officials on duty face fines or imprisonment up to 2 years, or both, if safety is endangered.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of demonstrations upon the metro railway
main_sections.description: Prohibits demonstrations on the metro railway premises and allows exclusion of participants. It also prohibits unauthorized posting of posters or writing/drawing on premises. Contravention can lead to imprisonment up to 3 months, fine up to 500 rupees, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for travelling on roof, etc., of a train
main_sections.description: Penalizes travelling on the roof of a train or in unauthorized parts, or projecting body parts out of a train, with imprisonment up to 1 month, fine up to 50 rupees, or both, and removal from the train.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for unlawfully entering or remaining upon the metro railway or walking on the metro railway line
main_sections.description: Penalizes unlawful entry/remaining on metro railway premises with imprisonment up to 3 months, fine up to 250 rupees, or both. Walking on the metro railway line without authority incurs imprisonment up to 6 months, fine up to 500 rupees, or both.

Penalizes metro railway officials on duty who endanger passenger safety through rash/negligent acts or omissions, or by disobeying rules, with imprisonment up to 5 years, fine up to 6000 rupees, or both.

Penalizes metro railway officials on duty entrusted with running trains/rolling stock who abandon their duty before reaching the destination without authority or proper handover, with imprisonment up to 4 years, fine up to 5000 rupees, or both.

Penalizes obstruction of trains or rolling stock through squatting, picketing, unauthorized keeping of rolling stock, tampering with signaling, or interfering with mechanisms, with removal and imprisonment up to 4 years, fine up to 5000 rupees, or both.

Holds companies and individuals responsible for the company's business liable for offences committed by the company, unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence. Directors, managers, or officers are also liable if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act 9 of 1890 and the rules, etc., made thereunder to the metro railway
main_sections.description: States that the Indian Railways Act, 1890, and rules made thereunder apply to the metro railway.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of Act and rules, etc., inconsistent with other enactments
main_sections.description: Specifies that this Act and any rules made under it will have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in other enactments.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Protects persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder from legal proceedings.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, subject to parliamentary approval.
Repeals the Calcutta Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Ordinance, 1984, and provides for savings.

important_rules: Rule: No person shall smoke in any compartment or carriage of the metro railway or in any underground metro railway station. (Section 9(1))
Rule: No person shall take or cause to be taken any dangerous or offensive goods upon the metro railway. (Section 7(1))
Rule: No person shall carry goods other than personal belongings not exceeding prescribed volume and weight while travelling on the metro railway. (Section 5(1))
Rule: No demonstration of any kind shall be held on any part of the metro railway or other premises thereof. (Section 11(1))
Rule: Metro railway officials on duty must not endanger the safety of passengers through rash or negligent acts or omissions, or by disobeying orders. (Section 14)

penalties: Fine up to 500 rupees for taking offensive goods.
Imprisonment up to 4 years and fine up to 5000 rupees for taking dangerous goods.
Fine up to 250 rupees for smoking in prohibited areas.
Fine up to 250 rupees, forfeiture of fare/ticket, or removal for drunkenness or nuisance.
Imprisonment up to 2 years, fine up to 500 rupees, or both, for intoxicated metro railway officials on duty if safety is endangered.
Imprisonment up to 3 months, fine up to 500 rupees, or both, for contravening demonstration prohibition or unauthorized writing/drawing.
Imprisonment up to 1 month, fine up to 50 rupees, or both, for travelling on the roof or unauthorized parts of a train.
Imprisonment up to 3 months, fine up to 250 rupees, or both, for unlawful entry or remaining on metro railway premises.
Imprisonment up to 6 months, fine up to 500 rupees, or both, for walking on the metro railway line without authority.
Imprisonment up to 5 years, fine up to 6000 rupees, or both, for metro railway officials endangering passenger safety.
Imprisonment up to 4 years, fine up to 5000 rupees, or both, for metro railway officials abandoning duty without authority.
Imprisonment up to 4 years, fine up to 5000 rupees, or both, for obstructing running of trains or tampering with signaling.
Companies and their responsible individuals are liable for offences committed by the company.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Metro railway officials authorized by the metro railway administration.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through fines, imprisonment, removal from trains/premises, forfeiture of fares/tickets, and legal proceedings as prescribed for various offences.

rights: Right to travel on the metro railway with personal belongings within prescribed limits.
Right to expect safe operation and maintenance of the metro railway.
Protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
duties: Duty to comply with provisions regarding carriage of goods, dangerous goods, smoking, and behaviour on the metro railway.
Duty to obey metro railway officials and desist from prohibited activities when warned.
Duty of metro railway administration to ensure operation and maintenance of the metro railway.
Duty of metro railway officials to perform duties without endangering passengers.
obligations: Obligation to obtain Central Government sanction for opening the metro railway for public carriage.
Obligation to adhere to any conditions imposed by the Central Government for the opening of the metro railway.
Obligation of companies and their responsible officers to prevent and report offences.

key_procedures: Procedure: Obtaining Central Government sanction for opening the metro railway, involving review of commissioner's report and assessment of public safety. (Section 4)
Procedure: Removal of passengers contravening goods carriage rules by authorized metro railway officials. (Section 5(2))
Procedure: Opening of packages by metro railway officials to ascertain contents if dangerous or offensive goods are suspected. (Section 7(2))
Procedure: Warning and removal of passengers persisting in smoking by metro railway officials. (Section 9(3))
Procedure: Removal of individuals committing nuisance or engaging in prohibited activities by metro railway officials. (Sections 10(1), 11(2), 12)
Procedure: Legal proceedings and punishment for various offences as defined in Chapters III and IV.
administration: Calcutta metro railway administration, with oversight and rule-making powers vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: Note: This Act is temporary and intended to bridge the period until regular arrangements for operation and maintenance are made.
Note: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from October 22, 1984.
Note: Provisions of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, and the Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978, are applicable where not explicitly contradicted by this Act.

title: THE BHOPAL GAS LEAK DISASTER (PROCESSING OF CLAIMS) ACT, 1985
purpose: To confer certain powers on the Central Government to secure that claims arising out of, or connected with, the Bhopal gas leak disaster are dealt with speedily, effectively, equitably and to the best advantage of the claimants and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to claims arising out of, or connected with, the Bhopal gas leak disaster which occurred on the 2nd and 3rd days of December, 1984. It covers claims for compensation or damages for loss of life, personal injury, damage to property, expenses incurred for containing or mitigating the disaster, and any other connected claims, including loss of business or employment. The Act's provisions apply within India and potentially outside India for purposes of claim representation.

key_definitions.bhopal_gas_leak_disaster: The occurrence on December 2nd and 3rd, 1984, involving the release of highly noxious and abnormally dangerous gas from a Union Carbide India Limited plant in Bhopal, resulting in extensive loss of life and damage to property.
key_definitions.claim: Includes claims for compensation or damages for loss of life or personal injury, damage to property, expenses for disaster containment/mitigation, and any other claims connected to the disaster, such as loss of business or employment. For deaths, claims are for the benefit of the spouse, children, and other heirs.
key_definitions.claimant: A person entitled to make a claim.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it is deemed to have come into force on February 20, 1985.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Bhopal gas leak disaster', 'claim', 'claimant', 'Commissioner', 'person', and 'Scheme'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to represent claimants
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the exclusive right to represent and act in place of claimants for all purposes connected with their claims, including instituting or withdrawing legal proceedings and entering into compromises. This power extends to claims for which proceedings were already instituted before the Act's commencement, with provisions for representation alongside claimants in foreign courts.

main_sections.section_title: Claimant’s right to be represented by a legal practitioner
main_sections.description: Ensures that the Central Government, while representing claimants, will consider their specific requirements and permit a legal practitioner of the claimant's choice to be associated in proceedings, at the claimant's expense.

Confers upon the Central Government the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for matters like summoning persons, examining them on oath, requiring discovery of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, requisitioning public records, issuing commissions, and other matters specified by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Commissioner and other officers and employees
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner and other officers and employees to assist in discharging its functions. The Commissioner will perform functions assigned by the Scheme, and along with subordinate officers, can exercise powers similar to the Central Government under section 5. Government officers are to aid the Commissioner. The Commissioner and authorized subordinate officers are deemed civil courts for certain criminal procedure purposes.

Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act (except the power to frame a Scheme) to the Government of Madhya Pradesh or designated officers of the Central or State Government, subject to specified conditions and limitations.

Specifies that any period after a claim is registered under the Scheme will be excluded when computing the limitation period for instituting suits or proceedings for claim enforcement. This exclusion does not apply to appeal proceedings.

Mandates the Central Government to frame a Scheme for carrying into effect the purposes of the Act. The Scheme can cover various matters including claim registration, processing, record maintenance, creation of a fund for administration, crediting and utilizing funds received in satisfaction of claims, appointment of officers for disbursal, and maintenance of accounts.

Clarifies that any sums paid by the Government to a claimant otherwise than as final disbursal of compensation will not prejudice the claimant's right to receive full compensation from adjudication or settlement. It also states that such prior payments will be deducted from the final disbursal.
Declares that the provisions of this Act and any Scheme framed thereunder will have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other enactment or instrument.

Repeals the Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster (Processing of Claims) Ordinance, 1985. It also provides that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The Central Government has the exclusive right to represent and act in place of all claimants for all purposes related to their claims.

The Central Government shall consider the claimant's requirements when representing them and permit a legal practitioner of the claimant's choice to be associated in proceedings at the claimant's expense.
Claims registered under the Scheme will have the period after registration excluded for computing the limitation period for enforcement proceedings.
The Central Government must frame a Scheme for the processing of claims and related matters, which will have an overriding effect on other laws.
Sums paid by the Government to a claimant before final disbursal will be deducted from the final compensation received.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Commissioner, and other appointed officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers conferred on the Central Government (including civil court powers), the Scheme framed under the Act, delegation of powers to state governments/officers, and the Commissioner and subordinate officers who are deemed civil courts for certain criminal procedural purposes.

rights: Claimants have the right to have their claims processed speedily, effectively, and equitably.
Claimants have the right to have a legal practitioner of their choice associated in the conduct of proceedings, at their expense.
Claimants are entitled to compensation or damages for losses arising from the disaster.
duties: The Central Government has the duty to represent claimants and process their claims.
The Central Government has the duty to frame a Scheme for processing claims.
Government officers and authorities have the duty to act in aid of the Commissioner.
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to ensure claims are dealt with to the best advantage of the claimants.
Claimants have an obligation to register their claims under the Scheme.
The Central Government has an obligation to consult claimant's requirements when representing them.

key_procedures: Claim Registration: Claims are to be registered under the provisions of the Scheme framed by the Central Government. This is a prerequisite for applying the special limitation provisions.
Claim Processing: The Scheme will provide for the processing of claims to secure their enforcement.
Representation by Central Government: The Central Government shall exclusively represent claimants in all claim-related matters, including legal proceedings and compromises.

Association of Legal Practitioner: Upon claimant's request, the Central Government shall permit a legal practitioner of the claimant's choice to be associated in proceedings at the claimant's expense.

Scheme Notification and Laying Before Parliament: Any Scheme framed by the Central Government must be notified in the Official Gazette and laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, with provisions for modification or annulment by Parliament.
administration: Central Government, with assistance from the Commissioner and other appointed officers and employees. Powers can also be delegated to the Government of Madhya Pradesh or its officers.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.
The Act and its Schemes apply notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other enactment.
The provisions related to the Commissioner's powers in relation to criminal procedure apply as amended in 1992.

title: The Handlooms (Reservation of Articles for Production) Act, 1985
purpose: To provide for the reservation of certain articles for exclusive production by handlooms and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to the production of articles by handlooms and other looms.

key_definitions.handloom: Any loom, other than a power loom.
key_definitions.power_loom: A loom which is worked by power as defined in clause (g) of section 2 of the Factories Act, 1948 (63 of 1948).
key_definitions.producer: A person engaged in the production of cloth on any loom, other than a handloom, and includes a person who owns, works or operates on a loom for the production of cloth.
key_definitions.processor: A person engaged in any ancillary process subsequent to the production of cloth, such as dyeing, bleaching, mercerising, calendering, embroidering, printing, raising, cloth embossing or any other finishing process, but does not include a producer.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date which is to be appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Advisory Committee', 'handloom', 'manufacturer', 'power loom', 'processor', and 'producer'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to specify articles for exclusive production by handlooms
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government, after considering recommendations from the Advisory Committee, to reserve any article or class of articles for exclusive production by handlooms through an order published in the Official Gazette. Such orders are subject to parliamentary approval.

Mandates the Central Government to constitute an Advisory Committee with persons having expertise to advise on matters related to reserving articles for handloom production. The committee considers factors like existing handloom production, employment generation, and protection of the handloom industry.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of production of articles exclusively reserved for handlooms
main_sections.description: States that once an article is reserved for exclusive handloom production, no other loom can be used for its production. However, it provides a three-month grace period for those already engaged in producing such articles on non-handlooms before the reservation date.

main_sections.section_title: Power to call for information or to furnish samples
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to require manufacturers to furnish information regarding their business activities or to provide samples of articles for inspection.

Authorizes officers appointed by the Central Government to enter any premises of a manufacturer, inspect records, and seek information related to the manufacture, storage, or sale of textile articles and power looms.

Empowers authorized officers to search and seize articles or power looms if there is a belief that they are being produced or are secreted in contravention of an order made under section 3, or are liable for forfeiture. It also allows seizure of relevant documents. Provisions for return of seized items and making copies of documents are included.

main_sections.section_title: Search and seizure to be made in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
main_sections.description: Specifies that search and seizure operations under this Act will be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
