main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of orders made under section 3
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravening orders made under section 3, including imprisonment, fine per loom, and forfeiture of the contravening articles or power looms to the Central Government.
Specifies penalties for making false statements or furnishing false information, or for damaging/destroying required samples or documents.
Deals with attempts to contravene or abetment of contravention of orders made under section 3, treating them as contraventions themselves.

Lays down provisions for offences committed by companies, making individuals in charge and responsible for the business liable, along with the company. It also includes liability for directors or officers if the offence is due to their consent, connivance, or neglect.
Declares all offences punishable under this Act as cognizable, notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act (except for making orders under sections 3, 18, and rules under section 19) to subordinate officers, State Governments, or their subordinate officers.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to State Governments as it considers necessary for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from legal proceedings for any action taken in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act.
Empowers the Central Government to exempt any article, class of articles, or any person or class of persons from any of the provisions of this Act, subject to conditions it may deem fit.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Articles reserved for exclusive production by handlooms cannot be produced by any other loom (Section 5).
Manufacturers must comply with orders to furnish information or samples (Section 6(2)).
Authorized officers can search premises and seize articles/power looms used in contravention of reservation orders (Section 8).
Searches and seizures must follow the procedures laid out in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 9).
Individuals and companies are liable for penalties if they contravene orders made under Section 3 (Sections 10, 13).
Making false statements or furnishing false information is punishable (Section 11).
Attempting to contravene or abetting contravention of orders is deemed a contravention (Section 12).

penalties: Imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five thousand rupees per loom, or both, for contravening Section 3 orders. Additional fine of up to five hundred rupees per loom per day for continuing contravention (Section 10(a)).
Forfeiture of contravened articles or power looms to the Central Government (Section 10(b)).
Imprisonment up to three months or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both, for false statements or failure to produce documents (Section 11).
Penalties as prescribed for offences committed by companies and their officers (Section 13).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and officers authorized by the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of inspection, search, seizure, calling for information and samples, and prosecution for contraventions. The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, is applicable to search and seizure procedures.

rights: Right to make copies or take extracts of seized documents in the presence of the authorized officer (Section 8(5)).
Right to apply to the Central Government for the return of seized documents/things if objecting to their retention (Section 8(6)).
Right to be heard by the Central Government before an order is passed regarding the return of seized documents/things (Section 8(7)).
Protection from liability for actions taken in good faith (Section 17).
duties: Manufacturers have a duty to comply with orders to furnish information or samples (Section 6(2)).
Manufacturers must cooperate with authorized officers during inspections (Section 7).
Individuals and companies have a duty to not contravene orders reserving articles for handloom production (Section 5, 10).
Individuals have a duty to not make false statements (Section 11).
obligations: Obligation to not produce reserved articles on non-handlooms, with a grace period for existing producers (Section 5).
Obligation to provide requested information and samples to the Central Government (Section 6).
Obligation to allow authorized officers to enter and inspect premises and records (Section 7).
Obligation for companies and their personnel to comply with the Act to prevent offences (Section 13).

key_procedures: Reservation of articles for handloom production: Central Government considers recommendations from an Advisory Committee and publishes an order in the Official Gazette. This order is laid before Parliament for potential modification or annulment (Section 3).
Information/Sample requests: Central Government issues an order requiring a manufacturer to provide specific information or samples within a stipulated period (Section 6).

Search and Seizure: An authorized officer with reason to believe a contravention has occurred or is imminent can search premises and seize articles, power looms, or documents. Procedures align with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Sections 8, 9).
Application for return of seized items: A person can apply to the Central Government to object to the retention of seized documents/things, requiring a hearing (Section 8(6), 8(7)).
administration: Central Government and its authorized officers, with provisions for delegation to State Governments or their officers.
important_notes: The Act overrides certain provisions of the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, concerning the reservation of articles for handlooms (Section 3(1)).
The Act specifies that all offences under it are cognizable (Section 14).
The Central Government has the power to exempt entities or activities from the Act's provisions (Section 18).

title: THE INTELLIGENCE ORGANISATIONS (RESTRICTION OF RIGHTS) ACT, 1985
purpose: To provide for the restriction of certain rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution in their application to the members of certain organisations established by the Central Government for purposes of intelligence or counter-intelligence so as to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline among them.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to members of Intelligence Organisations established by the Central Government for intelligence or counter-intelligence purposes, as specified in the Schedule.

key_definitions.Intelligence Organisation: Any organisation established by the Central Government for purposes of intelligence or counter-intelligence and specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.member of an Intelligence Organisation: Any person appointed to, or employed in, any Intelligence Organisation.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement through a Central Government notification.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Intelligence Organisation', 'member of an Intelligence Organisation', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions respecting right to form association, freedom of speech, etc.
main_sections.description: This section outlines specific restrictions on members of Intelligence Organisations regarding their right to form associations, freedom of speech, communication with the press, contact with external individuals on organizational matters, and use of the organisation's name.
This section specifies the penalty for contravening any provision of Section 3, which includes imprisonment up to two years, a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.
This section declares all offences punishable under Section 4 as cognizable, notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

This section empowers the Central Government to amend the Schedule by including or omitting organisations established for intelligence or counter-intelligence purposes. Such amendments are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
This section grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act. These rules must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for modification or annulment.

important_rules: Members of an Intelligence Organisation shall not be a member of, or be associated with, any trade union, labour union, or political association.
Members shall not be associated with any organisation not recognized by the Central Government as part of the Intelligence Organisation, or not of a purely social, recreational, or religious nature.
Members require prior permission from the head of the Intelligence Organisation to communicate with the press or publish any document.

Members are prohibited from contacting or communicating with any person on matters relating to the functioning, structure, personnel, or organizational affairs of their Intelligence Organisation, except for official duty.
Members cannot use the name of their Intelligence Organisation for unauthorized purposes.
Members are prohibited from participating in, addressing, or taking part in any political demonstrations or meetings organised by any body of persons for political or other prescribed purposes.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years.
Fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.
Both imprisonment and fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and implicitly the heads of the respective Intelligence Organisations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of penalties for contravention of Section 3. Offences are cognizable. Rules made under the Act will further detail enforcement mechanisms.

rights: Members retain rights not explicitly restricted by this Act, provided they do not contravene its provisions.
duties: To comply with the restrictions on association, speech, and communication outlined in Section 3.
To seek prior permission for communication with the press or publication of documents.
To use the organisation's name only for authorized purposes.
To maintain discipline within the organisation.
obligations: Members have an obligation to ensure their activities do not compromise the intelligence or counter-intelligence functions or the discipline of their organisation.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Central Government notification in the Official Gazette.
Amendment of the Schedule: Central Government notification in the Official Gazette, followed by laying before Parliament.
Making of Rules: Central Government notification in the Official Gazette, followed by laying before Parliament for potential modification or annulment.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The decision of the Central Government is final on whether a society, institution, association, or organisation is purely social, recreational, or religious.
The Act aims to ensure the proper discharge of duties and maintenance of discipline among members of intelligence and counter-intelligence organisations.

title: THE INLAND WATERWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA ACT, 1985
purpose: To provide for the constitution of an Authority for the regulation and development of inland waterways for purposes of shipping and navigation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to inland waterways in India. The scope includes regulation and development for shipping and navigation. It also extends to 'national waterways' as declared by law. The Authority is constituted to carry out these functions.

key_definitions.appurtenant_land: All lands appurtenant to a national waterway, whether demarcated or not.
key_definitions.authority: The Inland Waterways Authority of India constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.channel: Any waterway, whether natural or artificial.
key_definitions.conservancy: Includes dredging, training, closure, diversion or abandoning channels.
key_definitions.conservancy_measures: Measures for purposes of conservancy, but does not include measures for protection of banks against floods or for restricting banks which have become eroded mainly on account of reasons not connected with shipping and navigation.
key_definitions.infrastructure: Includes structures such as docks, wharves, jetties, landing stages, locks, buoys, inland ports, cargo handling equipment, road and rail access and cargo storage spaces.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Authority appointed under sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.national_waterway: The inland waterway declared by section 2 of the National Waterway (Allahabad -Haldia Stretch of the Ganga -Bhagirathi-Hooghly River) Act, 1982 (49 of 1982), to be a national waterway. Other waterways can also be declared national waterways by Parliament.
key_definitions.navigable_channel: A channel navigable during the whole or a part of the year.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Authority under this Act.
key_definitions.rules: Rules made by the Central Government under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the 'Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985' and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'appurtenant land', 'Authority', 'channel', 'conservancy', 'infrastructure', 'member', 'national waterway', 'navigable channel', 'prescribed', 'regulations', and 'rules'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of the Inland Waterways Authority of India
main_sections.description: Establishes the Inland Waterways Authority of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract. It also outlines the composition of the Authority (Chairman, Vice-Chairman, full-time and part-time members) appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Authority to act on business principles
main_sections.description: Mandates that the Authority shall, as far as possible, act on business principles in the discharge of its functions.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the Central Government to the Authority
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of assets, liabilities, contracts, and employees from the Central Government's Inland Water Transport Directorate to the newly constituted Authority.
Outlines the primary functions of the Inland Waterways Authority of India, which are related to the regulation and development of inland waterways for shipping and navigation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede the Authority
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to supersede the Authority under certain circumstances.
Confers the power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations for the efficient discharge of its functions.

important_rules: The Authority shall be constituted as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Authority shall consist of a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and a specified number of full-time and part-time members appointed by the Central Government.
The Authority shall act on business principles in discharging its functions.
Assets and liabilities of the Central Government related to the Inland Water Transport Directorate are transferred to the Authority.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Authority and to supersede the Authority if necessary.
The Central Government can make rules, and the Authority can make regulations, to carry out the Act's provisions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Inland Waterways Authority of India, under the overall supervision and direction of the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the functions and powers vested in the Authority, the ability to make regulations, and the power of the Central Government to issue directions and supersede the Authority.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right to contract and sue or be sued.
Right to associate with persons for advice.
Right to employ staff.
Right to levy and collect fees and charges.
Right to borrow money.
Right to receive grants and loans from the Central Government.
duties: To regulate and develop inland waterways for shipping and navigation.
To act on business principles.
To manage its finances, accounts, and undergo audit.
To submit an annual report.
obligations: To comply with directions issued by the Central Government.
To ensure its members are not disqualified for appointment.
To provide for the terms and conditions of service for its members, officers, and employees.
To consider the absorption of deputation employees from the Central Government.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Authority: Central Government appoints a date for its constitution and appoints members via notification.
Meetings of the Authority: Regulated by regulations, including quorum, time, place, and decision-making by majority votes with a casting vote for the presiding officer.
Transfer of assets and liabilities: Central Government appoints a day for the transfer of properties, assets, and liabilities from the Inland Water Transport Directorate to the Authority.
Making of rules and regulations: Central Government makes rules and the Authority makes regulations for carrying out the Act's provisions, which are then laid before Parliament.
administration: The Inland Waterways Authority of India, with oversight and direction from the Central Government.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act is to be appointed by the Central Government via notification.
The Central Government has the power to amend schemes, issue directions, supersede the Authority, and remove difficulties.
Certain laws might apply to the Authority, as specified in Section 27.
Members, officers, and employees of the Authority are considered public servants.
Action taken in good faith by the Authority's personnel is protected.
The Act provides for compulsory acquisition of land for the Authority.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL AND PROCESSED FOOD PRODUCTS EXPORT DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT, 1985
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an Authority for the development and promotion of exports of certain agricultural and processed food products and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the export of 'Scheduled products' and 'Special products' which are agricultural or processed food products listed in the First and Second Schedules, respectively. The scope also includes the registration of exporters and the functions of the Authority in relation to these products.

key_definitions.Authority: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority established under section 4.
key_definitions.export: Taking out of India by land, sea or air.
key_definitions.exporter: A person registered as an exporter of Scheduled products under section 12.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Authority and includes the Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.processing: Includes the process of preservation of Scheduled products or Special products such as canning, freezing, drying, salting, smoking, peeling or filleting and any other method of processing which the Authority may specify.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheduled product: Any of the agricultural or processed food products included in the First Schedule.
key_definitions.Special product: Any of the agricultural or processed food products included in the Second Schedule.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date (to be appointed by the Central Government).

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Authority', 'Chairman', 'export', 'exporter', 'member', 'prescribed', 'processing', 'regulations', 'Scheduled product', and 'Special product'.

Empowers the Central Government to add or omit agricultural or processed food products from the First or Second Schedule through notification in the Official Gazette, thereby including or excluding them as Scheduled or Special products.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and constitution of the Authority
main_sections.description: Details the establishment of the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It also outlines the composition of the Authority, including the Chairman, ex-officio members, representatives from various government bodies, Parliament, States/Union Territories, and industry. The head office is to be in Delhi.

This section, though only the title is visible in the provided text, is a crucial part outlining the core responsibilities and activities of the Authority in developing and promoting exports of scheduled and special products.
This section, though only the title is visible, pertains to the process and requirements for registering individuals or entities as exporters of Scheduled products.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit or control imports and exports of Scheduled products
main_sections.description: This section, only title visible, grants the Central Government the authority to regulate or ban the import and export of products listed in the schedules.
This section, only title visible, details the penalties for submitting false information or reports.
This section, only title visible, empowers the Central Government to frame rules for the implementation of the Act.
This section, only title visible, empowers the Authority to frame regulations for its functioning and the matters prescribed by the Act.

important_rules: Exporters of Scheduled products must be registered under section 12.
The Central Government has the power to prohibit or control the import and export of Scheduled products (Section 19).
The Central Government can issue directions to the Authority (Section 20).
The Authority must maintain accounts and these are subject to audit (Section 18).

penalties: Penalty for making false reports (Section 22).
Penalties for obstructing a member or officer of the Authority in the discharge of their duty and for failure to produce books and records (Section 23).
Other penalties (Section 24).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority, and the Central Government through various powers like issuing directions and making rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties for contravention of provisions, powers of the Central Government to control and direct the Authority, and through the regulatory framework established by rules and regulations made under the Act.

rights: The Authority has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The Authority has the power to contract, sue, and be sued.
Members of the Authority have the right to attend meetings and participate in proceedings (though some may not vote).
duties: The Authority has the duty to develop and promote exports of scheduled and special products.
Exporters have a duty to make returns as required (Section 14).
Officers and employees of the Authority must not undertake work unconnected with their duties without permission (Section 7(4)).
obligations: The Authority is obligated to function in accordance with the provisions of the Act and any directions from the Central Government.
The Central Government has an obligation to appoint the Chairman and other members, and to establish the Authority.
Employees transferred to the Authority have their terms and conditions of service protected.

key_procedures: Establishment and constitution of the Authority: Central Government appoints Chairman and other members as per specified criteria (Section 4).
Registration of exporters: Process involving application, cancellation, and fee payment as prescribed (Section 13).

Transfer of employees: Special provisions for transferring employees from the Processed Foods Export Promotion Council to the Authority, with options for employees and protection of service conditions (Section 8).
Rule and Regulation Making: The Central Government can make rules (Section 32) and the Authority can make regulations (Section 33) for the effective implementation of the Act.
administration: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority, under the overall control and direction of the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act can be amended by the Central Government to add or remove products from the Schedules (Section 3).
The Authority can be superseded by the Central Government in certain circumstances (Section 11).
No act or proceeding of the Authority or its committees is invalid due to vacancies or defects in constitution or appointment, provided merits are not affected (Section 4(7)).
Other laws are not barred from application unless inconsistent with this Act (Section 31).
Actions taken in good faith by individuals under the Act are protected (Section 28).

title: THE ENVIRONMENT (PROTECTION) ACT, 1986
purpose: To provide for the protection and improvement of environment and for matters connected therewith, implementing decisions of the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment held at Stockholm in June, 1972.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to all persons, industries, operations, and substances that can cause environmental pollution or harm to human beings, other living creatures, plants, and property.

key_definitions.environment: Includes water, air, and land, and the inter-relationship among them, and human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organisms, and property.
key_definitions.environmental pollutant: Any solid, liquid, or gaseous substance present in such concentration as may be, or tend to be, injurious to the environment.
key_definitions.environmental pollution: The presence in the environment of any environmental pollutant.
key_definitions.handling: In relation to any substance, means the manufacture, processing, treatment, package, storage, transportation, use, collection, destruction, conversion, offering for sale, transfer or the like of such substance.
key_definitions.hazardous substance: Any substance or preparation which, by reason of its chemical or physico-chemical properties or handling, is liable to cause harm to human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organism, property or the environment.
key_definitions.occupier: In relation to any factory or premises, means a person who has control over the affairs of the factory or the premises and includes, in relation to any substance, the person in possession of the substance.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the procedure for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'environment', 'environmental pollutant', 'environmental pollution', 'handling', 'hazardous substance', 'occupier', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to take measures to protect and improve environment
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government broad powers to take necessary measures to protect and improve the environment and prevent, control, and abate environmental pollution. This includes coordinating State government actions, planning nationwide programs, setting standards, restricting areas for industries, laying down procedures for handling hazardous substances, and establishing environmental laboratories.

Empowers the Central Government to issue written directions to any person, officer, or authority to comply with specific measures, including closure or regulation of industries, or stoppage of utilities.

main_sections.section_title: Persons carrying on industry, operation, etc., not to allow emission or discharge of environmental pollutants in excess of the standards
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person carrying on an industry, operation, or process from discharging or emitting environmental pollutants in excess of prescribed standards.

main_sections.section_title: Persons handling hazardous substances to comply with procedural safeguards
main_sections.description: Mandates that any person handling hazardous substances must do so in accordance with prescribed procedures and safeguards.
Grants empowered individuals the right to enter any place at reasonable times to perform functions, determine compliance with the Act, or examine equipment and records.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take sample and procedure to be followed in connection therewith
main_sections.description: Authorizes the taking of samples from any place for analysis and specifies the procedure to be followed.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of section 7 or section 8
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of Section 7 (emission/discharge standards) or Section 8 (handling of hazardous substances).

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of Act, rules, orders and directions
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for contravening any provision of the Act, rules, orders, or directions issued thereunder.
Provides for the establishment of an Environmental Protection Fund.
Specifies the procedure for taking cognizance of offenses under the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules made under this Act to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that rules made under the Act must be presented before both Houses of Parliament.

important_rules: No person carrying on any industry, operation, or process shall discharge or emit any environmental pollutant in excess of prescribed standards (Section 7).
No person shall handle any hazardous substance except in accordance with prescribed procedures and safeguards (Section 8).
If discharge of environmental pollutants in excess of standards occurs or is apprehended, the responsible person must prevent or mitigate pollution and forthwith intimate the authorities (Section 9).
The Central Government can issue directions to any person or authority regarding closure, prohibition, or regulation of industries or stoppage of services (Section 5).
Rules can be made to regulate environmental pollution, including standards for air, water, soil quality, limits for pollutants, and procedures for handling hazardous substances (Section 6).

penalties: For contravention of Section 7 or 8: Imprisonment for a term that may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both. If the contravention continues, with additional fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day during which such contravention continues.
For contravention of Sections 9, 10, and 11: Imprisonment for a term that may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees or with both.

For contravention of other provisions of the Act, rules, orders, and directions: Imprisonment for a term that may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both. If the contravention continues, with additional fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day during which such contravention continues.
Companies and Government Departments can also be penalized for contraventions.
Failure to pay penalties can lead to further offenses.
An adjudicating officer is appointed for penalties.
Penalty amounts are credited to the Environmental Protection Fund.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and authorities or officers appointed by it. State Governments and their officers also play a role in coordination and implementation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, sample analysis, issuance of directions, imposition of penalties, and legal proceedings initiated by the authorities.

rights: Right of empowered persons to enter and inspect premises (Section 10).
Right to appeal against directions issued under Section 5 to the National Green Tribunal (Section 5A).
duties: Duty of persons carrying on industry to not exceed emission/discharge standards (Section 7).
Duty of persons handling hazardous substances to comply with safeguards (Section 8).
Duty to intimate authorities and render assistance in case of accidental discharge of pollutants (Section 9).
Duty of officers appointed to be under the general control and direction of the Central Government or constituted authority (Section 4(2)).
obligations: Persons responsible for accidental discharge of pollutants have an obligation to prevent or mitigate it and to assist authorities.
Any person, officer, or authority to whom directions are issued under Section 5 is bound to comply.

key_procedures: Procedure for taking samples of environmental pollutants and analysis thereof (implied by Section 11 and Section 12).
Procedure for furnishing information to authorities in case of accidental discharge of pollutants (Section 9).
Procedure for appeals against directions issued under Section 5 to the National Green Tribunal (Section 5A).
Procedure for cognizance of offenses by courts (Section 19).
administration: The Central Government, with the power to constitute authorities and appoint officers for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to implement decisions taken at the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, Stockholm, 1972.
Different dates may be appointed for the commencement of different provisions of the Act and for different areas.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith in the execution of the Act (Section 18).
The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in certain matters (Section 22).
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws where there is an inconsistency, but it is subject to the provisions of other laws in certain aspects (Section 24).

title: THE CHILD AND ADOLESCENT LABOUR (PROHIBITION AND REGULATION) ACT, 1986
purpose: To prohibit the engagement of children in all occupations and to prohibit the engagement of adolescents in hazardous occupations and processes, and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to children and adolescents in various establishments, including shops, commercial establishments, workshops, farms, residential hotels, restaurants, eating houses, theatres, and other places of public amusement or entertainment. Specific provisions apply to railway administrations, port authorities, mines, and oilfields.

key_definitions.appropriate_government: In relation to an establishment under the control of the Central Government or a railway administration or a major port or a mine or oilfield, the Central Government, and in all other cases, the State Government.
key_definitions.adolescent: A person who has completed his fourteenth year of age but has not completed his eighteenth year.
key_definitions.child: A person who has not completed his fourteenth year of age or such age as may be specified in the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, whichever is more.
key_definitions.establishment: Includes a shop, commercial establishment, workshop, farm, residential hotel, restaurant, eating house, theatre or other place of public amusement or entertainment.
key_definitions.family: In relation to an occupier, means the individual, the wife or husband, as the case may be, of such individual, and their children, brother or sister of such individual. For the purposes of Section 3, 'family' in relation to a child means his mother, father, brother, sister and father’s sister and brother and mother’s sister and brother.
key_definitions.occupier: In relation to an establishment or a workshop, means the person who has the ultimate control over the affairs of the establishment or workshop.
key_definitions.workshop: Means any premises (including the precincts thereof) wherein any industrial process is carried on, but does not include any premises to which the provisions of section 67 of the Factories Act, 1948 for the time being, apply.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986', states its extent to the whole of India, and outlines the commencement of its provisions. Part I and II came into force at once, while Part III came into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appropriate Government', 'adolescent', 'child', 'day', 'establishment', 'family', 'occupier', 'port authority', 'prescribed', 'week', and 'workshop'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of employment of children in any occupation and process
main_sections.description: Prohibits the employment or permission to work of any child in any occupation or process. Exceptions are made for children helping their family in non-hazardous family enterprises after school hours or during vacations, and for artists in audio-visual entertainment industries under prescribed conditions, provided it does not affect their schooling.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of employment of adolescents in certain hazardous occupations and processes
main_sections.description: Prohibits the employment or permission to work of any adolescent in any of the hazardous occupations or processes set forth in the Schedule. The Central Government may notify non-hazardous work for adolescents.

Specifies that the provisions of Part III (Regulation of Conditions of Work of Adolescents) apply to an establishment or a class of establishments in which none of the hazardous occupations or processes referred to in section 3A is carried on.

Regulates the hours and period of work for adolescents. No adolescent shall work in excess of prescribed hours. Work periods cannot exceed three hours without a one-hour rest interval. The total spread of work, including rest, shall not exceed six hours. Adolescents are prohibited from working between 7 p.m. and 8 a.m., and no overtime is permitted. They cannot work in two establishments on the same day.

Outlines the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act. Specific penalties are prescribed for employing children or adolescents in prohibited occupations and for violating the regulations on working conditions.

main_sections.section_title: District Magistrate to implement the provisions
main_sections.description: Empowers the District Magistrate to implement the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No child shall be employed or permitted to work in any occupation or process, with specific exceptions for family help in non-hazardous enterprises and for artists in audio-visual entertainment under strict conditions.
No adolescent shall be employed or permitted to work in any hazardous occupations or processes listed in the Schedule.

Adolescents working in establishments covered by Part III shall not work in excess of prescribed hours. Each work period cannot exceed three hours without a one-hour rest interval, and the total spread of work, including rest, shall not exceed six hours.
Adolescents are prohibited from working between 7 p.m. and 8 a.m., and from working overtime.
Every adolescent employed shall be allowed a weekly holiday of one whole day.
Occupiers must maintain a register of adolescents employed, including their name, date of birth, hours of work, and nature of work.
Notices containing abstracts of sections 3A and 14 must be displayed prominently in establishments.
Rules can be made for the health and safety of adolescents, covering aspects like cleanliness, waste disposal, ventilation, lighting, drinking water, and fencing of machinery.

penalties: Penalties for employing children or adolescents in contravention of the Act are prescribed, including imprisonment and fines.
Penalties for contravention of regulations concerning working hours, rest intervals, and weekly holidays for adolescents.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors appointed under the Act, and District Magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection and monitoring of establishments, investigation of complaints, and prosecution of offenders.

rights: Right of children to not be employed in hazardous occupations or processes.
Right of adolescents to regulated working hours, rest intervals, and weekly holidays.
Right to health and safety for adolescents in establishments.
duties: Duty of occupiers to not employ children in prohibited occupations and adolescents in hazardous occupations.
Duty of occupiers to regulate working hours, provide rest intervals and weekly holidays for adolescents.
Duty of occupiers to maintain registers and display notices as required by the Act.
Duty of the Central and State Governments to frame rules for health and safety and to appoint Inspectors.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to constitute a Technical Advisory Committee for the addition of occupations/processes to the Schedule.
Obligation of the Central Government to appoint Inspectors.
Obligation of the District Magistrate to implement the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for amending the Schedule of hazardous occupations and processes by the Central Government, involving public notification and a notice period.
Procedure for the appointment of a Technical Advisory Committee to advise on the addition of occupations and processes to the Schedule.
Procedure for the reference of disputes regarding the age of an adolescent to a prescribed medical authority.
Procedure for issuing notices to Inspectors by occupiers regarding the employment of adolescents.
Procedure for the compounding of offences under the Act.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments administer this Act. Inspectors are appointed to enforce its provisions. The District Magistrate is responsible for the implementation of the Act's provisions.
important_notes: The definition of 'child' is updated to also refer to the age specified in the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, whichever is higher.
Substantial amendments were made by Act 35 of 2016, significantly altering the long title and several definitions and sections.
The Act was previously known as the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, before amendments.

title: The Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing Commodities) Act, 1987
purpose: To provide for the compulsory use of jute packaging material in the supply and distribution of certain commodities in the interests of production of raw jute and jute packaging material, and of persons engaged in the production thereof, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It covers the compulsory use of jute packaging material for the supply or distribution of specified commodities or classes of commodities.

key_definitions.commodity: Includes any essential commodity or any article manufactured or produced by any scheduled industry.
key_definitions.essential_commodity: Has the same meaning as in the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
key_definitions.jute_packaging_material: Means jute, jute yarn, jute twine, jute sacking cloth, hessian cloth, jute bags or any other packaging material containing not less than seventy-five per cent., by weight, of jute.
key_definitions.scheduled_industry: Has the same meaning as in the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.
key_definitions.Standing_Advisory_Committee: Means the Standing Advisory Committee constituted under section 4.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and that its commencement date is to be notified by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'commodity', 'essential commodity', 'jute packaging material', 'scheduled industry', and 'Standing Advisory Committee'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to specify commodities which are required to be packed in jute packaging material
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct, by order, that specific commodities or classes of commodities, or percentages thereof, must be packed in specified jute packaging material for supply or distribution. This is done based on recommendations from the Standing Advisory Committee and in the interest of raw jute and jute packaging material production.

Mandates the Central Government to constitute a Standing Advisory Committee with expertise to advise on which commodities should be packed in jute material. It also outlines the matters the committee must consider before making recommendations.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of packing in any material other than the jute packaging material
main_sections.description: Prohibits the supply or distribution of commodities for which an order has been made under section 3, unless they are packed in the specified jute packaging material. A grace period is provided for commodities previously packed in other materials.

main_sections.section_title: Power to call for information and samples
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to require persons obligated to use jute packaging material to furnish information and samples of jute packaging material for inspection.
Authorizes an appointed officer to enter, at reasonable times, any place where commodities packed in jute material are stored for supply or distribution, and to inspect them and request information.

Empowers an authorized officer to search any place, premises, or vehicle if there's reason to believe a commodity has been packed in contravention of section 5. The officer can seize such commodities and related items. The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure related to searches and seizures apply.
Prescribes a penalty for contravening section 5, which is a fine up to double the cost of the jute packaging material that should have been used.
Imposes a penalty of a fine up to five thousand rupees for failing to furnish required information or samples, or for providing false information under section 6.

Deals with offenses committed by companies, making both the company and individuals responsible for its conduct liable. It includes provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence to avoid liability.
Declares all offenses punishable under the Act to be cognizable, notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act (except for making orders under sections 3 and 16, or rules under section 17) to subordinate officers or State Governments/their officers.
Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to State Governments for the effective implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act, rules, or orders.
Grants the Central Government the power to exempt any person or class of persons from the operation of an order made under section 3, if it deems it necessary in the public interest.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. These rules, like orders, are subject to parliamentary scrutiny.

important_rules: Commodities specified under section 3 must be packed in the designated jute packaging material for supply or distribution.
Supplying or distributing commodities without using the specified jute packaging material is prohibited.
Persons required to use jute packaging material must furnish information and samples when requested by the Central Government.
Authorized officers have the power to enter, inspect, search, and seize commodities packed in contravention of section 5.
Offenses under the Act are cognizable.
The Central Government can issue directions to State Governments for the execution of the Act.
The Central Government has the power to exempt certain persons or commodities from the provisions of the Act.
The Central Government can make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

penalties: For contravention of section 5 (prohibition of packing in other materials): Fine up to double the cost of the jute packaging material that should have been used.
For false statements or failure to furnish information/samples under section 6: Fine up to five thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and its authorized officers, State Governments and their officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of inspection, search, seizure, delegation of powers, issuance of directions to State Governments, and imposition of penalties. Offences are cognizable.

rights: Right to be exempt from the Act's provisions under certain conditions (section 16).
Protection against legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith (section 15).
duties: Duty to pack specified commodities in jute packaging material as directed by the Central Government.
Duty to furnish information and samples when required.
Duty to comply with orders and rules made under the Act.
obligations: Manufacturers and distributors of specified commodities have an obligation to use jute packaging material.
Companies have an obligation to ensure compliance with the Act, with directors and officers also being liable in cases of consent, connivance, or neglect.

key_procedures: Central Government identifies commodities for compulsory jute packaging, considering recommendations from the Standing Advisory Committee (Section 3).
Order specifying commodities, packaging material, and effective date is published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament for approval or modification (Section 3(2)).
Authorized officers can enter, inspect, search, and seize non-compliant goods, following principles of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Sections 7 & 8).
Penalties are imposed for contraventions (Sections 9 & 10).
Central Government can delegate powers and issue directions for implementation (Sections 13 & 14).
Central Government can make rules for the Act's purpose (Section 17).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: Until the Standing Advisory Committee is constituted, the Central Government can make orders under section 3 after considering specific matters, and such orders cease to operate after three months from the Committee's first recommendation.
Any modification or annulment of orders or rules by Parliament does not affect the validity of anything done previously under that order or rule.
The Act applies to the whole of India.
All offenses under this Act are cognizable.

title: THE GOA, DAMAN AND DIU MINING CONCESSIONS (ABOLITION AND DECLARATION AS MINING LEASES) ACT, 1987
purpose: To provide for the abolition of mining concessions in Goa, Daman and Diu and their declaration as mining leases under the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, for the regulation of mines and development of minerals under Union control.
scope: Applies to mining concessions in operation in the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu, specified in the First and Second Schedules of the Act. It aims to regulate mines and develop minerals under the control of the Union.

key_definitions.appointed day: The 20th of December, 1961.
key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of Payments appointed under section 8.
key_definitions.concession holder: A person who has been granted a mining concession.
key_definitions.mining concession: A mining concession granted under the Portuguese Colonial Mining Laws, 1906 (Decree of 20th September, 1906).
key_definitions.mines and Minerals Act: The Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 (67 of 1957).

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Goa, Daman and Diu Mining Concessions (Abolition and Declaration as Mining Leases) Act, 1987.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'concession holder', 'mining concession', and 'Mines and Minerals Act'.

main_sections.section_title: Act to override all other enactments, etc.
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in any other enactment, judgment, decree, order, or instrument.

Abolishes mining concessions specified in the First Schedule from the appointed day and declares them as mining leases under the Mines and Minerals Act. Also addresses concessions in the Second Schedule and allows for correction of errors in the Schedules.

main_sections.section_title: General effect of declaring the mining concessions to be mining leases
main_sections.description: Declares concession holders as holders of mining leases under the Mines and Minerals Act, with the lease period extending up to six months from the date of assent. Allows for renewal of these leases.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of amounts to concession holders
main_sections.description: Specifies that concession holders shall be paid an amount by the Central Government for the abolition of their concessions, as detailed in the Schedules.
Mandates the payment of simple interest at 4% per annum on the specified amounts to concession holders from the date of assent until the payment is made to the Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Commissioner of Payments to be appointed
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments by the Central Government to disburse amounts to concession holders, and allows for the appointment of assisting personnel.

main_sections.section_title: Payment by the Central Government to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to pay the total amounts due to the Commissioner within thirty days from the specified date. Outlines the procedure for a deposit account and record maintenance.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Establishes the procedure for concession holders to prefer claims to the Commissioner, including timelines, proof submission, investigation, and the Commissioner's power to admit or reject claims. Appeals against the Commissioner's decision can be made to the principal civil court.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of Central Government to end on payment of claim
main_sections.description: States that the Central Government's liability regarding a claim is discharged upon payment of the admitted amount by the Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Disputes how to be dealt with
main_sections.description: Directs the Commissioner to refer any doubt or dispute regarding the right to receive payment to the court for decision, and to disburse accordingly.

main_sections.section_title: Undisbursed or unclaimed amount to be deposited to the general revenue account
main_sections.description: Specifies that any undisbursed or unclaimed money with the Commissioner for three years shall be deposited into the Central Government's general revenue account, but claims can still be preferred.
Deals with penalties for offenses under the Act.
Addresses offenses committed by companies.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Allows for the delegation of powers under the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Provides for the validation of certain actions or proceedings.

important_rules: Rule: Mining concessions specified in the First and Second Schedules are abolished and deemed to be mining leases under the Mines and Minerals Act, 1957 (Section 4).
Rule: The period of these deemed mining leases shall extend up to six months from the date of assent, and they may be renewed thereafter (Section 5).
Rule: Concession holders are entitled to receive specified amounts and simple interest (4% per annum) from the Central Government (Sections 6 & 7).
Rule: Claims for payment must be preferred before the Commissioner within thirty days from the specified date, with a possible extension of another thirty days (Section 10(1)).
Rule: The Commissioner has the power to investigate claims, summon witnesses, and receive evidence, with powers akin to a civil court (Section 10(6)).
Rule: Appeals against the Commissioner's decision can be made to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction (Section 10(8)).

penalties: Penalties are provided for offenses under the Act (Section 15).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through the Commissioner of Payments and other appointed persons.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments to disburse amounts, investigate claims, and facilitate the transition of mining concessions to mining leases. The Act also vests the Commissioner with civil court powers for investigations and allows for appeals to civil courts.

rights: Right to receive payment for abolished mining concessions.
Right to receive interest on the payment amount.
Right to have claims investigated by the Commissioner.
Right to appeal against the Commissioner's decision to the civil court.
Right to renewal of mining leases under the Mines and Minerals Act, 1957.
duties: Duty to prefer claims to the Commissioner within the specified timeframes.
Duty to file proof of claim as required by the Commissioner.
Duty of the Central Government to pay amounts and interest to the Commissioner.
Duty of the Commissioner to disburse payments and handle undisbursed amounts.
obligations: Obligation on concession holders to transition to mining lease holders under the Mines and Minerals Act, 1957.
Obligation on the Central Government to provide funds to the Commissioner for payments.

key_procedures: Procedure: Abolition of mining concessions and declaration as mining leases under the Mines and Minerals Act, 1957.
Procedure: Appointment of a Commissioner of Payments for disbursing amounts to concession holders.
Procedure: Central Government depositing funds to the Commissioner within thirty days of the specified date.
Procedure: Concession holders preferring claims to the Commissioner within thirty days, with a possible extension.
Procedure: Commissioner investigating claims, admitting or rejecting them, and disbursing admitted amounts.
Procedure: Referral of disputes regarding payment rights to the court by the Commissioner.
Procedure: Transfer of undisbursed or unclaimed amounts to the Central Government's general revenue account after three years.
Procedure: Appeal against the Commissioner's decision to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction.
administration: The Central Government, and specifically the Commissioner of Payments appointed under the Act.
important_notes: The Act overrides all other enactments in case of inconsistency.
Errors or misdescriptions in the Schedules can be corrected by the Central Government through notification.
The Act aims to make the provisions of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, applicable to the mines covered by the former concessions.
The period of deemed mining leases is limited to six months from the date of assent, after which renewal is subject to the Mines and Minerals Act, 1957.

title: THE NATIONAL HOUSING BANK ACT, 1987
purpose: To establish a bank to be known as the National Housing Bank to operate as a principal agency to promote housing finance institutions both at local and regional levels and to provide financial and other support to such institutions and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the National Housing Bank, its operations, its management, and its relationship with housing finance institutions.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of Directors of the National Housing Bank.
key_definitions.Chairman: The Chairman of the Board appointed under section 6.
key_definitions.housing finance institution: Includes every institution, whether incorporated or not, which primarily transacts or has as one of its principal objects, the transacting of the business of providing finance for housing, whether directly or indirectly.
key_definitions.Managing Director: The Managing Director appointed under section 6.
key_definitions.National Housing Bank: The National Housing Bank established under section 3.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.Reserve Bank: The Reserve Bank of India constituted under section 3 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date on which it comes into force.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as Board, Chairman, director, housing finance institution, Managing Director, National Housing Bank, notification, prescribed, and Reserve Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of National Housing Bank
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Housing Bank as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract. It also specifies the head office location and the power to establish offices and branches.

Specifies the authorized and paid-up capital of the National Housing Bank, with provisions for increase and issuance of capital to various entities. It also addresses the transfer of subscribed capital from the Reserve Bank to the Central Government.

Vests the general superintendence, direction, and management of the National Housing Bank's affairs in the Board of Directors. It emphasizes acting on business principles with due regard to public interest and outlines the powers of the Chairman and Managing Director.

Details the composition of the Board of Directors, including the Chairman, Managing Director, experts in various fields, representatives from housing finance institutions, shareholders, the Reserve Bank, and officials from Central and State Governments.

main_sections.section_title: Business of the National Housing Bank
main_sections.description: Outlines the business activities that the National Housing Bank is authorized to undertake.
Provides a definition for 'deposit' in the context of Chapter V.

main_sections.section_title: Requirement of registration and net owned fund
main_sections.description: Specifies the requirements for registration and net owned funds for housing finance institutions.
Details the penalties that may be imposed for contraventions of the Act.
Provides for the process of liquidation of the National Housing Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make regulations for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: The National Housing Bank shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract.

The Board of Directors shall have the general superintendence, direction, and management of the affairs and business of the National Housing Bank and shall act on business principles with due regard to public interest.
Housing finance institutions must comply with registration requirements and maintain a specified net owned fund.
The Reserve Bank has the power to regulate or prohibit the issue of prospectuses or advertisements soliciting deposits of money by housing finance institutions.
The National Housing Bank has the power to impose conditions for accommodation and to call for repayment before the agreed period.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of provisions of the Act, including fines and imprisonment as specified in Section 49.
Power of the National Housing Bank and Reserve Bank to impose penalties as specified in Section 52A.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Housing Bank, the Reserve Bank of India, and potentially other authorities as designated by the Act or Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection powers, collection of credit information, imposition of penalties, and legal proceedings. Chapter VA outlines specific recovery procedures and the establishment of an Appellate Tribunal.

rights: The National Housing Bank has the right to conduct business, lend, borrow, acquire and dispose of property, and call for repayment of loans.
Housing finance institutions have the right to operate within the framework of the Act, subject to regulations.
Depositors have rights regarding their deposits, including nomination provisions.
duties: The National Housing Bank has a duty to promote housing finance institutions and provide them with financial and other support.
Housing finance institutions have a duty to comply with registration requirements, maintain net owned funds, maintain a percentage of assets, and keep reserve funds.
Housing finance institutions have a duty to furnish statements and information to the National Housing Bank and the Reserve Bank.
The Board of Directors has a duty to act on business principles with due regard to public interest.
obligations: Obligation to maintain fidelity and secrecy by staff of the National Housing Bank.
Obligation for housing finance institutions to disclose information as required.
Obligation for the National Housing Bank to provide annual reports on housing.

key_procedures: Establishment of the National Housing Bank, including incorporation and appointment of Board members.
Management of the National Housing Bank through its Board of Directors, including meetings and committee formations.
Registration and net owned fund requirements for housing finance institutions.
Procedures for the Reserve Bank to regulate or prohibit the issue of prospectuses and advertisements for deposits.
Procedures for the National Housing Bank to collect information from housing finance institutions regarding deposits.
Procedures for audit of the National Housing Bank's accounts.
Procedures for applying to a recovery officer, enforcement of recovery orders, and appeals to an Appellate Tribunal as outlined in Chapter VA.
Procedures for imposing penalties for offenses.
administration: The Central Government and the Reserve Bank of India play significant roles in the establishment, oversight, and regulation of the National Housing Bank and housing finance institutions. The National Housing Bank itself is administered by its Board of Directors.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force.
Words and expressions used in the Act but not defined therein shall have the meanings assigned to them in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, or the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, as applicable.
The Central Government may, by notification, increase the authorized capital of the National Housing Bank.
Chapter V (Provisions relating to Housing Finance Institutions) has specific commencement dates and may not apply in certain cases.
Certain sections, like Section 48, have been omitted, and others, like Section 56, have been repealed.

title: The Religious Institutions (Prevention of Misuse) Act, 1988
purpose: To prevent the misuse of religious institutions for political and other purposes.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The Act governs religious institutions and their managers.

key_definitions.ammunition: Shall have the same meaning as in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Arms Act, 1959.
key_definitions.arms: Shall have the same meaning as in clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Arms Act, 1959.
key_definitions.manager: Means every person, including any religious functionary, who, for the time being, either alone or in association with other persons, administers, manages or otherwise controls the affairs of a religious institution, its functions or properties.
key_definitions.political_activity: Includes any activity promoting or propagating the aims or objects of a political party or any cause, issue or question of a political nature by organising meetings, demonstrations, processions, collection or disbursement of funds, or by the issue of directions or decrees, or by any other means, and includes also such activity by or on behalf of a person seeking election as a candidate for any election to Parliament, any State Legislature or any local authority.
key_definitions.political_party: Means an association or body of persons which is, or is deemed to be, registered with the Election Commission of India as a political party, or which has set up candidates for election to any legislature but is not registered, or organised to carry on any political activity or to acquire or exercise political power through election or otherwise.
key_definitions.religious_institution: Means an institution for the promotion of any religion or persuasion, and includes any place or premises used as a place of public religious worship, by whatever name or designation known.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and commencement date. It extends to the whole of India and was deemed to have come into force on May 26, 1988.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'ammunition', 'arms', 'manager', 'political activity', 'political party', and 'religious institution'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of use of religious institutions for certain purposes
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use or allowance of use of religious institution premises for specific purposes such as promoting political activity, harbouring accused persons, storing arms/ammunition, storing unlawful goods, erecting unauthorized constructions, carrying on unlawful acts, promoting disharmony between groups, activities prejudicial to India's sovereignty/unity/integrity, and acts violating the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on carrying arms and ammunition into a religious institution
main_sections.description: Prohibits the entry of arms or ammunition, or persons carrying them, into a religious institution, with exceptions for Kirpans worn by Sikhs and arms used in religious ceremonies.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of use of funds of religious institutions for certain activities
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use or allowance of use of funds or properties of religious institutions for the benefit of any political party, for any political activity, or for the commission of any punishable offence.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of religious for a for propagating political ideas
main_sections.description: Prohibits religious institutions or their managers from allowing ceremonies, festivals, congregations, processions, or assemblies held under their auspices to be used for any political activity.

Prescribes penalties for contravention of sections 3, 4, 5, or 6, including imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to ten thousand rupees for the manager and persons connected with the contravention.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification of persons convicted or charge-sheeted under this Act
main_sections.description: Details the disqualification of managers or employees convicted under the Act, removal from office, and disqualification for future appointments in religious institutions. It also provides for restraining accused persons pending trial.

main_sections.section_title: Certain persons bound to give information to police
main_sections.description: Obligates managers and employees of religious institutions to inform the police of any contravention or impending contravention of the Act, with failure to do so being punishable under the Indian Penal Code.
Repeals the Religious Institutions (Prevention of Misuse) Ordinance, 1988, and states that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Religious institutions and their managers are prohibited from using or allowing the use of their premises for promotion/propagation of political activity, harbouring accused persons, storing arms/ammunition, storing goods in contravention of law, erecting unauthorized constructions, carrying on unlawful/subversive acts, promoting disharmony between groups, engaging in activities prejudicial to India's sovereignty/unity/integrity, or violating the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act.
Rule 2: Entry of arms, ammunition, or persons carrying them into a religious institution is prohibited, with exceptions for Kirpans and arms used in religious ceremonies.
Rule 3: Funds or properties of religious institutions cannot be used for the benefit of political parties, for political activities, or for committing offences.
Rule 4: Ceremonies, festivals, congregations, processions, or assemblies held under the auspices of a religious institution cannot be used for political activity.
Rule 5: Managers and employees of religious institutions must report any contravention or impending contravention of the Act to the police.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees for contravening sections 3, 4, 5, or 6.
Punishment under section 176 of the Indian Penal Code for failure to give information to the police regarding contraventions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The police and courts are responsible for enforcing this Act. Managers and employees are obligated to provide information to the police.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through police investigation based on information or otherwise, prosecution in courts, imposition of penalties, and disqualification from office. Courts can also issue orders restraining accused individuals from exercising their duties pending trial.

rights: The right to wear and carry a Kirpan by any person professing the Sikh religion within a religious institution.
The right to use arms as part of any religious ceremony or ritual of the institution as established by custom or usage within a religious institution.
duties: Managers and employees of religious institutions have a duty to prevent the misuse of the institution for prohibited purposes.
Managers and employees have a duty to give information to the police about any contravention or impending contravention of the Act.
obligations: Religious institutions and their managers are obligated not to use or allow the use of their premises, funds, or properties for political or unlawful activities.
Religious institutions and their managers are obligated to prevent the entry of unauthorized arms and ammunition.

key_procedures: Procedure for contravention: If a religious institution or its manager contravenes sections 3, 4, 5, or 6, they are punishable with imprisonment and fine.

Procedure for disqualification: Upon conviction under the Act, a manager or employee is removed from office and disqualified from appointment in any religious institution for six years. If accused, a charge-sheeted person may be restrained from exercising duties pending trial.
Procedure for reporting: Managers and employees are bound to inform the officer in-charge of the local police station of any contravention or impending contravention of the Act.
administration: The Act does not explicitly name a single administrative department. Enforcement involves police and judicial authorities. The 'Statement of Objects and Reasons' indicates that the government was concerned with the misuse of religious institutions, implying general governmental oversight.
important_notes: The Act was preceded by The Religious Institutions (Prevention of Misuse) Ordinance, 1988, which it replaces.
The original extent of the Act excluded the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but this exclusion was omitted by the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.
The Act came into force retrospectively from May 26, 1988.

title: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the prevention of corruption and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to all citizens of India outside India. It covers offenses related to corruption involving public servants and commercial organizations.

key_definitions.election: Any election, by whatever means held under any law for the purpose of selecting members of Parliament or of any Legislature, local authority or other public authority.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public duty: A duty in the discharge of which the State, the public or the community at large has an interest. 'State' includes corporations, authorities, bodies, or Government companies owned, controlled, or aided by the Government.
key_definitions.public servant: Includes a wide range of individuals in government service, local authorities, corporations, judges, persons authorized by courts, arbitrators, election officials, university personnel, and office-bearers/employees of certain institutions receiving government aid.
key_definitions.undue advantage: Any gratification whatever, other than legal remuneration. 'Gratification' is not limited to pecuniary or money's worth, and 'legal remuneration' includes all remuneration permitted by the Government or the organization served.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial and personal extent.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'election', 'prescribed', 'public duty', 'public servant', and 'undue advantage'.
Empowers the Central or State Government to appoint Special Judges to try offenses under the Act within specified areas or for specific cases.
