Mandates that offenses specified in section 3(1) shall be tried exclusively by Special Judges and outlines procedures for trial, including day-to-day basis and time limits.

main_sections.section_title: Offence relating to public servant being bribed
main_sections.description: Defines the offense of a public servant accepting or obtaining any undue advantage from any person as a motive or reward for doing or forbearing to do any official act, or showing or forbearing to show favor or disfavor.

main_sections.section_title: Criminal misconduct by a public servant
main_sections.description: Defines criminal misconduct by a public servant, including habitually accepting illegal gratification or obtaining pecuniary resources or valuable things disproportionate to his known sources of income.
Specifies the police officers authorized to investigate offenses under the Act.
Requires previous sanction from the appropriate Government or authority for the prosecution of public servants for offenses under sections 7, 11, 15, and sub-section (1) of section 13.

important_rules: A public servant accepting or obtaining any undue advantage, which is other than legal remuneration, as a motive or reward for doing or forbearing to do any official act, or for showing or forbearing to show favor or disfavor to any person in the exercise of his official functions, is an offense.
A person who abets any of the offenses punishable under the Act shall, if the matter abetted is one for which punishment is prescribed, be punished with the punishment provided for the offense.

Criminal misconduct by a public servant includes habitually accepting illegal gratification or obtaining pecuniary resources or valuable things disproportionate to his known sources of income, which he cannot satisfactorily account for.
Previous sanction is necessary for the prosecution of a public servant for certain offenses under the Act.

When a public servant accepts or obtains or agrees to accept or obtain from any person any undue advantage, it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that he accepted or agreed to accept or obtain that undue advantage.
Trials by Special Judges are to be held, as far as practicable, on a day-to-day basis and should ideally be concluded within two years, with provisions for extension under specific circumstances.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than four years but which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine (for offenses under Section 7, 7A, 11).
Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than four years but which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine (for offenses under Section 8, 9, 10).
Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than four years but which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine (for offenses under Section 13).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with fine or with both (for attempt to commit an offense under Section 15).

Summary trial conviction can lead to imprisonment not exceeding one year or a fine not exceeding two thousand rupees, but if imprisonment exceeds one month, there is no appeal unless a higher sentence is awarded or the case is deemed unfit for summary trial.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Special Judges appointed under the Act, and police officers authorized to investigate.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation by authorized police officers, trial by Special Judges, and application of procedures under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, with modifications as specified in the Act.

rights: An accused person is a competent witness.
Right to appeal and revision as provided in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, subject to modifications.
Right to a fair trial, including day-to-day proceedings for cases tried by Special Judges.
duties: Public servants have a duty to discharge their public duties without corruption.
Public servants have a duty to report certain offenses if they come to their notice.
Commercial organizations have a duty to prevent corruption by their employees or persons associated with them.
obligations: Public servants are obligated not to accept or obtain undue advantages other than legal remuneration.
Public servants are obligated to account for their pecuniary resources or valuable things.
Commercial organizations are obligated to prevent persons associated with them from committing corruption offenses.

key_procedures: Appointment of Special Judges by the Central or State Government.
Cases are tried exclusively by Special Judges, who follow procedures prescribed by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for warrant cases by Magistrates.
Special Judges can take cognizance of offenses without commitment proceedings.
Special Judges can tender pardons to persons concerned in an offense for securing evidence.
Investigation of offenses is carried out by authorized police officers.
Previous sanction is required for prosecution of public servants.
Presumption of guilt arises when a public servant accepts an undue advantage.
Trials are to be conducted on a day-to-day basis and concluded within two years, with provisions for extension.
Appeals and revisions are governed by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, subject to the Act's provisions.
administration: The administration of the Act involves the Central Government, State Governments, the police, and the judiciary (Special Judges). Rule-making power rests with the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act does not affect the application of military, naval, air force, or other laws.
The Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law for the time being in force.
Amendments have been made to the Act, notably by The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, and The Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018.
The definition of 'public servant' is broad and inclusive.

title: The Labour Laws (Simplification of Procedure for Furnishing Returns and Maintaining Registers by Certain Establishments) Act, 1988
purpose: To provide for the simplification of procedure for furnishing returns and maintaining registers in relation to establishments employing a small number of persons under certain labour laws.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Specific provisions related to the Plantations Labour Act, 1951, do not extend to the State of Jammu and Kashmir (though this was later made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh). It applies to 'small establishments' and 'very small establishments' as defined by the Act, in relation to various 'Scheduled Acts'.

key_definitions.employer: In relation to a Scheduled Act, it has the same meaning as assigned in that Act. In relation to any other Scheduled Act, it means the person required to furnish returns or maintain registers under that Act.
key_definitions.establishment: Has the meaning assigned in a Scheduled Act and includes specific types of industrial/other establishments, factories, workshops, plantations, and newspaper establishments as defined in various other labour laws listed in the Act.
key_definitions.Form: Means a Form specified in the Second Schedule.
key_definitions.Scheduled Act: Means an Act specified in the First Schedule that is in force on the commencement of this Act and includes the rules made thereunder.
key_definitions.small establishment: An establishment employing not less than ten and not more than forty persons on any day of the preceding twelve months.
key_definitions.very small establishment: An establishment employing not more than nine persons on any day of the preceding twelve months.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the process for its commencement, which can be notified by the Central Government for different dates in different states.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'employer', 'establishment', 'Form', 'Scheduled Act', 'small establishment', and 'very small establishment'.
States that the Scheduled Acts shall have effect subject to the provisions of this Act from its commencement.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption from furnishing or maintaining of returns and registers required under certain labour laws
main_sections.description: Exempts employers of 'small establishments' or 'very small establishments' from furnishing returns or maintaining registers under Scheduled Acts, provided they furnish an annual return in Form I and maintain specific registers (Form II and Form III for small, Form III for very small) at the work spot. It also specifies certain mandatory continuations like issuing wage slips and filing accident returns. It allows for physical or electronic maintenance of records and specifies how returns can be furnished electronically. It clarifies that other provisions of Scheduled Acts, including inspection, apply to the returns and registers maintained under this Act. It also provides immunity from penalty for failure to furnish returns or maintain registers under the Scheduled Act if compliance is made under this Act.

Clarifies that the commencement of this Act does not affect the previous operation of any provision of a Scheduled Act, or any right, privilege, obligation, liability, penalty, forfeiture, or punishment acquired, accrued, or incurred before the relevant period, nor does it affect any legal proceedings related to them.
Prescribes penalties for employers who fail to comply with the provisions of this Act, including fines for the first conviction and imprisonment or higher fines for subsequent convictions.
Empowers the Central Government to amend any Form by notification in the Official Gazette, subject to parliamentary approval.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act by order, within two years of the President's assent.

important_rules: Rule: Employers of 'small establishments' or 'very small establishments' are exempt from furnishing returns and maintaining registers required by Scheduled Acts.
Rule: In lieu of exempted returns and registers, employers must furnish an annual return in Form I.
Rule: In lieu of exempted registers, employers must maintain registers in Form II and Form III (for small establishments) or Form III (for very small establishments) at the work spot.
Rule: Employers must continue to issue wage slips as prescribed and file returns relating to accidents.
Rule: Records can be maintained in physical or electronic form, provided a printout is available to the Inspector on demand.
Rule: Annual returns can be furnished in physical form or via electronic mail if the receiving authority has the facility.

penalties: First conviction: Fine up to rupees five thousand.
Second or subsequent conviction: Imprisonment for not less than one month but up to six months, or fine not less than rupees ten thousand but up to rupees twenty-five thousand, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors or other authorities prescribed under the respective Scheduled Acts, and the Central Government for general administration and removal of difficulties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the penalties prescribed for non-compliance and the inspection powers vested with authorities under the Scheduled Acts, which are extended to the returns and registers maintained under this Act.

rights: Right to simplified procedures for furnishing returns and maintaining registers for small and very small establishments.
Right to maintain records in physical or electronic form.
Immunity from penalties under Scheduled Acts for failure to maintain prescribed returns/registers if compliance with this Act is made.
duties: Duty to furnish an annual return in Form I.
Duty to maintain registers in Form II and/or Form III as applicable.
Duty to keep these records at the work spot.
Duty to continue issuing wage slips and filing accident returns as required.
Duty to make printouts of electronic records available to the Inspector on demand.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and the specified forms.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the definitions of 'small establishment' and 'very small establishment'.
Obligation to provide information as requested by authorities during inspections.
Obligation to comply with the Central Government's notifications regarding forms and difficulty removal.

key_procedures: Procedure for Exemption: Employers of 'small' or 'very small' establishments must furnish an annual return in Form I and maintain specified registers (Form II/III) instead of the returns and registers mandated by Scheduled Acts.
Procedure for Record Maintenance: Records can be kept in physical or electronic form. If electronic, a printout must be made available to the Inspector upon demand.
Procedure for Furnishing Returns: Annual returns can be submitted physically or via email if the receiving authority has the capability.
Procedure for Amendment of Forms: The Central Government can amend forms via notification, which is subject to parliamentary review and approval.
Procedure for Removal of Difficulties: The Central Government can issue orders to resolve difficulties in implementing the Act.
administration: Central Government (specifically for issuing notifications, amending forms, and removing difficulties). Enforcement is carried out by Inspectors or authorities under the Scheduled Acts.
important_notes: The definition of 'small establishment' was amended from 'nineteen' to 'forty' persons by Act 33 of 2014, effective from 01-01-2015.
The commencement date for certain provisions related to the Amendment Act of 2014 is 01-01-2015, while the original Act commenced on 01-05-1989.
The Act applies to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh as per Notification No. S.O. 3912(E) dated 30th October, 2019.
The scope of Section 1(2) concerning the Plantations Labour Act, 1951, excludes the State of Jammu and Kashmir prior to its specific inclusion for the Union Territories.

title: The Auroville Foundation Act, 1988
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of Auroville and to vest such undertakings in a foundation established for the purpose with a view to making long-term arrangements for the better management and further development of Auroville in accordance with its original charter and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the undertakings of Auroville, which is described as a cultural township founded by 'The Mother' on February 28, 1968. It also concerns the Sri Aurobindo Society and specified trusts or bodies listed in the Schedule. The scope includes the acquisition, transfer, and management of these undertakings to ensure their development in line with Auroville's charter. The Act has an overriding effect over other laws and contracts not ratified by the Foundation.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date of commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.auroville: So much of the undertakings as form part of, or are relatable to, the cultural township known as Auroville, and the charter of which was proclaimed by the ‘Mother’ on February 28, 1968.
key_definitions.society: Sri Aurobindo Society, registered under the West Bengal Societies Registration Act, 1961.
key_definitions.foundation: The Auroville Foundation established under sub-section (1) of section 10.
key_definitions.undertakings: The undertakings of the Society, trust or body which had vested in the Central Government under section 3.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Auroville Foundation Act, 1988.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Auroville', 'Society', 'Foundation', 'undertakings', 'Governing Board', 'Residents’ Assembly', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of certain undertakings of the Society, trusts and bodies
main_sections.description: On the appointed day, undertakings of the Society, trust, and body related to Auroville, along with their rights and interests, are transferred to and vest in the Central Government.

Details the comprehensive nature of the vesting, including all assets, rights, properties, and documents. It also clarifies that vested properties are freed from encumbrances and that pending legal proceedings continue. Licenses and instruments remain in force or are deemed to be granted to the Foundation if the undertakings are transferred to it.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings in the Foundation
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct that the undertakings, which vested in the Central Government, shall instead vest in the Auroville Foundation. Upon such vesting, the Foundation becomes the owner, and the Central Government's rights and liabilities become those of the Foundation.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the Foundation
main_sections.description: Establishes the Auroville Foundation as a body corporate for the purposes of the Act, effective from a date appointed by the Central Government.
Provides for the constitution of a Governing Board for the Foundation.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Governing Board
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Governing Board of the Foundation.
Provides for the establishment of a Residents’ Assembly for the Foundation.
Details the functions of the Residents’ Assembly.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect on other laws, with certain exceptions.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Governing Board the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

important_rules: Rule 1: On the appointed day, undertakings related to Auroville, along with all rights and interests, vest in the Central Government (Section 3).
Rule 2: The Central Government can direct these undertakings to vest in the Auroville Foundation, which then becomes the owner (Section 6).
Rule 3: The general management of the undertakings vests in the Foundation, or a Custodian appointed by the Central Government if no direction for vesting in the Foundation has been made (Section 7).
Rule 4: Persons in charge of management must deliver all assets and documents to the Foundation or Custodian upon vesting or appointment (Section 8).
Rule 5: The Foundation is established as a body corporate with a Governing Board and a Residents’ Assembly to manage Auroville's affairs (Sections 10, 11, 18).
Rule 6: The Act has an overriding effect on other laws and contracts, unless ratified by the Foundation (Sections 27, 28).
Rule 7: The Central Government has the power to make rules, and the Governing Board has the power to make regulations (Sections 31, 32).

penalties: Penalties are prescribed under Section 29 for contravention of the provisions of the Act or any rules or regulations made thereunder.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Auroville Foundation (through its Governing Board and appointed officers).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through vesting of undertakings, appointment of a Custodian, establishment of the Foundation and its governing bodies, and by prescribing penalties for non-compliance.

rights: The Foundation has the right to manage and develop Auroville in accordance with its charter.
The Foundation is entitled to receive all assets, properties, and rights related to Auroville's undertakings.
The Foundation has the right to continue in force licenses and instruments related to the undertakings.
The Foundation has the right to receive money due to the Society, trust, or body in relation to its undertakings, realized after the appointed day (Section 9).
duties: Persons in charge of management have a duty to deliver all assets, books of account, registers, and other documents to the Foundation or Custodian (Section 8).
The Society, trust, or body has a duty to furnish a complete inventory of its properties and assets to the Central Government or Foundation (Section 8).
The Foundation has a duty to manage and develop Auroville in accordance with its original charter.
obligations: The Foundation assumes the rights and liabilities of the Central Government concerning the acquired undertakings (Section 6).
The Central Government or Foundation is liable for certain prior liabilities related to the undertakings (Section 5).
The Foundation is obligated to operate in accordance with the Act, rules, and regulations.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Acquisition and Vesting of Undertakings: On the appointed day, undertakings of the Society, trust, or body relating to Auroville vest in the Central Government. Subsequently, the Central Government can direct these undertakings to vest in the Auroville Foundation.

Procedure 2: Management of Undertakings: The general superintendence, direction, control, and management of the undertakings vest in the Foundation or a Custodian appointed by the Central Government. Persons in charge must deliver all assets and documents.

Procedure 3: Establishment of the Foundation: The Central Government establishes the Auroville Foundation and appoints a date for its commencement. The Foundation is then incorporated as a body corporate.

Procedure 4: Governance: A Governing Board is constituted for the Foundation, with provisions for its members' terms, meetings, and powers. A Residents’ Assembly is also established with defined functions.
Procedure 5: Rule and Regulation Making: The Central Government can make rules, and the Governing Board can make regulations, subject to the Act and parliamentary oversight.
administration: The Auroville Foundation, with its Governing Board and administration, is the primary body for the management and development of Auroville. The Central Government retains oversight and rule-making powers.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act ensures that Auroville is managed and developed in accordance with its original charter.
Note 2: The Act has overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over other conflicting laws.
Note 3: Contracts not ratified by the Foundation cease to have effect.
Note 4: Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act (Section 30).

title: The National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988
purpose: To provide for the constitution of an Authority for the development, maintenance and management of national highways and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to national highways as defined under the National Highways Act, 1956, and any other highways vested in or entrusted to the Authority by the Government.

key_definitions.Authority: The National Highways Authority of India constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.employee: A person in the full-time service of the Authority.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Authority appointed under section 3, including the Chairman.
key_definitions.national highway: Any highway for the time being declared as a national highway under section 2 of the National Highways Act, 1956.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Authority under this Act.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement through notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Authority', 'Chairman', 'member', 'national highway', etc.

Details the establishment of the National Highways Authority of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It specifies the composition of the Authority, including a Chairman, full-time members, and part-time members, appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of members
main_sections.description: States that the term of office and other conditions of service for members will be as prescribed.

Outlines the grounds on which a person can be disqualified from being appointed as a member, including criminal conviction, insolvency, unsound mind, dismissal from government service, or having a prejudicial financial or other interest.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of officers, consultants and other employees of the Authority
main_sections.description: Empowers the Authority to appoint necessary officers and employees, and also to appoint advisers or consultants, on terms and conditions laid down by regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to vest or entrust any national highway in the Authority
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to vest or entrust any national highway or a stretch thereof in the Authority through a notification.

main_sections.section_title: Compulsory acquisition of land for the Authority
main_sections.description: States that any land required by the Authority for its functions is deemed to be for a public purpose and can be acquired under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.

Details the primary functions of the Authority, which include the development, maintenance, and management of national highways. It also lists various ancillary functions such as constructing facilities, regulating vehicle plying, providing consultancy services, and advising the Central Government.

important_rules: The Authority shall act, so far as may be, on business principles in the discharge of its functions (Section 10).
Every contract on behalf of the Authority must be made by the Chairman or a designated member/officer, and certain contracts require prior approval of the Central Government (Section 15).
The Authority's primary function is to develop, maintain, and manage national highways and other highways vested in or entrusted to it (Section 16(1)).

The Authority may construct offices, workshops, hotels, motels, restaurants, and rest-rooms at or near highways, as well as residential buildings and townships for its employees (Section 16(2)(b), (c)).
The Authority can provide facilities and amenities for highway users to ensure smooth traffic flow (Section 16(2)(f)).
The Authority can form companies under the Companies Act, 1956, to improve the efficiency of its functions (Section 16(2)(g)).
The Authority can collect fees on behalf of the Central Government for services rendered under the National Highways Act, 1956, and other fees on behalf of State Governments (Section 16(2)(k)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Highways Authority of India, and potentially the Central Government for certain powers and oversight.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, rules, and regulations made thereunder. Enforcement would also involve the Central Government's oversight powers, such as superseding the Authority or issuing directions.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (Section 3(2)).
Right to contract (Section 3(2)).
Right to sue and be sued (Section 3(2)).
Right to compulsory acquire land for its functions (Section 13).
Right to enter upon lands for purposes related to highways (Section 30).
duties: Duty to develop, maintain, and manage national highways (Section 16(1)).
Duty to act on business principles (Section 10).
Duty to regulate and control the plying of vehicles on highways for proper management (Section 16(2)(d)).
obligations: Obligation to perform contracts entered into (Section 14).
Obligation to adhere to terms and conditions for appointment of officers and employees (Section 9).
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for transactions and meetings (Sections 7, 15).

key_procedures: Constitution of the Authority: Central Government appoints Chairman, full-time, and part-time members via notification (Section 3).
Vesting of National Highways: Central Government vests or entrusts national highways to the Authority by notification (Section 11).

Transfer of Assets and Liabilities: Upon notification under Section 11, assets, liabilities, and contracts of the Central Government related to the highway are deemed transferred to the Authority (Section 12).

Contract Execution: Contracts are made by the Chairman or authorized personnel, with specific requirements for sealing, value limits, and Central Government approval for certain contracts (Section 15).
Reporting and Audit: The Authority prepares an annual report and accounts, which are audited and laid before Parliament along with the auditor's report (Sections 22, 23, 24).
Rule Making: Central Government can make rules, and the Authority can make regulations, both of which are laid before Parliament (Sections 34, 35, 37).
administration: The National Highways Authority of India, with oversight and rule-making powers vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act has been amended by the National Highways Laws (Amendment) Act, 1997, and the National Highways Authority of India (Amendment) Act, 2013.

The Central Government has the power to temporarily divest the Authority of the management of any national highway or to supersede the Authority if it fails to discharge its functions or acts in a manner prejudicial to the public interest (Sections 31, 32).
Employees of the Authority are considered public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code (Section 27).
Actions taken in good faith by the Authority or its employees are protected from legal proceedings (Section 28).

title: The Assam University Act, 1989
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Assam and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The jurisdiction of the University extends to the Cachar, Karimganj, North Cachar Hills, Karbi Anglong, and Hailakandi Districts of the State of Assam. All Colleges situated in these districts are affiliated to the University. The University is open to all classes, castes, and creeds.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.distance education system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more such means.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University, and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.University: The Assam University established under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, academic staff, distance education system, employee, and University, among others.

Establishes the Assam University, states its headquarters at Silchar with the possibility of establishing campuses elsewhere, and constitutes it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objects of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, promoting integrated courses, fostering inter-disciplinary studies, educating and training manpower for Assam's development, and improving the social, economic, intellectual, academic, and cultural conditions of the people of the State.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting diplomas and degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, conferring honorary degrees, utilizing distance education, instituting academic positions, recognizing and withdrawing recognition of institutions, creating posts, collaborating with other institutions, establishing campuses and centres, awarding fellowships and scholarships, establishing and maintaining colleges and halls, providing research and advisory services, organizing refresher courses, admitting colleges and institutions, appointing visiting professors, conferring autonomous status, determining admission standards, levying fees, supervising student residences, laying down conditions of service for employees, regulating discipline, promoting employee welfare, receiving benefactions, borrowing money, and performing other necessary acts.
Defines the geographical jurisdiction of the University and states that all colleges within this jurisdiction shall be affiliated to the University.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all individuals regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, prohibiting any religious tests for appointment, admission, or enjoyment of privileges. It allows for special provisions for women, physically handicapped, and weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University, granting powers to review work and progress, order inspections and inquiries, and issue directions that the University must comply with.

important_rules: The University must be open to all individuals regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, without imposing religious tests for employment, admission, or privileges.
The Visitor (President of India) has the power to review the University's work, conduct inspections and inquiries, and issue binding directions.
The University has broad powers to provide education, conduct research, grant degrees, affiliate institutions, and manage its operations and finances.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government can appoint persons to review the University's work and issue directions. The University itself is empowered to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, and directions issued by the Visitor. The University enforces discipline through its own disciplinary measures.

rights: Right to receive education and research facilities.
Right to be admitted without discrimination based on caste, creed, or religion.
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases (as implied by Section 33 and 34).
duties: Duty to disseminate and advance knowledge.
Duty to provide instructional and research facilities.
Duty to improve social and economic conditions and welfare of the people of Assam.
Duty to comply with directions from the Visitor.
obligations: The University is bound to comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
The University must ensure fairness and non-discrimination in admissions and employment.

key_procedures: Appointment of the Visitor (President of India) and their powers to review, inspect, and direct.
Establishment of University authorities like the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.
Making of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Procedure for inspection and inquiry by the Visitor.
Procedure for appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
administration: The Assam University, established by the Act, with its headquarters in Silchar. The President of India is the Visitor. Various authorities like the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council are part of its administration.
important_notes: The Act allows for special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped, or persons belonging to weaker sections of society.
The Act was amended by the Assam University (Amendment) Act, 1995.
The Act specifies the jurisdiction of the University to specific districts in Assam.

title: The Nagaland University Act, 1989
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Nagaland and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Nagaland. It establishes the Nagaland University, which will take over affiliations and privileges previously held by the North-Eastern Hill University within Nagaland. The University is open to all individuals regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, with provisions for special considerations for women, the physically handicapped, and weaker sections of society, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.University: The Nagaland University established under this Act.
key_definitions.distance education system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more such means.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University, and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.recognised Institution: An institution of higher learning recognised by the University.
key_definitions.teachers of the University: Professors, Readers, Lecturers and such other persons as may be appointed for imparting instruction or conducting research in the University or in any College or Institution maintained by the University and are designated as teachers by the Ordinances.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Nagaland University Act, 1989' and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, academic staff, Board of Studies, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, College, Court, Department, distance education system, employee, Executive Council, Hall, Institution, North-Eastern Hill University, Planning Board, Principal, recognised Institution, recognised teachers, Regulations, School, Statutes, Ordinances, teachers of the University, and University.

This section establishes the 'Nagaland University'. It specifies the headquarters to be at Lumami with potential for other campuses. It also constitutes the first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and members of various authorities as a body corporate, granting the University perpetual succession, a common seal, and the ability to sue and be sued.

This section outlines the objectives of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge through instruction and research, offering integrated courses in various disciplines, promoting innovations in teaching-learning and inter-disciplinary studies, educating and training manpower for the development of Nagaland, and improving the social, economic, intellectual, academic, and cultural conditions of the people of Nagaland.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of properties of North-Eastern Hill University
main_sections.description: This section stipulates that upon commencement of the Act, all properties of the North-Eastern Hill University within the State of Nagaland will be transferred to and vest in the Nagaland University, to be applied for its established objects.

This extensive section details the powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, granting diplomas and degrees, organizing extra-mural studies, conferring honorary degrees, providing distance education, instituting academic positions, recognizing institutions, creating posts, collaborating with other bodies, establishing campuses and specialized units, awarding fellowships and scholarships, establishing and maintaining Colleges and Institutions, providing research and advisory services, organizing refresher courses, admitting colleges and institutions to its privileges, appointing visiting professors, conferring autonomous status, determining admission standards, demanding fees, supervising student residences, laying down conditions of service for employees, regulating discipline, making provisions for employee welfare, receiving benefactions, acquiring and disposing of property, and borrowing money with Central Government approval.

The jurisdiction of the University extends to the entire State of Nagaland. All colleges, institutions, schools, and departments affiliated with or maintained by the North-Eastern Hill University in Nagaland will be affiliated with or maintained by the Nagaland University. The North-Eastern Hill University will cease to exercise its jurisdiction in Nagaland from the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: The University is open to all persons regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, or class. No religious test shall be imposed for appointment, admission, graduation, or enjoyment of privileges. However, special provisions can be made for women, the physically handicapped, and weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

The President of India is the Visitor of the University. The Visitor can appoint persons to review the University's work and progress, and based on their report and after consulting the Executive Council, can issue directions which the University must comply with. The Visitor also has the right to order inspections of the University's facilities.

important_rules: The University shall be open to all persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class, without any religious test.
Special provisions may be made for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped or persons belonging to weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The University shall have the power to provide for instruction and research, grant diplomas and degrees, organize extra-mural studies, and confer honorary degrees.
The University's jurisdiction is limited to the State of Nagaland.
All properties of the North-Eastern Hill University within Nagaland shall be transferred to the Nagaland University.
The President of India, as the Visitor, has the power to review the University's work, issue directions, and cause inspections.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government may, by notification, appoint a date for the commencement of the Act. The Visitor (President of India) has powers to direct actions and ensure compliance. The University itself is empowered to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Visitor, the Central Government's notifications, and the University's own regulatory and disciplinary mechanisms as outlined in its powers.

rights: Right to access education and University privileges for all individuals irrespective of caste, creed, sex, or race.
Right of the Visitor to review University work, issue directions, and conduct inspections.
Right of the University to grant diplomas, certificates, and degrees.
Right of the University to recognize institutions and appoint staff.
duties: Duty of the University to disseminate and advance knowledge.
Duty of the University to provide instructional and research facilities.
Duty of the University to promote innovations in teaching-learning and research.
Duty of the University to educate and train manpower for the development of Nagaland.
Duty of the University to improve the social and economic conditions and welfare of the people of Nagaland.
Duty of the University to comply with directions issued by the Visitor.
obligations: Obligation for the University to be open to all classes, castes, and creeds.
Obligation for the University to comply with the directions of the Visitor.
Obligation for the University to apply transferred properties to its established objects.
Obligation for the University to adhere to Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations for its functioning.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.

Visitor's Review and Inspection: The Visitor can appoint persons to review the University's work and progress. Based on the report, the Visitor can issue directions after obtaining the views of the Executive Council. The Visitor also has the right to order inspections.

Making Statutes and Ordinances: The Act outlines the power to make Statutes and Ordinances, and how they are to be made, though the detailed procedures are likely in separate sections of the Act not fully provided in the excerpt.
Publication of Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations: Section 47 mentions that these are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
administration: The administration of the University is through its various authorities like the Visitor, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Executive Council, and Academic Council, as detailed in the Act. The Central Government appoints the commencement date. The Ministry responsible for higher education in the Central Government would oversee the implementation aspects related to the Act.
important_notes: The Act was amended by The Repealing and Amending Act, 2001 (30 of 2001).
Section 48 has been repealed.
The commencement date for the Act was notified as September 6, 1994.

title: The Small Industries Development Bank of India Act, 1989
purpose: To establish the Small Industries Development Bank of India as the principal financial institution for the promotion, financing and development of industry in the small-scale sector and to co-ordinate the functions of the institutions engaged in the promotion, financing or developing industry in the small-scale sector.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to industrial concerns in the small-scale sector.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of directors of the Small Industries Development Bank of India.
key_definitions.Court: The High Court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the defendant or respondent has their registered office or carries on business, or the cause of action for legal proceedings wholly or in part arises.
key_definitions.Development Bank: The Industrial Development Bank of India established under section 3 of the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964.
key_definitions.Director: A Director nominated under sub-section (1) of section 6, and includes the chairman and managing director and whole-time director.
key_definitions.export: Export from India of products or services of any industrial concern in the small-scale sector.
key_definitions.import: Import into India of services or goods including all materials, commodities and articles in a solid, liquid or gaseous state and all forms of energy for the use of any industrial concern in the small-scale sector.
key_definitions.industrial concern in the small scale se: Any concern engaged or to be engaged in a wide range of activities including manufacture, preservation or processing of goods, shipping, mining, hotel industry, transport, generation/storage/distribution of electricity, maintenance/repair/testing/servicing of machinery, assembling/repairing/packing of articles, setting up of industrial areas/estates, fishing, providing special/technical knowledge or services for industrial growth, providing engineering/technical/financial/management/marketing services, service industry, providing medical/health services, providing IT/telecommunication/electronics services, leasing/sub-leasing/hire-purchase of industrial plants/equipment, and such other activities as specified by the Central Government, or research and development related to these, and which is regarded as a small-scale undertaking under section 11B of the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.
key_definitions.Small Industries Bank: The Small Industries Development Bank of India established under sub-section (1) of section 3.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the commencement date.
Defines various terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Small Industries Development Bank of India
main_sections.description: Establishes the Small Industries Development Bank of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract. It also specifies the head office and the establishment of offices/branches.
Specifies the authorized capital of the Small Industries Bank and allows for its increase by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Conversion of equity shares into redeemable preference shares
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to convert equity shares into redeemable preference shares under certain conditions, ensuring a minimum equity holding.
Outlines the management structure of the Small Industries Bank.
Details the constitution of the Board of Directors.
Defines the business that the Small Industries Bank can conduct.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of Small Industries Bank in case of default
main_sections.description: Specifies the rights of the Small Industries Bank when a borrower defaults.

main_sections.section_title: Power to seek assistance of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate
main_sections.description: Grants the Small Industries Bank the power to seek assistance from the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate.
Provides for the liquidation process of the Small Industries Bank.
Grants the power to make regulations for the Act.

important_rules: The Small Industries Development Bank of India shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Small Industries Bank shall establish offices, branches or agencies at any place in or outside India.
The authorised capital of the Small Industries Bank can be increased by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Board.
The Central Government can convert equity shares into redeemable preference shares, subject to certain conditions, to ensure a minimum equity holding.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Small Industries Bank, and potentially Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate for assistance in certain cases.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of rights in case of default, power to seek assistance of magistrates, and special provisions for enforcement of claims.

rights: Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
Right to contract.
Right to sue or be sued in its name.
Rights in case of default by borrowers.
duties: To act as the principal financial institution for the promotion, financing and development of industry in the small-scale sector.
To coordinate the functions of institutions engaged in the promotion, financing or developing industry in the small-scale sector.

key_procedures: Establishment and incorporation of the Small Industries Development Bank of India.
Management and constitution of the Board of Directors.
Conducting the business of the Small Industries Bank.
Seeking assistance from Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate in certain situations.
Liquidation of the Small Industries Bank.
Making regulations by the Central Government and the Small Industries Bank.
administration: Central Government and the Board of Directors of the Small Industries Development Bank of India.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The Act may be amended by subsequent Acts, as indicated in the 'List of Amending Acts'.

title: The National Commission for Women Act, 1990
purpose: To constitute a National Commission for Women and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The Act establishes the National Commission for Women to address issues related to women's rights and safeguards.

key_definitions.Commission: The National Commission for Women constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Commission and includes the Member-Secretary.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date it comes into force by notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Commission', 'Member', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the National Commission for Women
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Commission for Women, outlining its composition which includes a Chairperson, five Members nominated by the Central Government (with representation from Scheduled Castes and Tribes), and a Member-Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Defines the term of office for the Chairperson and Members (not exceeding three years), conditions for resignation, and grounds for removal by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and other employees of the Commission
main_sections.description: States that the Central Government shall provide the Commission with necessary officers and employees for its functions.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries and allowances to be paid out of grants
main_sections.description: Specifies that salaries and allowances of the Chairperson, Members, and staff are paid out of the grants received by the Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of the Commission
main_sections.description: Ensures that the proceedings of the Commission are not invalidated due to vacancies or defects in its constitution.
Empowers the Commission to appoint committees for special issues and to co-opt non-members.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be regulated by the Commission
main_sections.description: Outlines that the Commission and its committees shall meet as necessary and that the Commission shall regulate its own procedure. It also specifies how orders and decisions are authenticated.

Details the wide-ranging functions of the Commission, including investigating safeguards for women, presenting reports to the Central Government, recommending amendments to laws, taking up cases of violations, looking into complaints, undertaking studies on discrimination, promoting research, participating in planning, evaluating development, inspecting institutions, funding litigation, and reporting on matters pertaining to women.
States that the Central Government shall provide grants to the Commission for its purposes.
Mandates the Commission to maintain proper accounts and records, and specifies that these accounts will be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
Requires the Commission to prepare and submit an annual report on its activities to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and audit report to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Directs the Central Government to lay the annual report and audit report before each House of Parliament, along with a memorandum explaining the action taken on recommendations.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson, Members and staff of the Commission to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares that the Chairperson, Members, and staff of the Commission are considered public servants.
Requires the Central Government to consult the Commission on certain matters.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: The Commission shall consist of a Chairperson committed to the cause of women, five Members with diverse experience, and a Member-Secretary.
The Chairperson and Members shall hold office for a period not exceeding three years.
The Central Government can remove a Chairperson or Member under specific circumstances such as insolvency, conviction, unsound mind, or abuse of position, after providing a hearing.
The Commission has the power to investigate and examine matters relating to safeguards for women, present reports, and recommend amendments to laws.
The Commission can take up cases of violation of constitutional provisions and laws relating to women with appropriate authorities.
The Commission can call for special studies and investigations into problems faced by women.
The Commission has the power to inspect jails, remand homes, and other institutions where women are kept.
The Central Government shall lay the Commission's annual report and audit report before Parliament.
The Chairperson, Members, and staff of the Commission are considered public servants.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the National Commission for Women.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigations, recommendations, taking up cases with appropriate authorities, and the power to summon persons and demand documents during investigations (similar to a civil court).

rights: Women have the right to safeguards provided by the Constitution and other laws.
Women have the right to equality and development.
Women have the right to protection against discrimination and atrocities.
Women have the right to access to housing and basic services, and adequate support services.
Women have the right to relief and welfare measures.
duties: The Central Government has a duty to constitute and provide resources to the National Commission for Women.
The Central Government has a duty to consider and act upon the recommendations of the Commission.
The Commission has a duty to investigate, report, and recommend measures for the welfare and advancement of women.
The Commission has a duty to protect women from deprivation of rights and non-implementation of laws.
obligations: The Central Government is obligated to lay the Commission's reports before Parliament.
State Governments are obligated to consider reports relating to them and lay them before the State Legislature.
The Commission is obligated to prepare and submit annual reports.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Commission: The Central Government constitutes the National Commission for Women with a specified composition.
Term of Office and Removal: The Chairperson and Members serve for a fixed term, with provisions for resignation and removal under defined circumstances.
Functions Execution: The Commission performs its functions by investigating, presenting reports, making recommendations, taking up cases, and conducting studies.

Reporting and Laying Before Parliament: The Commission submits annual reports which, along with the Central Government's action taken memorandum, are laid before Parliament. State-specific reports are forwarded to State Governments for laying before State Legislatures.
Investigation Powers: The Commission has civil court powers during investigations, including summoning witnesses, demanding documents, and receiving evidence on affidavits.
administration: The Central Government.
important_notes: The Act was amended by The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, which omitted the exception of the State of Jammu and Kashmir from its extent.
The Act came into force on January 31, 1992.

title: The Armed Forces (Jammu and Kashmir) Special Powers Act, 1990
purpose: To confer special powers upon members of the armed forces operating in disturbed areas within the State of Jammu and Kashmir to assist civil administration in containing terrorism and subversive activities.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh) and applies to areas declared as 'disturbed areas'.

key_definitions.armed forces: Includes the military forces and air forces operating as land forces, and any other armed forces of the Union so operating.
key_definitions.disturbed area: An area declared as such by notification under Section 3.
key_definitions.terrorist act: Has the same meaning as in Explanation to Article 248 of the Constitution of India as applicable to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (the whole of Jammu and Kashmir), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on July 5, 1990).
Defines 'armed forces' and 'disturbed area', and states that other undefined words and expressions shall have meanings assigned in the Air Force Act, 1950, or the Army Act, 1950.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare areas to be disturbed areas
main_sections.description: Empowers the Governor of Jammu and Kashmir or the Central Government to declare any part or the whole of the State as a disturbed area if it is in a disturbed and dangerous condition, necessitating the use of armed forces to prevent terrorist acts or activities disrupting sovereignty and territorial integrity.

main_sections.section_title: Special powers of the armed forces
main_sections.description: Grants specific powers to commissioned officers, warrant officers, non-commissioned officers, or equivalent ranks in the armed forces in disturbed areas. These include powers to fire upon or use force (even causing death) to prevent unlawful assemblies or carrying of weapons, destroy arms dumps or fortified positions, arrest without warrant, and enter and search premises.

main_sections.section_title: Power of search to include powers to break open locks, etc.
main_sections.description: Authorizes persons conducting searches under the Act to break open locks if the key is withheld.

main_sections.section_title: Arrested persons and seized property to be made over to the police
main_sections.description: Mandates that any person arrested or property seized under the Act must be handed over to the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station with a report of the circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting in good faith under this Act
main_sections.description: Prohibits prosecution, suits, or legal proceedings against any person for anything done or purported to be done in good faith in exercise of powers under this Act, except with the previous sanction of the Central Government.

Repeals the Armed Forces (Jammu and Kashmir) Special Powers Ordinance, 1990, and states that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: In a disturbed area, armed forces personnel can use force, even to the extent of causing death, against persons acting in contravention of laws prohibiting assemblies of five or more persons or the carrying of weapons or explosives, after giving due warning.
Rule 2: Armed forces can destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, shelters used for armed attacks, or training camps/hide-outs used by armed gangs or wanted absconders.
Rule 3: Armed forces can arrest without warrant any person who has committed or is reasonably suspected of committing a cognizable offense and use necessary force for the arrest.

Rule 4: Armed forces can enter and search premises without warrant to make an arrest, recover wrongfully restrained persons, or seize stolen property, arms, ammunition, or explosives, using necessary force.

Rule 5: Armed forces can stop, search, and seize any vehicle or vessel reasonably suspected of carrying a proclaimed offender, a person involved in a non-cognizable offense, or unlawfully held arms/explosives, using necessary force.
Rule 6: Any person arrested or property seized under the Act must be handed over to the nearest police station promptly with details of the circumstances.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Members of the armed forces (commissioned officers, warrant officers, non-commissioned officers, and equivalent ranks).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of special powers granted by the Act, including use of force, arrest, search, and seizure.

rights: Right to protection from prosecution for acts done in good faith under the Act, subject to Central Government sanction.
duties: Duty to hand over arrested persons and seized property to the nearest police station with a report.
obligations: Obligation for armed forces personnel to act within the scope of powers granted by the Act.
Obligation for the Central Government to grant sanction for prosecution in certain cases.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Declaration of a disturbed area involves the Governor or Central Government issuing a notification in the Official Gazette based on opinion of disturbed conditions.
Procedure 2: Arrest and seizure involve armed forces personnel making an arrest or seizure, and then making over the person or property to the nearest police station with a report of circumstances.
administration: While specific administrative departments are not explicitly mentioned for day-to-day administration, the Central Government has a role in declaring disturbed areas and sanctioning prosecutions. The enforcement is carried out by the armed forces.
important_notes: The Act was initially promulgated to address increasing militant and subversive activities and the need for enhanced powers for security forces.
The Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh since October 30, 2019.

title: The Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) Act, 1990
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Broadcasting Corporation for India, to be known as Prasar Bharati, to define its composition, functions and powers and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It establishes the Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) and outlines its structure, functions, and operations.

key_definitions.Akashvani: The offices, stations and other establishments, by whatever name called, which, immediately before the appointed day, formed part of or were under the Director-General, All India Radio of the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed under section 3.
key_definitions.broadcasting: The dissemination of any form of communication like signs, signals, writing, pictures, images and sounds of all kinds by transmission of electro-magnetic waves through space or through cables intended to be received by the general public either directly or indirectly through the medium of relay stations and all its grammatical variations and cognate expressions shall be construed accordingly.
key_definitions.Corporation: The Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) established under section 3.
key_definitions.Doordarshan: The offices, kendras and other establishments, by whatever name called, which, immediately before the appointed day, formed part of or were under the Directorate-General, Doordarshan of the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement by notification by the Central Government.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Akashvani', 'appointed day', 'broadcasting', 'Corporation', 'Doordarshan', etc.

This section outlines the establishment of the Prasar Bharati Corporation, its corporate status, headquarters, and the composition of its governing body, the Prasar Bharati Board, which includes a Chairman, Executive Member, Member (Finance), Member (Personnel), Part-time Members, ex officio members, a nominated representative, and employee representatives.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chairman and other Members
main_sections.description: This section details the appointment process for the Chairman and other Members (excluding ex officio, nominated, and elected members) by the President of India based on a recommendation committee. It also specifies the qualifications for different types of members.
This section enumerates the functions and powers of the Prasar Bharati Corporation, which would typically involve broadcasting services and related activities.
This section likely pertains to the oversight role of a Parliamentary Committee concerning the Corporation's activities.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Broadcasting Council, term of office and removal, etc., of members thereof
main_sections.description: This section deals with the establishment, composition, tenure, and removal of members of a Broadcasting Council.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of certain assets, liabilities, etc., of Central Government to Corporation
main_sections.description: This section covers the transfer of assets and liabilities from the Central Government to the Corporation.
This section grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
This section empowers the Corporation to make regulations for the efficient performance of its functions.

important_rules: The Central Government may appoint a date for the commencement of the Act by notification (Section 1(3)).
The Prasar Bharati Board is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Corporation's affairs (Section 3(4)).
The Chairman and other Members (except ex officio, nominated, and elected) are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee (Section 4(1)).
The Chairman, Member (Finance), and Member (Personnel) shall hold office for specific terms and until a certain age, with provisions for amendment Acts affecting these terms (Section 6).

rights: Right to sue and be sued by the Corporation (Section 3(2)).
Right of persons associated with the Corporation to attend and discuss matters, but not to vote (Section 3(7)).
duties: The Corporation shall be managed under the superintendence, direction, and management of the Prasar Bharati Board (Section 3(4)).
Members of the Corporation are subject to removal and suspension under certain conditions (Section 7).
obligations: The Corporation has the power to acquire, hold and dispose of property, and to contract (Section 3(2)).
Whole-time Members are employees of the Corporation and are entitled to salaries, allowances, and subject to conditions of service as may be prescribed (Section 6(7)).

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairman and Members: A committee, chaired by the Chairman of the Council of States, recommends individuals for appointment by the President of India (Section 4).
Establishment of the Corporation: The Central Government notifies the date of establishment, after which the Corporation legally exists and operates (Section 3(1)).
Conduct of Meetings: The Board shall hold meetings as per prescribed procedures (implied by Section 8).
administration: The Central Government plays a significant role in the Act's administration through notifications, giving directions, obtaining information, and making rules. The Prasar Bharati Board is the primary administrative body of the Corporation.
important_notes: The Act underwent amendments in 2002, 2008, and 2011, which may have altered certain provisions, particularly concerning the term of office for Chairman and Executive Member (as indicated by the amendment act references).
A Broadcasting Council is established, suggesting a mechanism for public grievances or oversight of broadcasting content.
The Act specifies that Chairman and Members of the Corporation are considered public servants (Section 27).

title: The Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991
purpose: To prohibit the conversion of any place of worship and to provide for the maintenance of the religious character of any place of worship as it existed on the 15th day of August, 1947, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now applicable to Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh). It applies to all places of worship, prohibiting their conversion and mandating the preservation of their religious character as of August 15, 1947.

key_definitions.commencement of this Act: The commencement of this Act on the 11th day of July, 1991.
key_definitions.conversion: Includes alteration or change of whatever nature.
key_definitions.place of worship: Means a temple, mosque, gurudwara, church, monastery or any other place of public religious worship of any religious denomination or any section thereof, by whatever name called.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir, now extended), and the dates on which its provisions come into force.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'commencement of this Act', 'conversion', and 'place of worship'.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of conversion of places of worship
main_sections.description: Prohibits the conversion of any place of worship of any religious denomination or any section thereof into a place of worship of a different section of the same religious denomination or of a different religious denomination.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to the religious character of certain places of worship and bar of jurisdiction of courts, etc.
main_sections.description: Declares that the religious character of a place of worship existing on August 15, 1947, shall continue as it existed on that day. It also abates pending suits, appeals, or other proceedings regarding conversion and bars future proceedings, with certain exceptions.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid
main_sections.description: Exempts the place or place of worship commonly known as Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid situated in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, and any related legal proceedings from the purview of this Act.
Prescribes punishment for contravention of Section 3, including imprisonment and fine, and also covers attempts and abetment.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force.
This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2001.

important_rules: No person shall convert any place of worship of any religious denomination or any section thereof into a place of worship of a different section of the same religious denomination or of a different religious denomination or any section thereof (Section 3).
The religious character of a place of worship existing on the 15th day of August, 1947, shall continue to be the same as it existed on that day (Section 4(1)).

Any suit, appeal, or other proceeding pending on the commencement of the Act with respect to the conversion of the religious character of a place of worship existing on August 15, 1947, shall abate. No further proceedings shall lie in any court, tribunal, or authority regarding such matters (Section 4(2)).
The Act does not apply to the Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid in Ayodhya (Section 5).
The provisions of this Act shall override any inconsistent provisions in other existing laws (Section 7).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also liability to fine for contravention of Section 3.
Punishment for attempts to commit an offence punishable under Section 6(1).
Punishment for abetting or being a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable under Section 6(1).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, tribunals, and other authorities are involved in the abatement and barring of proceedings. The specific authority for direct enforcement and prosecution is not explicitly detailed beyond the penalties prescribed.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is primarily through the judicial system by barring proceedings related to conversion after the specified date and through criminal penalties for contravention of the prohibition on conversion.

rights: Right to have a place of worship maintain its religious character as it existed on August 15, 1947.
Protection against conversion of places of worship.
duties: Duty not to convert any place of worship.
Duty to maintain the religious character of a place of worship as it existed on August 15, 1947.
obligations: Obligation on individuals to refrain from converting places of worship.
Obligation on the legal system to abate and bar proceedings related to unlawful conversions post-August 15, 1947.

key_procedures: Abatement of pending suits, appeals, or other proceedings concerning the conversion of the religious character of places of worship existing on August 15, 1947, upon commencement of the Act (Section 4(2)).
Barring of future suits, appeals, or other proceedings in courts, tribunals, or other authorities regarding such matters after the commencement of the Act (Section 4(2)).
Prosecution and sentencing of individuals who contravene Section 3, including attempts and abetment (Section 6).
administration: The Act is administered through the judicial system and by relevant government authorities responsible for law enforcement and public order. The specific ministry is not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but the Statement of Objects and Reasons indicates it was moved by S.B. Chavan, who was likely a minister at the time.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to places of worship that are ancient and historical monuments or archaeological sites/remains under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, or similar laws.
The Act does not affect any suit, appeal, or proceeding that was finally decided, settled, or disposed of by a court, tribunal, or other authority before the commencement of the Act.
The Act does not apply to disputes settled by parties amongst themselves or conversions effected by acquiescence or barred by limitation before the commencement of the Act.
The exemption for Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid is absolute.
The commencement date for sections 3, 6, and 8 is immediate, while other provisions are deemed to have come into force on July 11, 1991.

title: The Destructive Insects and Pests (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1992
purpose: To further amend the Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914, specifically to validate the levy and collection of fees for services related to plant quarantine and to empower the government to levy such fees for services rendered and for maintaining plant quarantine organizations. This amendment was necessitated by court rulings that questioned the government's authority to levy these fees.
scope: This Act applies to the import of articles and insects that may be destructive to crops in India. It specifically addresses the regulation and inspection of imported plants, fruits, and seeds.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Destructive Insects and Pests (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1992, and specifies that it is deemed to have come into force on October 27, 1989.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 3 of Act 2 of 1914
main_sections.description: This section, which originally aimed to amend section 3 of the principal Act (Act 2 of 1914), was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2001.
