This section validates, notwithstanding any court order, a notification issued on October 27, 1989, under section 3(1) of the principal Act. It also validates any fees levied or collected for applications for import permits, inspection, fumigation, disinfection, disinfestation, or supervision of articles or insects. It clarifies that no suits for refund of such fees shall be maintained, and any uncollected fees may be recovered. It also clarifies that actions taken under the principal Act are deemed valid.

This section repeals the Destructive Insects and Pests (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1992 (Ord. 4 of 1992). It also states that anything done or action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Notification No. S.O.867(E), dated October 27, 1989, issued under section 3(1) of the principal Act, is deemed to have been validly issued.

Rule 2: Any fees levied or collected, or purported to have been levied or collected, for making an application for a permit to import, or for making inspection, fumigation, disinfection, disinfestation, or supervision of any article or insect under the principal Act or the said notification, are deemed to have been validly levied or collected.
Rule 3: Fees levied but not collected may be recovered under the principal Act as amended by this Act.
Rule 4: Anything done or action taken under or for the purposes of the principal Act shall be deemed to have been validly done or taken.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government is empowered to levy fees and regulate import through notifications under the principal Act, which is amended by this Act. The enforcement authority for specific actions and collection of fees would be implied to be governmental agencies responsible for plant quarantine and trade regulation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the validation of past actions and the continued authority of the Central Government to levy fees for services related to plant quarantine and import regulation under the principal Act.

rights: Right to question the levy or collection of fees in accordance with the provisions of the principal Act, as amended by this Act, or the notification issued under section 3 of the principal Act.
Right to claim refund of any fees paid in excess of the amount due under the principal Act, as amended by this Act, or the said notification.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application for a permit to import articles or insects.
Procedure 2: Inspection, fumigation, disinfection, disinfestation, or supervision of imported articles or insects.
Procedure 3: Levy and collection of fees for the aforementioned services.
administration: The administration of the principal Act, as amended, would fall under the purview of the Central Government, specifically departments dealing with agriculture, plant protection, and quarantine.
important_notes: The Act aims to address legal challenges to the government's authority to collect fees for plant quarantine services.
The validation extends to past actions and collections, ensuring continuity and preventing retrospective legal challenges.
The Act does not prevent persons from questioning the levy or collection of fees or claiming refunds for overpayments, within the framework of the amended Act and notification.

title: The National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
purpose: To constitute a National Commission for Minorities and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, with the objective of evaluating the safeguards provided in the Constitution for the protection of minorities and making recommendations for ensuring their implementation.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to communities notified as minorities by the Central Government.

key_definitions.Commission: The National Commission for Minorities constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Commission, including the Vice-Chairperson.
key_definitions.minority: A community notified as such by the Central Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India), and outlines the process for its commencement through a Central Government notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Commission', 'Member', 'minority', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the National Commission for Minorities
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Commission for Minorities, consisting of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, and five Members nominated by the Central Government. Five Members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office (three years) for the Chairperson and Members, their resignation process, and the grounds for removal by the Central Government. It also mentions that vacancies are filled by fresh nominations and terms of service are prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and other employees of the Commission
main_sections.description: Details the provision of a Secretary and other necessary officers and employees for the Commission by the Central Government, with their terms and conditions of service being prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries and allowances to be paid out of grants
main_sections.description: States that salaries and allowances of the Chairperson, Members, and staff, as well as administrative expenses, are paid out of the grants provided by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of the Commission
main_sections.description: Ensures that the existence of any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Commission does not invalidate its acts or proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be regulated by the Commission
main_sections.description: Grants the Commission the power to regulate its own procedure, including meeting times and places, and stipulates that its orders and decisions must be authenticated by the Secretary or an authorized officer.

Outlines the various functions of the Commission, including evaluating development progress, monitoring safeguards, making recommendations for their implementation, investigating complaints, studying discrimination, conducting research on socio-economic and educational development, and submitting reports to the Central Government. It also grants the Commission powers of a civil court when performing certain functions.
Specifies that the Central Government shall provide grants to the Commission for its purposes, and the Commission may utilize these sums for its functions.
Requires the Commission to maintain proper accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts, which are to be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
Mandates the Commission to prepare an annual report detailing its activities and forward it to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and audit report to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to lay the Commission's annual report and the audit report before both Houses of Parliament, along with a memorandum explaining the action taken on recommendations.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson, Members and staff of the Commission to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Chairperson, Members, and staff of the Commission as public servants under the Indian Penal Code.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions, covering matters like terms of service, accounts, and reports. These rules must be laid before Parliament.

Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act, with such orders to be laid before Parliament. This power is limited to a period of two years from the commencement of the Act.

important_rules: The Chairperson and Members shall hold office for a term of three years.
The Central Government shall provide a Secretary and other necessary officers and employees for the Commission.
The Commission shall evaluate the progress of development of minorities, monitor safeguards, and make recommendations.
The Commission shall investigate specific complaints regarding deprivation of rights and safeguards of minorities.
The Commission shall conduct studies on problems arising from discrimination against minorities.
The Commission shall prepare an annual report of its activities.
The Central Government shall lay the annual report and audit report before Parliament.
The Chairperson, Members, and staff of the Commission are considered public servants.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and by extension, the National Commission for Minorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the functions and powers assigned to the Commission, including the powers of a civil court. The Central Government enforces the Act by making rules, providing grants, and laying reports before Parliament.

rights: Minorities have rights and safeguards provided in the Constitution and laws, which the Commission monitors.
Individuals can lodge complaints with the Commission regarding deprivation of rights and safeguards.
The Commission has the right to summon and examine persons, require production of documents, and receive evidence on affidavits.
duties: The Central Government has a duty to constitute the Commission and provide it with necessary resources.
The Commission has a duty to perform its specified functions, including evaluation, monitoring, and making recommendations.
The Commission has a duty to prepare and submit annual reports.
The Central Government has a duty to lay reports before Parliament and take action on recommendations.
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to notify communities as minorities.
The Central Government has an obligation to make rules for the implementation of the Act.
State Governments have an obligation to lay before their respective Legislatures any recommendations from the Commission concerning them, along with action taken reports.

key_procedures: Nomination of Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and Members by the Central Government.
Resignation process for Chairperson and Members by writing to the Central Government.
Removal process for Chairperson or Member by the Central Government under specific conditions, with a right to be heard.
Filling of vacancies by fresh nomination.
The Commission meeting as and when necessary, with the Chairperson determining time and place.
The Commission regulating its own procedure.
Authentication of Commission's orders and decisions by the Secretary or an authorized officer.
Evaluation of minority development progress and monitoring of safeguards.
Investigating specific complaints regarding minority rights and safeguards with appropriate authorities.
Conducting studies and research on socio-economic and educational development of minorities.
Submission of periodical or special reports to the Central Government.
Central Government laying Commission's recommendations and action taken reports before Parliament.
State Governments laying Commission's recommendations concerning them before the State Legislature.
Preparation and submission of annual accounts and audit reports.
Preparation and submission of annual reports by the Commission.
Central Government making rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Central Government issuing orders to remove difficulties in implementation.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for the overall administration of the Act, including constituting the Commission, providing resources, making rules, and laying reports before Parliament. The National Commission for Minorities is the primary body for executing the Act's provisions.
important_notes: The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted from the extent clause by Act 34 of 2019, w.e.f. 31-10-2019, making the Act applicable to the entire territory of India.
The Act came into force on 17th May, 1993.
The composition of the Commission was amended by Act 41 of 1995, changing it to 'Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five Members'.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to a period of two years from the date of commencement of the Act.

title: The Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992
purpose: To provide for the development and regulation of foreign trade by facilitating imports into, and augmenting exports from, India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to foreign trade in goods, services, and technology involving India. Specific provisions also address Special Economic Zones. The Act's scope extends to actions that may be prejudicial to India's trade relations, national security, or international obligations.

key_definitions.Adjudicating Authority: The authority specified in, or under, section 13.
key_definitions.Appellate Authority: The authority specified in, or under, sub-section (1) of section 15.
key_definitions.conveyance: Any vehicle, vessel, aircraft or any other means of transport including any animal.
key_definitions.Director General: The Director General of Foreign Trade appointed under section 6.
key_definitions.import and export: In relation to goods, bringing into, or taking out of, India any goods by land, sea or air. In relation to services or technology, it includes various modes of supplying services or technology to or from India or involving Indian service consumers/suppliers, with specific provisions for Special Economic Zones.
key_definitions.Importer-exporter Code Number: The Code Number granted under section 7.
key_definitions.licence: A licence to import or export and includes a customs clearance permit and any other permission issued or granted under this Act.
key_definitions.Order: Any Order made by the Central Government under section 3.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.services: Service of any description which is made available to potential users and includes all the tradable services specified under the General Agreement on Trade in Services, excluding taxation.
key_definitions.service supplier: Any person who supplies a service and who intends to take benefit under the foreign trade policy.
key_definitions.specified goods or services or technolog: Goods or services or technology whose export, import, transfer, re-transfer, transit and transshipment is prohibited or restricted due to conditions related to India as a Nuclear Weapon State, national security, foreign policy, or international obligations concerning weapons of mass destruction.
key_definitions.technology: Any information (including information embodied in software), other than information in the public domain, that is capable of being used in the development, production or use of any goods or software, or the development of, or the carrying out of, an industrial or commercial activity or the provision of service of any kind.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for its provisions.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'import', 'export', 'services', 'technology', 'licence', and 'Director General'.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to make provisions relating to imports and exports
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions for the development and regulation of foreign trade, including prohibiting, restricting, or otherwise regulating the import or export of goods, services, or technology.
Allows the Central Government to formulate and announce the foreign trade policy and amend it through notification in the Official Gazette, with provisions for Special Economic Zones.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Director General and his functions
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of the Director General of Foreign Trade, who advises the Central Government on foreign trade policy and is responsible for its implementation. It also allows for delegation of powers to the Director General or subordinate officers.
Mandates that no person shall engage in import or export without an Importer-exporter Code Number, except under specific conditions for services or technology.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension and cancellation of Importer-exporter Code Number
main_sections.description: Outlines the grounds and procedures for suspending or cancelling an Importer-exporter Code Number, including contravention of the Act, rules, or policy, or acting in a manner prejudicial to India's trade interests.

main_sections.section_title: Issue, suspension and cancellation of licence
main_sections.description: Deals with the levying of fees for licences and the authority of the Director General to grant, renew, or refuse licences for import or export of specified goods, services, or technology.

main_sections.section_title: Power relating to search and seizure
main_sections.description: Grants powers for search and seizure of goods, documents, or conveyances related to contraventions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Contravention of provisions of this Act, rules, orders and foreign trade policy
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act, rules, orders, and foreign trade policy.

main_sections.section_title: Controls on export of specified goods, services and technology
main_sections.description: Introduces controls on the export of specified goods, services, and technology.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders passed under the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Repeals the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1947, and provides for savings.

important_rules: No person shall make any import or export except under an Importer-exporter Code Number granted by the Director General or an authorized officer (Section 7).
The Central Government can prohibit, restrict, or regulate the import or export of goods, services, or technology (Section 3(2)).
All goods to which an Order under Section 3(2) applies are deemed to have their import or export prohibited under the Customs Act, 1962 (Section 3(3)).
The Central Government may formulate and announce the foreign trade policy (Section 5).

No permit or licence is necessary for import or export of any goods, nor shall any goods be prohibited for import or export except as required under this Act, or rules or orders made thereunder (Section 3(4)).

Import and export of services or technology require an Importer-exporter Code Number only when the provider is availing benefits under the foreign trade policy or dealing with specified services or technologies (Section 7 proviso).

penalties: Contravention of the Act, rules, orders, or foreign trade policy can lead to penalties as prescribed (Section 11).
Penalties or confiscation under this Act do not interfere with other punishments that may be awarded under any other law (Section 12).
Specific penalties are outlined for offences related to controls on export of specified goods, services, and technology (Section 14E).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Director General of Foreign Trade and other officers authorized by the Central Government or the Director General.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of penalties, suspension or cancellation of Importer-exporter Code Numbers and licences, search and seizure of goods, and the application of relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

rights: Right to appeal against orders passed under the Act (Section 15).
Right to be heard before suspension or cancellation of Importer-exporter Code Number (Section 8(1)).
Right to receive a licence or permit unless refused with recorded reasons (Section 9(2)).
duties: Duty to obtain an Importer-exporter Code Number for import or export (Section 7).
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act, rules, orders, and foreign trade policy.
Duty to provide information requested by the Director General or authorized officer for the purpose of suspending or cancelling an Importer-exporter Code Number (Section 8(1)).
obligations: Importers and exporters have an obligation to conduct their trade in accordance with the regulations and policies set forth in the Act.
Entities involved in foreign trade have an obligation to ensure that their activities do not prejudice India's trade relations, national security, or international obligations.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining an Importer-exporter Code Number: Persons must apply for and obtain this code from the Director General or an authorized officer, following procedures specified by the Director General (Section 7).

Procedure for suspension/cancellation of Importer-exporter Code Number: The Director General or authorized officer may suspend or cancel the code after giving notice of the grounds and providing an opportunity for representation and hearing (Section 8(1)).
Procedure for appealing orders: Appeals against orders passed under the Act can be made to the Appellate Authority (Section 15).
administration: The Central Government, with the Director General of Foreign Trade acting as a key administrative figure.
important_notes: The Act came into force in parts, with Sections 11 to 14 effective immediately and other provisions deemed to have come into force on June 19, 1992 (Section 1(2)).
The definition of 'import' and 'export' was substituted in 2010 to include services and technology (Section 2(e)).
The Act allows for exceptions and modifications to the foreign trade policy for Special Economic Zones (Section 5 proviso).

title: The Rehabilitation Council of India Act, 1992
purpose: To provide for the constitution of the Rehabilitation Council of India for regulating and monitoring the training of rehabilitation professionals and personnel, promoting research in rehabilitation and special education, the maintenance of a Central Rehabilitation Register and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the regulation and monitoring of training for rehabilitation professionals and personnel in India, promotion of research in rehabilitation and special education, and the maintenance of a Central Rehabilitation Register. It also refers to the Persons With Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 for definitions related to disability.

key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Council appointed under sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.Council: The Rehabilitation Council of India constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.handicapped: A person suffering from any disability referred to in clause (i) of section 2 of the Persons With Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995.
key_definitions.mental retardation: A condition of arrested or incomplete development of mind of a person which is specially characterised by sub-normality of intelligence.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations.
key_definitions.recognised rehabilitation qualifications: Any of the qualifications included in the Schedule.
key_definitions.Register: The Central Rehabilitation Register maintained under sub-section (1) of section 23.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.rehabilitation: A process aimed at enabling persons with disabilities to reach and maintain their optimal physical, sensory, intellectual, psychiatric or social functional levels.
key_definitions.rehabilitation professionals: Includes audiologists and speech therapists, clinical psychologists, hearing aid and ear mould technicians, rehabilitation engineers and technicians, special teachers for educating and training the handicapped, vocational counsellors, employment officers and placement officers dealing with handicapped, multi-purpose rehabilitation therapists, technicians, and other categories notified by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Chairperson, Council, handicapped, mental retardation, notification, prescribed, recognised rehabilitation qualifications, Register, regulations, rehabilitation, and rehabilitation professionals. It also incorporates definitions from the Persons With Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 for undefined terms.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of Rehabilitation Council of India
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of the Rehabilitation Council of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It outlines the composition of the Council, including the Chairperson, representatives from Central Government ministries, University Grants Commission, Indian Council of Medical Research, States/Union Territories, voluntary organizations, medical practitioners, Members of Parliament, social workers, and the Member-Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of Chairperson and members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for the Chairperson and members as two years, or until their successor is appointed. It also covers filling casual vacancies, meeting frequency of the Council (at least once a year), and rules for presiding over meetings and voting.

Lists conditions that disqualify a person from being a member of the Council, including being of unsound mind, conviction of an offense involving moral turpitude, or being adjudicated as an insolvent.

Outlines circumstances under which a member's seat becomes vacant, such as becoming subject to disqualifications, absence from three consecutive meetings without excuse, or ceasing to be enrolled on the Indian Medical Register for certain members.

Details the Council's power to constitute an Executive Committee and other committees for various purposes. The Executive Committee is composed of the Chairperson and a specified number of members nominated by the Council. It outlines the powers and duties of these committees.

Provides for the appointment of a Member-Secretary by the Central Government to exercise powers and perform duties under the Council's direction. It also covers the Council's power to employ officers and other employees with the Central Government's sanction and to fix their allowances and terms of service.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies in the Council not to invalidate acts, etc.
main_sections.description: States that any act or proceeding of the Council or its committees will not be invalidated due to the existence of a vacancy or a defect in the constitution of the Council or committee.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of Rehabilitation Council and transfer of rights, liabilities and employees of Rehabilitation Council to Council
main_sections.description: Deals with the dissolution of the previous Rehabilitation Council upon the constitution of the new Council. It details the vesting of properties, transfer of rights and liabilities, continuation of contracts and legal proceedings, and the absorption or continuation of employees of the dissolved Council into the new Council.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of qualifications granted by University, etc., in India for rehabilitation professionals
main_sections.description: Empowers the Council to recognize qualifications granted by universities or other examining bodies in India for rehabilitation professionals.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of qualifications granted by institutions outside India
main_sections.description: Grants the Council the power to recognize qualifications granted by institutions outside India for rehabilitation professionals.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of persons possessing qualifications included in the Schedule to be enrolled
main_sections.description: Confers rights upon persons possessing recognized rehabilitation qualifications to be enrolled in the Register.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require information as to courses of study and examinations
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Council to seek information from universities and other examining bodies regarding their courses of study and examinations for rehabilitation professionals.
Empowers the Council to appoint inspectors to attend and report on examinations conducted for rehabilitation professionals.
Allows the Council to appoint visitors to attend and report on examinations conducted for rehabilitation professionals.
Grants the Council the power to withdraw recognition of any qualification if it finds that the course of study or examination is not up to the prescribed standards.
Empowers the Council to prescribe minimum standards of education for rehabilitation professionals.
Lays down the procedure for registration of rehabilitation professionals in the Central Rehabilitation Register.

main_sections.section_title: Privileges of persons who are registered on Register
main_sections.description: Specifies the privileges conferred upon persons whose names are entered on the Register.

main_sections.section_title: Professional conduct and removal of names from Register
main_sections.description: Deals with the professional conduct expected of registered rehabilitation professionals and the procedure for removal of names from the Register for misconduct.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal against order of removal from Register
main_sections.description: Provides for an appeal against an order of removal of a name from the Register.
Deals with the maintenance of the Central Rehabilitation Register.

main_sections.section_title: Information to be furnished by Council and publication thereof
main_sections.description: Requires the Council to furnish information to the Central Government and to publish such information.
Specifies the procedure for taking cognizance of offenses under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Employees of Council to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares employees of the Council as public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Council to make regulations, with the previous sanction of the Central Government, for the transaction of its business and other matters.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires that rules and regulations made under the Act be laid before each House of Parliament.

important_rules: Rule: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint the date on which the Act shall come into force.

Rule: The Council shall consist of a Chairperson, members representing various government ministries, institutions, voluntary organizations, medical practitioners, Parliament, and social workers, along with a Member-Secretary.

Rule: A member's seat shall become vacant if they become subject to disqualifications, are absent from three consecutive meetings without excuse, or cease to be enrolled on the Indian Medical Register (for certain members).
Rule: The Council shall constitute an Executive Committee and other committees to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Rule: The Council can recognize qualifications granted by Indian and foreign institutions for rehabilitation professionals.
Rule: Rehabilitation professionals meeting recognized qualifications have the right to be enrolled in the Central Rehabilitation Register.
Rule: The Council can withdraw recognition of qualifications if standards are not met.
Rule: Minimum standards of education for rehabilitation professionals are to be prescribed by the Council.
Rule: Names can be removed from the Register for professional misconduct, with a provision for appeal.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Rehabilitation Council of India, with oversight from the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the recognition and de-recognition of qualifications, maintenance of a Central Rehabilitation Register, prescribing educational standards, and through provisions for offenses and protection of actions taken in good faith.

rights: Right of persons possessing recognized rehabilitation qualifications to be enrolled in the Register.
Privileges for persons registered on the Register.
duties: Duty to regulate and monitor the training of rehabilitation professionals and personnel.
Duty to promote research in rehabilitation and special education.
Duty to maintain a Central Rehabilitation Register.
Duty to prescribe minimum standards of education for rehabilitation professionals.
Duty to consider professional conduct and remove names from the Register for misconduct.
obligations: Obligation for institutions and universities to provide information on courses and examinations when requested by the Council.
Obligation for the Council to lay rules and regulations before Parliament.

key_procedures: Recognition of qualifications: The Council recognizes qualifications from Indian and foreign institutions based on prescribed standards.
Registration: Rehabilitation professionals with recognized qualifications can be registered in the Central Rehabilitation Register.
Withdrawal of recognition: If standards are not met, the Council can withdraw recognition of a qualification.
Removal from Register: Names can be removed from the Register for professional misconduct, with an appeal process.
Rule making: The Central Government makes rules, and the Council makes regulations (with government sanction), both of which are laid before Parliament.
administration: The Rehabilitation Council of India, constituted under this Act, with administrative oversight and rule-making power vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act incorporates definitions from the Persons With Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995.
The Act was amended in 2000.
The commencement date of the Act was July 31, 1993, as per a notification.

title: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force Act, 1992
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for ensuring the security of the borders of India and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to persons appointed to the Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force, including officers, subordinate officers, under-officers, and other enrolled persons. Its geographical scope is for ensuring the security of the borders of India. The Act also covers matters connected therewith, including the constitution of the Force and conditions of service of its members.

key_definitions.active duty: Any duty as a member of the Force during the period such person is attached to or forms part of a unit engaged in operations against an enemy, or operating at a picket or engaged on patrol or other guard duty along the borders of India. It also includes duty declared by the Central Government as active duty for any area.
key_definitions.enemy: Includes all armed mutineers, armed rebels, armed rioters, pirates, and any person in arms against whom it is the duty of any person subject to this Act to take action.
key_definitions.Force: Means the Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force.
key_definitions.member of the Force: Means an officer, a subordinate officer, an under-officer or other enrolled person.
key_definitions.officer: A person appointed or in pay as an officer of the Force, but does not include a subordinate officer or an under-officer.
key_definitions.subordinate officer: A person appointed or in pay as a Subedar Major, a Subedar or a Sub-Inspector of the Force.
key_definitions.under-officer: A Head Constable, a Naik or a Lance Naik of the Force.
key_definitions.civil offence: An offence which is triable by a criminal court.
key_definitions.criminal court: A court of ordinary criminal justice in any part of India and includes a Court of a Special Judge appointed under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1952.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and stipulates that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'active duty', 'enemy', 'Force', 'member of the Force', 'officer', 'subordinate officer', 'under-officer', 'civil offence', 'criminal court', and others.

Specifies that officers, subordinate officers, under-officers, and other enrolled persons appointed to the Force are subject to this Act, and they remain subject until repatriated, retired, released, discharged, removed, or dismissed from the Force.

Establishes the Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force as an armed force of the Union for ensuring the security of India's borders and performing other entrusted duties. It also states that the Force shall be constituted and its members' conditions of service will be as prescribed.
Vests the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Force in the Central Government.
Details the process and conditions for the enrolment of persons into the Force.
Outlines the conditions under which members of the Force may be liable for service outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation and withdrawal from the post
main_sections.description: Governs the procedures and circumstances for resignation and withdrawal from service for members of the Force.

main_sections.section_title: Offences in relation to the enemy or terrorist and punishable with death
main_sections.description: Defines serious offences related to engaging with the enemy or terrorists that are punishable by death.
Defines the offence of mutiny within the Force.
Covers the offences of desertion from the Force and providing assistance to those who desert.
Addresses the offence of disobeying lawful commands of a superior officer.
Deals with offences that are also civil offences, meaning they are triable by a criminal court.
Specifies the punishments that can be awarded by Force Courts.
Outlines the different types of Force Courts established under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to convene a General Force Court
main_sections.description: Grants the authority to convene a General Force Court.

main_sections.section_title: Power to convene a Petty Force Court
main_sections.description: Grants the authority to convene a Petty Force Court.
Defines the role and appointment of the presiding officer of a Force Court.

main_sections.section_title: Oaths of member, Judge Attorney and witness
main_sections.description: Requires oaths to be taken by members of Force Courts, Judge Attorneys, and witnesses.

main_sections.section_title: Finding and sentence not valid unless confirmed
main_sections.description: Stipulates that findings and sentences of Force Courts are not valid without confirmation.
Describes the format and procedure for carrying out a sentence of death.
Details the process for the execution of sentences of imprisonment.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties conferable and imposable on members of the Force
main_sections.description: Allows for the conferral and imposition of powers and duties on members of the Force.

main_sections.section_title: Protection for acts of members of the Force
main_sections.description: Provides protection to members of the Force for acts done in good faith in the performance of their duties.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: Members of the Force are subject to the Act until properly repatriated, retired, released, discharged, removed, or dismissed.
Rule: The Central Government exercises general superintendence, direction, and control over the Force.
Rule: Enrolment into the Force is governed by specific procedures.
Rule: Members can be liable for service outside India under certain conditions.
Rule: Specific actions and omissions are defined as offences under the Act, with varying degrees of severity and penalties.
Rule: Force Courts are established for the trial of offences committed by members of the Force.
Rule: Findings and sentences of Force Courts require confirmation to be valid.
Rule: Sentences awarded by Force Courts, including death and imprisonment, have prescribed procedures for execution.
Rule: Members of the Force may be protected for acts done in good faith during their duty.
Rule: The Central Government has the power to make rules to implement the Act.

penalties: Death penalty for offences in relation to the enemy or terrorist.
Imprisonment and other punishments for various offences including mutiny, desertion, disobedience, and unbecoming conduct.
Minor punishments for less serious offences.
Collective fines can be imposed.
Deductions from pay and allowances.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, Director-General, commanding officers, Force Courts, and criminal courts (for civil offences).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through a system of internal Force Courts for service-related offences and regular criminal courts for civil offences. Enforcement involves arrest, trial, sentencing, and execution of punishments as prescribed by the Act and associated rules.

rights: Right to remedy for aggrieved persons (other than officers) under Section 14.
Right to remedy for aggrieved officers under Section 15.
Right to be informed of the charges.
Right to a fair trial.
Right to be presumed innocent until proven guilty.
duties: Duty to ensure the security of the borders of India.
Duty to obey lawful commands of superior officers.
Duty to maintain good order and discipline.
Duty to report offences.
Duty to appear for trial when required.
Duty to provide truthful evidence.
obligations: Obligation to be subject to the Act upon appointment.
Obligation to abide by the conditions of service.
Obligation to perform duties assigned.
Obligation to comply with the sentences awarded by Force Courts.
Obligation to not form associations or engage in speech that undermines the Force (as per Section 13).

key_procedures: Procedure for enrolment of persons into the Force.
Procedure for handling offences, including arrest, custody, and committal for trial.
Procedure for convening and conducting trials by different kinds of Force Courts (General, Petty, Summary).
Procedure for confirmation, revision, and execution of sentences.
Procedure for pardons, remissions, and commutations of sentences.
Procedure for making rules by the Central Government.
administration: The Central Government exercises general superintendence, direction, and control of the Force. Specific administrative roles are held by the Director-General and other appointed officials as defined in the Act.
important_notes: The Act's commencement date is appointed by the Central Government via notification.
References to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir are construed as references to corresponding laws in force there.
The Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
Certain definitions are based on or refer to other existing laws such as the Indian Penal Code, the Army Act, 1950, and the National Security Guard Act, 1986.

title: The Central Agricultural University Act, 1992
purpose: To provide for the establishment and incorporation of a University for the North-Eastern region for the development of agriculture and for the furtherance of the advancement of learning and prosecution of research in agriculture and allied sciences in that region.
scope: Applies to the North-Eastern region of India, comprising the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura. Its scope covers teaching, research, and extension education programs in agriculture and allied sciences.

key_definitions.academic_staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.agriculture: Includes basic and applied sciences of soil and water management, crop production, plant control, horticulture, animal husbandry, fisheries, forestry, home-science, agricultural engineering, marketing and processing of agricultural products, and land use and management.
key_definitions.extension_education: Educational activities focused on training farmers and other groups in agriculture, horticulture, fisheries, and related scientific technologies, including post-harvest technology and marketing.
key_definitions.North-Eastern_region: Comprises the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura.
key_definitions.University: The Central Agricultural University established under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'agriculture', 'extension education', 'North-Eastern region', and 'University'.
Establishes the Central Agricultural University, defines its headquarters at Imphal, Manipur, and constitutes it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objectives of the University, which include imparting education, advancing research, undertaking extension education programs, and other related activities in agriculture and allied sciences.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, conducting extension programs, granting degrees and certificates, establishing colleges and campuses, creating posts, awarding fellowships, determining admission standards, and managing property.

Specifies the geographical jurisdiction of the University for teaching, research, and extension education in agriculture to the North-Eastern States and mandates that all institutions under its purview are constituent units.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Declares the University open to all irrespective of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, prohibiting any test of religious belief for appointment, admission, or graduation. It allows for special provisions for women, handicapped, and weaker sections.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor and grants the Visitor the right to inspect the University and its institutions, and to inquire into its administration and finances, with provisions for notice and representation by the University.

important_rules: Rule 1: The University shall be open to all persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class, and no test of religious belief shall be imposed for admission or employment, except that special provisions may be made for women, handicapped, and weaker sections.

Rule 2: The President of India, as the Visitor, has the right to inspect and inquire into the University's operations and finances, with due notice to the University and consideration of its representations.
Rule 3: The University must comply with directions issued by the Visitor if the Board fails to take satisfactory action following an inspection or inquiry.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University authorities and the Visitor (President of India) are responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the University to regulate discipline, take disciplinary measures, and through the Visitor's power to annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act, Statutes, or Ordinances.

rights: Right of the University to make provision for instruction, research, and extension.
Right to grant degrees, diplomas, and certificates.
Right to establish and maintain colleges and campuses.
Right to supervise students' residences and promote their welfare.
Right to fix fees and charges.
Right to receive benefactions, donations, and gifts.
Right of the University to make representations to the Visitor.
Right of a representative of the University to be heard during Visitor's inspection/inquiry.
duties: Duty to impart education in agricultural and allied sciences.
Duty to undertake programs of extension education.
Duty to cooperate with other institutions.
Duty to lay down conditions of service for employees.
Duty to regulate and enforce discipline.
Duty to comply with directions from the Visitor.
obligations: Obligation to be open to all classes, castes, and creeds.
Obligation to act in conformity with the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances.
Obligation for the Board to comply with the Visitor's directions.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement of the Act: Central Government notifies the date of enforcement in the Official Gazette.

Procedure for inspection/inquiry by the Visitor: Visitor gives notice to the University, University makes representations within 30 days, Visitor considers representations and may proceed with inspection/inquiry. The University can appoint a representative.
Procedure for Visitor's directions: If the Board doesn't act satisfactorily, the Visitor may issue directions after considering explanations/representations, and the Board is bound to comply.
administration: The Central Agricultural University is administered by its own authorities (The University, Board, Academic Council, etc.), overseen by the Visitor (President of India).
important_notes: The Act was amended by the Central Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 2016 (45 of 2016).
The Act came into force on January 26, 1993.
The University's headquarters are at Imphal, Manipur, with the possibility of establishing other campuses within its jurisdiction.

title: THE GOLD BONDS (IMMUNITIES AND EXEMPTIONS) ACT, 1993
purpose: To provide for certain immunities to the subscribers of the Gold Bonds and for certain exemptions from direct taxes in relation to such Bonds and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. It aims to mobilize idle gold resources of residents in India by offering immunities and exemptions to encourage subscription to Gold Bonds.
scope: This Act applies to subscribers (individuals, Hindu undivided families, trusts, firms, or companies resident in India) who initially subscribe to the Gold Bonds, 1998. It provides immunities and tax exemptions related to these bonds.

key_definitions.Gold Bonds: The Gold Bonds, 1998, issued by the Central Government under a scheme framed by that Government. The specified date for framing the scheme was March 31, 1993, or a later date specified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.subscriber: An individual, a Hindu undivided family, trustees of a trust, a firm, or a company, being a resident or residents in India, who has or have initially subscribed to the Gold Bonds. The term 'individual' also includes their legal heirs or members of a Hindu undivided family having a share in the bonds after partition.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the 'Gold Bonds (Immunities and Exemptions) Act, 1993' and declares that it is deemed to have come into force on January 31, 1993.

Provides definitions for 'Gold Bonds' and 'subscriber'. It also states that any other undefined words and expressions used in the Act will have the meanings assigned to them in the Income-tax Act, 1961.

Empowers the Central Government to frame a scheme for subscription to the Gold Bonds, 1998, through a notification in the Official Gazette. The scheme must be laid before each House of Parliament after it is framed. The 'specified date' for subscription is March 31, 1993, or a later date notified by the Central Government.

Provides immunities to subscribers from certain provisions of the Wealth-tax Act, 1957, Gift-tax Act, 1958, Income-tax Act, 1961, Customs Act, 1962, Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976. Subscribers are not required to disclose the source of acquisition of gold or money used for acquiring it. No inquiry or investigation can be started against a subscriber solely based on owning Gold Bonds, and owning Gold Bonds is inadmissible as evidence in proceedings under these Acts. However, these immunities do not apply if proceedings regarding the subscribed gold were already initiated before the Act's commencement or in relation to prosecution for specific offences under the Indian Penal Code, Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, or for enforcing civil liability.

main_sections.section_title: Gold Bonds not to be taken into account in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies that the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, shall not apply to any interest accruing to the subscriber from the Gold Bonds or any long-term capital gains arising to the subscriber. It also states that the Gift-tax Act, 1958, shall not apply to gifts of Gold Bonds made by an individual subscriber to their spouse, child, or parent.

Repeals the Gold Bonds (Immunities and Exemptions) Ordinance, 1993. Anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Subscribers are granted immunities from disclosure requirements regarding the nature and source of gold acquisition and the money used for it, under specified tax and foreign exchange laws.
Rule 2: No inquiries or investigations can be initiated against subscribers solely on the ground of owning Gold Bonds under the specified Acts.
Rule 3: Owning Gold Bonds cannot be used as evidence in proceedings under the specified Acts, with certain exceptions.
Rule 4: Interest accruing from Gold Bonds and long-term capital gains arising to subscribers are exempt from Income-tax.
Rule 5: Gifts of Gold Bonds from an individual to their spouse, child, or parent are exempt from Gift-tax.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and potentially authorities under the Income-tax Act, Wealth-tax Act, Gift-tax Act, Customs Act, Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, and Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, although the act provides immunities from their actions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act's immunities and exemptions are enforced by limiting the actions of authorities under other specified Acts. The scheme for Gold Bonds is to be framed and notified by the Central Government and laid before Parliament.

rights: Right to not disclose the nature and source of acquisition of gold subscribed for Gold Bonds.
Right to not be subjected to inquiries or investigations solely based on owning Gold Bonds.
Right to have owning Gold Bonds be inadmissible as evidence in certain proceedings.
Right to exemption from Income-tax on interest accruing from Gold Bonds.
Right to exemption from Income-tax on long-term capital gains from Gold Bonds.
Right to gift Gold Bonds to spouse, child, or parent without incurring Gift-tax.
obligations: Obligation to subscribe to Gold Bonds as per the scheme framed by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Central Government frames a scheme for subscription to Gold Bonds, 1998, by notification in the Official Gazette, before a specified date (initially March 31, 1993).
Procedure 2: The framed scheme is laid before each House of Parliament as soon as it is framed.
Procedure 3: Subscribers avail of immunities and exemptions by subscribing to the Gold Bonds under the specified scheme.
administration: Central Government (specifically through notifications for the scheme)
important_notes: The immunities provided do not apply if proceedings concerning the subscribed gold were initiated before the Act's commencement.

The immunities do not apply to prosecutions for offences under specific chapters of the Indian Penal Code, the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987, the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, or for enforcement of civil liability.
The Act retroactively came into force on January 31, 1993.

title: The Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Act, 1993
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of certain area at Ayodhya and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, with a view to maintaining public order and promoting communal harmony.
scope: This Act applies to a specific area in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, India, as detailed in the Schedule. It addresses the acquisition of rights, management, and administration of property within this defined area.

key_definitions.area: The area including all buildings, structures, or other properties comprised therein, as specified in the Schedule of the Act.
key_definitions.authorised person: A person or body of persons or trustees of any trust authorised by the Central Government under section 7.
key_definitions.Claims Commissioner: The Claims Commissioner appointed under sub-section (2) of section 8.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Act, 1993' and specifies that it is deemed to have come into force on January 7, 1993.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'area', 'authorised person', 'Claims Commissioner', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of rights in respect of certain area
main_sections.description: Declares that upon commencement of the Act, the right, title, and interest in relation to the specified area shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government.

Explains that the vested area includes all assets, rights, properties (movable and immovable), and related documents previously owned or controlled by any person or the State Government. It also states that vested properties are freed from trusts, mortgages, liens, and other encumbrances, and any pending legal proceedings related to the property shall abate.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of person or State Government in charge of the management of the area to deliver all assets, etc.
main_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to secure possession of the vested area and mandates that the person or State Government in charge of the area's management must deliver all related assets, registers, and documents to the Central Government or an authorised person.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the area in another authority or body or trust
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct that the rights, title, and interest in the area or any part thereof may vest in another authority, body, or trust, subject to their compliance with specified terms and conditions.

States that the property vested in the Central Government shall be managed by the Central Government or an authorised person/body/trust. The management must ensure the maintenance of the position existing before the Act's commencement regarding the structure of Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid.

Specifies that the owner of any property within the area shall be given an amount equivalent to its market value. It also outlines the appointment of a Claims Commissioner to decide claims and sets a time limit for submitting claims.

main_sections.section_title: Act to override all other enactments
main_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, instruments, or court orders.
Prescribes penalties for persons in charge of management who fail to deliver assets, registers, or documents, including imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides that no legal proceedings shall be instituted against the Central Government, authorised persons, or their officers/employees for any action taken or intended to be taken in good faith under the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the Act's provisions, with a requirement for such rules to be laid before Parliament for approval or modification.
Repeals the Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Ordinance, 1993. It includes saving provisions regarding a specific plot (No. 242) and actions taken under the Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule: On and from the commencement of the Act, the right, title and interest in relation to the 'area' shall stand transferred to and vest in the Central Government (Section 3).
Rule: The vested area shall be deemed to include all assets, rights, properties, and documents previously held by any person or the State Government of Uttar Pradesh (Section 4(1)).
Rule: Vested properties are freed from all trusts, obligations, mortgages, charges, liens, and other encumbrances (Section 4(2)).

Rule: The person or State Government in charge of the management of the area must deliver all related assets, registers, and documents to the Central Government or an authorised person (Section 5(2)).
Rule: The Central Government is empowered to direct the vesting of the area or part thereof in another authority, body, or trust, subject to specified conditions (Section 6(1)).

Rule: The property vested in the Central Government shall be managed by the Central Government or an authorised person, ensuring the maintenance of the pre-existing position of the structure (Section 7).
Rule: Owners of property within the area shall be compensated with an amount equivalent to the market value (Section 8(1)).

Rule: Claims for compensation must be submitted to the Claims Commissioner within ninety days of the Act's commencement, with a possible extension of another ninety days for sufficient cause (Section 8(4)).
Rule: The Act's provisions shall override anything inconsistent contained in any other law, instrument, or court order (Section 9).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both, for any person in charge of management who fails to deliver any asset, register, or document to the Central Government or the authorised person (Section 10).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and authorised persons/bodies/trusts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the Central Government taking possession of the area, directing management, appointing a Claims Commissioner, and enforcing penalties for non-compliance. The Act's overriding nature ensures its provisions are enforced irrespective of other laws.

rights: Right of the Central Government to acquire the area and all related rights, titles, and interests.
Right of owners to receive compensation equivalent to the market value of their property.
Right of claimants to submit claims for compensation to the Claims Commissioner.
Right of the Central Government to delegate management to an authorised person or body.
Protection for actions taken in good faith by the Central Government and its agents.
duties: Duty of the person or State Government in charge of management to deliver all assets, registers, and documents to the Central Government or authorised person.
Duty of the Central Government or authorised person to manage the property, maintaining the pre-existing position of the structure.
Duty of the Central Government to appoint a Claims Commissioner.
Duty of the Central Government to make rules and lay them before Parliament.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to pay the market value to owners.
Obligation of any authority, body, or trust receiving delegated rights to comply with terms and conditions imposed by the Central Government.
Obligation to submit claims within stipulated timeframes.

key_procedures: Acquisition of Area: The Act automatically transfers the right, title, and interest of the specified area to the Central Government upon its commencement.
Securing Possession: The Central Government may take steps to secure possession of the vested area.
Delivery of Assets: Persons or the State Government managing the area must deliver all related assets and documents to the Central Government or an authorised person.
Compensation Claims: Owners or claimants must submit their claims to a Claims Commissioner within a specified period (90 days, extendable by 90 days).
Rule Making: The Central Government can make rules, which must be laid before Parliament for approval or modification.
administration: The Central Government, and any authorised person, body of persons, or trustees of any trust appointed by the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act is a result of a long-standing dispute concerning the Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid structure and aims to maintain public order and communal harmony.
The Act expressly overrides all other enactments and legal instruments in case of any inconsistency.
Specific provisions exist regarding the repeal of the Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Ordinance, 1993, with particular implications for plot No. 242.
The management of the property must ensure the maintenance of the position existing before the commencement of the Act regarding the structure's location.

title: THE SAARC CONVENTION (SUPPRESSION OF TERRORISM) ACT, 1993
purpose: To give effect to the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation Convention on Suppression of Terrorism and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to any offence under the Act committed outside India by any person, subject to the provisions of section 6. The Convention, as incorporated into the Act, applies to SAARC member states.

key_definitions.convention: Means the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation Convention on Suppression of Terrorism signed at Kathmandu on the 4th day of November, 1987 as set out in the Schedule.
key_definitions.convention_country: Means a country in which the Convention is for the time being in force.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies its application to offences committed outside India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Convention' and 'Convention country'.
Declares that Articles I to VIII of the Convention shall have the force of law in India, notwithstanding any other law.
Defines the offence of hostage-taking and prescribes punishment for it.

States that offences under the Act or specified in Article I of the Convention shall not be considered political offences for the purposes of the Extradition Act, 1962, in relation to a Convention country.

Outlines how offences committed outside India by Indian citizens, on Indian registered ships/aircraft, or in a Convention country, can be dealt with within India. Also allows the Central Government to direct where such offences can be inquired into or tried.
Requires the previous sanction of the Central Government for any prosecution under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Whoever, by force or threat of force or any other form of intimidation, seizes or detains any person and threatens to kill or injure that person with intent to cause a Convention country to do or abstain from doing any act as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat, commits the offence of hostage-taking.

Rule 2: Offences specified in Article I of the Convention, when committed outside India, can be dealt with in India if committed by an Indian citizen, on an Indian registered ship or aircraft, or in a Convention country.
Rule 3: No prosecution for an offence under this Act can be instituted without the previous sanction of the Central Government.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and liability to fine for the offence of hostage-taking.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government is responsible for granting sanction for prosecution and can issue orders regarding inquiry and trial of offences committed outside India. The Extradition Act, 1962, is also relevant for extradition purposes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution after obtaining sanction from the Central Government. Offences are considered non-political for extradition purposes. Mutual assistance and cooperation between Contracting States are also mechanisms for enforcement as per the Convention.

rights: Right to be prosecuted or extradited for specified terroristic acts.
Protection against legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
duties: Duty of Convention countries to ensure perpetrators of terroristic acts do not escape prosecution and punishment.
Duty to provide mutual assistance in connection with proceedings and to cooperate in preventing terroristic activities.
obligations: Obligation to make offences listed in Article I of the Convention extraditable offences in future treaties.
Obligation to afford the greatest measure of mutual assistance in proceedings related to terroristic offences.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: If a person suspected of committing an offence referred to in Article I or agreed to in terms of Article II is found in a Contracting State and extradition is requested, but the state does not extradite, it must submit the case without delay to its competent authorities for prosecution consideration.
Procedure 2: Contracting States shall afford mutual assistance, including the supply of evidence, for proceedings concerning terroristic offences.
Procedure 3: Contracting States shall cooperate through consultations, exchange of information, and other measures to prevent terroristic activities.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for granting sanction for prosecution and can issue directions regarding the trial of offences committed outside India. The SAARC Secretary-General acts as the depository for the Convention.
important_notes: Extradition shall be subject to the law of the requested State.
Contracting States are not obliged to extradite if it appears unjust or inexpedient due to triviality of the case, lack of good faith in the request, or other reasons.
The Convention itself is open for signature by SAARC member states and subject to ratification.

title: The Central Laws (Extension to Arunachal Pradesh) Act, 1993
purpose: To provide for the extension of certain Central laws to the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
scope: This act applies to the State of Arunachal Pradesh and extends certain Central laws to this state. The subject matter scope is defined by the list of Central laws mentioned in the Schedule.

key_definitions.Corresponding law: In relation to the State of Arunachal Pradesh, a law that is in force in that state and is equivalent to a law not in force in that state.
key_definitions.Corresponding new authority: A new authority constituted by or under any law extended to Arunachal Pradesh, which is equivalent to an authority that was competent to exercise powers or discharge functions in that state at the time of the passing of a particular law.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Central Laws (Extension to Arunachal Pradesh) Act, 1993' and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

This section states that the Acts mentioned in the Schedule, along with all rules, orders, regulations, and schemes made thereunder, are hereby extended to and shall be in force in the State of Arunachal Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to laws not in force in Arunachal Pradesh
main_sections.description: This section mandates that any reference in an Act listed in the Schedule to a law not in force in Arunachal Pradesh shall, in relation to that State, be construed as a reference to the corresponding law, if any, in force in Arunachal Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to authorities where new authorities have been constituted
main_sections.description: This section provides that any reference in any law in force in Arunachal Pradesh to an authority competent at the time of that law's passing shall have effect as if it were a reference to a corresponding new authority, where such a new authority has been constituted by or under any law now extended to the State.

This section empowers the Central Government to make provisions or give directions, by order notified in the Official Gazette, to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of any Act extended to Arunachal Pradesh. This power can be used to specify corresponding authorities or provide for the transfer of pending matters. Such orders must be made within two years of the Act's commencement and laid before each House of Parliament.

important_rules: All Acts mentioned in the Schedule, along with their associated rules, orders, regulations, and schemes, are now in force in the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
References to laws not in force in Arunachal Pradesh within the extended Acts should be interpreted as references to equivalent laws in force in the State.
References to old authorities within extended laws should be understood as references to new, corresponding authorities if they have been constituted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for removal of difficulties), and the respective authorities under the extended Central laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the extended Central laws and any orders or directions issued by the Central Government under Section 5 to remove difficulties.

key_procedures: Commencement: The Act comes into force on a date specified by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

Removal of Difficulties: The Central Government may issue notified orders to resolve any difficulties in implementing the extended Acts. These orders can specify corresponding authorities or transfer pending matters. Such orders are subject to parliamentary review.
administration: Central Government (for issuing notifications and orders to remove difficulties).
important_notes: The specific Central laws extended are listed in the Schedule.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to orders made within two years of the Act's commencement.
Every order made under the power to remove difficulties must be laid before each House of Parliament.

title: THE OIL AND NATURAL GAS COMMISSION (TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING AND REPEAL) ACT, 1993
purpose: To provide for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission to and in the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto and also to repeal the Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959.
scope: This act applies to the undertaking of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission and its transfer to the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited. It also covers the repeal of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959. The act's provisions regarding the undertaking, assets, liabilities, employees, and operations extend to matters within and outside India.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, for the vesting of the Commission's undertaking in the Corporation.
key_definitions.Corporation: The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited, a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.Commission: The Oil and Natural Gas Commission established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959.
key_definitions.prescribed: As prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it is deemed to have come into force on July 2, 1993.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Corporation', 'Commission', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Undertaking of Commission to vest in Corporation
main_sections.description: States that the undertaking of the Commission shall be transferred to and vest in the Corporation on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: General effect of vesting of undertaking in Corporation
main_sections.description: Details the consequences of the undertaking vesting in the Corporation, including the transfer of capital, assets, rights, liabilities, and the effect on contracts and pending proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Licences, etc., to be deemed to have been granted to Corporation
main_sections.description: Specifies that all licences, leases, concessions, permits, and other benefits granted to the Commission shall be deemed to have been granted to the Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Tax exemption or benefit to continue to have effect
main_sections.description: Ensures that tax exemptions, benefits, and provisions related to tax (like set off or carry forward of losses) granted to the Commission continue to apply to the Corporation. It also clarifies that the transfer is not considered a transfer for capital gains purposes under the Income-tax Act.
States that any guarantee given for or in favour of the Commission shall continue to be operative in relation to the Corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Commission
main_sections.description: Outlines the transfer of officers and employees from the Commission to the Corporation, their terms of service, and provisions regarding resignation, compensation, and retirement benefits. It also addresses members and the Chairman of the Commission.

Grants the Central Government the power to authorize Corporation officers to enter and inspect land, survey, take measurements, prospect for oil and natural gas, and examine documents related to land. It also defines authorized persons as public servants and makes the Corporation liable for compensation for damages.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, particularly concerning compensation for damages caused during prospecting. It also includes provisions for laying rules before Parliament.
