Repeals the Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959, on the appointed day, but requires the Corporation to comply with certain provisions related to annual accounts.
Repeals the Oil and Natural Gas Commission (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Ordinance, 1993, and saves anything done or action taken under that Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule 1: Undertaking of the Commission vests in the Corporation on the appointed day (Section 3).
Rule 2: All assets, rights, powers, privileges, properties, liabilities, and obligations of the Commission vest in the Corporation (Section 4(1) and 4(2)).
Rule 3: Existing contracts, deeds, and arrangements affecting the Commission become enforceable by or against the Corporation (Section 4(3)).
Rule 4: Pending legal proceedings against the Commission can be continued by or against the Corporation (Section 4(4)).
Rule 5: Licences, leases, and other benefits granted to the Commission are deemed to have been granted to the Corporation (Section 5).
Rule 6: Tax exemptions and benefits applicable to the Commission continue for the Corporation (Section 6).
Rule 7: Guarantees for the Commission continue for the Corporation (Section 7).
Rule 8: Officers and employees of the Commission become employees of the Corporation with similar terms and conditions, subject to certain conditions and the option to not join (Section 8).
Rule 9: The Corporation's officers/employees can enter and inspect land for prospecting, with compensation for damages (Section 9).
Rule 10: The Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959, is repealed (Section 11(1)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for appointing dates, authorizing entry, making rules), Corporation (for carrying out operations and paying compensation).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the transfer of the undertaking, vesting of assets and liabilities, continuation of contracts and proceedings, application of rules made by the Central Government, and powers of entry and inspection.

rights: Corporation's right to acquire and manage the undertaking, assets, and liabilities of the Commission.
Corporation's right to continue existing contracts and legal proceedings.
Corporation's right to benefit from tax exemptions and guarantees.
Employees' right to retain their terms of service, remuneration, and benefits (subject to conditions).
Right to compensation for land damage caused by Corporation officers/employees.
Right to have rules made by the Central Government laid before Parliament for scrutiny.
duties: Duty of the Commission's undertaking to vest in the Corporation.
Duty of the Corporation to assume all liabilities and obligations of the Commission.
Duty of the Corporation to maintain the terms and conditions of service for transferred employees.
Duty of the Corporation to pay compensation for land damage.
Duty of the Corporation to comply with relevant provisions of the repealed Act regarding annual accounts.
Duty of the Central Government to appoint an 'appointed day' and make rules.
obligations: Obligation of the Corporation to take over the entire capital of the Commission.
Obligation of the Corporation to honor contracts, deeds, and arrangements of the Commission.
Obligation of the Corporation to ensure employees' rights and benefits are maintained.
Obligation of the Corporation to compensate for any loss or damage to land during prospecting.
Obligation of the Corporation to continue the functions of welfare bodies for employees.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Central Government appoints an 'appointed day' via notification to effect the transfer and vesting of the Commission's undertaking.
Procedure 2: Corporation officers, authorized by the Central Government, can enter and inspect land for prospecting purposes.
Procedure 3: Compensation for land damage is determined and paid by the Corporation as prescribed by the Central Government.
Procedure 4: Rules made by the Central Government are laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period for modification or annulment.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for making rules and appointing the 'appointed day'. The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited administers the transferred undertaking.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on July 2, 1993.
The transfer of the undertaking is not considered a transfer for capital gains purposes under the Income-tax Act, 1961.
Members and the Chairman of the Commission are not entitled to compensation for loss of office or premature termination of contracts.
The repeal of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959, is effective from the 'appointed day'.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not invalidate actions taken under it.

title: The Punjab Municipal Corporation Law (Extension to Chandigarh) Act, 1994
purpose: To provide for the extension of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976 to the Union territory of Chandigarh.
scope: Applies to the Union territory of Chandigarh. It extends the provisions of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, with specific amendments and adaptations, to Chandigarh.

key_definitions.administrator: The administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.backward_classes: Any of the backward classes specified from time to time by the Administrator and whose names are published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.corporation: The Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.councillor: A person elected or nominated under sub-section (3) of section 4, in relation to the Corporation.
key_definitions.district: The district of Chandigarh covering the entire area of the Union territory of Chandigarh.
key_definitions.district_planning_committee: A Committee constituted under article 243ZD of the Constitution.
key_definitions.election_commission: The Election Commission of the Union territory of Chandigarh referred to in section 10.
key_definitions.finance_commission: The Finance Commission of the Union territory of Chandigarh referred to in section 84A.
key_definitions.licensed_architect: A person registered and licensed as an architect under section 16 of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952.
key_definitions.licensed_engineer: A person registered and licensed as an engineer under section 16 of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952.
key_definitions.licensed_plumber: A person registered and licensed as a plumber under section 16 of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952.
key_definitions.municipality: An institution of self-government constituted under article 243Q of the Constitution.
key_definitions.municipal_area: The territorial area of the Municipality as notified by the Administrator under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.population: The population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published.
key_definitions.prescribed_authority: Such authority or officer as the Administrator may, from time to time, by order published in the Official Gazette, prescribe. Different authorities or officers may be prescribed for different provisions.
key_definitions.public_street: Any street or the soil below the surface thereof which is specifically vested in the Corporation by an order of the Administrator.
key_definitions.rural_areas: The areas of the Union territory of Chandigarh which are not urban areas.
key_definitions.scheduled_caste: Any of the Scheduled Castes specified in Part II of the Schedule to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) (Union territories) Order, 1951.
key_definitions.urban_areas: Such areas as the Administrator may, having regard to population, density, revenue, employment in non-agricultural activities, economic importance, or other factors, specify by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Punjab Municipal Corporation Law (Extension to Chandigarh) Act, 1994, and deems it to have come into force on May 24, 1994.

main_sections.section_title: Extension and amendments of Punjab Act 42 of 1976
main_sections.description: Extends the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, to Chandigarh. It also provides for the construction of references to 'State', 'authorities', or 'City' in the extended Act, and specifies amendments to the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, as detailed in Part II of the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Punjab Act III of 1911 and savings
main_sections.description: Repeals the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, as it applies to Chandigarh, upon the commencement of this Act. It includes savings provisions to protect previous operations, rights, obligations, liabilities, and legal proceedings under the repealed Act. It also ensures that anything done or action taken under the repealed Act is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of the extended Act.

Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Special Officer to exercise the powers and functions of the Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh until the first meeting of the Corporation is held after the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Ordinance 7 of 1994 and saving
main_sections.description: Repeals the Punjab Municipal Corporation Law (Extension to Chandigarh) Ordinance, 1994. Any action taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed to have been taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule: References in the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976 to 'State', 'authorities', or 'City' shall be construed as references to 'Union territory of Chandigarh', 'Administrator', or 'Chandigarh' respectively, as specified in Part I of the Schedule.
Rule: The Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, shall be amended as specified in Part II of the Schedule, including definitions and provisions related to the Corporation and its functions.

Rule: Seats shall be reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and for women in general, with a minimum of one-third of the total seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and one-third of the total directly elected seats, respectively.
Rule: Seats may be reserved for backward classes of citizens if the Administrator deems it necessary.
Rule: The Corporation shall have a duration of five years from the date of its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved.
Rule: Elections to constitute the Corporation must be completed before its duration expires or within six months of its dissolution.

rights: Right to continue legal proceedings or remedies in respect of anything done or suffered under the repealed Punjab Municipal Act, 1911.
Right to hold office for members elected or nominated to the Corporation.
duties: Duty to apply corresponding provisions for things done or actions taken under the repealed Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, and the repealed Ordinance.
Duty of the Administrator to determine the number and extent of wards and the reservation of seats.
Duty of the Election Commission to prepare electoral rolls and conduct elections to the Corporation.
Duty of the Administrator to make available necessary staff to the Election Commission.
Duty of the Corporation to send its views to the Administrator within three months when consulted on altering municipal area limits.
obligations: Obligations acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, are preserved.
Obligations to follow the provisions of the extended Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, as amended for Chandigarh.

key_procedures: Procedure: Extension of Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976 to Chandigarh with specific amendments.
Procedure: Repeal of Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, and saving of past actions and rights.
Procedure: Appointment of a Special Officer by the Central Government if necessary.
Procedure: Repeal of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Law (Extension to Chandigarh) Ordinance, 1994.
Procedure: Notification by the Administrator to specify the municipal area of Chandigarh.
Procedure: Election of councillors, nomination of members by the Administrator, and inclusion of a Member of Parliament.
Procedure: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, women, and backward classes.
Procedure: Determination of wards and their extent by the Administrator.
Procedure: Determination of wards for reserved seats and rotation by the Election Commission.
Procedure: Superintendence, direction, and control of election preparation and conduct vested in the Election Commission.
administration: The Administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh, in conjunction with the Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh and the Election Commission.
important_notes: The repeal of Punjab Act III of 1911 does not affect previous operations, rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, investigations, or legal proceedings done or incurred thereunder.

Anything done or any action taken under the repealed Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, or the repealed Ordinance, is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act and continues in force until superseded.

References to 'State', 'authorities', or 'City' in the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, are construed as references to 'Union territory of Chandigarh', 'Administrator', or 'Chandigarh' respectively, as per Part I of the Schedule.

The Act makes significant amendments to the definitions and sections of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, as detailed in Part II of the Schedule, to adapt it for the Union territory of Chandigarh.
The reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and women shall cease to have effect on the expiration of the period specified in article 334 of the Constitution.

title: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a National Human Rights Commission, State Human Rights Commissions in States and Human Rights Courts for better protection of human rights and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It establishes commissions and courts to protect human rights.

key_definitions.armed_forces: The naval, military and air forces and includes any other armed forces of the Union.
key_definitions.chairperson: The Chairperson of the Commission or of the State Commission, as the case may be.
key_definitions.commission: The National Human Rights Commission constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.human_rights: The rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the individual guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in the International Covenants and enforceable by courts in India.
key_definitions.human_rights_court: The Human Rights Court specified under section 30.
key_definitions.international_covenants: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations on the 16th December, 1966 and such other Covenant or Convention adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations as the Central Government may, by notification, specify.
key_definitions.member: A Member of the Commission or of the State Commission, as the case may be.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public_servant: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
key_definitions.state_commission: A State Human Rights Commission constituted under section 21.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and the date it came into force (deemed to have come into force on September 28, 1993).

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'armed forces', 'Chairperson', 'Commission', 'Human Rights', 'Human Rights Court', 'International Covenants', 'Member', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'public servant', and 'State Commission'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of a National Human Rights Commission
main_sections.description: This section outlines the constitution of the National Human Rights Commission, including its composition (Chairperson and Members) and the role of its Secretary-General.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chairperson and other Members
main_sections.description: This section details the process of appointing the Chairperson and Members of the Commission by the President, based on recommendations from a specified committee.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation and removal of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: This section explains the conditions and procedures for the resignation and removal of the Chairperson and Members of the Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: This section specifies the term of office for the Chairperson and Members (three years or until age seventy), and their eligibility for re-appointment, along with ineligibility for further employment under government.
This section enumerates the various functions of the National Human Rights Commission.
This section details the procedure for the Commission to inquire into complaints of human rights violations.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of State Human Rights Commissions
main_sections.description: This section outlines the constitution of State Human Rights Commissions.
This section provides for the establishment of Human Rights Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: This section grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
This section deals with the repeal of any prior legislation and savings provisions.

important_rules: The National Human Rights Commission shall be constituted by the Central Government to exercise powers and perform functions under the Act.
The Chairperson and Members of the Commission shall be appointed by the President based on recommendations from a specific committee.
The Chairperson or any Member may resign by giving written notice to the President.
The Chairperson or a Member can only be removed by the President on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, after an inquiry and report by the Supreme Court.
The Chairperson shall hold office for a term of three years or until the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier, and shall be eligible for re-appointment.
A Member shall hold office for a term of three years and shall be eligible for re-appointment, but shall not hold office after attaining the age of seventy years.
The salaries and allowances and other terms and conditions of service of the Chairperson and Members shall be as prescribed and shall not be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
No act or proceedings of the Commission shall be questioned or invalidated due to any vacancy or defect in its constitution.
The Commission shall meet at such time and place as the Chairperson thinks fit and shall have the power to lay down its own procedure through regulations.
Human Rights Courts shall be specified by the State Government for the purpose of speedy trial of offences relating to human rights.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Human Rights Commission and State Human Rights Commissions are established to enforce the protection of human rights. Human Rights Courts are established for the speedy trial of offences relating to human rights.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act outlines procedures for inquiries into complaints, investigations, and the functioning of Human Rights Courts. The Commission has powers relating to inquiries and investigations. The Central and State Governments have powers to make rules and regulations.

rights: Rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the individual guaranteed by the Constitution.
Rights embodied in the International Covenants and enforceable by courts in India.
duties: To protect human rights as defined by the Constitution and International Covenants.

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairperson and Members of the National Human Rights Commission through a committee and Presidential warrant.
Removal of Chairperson and Members on grounds of misbehaviour or incapacity after Supreme Court inquiry.
Inquiry into complaints of human rights violations by the Commission.
Investigation of human rights violations.
Constitution of State Human Rights Commissions and Human Rights Courts.
Procedure for regulating the meetings and functioning of the Commission.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments are involved in the administration of this Act, particularly in constituting commissions, making rules, and establishing courts.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on September 28, 1993.
The provisions related to the application of certain laws in the State of Jammu and Kashmir have been addressed.
Amendments have been made by various Acts, including updates to definitions and composition of commissions.
Certain matters are not subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission as specified in Section 36.

title: THE TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 1995
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Board for payment of equity capital or any other financial assistance to industrial concerns and other agencies attempting development and commercial application of indigenous technology or adapting imported technology to wider domestic applications and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to industrial concerns and other agencies attempting the development and commercial application of indigenous technology, or adapting imported technology for wider domestic applications within India. The Board itself is constituted by the Central Government.

key_definitions.Board: The Technology Development Board constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund for Technology Development and Application constituted under sub-section (1) of section 9.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Secretary: The Secretary of the Board appointed under sub-section (1) of section 4.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Technology Development Board Act, 1995, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Fund', 'member', 'prescribed', and 'Secretary'. It also specifies that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Research and Development Cess Act, 1986, shall have their meanings as assigned in that Act.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the constitution of the Technology Development Board by the Central Government. It establishes the Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It lists the ex officio members (Secretaries of various Central Government Ministries/Departments like Science and Technology, Scientific and Industrial Research, Finance, Defence Research, Industrial Development, Rural Development) and up to four appointed members with specific experience. The Secretary of the Board is also an ex officio member. It also addresses the term of office for certain members and the powers of the Chairperson, and states that vacancies or defects in the Board's constitution or appointment of members do not invalidate its proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Secretary and other officers and employees of the Board
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to appoint a Secretary and other necessary officers and employees for efficient functioning. The terms and conditions of service for these appointees are to be determined by regulations.
Allows the Board to appoint committees for efficient discharge of its duties and functions. The Board can co-opt non-members to these committees, who can participate but not vote.

Outlines the primary functions of the Board, which include: (a) providing equity capital or financial assistance to industrial concerns and agencies for commercializing indigenous technology or adapting imported technology; (b) providing financial assistance to recognized R&D institutions for developing or adapting technology for commercial use; and (c) performing other functions as entrusted by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Application for grant of financial assistance, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for applying for financial assistance. Applications must be made in the prescribed form. The Board, after examination and inquiry, can grant or refuse assistance through a written order. Applicants must be given an opportunity to be heard before refusal.

main_sections.section_title: Grants and loans by the Central Government
main_sections.description: States that the Central Government may provide grants and loans to the Board, subject to parliamentary appropriation.

main_sections.section_title: Fund for Technology Development and Application
main_sections.description: Establishes a 'Fund for Technology Development and Application'. This fund is to be credited with grants and loans from the Central Government, sums received from other sources, recoveries from the Fund, and income from investments. The fund is to be applied for authorized expenses, salaries, and other expenses of the Board in discharging its functions.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of money receipts and liabilities
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of assets and liabilities upon commencement of the Act. It includes the transfer of money from the Venture Capital Fund, sums due to the Development Bank, and the continuation of contracts, agreements, and legal proceedings that were previously with the Development Bank and related to the Venture Capital Fund, now vesting with the Board.
Requires the Board to prepare and forward its budget for the next financial year, including estimated receipts and expenditures, to the Central Government in the prescribed form and time.
Mandates the Board to prepare an annual report on its activities for the previous financial year in the prescribed form and time, and submit a copy to the Central Government.

Requires the Board to maintain proper accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts in the prescribed form. The accounts are subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG) or a person appointed by them. The CAG has powers similar to those in auditing government accounts. The Board must submit its audited accounts and auditor's report to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and auditor’s report to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Stipulates that the Central Government shall cause the Board's annual report and auditor's report to be laid before each House of Parliament after they are received.

main_sections.section_title: Returns to be furnished to the Board
main_sections.description: Requires industrial concerns or institutions receiving financial assistance from the Board to furnish returns in the prescribed form and time. The Board can authorize an officer to verify the accuracy of these returns.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue written directions on questions of policy to the Board. The Board is bound by these directions. The Board shall be given an opportunity to express its views before directions are issued, as far as practicable. The Central Government's decision on whether a question is one of policy is final.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede the Board
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to supersede the Board by notification if it is of the opinion that the Board is unable to discharge its functions due to grave emergency, has persistently defaulted in complying with directions or discharging its duties leading to deterioration, or if it is necessary in the public interest. Supersession can be for a period not exceeding six months. Upon supersession, members vacate office, powers are exercised by persons directed by the Central Government, and the Board's property vests in the Central Government until reconstitution.
Allows for delegation of powers by the Central Government and the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Members, officers and employees of the Board to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares that members, officers, and employees of the Board are considered public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from legal proceedings for any action taken in good faith by any person under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make regulations, consistent with the Act and rules made by the Central Government, for its internal functioning.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires that all rules and regulations made under the Act shall be laid before Parliament.

important_rules: An applicant for financial assistance must be given an opportunity to be heard before their application is refused.
Industrial concerns or institutions receiving financial assistance must furnish regular returns to the Board.
The Board shall be bound by written directions on questions of policy issued by the Central Government.
All rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and the Technology Development Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Central Government and the Board, including issuing directions, superseding the Board, verifying returns, and pursuing legal proceedings.

rights: Right of applicant to be heard before refusal of financial assistance.
Right to protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Right of the Board to sue and be sued.
Right of co-opted committee members to attend and participate (but not vote).
duties: Duty of the Board to provide equity capital or financial assistance for technology development and application.
Duty of the Board to manage its funds and accounts properly.
Duty of industrial concerns and institutions receiving assistance to furnish returns.
Duty of the Board to be bound by policy directions from the Central Government.
Duty of the Central Government to lay reports before Parliament.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to constitute the Board.
Obligation of the Board to maintain proper accounts and prepare annual reports.
Obligation of the Board to operate within the framework of the Act and rules/regulations.

key_procedures: Application for financial assistance: An applicant submits a prescribed form to the Board. The Board examines the application, conducts inquiries, and issues a written order to grant or refuse assistance, ensuring the applicant is heard if refusal is considered.

Board's functioning: The Board, constituted by the Central Government, has a Chairperson and members. It appoints a Secretary and staff, and may form committees. It functions by providing financial assistance, managing its funds, preparing budgets and reports, and is subject to Central Government directions and audit by the CAG.

Supersession of the Board: If specific conditions are met (grave emergency, persistent default, public interest), the Central Government can supersede the Board for up to six months, during which an appointed person/persons exercise powers and the Board's property vests in the Government. The Board is then reconstituted.
administration: The Technology Development Board, constituted by the Central Government. Various Ministries/Departments of the Central Government are represented on the Board.
important_notes: The Act came into force on November 1, 1996, as per notification.
Words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Research and Development Cess Act, 1986, shall have their meanings as assigned in that Act.
The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
No act or proceeding of the Board shall be invalidated due to vacancy, defect in constitution or appointment, or procedural irregularity not affecting merits.

title: The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996
purpose: To provide for the extension of the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution relating to the Panchayats to the Scheduled Areas.
scope: Applies to Scheduled Areas as defined in clause (1) of article 244 of the Constitution. It mandates that State Legislatures make laws for Panchayats in these areas that are in consonance with customary law, social and religious practices, and traditional management practices of community resources, among other provisions.

key_definitions.Scheduled Areas: Scheduled Areas as referred to in clause (1) of article 244 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996.
Defines 'Scheduled Areas' with reference to the Constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of Part IX of the Constitution
main_sections.description: Extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution concerning Panchayats to the Scheduled Areas, subject to exceptions and modifications in Section 4.

main_sections.section_title: Exceptions and modifications to Part IX of the Constitution
main_sections.description: Outlines specific features that State Legislations on Panchayats in Scheduled Areas must adhere to, overriding general provisions of Part IX of the Constitution. These include consonance with customary law, village definition, Gram Sabha powers, reservation of seats, nomination of members, consultation on land acquisition, management of water bodies and minor minerals, and specific powers to be endowed to Panchayats.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of existing laws and Panchayats
main_sections.description: States that existing laws relating to Panchayats in Scheduled Areas, which are inconsistent with Part IX of the Constitution (as modified by this Act), will continue until amended or repealed, or for one year from the Act's assent. Existing Panchayats will continue until their term expires unless dissolved earlier.

important_rules: State legislation on Panchayats in Scheduled Areas must be in consonance with customary law, social and religious practices, and traditional management practices of community resources.
Every village shall have a Gram Sabha comprising persons in the electoral rolls for the village Panchayat.
Gram Sabha is competent to safeguard and preserve traditions, customs, cultural identity, community resources, and customary dispute resolution.
Gram Sabha must approve development plans before implementation and identify beneficiaries for poverty alleviation and other programs.
Village level Panchayats must obtain certification from Gram Sabha for fund utilization.
Reservation of seats in Panchayats shall be in proportion to population, with at least half for Scheduled Tribes, and all Chairperson seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
State Governments may nominate Scheduled Tribe members to intermediate or district level Panchayats if they lack representation, up to one-tenth of total elected members.
Gram Sabha or appropriate Panchayats must be consulted before land acquisition for development projects and for resettlement/rehabilitation of affected persons.
Planning and management of minor water bodies shall be entrusted to appropriate level Panchayats.
Recommendations of Gram Sabha or appropriate Panchayats are mandatory before granting prospecting licenses or mining leases for minor minerals, and for exploitation of minor minerals by auction.
Panchayats in Scheduled Areas must be endowed with specific powers, including enforcing prohibition, managing village markets, controlling money lending, and managing local plans and resources.
State legislation must ensure higher-level Panchayats do not assume powers of lower-level Panchayats or Gram Sabha.

rights: Right of Gram Sabha to approve development plans and identify beneficiaries.
Right of Gram Sabha to safeguard and preserve traditions, customs, cultural identity, community resources, and customary dispute resolution.
Right of Gram Sabha to be consulted on land acquisition and resettlement.
Right of Panchayats to manage village markets.
Right of Panchayats to control money lending to Scheduled Tribes.
Right of Panchayats to control institutions and functionaries in social sectors.
Right of Panchayats to control local plans and resources, including tribal sub-plans.
duties: Duty of State Legislature to make laws for Panchayats in consonance with customary practices.
Duty of Gram Sabha to approve plans and identify beneficiaries.
Duty of village level Panchayats to obtain certification of fund utilization from Gram Sabha.
Duty of Panchayats to manage minor water bodies.
Duty of Panchayats to enforce prohibition or regulate/restrict sale/consumption of intoxicants.
Duty of Panchayats to prevent alienation of land and restore unlawfully alienated land of Scheduled Tribes.
Duty of State Legislature to ensure safeguards against higher-level Panchayats assuming lower-level powers.
obligations: Obligation to consult Gram Sabha or appropriate Panchayats before land acquisition.
Obligation to obtain mandatory recommendations from Gram Sabha or appropriate Panchayats for mining leases and exploitation of minor minerals.
Obligation to endow Panchayats with powers to function as institutions of self-government.

key_procedures: Procedure for Gram Sabha to approve plans, programs, and projects for social and economic development before implementation by village level Panchayats.
Procedure for Gram Sabha to identify or select beneficiaries under poverty alleviation and other programs.
Procedure for village level Panchayats to obtain certification of fund utilization from Gram Sabha.
Procedure for consultation with Gram Sabha or appropriate Panchayats before land acquisition for development projects and before resettlement or rehabilitation of affected persons.
Procedure for granting prospecting license or mining lease for minor minerals, requiring mandatory prior recommendations from Gram Sabha or appropriate Panchayats.
Procedure for granting concession for exploitation of minor minerals by auction, requiring mandatory prior recommendation from Gram Sabha or appropriate Panchayats.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be administered by State Legislatures and Panchayati Raj institutions within Scheduled Areas.
important_notes: The Act extends Part IX of the Constitution to Scheduled Areas with exceptions and modifications.
State legislation must be in consonance with customary law and practices.
Existing laws in Scheduled Areas inconsistent with the Act will continue in force for a limited period.
Existing Panchayats will continue until their term expires unless dissolved by the State Legislature.

title: THE DEPOSITORIES ACT, 1996
purpose: To provide for regulation of depositories in securities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to depositories, participants, issuers, and beneficial owners of securities.

key_definitions.beneficial owner: A person whose name is recorded as such with a depository.
key_definitions.Board: The Securities and Exchange Board of India established under section 3 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992.
key_definitions.depository: A company formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956 and which has been granted a certificate of registration under sub-section (1A) of section 12 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992.
key_definitions.issuer: Any person making an issue of securities.
key_definitions.participant: A person registered as such under sub-section (1A) of section 12 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992.
key_definitions.security: Such security as may be specified by the Board.
key_definitions.service: Any service connected with recording of allotment of securities or transfer of ownership of securities in the record of a depository.

main_sections.description: Defines the short title, territorial extent, and commencement date of the Act. It commenced on September 20, 1995.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including beneficial owner, Board, depository, issuer, participant, security, and service. It also states that undefined terms used in the Act will have meanings assigned in the Companies Act, 1956, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, or the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992.

main_sections.section_title: Certificate of commencement of business by depositories
main_sections.description: States that a depository cannot operate without obtaining a certificate of commencement of business from the Board. The Board will grant the certificate only if satisfied that the depository has adequate systems and safeguards against manipulation.
Requires a depository to enter into an agreement with one or more participants as its agent. The form of the agreement is specified by bye-laws.
Allows any person, through a participant, to enter into an agreement with a depository to avail its services.

Details the process where a person availing depository services surrenders their security certificate to the issuer. The issuer cancels the certificate, registers the depository as the owner, and informs the depository. The depository then registers the person as the beneficial owner.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of transfer of securities with depository
main_sections.description: Mandates that a depository must register the transfer of securities in the name of the transferee upon receiving intimation from a participant. It also includes provisions for transfers in favor of asset reconstruction companies and for the issue of new shares by conversion of debt.

main_sections.section_title: Options to receive security certificate or hold securities with depository
main_sections.description: Grants subscribers of securities the option to either receive security certificates or hold securities with a depository. If they opt to hold with a depository, the issuer must inform the depository, which then records the allottee as the beneficial owner.

main_sections.section_title: Securities in depositories to be in fungible form
main_sections.description: Mandates that all securities held by a depository must be dematerialised and in fungible form. It also exempts depositories from certain provisions of the Companies Act, 1956 regarding securities held on behalf of beneficial owners.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of depositories and beneficial owner
main_sections.description: Clarifies that a depository is the registered owner for transferring ownership on behalf of the beneficial owner. However, the depository has no voting or other rights in respect of such securities. The beneficial owner retains all rights, benefits, and liabilities.
Requires every depository to maintain a register and index of beneficial owners in a manner prescribed by sections 150, 151, and 152 of the Companies Act, 1956.

main_sections.section_title: Pledge or hypothecation of securities held in a depository
main_sections.description: Allows a beneficial owner, with the depository's approval, to create a pledge or hypothecation of securities held through the depository. The beneficial owner must inform the depository, which then makes appropriate entries in its records, serving as evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Furnishing of information and records by depository and issuer
main_sections.description: Obligates depositories to provide information on beneficial owners to issuers at specified intervals and issuers to make relevant records available to depositories.

main_sections.section_title: Option to opt out in respect of any security
main_sections.description: Allows a beneficial owner to opt out of a depository for any specific security. The depository informs the issuer, which then issues the certificate of securities to the beneficial owner after fulfillment of conditions and payment of fees.

main_sections.section_title: Act 18 of 1891 to apply to depositories
main_sections.description: States that the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 applies to depositories as if they were banks.

main_sections.section_title: Depositories to indemnify loss in certain cases
main_sections.description: Holds depositories liable to indemnify beneficial owners for losses caused by the negligence of the depository or participant. The depository has the right to recover such losses from the negligent participant.

main_sections.section_title: Rights and obligations of depositories, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the rights and obligations of depositories, participants, and issuers are to be defined by regulations, as is the eligibility criteria for admitting securities into a depository.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to call for information and enquiry
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board (SEBI) to call for information from issuers, depositories, participants, or beneficial owners if it deems it necessary in the public interest or for investor protection.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to give directions in certain cases
main_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to issue directions in certain specified cases.

Introduces a chapter on penalties for various contraventions, including failure to furnish information, enter into agreements, redress grievances, delay in dematerialization, failure to reconcile records, non-compliance with directions, and unfair business practices. It also includes provisions for adjudication, settlement of proceedings, recovery of amounts, and crediting penalties to the Consolidated Fund of India.
Details offenses under the Act.
Addresses contraventions by companies.
Specifies how courts take cognizance of offenses.
Allows for the composition of certain offenses.
Grants the power to grant immunity from prosecution.
Provides for the establishment of Special Courts to try offenses under the Act.
Defines which offenses are triable by Special Courts.
Deals with appeals and revisions related to Special Court proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Code to proceedings before Special Court
main_sections.description: Specifies the application of the Code of Criminal Procedure to proceedings before Special Courts.
Contains provisions for the transition to the new Act.
Deals with general appeals.
Provides for appeals to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of Securities Appellate Tribunal
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure and powers of the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
Confirms the right to legal representation in proceedings.
Addresses the limitation period for appeals.

main_sections.section_title: Civil Court not to have jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters covered by the Act.
Provides for appeals to the Supreme Court.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Board not to apply to International Financial Services Centre
main_sections.description: States that the powers of the Board do not apply to International Financial Services Centres.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board (SEBI) to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

main_sections.section_title: Power of depositories to make bye-laws
main_sections.description: Allows depositories to make bye-laws for their operations, subject to approval.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the application of other laws is not barred.
Provides for the removal of difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the validation of certain past acts.
Repeals previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: Securities held by a depository must be dematerialised and in fungible form (Section 9(1)).
A depository is considered the registered owner for transfer purposes but has no voting rights or other rights in respect of held securities; these remain with the beneficial owner (Section 10).
Beneficial owners can pledge or hypothecate securities held through a depository with the depository's prior approval (Section 12(1)).
Depositories must indemnify beneficial owners for losses caused by their or their participants' negligence (Section 16(1)).
No depository can act without a certificate of commencement of business from SEBI (Section 3(1)).
An issuer must cancel security certificates surrendered by a beneficial owner and register the depository as the owner (Section 6(2)).
Issuers must provide copies of relevant records in respect of securities held by a depository (Section 13(2)).
Beneficial owners have the option to opt out of a depository for specific securities (Section 14(1)).

penalties: Penalty for failure to furnish information, return, etc. (Section 19A)
Penalty for failure to enter into an agreement (Section 19B)
Penalty for failure to redress investors' grievances (Section 19C)
Penalty for delay in dematerialisation or issue of certificate of securities (Section 19D)
Penalty for failure to reconcile records (Section 19E)
Penalty for failure to comply with directions issued by the Board (Section 19F)
Penalty for conducting business in an unfair manner (Section 19FA)
Penalty for contravention where no separate penalty has been provided (Section 19G)
Offences are described in Section 20.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the primary enforcement authority, responsible for calling for information, giving directions, adjudicating penalties, and establishing Special Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves calling for information, issuing directions, imposing penalties through adjudication, prosecuting offenses in Special Courts, and civil recovery of amounts. Appeals lie with the Securities Appellate Tribunal and then the Supreme Court.

rights: Beneficial owners are entitled to all rights and benefits in respect of their securities held by a depository (Section 10(3)).
Beneficial owners have the right to opt out of a depository for any specific security (Section 14(1)).
Right to legal representation in proceedings before the Securities Appellate Tribunal (Section 23C).
Right to appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and Supreme Court (Sections 23A, 23F).
duties: Depositories must ensure their systems and safeguards prevent manipulation of records and transactions (Section 3(3)).
Depositories must enter into agreements with participants (Section 4(1)).
Depositories must maintain a register and index of beneficial owners (Section 11).
Depositories must furnish information about transfers of securities to issuers (Section 13(1)).
Depositories must indemnify beneficial owners for losses due to negligence (Section 16(1)).
Issuers must cancel surrendered certificates and register depositories as owners (Section 6(2)).
Issuers must make relevant records available to depositories (Section 13(2)).
obligations: Beneficial owners are subject to all liabilities in respect of their securities held by a depository (Section 10(3)).
Beneficial owners must give intimation of pledge or hypothecation to the depository (Section 12(2)).
Beneficial owners who opt out must fulfill conditions and pay fees (Section 14(3)).

key_procedures: Obtaining a certificate of commencement of business from SEBI before operating as a depository (Section 3).
Surrendering security certificates to the issuer for dematerialization and registration with the depository (Section 6).
Registering transfer of securities by the depository upon intimation from a participant (Section 7).
A beneficial owner opting to hold securities with a depository, requiring the issuer to intimate details to the depository (Section 8).
A beneficial owner opting out of a depository for a security, involving intimation to the depository, entry in records, and subsequent issuance of a physical certificate by the issuer (Section 14).
Adjudication proceedings for penalties, including settlement of administrative and civil proceedings (Sections 19H, 19-IA).
Appeals to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and then to the Supreme Court (Sections 23A, 23F).
administration: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the primary administrative and regulatory body for this Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to regulate depositories for securities, facilitating dematerialization and electronic transfer of ownership, thereby enhancing transparency and efficiency in the securities market.
The Act is considered to have come into force retrospectively from September 20, 1995 (Section 1(3)).
Certain sections of the Companies Act, 1956 do not apply to a depository in respect of securities held on behalf of beneficial owners (Section 9(2)).
The Act provides for the establishment of Special Courts for the trial of offenses.

title: THE INDUSTRIAL RECONSTRUCTION BANK (TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS AND REPEAL) ACT, 1997
purpose: To provide for the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India to and in a Company (Industrial Investment Bank of India Limited) to be formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, and also to repeal the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984.
scope: The Act applies to the transfer of undertakings of the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India to the Industrial Investment Bank of India Limited. It covers officers and employees, contracts, legal proceedings, and financial and tax matters related to this transfer. The geographical scope is implied to be India, as it refers to the Republic of India and undertakings within or without India.

key_definitions.appointed day: Such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint under section 3.
key_definitions.Company: The Industrial Investment Bank of India Limited to be formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.Reconstruction Bank: The Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 24th day of January, 1997.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Company', and 'Reconstruction Bank'.

main_sections.section_title: Undertakings of the Reconstruction Bank to vest in company
main_sections.description: States that on the 'appointed day', the undertakings of the Reconstruction Bank shall be transferred to and vest in the Company.

main_sections.section_title: General effect of vesting of undertaking in Company
main_sections.description: Details the consequences of the vesting, including the Central Government's shareholding in the Company, the comprehensive nature of the transferred undertakings (assets, liabilities, rights, etc.), the continuation of contracts and legal proceedings with the Company, and the cessation of effect against the Reconstruction Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Reconstruction Bank
main_sections.description: Outlines the terms of employment for officers and employees of the Reconstruction Bank who are transferred to the Company, including their tenure, remuneration, benefits, and rights. It also covers provisions for those who opt not to continue employment and clarifies that no compensation is payable for such transfers. It also addresses retired employees and welfare funds.

main_sections.section_title: Concession, etc., to be deemed to have been granted to Company
main_sections.description: States that all fiscal and other concessions, licenses, benefits, privileges, and exemptions granted to the Reconstruction Bank shall be deemed to have been granted to the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Tax exemption or benefit to continue to have effect
main_sections.description: Provides for a tax exemption for the Company for five years from the appointed day and clarifies that the transfer of undertakings will not be construed as a transfer for capital gains purposes.
Ensures that any guarantee given for the Reconstruction Bank will continue to be operative in relation to the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Arrangement with Company on appointment of directors to prevail
main_sections.description: Deals with arrangements where the Company appoints directors to other concerns, making such provisions valid and effective and specifying the rights and liabilities of such appointed directors.

main_sections.section_title: Act 18 of 1891 to apply to the books of Company
main_sections.description: Deems the Company to be a bank for the purposes of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891.

main_sections.section_title: Shares, bonds and debentures to be deemed to be approved securities
main_sections.description: Declares that the shares, bonds, and debentures of the Company shall be deemed to be approved securities for the purposes of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and the Insurance Act, 1938.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution in Act, rules or regulations of company in place of the Reconstruction Bank
main_sections.description: Mandates the substitution of 'Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India' with 'Industrial Investment Bank of India Limited' and 'Reconstruction Bank' with 'Industrial Investment Bank' in all existing Acts, rules, or regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal and saving of Act 62 of 1984
main_sections.description: Repeals the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984, while saving certain provisions related to annual accounts, audit, and existing arrangements with industrial concerns.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984 [Repealed]
main_sections.description: This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2001.

Repeals the Industrial Reconstruction Bank (Transfer of Undertakings and Repeal) Ordinance, 1997, and provides that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: On the appointed day, the entire undertaking of the Reconstruction Bank shall be transferred to and vest in the Company (Industrial Investment Bank of India Limited).
All contracts, deeds, bonds, guarantees, and working arrangements affecting the Reconstruction Bank shall become enforceable by or against the Company.
Legal proceedings pending by or against the Reconstruction Bank shall be continued by or against the Company.

Officers and employees of the Reconstruction Bank (excluding Directors, Chairman, and Managing Director) become employees of the Company with the same terms and conditions of service, unless they opt not to continue within six months.
The Company shall be exempt from paying income-tax or any other tax for five years from the appointed day on income, profits, or gains derived.
The shares, bonds, and debentures of the Company are deemed to be approved securities for the purposes of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and the Insurance Act, 1938.
The Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984, stands repealed from the appointed day, with savings for certain provisions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (implied through notifications and appointments)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the vesting of undertakings, continuation of legal proceedings, and the provisions for employees and contracts.

rights: Employees have the right to continue in employment with the Company under the same terms and conditions.
Employees are entitled to the same benefits, rights, and privileges as they would have had under the Reconstruction Bank.
Retired employees are entitled to receive their benefits, rights, or privileges from the Company.
The Company retains all rights, powers, authorities, and privileges of the Reconstruction Bank.
duties: The Company has the duty to take over the entire undertaking of the Reconstruction Bank.
The Company has the duty to uphold the terms of employment and benefits for transferred employees.
The Company must comply with the provisions of Chapter VII of the repealed Act regarding annual accounts and audit.
The Company must comply with the provisions of Chapter VIII of the repealed Act concerning arrangements with industrial concerns.
obligations: The Company inherits all liabilities and obligations of the Reconstruction Bank.
Transferred employees have obligations to hold their office or service with the Company under the same terms and conditions.
Directors appointed by the Company to other concerns must act within the scope of their appointment.

key_procedures: Appointment of the 'appointed day' by the Central Government via notification.
Transfer and vesting of the Reconstruction Bank's undertakings in the Company on the appointed day.
Automatic transfer of employees' service to the Company, with an option to opt out within six months.
Continuation of contracts, deeds, and legal proceedings by or against the Company.
Compliance with certain chapters of the repealed Act for accounts, audit, and existing arrangements.
administration: Central Government (implied for appointing the 'appointed day' and general oversight)
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 24, 1997.
The Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984, is repealed.
No compensation is payable to officers or employees for the transfer of their services to the Company.
The transfer of undertakings is not considered a transfer for capital gains tax purposes.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect actions taken under it; they are deemed to be under the Act.

title: The Lalit Kala Akadami (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1997
purpose: To provide for the taking over of the management of the Lalit Kala Akadami for a limited period in the public interest and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the Lalit Kala Akadami, a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. Its scope is to take over the management of the society and its assets. The initial period of management is three years, extendable up to a total of five years. It applies to individuals in charge of the management and employees of the society.

key_definitions.Administrator: A person appointed as the Administrator under section 4.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Societies Registration Act: The Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860), as in force in the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
key_definitions.society: The Lalit Kala Akadami being a society registered under the Societies Registration Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is deemed to be January 24, 1997.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'prescribed', 'Societies Registration Act', and 'society'.

Vests the management of the Lalit Kala Akadami in the Central Government for a period of three years, extendable up to a total of five years. It outlines what is included in the management and states that existing contracts and offices held by management personnel are terminated.

Details the appointment of an Administrator by the Central Government to manage the society. It outlines the Administrator's powers, duties, and reporting structure, including the delivery of society property and accounting for documents.

main_sections.section_title: No right to compensation for premature termination of a contract
main_sections.description: States that no person is entitled to compensation for the premature termination of a management contract or for the loss of office due to the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Relinquishment of administration of the society
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to relinquish the management of the society before the expiry of the period if it deems it no longer necessary. Upon relinquishment, the administration vests back in the General Council of the society.

Specifies how the Societies Registration Act, 1860, applies to the Lalit Kala Akadami while its management is vested in the Central Government. It restricts certain actions by members and the General Council without Central Government approval.
Defines penalties for various offenses related to the withholding, wrongful possession, destruction, or failure to account for the society's property or documents.
Addresses offenses committed by companies, holding those in charge responsible, and includes provisions for directors, managers, and other officers.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of period of operation of Act
main_sections.description: Relates to the computation of the period of limitation for suits or applications by the society.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Protects the Central Government and any person acting in good faith under the Act from legal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Contracts in bad faith may be cancelled or varied
main_sections.description: Allows for the cancellation or variation of contracts entered into in bad faith.

main_sections.section_title: Power to terminate contract of employment
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to terminate any contract of employment.
Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any ordinance that might have been in force and provides for savings.

important_rules: Management of the society vests in the Central Government for a period of three years, extendable up to a total of five years (Section 3(1)).
All existing contracts related to the management of the society are terminated upon commencement of the Act (Section 3(3)).
All persons in charge of the management, including Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, and members of various committees, vacate their offices (Section 3(4)).
The Central Government shall appoint an Administrator to manage the society (Section 4(1)).
The Administrator has broad powers, including the disposal of society property, subject to Central Government directions (Section 4(4)).
Every person in possession of society property must deliver it to the Administrator (Section 4(5)).
Persons in charge of administration before commencement must furnish a complete inventory of properties, assets, liabilities, and obligations to the Administrator (Section 4(7)).
No compensation is payable for premature termination of contracts or loss of office (Section 5).
The Central Government can relinquish management if its purposes are fulfilled or no longer necessary (Section 6(1)).
While management is vested in the Central Government, members cannot appoint new General Council members, and resolutions require government approval (Section 7(1)).
Any person wrongfully withholding or failing to account for society property or documents is punishable (Section 8).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both, for wrongfully withholding, obtaining possession, retaining, failing to deliver, removing or destroying society property or documents, or failing to account for them (Section 8).

Offences by companies are punishable, with liability extended to persons in charge and responsible for the company's business. Directors, managers, or officers are also liable if the offense is committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect (Section 9).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through the Administrator appointed by it.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of an Administrator, the vesting of management in the Central Government, the termination of existing management structures, and the imposition of penalties for non-compliance. The Central Government can issue directions to the Administrator, and the Administrator can seek instructions from the Central Government. The Act also allows for legal proceedings against offenders.

rights: Right of the Central Government to take over and manage the society.
Right of the Administrator to exercise powers of the General Council/Executive Board, including disposal of property.
Right of the Central Government to issue directions to the Administrator.
Right of the Central Government to relinquish management.
Protection of action taken in good faith under the Act.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to appoint an Administrator.
Duty of the Administrator to carry on the management of the society on behalf of the Central Government.
Duty of persons in possession of society property to deliver it to the Administrator.
Duty of persons in charge of administration to furnish an inventory of properties, assets, liabilities, and obligations.
Duty of the Central Government to ensure proper management of the society.
obligations: Obligation of individuals to comply with the Act's provisions regarding property and documentation.
Obligation of companies and their officers to comply with the Act and prevent offenses.
Obligation for all concerned to cooperate with the Administrator.

key_procedures: Taking over of management: On commencement, management vests in the Central Government, and existing management personnel vacate their offices (Section 3).

Appointment and functioning of Administrator: Central Government appoints an Administrator who manages the society, with powers including property disposal, subject to government directions (Section 4).
Delivery of property and documentation: Persons in possession must deliver property to the Administrator and account for books and documents (Section 4(5), 4(6)).
Furnishing inventory: Previous administrators must provide a complete inventory of assets, liabilities, and agreements to the Administrator within ten days (Section 4(7)).
Relinquishment of management: Central Government may relinquish management by publishing an order in the Official Gazette (Section 6(1)).
Application of Societies Registration Act: While management is with the Central Government, certain actions require government approval (Section 7).
administration: The Central Government, through an appointed Administrator.
important_notes: The Act came into force retrospectively from January 24, 1997.
The initial period of management is three years, but can be extended by the Central Government for periods not exceeding one year at a time, with a total maximum period of five years.
Contracts in bad faith entered into by the society can be cancelled or varied.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over any other conflicting law.

title: The Vice-President's Pension Act, 1997
purpose: To provide for the payment of pension and other facilities to retiring Vice-Presidents.
scope: This act applies to persons who have held the office of Vice-President of India. It specifies pensions, family pensions, and various facilities to be provided to them and their families after they cease to hold office. It also covers provisions for the spouse of a deceased Vice-President.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Vice-President's Pension Act, 1997'.

This section details the pension payable to persons who cease to hold the office of Vice-President, including the rate of pension (50% of the salary of the Vice-President). It also outlines conditions under which the pension is not payable (e.g., holding office of Prime Minister, Minister, or MP). It includes provisions for family pension to the spouse of a deceased Vice-President and lists various entitlements such as furnished residence, telephone facilities, secretarial staff, office expenses, medical facilities, and travel facilities. It also specifies that re-elected Vice-Presidents or those elected as President are not eligible for benefits under this section during their tenure in those offices.

main_sections.section_title: Medical facilities to the family of deceased Vice-President.
main_sections.description: This section states that the spouse of a person who dies while holding the office of Vice-President is entitled to free medical attendance and treatment for life.

main_sections.section_title: Free accommodation to spouse of Vice-President.
main_sections.description: This section grants the spouse of a deceased Vice-President (whether they died in office or after ceasing to hold office) the right to use furnished accommodation without payment of license fee for the remainder of her life.

main_sections.section_title: Pension to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
main_sections.description: This section mandates that any sum payable under this Act shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

This section empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. It also includes a provision for laying these rules before each House of Parliament for modification or annulment.

This section, added by a later amendment, empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act. Such orders must be consistent with the Act's provisions and cannot be made after two years from the Act's commencement. Orders made under this section must also be laid before each House of Parliament.

important_rules: A retiring Vice-President is entitled to a pension at the rate of fifty percent of the salary of the Vice-President per month for the rest of his life.
The spouse of a deceased Vice-President is entitled to a family pension at the rate of fifty percent of the pension admissible to a retiring Vice-President, for the remainder of her life.
Retiring Vice-Presidents are entitled to rent-free furnished accommodation, telephone facilities, secretarial staff, office expenses, medical attendance and treatment, and travel facilities.
The spouse of a deceased Vice-President is entitled to free medical attendance and treatment for life.
The spouse of a deceased Vice-President is entitled to the use of furnished accommodation without payment of licence fee for life.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Central Government and laid before Parliament. Any difficulties in implementation can be addressed by orders from the Central Government.

rights: Right to receive a pension after ceasing to hold office as Vice-President.
Right to receive family pension for the spouse of a deceased Vice-President.
Right to furnished accommodation (rent-free).
Right to telephone facilities.
Right to secretarial staff and office expenses.
Right to medical attendance and treatment for self and family.
Right to travel anywhere in India with spouse, companion, or relative by the highest class.
Right to use furnished residence without payment of licence fee for the spouse of a deceased Vice-President.

key_procedures: Payment of pension to retiring Vice-Presidents upon ceasing to hold office, subject to certain conditions.
Payment of family pension to the spouse of a deceased Vice-President.
Application of Central Government rules to determine the specific entitlements for accommodation, medical facilities, etc.
Laying of rules and orders before Parliament for review and approval/modification.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: A person receiving pension under this Act is not entitled to it if they hold the office of Prime Minister, Minister, or any other office, or become a Member of Parliament and are in receipt of salary and allowances defrayed out of the Consolidated Fund of India or a State.

If a person is re-elected to the office of Vice-President, or gets elected to the office of President of India, they or their spouse are not eligible for benefits under this section for the period they hold such office.
Provisions for pension and facilities are subject to rules made by the Central Government.
The Act has been amended over time to update pension rates and other financial entitlements.

title: THE DOCK WORKERS (REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT) (INAPPLICABILITY TO MAJOR PORTS) ACT, 1997
purpose: To provide for the inapplicability of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, to dock workers of major port trusts and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This act applies to dock workers of major port trusts in India. The subject matter scope is the regulation of employment of dock workers, specifically making the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, inapplicable to major ports.

key_definitions.appointed day: In relation to a major port, the date specified under section 3 for that major port.
key_definitions.Board: Has the same meaning as in the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 (38 of 1963).
key_definitions.Dock Labour Board: A Dock Labour Board established under section 5A of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 (9 of 1948).
key_definitions.major port: Has the same meaning as in the Indian Ports Act, 1908 (15 of 1908).

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
