This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Dock Labour Board', and 'major port'.

main_sections.section_title: Inapplicability of the provisions of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 to major ports
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Central Government to direct, by notification in the Official Gazette, that the provisions of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, shall cease to have effect in relation to a major port. This direction can be made after a settlement is arrived at between the Dock Labour Board of the major port, its workmen, and the management of that major port, in accordance with the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the Dock Labour Board, etc., to the Board
main_sections.description: This section outlines the transfer of assets, liabilities, contracts, sums due, suits, legal proceedings, and employee services from the Dock Labour Board to the 'Board' (as defined) on the 'appointed day' for a major port. It also clarifies that the transfer of services does not entitle employees to compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or any other law.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Central Government can make the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 inapplicable to a major port after a settlement is reached between the Dock Labour Board, its workmen, and the port management, as per the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. This is done through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Rule 2: On the appointed day for a major port, all properties, assets, and funds of the Dock Labour Board vest in the 'Board'.
Rule 3: All debts, obligations, liabilities, contracts, and matters engaged by the Dock Labour Board vest in the 'Board'.
Rule 4: All sums of money due to the Dock Labour Board are deemed to be due to the 'Board'.
Rule 5: All suits and legal proceedings by or against the Dock Labour Board may be continued by or against the 'Board'.

Rule 6: Employees and workers serving under the Dock Labour Board continue their service under the 'Board' on terms and conditions no less favorable than their previous ones, unless their employment is duly terminated or their tenure, remuneration, or terms are duly altered by the 'Board'.
Rule 7: The transfer of employee services to the 'Board' does not entitle them to compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or any other law.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and potentially the 'Board' as it takes over functions from the Dock Labour Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette for making the Act inapplicable and by the transfer of powers and responsibilities from the Dock Labour Board to the 'Board'.

rights: Dock workers of major port trusts have the right to have their employment regulation governed by the 'Board' instead of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, once section 3 is invoked.
Employees and workers transferred to the 'Board' have the right to continue service on terms and conditions not less favorable than those they previously held.
duties: The Central Government has the duty to ensure settlements are arrived at before making the Act inapplicable to major ports.
The 'Board' has the duty to take over all assets, liabilities, and ongoing legal matters from the Dock Labour Board.
The 'Board' has a duty to ensure that the terms and conditions of service for transferred employees are not less favorable.
obligations: Dock Labour Boards have obligations related to their establishment and operation under the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, which are then transferred to the 'Board'.
Management of major ports have obligations to reach settlements with their workmen and the Dock Labour Board.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: For an Act to become inapplicable to a major port: (a) A settlement must be arrived at between the Dock Labour Board of the major port, its workmen, and the management of that major port, in accordance with the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. (b) The Central Government must issue a notification in the Official Gazette directing that the provisions of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, shall cease to have effect in relation to that major port from a specified date.

Procedure 2: Transfer of assets and liabilities to the 'Board': On the 'appointed day' for a major port, all property, assets, funds, debts, obligations, liabilities, contracts, sums due, and legal proceedings of the Dock Labour Board are automatically vested in or deemed to be transferred to the 'Board'.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for enacting notifications to bring the Act into force and to make the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 inapplicable to major ports. The 'Board' (as defined in the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963) administers the transferred functions and affairs.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act is determined by a notification from the Central Government, which was January 5, 1998.
The transfer of employee services to the 'Board' under section 4 does not entitle those employees to any compensation, and no such claim will be entertained by any court or tribunal.
The 'Board' is defined by reference to the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963.
A 'major port' is defined by reference to the Indian Ports Act, 1908.

title: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India and the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal to regulate telecommunication services, adjudicate disputes, dispose of appeals, protect the interests of service providers and consumers in the telecom sector, and promote and ensure the orderly growth of the telecom sector.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to telecommunication services, service providers, and consumers within India.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date with effect from which the Authority is established.
key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: The Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal established under section 14.
key_definitions.Authority: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Authority appointed under sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund constituted under sub-section (1) of section 22.
key_definitions.licensee: Any person licensed under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 (13 of 1885) for providing specified public telecommunication services.
key_definitions.licensor: The Central Government or the telegraph authority who grants a licence under section 4 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 (13 of 1885).
key_definitions.member: A member of the Authority appointed under sub-section (3) of section 3, including the Chairperson and the Vice-Chairperson.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Authority under this Act.
key_definitions.service provider: The Government as a service provider and includes a licensee.
key_definitions.telecommunication service: Service of any description (including electronic mail, voice mail, data services, audio tex services, video tex services, radio paging and cellular mobile telephone services) made available to users by any transmission or reception of signs, signals, writing, images and sounds or intelligence of any nature, by wire, radio, visual or other electro-magnetic means, but shall not include broadcasting services. The Central Government may notify other services to be telecommunication services, including broadcasting services.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of commencement.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Appellate Tribunal', 'Authority', 'Chairperson', 'Fund', 'licensee', 'licensor', 'member', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'regulations', 'service provider', and 'telecommunication service'.

Establishes the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. Specifies its composition (Chairperson, whole-time and part-time members) and head office location.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications for appointment of Chairperson and other members
main_sections.description: Outlines the qualifications required for the Chairperson and other members, emphasizing special knowledge and professional experience in relevant fields. Includes provisos for persons in government service and those not in government service.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office, conditions of service, etc., of Chairperson and other members
main_sections.description: Details the term of office (not exceeding three years or until age sixty-five, whichever is earlier), conditions of service, and provisions for vacation of office or removal of the Chairperson and members. Includes provisions regarding retirement of government employees upon selection and restrictions on future employment.

Defines the powers of the Chairperson regarding general superintendence and direction of the Authority's affairs, presiding over meetings, and exercising other prescribed functions. Allows for the appointment of a Vice-Chairperson to exercise delegated powers.

main_sections.section_title: Removal and suspension of member from office in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Specifies the grounds on which a member can be removed from office by the Central Government, including insolvency, conviction of an offense involving moral turpitude, physical or mental incapacity, acquisition of prejudicial interests, or abuse of position. Requires a reasonable opportunity of being heard for removal based on clauses (d) or (e).
Stipulates that the Authority shall meet at specified times and places and observe prescribed rules of procedure for its meetings, including quorum.
Details the functions of the Authority, which are regulatory in nature for the telecommunication sector.
Provides for the establishment of the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Civil court not to have jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters that the Appellate Tribunal is empowered to decide.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for wilful failure to comply with orders of Appellate Tribunal
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for wilful failure to comply with the orders of the Appellate Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of directions of Authority
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening directions issued by the Authority.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations for carrying out its functions.
Deals with the repeal of any previous enactments and savings provisions.

important_rules: Members of the Authority must not have financial or other interests that could prejudicially affect their functions.

The Chairperson and whole-time members are restricted from accepting employment with the Central or State Government or in telecommunication service companies for two years after leaving office without prior approval.
Members can be removed from office under specific conditions such as insolvency, conviction of an offense involving moral turpitude, incapacity, or acquisition of prejudicial interests.
Civil courts are barred from exercising jurisdiction over matters that the Appellate Tribunal is empowered to adjudicate.
Penalties are prescribed for wilful failure to comply with orders of the Appellate Tribunal and for contravention of directions issued by the Authority.

penalties: Penalty for wilful failure to comply with orders of Appellate Tribunal (Section 20).
Penalty for contravention of directions of Authority (Section 29).
Offences by companies (Section 30).
Offences by Government Departments (Section 31).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) and the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAAT).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of directions, adjudication of disputes, imposition of penalties, and appeals to higher courts.

rights: Right to seek adjudication of disputes before the Appellate Tribunal.
Right to appeal to the Supreme Court against orders of the Appellate Tribunal.
Protection of interests of service providers and consumers in the telecom sector.
Right to fair regulation and orderly growth of the telecom sector.
duties: Duty to regulate telecommunication services.
Duty to adjudicate disputes.
Duty to protect the interests of service providers and consumers.
Duty to promote and ensure orderly growth of the telecom sector.
obligations: Obligation to comply with directions issued by the Authority.
Obligation to comply with orders passed by the Appellate Tribunal.
Licensing obligations for service providers as per the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885.

key_procedures: Establishment and incorporation of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India.
Appointment and qualifications of the Chairperson and members of the Authority.
Conduct of meetings and transaction of business by the Authority.
Establishment and composition of the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal.
Procedure for settlement of disputes and appeals before the Appellate Tribunal.
Procedure for appeals to the Supreme Court.
Procedures related to finance, accounts, and audit of the Authority.
administration: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) and the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAAT), established under this Act, along with the Central Government for certain powers and oversight.
important_notes: The Act has been amended by various subsequent acts including The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Amendment) Act, 2000, The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Amendment) Act, 2014, The Finance Act, 2017, The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, The Telecommunications Act, 2023, and The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
The Act extends to the whole of India and was deemed to have come into force on January 25, 1997.

The Act specifies that words and expressions not defined in it but defined in the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, or the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, shall have the meanings assigned to them in those Acts.
For the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territories), the Act is construed with reference to the corresponding law in that State.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Authority and to make rules for the implementation of the Act.
The Authority has the power to make regulations.
Rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

title: THE NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH ACT, 1998
purpose: To declare certain institutions of pharmaceutical education and research to be institutions of national importance and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to institutions of pharmaceutical education and research that are declared as institutions of national importance. It also establishes a Council to oversee these institutes. The scope is national, focusing on pharmaceutical education, research, and related areas. It also allows for the establishment of new institutes by the Central Government.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of establishment of an Institute as mentioned in the Schedule.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of an Institute constituted under sub-section (3) of section 4.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of an Institute nominated under clause (a) of sub-section (3) of section (4).
key_definitions.Council: The Council established under sub-section (1) of section 30A.
key_definitions.Dean: The Dean of an Institute appointed under section 17.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of an Institute appointed under section 16.
key_definitions.Fund: The fund of an Institute to be maintained under section 21.
key_definitions.Institute: Any of the institutions mentioned in column (3) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Council nominated or elected under sub-section (2) of section 30A.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Senate: The Senate of an Institute referred to in section 13.
key_definitions.Society: The National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research Society, Sector-67, S.A.S. Nagar (Mohali), Punjab registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: The Statutes and the Ordinances of an Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the institutions mentioned in the Schedule, and those established under sub-section (2A) of section 4, as institutions of national importance.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Council', 'Dean', 'Director', 'Fund', 'Institute', 'member', 'prescribed', 'Schedule', 'Senate', 'Society', 'Statutes', and 'Ordinances'.

Establishes the listed institutions as bodies corporate with perpetual succession and common seal, capable of acquiring property and suing or being sued. It also allows the Central Government to establish new institutes and details the composition of the Board of Governors.
Allows an Institute, with prior approval of the Central Government, to establish one or more centres in different locations.

Specifies that upon incorporation, references to the Society are deemed references to the Institute, and all property, rights, and liabilities of the Society are transferred to the Institute. It also outlines employment terms for existing employees.

Details the functions of the Institutes, including promoting quality in pharmaceutical education and research, developing courses, granting degrees, cooperating with other institutions, conducting courses for professionals, maintaining literature, and acting as a nucleus for industry-academia interaction.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Board of an Institute
main_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of the Board of an Institute, including general superintendence, direction, and control of affairs, decision-making on policy, fee fixation, supervision of students, appointments, framing Statutes and Ordinances, and instituting awards.
Provides for the establishment of a Council.
Details the functions of the Council.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Institutes.
Empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: Institutes are to be open to all races, creeds, and classes (Section 9).
The Board of an Institute must meet at least three times a year (Section 4(6)).
The Central Government can issue directions to the Institutes (Section 33A).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Council are implied authorities for enforcement through their powers to issue directions, make rules, and oversee the Institutes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Central Government to issue directions, the Council's oversight functions, and the established authorities within each Institute (Board, Senate, Director, etc.). Specific penalties are not detailed in the provided text.

rights: Employees of the Society immediately before the appointed day retain their employment terms, remuneration, and benefits in the Institute, unless altered by Statutes, with provisions for termination compensation (Section 6(c)).
The right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract for Institutes (Section 4(2)).
The right to sue and be sued by the name of the Institute (Section 4(2)).
duties: Institutes have a duty to nurture and promote quality and excellence in pharmaceutical education and research (Section 7(i)).
Institutes have a duty to cooperate with other institutions for common objectives (Section 7(v)).
Institutes have a duty to pay due attention to studies on the distribution and usage of drugs by rural masses (Section 7(xv)).
obligations: Institutes are obligated to develop courses and grant degrees (Section 7(ii), (iii)).
Institutes are obligated to consider and pass resolutions on annual reports and accounts (Section 8(2)(e)).
Institutes are obligated to meet and maintain financial accounts and undergo audit (Section 23).

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).
Establishment of Institutes: The Central Government may establish new Institutes by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 4(2A)).
Board Meetings: The Board shall meet at least three times a year, with place, time, and procedure determined by the Board (Section 4(6)).

Statutes and Ordinances: Statutes and Ordinances are to be made, altered, modified, or rescinded by the Board and then published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament (Sections 26, 27, 28, 29, 36).
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative body, with specific responsibilities for notification, direction, and oversight. Each Institute is administered by its Board of Governors, Senate, Director, and other officers.
important_notes: The Act has been amended significantly, particularly by the National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (Amendment) Act, 2021, which introduced new clauses and modified existing ones, including relating to the Council and the definition of 'Institute'.
Section 5 concerning 'Vesting of properties' was omitted by the 2021 amendment.
Specific penalties for violations are not detailed in the provided excerpt; this might be covered in further sections or related rules.

title: The Lotteries (Regulation) Act, 1998
purpose: To regulate lotteries and to provide for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It regulates lotteries organized, conducted, or promoted by State Governments, and prohibits certain activities related to lotteries.

key_definitions.bumper_draw_of_a_lottery: A special draw of lottery conducted on or during any festival or other special occasion wherein the prize money offered is greater than the prize money offered in the case of other ordinary draws of lotteries.
key_definitions.lottery: A scheme, in whatever form and by whatever name called, for distribution of prizes by lot or chance to those persons participating in the chances of a prize by purchasing tickets.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on October 2, 1997).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'bumper draw of a lottery', 'lottery', and 'prescribed'.
Prohibits any State Government from organizing, conducting, or promoting any lottery, unless otherwise provided in section 4.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions subject to which lotteries may be organised, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies the conditions under which a State Government may organize, conduct, or promote a lottery. These include conditions related to prize offerings, ticket printing, sales, prize money crediting, draw conduct, unclaimed prize money, draw location, frequency of draws, bumper draws, and other conditions prescribed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of sale of ticket in a State
main_sections.description: Empowers a State Government to prohibit the sale of tickets of lotteries organized by any other State within its own State.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of organisation, etc., of lottery
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to prohibit a lottery organized in contravention of section 4 or where tickets are sold in contravention of section 5, by an order published in the Official Gazette.

Prescribes penalties for contravention of the Act. For State Government departments, the Head of the Department is punishable. For agents, promoters, or traders, rigorous imprisonment or fine or both are prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable
main_sections.description: Declares offences under the Act as cognizable and non-bailable.

Deals with offences committed by companies, making persons in charge of the company's business responsible, and also specifying liability for directors, managers, etc., in case of consent, connivance, or neglect.
Authorizes the Central Government to give directions to State Governments regarding the execution of the Act's provisions or rules made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the Act's provisions, with a procedure for laying rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to make rules to carry out the Act's provisions, particularly concerning prize money claim times, draw periods, and other prescribed matters, with a procedure for laying rules before the State Legislature.
Repeals the Lotteries (Regulation) Ordinance, 1998, and saves anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance, deeming it done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Prizes in State lotteries shall not be offered on any pre-announced number or on the basis of a single digit.
State Governments must print lottery tickets with their imprint and logo to ensure authenticity.
State Governments must sell tickets either directly or through distributors/selling agents.
Proceeds from lottery ticket sales must be credited to the public account of the State.
State Governments must conduct the draws of all lotteries themselves.
Unclaimed prize money, after a prescribed time, becomes the property of the State Government.
The place of draw must be located within the State concerned.
No lottery shall have more than one draw in a week.
Draws of all lotteries must be conducted within prescribed periods of the day.
The number of bumper draws shall not exceed six in a calendar year.

penalties: For contravention by a State Government Department: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both, for the Head of the Department.
For contravention by an officer (other than Head of Department) with consent, connivance, or neglect: liable to be proceeded against and punished.

For acting as an agent, promoter, or trader in a lottery organized in contravention of the Act, or selling/distributing/purchasing tickets of such lottery: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, and their respective authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penal provisions for contravention, powers of prohibition by the Central Government, and the issuance of directions and rules by both Central and State Governments.

rights: The right of a State Government to organize, conduct, or promote a lottery under specified conditions.
The right of a State Government to prohibit the sale of tickets of other States' lotteries within its territory.
The right of individuals to claim prizes, subject to rules regarding unclaimed prize money.
duties: Duty of State Governments to comply with the conditions for organizing lotteries.
Duty of State Governments to credit lottery proceeds to the public account.
Duty of State Governments to conduct draws themselves.
Duty of any person involved in a lottery to ensure compliance with the Act.
Duty of individuals involved in companies to ensure the company's compliance with the Act.
obligations: Obligation of State Governments to print authentic tickets.
Obligation of State Governments to conduct draws within prescribed times and locations.
Obligation of any person to not act as an agent, promoter, or trader in a lottery organized in contravention of the Act.
Obligation of any person to not sell, distribute, or purchase tickets of a lottery organized in contravention of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for State Governments to organize lotteries: must adhere to conditions outlined in Section 4, including prize structure, ticket authenticity, sales channels, fund crediting, draw conduct, unclaimed prize handling, draw location, draw frequency, and bumper draw limits.

Procedure for making rules by Central and State Governments: by notification in the Official Gazette, with rules made by the Central Government to be laid before both Houses of Parliament and rules made by State Governments to be laid before the respective State Legislature(s).
Procedure for Central Government prohibition of lotteries: by order published in the Official Gazette, for lotteries contravening Section 4 or Section 5.
administration: The Central Government and the State Governments administer this Act, with powers vested in the Central Government to issue directions and make rules, and in State Governments to make rules and enforce provisions within their respective territories.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 2, 1997.
The Act repeals the Lotteries (Regulation) Ordinance, 1998, but actions taken under the Ordinance are saved.
For offences by companies, individuals within the company are liable if they were in charge of the business or if the offence was committed with their consent or connivance or due to their neglect.

title: The Leaders and Chief Whips of Recognised Parties and Groups in Parliament (Facilities) Act, 1998
purpose: To provide for facilities to Leaders and Chief Whips of recognised parties and groups in Parliament.
scope: Applies to Leaders, Deputy Leaders, and Chief Whips of recognised parties and groups in the Council of States and the House of the People in India. Recognised groups and parties are defined by their strength in these Houses. It also amends the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959.

key_definitions.recognised_group: In relation to the Council of States, a party with 15 to 24 members; in relation to the House of the People, a party with 30 to 54 members.
key_definitions.recognised_party: In relation to the Council of States, a party with at least 25 members; in relation to the House of the People, a party with at least 55 members.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is deemed to be February 5, 1999.
Defines 'recognised group' and 'recognised party' based on the number of members in the Council of States and the House of the People.

main_sections.section_title: Facilities to the Leaders and Chief Whips of recognised groups and parties
main_sections.description: Entitles leaders, deputy leaders, and Chief Whips of recognised groups and parties to telephone and secretarial facilities, subject to rules made by the Central Government. Exclusions apply if they hold certain ministerial or opposition leader posts, or are entitled to similar facilities from other government bodies.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, with a provision for laying these rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 3 of Act 10 of 1959
main_sections.description: Amends the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959, by inserting a clause that exempts the office of each leader and deputy leader of a recognised party and group from disqualification. It also defines 'recognised party' and 'recognised group' within this context.

important_rules: Leaders, deputy leaders, and Chief Whips of recognised parties and groups are entitled to telephone and secretarial facilities.

These facilities are not provided if the individual holds a ministerial office, the office of Leader of the Opposition, or similar facilities by virtue of holding office in any Parliamentary or other committee/body set up by the Government, or provided in any other capacity by the Government or its controlled entities.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for making rules)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Central Government and laid before Parliament. The amendment to the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959, implies enforcement through ensuring these offices do not lead to disqualification.

rights: Right to telephone facilities for Leaders, Deputy Leaders, and Chief Whips of recognised parties and groups.
Right to secretarial facilities for Leaders, Deputy Leaders, and Chief Whips of recognised parties and groups.
Exemption from disqualification for holding the office of a leader or deputy leader of a recognised party and group.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.
obligations: Obligation to provide telephone and secretarial facilities subject to the conditions in Section 3.
Obligation for rules made by the Central Government to be laid before Parliament.

key_procedures: The Central Government may make rules by notification in the Official Gazette for carrying out the provisions of this Act.
Every rule made under sub-section (1) of Section 4 must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days, allowing for modifications or annulment by both Houses.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The commencement of the Act is deemed to be February 5, 1999.
Amendments to Section 2 and Section 3 were made by Act 18 of 2000, effective from June 7, 2000, and February 5, 1999, respectively.

title: The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
purpose: To provide for the registration and better protection of geographical indications relating to goods.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to agricultural goods, natural goods, manufactured goods, and handicrafts/industry goods. It also covers foodstuff. It identifies goods as originating or manufactured in a territory, region, or locality where a given quality, reputation, or characteristic is essentially attributable to its geographical origin.

key_definitions.authorised_user: A user of a geographical indication registered under section 17.
key_definitions.deceptively_similar: A geographical indication that so nearly resembles another geographical indication as to be likely to deceive or cause confusion.
key_definitions.district_court: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
key_definitions.geographical_indication: An indication that identifies goods (agricultural, natural, or manufactured) as originating or manufactured in a territory, region, or locality where a given quality, reputation, or other characteristic of such goods is essentially attributable to its geographical origin. For manufactured goods, one of the activities of production, processing, or preparation must take place in that territory, region, or locality. This can include names not explicitly of a country, region, or locality, if they relate to a specific geographical area and are used for goods originating from there.
key_definitions.goods: Any agricultural, natural, or manufactured goods, or any goods of handicraft or of industry, including foodstuff.
key_definitions.indication: Includes any name, geographical or figurative representation, or any combination of them, conveying or suggesting the geographical origin of goods.
key_definitions.name: Includes any abbreviation of a name.
key_definitions.package: Includes any case, box, container, covering, folder, receptacle, vessel, casket, bottle, wrapper, label, band, ticket, reel, frame, capsule, cap, lid, stopper, and cork.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.producer: In relation to goods, means a person who produces agricultural goods (including processing/packaging), exploits natural goods, or makes/manufactures handicraft/industrial goods. It also includes any person who trades or deals in these activities.
key_definitions.register: The Register of Geographical Indications referred to in section 6.
key_definitions.registered_proprietor: Any association of persons or of producers or any organisation entered in the register as proprietor of the geographical indication.
key_definitions.Registrar: The Registrar of Geographical Indications referred to in section 3.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date (to be notified by the Central Government).

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'authorised user', 'deceptively similar', 'geographical indication', 'goods', 'producer', 'registered proprietor', 'Registrar', etc. It also clarifies how expressions defined in the Trade Marks Act, 1999, should be interpreted and provides rules for interpreting references within the Act.
Appoints the Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks as the Registrar of Geographical Indications and empowers the Central Government to appoint other officers to assist the Registrar.

main_sections.section_title: Geographical Indications Registry and offices thereof
main_sections.description: Establishes the Geographical Indications Registry, specifies the location of its head office, and allows for the establishment of branch offices. It also outlines the territorial limits within which these offices can function and mandates a seal for the Registry.

Describes the Register of Geographical Indications where registered geographical indications, proprietors, and authorised users are to be entered. It allows for the register to be maintained electronically and states that no notice of trust will be entered or received by the Registrar. The register is under the control and management of the Registrar.

main_sections.section_title: Part A and Part B of the register
main_sections.description: Divides the register into Part A (for registration of geographical indications) and Part B (for registration of authorised users).

main_sections.section_title: Registration to be in respect of particular goods and area
main_sections.description: States that a geographical indication can be registered for any or all of the specified goods.
Details the exclusive rights granted to the registered proprietor of a geographical indication.
Defines what constitutes infringement of a registered geographical indication.
Explains what it means to apply a geographical indication.

main_sections.section_title: Falsifying and falsely applying geographical indications
main_sections.description: Deals with the offences of falsifying and falsely applying geographical indications.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for applying false geographical indications
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for applying false geographical indications.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for selling goods to which false geographical indication is applied
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for selling goods with a falsely applied geographical indication.

main_sections.section_title: Enhanced penalty on second or subsequent conviction
main_sections.description: Provides for enhanced penalties for repeat offenders.
Allows for the forfeiture of goods in certain cases related to offences.

main_sections.section_title: Cognizance of certain offences and the powers of police officer for search and seizure
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for taking cognizance of offences and grants police officers powers for search and seizure.

main_sections.section_title: Suit for infringement, etc., to be instituted before district court
main_sections.description: Specifies that suits for infringement or passing off are to be instituted before the District Court.

main_sections.section_title: Relief in suit for infringement or for passing off
main_sections.description: Details the relief available in suits for infringement or passing off.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: A geographical indication is defined by its origin in a specific territory, region, or locality, where its quality, reputation, or other characteristic is essentially attributable to that origin.
Registration of a geographical indication is to be in respect of particular goods and a specific geographical area.
The Act prohibits the registration of certain geographical indications, including those that are deceptive or likely to cause confusion.
Homonymous geographical indications (those with the same name but different origins) can be registered under certain conditions.
Infringement of a registered geographical indication is an offence.
Selling goods to which a false geographical indication is applied is subject to penalties.
Suits for infringement or passing off must be filed in the District Court.

penalties: Penalty for applying false geographical indications (Section 39).
Penalty for selling goods to which a false geographical indication is applied (Section 40).
Enhanced penalty on second or subsequent conviction (Section 41).
Forfeiture of goods (Section 46).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Geographical Indications, police officers (for search and seizure), and District Courts (for suits and adjudication of penalties).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration and maintenance of a Register of Geographical Indications, legal proceedings instituted in District Courts for infringement or passing off, and criminal prosecution for offences related to falsifying or falsely applying geographical indications. Police officers have powers of search and seizure.

rights: Exclusive right to use the registered geographical indication in relation to the goods.
Right to prevent unauthorized use of the registered geographical indication by third parties.
Right to take legal action against infringement or passing off.
Right to protection against the registration of deceptive geographical indications or trademarks.
duties: Producers and authorised users must use the geographical indication in accordance with the prescribed manner.
The registered proprietor must maintain the quality and characteristics of the goods associated with the geographical indication.
To ensure that the goods for which the indication is registered originate from the specified geographical area and possess the defined quality or reputation.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation to register as an authorised user if one wishes to use a registered geographical indication.
Obligation not to engage in any act that would falsely represent a geographical indication as registered.

key_procedures: Application for registration of a geographical indication, followed by advertisement, opposition, and eventual registration.
Application for registration as an authorised user of an existing registered geographical indication.
Procedures for rectification and correction of the Register of Geographical Indications.
Procedure for instituting a suit for infringement before the District Court.
Procedure for obtaining a certificate of validity of a registered geographical indication.
Procedure for dealing with offences, including search, seizure, and prosecution.
Appeals to the High Court against decisions of the Registrar or other authorities.
administration: The Central Government, through the Registrar of Geographical Indications (who is the Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks) and the Geographical Indications Registry.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India.
The commencement date for different provisions can be different and is to be notified by the Central Government.
Words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Trade Marks Act, 1999, shall have the meanings assigned to them in that Act.
No notice of any trust shall be entered in the register.
The Act provides for protection against the misuse of geographical indications, including by preventing their registration as trademarks, except under specific conditions.
It also addresses protection for prior users of trademarks and geographical indications.

title: THE INSURANCE REGULATORY AND DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT, 1999
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an Authority to protect the interests of holders of insurance policies, to regulate, promote and ensure orderly growth of the insurance industry and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto and further to amend the Insurance Act, 1938, the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 and the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to the insurance industry, including policyholders, insurers, and intermediaries.  Also amends the Insurance Act, 1938, the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956, and the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which the Authority is established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Authority: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Authority.
key_definitions.Fund: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Fund constituted under sub-section (1) of section 16.
key_definitions.Interim Insurance Regulatory Authority: The Insurance Regulatory Authority set up by the Central Government through Resolution No. 17(2)/94-Ins.-V, dated the 23rd January, 1996.
key_definitions.intermediary or insurance intermediary: Includes insurance brokers, re-insurance brokers, insurance consultants, corporate agents, third party administrator, surveyors and loss assessors and such other entities, as may be notified by the Authority from time to time.
key_definitions.member: A whole-time or a part-time member of the Authority and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: The regulations made by the Authority.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date which can be appointed by the Central Government via notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Authority', 'Chairperson', 'Fund', 'Interim Insurance Regulatory Authority', 'intermediary', 'member', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'regulations'. It also states that terms defined in other insurance-related acts (Insurance Act, 1938, LIC Act, 1956, GIBNA Act, 1972) shall have the meanings assigned to them in those acts.

Establishes the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property and contract. It also states the head office location is decided by the Central Government and the Authority can establish offices elsewhere in India.

Specifies the composition of the Authority: a Chairperson, not more than five whole-time members, and not more than four part-time members, appointed by the Central Government from individuals with relevant expertise in insurance, finance, law, etc. It also mandates that at least one person with experience in life insurance, general insurance, or actuarial science be appointed as Chairperson or whole-time member.

main_sections.section_title: Duties, powers and functions of Authority
main_sections.description: Outlines the primary duty of the Authority to regulate, promote, and ensure the orderly growth of the insurance and re-insurance business. Its powers and functions include issuing and managing registrations, protecting policyholder interests, specifying qualifications and conduct for intermediaries and agents, promoting efficiency, levying fees, calling for information, conducting inspections and investigations, and regulating rates for general insurance business not covered by the Tariff Advisory Committee.

important_rules: The Chairperson and whole-time members shall hold office for a term of five years, eligible for reappointment, with age limits of sixty-five for the Chairperson and sixty-two for whole-time members.
Part-time members shall hold office for a term not exceeding five years.
Members can relinquish office with three months' notice or be removed according to section 6.

The Central Government may remove a member if they are insolvent, mentally/physically incapable, convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, have conflicting financial interests, or have abused their position.
No act or proceeding of the Authority shall be invalid due to vacancies, defects in constitution, appointment, or procedural irregularities that do not affect the merits of the case.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (and potentially the Central Government in certain matters like superseding the Authority).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through its powers and functions, including issuing registrations, conducting inspections, investigations, and audits, and potentially through rules and regulations made under the Act.

rights: Policyholders have rights related to assignment of policy, nomination, insurable interest, settlement of insurance claims, and surrender value of policy.
Members have the right to be heard before removal from office under specific circumstances (section 6(2)).
duties: The Authority has the duty to regulate, promote, and ensure orderly growth of the insurance and re-insurance business.
The Authority has the duty to protect the interests of policyholders.
Chairperson and members of the Authority are considered public servants.
obligations: Insurers and intermediaries must maintain accounts and render statements of accounts as specified by the Authority.
Members shall not accept certain employments for two years after ceasing office without Central Government approval.
The Authority must ensure that its acts and proceedings are not invalidated by minor procedural defects or vacancies.

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairperson and members of the Authority by the Central Government.
Meetings of the Authority to be conducted according to regulations, with decisions made by majority vote.
Transfer of assets, liabilities, and legal proceedings from the Interim Insurance Regulatory Authority to the established Authority on the appointed day.
The Authority may appoint officers and employees, with their terms governed by regulations.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Authority and to supersede the Authority in certain situations.
The Authority can make regulations for its functioning and for the conduct of insurance business.
The Central Government can make rules for the Act, and rules and regulations are to be laid before Parliament.
administration: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (and the Central Government for certain powers).
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The powers of the Authority do not apply to the International Financial Services Centre (Section 23A).
The Act makes amendments to the Insurance Act, 1938, the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956, and the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972.

title: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to foreign exchange with the objective of facilitating external trade and payments and for promoting the orderly development and maintenance of foreign exchange market in India.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Also applies to all branches, offices, and agencies outside India owned or controlled by a person resident in India, and to any contravention committed outside India by any person to whom this Act applies.

key_definitions.foreign_exchange: Foreign currency and includes deposits, credits and balances payable in any foreign currency; drafts, travellers cheques, letters of credit or bills of exchange, expressed or drawn in Indian currency but payable in any foreign currency; drafts, travellers cheques, letters of credit or bills of exchange drawn by banks, institutions or persons outside India, but payable in Indian currency.
key_definitions.person_resident_in_India: A person residing in India for more than one hundred and eighty-two days during the course of the preceding financial year, but excludes certain individuals and includes bodies corporate registered or incorporated in India, and offices/branches/agencies in or outside India controlled by persons resident in India or outside India, respectively.
key_definitions.current_account_transaction: A transaction other than a capital account transaction, including payments due in connection with foreign trade, services, short-term banking and credit facilities, interest on loans, remittances for living expenses abroad, and expenses for foreign travel, education and medical care.
key_definitions.capital_account_transaction: A transaction which alters the assets or liabilities, including contingent liabilities, outside India of persons resident in India or assets or liabilities in India of persons resident outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), application to entities outside India controlled by residents, and commencement provisions.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as Adjudicating Authority, Appellate Tribunal, authorised person, currency, foreign currency, foreign exchange, foreign security, person resident in India, and current/capital account transactions.

Prohibits dealing in or transferring foreign exchange/securities to unauthorized persons, making payments to or for the credit of persons resident outside India, receiving payments from outside India otherwise than through an authorized person, and entering into financial transactions in India for assets acquired outside India.

Prohibits persons resident in India from acquiring, holding, owning, possessing or transferring any foreign exchange, foreign security, or immovable property situated outside India, except as otherwise provided.
Specifies penalties for contraventions of the Act, rules, or regulations made thereunder.
Establishes the Directorate of Enforcement.
Grants powers of search and seizure to authorized officers.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Reserve Bank to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall deal in or transfer any foreign exchange or foreign security to any person not being an authorised person (Section 3(a)).
No person shall make any payment to or for the credit of any person resident outside India in any manner (Section 3(b)).

No person resident in India shall acquire, hold, own, possess or transfer any foreign exchange, foreign security or any immovable property situated outside India, unless otherwise provided (Section 4).

Any person may sell or draw foreign exchange to or from an authorised person if such sale or drawal is a current account transaction, subject to reasonable restrictions that may be prescribed by the Central Government (Section 5).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act, rules, or regulations (Section 13).
Enforcement of orders of Adjudicating Authority (Section 14).
Power to recover arrears of penalty (Section 14A).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Directorate of Enforcement (Section 36), Adjudicating Authority (Section 16), Special Director (Appeals) (Section 17), Appellate Tribunal (Section 18).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through adjudication proceedings, appeals to the Special Director (Appeals) and Appellate Tribunal, and enforcement of orders by the Adjudicating Authority. Powers of search, seizure, etc., are also vested with authorized officers.

rights: Right of appellant to take assistance of legal practitioner or chartered accountant (Section 32).
duties: Duty to adhere to regulations regarding dealing in foreign exchange.
Duty to ensure that transactions are either current account transactions or capital account transactions as permitted.
Duty to realize and repatriate foreign exchange as per the Act and regulations.
obligations: Obligation to obtain prior permission from the Reserve Bank for certain transactions.
Obligation to comply with directions issued by the Reserve Bank to authorized persons.
Obligation to cooperate with investigations and enforcement actions.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission for current account and capital account transactions.
Procedure for dealing with contraventions, including adjudication and appeals.
Procedure for search, seizure, and confiscation of property.
administration: Central Government and the Reserve Bank of India.
important_notes: Different commencement dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The Reserve Bank may specify restrictions or conditions for capital account transactions.
Civil courts do not have jurisdiction over matters dealt with by the Adjudicating Authority or Appellate Tribunal (Section 34).

title: The National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a body at the National level for the Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to persons with autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation, multiple disabilities, and severe multiple disabilities. It also concerns registered organizations, parents of persons with disability, and professionals in the field.

key_definitions.autism: A condition of uneven skill development primarily affecting the communication and social abilities of a person, marked by repetitive and ritualistic behaviour.
key_definitions.cerebral_palsy: A group of non-progressive conditions of a person characterised by abnormal motor control and posture resulting from brain insult or injuries occurring in the pre-natal, perinatal or infant period of development.
key_definitions.mental_retardation: A condition of arrested or incomplete development of mind of a person which is specially characterised by sub-normality of intelligence.
key_definitions.multiple_disabilities: A combination of two or more disabilities as defined in clause (i) of section 2 of the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995.
key_definitions.severe_disability: Disability with eighty per cent. or more of one or more multiple disabilities.
key_definitions.persons_with_disability: A person suffering from any of the conditions relating to autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation or a combination of any two or more of such conditions and includes a person suffering from severe multiple disability.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including specific disabilities and related concepts.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disability, etc.
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Trust as a body corporate and outlines the composition of its Board of Trustees.

Enlists the primary objectives of the Trust, focusing on enabling and empowering persons with disability to live independently and integrally within the community, strengthening family support, and addressing specific challenges faced by these individuals.
Details the process by which organizations can be registered with the Trust.
Provides for the establishment of local level committees.
Outlines the procedure for appointing guardians for persons with disability.
Specifies the responsibilities and duties of a guardian appointed under the Act.
Details the provision of financial grants by the Central Government to the Trust.
Describes the establishment and management of the Trust's fund.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to issue directions to the Trust.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede Board
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to supersede the Board of the Trust under certain circumstances.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Board the power to make regulations for the conduct of its affairs.

important_rules: The Board shall consist of a Chairperson, nine persons appointed from registered organizations, eight ex-officio members representing relevant government ministries, three persons nominated by the Board representing trade, commerce, and industry, and the Chief Executive Officer as Member-Secretary.
The Chairperson and Members shall hold office for a term of three years, not exceeding the age of sixty-five years.
The Board shall meet at least once in three months.
The Trust shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract.

The objects of the Trust include enabling and empowering persons with disability to live independently, strengthening family support, extending support to registered organizations, and dealing with problems of persons with disability without family support.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board of the National Trust and potentially the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Board and the Central Government, including the ability to issue directions, supersede the Board, and through the mechanisms of accountability and monitoring outlined in Chapter VII.

rights: Persons with disability have the right to live as independently and as fully as possible within and as close to the community.
Persons with disability have the right to receive support to live within their own families.
Persons with disability have the right to have guardians and trustees appointed for their protection.
Persons with disability have the right to the realization of equal opportunities, protection of rights, and full participation.
duties: The Board has a duty to manage the affairs and business of the Trust.
Guardians have a duty to furnish inventory and annual accounts.
The Central Government has a duty to provide grants and issue directions when necessary.
obligations: The Board has an obligation to make arrangements for an adequate standard of living for beneficiaries.
The Board is obliged to evolve procedures for the appointment of guardians and trustees.

key_procedures: Procedure for constitution of the Board, including appointment of Chairperson and Members.
Procedure for registration of organizations under section 12.
Procedure for appointment of guardians for persons with disability.
Procedure for meetings of the Board, including quorum and voting.
Procedure for appointment of Chief Executive Officer and other staff of the Trust.
Procedure for the audit of accounts and submission of annual reports.
administration: The National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disability, with its Board of Trustees and Chief Executive Officer. The Central Government has overarching administrative and directive powers.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2019 to omit the exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The Act includes provisions for exemption from tax on income for the Trust.
Actions taken in good faith by individuals under the Act are protected.
Chairperson, Members, and officers of the Trust are deemed to be public servants.

title: THE INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY ACT, 2000
purpose: To provide legal recognition for transactions carried out by means of electronic data interchange and other means of electronic communication, commonly referred to as “electronic commerce”, which involve the use of alternatives to paper-based methods of communication and storage of information, to facilitate electronic filing of documents with the Government agencies and further to amend the Indian Penal Code, the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, the Banker’s Books Evidence Act, 1891 and the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to any offence or contravention committed outside India by any person. It does not apply to documents or transactions specified in the First Schedule, which can be amended by the Central Government through notification.

key_definitions.access: Gaining entry into, instructing or communicating with the logical, arithmetical, or memory function resources of a computer, computer system or computer network.
key_definitions.addressee: A person who is intended by the originator to receive the electronic record but does not include any intermediary.
key_definitions.adjudicating officer: An adjudicating officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 46.
key_definitions.affixing [electronic signature]: Adoption of any methodology or procedure by a person for the purpose of authenticating an electronic record by means of [electronic signature].
key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: The Appellate Tribunal referred to in sub-section (1) of section 48.
key_definitions.appropriate Government: As respects any matter, the State Government if enumerated in List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution or relating to any State law enacted under List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution; in any other case, the Central Government.
key_definitions.asymmetric crypto system: A system of a secure key pair consisting of a private key for creating a digital signature and a public key to verify the digital signature.
key_definitions.Certifying Authority: A person who has been granted a licence to issue an [electronic signature] Certificate under section 24.
key_definitions.certification practice statement: A statement issued by a Certifying Authority to specify the practices that the Certifying Authority employs in issuing [electronic signature] Certificates.
key_definitions.communication device: Cell phones, personal digital assistance or combination of both or any other device used to communicate, send or transmit any text, video, audio or image.
key_definitions.computer: Any electronic, magnetic, optical or other high-speed data processing device or system which performs logical, arithmetic, and memory functions by manipulations of electronic, magnetic or optical impulses, and includes all input, output, processing, storage, computer software or communication facilities which are connected or related to the computer in a computer system or computer network.
key_definitions.computer network: The interconnection of one or more computers or computer systems or communication device through the use of satellite, microwave, terrestrial line, wire, wireless or other communication media; and terminals or a complex consisting of two or more interconnected computers or communication device whether or not the interconnection is continuously maintained.
key_definitions.computer resource: Computer, computer system, computer network, data, computer database or software.
key_definitions.computer system: A device or collection of devices, including input and output support devices and excluding calculators which are not programmable and capable of being used in conjunction with external files, which contain computer programmes, electronic instructions, input data and output data, that performs logic, arithmetic, data storage and retrieval, communication control and other functions.
key_definitions.Controller: The Controller of Certifying Authorities appointed under sub-section (1) of section 17.
key_definitions.cyber cafe: Any facility from where access to the internet is offered by any person in the ordinary course of business to the members of the public.
key_definitions.cyber security: Protecting information, equipment, devices, computer, computer resource, communication device and information stored therein from unauthorised access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction.
key_definitions.data: A representation of information, knowledge, facts, concepts or instructions which are being prepared or have been prepared in a formalised manner, and is intended to be processed, is being processed or has been processed in a computer system or computer network, and may be in any form (including computer printouts magnetic or optical storage media, punched cards, punched tapes) or stored internally in the memory of the computer.
key_definitions.digital signature: Authentication of any electronic record by a subscriber by means of an electronic method or procedure in accordance with the provisions of section 3.
key_definitions.Digital Signature Certificate: A Digital Signature Certificate issued under sub-section (4) of section 35.
key_definitions.electronic form: With reference to information, any information generated, sent, received or stored in media, magnetic, optical, computer memory, micro film, computer generated micro fiche or similar device.
key_definitions.Electronic Gazette: The Official Gazette published in the electronic form.
key_definitions.electronic record: Data, record or data generated, image or sound stored, received or transmitted in electronic form.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Information Technology Act, 2000, its territorial extent (whole of India), commencement date, and applicability, including to offences committed outside India. It also mentions an exception for documents/transactions in the First Schedule.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, crucial for understanding its provisions. This includes definitions for 'access', 'addressee', 'adjudicating officer', 'electronic signature', 'Appellate Tribunal', 'appropriate Government', 'asymmetric crypto system', 'Certifying Authority', 'certification practice statement', 'communication device', 'computer', 'computer network', 'computer resource', 'computer system', 'Controller', 'cyber cafe', 'cyber security', 'data', 'digital signature', 'Digital Signature Certificate', 'electronic form', 'Electronic Gazette', and 'electronic record'.
Lays down the procedure for authenticating electronic records.
Defines and elaborates on the concept of an electronic signature.
Grants legal recognition to electronic records.
Grants legal recognition to electronic signatures.

main_sections.section_title: Use of electronic records and electronic signatures in Government and its agencies.
main_sections.description: Permits the use of electronic records and electronic signatures by and with Government agencies.

main_sections.section_title: Validity of contracts formed through electronic means.
main_sections.description: Establishes the validity of contracts formed through electronic means.
Deals with the attribution of electronic records to their originators.
Outlines the procedure for acknowledging the receipt of electronic records.

main_sections.section_title: Time and place of despatch and receipt of electronic record.
main_sections.description: Determines the time and place of despatch and receipt of electronic records.
Defines what constitutes a secure electronic record.
Defines what constitutes a secure electronic signature.
Specifies security procedures and practices to be followed.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Controller and other officers.
main_sections.description: Empowers the appointment of the Controller of Certifying Authorities and other officers.
Details the functions to be performed by the Controller.

main_sections.section_title: Licence to issue electronic signature Certificates.
main_sections.description: Provides for the issuance of licences to entities that wish to act as Certifying Authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties and compensation for unauthorised access, damage, or disruption to computer systems.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for failure to protect data.
main_sections.description: Provides for compensation for failure to protect sensitive personal data.
Grants the power to adjudicate contraventions of the Act.
Provides for the establishment of an Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals against orders made under the Act.
Lays down the procedure for filing appeals to the Appellate Tribunal.
Allows for appeals to the High Court from orders of the Appellate Tribunal.
Penalises the tampering with computer source documents.
Covers various offences related to computer systems and networks.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for dishonestly receiving stolen computer resource or communication device.
main_sections.description: Defines punishment for knowingly receiving stolen computer resources or communication devices.
Penalises identity theft committed using a computer resource.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource.
main_sections.description: Defines punishment for cheating by impersonation through a computer resource.
Penalises violations of privacy through electronic means.
Addresses and penalises acts of cyber terrorism.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form.
main_sections.description: Penalises the publication or transmission of obscene material in electronic form.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for publishing or transmitting of material containing sexually explicit act, etc., in electronic form.
main_sections.description: Provides punishment for publishing or transmitting material containing sexually explicit acts in electronic form.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for publishing or transmitting of material depicting children in sexually explicit act, etc., in electronic form.
main_sections.description: Penalises the publication or transmission of material depicting children in sexually explicit acts in electronic form.

main_sections.section_title: Preservation and retention of information by intermediaries.
main_sections.description: Mandates intermediaries to preserve and retain information.

main_sections.section_title: Power to issue directions for interception or monitoring or decryption of any information through any computer resource.
main_sections.description: Grants power to issue directions for interception, monitoring, or decryption of information through computer resources.

main_sections.section_title: Power to issue directions for blocking for public access of any information through any computer resource.
main_sections.description: Empowers the blocking of public access to information through computer resources.
Defines 'protected system' and its implications.

main_sections.section_title: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team to serve as national agency for incident response.
main_sections.description: Designates the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) as the national agency for incident response.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for Breach of confidentiality and privacy.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for breaching confidentiality and privacy.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption from liability of intermediary in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Provides for exemption from liability for intermediaries under certain conditions.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws where there is an inconsistency, except for specific provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Electronic records and electronic signatures have legal recognition.
Contracts can be validly formed through electronic means.
Specific procedures must be followed for authentication of electronic records using electronic signatures.
Intermediaries are granted exemption from liability under certain conditions.
Strict penalties and punishments are prescribed for various cybercrimes and contraventions.
The Central Government has the power to make rules and the Controller to make regulations to implement the Act.
The Act applies to offences or contraventions committed outside India.
The First Schedule specifies documents or transactions to which the Act does not apply, but this can be amended by the Central Government.

penalties: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc. (Section 43).
Compensation for failure to protect data (Section 43A).
Penalty for failure to furnish information, return, etc. (Section 44).
Residuary penalty for contraventions not specifically covered (Section 45).
Punishment for tampering with computer source documents (Section 65).
Punishment for various computer-related offences including identity theft, cheating by personation, violation of privacy, and cyber terrorism (Sections 66B, 66C, 66D, 66E, 66F).
Punishment for publishing or transmitting obscene or sexually explicit material in electronic form (Sections 67, 67A, 67B).
Penalty for breach of confidentiality and privacy (Section 72).
Penalty for misrepresentation (Section 71).
Penalties for publishing false electronic signature certificates or for fraudulent purposes (Sections 73, 74).
Confiscation of articles (Section 76).
