penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Controller of Certifying Authorities, adjudicating officers appointed under section 46, police officers, and other authorised officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation of contraventions, adjudication of penalties, prosecution for offences, and orders for compensation and confiscation. The Act also empowers police officers and other officers to enter, search, and seize.

rights: Right to legal recognition of electronic records and signatures.
Right to form valid contracts through electronic means.
Right to appeal against orders to the Appellate Tribunal and High Court.
Right to legal representation before the Appellate Tribunal.
Right to protection of action taken in good faith.
duties: Duty of subscribers to generate key pairs for digital signatures.
Duty of subscribers to take reasonable steps to protect their private keys.
Duty of Certifying Authorities to follow specified procedures and ensure compliance.
Duty of intermediaries to preserve and retain information as mandated.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding electronic transactions and security.
Obligation to protect data and prevent unauthorised access.
Obligation to adhere to security procedures and practices for electronic records and signatures.
Obligation to report and respond to cyber security incidents through the designated national agency.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a licence to issue electronic signature certificates.
Procedure for issuing, suspending, and revoking electronic signature certificates.
Procedure for attribution, acknowledgment, and determining the time/place of despatch and receipt of electronic records.
Procedure for adjudication of contraventions and imposition of penalties.
Procedure for appeal to the Appellate Tribunal and further appeal to the High Court.
Procedure for investigation of offences.
Procedure for issuing directions for interception, monitoring, decryption, and blocking of information.
Procedure for examining electronic evidence.
administration: The Controller of Certifying Authorities (appointed under section 17) plays a key administrative role, along with other officers. The Central Government is empowered to make rules, and the Controller to make regulations.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to documents or transactions specified in the First Schedule, but this can be amended by the Central Government.
Different dates may be appointed for the commencement of different provisions of the Act.
The Act has an overriding effect over other laws, except for specific exclusions.
The Central Government can notify the Examiner of Electronic Evidence.
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) is designated as the national agency for incident response.

title: THE COAL INDIA (REGULATION OF TRANSFERS AND VALIDATION) ACT, 2000
purpose: To empower the Central Government to direct the transfer of land, rights, title, or interest in relation to coal mines, coking coal mines, or coke oven plants from Coal India Limited or its subsidiary companies to other subsidiary companies of Coal India Limited, and to validate certain past transfers.
scope: This act applies to land, rights in or over land, and the right, title, and interest in relation to coal mines, coking coal mines, or coke oven plants that are vested in Coal India Limited or any of its subsidiary companies. It is enacted by the Parliament of India.

key_definitions.Coal India: Coal India Limited, a Government company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956, including its predecessor, the Coal Mines Authority Limited.
key_definitions.subsidiary company: Specifically listed subsidiary companies of Coal India (Central Coal Fields Limited, Bharat Coking Coal Limited, Western Coal Fields Limited, Eastern Coal Fields Limited, Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Limited, South-Eastern Coal Fields Limited, Northern Coal Fields Limited, Mahanadi Coal Fields Limited) and any other subsidiary company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956. It also includes their predecessor Government companies where applicable.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Coal India (Regulation of Transfers and Validation) Act, 2000.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Coal India' and 'subsidiary company'. It also states that undefined words and expressions used in the Act will have the meanings assigned to them in the Coking Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1972, or the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct transfer of land, rights, title or interest
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct the transfer of vested land, rights, or interest from Coal India to a subsidiary company, or from one subsidiary company to another, by notification in the Official Gazette, provided certain terms and conditions are met. It also details the legal implications of such transfers, including deeming the transferee subsidiary company to have been granted a fresh mining lease and inheriting all rights and liabilities.

Deems valid and effective any previous vesting of land, rights, or interest in a subsidiary company that was operating or controlling a coal mine, coking coal mine, or coke oven plant vested in Coal India or another subsidiary company before the Act's commencement, as if a direction had been made under section 3(1). This provision prevents legal proceedings challenging the subsidiary company's competence to operate or control such assets.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Central Government has the power to direct the transfer of land, rights, title, or interest related to coal mines, coking coal mines, or coke oven plants from Coal India to a subsidiary company, or between subsidiary companies, by issuing a notification in the Official Gazette.

Rule 2: Transfers directed by the Central Government under section 3 will be deemed effective from the date of vesting, with the transferee subsidiary company assuming the status of a lessee with a fresh mining lease.

Rule 3: Certain past transfers of land, rights, or interest to subsidiary companies are deemed valid and effective, preventing any legal challenges based on the subsidiary company's competence to operate or control the assets.

Rule 4: Any words and expressions used in this Act but not defined shall have the meanings assigned to them in the Coking Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1972 or the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directions issued by notification in the Official Gazette, and by deeming certain transfers valid to prevent legal challenges.

rights: Right of the Central Government to direct transfers of coal mine assets.
Right of subsidiary companies to be vested with assets as per Central Government directions.
Right of subsidiary companies to be deemed as having valid mining leases upon vesting.
Right of subsidiary companies to be protected from legal challenges regarding past operational competence due to validated transfers.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to ensure compliance with terms and conditions before directing transfers.
Duty of the transferee subsidiary company to accept the vested assets and associated rights and liabilities.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Coking Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1972, and the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973, for undefined terms.
obligations: Obligations of Coal India or a subsidiary company to transfer assets as directed by the Central Government.
Obligations of the transferee subsidiary company to fulfill the terms and conditions imposed by the Central Government.
Obligations to adhere to the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, and the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, as they relate to mining leases.
Obligations to cease any legal proceedings related to the validity of past transfers.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Central Government, if satisfied, may direct the transfer of land, rights, title, or interest vested in Coal India or a subsidiary company to another subsidiary company by issuing a notification in the Official Gazette.
Procedure 2: Upon such a direction, the transferee subsidiary company is deemed to have become the lessee as if a fresh mining lease had been granted under the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960.

Procedure 3: Any subsidiary company operating or controlling a coal mine, coking coal mine, or coke oven plant prior to the Act's commencement, and which was vested in Coal India or another subsidiary, is deemed to have been validly vested with the relevant assets.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act overrides any other law for the time being in force regarding the transfer of assets.

The validation of certain transfers under Section 4 prevents any suits or proceedings from being instituted, maintained, or continued in any court on the ground that the subsidiary company was not competent to operate or control the coal mine, coking coal mine, or coke oven plant.

title: THE CENTRAL ROAD AND INFRASTRUCTURE FUND ACT, 2000
purpose: To give statutory status to the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund for the development and maintenance of National Highways, railway projects, improvement of safety in railways, State and rural roads, and other infrastructure, by levying and collecting a cess (duty of excise and duty of customs) on motor spirit (petrol) and high speed diesel oil.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It covers the development and maintenance of national highways, rural roads, state roads, railway projects, and other infrastructure projects. The cess is levied on motor spirit (petrol) and high speed diesel oil produced in or imported into India.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which the Fund is established under sub-section (1) of section 6.
key_definitions.cess: A duty in the nature of duty of excise and customs, imposed and collected on motor spirit commonly known as petrol and high speed diesel oil for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.Fund: The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund established under sub-section (1) of section 6.
key_definitions.national highways: Highways specified in the Schedule to the National Highways Act, 1956, or any other highway declared as national highway under sub-section (2) of section 2 of the said Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement (deemed to have come into force on November 1, 2000, unless otherwise provided).
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'cess', 'Fund', 'national highways', and 'prescribed'.

Details the levy and collection of cess as a duty of excise and customs on specified items (petrol and high speed diesel oil) for the purposes of the Act. It outlines how the cess is collected and mentions its application in addition to other existing duties.

main_sections.section_title: Crediting of cess to Consolidated Fund of India
main_sections.description: States that the proceeds of the cess are first credited to the Consolidated Fund of India. The Central Government can then credit these proceeds to the Fund after parliamentary appropriation, for exclusive utilization for the Act's purposes, after deducting collection expenses.

main_sections.section_title: Grants and loans by the Central Government
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to credit sums of money to the Fund by way of grants or loans, after due appropriation by Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Central Road and Infrastructure Fund
main_sections.description: Establishes the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund and specifies the amounts to be credited to it, including sums from sections 4 and 5, unspent cess for national highways, sums realized from the Central Government's functions, and funds for State road development and maintenance.

Outlines the purposes for which the Fund can be utilized, including development and maintenance of national highways, rural roads, state roads, railway projects (construction of over/under bridges, safety works, new lines, gauge conversion, electrification), and other infrastructure projects.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of share of fund by Committee
main_sections.description: Establishes a committee, headed by the Finance Minister, to finalize the apportionment of the Fund's share for each infrastructure project based on project priorities.

Requires concerned departments of the Central Government to maintain proper accounts and prepare annual statements of accounts for their allocated shares of the fund. The accounts are to be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Central Government to administer the Fund
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to administer the Fund, including making decisions on investment in projects and taking measures to raise funds.

Defines the responsibilities of the Central Government, including administration and management of the Fund's share for roads and infrastructure, coordination of fund utilization, formulation of criteria for fund allocation for State roads, national highways, and other infrastructure projects.

main_sections.section_title: Administration of States’ share of the Fund
main_sections.description: Details the allocation and administration of the Fund's share for State roads, including provisions for resuming funds if a State fails to take recommended steps or delays application of allocated funds.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules made under this Act to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires that rules made under the Act be laid before Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulment.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions relating to existing Central Road and Infrastructure Fund
main_sections.description: Deals with provisions related to any existing Central Road and Infrastructure Fund prior to this Act.
Provides for the repeal of any prior legislation and includes saving clauses.

important_rules: Rule 1: With effect from a specified date, a cess (duty of excise and customs) shall be levied and collected on items specified in Schedule I for the purposes of this Act (Section 3(1)).
Rule 2: The cess levied shall be payable by the person producing the item, and in case of imports, it shall be imposed and collected on imported items specified in the Schedule (Section 3(2)).
Rule 3: The cess leviable shall be in addition to any other cess or duty leviable on those items under any other law (Section 3(3)).

Rule 4: The proceeds of the cess shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India and subsequently transferred to the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund upon parliamentary appropriation (Section 4).
Rule 5: The Fund shall be utilized for the development and maintenance of national highways, rural roads, state roads, railway projects, and other infrastructure projects (Section 7(1)).
Rule 6: The Central Government is responsible for the administration and management of the Fund, including coordination of utilization and formulation of allocation criteria (Section 10(1)).

Rule 7: If a State Government fails to take recommended steps or delays the application of allocated funds, the Central Government may resume the whole or part of any sums held for expenditure in that State (Section 11(3)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act's provisions, including levy and collection of cess, are enforced through the application of the Central Excise Act, 1944, and the Customs Act, 1962, and their respective rules. The Central Government also has the power to resume funds from States that fail to comply with its recommendations or directives.

rights: Right of citizens to have roads and infrastructure developed and maintained through the Fund.
Right to benefit from improved railway safety and infrastructure.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to administer the Fund, levy and collect cess, and ensure its proper utilization.
Duty of persons producing or importing specified items (petrol and diesel) to pay the levied cess.
Duty of State Governments and Union Territories to cooperate with the Central Government in matters related to motor vehicle regulation and timely utilization of allocated funds.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to establish and manage the Fund according to the Act's provisions.
Obligation of the Central Government to ensure that rules made under the Act are laid before Parliament.
Obligation of concerned departments to maintain proper accounts and subject them to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_procedures: Procedure for levying and collecting cess on motor spirit and high speed diesel oil, including its application in addition to other duties.
Procedure for crediting cess proceeds to the Consolidated Fund of India and then to the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund after parliamentary appropriation.
Procedure for the Central Government to establish the Fund and credit various sources of income to it.
Procedure for utilizing the Fund for specified development and maintenance purposes, including the role of a committee in apportioning shares for infrastructure projects.
Procedure for auditing the accounts of the Fund by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
Procedure for the Central Government to administer the Fund, including investment decisions and fundraising measures.
Procedure for the Central Government to formulate criteria for fund allocation for different types of road and infrastructure projects.
Procedure for the administration of States' share of the Fund, including the process of resuming funds in case of non-compliance.
administration: Central Government (specifically, departments involved in roads, railways, and infrastructure development, as well as the Ministry of Finance for the committee headed by the Finance Minister).
important_notes: The Act has been amended significantly, notably by Act 13 of 2018, which likely altered the long title, headings, and specific clauses related to the Fund's scope and administration.
The definition of 'infrastructure projects' is elaborated in Schedule II, which can be amended by the Central Government via notification.
Any notification issued by the Central Government under this Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and is subject to modification or annulment.
A portion of duties on petrol and high speed diesel oil was specifically allocated for national highways from March 1, 2005.

title: THE INDIAN COUNCIL OF WORLD AFFAIRS ACT, 2001
purpose: To declare the Indian Council of World Affairs to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the Indian Council of World Affairs, an institution declared to be of national importance, and its operations within India. It governs the incorporation, composition, powers, and functions of the Council and its governing body.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Governing Body.
key_definitions.Council: The Indian Council of World Affairs incorporated under section 4.
key_definitions.existing Council: The Indian Council of World Affairs, a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860) and functioning as such immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Council referred to in section 18.
key_definitions.Governing Body: The Governing Body of the Council.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Council and includes the President and Vice-President.
key_definitions.regulations: The regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.rules: The rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Indian Council of World Affairs Act, 2001, and specifies that it commenced on September 1, 2000, unless otherwise provided.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of the Indian Council of World Affairs as institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Indian Council of World Affairs, a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, as an institution of national importance due to its objectives.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act.

Constitutes the Indian Council of World Affairs as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, granting it powers to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract. Its head office is in Delhi, with branches allowed elsewhere in India upon Central Government approval.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the existing Council to the Council
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of all assets, liabilities, contracts, debts, and ongoing legal proceedings from the existing Council to the newly incorporated Council from the appointed day. It also ensures employees retain their rights and privileges.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation to transfer property or assets
main_sections.description: Mandates that any person in possession or control of property belonging to the existing Council must deliver it to the Director-General. Additionally, individuals in charge of the existing Council's property must provide a complete inventory of all assets and agreements within ten days of the Act's commencement.

Outlines the composition of the Council, initially comprising high-ranking government officials and later expanding to include nominated Vice-Presidents, the Director-General, Members of Parliament, distinguished individuals in diplomacy and international affairs, representatives from universities and research institutions, media personalities, and representatives from business chambers.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and vacancies among members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for members (three years), the continuation of service until a replacement is nominated, grounds for removal from office (disqualification, incapacity, absence, abuse of position), eligibility for re-nomination, resignation procedures, and the manner of filling vacancies.
States that the President shall exercise powers and discharge functions as laid down in the Act or prescribed by rules.
Defines the powers and functions of Vice-Presidents as those prescribed by rules or delegated by the President.
Members are entitled to such allowances, if any, as prescribed by rules.
Details the procedures for the Council's meetings, including the first meeting appointed by the Central Government and subsequent meetings governed by regulations.

Enumerate the primary objectives of the Council, including promoting the study of Indian and international affairs, fostering India's international relations, serving as an information clearing house, publishing literature, establishing contacts with similar organizations, arranging conferences, and undertaking other related activities.

main_sections.section_title: Governing Body and other committees of Council
main_sections.description: Establishes a Governing Body as the executive committee of the Council, responsible for exercising powers and functions conferred upon it by the Council through regulations.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the Council the power to make regulations for the transaction of its business.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires rules and regulations made under the Act to be laid before Parliament.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any previous enactment and includes a saving clause to ensure continuity.

important_rules: Members shall serve for a term of three years and can be re-nominated.
Members can be removed for disqualification, incapacity, absence, or abuse of position.
The President and Vice-Presidents have specific powers and functions as defined by the Act and rules.
The Council shall promote the study of Indian and international affairs, foster international relations, and act as an information clearing house.
The Governing Body is the executive committee of the Council.
Rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and Council (through its Governing Body and Director-General)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers to make rules and regulations, appointment of members, removal of members, and oversight of Council's activities. Enforcement of property transfer is mandated by Section 6.

rights: Employees of the existing Council retain their rights and privileges regarding pension, gratuity, and other service matters upon absorption into the new Council.
Members have the right to receive allowances as prescribed by rules.
Members shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before removal from office under specific circumstances.
duties: Every person in possession of property of the existing Council must deliver it to the Director-General.
Those in charge of the existing Council's property must furnish a complete inventory within ten days of the Act's commencement.
obligations: The Council has an obligation to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract.
The Council has an obligation to promote the study of Indian and international affairs and India's relations with other countries.
The Council has an obligation to serve as a clearing house of information and knowledge regarding world affairs.
The Council has an obligation to publish literature on relevant subjects.
The Council has an obligation to establish contacts with organizations promoting similar objects.

key_procedures: Transfer of assets and liabilities from the existing Council to the newly incorporated Council upon the appointed day.
Nomination and appointment procedures for members of the Council, including initial nominations and subsequent nominations by the Council.
Procedures for the conduct of meetings of the Council, with the first meeting being appointed by the Central Government and subsequent meetings governed by regulations.
Procedures for removal of members from the Council under specified disqualifications or circumstances.
administration: The Central Government and the Council (including its Governing Body and Director-General) are responsible for the administration of the Act.
important_notes: The Act commenced on September 1, 2000, except as otherwise provided.
The composition of the Council changed significantly on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Absorption of employees by the Council does not entitle them to compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or similar laws.
The office of a member of the Council does not disqualify them from being a Member of Parliament.

title: THE ADVOCATES’ WELFARE FUND ACT, 2001
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a welfare fund for the benefit of advocates and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to advocates whose names are entered in the State roll maintained by a State Bar Council and who are members of a State Bar Association or State Advocates’ Association. The appropriate Government (State or Central, depending on the advocate's roll) administers specific provisions.

key_definitions.advocate: An advocate whose name is entered in the State roll maintained by a State Bar Council under section 17 of the Advocates Act, 1961, and who is a member of a State Bar Association or State Advocates’ Association.
key_definitions.appropriate government: In the case of advocates admitted on the roll of a Bar Council of a State, the State Government; in the case of advocates admitted on the roll of a Bar Council of a Union territory, the Central Government.
key_definitions.cessation of practice: Removal of the name of an advocate from the State roll under section 26A of the Advocates Act, 1961.
key_definitions.fund: The Advocates’ Welfare Fund constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.trustee committee: The Advocates’ Welfare Fund Trustee Committee established under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.vakalatnama: Includes memorandum of appearance or any other document by which an advocate is empowered to appear or plead before any court, tribunal or other authority.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Advocates’ Welfare Fund Act, 2001', its extent to the whole of India, and its commencement date, which can be appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'advocate', 'appropriate Government', 'cessation of practice', 'Fund', 'Trustee Committee', and 'Vakalatnama'.

Provides for the constitution of the Advocates’ Welfare Fund and specifies the sources of its credit, including amounts paid by State Bar Councils, voluntary contributions, government grants, sums borrowed, sums collected from membership, insurance proceeds, and sums collected from stamp sales.

Establishes the Advocates’ Welfare Fund Trustee Committee as a body corporate. It outlines the composition of the committee, including ex-officio members like the Advocate-General (or a nominated senior advocate), Secretaries from Law and Home Departments, Chairman of the State Bar Council, Government Pleader/Public Prosecutor, nominated advocates, and the Secretary of the State Bar Council.
States that the Fund shall vest in, be held, and applied by the Trustee Committee for the purposes of the Act.
Outlines the functions of the Trustee Committee, subject to the Act and other laws.
Mandates that Vakalatnamas must bear Advocates’ Welfare Fund Stamps.

important_rules: Rule 1: All advocates whose names are entered in the State roll and who are members of a State Bar Association or State Advocates’ Association are covered by the Act.
Rule 2: The Advocates’ Welfare Fund is constituted for the benefit of advocates.
Rule 3: The Advocates’ Welfare Fund Trustee Committee is established to manage and apply the Fund.
Rule 4: Vakalatnamas must bear Advocates’ Welfare Fund Stamps.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Appropriate Government, State Bar Council, Trustee Committee
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for disqualification and removal of Trustee Committee members, powers to summon witnesses, bar of jurisdiction of civil courts, and power of the appropriate government to issue directions or supersede the Trustee Committee.

rights: Advocates have rights to benefits from the Advocates’ Welfare Fund.
Members of the Fund have rights to ex gratia grants and other benefits like Group Life Insurance.
Members have a right to appeal against decisions or orders of the Trustee Committee.
duties: State Bar Councils have duties related to printing and distribution of stamps and payment of monies to the Fund.
State Bar Associations and State Advocates’ Associations have duties outlined in Chapter IV.
Advocates are expected to be members of the Fund and adhere to provisions related to stamp usage.
obligations: Advocates have an obligation to ensure Vakalatnamas bear the prescribed stamps.
Members have obligations related to payments into the Fund as prescribed.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Establishment and functioning of the Advocates’ Welfare Fund Trustee Committee, including meetings, quorum, and voting.
Procedure 2: Process for disqualification and removal of Chairperson or Member of the Trustee Committee, including a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
Procedure 3: Resignation process for nominated Chairperson and Members and filling up of casual vacancies.
Procedure 4: Process for printing, distribution, and cancellation of Advocates’ Welfare Fund Stamps.
Procedure 5: Appeal process against decisions or orders of the Trustee Committee.
administration: The Trustee Committee, under the oversight of the Appropriate Government.
important_notes: The Act provides for exemption from income-tax for the Fund.
There are restrictions on the alienation or attachment of a member's interest in the Fund.
Certain persons may not be eligible for benefits as specified in the Act.
Protection of action taken in good faith is provided.
The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in certain matters.

title: THE ENERGY CONSERVATION ACT, 2001
purpose: To provide for efficient use of energy and its conservation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to energy conservation and its efficient use, including various sectors and entities involved in energy consumption and management.

key_definitions.accredited_energy_auditor: An energy auditor accredited in accordance with the provisions of clause (p) of sub-section (2) of section 13.
key_definitions.appellate_tribunal: The Appellate Tribunal for Energy Conservation referred to in section 30.
key_definitions.building: Any structure or erection or part of structure or erection constructed after energy conservation rules have been notified, with a minimum connected load of 100 Kilowatt (kW) or contract demand of 120 Kilovolt Ampere (kVA), and used for commercial, office, or residential purposes. The State Government may specify a lower connected load or contract demand.
key_definitions.bureau: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.carbon_credit_certificate: The certificate issued by the Central Government or any agency authorised by it under section 14AA.
key_definitions.carbon_credit_trading_scheme: The scheme for reduction of carbon emissions notified by the Central Government under clause (w) of section 14.
key_definitions.designated_agency: Any agency designated under clause (d) of section 15.
key_definitions.designated_consumer: Any consumer specified under clause (e) of section 14.
key_definitions.energy: Any form of energy derived from fossil fuels or non-fossil sources or renewable sources.
key_definitions.energy_audit: The verification, monitoring and analysis of use of energy including submission of technical report containing recommendations for improving energy efficiency with cost benefit analysis and an action plan to reduce energy consumption.
key_definitions.energy_auditor: Any individual possessing the qualifications prescribed under clause (m) of section 14.
key_definitions.energy_conservation_and_sustainable_buil: The code which provides norms and standards for energy efficiency and its conservation, use of renewable energy and other green building requirements for a building.
key_definitions.energy_consumption_standards: The norms for process and energy consumption standards specified under clause (a) of section 14.
key_definitions.energy_management_centre: The Energy Management Centre set up under the Resolution of the Government of India in the erstwhile Ministry of Energy, Department of Power No. 7(2)/87- EP(Vol. IV), dated the 5th July, 1989 and registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860).
key_definitions.energy_manager: Any individual possessing the qualifications prescribed under clause (m) of section 14.
key_definitions.energy_savings_certificate: Any energy savings certificate issued to the designated consumers under sub-section (1) of section 14A.
key_definitions.equipment_or_appliance: Any equipment or appliance which consumes, generates, transmits or supplies energy and includes any device that consumes any form of energy and produces a desired work.
key_definitions.governing_council: The Governing Council referred to in section 4.
key_definitions.member: The member of the Governing Council and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.notification: A notification in the Gazette of India or, as the case may be, the Official Gazette of a State.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered_entity: Any entity, including designated consumers, registered for carbon credit trading scheme specified under clause (w) of section 14.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Bureau under this Act.
key_definitions.state_commission: The State Electricity Regulatory Commission established under sub-section (1) of section 17 of the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998 (14 of 1998).
key_definitions.vehicle: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (28) of section 2 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (59 of 1988).
key_definitions.vessel: Includes every description of water craft used or capable of being used in inland waters or in coastal waters, including any ship, boat, sailing vessel, tug, barge or other description of vessel including non-displacement craft, amphibious craft, wing-in-ground craft, ferry, roll-on-roll-off vessel, container vessel, tanker vessel, gas carrier or floating unit or dumb vessel used for transportation, storage or accommodation within or through inland waters and coastal waters.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'accredited energy auditor', 'Appellate Tribunal', 'building', 'Bureau', 'carbon credit certificate', 'carbon credit trading scheme', 'designated agency', 'designated consumer', 'energy', 'energy audit', 'energy auditor', 'energy conservation and sustainable building code', 'energy consumption standards', 'Energy Management Centre', 'energy manager', 'energy savings certificate', 'equipment or appliance', 'Governing Council', 'member', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'registered entity', 'regulations', 'Schedule', 'State Commission', 'vehicle', and 'vessel'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Bureau of Energy Efficiency
main_sections.description: Establishes the Bureau of Energy Efficiency as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with powers to acquire, hold, dispose of property and contract. Its head office is in Delhi, and it can establish offices elsewhere in India.

States that the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Bureau's affairs vest in the Governing Council, which consists of members appointed by the Central Government. It also lists the ex officio members of the Governing Council.
Details the powers and functions of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency. This section also includes a provision for prohibiting the use of deceptive names.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to enforce efficient use of energy and its conservation
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to enforce efficient use of energy and its conservation. This includes powers related to issuing energy savings certificates, carbon credit certificates, specifying the value of energy, and notifying carbon credit trading schemes.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to enforce certain provisions for efficient use of energy and its conservation
main_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to enforce provisions for efficient use of energy and its conservation.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the establishment of an Appellate Tribunal for Energy Conservation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions to Bureau
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Authorizes the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Bureau to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Bureau of Energy Efficiency to make regulations for the efficient discharge of its functions.

important_rules: Efficient use of energy and its conservation is to be facilitated and enforced by the Central Government (Section 14) and State Governments (Section 15).
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency is established to promote energy efficiency and conservation (Section 3).
The Governing Council manages the affairs of the Bureau (Section 4).
Penalties are prescribed for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 26).
An Appellate Tribunal for Energy Conservation is established to hear appeals (Section 30).
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Bureau (Section 46) and to supersede the Bureau under certain circumstances (Section 47).
The Central Government and State Governments are empowered to make rules, and the Bureau is empowered to make regulations (Sections 56, 57, 58).

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act, as specified in Section 26.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Designated Agencies, State Commissions, and Adjudicating Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers granted to various authorities for inspection (Section 17), issuing directions (Sections 18, 46, 55), adjudication of penalties (Section 27), and making rules and regulations.

rights: Right of appellant to take assistance of legal practitioner or accredited auditor (Section 44).
Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal (Section 31) and Supreme Court (Section 45).
duties: Duty to use energy efficiently and conserve it.
Duty to comply with energy consumption standards and building codes.
Designated consumers have duties related to energy savings certificates and carbon trading schemes.
The Bureau has duties related to promoting energy efficiency and conservation.
obligations: Obligations to comply with directions issued by the Central and State Governments.
Obligations to furnish information when required by the Central Government (Section 52).
Companies are subject to provisions regarding default (Section 48).

key_procedures: Establishment of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and its management by the Governing Council.
Transfer of assets, liabilities, and employees of the Energy Management Centre to the Bureau.
Issuance of energy savings certificates and carbon credit certificates by the Central Government.
Establishment of a Fund by the Central Government and State Governments.
Power of inspection by designated authorities.
Adjudication of penalties by designated officers.
Appeals process to the Appellate Tribunal and Supreme Court.
administration: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Central Government, State Governments, Ministry or Department of the Central Government dealing with Power, and other related Ministries/Departments.
important_notes: The Act was initially not extended to the State of Jammu and Kashmir but has since been omitted.
Different dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.

Words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948, or the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998, have the meanings assigned to them in those Acts.

title: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an effective system for the protection of plant varieties, the rights of farmers and plant breeders, and to encourage the development of new varieties of plants. It aims to recognize and protect farmers' contributions to conserving and improving plant genetic resources and to stimulate investment in research and development by protecting plant breeders' rights.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to the protection of plant varieties and the rights of farmers and plant breeders.

key_definitions.authority: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority established under the Act.
key_definitions.breeder: A person, group of persons, farmer, group of farmers, or any institution that has bred, evolved, or developed any variety.
key_definitions.farmer: Any person who cultivates land himself, directly supervises cultivation through another person, or conserves, preserves, or adds value to wild species or traditional varieties through selection and identification of their useful properties.
key_definitions.farmers_variety: A variety traditionally cultivated and evolved by farmers or a wild relative/land race of a variety about which farmers possess common knowledge.
key_definitions.essentially_derived_variety: A variety predominantly derived from an initial variety, retaining its essential characteristics but being clearly distinguishable and conforming to the initial variety except for the act of derivation.
key_definitions.variety: A plant grouping (excluding microorganisms) within a single botanical taxon of the lowest known rank, defined by its characteristics, distinguishable from other groupings, and suitable for propagation while remaining unchanged.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001, states its extension to the whole of India, and outlines its commencement through notification by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Authority, breeder, farmer, farmers' variety, essentially derived variety, variety, and others.

Establishes the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession and power to acquire property, contract, sue, and be sued. It also details the appointment of the Chairperson and members.
Establishes and details the National Register of Plant Varieties.
Outlines the process and conditions for applying for the registration of plant varieties.
Specifies the procedure for registering essentially derived varieties.
Details the issuance of certificates for registered plant varieties.
Registration to confer right. Registration of a variety confers certain rights on the breeder.
Defines the rights granted to researchers concerning plant varieties.
Enshrines and details the specific rights of farmers under the Act.
Establishes the National Gene Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Authority to make order for compulsory licence in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to issue compulsory licenses under specific conditions.
Provides for the mechanism of appeals to the High Court against decisions made under the Act.
Details the grants to be provided by the Central Government for the purposes of the Act.
Establishes and manages the fund of the Authority.
Defines what constitutes infringement of rights related to plant varieties.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for applying false denomination, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for applying false denominations to plant varieties.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of inconsistency.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule regarding application for registration of plant varieties, including details on registrable varieties, eligible applicants, and compulsory variety denomination.
Rules pertaining to the duration and effect of registration, including the issue of certificates, publication of varieties, and benefit sharing.
Rules concerning farmers' rights, including their rights in relation to their own or community varieties, and provisions for the Gene Fund.
Rules detailing the conditions under which compulsory licenses can be granted for plant varieties.
Rules governing infringement, including definitions, suits for infringement, relief, and the use of scientific advisers.
Rules specifying offenses related to false denominations and misrepresentation of registered varieties, along with their associated penalties.

penalties: Penalty for applying a false denomination to a registered variety or its propagating material.
Penalty for selling varieties to which a false denomination is applied.
Penalty for falsely representing a variety as registered.
Penalty for subsequent offenses, which may be more severe.
Penalties for offenses committed by companies.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority, and potentially other authorities as prescribed.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, including suits for infringement, and criminal procedures for offenses. The Authority can also issue orders for compulsory licenses and make decisions on benefit sharing. Appeals can be made to the High Court.

rights: Rights of plant breeders to protect their new varieties.
Rights of farmers to conserve, use, sow, re-sow, exchange, share, and sell their farm-saved seeds, including varieties traditionally cultivated.
Rights of farming communities to benefit sharing from the use of their genetic resources.
Researcher's rights to use registered varieties for research and breeding purposes.
Right to appeal decisions made by the Authority or Registrar to the High Court.
duties: Duty of breeders to provide information regarding the origin of plant varieties.
Duty to deposit seeds or propagating material of registered varieties with the Authority.
Duty to adhere to variety denominations and avoid false representations.
Duty to comply with benefit-sharing arrangements.
obligations: Obligation to register new plant varieties to gain protection.
Obligation to pay annual fees for maintaining registration.
Obligation to adhere to the terms and conditions of compulsory licenses.
Obligation to contribute to the Gene Fund when required.

key_procedures: Procedure for application and registration of plant varieties, including examination and advertisement of applications.
Procedure for registration of essentially derived varieties.
Procedure for determining and sharing benefits accruing to breeders and farmers.
Procedure for surrendering, revoking, rectifying, or correcting certificates of registration.
Procedure for filing appeals against decisions of the Authority to the High Court.
Procedure for prosecuting offenses and imposing penalties.
administration: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority, established by the Central Government. The Central Government also has powers to make rules and give directions.
important_notes: The Act provides for exceptions to infringement, such as for research purposes and for farmers in specific circumstances.
The Act aims to balance the rights of plant breeders with the rights and contributions of farmers and farming communities.
The Act has an overriding effect over other laws in matters of protection of plant varieties and farmers' rights.
The Central Government can issue directions to the Authority and has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

title: THE DELIMITATION ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide for the readjustment of the allocation of seats in the House of the People to the States, the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State, the division of each State and each Union territory having a Legislative Assembly into territorial constituencies for elections to the House of the People and Legislative Assemblies of the States and Union territories and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to all States and Union territories in India that have a Legislative Assembly. It covers the allocation of seats in the House of the People and Legislative Assemblies, and the delimitation of territorial constituencies for elections.

key_definitions.Commission: The Delimitation Commission constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Election Commission: The Election Commission referred to in article 324 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Commission, including the Chairperson.
key_definitions.State: Includes a Union territory having a Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Delimitation Act, 2002.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'article', 'associate member', 'Commission', 'Election Commission', 'member', and 'State'.

Details the constitution of the Delimitation Commission, which comprises three members: a Chairperson (a former Supreme Court Judge), the Chief Election Commissioner or a nominated Election Commissioner (ex officio), and the State Election Commissioner of the concerned State (ex officio).

Outlines the duties of the Commission, including deeming the readjustment of seats made by a previous commission (based on the 1971 census) as valid for this Act. It also mandates the readjustment of the division of each State into territorial constituencies for elections to the House of the People and State Legislative Assembly, based on the 2001 census figures.

Specifies that the Commission shall associate ten persons (five MPs and five MLAs) from each State to assist it. These associate members are nominated by the Speaker of the House of the People and the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, respectively. Associate members do not have voting rights. The Commission can also call upon experts for assistance.
Provides for filling casual vacancies in the office of the Chairperson, a member, or an associate member due to death or resignation.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of the Commission.
main_sections.description: Grants the Commission the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning witnesses, requiring document production, and requisitioning public records. It also allows the Commission to require information from individuals. Decisions are made by majority opinion. The Commission can act despite temporary absences or vacancies.

Empowers the Commission to determine, by order, the number of seats in the House of the People allocated to each State and the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State. This determination is based on 1971 census figures for general allocation and 2001 census figures for reserved seats (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes).

Details the process for distributing seats into single-member territorial constituencies based on the 2001 census. It emphasizes criteria such as geographical compactness, administrative unit boundaries, communication facilities, and public convenience. It also mandates that assembly constituencies fall within parliamentary constituencies and that reserved constituencies for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are located in areas with higher proportions of their population.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of orders and their date of operation.
main_sections.description: Requires the Commission to publish its orders in the Gazette of India and Official Gazettes of concerned States, as well as in vernacular newspapers and through media. Orders, upon publication in the Gazette of India, have the force of law and cannot be questioned in court. Orders are also laid before the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies.

main_sections.section_title: Deferment of delimitation in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Introduces provisions for deferring delimitation in specific circumstances (details not provided in the excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Delimitation Commission's order with respect to the State of Jharkhand not to have any legal effect.
main_sections.description: States that the Delimitation Commission's order concerning the State of Jharkhand shall not have any legal effect (details not provided in the excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Power to maintain delimitation orders up-to-date.
main_sections.description: Grants the Commission the power to update delimitation orders as needed.
Repeals previous legislation (details not provided in the excerpt).

important_rules: Rule 1: The Commission shall readjust the division of each State into territorial constituencies for elections to the House of the People and State Legislative Assembly based on the census figures from the year 2001.
Rule 2: All constituencies shall be geographically compact areas, considering physical features, existing administrative boundaries, communication facilities, and public convenience.
Rule 3: Every assembly constituency must fall entirely within one parliamentary constituency.

Rule 4: Constituencies with reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes should be distributed across the state and located in areas where their population proportion is comparatively large or largest, respectively.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Delimitation Commission, with the Central Government and Speaker's roles in appointment and nomination.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Commission exercises powers similar to a civil court. Its orders, once published in the Gazette of India, have the force of law and are not subject to judicial review. Associate members and other called-upon individuals are duty-bound to assist the Commission.

rights: Right to have representation in the House of the People and State Legislative Assembly based on delimited constituencies.
Right to submit objections and suggestions regarding delimitation proposals.
duties: Duty of the Commission to undertake readjustment of seats and delimitation of constituencies.
Duty of associate members and other experts to assist the Commission.
Duty of District Election Officers to display published delimitation orders.
Duty of Central Government to constitute the Delimitation Commission.
Duty of Speakers to nominate associate members.
obligations: Obligation to follow the procedure laid down for delimitation.
Obligation to adhere to the criteria for delimiting constituencies.
Obligation for the Commission's orders to be published and laid before Parliament and State Assemblies.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Delimitation Commission by the Central Government.
Nomination of associate members by the Speaker of the House of the People and Speakers of State Legislative Assemblies.
Readjustment of the number of seats in the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies based on census data.
Delimitation of constituencies, ensuring geographical compactness and consideration of administrative boundaries.
Publication of delimitation proposals, consideration of objections and suggestions, and holding public sittings.
Publication of final delimitation orders in the Gazette of India and Official Gazettes, making them legally binding.
Laying of orders before the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies.
administration: The Delimitation Commission, assisted by the Election Commission's Secretary and staff. The Central Government is responsible for constituting the Commission.
important_notes: The 2001 census figures are used for delimitation, but a footnote indicates that for delimitation of Assembly and Parliamentary Constituencies, the words and figures 'census held in the year 2001' shall be construed as 'census held in the year 2011' as per Act No. 34 of 2019.
The words 'but does not include the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted from the definition of 'State' by Act 34 of 2019, effective from 31-10-2019.
The order of the Delimitation Commission with respect to the State of Jharkhand has no legal effect.
Associate members, while assisting the Commission, do not have voting rights.

title: The Haj Committee Act, 2002
purpose: To establish a Haj Committee of India and State Haj Committees for making arrangements for the pilgrimage of Muslims for Haj, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Haj Committee of India and State Haj Committees to make arrangements for the pilgrimage of Muslims for Haj. It covers pilgrims, committees, finance, and miscellaneous provisions related to Haj arrangements.

key_definitions.bye-laws: Bye-laws made under section 45 of the Act.
key_definitions.chief_executive_officer_or_executive_off: The Chief Executive Officer of the Committee or the Executive Officer of the State Committee appointed under the Act.
key_definitions.committee: The Haj Committee of India constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Haj Committee of India or a State Haj Committee, including the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Gazette of India or the Official Gazette of a State.
key_definitions.pilgrim: A Muslim proceeding to, or returning from, Haj.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under section 44 by the Central Government or under section 47 by the State Government.
key_definitions.state_committee: A State Haj Committee constituted under section 18, including a Joint State Committee.
key_definitions.state_government: In relation to a Union territory, the Administrator of that Union territory appointed by the President.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Haj Committee Act, 2002' and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

This section defines various terms used in the Act, including 'bye-laws', 'Chief Executive Officer or Executive Officer', 'Committee', 'member', 'notification', 'pilgrim', 'prescribed', 'State Committee', and 'State Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of Haj Committee of India
main_sections.description: This section establishes the Haj Committee of India, stating it will be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of acquiring property, contracting, suing, and being sued. Its headquarters will be in Mumbai.

This section details the composition of the Haj Committee of India, including members of Parliament, elected Muslim members from states, ex officio members representing specific ministries, and nominated Muslim members with special knowledge or representing women.

This section outlines the primary duties of the Haj Committee of India, which include collecting and disseminating information for pilgrims, assisting pilgrims, providing relief, finalizing and executing the annual Haj plan, approving budgets, coordinating travel facilities, and generally looking after pilgrim welfare.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of State Haj Committee
main_sections.description: This section deals with the establishment and incorporation of State Haj Committees.
This section establishes the Central Haj Fund.
This section establishes the State Haj Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Committee to issue Pilgrim Passes and levy fees
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Committee to issue Pilgrim Passes and levy fees.
This section provides for the repeal of previous enactments.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Haj Committee Act, 2002, comes into force on a date or dates appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Rule 2: The Haj Committee of India is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Rule 3: The Haj Committee of India shall consist of members of Parliament, elected Muslim members, ex officio members from relevant ministries, and nominated Muslim members.

Rule 4: The term of office for members of the Haj Committee of India (excluding ex officio and casual vacancy members) is three years, which can be extended by the Central Government for a period not exceeding six months at a time, and not beyond a total of one year.
Rule 5: The Haj Committee of India shall meet at least three times annually before the Haj season for planning and once after to review arrangements.

Rule 6: A person shall be disqualified from being nominated or continuing as a member of the Committee if they are not an Indian citizen, not a Muslim (except ex officio members), under twenty-five years of age, of unsound mind, an undischarged insolvent, convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, or have been previously removed for not acting in the interest of pilgrims or for corruption.

rights: Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property (movable and immovable) by the Committee.
Right to contract and sue and be sued by the Committee.
duties: Duties of the Committee include collecting and disseminating information for pilgrims, arranging orientation and training, assisting pilgrims, giving relief to distressed pilgrims, finalizing and executing the annual Haj plan, approving budgets, coordinating travel facilities, and looking after pilgrim welfare.
Duty of the Central Government to afford all reasonable assistance to the Committee in discharging its duties.
Duties of State Committees are outlined in Section 27.
Duty to make rules and bye-laws for the effective functioning of the committees.
obligations: Obligation to reconstitute the Haj Committee of India at least four months before its term expires.
Obligation to notify members in the Official Gazette.
Obligation to convene the first meeting of the Committee within forty-five days of member notification for electing Chairperson and Vice-Chairpersons.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Constitution of the Haj Committee of India: The Central Government will, by notification, appoint a date for the constitution of the Committee, which will be a body corporate. (Section 3)

Procedure 2: Election of Chairperson and Vice-Chairpersons: After the publication of members, the Central Government will convene the first meeting within forty-five days. The Committee will elect a Chairperson and two Vice-Chairpersons from its members. (Section 7)
Procedure 3: Reconstitution of the Committee: The Central Government must take steps for reconstitution at least four months before the expiry of the current Committee's term. (Section 8)

Procedure 4: Meetings of the Committee: The Committee shall meet at least three times a year before the Haj season and once after. Additional meetings can be held if requisitioned by one-third of members or if deemed necessary by the Chairperson. (Section 10)
Procedure 5: Resignation: A Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, or member may resign by writing to the Central Government, effective from the date of resignation. (Section 13)
Procedure 6: Removal: The Central Government may remove a member under specific conditions outlined in Section 14.
Procedure 7: Filing of Casual Vacancy: Casual vacancies in the office of the Chairperson or Vice-Chairperson shall be filled for the remainder of the term. (Section 7(7))
administration: The Central Government and State Governments are responsible for administration, including making rules, notifications, and overseeing the functioning of the Committees. The Ministry responsible for Haj affairs is implied.
important_notes: Note 1: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act and for different States for its commencement. (Section 1(2))
Note 2: A Minister shall not be the Chairperson of the Committee, and ex officio members shall not participate in the election of the Chairperson or Vice-Chairpersons. (Section 7(1))
Note 3: The term of office of members may be extended by the Central Government by notification, but not exceeding a total of one year. (Section 6(1))
Note 4: Not more than one member shall be elected from a State falling in the zones as specified in the Schedule. (Section 4(ii))
Note 5: Not more than fifty per cent. of the members may be renominated for a second term for reconstitution, as prescribed. (Section 8(2))
Note 6: Officers and employees of the Committee are considered public servants. (Section 39)

title: THE FOREIGN AIRCRAFT (EXEMPTION FROM TAXES AND DUTIES ON FUEL AND LUBRICANTS) ACT, 2002
purpose: To implement Agreements entered into by India with other countries in pursuance of the Convention on International Civil Aviation, specifically to exempt taxes and duties on fuel and lubricants supplied in India to aircraft of contracting parties.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Concerns fuel and lubricants supplied to aircraft of other countries operating under international agreements.

key_definitions.Agreements: Air Services Agreements or Air Transport Agreements entered into by India with parties to the Convention.
key_definitions.Convention: The Convention on International Civil Aviation opened for signatures at Chicago on the 7th December, 1944.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent, which is the whole of India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, namely 'Agreements' and 'Convention'.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption from levy of taxes and duties on fuel and lubricants supplied to aircraft of other countries
main_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to grant exemption from taxes and duties on fuel and lubricants supplied to aircraft of other countries, in accordance with international conventions or agreements. Such exemptions, when notified, have the force of law in India.

important_rules: Rule 1: In pursuance of the Convention or Agreement with any other country or countries, it is necessary to grant exemption from the levy of taxes and duties on fuel and lubricants filled into receptacles forming part of any aircraft of any other country or countries.
Rule 2: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make necessary provisions to give effect to the said Convention or Agreement.
Rule 3: Any provision made by the Central Government under this section shall apply accordingly and shall have the force of law in India, notwithstanding anything contrary contained in any other law.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette to make provisions for giving effect to conventions or agreements.

duties: Duty to comply with provisions made by the Central Government through notification for exemption of taxes and duties on fuel and lubricants for foreign aircraft.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to implement international agreements concerning fuel and lubricants for foreign aircraft.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Central Government identifies a need to grant exemption based on international Convention or Agreements.
Procedure 2: Central Government issues a notification in the Official Gazette to make provisions for granting the exemption.
Procedure 3: The provisions in the notification become effective and have the force of law, overriding other laws if contrary.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act is enacted to implement international obligations arising from the Convention on International Civil Aviation.
The exemptions granted under this Act have precedence over other laws in India.

title: THE SECURITISATION AND RECONSTRUCTION OF FINANCIAL ASSETS AND ENFORCEMENT OF SECURITY INTEREST ACT, 2002
purpose: To regulate securitisation and reconstruction of financial assets and enforcement of security interest and to provide for a Central database of security interests created on property rights, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and came into force on June 21, 2002. It applies to banks, financial institutions, asset reconstruction companies, borrowers, and various financial assets and security interests.

key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: A Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal established under the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993.
key_definitions.asset reconstruction: Acquisition by an asset reconstruction company of any right or interest of a bank or financial institution in any financial assistance for its realization.
key_definitions.asset reconstruction company: A company registered with the Reserve Bank of India for carrying on the business of asset reconstruction or securitisation.
key_definitions.bank: Includes a banking company, corresponding new bank, State Bank of India, subsidiary bank, multi-State co-operative bank, and other banks specified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.borrower: Any person or pooled investment vehicle granted financial assistance by a bank or financial institution, or who has given a guarantee or created security for such assistance. It also includes those who become borrowers of an asset reconstruction company or who have raised funds through debt securities.
key_definitions.Central Registry: The registry set up or caused to be set up under section 20 for maintaining records of securitisation, reconstruction, and security interest transactions.
key_definitions.debt: As defined in the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993, and includes unpaid portions of purchase price for tangible and intangible assets, and credit extended for acquiring such assets.
key_definitions.default: Non-payment of debt or other amounts by a borrower leading to classification as a non-performing asset, or non-payment after a ninety-day demand notice for debt securities.
key_definitions.financial asset: Debt or receivables, including secured or unsecured claims, claims secured by immovable or movable property, beneficial interests in property, financial assistance, and rights in tangible/intangible assets securing obligations.
key_definitions.financial institution: Includes public financial institutions, institutions specified by the Central Government, International Finance Corporation, debenture trustees, asset reconstruction companies, and specified non-banking financial companies.
key_definitions.financial lease: A lease agreement for a tangible asset where the lessor transfers rights to the lessee for a period in exchange for periodic payments, with the lessee becoming the owner at the end of the term or upon paying a residual amount.
key_definitions.hypothecation: A charge on movable property, existing or future, created in favor of a secured creditor without delivery of possession, to secure financial assistance.
key_definitions.non-performing asset: An asset or account classified as sub-standard, doubtful, or loss asset by a bank or financial institution according to their respective regulatory guidelines or Reserve Bank directions.
key_definitions.obligor: A person liable to the originator to pay a financial asset or discharge an obligation in respect of it.
key_definitions.originator: The owner of a financial asset acquired by an asset reconstruction company for securitisation or reconstruction.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title as the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002. It states the extent as the whole of India and the commencement date as June 21, 2002.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Appellate Tribunal', 'asset reconstruction', 'asset reconstruction company', 'bank', 'borrower', 'Central Registry', 'debt', 'default', 'financial asset', 'financial institution', 'financial lease', 'hypothecation', 'non-performing asset', 'obligor', and 'originator'.
Lays down the procedure for registration of asset reconstruction companies with the Reserve Bank of India.
Grants secured creditors the power to enforce their security interest without the intervention of any court or tribunal in case of a default by the borrower.
Establishes a Central Registry for the purpose of maintaining a database of security interests created on property rights.
Details the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: The provisions of this Act to override other laws
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall have an overriding effect over other laws in case of inconsistency.

important_rules: Rule: Secured creditors can enforce security interest without court intervention upon borrower's default (Section 13).
Rule: Asset reconstruction companies must be registered with the Reserve Bank of India (Section 3).
Rule: A Central Registry is to be established for security interest transactions (Section 20).
Rule: Provisions of this Act override other laws where inconsistencies arise (Section 35).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 27).
Specific penalties for offences defined in the Act (Section 29).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Reserve Bank of India (for registration and policy matters), Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate (to assist in taking possession of secured assets), and potentially other authorities as specified.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes measures for asset reconstruction, taking possession of secured assets, and imposing penalties for non-compliance. The Act also allows for the overriding effect of its provisions over other laws.

rights: Right of a borrower to receive compensation and costs in certain cases (Section 19).
Right to inspect particulars of securitisation, reconstruction, and security interest transactions (Section 26).
Right of enforcement of securities by registered creditors (Section 26D).
Right to lodge a caveat (Section 18C).
duties: Duty of asset reconstruction companies to register with RBI (Section 3).
Duty to report satisfaction of security interest by asset reconstruction companies or secured creditors (Section 25).
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation of borrowers to repay financial assistance.
Obligations related to the creation, modification, and satisfaction of security interests.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of asset reconstruction companies with the Reserve Bank of India.
Procedure for enforcement of security interest by secured creditors, including taking possession of secured assets.
Procedure for filing, modification, and reporting of securitisation, reconstruction, and security interest transactions with the Central Registry.
Procedure for appeal against measures taken to recover secured debts before the Appellate Tribunal.
administration: The Reserve Bank of India plays a significant role in regulating asset reconstruction companies and determining policy. The Central Government has powers to make rules and specify institutions. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate assists in enforcement.
important_notes: The Act may not apply in certain cases as specified (Section 31).
