The Central Government has the power to exempt a class or classes of banks or financial institutions from the Act's provisions (Section 31A).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 32).
Civil courts do not have jurisdiction in matters that the Debts Recovery Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal is empowered to determine (Section 34).
The Act's provisions are designed to override other laws (Section 35).

title: THE COMPETITION ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide, keeping in view of the economic development of the country, for the establishment of a Commission to prevent practices having adverse effect on competition, to promote and sustain competition in markets, to protect the interests of consumers and to ensure freedom of trade carried on by other participants in markets, in India, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh). Applies to economic activities relating to the production, storage, supply, distribution, acquisition or control of articles or goods, or the provision of services, of any kind, or in investment, or in the business of acquiring, holding, underwriting or dealing with shares, debentures or other securities of any other body corporate. Excludes activities of the Government relatable to sovereign functions including atomic energy, currency, defence and space.

key_definitions.acquisition: Directly or indirectly, acquiring or agreeing to acquire shares, voting rights or assets of any enterprise; or control over management or control over assets of any enterprise.
key_definitions.agreement: Includes any arrangement or understanding or action in concert, whether or not formal, in writing, or intended to be legally enforceable.
key_definitions.cartel: An association of producers, sellers, distributors, traders, or service providers who, by agreement amongst themselves, limit, control, or attempt to control the production, distribution, sale, price, or trade in goods or provision of services.
key_definitions.commission: The Competition Commission of India established under sub-section (1) of section 7.
key_definitions.consumer: Any person who buys goods or hires/avails services for a consideration, including users or beneficiaries with approval, for resale, commercial purpose, or personal use.
key_definitions.enterprise: A person or a department of the Government engaged in any economic activity related to goods or services, including investment or dealing in securities, excluding government sovereign functions.
key_definitions.goods: As defined in the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, and includes manufactured/processed/mined products, debentures, stocks, shares after allotment, and imported goods.
key_definitions.relevant_market: The market determined by the Commission with reference to the relevant product market or relevant geographic market, or both.
key_definitions.relevant_geographic_market: An area where competition conditions for supply or demand of goods/services are homogenous and distinct from neighboring areas.
key_definitions.relevant_product_market: All products or services considered interchangeable or substitutable by consumers or suppliers based on characteristics, price, intended use, and ease of switching.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the procedure for its commencement.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'acquisition', 'agreement', 'cartel', 'consumer', 'enterprise', 'goods', and 'relevant market'.
Prohibits agreements that cause or are likely to cause an appreciable adverse effect on competition in India.
Prohibits enterprises from abusing their dominant position in a relevant market.
Defines what constitutes a 'combination' for the purposes of the Act, including mergers, acquisitions, and amalgamations.
Regulates combinations that have, or are likely to have, an appreciable adverse effect on competition in India.
Establishes the Competition Commission of India.
Outlines the composition of the Competition Commission of India, including the Chairperson and other Members.
Specifies the duties and functions of the Competition Commission of India.

main_sections.section_title: Inquiry into certain agreements and dominant position of enterprise
main_sections.description: Details the process by which the Commission can inquire into certain agreements and the dominant position of an enterprise.
Prescribes penalties for contravention of orders passed by the Commission.
Mandates the Commission to undertake competition advocacy and create awareness about competition issues.
Establishes the Appellate Tribunal for hearing appeals against orders of the Commission.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of inconsistency.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Commission the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings provisions.

important_rules: Agreements that cause or are likely to cause an appreciable adverse effect on competition in India are prohibited (Section 3).
Abuse of dominant position by an enterprise in a relevant market is prohibited (Section 4).
Combinations that have, or are likely to have, an appreciable adverse effect on competition in India are regulated (Section 6).
The Competition Commission of India has the power to inquire into agreements, dominant positions, and combinations (Sections 19, 20).
The Commission can issue orders to cease and desist, modify agreements, or divide enterprises in cases of anti-competitive practices (Section 27).
Penalties are prescribed for contravention of Commission orders, failure to comply with directions, making false statements, and non-furnishing of information (Chapter VI).
The Central Government can issue directions to the Commission and has the power to supersede the Commission under certain circumstances (Sections 55, 56).
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws where there is inconsistency (Section 60).
Civil courts' jurisdiction is excluded in matters falling within the purview of the Commission (Section 61).

penalties: Contravention of orders of the Commission: Imprisonment and/or fine.
Failure to comply with directions of the Commission and Director General: Fine.
Making false statement or omission to furnish material information: Fine.
Contraventions in relation to furnishing of information: Fine.
Penalty for non-furnishing of information on combinations: Monetary penalty.
Contravention by companies: Fine applicable to directors and officers in charge.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competition Commission of India (CCI) and its Director General.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, investigations, passing orders, imposing penalties, and taking legal proceedings. The Commission also has powers to issue interim orders and execute its orders.

rights: Right to freedom of trade.
Consumers' right to protection from anti-competitive practices.
Right to appeal against orders of the Commission to the Appellate Tribunal.
Right to legal representation before the Commission and Appellate Tribunal.
duties: Duty of enterprises to not enter into anti-competitive agreements.
Duty of enterprises not to abuse dominant position.
Duty to provide true and correct information to the Commission and Director General.
Duty to comply with orders of the Commission and Appellate Tribunal.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to provide grants to the Commission.
Obligation of the Commission to maintain accounts and get them audited.
Obligation of the Commission to undertake competition advocacy.

key_procedures: Inquiry into agreements and dominant position: The Commission can inquire suo motu or on reference from a statutory authority. If a contravention is suspected, it can direct the Director General to investigate.

Inquiry into combinations: Parties proposing a combination must give notice to the Commission. The Commission then assesses if the combination has an appreciable adverse effect on competition and can pass orders accordingly.
Procedure for appeals: Appeals against orders of the Commission lie with the Appellate Tribunal. Further appeals lie with the Supreme Court.
Settlement and Commitment: Provisions exist for settlement of cases and commitments by enterprises to resolve competition concerns.
Rectification of orders: The Commission can rectify clerical or arithmetical mistakes in its orders.
administration: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) is the primary body responsible for administering this Act.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force.
The Act's provisions apply to acts taking place outside India but having an effect on competition in India.
The Commission has the power to exempt certain persons or classes of persons from the provisions of the Act.
The Commission has the power to regulate its own procedure.
The Act aims to promote and sustain competition and protect consumer interests.

title: The Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002
purpose: To provide for the control of land within National Highways, the right of way, and traffic moving on National Highways, and for the removal of unauthorized occupation thereon.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Covers National Highways declared as such under the National Highways Act, 1956, including Expressways or Express Highways vested in the Central Government. Encompasses all lands appurtenant to the Highway, structures on it, and accessories. Also regulates traffic and construction on highway land.

key_definitions.building: Any work of construction done in any manner by use of any material, including farm buildings, plinths, doorsteps, walls, drains, advertisement boards, and other fixed items.
key_definitions.construct: To construct, reconstruct, erect, re-erect, extend or alter structurally a building.
key_definitions.cost of land: The market value of the land as determined by the competent authority of the State Government or the Government of the Union territory.
key_definitions.Court: The principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction in a district, and includes the High Court in its ordinary original civil jurisdiction.
key_definitions.Highway: A National Highway declared as such under section 2 of the National Highways Act, 1956, and includes any Expressway or Express Highway vested in the Central Government, whether surfaced or unsurfaced. It also includes appurtenant lands, bridges, culverts, tunnels, causeways, carriageways, structures, trees, railings, fences, posts, paths, signs, signals, kilometre stones, and other Highway accessories and materials.
key_definitions.Highway Administration: The Highway Administration established under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.highway land: The land of which the Central Government is, or is deemed to be, the owner under sub-section (1) of section 23.
key_definitions.land: Includes benefits arising out of land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.
key_definitions.means of access: Any permanent means of access, whether private or public, for vehicles of any kind.
key_definitions.premises: Any land or building or part of a building, including gardens, grounds, outhouses, and fittings for beneficial enjoyment.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.unauthorised occupation: Any occupation of highway land without permission under this Act by a trespasser, a person paying or liable to pay rent, a person living in or using premises on a Highway, a rent-free tenant, a licensee of possession, or someone liable to pay damages for use or possession.
key_definitions.vehicle: A barrow, sledge, plough, drag, and any wheeled or tracked conveyance of any description capable of being used on a Highway.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including building, construct, cost of land, Court, Highway, Highway Administration, highway land, land, means of access, premises, prescribed, unauthorised occupation, and vehicle.
Empowers the Central Government to establish Highway Administrations by notification in the Official Gazette, defining their jurisdiction and any conditions or limitations on their powers.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Highway Administration
main_sections.description: States that a Highway Administration shall exercise its powers and functions within its specified jurisdiction, subject to conditions and limitations imposed by the Central Government.

Specifies that appeals against orders or actions (excluding notice issuance/serving) under sections 26, 27, 28, 36, 37, and 38 by the Highway Administration or authorized officer shall lie to the Court.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions as to making of interim order
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions for making an interim order, requiring notice and opportunity to be heard to the opposing party, with provisions for exceptional circumstances and a 14-day duration unless requirements are met.
Sets a period of sixty days from the date of the order for preferring an appeal to the Court, with provisions for admitting appeals after the expiry of this period if sufficient cause is shown.

main_sections.section_title: Highway land to be deemed as property of Central Government
main_sections.description: Declares that all lands forming parts of a Highway, whether vesting in or acquired for the Central Government, are deemed to be the property of the Central Government for the purposes of this and other Central Acts. It also mandates the maintenance of records for such lands.

main_sections.section_title: Prevention of occupation of highway land
main_sections.description: Prohibits the occupation of highway land without proper authorization.
Provides for the removal of unauthorized occupants from highway land.
Deals with offenses and penalties related to the contravention of the provisions of the Act.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in certain circumstances.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: Highway land is deemed property of the Central Government for the purposes of this Act and other Central Acts (Section 23).
Rule: Unauthorized occupation of highway land is prohibited (Section 24).
Rule: Unauthorized occupants can be removed from highway land (Section 26).
Rule: Access to National Highways requires permission obtained through a prescribed procedure (Section 29).
Rule: Construction on highway land is regulated, likely requiring permission (Section 38).
Rule: Leaving vehicles or animals in a dangerous position on a Highway is prohibited (Section 37).

penalties: Penalties for offences and contraventions of the Act are specified in Section 39.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Highway Administration, officers appointed on behalf of the Highway Administration, and potentially the Court for appeals and enforcement of orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers and functions exercised by the Highway Administration, including removal of unauthorized occupation, regulation of access and traffic, and imposition of penalties for offenses. Appeals against decisions can be made to the Court. The Act has an overriding effect, indicating strong enforcement mechanisms.

rights: Right to access to Highway, subject to permission (Section 28).
Right to appeal against orders passed by the Highway Administration to the Court (Section 14).
Right to be heard before an interim order is made (Section 17).
duties: Duty of village officials (Section 42).
Duty to comply with regulations regarding traffic and construction on Highways.
Duty to obtain permission for accessing or constructing on Highway land.
obligations: Obligation to prevent unauthorized occupation of highway land.
Obligation to repair damage to the Highway (Section 36).
Obligation to comply with directions for regulating traffic when a Highway is deemed unsafe (Section 31).

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission to access a Highway (Section 29).
Procedure for removal of unauthorized occupation of highway land (Section 26).
Procedure for making interim orders, including furnishing documents and providing an opportunity to be heard, with exceptions for exceptional circumstances (Section 17).
Procedure for filing an appeal to the Court within sixty days, with provisions for condonation of delay (Section 19).
Procedure for appointing officers to act on behalf of the Highway Administration (Section 20).
Procedure for service of notices (Section 47).
administration: Highway Administration established under section 3, which exercises powers and functions under the Act, with the Central Government having overall oversight and rule-making power (Section 50).
important_notes: Several sections related to Tribunals (Sections 5-13, 15, 16, 18) have been omitted due to the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, and the Finance Act, 2017, with appeals now lying to the 'Court' (principal Civil Court).
The Act has an overriding effect (Section 48), suggesting its provisions take precedence over other laws in case of conflict concerning National Highways.
The Central Government can delegate powers and transfer jurisdiction of Highway Administrations.

title: THE PREVENTION OF MONEY-LAUNDERING ACT, 2002
purpose: To prevent money-laundering and to provide for confiscation of property derived from, or involved in, money-laundering and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India.

key_definitions.Adjudicating Authority: An Adjudicating Authority appointed under sub-section (1) of section 6.
key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: The Appellate Tribunal referred to in section 25.
key_definitions.attachment: Prohibition of transfer, conversion, disposition or movement of property by an order issued under Chapter III.
key_definitions.banking company: A banking company or a co-operative bank to which the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 applies and includes any bank or banking institution referred to in section 51 of that Act.
key_definitions.financial institution: A financial institution as defined in clause (c) of section 45-I of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and includes a chit fund company, a housing finance institution, an authorised person, a payment system operator, a non-banking financial company and the Department of Posts in the Government of India.
key_definitions.intermediary: Includes a stock-broker, share transfer agent, banker to an issue, trustee to a trust deed, registrar to an issue, merchant banker, underwriter, portfolio manager, investment adviser or any other intermediary associated with securities market and registered under section 12 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992; or an association recognised or registered under the Forward Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1952 or any member of such association; or intermediary registered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority; or a recognised stock exchange referred to in clause (f) of section 2 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.
key_definitions.money-laundering: Has the meaning assigned to it in section 3.
key_definitions.person: Includes an individual, a Hindu undivided family, a company, a firm, an association of persons or a body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, every artificial juridical person not falling within any of the preceding sub-clauses, and any agency, office or branch owned or controlled by any of the above persons mentioned in the preceding sub-clauses.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the procedure for its commencement through notification.
Defines various terms used throughout the Act, such as Adjudicating Authority, Appellate Tribunal, attachment, banking company, financial institution, intermediary, money-laundering, and person.
Defines what constitutes the offence of money-laundering.
Specifies the punishment for the offence of money-laundering.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of property involved in money-laundering
main_sections.description: Deals with the power to attach property that is involved in money-laundering.

main_sections.section_title: Verification of identity by reporting entity
main_sections.description: Mandates reporting entities to verify the identity of their clients.
Requires reporting entities to maintain specific records.
Outlines the powers and procedures for search and seizure under the Act.
Grants the power to arrest individuals involved in money-laundering.
Establishes the Appellate Tribunal for hearing appeals against orders passed under the Act.
Provides for the establishment of Special Courts for the trial of offences under the Act.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Reporting entities must verify the identity of their clients (Section 11A).
Reporting entities must maintain records of transactions (Section 12).
Specific procedures for attachment, adjudication, and confiscation of property involved in money-laundering (Chapter III).
Provisions for summons, search, seizure, and arrest of individuals (Chapter V).
Establishment and functioning of an Appellate Tribunal for appeals (Chapter VI).
Establishment and powers of Special Courts for trial of offences (Chapter VII).
Reciprocal arrangements for assistance in matters related to money-laundering with foreign countries (Chapter IX).

penalties: Punishment for money-laundering (Section 4).
Fines imposed by the Director for non-compliance (Section 13).
Punishment for vexatious search (Section 62).
Punishment for false information or failure to give information (Section 63).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Director, Adjudicating Authorities, Special Courts, and other authorities appointed under the Act. The Central Government also plays a role in directing and empowering officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation, attachment, adjudication, confiscation of property, imposition of fines, arrest, and trial by Special Courts. Enforcement also involves reporting by banking companies, financial institutions, and intermediaries.

rights: Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against orders passed under the Act (Section 26).
Right to appeal to the High Court against orders of the Appellate Tribunal (Section 42).
Right to take assistance of an authorised representative before the Appellate Tribunal (Section 39).
No civil or criminal proceedings against reporting entities, their directors, and employees in certain cases (Section 14).
duties: Duty of reporting entities to verify identity of clients (Section 11A).
Duty of reporting entities to maintain records (Section 12).
Duty to furnish information as required by the Act (Sections 15, 50).
Duty to assist authorities in inquiries and investigations (Section 54).
obligations: Obligation to report suspicious transactions.
Obligation to maintain records for a specified period.
Obligation to comply with orders of attachment, adjudication, and confiscation.

key_procedures: Procedure for attachment of property involved in money-laundering (Chapter III).
Procedure for reporting by reporting entities (Section 15).
Procedure for search and seizure (Section 17).
Procedure for arrest (Section 19).
Procedure for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal (Chapter VI).
Procedure for trials before Special Courts (Chapter VII).
Procedure for reciprocal arrangements with foreign countries (Chapter IX).
administration: The Central Government, through various authorities and officers appointed under the Act, including the Director, Adjudicating Authorities, and Special Courts. The Reserve Bank of India and other regulatory bodies may also be involved in oversight and reporting.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force (Section 1(3)).
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws in case of inconsistency (Section 71).
Civil courts are barred from having jurisdiction in respect of matters under this Act (Section 41, Section 67).

title: THE CIGARETTES AND OTHER TOBACCO PRODUCTS (PROHIBITION OF ADVERTISEMENT AND REGULATION OF TRADE AND COMMERCE, PRODUCTION, SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION) ACT, 2003
purpose: To prohibit the advertisement of, and to provide for the regulation of trade and commerce in, and production, supply and distribution of, cigarettes and other tobacco products and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The act aims to protect public health by discouraging the use of tobacco, particularly among young people and non-smokers, and to improve public health in general.
scope: The act extends to the whole of India. It applies to cigarettes and other tobacco products, regulating their advertisement, trade, commerce, production, supply, and distribution. It also prohibits smoking in public places and the sale of tobacco products to individuals under eighteen years of age or within a specified radius of educational institutions. State amendments have introduced specific regulations for 'hookah bars'.

key_definitions.advertisement: Includes any visible representation by way of notice, circular, label, wrapper or other document, and any announcement made orally or by any means of producing or transmitting light, sound, smoke or gas.
key_definitions.cigarette: Includes any roll of tobacco wrapped in paper or in any other substance not containing tobacco, or a roll of tobacco wrapped in any substance containing tobacco that is likely to be offered to consumers as a cigarette. It excludes beedi, cheroot, and cigar.
key_definitions.public place: Any place to which the public have access, whether as of right or not, including auditoriums, hospitals, railway waiting rooms, amusement centers, restaurants, public offices, court buildings, educational institutions, libraries, and public conveyances. It excludes open spaces.
key_definitions.tobacco products: Means the products specified in the Schedule.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003. It specifies that the act extends to the whole of India and shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union (Central Government) to take control of the tobacco industry.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including advertisement, cigarette, distribution, export, import, Indian language, label, package, prescribed, production, public place, sale, smoking, specified warning, and tobacco products. State amendments add definitions for 'hookah bar'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of smoking in a public place.
main_sections.description: Prohibits smoking in any public place. However, hotels with thirty rooms or more, restaurants with seating for thirty people or more, and airports may provide separate smoking areas.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of advertisement of cigarettes and other tobacco products.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the advertisement of cigarettes and other tobacco products. It details various forms of prohibited advertisements, including display, sale of advertising material, distribution of leaflets, and erection of hoardings. Exceptions are made for advertisements on packages and at the entrance/inside shops where tobacco products are sold. It also prohibits promoting the use or consumption of tobacco products in exchange for sponsorship or gifts.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on sale of cigarette or other tobacco products to a person below the age of eighteen years and in particular area.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products to any person under eighteen years of age and in any area within a radius of one hundred yards of any educational institution.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on trade and commerce in, and production, supply and distribution of cigarettes and other tobacco products.
main_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on trade, commerce, production, supply, and distribution of cigarettes and other tobacco products.

important_rules: No person shall smoke in any public place, with exceptions for designated smoking areas in specified establishments.
No person shall advertise cigarettes or other tobacco products, directly or indirectly promoting their use or consumption.
No person shall sell, offer for sale, or permit the sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products to anyone under eighteen years of age.
No person shall sell, offer for sale, or permit the sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products within a radius of one hundred yards of any educational institution.
Specified warnings and nicotine and tar content information must be displayed on packages of cigarettes and other tobacco products in the manner prescribed by rules.

penalties: Punishment for failure to give specified warning and nicotine and tar contents (Section 20).
Punishment for smoking in certain places (Section 21).
Punishment for advertisement of cigarettes and tobacco products (Section 22).
Forfeiture of advertisement and advertisement material (Section 23).
Punishment for sale of cigarettes or any other tobacco products in certain places or to persons below the age of eighteen years (Section 24).
General provisions for offenses by companies (Section 26).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through its agencies and rules made under the Act. Specific powers are given to officers for entry, search, and seizure.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prohibition of activities, imposition of penalties, confiscation of goods, and legal prosecution. The Act also empowers officers to enter, search, and seize items related to violations.

rights: Right of non-smokers to be protected from involuntary exposure to tobacco smoke (implied by the prohibition of smoking in public places).
Right to access information regarding health warnings and tar/nicotine content on tobacco product packaging.
duties: Duty of every person to refrain from smoking in public places.
Duty of every person engaged in tobacco-related activities to comply with advertisement prohibitions.
Duty of every person to refrain from selling tobacco products to minors or near educational institutions.
Duty of manufacturers and distributors to display specified warnings and nicotine/tar content on packages.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to restrictions on trade, commerce, production, supply, and distribution of tobacco products.
Obligation to comply with rules made by the Central Government regarding packaging, warnings, and other aspects of tobacco products.

key_procedures: Procedure for making specified warnings on packages (Section 8).
Procedure for displaying warnings in Indian languages and specified formats (Sections 9 & 10).
Procedure for testing nicotine and tar contents (Section 11).
Procedure for entry and search by authorized officers (Section 12).
Procedure for seizure of offending goods (Section 13).
Procedure for adjudication of offenses and confiscation of packages (Sections 17 & 18).
Procedure for appeal against adjudication orders (Section 19).
administration: The Central Government is empowered to make rules for the implementation of the Act. State governments may also enact amendments relevant to their jurisdictions (e.g., regarding hookah bars).
important_notes: The Act is enacted based on resolutions from the World Health Assembly urging measures to protect non-smokers and discourage tobacco use, especially among children and young people.
State amendments have specifically addressed the issue of 'hookah bars', prohibiting their operation in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.
The Act can be amended by the Central Government to add new tobacco products to the Schedule (Section 30).

title: The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Central Vigilance Commission to inquire or cause inquiries to be conducted into offences alleged to have been committed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 by certain categories of public servants of the Central Government, corporations, government companies, societies, and local authorities owned or controlled by the Central Government, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope:
The Act applies to: 
- Public servants of the Central Government.
- Corporations established by or under any Central Act.
- Government companies owned or controlled by the Central Government.
- Societies owned or controlled by the Central Government.
- Local authorities owned or controlled by the Central Government.

The subject matter scope is primarily related to inquiring into offenses alleged to have been committed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

key_definitions.Central Vigilance Commissioner: The Central Vigilance Commissioner appointed under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.Commission: The Central Vigilance Commission constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Delhi Special Police Establishment: The Delhi Special Police Establishment constituted under sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
key_definitions.Government company: A Government company within the meaning of the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.Lokpal: The Lokpal established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Vigilance Commissioner: A Vigilance Commissioner appointed under sub-section (1) of section 4.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Central Vigilance Commissioner', 'Commission', 'Delhi Special Police Establishment', 'Government company', 'Lokpal', 'prescribed', and 'Vigilance Commissioner'.

Establishes the Central Vigilance Commission, defines its composition (Chairperson and Members), and outlines the eligibility criteria for appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners. It also mentions the appointment of a Secretary and the headquarters of the Commission being in New Delhi.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners are appointed by the President based on the recommendation of a Committee comprising the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Minister of Home Affairs, and the Leader of the Opposition in the House of the People. It also addresses situations where there is no recognized Leader of the Opposition and that vacancies in the Committee do not invalidate appointments.

main_sections.section_title: Terms and other conditions of service of Central Vigilance Commissioner
main_sections.description: Defines the tenure of office for the Central Vigilance Commissioner (four years or until age 65, whichever is earlier) and states ineligibility for reappointment. For Vigilance Commissioners, it also sets a four-year term or until age 65, allows for appointment as Central Vigilance Commissioner, and caps the aggregate term. It details the oath/affirmation requirement, resignation process, grounds for removal, ineligibility for certain appointments after ceasing office, and salary/allowances conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioner
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for removing the Central Vigilance Commissioner or a Vigilance Commissioner. Removal is by order of the President on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following an inquiry and report by the Supreme Court. It also provides for suspension during inquiry and lists grounds for removal by order of the President, including insolvency, conviction of an offense involving moral turpitude, engaging in paid employment outside duties, infirmity of mind or body, and acquiring financial interests that prejudicially affect functions. It also defines misbehaviour related to financial interests in government contracts.

main_sections.section_title: Functions and powers of Central Vigilance Commission
main_sections.description: Details the functions and powers of the Commission. Primarily, it involves exercising superintendence over the Delhi Special Police Establishment concerning the investigation of offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and giving directions to the Delhi Special Police Establishment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Vigilance Commission and Delhi Special Police Establishment (in relation to investigation of offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By exercising superintendence and giving directions to the Delhi Special Police Establishment for investigations into alleged offenses by specified public servants under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

rights: Right to inquire or cause inquiries to be conducted into alleged offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 by specified public servants.
duties: Duty to exercise superintendence over the functioning of the Delhi Special Police Establishment in relation to investigations of offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Duty to give directions to the Delhi Special Police Establishment.

key_procedures: Appointment of Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners: Made by the President upon recommendation of a Committee (Prime Minister, Home Minister, Leader of Opposition).

Removal of Central Vigilance Commissioner/Vigilance Commissioner: Requires Supreme Court inquiry and report for proved misbehaviour/incapacity, followed by Presidential order. President can also remove on specific grounds like insolvency, conviction, engaging in paid employment, or infirmity.
administration: Central Government (for making rules for staff and laying notifications/rules before Parliament), President (for appointments and removal of Commissioners).
important_notes: The Act incorporates and continues the Central Vigilance Commission constituted under an earlier Ordinance and Government Resolutions.
The Act amends the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.

title: THE REPATRIATION OF PRISONERS ACT, 2003
purpose: To provide for the transfer of certain prisoners from India to countries or places outside India, and for the reception in India of certain prisoners from countries or places outside India.
scope: Applies to prisoners (defined as persons undergoing a sentence of imprisonment ordered by a criminal court) who are citizens of a contracting State and wish to be transferred to that state, or Indian citizens imprisoned in a contracting state who wish to be transferred to India. The act's application to specific countries outside India is determined by notifications from the Central Government.

key_definitions.contracting State: The government of any country or place outside India with which the Central Government has made an arrangement (through a treaty or otherwise) for the transfer of prisoners to and from India. This also includes any other such government specified by the Central Government via notification.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prisoner: A person undergoing a sentence of imprisonment under an order passed by a criminal court, including courts established under the law in contracting States.
key_definitions.warrant: A warrant issued under sub-section (1) of section 7 or sub-section (2) of section 12, as the case may be.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Repatriation of Prisoners Act, 2003, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'contracting State', 'prescribed', 'prisoner', and 'warrant'. It also states that undefined terms used in the Act will have the meanings assigned to them in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Empowers the Central Government to apply the provisions of this Act to any country or place outside India through a notification in the Official Gazette. If the notification relates to a country with which India has a treaty for prisoner transfer, the notification must include the full text of the treaty and remain in force only for the duration of the treaty. The Central Government can also modify the application of the Act to a country via notification if necessary to give effect to a treaty.

main_sections.section_title: Application for transfer by a prisoner
main_sections.description: Allows any prisoner who is a citizen of a contracting State to apply to the Central Government for transfer of their custody from India to that contracting State. If the prisoner cannot apply due to ill health, mental condition, old age, or minority, any other entitled person can make the application on their behalf.

main_sections.section_title: Consideration of request by Central Government
main_sections.description: Details the process for the Central Government to consider an application for transfer. It involves requesting information from the prison in charge and satisfying conditions such as no pending proceedings, no death penalty awarded, no conviction under military law, and no prejudice to India's sovereignty or security before forwarding the application to the contracting State.

Outlines the information to be forwarded by the Central Government to the contracting State with the prisoner's application, including judgment copies, sentence details, medical reports, and antecedents. It also specifies information the Central Government may seek from the contracting State after it accepts the application, such as proof of citizenship, relevant laws for the offense, duration and enforcement of the sentence, and the State's willingness to accept the transfer.

main_sections.section_title: Consideration of request by Central Government
main_sections.description: Describes the Central Government's decision-making process upon receiving a communication from the contracting State confirming its willingness to accept the transfer and undertaking to comply with warrant conditions. If satisfied, the Central Government may issue a warrant for transfer, irrespective of other laws. The Central Government will then inform the contracting State and request it to specify the person and place for delivering the prisoner's custody within India.

main_sections.section_title: Provision to issue warrant for transfer
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for issuing a warrant for transfer. An officer authorized by the Central Government issues the warrant to the prison in charge, directing the delivery of the prisoner's custody to the person authorized by the contracting State, along with copies of the warrant and all relevant records and personal effects. The prison in charge must comply promptly and obtain a signature upon delivery. A copy of the warrant is then sent to the court that committed the prisoner.

main_sections.section_title: Operation of warrant and retaking prisoner
main_sections.description: States that the authorized person from the contracting State can receive, hold, and convey the prisoner out of India. If the prisoner escapes custody within India, they can be arrested without a warrant, delivered to the nearest police station, and will be liable for committing an offense under section 224 of the Indian Penal Code, as well as facing the original sentence if the transfer had not occurred.

Grants the Central Government the power to requisition records of any proceedings related to a prisoner being transferred to a contracting State and to direct that these records be sent to the contracting State's government.

main_sections.section_title: Power of court and Central Government shall not be affected
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the transfer of a prisoner to a contracting State does not affect the power of the original court to review its judgment or the power of the Central or State Government to suspend, remit, or commute the sentence according to existing laws.

Enables the Central Government to accept the transfer of an Indian citizen prisoner from a contracting State, subject to agreed terms and conditions. If accepted, the Central Government may issue a warrant to detain the prisoner in India according to section 13.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of prison and issue of warrant for receiving transfer in India
main_sections.description: Details the process for receiving a prisoner transferred into India. The Central Government, in consultation with a State Government, determines the prison where the prisoner will be lodged and the officer responsible for custody. An authorized officer issues a warrant for the prisoner's detention, specifying the bringing of the prisoner into India, the place of detention, the nature and duration of imprisonment consistent with Indian law and the terms of transfer, and any other prescribed matters. Imprisonment under such a warrant is deemed imprisonment under a competent court's sentence in India. If the sentence from the contracting State is incompatible with Indian law, the Central Government can adapt it to be compatible with the sentence for a similar offense in India, while trying to correspond as closely as possible to the original sentence.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Specifies that any rules, notifications, or orders made or issued under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament.

Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act's provisions.

important_rules: A prisoner applying for transfer must be a citizen of the contracting State and must not have been awarded the death penalty or convicted under military law. No inquiry, trial, or other proceeding should be pending against the prisoner, and the transfer must not be prejudicial to India's sovereignty, security, or other interests.

When a prisoner is transferred into India, the Central Government may adapt their sentence if it is incompatible with Indian law in its nature or duration, ensuring the adapted sentence is compatible with the sentence for a similar offense committed in India and, as far as possible, corresponds to the original sentence.

If a prisoner escapes custody after being transferred out of India or into India, they can be arrested without a warrant and are liable for offenses under section 224 of the Indian Penal Code, in addition to facing their original sentence.

penalties: If a prisoner escapes from custody within India after being transferred out of India or into India, they are liable for committing an offence under section 224 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
Such a prisoner is also liable to undergo the sentence of imprisonment in India which they would have had to undergo if the delivery of custody had not been made.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, and authorized officers thereof, as well as officers in charge of prisons and persons authorized by contracting States.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through a process involving applications, consideration by the Central Government, communication with contracting States, issuance of warrants, delivery of custody, and potential arrest for escape.

rights: A prisoner who is a citizen of a contracting State has the right to apply for transfer of their custody from India to that State.
An Indian citizen imprisoned in a contracting State has the right to apply for transfer of their custody to India.
The power of courts to review judgments and the power of the Central/State Government to suspend, remit, or commute sentences remain unaffected by a prisoner's transfer.
duties: Prisoners must comply with the terms and conditions of their transfer and sentence.
The officer in charge of a prison must comply with warrants for prisoner transfer.
The Central Government has a duty to ensure that prisoner transfers are not prejudicial to India's interests and adhere to treaty obligations.
Contracting States must undertake to administer the remaining part of the prisoner's sentence and comply with any conditions specified by the Central Government.
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to apply the Act only to countries with which arrangements for prisoner transfer exist or are made.
The Central Government is obligated to obtain necessary assurances from contracting States regarding sentence enforcement and compliance with conditions.
Contracting States have an obligation to accept the transfer of prisoners and administer their sentences as agreed upon.

key_procedures: Prisoner transfer from India to a contracting State: A prisoner (citizen of a contracting State) applies to the Central Government. The Central Government verifies conditions (no pending cases, no death penalty, etc.) and forwards the application with relevant documents to the contracting State. Upon acceptance and assurance from the contracting State, the Central Government issues a warrant for transfer, authorizing the delivery of the prisoner's custody to the contracting State's representative.

Prisoner transfer from a contracting State to India: The Central Government can accept the transfer of an Indian citizen prisoner from a contracting State. Upon acceptance, the Central Government issues a warrant to detain the prisoner in India, determining the prison and officer responsible for custody. The sentence may be adapted to be compatible with Indian law if necessary.

Escaped prisoner recapture: If a prisoner escapes custody during transfer within India, any person can arrest them without a warrant and deliver them to the nearest police station, with further legal consequences for the prisoner.
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative body, responsible for notifications, considering requests, issuing warrants, and making rules. State Governments are involved in determining prisons for transfers into India.
important_notes: The application of the Act to a contracting State can be made subject to specific conditions, exceptions, and modifications by the Central Government via notification, especially to give effect to a treaty.
The transfer of a prisoner does not affect the legal powers of Indian courts or the executive government regarding review, suspension, remission, or commutation of sentences.
If a prisoner's sentence from a contracting State is incompatible with Indian law, the Central Government may adapt the sentence to be compatible, aiming to approximate the original sentence.

title: THE INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT BANK (TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING AND REPEAL) ACT, 2003
purpose: To provide for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking of the Industrial Development Bank of India to a new company to be formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956, to carry on banking business, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, and also to repeal the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964.
scope: This Act applies to the transfer of the undertaking of the Industrial Development Bank of India (Development Bank) to a newly formed company (Company) and the repeal of the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964. It also covers the implications for officers and employees, tax benefits, and other legal provisions.

key_definitions.appointed day: Such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint under section 3.
key_definitions.Company: The Industrial Development Bank of India Limited to be formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956 (1 of 1956).
key_definitions.Development Bank: The Industrial Development Bank of India established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964 (18 of 1964).
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Reserve Bank: The Reserve Bank of India constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934).

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Company', 'Development Bank', 'notification', and 'Reserve Bank'.

main_sections.section_title: Undertaking of Development Bank to vest in Company
main_sections.description: States that the undertaking of the Development Bank shall be transferred to and vest in the Company on a specified appointed day. It also outlines the Company's status as a banking company under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, with specific exemptions and adaptations.

main_sections.section_title: General effect of transfer and vesting of undertaking
main_sections.description: Details the consequences of the transfer and vesting, including the treatment of shareholders, the comprehensive nature of the 'undertaking' transferred (assets, liabilities, rights, etc.), and the continuation of contracts, deeds, and legal proceedings by or against the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Development Bank
main_sections.description: Addresses the employment of officers and employees of the Development Bank, their transfer to the Company with similar terms and conditions, and provisions related to resignation, compensation, retirement benefits, and management personnel.

main_sections.section_title: Concession, etc., to be deemed to have been granted to Company
main_sections.description: Ensures that all fiscal and other concessions, licenses, benefits, privileges, and exemptions granted to the Development Bank are deemed to have been granted to the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Tax exemption or benefit to continue to have effect
main_sections.description: Confirms the continuation of tax exemptions, assessments, and benefits related to allowances or losses for the Company as they were available to the Development Bank under the Income-tax Act, 1961. It also clarifies that the transfer itself is not considered a taxable transfer.
States that any guarantee given for or in favor of the Development Bank will continue to be operative in relation to the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Shares, bonds and debentures to be deemed to be approved securities
main_sections.description: Declares that the shares, bonds, and debentures of the Company shall be considered approved securities for the purposes of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and the Insurance Act, 1938.
Asserts that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in any other enactment or instrument.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and do not derogate from, other existing laws.
Indicates that certain enactments specified in the Schedule to the Act shall be amended as provided therein.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution in Acts, rules, regulations or notifications by Company in place of Development Bank
main_sections.description: Mandates the substitution of references to the 'Industrial Development Bank of India' with 'Industrial Development Bank of India Limited referred to in clause (b) of section 2 of the Industrial Development Bank (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act, 2003' in all existing Acts, rules, regulations, or notifications.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal and saving of Act 18 of 1964
main_sections.description: Provides for the repeal of the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964 (18 of 1964), and includes a saving provision.

important_rules: The undertaking of the Development Bank vests in the Company on the appointed day.
The Company is deemed to be a banking company under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, with certain exemptions.
All assets, liabilities, rights, and obligations of the Development Bank related to its undertaking are transferred to the Company.
Contracts, deeds, and proceedings affecting the Development Bank are enforceable by or against the Company.
Officers and employees of the Development Bank become employees of the Company with existing terms and conditions.
Fiscal and other concessions granted to the Development Bank are deemed granted to the Company.
Tax exemptions and benefits available to the Development Bank continue for the Company.
Guarantees given for the Development Bank remain operative for the Company.
The shares, bonds, and debentures of the Company are deemed approved securities.
The Act has overriding effect over inconsistent laws.
The Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964, is repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Reserve Bank of India (for matters related to banking regulations), and other relevant authorities under applicable laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, adherence to the provisions of the Act, and the application of related laws. The Act itself provides mechanisms for transfer and vesting, and the overriding effect ensures compliance. Enforcement of banking regulations would fall under the purview of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, as applied to the Company.

rights: Rights of officers and employees to retain their tenure, remuneration, terms, conditions, obligations, and privileges.
Right of the Company to all assets, powers, authorities, and privileges of the Development Bank.
Right to continue existing contracts and legal proceedings.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to appoint the 'appointed day' by notification.
Duty of the Company to carry on banking business in accordance with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Duty to ensure that officers and employees continue under the same terms.
Duty to adhere to the overriding effect of the Act.
obligations: Obligations of the Development Bank related to its undertaking are transferred to the Company.
Obligations of the Company to its employees and in carrying out banking business.

key_procedures: Central Government notification to appoint the 'appointed day' for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking.
Formation and registration of the 'Company' under the Companies Act, 1956.
Transfer and vesting of the Development Bank's undertaking to the Company on the appointed day.
Integration of officers and employees of the Development Bank into the Company.
Amendment of certain enactments as specified in the Schedule.
Substitution of references to the Development Bank with the Company in existing Acts, rules, regulations, and notifications.
Repeal of the Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for appointing the 'appointed day' and issuing notifications. The Reserve Bank of India is involved in consultations regarding the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, as it applies to the Company. The Company itself, as a registered entity, will manage its operations.
important_notes: The Act came into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint (specifically, 2nd July, 2004, vide notification No. S.O. 769(E)).

Certain provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, were initially not required for the Company (e.g., obtaining a license under section 22, maintaining asset percentages under section 24 for five years). However, a further proviso indicates these exceptions cease after the commencement of Part XIII of the Finance Act, 2021.
The transfer of services of officers/employees to the Company does not entitle them to compensation under this Act or other laws.
Directors, chairman, managing directors, or whole-time directors of the Development Bank are not entitled to compensation for loss of office or premature termination of contracts.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions will take precedence over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.
The Act's provisions are supplementary to other existing laws.

title: The Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Repeal Act, 2003
purpose: To repeal the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985 and dissolve the Appellate Authority and Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction.
scope: This act applies to India. It specifically deals with the repeal of a previous act and the consequential dissolution of bodies established under it.

key_definitions.Appellate Authority: The Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction constituted under section 5 of the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985.
key_definitions.Board: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction established under section 4 of the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985.

main_sections.description: Names the act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via official gazette notification.
Defines 'Appellate Authority' and 'Board', and states that words/expressions not defined here but defined in the repealed Act of 1985 will retain their meanings from that Act.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Act 1 of 1986 and dissolution of Appellate Authority and Board
main_sections.description: Repeals the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985 and dissolves the Appellate Authority and the Board.

Details the consequences of the dissolution of the Appellate Authority and the Board, including vacation of office by appointed persons, reversion of deputed employees, regular employees becoming employees of the Central Government, abatement of pending proceedings, transfer of funds and property to the Central Government, and liabilities becoming those of the Central Government. It also includes provisions for companies whose appeals/references abated to refer to the National Company Law Tribunal under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and for schemes sanctioned under the repealed act to be deemed approved resolution plans under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

Provides savings for the repeal, clarifying that it does not affect other enactments, previous operations, acquired rights/liabilities, orders made by the Board for scheme sanction, validity of past actions, penalties, jurisdiction, or revive defunct matters. It also states that section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 applies to the effect of repeal unless otherwise provided.

Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, particularly concerning the handling of provident fund monies and other prescribed matters. It also outlines the procedure for laying rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.

important_rules: Rule: Any appeal, reference, or inquiry pending before the Appellate Authority or Board under the repealed Act of 1985 will stand abated on a date notified by the Central Government.
Rule: Companies whose proceedings have abated can make a reference to the National Company Law Tribunal under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 within 180 days.

Rule: Schemes sanctioned or under implementation under the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985 will be deemed approved resolution plans under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

Rule: Appeals against deemed approved resolution plans can be preferred before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal within ninety days if the statutory period for appeal had not expired before the notification of this Act.
Rule: All monies, property, liabilities, and obligations of the dissolved Appellate Authority and Board are transferred to and vested in the Central Government.

penalties: Penalty: Any penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of an offense committed against the repealed enactment will still be imposed as if this Act had not been passed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Central Government and by continuing or enforcing investigations and legal proceedings as if the Act had not been passed.

rights: Right: Employees employed on a regular basis by the Appellate Authority or Board will have the same rights and privileges as to pension, gratuity, and other like matters as they would have had if their rights had not been transferred to the Central Government.
Right: Any person may prefer an appeal to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal against a deemed approved resolution plan if the statutory period for appeal had not expired.
duties: Duty: Officers and employees deputed to the Appellate Authority or Board shall stand reverted to their parent cadre, Ministry, or Department.
obligations: Obligation: Liabilities and obligations of the Appellate Authority or Board subsisting before the commencement of this Act become obligations of the Central Government.

key_procedures: Procedure: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.
Procedure: Rules made under this Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period for potential modification or annulment.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: Note: No compensation will be paid for the premature termination of office or service contracts for Chairmen, Members, or other persons appointed by the Central Government, Appellate Authority, or Board.
Note: The transfer of services of officers/employees to the Central Government will not entitle them to any compensation under this Act or any other law, and no such claim shall be entertained.

Note: The repeal does not affect any principle or rule of law, established jurisdiction, form or course of pleading, practice or procedure, or existing usage, custom, privilege, restriction, exemption, office or appointment recognized by the repealed enactment.

Note: The repeal does not revive or restore any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, right, title, privilege, restriction, exemption, usage, practice, procedure or other matter or thing not now existing or in force.

title: THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR MINORITY EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS ACT, 2004
purpose: To constitute a National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to minority educational institutions, the Central Government, State Governments, Universities, and the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions.

key_definitions.affiliation: Recognition of a college by, association with, and admission to the privileges of a University.
key_definitions.appropriate_government: The Central Government for institutions under an Act of Parliament, and a State Government for other institutions under a State Act.
key_definitions.commission: The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.competent_authority: The authority appointed by the appropriate Government to grant no objection certificates for the establishment of educational institutions by minorities.
key_definitions.educational_rights_to_minorities: The rights of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
key_definitions.minority: A community notified as such by the Central Government.
key_definitions.minority_educational_institution: A college or an educational institution established and administered by a minority or minorities.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and commencement date (deemed to have come into force on 11th November, 2004).

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'affiliation', 'appropriate Government', 'Commission', 'Competent authority', 'educational rights to minorities', 'minority', and 'Minority Educational Institution'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions, consisting of a Chairperson and two members, to be nominated by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications for appointment as Chairperson or other Member
main_sections.description: Specifies the qualifications for the Chairperson (member of a minority community, former High Court Judge) and other Members (member of a minority community, person of eminence, ability, and integrity).

main_sections.section_title: Right to establish a Minority Educational Institution
main_sections.description: Grants the right to establish a Minority Educational Institution subject to obtaining a no objection certificate from the competent authority. It also outlines the procedure for granting or rejecting such certificates.

Details the functions of the Commission, including advising the government on minority education, inquiring into complaints regarding educational rights, intervening in court proceedings, reviewing safeguards, and deciding on the status of minority educational institutions.

Outlines the powers of the Commission, including the final decision-making authority in disputes between minority educational institutions and universities regarding affiliation, and possessing powers of a civil court.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in force concerning minority educational institutions.

important_rules: A person must be a member of a minority community to be appointed as Chairperson or Member of the Commission.
The Chairperson must be a former Judge of a High Court.
Minority Educational Institutions have the right to seek affiliation with any University, subject to the University's establishment Act.
The Commission shall inquire into complaints regarding deprivation or violation of minority educational rights.
The decision of the Commission in disputes between a minority educational institution and a university regarding affiliation shall be final.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions, and the appropriate Government (Central or State).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigations, inquiries, issuing decisions, making recommendations to the appropriate government, and intervening in court proceedings.

rights: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
Right of a Minority Educational Institution to seek affiliation to any University.
Right of an applicant for a no objection certificate to be heard.
Right to know the status of an affiliation application after sixty days.
duties: The Central Government's duty to constitute the Commission and provide necessary staff.
The Competent authority's duty to decide applications for no objection certificates expeditiously.
The Commission's duty to perform its functions and exercise its powers.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for and obtaining a no objection certificate for establishing a Minority Educational Institution.
Procedure for a Minority Educational Institution to seek affiliation to a University.
Procedure for the Commission to inquire into complaints regarding deprivation or violation of minority educational rights.
Procedure for the Commission to review safeguards and recommend measures for effective implementation.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for the overall administration, including constituting the Commission, appointing its members, and providing necessary staff. The Commission itself administers its functions and powers.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning it prevails over other laws concerning minority educational institutions.
The Commission's proceedings are not invalidated by vacancies or defects in its constitution.
The Commission's orders and decisions must be authenticated by the Secretary or an authorized officer.

title: The University of Allahabad Act, 2005
purpose: To declare the University of Allahabad as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the University of Allahabad, located in Uttar Pradesh, India. Its jurisdiction is initially defined within a 16-kilometer radius from the Convocation Hall of the University, with provisions for admitting other institutions to its privileges. It covers all aspects of the University's establishment, governance, and operations, including its employees, students, and academic activities.

key_definitions.academic_council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic_staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the Statutes.
key_definitions.appointed_day: The date of establishment of the University of Allahabad under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.centre: A unit of the University or of a University Institute providing teaching, consultancy, and research facilities.
key_definitions.chancellor: The Chancellor of the University appointed under section 13.
key_definitions.constituent_college: A college prescribed as such by the Statutes.
key_definitions.constituent_institute: An Institute prescribed as such by the Statutes.
key_definitions.director: The head of a University Institute or Constituent Institute.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University, including teachers and other staff.
key_definitions.executive_council: The Executive Council of the University.
key_definitions.finance_officer: The Finance Officer of the University appointed under section 18.
key_definitions.principal: The head of a University College or a Constituent College.
key_definitions.pro_vice_chancellor: The Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University appointed under section 15.
key_definitions.registrar: The Registrar of the University appointed under section 17.
key_definitions.regulations: The Regulations of the University.
key_definitions.teacher: Professors, Readers, and Lecturers appointed or recognized by the University.
key_definitions.university: The University of Allahabad established and incorporated under section 4.
key_definitions.university_appointed_teacher: A teacher appointed by the University for imparting instruction and conducting research.
key_definitions.university_college: A college or an institution maintained by the University or admitted to its privileges.
key_definitions.university_institute: An Institute established and maintained by the University.
key_definitions.university_recognized_teacher: A teacher recognized by the University for imparting instruction and conducting research.
key_definitions.vice_chancellor: The Vice-Chancellor of the University appointed under section 14.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The University of Allahabad Act, 2005' and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of University of Allahabad as Institution of national importance
main_sections.description: This section declares the University of Allahabad in Uttar Pradesh as an Institution of national importance.
This section provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'appointed day', 'University', 'Vice-Chancellor', and others.

This section establishes the University of Allahabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, enabling it to sue and be sued. It also outlines who constitutes the University and specifies its headquarters to be in Allahabad.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of incorporation of Allahabad University
main_sections.description: This section details the consequences of the University's incorporation on the 'appointed day', including how references to the old University will be treated, the transfer of properties, rights, and liabilities, and the conditions of service for existing employees.

This section outlines the main objectives of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, promoting integrated courses, fostering innovation, addressing disparities, and educating human resources for national development.

This section enumerates the extensive powers of the University, covering instruction, research, granting degrees and distinctions, organizing open learning programs, instituting academic positions, recognizing teachers, establishing colleges and institutes, admitting institutions, demanding fees, managing property, borrowing money, and performing all other necessary acts to achieve its objects.

This section defines the territorial jurisdiction of the University within a 16-kilometer radius from its Convocation Hall and stipulates that institutions previously affiliated with the University of Allahabad under the Uttar Pradesh State Universities Act, 1973, shall continue to be admitted to its privileges.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all persons irrespective of gender, class or creed
main_sections.description: This section ensures that the University is accessible to all individuals regardless of their gender, caste, creed, race, or class, prohibiting any religious tests for appointment or admission.

important_rules: The University must be open to all persons irrespective of gender, class, or creed, and no religious tests shall be imposed for appointment or admission.
The University has the power to grant, withdraw, or confer degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions based on examinations, evaluation, or other testing methods.
The University can establish and maintain University Colleges and University Institutes for instruction and research.
