The University can admit colleges and institutions within its territorial jurisdiction to its privileges as University Colleges, Constituent Institutes, and Constituent Colleges, and can also withdraw these privileges.
The University has the power to demand and receive payment of fees and other charges.
The University is empowered to regulate and enforce discipline among its students and employees and take necessary disciplinary measures.

The University can receive benefactions, donations, and gifts, and acquire, hold, manage, and dispose of property, provided that disposal of immovable property requires prior approval from the Central Government.

rights: Employees have rights regarding tenure, remuneration, terms and conditions of service, and privileges relating to pension, leave, gratuity, and provident fund.
Employees whose altered terms of service are not acceptable have the right to have their employment terminated with compensation.
Students have the right to be admitted to the University irrespective of gender, class, or creed.
duties: The University has a duty to disseminate and advance knowledge by providing instructional and research facilities.
The University has a duty to make provisions for integrated courses in various disciplines.

The University has a duty to take appropriate measures for promoting innovations in teaching-learning, interdisciplinary studies, research, removal of gender disparities and digital divide, and application of knowledge for social advancement.
The University has a duty to educate and train human resources for national development.
The University has a duty to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees.
The University has a duty to establish and recognize hostels and supervise student welfare.
The University has a duty to cooperate, collaborate, or associate with other universities and institutions.
obligations: The University has an obligation to ensure that its actions are consistent with its stated objects and powers.
The University must obtain prior approval from the Central Government for the disposal of immovable property.
The University must obtain approval from the Central Government for borrowing money on the security of its property.

key_procedures: Appointment of Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, and Finance Officer.
Formation and functioning of University authorities like the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.
Making of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Submission of Annual Report, Accounts, and Audit.
Procedure for appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
Process for filling casual vacancies in University authorities and bodies.
Procedure for removal of difficulties by the Central Government.
Publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their laying before Parliament.
administration: The University of Allahabad is administered by its various authorities and officers as defined in the Act, including the Visitor, Chief Rector, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans of Faculties, Registrar, Finance Officer, Executive Council, Academic Council, and Finance Committee. The Central Government has oversight powers, including the power to remove difficulties and approve certain financial transactions.
important_notes: Different provisions of the Act can come into force on different dates appointed by the Central Government.
The Act amends the Uttar Pradesh State Universities Act, 1973 (President's Act 10 of 1973).
Disposal of immovable property by the University requires prior approval of the Central Government.
Borrowing money by the University on the security of its property requires the approval of the Central Government.

title: THE SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONES ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for the establishment, development and management of the Special Economic Zones for the promotion of exports and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the establishment, development, and management of Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and the entities operating within them.

key_definitions.Special Economic Zone: Each Special Economic Zone notified under the proviso to sub-section (4) of section 3 and sub-section (1) of section 4 (including Free Trade and Warehousing Zone) and includes an existing Special Economic Zone.
key_definitions.Developer: A person who, or a State Government which, has been granted by the Central Government a letter of approval under sub-section (10) of section 3 and includes an Authority and a Co-Developer.
key_definitions.Entrepreneur: A person who has been granted a letter of approval by the Development Commissioner under sub-section (9) of section 15.
key_definitions.Domestic Tariff Area: The whole of India (including the territorial waters and continental shelf) but does not include the areas of the Special Economic Zones.
key_definitions.Export: Means taking goods, or providing services, out of India, from a Special Economic Zone, by land, sea or air or by any other mode, whether physical or otherwise; or supplying goods, or providing services, from the Domestic Tariff Area to a Unit or Developer; or supplying goods, or providing services, from one Unit to another Unit or Developer, in the same or different Special Economic Zone.
key_definitions.Import: Means bringing goods or receiving services, in a Special Economic Zone, by a Unit or Developer from a place outside India by land, sea or air or by any other mode, whether physical or otherwise; or receiving goods, or services by a Unit or Developer from another Unit or Developer of the same Special Economic Zone or a different Special Economic Zone.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the procedure for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Approval Committee', 'Authority', 'Board', 'Developer', 'Development Commissioner', 'Domestic Tariff Area', 'entrepreneur', 'existing Special Economic Zone', 'existing Unit', 'export', 'Free Trade and Warehousing Zone', 'import', 'infrastructure facilities', 'International Financial Services Centre', 'manufacture', 'notification', 'notified offences', 'Offshore Banking Unit', 'person', 'prescribed', 'Reserve Bank', 'Schedule', 'services', 'Special Economic Zone', 'State Government', and 'Unit'.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for making proposal to establish Special Economic Zone
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for proposing the establishment of a Special Economic Zone, which can be initiated by the Central Government, State Government, or any person. It details how proposals are to be made, forwarded, and approved by the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Special Economic Zone and approval and authorisation to operate it to, Developer
main_sections.description: Describes the process of officially establishing a Special Economic Zone and granting approval and authorization to a Developer to operate it.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption from taxes, duties or cess
main_sections.description: Specifies exemptions from taxes, duties, or cess for entities within Special Economic Zones.
Details the formation of the Board of Approval.

main_sections.section_title: Duties, Powers and functions of Board
main_sections.description: Encompasses the responsibilities, authorities, and operations of the Board of Approval.
Pertains to the appointment and role of the Development Commissioner for Special Economic Zones.
Lists the specific duties and responsibilities of the Development Commissioner.
Describes the formation of the Approval Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Approval Committee
main_sections.description: Details the authorities and operations of the Approval Committee.
Covers the procedures and requirements for setting up a Unit within a Special Economic Zone.
Introduces the concept of a single application form and return for various purposes within SEZs.

main_sections.section_title: Single enforcement officer or agency for notified offences
main_sections.description: Establishes a single enforcement officer or agency responsible for notified offenses within SEZs.
Grants powers for investigation, inspection, search, and seizure within SEZs.

main_sections.section_title: Designated Courts to try suits and notified offences
main_sections.description: Specifies the designation of Courts to handle legal suits and notified offenses related to SEZs.
Provides the right to appeal to the High Court against certain decisions.

main_sections.section_title: Exemptions, drawbacks and concessions to every Developer and entrepreneur
main_sections.description: Details the exemptions, drawbacks, and concessions available to Developers and entrepreneurs.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of Income-tax Act, 1961 to apply with certain modification in relation to Developers and entrepreneurs
main_sections.description: Explains how the Income-tax Act, 1961, applies with modifications to Developers and entrepreneurs in SEZs.
Concerns the establishment of a Special Economic Zone Authority.
Outlines the duties and responsibilities of the Special Economic Zone Authority.
Identifies the authorities responsible for the administration of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to modify provisions of this Act or other enactments in relation to Special Economic Zones
main_sections.description: Grants the power to modify provisions of this Act or other enactments concerning Special Economic Zones.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: Procedure for making proposals to establish a Special Economic Zone must be followed, involving submission to the State Government or directly to the Board of Approval (Section 3).
Developers and entrepreneurs are eligible for exemptions, drawbacks, and concessions (Section 26).
The Income-tax Act, 1961, applies with certain modifications to Developers and entrepreneurs (Section 27).
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws, meaning its provisions will prevail in cases of conflict (Section 51).
Single application forms and returns are to be used for various processes (Section 19).

penalties: Penalties for 'notified offences' are to be tried by Designated Courts (Section 23).
Powers of investigation, inspection, search, or seizure are vested under the Act (Section 22).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Development Commissioner, Approval Committee, Board of Approval, Special Economic Zone Authority, single enforcement officer or agency for notified offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation, inspection, search and seizure powers, and trial of notified offences by designated courts.

rights: Right to receive exemptions, drawbacks, and concessions for Developers and entrepreneurs (Section 26).
Right to appeal to the High Court (Section 24).
duties: Developers have obligations and entitlements as prescribed by the Central Government (Section 3(8)(b)).
obligations: Obligations of Developers include undertaking authorised operations as per terms and conditions (Section 3(8)(b)).

key_procedures: Proposal for establishing an SEZ: A person identifies an area and makes a proposal to the State Government or directly to the Board. The State Government forwards recommendations, and the Board approves, modifies, or rejects the proposal (Sections 3).
Setting up a Unit: Entrepreneurs obtain a letter of approval from the Development Commissioner (Section 15).
Single Window Clearance: Implemented through the Approval Committee to streamline processes (Chapter V).
Notifications: Any official communication or announcement is made via notification in the Official Gazette (Section 2(s)).
administration: The Central Government is responsible for prescribing rules and guidelines. Authorities responsible for administration are identified under Section 47.
important_notes: The Act was brought into force on different dates for different provisions, with major sections commencing on February 10, 2006, and others later (Section 1 commencement note).
The definition of 'person' is broad and includes various entities, including those notified by the Central Government (Section 2(v)).

The definition of 'services' for SEZ purposes includes tradable services covered by the WTO's General Agreement on Trade in Services, those prescribed by the Central Government, and those earning foreign exchange (Section 2(z)).
Existing SEZs and Units are covered by the Act (Sections 2(k), 2(l)).
Special Economic Zones can be designated as ports, airports, inland container depots, etc., in certain cases (Section 53).

title: THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for more effective protection of the rights of women guaranteed under the Constitution who are victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It addresses violence within the family and applies to situations involving a domestic relationship between an aggrieved person (woman) and a respondent (adult male person, or relative of husband/male partner in certain cases).

key_definitions.aggrieved person: Any woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent.
key_definitions.domestic relationship: A relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.
key_definitions.domestic violence: Any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent that harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being (mental or physical) of the aggrieved person; or harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person to coerce her to meet unlawful demands for dowry or property; or threatens the aggrieved person; or otherwise injures or causes harm (physical or mental) to the aggrieved person. This includes physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, and economic abuse.
key_definitions.respondent: Any adult male person who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the aggrieved person and against whom the aggrieved person has sought any relief under this Act. An aggrieved wife or female living in a relationship in the nature of a marriage may also file a complaint against a relative of the husband or the male partner.
key_definitions.shared household: A household where the aggrieved person lives or has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent. This includes households jointly or singly owned or tenanted by either of them, or those belonging to the joint family of which the respondent is a member.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. It states that the Act extends to the whole of India and will come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'aggrieved person', 'child', 'domestic incident report', 'domestic relationship', 'domestic violence', 'Magistrate', 'Protection Officer', 'respondent', 'service provider', and 'shared household'.
Defines what constitutes domestic violence, encompassing physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, and economic abuse. It also provides explanations for each type of abuse.

main_sections.section_title: Information to Protection Officer and exclusion of liability of informant
main_sections.description: Allows any person who believes domestic violence has occurred, is occurring, or is likely to occur, to report it to the Protection Officer. It also states that informants acting in good faith are not liable civilly or criminally.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of police officers, service providers and Magistrate
main_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of police officers, Protection Officers, service providers, and Magistrates upon receiving a complaint of domestic violence or encountering an incident. They must inform the aggrieved person of her rights and available services.

Empowers the State Government to appoint Protection Officers in each district, defining their jurisdiction. It also specifies that Protection Officers should ideally be women and possess prescribed qualifications and experience.

main_sections.section_title: Duties and functions of Protection Officers
main_sections.description: Details the duties of Protection Officers, including assisting the Magistrate, preparing domestic incident reports, assisting aggrieved persons in obtaining relief, providing legal aid information, maintaining lists of service providers, arranging shelter homes, facilitating medical examinations, and ensuring compliance with monetary relief orders.
Allows an aggrieved person to present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under the Act.
Empowers the Magistrate to pass a protection order restraining the respondent from committing acts of domestic violence or aiding or abetting such acts.
Authorizes the Magistrate to pass a residence order granting the aggrieved person the right to reside in the shared household.
Enables the Magistrate to order the respondent to pay monetary relief to the aggrieved person to meet expenses and losses incurred due to domestic violence.
Grants the Magistrate the power to pass custody orders in respect of any child of the aggrieved person and the respondent.
Allows the Magistrate to order the respondent to pay compensation for the injuries, mental anguish, or losses suffered by the aggrieved person or her child due to domestic violence.
Specifies the duration for which orders under the Act are effective and provides for their alteration or revocation.
States that the procedure to be followed by the Magistrate shall be as prescribed under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for matters relating to reliefs under this Act.
Provides for the right of appeal against any order made by the Magistrate.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for breach of protection order by respondent
main_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty for the respondent who breaches a protection order.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for not discharging duty by Protection Officer
main_sections.description: Defines a penalty for a Protection Officer who fails to discharge their duties under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from legal action for anyone acting in good faith under the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not in derogation of any other law
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Any person can inform the Protection Officer about suspected or potential domestic violence.

Police officers, Protection Officers, service providers, and Magistrates must inform aggrieved persons of their rights and available services (protection order, monetary relief, custody order, residence order, compensation order, free legal aid, and the right to file a complaint under Section 498A of the IPC).
Shelter homes and medical facilities must provide services to aggrieved persons upon request.
The Magistrate can issue protection orders to restrain respondents from committing acts of domestic violence.
The Magistrate can issue residence orders to secure the aggrieved person's right to reside in a shared household.
The Magistrate can grant monetary relief to cover expenses and losses due to domestic violence.
The Magistrate can issue custody orders for children.
The Magistrate can issue compensation orders for injuries and losses suffered.
Orders can be interim or ex parte, and their duration and alteration are governed by the Act.
Breach of a protection order by a respondent is a punishable offense.

penalties: Penalty for breach of protection order by respondent (Section 31): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both.
Penalty for not discharging duty by Protection Officer (Section 33): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both.
Cognizance of offence committed by Protection Officer (Section 34): Specifies the procedure for taking cognizance of offences committed by Protection Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate (Judicial Magistrate of the First Class or Metropolitan Magistrate), Protection Officers, Police Officers, Service Providers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through applications made to the Magistrate, issuance of various orders (protection, residence, monetary, custody, compensation), assistance from Protection Officers and service providers, and by invoking criminal penalties for breaches of orders or duties.

rights: Right of an aggrieved person to reside in the shared household.
Right to seek protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief, custody orders, and compensation orders.
Right to information about available services and legal aid.
Right to free legal services under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
Right to appeal against orders of the Magistrate.
duties: Duty of police officers, service providers, and Magistrate to inform aggrieved persons of their rights and services.
Duty of shelter homes to provide shelter to aggrieved persons.
Duty of medical facilities to provide medical aid to aggrieved persons.

Duty of Protection Officers to assist the Magistrate, make reports, assist aggrieved persons, ensure legal aid, maintain lists of service providers, arrange shelter homes and medical examinations, and ensure compliance with monetary relief orders.
Duty of the Government to appoint Protection Officers and notify medical facilities and shelter homes.
obligations: Obligation of the respondent to not commit acts of domestic violence.
Obligation of the respondent to comply with court orders (protection, residence, monetary, custody, compensation).
Obligation of individuals in charge of shelter homes and medical facilities to provide services.
Obligation of the respondent to pay monetary relief and compensation as ordered by the Magistrate.
Obligation of Protection Officers to perform their prescribed duties.

key_procedures: Filing an application by an aggrieved person to the Magistrate seeking relief (Section 12).
Service of notice of the application to the respondent (Section 13).
Counselling for the parties involved (Section 14).
Assistance of a welfare expert (Section 15).
Proceedings to be held in camera (in private) to protect the aggrieved person (Section 16).
Issuance of protection orders, residence orders, monetary reliefs, custody orders, and compensation orders by the Magistrate (Sections 18-22).
Granting of interim and ex parte orders (Section 23).
Providing copies of orders free of cost (Section 24).
Determining the duration and alteration of orders (Section 25).
Appeals against Magistrate's orders (Section 29).
Procedure for dealing with complaints and executing orders as per the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 28).
administration: The Act is administered by State Governments through the appointment of Protection Officers and notification of other facilities. The Magistrate plays a crucial role in adjudicating cases and issuing orders. The Central Government has the power to make rules.
important_notes: The Act aims to protect women from violence within the family, which is defined broadly to include various forms of abuse.
The Act is not in derogation of any other law, meaning victims can pursue remedies under other applicable laws simultaneously.
Special provisions are made for the appointment and duties of Protection Officers and the role of service providers.

title: The National Tax Tribunal Act, 2005
purpose: To provide for the adjudication by the National Tax Tribunal of disputes with respect to levy, assessment, collection and enforcement of direct taxes and also to provide for the adjudication by that Tribunal of disputes with respect to the determination of the rates of duties of customs and central excise on goods and the valuation of goods for the purposes of assessment of such duties as well as in matters relating to levy of tax on service, in pursuance of article 323B of the Constitution and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to disputes concerning direct taxes, customs duties, central excise duties, and service tax.

key_definitions.Bench: A Bench of the National Tax Tribunal.
key_definitions.Board of Direct Taxes: The Central Board of Direct Taxes constituted under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963.
key_definitions.Board of Excise and Customs: The Central Board of Excise and Customs constituted under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the National Tax Tribunal.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the National Tax Tribunal, including the Chairperson.
key_definitions.National Tax Tribunal: The National Tax Tribunal established under section 3 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and the commencement date which is to be appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms and expressions used in the Act, including 'Bench', 'Board of Direct Taxes', 'Chairperson', 'Member', and specific tax-related Acts.
Mandates the Central Government to establish a Tax Tribunal known as the National Tax Tribunal to exercise the jurisdiction, powers, and authority conferred by the Act.
States that the National Tax Tribunal shall consist of a Chairperson and such number of Members as deemed fit by the Central Government, appointed by notification.

Details the constitution of Benches by the Chairperson, their ordinary sitting places (National Capital Territory of Delhi or other notified places), the areas of jurisdiction for each Bench, and that each Bench shall consist of two members.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications for appointment of Chairperson and other Members
main_sections.description: Specifies the qualifications for the Chairperson (Judge of Supreme Court or Chief Justice of High Court) and Members (Judge of High Court, or Member of Income-tax Appellate Tribunal or Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal for at least five years).

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chairperson and other Members
main_sections.description: Outlines the appointment process by the Central Government on the recommendations of a Selection Committee comprising the Chief Justice of India (or nominee), Secretary of Ministry of Law and Justice, and Secretary of Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue).

main_sections.section_title: Terms of office of Chairperson and other Members
main_sections.description: Defines the term of office as five years, with eligibility for re-appointment, and sets age limits for the Chairperson (68 years) and Members (65 years).
This section likely deals with the right to appeal to the National Tax Tribunal against certain orders or decisions made under the direct tax and indirect tax laws.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of National Tax Tribunal
main_sections.description: This section would detail the procedural aspects of how the Tribunal operates and the powers it possesses in hearing and deciding cases.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of pending cases from High Court
main_sections.description: This section addresses the mechanism for transferring cases that were pending in High Courts to the National Tax Tribunal.
This section outlines the provision for filing an appeal from the National Tax Tribunal's orders to the Supreme Court.

important_rules: The Chairperson of the National Tax Tribunal must have been a Judge of the Supreme Court or a Chief Justice of a High Court.
Members of the Tribunal must be qualified as a High Court Judge or have significant experience in tax appellate tribunals.
The appointment of the Chairperson and Members is made by the Central Government on the recommendation of a specific Selection Committee.
The Chairperson and Members have a term of five years and are eligible for re-appointment, subject to age limits.
The salary and allowances of the Chairperson are to be equivalent to a sitting Supreme Court Judge, and for Members, equivalent to a High Court Judge.
The Tribunal's jurisdiction can be exercised by Benches, which are constituted by the Chairperson.
Benches ordinarily sit in Delhi or other notified places, with provisions for temporary sittings elsewhere.
Each Bench shall consist of two members.
Appeals to the Tribunal can be presented by the party in person, a chartered accountant, or a legal practitioner.
The Act was struck down by the Supreme Court's Order dated 25th September, 2014 in the Madras Bar Association Vs. Union of India.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through the National Tax Tribunal and its Benches.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the adjudication of disputes and the issuance of orders by the National Tax Tribunal. The Act also confers powers to punish for contempt.

rights: Right to appeal to the National Tax Tribunal against specific tax-related orders.
Right to be heard and present one's case before the Tribunal.
Right to appeal to the Supreme Court from the Tribunal's decisions.
duties: Duty to comply with the orders and decisions of the National Tax Tribunal.
Duty to ensure that tax assessments, collections, and enforcement are carried out in accordance with the law.
Duty of officers and employees of the Tribunal to discharge functions under the general superintendence of the Chairperson.

key_procedures: Establishment of the National Tax Tribunal and its Benches.
Appointment of Chairperson and Members based on specific qualifications and a selection committee recommendation.
Hearing of appeals by the Tribunal, with provisions for appearances by authorized representatives.
Transfer of pending cases from High Courts to the Tribunal.
Appeals from the Tribunal's orders to the Supreme Court.
administration: The Central Government establishes and provides officers and employees for the National Tax Tribunal. The Chairperson oversees the general superintendence of the Tribunal's officers and employees.
important_notes: The Act has been struck down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court's Order dated 25th September, 2014 in the Madras Bar Association Vs. Union of India.
Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act's commencement.

title: THE STATE EMBLEM OF INDIA (PROHIBITION OF IMPROPER USE) ACT, 2005
purpose: To prohibit the improper use of the State Emblem of India for professional and commercial purposes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and also applies to citizens of India outside India.

key_definitions.competent authority: Any authority competent under any law for the time being in force to register any company, firm, other body of persons or any trade mark or design or to grant a patent.
key_definitions.emblem: The State Emblem of India as described and specified in the Schedule, to be used as an official seal of the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, application to citizens outside India, and commencement date to be appointed by the Central Government.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'competent authority' and 'emblem'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of improper use of emblem.
main_sections.description: This section prohibits the use of the emblem or its colourable imitation without previous permission from the Central Government or an authorised officer, if it tends to create an impression of official government relation or that it is an official document. It includes former functionaries of government within the definition of 'person'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of use of emblem for wrongful gain.
main_sections.description: This section prohibits the use of the emblem for any trade, business, calling, or profession, or in the title of any patent, or in any trade mark or design, except under prescribed conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of registration of certain companies, etc.
main_sections.description: This section prohibits competent authorities from registering a trade mark or design that bears the emblem, or granting a patent with a title containing the emblem. It also states that the Central Government's decision on whether an emblem is specified or a colourable imitation is final.

main_sections.section_title: General powers of Central Government to regulate use of emblem.
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Central Government to make rules to regulate the use of the emblem in official seals and to notify its use on stationery, specify seal designs, restrict its display on vehicles, provide guidelines for public buildings and diplomatic missions, and specify conditions for its use in other contexts like educational purposes and by armed forces personnel.

This section outlines penalties for contravening sections 3 and 4. For section 3, it's imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. Repeat offenders face imprisonment of not less than six months and up to two years, with a fine up to five thousand rupees. For section 4, it's imprisonment of not less than six months and up to two years, with a fine up to five thousand rupees.
This section mandates that no prosecution for an offence under this Act can be instituted without the previous sanction of the Central Government or an authorised officer.
This section states that the Act does not exempt any person from suits or proceedings under any other existing law.
This section provides that the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other enactment or instrument.

This section empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, including specific matters like regulating use of the emblem, stationery, official seals, authorising officers for prosecution sanction, and any other prescribed matter. It also outlines the procedure for laying rules before Parliament.

important_rules: No person shall use the State Emblem of India or any colourable imitation thereof in a manner that creates an impression of government affiliation or official document status without prior permission from the Central Government or an authorised officer (Section 3).
No person shall use the emblem for any trade, business, calling, profession, or in the title of a patent, trade mark, or design, except under prescribed conditions (Section 4).
Competent authorities are prohibited from registering trade marks or designs bearing the emblem, or granting patents with titles containing the emblem (Section 5(1)).

penalties: Contravention of Section 3: Imprisonment up to two years or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. For subsequent convictions, imprisonment for not less than six months and up to two years, with fine up to five thousand rupees.
Contravention of Section 4 for wrongful gain: Imprisonment for not less than six months and up to two years, with fine up to five thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government or any officer authorised in this behalf.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Prosecutions require previous sanction of the Central Government or an authorised officer. The Central Government has general powers to regulate the use of the emblem through rules.

rights: Right to use the emblem for official purposes as regulated by the Central Government.
Right to seek permission from the Central Government for specific uses of the emblem.
duties: Duty not to use the emblem improperly or for wrongful gain.
Duty to comply with regulations on the use of the emblem set by the Central Government.
obligations: Obligation to obtain prior permission for any use of the emblem that might imply government association.
Obligation to adhere to the conditions and restrictions prescribed by the Central Government for the use of the emblem.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission to use the emblem: A person seeking to use the emblem must obtain previous permission from the Central Government or an authorised officer (Section 3).
Procedure for prosecution: No prosecution can be instituted without the previous sanction of the Central Government or an authorised officer (Section 8).

Procedure for rule making: The Central Government makes rules by notification in the Official Gazette. These rules are laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, and can be modified or annulled by Parliament (Section 11).
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The emblem's description is based on the Sarnath Lion Capital of Asoka, adapted to include a profile of three lions, a Dharma Chakra, a bull, and a galloping horse, with the motto 'Satyameva Jayate' in Devanagari script.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other enactments or instruments.
The Schedule provides a detailed description and design of the State Emblem of India, including its adaptation from the Sarnath Lion Capital and the motto 'Satyameva Jayate'.
Appendices I and II provide simplified and more detailed designs of the emblem for reproduction in various sizes.

title: THE CREDIT INFORMATION COMPANIES (REGULATION) ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for regulation of credit information companies and to facilitate efficient distribution of credit and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to companies engaged in the business of credit information, credit institutions, specified users, borrowers, and matters related to credit information.

key_definitions.board: The Board of directors of a credit information company.
key_definitions.borrower: Any person who has been granted loan or any other credit facility by a credit institution and includes a client of a credit institution.
key_definitions.client: Includes a guarantor, a person who proposes to give guarantee or security for a borrower, or a person who has obtained or seeks to obtain financial assistance from a credit institution in various forms, or who has raised or seeks to raise money by issue of security or other instruments, or whose financial standing has been assessed or is proposed to be assessed by a credit institution.
key_definitions.credit information: Any information relating to the amounts and nature of loans/advances, outstanding amounts under credit cards and other credit facilities, nature of security taken, guarantees furnished, creditworthiness of a borrower, and any other matter the Reserve Bank deems necessary for inclusion.
key_definitions.credit information company: A company formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956, and granted a certificate of registration under this Act.
key_definitions.credit institution: A banking company and includes corresponding new banks, State Bank of India, subsidiary banks, co-operative banks, National Bank, regional rural banks, non-banking financial companies, public financial institutions, financial corporations established by a State, housing finance institutions, companies engaged in credit cards and similar cards business, and other institutions specified by the Reserve Bank.
key_definitions.credit scoring: A system enabling a credit institution to assess the creditworthiness and capacity of a borrower to repay loans and discharge obligations.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement, which can be appointed by the Central Government via notification.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'board', 'borrower', 'client', 'credit information', 'credit information company', 'credit institution', 'credit scoring', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'regulations', 'Reserve Bank', and 'specified user'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition to commence or carry on business of credit information
main_sections.description: States that no company can commence or carry on the business of credit information without obtaining a certificate of registration from the Reserve Bank.
Details the process for companies intending to commence or already in the business of credit information to apply for registration with the Reserve Bank.

Outlines the conditions the Reserve Bank must be satisfied with before granting a certificate of registration, including minimum capital, satisfactory management, and assurance that the business will not be detrimental to public interest or the credit system. It also allows the Reserve Bank to determine the number of credit information companies.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Reserve Bank to cancel certificate of registration
main_sections.description: Specifies the grounds on which the Reserve Bank can cancel a certificate of registration, such as ceasing business, failing to comply with conditions or directions, or failing to submit to inspection.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal against order of Reserve Bank
main_sections.description: Provides for an appeal process for credit information companies aggrieved by the rejection or cancellation of their registration, to the Central Government or a designated authority/tribunal.
Addresses the minimum capital requirements for credit information companies.

important_rules: Rule 1: No company shall commence or carry on the business of credit information without obtaining a certificate of registration from the Reserve Bank (Section 3).
Rule 2: Companies in existence on the commencement of the Act must apply for registration within six months (Section 4(2)).

Rule 3: The Reserve Bank may grant a certificate of registration if satisfied about the applicant's minimum capital, management character, and absence of detriment to public interest or the credit system (Section 5(1)).
Rule 4: The Reserve Bank can cancel a registration certificate if the company ceases business, fails to comply with conditions or directions, or fails to allow inspection (Section 6(1)).
Rule 5: Credit institutions are required to become members of a credit information company (Section 15).

penalties: Chapter VII deals with Offences and Penalties. Section 23 outlines general offences and penalties.
Section 25 gives the Reserve Bank the power to impose penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Reserve Bank of India
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers granted under the Act, including granting/cancelling registration, issuing directions, conducting inspections, imposing penalties, and making regulations.

rights: Right to appeal against the Reserve Bank's order of rejection or cancellation of registration (Section 7).
Right to be heard before rejection of an application or cancellation of registration (Section 5(2), Section 6(3), Section 7(2)).
Borrowers have rights regarding the accuracy and security of their credit information and the alteration of their files and reports (Chapter VI).
duties: Duty of credit information companies to comply with the provisions of the Act and directions issued by the Reserve Bank (Section 6(1)(iv)).
Duty of credit information companies to maintain the accuracy and security of credit information (Section 19).
Duty of credit information companies to adhere to privacy principles (Section 20).
Duty of credit institutions to become members of a credit information company (Section 15).
obligations: Obligation for companies to obtain registration before commencing credit information business (Section 3).
Obligation for credit information companies to meet minimum capital requirements (Section 8).
Obligation for credit information companies to adhere to directions issued by the Reserve Bank regarding policy and management (Section 10, Section 11).
Obligation of fidelity and secrecy regarding credit information (Section 29).

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining registration: A company must apply to the Reserve Bank in the prescribed form and manner. The Reserve Bank will assess conditions related to minimum capital, management, and public interest before granting or rejecting the application (Sections 4 & 5).

Procedure for cancellation of registration: If grounds for cancellation exist, the Reserve Bank will usually grant time for compliance, unless detrimental to public interest. The company must be given a reasonable opportunity to be heard before cancellation (Section 6).

Procedure for appealing an order: An aggrieved company can appeal to the Central Government or a designated authority within thirty days of receiving the order. The applicant must be given an opportunity to be heard (Section 7).
administration: The Reserve Bank of India
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force (Section 1(3)).
The Reserve Bank has the power to specify the total number of credit information companies that can be granted registration (Section 5(3)).
The Reserve Bank can exempt certain entities or cases from the provisions of the Act (Section 32).
The Act does not bar the application of other laws (Section 33).

title: THE ANDHRA PRADESH LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for the creation of Legislative Council for the State of Andhra Pradesh and for matters supplemental, incidental and consequential thereto.
scope: This act applies to the State of Andhra Pradesh. It deals with the creation and composition of the Legislative Council for the state.

key_definitions.Representation of the People Act, 1950 (: Words and expressions defined in this act have the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council Act, 2005.
Defines terms used in the Act, referencing the Representation of the People Act, 1950 for undefined terms.

main_sections.section_title: Creation of Legislative Council for Andhra Pradesh.
main_sections.description: Provides for the creation of a Legislative Council for the State of Andhra Pradesh, specifying the total number of seats (90) and their distribution among elected and nominated members. It also outlines the process for the President to determine constituencies and allot seats.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Third Schedule and Fourth Schedule of Act 43 of 1950.
main_sections.description: Amends the Representation of the People Act, 1950 by inserting an entry for Andhra Pradesh in the Third Schedule (specifying seat distribution) and the Fourth Schedule (listing local authorities for elections to the Legislative Council).

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 15A of Act 43 of 1951.
main_sections.description: Amends section 15A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to reflect that the Legislative Council is constituted under the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council Act, 2005, instead of the Legislative Councils Act, 1957.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act establishes a Legislative Council for the State of Andhra Pradesh from a date appointed by the President.

Rule 2: The Legislative Council shall have 90 seats distributed as follows: 31 for members elected by electorates under Article 171(3)(a), 8 under Article 171(3)(b), 8 under Article 171(3)(c), 31 elected by the Legislative Assembly members, and 12 nominated by the Governor.
Rule 3: The President, in consultation with the Election Commission, shall determine the constituencies, their extent, and the number of seats per constituency for elections to the Council.
Rule 4: Steps shall be taken to constitute the Council according to the provisions of this Act and the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the Election Commission and the President of India for procedural aspects.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the President's orders and amendments to existing electoral laws.

rights: Right to have a Legislative Council for the State of Andhra Pradesh.
duties: Duty to make provisions for the creation of the Legislative Council.
Duty to amend relevant schedules of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Duty to amend section 15A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
obligations: Obligation for the President to appoint a date for the creation of the Council.
Obligation for the President, after consultation with the Election Commission, to determine constituencies and seat allocations.
Obligation to take steps to constitute the Council as per the Act and other relevant laws.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The President appoints a date for the creation of the Legislative Council and inserts 'Andhra Pradesh,' into Article 168(1)(a).
Procedure 2: The President, in consultation with the Election Commission, determines constituencies, their extent, and seat allocations for the Council.
Procedure 3: Steps are taken to constitute the Council based on the determined constituencies and seat allocations, adhering to this Act and the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text. However, the 'administration' would likely fall under the purview of the Election Commission of India and the State Government of Andhra Pradesh for electoral processes.
important_notes: The Legislative Council for Andhra Pradesh came into existence on 30th March, 2007, vide notification No. G.S.R. 262(E).
The Act involves amendments to the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

title: THE MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES DEVELOPMENT ACT, 2006
purpose: To provide for facilitating the promotion and development and enhancing the competitiveness of micro, small and medium enterprises and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to micro, small, and medium enterprises in India, as defined by the Act. It also covers matters related to delayed payments to micro and small enterprises.

key_definitions.advisory_committee: The committee constituted by the Central Government under sub-section (2) of section 7.
key_definitions.appointed_day: The day following immediately after the expiry of the period of fifteen days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance of any goods or any services by a buyer from a supplier.
key_definitions.buyer: Whoever buys any goods or receives any services from a supplier for consideration.
key_definitions.enterprise: An industrial undertaking or a business concern or any other establishment, by whatever name called, engaged in the manufacture or production of goods or in providing or rendering any service or services.
key_definitions.micro_enterprise: An enterprise classified as such under sub-clause (i) of clause (a) or sub-clause (i) of clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 7.
key_definitions.small_enterprise: An enterprise classified as such under sub-clause (ii) of clause (a) or sub-clause (ii) of clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 7.
key_definitions.medium_enterprise: An enterprise classified as such under sub-clause (iii) of clause (a) or sub-clause (iii) of clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 7.
key_definitions.supplier: A micro or small enterprise, which has filed a memorandum with the authority referred to in sub-section (1) of section 8, and includes certain specified entities like the National Small Industries Corporation and State Small Industries Development Corporations.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which can be appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Advisory Committee', 'appointed day', 'buyer', 'enterprise', 'goods', 'medium enterprise', 'micro enterprise', 'National Bank', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'Reserve Bank', 'small enterprise', 'supplier', 'Small Industries Bank', and 'State Government'.

Provides for the establishment of the National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, its head office, and its composition, which includes ex-officio members and appointed members representing various government bodies, parliament, and industry associations.

Outlines the grounds and procedures for the removal of a member from the Board, including insolvency, unsound mind, refusal to act, conviction of an offence, or abuse of position, with a provision for a hearing.

Details the functions of the Board, which include examining factors affecting the promotion and development of MSMEs, reviewing government policies, making recommendations, and advising on the use of the Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Member-Secretary of Board
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Member-Secretary of the Board shall exercise such powers and perform such functions as may be prescribed.
Deals with the classification of enterprises into micro, small, and medium categories, with provisions for an Advisory Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Memorandum of micro, small and medium enterprises
main_sections.description: Requires micro, small, and medium enterprises to file a memorandum.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of buyer to make payment
main_sections.description: Establishes the liability of a buyer to make payments to micro and small enterprises for goods or services supplied.

main_sections.section_title: Date from which and rate at which interest is payable
main_sections.description: Specifies the date from which and the rate at which interest is payable on delayed payments to micro and small enterprises.

main_sections.section_title: Reference to Micro and small Enterprises Facilitation Council
main_sections.description: Provides for references to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council for resolving disputes regarding delayed payments.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Councils.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of section 8 or section 22 or section 26
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of specific sections of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules by State Government
main_sections.description: Grants State Governments the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act within their respective States.
Empowers the Central Government to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Repeals the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985 (referred to as Act 32 of 1993 in the text).

important_rules: Buyers are liable to make payments to micro and small enterprises for goods and services supplied. (Section 15)
Interest is payable on delayed payments from the 'appointed day' at a rate which is three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank. (Section 16)
Micro and small enterprises can file a memorandum with the specified authority. (Section 8)
The National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises must meet at least once every three months. (Section 3(6))
Unpaid amounts along with interest must be specified in the annual statement of accounts of the buyer. (Section 22)

penalties: Penalty for contravention of section 8 (filing of memorandum), section 22 (specification of unpaid amount with interest in annual accounts), or section 26 (appointment of officers and employees). (Section 27)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (for delayed payment issues), and potentially other authorities or courts as specified by the Act and rules. The Central Government and State Governments also have powers to make rules and remove difficulties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, references to Facilitation Councils, and penalties for non-compliance with specific provisions. The Act also establishes mechanisms for dispute resolution and the enforcement of payment obligations.

rights: Right of micro and small enterprises to receive timely payments for goods and services supplied.
Right to claim interest on delayed payments.
Right to refer disputes regarding delayed payments to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council.
Right to the promotion, development, and enhancement of competitiveness.
duties: Duty of buyers to make payments to micro and small enterprises within the specified period.
Duty of buyers to specify unpaid amounts with interest in their annual statements of accounts.
Duty of the Central and State Governments to facilitate the promotion, development, and competitiveness of MSMEs.
obligations: Obligation for enterprises to file a memorandum.
Obligation for buyers to pay interest on delayed payments.

key_procedures: Procedure for classification of enterprises into micro, small, and medium categories as per section 7.
Procedure for filing a memorandum by micro and small enterprises as per section 8.
Procedure for buyer to make payment and consequences of default, including interest accrual.
Procedure for referring disputes to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council.
Procedure for the establishment and functioning of the National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.
administration: The Central Government (Ministry or Department having administrative control of micro, small and medium enterprises) and the National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. State Governments also have a role in administering rules within their states. Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Councils are established to resolve payment disputes.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on certain other laws or provisions where specified (e.g., Section 24 regarding delayed payments).
The Act repeals the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985.
Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act by the Central Government.
The composition of the National Board includes a wide representation from government, parliament, financial institutions, and MSME associations.
The Act emphasizes promoting the competitiveness of MSMEs in addition to their promotion and development.

title: THE PONDICHERRY (ALTERATION OF NAME) ACT, 2006
purpose: To alter the name of the Union territory of Pondicherry.
scope: This Act applies to the Union territory of Pondicherry and involves amendments to the Constitution of India and other relevant laws.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette for the coming into force of this Act.
key_definitions.appropriate_government: The Central Government, and as respects a law relating to a matter enumerated in the State List or the Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution in so far as any such matter is applicable in relation to the Union territory of Puducherry, also the administrator of the Union territory of Puducherry.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, Ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or any part of the Union territory of Pondicherry.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'appropriate Government', and 'law'.

main_sections.section_title: Alteration of name of the Union territory of Pondicherry
main_sections.description: States that as from the appointed day, the Union territory of Pondicherry shall be known as the Union territory of Puducherry.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Part VIII of the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends Part VIII of the Constitution by substituting the word 'Puducherry' for 'Pondicherry' wherever it occurs.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution under the heading 'II. THE UNION TERRITORIES' by substituting 'Puducherry' for 'Pondicherry' in entry 6.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution under the heading 'TABLE' by substituting 'Puducherry' for 'Pondicherry' in entry 30.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 20 of 1963
main_sections.description: Amends section 2 of the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, by substituting 'Puducherry' for 'Pondicherry' in sub-section (1), clause (h).

Empowers the appropriate Government to make adaptations and modifications to any law made before the appointed day to give effect to the name alteration. It also states that this does not prevent Parliament or the Legislative Assembly from amending such laws.

Allows courts, tribunals, or authorities to construe laws made before the appointed day in a manner necessary or proper, even if no specific adaptation has been made under section 8, without affecting the substance of the law.

Specifies that in legal proceedings pending before the appointed day, any reference to the administrator of the Union territory of Pondicherry shall be construed as a reference to the administrator of the Union territory of Puducherry.

important_rules: The Union territory of Pondicherry shall be known as the Union territory of Puducherry from the appointed day.
The Central Government may, by notification, appoint the date for the commencement of the Act.
The appropriate Government may adapt or modify existing laws to reflect the name change within one year of the appointed day.
Courts and tribunals can interpret existing laws in a way that gives effect to the name change, even if no specific adaptation is made.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Appropriate Government (Central Government or Administrator of Puducherry for specific matters)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through adaptation and modification of existing laws, and by construing legal proceedings with the updated name.

rights: The right to have the Union territory referred to by its new name, Puducherry.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to appoint the commencement date.
Duty of the appropriate Government to adapt laws.
obligations: Obligation to use the name 'Puducherry' in relation to the Union territory from the appointed day.
Obligation for legal proceedings to recognize the change in the administrator's designation.

key_procedures: Appointment of the commencement date by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Adaptation or modification of existing laws by the appropriate Government by order within one year of the appointed day.
Construction of laws by courts, tribunals, or authorities if no adaptation is made.
administration: Central Government (for appointing commencement date and general administration/adaptation of laws), and the Administrator of Puducherry (for laws relating to State/Concurrent List matters applicable in Puducherry).
important_notes: The commencement date was October 1, 2006, vide notification No. S.O. 1627(E), dated September 28, 2006.
The Act makes consequential amendments to the Constitution of India (Part VIII, First Schedule, Fourth Schedule) and the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963.

title: THE UTTARANCHAL (ALTERATION OF NAME) ACT, 2006
purpose: To alter the name of the State of Uttaranchal to the State of Uttarakhand.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Uttaranchal and its legal framework. It impacts the Constitution of India and any laws applicable to the state.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date appointed by the Central Government for the coming into force of this Act.
key_definitions.appropriate_government: For laws related to List I of the Seventh Schedule, it's the Central Government; for other laws, it's the State Government.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, Ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification, or other instrument having the force of law.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'appropriate Government', and 'law'.

main_sections.section_title: Alteration of name of the State of Uttaranchal
main_sections.description: Declares that as of the appointed day, the State of Uttaranchal shall be known as the State of Uttarakhand.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to replace 'Uttaranchal' with 'Uttarakhand' in the entry for the state.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution to replace 'Uttaranchal' with 'Uttarakhand' in the relevant entry.

Grants the appropriate Government the power to make necessary adaptations and modifications to any law made before the appointed day, within one year of the appointed day, to give effect to the name change.

Empowers courts, tribunals, or authorities to construe laws made before the appointed day in a manner necessary for their enforcement, even if no specific adaptation has been made, without affecting the substance of the law.

States that in any legal proceedings pending before the appointed day where the State of Uttaranchal is a party, the State of Uttarakhand shall be deemed to be substituted for the State of Uttaranchal.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State of Uttaranchal shall be known as the State of Uttarakhand from the appointed day.
Rule 2: The name 'Uttaranchal' in the First and Fourth Schedules of the Constitution shall be substituted with 'Uttarakhand'.
Rule 3: The appropriate Government may adapt or modify existing laws to reflect the name change within one year of the appointed day.
Rule 4: Legal proceedings involving the State of Uttaranchal will continue with the State of Uttarakhand substituted as a party.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and State Government, as defined by 'appropriate Government'.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the administration of this Act, adaptation of laws, and legal proceedings. The Act itself does not specify direct penalties for non-compliance with the name change but relies on the legal framework and the power to adapt laws.

rights: The right of the State to be recognized and referred to by its new name, Uttarakhand.
The right of the Central Government to appoint the 'appointed day' for the Act to come into force.
The right of the appropriate Government to adapt laws.
The right of courts, tribunals, and authorities to construe laws as necessary for enforcement.
duties: The duty of all entities to refer to the state as Uttarakhand from the appointed day.
The duty of the Central Government to notify the appointed day.
The duty of the appropriate Government to make necessary adaptations to laws.
obligations: Obligation to substitute 'Uttaranchal' with 'Uttarakhand' in official documents, legal instruments, and the Constitution.
Obligation to ensure legal proceedings reflect the change in the state's name.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Central Government issues a notification to appoint the 'appointed day' for the Act to come into force.
Procedure 2: The appropriate Government issues orders to adapt or modify existing laws to reflect the name change, within one year of the appointed day.
Procedure 3: Courts, tribunals, or authorities may construe laws in a manner that aligns with the name change, even without explicit adaptation.
administration: The Central Government and the State Government, as determined by the definition of 'appropriate Government'.
important_notes: The Act was brought into force on January 1, 2007, vide notification No. GSR 779(E), dated December 29, 2006.
The adaptation of laws under section 6 is permissible for one year from the appointed day.
The power to adapt laws does not prevent a competent legislature from amending them independently.

title: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006
purpose: To provide for the reservation in admission of students belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and the Other Backward Classes of citizens, to certain Central Educational Institutions established, maintained or aided by the Central Government, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to Central Educational Institutions established, maintained, or aided by the Central Government.  Covers admissions to teaching or instruction in branches of study leading to bachelor, master, and doctoral levels. Exempts certain categories of institutions and courses.

key_definitions.academic_session: The period in a calendar year, or a part thereof, during which a Central Educational Institution is open for teaching or instruction in any branch of study or faculty.
key_definitions.annual_permitted_strength: The number of seats, in a course or programme for teaching or instruction in each branch of study or faculty authorised by an appropriate authority for admission of students to a Central Educational Institution.
key_definitions.appropriate_authority: The University Grants Commission, the Bar Council of India, the Medical Council of India, the All India Council for Technical Education or any other authority or body established by or under a Central Act for the determination, coordination or maintenance of the standards of higher education in any Central Educational Institution.
key_definitions.Central_Educational_Institution: Includes universities established by Central Act, institutions of national importance set up by Parliament, deemed universities maintained or aided by the Central Government, institutions maintained by or receiving aid from the Central Government and affiliated to Central Act universities or national importance institutions, and educational institutions set up by the Central Government under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.faculty: The faculty of a Central Educational Institution.
key_definitions.Minority_Educational_Institution: An institution established and administered by the minorities under clause (1) of article 30 of the Constitution and so declared by an Act of Parliament or by the Central Government or declared as a Minority Educational Institution under the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions Act, 2004.
key_definitions.Other_Backward_Classes: Classes of citizens who are socially and educationally backward, and are so determined by the Central Government.
key_definitions.Scheduled_Castes: Scheduled Castes notified under article 341 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.Scheduled_Tribes: Scheduled Tribes notified under article 342 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.specified_north_eastern_region: The area comprising of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura and the tribal areas of Assam referred to in the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution.
key_definitions.State_seats: Seats, if any, out of the annual permitted strength in each branch of study or faculty as are earmarked to be filled from amongst the eligible students of the State in which such institution is situated.
key_definitions.teaching_or_instruction_in_any_branch_of: Teaching or instruction in a branch of study leading to three principal levels of qualifications at bachelor (undergraduate) masters (postgraduate) and doctoral levels.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006'.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'academic session', 'annual permitted strength', 'appropriate authority', 'Central Educational Institution', 'faculty', 'Minority Educational Institution', 'Other Backward Classes', 'Scheduled Castes', 'Scheduled Tribes', 'specified north-eastern region', 'State seats', and 'teaching or instruction in any branch of study'.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of seats in Central Educational Institutions
main_sections.description: Specifies the percentage of seats to be reserved for Scheduled Castes (15%), Scheduled Tribes (7.5%), and Other Backward Classes (27%) out of the annual permitted strength in each branch of study or faculty. Includes provisos for specific situations, particularly concerning State seats in tribal areas and when existing reservations exceed 50%.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply in certain cases
main_sections.description: Exempts certain institutions and courses from the provisions of Section 3. These include institutions of excellence, research institutions, institutions of national and strategic importance specified in the Schedule, Minority Educational Institutions, and courses/programmes at high levels of specialization (including post-doctoral) as specified by the Central Government.

Requires Central Educational Institutions to increase their annual permitted strength over and above the existing numbers so that the number of seats available for unreserved categories is not less than the number available or actually filled in the academic session immediately preceding the Act's commencement. Allows for a phased increase over a maximum of six years in certain circumstances due to limitations, ensuring commensurate reservation for OBCs.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of seats in admissions to begin in calendar year, 2008
main_sections.description: Mandates that Central Educational Institutions must take all necessary steps to implement the provisions of Sections 3, 4, and 5 for admissions commencing on and from the calendar year 2008.
Stipulates that every notification issued under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days. Parliament has the power to modify or annul the notification.

important_rules: Rule 1: 15% of seats in Central Educational Institutions must be reserved for Scheduled Castes.
Rule 2: 7.5% of seats in Central Educational Institutions must be reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
Rule 3: 27% of seats in Central Educational Institutions must be reserved for Other Backward Classes.
Rule 4: Central Educational Institutions must increase their seat capacity to maintain the number of unreserved seats at the level of the preceding academic session.
Rule 5: The reservation policy will come into effect for admissions commencing from the calendar year 2008.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the 'appropriate authority' (defined as UGC, Bar Council of India, Medical Council of India, AICTE, or similar bodies).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the Central Government, laid before Parliament for approval. Institutions are required to take necessary steps to implement the provisions. The Central Government can amend the Schedule of exempted institutions.

rights: Right of students belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes to reservation in admission to Central Educational Institutions.
Right of Parliament to modify or annul notifications issued under the Act.
duties: Duty of Central Educational Institutions to provide reservation in admission as per the Act.
Duty of Central Educational Institutions to increase their annual permitted strength to accommodate reservation.
Duty of the Central Government to specify institutions of excellence and strategic importance that are exempted.
Duty to lay notifications before Parliament.
obligations: Obligation of Central Educational Institutions to adhere to the reservation percentages and timelines.
Obligation of the Central Government to consult appropriate authorities when specifying exemptions.
Obligation to maintain standards of education while implementing reservation.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Identification and notification of Central Educational Institutions subject to the Act.
Procedure 2: Calculation and earmarking of reserved seats (15% SC, 7.5% ST, 27% OBC) out of the annual permitted strength.
Procedure 3: Mandatory increase of seats in Central Educational Institutions to maintain the quantum of unreserved seats.
Procedure 4: Phased increase of seats over a maximum of six years in cases of limitations, with commensurate OBC reservation.
Procedure 5: Commencement of reservation policy for admissions from the calendar year 2008.
Procedure 6: Issuance of notifications by the Central Government and their laying before Parliament for approval.
administration: Central Government (in consultation with appropriate authorities like UGC, AICTE, etc.)
important_notes: The Act does not apply to Minority Educational Institutions.

Certain 'institutions of excellence, research institutions, institutions of national and strategic importance' are exempted, as specified in the Schedule (which can be amended by the Central Government).
Courses or programmes at high levels of specialization, including post-doctoral levels, can be exempted.
The reservation policy for State seats in a Central Educational Institution situated in tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule will be governed by the State Government's policy.
If existing reservations for SC/ST exceed 50% of the annual permitted strength, OBC reservation may be restricted or not applied, with exceptions for the North-Eastern region.

title: THE ENGLISH AND FOREIGN LANGUAGES UNIVERSITY ACT, 2006
