purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching University for the promotion and development of English and other Foreign Languages and their Literature, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

scope.geographical: The jurisdiction of the University shall extend to the whole of India.
scope.subject_matter: Teaching of English and Foreign Languages and their Literature, instructional, research and extension facilities, training of language teachers, expertise in language and teacher education for foreign professionals, indigenous language proficiency testing, innovative teaching-learning materials, inter-disciplinary studies and research in Literary and Cultural Studies, and intercultural understanding of civilizations.

key_definitions.academic_council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic_staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.distance_education_system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more such means.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.university: The Central Institute of English, Hyderabad Society founded by the Central Government at Hyderabad in 1958 as a Society registered under the Hyderabad Society Registration Act, 1350 (Act 1 of 1350 Fasli) which was renamed as Central Institute of English and Foreign Languages, Hyderabad Society in 1972 and declared in 1973 as an Institution deemed to be a University under section 3 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956 (3 of 1956); and which is incorporated as a university under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act and the Statutes made thereunder.

Establishes the University by the name 'The English and Foreign Languages University', specifies its headquarters at Hyderabad and campuses at Lucknow and Shillong, and outlines its perpetual succession and common seal.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of the Central Institute of English and Foreign Languages, Hyderabad Society and transfer of all the properties and effect of establishment of the University
main_sections.description: Details the dissolution of the Society, transfer of its properties, rights, debts, liabilities, and obligations to the University, and the continuity of employment for existing staff.
Outlines the primary objectives of the University, focusing on the dissemination of knowledge, research, teacher training, and intercultural understanding in English and Foreign Languages.

Enumerate the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction, granting degrees, organizing extramural studies, conferring honorary degrees, offering distance education, establishing academic positions, collaborating with other institutions, and managing property.
Specifies that the University's jurisdiction extends to the entire country.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creeds
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all individuals regardless of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, prohibiting any religious tests for appointment, admission, or privileges. It allows for special provisions for women, persons with disabilities, and weaker sections.
Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and grants the Visitor the power to appoint individuals to review the University's work and progress.

important_rules: Rule 1: The University shall be open to all persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class, and no test of religious belief or profession shall be imposed for appointment, admission, graduation, or privileges, with exceptions for special provisions for women, persons with disabilities, and weaker sections.
Rule 2: The President of India shall be the Visitor of the University.
Rule 3: The University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal, and shall sue and be sued by its name.

Rule 4: All properties, rights, debts, liabilities, and obligations of the dissolved Central Institute of English and Foreign Languages, Hyderabad Society shall be transferred to and vested in the University.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University's Executive Council and other specified authorities, with oversight from the Visitor (President of India) and Central Government where applicable.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of powers vested in the University's authorities as defined in the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations, including disciplinary measures for students and employees, and the oversight functions of the Visitor.

rights: Right to receive instruction, research, and extension facilities in English and Foreign Languages.
Right to be admitted and graduate without religious or caste-based discrimination.
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases.
Existing employees have rights to pension and gratuity as if the Act had not been passed.
duties: Duty to disseminate and advance knowledge in English and Foreign Languages.
Duty to train language teachers.
Duty to provide expertise to foreign professionals.
Duty to evolve indigenous language proficiency testing.
Duty to provide for innovative teaching-learning materials.
Duty to promote inter-disciplinary studies and research.
obligations: The University has an obligation to apply all transferred properties and rights to its established objects.
The University has an obligation to discharge and satisfy all debts, liabilities, and obligations of the dissolved Society.
The University has an obligation to uphold the principles of non-discrimination in admissions and appointments.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette.
Establishment of the University: Done by the Act itself, with headquarters and campuses specified.
Transfer of Society's assets and liabilities: Occurs automatically upon commencement of the Act.
Visitor's Review: The Visitor can appoint persons to review the University's work and progress, upon which the Visitor may take action after consulting the Executive Council.
Making of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations: Governed by specific sections (28, 30, 31) and to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
administration: The Act establishes 'The English and Foreign Languages University' as a statutory body. The administration is vested in various officers and authorities of the University, including the Visitor, Chief Rector, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Executive Council, and Academic Council. The Central Government's role is evident in initial notifications and approvals for certain actions (e.g., establishing campuses outside India, disposing of property, borrowing money).
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the 57th Year of the Republic of India.
The Act came into force on 3rd August 2007.
The Act dissolves the previous Society and establishes a new University, ensuring continuity of operations and employee rights.

title: The Sports Broadcasting Signals (Mandatory Sharing with Prasar Bharati) Act, 2007
purpose: To provide access to the largest number of listeners and viewers, on a free to air basis, of sporting events of national importance through mandatory sharing of sports broadcasting signals with Prasar Bharati and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Covers the mandatory sharing of sports broadcasting signals for sporting events of national importance with Prasar Bharati.

key_definitions.broadcaster: Any person who provides a content broadcasting service and includes a broadcasting network service provider when they manage and operate their own television or radio channel service.
key_definitions.broadcasting: Assembling and programming any form of communication content (signs, signals, writing, pictures, images, sounds) and transmitting it electronically via electromagnetic waves or digital data to be accessible through receiving devices.
key_definitions.sporting events of national importance: Such national or international sporting events, held in India or abroad, as may be notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette to be of national importance.
key_definitions.Prasar Bharati: The Corporation known as Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) Act, 1990.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement (deemed to have come into force on 11th November, 2005).

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including broadcaster, broadcasting, broadcasting service, broadcasting network service, content, content broadcasting service, Prasar Bharati, and sporting events of national importance. It also references definitions from other relevant acts if not defined herein.

main_sections.section_title: Mandatory sharing of certain sports broadcasting signals
main_sections.description: Mandates that content rights owners or broadcasting service providers must share live broadcasting signals (without advertisements) of sporting events of national importance with Prasar Bharati for re-transmission on its terrestrial and DTH networks. It also specifies the advertisement revenue sharing ratio between the rights owner/holder and Prasar Bharati.

Empowers the Central Government to specify penalties for violations of terms and conditions related to signal sharing, including suspension or revocation of licenses. The maximum pecuniary penalty is one crore rupees. It includes provisions for a reasonable opportunity to be heard before imposing penalties and a saving clause for acts or omissions prior to the Ordinance.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to issue Guidelines
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue Guidelines for the mandatory sharing of broadcasting signals with Prasar Bharati for sporting events of national importance. It also validates Guidelines issued before the Ordinance.

Deems the Guidelines issued by the Central Government on November 11, 2005 (Downlinking) and December 2, 2005 (Uplinking) for mandatory sharing of sports broadcasting signals as valid under this Act. It also validates any actions taken by the Central Government or Prasar Bharati in pursuance of these Guidelines.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and Guidelines to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that all rules and Guidelines made or issued under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modification or annulment by Parliament.

States that relevant provisions from the Guidelines for Downlinking and Uplinking issued on November 11, 2005, and December 2, 2005, respectively, shall remain in force until fresh Guidelines are issued under this Act.

Repeals the Sports Broadcasting Signals (Mandatory Sharing with Prasar Bharati) Ordinance, 2007. Actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule: No content rights owner or broadcasting service provider shall carry a live television broadcast or radio commentary of sporting events of national importance unless it simultaneously shares the live broadcasting signal (without advertisements) with Prasar Bharati for re-transmission. (Section 3(1))

Rule: Advertisement revenue sharing between the content rights owner/holder and Prasar Bharati shall be in the ratio of not less than 75:25 for television coverage and 50:50 for radio coverage. (Section 3(2))
Rule: The Central Government may specify a percentage of revenue received by Prasar Bharati to be utilized for broadcasting other sporting events. (Section 3(3))

Rule: Any rule or Guideline made or issued under this Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a total period of thirty days, with provisions for modification or annulment by Parliament. (Section 8)

penalties: Suspension or revocation of licence, permission or registration for violation of terms and conditions specified under section 3.
Pecuniary penalty not exceeding one crore rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through specified penalties, including license suspension/revocation and pecuniary fines. Also through rules and guidelines issued by the Central Government.

rights: Right of the public to access sporting events of national importance on a free-to-air basis.
Right of Prasar Bharati to receive broadcasting signals of sporting events of national importance for re-transmission.
duties: Duty of content rights owners and broadcasting service providers to share live broadcasting signals of sporting events of national importance with Prasar Bharati.
Duty of the Central Government to issue Guidelines and make rules for the effective implementation of the Act.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to specified terms and conditions for signal sharing.
Obligation to comply with the advertisement revenue sharing ratio.
Obligation to provide a reasonable opportunity to service providers before imposing penalties.

key_procedures: Procedure for mandatory sharing of broadcasting signals: Content rights owners/broadcasters must share live signals of national importance sporting events (without ads) with Prasar Bharati for re-transmission. (Section 3(1))
Procedure for imposing penalties: Central Government may specify penalties for violations. No penalty shall be imposed without giving a reasonable opportunity to the service provider. (Section 4)
administration: Central Government (through its power to issue Guidelines and make rules)
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on 11th November, 2005.
Guidelines issued before the Ordinance (Nov 2005 and Dec 2005) are validated and deemed to have been issued under this Act.
No act or omission prior to the Ordinance (Nov 11, 2005 to Ordinance promulgation date) is subject to penalties under this Act.

Words and expressions not defined in this Act are to have meanings assigned in the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997, the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, and the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933.

title: The National Rural Employment Guarantee (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 2007
purpose: To provide for the extension of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh). It extends the provisions of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, and its associated rules, orders, and schemes to this region.

key_definitions.principal Act: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 (42 of 2005).

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the National Rural Employment Guarantee (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 2007. It also specifies that the Act will come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette, allowing for different commencement dates for different areas within the State.

main_sections.section_title: Extension and amendment of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
main_sections.description: This section formally extends the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, along with all its rules, orders, and schemes, to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It also amends the principal Act by omitting the words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' from sub-section (2) of section 1, thereby removing the exclusion of Jammu and Kashmir.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of reference to a law not in force in Jammu and Kashmir
main_sections.description: This section clarifies how references to laws mentioned in the principal Act should be interpreted in relation to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. If a law mentioned in the principal Act is not in force in Jammu and Kashmir, any such reference will be construed as a reference to the corresponding law, if any, that is in force in that State.

important_rules: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, and all its associated rules, orders, and schemes are extended to and shall be in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir from the applicability of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, is removed.
References in the principal Act to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir shall be interpreted as references to corresponding laws in force in the State.
key_procedures: The Central Government will appoint a date for the commencement of the Act through a notification in the Official Gazette. Different dates may be appointed for different areas.
References to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir within the principal Act will be interpreted as references to corresponding laws in force in the State.
administration: Central Government (for appointing commencement dates and issuing notifications)
important_notes: The Act was made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.

title: THE CARRIAGE BY ROAD ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for the regulation of common carriers, limiting their liability and declaration of value of goods delivered to them to determine their liability for loss of, or damage to, such goods occasioned by the negligence or criminal acts of themselves, their servants or agents and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh). It regulates persons engaged in the business of common carriers, which includes collecting, storing, forwarding, distributing, or transporting goods for hire by motorized transport on road, for all persons un discriminatingly. This also includes goods booking companies, contractors, agents, brokers, and courier agencies engaged in door-to-door transportation of documents, goods, or articles.

key_definitions.common_carrier: A person engaged in the business of collecting, storing, forwarding, or distributing goods to be carried by goods carriages under a goods receipt or transporting for hire of goods from place to place by motorised transport on road, for all persons un discriminatingly. It includes goods booking companies, contractors, agents, brokers, and courier agencies engaged in door-to-door transportation of documents, goods, or articles, but excludes the Government.
key_definitions.consignee: The person named as consignee in the goods forwarding note.
key_definitions.consignment: Documents, goods, or articles entrusted by the consignor to the common carrier for carriage, the description or details of which are given in the goods forwarding note.
key_definitions.consignor: A person, named as consignor in the goods forwarding note, by whom or on whose behalf the documents, goods, or articles covered by such forwarding note are entrusted to the common carrier for carriage thereof.
key_definitions.goods: Includes containers, pallets, or similar articles of transport used to consolidate goods; and animals or livestock.
key_definitions.person: Includes any association or body of persons, whether incorporated or not, a road transport booking company, contractor, and an agent or a broker carrying on the business of a common carrier.
key_definitions.registering_authority: A State Transport Authority or a Regional Transport Authority constituted under section 68 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
key_definitions.registration: The registration granted or renewed under sub-section (5) of section 4.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir), and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'common carrier', 'consignee', 'consignment', 'consignor', 'goods', 'goods forwarding note', 'goods receipt', 'person', 'prescribed', 'registering authority', and 'registration'.

main_sections.section_title: Persons not to engage in business of common carrier without registration
main_sections.description: Mandates that no person can engage in the business of a common carrier without a certificate of registration. It also specifies timelines for existing common carriers to apply for registration.

main_sections.section_title: Application for grant or renewal of registration
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for applying for the grant or renewal of a certificate of registration. It details the application process, the information required, fees, and the conditions the applicant must fulfill. It also specifies the validity of the certificate and the holder's responsibilities regarding branch offices, main office shifting, and submission of annual returns.

Details the grounds and procedures for suspending or cancelling a certificate of registration. This can occur due to failure to comply with provisions (like not rectifying issues within a given period) or due to specific complaints from consignors regarding non-issuance of receipts, non-disclosure of whereabouts, detention of goods, unreasonable charges, or non-payment to truck owners. It also addresses violations related to gross vehicle weight.

Provides the right to appeal against orders of the registering authority refusing, suspending, or revoking a registration. Appeals are to be made to the State Transport Appellate Tribunal within a specified period and with prescribed fees.
Requires the State Transport Authority to submit an annual return to the Ministry or Department of the Central Government dealing with road transport and highways.
Defines the general liability of a common carrier for loss or damage to goods entrusted to them.

main_sections.section_title: Notice for institution of a suit
main_sections.description: Specifies the requirement to give prior notice before instituting a suit against a common carrier.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for contravention in relation to non-registration, carrying goods of dangerous or hazardous nature, or prohibited goods
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishments for various contraventions, including operating without registration, carrying dangerous or hazardous goods, or carrying prohibited goods.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and provisions saved.

important_rules: No person shall engage in the business of a common carrier after the commencement of this Act unless they have been granted a certificate of registration (Section 3(1)).
Common carriers must issue a goods receipt for every consignment (implied by Section 9).
Common carriers must not load motor vehicles beyond the gross vehicle weight mentioned in the registration certificate (Section 4(8)).
Common carriers are liable for loss or damage to goods entrusted to them (Section 10).
Common carriers are responsible for the safe carriage of goods (Section 17).

penalties: Punishment for contravention related to non-registration, carrying dangerous or hazardous goods, or prohibited goods (Section 18).
Penalty prescribed under Section 194 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, for violation of gross vehicle weight provisions (Section 5(3)).
Revocation of certificate of registration for specified contraventions (Section 5).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registering authorities (State Transport Authority or Regional Transport Authority), and any other authority authorized under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration and renewal processes, imposition of penalties for violations, suspension or cancellation of registration, and potential legal action through suits after issuing notice.

rights: Right of appeal against orders of the registering authority (Section 6).
Right to be heard before registration is refused or cancelled (Section 4(5), Section 5(4)).
Right of the common carrier in case of consignee's default (Section 15).
duties: Duty to obtain registration to operate as a common carrier (Section 3).
Duty to maintain a register as prescribed (Section 4(7)(a)).
Duty to display the certificate of registration at the office (Section 4(7)(d)).
Duty to submit annual returns (Section 4(7)(c)).
Duty to not load vehicles beyond gross vehicle weight (Section 4(8)).
Duty to complete delivery and transactions for already accepted consignments even after revocation of registration (Section 5(6)).
obligations: Obligation to apply for registration within specified timelines for existing businesses (Section 3(2)).
Obligation to provide a goods forwarding note and goods receipt (implied by Sections 8 and 9).
Obligation to comply with conditions specified in the certificate of registration (Section 4(5)).
Obligation to surrender the certificate of registration upon revocation (Section 5(6)).
Obligation to obtain a declaration of no outstanding liability before surrendering a certificate (Section 5(7)).

key_procedures: Application for grant or renewal of a certificate of registration, including details of branch offices, and satisfying prescribed conditions (Section 4).
Procedure for refusal of registration or renewal, including giving the applicant an opportunity to be heard and providing written reasons within a specific timeframe (Section 4(5)).
Procedure for suspension or cancellation of registration, involving notice, opportunity to rectify, and enquiry (Section 5).
Appeal procedure against orders of the registering authority (Section 6).
Procedure for the common carrier to claim rights in case of consignee's default (Section 15).
administration: The Ministry or Department of the Central Government dealing with road transport and highways, and the Transport Research Wing of this Ministry/Department are involved in receiving annual returns. Registering authorities (State/Regional Transport Authorities) administer the registration process.
important_notes: The Act was extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by notification.
The Act defines 'person' broadly to include associations and bodies, not just individuals.
The Act provides for the possibility of compounding of offences (Section 19).

title: THE TYRE CORPORATION OF INDIA LIMITED (DISINVESTMENT OF OWNERSHIP) ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for disinvestment of the Government's equity in the Tyre Corporation of India Limited and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, enabling private sector investment for optimal utilization of facilities and ensuring public interest through the continued manufacture, production, and distribution of essential articles.
scope: This Act applies to the Tyre Corporation of India Limited, Kolkata, and its shares. It concerns the disinvestment of the Government's ownership in this company. Geographically, it is enacted by the Parliament of India and relates to a company based in India.

key_definitions.the company: Refers to the Tyre Corporation of India Limited.
key_definitions.disinvestment: The transfer, exchange, or relinquishment of shares in the company by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Tyre Corporation of India Limited (Disinvestment of Ownership) Act, 2007'.

Empowers the Central Government, upon the recommendation of the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises, to order the disinvestment of shares in the Tyre Corporation of India Limited. The order specifies the terms and conditions for the transfer, exchange, or relinquishment of these shares to any person.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of consideration for disinvestment in the company
main_sections.description: Details the payment of consideration for the transfer and vesting of shares. The consideration is to be paid to the Central Government by the transferee, taking into account the optimum valuation of the company's land, assets, and liabilities as specified by the Central Government. The manner of payment is to be agreed upon by the transferor, the company, and the transferee.

Outlines the methods by which disinvestment of shares can be effected as specified in the Central Government's order. These methods include public offer, preferential allotment, private placement, or directing the company to make a further issue of equity capital.

main_sections.section_title: Provision in respect of officers and other employees of the company
main_sections.description: Specifies that officers and employees (except Chairman and Directors) serving immediately before disinvestment will continue in service on their existing terms and conditions for a period of three years from the disinvestment date. Employees who opt not to continue in service are deemed to have resigned.

Declares that the provisions of this Act will prevail over any inconsistent provisions in the Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers, Limited (Nationalisation) Act, 1984, or any other law in force.

important_rules: Rule 1: Disinvestment of shares in the Tyre Corporation of India Limited can be ordered by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises.
Rule 2: Consideration for disinvestment must be paid to the Central Government, based on an optimized valuation of the company's assets and liabilities.
Rule 3: Officers and employees (excluding Chairman and Directors) will continue their employment for three years post-disinvestment on existing terms.
Rule 4: This Act supersedes any conflicting provisions in the Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers, Limited (Nationalisation) Act, 1984, or other laws.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the Central Government under Section 2, specifying terms and conditions for disinvestment and methods of disinvestment.

rights: Right of the Central Government to disinvest equity in the company.
Right of employees to continue service for three years on existing terms.
Right of employees to opt out of service, with deemed resignation.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to ensure optimum utilization of facilities and public interest.
Duty of transferees to pay consideration as agreed upon.
Duty of the company to facilitate disinvestment as directed.
Duty of officers and employees to continue service unless they opt out.
obligations: Obligation to pay consideration for shares based on valuation.
Obligation to adhere to terms and conditions of disinvestment.
Obligation to comply with the overriding effect of this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Central Government, upon recommendation, issues an order for disinvestment, specifying terms and conditions for transfer, exchange, or relinquishment of shares.
Procedure 2: Consideration for disinvestment is paid by the transferee to the Central Government, with the manner of payment agreed upon by relevant parties.
Procedure 3: Disinvestment can be effected through public offer, preferential allotment, private placement, or company-directed equity issuance, as specified in the government order.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act specifically mentions that the Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited were nationalized in 1984 and transferred to the Tyre Corporation of India Limited.
The purpose of disinvestment is to enable private sector investment for securing optimum utilization of facilities.
The overriding effect of this Act ensures its primacy over the 1984 Nationalisation Act and other existing laws.

title: THE ARMED FORCES TRIBUNAL ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for the adjudication or trial by the Armed Forces Tribunal of disputes and complaints related to commission, appointments, enrolment, and conditions of service for persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957, and the Air Force Act, 1950. It also covers appeals arising from court martial proceedings under these Acts and matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to all persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957, and the Air Force Act, 1950. It also extends to retired personnel of these forces and their dependants, heirs, and successors, concerning their service matters.

key_definitions.Administrative Member: A member of the Tribunal who is not a Judicial Member.
key_definitions.Judicial Member: A member of the Tribunal appointed as such, including the Chairperson, who possesses qualifications specified in sub-section (2) of section 6 (i.e., is or has been a Judge of a High Court).
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Tribunal.
key_definitions.Member: A member (Judicial or Administrative) of the Tribunal, including the Chairperson.
key_definitions.Tribunal: The Armed Forces Tribunal established under section 4.
key_definitions.service matters: All matters relating to the conditions of service for persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957, and the Air Force Act, 1950. This includes remuneration, pension, tenure, promotion, termination, and summary disposal/trials where dismissal is awarded, but excludes certain orders under specific sections of the Acts, transfers/postings, leave, and summary court martial except where punishment is dismissal or imprisonment for more than three months.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification.

Specifies that the Act applies to all persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957, and the Air Force Act, 1950, as well as retired personnel and their dependants regarding service matters.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including Administrative Member, Judicial Member, Chairperson, Member, Tribunal, service matters, court martial, etc.
Empowers the Central Government to establish the Armed Forces Tribunal by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Composition of Tribunal and Benches thereof
main_sections.description: Outlines the composition of the Tribunal (Chairperson, Judicial Members, Administrative Members) and the formation and functioning of its Benches. It also details the Chairperson's powers regarding Benches and member transfers.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority in service matters
main_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction, powers, and authority of the Tribunal in service matters.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority in matters of appeal against court martial
main_sections.description: Specifies the Tribunal's jurisdiction, powers, and authority concerning appeals against court martial findings or sentences.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Stipulates that civil courts shall have no jurisdiction over matters within the Tribunal's purview.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in matters covered by it.

important_rules: Rule: Applicability to persons subject to Army Act, Navy Act, and Air Force Act, including retired personnel and their dependants for service matters.
Rule: The Tribunal shall consist of a Chairperson and a specified number of Judicial and Administrative Members.
Rule: Benches of the Tribunal shall ordinarily sit at Delhi (Principal Bench) and other specified locations.
Rule: Chairperson and Members hold office for a term of four years, eligible for re-appointment, with age limits specified.

Rule: On ceasing office, the Chairperson is ineligible for further government employment. A Member is eligible for other Tribunals but not other government employment. Neither can appear before the Tribunal.
Rule: Civil courts are excluded from exercising jurisdiction over matters the Tribunal is empowered to determine.

penalties: Power to punish for contempt (Section 19).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Armed Forces Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the adjudication and trial of disputes, and by hearing appeals against court martial orders. Enforcement of Tribunal orders is also detailed (Section 29).

rights: Right of applicant or appellant to take assistance of a legal practitioner (Section 25).
Right to appeal to the Supreme Court (Section 30).
duties: Persons subject to the specified Acts have disputes and complaints adjudicated by the Tribunal.
The Central Government has a duty to establish the Tribunal and provide staff.
Chairperson and Members have duties related to their office, including not holding other offices and not appearing before the Tribunal after ceasing their tenure.
obligations: Retired personnel and dependants have an obligation to approach the Tribunal for their service matters.
Chairperson and Members are subject to rules regarding resignation, removal, and terms of service.

key_procedures: Application not to be admitted unless other remedies exhausted (Section 21).
Procedure and powers of the Tribunal (Section 23).
Right of applicant or appellant to take assistance of a legal practitioner and of Government to appoint counsel (Section 25).
Condition as to making of interim order (Section 26).
Power of Chairperson to transfer cases from one Bench to another (Section 27).
Decision to be by majority (Section 28).
Execution of order of Tribunal (Section 29).
Appeal to Supreme Court (Section 30).
Leave to appeal (Section 31).
Condonation (Section 32).
administration: The Central Government is responsible for establishing the Tribunal, appointing its staff, and making rules. The Chairperson of the Tribunal exercises financial and administrative powers over the Benches.
important_notes: The Act came into force on June 15, 2008 (vide notification No. S.O. 14(E), dated 13th June, 2008).

Section 9A specifies that qualifications, terms, and conditions for Chairperson and Members appointed after the commencement of Part XIV of Chapter VI of the Finance Act, 2017, are governed by that Act's Section 184. Those appointed before that date continue to be governed by the Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning it takes precedence over other laws in its domain.

Certain matters are explicitly excluded from the definition of 'service matters', such as specific orders under sections 18 of the Army/Air Force Acts and section 15(1) of the Navy Act, and transfers/postings, and leave of any kind.

title: THE JAWAHARLAL INSTITUTE OF POST-GRADUATE MEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH, PUDUCHERRY ACT, 2008
purpose: To declare the Institution known as the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, and its operations concerning medical education, research, and healthcare services. It establishes the Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, granting it powers to acquire property, contract, sue, and be sued. The Act also covers the composition, powers, and functions of the Institute's governing bodies, staff, and the granting of medical degrees and diplomas.

key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Institute referred to in section 16.
key_definitions.Governing Body: The Governing Body of the Institute.
key_definitions.Institute: The institution known as the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, incorporated under this Act.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Institute.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.specified: Specified by regulations made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, as an institution of national importance.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Fund', 'Governing Body', 'Institute', 'member', 'prescribed', and 'specified'.

Constitutes the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowering it to acquire property, contract, and sue and be sued.

Outlines the composition of the Institute, specifying ex officio members (including government secretaries, vice-chancellors, directors) and nominated members (including scientists, medical faculty representatives, and Members of Parliament).

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of, and vacancies among members
main_sections.description: Details the term of office for members, the conditions under which their term ends, the process for filling casual vacancies, eligibility for re-nomination/re-election, resignation procedures, and the manner of filling vacancies.

main_sections.section_title: President of Institute, his powers and functions
main_sections.description: Establishes the position of the President of the Institute, who is nominated by the Central Government, and outlines their powers and functions as laid down in the Act or as prescribed.
Specifies that the President and other members shall receive such allowances from the Institute as may be prescribed.
Defines the procedure for the Institute's meetings, including the first meeting and subsequent meetings, with respect to time, place, and rules of procedure, including quorum.

main_sections.section_title: Governing Body and other committees of Institute
main_sections.description: Establishes the Governing Body as the executive committee of the Institute, outlines its composition, the President's role as Chairperson, and the procedures for its functioning and the establishment of other committees.

Details the appointment and tenure of the Director of the Institute, their role as chief executive officer, and the appointment of other officers and employees, including their salaries, allowances, and conditions of service.

Ennumerates the primary objects of the Institute, which include developing patterns of teaching in medical education, providing high-order educational facilities, and achieving self-sufficiency in postgraduate medical education.

Specifies the functions of the Institute to promote its objects, including providing teaching in modern medicine and allied sciences, conducting research, establishing medical colleges, hospitals, dental and nursing colleges, rural and urban health organizations, and training health workers.
Concerns the vesting of property in the Institute.
Relates to payments made to the Institute.
Details the establishment and management of the Fund of the Institute.
Concerns the preparation and approval of the Institute's budget.
Lays down provisions for the accounts of the Institute and their audit.
Requires the Institute to prepare an annual report.
Deals with pension and provident funds for the staff of the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Authentication of orders and instruments of Institute
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for authenticating orders and instruments issued by the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Acts and proceedings not to be invalidated by vacancies, etc.
main_sections.description: Ensures that vacancies or irregularities in the appointment of members do not invalidate the acts or proceedings of the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of medical degrees, diplomas, etc., by Institute
main_sections.description: Empowers the Institute to grant medical degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of medical qualifications granted by Institute
main_sections.description: Concerns the recognition of medical qualifications granted by the Institute.
States that the Central Government exercises control over the Institute.
Provides for the resolution of differences that may arise.
Requires the Institute to furnish returns and information as directed.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of service of existing employees
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of service of existing employees to the Institute.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Institute the power to make regulations for the conduct of its business and other matters.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament
main_sections.description: Specifies that rules and regulations made under the Act shall be laid before Parliament.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: The Institute shall consist of specified ex officio and nominated members.
The President of the Institute shall be nominated by the Central Government.
The Governing Body shall be the executive committee of the Institute.
The Director shall be the chief executive officer of the Institute and shall act as Secretary to the Institute and the Governing Body.
The Institute shall provide undergraduate and postgraduate teaching in modern medicine and allied sciences, and facilities for research.
The Institute shall establish and maintain medical colleges, hospitals, dental and nursing colleges, and rural/urban health organizations.
The Institute may demand and receive fees and charges with the prior approval of the Central Government, with student fees not exceeding those specified by a Central Government medical institute.
At least twenty out of every seventy-five seats in undergraduate courses shall be reserved for local applicants.
Free treatment shall be provided to poor patients in the same manner as by a Central Government medical institute.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Institute, Governing Body
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prescribed rules and regulations, oversight by the Central Government, and the powers vested in the Institute and its Governing Body.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right to contract.
Right to sue and be sued.
Right to grant medical degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.
Right to receive grants, gifts, and donations.
duties: Duty to develop patterns of teaching in medical education.
Duty to provide high-order educational facilities.
Duty to attain self-sufficiency in postgraduate medical education.
Duty to conduct teaching in modern medicine and allied sciences.
Duty to provide facilities for research.
Duty to establish and maintain various healthcare and educational institutions.
Duty to train teachers and health workers.
Duty to provide free treatment to the poor.
Duty to reserve seats for local applicants.
Duty to comply with Central Government control and directives.
Duty to prepare annual reports, budgets, and maintain accounts.
obligations: Obligation to operate within the framework of the Act, rules, and regulations.
Obligation to adhere to the objects and functions outlined in the Act.
Obligation to ensure proper management of its Fund, accounts, and audit.
Obligation to lay rules and regulations before Parliament.

key_procedures: Appointment of the President of the Institute by the Central Government.
Constitution of the Governing Body by the Institute.
Appointment of the Director of the Institute by the Institute (with the first Director appointed by the Central Government).
Procedure for the transaction of business at Institute meetings, including quorum.
Procedure for the exercise of powers and discharge of functions by the Governing Body.
Procedure for the appointment of other officers and employees by the Institute.
Process for receiving and dealing with property and funds.
Procedure for the grant of medical degrees and diplomas.
Procedure for making rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Institute.
Procedure for laying rules and regulations before Parliament.
Procedure for the Central Government to remove difficulties.
administration: The Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, functioning under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Central Government exercises overall control and has the power to make rules.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act is to be appointed by the Central Government via notification.
The Act declares the Institute as an institution of national importance.
The Act allows for the establishment of various specialized institutions, including a dental college, nursing college, and rural/urban health organizations.
Fees charged to students for medical courses cannot exceed those specified by a Central Government medical institute.
A minimum of twenty seats out of every seventy-five in undergraduate courses must be reserved for local applicants.
Free treatment for the poor is mandated, mirroring the practice of Central Government medical institutes.

title: THE AIRPORTS ECONOMIC REGULATORY AUTHORITY OF INDIA ACT, 2008
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an Airports Economic Regulatory Authority to regulate tariff and other charges for the aeronautical services rendered at airports and to monitor performance standards of airports and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to: all airports where air transport services are operated or intended to be operated (excluding those of the Armed Forces or paramilitary Forces), all private airports and leased airports, all civil enclaves, and all major airports. A major airport is defined as one with an annual passenger throughput exceeding three and a half million, or as specified by the Central Government.

key_definitions.aeronautical_service: Any service provided for navigation, surveillance, and supportive communication for air traffic management; landing, housing, or parking of aircraft or other ground facilities connected to aircraft operations; ground safety services; ground handling services for aircraft, passengers, and cargo; cargo facilities; fuel supply to aircraft; and services for a stakeholder at an airport, where charges may be determined by the Authority.
key_definitions.airport: A landing and taking off area for aircraft, usually with runways, maintenance, and passenger facilities, and includes an aerodrome as defined in the Aircraft Act, 1934.
key_definitions.airport_user: Any person availing of passenger or cargo facilities at an airport.
key_definitions.authority: The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority established under section 3.
key_definitions.major_airport: Any airport with an annual passenger throughput exceeding three and a half million, or any other airport or group of airports specified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.service_provider: Any person providing aeronautical services eligible to levy and charge user development fees from embarking passengers, including the airport managing authority.
key_definitions.stakeholder: Includes an airport licensee, airlines operating at an airport, a person providing aeronautical services, and any association representing passenger or cargo facility users.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its commencement date as notified by the Central Government, and specifies the types of airports to which it applies.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'aeronautical service', 'airport', 'airport user', 'Authority', 'major airport', 'service provider', and 'stakeholder'.

Mandates the Central Government to establish the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority within three months of the Act's commencement. It outlines the Authority's corporate status, perpetual succession, common seal, and powers to acquire property and contract. The head office location is to be specified by the Central Government.

Specifies that the Authority shall consist of a Chairperson and two other Members appointed by the Central Government. It also includes provisions for an additional Member in matters involving civil enclaves at defense airfields. Members must have expertise in aviation, economics, law, commerce, or consumer affairs, with specific eligibility criteria for former government servants. The Chairperson is the Chief Executive.

Details the grounds and procedures for the Central Government to remove or suspend the Chairperson or any Member from office, including insolvency, conviction of an offense involving moral turpitude, physical or mental incapacity, acquisition of prejudicial financial interest, or abuse of position.
Outlines the powers and functions of the Authority, which include regulating tariff and other charges for aeronautical services and monitoring performance standards at airports.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for wilful failure to comply with orders of Appellate Tribunal
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for willful non-compliance with orders issued by the Appellate Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for non-compliance of orders and directions under this Act
main_sections.description: Details punishments for failing to comply with orders and directions issued under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for non-compliance with order of Authority or Appellate Tribunal
main_sections.description: Specifies punishments for non-compliance with orders from either the Authority or the Appellate Tribunal.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations for carrying out its functions under the Act.

important_rules: The Central Government must establish the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority within three months of the Act's commencement.
Members of the Authority must possess relevant expertise in aviation, economics, law, commerce, or consumer affairs.
The Chairperson and Members shall hold office for a term of five years and are not eligible for re-appointment. They also have age limits for holding office.
Chairperson and Members are prohibited from holding other offices and have restrictions on future employment and representation for two years after ceasing office.
The Chairperson has powers of general superintendence and direction over the Authority's affairs.
The Central Government may remove Members under specific conditions like insolvency, moral turpitude conviction, incapacity, or prejudicial interest.
The Act outlines procedures for the formation of a Selection Committee to recommend candidates for the Chairperson and Members.
Penalties and punishments are prescribed for non-compliance with orders and directions from the Authority or the Appellate Tribunal.

penalties: Penalty for wilful failure to comply with orders of the Appellate Tribunal (Section 37).
Punishment for non-compliance with orders and directions under this Act (Section 38).
Punishment for non-compliance with orders of the Authority or Appellate Tribunal (Section 39).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority and the Appellate Tribunal (for its orders). The Central Government also plays a role in appointments, oversight, and superseding the Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of penalties and punishments for non-compliance with orders and directions issued by the Authority and the Appellate Tribunal. The Central Government can also enforce certain provisions, such as by making rules and superseding the Authority.

rights: Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against certain orders (Section 18).
Right to appeal to the Supreme Court from orders of the Appellate Tribunal (Section 31).
Right to legal representation before the Appellate Tribunal (Section 30).
duties: The Authority has a duty to regulate tariffs and charges for aeronautical services and monitor performance standards at airports.
Members and employees of the Authority are considered public servants (Section 43).
The Central Government has a duty to establish the Authority and appoint its members.
obligations: Service providers are obligated to comply with directions and orders from the Authority and the Appellate Tribunal.
Airport users have the right to access services and facilities under regulated conditions.
The Central Government is obligated to make rules and regulations to operationalize the Act.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Authority by the Central Government.
Appointment of Chairperson and Members through a Selection Committee process.
Terms of office and conditions of service for Chairperson and Members.
Processes for removal and suspension of Members.
Functions of the Authority including calling for information and conducting investigations.
Procedure for filing applications for settlement of disputes and appeals to the Appellate Tribunal.
Procedure for making rules and regulations.
administration: The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India, established by the Central Government. The Central Government also oversees certain aspects, including rule-making, superseding the Authority, and laying rules/regulations before Parliament.
important_notes: The Appellate Tribunal, originally part of the Act, was omitted by Act 7 of 2017, with appeals now being referred to the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal.
The Act came into force on different dates for different chapters (e.g., 1st January, 2009, for preliminary chapters).
The Act is subject to amendments, as indicated by the inclusion of omitted sections and updated figures in definitions.
Civil courts' jurisdiction is barred in matters concerning the Authority and Appellate Tribunal.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

title: THE GRAM NYAYALAYAS ACT, 2008
purpose: To provide for the establishment of Gram Nyayalayas at the grass roots level for the purposes of providing access to justice to the citizens at their doorsteps and to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of social, economic or other disabilities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Nagaland, the State of Arunachal Pradesh, the State of Sikkim and to the tribal areas (specified in Parts I, II, IIA and III of the Table below paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution within the State of Assam, the State of Meghalaya, the State of Tripura and the State of Mizoram, respectively). The Gram Nyayalayas are established for every Panchayat at intermediate level or a group of contiguous Panchayats at intermediate level in a district or where there is no Panchayat at intermediate level, for a group of contiguous Gram Panchayats.

key_definitions.Gram Nyayalaya: A court established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Gram Panchayat: An institution of self-government constituted at the village level under article 243B of the Constitution for rural areas.
key_definitions.High Court: In relation to any State, the High Court for that State; in relation to a Union territory to which the jurisdiction of the High Court for a State has been extended by law, that High Court; in relation to any other Union territory, the highest Court of criminal appeal for that territory other than the Supreme Court of India.
key_definitions.Nyayadhikari: The presiding officer of a Gram Nyayalaya appointed under section 5.
key_definitions.Panchayat at intermediate level: An institution of self-government constituted at the intermediate level under article 243B of the Constitution for rural areas.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Schedule: The Schedule appended to this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except specific states and tribal areas), and commencement date which is to be notified by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as Gram Nyayalaya, Gram Panchayat, High Court, Nyayadhikari, etc.

Details the process for establishing Gram Nyayalayas by the State Government in consultation with the High Court for Panchayats at intermediate level or groups of Gram Panchayats. It also specifies the local limits of jurisdiction and notes that these are in addition to existing courts.
States that the State Government shall appoint a Nyayadhikari for every Gram Nyayalaya in consultation with the High Court.

Outlines the qualifications for a Nyayadhikari, stating they must be eligible to be appointed as a Judicial Magistrate of the first class and mandates representation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, women, and other specified classes.

main_sections.section_title: Nyayadhikari to hold mobile courts and conduct proceedings in villages
main_sections.description: Mandates the Nyayadhikari to visit villages and conduct trials/proceedings in close proximity to where parties reside or where the cause of action arose, with prior publicity for mobile court locations. The State Government is to provide facilities like vehicles.
Specifies that Gram Nyayalayas shall exercise both civil and criminal jurisdiction as provided by the Act, notwithstanding other procedural codes.
Details the criminal jurisdiction, allowing Gram Nyayalayas to take cognizance of offences and try all offences specified in the First Schedule and those notified by the State Government.

Outlines the civil jurisdiction, empowering Gram Nyayalayas to try suits and proceedings of a civil nature specified in the Second Schedule and those notified by the Central and State Governments. Pecuniary limits are to be specified by the High Court.
Grants the Central Government and State Government the power to amend the First and Second Schedules through notification, to add or omit items within their legislative competence.

main_sections.section_title: Overriding effect of Act in criminal trial
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act have overriding effect in criminal trials, but the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, applies where not inconsistent. The Gram Nyayalaya is deemed a Court of Judicial Magistrate of the first class for this purpose.

main_sections.section_title: Gram Nyayalaya to follow summary trial procedure
main_sections.description: Directs Gram Nyayalayas to follow summary trial procedures as specified in Chapter XXI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and allows for re-hearing the case if summary trial is deemed undesirable.
Specifies the provisions for appeals in criminal cases tried by Gram Nyayalayas.
Specifies the provisions for appeals in civil cases tried by Gram Nyayalayas.

main_sections.section_title: Assistance of police to Gram Nyayalayas
main_sections.description: Mandates the assistance of police to Gram Nyayalayas.

main_sections.section_title: Nyayadhikaris and employees, etc., to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares Nyayadhikaris and employees of Gram Nyayalayas as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Power of High Court to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power to make rules under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules under the Act.

important_rules: Gram Nyayalayas are to be established at the grass roots level to provide access to justice at citizens' doorsteps.
Nyayadhikaris must be eligible to be appointed as Judicial Magistrates of the first class.
Nyayadhikaris are to hold mobile courts and conduct proceedings in villages.
Gram Nyayalayas shall exercise both civil and criminal jurisdiction.
Gram Nyayalayas shall follow summary trial procedure in criminal cases.
The Limitation Act, 1963, and relevant chapters of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, shall apply to suits and offences triable by Gram Nyayalayas respectively.

rights: Access to justice at citizens' doorsteps.
Opportunities for securing justice are not denied due to social, economic, or other disabilities.
duties: Nyayadhikari to conduct mobile courts and visit villages.
State Government to provide facilities for mobile courts.
Ministerial officers and employees of Gram Nyayalaya to perform assigned duties.
Police to assist Gram Nyayalayas.

key_procedures: Establishment of Gram Nyayalayas by the State Government in consultation with the High Court.
Appointment of Nyayadhikari by the State Government in consultation with the High Court.
Gram Nyayalaya to conduct criminal trials following summary procedure.
Gram Nyayalaya to attempt conciliation and settlement of civil disputes.
Procedures for appeal in criminal and civil cases.
administration: The administration of this Act appears to be a shared responsibility between the Central Government (for amending schedules and appointing commencement dates), State Governments (for establishing Nyayalayas, appointing officers, making rules), and the High Courts (for consultation, specifying pecuniary limits, and making rules). The Gram Nyayalaya itself, headed by the Nyayadhikari, is the primary judicial body.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 2nd October, 2009.
The State of Jammu and Kashmir has been omitted from the extent of the Act.
The pecuniary limits of the Gram Nyayalaya are to be specified by the High Court in consultation with the State Government.

title: THE LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP ACT, 2008
purpose: To make provisions for the formation and regulation of limited liability partnerships and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to limited liability partnerships formed and registered under this Act.

key_definitions.address: In relation to a partner, it means their usual residential address (if individual) or registered office address (if body corporate).
key_definitions.advocate: As defined in the Advocates Act, 1961.
key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal constituted under the Companies Act, 2013.
key_definitions.body corporate: A company as defined in the Companies Act, 2013, and includes LLPs registered under this Act, LLPs incorporated outside India, and companies incorporated outside India. Excludes corporation sole, co-operative societies, and other specified bodies.
key_definitions.business: Includes every trade, profession, service, and occupation, except activities specifically excluded by the Central Government.
key_definitions.chartered accountant: A chartered accountant as defined in the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, with a certificate of practice.
key_definitions.company secretary: A company secretary as defined in the Company Secretaries Act, 1980, with a certificate of practice.
key_definitions.cost accountant: A cost accountant as defined in the Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959, with a certificate of practice.
key_definitions.Court: The Court having jurisdiction as per section 77 for offences under this Act.
key_definitions.designated partner: Any partner designated as such pursuant to section 7.
key_definitions.entity: Any body corporate, and for specific sections (18, 46-50, 52-53), includes a firm set up under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
key_definitions.financial year: The period from April 1st to March 31st of the following year. For LLPs incorporated after September 30th, it can end on March 31st of the next year.
key_definitions.foreign limited liability partnership: An LLP formed, incorporated, or registered outside India that establishes a place of business within India.
key_definitions.limited liability partnership: A partnership formed and registered under this Act.
key_definitions.limited liability partnership agreement: Any written agreement between partners or between the LLP and its partners that defines their mutual rights and duties.
key_definitions.name: In relation to a partner, it means their forename, middle name, and surname (if individual) or registered name (if body corporate).
key_definitions.partner: Any person who becomes a partner in the LLP according to the LLP agreement.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Registrar: A person appointed by the Central Government as Registrar, Additional Registrar, Joint Registrar, Deputy Registrar, or Assistant Registrar.
key_definitions.small limited liability partnership: An LLP where contribution does not exceed twenty-five lakh rupees (or higher prescribed amount up to five crore rupees) and turnover does not exceed forty lakh rupees (or higher prescribed amount up to fifty crore rupees) for the preceding financial year, or meets other prescribed requirements.
key_definitions.Tribunal: The National Company Law Tribunal constituted under the Companies Act, 2013.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date which is appointed by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'limited liability partnership', 'partner', 'designated partner', 'business', 'financial year', and 'Tribunal'.

main_sections.section_title: Limited liability partnership to be body corporate
main_sections.description: States that an LLP is a body corporate formed and incorporated under the Act, possessing perpetual succession and being a legal entity separate from its partners.

main_sections.section_title: Non-applicability of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932
main_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, do not apply to a limited liability partnership, except where otherwise provided.

Specifies who can be a partner (individual or body corporate) and lists conditions under which an individual is not capable of becoming a partner (unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, pending insolvency application).
Mandates that every LLP must have at least two partners. It also outlines the liability of a sole partner if the number falls below two and the business continues for more than six months.
Requires every LLP to have at least two designated partners, who must be individuals, with at least one being a resident in India. Special provisions apply if partners are bodies corporate.
Deals with the incorporation document required for forming an LLP.
Covers the process of incorporation through registration.

main_sections.section_title: Registered office of limited liability partnership and change therein
main_sections.description: Addresses the registered office of an LLP and the procedure for changing it.
Details the legal consequences and effects of an LLP's registration.
Concerns the name of the limited liability partnership.

main_sections.section_title: Extent of liability of limited liability partnership
main_sections.description: Defines the extent of liability of the LLP itself.
Defines the extent of liability of individual partners.

main_sections.section_title: Unlimited liability in case of fraud
main_sections.description: Outlines circumstances where a partner may face unlimited liability, specifically in cases of fraud.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance of books of account, other records and audit, etc.
main_sections.description: Mandates the maintenance of books of account, other records, and the requirement for audit for LLPs.
Requires LLPs to file an annual return.

main_sections.section_title: Investigation of the affairs of limited liability partnership
main_sections.description: Provides for the investigation into the affairs of an LLP.

main_sections.section_title: Conversion from firm into limited liability partnership
main_sections.description: Details the process and provisions for converting a firm into an LLP.

main_sections.section_title: Conversion from private company into limited liability partnership
main_sections.description: Details the process and provisions for converting a private company into an LLP.

main_sections.section_title: Conversion from unlisted public company into limited liability partnership
main_sections.description: Details the process and provisions for converting an unlisted public company into an LLP.
Deals with provisions related to foreign LLPs operating within India.
Covers the procedures and circumstances for the winding up and dissolution of an LLP.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the provisions of the Companies Act
main_sections.description: Specifies the applicability of certain provisions of the Companies Act to LLPs.
Outlines general penalties for contraventions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Registrar to strike defunct limited liability partnership off register
main_sections.description: Grants the Registrar the power to strike off defunct LLPs from the register.
Confers power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Every LLP must have at least two partners.
Every LLP must have at least two designated partners, who must be individuals, and at least one must be a resident in India.
An LLP is a body corporate, a legal entity separate from its partners, and has perpetual succession.
LLPs must maintain books of account and other records and are subject to audit.
LLPs must file an annual return.
An individual is disqualified from being a partner if they are of unsound mind, an undischarged insolvent, or have a pending application to be adjudicated as an insolvent.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of sections 7 and 9 (regarding designated partners).
Penalty for improper use of words 'limited liability partnership' or 'LLP'.
Penalty for false statement.
General penalties for offences under the Act.
Enhanced punishment for certain offences.
Adjudication of penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Companies and the Courts/Tribunals as specified in the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of penalties, prosecution, investigation, and the power of the Registrar to strike off defunct LLPs.

rights: Right to form and register an LLP.
Right to have a limited liability.
Right to perpetual succession.
Rights as defined in the Limited Liability Partnership Agreement.
duties: Duty to have at least two partners.
Duty to have at least two designated partners (one resident in India).
Duty to maintain books of account and other records.
Duty to file annual returns.
Duty to comply with the LLP agreement.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation to contribute to the LLP as per the LLP agreement.
Obligation to discharge duties of designated partners.
Obligation to notify changes in partners and designated partners to the Registrar.

key_procedures: Procedure for incorporation of an LLP, including filing of incorporation document and registration.
Procedure for appointing and changing designated partners.
Procedure for changing the registered office of an LLP.
Procedure for reserving and changing the name of an LLP.
Procedure for investigation of the affairs of an LLP.
Procedure for conversion of a firm, private company, or unlisted public company into an LLP.
Procedure for winding up and dissolution of an LLP.
administration: The Central Government, through the Registrar of Companies and other appointed officials, administers the Act.
important_notes: Different commencement dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The Companies Act, 2013, provisions are to be used for terms not defined in this Act.
The Central Government has the power to exclude certain activities from the definition of 'business' via notification.

title: THE TAMIL NADU LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL ACT, 2010
purpose: To provide for the creation of a Legislative Council for the State of Tamil Nadu and for matters supplemental, incidental and consequential thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Tamil Nadu, India. It concerns the establishment and functioning of the Legislative Council of Tamil Nadu.

key_definitions.representation_of_the_people_act_1950: Definitions for words and expressions used in this Act, not otherwise defined, shall have the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Tamil Nadu Legislative Council Act, 2010.
Defines terms used in the Act, referencing the Representation of the People Act, 1950 for terms not otherwise defined.

main_sections.section_title: Creation of Legislative Council for Tamil Nadu
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a Legislative Council for Tamil Nadu, specifying the number of seats (78) and their distribution among elected and nominated members. It also mandates the President to determine constituencies and allot seats.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Third Schedule and Fourth Schedule to Act 43 of 1950
main_sections.description: Amends the Representation of the People Act, 1950 by inserting details about Tamil Nadu's Legislative Council seats in the Third Schedule and specifying the local authorities for elections in the Fourth Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 15A of Act 43 of 1951
main_sections.description: Amends Section 15A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to include the creation of the Legislative Council of Tamil Nadu under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: A Legislative Council shall be established for the State of Tamil Nadu from a date appointed by the President.
Rule 2: The Legislative Council of Tamil Nadu shall have a total of 78 seats.
Rule 3: The seats in the Legislative Council will be filled by persons elected from various electorates and by persons nominated by the Governor, as per Article 171 of the Constitution.
