Rule 4: The President, in consultation with the Election Commission, shall determine the constituencies, their extent, and the number of seats per constituency for the Legislative Council.
Rule 5: Steps shall be taken to constitute the Legislative Council in accordance with this Act and the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951.
Rule 6: The Representation of the People Act, 1950, is amended to include Tamil Nadu's Legislative Council details in its Third and Fourth Schedules.
Rule 7: The Representation of the People Act, 1951, is amended to recognize the creation of the Legislative Council of Tamil Nadu under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act's provisions are primarily enacted by Parliament and implemented through Presidential orders and amendments to other Acts. The Election Commission of India plays a role in the determination of constituencies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through Presidential orders for appointment of dates and determination of constituencies, and through amendments to the Representation of the People Acts.

rights: The right of the State of Tamil Nadu to have a Legislative Council.
Rights of elected and nominated members to fill seats in the Legislative Council.
Rights related to the electoral process as defined in related Representation of the People Acts.
duties: Duty of the President to appoint a date for the establishment of the Council.
Duty of the President to determine constituencies in consultation with the Election Commission.
Duty to take steps to constitute the Council as per the Act and related Representation of the People Acts.
obligations: Obligation to amend the Third and Fourth Schedules of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Obligation to amend Section 15A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Appointment of the date for the creation of the Legislative Council by the President via order.
Procedure 2: Determination of constituencies, their extent, and seat allocation by the President, after consultation with the Election Commission.
Procedure 3: Constitution of the Legislative Council following the aforementioned determinations, adhering to the provisions of this Act and the Representation of the People Acts.
administration: The administration and day-to-day functioning of the Legislative Council will be governed by the Constitution of India, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Council Act, 2010, and other relevant electoral laws. The administrative oversight for its establishment falls under the purview of the President and relevant government departments.
important_notes: The Act requires a Presidential Order to bring the Legislative Council into effect.
The numbers of seats and their allocation are based on constitutional provisions (Article 171).
The Act relies heavily on existing electoral legislation (Representation of the People Act, 1950 and 1951) for its implementation.

title: THE CIVIL LIABILITY FOR NUCLEAR DAMAGE ACT, 2010
purpose: To provide for civil liability for nuclear damage and prompt compensation to victims of a nuclear incident through a no-fault liability regime, channeling liability to the operator, appointing a Claims Commissioner, establishing a Nuclear Damage Claims Commission, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

scope.geographical: The whole of India, and also extends to nuclear damage suffered in or over maritime areas beyond territorial waters, exclusive economic zone of India, on board ships or aircraft registered in India, or on or by artificial islands, installations, or structures under India's jurisdiction.
scope.subject_matter: Civil liability for nuclear damage and compensation for victims of nuclear incidents, specifically applying to nuclear installations owned or controlled by the Central Government, either directly or through its authorities, corporations, or government companies.

key_definitions.nuclear_damage: Includes loss of life or personal injury, loss of or damage to property, economic loss, costs of environmental reinstatement, loss of income from environmental impairment, costs of preventive measures and resulting loss/damage, and any other economic loss permitted by general Indian civil liability law, arising from ionizing radiation emitted by a nuclear source or material.
key_definitions.nuclear_incident: Any occurrence or series of occurrences having the same origin that causes nuclear damage or creates a grave and imminent threat of causing such damage (with respect to preventive measures).
key_definitions.operator: In relation to a nuclear installation, the Central Government or any authority, corporation, or government company licensed for its operation.
key_definitions.nuclear_installation: Includes nuclear reactors (excluding those on transport vehicles for power), facilities for producing or processing nuclear material (including reprocessing), and facilities for storing nuclear material (excluding storage incidental to carriage).

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Provides the short title, defines the territorial extent of the Act, specifies its application to various maritime zones and Indian registered vessels/aircraft, clarifies its application to government-controlled nuclear installations, and outlines the commencement of the Act.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including Chairperson, Claims Commissioner, Commission, environment, Member, notification, nuclear damage, nuclear fuel, nuclear incident, nuclear installation, nuclear material, nuclear reactor, operator, prescribed, preventive measures, radioactive products or waste, and Special Drawing Rights.

main_sections.section_title: Atomic Energy Regulatory Board to notify nuclear incident
main_sections.description: Mandates the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board to notify a nuclear incident within fifteen days of its occurrence, unless the threat is insignificant. It also requires wide publicity of the notified incident.

Establishes the operator's liability for nuclear damage caused by a nuclear incident originating from, involving, or sent to their installation. It outlines specific conditions for liability during transit and states that the operator's liability is strict and based on no-fault principles. It also addresses joint and several liability when multiple operators are involved and defines the operator in cases of transit or other specific scenarios.
Specifies the financial limits of the operator's liability for nuclear damage, which is to be prescribed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for nuclear damage and its adjudication
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Claims Commissioner for adjudicating compensation for nuclear damage and outlines the process for this adjudication.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Nuclear Damage Claims Commission
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a Nuclear Damage Claims Commission to handle claims for nuclear damage.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters that the Claims Commissioner or the Commission is empowered to adjudicate.
Deals with offenses and their corresponding penalties under the Act.

important_rules: The operator of a nuclear installation is strictly liable, on a no-fault basis, for nuclear damage caused by a nuclear incident occurring in their installation or involving nuclear material originating from or sent to their installation (Section 4).
The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board must notify a nuclear incident within fifteen days, unless it's insignificant, and give it wide publicity (Section 3).
The operator must maintain insurance or other financial securities to cover their liability (Section 8).
Compensation for nuclear damage is to be adjudicated by a Claims Commissioner and potentially the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission (Sections 9, 12, 16, 31, 32).
The jurisdiction of civil courts is excluded for matters that can be dealt with by the Claims Commissioner or the Commission (Section 35).

penalties: Offences under the Act are subject to penalties as prescribed by Section 39.
Offences committed by companies are subject to penalties, with provisions for their officers being liable (Section 40).
Offences committed by Government Departments are also addressed (Section 41).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The enforcement mechanisms involve the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board for notification, Claims Commissioners for adjudication, and the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission for handling claims and awards. The Central Government also has powers to give directions and call for information.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement occurs through the notification of incidents, adjudication of claims for compensation, the establishment and functioning of the Claims Commissioner and the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission, and by prosecuting offenders for violations of the Act.

rights: Right of victims to claim compensation for nuclear damage.
Right of an operator to have recourse against a third party if the damage was caused by that third party (Section 17).
Right to claim compensation for various types of losses including loss of life, personal injury, property damage, economic loss, environmental damage, and costs of preventive measures.
duties: Duty of the operator to be liable for nuclear damage.
Duty of the operator to maintain insurance or financial securities.
Duty of the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board to notify and publicize nuclear incidents.
Duty to adhere to the procedures for making claims before the Claims Commissioner or Commission.
obligations: Obligation of the operator to compensate for nuclear damage under a no-fault regime.
Obligation to follow the prescribed procedures for claim submission and adjudication.
Obligation to comply with directions issued by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Notification of a nuclear incident by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board and publicizing it (Section 3).
Claims Commissioner inviting applications for compensation, and individuals making applications (Sections 13, 15).
Adjudication of claims by the Claims Commissioner or the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission, including hearing evidence and passing awards (Sections 12, 16, 32).
Transfer of pending cases to the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission (Section 33).
Enforcement of awards made by the Claims Commissioner or Commission (Section 36).
administration: The Central Government, through its relevant authorities and departments, is involved in the administration, including the appointment of officials, making rules, and issuing notifications. The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, Claims Commissioners, and the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission are key administrative bodies.
important_notes: The Act has specific exclusions for operator liability in cases of grave natural disasters of an exceptional character or acts of armed conflict, hostility, civil war, insurrection, or terrorism (Section 5).
The Act is to be in addition to any other law, and does not affect the operation of other laws, except where expressly provided (Section 46).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 47).

title: The Orissa (Alteration of Name) Act, 2011
purpose: To alter the name of the State of Orissa to the State of Odisha.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Orissa (renamed Odisha) and its laws. It also affects the Constitution of India by amending specific articles and schedules.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed by the Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, for the coming into force of this Act.
key_definitions.appropriate Government: As respects a law relating to a matter enumerated in List I in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, the Central Government; and as respects any other law, the State Government.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, Ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or any part of the State of Orissa.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'appropriate Government', and 'law'.

main_sections.section_title: Alteration of name of State of Orissa
main_sections.description: States that as from the appointed day, the State of Orissa shall be known as the State of Odisha.
Amends Article 164 of the Constitution by substituting 'Odisha' for 'Orissa' in the proviso to clause (1).
Amends Article 273 of the Constitution by substituting 'Odisha' for 'Orissa' in clause (1).

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution by substituting 'Odisha' for 'Orissa' in the entry for the state.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution by substituting 'Odisha' for 'Orissa' in the relevant entry.
Empowers the appropriate Government to make adaptations and modifications to any law made before the appointed day to give effect to the name alteration.

Allows courts, tribunals, or authorities to construe pre-existing laws in a manner necessary or proper, even if no or insufficient adaptation has been made, without affecting the substance of the law.
Deems the State of Odisha to have been substituted for the State of Orissa in any legal proceedings pending immediately before the appointed day.

important_rules: The State of Orissa shall be known as the State of Odisha from the appointed day.
Amendments to Articles 164, 273, and entries in the First and Fourth Schedules of the Constitution to reflect the name change.
The appropriate Government has the power to adapt existing laws before the appointed day to reflect the name change.
Courts and tribunals can construe existing laws in a way that gives effect to the name change, even without specific adaptations.
In ongoing legal proceedings, the State of Odisha will be automatically substituted for the State of Orissa.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the State Government (as per 'appropriate Government' definition) have powers to adapt laws and enforce the act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the power to adapt laws (Section 8), the power to construe laws (Section 9), and by deeming substitution in legal proceedings (Section 10).

obligations: The obligation to recognize the State of Odisha as the successor to the State of Orissa.
The obligation to amend or adapt laws and constitutional provisions to reflect the new name.

key_procedures: The Central Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint a date for the commencement of the Act.
The appropriate Government may, by order, make adaptations and modifications to existing laws within one year of the appointed day.
Courts, tribunals, or authorities may construe laws in a necessary and proper manner if adaptations are insufficient.
administration: The Central Government (for matters concerning List I of the Seventh Schedule) and the State Government (for other laws) are responsible for the administration of this Act, particularly in adapting laws.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 1st November, 2011, vide notification No. G.S.R. 791(E), dated 1st November, 2011.
The power to adapt laws under Section 8 is limited to one year from the appointed day.

title: The National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Second Act, 2011
purpose: To make special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi for a further period up to December 31, 2026, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, providing relief and minimizing hardship against punitive action related to unauthorized development.
scope: The Act extends to the entire National Capital Territory of Delhi, excluding the Delhi Cantonment. It addresses issues related to unauthorized developments, encroachments, slum dwellers, jhuggi-jhompri clusters, unauthorized colonies, village abadi areas and their extensions, farm houses, and various institutions like schools, dispensaries, religious and cultural institutions, storages, warehouses, and godowns.

key_definitions.building_bye-laws: Bye-laws made under the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, or regulations made under the Delhi Development Act, 1957, relating to buildings.
key_definitions.delhi: The entire area of the National Capital Territory of Delhi except the Delhi Cantonment.
key_definitions.encroachment: Unauthorised occupation of Government land or public land (excluding streets, lanes, footpaths, and parks) by temporary, semi-permanent, or permanent structures for residential, commercial, or any other use.
key_definitions.local_authority: The Delhi Municipal Corporation, the New Delhi Municipal Council, or the Delhi Development Authority, legally entitled to exercise control within their respective jurisdictions.
key_definitions.master_plan: The Master Plan for Delhi as notified under the Delhi Development Act, 1957.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.punitive_action: Action taken by a local authority under relevant law against unauthorized development, including demolition, sealing of premises, and displacement of persons or businesses.
key_definitions.relevant_law: Refers to the Delhi Development Act, 1957; the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957; and the New Delhi Municipal Council Act, 1994, depending on the authority.
key_definitions.special_area: Has the meaning assigned in the Building Regulations for Special Area, Unauthorised Regularised Colonies and Village Abadis, 2010.
key_definitions.unauthorised_development: Use of land or building, construction, or colony development in contravention of sanctioned plans, without sanction, or in contravention of permitted land use under Master Plan, Zonal Plan, or layout plan, including encroachment.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration
main_sections.description: This section specifies the name of the Act, its geographical extent (National Capital Territory of Delhi), commencement date (January 1, 2012), and its duration until December 31, 2026, with provisions for repeal.

This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'building bye-laws', 'Delhi', 'encroachment', 'local authority', 'Master Plan', 'notification', 'punitive action', 'relevant law', 'special area', and 'unauthorised development'.

main_sections.section_title: Enforcement to be kept in abeyance
main_sections.description: This section mandates the Central Government to take measures to finalize norms, policy guidelines, and strategies to deal with various forms of encroachment and unauthorized development before the Act's expiry. It also states that enforcement actions under relevant laws are to be kept in abeyance for the period of this Act concerning specific categories of unauthorized developments.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of this Act not to apply in certain cases
main_sections.description: This section outlines specific exceptions where the provisions of this Act might not apply, though the exact conditions are not detailed in the provided text extract.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions
main_sections.description: This section grants the Central Government the authority to issue directions to local authorities or other agencies regarding the implementation of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of acts done or omitted to be done, etc., during 1st January, 2012 up to the date of enactment of this Act
main_sections.description: This section provides for the validation of any acts done or omitted to be done between January 1, 2012, and the date of the Act's enactment. This likely addresses any actions taken during a period when the legal framework might have been uncertain or transitional.

important_rules: Enforcement actions under relevant laws concerning unauthorized development, encroachment, slum dwellers, jhuggi-jhompri clusters, unauthorized colonies, village abadi areas and extensions, farm houses, schools, dispensaries, religious institutions, cultural institutions, storages, warehouses, and godowns used for agricultural inputs or produce in rural areas built on agricultural land, are to be kept in abeyance during the period of this Act.
The Central Government must take all possible measures to finalize norms, policy guidelines, and feasible strategies to deal with these issues before the expiry of this Act.

Orderly arrangements for relocation and rehabilitation of slum dwellers and Jhuggi-Jhompri clusters in Delhi must be made in accordance with the provisions of the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board Act, 2010.
The Act shall cease to have effect on December 31, 2026, except for things done or omitted to be done before that date.
The Central Government can give directions to local authorities or other agencies for the implementation of this Act.

penalties: While the provided text details the suspension of punitive actions, it does not explicitly list penalties for violations of this specific Act. Penalties would likely be under the 'relevant laws' mentioned if actions taken during the abeyance period are deemed unlawful post-Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government has the overarching authority to give directions. Enforcement of 'relevant laws' is carried out by the Delhi Municipal Corporation, the New Delhi Municipal Council, and the Delhi Development Authority, though their punitive actions are suspended under this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act primarily works by suspending punitive actions by local authorities related to unauthorized developments. The Central Government is mandated to develop policies and strategies for orderly arrangements concerning these issues. Enforcement of the Act itself would stem from the Central Government's directives and the eventual implementation of the finalized norms and policies.

rights: Right to relief and minimization of hardship against punitive action by any agency in respect of persons covered by the policies referred to in the Act.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to finalize norms, policy guidelines, and strategies to deal with encroachment and unauthorized development.
Duty of the Central Government to make orderly arrangements for relocation and rehabilitation of slum dwellers and Jhuggi-Jhompri clusters.
Duty of local authorities to keep enforcement actions in abeyance as per the provisions of this Act.
obligations: Obligation on the Central Government to ensure that no hardship is caused to the public until the revision of the Master Plan is undertaken.
Obligation to adhere to the duration of the Act, which ceases to have effect on December 31, 2026.

key_procedures: The Central Government must take all possible measures to finalize norms, policy guidelines, feasible strategies, and make orderly arrangements for relocation and rehabilitation of slum dwellers and Jhuggi-Jhompri clusters.
Local authorities are required to keep enforcement actions (demolition, sealing, displacement) related to unauthorized development and encroachment in abeyance during the period of the Act.

The Act's provisions cease to have effect on December 31, 2026, and the General Clauses Act, 1897, will apply as if the Act had been repealed, preserving rights and liabilities accrued before its cessation.
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrator, with the Delhi Development Authority, Delhi Municipal Corporation, and New Delhi Municipal Council acting as relevant local authorities whose actions are governed by this Act.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to provide relief during the period when the Master Plan for Delhi was being revised or formulated for future years (e.g., 2021, 2041).
The Act has been extended multiple times since its initial enactment in 2007, indicating the ongoing nature of the challenges related to urban development and unauthorized constructions in Delhi.

The specific conditions under which Section 4 ('Provisions of this Act not to apply in certain cases') applies are not detailed in the provided extract, requiring reference to the full text for clarity.
Subsequent amendments have extended the Act's duration and modified certain definitions and provisions, for example, by the Acts of 2017, 2020, and 2023.

title: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
purpose: To provide protection against sexual harassment of women at the workplace and for the prevention and redressal of complaints of sexual harassment, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to all women, of any age, whether employed or not, who allege to have been subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace. This includes various types of workplaces, both in the private and public sectors, and also dwelling places or houses where domestic workers are employed. Establishments with less than ten workers, or where the complaint is against the employer, are covered by the Local Complaints Committee.

key_definitions.aggrieved woman: A woman of any age who alleges to have been subjected to any act of sexual harassment by the respondent, or a woman employed in a dwelling place or house.
key_definitions.appropriate Government: Central Government for workplaces financed by the Central Government/Union territory administration; State Government for workplaces financed by the State Government or within its territory not covered by the Central Government. For other workplaces, it's the State Government.
key_definitions.employee: A person employed at a workplace for any work on regular, temporary, ad hoc or daily wage basis, including co-workers, contract workers, probationers, trainees, and apprentices, whether for remuneration or not, or working voluntarily.
key_definitions.employer: Head of government departments/local authorities, or person responsible for management, supervision, and control of a workplace. In relation to a dwelling place/house, it's the person or household employing a domestic worker.
key_definitions.sexual harassment: Includes unwelcome acts or behavior such as physical contact and advances, demand for sexual favors, sexually colored remarks, showing pornography, or any other unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement (to be notified by the Central Government).
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'aggrieved woman', 'appropriate Government', 'employee', 'employer', 'sexual harassment', and 'workplace'.

States that no woman shall be subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace and outlines circumstances that may amount to sexual harassment, such as implied promises of preferential treatment, threats, interference with work, or humiliating treatment.

Mandates every employer to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) for workplaces. Details the composition of the ICC, including a Presiding Officer (senior woman employee), at least two employee members committed to women's cause or with legal knowledge, and one member from NGOs or associations. Specifies tenure and conditions for removal of members.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and jurisdiction of Local Committee
main_sections.description: Requires District Officers to constitute a Local Committee (LC) to receive complaints from establishments with less than ten workers or where the complaint is against the employer. Outlines the LC's jurisdiction within the district and designates nodal officers for receiving complaints.
Lays down the procedure for filing a complaint of sexual harassment.
Details the process of inquiry into a complaint of sexual harassment.
Enumerates the responsibilities of employers in preventing and addressing sexual harassment, including constituting ICCs, organizing awareness programs, and taking action on complaints.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for non-compliance with provisions of Act
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for employers who fail to comply with the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Every employer must constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) in writing for their workplace.

The ICC should consist of a Presiding Officer (senior woman employee), at least two employee members committed to women's cause or with legal knowledge, and one member from NGOs or associations. At least half of the nominated members must be women.
A Local Committee (LC) must be constituted by the District Officer for establishments with less than ten workers or when the complaint is against the employer.
No woman shall be subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace.
Employers have a duty to prevent sexual harassment, take action on complaints, and create a safe working environment.

penalties: Penalty for non-compliance with provisions of the Act by the employer.
Penalty for making a false or malicious complaint or giving false evidence.
Penalty for publication or making known the contents of a complaint and inquiry proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Officer (for Local Committees), employer (for Internal Complaints Committees), and the 'Appropriate Government' (for overall monitoring and enforcement). Courts have cognizance of offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the constitution and functioning of Internal Complaints Committees and Local Committees, inquiries into complaints, imposition of penalties, and monitoring by the Appropriate Government.

rights: Right of every woman to be protected from sexual harassment at the workplace.
Right to file a complaint of sexual harassment.
Right to a fair and impartial inquiry into the complaint.
Right to privacy and confidentiality of complaint proceedings.
Right to appeal against the findings or action taken on a complaint.
duties: Duty of the employer to prevent sexual harassment and provide a safe working environment.
Duty of the employer to constitute and support an Internal Complaints Committee.
Duty of the appropriate Government to monitor implementation and publicize the Act.
Duty of the District Officer to notify a District Officer and constitute Local Committees.
Duty of every person to not subject women to sexual harassment.
obligations: Obligation of the employer to take action on the recommendations of the ICC.
Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Constitution of Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) by employers.
Constitution of Local Complaints Committee (LC) by District Officers.
Filing of a complaint of sexual harassment by an aggrieved woman.
Conciliation proceedings initiated by the ICC or LC.
Inquiry into the complaint by the ICC or LC.
Submission of an inquiry report by the committee.
Determination and payment of compensation.
Filing of an appeal against the inquiry report or action taken.
administration: The 'Appropriate Government' (Central or State Government as defined) is responsible for monitoring the implementation of the Act and taking measures to publicize it. District Officers administer the formation and functioning of Local Committees.
important_notes: The Act aims to give effect to the Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women.
The Act is not in derogation of any other law that provides for more favorable provisions to the aggrieved woman.
The Appropriate Government has the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

title: THE NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF DESIGN ACT, 2014
purpose: To declare certain institutions of design as institutions of national importance for the promotion of quality and excellence in education, research and training in all disciplines relating to Design and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the institutions mentioned in the Schedule, which are declared as institutions of national importance. It covers education, research, and training in all disciplines relating to design. The Institute can establish campuses within or outside India.

key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Governing Council nominated under clause (a) of section 11.
key_definitions.Dean: In relation to any Institute campus, the Dean of such Institute campus.
key_definitions.design: A rational, logical and sequential innovative process for the purpose of transferring culture to viable products and services and for providing a competitive edge to products and services, and includes industrial design, communication design, textile and apparel design, lifestyle design, experiential design, exhibition design, craft and traditional sector design.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of an Institute appointed under section 18.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of an Institute maintained under section 23.
key_definitions.Governing Council: The Governing Council of an Institute constituted under section 11.
key_definitions.Institute: Any of the institutions mentioned in column (4) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.Institute campus: The campus of an Institute established by such Institute at any place within India or outside India.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Registrar: The Registrar of an Institute appointed under section 20.
key_definitions.Schedule: The Schedule annexed to this Act.
key_definitions.Society: Any of the societies registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860), and mentioned in column (3) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: The Statutes and the Ordinances of an Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares specific institutions, as mentioned in the Schedule, as institutions of national importance due to their objectives.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as Chairperson, Dean, design, Director, Fund, Governing Council, Institute, Institute campus, notification, prescribed, Registrar, Schedule, Senate, Society, Statutes, and Ordinances.

States that each Institute shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract. It also allows Institutes to establish campuses within or outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of the incorporation of the Institute
main_sections.description: Details the consequences of incorporation, including the substitution of the Society with the Institute in laws, contracts, and instruments, the vesting of property in the Institute, and the transfer of rights and liabilities. It also addresses the employment terms and conditions of persons employed by the Society before the commencement of the Act.

Outlines the powers and duties of each Institute, including providing education, research, and training in design, developing courses, granting degrees and diplomas, conferring honorary degrees, instituting fellowships, fixing fees, managing hostels, maintaining discipline, appointing staff, framing Statutes and Ordinances, cooperating with other institutions, acting as a nucleus for academia-industry interaction, establishing workshops and laboratories, acquiring patents, undertaking consultancy, receiving gifts and grants, encouraging education of persons engaged in design-related activities, publishing literature, establishing libraries and museums, nominating personnel for study, retaining professional advisers, encouraging artisans, constructing buildings, borrowing money, and performing all necessary acts for achieving its objects. It also stipulates that disposal of immovable property requires prior approval of the Visitor.

main_sections.section_title: Institute be open to all races, creeds and classes
main_sections.description: Ensures that the Institute is open to all individuals irrespective of race, creed, or class.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Institute to be public authority under Right to Information Act, 2005
main_sections.description: Declares each Institute as a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Each Institute shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Each Institute shall have the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract.
Each Institute shall be open to all races, creeds, and classes.
The Institute shall not dispose of any immovable property without the prior approval of the Visitor.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Governing Council, Director, Registrar, Senate (depending on the specific provision)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the establishment of authorities, statutes, ordinances, and rules. The Central Government has oversight and the power to issue directions.

rights: Right to establish campuses within or outside India.
Right to provide instructions, research, and training in design.
Right to develop courses and grant degrees/diplomas.
Right to confer honorary degrees and awards.
Right to institute and award fellowships and scholarships.
Right to fix and receive fees.
Right to establish and manage student accommodations.
Right to supervise student discipline and welfare.
Right to cooperate with educational institutions globally.
Right to act as a nucleus for academia-industry interaction.
Right to acquire patents and licenses.
Right to undertake consultancy.
Right to receive gifts, grants, and donations.
Right to borrow and raise money.
duties: To promote quality and excellence in design education, research, and training.
To nurture and promote excellence in areas and disciplines relating to design.
To supervise and control the residence and discipline of students.
To make arrangements for promoting students' health, general welfare, and cultural life.
To cooperate with educational or other institutions.
To prepare, print, publish, and circulate literature related to industrial design and allied fields.
To establish and maintain museums, libraries, and collections.
obligations: Employees of the former Society shall continue their service under the Institute with the same tenure, remuneration, terms, and conditions, unless altered by Statutes, with provisions for termination and compensation if alterations are not acceptable.

key_procedures: Appointment of Director (section 18).
Appointment of Registrar (section 20).
Establishment of Governing Council (section 11).
Conduct of Meetings of the Governing Council (section 13).
Framing of Statutes (section 29).
Framing of Ordinances (section 31).
Collection and maintenance of accounts and audit (section 25).
Appointment of staff (section 27).
administration: The Act establishes the Governing Council, Senate, Director, and other officers for the administration of each Institute. The Central Government has overarching powers, including the power to issue directions and make rules. The Visitor also plays a role, particularly in approving the disposal of immovable property.
important_notes: Amendments were made by Act 38 of 2019, effective from January 13, 2020, which substituted certain words and clauses, and added new provisions.
Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad, and its campuses at Bengaluru and Gandhinagar have specific commencement dates mentioned.
The Act declares certain institutions as institutions of national importance.
The Institute is a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005.

title: The Indian Institutes of Information Technology Act, 2014
purpose: To declare certain institutions of information technology as institutions of national importance, with a view to develop new knowledge in information technology, provide manpower of global standards for the information technology industry, and to provide for other connected or incidental matters.
scope: This Act applies to the institutions of information technology mentioned in the Schedule and declared as institutions of national importance. It covers their establishment, governance, functions, and operations within India.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of an Institute.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board of Governors.
key_definitions.Council: The Council of Institutes established under the Act.
key_definitions.existing Institute: An institute mentioned in column (3) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.Institute: Any of the institutions mentioned in column (5) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: Statutes and Ordinances of an Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares that the Institutes mentioned in the Schedule are institutions of national importance.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Council', 'Director', 'Institute', 'Schedule', etc.
States that each existing Institute shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of acquiring property and contracting.
Details the consequences of incorporation, including the transfer of assets, liabilities, and personnel from existing societies to the new Institutes.
Outlines the main objectives of each Institute, including advancing knowledge in IT, developing skilled youth, and promoting transparency.
Specifies the powers and functions of the Institute, such as providing instruction, conducting research, granting degrees, appointing faculty, creating posts, and disseminating knowledge.

main_sections.section_title: Institute to be open to all races, creeds and classes
main_sections.description: Ensures that Institutes are open to all persons irrespective of background and that admissions are merit-based and transparent.
Designates the President of India as the Visitor of every Institute and grants the Visitor the power to review work and progress.
Establishes a Council of Institutes to oversee and coordinate the activities of the various Institutes.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Institutes.

important_rules: Institutes are declared as institutions of national importance (Section 2).
Institutes shall be bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (Section 4).
All assets, liabilities, and personnel of existing societies are transferred to the corresponding Institutes upon incorporation (Section 5).
Institutes must be open to all persons irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, domicile, ethnicity, social or economic background (Section 8).
Admissions to all programmes of study shall be based on merit assessed through transparent and reasonable criteria (Section 8).
Each Institute shall be a not-for-profit legal entity, with any surplus revenue reinvested for its growth and development or research (Section 10).
The President of India shall be the Visitor of every Institute (Section 11).
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Institutes (Section 46).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, the Visitor (President of India), and the Council of Institutes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Central Government to issue directions, the Visitor's power to review and inquire, and the governance structures established by the Act (Board of Governors, Senate, Finance Committee, etc.). Specific penalties for non-compliance are not detailed in the provided text but would likely be governed by general law or rules made under the Act.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (Section 4).
Right to contract and sue or be sued (Section 4).
Employees have rights to their existing tenure, remuneration, and terms/conditions of service, with provisions for compensation if altered unfavorably (Section 5(d)).
Students have rights to pursue their academic courses and are deemed migrated to the corresponding Institute (Section 5(e)).
Right to provide instruction and grant degrees (Section 7(a), 7(c)).
Right to conduct research and innovation (Section 7(b)).
Right to appoint faculty and staff (Section 7(d), 7(f)).
Right to receive gifts, grants, and donations (Section 7(k)).
Right to co-operate with international institutions (Section 7(l)).
Right to establish and maintain infrastructure (Section 7(m)).
duties: To emerge amongst the foremost institutions in information technology and allied fields (Section 6(a)).
To advance new knowledge and innovation (Section 6(b)).
To develop competent and capable youth with social and environmental orientation (Section 6(c)).
To promote and provide transparency in admissions, appointments, evaluation, administration, and finance (Section 6(d)).
To conduct all teaching in accordance with Statutes and Ordinances (Section 9).
To provide annual reports to the Central Government (Section 39).
obligations: To be open to all races, creeds, and classes (Section 8).
Not to accept bequests with conditions opposed to the spirit of openness (Section 8(2)).
To ensure admissions are based on merit and transparency (Section 8(3)).
To operate as a not-for-profit entity (Section 10).
To comply with directions issued by the Central Government (Section 46).
To be a public authority under the Right to Information Act (Section 47).

key_procedures: Establishment of Institutes as corporate bodies with perpetual succession and common seal (Section 4).
Transfer of properties, rights, and liabilities from existing societies to the new Institutes (Section 5).
Appointment of faculty and staff according to Council policy (Section 7(d), 7(f)).
Disposal of property, with prior approval of the State Government if land was provided free of cost, and prior approval of the Visitor for immovable property (Section 7(j), 7(2)).
Making of Statutes and Ordinances, including the process for their creation (Sections 33, 34, 35, 36).
Submission of annual reports by the Director and each Institute to the Central Government (Sections 38, 39).
Provision of returns and information to the Central Government (Section 45).
administration: The administration of the Act is overseen by the Central Government, with the President of India as the Visitor. The Council of Institutes plays a significant role in coordination, and each Institute is managed by its Board of Governors, Senate, Director, and Registrar.
important_notes: Institutes are considered Central Educational Institutions for the purposes of the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (Section 8(3) Proviso).
Disposal of land provided free of cost by a State Government requires prior approval of that State Government (Section 7(j) Proviso).
Disposal of any immovable property requires prior approval of the Visitor (Section 7(2)).
The Act includes provisions for transitional arrangements and powers to remove difficulties (Sections 48, 49).

title: THE BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS ACT, 2016
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a national standards body for the harmonious development of the activities of standardisation, conformity assessment and quality assurance of goods, articles, processes, systems and services and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to goods, articles, processes, systems, and services.

key_definitions.article: Any substance, artificial or natural, or partly artificial or partly natural, whether raw or partly or wholly processed or manufactured or handmade within India or imported into India.
key_definitions.bureau: The Bureau of Indian Standards established under section 3.
key_definitions.conformity_assessment: Demonstration that requirements as may be specified relating to an article, process, system, service, person or body are fulfilled.
key_definitions.indian_standard: The standard including any tentative or provisional standard established and published by the Bureau, in relation to any goods, article, process, system or service, indicative of the quality and specification of such goods, article, process, system or service.
key_definitions.standard_mark: The mark specified by the Bureau, and includes Hallmark, to represent conformity of goods, article, process, system or service to a particular Indian Standard or conformity to a standard, the mark of which has been established, adopted or recognised by the Bureau.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and the commencement date as notified by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'article', 'Bureau', 'conformity assessment', 'Indian Standard', 'Standard Mark', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Bureau and Constitution of Governing Council
main_sections.description: Establishes the Bureau of Indian Standards as a body corporate and outlines the constitution and functions of its Governing Council, which is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Bureau's affairs.
Details the various powers and functions that the Bureau is authorized to perform under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government to direct compulsory use of Standard Mark
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct the compulsory use of the Standard Mark for certain goods.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition to manufacture, sell, etc., certain goods without Standard Mark
main_sections.description: Prohibits the manufacture, sale, import, etc., of certain specified goods unless they bear the Standard Mark.
Specifies the penalties that can be imposed for contravening the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Bureau the power to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Prohibition to publish, reproduce or record Indian Standards without authorization from the Bureau (Section 11).
Licence or certificate of conformity can be granted for goods or articles conforming to a standard (Section 13).
Certification of Standard Mark for jewellers and sellers of certain specified goods or articles (Section 14).
Prohibition to import, sell, exhibit, etc., goods that do not conform to the Standard Mark where its use is compulsory (Section 15).
Obligations of licence holders, sellers, etc., to ensure conformity to standards (Section 18).

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the Act, including imprisonment and/or fine (Section 29).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bureau of Indian Standards, Certification Officers, and potentially other authorities as empowered by the Act or rules/regulations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of search and seizure (Section 28), imposition of penalties for contravention (Section 29), and compensation for non-conforming goods (Section 31).

rights: Right to use the Standard Mark upon obtaining a licence or certificate of conformity (Section 13).
Right to appeal against certain orders or decisions made under the Act (Section 34).
duties: Duty to comply with Indian Standards for goods, articles, processes, systems, and services.
Duty of licence holders, sellers, etc., to ensure conformity to standards (Section 18).
obligations: Obligation to obtain necessary licenses or certificates for certain activities.
Obligation not to manufacture, sell, import, etc., certain goods without the Standard Mark where compulsory.

key_procedures: Grant of licence or certificate of conformity: Involves demonstrating conformity to a standard and obtaining approval from the Bureau (Section 13).
Search and Seizure: Procedures for conducting searches and seizing goods or articles suspected of contravening the Act (Section 28).
Compounding of Offence: Procedure for compounding an offence committed under the Act (Section 33).
Appeal: Procedure for filing appeals against orders or decisions made under the Act (Section 34).
administration: The Ministry or Department of the Central Government having administrative control of the Bureau.
important_notes: The Bureau is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Members, officers, and employees of the Bureau are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Section 35).
Actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act are protected (Section 36).

title: THE REAL ESTATE (REGULATION AND DEVELOPMENT) ACT, 2016
purpose: To establish the Real Estate Regulatory Authority for regulation and promotion of the real estate sector and to ensure sale of plot, apartment or building, as the case may be, or sale of real estate project, in an efficient and transparent manner and to protect the interest of consumers in the real estate sector and to establish an adjudicating mechanism for speedy dispute redressal and also to establish the Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals from the decisions, directions or orders of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority and the adjudicating officer and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union Territory of Ladakh). It applies to the regulation and promotion of the real estate sector, including sale of plots, apartments, buildings, and real estate projects.

key_definitions.adjudicating officer: The adjudicating officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 71.
key_definitions.advertisement: Any document described or issued as advertisement through any medium and includes any notice, circular or other documents or publicity in any form, informing persons about a real estate project, or offering for sale of a plot, building or apartment or inviting persons to purchase in any manner such plot, building or apartment or to make advances or deposits for such purposes.
key_definitions.agreement for sale: An agreement entered into between the promoter and the allottee.
key_definitions.allottee: In relation to a real estate project, the person to whom a plot, apartment or building, as the case may be, has been allotted, sold (whether as freehold or leasehold) or otherwise transferred by the promoter, and includes the person who subsequently acquires the said allotment through sale, transfer or otherwise but does not include a person to whom such plot, apartment or building, as the case may be, is given on rent.
key_definitions.apartment: Whether called block, chamber, dwelling unit, flat, office, showroom, shop, godown, premises, suit, tenement, unit or by any other name, means a separate and self-contained part of any immovable property, including one or more rooms or enclosed spaces, located on one or more floors or any part thereof, in a building or on a plot of land, used or intended to be used for any residential or commercial use such as residence, office, shop, showroom or godown or for carrying on any business, occupation, profession or trade, or for any other type of use ancillary to the purpose specified.
key_definitions.carpet area: The net usable floor area of an apartment, excluding the area covered by the external walls, areas under services shafts, exclusive balcony or verandah area and exclusive open terrace area, but includes the area covered by the internal partition walls of the apartment.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date from which it comes into force.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'adjudicating officer', 'advertisement', 'agreement for sale', 'allottee', 'apartment', 'Appellate Tribunal', 'appropriate Government', 'architect', 'Authority', 'building', 'carpet area', 'Chairperson', 'commencement certificate', 'common areas', 'company', 'competent authority', 'completion certificate', 'day', 'development', 'development works', 'engineer', 'estimated cost of real estate project', 'external development works'.

main_sections.section_title: Prior registration of real estate project with Real Estate Regulatory Authority
main_sections.description: Mandates prior registration of real estate projects with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority.
Outlines the functions and duties that promoters are required to undertake.
Specifies the rights and duties that allottees are entitled to and must adhere to.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Real Estate Regulatory Authority
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and incorporation of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Real Estate Appellate Tribunal
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal for hearing appeals.
Details the punishment for failing to register a real estate project as required by Section 3.

important_rules: Promoters must obtain prior registration of real estate projects with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority before marketing or selling.
Promoters have specific functions and duties, including adhering to sanctioned plans and project specifications.
Allottees have defined rights and duties in relation to real estate projects.
The Act establishes a Real Estate Regulatory Authority to regulate and promote the sector.
An Appellate Tribunal is established to hear appeals against decisions of the Authority and adjudicating officers.
Penalties are prescribed for contraventions of various provisions of the Act.

penalties: Punishment for nonregistration under section 3.
Penalty for contravention of section 4.
Penalty for contravention of other provisions of this Act.
Penalty for nonregistration and contravention under sections 9 and 10.
Penalty for failure to comply with orders of Authority or Appellate Tribunal by promoter, real estate agent, or allottee.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Real Estate Regulatory Authority, Adjudicating Officer, and Real Estate Appellate Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of penalties, recovery of interest or penalty or compensation, and enforcement of orders by the Authority and the Appellate Tribunal. Cognizance of offences is also provided for.

rights: Rights of allottees (detailed in Section 19).
duties: Duties of promoter (detailed in Section 11).
Duties of allottees (detailed in Section 19).
obligations: Obligations of promoter regarding advertisement or prospectus (Section 12).
Obligations of promoter regarding taking deposits or advance payments (Section 13).
Obligations of promoter regarding adherence to sanctioned plans (Section 14).
Obligations of promoter in case of transfer of a project (Section 15).
Obligations of promoter regarding insurance of real estate project (Section 16).
Obligations of Authority consequent upon lapse or revocation of registration (Section 8).

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of real estate projects (Sections 3, 4, 5).
Procedure for extension and revocation of registration (Sections 6, 7).
Procedure for registration of real estate agents (Section 9).
Procedure for filing complaints with the Authority or adjudicating officer (Section 31).
Procedure for adjudication of disputes (Sections 71, 72).
Procedure for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal (Sections 44, 58).
administration: The Real Estate Regulatory Authority (established under Section 20) and the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal (established under Section 43) are the primary administrative bodies. The Central Advisory Council (established under Section 41) also plays a role.
important_notes: The Act came into force on different dates for different provisions, with the initial commencement being May 1, 2016.
The Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh since October 30, 2019.
Section 89 states that this Act has overriding effect, meaning it supersedes other laws to the extent of inconsistency.

title: THE NATIONAL WATERWAYS ACT, 2016
purpose: To make provisions for existing national waterways and to provide for the declaration of certain inland waterways to be national waterways and also to provide for the regulation and development of the said waterways for the purposes of shipping and navigation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to inland waterways in India declared as national waterways for the purposes of shipping and navigation. The Union Government is responsible for their control and development.

key_definitions.national_waterway: An inland waterway declared by section 2 of the National Waterways Act, 2016, to be a national waterway. Any other waterway declared by Parliament by law to be a national waterway shall also be deemed to be a national waterway, and the provisions of the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985, shall apply with necessary modifications.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the National Waterways Act, 2016, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Existing national waterways and declaration of certain inland waterways as national waterways
main_sections.description: Confirms existing national waterways (sl. no. 1 to 5 in the Schedule) continue to be national waterways for shipping and navigation. It also declares inland waterways (sl. no. 6 to 111 in the Schedule) as national waterways for the same purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of control and development by Union of waterways specified in Schedule for certain purposes
main_sections.description: Declares that it is in the public interest for the Union to take control of the regulation and development of the waterways specified in the Schedule for shipping and navigation, as provided in the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 82 of 1985
main_sections.description: Amends clause (h) of section 2 of the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985, to define 'national waterway' as declared by section 2 of the National Waterways Act, 2016, and provides for future declarations by Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of certain enactments and saving
main_sections.description: Repeals five specific Acts related to national waterways enacted prior to 2016. It includes a saving clause stating that anything done or action taken under the repealed Acts, if in conformity with the provisions of this Act, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: All waterways declared as national waterways are for the purposes of shipping and navigation.
The Union Government has the authority to control and develop these national waterways.
Existing national waterways declared under previous acts continue to be national waterways under this Act.
New inland waterways are declared as national waterways by this Act.
Actions taken under repealed acts are saved if they conform to this Act.
key_procedures: Declaration of existing inland waterways as national waterways.
Declaration of new inland waterways as national waterways.
Central Government appoints the commencement date through notification.
Amendment of definition of 'national waterway' in the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985.
administration: The Inland Waterways Authority of India (as per the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985, which is amended by this Act) likely administers this Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to consolidate and expand the network of national waterways in India.
The Schedule provides detailed geographical limits for each national waterway.
The commencement date of the Act was April 12, 2016.

title: THE DR. RAJENDRA PRASAD CENTRAL AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY ACT, 2016
purpose: To provide for the establishment and incorporation of a University by conversion of the existing Rajendra Agricultural University, Pusa, Bihar to Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University for the development of agriculture and for the furtherance of the advancement of learning and pursuit of research in agriculture and allied sciences and to declare it to be an institution of national importance.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University. Its jurisdiction for teaching, research, and extension education in agriculture and allied subjects extends to the whole country with special reference to the State of Bihar. All existing colleges, directorates, research stations, experiment stations, and Krishi Vigyan Kendras of the Rajendra Agricultural University become constituent units.

key_definitions.agriculture: Includes the basic and applied sciences of soil and water management, crop production (including all garden crops), control of plants, pests and diseases, horticulture (including floriculture), animal husbandry (including veterinary and dairy science), fisheries, forestry (including farm forestry), home science, agricultural engineering and technology, marketing and processing of agricultural and animal husbandry products, and land use and management.
key_definitions.extension education: Refers to educational activities concerned with the training of orchardists, farmers, and other groups serving agriculture, horticulture, fisheries, and improved practices related thereto, and the various phases of scientific technology related to agriculture and agricultural production, including post-harvest technology and marketing.
key_definitions.University: Means the Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University established under this Act.
key_definitions.academic staff: Includes such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.employee: Means any person appointed by the University and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.teachers: Means Professors, Associate Professors, Assistant Professors, Teaching Faculty Members and their equivalents appointed for imparting instruction or conducting research or extension education programmes or a combination of these in the University, college or any institute maintained by the University and designated as teachers by the Ordinances.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University as an institution of national importance.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'agriculture', 'extension education', 'University', 'academic staff', 'employee', and 'teachers'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University
main_sections.description: Establishes and incorporates the Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University as a body corporate, taking over the existing Rajendra Agricultural University. It specifies the headquarters at Pusa, Bihar, and the University's perpetual succession and common seal.

Outlines the objects of the University, including imparting education in agriculture and allied sciences, conducting research, undertaking extension education programs (especially in Bihar), promoting partnerships, and undertaking other related activities.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research in agriculture, disseminating research findings, granting diplomas and degrees, conferring honorary degrees, establishing and maintaining colleges and research units, creating posts, awarding fellowships, determining admission standards, providing accommodation, regulating discipline, fixing fees, borrowing money, receiving donations, and generally performing acts conducive to its objects.

Defines the jurisdiction of the University for teaching, research, and extension education to cover the entire country, with a special focus on Bihar. It also specifies that existing institutions of the Rajendra Agricultural University will be constituent units.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all irrespective of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, without imposing religious tests. It allows for special provisions for women, persons with disability, and weaker sections, including Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and outlines the Visitor's powers to inspect and inquire into the University's functioning and finances, with provisions for notice and representation by the University.

important_rules: The University shall be open to all persons irrespective of sex, caste, creed, race, or class, and no religious test shall be imposed for appointment or admission, with exceptions for special provisions for employment or admission of women, persons with disability, or weaker sections.
The University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal, and shall sue and be sued in its own name.
The University shall have the power to grant diplomas, certificates, degrees, and other academic distinctions, and to withdraw them for good and sufficient cause.
The University's jurisdiction for teaching, research, and extension education extends to the whole country with special reference to the State of Bihar.
All existing colleges, directorates, research stations, experiment stations, and Krishi Vigyan Kendras of the Rajendra Agricultural University shall be constituent units of the new University.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement through the University's own disciplinary measures and potentially by the Visitor (President of India) through inspections and inquiries.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of University authorities, statutes, ordinances, and regulations, and the disciplinary powers vested in the University. The Visitor's role also includes oversight and inquiry.

rights: The right to be admitted or appointed without discrimination based on religion, caste, etc. (with provisions for affirmative action).
The right to appeal in disciplinary cases against students.
The right to appear and be heard during inspections or inquiries conducted by the Visitor.
The right to make representations to the Visitor.
duties: Duty to impart education in agriculture and allied sciences.
Duty to further advancement of learning and research in agriculture and allied sciences.
Duty to undertake extension education programs, particularly in Bihar.
Duty to promote partnerships with national and international institutions.
Duty to be open to all classes, castes, and creeds.
Duty to cooperate with the Visitor during inspections and inquiries.
Duty to communicate the results of inspections and inquiries and the action taken to the Visitor.
obligations: Obligation to establish and maintain colleges, campuses, Krishi Vigyan Kendras, and other research units.
Obligation to create teaching, research, extension education, administrative, and ministerial posts.
Obligation to supervise student residences and promote their health and general welfare.
Obligation to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees.
Obligation to fix, demand, and receive fees and other charges as prescribed.
Obligation to borrow money with the approval of the Central Government.
Obligation to receive benefactions, donations, and gifts and manage property for its purposes.

key_procedures: Making of Statutes: The power to make Statutes rests with the University, subject to their being made in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
Making of Ordinances: The power to make Ordinances rests with the University, subject to their being made in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

Conduct of Inspections and Inquiries by the Visitor: The Visitor gives notice to the University, the University has 30 days (or as determined by the Visitor) to make representations, and then the Visitor may proceed with the inspection/inquiry. The University can appoint a representative.

Reporting to the Visitor: The Vice-Chancellor communicates the results of inspection/inquiry and the Visitor's views/advice to the Board. The Board communicates its proposed or taken action back to the Visitor.
administration: The Act implies that the administration of the University is carried out by its various officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Comptroller) and authorities (Board of Management, Academic Council, Research Council, Extension Education Council, Finance Committee, Faculties, Board of Studies). The Central Government has oversight, particularly in matters of commencement and borrowing.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act is to be appointed by the Central Government through a notification.
The University may establish campuses at other places within its jurisdiction.
Special provisions may be made for the employment or admission of women, persons with disability, or persons belonging to weaker sections of society.

title: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016
purpose: To provide for the establishment of funds under the public accounts of India and the public accounts of each State for monies received from user agencies towards compensatory afforestation and related charges, to constitute an authority at the national and state levels for fund administration, and to utilize collected monies for afforestation, forest protection, infrastructure development, and other related activities, as directed by the Supreme Court.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to monies received from user agencies for diversion of forest land under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980. It establishes national and state-level funds and authorities for their management and utilization.

key_definitions.ad_hoc_Authority: The ad hoc Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority constituted under a Supreme Court order.
key_definitions.compensatory_afforestation: Afforestation done in lieu of forest land diversion for non-forestry use under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
key_definitions.environmental_services: Includes provision of goods (wood, non-timber forest products, water), services (grazing, tourism, wildlife protection), regulating services (flood moderation, carbon sequestration), and supporting services (biodiversity, nutrient cycling).
key_definitions.national_Authority: National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority.
key_definitions.national_Fund: The National Compensatory Afforestation Fund established under section 3.
key_definitions.net_present_value: Quantification of environmental services for diverted forest land, determined by an expert committee.
key_definitions.penal_compensatory_afforestation: Afforestation work undertaken in addition to compensatory afforestation for non-forestry activities carried out without prior approval.
key_definitions.state_Authority: State Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority.
key_definitions.state_Fund: State Compensatory Afforestation Fund established by each State.
key_definitions.user_agency: Any person, organization, company, or government department requesting diversion or using forest land for non-forest purposes.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, with subsequent applicability to Union territories), and the provision for its commencement date.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'ad hoc Authority', 'compensatory afforestation', 'environmental services', 'National Authority', 'National Fund', 'net present value', 'penal compensatory afforestation', 'State Authority', 'State Fund', and 'user agency'.

Establishes the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund under the public account of India, its management by the National Authority, and specifies what monies are to be credited to it, including those from the ad hoc Authority and a portion from State Funds.

Provides for the establishment of a State Compensatory Afforestation Fund under the public account of each State, managed by the State Authority, and lists the monies to be credited to it, including unspent balances, transfers from the National Fund, and monies realized from user agencies.
Details the constitution of the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority.
Details the constitution of the State Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority in each State.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of National Authority
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the National Authority in managing the National Fund and undertaking related activities.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of State Authority
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the State Authority in managing the State Fund and undertaking related activities within the respective State.
