Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the National Authority and State Authorities for the effective implementation of the Act.

important_rules: Monies collected from user agencies towards compensatory afforestation, additional compensatory afforestation, penal compensatory afforestation, and net present value are to be credited to the National Fund and State Funds.
The National Fund shall receive 10% of funds realized from user agencies in each State that are credited directly into the State Fund.

The National Fund and State Funds are to be utilized for undertaking artificial regeneration (plantations), assisted natural regeneration, protection of forests, forest-related infrastructure development, Green India Programme, wildlife protection, and other related activities.
An independent system of concurrent monitoring and evaluation should be evolved and implemented through the Compensatory Afforestation Fund to ensure effective and proper utilization of funds.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: National Authority and State Authorities, under the overall guidance and directions of the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment and management of the National and State Funds, constitution of National and State Authorities, and the power of the Central Government to issue directions.

rights: Right to utilize funds for specified afforestation and forest conservation activities.
Right to receive grants-in-aid, loans, or donations for the National Authority.
duties: Duty to establish and manage National and State Funds.
Duty to ensure transparent and effective utilization of collected funds.
Duty to undertake compensatory afforestation and related activities.
Duty to submit to audit and annual reports.
obligations: Obligation to deposit monies received from user agencies into the respective funds.
Obligation of States to transfer 10% of realized funds to the National Fund.
Obligation to comply with rules and directions issued under the Act.

key_procedures: Establishment of the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund and State Compensatory Afforestation Funds.
Constitution of the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority and State Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authorities.
Disbursement and utilization of funds from the National and State Funds for specified purposes.
Accounting, audit, and annual reporting of fund management and activities.
Transfer of monies collected by State Governments and Union territory Administrations to the National Fund upon its establishment.
administration: The Central Government, through the National Authority and State Governments through State Authorities.
important_notes: The Act was enacted based on Supreme Court orders and observations concerning the creation and utilization of compensatory afforestation funds.
The Act ensures that funds collected are not treated as funds under Article 266 and 283 of the Constitution, as per Supreme Court directions.
The Act aims to address the accumulation of unspent funds by establishing a permanent institutional mechanism.
The Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

title: The Specified Bank Notes (Cessation of Liabilities) Act, 2017
purpose: To provide for the cessation of liabilities on specified bank notes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, in the public interest.
scope: This Act applies to specified bank notes (bank notes of the denominational value of five hundred rupees or one thousand rupees of the series existing on or before the 8th day of November, 2016) and individuals, companies, and entities within India. It defines specific provisions related to their exchange, holding, and penalties for contravention.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The 31st day of December, 2016.
key_definitions.grace_period: The period to be specified by the Central Government, by notification, during which specified bank notes can be deposited.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.reserve_bank: The Reserve Bank of India constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
key_definitions.specified_bank_note: A bank note of the denominational value of five hundred rupees or one thousand rupees of the series existing on or before the 8th day of November, 2016.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Specified Bank Notes (Cessation of Liabilities) Act, 2017' and deems it to have come into force on December 31, 2016.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'grace period', 'notification', 'Reserve Bank', and 'specified bank note'. It also states that undefined terms will take their meanings from the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, or the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

main_sections.section_title: Specified bank notes to cease to be liability of Reserve Bank or Central Government
main_sections.description: Declares that from the appointed day, specified bank notes, which have ceased to be legal tender, will no longer be liabilities of the Reserve Bank or have the guarantee of the Central Government.

Outlines provisions for the exchange of specified bank notes within the grace period for specific individuals (e.g., citizens outside India during a certain period) or classes of persons. It also details the Reserve Bank's role in crediting the value of notes to compliant bank accounts and the process for aggrieved persons to make representations.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on holding transferring or receiving specified bank notes
main_sections.description: Prohibits holding, transferring, or receiving specified bank notes from the appointed day, with certain exceptions, including limited holding for study/research, by authorized agencies, or by court order.
Specifies penalties for knowingly and willfully making false declarations or statements when tendering specified bank notes under section 4.
Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of section 5, which prohibits holding, transferring, or receiving specified bank notes.

Deals with offenses committed by companies, making them and their responsible individuals liable. It also addresses situations where offenses are committed with the consent or connivance of directors or officers.
Empowers Magistrate courts to impose fines for contraventions of the Act, notwithstanding section 29 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act by the Government, the Reserve Bank, or their officers.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, subject to parliamentary review.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, within a specified period.
Repeals the Specified Bank Notes (Cessation of Liabilities) Ordinance, 2016, and states that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

important_rules: Specified bank notes (INR 500 and INR 1000 denominations issued before Nov 8, 2016) cease to be liabilities of the Reserve Bank and do not have the guarantee of the Central Government from December 31, 2016.
Holding, transferring, or receiving specified bank notes is prohibited from December 31, 2016, with exceptions for limited quantities for study/research, authorized entities, or by court order.

Exchange of specified bank notes within the grace period is allowed for specific categories of persons, such as citizens who were outside India during the demonetization period, subject to conditions.
False declarations or statements made during the exchange process can lead to fines up to fifty thousand rupees or five times the value of the notes, whichever is higher.
Contravention of the prohibition on holding, transferring, or receiving specified bank notes can result in fines up to ten thousand rupees or five times the value of the notes, whichever is higher.

penalties: For contravention of section 4 (false declarations/statements): Fine up to fifty thousand rupees or five times the amount of the face value of the specified bank notes tendered, whichever is higher.

For contravention of section 5 (holding, transferring, or receiving): Fine up to ten thousand rupees or five times the amount of the face value of the specified bank notes involved, whichever is higher.
Offences by companies: The company and responsible individuals are liable.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Reserve Bank of India and the Central Government (through its agencies and rule-making powers). Magistrate courts are empowered to impose fines.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of fines as specified in the Act. The Reserve Bank is involved in facilitating exchange and verifications. The Central Government has the power to make rules and orders to remove difficulties.

rights: Right to exchange specified bank notes within the grace period under specific conditions (e.g., being outside India).
Right to deposit notes in a KYC-compliant bank account if Reserve Bank is satisfied with genuine reasons for delay.
Right to make a representation to the Central Board of the Reserve Bank if aggrieved by a refusal to credit note value.
Limited right to hold a small number of specified bank notes (up to 10 or 25 for numismatic purposes) after the grace period.
Protection for actions taken in good faith by Government, RBI, and their officers.
duties: Duty not to hold, transfer, or receive specified bank notes after the appointed day (with exceptions).
Duty to make true and accurate declarations or statements when tendering specified bank notes.
Duty for companies to ensure compliance and for responsible individuals to prevent contraventions.
obligations: Obligation for individuals and entities to comply with the cessation of liabilities on specified bank notes.
Obligation for the Reserve Bank to specify procedures for exchange and to verify reasons for delayed deposits.
Obligation for the Central Government to specify grace periods and conditions via notification.

key_procedures: Tendering specified bank notes for exchange within the grace period by eligible persons with declarations to the Reserve Bank.
Reserve Bank verification of reasons for delayed deposit and crediting value to a KYC-compliant bank account.
Making a representation to the Central Board of the Reserve Bank within fourteen days of refusal of credit.
Making rules by the Central Government and laying them before Parliament.
Removing difficulties by the Central Government through orders published in the Official Gazette, subject to parliamentary review.
administration: The Central Government and the Reserve Bank of India.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on December 31, 2016.
The grace period for depositing specified bank notes is to be specified by the Central Government through notification.
Holding of up to 10 notes (or 25 for numismatic purposes) is permitted after the grace period.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are considered valid under this Act.

title: The Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
purpose: To make provision for the levy and collection of tax on intra-State supply of goods or services or both by the Union territories and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Ladakh, Chandigarh, and other territories. It covers intra-State supplies of goods or services or both.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which the provisions of this Act shall come into force.
key_definitions.commissioner: The Commissioner of Union territory tax appointed under section 3.
key_definitions.designated_authority: Such authority as may be notified by the Commissioner.
key_definitions.exempt_supply: Supply of any goods or services or both which attracts nil rate of tax or which may be exempt from tax under section 8, or under section 6 of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, and includes non-taxable supply.
key_definitions.existing_law: Any law, notification, order, rule or regulation relating to levy and collection of duty or tax on goods or services or both passed or made before the commencement of this Act by Parliament or any Authority or person having the power to make such law, notification, order, rule or regulation.
key_definitions.government: The Administrator or any Authority or officer authorised to act as Administrator by the Central Government.
key_definitions.output_tax: In relation to a taxable person, the Union territory tax chargeable under this Act on taxable supply of goods or services or both made by him or by his agent but excludes tax payable by him on reverse charge basis.
key_definitions.union_territory: The territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; Lakshadweep; Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu; Ladakh; Chandigarh; or other territory. Each specified territory is considered a separate Union territory.
key_definitions.union_territory_tax: The tax levied under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent (Union territories), and the commencement date.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'exempt supply', 'Union territory', and 'Union territory tax'.
Empowers the Administrator to appoint Commissioners and other officers for the purpose of the Act, deeming existing law officers as appointed under this Act.
Specifies the powers and duties of Union territory tax officers, including the delegation of powers by the Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Authorisation of officers of central tax as proper officer in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Authorises officers appointed under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act to act as proper officers for the purposes of this Act under specified conditions, preventing parallel proceedings.

Provides for the levy and collection of Union territory tax on intra-State supplies of goods or services or both, excluding alcoholic liquor for human consumption. It also specifies provisions for petroleum products, reverse charge mechanism, and electronic commerce operators.

main_sections.section_title: Power to grant exemption from tax
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to grant exemptions from tax, either generally or in specific cases, based on public interest and recommendations of the Council.

main_sections.section_title: Power not to recover Goods and Services Tax not levied or short-levied as a result of general practice
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to direct that Union territory tax not levied or short-levied due to a general practice shall not be recovered, subject to certain conditions and recommendations.
Deals with the migration of existing taxpayers to the new tax regime.

main_sections.section_title: Application of provisions of Central Goods and Services Tax Act
main_sections.description: States that provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act are applicable to this Act.
Confers the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule related to the levy and collection of Union territory tax on intra-State supplies of goods or services or both (Section 7(1)).
Rules regarding the levy of Union territory tax on specific items like petroleum products, to be notified by the Central Government (Section 7(2)).
Rules for payment of tax on a reverse charge basis by the recipient for specified categories of supply of goods or services or both (Section 7(2) and 7(4)).
Rules for electronic commerce operators to pay tax if they supply specified services through their platform (Section 7(5)).
Rules for granting exemptions from tax, either absolutely or subject to conditions, in public interest (Section 8(1) and 8(2)).
Rules for the migration of existing taxpayers (Section 17).
Rules for transitional arrangements for input tax credit (Section 18).
Rules for transitional provisions relating to job work (Section 19).
Miscellaneous transitional provisions (Section 20).
Rules for the application of provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act (Section 21).

rights: Right to claim input tax credit (implied through sections on transitional arrangements and utilization of credit).
Right to receive exemption from tax under specified conditions (Section 8).
Right to seek Advance Ruling on tax liability (Chapter VII).
duties: Duty to pay Union territory tax on intra-State supplies of goods or services or both (Section 7(1)).
Duty to pay tax on a reverse charge basis where applicable (Section 7(2) and 7(4)).
Duty of electronic commerce operators to pay tax for certain supplies made through their platform (Section 7(5)).
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation to register under the Act if liable.
Obligation to maintain accounts and records as prescribed.
Obligation to assist proper officers in carrying out their duties (Section 11).

key_procedures: Levy and collection of tax on intra-State supplies of goods or services or both (Section 7).
Granting of exemptions from tax by the Central Government (Section 8).
Migration of existing taxpayers (Section 17).
Transitional arrangements for input tax credit (Section 18).
Procedures for Advance Rulings (Chapter VII).
Procedures related to Inspection, Search, Seizure and Arrest (Chapter V).
Procedures for Demands and Recovery (Chapter VI).
administration: The Administrator, Commissioners, and other officers appointed under the Act. Officers of central tax are also authorised as proper officers under certain circumstances.
important_notes: The Act is to be read in conjunction with the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, the State Goods and Services Tax Act, and the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act for terms and expressions not defined within this Act.
Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The levy of tax on certain petroleum products is subject to notification by the Central Government.
Exemptions from tax are granted in public interest and on the recommendation of the Council.
The Act can be amended by subsequent amending acts as listed.

title: The Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017
purpose: To provide for compensation to the States for the loss of revenue arising on account of implementation of the goods and services tax in pursuance of the provisions of the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to States and Union territories as defined under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act and the Union Territories Goods and Services Tax Act.

key_definitions.central tax: Central goods and services tax levied and collected under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act.
key_definitions.cess: Goods and services tax compensation cess levied under section 8.
key_definitions.compensation: An amount, in the form of goods and services tax compensation, as determined under section 7.
key_definitions.transition period: A period of five years from the transition date.
key_definitions.base year: The financial year ending 31st March, 2016, for the purpose of calculating compensation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'central tax', 'cess', 'compensation', 'transition period', 'base year', 'State', and 'taxable supply'.
Specifies the projected nominal growth rate of revenue subsumed for a State during the transition period as fourteen per cent. per annum.
Designates the financial year ending 31st March, 2016, as the base year for calculating compensation.
Outlines the methodology for calculating the base year revenue for a State, including the types of taxes subsumed into GST and specific exclusions.
Explains how to calculate the projected revenue for any year by applying the projected growth rate over the base year revenue.
Details the process for calculating and releasing compensation to States, including provisional and final calculations and adjustments for excess releases.
This section deals with the levy and collection of the goods and services tax compensation cess.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, on the recommendations of the Council.

important_rules: Rule 1: Compensation to States for revenue loss due to GST implementation is payable during the transition period (section 7(1)).
Rule 2: Compensation is provisionally calculated and released every two months, and finally calculated annually after audited revenue figures are received (section 7(2)).
Rule 3: The projected growth rate of revenue subsumed for a State during the transition period is fixed at fourteen per cent. per annum (section 3).
Rule 4: The financial year ending 31st March, 2016, is designated as the base year for compensation calculation (section 4).
Rule 5: Base year revenue includes revenue from taxes subsumed into GST, net of refunds, with specific exclusions for certain petroleum products and alcoholic liquor (section 5).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through notifications and rules, and potentially other authorities as specified in the Act and related legislation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the calculation and release of compensation as per section 7, and through the levy and collection of cess as per section 8. Rules made under the Act also facilitate enforcement.

rights: Right of States to receive compensation for revenue loss due to GST implementation during the transition period.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to provide compensation to the States.
Duty of States to provide revenue figures as required for compensation calculation.
Duty to comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to levy and collect the goods and services tax compensation cess (section 8).
Obligation to credit the proceeds of the cess to the Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund (section 10).
Obligation for the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India to audit revenue figures for compensation calculation (section 5(5), 7(2), 7(3)(b), 7(4)(b)).

key_procedures: Calculation of projected revenue for any year: Apply the projected growth rate over the base year revenue (section 6).
Calculation of annual compensation: Subtract actual collected revenue from projected revenue for the financial year (section 7(3)).
Calculation of provisional compensation: Calculate projected revenue on a pro-rata basis for the two-month period and subtract actual collected revenue for that period (section 7(4)).
Release of compensation: Provisionally released every two months and finally calculated annually (section 7(2)).
administration: The Central Government, with the recommendations of the Goods and Services Tax Council for making rules.
important_notes: The Act is based on the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016.
The Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh are also covered by the Act vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.
The definitions of 'State' and 'Union territories' are linked to the Central Goods and Services Tax Act and the Union Territories Goods and Services Tax Act.

title: The Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017
purpose: To consolidate the laws relating to admiralty jurisdiction, legal proceedings in connection with vessels, their arrest, detention, sale and other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to every vessel, irrespective of the owner's residence or domicile. Excludes inland vessels as defined in the Inland Vessels Act, 1917, vessels under construction not launched (unless notified by Central Government), warships, naval auxiliaries, or other vessels owned/operated by the Central or State Government for non-commercial purposes, and foreign vessels used for non-commercial purposes (unless notified). Jurisdiction extends to territorial waters and can be extended by notification. Applies to maritime claims as defined in Section 4.

key_definitions.admiralty_jurisdiction: Jurisdiction exercisable by a High Court in respect of maritime claims specified in the Act.
key_definitions.admiralty_proceeding: Any proceeding before a High Court exercising admiralty jurisdiction.
key_definitions.arrest: Detention or restriction for removal of a vessel by order of a High Court to secure a maritime claim, including seizure for judgment satisfaction.
key_definitions.goods: Any property including live animals, containers, pallets, etc., carried on or under the deck of a vessel.
key_definitions.high_court: Includes High Courts of Calcutta, Bombay, Madras, Karnataka, Gujarat, Orissa, Kerala, Judicature at Hyderabad, and any other notified High Court.
key_definitions.maritime_claim: A claim referred to in Section 4.
key_definitions.maritime_lien: A maritime claim against the owner, demise charterer, manager, or operator of a vessel, as specified in Section 9.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes any ship, boat, sailing vessel, hovercraft, offshore industry mobile unit, sunken, stranded, or abandoned vessel, and their remains, used or constructed for navigation by water.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its application to vessels (with exclusions), and outlines the commencement provisions.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including admiralty jurisdiction, maritime claim, vessel, and others.
Confers admiralty jurisdiction on High Courts over maritime claims within their territorial waters, with provisions for extension by the Central Government.

Details the various types of claims over which the High Court may exercise jurisdiction, including disputes over ownership, chartering, loss or damage, salvage, towage, pilotage, supplies, construction, port dues, crew claims, disbursements, average, sale contracts, insurance premiums, agency fees, environmental damage, and claims related to sunken or abandoned vessels.

Empowers the High Court to order the arrest of a vessel to secure a maritime claim, outlining conditions for arrest based on owner liability, demise charterer liability, mortgages, ownership disputes, or maritime liens.
Allows the High Court to exercise admiralty jurisdiction through actions against a person in respect of any maritime claim.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on actions in personam in certain cases
main_sections.description: Sets conditions for entertaining actions in personam for specific maritime claims (collision, maneuvers, non-compliance with collision regulations), requiring the cause of action to arise in India or the defendant to reside/carry on business in India. It also addresses prior proceedings in foreign courts.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting of rights on sale of vessels
main_sections.description: States that a vessel sold by the High Court in admiralty jurisdiction vests in the purchaser free from all encumbrances, liens, attachments, and registered mortgages.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: Rule: A vessel can be arrested to provide security against a maritime claim if the court believes the owner or demise charterer is liable, or if the claim is based on a mortgage, ownership dispute, or maritime lien.
Rule: The High Court can order the arrest of any other vessel in lieu of the vessel against which a maritime claim has been made, subject to certain conditions.
Rule: Actions in personam for collision-related claims generally require the cause of action to arise in India or the defendant to reside/carry on business in India.
Rule: A vessel sold by the High Court vests in the purchaser free from all prior encumbrances.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: High Courts exercising admiralty jurisdiction.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders for arrest, detention, sale of vessels, and other proceedings as per the Code of Civil Procedure, subject to specific provisions of the Act.

rights: Right to bring a maritime claim against a vessel.
Right to arrest a vessel to secure a maritime claim.
Right to have maritime claims settled by the High Court.
Right to have a vessel vest in the purchaser free of encumbrances upon sale.
Rights of masters and crew for wages, repatriation, and social insurance contributions.
duties: Duty to comply with court orders regarding vessel arrest and sale.
Duty to provide security against maritime claims.
Duty to adhere to collision regulations.
Obligations of owners, charterers, managers, or operators to satisfy maritime claims.
obligations: Obligations arising from contracts relating to carriage of goods or passengers.
Obligations of employers towards crew members.
Obligations to pay port dues, canal charges, etc.
Obligations to prevent and mitigate environmental damage from vessels.

key_procedures: Filing an admiralty proceeding in the High Court.
Applying for the arrest of a vessel in rem to secure a maritime claim.
Exercising admiralty jurisdiction through actions in personam.
Sale of a vessel by the High Court to satisfy a claim.
Transfer of proceedings by the Supreme Court.
administration: The Central Government, through notifications and rule-making powers.
important_notes: The Act excludes certain types of vessels and purposes from its application.
The High Court has the power to settle accounts between parties and order the sale of a vessel.
The Act aims to consolidate and simplify admiralty law in India.

title: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 2017
purpose: To provide for the extension of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh) and extends the provisions of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 to this region.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 2017 and states its commencement date as July 8, 2017.

main_sections.section_title: Extension and amendment of Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
main_sections.description: Extends the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, along with all its rules, notifications, schemes, and orders, to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It also amends the principal Act by omitting the words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' from its sub-section (2) of section 1, making the principal Act fully applicable to the region.

Repeals the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Ordinance, 2017. It also states that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be considered as done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (implied by extension of the principal Act)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and its associated rules, notifications, schemes, and orders.

key_procedures: Extension of the principal Act and associated legal instruments to Jammu and Kashmir.
Amendment of the principal Act to remove the exception for Jammu and Kashmir.
Repeal of the Ordinance and continuation of actions taken under it.
administration: Central Government (implied by the nature of the IGST Act)
important_notes: The Act was made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.

title: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
purpose: To make a provision for the levy and collection of tax on inter-State supply of goods or services or both by the Central Government and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to inter-State supplies of goods or services or both.

key_definitions.Central Goods and Services Tax Act: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
key_definitions.central tax: The tax levied and collected under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act.
key_definitions.continuous journey: A journey for which a single or more than one ticket or invoice is issued at the same time, either by a single supplier of service or through an agent acting on behalf of more than one supplier of service, and which involves no stopover between any of the legs of the journey for which one or more separate tickets or invoices are issued.
key_definitions.customs frontiers of India: The limits of a customs area as defined in section 2 of the Customs Act, 1962.
key_definitions.export of goods: Taking goods out of India to a place outside India.
key_definitions.export of services: The supply of any service when the supplier is located in India, the recipient is located outside India, the place of supply is outside India, payment is received in convertible foreign exchange (or Indian rupees where permitted), and the supplier and recipient are not merely establishments of a distinct person.
key_definitions.fixed establishment: A place (other than the registered place of business) characterized by a sufficient degree of permanence and suitable structure in terms of human and technical resources to supply or receive and use services for its own needs.
key_definitions.import of goods: Bringing goods into India from a place outside India.
key_definitions.import of services: The supply of any service where the supplier is located outside India, the recipient is located in India, and the place of supply is in India.
key_definitions.integrated tax: The integrated goods and services tax levied under this Act.
key_definitions.intermediary: A broker, an agent or any other person who arranges or facilitates the supply of goods or services or both, or securities, between two or more persons, but does not include a person who supplies such goods or services or both or securities on his own account.
key_definitions.online information and database access o: Services whose delivery is mediated by information technology over the internet or an electronic network and the nature of which renders their supply impossible to ensure in the absence of information technology.
key_definitions.taxable territory: The territory to which the provisions of this Act apply.
key_definitions.zero-rated supply: As assigned in section 16 of the Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provisions for its commencement through notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'integrated tax', 'export of goods/services', 'import of goods/services', 'supply', and references to other related Acts.
Empowers the Board to appoint central tax officers for exercising powers under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Authorisation of officers of State tax or Union territory tax as proper officer in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Authorizes officers appointed under State or Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Acts to be proper officers for the purposes of this Act, subject to specified conditions.

Provides for the levy and collection of integrated goods and services tax on all inter-State supplies of goods or services or both, except alcoholic liquor for human consumption. It also covers levy on imported goods and specifies conditions for levying tax on certain goods like petroleum products.

main_sections.section_title: Power to grant exemption from tax
main_sections.description: Confers power on the Government to grant exemption from tax on the recommendations of the Council.
Defines what constitutes an inter-State supply of goods or services or both.
Defines what constitutes a zero-rated supply.

important_rules: Integrated tax shall be levied on all inter-State supplies of goods or services or both at rates not exceeding forty percent, as notified by the Government on the recommendations of the Council.
Integrated tax on goods imported into India shall be levied and collected in accordance with the provisions of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975.

The Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify categories of supply of goods or services or both, the tax on which shall be paid on reverse charge basis by the recipient.

The integrated tax on petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor spirit, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel shall be levied from such date as may be notified by the Government on the recommendations of the Council.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central tax officers appointed under the Act, and authorized State/Union Territory tax officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of officers, levy and collection of tax, and application of provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act.

rights: Right to claim refund of integrated tax paid on supply of goods to tourists leaving India (Section 15).
Right to transfer input tax credit (Section 18).
duties: Duty to pay integrated tax on inter-State supplies of goods or services or both (Section 5).
Duty to comply with provisions of the Act and related rules and regulations.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on reverse charge basis where specified (Section 5(3)).
Obligation to follow procedures for apportionment of tax and settlement of funds (Chapter VIII).

key_procedures: Levy and collection of integrated tax on inter-State supplies (Section 5).
Granting of exemption from tax by the Government (Section 6).
Determination of the place of supply for goods and services (Chapter V).
Apportionment of tax and settlement of funds between the Central Government and State Governments (Chapter VIII).
Transfer of input tax credit (Section 18).
administration: The Board and appointed central tax officers. State tax or Union territory tax officers may also be authorized.
important_notes: The Act was originally not extended to the State of Jammu and Kashmir but was later extended.
Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
Provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act are applicable to this Act where not inconsistent (Section 20).

title: The Indian Institutes of Information Technology (Public-Private Partnership) Act, 2017
purpose: To declare certain Indian Institutes of Information Technology established under public-private partnership as institutions of national importance, with the view to develop new knowledge in information technology, provide manpower of global standards for the IT industry, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to specific Indian Institutes of Information Technology (IIITs) established under public-private partnership, as listed in the Schedule, and any other IIITs established under Section 11. It covers their establishment, governance, operations, and status as institutions of national importance.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of establishment of the Institutes established under sub-section (2) of section 4.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of an Institute.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board appointed under sub-section (2) of section 14.
key_definitions.Co-ordination Forum: The Co-ordination Forum established under sub-section (1) of section 38.
key_definitions.existing Institute: An Institute mentioned in column (3) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.industry partner: An individual, trust, company, society, or financial institution, or a combination thereof, that collaborates in the establishment of an Institute under public-private partnership.
key_definitions.Institute: Any of the institutions mentioned in column (5) of the Schedule and any other Institutes established under section 11.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public-private partnership: A partnership under a scheme of the Central Government involving collaboration between the Central Government, State Government, and industry partners for the establishment of an Institute.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: The Statutes and Ordinances of an Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares each of the Institutes mentioned in the Schedule as an institution of national importance.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act.

States that existing Institutes mentioned in the Schedule and any new Institutes established under section 11 shall be body corporates with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue and be sued.

Details the consequences of incorporation, including the transfer of property, rights, debts, and liabilities, and the continuation of employment terms and conditions for existing employees. It also covers the continuation of academic courses and legal proceedings.

Outlines the objectives of each Institute, which include emerging as foremost institutions in IT and allied fields globally, advancing new knowledge and innovation, developing competent youth with innovative and entrepreneurial spirit, and promoting transparency in all its operations.

Specifies the powers and functions of an Institute, such as providing instructions in IT and allied fields, conducting research, granting degrees, creating posts and making appointments, appointing adjunct faculty, making provisions for knowledge dissemination, creating websites, determining fees, dealing with property (with government approval for immovable property disposal), receiving gifts and donations, cooperating with other institutions, establishing infrastructure, and instituting fellowships and scholarships.

main_sections.section_title: Institutes to be open to all races, creeds and classes
main_sections.description: Mandates that each Institute shall be open to all citizens irrespective of various discriminatory factors. It also states that bequests or donations with objectionable conditions will not be accepted and that admissions will be merit-based and transparent. Institutes are also designated as Central Educational Institutions for reservation purposes.
Establishes the Board of Governors as an authority of the Institute.
Details the powers and functions of the Board of Governors.
Establishes the Senate as an authority of the Institute.
Details the powers and functions of the Senate.
Establishes the Finance Committee as an authority of the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Finance Committee
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Finance Committee.
Covers the provisions related to the accounts and audit of the Institute's funds.
Establishes a Co-ordination Forum for coordination purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Functions and duties of Co-ordination Forum
main_sections.description: Specifies the functions and duties of the Co-ordination Forum.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the Institutes.

main_sections.section_title: Institute to be public authority under Right to Information Act
main_sections.description: Declares each Institute as a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Every Institute shall be open to all citizens irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, domicile, ethnicity, social or economic background.
Admissions to every program of study shall be based on merit assessed through transparent and reasonable criteria disclosed in the prospectus.
No Institute shall dispose of any land or other immovable property without the prior approval of the concerned State Government and the Central Government.
Each Institute is declared a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005, requiring transparency in its operations.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, and the Institutes themselves through their respective authorities (Board of Governors, Senate, Director).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment and governance structures defined in the Act, the powers vested in the Central Government to issue directions and make rules, and the legal status of Institutes as bodies corporate capable of suing and being sued. Specific penalties for contravention of the Act are not detailed in the provided excerpt but would typically be found in later sections or associated rules.

rights: Right to establish and operate as institutions of national importance.
Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (with restrictions on immovable property).
Right to sue and be sued.
Right to grant degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.
Right to determine and receive fees and charges.
Right to receive gifts, grants, and donations.
Right to cooperate with educational institutions globally.
Right to be a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
duties: Duty to operate as institutions of national importance.
Duty to develop new knowledge and provide skilled manpower in IT.
Duty to be open to all citizens irrespective of background.
Duty to ensure transparency in admissions, appointments, academic evaluation, administration, and finance.
Duty to comply with provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Duty to provide returns and information to the Central or State Governments.
obligations: Obligation to establish and maintain infrastructure for achieving objectives.
Obligation to ensure that employment terms and conditions for existing employees are maintained unless duly altered.
Obligation to seek prior approval from State and Central Governments for the disposal of immovable property.

key_procedures: Establishment of Institutes under public-private partnership involving Central Government, State Government, and industry partners.
Declaration of Institutes as institutions of national importance.
Incorporation of Institutes as body corporates.
Governance of Institutes through the Board of Governors, Senate, and Finance Committee.
Process for making Statutes and Ordinances by the Institute.
Procedure for receiving funds, maintaining accounts, and undergoing audits.
Establishment and functioning of the Co-ordination Forum.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules and issue directions.
Process for removing difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
administration: The administration of the Act involves the Central Government (through ministries/departments responsible for education and IT), State Governments, and the governing bodies of each Institute (Board of Governors, Senate, Director). The Co-ordination Forum also plays a role in coordination.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, not immediately upon enactment.
Disposal of immovable property by an Institute requires prior approval from the concerned State Government and the Central Government.
Each Institute is considered a Central Educational Institution for the purposes of the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006.
Transitional provisions are in place to manage the transition from existing institutes to incorporated entities under the Act.

title: THE REPEALING AND AMENDING ACT, 2017
purpose: To repeal certain enactments and to amend certain other enactments.
scope: This act applies to the repeal and amendment of specific enactments as listed in the schedules. The geographical scope is India.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the 'Repealing and Amending Act, 2017'.
This section states that the enactments specified in the First Schedule are repealed to the extent mentioned in the fourth column of that schedule.
This section states that the enactments specified in the Second Schedule are amended to the extent and in the manner mentioned in the fourth column of that schedule.

This section outlines savings provisions. It clarifies that the repeal of an enactment does not affect other enactments that have applied, incorporated, or referred to the repealed enactment. It also preserves the validity, effect, or consequences of anything already done, and any acquired rights, obligations, or liabilities. Furthermore, it ensures that existing principles of law, jurisdiction, practice, procedure, custom, privilege, restriction, exemption, office, or appointment are not affected, even if recognized or derived from a repealed enactment. Finally, it states that the repeal does not revive any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, right, title, privilege, restriction, exemption, usage, practice, procedure, or any other matter or thing that is not currently existing or in force.

important_rules: Rule: Enactments listed in the First Schedule are repealed to the extent specified.
Rule: Enactments listed in the Second Schedule are amended as detailed.
Rule: The repeal does not affect other enactments that may have used or referred to the repealed enactment.
Rule: The repeal does not affect any actions taken or rights acquired prior to the repeal.
Rule: The repeal does not revive anything that is no longer in force.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text, as this is a repealing and amending act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

rights: Preservation of rights, titles, obligations, or liabilities already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal of an enactment.
Preservation of remedies or proceedings in respect thereof.
Preservation of releases or discharges of debts, penalties, obligations, liabilities, claims, or demands.
Preservation of indemnities already granted.
duties: Preservation of obligations already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal of an enactment.
obligations: Preservation of obligations already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal of an enactment.

key_procedures: Procedure: Identification of enactments to be repealed from the First Schedule.
Procedure: Identification of enactments to be amended from the Second Schedule.
Procedure: Application of the 'Savings' clause to ensure continuity and avoid unintended consequences of repeals and amendments.
administration: Parliament of India
important_notes: The Act is a repealing and amending Act, meaning its primary function is to clean up outdated legislation and make minor corrections to existing laws.
The 'Savings' clause is extensive and aims to prevent disruption to ongoing legal matters, acquired rights, and established legal principles.
The First Schedule lists numerous historical enactments that are being repealed entirely or in part.
The Second Schedule lists a few recent enactments that are being amended, with specific changes detailed.

title: THE INDIAN INSTITUTE OF PETROLEUM AND ENERGY ACT, 2017
purpose: To declare the institution known as the Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy (IIPE) located in Vishakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. It covers its incorporation, governance, functions, powers, finances, and administration.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed under sub-section (2) of section 1 for the coming into force of this Act.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of the Institute constituted under sub-section (1) of section 5.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the General Council.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of the Institute appointed under section 20.
key_definitions.fund: The fund of the Institute to be maintained under section 24.
key_definitions.General Council: The General Council constituted under sub-section (1) of section 15.
key_definitions.Institute: The Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy incorporated under section 4.
key_definitions.President: The President of the Board appointed under clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 5.
key_definitions.Registrar: The Registrar of the Institute referred to in section 21.
key_definitions.Senate: The Senate of the Institute referred to in section 17.
key_definitions.Society: The Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy Society, Vishakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh registered under the Andhra Pradesh Societies Registration Act, 2001.
key_definitions.Statutes: Statutes of the Institute made under this Act.
key_definitions.Ordinances: Ordinances of the Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and outlines its commencement, which can be appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette, allowing for different dates for different provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy, Vishakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, as an institution of national importance.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Director', 'fund', 'General Council', 'Institute', 'President', 'Registrar', 'Senate', 'Society', 'Statutes', and 'Ordinances'.

States that the Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy is incorporated as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract. It can sue and be sued in its corporate name.

Details the constitution of the Board of Governors, including its members (President, Director ex officio, nominees from promoting companies, Indian Institute of Science, General Council, Senate, and Alumni Association). The Registrar acts as the Secretary.

Enlists the broad functions of the Institute, including nurturing education and research in petroleum and energy, providing academic programs, granting degrees, promoting research and development, fostering interaction with industry, managing its properties, receiving grants, and performing all necessary acts to achieve its objects.

Outlines the powers of the Board of Governors, which include general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs. Specific powers include taking policy decisions, laying down policies for courses, degrees, faculty recruitment, resource mobilization, loans, framing Statutes, and considering the annual report and accounts.
States that the Central Government shall have the power of administrative control over the Institute.
Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.
Provides for transitional arrangements to ensure a smooth transition to the incorporated Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Statutes, Ordinances and notifications to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates the publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and notifications in the Official Gazette and requires them to be laid before Parliament.

important_rules: The Institute is declared an institution of national importance.
The Institute shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Board of Governors is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs.
The Central Government exercises administrative control over the Institute.
Statutes and Ordinances made under the Act must be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.

rights: Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
Right to contract.
Right to sue and be sued.
Right to grant degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions.
Right to withdraw degrees, diplomas, certificates, or other academic distinctions for good and sufficient reasons.
Right to confer honorary degrees or other distinctions.
Right to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, exhibitions, prizes and medals.
Right to borrow money for the purposes of the Institute.
Right to receive gifts, grants, donations, benefactions, bequests, and transfers of properties.
duties: Duty to nurture and promote quality and excellence in education and research in petroleum and energy.
Duty to provide programs and courses of instruction and research.
Duty to manage the content, quality, design and continuous evaluation of academic and research programs.
Duty to promote research and development for the benefit of the oil, gas and petrochemical industry and the energy sector.
Duty to foster close educational and research interaction.
Duty to co-operate with educational and research institutions globally.
Duty to organize symposia, seminars, and conferences.
Duty to establish, maintain and manage halls, residences and hostels.
Duty to supervise, control and regulate the discipline of employees and students.
Duty to make arrangements for promoting the health and general welfare of employees and students.
Duty to deal with its properties for advancing its objects.
Duty to integrate new technology in the classroom.
Duty to develop and maintain an information resource centre.
Duty to provide further education to working professionals.
Duty to offer customized programs for continuing education.
Duty to encourage industry sponsorship for higher degrees.
Duty to foster creation of new knowledge and applied technology.
Duty to be proactive in supporting skill development programs.
Duty to focus on petroleum and related technologies under the umbrella of energy.
Duty to perform all necessary acts for the attainment of its objects.
obligations: The Institute is obligated to comply with the provisions of the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances.
The Board is obligated to review the acts of the Senate.
The Institute's properties are vested in it subject to the provisions of the Act.
References to the Society in contracts are deemed to be references to the Institute.
All rights and liabilities of the Society are transferred to the Institute.

key_procedures: Appointment of the President and members of the Board of Governors by the Central Government and nominations by various bodies as specified in Section 5.
The Board of Governors, subject to the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances, exercises powers related to the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs.
The framing, alteration, modification, or rescission of Statutes by the Board of Governors and their subsequent publication in the Official Gazette and laying before Parliament (Sections 32, 33, 45).
The framing, alteration, modification, or rescission of Ordinances by the Academic Council and their subsequent publication in the Official Gazette and laying before Parliament (Sections 34, 35, 45).
Granting of degrees, diplomas, certificates, etc., by the Institute and withdrawal of such academic distinctions for good and sufficient reasons (Section 9(iii)).
Setting standards of admission to the Institute through examination or other testing methods (Section 9(v)).
The Central Government exercising control over the Institute (Section 41).
The Central Government issuing orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act (Section 43).
administration: The Central Government exercises administrative control over the Institute (Section 41). Specific departments are not explicitly mentioned for day-to-day administration, but the Board of Governors and Director are key administrative figures.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The first President shall be appointed by the Central Government on such terms and conditions as it deems fit, for a period not exceeding six months from the date the first Statutes come into force.

Members of the Board are entitled to such allowances as provided for in the Statutes, but no salary is payable except to the member referred to in clause (f) of section 5 (likely referring to faculty members who might have their regular salary).

title: The Repealing and Amending (Second) Act, 2017
purpose: To repeal certain enactments and to amend certain other enactments.
scope: This act applies to India and its Parliament. It repeals and amends existing laws specified in its schedules.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Repealing and Amending (Second) Act, 2017.
States that the enactments specified in the First Schedule are hereby repealed.
States that the enactments specified in the Second Schedule are hereby amended to the extent and in the manner mentioned in the fourth column thereof.

Details the effect of the repeal, ensuring that it does not affect other enactments, validity of past actions, acquired rights, obligations, liabilities, remedies, or principles of law. It also clarifies that the repeal will not revive any jurisdiction or matter not currently in force.

important_rules: Section 2 mandates the repeal of all enactments listed in the First Schedule.
Section 3 mandates the amendment of enactments listed in the Second Schedule according to the specifications provided.
Section 4 ensures that the repeal and amendments do not invalidate past actions or affect existing rights and obligations.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be governmental authorities responsible for the administration of laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of repealing and amending existing legislation as detailed in the schedules.

rights: Rights acquired or accrued prior to the repeal remain unaffected (as per Section 4).
duties: Obligations acquired or incurred prior to the repeal remain unaffected (as per Section 4).

key_procedures: The Act's procedure involves identifying enactments for repeal and amendment through its schedules, enacting the repeal, and enacting the amendments.
Section 4 outlines the procedure for interpreting the impact of the repeal and amendments on existing legal frameworks and past actions.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but would typically fall under the Ministry of Law and Justice in India.
important_notes: The Act's primary function is to clear out obsolete laws and update others, rather than introducing new substantive law.
Section 4 is crucial for understanding the continuity of legal effects despite the repeal and amendment of specific enactments.

title: THE FUGITIVE ECONOMIC OFFENDERS ACT, 2018
purpose: To provide for measures to deter fugitive economic offenders from evading the process of law in India by staying outside the jurisdiction of Indian courts, and to preserve the sanctity of the rule of law in India.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to any individual who is, or becomes, a fugitive economic offender on or after the date of coming into force of this Act (deemed to have come into force on 21st April, 2018).

key_definitions.administrator: An Administrator appointed under sub-section (1) of section 15.
key_definitions.benami_property_and_benami_transaction: Have the same meanings as assigned to them under clauses (8) and (9) respectively of section 2 of the Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (45 of 1988).
key_definitions.contracting_state: Any country or place outside India in respect of which arrangements have been made by the Central Government with the Government of such country through a treaty or otherwise.
key_definitions.deputy_director: The Deputy Director appointed under sub-section (1) of section 49 of the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002 (15 of 2003).
key_definitions.director: The Director appointed under sub-section (1) of section 49 of the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002 (15 of 2003).
key_definitions.fugitive_economic_offender: Any individual against whom a warrant for arrest in relation to a Scheduled Offence has been issued by any Court in India, who has left India so as to avoid criminal prosecution or, being abroad, refuses to return to India to face criminal prosecution.
key_definitions.key_managerial_personnel: Has the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (51) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013).
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.person: Includes an individual, Hindu Undivided Family, company, trust, partnership, limited liability partnership, association of persons or body of individuals (whether incorporated or not), every artificial juridical person, and any agency, office or branch owned or controlled by any of the above.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.proceeds_of_crime: Any property derived or obtained, directly or indirectly, by any person as a result of criminal activity relating to a Scheduled Offence, or the value of any such property, or where such property is taken or held outside the country, then the property equivalent in value held within the country or abroad.
key_definitions.schedule: The Schedule appended to this Act.
key_definitions.scheduled_offence: An offence specified in the Schedule, if the total value involved in such offence or offences is one hundred crore rupees or more.
key_definitions.special_court: A Court of Session designated as a Special Court under sub-section (1) of section 43 of the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002 (15 of 2003).

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title as 'The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018', states its extent to the whole of India, and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on 21st April, 2018).

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'benami property', 'contracting state', 'fugitive economic offender', 'proceeds of crime', 'Scheduled Offence', and 'Special Court'.
Clarifies that the provisions of the Act apply to individuals who are or become fugitive economic offenders on or after the Act's commencement date.

main_sections.section_title: Application for declaration of fugitive economic offender and procedure therefor
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for the Director or an authorized officer to file an application in the Special Court for declaring an individual as a fugitive economic offender, including the required contents of the application.
Empowers the Director or authorized officer to attach property related to a fugitive economic offender, with or without a court's permission, and specifies the duration and conditions of attachment.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Director and other officers
main_sections.description: Grants the Director and other officers powers similar to those of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for matters like discovery, enforcing attendance, compelling production of records, and receiving evidence.

Allows the Director or authorized officer to enter any place and inspect records, check or verify proceeds of crime, and gather information if they have reason to believe an individual may be a fugitive economic offender.
Outlines the powers of search and seizure by authorized officers if they believe a person is a fugitive economic offender, possesses proceeds of crime, or records related to it.

Details the procedure for searching an individual if an authorized authority believes the person is in possession of records or proceeds of crime relevant to proceedings under the Act, including rights of the person being searched.

important_rules: An application for declaring an individual as a fugitive economic offender must include reasons for the belief, whereabouts of the offender, a list of properties believed to be proceeds of crime (including those outside India), a list of benami properties, and a list of persons with an interest in the properties.

The Director or an authorized officer can attach property believed to be proceeds of crime or owned by a fugitive economic offender, especially if it's likely to be made unavailable for confiscation. Such attachment must be followed by an application to the Special Court within thirty days.

The Director or authorized officers have civil court powers for discovery, enforcing attendance, compelling production of records, receiving evidence on affidavits, issuing commissions, and other prescribed matters.

When searching a person, the authority must, if requested, take the person to the nearest Gazetted Officer or Magistrate within twenty-four hours. The search should be conducted in the presence of at least two witnesses, and no female shall be searched by anyone except a female.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Director or other officers authorized under the Act, and Special Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through applications to Special Courts for declaration of fugitive economic offenders, attachment and confiscation of property, and other legal proceedings initiated by authorized officers.

rights: Right of a person to be taken to the nearest Gazetted Officer or Magistrate if requested during a search (Section 9(b)).
Right of persons interested in immovable property attached under Section 5(1) to enjoy the property.
Right of a person to be discharged if the Gazetted Officer or Magistrate sees no reasonable ground for search (Section 9(d)).
obligations: Individuals who are or become fugitive economic offenders are subject to the Act's provisions.
An individual who is a fugitive economic offender must face criminal prosecution in India.
The Director or authorized officers have a duty to record reasons for their beliefs and actions.

key_procedures: Filing an application by the Director or authorized officer in the Special Court for declaration of a fugitive economic offender.
Attachment of property by the Director or authorized officer, either with court permission or provisionally before filing an application.
Conducting surveys and searches by authorized officers to gather evidence and locate proceeds of crime or relevant records.
Conducting searches of persons if there's reason to believe they possess relevant records or proceeds of crime.
Hearing of applications by the Special Court.
Declaration of an individual as a fugitive economic offender by the Special Court.
Management of confiscated properties.
administration: The Director, as appointed under the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002, and other officers authorized by the Director. The Central Government also has powers related to the Act, including amending the Schedule and making rules.
important_notes: The Act is designed to operate alongside existing laws, as indicated by Section 22 ('Application of other laws not barred').
The Act grants overriding effect to its provisions where there is an inconsistency with other laws, except for the application of other laws as mentioned in Section 22 (Section 21).
The total value involved in a Scheduled Offence must be one hundred crore rupees or more for it to be considered a 'Scheduled Offence' under this Act.

title: The National Commission for Backward Classes (Repeal) Act, 2018
purpose: To repeal the National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993.
scope: This act applies to the repeal of the National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993, and its implications.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

Repeals the National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993, and dissolves the Commission constituted under that Act. It also includes savings provisions to ensure that the previous operation of the repealed Act, rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, confiscations, punishments, proceedings, and remedies are not affected. It also clarifies that the mention of specific matters in sub-section (2) does not prejudice the general application of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897.

important_rules: Rule 1: The National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993 is repealed.
Rule 2: The National Commission for Backward Classes constituted under the repealed Act stands dissolved.

Rule 3: The repeal does not affect the previous operation of the repealed Act, nor any rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, or proceedings incurred or commenced under it. These can be continued or enforced as if the Act had not been repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for commencement notification)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Official Gazette.

rights: Right to have any penalty, confiscation or punishment incurred under the repealed Act imposed or made.
obligations: Obligation to comply with any proceeding or remedy that may be instituted, continued or enforced under the savings provisions.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint a date for the commencement of this Act.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act came into force on 15th August, 2018.
The repeal is subject to the general application of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, regarding the effect of repeal.

title: The National Sports University Act, 2018
purpose: To establish and incorporate a National Sports University in the State of Manipur, as a specialized University, to promote sports education in areas like sports sciences, sports technology, sports management, and sports coaching, and to function as a national training centre for select sports disciplines by adopting best international practices.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the establishment and functioning of the National Sports University, its campuses, colleges, institutions, and centers across India and potentially outside India with Central Government approval.

key_definitions.University: The National Sports University established and incorporated as a University under this Act.
key_definitions.academic staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: Respectively, the Statutes and the Ordinances of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.teachers of the University: Professors, Associate Professors, Assistant Professors and such other persons as may be appointed for imparting instructions, training or conducting research in the University or in any Outlying Campus, College or Institution or Regional Centres and Study Centres maintained by the University and are designated as teachers by the Ordinances.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement (deemed to have come into force on 31st May, 2018).
Defines various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Academic and Activity Council', 'academic staff', 'University', 'employee', 'Statutes', 'Ordinances', etc.

Establishes the 'National Sports University' with its headquarters in Manipur and the power to establish Outlying Campuses, Colleges, Regional Centres and Study Centres in India and abroad with Central Government approval. It also constitutes the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the various objectives of the University, including becoming an institute of advanced study in physical education and sports sciences, promoting research and development, strengthening sports training, establishing centers of excellence, providing professional leadership, vocational guidance, and producing qualified professionals, ultimately aiming to make India a sporting power.

Details the extensive powers and functions of the University, which include designing courses, conducting academic and training programs, granting degrees and certificates, establishing and maintaining campuses and centers, conferring honorary degrees, appointing staff, collaborating with other institutions, providing distance education, awarding scholarships, conducting research, and managing property.

important_rules: Rule 1: The University shall be open to all caste, creed, race or class (Section 6).
Rule 2: The Central Government has the power to review the work and progress of the University (Section 7).
Rule 3: The University shall have specific officers including Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans of Schools, Registrar, Finance Officer, and Controller of Examinations (Sections 8-16).

rights: The right to sue and be sued by the name of the National Sports University (Section 3(4)).
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases against students (Section 34).
duties: Duty to promote sports education and training.
Duty to conduct research and dissemination of knowledge.
Duty to train talented athletes.
Duty to uphold the objects of the University as outlined in Section 4.
obligations: Obligations related to the conditions of service of employees, including their code of conduct (Section 5(xxii)).
Obligations to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees (Section 5(xxiii)).

key_procedures: Procedure for making Statutes (Section 25).
Procedure for making Ordinances (Section 26).
Procedure for appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students (Section 33).
administration: The Central Government is involved in approving certain actions like establishing Outlying Campuses outside India and borrowing money. The University itself is administered through its various authorities like the Court, Executive Council, and Academic and Activity Council, and its officers.
