important_notes: The Act was deemed to have come into force on 31st May, 2018, even though it was enacted later.
The University can establish Outlying Campuses and Study Centres outside India with prior approval of the Central Government.
The Act includes provisions for transitional matters and repeal and savings (Sections 43 and 44).

title: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Teachers’ Cadre) Act, 2019
purpose: To provide for the reservation of posts in direct recruitment to the teachers' cadre in certain Central Educational Institutions for persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the socially and educationally backward classes, and the economically weaker sections, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to Central Educational Institutions (defined as Universities established by Central Act, institutions of national importance, deemed universities maintained by or receiving aid from the Central Government, institutions affiliated to such universities or constituent units of deemed universities, and educational institutions established by the Central Government under the Societies Registration Act, 1860) for direct recruitment to the teachers' cadre. Excludes institutions of excellence, research institutions, institutions of national and strategic importance, and Minority Educational Institutions.

key_definitions.appropriate authority: The University Grants Commission established under the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, or any other authority or body established by or under a Central Act for the determination, coordination or maintenance of the standards of higher education in any Central Educational Institution.
key_definitions.central educational institution: Includes Universities established by Central Act, institutions of national importance, institutions declared as deemed to be University and maintained by or receiving aid from the Central Government, institutions maintained by or receiving aid from the Central Government and affiliated to specified institutions, and educational institutions established by the Central Government under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.direct recruitment: The process of appointing faculty by inviting applications against public advertisement from persons eligible to teach in a Central Educational Institution.
key_definitions.economically weaker sections: Such weaker sections as are referred to in Explanation to clause (6) of article 15 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.teachers' cadre: A class of all the teachers of a Central Educational Institution, regardless of the branch of study or faculty, who are remunerated at the same grade of pay, excluding any allowance or bonus.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Teachers’ Cadre) Act, 2019 and states it is deemed to have come into force on March 7, 2019.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including appropriate authority, branch of study, Central Educational Institution, direct recruitment, economically weaker sections, faculty, Minority Educational Institution, sanctioned strength, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, socially and educationally backward classes, and teachers’ cadre.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of posts in recruitments by Central Educational Institutions
main_sections.description: Mandates reservation of posts in direct recruitment to the teachers' cadre in Central Educational Institutions, to the extent and manner specified by the Central Government by notification. States that a Central Educational Institution is to be regarded as one unit for the purpose of reservation.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies that Section 3 (reservation) does not apply to institutions of excellence, research institutions, institutions of national and strategic importance (listed in a Schedule), and Minority Educational Institutions. Allows the Central Government to amend the Schedule by notification.
Requires every notification made by the Central Government under this Act to be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modification or annulment by Parliament.

Repeals the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Teachers' Cadre) Ordinance, 2019. States that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Reservation of posts in direct recruitment to the teachers' cadre in Central Educational Institutions shall be implemented as specified by the Central Government via notification.
Each Central Educational Institution shall be considered a single unit for the purpose of applying reservation.
The provisions for reservation do not apply to specific categories of institutions like institutions of excellence and Minority Educational Institutions.
Notifications issued by the Central Government under this Act are subject to review and potential modification or annulment by Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implicitly the Central Government and the relevant educational institutions, guided by the appropriate authority (UGC or equivalent).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the Central Government specifying reservation quotas and procedures, and through the mandate for Central Educational Institutions to adhere to these provisions.

rights: Right to reservation in teachers' cadre appointments for eligible individuals from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, socially and educationally backward classes, and economically weaker sections in specified Central Educational Institutions.
duties: Duty of Central Educational Institutions to implement reservation in direct recruitment to the teachers' cadre as per Central Government notifications.
Duty of the Central Government to specify the extent and manner of reservation by notification.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to ensure that notifications are laid before Parliament.
Obligation to adhere to the definitions and scope outlined in the Act.

key_procedures: Direct recruitment to the teachers' cadre in Central Educational Institutions will include reservation for specified categories as notified by the Central Government.
The Central Government will issue notifications to specify the reservation quotas and implementation details.
Notifications issued by the Central Government are laid before Parliament for review.
In case of certain listed institutions or Minority Educational Institutions, Section 3 of the Act (reservation) does not apply.
administration: Central Government, through the Ministry responsible for higher education and potentially other allied bodies like the University Grants Commission (UGC).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on March 7, 2019.

Certain categories of institutions are exempted from the reservation provisions, including institutions of excellence, research institutions, institutions of national and strategic importance, and Minority Educational Institutions.
The Central Government has the power to amend the list of exempted institutions.

title: THE INDIA INTERNATIONAL ARBITRATION CENTRE ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide for the establishment and incorporation of the India International Arbitration Centre for creating an independent and autonomous regime for institutionalised arbitration, acquiring and transferring the undertakings of the International Centre for Alternative Dispute Resolution, vesting such undertakings in the India International Arbitration Centre for better management of arbitration, making it a hub for institutional arbitration, and declaring it an institution of national importance.
scope: This Act applies to India and concerns the establishment, incorporation, management, and functioning of the India International Arbitration Centre. It also covers the acquisition and transfer of undertakings of the International Centre for Alternative Dispute Resolution.

key_definitions.Centre: The India International Arbitration Centre established and incorporated under section 3.
key_definitions.Society: The International Centre for Alternative Dispute Resolution, registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.undertakings: The undertakings of the Society which vest with the Central Government under section 7.
key_definitions.specified date: The date as may be specified by the Central Government by notification.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Centre.
key_definitions.Member: Full-time or Part-time Member of the Centre and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer appointed under section 21.
key_definitions.Fund: The Fund of the Centre to be maintained under section 25.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is deemed to have come into force on March 2, 2019.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Centre', 'Society', 'undertakings', 'specified date', 'Chairperson', 'Member', 'Chief Executive Officer', and 'Fund'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of India International Arbitration Centre
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish the India International Arbitration Centre, which will be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of India International Arbitration Centre as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Centre as an institution of national importance. The head office is in New Delhi, with the power to establish branches elsewhere with the Central Government's approval.

States that on and from the specified date, the undertakings of the Society and the Society's right, title, and interest in relation to such undertakings shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government.

Details the implications of the vesting, including the inclusion of all assets, rights, powers, properties, funds, and documents. It also addresses the discharge from encumbrances and the continuation of existing licenses and instruments.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of undertaking in Centre
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct, by notification, that the undertakings vested in the Central Government shall vest in the Centre.
Outlines the objectives of the Centre, which include the development of an independent and autonomous regime for institutionalised arbitration.
Specifies the various functions the Centre is to perform, related to the promotion and management of institutional arbitration.
Describes the establishment and maintenance of the Fund of the Centre.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Centre the power to make regulations for carrying out its functions.
Provides for the repeal of any prior enactment and savings.

important_rules: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish the India International Arbitration Centre (Section 3).
The India International Arbitration Centre is declared an institution of national importance (Section 4).
On the specified date, the undertakings of the Society (International Centre for Alternative Dispute Resolution) and its rights shall transfer to and vest in the Central Government (Section 7).
The Central Government may direct that the undertakings vested in it shall vest in the Centre (Section 10).
The Centre shall have objects and functions related to promoting and managing institutional arbitration (Sections 14 & 15).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the India International Arbitration Centre.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, rules, and regulations prescribed and made under the Act. Enforcement also involves the transfer and vesting of undertakings and the operationalization of the Centre's functions.

rights: The Centre has the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to enter into contracts (Section 3).
The Centre shall be deemed to be substituted in licenses or instruments previously granted to the Society (Section 8(3)).
Suits, appeals, or other proceedings related to vested property may be continued by or against the Central Government or the Centre (Section 8(4)).
duties: The Central Government is responsible for establishing and incorporating the Centre (Section 3).
Persons in charge of undertakings are required to deliver all assets to the Custodian (implied from Section 12, though not fully detailed in provided text).
obligations: The Centre must adhere to the provisions of the Act when acquiring, holding, or disposing of property and entering into contracts (Section 3).

key_procedures: Establishment of the Centre by Central Government notification (Section 3).
Transfer and vesting of undertakings of the Society to the Central Government on the specified date (Section 7).
Direction by the Central Government for the vesting of undertakings from the Central Government to the Centre (Section 10).
Appointment of Chairperson and Members of the Centre (Section 5).
Making of rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Centre (Sections 30 & 31).
administration: Central Government, Ministry of Law and Justice, Department of Legal Affairs, and Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure (ex officio members). The Centre itself is administered by its Chairperson, Members, and Chief Executive Officer.
important_notes: The Act has undergone amendments by Act 23 of 2022, which changed the name from 'New Delhi International Arbitration Centre' to 'India International Arbitration Centre' effective from January 27, 2023.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on March 2, 2019 (Section 1(2)).
Vesting of undertakings frees them from trusts, mortgages, charges, liens, and other encumbrances (Section 8(2)).

title: THE BANNING OF UNREGULATED DEPOSIT SCHEMES ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide for a comprehensive mechanism to ban the unregulated deposit schemes, other than deposits taken in the ordinary course of business, and to protect the interest of depositors and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, including the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh. It applies to deposit takers and depositors involved in or affected by unregulated deposit schemes.

key_definitions.deposit: An amount of money received by way of an advance or loan or in any other form, by any deposit taker with a promise to return, whether after a specified period or otherwise, either in cash or in kind or in the form of a specified service, with or without any benefit in the form of interest, bonus, profit or in any other form. Certain specific types of receipts are excluded from this definition.
key_definitions.deposit_taker: Includes an individual or group of individuals, proprietorship concern, partnership firm, limited liability partnership, company, association of persons, trust, co-operative society, multi-State co-operative society, or any other arrangement receiving or soliciting deposits, but excludes certain corporations and banking entities.
key_definitions.regulated_deposit_scheme: Schemes specified under column (3) of the First Schedule.
key_definitions.unregulated_deposit_scheme: A Scheme or an arrangement under which deposits are accepted or solicited by any deposit taker by way of business and which is not a Regulated Deposit Scheme, as specified under column (3) of the First Schedule. This also includes prize chits or money circulation schemes banned under the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act, 1978.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of its commencement (deemed to be 21st February, 2019).

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appropriate Government', 'company', 'Competent Authority', 'deposit', 'depositor', 'deposit taker', 'Designated Court', 'insurer', 'notification', 'person', 'prescribed', 'property', 'public financial institution', 'Regulated Deposit Scheme', 'Regulator', and 'Unregulated Deposit Scheme'.
Prohibits the operation and promotion of Unregulated Deposit Schemes and bars deposit takers from accepting deposits in pursuance of such schemes.

main_sections.section_title: Fraudulent default in Regulated Deposit Schemes
main_sections.description: Prohibits deposit takers from committing fraudulent default in repayment or service delivery when accepting deposits under a Regulated Deposit Scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Wrongful inducement in relation to Unregulated Deposit Schemes
main_sections.description: Prohibits knowingly making false, deceptive, or misleading statements or concealing material facts to induce investment in Unregulated Deposit Schemes.

main_sections.section_title: Certain scheme to be Unregulated Deposit Scheme
main_sections.description: Declares prize chits and money circulation schemes banned under the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act, 1978, as Unregulated Deposit Schemes under this Act.

Empowers the appropriate Government to appoint one or more officers, not below the rank of Secretary, as the Competent Authority and to appoint other officers to assist the Competent Authority. It also outlines the power of the Competent Authority to provisionally attach deposits and property if it believes a deposit taker is soliciting deposits in contravention of section 3.
Empowers the appropriate Government to constitute a Designated Court for the purposes of this Act.
Mandates the Central Government to maintain a central database of deposit takers.

main_sections.section_title: Information of business by deposit taker
main_sections.description: Requires deposit takers to furnish information regarding their business to the Central Government.
Specifies that information regarding deposit takers shall be shared with other authorities.
Establishes the priority of depositors' claims over other debts.
Deals with the precedence of attachment of property in relation to depositors' claims.

main_sections.section_title: Application for confirmation of attachment and sale of property
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for applying for confirmation of attachment and sale of property for the benefit of depositors.

main_sections.section_title: Confirmation of attachment by Designated Court
main_sections.description: Specifies the role of the Designated Court in confirming the attachment of property.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of property of mala fide transferees
main_sections.description: Allows for the attachment of property transferred mala fide by the deposit taker.
Provides for payment in lieu of attachment of property.
Details the powers of the Designated Court in handling cases under the Act, including attachment, sale of property, and distribution of proceeds.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders of the Designated Court to the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Supreme Court to transfer cases
main_sections.description: Grants the Supreme Court the power to transfer cases from one Designated Court to another.
Prescribes punishment for operating or promoting Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
Prescribes punishment for fraudulent default in Regulated Deposit Schemes.
Prescribes punishment for wrongful inducement in relation to Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
Prescribes enhanced punishment for repeat offenders.

main_sections.section_title: Offences by deposit takers other than individuals
main_sections.description: Deals with offences committed by deposit takers which are not individuals.
Prescribes punishment for contravention of the requirement to provide business information.
Specifies the conditions under which offences under the Act can be taken cognizance of.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable
main_sections.description: Declares offences under the Act as cognizable and non-bailable.

main_sections.section_title: Competent Authority to be informed of offences
main_sections.description: Requires that the Competent Authority be informed of offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Investigation of offences by Central Bureau of Investigation
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to investigate offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter, search and seize without warrant
main_sections.description: Grants powers to enter, search, and seize without warrant in certain circumstances related to contravention of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to proceedings before Designated Court
main_sections.description: States that the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, shall apply to proceedings before the Designated Court.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of advertisement of Unregulated Deposit Scheme
main_sections.description: Deals with the prohibition of publishing advertisements of Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws to the extent of its provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the application of other laws is not barred.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government, etc., to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers State Governments and Union territory administrations to make rules.
Specifies the procedure for laying rules before Parliament or State Legislatures.
Grants the Central Government the power to amend the First Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply certain deposits
main_sections.description: Specifies certain deposits to which the Act shall not apply.
Provides for amendments to certain other enactments.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous provisions and savings.

important_rules: Unregulated Deposit Schemes are banned and cannot be promoted, operated, or solicited for participation or enrollment.
Deposit takers must not commit fraudulent default in repayment or service delivery for Regulated Deposit Schemes.
No person shall make false, deceptive, or misleading statements to induce investment in Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
Prize chits and money circulation schemes banned under the 1978 Act are considered Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
The Competent Authority has the power to provisionally attach deposits and property if a deposit taker is soliciting funds in contravention of the ban on Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
Depositors have priority claims over other debts in the event of attachment of property.
The Central Government shall maintain a central database of deposit takers.
Offences under the Act are cognizable and non-bailable.

penalties: Punishment for contravention of section 3 (banning of UDS): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees, or with both.
Punishment for contravention of section 4 (fraudulent default in RDS): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees.
Punishment for contravention of section 5 (wrongful inducement): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees.
Punishment for contravention of section 10 (information of business): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five lakh rupees.
Punishment for repeat offenders includes enhanced imprisonment and fines.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent Authority (appointed by the appropriate Government), Designated Court, and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation by the CBI, powers of entry, search, and seizure by authorized officers, provisional attachment of property by the Competent Authority, and adjudication and sentencing by the Designated Court. The Act also has an overriding effect and allows for the application of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

rights: Depositors have the right to the priority of their claims on attached property.
The right to appeal Designated Court orders to the High Court.
Protection of actions taken in good faith by individuals acting under the Act.
duties: Deposit takers have a duty not to operate Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
Deposit takers have a duty not to commit fraudulent default in Regulated Deposit Schemes.
Deposit takers have a duty to provide business information as required.
Individuals and entities must not make wrongful inducements to invest in Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
obligations: The Central Government has an obligation to maintain a central database of deposit takers.
Appropriate Governments have obligations to appoint Competent Authorities and Designated Courts.
The Act imposes obligations on deposit takers to comply with its provisions regarding regulated and unregulated deposit schemes.

key_procedures: Appointment of Competent Authority and Designated Court by the appropriate Government.
Provisional attachment of deposits and property by the Competent Authority upon belief of contravention of section 3.
Application to the Designated Court for confirmation of attachment and sale of property.
Attachment of property of mala fide transferees.
Investigation of offences by the CBI.
Powers of entry, search, and seizure without warrant.
Filing of appeals against Designated Court orders to the High Court.
administration: The administration of the Act involves the Central Government, State Governments, Competent Authorities appointed by them, and Designated Courts. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is involved in the investigation of offences.
important_notes: The Act is not applicable to certain types of deposits as specified in section 41.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws, but the application of other laws is not barred.
The Act provides protection for actions taken in good faith.
The Central Government has the power to make rules and amend the First Schedule, and State Governments can also make rules.
The Act came into force retrospectively from 21st February, 2019.

title: THE PROHIBITION OF ELECTRONIC CIGARETTES (PRODUCTION, MANUFACTURE, IMPORT, EXPORT, TRANSPORT, SALE, DISTRIBUTION, STORAGE AND ADVERTISEMENT) ACT, 2019
purpose: To prohibit the production, manufacture, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, storage and advertisement of electronic cigarettes in the interest of public health to protect the people from harm and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to all forms of electronic cigarettes, including Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems, Heat Not Burn Products, e-Hookah and the like devices, by whatever name called and whatever shape, size or form they may have. It prohibits production, manufacture, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, storage, and advertisement of these products. It is declared expedient for the Union to take control of the electronic cigarettes industry.

key_definitions.advertisement: Any audio or visual publicity, representation or pronouncement made by means of any light, sound, smoke, gas, print, electronic media, internet or website or social media and includes through any notice, circular, label, wrapper, invoice or other document or device.
key_definitions.authorised officer: Any police officer not below the rank of sub-inspector; or any other officer, not below the rank of sub-inspector, authorised by the Central Government or the State Government by notification.
key_definitions.distribution: Includes distribution by way of samples, whether free or otherwise.
key_definitions.electronic cigarette: An electronic device that heats a substance, with or without nicotine and flavours, to create an aerosol for inhalation and includes all forms of Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems, Heat Not Burn Products, e-Hookah and the like devices, by whatever name called and whatever shape, size or form it may have, but does not include any product licensed under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
key_definitions.manufacture: A process for making or assembling electronic cigarettes and any part thereof, which includes any sub-process, incidental or ancillary to the manufacture of electronic cigarettes and any part thereof.
key_definitions.sale: Any transfer of property in goods (including online transfer) by one person to another, whether for cash or on credit, or by way of exchange, and whether wholesale or retail, and includes an agreement for sale, and offer for sale and exposure for sale.
key_definitions.person: Includes any individual or group of individuals; a firm (whether registered or not); a Hindu Undivided Family; a trust; a limited liability partnership; a co-operative society; any corporation or company or body of individuals; and every artificial juridical person not falling within any of the preceding sub-clauses.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes (Production, Manufacture, Import, Export, Transport, Sale, Distribution, Storage and Advertisement) Act, 2019, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on September 18, 2019.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of control by Union
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to take control of the electronic cigarettes industry.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including advertisement, authorised officer, distribution, electronic cigarette, export, import, manufacture, notification, person, place, production, and sale.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on production, manufacturing, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, advertisement of electronic cigarettes
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from producing, manufacturing, importing, exporting, transporting, selling, distributing, or advertising electronic cigarettes, or taking part in any advertisement that promotes their use, directly or indirectly.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on storage of electronic cigarettes
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person, being the owner or occupier or having control or use of any place, from knowingly permitting it to be used for the storage of any stock of electronic cigarettes. It includes provisions for the disposal of existing stocks.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter, search and seize without warrant
main_sections.description: Empowers an authorised officer to enter and search any place where trade, production, supply, distribution, storage, transport, or advertisement of electronic cigarettes is carried on. It also allows for seizure of records or property and attachment of property if seizure is not practicable. Searches, seizures, and attachments are to be made in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Prescribes punishment for contravening Section 4, including imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to one lakh rupees, or both. For second or subsequent offences, imprisonment can extend to three years and a fine up to five lakh rupees.
Prescribes punishment for contravening Section 5, including imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both.

States that offences under Section 4 or Section 5 are triable in any place where the offender is liable to be tried under any law. All offences are to be tried by the Court of Judicial Magistrate of the first class according to the procedure in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Deals with offences committed by companies, holding individuals in charge responsible, and allows for prosecution if the offence was committed with consent, connivance, or neglect of directors or officers.
Specifies that no court shall take cognizance of an offence under the Act except upon a complaint in writing made by an authorised officer.
Declares offences under Section 4 as cognizable, notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force, unless otherwise expressly provided.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law prohibiting the activities covered by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act by the Central or State Governments or their officers.

Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, within two years of its commencement. Such orders must be laid before Parliament.

Repeals the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes (Production, Manufacture, Import, Export, Transport, Sale, Distribution, Storage and Advertisement) Ordinance, 2019, and states that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: No person shall produce, manufacture, import, export, transport, sell, distribute, or advertise electronic cigarettes, or participate in their advertisement. (Section 4)
No person shall permit any place to be used for the storage of electronic cigarettes. (Section 5)
Existing stock of electronic cigarettes on the commencement date must be disposed of by preparing a list and submitting it to the nearest authorised officer for disposal according to law. (Section 5)

Authorised officers have the power to enter, search, and seize places and items related to the production, sale, or advertisement of electronic cigarettes without a warrant, following the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. (Section 6)
Offences under Section 4 are cognizable. (Section 13)
The Act has overriding effect over other laws if there is an inconsistency, unless expressly provided otherwise. (Section 14)

penalties: Contravention of Section 4: Imprisonment up to one year or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both. For second or subsequent offence: imprisonment up to three years and fine up to five lakh rupees. (Section 7)
Contravention of Section 5: Imprisonment up to six months or fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both. (Section 8)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised Officers, who can be police officers not below the rank of sub-inspector, or other officers authorised by the Central or State Government. (Section 3(b))
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, search, and seizure without warrant (Section 6), and by judicial magistrates of the first class trying offences (Section 9). Cognizance of offences is taken only upon a complaint by an authorised officer (Section 12). Searches, seizures, and attachments are conducted in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 6(4)). Disposal of seized stock follows Chapter XXXIV of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 10).

rights: Right to protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act (Central/State Government and officers). (Section 16)
Right to have difficulties in implementing the Act removed by the Central Government. (Section 17)
duties: Duty of any person not to produce, manufacture, import, export, transport, sell, distribute, or advertise electronic cigarettes. (Section 4)
Duty of any person not to permit any place to be used for storage of electronic cigarettes. (Section 5)
Duty of owners/occupiers of places with existing stocks of electronic cigarettes to prepare a list and submit the stock to the authorised officer for disposal. (Section 5)
obligations: Obligation of companies to ensure their business complies with the Act, with liability for offences committed by the company. (Section 11)
Obligation for individuals to cooperate with authorised officers during searches and seizures. (Implied from Section 6)
Obligation for authorised officers to act according to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, when conducting searches, seizures, and attachments. (Section 6(4))

key_procedures: Disposal of existing stocks of electronic cigarettes: Owner/occupier prepares a list of stock and submits it to the nearest authorised officer, who then takes measures for disposal according to law. (Section 5)

Search, seizure, and attachment: An authorised officer can enter and search any place if there's reason to believe a contravention has occurred. Records or property can be seized, or attached if seizure is not practicable. All actions are to be in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. (Section 6)

Trial of offences: Offences are tried by the Court of Judicial Magistrate of the first class according to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, upon a written complaint by an authorised officer. (Sections 9, 12)
administration: The Central Government is responsible for authorising officers, making notifications, and removing difficulties (Section 17). State Governments can also authorise officers (Section 3(b)).
important_notes: The Act includes a definition for 'electronic cigarette' which specifically excludes products licensed under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. (Section 3(d))
Existing stocks of electronic cigarettes at the commencement of the Act are subject to specific disposal procedures. (Section 5)
Offences under Section 4 are cognizable. (Section 13)
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act within two years of its commencement. (Section 17)
The Act repeals the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Ordinance, 2019, but actions taken under the Ordinance are considered valid. (Section 18)

title: THE NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI (RECOGNITION OF PROPERTY RIGHTS OF RESIDENTS IN UNAUTHORISED COLONIES) ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi for recognizing the property rights of residents in unauthorized colonies by securing the rights of ownership or transfer or mortgage in favour of residents possessing properties on the basis of Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sale, Will, possession letter or any other documents evidencing payment of consideration, as a one-time special measure.
scope: Applies to unauthorized colonies within the National Capital Territory of Delhi. The act covers residents possessing properties in these colonies based on specific documents.

key_definitions.resident: A person having physical possession of property in an unauthorized colony based on a registered sale deed or latest Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sale, Will, possession letter and other documents evidencing payment of consideration. Includes legal heirs, but excludes tenants, licensees, or permissive users.
key_definitions.unauthorised colony: A colony or development comprising a contiguous area where permission for layout or building plans has not been obtained and which has been identified for regularization based on Delhi Development Authority notification S.O. 683(E), dated 24th March, 2008.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it extends to the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
Defines 'resident' and 'unauthorised colony' for the purposes of the Act.

Deals with the regularization of immovable property transactions in unauthorized colonies based on specific documents, fixing of charges, payment of stamp duty and registration charges, eligibility of residents, and exclusion of tenants, licensees, or permissive users.

important_rules: Transactions of immovable properties in unauthorized colonies can be regularized by the Central Government, by notification, based on the latest Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sale, Will, possession letter, and other documents evidencing payment of consideration, for conferring ownership, transfer, or mortgage rights.

The Central Government may fix charges for the regularization of these transactions, payable for conferring or recognizing ownership, transfer, or mortgage rights through a conveyance deed or authorization slip.
Stamp duty and registration charges for conveyance deeds or authorization slips shall be payable on the amount mentioned therein.

Residents with registered or unregistered/notarized Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sale, Will, possession letter, and other documents evidencing payment of consideration are eligible for ownership, transfer, or mortgage rights upon payment of the specified charges.
No stamp duty and registration charges are payable on any previous sale transactions made prior to the transactions referred to for regularization.
Tenants, licensees, or permissive users are not eligible for property rights under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette.

rights: Right of ownership, transfer, or mortgage for eligible residents in unauthorized colonies.
obligations: Payment of charges fixed by the Central Government for regularization.
Payment of stamp duty and registration charges on the conveyance deed or authorization slip.

key_procedures: The Central Government shall issue a notification in the Official Gazette to regularize transactions of immovable properties based on specified documents.
The Central Government shall notify charges payable for conferring or recognizing property rights through a conveyance deed or authorization slip.
Eligible residents must pay the specified charges to obtain the right of ownership, transfer, or mortgage through a conveyance deed or authorization slip.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: This Act overrides the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, and the Registration Act, 1908, as applicable to the National Capital Territory of Delhi, and any rules, regulations, or bye-laws made thereunder, as well as the judgment of the Supreme Court in Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. Vs. State of Haryana & others.
The Act provides a one-time special measure for recognizing property rights in unauthorized colonies.

title: The Recycling of Ships Act, 2019
purpose: To provide for the regulation of recycling of ships by setting certain standards and laying down the statutory mechanism for enforcement of such standards and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, aligning with the Hong Kong International Convention for the Safe and Environmentally Sound Recycling of Ships, 2009.
scope: Applies to existing and new ships registered in India (wherever they may be), other ships entering Indian ports/shipyards/terminals or within India's Exclusive Economic Zone/territorial waters, warships/naval auxiliaries for government non-commercial service destined for recycling in India, and ship recycling facilities operating in India or its exclusive territorial jurisdiction.

key_definitions.Administration: The Government of the country whose flag the ship is entitled to fly, or under whose authority it is operating.
key_definitions.Competent Authority: An Authority designated by the Central Government for performance of specific duties within geographical areas or areas of expertise.
key_definitions.hazardous material: Any material or substance which is liable to cause harm to human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organisms, property or the environment.
key_definitions.National Authority: An Authority designated by the Central Government to administer, supervise, and monitor all activities relating to ship recycling.
key_definitions.ship: A vessel and floating structure of any type whatsoever operating or having operated in the marine environment, including submersibles, floating craft, floating platforms, self-elevating platforms, floating storage units, and the like.
key_definitions.ship owner: Includes the registered owner, the manager or bareboat charterer assuming responsibility for operation, the operator of a government-owned ship, or a person/company owning the ship for a limited period pending sale or handover for recycling.
key_definitions.Ship Recycler: The owner or operator of a ship recycling facility who has assumed responsibility for its operation and agreed to comply with the Act's requirements.
key_definitions.ship recycling: The activity of dismantling a ship at a facility to recover components and materials for reprocessing and reuse, while managing hazardous materials, including associated operations like storage and treatment on-site.
key_definitions.ship recycling facility: A defined area (site, yard, or facility) used for ship recycling that meets specified regulatory requirements.
key_definitions.ship recycling plan: A ship-specific plan developed by a facility to recycle a ship safely and in an environmentally sound manner.
key_definitions.worker: A person employed directly or through an agency (including a contractor) in ship recycling or related incidental work, with or without remuneration, excluding members of the armed forces.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, details the commencement provisions by notification of the Central Government, and specifies the scope of application of the Act's provisions to various types of ships and ship recycling facilities.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'Administration', 'Competent Authority', 'hazardous material', 'National Authority', 'ship', 'ship owner', 'Ship Recycler', 'ship recycling', 'ship recycling facility', 'ship recycling plan', and 'worker'. It also references definitions from other related Acts.

Empowers the Central Government to designate an officer, not below the rank of Joint Secretary, as the National Authority responsible for administering, supervising, and monitoring all ship recycling activities under the Act.
Authorizes the Central Government to designate an Authority, to be known as the Competent Authority, for carrying out specific duties within defined geographical areas or areas of expertise.

Prohibits the installation or use of specific hazardous materials on ships as notified by the Central Government. It also allows for exemptions and requires ships to comply with prescribed restrictions and conditions regarding hazardous materials.

Mandates various types of surveys for ships: initial surveys before issuing hazardous materials inventory certificates, renewal surveys, additional surveys after changes, final surveys before recycling, and other prescribed surveys. These surveys are to be conducted by the National Authority or authorized entities.

main_sections.section_title: Certificate on inventory of hazardous materials
main_sections.description: Requires owners of new ships to apply to the National Authority for a certificate detailing the hazardous materials on board. This section also implies provisions for existing ships.
Deals with the process and requirements for authorizing a ship recycling facility, likely involving the submission of plans and adherence to specific standards.
Introduces the requirement for a 'ready for recycling certificate', which is likely issued after the ship meets certain conditions or has undergone specific processes before dismantling.
Requires the development of a specific ship recycling plan by the facility for each ship to ensure safe and environmentally sound dismantling.

main_sections.section_title: Obligations on part of ship owner
main_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities and duties that ship owners must fulfill in relation to the recycling of their ships.

main_sections.section_title: Safe and environmentally sound management of hazardous materials
main_sections.description: Emphasizes the obligation to manage hazardous materials in a safe and environmentally sound manner during the ship recycling process.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of Act or rules or regulations
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for violations of the Act's provisions, rules, or regulations for which no specific punishment is otherwise provided.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of this Act or rules or regulations for which no specific punishment is provided
main_sections.description: Addresses penalties for contraventions where no specific punishment is already detailed in the Act or its associated rules/regulations.
Details the punishments applicable to other offenses defined or covered under the Act.
Establishes liability and penalties for offenses committed by companies, including provisions for individual accountability within the company.
Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Confers power upon the National Authority to make regulations for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: Ships must comply with restrictions and conditions regarding hazardous materials (Section 6(2)).
Rule: Hazardous materials prohibited by the Central Government cannot be installed or used on ships (Section 6(1)).
Rule: Ship owners must obtain a 'certificate on inventory of hazardous materials' for new ships (Section 8(1)).
Rule: Ship recycling facilities must adhere to specified requirements to be authorized (Section 11, Section 2(o)).
Rule: A specific 'ship recycling plan' must be developed for each ship to ensure safe and environmentally sound recycling (Section 17).
Rule: Ship owners have specific obligations related to the recycling of their vessels (Section 19).
Rule: Hazardous materials must be managed safely and in an environmentally sound manner during recycling (Section 21).

penalties: Penalty for contravention of provisions of the Act or rules or regulations for which no specific punishment is provided (Section 32).
Punishment for other offenses defined under the Act (Section 33).
Specific penalties for offenses committed by companies (Section 34).
Amount payable by owner, master or agent (Section 37).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: National Authority, Competent Authority, and the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers to search and seize records, inspect, dismiss, exclude or detain ships, conduct surveys, authorize facilities, and impose penalties and compensation for contraventions. Enforcement is also facilitated by the requirement for various certificates and plans.

rights: Right to appeal against decisions of the Competent Authority (Section 25).
Right to appeal against decisions of the National Authority (Section 26).
Right to compensation for damages caused by contravention (Section 39).
duties: Duty to comply with controls on hazardous materials (Section 6).
Duty to undergo required surveys (Section 7).
Duty of ship owners to obtain necessary certificates (Section 8).
Duty of ship owners to fulfill obligations related to ship recycling (Section 19).
Duty of Ship Recyclers to ensure safe and environmentally sound management of hazardous materials (Section 21, 22).
Duty to report completion of recycling (Section 23).
Duty to report to the National Authority (Section 24).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the standards and mechanisms set forth by the Act for ship recycling.
Obligation to facilitate safe and environmentally sound recycling practices.
Obligation to ensure the safety and health of workers involved in recycling.
Obligation to manage hazardous materials responsibly.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a 'certificate on inventory of hazardous materials' for new ships (Section 8).
Procedure for authorising a ship recycling facility (Section 11, Section 12).
Procedure for granting permission for ship recycling, including the development of a ship recycling plan and statement of acceptance (Section 20).
Procedure for obtaining a 'ready for recycling certificate' (Section 16).
Procedure for reporting the completion of ship recycling and submitting a statement of completion (Section 23).
Procedure for appeals against decisions made by the Competent Authority and National Authority (Sections 25, 26).
administration: National Authority and Competent Authority, designated by the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act aligns with the Hong Kong International Convention for the Safe and Environmentally Sound Recycling of Ships, 2009.
Different provisions of the Act may come into force on different dates as notified by the Central Government (Section 1(2)).

Certain ships, such as warships and naval auxiliaries for non-commercial purposes, and ships below 500 gross tonnage, are exempted from specific chapters or provisions, though the Central Government may notify measures for them (Section 5).
The Central Government may exempt certain classes or categories of ships from provisions related to prohibited hazardous materials (Section 6(1)).
The Act is not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force (Section 41).
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act (Section 46).

title: THE NATIONAL MEDICAL COMMISSION ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide for a medical education system that improves access to quality and affordable medical education, ensures availability of adequate and high quality medical professionals in all parts of the country; that promotes equitable and universal healthcare that encourages community health perspective and makes services of medical professionals accessible to all the citizens; that promotes national health goals; that encourages medical professionals to adopt latest medical research in their work and to contribute to research; that has an objective periodic and transparent assessment of medical institutions and facilitates the maintenance of a medical register for India and enforces high ethical standards in all aspects of medical services; that is flexible to adapt to changing needs and has an effective grievance redressal mechanism.
scope: The act extends to the whole of India. It applies to medical education, the practice of modern scientific medicine, assessment of medical institutions, and the registration of medical practitioners.

key_definitions.Autonomous Board: Any of the Autonomous Boards constituted under section 16.
key_definitions.Commission: The National Medical Commission constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.medicine: Modern scientific medicine in all its branches and includes surgery and obstetrics, but does not include veterinary medicine and surgery.
key_definitions.medical institution: Any institution within or outside India which grants degrees, diplomas or licences in medicine and includes affiliated colleges and deemed to be Universities.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title as the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, its extent across the whole of India, and the provision for commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Autonomous Board', 'Chairperson', 'Commission', 'health University', 'licence', 'medical institution', 'medicine', 'State Medical Council', among others.

Establishes the National Medical Commission by the Central Government to exercise powers and perform functions assigned under the Act. It is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with its head office in New Delhi.

Details the composition of the National Medical Commission, including a Chairperson, ten ex officio Members (Presidents of Autonomous Boards, Director General of Health Services, Director General of ICMR, Directors of AIIMS/other institutes, and a representative from the Ministry of Health), and twenty-two part-time Members (experts in various fields and nominees from States/Union Territories).
Relates to the National Eligibility cum-Entrance Test, likely for admission to medical courses.
Relates to the National Exit Test, likely for qualifying to practice medicine.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Under-Graduate Medical Education Board
main_sections.description: Outlines the specific powers and functions of the Under-Graduate Medical Education Board.
Deals with State Medical Councils, which are constituted under state laws for regulating medical practice and registration.
Concerns the maintenance of a National Medical Register by the Ethics and Medical Registration Board and State Registers maintained by respective states.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of persons to have licence to practice and to be enrolled in National Register or State Register and their obligations thereto
main_sections.description: Covers the rights of individuals to obtain a license to practice medicine and be enrolled in the National or State Register, along with their corresponding obligations.
Specifies conditions or limitations that may prevent practice of medicine.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of medical qualifications granted by Universities or medical institutions in India
main_sections.description: Details the process and criteria for recognizing medical qualifications obtained from Indian universities and institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of medical qualifications granted by medical institutions outside India
main_sections.description: Addresses the recognition of medical qualifications obtained from foreign medical institutions.
Pertains to financial grants provided by the Central Government to the Commission.
Establishes and describes the National Medical Commission Fund.
Covers the audit procedures and accounting practices for the Commission's funds.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions to Commission and Autonomous Boards
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Commission and Autonomous Boards.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede Commission
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to supersede the National Medical Commission under certain circumstances.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Commission the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.
Deals with the repeal of previous laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Rule: The National Medical Commission shall be constituted by the Central Government to exercise powers and perform functions assigned by the Act.
Rule: The Commission shall consist of a Chairperson, ten ex officio Members, and twenty-two part-time Members.
Rule: The Central Government shall appoint the Chairperson and certain Members based on recommendations from a Search Committee.
Rule: Medical qualifications granted by Universities or medical institutions in India and outside India need to be recognized as per the specified sections.
Rule: The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Commission and Autonomous Boards.
Rule: The Central Government can supersede the Commission under specific circumstances.
Rule: The Central Government can make rules, and the Commission can make regulations, subject to the Act.

penalties: Section 54: Cognizance of offences (specific penalties are not detailed in the provided text but the section title indicates their existence).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Medical Commission, Autonomous Boards, State Medical Councils, and the Central Government are involved in enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of regulatory bodies (Commission, Boards), maintenance of registers, recognition of qualifications, and the power of the Central Government to issue directions and supersede the Commission. Enforcement also involves cognizance of offences.

rights: Right of persons to have a licence to practice medicine.
Right of persons to be enrolled in the National Register or State Register.
duties: Obligations of persons to have a licence to practice and to be enrolled in the National Register or State Register.
Obligations of universities and medical institutions.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a licence to practice medicine.
Obligation to be enrolled in the National Register or State Register.
Obligations of universities and medical institutions as prescribed by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointment of Chairperson and Members of the Commission through a Search Committee.
Procedure for constitution and functioning of Autonomous Boards.
Procedure for recognition of medical qualifications (Indian and foreign).
Procedure for maintaining National and State Registers.
Procedure for establishment of new medical colleges (implied through Section 28).
Procedure for making rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Commission.
administration: The National Medical Commission administers the Act, with oversight and direction from the Central Government. Autonomous Boards (Under-Graduate Medical Education Board, Post-Graduate Medical Education Board, Medical Assessment and Rating Board, Ethics and Medical Registration Board) are also key administrative bodies.
important_notes: The Act provides for different commencement dates for different provisions.
The definition of 'medicine' specifically excludes veterinary medicine and surgery.
The Act aims to promote equitable and universal healthcare and encourage community health perspective.
The Central Government has significant powers, including the power to give directions and supersede the Commission.

title: THE INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL SERVICES CENTRES AUTHORITY ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an Authority to develop and regulate the financial services market in the International Financial Services Centres in India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the International Financial Services Centres set up under section 18 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005. It governs financial products, financial services, and financial institutions within these centers.

key_definitions.appropriate regulator: Any financial sector regulator specified in the First Schedule to this Act.
key_definitions.Authority: The International Financial Services Centres Authority established under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.financial institution: A unit set up in an International Financial Services Centre and which is engaged in rendering financial services in respect of any financial product.
key_definitions.financial product: Includes securities, contracts of insurance, deposits, credit arrangements, foreign currency contracts (excluding immediate exchange contracts), and any other product notified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.financial service: Includes activities like buying/selling financial products, accepting deposits, safeguarding assets, effecting insurance contracts, managing assets, exercising rights related to financial products, operating investment schemes, maintaining ownership records, underwriting, providing financial standing information, selling/providing payment instruments, making arrangements for these services, and rendering advice or solicitation related to financial products or services. It also includes any other service notified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.foreign currency: Has the meaning assigned to it in clause (m) of section 2 of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
key_definitions.International Financial Services Centre: An International Financial Services Centre set up, before or after the commencement of this Act, under section 18 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Authority and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made by the Central Government under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Authority under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and stipulates that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette, allowing for different dates for different provisions.
Specifies that the Act applies to International Financial Services Centres established under section 18 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appropriate regulator', 'Authority', 'financial institution', 'financial product', 'financial service', 'foreign currency', 'International Financial Services Centre', 'Member', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'regulations'.

Establishes the International Financial Services Centres Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It outlines the Central Government's power to establish the Authority, its head office location, and its ability to establish offices elsewhere.

Details the composition of the Authority, which includes a Chairperson, ex officio members nominated by RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA, two ex officio members from the Ministry of Finance, and two other members appointed on the recommendation of a Selection Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Terms of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and other Members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for the Chairperson and Members (three years, eligible for re-appointment), age limits, and conditions of service. It also includes provisions for resignation and restrictions on accepting employment after ceasing to hold office.

Outlines the grounds on which the Central Government may remove a Member from office, including insolvency, mental or physical incapacity, conviction of an offence involving moral turpitude, acquiring prejudicial financial interest, or abusing their position.

Governs the meetings of the Authority, including meeting times and places, quorum, and rules of procedure. It also addresses the presiding member in the Chairperson's absence and decision-making by majority vote with a casting vote for the Chairperson.

Defines the primary duty of the Authority as developing and regulating financial products, financial services, and financial institutions in International Financial Services Centres. It also includes regulating existing and notified financial products/services/institutions and recommending new ones to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Authority in relation to financial products, financial services and financial institutions
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority all powers exercisable by an 'appropriate regulator' as specified in the First Schedule, within the International Financial Services Centres, notwithstanding anything in other laws.
Relates to transactions conducted in foreign currency within the International Financial Services Centres.
Grants the Authority the power to issue directions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede Authority
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to supersede the Authority under certain circumstances.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have an overriding effect on other laws.

main_sections.section_title: Power to modify provisions of other enactments in relation to International Financial Services Centres
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to modify provisions of other enactments concerning International Financial Services Centres.
Provides for the amendment of certain enactments as specified in the Second Schedule.

important_rules: The Authority shall develop and regulate financial products, financial services, and financial institutions in International Financial Services Centres.
The Authority shall regulate financial products, services, and institutions permitted before the Act's commencement and those notified by the Central Government.
Members of the Authority are subject to specific terms of office, re-appointment eligibility, and age limits.
Members can be removed for reasons such as insolvency, incapacity, or acquiring prejudicial interests.
The Authority's proceedings are not invalidated by vacancies or defects in the constitution or appointment of members.
The Chairperson has general superintendence and direction over administrative matters.
The Central Government has the power to supersede the Authority if it is of the opinion that the Authority has failed to discharge its duties or has exceeded its powers.
The Central Government can make rules, and the Authority can make regulations, to carry out the Act's provisions.
The Act's provisions override other laws where applicable.

rights: Right of the Authority to regulate financial products, services, and institutions.
Right of the Authority to exercise powers of appropriate regulators within IFSCs.
Right of the Central Government to issue directions, supersede the Authority, and modify other enactments.
duties: Duty of the Authority to develop and regulate the financial services market in IFSCs.
Duty of members to disclose interests in matters before the Authority.
Duty of the Central Government to appoint members and notify commencement dates.
obligations: Obligations of Members regarding their term of office, resignation, and post-employment restrictions.
Obligations regarding the maintenance of the Authority's website and submission of returns and reports.

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairperson and Members by the Central Government, including nomination by specific regulators and a Selection Committee.
Conduct of Authority meetings with specified quorum and voting procedures.
Procedure for removal of a Member from office.
Procedure for the Central Government to supersede the Authority.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules and the Authority to make regulations.
Procedure for the Central Government to modify provisions of other enactments.
Procedure for the Central Government to remove difficulties.
administration: The International Financial Services Centres Authority, established by the Central Government, is the primary administrative body. The Central Government also plays a role in its establishment, appointment of members, and oversight.
important_notes: Different provisions of the Act can come into force on different dates as notified by the Central Government.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws in relation to International Financial Services Centres.
The First Schedule lists 'appropriate regulators' and the respective Acts they regulate.
The Second Schedule lists enactments that are amended by this Act.

title: THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR HOMOEOPATHY ACT, 2020
purpose: To provide for a medical education system that improves access to quality and affordable medical education, ensures availability of adequate and high quality Homoeopathy medical professionals in all parts of the country; that promotes equitable and universal healthcare that encourages community health perspective and makes services of Homoeopathy medical professionals accessible and affordable to all the citizens; that promotes national health goals; that encourages Homoeopathy medical professionals to adopt latest medical research in their work and to contribute to research; that has an objective periodic and transparent assessment of medical institutions and facilitates maintenance of a Homoeopathy medical register for India and enforces high ethical standards in all aspects of medical services; that is flexible to adapt to the changing needs and has an effective grievance redressal mechanism.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the regulation of homoeopathy medical education, assessment of medical institutions, and maintenance of registers of homoeopathy practitioners.

key_definitions.Autonomous Board: Any of the Autonomous Boards constituted under section 18.
key_definitions.Commission: The National Commission for Homoeopathy constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Homoeopathy: The Homoeopathic System of Medicine and includes the use of biochemic remedies supplemented by such modern advances, scientific and technological development as the Commission may, in consultation with the Central Government, declare by notification from time to time.
key_definitions.Medical institution: Any institution within or outside India which grants degrees, diplomas or licences in Homoeopathy and includes affiliated colleges and deemed to be Universities.
key_definitions.National Register: A National Medical Register for Homoeopathy maintained by the Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy under section 32.
key_definitions.State Medical Council: A State Medical Council of Homoeopathy constituted under any law for the time being in force in any State or Union territory for regulating the practice and registration of practitioners of Homoeopathy.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of its commencement.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of National Commission for Homoeopathy
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of the National Commission for Homoeopathy by the Central Government and outlines its corporate status, perpetual succession, and power to sue and be sued.

main_sections.description: Specifies the powers and functions of the Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Homoeopathy.

main_sections.description: Provides for the maintenance of a National Register and State Registers of Homoeopathy practitioners.

main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for recognition of homoeopathy qualifications obtained in India.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions to Commission and Autonomous Boards
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Commission and Autonomous Boards.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Commission to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.
Repeals previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: The Central Government shall, by notification, constitute the National Commission for Homoeopathy to exercise powers and perform functions assigned to it.
The Commission shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Chairperson and Members (other than ex officio Members) shall hold office for a term not exceeding four years and shall not be eligible for re-appointment.

rights: Rights of persons to practice Homoeopathy (Section 34).

Procedure for obtaining permission for establishment of new medical institutions (Section 29).

title: THE DIRECT TAX VIVAD SE VISHWAS ACT, 2020
purpose: To provide for resolution of disputed tax and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to assessees under the Income-tax Act, 1961, with pending appeals, petitions, objections, or assessments related to disputed tax, interest, penalties, or fees. It covers tax arrears as defined in the Act.

key_definitions.appellant: A person in whose case an appeal, writ petition, or special leave petition is pending or has been decided, or who has filed objections before the Dispute Resolution Panel, or has applied for revision, as defined more specifically within the Act.
key_definitions.appellate_forum: The Supreme Court, High Court, Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, or the Commissioner (Appeals).
key_definitions.declarant: A person who files a declaration under section 4 of the Act.
key_definitions.declaration: The declaration filed under section 4 of the Act.
key_definitions.designated_authority: An officer not below the rank of a Commissioner of Income-tax notified by the Principal Chief Commissioner for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.disputed_fee: Fee determined under the Income-tax Act, 1961, in respect of which an appeal has been filed by the appellant.
key_definitions.disputed_income: The whole or so much of the total income as is relatable to the disputed tax.
key_definitions.disputed_interest: Interest determined under the Income-tax Act, 1961, where it is not charged on disputed tax and an appeal has been filed.
key_definitions.disputed_penalty: Penalty determined under the Income-tax Act, 1961, where it is not levied on disputed income or tax and an appeal has been filed.
key_definitions.disputed_tax: Income-tax, including surcharge and cess, payable by the appellant under the Income-tax Act, 1961, as computed based on the status of pending or decided appeals, orders, or objections.
key_definitions.last_date: Such date as may be notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.tax_arrear: The aggregate amount of disputed tax, interest, and penalty, or disputed interest, disputed penalty, or disputed fee, as determined under the Income-tax Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appellant', 'appellate forum', 'declarant', 'declaration', 'designated authority', 'disputed fee', 'disputed income', 'disputed interest', 'disputed penalty', 'disputed tax', 'Income-tax Act', 'last date', 'prescribed', 'specified date', and 'tax arrear'. It also clarifies that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Income-tax Act shall have the meanings assigned to them in that Act.

Specifies the amount payable by a declarant who files a declaration under section 4 in respect of tax arrear. The amount payable varies based on the nature of the tax arrear and whether it is paid on or before December 31, 2020, or later, and also considers cases involving search under sections 132 or 132A of the Income-tax Act. It also outlines provisions for cases where the income-tax authority files an appeal or where the appellant has already received a favorable decision from higher appellate forums.

main_sections.section_title: Filing of declaration and particulars to be furnished.
