main_sections.description: Details the process of filing a declaration, which includes filing before the designated authority in the prescribed form and manner. It states that upon filing the declaration, any pending appeals or petitions related to the disputed tax arrear shall be deemed withdrawn. It also requires the declarant to withdraw any pending appeals, writ petitions, arbitration, conciliation, or mediation proceedings and furnish proof of such withdrawal.

Outlines the time and manner of payment of the amount determined under section 3. It also requires the declarant to furnish proof of withdrawal of proceedings and intimation of payment to the designated authority.

main_sections.section_title: Immunity from initiation of proceedings in respect of offence and imposition of penalty in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Grants immunity from initiation of proceedings for offenses and imposition of penalties in certain cases upon fulfilling the conditions of the Act.
States that there shall be no refund of any amount paid under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: No benefit, concession or immunity to declarant.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the declarant shall not receive any benefit, concession, or immunity other than what is provided under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Specifies certain cases where the provisions of this Act shall not apply. (Details not fully provided in the excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to issue directions, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board (likely the Central Board of Direct Taxes) to issue directions for the proper implementation of the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: A declarant filing a declaration in respect of tax arrear must pay a specified amount, which is either the disputed tax amount, or the disputed tax plus ten or thirty-five percent of the disputed tax, or twenty-five percent of the disputed interest/penalty/fee, depending on the nature of the tax arrear. These percentages may vary based on the payment date and whether the tax arrear involves search assessments.

Rule 2: If the income-tax authority files an appeal, or if the appellant has already secured a favorable decision from higher appellate forums, the amount payable is reduced to one-half of the amount calculated as per the main table.
Rule 3: Upon filing a declaration, any pending appeals or petitions related to the disputed tax arrear are deemed withdrawn.

Rule 4: The declarant must withdraw any pending appeals, writ petitions, or other dispute resolution proceedings (arbitration, conciliation, mediation) after a certificate is issued and furnish proof of withdrawal.
Rule 5: The declarant must furnish an undertaking waiving their right to pursue the withdrawn proceedings.

penalties: Immunity from initiation of proceedings in respect of offence and imposition of penalty in certain cases (Section 6).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Designated authority (an officer not below the rank of Commissioner of Income-tax notified by the Principal Chief Commissioner).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the filing of declarations, payment of amounts as specified, withdrawal of pending proceedings, and furnishing of undertakings. The Act itself provides a mechanism for dispute resolution by offering a settlement route for past tax disputes.

rights: Right to seek resolution of disputed tax under the scheme.
Right to immunity from further proceedings for offenses and penalties in certain cases upon compliance.
Option to include the amount of tax related to tax credit or loss in disputed tax, or carry forward the reduced amount.
duties: Duty to file a declaration before the designated authority.
Duty to pay the amount determined under section 3.
Duty to withdraw all pending appeals, writ petitions, arbitration, conciliation, or mediation proceedings.
Duty to furnish proof of withdrawal of proceedings and intimation of payment.
Duty to furnish an undertaking waiving rights in withdrawn proceedings.
obligations: Obligation to settle tax disputes by paying a reduced amount.
Obligation to not seek refunds of amounts paid under the Act.
Obligation to not claim any benefit, concession, or immunity other than provided by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Filing a Declaration: A declarant files a declaration with the designated authority in the prescribed form and manner, in respect of a tax arrear.

Procedure 2: Payment of Amount: The declarant pays the amount determined under section 3, which is a percentage of the disputed tax, interest, penalty, or fee, depending on the nature of the arrear and payment timeline.

Procedure 3: Withdrawal of Proceedings: Upon filing the declaration, the declarant must withdraw any pending appeals, writ petitions, or other dispute resolution proceedings. Proof of withdrawal must be furnished.

Procedure 4: Issuance of Certificate and Grant of Immunity: After payment and withdrawal of proceedings, a certificate is issued, and the declarant receives immunity from further proceedings related to the settled dispute.
administration: The Act is administered by the designated authorities notified by the Principal Chief Commissioner. The Central Board of Direct Taxes likely plays a supervisory role. The Central Government is empowered to make rules and remove difficulties.
important_notes: The Act provides for a one-time measure for resolution of disputed tax and does not apply to cases where an order has been passed by the Settlement Commission under Chapter XIX-A of the Income-tax Act.
No refund of any amount paid under the Act will be provided.
The Act is not applicable in certain specific cases, as detailed in Section 9.
The definition of 'specified date' is January 31, 2020.
Amendments have been made by Act 38 of 2020 and Act 13 of 2021, impacting dates and definitions.

title: The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda Act, 2020
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda and to declare it as an Institution of national importance for the promotion of quality and excellence in education, research and training in Ayurveda and allied disciplines.
scope: This Act applies to the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, which is established by the conglomeration of three preceding institutions: the Institute of Post Graduate Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Jamnagar; Shree Gulabkunverba Ayurved Mahavidyalaya, Jamnagar; and the Indian Institute of Ayurvedic Pharmaceutical Sciences, Jamnagar. It also includes the Maharishi Patanjali Institute for Yoga Naturopathy Education and Research, Jamnagar, as a Department of Swasthvritta.

key_definitions.Anteceding Institutions: The Institute of Post Graduate Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Jamnagar, Shree Gulabkunverba Ayurved Mahavidyalaya, Jamnagar, and the Indian Institute of Ayurvedic Pharmaceutical Sciences, Jamnagar.
key_definitions.Institute: The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda established by conglomerating Anteceding Institutions and incorporated under section 4.
key_definitions.Gujarat Ayurved University Act, 1965: The Act under which Gujarat Ayurved University was established and incorporated.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of the Institute appointed under sub-section (1) of section 11.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette. Different dates can be appointed for different provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, as incorporated under this Act, to be an institution of national importance.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Anteceding Institutions', 'Department of Swasthvritta', 'Director', 'Fund', 'Governing Body', 'Gujarat Ayurved University', 'Indian Institute of Ayurvedic Pharmaceutical Sciences, Jamnagar', 'Institute', 'Institute of Post Graduate Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Jamnagar', 'member', 'prescribed', 'regulation', and 'Shree Gulabkunverba Ayurved Mahavidyalaya, Jamnagar'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Anteceding Institutions as Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda
main_sections.description: Establishes the three Anteceding Institutions as a body corporate under the Act, to be known as the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda. It also grants the Institute perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of incorporation of Anteceding Institutions as Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda
main_sections.description: Outlines the consequences of incorporation, including deeming references to Anteceding Institutions as references to the Institute, vesting of property, transfer of rights and liabilities, continuation of employment for existing staff with provisions for alteration of terms, appointment of the Director and Deputy Directors, migration of students, and continuation of legal proceedings.

Specifies the composition of the Institute, which includes ex officio members such as the Minister in charge of AYUSH, the Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of AYUSH, the Secretary, Department of Health, Government of Gujarat, the Director of the Institute, the technical head of Ayurveda, a nominee from the Ministry of Finance, the Vice-Chancellor of Gujarat Ayurved University, the Director-General of the Central Council for Research in Ayurveda, a nominee from the Ministry of Human Resource Development, three nominated experts in Ayurveda, and three Members of Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Terms of office of, and vacancies among, members
main_sections.description: Defines the term of office for members, including nominated, elected, and ex officio members. It also covers provisions for filling casual vacancies and resignation.

Establishes the position of a President of the Institute, to be nominated by the Central Government from among the members. The President exercises powers and functions as laid down in the Act or prescribed.
Details the procedure for meetings of the Institute, including the first meeting and subsequent meetings, which will be governed by regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Governing Body and other committees of Institute
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a Governing Body as the executive committee of the Institute. The President of the Institute chairs the Governing Body. It also allows for the constitution of other standing and ad hoc committees.

Establishes the role of a chief executive officer designated as the Director, appointed by the Institute. The first Director is deemed to be the existing Director of the Institute of Post Graduate Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Jamnagar.

important_rules: Rule: The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, established by this Act, is declared an institution of national importance.
Rule: The Anteceding Institutions are conglomerated and established as a body corporate named the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda.
Rule: All property, rights, and liabilities of the Anteceding Institutions are transferred to the Institute.
Rule: Employees of the Anteceding Institutions become employees of the Institute with their existing terms and conditions of service, subject to potential alterations.
Rule: The Institute shall have a President, nominated by the Central Government, who exercises prescribed powers and functions.
Rule: A Governing Body is established as the executive committee of the Institute, chaired by the President.
Rule: The Institute shall have a Director as its chief executive officer.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and by extension, the Institute and its appointed authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules and regulations made under the Act, notifications in the Official Gazette, and legal proceedings instituted by or against the Institute.

rights: The right to grant degrees, diplomas, etc.
The right to have its medical qualifications recognized.
The right to sue and be sued in its own name.
duties: To promote quality and excellence in education, research, and training in Ayurveda.
To manage its fund and prepare a budget.
To maintain accounts and undergo audit.
To submit an annual report.
To adhere to rules and regulations made under the Act.
obligations: To ensure the continuation of service for employees of Anteceding Institutions under specific conditions.
To ensure that students pursuing courses in Anteceding Institutions are deemed to have migrated and registered with the Institute.

key_procedures: Procedure for the establishment and incorporation of the Institute by conglomerating Anteceding Institutions.
Procedure for the appointment of the Director and Deputy Directors.
Procedure for the composition and meetings of the Institute and its Governing Body.
Procedure for the regulation of academic courses, research, and training.
Procedure for the resolution of differences between the Institute and the Central Government.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules and the Institute to make regulations.
administration: The Central Government exercises control over the Institute. The Ministry of AYUSH is prominently involved through its ex officio members in the Institute's composition and the Central Government's power to make rules and notifications.
important_notes: The Act came into force on October 15, 2020.
The Institute is recognized as an institution of national importance.
The Act provides for transitional provisions to ensure a smooth transition from the Anteceding Institutions to the new Institute.

title: THE JAMMU AND KASHMIR OFFICIAL LANGUAGES ACT, 2020
purpose: To provide for the languages to be used for the official purposes of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. Subject matter is the official languages and promotion of regional languages within the Union territory.

key_definitions.Administrator: The Lieutenant Governor of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.Union territory: The Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir), and when it comes into force. The commencement date can be appointed by the Central Government, with the Administrator having the power to appoint different dates for different areas.
Defines key terms used in the Act, namely 'Administrator' and 'Union territory'.

Declares Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi, and English as the official languages for all or any official purposes of the Union territory. It allows English to continue for existing administrative and legislative purposes and mandates that business in the Legislative Assembly be transacted in the official languages.

main_sections.section_title: Promotion and development of regional languages.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Administrator to take steps for the promotion and development of regional languages, including strengthening existing institutional mechanisms like the Academy of Art, Culture and languages. It specifically mandates special efforts for the promotion and development of Gojri, Pahari, and Punjabi languages.

important_rules: Rule 1: The official languages of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir shall be Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi, and English.
Rule 2: English may continue to be used for administrative and legislative purposes for which it was used before the commencement of the Act.
Rule 3: Business in the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory shall be transacted in the official language or languages of the Union territory.
Rule 4: The Administrator shall take steps to promote and develop regional languages of the Union territory, with special focus on Gojri, Pahari, and Punjabi.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Administrator of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications by the Administrator and the Central Government, and by strengthening institutional mechanisms for language promotion.

rights: Right to use specified languages for official purposes in the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
Right to continue using English for existing administrative and legislative purposes.
duties: Duty to promote and develop regional languages of the Union territory.
Duty to make special efforts for the promotion and development of Gojri, Pahari, and Punjabi languages.
obligations: Obligation to transact business in the Legislative Assembly in the official language(s).
Obligation to implement steps for language promotion as directed by the Administrator.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Central Government may, by notification, appoint the date for the commencement of the Act. The Administrator may appoint different dates for different areas.
Procedure 2: The Administrator may, by notification, appoint a date for the official languages to be used for all or any of the official purposes of the Union territory.
administration: The Administrator of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Central Government.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act is 29th September, 2020.
The Administrator has the power to appoint different commencement dates for different areas within the Union territory.

title: The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development Act, 2021
purpose: To establish the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development to support the development of long-term non-recourse infrastructure financing in India, including the development of bond and derivatives markets necessary for infrastructure financing, and to carry on the business of financing infrastructure.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It establishes a national bank for financing infrastructure projects.

key_definitions.Institution: The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development established under section 3.
key_definitions.infrastructure: Sectors covered in the list of infrastructure sectors notified by the Central Government from time to time.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Directors constituted under section 6.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board appointed under clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 6.
key_definitions.Managing Director: The director appointed under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 6.
key_definitions.financial institution: Has the meaning assigned to it in clause (m) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002.
key_definitions.Reserve Bank: The Reserve Bank of India established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title, extent (whole of India), and commencement provisions for the Act, stating it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Institution', 'infrastructure', 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Managing Director', 'financial institution', and 'Reserve Bank'. It also refers to definitions in other relevant Acts for undefined terms.

Establishes the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of acquiring, holding, and disposing of property, and suing or being sued. Its head office is in Mumbai, with the possibility of establishing offices elsewhere.

Outlines the developmental and financial objectives of the Institution. Developmentally, it aims to coordinate with various stakeholders to facilitate long-term non-recourse infrastructure financing and the development of domestic bond and derivatives markets. Financially, it aims to lend or invest in infrastructure projects to foster sustainable economic development.

Specifies the authorised share capital of the Institution at one hundred thousand crore rupees, divided into shares. It allows the Board to increase or reduce the capital and defines who can hold shares, with the Central Government required to hold at least twenty-six per cent.

Details the composition of the Board of Directors, including the Chairperson, Managing Director, Deputy Managing Directors, nominated directors from the Central Government, elected directors by shareholders, and independent directors. It also outlines conditions for appointment and the role of the Chairperson.
States that the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Institution's affairs vest in the Board, which exercises all powers and acts on business principles.
Empowers the Board to delegate its powers, by general or special order, to any director, committee, or officer.

important_rules: The Institution is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Board of Directors is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Institution's affairs.
The Board must act on business principles.
The Central Government must hold at least twenty-six per cent. of the Institution's shares at all times.
The Institution's head office shall be in Mumbai.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Board of Directors, with provisions for adjudication and prosecution.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Central Government to make rules, and the Board to make regulations. Sections related to sanctions for enquiry, investigation, and prosecution are included.

rights: The Institution has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The Institution has the right to contract.
The Institution has the right to sue or be sued.
duties: The Institution has a duty to support the development of long-term non-recourse infrastructure financing.
The Institution has a duty to coordinate with various stakeholders to facilitate infrastructure financing.
The Board has a duty to act on business principles.
obligations: Directors have obligations as to fidelity and secrecy (Section 38).
The Institution has obligations related to receiving receivables in trust (Section 28).

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairperson, Managing Director, Deputy Managing Directors, and other directors to the Board (Section 6).
Constitution and functioning of committees of the Board (Section 15).
Preparation of balance sheets and accounts, and audit procedures (Sections 25 and 26).
Procedures for making rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Board (Sections 31 and 32).
administration: The Central Government and the Board of Directors.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force.
The appointment of directors under clauses (d) and (f) of sub-section (1) of section 6 are deemed independent directors for the purpose of immunities available under the Companies Act, 2013.
The Act has overriding effect over other laws in certain circumstances (Section 45).

title: The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021
purpose: To provide for the constitution of the Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas for better coordination, research, identification and resolution of problems surrounding the air quality index and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the National Capital Region and also to adjoining areas in so far as it relates to matters concerning air pollution in the National Capital Region. Adjoining areas are defined as areas in Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh, adjoining the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the National Capital Region, where any source of pollution is located, causing adverse impact on air quality in the National Capital Region.

key_definitions.adjoining areas: The areas in the States of Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, adjoining the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the National Capital Region, where any source of pollution is located, causing adverse impact on air quality in the National Capital Region.
key_definitions.associate member: A member who is co-opted under sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.chairperson: The Chairperson of the Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas.
key_definitions.commission: The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.member: A Member of the Commission and includes the Chairperson thereof.
key_definitions.national capital region: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (f) of section 2 of the National Capital Region Planning Board Act, 1985 (2 of 1985).
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial application to the National Capital Region and adjoining areas, and its deemed commencement date.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'adjoining areas', 'Associate Member', 'Chairperson', 'Commission', 'Member', 'National Capital Region', and 'prescribed'.

Details the constitution of the Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas, including its composition, ex officio members, associate members, and the role of the Member-Secretary. It also establishes the headquarters and the Commission's exclusive jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chairperson, Members and Member-Secretary
main_sections.description: Outlines the appointment process for the Chairperson, full-time Members, and Member-Secretary by the Central Government, including the role of a Selection Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation and removal of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Provides for the resignation of the Chairperson or Members and the grounds and procedure for their removal by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for the Chairperson and Members (excluding ex officio Members) as three years or until the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier, and their eligibility for re-appointment.

main_sections.section_title: Member to act as Chairperson or to discharge his functions in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Describes the procedure for appointing a Member to act as Chairperson in case of vacancy or absence of the Chairperson.

main_sections.section_title: Terms and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: States that the salaries, allowances, and other terms and conditions of service for the Chairperson and Members (excluding ex officio Members) shall be as prescribed, and that these shall not be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of Commission
main_sections.description: Ensures that the proceedings of the Commission are not invalidated due to any vacancy or defect in its constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be regulated by Commission
main_sections.description: Grants the Commission power to regulate its own procedure, including meeting times and places, and to delegate powers.

main_sections.section_title: Sub-Committees and other staff of Commission
main_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of at least three Sub-Committees: Monitoring and Identification, Safeguarding and Enforcement, and Research and Development.
Outlines the powers and functions of the Commission related to air quality management.
Requires the Commission to submit an annual report.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of Act, rules, order or direction
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act, rules, orders, or directions issued by the Commission.
Provides for the imposition of environmental compensation.
Details the grants that may be provided by the Central Government to the Commission.
Covers the accounts and audit procedures for the Commission.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders or decisions made under the Act.
Empowers the constitution of special investigation teams.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue direction
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to call for information
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to call for information.
Limits the jurisdiction of civil courts in certain matters.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Members and officers to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares Members and officers of the Commission as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Commission to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Commission to make regulations for its functioning.
Allows the Central Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in certain respects.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal and savings of order constituting Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority for National Capital Region
main_sections.description: Deals with the repeal and savings related to the order constituting the Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority for the National Capital Region.
Contains general savings provisions.
Provides for the repeal of previous provisions and savings.

important_rules: The Commission shall have exclusive jurisdiction in the National Capital Region and adjoining areas in respect of matters covered by this Act, and no other body shall have power in such matters. Orders and directions of the Commission shall prevail in case of conflict with other authorities.
The Chairperson and full-time Members, other than ex officio Members, shall be appointed by the Central Government on the recommendations of a Selection Committee.

The Chairperson or a Member may resign by giving written notice to the Central Government. The Central Government may remove a Member for specific reasons after giving them an opportunity to be heard.
The Commission shall have at least three Sub-Committees: Monitoring and Identification; Safeguarding and Enforcement; and Research and Development.
The Central Government may make rules, and the Commission may make regulations, to carry out the provisions of the Act.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of provisions of Act, rules, order or direction (Section 14).
Environmental compensation (Section 15).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas, and empowered by the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties and environmental compensation for contraventions, and by exercising its powers and functions related to air quality management. The Commission can also form special investigation teams.

rights: Right to appeal against orders or decisions made under the Act (Section 18).
Protection of action taken in good faith by individuals acting under the Act (Section 23).
duties: Duty of the Commission to coordinate, research, identify, and resolve problems surrounding air quality.
Duty of Members and officers to act as public servants (Section 24).
Duty of the Commission to submit an annual report (Section 13).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act, rules, orders, and directions issued by the Commission.
Obligation for individuals and authorities within the National Capital Region and adjoining areas to adhere to the jurisdiction and directives of the Commission.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Commission: Central Government to constitute the Commission by notification, specifying its composition and appointment of members through a Selection Committee. (Sections 3 & 4)
Appointment and Removal of Members: Appointment by Central Government on recommendations, with provisions for resignation and removal based on specified grounds. (Sections 4 & 5)
Regulation of Procedure: The Commission to meet at convenient times and places and to lay down its own procedure by regulations. Orders and decisions to be authenticated. (Section 10)
Sub-Committee Formation: Establishment of specific Sub-Committees for monitoring, safeguarding, and research. (Section 11)
Rule and Regulation Making: Central Government to make rules, and the Commission to make regulations. (Sections 25 & 26)
Appeals: Procedure for filing appeals against orders/decisions. (Section 18)
administration: The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas is the primary body responsible for administration, with oversight and rule-making powers vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 13, 2021. (Section 1(3))
The Commission has exclusive jurisdiction in the National Capital Region and adjoining areas, and its orders prevail over those of other authorities in case of conflict. (Section 3(6))
The Central Government has the power to issue directions and call for information to ensure effective implementation of the Act. (Sections 20 & 21)
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning it prevails over other laws in force to the extent of any inconsistency. (Section 28)
Specific provisions exist for the repeal and savings of previous orders and enactments related to air quality management in the region. (Sections 29 & 31)

title: The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021
purpose: To further amend various existing Acts to reform the functioning and structure of Tribunals in India, including provisions related to the conditions of service for Chairpersons and Members, and to make consequential amendments to several other Acts.
scope: This Act applies to the Central Government, various Tribunals established under different Acts of Parliament, and individuals appointed as Chairpersons or Members of these Tribunals. It amends multiple acts including the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, Cinematograph Act, 1952, Copyright Act, 1957, Income-Tax Act, 1961, Customs Act, 1962, and many others listed in its chapters. Geographically, it applies across India where these amended Acts are in force.

key_definitions.Chairperson: Includes Chairperson, Chairman, President, and Presiding Officer of a Tribunal.
key_definitions.Member: Includes Vice-Chairman, Vice-Chairperson, Vice-President, Account Member, Administrative Member, Judicial Member, Expert Member, Law Member, Revenue Member, and Technical Member of a Tribunal.
key_definitions.Schedule: Means the Schedule appended to this Act.
key_definitions.Tribunal: Means a Tribunal, Appellate Tribunal, or Authority as specified in column (2) of the First Schedule.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021' and specifies that it is deemed to have come into force on April 4, 2021.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Chairperson', 'Member', 'notified date', 'Schedule', and 'Tribunal'.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications, appointment, etc., of Chairperson and Members of Tribunal
main_sections.description: Outlines the qualifications, appointment process, salaries, allowances, resignation, removal, and other conditions of service for Chairpersons and Members of Tribunals. It establishes a Search-cum-Selection Committee for making recommendations, with specific compositions for general Tribunals and State Administrative Tribunals. It also sets a minimum age of fifty years for appointment.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of Chairperson or Member of Tribunal
main_sections.description: Details the grounds and procedures for the removal of a Chairperson or Member of a Tribunal by the Central Government based on recommendations from the Committee, including insolvency, conviction, incapacity, financial interest, or abuse of position. It mandates providing an opportunity to be heard before removal on certain grounds.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of Chairperson and Member of Tribunal
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for a Chairperson (four years or till age seventy, whichever is earlier) and a Member (four years or till age sixty-seven, whichever is earlier). It includes a proviso for appointments made between May 26, 2017, and the notified date, allowing for potentially longer terms or retirement ages as per the original appointment order, up to a maximum of five years.
States that Chairpersons and Members are eligible for re-appointment, with preference given to service rendered. Re-appointments are to be made in the same manner as initial appointments.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for the salary, allowances, and benefits of Chairpersons and Members, equivalent to Central Government officers holding similar posts. It allows for reimbursement of house rent higher than standard allowances under certain conditions and prohibits varying salary and allowances to the disadvantage of the appointee after their appointment.
Amends Section 7D of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, to link the conditions of service of certain persons to the provisions of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, instead of the Finance Act, 2017.

Makes several amendments to the Cinematograph Act, 1952, including omitting certain clauses and sections related to Tribunals and substituting 'High Court' for 'Tribunal' in various provisions. It also omits specific clauses from Section 8(2).

Amends the Copyright Act, 1957, by omitting clause (aa) of Section 2, re-lettering clause (fa) and inserting a definition for 'Commercial Court', and substituting a new definition for 'prescribed' in clause (u).
Grants the Central Government the power to amend the Schedule appended to the Act by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Specifies that any rules made under this Act shall be laid before each House of Parliament.
Deals with provisions to facilitate the transition and implementation of the reforms introduced by this Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make provisions, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any inconsistent provisions and savings for actions taken under previous laws.

important_rules: Rule 1: Persons appointed as Chairperson or Member must have completed the age of fifty years.
Rule 2: The Search-cum-Selection Committee's recommendations for appointments must be decided upon by the Central Government preferably within three months.
Rule 3: The salary and allowances, and other terms and conditions of service of a Chairperson or Member cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
Rule 4: Rules made under this Act must be laid before each House of Parliament.

rights: Right of Chairperson or Member to be informed of charges and given an opportunity to be heard before removal on grounds of incapacity, financial interest, or abuse of position.
Right of Chairperson or Member to have salary and allowances and other terms of service not varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
duties: Duty of Central Government to make rules for qualifications, appointment, salaries, etc., of Chairpersons and Members.
Duty of Central Government to appoint Chairpersons and Members on the recommendation of the Search-cum-Selection Committee.
Duty of Search-cum-Selection Committee to recommend a panel of two names for each post.
Duty of Central Government to lay rules before Parliament.
Duty of Central Government to remove difficulties in implementation.
obligations: Obligation for individuals seeking appointment as Chairperson or Member to have completed 50 years of age.
Obligation for Central Government to consider the experience and specialization in the relevant field when making rules for qualifications.
Obligation for Central Government to decide on committee recommendations within a preferred timeframe.
Obligation to follow specific procedures for removal of Chairperson or Member on certain grounds.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointment of Chairperson and Members: A Search-cum-Selection Committee is constituted. The Committee recommends a panel of two names to the Central Government, which then makes the appointment. The process involves specific compositions for the committee depending on the type of tribunal.

Procedure for removal of Chairperson or Member: Removal requires a recommendation from the Committee. For grounds of incapacity, financial interest, or abuse of position, the individual must be informed of the charges and given an opportunity to be heard.
Procedure for amendment of Schedules: The Central Government can amend the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for making rules, appointing Chairpersons and Members, and administering various aspects of the Act, including removing difficulties. The specific ministry or department administering a Tribunal is involved in the Search-cum-Selection Committee process.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 4, 2021.

Provisions related to Chairperson and Member terms and retirement ages may be subject to earlier appointment orders for individuals appointed between May 26, 2017, and the notified date, with a maximum term of five years.
The Search-cum-Selection Committee's composition varies for general tribunals and State Administrative Tribunals.
The Act extensively amends numerous other legislative acts, indicating a significant reform in the tribunal system.

title: The Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021
purpose: To repeal the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020, the Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020, and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020, and to amend the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
scope: This act applies to the repeal of specific farm laws enacted in 2020 and an amendment to the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, within India.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Acts 20 of 2020, 21 of 2020 and 22 of 2020
main_sections.description: Repeals the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020, the Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020, and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020.
Amends the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, by omitting sub-section (1A) of section 3.

important_rules: Rule: The Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020 (Act No. 20 of 2020) is repealed.
Rule: The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020 (Act No. 21 of 2020) is repealed.
Rule: The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020 (Act No. 22 of 2020) is repealed.
Rule: Sub-section (1A) of section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (Act No. 10 of 1955) shall be omitted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be government authorities responsible for the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, for the amendment portion.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would primarily involve the legal discontinuation of the repealed acts and the modification of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

key_procedures: Procedure: Repeal of specified Acts (Acts 20 of 2020, 21 of 2020, and 22 of 2020).
Procedure: Amendment of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, by omitting sub-section (1A) of section 3.
administration: The administration of the amended Essential Commodities Act, 1955, would fall under the relevant government department, likely the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution.
important_notes: Note: The Statement of Objects and Reasons mentions that the repealed acts were enacted with the objective of improving the condition of farmers, providing them freedom to sell produce, creating an ecosystem for engagement with buyers, facilitating electronic trading, and providing a legal framework for farming contracts.

Note: The repeal is stated to be in view of the need to take everyone together on the path of inclusive growth and development, and in light of the fact that the operation of the aforesaid Farm Laws had been stayed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

title: The Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022
purpose: To authorize the taking of measurements of convicts and other persons for the purposes of identification and investigation in criminal matters, to preserve records, and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto. It aims to modernize identification techniques and expand the scope of persons whose measurements can be taken to improve the efficiency and expedition of crime investigation and increase conviction rates.
scope: The Act applies to persons convicted of an offence, persons ordered to give security for good behaviour or maintaining peace, persons arrested in connection with an offence, or persons detained under preventive detention law. It also applies to investigations and proceedings under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and any other law for the time being in force. Geographically, it applies throughout India, with provisions for State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to notify agencies within their jurisdictions.

key_definitions.Magistrate: Includes Metropolitan Magistrate in a metropolitan area, Judicial Magistrate of the first class in any other area, or Executive Magistrate for ordering security for good behaviour or maintaining peace.
key_definitions.measurements: Includes finger-impressions, palm-print impressions, foot-print impressions, photographs, iris and retina scan, physical, biological samples and their analysis, behavioural attributes including signatures, handwriting or any other examination referred to in section 53 or section 53A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
key_definitions.police officer: An officer-in-charge of a police station or an officer not below the rank of Head Constable.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prison officer: An officer of prison not below the rank of Head Warder.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Magistrate', 'measurements', 'police officer', 'prescribed', and 'prison officer'. It also states that undefined terms have the same meanings as in the Indian Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Authorizes police officers or prison officers to take measurements of persons convicted of an offence, ordered to give security for good behaviour/peace, arrested in connection with an offence, or detained under preventive detention law, as may be prescribed. It includes a proviso exempting persons arrested for certain offences from being obliged to allow the taking of biological samples.

main_sections.section_title: Collection, storing, preservation of measurements and storing, sharing, dissemination, destruction and disposal of records
main_sections.description: Mandates the National Crime Records Bureau to collect, store, preserve, destroy, process, share, and disseminate records of measurements at a national level for crime prevention, detection, investigation, and prosecution. Records are to be retained for seventy-five years, with provisions for destruction if a person is released without trial or acquitted. State Governments and Union Territory Administrations can notify agencies for these purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Magistrate to direct a person to give measurements
main_sections.description: Empowers a Magistrate to order any person to provide measurements if deemed expedient for any investigation or proceeding under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, or any other law. The person must comply with such directions.

main_sections.section_title: Resistance to allow taking of measurements
main_sections.description: States that if a person resists or refuses to allow measurements to be taken, police or prison officers are authorized to take them. Resistance or refusal is deemed an offence under section 186 of the Indian Penal Code.
Prohibits any suit or proceeding against any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act or its rules.

Empowers the Central Government or State Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes. These rules can cover the manner of taking, collecting, storing, preserving, sharing, disseminating, destroying, and disposing of measurements and records. It also outlines the procedure for laying rules before Parliament or State Legislatures.

Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove any difficulty in giving effect to the Act's provisions, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act and are made within three years of its commencement. Such orders must be laid before Parliament.

Repeals the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920. It includes a saving clause stating that actions taken under the repealed Act will be deemed to have been taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act, unless inconsistent. It also refers to the general application of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897.

important_rules: Measurements of persons convicted of offences, or arrested or detained under certain laws, must be allowed to be taken by police or prison officers as prescribed.
The National Crime Records Bureau is responsible for collecting, storing, preserving, and disseminating measurement records at the national level.
Measurement records will be retained digitally for seventy-five years from collection.
Measurement records of individuals released without trial or acquitted will be destroyed unless a court or Magistrate directs otherwise in writing.
Resistance or refusal to allow the taking of measurements is an offence under Section 186 of the Indian Penal Code.

penalties: Resistance to or refusal to allow the taking of measurements is deemed an offence under section 186 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers and prison officers are authorized to take measurements. The National Crime Records Bureau is responsible for national-level data management. Magistrates have the power to direct persons to give measurements.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the authorized actions of police and prison officers, and through judicial orders by Magistrates. The National Crime Records Bureau manages the collection, storage, and dissemination of data. Resistance is a punishable offence under the Indian Penal Code.

rights: Right to have measurement records destroyed if released without trial or acquitted (unless a court directs otherwise).
duties: Duty to allow measurements to be taken if convicted, arrested, detained, or ordered to give security for good behaviour/peace.
Duty to comply with a Magistrate's order to give measurements.
obligations: Obligation not to resist or refuse to allow the taking of measurements.

key_procedures: Taking of measurements: A police officer or prison officer can take measurements of a person if they are convicted, arrested, detained, or ordered to give security for good behaviour/peace. The manner of taking measurements is prescribed by rules.
Direction by Magistrate: A Magistrate can order any person to give measurements for investigation or proceedings under relevant laws. The person must comply.

Collection, storing, and dissemination: The National Crime Records Bureau collects, stores, preserves, and disseminates measurement records. State/UT governments can also notify agencies for this purpose.
Destruction of records: Records of individuals not previously convicted, who are released without trial or acquitted, shall be destroyed unless a court/Magistrate orders otherwise.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments are responsible for making rules under the Act. The National Crime Records Bureau is designated for national-level data management. State Governments and Union Territory Administrations can notify appropriate agencies for collection, preservation, and sharing of measurements.
important_notes: The definition of 'measurements' is significantly expanded to include modern techniques beyond traditional finger and footprints.
The period for retaining measurement records is set at seventy-five years.
The Act repeals the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920.
A person arrested for an offence (with specific exceptions) may not be obliged to provide biological samples.

title: The Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022
purpose: To give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea relating to the repression of piracy on high seas and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the high seas. It covers acts of piracy, attempts to commit piracy, and organizing or directing others to participate in piracy. It also defines 'piracy' in accordance with international law and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

key_definitions.authorised_personnel: Officers and sailors assigned to warships or military aircraft of the Indian Navy, or officers and enrolled persons of the Coast Guard assigned to ships or aircraft of the Indian Coast Guard, or officers of the Central Government or the State Government authorized for any ship or aircraft clearly marked and identifiable as being on Government service.
key_definitions.code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.convention: The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982.
key_definitions.designated_court: A Court of Session specified as such under section 8.
key_definitions.high_seas: Includes the Exclusive Economic Zone and all waters beyond the jurisdiction of any other State. 'Exclusive Economic Zone' means the Exclusive Economic Zone of any other State including the Exclusive Economic Zone of India.
key_definitions.piracy: Includes any illegal act of violence or detention or any act of depredation committed for private ends by any person or by the crew or any passenger of a private ship and directed on the high seas against another ship or any person or property on board such ship; any act of voluntary participation in the operation of a ship with knowledge of facts, making it a pirate ship; any act of inciting or of intentionally facilitating an act of piracy; or any act which is deemed piratical under the international law including customary international law.
key_definitions.pirate_ship: A ship which is intended by the person in dominant control to be used for the purposes of committing any of the acts of piracy, or has been used to commit any such act, so long as it remains under the control of the person guilty of that act.
key_definitions.ship: Includes vessel or water craft of every description, including non-displacement craft; sea planes and other aircraft, used or capable of being used as means of transportation on water or engaged in any operations at sea.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, the date of commencement notified by the Central Government, and specifies that the Act applies to the high seas.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including authorized personnel, Code, Convention, Designated Court, high seas, piracy, pirate ship, ship, and stateless person. It also states that terms not defined in this Act but defined in the Convention, Indian Penal Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, or the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976, shall have their respective meanings.

Prescribes the punishment for committing piracy, which can include imprisonment for life or fine, or death or imprisonment for life if the act of piracy causes death or an attempt thereof. It also allows for restitution or forfeiture of property involved.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for attempt to commit piracy, etc.
main_sections.description: States that anyone who attempts to commit piracy, or aids, abets, conspires, or procures its commission, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to ten years or with fine or both.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for organising or directing others to participate in an act of piracy.
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for participating, organizing, or directing others to participate in an act of piracy, with imprisonment up to fourteen years or fine or both.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of power of arrest, investigation, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution, exercisable by a police officer under the Code, on its officers or officers of a State Government for the purposes of this Act, through notification.

main_sections.section_title: Arrest of persons and seizure of ship and property.
main_sections.description: Authorizes authorized personnel to board a ship suspected of piracy on the high seas, arrest persons, and seize the pirate ship and property on board. Disposal of seized items is by court order only.

Mandates the Central Government, in consultation with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court, to specify one or more Courts of Sessions as Designated Courts and their territorial jurisdiction based on the port or place of disembarkation within India.

Grants the Designated Court jurisdiction to try offenses under this Act if committed by a person apprehended by authorized personnel or police, regardless of nationality, or by an Indian citizen, resident foreign national, or stateless person. It excludes warships or government-owned ships under government control at the time of the offense.

main_sections.section_title: Trial of offences by Designated Court.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for trials by Designated Courts, including their exclusive jurisdiction over offenses under this Act, powers regarding detention of accused persons, taking cognizance of offenses, and the ability to try other offenses under different laws concurrently. It also mandates day-to-day trials where practicable.

Establishes a presumption of guilt against an accused person if arms, ammunition, explosives, or equipment used or intended to be used in the commission of the offense are recovered, or if there is evidence of force, threat, or intimidation, or an intended threat of violence.

Restricts the release on bail of persons accused of offenses under this Act, requiring the Public Prosecutor to be given an opportunity to oppose the application and the court to be satisfied that the accused is not guilty and unlikely to commit further offenses while on bail. It preserves the special powers of the High Court regarding bail.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Code in proceedings before Designated Court.
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure apply to proceedings before a Designated Court, and the prosecutor before such court is deemed to be a Public Prosecutor appointed under the Code.

Declares offenses under this Act as extraditable and to be included in all extradition treaties. In the absence of a treaty, offenses are extraditable on the basis of reciprocity. It also clarifies the application of the Extradition Act, 1962, to offenses under this Act, deeming ships registered in other states to be within the jurisdiction of those states.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides immunity from suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings against authorized personnel or government entities for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.

important_rules: Piracy is punishable with imprisonment up to life or death, and forfeiture of property.
Attempting piracy, aiding, abetting, or conspiring to commit piracy is punishable with imprisonment up to ten years.
Organizing or directing others to participate in piracy is punishable with imprisonment up to fourteen years.
Authorized personnel can board ships suspected of piracy, arrest individuals, and seize ships and property.
Designated Courts are established for speedy trials of piracy offenses.
Bail for piracy offenses is restricted, requiring a high threshold of evidence for release.
Offenses under this Act are considered extraditable.

penalties: Imprisonment which may extend to imprisonment for life or with fine or with both for committing piracy.
Death or imprisonment for life, if piracy causes death or an attempt thereof.
Restitution or forfeiture of property involved in the commission of piracy.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years or with fine or with both for attempting piracy or aiding/abetting/conspiring.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to fourteen years or with fine or with both for organizing or directing others to participate in piracy.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorized personnel (Indian Navy, Coast Guard, authorized officers of Central/State Government), Designated Courts, and the Central Government (for notifications and conferring powers).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution conferred on authorized personnel. Speedy trials are conducted by Designated Courts. Extradition provisions are used for international cooperation.

rights: Right to protection from arbitrary legal proceedings for authorized personnel acting in good faith.
Right to speedy trial for accused individuals before Designated Courts.
duties: Duty to uphold the provisions of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea regarding piracy.
Duty of authorized personnel to prevent and repress piracy on the high seas.
Duty of Designated Courts to conduct trials efficiently and equitably.
obligations: Obligation for all States to cooperate in the repression of piracy on high seas (as per Convention).
Obligation for the Central Government to notify commencement dates and designate Courts.
Obligation for courts to follow the specific provisions for bail and trial proceedings outlined in the Act.

key_procedures: Notification by the Central Government to bring the Act into force.
Designation of Courts of Session as Designated Courts and their territorial jurisdiction.
Arrest of suspected pirates and seizure of ships/property by authorized personnel.
Forwarding of accused persons to Designated Courts or Magistrates for initial detention.
Trial of offenses by Designated Courts on a day-to-day basis where practicable.
Application for bail under strict conditions.
Extradition procedures for offenders.
Protection of actions taken in good faith by authorized personnel and government.
administration: The Central Government, in conjunction with State Governments, is responsible for the administration of the Act, including notifications, conferring powers, and designating courts. The Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Home Affairs would likely be involved.
important_notes: The Act is enacted to give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.
The presumption clause (Section 11) shifts the burden of proof to the accused under specific circumstances.
Special provisions for bail aim to prevent accused individuals from absconding or re-offending.
The Act aims to consolidate and strengthen India's legal framework against maritime piracy.

title: The Post Office Act, 2023
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to Post Office in India and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, enabling the evolution of the post office into a network for the delivery of citizen-centric services.
scope: Applies to the Post Office services in India. It covers the provision of postal services, postage stamps, addresses, and arrangements with foreign countries.

key_definitions.Director General: The Director General of Postal Services appointed by the Central Government, including any officer authorized by the Central Government to perform the duties of the Director General.
key_definitions.item: An indivisible article which the Post Office accepts for providing a service.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Post Office: The Department of Posts and includes every house, building, room, place or any other asset used by the Post Office for providing any service.
key_definitions.prescribe: Prescribe by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.postcode: A series of digits, letters or digital code or a combination of digits, letters or digital code used to identify a geographic area or location, and ease the process of sorting and delivery of items and for other purposes.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Director General', 'item', 'notification', 'Post Office', 'prescribe', 'regulations', and 'postcode'.

main_sections.section_title: Services to be provided by Post Office
main_sections.description: States that the Post Office shall provide services prescribed by the Central Government. The Director General may make regulations for activities and fix charges for these services. Services are subject to other laws.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusive privilege in respect of postage stamps
main_sections.description: Grants the Post Office the exclusive privilege of issuing postage stamps and allows the Director General to make regulations regarding their supply and sale.
Empowers the Central Government to prescribe standards for addressing, address identifiers, and the usage of postcodes.

main_sections.section_title: Power to give effect to arrangements with other countries
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to make rules to implement arrangements with foreign countries for postal services.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of sums due in respect of services provided by Post Office
main_sections.description: Establishes that persons availing Post Office services are liable to pay charges, and unpaid charges are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Official mark to be evidence of certain facts denoted
main_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to prescribe conditions for official marks on items to serve as prima facie evidence of denoted facts.

main_sections.section_title: Power to intercept, open or detain any item or deliver item to customs authority
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to empower officers to intercept, open, or detain items for reasons of state security, public order, etc., and to deliver items to customs authorities if they are suspected to contain dutiable or prohibited goods.
Exempts the Post Office and its officers from liability for loss, delay, or mis-delivery of services, except in cases of fraud or wilful misconduct by officers, or as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Delegation of power, other than rulemaking powers to Director General
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to authorize the Director General to exercise certain powers conferred upon the Central Government by the Act, excluding rulemaking powers.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Director General, with the prior approval of the Central Government, to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of rules and regulations in Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires all rules and regulations made under the Act to be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulment.
Authorizes the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, with a time limit.
Repeals the Indian Post Office Act, 1898, and provides savings for existing rules, notifications, and orders that are consistent with the new Act.

important_rules: The Post Office shall provide such services as prescribed by the Central Government.
The Director General can make regulations regarding postal activities and fix charges for services.
The Post Office has the exclusive privilege of issuing postage stamps.
Charges for Post Office services are payable by the user and are recoverable as land revenue if not paid.
The Central Government can empower officers to intercept, open, or detain mail for security or public order reasons.
The Post Office and its officers are generally exempted from liability for service issues, except in specific prescribed circumstances or due to fraud/wilful misconduct.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (through empowered officers, Director General) and Post Office.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules and regulations made by the Central Government and Director General, interception/detention of items, recovery of dues as land revenue, and parliamentary oversight of rules and regulations.

rights: Right to receive postal services as prescribed.
Right to use postage stamps issued by the Post Office.
Right to benefit from postal services subject to terms and conditions.
duties: Duty to pay charges for services availed from the Post Office.
Duty to comply with prescribed standards for addressing and postcode usage.
obligations: Obligation to pay for services rendered by the Post Office.
Obligation to adhere to regulations concerning postage stamps and postal stationery.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Upon notification by the Central Government.
Making Rules: Central Government makes rules by notification.
Making Regulations: Director General makes regulations with prior Central Government approval by notification.
Laying Rules/Regulations before Parliament: As soon as may be after they are made, for a total of thirty days.
Removal of Difficulties: Central Government may issue orders to remove difficulties, within two years of commencement.
administration: Department of Posts (under the Central Government)
important_notes: The Act aims to modernize postal services beyond traditional mail to include citizen-centric services.
All rules, notifications, and orders made under the repealed Indian Post Office Act, 1898, continue in force if consistent with this Act, until superseded.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to two years from the Act's commencement date.

title: THE TELECOMMUNICATIONS ACT, 2023
purpose: To amend and consolidate the law relating to development, expansion and operation of telecommunication services and telecommunication networks; assignment of spectrum; and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to any offence committed or contravention made outside India by any person, as provided in this Act.

key_definitions.appointed_day: Such date as the Central Government may, by notification appoint under sub-section (3) of section 1.
key_definitions.assignment: Permission for a radio station to use a radio frequency or radio frequency channel under specified conditions.
key_definitions.authorisation: A permission, by whatever name called, granted under this Act for providing telecommunication services, establishing, operating, maintaining or expanding telecommunication networks, or possessing radio equipment.
key_definitions.spectrum: The range of frequencies of Hertzian or radio waves.
key_definitions.telecommunication: Transmission, emission or reception of any messages, by wire, radio, optical or other electro-magnetic systems, whether or not such messages have been subjected to rearrangement, computation or other processes by any means in the course of their transmission, emission or reception.
key_definitions.telecommunication_network: A system or series of systems of telecommunication equipment or infrastructure, including terrestrial or satellite networks or submarine networks, or a combination of such networks, used or intended to be used for providing telecommunication services, but does not include such telecommunication equipment as notified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.user: A natural or legal person using or requesting a telecommunication service, but does not include person providing such telecommunication service or telecommunication network.

main_sections.description: This section specifies the short title of the Act as the Telecommunications Act, 2023, its territorial extent across India, and the provision for commencement through notification by the Central Government.

This section provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, crucial for understanding its provisions. Key definitions include 'appointed day', 'assignment', 'authorisation', 'spectrum', 'telecommunication', 'telecommunication network', 'telecommunication service', and 'user'.

This section outlines the requirement for any person intending to provide telecommunication services, establish or operate telecommunication networks, or possess radio equipment to obtain an authorisation from the Central Government. It also covers provisions for different terms and conditions, exemptions, and the continuation of existing licenses.

This section establishes the Central Government as the owner of spectrum and details the process for its assignment. It mandates assignment through auction, except for items listed in the First Schedule, which are assigned administratively. Provisions for amending the First Schedule and exemptions are also included.
The Central Government is empowered to re-farm or harmonise assigned frequency ranges to enable more efficient use of spectrum, subject to prescribed terms and conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Definition of terms used in this Chapter
main_sections.description: Defines terms specific to Chapter III concerning the right of way for telecommunication networks.

main_sections.section_title: Right of way for telecommunication network in public property
main_sections.description: Grants the right of way for telecommunication networks on public property.
Establishes the 'Digital Bharat Nidhi'.
Introduces the concept of a regulatory sandbox for innovation and technology development.
Outlines measures to protect users of telecommunication services.

main_sections.section_title: Dispute resolution mechanism to redress user grievances
main_sections.description: Establishes a mechanism for resolving user grievances.

main_sections.section_title: Definitions of terms used in this Chapter
main_sections.description: Defines terms specific to Chapter VIII concerning adjudication of certain contraventions.

main_sections.section_title: Breach of terms and conditions of authorisation or assignment
main_sections.description: Addresses contraventions related to breaches of terms and conditions of authorisation or assignment.
Deals with general contraventions of the Act.
Provides general provisions concerning offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for implementing the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of certain Acts and savings
main_sections.description: Provides for the repeal of certain existing Acts and savings, indicating the transition from previous legislation.

important_rules: Rule: Any person intending to provide telecommunication services, establish or operate telecommunication networks, or possess radio equipment must obtain an authorisation from the Central Government (Section 3(1)).
Rule: Spectrum assignment will primarily be through auction, except for specified entries in the First Schedule which will use an administrative process (Section 4(4)).
Rule: The Central Government can exempt certain uses of spectrum from assignment requirements (Section 4(6)).
Rule: Any telecommunication network must have a right of way, whether on public property or other property, under specified conditions (Sections 11 and 12).
Rule: Users have duties as outlined in the Act (Section 29).

penalties: Penalties for contraventions of the Act are detailed in Chapter VIII (Adjudication of Certain Contraventions) and Chapter IX (Offences). Specific penalties are not explicitly listed in the provided text but are implied through sections like 'Contraventions of Act' (Section 33) and 'General provisions relating to offences' (Section 42).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and designated authorities like the Adjudicating Officer and Designated Appeals Committee are involved in enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement mechanisms include adjudication of contraventions, appeals, power to search, and supply of information to authorised officers.

rights: Right of way for telecommunication networks on public and other properties (Sections 11 and 12).
Continuity of existing licenses and assignments under specified conditions (Sections 3(6) and 4(8), 4(9)).
Right to appeal decisions of the Adjudicating Officer and Designated Appeals Committee (Sections 39 and 40).
duties: Duty of users to comply with the Act and prescribed regulations (Section 29).
Authorised entities must identify users through verifiable biometric identification for certain services (Section 3(7)).
