obligations: Obligation to obtain authorisation for telecommunication activities (Section 3(1)).
Obligation to obtain spectrum assignment for using spectrum (Section 4(2)).
Obligation to comply with terms and conditions of authorisation and assignment.
Obligation to protect public safety and national security as mandated by the Act (Section 20 and 21).

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining authorisation for telecommunication services, networks, or radio equipment (Section 3).
Procedure for assignment of spectrum, including auction or administrative process (Section 4).
Procedure for dispute resolution for user grievances (Section 30).
Procedure for adjudication of contraventions by the Adjudicating Officer and Designated Appeals Committee (Sections 35-37).
Procedure for search and seizure by authorised officers (Section 43).
administration: The Central Government is primarily responsible for the administration of this Act, including making rules, issuing notifications, and assigning spectrum and authorisations.
important_notes: Note: Exemptions from authorization and spectrum assignment requirements may be granted by the Central Government in public interest (Sections 3(3) and 4(6)).

Note: Existing licenses and assignments granted under the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, and the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, shall continue under this Act unless otherwise notified (Sections 3(4), 3(6), 4(7)).
Note: The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred for matters under Chapter VIII (Adjudication of Certain Contraventions) (Section 41).
Note: Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 51).

title: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 2023
purpose: To provide for the immediate effect for a limited period of provisions in Bills relating to the imposition or increase of duties of customs or excise.
scope: Applies to provisions in Bills introduced in Parliament by the Central Government that provide for the imposition or increase of duties of customs or excise. The geographical scope is India, as it concerns laws enacted by the Parliament of India.

key_definitions.declared provision: A provision in a Bill in respect of which a declaration has been made under section 3, meaning it is expedient in the public interest for the provision to have immediate effect.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 2023.
Defines a 'declared provision' as a provision in a Bill for which a declaration has been made under section 3.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make declaration
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to include a declaration in a Bill that it is expedient in the public interest for any provision relating to the imposition or increase of customs or excise duty (with or without tariff classification change) to have immediate effect.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of declarations under this Act, and duration thereof
main_sections.description: Specifies that a declared provision has the force of law immediately upon the introduction of the Bill containing it. It also details circumstances under which this force of law ceases: when the provision becomes law as an enactment (with or without amendment), when Parliament directs its cessation via notification, or after seventy-five days from the Bill's introduction if it hasn't already ceased.

main_sections.section_title: Refunds to be made in certain cases
main_sections.description: Mandates refunds of duties collected that would not have been collected if the enacted provision had been the declared provision, in cases where the declared provision is amended before becoming law. Also requires refunds if the declared provision ceases to have force of law under section 4(2)(b) or (c).
Repeals The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931 (16 of 1931).

important_rules: Rule 1: A provision in a Bill related to the imposition or increase of customs or excise duty can be declared by the Central Government to have immediate effect if deemed expedient in the public interest.
Rule 2: A declared provision gains the force of law immediately when the Bill containing it is introduced.
Rule 3: The force of law of a declared provision ceases when it becomes an enactment, upon a directive from Parliament, or after 75 days of the Bill's introduction if not already enacted or ceased.

Rule 4: Refunds must be made if duties were collected under a declared provision that was later amended or if the provision ceases to have effect, and those duties would not have been collected under the final law.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Parliament
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legislative process of introducing Bills, making declarations, and issuing notifications. Enforcement of refunds is also stipulated.

rights: Taxpayers have a right to refunds if duties collected under a provisional measure would not have been legally due under the final enacted law.
duties: The Central Government has a duty to consider public interest when making a declaration.
The Central Government has a duty to ensure refunds are made where required.
obligations: The Central Government is obligated to introduce Bills with appropriate declarations if it deems them necessary for immediate effect of tax provisions.
The Government is obligated to manage the cessation of declared provisions and process any necessary refunds.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Introduction of a Bill by the Central Government containing provisions for imposing or increasing customs/excise duties. Inclusion of a declaration by the Central Government stating it is expedient in the public interest for these provisions to have immediate effect.

Procedure 2: Upon introduction of the Bill with a declared provision, that provision immediately has the force of law. The law will either be enacted, amended and enacted, or will cease to have effect after 75 days or by parliamentary directive.

Procedure 3: If the enacted provision differs from the declared provision and duties were collected based on the declared provision, refunds are to be processed. Similarly, if the declared provision ceases to have effect without becoming law, refunds are to be processed.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act allows for temporary application of tax laws before they are fully enacted, ensuring immediate revenue collection or implementation of tax policy changes.
The 75-day limit provides a safeguard against indefinite provisional collection of taxes.
The Act repeals the earlier Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931, indicating an update or replacement of this legal framework.

title: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024
purpose: To prevent unfair means in public examinations and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to public examinations conducted by designated public examination authorities. Covers actions by candidates, persons associated with service providers, institutions, and the service providers themselves. Scope is national, as enacted by Parliament.

key_definitions.candidate: A person granted permission to appear in a public examination, including a scribe acting on their behalf.
key_definitions.communication_device: Defined as per the Information Technology Act, 2000.
key_definitions.competent_authority: The Ministry or Department of the Central Government administratively concerned with the public examination authority.
key_definitions.institution: Any agency, organisation, body, association of persons, business entity, company, partnership, or single proprietorship firm, other than the public examination authority and its engaged service provider.
key_definitions.public_examination: Any examination conducted by a specified public examination authority or another authority notified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.public_examination_authority: An authority notified by the Central Government for conducting public examinations.
key_definitions.service_provider: Any agency, organisation, body, association of persons, business entity, company, partnership, or single proprietorship firm engaged by the public examination authority for conducting public examinations, including associates and subcontractors.

main_sections.description: Names the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'candidate', 'institution', 'public examination', and 'service provider'.

Defines various acts or omissions constituting unfair means in public examinations, including leakage of question papers, collusion, unauthorized access, tampering with answer sheets, and manipulation of security or seating arrangements.
Prohibits collusion or conspiracy to facilitate unfair means in public examinations.

Prohibits unauthorized entry into examination centers with the intent to disrupt examinations and outlines offenses related to leaking or possessing question papers and revealing confidential information by authorized personnel.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for offences under this Act
main_sections.description: Specifies the penalties for individuals, service providers, and their management for committing offenses under the Act, including imprisonment, fines, and debarment from future examinations.

Prescribes severe punishment, including imprisonment and substantial fines, for committing organized crime related to public examinations, and outlines forfeiture of property for involved institutions.

important_rules: Rule: No premises other than an authorized examination center shall be used for holding a public examination without written approval from the public examination authority, except in cases of force majeure.
Rule: Service providers or persons associated with them must immediately report incidents of unfair means or offenses to the police and the public examination authority.
Rule: If an offense is committed by a service provider with the consent or connivance of its director, manager, secretary, or other officer, such person is also liable for prosecution.
Rule: Any person involved in an organized crime related to public examinations shall face imprisonment and significant fines.
Rule: All offenses under this Act are cognizable, non-bailable, and non-compoundable.

penalties: For individuals resorting to unfair means: Imprisonment of not less than three years but up to five years, and fine up to ten lakh rupees. Additional imprisonment for default of fine.
For service providers: Fine up to one crore rupees, recovery of proportionate examination costs, and debarment from conducting public examinations for four years.

For Directors, Senior Management, or persons in charge of service provider firms involved with consent/connivance: Imprisonment of not less than three years but up to ten years, and fine of one crore rupees. Additional imprisonment for default of fine.
For organized crimes: Imprisonment of not less than five years but up to ten years, and fine not less than one crore rupees. Additional imprisonment for default of fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement by police authorities, guided by the empowered officers for investigation. The competent authority and public examination authority are involved in reporting and administration.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Offences are cognizable, allowing for immediate police action. Investigation is conducted by empowered officers. Penalties are imposed upon conviction, including imprisonment, fines, and debarment from future responsibilities.

rights: Right to a fair and unbiased public examination.
Protection of actions taken in good faith by public servants involved in the administration of the Act.
duties: Duty of service providers to report unfair means or offenses.
Duty of individuals involved in public examinations to not engage in unfair means or conspiracies.
Duty of authorized personnel not to leak or reveal confidential information related to examinations.
obligations: Obligation for individuals and institutions to adhere to the provisions of the Act.
Obligation for service providers to ensure authorized examination centers are used and to prevent unfair means.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement: The Central Government notifies the date of commencement in the Official Gazette.

Procedure for reporting offenses: Service providers must report unfair means or offenses to police and the public examination authority. If the service provider is involved, the public examination authority reports to the police.
Procedure for investigation: Officers empowered under the Act investigate offenses.
Procedure for rules making: The Central Government has the power to make rules for the implementation of the Act.
Procedure for removing difficulties: The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
administration: The Ministry or Department of the Central Government administratively concerned with the public examination authority (defined as 'competent authority').
important_notes: Note: The Act specifies that its provisions are in addition to other laws.
Note: Until the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is in force, the Indian Penal Code, 1860, will be applicable for certain provisions related to punishment.
Note: Any person claiming an offense was committed without their knowledge and that they exercised due diligence to prevent it may not be liable for punishment.
Note: The definition of 'company' includes companies as defined in the Companies Act, 2013, and limited liability partnerships as defined in the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.

title: The Boilers Act, 2025
purpose: To provide for the regulation of boilers, safety of life and property from the danger of explosions of steam-boilers, and for uniformity in registration and inspection during manufacture, erection, and use of boilers in the country.
scope: Applies to all boilers and boiler components, including those belonging to the Central and State Governments. Excludes locomotive boilers under railway control, boilers in steam-propelled vessels, boilers under Army, Navy, or Air Force control, and sterilizers/disinfectors with a capacity not exceeding one hundred litres.

key_definitions.accident: An explosion of a boiler or boiler components that weakens its strength, or an uncontrolled release of water or steam therefrom, liable to cause death, injury, or property damage.
key_definitions.boiler: A pressure vessel where steam is generated for external use by heat application, wholly or partly under pressure when steam is shut off. Excludes vessels with capacity less than twenty-five litres, pressure less than 1 kg/cm² design or working gauge pressure, or those heating water below 100°C.
key_definitions.boiler components: Steam piping, feed piping, economiser, superheater, mounting or other fitting, and any external or internal part of a boiler subject to pressure exceeding 1 kg/cm² gauge.
key_definitions.owner: Includes any person possessing or using a boiler as an agent of the owner, or any person using a boiler hired or obtained on loan from the owner.

main_sections.description: Defines the short title of the Act, its commencement date (variable by notification), and its application scope, including exclusions.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as accident, boiler, boiler components, Chief Inspector, etc.
Establishes the Central Boilers Board, outlines its composition, term of office, procedure, and powers.

main_sections.section_title: Chief Inspector, Deputy Chief Inspector and Inspector
main_sections.description: Details the appointment of Chief Inspectors, Deputy Chief Inspectors, and Inspectors by the State Government, their powers, duties, and qualifications.
Requires reporting of accidents involving boilers or boiler components.
Covers various offences related to boilers and their corresponding penalties, including recovery, prosecution, and adjudication.
Empowers the Central Government to grant exemptions from the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Boilers Board the power to make regulations for the Act's provisions.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and provisions for savings.

important_rules: No person shall manufacture or cause to be manufactured any boiler or boiler components unless they meet prescribed conditions and are subject to inspection during manufacture.
Boilers and boiler components must be inspected during erection, and conditions precedent for their repair must be met.
Use of unregistered or uncertified boilers is prohibited.
Owners must report accidents involving boilers or boiler components.
Welders working on boilers or boiler components must obtain a certificate from a competent authority.
Alterations and renewals of boilers, steam-pipes, or boiler components require adherence to specific conditions and may necessitate re-inspection and re-certification.

penalties: Minor penalties for certain offences.
Penalties for illegal use of boilers.
Punishment for specific offences.
Penalty for tampering with register marks.
Penalty for breach of rules or regulations.
Recovery of penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chief Inspector, Deputy Chief Inspectors, and Inspectors appointed by the State Government, under the general superintendence and control of the Chief Inspector.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection during manufacture, erection, and use; certification and registration; reporting of accidents; and prosecution for offences and breaches of rules and regulations. Penalties are imposed and recovered as prescribed.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of Inspectors, Chief Inspectors, and the Central Government.
Right to be heard before refusal of a welder's certificate.
Right to obtain a welder's certificate upon fulfilling specified conditions.
duties: Duty of the owner to allow inspection of boilers.
Duty of the owner to report accidents.
Duty of owners to produce certificates and provisional orders when required.
Duty of owners regarding the proper maintenance and safe working of boilers.
Duty of persons undertaking welding work to obtain a welder's certificate.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act, rules, and regulations.
Obligation for manufacturers to adhere to conditions precedent for manufacture.
Obligation for owners to ensure boilers are registered and certified before use.
Obligation to obtain necessary certificates for boilers, boiler components, and welding work.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a welder's certificate, including examination and grant by a competent authority.
Procedure for inspection of boilers during manufacture and erection.
Procedure for registration and renewal of boiler certificates.
Procedure for reporting and investigating accidents.
Procedure for appeals against decisions made under the Act.
Procedure for prosecution and adjudication of offences and penalties.
administration: The Central Government has overall administrative control, including power to make rules and give directions. State Governments appoint Inspectors and manage boilers within their territories. The Central Boilers Board is constituted to regulate design, manufacture, erection, and use of boilers.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for the commencement of different provisions of the Act.
The Central Government can exempt certain categories of boilers or boiler components from the purview of the Act.
The Central Boilers Board has the power to make regulations, and the Central and State Governments have the power to make rules.

title: The Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025
purpose: To confer upon the Central Government certain powers to provide for the requirement of passports or other travel documents for persons entering and exiting India, and for regulating matters related to foreigners, including visa requirements and registration, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to all persons entering or exiting India, and all foreigners present in India. It covers immigration functions, the regulation of foreigners, and related matters within the territory of India.

key_definitions.accommodation: A temporary or permanent premises of any nature where a foreigner is accommodated.
key_definitions.carrier: A person or entity engaged in the business of transporting passengers or cargo by air, water, or land.
key_definitions.foreigner: A person who is not a citizen of India.
key_definitions.immigration_function: Functions relating to visa issuance, regulation of entry, transit, stay, movement within, and exit from India.
key_definitions.passport: A passport issued or deemed to have been issued under the provisions of the Passport Act, 1967, or a passport issued by a foreign government subject to prescribed conditions.
key_definitions.visa: An authorization permitting a foreigner to enter, transit through, stay in, or exit the territory of India.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025' and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including accommodation, carrier, foreigner, immigration function, passport, visa, and others.

main_sections.section_title: Requirement of passport or other travel document and visa
main_sections.description: Mandates that persons entering or exiting India must possess a valid passport or travel document, and foreigners must also have a valid visa. It also outlines grounds for inadmissibility and allows for the seizure of invalid or fraudulent documents.
Provides for the constitution of a Bureau of Immigration to perform immigration functions, with its supervision and control vested in the Central Government.
Requires foreigners to register with the Registration Officer upon arrival in India under prescribed conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Power to issue orders, directions or instructions
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government broad powers to issue orders, directions, or instructions to regulate the entry, departure, presence, and conduct of foreigners in India.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of keeper of accommodation and others to furnish particulars
main_sections.description: Imposes a duty on keepers of accommodation to report particulars of foreigners housed therein, and on foreigners to provide necessary information.
Outlines the obligations of carriers concerning the documentation of passengers.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of carrier to pay penalty
main_sections.description: Establishes penalties for carriers in certain situations.

main_sections.section_title: Contravention or attempts to contravene provisions of Act
main_sections.description: Deals with offenses related to contravening the provisions of the Act or attempting to do so.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for entry without valid passport or other travel document
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for entering India without the required valid travel documents.
Grants power to arrest individuals in relation to offenses under the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Addresses the repeal of any previous laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Rule: No person shall enter or attempt to enter India without a valid passport or travel document, and foreigners require a valid visa.
Rule: Foreigners must possess valid passports, travel documents, and visas while in India, unless exempted.
Rule: Foreigners may be prohibited from entering or staying in India if they pose a threat to national security, sovereignty, integrity, relations with foreign states, or public health.
Rule: Foreigners arriving in India are required to register with the concerned Registration Officer.
Rule: Keepers of accommodation must submit particulars of foreigners accommodated therein to the Registration Officer.
Rule: Carriers have obligations regarding the documentation of passengers they transport.
Rule: Contravention of the Act's provisions or attempts to do so constitute offenses.

penalties: Penalty for entry without a valid passport or other travel document.
Penalty for using or supplying forged or fraudulently obtained passports, travel documents, or visas.
Penalty for contraventions of other provisions of the Act.
Penalty for abetment of offenses under the Act.
Liability of carriers to pay penalties for specific infringements.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Immigration Officers, Bureau of Immigration, Registration Officers, and other authorised authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through examination of documents, requiring information, seizure of documents, issuing orders/directions/instructions, registration of foreigners, arrest, and imposition of penalties.

rights: Right to enter India if possessing valid travel documents and visa (unless inadmissible).
duties: Duty of persons to possess valid passports/travel documents and visas when entering/exiting India.
Duty of foreigners to possess valid passports/travel documents and visas while in India.
Duty of foreigners to register upon arrival.
Duty of keepers of accommodation to furnish particulars of foreigners.
Duty of foreigners to furnish particulars to keepers of accommodation.
obligations: Obligation of carriers to ensure passengers have necessary documentation.
Obligation of foreigners to comply with orders, directions, or instructions issued by the Central Government regarding their presence and activities in India.
Obligation of foreigners to meet the cost of their removal if required not to remain in India.

key_procedures: Procedure: Entry into India requires possession of a valid passport or travel document and, for foreigners, a valid visa. Immigration Officers may examine these documents and require information.
Procedure: Exit from India requires possession of a valid passport or travel document and, for foreigners, a valid visa.
Procedure: Foreigners arriving in India must register with the Registration Officer.
Procedure: Keepers of accommodation must submit foreigner particulars to the Registration Officer.
Procedure: The Central Government may issue orders and directions to regulate various aspects of a foreigner's stay in India.
administration: Central Government, with the Bureau of Immigration playing a key role.
important_notes: Exceptions to passport/visa requirements can be made under section 33 or through intergovernmental agreements.
Decisions of the Immigration Officer regarding entry/exit are generally final and binding.
The Central Government has the power to exempt certain cases from the provisions of the Act.
The Act does not bar the application of other laws.

title: The Mussalman Wakf (Repeal) Act, 2025
purpose: To repeal the Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923, to ensure uniformity, transparency, and accountability in the administration and management of waqf properties through the Waqf Act, 1995, and to eliminate inconsistencies and ambiguities arising from the existence of the redundant Act.
scope: This Act applies to India. It specifically repeals the Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Mussalman Wakf (Repeal) Act, 2025, and that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

This section repeals the Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923. It clarifies that the repeal will not affect the previous operation of the repealed Act, anything duly done or suffered thereunder, or any obligation, liability, legal proceeding, or remedy accrued or incurred under the repealed Act. Such proceedings or remedies can be continued or enforced as if this Act had not been passed.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923 (Act 42 of 1923) is hereby repealed.
Rule 2: The repeal of the Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923 does not invalidate past operations, actions, obligations, liabilities, or legal proceedings conducted under the repealed Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for commencement notification)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Official Gazette to bring the Act into force.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint a date for the commencement of this Act.
administration: Central Government (for commencement notification)
important_notes: The Act became effective on the 9th day of April, 2025, vide notification No. S.O. 1676 (E), dated 9th day of April, 2025.
The repealed Act, Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923, was a colonial-era legislation found to be outdated and inadequate for modern waqf property management.

title: The Protection of Interests in Aircraft Objects Act, 2025
purpose: To provide for the protection of interests in aircraft objects and to implement the Convention on International Interests in Mobile Equipment and the Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in Mobile Equipment on Matters Specific to Aircraft Equipment signed at Cape Town on 16th November, 2001, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to aircraft objects within India. The Convention and Protocol have the force of law in India in respect of aircraft objects, subject to declarations made by India. Remedies on insolvency apply where the debtor is an Indian entity or domiciled in India, the international interest is registered, and the parties have not excluded its application.

key_definitions.agreement: Means a security agreement, a title reservation agreement, or a leasing agreement.
key_definitions.aircraft: Has the meaning assigned to it in Article I (2)(a) of the Protocol.
key_definitions.aircraft objects: Has the meaning assigned to it in Article I (2)(c) of the Protocol.
key_definitions.Convention: The Convention on International Interests in Mobile Equipment signed at Cape Town on 16th November, 2001.
key_definitions.creditor: Has the meaning assigned to it in Article 1(i) of the Convention.
key_definitions.debtor: Has the meaning assigned to it in Article 1(j) of the Convention.
key_definitions.Protocol: The Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in Mobile Equipment on Matters specific to Aircraft Equipment signed at Cape Town on 16th November, 2001.
key_definitions.registry authority: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation constituted under section 3 of the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024.

main_sections.description: Names the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'agreement', 'aircraft', 'aircraft objects', 'Convention', 'creditor', 'debtor', 'Protocol', and 'registry authority'. It also states that undefined terms used in the Act but defined in the Convention or Protocol shall have their meanings from those instruments.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Convention and Protocol in India
main_sections.description: States that the Convention and Protocol shall have the force of law in India regarding aircraft objects, in accordance with India's declarations.

main_sections.section_title: Power of registry authority to issue directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the registry authority to issue directions for the implementation of the Convention and Protocol provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of debtor and creditor to an agreement
main_sections.description: Specifies that debtors must maintain and submit records of dues to the registry authority, and creditors must declare default by notifying the registry authority to exercise remedies under the Convention or Protocol.

Makes provisions of Article XI of the Protocol applicable for insolvency remedies under Indian law, subject to specific conditions regarding the debtor's location, registration of the international interest, and absence of exclusion by agreement.
States that Article XIII of the Protocol applies to de-registration and export requests, subject to the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024.
Designates the High Court with territorial jurisdiction as the relevant court for the purposes of Article 53 of the Convention.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of Act to have overriding effect
main_sections.description: Establishes that the Act's provisions prevail over any inconsistent existing laws. It also clarifies that the Act's provisions are in addition to other laws and do not affect the rights of the Central Government or public service providers to arrest or detain aircraft objects for amounts due.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions and implementing the Convention/Protocol, with specific mention of rules for issuing directions and for reporting obligations of debtors and creditors. Rules must be laid before Parliament and are subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government in respect of declarations
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make, amend, or withdraw declarations under the Convention or Protocol, and to amend the Second Schedule accordingly.

Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act and are made within three years of commencement. Orders must be laid before Parliament.

important_rules: Debtors must maintain and submit records of dues related to aircraft object ownership or use to the registry authority.
Creditors must notify the registry authority of a default to exercise remedies under the Convention or Protocol.
Article XI of the Protocol regarding remedies on insolvency applies under specified conditions.
Article XIII of the Protocol regarding de-registration and export request authorisation applies.
The Act's provisions have overriding effect in case of inconsistency with other laws.
The Central Government may make rules to implement the Act and the Convention/Protocol, which are subject to parliamentary review.
The Central Government can make, amend, or withdraw declarations under the Convention or Protocol.
The Central Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act within a specified period.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registry authority (Directorate General of Civil Aviation) and High Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directions issued by the registry authority, application of Convention and Protocol provisions having the force of law, and jurisdiction of High Courts for legal remedies. Specific enforcement mechanisms for insolvency and de-registration/export are detailed.

rights: Right to exercise remedies on insolvency under specified conditions.
Right to de-register and request export authorisation subject to applicable laws.
Right for the Central Government or public service providers to arrest or detain aircraft objects for outstanding payments.
duties: Duty of the debtor to maintain and submit records of dues.
Duty of the creditor to declare default to the registry authority.
obligations: Obligations arising from agreements (security, title reservation, leasing).
Obligation to comply with directions from the registry authority.
Obligation to comply with rules made by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for declaring default by a creditor to the registry authority.
Procedure for remedies on insolvency, as per Article XI of the Protocol.
Procedure for de-registration and export request authorisation, as per Article XIII of the Protocol.
Procedure for making, amending, or withdrawing declarations by the Central Government.
Procedure for Central Government to make rules, including prior publication and parliamentary laying.
administration: Central Government (through rule-making power and power to make declarations and remove difficulties) and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (as the registry authority).
important_notes: The Act implements international conventions (Cape Town Convention and its Aircraft Protocol).
The Act has overriding effect over other laws in case of inconsistency.
Specific rights of the Central Government and public service providers to detain aircraft objects are preserved.
The power to remove difficulties is time-bound (three years from commencement).

title: The Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025
purpose: To provide for the responsibilities, liabilities, rights and immunities attached to carriers with respect to the carriage of goods by sea and for matters connected therewith or related thereto, by giving the force of law to the Hague-Visby Rules as amended.
scope: The Act applies to the carriage of goods by sea in ships carrying goods from any port in India to any other port, whether in or outside India. The 'applicable rules' are laid down in the Schedule to the Act.

key_definitions.applicable rules: The applicable rules provided in the Schedule to this Act.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Schedule: The Schedule annexed to this Act, containing the applicable rules relating to bills of lading.
key_definitions.carriage of goods: Covers the period from the time when the goods are loaded on to the time when they are discharged from the ship.
key_definitions.carrier: Includes the owner or the charterer who enters into a contract of carriage with a shipper.
key_definitions.contract of carriage: Applies only to contracts of carriage covered by a bill of lading or any similar document of title, in so far as such document relates to the carriage of goods by sea.
key_definitions.goods: Includes any property including live animals as well as containers, pallets or similar articles of transport or packaging supplied by the consignor, irrespective of whether such property is to be or is carried on or under deck.
key_definitions.ship: Means any vessel used for the carriage of goods by sea.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025 and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'applicable rules', 'notification', and 'Schedule'.

States that the applicable rules in the Schedule have effect in relation to the carriage of goods by sea from any port in India to any other port, in or outside India, subject to the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: No implied absolute undertaking in contracts to which applicable rules apply.
main_sections.description: Prohibits an implied absolute undertaking by the carrier to provide a seaworthy ship in contracts governed by the applicable rules.

main_sections.section_title: Statement as to application of Schedule to be included in bills of lading.
main_sections.description: Requires every bill of lading or similar document of title issued in India, relating to a contract covered by the applicable rules, to include an express statement that it is subject to the applicable rules.

main_sections.section_title: Modification of Article VI of applicable rules in relation to goods carried in sailing ships and by specified routes.
main_sections.description: Modifies Article VI of the applicable rules for the carriage of goods by sea in sailing ships and for specified routes to Sri Lanka, allowing for goods of any class and omitting a specific proviso.

main_sections.section_title: Modification of paragraphs 4 and 5 of Article III in relation to bulk cargoes.
main_sections.description: Modifies the effect of bill of lading as prima facie evidence of receipt for bulk cargo weights ascertained or accepted by a third party, when such fact is stated in the bill of lading.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue necessary directions for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to amend Schedule.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to amend the Schedule by notification, with the amendment having the force of law.
Mandates that every notification issued under the Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modification or annulment.
Authorizes the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, within two years of its commencement. Such orders must be laid before Parliament.

Repeals the Indian Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925, but includes savings provisions to ensure continuity of previous operations, rights, liabilities, and proceedings. It also clarifies the effect of repeal under the General Clauses Act and preserves the operation of certain provisions of the Merchant Shipping Act.

important_rules: Rule derived from Article III(1): The carrier must exercise due diligence to make the ship seaworthy, properly man, equip, supply it, and ensure holds and other cargo spaces are fit and safe before and at the beginning of the voyage.
Rule derived from Article III(2): The carrier must properly and carefully load, handle, stow, carry, keep, care for, and discharge the goods.

Rule derived from Article III(3) & (4): Upon demand, the carrier must issue a bill of lading showing details of the goods, and this bill of lading serves as prima facie evidence of receipt, unless transferred to a good faith third party.
Rule derived from Article III(5): The shipper guarantees the accuracy of particulars furnished for the bill of lading and must indemnify the carrier against losses due to inaccuracies.
Rule derived from Article III(6)(c): Suit for loss or damage must be brought within one year after delivery or the date goods should have been delivered, with possible extensions.

Rule derived from Article IV: The carrier is not liable for certain losses or damages, including those arising from unseaworthiness caused by lack of due diligence before the voyage, or from specific causes listed in Article IV.
Rule derived from Article V: Any clause relieving the carrier from liability or lessening their responsibility otherwise than as provided in the applicable rules is null and void.
Rule derived from Article VI: Modifications to the contract of carriage are permitted for certain classes of goods or under special circumstances, but not for ordinary commercial shipments.

penalties: While the document explicitly mentions indemnification by the shipper to the carrier for inaccurate particulars (Article III(5)), it does not detail specific monetary penalties or fines for violations of the Act itself. Enforcement would likely involve civil remedies and adherence to contractual obligations.
Article III(6)(c) sets a time limit for bringing suits for loss or damage (1 year, with possible extension), which acts as a form of procedural enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government has powers to issue directions (Section 8) and amend the Schedule (Section 9). Enforcement of liabilities and rights would primarily be through civil legal proceedings by aggrieved parties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal recourse by parties affected by breaches of the Act's provisions and the 'applicable rules'. The Central Government can issue directions and amend the Schedule to facilitate implementation. Court proceedings are implied for resolving disputes and enforcing liabilities.

rights: Carrier's right to be indemnified by the shipper for inaccuracies in particulars furnished for the bill of lading (Article III(5)).
Carrier's right to be discharged from liability if suit is not brought within one year (Article III(6)(c)).
Carrier's immunities as set forth in Article IV (e.g., not liable for loss or damage arising from unseaworthiness due to lack of due diligence, acts of God, etc.).
Shipper's right to demand a bill of lading showing specified particulars (Article III(3)).
Right to extend the one-year period for bringing suit by agreement (Article III(6)(c)).
duties: Carrier's duty to exercise due diligence to make the ship seaworthy, properly man, equip, and supply it, and make cargo spaces fit and safe (Article III(1)).
Carrier's duty to properly and carefully load, handle, stow, carry, keep, care for, and discharge the goods (Article III(2)).
Carrier's duty to issue a bill of lading on demand showing specified particulars (Article III(3)).
Shipper's duty to guarantee accuracy of particulars furnished for the bill of lading (Article III(5)).
obligations: Obligation for bills of lading to contain an express statement that they are subject to the applicable rules (Section 5).
Obligation for the carrier to provide a seaworthy ship before and at the beginning of the voyage (Article III(1)).
Obligation for the carrier to properly handle the goods during carriage (Article III(2)).
Obligation for the shipper to indemnify the carrier for inaccuracies in provided particulars (Article III(5)).
Obligation to bring suit within one year for loss or damage (Article III(6)(c)).

key_procedures: Issuance of a bill of lading: Upon demand by the shipper, the carrier or its agent must issue a bill of lading showing leading marks, number/quantity/weight of packages, and apparent order/condition of goods, provided the carrier has no reasonable grounds for suspecting inaccuracies or means to check them.

Notification of loss or damage: Written notice of loss or damage must be given to the carrier or agent at the port of discharge before or at the time of removal of goods, or within three days if the loss is not apparent. Failure to do so makes removal prima facie evidence of delivery as per the bill of lading.

Bringing suit for loss or damage: Suit must be brought within one year after delivery or the date goods should have been delivered, though this period can be extended by agreement, and courts may allow a further three-month extension.
Procedure for amending the Schedule: The Central Government can amend the Schedule by notification, which takes effect as if enacted in the Act. Such notifications must be laid before Parliament.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for issuing notifications, directions, and potentially removing difficulties related to the Act.
important_notes: The Act incorporates and gives the force of law to the Hague-Visby Rules (as amended by Protocols of 1968 and 1979) concerning bills of lading, subject to modifications.
Section 4 explicitly states there is no implied absolute undertaking by the carrier to provide a seaworthy ship.

Section 12(3) clarifies that this Act does not affect the operation of Section 331 and Part XA of the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, or other enactments limiting the liability of sea-going vessel owners.

title: THE SOCIETIES REGISTRATION ACT, 1860
purpose: To provide for the registration of literary, scientific, and charitable societies, and to improve their legal condition for the promotion of literature, science, the fine arts, diffusion of useful knowledge, diffusion of political education, or for charitable purposes.
scope: Applies to societies formed for literary, scientific, and charitable purposes across India, with specific modifications and extensions to various Union Territories and States. It also covers societies formed before its enactment. The Act applies to the formation, registration, management, dissolution, and legal standing of such societies.

key_definitions.society: An association formed by memorandum of association and registration under this Act for literary, scientific, or charitable purposes, or for the diffusion of useful knowledge or political education.
key_definitions.member: Any person who having been admitted a member of the society, or shall have agreed to become a member; and has signed the register of the society. Disqualified members are those who have not paid their subscription or are indebted to the society.
key_definitions.governing body: The members of the society who are from time to time duly elected or appointed to manage the affairs of the society, and shall include all persons so elected or appointed, and all persons who, at the date of commencement of this Act, were members of the said governing body.

main_sections.section_title: Societies formed by memorandum of association and registration.
main_sections.description: Details how societies can be formed by a memorandum of association and subsequent registration.
Outlines the contents and requirements of the memorandum of association for a society.
Describes the process of registering a society and the associated fees.

main_sections.section_title: Annual list of managing body to be filed.
main_sections.description: Requires societies to file an annual list of their managing body with the Registrar.
Explains how the property of a society is vested in its members.
Governs the procedures for filing lawsuits by and against registered societies.

main_sections.section_title: Societies enabled to alter, extend or abridge their purposes.
main_sections.description: Allows societies to modify their stated purposes under certain conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Provision for dissolution of societies and adjustment of their affairs.
main_sections.description: Provides a framework for the dissolution of societies and the settlement of their affairs.
Specifies the types of societies to which the Act is applicable.

important_rules: Societies must be formed by a memorandum of association and registered to gain legal standing.
The memorandum of association must contain specific details about the society's name, objectives, and members.
An annual list of the managing body must be filed with the Registrar.
Property of the society vests in the governing body appointed under the Act.
Societies can alter their purposes, but this requires adherence to specified procedures.
Dissolution of a society must follow the procedures laid out in the Act, ensuring proper adjustment of affairs.

penalties: Recovery of penalty accruing under bye-law.
Members guilty of offences punishable as strangers.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Societies (and in some cases, the State Government or Administration of the Union Territory).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, recovery of penalties, and by the Registrar's power to register, refuse registration, or renew certificates of registration.

rights: Societies have the right to sue and be sued.
Members have the right to have their costs recovered if they are successful defendants in a suit.
Societies have the right to alter, extend, or abridge their purposes.
Members have the right to receive back their own property upon dissolution, provided it was not given without expectation of return.
duties: Societies have a duty to file an annual list of their managing body.
Societies have a duty to comply with the provisions of their memorandum of association and the Act.
Members have a duty to pay their subscriptions and discharge debts to the society.
Upon dissolution, members have a duty not to receive profit from the society's assets.
obligations: Obligation to register the society.
Obligation to maintain and file records as required by the Act.
Obligation to adhere to the objects stated in the memorandum of association.
Obligation to follow dissolution procedures.

key_procedures: Procedure for forming and registering a society: involves creating a memorandum of association, filing it with the Registrar, and paying the prescribed fee.
Procedure for filing the annual list of the managing body: submission of a list of elected or appointed members of the governing body to the Registrar.
Procedure for dissolution of a society: requires following specific steps for winding up affairs and adjusting assets and liabilities.
Procedure for altering a society's purposes: involves passing a special resolution and registering the alteration with the Registrar.
administration: The Registrar of Societies (and in specific territories, Additional Registrars under the control of the Registrar). The State Government or Administration of the Union Territory has oversight and decision-making powers in certain matters.
important_notes: The Act is based on the Literary and Scientific Institutions Act, 1854.
Various State Governments and Union Territories have enacted amendments and extensions to this Act, introducing specific rules and fees.
The Act does not apply to Joint-stock Companies.
Societies formed before this Act came into force were required to file their memorandum and other documents with the Registrar of Joint-stock Companies.

title: The Prisons Act, 1894
purpose: To amend the law relating to prisons in India and to provide rules for the regulation of such prisons.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. It specifically excludes civil jails in the State of Bombay (as it existed immediately before the 1st November, 1956) outside the city of Bombay, which continue to be administered under provisions of the Bombay Civil Jails Act, 1874. The Act applies to all prisoners detained in prisons under the general or special orders of a State Government.

key_definitions.prison: Any jail or place used permanently or temporarily under the general or special orders of a State Government for the detention of prisoners, including all lands and buildings appurtenant thereto. It excludes police custody places, places appointed under Section 541 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1882, and subsidiary jails declared by the State Government.
key_definitions.criminal prisoner: Any prisoner duly committed to custody under the writ, warrant or order of any Court or authority exercising criminal jurisdiction, or by order of a Court-martial.
key_definitions.convicted criminal prisoner: Any criminal prisoner under sentence of a Court or Court-martial, and includes a person detained under Chapter VIII of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1882, or under the Prisoners Act, 1871.
key_definitions.civil prisoner: Any prisoner who is not a criminal prisoner.
key_definitions.remission system: The rules for the time being in force regulating the award of marks to, and the consequent shortening of sentences of, prisoners in jail.
key_definitions.history-ticket: The ticket exhibiting such information as is required in respect of each prisoner by this Act or the rules thereunder.
key_definitions.Medical Subordinate: An Assistant Surgeon, Apothecary or qualified Hospital Assistant.
key_definitions.prohibited article: An article the introduction or removal of which into or out of a prison is prohibited by any rule under this Act.

main_sections.description: This section states the title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except former Part B States), and its commencement date (July 1, 1894). It also contains a special provision regarding civil jails in the State of Bombay.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'prison', 'criminal prisoner', 'convicted criminal prisoner', 'civil prisoner', 'remission system', 'history-ticket', 'Inspector General', 'Medical Subordinate', and 'prohibited article'.
The State Government is mandated to provide accommodation for prisoners in prisons constructed and regulated to comply with the Act's requisitions regarding prisoner separation.

An Inspector General is to be appointed for each State Government's territories to exercise general control and superintendence of all prisons within those territories, subject to the State Government's orders.

For every prison, there shall be a Superintendent, a Medical Officer, a Medical Subordinate, a Jailer, and other necessary officers as determined by the State Government. A proviso allows the State Government of Bombay to designate the Superintendent to also hold the office of Jailer in specified prisons.

main_sections.section_title: Control and duties of officers of prisons
main_sections.description: All prison officers must obey the Superintendent's directions. Officers subordinate to the Jailer shall perform duties assigned by the Jailer with the Superintendent's sanction or as prescribed by rules.

main_sections.section_title: Officers not to have business dealings with prisoners
main_sections.description: No prison officer or anyone acting on their behalf can sell or let any article to a prisoner, or have any financial or business dealings, directly or indirectly, with a prisoner.

main_sections.section_title: Officers not to be interested in prison-contracts
main_sections.description: No prison officer, nor anyone acting on their behalf, can have any interest in contracts for prison supplies or benefit from the sale or purchase of articles on behalf of the prison or belonging to a prisoner.

The Superintendent manages the prison in all matters of discipline, labor, expenditure, punishment, and control, subject to the Inspector General's orders. Superintendents of prisons other than central prisons or those in presidency towns must obey orders from the District Magistrate (unless inconsistent with the Act or rules) and report these to the Inspector General.

main_sections.section_title: Records to be kept by Superintendent
main_sections.description: The Superintendent is responsible for maintaining records, including a register (details to be specified by the Act or rules).

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for introduction or removal of prohibited articles into or from prison and communication with prisoners
main_sections.description: This section outlines penalties for prohibited actions related to prisons, such as introducing prohibited articles, removing them, or communicating with prisoners.
This section defines what constitutes an offense within a prison.
This section grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: All prison officers must obey the directions of the Superintendent (Section 8).
Officers subordinate to the Jailer must perform duties assigned by the Jailer with the Superintendent's sanction or as per rules (Section 8).
Prison officers are prohibited from having business dealings with prisoners (Section 9).
Prison officers are prohibited from having any interest in prison contracts or benefiting from them (Section 10).
The Superintendent manages the prison in all aspects of discipline, labor, expenditure, punishment, and control (Section 11).
State Governments must provide adequate accommodation for prisoners, ensuring separation as required by the Act (Section 4).
State Governments must appoint an Inspector General for the superintendence of prisons (Section 5).
Prohibited articles cannot be introduced into or removed from a prison, and communication with prisoners is regulated (Section 42).

penalties: Penalty for introduction or removal of prohibited articles into or from prison and communication with prisoners (Section 42).
Penalties for prison-offences (Section 46).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Inspector General, Superintendent, Jailer, and other prison officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the disciplinary and punitive measures outlined in the Act, including punishments for prison-offences and penalties for violations of rules regarding prohibited articles and communication.

rights: Prisoners have rights related to their accommodation, food, clothing, and bedding as prescribed by the Act and rules (Chapter VI, VII, VIII).
duties: All prison officers have duties to obey superiors and perform assigned tasks (Chapter III).
The Superintendent has duties related to prison management, record-keeping, and discipline (Chapter III).
The Medical Officer has duties related to prisoner health and reporting (Chapter III).
The Jailer has responsibilities for the custody and management of prisoners (Chapter III).
obligations: State Governments have the obligation to provide and regulate prisons and their accommodation (Section 4).
Prisoners are subject to the discipline and regulations of the prison as per the Act and rules.

key_procedures: Admission, removal, and discharge of prisoners (Chapter IV).
Discipline of prisoners, including separation, association, segregation, and solitary confinement (Chapter V).
Management of prisoner health, including sick prisoners and hospital care (Chapter VIII).
Procedures for dealing with prison-offences and their punishment (Chapter XI).
Procedures for handling specific situations like confinement in irons (Chapter XII).
administration: State Government, with the oversight of the Inspector General of Prisons.
important_notes: The Act underwent amendments and extensions in various States and Union Territories after its enactment.
Specific provisions for the Bombay State's civil jails are excluded from the general application of the Act.

title: THE CHARITABLE AND RELIGIOUS TRUSTS ACT, 1920
purpose: To provide more effectual control over the administration of Charitable and Religious Trusts, facilitate obtaining information regarding trusts created for public purposes of a charitable or religious nature, enable trustees to obtain directions of a Court on certain matters, and make special provision for expenditure in certain suits against trustees.
scope: Applies to charitable and religious trusts for public purposes. It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, with provisions for states to exclude specific areas or trusts. The Act does not apply to trusts covered by the Wakf Act, 1954, or to wakf property in Bengal if inconsistent with the Bengal Wakf Act, 1934. Its application has been extended to various Union Territories and certain districts. The 'Court' is defined as the Court of the District Judge or any other empowered court, including the High Court in its ordinary original civil jurisdiction.

key_definitions.the_Court: The Court of the District Judge or any other Court empowered in that behalf by the State Government, and includes the High Court in the exercise of its ordinary original civil jurisdiction.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its territorial extent, with provisions for exclusion by state governments.
Defines 'the Court' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to apply to the Court in respect of trusts of a charitable or religious nature
main_sections.description: Allows any person interested in a charitable or religious trust to apply to the Court for directions regarding the trust's nature, objects, management, application of subject-matter, and income, or for the examination and audit of trust accounts (up to three years prior).
Outlines the requirements for a petition, including the petitioner's interest and the sought particulars/audit, and mandates signing and verification as per the Code of Civil Procedure.

Details the Court's procedure upon receiving a petition, including evidence, inquiry, fixing hearing dates, serving notice, hearing parties, allowing written statements, staying proceedings if a suit is instituted to deny the trust's existence or applicability, deciding the question if no suit is filed, and making orders or dismissing the petition. It also clarifies that the Court shall not try questions of title between the petitioner and adverse claimants.

main_sections.section_title: Failure of trustee to comply with order under section 5
main_sections.description: States that a trustee's failure to comply with an order under section 5, without reasonable excuse, constitutes a breach of trust grounds for a suit under section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure, without requiring prior Advocate General consent.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of trustee to apply for directions
main_sections.description: Empowers trustees of charitable or religious trusts to petition the Court for opinion, advice, or direction on matters affecting the trust's management or administration, provided the question is not considered improper for summary disposal. The Court may give advice forthwith or fix a hearing date and shall afford an opportunity to be heard. Trustees acting in good faith on Court's advice are deemed to have discharged their duty.

main_sections.section_title: Costs of petition under this Act
main_sections.description: Grants the Court discretion over costs, charges, and expenses related to petitions, allowing them to be met from trust property/income or borne by persons as deemed fit, with a proviso for those not notified or heard.

Specifies circumstances under which petitions will not be entertained: pending suits under section 92 of the CPC, trust property vested in specific authorities (Treasurer of Charitable Endowments, Administrator-General, Official Trustee, or registered society), or if a scheme for administration is already settled or approved.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Courts as to costs in certain suits against trustees of charitable and religious trusts
main_sections.description: Allows Courts in suits under the Religious Endowments Act, 1863, or section 92 of the CPC to direct defendants (trustees) to furnish security or deposit funds for the plaintiff's expenditure in such suits, if necessary in the public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure to apply
main_sections.description: States that provisions of the CPC related to affidavit proof, enforcing attendance and examination on oath, enforcing production of documents, issuing commissions, service of summonses (for notices), and execution of decrees (for orders) apply to proceedings under this Act.
Prohibits appeals from any order passed or any opinion, advice, or direction given under this Act.

important_rules: Any person interested in a charitable or religious trust can petition the Court for particulars of the trust's nature, objects, management, and finances, or for an audit of accounts up to three years prior (Section 3).
Petitions must be in writing, signed, and verified as per the Code of Civil Procedure (Section 4).

The Court will hear petitions after inquiry and notice to trustees. If a dispute arises regarding the trust's existence or applicability, and a suit is filed within three months, proceedings will be stayed until the suit is decided (Section 5).
Trustees can petition the Court for advice or directions on trust administration, and acting in good faith on such advice will discharge their responsibility (Section 7).
The Court has discretion over costs of petitions, which can be borne by trust property or other persons (Section 8).
The Act does not apply if a relevant suit is pending, trust property is vested in certain official custodians, or a scheme is already in place (Section 9).
Courts can order security or deposits from trustees in certain suits to cover plaintiff's expenditure (Section 10).

penalties: Failure of a trustee to comply with a Court order under section 5 is a breach of trust, potentially leading to a suit under section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure, with potential liabilities under other laws (Section 6).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Court (defined as the District Judge's Court or an empowered court, including the High Court).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through petitions filed by interested persons or trustees seeking Court orders. Enforcement also involves the application of provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure for executing orders and enforcing attendance, examination, and production of documents.

rights: Right of any person interested in a charitable or religious trust to apply to the Court for information and audit of accounts (Section 3).
Right of a trustee to apply to the Court for directions on trust administration (Section 7).
duties: Duty of trustees to furnish particulars of the trust and its management when directed by the Court (Section 3).
Duty of trustees to present a written statement of their case when required by the Court (Section 5(2)).
Duty of trustees to comply with Court orders regarding trust administration (Section 6).
obligations: Obligation to file petitions with specific contents and verification (Section 4).
Obligation to provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard to all persons appearing in connection with a petition (Section 7(3)).
Obligation to provide security or deposit funds if ordered by the Court in certain suits (Section 10).

key_procedures: Filing a petition by an interested person to the Court for trust information and/or audit, including stating interest and sought particulars, and verification as per CPC (Sections 3 & 4).

Court's process upon petition: inquiry, notice to trustee and others, hearing petitioner and trustee, allowing written statements, possibility of staying proceedings if a suit is filed to challenge the trust, and passing an order or dismissing the petition (Section 5).
Trustee's application to the Court for opinion, advice, or direction on trust administration, with Court providing advice or fixing a hearing after notice to interested parties (Section 7).
Court's discretion in awarding costs for petitions and proceedings (Section 8).
Court's power to direct security or deposits in certain suits against trustees (Section 10).
administration: The administration of the Act is through the Courts (District Judge's Court or other empowered courts).
important_notes: The Act's extension and non-applicability to certain regions and trust types are detailed, including the exception for Jammu and Kashmir and provisions for state government notifications (Section 1(2)).
The definition of 'the Court' is broad and includes the High Court in its original civil jurisdiction (Section 2).
No appeals are allowed from orders, opinions, advice, or directions given under this Act (Section 12).

title: THE HINDU ADOPTIONS AND MAINTENANCE ACT, 1956
purpose: To amend and codify the law relating to adoptions and maintenance among Hindus.
scope: Applies to any person who is a Hindu by religion (including specific denominations), or a Buddhist, Jaina, or Sikh by religion. It also applies to any person not Muslim, Christian, Parsi, or Jew by religion, unless proven otherwise. It extends to the whole of India. Does not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes unless the Central Government directs otherwise.

key_definitions.custom and usage: Signify any rule which, having been continuously and uniformly observed for a long time, has obtained the force of law among Hindus in any local area, tribe, community, group or family. The rule must be certain, not unreasonable or opposed to public policy. For rules applicable only to a family, it must not have been discontinued.
key_definitions.maintenance: Includes provision for food, clothing, residence, education, and medical attendance and treatment. For an unmarried daughter, it also includes reasonable expenses for her marriage.
key_definitions.minor: Means a person who has not completed his or her age of eighteen years.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it extends to the whole of India.

Defines who the Act applies to based on religion and clarifies that it generally applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jainas, Sikhs, and certain other non-Abrahamic religious groups, with exceptions for Scheduled Tribes.
Provides definitions for 'custom', 'usage', 'maintenance', and 'minor'.
States that any existing Hindu law, custom, or usage that is inconsistent with this Act will cease to have effect, and other existing laws will cease to apply to Hindus if inconsistent with this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Adoptions to be regulated by this Chapter
main_sections.description: Mandates that all adoptions by or to Hindus must be in accordance with this Chapter, otherwise, the adoption is void and creates no new rights or severs old ones.
Outlines the conditions for a valid adoption: capacity and right of the adopter, capacity of the giver, capability of the adopted person, and compliance with other Chapter provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Capacity of a male Hindu to take in adoption
main_sections.description: Specifies that a male Hindu of sound mind and not a minor can adopt, with the consent of his living wife, unless specific conditions apply to the wife.

main_sections.section_title: Capacity of a female Hindu to take in adoption
main_sections.description: Specifies that a female Hindu of sound mind and not a minor can adopt, with the consent of her living husband, unless specific conditions apply to the husband.

main_sections.section_title: Persons capable of giving in adoption
main_sections.description: Details who can give a child in adoption (father, mother, or guardian), emphasizing equal rights of parents and conditions for guardian adoption with court permission.
Sets conditions for who can be adopted: must be Hindu, not already adopted, not married (unless custom allows), and under fifteen years of age (unless custom allows).

main_sections.section_title: Other conditions for a valid adoption
main_sections.description: Lists additional requirements for a valid adoption, including conditions related to existing children, age difference between adopter and adopted, simultaneous adoption, and the actual giving and taking of the child.

Explains that an adopted child is legally the child of the adoptive parents from the date of adoption, with all ties to the birth family severed and replaced by new ties. Certain exceptions apply regarding marriageability and existing property rights.

main_sections.section_title: Right of adoptive parents to dispose of their properties
main_sections.description: States that adoption does not prevent adoptive parents from disposing of their property.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of adoptive mother in certain cases
main_sections.description: Clarifies who is considered the adoptive mother and step-mothers/fathers in various adoption scenarios, including multiple wives and subsequent marriages.

main_sections.section_title: Valid adoption not to be cancelled
main_sections.description: Prohibits the cancellation of a valid adoption or the renunciation of adopted status by the child.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption as to registered documents relating to adoption
main_sections.description: Introduces a presumption of validity for registered documents concerning adoptions.

important_rules: A valid adoption requires the adopter to have the capacity and right to adopt, the giver to have the capacity to give, the adopted person to be capable of being adopted, and compliance with all other conditions in Chapter II.
A male Hindu adopting must have his wife's consent if she is living, unless she has renounced the world, converted to another religion, or is declared of unsound mind by a court.
A female Hindu adopting must have her husband's consent if he is living, unless he has renounced the world, converted to another religion, or is declared of unsound mind by a court.
No person can be adopted if they are already adopted, have been married (unless custom permits), or have completed fifteen years of age (unless custom permits).

The adoptive father/mother must not have a living son, son's son, or son's son's son (for adoption of a son) or a living daughter or son's daughter (for adoption of a daughter) at the time of adoption.
There must be an age difference of at least twenty-one years between the adoptive parent and the child being adopted, for adoptions involving opposite genders.
The same child cannot be adopted simultaneously by two or more persons.
The child must be actually given and taken in adoption with the intent to transfer the child from its birth family.
An adopted child is deemed to be the child of the adoptive parents for all purposes from the date of adoption, and ties to the birth family are severed.
A valid adoption cannot be cancelled, and the adopted child cannot renounce their status or return to their birth family.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but likely involves civil courts for matters related to adoption validity and guardianship.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By ensuring adoptions are made in accordance with the Chapter's provisions. Void adoptions have no legal effect. Court intervention is required for guardians giving children in adoption.

rights: Right of a male Hindu to take a child in adoption (with wife's consent).
Right of a female Hindu to take a child in adoption (with husband's consent).
Equal right of father and mother to give a child in adoption (with consent of the other).
Right of a guardian to give a child in adoption with court permission.
Right of adoptive parents to dispose of their property.
Rights of the adopted child as a legal child of the adoptive parents.
duties: Duty to obtain consent of spouse for adoption if they are living.
Duty of parents/guardians to act for the welfare of the child when giving in adoption.
Duty to ensure the adoption is made in compliance with the Act's conditions.
obligations: Obligation to provide maintenance for wife, widowed daughter-in-law, children, and aged parents (detailed in Chapter III).
Obligation to maintain relatives in the family of birth for an adopted child, if vested property requires it.

key_procedures: Adoption procedure for a male Hindu: must have sound mind, not be a minor, and generally requires the consent of his living wife. If more than one wife, consent of all is necessary unless specific exceptions apply.

Adoption procedure for a female Hindu: must have sound mind, not be a minor, and generally requires the consent of her living husband. If specific exceptions apply to the husband, his consent is not needed.

Procedure for giving a child in adoption: Generally, the father or mother has the right, with the consent of the other parent. If both are unable or unavailable, the guardian may give the child in adoption with previous permission from the court.

Court permission for guardian adoption: The court must be satisfied that the adoption is for the welfare of the child, considering the child's wishes, and that no undue payments were made for the adoption.
administration: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but likely overseen by various state and central government departments responsible for social justice, family welfare, and legal affairs.
important_notes: The Act uses the term 'Hindu' inclusively, covering various denominations and converts.
