The Act aims to override previous Hindu law and customs regarding adoption and maintenance where it provides specific rules.

Adopted children continue to have certain rights and obligations related to their birth family's property and maintenance obligations, though their primary legal status becomes that of the adoptive family.
The definition of 'maintenance' is comprehensive, covering basic needs and expenses for marriage of an unmarried daughter.
The Act specifies a minimum age difference of 21 years for adoptions between male and female adoptees.

title: The Carriage by Air Act, 1972
purpose: To give effect to the Convention for the unification of certain rules relating to international carriage by air signed at Warsaw on the 12th day of October, 1929 and to the said Convention as amended by the Hague Protocol on the 28th day of September, 1955, and also to the Montreal Convention signed on the 28th day of May, 1999. It also makes provisions for applying the rules contained in these conventions, in their original and amended forms, to non-international carriage by air.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to international carriage by air governed by the specified conventions and can be extended to non-international carriage by air through government notification. It covers the rights and liabilities of carriers, passengers, consignors, consignees, and other persons involved in air carriage.

key_definitions.amended Convention: The Convention for the unification of certain rules relating to international carriage by air as amended by the Hague Protocol on the 28th day of September, 1955.
key_definitions.Convention: The Convention for the unification of certain rules relating to international carriage by air signed at Warsaw on the 12th day of October, 1929.
key_definitions.Montreal Convention: The Convention for the unification of certain rules for international carriage by air signed at Montreal on the 28th day of May, 1999.
key_definitions.Annexure: The Annexure to this Act, which contains lists of High Contracting Parties and dates of enforcement for the conventions.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'amended Convention', 'Convention', 'Montreal Convention', and 'Annexure'.

States that the rules in the First Schedule (Warsaw Convention) have the force of law in India for applicable carriage by air, regardless of aircraft nationality. It also details how High Contracting Parties and enforcement dates are determined and allows the Central Government to modify the list of High Contracting Parties.

main_sections.section_title: Application of amended Convention to India
main_sections.description: States that the rules in the Second Schedule (Hague Protocol amended Convention) have the force of law in India for applicable carriage by air. It outlines the process for identifying High Contracting Parties and their enforcement dates, and empowers the Central Government to modify these.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Montreal Convention to India
main_sections.description: States that the rules in the Third Schedule (Montreal Convention) have the force of law in India for applicable carriage by air. It details how State Parties and their enforcement dates are listed and allows the Central Government to modify this list. It also empowers the Central Government to implement revised limits of liability under the Montreal Convention.

Determines carrier liability in case of passenger death, overriding other laws like the Fatal Accidents Act. It specifies who the liability is enforceable for, defines 'member of a family', and outlines procedures for bringing legal actions and distributing recovered amounts. It also allows courts to limit liability.
Specifies that sums in francs mentioned in the rules of the First or Second Schedule are to be converted into rupees at the prevailing exchange rate on the date damages are ascertained by the Court.
Specifies that sums in Special Drawing Rights mentioned in the Third Schedule are to be converted into rupees at the prevailing exchange rate on the date damages are ascertained by the Court.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions regarding suits against High Contracting Parties who undertake carriage by air
main_sections.description: Deems High Contracting Parties who haven't availed certain protocol provisions to have submitted to the jurisdiction of Indian courts for suits concerning carriage undertaken by them. It allows High Courts to make procedural rules but prohibits attachment or sale of property of a High Contracting Party.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to carriage by air which is not international
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to apply the rules of the First, Second, and Third Schedules, along with relevant sections of the Act, to non-international carriage by air, subject to specified exceptions, adaptations, and modifications.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act and mandates that such rules and notifications be laid before Parliament for approval.
This section has been repealed.

important_rules: Rules contained in the First Schedule (Warsaw Convention) govern international carriage by air.
Rules contained in the Second Schedule (Hague Protocol amended Convention) govern international carriage by air, as amended.
Rules contained in the Third Schedule (Montreal Convention) govern international carriage by air, as per the Montreal Convention.
In case of death, carrier liability is determined by the rules in the Schedules, overriding other laws.
Sums in francs and Special Drawing Rights are converted to rupees based on the exchange rate on the date damages are ascertained.
The Central Government can extend the application of the Act's rules to non-international carriage by air with modifications.
High Contracting Parties are deemed to have submitted to Indian court jurisdiction for suits related to carriage they undertake.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Courts of India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through application of the rules contained in the Schedules, which have the force of law in India. Enforcement of liability occurs through legal actions in courts. The Central Government enforces the Act through notifications and rule-making powers.

rights: Rights of carriers, passengers, consignors, and consignees as defined by the Conventions and codified in the Schedules.
Right to bring legal action for damages, including in case of death.
Right to benefit from the action for damages in case of death.
duties: Duty of carriers to comply with the rules of the Conventions.
Duty to adhere to limitations of liability as specified.
Duty to provide compensation for damages as per the rules.
obligations: Obligations of High Contracting Parties to implement and abide by the Convention rules.
Obligation for carriers to meet liabilities arising from carriage by air.
Obligation for individuals to comply with the provisions of the Act and its rules.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining High Contracting Parties and enforcement dates of conventions through the Annexure, which can be modified by the Central Government.
Procedure for conversion of foreign currency (francs, SDRs) into rupees for damage assessment.
Procedure for bringing legal actions to enforce liability, particularly in cases of passenger death.
Procedure for the Central Government to issue notifications applying the Act's rules to non-international carriage by air.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules for the Act's implementation, subject to parliamentary approval.
administration: The Central Government (specifically, the Ministry responsible for civil aviation, though not explicitly stated in the provided text).
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2009 and 2016.
The Act incorporates three key international conventions: Warsaw Convention (1929), Hague Protocol amended Convention (1955), and Montreal Convention (1999).
The Central Government has the power to add or omit High Contracting Parties or State Parties from the Annexure, thereby affecting which entities are covered by the Act.
The Central Government can also notify revised limits of liability under the Montreal Convention.
The rules of the Schedules have the force of law in India, irrespective of the aircraft's nationality.

title: THE SMUGGLERS AND FOREIGN EXCHANGE MANIPULATORS (FORFEITURE OF PROPERTY) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the forfeiture of illegally acquired properties of smugglers and foreign exchange manipulators and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, with the objective of effectively preventing smuggling activities and foreign exchange manipulations that have a deleterious effect on the national economy.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (though made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh by a later notification). It applies to persons convicted under specific customs and foreign exchange acts with a certain value of goods or amount involved, persons detained under the Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974, their relatives, associates, and subsequent holders of illegally acquired property. The Act's provisions can be determined with reference to events that occurred before its commencement.

key_definitions.competent authority: An officer of the Central Government authorized to perform the functions of a competent authority under this Act.
key_definitions.illegally acquired property: Property acquired wholly or partly out of or by means of income, earnings, or assets derived from or attributable to any prohibited activity under laws related to matters within Parliament's legislative power, or from income/earnings in respect of which such laws have been contravened, or from sources that cannot be proved and cannot be attributed to lawful acts. It also includes property traceable to such illegally acquired property, or property held by a person which was previously illegally acquired property by a previous holder unless transferred in good faith for adequate consideration.
key_definitions.property: Includes any interest in property, movable or immovable.
key_definitions.associate: Includes individuals residing in the person's residential premises, managing their affairs, keeping accounts, associations of persons, partnership firms, or private companies where the person is a member, partner, or director, and trustees of trusts created by the person or where the person contributed significantly to the trust's assets. It also includes any other person holding property on behalf of the individual, as determined by the competent authority.
key_definitions.relative: Includes spouse, siblings, siblings of the spouse, lineal ascendants or descendants, lineal ascendants or descendants of the spouse, and spouses of relatives mentioned previously.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent, and declares its commencement date, which is deemed to have come into force on November 5, 1975.

Details the categories of persons to whom the provisions of the Act apply, including those convicted of certain customs and foreign exchange offenses, those detained under specific preventive detention acts, their relatives, associates, and holders of illegally acquired property.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Appellate Tribunal', 'competent authority', 'illegally acquired property', 'prescribed', 'property', and 'trust'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of holding illegally acquired property
main_sections.description: Declares it unlawful for any person to whom the Act applies to hold illegally acquired property, either directly or indirectly. States that such property shall be liable to forfeiture.

Empowers the Central Government to authorize officers (not below the rank of Joint Secretary) to perform the functions of a competent authority and specifies that these authorities will act in respect of persons or classes of persons directed by the Central Government.

Outlines the procedure for issuing a notice of forfeiture. If the competent authority believes property is illegally acquired, it must record reasons and serve a notice on the affected person, requiring them to explain the sources of income, earnings, or assets and show cause why the property should not be forfeited. A copy of the notice is also to be served on any other person holding the property on behalf of the affected person.

main_sections.section_title: Forfeiture of property in certain cases
main_sections.description: Describes the process of forfeiture after considering the explanation to the show-cause notice. The competent authority must provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard to the affected person and any other person holding the property, before recording a finding on whether the property is illegally acquired and liable for forfeiture.

important_rules: It is unlawful for any person to whom the Act applies to hold any illegally acquired property, either directly or through another person on their behalf.
If a person holds illegally acquired property in contravention of the Act, such property is liable to be forfeited to the Central Government.
The competent authority must have reason to believe, with reasons recorded in writing, that property is illegally acquired before initiating forfeiture proceedings.
Affected persons must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before a forfeiture order is made.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority, Central Government, and Appellate Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through issuance of notices, conducting inquiries, recording findings, issuing forfeiture orders, and taking possession of forfeited property. The Act also grants powers of a civil court to the competent authority and Appellate Tribunal.

rights: Right to be heard before forfeiture proceedings are finalized.
Right to seek recourse through an Appellate Tribunal.
Right to have property considered for forfeiture only if it's illegally acquired according to the Act's definitions.
duties: Duty not to hold illegally acquired property.
Duty to respond to a notice of forfeiture by indicating sources of income and providing evidence.
Duty to cooperate with the competent authority and Appellate Tribunal.
Duty of certain officers to assist the competent authority and Appellate Tribunal.

key_procedures: Initiation of forfeiture proceedings by a competent authority based on belief of illegally acquired property, with reasons recorded.
Service of notice of forfeiture on the affected person and any other person holding the property, requiring a show-cause response.
Consideration of explanations and materials by the competent authority, followed by a hearing for the affected parties.
Recording of findings by the competent authority on whether the property is illegally acquired and liable for forfeiture.
Appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against orders of forfeiture.
Power of the competent authority to take possession of forfeited property.
Rectification of mistakes by the competent authority or Appellate Tribunal.
administration: Central Government (through authorized officers designated as 'competent authority') and the Appellate Tribunal.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over other laws in case of inconsistency, except for certain properties held in trust.
Findings in proceedings under other laws are not conclusive for proceedings under this Act.
Notices or orders are not to be invalidated for errors in description.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Special provisions exist for certain trust properties.

title: The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
purpose: To provide for the adjudication or trial by Administrative Tribunals of disputes and complaints with respect to recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of any State or of any local or other authority within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India or of any corporation or society owned or controlled by the Government, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to persons appointed to public services and posts connected with the affairs of the Union, any State, any local or other authority within India, or under the control of the Government of India, or any corporation or society owned or controlled by the Government. It extends to the whole of India concerning the Central Administrative Tribunal, and to individual States concerning State Administrative Tribunals.

key_definitions.Administrative Member: A Member of a Tribunal who is not a Judicial Member.
key_definitions.Administrative Tribunal: In relation to a State, means the Administrative Tribunal for the State or the Joint Administrative Tribunal for that State and any other State or States.
key_definitions.appointed day: In relation to a Tribunal, the date from which it is established by notification.
key_definitions.appropriate Government: The Central Government for the Central Administrative Tribunal or a Joint Administrative Tribunal; the State Government for a State Administrative Tribunal.
key_definitions.Central Administrative Tribunal: The Administrative Tribunal established under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.Joint Administrative Tribunal: An Administrative Tribunal for two or more States established under sub-section (3) of section 4.
key_definitions.Judicial Member: A Member of a Tribunal appointed as such under this Act, and includes the Chairman, who possesses specific qualifications.
key_definitions.Member: A Member (whether Judicial or Administrative) of a Tribunal, and includes the Chairman.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.post: A post within or outside India.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.service matters: All matters relating to the conditions of service of a person in connection with the affairs of the Union or any State, or any local/other authority, or any corporation/society owned/controlled by the Government, including remuneration, tenure, leave, disciplinary matters, and other related issues.
key_definitions.service rules as to redressal of grievan: Rules, regulations, orders, or other instruments in force for the redressal of grievances otherwise than under this Act.
key_definitions.society: A society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, or corresponding law.
key_definitions.Tribunal: The Central Administrative Tribunal or a State Administrative Tribunal or a Joint Administrative Tribunal.
key_definitions.Vice-Chairman: A Member authorised by the appropriate Government to perform administrative functions at places where Benches are set up.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India for CAT, specific states for SATs), and commencement dates for the Central Administrative Tribunal and State Administrative Tribunals.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain persons
main_sections.description: Specifies categories of persons to whom the Act does not apply, including members of naval, military, or air forces, officers/servants of Supreme Court or High Courts, and secretarial staff of Parliament or State Legislatures.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrative Member', 'Administrative Tribunal', 'application', 'appropriate Government', 'Bench', 'Central Administrative Tribunal', 'Chairman', 'Judicial Member', 'service matters', etc.

Details the establishment of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) by the Central Government, State Administrative Tribunals (SATs) on request from State Governments, and Joint Administrative Tribunals (JATs) for two or more States. It also includes provisions for the designation of Members of State Tribunals as CAT Members and vice-versa.

main_sections.section_title: Composition of Tribunals and Benches thereof
main_sections.description: Outlines the composition of each Tribunal, consisting of a Chairman and Judicial and Administrative Members. It specifies that Benches shall consist of one Judicial Member and one Administrative Member and details the Chairman's powers regarding discharging functions of Members and transferring Members between Benches.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of the Central Administrative Tribunal
main_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction, powers, and authority of the Central Administrative Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of State Administrative Tribunals
main_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction, powers, and authority of State Administrative Tribunals.
Specifies the procedure for making applications to tribunals.

main_sections.section_title: Applications not to be admitted unless other remedies exhausted
main_sections.description: Stipulates that applications will not be admitted if other remedies have not been exhausted.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of courts except the Supreme Court under article 136 of the Constitution
main_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of all courts except the Supreme Court (under Article 136 of the Constitution) from entertaining matters that fall within the purview of the Administrative Tribunals.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have an overriding effect over other laws in force.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Applications to tribunals can be made by aggrieved persons concerning recruitment and conditions of service (Section 19).
Applications are generally not to be admitted unless other remedies have been exhausted (Section 20).
Limitations for filing applications are specified (Section 21).
Tribunals have the power to punish for contempt (Section 17).
Proceedings before a Tribunal are to be considered judicial proceedings (Section 30).
Members and staff of the Tribunal are deemed to be public servants (Section 31).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 32).
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws (Section 33).

penalties: Power to punish for contempt (Section 17).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tribunals established under the Act (Central Administrative Tribunal, State Administrative Tribunals, Joint Administrative Tribunals).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the adjudication of disputes and complaints related to recruitment and conditions of service, and by issuing orders which are to be executed.

rights: Right of an applicant to take the assistance of a legal practitioner (Section 23).
Right of Government, etc., to appoint presenting officers (Section 23).
Right to seek adjudication of disputes and complaints related to recruitment and service matters.
Right to approach the Supreme Court under Article 136 of the Constitution against orders of Tribunals.
duties: To adhere to the procedures and rules laid down by the Act and the Tribunals.
To comply with the orders and decisions of the Tribunals.
Exhaustion of other remedies before approaching the Tribunal (generally, Section 20).
obligations: For the Central Government to establish the Central Administrative Tribunal.
For State Governments to request the establishment of State Administrative Tribunals.
For all parties involved to follow the prescribed procedures and limitations for applications.
For employees covered by the Act to have their recruitment and service matters adjudicated by the Tribunals.

key_procedures: Making an application to a Tribunal (Section 19).
Exhaustion of other remedies before admitting an application (Section 20).
Adherence to limitation periods for filing applications (Section 21).
Procedure and powers of Tribunals in conducting proceedings (Section 22).
Right to legal assistance or appointment of presenting officers (Section 23).
Conditions for making interim orders (Section 24).
Transfer of cases between Benches by the Chairman (Section 25).
Decision-making by majority vote (Section 26).
Execution of orders of a Tribunal (Section 27).
administration: The Central Government is responsible for establishing the Central Administrative Tribunal and making rules. State Governments are involved in establishing State Administrative Tribunals and making rules. The Tribunals themselves administer justice in service matters.
important_notes: The Act provides for the adjudication of disputes and complaints related to recruitment and conditions of service, thus creating specialized administrative tribunals.
Jurisdiction of civil courts is excluded except for the Supreme Court's power under Article 136.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws.
Specific categories of persons, such as members of armed forces and certain judicial staff, are excluded from the purview of the Act.

title: THE RAILWAY CLAIMS TRIBUNAL ACT, 1987
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Railway Claims Tribunal for inquiring into and determining claims against a railway administration for loss, destruction, damage, deterioration or non-delivery of animals or goods entrusted to it to be carried by railway or for the refund of fares or freight or for compensation for death or injury to passengers occurring as a result of railway accidents or untoward incidents, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to claims against a railway administration for loss, damage, non-delivery of goods/animals, refund of fares/freight, and compensation for death or injury to passengers due to railway accidents or untoward incidents.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date with effect from which the Claims Tribunal is established under section 3.
key_definitions.bench: A Bench of the Claims Tribunal.
key_definitions.chairman: The Chairman of the Claims Tribunal.
key_definitions.claims_tribunal: The Railway Claims Tribunal established under section 3.
key_definitions.judicial_member: A Member of the Claims Tribunal appointed as such under this Act, and includes the Chairman or Vice-Chairman who possesses any of the qualifications specified in sub-section (3) of section 5.
key_definitions.member: A Member (whether Judicial or Technical) of the Claims Tribunal, and includes the Chairman and Vice-Chairman.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules.
key_definitions.technical_member: A Member of the Claims Tribunal who is not a Judicial Member, and includes the Chairman or a Vice-Chairman who possesses any of the qualifications specified in sub-section (4) of section 5.
key_definitions.vice_chairman: A Vice-Chairman of the Claims Tribunal.
key_definitions.untoward_incident: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in clause (c) of section 123 of the Railways Act, 1989.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987, specifies its extent to the whole of India, and mentions that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'application', 'appointed day', 'Bench', 'Chairman', 'Claims Tribunal', 'Judicial Member', 'Member', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'Railways Act', 'rules', 'Technical Member', 'Vice-Chairman', and 'untoward incident'.

The Central Government is empowered to establish a Claims Tribunal, to be known as the Railway Claims Tribunal, to exercise the jurisdiction, powers, and authority conferred on it by or under this Act and under Chapter VII of the Railways Act, 1989.

main_sections.section_title: Composition of Claims Tribunal and Benches thereof
main_sections.description: This section details the composition of the Claims Tribunal, including the Chairman, Vice-Chairmen, Judicial Members, and Technical Members. It also outlines how jurisdiction can be exercised by Benches and allows for single-member Benches in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications for appointment as Chairman, Vice-Chairman or other Member
main_sections.description: This section specifies the qualifications required for appointment as Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Judicial Member, and Technical Member, often involving experience as a Judge, in the Indian Legal Service, civil judicial posts, or under a railway administration.

main_sections.section_title: Vice-Chairman to act as Chairman or to discharge his functions in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: This section describes the provisions for a Vice-Chairman to act as Chairman in case of a vacancy or the Chairman's inability to discharge functions.
Outlines the term of office for the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and other Members, which is five years or until they attain a certain age (65 for Chairman, 62 for others).
Details the process for resignation by the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, or other Member, and the grounds and procedure for their removal from office.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries and allowances and other terms and conditions of service
main_sections.description: States that the salaries, allowances, and other terms and conditions of service for the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and other Members shall be as prescribed, and these cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of Claims Tribunal
main_sections.description: This section is crucial as it defines the powers and authority of the Claims Tribunal in determining claims.
This section likely specifies circumstances under which the jurisdiction of the Claims Tribunal is barred.
This section would detail how an application is made to the Claims Tribunal.
This section likely deals with the time limits for filing applications.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of Claims Tribunal
main_sections.description: This section outlines the procedural aspects and powers of the Claims Tribunal during its proceedings.
This section would detail the provisions related to appeals against the decisions of the Claims Tribunal.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_procedures: Application to Claims Tribunal (Section 16)
Procedure and powers of Claims Tribunal (Section 18)
Appeals against decisions (Section 23)
administration: Central Government (for establishment and making rules), President (for appointments), Chief Justice of India (consultation for Chairman appointment).
important_notes: The Act has been amended by various other Acts, for example, by the insertion of 'or untoward incidents' in the purpose clause.
Section 9A provides for overriding provisions for appointments made after the commencement of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, and the Finance Act, 2017.

title: THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM (REPEAL) ACT, 2004
purpose: To repeal the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002.
scope: This act applies to all of India. It primarily deals with the repeal of the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, and the consequences thereof.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002 (Act 15 of 2002).

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Prevention of Terrorism (Repeal) Act, 2004, and states its commencement date as September 21, 2004.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Act 15 of 2002 and saving
main_sections.description: Repeals the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002. It includes provisions to save previous operations, rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, forfeitures, punishments, investigations, legal proceedings, and remedies under the repealed Act, with a limitation on cognizance of offenses after one year. It also mandates a review of cases by a Review Committee within one year of the Act's commencement, with provisions for case withdrawal or investigation closure if no prima facie case exists. The Review Committee is granted powers similar to a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Repeals the Prevention of Terrorism (Repeal) Ordinance, 2004 (Ord. 1 of 2004). Actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002 is repealed.
Rule 2: Previous operations, rights, liabilities, penalties, etc., under the repealed Act are saved.
Rule 3: No court shall take cognizance of an offense under the repealed Act after one year from the commencement of this Act.
Rule 4: A Review Committee must review cases registered under the repealed Act within one year.
Rule 5: If the Review Committee finds no prima facie case, cases shall be deemed withdrawn or investigations closed.
Rule 6: The Prevention of Terrorism (Repeal) Ordinance, 2004 is repealed.

penalties: Any penalty, forfeiture or punishment incurred in respect of any offence under the principal Act (Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002) may still be imposed as if the principal Act had not been repealed, subject to the one-year limitation on cognizance.
If the Review Committee determines there is no prima facie case, cases where cognizance has been taken shall be deemed withdrawn, and pending investigations shall be closed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Review Committee constituted by the Central Government, and courts of law for any residual legal proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By the Review Committee reviewing cases and issuing directions, and by courts continuing or enforcing legal proceedings as if the repealed Act had not been repealed, with the stipulated time limitation.

rights: Right to have previous operations, rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, forfeitures, and punishments incurred under the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, be saved.
Right to have investigations, legal proceedings, or remedies continued or enforced under the repealed Act, subject to limitations.
duties: Duty of the Review Committee to review all cases registered under the principal Act within one year.
Duty of the Central Government to constitute Review Committees as necessary.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that no court takes cognizance of an offense under the principal Act after the expiry of one year from the commencement of this Act.
Obligation to comply with the directions of the Review Committee regarding case withdrawal or investigation closure.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Upon commencement of the Act, the Review Committee (or newly constituted committees) must review all cases registered under the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, within one year.
Procedure 2: If the Review Committee opines there is no prima facie case, it issues directions for cases to be deemed withdrawn (if cognizance taken) or investigations to be closed (if pending).
administration: Central Government (for constituting Review Committees).
important_notes: No court shall take cognizance of an offence under the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, after the expiry of the period of one year from the commencement of this Act.
The Review Committee's review must be completed within one year from the commencement of this Act.
Actions taken under the Prevention of Terrorism (Repeal) Ordinance, 2004, are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

title: THE NATIONAL GREEN TRIBUNAL ACT, 2010
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a National Green Tribunal for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources, including enforcement of any legal right relating to environment and giving relief and compensation for damages to persons and property, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to cases relating to environmental protection, conservation of forests and other natural resources, enforcement of environmental legal rights, and relief/compensation for environmental damages. It is established by the Central Government and has territorial jurisdiction as specified.

key_definitions.accident: An accident involving a fortuitous, sudden, or unintended occurrence while handling any hazardous substance or equipment, plant, or vehicle, resulting in continuous, intermittent, or repeated exposure to death, injury to any person, or damage to any property or environment, excluding accidents solely due to war or civil disturbance.
key_definitions.environment: Includes water, air, and land, and the interrelationship among and between them, and human beings, other living creatures, plants, microorganisms, and property.
key_definitions.hazardous substance: Any substance or preparation defined as hazardous in the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and exceeding quantities specified by the Central Government under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991.
key_definitions.substantial question relating to environ: Includes direct violation of a statutory environmental obligation by a person, affecting the community at large, causing substantial damage to the environment or property, or broadly measurable damage to public health, or environmental consequences relating to a specific activity or point source of pollution.
key_definitions.Tribunal: The National Green Tribunal established under section 3 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'accident', 'environment', 'hazardous substance', 'substantial question relating to environment', and 'Tribunal'. It also refers to definitions in other environmental enactments.
Empowers the Central Government to establish a Tribunal, to be known as the National Green Tribunal, for exercising jurisdiction, powers, and authority conferred by the Act.

Specifies the composition of the Tribunal, including a full-time Chairperson, Judicial Members, and Expert Members. It also outlines provisions for inviting specialized knowledge, specifying places of sitting and territorial jurisdiction, and regulating practices and procedures.
Grants the Tribunal the power to settle disputes relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources.
Details the procedure and powers of the Tribunal, including its ability to apply certain principles and take decisions by majority.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to comply with orders of Tribunal
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for failure to comply with the orders of the Tribunal.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in certain circumstances.

important_rules: The Tribunal shall be established by the Central Government to effectively and expeditiously dispose of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources.

The Tribunal shall consist of a full-time Chairperson, not less than ten but subject to a maximum of twenty full-time Judicial Members, and not less than ten but subject to a maximum of twenty full-time Expert Members.
The Tribunal is empowered to settle disputes, grant relief, compensation, and restitution for environmental damage.
The Tribunal shall apply principles like the 'polluter pays' principle and the 'precautionary principle'.
Penalties are prescribed for failure to comply with the orders of the Tribunal.

penalties: Penalty for failure to comply with orders of the Tribunal (Section 26)
Offences by companies (Section 27)
Offences by Government Departments (Section 28)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Green Tribunal, established by the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial proceedings and by imposing penalties for non-compliance with its orders. The Act also provides for the execution of the Tribunal's awards and orders.

rights: Right to seek relief and compensation for environmental damage.
Right to have legal rights relating to environment enforced.
Right to access judicial and administrative proceedings for environmental matters (implied by the purpose and jurisdiction of the Tribunal).
duties: Duty to comply with orders of the Tribunal.
Duty to protect and conserve forests and other natural resources (implied).
obligations: Obligations arising from the enforcement of any legal right relating to environment.
Obligations to provide relief and compensation for damages to persons and property due to environmental issues.

key_procedures: Application or appeal to the Tribunal (Section 18): Specifies the process for filing applications or appeals before the Tribunal.
Procedure and powers of the Tribunal (Section 19): Outlines the procedural aspects and powers vested in the Tribunal for conducting its proceedings.
Execution of award or order or decision of Tribunal (Section 25): Details the mechanism for enforcing the awards, orders, or decisions made by the Tribunal.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for establishing and making rules for the Tribunal. The Tribunal itself administers justice in environmental matters.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect over other laws in relation to environmental protection and conservation.
The Tribunal applies principles such as the precautionary principle, polluter pays principle, and the principle of equity and sustainable development.
A person convicted of an offence under the Act may be punishable with imprisonment and/or fine.
The right to a healthy environment has been construed as part of the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution.

title: THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT, 2012
purpose: To protect children from offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography and provide for establishment of Special Courts for trial of such offences and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It covers acts of sexual assault, sexual harassment, and pornography involving children (persons below the age of eighteen years).

key_definitions.child: Any person below the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.penetrative sexual assault: Includes various forms of penetration of a child's body parts (vagina, mouth, urethra, anus) or using objects for penetration, as well as oral contact with child's sexual organs.
key_definitions.aggravated penetrative sexual assault: Penetrative sexual assault committed by specific individuals (police, armed forces, public servant, staff of institutions like jails, hospitals, educational institutions, religious institutions) or under specific circumstances (gang assault, use of deadly weapons, causing grievous hurt, pregnancy, life-threatening diseases, death, disability, repeated offenses, against children below twelve years, by relatives or those in domestic relationships, by those in positions of trust, against pregnant children, attempted murder, during communal violence or natural calamities, or by repeat offenders).
key_definitions.sexual assault: Has the same meaning as assigned to it in section 7 (not detailed in the provided text).
key_definitions.sexual harassment: Has the same meaning as assigned to it in section 11 (not detailed in the provided text).
key_definitions.child pornography: Any visual depiction of sexually explicit conduct involving a child, including photographs, videos, digital or computer-generated images, and modified images appearing to depict a child.

main_sections.description: Names the act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India), and provides for its commencement by notification of the Central Government.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'child', 'penetrative sexual assault', 'aggravated penetrative sexual assault', 'child pornography', and other related terms. It also references definitions from other relevant acts.
Defines what constitutes 'penetrative sexual assault' involving a child.
Specifies the punishment for penetrative sexual assault, including enhanced penalties for assaults on children below sixteen years of age, and outlines the use of fine for victim compensation.
Defines 'aggravated penetrative sexual assault' under various aggravating circumstances.
Outlines the procedure and obligation for reporting offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of media, studio and photographic facilities to report cases
main_sections.description: Imposes a duty on media, studios, and photographic facilities to report cases of child sexual abuse.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for failure to report or record a case
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for failing to report or record a case as required.

main_sections.section_title: Recording of statement of a child
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for recording the statement of a child victim.
Provides for the designation of Special Courts for the trial of offences under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Trials to be conducted in camera
main_sections.description: Mandates that trials for offences under this Act be conducted in camera to protect the child victim.

main_sections.section_title: Act not in derogation of any other law
main_sections.description: Clarifies that this Act does not affect the application of any other existing law.

important_rules: Any person who commits penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with imprisonment of not less than ten years, extending to life imprisonment, and a fine.
Penetrative sexual assault on a child below sixteen years of age carries a punishment of not less than twenty years, extending to imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life), and a fine.
Aggravated penetrative sexual assault, committed under specific circumstances or by certain individuals, leads to severe penalties.
Media, studios, and photographic facilities have an obligation to report cases of offences under this Act.
Failure to report or record a case, or filing a false complaint, are punishable offences.
Statements of child victims are to be recorded following specific procedures to ensure their well-being.
Trials for offences under this Act are to be conducted in camera.
Special Courts are designated for the trial of these offences.

penalties: Imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life for penetrative sexual assault.

Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life) for penetrative sexual assault on a child below sixteen years of age.
Penalties for aggravated penetrative sexual assault are significantly higher and are detailed based on the aggravating factors.
Punishment for using a child for pornographic purposes.
Punishment for storage of pornographic material involving a child.
Punishment for abetment of an offence.
Punishment for attempt to commit an offence.
Punishment for failure to report or record a case.
Punishment for false complaint or false information.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Law enforcement agencies (police), Special Courts, and Special Public Prosecutors established under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation by police, prosecution by Special Public Prosecutors, and trial by designated Special Courts. The Act also mandates reporting obligations for certain entities and specifies procedures for evidence collection and trial conduct.

rights: Right of a child to protection from sexual assault, sexual harassment, and pornography.
Right of a child to have their privacy and confidentiality protected throughout the judicial process.
Right of a child to take assistance of experts.
Right of a child to take assistance of a legal practitioner.
duties: Duty of the State to make special provisions for children.
Duty of persons and entities to report offences against children.
Duty of media, studios, and photographic facilities to report cases.
Duty of individuals in positions of trust or authority to protect children from sexual offences.
obligations: Obligation to report offences against children.
Obligation to establish and maintain Special Courts.
Obligation to appoint Special Public Prosecutors.
Obligation to conduct trials in camera to protect child victims.

key_procedures: Reporting of offences by any person, with specific obligations on media, studios, and photographic facilities.
Recording of statements of child victims by police and, if necessary, by a Magistrate.
Medical examination of a child victim.
Designation and functioning of Special Courts.
Conducting trials in camera.
Recording of evidence of child witnesses within a specified period and disposal of cases.
Procedure for determination of age of the offender if the offender is a child.
administration: The Central Government, through notifications, appoints the commencement date. The Act also empowers the Central Government to make rules and remove difficulties. Special Courts and Special Public Prosecutors are established for its implementation.
important_notes: The Act emphasizes the best interests and well-being of the child as paramount at every stage.
The Act is not in derogation of any other law, meaning other applicable laws remain in force.
Public awareness about the Act is to be promoted.
The implementation of the Act is to be monitored.

title: The Indian Institutes of Management Act, 2017
purpose: To declare certain Institutes of management as institutions of national importance with a view to empower these institutions to attain standards of global excellence in management, management research and allied areas of knowledge and to provide for certain other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the Institutes of Management mentioned in the Schedule, which are declared as institutions of national importance. Geographically, it pertains to India. Subject matter scope covers management education, research, and related activities.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council referred to in section 14.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors referred to in sub-section (1) of section 10.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board of Governors of the Institutes appointed under clause (a) of sub-section (2) of section 10.
key_definitions.Coordination Forum: The Coordination Forum established under section 29.
key_definitions.Institute: Any Institute mentioned in column (5) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.Society: Any of the societies registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 or other specified State Societies Registration Acts, mentioned in column (3) of the Schedule.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette, with different dates possible for different provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Hereby declares each Institute mentioned in the Schedule as an institution of national importance.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Coordination Forum', 'Institute', 'notification', 'Ordinances', 'prescribed', 'regulations', 'Schedule', and 'society'.

Declares every Institute as a body corporate by its specified name. It also includes provisions for the National Institute of Industrial Engineering, Mumbai, to be called the Indian Institute of Management, Mumbai, and for the Indian Institute of Management, Guwahati.

Outlines the consequences of incorporation, including the transfer of references in contracts, vesting of properties, transfer of rights and liabilities, continuation of employment for existing staff, migration of students, and continuation of legal proceedings.

Lists the objects of each Institute, which include educating and supporting leaders, carrying out research, advancing knowledge, providing high-quality management education, promoting inclusive and sustainable development, supporting social and gender equity, developing educational programs, setting up centers, and collaborating with other institutions.

Details the powers and functions of each Institute, such as administration, providing courses, conducting research, awarding degrees, granting scholarships, managing infrastructure, setting fees, acquiring property, creating posts, appointing committees, and receiving grants.
Establishes the Board of Governors as an authority of the Institute.
Establishes the Academic Council as an authority of the Institute.
Provides for the establishment of a Coordination Forum.

important_rules: Each Institute shall be a body corporate by its specified name and shall have perpetual succession and a common seal.
On commencement of the Act, references to existing Institutes in contracts and instruments shall be deemed references to corresponding Institutes.
All properties, rights, debts, and liabilities of existing Institutes shall be transferred to corresponding Institutes.
Employees of existing Institutes shall continue their service in corresponding Institutes under similar terms and conditions.
Students pursuing courses in existing Institutes shall be deemed to have migrated to corresponding Institutes.
Institutes must educate and support leaders, carry out research for national development, provide high-quality management education, and promote social and gender equity.
Institutes have powers to conduct courses, research, grant degrees, manage finances, acquire property, and create academic and administrative posts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and by extension, the Institutes themselves through their governing bodies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, rules made by the Central Government, and regulations made by the Boards of the Institutes. The Central Government has powers to make rules and remove difficulties.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right to sue and be sued.
Right to grant degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.
Right to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, prizes, and medals.
Right to receive grants, gifts, and contributions.
Right for employees to hold office or service with the same tenure, remuneration, and terms and conditions unless altered.
duties: Duty to educate and support leaders.
Duty to carry out research advancing new knowledge and innovation.
Duty to provide management education of high quality.
Duty to sensitise management education to national development goals.
Duty to support and develop programs promoting social and gender equity.
Duty to carry out administration and management of the Institutes.
Duty to provide by regulations for admission of candidates.
Duty to conduct examinations and establish evaluation processes.
Duty to maintain infrastructure.
Duty to create partnership, affiliation, and other classes of membership.
obligations: Obligation to act in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
Obligation for the Board to approve acquisition, holding, and dealing with property.
Obligation for prior intimation to the Central Government for immovable property acquisition.
Obligation to make appointments to posts created under the Institute.
Obligation to report accounts and information to the Central Government.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Central Government notifies the date of commencement in the Official Gazette.
Declaration of National Importance: Achieved through a declaration in the Act based on the Institutes' objectives.
Incorporation: Institutes become body corporates upon commencement of the Act.
Transfer of Assets and Liabilities: Automatic transfer from existing to corresponding Institutes.
Employment Continuation: Existing employees continue under new Institutes with existing terms.
Student Migration: Automatic migration of students from existing to corresponding Institutes.
Making of Rules: Central Government's power to make rules under the Act.
Making of Regulations: Board's power to make regulations.
Making of Ordinances: Academic Council's power to make Ordinances.
administration: Central Government (for making rules and notifications) and the respective Boards of Governors and Directors of the Institutes (for day-to-day administration and operational matters).
important_notes: Different dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The National Institute of Industrial Engineering, Mumbai, is renamed the 'Indian Institute of Management, Mumbai'.
The Indian Institute of Management, Guwahati, is brought under the purview of this Act.
Any property acquired wholly or partly from State or Central Government funds has specific conditions for disposal.
Institutes are considered public authorities under the Right to Information Act, 2005.

title: The Bilateral Netting of Qualified Financial Contracts Act, 2020
purpose: To ensure financial stability and promote competitiveness in Indian financial markets by providing enforceability of bilateral netting of qualified financial contracts and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to qualified financial contracts entered into on a bilateral basis between qualified financial market participants, where at least one participant is regulated by an authority specified in the First Schedule. This includes entities regulated by the Reserve Bank of India, IRDAI, PFRDA, IFSCA, and other entities notified by the relevant authority. The Act also covers contracts entered into with netting agreements or otherwise, and addresses situations involving insolvent parties, guarantors, and those providing collateral.

key_definitions.administration: Proceedings of the nature of placing under administration, including moratorium, reorganisation, winding up, liquidation, insolvency, bankruptcy, composition with creditors, receivership, conservatorship, or any similar proceedings against a qualified financial market participant.
key_definitions.administration practitioner: The liquidator, receiver, trustee, conservator, resolution professional, or any other person or entity administering the affairs of a party subject to administration.
key_definitions.authority: The Central Government or any of the regulatory authorities specified in the First Schedule.
key_definitions.close-out netting: A process involving the termination of obligations under a qualified financial contract with a defaulting party and subsequent combining of positive and negative replacement values into a single net payable or receivable.
key_definitions.collateral: Money, securities, guarantees, letters of credit, obligations to reimburse, and any other asset commonly used as collateral.
key_definitions.netting: Determination of net claims or obligations after setting off or adjusting all claims or obligations arising from mutual dealings between parties to qualified financial contracts, including close-out netting.
key_definitions.qualified financial contract: A bilateral agreement or contract or transaction, or type of contract, designated as such by the relevant authority, excluding certain contracts specified by the Central Government or multilateral contracts under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, and the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
key_definitions.qualified financial market participant: Includes banking institutions, non-banking financial companies, other financial institutions regulated by the RBI, individuals, partnerships, companies, international development banks, insurance/reinsurance companies regulated by IRDAI, pension funds regulated by PFRDA, financial institutions regulated by IFSCA, and any other entity notified by the relevant authority.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Bilateral Netting of Qualified Financial Contracts Act, 2020, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as administration, administration practitioner, authority, close-out netting, collateral, netting, qualified financial contract, and qualified financial market participant.

Specifies that the Act applies to bilateral qualified financial contracts between qualified financial market participants where at least one participant is regulated by an authority listed in the First Schedule.
Grants powers to the relevant authority to designate bilateral agreements as qualified financial contracts and to specify entities as qualified financial market participants.

Establishes the enforceability of netting for qualified financial contracts, whether under a netting agreement or otherwise. It states that such contracts are not void and that close-out netting is enforceable against insolvent parties and related parties, even during administration proceedings.

Details the process for invoking close-out netting, including notice requirements and the calculation of a single net amount by terminating, liquidating, or accelerating obligations and determining values. It also covers the realization of collateral.
Describes how the net amount is determined in close-out netting, involving the calculation of values and the determination of a net balance.

main_sections.section_title: Limitations on powers of administration practitioner
main_sections.description: Defines limitations on the powers of an administration practitioner concerning close-out netting.
Grants the power to amend the Schedules to the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of this Act to override other laws
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall override other laws.
Confers power to remove difficulties encountered in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: Netting of qualified financial contracts is enforceable, either according to the terms of a netting agreement or as per section 6 if no netting agreement exists.
A qualified financial contract shall not be deemed void or unenforceable due to any existing law.

Close-out netting is enforceable against an insolvent party, guarantors, or persons providing collateral, and is not affected by the appointment of an administration practitioner or any administration-related proceedings.
Even if a qualified financial market participant is under administration, close-out netting shall apply, notwithstanding any court orders, moratoriums, or other legal provisions.
The amount payable or claims in accordance with close-out netting are final, irrevocable, and binding on parties and the administration practitioner.
Close-out netting can be initiated by a notice upon an event of default or a termination event, without prior notice or consent from an insolvent party or its administration practitioner.

All obligations under qualified financial contracts must be reduced to or replaced with a single net amount through termination, liquidation, or acceleration of rights and obligations, calculation of values, and determination of the net balance.
Realization, appropriation, or liquidation of collateral under a collateral arrangement takes effect without prior notice or consent from any party, unless otherwise agreed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government or any of the regulatory authorities specified in the First Schedule.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the enforceability of netting agreements, the application of close-out netting procedures, and the override provisions of the Act which state that its provisions prevail over other laws.

rights: Right to enforce netting of qualified financial contracts.
Right to enforce close-out netting against insolvent parties.
Right to terminate relevant transactions under a netting agreement upon a termination event.
duties: Duty to ensure all obligations under qualified financial contracts are reduced to a single net amount.
Duty to comply with the provisions of netting agreements and this Act.
obligations: Obligation to pay the net balance determined through close-out netting.
Obligation to adhere to the terms of netting agreements and collateral arrangements.

key_procedures: Invocation of close-out netting: A party can initiate close-out netting by providing notice to the other party upon an event of default or termination event. This involves terminating, liquidating, or accelerating obligations, calculating their values, and determining a net balance.
Netting of qualified financial contracts: Enforceable either as per the netting agreement or as outlined in section 6, ensuring a single net amount is determined.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be managed by the Central Government and the regulatory authorities specified in the First Schedule.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions.
The definition of qualified financial contracts excludes contracts entered into between specific parties or on a multilateral basis under certain other Acts.
Provisions of this Act override other laws.

title: THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR INDIAN SYSTEM OF MEDICINE ACT, 2020
purpose: To provide for a medical education system that improves access to quality and affordable medical education, ensures availability of adequate and high-quality medical professionals of Indian System of Medicine, promotes equitable and universal healthcare, encourages a community health perspective, makes services of such professionals accessible and affordable, promotes national health goals, encourages adoption of latest medical research, facilitates periodic and transparent assessment of medical institutions, maintains a medical register for Indian System of Medicine, enforces high ethical standards, is flexible to adapt to changing needs, and has an effective grievance redressal mechanism.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to the Indian System of Medicine, including Ashtang Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, and Sowa-Rigpa, supplemented by modern advances. It governs medical education, assessment of institutions, and the practice and registration of medical professionals in these systems.

key_definitions.Autonomous Board: Any of the Autonomous Boards constituted under section 18.
key_definitions.Commission: The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Indian System of Medicine: The Ashtang Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa Systems of Medicine supplemented by such modern advances, scientific and technological development as the Commission may, in consultation with the Central Government, declare by notification from time to time.
key_definitions.medical institution: Any institution within or outside India which grants degrees, diplomas or licenses in Indian System of Medicine and includes affiliated colleges and deemed to be Universities.
key_definitions.National Register: A National Medical Register for Indian System of Medicine maintained by the Board of Ethics and Registration for Indian System of Medicine under section 32.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its territorial extent (whole of India), and outlines the process for its commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including Autonomous Board, Commission, Indian System of Medicine, medical institution, National Register, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of National Commission for Indian System of Medicine
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract. Its head office is to be in New Delhi.

Details the composition of the Commission, which includes a Chairperson, fifteen ex officio Members, and twenty-three part-time Members. It also specifies the qualifications for the Chairperson and the appointment process for ex officio and part-time Members, including restrictions on association with private medical institutions.
Outlines the powers and functions of the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine.
Relates to the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test.
Relates to the National Exit Test.
Provides for the constitution of Autonomous Boards.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Board of Ethics and Registration for Indian System of Medicine
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Board of Ethics and Registration for Indian System of Medicine.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Indian System of Medicine
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Indian System of Medicine.

main_sections.section_title: National Register and State Register of Indian System of Medicine
main_sections.description: Deals with the maintenance of the National Register and State Registers for Indian System of Medicine.
Specifies the rights of persons to practice Indian System of Medicine.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of qualifications granted by Universities or medical institutions in India
main_sections.description: Covers the recognition of medical qualifications awarded by Indian institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson, Members, officers of Commission and of Autonomous Boards to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Chairperson, Members, and officers of the Commission and Autonomous Boards as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede Commission
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to supersede the Commission under certain circumstances.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Commission to make regulations.
Provides for the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: The Chairperson of the Commission must possess outstanding ability, proven administrative capacity, integrity, a postgraduate degree in Indian System of Medicine, and at least twenty years of experience, with ten years as a leader in healthcare delivery or development of Indian System of Medicine.

Members of the Commission and its associated bodies are prohibited from directly or indirectly owning or being associated with the managing body of a private or non-government medical institution regulated by this Act.
The Central Government shall appoint the Chairperson and Presidents of Autonomous Boards on the recommendation of a Search Committee.
The Central Government has the power to give directions to the Commission, Autonomous Boards, and State Governments.
Universities and medical institutions have obligations under the Act.
The Act outlines specific procedures for the completion of courses of studies in medical institutions.
Rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine, its Autonomous Boards, and the Central Government are the primary bodies responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is carried out through various mechanisms including the assessment and rating of medical institutions, maintenance of registers, recognition of qualifications, and imposition of penalties for contraventions (details of specific penalties not fully detailed in the provided text but implied through various sections like 'cognizance of offences').

rights: Right of persons to be enrolled in the National Register.
Right of persons to practice any of the Indian System of Medicine (subject to registration and other provisions).
duties: Obligations of persons to be enrolled in the National Register.
Obligation of Universities and medical institutions to comply with the Act.
obligations: Obligations related to registration in the National Register.
Obligations of medical institutions regarding their courses and standards.
Obligation of State Governments to promote public health.

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairperson and Members of the Commission and Presidents and Members of Autonomous Boards through a Search Committee process.
Constitution and functioning of various Autonomous Boards (Board of Ayurveda, Board of Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa, Board of Ethics and Registration, Medical Assessment and Rating Board).
Process for recognition of medical qualifications granted by Indian and foreign institutions.
Maintenance and updating of the National Register and State Registers.
Procedures for granting permission for the establishment of new medical institutions.
Process for assessment and rating of medical institutions.
Procedure for making rules and regulations.
administration: The Central Government, through the Ministry of AYUSH, plays a significant role in the administration of the Act, including constituting the Commission, appointing its members, and providing grants. The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine and its Autonomous Boards are responsible for day-to-day administration and implementation.
important_notes: Different dates can be appointed for the commencement of different provisions of the Act.
The Act establishes a National Commission for Indian System of Medicine which supersedes previous regulatory bodies.
The Act aims to ensure transparency, accountability, and quality in medical education and practice of Indian System of Medicine.

A key provision is the establishment of National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test, National Exit Test, Post-Graduate National Entrance Test, and National Teachers’ Eligibility Test for Indian System of Medicine.

title: The Public Gambling Act, 1867
purpose: To provide for the punishment of public gambling and the keeping of common gaming-houses in specified regions.
scope: Applies to cities, towns, suburbs, railway stations, and places within a three-mile radius of railway stations within the areas specified in the Act, which have been extended by the State Government. Sections 13 and 17 have a broader application.

key_definitions.common_gaming_house: Any house, walled enclosure, room, or place where instruments of gaming (cards, dice, tables, etc.) are kept or used for the profit or gain of the person owning, occupying, using, or keeping such place. This includes profit from charges for the use of instruments or the place itself.

main_sections.description: Defines 'Common gaming-house'.
Outlines the procedure and authority for extending the Act's provisions to specific cities, towns, and places.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for owning or keeping, or having charge of, a gaming-house
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for individuals who own, occupy, manage, or assist in conducting a common gaming-house, or advance money for gambling in such a place.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for being found in gaming-house
main_sections.description: Penalizes individuals found in a gaming-house for the purpose of gaming. It also creates a presumption that anyone found in such a place during gaming was there for that purpose.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter and authorise police to enter and search
main_sections.description: Grants authority to Magistrates and police officers to enter and search suspected gaming-houses, take persons into custody, and seize instruments of gaming, money, and other articles.

main_sections.section_title: Finding cards, etc., in suspected houses, to be evidence that such houses are common gaming-houses
main_sections.description: States that finding gaming instruments in a searched premises or on persons within it is evidence that the place is a common gaming-house and that the persons were there to gamble.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on persons arrested for giving false names and addresses
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties for individuals found in a gaming-house who refuse to give their name and address or provide false information.

main_sections.section_title: On conviction for keeping a gaming-house, instruments of gaming to be destroyed
main_sections.description: Mandates the destruction of instruments of gaming and the forfeiture or return of seized money and articles upon conviction for keeping a gaming-house.

main_sections.section_title: Proof of playing for stakes unnecessary
main_sections.description: Clarifies that proof of playing for stakes is not required to convict someone for keeping or being involved in a common gaming-house.

main_sections.section_title: Magistrate may require any person apprehended to be sworn and give evidence
main_sections.description: Empowers Magistrates to compel apprehended persons to give evidence on oath regarding unlawful gaming or obstruction of entry, without allowing them to claim self-incrimination.
Grants immunity from prosecution to individuals who have been involved in gaming but provide a true and faithful discovery of relevant information as witnesses.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain games
main_sections.description: Exempts games of mere skill from the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Gaming and setting birds and animals to fight in public streets
main_sections.description: Addresses public gambling and the fighting of birds and animals in public streets, allowing for apprehension without warrant.
Specifies the authority responsible for trying offenses under the Act.
Details enhanced penalties for repeat offenders.

main_sections.section_title: Portion of fine may be paid to informer
main_sections.description: Allows a portion of collected fines to be paid to informants.
Governs the process of recovering and applying fines collected under the Act.

important_rules: No person shall own, keep, use, or have charge of a common gaming-house.
No person shall knowingly permit their property to be used as a common gaming-house.
No person shall advance or furnish money for gambling in a common gaming-house.
Persons found in a common gaming-house are presumed to be there for gaming purposes.
Instruments of gaming found in a common gaming-house are evidence of its use for gaming.
Games of mere skill are exempt from the Act.
Public gambling and animal/bird fighting in public streets are prohibited.

penalties: Penalty for owning/keeping/managing a gaming-house: Fine not exceeding two hundred rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding three months.
