Penalty for being found in a gaming-house: Fine not exceeding one hundred rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding one month.
Penalty for giving false name/address: Fine not exceeding five hundred rupees and costs, or imprisonment not exceeding one month.
Enhanced penalty for subsequent offenses.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrates and Police Officers (appointed by the State Government for specific ranks).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through apprehension without warrant in public streets, entry and search of suspected premises, seizure of gaming instruments and money, and prosecution of offenders.

rights: Right to be indemnified for witnesses who make a true discovery of information regarding gaming.
Right to have instruments of gaming destroyed upon conviction for keeping a gaming-house.
Right to potentially have seized money or articles returned if entitled.
duties: Duty to not engage in public gambling or keep a common gaming-house.
Duty to not permit property to be used as a common gaming-house.
Duty to provide accurate name and address when apprehended.
Duty to give evidence when required by a Magistrate regarding unlawful gaming.
obligations: Obligation for owners/occupiers of property not to allow it to be used as a gaming-house.
Obligation for those involved in gaming to provide truthful testimony when summoned as witnesses.

key_procedures: Procedure for extending the Act to specific areas via notification.
Procedure for Magistrates/Police to enter and search suspected gaming-houses, seize evidence, and apprehend individuals.
Procedure for compelling apprehended individuals to testify under oath.
Procedure for the destruction of gaming instruments and forfeiture of money/articles upon conviction.
Procedure for appraising fines and paying portions to informers.
administration: The State Government is responsible for extending the Act and appointing police officers for enforcement. Magistrates are responsible for trying offenses and ordering the destruction of gaming instruments.
important_notes: The Act's application can be extended to various locations by the State Government.
Games of mere skill are explicitly excluded from the scope of this Act.
Possession of gaming instruments in a suspected house creates a presumption of its use as a common gaming-house.

title: THE LIVE-STOCK IMPORTATION ACT, 1898
purpose: To make better provision for the regulation of the importation of live stock and live-stock products, particularly those liable to be affected by infectious or contagious disorders.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Subject matter scope includes the importation of live-stock, live-stock products, and related items such as fodder, dung, stable-litter, clothing, harness, or fittings that have been in contact with live-stock.

key_definitions.infectious or contagious disorders: Includes tick-pest, anthrax, glanders, farcy, scabies, and any other disease or disorder specified by the Central Government via official gazette notification.
key_definitions.live-stock: Includes horses, kine, camels, sheep, and any other animal specified by the Central Government via official gazette notification.
key_definitions.import: The act of bringing or taking, by sea, land, or air into India.
key_definitions.live-stock products: Includes meat and meat products of all kinds (fresh, chilled, frozen), tissue, organs of poultry, pig, sheep, goat; egg and egg powder, milk and milk products; bovine, ovine, and caprine embryos, ova, semen; pet food products of animal origin, and any other animal product specified by the Central Government via official gazette notification.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Live-stock Importation Act, 1898, and specifies its territorial extent.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'infectious or contagious disorders', 'live-stock', 'import', and 'live-stock products'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate importation of live-stock
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to regulate, restrict, or prohibit the import of live-stock and related items into India or specified places if they are liable to infectious or contagious disorders. It also stipulates that notifications under this section operate under the Customs Act, 1962, giving customs officers relevant powers.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate Importation of live-stock products
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to regulate, restrict, or prohibit the import of live-stock products that may affect human or animal health.

main_sections.section_title: Power for State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to make rules for the detention, inspection, disinfection, or destruction of imported live-stock and related items. It also allows for the regulation of officers appointed for these purposes and prescribes penalties for breaches of these rules.

main_sections.section_title: Protection to persons acting under Act
main_sections.description: Provides legal protection to individuals acting in good faith under the provisions of this Act, preventing suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings against them.

important_rules: Rule 1: Importation of live-stock and related items can be regulated, restricted, or prohibited by the Central Government if they are liable to infectious or contagious disorders (Section 3).
Rule 2: Importation of live-stock products can be regulated, restricted, or prohibited by the Central Government if they are liable to affect human or animal health (Section 3A).
Rule 3: State Governments can make rules for the detention, inspection, disinfection, or destruction of imported live-stock and related items (Section 4).

penalties: Breach of rules made by the State Government under Section 4 can be punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for regulating imports via notification) and State Governments (for making rules regarding detention, inspection, etc.). Customs officers are empowered under Section 3(2) and Section 3A(2) in relation to customs law.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the Central Government to regulate, restrict, or prohibit imports. State Governments enforce their rules through appointed officers. Customs authorities enforce import regulations under the purview of the Customs Act, 1962.

rights: Right to protection from legal proceedings for persons acting in good faith under the Act (Section 5).
obligations: Obligation for importers to comply with regulations, restrictions, or prohibitions on the import of live-stock and live-stock products as notified by the Central Government.
Obligation to comply with rules made by State Governments regarding detention, inspection, disinfection, or destruction of imported live-stock and related items.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Central Government issues notifications in the Official Gazette to regulate, restrict, or prohibit the import of live-stock or live-stock products. These notifications have the force of law and are enforced by customs authorities.

Procedure 2: State Governments make rules for the management of imported live-stock, including detention, inspection, disinfection, and destruction, and may appoint officers to oversee these procedures.
administration: Central Government (for import regulations) and State Governments (for post-import management rules). Customs authorities are involved in enforcement at entry points.
important_notes: The Act was extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, and Pondicherry with modifications.
The Act was amended in 2001 to include live-stock products.
The Act's applicability to Jammu and Kashmir was omitted.

title: The Prisoners Act, 1900
purpose: To consolidate the law relating to prisoners confined by order of a Court.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. It applies to prisoners confined by order of a court, including those in Presidency-towns and outside thereof. References to prisons are construed to include Reformatory Schools.

key_definitions.Court: Includes a Coroner and any officer lawfully exercising civil, criminal or revenue jurisdiction.
key_definitions.prison: Includes any place which has been declared by the State Government, by general or special order, to be a subsidiary jail.
key_definitions.States: Means the territories to which this Act extends.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Court', 'prison', and 'States'.

main_sections.section_title: Officers in charge of prisons to detain persons duly committed to their custody
main_sections.description: Mandates officers in charge of prisons to receive and detain persons committed to their custody by any Court, as per the exigency of the writ, warrant, or order, until discharged or removed by law.

main_sections.section_title: Officers in charge of prisons to return writs, etc., after execution or discharge
main_sections.description: Requires officers in charge of prisons to return writs, orders, or warrants to the issuing Court after execution or discharge of the person, along with a certificate of execution or reason for discharge.

main_sections.section_title: Warrants, etc., to be directed to Police-officers
main_sections.description: Specifies that writs or warrants for the arrest of any person issued by the High Court in its criminal jurisdiction shall be directed to and executed by a Police officer within the local limits of that jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Power for State Governments to appoint Superintendents of Presidency prisons
main_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to appoint officers authorized to receive and detain prisoners committed to their custody under Part III, referred to as 'the Superintendent'.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of persons sentenced to imprisonment or death by High Court
main_sections.description: Details the process of delivering persons sentenced to imprisonment or death by the High Court to the Superintendent, along with the warrant for execution and subsequent return of the warrant.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of persons sentenced to transportation by High Court
main_sections.description: Outlines the delivery of persons sentenced to transportation by the High Court to the Superintendent for intermediate custody, with transportation commencing from such delivery.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of persons committed by High Court in execution of a decree or for contempt
main_sections.description: Specifies the delivery of persons committed by the High Court for execution of a decree, contempt of court, or any other cause to the Superintendent with the warrant of commitment.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of persons sentenced by Presidency Magistrates
main_sections.description: Details the delivery of persons sentenced to imprisonment or committed for failure to find security by a Presidency Magistrate to the Superintendent, along with the warrant.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of persons committed for trial by High Court
main_sections.description: Describes the delivery of persons committed by a Magistrate or Justice of the Peace for trial by the High Court to the Superintendent, with a warrant directing their production for trial.

main_sections.section_title: Custody pending hearing by High Court under section 350 of the Code of Civil Procedure of application for insolvency
main_sections.description: Allows the High Court to deliver a judgment-debtor to the Superintendent for custody pending the hearing of an insolvency application, subject to security provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of persons arrested in pursuance of warrant of High Court or Civil Court in Presidency-town
main_sections.description: Covers the process of bringing persons arrested under warrants from the High Court or Civil Courts in Presidency-towns before the issuing court, or to the Superintendent for intermediate custody if the court is not sitting.

main_sections.section_title: References in this Part to prisons, etc., to be construed as referring also to Reformatory Schools
main_sections.description: Clarifies that in Part IV, references to prisons or imprisonment also apply to Reformatory Schools or detention therein.

main_sections.section_title: Power for officers in charge of prisons to give effect to sentences of certain Courts
main_sections.description: Grants officers in charge of prisons outside Presidency towns the power to give effect to sentences or orders from certain Courts or tribunals acting under the authority of the Central Government, State Governments, or formerly His Majesty/Crown Representative. Special provisions apply to sentences from Indian States.

main_sections.section_title: Warrant of officer of such Court to be sufficient authority
main_sections.description: States that a warrant under the official signature of an officer of the Courts/tribunals mentioned in Section 15 is sufficient authority for holding a person in confinement or sending them for transportation.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where officer in charge of prison doubts the legality of warrant sent to him for execution under this Part
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for an officer in charge of a prison who doubts the legality or competency of a warrant or order sent for execution under Part IV. They must refer the matter to the State Government.
Concerns the removal of prisoners.

main_sections.section_title: Lunatic prisoners how to be dealt with
main_sections.description: Addresses how lunatic prisoners are to be dealt with.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of places for confinement of persons under sentence of transportation and removal thereto
main_sections.description: Deals with the appointment of places for the confinement of persons sentenced to transportation and their removal to those places.

main_sections.section_title: Release, on recognizance, by order of High Court, of prisoner recommended for pardon
main_sections.description: Describes the release of a prisoner, recommended for pardon, on recognizance by order of the High Court.

important_rules: Officers in charge of prisons must detain all persons duly committed to their custody by any Court, according to the exigency of the writ, warrant, or order, until discharged or removed by law (Section 3).
Officers in charge of prisons must return writs, orders, or warrants to the issuing Court after execution or discharge, with a certificate of execution or reason for discharge (Section 4).
Warrants for arrest issued by the High Court in its criminal jurisdiction must be directed to and executed by a Police officer (Section 5).
State Governments can appoint Superintendents for Presidency prisons to receive and detain prisoners (Section 6).
Persons sentenced by the High Court to imprisonment or death are to be delivered to the Superintendent with a warrant for execution (Section 7).
Persons sentenced to transportation by the High Court are to be delivered to the Superintendent for intermediate custody (Section 8).
Persons committed by the High Court for decree execution, contempt, or other causes are to be delivered to the Superintendent with a warrant (Section 9).
Persons sentenced by Presidency Magistrates or committed for security failure are to be delivered to the Superintendent with a warrant (Section 10).
Persons committed for trial by the High Court are to be delivered to the Superintendent with a warrant for production at trial (Section 11).
Judgment-debtors may be delivered to the Superintendent for custody pending insolvency application hearings (Section 12).
Persons arrested under warrants from the High Court or Civil Courts in Presidency-towns are to be brought before the court or delivered to the Superintendent for intermediate custody (Section 13).
Officers in charge of prisons outside Presidency towns can give effect to sentences from certain authorized Courts/tribunals (Section 15).
A warrant from an authorized officer of certain Courts/tribunals is sufficient authority for holding a person in confinement or for transportation (Section 16).
If an officer doubts the legality of a warrant, they must refer it to the State Government (Section 17).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officers in charge of prisons, Police officers, State Governments, High Courts, Presidency Magistrates, Civil Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the execution of warrants and orders by designated authorities, the detention and transfer of prisoners as per legal provisions, and reference of legal doubts to the State Government.

rights: Right to be detained according to the exigency of a valid writ, warrant, or order (Section 3).
Right to be discharged or removed in due course of law (Section 3).
Right to be brought before the issuing Court without delay if arrested under certain warrants (Section 13(1)).
Right to be presented before the court at the next sitting if delivered to the Superintendent for intermediate custody (Section 13(2)).
duties: Duty of officers in charge of prisons to receive and detain persons duly committed to their custody (Section 3).
Duty of officers in charge of prisons to return writs, etc., after execution or discharge (Section 4).
Duty of Police officers to execute warrants issued by the High Court (Section 5).
Duty of the Superintendent to receive and detain prisoners committed to their custody (Section 6).
Duty of the Superintendent to produce prisoners for trial as required by the Court (Section 11).
Duty of the Superintendent to detain judgment-debtors in safe custody as ordered (Section 12).
Duty to refer doubts about warrant legality to the State Government (Section 17).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the exigency of any writ, warrant, or order of commitment (Section 3).
Obligation to be delivered to the Superintendent as per court orders (Sections 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12).
Obligation to be brought before the issuing Court or presented at the next sitting if arrested (Section 13).

key_procedures: Procedure for detaining prisoners: Officer in charge of prison receives and detains persons committed by any Court as per writ, warrant, or order until discharged (Section 3).
Procedure for returning writs: After execution or discharge, the officer in charge returns the writ to the issuing Court with a certificate of execution or reason for discharge (Section 4).
Procedure for delivery of sentenced prisoners by High Court: High Court delivers sentenced persons to the Superintendent with a warrant (Section 7).
Procedure for delivery of persons for trial: Persons committed for trial are delivered to the Superintendent with a warrant for production at the criminal session (Section 11).

Procedure for arrested persons in Presidency-towns: Arrested persons are brought before the issuing court or delivered to the Superintendent for intermediate custody if the court is not sitting (Section 13).
Procedure for doubts on warrant legality: If an officer doubts a warrant's legality, they refer the matter to the State Government (Section 17).
administration: State Governments (for appointing Superintendents and receiving references on warrant legality), High Courts, Presidency Magistrates, Civil Courts, Officers in charge of prisons, Police officers.
important_notes: The Act has been amended and extended to various territories over time, and some parts have been omitted or repealed (as indicated by footnotes and omitted sections).
References to 'prisons' and 'imprisonment' in Part IV include Reformatory Schools and detention therein (Section 14).
Certain sections, particularly Part V concerning penal servitude, have been omitted.
Parts IX has been repealed.

title: The Works of Defence Act, 1903
purpose: To provide for imposing restrictions upon the use and enjoyment of land in the vicinity of works of defence in order that such land may be kept free from buildings and other obstructions, and for determining the amount of compensation to be made on account of such imposition.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It covers land in the vicinity of works of defence or sites intended for such works. The scope includes geographical areas designated as 'Districts' for military purposes and any area declared a 'District' by the Central Government for the purposes of the Act.

key_definitions.land: Includes benefits to arise out of land, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.
key_definitions.person interested: Includes all persons claiming an interest in compensation to be made on account of the imposition of restrictions upon the use and enjoyment of land under this Act. A person is deemed interested in land if they are interested in an easement affecting the land.
key_definitions.District: One of the Districts into which India is, for military purposes for the time being, divided; it includes a Brigade area which does not form part of any District, and any area which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare to be a District.
key_definitions.Central Officer Commanding the District: The officer for the time being in command of the forces in a District.
key_definitions.Commanding Officer: The officer for the time being in command of a work of defence.
key_definitions.Collector: Includes any officer specially appointed by the Central Government to perform the functions of a Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.Court: A principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction, unless the Central Government has appointed a special judicial officer within any specified local limits to perform the functions of the Court under this Act.
key_definitions.maintain: When used in relation to a house or other construction, does not include the doing of any act necessary for keeping such house or construction until the making of the award or until the exercise of demolition powers in case of emergency, in the state in which it was at the time of the publication of the notice.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act as 'The Works of Defence Act, 1903' and specifies its extent to the whole of India.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'land', 'person interested', 'District', 'Central Officer Commanding the District', 'Commanding Officer', 'Collector', 'Court', 'maintain', and defines who is 'entitled to act' in certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to laws not in force, or any functionary not in existence, in any area
main_sections.description: Clarifies how references to laws not in force or functionaries not in existence in a specific area should be interpreted in relation to that area.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration and notice that restrictions will be imposed
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Central Government to declare the necessity of imposing restrictions on land near works of defence. It includes publication in the Official Gazette and public notice of the declaration and a sketch plan.

main_sections.section_title: Power to do preliminary Acts after publication of notice
main_sections.description: Grants authority to designated officers and their workmen to enter land after notice publication for surveying, taking levels, digging, setting out boundaries, marking levels, and clearing obstacles if necessary.

Requires the authorized officer to pay or tender payment for any damage caused during preliminary acts and provides for the final decision of the Collector or chief revenue officer in case of disputes over compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Further powers exercisable after publication of notice
main_sections.description: Details the powers to enter and demolish buildings, cut trees, remove banks, make drains, and level land after notice publication, subject to certain conditions regarding the timing of these actions relative to the award and the possibility of exercising these powers in emergencies or for contraventions.

Specifies the types of restrictions that can be imposed on land within a certain distance from works of defence, including prohibitions on altering ground levels and maintaining or erecting buildings or other constructions without written approval and prescribed conditions.

important_rules: Rule 1: After the publication of the notice under section 3(2), designated officers and their workmen may enter and survey any land, take levels, dig the sub-soil, and do other acts to determine if and what restrictions should be imposed. They can also set out boundaries and mark them, even cutting down crops, fences, or jungle if necessary for the survey, provided proper notice is given for dwelling-house enclosures.

Rule 2: The officer conducting preliminary acts must pay or tender payment for any damage caused. Disputes regarding the sufficiency of compensation are to be referred to the Collector or chief revenue officer for a final decision.

Rule 3: After the declaration and public notice, authorized officers and their workmen can demolish buildings, cut trees, remove banks, make drains, level land, and clear it, subject to not destroying evidence of property boundaries. These powers cannot generally be exercised before an award is made (section 12) or after six months from the award, unless in case of emergency or to remove contraventions.

Rule 4: Restrictions imposed from and after the publication of notice under section 3(2) can include prohibition of ground-level variations and maintenance, erection, addition to, or alteration of buildings and constructions above ground without written approval and prescribed conditions, within a specified distance from the work of defence.

penalties: Section 36: Mentions penalties, but the details are not provided in the excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Designated officers authorized by the Central Government, the Collector, and Magistrates (as per section 37).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of restrictions, demolition of constructions, and legal proceedings initiated by designated authorities. Section 37 states that Magistrates are to enforce the terms of the Act.

rights: Right to compensation for damage caused during preliminary acts (Section 5).
Right to receive compensation for imposition of restrictions on land use and enjoyment.
Right to have compensation determined by a Collector or Court.
Right to have compensation apportioned among interested persons (Part IV).
Right to have deposited compensation invested appropriately, especially for persons incompetent to alienate land (Sections 32, 33).
Right to appeal to a Court regarding compensation (Part III).
duties: Duty to allow authorized officers and workmen to enter and survey land for imposition of restrictions (Section 4).
Duty to comply with restrictions imposed on the use and enjoyment of land (Section 7).
Duty to make statements as to names and interests when required (Section 10).
Duty to attend inquiries and produce documents when summoned (Section 15).
Duty to make compensation payments or deposits (Section 31).
obligations: Obligation to pay compensation for damage caused during preliminary acts.
Obligation to adhere to restrictions on land use and enjoyment around works of defence.
Obligation to provide information regarding land interests when requested.
Obligation to comply with summons for inquiries and document production.
Obligation to pay or deposit compensation as determined.

key_procedures: Declaration and Notice of Restrictions: Central Government declares necessity, publishes in Official Gazette, and gives public notice with a sketch plan (Section 3).
Preliminary Acts: Authorized officers may survey land, take levels, dig, set out boundaries, and clear obstacles after notice publication (Section 4).
Payment for Damage: Compensation for damage during preliminary acts is paid or tendered, with disputes settled by the Collector (Section 5).
Imposition of Restrictions and Demolition: Authorized officers can demolish buildings, clear land, etc., after notice publication, subject to timing and emergency provisions (Section 6).
Inquiry and Award: Collector conducts an inquiry and makes an award determining compensation (Sections 12-17).
Reference to Court: Parties dissatisfied with the award can refer the matter to a Court (Sections 18-28).
Apportionment of Compensation: Details of apportionment are specified, and disputes are addressed (Sections 29-30).
Payment of Compensation: Compensation is paid or deposited in Court, with provisions for investment of funds (Sections 31-34).
administration: The Central Government (for declarations and authorization), the Collector (for inquiries, awards, and dispute resolution), designated officers authorized by the Central Government, and Magistrates for enforcement.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India.
The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, and Pondicherry.
The definition of 'land' is broad and includes benefits arising from land and permanently attached things.
The definition of 'person interested' includes those with claims to compensation and those interested in easements.
The 'Collector' can be any officer specially appointed by the Central Government.
The 'Court' can be a principal Civil Court or a special judicial officer appointed by the Central Government.
Provisions exist for persons 'entitled to act' on behalf of others who may be under a disability (e.g., minors, married women, lunatics), with limitations on receiving compensation money.
Demolition powers under Section 6 can be exercised in case of emergency or to remove contraventions of the Act, even outside the usual timeframes.
Section 38 states that completion of imposition of restrictions is not compulsory, but compensation must be awarded if not completed.
Section 39 allows for demolition of part of a house or building and imposition of restrictions on part of land.
Section 40 grants exemption from stamp duty and fees for documents made under the Act.
Section 41 provides for notice in case of suits for acts done in pursuance of the Act.
Section 43 details appeals in proceedings before the Court.

title: THE EXPLOSIVE SUBSTANCES ACT, 1908
purpose: To further amend the law relating to explosive substances.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to citizens of India outside India. It deals with offenses related to explosive substances and special category explosive substances.

key_definitions.explosive_substance: Includes any materials for making any explosive substance; any apparatus, machine, implement or material used, or intended to be used, or adapted for causing, or aiding in causing, any explosion in or with any explosive substance; and any part of any such apparatus, machine or implement.
key_definitions.special_category_explosive_substance: Includes RDX, PETN, HMX, TNT, LTPE, composition exploding (CE) (2, 4, 6 phenyl methyl nitramine or tetryl), OCTOL (mixture of HMX and TNT), plastic explosive kirkee-1 (PEK-1) and RDX/TNT compounds, other similar explosives and combinations thereof, remote control devices causing explosion, and any other substance specified by the Central Government by notification.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and its application to citizens of India outside India.
Defines 'explosive substance' and 'special category explosive substance'.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for causing explosion likely to endanger life or property
main_sections.description: Details the punishment for unlawfully and maliciously causing an explosion with an explosive substance or a special category explosive substance that is likely to endanger life or cause serious injury to property.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for attempt to cause explosion, or for making or keeping explosive with intent to endanger life or property
main_sections.description: Outlines the punishment for attempting to cause an explosion, conspiring to cause an explosion, or making or possessing any explosive substance with the intent to endanger life or cause serious injury to property.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for making or possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances
main_sections.description: Specifies the punishment for making or possessing any explosive substance or special category explosive substance under circumstances that give rise to a reasonable suspicion of unlawful intent, unless a lawful object can be shown.
States that any person who procures, counsels, aids, abets, or is accessory to the commission of any offense under this Act shall be punished with the same punishment provided for the offense.
Prohibits courts from proceeding to the trial of any person for an offense against this Act except with the consent of the District Magistrate.

important_rules: Any person who unlawfully and maliciously causes an explosion with an explosive substance likely to endanger life or cause serious injury to property shall be punished with imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment of not less than ten years, and a fine.

Any person who unlawfully and maliciously causes an explosion with a special category explosive substance likely to endanger life or cause serious injury to property shall be punished with death or rigorous imprisonment for life, and a fine.

Any person who unlawfully and maliciously attempts to cause an explosion, conspires to cause an explosion, or makes or possesses an explosive substance with the intent to endanger life or cause serious injury to property shall be punished with imprisonment for life or up to ten years, and a fine.

Any person who makes or possesses a special category explosive substance with intent to endanger life or cause serious injury to property shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for life or up to ten years, and a fine.

Any person making or possessing an explosive substance or special category explosive substance under suspicious circumstances, without demonstrating a lawful object, faces imprisonment up to ten years or rigorous imprisonment for life (for special category), and a fine.

penalties: Imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, and fine (for causing explosion with explosive substance).
Death, or rigorous imprisonment for life, and fine (for causing explosion with special category explosive substance).

Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine (for attempt to cause explosion or for making/keeping explosive with intent, with explosive substance).

Rigorous imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine (for attempt to cause explosion or for making/keeping explosive with intent, with special category explosive substance).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine (for making or possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances with explosive substance).

Rigorous imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine (for making or possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances with special category explosive substance).
Punishment provided for the offense for abettors.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Magistrate (for consent to trial)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Courts proceed with trials upon consent from the District Magistrate.

duties: Individuals must not unlawfully and maliciously cause explosions or possess explosive substances with intent to endanger life or property.
Individuals making or possessing explosive substances must be able to demonstrate a lawful object for such actions.

key_procedures: Any person accused of an offense under this Act requires the consent of the District Magistrate for a court to proceed with their trial.
administration: Central Government (specified for defining special category explosives)
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various territories including Goa, Daman and Diu, Pondicherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Lakshadweep, and the State of Sikkim with modifications or as per specific notifications.
The definition of 'explosive substance' is broad and includes materials, apparatus, and implements related to explosions.

title: THE DESTRUCTION OF RECORDS ACT, 1917
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law providing for the destruction or other disposal of certain documents in the possession or custody of Courts and Revenue and other public officers.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. (Subject to State Amendments, e.g., Karnataka Act 3 of 1963 which further excludes territories specified in clause (a) and clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 7 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956). The Act applies to documents in the possession or custody of Courts, Revenue Courts and officers, and any other public officers.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent. It also includes a State Amendment for Karnataka.
This section concerning definitions has been repealed.

main_sections.section_title: Power to certain authorities to make rules for disposal of documents.
main_sections.description: Empowers specific authorities (High Courts, Chief Controlling Revenue-authority, State Governments or authorized officers, Central Government or authorized officers) to make rules for the disposal, by destruction or otherwise, of documents not of sufficient public value to justify their preservation. It also specifies the approval process for these rules.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of former rules for disposal of documents.
main_sections.description: Deems rules and orders made before the enactment of this Act for the disposal of documents by public officers, even if not under the previous Act (Destruction of Records Act, 1879), to have had the force of law and states that such rules will continue in force until superseded.
States that the Act does not authorize the destruction of any document that is required by any law in force to be kept and maintained.
This section concerning repeals has been repealed by the Repealing Act, 1927.

important_rules: Rules for the disposal of documents not of sufficient public value can be made by specified authorities (High Courts, Chief Controlling Revenue-authority, State Government or authorized officers, Central Government or authorized officers).
Rules made by High Courts, Chief Controlling Revenue-authorities, or State Government authorized officers require the previous approval of the State Government.
Rules made by Central Government authorized officers require the previous approval of the Central Government.
The Act does not permit the destruction of documents that are legally mandated to be preserved.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities specified in Section 3, including High Courts, Chief Controlling Revenue-authority, State Governments, and the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the making and enforcement of rules for the disposal of documents by the specified authorities.

rights: Right of specified authorities to make rules for document disposal.
Right to preserve documents legally mandated to be kept.
duties: Duty of authorities to manage and dispose of documents appropriately.
Duty to comply with rules made under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to not destroy documents that are legally required to be maintained.

key_procedures: Authorities specified in Section 3 can make rules for the disposal of documents not of sufficient public value.
These rules are subject to approval by the relevant State or Central Government.
Documents that are legally required to be kept and maintained are exempt from destruction under this Act.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implies administration through the relevant judicial, revenue, and government departments whose documents are covered.
important_notes: The Act has been modified as on 3rd December, 2018, indicating amendments and updates.
Section 2 (Definitions) and Section 6 (Repeals) have been repealed.
The Schedule (Repeal of Enactments) has also been repealed.
Various territorial extensions and amendments (e.g., Goa, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, Pondicherry, Karnataka) are noted, impacting the Act's application.
For the definition of Chief Controlling Revenue-authority, reference is made to the General Clauses Act, 1897.

title: The International Monetary Fund and Bank Act, 1945
purpose: To implement the International Monetary Fund and Bank Agreements drawn up at the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference held at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, in July, 1944. This includes the establishment and operation of the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The act's subject matter scope pertains to the implementation of agreements related to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD).

key_definitions.Fund Agreement: An agreement for the establishment and operation of an international body to be called the International Monetary Fund.
key_definitions.Bank Agreement: An agreement for the establishment and operation of an international body to be called the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
key_definitions.International Bank: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
key_definitions.Reserve Bank: The Reserve Bank of India, which shall be the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the International Fund and International Bank.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The International Monetary Fund and Bank Act, 1945', its extent to the whole of India, and that it comes into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Payments to International Fund and Bank
main_sections.description: Authorizes payments out of the Consolidated Fund of India for subscriptions, sums payable, charges, and implementation of guarantees to the International Fund and International Bank, as per their respective agreements. It also allows the Central Government to create and issue non-interest bearing, non-negotiable notes or other obligations to these institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Reserve Bank to be depository for International Fund and Bank
main_sections.description: Designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the International Fund and International Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Reserve Bank to use, receive, acquire, etc., special drawing rights on behalf of Central Government
main_sections.description: Empowers the Reserve Bank to manage special drawing rights of the Central Government in the International Fund, including using, receiving, acquiring, holding, transferring, or operating them.

Grants the Central Government or the Reserve Bank the authority to require any person to furnish detailed information essential for complying with requests from the International Fund. It also deems officers and persons receiving such information as public servants and specifies conditions for prosecutions related to furnishing information.

main_sections.section_title: Certain provisions of Agreements to have force of law
main_sections.description: Declares that certain provisions of the Fund and Bank Agreements, as set out in the Schedule, shall have the force of law in India. It includes a proviso regarding the import of goods and exemption from duties and taxes.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, for the effective implementation of the provisions set out in the Schedule and for carrying out the Act's purposes. It also includes provisions for laying such rules before Parliament.

important_rules: Rule: Exchange contracts contrary to member's exchange control regulations, maintained consistently with the Agreement, shall be unenforceable in any member's territories (as per paragraph (b) of section 2 of Article VIII of the Fund Agreement).

Rule: The International Fund shall possess full juridical personality, including the capacity to contract, acquire and dispose of property, and institute legal proceedings (as per SECTION 2 of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).
Rule: The Fund, its property, and assets shall enjoy immunity from all forms of judicial process, except when expressly waived by the Fund (as per SECTION 3 of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).

Rule: Property and assets of the Fund shall be immune from search, requisition, confiscation, expropriation, or any other form of seizure by executive or legislative action (as per SECTION 4 of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).
Rule: The archives of the Fund shall be inviolable (as per SECTION 5 of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).

Rule: To the extent necessary for carrying out activities, all property and assets of the Fund shall be free from restrictions, regulations, controls, and moratoria (as per SECTION 6 of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).
Rule: Official communications of the Fund shall be accorded the same treatment as those of other members (as per SECTION 7 of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).

Rule: Governors, executive directors, alternates, and officers/employees of the Fund shall be immune from legal process for acts performed in their official capacity, with certain exceptions (as per SECTION 8 of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).

Rule: The Fund, its assets, property, income, operations, and transactions shall be immune from all taxation and customs duties. The Fund shall also be immune from liability for collecting or paying any tax or duty (as per SECTION 9(a) of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).

Rule: No tax shall be levied on salaries and emoluments paid by the Fund to non-local citizen executive directors, alternates, officers, or employees (as per SECTION 9(b) of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).

Rule: No taxation of any kind shall be levied on obligations or securities issued by the Fund, including dividends or interest, under specific discriminatory or jurisdictional conditions (as per SECTION 9(c) of Article IX of the Fund Agreement).
Rule: No tax of any kind shall be levied on special drawing rights or on operations or transactions in special drawing rights (as per ARTICLE XXI (b) of the Fund Agreement).

penalties: Prosecution under sections 176 or 177 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) for failing to furnish required information under section 4, with no defense allowed for asserting that more detail was essential than required.
No prosecution for an offense related to required information under section 4 can be instituted without the previous sanction of the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and Reserve Bank of India (for information gathering and enforcement of rules).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By requiring individuals to furnish specific information necessary for compliance with IMF requests, and through legal proceedings related to the furnishing of such information. The Central Government can also make rules to give effect to the Act.

rights: Right of the Central Government to call for information from any person.
Right of officers and persons receiving information under section 4 to be deemed public servants.
Right of the Central Government to make rules for the Act's implementation.
Privileges and immunities for the International Fund and its personnel as specified in the Fund Agreement (which have the force of law).
Privileges and immunities for the International Bank and its personnel as specified in the Bank Agreement (which have the force of law).
duties: Duty of any person required by order in writing to furnish detailed information to comply with such an order.
Duty of officers and persons to act as public servants when receiving information under section 4.
Duty to comply with rules made by the Central Government under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to make payments to the International Fund and Bank as specified in section 2.
Obligation to comply with information requests from the Central Government or Reserve Bank under section 4.

key_procedures: Procedure for making payments to the International Fund and Bank, requiring appropriation by Parliament and payment from the Consolidated Fund of India.
Procedure for the Reserve Bank to act as a depository for currency holdings.
Procedure for the Reserve Bank to manage special drawing rights.
Procedure for the Central Government or Reserve Bank to require information from individuals.
Procedure for making rules by the Central Government, including laying them before Parliament for modification or annulment.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act was originally an Ordinance (No. 47 of 1945) and was converted into an Act by Act 25 of 1959.
Amendments have been made over time, particularly concerning references to Articles and paragraphs within the Fund and Bank Agreements, and dates of effect.
Section 6, which dealt with the amendment of section 17 of the Indian Securities Act, 1934 (Act 2 of 1934), has been repealed.
The Act has been extended to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu.
Provisions of the Fund and Bank Agreements set out in the Schedule have the force of law, with provisos concerning customs duties and subsequent sales.
The immunities and privileges granted to the Fund and Bank do not exempt them from duties or taxes that form part of the price of goods sold or are charges for services rendered.

title: THE ARMED FORCES (EMERGENCY DUTIES) ACT, 1947
purpose: To enable duties in connection with vital services to be imposed in an emergency on the Armed Forces.
scope: This Act applies to persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Air Force Act, 1950, or the Navy Act, 1957, when employed upon or in connection with a declared vital service in a State. The Act's application has been extended to various territories over time.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its territorial application.

Empowers the Central Government to declare specified services as vital to the community, and makes it a duty for persons subject to the Army, Air Force, or Navy Acts to obey commands related to employment in such services.

Validates commands given between September 30, 1946, and the commencement of the Act, relating to vital services, but prohibits punishment for not obeying such commands if the person was not subject to punishment under the relevant Acts.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any person subject to the Army Act, 1950, Air Force Act, 1950, or Navy Act, 1957, must obey commands given by a superior officer in relation to a declared vital service.
Rule 2: Commands given in relation to vital services are deemed lawful within the meaning and for the purposes of the Army Act, 1950, Air Force Act, 1950, or Navy Act, 1957.

penalties: No specific penalties are detailed in the provided text. However, Section 3 states that no person shall be punished *by reason only of his not having obeyed* certain past commands validated by the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for declarations) and superior officers (for issuing commands). The enforcement of obedience to commands falls under the existing disciplinary provisions of the Army Act, Air Force Act, and Navy Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through commands issued by superior officers to personnel subject to the specified Armed Forces Acts, with obedience enforced by those Acts.

rights: Right to have commands related to vital services deemed lawful.
duties: Duty to obey commands given by a superior officer in relation to employment upon or in connection with a declared vital service.
obligations: Obligation to serve in declared vital services as directed by superior officers.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Central Government declares a specified service in a State to be of vital importance by notification in the Official Gazette.
Procedure 2: The declaration remains in force for one month initially but can be extended by subsequent notifications.
Procedure 3: Upon declaration, personnel subject to the Army, Air Force, or Navy Acts must obey commands related to the specified service.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act was originally applicable to 'Armed Forces of the Crown' but the words 'of the Crown' were omitted by the A.O. 1950.
The scope of the Act has been extended to various regions and states over time.
Amendments have been made to reference current versions of the Army, Air Force, and Navy Acts.
Section 3 provides a specific condition regarding punishment for past commands.

title: THE CENSUS ACT, 1948
purpose: To provide for certain matters in connection with the taking of census.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The Act facilitates the Central Government's declaration to take a census in the whole or any part of the territories to which the Act extends.

key_definitions.premises: Any land, building or part of a building and includes a hut, shed or other structure or any part thereof.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.vehicle: Any vehicle used or capable of being used for the purpose of road transport, whether propelled by mechanical power or otherwise.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Census Act, 1948' and states that it extends to the whole of India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'premises', 'prescribed', and 'vehicle'.
Empowers the Central Government to declare its intention to take a census in any part of India by notification in the Official Gazette.
Details the appointment of a Census Commissioner and Directors of Census Operations by the Central Government, and census officers by the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Staff of every local authority to be made available for taking census
main_sections.description: Mandates local authorities to make their staff available for census-related duties when directed by the Central Government or its authorized authority.

main_sections.section_title: Status of census authorities as public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Census Commissioner, Directors of Census Operations, and all census officers as public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Discharge of duties of census-officers in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies that certain individuals in charge of forces, institutions, or establishments (like military officers, prison superintendents, hotel managers, railway officers) shall perform census duties for persons under their command or in their care, and are deemed to have committed an offense under Section 187 of the IPC if they refuse.

main_sections.section_title: Power to call upon certain persons to give assistance
main_sections.description: Authorizes District Magistrates or other appointed authorities to call upon landowners, local authority members, and factory/firm staff to assist in taking the census, making them public servants while so engaged.

main_sections.section_title: Requisitioning premises, of vehicles, etc., for taking of a census
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to requisition premises, vehicles, vessels, or animals needed for census purposes.
Outlines the procedure for paying compensation for requisitioned premises or vehicles/vessels/animals, including provisions for arbitration in case of disputes over the amount or entitlement.
Allows the Central Government to order individuals to furnish information related to property intended for requisitioning or for determining compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of entry into and inspection of premises, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers authorized persons to enter and inspect premises, vehicles, vessels, or animals for census-related purposes, including determining the need for requisitioning or ensuring compliance.
Provides for the summary eviction of persons remaining in possession of requisitioned premises in contravention of an order.
Details the process of releasing requisitioned premises and returning possession to the rightful owner or claimant.

main_sections.section_title: Asking of questions and obligation to answer
main_sections.description: Requires individuals to answer truthfully and to the best of their knowledge all questions asked by a census-officer relevant to the census.
Specifies penalties for various offenses related to the census, including refusing to answer questions, obstructing census officers, and making false statements.

main_sections.section_title: Records of census not open to inspection of admissible in evidence
main_sections.description: States that records of the census shall not be open to inspection by any person and shall not be admissible as evidence in any civil, criminal, or revenue proceeding.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including the appointment of census staff, the collection and publication of census data, and the requisitioning of property.

important_rules: Individuals must answer all questions asked by a census-officer truthfully and to the best of their knowledge (Section 8).
Occupiers of premises must permit census officers access and the affixing of numbers (Section 9).
Occupiers or managers of premises must fill up the census schedule accurately (Section 10).
Certain authorities (military, prison, educational institution, hotel managers, etc.) have a duty to perform census officer duties for persons under their charge (Section 6).
Local authorities must make their staff available for census duties when directed (Section 4A).
The Central Government can requisition premises, vehicles, vessels, or animals for census purposes (Section 7A).
Compensation must be paid for requisitioned property (Section 7B).

penalties: Refusal to answer questions or providing false answers (Section 11).
Obstructing a census officer in the discharge of their duty (Section 11).
Disclosing information collected during the census (Section 11).
Contravention of orders regarding requisitioning (Section 7H).
Refusing or neglecting to perform duties directed under Section 6 (deemed an offense under Section 187 of the Indian Penal Code).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and State Governments, through appointed census authorities (Census Commissioner, Directors of Census Operations, census officers, District Magistrates).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of census staff, the power to call for assistance, the requisitioning of property, and penalties for non-compliance. Prosecutions require sanction from the Central Government (Section 12).

rights: Right to receive compensation for requisitioned property (Section 7B).
Right to refer compensation disputes to arbitration (Section 7B).
duties: Duty of individuals to answer census questions truthfully (Section 8).
Duty of occupiers to permit access and affixing of numbers (Section 9).
Duty of occupiers or managers to fill up census schedules (Section 10).
Duty of certain authorities to perform census duties for persons under their charge (Section 6).
Duty of local authorities to provide staff for census (Section 4A).
Duty of persons to provide assistance when called upon by authorities (Section 7).
obligations: Obligation to cooperate with census officers.
Obligation to comply with requisitioning orders.
Obligation for owners of requisitioned property to allow lawful use and for persons to vacate such premises.

key_procedures: Declaration of intention to take a census by the Central Government (Section 3).
Appointment of census staff (Section 4).
Requisitioning of premises, vehicles, etc., by the Central Government (Section 7A).
Determination and payment of compensation for requisitioned property (Section 7B).
Obtaining information for requisitioning and compensation (Section 7C).
Entry into and inspection of premises for census purposes (Section 7D).
Eviction from requisitioned premises (Section 7E).
Release of premises from requisition (Section 7F).
Collection and collation of census data by census officers.
Grant of statistical abstracts (Section 17).
administration: The Central Government and State Governments, through the Census Commissioner, Directors of Census Operations, and various census officers.
important_notes: The Act was originally intended for the Provinces and Acceding States but has been adapted over time to apply to the whole of India, with specific omissions or adaptations for regions like Jammu and Kashmir.
The taking of a census can be temporarily suspended in municipalities under other laws for mode of taking census (Section 16).
Sanction is required for prosecutions under the Act (Section 12).
Certain offenses related to census taking are made cognizable and triable summarily (Section 13A).
Census records are not open to inspection and are not admissible in evidence (Section 15).
Protection of service interests of census staff is provided (Section 15A), as is protection for action taken in good faith (Section 15B).

title: The Seaward Artillery Practice Act, 1949
purpose: To provide facilities for carrying out seaward artillery practice.
scope: The Act extends to all States with a sea coast. It also applies to vessels registered in India or belonging to persons domiciled in India, regardless of their location. The scope also covers the sea and adjoining shores within a 'notified area'.

key_definitions.notified area: Any part of the area of the sea and the shores adjoining that area which may be specified by notification under section 3.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.seaward artillery practice: Artillery practice or coastal firing towards the sea, whether within or beyond territorial waters, and includes air armament practice.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes any ship, boat, country craft or any other description of vessel.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as 'The Seaward Artillery Practice Act, 1949', its territorial extent (all States with a sea coast), and its application (including vessels registered in or owned by persons domiciled in India).
This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'notified area', 'prescribed', 'seaward artillery practice', and 'vessel'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to authorise seaward artillery practice
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to authorize seaward artillery practice by notification in the Official Gazette, specifying the area and duration. It also mandates the publication of the notification's substance in local newspapers and other prescribed manners, with a minimum 14-day interval between notification and practice.
Allows the Central Government to delegate the power to issue notifications under section 3 to specified State Governments.

main_sections.section_title: Powers exercisable for purposes of seaward artillery practice
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers of forces engaged in authorized seaward artillery practice. These include prohibiting or restricting the use of the notified area by vessels, taking measures to prevent unauthorized entry, and carrying out practice with lethal missiles. The Officer Commanding can also declare a danger zone, requiring the Collector to prohibit entry and remove persons or property.

States that compensation is payable for any damage to person or property, or interference with rights or privileges, arising from seaward artillery practice authorized under the Act, including expenses incurred for protection.

Details the procedure for assessing compensation. The Collector deputes Revenue Officers to assess claims, conduct local investigations, and disburse compensation on the spot. It also outlines the appeals process to the Collector and states that the Collector's decision is final. No fees are charged for claims or appeals.

Defines offenses related to seaward artillery practice, such as obstructing practice, unauthorized entry into camps or danger zones, or interfering with practice apparatus. Penalties include a fine up to twenty rupees or imprisonment up to fifteen days, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under this Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder. It also exempts the Central and State Governments from liability for damages caused in good faith.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules to give effect to the Act. These rules can cover the manner of notification publication, regulating the use of notified areas, compensation procedures and rates, and any other prescribed matters. Rules must be laid before Parliament for approval or modification.

important_rules: Rules may be made to regulate the use of the notified area for seaward artillery practice to ensure public safety and minimize inconvenience to inhabitants.
Rules may specify minimum rates for compensation for removal from danger zones and the general procedure for making claims, granting compensation, and filing appeals.
Rules can provide principles for assessing compensation.
The Central Government may make different rules for different States or areas.
Any rule made under section 9 must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days and is subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.

penalties: Fine which may extend to twenty rupees or with imprisonment which may extend to fifteen days, or with both, for offenses such as wilful obstruction, unauthorized entry into camps or danger zones, or interference with practice apparatus.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, through authorized forces engaged in practice and the Collector of the district.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification of authorized practice areas and periods, directions prohibiting or restricting use of the area, removal from danger zones, and prosecution for offenses.

rights: Right to compensation for damage to person or property or interference with rights or privileges arising from seaward artillery practice.
Right to be heard by a Revenue Officer when claims for compensation are being assessed.
Right to appeal to the Collector against a Revenue Officer's decision on compensation.
duties: Duty of persons engaged in practice to ensure no unauthorized person enters the notified area.
Duty of the Officer Commanding to declare danger zones and ensure removal of persons and property from them.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to publish notifications in the Official Gazette and local newspapers.
Obligation to pay compensation for damages and interference caused by seaward artillery practice.

key_procedures: Authorization of Seaward Artillery Practice: Central Government issues a notification specifying the area and period, publishes it in the Official Gazette, and informs the public through local newspapers and other prescribed means.
Exercise of Powers: Forces engaged in practice can prohibit or restrict use of the notified area, prevent unauthorized entry, and declare danger zones.
Compensation Assessment and Disbursement: Revenue Officers assess claims on-site, hear claimants, determine compensation, and disburse it. Appeals can be made to the Collector.
Rule Making: Central Government makes rules, which are then laid before Parliament for approval or modification.
administration: Central Government (and delegated State Governments)
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Pondicherry, and the Union territory of Lakshadweep with modifications.
The Collector's decision on compensation appeals is final, and no suit lies in civil courts regarding matters decided by the Collector.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.
A minimum interval of fourteen days must be maintained between the publication of the notification and the commencement of seaward artillery practice.

title: The Prize Competitions Act, 1955
purpose: To provide for the control and regulation of prize competitions.
scope: Applies to the States of Andhra, Bombay, Madras, Orissa, Uttar Pradesh, Hyderabad, Madhya Bharat, Patiala and East Punjab States Union, Saurashtra, and all Part C States.  It also extends to Dadar and Nagar Haveli, Goa, Daman and Diu, and the Union territory of Pondicherry. The act covers prize competitions involving puzzles based on letters, words, or figures, where prizes are offered.

key_definitions.licensing_authority: An officer or authority appointed by the State Government to grant licences under the Act.
key_definitions.money: Includes a cheque, postal-order, or money-order.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prize_competition: Any competition, regardless of its name, where prizes are offered for the solution of a puzzle based on the building up, arrangement, combination, or permutation of letters, words, or figures.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Prize Competitions Act, 1955. It specifies the geographical extent of the Act and the process for its commencement through a Central Government notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'licensing authority', 'money', 'prescribed', and 'prize competition'.
Clarifies that references to 'printing' include writing and other visible representations, and that 'distribution' includes distribution within and outside the territories to which the Act extends.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of prize competitions where the prize offered exceeds one thousand rupees a month
main_sections.description: Prohibits the promotion or conduct of prize competitions where the total value of prizes in a month exceeds one thousand rupees, and limits the number of entries to two thousand per competition.

main_sections.section_title: Licensing of prize competitions where the prize offered does not exceed one thousand rupees a month
main_sections.description: Mandates that prize competitions where the total monthly prize value does not exceed one thousand rupees must be licensed in accordance with the Act and its rules.

Outlines the procedure for obtaining a licence, including written application, inquiry by the licensing authority, reasons for refusal, and prescribed fees, period, conditions, and form of the licence.

main_sections.section_title: Promoters of prize competitions to keep accounts and submit the same to the licensing authority
main_sections.description: Requires promoters or conductors of prize competitions to maintain accounts and submit statements of accounts to the licensing authority in the prescribed form and at prescribed intervals.

main_sections.section_title: Power to cancel or suspend licences
main_sections.description: Grants the licensing authority the power to cancel or suspend a licence after giving the holder an opportunity to be heard, on grounds of breach of conditions or contravention of section 7. Reasons for cancellation or suspension must be recorded and provided to the holder.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for promoting or conducting any prize competition in contravention of the provisions of sections 4 and 5
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties (imprisonment up to three months, fine up to one thousand rupees, or both) for promoting or conducting prize competitions in contravention of sections 4 and 5.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to keep and submit accounts
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties (imprisonment up to one month, fine up to five hundred rupees, or both) for failing to keep or submit accounts as required by section 7, or for submitting false accounts. This does not affect provisions in section 8.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for other offences in connection with prize competitions
main_sections.description: Details penalties (imprisonment up to three months, fine up to five hundred rupees, or both) for various other offences related to prize competitions, including printing/publishing prohibited matter, selling/distributing prohibited documents, advertising prize competitions, and using premises for such activities without a licence or in contravention of the Act.

Addresses offences committed by companies, holding individuals in charge responsible. It includes a proviso for exculpation if the offence was without knowledge or due diligence, and also holds directors or officers liable for offences committed with consent, connivance, or gross neglect.

main_sections.section_title: Power of licensing authority to call for and inspect accounts and documents
main_sections.description: Empowers the licensing authority to require the production of accounts and documents, and to inspect them at reasonable times.

Grants police officers of a certain rank, authorized by the State Government, the power to enter, search, seize, and take into custody individuals and items related to prize competitions conducted in contravention of the Act. Searches are to be conducted as per the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

main_sections.section_title: Forfeiture newspapers and publications containing prize competitions
main_sections.description: Allows the State Government to declare forfeiture of any newspaper or publication containing prize competitions or advertisements that contravene the Act or are not in accordance with a licence.
Provides for appeals to the State Government against decisions of the licensing authority regarding licence refusal, cancellation, or suspension. The State Government's decision is final.

main_sections.section_title: Licensing authority and other officers to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the licensing authority and other officers acting under the Act as public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
Specifies that only Presidency Magistrates or Magistrates of the first class have the jurisdiction to try offences under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under this act
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act or its rules by the licensing authority or government officers.

Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, subject to previous publication and notification in the Official Gazette. This includes specific powers without prejudice to the generality of the provisions.

important_rules: Rule 1: No person shall promote or conduct prize competitions where the total monthly prize value exceeds one thousand rupees, and the number of entries must not exceed two thousand.
Rule 2: Prize competitions with a monthly prize value not exceeding one thousand rupees require a licence.
Rule 3: Promoters must maintain accounts for prize competitions and submit them to the licensing authority.
Rule 4: Licences can be cancelled or suspended for breach of conditions or contravention of accounting provisions.
Rule 5: Specific penalties are prescribed for various contraventions of the Act, including promoting prohibited competitions, failure to submit accounts, and other related offences.
Rule 6: Searches for prize competition-related activities contravening the Act must be conducted according to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

penalties: Imprisonment for up to three months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, for promoting/conducting prize competitions in contravention of sections 4 and 5.
Imprisonment for up to one month, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both, for failure to keep or submit accounts, or for submitting false accounts.

Imprisonment for up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both, for other offences related to prize competitions, such as unauthorized printing, publishing, advertising, or distribution of competition materials.
Companies and their responsible officers are liable for offences committed by the company.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing authority, State Government, Police officers (not below the rank of Sub-Inspector).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through licensing procedures, inspection of accounts, power of entry and search, seizure of offending materials, forfeiture of publications, imposition of penalties (fines and imprisonment), and appellate review by the State Government. Offences are tried by Presidency Magistrates or Magistrates of the first class.

rights: Right to appeal to the State Government against decisions of the licensing authority.
Right to be heard before a licence is cancelled or suspended.
Protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Individuals may be exculpated from company offences if they prove the offence was without their knowledge or they exercised due diligence.
duties: Duty to obtain a licence for prize competitions not exceeding one thousand rupees in monthly prize value.
Duty to keep and submit accounts of prize competitions to the licensing authority.
Duty to comply with the conditions of the licence.
Duty for individuals in charge of companies to prevent offences.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the maximum prize value and entry limits specified in section 4.
Obligation to comply with prescribed application procedures for licences.
Obligation to cooperate with licensing authorities during inspections and inquiries.
Obligation to adhere to search and seizure procedures conducted by authorized police officers.

key_procedures: Applying for a licence: Submit a written application in the prescribed form and manner to the licensing authority.
Licensing authority's process: Conduct inquiry, grant or refuse the licence, and provide reasons for refusal in writing.
Account submission: Promoters must maintain accounts and submit statements of accounts to the licensing authority at prescribed intervals.
Licence cancellation/suspension: Licensing authority must give a reasonable opportunity of being heard and record reasons for cancellation or suspension.
Appeals: File an appeal to the State Government within the prescribed time against decisions of the licensing authority.
Search and seizure: Authorized police officers can enter, search premises, seize items, and take persons into custody if there's suspicion of contravention of the Act, following CrPC procedures.
