Rule making: State Government can make rules subject to previous publication and notification.
administration: State Government (through the licensing authority appointed by it), Central Government (for commencement notification).
important_notes: The Act was enacted based on resolutions passed by State Legislatures under Article 252(1) of the Constitution, indicating a move towards centralized legislation on this matter.
The definition of 'prize competition' is broad and covers various forms of puzzles.
Section 4 places an outright prohibition on prize competitions exceeding a certain prize value per month.
Section 14 clarifies that searches must be conducted in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
Section 17 states that licensing authorities and other officers are deemed public servants, implying they are subject to specific legal protections and responsibilities.

title: THE PRISONERS (ATTENDANCE IN COURTS) ACT, 1955
purpose: To provide for the attendance in courts of persons confined in prisons for obtaining their evidence or for answering a criminal charge.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as per original text, though subsequent notifications extend its application). Applies to civil and criminal courts seeking the attendance of prisoners for evidence or to answer a charge.

key_definitions.confinement in a prison: References to confinement in a prison, by whatever form of words, include references to confinement or detention in a prison under any law providing for preventive detention.
key_definitions.prison: Includes any place declared by the State Government, by general or special order, to be a subsidiary jail; and any reformatory, Borstal institution or other institution of a like nature.
key_definitions.State Government: In relation to a Union territory, means the Administrator thereof.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the process for its commencement via notification by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'confinement in a prison', 'prison', and 'State Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of courts to require appearance of prisoners to give evidence or answer a charge
main_sections.description: Grants power to civil and criminal courts to order the production of prisoners for giving evidence or to answer a charge. Includes provisions for counter-signatures by district judges and district magistrates for subordinate courts.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to exempt certain persons from operation of section 3
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to exempt certain persons or classes of persons from being removed from prison, considering factors like the nature of the offence, likelihood of public disorder, and public interest.
Mandates the officer in charge of a prison to take the prisoner to court as ordered, detain them, and then return them to prison after their examination or when authorized.

main_sections.section_title: Officer in charge of prison when to abstain from carrying out order
main_sections.description: Outlines circumstances under which the officer in charge of a prison may abstain from carrying out an order, such as sickness, being under committal for trial or remand, or if the period of custody would expire before the prisoner could be returned. Provides an exception for criminal courts under specific conditions.

Allows civil courts to issue commissions for the examination of prisoners in prison under specific conditions, particularly when attendance in court is not feasible or the prison is located outside the state or at a significant distance.

main_sections.section_title: Certain provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Code of Civil Procedure to apply
main_sections.description: Specifies that provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, shall apply to the examination of prisoners on commission or otherwise, as far as possible, unless otherwise provided by this Act.

Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including procedures for counter-signatures, fitness declarations, costs, service of process, escort, and other enforcement matters.

Repeals Part IX of the Prisoners Act, 1900, and its schedules. Also provides for the repeal of any corresponding laws in Part B States, with provisions for continuity of actions taken under such repealed laws.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any civil or criminal court can order the appearance of a prisoner if their evidence is material to a pending matter or if they are to answer a criminal charge.
Rule 2: Orders from subordinate civil courts require counter-signature from the district judge; orders from inferior criminal courts require counter-signature from the district magistrate.
Rule 3: The officer in charge of a prison must produce the prisoner to court as ordered and ensure their safe custody and return.

Rule 4: The officer in charge may abstain from carrying out an order if the prisoner is unfit due to sickness, under committal or remand, or if the return journey time exceeds the remaining custody period.
Rule 5: Civil courts can issue commissions for prisoner examination if physical appearance is not feasible or the prison is distant.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (for making rules and exemptions), Courts (for issuing orders), Officer in charge of prison (for executing orders).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders, counter-signatures, and adherence to procedures for prisoner production, detention, and return as detailed in the Act and rules made thereunder.

rights: Right of a court to obtain evidence or hear a charge from a prisoner.
Right of a prisoner to be brought before a court for evidence or to answer a charge.
duties: Duty of the officer in charge of a prison to comply with court orders for prisoner production, unless specific exceptions apply.
Duty of the State Government to consider public order and public interest when exempting persons.
Duty of courts to follow prescribed procedures and obtain necessary counter-signatures.
Duty of the State Government to make rules for effective implementation of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: A court (civil or criminal) identifies the need for a prisoner's presence. A formal order is made in the prescribed form (First or Second Schedule). The order is directed to the officer in charge of the prison. For subordinate courts, the order requires counter-signature.
Procedure 2: Upon receiving the order, the officer in charge of the prison shall arrange for the prisoner to be taken to court, ensure their presence, and then arrange for their return to prison.

Procedure 3: In cases where direct production is not possible, a civil court can issue a commission for the prisoner's examination within the prison, following provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.
Procedure 4: State Governments may make rules regarding the procedure for obtaining counter-signatures, declaring unfitness for removal, costs, service of process, escort, and custody of prisoners.
administration: State Government (for making rules and exemptions), Central Government (for commencement notification).
important_notes: The Act was originally not applicable to the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but subsequent notifications have extended its application.
The Act aims to balance the need for judicial proceedings with the security and management of prisoners.
Provisions exist to prevent the removal of prisoners who are unfit due to sickness or if their removal would cause public disorder.

title: THE ALL-INDIA INSTITUTES OF MEDICAL SCIENCE ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the establishment of All-India Institutes of Medical Sciences.
scope: Applies to the establishment and functioning of All-India Institutes of Medical Sciences across India. The scope has been expanded through amendments to include 'corresponding Institutes' and other newly established Institutes.

key_definitions.corresponding_institute: The Institutes referred to in column (3) of the Table given under section 27A.
key_definitions.existing_institute: The All-India Institute of Medical Sciences established under sub-section (1) of section 3 before the commencement of the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (Amendment) Act, 2012, and located at New Delhi.
key_definitions.fund: The Fund of the Institute referred to in section 16.
key_definitions.institute: The All-India Institute of Medical Sciences established under section 3, and includes corresponding Institutes and other Institutes established on or after the commencement of the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (Amendment) Act, 2012.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Institute.
key_definitions.regulation: A regulation made by the Institute.
key_definitions.rules: A rule made by the Central Government.
key_definitions.society: The society referred to in column (2) of the Table given under section 27A.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'corresponding Institute', 'existing Institute', 'Fund', 'Institute', 'member', 'regulation', 'rules', and 'society'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the Institute
main_sections.description: States that an institution named the All India Institute of Medical Sciences shall be established. It also provides for the establishment of other such Institutes by the Central Government. Every Institute is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the members of every Institute, which include ex-officio members like the Vice-Chancellor of Delhi University (for existing Institute) or a nominated Vice-Chancellor (for other Institutes), Director General of Health Services, Director of the Institute, representatives from the Central Government, Indian Science Congress Association, Indian Universities, and Members of Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Institutes as institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the existing Institute, corresponding Institutes, and any newly established Institutes as institutions of national importance.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of, and vacancies among, members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for members (five years for nominated/elected members, and continuous for ex-officio members). It also details the conditions under which the term of office of an elected member ends, how casual vacancies are filled, and the process for resignation.

Establishes a President for every Institute, nominated by the Central Government from among its members. The President of the existing Institute may also serve as President for other newly established Institutes until separate appointments are made. The President exercises powers as laid down in the Act or prescribed by rules/regulations.

States that the President and members shall receive such allowances as may be prescribed by rules. Provisions are made for the apportionment of allowances when a person is President of multiple Institutes.

Details the procedure for meetings of the Institute. The first meeting is appointed by the Central Government, and subsequent meetings are held as per regulations. The provision for the first meeting does not apply to the existing Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Governing Body and other Committees of the Institute
main_sections.description: Establishes a Governing Body for every Institute, constituted from its members. The Governing Body acts as the executive committee. The President of the Institute is the Chairman of the Governing Body. The Act also allows the Institute to constitute standing and ad hoc committees.

Provides for a chief executive officer, designated as the Director of the Institute, who is appointed by the Institute, subject to rules made by the Central Government. Special provisions exist for the appointment of the first Director of newly established Institutes.

important_rules: All-India Institutes of Medical Sciences are to be established by the Central Government.
Each Institute is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The composition of the Institute includes ex-officio members, government representatives, nominated experts, and members of Parliament.
Institutes are declared as institutions of national importance.
Members have a term of office of five years, with provisions for ex-officio members and casual vacancies.
A President is nominated for each Institute by the Central Government.
The Governing Body acts as the executive committee of the Institute.
The Central Government has control over the Institutes.

rights: The Institute has the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The Institute can sue and be sued in its own name.
duties: To function in accordance with the Act, rules, and regulations.
To manage its own affairs and discharge its objects and functions.
obligations: To adhere to the control and restrictions prescribed by rules for the constitution of committees.
To ensure that the staff appointed are in accordance with the rules made by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Institute by notification by the Central Government.
Nomination or election of members to the Institute.
Convening and conducting meetings of the Institute as per regulations.
Constitution and functioning of the Governing Body and other committees as per regulations.
Appointment of the Director and other staff of the Institute.
Submission of budget, accounts, and annual reports to the Central Government.
administration: Central Government (specifically mentioned for appointments, notifications, control, rules, and oversight)
important_notes: The Act has been amended significantly by the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (Amendment) Act, 2012 (37 of 2012), which introduced provisions for multiple Institutes, 'corresponding Institutes', and updated definitions and composition.
The Act has been extended to the Union territory Goa, Daman and Diu.

title: The National Highways Act, 1956
purpose: To provide for the declaration of certain highways to be national highways and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to highways declared as national highways, including their appurtenant lands, bridges, culverts, tunnels, causeways, carriageways, fences, trees, posts, and milestones. It also covers the acquisition of land for the development, maintenance, management, or operation of national highways.

key_definitions.competent authority: Any person or authority authorized by the Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, to perform the functions of the competent authority for a specified area.
key_definitions.land: Includes benefits to arise out of land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.
key_definitions.national highways: Highways declared as such by the Central Government, either by inclusion in the Schedule or by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the National Highways Act, 1956, specifies its extent to the whole of India, and outlines the commencement of the Act upon notification by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain highways to be national highways
main_sections.description: Provides for the declaration of highways specified in the Schedule as national highways. It also empowers the Central Government to declare any other highway as a national highway or omit any highway from the Schedule through official notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'competent authority' and 'land'.
Grants the Central Government the power to acquire land for the building, maintenance, management, or operation of national highways through a notification of intention to acquire.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter for survey, etc.
main_sections.description: Authorizes persons authorized by the Central Government to enter land for inspection, survey, measurement, valuation, enquiry, taking levels, digging, setting out boundaries, and marking levels after a notification under section 3A is issued.

Details the procedure for hearing objections from persons interested in land proposed for acquisition, allowing them to object in writing within twenty-one days and be heard by the competent authority.

Outlines the process for declaring land acquired after objections are disallowed or not received. It states that upon publication of the declaration, the land vests absolutely in the Central Government. It also includes provisions for the lapse of the notification if no declaration is published within one year and that the declaration cannot be questioned in court.

Empowers the competent authority to take possession of land that has vested in the Central Government, directing the owner or possessor to surrender it within sixty days. It specifies procedures for enforcement through the Commissioner of Police or Collector if possession is not surrendered.

main_sections.section_title: Right to enter into the land where land has vested in the Central Government
main_sections.description: Grants authorized persons the right to enter land that has vested in the Central Government for the purpose of carrying out works related to national highways.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of amount payable as compensation
main_sections.description: Specifies the process for determining compensation for acquired land, including a public notice for claims, the consideration of market value, damages, and expenses for relocation. It also allows for arbitration if the determined amount is not acceptable.

Details the deposit of determined compensation amounts by the Central Government with the competent authority before taking possession and the subsequent payment to entitled persons. It also addresses disputes over apportionment and interest on excess amounts determined by an arbitrator.

main_sections.section_title: Competent authority to have certain powers of civil court
main_sections.description: Confers civil court powers on the competent authority for summoning persons, examining them on oath, requiring discovery of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, requisitioning public records, and issuing commissions for witness examination.

main_sections.section_title: Land Acquisition Act 1 of 1894 not to apply
main_sections.description: Explicitly states that the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, shall not apply to acquisitions made under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: National highways to vest in the Union
main_sections.description: Declares that all national highways shall vest in the Union and defines 'highways' to include appurtenant lands, structures, fences, trees, and milestones.

main_sections.section_title: Responsibility for development and maintenance of national highways
main_sections.description: Assigns the responsibility for the development and maintenance of national highways to the Central Government, with the power to direct that such functions may also be exercised by State Governments or subordinate authorities.
Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to State Governments regarding the implementation of the Act's provisions within their states.

main_sections.section_title: Fees for services or benefits rendered on national highways
main_sections.description: Allows for the collection of fees for services or benefits provided on national highways.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to enter into agreements for development and maintenance of national highways
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to enter into agreements with other entities for the development and maintenance of national highways.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for mischief by injury to national highway
main_sections.description: Provides for punishment for mischief causing injury to a national highway.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of notifications, rules, etc., before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that notifications, rules, and other documents issued under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any highway specified in the Schedule is declared a national highway.
Rule 2: The Central Government can declare any other highway as a national highway or remove it from the Schedule by notification.
Rule 3: Land can be acquired for the building, maintenance, management, or operation of a national highway after issuing a notification and hearing objections.
Rule 4: Compensation for acquired land must be determined, deposited, and paid to the entitled persons.
Rule 5: The Central Government is responsible for the development and maintenance of national highways, but can delegate these functions.
Rule 6: The Central Government can issue directions to State Governments for the implementation of the Act.

penalties: Punishment for mischief by injury to a national highway (Section 8B).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Competent Authority, Commissioner of Police (in metropolitan areas), Collector of a District (in other areas).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, declarations of acquisition, hearings of objections, determination and deposit of compensation, taking possession of land, and enforcement by police or revenue authorities for surrender of land. Rules made by the Central Government also govern enforcement.

rights: Right of persons interested in land to object to acquisition.
Right to receive compensation for acquired land.
Right to have disputes regarding compensation apportionment referred to civil court.
Right to have compensation determined by an arbitrator if not acceptable.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to develop and maintain national highways.
Duty of the competent authority to hear objections and determine compensation.
Duty to surrender possession of acquired land upon direction.
Duty to deposit determined compensation amounts.
Duty to lay notifications and rules before Parliament.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to publish notifications and declarations for acquisition and to deposit compensation.
Obligation of any person in possession to surrender land upon notice.
Obligation of the competent authority to determine and pay compensation.
Obligation to follow procedures outlined in the Act for land acquisition and compensation.

key_procedures: Procedure for declaring a highway as a national highway (Section 2).
Procedure for acquiring land for national highways: notification of intention, survey, hearing objections, declaration of acquisition, taking possession (Sections 3A-3E, 3F).
Procedure for determining compensation: public notice, inviting claims, determination by competent authority, arbitration if needed (Section 3G).
Procedure for depositing and paying compensation (Section 3H).
Procedure for making rules by the Central Government (Section 9).
Procedure for laying notifications, rules, etc., before Parliament (Section 10).
administration: Central Government, with powers delegated to the Competent Authority, and potentially State Governments or subordinate authorities for development and maintenance functions.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1997 to remove exceptions for parts of highways within municipal areas and to substitute section 3 definitions.
The Act aims to streamline land acquisition for national highways by specifying procedures and excluding the applicability of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for acquisitions under this Act.

title: THE HINDU SUCCESSION ACT, 1956
purpose: To amend and codify the law relating to intestate succession among Hindus.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to any person who is a Hindu by religion (including followers of Brahmo, Prarthana, Arya Samaj, Virashaiva, Lingayat), Buddhist, Jaina, or Sikh. Also applies to any person not a Muslim, Christian, Parsi, or Jew by religion, unless it can be proven they would not have been governed by Hindu law or custom otherwise. Excludes members of Scheduled Tribes unless the Central Government directs otherwise. Does not apply to properties regulated by the Indian Succession Act, 1925 due to the Special Marriage Act, 1954, or to certain estates descending to a single heir by covenant or pre-enactment legislation, or the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilagam Estate and Palace Fund.

key_definitions.agnate: One person is said to be an 'agnate' of another if the two are related by blood or adoption wholly through males.
key_definitions.aliyasantana law: The system of law applicable to persons governed by the Madras Aliyasantana Act, 1949, or by customary aliyasantana law.
key_definitions.cognate: One person is said to be a 'cognate' of another if the two are related by blood or adoption but not wholly through males.
key_definitions.custom: Any rule which, having been continuously and uniformly observed for a long time, has obtained the force of law among Hindus in any local area, tribe, community, group or family, provided it is certain, not unreasonable or opposed to public policy, and in the case of family rules, not discontinued.
key_definitions.usage: Signifies any rule which, having been continuously and uniformly observed for a long time, has obtained the force of law among Hindus in any local area, tribe, community, group or family, provided it is certain, not unreasonable or opposed to public policy, and in the case of family rules, not discontinued.
key_definitions.heir: Any person, male or female, who is entitled to succeed to the property of an intestate under this Act.
key_definitions.intestate: A person is deemed to die intestate in respect of property of which he or she has not made a testamentary disposition capable of taking effect.
key_definitions.marumakkattayam law: The system of law applicable to persons governed by specific Madras, Travancore, or Cochin Acts concerning inheritance traced through the female line, but does not include aliyasantana law.
key_definitions.nambudri law: The system of law applicable to persons governed by the Madras Nambudri Act, 1932, the Cochin Nambudri Act, or the Travancore Malayala Brahmin Act.
key_definitions.related: Means related by legitimate kinship. Illegitimate children are deemed related to their mother and each other, and their legitimate descendants are related to them and each other.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial extent.

Defines who the Act applies to based on religion and provides explanations for who is considered Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina, or Sikh by religion. Also specifies that it does not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes unless notified by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including agnate, aliyasantana law, cognate, custom, usage, full blood, half blood, uterine blood, heir, intestate, marumakkattayam law, nambudri law, and related. It also clarifies gender interpretation.

States that any text, rule, interpretation of Hindu law, custom, or usage in force before the Act ceases to have effect if provision is made in the Act. It also states that any other law in force before the Act ceases to apply to Hindus if it is inconsistent with the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Section 6(1): On and from the commencement of the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, in a Joint Hindu family governed by Mitakshara law, a daughter becomes a coparcener by birth, has the same rights and liabilities as a son, and any reference to a Hindu Mitakshara coparcener includes a daughter.

Section 6(3): Where a Hindu dies after the commencement of the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, their interest in a Joint Hindu family property governed by Mitakshara law devolves by testamentary or intestate succession, not survivorship. The coparcenary property is deemed divided as if a partition had taken place, with daughters receiving the same share as sons, and shares allotted to pre-deceased children.

Section 6(4): After the commencement of the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, no court shall recognize the right to proceed against a son, grandson, or great-grandson for a debt solely based on the pious obligation under Hindu law.

Section 4: Any text, rule, or interpretation of Hindu law or custom in force before the Act ceases to apply if provided for in the Act. Other laws inconsistent with this Act also cease to apply to Hindus.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the courts and relevant government bodies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and application of the Act's provisions in matters of succession and property division. The Act's overriding effect ensures its provisions are prioritized over conflicting laws or customs.

rights: Daughter's right to be a coparcener by birth (Section 6(1)).
Daughter's right to the same share in coparcenary property as a son (Section 6(3)).
Right of surviving children of pre-deceased sons or daughters to inherit their share (Section 6(3)).
Right to absolute ownership of property for a female Hindu (implied by Section 14, not fully provided).
obligations: Daughter's liabilities in respect of coparcenary property are the same as a son's (Section 6(1)).
Obligation to discharge ancestral debts by sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons (previously based on pious obligation, now modified by Section 6(4)).

key_procedures: Devolution of interest in coparcenary property: Section 6 outlines the procedure for division of coparcenary property upon the death of a Hindu Mitakshara coparcener, including the allotment of shares to daughters and children of pre-deceased coparceners.
Application of the Act: Section 2 details the applicability of the Act based on religion and specific exclusions.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but would typically fall under the Ministry of Law and Justice or similar governmental bodies responsible for legal affairs.
important_notes: Section 6(1) and 6(3) were significantly amended by the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 (39 of 2005), which came into effect on September 9, 2005.
Section 6(1) proviso: Dispositions or alienations, including partitions or testamentary dispositions, that took place before December 20, 2004, are not affected by the amendments to Section 6.
Section 6(4) proviso: The new rules regarding the pious obligation for debt discharge do not affect debts contracted before the commencement of the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005.
Section 6(5): The amendments to Section 6 do not apply to partitions effected before December 20, 2004.
The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted from Section 1(2) by Act 34 of 2019.

title: The Probation of Offenders Act, 1958
purpose: To provide for the release of offenders on probation or after due admonition and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. The Act comes into force in a State on a date appointed by the State Government, with different dates for different parts of the State. Applies to individuals found guilty of certain offences.

key_definitions.Code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (5 of 1898)
key_definitions.probation officer: An officer appointed to be a probation officer or recognised as such under section 13.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the procedure for its commencement in different states.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Code', 'probation officer', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of court to release certain offenders after admonition.
main_sections.description: Empowers courts to release offenders guilty of specific offences (punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both, under IPC or other laws) after due admonition, provided they have no previous convictions and the court deems it expedient.

main_sections.section_title: Power of court to release certain offenders on probation of good conduct.
main_sections.description: Authorizes courts to release offenders (not punishable with death or life imprisonment) on probation of good conduct by entering into a bond, with or without sureties, for a period not exceeding three years, with conditions to keep peace and be of good behaviour.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on imprisonment of offenders under twenty-one years of age.
main_sections.description: Mandates that courts shall not sentence persons under twenty-one years of age to imprisonment for an offence unless satisfied that dealing with them under sections 3 or 4 is not desirable, and requires recording reasons for imprisonment.

Specifies the categories of individuals who can serve as probation officers, including those appointed or recognized by the State Government, or persons provided by recognized societies, or exceptional cases approved by the court.

important_rules: Rule: Offenders released under section 4 must have a fixed place of abode or regular occupation in the jurisdiction or where they are likely to live.
Rule: Before releasing an offender on probation of good conduct (section 4), the court must consider the report of the probation officer.
Rule: Courts may impose additional conditions for supervision orders, such as residence and abstention from intoxicants, to prevent repetition of offences.
Rule: A person dealt with under section 3 or 4 shall not suffer disqualification attaching to a conviction, unless they are subsequently sentenced for the original offence.

penalties: Imposition of a penalty not exceeding fifty rupees for the first failure to observe bond conditions, without prejudice to the continuance of the bond.
If the penalty is not paid, the offender may be sentenced for the original offence.
Sentence for the original offence if an offender fails to observe bond conditions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts empowered to try and sentence offenders, and High Courts or other appellate/revisional courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Issuance of warrants for arrest or summons to offenders and sureties if bond conditions are breached; courts can remand offenders to custody or grant bail; imposition of penalties or sentencing for the original offence.

rights: Right of the offender to be heard before variation of probation conditions.
Right of the offender to receive a copy of the supervision order.
Right to have previous conviction considered only if it's under section 3 or 4 of this Act for the purpose of admonition.
Right to not suffer disqualification from conviction if dealt with under section 3 or 4 (unless subsequently sentenced for the original offence).
duties: Duty of the offender to appear and receive sentence when called upon during the probation period.
Duty of the offender to keep the peace and be of good behaviour during the probation period.
Duty of the offender to observe conditions specified in the supervision order.
Duty of the offender to enter into a bond with or without sureties.
obligations: Obligation of the court to consider the probation officer's report before releasing an offender on probation.
Obligation of the court to record reasons for sentencing an offender under twenty-one years of age to imprisonment.
Obligation of the court to explain the terms and conditions of a supervision order to the offender.
Obligation of probation officers to report to the court if an offender fails to observe bond conditions.

key_procedures: Procedure for releasing an offender after admonition: Court finds person guilty, considers circumstances and character, no previous conviction, and deems it expedient; court releases after admonition instead of sentencing or probation.

Procedure for releasing an offender on probation of good conduct: Court finds person guilty (offence not punishable with death/life imprisonment), considers circumstances and character, deems it expedient; court directs release on entering a bond, with or without sureties, to appear and receive sentence when called upon, keep peace and good behaviour.

Procedure for offenders failing to observe bond conditions: Court has reason to believe of failure; issues warrant or summons; court may remand to custody or grant bail; court may sentence for original offence or impose a penalty if it's a first failure.
administration: State Government (for appointing probation officers and bringing the Act into force), Courts, District Magistrate.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India. Previous references to Jammu and Kashmir have been omitted.
The report of a probation officer is confidential, but the court may communicate its substance to the offender and offer an opportunity to produce relevant evidence.
Courts can vary conditions of probation bonds, including extending or diminishing duration, or altering/inserting conditions, after giving the offender and surety an opportunity to be heard.

title: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
purpose: To provide for the prevention and control of water pollution and the maintaining or restoring of wholesomeness of water, for the establishment of Boards for the prevention and control of water pollution, and to confer upon these Boards powers and functions relating thereto.
scope: Applies to the States of Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tripura, and West Bengal, and Union territories. It can also apply to other states that adopt the Act by resolution.

key_definitions.board: The Central Board or a State Board.
key_definitions.central_board: The Central Pollution Control Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.member: A member of a Board and includes the chairman thereof.
key_definitions.occupier: In relation to any factory or premises, the person who has control over the affairs of the factory or the premises, and includes, in relation to any substance, the person in possession of the substance.
key_definitions.outlet: Includes any conduit pipe or channel, open or closed, carrying sewage or trade effluent or any other holding arrangement which causes, or is likely to cause, pollution.
key_definitions.pollution: Such contamination of water or such alteration of the physical, chemical or biological properties of water or such discharge of any sewage or trade effluent or of any other liquid, gaseous or solid substance into water (whether directly or indirectly) as may, or is likely to, create a nuisance or render such water harmful or injurious to public health or safety, or to domestic, commercial, industrial, agricultural or other legitimate uses, or to the life and health of animals or plants or of acquatic organisms.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act by the Central Government or, as the case may be, the State Government.
key_definitions.sewage_effluent: Effluent from any sewerage system or sewage disposal works and includes sullage from open drains.
key_definitions.sewer: Any conduit pipe or channel, open or closed, carrying sewage or trade effluent.
key_definitions.state_board: A State Pollution Control Board constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.state_government: In relation to a Union territory means the Administrator thereof appointed under article 239 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.stream: Includes river; water course (whether flowing or for the time being dry); inland water (whether natural or artificial); sub-terranean waters; sea or tidal waters to such extent or, as the case may be, to such point as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify in this behalf.
key_definitions.trade_effluent: Includes any liquid, gaseous or solid substance which is discharged from any premises used for carrying on any industry, operation or process, or treatment and disposal system, other than domestic sewage.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its application to certain states and Union territories, and defines its commencement date.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'pollution', 'stream', 'sewage effluent', 'trade effluent', etc.
Provides for the constitution of the Central Pollution Control Board, its composition, and its corporate status.
Provides for the constitution of State Pollution Control Boards, their composition, and their name.
Outlines the various functions and responsibilities of the Central Board.
Outlines the various functions and responsibilities of the State Boards.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to restrict the application of the Act to certain areas.
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to restrict the application of the Act to specific areas.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take samples of effluents and procedure to be followed in connection therewith.
main_sections.description: Details the power of authorized personnel to take samples of effluents and the procedure that must be followed.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on use of stream or well for disposal of polluting matter, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of any stream or well for the disposal of polluting matter.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on new outlets and new discharges.
main_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on establishing new outlets for sewage or trade effluents and new discharges into water bodies.

main_sections.section_title: Failure to comply provisions of section 20 or directions issued thereunder.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for failing to comply with provisions of section 20 or directions issued under it.
Defines penalties for specific acts that contravene the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of section 25 or section 26.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravening the provisions of sections 25 or 26, which deal with new outlets and existing discharges.

important_rules: Rule: No person shall knowingly cause or permit to remain in any stream any poisonous, noxious, or       polluting matter, or any such substance as is likely to render such water damnified to public health or       to destroy or injuriously affect the nature of the streams. (Section 24)

Rule: No person shall, without the previous consent of the State Board, establish or take any steps to       establish any outlet for the discharge of any sewage or trade effluent, or any disposal system which       discharges or is likely to discharge any sewage or trade effluent into a stream or sewer or       on land.

Rule: No person shall, after the commencement of this Act, make any new discharge of sewage or       trade effluent into any stream or sewer or on land, or through a new outlet, or by means of a new       outlet, unless the sewage or trade effluent is in all such respects as the State Board may       specify.

penalties: Penalty for failure to comply with provisions of section 20 or directions issued thereunder.
Penalty for failure to comply with provisions of section 32, or directions issued under section 33 or section 33A.
Penalty for contravention of section 24.
Penalty for contravention of section 25 or section 26.
Penalty for contravention by Government Department.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Boards are primarily responsible for enforcement within their respective states, with the Central Board providing guidance and oversight. Courts and potentially the National Green Tribunal are involved in adjudicating offenses.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, sample collection, issuance of directions, imposing penalties, and legal action via courts.

rights: Right to receive clean water, free from harmful pollution.
duties: Duty to prevent and control water pollution.
Duty to comply with directions and regulations issued by the Boards.
Duty to obtain consent from the State Board before discharging effluents.
obligations: Obligation not to discharge polluting matter into streams or wells.
Obligation to maintain wholesomeness of water.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining consent from the State Board for establishing new outlets or making new discharges of sewage or trade effluent.
Procedure for taking samples of effluents, including the method and documentation.
Procedure for appeals against refusal or withdrawal of consent by the State Board.
Procedure for taking emergency measures in case of sudden pollution of a stream or well.
Procedure for making applications to courts for restraining apprehended pollution.
administration: The Central Government and the respective State Governments, through the Central Pollution Control Board and State Pollution Control Boards.
important_notes: The Act was adopted by several states through resolutions passed under article 252 of the Constitution.
The National Green Tribunal has been introduced as an appellate authority for certain decisions.
The Act allows for the establishment of Joint Boards for the prevention and control of water pollution in more than one State.

title: THE DISTURBED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the speedy trial of certain offences in certain areas and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to areas declared as 'disturbed areas' where there is extensive disturbance of public peace and tranquillity. It also applies to 'scheduled offences' committed in such areas.

key_definitions.Code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.disturbed area: An area declared as a disturbed area under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.period of disturbance: The period during which an area is declared a disturbed area for the purposes of section 3.
key_definitions.scheduled offence: An offence specified in the Schedule, which is part of, arises out of, or is connected with a disturbance as referred to in section 3.
key_definitions.Special Court: A Special Court constituted under section 4 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date from which it comes into force.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Code', 'disturbed area', 'period of disturbance', 'scheduled offence', and 'Special Court'.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of an area as disturbed area
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions and procedure for a State Government to declare an area as a disturbed area due to extensive disturbance of public peace and tranquillity caused by differences between religious, racial, language, or regional groups, castes, or communities. It also specifies the duration for which the area remains disturbed and allows for amendments.

Details the process of constituting Special Courts for the speedy trial of scheduled offences in disturbed areas. It specifies the composition of the court (a single judge), the appointment process by the High Court upon request from the State Government, and the qualifications and age limits for judges.
Establishes the exclusive jurisdiction of Special Courts to try scheduled offences committed in disturbed areas. It also allows Special Courts to try other connected offences in the same trial.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of Special Courts
main_sections.description: Governs the procedure and powers of Special Courts, including taking cognizance of scheduled offences, exercising powers of a Court of Session, trying offences summarily, and tendering pardons. It adapts the Code of Criminal Procedure for trials before Special Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Power to transfer cases to regular courts
main_sections.description: Empowers a Special Court to transfer a case to a regular court if it determines that the offence is not a scheduled offence.
Confers upon the High Court the powers of appeal and revision in relation to proceedings before a Special Court, as if the Special Court were a Court of Session.

Declares that the provisions of this Act override the Code of Criminal Procedure and other laws, except where specifically provided. It clarifies that the Code of Criminal Procedure applies to proceedings before a Special Court, with Special Courts being deemed as Courts of Session.

Exempts the jurisdiction and procedure applicable to courts or authorities under laws relating to naval, military, or air forces, or other armed forces of the Union. It clarifies that for the purposes of such laws, a Special Court is deemed to be a court of ordinary criminal justice.

important_rules: A State Government can declare an area as a disturbed area if there is extensive disturbance of public peace and tranquillity.
Disturbed areas are declared for specific periods, with initial periods not exceeding three months, extendable by the State Government.
Special Courts are constituted by the State Government for the speedy trial of scheduled offences in disturbed areas.
Judges of Special Courts must be qualified to be High Court judges or have served as Sessions Judges/Additional Sessions Judges for at least one year.
Scheduled offences committed in a disturbed area during the period of disturbance are triable exclusively by the Special Court constituted for that area.
Special Courts can also try offences connected with scheduled offences.
Scheduled offences are cognizable.
Special Courts have the powers of a Court of Session and can try offences summarily under certain conditions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (for declaration of disturbed areas and constitution of Special Courts), High Court (for appointment of judges and exercise of appellate/revisionary powers), Special Courts (for trial of offences).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment and functioning of Special Courts, and the application of procedures under the Act and the Code of Criminal Procedure.

rights: Right to speedy trial of scheduled offences in disturbed areas.
duties: Duty of the State Government to maintain public peace and tranquillity.
Duty of the Special Court to try scheduled offences speedily.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the procedures laid down in the Act and the Code of Criminal Procedure for trials before Special Courts.

key_procedures: Declaration of a disturbed area by the State Government via notification.
Constitution of Special Courts by the State Government.
Appointment of judges for Special Courts by the High Court.
Trial of scheduled offences by Special Courts, with powers analogous to Courts of Session.
Summary trial of certain scheduled offences by Special Courts.
Transfer of cases not falling under scheduled offences to regular courts.
Appeal and revision to the High Court.
administration: State Governments and High Courts play a role in the administration of the Act. The Central Government appoints the commencement date. Various departments of State Governments would be involved in maintaining law and order leading to declaration of disturbed areas.
important_notes: The Act was originally extended to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but this exception has been omitted.
State amendments from Karnataka and Manipur have been noted, potentially altering the scope or specific provisions of the Act within those states.
The Act's provisions override conflicting provisions in the Code of Criminal Procedure and other laws.
The Act does not affect the jurisdiction or procedure under laws relating to armed forces.

title: The Coconut Development Board Act, 1979
purpose: To provide for the development under the control of the Union of the coconut industry and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The scope of 'coconut industry' excludes the coir industry and industries that manufacture products from coconut oil (including by-products).

key_definitions.Board: The Coconut Development Board established under section 4.
key_definitions.Chairman: The non-executive Chairman of the Board appointed under section 4(4)(a).
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer of the Board appointed under section 7(1).
key_definitions.coconut: The fruit of the coconut palm, including green coconut, ripe coconut, and copra. 'Coconut palm' means the coconut tree, Cocos Nucifera Linn.
key_definitions.coconut industry: Does not include the coir industry or an industry from which products (including by-products) out of coconut oil are manufactured.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board, including the Chairman.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of India), and the date it comes into force as appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to take control of the coconut industry.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'Chairman', 'Chief Executive Officer', 'coconut', 'coconut industry', 'member', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and constitution of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the establishment of the Coconut Development Board, its corporate status, perpetual succession, common seal, power to acquire property, and its composition. The Board consists of a non-executive Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, ex-officio members from government departments and research institutes, members of Parliament, representatives of State Governments where coconut is grown, representatives of other States and Union Territories, representatives of coconut growers and the processing industry, and other nominated members.

main_sections.section_title: Allowances payable to Chairman and members
main_sections.description: States that the Chairman and members of the Board shall receive such allowances as fixed by the Central Government.
Outlines the procedure for resignation by members (other than ex-officio members) by giving written notice to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Officers of the Board and other staff
main_sections.description: Describes the appointment of a Chief Executive Officer, Chief Coconut Development Officer, and a Secretary, along with their powers, duties, salaries, allowances, and conditions of service. The Board can also appoint other officers and employees.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision for transfer of employees to the Board
main_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of officers and employees from the Directorate of Coconut Development to the Board, ensuring their terms and conditions of service are not less favorable.
Mentions the power of the Board to appoint committees.
Outlines the functions of the Board.
Deals with the dissolution of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Grants and loans by the Central Government
main_sections.description: Describes the provision of grants and loans to the Board by the Central Government.
Concerns the establishment and constitution of a Coconut Development Fund.
Details the borrowing powers of the Board.
Covers the accounts and audit procedures for the Board.
Allows the Central Government to issue directions to the Board.
Mandates the submission of returns and reports by the Board to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith by the Board or its members.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under this Act.
Grants the Board the power to make regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires that rules and regulations made under the Act be laid before Parliament.

important_rules: The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of holding property and entering into contracts.
The Central Government may issue directions to the Board.
The Board must submit returns and reports to the Central Government.
Actions taken in good faith by the Board or its members are protected.
The Central Government has the power to make rules and the Board has the power to make regulations under the Act.

rights: Officers deputed by the Central Government have the right to attend Board meetings and participate in discussions but not to vote.
Persons associated with the Board for assistance or advice have the right to participate in discussions relevant to their association but not to vote.
duties: The Board has the duty to work towards the development of the coconut industry.
Officers and employees of the Board shall not undertake work unconnected with their duties without Central Government permission.
obligations: The Board is obligated to manage its finances and accounts appropriately and be subject to audit.
The Board is obligated to comply with directions issued by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Coconut Development Board by Central Government notification.
Appointment of Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, and other members of the Board.
Transfer of employees from Directorate of Coconut Development to the Board with options and protection of service conditions.
Submission of returns and reports to the Central Government.
Making of rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Board.
Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament.
administration: The Central Government, through its relevant ministries and departments, exercises control and oversight over the Coconut Development Board. The Board itself is administered by its Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, and other officers.
important_notes: The Act was amended by Act 22 of 2021, significantly changing clauses related to the appointment of the Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, and other members of the Board.
The Act specifies that the Chief Executive Officer shall not be below the rank of Joint Secretary to the Government of India.
The Act makes special provisions for the transfer of employees from the Directorate of Coconut Development to the Board, with emphasis on protecting their service conditions.

title: THE INDUSTRIAL FINANCE CORPORATION (TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING AND REPEAL) ACT, 1993
purpose: To provide for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking of the Industrial Finance Corporation of India to and in a company to be formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, and also to repeal the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948.
scope: This Act applies to the Industrial Finance Corporation of India and the new company formed to take over its undertaking. It covers the transfer of the undertaking, assets, liabilities, and employees, as well as the repeal of the previous Act. The scope is national, concerning a specific financial institution.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette for the transfer of the undertaking.
key_definitions.company: The Industrial Finance Corporation of India Limited, to be formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.corporation: The Industrial Finance Corporation of India established under the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it is deemed to have come into force on October 1, 1992.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Company', and 'Corporation'.

main_sections.section_title: Undertaking of the Corporation to vest in the company
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the undertaking of the Corporation shall be transferred to and vest in the Company.

main_sections.section_title: General effect of vesting of undertaking in the Company
main_sections.description: Details the consequences of the undertaking vesting in the Company, including shareholders becoming shareholders of the Company, the inclusion of all assets and liabilities, the continuation of contracts and deeds, and the continuation of legal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Concession, etc., to be deemed to have been granted to the Company
main_sections.description: Ensures that all fiscal and other concessions, licenses, benefits, privileges, and exemptions granted to the Corporation are deemed to have been granted to the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Tax exemption or benefit to continue to have effect
main_sections.description: Provides that tax exemptions, benefits, and carry-forward of allowances or losses available to the Corporation under the Income-tax Act, 1961, will continue for the Company. It also clarifies that the transfer is not considered a capital gains event for tax purposes.
Ensures that any guarantees given for or in favor of the Corporation will continue to be operative in relation to the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Corporation
main_sections.description: Outlines the terms of employment for the Corporation's employees who join the Company, ensuring continuity of service, remuneration, and benefits. It also addresses situations where employees opt not to join the Company and clarifies that no compensation is payable for the transfer of services. Special provisions are made for retired employees and the management of funds.

main_sections.section_title: Act 18 of 1891 to apply to the books of the Company
main_sections.description: Deems the Company to be a bank for the purposes of the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891.

main_sections.section_title: Shares, bonds and debentures to be deemed to be approved securities
main_sections.description: Declares that the shares, bonds, and debentures of the Company shall be considered approved securities for the purposes of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and the Insurance Act, 1938.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal and saving of Act 15 of 1948
main_sections.description: Repeals the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948, on the appointed day, but makes provisions for the Company to comply with certain sections of the repealed Act regarding annual accounts.

Repeals the Industrial Finance Corporation (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Ordinance, 1993, and states that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The undertaking of the Industrial Finance Corporation of India shall vest in the newly formed Industrial Finance Corporation of India Limited on the appointed day.
Shareholders of the Corporation shall become registered shareholders of the Company.
All contracts, deeds, bonds, and other instruments affecting the Corporation shall continue to be enforceable by or against the Company.
Fiscal and other concessions, licenses, benefits, privileges, and exemptions granted to the Corporation shall be deemed to have been granted to the Company.
Tax exemptions and benefits available to the Corporation under the Income-tax Act, 1961, shall continue for the Company.
Guarantees given to the Corporation shall remain operative in relation to the Company.
Employees of the Corporation (excluding specific management positions) shall become employees of the Company under similar terms and conditions, unless they opt out.
The Company shall be considered a bank for the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891.
The shares, bonds, and debentures of the Company are deemed approved securities for certain Acts.
The Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948, is repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (implied through notifications and appointment of dates)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legal framework established by the Act, including the vesting of the undertaking, the continuation of contracts and legal proceedings, and the repeal of previous legislation. Specific enforcement mechanisms are not detailed in the provided text.

rights: Shareholders of the Corporation have the right to be registered as shareholders of the Company.
Employees have rights to the same tenure, remuneration, terms, conditions, and benefits as they had with the Corporation.
The Company has the right to inherit all assets, powers, authorities, and privileges of the Corporation.
The Company can continue to enforce contracts and legal proceedings.
The Company benefits from existing fiscal and other concessions granted to the Corporation.
The Company benefits from continued tax exemptions and allowances.
The Company benefits from existing guarantees.
duties: The Company has a duty to take over the undertaking of the Corporation.
The Company has a duty to honor existing contracts and liabilities.
The Company has a duty to maintain the terms and conditions of employment for transferred employees.
The Company must comply with provisions of the repealed Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948, regarding annual accounts.
The Company must adhere to provisions related to the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891.
The Company's shares, bonds, and debentures must be treated as approved securities.
obligations: The Company assumes all liabilities and obligations of the Corporation.
Employees continue their obligations to the Company.
The Company is obligated to ensure continuity of benefits for its employees.
The trusts of the provident fund and gratuity fund must continue their functions within the Company.

key_procedures: The Central Government appoints an 'appointed day' via notification in the Official Gazette for the transfer and vesting of the Corporation's undertaking.
The Industrial Finance Corporation of India Limited is formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
On the appointed day, the undertaking of the Corporation automatically transfers to and vests in the Company.
Shareholders of the Corporation are automatically registered as shareholders of the Company.
Employees of the Corporation, unless they opt out within six months, automatically become employees of the Company.
administration: The Central Government plays a key role in appointing the 'appointed day' through notifications. The Companies Act, 1956, is foundational for the formation of the new Company. Specific departmental administration is not explicitly detailed.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 1, 1992.
Officers and employees who opt not to continue with the Company are deemed to have resigned and are not entitled to compensation for the transfer of service.
Directors, Chairman, and Managing Director are not entitled to compensation for loss of office or premature termination of management contracts.
The repeal of the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948, is effective on the appointed day, with saving clauses for specific provisions related to annual accounts.

title: The National Institutes of Technology, Science Education and Research Act, 2007
purpose: To declare certain institutions of technology, science education and research to be Institutions of national importance and to provide for instruction and research in branches of engineering, technology, management, education, sciences and arts, and for the advancement of learning and dissemination of knowledge in such branches, and for certain other matters connected with such institutions.
scope: The Act applies to the institutions mentioned in the First, Second, and Third Schedules, declaring them as Institutions of National Importance. It governs their incorporation, powers, functioning, administration, and the establishment of a Council for coordination. The scope is national, focusing on higher education and research in specified fields.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of an Institute.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board.
key_definitions.Corresponding Institute: The Institute specified in the Schedules corresponding to a society mentioned in the Schedules.
key_definitions.Council: The Council established under sub-section (1) of section 30.
key_definitions.Deputy Director: The Deputy Director of an Institute.
key_definitions.Institute: Any of the Institutions mentioned in the Schedules.
key_definitions.Notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Schedule: Refers to the First, Second, and Third Schedules of the Act.
key_definitions.Society: Any society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, and mentioned in the Schedules.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: Statutes and Ordinances of an Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the National Institutes of Technology, Science Education and Research Act, 2007, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain Institutions as Institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the institutions mentioned in the Schedules as Institutions of national importance.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Institute', 'Council', 'Director', 'Registrar', 'Senate', 'Society', and 'Statutes and Ordinances'.

Declares the Institutes mentioned in the Schedules as bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of suing and being sued. It also incorporates the Bengal Engineering and Science University, Shibpur, as the Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur.

Outlines the consequences of incorporation, including the substitution of 'Institute' for 'society' in other laws and contracts, vesting of property, transfer of rights and liabilities, and continuity of employment for existing staff with provisions for alteration of terms.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of incorporation of Bengal Engineering and Science University, Shibpur
main_sections.description: Details the effects of incorporating the Bengal Engineering and Science University, Shibpur, into the Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur, including property transfer, rights, liabilities, and employment of personnel.

Lists the powers and duties of the Institutes, including providing instruction and research, granting degrees, conferring honorary degrees, fixing fees, managing hostels, supervising students, establishing NCC units, framing Statutes and Ordinances, managing property, receiving grants, co-operating with other institutions, and undertaking consultancy.

main_sections.section_title: Institutes to be open to all races, creeds and classes
main_sections.description: Mandates that Institutes must be open to all individuals regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, and prohibits conditions opposed to this principle in admissions, appointments, or acceptance of bequests.
States that all teaching at Institutes must be conducted in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances.
Designates the President of India as the Visitor of every Institute and grants the Visitor the power to review work, conduct inquiries, and issue directions.
Enumerates the authorities of the Institutes, which typically include the Board of Governors, Senate, and other officers.
Details the composition and establishment of the Board of Governors for each Institute.
Provides for the establishment of a Council to coordinate the activities of the Institutes.
Specifies the functions to be performed by the Council.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders for removing difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with provisions for the transition from existing arrangements to the framework established by the Act.

important_rules: Institutes must provide instruction and research in specified branches of engineering, technology, management, education, sciences, and arts (Section 6(1)(a)).
Institutes are to be open to all persons regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class (Section 7(1)).
No conditions opposed to the spirit of inclusivity can be accepted in bequests or donations (Section 7(2)).
All teaching must be conducted in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances (Section 8).
The President of India is the Visitor of every Institute and has powers of review and inquiry (Section 9).
Institutes cannot dispose of immovable property without prior approval of the Central Government (Section 6(2)).

rights: Right to receive instruction and research opportunities at Institutes.
Rights of employees to hold office under the same tenure, remuneration, and terms as before incorporation, with provisions for alteration and compensation.
Right to be admitted or appointed without discrimination based on race, creed, caste, or class.
duties: Duty of Institutes to provide instruction and research.
Duty of Institutes to be open to all.
Duty to conform to Statutes and Ordinances for teaching.
Duty of the Visitor (President) to review and ensure proper functioning of Institutes.
obligations: Obligations of Institutes to manage property for advancing their objects.
Obligations of Institutes to coordinate with other educational institutions globally.
Obligations to comply with the directions of the Visitor.
Obligation of the Central Government to appoint dates for commencement and potentially new Directors.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Central Government appoints date by notification (Section 1(2)).
Declaration of National Importance: Based on the objects of institutions listed in Schedules (Section 2).
Incorporation: Institutes become bodies corporate (Section 4).
Transfer of property, rights, and liabilities upon incorporation (Sections 5 and 5A).
Framing of Statutes and Ordinances by Institutes (Sections 25, 26, 27, 28).
Visitor's Review and Inquiry: President appoints persons to review and report on Institute's affairs (Section 9(2)).
Central Government's Power to Remove Difficulties: Making orders for smooth implementation (Section 36).
Transitional Provisions for smooth transition (Section 37).
administration: The Central Government plays a significant role in appointing commencement dates, providing grants, approving immovable property disposal, and potentially overseeing the Council. The Institutes themselves are administered by their respective Boards of Governors and other authorities.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2012, 2014, and 2018, with specific insertions and omissions indicated by footnotes, affecting the scope of the schedules and specific sections.
The commencement date for different provisions can be different, as determined by the Central Government (Section 1(2)).
The incorporation of Bengal Engineering and Science University, Shibpur, is a specific transitional provision that occurred with the 2014 amendment.

Any alteration to the tenure, remuneration, terms, and conditions of service of employees of the Bengal Engineering and Science University, Shibpur, must not be to their disadvantage without prior Central Government approval (Section 5A(d)).

title: THE RASHTRIYA RAKSHA UNIVERSITY ACT, 2020
purpose: To establish and declare an institution to be known as the Rashtriya Raksha University as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the Rashtriya Raksha University. Its headquarters are in Gandhinagar, Gujarat. It can establish centers and campuses in other places in India and abroad. It applies to all races, creeds, and classes for admission and teaching.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University referred to in section 17.
key_definitions.affiliated college: An institution recognised as such by the Executive Council in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Statutes made thereunder.
key_definitions.college: An institution maintained by or admitted to the privileges of the University and includes an affiliated college.
key_definitions.distance education system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as, broadcasting, telecasting, internet, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more such modes.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University and includes teachers, other academic and non-academic staff of the University.
key_definitions.University: The Rashtriya Raksha University established under section 4.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Rashtriya Raksha University as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Rashtriya Raksha University as an institution of national importance.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Academic Council, affiliated college, college, distance education system, employee, and University.

Establishes the Rashtriya Raksha University as a body corporate, superseding the Raksha Shakti University. It grants perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract. The headquarters are at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, with provisions for establishing centers and campuses elsewhere.

Details the consequences of the incorporation of the University, including the transfer of references, property, rights, liabilities, and employees from the Raksha Shakti University. It also covers the continuation of academic courses and legal proceedings.

Outlines the objects of the University, which include promoting global standards, providing high standards of learning and research, and advancing education, research, training, and scholarship in policing, security, law enforcement, criminal justice, cyber security, and related areas of internal security. It also aims to build human capital with ideals of citizenship and citizen-centric services.
