Enumerate the powers and functions of the University, including providing instructions and research in various police science and related subjects, designing and conducting courses, holding examinations, granting degrees, providing facilities through distance education, introducing semester and credit systems, obtaining accreditation, establishing centers and laboratories, supervising students, making appointments, cooperating with other institutions, and providing for research and development.

important_rules: The Rashtriya Raksha University shall be established as a body corporate under this Act, named Rashtriya Raksha University, superseding the Raksha Shakti University.
The University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal with the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract.
The University shall be open to all races, creeds, and classes.
The University shall promote global standards and provide dynamic and high standards of learning and research in policing, security, law enforcement, and related areas.
The University shall have the power to plan and prescribe courses of study, hold examinations, grant degrees, and provide facilities through a distance education system.

rights: Employees of the Raksha Shakti University shall hold their office or service in the University with the same tenure, remuneration, terms, and conditions, and with the same rights and privileges as before the Act.
Students pursuing courses in the Raksha Shakti University shall be deemed to have migrated and registered with the University at the same level of course.
duties: The University shall supervise and control the residence and regulate the discipline of students.
The University shall make provisions for research and development in its areas of core competence.
obligations: The University shall be subject to the provisions of this Act.
The University shall comply with the rules made by the Central Government in respect of matters relating to the Governing Body.

administration: Central Government (for making rules and issuing directions, and reviewing work and progress).
important_notes: The Act repeals the Gujarat Act 14 of 2009.
The University is declared an institution of national importance.
The Act provides for transitional provisions for employees and students of the former Raksha Shakti University.

title: THE NATIONAL FORENSIC SCIENCES UNIVERSITY ACT, 2020
purpose: To establish and declare the National Forensic Sciences University as an institution of national importance to facilitate and promote studies and research, and to achieve excellence in the field of forensic science in conjunction with applied behavioural science studies, law, criminology, other allied areas, and technology, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the National Forensic Sciences University. Its geographical scope includes campuses within India and potentially outside India. The subject matter scope covers forensic science, applied behavioral science studies, law, legal studies, criminology, and other allied areas and technology.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University as referred to in section 18.
key_definitions.academic staff: Teachers and such categories of staff as are designated to be academic staff by the Statutes.
key_definitions.affiliated college: An institution recognised as such by the Board of Governors in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Statutes made thereunder.
key_definitions.Board of Governors: The Board of Governors of the University as referred to in section 15.
key_definitions.campus: The campus of the Gujarat Forensic Sciences University situated at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, and that of the Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Sciences situated at Rohini, New Delhi, or such other campus as may be established by the University at any place within India or outside India.
key_definitions.University: The National Forensic Sciences University established under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government in the Official Gazette, allowing for different dates for different provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of National Forensic Sciences University as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the National Forensic Sciences University as an institution of national importance, acknowledging its objectives.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'academic staff', 'affiliated college', 'Board of Governors', 'campus', 'Chancellor', 'college', 'Court', 'Dean', 'department', 'distance education system', 'employee', 'Executive Registrar', 'Finance Committee', 'Fund', 'notification', 'School', 'Statutes', 'Ordinances', 'student', 'teachers', 'University', and 'Vice-Chancellor'.

Establishes the National Forensic Sciences University by merging the Gujarat Forensic Sciences University and the Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Sciences. It declares it as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire property and contract. The headquarters are in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, and campuses include those in Gujarat and New Delhi, with provisions for additional campuses.

Outlines the consequences of the University's incorporation, including deeming references to the previous institutions as references to the new University, the continuation of past appointments and academic distinctions, the applicability of existing statuses, the vesting of properties, the transfer of rights and liabilities, and the continuation of employment for existing staff under similar terms. It also addresses the migration of students and the continuation of legal proceedings.

Enumerates the objectives of the University, including promoting academic learning and practices in forensic science and allied fields, fostering research and applied applications, providing advanced facilities, creating global standards of education and training, and coordinating with governments to improve criminal justice institutions.
This section title indicates that it pertains to financial grants provided by the Central Government to the University.
This section likely deals with the establishment and management of the University's corpus fund.
This section likely details the creation, management, and sources of the University's fund.
This section addresses the procedures for maintaining accounts and conducting audits for the University.
This section introduces the concept of Statutes for the University.
This section explains the process by which Statutes are to be formulated.
This section introduces the concept of Ordinances for the University.
This section explains the process by which Ordinances are to be formulated.
This section establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for the University.

main_sections.section_title: Redressal for debarment from examination and disciplinary action against students
main_sections.description: This section provides mechanisms for redressal concerning debarment from examinations and disciplinary actions against students.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of rules, Statutes, Ordinances and notifications
main_sections.description: This section specifies the procedure for laying down rules, Statutes, Ordinances, and notifications before Parliament.
This section grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the Act.
This section contains provisions for managing the transition to the new University structure.
This section repeals the Gujarat Forensic Sciences University Act, 2008 (Gujarat Act 17 of 2008).

important_rules: The Gujarat Forensic Sciences University and Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Sciences are merged to form the National Forensic Sciences University (Section 4).
The National Forensic Sciences University is declared an institution of national importance (Section 2).
The University shall have a Board of Governors and an Academic Council to manage its affairs (Sections 15, 18).
The University's objects include promoting studies, research, and excellence in forensic science and allied fields (Section 6).
The University shall be open to all races, creeds, and classes (Section 9).
The University shall have a Fund managed according to its provisions (Section 35).
Statutes and Ordinances shall govern the University's functioning, with specific procedures for their making (Sections 40-43).
A Tribunal of Arbitration is established for dispute resolution (Section 44).
Provisions exist for the redressal of examination debarment and disciplinary actions against students (Section 45).
The Central Government has the power to make rules, issue directions, and remove difficulties related to the Act (Sections 47, 51, 54).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: While not explicitly detailed in the provided text, enforcement would likely involve the University's administration, the Board of Governors, and potentially the Ministry of Education or Ministry of Home Affairs, with the Central Government having overarching powers to issue directions and remove difficulties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is likely to be through the established authorities of the University (Board of Governors, Vice-Chancellor, etc.), adherence to Statutes and Ordinances, and directives from the Central Government. Specific penalties for violations are not detailed in the provided excerpt but would typically be outlined in the full Act or related regulations.

rights: Students have the right to pursue academic and research courses (Section 5(h), 5(i)).
Employees have rights to their existing tenure, remuneration, and terms and conditions of service unless altered not detrimentally (Section 5(f)).
The University has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract (Section 4(2)).
The University is a public authority under the Right to Information Act (Section 49).
duties: The University has a duty to facilitate and promote academic learning and practices (Section 6(i)).
The University has a duty to foster research and applied applications (Section 6(ii)).
The University has a duty to promote and provide advanced institutional and research facilities (Section 6(iii)).
The University has a duty to create capacities and capabilities of global standards (Section 6(iv)).
The University has a duty to coordinate with Central and State Governments (Section 6(v)).
The University must be open to all races, creeds, and classes (Section 9).
obligations: The University must operate according to the provisions of the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances.
The University must ensure that staff employment terms and conditions are not detrimentally altered without due process (Section 5(f)).

key_procedures: Establishment and incorporation of the University by merging existing institutions (Section 4).
Making of Statutes and Ordinances (Sections 41, 43).
Redressal for debarment from examination and disciplinary action against students (Section 45).
Laying of rules, Statutes, Ordinances, and notifications before Parliament (Section 53).
Removal of difficulties by the Central Government (Section 54).
administration: The administration of the University involves various authorities and officers, including the Chancellor, Court, Board of Governors, Academic Council, Vice Chancellor, Campus Directors, Dean, Executive Registrar, Finance Officer, and Finance Committee. The Central Government plays a significant role in rule-making, issuing directions, and overseeing certain aspects of the University's functioning.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Gujarat Forensic Sciences University Act, 2008 (Gujarat Act 17 of 2008) (Section 56).
The Central Government can appoint different commencement dates for different provisions of the Act (Section 1(2)).
The Act ensures continuity of service, tenure, and remuneration for employees of the predecessor institutions (Section 5(f)).

Specific provisions are made for the continuation of academic courses and degrees for students enrolled in the Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Sciences under the Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, Delhi (Section 5(i)).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 50).

title: THE INDIAN RED CROSS SOCIETY ACT, 1920
purpose: To constitute an Indian Red Cross Society for the future administration of monies and gifts received for medical and other aid to the sick and wounded, and for the continuation of similar work in peacetime on a wider basis, and to provide for the affiliation of other societies with similar objects.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Indian Red Cross Society, its Managing Body, and its branches within India. It also covers the transfer of property from the Joint War Committee to the Society.

key_definitions.Society: The Indian Red Cross Society, constituted by this Act.
key_definitions.Committee: The Joint War Committee, Indian Branch, of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem in England and the British Red Cross Society, immediately before the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Managing Body: The Managing Body of the Indian Red Cross Society, appointed from among the nominated members of the Society.
key_definitions.President: The President of India, who is the President of the Society.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Indian Red Cross Society Act, 1920.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Indian Red Cross Society
main_sections.description: Establishes the Indian Red Cross Society. The first members are to be nominated by the members of the Joint War Committee and shall number between twenty-five and fifty.
The Committee shall appoint a Managing Body from the nominated members of the Society. The number of members of the Managing Body shall be between ten and thirty.

Constitutes the first members and future members of the Society as a body corporate under the name of the Indian Red Cross Society, with perpetual succession and the power to hold property and sue or be sued.
Declares the President of India as the President of the Society.

Details the composition of the Managing Body, including a Chairman nominated by the President, six members nominated by the President, and twelve members elected by State Branch Committees. It also addresses the reconstitution of the Managing Body after the Indian Red Cross Society (Amendment) Act, 1992.

main_sections.section_title: Secretary General and Treasurer of the Society
main_sections.description: The Managing Body shall appoint a Secretary-General and a Treasurer with the President's approval. Their terms of office and conditions of service are to be determined by rules.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Chairman and Vice-Chairman
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Chairman, including presiding over meetings and re-appropriating budgetary allocations, and the Vice-Chairman, including acting in the Chairman's absence.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the President to supersede the Managing Body
main_sections.description: Grants the President the power to supersede the Managing Body for up to six months if there is gross mismanagement or if the Body acts prejudicially to the Society's objectives, after providing an opportunity to show cause.

Empowers the Managing Body, with the President's approval, to make rules for the management, functions, control, and procedure of the Society, covering matters like membership, appointments, and delegation of powers. Rules must be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution and transfer of property of Joint War Committee
main_sections.description: Upon the nomination of the Society's members and appointment of the Managing Body, the Joint War Committee shall be dissolved, its property shall vest in the Society, and its debts and liabilities shall be transferred to the Society.

main_sections.section_title: Purposes to which funds of Society may be applied
main_sections.description: Specifies that the corpus or income of property vested in the Society can be applied for the relief of sickness, suffering, or distress caused by war, and for maintaining Red Cross Depots for military purposes. Income can also be applied for the relief of sickness or suffering in India.
The document mentions the constitution of Branch Committees, but the details of this section are not fully provided in the excerpt.
The document indicates that the Act provides for the affiliation of other societies and bodies having similar objects, but the details of this section are not fully provided in the excerpt.

main_sections.section_title: Decision of Managing Body as to purposes final
main_sections.description: The decision of the Managing Body regarding the purposes for which funds are to be applied shall be final. The details of this section are not fully provided in the excerpt.
This section likely deals with the Society's ability to receive and use gifts. The details are not fully provided in the excerpt.
This section would detail the powers vested in the Branch Committees. The details are not fully provided in the excerpt.
This section likely addresses the transfer of property to Pakistan, particularly concerning assets related to the Joint War Committee. The details are not fully provided in the excerpt.

important_rules: Rules for the management, functions, control, and procedure of the Society can be made by the Managing Body with the President's approval (Section 5).

These rules can cover conditions of membership, appointment and term of office of Managing Body members, choice of representatives on international committees, election procedures for State Branch Committees, constitution of Finance, Medical, and other committees, delegation of powers to these committees, powers of the Managing Body in supervising State Branch Committees, delegation of financial and administrative powers to the Chairman and Vice-Chairman, disqualifications for membership of the Managing Body, and the term of office and conditions of service for the Secretary-General, Treasurer, and other officers.
Any rule made under Section 5 must be laid before each House of Parliament and is subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.

The Managing Body must be reconstituted within six months of the commencement of the Indian Red Cross Society (Amendment) Act, 1992, with elections for members of State Branch Committees for a term of two years, with a maximum of two consecutive terms for elected members (Section 4B).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Managing Body, assisted by the Secretary-General and Treasurer, and ultimately overseen by the President of India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Managing Body, Chairman, Vice-Chairman, President, and the ability to make rules and supersede the Managing Body. Disciplinary proceedings can be instituted against officers.

rights: The Society has the right to perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Society has the power to hold and acquire property, moveable and immoveable.
The Society can sue and be sued by its name.
duties: The Society has a duty to administer funds for the relief of sickness, suffering, or distress caused by war.
The Society has a duty to apply income for the relief of sickness or suffering in India.
The Managing Body has a duty to appoint a Secretary-General and Treasurer with the President's approval.
The Managing Body has duties related to the management and functioning of the Society as outlined in the Act and rules.
obligations: The Society is obligated to discharge and satisfy debts and liabilities transferred from the Joint War Committee.
The Managing Body is obligated to reconstitute itself according to Section 4B after the 1992 amendment, with elections and term limits for members.

key_procedures: Nomination of first members of the Society and appointment of the Managing Body by the Joint War Committee within three months of the Act's commencement (Section 2 & 3).
Appointment of Secretary-General and Treasurer by the Managing Body with the President's approval (Section 4C).
Nomination of Chairman and members of the Managing Body by the President, and election of members by State Branch Committees (Section 4B).
Application of funds for specified purposes related to war relief and general relief in India (Section 7).
Process for making rules by the Managing Body and their laying before Parliament (Section 5).
Procedure for the President to supersede the Managing Body, including providing an opportunity to show cause (Section 4E).
administration: The Indian Red Cross Society, with its Managing Body, Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary-General, Treasurer, and President of India overseeing its functions.
important_notes: The Act has been extended with modifications to Goa, Daman and Diu, and the Union territories of Lakshadweep and Pondicherry.
Sub-section (2) of Section 2 was omitted by Act 22 of 1956.
Sections 4A, 4B, 4C, 4D, and 4E were inserted by Act 14 of 1992.
Section 5 was renumbered as sub-section (1) and amended by Act 14 of 1992, with new provisions regarding the laying of rules before Parliament being inserted as sub-section (2) by the same Act.
The Act consolidates the administration of various funds and gifts received for public aid, particularly those from the Joint War Committee.

title: The Manoeuvres Field Firing and Artillery Practice Act, 1938
purpose: To provide facilities for military manoeuvres and for field firing and artillery practice.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to military manoeuvres, field firing, and artillery practice conducted by military forces.

key_definitions.notified area: An area defined in a notification issued under sub-section (1) of section 9.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent. It was initially extended to the whole of India except Part B States, but later amendments extended it to various Union Territories.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to authorise manoeuvres
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to authorize military manoeuvres over a specified area for a period not exceeding three months. It outlines procedures for notification and public notice.

main_sections.section_title: Powers exercisable for purposes of manoeuvres
main_sections.description: Defines the powers of military forces engaged in manoeuvres, including passing over, encamping, constructing temporary military works, and supplying water from sources within the specified area. It also lists exceptions where these powers cannot be exercised, such as sacred places, places of worship, burial grounds, dwelling houses, educational institutions, factories, and gardens.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Officer Commanding to repair damage
main_sections.description: Mandates the Officer Commanding the military forces to restore lands used for manoeuvres to their previous condition as soon and as far as practicable.

main_sections.section_title: Right to compensation for damage caused by manoeuvres
main_sections.description: Establishes the right to compensation for any damage to person or property, or interference with rights or privileges, arising from military manoeuvres. Compensation is payable from the Defence Estimates.

Details the procedure for assessing compensation. The Collector deputes Revenue Officers to determine compensation, with provisions for local investigation, hearing claimants, and disbursing compensation on the spot. Appeals can be made to a commission constituted by the Collector.
Specifies offenses related to manoeuvres, such as wilfully obstructing them, unauthorized entry into camps, or interfering with apparatus. Punishable with a fine up to ten rupees.
Defines 'field firing' to include air armament practice and 'notified area'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to authorise field firing and artillery practice
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to define areas for field firing and artillery practice and authorize such practice within those areas for specified periods. It outlines notification and public announcement procedures.

main_sections.section_title: Powers exercisable for purposes of field firing and artillery practice
main_sections.description: Grants powers to forces engaged in field firing and artillery practice, including carrying out practice with lethal missiles and exercising rights similar to those for manoeuvres. It allows for declaration of danger zones and removal of persons and animals.

Extends the compensation provisions of sections 5 and 6 to field firing and artillery practice. It also includes compensation for exclusion or removal from danger zones and for losses resulting from such exclusion.

Defines offenses related to field firing and artillery practice, including obstruction, unauthorized entry into camps or danger zones, and interference with apparatus. Punishable with a fine up to ten rupees.

Authorizes the State Government to make rules for the implementation of the Act, including procedures for public notices, regulating land use, assessment of compensation, and principles for assessing compensation. Rules must be laid before the State Legislature.

important_rules: Rule 1: State Government can authorize military manoeuvres over a specified area for a period not exceeding three months, with prior public notice of at least three months.
Rule 2: Military forces engaged in manoeuvres can pass over, encamp, construct temporary military works, and take water from sources within the authorized area, subject to certain limitations.
Rule 3: Compensation is payable for damage caused by manoeuvres, assessed by Revenue Officers and appealed to a commission.
Rule 4: State Government can authorize field firing and artillery practice in defined areas, with specified notification procedures.
Rule 5: Forces can carry out field firing and artillery practice with lethal missiles, and can declare danger zones from which persons and domestic animals must be removed.
Rule 6: Compensation is payable for damage caused by field firing and artillery practice, including exclusion from danger zones.

Rule 7: State Governments can make rules to prescribe publication of notices, regulate land use for safety and minimum inconvenience, and govern the procedure and principles for compensation assessment.

penalties: Fine which may extend to ten rupees for obstructing manoeuvres, unauthorized entry into camps, or interfering with apparatus.
Fine which may extend to ten rupees for obstructing field firing or artillery practice, unauthorized entry into camps or danger zones, or interfering with practice apparatus.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (through notifications, rule-making, and Collector's office), Officer Commanding military forces.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications authorizing activities, declaration of danger zones, deputation of Revenue Officers for compensation assessment, establishment of commissions for appeals, and imposition of penalties for offenses.

rights: Right to compensation for damage to person or property or interference with rights caused by manoeuvres or field firing/artillery practice.
Right to appeal decisions on compensation assessments.
Right to be excluded from danger zones during field firing and artillery practice.
duties: Duty of Officer Commanding to repair damage to lands used for manoeuvres.
Duty to publish public notices for proposed manoeuvres and field firing/artillery practice.
Duty to provide adequate warning and conduct entry into occupied dwelling houses in the presence of respectable inhabitants.
Duty to prohibit entry into danger zones and secure removal of persons and domestic animals.
obligations: Obligation to pay compensation for damages caused by military activities.
Obligation for military forces to follow regulations regarding water supply and avoid interfering with sacred places, dwelling houses, etc., during manoeuvres.
Obligation for the State Government to lay down rules for public safety and convenience.

key_procedures: Procedure for Authorizing Manoeuvres: State Government issues notification, publishes notice of intention at least three months in advance, and then issues the notification. Public notices are repeated one month and one week before commencement.

Procedure for Assessing and Appealing Compensation: Revenue Officer determines compensation on local investigation. Dissatisfied claimants can appeal to a commission constituted by the Collector within fifteen days. Commission's decision is final.

Procedure for Authorizing Field Firing/Artillery Practice: State Government defines notified areas and issues notifications for practice periods. Public notice is published at least two months in advance and repeated one week before commencement. Specific procedures for local announcements (newspaper, drumbeat) are also mandated.

Procedure for Declaring Danger Zones: Officer Commanding can declare a danger zone, and the Collector, upon application, prohibits entry and secures removal of persons and animals during practice times.
administration: State Government (primarily through its revenue and administrative departments, including the Collector)
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various Union Territories over time.

The Act does not authorize interference with wells or tanks held sacred, places of worship, burial grounds, dwelling houses, educational institutions, factories, gardens, or ancient monuments, except under specific conditions.
Compensation for exclusion from danger zones must be disbursed at minimum prescribed rates before enforcement.
Decisions of the compensation commission are final and not subject to Civil Court jurisdiction.

title: THE DENTISTS ACT, 1948
purpose: To regulate the profession of dentistry and for that purpose to constitute Dental Councils.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the regulation of the profession of dentistry, including dental practitioners, dental hygienists, and dental mechanics.

key_definitions.dental_hygienist: A person, not being a dentist or a medical practitioner, who scales, cleans or polishes teeth, or gives instruction in dental hygiene.
key_definitions.dental_mechanic: A person who makes or repairs denture and dental appliances.
key_definitions.dentistry: Includes the performance of any operation on, and the treatment of, any disease, deficiency or lesion of, human teeth or jaws, and the performance of radiographic work in connection with human teeth or jaws or the oral cavity; the giving of any anaesthetic in connection with any such operation or treatment; the mechanical construction or the renewal of artificial dentures or restorative dental appliances; the performance of any operation on, or the giving of any treatment, advice or attendance to, any person preparatory to, or for the purpose of, or in connection with, the fitting, inserting, fixing, constructing, repairing or renewing of artificial dentures or restorative dental appliances, and the performance of any such operation and the giving of any such treatment, advice or attendance, as is usually performed or given by dentists.
key_definitions.medical_practitioner: A person who holds a qualification granted by an authority specified or notified under section 3 of the Indian Medical Degrees Act, 1916 (7 of 1916), or specified in the Schedules to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (102 of 1956), or specified in any other law for the time being in force in any State, or who practices any system of medicine and is registered or is entitled to be registered in any State medical register by whatever name called.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules or regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.State_Council: A State Dental Council constituted under section 21, and includes a Joint State Council constituted in accordance with an agreement under section 22.
key_definitions.register: A register maintained under this Act.
key_definitions.recognised_dental_qualification: Any of the qualifications included in the Schedule.
key_definitions.recognised_dental_hygiene_qualification: A qualification recognised by the Council under section 11.
key_definitions.registered_dentist: A person whose name is for the time being registered in a register of dentists.
key_definitions.registered_dental_hygienist: A person whose name is for the time being registered in a register of dental hygienists.
key_definitions.registered_dental_mechanic: A person whose name is for the time being registered in a register of dental mechanics.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Dentists Act, 1948' and states that it extends to the whole of India.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'the Council', 'dental hygienist', 'dental mechanic', 'dentistry', 'dentist', 'medical practitioner', 'prescribed', 'State Council', 'register', 'recognised dental qualification', 'recognised dental hygiene qualification', 'registered dentist', 'registered dental hygienist', and 'registered dental mechanic'.

Details the constitution and composition of the Dental Council of India, specifying the categories of members including elected dentists, members from the Medical Council of India, principals/deans of dental colleges, university representatives, state government nominees, Central Government nominees, and ex-officio members like the Director General of Health Services.
Declares the Dental Council of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire property and sue and be sued.
Empowers the Dental Council of India to recognize dental qualifications granted by authorities in India or outside India.
Concerns the preparation and maintenance of the Indian Register of Dentists.
Deals with the preparation and maintenance of registers of dentists, dental hygienists, and dental mechanics.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for individuals who falsely claim to be registered under the Act.
Prohibits the practice of dentistry by persons who are not registered under the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Recognition of dental qualifications is essential for practicing dentistry.
Rule 2: The Dental Council of India is responsible for maintaining the Indian Register of Dentists.
Rule 3: Practicing dentistry without being registered is prohibited.
Rule 4: Specific qualifications are required for registration as a dentist, dental hygienist, and dental mechanic.
Rule 5: The Dental Council of India has powers to inspect dental colleges and withdraw recognition of qualifications if standards are not met.

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered.
Penalty for misuse of titles.
Penalty for practice by unregistered persons.
Penalty for failure to surrender certificate of registration.
Penalties for companies engaging in dentistry.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Dental Council of India and State Dental Councils are the primary bodies responsible for the enforcement of the Act. The Central Government also plays a role in certain aspects, such as dispute resolution regarding elections and making rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the maintenance of registers, recognition and withdrawal of qualifications, inspection of institutions, and imposition of penalties for violations. Legal proceedings can be initiated for offenses.

rights: Right to practice dentistry if registered.
Right to have one's name entered in the register if eligible.
Right to seek recognition of dental qualifications.
Right to elect and be elected to the Dental Council of India and State Councils (for eligible dentists).
duties: Duty to maintain professional conduct.
Duty to possess recognized qualifications for practice.
Duty to get registered under the Act.
Duty to furnish information as required by the Council.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules/regulations made thereunder.
obligations: Registered dentists have an obligation to practice dentistry ethically and professionally.
Dental institutions have an obligation to provide education that meets the standards set by the Dental Council of India.
All individuals involved in the dental profession have an obligation to uphold the integrity and standards of dentistry.

key_procedures: Procedure for constitution and composition of the Dental Council of India and State Dental Councils, including elections and nominations.
Procedure for the recognition of dental qualifications, including inspection of institutions and withdrawal of recognition.
Procedure for the preparation and maintenance of registers of dentists, dental hygienists, and dental mechanics, including qualifications for registration and renewal.
Procedure for the election of the President and Vice-President of the Council.
Procedure for handling casual vacancies in the Council.
administration: The Dental Council of India and State Dental Councils are the primary administrative bodies. The Central Government has oversight and rule-making powers.
important_notes: The Act has been amended over time and extended to various Union Territories.
Certain provisions related to Jammu and Kashmir have been adapted or omitted due to reorganization.
The Act differentiates between dentists, dental hygienists, and dental mechanics, with specific regulations for each.
The role of the Dental Council of India is central to maintaining standards and regulating the profession.

title: The National Council for Teacher Education Act, 1993
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a National Council for Teacher Education for the planned and co-ordinated development of the teacher education system throughout the country, the regulation and proper maintenance of norms and standards in the teacher education system, including qualifications of school teachers, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to institutions offering teacher education courses, students and teachers of these institutions, pre-primary, primary, upper primary, secondary, and senior secondary schools, colleges providing senior secondary or intermediate education, and teachers for these educational institutions. It also applies to schools established, owned, or controlled by the Central Government, State Government, or local authority, and schools receiving aid or not receiving aid from these entities.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of establishment of the National Council for Teacher Education.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Council appointed under the Act.
key_definitions.Council: The National Council for Teacher Education established under the Act.
key_definitions.examining body: A University, agency, or authority to which an institution is affiliated for conducting examinations in teacher education qualifications.
key_definitions.institution: An institution that offers courses or training in teacher education.
key_definitions.local authority: A Municipal Corporation, Municipal Committee, Municipal Council, Zila Parishad, District Board, Nagar Panchayat, Panchayati, or other authority legally entitled to or entrusted with the control or management of a municipal or local fund.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Council, including the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson.
key_definitions.Member-Secretary: The Member-Secretary of the Council appointed under the Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under section 31.
key_definitions.recognised institution: An institution recognised by the Council under section 14.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made under section 32.
key_definitions.school: Any recognised school imparting pre-primary, primary, upper primary, secondary or senior secondary education, or a college imparting senior secondary education, and includes schools established, owned and controlled by the Central Government, State Government or a local authority, schools receiving aid or grants, and schools not receiving any aid or grants.
key_definitions.teacher education: Programs of education, research, or training of persons for equipping them to teach at pre-primary, primary, secondary and senior secondary stages in schools, and includes non-formal education, part-time education, adult education, and correspondence education.
key_definitions.teacher education qualification: A degree, diploma, or certificate in teacher education awarded by a University or examining body in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.University: A University defined under the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, and includes an institution deemed to be a University under that Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for the Central Government to appoint the commencement date through a notification. It also outlines the applicability of the Act to various educational institutions and personnel.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Chairperson', 'Council', 'examining body', 'institution', 'local authority', 'Member', 'Member-Secretary', 'prescribed', 'recognised institution', 'Regional Committee', 'regulations', 'school', 'teacher education', 'teacher education qualification', and 'University'.

Provides for the establishment of the National Council for Teacher Education. It states that the Council shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. The head office is in Delhi, with the possibility of establishing regional offices. It also details the composition of the Council, including the appointment of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Member-Secretary, ex-officio members, and appointed members representing various educational stakeholders.
Outlines the various functions of the Council, which are to be detailed in this section. (Specific functions are not provided in the excerpt but are implied to be listed here).

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of institutions offering course or training in teacher education
main_sections.description: Deals with the process and conditions for the recognition of institutions that offer courses or training in teacher education.

main_sections.section_title: Contravention of provisions of the Act and consequences thereof
main_sections.description: Specifies the consequences for contravening the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the establishment of Regional Committees by the Council.
Details the provisions related to the Fund of the Council.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Council the power to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

penalties: Consequences of contravention of the Act's provisions (detailed in Section 17).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Council for Teacher Education, and potentially the Central Government through its powers to make rules and issue directions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the recognition process for institutions, enforcement of norms and standards, imposition of consequences for contravention of provisions, and potentially through inspections and appeals.

rights: Right of recognised institutions to offer teacher education courses.
Right of appeal against certain decisions of the Council (detailed in Section 18).
duties: Institutions offering teacher education must be recognised by the Council (Section 14).
Affiliating bodies must grant affiliation only after recognition or permission by the Council (Section 16).
Members of the Council must meet the specified qualifications and not be subject to disqualifications (Sections 4, 5).
obligations: The Council has the obligation to achieve planned and co-ordinated development of the teacher education system.
The Council has the obligation to regulate and maintain norms and standards in teacher education.
The Central Government has the obligation to appoint members and make rules and notifications as required by the Act.

key_procedures: Establishment of the National Council for Teacher Education.
Appointment of Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and Member-Secretary.
Meetings of the Council, including quorum and voting procedures.
Recognition of teacher education institutions.
Permission for new courses by recognised institutions.
Affiliation process by examining bodies.
Process for appeals against Council decisions.
Establishment and functioning of Regional Committees.
Preparation of budgets, accounts, and audit of the Council's finances.
Making of rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Council.
administration: The National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), with the Central Government playing a significant role in its establishment, appointment of key officials, and rule-making.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2011 and 2019, with some provisions coming into effect on June 1, 2012, and the omission of 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' effective October 31, 2019.
The Act requires the Council to meet at least once every year.

title: THE PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF INFECTIOUS AND CONTAGIOUS DISEASES IN ANIMALS ACT, 2009
purpose: To provide for the prevention, control and eradication of infectious and contagious diseases affecting animals, for the prevention of outbreak or spreading of such diseases from one State to another, and to meet the international obligations of India for facilitating import and export of animals and animal products, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to all animals (as defined in the Act) and covers the prevention, control, and eradication of infectious and contagious diseases affecting them. It is intended to operate on a national basis to avoid adverse economic impacts and to harmonize control procedures and prevent inter-State transmission of animal diseases. The Act's commencement can be varied for different States or areas within States, and for different provisions.

key_definitions.animal: Includes cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat, yak, mithun; dog, cat, pig, horse, camel, ass, mule, poultry, bees; and any other animal or bird as the Central Government may specify. The definition has been expanded to include fish, molluscs, crustaceans, and amphibians.
key_definitions.scheduled disease: Means any disease included in the Schedule to the Act.
key_definitions.infected animal: Means an animal which is infected with any scheduled disease.
key_definitions.controlled area: Means any local area which has been declared as such by the State Government under section 6(1).
key_definitions.infected area: Means an area declared as such under section 20.
key_definitions.Veterinary Officer: Means any officer appointed as such by the State Government under section 3(b).
key_definitions.Veterinarian: Means a person having a recognised veterinary qualification who is allowed to treat animal diseases under the law.
key_definitions.compulsory vaccination: Means vaccination of any animal against any scheduled disease in respect of which vaccination is made mandatory under the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent (nationwide with potential for varying commencement dates for different states/areas/provisions), and commencement provisions.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'animal', 'Check Post', 'Competent Officer', 'controlled area', 'scheduled disease', 'Veterinary Officer', and others.
Empowers the State Government to appoint Veterinarians and Veterinary Officers, specifying their local jurisdiction.

Makes it obligatory for owners, NGOs, public bodies, or village panchayats to report suspected scheduled diseases to Village Officers or Veterinarians. It also outlines the reporting chain up to the Director of Animal Husbandry and inter-state intimation.

Mandates owners or persons in charge of infected animals to segregate them from healthy animals and prevent contact. It also outlines confinement and prohibition of grazing/drinking from common sources.

main_sections.section_title: Notification of controlled areas and free areas
main_sections.description: Allows the State Government to declare any area as a 'controlled area' to prevent, control, or eradicate scheduled diseases. It outlines the procedure for notification, publication, compulsory vaccination within controlled areas, and the declaration of 'free areas'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of movement of animals from controlled area
main_sections.description: Prohibits the movement of animals belonging to a specified species from a controlled area. Exceptions are made for movement for vaccination or when accompanied by a valid vaccination certificate.

main_sections.section_title: Vaccination, marking and issue of vaccination certificate
main_sections.description: Details the process of vaccination, including who can administer it, the requirement for marking vaccinated animals (branding, tattooing, ear tagging), and the information to be included in a vaccination certificate.
Empowers the State Government to declare an area as an 'infected area' if it is satisfied that the area is infected with a scheduled disease.

main_sections.section_title: Segregation, examination and treatment of infected animals
main_sections.description: Deals with the segregation, examination, and treatment of infected animals.

main_sections.section_title: Resort to euthanasia for infected animals
main_sections.description: Provides for the resort to euthanasia for infected animals when deemed necessary.
Covers the disposal of carcasses of animals.

main_sections.section_title: Enforcement of orders and recovery of expenses
main_sections.description: Deals with the enforcement of orders issued under the Act and the recovery of expenses incurred.
Outlines various penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act within its jurisdiction.
Deals with the repeal of any previous laws on the subject and savings for actions taken thereunder.

important_rules: Reporting of scheduled diseases is obligatory for owners, NGOs, public bodies, and village panchayats.
Owners of suspected infected animals must segregate them and prevent contact with healthy animals.
Movement of animals from declared controlled areas is prohibited, with specific exceptions for vaccination.
Compulsory vaccination against scheduled diseases is mandated in controlled areas.
Animals in free areas must be duly immunized against specific diseases to be allowed entry.

penalties: Penalty for issuing vaccination certificates without authority or administering defective vaccines (Section 31).
General penalties for contravention of provisions of the Act (Section 32).
Penalty for placing infected animals or carcasses in rivers etc. (Section 33).
Penalties for offences committed by companies (Section 34).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Governments, through appointed Veterinary Officers, Competent Officers, and Village Officers. The Director of Animal Husbandry in each State also plays a significant role. The Central Government has rule-making powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of officials, declaration of controlled and infected areas, prohibition of movement, compulsory vaccination, inspection and detention at check posts, and imposition of penalties for violations.

rights: Right to movement of animals for vaccination or with valid vaccination certificates from controlled areas (Section 7(3)).
Right to receive timely information and necessary vaccines for compulsory vaccination (Section 6(4)).
duties: Duty to report scheduled diseases (Section 4).
Duty to segregate infected animals (Section 5).
Duty to get animals compulsorily vaccinated (Section 6(4)).
Duty of Village Officers to assist in enforcement (Section 30).
Duty to prevent escape of causative organisms (Section 35).
obligations: Obligation to report scheduled diseases.
Obligation to segregate infected animals.
Obligation to comply with vaccination requirements.
Obligation to adhere to movement restrictions from controlled areas.
Obligation for certain persons to be public servants (Section 40).

key_procedures: Reporting of suspected scheduled diseases to Village Officers or Veterinarians, and subsequent reporting up the chain of command.
Declaration of controlled areas by the State Government through notification and public dissemination.
Compulsory vaccination of animals within controlled areas, with the State Government providing vaccines.
Movement of animals from controlled areas only for vaccination or with a valid vaccination certificate.
Declaration of infected areas and their subsequent denotification.
Segregation, examination, and potential euthanasia of infected animals.
Establishment and operation of Check Posts and Quarantine Camps for inspection and detention of animals.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Governments, with the Central Government having powers to make rules and specify certain animals. The Department of Animal Husbandry or Veterinary Services, as notified by the State Government, plays a key role.
important_notes: Different dates can be appointed for the commencement of the Act for different States, areas, or provisions.
The Act aims to meet international obligations for facilitating import and export of animals and animal products.
The Act emphasizes harmonizing control procedures and preventing inter-State transmission of animal diseases.
Public servants defined under Section 40 are protected under Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
The Central Government has the power to amend the Schedule.
The Act can be amended by the Central Government to remove difficulties.

title: THE APPRENTICES ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the regulation and control of training of apprentices and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. The provisions of the Act do not apply to any area or industry unless specified by the Central Government via notification. Special apprenticeship schemes notified by the Central Government are also exempted. The Act applies to apprentices undergoing apprenticeship training in designated trades.

key_definitions.apprentice: A person who is undergoing apprenticeship training in pursuance of a contract of apprenticeship.
key_definitions.apprenticeship_training: A course of training in any industry or establishment undergone in pursuance of a contract of apprenticeship and under prescribed terms and conditions.
key_definitions.designated_trade: Any trade or occupation or any subject field in engineering or non-engineering or technology or any vocational course which the Central Government, after consultation with the Central Apprenticeship Council, may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify as a designated trade for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.employer: Any person who employs one or more other persons to do any work in an establishment for remuneration and includes any person entrusted with the supervision and control of employees in such establishment.
key_definitions.establishment: Includes any place where any industry is carried on. If an establishment consists of different departments or branches, all such departments or branches shall be treated as part of that establishment.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, commencement date, and specifies conditions for its application to certain areas or industries and special apprenticeship schemes.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'apprentice', 'apprenticeship training', 'designated trade', 'employer', 'establishment', 'appropriate Government', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications for being engaged as an apprentice
main_sections.description: Outlines the minimum age (not less than fourteen years, or eighteen for hazardous industries) and educational and physical fitness standards required for an apprentice.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of training places for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in designated trades
main_sections.description: Mandates employers to reserve training places for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in designated trades, with the number of reservations based on prescribed ratios and the population of these communities.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of training places for Other Backward Classes in designated trades
main_sections.description: Mandates employers to reserve training places for Other Backward Classes in designated trades, with the number of reservations based on prescribed ratios and the population of these communities.

Stipulates that no person can be engaged as an apprentice unless a contract of apprenticeship is entered into with the employer. It also details the commencement of training and permissible terms of the contract.
Deals with the process of novation (substitution) of an apprenticeship contract.
Specifies the duration of apprenticeship training.
Details the responsibilities of employers towards apprentices, including providing training, ensuring health and safety, and making payments.
Outlines the duties and responsibilities of apprentices during their training period.
Provides for mechanisms to resolve disputes arising between employers and apprentices.

main_sections.section_title: Holding of test and grant of certificate and conclusion of training
main_sections.description: Covers the process of conducting tests, granting certificates upon successful completion of training, and the conclusion of the apprenticeship.
Grants powers to designated authorities to enter establishments, inspect records, and conduct other necessary actions to ensure compliance with the Act.
Defines offences related to contravention of the provisions of the Act and prescribes penalties for such offences.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: A person must not be less than fourteen years of age (or eighteen for hazardous industries) and must meet prescribed educational and physical fitness standards to be engaged as an apprentice.
Rule 2: Training places must be reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes in designated trades based on prescribed ratios and population figures.
Rule 3: An apprenticeship training can only commence after a contract of apprenticeship has been entered into between the apprentice (or guardian) and the employer.
Rule 4: Employers have obligations to provide training, ensure health, safety, welfare, and timely payment to apprentices.
Rule 5: Apprentices have obligations to faithfully serve the employer, attend training, and obey lawful orders.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for various offences under the Act, including contravention of provisions, failure to comply with directions, and obstruction of authorities.
Penalties for offences where no specific penalty is provided are also outlined.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Apprenticeship Advisers (Central, State), Deputy and Assistant Apprenticeship Advisers, and other authorities appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry and inspection, verification and registration of apprenticeship contracts, settlement of disputes, and prosecution for offences.

rights: Right to receive proper apprenticeship training in a designated trade.
Right to receive payment as per prescribed rates.
Right to health, safety, and welfare provisions.
Right to have disputes settled.
Right to a certificate upon successful completion of training.
duties: Duty to faithfully serve the employer during the apprenticeship period.
Duty to attend training and related instruction classes.
Duty to obey lawful commands of the employer.
Duty to maintain the employer's property and confidential information.
obligations: Employers are obligated to provide apprenticeship training, ensure safety, pay stipends, and maintain records.
Apprentices are obligated to undergo training diligently and abide by the terms of the contract and the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Engagement of an apprentice requires entering into a contract of apprenticeship.
Procedure 2: Apprenticeship contracts must be sent to the Apprenticeship Adviser for verification and registration (or entered on the portal-site once developed).
Procedure 3: Disputes between employers and apprentices can be settled through prescribed mechanisms.
Procedure 4: Upon completion of training, a test is conducted, and a certificate is granted if successful.
administration: The Act is administered by the Central Government and State Governments, with the involvement of Apprenticeship Councils, Apprenticeship Advisers, and other authorities.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act's application can be extended to specific areas or industries by Central Government notification.
Note 2: Special apprenticeship schemes notified by the Central Government may be exempt from the Act's provisions.
Note 3: The Act distinguishes between apprentices and workers, stating that apprentices are trainees and not workers.

title: The Airports Authority of India Act, 1994
purpose: To provide for the constitution of the Airports Authority of India and for the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of the International Airports Authority of India and the National Airports Authority to and in the Airports Authority of India so constituted for the better administration and cohesive management of airports and civil enclaves whereat air transport services are operated or are intended to be operated and of all aeronautical communication stations for the purposes of establishing or assisting in the establishment of airports and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to: (a) all airports where air transport services are operated or intended to be operated (excluding those belonging to armed forces), (aa) all private airports in relation to air traffic service and directions under section 37 and for Chapter VA, (b) all civil enclaves, (c) all aeronautical communication stations, and (d) all training stations, establishments and workshops related to air transport services.

key_definitions.aeronautical communication station: A station in the aeronautical communication service including aeronautical practising service, aeronautical fixed service, aeronautical mobile service and aeronautical radio communication service.
key_definitions.airport: A landing and taking off area for aircrafts, usually with runways and aircraft maintenance and passenger facilities, and includes aerodrome as defined in the Aircraft Act, 1934.
key_definitions.air traffic service: Includes flight information service, alerting service, air traffic advisory service, air traffic control service, area control service, approach control service, and airport control service.
key_definitions.air transport service: Any service, for any kind of remuneration, for the transport by air of persons, mail or any other thing, animate or inanimate, whether such service relates to a single flight or series of flights.
key_definitions.Authority: The Airports Authority of India constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.civil enclave: The area allotted at an airport belonging to any armed force of the Union, for use by persons availing air transport services or for handling baggage or cargo, including buildings and structures thereon.
key_definitions.private airport: An airport owned, developed or managed by any person or agency other than the Authority or any State Government, or jointly where the private entity's share in assets is more than fifty percent.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, the date of commencement (to be appointed by the Central Government), and the scope of its application to various types of airports, civil enclaves, and aeronautical communication stations.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'airport', 'air transport service', 'Authority', 'civil enclave', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of the Authority
main_sections.description: Establishes the Airports Authority of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, detailing its composition (Chairperson, Director General of Civil Aviation, and other members) appointed by the Central Government.
Outlines the primary functions of the Airports Authority of India. (Details not provided in the extract).

main_sections.section_title: EVICTION OF UNAUTHORISED OCCUPANTS, ETC., OF AIRPORT PREMISES
main_sections.description: Chapter VA deals with the eviction of unauthorized occupants from airport premises, including definitions, appointment of eviction officers, procedures for eviction, disposal of property, removal of unauthorized constructions, payment of rent or damages, appeals, and offenses.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and provisions for saving existing matters.

important_rules: Rule: All airports where air transport services are operated or intended to be operated are subject to this Act, except those belonging to armed forces.
Rule: The Airports Authority of India is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and enter into contracts.
Rule: The Authority shall be managed by a Chairperson and members appointed by the Central Government, chosen for their expertise in relevant fields.
Rule: Members are disqualified if convicted of certain offenses, are undischarged insolvents, of unsound mind, dismissed from government service, or have conflicting financial interests.
Rule: Whole-time members hold office for five years or until sixty years of age, while part-time members hold office for three years. Appointments can be terminated under specific conditions.

penalties: Offences under Chapter VA (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) are punishable. Specific penalties are detailed within the chapter (not fully elaborated in the provided text).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Airports Authority of India and its appointed eviction officers are responsible for enforcement, particularly concerning airport premises.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers vested in eviction officers, including issuing notices, carrying out evictions, removing unauthorized constructions, and pursuing legal action for offenses.

rights: Right to the orderly administration and cohesive management of airports.
Right to charge fees, rent, and development fees at airports.
Right to compulsorily acquire land for the Authority's purposes.
Right to issue directions to private airports under certain conditions.
Right to take action against unauthorized occupants of airport premises.
duties: Duty to provide for the constitution and incorporation of the Airports Authority of India.
Duty to manage and administer airports and civil enclaves effectively.
Duty to ensure air transport services operate smoothly and safely.
Duty to act on business principles.
Duty to submit annual reports and financial estimates.
obligations: Obligation to transfer and vest undertakings of previous authorities into the new Authority.
Obligation to comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
Obligation for officers and employees of the Authority to be public servants.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointment of Chairperson and members of the Authority, including qualifications and disqualifications.
Procedure for conducting meetings of the Authority, including quorum and voting.
Procedure for the eviction of unauthorized occupants from airport premises, involving notice, eviction, and disposal of property.
Procedure for the Central Government to temporarily divest the Authority of airport management or to supersede the Authority.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules and the Authority to make regulations, which must be laid before Parliament.
administration: The Airports Authority of India, constituted under the Act, is the primary administrative body. The Central Government also plays a significant role in its constitution, appointment of members, and oversight.
important_notes: The Act came into force on April 1, 1995.
The Act provides for the vesting of undertakings of the International Airports Authority and the National Airports Authority into the newly constituted Airports Authority of India.
Private airports are subject to certain provisions of the Act, particularly concerning air traffic services and eviction procedures.
The Central Government has powers to issue directions to the Authority and to temporarily divest the Authority of airport management or supersede it in certain circumstances.

title: THE POLICE ACT, 1861
purpose: To re-organize the police and to make it a more efficient instrument for the prevention and detection of crime.
scope: Applies to any presidency, State or place, or any part of any presidency, State or place, in which this Act shall be ordered to take effect. The Act has been applied to various regions and modified in its application to different States and Union Territories. It establishes a unified police force under the State Government and outlines its administration, duties, and powers.

key_definitions.Magistrate of the district: The chief officer charged with the executive administration of a district and exercising the powers of a Magistrate, by whatever designation the chief officer charged with such executive administration is styled.
key_definitions.Magistrate: Includes all persons within the general police-district, exercising all or any of the powers of a Magistrate.
key_definitions.Police: Includes all persons who shall have been enrolled under this Act.
key_definitions.General police-district: Embraces any presidency, State or place, or any part of any presidency, State or place, in which this Act shall be ordered to take effect.
key_definitions.District Superintendent and District Sup: Includes any Assistant District Superintendent or other person appointed by general or special order of the State Government to perform all or any of the duties of a District Superintendent of Police under this Act in any district.
key_definitions.Property: Includes any moveable property money, or valuable security.
key_definitions.Cattle: Besides horned cattle, includes elephants, camels, horses, asses, mules, sheep, goats and swine.

main_sections.description: Defines key terms and expressions used in the Act, such as 'Magistrate of the district', 'Magistrate', 'Police', 'general police-district', 'District Superintendent', 'property', 'person', 'month', and 'cattle'.

Declares the entire police establishment under a State Government to be one police force, formally enrolled, and constituted as ordered by the State Government. It also states that the pay and conditions of service for subordinate ranks are determined by the State Government.

Vests the superintendence of the police throughout a general police-district in the State Government, which exercises these powers, and prohibits any person, officer, or Court from superseding or controlling any police functionary without authorization.

States that the administration of the police throughout the general police district is vested in an Inspector-General of Police, and such Deputy and Assistant Inspectors-General as deemed fit by the State Government. It also vests the administration of police within the local jurisdiction of a Magistrate in a District Superintendent and Assistant District Superintendents.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment, dismissal, etc., of inferior officers
main_sections.description: Empowers the Inspector-General, Deputy Inspectors-General, Assistant Inspector-General, and District Superintendents to dismiss, suspend, or reduce subordinate police officers who are remiss, negligent, or unfit for duty. It also outlines punishments like fines, confinement to quarters, deprivation of good-conduct pay, and removal from office of distinction.
States that every police officer, other than an officer mentioned in section 4, shall receive a certificate on appointment.
Outlines the duties of police officers.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of public assemblies and processions and licensing of the same.
main_sections.description: Deals with the regulation of public assemblies and processions and the licensing thereof, including music in the streets.
Defines the geographical and subject matter scope of the Act.

important_rules: Police officers are not to resign without leave or two months' notice (Section 9).
Police officers are not to engage in other employment (Section 10).
Inspector-General has the power to make rules (Section 12).
Additional police officers may be employed at the cost of individuals (Section 13).
Additional force may be appointed in the neighborhood of railway and other works (Section 14).
Additional police may be quartered in disturbed or dangerous districts (Section 15).
Compensation may be awarded to sufferers from misconduct of inhabitants or persons interested in land (Section 15A).
Police officers are always on duty and may be employed in any part of the district (Section 22).
Police officers must take charge of unclaimed property and be subject to Magistrate's orders for disposal (Section 25).
Persons refusing to deliver up certificates, etc., on ceasing to be police officers will be penalized (Section 28).
Penalties for neglect of duty, etc. (Section 29).
Regulation of public assemblies and processions and licensing of the same, including music in the streets (Section 30).
Police must keep order in public roads, etc. (Section 31).
Penalties for disobeying orders issued under sections 30, 30A, and 31 (Section 32).

Punishments for certain offenses on roads, etc., including slaughtering cattle, furious riding, cruelty to animals, obstructing passengers, exposing goods for sale, throwing dirt into streets, being found drunk or riotous, indecent exposure, and neglect to protect dangerous places (Section 34).
Police officers are to keep a diary (Section 44).
State Government may prescribe the form of returns (Section 45).

penalties: Fines not exceeding one month's pay for discharging duty carelessly or negligently (Section 7).
Confinement to quarters for a term not exceeding fifteen days, with or without punishment drill, extra guard, fatigue or other duty (Section 7).
Deprivation of good-conduct pay (Section 7).
Removal from any office of distinction or special emolument (Section 7).
Penalties for neglect of duty, etc. (Section 29).
Penalties for disobeying orders issued under sections 30, 30A, and 31 (Section 32).
Punishments for certain specified offenses on roads, etc. (Section 34).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Inspector-General of Police, Deputy Inspectors-General, Assistant Inspectors-General, District Superintendents of Police, and Magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment, dismissal, suspension, and reduction of police officers; imposition of fines and other punishments; making rules; regulating public assemblies and processions; and prosecuting offenders.

rights: Right to receive a certificate of appointment (Section 8).
Police officers are always on duty (Section 22).
Police officers may lay information, etc. (Section 24).
Police officers to take charge of unclaimed property (Section 25).
Police officers have the power to exercise authority (Section 20).
duties: To prevent and detect crime (Preamble, Section 23).
To maintain order (Section 23).
To execute warrants and orders (Section 23).
To attend before Magistrates (Section 23).
To protect life and property (Section 23).
To manage traffic and public thoroughfares (Section 23).
To obey orders of superior officers (implied).
To perform any duty lawfully imposed upon them by the State Government or Magistrate (implied).
obligations: Not to resign without leave or two months' notice (Section 9).
Not to engage in other employment (Section 10).
To deliver up certificate, etc., on ceasing to be a police officer (Section 28).
To comply with rules made by the Inspector-General (Section 12).

key_procedures: Appointment, dismissal, suspension, and reduction of subordinate police officers by superior officers (Section 7).
Issuance of certificates to police officers upon appointment (Section 8).
Procedure for dealing with unclaimed property: taking charge, Magistrate's orders for disposal, proclamation, and confiscation if no claimant appears (Sections 25, 26, 27).
Regulation of public assemblies and processions: obtaining licenses, and powers regarding violations (Sections 30, 30A).
Recovery of penalties and fines imposed by Magistrates (Section 37).
Procedures related to actions against police officers, including the plea that an act was done under warrant (Section 43).
administration: State Government, Inspector-General of Police, Deputy Inspectors-General, Assistant Inspectors-General, and District Superintendents of Police.
important_notes: The Act has been applied to various regions and modified in its application to different States and Union Territories, as indicated in the extensive footnotes.
Certain sections have been repealed or amended by subsequent legislation.
The Act provides for the creation of special police districts encompassing parts of two or more States.
The Act distinguishes between 'Magistrate of the district' and 'Magistrate' for interpretation purposes.
The definition of 'cattle' is broader than just horned cattle.

title: THE RECOVERY OF DEBTS AND BANKRUPTCY ACT, 1993
purpose: To provide for the establishment of Tribunals for expeditious adjudication and recovery of debts due to banks and financial institutions, insolvency resolution and bankruptcy of individuals and partnership firms, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as of the last update provided, though a notification extended applicability to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh). The provisions generally apply where the amount of debt due is not less than ten lakh rupees (or a lower amount specified by the Central Government).
