Penalties can be recovered from the proprietor if the driver or owner is unknown or cannot be found, subject to certain provisos (Section 13).
Penalties and balances of fines, costs, or charges can be levied by distress and sale of movable property by warrant (Section 16).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate or Commissioner of Police of a Presidency-town.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through licensing, inspection, seizure of non-compliant carriages, imposition of fines, and recovery through distress and sale of property. Summons can be issued and served by registered post. Offenders may be apprehended and detained if penalties are not paid.

rights: Right of a proprietor to have their name substituted in the license upon transfer of ownership without extra charge for the year.
Right of surplus proceeds from the sale of a seized carriage and horse, if claimed within two months.
duties: Duty of proprietors to ensure stage-carriages are licensed and comply with all provisions of the Act.
Duty to have license particulars painted on the carriage.
Duty to not exceed the licensed number of passengers or luggage, or use fewer animals than specified.
Duty to prevent ill-treatment of animals.
Duty of drivers to operate safely and without misconduct.
obligations: Obligation to pay license fees.
Obligation to pay imposed penalties and fines.
Obligation to cooperate with enforcement authorities.

key_procedures: Application for a stage-carriage license.
Refusal or granting of a license with specified particulars.
Painting of license particulars on the stage-carriage.
Seizure of non-compliant stage-carriages.
Adjudication of penalties by Magistrate or Commissioner of Police.
Recovery of penalties through distress and sale of property.
Apprehension and detention of offenders if penalties are not paid.
Issuance and service of summons via registered post.
administration: Magistrate or Commissioner of Police of a Presidency-town. State Governments have powers to fix license fees and grant exemptions.
important_notes: The Act has been amended over time and its application may be subject to local laws.
Provisions related to 'Chief Commissioner of Police' have been repealed.
The Act applies to all animals used for drawing stage-carriages, not just horses.

title: THE INDIAN TOLLS ACT, 1864
purpose: To amend Act 8 of 1851 (for enabling Government to levy Tolls on Public Roads and Bridges). It provides for the levy of certain rates of toll.
scope: The Act applies to public roads and bridges for which tolls are leviable. The State Government has the power to extend this Act and Act 8 of 1851 to various places. It has been extended to numerous scheduled districts and Union territories over time, with some repeals in specific regions.

main_sections.description: This section, which dealt with the Schedule of Act 8 of 1851, has been omitted by the Devolution Act, 1920.

main_sections.section_title: Collectors of tolls may compound for tolls leviable under Act 8 of 1851 or this Act.
main_sections.description: Allows persons managing toll collection to compound with individuals for a fixed sum, not exceeding one year, in lieu of statutory toll rates.
Grants the State Government the authority to extend this Act to places where Act 8 of 1851 is in force, and vice versa.
This section, related to interpretation and local government, has been repealed by the A.O.1937.

important_rules: Collectors of tolls are empowered to agree upon a fixed sum with individuals for toll payments for themselves or their vehicles/animals, for a period not exceeding one year.
The State Government can extend the application of the Indian Tolls Act, 1864 to any place where Act 8 of 1851 is already in force.
The State Government of a place where Act 8 of 1851 is not in force can extend both Act 8 of 1851 and the Indian Tolls Act, 1864 to that place.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and persons entrusted with the management of toll collection.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levying of tolls on public roads and bridges, and through the compounding of such tolls by authorized collectors.

rights: Right of the Government to levy tolls on public roads and bridges (established by Act 8 of 1851 and amended by this Act).
Right of toll collectors to compound for tolls.

key_procedures: Compounding of tolls: A person managing toll collection may, at their discretion, agree with an individual for a fixed sum for toll payment, valid for up to one year.
Extension of Act: The State Government can formally extend the applicability of the Indian Tolls Act, 1864, and Act 8 of 1851 to specific geographical areas.
administration: State Government, and individuals entrusted with the management of toll collection.
important_notes: The schedule of Act 8 of 1851 was repealed and a new schedule substituted, which has since been omitted.
The Act has been extended to various territories and has also been repealed in certain regions like Mysore.
The Act is to be deemed in force in Punjab from March 24, 1864, and tolls levied prior to the Indian Tolls Act, 1888 are deemed lawful.
The Bombay Presidency has its own governing Act for tolls (Tolls on Roads and Bridges Act, 1875), but Act 15 of 1864 is deemed to have been extended thereto.

title: The Saráís Act, 1867
purpose: To provide for the regulation of public Saráís and Puraos.
scope: The Act initially extends to the territories under the government of the Lieutenant Governor of the North-West Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal. The State Government can extend it to other territories, excluding Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay. It applies to all public Saráís and Puraos, with exceptions for those under direct management of the State Government or Municipal Committees (except for Section 8).

key_definitions.Saráí: Any building used for the shelter and accommodation of travellers, including parts of a building used as such. It also includes a Purao to the extent the Act's provisions are applicable.
key_definitions.Keeper of a Sarai: Includes the owner and any person having or acting in the care or management thereof.
key_definitions.Magistrate of the District: The chief officer charged with the executive administration of a district in criminal matters, whatever may be his designation.

main_sections.description: This section originally dealt with the repeal of Bengal Regulation 14 of 1807, section 11, Clause 5, and has been repealed by the Amending Act, 1891.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Saráí', 'Keeper of a Saráí', and 'Magistrate of the District'.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of this Act to be given to keepers of Saráís
main_sections.description: Requires the Magistrate of the District to give written notice of the Act to keepers of Saráís and require them to register their Saráí.

main_sections.section_title: Registers of Saráís to be kept
main_sections.description: Mandates the Magistrate of the District to maintain a register of Saráís, including the names and residences of keepers and the situation of the Saráís. No charge shall be made for such entries.

main_sections.section_title: Lodgers, &c., not to be received in Saráís until registered
main_sections.description: Prohibits the reception of any lodger, person, cattle, animal, or vehicle in a Saráí until the Saráí and its keeper are registered.

main_sections.section_title: Magistrate may refuse to register keeper not producing certificate of character
main_sections.description: Empowers the Magistrate to refuse registration of a Saráí keeper if they do not produce a certificate of character as directed by the State Government.

Outlines the obligations of Saráí keepers, including reporting infectious diseases, providing access for inspection, keeping the Saráí clean, removing noxious vegetation, maintaining repairs, providing watchmen, and exhibiting a list of charges.

main_sections.section_title: Power to order reports from keepers of Saráís
main_sections.description: Grants the Magistrate the power to require Saráí keepers to report on persons who resorted to the Saráí, either orally or in writing, using provided schedules if necessary.

main_sections.section_title: Power to shut up, secure, clear, and clean deserted Saráís
main_sections.description: Allows the Magistrate to take action to secure, enclose, clean, or clear deserted Saráís that have become a nuisance, with expenses recoverable from the owner or through sale of materials.

main_sections.section_title: Taking down or repairing ruinous Saráís
main_sections.description: Empowers the Magistrate to order the taking down, repair, or securing of ruinous or dangerous Saráís, with expenses recoverable from the keeper.

main_sections.section_title: Sale of materials of ruinous Saráís
main_sections.description: Permits the Magistrate to sell the materials of ruinous Saráís taken down under Section 10 to cover expenses, returning any surplus to the owner or recovering any deficit.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for permitting Saráís to be filthy or overgrown
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties on Saráí keepers who allow their Saráís to be in a filthy, unwholesome, or overgrown state after receiving notice or being convicted of such an offense.

main_sections.section_title: Power for State Government to make regulations
main_sections.description: Authorizes the State Government to make regulations for the better attainment of the Act's objects, which must be published in the official gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for infringing Act or regulations
main_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty not exceeding twenty rupees for each offense against the Act or regulations, with a further daily penalty for continuing offenses. Penalties are recoverable as fines under the Code of Criminal Procedure.

main_sections.section_title: Conviction for third offence to disqualify persons from keeping Saráís
main_sections.description: Stipulates that a keeper convicted of a third offense under this Act will be disqualified from keeping a Saráí without the written license of the Magistrate, who can withhold or grant it on conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Nothing in Act to apply to certain Saráís
main_sections.description: Exempts Saráís directly managed by the State Government or Municipal Committees from the provisions of the Act, except for Section 8.
Specifies the initial territorial extent of the Act and grants power to the State Government to extend it to other territories.
Provides the short title for the Act: The Saráís Act, 1867.

important_rules: Saráí keepers must notify the nearest police station if any person in the Saráí is ill of an infectious disease or dies of it.
Saráí keepers must provide free access and allow inspection of the Saráí by authorized Magistrates or persons.
Saráí keepers must thoroughly cleanse rooms, verandahs, drains, and water sources to the satisfaction of the Magistrate.
Saráí keepers must remove noxious vegetation and trees/branches that could aid thieves.
Saráí keepers must keep the gates, walls, fences, roofs, and drains in repair.
Saráí keepers must provide a sufficient number of watchmen for the safety of persons and animals, as deemed necessary by the Magistrate.
Saráí keepers must exhibit a list of charges for the use of the Saráí in a designated place, form, and language.
Saráí keepers must report to the Magistrate about every person who resorted to the Saráí during the preceding day or night when required.
Owners or claimants of deserted Saráís must secure, enclose, clean, or clear them upon receiving notice from the Magistrate.
Keepers of ruinous Saráís must take down, repair, or secure them within three days of receiving notice from the Magistrate.

penalties: For infringing Act or regulations: A penalty not exceeding twenty rupees for each offense.
For continuing offenses: A further penalty not exceeding one Rupee per day.
For allowing a Saráí to remain filthy or overgrown after notice or conviction: Liable to penalties provided in Section 14.
Expenses incurred by the Magistrate in cleansing or clearing deserted or ruinous Saráís are recoverable as penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate of the District
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through conviction before any Magistrate. Penalties are recoverable in the same manner as fines under the Code of Criminal Procedure. Expenses incurred by the Magistrate for cleansing or repairs are also recoverable.

rights: Right of travelers to shelter and accommodation in registered Saráís.
Right of the Magistrate to inspect Saráís.
Right of the owner of materials of a ruinous Saráí to any surplus proceeds from sale after expenses.
duties: Duty of Saráí keepers to register their Saráís.
Duty of Saráí keepers to maintain hygiene and safety standards.
Duty of Saráí keepers to report diseases and provide access for inspection.
Duty of owners of deserted Saráís to secure and clean them.
Duty of Saráí keepers to display charges.
Duty of the Magistrate to maintain a register of Saráís.
obligations: Obligation of Saráí keepers to comply with the Act and any regulations made thereunder.
Obligation of owners of Saráís to pay for expenses incurred by the Magistrate in securing or repairing ruinous Saráís.
Obligation of persons to obtain a license from the Magistrate to keep a Saráí after a third conviction.

key_procedures: Registration of Saráís: Keepers must be given notice by the Magistrate to register their Saráí. The Magistrate maintains a register.
Inspection of Saráís: Saráí keepers must provide free access to Magistrates or authorized persons for inspection.
Reporting infectious diseases: Keepers must notify the nearest police station about infectious diseases or deaths.
Dealing with deserted Saráís: Magistrate can give notice to owners to secure/clean; if not complied with, Magistrate can execute work and recover expenses.
Dealing with ruinous Saráís: Magistrate can order repairs/demolition; if not complied with, Magistrate executes work and recovers expenses from the keeper.
Sale of materials of ruinous Saráís: Magistrate can sell materials to cover expenses.
Making regulations: State Government can make, repeal, alter, or add to regulations, which must be published in the official gazette.
administration: Magistrate of the District, with oversight and rule-making powers by the State Government.
important_notes: Section 1 has been repealed.
The definition of 'Magistrate of the District' should now be read as 'District Magistrate'.
Certain words and definitions ('L.G.') have been repealed or amended by later acts.
The Act has been extended to various Scheduled Districts and other areas through notifications.
Section 8 applies to all Saráís, while other sections do not apply to Saráís under direct management of the State Government or Municipal Committees.

title: THE BOMBAY CIVIL COURTS’ ACT, 1869
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the District and Subordinate Civil Courts in the Presidency of Bombay.
scope: Extends to the territories (other than Sind) under the Government of the Governor of Bombay in Council in which the Code of Civil Procedure is in force. The Governor of Bombay in Council may extend this Act to other territories under such Government or to Sind.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as "The Bombay Civil Courts’ Act, 1869" and defines its territorial extent.
Empowers the Governor of Bombay in Council to alter the limits of existing Districts and create new ones by notification in the Government Gazette.
Empowers the Governor of Bombay in Council to alter the position of Sadr stations in existing Districts and fix them in new Districts.
Establishes a District Court in each District presided over by a District Judge, who is appointed, suspended, or removed by the Governor of Bombay in Council.
Specifies that the District Court is ordinarily held at the Sadr station but can be held elsewhere within the District with High Court sanction.
Declares the District Court as the principal Court of original civil jurisdiction in the District.
States that the District Court is the Court of Appeal from all decrees and orders of Subordinate Courts, except as provided in specific sections.

Grants the District Judge general control over Civil Courts and their establishments within the District, including inspection and direction on matters not covered by law. Also requires referral of matters to the High Court for rule-making.

main_sections.section_title: Writs and orders. Reports and returns.
main_sections.description: Mandates the District Judge to obey writs and orders from the High Court, make returns, and furnish reports and returns as required by the High Court or the Governor of Bombay in Council.
Describes the seal to be used by the District Judge: a circular seal two inches in diameter with the Royal Arms and specified inscription.

Allows the Governor of Bombay in Council, with Governor General's sanction, to appoint Joint Judges with co-extensive powers and concurrent jurisdiction with the District Judge, with certain limitations.

main_sections.section_title: Enactments applying to District Judge to apply to Joint Judge. Joint Judge’s seal.
main_sections.description: States that regulations and acts applying to District Judges also apply to Joint Judges, and that the Joint Judge uses the same seal as the District Judge.
Authorizes the Governor of Bombay in Council to appoint one or more Assistants to the District Judge, with the power to suspend or remove them.
Specifies that Assistant Judges ordinarily hold court at the same place as the District Judge but can hold it elsewhere with District Judge and High Court sanction.
Details the original jurisdiction of Assistant Judges, including referral of suits and applications by the District Judge, and specifies appeal routes based on the subject-matter value.
Allows the Governor of Bombay in Council to empower Assistant Judges to try appeals referred by the District Judge, with decrees and orders having the same force as those of a District Judge.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of Assistant Judge’s appellate jurisdiction.
main_sections.description: States that conferred appellate jurisdiction continues as long as the individual holds the office of Assistant Judge, but can be withdrawn by the Governor of Bombay in Council.

main_sections.section_title: Power to invest Assistant Judge with powers of District Judge.
main_sections.description: Enables the Governor of Bombay in Council to invest Assistant Judges with all or any powers of a District Judge within a specific part of a District, altering jurisdiction accordingly.

main_sections.section_title: Assistant Judge to use seal of District Judge.
main_sections.description: Requires Assistant Judges to use the seal of the District Judge to whom they are Assistant.
Specifies that the number of Civil Courts subordinate to the District Court is determined by the Governor of Bombay in Council.
Outlines the appointment of Subordinate Judges by the Governor of Bombay in Council and sets qualifications for the role.

main_sections.section_title: Power to fix local limits of jurisdiction of Subordinate Judges.
main_sections.description: Grants the Governor of Bombay in Council the power to fix and alter the local limits of the ordinary jurisdiction of Subordinate Judges.
Details the location of Subordinate Courts, the fixing of sitting days, and the possibility of one person holding multiple Subordinate Court judgeships.
Divides Subordinate Judges into two classes and defines the jurisdiction of each class based on the value of the subject-matter.

main_sections.section_title: Special jurisdiction of Subordinate Judge of first class.
main_sections.description: Mentions that Subordinate Judges of the first class exercise special jurisdiction in addition to their ordinary jurisdiction.
Refers to appeals from the decisions of Subordinate Judges.

main_sections.section_title: Appellate jurisdiction of Subordinate Judge of first class.
main_sections.description: Details the appellate jurisdiction of a Subordinate Judge of the first class.

main_sections.section_title: Power to invest Subordinate Judges with small cause powers.
main_sections.description: Grants the power to invest Subordinate Judges with small cause powers.
Addresses the seal to be used by Subordinate Judges.
Deals with the reference of Government suits.

main_sections.section_title: Commission of enquiry into alleged misconduct.
main_sections.description: Provides for commissions of inquiry into alleged misconduct of judges.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension of Subordinate Judges by High Court or District Judge.
main_sections.description: Allows for the suspension of Subordinate Judges by the High Court or District Judge, saving the Government's power to suspend or dismiss.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary vacancy of office of District Judge.
main_sections.description: Addresses temporary vacancies in the office of the District Judge.

main_sections.section_title: Delegation of powers of District Judge.
main_sections.description: Allows for the delegation of powers of the District Judge.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary vacancy of office of Subordinate Judge.
main_sections.description: Deals with temporary vacancies in the office of a Subordinate Judge.
Covers the appointment and other aspects of ministerial officers.
Outlines the duties of ministerial officers.

main_sections.section_title: Power to appoint Clerks of the Courts.
main_sections.description: Grants the power to appoint Clerks of the Courts.
Allows for the making of rules for keeping proceedings.
Covers fees for process.
Relates to the sittings of Courts and their vacation periods.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Governor of Bombay in Council, High Court, District Judge
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment, suspension, removal, and direction of judicial officers and ministerial staff, as well as through control and inspection of courts.

duties: District Judge's duty: general control over Civil Courts, inspection of proceedings, giving necessary directions, referring matters to High Court.
District Judge's duty: obey writs/orders from High Court, make returns/reports.
Subordinate Judge's duty: hold Courts at appointed places, notify sitting days, follow rules for time in each court if serving multiple.
Ministerial officers' duties as prescribed.
obligations: District Judges are liable to suspension or removal by the Governor of Bombay in Council.
Assistant Judges must use the District Judge's seal.
Subordinate Judges must follow prescribed qualifications for appointment.
Judicial officers must obey directions and rules set by higher authorities.

key_procedures: Alteration/creation of Districts and fixing Sadr Stations: Notification by Governor of Bombay in Council in Government Gazette.
Appointment of Judges (District, Joint, Assistant, Subordinate): By Governor of Bombay in Council, with specific sanctions/controls.
Holding of Courts: Ordinarily at Sadr station, or elsewhere with sanction.
Referral of suits/applications to Assistant Judge: By District Judge, subject to value limits.
Appeals: To District Judge or High Court based on value, or to Assistant Judge as empowered.
Suspension/Removal of Judges: By Governor of Bombay in Council (District Judges), or High Court/District Judge (Subordinate Judges).
Inquiry into misconduct: Through a commission of enquiry.
Fixing local limits of Subordinate Judges' jurisdiction: By Governor of Bombay in Council.
Setting sitting days for Subordinate Courts: By District Judge, subject to High Court control.
administration: Governor of Bombay in Council, with oversight from the Governor General of India in Council and the High Court.
important_notes: Section 2 repealed by the Obsolete Enactments Act, 1870.
Some parts of Section 5 and 14 were repealed by Act 12 of 1876.
Certain words in Section 16 were repealed by Act 7 of 1889.
Section 22A was inserted by Act 9 of 1880.
The Schedule is marked as repealed.

title: The Dehra Dun Act, 1871
purpose: To give validity to the operation of the General Regulations and Acts within the district of Dehra Dun.
scope: Applies to the Dehra Dun district, excluding the portion known as Jaunsar Bawar. It extends the regulations and acts in force in Saharanpur to Dehra Dun.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of Regulations and Acts in force in Saharanpur to Dehra Dun
main_sections.description: Declares that the Regulations and Acts currently in force in the district of Saharanpur are hereby extended to the district of Dehra Dun.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of High Court and Board of Revenue over Dehra Dun
main_sections.description: States that the High Court and the Board of Revenue of Uttar Pradesh shall exercise in Dehra Dun all the powers they are authorized to exercise in any part of Agra.

main_sections.section_title: District Court of Saharanpur to be District Court of Dehra Dun
main_sections.description: Establishes that the District Court of Saharanpur shall serve as the District Court of Dehra Dun until the State Government directs otherwise.
Specifies that the provisions of this Act do not apply to the part of the Dehra Dun district known as Jaunsar Bawar.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: High Court and Board of Revenue of Uttar Pradesh, and the District Court of Saharanpur.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of their existing authorized powers within the Dehra Dun district.

administration: The administration of the Dehra Dun district, including the application of regulations and acts, is overseen by the State Government and judicial authorities as specified.
important_notes: The Act was amended by the A. O. 1950, substituting 'Uttar Pradesh' for 'the North-Western Provinces'.
Certain words and phrases have been repealed by Act 16 of 1874 and Act 12 of 1891.

title: THE MADRAS CIVIL COURTS’ ACT, 1873
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the Civil Courts of the Madras Presidency subordinate to the High Court.
scope: Extends to all territories under the government of the Governor of Fort. St. George in Council, except the tracts under the jurisdiction of the Agents for Ganjam and Vizagapatam. Applies to the establishment, constitution, jurisdiction, and administration of Civil Courts in the Madras Presidency.

key_definitions.District Judge: The Judge of a District Court.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date it comes into force.
Empowers the Local Government to fix and alter the number of District Courts, with the sanction of the Governor General in Council for any increase.

main_sections.section_title: Number of Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs
main_sections.description: Empowers the Local Government to fix and alter the number of Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs for each District, with the sanction of the Governor General in Council for any addition.

Specifies that the place at which any Court shall be held can be fixed and altered by the Local Government for District Courts and Subordinate Judge's Courts, and by the High Court for District Munsif's Courts. Places fixed for a Court are deemed to be within its local jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment to vacancy in office of District Judge or Subordinate Judge
main_sections.description: Details the process for appointing a duly qualified person to a vacant office of District Judge or Subordinate Judge, or when an addition to their numbers is sanctioned.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment to vacancy in office of District Munsif
main_sections.description: Details the process for appointing a person to a vacant office of District Munsif, or when an addition to their numbers is sanctioned by the High Court, subject to qualifications. It also covers the publication and annulment of such appointments.

main_sections.section_title: District Courts, Subordinate Judges, and District Munsifs
main_sections.description: Designates existing Zila Courts, Principal Sadar Amins, and District Munsifs as the respective District Courts, Subordinate Judges, and District Munsifs under this Act.
Requires every Court to use a seal of a form and dimensions prescribed by the Local Government.

main_sections.section_title: Local limits of jurisdiction of District Court or Subordinate Judge
main_sections.description: States that the Local Government shall fix and vary the local limits of jurisdiction for District Judges or Subordinate Judges. If multiple Subordinate Judges are in a district, the District Judge may assign their specific local limits.

States that the High Court shall fix and modify the local jurisdiction of District Munsifs. If multiple District Munsifs are assigned the same local jurisdiction, the High Court will designate a Principal District Munsif and others as Additional District Munsifs.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of District Judge or Subordinate Judge in original suits
main_sections.description: Confers jurisdiction to District Judges and Subordinate Judges over all original suits and proceedings of a civil nature, subject to the Code of Civil Procedure. The jurisdiction of a District Munsif extends to suits and proceedings where the subject-matter does not exceed two thousand five hundred rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals from decrees of District Courts
main_sections.description: Outlines the appellate jurisdiction: appeals from District Courts lie to the High Court. Appeals from Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs lie to the District Court, unless the subject-matter exceeds five thousand rupees, in which case they lie to the High Court. It also provides for the High Court to direct appeals from District Munsifs to Subordinate Judges' Courts and for the District Judge to manage such appeals.

main_sections.section_title: Valuation of suits for immovable property
main_sections.description: Specifies how the value of suits concerning land, houses, or gardens is to be fixed for jurisdictional purposes, as provided by the Court Fees' Act, 1870.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require witness or party to make oath or affirmation
main_sections.description: Grants Courts the power to require witnesses or parties to make oaths or affirmations as prescribed by law.

main_sections.section_title: Law administered by Courts to Natives
main_sections.description: Defines the rules of decision for questions of succession, inheritance, marriage, caste, or religious usage/institution for Muhammadans (Muhammadan law) and Hindus (Hindu law), or any custom having the force of law. In cases lacking specific rules, Courts must act according to justice, equity, and good conscience.

main_sections.section_title: Judges not to try suits in which they are interested; nor to try appeals from decrees passed by them in other capacities
main_sections.description: Prohibits Judges from trying suits or proceedings in which they are personally interested or from hearing appeals against decrees or orders they passed in another capacity. Such cases must be reported to the superior Court for disposal.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension of Judge by Local Government
main_sections.description: Empowers the Local Government to suspend or remove any District Judge, Subordinate Judge, or District Munsif for misconduct.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension of Subordinate Judge by High Court
main_sections.description: Allows the High Court to suspend a Subordinate Judge in urgent cases pending orders from the Local Government, and requires the High Court to report the circumstances immediately.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension of District Munsif by High Court. Commission of Inquiry
main_sections.description: Empowers the High Court to suspend a District Munsif alleged to have misconducted himself or to appoint a commission for inquiry. It applies Act XXXVII of 1850 to such inquiries and grants the High Court powers to remove, suspend, or reduce the Munsif based on the inquiry report.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension of District Munsif by District Judge
main_sections.description: Grants District Judges the power to suspend a District Munsif under their control in urgent cases, requiring them to report the circumstances and evidence to the High Court for its order.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment, suspension or removal of Ministerial Officers of District Courts
main_sections.description: States that Ministerial Officers of District Courts are appointed, suspended, or removed by the Judges of those Courts, subject to the High Court's control, with their orders being final in such matters.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and removal of ministerial officers of subordinate Courts
main_sections.description: Specifies that Ministerial Officers of Subordinate Judges' Courts and District Munsifs' Courts are appointed and removed by those respective Judges and Munsifs, subject to approval or confirmation.

main_sections.section_title: Rules regulating such appointments. Duties of Ministerial Officers. Present Ministerial Officers
main_sections.description: Refers to rules regulating appointments of ministerial officers, their duties, and the status of present ministerial officers.
Introduces provisions for the transfer of Ministerial Officers.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary discharge of duties of District Judge
main_sections.description: Addresses the temporary discharge of duties of a District Judge.

main_sections.section_title: District Judge may nominate to vacancy in office of District Munsif
main_sections.description: Allows the District Judge to nominate individuals for vacancies in the office of District Munsif.

main_sections.section_title: District Judge to control Civil Courts of District
main_sections.description: Establishes the District Judge's control over the Civil Courts within their District.

main_sections.section_title: Investiture of District or Subordinate Judge with Small Cause jurisdiction. Investiture of District Munsif with similar jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Deals with the conferral of Small Cause Court jurisdiction upon District Judges, Subordinate Judges, and District Munsifs.

main_sections.section_title: Exercise by Subordinate Judge of jurisdiction of District Judge in certain proceedings
main_sections.description: Allows a Subordinate Judge to exercise the jurisdiction of a District Judge in specific proceedings.
Refers to court vacations.

important_rules: Rule for appointing District Judges and Subordinate Judges by the Local Government.
Rule for appointing District Munsifs by the High Court, subject to qualifications and Local Government sanction.
Rule for fixing and altering court localities by Local Government or High Court.
Rule for fixing and varying local limits of jurisdiction for District Judges and Subordinate Judges by the Local Government.
Rule for fixing and modifying local jurisdiction of District Munsifs by the High Court.
Rule for jurisdiction of District Judges and Subordinate Judges over all civil suits and proceedings.
Rule for jurisdiction of District Munsifs up to a subject-matter value of two thousand five hundred rupees.
Rule for appeals from District Courts to the High Court.
Rule for appeals from Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs to the District Court (or High Court if value exceeds five thousand rupees).
Rule regarding the law to be administered to Natives, based on Muhammadan law, Hindu law, or custom, and justice, equity, and good conscience where no specific rule exists.
Rule prohibiting Judges from trying suits or appeals in which they are interested.
Rule regarding the suspension or removal of Judges for misconduct by the Local Government.
Rule regarding the suspension of Subordinate Judges by the High Court.
Rule regarding the suspension or inquiry into misconduct of District Munsifs by the High Court.
Rule regarding the suspension of District Munsifs by the District Judge, with reporting to the High Court.
Rule for appointment, suspension, or removal of Ministerial Officers of District Courts by the Judges thereof, subject to High Court control.
Rule for appointment and removal of Ministerial Officers of subordinate Courts by Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs, subject to approval.

penalties: Suspension or removal of Judges (District Judge, Subordinate Judge, District Munsif) for misconduct.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local Government, High Court, District Judge.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through suspension and removal of judicial officers, commissions of inquiry for misconduct, and by directing the disposal of suits and appeals.

rights: Right of parties to have their cases heard in accordance with specified laws and equity.
Right to appeal certain court decisions.
duties: Duty of Judges to avoid trying cases in which they are interested.
Duty of Courts to administer law according to the Act and principles of justice, equity, and good conscience.
Duty of High Court to report suspensions of Subordinate Judges to the Local Government.
Duty of District Judges to report suspensions of District Munsifs to the High Court.
Duty of Ministerial Officers to perform their duties as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation for Courts to use a prescribed seal.
Obligation for judicial officers to report circumstances of disqualification or interest to superior courts.
Obligation for High Court to apply provisions of Act XXXVII of 1850 for inquiries into misconduct.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointing District Judges and Subordinate Judges.
Procedure for appointing District Munsifs.
Procedure for fixing court localities and local limits of jurisdiction.
Procedure for appeals from decrees and orders of various civil courts.
Procedure for handling suits or appeals where a Judge is interested.
Procedure for suspension and removal of Judges for misconduct.
Procedure for conducting inquiries into the misconduct of District Munsifs.
Procedure for appointment, suspension, and removal of ministerial officers.
administration: The administration of this Act involves the Local Government (for establishing courts, appointing certain judges, and for general administrative powers), the High Court (for appointing District Munsifs, fixing their jurisdiction, and for control over certain suspensions), and the District Judge (for control over civil courts within the district and temporary suspensions of District Munsifs).
important_notes: The Act extends to specific territories within the Madras Presidency.
Certain sections have been repealed and amended by subsequent acts (e.g., Repealing Act, 1873; Act 21 of 1885).
The jurisdiction of District Munsifs is limited by the monetary value of the subject-matter of suits.
Specific religious laws and customs are to be applied in cases concerning Natives.

title: The Government Savings Promotion Act, 1873
purpose: To regulate and channelise savings from the general public into Government Savings Schemes, and to amend the law relating to the payment of deposits in Government Savings Banks.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to accounts opened under any of the Savings Schemes, deposits in Government Savings Banks (including Post Office Savings Banks, State Bank of India, banking companies, or other specified institutions), and pertains to savings of individuals, minors, deceased persons, and persons of unsound mind.

key_definitions.account: An account opened under any of the Savings Schemes.
key_definitions.administrator: An administrator as defined in clause (a) of section 2 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925.
key_definitions.authorised_officer: An officer authorized by the Director General Posts (for Post Office Savings Bank) or by the State Bank of India, a banking company, or any other company or institution (for other institutions).
key_definitions.banking_company: A banking company as defined in clause (c) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
key_definitions.depositor: An individual by whom, or on whose behalf, money has been deposited in a Government Savings Bank. 'Deposit' means the money so deposited.
key_definitions.executor: An executor as defined in clause (c) of section 2 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925.
key_definitions.government_savings_bank: A Post Office Savings Bank; or State Bank of India or a banking company, or any other company or institution, as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.guardian: In relation to a minor or a person of unsound mind, it means either of the parents; where neither parent is alive or capable of acting, a person entitled under law to care of the property; or a legal guardian appointed by a court.
key_definitions.minor: A person who has not attained the age of majority under the Indian Majority Act, 1875.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.savings_schemes: The Government Savings Schemes, including Savings Certificates and Public Provident Fund Scheme, listed in the Schedule.
key_definitions.schedule: The Schedule annexed to this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Government Savings Promotion Act, 1873' and specifies its local extent to the whole of India.
This section was omitted by the Finance Act, 2018 and previously related to the Act not applying to deposits in Anchal Savings Bank.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'account', 'administrator', 'Authorised Officer', 'banking company', 'depositor', 'executor', 'Government Savings Bank', 'guardian', 'minor', 'prescribed', 'Savings Schemes', and 'Schedule'.

Empowers the Central Government to frame, amend, or discontinue Savings Schemes by notification in the Official Gazette to promote household savings. It also allows for the inclusion or omission of schemes in the Schedule and specifies provisions that can be included in a scheme (eligibility, terms, interest, limits, closure, loans, transfer, etc.).

Allows a minor of ten years or older to open and operate an account if permitted by a Savings Scheme. It also allows the guardian of a minor to open and operate an account on behalf of the minor until they become a major.

Deals with the nomination of individuals to receive sums due in case of the depositor's death. It specifies that nominees can be designated by guardians for minors or persons of unsound mind. A nomination becomes void if the nominee predeceases the depositor. If a nominee is a minor, a person can be appointed to receive the deposit during the nominee's minority. Transfer of a deposit cancels a previous nomination.

Outlines the process for payment of deposits upon the depositor's death. If a nomination is in force, payment is made to the nominee. If the nominee is a minor, payment is made to an appointed person or the minor's guardian. If there are multiple nominees and some are deceased, payment is made to the survivors. If the deposit belongs to a minor or person of unsound mind without a nominee, it is paid to the guardian. If no nomination is in force and no probate or letters of administration are produced within three months, the Authorised Officer may pay the deposit (up to a prescribed limit) to any person appearing entitled to receive it or administer the estate, following prescribed procedures.

main_sections.section_title: Payment to be a discharge. Saving of right of executor. Saving of right of creditor.
main_sections.description: States that payments made according to the Act are a full discharge from liability. It preserves the right of executors or administrators to recover funds from the recipient after debts are paid. It also allows creditors or claimants to recover their debts from money paid to any person if it remains unadministered in their hands.

Authorizes the Authorised Officer of a Government Savings Bank to take security from persons receiving money under sub-section (4) of section 4A for the due administration of that money. The security can be assigned to interested parties.

main_sections.section_title: Power to administer oath. Penalty for false statements.
main_sections.description: Grants Authorised Officers the power to administer oaths or affirmations to ascertain entitlement to deposits. Any person making a false statement under oath or affirmation is deemed guilty of an offence under section 193 of the Indian Penal Code.
Empowers the Central Government, through a designated authority, to call for information, documents, and evidence necessary for carrying out the purposes of the Act in relation to any account.

main_sections.section_title: Deposit when excluded in computing court fees.
main_sections.description: Specifies that if the amount of a deceased depositor's estate in a Government Savings Bank does not exceed a prescribed limit, it is excluded when computing court fees on probate, letters of administration, or a succession certificate. The claimant must provide a certificate of the deposit amount signed by the Authorised Officer.
This section was omitted by the Government Savings Banks (Amendment) Act, 1959, and previously dealt with the Act not applying to deposits belonging to estates of European soldiers or deserters.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of deposits to minor or guardian.
main_sections.description: Allows deposits made by or on behalf of a minor to be paid to the minor personally (if they made the deposit) or to their guardian (for the minor's use) along with accrued interest. The receipt of the minor or guardian serves as a sufficient discharge.
This section was omitted by the Government Savings Banks (Amendment) Act, 1959, and previously dealt with the legalization of past payments.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of deposits belonging to lunatics.
main_sections.description: Concerns the payment of deposits belonging to lunatics. (The full details are not provided in the excerpt, but it implies a process for handling such deposits).

main_sections.section_title: Operation of account by differently abled persons.
main_sections.description: Relates to the operation of accounts by differently-abled persons. (Details are not fully present in the excerpt).
This section was omitted. Its previous content is not specified in the excerpt.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection against liability for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act or any rule or direction made thereunder.
Offers protection against attachment for any amount deposited in a Government Savings Bank under this Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any prior enactments and contains savings provisions, ensuring that actions taken or rights accrued under the repealed laws are not affected.

important_rules: Deposits made by or on behalf of a minor can be paid to the minor (if they made the deposit) or their guardian, along with interest. The receipt of the minor or guardian is a sufficient discharge.

Nominees can be designated to receive sums due upon the depositor's death. If a nominee predeceases the depositor, the nomination becomes void. If the nominee is a minor, a person can be appointed to receive the deposit during the nominee's minority.
Upon the death of a depositor with a valid nomination, the deposit shall be paid to the nominee. If the nominee is a minor, payment is made to an appointed person or the guardian.

If no nomination is in force and legal documentation (probate, letters of administration, succession certificate) is not produced within three months of death, the Authorised Officer may pay deposits up to a prescribed limit to the person appearing entitled, following prescribed procedures.
Payments made according to the Act's provisions serve as a full discharge from liability.
Creditors or claimants against a deceased depositor's estate can recover their debts from money paid under the Act that remains unadministered in the recipient's hands.

penalties: Any person who makes a false statement under oath or affirmation during an inquiry under this Act is deemed guilty of an offence under section 193 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised Officers of Government Savings Banks, and the Central Government through any designated authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Authorised Officers have powers to administer oaths, take evidence, and call for information. The Central Government can frame rules and notifications to govern savings schemes and their operation. Enforcement involves payment procedures for deceased depositors, minors, and lunatics, and the possibility of taking security for due administration.

rights: Depositors have the right to nominate individuals to receive their deposits upon death.
Nominees have the right to receive deposits upon the depositor's death, subject to the nomination's validity.
Executors, administrators, or representatives of a deceased depositor have the right to recover remaining funds from the recipient after due administration.
Creditors or claimants have the right to recover their debts from unadministered funds paid to a recipient.
Minors, through their guardians, have the right to operate accounts and receive deposits.
Persons claiming to be entitled to deposits of a deceased depositor have the right to receive payment after establishing their entitlement.
duties: Depositors have a duty to provide accurate information when opening accounts and making nominations.
Nominees have a duty to administer received deposits appropriately.
Individuals receiving deposits of deceased persons have a duty to administer the estate and settle debts lawfully.
Authorised Officers have a duty to ensure due administration of money paid out, and may take security for this purpose.
Individuals must not make false statements under oath or affirmation during inquiries.
The Central Government has a duty to frame and notify Savings Schemes to promote household savings.
obligations: Those who receive payments under sub-section (4) of section 4A have an obligation to administer the money due and properly.
Claimants for probate, letters of administration, or a succession certificate must provide a certificate of the deposit amount to the Court.

key_procedures: Opening and operating accounts by minors (aged 10+ or via guardian) if permitted by a Savings Scheme.
Making nominations for deposits, including appointing a guardian for a minor nominee.

Payment of deposits upon the death of a depositor: first to nominee, then to appointed person if nominee is minor, then to guardian if nominee is minor and no person appointed, or to guardian if deposit belongs to a minor/person of unsound mind without a nominee. If no nomination, payment to entitled person after 3 months or within prescribed limits at the Authorised Officer's discretion.
Authorised Officers administering oaths and taking evidence to ascertain entitlement to deposits.
Excluding certain deposit amounts from court fee computation for probate, letters of administration, or succession certificates, upon presentation of a certificate from the Authorised Officer.
administration: The Central Government (through Authorised Officers and designated authorities) is responsible for administering this Act, including framing rules and notifications for Savings Schemes and overseeing their implementation.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various Union territories over time.
Section 2 and Section 9 have been omitted by subsequent amendments.
The definition of 'Authorised Officer' has been updated to include officers from State Bank of India, banking companies, and other institutions.
The definition of 'minor' is linked to the Indian Majority Act, 1875.
The definition of 'Savings Schemes' includes Savings Certificates and Public Provident Fund Scheme as listed in the Schedule.
Payments made in accordance with the Act's provisions are considered a full discharge from liability.
The Act provides protection against attachment for amounts deposited in Government Savings Banks.

title: The Northern India Canal and Drainage Act, 1873
purpose: To regulate irrigation, navigation, and drainage in Northern India, acknowledging the State Government's entitlement to use and control water resources for public purposes and amending existing laws related to these areas.
scope: Extends to Uttar Pradesh and territories previously comprised in Punjab and Delhi. Applies to all lands, whether permanently settled, temporarily settled, or revenue-free.  Specifically applies to the use and control of water from rivers, streams, lakes, and natural collections of still water for irrigation, navigation, and drainage works.

key_definitions.canal: Includes State Government-constructed or maintained canals, channels, reservoirs for water supply or storage, associated works, and parts of rivers, streams, lakes, or natural drainage channels to which Part II of the Act is applied.
key_definitions.water-course: A channel supplied with water from a canal, not maintained at the State Government's cost, and its subsidiary works.
key_definitions.drainage-work: Includes escape channels, dams, weirs, embankments, sluices, groins, and other works for land protection from flood or erosion, maintained by the State Government, but excludes sewage removal works from towns.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes boats, rafts, timber, and other floating bodies.
key_definitions.commissioner: A Commissioner of a division, or an officer exercising Commissioner's powers under the Act.
key_definitions.collector: The head revenue officer of a district, or an officer exercising Collector's powers under the Act.
key_definitions.canal-officer: An officer appointed to exercise control or jurisdiction over a canal or part thereof. Includes Superintending, Divisional, and Sub-divisional Canal-officers.
key_definitions.district: A district as fixed for revenue purposes.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical and land applicability.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'canal', 'water-course', 'drainage-work', 'vessel', 'Commissioner', 'Collector', 'Canal-officer', and 'District'.
Empowers the State Government to declare officers responsible for specific powers and duties within defined local limits, and establishes a hierarchy of authority for Canal-officers.

main_sections.section_title: Notification to issue when water-supply is to be applied for public purposes.
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the State Government to notify its intention to use water from natural sources for existing or projected canals or drainage works, specifying a notice period.

main_sections.section_title: Damage for which compensation shall not be awarded. Matters in respect of which compensation may be awarded.
main_sections.description: Specifies types of damage for which compensation will not be awarded (e.g., percolation stoppage, climate deterioration) and those for which it may be awarded (e.g., stoppage of water supply to channels, works for profit, irrigation, water-courses, or other substantial damage).

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter and survey, etc. Power to clear land. Power to inspect and regulate water-supply. Notice of intended entry into houses. Compensation for damage caused by entry.
main_sections.description: Grants powers to Canal-officers to enter land for surveys, clear land, inspect and regulate water supply, with provisions for notice before entering houses and compensation for damage caused.

main_sections.section_title: In absence of written contract, water-supply to be subject to rules.
main_sections.description: States that in the absence of a written contract, water supply will be governed by the rules established under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Liability when person using unauthorizedly cannot be identified.
main_sections.description: Determines liability for water use when the unauthorized user cannot be identified.

main_sections.section_title: Charge on occupier for water, how determined. “Occupier’s rate.”
main_sections.description: Defines how the charge for water supplied to an occupier is determined, referred to as 'Occupier's rate'.
Introduces the concept of an 'Owner's rate' for water supply.
Establishes that certified amounts due under the Act are recoverable in the same manner as land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Detainer of vessels violating rules. Liability of owners of vessels causing damage.
main_sections.description: Covers the detainer of vessels that violate rules and establishes the liability of vessel owners for any damage caused.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit obstructions or order their removal.
main_sections.description: Grants the power to prohibit obstructions in drainage paths or to order their removal.
Defines the term 'labourer' in the context of obtaining labour for canal and drainage works.
Outlines the offences defined by the Act and prescribes the penalties for them.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make, alter and cancel rules. Publication of rules.
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to create, modify, and repeal rules under the Act, with provisions for their publication.

important_rules: Water-supply for public purposes requires a State Government notification, specifying a date not earlier than three months from the notification date for its commencement (Section 5).
Canal-officers have powers to enter land, remove obstructions, close channels, and take necessary actions for the application or use of water after the specified date (Section 6).

Compensation may be awarded for specific damages, such as stoppage or diminution of water supply to defined channels, works for profit, or irrigation, and for other substantial damages. Compensation is determined by considering the diminution in market value or annual net profits (Section 8).
Canal-officers can enter any land for surveys, clearing land, inspecting, and regulating water supply, with notice required for entering houses and compensation for damages (Section 14).
Persons desiring to use canal water must apply, and may be held liable for the cost of any necessary works (Section 16).
In the absence of a written contract, water supply is subject to the rules made under the Act (Section 31).
Certified amounts due under the Act are recoverable as land revenue (Section 45).
Owners of vessels causing damage while navigating canals are liable for such damage (Section 49).
Obstructions in drainage paths can be prohibited or ordered for removal, with powers to remove them if not complied with (Sections 55-56).

penalties: Penalties for offences defined under the Act (Section 70).
Fines for offences in navigating canals (Section 50).
Charges recoverable in addition to penalties for unauthorized use or waste of water (Section 35).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Collectors, and Canal-officers are the primary authorities for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers granted to Canal-officers for entering land, removing obstructions, closing channels, and regulating water supply; through the recovery of certified dues as land revenue; through the seizure and detention of vessels and cargo for unpaid charges; and through prosecution for offences defined under the Act.

rights: Right to claim compensation for certain damages caused by the application or use of water (Section 8).
Right to means of crossing canals, provided by the Government (Section 17).
Right to use water-courses, subject to conditions and payment of rates.
Right to make objections to proposed construction or transfer of water-courses (Section 24).
duties: Duty to construct works for passing water across roads, etc., if using a water-course (Section 18).
Duty to pay water-rates as determined by the Act (Parts V).
Duty to comply with rules regarding canal navigation (Part VI).
Duty to allow labourers to be supplied for urgently required canal and drainage works (Part VIII).
Duty to adhere to conditions binding on applicants placed in occupation of land for water-course construction or transfer (Section 29).
obligations: Obligation of applicants for new water-courses to pay expenses before occupation (Section 28).
Obligation of landowners to allow the State Government to use and control water for public purposes.
Obligation of persons using water-courses to maintain them as per the Act's provisions.
Obligation for owners of vessels to pay for damage caused.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying water for public purposes: State Government issues notification, Collector gives public notice of intent and compensation claims, Canal-officer takes necessary actions (Sections 5-7).

Procedure for construction/transfer of water-courses: Application by individuals, Canal-officer's procedure including objections, placement in occupation, and recovery of expenses and compensation (Sections 21-30).
Procedure for recovery of dues: Certified dues are recoverable as land-revenue; Lambardars may be required to collect canal-dues (Sections 45-47).

Procedure for recovery of charges on seized vessels/cargo: Seizure and detention of vessels/cargo for unpaid charges, followed by procedures for recovery and disposal of sale proceeds (Sections 51-54).

Procedure for obtaining labour: Identification of 'labourers', prescription of numbers to be supplied by beneficiaries, and procedure for obtaining labour for urgently required works (Sections 63-66).
administration: The State Government, through various appointed officers including Canal-officers, Commissioners, and Collectors, administers this Act. Rule-making authority also rests with the State Government (Section 75).
important_notes: Certain types of damage are explicitly excluded from compensation awards (Section 8(a)-(d)).
The Act clarifies that no right to canal-water is acquired merely by user (Section 32).
The Act allows for the prosecution of offenders under other relevant laws, in addition to the penalties prescribed by this Act (Section 71).
The Act defines 'labourer' for the purpose of obtaining labour for essential works, indicating a potential for compulsory labour under specific circumstances (Section 63).

title: THE LAWS LOCAL EXTENT ACT, 1874
purpose: To declare the local extent of certain Acts passed by the Governor General of India in Council, the Legislative Council of India, and the Council of the Governor General of India assembled for the purpose of making Laws and Regulations; and to consolidate the laws relating to the local extent of certain Acts and Regulations in the Presidencies of Fort St. George and Bombay, and in the Lower and the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.
scope: The act defines the local extent of various enactments across different regions of India, specifically mentioning the Presidencies of Fort St. George and Bombay, and the Lower and North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal. It also refers to 'Scheduled Districts' which are defined in the sixth schedule.

key_definitions.Scheduled Districts: The territories mentioned in the sixth schedule annexed to the Act.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Laws Local Extent Act, 1874.
Defines the term 'Scheduled Districts' as the territories mentioned in the sixth schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Local extent of Acts in first schedule.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Acts mentioned in the first schedule are in force throughout India, excluding the territories comprised in Part B States (as of November 1, 1956) and the Scheduled Districts.

main_sections.section_title: Local extent of enactments in second schedule.
main_sections.description: States that the enactments in the second schedule are in force throughout the territories subject to the government of the Governor of Fort St. George in Council, excluding the Scheduled Districts under that government.

main_sections.section_title: Local extent of enactments in third schedule.
main_sections.description: States that the enactments in the third schedule are in force throughout the territories subject to the government of the Governor of Bombay in Council, excluding the Scheduled Districts under that government.

main_sections.section_title: Local extent of enactments in fourth schedule.
main_sections.description: States that the enactments in the fourth schedule are in force throughout the territories subject to the government of the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal, excluding the Scheduled Districts under that government.

main_sections.section_title: Local extent of enactments in fifth schedule.
main_sections.description: States that the enactments in the fifth schedule are in force throughout the territories subject to the government of the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William, excluding the Scheduled Districts under that government.

This section outlines several exceptions and clarifications, including the power of the Central or State Government to extend Acts, the operation of existing extensions to Scheduled Districts, the revival of repealed enactments, and the extension of laws to specific towns or areas.
This section indicates that the enactments mentioned were repealed by the Repealing Act, 1876 (12 of 1876).

important_rules: The Acts mentioned in the first schedule are in force throughout India, except for Part B States and Scheduled Districts.
Enactments in the second schedule apply to the territories under the Governor of Fort St. George in Council, excluding Scheduled Districts.
Enactments in the third schedule apply to the territories under the Governor of Bombay in Council, excluding Scheduled Districts.
Enactments in the fourth schedule apply to the territories under the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal, excluding Scheduled Districts.
Enactments in the fifth schedule apply to the territories under the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces, excluding Scheduled Districts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be governmental authorities based on the context of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By determining the local extent of various enactments.

key_procedures: Determination of the local application of specific Acts and Regulations based on their inclusion in the various schedules.
The Act itself serves as a declaration of the existing or intended local extent of other legal instruments.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the relevant governmental departments responsible for legislation and administration in the respective territories.
important_notes: The Act has been subject to numerous repeals and amendments over time, as indicated by footnotes referencing subsequent legislation.
The definition of 'Scheduled Districts' is crucial for understanding the scope of the Act and the enactments it references.
The Act's relevance is tied to the historical administrative divisions and legal framework of British India.

title: The Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876
purpose: To provide relief for landholders in Chutia Nagpur who are in debt and whose immoveable property is subject to mortgages, charges, and liens.
scope: Applies to landholders in Chutia Nagpur whose immoveable property is encumbered by debts and liabilities other than those due to the Government. It covers the management and settlement of such properties and debts.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to vest management of property in an officer appointed by Commissioner
main_sections.description: Describes the process by which the Commissioner can appoint a Manager and vest in them the management of a landholder's immoveable property upon application by the landholder, their guardian, heir, or curator, or when the property is attached by a Civil Court. This application must state that the holder is subject to debts or liabilities other than those due to the Government.

Outlines the consequences of the vesting order, including barring pending suits, freeing the holder and heir from arrest for prior debts, making their moveable property not liable for attachment for prior debts, ceasing the power to alienate property, freeing immoveable property from attachment (except for government debts), and ceasing the power to contract pecuniary liabilities.

main_sections.section_title: Manager to receive rents and profits, and pay therefrom
main_sections.description: Specifies the duties of the Manager, which include receiving rents and profits, and paying from these sums the Government demand, rent due to superior landlords, annual sums for maintenance of the holder and their family, costs of repairs and improvements, costs of management, and finally, the debts and liabilities.

main_sections.section_title: Notice to claimants against holder of property
main_sections.description: Mandates the Manager to publish notices in English, Urdu, and Hindi, calling upon all claimants to notify their claims within three months. The notice is to be posted at kachahris and other suitable places. It also details how the notice should be published.

Requires claimants to provide full particulars of their claim, along with all supporting documents. If a document is an entry in a book, the claimant must produce the book and a copy of the entry. Documents not produced at this stage may be excluded as evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Debt not duly notified to be barred
main_sections.description: States that any debt or liability not duly notified to the Manager within the specified time and manner will be barred. It includes a provision for admitting claims within an additional nine months if the claimant proves inability to comply with earlier provisions.
Grants the Manager the power to determine the amount of principal debts, liabilities, and interest justly due to creditors and holders of mortgages, charges, or liens.

main_sections.section_title: Power to inquire into consideration for leases
main_sections.description: Empowers the Manager, with the sanction of the Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner, to inquire into the consideration for leases granted within the three years preceding the vesting order. The Manager can set aside such leases or require payment of adequate consideration.

Establishes an appeal process against decisions made under sections six, seven, eight, or nine. Appeals lie first to the Deputy Commissioner, and then to the Commissioner. If the Deputy Commissioner is the Manager, the appeal goes directly to the Commissioner.
Requires the Manager to prepare and submit a schedule of debts and a scheme for their settlement to the Commissioner for approval. The Commissioner can return the scheme for revision.

main_sections.section_title: Restoration of owner to his property
main_sections.description: Details the conditions under which the owner is restored to their property: either when all debts and liabilities are discharged, or if the Commissioner decides within six months that the Act's provisions should no longer apply. It also outlines the revival of barred proceedings and debts, and reinstatement of mortgagees in certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Power to call for further particulars
main_sections.description: Allows the Manager to request further and more detailed particulars of any claim and to refuse to proceed if these are not supplied.

main_sections.section_title: Power to summon witnesses and compel production of documents
main_sections.description: Grants the Manager powers similar to those of a Civil Court to summon witnesses and compel the production of documents.

main_sections.section_title: Investigation to be deemed a judicial proceeding
main_sections.description: Declares that investigations under the Act are to be considered judicial proceedings, and statements of persons examined are admissible as evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Manager to have powers of holder of estate
main_sections.description: States that the Manager shall have the powers of the holder of the estate, including the power to remove a mortgagee or conditional vendee in possession.
Grants the Manager the power to lease the property.

main_sections.section_title: Power to raise money by mortgage or sale
main_sections.description: Empowers the Manager to raise money by mortgaging or selling the property, and specifies that the Manager's receipts are valid.
Provides the power to make rules under the Act.
Allows for the appointment of new Managers.
Declares that Managers are to be considered public servants.
Bars suits against the Government or any person for anything done or purporting to be done under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of jurisdiction of Courts in Chutia Nagpur in respect of certain suits
main_sections.description: Saves the jurisdiction of Courts in Chutia Nagpur regarding certain suits not affected by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to affect powers conferred by Bengal Act II of 1869
main_sections.description: Clarifies that this Act does not affect powers conferred by Bengal Act II of 1869.

important_rules: A Manager appointed under the Act must receive and recover all rents and profits from the encumbered property.

From collected rents and profits, the Manager must pay Government revenue, rent to superior landlords, maintenance for the holder and their family, costs of repairs and improvements, management costs, and then apply the residue to debts and liabilities.

All claimants against the encumbered property holder must notify their claims in writing to the Manager within three months of the vesting order publication, providing full particulars and all supporting documents.

Debts or liabilities not duly notified within the prescribed time and manner are barred, unless a claim is admitted within a further nine months due to proven inability to comply with notification requirements.
The Manager has the power to determine the just amount of all principal debts, liabilities, and interest due.
The Manager can inquire into the consideration for leases granted within three years prior to the vesting order and may set aside or modify such leases if the consideration is deemed insufficient.
An appeal process is established for decisions regarding claims and debts, first to the Deputy Commissioner and then to the Commissioner.
The Manager must prepare a scheme for the settlement of debts, subject to the Commissioner's approval.
The owner is restored to their property after all debts are discharged or if the Commissioner deems the Act's provisions no longer applicable within six months of the vesting order.
The Manager has the power to summon witnesses, compel the production of documents, and conduct investigations that are deemed judicial proceedings.
The Manager possesses the powers of the estate holder, including removing mortgagees or conditional vendees in possession.
The Manager can lease the property and raise money by mortgage or sale.
Managers are considered public servants.

penalties: Section 3(First): All pending proceedings, processes, executions, and attachments related to the debts and liabilities become null and void.
Section 3(Second): The holder and heir are not liable to arrest for prior debts (other than government debts).
Section 3(Second): Moveable property is not liable to attachment or sale for prior debts (other than government debts).
Section 3(Third): The holder and heir are incompetent to mortgage, charge, lease, or alienate their immoveable property or grant valid receipts for rents and profits.
Section 3(Third): Immoveable property is exempt from attachment or sale (except for government debts).
Section 3(Third): The holder and heir are incapable of entering into any contract that involves pecuniary liability.
Section 7: Debts or liabilities not duly notified are barred.
Section 9: Leases with insufficient consideration may be set aside, or the holder of the lease may be required to pay appropriate consideration, failing which the lease is cancelled.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, and the appointed Manager.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of a Manager who takes control of the property, investigates and settles debts, manages the property's income and expenses, and enforces the provisions of the Act. Enforcement also includes legal barring of suits and claims, and potential cancellation of leases.

rights: Right of the landholder or heir to receive an annual sum for maintenance from the property's income.
Right to be restored to possession and enjoyment of the property once debts are discharged, or if the Commissioner decides the Act's provisions should cease.
Right to appeal decisions regarding claims and debts.
Right for mortgagees or conditional vendees dispossessed under section sixteen to be reinstated if their claim is unsatisfied.
Right to have a portion of the time between restoration and the vesting order excluded for limitation periods on revived proceedings and debts.
duties: Duty of the Manager to receive and recover all rents and profits.
Duty of the Manager to pay Government demand, rent to superior landlords, maintenance sums, repair costs, management costs, and debts/liabilities.
Duty of claimants to notify claims with full particulars and supporting documents.
Duty of the holder and heir to cease alienating property and entering into new pecuniary liabilities once management is vested.
obligations: Obligation to notify all debts and liabilities to the Manager within three months.
Obligation to provide full particulars and supporting documents for all claims.
Obligation of the landholder to allow management of their property by the appointed Manager.
Obligation of the holder and heir to refrain from mortgaging, charging, leasing, alienating, or entering into contracts with pecuniary liability while management is vested.

key_procedures: Application by the landholder (or guardian/heir) to the Deputy Commissioner for the Act's provisions to be applied.
Commissioner's decision to appoint a Manager and publish a vesting order in the Calcutta Gazette.
Manager publishes notices calling for claims within three months.
Claimants submit claims with full particulars and documents.
Manager investigates claims and determines debts, with rights of appeal to the Deputy Commissioner and then the Commissioner.
Manager prepares and submits a scheme for debt settlement to the Commissioner.
Upon discharge of debts or Commissioner's decision, the owner is restored to their property.
If restoration occurs under specific conditions, barred proceedings and debts are revived, and mortgagees may be reinstated.
administration: The Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner, with the Manager appointed to administer specific properties.
