important_notes: The Act does not apply to debts or liabilities due to the Government, except for the Government demand (revenue).
Moveable property of the holder and heir is not liable for attachment for prior debts other than those due to the Government.
The Act provides for the potential revival of barred proceedings and debts upon restoration of the owner in certain circumstances.
The Act does not affect powers conferred by Bengal Act II of 1869.

title: The Northern India Ferries Act, 1878
purpose: To regulate ferries in Northern India.
scope: This Act extends to Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, the Central Provinces, Assam, Delhi, and Ajmer. It applies to all ferries, including bridges of boats, pontoons, rafts, swing-bridges, flying-bridges, and temporary bridges, along with their approaches and landing places.

key_definitions.ferry: Includes a bridge of boats, pontoons or rafts, a swing-bridge, a flying-bridge and a temporary bridge, and the approaches to, and landing-places of, a ferry.
key_definitions.Punjab: Means the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the State of Punjab.
key_definitions.Ajmer: Means the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the State of Ajmer.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and the procedure for its commencement in different territories.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'ferry', 'Punjab', and 'Ajmer'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare, establish, define and discontinue public ferries
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to declare ferries as public ferries, establish new ones, define their limits, change their course, and discontinue them. These actions are to be done via official gazette notifications.

Vests the immediate superintendence of public ferries in the District Magistrate or another appointed officer, unless management is vested in a municipality or local board. This officer is responsible for arrangements for boats and toll collection.

main_sections.section_title: Management may be vested in municipality
main_sections.description: Allows the State Government to direct that a public ferry within a town's limits be managed by the municipal authority.

main_sections.section_title: Management may be vested in District Council or District or Local Board
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to direct that a public ferry within the jurisdiction of a District Council or Local Board be managed by that council or board.
Outlines the process for letting out ferry tolls by public auction for a specified term, requiring approval from higher authorities. It also details conditions for the lessee.

Empowers the Commissioner or other appointed officer, under the control of the State Government, to make rules for the control, management, and regulation of public ferries, including rules for letting tolls, construction of bridges, and boat operations. Also includes a provision for laying rules before the State Legislature.

main_sections.section_title: Private ferry not to ply within two miles of public ferry without sanction
main_sections.description: Prohibits the establishment or operation of a private ferry within a two-mile radius of a public ferry without sanction. Allows for modifications to this distance by the State Government and specifies exceptions.

States that tolls, at rates fixed by the State Government, shall be levied on all persons, animals, vehicles, and other things crossing a river by a public ferry, unless exempted by the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for breach of provisions as to table of tolls, list of tolls and return of traffic
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for violating provisions related to toll tables, lists of tolls, and traffic returns.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for taking unauthorised toll, and for causing delay
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for levying unauthorized tolls and for causing delays in ferry operations.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for breach of rules made under sections 12 and 19
main_sections.description: Details penalties for contravening rules made under sections 12 and 19 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for maintaining private ferry within prohibited limits
main_sections.description: Establishes penalties for operating a private ferry within the prohibited distance of a public ferry.
Grants the power to arrest individuals without a warrant for offenses under this Act.
Allows for the summary trial of certain offenses under this Act.
Ousts the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters covered by this Act.

important_rules: Private ferries cannot operate within two miles of a public ferry without official sanction, though the State Government can modify this distance or grant exemptions. Exceptions exist for certain types of plying between places with a minimum distance.
Anyone using the approaches or landing places of a public ferry is liable to pay the applicable toll.
Tolls are to be levied on all persons, animals, vehicles, and other things crossing a river by a public ferry, unless specifically exempted by the State Government.
The lessee of ferry tolls must conform to the rules made for the management and control of the ferry and provide security for good conduct and punctual rent payment.
Lessee must make traffic returns as required by the overseeing officer.
Rules can be made for regulating the time and manner of constructing and maintaining bridges of boats, pontoons, or rafts, and for opening them for passage of vessels and rafts.

penalties: Penalty for breach of provisions as to table of tolls, list of tolls and return of traffic.
Penalty for taking unauthorized toll, and for causing delay.
Penalty for breach of rules made under sections 12 and 19.
Penalty for maintaining private ferry within prohibited limits.
Penalties on passengers offending.
Penalty for rash navigation and stacking of timber.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate of the district, State Government, Commissioner of a division, or other appointed officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties, fines, cancellation of leases, arrest without warrant, and summary trials.

rights: Right to compensation for loss sustained due to a private ferry being taken over as a public ferry.
Right to use public ferries upon payment of authorized tolls.
Right to have ferries managed and maintained according to established rules.
duties: Duty to pay tolls for using public ferries.
Duty to comply with rules and regulations governing ferry operations.
Duty of lessees to manage ferries according to lease terms and rules.
Duty of lessees to provide necessary boats and maintain them in good condition.
Duty to report traffic returns.
obligations: Obligation to establish and maintain public ferries as directed by the State Government.
Obligation to ensure the safe and efficient operation of ferries.
Obligation to ensure that private ferries do not infringe on the rights of public ferries.

key_procedures: Declaring, establishing, defining, and discontinuing public ferries through notification in the Official Gazette.
Vesting management of public ferries in municipalities or district boards.
Letting ferry tolls by public auction, with approval or sanction from relevant authorities.
Recovery of arrears from lessees as if they were arrears of land-revenue.
Cancellation of a lease by the State Government with prior notice and payment of compensation.
Surrender of a lease by the lessee upon notice and payment of compensation.
Making rules for ferry management and operations by Commissioners or appointed officers, subject to State Government control.
Seeking sanction from the Magistrate for operating a private ferry near a public ferry.
administration: The State Government, Commissioners of divisions, District Magistrates, and Municipal authorities or District/Local Boards as directed.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various territories and amended by subsequent legislation.
Provisions exist for joint exercise of powers by State Governments when a river lies between two States.
Alterations in ferry course or limits due to river changes can be made by an order of the Commissioner or an appointed officer.
The State Government can exempt certain persons, animals, vehicles, or other things from toll payment.
Jurisdiction of Civil Courts is barred in matters related to this Act.

title: THE LEGAL PRACTITIONERS ACT, 1879
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to Legal Practitioners in certain Provinces, and to empower Provincial Governments to extend such portions of the Act as they deem fit to other Provinces.
scope: Initially applied to specific provinces in British India, with provisions for extension to other provinces. The scope of application has been significantly modified over time due to subsequent legislation, particularly the Advocates Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: Repealed by the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 2023.
Repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938.
Repealed by the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 2023.
Repealed by the Advocates Act, 1961.
Repealed by the Advocates Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to make rules as to qualifications, etc., of pleaders and mukhtars. Publication of rules.
main_sections.description: Repealed by the Advocates Act, 1961.
Repealed by the Advocates Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules as to qualifications, etc., of revenue-agents.
main_sections.description: Repealed by the Advocates Act, 1961.
Repealed by the Advocates Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: On persons illegally practising as pleaders, mukhtars or revenue-agents.
main_sections.description: Repealed by the Advocates Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Power to frame and publish lists of touts.
main_sections.description: Repealed by the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 2023.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Chapter VI of Bom. Reg. II of 1827 and Acts 1 of 1846 and 20 of 1853.
main_sections.description: Repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938.

penalties: On persons illegally practising as pleaders, mukhtars or revenue-agents (Repealed).
On suspended or dismissed pleader, etc., failing to deliver certificate (Repealed).
On suspended or dismissed practitioner practising during suspension or after dismissal (Repealed).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities were designated, including High Courts and Chief Controlling Revenue Authorities, though many sections related to enforcement have been repealed.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for suspension, dismissal, and penalties for illegal practice, though specific details are largely repealed.

rights: Right to practice as a pleader, mukhtar, or revenue-agent upon obtaining a certificate (provisions largely repealed).
duties: Duty to obtain certificates to practice.
Duty to surrender certificates upon dismissal (provisions repealed).
Duty to adhere to rules regarding qualifications and conduct.
obligations: Obligation to be qualified to practice.
Obligation to not practice illegally or during suspension/dismissal.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining certificates for practice (largely repealed).
Procedure for suspension and dismissal of practitioners for criminal offences or unprofessional conduct (largely repealed).
Procedure for calling for records in cases of professional misconduct (largely repealed).
administration: Initially, Provincial Governments and designated authorities like High Courts and Chief Controlling Revenue Authorities.
important_notes: This Act has undergone extensive amendments and repeals, particularly with the enactment of the Advocates Act, 1961, which has significantly altered its applicability and provisions.
The Second Schedule details the value of stamps for various certificates of practice, indicating fees associated with different levels of practice.

title: The Religious Societies Act, 1880
purpose: To simplify the manner in which certain bodies of persons associated for the purpose of maintaining religious worship may hold property acquired for such purpose, and to provide for the dissolution of such bodies and the adjustment of their affairs and for the decision of certain questions relating to such bodies.
scope: Applies to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. It does not apply to any Hindus, Muhammadans, or Buddhists, or to any persons whom the State Government may from time to time, by notification in the Official Gazette, exclude from its operation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and defines its local extent. It also outlines specific exclusions from its operation.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of new trustee in cases not otherwise provided for.
main_sections.description: Deals with the appointment of new trustees for religious property when no method is prescribed by the governing instrument or when the prescribed method cannot be followed.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment under section 2 to be recorded in a memorandum under the hand of the chairman of the meeting.
main_sections.description: Requires appointments of new trustees under section 2 to be documented in a memorandum signed by the chairman of the meeting, attested by witnesses, and deemed registrable under the Indian Registration Act.

main_sections.section_title: Property to vest in new trustees without conveyance.
main_sections.description: States that upon appointment of new trustees, the trust property will vest in them (jointly with continuing old trustees or wholly if no old trustees remain) without the need for any conveyance or other assurance.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of existing modes of appointment and conveyance.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not invalidate any existing lawful methods of appointing trustees or conveying property.

main_sections.section_title: Provision for dissolution of societies and adjustment of their affairs.
main_sections.description: Allows for the dissolution of religious societies by a majority of not less than three-fifths of the members. It outlines procedures for settling property, claims, and liabilities, with provisions for dispute resolution by the principal Court of original civil jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Upon a dissolution no member to receive profit.
main_sections.description: Stipulates that upon dissolution, any remaining property, after satisfying debts and liabilities, shall not be distributed among members but shall be given to another religious or charitable purpose, as determined by a majority of members or by the Court.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of certain provisions of instruments.
main_sections.description: Exempts provisions related to dissolution and property distribution in existing instruments from the application of sections 6 and 7.

main_sections.section_title: Questions may be submitted to High Court.
main_sections.description: Allows interested parties to submit questions regarding membership or the validity of appointments under the Act to the High Court for an opinion, which will have the force of a declaratory decree.

important_rules: Rule: When a religious society's property is vested in trustees and a new trustee needs to be appointed, but no method is prescribed or the prescribed method cannot be followed, a new trustee may be appointed by agreement of the body or by a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present at a meeting.
Rule: Every appointment of new trustees must be documented in a memorandum signed by the chairman, attested by witnesses, and registered.
Rule: Property vested in trustees shall automatically vest in new trustees without conveyance upon their appointment.
Rule: A religious society can be dissolved by a decision of not less than three-fifths of its members, and steps must be taken to settle its affairs.
Rule: Upon dissolution, any remaining property must be given to another religious or charitable purpose, not distributed among members.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The principal Court of original civil jurisdiction for disputes related to dissolution and adjustment of affairs. The High Court for questions regarding membership or validity of appointments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders in case of disputes during dissolution, and through High Court opinions which have the force of declaratory decrees for questions of membership or appointment validity.

rights: Right to appoint new trustees if no provision exists or if the existing provision is unworkable.
Right to have property vested in new trustees without conveyance.
Right to dissolve the society by a majority vote.
Right to have disputes regarding dissolution adjusted by the Court.
Right to seek the High Court's opinion on questions of membership or appointment validity.
duties: Duty to record appointments of new trustees in a memorandum.
Duty to follow procedures for dissolution and settlement of affairs.
Duty to ensure that no member receives profit upon dissolution.
Duty to comply with Court orders regarding dissolution disputes.
Duty to serve copies of petitions to the High Court on interested parties.

key_procedures: Procedure: Appointment of a new trustee: (1) If no method is prescribed or possible, the body agrees on a method or a majority of at least two-thirds of members present at a meeting appoints the trustee. (2) The appointment is recorded in a memorandum signed by the chairman and attested by two or more witnesses. (3) The property vests in the new trustees without conveyance.

Procedure: Dissolution of a society: (1) A meeting is convened for dissolution. (2) A decision to dissolve is made by not less than three-fifths of the members. (3) Steps are taken to dispose of property and settle claims/liabilities according to the society's rules or the meeting's determination. (4) Disputes are referred to the principal Court of original civil jurisdiction. (5) Remaining property is given to another religious or charitable purpose by member vote or Court decision.
administration: The Act implies administration through the relevant Courts (Principal Court of original civil jurisdiction and High Court) for dispute resolution and clarification, and through the members of the religious societies themselves for operational matters and appointments.
important_notes: Note: The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli and the Union territory of Pondicherry.
Note: The Act does not apply to Hindus, Muhammadans, or Buddhists, or to any groups excluded by the State Government.
Note: Existing lawful methods of appointing trustees and conveying property are not invalidated.
Note: Provisions in existing instruments for dissolution and property distribution are saved and may override sections 6 and 7.
Note: Opinions given by the High Court under section 9 have the force of a declaratory decree.

title: The Kazis Act, 1880
purpose: To empower the Government to appoint persons to the office of Kazi for local areas where a considerable number of Muhammadans desire such appointments, primarily for the celebration of marriages and performance of certain other rites and ceremonies, reversing a previous repeal of such powers.
scope: Applies to the territories administered by the Governor of Fort Saint George in Council initially, with provisions for extension to other territories by the State Government. Specifically concerns the appointment and functions of Kazis for Muhammadan communities within designated local areas.

key_definitions.Kazi: A person appointed by the State Government to perform religious rites and ceremonies, primarily for the Muhammadan community, in a specific local area. The Act clarifies that this appointment does not confer judicial or administrative powers.
key_definitions.Naib Kazi: A person appointed by a Kazi to act in his place in all or any of the matters pertaining to the Kazi's office.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Kazi's Act, 1880. It also defines the initial local extent of the Act, which was the territories administered by the Governor of Fort Saint George in Council, and allows for its extension to other territories.

main_sections.section_title: Power to appoint Kazis for any local area
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint Kazis for any local area if a considerable number of Muhammadans resident therein desire it. It outlines the process of consultation with principal Muhammadan residents and the conclusive decision of the State Government on appointment validity. It also details the grounds and process for suspending or removing a Kazi.

Allows an appointed Kazi to appoint one or more Naib Kazis to act on his behalf. It also states that if a Kazi is suspended or removed, his Naib(s) shall be deemed to be suspended or removed accordingly.

main_sections.section_title: Nothing in Act to confer judicial or administrative powers; or to render the presence of Kazi necessary; or to prevent any one acting as Kazi
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act, and any appointments made under it, do not confer judicial or administrative powers on Kazis or Naib Kazis. It also states that the presence of a Kazi or Naib Kazi is not made necessary for the celebration of marriages or performance of rites, and it does not prevent any other person from performing Kazi functions.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State Government may appoint Kazis for a local area if a significant portion of the Muhammadan residents desire it. (Section 2)
Rule 2: The State Government's decision on the validity of a Kazi's appointment is final. (Section 2)
Rule 3: A Kazi can be suspended or removed for misconduct, prolonged absence, insolvency, desire to resign, unfitness, or incapacity to perform duties. (Section 2)
Rule 4: A Kazi can appoint Naib Kazis to assist or act in his place, and can suspend or remove them. (Section 3)
Rule 5: No judicial or administrative powers are conferred by this Act. (Section 4)
Rule 6: The presence of an appointed Kazi is not mandatory for marriages or other ceremonies. (Section 4)
Rule 7: The Act does not prevent any person from performing the functions of a Kazi. (Section 4)

penalties: No specific monetary penalties or imprisonment are detailed in the provided text for violations of this Act. Enforcement primarily revolves around the State Government's power to appoint, suspend, or remove Kazis and Naib Kazis.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the power to appoint, suspend, and remove Kazis and Naib Kazis, and by extending the Act's provisions to different territories.

rights: The right of Muhammadan residents in a local area to petition for the appointment of a Kazi.
duties: Duty of the State Government to consider petitions for Kazi appointments and to consult principal Muhammadan residents.
Duty of appointed Kazis to perform their functions (implied, though not detailed beyond reference to marriage and rites).
Duty of Naib Kazis to act in the Kazi's place when appointed.
obligations: The State Government has the obligation to appoint persons to the office of Kazi if it deems fit and if the conditions under Section 2 are met.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: For appointing a Kazi: State Government identifies a local area where a considerable number of Muhammadans desire a Kazi, consults with principal Muhammadan residents, and then appoints fit persons if deemed appropriate. The decision of the State Government on appointment validity is conclusive.

Procedure 2: For suspending or removing a Kazi: The State Government can suspend or remove a Kazi if they are guilty of misconduct, absent for six months, leave the area permanently, are declared insolvent, wish to resign, refuse duties, or are deemed unfit or incapable. The Naib Kazi is also affected by the Kazi's suspension or removal.
administration: The State Government is responsible for the administration of this Act, including the appointment, suspension, and removal of Kazis and the extension of the Act's territorial scope.
important_notes: The Act explicitly states that no judicial or administrative powers are conferred by these appointments, nor is the presence of a Kazi made necessary for ceremonies, nor does it prevent others from acting as Kazis.
The Act was amended to reflect changes in the administrative structure of India (e.g., substitution of 'the Provinces' with 'India').
The Act has been extended to various Union territories, including Lakshadweep and Pondicherry, and to certain areas in former presidencies and provinces.

title: THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881
purpose: To define and amend the law relating to Promissory Notes, Bills of Exchange and Cheques.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. It covers instruments in writing that are promissory notes, bills of exchange, or cheques. It also includes provisions for inland and foreign instruments, as well as specific rules for crossed cheques and dishonour of cheques for insufficient funds.

key_definitions.promissory_note: An instrument in writing (not being a bank-note or a currency-note) containing an unconditional undertaking, signed by the maker, to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person, or to the bearer of the instrument.
key_definitions.bill_of_exchange: An instrument in writing containing an unconditional order, signed by the maker, directing a certain person to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person or to the bearer of the instrument.
key_definitions.cheque: A bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and not expressed to be payable otherwise than on demand and it includes the electronic image of a truncated cheque and a cheque in the electronic form.
key_definitions.banker: Includes any person acting as a banker and any post office savings bank.
key_definitions.holder: Any person entitled in his own name to the possession of a negotiable instrument and to receive or recover the amount due thereon from the parties thereto.
key_definitions.holder_in_due_course: Any holder of a negotiable instrument, to whom, or to whose order, the instrument has been transferred for consideration, and who became the holder of the instrument before its amount was overdue and without notice that it had been previously dishonoured.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, Local extent, Saving of usages relating to hundis, etc., Commencement.
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial applicability (whole of India), saves local usages relating to instruments in an oriental language unless an intention to be governed by the Act is indicated, and specifies the commencement date (March 1, 1882).
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'Banker'.
Defines what constitutes a promissory note.
Defines what constitutes a bill of exchange. It clarifies conditions for certainty of amount and payee.
Defines a cheque as a bill of exchange drawn on a banker, payable on demand, and includes electronic forms.
Deals with the delivery of negotiable instruments.

main_sections.section_title: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account.
main_sections.description: Introduces criminal liability for dishonour of cheques due to insufficient funds, a significant addition to the original Act.

important_rules: An instrument must be in writing to be a promissory note or bill of exchange.
The undertaking or order to pay must be unconditional.
The amount payable must be a certain sum of money.
A bill of exchange can be drawn on any person, but a cheque must be drawn on a specified banker.
Negotiation of an instrument can be by delivery or endorsement.
Presentation of a cheque to a banker for payment is crucial to charge the drawer.
Dishonour of a cheque for insufficiency of funds carries penalties.

penalties: For dishonour of cheques due to insufficient funds (Section 138): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of law, empowered to try cases related to dishonour of cheques.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings initiated upon a complaint made to the Magistrate, following specific procedures outlined in Chapter XVII, including service of summons, evidence by affidavit, and summary trials.

rights: Right of the holder to receive payment.
Right of a holder in due course to receive payment even if the instrument was obtained by fraud or for unlawful consideration.
Right of a holder to present a cheque for payment.
Right to receive notice of dishonour.
Right to claim compensation in case of dishonour.
duties: Duty of the maker of a promissory note or drawer of a bill of exchange to pay.
Duty of the drawee to accept a bill of exchange (unless validly refused).
Duty to present cheques for payment within a reasonable time.
Duty to give notice of dishonour.
Duty to pay on demand if the instrument is payable on demand.
Duty of a drawer to make good the loss to the holder if a cheque is dishonoured for want of funds.
obligations: Obligation of parties to an instrument to honour their commitments.
Obligation to pay interest if stipulated or reasonable interest if not.
Obligation to provide indemnity in case of loss of an instrument before payment.
Obligation to inform the bank about any material alteration.

key_procedures: Presentment for acceptance of a bill of exchange.
Presentment for payment of promissory notes, bills of exchange, and cheques.
Giving notice of dishonour to parties liable.
Noting and protesting dishonoured instruments (especially foreign bills).
Procedure for crossing of cheques and payment of crossed cheques.
Procedure for taking cognizance of offences related to dishonour of cheques for insufficient funds, including issuing summons, recording evidence, and passing judgments.
Procedure for appealing convictions under Section 138.
administration: The Act is administered through the judicial system, with powers vested in courts to adjudicate disputes and enforce penalties, particularly for offenses related to dishonoured cheques. The Reserve Bank of India also plays a role in recognizing clearing houses for electronic cheques.
important_notes: The Act does not affect any local usage relating to instruments in an oriental language, provided such usages are not excluded by express intention.
Section 2 was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1891.
Section 138 and subsequent sections related to penalties for dishonour of cheques were introduced later, significantly enhancing the Act's scope and impact on commercial transactions.

title: THE POWERS-OF-ATTORNEY ACT, 1882
purpose: To amend the law relating to Powers-of-Attorney.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. The act covers instruments creating powers-of-attorney and payments/acts made under such powers.

key_definitions.Power-of-Attorney: Includes any instrument empowering a specified person to act for and in the name of the person executing it.

main_sections.description: Declares the short title of the Act as the Powers-of-Attorney Act, 1882, its application to the whole of India, and its commencement date as May 1, 1882.
Defines 'Power-of-Attorney' to include any instrument empowering a specified person to act for and in the name of the person executing it.
Allows the donee of a power-of-attorney to execute or do any instrument or thing in their own name and signature, which will be as legally effective as if done by the donor.

main_sections.section_title: Payment by attorney under power, without notice of death, etc., good
main_sections.description: Protects persons making payments or acts in good faith under a power-of-attorney from liability if the donor had died, become of unsound mind, or insolvent, or had revoked the power, provided these facts were unknown at the time of the act. It also preserves rights against the payee.

main_sections.section_title: Deposit of original instruments creating powers-of-attorney
main_sections.description: Provides for the deposit of original instruments creating powers-of-attorney, along with verification evidence, in the High Court or District Court. It establishes a system for searching, inspecting, and obtaining certified copies of these deposited instruments.

Grants married women of full age the power to appoint an attorney, as if unmarried, to execute non-testamentary instruments or perform other acts they could do themselves. The Act's provisions for powers-of-attorney apply to such appointments.
This section, originally referring to Act 28 of 1866, section 39, has been repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: Donees of a power-of-attorney can execute instruments or perform acts in their own name, and these actions will be legally valid as if done by the donor.

Rule 2: Payments or acts made in good faith under a power-of-attorney are considered valid even if the donor has died, become of unsound mind, insolvent, or revoked the power, provided the person making the payment or act was unaware of these circumstances at the time.
Rule 3: Original instruments creating powers-of-attorney, with verification, can be deposited in the High Court or District Court for public search and inspection.
Rule 4: Certified copies of deposited powers-of-attorney are sufficient evidence of their contents and deposit.
Rule 5: Married women of full age can appoint attorneys to execute non-testamentary instruments or perform other acts they are legally capable of performing themselves.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: High Courts and District Courts are involved in the deposit and certification process.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legal validity of actions taken under powers-of-attorney and the process of depositing and certifying these instruments.

rights: Right of the donee of a power-of-attorney to act in their own name.
Right to deposit original instruments creating powers-of-attorney.
Right to search and inspect deposited instruments.
Right to obtain certified copies of deposited instruments.
Right of a married woman to appoint an attorney.
Right of a person interested in money to pursue remedies against the payee if a payment made under a power-of-attorney was not valid in retrospect.
duties: Duty to act in good faith when making payments or performing acts under a power-of-attorney.
Duty to provide verification evidence (affidavit, statutory declaration) when depositing instruments.
Duty of the court to keep a separate file of deposited instruments and allow searching and inspection.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that payments or acts are made without notice of the donor's death, unsoundness of mind, insolvency, or revocation, to gain protection under Section 3.
Obligation for the High Court to make rules for the deposit and fees, with the concurrence of the State Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for executing acts under a power-of-attorney: The donee executes the instrument or performs the act in their own name and signature, making it legally binding as if done by the donor.

Procedure for protection of payments/acts: A person making a payment or act under a power-of-attorney is protected if they act in good faith and were unaware of the donor's death, unsoundness of mind, insolvency, or revocation at the time.
Procedure for depositing powers-of-attorney: An instrument creating a power-of-attorney, with verified execution, can be deposited in the High Court or District Court.
Procedure for accessing deposited powers-of-attorney: The public can search the file of deposited instruments, inspect them, and obtain certified copies.
Procedure for married women appointing attorneys: A married woman can execute a non-testamentary instrument to appoint an attorney, with the Act's provisions applying.
administration: High Courts and District Courts are involved in the administration of Section 4 concerning the deposit and certification of powers-of-attorney. State Governments are involved in concurring with fee rules made by the High Court.
important_notes: The act has been extended to various Union Territories.
Certain words related to 'lunatic', 'lunacy', and 'bankruptcy' have been omitted through amendments.
Section 6, which repealed a section of the Indian Evidence Act, 1866, has itself been repealed.
Section 5 applies only to instruments executed after the Act comes into force.

title: The Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the Courts of Small Causes established in the Presidency towns (Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay).
scope: Applies to the towns of Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay. Covers jurisdiction, procedure, new trials, appeals, recovery of possession of immovable property, distresses, references to High Court, fees, costs, misconduct of officers, contempt of court, and miscellaneous provisions related to Small Cause Courts.

key_definitions.Small Cause Court: The Court of Small Causes constituted under this Act in the town of Calcutta, Madras or Bombay, as the case may be.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882, and specifies its commencement date as July 1, 1882. It also includes savings for the Army Act and decrees passed before the commencement date.
Defines 'Small Cause Court' and 'Registrar' for the purposes of the Act.
Establishes a Court of Small Causes in each of the towns of Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay.

main_sections.section_title: Court to be deemed under superintendence, etc., of High Court
main_sections.description: Declares that the Small Cause Court is subject to the superintendence of the relevant High Court and subordinate to it, granting the High Court similar powers as it has over courts subject to its appellate jurisdiction.
Provides for the appointment of a Chief Judge and other Judges as deemed fit by the State Government. A Maharashtra amendment allows for the appointment of an Additional Chief Judge.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Registrar and other officers
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Registrar, Deputy Registrar, clerks, bailiffs, and other ministerial officers necessary for the court's administration.

main_sections.section_title: Local limits of jurisdiction of Court
main_sections.description: Specifies the local limits within which the Court has jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Suits in which Court has jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Details the types of suits over which the Court has jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Summons against person occupying property without leave
main_sections.description: Allows for the issuance of a summons against a person occupying property without permission.
Specifies the geographical application of Chapter VIII, which deals with distresses.
Outlines the circumstances under which a reference to the High Court is compulsory.
Deals with the fees charged for instituting suits.
This section has been repealed.
This section has been repealed.

main_sections.section_title: Persons by whom process may be served
main_sections.description: Specifies the individuals authorized to serve court processes.

important_rules: Rules made by the High Court govern the procedure and practice of the Small Cause Court, which can supersede or add to existing provisions (Section 9).
The Chief Judge is responsible for distributing the business of the Court among the Judges (Section 10).

In case of a difference of opinion among Judges, the majority opinion prevails; if equally divided, the Chief Judge or the senior-most Judge has the casting vote (Section 11, with Maharashtra amendment providing for a further hearing by a nominated judge).
Judges or other officers of the Court are prohibited from practicing or trading (Section 15).
The Court is empowered to issue summonses for the recovery of possession of immovable property from unauthorized occupants (Sections 41-49).

Chapter VIII regulates distresses for rent, including the appointment of bailiffs and appraisers, the issuance of distress-warrants, seizure of property, impounding, inventory, notice of sale, and application of proceeds (Sections 50-68).
References to the High Court can be compulsory under certain circumstances, requiring security from the party against whom a contingent judgment is given (Sections 69-70).
Fees are prescribed for the institution of suits and for processes (Sections 71-73).
The Act provides for the punishment of misconduct by inferior ministerial officers (Sections 78-82).
Provisions are made for dealing with contempt of court, including imprisonment for refusing to answer or produce documents (Sections 83-88).

penalties: Penalty for making illegal distresses (Section 68).
Extortion or default of officers can lead to penalties (Section 80).
Imprisonment or committal for contempt of court for refusing to answer or produce documents (Section 87).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Courts of Small Causes, High Courts, and State Governments are involved in the enforcement and administration of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, issuance of warrants, court orders, fines, and imprisonment as prescribed by the Act and related procedural codes.

rights: Right to institute suits within the Court's jurisdiction.
Right to a fair procedure as laid down by the Act and High Court rules.
Right to appeal or seek a new trial in certain cases.
Right to recover possession of immovable property under specific conditions.
Right to compensation for illegal distresses or when an order is obtained without entitlement.
duties: Duty of Judges and officers to administer justice impartially.
Duty to follow the prescribed procedure and practice.
Duty to execute orders and warrants faithfully.
Duty to adhere to the prohibitions against practicing or trading.
Duty to pay prescribed fees and costs.
obligations: Obligation to pay rent for which distress may be levied.
Obligation to provide security when required for references to the High Court.
Obligation to appear and answer in court when summoned.
Obligation to comply with court orders and decrees.

key_procedures: Institution of suits, including the requirement for a plaint and any necessary written statement (e.g., for set-off).
Conduct of trials, including the return of documents, compensation payable in certain cases, and execution of decrees.
Procedure for recovery of possession of immovable property, involving summons, orders for possession, and potential security to bring a suit.
Procedure for distresses, including application for distress-warrant, seizure, inventory, appraisement, sale, and accounting of proceeds.
Procedure for new trials and appeals from decrees and orders of the Small Cause Court.
Procedure for references to the High Court, including compulsory references and security requirements.
Procedure for dealing with misconduct of inferior ministerial officers and contempt of court.
administration: The High Court of Judicature (at Fort William, Madras, or Bombay), and the State Government are responsible for the administration and oversight of the Small Cause Courts.
important_notes: The Act repealed certain previous enactments and amended others (Section 2, 3).
The Act does not affect the Army Act, 1881, or rights/liabilities under decrees passed before July 1, 1882 (Section 1).
High Court rules can significantly alter the procedure and practice of the Small Cause Court (Section 9).

Specific monetary limits and other conditions apply to the jurisdiction and powers of the Court, with provisions for consent to try suits beyond pecuniary limits and transfer of cases to the High Court (Sections 18, 20, 63).
The Act provides for savings for certain rents in the context of distresses (Section 50).
Certain sections related to repeal have been repealed by later acts (e.g., Section 2, 3, 78, 83-86).
The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, is now the relevant legislation for procedural aspects where referenced (Footnote 4).

title: THE PUNJAB DISTRICT BOARDS ACT, 1883
purpose: To make better provision for local self-government in the Districts of the Panjab, by amending the law for the levy and expenditure of rates on land and providing for the constitution, powers, and regulation of district boards and local boards.
scope: Applies to the territories administered by the Lieutenant-Governor of the Panjab. It establishes district boards and local boards within districts, with authority extending throughout the district or a specified portion thereof, excluding military cantonments and municipalities.  The act also concerns the levy and expenditure of local rates on land.

key_definitions.Land: Land assessed to the land-revenue, including land where land-revenue has been released, compounded for, redeemed, or assigned.
key_definitions.Land-revenue: Includes trini or grazing-dues levied for grazing on Government lands.
key_definitions.Landholder: Any person responsible for paying land-revenue, or a proprietor of land where land-revenue has been released, compounded for, redeemed, or assigned.
key_definitions.Annual value: Double the land-revenue assessed on land, with provisions for permanently assessed land, compounded or redeemed land, and land where no land-revenue is assessed. It also includes rates for canal irrigation improvements.
key_definitions.Financial year: The year commencing on the first day of April.
key_definitions.Prescribed day: Such day as the Local Government may prescribe.
key_definitions.Punjab: Refers to the territories comprised in the State of Punjab before November 1, 1956.
key_definitions.Notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.Deputy Commissioner: The Deputy Commissioner of a district, or any officer specially appointed by the Local Government to perform the functions of a Deputy Commissioner under this Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act, specifies its territorial extent to the Panjab territories, and states that it comes into force on dates determined by local government notifications for each district.

Repeals the Panjab Local Rates Act, 1878, from the date the current Act comes into force in a district. Previously imposed rates and notifications under the repealed Act are deemed to have been made under this Act.

Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, including 'Land', 'Land-revenue', 'Landholder', 'Annual value', 'Financial year', 'Prescribed day', 'Punjab', 'Notification', 'Notified', and 'Deputy Commissioner'.

Establishes a local rate on all land, not exceeding one anna for every rupee of its annual value. The proportion of the rate to the annual value is fixed by the Local Government, which may delegate this power to the district board.

main_sections.section_title: Road, school and post cesses to merge in the rate
main_sections.description: Mandates that authorized rates and cesses for roads, schools, and district posts will merge into the local rate from a notified date, and no other rate or cess will be leviable for these purposes thereafter.

Specifies that the landholder is liable for the local rate, with provisos for cases where landholders pay land-revenue in kind to assignees or village headmen, and where the Government pays the local rate on 'trini' under existing leases.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of proceeds of local rate
main_sections.description: Dictates that four-fifths of the net proceeds of the local rate, after collection expenses, are allotted to the district board. The remaining one-fifth goes to the Local Government, which can allot it to district boards or use it for specified public purposes. There are provisions for municipalities and military cantonments.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of district and local boards
main_sections.description: Empowers the Local Government to establish a district board for each district and one or more local boards within districts. The authority of these boards is defined, excluding areas within military cantonments or municipalities.

main_sections.section_title: Number and appointment or election of members
main_sections.description: States that district and local boards will have at least six members, appointed or elected according to rules. It outlines conditions for appointment versus election, ensuring a majority of non-salaried government officials and a significant proportion of landholders.

Specifies that ex-officio members remain on the board while holding office. The term for other members is fixed by the Local Government, not exceeding three years, and may include rotation. Outgoing members are eligible for re-election or re-appointment.
Allows members of local or district boards to resign by notifying the Commissioner in writing. Resignation is effective upon acceptance.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the Local Government as to removal of members
main_sections.description: Grants the Local Government the power to remove members of boards.
Outlines the responsibilities and functions of the district board.
Outlines the responsibilities and functions of the local board.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of taxation conferred on district boards
main_sections.description: Grants district boards the authority to impose certain taxes.
Establishes a district fund for each district board.

main_sections.section_title: Control of Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner over boards and joint committees
main_sections.description: Defines the control exercised by the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner over district boards, local boards, and joint committees.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Local Government to supersede in case of incompetency, persistent default or abuse of powers
main_sections.description: Grants the Local Government the power to supersede a board in cases of incompetence, persistent default, or abuse of power.
Empowers boards to make regulations concerning various matters.
Details the procedures for recovering rates.

main_sections.section_title: Local rate or tax how to be assessed and collected
main_sections.description: Explains the methods for assessing and collecting the local rate or taxes.
Provides for appeals related to rates and taxes.

important_rules: All land is subject to a local rate, not exceeding one anna per rupee of its annual value.
Road, school, and post cesses merge into the local rate.
The landholder is generally liable for the local rate.
Four-fifths of the net local rate proceeds go to the district board.
District boards and local boards must have at least six members.
At least two-thirds of board members must be non-salaried government officials, and at least half must be landholders in the district.
Members' term of office does not exceed three years, with provisions for rotation.
District boards have powers of taxation and are responsible for managing a district fund.
The Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner exercise control over boards.
The Local Government can supersede a board for incompetence, persistent default, or abuse of power.
Boards can make regulations, and infringement of these regulations carries penalties.
Procedures are established for assessing, collecting, and appealing local rates and taxes.

penalties: Penalty for infringement of regulations made by a board (Section 57).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, and the Local Government are the primary enforcement authorities. The Act also implies enforcement through the courts for recovery of rates and taxes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the levy and collection of rates and taxes, the exercise of control and oversight by Commissioners and Deputy Commissioners, the Local Government's power to make rules, supersede boards, and prosecute individuals. Section 70 details the recovery of rates.

rights: Landholders have the right to recover a share of the local rate from occupancy tenants under specific conditions (Section 8).
Landholders have the right to appeal against assessments and collections of rates and taxes (Section 72).
duties: Landholders have a duty to pay the local rate (Section 7).
District boards have a duty to provide for local self-government, manage funds, and perform specific duties (Sections 20, 35, 37).
Local boards have duties within their designated areas (Section 21).
obligations: The Local Government has obligations to establish boards, set rules, and oversee their functions.
Boards have an obligation to conduct their business with proper records and publication of proceedings (Section 25).
Members, officers, and servants of boards have an obligation to avoid being interested in contracts made with a board or joint committee (Section 62).

key_procedures: Procedure for imposing taxes by district boards (Section 31).
Procedure for the establishment and constitution of district and local boards (Sections 10, 11).
Procedure for members to resign (Section 13).
Procedure for the Local Government to supersede a board (Section 51).
Procedure for making rules and regulations (Sections 55, 56, 60).
Procedure for the assessment and collection of local rates and taxes (Section 71).
Procedure for appeals against rates and taxes (Section 72).
administration: The Local Government, through its various officers like the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner, is responsible for the administration and oversight of the Act. District boards and local boards are the primary administrative bodies at the local level.
important_notes: The Act specifies that it extends only to the territories administered by the Lieutenant-Governor of the Panjab.
The Act includes provisions for the merger of existing road, school, and post cesses into the local rate.
Special provisions exist for the management of funds within municipalities and military cantonments.
The Local Government has the power to except any local area from the operation of the Act.
The Act consolidates and updates the law regarding local rates and local self-government in the Panjab.

title: The Deo Estate Act, 1886
purpose: To apply the provisions of the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876, to the Deo Estate in the Gaya District, for the management of the immoveable property of Raja Bhikam Narayan Singh Bahadur due to his debts and liabilities.
scope: This Act applies to the Deo Estate in the Gaya District, specifically to the immoveable property of Raja Bhikam Narayan Singh Bahadur.

key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of the Patna division.
key_definitions.Deputy Commissioner: The Collector of the Gaya district.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Deo Estate Act, 1886' and that it comes into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act VI of 1876 to the Deo Estate
main_sections.description: Details the application of the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876 (and amendments) to the Deo Estate with specific modifications, including definitions of key officials, management of property, inclusion of maintenance recipients, specific debt and interest clauses, priority of certain creditors, conditions for sale of property, and court jurisdiction for claims.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of Priority of Crown debts
main_sections.description: Ensures that the Act does not affect the priority of any debt due or liability incurred to the Government.

important_rules: Modification of definitions: 'Commissioner', 'Deputy Commissioner', and 'holder' are redefined in the context of this Act.
Manager appointment: The Commissioner can appoint a manager without further application from the Raja or consent of the Lieutenant-Governor.
Maintenance claims: Persons entitled to maintenance from the property are included in the scope of the Act.
Debt and interest verification: Debts and interest rates specified in the schedule are deemed justly due unless errors are proven.
Payment priority: The Maharaja of Darbhanga has priority for interest payments on a specific portion of his principal debt.
Conditions for sale of property: Notice to the Maharaja of Darbhanga is required before selling property where he is a mortgagee, and proceeds are subject to his consent until his debt is reduced.
Court jurisdiction for maintenance claims: Suits related to maintenance claims require the previous consent of the Commissioner.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner of the Patna division and the Collector of the Gaya district (acting as Deputy Commissioner).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of a manager and the application of the modified provisions of the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876.

rights: The right of creditors to receive principal and interest due to them (subject to the conditions of the Act).
The right of persons entitled to maintenance to claim from the property.
The priority right of the Maharaja of Darbhanga for interest payments.
The right of the Government to maintain the priority of its debts.
duties: The duty of the Raja to subject his immoveable property to management.
The duty of the manager to manage the property according to the approved scheme.
The duty of the manager to provide notice to the Maharaja of Darbhanga before selling mortgaged property.
The duty to ensure that the Maharaja of Darbhanga's debt is reduced before paying other creditors from sale proceeds.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the conditions of the scheme for debt settlement.
Obligation to obtain consent of the Maharaja of Darbhanga for certain sale proceeds and to leave unsold property sufficient to meet his interest.

key_procedures: Application of the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876, with modifications to the Deo Estate.
Appointment of a manager by the Commissioner.
Vesting of management of the Raja's immoveable property in the manager.
Preparation and approval of a scheme for settlement of debts and liabilities under section 11 of Act VI of 1876, incorporating specific provisions for the Maharaja of Darbhanga.
Enforcement of debt repayment according to the approved scheme.
Procedure for sale of property by the manager, with specific conditions regarding notice and consent for the Maharaja of Darbhanga.
Jurisdiction of Courts for claims, with special consent required for maintenance claims.
administration: The Commissioner of the Patna division and the Collector of the Gaya district.
important_notes: The Act is a special measure to apply a general law (Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876) to a specific estate.
All modifications listed in Section 2 are crucial for the application of the general Act to this specific case.
The schedule provides a detailed list of creditors, principal amounts, interest rates, and balances due as of December 31, 1885.

title: The Bengal, Agra and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to Civil Courts in Bengal, the North-Western Provinces and Assam.
scope: The Act extends to the territories administered by the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal, the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces, and the Chief Commissioner of Assam, excluding areas not subject to the ordinary civil jurisdiction of the High Courts. It also applies to Scheduled Districts and has been extended to various other regions through specific notifications and regulations.

main_sections.description: Provides the title of the Act, its territorial extent of application, and the date it came into force (July 1, 1887).

Repeals the Bengal Civil Courts Act, 1871, and any enactment repealed by it. It also states that courts, appointments, rules, orders, and powers constituted or conferred under the repealed Act shall be deemed to have been constituted, made, conferred, and published under this Act. References to the repealed Act shall be construed as references to this Act.
Establishes the following classes of Civil Courts: the Court of the District Judge, the Court of the Additional Judge, the Court of the Subordinate Judge, and the Court of the Munsif.

main_sections.section_title: Number of District Judges, Subordinate Judges and Munsifs
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to alter the number of District Judges, Subordinate Judges, and Munsifs.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies among District or Subordinate Judges
main_sections.description: Deals with filling vacancies in the office of District Judge or Subordinate Judge due to death, resignation, removal, or other causes, or due to an increase in the number of judges. It allows the State Government or the High Court to fill such vacancies or appoint additional judges. It also permits the appointment of a District Judge or Subordinate Judge to discharge the functions of another judge for a specified period.

Allows the State Government to appoint Additional Judges to assist the District Judge in the speedy disposal of pending business, after consulting the High Court. Additional Judges can discharge any functions assigned by the District Judge and exercise the same powers.
States that the District Judge, subject to the superintendence of the High Court, has administrative control over all Civil Courts within the local limits of his jurisdiction.

Specifies the procedure for assuming temporary charge of the District Court in case of the District Judge's death, resignation, removal, incapacitation, or absence. The Additional Judge or the senior Subordinate Judge present shall assume charge and can exercise the powers of the District Judge under High Court rules.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of proceedings on vacation of office of Subordinate Judge
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for transferring proceedings from the Court of a Subordinate Judge in case of death, resignation, removal, incapacitation, or absence. The District Judge can transfer these proceedings to his own Court or another competent Court. The transferred proceedings will be disposed of as if instituted in the transferee court. The District Judge can also exercise the jurisdiction of the Subordinate Judge's court in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Power to fix local limits of jurisdiction of Courts
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to fix and alter the local limits of the jurisdiction of any Civil Court. If local jurisdiction is assigned to multiple Subordinate Judges or Munsifs, the District Judge can assign specific civil business. It also addresses the validity of decrees or orders made by a judge when a case arises from a place beyond the local area but within the fixed limits. It clarifies that a Small Cause Court Judge also appointed as a Subordinate Judge or Munsif is considered as such for this section. Existing local limits are deemed to be fixed under this section.
Empowers the State Government to fix and alter the place of sitting of Civil Courts.

important_rules: All Civil Courts are constituted under this Act: Court of the District Judge, Court of the Additional Judge, Court of the Subordinate Judge, and Court of the Munsif.
The State Government can alter the number of District Judges, Subordinate Judges, and Munsifs.
In case of vacancies in the office of District or Subordinate Judge, the State Government or High Court can fill the vacancy or appoint additional judges.
Additional Judges can be appointed to assist the District Judge for speedy disposal of business and will discharge functions assigned by the District Judge.
District Judges have administrative control over Civil Courts within their jurisdiction, subject to the High Court's superintendence.
In the absence or incapacitation of a District Judge, the Additional Judge or senior Subordinate Judge assumes temporary charge.
The District Judge can transfer proceedings from a Subordinate Judge's court in case of vacancy or incapacitation.
The State Government can fix and alter the local limits of jurisdiction for Civil Courts.
The State Government can fix and alter the place of sitting of Civil Courts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: High Court (administrative control and superintendence), State Government (appointments, fixing jurisdiction)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the hierarchy of civil courts, administrative control, and jurisdiction assignment as outlined in the Act.

rights: Right of litigants to have their cases heard by designated Civil Courts.
Right of judges to exercise powers assigned to them.
Right of the High Court to superintend Civil Courts.
duties: Duty of District Judges to exercise administrative control over Civil Courts under their jurisdiction.
Duty of Additional Judges and Subordinate Judges to assume charge of the District Court in specified circumstances.
Duty of Judges not to try suits in which they are interested (Section 38 is mentioned in the arrangement but not fully provided in the text).

key_procedures: Filling vacancies in the office of District or Subordinate Judge by the State Government or High Court.
Appointment of Additional Judges by the State Government after consultation with the High Court.
Assuming temporary charge of the District Court by an Additional Judge or senior Subordinate Judge in case of the District Judge's absence or incapacitation.
Transfer of proceedings from a Subordinate Judge's court by the District Judge.
Fixing and altering local limits of jurisdiction by the State Government.
Fixing and altering the place of sitting of Civil Courts by the State Government.
administration: High Court (superintendence and rule-making), State Government (appointments, fixing jurisdiction and limits).
important_notes: The Act has been subject to numerous amendments and extensions to various regions, including Scheduled Districts, and has been modified in its application to specific provinces/states.
Certain sections were repealed by subsequent legislation (e.g., A.O. 1937, Decentralization Act, 1914).
State amendments exist, notably for Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, which substitute 'Civil Judge (Senior Division)' and 'Civil Judge (Junior Division)' for 'Subordinate Judge' and 'Munsif' respectively.

title: The Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887
purpose: To amend the law relating to the tenancy of land in the Punjab.
scope: Applies to the whole of the territories administered by the Lieutenant-Governor of the Punjab, except the Hazara district. It governs the relationship between landlords and tenants, focusing on agricultural land.

key_definitions.land: Land used for agricultural purposes or purposes subservient to agriculture, or for pasture, excluding land occupied as the site of buildings in towns or villages. It includes the sites of buildings and structures on such land.
key_definitions.pay: Includes 'deliver' and 'render' when referring to rent.
key_definitions.rent: Anything payable to a landlord in money, kind, or service by a tenant for the use or occupation of land.
key_definitions.arrear of rent: Rent that remains unpaid after its due date.
key_definitions.tenant: A person holding land under another and liable to pay rent. Excludes inferior landowners, mortgagees of landowner's rights, persons to whom holdings are transferred for recovery of land revenue arrears, and those leasing unoccupied land for subletting.
key_definitions.landlord: A person under whom a tenant holds land and to whom rent is payable.
key_definitions.tenancy: A parcel of land held by a tenant from a landlord under a single lease or set of conditions.
key_definitions.land_revenue: Land revenue assessed or assessable under law, including irrigation betterment rates and sums payable to the government or assigned persons.
key_definitions.improvement: A work suitable to and consistent with the tenancy's conditions that increases and continues to increase its value. It can be executed on the tenancy or for its direct benefit.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Punjab, excluding Hazara district), and the process for its commencement through notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'land', 'rent', 'tenant', 'landlord', 'tenancy', 'land-revenue', and 'improvement'.
Establishes categories of tenants who possess a right of occupancy.

main_sections.section_title: Respective rights of landlord and tenant to produce
main_sections.description: Defines the rights of landlords and tenants concerning the produce of the land.

main_sections.section_title: Grounds of ejectment of occupancy tenant
main_sections.description: Outlines the specific reasons for which an occupancy tenant can be ejected.

main_sections.section_title: Private transfer of right of occupancy under section 5 by tenant
main_sections.description: Deals with the conditions and procedures for private transfers of occupancy rights by tenants.

main_sections.section_title: Title of occupancy-tenant to make improvements
main_sections.description: Confirms the right of an occupancy tenant to make improvements on their tenancy.
Defines the role and jurisdiction of Revenue Officers.

main_sections.section_title: Revenue Courts and suits cognizable by them
main_sections.description: Specifies the jurisdiction of Revenue Courts and the types of suits they can hear.

main_sections.section_title: Power for Financial Commissioner to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Financial Commissioner the power to create rules for the Act.

important_rules: Rule regarding the definition of 'land' which excludes urban building sites but includes agricultural land and pasture.
Rule defining 'rent' as any payment by a tenant to a landlord for land use.
Rule defining 'tenant' and explicitly excluding certain categories of individuals.
Rule outlining grounds for ejectment of occupancy tenants.
Rules governing the making and compensation for 'improvements' to tenancies.
Rules related to the jurisdiction and procedures of Revenue Officers and Revenue Courts.

penalties: Ejectment of tenant for specific grounds (e.g., non-payment of rent, unauthorized use of land).
Liability to pay compensation for improvements upon ejectment or rent enhancement.
Potential for wrongful dispossession to be remedied.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Officers and Revenue Courts, under the superintendence and control of higher authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through applications and proceedings before Revenue Officers and Revenue Courts, including suits, appeals, reviews, and revisions. Enforcement also involves the execution of decrees and the service of notices and proclamations.

rights: Right of occupancy for certain tenants.
Right to compensation for improvements made to the land.
Right to relief against wrongful dispossession or ejectment.
Right to appeal, review, and revision of decisions made by Revenue Officers and Courts.
duties: Duty to pay rent by the tenant.
Duty to adhere to the terms of the tenancy and the provisions of the Act.
Duty to allow landlords to make improvements under certain conditions.
Duty to comply with orders and decrees issued by Revenue Officers and Courts.
obligations: Tenants are obligated to pay rent when it becomes due.
Tenants have an obligation to cultivate land in accordance with its purpose.
Landlords have obligations related to compensation for improvements and may have duties regarding the maintenance of land.
Parties are obligated to participate in legal proceedings and comply with court orders.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining rent, including enhancement and reduction of rents through suits.
Procedure for relinquishment and abandonment of tenancies.
Procedure for ejectment of tenants, including applications to Revenue Officers and restrictions on ejectment.
Procedure for determining compensation for improvements.
Procedures for jurisdiction, appeals, review, and revision of cases by Revenue Officers and Courts.
Procedure for the service of summons, notices, orders, and proclamations.
administration: The Financial Commissioner, Local Government, and Revenue Officers/Courts are involved in the administration and implementation of this Act.
important_notes: The Act specifically excludes the Hazara district from its territorial jurisdiction.
Rules can be made in anticipation of the Act's commencement but only take effect upon commencement.
Certain entries in records-of-rights and agreements contrary to the Act are declared null and void.
The Act is distinct from the Punjab Land-revenue Act, 1887, though it references definitions and concepts from it.
Imprisonment of tenants for arrears of rent is prohibited.

title: The King of Oudh’s Estate Act, 1887
purpose: To provide for the administration of the estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh, ensuring that claims against the estate are settled and remaining property is distributed among his family and dependents, while exempting this process from Civil Court jurisdiction.
scope: The act applies to the estate of His late Majesty Wajid Ali Shah, King of Oudh. Geographically, it pertains to the administration of his property and the settlement of claims related to his estate within the jurisdiction of the Governor General in Council.

main_sections.section_title: Administration of the estate of the late king of Oudh by the Governor General in Council
main_sections.description: Grants the Governor General in Council exclusive authority for the administration of the late King of Oudh's property, including settling claims and distributing remaining assets among his family and dependents. It also states that no act of the Governor General in Council in this regard shall be questioned in any Court.

main_sections.section_title: Indemnity to Agent to the Governor General
main_sections.description: Provides indemnity and discharges from liability the Agent to the Governor General and any persons acting under his orders for acts done in connection with the preservation and administration of the late King of Oudh's estate since September 20, 1887. No suits can be instituted against them or the Secretary of State for India in Council for these acts.

Declares that this Act takes precedence over any testamentary or other disposition made by the late King and any proceedings instituted in Civil Courts for administering his estate. It also obliges any person who has received or realized any portion of the estate under any probate to account for it to an officer appointed by the Governor General in Council.

important_rules: The Governor General in Council shall have exclusive authority to administer the estate of the late King of Oudh.
Claims against the estate are to be settled, and remaining property distributed by the Governor General in Council.
Acts of the Governor General in Council concerning estate administration and distribution are not subject to review by any Court.
The Agent to the Governor General and persons acting under his orders are indemnified for acts related to estate preservation and administration since September 20, 1887.
This Act overrides any prior testamentary dispositions or ongoing Civil Court proceedings regarding the King's estate.
Individuals who have received portions of the estate under probate must account for them to the appointed officer.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Governor General in Council, and potentially an appointed officer for accounting under Section 3.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exclusive authority vested in the Governor General in Council and by requiring accounting from individuals who have profited from the estate under probate.

rights: Right of the Governor General in Council to exclusive authority over the King's estate administration and distribution.
duties: Duty of the Governor General in Council to administer the estate and satisfy claims.
Duty of the Governor General in Council to distribute remaining property.
Duty of persons holding portions of the estate under probate to account therefor to an appointed officer.
obligations: Obligation to respect the exclusive authority of the Governor General in Council.
Obligation for those who received estate assets under probate to account for them.

key_procedures: Administration of the estate by the Governor General in Council, including settlement of claims and distribution of assets.
Indemnification process for the Agent to the Governor General and his subordinates.
Accounting procedure for individuals who have received parts of the estate under probate.
administration: Governor General in Council.
important_notes: The act explicitly overrides any testamentary or other disposition made by the late King.
The act overrides any existing or future proceedings in Civil Courts concerning the administration of the estate.
The act establishes an indemnity for the Agent to the Governor General and others acting under his orders for actions taken since September 20, 1887.

title: The City of Bombay Municipal (Supplementary) Act, 1888
purpose: To supplement certain provisions of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, and the Calcutta Municipal Consolidation Act, 1889, specifically concerning Benches, Magistrates, and Courts of Small Causes, and to establish procedures for appeals and references to the High Court in Bombay.
scope: This act primarily applies to the City of Bombay, with provisions also referencing the Calcutta Municipal Consolidation Act, 1889. Its scope covers the jurisdiction of Municipal Authorities, Presidency Magistrates, and Courts of Small Causes, and related appeals and legal references within Bombay.

main_sections.section_title: Confirmation of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, and the Calcutta Municipal Consolidation Act, 1889, so far as regards Benches, Magistrates and Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Confirms the validity of the specified Municipal Acts regarding the jurisdiction of Appellate Benches, Presidency Magistrates, and Courts of Small Causes, and their decisions and proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Reference of questions by the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court to the Bombay High Court
main_sections.description: Allows the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court to refer questions of law, usage, or document construction to the High Court of Judicature at Bombay for decision, when doubt is entertained. It also incorporates relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure for such references.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal to the Bombay High Court from certain orders of the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court
main_sections.description: Establishes an appeal to the High Court of Judicature at Bombay from decisions of the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court under sections 503 or 504 of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, if the claim amount exceeds two thousand rupees. It also details the applicability of the Code of Civil Procedure for these appeals and the finality of decisions if no appeal lies.
