main_sections.section_title: Appeal to the Bombay High Court from orders of Presidency Magistrates in Bombay
main_sections.description: Grants an appeal to the High Court of Judicature at Bombay from orders of Presidency Magistrates under section 515 of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888. It empowers the High Court to make rules for appeal admission and procedure, mandates deferral of action by the Municipal Commissioner until appeal disposition, and outlines the execution of High Court orders, including costs.

main_sections.section_title: Period of limitation for appeals to the Bombay High Court under the two last foregoing sections
main_sections.description: Defines the period of limitation for appeals to the Bombay High Court under sections 3 and 4 of this act for the purposes of the Indian Limitation Act, 1877, treating them as appeals under the Code of Civil Procedure in specific unprovided cases.

important_rules: Rule 1: Decisions and proceedings of Appellate Benches, Presidency Magistrates, and Courts of Small Causes, as defined by the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, and the Calcutta Municipal Consolidation Act, 1889, are confirmed as valid.
Rule 2: The Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court can refer questions of law or document construction that affect merits to the Bombay High Court for decision.

Rule 3: Appeals to the Bombay High Court are allowed from specific decisions of the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court (under sections 503 or 504) and from orders of Presidency Magistrates (under section 515), provided certain conditions regarding claim amount or specific sections are met.
Rule 4: The Municipal Commissioner must defer action on a Presidency Magistrate's order pending appeal to the High Court and must give effect to the High Court's decision upon disposition.

penalties: Costs awarded by the High Court in appeals from Presidency Magistrates' orders can be recovered by a Presidency Magistrate as if they were a fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Presidency Magistrates, Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes of Bombay, High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Municipal Commissioner for the City of Bombay.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal appeals to the High Court, references of legal questions, execution of High Court orders by subordinate courts, and recovery of costs as fines.

rights: Right to appeal to the High Court of Judicature at Bombay from specific decisions of the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court.
Right to appeal to the High Court of Judicature at Bombay from orders of Presidency Magistrates.
Right to have an appeal heard and decided by the High Court.
Right to have High Court orders concerning appeals executed.
duties: Duty of the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court to draw up statements for references to the High Court when doubt exists.
Duty of the Municipal Commissioner to defer action on a Presidency Magistrate's order until appeal is disposed of.
Duty of the Municipal Commissioner to give effect to the High Court's order on appeal.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the period of limitation for appeals.
Obligation to comply with the Code of Civil Procedure in relation to appeals and references.
Obligation to pay costs as directed by the High Court.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Reference of a question of law or usage by the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court to the Bombay High Court, involving drawing up a statement of facts and the point of doubt, and submitting it with an opinion.

Procedure 2: Appeal from a decision of the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court (under sections 503/504) to the Bombay High Court, subject to the claim amount exceeding two thousand rupees, and applying Code of Civil Procedure provisions for appeals from original decrees.

Procedure 3: Appeal from an order of a Presidency Magistrate (under section 515) to the Bombay High Court, with the High Court regulating admission and procedure, and the Municipal Commissioner deferring action until the appeal is disposed of.
Procedure 4: Execution of orders passed by the High Court in appeals, either directly or through the Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes, and recovery of awarded costs.
administration: The administration of appeals and references falls under the purview of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, with operational aspects involving the Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes of Bombay and the Municipal Commissioner for the City of Bombay.
important_notes: The provisions of sections 618 to 621 of the Code of Civil Procedure (XIV of 1882) are applicable to references made to the High Court by the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court.
Appeals from the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court are subject to a monetary threshold (claim amount exceeding two thousand rupees) for certain decisions.
Decisions of the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court under sections 503 or 504, if not appealable under sub-section (1) of section 3, are final.
The High Court has the power to make rules for regulating appeals from Presidency Magistrates' orders and the procedure for their adjudication.
The period of limitation for these appeals is specifically defined in relation to the Indian Limitation Act, 1877.

title: An Act to make further provision for the Administration of the Estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh.
purpose: To provide for the mode in which property may be transferred, and suits and other proceedings may be instituted, in the course of the administration of the estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh.
scope: This act applies to the administration of the estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh, specifically concerning property transfers and legal proceedings related to the estate within British India.

key_definitions.Agent to the Governor General in Council: The person holding the office responsible for managing the estate of the late King of Oudh, subject to the control of the Governor General in Council.
key_definitions.His late Majesty the King of Oudh: Refers to the late King of Oudh whose estate is being administered.

main_sections.section_title: Transfers of property by and to the Agent to the Governor General in Council, and institution of legal proceedings by him.
main_sections.description: This section outlines the powers of the Agent to the Governor General in Council for the Affairs of the late King of Oudh. It allows the Agent, under the control of the Governor General in Council, to dispose of the King's movable and immovable property, take conveyance of property in which the King had a beneficial interest, and institute legal proceedings in any court concerning the estate's property or administration.

main_sections.section_title: Consequences ensuring on death, resignation or removal Agent.
main_sections.description: This section details the consequences that follow the departure from British India, death, resignation, or removal of the Agent. It states that any property vested in the Agent shall pass to his successor, and any legal proceedings instituted by the Agent can be continued by his successor.

important_rules: The Agent to the Governor General in Council for the Affairs of the late King of Oudh has the authority to transfer movable and immovable property of the late King, as if the King himself could have done so in his lifetime.
The Agent can accept conveyance of any movable or immovable property in which the late King had a beneficial interest.
The Agent can initiate legal proceedings (suits, criminal, or revenue cases) related to the possession, dispossession, recovery of dues, or general administration of the late King's estate.
Upon the departure, death, resignation, or removal of the Agent, all property vested in him as Agent shall transfer to his successor.
Legal proceedings initiated by an Agent can be continued by his successor without interruption.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Governor General in Council (through the appointed Agent)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legal powers granted to the Agent to manage the estate, transfer property, and institute legal proceedings.

rights: Right of the Agent to dispose of the late King's property.
Right of the Agent to acquire property for the estate.
Right of the Agent to institute legal proceedings for the estate.
Right of the successor Agent to continue legal proceedings.
duties: Duty of the Agent to act subject to the control of the Governor General in Council.
Duty of the Agent to manage the estate for the benefit of its claimants, family, and dependents as per Act XIX of 1887.

key_procedures: Transfer of Property: The Agent can dispose of or acquire property in their name of office.
Institution of Legal Proceedings: The Agent can initiate suits or other proceedings in any Civil, Criminal, or Revenue Court.
Succession of Powers: Upon the departure, death, resignation, or removal of an Agent, their successor automatically assumes control of vested property and continues any ongoing legal proceedings.
administration: The Governor General in Council and the appointed Agent to the Governor General in Council for the Affairs of the late King of Oudh.
important_notes: The powers granted to the Agent are subject to the control of the Governor General in Council.
The act builds upon and clarifies provisions made in Act XIX of 1887 regarding the administration of the King of Oudh's estate.

title: The North-Western Provinces and Oudh Act, 1890
purpose: To provide for the better administration of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh and to amend certain enactments in force in those provinces and in Oudh.
scope: This act applies to the North-Western Provinces and Oudh. Part I specifically addresses changes in the North-Western Provinces, particularly concerning the Jhansi Division. Part II focuses on Oudh. Part III deals with both regions jointly.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the North-Western Provinces and Oudh Act, 1890.
Specifies that Part I comes into force on a day directed by the Lieutenant-Governor through an Official Gazette notification.
These sections, related to the amendment of Act 19 of 1873, have been repealed by the United Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1901.

main_sections.section_title: Laws in force in certain districts of the Allahabad Division to apply to Jhansi
main_sections.description: This section details the application of existing laws to the Jhansi Division upon its annexation to the Allahabad Division. It specifies which laws will come into force in Jhansi and which existing laws in Jhansi will be repealed.

main_sections.section_title: Discharge of functions assigned to Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner by Act 17 of 1886
main_sections.description: This section reassigns the functions previously assigned to the Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner by the Jhansi and Morar Act, 1886, to the District Judge and the High Court, respectively. It also clarifies references to Courts in the Jhansi district.

main_sections.section_title: Jhansi Division to cease to be a Scheduled District
main_sections.description: Declares that the Jhansi Division will cease to be a Scheduled District from the day Part I comes into force.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act 12 of 1887 to Jhansi, and disposal of pending cases
main_sections.description: This section outlines the application of the Bengal, North-Western Provinces and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887, to Jhansi. It also provides detailed instructions on how pending civil cases and appeals in the Jhansi Division should be disposed of by different courts.
Specifies that Part II comes into force on a day directed by the Chief Commissioner of Oudh through an Official Gazette notification.

main_sections.section_title: Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces to be the Board of Revenue of, and Chief Revenue-authority in, Oudh
main_sections.description: This section establishes that the Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces will also serve as the Board of Revenue and Chief Revenue-authority for Oudh. It also clarifies references to the Board of Revenue in enactments concerning Oudh.

This section addresses the disposal of appeals pending when Part II comes into force. It states that such appeals will be disposed of as if the Act had not been passed, with a provision for the State Government to transfer appeals from the Commissioner or Collector to the District Judge.
Specifies that Part III comes into force on a day directed by the Lieutenant Governor of the North-Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh through an Official Gazette notification.

main_sections.section_title: Place where the Board may sit
main_sections.description: This section allows the Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh to sit in specified places within the North-Western Provinces or Oudh for the disposal of cases, subject to notification by the State Government. It also grants the Board discretion to sit in any place for other cases.

important_rules: All enactments in force in temporarily-settled districts of the Allahabad Division (except specific acts) shall apply to the Jhansi Division from the day Part I comes into force.
Certain enactments in force in the Jhansi Division (except specific acts) shall be repealed in that division from the day Part I comes into force.
Functions assigned by the Jhansi and Morar Act, 1886, to the Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner will be discharged by the District Judge and High Court, respectively.
The Jhansi Division shall cease to be a Scheduled District.
Pending civil cases in the Jhansi Division will be transferred to specific civil courts (Munsif, Subordinate Judge, District Judge, High Court) based on the original court.
Decrees and orders passed by Civil Courts in Jhansi, if not appealed, will be deemed to have been passed by specific civil courts for the purpose of the Civil Courts Act, 1887.
The Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces will also function as the Board of Revenue and Chief Revenue-authority for Oudh.
Appeals pending when Part II comes into force shall be disposed of as if the Act had not been passed, unless transferred by the State Government.
The Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh can sit in designated places for case disposal.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement through the judicial system (civil courts, High Court, District Judge) and administrative authorities (Lieutenant Governor, Chief Commissioner, State Government) through notifications and orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the established judicial and administrative processes, including the transfer and disposal of cases, application of laws, and the functioning of revenue authorities.

key_procedures: Notification by the Lieutenant-Governor to bring Part I into force.
Notification by the Chief Commissioner to bring Part II into force.
Notification by the Lieutenant Governor and Chief Commissioner to bring Part III into force.
Transfer and disposal of pending civil cases in Jhansi Division to designated courts.
Determination of the court for appeals from decrees and orders passed by civil courts in Jhansi.
Determination of the period of limitation for appeals from decrees and orders mentioned in section 9(3).
Disposal of pending appeals under Part II as if the Act had not been passed, with the possibility of transfer by the State Government.
Notification by the State Government to appoint places where the Board of Revenue may sit.
administration: The administration is overseen by the Lieutenant Governor of the North-Western Provinces, the Chief Commissioner of Oudh, and the State Government (or equivalent authorities at the time). The Board of Revenue plays a significant role in revenue administration.
important_notes: Numerous sections of the Act have been repealed by subsequent legislation, including the United Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1901, and various Repealing Acts.

The Act signifies a territorial and administrative reorganization, specifically the annexation of the Jhansi Division and the unification of revenue administration for Oudh with the North-Western Provinces.

References to 'State Government' are often substitutions for earlier authorities like the Chief Commissioner or the Lieutenant Governor and Chief Commissioner, indicating a later amendment or adaptation of the text.

title: The Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit Act, 1893
purpose: To settle specific property, including Municipal Corporation bonds and a Mansion-house named 'Petit Hall', in perpetuity to support and accompany the title and dignity of Baronet conferred on Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit and his successors, ensuring the proper maintenance of the title and its associated dignity.
scope: Applies to the property specified (Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay bonds and 'Petit Hall' in the Island of Bombay) and to the individuals who succeed to the Baronetcy conferred by Letters Patent on Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, specifically his second son Framjee Dinshaw Petit and their male heirs, as well as other male heirs of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit. The Act is enacted by the Governor General of India in Council and concerns property within the jurisdiction of Bombay.

key_definitions.The Corporation: The body incorporated under the style and title of 'The Trustees of the Dinshaw Manockjee Petit Baronetcy', comprising the Accountant-General of Bombay, the Collector of Bombay, and the Chief Presidency Magistrate of Bombay, and their successors for the time being.

main_sections.description: Establishes a corporation with perpetual succession and a common seal, named 'The Trustees of the Dinshaw Manockjee Petit Baronetcy', consisting of the Accountant-General, Collector, and Chief Presidency Magistrate of Bombay for the time being, and their successors. This Corporation is constituted as the Trustee for executing the powers and purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Heirs of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit to take his name
main_sections.description: Mandates that Framjee Dinshaw Petit and all subsequent heirs male of his body, and all other heirs male of the body of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit who succeed to the Baronetcy, must adopt and use the name 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit' in lieu of any other names they may bear, and shall style themselves by these names on all occasions.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting and application of income of settled property
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay bonds producing an annual income of one lakh and twenty-five thousand rupees to the Corporation. It outlines the trusts for these bonds, including their investment in government-guaranteed securities, and the application of their income for the benefit of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit during his life, then for Framjee Dinshaw Petit during his life if he survives Sir Dinshaw, and subsequently for the heir male who succeeds to the Baronetcy. It also specifies provisions for failure of heirs male and the ultimate reversionary interest for Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit.

Specifies that during the minority of any Baronet entitled to the dignity, the Corporation shall apply only such portion of the annual income as they deem proper for the Baronet's maintenance, education, and benefit. The residue is to be invested in government-guaranteed securities, and upon the Baronet attaining majority, these investments and accumulations are to be transferred to him.

main_sections.section_title: Mansion-house limited to the use of the Baronet for the time being
main_sections.description: Declares that the Mansion-house and hereditaments known as 'Petit Hall' shall be held by the Corporation upon trust. It is to be for the use of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit during his life, then for Framjee Dinshaw Petit during his life if he survives Sir Dinshaw, and thereafter for the heirs male of Framjee Dinshaw Petit (or Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit in default) who succeed to the Baronetcy. The section also includes provisions for an ultimate remainder or reversion for Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, his heirs and assigns.

main_sections.section_title: Devolution of interest where beneficiary refuses, neglects or discontinues to use the names Dinshaw Manockjee Petit
main_sections.description: Establishes a provision for the suspension of interest if any beneficiary who succeeds to the Baronetcy refuses, neglects, or discontinues to use the name 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit' for a specified period after becoming entitled to the income or possession of the property, or after attaining majority if under age. During such suspension, the income and possession are to be managed by the Corporation.

important_rules: Rule 1: All heirs male succeeding to the Baronetcy must adopt and use the name 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit' on all occasions. (Section 2)
Rule 2: Municipal bonds generating an annual income of one lakh and twenty-five thousand rupees must be transferred to the Corporation for trust purposes. (Section 3)
Rule 3: The Mansion-house 'Petit Hall' and associated hereditaments are to be held in trust for the designated beneficiaries and heirs. (Section 5)
Rule 4: The income from settled property is to be applied for the benefit of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, then Framjee Dinshaw Petit, and then the heir succeeding to the Baronetcy. (Sections 3 & 5)
Rule 5: During the minority of a Baronet, the Corporation can decide on the amount of income to be used for their maintenance and education, investing the rest. (Section 4)
Rule 6: If a successor fails to use the name 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit' for a specified period, their interest in the trust property is suspended for their lifetime. (Section 6)

penalties: Suspension of estate or interest in trust funds and premises for the remainder of the person's natural life if they refuse, neglect, or discontinue to use the name 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit' as prescribed. (Section 6)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Corporation ('The Trustees of the Dinshaw Manockjee Petit Baronetcy'), comprising the Accountant-General of Bombay, the Collector of Bombay, and the Chief Presidency Magistrate of Bombay, and their successors.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Corporation is constituted as the Trustee for executing the powers and purposes of the Act. Enforcement would likely involve the Corporation managing the settled property, distributing income according to the Act's provisions, and taking action to suspend interests or ensure compliance with name usage requirements.

rights: Right of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit to the income of the settled property during his natural life. (Section 3)
Right of Framjee Dinshaw Petit to the income of the settled property during his natural life, provided he survives Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit. (Section 3)
Right of the heir male succeeding to the Baronetcy to the benefit of the settled property. (Section 3)
Right of the Baronet to have a portion of the income applied for their maintenance, education, and benefit during minority. (Section 4)
Right of the Baronet to receive accumulated investments upon attaining majority. (Section 4)
Right of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit to assign, transfer, bequeath, or dispose of the ultimate remainder or reversionary interest in the settled property. (Section 3 & 5)
Right of the beneficiary for the time being to use the Mansion-house 'Petit Hall' as per the limitations. (Section 5)
duties: Duty of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit to settle bonds and the Mansion-house on the trusts specified. (Preamble)
Duty of Framjee Dinshaw Petit and subsequent heirs male to adopt and use the name 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit'. (Section 2)
Duty of the Corporation to act as Trustees and execute the powers and purposes of the Act. (Section 1)
Duty of the Corporation to invest and manage the settled property according to the Act's provisions. (Sections 3 & 4)
Duty of the Corporation to pay and apply the income for the benefit of the designated beneficiaries. (Sections 3 & 4)
Duty of the Corporation to maintain the Mansion-house and hereditaments in repair. (Implied by Section 13, though Section 13 text is not fully provided)
Duty of the beneficiary to use the name 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit' to avoid suspension of interest. (Section 6)
obligations: Obligation to settle bonds producing an annual income of one lakh and twenty-five thousand rupees. (Preamble & Section 3)
Obligation to settle the Mansion-house 'Petit Hall' and other hereditaments. (Preamble & Section 5)
Obligation to adopt and bear the names 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit' by all successors to the Baronetcy. (Section 2)

key_procedures: Procedure for the Corporation to receive, hold, and invest Municipal bonds: Bonds are transferred to the Corporation, which then invests the proceeds from discharge or sale in government-guaranteed securities, and alters these securities as necessary. (Section 3)

Procedure for applying income for beneficiaries: Dividends, interest, and annual income are paid to Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, then to Framjee Dinshaw Petit, and then to the heir succeeding to the Baronetcy. (Section 3)
Procedure for managing income during minority: The Corporation applies income for the Baronet's maintenance and education, investing the surplus and transferring it upon majority. (Section 4)
Procedure for ensuring name usage: Successors must use the name 'Dinshaw Manockjee Petit'. Failure to do so for a year leads to suspension of interest. (Section 6)
administration: The administration of this act is entrusted to 'The Trustees of the Dinshaw Manockjee Petit Baronetcy', which is a corporation formed by the Accountant-General of Bombay, the Collector of Bombay, and the Chief Presidency Magistrate of Bombay, and their successors.
important_notes: The Act is enacted to fulfill an engagement made with Her Majesty's Government. (Preamble)
The primary objective is to support and accompany the title and dignity of Baronet conferred on Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit.
Provisions for the ultimate remainder or reversionary interest are made for Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, his executors, administrators, and assigns.

The Act specifies that the limitations concerning the application of income for the heir male succeeding to the Baronetcy are to be followed 'notwithstanding any rule of law or equity to the contrary'. (Section 3)

title: THE CENTRAL PROVINCES COURT OF WARDS ACT, 1899
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the Court of Wards in the Central Provinces.
scope: Applies to the territories for the time being administered by the Local Government of the Central Provinces. It concerns the superintendence of property and persons of disqualified landholders.

key_definitions.Government ward: Any person of whose property, or of whose person and property, the Court of Wards may, for the time being, have the superintendence under this Act.
key_definitions.land: Includes the rights of a land-holder in respect of the land of which he is the malguzar or zamindar or the muafidar, jagirdar, ubaridar or other assignee of land-revenue, or in which he is interested.
key_definitions.land-holder: Means a malguzar as defined in the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881, and the zamindar of any zamindari in a Scheduled District, and includes a muafidar, jagirdar, ubaridar or other assignee of land-revenue, and any person not hereinbefore specified who is interested in land and belongs to a class of which the Local Government, with the previous sanction of the Governor General in Council, has declared the members to be land-holders for the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and that it comes into force immediately.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Government ward', 'land', and 'land-holder'.

main_sections.section_title: Commissioner to be Court of Wards
main_sections.description: Designates the Commissioner as the Court of Wards for the limits of his division, subject to Section 9.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence by Court of Wards of property of disqualified landholder
main_sections.description: Empowers the Court of Wards to assume superintendence of the property of a disqualified landholder with the Local Government's prior sanction.

main_sections.section_title: Land-holders to be deemed disqualified in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies categories of landholders deemed disqualified to manage their property: minors, those adjudged of unsound mind, and those declared incapable by the Local Government due to physical/mental defects, conviction of non-bailable offenses, or being female. No suits can be filed in Civil Courts regarding such declarations.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence by Court of Wards on application of proprietor
main_sections.description: Allows a landholder to apply to have their property placed under the Court of Wards' superintendence, subject to the Local Government's order if deemed expedient in the public interest. No suits can be filed against such orders.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary provisions for custody of heirs and protection of property in certain cases
main_sections.description: Outlines powers for temporary custody and protection of property and heirs when a landholder dies and the heir is or might be disqualified. Requires reporting to the Local Government.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence by Court of Wards of person of disqualified landholder
main_sections.description: Grants the Court of Wards the power to assume superintendence of the person of a minor or mentally unsound landholder, with the Local Government's sanction, with an exception for married women in their husband's custody.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence by Court of Wards where disqualified landholder owns land in more than one division
main_sections.description: Specifies that if a landholder owns land in multiple divisions, only one designated Court of Wards (determined by the Local Government) will assume superintendence.

main_sections.section_title: Assumption of superintendence to be notified and to extend to whole of Government ward's property
main_sections.description: Mandates notification of the assumption of superintendence in the official Gazette, states that all of the ward's property (known or unknown, and subsequently inherited) is under superintendence, and allows discretion regarding subsequently acquired property.

main_sections.section_title: Barring of suits to contest authority to assume superintendence
main_sections.description: Prohibits suits in Civil Courts to contest the Court of Wards' authority to assume superintendence on grounds of the person not being a landholder or minor.

main_sections.section_title: Notices to claimants against Government ward
main_sections.description: Requires notification in the Gazette and other specified manners for claimants against a Government ward or their property to submit claims within six months. Unsubmitted claims are deemed discharged, with a provision for late submission if inability to comply is proven, but without interest.

main_sections.section_title: Claimants to furnish full particulars and documents
main_sections.description: Dictates that claimants must provide full particulars and supporting documents (with copies) for their claims. Original documents are returned after verification, and failure to produce a document renders it inadmissible as evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Stay of proceedings of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: Allows the Court of Wards to apply to a Civil Court to stay execution proceedings against a Government ward's immovable property, rents, or crops within one year of notification, with terms regarding interest or compensation.

Details the process of the Court of Wards investigating and deciding on submitted claims. It also allows for proposals for claim reduction and outlines conditions for future recovery if a reduced claim remains unsatisfied. Suits can still be filed in Civil Courts, but the Court of Wards' decision is not provable as against the defendant.

Requires the Court of Wards to submit a schedule of debts and liabilities to the Local Government. The Local Government may order the relinquishment of superintendence if the estate is irrecoverably involved or for other sufficient reasons.

important_rules: Disqualified landholders (minors, unsound mind, declared incapable by Local Government) have their property placed under the superintendence of the Court of Wards (Section 4, 5).
The Court of Wards can assume superintendence of property upon application by the landholder if deemed expedient in the public interest (Section 6).
All property of a Government ward, including subsequently inherited property, is under the superintendence of the Court of Wards (Section 10).
Claimants against a Government ward must submit claims within six months of notification, or they are deemed discharged (Section 12).
Failure to produce supporting documents for a claim can result in the document being inadmissible as evidence (Section 13).
Civil Court proceedings against a Government ward's property can be stayed by the Court of Wards (Section 14).
The Court of Wards investigates and adjudicates claims, with provisions for claim reduction and binding agreements (Section 15).
The Local Government can order the relinquishment of superintendence by the Court of Wards if the estate is in severe financial distress or for other valid reasons (Section 16).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Court of Wards, which is the Commissioner of the division.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assumption and management of property, adjudication of claims, staying of Civil Court proceedings, and reporting to the Local Government.

rights: Landholders have the right to apply to have their property placed under the Court of Wards' superintendence (Section 6(1)).
Claimants, if unable to comply with submission deadlines, may have their claims received later, but without interest accrual (Section 12(2) proviso).
Claimants whose reduced claims are still unsatisfied upon relinquishment of superintendence can recover a proportional amount of their original admitted claim (Section 15(2) proviso).
duties: Landholders must allow their property to be placed under the superintendence of the Court of Wards if declared disqualified or if they apply for it (Sections 4, 5, 6).
Claimants must submit claims in writing with full particulars and supporting documents within the stipulated period (Sections 12, 13).
The Court of Wards has duties to manage the property, investigate claims, and protect the interests of the Government ward.
obligations: The Court of Wards is obligated to report its actions to the Local Government in certain circumstances (Section 7(2)).
The Court of Wards is obligated to investigate claims and make decisions (Section 15).
The Court of Wards must adhere to the orders and directions of the Local Government (Section 38).

key_procedures: Assumption of Superintendence: The Court of Wards, with Local Government sanction, assumes superintendence of a disqualified landholder's property (Section 4). This is notified in the Gazette (Section 10).

Claim Submission and Adjudication: After notification, claimants must submit claims within six months (Section 12). Claims are investigated, decided upon, and potential proposals for reduction are made (Section 15).
Relinquishment of Superintendence: The Local Government may order the relinquishment of superintendence if the estate is in distress (Section 16).
administration: The Court of Wards, which is the Commissioner of the division, operates under the control and direction of the Local Government.
important_notes: No suit can be brought in any Civil Court to contest a declaration by the Local Government regarding disqualification of a landholder (Section 5(2)).
No suit can be brought in any Civil Court to contest the authority of the Court of Wards regarding assumption of superintendence (Section 11).
The Court of Wards' discretion in assuming or refraining from assuming superintendence of subsequently acquired property cannot be questioned in a Civil Court (Section 39).

title: THE CENTRAL PROVINCES FINANCIAL COMMISSIONER’S ACT, 1908
purpose: To provide for the appointment of a Financial Commissioner for the Central Provinces and to further amend the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881.
scope: This act applies to the Central Provinces and amends the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881. It establishes a Financial Commissioner and defines the roles and subordination of revenue officers within the Central Provinces administration.

key_definitions.Revenue-officers: Classes of officers responsible for revenue matters, including the Chief Commissioner, Financial Commissioner, Commissioners, Deputy Commissioners, Assistant Commissioners, Tahsildars, and Naib-tahsildars.
key_definitions.Financial Commissioner: A newly appointed officer for the Central Provinces with specific powers and subordination as defined by the act and amendments to the Land-revenue Act.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Central Provinces Financial Commissioner’s Act, 1908, and states that it comes into force on a date specified by the Chief Commissioner with the sanction of the Governor General in Council.

Establishes the position of a Financial Commissioner for the Central Provinces and outlines the Chief Commissioner's authority, with the sanction of the Governor General in Council, to appoint, suspend, or remove the Financial Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Assignment of powers to Financial Commissioner
main_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Commissioner, with the sanction of the Governor General in Council, to assign powers and functions of the Local Government, Chief Commissioner, or Chief Controlling Revenue-authority to the Financial Commissioner, subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 5 and 6, Act XVIII, 1881
main_sections.description: Replaces sections 5 and 6 of the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881. Section 5 lists the classes of Revenue-officers. Section 6 details the subordination of Revenue-officers, establishing a hierarchy from the Governor General in Council down to village-survey officers.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of sections 17 and 25 Act XVIII, 1881
main_sections.description: Amends sections 17 and 25 of the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881, by adding 'or the Financial Commissioner' after 'Chief Commissioner' wherever they appear.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of sections 22 and 23 Act XVIII, 1881
main_sections.description: Amends sections 22 (clause c) and 23 (clause c) of the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881, by substituting 'Financial Commissioner' for 'Chief Commissioner'.

important_rules: Rule: The Chief Commissioner is subject to the control of the Governor General in Council in all revenue matters.
Rule: The Financial Commissioner is subject to the control of the Chief Commissioner.
Rule: All other Revenue-officers are subordinate to the Chief Commissioner and the Financial Commissioner.
Rule: Revenue-officers within a division are subordinate to the Commissioner of that division.
Rule: Revenue-officers within a district are subordinate to the Deputy Commissioner of that district.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Chief Commissioner, with the sanction of the Governor General in Council, is responsible for appointing and controlling the Financial Commissioner. Enforcement of revenue matters would fall under the purview of the defined revenue officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would occur through the established hierarchy of revenue officers as detailed in the amended sections of the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881.

rights: The Chief Commissioner has the right to appoint, suspend, or remove the Financial Commissioner.
The Chief Commissioner has the right to assign powers to the Financial Commissioner.
duties: Duty of the Chief Commissioner to oversee the Financial Commissioner and other revenue officers.
Duty of the Financial Commissioner to be subordinate to the Chief Commissioner and to exercise assigned powers.
Duty of all Revenue-officers to be subordinate to their superiors as defined in the act.
obligations: Obligation for the Chief Commissioner to seek sanction from the Governor General in Council for certain appointments and power assignments.
Obligation for the act to be brought into force via notification in the official Gazette.

key_procedures: Procedure: Appointment of the Financial Commissioner requires the Chief Commissioner to obtain prior sanction from the Governor General in Council.
Procedure: Assignment of powers to the Financial Commissioner is done by the Chief Commissioner via notification, with prior sanction from the Governor General in Council.
Procedure: The Act comes into force upon a notification by the Chief Commissioner, with the previous sanction of the Governor General in Council.
administration: The administration of revenue matters in the Central Provinces, with the newly established role of the Financial Commissioner, falls under the Chief Commissioner and the Governor General in Council.
important_notes: The Act specifically amends the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881 (Act XVIII of 1881), by substituting and amending certain sections.
An officer in charge of a village-survey in a district not under settlement can be invested with the powers of a Revenue-officer and subordinated by the Chief Commissioner.

title: THE PRESIDENCY-TOWNS INSOLVENCY ACT, 1909
purpose: To amend the law relating to insolvency in the Presidency-towns.
scope: This Act applies to insolvency matters within the Presidency-towns of Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay.

key_definitions.debt: Includes a judgment-debt, and 'debtor' includes a judgment-debtor.
key_definitions.official assignee: Includes an acting official assignee and a deputy official assignee, whether permanent or acting.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules.
key_definitions.property: Includes any property over which or the profits of which any person has a disposing power which he may exercise for his own benefit.
key_definitions.rules: Means rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.secured creditor: Includes a landlord who under any enactment for the time being in force has a charge on land for the rent of that land.
key_definitions.the Court: Means the Court exercising jurisdiction under this Act.
key_definitions.transfer of property: Includes a transfer of any interest therein and any charge created thereon.
key_definitions.States: Means all the territories which immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised within Part A States and Part C States.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Presidency-towns Insolvency Act, 1909, and states its commencement date as January 1, 1910.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as creditor, debt, official assignee, property, and the Court.
Specifies that the High Courts at Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay have jurisdiction in insolvency under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction to be exercised by a single Judge
main_sections.description: States that matters under this Act shall ordinarily be handled by a single Judge of the Court, assigned by the Chief Justice.
Allows the Judge to exercise jurisdiction, in whole or in part, in chambers, subject to the Act and rules.

main_sections.section_title: Delegation of powers to officers of Court
main_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Justice to delegate certain powers to appointed Court officers, including hearing debtor petitions, conducting public examinations, making chamber orders, and examining summoned persons. These officers cannot commit for contempt.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Court to decide all questions arising in insolvency
main_sections.description: Grants the Court full power to decide all questions of priorities and other matters, whether of law or fact, arising in insolvency cases.
This section outlines the specific actions that constitute an act of insolvency.
Grants the power to issue an order of adjudication in insolvency matters.
Details the consequences and legal impact of an order of adjudication.
Covers the process and conditions under which an insolvent may be discharged.
Specifies which debts are eligible to be proved and claimed in an insolvency proceeding.
Establishes the order in which different types of debts will be paid from the insolvent's estate.

main_sections.section_title: Description of insolvents property divisible amongst creditors
main_sections.description: Defines what constitutes the insolvent's property that is available for distribution to creditors.
Deals with the invalidation of property transfers made voluntarily by the debtor.

main_sections.section_title: Avoidance of preference in certain cases
main_sections.description: Addresses the avoidance of preferential transfers made by the insolvent to certain creditors.

main_sections.section_title: Possession of property by official assignee
main_sections.description: Outlines the official assignee's role in taking possession of the insolvent's property.

main_sections.section_title: Duty and powers of official assignee as to realization
main_sections.description: Details the responsibilities and authority of the official assignee in realizing the insolvent's assets.
Explains the process of declaring and distributing dividends to creditors.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and removal of official assignees of insolvents estate
main_sections.description: Covers the appointment and removal of official assignees responsible for managing insolvents' estates.
Provides for the formation and role of a committee of inspection in insolvency proceedings.
Specifies penalties for undischarged insolvents who obtain credit.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment of insolvent for certain offences
main_sections.description: Outlines punishments for insolvents who commit certain offenses.
Describes a simplified administration process for smaller insolvency cases.
Empowers the making of rules to govern procedures and other aspects of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: (Prescribed) The Act refers to 'prescribed' meaning prescribed by rules made under the Act, indicating a detailed procedural framework exists.

Rule 2: (Delegation of Powers) The Chief Justice can delegate powers to Court officers for matters like hearing debtor petitions, holding public examinations, and making chamber orders, with limitations on committing for contempt.
Rule 3: (Court's Power) The Court has the ultimate authority to decide all questions of priorities and other legal or factual issues arising in an insolvency case.
Rule 4: (Proof of Debts) Section 48 refers to 'Rules to proof of debts', implying specific procedures for creditors to establish their claims.
Rule 5: (Dividend Distribution) Section 48 implies rules for the declaration and distribution of dividends, as per Section 69.
Rule 6: (Official Assignee Powers) Section 85 refers to 'Discretionary powers and control thereof' of the official assignee, suggesting specific rules govern their actions.
Rule 7: (Procedure Rules) Section 112 explicitly states 'Rules' giving authority for making rules to govern procedures under the Act, with provisions for sanction and publication.

penalties: Undischarged insolvent obtaining credit: Penalties apply.
Punishment of insolvent for certain offences: Specific punishments are defined.
Disqualifications of insolvent: Insolvents may face disqualifications.
Criminal liability after discharge or composition: Provisions exist for criminal liability even after discharge or composition.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Courts exercising jurisdiction under this Act (High Courts at Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay), and the Official Assignee.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, adjudication orders, seizure and realization of property, distribution of dividends, and potential criminal prosecution for offenses outlined in Part VIII.

rights: Creditors have the right to prove their debts and receive dividends.
Insolvents have the right to apply for discharge.
Insolvents have the right to any surplus property after debts are paid.
Insolvents have a right to apply for a protection order.
A discharged insolvent has the right to renewal of application and variation of terms of order.
The Government has rights to unclaimed dividends.
Creditors have rights under Section 123 for claims to monies credited to Government.
duties: Insolvent's duty as to discovery and realization of property.
Insolvent's duty to assist in realization of property after discharge.
Official assignee's duty to furnish list of creditors.
Official assignee's duty and powers as to realization of property.
Duties of Court executing decree as to property taken in execution.
obligations: Debtors have an obligation to petition for insolvency under certain conditions.
Insolvents have an obligation to appear for public examination.
Insolvents have an obligation to disclose their property.
Insolvents have an obligation to comply with court orders regarding their property and conduct.
Legal representatives have obligations regarding payments or transfers of estates of deceased insolvents.
The Government has obligations related to unclaimed dividends.

key_procedures: Filing of insolvency petitions (by creditors or debtors).
Adjudication order by the Court.
Public examination of the insolvent.
Submission and approval of composition or schemes of arrangement by creditors and the Court.
Discovery, seizure, and realization of the insolvent's property by the Official Assignee.
Declaration and distribution of dividends to creditors.
Application for and granting of discharge of the insolvent.
Summary administration for small insolvencies.
Administration in insolvency of the estate of a person dying insolvent.
administration: The High Courts at Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay, and the Official Assignee.
important_notes: The Act has undergone amendments in Bombay, Bengal, and Madras.
The words 'and the town of Rangoon' and 'and the town of Karachi' have been omitted from the original text, indicating territorial changes.
Certain clauses related to definitions have been omitted.
The definition of 'States' was updated to reflect post-1956 territories.
Section 119 is a repetition of Section 118 concerning formal defects not invalidating proceedings.
Sections 120 and 121 state that certain provisions bind the Government.
The First Schedule deals with Meetings of Creditors, and the Second Schedule with Proof of Debts. The Third Schedule has been repealed.

title: The Co-operative Societies Act, 1912
purpose: To facilitate the formation of Co-operative Societies for the promotion of thrift and self-help among agriculturists, artisans and persons of limited means, and to amend the law relating to Co-operative Societies.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. The Act applies to the formation, registration, rights, liabilities, duties, privileges, property, funds, inspection, dissolution, and winding-up of co-operative societies.

key_definitions.by_laws: The registered by-laws for the time being in force, and includes a registered amendment of the by-laws.
key_definitions.committee: The governing body of a registered society to whom the management of its affairs is entrusted.
key_definitions.member: Includes a person joining in the application for the registration of a society and a person admitted to membership after registration in accordance with the by-laws and any rules.
key_definitions.officer: Includes a chairman, secretary, treasurer, member of committee, or other person empowered under the rules or the by-laws to give directions in regard to the business of the society.
key_definitions.registered_society: A society registered or deemed to be registered under this Act.
key_definitions.registrar: A person appointed to perform the duties of a Registrar of Co-operative Societies under this Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, and specifies its territorial extent.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'by-laws', 'committee', 'member', 'officer', 'registered society', 'Registrar', and 'rules'.
Empowers the State Government to appoint a Registrar of Co-operative Societies and assistants, and to confer powers on them.

Specifies the types of societies that can be registered under the Act, focusing on those promoting economic interests of members in accordance with co-operative principles, or facilitating operations of such societies. It also outlines conditions for limited or unlimited liability.
States that upon registration, a society becomes a body corporate with perpetual succession, common seal, and powers to hold property, enter contracts, and sue and be sued.

Grants registered societies a priority claim over other creditors to enforce outstanding demands against members or past members for seed, manure, or loans for their purchase, subject to prior claims of the Government or landlord.
Deals with the process and grounds for the dissolution of a registered society.
Refers to the making of rules under this Act.

important_rules: No member of a registered society shall exercise the rights of a member unless or until they have made prescribed payments or acquired prescribed interest in the society (Section 12).
Each member has one vote in societies not limited by shares; votes are prescribed by by-laws in societies limited by shares (Section 13).

Transfer of shares or interest is subject to maximum holding conditions and, for unlimited liability societies, requires holding for at least one year and transfer to the society or another member (Section 14).
Every registered society must maintain a registered address and notify the Registrar of any changes (Section 15).
Copies of the Act, rules, and by-laws must be kept open for inspection free of charge at reasonable times at the society's registered address (Section 16).
The Registrar must audit the accounts of every registered society at least once a year (Section 17).
Registered societies are bodies corporate with perpetual succession, common seal, and power to hold property, enter contracts, and institute legal proceedings (Section 18).
Societies have a prior claim over other creditors for outstanding demands from members or past members, subject to government/landlord claims (Section 19).
Funds of registered societies are restricted from being divided by way of profit (Section 33).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Co-operative Societies, and any person authorised by the Registrar.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers conferred upon the Registrar, including appointment of staff, registration and amendment of by-laws, audit of accounts, inquiry into affairs, and dissolution/cancellation of registration. Specific penalties are not detailed in the provided text snippet but would likely be covered in later sections or rules.

rights: Right to be a body corporate with perpetual succession.
Right to hold property.
Right to enter into contracts.
Right to institute and defend suits and other legal proceedings.
Right to do all things necessary for the purposes of its constitution.
Prior claim to enforce outstanding demands from members/past members (subject to prior claims of Government/landlord).
duties: Maintain a registered address and notify changes.
Keep copies of the Act, rules, and by-laws open for inspection.
Submit to annual audit of accounts.
Allow access to books, accounts, papers, and securities by authorized persons.
Furnish information regarding transactions and working of the society when required.
Ensure members make due payments or acquire prescribed interest before exercising rights.
Adhere to restrictions on holding share capital and interest.
Comply with conditions for transfer of shares or interest.
obligations: For societies with limited liability and share capital, members other than registered societies cannot hold more than a prescribed portion of share capital (max 1/5) or have interest exceeding one thousand rupees.
Societies with unlimited liability must ensure members hold shares/interest for at least one year and transfers are made to the society or another member.
Funds are not to be divided by way of profit.
Contribution to charitable purposes is subject to conditions.

key_procedures: Application for Registration: Made to the Registrar, signed by qualified persons, and accompanied by proposed by-laws and required information (Section 8).
Registration: If the Registrar is satisfied with compliance and that by-laws are not contrary to the Act/rules, they may register the society and its by-laws (Section 9).
Amendment of By-laws: A copy of the amendment must be forwarded to the Registrar. If satisfied, the Registrar may register the amendment (Section 11).
Audit: The Registrar audits or causes to be audited the accounts of every registered society annually, including examination of overdue debts and valuation of assets/liabilities (Section 17).
Dissolution: Procedures for the dissolution of a society (Section 39).
Cancellation of Registration: Grounds and procedures for cancelling a society's registration (Section 40).
administration: The Registrar of Co-operative Societies, appointed by the State Government, and persons appointed to assist the Registrar.
important_notes: The Act has been repealed in its application to various Indian states and has been amended in other regions (Footnote 1).
The territorial extent excludes Part B States as they existed before November 1, 1956 (Section 1(2)).
Societies with limited liability and a share capital have restrictions on a member's interest in the share capital and total interest.
The liability of a society whose member is another registered society shall be limited, unless otherwise directed.
The liability of a society formed for lending to agriculturist members shall be unlimited, unless otherwise directed.

title: The Local Authorities Loans Act, 1914
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the borrowing powers of local authorities.
scope: Applies to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. It governs the borrowing powers of 'local authorities' for specific purposes.

key_definitions.local_authority: Any person legally entitled to the control or management of any local or municipal fund, or legally entitled to impose any cess, rate, duty or tax within any local area.
key_definitions.funds: Includes any local or municipal fund to the control or management of which such authority is legally entitled, and any cess rate duty or tax which such authority is legally entitled to impose, and any property vested in such authority.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.work: Includes a survey, whether incidental to any other work or not.
key_definitions.the_Government_or_the_appropriate_Govern: In relation to cantonment authorities and port authorities in major ports, the Central Government, and in relation to other local authorities, the State Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial applicability.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'local authority', 'funds', 'prescribed', 'work', and 'the Government'/'the appropriate Government'.

Outlines the conditions under which a local authority can borrow money on the security of its funds for specific purposes such as carrying out works, famine relief, epidemic prevention, and repayment of previous loans.

main_sections.section_title: Power to Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to make rules consistent with the Act regarding various aspects of borrowing, including the nature of funds, works, application procedures, inquiries, publication of particulars, loans from other sources, recording and enforcing conditions, manner of raising loans, inspection of works, repayment terms, utilization of unexpended balances, and other incidental matters.

main_sections.section_title: Remedy by attachment if loan not repaid
main_sections.description: Describes the procedure for attaching the funds of a local authority if a borrowed loan or interest is not repaid according to the loan conditions. It outlines the powers of an appointed officer to manage the attached funds and apply proceeds to satisfy the loan and associated costs.

Allows certain local authorities, with previous sanction from the appropriate Government, to borrow money by issuing short-term bills or promissory notes (not exceeding twelve months) for lawful borrowing purposes, subject to existing borrowing limits.

main_sections.section_title: Loans not to be effected except under this Act
main_sections.description: Prohibits local authorities from borrowing money or charging their funds except as provided by or under this Act. Contracts made otherwise are void, with exceptions for borrowing powers conferred by special enactments.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to loans existing previous to the fifth of September, 1871
main_sections.description: Specifies that the remedy of attachment under Section 5 is available for the recovery of money lent by the Secretary of State in Council to any local authority before September 5, 1871, and the interest due.
This section indicates that it was repealed by the Repealing Act, 1927.

important_rules: A local authority may borrow on the security of its funds for specific purposes including carrying out authorized works, famine/scarcity relief, preventing epidemic diseases, ancillary measures to relief and prevention, and repayment of previously borrowed money.
The period for repayment of a new loan for repaying a previous loan cannot exceed the maximum period fixed for the original loan.
Loans exceeding twenty-five lakhs of rupees (other than those made by the appropriate Government) require approval of the appropriate Government for terms including the date of flotation.
Local authorities cannot borrow or spend money for purposes not authorized by law or borrow by issuing bills/promissory notes payable within twelve months unless specifically allowed by rules.

The appropriate Government can make rules regarding the nature of funds for security, works for which money can be borrowed, application procedures, inquiries, publication of proceedings, loans from other sources, recording/enforcing conditions, manner of raising loans, inspection of works, repayment terms, utilization of unexpended balances, and other incidental matters.
If a loan or interest is not repaid, the appropriate Government can attach the funds used as security, and an appointed officer can manage and apply the proceeds to satisfy the debt and costs.
No attachment shall defeat prior legal charges on the funds; such prior charges must be paid first.
Local authorities shall not borrow money or charge their funds except under this Act; any other contract will be void, unless specific enactments allow otherwise.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The 'appropriate Government' (Central Government for cantonment and major port authorities, State Government for others) and officers appointed by the appropriate Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the attachment of local authority funds if loans are not repaid, and through the application of rules made by the appropriate Government.

rights: Local authorities have the right to borrow money for specified purposes.
Local authorities have the right to use funds for carrying out authorized works.
Local authorities have the right to repay previously borrowed money.
The lender (or the appropriate Government) has the right to attach funds if a loan is not repaid.
duties: Local authorities have a duty to repay borrowed money and interest according to loan conditions.
Local authorities have a duty to manage funds and works legally.
Local authorities have a duty to comply with rules made by the appropriate Government.
obligations: Local authorities are obligated to borrow only under the provisions of this Act, unless exempted by special enactments.
Local authorities are obligated to allow attachment of funds and cooperate with appointed officers in case of default.

key_procedures: Borrowing: A local authority may borrow subject to prescribed conditions and on the security of its funds for authorized purposes.
Application for Permission to Borrow: Local authorities must follow prescribed procedures for applying for permission to borrow.
Inquiries for Loans: The appropriate Government may conduct inquiries into proposed loans and the manner of conducting such inquiries is prescribed.
Repayment of Loans: Loans must be repaid in installments (if any) with interest, according to prescribed time and manner.

Attachment of Funds for Default: If a loan or interest is not repaid, the appropriate Government can attach the security funds. An appointed officer manages and applies the proceeds to satisfy the debt and costs.
Issue of Short-Term Bills: With previous sanction, local authorities can issue bills/promissory notes payable within twelve months.
administration: The 'appropriate Government' (Central Government or State Government, depending on the type of local authority) administers this Act and makes rules for its implementation.
important_notes: The Act has been amended in its application to the Central Provinces (now Madhya Pradesh) and partially extended to Berar.
Sub-section (2) of Section 1 was substituted and Section 2's definition of 'the Government'/'the appropriate Government' was also adapted.
A second proviso was added to Section 3(1) regarding loans exceeding twenty-five lakhs of rupees.
Section 9 and Schedule II were repealed by the Repealing Act, 1927.
Provisions regarding the application of the Act to loans existing before September 5, 1871, were substituted in Section 8.
Rules made under the Act, when published in the Official Gazette, have the effect of law.
Rules made by the Central Government are subject to parliamentary review.

title: The King of Oudh’s Estate Validation Act, 1917
purpose: To validate certain deeds of conveyance and a trust deed relating to properties of the late King of Oudh, to clarify the status of a specific share in a Government Promissory Note and its associated interest, and to provide for the distribution of certain funds.
scope: The Act applies to specific deeds concerning the estate of the late Wajid Ali Shah, King of Oudh. It deals with properties, an Emambarra, mosque, burial ground, and a fund (Sibtainabad Endowment Fund), and establishes rules for distribution of funds and interest related to the late King's estate, impacting beneficiaries of the estate and potentially those entitled to the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund.

key_definitions.late King: Refers to His late Majesty, Wajid Ali Shah, King of Oudh.
key_definitions.Sibtainabad Endowment Fund: A fund constituted for the up-keep and maintenance of a certain Emambarra, mosque, and burial ground.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the King of Oudh’s Estate Validation Act, 1917.

Validates three deeds of conveyance and a trust deed, along with all acts done thereunder, with specific provisos for reinterpreting the trust deed concerning a share in a Government Promissory Note and monetary amounts mentioned within it.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of Rs. 77,856 from the Fund
main_sections.description: Directs that a sum of Rs. 77,856 shall be released from the trusts of the trust deed and paid from the surplus monies of the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund to an officer appointed by the Governor General in Council for distribution.

Declares that the Rs. 77,856 mentioned in section 3, any further surplus monies declared by the Governor General in Council, and all interest accrued since January 1, 1914, on the specified share of the Government Promissory Note are to be treated as pensions. It also declares the said share of the note as a grant of money, making the Pensions Act, 1871, applicable with certain modifications for claims, commutation, and rule-making.

important_rules: The three deeds of conveyance and the trust deed relating to the late King of Oudh's estate are validated. (Section 2)

The trust deed shall be construed as if no reference was made to the Rs. 200,000 share of the Government Promissory Note, with specified alterations to monetary values mentioned in its recitals, effective from January 1, 1914. (Section 2)
The sum of Rs. 77,856 from the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund surplus is to be released and paid for distribution. (Section 3)

The Rs. 77,856, future declared surplus monies, and interest accrued since January 1, 1914, on the specified share of the Government Promissory Note are to be treated as pensions under the Pensions Act, 1871. (Section 4)
The specified share of the Government Promissory Note is to be treated as a grant of money under the Pensions Act, 1871. (Section 4)
Claims under Section 5 of the Pensions Act, 1871, as applied, must be preferred to an officer authorized by the Local Government. (Section 4(i))
Commutation of pension under Section 10 of the Pensions Act, 1871, can be exercised without the holder's consent if the payment rate is less than one rupee per month. (Section 4(ii))
The power to make rules under Sections 5 and 14 of the Pensions Act, 1871, extends to prescribing persons/classes of persons and principles for all distributions under this Act. (Section 4(iii))

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Governor General in Council (for appointing officers and declaring surplus monies), Local Government (for authorizing officers for claims), and potentially authorities under the Pensions Act, 1871, for matters related to pensions and grants.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the validation and confirmation of deeds, the release and distribution of funds, and the application of the Pensions Act, 1871, with specific modifications for claims, commutation, and rule-making related to the declared pensions and grants.

rights: Right to receive distributions of funds and interest declared as pensions or grants from the late King's estate.
Right to prefer claims under the Pensions Act, 1871, subject to authorization by the Local Government.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act, particularly regarding the validation of deeds and the distribution of funds.
Duty to manage and distribute funds and interest in accordance with the rules to be made under the Act.
obligations: Obligation for the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund to release Rs. 77,856.
Obligation for the Governor General in Council to appoint officers for receiving and distributing funds and to declare future surplus monies.
Obligation to adhere to the modified application of the Pensions Act, 1871, for claims and commutation.

key_procedures: Validation of Deeds: The Act automatically validates three deeds of conveyance and one trust deed, with specific legal reinterpretation of the trust deed's provisions regarding a Government Promissory Note share and associated monetary figures.
Release and Payment of Funds: Rs. 77,856 from the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund surplus is to be released and paid to an officer appointed by the Governor General in Council.
Declaration of Pensions/Grants: Funds and interest are declared as pensions and grants under the Pensions Act, 1871.
Claim Submission: Claims under the Pensions Act, 1871, are to be submitted to an officer authorized by the Local Government.
Commutation of Pension: Commutation of pension payments can be exercised without consent if the payment rate is below one rupee per month.
Rule Making: Powers to make rules for distribution principles and beneficiaries are granted, extending beyond the original scope of the Pensions Act, 1871.
administration: Governor General in Council and the Local Government, through appointed officers, and potentially relevant authorities under the Pensions Act, 1871.
important_notes: The validation of deeds is subject to specific modifications, particularly concerning the trust deed's reference to a share in a Government Promissory Note and certain monetary values.
The Act explicitly states that the sum of Rs. 77,856 is released from the trusts of the trust deed.
The application of the Pensions Act, 1871, is modified in key areas, including claim submission, commutation powers, and rule-making authority.

title: THE POST OFFICE CASH CERTIFICATES ACT, 1917
purpose: To restrict the transfer of Post Office 5-year Cash Certificates and to provide for the payment of Certificates standing in the name of deceased persons.
scope: Applies to Post Office 5-year Cash Certificates. Geographically, it initially applied to areas under Central Indian jurisdiction, with extensions noted to Berar, Khondmals District, Angul District, Porahat Estate, Goa, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Pondicherry.

key_definitions.transfer: In section 2, 'transfer' means a transfer inter vivos and does not include a transfer by operation of law.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Post Office Cash Certificates Act, 1917.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of transfer of Post Office 5-year Cash Certificates without the consent of an authorised officer
main_sections.description: Prohibits the transfer of Post Office 5-year Cash Certificates without the prior written consent of an officer of the Post Office authorized by the Central Government. This prohibition applies to transfers made before or after the commencement of the Act. 'Transfer' is defined as an inter vivos transfer, excluding transfers by operation of law.

main_sections.section_title: Payment on death of holder of Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for payment of a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate upon the death of its holder. It states that payment can be made in the manner provided by the Government Savings Banks Act, 1873, for deceased depositors. Provisions of sections 4 to 9 of the said Act apply, treating the certificate holder as a depositor and the certificate sum as a deposit. The monetary limit for simplified payment procedures in section 8 of the 1873 Act was increased from 'three thousand' to 'five thousand'. Powers vested in the Secretary of a Government Savings Bank are exercisable by the Post Master General for the area of issue, or if that area is in Pakistan, by a Post Master General specified by the Central Government. If certificates are from multiple post offices, powers are exercisable by the Post Master General for the area where any of the post offices are situated. This section also clarifies that no person is required to accept payment before the certificate reaches maturity.

important_rules: Rule 1: No transfer of a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate is valid without the previous written consent of an authorized Post Office officer.
Rule 2: Payment of a deceased holder's Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate will follow the procedures outlined in the Government Savings Banks Act, 1873, for deceased depositors.
Rule 3: The sum due on a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate belonging to a deceased person may be paid as per the provisions of sections 4 to 9 of the Government Savings Banks Act, 1873.
Rule 4: The Post Master General has the authority to make payments for deceased holders' certificates, acting in place of the Government Savings Bank Secretary.
Rule 5: A person is not obligated to accept payment for a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate before its maturity date.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Post Office officials, specifically the Post Master General and authorized officers of the Post Office.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the requirement of prior written consent for transfers and by applying the payment procedures for deceased depositors as stipulated in the Government Savings Banks Act, 1873.

rights: The right to transfer a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate with the consent of an authorized officer.
The right to receive payment on a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate upon the death of the holder, according to the prescribed procedure.
The right to not accept payment for a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate before its maturity date.
duties: The duty to obtain prior written consent from an authorized officer before transferring a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate.
The duty of the Post Office to make payment of certificates belonging to deceased persons in accordance with the specified legal provisions.

key_procedures: Procedure for Transfer: Obtain prior written consent from an officer of the Post Office authorized by the Central Government before making any transfer (inter vivos) of a Post Office 5-year Cash Certificate.

Procedure for Payment on Death: Upon the death of a certificate holder, payment of the sum due may be made by the Post Master General as per sections 4 to 9 of the Government Savings Banks Act, 1873, for deceased depositors. This involves applying the provisions of the said Act, with specific references to monetary limits and authority.
Procedure for Maturity Payment: A holder is not obliged to accept payment for a certificate before it reaches its maturity date.
administration: The Post Office, with administrative functions potentially overseen by the Central Government through authorized officers and Post Masters General.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various regions and territories over time, indicating its application beyond the original Central Indian jurisdiction.

The monetary limit for simplified payment of deceased depositors' estates under section 8 of the Government Savings Banks Act, 1873, was increased by this Act from 'three thousand' to 'five thousand' for Post Office Cash Certificates.
The provisions for payment on death are subject to the condition that the certificate has reached maturity, unless otherwise agreed or stipulated by law.
Transfers by operation of law are explicitly excluded from the definition of 'transfer' requiring consent.

title: The Poisons Act, 1919
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law regulating the importation, possession, and sale of poisons.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It primarily concerns the regulation of specified poisons, including their possession for sale, sale, and importation. Specific provisions may apply to certain areas or classes of persons.

key_definitions.poison: Any substance specified as a poison in a rule made or notification issued under this Act.
