Disclosure of Interest: Members with an interest in a business receiving or to receive assistance must immediately disclose it and either resign or follow the Administration's directions for disclosure. Advisory Board members with interest must disclose and abstain from participating in relevant proceedings.
Auditing of Accounts: The Administration must maintain accounts, which are audited annually by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
administration: The Rehabilitation Finance Administration, established as a Corporation, with the Central Government having significant oversight and directive powers.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1950 to include businesses where a substantial portion is owned by displaced persons, and to modify the definition of 'displaced person' and loan provisions.
The Act was made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh via a notification in 2019, overriding the initial exclusion.
The initial financial limit for loan advances was twelve crores and fifty lakhs of rupees, and for guarantees was two crores of rupees.
The Administration pays 3% interest per annum to the Central Government on advanced money.

title: THE DOCK WORKERS (REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT) ACT, 1948
purpose: To provide for regulating the employment of dock workers.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, with an exclusion for the State of Jammu and Kashmir (though later extended). It applies to dock workers and employers in ports, concerning the loading, unloading, movement, or storage of cargoes, and related ship preparation for receiving or discharging cargoes or leaving port.

key_definitions.Board: A Dock Labour Board established under section 5A.
key_definitions.cargo: Includes anything carried or to be carried in a ship or other vessel.
key_definitions.dock worker: A person employed or to be employed in, or in the vicinity of, any port on work in connection with the loading, unloading, movement or storage of cargoes, or work in connection with the preparation of ships or other vessels for the receipt or discharge of cargoes or leaving port.
key_definitions.employer: In relation to a dock worker, means the person by whom he is employed or to be employed.
key_definitions.Government: In relation to any major port, the Central Government and, in relation to any other port, the State Government.
key_definitions.scheme: A scheme made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'cargo', 'dock worker', 'employer', 'Government', and 'scheme'.

main_sections.section_title: Scheme for ensuring regular employment of workers
main_sections.description: Outlines the provisions that can be made by a scheme, focusing on the registration of dock workers and employers to ensure regular employment, and regulating their employment. It details specific aspects a scheme may cover, including obligations, recruitment, remuneration, minimum pay, and prohibitions on employment.

main_sections.section_title: Making, variation and revocation of schemes
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to make, amend, vary, or revoke schemes for ports or groups of ports through notification, subject to previous publication. It also allows the Government to direct port authorities to prepare draft schemes.

Provides for the constitution of Advisory Committees to advise the Government on matters arising from the administration of the Act or schemes. It specifies the composition of the committee, requiring equal representation from the Government, dock workers, and employers.

Empowers the Government to establish Dock Labour Boards for ports or groups of ports. These Boards are bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, responsible for administering schemes.

Defines the responsibilities of a Dock Labour Board, including administering the scheme for its port and exercising powers and functions conferred by the scheme. It also states that Boards are bound by directions from the Government.

Mandates that each Board maintain proper accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts. It details the audit process by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India or appointed auditors and the reporting requirements.
Requires each Board to prepare an annual report detailing its activities for the previous financial year and submit it to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and audited accounts, to be laid before Parliament or Legislature
main_sections.description: Specifies that the annual report, audited accounts, auditor's report, and government review of a Board's working are to be laid before Parliament or the State Legislature within a specified period.

Authorizes the Government to appoint Inspectors for the purposes of the Act. It defines their powers, including entering premises, inspecting documents, and taking evidence to ascertain compliance with schemes.
Grants the Government the power to appoint a person to inquire into the working of a Board and submit a report.
Allows the Government to supersede a Dock Labour Board in cases of grave emergency or persistent default or abuse of powers, after providing an opportunity for the Board to show cause.

main_sections.section_title: Acts or proceeding of Board and Advisory Committee not to be invalidated
main_sections.description: States that the acts or proceedings of a Board or Advisory Committee are not invalidated by reason of any defect in their constitution or appointment of members.
Deals with the cognizance of offences under the Act.
Addresses offences committed by companies.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Schemes and rules to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that schemes and rules made under the Act be laid before Parliament.
Provides for savings, likely in relation to other laws or existing arrangements.

important_rules: A scheme may provide for the registration of dock workers and employers to ensure regular employment and regulate their employment. (Section 3(1))
Schemes can define the obligations of dock workers and employers and the circumstances under which the scheme ceases to apply to them. (Section 3(2)(b))
Schemes can provide for regulating recruitment, registration, removal from registers, and imposition of registration fees for dock workers and employers. (Section 3(2)(c))
Schemes can regulate the terms and conditions of employment for dock workers, including remuneration, hours of work, and holidays. (Section 3(2)(d))
Schemes must secure minimum pay for dock workers who are available for work but cannot find full employment. (Section 3(2)(e))
Schemes can prohibit, restrict, or control the employment of dock workers and employers not covered by the scheme. (Section 3(2)(f))

Schemes may specify penalties for contravention, including imprisonment (up to three months for first contravention, six months for subsequent) or fine (up to five hundred rupees for first contravention, one thousand rupees for subsequent), or both. (Section 3(3))
The Government can make, amend, vary, or revoke schemes for ports through notification, subject to previous publication. (Section 4(1))
Advisory Committees must include an equal number of members representing the Government, dock workers, and employers. (Section 5(2))
Dock Labour Boards, when established, are bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. (Section 5A(2))
Dock Labour Boards are bound by directions from the Government. (Section 5B(2))
Inspectors have the power to enter premises/vessels where dock workers are employed, require production of documents, and examine them. (Section 6(3))

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months for a first contravention of a scheme, or six months for any subsequent contravention.
Fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for a first contravention of a scheme, or one thousand rupees for any subsequent contravention.
Both imprisonment and fine as specified above.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (Central or State) and appointed Inspectors.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through schemes made under the Act, which specify regulations and contraventions. Inspectors are empowered to investigate and ensure compliance. Dock Labour Boards administer the schemes and are subject to government direction and potential supersession.

rights: Right to receive minimum pay if full employment is not available (subject to scheme conditions). (Section 3(2)(e))
Right to have employment regulated by schemes ensuring greater regularity. (Section 3(1))
duties: Dock workers and employers have obligations as defined by the scheme for their application. (Section 3(2)(b))
obligations: Dock workers and employers must fulfill obligations specified in the scheme for it to apply to them. (Section 3(2)(b))
Dock Labour Boards must administer schemes and follow Government directions. (Section 5B)
Dock Labour Boards must maintain accounts and facilitate audits. (Section 5C)
Boards must provide facilities and documents for inquiries ordered by the Government. (Section 6A(2))

key_procedures: Making a scheme: Government issues a notification after previous publication, or directs a port authority to prepare a draft scheme. (Section 4)
Establishing a Dock Labour Board: Government issues a notification. (Section 5A(1))
Administering a scheme: A Dock Labour Board is responsible for administering the scheme for its port. (Section 5B(1))
Audit of accounts: Board accounts are audited annually by the Comptroller and Auditor-General or other qualified auditors. (Section 5C(2))
Reporting: Boards prepare annual reports and audited accounts to be submitted to the Government and laid before Parliament/Legislature. (Sections 5D, 5E)
Inquiry into a Board's working: Government can appoint a person to investigate and report. (Section 6A)
Superseding a Board: Government can supersede a Board after an inquiry or otherwise, following due process. (Section 6B)
administration: The Government (Central or State), and through Dock Labour Boards, Advisory Committees, and Inspectors appointed under the Act.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various Union Territories over time. (Footnotes 1, and note for Jammu and Kashmir)
Schemes can provide for penalties for contravention, including imprisonment and/or fine. (Section 3(3))
The Government can supersede a Dock Labour Board under specific circumstances after providing an opportunity for the Board to be heard. (Section 6B)

title: The West Godavari District (Assimilation of Laws on Federal Subjects) Act, 1949
purpose: To assimilate certain laws in force in different parts of the West Godavari District of the Province of Madras, specifically concerning matters enumerated in List I of the Seventh Schedule to the Government of India Act, 1935.
scope: Applies to the West Godavari District of the Province of Madras. It specifically addresses the assimilation of laws between the Eluru Taluk and the 'scheduled area' comprising specific villages listed in the Schedule.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed for the coming into force of this Act.
key_definitions.Eluru Taluk: The taluk of that name in the West Godavari district of the State of Madras.
key_definitions.law: Any Act, Ordinance, Regulation, rule, order or bye-law, relating to any of the matters enumerated in List I in the Seventh Schedule to the Government of India Act, 1935.
key_definitions.Scheduled area: The area comprised in the villages which are specified in the Schedule to this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Eluru Taluk', 'law', and 'Scheduled area'.

Specifies the process of assimilation. Laws in force in Eluru Taluk but not the scheduled area will extend to the scheduled area. Laws in force in the scheduled area but not Eluru Taluk will cease to be in force in the scheduled area, except for things done or omitted before the appointed day.
Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties arising from the transition between different sets of laws.

important_rules: Laws extending to or in force in Eluru Taluk, but not in the scheduled area, shall extend to or come into force in the scheduled area from the appointed day.
Laws in force in the scheduled area, but not in Eluru Taluk, shall cease to be in force in the scheduled area from the appointed day, except in relation to past actions or omissions.
The Central Government can issue orders to resolve any difficulties encountered during the transition from the old laws to the new assimilated laws.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for removal of difficulties)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Orders notified in the Official Gazette for removal of difficulties.

key_procedures: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint a date for the Act to come into force.
In case of difficulties in the transition of laws, the Central Government may issue orders in the Official Gazette to resolve them.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act addresses the change in status of certain areas from 'partially excluded areas' to regular areas, necessitating the assimilation of laws related to federal subjects.
The 'scheduled area' is explicitly defined by a list of villages in Polavaram Firka, Zangareddigudem Firka, and Jeelugumilli Firka.

title: THE CHARTERED ACCOUNTANTS ACT, 1949
purpose: To make provision for the regulation and development of the profession of chartered accountants and for that purpose to establish an Institute of Chartered Accountants.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to individuals who are members of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and defines who can be a chartered accountant, how they are enrolled, and their professional conduct. It also covers the establishment and functioning of the Institute, its Council, Regional Councils, and disciplinary bodies.

key_definitions.associate: An associate member of the Institute.
key_definitions.authority: The Appellate Authority constituted under section 22A.
key_definitions.board: The Quality Review Board constituted under section 28A.
key_definitions.board_of_discipline: The Board of Discipline constituted under sub-section (1) of section 21A.
key_definitions.chartered_accountant: A person who is a member of the Institute.
key_definitions.coordination_committee: The Coordination Committee constituted under section 9A.
key_definitions.companies_act: The Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013) or any other previous company law as defined in clause (67) of section 2 of the said Act.
key_definitions.council: The Council of the Institute constituted under section 9.
key_definitions.firm: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, and includes a limited liability partnership defined in clause (n) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, or a sole proprietorship registered with the Institute.
key_definitions.director_(discipline): The Director (Discipline) referred to in section 21 and includes Joint Director (Discipline).
key_definitions.disciplinary_committee: The Disciplinary Committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 21B.
key_definitions.disciplinary_directorate: The Disciplinary Directorate established under sub-section (1) of section 21.
key_definitions.fellow: A fellow member of the Institute.
key_definitions.holder_of_a_restricted_certificate: A person holding a permanent or temporary restricted certificate granted by a State Government under the Restricted Certificates Rules, 1932.
key_definitions.institute: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.partner: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, or in clause (q) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, as the case may be.
key_definitions.partnership: A partnership as defined in section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932; or a limited liability partnership which has no company as its partner.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.register: The Register of members of the Institute maintained under section 19 or the Register of firms of the Institute maintained under section 20B, as the case may be.
key_definitions.registered_accountant: Any person who has been enrolled on the Register of Accountants maintained by the Central Government under the Auditor’s Certificates Rules, 1932.
key_definitions.specified: Specified by rules made by the Central Government under this Act.
key_definitions.sole_proprietorship: An individual who engages himself in the practice of accountancy or offers to perform services referred to in clauses (ii) to (iv) of sub-section (2).
key_definitions.standing_committee: A Standing Committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 17.
key_definitions.tribunal: A Tribunal established under sub-section (1) of section 10B.
key_definitions.year: The period commencing on the 1st day of April of any year and ending on the 31st day of March of the succeeding year.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, specifies its extent to the whole of India, and outlines the process for its commencement through a Central Government notification.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'associate', 'chartered accountant', 'Institute', 'Council', 'firm', and 'year'. It also defines when a member is deemed 'to be in practice'.

Constitutes a body corporate by the name of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, granting it perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued.

main_sections.section_title: Entry of names in the Register of members
main_sections.description: Specifies the categories of persons who are entitled to have their names entered in the Register of members, including registered accountants, holders of restricted certificates, and those who pass prescribed examinations and complete prescribed training.
This section, though present in the arrangement of sections, is incomplete in the provided text. It likely deals with the classification of members into Fellows and Associates.
Establishes a Disciplinary Directorate.
Provides for the constitution of a Board of Discipline.
Provides for the constitution of a Disciplinary Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Authority, Disciplinary Committee, Board of Discipline and Director (Discipline) to have powers of civil court
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority, Disciplinary Committee, Board of Discipline, and Director (Discipline) the powers of a civil court.
Defines what constitutes professional or other misconduct for members of the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and functions of Regional Councils
main_sections.description: Deals with the establishment and responsibilities of Regional Councils.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for individuals who falsely claim to be a member of the Institute or engage in related fraudulent activities.

main_sections.section_title: Companies not to engage in accountancy
main_sections.description: Prohibits companies from engaging in the practice of accountancy.

main_sections.section_title: Unqualified persons not to sign documents
main_sections.description: Restricts unqualified persons from signing documents that require the signature of a chartered accountant.
Provides for the establishment of a Quality Review Board.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.
Grants the Council of the Institute the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules made by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Rules, regulations and notifications to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that all rules, regulations, and notifications issued under the Act must be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith by individuals or authorities acting under the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Members, etc., to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members of the Institute and certain officers to be public servants for the purposes of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to affect right of accountants to practise as such in Part B States
main_sections.description: States that the Act does not affect the right of accountants to practise as such in Part B States, implying a transitional provision or an exception.

important_rules: A member is deemed 'to be in practice' if they engage in accountancy, auditing, verification of financial transactions, or provide professional services related to accounting procedures, or hold themselves out as an accountant, for remuneration.
Persons registered as accountants or holders of restricted certificates at the commencement of the Act are entitled to have their names entered in the Register of members.
Persons who pass prescribed examinations and complete prescribed training are eligible for membership in the Institute.
Unqualified persons are prohibited from signing documents that require the signature of a chartered accountant.
Companies are not permitted to engage in accountancy practice.

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member (Section 24).
Penalty for using the name of the Council, awarding degrees of chartered accountancy, etc. (Section 24A).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Council of the Institute, the Disciplinary Directorate, the Board of Discipline, the Disciplinary Committee, the Authority (Appellate Authority), and the Central Government, depending on the specific provision.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of disciplinary bodies, the imposition of penalties for misconduct and violations, the review of quality of services, and the power of the Central Government to make rules and issue directions. Powers of civil courts are vested in certain authorities.

rights: Right of eligible persons to be enrolled as members of the Institute.
Right to practice as a chartered accountant upon fulfilling the prescribed conditions.
Right to appeal against decisions of disciplinary bodies to the Appellate Authority.
duties: Duty to abide by the professional and other misconduct definitions.
Duty to maintain professional standards and quality of services.
Duty to adhere to regulations and rules prescribed by the Council and the Central Government.
Duty to have names entered in the Register of members as per the prescribed manner.
Members, etc., are to be considered public servants.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a certificate of practice for those intending to practice.
Obligation to complete prescribed training and pass examinations.
Obligation to maintain the Register of members and firms.
Obligation to cooperate with disciplinary proceedings and quality reviews.

key_procedures: Procedure for entry of names in the Register of members (Section 4).
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Council, its committees, and Regional Councils.

Procedure for handling cases of professional or other misconduct, including investigation by the Disciplinary Directorate, inquiry by the Board of Discipline and Disciplinary Committee, and appeals to the Authority (Sections 21-22G).
Procedure for the establishment and functioning of the Quality Review Board (Sections 28A-28D).
Procedure for making rules and regulations by the Central Government and the Council (Sections 29A, 30, 30A).
administration: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, governed by its Council, is the primary administrative body. The Central Government also plays a significant role in rule-making, oversight, and direction.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2022 to include provisions for the Quality Review Board, Appellate Authority, and to broaden the definition of 'firm' and 'partnership'.
The Act does not affect the right of accountants to practise in Part B States (Section 32), indicating a historical context or transitional provision.
The commencement date was notified as 1st July, 1949.

title: THE INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES (BANKING AND INSURANCE COMPANIES) ACT, 1949
purpose: To provide for the adjudication of industrial disputes concerning banking and insurance companies having branches or other establishments in more than one State.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (though its applicability to Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh has been notified later). It specifically applies to industrial disputes concerning banking and insurance companies.

key_definitions.award: As assigned in section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
key_definitions.banking company: As assigned in section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
key_definitions.industrial dispute: As assigned in section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
key_definitions.insurance company: As assigned in section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its territorial extent.
Defines key terms by referring to the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, as amended by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of references by State Governments of certain industrial disputes for adjudication, inquiry or settlement
main_sections.description: Prohibits State Governments and their subordinate authorities from referring industrial disputes concerning banking or insurance companies to any tribunal or authority.

main_sections.section_title: Abatement of proceedings relating to disputes pending before State tribunals and reference of such disputes to tribunals constituted by the Central Government
main_sections.description: Deals with the abatement of proceedings for disputes pending before State tribunals before April 30, 1949, and mandates their reference to tribunals constituted by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Central Government to refer disputes in respect of which awards or decisions have been made for adjudication
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to refer disputes, even if an award or decision has been made by a State Government's tribunal, to an Industrial Tribunal constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and to stay the implementation of the existing award or decision.
Repeals the Industrial Disputes (Banking and Insurance Companies) Second Ordinance, 1949, and provides for the deeming of actions taken under the Ordinance as taken under the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: State Governments are prohibited from referring industrial disputes concerning banking or insurance companies to any tribunal or authority.
Rule 2: Industrial disputes concerning banking or insurance companies that were pending before State tribunals as of April 30, 1949, are deemed withdrawn and proceedings have abated.
Rule 3: The Central Government shall refer such abated disputes to Industrial Tribunals constituted by the Central Government for adjudication.

Rule 4: The Central Government can refer disputes concerning banking or insurance companies for which an award or decision has already been made by a State tribunal, to a Central Government-constituted Industrial Tribunal and stay the implementation of the prior award.
Rule 5: The Central Government can declare that a previously made award or decision by a State tribunal shall cease to be in operation after a new award is submitted by the Central Tribunal.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the constitution of Industrial Tribunals and reference of disputes for adjudication, as well as the power to stay or nullify existing awards.

rights: Right of banking and insurance companies to have their industrial disputes adjudicated by Central Government-appointed tribunals.
duties: Duty of State Governments not to refer certain industrial disputes to their tribunals.
Duty of the Central Government to refer abated disputes to appropriate tribunals.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, as amended by this Act, for the adjudication of specified disputes.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Reference of abated disputes by the Central Government to an Industrial Tribunal for adjudication.
Procedure 2: Reference of disputes with existing awards by the Central Government to an Industrial Tribunal for adjudication, including the power to stay the implementation of the existing award.
Procedure 3: Declaration by the Central Government that a previous award shall cease to be in operation after a new award is submitted.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act was enacted to address a specific situation regarding industrial disputes in banking and insurance companies, particularly those with multi-State operations.
The Act refers to and amends the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, for definitions and procedural aspects.
Section 3 of the Act was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1952.
The Act has been extended to the Scheduled Areas of the State of Orissa and amended in Uttar Pradesh.
Applicability to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh has been notified.

title: THE SCHEDULED SECURITIES (HYDERABAD) ACT, 1949
purpose: To provide for the control of the transfer of certain securities and for the issue of duplicate securities in respect thereof.
scope: This act applies to specific Government securities of Hyderabad as listed in the schedule, and their transfer and issuance of duplicate securities. It also applies to actions taken by the Reserve Bank of India and the Central Government concerning these securities.

key_definitions.scheduled security: Any Government security specified in the Schedule to this Act, excluding any duplicate security issued under section 4.
key_definitions.transfer: In relation to a scheduled security, includes the transfer of any interest in the scheduled security.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Scheduled Securities (Hyderabad) Act, 1949.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Bank', 'scheduled security', and 'transfer'.

main_sections.section_title: Title to scheduled security not affected by previous transfers.
main_sections.description: States that the Reserve Bank of India shall not recognize transfers of scheduled securities to parties other than the Government of Hyderabad, made before December 31, 1948, without the Central Government's approval. It clarifies that despite any such transfers, the scheduled security remains vested in the Government of Hyderabad.

Empowers the Reserve Bank of India to issue duplicate securities to the Government of Hyderabad in lieu of scheduled securities deemed lost, with the effect of securities issued under the Public Debt (Central Government) Act, 1944. It also states that all rights and remedies concerning the original scheduled securities are extinguished upon the issue of duplicates, and that the Bank shall impound and cancel presented original securities.
Prohibits the institution of suits or legal proceedings in any court for enforcing rights or remedies related to scheduled securities without the prior consent of the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides immunity from suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings to the Central Government, the Bank, or any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act.

Repeals the Scheduled Securities (Hyderabad) Ordinance, 1948. It further clarifies that anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act as if the Act had commenced on December 31, 1948.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Reserve Bank of India cannot recognize transfers of scheduled securities made before December 31, 1948, to entities other than the Government of Hyderabad without the Central Government's written approval.
Rule 2: The Reserve Bank of India shall issue duplicate securities to the Government of Hyderabad in lieu of lost scheduled securities.
Rule 3: Upon issuance of duplicate securities, all rights and remedies related to the original scheduled securities are extinguished.
Rule 4: The Reserve Bank of India must impound and cancel any presented scheduled securities.
Rule 5: No legal proceedings concerning scheduled securities can be initiated without the Central Government's prior consent.
Rule 6: Actions taken in good faith under this Act by the Central Government, the Bank, or any person are protected from legal action.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Reserve Bank of India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the bar of jurisdiction for legal proceedings, the requirement for Central Government consent for legal action, and the protection for actions taken in good faith. The Reserve Bank of India is responsible for the administrative actions of issuing duplicate securities and impounding/canceling original ones.

rights: The Government of Hyderabad has the right to receive duplicate securities in lieu of lost scheduled securities.
The Government of Hyderabad has the right to the vested title of the scheduled security.
duties: The Reserve Bank of India has the duty to issue duplicate securities to the Government of Hyderabad.
The Reserve Bank of India has the duty to impound and cancel presented scheduled securities.
The Reserve Bank of India has the duty to seek Central Government approval for recognizing certain transfers.
Individuals and entities must obtain Central Government consent before instituting legal proceedings regarding scheduled securities.
obligations: All transfers of scheduled securities not to the Government of Hyderabad made prior to December 31, 1948, require Central Government approval to be recognized by the Bank.
The scheduled security shall be deemed vested in the Government of Hyderabad.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: For lost scheduled securities: The Reserve Bank of India shall issue duplicate securities to the Government of Hyderabad, extinguishing all rights related to the original securities. The Bank will impound and cancel the original securities if presented.

Procedure 2: For legal proceedings: Any suit or legal proceeding for enforcing rights or remedies concerning scheduled securities requires the prior consent of the Central Government before being instituted in any court.
administration: The Central Government and the Reserve Bank of India.
important_notes: The Act retroactively deems actions taken under the repealed Ordinance XXXVII of 1948 as if they were taken under this Act, effective from December 31, 1948.
The Act specifies particular Government securities of Hyderabad, listed in the Schedule, for its application.

title: The Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Act, 1951
purpose: To provide for the erection and management of a National Memorial to perpetuate the memory of those killed or wounded on the 13th day of April, 1919, in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar.
scope: The Act applies to the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial located in Amritsar. It governs the management and administration of this memorial by a body of Trustees.

key_definitions.Memorial: The Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial to perpetuate the memory of those killed or wounded on the 13th day of April, 1919, on the site known as the Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar.
key_definitions.Trust: The Trust for the erection and management of the Memorial.
key_definitions.Trustees: The Trustees of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Act, 1951.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Memorial', 'Trust', and 'Trustees'.
Outlines the objectives of the Trust, which include erecting and maintaining buildings, acquiring property for the memorial, and raising funds for it.

main_sections.section_title: Trustees of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial
main_sections.description: Specifies the composition of the Board of Trustees, including the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Minister in-charge of Culture, the Leader of the Opposition, the Governor of Punjab, the Chief Minister of Punjab, and three eminent persons nominated by the Central Government. It also establishes the Trustees as a corporate body.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of nominated Trustees
main_sections.description: Defines the term of office for nominated Trustees as five years, with eligibility for renomination, and allows for termination of their term by the Central Government.
States that all property and funds mentioned in the Schedule, and any future property acquired for the Memorial, shall vest in the Trustees.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Trustees to appoint committee of management
main_sections.description: Grants the Trustees the power to appoint a committee of management to oversee the Trust's affairs, with defined powers and limitations.
Requires the Trust to meet annually to approve audited accounts and conduct other necessary business.

main_sections.section_title: Validity of acts of Trustees not to be questioned by reason of vacancy, etc.
main_sections.description: Ensures that the actions of the Trustees are not invalidated due to any vacancy or defect in their constitution.
Mandates annual audit of the Trust's accounts by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, with the audit report to be presented to Parliament.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the objects of the Act, covering aspects like fund management, accounts, memorial maintenance, and public access. It also specifies that rules must be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Trustees to make regulations
main_sections.description: Allows the Trustees to make regulations concerning meetings, circulation of decisions, management committee, and appointment of staff.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Stipulates that all rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulment.

important_rules: Rules made by the Central Government can provide for the manner of keeping, depositing, or investing memorial funds, authentication of payment orders, and the form of accounts.
Rules can also cover the erection, improvement, maintenance, and management of the Memorial, and conditions for public access and conduct within its precincts.
Breach of rules related to public access and conduct within the Memorial's precincts can be punishable with a fine up to one hundred rupees.

Trustees can make regulations on convening meetings, quorum, procedure, decision-making by circulation, term and powers of the management committee, and appointment and terms of service of officers and servants.

penalties: A fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for breach of rules regarding public access to and conduct within the precincts of the Memorial (Section 9(3)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Trustees of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial, and the Central Government for rule-making and oversight.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is primarily through the Trustees managing the memorial, the application of rules and regulations made under the Act, and the audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. Penalties are specified for certain breaches of rules.

rights: The Trustees have the right to sue and be sued, acquire and hold property, enter into contracts, and do all necessary acts for the purposes of the Act.
The public has rights of access to the Memorial under conditions and regulations set by the Trustees.
The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India has the right to demand production of documents and inspect the Trust's office for audit purposes.
duties: The Trust has a duty to erect and maintain the Memorial and suitable buildings, parks, etc.
The Trust has a duty to acquire lands, buildings, and other properties for its purposes.
The Trust has a duty to raise and receive funds for the Memorial.
The Trustees have a duty to manage the affairs of the Trust and appoint a committee of management if necessary.
The Trust has a duty to approve audited accounts annually.
The Trust has a duty to forward audited accounts and audit reports to the Central Government annually.
The Central Government has a duty to cause the audit report to be laid before each House of Parliament.
obligations: The Trust is obligated to ensure that all property and funds are vested in the Trustees for the purposes of the Memorial.
The Trust is obligated to comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
The Trust is obligated to pay any expenditure incurred in connection with the audit of its accounts to the Comptroller and Auditor-General.

key_procedures: Appointment of Trustees: The Prime Minister, Minister in-charge of Culture, Leader of Opposition, Governor of Punjab, Chief Minister of Punjab, and three eminent persons nominated by the Central Government form the Board of Trustees.
Management of Affairs: The Trustees may appoint a committee of management to handle the day-to-day affairs of the Trust.
Approval of Accounts: The Trust must hold an annual meeting to approve audited accounts.
Audit Process: Accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India at specified intervals.
Reporting to Parliament: Audited accounts and audit reports are submitted to the Central Government, which then lays them before Parliament.
Rule-making by Central Government: The Central Government can make rules, which must be laid before Parliament.
Regulation-making by Trustees: Trustees can make regulations concerning their meetings and the management committee, which must also be laid before Parliament.
administration: The Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Trust, administered by the Trustees, with oversight and rule-making powers vested in the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act has been amended by The Delegated Legislation Provisions (Amendment) Act, 2004, and The Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial (Amendment) Act, 2006.
Clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 4 was omitted by Act 39 of 2019.
The wording of Clause (d) of sub-section (1) of Section 4 was substituted by Act 39 of 2019.

title: The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
purpose: To provide for the institution of provident funds, pension fund, and deposit-linked insurance fund for employees in factories and other establishments.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to every establishment which is a factory engaged in industries specified in Schedule I and employing twenty or more persons, and to other establishments employing twenty or more persons or classes of such establishments as specified by the Central Government. Can be applied to establishments employing fewer than twenty persons with prior notice, or by agreement between employer and majority of employees.

key_definitions.appropriate_government: Central Government for establishments controlled by the Central Government, connected with railways, major ports, mines, oil fields, controlled industries, or having branches in multiple states; State Government for other establishments.
key_definitions.authorised_officer: Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Deputy Provident Fund Commissioner, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, or any other officer authorized by the Central Government.
key_definitions.basic_wages: All emoluments earned by an employee while on duty or on leave with wages, in accordance with the contract of employment, paid or payable in cash. Excludes cash value of food concession, dearness allowance, house-rent allowance, overtime allowance, bonus, commission, and other similar allowances.
key_definitions.contribution: A contribution payable in respect of a member under a Scheme or the contribution payable in respect of an employee to whom the Insurance Scheme applies.
key_definitions.controlled_industry: Any industry declared by a Central Act to be expedient in the public interest for Union control.
key_definitions.employer: Owner or occupier of a factory (including legal representatives and managers); for other establishments, the person or authority with ultimate control, including managers, managing directors, or managing agents.
key_definitions.employee: Any person employed for wages in any kind of work in or in connection with an establishment, getting wages directly or indirectly from the employer. Includes persons employed through a contractor and apprentices not engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961 or standing orders.
key_definitions.factory: Any premises, including precincts, where a manufacturing process is carried on or ordinarily carried on, with or without the aid of power.
key_definitions.fund: The provident fund established under a Scheme.
key_definitions.industry: Any industry specified in Schedule I or any other industry added by notification under section 4.
key_definitions.insurance_fund: The Deposit-linked Insurance Fund established under sub-section (2) of section 6C.
key_definitions.insurance_scheme: The Employees’ Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme framed under sub-section (1) of section 6C.
key_definitions.manufacture_or_manufacturing_process: Any process for making, altering, repairing, ornamenting, finishing, packing, oiling, washing, cleaning, breaking up, demolishing or otherwise treating or adapting any article or substance with a view to its use, sale, transport, delivery or disposal.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Fund.
key_definitions.occupier_of_a_factory: The person with ultimate control over the affairs of the factory; if managed by an agent, the agent is the occupier.
key_definitions.pension_fund: The Employees’ Pension Fund established under sub-section (2) of section 6A.
key_definitions.pension_scheme: The Employees’ Pension Scheme framed under sub-section (1) of section 6A.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.recovery_officer: Any officer of the Central Government, State Government or the Board of Trustees authorized by the Central Government to exercise recovery powers.
key_definitions.scheme: The Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme framed under section 5.

main_sections.description: Defines the short title, territorial extent, and the conditions under which the Act applies to various establishments.
Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, including 'appropriate Government', 'basic wages', 'employer', 'employee', 'factory', 'Fund', 'industry', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment to include all departments and branches
main_sections.description: Clarifies that an establishment includes all its departments and branches.

main_sections.section_title: Power to apply Act to an establishment which has a common provident fund with another establishment
main_sections.description: Grants power to apply the Act to an establishment having a common provident fund with another.

main_sections.section_title: Power to add to Schedule I
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to add industries to Schedule I.
Deals with the framing of Employees' Provident Fund Schemes by the Central Government.
Provides for the establishment of a Central Board.

main_sections.section_title: Contributions and matters which may be provided for in Schemes
main_sections.description: Outlines provisions related to contributions and other matters that can be included in the Schemes.
Provides for the establishment of an Employees' Pension Scheme.
Provides for the establishment of an Employees' Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of moneys due from employers
main_sections.description: Empowers the determination of amounts due from employers.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of moneys due from employers
main_sections.description: Specifies the methods for recovering money due from employers.

main_sections.section_title: Priority of payment of contributions over other debts
main_sections.description: Establishes the priority of contributions over other debts.

main_sections.section_title: Employer not to reduce wages, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits employers from reducing wages or altering other conditions of service to the disadvantage of employees due to the Act.
Deals with the appointment and powers of Inspectors.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or Schemes.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain establishments
main_sections.description: Provides exemptions for certain categories of establishments from the purview of the Act.
Grants power to the Central Government to exempt establishments or employees from the provisions of the Act.
Allows for the delegation of powers vested in the Central Government or other authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Enables the Central Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: Employers must contribute to the Provident Fund, Pension Fund, and Deposit-linked Insurance Fund as prescribed by the Schemes.
Employees' wages are subject to specific inclusions and exclusions for calculating basic wages for contribution purposes.
Employers are prohibited from reducing wages or altering conditions of service to the detriment of employees due to the Act.
Contributions to the Fund have priority over other debts in cases of insolvency or winding up of establishments.
Inspectors have the power to enter establishments, inspect records, and take evidence for enforcing the Act.
Provisions exist for the recovery of moneys due from employers, including through certificates to Recovery Officers.
The Act can be applied to establishments with 20 or more employees, with provisions for exceptions and specific conditions.
The Central Government has the power to exempt certain establishments or employees from the provisions of the Act under specified conditions.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of provisions, including fines and imprisonment.
Enhanced punishment for certain offenses after previous conviction.
Certain offenses are cognizable.
Power of court to make orders for compliance.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforced by the Central Provident Fund Organization (though not explicitly named as such in the provided text, the functions described point to this organization), Central Government, State Governments, and authorized officers/inspectors.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through determination of moneys due from employers, recovery proceedings, inspections, penal provisions for contravention, and court actions.

rights: Employees have the right to contributions to their provident fund, pension fund, and deposit-linked insurance fund.
Employees have the right to appeal against certain orders passed under the Act.
Employees have the right to receive benefits from the Funds as per the Schemes.
duties: Employers have the duty to deduct and pay contributions to the Funds.
Employers have the duty to maintain records and furnish information as required.
Employers have the duty not to reduce wages or alter service conditions to the disadvantage of employees.
Employers have the duty to cooperate with Inspectors and authorized officers.
obligations: Obligation for establishments meeting the criteria to comply with the Act and its Schemes.
Obligation to pay contributions on time.
Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the framed Schemes and the Act.

key_procedures: Determination of moneys due from employers by authorized officers.
Recovery of moneys due from employers through specified modes, including certificate proceedings and application of Income-tax Act provisions.
Appeals to Tribunals against certain orders.
Filing of appeals with a deposit of the amount due.
Procedure for taking assistance of legal practitioners and appointment of presenting officers for appeals.
Application of the Act to establishments by notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government or by agreement between employer and employees.
Exemption of establishments or employees by the Central Government through notification.
administration: The Central Government, State Governments, Central Provident Fund Commissioner, and other authorized officers and the Board of Trustees administer the Act.
important_notes: The Act has been extended to various Union Territories over time.
Specific industries are listed in Schedule I to which the Act applies.
The Central Government can exempt establishments or employees from the Act's provisions.
The Act can be applied to establishments with fewer than twenty employees under certain conditions.
The definition of 'basic wages' for calculating contributions excludes several allowances and perquisites.

title: The Delivery of Books and Newspapers (Public Libraries) Act, 1954
purpose: To provide for the delivery of books and newspapers to the National Library and other designated public libraries.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to publishers of books and newspapers published within these territories. It also applies to books and newspapers published by or under the authority of the Government, excluding those meant for official use only. The Act covers the National Library at Calcutta and three other public libraries specified by the Central Government.

key_definitions.book: Includes every volume, part or division of a volume and pamphlet, in any language, and every sheet of music, map, chart or plan separately printed or lithographed, but does not include a newspaper published in conformity with the provisions of section 5 of the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867.
key_definitions.newspaper: Means any printed periodical work containing public news or comments on public news published in conformity with the provisions of section 5 of the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867.
key_definitions.public libraries: Means the National Library at Calcutta and any three other libraries which may be specified by the Central Government in this behalf by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Delivery of Books and Newspapers (Public Libraries) Act, 1954' and specifies its territorial extent to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now applicable to Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'book', 'newspaper', and 'public libraries'.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of books to public libraries
main_sections.description: Mandates publishers to deliver one copy of every book published to the National Library and one copy to each of the other three public libraries within thirty days of publication, at their own expense. Specifies the format and quality of the copies to be delivered.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery of newspapers to public libraries
main_sections.description: Requires publishers to deliver one copy of each issue of a newspaper to each public library as notified by the Central Government, as soon as it is published.
Stipulates that the person in charge of a public library or an authorized person must provide a written receipt to the publisher upon delivery of a book or newspaper.

Prescribes penalties for contravention of the Act or rules, including a fine up to fifty rupees and an additional fine equivalent to the value of the book or newspaper. The court may direct part of the fine as compensation to the library.
Specifies that cognizance of offences under the Act can only be taken upon a complaint by an empowered officer and that only presidency magistrates or first-class magistrates can try such offences.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to books and newspapers published by Government
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act applies to books and newspapers published by or under the authority of the Government, except for books meant for official use only.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, which must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

important_rules: Publishers must deliver a copy of every book published to the National Library and three other specified public libraries within thirty days of publication, at their own expense.
The copy of the book delivered to the National Library must be the best copy, including all maps and illustrations, bound, sewed, or stitched together on the best paper.
The copy delivered to other public libraries should be on the paper used for the largest number of copies printed for sale and in the condition prepared for sale.
Publishers must deliver one copy of each issue of a newspaper to each notified public library as soon as it is published, at their own expense.
Second or subsequent editions of a book with no additions or alterations do not require re-delivery if a copy of a previous edition has already been delivered.

penalties: Fine which may extend to fifty rupees.
If the contravention is in respect of a book, an additional fine equivalent to the value of the book.
The court may direct that the whole or any part of the fine realised shall be paid as compensation to the public library to which the book or newspaper ought to have been delivered.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (through empowered officers for cognizance of offences).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings initiated upon complaint by an empowered officer. Courts of presidency magistrate or first-class magistrate have jurisdiction.

rights: Publishers have the right to receive a written receipt for delivered books/newspapers.
Public libraries have the right to receive copies of published books and newspapers as specified.
duties: Publishers have the duty to deliver copies of books and newspapers to specified public libraries within stipulated times.
Publishers have the duty to deliver books at their own expense.
Publishers have the duty to ensure delivered books are in the specified format and quality.
obligations: The obligation to deliver books and newspapers to public libraries.
The obligation to comply with the format and delivery requirements specified in the Act.
The obligation for publishers to bear the cost of delivery.

key_procedures: Publisher publishes a book or newspaper.
Within thirty days of publication (for books) or upon publication (for newspapers), the publisher delivers a copy to the National Library and other specified public libraries at their own expense.
The library staff provides a written receipt for the delivered items.
If a publisher contravenes the Act, an empowered officer of the Central Government can initiate a complaint.
The case is tried by a presidency magistrate or a first-class magistrate.
The court may impose penalties and award compensation.
administration: Central Government (power to make rules, specify libraries, empower officers).
important_notes: The Act applies to books and newspapers published by or under the authority of the Government, but excludes books meant solely for official use.
The Act was amended in 1956 to include newspapers and to enhance penalties.
As of 2019, the Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

title: THE HIGH COURT JUDGES (SALARIES AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) ACT, 1954
purpose: To regulate salaries and certain conditions of service of the Judges of High Courts.
scope: This act applies to the Judges of High Courts in India. This includes Chief Justices, acting Chief Justices, additional Judges, and acting Judges. It covers their salaries, pensions, leave entitlements, and other conditions of service.

key_definitions.acting Chief Justice: A Judge appointed under article 223 of the Constitution to perform the duties of the Chief Justice.
key_definitions.acting Judge: A person appointed to act as a Judge under clause (2) of article 224 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.actual service: Includes time spent on duty as a Judge, performing other functions at the request of the President, vacations (excluding leave absence), joining time on transfer, time as a Judge of a former Indian High Court, time as an ad hoc Supreme Court Judge, and vacation taken as a Judge of a former Indian High Court.
key_definitions.additional Judge: A person appointed as an additional Judge under clause (1) of article 224 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.High Court: A High Court for a State, including High Courts that exercised jurisdiction in Part A States or corresponding Provinces before the Constitution commenced.
key_definitions.Judge: A Judge of a High Court, including the Chief Justice, acting Chief Justice, additional Judge, and acting Judge.
key_definitions.pension: Any kind of pension or gratuity payable to or in respect of a Judge, including death or retirement benefits.
key_definitions.service for pension: Includes actual service, leave on full allowances at the monthly salary rate, and joining time on return from leave out of India.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The High Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1954'.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'acting Chief Justice', 'acting Judge', 'actual service', 'additional Judge', 'High Court', 'Judge', 'pension', 'service for pension', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Kinds of leave admissible to a judge
main_sections.description: Specifies the types of leave admissible to a judge: leave on full allowances, leave on half allowances, or leave partly on full and partly on half allowances. It also defines how leave on full allowances is reckoned relative to leave on half allowances and mentions the possibility of casual leave.

main_sections.section_title: Leave account showing the amount of leave due
main_sections.description: Mandates the maintenance of a leave account for each Judge, detailing the amount of leave due. It specifies what is credited to this account, including one-fourth of actual service time, compensation for un-enjoyed vacation, and leave earned in previous pensionable posts.
Entitles a Judge to claim the cash equivalent of leave salary on retirement for the period of leave at their credit, calculated on full allowances basis.

main_sections.section_title: Aggregate amount of leave which may be granted
main_sections.description: Sets the maximum aggregate amount of leave a Judge can be granted during their service, specified in terms of leave on half allowances and leave on full allowances. It also defines the maximum period of leave that can be granted at one time.

main_sections.section_title: Commutation of leave on half allowances into leave on full allowances
main_sections.description: Allows a Judge to commute leave on half allowances into leave on full allowances on medical certificate, up to a maximum of three months during their service.
Permits granting of leave on half allowances in excess of the credited amount, either on medical certificate or otherwise, for a limited period, provided the Judge is expected to return to duty.
States that rules for special disability leave applicable to Central Civil Services, Class I officers will apply to Judges disabled in the performance of their duties.
Allows for extraordinary leave to be granted to a Judge for a limited period in excess of other permissible leave, during which no salary or allowances are payable.
Specifies that the monthly rate of leave salary payable to a Judge will be in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 3.

Allows a Judge to combine vacation with leave under specific conditions regarding the timing and duration of the leave relative to the vacation, with provisos related to appointing an acting Chief Justice or the Judge's expected return to duty.

main_sections.section_title: Consequences of overstaying leave or vacation
main_sections.description: States that a Judge overstaying leave or vacation will not receive salary for the period of absence, unless such absence is due to circumstances beyond their control, in which case it may be treated as leave.

main_sections.section_title: Authority competent to grant leave, etc.
main_sections.description: Designates the Governor of the State where the High Court's principal seat is located, in consultation with the Chief Justice of that High Court, as the authority competent to grant, refuse, revoke, or curtail leave to a Judge.
Specifies the monthly salaries for the Chief Justice of a High Court and for a Judge of a High Court.
Introduces the provisions for pension payable to Judges upon retirement, subject to the Act's stipulations.

important_rules: Leave granted to a Judge can be on full allowances, half allowances, or a combination of both.
A leave account must be maintained for each Judge, crediting leave earned through actual service, un-enjoyed vacation, and previous pensionable posts.
Judges are entitled to encash leave salary on retirement for leave at their credit.
The maximum aggregate leave that can be granted is three years plus compensation for un-enjoyed vacation.
Leave on full allowances can be commuted into leave on full allowances on medical certificate up to a maximum of three months.
Leave not due can be granted on medical certificate or otherwise for up to six months, provided the Judge is expected to return to duty.
Special disability leave rules for Central Civil Services Class I officers apply to Judges.
Extraordinary leave, without pay or allowances, can be granted for a limited period.
Judges can combine vacation with leave under specific conditions.
Overstaying leave or vacation results in forfeiture of salary for the period of absence, unless due to unavoidable circumstances.
The Governor of the state, in consultation with the Chief Justice, is the authority competent to grant leave.
Specific monthly salaries are stipulated for Chief Justices and Judges of High Courts.
Provisions exist for pension payable to Judges upon retirement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but implied to be through administrative and judicial mechanisms related to the High Courts and the Governor's office.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied to be through the administrative procedures for granting leave, calculating salaries and pensions, and the consequences of overstaying leave or vacation.

rights: Right to various kinds of leave (full allowances, half allowances, extraordinary leave, special disability leave, leave not due).
Right to combine leave with vacation.
Right to encash leave salary on retirement.
Right to pension upon retirement.
Right to rent-free houses, conveyance facilities, and sumptuary allowance (as indicated in Chapter IV and Schedule headings, though not detailed in text).
Right to medical treatment facilities (as indicated in Chapter IV and Schedule headings, though not detailed in text).
duties: Duty to perform official duties as a Judge.
Duty to return to duty at the end of granted leave or vacation, unless otherwise specified.
obligations: To adhere to the limits and conditions specified for granting and taking leave.
To abide by the rules regarding overstaying leave or vacation.

key_procedures: Procedure for maintaining a leave account for each Judge, crediting and debiting leave.
Procedure for granting leave, including obtaining medical certificates where required.
Procedure for commuting leave on half allowances into leave on full allowances.
Procedure for combining leave with vacation, subject to conditions.
Procedure for calculating and paying salaries and pensions.
Procedure for handling overstaying of leave or vacation, including potential debiting of leave or forfeiture of salary.
administration: The administration of this act involves the High Courts themselves, the respective State Governors in consultation with Chief Justices for leave matters, and the administrative machinery responsible for the payment of salaries and pensions.
important_notes: The Act has been subject to several amendments over the years, as indicated by the insertion and omission of clauses and the references to amendment acts and their effective dates.
Certain sections and clauses have been omitted by later amendments (e.g., Section 10, 18, 25, and parts of Section 2).
The Act refers to Articles of the Constitution and other Acts (e.g., Government of India Act, 1935), indicating its integration within the broader legal framework of India.
Specific financial entitlements like salaries and pensions are subject to prevailing government regulations and are updated through amendments.
The Act allows for the application of rules from Central Civil Services for specific situations like special disability leave.

title: The Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur (New State) Act, 1954
purpose: To provide for the formation of the new State of Himachal Pradesh by uniting the existing States of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the existing States of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur, and the newly formed State of Himachal Pradesh. It concerns the formation of the new state, representation in the central and state legislatures, courts, and administrative provisions.

key_definitions.existing_states: The States specified as Bilaspur and Himachal Pradesh in Part C of the First Schedule to the Constitution immediately before the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.existing_state: Either of the existing States (Bilaspur or Himachal Pradesh).
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, ordinance, regulation, order, rule, scheme, notification, bye-law or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or in any part of either of the existing States.
key_definitions.order: An order published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.parliamentary_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.sitting_member: In relation to either House of Parliament or in relation to the Legislature of the existing State of Himachal Pradesh, means a person who immediately before the commencement of this Act is a member of that House or that Legislature, as the case may be.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Formation of the new State of Himachal Pradesh
main_sections.description: Establishes the new Part C State of Himachal Pradesh by uniting the existing States of Bilaspur and Himachal Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the formation of the new State of Himachal Pradesh, including omitting Bilaspur as a separate state and adjusting territorial descriptions.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in the Council of States
main_sections.description: Allocates one seat to the new State in the Council of States and specifies how the sitting member will represent the new State.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution to adjust the Table of Seats for Part C States to include the new Himachal Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Representation in the House of the People
main_sections.description: Allots 4 seats to the new State in the House of the People until other provision is made by law.

main_sections.section_title: Parliamentary constituencies of the new State and their delimitation
main_sections.description: Defines the initial parliamentary constituencies of the new State and states that the Delimitation of Parliamentary Constituencies (Part C States) Order, 1951, will apply with amendments.

main_sections.section_title: Court of the Judicial Commissioner for the new State
main_sections.description: Provides for the amalgamation of the existing Courts of the Judicial Commissioner into a single Court for the new State, defining its jurisdiction, powers, and the status of its officers and advocates.
States that existing laws in the constituent states will continue to be in force in the new State, subject to modifications.
Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: The new State of Himachal Pradesh is formed by uniting the existing States of Bilaspur and Himachal Pradesh.
The First and Fourth Schedules of the Constitution are amended to reflect the new State and its representation.
Existing laws continue in force in the new State, subject to adaptation and construction.
Existing taxes continue to be levied in the new State.
The Courts of the Judicial Commissioner of the existing states are amalgamated into a single court for the new State.
Proceedings pending in the existing courts are transferred to the new court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, Parliament, and the relevant administrative and judicial authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through parliamentary enactment, constitutional amendments, notifications in the Official Gazette, and the functioning of established judicial and administrative bodies.

rights: Right to representation in the Council of States and the House of the People for the new State.
Right for advocates, vakils, and pleaders practicing in existing courts to continue practice in the new court, subject to rules.
duties: Duty to form the new State of Himachal Pradesh.
Duty to amend constitutional schedules for representation.
Duty to ensure continuity of laws, taxes, and administrative functions.
Duty for the Judicial Commissioner's Court to function with existing jurisdiction and powers.
obligations: Obligation for the Central Government to appoint the commencement date.
Obligation for the Delimitation Commission to revise its orders if necessary for the new State's representation.
Obligation for the new Court to handle pending proceedings from existing courts.

key_procedures: Formation of the new State by uniting existing states.
Amendment of constitutional schedules via parliamentary action.
Delimitation of parliamentary constituencies for the new State.
Amalgamation of Judicial Commissioner's Courts and transfer of pending proceedings.
The Central Government may issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for appointing the commencement date and making orders to remove difficulties. The Act also impacts the functioning of the Judicial Commissioner's Courts and parliamentary bodies.
important_notes: Several sections, particularly those related to the Legislative Assembly of the new State, were repealed by the Adaptation of Laws (No. 3) Order, 1956.
The Act clarifies that references to Himachal Pradesh in the Representation of the People Act, 1950, as amended, shall be construed as references to the new State.

title: THE PROTECTION OF CIVIL RIGHTS ACT, 1955
purpose: To prescribe punishment for the preaching and practice of 'Untouchability', for the enforcement of any disability arising therefrom and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to individuals who preach or practice 'untouchability' and enforces disabilities arising from it, thereby affecting civil rights. It also covers offenses related to social disabilities, denial of services, and restrictions on exercising rights due to the abolition of 'untouchability'.

key_definitions.civil_rights: Any right accruing to a person by reason of the abolition of 'untouchability' by article 17 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.hotel: Includes a refreshment room, a boarding house, a lodging house, a coffee house and a cafe.
key_definitions.place: Includes a house, building and other structure and premises; and also includes a tent, vehicle and vessel.
key_definitions.place_of_public_entertainment: Includes any place to which the public are admitted and in which an entertainment is provided or field. 'Entertainment' includes any exhibition performance, game, sport and any other form of amusement.
key_definitions.place_of_public_worship: A place, by whatever name known, which is used as a place of public religious worship or which is dedicated generally to, or is used generally by persons professing any religion or belonging to any religious denomination or any section thereof, for the performance of any religious service, or for offering prayers therein, and includes all lands and subsidiary shrines appurtenant or attached to any such place, a privately owned place of worship which is in fact allowed by the owner thereof to be used as a place of public worship, and such land or subsidiary shrine appurtenant to such privately owned place of worship as is allowed by the owner thereof to be used as a place of public religious worship.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheduled_Castes: Has the meaning assigned to it in clause (24) of article 366 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.shop: Any premises where goods are sold either wholesale or by retail or both wholesale and by retail, and includes any place from where goods are sold by a hawker or vendor or from a mobile van or cart; a laundry and a hair cutting saloon; any other place where services are rendered to customers.
