main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of its commencement, which is to be appointed by the Central Government through notification.

This section defines various terms used in the Act, including 'civil rights', 'hotel', 'place', 'place of public entertainment', 'place of public worship', 'prescribed', 'Scheduled Castes', and 'shop'.

This section outlines the punishment for preventing a person, on the ground of 'untouchability', from entering a place of public worship or performing religious services therein, or from using sacred waters or bathing at ghats in the same manner as others.

This section specifies the punishment for enforcing various social disabilities on any person on the ground of 'untouchability', including restrictions on access to shops, hotels, public entertainment, utensils, practice of profession, use of public utilities, public conveyances, residential premises, observance of customs, and use of jewellery.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for refusing to admit person to hospitals, etc.
main_sections.description: This section prescribes punishment for refusing admission to any person to a hospital, dispensary, educational institution, or hostel on the ground of 'untouchability', or for discriminating against such a person after admission.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for refusing to sell goods or render services
main_sections.description: This section details the punishment for refusing to sell goods or render any service to a person on the ground of 'untouchability' at the same time, place, and on the same terms as provided to others.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for other offences arising out of “untouchability”
main_sections.description: This section covers broader offenses related to 'untouchability', including preventing the exercise of rights accruing from the abolition of 'untouchability', molesting, injuring, annoying, boycotting, inciting others to practice 'untouchability', insulting members of Scheduled Castes, and offenses committed in reprisal for exercising such rights.

main_sections.section_title: Unlawful compulsory labour when to be deemed to be a practice of “untouchability”
main_sections.description: This section deems compelling any person, on the ground of 'untouchability', to do scavenging, sweeping, removing carcasses, flaying animals, or other similar jobs as enforcing a disability arising out of 'untouchability' and prescribes punishment for it.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation or suspension of licences in certain cases
main_sections.description: This section empowers the State Government to cancel or suspend licences granted to individuals or institutions that violate the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Resumption or suspension of grants made by Government
main_sections.description: This section allows the Government to resume or suspend any grants made by it to any local authority, society, or any other organisation if they fail to comply with the provisions of the Act.
This section deals with the punishment for abetting any offense punishable under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to impose collective fine
main_sections.description: This section grants the State Government the power to impose a collective fine on the inhabitants of an area where offenses under this Act have been committed, if it is believed that the inhabitants have been generally, or a particular group of them has been, aware of the commission of such offenses or have facilitated or connived at their commission.
This section provides for enhanced penalties for individuals convicted of an offense under this Act for a second or subsequent time.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption by Courts in certain cases
main_sections.description: This section lays down certain presumptions that courts shall make in specific cases related to offenses under the Act, simplifying the burden of proof for the prosecution.

main_sections.section_title: Limitation of Jurisdiction of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: This section restricts the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters that the Act empowers State Governments or other authorities to decide.

This section addresses the liability of companies for offenses committed under the Act, stating that if an offense is committed by a company, every person who was in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of its business at the time of the offense shall be liable.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: This section provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder, ensuring that no suit, prosecution, or other legal proceeding shall lie against them.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable and triable summarily
main_sections.description: This section declares offenses under the Act to be cognizable and specifies that they shall be triable summarily.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of State Government to ensure that the rights accruing from the abolition of “untouchability” may be availed of by the concerned persons
main_sections.description: This section imposes a duty on the State Government to ensure that persons affected by 'untouchability' can avail themselves of the rights that have accrued to them due to its abolition.
This section states that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, not to apply to persons above the age of fourteen years
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, shall not apply to persons above the age of fourteen years who have committed an offense under this Act.
This section empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
This section repeals the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, and the Hyderabad Scheduled Castes (Legal Disabilities Removal) Act, 1949.

important_rules: No person shall, on the ground of 'untouchability', prevent any person from entering a place of public worship or from worshipping or offering prayers or performing any religious service therein, or bathing in, or using the waters of, any sacred tank, well, spring or watercourse, river or lake or bathing at any ghat of such tank, water-course, river or lake, in the same manner and to the same extent as is permissible to others.

No person shall, on the ground of 'untouchability', enforce any disability regarding access to any shop, public restaurant, hotel or place of public entertainment; the use of any utensils, and other articles kept in any public restaurant, hotel, dharamshala, sarai or musafirkhana for the use of the general public or any section thereof; the practice of any profession or the carrying on of any occupation, trade or business or employment in any job; the use of, or access to, any river, stream, spring, well, tank, cistern, water-tap or other watering place, or any bathing ghat, burial or cremation ground, any sanitary convenience, any road, or passage, or any other place of public resort which other members of the public, or any section thereof, have a right to use or have access to; the use of, or access to, any place used for a charitable or a public purpose maintained wholly or partly out of State funds or dedicated to the use of the general public or any section thereof; the enjoyment of any benefit under a charitable trust created for the benefit of the general public or of any section thereof; the use of, or access to, any public conveyance; the construction, acquisition, or occupation of any residential premises in any locality, whatsoever; the use of any dharamshala, sarai or musafirkhana which is open to the general public, or to any section thereof; the observance of any social or religious custom, usage or ceremony or taking part in, or taking out, any religious, social or cultural procession; the use of jewellery and finery.

No person shall, on the ground of 'untouchability', refuse admission to any person to any hospital, dispensary, educational institution or any hostel if such institution is established or maintained for the benefit of the general public or any section thereof, or do any act which discriminates against any such person after admission.

No person shall, on the ground of 'untouchability', refuse to sell any goods or refuse to render any service to any person at the same time and place and on the same terms and conditions as such goods are sold or services are rendered to other persons in the ordinary course of business.
No person shall, on the ground of 'untouchability', insult or attempt to insult a member of a Scheduled Caste.

Compelling any person, on the ground of 'untouchability', to do any scavenging or sweeping or to remove any carcass or to flay any animal, or to remove the umbilical cord or to do any other job of a similar nature shall be deemed to have enforced a disability arising out of 'untouchability'.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term of not less than one month and not more than six months and also with fine which shall be not less than one hundred rupees and not more than five hundred rupees for offenses under Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7(1)(a) to (d), 7(2), and 7A.

Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than two years and also with fine for offenses committed as a reprisal or revenge for exercising rights accruing from the abolition of 'untouchability' where the original offense is punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding two years (Section 7(1A)).

Imprisonment for a term of not less than three months and not more than six months and also with fine which shall not be less than one hundred rupees and not more than five hundred rupees for unlawful compulsory labour deemed to be a practice of 'untouchability' (Section 7A(2)).
Enhanced penalty on subsequent conviction (Section 11).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Governments and their designated authorities, police, and courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Offenses are cognizable and triable summarily. State Governments have a duty to ensure rights are availed. Provisions for cancellation of licenses, resumption of grants, and imposition of collective fines facilitate enforcement. Courts are empowered to presume guilt in certain cases.

rights: Right to civil rights accruing from the abolition of 'untouchability'.
Right of access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, places of public entertainment.
Right to use any utensils, and other articles kept in public places for general use.
Right to practice any profession, carry on any occupation, trade, or business, or be employed in any job.

Right to use, or access to, rivers, streams, springs, wells, tanks, cisterns, water-taps, watering places, bathing ghats, burial or cremation grounds, sanitary conveniences, roads, passages, and other public resorts.
Right to use, or access to, places maintained for charitable or public purposes.
Right to enjoy benefits under charitable trusts for the general public.
Right to use, or access to, public conveyances.
Right to construct, acquire, or occupy residential premises in any locality.
Right to use dharamshalas, sarai, or musafirkhana open to the general public.
Right to observe social or religious customs, usages, or ceremonies, and to take part in or out any religious, social, or cultural procession.
Right to use jewellery and finery.
Right to access to hospitals, dispensaries, educational institutions, or hostels maintained for the general public.
Right to be free from discrimination on the ground of 'untouchability' in any form.
duties: Duty of every person to not enforce any disability on the ground of 'untouchability'.
Duty of every person to not refuse to sell goods or render services on the ground of 'untouchability'.
Duty of every person to not discriminate against any person on the ground of 'untouchability'.
Duty of State Government to ensure that the rights accruing from the abolition of 'untouchability' are availed of by the concerned persons.
obligations: Obligation to punish those who preach or practice 'untouchability' or enforce disabilities arising from it.
Obligation to ensure that all persons can exercise their civil rights without discrimination.
Obligation to take action against individuals or entities violating the Act through penalties, license cancellations, or suspension of grants.

key_procedures: Reporting of offenses related to 'untouchability' to the police or appropriate authorities.
Investigation of offenses by the police.
Trial of offenses, which are cognizable and triable summarily by courts.
Application of presumptions by courts in certain cases to aid prosecution.
Enforcement of penalties including imprisonment and fines.
Cancellation or suspension of licenses by the State Government.
Resumption or suspension of government grants.
Rules may be made by the State Government for carrying out the Act's purposes, which would outline further procedural aspects.
administration: State Governments, through their designated authorities and police forces, are primarily responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act, with the judiciary handling the trials and penalties. The Central Government appoints the commencement date and can issue notifications.
important_notes: The Act was amended significantly in 1976 (Act 106 of 1976), which introduced several new provisions and modified existing ones, including the inclusion of 'Scheduled Castes', enhanced penalties, and clearer definitions of offenses.

The 'Explanation' to Section 3 defines persons professing Buddhist, Sikh, Jaina, or certain forms of Hindu religions as Hindus for the purposes of that section, indicating the broad interpretation of religious groups covered.

Section 16A makes it clear that the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, does not apply to persons above fourteen years of age convicted under this Act, suggesting a stricter approach to juvenile offenders in cases of 'untouchability'.

title: The Citizenship Act, 1955
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.
scope: Applies to all persons concerning their acquisition, determination, and renunciation of Indian citizenship. Geographically, it covers India and its territories, with provisions extending to persons born or residing outside India.

key_definitions.a_government_in_india: The Central Government or a State Government.
key_definitions.illegal_migrant: A foreigner who has entered India without a valid passport or other travel documents and prescribed authority, or who remains in India beyond the permitted period with valid documents.
key_definitions.indian_consulate: The office of any consular officer of the Government of India where a register of births is kept, or where there is no such office, such office as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.minor: A person who has not attained the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.overseas_citizen_of_india_cardholder: A person registered as an Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder by the Central Government under section 7A.
key_definitions.person: Does not include any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.undivided_india: India as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935, as originally enacted.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Citizenship Act, 1955.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'illegal migrant', 'minor', 'prescribed', and 'undivided India'. It also clarifies the deemed place of birth for persons born on registered or unregistered ships/aircraft and the interpretation of a father's status at the time of a person's birth if the father has died.

Outlines the conditions under which a person born in India acquires citizenship by birth, with different provisions based on the date of birth and the citizenship status of parents. It also specifies exceptions where a person born in India will not be a citizen by birth, such as if parents possess diplomatic immunity or are enemy aliens.

Details how a person born outside India can become a citizen by descent, with variations based on the date of birth and the citizenship status of parents. It includes provisos for registration of birth and conditions related to parents serving under a Government in India or being citizens by descent only. It also addresses minors who are citizens of India by descent and also citizens of another country.

Specifies categories of persons (not being illegal migrants) who can be registered as citizens of India by the Central Government, including persons of Indian origin, spouses of Indian citizens, minor children of Indian citizens, and persons of full age and capacity whose parents are registered citizens. It also includes conditions and explanations regarding ordinary residence and the definition of 'Indian origin'.

Provides for the grant of a certificate of naturalisation by the Central Government to persons of full age and capacity who meet the qualifications specified in the Third Schedule. It allows the Central Government to waive conditions for those who have rendered distinguished service.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions as to citizenship of persons covered by the Assam Accord
main_sections.description: Introduces special provisions concerning citizenship for individuals covered by the Assam Accord.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions as to citizenship of person covered by proviso to clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 2
main_sections.description: Addresses special provisions for the citizenship of persons mentioned in a specific proviso of section 2.
Deals with citizenship of persons in the case of incorporation of territory into India.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder
main_sections.description: Concerns the registration of Overseas Citizen of India Cardholders.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of rights on Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder
main_sections.description: Deals with the rights conferred upon Overseas Citizen of India Cardholders.

main_sections.section_title: Renunciation of Overseas Citizen of India Card
main_sections.description: Covers the renunciation of the Overseas Citizen of India Card.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation of registration as Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder
main_sections.description: Relates to the cancellation of registration as an Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder.
Specifies the procedure and conditions under which an Indian citizen can renounce their citizenship.
Outlines circumstances under which Indian citizenship can be terminated.
Details the grounds and procedure for the Central Government to deprive a person of their Indian citizenship.

main_sections.section_title: Certificate of Citizenship in case of doubt
main_sections.description: Provides for the issuance of a certificate of citizenship by the Central Government in cases of doubt regarding citizenship status.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of application under sections 5, 6 and 7A
main_sections.description: Governs the disposal of applications made under sections related to registration (5), naturalisation (6), and Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder registration (7A).
Concerns the authority and procedure for the issue of national identity cards.
Deals with the power of revision concerning orders made under this Act.
Provides for the review of decisions or orders made under the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act to other authorities.
Specifies offenses related to the contravention of provisions of this Act and prescribes penalties.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: A person born in India on or after January 26, 1950, but before July 1, 1987, is a citizen by birth.
A person born in India on or after July 1, 1987, is a citizen by birth if either parent was an Indian citizen at the time of birth.
A person born outside India on or after January 26, 1950, but before December 10, 1992, is a citizen by descent if the father was an Indian citizen at the time of birth.
A person born outside India on or after December 10, 1992, is a citizen by descent if either parent was an Indian citizen at the time of birth.
Persons of Indian origin can be registered as citizens if they meet specified ordinary residence requirements in India.
Minors can be registered as citizens if their parents are Indian citizens.
An Indian citizen can renounce their citizenship by a declaration in the prescribed form.
Indian citizenship can be terminated, deprived, or renounced under specific conditions outlined in the Act.

penalties: Penalties for offences related to the contravention of provisions of this Act are prescribed under Section 17.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government is the primary authority responsible for enforcing this Act, including making rules, granting citizenship, and taking actions like deprivation of citizenship.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the Central Government's power to grant, deny, or revoke citizenship, make rules, and through the provisions related to offences and their penalties.

rights: Right to acquire Indian citizenship by birth, descent, registration, and naturalisation.
Rights conferred on Overseas Citizen of India Cardholders.
duties: Duty to register birth at an Indian consulate in certain cases of citizenship by descent.
Duty to take the oath of allegiance for naturalisation and registration.
Duty to renounce citizenship of another country if a minor is a citizen of India by descent and also a citizen of another country, upon attaining full age.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the conditions and restrictions prescribed for registration and naturalisation.
Obligation to not be an illegal migrant when applying for registration or naturalisation.

key_procedures: Procedure for acquisition of citizenship by birth, descent, registration, and naturalisation.
Procedure for renunciation of citizenship.
Procedure for termination and deprivation of citizenship.
Procedure for registration of Overseas Citizen of India Cardholders.
Procedure for disposal of applications for citizenship.
administration: The Central Government (specifically, the Ministry of Home Affairs is typically involved in citizenship matters).
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Union territories like Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Goa, Daman and Diu, and Pondicherry.

Amendments to the Act have been made over time, notably by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003, and subsequent amendments, which have altered definitions and eligibility criteria, particularly for 'illegal migrant' and citizenship by birth and descent.

The proviso to section 2(1)(b) clarifies that certain individuals from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, or Pakistan belonging to specific religious communities who entered India on or before December 31, 2014, and received exemption, are not treated as illegal migrants.

title: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956
purpose: To provide for the prevention of immoral traffic in persons, in pursuance of the International Convention signed at New York on the 9th day of May, 1950.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to offenses related to keeping brothels, living on earnings of prostitution, procuring, inducing, detaining, seducing, and soliciting for the purpose of prostitution, and related activities. It also includes provisions for rescue, intermediate custody, protective homes, and the establishment of special courts.

key_definitions.brothel: Includes any house, room, conveyance, or place, or any portion thereof, used for purposes of sexual exploitation or abuse for the gain of another person or for the mutual gain of two or more prostitutes.
key_definitions.child: A person who has not completed the age of sixteen years.
key_definitions.corrective institution: An institution established or licensed under section 21, where persons in need of correction may be detained under this Act, and includes a shelter for undertrials.
key_definitions.magistrate: A magistrate specified as competent to exercise powers conferred by specific sections of the Act.
key_definitions.major: A person who has completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.minor: A person who has completed the age of sixteen years but has not completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prostitution: Sexual exploitation or abuse of persons for commercial purpose. The term 'prostitute' is construed accordingly.
key_definitions.protective home: An institution established or licensed under section 21, where persons in need of care and protection may be kept, and which is equipped with qualified persons and facilities. It excludes shelters for undertrials and corrective institutions.
key_definitions.public place: Any place intended for use by, or accessible to, the public, and includes any public conveyance.
key_definitions.special police officer: A police officer appointed by the State Government to be in charge of police duties within a specified area for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.trafficking police officer: A police officer appointed by the Central Government under sub-section (4) of section 13.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956', its extent to the whole of India, and the commencement dates for its provisions.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'brothel', 'child', 'corrective institution', 'magistrate', 'major', 'minor', 'prescribed', 'prostitution', 'protective home', 'public place', 'special police officer', and 'trafficking police officer'.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for keeping a brothel or allowing premises to be used as a brothel
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for persons who keep, manage, or assist in the management of a brothel, or who use or knowingly allow premises to be used as a brothel, or who let premises with the knowledge of their intended use as a brothel. It also outlines a presumption of knowledge for landlords or owners in certain cases and states that conviction voids lease agreements.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for living on the earnings of prostitution
main_sections.description: Punishes persons over eighteen who knowingly live on the earnings of prostitution of others. It includes a presumption that living with or habitually being in the company of a prostitute, or exercising control over their movements, or acting as a tout/pimp, implies living on such earnings unless proven otherwise. Special provisions are made for earnings related to a child or minor.

main_sections.section_title: Procuring, inducing or taking person for the sake of prostitution
main_sections.description: Defines and punishes offenses related to procuring, inducing, or taking any person for the purpose of prostitution. It includes provisions for increased punishment if the victim is a child or a minor, or if the offense is committed against their will. It also specifies the jurisdiction for trying such offenses.

main_sections.section_title: Detaining a person in premises where prostitution is carried on
main_sections.description: Punishes any person who detains another person in a brothel or in any premises with the intent that such person may have sexual intercourse. It includes provisions for presumption of detention if a child is found in a brothel, or if a child or minor found in a brothel shows signs of sexual abuse. It also defines circumstances that create a presumption of detention for purposes of prostitution.

main_sections.section_title: Prostitution in or in the vicinity of public places
main_sections.description: Punishes any person who engages in prostitution in or in the vicinity of any public place, or solicits any person in or in the vicinity of any public place for the purpose of prostitution.

main_sections.section_title: Seducing or soliciting for purpose of prostitution
main_sections.description: Punishes any person who seduces or solicits any other person for the purpose of prostitution.

main_sections.section_title: Seduction of a person in custody
main_sections.description: Punishes any person who seduces any person in lawful custody.
Provides for the detention of persons in a corrective institution under certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Notification of address of previously convicted offenders
main_sections.description: Requires previously convicted offenders to notify their address to the police.

main_sections.section_title: Special police officer and advisory body
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of special police officers and advisory bodies to assist in the enforcement of the Act.
Declares that offenses under this Act are cognizable, meaning police can arrest without a warrant.
Empowers police officers to search premises without a warrant under certain conditions related to suspected immoral traffic.
Empowers police to rescue persons from brothels or premises used for prostitution.

main_sections.section_title: Intermediate custody of persons removed under section 15 or rescued under section 16
main_sections.description: Provides for the intermediate custody of persons removed or rescued under sections 15 and 16.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions to be observed before placing persons rescued under section 16 to parents or guardians
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions that must be met before rescued persons are placed with their parents or guardians.

main_sections.section_title: Closure of brothel and eviction of offenders from the premises
main_sections.description: Empowers courts to order the closure of brothels and eviction of offenders from the premises.

main_sections.section_title: Application for being kept in a protective home or provided care and protection by court
main_sections.description: Allows individuals to apply to be kept in a protective home or to be provided care and protection by the court.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of prostitute from any place
main_sections.description: Empowers authorities to remove prostitutes from any place under certain circumstances.
Deals with the establishment and management of protective homes.
Specifies the procedure for the trial of offenses under the Act.
Empowers the State Government to establish special courts for the trial of offenses under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to establish special courts
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish special courts for the trial of offenses under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Court to try cases summarily
main_sections.description: Grants courts the power to try cases summarily.
Empowers the Central and State Governments to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to be in derogation of certain other Acts
main_sections.description: Clarifies that this Act does not affect the operation of certain other laws.
Provides for the repeal of any existing laws on the subject and savings.

important_rules: Keeping or managing a brothel is punishable with rigorous imprisonment of not less than one year and not more than three years for a first conviction, and not less than two years and not more than five years for subsequent convictions. Fines are also applicable.

Allowing premises to be used as a brothel, either as a tenant, occupier, or by a landlord who knowingly permits it, is punishable with imprisonment up to two years and a fine for the first conviction, and rigorous imprisonment up to five years for subsequent convictions.

Living on the earnings of prostitution is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or a fine, or both. If the earnings relate to a child or minor, the punishment is rigorous imprisonment for not less than seven and not more than ten years.

Procuring, inducing, or taking a person for prostitution is punishable with rigorous imprisonment of not less than three years and not more than seven years, with increased penalties if the offense is committed against the will of the person, or if the victim is a child or minor.

Detaining a person in a brothel or premises for sexual intercourse is punishable with imprisonment of not less than seven years, potentially for life, or up to ten years. A court may impose a lesser sentence for adequate reasons.
Prostitution or solicitation in or near public places is an offense.
Offenses under this Act are cognizable, allowing for arrest without a warrant.
Police officers have the power to search premises without a warrant under specific circumstances and to rescue persons from brothels.
Conviction for using premises as a brothel voids any lease or agreement for those premises.
Previously convicted offenders must notify their address to the police.

penalties: Keeping a brothel: Rigorous imprisonment of 1-3 years (first conviction), 2-5 years (subsequent conviction), and fine.
Allowing premises to be used as a brothel: Imprisonment up to 2 years and fine (first conviction), rigorous imprisonment up to 5 years and fine (subsequent conviction).
Living on earnings of prostitution: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine, or both. For earnings from a child/minor: Imprisonment of 7-10 years.

Procuring/Inducing/Taking for prostitution: Rigorous imprisonment of 3-7 years, with extended terms for offenses against the will of the victim or involving a child/minor (life imprisonment for child, 7-14 years for minor).
Detaining in a brothel/premises for prostitution: Imprisonment of not less than 7 years, potentially life, or up to 10 years, with a possibility of a lesser sentence for special reasons.
Fines are generally applicable for various offenses.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Special Police Officers, Trafficking Police Officers, and other police officers as authorized under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation, search without warrant, rescue of persons, arrest, prosecution, trial in courts (including special courts), and enforcement of sentences and orders (like closure of brothels and eviction).

rights: Right to be rescued from situations of immoral traffic.
Right to be placed in protective homes or provided care and protection by the court.
Right of individuals to apply for placement in a protective home or to receive care and protection.
Right to legal proceedings according to the Act's provisions.
duties: Duty of persons to not engage in keeping or managing brothels.
Duty of persons to not live on the earnings of prostitution.
Duty of persons to not procure, induce, or take others for prostitution.
Duty of persons to not detain others in premises for prostitution.
Duty of persons to not solicit or engage in prostitution in or near public places.
Duty of previously convicted offenders to notify their address.
obligations: Obligation of owners, lessors, or landlords not to knowingly let premises for brothel purposes.
Obligation of authorities to appoint special police officers and advisory bodies.
Obligation of courts to try cases and issue orders for closure, eviction, and placement in protective homes.
Obligation of government to establish and maintain protective homes and corrective institutions.
Obligation of individuals to comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules or orders made thereunder.

key_procedures: Search of premises for suspected immoral traffic offenses, potentially without a warrant.
Rescue of persons found in brothels or involved in prostitution.
Arrangement of intermediate custody for rescued or removed persons.
Placement of rescued persons with parents/guardians after observing specific conditions.
Application by individuals for admission into protective homes or to receive court-provided care.
Trial of offenses by courts, with provisions for summary trials and special courts.
Establishment and operation of protective homes and corrective institutions.
Application of rules made by the Central and State Governments for the implementation of the Act.
administration: The Act is administered by the Central Government and State Governments, who are empowered to make rules, appoint special police officers, establish special courts, and set up protective homes and corrective institutions.
important_notes: The Act is based on an International Convention for the prevention of immoral traffic.
The Act has been extended to various Union Territories.
Amendments have been made to the Act over time, notably in 1978 and 1986, to strengthen its provisions and broaden its scope, including the definition of prostitution and penalties.
There are presumptions of guilt for certain offenses if specific conditions are met (e.g., knowing allowance of premises for prostitution, living on earnings, detention).

title: THE WOMEN’S AND CHILDREN’S INSTITUTIONS (LICENSING) ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the licensing of institutions for women and children and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It applies to institutions established and maintained for the reception, care, protection, and welfare of women or children. The Act comes into force in a State on a date appointed by the State Government.

key_definitions.child: A boy or girl who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.institution: An institution established and maintained for the reception, care, protection and welfare of women or children.
key_definitions.licensing_authority: The State Government or such officer or authority as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made by the State Government under this Act.
key_definitions.woman: A female who has completed the age of eighteen years.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir), and the commencement date, which is to be appointed by the State Government.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'child', 'institution', 'licensing authority', 'prescribed', and 'woman'.
Prohibits the establishment or maintenance of an institution without a licence granted under the Act after its commencement.

Requires any person desiring to establish an institution to apply to the licensing authority in the prescribed form and with prescribed particulars. A grace period of three months is provided for institutions existing at the commencement of the Act to apply for a licence.

Outlines the process for granting licences. The licensing authority may grant or refuse a licence after inquiry. Grounds for refusal must be communicated. Licences have a specified duration, can be renewed, and are subject to prescribed conditions, which may include entrusting management to women. No fee is charged for a licence.
States that a licence granted under the Act is not transferable.

Allows the licensing authority to revoke a licence if conditions are breached, or if the authority is not satisfied with the institution's condition, management, or superintendence. An opportunity to show cause must be given before revocation. Revocation means the institution ceases to function, with specific provisions for appeals. The licensing authority can direct the transfer of inmates to their guardians or other institutions.

Provides for appeals to the State Government against orders of refusal or revocation of a licence by a licensing authority (other than the State Government). The State Government's order on appeal is final.
Prescribes punishment for contravening the Act, rules, or licence conditions, which may include imprisonment up to three months, a fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain institutions
main_sections.description: Exempts hostels/boarding houses attached to educational institutions and protective homes established under the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956, from the provisions of this Act.

Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including rules for application forms, licence conditions, management, care of inmates, inspection, registers, returns, discharge and transfer of inmates, appeals, and service of orders.

Repeals any corresponding State Act upon the commencement of this Act in that State. It also includes savings provisions, deeming actions taken under the repealed State Act as valid under this Act if not inconsistent.

important_rules: No person shall establish or maintain an institution for women or children without a licence granted under this Act.
Institutions existing at the commencement of the Act must apply for a licence within three months.
Licences are subject to conditions prescribed by the State Government, which may include entrusting management to women.
A licence must be renewed before its expiration.
Breach of licence conditions or provisions of the Act can lead to licence revocation.
Inmates of a revoked institution may be restored to their guardians or transferred to another institution.
Appeals against licensing authority decisions lie with the State Government.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months
Fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees
Both imprisonment and fine
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing authority (State Government or prescribed officer/authority), and the State Government for appeals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the licensing and revocation process, inspection (as prescribed by rules), and penalties for contravention of the Act or its rules.

rights: Right to apply for a licence to establish or maintain an institution.
Right to be informed of the grounds for licence refusal.
Right to show cause against licence revocation.
Right to appeal against licence refusal or revocation.
Right to have an institution managed by women, wherever practicable (as a condition of licence).
duties: Duty to obtain a licence before establishing or maintaining an institution.
Duty to comply with the conditions of the licence.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
Duty to cooperate with inquiries by the licensing authority.
Duty to manage the institution satisfactorily to avoid revocation.
obligations: Obligation to apply for a licence within three months if an institution is existing at the commencement of the Act.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for application, renewal, and appeals.
Obligation to ensure the care, protection, and welfare of women and children in the institution as per rules.

key_procedures: Application for a licence: A person desiring to establish an institution must apply to the licensing authority in the prescribed form and with prescribed particulars. Institutions existing at commencement have a three-month window to apply.
Grant or refusal of a licence: The licensing authority makes an inquiry and grants or refuses the licence in writing. Grounds for refusal must be communicated.
Licence renewal: An application for renewal must be made sixty days before expiry. Renewal may be permitted after expiry if sufficient cause is shown.

Revocation of a licence: If conditions are breached or the institution's management is unsatisfactory, the licensing authority can revoke the licence after providing an opportunity to show cause. An appeal against revocation is possible.
Appeal process: A person aggrieved by a licensing authority's order can appeal to the State Government within a prescribed period. The State Government's decision is final.
administration: The State Government, either directly or through a prescribed officer or authority (licensing authority), is responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act. The State Government also has the power to make rules.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to hostels or boarding houses attached to, or controlled or recognized by, educational institutions.
The Act does not apply to any protective home established under the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956.
Licences have a specified period of validity and are subject to renewal.
No fee is charged for the grant of a licence.

title: The Lok Sahayak Sena Act, 1956
purpose: To provide for the constitution of Lok Sahayak Sena for imparting military training to citizens of India.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to citizens of India between the ages of eighteen and forty years who offer themselves for enrolment as volunteers in the Lok Sahayak Sena.

key_definitions.camp: Any place established under section 4 as a camp where any body of volunteers is for the time being undergoing training.
key_definitions.Force: The Lok Sahayak Sena constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.superior_officer: Any officer, junior commissioned officer, warrant officer or non-commissioned officer of the regular Army or of the Territorial Army.
key_definitions.volunteer: A person enrolled in the Force under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Lok Sahayak Sena Act, 1956, and states that it extends to the whole of India.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'camp', 'Force', 'prescribed', 'superior officer', and 'volunteer'. It also states that undefined terms used in the Act shall have the meanings assigned to them in the Army Act, 1950, or the Territorial Army Act, 1948.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Lok Sahayak Sena
main_sections.description: Establishes the Lok Sahayak Sena to be raised and maintained by the Central Government through the enrolment of volunteers.
Empowers the Central Government to establish, close down, or re-establish camps for the purposes of the Force.

Outlines the eligibility criteria for enrolment as a volunteer (citizens of India, aged 18-40) and the process of enrolment by a prescribed authority under prescribed conditions and for a prescribed period.

Clarifies that volunteers are not liable for military service solely on the ground of being a volunteer, but they may be called upon to undergo prescribed training and perform duties and discharge obligations as directed by the prescribed authority.
States that volunteers are entitled to discharge upon the expiration of their enrolment period but can also be discharged earlier by a prescribed authority under prescribed conditions.

Details offences committed by volunteers, such as failing to attend when required, being absent without leave, using criminal force or insubordinate language to a superior officer, disobeying lawful commands, neglecting orders, using criminal force to other volunteers or persons subject to the Army/Territorial Army Acts, or acts prejudicial to good order and discipline. Penalties include a fine up to fifty rupees or confinement to barracks for up to seven days. It also outlines the procedure for recovering fines.

main_sections.section_title: Liability for causing loss of, or damage to, Government property
main_sections.description: Makes volunteers liable for wilfully or negligently causing loss or damage to Government property. The prescribed authority can order the volunteer to make good the loss, and if not paid, it can be recovered as an arrear of land revenue.

States that a certificate signed by a prescribed officer indicating a volunteer's failure to attend as required is evidence of such failure, without requiring proof of the officer's signature or appointment.

Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering matters like enrolment, training, discipline, duties, discharge, calling out for training, determination of authorities, signing of certificates, and any other prescribed matters. It also includes a provision for laying rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.

important_rules: Volunteers are not liable for military service solely by virtue of being a volunteer.
Volunteers may be required to undergo prescribed training and perform duties as directed by the prescribed authority.
Volunteers causing willful or negligent loss or damage to Government property are liable to make good the loss.
Failure to attend a required place without sufficient cause is an offence.
Absence from camp without leave while in camp on duty is an offence.
Using criminal force or insubordinate language towards a superior officer is an offence.
Disobeying lawful commands of a superior officer is an offence.
Neglecting to obey orders from the officer commanding the camp is an offence.
Using criminal force to or assaulting any other volunteer or person subject to Army/Territorial Army Acts is an offence.
Committing acts prejudicial to good order or military discipline in camp is an offence.

penalties: Summary punishment by the prescribed authority with a fine of up to fifty rupees or, in default, confinement to barracks for up to seven days for certain offences.
Recovery of fines imposed by the prescribed authority as if imposed by a magistrate.
Requirement to make good loss or damage to Government property, with recovery as an arrear of land revenue if not paid.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The prescribed authority (as defined by rules made under the Act). Fines can also be recovered through a magistrate, and loss/damage to Government property can be recovered through the Collector of the district.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Summary punishment for offences, recovery of fines through magistrates, and recovery of damages for Government property as land revenue arrears. Certificates of non-attendance are considered evidence.

rights: Right to receive discharge from the Force on the expiration of the enrolment period.
Right to be heard before an order is made requiring them to make good loss or damage to Government property.
duties: To undergo prescribed training.
To perform such duties and discharge such obligations as directed by the prescribed authority while undergoing training.
To attend at any place when duly required.
To maintain good order and military discipline in camp.
obligations: To make good loss or damage to Government property caused by wilful or negligent action.

key_procedures: Enrolment process for eligible citizens by a prescribed authority under prescribed conditions and for a prescribed period.
Discharge process, either upon expiry of the enrolment period or earlier by a prescribed authority.
Procedure for dealing with offences: summary punishment by the prescribed authority, with provision for fine or confinement.
Procedure for recovery of fines through the magistrate.

Procedure for recovery of damages to Government property, involving an opportunity to be heard, determination of the amount by the prescribed authority, and subsequent recovery as land revenue arrears if not paid.
Process for making and laying rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for the constitution and establishment of camps for the Lok Sahayak Sena. The Central Government also has the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
important_notes: The Act refers to the Army Act, 1950 (46 of 1950), and the Territorial Army Act, 1948 (56 of 1948) for definitions of certain terms.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modification or annulment by both Houses of Parliament.
The prescribed authority plays a significant role in the administration and enforcement of various provisions of the Act.

title: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956
purpose: To provide for an increase in the number of Judges of the Supreme Court, excluding the Chief Justice.
scope: Applies to the Supreme Court of India and its Judges.

main_sections.description: This act may be called the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956.

main_sections.section_title: Maximum number of Supreme Court Judges other than Chief Justice
main_sections.description: The maximum number of Judges of the Supreme Court, excluding the Chief Justice of India, shall be thirty-three.

important_rules: The maximum number of Supreme Court Judges, excluding the Chief Justice, is set at thirty-three.
The number of Judges was increased from a previous number (subs. by Act 37 of 2019, s. 2, for “thirty” (w.e.f. 09-08-2019)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Parliament (by enacting the law)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendment to the Act.

rights: The right of the Supreme Court to have a specified maximum number of judges.
duties: The duty of Parliament to legislate on the number of judges.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 2 by Parliament to increase the number of judges.
administration: Supreme Court of India
important_notes: The number of judges was increased to thirty-three by Act 37 of 2019, with effect from 09-08-2019.
The original enactment was in 1956.

title: THE KHADI AND VILLAGE INDUSTRIES COMMISSION ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Commission for the development of Khadi and Village Industries and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as of the original enactment, though later extended). It applies to industries located in rural areas and to the development of Khadi and Village Industries.

key_definitions.Commission: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission established under section 4.
key_definitions.fixed_capital_investment: Includes investment in plant and machinery and land and building of an industry.
key_definitions.khadi: Any cloth woven on handlooms in India from cotton, silk or woolen yarn handspun in India or from a mixture of any two or all of such yarns.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Commission.
key_definitions.rural_area: The area comprised in any village, and includes the area comprised in any town, the population of which does not exceed twenty thousand or such other figure as the Central Government may specify from time to time.
key_definitions.village_industry: Any industry located in a rural area which produces any goods or renders any service with or without the use of power and in which the fixed capital investment per head of an artisan or a worker does not exceed one lakh rupees (or as specified by Central Government); it also includes any other non-manufacturing unit established for the sole purpose of promoting, maintaining, assisting, servicing, or managing any village industry.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial applicability.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Commission', 'Khadi', 'Village Industry', 'rural area', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and constitution of the Commission
main_sections.description: Establishes the Khadi and Village Industries Commission as a body corporate and outlines its composition, which includes non-official members with specialized knowledge, members from specific disciplines, the Chairman of the State Bank of India (ex-officio), a Chief Executive Officer (ex-officio), and a Financial Adviser (ex-officio).
Details the various powers and functions of the Commission, likely related to the development, promotion, and support of Khadi and Village Industries.
Specifies the requirements for maintaining accounts by the Commission and the audit of these accounts.

important_rules: Rule (derived from definitions): A 'village industry' is one located in a rural area with specified limits on fixed capital investment per worker.

Rule (derived from Section 4(2)(a)): The Commission includes six non-official members representing six geographical zones of the country, with specialized knowledge and experience in khadi or village industries.

Rule (derived from Section 6): Individuals are disqualified from being members of the Commission if they are of unsound mind, adjudged insolvent, convicted of an offense involving moral turpitude, or have certain financial interests in contracts or businesses related to the Commission.

rights: The Commission has the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract.
Persons associated with the Commission for specific purposes have the right to participate in discussions relevant to those purposes but not to vote.
duties: The Chief Executive Officer has the duty to place matters of financial import before the Commission for consideration if suggested by the Financial Adviser.
The Financial Adviser has the duty to bring matters of financial import to the notice of the Commission through the Chief Executive Officer.
obligations: Members of the Commission must not have disqualifying financial interests.
Members removed from the Commission must be given an opportunity to show cause against removal.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Commission: The Central Government fixes a date, by notification, for the establishment of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.

Appointment of Members: The Central Government appoints members to the Commission, including the Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, and Financial Adviser, with specified qualifications and representation.
Removal of Members: The Central Government may remove a member by notification, after providing an opportunity to show cause.
administration: The Central Government and the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.
important_notes: The definition of 'rural area' and 'village industry' can be modified by the Central Government through notification.
A proviso exists to continue certain industries as village industries even if located outside a rural area, if recognized before a certain amendment act.
For industries located in hilly areas, the fixed capital investment limit for village industries is higher.
The Act was later extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

title: THE JAMMU AND KASHMIR (EXTENSION OF LAWS) ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the extension of certain laws to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It extends certain listed Acts and Ordinances to the state and makes amendments to them. As per a notification in 2019, it is also applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Jammu and Kashmir (Extension of Laws) Act, 1956, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Extension and amendment of certain laws
main_sections.description: Extends the Acts and Ordinances mentioned in the Schedule, along with their rules, orders, and regulations, to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It also specifies that these laws will be amended as indicated in the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir
main_sections.description: Provides that any reference in the extended Acts or Ordinances to a law not in force in Jammu and Kashmir shall be construed as a reference to the corresponding law, if any, in force in that State.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to authorities where new authorities have been constituted
main_sections.description: States that any reference in any law in force in Jammu and Kashmir to an authority competent at the time of passing that law, shall, where a corresponding new authority has been constituted by or under any law extended to the state, be treated as a reference to the new authority.

Specifies that any law in force in Jammu and Kashmir that corresponds to an Act or Ordinance extended by this Act shall stand repealed upon the commencement of this Act. It includes provisos that save previous operations, rights, liabilities, penalties, and legal proceedings under the repealed laws, and validates things done or actions taken under repealed laws as if done under the corresponding extended provisions.

Grants the Central Government the power to issue orders, notified in the Official Gazette, to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of any Act or Ordinance extended to Jammu and Kashmir. Such orders can, among other things, specify corresponding authorities, transfer pending matters, and recognize actions taken under repealed laws.

important_rules: Rule: The Acts and Ordinances listed in the Schedule are extended to Jammu and Kashmir and will be in force there.
Rule: The listed Acts and Ordinances will be amended as specified in the Schedule.
Rule: References to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir will be construed as references to corresponding local laws.
Rule: References to authorities will be treated as references to new authorities if they have been constituted under extended laws.
Rule: Existing corresponding laws in Jammu and Kashmir will be repealed, but past actions, rights, and liabilities will be preserved.
Rule: The Central Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the extended laws.

penalties: Penalties incurred under any law repealed by this Act are preserved and may be imposed as if the Act had not been passed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for removing difficulties and appointing commencement date), and authorities under the extended Acts and Ordinances.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the extended Acts and Ordinances and any rules, orders, or regulations made thereunder. The Central Government may also issue orders to remove difficulties.

rights: Rights, privileges, obligations, or liabilities acquired, accrued, or incurred under any law repealed by this Act are saved.
obligations: Obligations incurred under any law repealed by this Act are saved.

key_procedures: Procedure: The Central Government may appoint a commencement date via notification in the Official Gazette.

Procedure: In case of difficulties, the Central Government may issue orders to remove them, which may involve specifying authorities, transferring pending matters, or recognizing actions taken under repealed laws.
administration: Central Government (for appointing commencement date and removing difficulties), and relevant authorities under the extended Acts and Ordinances.
important_notes: Note: The Act came into force on 1st November, 1956.
Note: As of October 30, 2019, the Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
Note: Section 5 provides comprehensive savings for previous operations, rights, liabilities, penalties, and legal proceedings under repealed laws, ensuring continuity where necessary.
Note: Section 6 empowers the Central Government to issue orders for removing difficulties, indicating a mechanism for adapting the extended laws to local conditions.

title: The Central Sales Tax Act, 1956
purpose: To formulate principles for determining when a sale or purchase of goods takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce or outside a State or in the course of import into or export from India, to provide for the levy, collection and distribution of taxes on sales of goods in the course of inter-State trade or commerce and to declare certain goods to be of special importance in inter-State trade or commerce and specify the restrictions and conditions to which State laws imposing taxes on the sale or purchase of such goods of special importance shall be subject.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to dealers (persons carrying on the business of buying, selling, supplying or distributing goods) and governs sales and purchases of goods that occur in the course of inter-State trade or commerce, outside a State, or in the course of import or export. Certain specific goods are also declared of special importance.

key_definitions.appropriate State: In relation to a dealer, it's the State where the dealer has one or more places of business, or if they have places in different States, then each such State with respect to its territory.
key_definitions.business: Includes any trade, commerce, manufacture, or adventure/concern in the nature of trade, commerce, or manufacture, whether profit-motivated or not, and any transaction connected or incidental to it.
key_definitions.crossing the customs frontiers of India: Means crossing the limits of the area of a customs station where imported goods or export goods are kept before clearance by customs authorities.
key_definitions.dealer: Any person who carries on the business of buying, selling, supplying, or distributing goods, directly or indirectly, for cash, deferred payment, or for commission, remuneration, or other valuable consideration. It includes various entities like local authorities, companies, cooperative societies, firms, HUFs, associations of persons, agents, and auctioneers. Explanation 1 clarifies that agents of out-of-State dealers and branches/offices of out-of-State firms/companies are also considered dealers.
key_definitions.goods: Includes petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor spirit (petrol), natural gas, aviation turbine fuel, and alcoholic liquor for human consumption.
key_definitions.place of business: Includes the place of business of an agent, a warehouse/godown where goods are stored, and a place where books of account are kept.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered dealer: A dealer who is registered under section 7.
key_definitions.sale: Means any transfer of property in goods by one person to another for cash or deferred payment or for any other valuable consideration. It includes transfers not in pursuance of a contract, transfers involved in works contracts, hire-purchase, transfer of right to use goods, supply to a member by an unincorporated association, and supply of food/drink. It does not include mortgage, hypothecation, charge, or pledge on goods.
key_definitions.sale price: The amount payable to a dealer for the sale of goods, less cash discount, but inclusive of sums charged for anything done by the dealer before delivery, excluding freight/delivery/installation costs if separately charged. For works contracts, sale price is determined in the prescribed manner.
key_definitions.sales tax law: Any law in force in any State providing for the levy of taxes on sale or purchase of goods generally or on specified goods.
key_definitions.turnover: The aggregate of sale prices received and receivable by a dealer liable to tax under this Act in respect of inter-State sales during a prescribed period, determined as per the Act and rules.
key_definitions.works contract: A contract for carrying out any work including assembling, construction, building, altering, manufacturing, processing, fabrication, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, repair, or commissioning of any movable or immovable property.
key_definitions.year: The year applicable to a dealer under the general sales tax law of the appropriate State, or the financial year if no such year is applicable.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India, formerly excluding Jammu and Kashmir), and the procedure for commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'appropriate State', 'business', 'dealer', 'goods', 'place of business', 'prescribed', 'registered dealer', 'sale', 'sale price', 'sales tax law', 'turnover', 'works contract', and 'year'.

main_sections.section_title: When is a sale or purchase of goods said to take place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce
main_sections.description: Lays down the principles for determining if a sale or purchase occurs in inter-State trade or commerce. This happens if the sale/purchase occasions the movement of goods from one State to another, or is effected by a transfer of title documents during such movement.

main_sections.section_title: When is a sale or purchase of goods said to take place outside a State
main_sections.description: Specifies the conditions under which a sale or purchase is deemed to take place outside a State, subject to the provisions of section 3.

main_sections.section_title: When is a sale or purchase of goods said to take place in the course of import or export
main_sections.description: Defines when a sale or purchase of goods is considered to be in the course of import into or export from India.

main_sections.section_title: Liability to tax on inter-State sales
main_sections.description: Establishes the liability of a dealer to pay tax on sales in the course of inter-State trade or commerce.
Provides for the requirement of dealers to register under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rates of tax on sales in the course of inter-State trade or commerce
main_sections.description: Specifies the rates of tax applicable to inter-State sales.

main_sections.section_title: Levy and collection of tax and penalties
main_sections.description: Deals with the imposition, levy, and collection of tax and penalties under the Act.
Outlines the penalties that can be imposed for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Addresses the tax liability of a company that is being liquidated.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of directors of private company in liquidation
main_sections.description: Specifies the liability of directors of a private company in liquidation for the company's tax dues.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals to highest appellate authority of State
main_sections.description: Provides for the mechanism of appeals to the highest appellate authority within a State.
Establishes the Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority to settle disputes in inter-State trade or commerce.
Details the process and grounds for filing appeals to the Appellate Authority.

important_rules: A sale or purchase is in the course of inter-State trade or commerce if it occasions the movement of goods from one State to another or is effected by a transfer of title documents during such movement (Section 3).
The Act specifies definitions for key terms like 'dealer', 'goods', 'sale', and 'turnover' to ensure clarity in application.
Dealers engaged in inter-State trade or commerce must register under section 7.
Rates of tax on inter-State sales are prescribed under section 8.
The Act provides for the levy, collection, and imposition of penalties on inter-State sales.
Provisions exist for companies in liquidation and the liability of their directors regarding taxes.
Appeals against orders can be made to the highest appellate authority of the State (Section 18A) and further to the Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority (Section 19 onwards).

penalties: Penalties are imposable for contravention of the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder, as detailed in Section 10 and Section 10A (imposition of penalty in lieu of prosecution).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforcement is primarily carried out by the State tax authorities, with oversight and appellate mechanisms provided by the Central Sales Tax Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the assessment of tax liability, collection of tax, and imposition of penalties for non-compliance. Procedures for appeals and dispute resolution are also established.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment orders to higher authorities.
Right to have sale price determined in accordance with prescribed rules, especially in works contracts.
Right to benefit from cash discounts allowed in trade practices when calculating sale price.
duties: Duty of dealers to register under the Act if liable.
Duty of dealers to pay taxes on inter-State sales as per the Act.
Duty of dealers to maintain proper accounts and furnish returns.
Duty to comply with the provisions related to the levy, collection, and assessment of tax.
Duty to adhere to the principles for determining inter-State sales, sales outside a State, and sales in the course of import/export.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax at prescribed rates on inter-State sales.
Obligation to follow procedures for determining turnover and sale price.
Obligation to comply with orders passed by tax authorities and appellate bodies.
Obligation for companies in liquidation and their directors to settle outstanding tax liabilities.

key_procedures: Determination of when a sale or purchase takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce (Section 3), outside a State (Section 4), or in the course of import/export (Section 5).
Registration of dealers (Section 7).
Levy, collection, and assessment of tax and penalties (Section 9).
Appeals to the highest appellate authority of the State (Section 18A).
Appeals and procedures before the Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority (Sections 20-23).
Determination of turnover for tax purposes (Section 8A and Section 2(j)).
administration: While the Act is 'Central', its administration and collection of taxes are largely handled by the respective State governments. The Central Government plays a role in framing rules and establishing appellate authorities.
important_notes: The Act was extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, and certain districts of Nagaland with modifications.
The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' were omitted from the extent clause by Act 5 of 1958.
Different dates were appointed for the commencement of various provisions of the Act.
Sections 14 and 15 related to 'Goods of Special Importance' were omitted.

title: The Copyright Act, 1957
purpose: To amend and consolidate the law relating to copyright in India.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It governs copyright in various types of works including literary, dramatic, musical, artistic works, cinematograph films, and sound recordings. It applies to authors, owners of copyright, performers, broadcasting organizations, and the public in relation to copyright matters.

key_definitions.adaptation: Includes conversion of a dramatic work into a non-dramatic work, literary or artistic work into a dramatic work, abridgement or version of a literary or dramatic work conveyed by pictures, arrangement or transcription of a musical work, and any rearrangement or alteration of a work.
key_definitions.cinematograph film: Means any work of visual recording including a sound recording accompanying such visual recording, and includes video films.
key_definitions.infringing copy: A reproduction of a work (literary, dramatic, musical, artistic, cinematograph film, sound recording) made or imported in contravention of the Act.
key_definitions.literary work: Includes computer programmes, tables and compilations including computer databases.
key_definitions.musical work: Means a work consisting of music and includes any graphical notation of such work but does not include any words or any action intended to be sung, spoken or performed with the music.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as adaptation, Appellate Board, artistic work, author, broadcast, cinematograph film, communication to the public, dramatic work, engravings, exclusive licence, Government work, Indian work, infringing copy, lecture, literary work, musical work, performance, performer, and photograph.
Specifies the classes of works in which copyright subsists, including original literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works, cinematograph films, and sound recordings.

Defines copyright in relation to different classes of works, granting exclusive rights to the owner such as the right to reproduce the work, to issue copies, to perform the work in public, to make adaptations, etc.

Deals with when copyright is infringed, including doing any of the acts restricted by copyright without permission, and permitting a place for public performance for profit where such performance constitutes an infringement.

main_sections.section_title: Offences of infringement of copyright or other rights conferred by this Act
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for infringement of copyright or other rights conferred by the Act.

important_rules: Copyright subsists in original literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works, cinematograph films, and sound recordings (Section 13).
Copyright includes exclusive rights to do certain acts in respect of the work, such as reproduction, issuance of copies, public performance, etc. (Section 14).
First owner of copyright is generally the author, except in specific cases like works made for hire or commissioned artistic works (Section 17).
Copyright can be assigned, but the assignment must be in writing and signed by the assignor (Section 19).
Copyright infringement occurs when a person does any act restricted by copyright without the owner's permission (Section 51).
Importation of infringing copies is prohibited (Section 53).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees.
Enhanced penalty on second and subsequent convictions (Section 63A).
Penalty for knowing use of infringing copy of a computer programme (Section 63B).
Penalty for possession of plates for making infringing copies (Section 65).
Penalty for making false entries in the register (Section 67).
Penalty for contravention of Section 52A (Particulars to be included in records and video Films) (Section 68A).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers have the power to seize infringing copies (Section 64). The Act also provides for civil remedies through courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through civil remedies such as injunctions, damages, and accounts of profits, as well as criminal proceedings leading to fines and imprisonment.

rights: The exclusive rights of the copyright owner, including reproduction, distribution, adaptation, public performance, and communication to the public (Section 14).

Author's special rights, including the right to claim authorship and the right to restrain or claim damages for distortion, mutilation, modification, or other acts prejudicially affecting the work (Section 57).
Performer's rights, including the right to an equitable remuneration for the exploitation of their performance (Section 38).
Broadcast reproduction right for broadcasting organizations (Section 37).
