duties: Owners of copyright have a duty to register their copyright for certain benefits and to maintain records.
Users of copyrighted material have a duty to obtain licenses or permissions where required.
obligations: The Act imposes obligations on individuals and entities dealing with copyrighted works to respect the rights of copyright holders.
Copyright societies have obligations to administer rights of owners and submit returns and reports (Section 36).

key_procedures: Registration of Copyright: Involves applying to the Registrar of Copyrights with the prescribed particulars, after which entries are made in the Register of Copyrights (Sections 44-45).
Assignment of Copyright: Requires a written agreement signed by the assignor (Section 19).
Seeking Civil Remedies: Copyright holders can file suits in courts for infringement, seeking injunctions, damages, etc. (Chapter XII).
Criminal Proceedings: For offences related to infringement, police can seize infringing copies, and offenders can be prosecuted (Chapter XIII).
Appeals: Appeals against orders of the Registrar of Copyrights and the Appellate Board can be filed (Chapter XIV).
administration: The administration of the Copyright Act primarily involves the Copyright Office and the Registrar of Copyrights. The Appellate Board (Section 11) also plays a crucial role in hearing appeals. Various departments under the Central Government may also be involved in policy-making and enforcement.
important_notes: Certain acts are not considered infringements of copyright, such as fair dealing for research, private study, criticism, review, or reporting current events (Section 52).
The Act makes special provisions for copyright in designs registered or capable of being registered under the Designs Act, 2000 (Section 15).

The Act also addresses international copyright, providing for the extension of copyright to foreign works and the application of its provisions to works of foreign authors and organizations (Chapter IX).

title: THE COAL BEARING AREAS (ACQUISITION AND DEVELOPMENT) ACT, 1957
purpose: To establish greater public control over the coal mining industry in the economic interest of India by providing for the acquisition by the State of unworked land containing or likely to contain coal deposits or of rights in or over such land, for the extinguishment or modification of such rights, and for related matters.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, except for the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as of the original enactment, but later extended). It applies to land containing or likely to contain coal deposits and rights related to such land. It also covers prospecting licences and mining leases concerning coal. The scope is primarily focused on acquiring land and rights for coal prospecting and mining operations under Central Government control.

key_definitions.competent authority: Any person appointed to be a competent authority under section 3.
key_definitions.Government company: A Government company as defined in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956, in which any land or rights in or over land shall have vested under section 11.
key_definitions.Mineral Concession Rules: The rules for the time being in force made under the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948.
key_definitions.person interested: Includes all persons claiming an interest in compensation to be made on account of the acquisition of land, or of the acquisition, extinguishment or modification of any rights in or over land, under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent (initially excluding Jammu and Kashmir, but later extended), and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'competent authority', 'Government company', 'Mineral Concession Rules', 'mining lease', 'person interested', 'prescribed', and 'Tribunal'.
Empowers the Central Government to appoint one or more competent authorities for the purposes of the Act, with the possibility of appointing different authorities for different provisions or areas.

main_sections.section_title: Preliminary notification respecting intention to prospect for coal in any area and powers of competent authorities thereupon
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to issue a notification of its intention to prospect for coal in a locality, and grants powers to the competent authority to enter, survey, bore, and mark land for prospecting. It excludes areas where coal mining operations are already in progress or premises used for ancillary processes.

main_sections.section_title: Power to acquire land or rights in or over land notified under section 4
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to acquire land or rights in or over land notified under section 4, within a specified time limit. If acquisition notice is not given within the allowed period, the section 4 notification ceases to have effect.

Provides a mechanism for any person interested in the land to object to the acquisition within thirty days of the notification under section 7. It specifies that the objection cannot be based on a desire to undertake mining operations personally. The competent authority hears objections and makes recommendations to the Central Government.

When the Central Government is satisfied after considering objections, it can make a declaration of acquisition. This declaration is published in the Official Gazette and specifies the land or rights to be acquired. Special provisions exist for cases where the land belongs to a State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting of land or rights in Central Government
main_sections.description: Upon publication of the declaration, the acquired land or rights vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances. If mining lease rights are acquired, the Central Government is deemed to be the lessee.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of land or rights in a Government company
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct that acquired land or rights shall vest in a Government company instead of the Central Government itself, provided the company agrees to comply with specified terms and conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for prospecting licences ceasing to have effect, rights under mining leases being acquired, etc.
main_sections.description: Deals with the compensation to be paid for prospecting licenses ceasing to have effect and for the acquisition of rights under mining leases.
Specifies the method for determining the compensation to be paid for acquired land or rights. It establishes a Tribunal for this purpose.
Outlines the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: A preliminary notification must be issued before prospecting for coal in any area, giving a brief description and approximate area of the land. (Section 4(2))

Rule: On issuing a prospecting notification, the competent authority and its workmen can enter, survey, bore, and mark land for prospecting, with a proviso to give notice before entering enclosed areas attached to dwelling houses. (Section 4(3))
Rule: Notifications under section 4 must exclude land where coal mining operations are actively being carried on or premises for ancillary processes. (Section 4(4))
Rule: Upon a prospecting notification, prospecting licenses and mining leases authorizing operations in the land cease to have effect. (Section 5)
Rule: Compensation must be paid or tendered for necessary damage caused during prospecting activities, with disputes referred to the Central Government. (Section 6)
Rule: Objections to acquisition must be submitted in writing within thirty days of the acquisition notification, and the objector must be given an opportunity to be heard. (Section 8(1), 8(2))
Rule: Acquired land or rights vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances. (Section 10(1))
Rule: The Central Government can direct that acquired land or rights vest in a Government company. (Section 11(1))

penalties: Penalties for contravening any provision of the Act or rules made thereunder. Specific details of penalties are outlined in Section 23.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the appointed 'competent authority'.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders, appointments of authorities, acquisition proceedings, public gazette publication, and legal action for contravention of provisions. Enforcement also involves conducting surveys, taking possession of acquired land, and determining compensation.

rights: Right of 'persons interested' to claim compensation for acquired land or rights. (Section 2(d))
Right of objectors to be heard either in person or by a legal practitioner during acquisition proceedings. (Section 8(2))
Right to receive compensation for acquired land or rights. (Section 13, 14, 17)
duties: Duty of the competent authority to pay or tender compensation for damages caused during prospecting. (Section 6(1))
Duty of the Central Government to consult State Governments before acquiring land or rights belonging to them that have not been leased out. (Section 9(1))
Duty to comply with the Mineral Concession Rules in prospecting and mining operations conducted by the Central Government. (Section 18)
obligations: Obligation for a Government company to comply with terms and conditions imposed by the Central Government if land/rights are vested in it. (Section 11(1))
Obligation to provide information when requested by the competent authority. (Section 21)

key_procedures: Preliminary Notification for Prospecting: Central Government issues a notification of intention to prospect in an area. (Section 4(1))
Prospecting Activities: Competent authority surveys, bores, and marks land, causing necessary damage and providing compensation. (Section 4(3), 6)
Acquisition Notice: Central Government issues a notice of intention to acquire the land or rights within a specific period. (Section 7(1))
Objection Submission and Hearing: Persons interested can submit written objections within 30 days, and the competent authority holds hearings. (Section 8)
Declaration of Acquisition: Central Government makes a declaration of acquisition based on recommendations. (Section 9(1))
Vesting of Property: Acquired land/rights vest in the Central Government or a Government company. (Section 10, 11)
Compensation Determination: Compensation is determined through a process involving a Tribunal. (Section 14)
administration: The Central Government and appointed 'competent authorities'. Specific administrative functions related to mining and minerals are likely to fall under relevant ministries or departments dealing with coal and mines.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1971, introducing a time limit for making declarations of acquisition after the initial notification.
The Act has been extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
The Act provides for the establishment of a Tribunal for determining compensation.
Section 25 provides protection of action taken in good faith under the Act.

title: THE RAILWAY PROTECTION FORCE ACT, 1957
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed Force of the Union for the better protection and security of railway property, passenger area and passengers and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the Railway Protection Force, its members, and railway property, passenger areas, and passengers.

key_definitions.Force: The Railway Protection Force constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Director-General: The Director-General of the Force appointed under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.enrolled member of the Force: Any subordinate officer, under officer or any other member of the Force of a rank lower than that of under officer.
key_definitions.Force custody: The arrest or confinement of a member of the Force in accordance with rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.member of the Force: A person appointed to the Force under this Act.
key_definitions.passenger: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989).
key_definitions.passenger area: Shall include railway platform, train, yard and such other area as is frequently visited by passengers.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.railway property: Includes any goods, money or valuable security, or animal, belonging to, or in the charge or possession of, a railway administration.
key_definitions.subordinate officer: A person appointed to the Force as an Inspector, Sub-Inspector or an Assistant Sub-Inspector.
key_definitions.superior officer: Any of the officers appointed under section 4 and includes any other officer appointed by the Central Government as a superior officer of the Force.
key_definitions.under officer: A person appointed to the Force as a Head Constable or Naik.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date which is to be appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Force', 'Director-General', 'enrolled member of the Force', 'Force custody', 'member of the Force', 'passenger', 'passenger area', 'prescribed', 'railway property', 'subordinate officer', 'superior officer', and 'under officer'. It also refers to definitions in the Indian Railways Act, 1890.

Provides for the constitution and maintenance of the Railway Protection Force by the Central Government for the protection and security of railway property. It specifies the composition of the Force, including superior officers, subordinate officers, under officers, and enrolled members, and their pay and remuneration.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and powers of superior officers
main_sections.description: Details the appointment of a Director-General and other superior officers (Inspector-General, Additional Inspector-General, Deputy Inspector-General, Assistant Inspector-General, Senior Commandants, Commandants, or Assistant Commandants) by the Central Government. It also states that these superior officers possess and exercise powers and authority over members of the Force under their command.
This section, which previously dealt with classes and ranks among members of the Force, has been omitted.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of members of the Force
main_sections.description: Lays down that the appointment of enrolled members of the Force rests with the Inspector-General, Additional Inspector-General, or Deputy Inspector-General, in accordance with rules made under the Act. It also allows other superior officers to exercise this power if specified by the respective Inspector-General, Additional Inspector-General, or Deputy Inspector-General.

main_sections.section_title: Certificates to members of the Force
main_sections.description: States that every member of the Force receives a certificate upon appointment, which vests them with the powers of a member of the Force. The certificate ceases to have effect when the person ceases to be a member of the Force.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence and administration of the Force
main_sections.description: vests the superintendence of the Force in the Central Government. The command, supervision, and administration of the Force lie with the Director-General. Administration within specified railway limits is carried out by an Inspector-General, Additional Inspector-General, or Deputy Inspector-General under the general supervision of the General Manager of the Railway.

main_sections.section_title: Dismissal, removal, etc., of members of the force
main_sections.description: Empowers superior officers to dismiss, suspend, or reduce in rank any enrolled member found remiss, negligent, or unfit for duty. It also outlines punishments like fines, confinement to quarters, removal from office of distinction, or deprivation of emoluments for careless or negligent discharge of duty. An enrolled member aggrieved by an order can prefer an appeal.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and members of the Force to be deemed to be railway servants
main_sections.description: Declares that the Director-General and every member of the Force are to be regarded as railway servants for all purposes under the Indian Railways Act, 1890 (excluding Chapter VIA), and are entitled to exercise powers conferred on railway servants.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of members of the Force
main_sections.description: Specifies the duties of every superior officer and member of the Force, including promptly executing lawful orders, protecting and safeguarding railway property, passenger areas, and passengers, removing obstructions, and performing any other act conducive to better protection and security.

Grants members of the Force the power to arrest without a warrant or magistrate's order any person who voluntarily causes hurt, attempts to cause hurt, wrongfully restrains, assaults, threatens to assault, or uses criminal force against them or another member in the execution of their duty. It also allows arrest of persons concerned in or reasonably suspected of being concerned in cognizable offenses related to railway property, passenger areas, and passengers, or those taking precautions to conceal their presence under suspicious circumstances.

Allows a member of the Force, not below the rank of Senior Rakshak, to detain and search a person and their belongings without a warrant if they believe an offense under section 12 has been or is being committed and a warrant would allow the offender to escape or conceal evidence. The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, relating to searches apply.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed after arrest
main_sections.description: Mandates that any member of the Force making an arrest under the Act must, without unnecessary delay, hand over the arrested person to a police officer with a detailed report, or take them to the nearest police station in the absence of a police officer.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and members of the Force to be considered always on duty and liable to be employed in any part of the railways
main_sections.description: States that every member of the Force is considered always on duty and liable to be employed at any place within India for the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Members of the Force must promptly execute all lawful orders from their superiors.
Members of the Force have a duty to protect and safeguard railway property, passenger areas, and passengers.

Members of the Force are empowered to arrest individuals without a warrant under specific circumstances related to offenses against themselves, other members, or concerning railway property, passenger areas, and passengers.
Members of the Force can conduct searches without a warrant under certain conditions to prevent escape or concealment of evidence related to offenses.
Upon arrest, the individual must be promptly handed over to the police or taken to the nearest police station.
All members of the Force are considered to be on duty at all times and can be deployed anywhere in India.

penalties: Dismissal, suspension, or reduction in rank for being remiss, negligent, or unfit for duty.
Fine not exceeding seven days' pay.
Reduction in pay scale.
Confinement to quarters for up to fourteen days.
Removal from any office of distinction.
Deprivation of any special emolument.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Superior officers of the Railway Protection Force, ultimately under the superintendence of the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary actions by superior officers, including dismissal, suspension, reduction in rank, and imposition of fines or other punishments. Appeals against these orders can be preferred to a prescribed authority.

rights: Members of the Force are deemed to be railway servants and are entitled to exercise powers conferred on railway servants by or under the Indian Railways Act, 1890.
Members of the Force can appeal disciplinary orders made against them.
duties: To promptly execute all lawful orders from superior authority.
To protect and safeguard railway property, passenger areas, and passengers.
To remove any obstruction in the movement of railway property or passenger areas.
To perform any other act conducive to the better protection and security of railway property, passenger areas, and passengers.
obligations: Members of the Force are considered always on duty and liable for deployment anywhere in India.
Members of the Force must surrender their certificate, arms, etc., upon ceasing to be members.

key_procedures: Appointment of enrolled members of the Force is handled by the Inspector-General, Additional Inspector-General, or Deputy Inspector-General.
Disciplinary proceedings against enrolled members can result in dismissal, suspension, or punishment, with an appeal process available.
Arrests can be made without a warrant by members of the Force under specified circumstances.
Searches can be conducted without a warrant by Senior Rakshaks if certain conditions are met.
After an arrest, the individual must be handed over to a police officer or taken to the nearest police station without unnecessary delay.
administration: The Central Government has superintendence over the Force. The Director-General is responsible for command, supervision, and administration. Within specified railway limits, the administration is carried out by an Inspector-General, Additional Inspector-General, or Deputy Inspector-General under the general supervision of the General Manager of the Railway.
important_notes: Section 5, which dealt with classes and ranks among members of the Force, has been omitted.
The Act defines 'passenger' and 'passenger area' with reference to the Railways Act, 1989, indicating an integration with broader railway legislation.
Provisions for the application of other Acts (Act 22 of 1922 and certain other Acts) to members of the Force are mentioned, suggesting specific legal contexts for their actions and status.

title: THE INTER-STATE CORPORATIONS ACT, 1957
purpose: To provide for the reorganisation of certain corporations functioning in two or more States by virtue of section 109 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to inter-State corporations as defined in Section 2, which are bodies corporate constituted under specific Acts (listed in the Schedule) and functioning in two or more States due to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, or similar enactments.

key_definitions.inter-State corporation: Any body corporate constituted under any of the Acts specified in the Schedule and functioning in two or more States by virtue of section 109 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, or of any other enactment relating to reorganisation of States.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act.
Defines 'inter-State corporation'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Governments to frame schemes
main_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to frame schemes for the reconstitution, reorganisation, or dissolution of inter-State corporations functioning within their jurisdiction. These schemes include proposals for transferring assets, rights, liabilities, and employees.

Details the process for the Central Government to approve and implement schemes for reorganisation or dissolution of inter-State corporations. It outlines the matters that can be included in an order made under this section, such as dissolution, reconstitution, transfer of assets/liabilities/employees, and modifications to the parent Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to add to the Schedule
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to notify and add to the Schedule any Act under which a body corporate constituted for a State is functioning in two or more States due to reorganisation.

important_rules: State Governments can propose schemes for reconstituting, reorganising, or dissolving inter-State corporations.
These schemes must include provisions for the transfer of assets, rights, liabilities, and employees.
The Central Government, after consulting State Governments, can approve these schemes with or without modifications.
The Central Government's order giving effect to the scheme can include dissolution, reconstitution, transfer of assets/liabilities/employees, and adaptations to existing Acts.
Any order made by the Central Government under Section 4 must be published in the Official Gazette and will modify the parent Act until altered by a competent Legislature.
Orders made under Section 4 are subject to parliamentary approval (modification or annulment) if both Houses agree within a specified period.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, in consultation with State Governments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders made by the Central Government, which are published in the Official Gazette and subject to parliamentary review. The provisions of these orders override the parent Act under which the inter-State corporation was constituted.

rights: The right of State Governments to propose schemes for reorganisation or dissolution.
The right of the Central Government to approve or modify these schemes.
The rights of employees to be transferred or re-employed under specified terms and conditions.
duties: Duty of State Governments to forward schemes to the Central Government.
Duty of the Central Government to consult State Governments.
Duty to publish orders in the Official Gazette.
Duty to lay orders before both Houses of Parliament for approval.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the terms of the reorganisation or dissolution scheme approved by the Central Government.
Obligation for transferees to assume the assets, rights, and liabilities of the inter-State corporation.

key_procedures: A State Government identifies a need for reorganisation/dissolution of an inter-State corporation functioning within its state.
The State Government frames a scheme detailing proposals for reconstitution, reorganisation, or dissolution, including asset/liability/employee transfers.
The State Government forwards the scheme to the Central Government.
The Central Government consults the concerned State Governments.
The Central Government approves the scheme, with or without modifications.
The Central Government issues an order to give effect to the approved scheme.
The order is published in the Official Gazette.
The order is laid before both Houses of Parliament for a total of thirty days.
If Parliament modifies or annuls the order, it takes effect in that modified form or becomes ineffective accordingly.
The Act under which the inter-State corporation was constituted has effect subject to the provisions of the Central Government's order.
administration: Central Government, in conjunction with State Governments.
important_notes: The Act is a consequence of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
The Schedule lists specific Acts under which inter-State corporations are covered; the Central Government can add to this list.
Sub-section (5) of Section 4, regarding parliamentary approval of orders, was substituted by Act 20 of 1983.

title: THE NAGA HILLS-TUENSANG AREA ACT, 1957
purpose: To provide for the formation of the Naga Hills -Tuensang Area of Assam as an administrative unit.
scope: This act applies to the formation of a new administrative unit in the State of Assam, specifically comprising the tribal areas known as the Naga Hills District and Tuensang Frontier Division of the North East Frontier Agency.

key_definitions.Naga Hills-Tuensang Area: A new administrative unit formed in the State of Assam, comprising the tribal areas known as the Naga Hills District and Tuensang Frontier Division of the North East Frontier Agency.
key_definitions.law: Any law, ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in India or any part thereof.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act as the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area Act, 1957, and stipulates that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

Declares the formation of a new administrative unit named Naga Hills-Tuensang Area in the State of Assam, effective from the commencement of the Act. This unit comprises the Naga Hills District and the Tuensang Frontier Division of the North East Frontier Agency.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution by inserting a new sub-paragraph (2B) defining the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area, modifying sub-paragraph (3) to exclude this area from certain provisions, and updating specific items in Parts A and B of the Table within the Sixth Schedule.

Amends the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956, by omitting 'Naga Hills' from a specific entry in the First Schedule and removing the heading 'Naga Hills District' and related entries from the Second Schedule pertaining to Assam.
This section, relating to the amendment of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1960.

main_sections.section_title: Provision as to the sitting member of Parliament
main_sections.description: Ensures that the sitting member of the House of the People representing the Autonomous Districts Parliamentary constituency in Assam shall be deemed to have been elected to the altered constituency, notwithstanding the changes made by section 4.

main_sections.section_title: Territorial extent of laws not to be affected
main_sections.description: Clarifies that section 2 of this Act does not alter the territorial extent of any law in force before its commencement. References in such laws to the Naga Hills District, Naga Tribal Area, or Tuensang Frontier Division will continue to have their existing meanings until otherwise provided by a competent authority. The explanation defines 'law' broadly.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for commencement date notification), competent legislatures or authorities (for changes in territorial references of laws).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette for commencement, and by legislative or authoritative action for amendments to laws.

key_procedures: Appointment of commencement date: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint the date on which the Act shall come into force.
Amendment of Laws: Amendments to the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution and the Delimitation Order are made directly by this Act.
administration: Implicitly, the Central Government and the administration of the newly formed Naga Hills-Tuensang Area.
important_notes: The Act was brought into force on December 1st, 1957, via notification No. S.R. O. 3843.
Section 5, concerning amendments to the Representation of the People Act, 1950, has been repealed.
Territorial references in existing laws to the Naga Hills District, Naga Tribal Area, or Tuensang Frontier Division remain valid until changed by competent authorities.

title: THE PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT (REQUIREMENT AS TO RESIDENCE) ACT, 1957
purpose: To make special provisions for requirement as to residence in regard to certain classes of public employment in certain areas, in pursuance of clause (3) of article 16 of the Constitution, and to repeal existing laws prescribing any such requirement.
scope: This Act applies to public employment in specific areas and for specific classes of services or posts under the State Government of Andhra Pradesh, the Administrator of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, or Tripura, and local or other authorities within the Telangana area of Andhra Pradesh or within the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, or Tripura. It also repeals existing laws that prescribed residence requirements for employment under the Government of a State or Union territory, or any local or other authority within that State or Union territory.

key_definitions.subordinate_service_or_post: Means any service or post appointments to which are not notified in the Official Gazette but includes any service of tehsildars.
key_definitions.Telangana_area: Comprises all the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
key_definitions.Himachal_Pradesh: Includes the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957' and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of existing laws prescribing requirements as to residence
main_sections.description: Upon commencement of this Act, any existing law in any State or Union territory that prescribed a requirement as to prior residence for employment under the Government or a local/other authority within that State or Union territory will cease to have effect and is repealed.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules in respect of certain classes of public employment in certain areas
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, prescribing a requirement as to prior residence within specific areas for appointments to: (a) subordinate services or posts under the State Government of Andhra Pradesh, (b) subordinate services or posts under the control of the Administrator of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, or Tripura, or (c) any service or post under a local or other authority (except a cantonment board) within the Telangana area of Andhra Pradesh or within the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, or Tripura.

Requires every rule made under this Act to be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a total of thirty days. If both Houses agree to modify the rule or not make it, it will have effect only in the modified form or no effect, respectively. This is without prejudice to anything previously done under the rule.

States that section 3 and all rules made thereunder will cease to have effect after fifteen years from the commencement of the Act. This cessation will not affect the validity of any appointment previously made under those rules.

important_rules: Rules can be made by the Central Government prescribing a residence requirement prior to appointment for certain subordinate services/posts in Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, or Tripura, and for services/posts under local/other authorities in the Telangana area or these Union territories.
Every rule made under the Act must be laid before Parliament for scrutiny and can be modified or annulled by a joint agreement of both Houses.
Section 3 and its associated rules have a limited duration of fifteen years from the Act's commencement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for making rules), Parliament (for scrutiny of rules), and presumably relevant State/Union territory administrations for day-to-day implementation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Central Government under Section 3, subject to Parliamentary oversight. Existing laws prescribing residence requirements are repealed. Appointments are made in accordance with the rules.

rights: Citizens have a right to public employment as per Article 16 of the Constitution, subject to any special provisions made under this Act.
duties: The Central Government has the duty to make rules as per Section 3, if deemed necessary for specific areas and services.
Public authorities making appointments in the specified areas and services have a duty to comply with the rules made under this Act.
obligations: Candidates for certain public employment in specified areas may have an obligation to meet the prior residence requirement as stipulated by the rules.

key_procedures: The Central Government issues a notification in the Official Gazette to bring the Act into force.
The Central Government, through a notification in the Official Gazette, makes rules prescribing residence requirements for specific appointments.
Rules made under the Act are presented to both Houses of Parliament for a period of thirty days for scrutiny and potential modification or annulment.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act specifically addresses clause (3) of Article 16 of the Constitution, which allows for special provisions regarding residence requirements in certain employment categories.
The Act repeals any pre-existing laws that imposed residence requirements for public employment within states or Union territories, unless covered by the new rules under Section 3.
The provisions of Section 3 and its rules are temporary and will cease to have effect after fifteen years, with no impact on prior appointments made under them.
Amendments were made in 1969 and 1964, particularly concerning the definition of 'Himachal Pradesh' and the procedure for parliamentary scrutiny of rules.

title: THE ARMED FORCES (SPECIAL POWERS) ACT, 1958
purpose: To enable certain special powers to be conferred upon members of the armed forces in disturbed areas in the specified North-Eastern States of India.

scope.geographical: The whole of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura.
scope.subject_matter: Empowerment of armed forces with special powers to maintain public order in disturbed areas, including the power to use force, destroy property, and arrest individuals without warrant.

key_definitions.armed_forces: Means the military forces and the air forces operating as land forces, and includes any other armed forces of the Union so operating.
key_definitions.disturbed_area: Means an area which is for the time being declared by notification under section 3 to be a disturbed area.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent to the North-Eastern states of India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'armed forces' and 'disturbed area'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare areas to be disturbed areas
main_sections.description: Empowers the Governor of a State, the Administrator of a Union territory, or the Central Government to declare an area as a 'disturbed area' if it is in a disturbed or dangerous condition requiring the use of armed forces.

main_sections.section_title: Special powers of the armed forces
main_sections.description: Outlines the special powers that can be exercised by officers and personnel of the armed forces in a disturbed area. These include using force (even to the causing of death), destroying specific types of property, arresting individuals without a warrant, and entering and searching premises.

main_sections.section_title: Arrested persons to be made over to the police
main_sections.description: Mandates that any person arrested under the Act must be handed over to the officer in charge of the nearest police station with the least possible delay, along with a report of the circumstances of the arrest.

main_sections.section_title: Protection to persons acting under Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection to individuals acting under the powers conferred by this Act, stipulating that no prosecution, suit, or legal proceeding can be instituted against them without the previous sanction of the Central Government.
This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1960.

important_rules: Any commissioned officer, warrant officer, non-commissioned officer, or person of equivalent rank in the armed forces can use force, potentially causing death, against individuals contravening laws prohibiting assembly of five or more persons, carrying weapons, or possessing firearms/explosives in a disturbed area, after giving due warning.
Armed forces personnel can destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, shelters used by armed attackers, training camps, or hide-outs used by armed gangs or wanted absconders in a disturbed area.

Armed forces personnel can arrest, without warrant, any person who has committed or is reasonably suspected of having committed or about to commit a cognizable offense and use necessary force to effect the arrest.

Armed forces personnel can enter and search premises without warrant to make an arrest, recover wrongfully restrained persons, or seize suspected stolen property, arms, ammunition, or explosives, using necessary force.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Members of the armed forces (commissioned officers, warrant officers, non-commissioned officers, and equivalent ranks).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By exercising the special powers conferred by Section 4 of the Act in declared 'disturbed areas'.

duties: To make over arrested persons to the police with the least possible delay and a report of circumstances.
To act within the powers conferred by the Act.
To obtain previous sanction of the Central Government before instituting legal proceedings against persons acting under the Act.

key_procedures: Declaration of a 'disturbed area': The Governor, Administrator, or Central Government, upon being of the opinion that an area is in a disturbed or dangerous condition necessitating the use of armed forces, may declare it as a 'disturbed area' by notification.

Powers of armed forces in a disturbed area: Upon declaration, authorized personnel of the armed forces can exercise powers including using force, destroying property, and making arrests without warrant.
Handing over arrested persons: Any person arrested under the Act must be promptly handed over to the nearest police station with a detailed report.
administration: The Central Government has the power to declare areas as disturbed and grant sanction for legal proceedings against persons acting under the Act. The Act is administered through the deployment of armed forces in aid of civil power.
important_notes: The Act has undergone several amendments to change the list of states and union territories to which it applies.
The use of armed forces is intended to be in 'aid of the civil power', indicating a supportive role rather than a replacement of civilian administration.

title: THE ORISSA WEIGHTS AND MEASURES (DELHI REPEAL) ACT, 1958
purpose: To provide for the repeal of the Orissa Weights and Measures Act, 1943, in its application to the Union territory of Delhi.
scope: This act applies to the Union territory of Delhi. It specifically deals with the repeal of the Orissa Weights and Measures Act, 1943, when the Rajasthan Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958, or any part of it, comes into force in Delhi.

key_definitions.Orissa Act: The Orissa Weights and Measures Act, 1943 (Orissa Act 7 of 1943), as extended to Delhi by notification under section 7 of the Delhi Laws Act, 1912 (13 of 1912).
key_definitions.Rajasthan Act: The Rajasthan Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958 (Rajasthan Act 32 of 1958), as extended to the Union territory of Delhi by notification under section 2 of the Union Territories (Laws) Act, 1950 (30 of 1950).

main_sections.description: States that the short title of the Act is the Orissa Weights and Measures (Delhi Repeal) Act, 1958.
Defines the terms 'Orissa Act' and 'Rajasthan Act' for the purposes of this Act.

Provides for the repeal of the Orissa Act (or any provision thereof) on the date the Rajasthan Act (or any provision thereof) comes into force in the Union territory of Delhi. It specifies that the repeal will not affect previous operations, acquired rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, forfeitures, or punishments incurred under the repealed Act, nor will it affect any ongoing investigations or legal proceedings. These can continue as if the Act had not been repealed.

important_rules: On the date the Rajasthan Act (or any provision within it) comes into force in Delhi (or any part of it, for any class of undertakings or goods), the Orissa Act (or any provision within it) applicable to those undertakings or goods shall stand repealed.

penalties: The repeal shall not affect any penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed against the Orissa Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated for this repeal act, but the enforcement of the Rajasthan Act, upon its commencement, would be the relevant authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The repeal is triggered by the commencement of the Rajasthan Act in Delhi.

rights: The repeal shall not affect any right or privilege acquired, accrued, or incurred under the Orissa Act.
obligations: The repeal shall not affect any obligation or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred under the Orissa Act.

key_procedures: The commencement of the Rajasthan Act (or any part thereof) in the Union territory of Delhi, by notification under its section 1(3), triggers the repeal of the Orissa Act.
administration: Not explicitly stated for this repeal act.
important_notes: The repeal is conditional upon the Rajasthan Act coming into force in Delhi.
The repeal is not retrospective in effect regarding past operations, rights, liabilities, or penalties.
The repeal does not disrupt ongoing legal proceedings or remedies.

title: The Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958
purpose: To provide for the control of rents and evictions and of rates of hotels and lodging houses, and for the lease of vacant premises to Government, in certain areas in the Union territory of Delhi.
scope: The Act extends to the areas included within the limits of the New Delhi Municipal Committee and the Delhi Cantonment Board, and to such urban areas within the limits of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi as are specified in the First Schedule. The Central Government may, by notification, extend or exclude any urban area within the limits of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi from its operation. The Act does not apply to premises belonging to the Government or created by a grant from the Government, premises with a monthly rent exceeding three thousand and five hundred rupees, or newly constructed premises for a period of ten years from completion.

key_definitions.basic rent: The basic rent of premises let out before June 2, 1944, as determined in accordance with the Second Schedule.
key_definitions.controller: A Controller appointed under sub-section (1) of section 35, including an additional Controller.
key_definitions.fair rate: The fair rate fixed under section 31, including rates revised under section 32.
key_definitions.hotel or lodging house: A building or part of a building where lodging with or without board or other services is provided for monetary consideration.
key_definitions.landlord: A person who receives or is entitled to receive rent of any premises, on their own behalf or on behalf of others, or as a trustee, guardian, or receiver.
key_definitions.lawful increase: An increase in rent permitted under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.manager of a hotel: Includes any person in charge of the management of the hotel.
key_definitions.owner of a lodging house: A person who receives or is entitled to receive monetary consideration from any person on account of board, lodging, or other services provided in the lodging house.
key_definitions.premises: Any building or part of a building let separately for residence, commercial use, or any other purpose, including appurtenant gardens, grounds, outhouses, and any furniture supplied by the landlord. It does not include a room in a hotel or lodging house.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.standard rent: The standard rent referred to in section 6, or where increased under section 7, the increased rent.
key_definitions.tenant: Any person by whom or on whose account or behalf rent is payable, or would be payable but for a special contract. It includes a sub-tenant, a person continuing in possession after termination of tenancy, and certain heirs of such persons under specific conditions. It does not include persons against whom an eviction order is made (unless reopenable) or persons granted a license under the Indian Easements Act, 1882.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of commencement.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as basic rent, Controller, landlord, premises, standard rent, and tenant.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain premises
main_sections.description: Exempts certain premises from the application of the Act, including government-owned premises, tenancies created by government grants, premises with high rents, and newly constructed premises for a specified period.

main_sections.section_title: Rent in excess of standard rent not recoverable
main_sections.description: Stipulates that a tenant is not liable to pay rent exceeding the standard rent, except for lawful increases. Any agreement to the contrary is deemed to be for the standard rent only.

main_sections.section_title: Unlawful charges not to be claimed or received
main_sections.description: Prohibits claiming or receiving rent in excess of standard rent, any premium or pugree, or more than one month's rent in advance without the Controller's permission. It also prohibits tenants from claiming payment for relinquishing their tenancy.
Details the provisions for fixing the standard rent of premises.
Provides protection to tenants against eviction, outlining conditions under which eviction is permissible.

main_sections.section_title: Deposit of rent by the tenant
main_sections.description: Allows tenants to deposit rent with the Controller under certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Controllers and additional Controllers
main_sections.description: Deals with the appointment of Controllers and additional Controllers.

main_sections.section_title: Landlord’s duty to keep the premises in good repair
main_sections.description: Obligates landlords to maintain the rented premises in good repair.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No tenant shall be liable to pay rent exceeding the standard rent, except for lawful increases (Section 4).
Landlords are prohibited from claiming unlawful charges like premiums or receiving more than one month's rent in advance without the Controller's permission (Section 5).
Tenants have protection against eviction and can deposit rent with the Controller if the landlord refuses to accept it (Section 14, Section 27).
Landlords have a duty to keep the premises in good repair (Section 44).
Cutting off or withholding essential supply or service to a tenant is illegal (Section 45).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 48).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Controllers appointed under the Act, who exercise powers similar to magistrates and civil courts for recovery and execution of orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of Controllers with specific powers, summary trial procedures for certain applications, and civil court powers for execution of orders. Penalties are prescribed for offenses.

rights: Tenant's right to protection against eviction.
Tenant's right to pay standard rent.
Tenant's right to deposit rent with the Controller.
Right of certain persons (e.g., members of armed forces, government employees, widows) to recover immediate possession of premises under specific conditions (Section 14A-14D).
Right of landlord to recover possession for occupation, repairs, rebuilding, or in case of tenancies for a limited period, under specific conditions (Section 19-22).
duties: Landlord's duty to keep premises in good repair (Section 44).
Landlord's duty to give notice of new construction to the Government (Section 46).
obligations: Obligation of landlords not to cut off or withhold essential supply or service (Section 45).
Obligation of tenants to pay rent.

key_procedures: Procedure for fixing standard rent by the Controller (Section 9).
Procedure for the deposit of rent by the tenant (Section 27-29).
Special procedure for disposal of eviction applications based on bona fide requirement (Section 25B).
Procedure for appeals to the Tribunal (Section 38).
Procedure to be followed by the Controller in hearings (Section 37).
administration: The Central Government and the Delhi Administration (through appointed Controllers and Tribunals).
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1976 and 1988, significantly impacting the definition of 'tenant' and exemptions.
The Central Government has the power to extend or exclude areas from the Act's operation.
The Act has specific provisions for hotels and lodging houses.

title: The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959
purpose: To declare that certain offices of profit under the Government shall not disqualify the holders thereof for being chosen as, or for being, members of Parliament.
scope: Applies to individuals who are members of Parliament or seek to become members of Parliament in India. It specifies certain offices of profit that do not lead to disqualification from being a member of Parliament. The scope is national, covering offices under the Government of India and the Government of any State.

key_definitions.compensatory_allowance: Any sum of money payable to the holder of an office by way of daily allowance (not exceeding the daily allowance to which a member of Parliament is entitled), any conveyance allowance, house-rent allowance, or travelling allowance for the purpose of enabling the holder to recoup any expenditure incurred in performing the functions of that office.
key_definitions.statutory_body: Any corporation, committee, commission, council, board, or other body of persons, whether incorporated or not, established by or under any law for the time being in force.
key_definitions.non_statutory_body: Any body of persons other than a statutory body.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959'.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'compensatory allowance', 'statutory body', and 'non-statutory body'.

main_sections.section_title: Certain offices of profit not to disqualify
main_sections.description: Lists specific offices of profit under the Government of India or any State that do not disqualify a person from being chosen as or being a member of Parliament. This includes offices held by Ministers, Leaders of the Opposition, Deputy Chairmen of Planning Commissions, chairpersons/members of various commissions, committees, boards, forces, Home Guards, Sheriffs, university bodies, delegations, certain statutory and non-statutory bodies (with exceptions listed in the Schedule), and village revenue officers with specific remunerations and duties.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary suspension of disqualification in certain cases
main_sections.description: Provides for a temporary suspension of disqualification for a period not exceeding six months from the commencement of the Act for members of Parliament who held an office of profit that was not disqualifying under a repealed law but becomes disqualifying under the new Act.

Repeals the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1950, the Parliament Prevention of Disqualification Act, 1951, the Prevention of Disqualification Act, 1953, and any other inconsistent provisions in other enactments.

important_rules: Rule: Offices of profit held by Ministers, Ministers of State, or Deputy Ministers (Union or State) do not disqualify a person from being a member of Parliament.
Rule: The office of the Leader of the Opposition in Parliament does not disqualify a person.
Rule: The office of the Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission does not disqualify a person.

Rule: The office of Chairperson or member of various statutory and non-statutory bodies is declared not to disqualify a member of Parliament, provided the holder is not entitled to remuneration other than compensatory allowance, with specific exclusions listed in the Schedule.
Rule: Offices held by members of the National Cadet Corps, Territorial Army, Reserve and Auxiliary Air Forces, or Home Guards do not disqualify a person.
Rule: The office of Sheriff in Bombay, Calcutta, or Madras does not disqualify a person.
Rule: Offices related to universities, such as chairman or member of a syndicate, senate, etc., do not disqualify a person.
Rule: Offices of chairpersons or members of temporary committees set up for advising the government or making inquiries, if remunerated only by compensatory allowance, do not disqualify a person.

Rule: Offices of village revenue officers (lambardar, malguzar, patel, deshmukh) who collect land revenue and are remunerated by a share or commission on the collected revenue, and do not discharge police functions, do not disqualify a person.
Rule: Offices of Chairperson or trustee of any Trust (public or private), not specified in the Schedule, do not disqualify a person.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act itself declares certain offices as non-disqualifying. Enforcement would likely involve the presiding officers of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) and election authorities to determine eligibility and disqualification based on these provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By declaring specific offices as not leading to disqualification, the Act prevents such offices from being a ground for a member of Parliament to be disqualified. Any challenges to a member's eligibility based on holding an office of profit would be evaluated against the provisions of this Act.

rights: The right of individuals to hold certain specified offices of profit under the Government without being disqualified from being a member of Parliament.
The right of the Parliament to enact laws to prevent disqualification of its members.
duties: Duty of individuals to ensure that any office held does not, by the definitions and exclusions in this Act, lead to disqualification from Parliament.
Duty of election authorities and Parliament to apply the provisions of this Act when determining a candidate's eligibility or a member's continued membership.

key_procedures: Determination of whether an office is an 'office of profit under the Government'.
Assessment of whether the remuneration received for an office is solely 'compensatory allowance' as defined by the Act.
Verification against the list of offices specified in Section 3 and the Schedule to determine if holding such an office disqualifies a person from being a Member of Parliament.
administration: While the Act itself does not specify a single administrative department, its provisions are relevant to the functioning of Parliament, the Election Commission of India, and various government departments that establish or oversee the bodies listed in the Act.
important_notes: The Act is subject to amendments, as indicated by the footnotes referencing various amending Acts and their effective dates.

The Schedule, which lists specific bodies where holding the office of Chairperson is excluded from the non-disqualifying provisions (Part I), and offices of Chairperson or Secretary are excluded (Part II), is an integral part of Section 3(i) and is subject to changes through amendments.
Explanations 2 and 3 clarify the meaning of 'Leader of the Opposition' and 'recognised party'/'recognised group' by referencing other specific Acts.

title: THE COST ACCOUNTANTS ACT, 1959
purpose: To make provision for the regulation and development of the profession of cost accountants.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to individuals who are members of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India and engage in the practice of cost accountancy. It also covers the establishment and functioning of the Institute, its Council, Regional Councils, Quality Review Board, and disciplinary procedures.

key_definitions.associate: An associate member of the Institute.
key_definitions.Authority: The Appellate Authority referred to in section 22A.
key_definitions.Board: The Quality Review Board constituted under section 29A.
key_definitions.Board of Discipline: The Board of Discipline constituted under sub-section (1) of section 21A.
key_definitions.Companies Act: The Companies Act, 2013 or any other previous company law.
key_definitions.cost accountant: A person who is a member of the Institute.
key_definitions.Council: The Council of the Institute constituted under section 9.
key_definitions.Director (Discipline): The Director (Discipline) referred to in section 21 and includes Joint Director (Discipline).
key_definitions.Disciplinary Committee: The Disciplinary Committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 21B.
key_definitions.Disciplinary Directorate: The Disciplinary Directorate established under sub-section (1) of section 21.
key_definitions.dissolved company: The Institute of Cost and Works Accountants registered under the Companies Act.
key_definitions.fellow: A fellow member of the Institute.
key_definitions.firm: As defined in section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, and includes a limited liability partnership and a sole proprietorship registered with the Institute.
key_definitions.Institute: The Institute of Cost Accountants of India constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.partner: As defined in the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 or the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.
key_definitions.partnership: A partnership as defined in the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, or a limited liability partnership which has no company as its partner.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.Register: The Register of members of the Institute maintained under section 19 or Register of firms of the Institute maintained under section 20B.
key_definitions.specified: Specified by rules made by the Central Government under this Act.
key_definitions.sole proprietorship: An individual who engages himself in the practice of cost accountancy or offers to perform services referred to in clauses (ii) to (iv) of sub-section (2).
key_definitions.Standing Committee: A Standing Committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 17.
key_definitions.Tribunal: A Tribunal established under sub-section (1) of section 10B.
key_definitions.year: The period commencing on the 1st day of April of any year and ending on the 31st day of March of the succeeding year.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date on which it comes into force as notified by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'associate', 'cost accountant', 'Institute', 'Council', 'fellow', 'firm', and 'practice of cost accountancy'. It also clarifies the meaning of 'to be in practice'.

Constitutes the Institute of Cost Accountants of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued in its name.

main_sections.section_title: Entry of names in the Register of members
main_sections.description: Specifies the categories of persons entitled to have their names entered in the Register of members, including former members of the dissolved company, those who pass prescribed examinations and training, and those engaged in practice.

Divides members into two classes: associates and fellows. Any person whose name is entered in the Register becomes an associate member and can use the letters ACMA. Former fellows of the dissolved company are entered as fellows.
Outlines the various functions and powers of the Council of the Institute, which include managing the affairs of the Institute, promoting the profession, and making regulations.
Establishes the Disciplinary Directorate responsible for receiving and processing complaints of professional or other misconduct against members.
Defines what constitutes professional or other misconduct for members of the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, etc.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who falsely claim to be members of the Institute or use its name or designations.

main_sections.section_title: Companies not to engage in cost accountancy
main_sections.description: Prohibits companies from engaging in the practice of cost accountancy.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of the Institute of Cost and Works Accountants registered under the Companies Act, 1956
main_sections.description: Provides for the dissolution of the previously registered Institute of Cost and Works Accountants under the Companies Act, 1956.
Empowers the Central Government to give directions to the Institute and the Council.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Council of the Institute to make regulations, subject to the approval of the Central Government, for the administration and functioning of the Institute.

important_rules: Members in practice are defined as those who, in consideration of remuneration, engage in cost accountancy practice, offer or perform services related to costing or pricing of goods/services, or prepare, verify, certify, or audit cost accounting statements.
A member who is a whole-time salaried employee is not considered to be in practice.
The Institute is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Specific categories of persons are entitled to be registered as members based on prior qualifications, examinations, and training.
Members are classified as 'associates' or 'fellows'.
Companies are prohibited from engaging in cost accountancy.
Unqualified persons are prohibited from signing cost accounting documents.

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, or for using the name of the Council, or for awarding degrees of cost accountancy.
Penalty for companies engaging in cost accountancy.
Penalty for unqualified persons signing documents.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Council of the Institute, Disciplinary Directorate, Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee, and the Appellate Authority are involved in the enforcement and disciplinary proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary proceedings for misconduct, imposition of penalties, and prosecution for offenses. The Directorate (Discipline), Board of Discipline, and Disciplinary Committee have powers of a civil court.

rights: Right to use the designation ACMA for associate members.
Right to have names entered in the Register under specified conditions.
duties: Members have a duty to conduct themselves professionally and avoid misconduct.
Members in practice must adhere to prescribed standards and procedures.
obligations: Members are obligated to maintain their registration and comply with the Act and regulations.
The Institute has an obligation to regulate the profession and impart education.

key_procedures: Procedure for entering names in the Register of members, including passing examinations and completing training.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Council and its committees.
Procedure for disciplinary proceedings initiated by the Disciplinary Directorate, involving the Board of Discipline and Disciplinary Committee.
Procedure for appeals against orders of the Disciplinary Committee to the Appellate Authority.
Procedure for the establishment and functioning of the Quality Review Board.
administration: The Council of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India is the primary administrative body, with oversight from the Central Government. The Disciplinary Directorate, Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee, and Appellate Authority handle specific functions related to misconduct and appeals. The Quality Review Board oversees quality.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2022 to update terminology and certain provisions.
The Act incorporates provisions for the dissolution of a previously existing Institute registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
Members are considered public servants for certain purposes.
The Central Government has the power to make rules, and the Council has the power to make regulations for the Act's implementation.

title: The Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1959
purpose: To provide for the transfer of certain territories from the State of Rajasthan to the State of Madhya Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to specific territories transferred from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh, and its provisions govern the legal, administrative, and constitutional implications of this transfer.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The 1st day of October, 1959.
key_definitions.assembly_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.council_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.parliamentary_constituency: Has the same meaning as in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
key_definitions.sitting_member: A person who, immediately before the appointed day, is a member of the House of the People or of the Legislature of a State.
key_definitions.transferred_territories: The territories specified in the First Schedule, transferred from the State of Rajasthan to the State of Madhya Pradesh by section 3.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1959.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'assembly constituency', 'council constituency', 'parliamentary constituency', 'sitting member', and 'transferred territories'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of territories from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh
main_sections.description: Specifies the transfer of territories from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh as of the appointed day, including their inclusion in Bhanpura pargana of Mandsaur district and allows for subsequent alterations of district boundaries by the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the inclusion of transferred territories in Madhya Pradesh and their exclusion from Rajasthan.

States that the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956, and the Constitution of Council Constituencies (Madhya Pradesh) Order, 1957, will have effect subject to modifications specified in the Second Schedule.
Ensures that sitting members of the House of the People and Legislative Assemblies representing constituencies affected by the territorial transfer continue in their positions.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of Madhya Pradesh High Court
main_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the Madhya Pradesh High Court to the transferred territories and clarifies the handling of pending proceedings in the Rajasthan High Court related to these territories.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in transferred territories under existing Appropriation Acts
main_sections.description: Provides that existing appropriation Acts of Madhya Pradesh will apply to the transferred territories, allowing for expenditure in those areas.
Deals with the transfer of assets (land, goods) and liabilities (rights, obligations) of the State of Rajasthan in relation to the transferred territories to the State of Madhya Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards
main_sections.description: Ensures that State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards constituted for Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh are deemed to be constituted for their respective states with altered areas.

Specifies the extension of laws from Mandsaur district to the transferred territories and the cessation of laws that were only in force in the transferred territories but not in the Mandsaur district.
Grants courts, tribunals, or authorities the power to construe laws extended to the transferred territories for their proper application.

Provides for the substitution or addition of the State of Madhya Pradesh as a party in legal proceedings where the State of Rajasthan was a party concerning transferred property, rights, or liabilities.

Details the transfer of pending proceedings (excluding High Court matters) from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh if they exclusively relate to the transferred territories, with the Rajasthan High Court having final decision-making power on transfer disputes.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of provisions inconsistent with other laws
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act will prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.
Empowers the President to issue orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to give effect to the Act, subject to parliamentary approval.

important_rules: Rule: As from the appointed day (October 1, 1959), territories specified in the First Schedule are transferred from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh and cease to be part of Rajasthan.
Rule: These transferred territories are to be included in and form part of Bhanpura pargana of Mandsaur district in Madhya Pradesh.

Rule: All laws in force in Mandsaur district immediately before the appointed day that do not extend to the transferred territories shall extend to them, and laws exclusively in force in the transferred territories shall cease to be in force there, except for past actions.
Rule: Assets (land, goods) and liabilities (rights, obligations) of Rajasthan in the transferred territories pass to Madhya Pradesh.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the State Governments of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, and relevant authorities for specific laws extended or modified.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and construction of laws, the transfer of proceedings, and administrative actions by the respective state governments.

rights: The right of Madhya Pradesh to incorporate the transferred territories.
The right of sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures to continue in their seats despite constituency alterations.
The right of the Madhya Pradesh High Court to exercise jurisdiction over the transferred territories.
The right of the State Government to spend moneys from appropriation Acts in the transferred territories.
duties: The duty of Rajasthan to transfer territories, assets, and liabilities.
The duty of Madhya Pradesh to assume jurisdiction and responsibilities over the transferred territories.
The duty of courts, tribunals, and authorities to apply and construe laws as per the Act.
obligations: Obligation of Madhya Pradesh to inherit the rights, liabilities, and obligations of Rajasthan in the transferred territories.
Obligation of the State Governments to ensure smooth transition and effectuate the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: Transfer of territories from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh is effected as from the appointed day (October 1, 1959).
Procedure: Amendments to the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the territorial changes.
Procedure: Modifications to Delimitation Orders to align constituencies with the new territorial boundaries.
Procedure: Extension of Madhya Pradesh High Court's jurisdiction to the transferred territories.
Procedure: Transfer of pending legal proceedings (excluding High Court cases) from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh if they exclusively relate to the transferred territories.
administration: The administration of the transferred territories would fall under the respective departments and authorities of the State of Madhya Pradesh.
important_notes: The Act's provisions have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law (Section 15).
The President has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act (Section 16).
The Central Government can make rules to give effect to the Act, subject to parliamentary scrutiny (Section 17).

title: THE PREFERENCE SHARES (REGULATION OF DIVIDENDS) ACT, 1960
purpose: To regulate dividends on preference shares of certain companies.
scope: Applies to the whole of India, with an exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union Territory) except for provisions related to banking and insurance companies and financial corporations. Specific modifications apply to the Union territory of Pondicherry.

key_definitions.company: An Indian company as defined in clause (26) of section 2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961), and includes a company referred to in sub-clause (ii) of clause (17) of the said section which has made arrangements for the declaration and payment of dividends within India.
key_definitions.preference share: A share which carries, as respects dividends, a preferential right to be paid a fixed amount or an amount calculated at a fixed rate.
key_definitions.previous year: Has the same meaning as in the Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961).
key_definitions.stipulated dividend: In relation to a preference share, means the fixed amount or the amount calculated at a fixed rate which the holder of such share has a preferential right to be paid as dividend.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement. It also specifies the territorial applicability and any modifications for specific Union territories.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Companies Act', 'company', 'preference share', 'previous year', and 'stipulated dividend'.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of dividends on preference shares in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Details the regulation of dividends on preference shares, specifying additional percentages to be paid in cases where dividends were free of income-tax or subject to deduction, for shares issued and subscribed before specific dates.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions in relation to companies where a portion of their income is not chargeable to income-tax.
