main_sections.description: Addresses special provisions for companies where a portion of their profits is exempt from income-tax, particularly concerning the calculation of increased dividends on preference shares.
Specifies the maximum deduction that can be made by a company from dividends on preference shares on account of income-tax payable by the company.

States that the provisions of the Act have effect notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law, company's constitution, or agreements. It also allows for companies to increase dividends beyond the specified limits under certain conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to participating preference dividends.
main_sections.description: Excludes the application of certain sections of the Act to the part of dividends on preference shares that are considered 'participating preference dividends' as defined in the Companies Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, with provisions for laying such rules before Parliament.

important_rules: Rule: Where a stipulated dividend on a preference share (issued and subscribed for before April 1, 1960) is free of income-tax or paid without deduction, the share shall carry a right to be paid without deduction an amount exceeding the stipulated dividend by 30% for dividends declared after the Act's commencement.

Rule: Where a stipulated dividend on a preference share (issued and subscribed for before April 1, 1960) is subject to income-tax and a deduction is made, the share shall carry a right to be paid subject to the deduction an amount exceeding the stipulated dividend by 11% for dividends declared after the Act's commencement.

Rule: If a company declared a dividend for a previous year relevant to assessment years 1960-61 or later, after March 31, 1959, and before the Act's commencement, it must declare an additional dividend to meet the 30% or 11% excess requirements.
Rule: The deduction made by a company from a dividend on account of income-tax payable by the company does not include any amount deducted under section 194 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for making rules), Company (for declaring dividends as per Act)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act itself, and potentially through actions taken by regulatory bodies overseeing companies and taxation.

rights: Holders of preference shares have a preferential right to be paid a stipulated dividend.
In certain cases, preference shareholders have a right to receive dividends exceeding the stipulated dividend by 30% or 11%.
duties: Companies have a duty to declare and pay dividends on preference shares according to the regulations set forth in the Act.
obligations: Companies are obligated to pay additional amounts on preference shares as stipulated by the Act, ensuring the specified percentage increase over the stipulated dividend.
Companies must comply with the over-riding effect of the Act, which supersedes conflicting provisions in other laws, company documents, or agreements.

key_procedures: Dividend Declaration: Companies must declare dividends on preference shares, taking into account the stipulated dividend and the additional percentage increases mandated by the Act, depending on the share's issue date and tax treatment.
Rule Making: The Central Government can make rules to carry out the Act's purposes, which are then presented to Parliament for approval or modification.
administration: Central Government (through rule-making power)
important_notes: The Act may not apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir, except for provisions related to banking, insurance companies, and financial corporations.
Specific modifications apply to the Union territory of Pondicherry, including the omission of sections 3 and 4, and modified provisions in section 4A and section 5.
The Act's provisions have an over-riding effect, meaning they take precedence over any other laws, company articles of association, or shareholder agreements.
Companies can increase dividend amounts beyond the limits specified in sections 3 or 4 of this Act, provided they follow the procedures outlined in section 106 of the Companies Act.

title: THE DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT, 1961
purpose: To prohibit the giving or taking of dowry.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to marriages and actions related to dowry as defined in the Act.

key_definitions.dowry: Any property or valuable security given or agreed to be given either directly or indirectly by one party to a marriage to the other party, or by the parents of either party or by any other person, to either party to the marriage or to any other person, at or before or any time after the marriage in connection with the marriage of the said parties. Excludes dower or mahr in the case of Muslims. (Haryana amendment defines 'marriage expenses' including certain ceremonies and gifts).
key_definitions.valuable_security: Has the same meaning as in section 30 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, specifies its extent to the whole of India, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines what constitutes 'dowry' for the purposes of the Act, including property or valuable security given or agreed to be given in connection with a marriage. Also includes a state amendment from Haryana with a broader definition of marriage expenses.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for giving or taking dowry.
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for the act of giving, taking, or abetting the giving or taking of dowry. Includes minimum imprisonment and fine, with provisions for lesser sentences under special circumstances. Also outlines exceptions for presents given to the bride or bridegroom under specific conditions.
Specifies penalties for demanding dowry, directly or indirectly, from parents or relatives of the bride or bridegroom.
Prohibits advertisements offering property, money, or business interests as consideration for marriage, and prescribes penalties for such advertisements.

main_sections.section_title: Agreement for giving or taking dowry to be void.
main_sections.description: Declares any agreement for the giving or taking of dowry to be void.

main_sections.section_title: Dowry to be for the benefit of the wife or her heirs.
main_sections.description: Mandates that any dowry received by a person other than the woman in connection with whose marriage it is given must be transferred to that woman within a specified period, or to her heirs if she dies before receiving it. Penalties are prescribed for failure to transfer.

Outlines the procedure for courts to take cognizance of offences under the Act, specifying the minimum court rank, types of complaints or reports that can initiate proceedings, and that statements by the aggrieved person are not subject to prosecution under this Act. Includes state amendments from Haryana with specific procedural details.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable for certain purposes and to be bailable and non-compoundable.
main_sections.description: States that offenses under the Act are to be treated as cognizable for investigation purposes, but not for arrest without a warrant. Further clarifies that these offenses are non-bailable and non-compoundable.

main_sections.section_title: Burden of proof in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Places the burden of proof on the accused to prove they have not committed an offense under sections 3 or 4.

Empowers the State Government to appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers and outlines their powers and functions, including ensuring compliance with the Act and preventing the taking or demanding of dowry.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the State Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Any agreement for the giving or taking of dowry is void.
Dowry received by someone other than the bride must be transferred to her or her heirs within three months of marriage or receipt.

Presents given to the bride or bridegroom at the time of marriage are not considered dowry if they are not demanded and are entered in a list, provided they are customary and not excessive in value for the bridegroom's presents.
Advertisements offering marriage consideration in terms of property or money are prohibited.
The burden of proof lies with the accused in cases of dowry prosecution.

penalties: Giving or taking dowry: Imprisonment not less than five years and a fine not less than fifteen thousand rupees or the value of the dowry, whichever is more.
Demanding dowry: Imprisonment not less than six months, extendable to two years, and a fine up to ten thousand rupees.
Advertisement related to dowry: Imprisonment not less than six months, extendable to five years, and a fine up to fifteen thousand rupees.

Failure to transfer dowry to the woman/heirs: Imprisonment not less than six months, extendable to two years, and a fine not less than five thousand rupees, extendable to ten thousand rupees, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Government, and Courts (Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial proceedings, investigation by police (under specific ranks), cognizance of offenses by specified courts upon complaint or police report, and by Dowry Prohibition Officers who monitor compliance and prevent dowry-related activities.

rights: Right to receive dowry if it was meant for the woman, or for her heirs if she is deceased.
Right to complain to the court or recognized welfare institutions about dowry offenses.
duties: Duty to transfer dowry to the rightful beneficiary (woman or her heirs) within prescribed timeframes.
Duty to refrain from giving, taking, demanding, or abetting dowry.
Duty for persons advertising marriage considerations to comply with the ban on advertisements.
obligations: Obligation for any person receiving dowry (other than the bride) to hold it in trust and transfer it.
Obligation for courts to take cognizance of offenses and impose penalties as prescribed.
Obligation for State Governments to appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers and define their jurisdiction.

key_procedures: Initiation of proceedings: Cognizance taken by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class, either on their own knowledge, a police report, or a complaint by the aggrieved person, their parent/relative, or a recognized welfare institution.

Transfer of dowry: If dowry is received by someone other than the woman, they must transfer it within three months of marriage, receipt, or the woman attaining majority (if a minor at the time of receipt).

Enforcement of transfer order: If a convicted person fails to transfer property as ordered, the court can direct the transfer within a specified period, and failure to comply can result in recovery of the property's value as a fine.
administration: Central Government and State Governments (responsible for appointing officers and making rules).
important_notes: The Act was extended to the whole of India, with the exception of the State of Jammu and Kashmir being omitted by Act 34 of 2019.
The definition of dowry and related penalties have been amended over time by various acts, increasing the severity of punishments and clarifying certain aspects.
State amendments from Haryana have introduced specific definitions and procedural nuances.
Presents made to the bride at the time of marriage are not considered dowry unless they are demanded as consideration for the marriage.

title: THE UNION TERRITORIES (STAMP AND COURT-FEES LAWS) ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the amendment and repeal of certain laws relating to stamp duties and court-fees as in force in certain Union territories.
scope: This Act applies to the Union territories of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, and Tripura, and pertains to laws concerning stamp duties and court-fees.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in Himachal Pradesh.
main_sections.description: This section details the amendment of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as it was in force in Himachal Pradesh. It specifies that Schedule I-A of the Act will be substituted with modifications as may be specified in a notification by the Central Government, aligning it with the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in the State of Punjab on a particular date.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in Himachal Pradesh.
main_sections.description: This section states that the Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in Himachal Pradesh, shall stand repealed on the date the Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in the State of Punjab, is extended to Himachal Pradesh by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in Manipur and Tripura.
main_sections.description: This section provides for the repeal of the Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in Manipur and Tripura. It states that the Act will stand repealed in these Union territories on the date the Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in the State of Assam, is extended to them by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in Manipur and Tripura.
main_sections.description: This section deals with the repeal of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as it was in force in Manipur and Tripura. It specifies that the Act will stand repealed in these Union territories on the date the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in the State of Assam, is extended to them by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy of stamp duties in certain cases.
main_sections.description: This section validates the levy and collection of stamp duties in the Union territory of Manipur during a specific period (from April 16, 1950, to the date of extension of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, from Assam). It deems these duties to have always been levied and collected in accordance with the law, provided they were collected under the belief that the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in Assam before April 16, 1950, was applicable.

important_rules: Rule 1: On a date appointed by the Central Government, Schedule I-A of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in Himachal Pradesh, will be substituted with modifications to align it with the Punjab version of the Act.
Rule 2: The Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in Himachal Pradesh, will be repealed upon the extension of the Punjab's Court-fees Act, 1870, to Himachal Pradesh.
Rule 3: The Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in Manipur and Tripura, will be repealed upon the extension of Assam's Court-fees Act, 1870, to these Union territories.
Rule 4: The Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in Manipur and Tripura, will be repealed upon the extension of Assam's Indian Stamp Act, 1899, to these Union territories.

Rule 5: Stamp duties levied and collected in Manipur between April 16, 1950, and the extension date of the Assam Indian Stamp Act, 1899, are deemed to have been legally levied and collected if collected under the belief of the Assam Act's applicability.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for notifications and appointments), State Governments (for extension of laws to Union Territories)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette for appointments and extension of laws.

obligations: Obligation to follow the amended Indian Stamp Act, 1899, in Himachal Pradesh.
Obligation to adhere to the extended Court-fees Act and Indian Stamp Act in Manipur and Tripura, as specified by notifications.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Central Government issues a notification to appoint a date for the amendment of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, in Himachal Pradesh and specifies the modifications to Schedule I-A.

Procedure 2: State Governments extend the Court-fees Act, 1870, and the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, from their respective states (Punjab or Assam) to the Union territories (Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura) via notification under Section 2 of the Union Territories (Laws) Act, 1950.
administration: Ministry of Law and Justice (implied, as it is a parliamentary act), with implementation involving the Central Government and State Governments.
important_notes: Note 1: The repeal of existing laws in Union territories is contingent upon the extension of corresponding laws from specific states.
Note 2: Section 6 provides a retrospective validation for stamp duty collection in Manipur, ensuring legal continuity under certain conditions.

title: THE DEPOSIT INSURANCE AND CREDIT GUARANTEE CORPORATION ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a corporation for the purpose of insurance of deposits and guaranteeing of credit facilities and for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to banking companies, co-operative banks, and credit institutions.

key_definitions.banking: Accepting deposits from the public for lending or investment, repayable on demand or otherwise, and withdrawable by cheque, draft, order or otherwise.
key_definitions.banking company: Any company that transacts the business of banking in India, including the State Bank and subsidiary banks, but excluding certain specific entities.
key_definitions.deposit: The aggregate of unpaid balances due to a depositor (excluding certain government entities and financial institutions) in respect of all their accounts, including credit balances in cash credit accounts, but excluding deposits received outside India and certain specially exempted deposits.
key_definitions.credit institution: Includes banking companies, corresponding new banks, Regional Rural Banks, co-operative banks, and financial institutions.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the commencement date to be appointed by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'banking', 'banking company', 'Board', 'company', 'co-operative bank', 'Corporation', 'defunct banking company', 'defunct co-operative bank', 'deposit', 'eligible co-operative bank', 'existing banking company', 'existing co-operative bank', and 'financial institution'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of Deposit Insurance Corporation
main_sections.description: Establishes the Deposit Insurance Corporation.
Concerns the registration of banking companies that were in existence at the commencement of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of Corporation in respect of insured deposits
main_sections.description: Outlines the extent of the Corporation's liability towards depositors for insured deposits.

main_sections.section_title: Guaranteeing of credit facilities and indemnifying credit institutions
main_sections.description: Deals with the Corporation's function of guaranteeing credit facilities and indemnifying credit institutions.
Specifies penalties for contraventions of the Act's provisions.

important_rules: Banking companies and co-operative banks are to be registered as insured banks.
The Corporation is liable to depositors in respect of insured deposits.
The Corporation guarantees credit facilities and indemnifies credit institutions.
The Act outlines procedures for the management, funds, accounts, and audit of the Corporation.
Provisions exist for penalties and the trial of offences under the Act.

penalties: Section 47 specifies penalties for various offenses under the Act, which may include fines.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Reserve Bank of India and the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation appear to be the primary authorities involved in enforcement and oversight.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves registration of banks, oversight of their operations, investigation of contraventions, and imposition of penalties. The Reserve Bank has powers related to inspection and issuing directions.

rights: Depositors have the right to claim insured amounts from the Corporation in case of a bank's winding up or other specified circumstances.
duties: Banking companies and co-operative banks have a duty to be registered as insured banks.
Insured banks have duties related to payment of premiums.
The Corporation has a duty to insure deposits and guarantee credit facilities.
The Corporation has access to records of insured banks.
Directors have a duty of fidelity and secrecy.
obligations: Credit institutions that receive guarantees have obligations towards the Corporation.
In case of winding up or scheme of arrangement, liquidators or transferee banks have obligations to repay the Corporation.

key_procedures: Registration of banking companies and co-operative banks as insured banks.
Manner of payment by the Corporation to depositors in case of winding up of insured banks.
Manner of payment by the Corporation in case of schemes of compromise, arrangement, reconstruction, or amalgamation of insured banks.
Procedure for repayment of amounts to the Corporation by liquidators or transferee banks.
Procedures related to the audit of the Corporation's accounts.
administration: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation, with oversight and direction from the Central Government and the Reserve Bank of India.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1978 to include credit guarantee functions and expand the scope.
Certain provisions of the Companies Act, 1956 and the Insurance Act, 1938 do not apply to the Corporation.
Specific provisions exist for International Financial Services Centres.

title: THE FOREIGNERS LAW (APPLICATION AND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1962
purpose: To apply the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939 and the Foreigners Act, 1946 to certain persons to whom they do not at present apply and further to amend the Foreigners Act, 1946.
scope: This Act applies to any person, or any of their parents or grandparents, who were at any time a citizen or subject of a country at war with or committing external aggression against India, or a country assisting such a country. It extends the application of the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, and the Foreigners Act, 1946, to these individuals as if they were foreigners under those Acts.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the "Foreigners Law (Application and Amendment) Act, 1962."

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act 16 of 1939 and Act 31 of 1946 to certain persons
main_sections.description: Extends the provisions of the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, and the Foreigners Act, 1946, and their associated rules and orders, to individuals whose ancestry (self, parents, or grandparents) originated from countries at war with or committing aggression against India, or assisting such countries. These individuals are treated as foreigners for the purposes of these Acts.
This section, which presumably amended the Foreigners Act, 1946, has been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1974.

Repeals the Foreigners Law (Application and Amendment) Ordinance, 1962 (5 of 1962). It also stipulates that any actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are considered to have been taken under this Act, as if the Act commenced on October 26, 1962.

important_rules: Rule 1: The provisions of the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, and the Foreigners Act, 1946, and the rules and orders made thereunder, shall apply to persons who, or whose parents or grandparents, were citizens of countries at war with or committing aggression against India, or assisting such countries.
Rule 2: Such individuals are to be treated as foreigners for the purposes of the aforementioned Acts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be authorities responsible for enforcing the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, and the Foreigners Act, 1946.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By applying the provisions and enforcement mechanisms of the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, and the Foreigners Act, 1946.

obligations: Obligation to comply with the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, and the Foreigners Act, 1946, for individuals covered by Section 2.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application of existing foreigner registration and related laws to a defined group of individuals based on their national origin during times of conflict or aggression involving India.
Procedure 2: Repeal of a prior ordinance with a saving clause that validates past actions taken under it.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but likely falls under the Ministry of Home Affairs or a similar department responsible for internal security and foreigners' affairs.
important_notes: Note 1: Section 3 has been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 56 of 1974.
Note 2: Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance (5 of 1962) are deemed to have been taken under this Act, with a retrospective commencement date of October 26, 1962.

title: The Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of the right of user in land for laying pipelines for the transport of petroleum and minerals, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Extends to the whole of India, initially applicable to West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, and Delhi. The Central Government can extend its application to other states and union territories. It applies to land where pipelines for petroleum and minerals are proposed to be laid by the Central Government, State Governments, or corporations.

key_definitions.competent authority: Any person or authority authorized by the Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, to perform the functions of the competent authority under this Act. Different persons or authorities may be authorized for different areas or functions.
key_definitions.corporation: Any body corporate established under any Central, Provincial or State Act, including companies formed under the Companies Act, 1956, or any prior companies law.
key_definitions.minerals: As defined in the Mines Act, 1952, and includes mineral oils and stowing sand, but excludes petroleum.
key_definitions.petroleum: Has the same meaning as in the Petroleum Act, 1934, and includes natural gas and refinery gas.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir, with later application extended), and its initial application to specific states and union territories, with provisions for extension.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'competent authority', 'corporation', 'minerals', 'petroleum', and 'prescribed'.

Outlines the procedure for the Central Government to declare its intention to acquire the right of user in land for laying pipelines, requiring publication in the Official Gazette and notification to the public.

Grants authorized persons the power to enter land specified in the notification for surveying, taking levels, digging, marking, and performing other acts necessary to ascertain the feasibility of laying pipelines, with a duty to cause minimal damage.

Allows any person interested in the land to object to the laying of pipelines within twenty-one days of the notification, requiring written objections and providing an opportunity for a hearing. The competent authority's decision on objections is final.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of acquisition of right of user
main_sections.description: Describes the process of acquiring the right of user. If no objections are raised or if objections are disallowed, the competent authority reports to the Central Government, which, if satisfied, declares the acquisition of the right of user through an Official Gazette notification. The right vests absolutely in the Central Government, or can be directed to vest in a State Government or corporation. Time limits for notification and declaration are specified.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government or State Government or corporation to lay pipelines
main_sections.description: States that where the right of user has vested, authorized persons can enter the land to lay pipelines. It prohibits laying pipelines under residential land, land with permanent structures, land appurtenant to dwelling houses, or at a depth less than one meter. It also allows for the use of land for transporting other minerals or petroleum if the initial purpose was different. Disputes regarding certain prohibitions are referred to the competent authority.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter land for inspection, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants authorized persons the power to enter land for maintaining, examining, repairing, altering, or removing pipelines, or for inspections, with reasonable notice to the occupier, unless an emergency exists. Minimal damage is to be caused.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions regarding the use of land
main_sections.description: Restricts the owner or occupier from constructing buildings, structures, tanks, wells, reservoirs, dams, or planting trees on land where the right of user has been acquired. It also prohibits any act that could damage the pipeline. Contravention can lead to removal or filling up of such constructions by the District Judge, with costs recoverable from the owner/occupier.
Deals with compensation payable to any person interested in the land for any damage, loss, or injury sustained due to the exercise of powers under sections 4, 7, or 8.

important_rules: Rule: Any person authorized by the Central Government, State Government, or corporation can enter land for surveying, taking levels, digging, marking boundaries, and performing other necessary acts to ascertain the feasibility of laying pipelines, causing minimal damage.

Rule: Persons interested in the land have 21 days from the notification date to file written objections regarding pipeline laying, with an opportunity for a hearing. The competent authority's decision on objections is final.
Rule: Land where the right of user is acquired can only be used for laying, maintaining, examining, repairing, altering, or removing pipelines, and for their utilization.

Rule: Owners or occupiers of land with acquired right of user cannot construct buildings, structures, tanks, wells, reservoirs, dams, or plant trees on that land, nor can they permit any act that damages the pipeline.
Rule: Compensation is payable for any damage, loss, or injury sustained by persons interested in the land due to the exercise of powers related to pipeline laying and maintenance.

penalties: Penalty for contravening restrictions on land use: The District Judge may order removal of unauthorized constructions or filling up of wells/tanks, with costs recoverable from the owner/occupier.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority, Central Government, State Governments, Corporations, and District Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, authorized entry for surveys and pipeline laying, hearing of objections, declaration of acquisition, imposition of restrictions, and legal proceedings for contraventions.

rights: Right to use the land for its original purpose, subject to restrictions.
Right to receive compensation for damage, loss, or injury.
Right to be heard in case of objections to pipeline laying.
duties: Duty to allow entry for survey and pipeline laying activities.
Duty to cause minimal damage during survey and construction.
Duty of owners/occupiers to adhere to restrictions on land use.
Duty to not damage pipelines.
obligations: Obligation to publish notifications and publicize acquisition intentions.
Obligation to hear objections and make decisions.
Obligation to pay compensation for damages.

key_procedures: Procedure for Acquisition of Right of User: Issuance of notification of intention, public notification, survey and inspection of land, hearing of objections, reporting to Central Government, declaration of acquisition, and vesting of right of user.
Procedure for Laying Pipelines: Authorized persons can enter land after right of user vests to lay, maintain, and repair pipelines, subject to specific prohibitions.

Procedure for Enforcing Land Use Restrictions: Competent authority applies to the District Judge for removal of unauthorized constructions or filling of wells/tanks on land with acquired right of user.
administration: Central Government, State Governments, and authorized Corporations.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1977, introducing significant changes including changes to the definition of minerals, extension of the Act to include minerals alongside petroleum, and stricter time limits for declarations.
The Act was extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh via notification in 2019.
Specific prohibitions exist regarding laying pipelines under residential land, land with permanent structures, land appurtenant to dwelling houses, or at shallow depths.
The Act provides for penalties for violations of land use restrictions.

title: THE WAREHOUSING CORPORATIONS ACT, 1962
purpose: To provide for the incorporation and regulation of corporations for the purpose of warehousing of agricultural produce and certain other commodities and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the Central Warehousing Corporation and State Warehousing Corporations, and covers the warehousing of 'agricultural produce' and 'notified commodities'.

key_definitions.agricultural produce: Includes foodstuffs, cattle fodder, raw cotton, raw jute, and vegetable oils.
key_definitions.appropriate government: Central Government for the Central Warehousing Corporation, and State Government for a State Warehousing Corporation.
key_definitions.co-operative society: A society registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, engaged in processing, marketing, storage, export or import of agricultural produce or any notified commodity, or in insurance business.
key_definitions.notified commodity: Any commodity (other than agricultural produce) declared by the Central Government to be a notified commodity for the purposes of this Act, within Parliament's legislative competence.
key_definitions.warehousing corporation: A Warehousing Corporation established or deemed to be established under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the provision for commencement through notification by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'agricultural produce', 'appropriate Government', 'Central Warehousing Corporation', 'co-operative society', 'notified commodity', and 'Warehousing Corporation'.

Establishes the Central Warehousing Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and powers to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract. It also specifies the head office.

Details the authorized share capital of the Central Warehousing Corporation, the proportion to be subscribed by the Central Government and other institutions (State Bank, scheduled banks, co-operative societies, etc.), and restrictions on share transfer.

main_sections.section_title: Shares to be guaranteed by Central Government and to be trust or approved securities
main_sections.description: States that shares of the Central Warehousing Corporation are guaranteed by the Central Government regarding principal repayment and dividend. It also specifies that these shares are deemed to be trust or approved securities under relevant Acts.

Vests the general superintendence and management of the Corporation's affairs in a board of directors, assisted by an Executive Committee and a managing director. The board is to act on business principles, guided by Central Government policy.

Outlines the composition of the board of directors for the Central Warehousing Corporation, including directors nominated or elected by the Central Government, State Bank, scheduled banks, co-operative societies, and other financial institutions, as well as a managing director.

Specifies the functions of the Central Warehousing Corporation, which include acquiring, holding, and dealing with agricultural produce, notified commodities, and other goods. It also mentions the power to carry on the business of warehousing.
Provides for the establishment of State Warehousing Corporations.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the State Warehousing Corporation
main_sections.description: Details the functions of the State Warehousing Corporation, similar to the Central Warehousing Corporation but at the state level.

main_sections.section_title: Submission of programme of activities and financial estimates
main_sections.description: Requires the Warehousing Corporations to submit their program of activities and financial estimates.
Grants borrowing powers to the Warehousing Corporations.

main_sections.section_title: Accounts and audit of Warehousing Corporation
main_sections.description: Deals with the accounts and audit of the Warehousing Corporations.
Provides for the winding up of Warehousing Corporations.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Warehousing Corporations to make regulations
main_sections.description: Grants Warehousing Corporations the power to make regulations.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: The Central Warehousing Corporation shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Shares of the Central Warehousing Corporation are guaranteed by the Central Government and are considered trust/approved securities.
The Central Warehousing Corporation's board of directors shall act on business principles, guided by Central Government policy.
State Warehousing Corporations are to be established for each State.
Warehousing Corporations are required to submit programs of activities and financial estimates.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (by the Corporations).
Right to contract (by the Corporations).
Shareholders' right to dividend and repayment of principal (guaranteed by Central Govt. for CWC shares).
duties: Duty to act on business principles (Board of Directors of CWC).
Duty to be guided by Central Government policy (Board of Directors of CWC).
Duty to maintain two funds (Warehousing Fund and General Fund) by the Corporation.
Duty to prepare and submit programs of activities and financial estimates.
Duty to maintain accounts and undergo audit.
obligations: Obligation to subscribe to share capital as specified.
Obligation for the Central Government to subscribe for 40% of the share capital of the Central Warehousing Corporation.
Obligation for the Central Government to guarantee shares of the Central Warehousing Corporation.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Central Warehousing Corporation by notification.
Subscription of share capital by the Central Government and other specified institutions.
Nomination and election of directors to the board.
Submission of program of activities and financial estimates by Corporations.
Making of rules by the Central Government and regulations by the Corporations.
administration: Central Warehousing Corporation is managed by a board of directors and administered by the Central Government for policy guidance. State Warehousing Corporations are managed similarly at the state level, with the State Government providing guidance. The Act generally allows for Central Government rules and Corporation regulations for administration.
important_notes: The Act was originally not applicable to the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but this was later omitted.
The definition of 'nationalised bank' was added subsequently.
The definition of 'notified commodity' includes a condition related to Parliament's power to legislate on such commodities.
Specific dates for commencement and amendments are provided in footnotes.

title: THE CARDAMOM ACT, 1965
purpose: To provide for the development under the control of the Union of the cardamom industry.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, with a specific provision that it does not apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir except for its provisions relating to the control of export and import of cardamom. It can be brought into force on different dates for different provisions.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act (The Cardamom Act, 1965), its territorial extent (whole of India, with an exception for Jammu and Kashmir concerning export/import control), and the commencement date which is to be appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
main_sections.description: Declares that it is in the public interest for the Union to control the cardamom industry.
Repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act (10 of 1986).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (implied by the declaration of control and power to appoint commencement dates).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette for commencement and potentially through the provisions related to control of export and import.

administration: Central Government (implied)
important_notes: Most of the Act's Chapters and Sections (Chapters II to VI, and Sections 3 to 33) have been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act (10 of 1986) with effect from February 26, 1987. This indicates that the original provisions related to the Cardamom Board, registration of owners, finance, accounts, audit, control by the Central Government, and miscellaneous provisions are no longer in effect.

The provisions related to the control of export of cardamom from India and import thereof into India were made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019. This suggests that even though most of the act is repealed, some aspects of control related to international trade might still be relevant or were intended to be preserved in specific contexts.

title: THE JAMMU AND KASHMIR REPRESENTATION OF THE PEOPLE (SUPPLEMENTARY) ACT, 1968
purpose: To supplement the Jammu and Kashmir Representation of the People Act, 1957, by extending certain provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to orders made by the Jammu and Kashmir High Court.
scope: Applies to orders made by the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir. It specifically makes sections 116A, 116B, and 116C of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, applicable with modifications to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Jammu and Kashmir Representation of the People (Supplementary) Act, 1968, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on February 9, 1968.

main_sections.section_title: Application of sections 116A, 116B and 116C of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to orders made by Jammu and Kashmir High Court
main_sections.description: Extends the application of sections 116A, 116B, and 116C of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to every order made by the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir. It specifies modifications for references to the High Court, State Legislature, Speaker/Chairman, and provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, in relation to Jammu and Kashmir.

Repeals the Jammu and Kashmir Representation of the People (Supplementary) Ordinance, 1968 (2 of 1968). It also provides a saving clause, stating that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and relevant authorities overseeing election petitions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By applying the provisions of Sections 116A, 116B, and 116C of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, with modifications.

administration: Not explicitly stated, but related to the administration of election law in Jammu and Kashmir.
important_notes: The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.

title: THE BORDER SECURITY FORCE ACT, 1968
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an Armed Force of the Union for ensuring the security of the borders of India and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to all officers, subordinate officers, under-officers, and other persons enrolled under the Border Security Force, within India and potentially outside India. It covers the constitution, conditions of service, offences, punishments, arrest, trial procedures, confirmation, revision, and execution of sentences related to the Border Security Force.

key_definitions.active_duty: Any duty as a member of the Force during the period such person is attached to, or forms part of, a unit of the Force that is engaged in operations against an enemy, or is operating at a picket, engaged on patrol, or other guard duty along the borders of India. It also includes duty during any period declared by the Central Government as active duty with reference to any area where persons subject to this Act may be serving.
key_definitions.civil_offence: An offence which is triable by a criminal court.
key_definitions.enemy: Includes all armed mutineers, armed rebels, armed rioters, pirates, and any person in arms against whom it is the duty of any person subject to this Act to take action.
key_definitions.member_of_the_Force: Means an officer, a subordinate officer, an under-officer or other enrolled person.
key_definitions.offence: Means any act or omission punishable under this Act and includes a civil offence.
key_definitions.Security_Force_Court: Means a court referred to in section 64.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Border Security Force Act, 1968, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

This section defines various terms used throughout the Act, including 'active duty', 'civil offence', 'enemy', 'Force', 'member of the Force', 'offence', and 'Security Force Court', among others. It also addresses references to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir.

This section outlines who is subject to the Act, including officers, subordinate officers, under-officers, and other enrolled persons. It also states that they remain subject until retired, discharged, released, removed, or dismissed from the Force.

This section establishes the Border Security Force as an armed force of the Union for ensuring the security of India's borders. It states that the Force shall be constituted and its members' conditions of service shall be as prescribed.

This section vests the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Force in the Central Government. The command and supervision are vested in a Director-General appointed by the Central Government, who is assisted by other prescribed officers.

This section details that the persons to be enrolled, the mode of enrolment, and the procedure for enrolment shall be as prescribed by the Central Government. It also deems any person receiving pay for three continuous months as enrolled.
This section states that every member of the Force is liable to serve in any part of India as well as outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation and withdrawal from the post
main_sections.description: This section prohibits any member of the Force from resigning their appointment or withdrawing from their duties without the prior written permission of the prescribed authority.

main_sections.section_title: Tenure of service under the Act
main_sections.description: This section states that every person subject to this Act holds office during the pleasure of the President.

main_sections.section_title: Termination of service by Central Government
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Central Government to dismiss or remove from service any person subject to the Act, subject to the Act's provisions and rules.

main_sections.section_title: Dismissal, removal or reduction by the Director-General and by other officers
main_sections.description: This section grants the Director-General or any Inspector-General the power to dismiss, remove from service, or reduce to a lower grade or rank any person subject to the Act, other than an officer.

main_sections.section_title: Offences in relation to the enemy and punishable with death
main_sections.description: This section, and subsequent sections in Chapter III, detail various offences that members of the Force can commit, ranging from offences against the enemy to violations of good order and discipline.

main_sections.section_title: Punishments awardable by Security Force Courts
main_sections.description: This section, and subsequent sections in Chapter IV, outline the punishments that can be awarded by Security Force Courts.
This section, and subsequent sections in Chapter V, cover the procedures for the custody of offenders and proceedings before trial.
This section, and subsequent sections in Chapter VI, describe the different kinds of Security Force Courts and their powers.
This section, and subsequent sections in Chapter VII, detail the procedures to be followed by Security Force Courts during trials.

main_sections.section_title: Finding and sentence not valid, unless confirmed
main_sections.description: This section, and subsequent sections in Chapter VIII, deal with the confirmation and revision of findings and sentences of Security Force Courts.
This section, and subsequent sections in Chapter IX, cover the execution of sentences, pardons, remissions, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties conferrable and imposable on members of the Force
main_sections.description: This section, and subsequent sections in Chapter X, address miscellaneous provisions, including powers and duties of members, protection for acts, rule-making powers, and provisions for existing Border Security Force.

important_rules: Rule 1: No member of the Force shall resign their appointment or withdraw from their duties without the prior written permission of the prescribed authority.
Rule 2: Every person subject to this Act holds office during the pleasure of the President.
Rule 3: Any person subject to this Act who commits an offence specified in Chapter III shall be liable to punishment as prescribed, which may include death, imprisonment, or other penalties.
Rule 4: Findings and sentences of Security Force Courts are not valid unless confirmed by the prescribed authority.
Rule 5: Sentences awarded by Security Force Courts must be executed according to the provisions of Chapter IX.

penalties: Punishments awardable by Security Force Courts include death, imprisonment (rigorous or simple), forfeiture of pay, dismissal from the Force, reduction in rank, and such other punishments as may be prescribed.
Minor punishments may be awarded by Commandants and other officers for certain minor offences.
Collective fines may be imposed on a group or body of persons subject to this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Border Security Force, its command structure (Director-General, Inspector-Generals, Commandants), and Security Force Courts are responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement occurs through the investigation of offences, arrest of offenders, trial by Security Force Courts, confirmation and revision of sentences, and execution of punishments. Civil authorities may also be involved in certain circumstances.

rights: Right to hold office during the pleasure of the President (subject to the Act).
Right to fair trial by a Security Force Court (as per procedures outlined).
duties: Duty to ensure the security of the borders of India.
Duty to obey lawful commands of superior officers.
Duty to maintain good order and discipline.
Duty to report offences and irregularities.
Duty to perform service anywhere in India and outside India as required.
obligations: Obligation to remain subject to the Act until lawfully retired, discharged, released, removed, or dismissed.
Obligation to adhere to the prescribed conditions of service.
Obligation to not resign or withdraw from duties without permission.

key_procedures: Enrolment: Persons are enrolled in the Force according to prescribed procedures.
Arrest and Custody: Procedures for the arrest and custody of offenders are detailed in Chapter V.
Security Force Court Proceedings: Includes convening courts, composition of courts, evidence rules, challenges, and trial procedures as outlined in Chapters VI and VII.
Confirmation and Revision: Findings and sentences of Security Force Courts are subject to confirmation and revision as per Chapter VIII.
Execution of Sentence: Procedures for carrying out sentences, including imprisonment and fines, are detailed in Chapter IX.
administration: The Central Government exercises general superintendence, direction, and control. The Director-General of the Force, assisted by Inspectors-General, Deputy Inspectors-General, Commandants, and other officers, manages the Force.
important_notes: The Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh as of October 30, 2019.
References to any law not in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir are construed as references to the corresponding law in force in that State.
The Act contains a comprehensive list of offences and corresponding punishments, covering a wide range of misconduct.

title: THE DIPLOMATIC AND CONSULAR OFFICERS (OATHS AND FEES) (EXTENSION TO JAMMU AND KASHMIR) ACT, 1973
purpose: To provide for the extension of the Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948 to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Jammu and Kashmir and, as per a notification in 2019, to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh. It extends the provisions of the Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948 to these regions.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 1973, and states that it comes into force at once.

Extends the Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948 (principal Act) to and in relation to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It also states that the provisions of the principal Act and its rules will apply to Jammu and Kashmir as they do to any other State, and omits clause (d) of section 2 of the principal Act.
This section, which referred to an amendment of section 8, was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1978.

important_rules: The Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948, and the rules made thereunder, shall apply to and in relation to the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh) in the same way as they apply to and in relation to any other State.
Clause (d) of section 2 of the principal Act (Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948) shall be omitted in its application to Jammu and Kashmir.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but would likely be the relevant authorities responsible for the administration of the principal Act and its extensions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By applying the provisions of the Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948, to the extended territories.

administration: The administration of this act would fall under the purview of the Indian Parliament and the executive branches responsible for implementing laws related to diplomatic and consular affairs.
important_notes: The Act was extended to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Vide Notification No. S.O. 3912 (E), dated 30th October, 2019, this Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

title: The Parliamentary Proceedings (Protection of Publication) Act, 1977
purpose: To protect the publication of reports of proceedings of Parliament.
scope: Applies to the whole of India, with a specific exclusion for the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh). It covers publications in newspapers and broadcasts by wireless telegraphy related to Parliamentary proceedings.

key_definitions.newspaper: Any printed periodical work containing public news or comments on public news, and includes a news agency supplying material for publication in a newspaper.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date from which it is deemed to have come into force.
Defines the term 'newspaper' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of reports of Parliamentary proceedings privileged
main_sections.description: Establishes that publications of substantially true reports of Parliamentary proceedings in newspapers are privileged from civil or criminal proceedings, unless proven to be made with malice or not for the public good.

main_sections.section_title: Act also to apply to Parliamentary proceedings broadcast by wireless telegraphy
main_sections.description: Extends the provisions of the Act to cover reports or matters broadcast by means of wireless telegraphy from broadcasting stations within the territorial limits of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Publication of a substantially true report of any Parliamentary proceedings in a newspaper is privileged from civil or criminal proceedings.
Rule 2: The privilege under Rule 1 does not apply if the publication is proved to have been made with malice.
Rule 3: The privilege under Rule 1 does not apply to the publication of any matter that is not for the public good.
Rule 4: The Act's provisions apply equally to reports or matters broadcast by wireless telegraphy from broadcasting stations within the Act's extent.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of law in India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through civil or criminal proceedings in courts, where the defense of privilege can be raised for publications of Parliamentary proceedings.

rights: Right to publish substantially true reports of Parliamentary proceedings in newspapers without liability, provided certain conditions are met.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that the publication is not made with malice.
Obligation to ensure that the publication is for the public good.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: A person publishing a report of Parliamentary proceedings in a newspaper can claim privilege from civil or criminal proceedings in a court.
Procedure 2: If the publication is challenged, the court will determine if the report was substantially true, published in a newspaper, and if it was made with malice or not for the public good.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely falls under the purview of the Ministry of Law and Justice or a similar legislative affairs department.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on March 25, 1977.
The Act has been made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

title: The Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital (Acquisition) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1977
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and for the management of the Kalavati Saran Hospital, with a view to ensuring better facilities for higher medical education for women and medical facilities for women and children in the Union territory of Delhi and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the Union territory of Delhi. Specifically concerns the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and the Kalavati Saran Hospital. It impacts the Central Government, the existing administration of these institutions, their officers and employees, and their properties and assets.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which the Act comes into force.
key_definitions.Board_of_Administration: The Board of Administration constituted by the Central Government under the Scheme.
key_definitions.Board_of_Management: The Board of Management of the Kalavati Saran Hospital, constituted by the Central Government.
key_definitions.Fund: The Lady Hardinge Hospital for Women and Children, Delhi, Fund established by the Scheme.
key_definitions.Kalavati_Saran_Hospital: The institution known as the Kalavati Saran Children's Hospital, New Delhi, including attached dispensaries, laboratories, and libraries.
key_definitions.Lady_Hardinge_Medical_College_and_Hospit: The institutions known as the Lady Hardinge Medical College for Women, New Delhi, and the Lady Hardinge Hospital for Women and Children, New Delhi, including attached dispensaries, lecture-rooms, museums, laboratories, libraries, hostels, and boarding-houses.
key_definitions.Scheme: The Scheme for the administration of the Fund settled by the Central Government under the Charitable Endowments Act, 1890.
key_definitions.Treasurer: The Treasurer of Charitable Endowments for India, appointed under the Charitable Endowments Act, 1890.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and the provision for its commencement on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board of Administration', 'Board of Management', 'Fund', 'Kalavati Saran Hospital', 'Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital', 'Scheme', and 'Treasurer'.

main_sections.section_title: Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital to vest in Central Government
main_sections.description: Details the vesting of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital, including its lands, buildings, equipment, assets, liabilities, and rights, in the Central Government on the appointed day. It also clarifies the construction of related deeds and documents and the discharge of the property from trusts and incumbrances. Pending legal proceedings are transferred to the Central Government.

Specifies that the Central Government shall pay an amount of rupees one lakh to the Treasurer for the acquisition of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital. This payment is to be made within three months of the appointed day, with interest accruing if delayed.

main_sections.section_title: Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital to be administered as Government institution
main_sections.description: Declares that from the appointed day, the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital will be administered by the Central Government as a Government institution, with regard to the purposes specified in the Scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Kalavati Saran Hospital to be managed as Government institution
main_sections.description: States that from the appointed day, the Kalavati Saran Hospital shall be managed by the Central Government as a Government institution, notwithstanding any contractual provisions to the contrary. The management will consider the original purposes for which the hospital was set up, and the Board of Management shall stand dissolved.

main_sections.section_title: Act to override all other enactments
main_sections.description: Establishes that the provisions of this Act will prevail over any inconsistent provisions in any other law, instrument, decree, or order.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions relating to officers and other employees of Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and Kalavati Saran Hospital
main_sections.description: Outlines the transfer of officers and employees of both institutions to the Central Government on the appointed day, retaining their existing terms and conditions. It provides for termination of employment under certain conditions and compensation. It also states that the transfer of services does not entitle employees to compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and substitutes trustees for provident/gratuity funds.

Specifies a penalty for contravention of any provision of the Act or rules made thereunder. The penalty is imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: The Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital, along with its properties and liabilities, shall vest in the Central Government on the appointed day.
Rule: The Central Government shall pay an amount of rupees one lakh to the Treasurer for the acquisition of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital.
Rule: The Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital shall be administered by the Central Government as a Government institution.
Rule: The Kalavati Saran Hospital shall be managed by the Central Government as a Government institution.
Rule: Officers and employees of the acquired institutions shall become employees of the Central Government, retaining their terms and conditions, with provisions for termination and compensation.
Rule: All existing contracts, deeds, and agreements related to the institutions shall continue to be in force in favour of the Central Government.
Rule: Contracts made in bad faith or detrimental to the interests of the institutions can be cancelled or varied by the Central Government.
Rule: Possession of property must be delivered to the Central Government upon demand.
Rule: Any person contravening the Act or rules is liable to imprisonment or fine.
Rule: The Central Government has the power to make rules to implement the Act.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months.
Fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
Both imprisonment and fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including vesting of property, transfer of employees, and the power to make rules. Offences can be taken cognizance of by a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class.

rights: The Central Government has the right to acquire the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and manage the Kalavati Saran Hospital.
Employees have the right to continue their employment with the same tenure, remuneration, and terms and conditions, or to receive compensation upon termination under specific conditions.
The Central Government has the right to cancel or vary contracts made in bad faith.
The Central Government has the right to demand delivery of possession of property.
duties: The Central Government has a duty to pay the acquisition amount to the Treasurer.
The Central Government has a duty to administer the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and manage the Kalavati Saran Hospital with regard to their specified purposes.
The Central Government has a duty to ensure that officers and employees retain their rights and privileges.
obligations: The Central Government is obligated to uphold the purpose of ensuring better medical education and facilities.
The Central Government is obligated to manage the institutions in accordance with the Scheme and original purposes.
Officers and employees have an obligation to deliver property and cooperate with the transition, unless they opt out.

key_procedures: Procedure: Commencement of the Act: The Central Government issues a notification in the Official Gazette appointing a date for the Act to come into force.

Procedure: Acquisition and Vesting: On the appointed day, the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital, along with all its associated properties and liabilities, automatically vests in the Central Government.
Procedure: Payment of Acquisition Amount: The Central Government pays rupees one lakh to the Treasurer within three months of the appointed day. Interest applies if payment is delayed.

Procedure: Administration/Management: The Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital is administered by the Central Government as a Government institution. The Kalavati Saran Hospital is managed as a Government institution.

Procedure: Employee Transition: Officers and employees become employees of the Central Government, retaining their existing terms, unless they opt out or their terms are altered. Provisions exist for termination and compensation.
Procedure: Handling of Legal Proceedings: Pending legal actions related to the institutions are continued by or against the Central Government.
Procedure: Cancellation/Variation of Contracts: The Central Government can cancel or vary contracts made in bad faith.
Procedure: Delivery of Possession: Individuals in possession of property must deliver it to the Central Government upon demand.
Procedure: Rule Making: The Central Government can make rules to carry out the Act's purposes.
Procedure: Enforcement of Offences: Offences are investigated, and legal proceedings initiated as per the Act, with cognizance taken by specific magistrates.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act overrides all other inconsistent enactments.
The acquisition amount of rupees one lakh is a fixed sum and not necessarily reflective of market value.
Employees who do not wish to become employees of the Central Government must provide written notice within thirty days of the appointed day.
The Act ensures that the properties are freed from trusts, mortgages, liens, and other incumbrances upon vesting in the Central Government.
The management of both institutions is to be guided by their original purposes and the established Scheme.

title: The Interest Act, 1978
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the allowance of interest in certain cases.
scope: Applies to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh). It governs the allowance of interest in legal proceedings concerning debts and damages.

key_definitions.court: Includes a tribunal and an arbitrator.
key_definitions.current_rate_of_interest: The highest of the maximum rates at which interest may be paid on different classes of deposits (excluding savings accounts and those maintained by charitable or religious institutions) by different classes of scheduled banks, as per Reserve Bank of India directions.
key_definitions.debt: A liability for an ascertained sum of money, including a debt payable in kind, but excluding a judgment debt.
key_definitions.personal_injuries: Includes any disease and any impairment of a person’s physical or mental condition.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir, now extended), and the date of commencement.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'court', 'current rate of interest', 'debt', and 'personal injuries'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of court to allow interest
main_sections.description: Grants the court the power to allow interest on debts or damages in certain proceedings, specifying the periods for which interest can be awarded and conditions for its allowance, especially in cases of personal injuries.

States that interest is payable in cases where it is already payable by virtue of any enactment or other rule of law or usage. It also specifies situations where the court shall allow interest, such as in cases of security deposits, fiduciary relationships, fraud, or claims for dower or maintenance.

main_sections.section_title: Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to apply
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, are not affected by this Act.
Repeals the Interest Act, 1839, and any corresponding laws. It also provides savings for suits and legal proceedings pending at the commencement of this Act.

important_rules: Interest can be allowed by a court on debts or damages at a rate not exceeding the current rate of interest.
Interest on debts payable by written instrument can be awarded from the date the debt is payable to the date of institution of proceedings.
Interest on debts not related to written instruments can be awarded from the date mentioned in a written notice claiming interest to the date of institution of proceedings.
Interest shall not be allowed for the period after repayment of the debt or damages before the institution of proceedings.
In cases of personal injuries, interest on damages exceeding four thousand rupees shall be included in the judgment unless there are special reasons.
Interest is payable where it is already payable by virtue of any enactment, rule of law, or usage.
Interest shall be allowed on security deposits from the date of deposit.
Interest shall be allowed on obligations arising from a fiduciary relationship from the date of the cause of action.
Interest shall be allowed where money or property is obtained or retained by fraud, from the date of the cause of action.
Interest shall be allowed for claims of dower or maintenance from the date of the cause of action.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, tribunals, and arbitrators.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial proceedings for the recovery of debts and damages where interest can be awarded or is mandated by law.

rights: Right to claim interest on debts or damages in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
Right to receive interest on security deposits, fiduciary obligations, fraud, dower, or maintenance claims.
Right to claim interest as per existing enactments or rules of law.
duties: Duty to pay interest when legally obligated, as determined by the court or statute.
Duty to provide for interest in written instruments where specified.
obligations: Obligation to pay interest on debts or damages under specified circumstances as per the Act.
Obligation to allow interest in cases mandated by other enactments or rules of law.

key_procedures: Initiating proceedings for the recovery of debt or damages where interest is claimed.
Providing written notice to the liable party claiming interest, if the debt is not payable by a written instrument.
Court determining the entitlement to interest, the rate, and the period for which it is payable based on the evidence and provisions of the Act.
Court exercising its power to allow interest, considering conditions and exceptions outlined in Section 3.
Court allowing interest in specific cases mentioned in Section 4 (security deposits, fiduciary relations, fraud, dower/maintenance) unless special reasons exist not to.
Application of Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in relevant proceedings.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be administered through the judiciary (courts, tribunals, arbitrators) under the purview of relevant government ministries overseeing legal affairs.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to any debt or damages upon which interest is payable as of right by agreement, or where payment of interest is barred by express agreement.
The Act does not affect compensation recoverable for the dishonour of negotiable instruments or the provisions of Order II, Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
The court is not empowered to award interest upon interest.
The Act's provisions do not apply to suits or legal proceedings pending at its commencement; the corresponding law applicable before commencement will continue to apply.

title: The Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980
purpose: To provide for the conservation of forests and for matters connected therewith or ancillary or incidental thereto, with objectives including achievement of national targets of Net Zero Emission, maintaining or enhancing forest carbon stocks, creating carbon sinks, increasing forest and tree cover, preserving biodiversity, and enhancing forest-based economic, social, and environmental benefits.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to land declared or notified as forest, or recorded as forest in government records as of October 25, 1980, with specific exclusions for certain categories of land.

key_definitions.reserved_forest: Reserved forest within the meaning of any law for the time being in force in a State.
key_definitions.non_forest_purpose: The breaking up or clearing of any forest land or portion thereof for cultivation of specific crops, or any purpose other than reafforestation, but excluding works relating to forest and wildlife conservation, development, and management as specified in the Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980', its extent to the whole of India, and its deemed commencement date of October 25, 1980.

Specifies the types of land covered by the Act, including legally declared forests and lands recorded as forest in government records, and lists categories of land excluded from the Act's provisions, such as land alongside roads for access, certain tree plantations, and specific strategic or security-related projects.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on the dereservation of forests or use of forest land for non-forest purpose.
main_sections.description: Prohibits State Governments or other authorities from dereserving reserved forests or using forest land for non-forest purposes without prior approval from the Central Government. It also restricts assignment of forest land by lease or otherwise to private entities and clearing of naturally grown trees for reafforestation without prior approval.
Allows any person aggrieved by an order or decision of a State Government or other authority made under section 2 to file an appeal to the National Green Tribunal.
Empowers the Central Government to constitute an Advisory Committee to advise on matters related to granting approval under section 2 and other forest conservation issues.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
main_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty of simple imprisonment up to fifteen days for contravening or abetting the contravention of the provisions of section 2.

main_sections.section_title: Offences by authorities and Government departments.
