main_sections.description: Deals with offences committed by government departments and authorities, holding the head of the department or responsible persons liable, with provisions for exculpation if due diligence is proven. It also holds officers or persons responsible if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions for the implementation of the Act to various governmental authorities and recognized organizations.
Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, with a requirement for laying such rules before both Houses of Parliament for modification or annulment.
Repeals the Forest (Conservation) Ordinance, 1980, and provides that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: No State Government or other authority shall dereserve reserved forest or use forest land for non-forest purposes without prior approval of the Central Government.
Forest land or any portion thereof cannot be assigned by lease or otherwise to any private person or organization without prior approval and adherence to specified terms and conditions.
Clearing of naturally grown trees in forest land for reafforestation requires prior approval from the Central Government.
Specific categories of land, such as those alongside roads for access or for strategic projects, are excluded from the Act's provisions.
Penalties are prescribed for contravening the provisions of section 2, including simple imprisonment.

penalties: Simple imprisonment for a period which may extend to fifteen days for contravention or abetment of contravention of Section 2.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, State Governments, and other authorities as per their respective roles and powers under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through restrictions on dereservation and use of forest land, requiring prior approval from the Central Government for such actions, and through penalties for contravention. The National Green Tribunal hears appeals against orders and decisions.

rights: Right to appeal to the National Green Tribunal against orders or decisions of State Government or other authorities made under section 2.
duties: Duty of State Governments and other authorities to obtain prior approval of the Central Government before dereserving forests or using forest land for non-forest purposes.
Duty to comply with terms and conditions specified by the Central Government for assignment of forest land.
Duty to ensure that actions taken do not contravene the provisions of Section 2.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Act regarding forest conservation and management.
Obligation for government departments and authorities to prevent the commission of offences under the Act and to ensure due diligence.

key_procedures: Obtaining prior approval from the Central Government for any order directing that reserved forest shall cease to be reserved, or that forest land may be used for a non-forest purpose.
Filing an appeal to the National Green Tribunal against an order or decision of the State Government or other authority made under section 2.
Constitution of an Advisory Committee by the Central Government to advise on matters related to section 2 and forest conservation.
Making of rules by the Central Government and their subsequent laying before Parliament.
administration: Central Government, with advisory support from an Advisory Committee. State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are also involved in implementation.
important_notes: The Act was amended significantly by the Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 (Act 15 of 2023).
The exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir was removed by Act 34 of 2019.
Certain categories of land and projects are explicitly excluded from the purview of the Act.
The Act is designed to align with national targets for Net Zero Emission and carbon sinks.

title: The Company Secretaries Act, 1980
purpose: To make provision for the regulation and development of the profession of Company Secretaries.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to persons who are members of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India and regulates the profession of Company Secretaries.

key_definitions.Associate: An Associate Member of the Institute.
key_definitions.Authority: The Appellate Authority referred to in section 22A.
key_definitions.Board: The Quality Review Board constituted under section 29A.
key_definitions.Board of Discipline: The Board of Discipline constituted under sub-section (1) of section 21A.
key_definitions.Companies Act: The Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013) or any other previous company law as defined in clause (67) of section 2 of the said Act.
key_definitions.Company Secretary: A person who is a member of the Institute.
key_definitions.Council: The Council of the Institute constituted under section 9.
key_definitions.Director (Discipline): The Director (Discipline) referred to in section 21 and includes Joint Director (Discipline).
key_definitions.Disciplinary Committee: The Disciplinary Committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 21B.
key_definitions.Disciplinary Directorate: The Disciplinary Directorate established under sub-section (1) of section 21.
key_definitions.dissolved company: The Institute of Company Secretaries of India registered under the Companies Act.
key_definitions.Fellow: A Fellow Member of the Institute.
key_definitions.firm: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (9 of 1932), and includes a limited liability partnership or a sole proprietorship registered with the Institute.
key_definitions.Institute: The Institute of Company Secretaries of India constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.partner: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (9 of 1932) or in clause (q) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 (6 of 2009), as the case may be.
key_definitions.partnership: A partnership as defined in section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (9 of 1932); or a limited liability partnership which has no company as its partner.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.Register: The Register of members of the Institute maintained under section 19 or the Register of firms of the Institute maintained under section 20B, as the case may be.
key_definitions.sole proprietorship: An individual who engages himself in the practice of the profession of the company secretaries or offers to perform services referred to in clauses (b) to (f) of sub-section (2).
key_definitions.specified: Specified by rules made by the Central Government under this Act.
key_definitions.Standing Committee: The Standing Committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 17.
key_definitions.Tribunal: A Tribunal established under sub-section (1) of section 10B.
key_definitions.year: The period commencing on the 1st day of April of any year and ending on the 31st day of March of the succeeding year.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the procedure for its commencement via notification in the Official Gazette.

This section defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Associate', 'Fellow', 'Company Secretary', 'Institute', 'Council', 'Companies Act', and others. It also defines 'to be in practice' for members of the Institute.

This section constitutes the Institute of Company Secretaries of India as a body corporate, with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowering it to acquire and dispose of property and sue or be sued.

main_sections.section_title: Entry of names in the Register of members
main_sections.description: This section outlines the eligibility criteria for individuals to have their names entered in the Register of members of the Institute, including former members of the dissolved company, diploma holders, and those who pass prescribed examinations and training.

This section categorizes members into Associates and Fellows. It states that a person whose name is entered in the Register is deemed an Associate and entitled to use 'A.C.S.' after their name. It also begins to define the conditions for becoming a Fellow.
This section likely deals with the conditions and requirements for obtaining a certificate of practice as a Company Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Members to be known as Company Secretaries
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that all members of the Institute shall be known as Company Secretaries.
This section likely outlines conditions or circumstances that would disqualify a person from being a member or practicing as a Company Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Council of the Institute
main_sections.description: This section details the formation and composition of the Council, which is the governing body of the Institute.
This section specifies the various powers and responsibilities of the Council of the Institute.
This section deals with the maintenance of the official Register of members of the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Removal from the Register of members
main_sections.description: This section outlines the procedures and grounds for removing a member's name from the Register.
This section establishes the Disciplinary Directorate, which is likely responsible for investigating complaints of misconduct.
This section provides for the constitution and functions of the Board of Discipline, which may hear and decide cases of misconduct.
This section details the establishment and powers of the Disciplinary Committee, which likely handles more serious cases of misconduct.
This section defines what constitutes professional or other misconduct for members of the Institute.
This section establishes an Appellate Authority to hear appeals against decisions made under the disciplinary provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and functions of Regional Councils
main_sections.description: This section outlines the formation and duties of Regional Councils, which likely assist the Institute in its functions across different regions.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, etc.
main_sections.description: This section specifies penalties for individuals who falsely claim to be members of the Institute or engage in unauthorized practices.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for using name of the Council, or awarding degree of Company Secretary
main_sections.description: This section penalizes the misuse of the Institute's name or the unauthorized award of Company Secretary degrees.

main_sections.section_title: Companies not to engage in Company Secretaryship
main_sections.description: This section likely restricts companies from engaging in activities that are the exclusive domain of practicing Company Secretaries.

main_sections.section_title: Unqualified persons not to sign documents
main_sections.description: This section prohibits persons who are not qualified as Company Secretaries from signing certain documents.
This section addresses the liabilities and penalties for companies that commit offenses under the Act.
This section likely requires obtaining prior sanction from a specified authority before prosecuting an offense under the Act.
This section establishes a Quality Review Board to oversee the quality of services provided by Company Secretaries.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India registered under the Companies Act
main_sections.description: This section deals with the dissolution of the previous entity of the Institute registered under the Companies Act and its transition to the new body constituted by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the dissolved company to the Institute
main_sections.description: This section governs the transfer of assets and liabilities from the dissolved company to the Institute established by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions respecting employees of the dissolved company
main_sections.description: This section addresses the employment status and conditions of employees of the dissolved company after the new Institute is formed.

main_sections.section_title: Members, etc., to be public servants
main_sections.description: This section likely designates members and officials of the Institute as public servants for the purposes of certain legal provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: This section grants the Central Government the authority to frame rules under the Act.
This section empowers the Council of the Institute to make regulations for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules, regulations and notifications to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: This section mandates that rules, regulations, and notifications issued under the Act must be presented before Parliament.

important_rules: Rule defining what constitutes 'to be in practice' for a Company Secretary, covering activities like company formation, amalgamation, secretarial auditing, and advising on legal and procedural matters.
Rules regarding the eligibility for entry into the Register of members, including holding specific diplomas, passing examinations, and completing prescribed training.
Provisions that unqualified persons are not permitted to sign documents related to company secretarial practice.

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, Fellow, or Associate of the Institute.
Penalty for using the name of the Council or awarding the degree of Company Secretary without authority.
Penalties for companies that engage in Company Secretaryship activities or commit offenses under the Act.
Penalties for unqualified persons signing documents.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Council of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, the Disciplinary Directorate, the Board of Discipline, the Disciplinary Committee, and the Appellate Authority are established for enforcement and disciplinary actions. The Central Government also has powers to make rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is carried out through the Disciplinary Directorate investigating misconduct, the Board of Discipline and Disciplinary Committee adjudicating cases, and the Appellate Authority hearing appeals. Penalties are prescribed for violations. The Central Government can also issue notifications and make rules.

rights: Members have the right to use their designation (e.g., 'A.C.S.' or 'F.C.S.') after their name.
Members in practice have the right to offer professional services as defined in the Act.
Members have the right to appeal against decisions of disciplinary bodies.
duties: Members have a duty to adhere to professional standards and ethical conduct.
Members must maintain their names on the Register and comply with the Act and regulations.
Members in practice have a duty to perform their services with diligence and competence.
obligations: To pay prescribed fees to the Institute.
To undergo specified training and pass examinations to become a member.
To disclose information as required by the Council or disciplinary bodies.
To comply with the directives and regulations issued by the Council and the Central Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for entry of names into the Register of members, involving application, examination, and training requirements.

Procedure for handling cases of professional or other misconduct, involving investigation by the Disciplinary Directorate, adjudication by the Board of Discipline or Disciplinary Committee, and appeals to the Appellate Authority.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Council and its committees.
Procedure for the dissolution of the previous Institute and transfer of assets and liabilities.
administration: The Council of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, with oversight from the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force on January 1, 1981.
The definition of 'Companies Act' has been updated to refer to the Companies Act, 2013.
The Act provides for the establishment of an Appellate Authority and a Quality Review Board, indicating a framework for dispute resolution and quality assurance.
Honorary Fellows have no voting rights and are exempt from paying fees.
The Act distinguishes between being 'in practice' and other forms of membership.

title: THE AIR (PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF POLLUTION) ACT, 1981
purpose: To provide for the prevention, control and abatement of air pollution, and for the establishment of Boards to carry out these purposes, conferring upon them the necessary powers and functions.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to individuals, industries, automobiles, and government departments that are involved in activities causing or potentially causing air pollution. Its subject matter scope covers the definition of air pollution, the establishment and functions of pollution control boards, measures for prevention and control of air pollution, and penalties for non-compliance.

key_definitions.air_pollutant: Any solid, liquid, or gaseous substance (including noise) present in the atmosphere in such concentration as may be or tends to be injurious to human beings, other living creatures, plants, property, or the environment.
key_definitions.air_pollution: The presence in the atmosphere of any air pollutant.
key_definitions.automobile: Any vehicle powered either by an internal combustion engine or by any method of generating power to drive such vehicle by burning fuel.
key_definitions.Board: The Central Board or a State Board established under the Act.
key_definitions.emission: Any solid or liquid or gaseous substance coming out of any chimney, duct or flue or any other outlet.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India), and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'air pollutant', 'air pollution', 'automobile', 'Board', 'emission', 'industrial plant', 'occupier', and 'prescribed'.

This section states that the Central Pollution Control Board constituted under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, shall also exercise powers and perform functions for the prevention and control of air pollution under this Act.

This section outlines the procedure for constituting State Boards for the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution in states where the Water Act is not in force or where a State Board has not been constituted under that Act. It also specifies the composition of such State Boards.
This section details the various functions of the Central Board related to the prevention and control of air pollution.
This section details the various functions of the State Boards related to the prevention and control of air pollution.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare air pollution control areas
main_sections.description: This section empowers the State Government to declare certain areas as air pollution control areas.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on use of certain industrial plants
main_sections.description: This section imposes restrictions on the use of industrial plants and lays down standards for the emission of air pollutants.

main_sections.section_title: Persons carrying on industry, etc., not to allow emission of air pollutants in excess of the standard laid down by State Board.
main_sections.description: This section prohibits persons carrying on industry from allowing the emission of air pollutants in excess of the standards laid down by the State Board.
This section grants power to Boards or their authorized officers to enter and inspect any premises or industrial plant.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take samples of air or emission and procedure to be followed in connection therewith
main_sections.description: This section empowers the taking of samples of air or emissions and outlines the procedure to be followed.
This section provides the Board with the power to issue directions for the prevention, control, or abatement of air pollution.
This section provides for appeals against certain orders to the National Green Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Failure to comply with the provisions of section 21 or section 22 or with the directions issued under section 31A
main_sections.description: This section specifies penalties for failing to comply with sections 21, 22, or directions issued under section 31A.
This section outlines the procedure for taking cognizance of offences under the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Persons carrying on any industry, operation, or process, or owning or operating any industrial plant, shall not allow the emission into the atmosphere of any air pollutant in excess of such standard for the time being laid down by the State Board. (Section 22)

Rule 2: No person shall use any industrial plant or equipment in any air pollution control area for the purpose of any industrial operation or process or for any other purpose specified by the State Government unless such person has obtained the consent of the State Board. (Section 21)
Rule 3: The State Government may, by notification, declare in such manner as may be prescribed, any area or areas to be air pollution control area or areas. (Section 19)

penalties: Failure to comply with provisions of section 21 or 22, or directions under section 31A: Imprisonment for a term that may extend to three months and with a fine that may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both. For continuing failure, an additional fine may be imposed. (Section 37)

Penalties for certain acts (e.g., obstructing inspection, contravening provisions of section 21 or 22): Imprisonment for a term that may extend to three months and with a fine that may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both. (Section 38)
Penalty for contravention by Government Department: Similar penalties as for other persons. (Section 38A)
Penalty for contravention of certain provisions: Imprisonment for a term that may extend to three months and with fine or with both. (Section 39)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Boards and the Central Board, empowered by the Act, along with the National Green Tribunal for appeals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, inspection, taking samples, issuing directions, and prosecuting offenders in courts. Adjudicating officers are also appointed for penalty imposition.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of the Board to the National Green Tribunal (Section 31B).
Right to appeal against penalty orders to the designated Appellate Authority (Section 39B).
duties: Duty of persons carrying on industry to not exceed emission standards set by the State Board (Section 22).
Duty to obtain consent from the State Board before using industrial plants in control areas (Section 21).
Duty to furnish information to the State Board and other agencies when required (Section 23).
Duty to allow entry and inspection by authorized personnel (Section 24).
Duty of Boards to lay down standards for air quality and for emission from automobiles (Sections 16, 17, 20).
obligations: Occupiers of factories or premises have an obligation to control air pollution.
Government Departments have obligations to comply with the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining consent from the State Board for industrial plants (Section 21).
Procedure for taking samples of air or emission and their analysis (Sections 26, 27, 29, 30).
Procedure for appeals against orders of the Board to the National Green Tribunal (Section 31B).
Procedure for imposing penalties by adjudicating officers and subsequent appeals (Sections 39A, 39B).
administration: The Central Government (for the Central Board and rules) and State Governments (for State Boards and rules) administer the Act. The Central Pollution Control Board and State Pollution Control Boards are the primary bodies responsible for the day-to-day administration and enforcement.
important_notes: The Act recognizes the importance of international decisions (United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, Stockholm, 1972) in its preamble.
The Act is a successor to or complements the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, by establishing parallel structures and functions for air pollution control.
Noise pollution is included within the definition of 'air pollutant' through an amendment.
A provision exists for the Central Board to exercise powers of a State Board in Union territories.
Actions taken in good faith by any person under the Act are protected from legal proceedings (Section 42).

title: The Armed Forces (Punjab and Chandigarh) Special Powers Act, 1983
purpose: To confer special powers upon members of the armed forces in disturbed areas within the State of Punjab and the Union territory of Chandigarh.

scope.geographical: The whole of the State of Punjab and the Union territory of Chandigarh.
scope.subject_matter: Empowering armed forces with special powers for maintaining public order in disturbed areas, including powers of search, arrest, and use of force.

key_definitions.armed_forces: The military forces and the air forces operating as land forces, and includes any other armed forces of the Union so operating.
key_definitions.disturbed_area: An area declared as such by notification under section 3, indicating a disturbed or dangerous condition requiring the use of armed forces in aid of civil power.

main_sections.description: Specifies the title of the Act, its geographical extent, and its commencement date (deemed to be October 15, 1983).
Defines 'armed forces' and 'disturbed area', and states that other terms are to be understood as defined in the Air Force Act, 1950, or the Army Act, 1950.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare areas to be disturbed areas
main_sections.description: Outlines the authority (Governor of Punjab, Administrator of Chandigarh, or Central Government) and the conditions under which an area can be declared a 'disturbed area' through a notification.

main_sections.section_title: Special powers of the armed forces
main_sections.description: Details the specific powers granted to commissioned officers, warrant officers, non-commissioned officers, or equivalent ranks in the armed forces operating in a disturbed area.

main_sections.section_title: Power of search to include powers to break open locks, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the power to break open any lock, almirah, safe, box, cupboard, drawer, package, or other thing if the key is withheld during a search.

main_sections.section_title: Arrested person and seized property to be made over to the police
main_sections.description: Mandates that any person arrested and any property, arms, ammunition, explosives, vehicles, or vessels seized under the Act must be handed over to the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station with minimal delay, along with a report of the circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting in good faith under this Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection against prosecution, suits, or legal proceedings for anything done or purported to be done in the exercise of powers under this Act, requiring prior sanction from the Central Government.

Repeals the Armed Forces (Punjab and Chandigarh) Special Powers Ordinance, 1983, and states that anything done or actions taken under that Ordinance are deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule: In a disturbed area, armed forces personnel can use force, including causing death, after issuing due warning, against individuals contravening laws prohibiting assembly of five or more persons or carrying prohibited items (weapons, firearms, explosives).
Rule: Armed forces can destroy arms dumps, fortified positions, shelters used for armed attacks, training camps for armed volunteers, or hide-outs used by armed gangs or absconders.
Rule: Arrest without warrant any person who has committed or is reasonably suspected of committing a cognizable offense, using necessary force.
Rule: Enter and search premises without warrant to make an arrest, recover wrongfully restrained persons, or seize suspected stolen property, illegal arms, ammunition, or explosives.

Rule: Stop, search, and seize vehicles or vessels suspected of carrying proclaimed offenders, persons committing non-cognizable offenses, or individuals unlawfully holding arms, ammunition, or explosives, using necessary force.
Rule: Break open locks or containers during a search if the key is withheld.
Rule: Hand over arrested persons and seized items to the nearest police station promptly with a report of circumstances.

penalties: The act itself does not specify explicit penalties for violations of its provisions within the provided text. Penalties would likely be covered under other relevant laws for offenses committed.
Consequences for actions taken under the act are protected, requiring Central Government sanction for prosecution against individuals acting in good faith.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Members of the armed forces (commissioned officers, warrant officers, non-commissioned officers, or persons of equivalent rank) operating in declared disturbed areas.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of special powers including use of force, arrest, search, seizure, and destruction of property as detailed in Section 4.

rights: Right to protection from prosecution, suits, or legal proceedings for acts done in good faith under the Act (subject to Central Government sanction).
duties: Duty to make over arrested persons and seized property to the police with least possible delay.
Duty to provide a report of circumstances occasioning arrest or seizure.
obligations: Obligation for armed forces personnel to exercise their powers reasonably and in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
Obligation to give due warning before using force, where considered necessary.

key_procedures: Procedure for declaring a 'disturbed area': The Governor of Punjab, Administrator of Chandigarh, or Central Government must be of the opinion that the area is in a disturbed or dangerous condition requiring armed forces aid. A notification in the Official Gazette is then issued.
Procedure for search and seizure: Armed forces can enter and search premises without warrant, seize suspected items, and stop/search/seize vehicles or vessels.
Procedure for arrest: Armed forces can arrest without warrant individuals involved in or suspected of cognizable offenses.
Procedure for handling arrested persons and seized property: Handover to the nearest police station with a report.
administration: The Central Government, the Governor of Punjab, and the Administrator of Chandigarh have roles in declaring disturbed areas and granting sanction for prosecution.
important_notes: The Act is a special power act, intended to supplement civil power in specific circumstances.
The Act was deemed to have come into force retroactively on October 15, 1983.
Protection for actions taken is provided, but subject to the Central Government's sanction for any legal proceedings.

title: The Indian Veterinary Council Act, 1984
purpose: To regulate veterinary practice and to provide for the establishment of a Veterinary Council of India and State Veterinary Councils and the maintenance of registers of veterinary practitioners.
scope: The Act extends to the States of Haryana, Bihar, Orissa, Himachal Pradesh, and Rajasthan, and all Union territories. It can also be extended to other States that adopt it by resolution. It also extends to Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. It regulates veterinary practice and veterinary institutions.

key_definitions.Council: The Veterinary Council of India established under section 3.
key_definitions.recognised veterinary qualification: Any of the veterinary qualifications included in the First Schedule or the Second Schedule.
key_definitions.register: A register maintained under this Act.
key_definitions.registered veterinary practitioner: A person whose name is for the time being duly registered in a register.
key_definitions.State Veterinary Council: A Veterinary Council established under section 32, including a Joint State Veterinary Council.
key_definitions.veterinary institution: Any University or other institution within or without India which grants degrees, diplomas or licences in veterinary science and animal husbandry.
key_definitions.veterinary medicine: Modern scientific veterinary medicine in all its branches, including veterinary surgery and obstetrics.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date on which it comes into force.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Council', 'recognised veterinary qualification', 'register', 'registered veterinary practitioner', 'State Veterinary Council', 'veterinary institution', and 'veterinary medicine'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and composition of the Council
main_sections.description: Establishes the Veterinary Council of India as a body corporate and specifies its composition through nominations and elections.
Provides for the establishment and maintenance of the Indian veterinary practitioners register.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and composition of State Veterinary Councils
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and composition of State Veterinary Councils.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for individuals who falsely claim to be registered veterinary practitioners.
Addresses the issue of veterinary practice by individuals who are not registered.

important_rules: A person must hold a recognised veterinary qualification to be nominated or elected to the Council (Section 3(7)).
The Council shall meet at least twice a year (Section 9(1)).
The quorum for Council meetings shall be nine (Section 9(2)).
The President has a casting vote in case of an equality of votes (Section 9(5)).
The Council can appoint a Secretary and other officers and employees with the previous sanction of the Central Government (Section 11(1)).
The Council can recognize veterinary qualifications granted by veterinary institutions in India (Section 15) and in countries with reciprocity (Section 16).
Minimum standards of veterinary education are to be maintained (Section 22).
Persons enrolled on the Indian veterinary practitioners register have certain privileges and rights (Chapter IV).
Professional conduct is regulated (Chapter V).
State Veterinary Councils are to maintain State veterinary practitioners registers (Section 44).

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered (Section 55).
Penalty for misuse of titles (Section 56).
Penalty for practice by unregistered persons (Section 57).
Penalty for failure to surrender a certificate of registration (Section 58).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforcement is likely carried out by the Central Government, State Governments, the Veterinary Council of India, and State Veterinary Councils as specified throughout the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions related to registration, recognition of qualifications, professional conduct, and penalties for violations.

rights: Rights of persons enrolled on the Indian veterinary practitioners register (Section 30).
duties: Registered veterinary practitioners must notify any change of residence or practice (Section 28).
Veterinary institutions are subject to inspection and examination (Section 19).
obligations: Veterinary institutions must provide information regarding courses of study and examinations when required (Section 18).

key_procedures: Nomination or election of members to the Veterinary Council of India (Sections 3, 4).
Election of President and Vice-President of the Council (Section 3(4)).
Meeting procedures of the Council, including quorum and voting (Section 9).
Registration of veterinary practitioners in the Indian veterinary practitioners register (Section 24).
Registration of additional qualifications (Section 26).
Removal of names from the Indian veterinary practitioners register (Section 27).
Preparation and maintenance of State veterinary practitioners registers (Section 44).
Scrutiny of applications for registration with State Veterinary Councils (Section 47).
administration: The Central Government and State Governments, through the Veterinary Council of India and State Veterinary Councils respectively, administer the Act.
important_notes: The Act was extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh by Act 34 of 2019 (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).
The Act provides for the possibility of disputes regarding elections being referred to the Central Government for final decision (Section 4(2)).
Vacancies in the Council do not invalidate its acts or proceedings (Section 10).

title: THE TERRORIST AFFECTED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1984
purpose: To provide for the speedy trial of certain offences in terrorist affected areas and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (though later extended to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh). It concerns offences committed in areas declared as 'terrorist affected areas'.

key_definitions.Code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.High Court: The High Court within the territorial limits of whose jurisdiction a Special Court is proposed to be, or is, established.
key_definitions.judicial zone: A judicial zone constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Public Prosecutor: A Public Prosecutor or an Additional Public Prosecutor or a Special Public Prosecutor appointed under section 9, including any person acting under their directions.
key_definitions.scheduled offence: An offence specified in the Schedule and committed in a terrorist affected area.
key_definitions.Special Court: A Special Court or an Additional Special Court established under section 4.
key_definitions.terrorist: A person who indulges in wanton killing of persons, violence, disruption of essential services/communications, or damaging property with intent to cause public fear, affect harmony between groups, coerce the government, or endanger India's sovereignty and integrity.
key_definitions.terrorist affected area: An area declared as a terrorist affected area under section 3.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date it came into force (deemed to have come into force on July 14, 1984).

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Code, High Court, judicial zone, notification, Public Prosecutor, scheduled offence, Special Court, terrorist, and terrorist affected area.

Outlines the process by which the Central Government can declare an area as a 'terrorist affected area' and constitute it into one or more 'judicial zones'. It also specifies the duration of such a declaration, with provisions for extending it and commencing the period from an earlier date.

Details the establishment of Special Courts by the Central Government for the speedy trial of scheduled offences in judicial zones. It also allows for the establishment of Additional Special Courts outside the state if trials within the state are unlikely to be fair, impartial, completed with dispatch, or feasible without risks to safety.

main_sections.section_title: Composition and appointment of Judges of Special Courts
main_sections.description: Explains how Judges and Additional Judges of Special Courts are appointed by the Central Government with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court. It specifies the qualification for appointment (Sessions Judge or Additional Sessions Judge) and provisions for the distribution of business among judges.

Allows a Special Court to sit at any place other than its ordinary sitting place if deemed expedient. It also provides for the possibility of holding trials at a different location for the protection of the accused or witnesses or in the interests of justice, upon certification by the Public Prosecutor.

Defines the exclusive jurisdiction of the Special Court to try scheduled offences committed within a judicial zone during the period it is a terrorist affected area. It includes provisions for transferring pending cases and for cases where the period of declaration commenced retroactively. It also covers the jurisdiction of Additional Special Courts established outside the state.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Special Courts with respect to other offences
main_sections.description: Grants Special Courts the power to try offences other than scheduled offences if they are connected with a scheduled offence in the same trial. It also allows conviction and sentencing for any offence found to have been committed by the accused during a trial.

Deals with the appointment of Public Prosecutors, Additional Public Prosecutors, and Special Public Prosecutors for Special Courts by the Central Government. It also specifies eligibility criteria for these appointments.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of Special Courts
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for Special Courts, including their power to take cognizance of scheduled offences upon a complaint or police report. It also allows for summary trials under certain conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Supreme Court to transfer case
main_sections.description: Empowers the Supreme Court to transfer a case from one Special Court to another.
Provides for measures to protect witnesses during trials.

main_sections.section_title: Power to transfer cases to regular courts
main_sections.description: Allows for the transfer of cases from Special Courts to regular criminal courts under certain circumstances.
Specifies the provisions for appeals against the orders or judgments of Special Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Modified application of certain provisions of the Code
main_sections.description: Indicates that certain provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, are applied with modifications.
Provides for the abolition of certain Special Courts.
States that the provisions of this Act have an overriding effect over other laws inconsistent with it.
Allows for the delegation of certain powers by the Central Government.
Grants the power to the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Contains saving clauses, likely to protect past actions or proceedings.
Indicates an amendment to the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
Provides for the repeal of any existing law and includes a saving clause.

important_rules: Scheduled offences committed in a declared 'terrorist affected area' during the specified period shall be triable exclusively by the Special Court established for that judicial zone.
If a trial within a state is deemed unfair, not dispatchable, or poses a grave risk, an Additional Special Court may be established outside the state.
Special Courts can try offences other than scheduled offences if they are connected with the scheduled offence in the same trial.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws that are inconsistent with its provisions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, High Courts (for judicial appointments), and the Special Courts themselves are involved in enforcement. Public Prosecutors play a key role.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment and functioning of Special Courts, the speedy trial of scheduled offences, and the application of modified procedures from the Code of Criminal Procedure.

rights: Right to a speedy trial for scheduled offences.
Protection of witnesses.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to establish Special Courts and declare terrorist affected areas.
Duty of the Chief Justice of the High Court to concur in the appointment of Judges.
Duty of Public Prosecutors to conduct cases.
obligations: Obligation of accused persons to face trial in Special Courts.
Obligation for ensuring fair and impartial trials.

key_procedures: Declaration of a 'terrorist affected area' by the Central Government via notification.
Establishment of Special Courts by the Central Government for speedy trial of scheduled offences.
Appointment of Judges for Special Courts by the Central Government with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court.
Taking cognizance of scheduled offences by Special Courts upon complaint or police report.
Transfer of cases to Special Courts or Additional Special Courts as specified.
Appeals against judgments of Special Courts.
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative authority for establishing courts, declaring areas, and making rules. The High Courts are involved in the appointment of judges.
important_notes: The Act can be applied retrospectively, with a maximum of six months prior to the notification for the commencement of the declared period.
The provisions of the Act override other laws where there is an inconsistency.
The Act aims to ensure that trials are conducted with utmost dispatch and fairness, even if this means establishing courts outside the affected state.

title: The Spices Board Act, 1986
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Board for the development of export of spices and for the control of cardamom industry, including the control of cultivation of cardamom, and matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the development and export of spices, and the control of the cardamom industry, including cultivation, registration of owners of cardamom estates, and export certificates for spices.

key_definitions.Board: The Spices Board constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.cardamom: The fruit of the cardamom plant and includes green cardamom, bleached cardamom, bleachable white cardamom, sun-dried cardamom, cardamom seeds, powdered cardamom, and oil extracted from cardamom.
key_definitions.cardamom plant: ELETTARIA CARDAMOMUM MATON, AMMOM UM SUBULATUM ROXB, and any other plant which the Board may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare to be a cardamom plant for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.estate: The area administered as one unit which contains land planted with cardamom plants.
key_definitions.export: Taking out of India by land, sea, and air.
key_definitions.import: Bringing into India by land, sea, and air.
key_definitions.owner: In relation to any land planted with cardamom plants, includes any agent of the owner, and a mortgagee, lessee, or other person in actual possession of the land.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered estate: An estate in respect of which an owner is registered under sub-section (1) of section 8 and includes any estate in respect of which an owner is required to be registered under the provisions of that sub-section.
key_definitions.registered owner: An owner of a registered estate which has been or is registered or is required to be registered under sub-section (1) of section 8.
key_definitions.spices: The spices specified in the Schedule, with the Central Government having the power to add or omit spices.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its extent (whole of India), and mentions that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'cardamom', 'cardamom plant', 'certificate', 'dealer', 'estate', 'export', 'import', 'manufacturer', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'registered estate', 'registered owner', and 'spices'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the constitution of the Spices Board, its corporate nature, the number and representation of its members (Chairman, MPs, Central Government ministries, growers, exporters, states, and specific institutions), term of office, and the powers and duties of the Chairman and Vice-Chairman. It also states that vacancies or defects do not invalidate the Board's proceedings.
Empowers the Board to appoint a Secretary and other officers and employees for efficient functioning, with their terms and conditions of service determined by regulations.
Allows the Board to constitute advisory committees for efficient discharge of its functions, with the number of members determined by the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the Cardamom Board and the Spices Export Promotion Council to the Board
main_sections.description: Specifies the transfer of assets, liabilities, contracts, debts, and employees from the Cardamom Board and the Spices Export Promotion Council to the newly constituted Spices Board upon commencement of the Act, ensuring continuity of service for employees.

Outlines the extensive functions of the Board, including developing, promoting, and regulating export of spices; issuing export certificates; undertaking promotion programs; assisting research; stabilizing prices; evolving quality standards; controlling quality; licensing manufacturers; marketing spices; providing warehousing; collecting statistics; advising the government; promoting co-operative efforts among cardamom growers; ensuring remunerative returns to growers; providing assistance for cultivation and processing of cardamom; regulating cardamom sales and prices; providing training; increasing cardamom consumption; registering brokers; improving cardamom marketing; and securing better working conditions for workers.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of owners of cardamom estates
main_sections.description: Mandates that every owner of land planted with cardamom plants must apply for registration within one month of becoming an owner. The State Government can extend this period. Registration remains in force until cancelled.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect section 8, including rules on application forms, fees, particulars, procedures for registration and cancellation, and the supply of information to the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Returns to be made by registered owners
main_sections.description: Requires registered owners to furnish returns to the Board in a prescribed form, at prescribed times, and in the prescribed manner. The Board can authorize an officer to visit estates to verify returns or ascertain productive capacity.

main_sections.section_title: No person to export spices without certificate
main_sections.description: States that no person can export any spice without a certificate after the commencement of the Act, unless otherwise provided.
Details the process of granting export certificates.
Empowers the Board to cancel or suspend export certificates under certain conditions.
Provides for an appeal against orders related to certificates.

main_sections.section_title: Power to permit export without certificate
main_sections.description: Allows the Board to permit export of spices without a certificate in specific cases.

main_sections.section_title: Power to control price and distribution of cardamom
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to control the price and distribution of cardamom.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit or control import of cardamom
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prohibit or control the import of cardamom.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to issue directions to the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to supersede the Board
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to supersede the Board in case of persistent default or if it is necessary in public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Grants and loans by the Central Government
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Central Government may provide grants and loans to the Board.
Establishes a fund for the Board, into which all revenues are credited and from which all expenses are paid.
Requires the Board to prepare and submit a budget annually.
Mandates the Board to prepare an annual report on its activities.
Specifies that the Board's accounts are subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and auditor’s report to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires the annual report and the auditor's report to be laid before Parliament.
Prescribes a penalty for furnishing false returns.

main_sections.section_title: Penalties for obstructing an officer or member of the Board in the discharge of his duties and for failure to produce books and records
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for obstructing Board officials or failing to produce required documents.

main_sections.section_title: Penalties for contravention of section 11 or any order made under section 17
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for violating section 11 (export without certificate) or orders made under section 17 (control of import).
Covers general penalties for contraventions of the Act or rules/regulations made thereunder.
Provides for the adjudication of penalties.
Defines how offences committed by companies are treated.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of Act 52 of 1962 to apply to export of spices and import of cardamom
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of Act 52 of 1962 (likely related to customs or import/export control) apply to the export of spices and import of cardamom.

main_sections.section_title: Previous sanction of the Central Government
main_sections.description: Requires previous sanction of the Central Government for certain actions.
Allows the Central Government and the Board to delegate their powers.

main_sections.section_title: Members, officers and employees of the Board to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members, officers, and employees of the Board as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Grants the power to enter premises for the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Board to make regulations for carrying into effect its functions.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: Every owner of land planted with cardamom plants must apply for registration as an owner within one month of becoming an owner (Section 8(1)).
No person shall export any spice without a certificate granted under section 12 (Section 11).
Registered owners must furnish returns to the Board in the prescribed form, at the prescribed times, and in the prescribed manner (Section 10(1)).
The Central Government has the power to control the price and distribution of cardamom (Section 16).
The Central Government can prohibit or control the import of cardamom (Section 17).

penalties: Penalty for making false returns (Section 26).
Penalties for obstructing an officer or member of the Board, or for failure to produce books and records (Section 27).
Penalties for contravention of Section 11 (export without certificate) or any order made under Section 17 (control of import) (Section 29).
Other penalties for contraventions of the Act or rules/regulations (Section 30).
Provisions for adjudication of penalties (Section 30A).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Spices Board and potentially other authorities as designated by the Central Government or specified in related laws (e.g., Act 52 of 1962 for import/export).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties for contraventions, cancellation/suspension of certificates, adjudication of penalties, and application of provisions of other relevant acts like Act 52 of 1962. The Board also has powers to enter premises and verify returns.

rights: Right to appeal against orders related to certificates (Section 14).
Employees of the former Cardamom Board and Spices Export Promotion Council have rights and privileges as to pension, gratuity, etc., upon their absorption into the Spices Board (Section 6(1)(e)).
duties: Owners of cardamom estates have a duty to register their estates (Section 8(1)).
Registered owners have a duty to furnish returns to the Board (Section 10(1)).
No person has the right to export spices without a certificate (contrary to the duty to obtain one) (Section 11).
obligations: The Board has an obligation to develop, promote, and regulate export of spices.
The Board has obligations related to the promotion and regulation of the cardamom industry, including ensuring remunerative returns to growers and improving marketing.
The Central Government has obligations to control the price and distribution of cardamom and to prohibit or control its import.

key_procedures: Registration of owners of cardamom estates: Application to the registering officer within one month of becoming an owner, subject to extension by the State Government (Section 8).
Obtaining an export certificate for spices: Application for and grant of a certificate as per sections 11 and 12.
Reporting: Registered owners must furnish returns to the Board (Section 10).
Enforcement: Penalties are levied for contraventions, and adjudication of penalties is provided for (Sections 26, 27, 29, 30, 30A).
Rule and Regulation Making: Central Government makes rules (Section 38) and the Board makes regulations (Section 39), which must be laid before Parliament (Section 40).
administration: The Spices Board is constituted for the purposes of this Act, with the Central Government having oversight and powers of direction, control, and supersession. State Governments have powers related to the registration of cardamom estates.
important_notes: The Act transferred assets and liabilities of the erstwhile Cardamom Board and Spices Export Promotion Council to the newly constituted Spices Board (Section 6).
The Central Government can, by notification, add or omit spices from the Schedule (Section 2(n) Proviso).
Absorption of employees from previous bodies into the Board does not entitle them to compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Section 6(2)).

title: The Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund (Repeal) Act, 1986
purpose: To repeal the Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947, and to provide for matters incidental thereto, including the dissolution of the Coal Mines Labour Housing Board and the transfer of its assets and liabilities.
scope: This Act applies to coal mines in India. It primarily deals with the dissolution of the Coal Mines Labour Housing Board and the management of the funds and properties previously under its control.

key_definitions.the Act: The Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947 (32 of 1947).
key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which The Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund (Repeal) Act, 1986, comes into force.
key_definitions.Housing Board: The Coal Mines Labour Housing Board constituted under section 6 of the Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'the Act', 'appointed day', and 'Housing Board'.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Act 32 of 1947 and dissolution of Housing Board
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947, is repealed, and the Coal Mines Labour Housing Board is dissolved.
Outlines the consequences of the dissolution of the Housing Board, including the transfer of its rights, properties, liabilities, obligations, and contracts to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of rights in a Government company
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct that the rights, title, and interest of the Housing Board in relation to any property shall vest in a Government company, along with the corresponding liabilities and obligations.

main_sections.section_title: Continuation of suits, etc., against Central Government
main_sections.description: Specifies that any pending suits, appeals, or other proceedings related to the Housing Board shall not abate due to its dissolution and may be continued by or against the Central Government or a Government company. It also allows for the institution of new suits or appeals by or against the Central Government or the Government company if the cause of action arose before the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Moneys, etc., of the Fund to be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India
main_sections.description: Mandates that all moneys and cash balances standing to the credit of the housing account and the general welfare account of the Coal Mines Labour Housing and General Welfare Fund shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India on the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Collection and payment of arrears of duty
main_sections.description: Provides for the collection and payment of arrears of duty levied under the repealed Act, ensuring these are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

important_rules: On the appointed day, the Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947 shall stand repealed.
On the appointed day, the Coal Mines Labour Housing Board shall stand dissolved.

All rights, properties, liabilities, and obligations of the dissolved Housing Board shall vest in or become those of the Central Government, unless directed otherwise by the Central Government to vest in a Government company.
Pending legal proceedings concerning the Housing Board shall continue with the Central Government or a Government company.
All moneys and cash balances of the Coal Mines Labour Housing and General Welfare Fund shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.
Arrears of duty collected or uncollected before the appointed day shall be paid into the Reserve Bank of India for credit to the Consolidated Fund of India.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the transfer of assets and liabilities, the continuation of legal proceedings, and the crediting of funds to the Consolidated Fund of India. Specific enforcement mechanisms for collecting arrears of duty are also outlined.

rights: The Central Government inherits all rights and privileges of the Housing Board.
The Central Government has the power to direct the vesting of properties in a Government company.
duties: The Central Government is responsible for taking over the liabilities and obligations of the Housing Board.
Collecting agencies are responsible for collecting and paying any arrears of duty.
obligations: The Central Government assumes all borrowings, liabilities, and obligations of the Housing Board.
A Government company, if vested with property, assumes the related liabilities and obligations of the Housing Board.

key_procedures: The Central Government may, by notification, appoint a date for the commencement of the Act.
Upon the appointed day, the Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947 is repealed, and the Housing Board is dissolved.
The Central Government manages the transfer of all rights, properties, liabilities, and obligations of the dissolved Housing Board.
The Central Government can issue directions for the vesting of Housing Board property in a Government company.
Any outstanding legal proceedings are continued by or against the Central Government or the designated Government company.
Funds are transferred and credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.
Arrears of duty are collected and paid into the Reserve Bank of India for credit to the Consolidated Fund of India.
administration: The Central Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 1st October, 1986.
The Central Government has the discretion to transfer the rights and liabilities of the Housing Board to a Government company under specific conditions.

title: THE EXPENDITURE-TAX ACT, 1987
purpose: To provide for the levy of a tax on expenditure incurred in certain hotels or restaurants and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh). It applies to chargeable expenditure incurred in hotels where room charges are three thousand rupees or more per day, and in restaurants before June 1, 1992.

key_definitions.assessee: A person responsible for collecting the expenditure-tax payable under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.chargeable_expenditure: The expenditure referred to in section 5.
key_definitions.hotel: Includes a building or part of a building where residential accommodation is, by way of business, provided for a monetary consideration.
key_definitions.restaurant: Any premises, not being a restaurant situated in a hotel, in which the business of sale of food or drink to the public is carried on and such premises, at the beginning of any month, are equipped with, or have access to, facilities for air-conditioning.
key_definitions.room_charges: Charges for a unit of residential accommodation in a hotel and includes charges for furniture, air-conditioner, refrigerator, radio, music, telephone, television, and such other services as are normally included by a hotel in room rent, but does not include charges for food, drinks and any other services.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of commencement.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as assessee, assessment year, Board, chargeable expenditure, expenditure-tax, hotel, Income-tax Act, person responsible for collecting, prescribed, restaurant, and room charges.
Details the conditions under which the Act applies to chargeable expenditure incurred in hotels and restaurants.
States the charge of expenditure-tax on chargeable expenditure incurred in hotels and restaurants at specified rates and periods.
Defines what constitutes chargeable expenditure in relation to hotels and restaurants, including what is included and excluded.
Specifies the tax authorities who have powers and perform functions under this Act, drawing parallels with the Income-tax Act, and outlines their administrative hierarchy and oversight.
Lays down the procedure for collecting expenditure-tax from chargeable expenditure incurred in hotels and restaurants and the timeline for paying the collected tax to the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Person responsible for collecting tax to furnish prescribed return.
main_sections.description: Requires every person responsible for collecting the tax to furnish a prescribed return annually, detailing payments received, tax collected, tax paid, and other particulars.

important_rules: Rule: If a composite charge is payable for a hotel unit and food, the room charges included therein shall be determined in the prescribed manner.

Rule: If a composite charge is payable for a hotel unit, food, drinks and other services, or if charges are understated/overstated to manipulate room charges, the Assessing Officer shall determine room charges on a reasonable basis.
Rule: Expenditure incurred in foreign exchange before October 1, 1992, is not considered chargeable expenditure in hotels.

Rule: Expenditure incurred by persons within the purview of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961 or the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, 1963, is not considered chargeable expenditure.
Rule: Expenditure incurred in any shop or office not owned or managed by the hotel business is not chargeable expenditure.
Rule: Expenditure by way of any tax, including tax under this Act, is not chargeable expenditure.

penalties: Penalty for failure to collect or pay expenditure-tax.
Penalty for failure to furnish prescribed return.
Penalty for concealment of chargeable expenditure.
Penalty for failure to comply with notice.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tax authorities, including officers of the Income-tax Department, as specified in Section 6.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, collection, and recovery procedures as outlined in the Act, including penalties for non-compliance and provisions for appeals.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of tax authorities.
Right to seek rectification of mistakes in assessments.
duties: Duty to collect expenditure-tax where chargeable expenditure is incurred.
Duty to pay collected tax to the Central Government by the 10th of the following month.
Duty to furnish prescribed annual returns.
Duty to follow orders, instructions, and directions of the Board and higher tax authorities.
obligations: Obligation to pay expenditure-tax at the prescribed rates.
Obligation to ensure accurate determination of room charges and chargeable expenditure.
Obligation to comply with notices issued by tax authorities.

key_procedures: Collection and payment of expenditure-tax: Tax collected monthly must be paid to the Central Government by the 10th of the following month.
Furnishing of returns: Annual returns detailing chargeable expenditure, tax collected, and tax paid must be furnished within four months of March 31st.
Assessment: Procedures for assessment, best judgment assessment, and reassessment of escaped expenditure are outlined.
Appeals: Provisions for appeals to the Commissioner (Appeals) and the Appellate Tribunal are included.
administration: The Board (Central Board of Direct Taxes) and various tax authorities under the Income-tax Act administer this Act.
important_notes: The Act was amended to include restaurants and to adjust the scope and rates of tax over time.
Certain hotels may be exempted from tax during specific periods as per the Income-tax Act.
The application of the Act to Jammu and Kashmir has been updated.
Provisions of the Income-tax Act are applicable where not otherwise specified.
Offences under the Act are subject to specific penalties and procedures for institution of proceedings and composition of offences.

title: The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991
purpose: To provide for public liability insurance for the purpose of providing immediate relief to the persons affected by accident occurring while handling any hazardous substance and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to owners of undertakings handling hazardous substances within India. It covers accidents involving fortuitous, sudden, or unintended occurrences while handling hazardous substances that result in death, injury to persons, or damage to property. It excludes accidents by reason only of war or radio-activity.

key_definitions.accident: An accident involving a fortuitous or sudden or unintended occurrence while handling any hazardous substance resulting in continuous or intermittent or repeated exposure to death of, or injury to, any person or damage to any property, but does not include an accident by reason only of war or radio-activity.
key_definitions.handling: In relation to any hazardous substance, means the manufacture, processing, treatment, package, storage, transportation by vehicle, use, collection, destruction, conversion, offering for sale, transfer or the like of such hazardous substance.
key_definitions.hazardous substance: Any substance or preparation which is defined as hazardous substance under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and exceeding such quantity as may be specified, by notification, by the Central Government.
key_definitions.owner: A person who owns, or has control over handling, any hazardous substance at the time of accident and includes a partner in a firm, a member of an association, or a director, manager, secretary or other officer of a company directly in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business.

main_sections.description: Names the act as 'The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991' and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'accident', 'Collector', 'handling', 'hazardous substance', 'insurance', 'notification', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'Relief Fund', 'rules', 'vehicle', and incorporates meanings from other specified Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Liability to give relief in certain cases on principle of no fault
main_sections.description: Establishes the owner's liability to reimburse amounts or provide relief for death, injury, or property damage resulting from an accident, irrespective of fault. It covers death, medical expenses, loss of wages, other injuries, and damage to private property.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of owner to take out insurance policies
main_sections.description: Mandates every owner of an undertaking to take out one or more insurance policies before handling hazardous substances to cover liability for relief. It also requires renewal of these policies and specifies the minimum insurance amount based on paid-up capital, with a maximum of five hundred crore rupees. It also introduces a contribution to the Environmental Relief Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Verification and publication of accident by Collector
main_sections.description: Empowers the Collector to verify accidents within their jurisdiction and publicize them to invite claims for relief.

Details who can make an application for relief (injured person, owner of damaged property, legal representatives of the deceased, or their authorized agent) and specifies that applications must be made to the Collector within five years of the accident.

Outlines the Collector's process for holding inquiries into claims, making awards, and specifying the relief amount and beneficiaries. It also details the process for depositing award amounts by insurers and owners, and the disbursement of relief from the Environmental Relief Fund. It aims for expeditious disposal of claims within three months.
Details the establishment and management of the Environmental Relief Fund, which is used to provide relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances.
Prescribes penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act.
Prescribes penalties for failing to comply with directions issued under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention by Government Department
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions by Government Departments.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Every owner handling hazardous substances must take out an insurance policy before starting operations.
Insurance policies must be renewed to remain valid throughout the period of handling hazardous substances.
The insurance policy amount must not be less than the paid-up capital of the undertaking, with a maximum of five hundred crore rupees.
Owners must contribute an additional amount to the Environmental Relief Fund, not exceeding the premium amount.
Applications for relief must be made within five years of the accident.
Claims for relief should be disposed of expeditiously, ideally within three months of application.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Penalty for non-compliance with directions issued under the Act.
Penalty for contravention by a Government Department.
Offence for failure to pay penalty or additional penalty, leading to imprisonment and/or fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector is a key authority for receiving applications, holding inquiries, making awards, and enforcing payments. Other authorities may be involved in enforcing penalties and directions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes holding inquiries, making awards, recovering amounts as arrears of land revenue or public demand, imposing penalties, and in case of repeated offenses, imprisonment.

rights: Right of persons affected by an accident to claim immediate relief.
Right of property owners to claim compensation for damage.
Right of legal representatives to claim relief in case of death.
Right to appeal against decisions of the adjudicating officer.
duties: Duty of the owner to take out and renew insurance policies.
Duty of the owner to provide relief as prescribed or awarded.
Duty of the insurer to pay amounts as per the award and insurance policy.
Duty of the owner to contribute to the Environmental Relief Fund.
Duty of the Collector to verify accidents, publicize them, and conduct inquiries.
Duty of the owner to cooperate with authorities during inspections and searches.
obligations: Obligation to reimburse amounts or provide relief for death, injury, or property damage resulting from an accident.
Obligation to deposit awarded amounts within specified periods.
Obligation to comply with directions given by authorities.
Obligation to not handle hazardous substances without necessary insurance.

key_procedures: An accident occurs involving a hazardous substance.
The Collector verifies the accident and publicizes it.
Affected persons or their representatives apply for relief to the Collector within five years.
The Collector notifies the owner and provides an opportunity for a hearing.
The Collector holds an inquiry and makes an award determining relief amount and beneficiaries.
The insurer and owner deposit the awarded amounts as directed by the Collector.
Relief is paid from the Environmental Relief Fund or directly by the insurer/owner.
