administration: The Central Government is responsible for making rules and notifications, and the Collector plays a significant role in the day-to-day administration at the local level. The Act also mentions an Advisory Committee and an adjudicating officer for appeals.
important_notes: The Act operates on the principle of no-fault liability, meaning the claimant does not need to prove the owner's negligence.
Workmen are excluded from the definition of 'person' for claims under Section 3, implying their claims are covered under other relevant legislation like the Workmen's Compensation Act.
The Central Government can exempt certain owners (Government entities, local authorities) if they maintain a dedicated fund for meeting liabilities.
The Act is amended by the Public Liability Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1992, the Companies Act, 2013, and The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023.

title: The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991
purpose: To supplement the provisions of the Constitution relating to the Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers for the National Capital Territory of Delhi and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the National Capital Territory of Delhi. It governs the establishment, composition, powers, and functions of the Legislative Assembly, the Lieutenant Governor, and the Council of Ministers for Delhi.

key_definitions.assembly constituency: A constituency provided under this Act for the purpose of elections to the Legislative Assembly.
key_definitions.Capital: The National Capital Territory of Delhi.
key_definitions.Election Commission: The Election Commission referred to in article 324 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.Legislative Assembly: The Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
key_definitions.Lieutenant Governor: The administrator appointed under article 239 of the Constitution for the National Capital Territory of Delhi and designated as Lieutenant Governor by the President.
key_definitions.Minister: A member of the Council of Ministers referred to in clause (4) of article 239AA of the Constitution, by whatever name called and includes a Deputy Minister.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification. Different dates can be appointed for different provisions.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'article', 'assembly constituency', 'Capital', 'Election Commission', 'Legislative Assembly', 'Lieutenant Governor', 'Minister', and 'Scheduled Castes'.

Establishes the Legislative Assembly with a total of seventy seats to be filled by direct election from territorial constituencies. It also outlines the division of the Capital into single-member constituencies and reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications for membership of Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Specifies the qualifications for a person to be a member of the Legislative Assembly, including being a citizen of India, taking an oath/affirmation, being not less than twenty-five years of age, and possessing other prescribed qualifications.
States that the Legislative Assembly continues for five years from its first meeting unless sooner dissolved. This duration can be extended by the President during a Proclamation of Emergency.

main_sections.section_title: Sessions of Legislative Assembly, prorogation and dissolution
main_sections.description: Details the Lieutenant Governor's power to summon the Assembly, and prorogue or dissolve it. It also stipulates that not more than six months shall intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.

main_sections.section_title: Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Covers the election of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, vacation of office, resignation, and removal from office. It also outlines provisions for presiding over sittings when the Speaker or Deputy Speaker is absent or the office is vacant.

main_sections.section_title: Matters in which Lieutenant Governor to act in his sole discretion
main_sections.description: Specifies matters in which the Lieutenant Governor is required to act in his sole discretion.
Defines terms specific to Part IV-A, which deals with provisions relating to the maintenance of the democratic and administrative balance in the governance of the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of National Capital Civil Service Authority
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of the National Capital Civil Service Authority.
Repeals the Delhi Administration Act, 1966.

important_rules: The Legislative Assembly shall consist of seventy members elected directly from territorial constituencies.
Seats shall be reserved for Scheduled Castes in the Legislative Assembly in proportion to their population.
A member of the Legislative Assembly must be a citizen of India, at least twenty-five years old, and have taken the prescribed oath or affirmation.
The Legislative Assembly has a duration of five years unless sooner dissolved.
The Lieutenant Governor has the power to summon, prorogue, and dissolve the Legislative Assembly.
The Speaker and Deputy Speaker are elected by the Assembly and can be removed by a resolution.
The Lieutenant Governor is required to act in his sole discretion in certain specified matters.

rights: Members of the Legislative Assembly have powers and privileges as may be determined by Parliament.
Ministers have rights as respects the Legislative Assembly.
The Lieutenant Governor has the right to address and send messages to the Legislative Assembly.
duties: Members must make and subscribe an oath or affirmation.
The Chief Minister has duties to furnish information to the Lieutenant Governor.
obligations: Members are subject to disqualifications on grounds of defection.
Members are liable to penalties for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation or when not qualified or disqualified.

key_procedures: Summoning, prorogation, and dissolution of the Legislative Assembly by the Lieutenant Governor.
Election of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker by the Legislative Assembly.
Removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker by a resolution of the Assembly with prior notice.
Submission of an annual financial statement to the Legislative Assembly.
Procedure for appropriation and supplementary grants.
Delimitation of constituencies by the Election Commission.
administration: The Central Government plays a significant role in appointing the Lieutenant Governor, issuing notifications, and making rules under specific parts of the Act. The Legislative Assembly and its elected Speaker and Deputy Speaker administer the internal proceedings of the Assembly. The Election Commission is responsible for delimitation of constituencies.
important_notes: The duration of the Legislative Assembly can be extended by the President during a Proclamation of Emergency.
The Act is supplemented by various amending Acts as listed at the beginning of the document.
The provisions regarding the delimitation of constituencies are subject to the Delimitation Act, 2002.

The 'population' for the purpose of seat reservation refers to the population as ascertained in the last preceding census for which figures have been published, with specific provisions for the post-2026 census and readjustments based on the 2001 census.

title: The Multimodal Transportation of Goods Act, 1993
purpose: To provide for the regulation of the multimodal transportation of goods, from any place in India to a place outside India, on the basis of a multimodal transport contract and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Regulates the multimodal transportation of goods from any place in India to a place outside India based on a multimodal transport contract.

key_definitions.carrier: A person who performs or undertakes to perform for hire, the carriage or part thereof, of goods by road, rail, inland waterways, sea or air.
key_definitions.multimodal_transportation: Carriage of goods, by at least two different modes of transport under a multimodal transport contract, from the place of acceptance of the goods in India to a place of delivery of the goods outside India.
key_definitions.multimodal_transport_operator: A person who concludes a multimodal transport contract on his own behalf or through another person acting on his behalf; acts as principal, not as an agent of the consignor, or consignee or of the carrier; and is registered under section 4.
key_definitions.multimodal_transport_document: A negotiable or non-negotiable document evidencing a multimodal transport contract and which can be replaced by electronic data interchange messages permitted by applicable law.
key_definitions.goods: Any property including live animals, containers, pallets or such other articles of transport or packaging supplied by the consignor, irrespective of whether such property is to be or is carried on or under the deck.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir, now applicable to Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on October 16, 1992).

Defines various terms used in the Act, including carrier, competent authority, consignee, consignment, consignor, delivery, endorsee, endorsement, goods, mode of transport, multimodal transportation, multimodal transport contract, multimodal transport document, multimodal transport operator, negotiable multimodal transport document, non-negotiable multimodal transport document, prescribed, special drawing rights, and taking charge.

main_sections.section_title: No person to carry on business without registration
main_sections.description: Mandates that no person can carry on or commence the business of multimodal transportation unless they are registered under the Act. Provides a grace period for existing businesses.

Outlines the process for applying for registration as a multimodal transport operator. Specifies conditions for registration, including financial turnover or share capital, and having offices or agents in other countries. Also covers the validity and renewal of registration certificates.

Details the grounds on which the competent authority can cancel a multimodal transport operator's registration, such as providing false information, contravening Act provisions, or not entering into contracts for a specified period. Requires a reasonable opportunity to be heard before cancellation.
Provides for the right to appeal to the Central Government against the refusal or cancellation of registration. Specifies the period for filing an appeal and the procedure to be followed.

States that upon taking charge of goods and entering into a contract, the multimodal transport operator shall, at the consignor's option, issue a negotiable or non-negotiable multimodal transport document. Requires the operator to have valid insurance cover.

main_sections.section_title: Multimodal transport document to be regarded as document of title
main_sections.description: Declares that the consignee or endorsee named in a multimodal transport document shall have all the rights and liabilities of the consignor. It also clarifies that this does not prejudice the operator's right to claim freight or enforce liabilities.

Specifies the mandatory particulars that must be included in a multimodal transport document, such as the general nature of goods, leading marks, character of goods (including dangerous goods), number of packages or units, and gross weight and quantity of the goods as declared by the consignor.

important_rules: No person can engage in multimodal transportation business without registration under the Act.
A multimodal transport operator must issue a multimodal transport document at the consignor's option after taking charge of goods and having valid insurance cover.
The multimodal transport document is to be considered a document of title.
The multimodal transport document must contain specific particulars about the goods.

rights: Consignees and endorsees have rights and liabilities similar to the consignor concerning the goods mentioned in the multimodal transport document.
Multimodal transport operators have the right to claim freight from the consignor and enforce liabilities of the consignee or endorsee.
Multimodal transport operators have a right of lien on goods and documents.
duties: Consignors have responsibilities regarding the nature and value of goods and ensuring correct declarations.
Multimodal transport operators have a duty to issue a multimodal transport document and ensure valid insurance cover.
Operators have duties related to the carriage of goods, including handling dangerous goods and providing timely delivery.
Operators are responsible for loss or damage to goods during multimodal transportation.
obligations: Operators must be registered to conduct multimodal transportation business.
Operators must comply with the provisions of the Act and its rules.
Operators must provide a multimodal transport document that is accurate and complete.
Operators are obligated to compensate for loss or damage to goods under specified conditions.

key_procedures: Application for registration as a multimodal transport operator, including submission of required documents and fees.
Issuance of a multimodal transport document by the operator to the consignor after taking charge of goods.
Procedure for preferring an appeal against refusal or cancellation of registration to the Central Government.
administration: Central Government (via Competent Authority)
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now applicable to Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh).
The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 16, 1992.
The Multimodal Transportation of Goods Act, 1993, overrides other enactments in case of conflict.
The Act includes provisions for special drawing rights in relation to liabilities.

title: THE PUBLIC RECORDS ACT, 1993
purpose: To regulate the management, administration and preservation of public records of the Central Government, Union territory Administrations, public sector undertakings, statutory bodies and corporations, commissions and committees constituted by the Central Government or a Union territory Administration and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to public records of the Central Government, Union territory Administrations, public sector undertakings, statutory bodies and corporations, commissions, and committees constituted by the Central Government or a Union territory Administration. The Act also extends to the Union territory Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

key_definitions.Board: The Archival Advisory Board constituted under sub-section (1) of section 13.
key_definitions.Director General: The Director General of Archives appointed by the Central Government and includes any officer authorised by that Government to perform the duties of the Director General.
key_definitions.head of the Archives: A person holding the charge of the Archives of the Union territory Administration.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public records: Includes any document, manuscript and file; any microfilm, microfiche and facsimile copy of a document; any reproduction of image or images embodied in such microfilm (whether enlarged or not); and any other material produced by a computer or by any other device, of any records creating agency.
key_definitions.records creating agency: Includes ministries, departments or offices of the Central Government; offices of statutory bodies, corporations, commissions, or committees wholly or substantially controlled or financed by the Central Government or Union territory Administration; and departments or offices of a Union territory Administration.
key_definitions.records officer: An officer nominated by the records creating agency under sub-section (1) of section 5.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Director General', 'head of the Archives', 'prescribed', 'public records', 'records creating agency', and 'records officer'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Central Government to coordinate, regulate and supervise operations connected with administration, management, etc., of public records.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to coordinate, regulate, and supervise operations related to the administration, management, preservation, selection, disposal, and retirement of public records. It also authorizes the Director General or head of Archives to carry out specific functions related to Archives management.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition against taking of public records out of India.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the removal of public records from India without prior approval from the Central Government, with an exception for official purposes.
Mandates every records creating agency to nominate a 'records officer' and allows for the establishment of record rooms under the charge of a records officer.

Details the responsibilities of the records officer, including arrangement, maintenance, preservation, weeding, appraisal, destruction, compilation of schedules and indices, submission of reports, and transfer of records.

main_sections.section_title: Records officer to take appropriate action in the event of unauthorised removal, destruction, etc., of public records in his custody.
main_sections.description: Requires the records officer to take immediate action for the recovery or restoration of any unauthorizedly removed, destroyed, defaced, or altered public records and to report such incidents.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction or disposal of public records.
main_sections.description: States that no public record shall be destroyed or disposed of except in a prescribed manner and subject to prescribed conditions, with a special provision for records created before 1892.
Specifies penalties for contravening provisions of section 4 (taking public records out of India) or section 8 (destruction or disposal of public records).
Prohibits the transfer of public records bearing security classification to the National Archives of India or the Archives of the Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Receipt of records from private sources.
main_sections.description: Empowers the National Archives of India or the Archives of the Union territory to accept historical or national importance records from private sources and to make them available to bona fide research scholars.

Outlines the conditions under which unclassified public records older than thirty years, transferred to the National Archives, may be made available to bona fide research scholars. It also allows records creating agencies to grant access to public records.
Provides for the constitution of an Archival Advisory Board by the Central Government, detailing its composition which includes ex-officio members and nominated members.
Specifies the functions of the Archival Advisory Board, including advising the government on record management, laying down training guidelines, and directing acquisition of records.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Director General to lay down norms and standards for courses in archival science.
main_sections.description: Grants the Director General the authority to set norms and standards for archival science courses, curricula, assessment, and examinations.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for any action taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, with specific areas for such rules mentioned.
Requires rules made under the Act to be laid before Parliament.

important_rules: No public record shall be destroyed or disposed of except in a prescribed manner and subject to prescribed conditions (Section 8(1)).

No record created before the year 1892 shall be destroyed unless it is so defaced or in such condition that it cannot be put to any archival use, as determined by the Director General or head of the Archives (Section 8(2)).
No person shall take or cause to be taken out of India any public records without prior approval of the Central Government, unless it is for an official purpose (Section 4).

Unclassified public records older than thirty years, transferred to the National Archives or Archives of the Union territory, may be made available to any bona fide research scholar, subject to prescribed exceptions and restrictions (Section 12(1)).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or a fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or both, for contravening Section 4 or Section 8.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, Director General, head of Archives, and records officers are involved in enforcement and supervision.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Central Government to coordinate, regulate and supervise operations; authorization of the Director General or head of Archives to carry out specific functions; nomination and responsibilities of records officers; imposition of penalties for contraventions; and the general framework for management and preservation of public records.

rights: Right of bona fide research scholars to access unclassified public records older than thirty years (subject to conditions).
Right to obtain authenticated copies of, or extracts from, public records (exercised by Director General/head of Archives).
Right of records creating agencies to grant access to public records in their custody (subject to conditions).
duties: Duty of every records creating agency to nominate a records officer (Section 5(1)).
Duty of records officers to ensure proper arrangement, maintenance, preservation, review, appraisal, and destruction of public records under their charge (Section 6).
Duty of records officers to report unauthorized removal, destruction, defacement or alteration of public records (Section 7(2)).
Duty of government officers or other persons to render assistance to records officers for the recovery or restoration of public records (Section 7(3)).
Duty of the Central Government to coordinate, regulate and supervise operations connected with public records (Section 3(1)).
obligations: Obligation not to take public records out of India without prior approval (Section 4).
Obligation not to destroy or dispose of public records except in a prescribed manner and subject to prescribed conditions (Section 8(1)).

key_procedures: Nomination of a records officer by each records creating agency (Section 5(1)).
Periodical review and appraisal of public records by the records officer (Section 6(1)(b) & (c)).
Destruction or disposal of public records according to prescribed manner and conditions (Section 8(1)).
Reporting by records officers on unauthorized removal, destruction, defacement or alteration of public records and actions taken (Section 7(2)).
Making public records available to bona fide research scholars after thirty years, subject to conditions (Section 12(1)).
administration: The Central Government, through various ministries (e.g., Ministry of Culture), the Director General of Archives, the head of the Archives in Union territories, and records officers within records creating agencies.
important_notes: The Act was extended to the Union territory Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by Act 34 of 2019.
No prior approval is required to take public records out of India if they are sent for an official purpose (Section 4 proviso).
Records bearing security classification are not to be transferred to the National Archives of India or the Archives of the Union territory (Section 10).

title: THE TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1995
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of specified textile undertakings and the rights of their owners, with the objective of augmenting the production and distribution of cloth and yarn to serve the interests of the general public. It also covers related and incidental matters.
scope: The Act applies to specific textile undertakings listed in the First Schedule and their owners. Geographically, it applies to undertakings within India and potentially outside India, as mentioned in Section 4(1). The subject matter scope covers the acquisition, transfer, management, and payment related to these textile undertakings, as well as provisions concerning employees and the winding up of affairs.

key_definitions.appointed day: The 1st day of April, 1994.
key_definitions.bank: Includes the State Bank of India, subsidiary banks, corresponding new banks constituted under banking acts of 1970 and 1980, and any other scheduled bank.
key_definitions.commissioner: A Commissioner of Payments appointed under Section 17.
key_definitions.custodian: A Custodian appointed under the Textile Undertakings (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1983, or the Laxmirattan and Atherton West Cotton Mills (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1976.
key_definitions.national textile corporation: The National Textile Corporation Limited formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.owner: In relation to a textile undertaking, it means the immediate proprietor, lessee, or occupier before the appointed day. It includes liquidators or receivers of companies being wound up, and their agents or managers, but excludes persons authorized to take over management under specific Acts.
key_definitions.textile undertaking: An undertaking specified in the First Schedule whose management was taken over by the Central Government before the appointed day under the Textile Undertakings (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1983, or the Laxmirattan and Atherton West Cotton Mills (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1976.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for its provisions. Sections 31 and 32 are effective immediately, while other provisions are deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1994.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'bank', 'Commissioner', 'Custodian', 'National Textile Corporation', 'notification', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'specified date', 'subsidiary textile corporation', 'textile', 'textile company', and 'textile undertaking'.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of rights of owners and vesting of the textile undertakings
main_sections.description: Declares that on the appointed day, the rights, title, and interest of the owner in every textile undertaking shall transfer to and vest absolutely in the Central Government. Subsequently, these undertakings shall transfer to and vest in the National Textile Corporation. It also clarifies that lease-hold rights remain vested in the Central Government, to be discharged by the National Textile Corporation, and that no court can order divestment from the National Textile Corporation.

Specifies that vested textile undertakings include all related assets, rights, property (movable and immovable), powers, privileges, and liabilities. It also states that vested property is freed from trusts, obligations, mortgages, charges, liens, and other encumbrances. Licenses and instruments related to the undertaking are deemed to be transferred to the National Textile Corporation. Provisions are made for mortgagees and holders of other interests to claim payment from the First Schedule amounts, and for pending legal proceedings to continue by or against the National Textile Corporation. It also addresses the delivery of possession of undertakings and documents by persons in custody.
Outlines the penalties for contravening any provision of the Act or any rule, scheme, or order made thereunder.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of certain enactments and savings in relation to actions taken under them.

important_rules: On the appointed day (April 1, 1994), the rights, title, and interest of owners in textile undertakings vest absolutely in the Central Government, and then in the National Textile Corporation.
Vested textile undertakings include all assets, rights, property, and liabilities. Any encumbrances on the property are discharged.
Licenses and instruments related to textile undertakings are deemed to be granted to the National Textile Corporation.
Mortgagees and holders of other interests can claim payment from the specified amounts, but their claims are not enforceable against the vested property.
Pending legal proceedings related to vested property will continue by or against the National Textile Corporation.
Persons in possession or custody of a textile undertaking or its parts must deliver them to the Central Government or National Textile Corporation.
Employees of textile undertakings have provisions for their continued employment, provident funds, and transfer to subsidiary corporations.

penalties: Contravention of any provision of the Act or any rule, scheme, or order made thereunder is punishable.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the National Textile Corporation are the primary entities responsible for the enforcement of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the vesting of undertakings, the appointment of Commissioners of Payments, the continuation of legal proceedings, the imposition of penalties for contraventions, and the government's power to make rules and remove difficulties.

rights: Owners of mortgagees or those holding other interests have the right to claim payment from specified amounts.
Employees have the right to continued employment and benefits related to provident and other funds.
The National Textile Corporation has the right to operate and manage the acquired undertakings.
The Central Government has rights related to lease-hold rents and the overall management of the nationalized sector.
duties: Owners are liable for certain prior liabilities of the textile undertakings.
Persons in charge of management of textile undertakings have a duty to deliver all assets, books of account, registers, and other documents.
Mortgagees and holders of charges, liens, or other interests have a duty to intimate these to the Commissioner.
The National Textile Corporation has duties related to the management of undertakings, payment of lease-hold rents, and disbursement of amounts to claimants.
obligations: The National Textile Corporation has obligations to manage the undertakings efficiently, ensure production and distribution of cloth and yarn, and secure the employment of workmen.
The Central Government has obligations to pay amounts to owners and Commissioners of Payments.
Owners have obligations to transfer their undertakings as per the Act.

key_procedures: Acquisition and vesting of textile undertakings from owners to the Central Government, and then to the National Textile Corporation, effective from the appointed day.
Transfer of all assets, rights, and liabilities of the textile undertakings to the National Textile Corporation.
Appointment of Commissioners of Payments to manage claims against the owners.
Payment of amounts to owners of textile undertakings through the Commissioner of Payments.
Management of textile undertakings by the National Textile Corporation, including disposal of assets in certain circumstances.
Provisions for the employment and welfare of employees of the textile undertakings.
Procedure for making claims to the Commissioner, examination and admission/rejection of claims, and disbursement of money.
Deposit of undisbursed or unclaimed amounts to a general reserve account.
administration: The Central Government and the National Textile Corporation are responsible for administering this Act. The Ministry or Department related to textiles under the Central Government would likely oversee the overall implementation.
important_notes: The Act overrides all other existing enactments.
Contracts entered into by the textile undertakings will cease to have effect unless ratified by the National Textile Corporation.
Textile companies whose undertakings are nationalized cannot be wound up by a court.
The Act includes provisions for validation of certain actions and removal of difficulties.

title: The Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999
purpose: To repeal the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to the States of Haryana and Punjab and all Union territories. Other states can adopt it by resolution under Article 252(2) of the Constitution. The repeal of the principal Act takes effect from the date this Act comes into force in each respective State or Union territory.

main_sections.description: Defines the short title, the geographical and territorial applicability of the Act, and the date from which it is deemed to have come into force in different regions.
Formally repeals the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976.

Specifies what is not affected by the repeal of the principal Act, including vesting of vacant land and validity of exemptions granted under certain conditions. It also addresses the restoration of land where possession has not been taken over.

States that legal proceedings related to orders made under the principal Act shall abate, with a proviso that this does not apply to proceedings related to specific sections (11, 12, 13, 14) if possession of the land has already been taken over.

Repeals the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Ordinance, 1999, and clarifies that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: The Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, is repealed.
The repeal does not affect the vesting of vacant land if possession has been taken over by the State Government or authorized persons.
The repeal does not affect the validity of exemptions granted under section 20(1) of the principal Act or actions taken thereunder.
Land deemed vested in the State Government under section 10(3) of the principal Act will not be restored unless any amount paid by the State Government has been refunded.
Legal proceedings relating to orders made under the principal Act will abate, unless they pertain to sections 11, 12, 13, or 14 where possession has been taken over.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Governments or persons duly authorized by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and the taking over of possession of land.

rights: Right to have legal proceedings related to the repealed Act abated (unless an exception applies).
duties: Duty to refund any amount paid by the State Government for land that is not restored.
Duty to comply with any actions taken under the repealed Ordinance which are deemed to be under this Act.

key_procedures: Adoption of the Act by other states through a resolution passed under Article 252(2) of the Constitution.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be managed by State Governments and authorized authorities.
important_notes: The repeal is made effective retrospectively to January 11, 1999, for Haryana, Punjab, and Union territories.
Any judgment of a court to the contrary shall not affect the validity of exemptions granted under section 20(1) of the principal Act.

title: THE CENTRAL INDUSTRIAL SECURITY FORCE (AMENDMENT AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1999
purpose: To further amend the Central Industrial Security Force Act, 1968, and to validate certain revision petitions disposed of under the rules made under the said Act.
scope: The act amends the Central Industrial Security Force Act, 1968, to improve its provisions regarding the constitution and regulation of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) for the protection of industrial undertakings, employees, and to include provision of technical consultancy services to private sector industrial establishments. It also validates past actions related to revision petitions.

key_definitions.industrial_establishment: Means an industrial undertaking or a company as defined under section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956 or a firm registered under section 59 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, which is engaged in any industry, or in any trade, business or service.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Central Industrial Security Force (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1999.

This section substitutes the long title of the principal Act (Central Industrial Security Force Act, 1968) to include provisions for the better protection and security of industrial undertakings owned by the Central Government, certain other industrial undertakings, employees, and to provide technical consultancy services to industrial establishments in the private sector.
This section inserts a new clause (ca) to sub-section (1) of section 2 of the principal Act, defining 'industrial establishment'.
This section amends sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act by inserting words to allow the Force to perform other duties entrusted by the Central Government.

This section amends section 8 of the principal Act by adding 'order for compulsory retirement of' to the powers and by inserting new sub-clauses (d), (e), and (f) to clause (ii) which include withholding of increment of pay, withholding of promotion, and censure as disciplinary actions.

This section extensively amends section 9 of the principal Act. It modifies references to sub-sections and inserts new sub-sections (2A) and (2B) to introduce a revision petition process for enrolled members aggrieved by orders passed in appeal, and empowers a prescribed authority to review such proceedings.

This section amends section 10 of the principal Act by inserting new clauses (f), (g), and (h) to expand the duties of the Force to include providing technical consultancy services to private sector establishments, protecting government-funded organizations and their employees, and undertaking any other duty entrusted by the Central Government.

This section inserts a new section 14A titled 'Technical Consultancy Service to industrial establishments'. It empowers the Director-General to direct members of the Force to provide technical consultancy services relating to security to private sector industrial establishments upon request, on payment of a prescribed fee. The fee is to be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India. It also defines 'Managing Director' in relation to an industrial establishment.

This section amends sub-section (2) of section 22 of the principal Act by inserting clauses to prescribe the authority and procedure for revision petitions under section 9, and the manner and fee for technical consultancy services under section 14A.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of the disposal of certain revision petitions
main_sections.description: This section provides for the validation of rule 49 of the Central Industrial Security Force Rules, 1969, and any disposal of revision petitions made or actions taken under it, notwithstanding any court judgment to the contrary. It clarifies that such actions are deemed to have been made under the principal Act as amended by this Act, removing any invalidity due to the Central Government's perceived lack of power to make the rule.

important_rules: Rule 49 of the Central Industrial Security Force Rules, 1969: This rule pertains to the disposal of revision petitions. Its past application and any actions taken under it are validated by this Act.
The Act introduces provisions for the disposal of revision petitions by a prescribed authority within a prescribed period, following a prescribed procedure.
The Act specifies that technical consultancy services under section 14A are to be provided on payment of a prescribed fee and in a prescribed manner.

penalties: Withholding of increment of pay with or without cumulative effect.
Withholding of promotion.
Censure.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, and the authorities prescribed under section 9 and section 22 for handling revision petitions and disciplinary actions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary proceedings as defined in section 8, appeal processes, revision petition processes as introduced in section 9, and through the Central Government's general oversight and power to entrust duties.

rights: An enrolled member of the Force aggrieved by an order passed in appeal has the right to prefer a revision petition within six months.
The right to receive technical consultancy services related to security for industrial establishments in the private sector, subject to request and payment of fees.
duties: The Central Industrial Security Force has the duty to provide better protection and security to industrial undertakings owned by the Central Government and certain other industrial undertakings.
The Force has the duty to protect and safeguard employees of such undertakings.
The Force has the duty to provide technical consultancy services to industrial establishments in the private sector.
The Force has the duty to protect and safeguard organizations owned or funded by the Government and their employees.
The Force has the duty to perform any other duty entrusted by the Central Government.
obligations: Industrial establishments in the private sector have an obligation to pay prescribed fees for technical consultancy services.
The Director-General has an obligation to direct members of the Force to provide technical consultancy services when requested by eligible establishments.

key_procedures: Revision Petition Process: An enrolled member aggrieved by an appellate order can file a revision petition within six months. A prescribed authority will dispose of this petition following a prescribed procedure.

Review of Proceedings: The prescribed revision authority can, on its own motion or on petition, call for records of proceedings under section 8, or sub-section (2), (2A), or (2B) of section 9, conduct an inquiry, and pass orders as it deems fit within a prescribed period.

Provision of Technical Consultancy Services: The Director-General, on request from a private sector industrial establishment, may direct CISF members to provide technical consultancy services relating to security, in a prescribed manner and on payment of a prescribed fee.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for the overall administration and direction of the Central Industrial Security Force. Specific administrative functions related to appeals, revisions, and consultancy services are delegated to prescribed authorities.
important_notes: The Act retrospectively validates rule 49 of the Central Industrial Security Force Rules, 1969, and actions taken under it, removing any past legal doubts about the validity of these actions.
The fee collected for technical consultancy services is to be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.
The definition of 'industrial establishment' has been broadened to include companies and firms engaged in industry, trade, business, or service.

title: The Unit Trust of India (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act, 2002
purpose: To provide for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking (excluding the specified undertaking) of the Unit Trust of India to a specified company, and the transfer and vesting of the specified undertaking of the Unit Trust of India in an Administrator, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, and also to repeal the Unit Trust of India Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the Unit Trust of India, its undertaking, specified undertaking, a specified company to be formed, and an Administrator appointed by the Central Government. The geographical scope is within India and potentially outside India for assets and liabilities.

key_definitions.administrator: A person or body of persons appointed as Administrator under section 7.
key_definitions.appointed_day: The date the Central Government appoints by notification in the Official Gazette under section 4.
key_definitions.specified_company: A company to be formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956, whose entire capital is subscribed by financial institutions or banks specified by the Central Government for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking.
key_definitions.specified_undertaking: Includes all business, assets, liabilities, and properties of the Trust representing and relatable to the schemes and Development Reserve Fund specified in Schedule I.
key_definitions.trust: The Unit Trust of India established under the Unit Trust of India Act, 1963.
key_definitions.undertaking: Includes all business, assets, liabilities, and properties of the Trust representing and relatable to the schemes and plans specified in Schedule II.

main_sections.description: Names the Act and specifies that it is deemed to have come into force on October 29, 2002.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'appointed day', 'specified company', 'specified undertaking', 'Trust', and 'undertaking'.

Details the transfer of the Trust's initial capital (contributed by Development Bank, LIC, State Bank, etc.) to the Central Government on the appointed day. It also outlines the refund of this capital to the contributing institutions by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Undertaking of Trust to vest in specified company and specified undertaking of Trust to vest in Administrator
main_sections.description: States that on a date appointed by the Central Government, the Trust's undertaking (excluding the specified undertaking) will vest in the specified company, and the specified undertaking will vest in the Administrator. It also clarifies the finality of the Central Government's decision on what constitutes the undertaking or specified undertaking.

main_sections.section_title: General effect of vesting of undertaking or specified undertaking in specified company or Administrator
main_sections.description: Explains the comprehensive nature of the vesting, including all assets, liabilities, rights, powers, contracts, deeds, and obligations. It clarifies that existing contracts and proceedings affecting the Trust will be enforceable by or against the specified company or Administrator.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Trust
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of officers and employees of the Trust to the specified company, outlining terms of employment, remuneration, and benefits. It also addresses situations where employees opt not to continue and clarifies that no compensation is payable for such transfers.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Administrator to manage specified undertaking
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint an Administrator to manage the specified undertaking from the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal and saving of Act 52 of 1963
main_sections.description: Repeals the Unit Trust of India Act, 1963, with provisions for saving certain actions or things done under the repealed Act.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over any other law for the time being in force.
Provides for the repeal of any ordinance or Act that might have been in force and contains a saving clause.

important_rules: On the appointed day, the initial capital of the Trust is transferred to and vests in the Central Government.
The Trust's undertaking (excluding the specified undertaking) vests in the specified company, and the specified undertaking vests in the Administrator.
All assets, liabilities, rights, powers, and obligations related to the transferred undertaking or specified undertaking vest in the specified company or Administrator, respectively.
Existing contracts, deeds, and arrangements affecting the Trust become enforceable by or against the specified company or Administrator.
Officers and employees of the Trust (excluding trustees, chairman, and executive trustee) are transferred to the specified company with similar terms and conditions of service.
The Central Government shall appoint an Administrator to manage the specified undertaking.

rights: Employees retain their tenure, remuneration, and benefits upon transfer to the specified company.
Retired employees are entitled to their benefits, rights, or privileges from the specified company.
Tax exemptions granted to provident and gratuity funds continue to apply to the specified company.
duties: The specified company and Administrator have the duty to assume all liabilities and obligations of the Trust related to the transferred undertaking/specified undertaking.
The specified company or Administrator must continue to manage unit schemes and distribute income/redeem units as the Trust would have.
The Administrator has the duty to manage the specified undertaking.
Provident fund and gratuity fund bodies of the Trust continue to discharge their functions in the specified company.
obligations: The specified company and Administrator assume all existing obligations of the Trust related to the transferred undertaking/specified undertaking.
Employees transferred to the specified company continue to have the same obligations as they had with the Trust.

key_procedures: The Central Government notifies the 'appointed day' for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking and specified undertaking.
A 'specified company' is formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956, with its capital subscribed by specified financial institutions or banks.
The Central Government appoints an Administrator to manage the specified undertaking.
The transfer of officers and employees involves their becoming employees of the specified company, with an option to not continue.
The Central Government has the power to make a Scheme under section 20 to alter Schedules I and II or carry out the provisions of the Act.
administration: The Central Government is the primary administrative authority, responsible for appointing the 'appointed day', specifying institutions for the 'specified company', appointing the 'Administrator', and having the power to make a 'Scheme'.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 29, 2002.
The decision of the Central Government regarding what constitutes the 'undertaking' or 'specified undertaking' is final.
No compensation is payable to officers or employees for the transfer of their services, nor to the Chairman, trustees, or executive trustee for loss of office.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws.
The Unit Trust of India Act, 1963, is repealed, with certain savings.

title: THE SUPPRESSION OF UNLAWFUL ACTS AGAINST SAFETY OF MARITIME NAVIGATION AND FIXED PLATFORMS ON CONTINENTAL SHELF ACT, 2002
purpose: To give effect to the International Maritime Organisation Convention for Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Maritime Navigation and the Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Fixed Platforms Located on the Continental Shelf and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, including its territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and other maritime zones. It applies to offences committed outside India by any person, to ships navigating into, through, or from waters beyond India's territorial limits, and to offences committed on board ships in Indian territorial waters or against fixed platforms on India's continental shelf. It also applies to offenders found in Convention States, Protocol States, or other States.

key_definitions.Code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.Continental Shelf of India: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976).
key_definitions.Convention: The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Maritime Navigation, signed at Rome on the 10th day of March, 1988, as amended from time to time.
key_definitions.Convention State: A State Party to the Convention.
key_definitions.fixed platform: An artificial island, installation or structure permanently attached to the seabed for the purpose of exploration for, or exploitation of resources or for other economic purposes.
key_definitions.Protocol: The Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Fixed Platforms Located on the Continental Shelf adopted at Rome on the 10th day of March, 1988, as amended from time to time.
key_definitions.Protocol State: A State Party to the Protocol.
key_definitions.ship: A vessel of any type whatsoever not permanently attached to the seabed and includes dynamically supported craft, submersibles, or any other floating craft.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, application to various scenarios and entities, and the procedure for its commencement.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Code', 'Continental Shelf of India', 'Convention', 'Convention State', 'fixed platform', 'Protocol', 'Protocol State', and 'ship'.

main_sections.section_title: Offences against ship, fixed platform, cargo of a ship, maritime navigational facilities, etc.
main_sections.description: Details various unlawful and intentional acts that constitute offences, including violence against persons on board, destruction or damage to ships or platforms, seizure of ships or platforms, placing destructive devices, interference with navigational facilities, and communicating false information. It also outlines penalties and specifies when such acts are deemed offences committed within India.

Empowers the Central Government to confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution on gazetted officers of the Coast Guard or other Central Government gazetted officers, notwithstanding the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Provides for the establishment of Designated Courts by State Governments, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court, for the speedy trial of offences under this Act.

Specifies that all offences under this Act are exclusively triable by a Designated Court. It also outlines procedures for the detention of accused persons and allows Designated Courts to take cognizance of offences upon a complaint without committal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Code to proceedings before a Designated Court
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply to proceedings before a Designated Court, unless otherwise provided in this Act.

Imposes restrictions on granting bail to persons accused of offences under this Act. Bail can only be granted if the Public Prosecutor has had an opportunity to oppose the application, and the Court is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty and will not commit further offences while on bail.
Deals with the extradition of offenders to Convention States or Protocol States.

main_sections.section_title: Contracting parties to Convention or Protocol
main_sections.description: Refers to States that are contracting parties to the Convention or Protocol.

main_sections.section_title: Power to treat certain ships to be registered in Convention States
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to treat certain ships as registered in Convention States.
Requires prior sanction for initiating prosecution under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Presumptions as to offences under section 3
main_sections.description: Establishes presumptions regarding offences committed under section 3.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Whoever unlawfully and intentionally commits an act of violence against a person on board a fixed platform or a ship which is likely to endanger its safety or safe navigation is punishable with imprisonment up to ten years and a fine.
Destroying a fixed platform or ship, or causing damage that endangers its safety or navigation, is punishable with imprisonment for life.
Seizing or exercising control over a fixed platform or ship by force or intimidation is punishable with imprisonment for life.
Placing a device or substance likely to destroy or damage a fixed platform or ship, endangering its safety or navigation, is punishable with imprisonment up to fourteen years.
Destroying or damaging maritime navigational facilities or interfering with their operation, if it endangers safe navigation, is punishable with imprisonment up to fourteen years.
Communicating false information that endangers safe navigation is punishable with imprisonment up to fourteen years and a fine.
Causing death during the commission of or attempt to commit offences under section 3 (clauses a to d for platforms, a to f for ships) is punishable with death.
Attempting to commit or abetting the commission of an offence under sub-section (1) of section 3 is punishable as if the offence itself was committed.

Unlawfully or intentionally threatening a person to compel them to act or refrain from acting, if such a threat is likely to endanger the safe navigation of a ship or safety of a fixed platform, is punishable with the same penalty as the corresponding offence in sub-section (1) of section 3.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years and fine (for acts of violence against persons).
Imprisonment for life (for destroying or damaging ships/platforms, or seizing control).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to fourteen years (for placing destructive devices, damaging navigational facilities, or communicating false information).
Death (for causing death during the commission of certain offences).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years (for threatening to endanger a ship or fixed platform).
The same punishment as provided for the substantive offence for attempts and abetment.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Gazetted officers of the Coast Guard or other Central Government gazetted officers (for investigation and prosecution), Designated Courts (for trial).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation by empowered officers, speedy trials by Designated Courts, and application of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Provisions for bail are restricted. Extradition provisions are also in place.

rights: Right to a speedy trial before a Designated Court.
Right to be represented by legal counsel (implied by application of the Code of Criminal Procedure).
Protection against arbitrary detention (as per provisions for bail and committal to Designated Courts).
duties: Duty to not commit unlawful acts against the safety of maritime navigation and fixed platforms.
Duty of all officers of police and Government to assist empowered officers in executing the provisions of the Act.
obligations: Obligation for accused persons to face trial in Designated Courts.
Obligation for the Central Government to notify Convention/Protocol States when a person is taken into custody under sub-section (6) of section 3.

key_procedures: Investigation and arrest powers conferred on specific gazetted officers.
Designated Courts are to hold trials on a day-to-day basis as far as practicable.
Magistrates can authorize detention of accused persons for limited periods before forwarding them to the Designated Court.
Designated Courts can take cognizance of offences upon a complaint without committal.
Bail applications require the Public Prosecutor's opportunity to oppose and a high standard of proof for release.
Extradition procedures as per international agreements and domestic law.
administration: Central Government (for conferring investigation powers and notification), State Government (for specifying Designated Courts), Chief Justice of the High Court (for concurrence in specifying Designated Courts).
important_notes: The Act shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may appoint by notification in the Official Gazette.
A stateless person, for the purposes of the Act, is a person whose habitual residence is in India but does not have nationality of any country.
The Act aims to implement international conventions, therefore, provisions related to Convention States and Protocol States are significant for extraterritorial application and extradition.

title: THE OFFSHORE AREAS MINERAL (DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATION) ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide for the development and regulation of mineral resources in the territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and other maritime zones of India, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to all minerals in the offshore areas of India, excluding mineral oils and hydrocarbons. The 'offshore area' is defined as the territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and other maritime zones of India under the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976. It also applies to the regulation of mines and development of minerals in these areas under Union control.

key_definitions.administering authority: An authority notified in the Official Gazette by the Central Government for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.composite licence: An exploration licence-cum-production lease, a two-stage operating right for exploration followed by production operations.
key_definitions.exploration licence: A licence granted for the purpose of undertaking exploration operations.
key_definitions.exploration operation: Any operation undertaken for the purpose of exploring, locating, or proving mineral deposits.
key_definitions.mineral: Includes all minerals except mineral oil and hydrocarbon resources related thereto.
key_definitions.offshore area: The territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone and other maritime zones of India.
key_definitions.operating right: The right of a holder of a reconnaissance permit, a composite licence, an exploration licence, or a production lease.
key_definitions.production lease: A lease that confers an exclusive right for the purpose of undertaking production operations.
key_definitions.production operation: Any operation undertaken for the purpose of winning any mineral from the offshore area, including directly or indirectly necessary or incidental operations.
key_definitions.reconnaissance operation: Any preliminary geo-scientific survey undertaken for the purpose of searching or locating mineral deposits.
key_definitions.reconnaissance permit: A permit granted for the purpose of undertaking reconnaissance operations.
key_definitions.standard block: A block of the offshore area of one minute latitude by one minute longitude, including the seabed and its subsoil and waters superjacent to the seabed within such block.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes any ship, barge, boat, container, sailing vessel or stationary vessel or any other vessel of any description, submersible or otherwise and remotely operated or otherwise, used in any operation or any activity pursuant thereto.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of Union control.
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to take under its control the regulation of mines and the development of minerals in offshore areas.

Specifies that the Act applies to all minerals in the offshore areas, excluding mineral oils and hydrocarbons. It also clarifies that its provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other existing law in the offshore areas.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'administering authority', 'composite licence', 'exploration licence', 'mineral', 'offshore area', 'operating right', 'production lease', 'reconnaissance operation', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Reconnaissance, exploration or production to be under permit, licence or lease.
main_sections.description: States that no person can undertake reconnaissance, exploration, or production operations in offshore areas without a valid permit, licence, or lease granted under the Act. It also includes provisos for exceptions and requirements for data submission and confidentiality.

Outlines the conditions for granting an operating right, requiring the applicant to be an Indian national or a company and satisfy prescribed conditions. It also includes a proviso regarding grants to entities other than the Government, Government companies, or corporations for certain minerals.

main_sections.section_title: Power of entry, inspection, search and seizure.
main_sections.description: Grants powers to designated authorities to enter, inspect, search, and seize in relation to offshore areas for the purposes of the Act.
Defines what constitutes an offence under this Act.
Deals with civil liability arising from the Act and the process of adjudication.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall undertake any reconnaissance operation, exploration operation, or production operation in the offshore areas except under and in accordance with the prescribed terms and conditions of a permit, licence, or lease granted under this Act.

Every permittee, licensee, and lessee, and authorized government organizations/agencies/private entities must furnish all exploration and operational data, reports, samples, and other information to the administering authority as prescribed.

All exploration and operational data, reports, samples, and information collected pursuant to an operation shall be held in strict confidence and any dissemination or sharing is subject to prescribed terms and conditions.

The Central Government may authorize seaward artillery practice and provide for special measures for public safety, defense, naval operations, national security, and strategic considerations during war-like conditions or otherwise.
No operating right shall be granted, extended, or acquired otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of this Act and its rules; any contravention makes such rights void.

penalties: Offences under the Act (detailed in Chapter IV) are subject to penalties as prescribed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the 'administering authority' notified by the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, inspection, search, and seizure (Chapter III), adjudication (Chapter V), prosecution for offences (Chapter IV), and issuance of directions by the Central Government and administering authority (Section 21, 34B).

rights: Holders of permits, licences, or leases have the exclusive right to undertake specified operations within their granted areas.
Indian nationals and companies are eligible to be granted operating rights.
Right to appeal against certain orders.
duties: To undertake operations strictly under and in accordance with the terms and conditions of the granted permit, licence, or lease.
To furnish all exploration and operational data, reports, samples, and other information to the administering authority.
To maintain strict confidentiality of data, reports, and samples.
To ensure safety of persons and property (Section 19).
To prevent and control pollution and protect the marine environment (Section 20).
obligations: Obligation to obtain prescribed permits, licences, or leases before commencing operations.
Obligation to comply with directions issued by the Central Government or administering authority.
Obligation to pay royalty and fixed rent as prescribed (Sections 16, 17).

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining reconnaissance permits, exploration licences, composite licences, and production leases.
Procedure for furnishing exploration and operational data, reports, samples, and other information.
Procedure for entry, inspection, search, and seizure.
Procedure for adjudication of civil liability.
Procedure for compounding of offences.
Procedure for appeals and revision.
administration: The Central Government and an 'administering authority' notified by the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act excludes mineral oils and hydrocarbons from its scope.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions and revise orders.
Actions taken in good faith by individuals are protected.
The Act provides for the establishment of an Offshore Areas Mineral Trust (Section 16A).

title: THE BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide for conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components and fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising out of the use of biological resources, knowledge and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to all biological resources occurring in India or obtained from India, and traditional knowledge associated therewith. It regulates access to these resources and knowledge for research, bio-survey, bio-utilization, and commercial utilization. It also establishes authorities for conservation and benefit sharing.

key_definitions.access: Collecting, procuring or possessing any biological resource occurring in or obtained from India or traditional knowledge associated thereto, for the purposes of research or bio-survey or commercial utilisation.
key_definitions.biological_diversity: The variability among living organisms from all sources and the ecological complexes of which they are part and includes diversity within species or between species and of eco-systems.
key_definitions.biological_resources: Includes plants, animals, micro-organisms or parts of their genetic material and derivatives (excluding value added products), with actual or potential use or value for humanity, but does not include human genetic material.
key_definitions.commercial_utilisation: End uses of biological resources for commercial utilization such as drugs, industrial enzymes, food flavours, fragrance, cosmetics, emulsifiers, oleoresins, colours, extracts and genes used for improving crops and livestock through genetic intervention, but does not include conventional breeding or traditional practices in use in any agriculture, horticulture, poultry, dairy farming, animal husbandry or bee keeping.
key_definitions.fair_and_equitable_benefit_sharing: Sharing of benefits as determined by the National Biodiversity Authority under section 21.
key_definitions.sustainable_use: The use of components of biological diversity in such manner and at such rate that does not lead to the long-term decline of the biological diversity thereby maintaining its potential to meet the needs and aspirations of present and future generations.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'access', 'biological diversity', 'biological resources', 'commercial utilisation', 'fair and equitable benefit sharing', 'sustainable use', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Certain persons not to undertake Biodiversity related activities without approval of National Biodiversity Authority
main_sections.description: Specifies that non-citizens, non-resident Indian citizens, and foreign-controlled Indian entities require prior approval from the National Biodiversity Authority to access biological resources or associated knowledge for research, commercial utilization, or bio-survey/bio-utilization.

main_sections.section_title: Results of research not to be transferred to certain persons without approval of National Biodiversity Authority
main_sections.description: Prohibits the transfer or sharing of research results on biological resources or traditional knowledge for monetary consideration or otherwise to specific persons (as defined in section 3(2)) without prior written approval from the National Biodiversity Authority, with an exception for codified traditional knowledge exclusively for Indians.
Provides for the establishment of the National Biodiversity Authority.
Provides for the establishment of State Biodiversity Boards in each State.
Provides for the constitution of Biodiversity Management Committees at the local level.
Outlines the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: No person (as defined in Section 3(2)) shall undertake activities related to accessing biological resources occurring in India or associated knowledge for research, commercial utilization, bio-survey, or bio-utilization without the prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority.

Rule: Results of research on biological resources or traditional knowledge from India shall not be transferred to certain specified persons/entities without prior written approval of the National Biodiversity Authority, except for codified traditional knowledge for Indians.
Rule: Fair and equitable benefit sharing mechanisms are to be determined by the National Biodiversity Authority for the use of biological resources and associated traditional knowledge.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of various provisions of the Act, including unauthorized access to biological resources, transfer of research results without approval, and contravention of directions or orders issued by the Central Government, State Government, National Biodiversity Authority, or State Biodiversity Boards.
Specific penalties are detailed in Sections 55, 55A, and 56 of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards, Central Government, State Governments, and Biodiversity Management Committees, as per their respective roles and powers defined in the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through approvals, directions, imposition of penalties, adjudication of penalties, and legal proceedings for contravention of the Act's provisions. Powers of entry, inspection, and survey are also granted.

rights: Right to fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising out of the use of biological resources and associated knowledge.
Right of benefit claimers (conservers, holders of traditional knowledge) to receive benefits.
Right to appeal against orders of the National Biodiversity Authority or State Biodiversity Boards.
Right to approach the National Green Tribunal for certain appeals.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to develop national strategies and plans for conservation, promotion, and sustainable use of biological diversity.
Duty of the State Government to develop strategies and plans for conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity within the State.
Duty of the National Biodiversity Authority and State Biodiversity Boards to perform their functions related to conservation, regulation of access, and benefit sharing.
Duty of Biodiversity Management Committees to prepare and maintain the People's Biodiversity Register.
obligations: Obligation for certain persons to obtain prior approval from the National Biodiversity Authority for accessing biological resources or associated knowledge.
Obligation to share results of research and transfer biological resources in accordance with the Act's provisions.
Obligation to comply with directions and orders issued by the National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards, Central Government, and State Governments.
Obligation to make contributions to the National Biodiversity Fund, State Biodiversity Fund, or Local Biodiversity Fund as may be determined.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining approval from the National Biodiversity Authority for accessing biological resources or associated knowledge.
Procedure for transfer of research results and sharing of benefits.
Procedure for the establishment and functioning of the National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards, and Biodiversity Management Committees.
Procedure for appealing decisions of the authorities.
Procedure for adjudication and imposition of penalties.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments, through the National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards, and Biodiversity Management Committees.
important_notes: The Act reaffirms the sovereign rights of India over its biological resources.
The Act aims to give effect to the objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Nagoya Protocol.
Certain provisions may not apply in specific cases, as indicated in Section 40.
The Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, other existing laws (Section 59).

title: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
purpose: To provide for the responsibility of the Central Government to ensure inter-generational equity in fiscal management and long-term macro-economic stability by removing fiscal impediments in the effective conduct of monetary policy and prudent debt management consistent with fiscal sustainability through limits on the Central Government borrowings, debt and deficits, greater transparency in fiscal operations of the Central Government and conducting fiscal policy in a medium-term framework and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Pertains to the fiscal management and transparency of the Central Government of India.

key_definitions.fiscal_deficit: The excess of total disbursements, from the Consolidated Fund of India, excluding repayment of debt, over total receipts into the Fund (excluding the debt receipts), during a financial year.
key_definitions.central_government_debt: The total outstanding liabilities of the Central Government on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India, including external debt valued at current exchange rates; the total outstanding liabilities in the public account of India; and financial liabilities of bodies corporate or entities owned or controlled by the Central Government, which the Government is to repay or service from the annual financial statement, reduced by the cash balance available at the end of that date.
