key_definitions.fiscal_indicators: Measures such as numerical ceilings and proportions to gross domestic product, as may be prescribed, for evaluation of the fiscal position of the Central Government.
key_definitions.general_government_debt: The sum total of the debt of the Central Government and the State Governments, excluding inter-Governmental liabilities.
key_definitions.gross_domestic_product: The sum of the gross value added by all resident production units plus that part of taxes, less subsidies, on products, which is not included in the valuation of output, during a financial year, reckoned at current market prices.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.real_gross_domestic_product: Gross domestic product, reckoned at constant prices.
key_definitions.real_output_growth: Growth in real gross domestic product.
key_definitions.reserve_bank: The Reserve Bank of India constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its geographical extent (whole of India), and the procedure for its commencement through notification.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including fiscal deficit, Central Government debt, fiscal indicators, general Government debt, gross domestic product, prescribed, real gross domestic product, real output growth, and Reserve Bank.

main_sections.section_title: Fiscal policy statements to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to lay before Parliament annual statements of fiscal policy, including the Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement, Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, Macro-economic Framework Statement, and Medium-term Expenditure Framework Statement. It outlines the content and purpose of these statements.

Establishes fiscal management principles for the Central Government, including limits on fiscal deficit, general Government debt, and Central Government debt, and dictates measures for ensuring fiscal discipline. It also specifies conditions for deviations from these targets.

Restricts the Central Government from borrowing from the Reserve Bank, with certain exceptions for temporary cash flow needs and primary issues of Government securities under specific conditions related to fiscal targets.
Requires the Central Government to take measures for greater transparency in its fiscal operations and to minimize secrecy in the preparation of financial statements and demands for grants.

Mandates semi-annual reviews of budget receipts and expenditures by the Finance Minister, which are to be presented to Parliament. It also outlines measures to be taken by the Central Government in case of revenue shortfalls or expenditure excesses, including seeking Parliamentary approval for deviations.
This section appears in the arrangement of sections but is not fully provided in the document extract to detail its content.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be laid before each House of Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires that rules made under the Act be laid before each House of Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in respect of matters arising under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not bar the application of other existing laws.
Empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: The Central Government shall lay the Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement, Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, Macro-economic Framework Statement, and Medium-term Expenditure Framework Statement before Parliament annually.
The Central Government shall aim to limit the fiscal deficit to three per cent. of GDP by March 31, 2021.

The Central Government shall endeavor to ensure that general Government debt does not exceed sixty percent. and Central Government debt does not exceed forty percent. of GDP by the end of financial year 2024-2025.
The Central Government shall not give additional guarantees on the Consolidated Fund of India exceeding one-half percent. of GDP in any financial year.

The Central Government shall not borrow from the Reserve Bank, with specific exceptions for temporary cash needs and under certain conditions for subscribing to primary issues of government securities.
The Central Government shall take measures for greater transparency in its fiscal operations.
The Minister-in-charge of Finance shall review budget receipts and expenditures on a semi-annual basis and present the outcomes to Parliament.

In case of revenue shortfall or expenditure excess, the Central Government shall take appropriate measures to increase revenue or reduce expenditure, unless Parliament approves otherwise or the expenditure is constitutionally mandated, contractual, or cannot be postponed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Minister-in-charge of the Ministry of Finance, Parliament.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through laying of statements and reports before Parliament, review of fiscal trends, parliamentary approval for deviations, and potential application of rules made under the Act.

rights: Right to have fiscal policy statements laid before Parliament.
Right to know the fiscal management principles and targets.
Right to expect transparency in fiscal operations.
Right to have deviations from fiscal targets explained and approved by Parliament.
Protection of action taken in good faith under the Act.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to ensure fiscal responsibility and macro-economic stability.
Duty to adhere to fiscal deficit and debt limits.
Duty to conduct fiscal policy in a medium-term framework.
Duty to ensure transparency in fiscal operations.
Duty to take corrective measures for revenue shortfalls or expenditure excesses.
Duty to lay fiscal policy statements before Parliament.
Duty of the Minister-in-charge of Finance to review fiscal trends.
obligations: Obligation to comply with fiscal deficit and debt targets.
Obligation to seek Parliamentary approval for deviations from fiscal targets.
Obligation to make disclosures for fiscal transparency.
Obligation to report on fiscal reviews.

key_procedures: Laying of Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement, Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, Macro-economic Framework Statement, and Medium-term Expenditure Framework Statement before Parliament annually.
Review of receipts and expenditures on a half-yearly basis by the Minister-in-charge of Finance and presentation of outcomes to Parliament.
Taking appropriate measures for increasing revenue or reducing expenditure in case of shortfalls or excesses, with potential need for Parliamentary approval for deviations.
administration: The Central Government, specifically indicated by the Minister-in-charge of the Ministry of Finance for reviews and by the Central Government for making rules and notifications.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2018, with several sections being omitted or substituted, affecting specific targets and clauses related to fiscal management.
The commencement date of the Act was July 5, 2004.

Deviations from fiscal deficit targets are permitted under specific circumstances such as national security, act of war, national calamity, collapse of agriculture, structural reforms with unanticipated fiscal implications, or significant decline in real output growth, but require justification and a path for return to targets.

Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, or expenditure required under agreement/contract, or expenditure that cannot be postponed/curtailed, is exempt from certain corrective measures in case of revenue shortfalls or expenditure excesses.

title: The Parel Investments and Trading Private Limited and Domestic Gas Private Limited (Taking Over of Management) Repeal Act, 2005
purpose: To repeal the Parel Investments and Trading Private Limited and Domestic Gas Private Limited (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1979, following the assignment and transfer of the undertakings and business of the said companies to the Central Government and subsequently to Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited.
scope: This act applies to the Parel Investments and Trading Private Limited (PITCL) and Domestic Gas Private Limited (DGPL). It deals with the repeal of a previous act that took over the management of these companies, and the revesting of their management and assets not related to liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) back to their respective boards of directors.

key_definitions.PITCL: Parel Investments and Trading Private Limited
key_definitions.the said Companies: Parel Investments and Trading Private Limited and Domestic Gas Private Limited collectively

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Parel Investments and Trading Private Limited and Domestic Gas Private Limited (Taking Over of Management) Repeal Act, 2005'.

Repeals the Parel Investments and Trading Private Limited and Domestic Gas Private Limited (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1979. It also provides for the revesting of management of PITCL and DGPL in their respective boards of directors, and the continuation of possession of assets not related to LPG. It further clarifies that actions taken under the repealed Act by the Central Government or the Custodian remain in force.

important_rules: The Parel Investments and Trading Private Limited and Domestic Gas Private Limited (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1979 is hereby repealed.
Upon repeal, the management of PITCL and DGPL shall be vested and deemed to have been vested in their respective boards of directors, to be appointed after the repeal.

Possession of assets of PITCL and DGPL related to their business, other than LPG business and not taken over by the Central Government under the repealed Act, shall be deemed to have been taken over and continued with the said Companies through their respective boards of directors.

Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or action taken, including any agreement entered into under the repealed Act by the Central Government or the Custodian, shall continue to be in force and have effect as if this Act had not been passed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Custodian (historically), and Boards of Directors (post-repeal for their respective businesses)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal provisions and contractual agreements as established by the previous Act and the subsequent Deeds of Assignment.

rights: The right of PITCL and DGPL to have their management vested in their respective boards of directors.
The right of PITCL and DGPL to retain possession of assets not related to LPG business.
duties: Duty of the Central Government and Custodian to facilitate the transfer of management and assets as per the Deeds of Assignment.
Duty of the respective boards of directors to manage the companies and their assets (excluding LPG business) in accordance with law.
obligations: Obligation to honor agreements entered into under the repealed Act.
Obligation to comply with the terms of the Memorandum of Compromise and Deeds of Assignment.

key_procedures: Appointment of respective boards of directors for PITCL and DGPL after the repeal of the 1979 Act.
Revesting of management of PITCL and DGPL in these newly appointed boards.
Continuation of possession of assets not related to LPG business by the said Companies through their boards.
administration: The Act itself is enacted by Parliament. The administration of the companies' affairs post-repeal falls under the respective boards of directors, with the Central Government having played a role in the acquisition and transfer of undertakings.
important_notes: The repeal is effective following the assignment and transfer of the companies' undertakings to the Central Government and then to Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited.
The act saves things done or actions taken under the repealed Act, ensuring continuity of legal obligations and agreements.

title: The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005
purpose: To prohibit unlawful activities in relation to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, safeguarding national security and preventing non-State actors and terrorists from acquiring such weapons.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, including its Exclusive Economic Zone. It applies to acts committed in India and acts committed outside India by Indian citizens, companies registered in India, ships and aircraft registered in India, foreigners in India, and persons in the service of the Government of India. It also applies to the export, transfer, re-transfer, transit, and trans-shipment of specified materials, equipment, and technologies pertinent to India as a Nuclear Weapon State, national security, or international obligations.

key_definitions.biological_weapons: Microbial or other biological agents, or toxins, of types and quantities with no justification for peaceful purposes; and weapons, equipment, or delivery systems specially designed to use such agents or toxins for hostile purposes or in armed conflict.
key_definitions.chemical_weapons: Toxic chemicals and their precursors (except for specified peaceful or protective purposes), munitions and devices designed to cause harm through these chemicals, and equipment specifically designed for their employment.
key_definitions.fissile_material: As defined in the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
key_definitions.radioactive_material: As defined in the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
key_definitions.item: Materials, equipment, and technology of any description, notified under this Act or any other Act related to relevant activity.
key_definitions.non_State_actor: A person or entity not acting under the lawful authority of any country.
key_definitions.nuclear_weapon_or_other_nuclear_explosiv: As determined by the Central Government.
key_definitions.relevant_activity: Development, production, handling, operation, maintenance, storage, or dissemination of nuclear, chemical, or biological weapons, or missiles designed for their delivery.
key_definitions.terrorist: As defined in the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.
key_definitions.weapons_of_mass_destruction: Any biological, chemical, or nuclear weapons.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

main_sections.section_title: Act in addition to other laws
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to any other relevant laws in force concerning matters covered by this Act.

Defines the territorial extent of the Act (whole of India including EEZ) and specifies who is liable under the Act for acts committed within or outside India, including citizens abroad, companies, ships, aircraft, foreigners in India, and government personnel.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as biological weapons, chemical weapons, fissile material, item, non-State actor, relevant activity, terrorist, and weapons of mass destruction.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition relating to weapons of mass destruction
main_sections.description: Prohibits unlawful manufacture, acquisition, possession, development, transport, or transfer of nuclear, biological, or chemical weapons and their means of delivery.
Specifies that offences under this Act are punishable and details various punishments for violations.

important_rules: No person shall unlawfully manufacture, acquire, possess, develop, or transport a nuclear weapon or other nuclear explosive device and their means of delivery.
No person shall unlawfully transfer, directly or indirectly, to any one a nuclear weapon or other nuclear explosive device, or transfer control over such a weapon, knowing it to be such.
No person shall unlawfully manufacture, acquire, possess, develop, or transport a biological or chemical weapon or their means of delivery.
No person shall unlawfully transfer, directly or indirectly, to any one biological or chemical weapons.
No person shall unlawfully transfer, directly or indirectly, to any one missiles specially designed for the delivery of weapons of mass destruction.
No person shall, directly or indirectly, transfer to a non-State actor or terrorist any material, equipment, and technology notified under this Act or any other Act related to relevant activity.

No person shall transfer, acquire, possess, or transport fissile or radioactive material intended to be used to cause death, serious injury, or property damage for intimidating purposes or compelling governments/organizations to act or abstain from acting.

penalties: Punishment for unauthorized export.
Punishment for violation of other provisions of the Act.
Penalty for using false or making forged documents.
Punishment for offences with respect to which no provision has been made.
Punishment for aiding non-State actor or terrorist.
Penalties for offences by companies.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, which may delegate powers to designated authorities, including a Licensing Authority and an Appellate Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of prohibitions and the imposition of penalties specified in the Act. The Central Government can also appoint Advisory Committees and delegate powers for effective implementation. Mechanisms provided under other relevant Acts shall continue to deal with matters covered by those Acts, with the Central Government's decision being final in case of doubt.

duties: Duty to comply with the prohibitions relating to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems.
Duty to not transfer materials, equipment, or technology to non-State actors or terrorists.
Duty to not engage in unlawful activities related to relevant items or activities.

key_procedures: Identification, designation, categorization, or regulation of export, transfer, re-transfer, trans-shipment, or transit of items related to relevant activity by the Central Government.
Designation or notification of items related to relevant activity for the purposes of the Act by the Central Government.
Appointment of Advisory Committees by the Central Government.
Delegation of powers by the Central Government to other authorities.
Appointment of a Licensing Authority and an Appellate Authority by the Central Government.
Procedures for handling offences and imposing penalties as outlined in sections 14-21.
administration: Central Government (may delegate powers to designated authorities, Licensing Authority, and Appellate Authority).
important_notes: The Act is in addition to other laws.
The Central Government's determination regarding nuclear weapons or other nuclear explosive devices is final.
The Central Government's decision in case of doubt regarding the scope of relevant Acts or this Act is final.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

title: THE COASTAL AQUACULTURE AUTHORITY ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Coastal Aquaculture Authority for regulating the activities connected with coastal aquaculture in the coastal areas and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to coastal areas, regulating coastal aquaculture activities. It also aims to protect the coastal environment and livelihoods of people in coastal areas.

key_definitions.aquaculture_input: Any material used in coastal aquaculture for maintaining water and soil quality, and for the growth and health of reared organisms. Includes seed, fertilizer, feed, growth supplement, probiotic, environment remediator, and disinfectant.
key_definitions.aqua_mapping: Geospatial coastal area distribution maps showing potential and suitable areas for coastal aquaculture.
key_definitions.aqua_zonation: Spatial planning zones for different species or methods of coastal aquaculture, notified by a State Government or the Authority for sustainable coastal aquaculture.
key_definitions.Authority: The Coastal Aquaculture Authority established under the Act.
key_definitions.biosecured_facility: A coastal aquaculture unit that implements biosecurity measures to prevent disease-causing pathogens.
key_definitions.biosecurity: Measures, strategies, or integrated approaches to analyze, manage, and prevent the risk of introduction or spread of harmful organisms, and minimize the risk of infectious disease transmission within coastal aquaculture units.
key_definitions.Brood_Stock_Multiplication_Centre: A coastal aquaculture unit that rears post larvae or juveniles, which are specific pathogen free, tolerant, or resistant, from a Nucleus Breeding Centre under strict biosecurity and disease surveillance.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Authority.
key_definitions.coastal_aquaculture: Rearing and cultivation of any life stages of fish, crustacean, mollusc, finfish, seaweed, or other aquatic life under controlled conditions in saline or brackish water in coastal areas. Excludes freshwater aquaculture.
key_definitions.coastal_aquaculture_unit: Any facility engaged in coastal aquaculture or allied activities, including Nucleus Breeding Centres, Brood Stock Multiplication Centres, hatcheries, and farms.
key_definitions.coastal_area: Area declared as Coastal Regulation Zone or such other area specified by the Central Government.
key_definitions.coastal_environment: The land and water area in the coastal area, including the system of living organisms and physical surroundings.
key_definitions.farm: A coastal aquaculture unit where culturing of aquatic life is done in ponds, pens, cages, etc., in coastal areas. Includes nursery rearing but not freshwater aquaculture.
key_definitions.hatchery: A coastal aquaculture unit engaged in breeding and seed production of aquatic life in saline or brackish water. Includes rearing of nauplii and live feed but not freshwater aquaculture.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Authority, including the Chairperson.
key_definitions.Nucleus_Breeding_Centre: A coastal aquaculture unit with biosecured activity for producing domesticated specific pathogen free, tolerant, or resistant stocks.
key_definitions.operator: Any person or firm engaged in the operation of coastal aquaculture activity.
key_definitions.owner: In relation to a coastal aquaculture unit, includes legal heirs, agents, operators, mortgagees, lessees, sub-lessees, or persons in actual possession.
key_definitions.pharmacologically_active_substance_or_an: A substance that exhibits antimicrobial activity against microorganisms.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Authority under this Act.
key_definitions.specific_pathogen_free_or_specific_patho: Free of, resistant to, or tolerant to pathogens listed by the World Organisation for Animal Health or notified by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that certain provisions (Section 27) come into force immediately, while others come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'aquaculture input', 'aqua mapping', 'aqua zonation', 'Authority', 'biosecured facility', 'biosecurity', 'Brood Stock Multiplication Centre', 'Chairperson', 'coastal aquaculture', 'coastal aquaculture unit', 'coastal area', 'coastal environment', 'farm', 'hatchery', 'member', 'Nucleus Breeding Centre', 'operator', 'owner', 'pharmacologically active substance or antimicrobial agent', 'prescribed', 'regulations', and terms related to specific pathogen status. It also states that undefined terms will have meanings as per the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to take measures to protect environment
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to take necessary measures, including prescribing guidelines, to regulate coastal aquaculture and ensure it does not harm the coastal environment, promoting responsible coastal aquaculture.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Authority and appointment of Chairperson and members
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Coastal Aquaculture Authority. Details its composition, including the Chairperson (a former High Court Judge) and members representing various expert fields and government ministries, as well as coastal states and Union territories. Also specifies the term of office and appointment of members.

Outlines the conditions under which a person is disqualified from being appointed as a member of the Authority, including conviction of certain offenses, being an undischarged insolvent, being of unsound mind, dismissal from government service, or having a financial or other interest likely to affect their functions.
States that a member ceasing to hold office is eligible for reappointment for not more than two consecutive terms.

Specifies rules regarding the meetings of the Authority, including times, places, quorum, and the procedure for presiding over meetings. Decisions are made by a majority vote, with the Chairperson having a casting vote.
Allows the Authority to constitute committees for efficient discharge of its functions, specifying the number of persons, functions, and terms and conditions for such committees.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancy in Authority not to invalidate proceeding
main_sections.description: Ensures that any act or proceeding of the Authority is not invalidated due to vacancies, defects in constitution, or procedural irregularities that do not affect the merits of the case.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of officers, consultants and other employees of Authority
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to appoint necessary officers, consultants, and employees on terms and conditions specified by regulations.
Likely deals with the appointment and role of the Secretary of the Authority (though the full text of this section is not provided in the excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Authentication of orders and other instruments of Authority
main_sections.description: Governs the formal authentication of orders and other official documents issued by the Authority.
Details the various functions and responsibilities of the Coastal Aquaculture Authority.
Confers the power of entry upon the Authority or its authorized officers for the purpose of carrying out its functions.
Prohibits the use of specific materials in coastal aquaculture.
Mandates registration for carrying out coastal aquaculture activities.
Deals with the authorization of officers by the Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for carrying on coastal aquaculture in contravention of provisions of Act
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals or entities carrying out coastal aquaculture in violation of the Act's provisions.
Provides a mechanism for appealing decisions made under the Act.
Specifies how offenses under the Act will be taken cognizance of by courts.
Details how payments will be made to the Authority.
Establishes the fund of the Coastal Aquaculture Authority and specifies its sources and utilization.
Requires the Authority to prepare and present an annual budget.
Mandates the preparation and submission of an annual report by the Authority.
Covers the accounting procedures and auditing of the Authority's accounts.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson and other members, officers and other employees of Authority, etc., to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Chairperson, members, officers, and employees of the Authority as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith by individuals acting under the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Arrears of cost and penalty recoverable as arrears of land revenue
main_sections.description: Stipulates that arrears of costs and penalties under the Act are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Authority to make regulations
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Requires that all rules and regulations made under the Act be laid before Parliament for a specified period.
Deals with the validation of certain actions or proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain provisions and amendments retrospectively
main_sections.description: Provides for the retrospective validation of certain provisions and amendments to the Act.

important_rules: Coastal aquaculture activities must be registered with the Authority (Section 13).
Coastal aquaculture must not cause detriment to the coastal environment (Section 3).
Specific materials are prohibited for use in coastal aquaculture (Section 12A).
Coastal aquaculture units must adhere to biosecurity measures to prevent disease spread (Section 2(ad), 2(ae)).
All rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament (Section 26).

penalties: Penalty for carrying on coastal aquaculture in contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 14).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Coastal Aquaculture Authority and its authorized officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration requirements, prohibition of certain materials, penalties for contravention, and by taking cognizance of offenses. Arrears of costs and penalties are recoverable as arrears of land revenue (Section 22A).

rights: Right to appeal against decisions made under the Act (Section 14A).
duties: Duty of the Central Government to take measures to protect the coastal environment and promote responsible coastal aquaculture (Section 3).
Duty of operators to comply with the Act's provisions and regulations.
obligations: Obligation to register for coastal aquaculture activities.
Obligation to adhere to biosecurity measures.
Obligation to comply with rules and regulations made by the Central Government and the Authority.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Coastal Aquaculture Authority, including appointment of Chairperson and members.
Meetings of the Authority and decision-making processes.
Registration process for coastal aquaculture activities.
Process for appealing decisions made under the Act.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules and the Authority to make regulations.
Procedure for auditing the Authority's accounts.
administration: The Coastal Aquaculture Authority, with the Central Government having overarching powers, including rule-making and oversight.
important_notes: The Act aims to balance aquaculture development with environmental protection and livelihood support in coastal areas.
Amendments introduced by Act 27 of 2023 significantly updated definitions and structure.
The Act draws upon definitions from the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 for terms not explicitly defined within it.

title: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
purpose: To provide for the enhancement of livelihood security of the households in rural areas of the country by providing at least one hundred days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to rural areas, defined as any area in a State except those covered by any urban local body or a Cantonment Board. It guarantees employment to every household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.

key_definitions.adult: A person who has completed eighteen years of age.
key_definitions.household: Members of a family related by blood, marriage or adoption, normally residing together and sharing meals or holding a common ration card.
key_definitions.rural area: Any area in a State except those areas covered by any urban local body or a Cantonment Board established or constituted under any law for the time being in force.
key_definitions.unskilled manual work: Any physical work which any adult person is capable of doing without any skill or special training.

main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act, its geographical extent (whole of India), and commencement date. It also states that different dates can be appointed for different areas and the Act must be applicable within five years of enactment.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'adult', 'applicant', 'Block', 'Central Council', 'District Programme Coordinator', 'household', 'implementing agency', 'minimum wage', 'National Fund', 'notification', 'preferred work', 'prescribed', 'Programme Officer', 'project', 'rural area', 'Scheme', 'State Council', 'unskilled manual work', and 'wage rate'.

main_sections.section_title: Guarantee of rural employment to households
main_sections.description: States that the State Government shall provide at least one hundred days of guaranteed unskilled manual work in a financial year to every household in notified rural areas whose adult members volunteer. It also specifies wage entitlement, disbursement timeline (weekly or not later than a fortnight), and provision for additional employment.

main_sections.section_title: Employment Guarantee Schemes for rural areas
main_sections.description: Mandates State Governments to make a Scheme for guaranteed employment within six months of the Act's commencement. It outlines the requirement for at least 100 days of employment per household, subject to conditions and volunteerism. It also provides for interim schemes if state-specific schemes are not notified.

Empowers the Central Government to specify wage rates, which cannot be less than sixty rupees per day. If no Central Government rate is fixed, the State Government's minimum wage for agricultural labourers will apply.

Entitles an applicant to a daily unemployment allowance if employment is not provided within fifteen days of application or seeking date. The allowance rate is determined by the State Government, with minimums of one-fourth and one-half of the wage rate for the first thirty days and the remaining period, respectively. Liability for this allowance ceases under specific conditions like reporting for work, completion of sought employment period, or achieving 100 days of work.

Establishes the Central Employment Guarantee Council to discharge functions and duties assigned by the Act. It is headquartered in Delhi and comprises a Chairperson and representatives from Central Ministries.
Outlines the responsibilities of Gram Panchayats in implementing the Scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Social audit of work by Gram Sabha
main_sections.description: Mandates social audits of work by the Gram Sabha.
Specifies penalties for non-compliance with the Act's provisions.
States that this Act has an overriding effect on other laws in case of conflict.

important_rules: Households in rural areas are guaranteed at least one hundred days of unskilled manual work in a financial year if adult members volunteer.
Wages must be disbursed on a weekly basis or within a fortnight of work completion.
State Governments must notify Employment Guarantee Schemes within six months of the Act's commencement.
Unemployment allowance is payable if employment is not provided within fifteen days of application, with specific minimum rates.
An applicant can be disentitled to unemployment allowance for three months if they do not accept provided employment, fail to report for work, or remain absent without permission.

penalties: Penalty for non-compliance is specified in Section 25.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities are involved, including the Central Government, State Governments, Central Employment Guarantee Council, State Employment Guarantee Council, District Programme Coordinator, Programme Officer, and Gram Panchayats.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves the establishment of schemes, provision of guaranteed employment, payment of wages and unemployment allowances, monitoring through councils and audits, and penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to at least one hundred days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year for households in rural areas whose adult members volunteer.
Right to receive wages at the specified wage rate for days worked.
Right to receive unemployment allowance if employment is not provided within the stipulated time.
Right to facilities as specified in Schedule II.
Right to seek employment under the Scheme at any time even after disentitlement to unemployment allowance.
duties: Duty of the State Government to provide guaranteed employment.
Duty of the Central Government to specify wage rates and provide directions.
Duty of implementing agencies to provide employment and facilities.
Duty of applicants to report for work when notified.
Duty of Gram Sabha to conduct social audits.
obligations: Households have an obligation to volunteer their adult members for unskilled manual work.
Individuals have an obligation to accept provided employment and report for work when notified.

key_procedures: Application for employment under a Scheme.
Notification by the Programme Officer or implementing agency to report for work.
Disbursement of wages on a weekly basis or within a fortnight.
Disbursement of unemployment allowance, if eligible, within fifteen days of becoming due.
Social audit of work by the Gram Sabha.
Grievance redressal mechanism as per Section 19.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments, along with various councils and designated officers (District Programme Coordinator, Programme Officer), are responsible for the administration of the Act. The Central Employment Guarantee Council and State Employment Guarantee Councils play significant roles in monitoring and advising.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2009 to include 'Mahatma Gandhi' in its title.
The Act was made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh in 2019.
Specific features of the Scheme are detailed in Schedule I, and minimum facilities for persons employed are in Schedule II.
The Central Government has the power to give directions to State Governments and to make rules.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws in case of conflict.

title: The Government Securities Act, 2006
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to Government securities and their management by the Reserve Bank of India.
scope: Applies to Government securities created and issued by the Central Government or a State Government, whether before or after the commencement of the Act. It applies to all States except Jammu and Kashmir initially, and to Union territories. It can also apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir upon adoption by its legislature.

key_definitions.agent: A scheduled bank or any other person specified as such.
key_definitions.bond_ledger_account: An account with the Bank or an agent where Government securities are held in dematerialised form at the credit of the holder.
key_definitions.constituents_subsidiary_general_ledger_a: A subsidiary general ledger account opened and maintained with the Bank by an agent on behalf of its constituents.
key_definitions.government: In relation to a Government security, it means the Central or State Government issuing the security.
key_definitions.government_security: A security created and issued by the Government for raising a public loan or for other notified purposes, having one of the forms mentioned in section 3.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by regulations made under this Act.
key_definitions.specified: Specified by the Bank in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act, defines its applicability to Government securities issued by Central or State Governments, and outlines the commencement date, initially for all States except Jammu and Kashmir, and Union territories, with provisions for adoption by Jammu and Kashmir.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'agent', 'Bank', 'bond ledger account', 'constituents’ subsidiary general ledger account', 'Government', 'Government security', 'prescribed', 'promissory note', and 'specified'.

Specifies the permissible forms of Government securities, which can be prescribed or include Government promissory notes, bearer bonds, stock, or securities held in a bond ledger account. 'Stock' is further defined in relation to registered securities and those held in subsidiary general ledger accounts.

Details the opening and maintenance of subsidiary general ledger accounts, including constituents' subsidiary general ledger accounts and bond ledger accounts, by the Bank. It clarifies that Government securities can be held on behalf of constituents in such accounts, and the holder is deemed the holder, with the constituent as the beneficial owner entitled to benefits and liabilities.

Outlines the requirements for valid transfer of Government securities, mandating that the transfer must convey full title. It specifies the form and manner of transfer and provides for execution on behalf of individuals unable to write. It also states that this section does not affect orders made by the Bank or Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Holding of Government securities by holders of public offices
main_sections.description: Allows Government securities to be held in the name of a public office if declared by the Government. It details the automatic transfer of such securities to succeeding holders of the office and outlines procedures for transfers to other parties or by authorized persons during temporary absence. This section applies to both single and joint holders of offices.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of title to Government security of deceased sole holder or joint holders
main_sections.description: Governs the recognition of title to Government securities upon the death of a sole or all joint holders. It primarily recognizes executors, administrators, or holders of succession certificates. It also allows recognition based on court decrees, orders from empowered authorities, or other prescribed documents. A provision for simplified recognition for securities up to a certain value (initially Rs. 1 lakh, extendable to Rs. 1 crore) is included.

main_sections.section_title: Right of survivors of joint holders or several payees
main_sections.description: Establishes that in case of joint holders of a Government security, the title vests in the survivor(s) upon the death of one or more. Similarly, if a security is payable to several payees, it becomes payable to the survivor(s) or their representatives. This is subject to rights of representatives against survivors.

main_sections.section_title: Nomination by holders of Government securities
main_sections.description: Allows holders of Government securities (other than promissory notes or bearer bonds) to nominate one or more persons who would become entitled to the security and payment upon the death of the sole holder or all joint holders, to the exclusion of others, unless the nomination is varied or cancelled. It also covers scenarios with multiple nominees, minors, and declares that payments made to nominees constitute a full discharge for the Government or Bank.

important_rules: Rule: Government securities can be held in dematerialised form in a subsidiary general ledger account or bond ledger account.
Rule: Transfers of Government securities must be in the prescribed form and manner and must convey full title.

Rule: Upon the death of a sole or all joint holders, title to Government securities generally passes to executors, administrators, or succession certificate holders, with provisions for simplified procedures for lower-value securities or through nomination.
Rule: For Government securities held jointly, title vests in the survivor(s) upon the death of any holder.

Rule: Holders of Government securities can nominate individuals to receive the security and payment upon their death, overriding other succession laws except for specific provisions related to nominees.

penalties: Contravention of provisions and penalties are covered under Section 30, though specific details of penalties are not provided in the excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Reserve Bank of India (referred to as 'Bank').
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the Bank's powers to require information, cause inspections, issue directions (Section 29), make orders (Sections 12, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20), and through prescribed procedures and regulations.

rights: Right to full title transfer of Government securities.
Beneficial owners have the right to claim benefits and be subject to liabilities for securities held in constituents' subsidiary general ledger accounts.
Right of survivors to hold Government securities upon the death of joint holders.
Nominees have the right to receive Government securities and payments upon the death of the holder(s), subject to nomination rules.
duties: Holders of constituents' subsidiary general ledger accounts have a duty to maintain records and adopt procedures for safeguarding constituents' interests.
Holders of public offices who transfer securities must do so by signature and name of the office as laid down in section 5.
obligations: The Government or the Bank is absolved of liability after making payments to nominees as per nomination rules.

key_procedures: Transfer of Government securities: Must be in prescribed form and manner, conveying full title. For those unable to write, execution can be done on their behalf as prescribed.
Recognition of title upon death: Generally requires executors, administrators, or succession certificates. Simplified procedures may apply for lower value securities or through nomination.
Nomination: Holders can nominate persons, who become entitled upon death. Procedures for nomination, variation, cancellation, and for minor nominees are prescribed.
administration: The Reserve Bank of India (referred to as 'Bank').
important_notes: The Act applies to Government securities issued by both Central and State Governments.
Special provisions exist for holding Government securities in the name of public offices.
The Act overrides certain provisions of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, and the Indian Succession Act, 1925, in specific contexts related to Government securities.
The Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988, does not prohibit holding Government securities on behalf of a constituent in a constituents' subsidiary general ledger account.
The Reserve Bank of India's powers under this Act may not apply to International Financial Services Centres (Section 31A).

title: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
purpose: To provide for the prohibition of solemnisation of child marriages and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India and applies to all citizens of India without and beyond India. An exception is made for the Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry. State amendments may alter applicability within specific states.

key_definitions.child: A person who, if a male, has not completed twenty-one years of age, and if a female, has not completed eighteen years of age.
key_definitions.child_marriage: A marriage to which either of the contracting parties is a child.
key_definitions.contracting_party: Either of the parties whose marriage is or is about to be thereby solemnised.
key_definitions.Child_Marriage_Prohibition_Officer: Includes the Child Marriage Prohibition Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 16.
key_definitions.district_court: Includes Family Court, city civil court, principal civil court of original jurisdiction, and any other civil court specified by the State Government to have jurisdiction.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India, with an exception), and the procedure for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'child', 'child marriage', 'contracting party', 'Child Marriage Prohibition Officer', 'district court', and 'minor'.

main_sections.section_title: Child marriages to be voidable at the option of contracting party being a child
main_sections.description: States that child marriages are voidable at the option of the contracting party who was a child at the time of marriage. Petitions for annulment can be filed by the child contracting party within two years of attaining majority.

main_sections.section_title: Provision for maintenance and residence to female contracting party to child marriage
main_sections.description: Empowers the district court to order maintenance and residence for the female contracting party to a child marriage until her remarriage, considering her needs and the means of the paying party.

main_sections.section_title: Custody and maintenance of children of child marriages
main_sections.description: Mandates the district court to make orders for the custody and maintenance of children born of child marriages, with the welfare and best interests of the child as the paramount consideration.

main_sections.section_title: Legitimacy of children born of child marriages
main_sections.description: Declares that children begotten or conceived of a child marriage, even if annulled, are deemed legitimate for all purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for male adult marrying a child
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for a male adult (above 18 years) who contracts a child marriage, with rigorous imprisonment and/or fine.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for solemnising a child marriage
main_sections.description: Provides punishment for anyone who performs, conducts, directs, or abets a child marriage, unless they prove they believed it was not a child marriage.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for promoting or permitting solemnisation of child marriages
main_sections.description: Punishes persons in charge of a child who promote or permit a child marriage, or negligently fail to prevent it. A proviso exempts women from imprisonment in the central act, but this is omitted in the Karnataka amendment.

main_sections.section_title: Marriage of a minor child to be void in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Declares marriages void if a minor child is taken, enticed, compelled by force or deceit, sold for marriage, or trafficked after marriage for immoral purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Power of court to issue injunction prohibiting child marriages
main_sections.description: Grants Judicial Magistrates and Metropolitan Magistrates the power to issue injunctions prohibiting child marriages upon application or information.
Provides for the appointment of Child Marriage Prohibition Officers by the State Government.

important_rules: Child marriages are voidable at the option of the child contracting party.
The district court must consider the welfare and best interests of children born of child marriages when making custody and maintenance orders.
A male adult marrying a child faces punishment of rigorous imprisonment and/or fine.
Those solemnising, promoting, or permitting child marriages are also liable to punishment.
Marriages involving a minor child taken, enticed, compelled, sold, or trafficked for marriage are null and void.
Courts have the power to issue injunctions to prevent child marriages.

penalties: Punishment for male adult marrying a child: Rigorous imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees or both.
Punishment for solemnising a child marriage: Rigorous imprisonment up to two years and/or fine up to one lakh rupees.
Punishment for promoting or permitting child marriages: Rigorous imprisonment up to two years and fine up to one lakh rupees (with an exception for women in the original act).
State amendments may alter the terms of imprisonment or fines.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Child Marriage Prohibition Officers, District Magistrates, Judicial Magistrates of the first class, Metropolitan Magistrates, and District Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation, prosecution for offences, issuance of injunctions, annulment of marriages, and orders for maintenance and custody. District Magistrates can take measures to stop child marriages, using minimum force if required.

rights: The right of a child contracting party to make a child marriage voidable.
The right of a female contracting party to maintenance and residence until remarriage.
The right of children born of child marriages to custody, maintenance, and legitimacy.
The right of any person to complain about an impending child marriage and seek an injunction.
duties: The duty of persons in charge of a child to prevent them from entering into child marriages.
The duty of individuals to refrain from solemnising, promoting, or permitting child marriages.
The duty of authorities to investigate and take action against child marriages.
obligations: Obligation of the male contracting party (or his parent/guardian) to pay maintenance to the female contracting party.
Obligation of parties and parents/guardians to return gifts received during a child marriage when a decree of nullity is granted.
Obligation of the district court to make orders for the welfare of children of child marriages.

key_procedures: Filing a petition for annulment of a child marriage by the child contracting party in the district court (within two years of attaining majority).
The district court granting a decree of nullity and making orders for the return of gifts.
The district court making orders for maintenance and residence for the female contracting party.
The district court making orders for custody and maintenance of children born of child marriages.
Application to a Judicial Magistrate or Metropolitan Magistrate for an injunction to prohibit a child marriage.
District Magistrate acting as Child Marriage Prohibition Officer to prevent mass child marriages on specific days.
administration: The administration of this Act involves the Central Government (for commencement notification) and State Governments (for appointing Child Marriage Prohibition Officers and specifying courts). The District Courts and Magistracy play a crucial role in enforcement.
important_notes: State amendments can significantly alter the provisions of the Act, for example, making certain child marriages void ab initio (Karnataka and Haryana).
The exception for Renoncants of Pondicherry is noted. Amendments have removed the exception for Jammu and Kashmir.
The proviso in Section 11(1) regarding women not being punishable with imprisonment has been omitted in the Karnataka amendment.

title: The Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act, 2007
purpose: To make provisions for the development and regulation of warehouses, negotiability of warehouse receipts, establishment of a Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India, with an exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh). It covers the business of maintaining warehouses and issuing warehouse receipts.

key_definitions.accreditation agency: An agency registered with the Authority to issue certificates of accreditation to warehouses.
key_definitions.actionable claim: As defined in section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.
key_definitions.Authority: The Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority established under the Act.
key_definitions.depositor: A person who delivers goods to a warehouseman for storage.
key_definitions.goods: All tangible movable goods (other than actionable claims, money and securities), whether fungible or not.
key_definitions.negotiable warehouse receipt: A warehouse receipt under which the goods are deliverable to the depositor or order, and its endorsement transfers the goods.
key_definitions.non-negotiable warehouse receipt: A warehouse receipt that is not a negotiable warehouse receipt.
key_definitions.warehouse: Any premises conforming to Authority-specified requirements, where a warehouseman takes custody of deposited goods.
key_definitions.warehousing business: The business of maintaining warehouses for storage of goods and issuing negotiable warehouse receipts.
key_definitions.warehouse receipt: An acknowledgement, written or electronic, of receipt of goods for storage issued by a warehouseman.
key_definitions.warehouseman: Any person granted a registration certificate by the Authority or an accreditation agency to carry on the business of warehousing.

main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act, its geographical application (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir), and the date it comes into force through notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'accreditation agency', 'Authority', 'goods', 'warehouse', 'warehouse receipt', and 'warehouseman'.

main_sections.section_title: Requirement of registration for warehouses issuing negotiable warehouse receipts
main_sections.description: Mandates registration for anyone commencing or carrying on warehousing business, with provisions for existing businesses and exceptions for warehouses not issuing negotiable receipts.

Details the process for applying for registration of a warehouse, including application form, fees, conditions for granting registration, and satisfaction of adequacy of facilities and applicant's criteria.

Outlines the process for accrediting agencies to issue certificates of accreditation for warehouses issuing negotiable warehouse receipts, including determination of number of agencies, application requirements, and prescribed forms and conditions.

Defines the liability of warehousemen for loss or injury to goods, specifying compensation in cases of failure to exercise due care, unavoidable circumstances, or negligence. It also lists circumstances for which a warehouseman is not responsible (force majeure, etc.).

Specifies the duty of a warehouseman to deliver goods to the holder of a negotiable receipt on demand, provided certain conditions are met (satisfying lien, surrendering receipt, acknowledging receipt). It also places the burden of proof on the warehouseman if they refuse to deliver.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of warehouseman to keep records and accounts of warehouse business
main_sections.description: Requires warehousemen to maintain complete and accurate records and accounts of all warehouse transactions, including goods received and withdrawn, issued, returned, or cancelled receipts. These records must be made available for Authority inspection.

main_sections.section_title: Special powers of warehouseman to deal with perishable and hazardous goods
main_sections.description: Grants warehousemen special powers to deal with perishable or hazardous goods that may deteriorate or damage other property, including the right to notify the holder to satisfy the lien and remove the goods.
Provides for the establishment and incorporation of the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority.
Details the powers and functions of the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority.
Covers offences and penalties related to contravention of the provisions of the Act.
States that this Act has an overriding effect on other laws in case of conflict, concerning matters covered by this Act.

important_rules: No person shall commence or carry on the warehousing business unless they have obtained a registration certificate from the Authority for the concerned warehouse, unless the warehouse does not propose to issue negotiable warehouse receipts.
A warehouseman is liable for loss of, or injury to, goods caused by their failure to exercise reasonable care, similar to that of a vigilant owner.
Warehousemen must deliver goods to the holder of a negotiable receipt upon demand, after the holder satisfies the lien, surrenders the receipt, and acknowledges receipt of the goods.
Warehousemen must maintain complete and accurate records and accounts of all warehouse operations and make them available for inspection by the Authority.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for offences under the Act, including offenses by companies.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority and Courts (for cognizance of offences).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration requirements, power to inspect records, imposition of penalties for offences, and legal proceedings for cognizance of offences.

rights: Right to receive goods from the warehouseman upon fulfilling the conditions (satisfying lien, surrendering receipt, acknowledging receipt).
Right to receive compensation for loss or damage to goods due to warehouseman's negligence or failure to exercise due care.
Right to appeal to the Appellate Authority against decisions of the Authority.
duties: Duty of warehouseman to exercise due care in safeguarding deposited goods.
Duty of warehouseman to deliver goods to the rightful holder of the warehouse receipt.
Duty of warehouseman to maintain accurate records and accounts.
Duty of depositor to satisfy the warehouse lien and fulfill conditions for delivery.
obligations: Obligation for warehousemen to register with the Authority if issuing negotiable warehouse receipts.
Obligation to comply with regulations and guidelines issued by the Authority.
Obligation to pay fees and security deposits as prescribed for registration.

key_procedures: Application for registration of a warehouse with the Authority, including fulfilling prescribed forms, fees, terms, and conditions, and demonstrating adequate facilities and applicant's competence.
Application for registration as an accreditation agency, including fulfilling prescribed qualifications, fees, and security deposits.
Delivery of goods by a warehouseman to the holder of a warehouse receipt upon demand, after satisfying the lien, surrendering the receipt, and acknowledging receipt of goods.
Dealing with perishable or hazardous goods by a warehouseman, including notifying the holder and requiring removal of goods.
Appeals to the Appellate Authority against decisions of the Authority.
administration: The Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority is established to administer the Act. The Central Government also has powers related to directions, superseding the Authority, and making rules.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 25th October, 2010.
The Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh from 30th October, 2019.
A warehouse registered under this Act is also eligible to issue non-negotiable warehouse receipts.
The Chairperson and members of the Authority are considered public servants.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

title: THE PAYMENT AND SETTLEMENT SYSTEMS ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for the regulation and supervision of payment systems in India and to designate the Reserve Bank of India as the authority for that purpose and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to the regulation and supervision of payment systems, including banks, post office savings banks, banking companies, co-operative banks, and other entities specified by the Reserve Bank. It also applies to derivatives and trade repositories as specified by the Reserve Bank. Certain provisions may not apply to stock exchanges or clearing corporations of stock exchanges, and specifically, powers of the Reserve Bank may not apply to International Financial Services Centres.

key_definitions.bank: Includes a bank in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act, 1934, post office savings bank, a banking company, a co-operative bank, and other banks specified by the Reserve Bank.
key_definitions.derivative: An instrument to be settled at a future date, whose value is derived from changes in interest rates, foreign exchange rates, credit ratings, security prices, or other underlying factors.
key_definitions.electronic funds transfer: Any transfer of funds initiated by a person through electronic means, including point of sale, ATM, direct deposit/withdrawal, telephone, internet, and card payments.
key_definitions.payment system: A system enabling payment between a payer and a beneficiary, involving clearing, payment, or settlement services. It excludes stock exchanges but includes credit card, debit card, smart card, and money transfer operations.
key_definitions.system participant: A bank or any other person participating in a payment system, including the system provider.
key_definitions.system provider: A person who operates an authorised payment system.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the process for its commencement, which is to be appointed by the Central Government by notification.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'bank', 'derivative', 'electronic funds transfer', 'payment system', 'system participant', and 'system provider'.
The Reserve Bank is designated as the authority for the regulation and supervision of payment systems. It exercises these powers through a Payments Regulatory Board.

main_sections.section_title: Payment system not to operate without authorisation
main_sections.description: No person, except the Reserve Bank, can operate a payment system without authorization from the Reserve Bank. Exceptions are provided for existing systems for a limited period, agents, intra-company payments, and entities exempted by the Reserve Bank.
Any person wishing to operate a payment system must apply to the Reserve Bank for authorization in the prescribed form and manner, accompanied by prescribed fees.
Upon receiving an application for authorization, the Reserve Bank may conduct necessary inquiries to ascertain the genuineness of the application.
This section outlines the penalties that can be imposed for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Reserve Bank to make regulations
main_sections.description: The Reserve Bank has the power to make regulations, consistent with the Act, to carry out its provisions.

important_rules: No person, other than the Reserve Bank, shall commence or operate a payment system without authorization from the Reserve Bank (Section 4).
System providers must act in accordance with the Act, regulations, and any directions issued by the Reserve Bank (Section 20).
System providers have a duty to keep documents in the payment system confidential (Section 22).
The Reserve Bank is designated as the authority for the regulation and supervision of payment systems (Section 3).
The Reserve Bank has the power to determine standards for payment systems (Section 10).

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 26).
The Reserve Bank has the power to impose penalties (Section 30).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Reserve Bank of India, acting through the Payments Regulatory Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through authorization, regulation, supervision, power to call for information, enter and inspect, carry out audits, issue directions, and impose penalties. Offences can also be compounded.

rights: Right to apply for authorization to operate a payment system (Section 5).
Right to appeal to the Central Government against the revocation of authorization (Section 9).
duties: Duty of system provider to act in accordance with the Act and regulations (Section 20).
Duty to keep documents in the payment system confidential (Section 22).
Duty to provide returns, documents, or other information when called upon by the Reserve Bank (Section 12).
obligations: Obligation to obtain authorization to operate a payment system (Section 4).
Obligation to comply with directions issued by the Reserve Bank (Section 19).

key_procedures: Application for authorization of a payment system: A person desirous of commencing or carrying on a payment system must apply to the Reserve Bank in the prescribed form and manner, accompanied by prescribed fees (Section 5).
Inquiry by the Reserve Bank: Upon receipt of an application, the Reserve Bank may make inquiries to satisfy itself about the application's genuineness before issuing authorization (Section 6).
Issue or refusal of authorization: The Reserve Bank may issue or refuse an authorization based on its inquiries (Section 7).
Revocation of authorization: The Reserve Bank can revoke an authorization under certain conditions (Section 8).
Appeal against revocation: An appeal against the revocation of authorization can be made to the Central Government (Section 9).
administration: The Reserve Bank of India, through the Payments Regulatory Board.
important_notes: The Act has overriding effect over other laws where there is an inconsistency, except as otherwise provided (Section 32).
Certain acts done in good faith under the Act are protected from legal proceedings (Section 36).
The Act does not apply to stock exchanges or clearing corporations of stock exchanges (Section 34).
Specific provisions regarding 'issuer' and 'legal entity identifier' and 'trade repository' were inserted by Act 18 of 2015.
Provisions related to the composition and function of the Payments Regulatory Board were amended by the Finance Act, 2017.

title: THE SASHASTRA SEEMA BAL ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for ensuring the security of the borders of India and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), an armed force of the Union, for ensuring the security of India's borders. It covers officers, subordinate officers, under-officers, and other enrolled persons of the Force.

key_definitions.active duty: Means any duty as a member of the Force during the period in which such person is attached to, or forms part of, a unit of the Force which is engaged in operations against any enemy, or which is operating at a picket or engaged on patrol or other guard duty along the borders of India, and includes duty declared by the Central Government as active duty.
key_definitions.enemy: Includes all mutineers, armed rebels, armed rioters, pirates, terrorists and any person in arms against whom it is the duty of any person subject to this Act to take action.
key_definitions.member of the Force: Means an officer, a subordinate officer, an under-officer or other enrolled person.
key_definitions.offence: Means any act or omission punishable under this Act and includes a civil offence.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Sashastra Seema Bal Act, 2007 and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'active duty', 'enemy', 'Force', 'member of the Force', 'offence', and others.

Specifies that officers, subordinate officers, under-officers, and other persons enrolled under the Act are subject to its provisions until they are repatriated, retired, released, discharged, removed, or dismissed from the Force.

Establishes the Sashastra Seema Bal as an armed force of the Union for border security and other entrusted duties. It also states that the Force shall be constituted and its members' conditions of service shall be as prescribed.
Vests the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Force in the Central Government. The command and supervision of the Force are vested in the Director-General.

important_rules: Members of the Sashastra Seema Bal are subject to the Act until their service with the Force is terminated.
The Sashastra Seema Bal is constituted for border security and other duties assigned by the Central Government.
The Central Government has overall control and direction of the Force, with the Director-General responsible for command and supervision.

penalties: Offences ranging from those punishable with death (in relation to enemy) to minor offences like absence without leave, disobedience, and unbecoming conduct.
Punishments can be awarded by Force Courts or through minor punishments.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, the Director-General, and other designated officers are involved in the enforcement and regulation of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the constitution of Force Courts (General, Petty, Summary), adherence to procedures, confirmation and revision of proceedings, and execution of sentences.

rights: Right to redressal of grievances for both officers and non-officers.
Protection for acts of members of the Force done in good faith.
duties: Duty to ensure the security of the borders of India.
Duty to perform other duties as may be entrusted by the Central Government.
Members are subject to the Act and its regulations regarding service conditions and conduct.
Duty to report offences and follow orders from superior officers.
obligations: Obligation to be subject to the Act if appointed to the Force.
Obligation to adhere to the rules and regulations prescribed under the Act.
Obligation to be subject to the jurisdiction of Force Courts for offences committed under the Act.

key_procedures: Proceedings before trial, including arrest and custody of offenders.
Conduct of Force Courts (General, Petty, Summary), including convening, composition, and powers.
Procedure of Force Courts, covering evidence, summoning witnesses, and handling of accused.
Confirmation and revision of findings and sentences of Force Courts.
Execution of sentences, including death, imprisonment, and recovery of fines.
Pardon, remission, and suspension of sentences.
administration: Central Government (overall superintendence, direction, and control); Director-General (command and supervision of the Force). Rules and regulations are prescribed.
important_notes: The Act defines 'active duty' broadly to include operations against the enemy and border patrols, and also allows the Central Government to declare specific periods as active duty.
The Act makes provisions for civil offences and their trial by criminal courts, with a choice between criminal and Force Courts in some instances.
The Act incorporates provisions for the protection of members of the Force for acts done in good faith.

title: The Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology Act, 2007
purpose: To declare the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology as an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology, Jais, District Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh. It covers the establishment, governance, functions, and administration of the Institute.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date appointed for the Act to come into force.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of the Institute.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the General Council.
key_definitions.General Council: The General Council established under the Act.
key_definitions.Institute: The Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology, incorporated under the Act.
key_definitions.Society: The Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology Society, Jais, District Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: Statutes and Ordinances of the Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology as an institution of national importance due to its objectives.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act.
Establishes the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Outlines the constitution of the Board of Governors, including its members and the role of the Registrar as Secretary.

Details the various functions the Institute is to perform, including promoting education and research in petroleum and hydrocarbons, granting degrees, managing academic programs, and fostering interaction with the industry.

Specifies the powers of the Board of Governors, including general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs, decision-making on policy, instituting courses, and framing Statutes.

important_rules: The Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology is declared an institution of national importance.
The Institute shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Board of Governors is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs.
The Institute shall perform functions related to nurturing and promoting excellence in education and research in petroleum and hydrocarbons.
The Board shall meet ordinarily four times during a calendar year.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and various authorities of the Institute as defined by the Act and Statutes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances, and by the powers vested in the Board, General Council, and Senate. Section 8 outlines provisions for employee termination if alterations to terms of employment are not acceptable.

rights: The Institute has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract.
Employees retain their tenure, remuneration, terms, conditions, and rights regarding pension, leave, gratuity, and provident fund unless altered by Statutes.
The Institute has the right to grant, withdraw, and confer degrees, diplomas, certificates, honorary degrees, fellowships, scholarships, etc.
duties: The Institute has a duty to nurture and promote quality and excellence in education and research in petroleum and hydrocarbons.
