The Institute has a duty to provide for programs of instruction and research.
The Institute has a duty to manage the content, quality, design, and evaluation of its academic and research programs.
The Institute has a duty to frame Statutes and Ordinances.
The Board has a duty to oversee the general superintendence, direction, and control of the affairs of the Institute.
obligations: The Institute is obligated to be open to all races, creeds, and classes (Section 11).
The Institute must ensure that employees continue in service under the same terms and conditions unless altered by Statutes (Section 8(c)).

key_procedures: The commencement of the Act is triggered by a notification from the Central Government appointing specific dates for its provisions.
The Board of Governors is constituted by the Central Government.
The Board of Governors meets ordinarily four times a year.
The term of office for members of the Board is generally three years.
Properties vested in the Society are transferred to the Institute on the appointed day.
The Statutes and Ordinances are made and can be altered or rescinded by the Institute (Section 9(xvii), Section 10(g)).
Acts and proceedings are not invalidated by vacancies (Section 35).
administration: The Central Government oversees certain appointments and notifications. The Board of Governors, General Council, Senate, Director, and Registrar are key administrative bodies of the Institute.
important_notes: Different dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The first President of the Board has a specific tenure not exceeding six months from the date the first Statutes come into force.
If alterations to employee terms of service are not acceptable, their employment may be terminated with compensation.
Statutes, Ordinances, and notifications are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.

title: THE NATIONAL INVESTIGATION AGENCY ACT, 2008
purpose: To constitute an investigation agency at the national level to investigate and prosecute offences affecting the sovereignty, security and integrity of India, security of State, friendly relations with foreign States and offences under Acts enacted to implement international treaties, agreements, conventions and resolutions of the United Nations, its agencies and other international organisations and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It also applies to: citizens of India outside India; persons in the service of the Government wherever they may be; persons on ships and aircrafts registered in India wherever they may be; and persons who commit a Scheduled Offence beyond India against Indian citizens or affecting the interest of India. The Act primarily deals with Scheduled Offences, which are defined as offences specified in the Schedule.

key_definitions.Agency: The National Investigation Agency constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.High Court: The High Court within whose jurisdiction the Special Court is situated.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules.
key_definitions.Public Prosecutor: A Public Prosecutor or an Additional Public Prosecutor or a Special Public Prosecutor appointed under section 15.
key_definitions.Scheduled Offence: An offence specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.Special Court: A Court of Session designated as Special Court under section 11 or, as the case may be, under section 22.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and outlines its territorial extent and application, including to citizens outside India and those in government service.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Agency', 'Code', 'Scheduled Offence', and 'Special Court'.
Establishes the National Investigation Agency (NIA) as a special agency for the investigation and prosecution of Scheduled Offences. It also grants NIA officers powers similar to police officers.
States that the superintendence of the Agency vests in the Central Government and outlines the administrative role of the Director-General.

Details the procedure for the investigation of Scheduled Offences by the NIA, including how information is received, processed by the State and Central Governments, and when the NIA takes over an investigation. It also covers suo motu investigations and investigations of offences outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to designate Court of Session as Special Courts
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to designate Courts of Session as Special Courts for the trial of Scheduled Offences.

Defines the exclusive jurisdiction of Special Courts for trying Scheduled Offences investigated by the Agency and provides for the transfer of cases by the Supreme Court or High Court under specific circumstances.
Lays down the provisions for the appointment of Public Prosecutors, Additional Public Prosecutors, and Special Public Prosecutors by the Central Government.

important_rules: Rule 1: Investigation of Scheduled Offences must be initiated upon receipt of information recorded under section 154 of the Code, with reports forwarded to the State and then Central Government for determination if it's a Scheduled Offence and a fit case for NIA investigation.
Rule 2: The Central Government can, suo motu, direct the NIA to investigate a Scheduled Offence if it is of the opinion that such an offence has been committed.

Rule 3: NIA officers have powers similar to police officers throughout India and, subject to international treaties and domestic law, outside India, for investigating Scheduled Offences and making arrests.
Rule 4: Special Courts are designated by the Central Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court for the trial of Scheduled Offences.
Rule 5: Scheduled Offences investigated by the Agency shall be tried exclusively by the Special Court within whose local jurisdiction the offence was committed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: National Investigation Agency (NIA) and designated Special Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation by the NIA and trial by designated Special Courts. The Act grants NIA officers powers similar to police officers and outlines procedures for Special Courts.

rights: Right to fair and impartial trial by Special Courts.
Right to speedy trial by Special Courts.
Protection of witnesses in trials.
duties: Duty of State Government to forward reports of Scheduled Offences to the Central Government.
Duty of State Government and police officers to transmit relevant documents and records to the Agency when NIA takes over an investigation.
Duty of State Government to extend all assistance and co-operation to the Agency.
Duty of the officer-in-charge of a police station to continue investigation until the Agency takes up the case.
obligations: Obligation to investigate and prosecute offences affecting sovereignty, security, integrity of India, and other specified grave offences.
Obligation for individuals to cooperate with the NIA during investigations.

key_procedures: Procedure for reporting and investigating Scheduled Offences, involving forwarding reports from police stations to State and Central Governments.
Procedure for the Central Government to direct the NIA to investigate a Scheduled Offence, including suo motu direction.
Procedure for the designation of Special Courts by the Central Government in consultation with Chief Justices of High Courts.
Procedure for the trial of Scheduled Offences exclusively by the designated Special Courts.
Procedure for transfer of cases by the Supreme Court or High Court to other Special Courts under certain exigencies.
Procedure for appointment of Public Prosecutors for Special Courts.
administration: The Central Government oversees the superintendence and administration of the National Investigation Agency.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2019, with significant insertions and substitutions affecting the scope and application of the Act, particularly regarding offences committed outside India.
The Act aims to provide a robust legal framework for investigating and prosecuting serious offences that impact national security and India's international relations.

title: THE NATIONAL JUTE BOARD ACT, 2008
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a National Jute Board for the development of the cultivation, manufacture and marketing of jute and jute products and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India.

key_definitions.appointed day: Such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint for the purpose of section 3.
key_definitions.Board: The National Jute Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board.
key_definitions.Council: The Jute Manufactures Development Council established under section 3 of the Jute Manufactures Development Council Act, 1983 (27 of 1983).
key_definitions.Jute: The plants of jute, kenaf and mesta.
key_definitions.jute manufacture: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in the Jute Manufactures Cess Act, 1983 (28 of 1983).
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Board under this Act.
key_definitions.Society: The National Centre for Jute Diversification, a society set up by the Central Government in the Ministry of Textiles and registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860).
key_definitions.year: The year commencing on the 1st day of April and ending on the 31st day of March next following.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date it comes into force.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Council', 'Jute', 'jute manufacture', 'member', 'prescribed', 'regulations', 'Society', and 'year'.
Details the constitution of the National Jute Board, its corporate status, head office location, and the composition of its members, including ex officio, elected, nominated, and expert members.
Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Secretary and other officers and employees for the efficient discharge of the Board's functions and specifies their terms and conditions of service.

Outlines the primary duty of the Board to promote the development of jute and jute products and lists various measures the Board may undertake, including integrated approach to cultivation, quality improvement, marketing, standardisation, research, infrastructure development, and welfare of growers and workers.

main_sections.section_title: The Council and Society to vest in Board
main_sections.description: States that on and from the appointed day, the Jute Manufactures Development Council and the National Centre for Jute Diversification shall be transferred to and vest in the National Jute Board, including all their assets, rights, powers, and liabilities.

important_rules: The Board shall be a body corporate by the name 'National Jute Board', with perpetual succession and a common seal, and power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract.

The Board shall consist of a Chairperson (ex officio Secretary in charge of textiles), Members of Parliament, ex officio members from relevant ministries, nominated members representing State Governments, jute farmers, jute workers, experts, and representatives from micro, small, and medium enterprises, the organized and decentralized jute industry, and exporters.
The Board's primary duty is to promote the development of jute and jute products by undertaking measures for cultivation, quality, marketing, research, and welfare.
The Jute Manufactures Development Council and the National Centre for Jute Diversification shall vest in the National Jute Board on the appointed day.

rights: The Board has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of movable and immovable property.
The Board has the right to contract and sue and be sued in its name.
The Board has the right to establish offices or agencies in or outside India with the Central Government's approval.
The Board has the right to receive grants and loans from the Central Government.
duties: It shall be the duty of the Board to promote the development of jute and jute products.
The Board has a duty to advise the Central Government on all matters relating to the development of raw jute and the jute industry.
The Board has a duty to prepare and furnish reports relating to the jute sector as required by the Central Government.
obligations: The Board is obligated to ensure the efficient discharge of its functions.
The Board is obligated to manage its finances, accounts, and audit as per the Act.
The Board is obligated to comply with directions issued by the Central Government.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Board: The Central Government constitutes the National Jute Board by notification on the 'appointed day'.
Appointment of Secretary and Officers: The Central Government appoints the Secretary and other officers and employees for the Board.
Vesting of Assets: On the 'appointed day', the Council and the Society are transferred to and vest in the Board.
Budget Preparation: The Board shall prepare and submit its budget for the approval of the Central Government.
Annual Report: The Board shall prepare an annual report of its activities and submit it to the Central Government.
Accounts and Audit: The Board shall maintain accounts and get them audited annually.
administration: The Ministry of Textiles, Central Government, is involved in the administration, particularly through the ex officio Chairperson and the appointment of the Secretary and other officers.
important_notes: The Act came into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint (April 1, 2010).
The Board may establish offices or agencies at other places in or outside India with the previous approval of the Central Government.
The Board shall elect a Vice-Chairperson from among its members.
The Board may make regulations for the transaction of its business, including quorum at meetings.

title: THE CENTRAL UNIVERSITIES ACT, 2009
purpose: To establish and incorporate universities for teaching and research in the various States and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to universities established under it across various States in India. Specific sections detail provisions for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, the State of Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, and Telangana. The territorial jurisdiction of each university is defined, and in some cases, extends to the whole of India (e.g., Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya).

key_definitions.academic_council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.academic_staff: Such categories of staff as are designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.board_of_studies: The Board of Studies of a Department of the University.
key_definitions.college: A college maintained by the University.
key_definitions.distance_education_system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, internet, correspondence courses, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more such means.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University and includes teachers and other staff of the University.
key_definitions.institution: An academic institution, not being a College, maintained by the University.
key_definitions.regulations: The Regulations made by any authority of the University under this Act for the time being in force.
key_definitions.statutes: The Statutes of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.teachers_of_the_university: Professors, Associate Professors, Assistant Professors and such other persons as may by appointed for imparting instruction or conducting research in the University or in any College or Institution maintained by the University and are designated as teachers by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.university: A University established and incorporated as a University under this Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Central Universities Act, 2009, and states it is deemed to have come into force on January 15, 2009.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Academic Council, academic staff, employee, University, etc.

Details the establishment of specific universities as bodies corporate, including Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya, Doctor Harisingh Gour Vishwavidyalaya, and Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University, and provides for the establishment of new universities in various states as specified in the First Schedule. It also outlines their headquarters, jurisdiction, and the constitution of their initial governing bodies.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision with respect to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir
main_sections.description: Establishes Central University of Kashmir and Central University of Jammu, defining their territorial jurisdictions and transferring assets and liabilities.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision with respect to State of Bihar
main_sections.description: Establishes Central University of South Bihar and Mahatma Gandhi Central University, defining their territorial jurisdictions based on the River Ganges.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Central University of Andhra Pradesh
main_sections.description: Establishes the Central University of Andhra Pradesh with territorial jurisdiction over the entire State of Andhra Pradesh.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh
main_sections.description: Establishes the Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh to provide higher education and research facilities primarily for the tribal population.
Establishes the Sindhu Central University with territorial jurisdiction over the Union territory of Ladakh.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya in Gujarat
main_sections.description: Establishes Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya in Gujarat, formerly the National Rail and Transportation Institute, with territorial jurisdiction across India and sponsored/funded by the Ministry of Railways.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Sammakka Sarakka Central Tribal University
main_sections.description: Establishes Sammakka Sarakka Central Tribal University in Telangana to provide higher education and research facilities primarily for the tribal population.

Details the legal effects of the establishment of universities, including the continuation of references in contracts, vesting of properties, transfer of rights and liabilities, and continuity of employment for existing staff.
Outlines the objectives of the Universities established under this Act.
Specifies the powers that a University established under this Act possesses.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all castes, creed, race or class
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is accessible to all individuals irrespective of their caste, creed, race, or class.
Appoints the Visitor of the University and outlines their role.
Lists the officers of the University.
Defines the role and powers of the Chancellor.
Defines the role and powers of the Vice-Chancellor.
Defines the role and powers of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
Defines the role and appointment of Deans of Schools.
Defines the role and appointment of the Registrar.
Defines the role and appointment of the Finance Officer.
Defines the role and appointment of the Controller of Examinations.
Defines the role and appointment of the Librarian.
Provides for the appointment of other officers as may be necessary.
Lists the principal authorities of the University.
Describes the composition and functions of the Court of the University.
Describes the composition and functions of the Executive Council.
Describes the composition and functions of the Academic Council.
Describes the composition and functions of the Boards of Studies.
Describes the composition and functions of the Finance Committee.
Provides for the establishment of other authorities as may be specified.
Grants the power to make Statutes for the University.
Details the procedure for making Statutes.
Grants the power to make Ordinances for the University.
Provides for the making of Regulations.
Requires the University to prepare and submit an annual report.
Requires the University to maintain annual accounts and have them audited.
Empowers the University to call for returns and information.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions of service of employees, etc.
main_sections.description: Lays down the conditions of service for the employees of the University.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students
main_sections.description: Defines the procedure for appeals and arbitration in disciplinary cases involving students.
Confirms the right to appeal for individuals.
Deals with the establishment and management of provident and pension funds.

main_sections.section_title: Disputes as to constitution of authorities and bodies
main_sections.description: Addresses how disputes regarding the constitution of authorities and bodies are resolved.
Outlines the procedure for filling casual vacancies in authorities and bodies.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings of authorities or bodies not invalidated by vacancies
main_sections.description: States that vacancies in authorities or bodies do not invalidate their proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Protects actions taken in good faith by individuals under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of proof of University record
main_sections.description: Specifies the acceptable modes of proving University records.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates the publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their presentation before Parliament.
Contains provisions for the transition from previous legal frameworks to this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madhya Pradesh Act 22 of 1973
main_sections.description: Amends the Madhya Pradesh Vishwavidyalaya Adhiniyam, 1973.
Amends the Uttar Pradesh State Universities Act, 1973 (President's Act 10 of 1973).
Repeals previous enactments and includes savings provisions.

important_rules: Universities are established as bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Universities are open to all castes, creed, race, or class.
Conditions of service for employees are governed by the Act and university statutes/ordinances.
Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations must be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the authorities of each University are responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of the Act's provisions, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations, and by the Visitor's powers.

rights: Right to appeal for individuals.
Employees have rights to pension, leave, gratuity, and provident fund.
Right to sue and be sued in the name of the University.
duties: Universities have a duty to provide teaching and research facilities.
Universities have a duty to prepare and submit annual reports and accounts.
Employees have duties as per their employment contracts and university regulations.
obligations: Universities are obliged to be bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Universities are obliged to be open to all castes, creed, race, or class.
The Central Government has obligations related to removing difficulties and publishing regulations.

key_procedures: Establishment of new universities under section 3.
Procedures for making Statutes (Section 27) and Ordinances (Section 28).
Procedure for appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students (Section 34).
Procedure for filling casual vacancies (Section 38).
administration: The Ministry of Education (formerly Ministry of Human Resource Development) of the Central Government is generally responsible for higher education, and by extension, the administration of central universities established under this Act. Specifics on administration for individual universities would be detailed in their respective Statutes and Ordinances.
important_notes: The Act deems to have come into force on January 15, 2009, even though enacted on March 20, 2009.
Specific provisions are made for special provisions concerning the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the State of Bihar, including the renaming and re-jurisdictioning of existing universities.
The Act has been amended to include new universities and adjust provisions for specific regions.

title: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
purpose: To provide for free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to conferment of rights on children to free and compulsory education, subject to Articles 29 and 30 of the Constitution. Does not apply to Madrasas, Vedic Pathsalas, and educational institutions primarily imparting religious instruction.

key_definitions.appropriate Government: In relation to schools controlled by the Central Government or Union territory without legislature, it's the Central Government. In relation to other schools in a State, it's the State Government; in a Union territory with a legislature, it's the Government of that Union territory.
key_definitions.capitation fee: Any kind of donation or contribution or payment other than the fee notified by the school.
key_definitions.child: A male or female child of the age of six to fourteen years.
key_definitions.elementary education: Education from first class to eighth class.
key_definitions.school: Any recognized school imparting elementary education, including government, local authority, aided, specified category, and unaided schools.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Provides the short title, extent (whole of India), application (subject to Articles 29 and 30 of the Constitution, excluding religious institutions), and commencement (date notified by Central Government).
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appropriate Government', 'capitation fee', 'child', 'elementary education', 'school', and 'child with disability'.

main_sections.section_title: Right of child to free and compulsory education
main_sections.description: Establishes the right of every child aged six to fourteen years to free and compulsory education in a neighbourhood school until completion of elementary education. No child shall be liable to pay any fees or charges that prevent them from pursuing education. Children with disabilities have the same rights as other children with disabilities under relevant acts, with provisions for home-based education for certain categories.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of appropriate Government and local authority to establish school
main_sections.description: Mandates the appropriate Government and local authority to establish a school in their neighborhood area within three years from the commencement of the Act, if one is not already established.

main_sections.section_title: Extent of school’s responsibility for free and compulsory education
main_sections.description: Determines the extent to which schools are responsible for providing free and compulsory education, including provisions for admission of children from disadvantaged groups and weaker sections.

main_sections.section_title: No capitation fee and screening procedure for admission
main_sections.description: Prohibits schools from demanding capitation fees and from conducting any screening procedure for the admission of children.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of physical punishment and mental harassment to child
main_sections.description: Prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment of a child.

main_sections.section_title: No school to be established without obtaining certificate of recognition
main_sections.description: States that no school shall be established or functioned without obtaining a certificate of recognition from the prescribed authority.
Requires the constitution of a School Management Committee for each school to manage the school in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications for appointment and terms and conditions of service of teachers
main_sections.description: Lays down the qualifications for the appointment of teachers and the terms and conditions of their service.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of teachers and redressal of grievances
main_sections.description: Outlines the duties of teachers and the mechanisms for redressing their grievances.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of deployment of teachers for non-educational purposes
main_sections.description: Prohibits the deployment of teachers for non-educational purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of private tuition by teacher
main_sections.description: Prohibits teachers from giving private tuition.
Specifies the curriculum and evaluation procedure for elementary education, aiming for a child-centred and child-friendly approach.

main_sections.section_title: Monitoring of child’s right to education
main_sections.description: Provides for the monitoring of the child's right to education by various authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Power of appropriate Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Every child aged six to fourteen years has the right to free and compulsory elementary education in a neighborhood school.
No child shall be liable to pay any fee or charges that prevent them from pursuing or completing elementary education.
Children not admitted or who have not completed elementary education shall be admitted in a class appropriate to their age and shall receive special training to catch up.
Children admitted to elementary education are entitled to free education until completion, even if they exceed fourteen years of age.
Schools shall not demand capitation fees or conduct screening procedures for admission.
No child shall be denied admission due to lack of age proof; admission shall be provided on the basis of the child's and parents' declaration.
Children shall not be held back, expelled, or required to pass any board examination until completion of elementary education.
Physical punishment and mental harassment of children are prohibited.
Schools must obtain a certificate of recognition before establishment or operation.
Teachers are prohibited from engaging in private tuition and deployment for non-educational purposes.

penalties: Delay in issuing transfer certificates by head-teachers or in-charges makes them liable for disciplinary action.
Failure to establish a school within the prescribed area and time by the appropriate Government and local authority may lead to consequences as prescribed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Appropriate Government, local authorities, School Management Committees, National and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of schools, ensuring admission, providing free and compulsory education, monitoring rights, redressal of grievances, and by the enforcement of rules and regulations related to school functioning and teacher conduct.

rights: Right to free and compulsory elementary education for children aged six to fourteen years.
Right to admission in a class appropriate to a child's age if not admitted or completed education earlier.
Right to receive special training to catch up with peers.
Right to free education until completion of elementary education, even beyond fourteen years.
Right to seek transfer to another school for completing elementary education.
Right to be free from physical punishment and mental harassment.
Right to admission without capitation fees or screening procedures.
duties: Duty of the appropriate Government and local authority to establish schools.
Duty of the appropriate Government to provide free and compulsory elementary education to every child.
Duty of parents and guardians to admit and ensure attendance of their children in school.
Duty of teachers to perform their duties diligently and adhere to prescribed qualifications and conduct.
Duty of head-teachers or in-charges to issue transfer certificates promptly.
obligations: Obligation of the appropriate Government to provide free elementary education.
Obligation of parents and guardians to ensure their child attends school.
Obligation of schools to admit children without capitation fees or screening.
Obligation of teachers to refrain from private tuition and non-educational deployment.

key_procedures: Admission of children: No capitation fee or screening. If age proof is not available, admission is based on declaration. Children not admitted or who couldn't complete education are admitted to a class appropriate to their age and provided special training.

Transfer of students: Children have the right to transfer to another school to complete elementary education. Head-teachers must issue transfer certificates immediately; delay can lead to disciplinary action.
Establishment of schools: Appropriate Government and local authorities must establish schools within a neighborhood area if none exist, within three years of the Act's commencement.
School Management Committee formation: Each school must constitute a School Management Committee.
administration: The 'appropriate Government' (Central Government or State Government, depending on the school's control) and 'local authority' are responsible for implementing the Act. The Central Government also has a role in developing frameworks, standards, and providing support.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to Madrasas, Vedic Pathsalas, and educational institutions primarily imparting religious instruction.
The Act extends to the whole of India, with specific mentions of its application to Jammu and Kashmir being omitted.

Children with disabilities have rights equivalent to those under the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995, with provisions for home-based education for certain severe disability categories.
Children admitted to elementary education are entitled to free education until completion, even if they turn fourteen during the course of study.

title: THE CLINICAL ESTABLISHMENTS (REGISTRATION AND REGULATION) ACT, 2010
purpose: To provide for the registration and regulation of clinical establishments in the country with a view to prescribe minimum standards of facilities and services to achieve the mandate of article 47 of the Constitution for improvement in public health.
scope: The Act initially applies to the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram, and Sikkim, and Union territories. It can be adopted by other states through a resolution. It covers all clinical establishments, including hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, and diagnostic centers, whether government-owned, privately owned, or run by trusts, corporations, local authorities, or single doctors. It explicitly excludes clinical establishments owned or managed by the Armed Forces.

key_definitions.authority: The district registering authority set up under section 10.
key_definitions.certificate: Certificate of registration issued under section 30.
key_definitions.clinical_establishment: Includes hospitals, maternity homes, nursing homes, dispensaries, clinics, sanatoria, or institutions offering diagnosis, treatment, or care for illness, injury, deformity, abnormality, or pregnancy in any recognized system of medicine. It also includes places for diagnostic or investigative services using medical equipment. It covers establishments run by government, trusts, corporations, local authorities, or single doctors, but excludes those run by the Armed Forces.
key_definitions.emergency_medical_condition: A medical condition with acute symptoms of sufficient severity where the absence of immediate medical attention could lead to serious jeopardy of health, serious impairment of bodily functions, or serious dysfunction of any organ.
key_definitions.recognised_system_of_medicine: Includes Allopathy, Yoga, Naturopathy, Ayurveda, Homoeopathy, Siddha, Unani, or any other system recognized by the Central Government.
key_definitions.to_stabilise: To provide necessary medical treatment for an emergency medical condition to prevent material deterioration during transfer.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its initial application to certain states and Union territories, and outlines the commencement of the Act.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'authority', 'certificate', 'clinical establishment', 'emergency medical condition', 'National Council', 'recognised system of medicine', and others.

Establishes the National Council for clinical establishments and outlines its composition, including ex-officio members, elected representatives from various medical councils and bodies, and nominated representatives.

Details the functions of the National Council, including compiling and publishing a National Register of clinical establishments, classifying them, developing and reviewing minimum standards, collecting statistics, and performing other functions as directed by the Central Government.
Establishes the authority responsible for the registration of clinical establishments.
Deals with the process and requirement of registration for clinical establishments.
Specifies the conditions that must be met for a clinical establishment to be registered.
Provides for the classification of clinical establishments into different categories.

main_sections.section_title: Application for provisional certificate of registration
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for applying for a provisional certificate of registration.
Details the process for applying for permanent registration of a clinical establishment.
Pertains to the issuance of a certificate of permanent registration.
Describes the grounds and procedures for canceling the registration of a clinical establishment.
Grants powers for the inspection of registered clinical establishments.
Provides for the right to appeal against decisions made under the Act.
Introduces penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Specifies monetary penalties for operating a clinical establishment without registration.

main_sections.section_title: Disobedience of direction, obstruction and refusal of information
main_sections.description: Defines penalties for disobedience of directions, obstruction, and refusal to provide information.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules under the Act.

important_rules: Clinical establishments must be registered under the Act (Section 11).
The Act outlines conditions for registration, including adherence to prescribed standards (Section 12).
Provisional registration can be obtained initially, followed by application for permanent registration (Sections 14, 24).
Clinical establishments must display their registration certificates (Section 18).
Registration certificates are non-transferable (Section 20).
The National Council is responsible for developing minimum standards for healthcare provided by clinical establishments (Section 5(c), 5(d)).
The National Council is to compile and publish a National Register of clinical establishments (Section 5(a)).

penalties: General penalties for contravention of the Act (Section 40).
Monetary penalty for operating a clinical establishment without registration (Section 41).
Penalties for disobedience of directions, obstruction, and refusal to provide information (Section 42).
Penalty for minor deficiencies (Section 43).
Penalties for contraventions by companies (Section 44).
Penalties for offences by Government Departments (Section 45).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The 'authority' (district registering authority) is responsible for registration and likely enforcement at the local level, with broader powers for inspection and potentially cancellation of registration. The National Council and State Governments also play roles in regulation and rule-making.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes registration, inspection of establishments, levying fees, imposing penalties for non-compliance, and cancellation of registration. The Central and State Governments can make rules and give directions for enforcement.

rights: Right to appeal against decisions made under the Act (Section 36).
duties: Duty to register the clinical establishment (Section 11).
Duty to comply with the conditions for registration (Section 12).
Duty to display the certificate of registration (Section 18).
Duty to cooperate with inspections (implied by Section 33, 34, 42).
Duty to provide information when required (implied by Section 42).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to minimum standards prescribed for clinical establishments.
Obligation for the National Council to collect statistics regarding clinical establishments (Section 5(e)).

key_procedures: Application for and issuance of a provisional certificate of registration (Sections 14, 15, 17).
Application for and grant or refusal of permanent registration, including verification and handling objections (Sections 24, 25, 26, 27, 29, 30).
Renewal of registration (Section 22).
Inspection of registered clinical establishments (Section 33).
Appeals against orders passed under the Act (Section 36).
administration: The Central Government and State Governments are responsible for administering the Act, including rule-making. The 'authority' (district registering authority) is the primary body for registration and day-to-day administration at the district level. The National Council for Clinical Establishments oversees standards and national registration.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for commencement for different categories of clinical establishments and recognised systems of medicine (Section 1(3) proviso).
The Armed Forces are excluded from the definition of clinical establishments (Section 2(c) explanation).
The National Council must be established and its functions, including setting standards and compiling a register, must be undertaken within specific timeframes (Sections 3(1), 5(a), 5(d)).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 47).

title: THE FOREIGN CONTRIBUTION (REGULATION) ACT, 2010
purpose: To consolidate the law to regulate the acceptance and utilisation of foreign contribution or foreign hospitality by certain individuals or associations or companies and to prohibit acceptance and utilisation of foreign contribution or foreign hospitality for any activities detrimental to the national interest and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to citizens of India outside India, and associate branches or subsidiaries, outside India, of companies or bodies corporate, registered or incorporated in India. It regulates foreign contribution and foreign hospitality.

key_definitions.association: An association of individuals, whether incorporated or not, having an office in India, including a society and any other organization.
key_definitions.foreign_contribution: Donation, delivery or transfer made by any foreign source of any article (under a certain market value), any currency (Indian or foreign), or any security. This also includes interest accrued or other income derived from deposited foreign contribution. Excludes fees for goods or services rendered in the ordinary course of business.
key_definitions.foreign_hospitality: Any offer, not purely casual, made in cash or kind by a foreign source for providing costs of travel to a foreign country or territory, or free boarding, lodging, transport, or medical treatment.
key_definitions.foreign_source: Includes governments of foreign countries, international agencies (excluding specified UN agencies), foreign companies, multinational corporations, companies with significant foreign shareholding, foreign trade unions, foreign trusts or foundations, associations of individuals formed or registered outside India, and citizens of foreign countries.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act, its territorial extent, application to citizens outside India and foreign subsidiaries of Indian companies, and the commencement date.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'association', 'foreign contribution', 'foreign hospitality', 'foreign source', 'political party', etc.

Prohibits certain individuals and entities, including candidates for election, journalists, public servants, members of legislature, political parties, and organizations of a political nature, from accepting foreign contribution.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of certain persons with Central Government
main_sections.description: Requires certain persons who intend to receive foreign contribution to obtain registration from the Central Government.
Empowers authorized officers to inspect accounts or records of any person who has received or made any transaction related to foreign contribution.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for contravention of any provision of the Act
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening any provision of the Act, which can include imprisonment and fines.

important_rules: No foreign contribution shall be accepted by a candidate for election.
No foreign contribution shall be accepted by a correspondent, columnist, cartoonist, editor, owner, printer, or publisher of a registered newspaper.
No foreign contribution shall be accepted by a public servant, Judge, Government servant, or employee of any corporation or other body controlled or owned by the Government.
No foreign contribution shall be accepted by a member of any Legislature.
No foreign contribution shall be accepted by a political party or office-bearer thereof.
No foreign contribution shall be accepted by an organization of a political nature as specified by the Central Government.

No foreign contribution shall be accepted by an association or company engaged in the production or broadcast of audio news or audio-visual news or current affairs programmes through any electronic media.

penalties: Penalty for making false statement, declaration, or delivering false accounts.
Penalty for article, currency, or security obtained in contravention of section 10.
Punishment for contravention of any provision of the Act.
Additional fine where article, currency, or security is not available for confiscation.
Penalty for offences where no separate punishment has been provided.
Prohibition of acceptance of foreign contribution.
Offences by companies.
Confiscation of article or currency or security obtained in contravention of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, search, seizure, adjudication, and prosecution for offences. The Central Government has the power to make rules and give directions.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of confiscation.
Right to revision of orders by the Central Government.
duties: Duty to obtain registration for receiving foreign contribution.
Duty to maintain accounts of foreign contribution.
Duty to get accounts audited.
Duty to intimate to the Central Government about receipt of foreign contribution.
Duty not to transfer foreign contribution to other persons.
Duty to utilize foreign contribution only for specified purposes and not for administrative expenses beyond a prescribed limit.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation to provide information or documents as required by the Central Government.
Obligation to dispose of assets created out of foreign contribution in accordance with the Act upon cancellation or surrender of certificate.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining registration for accepting foreign contribution.
Procedure for renewal of certificates of registration.
Procedure for suspension and cancellation of certificates.
Procedure for inspection, search, and seizure of accounts, records, articles, currency, or securities.
Procedure for adjudication and confiscation of articles, currency, or securities obtained in contravention of the Act.
Procedure for appeal against orders and revision by the Central Government.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act does not apply to certain Government transactions.
The application of other laws is not barred.
The Central Government has the power to exempt certain cases from the provisions of the Act.
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

title: THE FACTORING REGULATION ACT, 2011
purpose: To provide for and regulate assignment of receivables by making provision for registration thereof and rights and obligations of parties to contract for assignment of receivables and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Covers the business of factoring, assignment of receivables, and related rights, obligations, and penalties for factors and debtors.

key_definitions.assignment: Transfer by agreement to a factor of an undivided interest, in whole or in part, in the receivables of an assignor due from a debtor. Includes transfers where the assignor or debtor is outside India. Excludes creation of rights in receivables as security for loans and advances.
key_definitions.assignee: A factor in whose favor the receivable is transferred.
key_definitions.assignor: Any person who is the owner of any receivable.
key_definitions.bank: Includes a banking company, corresponding new bank, State Bank of India, subsidiary bank, certain specified co-operative societies, and other banks specified by the Central Government on RBI's recommendation.
key_definitions.debtor: Any person liable to the assignor, whether under a contract or otherwise, to pay any receivable or discharge any obligation in respect of the receivable.
key_definitions.factor: A non-banking financial company registered under the RBI Act, 1934, or a body corporate, bank, or company engaged in the factoring business.
key_definitions.factoring_business: Acquisition by assignment of receivables of an assignor for consideration, for collection or financing. Excludes credit facilities by banks/NBFCs against receivables and activities of commission agents for agricultural produce or goods.
key_definitions.receivables: Money owed by a debtor and not yet paid to the assignor for goods or services, including payment for tolls or use of infrastructure/services.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and commencement provisions.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'assignment', 'assignee', 'assignor', 'bank', 'debtor', 'factor', 'factoring business', and 'receivables'.

Mandates that no factor can commence or carry on factoring business without obtaining a certificate of registration from the Reserve Bank of India. Outlines the application process and compliance requirements.
Allows an assignor to assign any receivable to a factor in writing, for an agreed consideration. Requires the assignor to disclose any defenses or set-off rights of the debtor to the assignee.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of certain assignments of receivables transactions
main_sections.description: Requires registration of certain types of assignments of receivables transactions.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Provides for amendments to certain other enactments as may be necessary.

important_rules: Rule 1: A factor must obtain a certificate of registration from the Reserve Bank of India to carry on factoring business (Section 3(1)).
Rule 2: An assignor can assign a receivable to a factor by a written agreement, and must disclose any debtor defenses or set-off rights to the factor (Section 7(1)).
Rule 3: Provisions of Chapter IIIB of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, relating to non-banking financial companies, apply mutatis mutandis to factors (Section 4).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 21).
Penalties for non-compliance with directions issued by the Reserve Bank of India (Section 22).
The Reserve Bank can prohibit a factor from undertaking factoring business for non-compliance with directions (Section 6(3)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through granting or cancelling registration certificates, issuing directions, imposing penalties, and prohibiting factors from business operations.

rights: Debtors have the right to protection as per the principle of debtor protection (Section 15).
Debtors have the right to raise defenses and set-off claims against the assignee (Section 16).
The public has the right to inspect registered assignments (Section 20).
duties: Factors have a duty to register with the Reserve Bank of India before commencing business (Section 3(1)).
Assignors have a duty to disclose debtor defenses and set-off rights to the assignee (Section 7(1)).
Factors have a duty to comply with directions issued by the Reserve Bank of India (Section 6(2)).
An assignor is a trustee of the assignee in certain cases (Section 13).
obligations: Obligations of parties to a contract for assignment of receivables are detailed (Section 11).
Liability of a debtor is defined (Section 12).
Specific obligations for debtors in case of assignors being micro or small enterprises (Section 14).

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of factors with the Reserve Bank of India (Section 3).
Procedure for assignment of receivables through a written agreement (Section 7).
Procedure for registration of certain assignments of receivables transactions (Section 19).
Procedure for public inspection of registered assignments (Section 20).
administration: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the primary regulatory and administrative authority for this Act, responsible for registration, issuing directions, and enforcement.
important_notes: The Act's provisions override other laws where there is a conflict, unless otherwise specified (Section 26).
The application of other laws is not barred by this Act (Section 27).
Certain entities like banks, statutory corporations, and government companies are exempted from the requirement of registration as a factor (Section 5).

title: The Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research Act, 2011
purpose: To establish an Academy for the advancement of learning and prosecution of research in science and technology in association with the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, and to declare it an institution of national importance, providing for its incorporation and related matters.
scope: Applies to the whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh). It concerns the establishment and functioning of the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research.

key_definitions.Academy: The Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research established under this Act.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research.
key_definitions.Council of Scientific and Industrial Res: A society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board appointed under section 12.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of the Academy appointed under section 22.
key_definitions.distinguished scientists or outstanding: Scientists of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research designated as such.
key_definitions.existing Academy: The Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research established in pursuance of a Government of India Resolution dated July 1, 2010.
key_definitions.Faculty of the Academy: Includes Academy Professors, Professors of Eminence, Distinguished Professors, Outstanding Professors, Senior Professors, Emeritus Professors, Professors, Associate Professors, Assistant Professors, visiting faculty, and scientists of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research assigned for instruction or research.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the process for its commencement.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Academy', 'Board', 'Council of Scientific and Industrial Research', 'Chairperson', 'Chancellor', 'Director', 'distinguished scientists'/'outstanding scientists', 'existing Academy', 'Faculty of the Academy', and 'notification'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Academy as a body corporate, its headquarters, and the possibility of regional centres and campuses. It also states the Academy has perpetual succession and a common seal.

Outlines the objectives of the Academy, including disseminating advanced knowledge, undertaking inter-disciplinary research, conducting innovative teaching, educating and training manpower, establishing industry linkages, and promoting research for societal benefit. It emphasizes focusing on areas not ordinarily taught in regular universities and creating leaders in science and technology.

main_sections.section_title: Relationship of Academy with Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
main_sections.description: Defines the relationship between the Academy and the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, allowing the use of infrastructure and manpower. It mandates a Memorandum of Understanding for affiliation and the award of degrees/diplomas by the Academy to students of CSIR, with provisions for migration of existing students.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Academy as an institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research as an institution of national importance.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of assets, liabilities, etc., of existing Academy to Academy established under this Act and other provisions, etc.
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of assets, liabilities, rights, and employees from the existing Academy to the newly established Academy. It also covers the continuation of legal proceedings and the entitlement of students pursuing courses in the existing Academy.

Enumerate the functions and powers of the Academy, including providing instruction and research, establishing administrative standards, creating posts, laying down recruitment standards, and determining compensation packages.

important_rules: The Academy shall primarily focus on research and imparting instruction in areas not ordinarily taught in regular academic universities in India.
The curricula, pedagogy, and evaluation of the Academy shall be innovative and aimed at creating high-quality personnel with cross-disciplinary knowledge.
The Academy shall be provided with or allowed to use the infrastructure and scientific manpower of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research for teaching and research.
The Academy must enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research for academic affiliation and award of degrees/diplomas.
Employees of the existing Academy shall hold their office in the new Academy under the same terms and conditions of service, with an option to opt out within six months.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
Right to sue and be sued.
Employees of the existing Academy have the right to continue in the new Academy under existing terms or opt out.
Students pursuing courses in the existing Academy are entitled to continue their studies and receive degrees/diplomas from the new Academy.
duties: To disseminate advanced knowledge in science and technology.
To undertake inter-disciplinary studies and research.
To conduct courses integrating inter-disciplinary and multi-disciplinary areas.
To take measures for innovations in teaching and learning processes.
To create an ambience for learning and scholarship.
To educate and train manpower in scientific and technological fields.
To establish linkages with industries.
To collaborate with reputed universities and institutions.
To promote research for social, economic, cultural, intellectual, and academic welfare.
obligations: To enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with CSIR.
To award degrees or diplomas to students of CSIR after the MoU.
To ensure its faculties and students are provided with necessary academic and research environments.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Academy by the Central Government through notification.
Transfer of assets, liabilities, and employees from the existing Academy to the new Academy upon establishment.
Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Academy and CSIR for academic affiliation and award of degrees/diplomas.
The Central Government may appoint different dates for different provisions of the Act to come into force.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for appointing the date of establishment and specifying the headquarters of the Academy. The Act establishes various authorities like the Board of Governors, Senate, Chancellor, and Director to administer the Academy.
important_notes: The Act applies to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as per the original text, though a later notification makes it applicable to the Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh).
Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force.
Absorption of employees by the Academy in its regular service under section 7 shall not entitle them to compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or other laws.

title: THE PENSION FUND REGULATORY AND DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT, 2013
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an Authority to promote old age income security by establishing, developing and regulating pension funds, to protect the interests of subscribers to schemes of pension funds and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India.

key_definitions.Authority: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority established under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.central_recordkeeping_agency: An agency registered under section 27 to perform the functions of recordkeeping, accounting, administration and customer service for subscribers to schemes.
key_definitions.intermediary: Includes pension fund, central recordkeeping agency, National Pension System Trust, pension fund adviser, retirement adviser, point of presence and such other person or entity connected with collection, management, recordkeeping and distribution of accumulations.
key_definitions.National Pension System: The contributory pension system whereby contributions from a subscriber are collected and accumulated in an individual pension account using a system of points of presence, a central recordkeeping agency and pension funds as may be specified by regulations.
key_definitions.subscriber: Includes a person who subscribes to a scheme of a pension fund.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the process for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Authority', 'central recordkeeping agency', 'intermediary', 'National Pension System', 'subscriber', and others.

Establishes the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, defining it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of acquiring property and suing or being sued. The head office is to be in the National Capital Region.

Specifies that the Authority shall consist of a Chairperson, three whole-time members, and three part-time members, to be appointed by the Central Government from persons with expertise in economics, finance, or law.

main_sections.section_title: Duties, powers and functions of Authority
main_sections.description: Outlines the broad responsibilities, powers, and functions of the Authority.
Introduces and defines the National Pension System.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure by an intermediary or any other person to comply with provisions of this Act, rules, regulations and directions
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for non-compliance with the Act, rules, regulations, and directions issued by the Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Pension Regulatory and Development Fund
main_sections.description: Details the establishment and constitution of the Pension Regulatory and Development Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Subscriber Education and Protection Fund
main_sections.description: Details the establishment and constitution of the Subscriber Education and Protection Fund.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations under the Act.

important_rules: The Act defines the structure and appointment process for the Chairperson and members of the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, including their terms of office and conditions of service.
Members can be removed from office under specific circumstances, such as insolvency, mental or physical incapacity, conviction of certain offences, or abuse of position.
There are restrictions on the future employment of Chairperson and whole-time members after they cease to hold office, requiring prior approval from the Central Government.
The Authority has powers of general superintendence and direction in administrative matters, to be exercised by the Chairperson.
Meetings of the Authority are to be conducted according to rules of procedure, with decisions made by majority vote.
Members with pecuniary interests in matters before the Authority must disclose their interest and abstain from deliberation and decision-making.
The Act establishes the National Pension System and outlines provisions for the Central Recordkeeping Agency, Points of Presence, and Pension Funds.
Restrictions are placed on foreign companies and individuals regarding participation in the pension sector.
Investment of subscriber funds outside India is prohibited.
The Act provides for the registration of intermediaries such as central recordkeeping agencies, pension funds, and points of presence.
Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance by intermediaries or other persons.
The Central Government has the power to issue directions to the Authority and to supersede the Authority under certain conditions.

penalties: Penalty for failure by an intermediary or any other person to comply with provisions of this Act, rules, regulations and directions (Section 28).
Specific penalties for offences committed under the Act (Section 32).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority is the primary enforcement authority, along with the Central Government for certain powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the Authority's powers of investigation, search and seizure, issuing directions, ensuring compliance, adjudication of penalties, and through legal proceedings for offences. The Securities Appellate Tribunal and Supreme Court are involved in appeals.

rights: Subscribers have rights related to their individual pension accounts and schemes.
The Authority has the right to investigate, search, seize, and issue directions to ensure compliance.
duties: The Authority has a duty to promote old age income security and protect subscriber interests.
Intermediaries and other persons have a duty to comply with the Act, rules, and regulations.
Members of the Authority have a duty to disclose pecuniary interests.
The Central Government has a duty to appoint members, issue notifications, and make rules.
obligations: Intermediaries have obligations related to registration, recordkeeping, and service delivery.
Subscribers have obligations related to making contributions to their pension accounts.
The Authority is obligated to establish and manage funds such as the Pension Regulatory and Development Fund and the Subscriber Education and Protection Fund.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority: Central Government appoints a date by notification, leading to the establishment of the Authority as a body corporate.
Appointment of Authority members: Central Government appoints Chairperson and members based on specified criteria.
Registration of Intermediaries: Intermediaries like central recordkeeping agencies and pension funds must obtain registration from the Authority under Section 27.
Investigation and Enforcement: The Authority can investigate non-compliance, conduct search and seizure, and issue directions for compliance.
Adjudication: The Authority has the power to adjudicate penalties for violations of the Act.
Appeals: Decisions of the Authority can be appealed to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and subsequently to the Supreme Court.
administration: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, established under the Act.
important_notes: Different commencement dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.

Words and expressions not defined in this Act are to be interpreted as defined in the Insurance Act, 1938; the Companies Act, 1956; the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956; and the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992.
The head office of the Authority is located in the National Capital Region.
Section 50A specifies that certain powers of the Authority do not apply to International Financial Services Centres.

title: THE STREET VENDORS (PROTECTION OF LIVELIHOOD AND REGULATION OF STREET VENDING) ACT, 2014
purpose: To protect the rights of urban street vendors and to regulate street vending activities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as per original text, but state amendments have been made). Does not apply to land, premises, and trains owned and controlled by the Railways under the Railway Act, 1989. Applies to urban street vendors and street vending activities.

key_definitions.appropriate_government: In respect of matters relating to a Union territory without Legislature, the Central Government; for Union territories with Legislature, the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi or the Government of Union territory of Puducherry; and for a State, the State Government.
key_definitions.holding_capacity: The maximum number of street vendors who can be accommodated in any vending zone, determined by the local authority on the recommendations of the Town Vending Committee.
key_definitions.local_authority: A Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Nagar Panchayat, Cantonment Board, civil area committee appointed under the Cantonment Act, 2006, or any other body entitled to function as a local authority for providing civic services and regulating street vending. Includes the planning authority.
key_definitions.mobile_vendors: Street vendors who carry out vending activities in designated areas by moving from one place to another.
key_definitions.natural_market: A market where sellers and buyers have traditionally congregated for the sale and purchase of products or services, as determined by the local authority on the recommendations of the Town Vending Committee.
key_definitions.planning_authority: An Urban Development Authority or any other authority designated by the appropriate Government responsible for regulating land use through master plans, development plans, etc.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act by the appropriate Government.
key_definitions.scheme: A scheme framed by the appropriate Government under section 38.
key_definitions.stationary_vendors: Street vendors who carry out vending activities on a regular basis at a specific location.
key_definitions.street_vendor: A person engaged in vending articles, goods, wares, food items, merchandise of everyday use, or offering services to the general public, in a street, lane, sidewalk, footpath, pavement, public park or any other public place or private area, from a temporary built-up structure or by moving from place to place. Includes hawker, peddler, squatter and other synonymous terms.
key_definitions.Town_Vending_Committee: The body constituted by the appropriate Government under section 22.
key_definitions.vending_zone: An area, place, or location designated by the local authority, on the recommendations of the Town Vending Committee, for street vendors' use, including footpaths, sidewalks, pavements, embankments, street portions, waiting areas, or any other suitable place for vending and services.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and provisions.
main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except J&K as originally enacted, with subsequent amendments), commencement date, and any specific provisions or exemptions.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'holding capacity', 'local authority', 'street vendor', 'vending zone', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Survey of street vendors and protection from eviction or relocation.
main_sections.description: Mandates the Town Vending Committee to conduct surveys of existing street vendors and prohibits their eviction or relocation until the survey is complete and certificates of vending are issued.

Details the process of issuing certificates of vending to street vendors identified in the survey, subject to age requirements and scheme conditions. It also addresses provisional certificates and scenarios where vendor numbers exceed holding capacity.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation or suspension of certificate of vending.
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a certificate of vending can be cancelled or suspended by the Town Vending Committee, including breach of conditions, misrepresentation, or fraud.
Enshrines the fundamental rights of street vendors as defined by the Act.
Specifies the responsibilities and obligations of street vendors.

main_sections.section_title: Relocation or eviction of street vendors.
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedures and grounds for relocation or eviction of street vendors.
Provides for the constitution and functions of the Town Vending Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Prevention of harassment by police and other authorities.
main_sections.description: Aims to protect street vendors from harassment by law enforcement and other governmental bodies.
Details the penalties that may be imposed for contravening the provisions of the Act.
Grants the appropriate Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the power to make bye-laws.

important_rules: Street vendors identified in a survey must be accommodated in vending zones, adhering to a norm of 2.5% of the population of the ward/zone/town/city, subject to the plan and holding capacity of the vending zones.
No street vendor can be evicted or relocated until the survey is completed and certificates of vending are issued to all vendors.

A street vendor must give an undertaking that they will carry on vending themselves or through a family member, have no other means of livelihood, and will not transfer the certificate or the specified place.
In case of death, permanent disability, or illness of a street vendor, a family member (spouse, then dependent child) may vend in their place until the certificate's validity.
Street vendors must maintain cleanliness and public hygiene in their vending areas and keep civic amenities in good condition.
Street vendors are required to pay vending fees as specified in the scheme.

penalties: Penalty for contraventions as specified in Section 28.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Town Vending Committee, local authority, appropriate Government, and other designated authorities as per the Act's provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the conduct of surveys, issuance and cancellation/suspension of certificates of vending, dispute resolution mechanisms, imposition of penalties, and enforcement of rules and schemes made under the Act.

rights: Protection from eviction or relocation until surveyed and issued a certificate of vending.
Right to a certificate of vending if eligible.
Right to a new site or area on relocation (Section 13).
Prevention of harassment by police and other authorities (Section 27).
duties: To carry on vending activities personally or through a family member.
To have no other means of livelihood.
Not to transfer the certificate of vending or the place specified therein.
To maintain cleanliness and public hygiene.
To maintain civic amenities in vending zones in good condition.
To pay vending fees.
obligations: To comply with the terms and conditions of the certificate of vending and the scheme.
To adhere to the restrictions and conditions specified in the plan for street vending.

key_procedures: Conducting a survey of existing street vendors by the Town Vending Committee.
Issuance of a certificate of vending by the Town Vending Committee to eligible street vendors.
Renewal of certificates of vending.
Cancellation or suspension of certificates of vending upon breach of conditions or fraud.
Redressal of grievances or resolution of disputes of street vendors by the committee under section 20.
Relocation or eviction of street vendors under specified conditions.
Seizure and reclaiming of goods.
Constitution and functioning of the Town Vending Committee.
