Development and implementation of a plan for street vending.
administration: The Act is administered by the 'appropriate Government' (Central Government for Union territories without Legislature, State Governments for States, etc.), local authorities, and Town Vending Committees constituted under the Act.
important_notes: The Act explicitly states that it does not confer ownership rights on street vendors (Section 29).
Provisions of the Act do not apply to any land, premises, and trains owned and controlled by the Railways under the Railway Act, 1989.
State Amendments and adaptation orders have been made, particularly concerning the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, to include these regions within the Act's applicability.

title: The National Judicial Appointments Commission Act, 2014
purpose: To regulate the procedure to be followed by the National Judicial Appointments Commission for recommending persons for appointment as the Chief Justice of India and other Judges of the Supreme Court and Chief Justices and other Judges of High Courts and for their transfers and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the process of recommending persons for appointment as Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and for the transfer of Judges of High Courts. It is administered by the Central Government and the National Judicial Appointments Commission.

key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Commission.
key_definitions.Commission: The National Judicial Appointments Commission referred to in article 124A of the Constitution.
key_definitions.High Court: The High Court in respect of which recommendation for appointment of a Judge is proposed to be made by the Commission.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Commission and includes its Chairperson.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by the rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Commission under this Act.

main_sections.description: Names the act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as Chairperson, Commission, High Court, Member, prescribed, and regulations.
States that the Headquarters of the Commission shall be at Delhi.

main_sections.section_title: Reference to Commission for filling up of vacancies
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the Central Government to inform the Commission about existing and upcoming vacancies in the Supreme Court and High Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for selection of Judge of Supreme Court
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for the Commission to recommend persons for appointment as the Chief Justice of India and Judges of the Supreme Court, emphasizing seniority, ability, and merit.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for selection of Judge of High Court
main_sections.description: Describes the process for the Commission to recommend persons for appointment as Chief Justices and Judges of High Courts, including consultation with the concerned Chief Justice and other stakeholders.

main_sections.section_title: Power of President to require reconsideration
main_sections.description: Grants the President the power to ask the Commission to reconsider its recommendations for appointments.
Empowers the Central Government to appoint officers and employees for the Commission, and specifies their terms and conditions of service.
States that the Commission shall recommend the transfer of Chief Justices and other Judges of High Courts, and shall specify the procedure for such transfers by regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed by Commission in discharge of its functions
main_sections.description: Grants the Commission the power to specify its own procedures for discharging its functions and conducting meetings through regulations.
Authorizes the Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, including matters related to fees, allowances, and conditions of service.
Empowers the Commission to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules, covering various aspects of selection, appointment, and transfer of judges.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Specifies that all rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a total period of thirty days and are subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.
Authorizes the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, with a time limit of five years from the commencement of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Central Government shall, within thirty days of the Act coming into force, intimate existing vacancies in the Supreme Court and High Courts to the Commission.
Rule 2: The Central Government shall, six months prior to the completion of a Judge's term, refer to the Commission for recommendations to fill the vacancy.
Rule 3: The Central Government shall, within thirty days of the occurrence of a vacancy due to death or resignation, refer to the Commission for recommendations.
Rule 4: A member of the Commission whose name is being considered for recommendation shall not participate in the meeting where their name is discussed.

Rule 5: The Commission shall not recommend a person for appointment if any two members of the Commission do not agree for such recommendation (applicable to Supreme Court and High Court appointments).
Rule 6: The President may require the Commission to reconsider its recommendation, but must appoint if the Commission reiterates its recommendation after reconsideration.
Rule 7: Rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before Parliament and are subject to parliamentary modification or annulment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and the National Judicial Appointments Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the procedures outlined in the Act for recommendation, appointment, and transfer of Judges, and through the power of the Central Government to make rules and the Commission to make regulations. The Act itself is subject to parliamentary oversight.

rights: The right of eligible persons to be considered for appointment as Judges based on merit and suitability.
The right of the President to seek reconsideration of recommendations.
The right of Parliament to modify or annul rules and regulations made under the Act.
duties: Duty of the Central Government to intimate vacancies to the Commission.
Duty of the Commission to follow prescribed procedures for selection and transfer.
Duty of the Commission to consider ability, merit, and other suitability criteria.
Duty of the Commission to consult relevant authorities as specified.
obligations: The obligation of the Commission to make recommendations for appointments and transfers.
The obligation of the Central Government to appoint officers and employees for the Commission.
The obligation to lay rules and regulations before Parliament.

key_procedures: Filling Judicial Vacancies: The Central Government must notify the Commission of vacancies in the Supreme Court and High Courts within specified timeframes.

Supreme Court Judge Selection: The Commission recommends the senior-most Judge as CJI if fit, and other Judges based on ability, merit, and suitability. Members whose names are considered do not participate.

High Court Judge Selection: The Commission recommends High Court Judges for CJ posts based on seniority, ability, merit, and suitability. It also seeks nominations and consults the concerned Chief Justice, senior Judges, and other stakeholders. Views of the Governor and Chief Minister are also elicited.
Judicial Transfers: The Commission recommends transfers of High Court Chief Justices and Judges, specifying the procedure by regulations.
Reconsideration of Recommendations: The President can request the Commission to reconsider a recommendation, but must appoint if the Commission reiterates its decision.
Rule and Regulation Making: The Central Government makes rules, and the Commission makes regulations, to carry out the Act's provisions. These are subject to parliamentary review.
administration: Central Government and the National Judicial Appointments Commission.
important_notes: The Act was struck down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India on 16th October, 2015, in the case of Supreme Court Advocates-on Record Association & Anr. Vs. Union of India. Therefore, its provisions are no longer in effect.
The Act came into force on 13th April, 2015.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to five years from the commencement of the Act.

title: THE REPEALING AND AMENDING (SECOND) ACT, 2015
purpose: To repeal certain enactments and to amend certain other enactments.
scope: This act applies to enactments that are specified for repeal or amendment. The geographical scope is India, as it is an Act of the Parliament of India. The subject matter scope is the repeal and amendment of existing legal acts.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Repealing and Amending (Second) Act, 2015.
This section provides for the repeal of enactments specified in the First Schedule to the extent mentioned in the fourth column of that Schedule.
This section provides for the amendment of enactments specified in the Second Schedule to the extent and in the manner mentioned in the fourth column of that Schedule.

This section outlines what the repeal by this Act will NOT affect. This includes any Act in which a repealed enactment has been applied, incorporated, or referred to. It also preserves the validity, invalidity, effect, or consequences of anything already done or suffered, and any rights, obligations, or liabilities already acquired, accrued, or incurred. Furthermore, it does not affect any remedy or proceeding in respect thereof, nor revive or restore any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, right, title, privilege, restriction, exemption, usage, practice, procedure, or other matter or thing not currently existing or in force. It also states that the repeal does not affect any principle or rule of law, established jurisdiction, form or course of pleading, practice or procedure, or existing usage, custom, privilege, restriction, exemption, office or appointment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text. Typically, enforcement would be by the relevant authorities responsible for the acts being amended or repealed.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text. Enforcement would depend on the nature of the specific amendments made to other enactments.

rights: The right to continue existing rights, obligations, and liabilities that were acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal.
duties: The duty to adhere to the new amendments made to certain enactments.
obligations: The obligation to continue fulfilling existing obligations, liabilities, and claims that were already in force before the repeal.

administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text. Administration would typically fall under the Ministry of Law and Justice or the relevant ministries/departments overseeing the enactments being amended or repealed.
important_notes: The Act repeals numerous other Acts, in whole or in part, as listed in the First Schedule.
The Act amends certain other Acts, as detailed in the Second Schedule.
The 'Savings' section (Section 4) is crucial for understanding that the repeal or amendment does not invalidate past actions or accrued rights.

title: THE COAL MINES (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) ACT, 2015
purpose: To provide for the allocation of coal mines and vesting of the right, title and interest in and over the land and mine infrastructure together with mining leases to successful bidders and allottees, with a view to ensure continuity in coal mining operations and production of coal, and for promoting optimum utilisation of coal resources consistent with the requirement of the country in national interest, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. This act was enacted in pursuance of directions from the Supreme Court regarding the cancellation of coal block allocations.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to Schedule I coal mines, which include coal mines and coal blocks whose allocation was cancelled by the Supreme Court, as well as coal-bearing land and existing mine infrastructure acquired by prior allottees. Schedule II coal mines are a subset of Schedule I mines.

key_definitions.additional_levy: The additional levy as determined by the Supreme Court in Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 120 of 2012 as two hundred and ninety-five rupees per metric tonne of coal extracted.
key_definitions.allotment_order: The allotment order issued under section 5.
key_definitions.appointed_date: For Schedule I coal mines (excluding Schedule II), it's September 24, 2014 (date of cancellation of prior allotments). For Schedule II coal mines, it's April 1, 2015 (date of cancellation of prior allotments).
key_definitions.coal_mining_operations: Any operation undertaken for the purpose of winning coal.
key_definitions.mine_infrastructure: Includes tangible assets used for coal mining operations, such as civil works, workshops, immovable coal winning equipment, foundations, electrical systems, communication systems, relief centers, administrative offices, coal handling arrangements, crushing and conveying systems, railway sidings, pits, shafts, inclines, underground transport systems, hauling systems (excluding movable equipment unless embedded in land), and land demarcated for afforestation and rehabilitation.
key_definitions.nominated_authority: The authority nominated by the Central Government under section 6.
key_definitions.prior_allottee: Prior allottee of Schedule I coal mines who had been allotted coal mines between 1993 and March 31, 2011, whose allotments were cancelled by the Supreme Court. This includes allotments de-allocated prior to or during the pendency of the relevant Writ Petition. If a mining lease was executed in favour of a third party after allocation, that third party is deemed a prior allottee.
key_definitions.schedule_i_coal_mines: All coal mines and coal blocks whose allocation was cancelled by the Supreme Court, including de-allocated ones; coal bearing land acquired by prior allottees; and existing mine infrastructure.
key_definitions.schedule_ii_coal_mines: Forty-two Schedule I coal mines listed in Schedule II, in relation to which the Supreme Court order dated September 24, 2014, was made.
key_definitions.specified_end_use: Production of iron and steel; generation of power (including captive use); washing of coal; cement; and such other end-uses as the Central Government may notify.

main_sections.description: States the short title as 'The Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015', declares its extent to the whole of India, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on October 21, 2014.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to expediency of Union action.
main_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to take action for the development of Schedule I coal mines and continuous extraction of coal for optimum utilization.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'additional levy', 'allotment order', 'appointed date', 'coal mining operations', 'mine infrastructure', 'nominated authority', 'prior allottee', 'Schedule I coal mines', 'Schedule II coal mines', 'specified end-use', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Eligibility to participate in auction and payment of fees.
main_sections.description: Details the process of allocating Schedule I coal mines through public auction, specifies eligibility criteria for bidders (including conditions for prior allottees), and mentions payment of fees. It also covers the Central Government's power to select companies for reconnaissance permits, prospecting licenses, or mining leases through auction.

main_sections.section_title: Allotment of mines to Government companies or corporations.
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to allot Schedule I coal mines to Government companies or corporations or joint ventures, especially for awarded power projects based on competitive bids for tariff. It sets conditions on shareholding by non-Government entities and prohibits alienation of interest in such joint ventures.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government to act through nominated authority.
main_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to appoint a nominated authority (not below the rank of Joint Secretary) to act on its behalf for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Utilisation of movable property used in coal mining operations.
main_sections.description: Deals with the treatment of movable property used in coal mining operations of prior allottees.

main_sections.section_title: Discharge or adoption of third party contracts with prior allottees.
main_sections.description: Provides for the discharge or adoption of contracts entered into by prior allottees with third parties.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions in relation to secured creditors.
main_sections.description: Outlines the provisions concerning secured creditors of prior allottees.

main_sections.section_title: Void alienations and permitted security interests.
main_sections.description: Addresses alienations made by prior allottees and specifies permitted security interests.
Specifies the liabilities that prior allottees will have to bear.

main_sections.section_title: Commissioner of payments to be appointed and his powers.
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments and outlines their powers.

main_sections.section_title: Valuation of compensation for payment to prior allottee.
main_sections.description: Deals with the valuation of compensation to be paid to prior allottees.

main_sections.section_title: Responsibility of Central Government after appointed date.
main_sections.description: Defines the responsibilities of the Central Government after the appointed date.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government to appoint designated custodian.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint a designated custodian.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of designated custodian in respect of Schedule II coal mines.
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the designated custodian specifically concerning Schedule II coal mines.
Grants the Central Government powers for the acquisition of land.
Concerns the realization of the additional levy.
Specifies penalties for certain offences committed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to comply with directions of Central Government.
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties for failure to comply with directions issued by the Central Government.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of certain Acts contained in Schedule IV.
main_sections.description: Provides for the amendment of certain Acts as listed in Schedule IV.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing provisions and savings in relation to past actions.

important_rules: Schedule I coal mines are to be allocated through public auction, subject to prescribed rules and fees not exceeding five crore rupees.
Companies can be selected through competitive bidding for reconnaissance permits, prospecting licenses, or mining leases.
Prior allottees are eligible to participate in auctions if they have paid the additional levy within the prescribed period; non-payment disqualifies them, their promoters, or associated companies.
Prior allottees convicted for offenses related to coal block allocation and sentenced to imprisonment for more than three years are ineligible for auction participation.
The Central Government can allot Schedule I coal mines to Government companies or corporations, or joint ventures of such entities, or companies awarded power projects on competitive bids for tariff.
In joint ventures between Government companies/corporations, no entity other than a Government company/corporation can hold more than twenty-six percent of the paid-up share capital.
Joint ventures of Government companies/corporations are prohibited from alienating or transferring any interest (except for loans/advances from banks/financial institutions) in the joint venture.
No allotment under sub-section (1) of section 5 shall be made to a prior allottee if the additional levy has not been paid within the specified period.
The Central Government shall appoint a nominated authority (not below Joint Secretary rank) to act on its behalf.
The Act vests rights, title, and interest in land and mine infrastructure of allocated coal mines with successful bidders/allottees.
Provisions exist for the utilization of movable property, discharge or adoption of third-party contracts, and handling of secured creditors' interests of prior allottees.
Alienations by prior allottees are void unless they are permitted security interests.
Penalties are prescribed for certain offences, including failure to comply with Central Government directions.

penalties: Penalties for certain offences (section 23).
Penalty for failure to comply with directions of Central Government (section 24).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, Nominated Authority, Designated Custodian.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appointment of a nominated authority to act on behalf of the Central Government, appointment of a designated custodian for Schedule II mines, imposition of penalties for offences, and by overriding other laws.

rights: Successful bidders and allottees have rights to the allocated coal mines, including land and mine infrastructure.
Prior allottees have rights to compensation and provisions related to their movable property and contracts.
Secured creditors have rights as defined under the Act.
Companies selected through auction have the right to obtain reconnaissance permits, prospecting licenses, or mining leases.
duties: Prior allottees have a duty to pay the additional levy.
Entities participating in auctions or receiving allotments have duties to comply with the terms and conditions.
Companies have a duty to comply with directions from the Central Government.
obligations: Obligations related to the discharge or adoption of third-party contracts by prior allottees.
Obligations of prior allottees concerning their liabilities.
Obligations of joint ventures of Government companies/corporations regarding alienation of interests.
Obligations of entities to ensure continuity in coal mining operations and production of coal.

key_procedures: Public auction of Schedule I coal mines by the Central Government, with prescribed rules and fees.
Selection of companies through competitive bidding for reconnaissance permits, prospecting licenses, or mining leases.
Allotment of Schedule I coal mines to Government companies or corporations, or joint ventures, or companies awarded power projects.
Appointment of a nominated authority by the Central Government to act on its behalf.
Appointment of a designated custodian by the Central Government for Schedule II coal mines.
Issuance of vesting orders or allotment orders by the nominated authority.
Procedure for the discharge or adoption of third-party contracts.
Procedure for the valuation of compensation for payment to prior allottees.
Procedure for the realization of additional levy.
Procedure for the acquisition of land.
Procedure for making rules by the Central Government.
administration: Central Government, assisted by a nominated authority.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over other laws where there is inconsistency.
The Supreme Court's judgment dated August 25, 2014, and its order dated September 24, 2014, are the basis for this Act, leading to the cancellation of prior coal block allocations.
Specific details regarding Schedule I, Schedule II, Schedule III, and Schedule IV coal mines and amendments are contained in the Schedules appended to the Act.

Words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957, the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, and the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973, shall have the meanings assigned to them in those Acts.

title: The Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015
purpose: To make provisions to deal with the problem of black money in the form of undisclosed foreign income and assets, to provide for the procedure for dealing with such income and assets, and to impose tax on any undisclosed foreign income and asset held outside India, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to assessees who are residents in India, or non-residents or not ordinarily residents who were resident in India in the previous year relevant to the income or acquisition of the asset.

key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: The Appellate Tribunal constituted under section 252 of the Income-tax Act.
key_definitions.assessee: A person who is a resident in India or a non-resident/not ordinarily resident who was resident in India in the relevant previous year.
key_definitions.assessment year: The period of twelve months commencing on the 1st day of April every year.
key_definitions.Board: The Central Board of Direct Taxes constituted under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963.
key_definitions.participant: A partner in a firm or a member in an association of persons or body of individuals.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.previous year: Defined by specific periods related to business setup/closure, new income sources, discontinuance of business, or dissolution/liquidation, preceding the assessment year.
key_definitions.resident: A person who is resident in India within the meaning of section 6 of the Income-tax Act.
key_definitions.undisclosed asset located outside India: An asset (including financial interest in any entity) located outside India, held by the assessee or for which they are the beneficial owner, with no satisfactory explanation for the source of investment.
key_definitions.undisclosed foreign income and asset: The total amount of undisclosed income from a source outside India and the value of an undisclosed asset located outside India.
key_definitions.unincorporated body: A firm, an association of persons, or a body of individuals.
key_definitions.value of an undisclosed asset: Has the meaning assigned to it in sub-section (2) of section 3.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, that it extends to the whole of India, and its commencement date (1st April, 2016).
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'assessee', 'undisclosed asset located outside India', and 'undisclosed foreign income and asset'.

Imposes a tax at the rate of thirty per cent on the total undisclosed foreign income and asset of an assessee for every assessment year commencing on or after 1st April, 2016. An undisclosed asset is charged tax on its value in the previous year it comes to the notice of the Assessing Officer.

main_sections.section_title: Scope of total undisclosed foreign income and asset
main_sections.description: Defines what constitutes the total undisclosed foreign income and asset, including undisclosed income from sources outside India and the value of undisclosed assets outside India. Excludes variations made under specific sections of the Income-tax Act from being included.

main_sections.section_title: Computation of total undisclosed foreign income and asset
main_sections.description: Specifies how the total undisclosed foreign income and asset is computed, disallowing deductions for expenditures, allowances, or set-off of losses. Allows reduction from the value of an undisclosed asset if it was acquired from income already assessed or assessable to tax.
Specifies that income-tax authorities under section 116 of the Income-tax Act are the tax authorities for this Act. Their jurisdiction is the same as under the Income-tax Act.

important_rules: Tax is charged at 30% on total undisclosed foreign income and asset from assessment year commencing on or after 1st April, 2016.
An undisclosed asset located outside India is charged to tax on its value in the previous year it comes to the notice of the Assessing Officer.
No deduction for any expenditure, allowance, or set-off of any loss is allowed in computing total undisclosed foreign income and asset.
Income assessed to tax under the Income-tax Act prior to or during the applicability of this Act can be reduced from the value of an undisclosed asset if the assessee provides satisfactory evidence.
Income included in the total undisclosed foreign income and asset under this Act shall not form part of the total income under the Income-tax Act.

penalties: Penalty in relation to undisclosed foreign income and asset (Section 41)
Penalty for failure to furnish return in relation to foreign income and asset (Section 42)
Penalty for failure to furnish accurate particulars about an asset located outside India (Section 43)
Penalty for default in payment of tax arrear (Section 44)
Penalty for other defaults (Section 45)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Income-tax authorities specified in section 116 of the Income-tax Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, recovery of tax dues, imposition of penalties, and prosecution for offences.

rights: Right to appeal to Commissioner (Appeals), Appellate Tribunal, High Court, and Supreme Court.
Declaration of undisclosed foreign asset not admissible in evidence against the declarant (under Chapter VI).
Exemption from wealth-tax in respect of voluntarily disclosed assets (under Chapter VI).
duties: Duty to declare undisclosed foreign income and assets.
Duty to furnish return of income including information about foreign assets.
Duty to pay tax on undisclosed foreign income and assets.
Duty to cooperate with tax authorities for discovery and production of evidence.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on undisclosed foreign income and assets as per the Act.
Obligation to provide accurate information to tax authorities.
Obligation to comply with notices and demands issued by tax authorities.

key_procedures: Assessment and reassessment of undisclosed foreign income and assets.
Appeals process: appeals to Commissioner (Appeals), Appellate Tribunal, High Court, and Supreme Court.
Recovery of tax dues by Assessing Officer and Tax Recovery Officer.
Declaration of undisclosed foreign asset under Chapter VI (Tax Compliance for Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets).
administration: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and the income-tax authorities specified in section 116 of the Income-tax Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to bring undisclosed foreign income and assets into the tax net.
It provides for a specific tax compliance window under Chapter VI.
Income declared under this Act is not included in the total income under the Income-tax Act.
Proceedings under this Act are considered judicial proceedings.
This Act is not in derogation of any other law or any other provision of this Act.

title: THE REPEALING AND AMENDING ACT, 2015
purpose: To repeal certain enactments and to amend certain other enactments.
scope: Applies to various enactments as specified in the Schedules. It has a national scope within India, as indicated by references to the Republic of India and Parliament.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Repealing and Amending Act, 2015.
States that the enactments specified in the First Schedule are repealed to the extent mentioned in the fourth column of that Schedule.
States that the enactments specified in the Second Schedule are amended to the extent and in the manner mentioned in the fourth column of that Schedule.

Provides saving provisions, ensuring that the repeal of any enactment does not affect Acts in which it has been applied, incorporated, or referred to. It also preserves the validity, effect, or consequences of anything already done, and rights, obligations, or liabilities already acquired. It further states that the repeal does not affect any principle or rule of law, jurisdiction, practice, or procedure, nor does it provide or restore any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, right, title, privilege, restriction, exemption, usage, practice, procedure, or other matter or thing not then existing or in force.

important_rules: Rule 1: Enactments specified in the First Schedule are repealed to the extent mentioned in the fourth column of that Schedule.
Rule 2: Enactments specified in the Second Schedule are amended to the extent and in the manner mentioned in the fourth column of that Schedule.

Rule 3: The repeal of an enactment by this Act does not affect the validity or consequences of past actions, existing rights, obligations, liabilities, remedies, or proceedings. It also does not affect existing principles of law, jurisdiction, practices, or usages. Furthermore, it does not restore any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, or other matter that is not currently in existence or force.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text, as the act is about repealing and amending existing laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text, as the act is about repealing and amending existing laws.

rights: Preservation of rights already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal.
duties: Preservation of obligations already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal.
obligations: Preservation of obligations already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Identification and listing of enactments to be repealed in the First Schedule.
Procedure 2: Identification and listing of enactments to be amended in the Second Schedule, with specific details of amendments in the fourth column.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but typically such acts are administered by the Ministry of Law and Justice.
important_notes: The First Schedule lists numerous acts from 1897 to 2013 that are being repealed, with many of these being amendments to other acts.

The Second Schedule lists two acts (The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 and The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2011) that are being amended. The amendments include textual substitutions and year corrections.
The saving clause (Section 4) is extensive and designed to prevent unintended consequences from the repeals and amendments.

title: THE COMMERCIAL COURTS ACT, 2015
purpose: To provide for the constitution of Commercial Courts, Commercial Appellate Courts, Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division in the High Courts for adjudicating commercial disputes of specified value and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It establishes Commercial Courts at the District level and Commercial Divisions/Appellate Divisions in High Courts for adjudicating commercial disputes of a 'Specified Value'.

key_definitions.commercial_appellate_courts: Commercial Appellate Courts designated under section 3A.
key_definitions.commercial_appellate_division: Commercial Appellate Division in a High Court constituted under sub-section (1) of section 5.
key_definitions.commercial_court: Commercial Court constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.commercial_dispute: A dispute arising out of various commercial transactions including merchants' transactions, import/export, admiralty law, aircraft-related transactions, carriage of goods, construction, franchising, distribution, management, joint ventures, shareholders agreements, investment agreements, intellectual property rights, sale of goods, natural resources, insurance, and other disputes notified by the Central Government. It also includes disputes involving immovable property recovery or realization of monies out of immovable property used as security, or where one party is the State or its agencies.
key_definitions.commercial_division: Commercial Division in a High Court constituted under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.district_judge: Has the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (a) of article 236 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.document: Any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks, or electronic means, or by more than one of those means, intended to be used, or which may be used, for the purpose of recording that matter.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.schedule: The Schedule appended to the Act.
key_definitions.specified_value: In relation to a commercial dispute, the value of the subject-matter in respect of a suit as determined in accordance with section 12, which shall not be less than three lakh rupees or such higher value as may be notified by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date of commencement (deemed to have come into force on October 23, 2015).

Defines key terms used in the Act, including Commercial Courts, Commercial Divisions, commercial disputes, Specified Value, etc. It also states that undefined words and expressions will have the same meanings as in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
Empowers the State Government, in consultation with the High Court, to constitute Commercial Courts at the District level. It specifies provisions for pecuniary value and territorial jurisdiction.
Allows the State Government, in consultation with the High Court, to designate Commercial Appellate Courts at the District Judge level.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Commercial Division of High Court.
main_sections.description: Directs the Chief Justice of High Courts with ordinary original civil jurisdiction to constitute a Commercial Division, consisting of one or more Benches of a single Judge, for adjudicating commercial disputes.

Requires the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court to constitute a Commercial Appellate Division, with one or more Division Benches, for hearing appeals against orders of Commercial Courts and Commercial Divisions.
Grants Commercial Courts the jurisdiction to try all suits and applications related to commercial disputes of a Specified Value arising within their vested territorial jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of Commercial Divisions of High Courts.
main_sections.description: Specifies that all suits and applications relating to commercial disputes of a Specified Value filed in a High Court with ordinary original civil jurisdiction shall be heard and disposed of by the Commercial Division of that High Court. This also includes certain arbitration matters and appeals transferred under specific Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Bar against revision application or petition against an interlocutory order.
main_sections.description: Prohibits civil revision applications or petitions against any interlocutory order of a Commercial Court. Such challenges can only be raised in an appeal against the final decree.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction in respect of arbitration matters.
main_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction of Commercial Divisions and Commercial Courts for applications and appeals arising out of arbitration matters that are commercial disputes of a Specified Value, distinguishing between international and other arbitrations.
Lays down the criteria for determining the 'Specified Value' of a commercial dispute, which must be not less than three lakh rupees or a higher value as notified by the Central Government.
Mandates that before filing a suit for a commercial dispute, the plaintiff must exhaust the remedy of pre-institution mediation and settlement.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals from decrees of Commercial Courts and Commercial Divisions.
main_sections.description: Governs appeals from the decrees of Commercial Courts and Commercial Divisions, specifying the appellate authorities and timelines.

main_sections.section_title: Amendments to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 in its application to commercial disputes.
main_sections.description: Details the amendments made to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to streamline the procedure for commercial disputes, including provisions for case management, timelines, and evidence.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in respect of matters covered by this Act.
Provides for the repeal of any prior inconsistent provisions and savings for actions taken under previous laws.

important_rules: Pre-Institution Mediation: Before filing a suit for a commercial dispute, parties must attempt pre-institution mediation and settlement (Section 12A).

No Revision Against Interlocutory Orders: No civil revision application or petition can be filed against an interlocutory order of a Commercial Court. Such challenges must be raised in the appeal against the final decree (Section 8).
Timely Disposal: The Act emphasizes expeditious disposal of commercial disputes and appeals.
Amendments to CPC: The Act introduces specific amendments to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to expedite commercial litigation, including provisions for case management and timelines.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforcement is primarily through the established judicial system, with specific courts and divisions designated for commercial disputes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the adjudication of suits and applications by Commercial Courts, Commercial Divisions, and Commercial Appellate Divisions, with adherence to the procedural amendments introduced by the Act.

rights: Right to have commercial disputes of Specified Value adjudicated by specialized Commercial Courts and Divisions.
Right to appeal against decrees of Commercial Courts and Commercial Divisions.
Right to access justice in a timely manner for commercial disputes.
duties: Duty to attempt pre-institution mediation for commercial disputes.
Duty to adhere to the procedural timelines and case management rules introduced by the Act and amendments to the CPC.
Duty to comply with the orders and decrees of Commercial Courts and Divisions.
obligations: Plaintiffs have an obligation to exhaust the pre-institution mediation process.
Parties are obligated to follow the amended procedures for filing and prosecuting commercial suits.

key_procedures: Pre-institution mediation and settlement process before filing a suit.
Filing of suits and applications in the designated Commercial Courts or Commercial Divisions based on Specified Value and territorial jurisdiction.
Case management and adherence to timelines as per amended Code of Civil Procedure.
Appeals against decrees of Commercial Courts and Commercial Divisions.
administration: Various State Governments and High Courts are responsible for the constitution and administration of Commercial Courts, Commercial Divisions, and Commercial Appellate Divisions. The Central Government has the power to make rules and notify higher Specified Values.
important_notes: The Act aims to expedite the resolution of commercial disputes.
The definition of 'commercial dispute' is broad and covers a wide range of business-related conflicts.
The 'Specified Value' threshold for a dispute to be considered commercial is subject to modification by the Central Government.

title: THE JUVENILE JUSTICE (CARE AND PROTECTION OF CHILDREN) ACT, 2015
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to children alleged and found to be in conflict with law and children in need of care and protection by catering to their basic needs through proper care, protection, development, treatment, social re-integration, by adopting a child-friendly approach in the adjudication and disposal of matters in the best interest of children and for their rehabilitation through processes provided, and institutions and bodies established, herein under and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to all matters concerning children in need of care and protection and children in conflict with law, including apprehension, detention, prosecution, penalty or imprisonment, rehabilitation, social re-integration, adoption, and restoration of such children.

key_definitions.child: A person who has not completed eighteen years of age.
key_definitions.child in conflict with law: A child who is alleged or found to have committed an offence and who has not completed eighteen years of age on the date of commission of such offence.
key_definitions.child in need of care and protection: Includes children who are abandoned, begging, working in contravention of law, abused, neglected, mentally ill, orphaned, missing, runaways, victims of armed conflict, or at risk of child marriage or drug abuse.
key_definitions.adoption: The process through which the adopted child is permanently separated from his biological parents and becomes the lawful child of his adoptive parents with all the rights, privileges and responsibilities that are attached to a biological child.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, commencement date, and its applicability to all matters concerning children in need of care and protection and children in conflict with law.
Defines various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'abandoned child', 'adoption', 'child', 'child in conflict with law', 'child in need of care and protection', 'Board', 'Committee', etc.

main_sections.section_title: General principles to be followed in administration of Act
main_sections.description: Outlines the fundamental principles that must guide the administration of the Act, emphasizing the best interest of the child.
Establishes the constitution of Juvenile Justice Boards for inquiring into offences committed by children in conflict with law.

main_sections.section_title: Apprehension of child alleged to be in conflict with law
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for apprehending a child alleged to have committed an offence.

main_sections.section_title: Bail to a person who is apparently a child alleged to be in conflict with law
main_sections.description: Specifies the provisions related to granting bail to a child in conflict with law.

main_sections.section_title: Inquiry by Board regarding child in conflict with law
main_sections.description: Describes the process of inquiry to be conducted by the Juvenile Justice Board concerning a child in conflict with law.
Establishes the constitution of Child Welfare Committees for dealing with children in need of care and protection.
Details the procedure for producing a child in need of care and protection before the Child Welfare Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for declaring a child legally free for adoption
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for declaring a child as legally free for adoption.
Covers the general provisions related to adoption.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on disclosure of identity of children
main_sections.description: Prohibits the disclosure of the identity of children involved in legal proceedings under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Classification of offences and designated court
main_sections.description: Classifies offences related to children and designates the courts responsible for trying them.
Repeals previous legislation and provides for savings.

important_rules: Rule 1: The provisions of this Act shall apply to all matters concerning children in need of care and protection and children in conflict with law.
Rule 2: The best interest of the child must be the paramount consideration in all decisions and actions taken under this Act.
Rule 3: Children in conflict with law shall be apprehended, detained, prosecuted, and rehabilitated with a child-friendly approach.
Rule 4: Procedures for dealing with children in conflict with law and children in need of care and protection must be distinct and appropriate to their respective needs.
Rule 5: Any person aware of a child in need of care and protection has a mandatory reporting obligation.
Rule 6: The identity of children involved in proceedings under this Act must be protected and not disclosed.
Rule 7: Specific procedures and institutions are established for the care, protection, rehabilitation, and social re-integration of children.

penalties: Penalty for non-reporting of a child in need of care and protection (Section 34).
Penalty for non-registration of child care institutions (Section 42).
Punitive measures for adoption without following prescribed procedures (Section 80).
Punishment for various offences against children, including cruelty, exploitation, child labour, sale and procurement of children, etc. (Sections 75, 76, 78, 79, 81, 83, 84, 85).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities are involved, including the Juvenile Justice Board, Child Welfare Committee, Child Welfare Police Officer, Special Juvenile Police Unit, District Child Protection Unit, State Child Protection Society, Central Adoption Resource Authority, and designated courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves apprehension, inquiry, bail, orders of placement in institutions, adoption procedures, and prosecution for offences committed against children. The Act also provides for monitoring of implementation and the establishment of funds for child welfare.

rights: Right to care, protection, development, and rehabilitation.
Right to be treated with dignity and in a child-friendly manner.
Right to have their best interests considered in all matters.
Right to legal aid.
Right to privacy and protection of identity.
duties: Duty of the State to ensure that all needs of children are met and their basic human rights are protected.
Duty of parents, guardians, and any person having knowledge of a child in need of care and protection to report to the authorities.
Duty of institutions to be registered and to provide care and rehabilitation services.
Duty of law enforcement agencies to handle children in conflict with law with a child-friendly approach.
obligations: Obligation to follow child-friendly procedures in all matters concerning children.
Obligation to adhere to the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child and other international instruments.
Obligation to ensure the social re-integration of children.
Obligation for prospective adoptive parents to follow prescribed adoption procedures.
Obligation for authorities to establish and maintain institutions for the care and protection of children.

key_procedures: Procedure for apprehension, bail, and inquiry of a child in conflict with law by the Juvenile Justice Board.
Procedure for producing a child in need of care and protection before the Child Welfare Committee.
Procedure for declaring a child legally free for adoption.
Procedure for adoption by Indian and inter-country prospective adoptive parents.
Procedure for registration and functioning of child care institutions.
Procedure for rehabilitation and social re-integration of children.
Procedure for handling offences against children and their trial in designated courts.
Procedure for appeals and revision.
administration: The Act is administered by various governmental and non-governmental bodies at the central, state, and district levels, including the Ministry of Women and Child Development (implied through Central Adoption Resource Authority and State Child Protection Societies), Juvenile Justice Boards, Child Welfare Committees, Child Welfare Police Officers, and Special Juvenile Police Units.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to consolidate and amend the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000.
It incorporates standards prescribed in international instruments such as the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Beijing Rules.
The Act emphasizes a child-friendly approach and the best interests of the child in all proceedings.
The definition of 'child' is a person who has not completed eighteen years of age.
Specific provisions exist for children in conflict with law and children in need of care and protection, ensuring distinct procedures for each category.
The Act provides for various types of institutions and facilities for the care, protection, and rehabilitation of children.

title: The Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016
purpose: To give effect to the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft and for matters connected therewith, addressing unlawful acts of seizure or exercise of control of aircraft which jeopardize safety of persons and property, and to incorporate amendments required by a Supplementary Protocol to the Convention.
scope: Applies to the whole of India and to any offence committed outside India by any person. It covers unlawful seizure of aircraft, acts of violence connected with hijacking, and related offences.

key_definitions.agency: The National Investigation Agency constituted under section 3 of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.
key_definitions.aircraft: Any aircraft, whether or not registered in India, other than a military aircraft or an aircraft used in customs or police service.
key_definitions.convention_country: A country in which the Hague Convention is in force.
key_definitions.hague_convention: The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft signed at The Hague on December 16, 1970, and includes the Protocol Supplementary to the Convention signed at Beijing on September 10, 2010.
key_definitions.hostage: A passenger or crew member, security personnel, or ground support staff who is unlawfully seized or detained on an aircraft or at an airport with the intention to secure demands.
key_definitions.security_personnel: Personnel deployed by the Central Government or authorized agency to ensure civil aviation security against unlawful interference, including acts like unlawful seizure, hostage-taking, forcible intrusion, introduction of weapons, and communication of false information.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Defines the title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), its application to offences committed outside India, and the commencement date to be notified by the Central Government.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Agency', 'aircraft', 'aircraft registered in India', 'Convention country', 'Hague Convention', 'hostage', 'military aircraft', 'notification', and 'security personnel'.

Defines the offence of hijacking, including unlawful seizure or control of an aircraft by force, threat, coercion, intimidation, or technological means. It also covers threats, attempts, abetment, organization, direction, participation as an accomplice, and assisting in evading investigation or prosecution.

Prescribes punishment for hijacking, including death penalty if it results in the death of a hostage, security personnel, or any uninvolved person as a direct consequence. Otherwise, it's life imprisonment and fine, with confiscation of property.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of powers of investigations, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution on officers of the Central Government or the Agency, overriding the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. All police and government officers are required to assist.

Establishes jurisdiction for offences committed outside India if the offender is found in India. It also specifies conditions under which courts can take cognizance of such offences, including if they occur within India, against Indian-registered aircraft, or involve Indian citizens.

Provides for the designation of a Court of Sessions as a Designated Court for speedy trials, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court. Special Courts under the NIA Act, 2008, are also designated courts. Designated Courts are to hold trials on a day-to-day basis where practicable.

Deems offences under sections 3 and 5 as extraditable offences for all extradition treaties of India with Convention countries. It also outlines the application of the Extradition Act, 1962, to such offences.

important_rules: Rule: An aircraft is considered 'in service' from the start of pre-flight preparation until 24 hours after landing, or until authorities take over responsibility in case of forced landing.
Rule: Offences under this Act committed outside India can be tried in India as if committed within India, subject to specific conditions.
Rule: Designated Courts shall, as far as practicable, hold trials on a day-to-day basis to ensure speedy disposal.
Rule: Offences under this Act are extraditable and included in India's extradition treaties with Convention countries.
Rule: Prosecution for offences under this Act requires previous sanction.

penalties: Death penalty: If the hijacking offence results in the death of a hostage, security personnel, or any person not involved in the offence as a direct consequence.
Imprisonment for life and fine: For the offence of hijacking, with the movable and immovable property also liable to be confiscated.
Punishment for acts of violence: Same as if the act of violence had been committed in India.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officers of the Central Government or the National Investigation Agency (NIA), and all police and government officers are empowered to assist.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through arrest, investigation, and prosecution powers conferred on specific officers, and by designated courts for speedy trials. Extradition provisions are also utilized for offenders found abroad.

rights: Right to a speedy trial before a Designated Court.
Protection of actions taken in good faith under the Act.
duties: Duty of police and government officers to assist in the execution of the Act.
Duty to comply with provisions related to extradition.
obligations: Obligation to prevent and suppress unlawful seizure of aircraft.
Obligation to prosecute offenders of hijacking and related acts.

key_procedures: Procedure for conferring investigation and prosecution powers on specific officers by the Central Government via notification.
Procedure for the establishment and functioning of Designated Courts for speedy trials.
Procedure for taking cognizance of offences by the Designated Court upon perusal of a report or complaint.
Procedure for extradition of offenders under the Extradition Act, 1962.
administration: Central Government, National Investigation Agency (NIA), State Governments (for designating courts).
important_notes: Note: The Act incorporates amendments from the Protocol Supplementary to the Convention signed at Beijing on September 10, 2010, to address new types of threats to civil aviation.
Note: The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, apply to proceedings before a Designated Court, unless otherwise specified.
Note: Previous sanction is necessary for prosecution.

title: THE RIGHTS OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES ACT, 2016
purpose: To give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, by promoting their empowerment and ensuring equality and non-discrimination.
scope: This Act applies to all persons with disabilities, their rights and entitlements, education, skill development, employment, social security, health, rehabilitation, recreation, and specific provisions for persons with benchmark disabilities and those with high support needs. It also outlines the duties of appropriate governments, registration of institutions, certification of disabilities, advisory boards, commissioners, special courts, and funds for persons with disabilities. The Act is enacted by the Parliament of India and applies throughout India.

key_definitions.appropriate Government: In relation to the Central Government or any establishment wholly or substantially financed by that Government, or a Cantonment Board, the Central Government. In relation to a State Government or any establishment, wholly or substantially financed by that Government, or any local authority, other than a Cantonment Board, the State Government.
key_definitions.barrier: Any factor including communicational, cultural, economic, environmental, institutional, political, social, attitudinal or structural factors which hampers the full and effective participation of persons with disabilities in society.
key_definitions.person with disability: A person with long term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders his full and effective participation in society equally with others.
key_definitions.person with benchmark disability: A person with not less than forty per cent. of a specified disability where specified disability has not been defined in measurable terms and includes a person with disability where specified disability has been defined in measurable terms, as certified by the certifying authority.
key_definitions.reasonable accommodation: Necessary and appropriate modification and adjustments, without imposing a disproportionate or undue burden in a particular case, to ensure to persons with disabilities the enjoyment or exercise of rights equally with others.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'barrier', 'person with disability', 'person with benchmark disability', and 'reasonable accommodation'.
Establishes the principle of equality and non-discrimination for persons with disabilities.
Outlines the responsibilities of educational institutions concerning the education of persons with disabilities.
Prohibits discrimination against persons with disabilities in employment.
Mandates the appropriate Governments to undertake awareness campaigns about disabilities.
Lays down provisions for ensuring accessibility for persons with disabilities in various aspects of life.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for contravention of provisions of Act or rules or regulations made thereunder
main_sections.description: Specifies the penalties for violating the provisions of the Act, rules, or regulations.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Persons with disabilities have the right to equality and non-discrimination (Section 3).
Educational institutions have a duty to promote inclusive education (Section 16).
There should be no discrimination in employment based on disability (Section 20).
Appropriate Governments must conduct awareness campaigns (Section 39).
Accessibility must be ensured in various domains (Section 40).
Contravention of the Act's provisions carries penalties (Section 89).

penalties: Punishment for contravention of provisions of the Act, rules, or regulations made thereunder (Section 89).
Offences committed by companies (Section 90).
Punishment for fraudulently availing any benefit meant for persons with benchmark disabilities (Section 91).
Punishment for offences of atrocities (Section 92).
Punishment for failure to furnish information (Section 93).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The 'appropriate Government' (Central or State Government), Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, State Commissioners for Persons with Disabilities, Special Courts, and other authorities designated under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, recommendations by Commissioners, imposition of penalties, and establishment of Special Courts for speedy trials.

rights: Right to equality and non-discrimination.
Right to live independently and be included in the community.
Right to protection from cruelty, violence, and exploitation.
Right to access justice.
Right to legal capacity.
Right to education.
Right to skill development and employment.
Right to social security, health, rehabilitation, and recreation.
Right to accessibility in various forms.
Right to vote.
Reproductive rights.
duties: Duty of educational institutions to provide inclusive education.
Duty of employers to ensure non-discrimination in employment.
Duty of appropriate Governments to make infrastructure and services accessible.
Duty to conduct awareness campaigns.
Duty to develop human resources for disability.
obligations: Obligation of appropriate Governments to implement the provisions of the Act.
Obligation of employers to provide reasonable accommodation.
Obligation of service providers to ensure accessibility.
Obligation to register institutions and adhere to regulations.
Obligation to certify disabilities as per guidelines.

key_procedures: Procedure for the commencement of the Act (Section 1(2)).
Procedure for the appointment and functions of the Chief Commissioner and State Commissioners for Persons with Disabilities (Sections 74-83).
Procedure for the establishment and functions of Central and State Advisory Boards and District Level Committees (Sections 60-73).
Procedure for the registration of institutions for persons with disabilities and grant of certificates (Sections 49-55).
Procedure for the certification of specified disabilities and appeals against decisions (Sections 56-59).
Procedure for the establishment of Special Courts (Section 84).
administration: The 'appropriate Government' (Central or State Government) is responsible for the overall administration. Specific roles are also assigned to the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, State Commissioners for Persons with Disabilities, Central and State Advisory Boards, and District Level Committees.
important_notes: The Act gives effect to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
It emphasizes the principles of inherent dignity, individual autonomy, non-discrimination, and full and effective participation of persons with disabilities.
The Act defines 'benchmark disability' as having not less than forty per cent. of a specified disability.
Specific provisions are made for persons with high support needs.
A National Fund for Persons with Disabilities and State Funds for Persons with Disabilities are established.
The Act also addresses offences and penalties for non-compliance.

title: THE REPEALING AND AMENDING ACT, 2016
purpose: To repeal certain enactments and to amend certain other enactments.
scope: This Act applies to the enactments listed in the First and Second Schedules, affecting their repeal or amendment. It has nationwide applicability within India.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Repealing and Amending Act, 2016.
Repeals the enactments specified in the First Schedule to the extent mentioned in the fourth column of that schedule.
Amends the enactments specified in the Second Schedule to the extent and in the manner mentioned in the fourth column thereof.

Provides that the repeal of any enactment by this Act shall not affect: any other enactment in which the repealed enactment has been applied, incorporated, or referred to; the validity, invalidity, effect, or consequences of anything already done or suffered; any right, title, obligation, or liability already acquired, accrued, or incurred; any remedy or proceeding in respect thereof; any release or discharge of any debt, penalty, obligation, liability, claim, or demand; any indemnity already granted; or the proof of any past act or thing. It also clarifies that the repeal does not revive or restore any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, right, title, privilege, restriction, exemption, usage, practice, procedure, or other matter or thing not then existing or in force.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text for this Act itself, as it's a repealing and amending act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not applicable in the context of a repealing and amending act.

administration: Not specified for this Act, as its function is to modify other acts.
important_notes: The Act contains two schedules: The First Schedule lists enactments to be repealed, and the Second Schedule lists enactments to be amended.

The 'Savings' clause (Section 4) is a standard provision in repealing and amending acts to ensure that past actions, existing rights, and ongoing proceedings are not adversely affected by the repeal or amendment of laws.

title: THE HUMAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS AND ACQUIRED IMMUNE DEFICIENCY SYNDROME (PREVENTION AND CONTROL) ACT, 2017
purpose: To provide for the prevention and control of the spread of Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome and for the protection of human rights of persons affected by the said virus and syndrome and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to all individuals, establishments, and government bodies concerning HIV and AIDS prevention, control, and the protection of human rights of affected individuals.

key_definitions.AIDS: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, a condition caused by Human Immunodeficiency Virus that weakens the body's immune system.
key_definitions.discrimination: Any act or omission that imposes a burden or denies a benefit based on HIV-related grounds.
key_definitions.informed consent: Consent given for a proposed intervention after being fully informed of risks, benefits, and alternatives, without coercion.
key_definitions.establishment: A body corporate, co-operative society, organization, institution, or group of persons carrying out systematic activity for production, supply, or distribution of goods or services.
key_definitions.healthcare provider: Any individual whose profession is related to maintaining another individual's health, including physicians, nurses, counselors, etc.
key_definitions.HIV-affected person: An individual who is HIV-positive, whose partner is HIV-positive, or who has lost a partner due to AIDS.
key_definitions.HIV-positive person: A person whose HIV test has been confirmed positive.
key_definitions.significant-risk: Circumstances or the presence of specific body substances that pose a risk for transmitting or contracting HIV infection.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its geographical extent (whole of India), and the provision for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as AIDS, HIV, discrimination, informed consent, establishment, healthcare provider, etc.
This section prohibits discrimination against individuals based on their HIV status or association with HIV-positive individuals.

main_sections.section_title: Informed consent for undertaking HIV test or treatment
main_sections.description: This section mandates informed consent before an individual can undergo an HIV test or treatment.
This section outlines the obligation of establishments to maintain the confidentiality of data related to HIV and AIDS.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government and State Government to take measures
main_sections.description: This section requires the Central and State Governments to take necessary measures for the prevention and control of HIV and AIDS.
This section provides for the appointment of an Ombudsman to address grievances related to the Act.
This section details the penalties that can be imposed for contravening the provisions of the Act.
This section states that the provisions of this Act shall have an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict.

important_rules: Rule: Prohibition of discrimination against persons based on HIV status or association with HIV-positive individuals.
Rule: Requirement of informed consent for HIV testing or treatment.
Rule: Obligation of establishments to maintain confidentiality of HIV-related data.
Rule: Duty of the Central and State Governments to take measures for HIV prevention, control, care, support, and treatment.
Rule: Establishment of a grievance redressal mechanism through an Ombudsman.
Rule: Prohibition of victimisation of persons for actions taken in good faith under this Act.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Penalty for failure to comply with the orders of the Ombudsman.
Penalty for breach of confidentiality in legal proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities, including the Ombudsman, courts, and potentially designated government agencies, would be responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties prescribed for contraventions, failure to comply with orders, and breach of confidentiality. The Act also establishes an Ombudsman for grievance redressal and outlines special procedures in courts.

rights: Right to protection from discrimination.
Right to informed consent for HIV testing and treatment.
Right to confidentiality of HIV status.
Right to access to anti-retroviral therapy and opportunistic infection management.
Right to welfare measures and support.
Right to a safe working environment.
Right of residence.
Right to protection of property for children affected by HIV or AIDS.
Right to protection from victimisation.
duties: Duty to prevent transmission of HIV.
Duty of establishments to provide a safe working environment.
Duty of establishments to have an HIV and AIDS policy.
Duty of healthcare providers and others to maintain confidentiality.
Duty of Central and State Governments to implement welfare measures and programs.
obligations: Obligation of establishments to provide a safe working environment.
Obligation to maintain confidentiality of data.
Obligation to take measures for prevention and control of HIV and AIDS.
Obligation to provide anti-retroviral therapy and opportunistic infection management.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining informed consent for HIV testing and treatment.
Procedure for disclosure of HIV status, including to partners.
Procedure for grievance redressal through the Ombudsman, including filing complaints and orders of the Ombudsman.
Procedure for special provisions in court, such as suppression of identity and maintenance applications.
Procedure for appointment and powers of the Ombudsman.
administration: The Central Government and State Governments are responsible for the administration of this Act, including making rules and laying down guidelines. The Act also provides for the appointment of an Ombudsman.
important_notes: The adoption of medically advised safeguards to minimize the risk of infection does not amount to discrimination.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws in case of conflict.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.
The Central Government has the power to make rules and remove difficulties.

title: THE FOOTWEAR DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT INSTITUTE ACT, 2017
purpose: To establish and declare the Footwear Design and Development Institute as an institution of national importance for the promotion and development of quality and excellence in education, research and training in all disciplines relating to footwear and leather products design and development and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the Footwear Design and Development Institute and its campuses as specified in the Schedule. It covers education, research, and training in footwear and leather products design and development, including fashion and retail. It also extends to the transfer of culture to viable products and services in these sectors.

key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Institute nominated under clause (a) of sub-section (3) of section 4.
key_definitions.design: A rational, logical and sequential innovation process for the purposes of transferring culture to viable products and services in footwear and leather products, including fashion and retail thereof and for providing a competitive edge to products and services.
key_definitions.development: The systematic use of scientific and technical knowledge to meet specific objective or requirements and includes an extension of the theoretical or practical aspects of concepts, design, discovery and invention including business thereof.
key_definitions.Institute: The Footwear Design and Development Institute established under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.leather products: Includes a product made of leather or any other material or combination thereof.
key_definitions.Society: The Footwear Design and Development Institute registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860).

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Footwear Design and Development Institute as an institution of national importance.
main_sections.description: Declares the Footwear Design and Development Institute as an institution of national importance.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Chairperson', 'design', 'development', 'Institute', 'leather products', and 'Society'.

Establishes the Footwear Design and Development Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It also outlines the composition of the Governing Council, including the Chairperson, ex officio members, and nominated professionals.
States that all properties vested in the Society immediately before the commencement of the Act shall vest in the Institute upon commencement.

Details the effects of the Institute's incorporation, including the transfer of references, rights, liabilities, employment terms, and legal proceedings from the Society to the Institute. It also addresses the migration of students.

Enumerates the various functions of the Institute, including nurturing and promoting education and research, conducting courses, granting degrees, holding examinations, instituting fellowships, collaborating with other institutions, conducting skill development programs, and providing consultancy services.
