Outlines the powers of the Governing Council, which is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs. This includes making policy decisions, instituting academic posts, framing Statutes and Ordinances, and receiving gifts and grants. It also specifies that the Council cannot dispose of immovable property without the Central Government's approval.

important_rules: The Institute shall be established as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (Section 4(1), 4(2)).
The Governing Council shall be responsible for the general superintendence, direction and control of the affairs of the Institute (Section 8(1)).
The Governing Council shall meet at least two times in a year (Section 4(6)).
The Governing Council shall not dispose of any immovable property without the prior approval of the Central Government (Section 8(4)).
The Institute shall function as a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (Section 34).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Governing Council of the Institute appear to be the primary authorities for enforcement and oversight.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is likely through the powers vested in the Central Government and the Governing Council as outlined in the Act, including the ability to make rules, provide grants, and oversee the Institute's operations. Specific penalties for violations are not detailed in the provided text.

rights: Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property (Section 4(2)).
Right to sue or be sued (Section 4(2)).
Right to enter into contracts (Section 4(2)).
Rights of employees regarding pension, leave, gratuity, provident fund, and other matters, which are to be maintained unless altered by Statutes (Section 6(c)).
Right to receive gifts, grants, donations or benefactions (Section 8(2)(e)).
Right to grant degrees, diplomas, certificates, or any other qualification (Section 7(iii)).
Right to institute fellowships, scholarships and confer awards, honorary degrees or other academic distinctions or titles (Section 7(iv)).
Right to provide consultancy, testing, inspection, certification, project implementation and design support (Section 7(viii)).
duties: Duty to nurture and promote quality and excellence in education and research (Section 7(i)).
Duty to develop and conduct courses (Section 7(ii)).
Duty to co-operate, associate and collaborate with other institutions (Section 7(v)).
Duty to frame Statutes and Ordinances (Section 7(xv)).
Duty to do all such things as may be necessary, incidental or conducive to the attainment of the objects of the Institute (Section 7(xvi)).
Duty to take decisions on questions of policy relating to the administration and working of the Institute (Section 8(2)(a)).
Duty to consider and pass resolutions on the annual report, annual audited accounts and budget estimates (Section 8(2)(d)).
obligations: Obligation to ensure the Institute is open to all races, creeds and classes (Section 9).

Obligation for employees to hold office or service in the Institute by the same tenure, at the same remuneration and upon the same terms and conditions as before, unless altered by Statutes (Section 6(c)).
Obligation for employees whose altered terms are not acceptable to be compensated by the Institute (Section 6(c)).
Obligation for persons pursuing academic or research courses to be deemed to have migrated and registered with the corresponding Institute campus (Section 6(d)).
Obligation to maintain the Fund of the Institute under section 21 (Section 3(e)).
Obligation to maintain accounts and ensure audit as per section 23.
Obligation to provide returns and information to the Central Government as per section 36.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).

Nomination of Chairperson and Governing Council Members: The Chairperson is nominated by the Central Government. Other members are ex officio or nominated by the Central Government representing various sectors and institutions (Section 4(3)).
Term of Office and Allowances: The term of office for the Chairperson and non-ex officio members is three years, with entitlement to allowances determined by the Central Government (Section 4(4)).
Meeting of the Governing Council: The Governing Council shall meet at least two times in a year (Section 4(6)).
Granting of Degrees and Qualifications: The Institute has the power to hold examinations and grant degrees, diplomas, certificates, or any other qualification (Section 7(iii)).
Framing of Statutes and Ordinances: The Governing Council has the power to frame, alter, modify, or rescind Statutes and Ordinances (Section 8(2)(c)).
Appointing Committees: The Governing Council can appoint committees for the exercise of its powers and performance of duties (Section 8(3)).
Disposal of Immovable Property: The Governing Council requires prior approval of the Central Government to dispose of immovable property (Section 8(4)).
Making Rules: The Central Government has the power to make rules under the Act (Section 35).
administration: The Central Government, and the Governing Council of the Institute.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act (Section 1(2)).
The Institute is declared an institution of national importance (Section 2).
The Governing Council operates under the overall control of the Central Government (Section 8(1)).
The Governing Council cannot dispose of any immovable property without the prior approval of the Central Government (Section 8(4)).
Statutes and Ordinances must be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament (Section 38).

title: THE CENTRAL GOODS AND SERVICES TAX (EXTENSION TO JAMMU AND KASHMIR) ACT, 2017
purpose: To provide for the extension of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
scope: This act applies to the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh) and the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 along with its associated rules, notifications, and orders.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is deemed to be the 8th day of July, 2017.

main_sections.section_title: Extension and amendment of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
main_sections.description: Extends the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and its related provisions to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It also details specific amendments to the principal Act, including the omission of the exclusion of Jammu and Kashmir from certain sections and the modification of provisions related to the Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal.

Repeals the Central Goods and Services Tax (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Ordinance, 2017, and provides that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and all rules, notifications, and orders made thereunder by the Central Government are extended to and shall be in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir from sub-section (2) of section 1 of the principal Act is omitted.
The exclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir from clause (ii) of the Explanation in section 22 of the principal Act is inserted after the word 'Constitution'.
In section 109, sub-section (6) of the principal Act, the words 'except for the State of Jammu and Kashmir' are inserted after 'each State or Union territory'.

For the State of Jammu and Kashmir, the State Bench of the Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal constituted under the principal Act shall be the State Appellate Tribunal constituted under the Jammu and Kashmir Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and relevant authorities under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and mechanisms established by the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, as extended to Jammu and Kashmir.

administration: Central Government, and relevant tax authorities under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
important_notes: The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.
The commencement of this Act is deemed to have taken effect on the 8th day of July, 2017.

title: THE MUSLIM WOMEN (PROTECTION OF RIGHTS ON MARRIAGE) ACT, 2019
purpose: To protect the rights of married Muslim women and to prohibit divorce by pronouncing talaq by their husbands and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh as per notification). It applies to Muslim husbands who pronounce talaq and married Muslim women upon whom talaq is pronounced.

key_definitions.electronic_form: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (r) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (21 of 2000).
key_definitions.Magistrate: A Judicial Magistrate of the first class exercising jurisdiction under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), in the area where the married Muslim woman resides.
key_definitions.talaq: Talaq-e-biddat or any other similar form of talaq having the effect of instantaneous and irrevocable divorce pronounced by a Muslim husband.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir, now Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on 19th September, 2018).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'electronic form', 'Magistrate', and 'talaq'.

main_sections.section_title: Talaq to be void and illegal.
main_sections.description: Declares any pronouncement of talaq by a Muslim husband upon his wife, by words (spoken or written), in electronic form, or in any other manner, as void and illegal.
Prescribes punishment for a Muslim husband who pronounces talaq as referred to in section 3, with imprisonment up to three years and liability to fine.
Entitles a married Muslim woman upon whom talaq is pronounced to receive subsistence allowance from her husband for herself and dependent children, as determined by the Magistrate.
Entitles a married Muslim woman to the custody of her minor children in the event of a talaq pronounced by her husband, in a manner determined by the Magistrate.

main_sections.section_title: Offence to be cognizable, compoundable, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies that offences under this Act are cognizable, compoundable at the instance of the woman with Magistrate's permission, and details bail conditions, notwithstanding the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Repeals the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Second Ordinance, 2019, and provides for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance to be deemed taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any pronouncement of talaq by a Muslim husband upon his wife, in any form (spoken, written, electronic, or otherwise), is void and illegal.
Rule 2: A Muslim husband who pronounces talaq is liable to imprisonment for up to three years and a fine.
Rule 3: A Muslim woman upon whom talaq is pronounced is entitled to subsistence allowance for herself and her dependent children, as determined by the Magistrate.
Rule 4: A Muslim woman upon whom talaq is pronounced is entitled to the custody of her minor children, as determined by the Magistrate.
Rule 5: Offences under this Act are cognizable, and can be compounded with the permission of the Magistrate.
Rule 6: Bail for an accused under this Act requires the Magistrate to be satisfied of reasonable grounds after hearing the affected woman.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years.
Liability to fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate (Judicial Magistrate of the first class exercising jurisdiction in the area where the married Muslim woman resides).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Offences are cognizable. Information can be given to the officer in charge of a police station. Offences are compoundable with the permission of the Magistrate. Bail requires Magistrate's satisfaction after hearing the affected woman.

rights: Right to subsistence allowance for herself and dependent children upon pronouncement of talaq.
Right to custody of minor children upon pronouncement of talaq.
Right to initiate proceedings for cognizable offences under the Act.
Right to consent to compounding of an offence.
Right to be heard by the Magistrate before bail is granted to the accused.
duties: Husbands have a duty not to pronounce talaq in a manner that is void and illegal.
Husbands have a duty to provide subsistence allowance to their wives and dependent children upon pronouncement of talaq.
Husbands have a duty to allow custody of minor children to their wives upon pronouncement of talaq.
Accused individuals have a duty to face trial for offences under the Act.
obligations: Muslim husbands are obligated to refrain from pronouncing talaq in the manner prohibited by the Act.
Muslim husbands are obligated to provide subsistence allowance and ensure child custody as determined by the Magistrate.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining subsistence allowance and child custody: The Magistrate, upon the pronouncement of talaq, will determine the amount of subsistence allowance for the wife and dependent children, and the custody arrangements for minor children.
Procedure for filing a complaint: Information relating to the commission of an offence can be given to the officer in charge of a police station by the married Muslim woman or her relative.
Procedure for compounding an offence: The married Muslim woman can request the Magistrate to compound an offence, and the Magistrate may permit it on specified terms and conditions.

Procedure for granting bail: An accused person cannot be released on bail unless the Magistrate, after application and hearing the affected woman, is satisfied of reasonable grounds for granting bail.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely the Ministry of Law and Justice or Ministry of Minority Affairs, with enforcement through the judiciary (Magistrates) and police.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on 19th September, 2018.
The Act is applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
The provisions of this Act are without prejudice to the generality of any other law for the time being in force.

title: THE TRANSGENDER PERSONS (PROTECTION OF RIGHTS) ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide for the protection of rights of transgender persons and their welfare, and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Covers protection of rights, prohibition against discrimination, recognition of identity, welfare measures, obligations of establishments, education, social security, health of transgender persons, and the National Council for Transgender Persons.

key_definitions.appropriate_government: In relation to the Central Government or any establishment wholly or substantially financed by it, the Central Government; in relation to a State Government or any establishment wholly or substantially financed by it, or any local authority, the State Government.
key_definitions.establishment: Includes bodies or authorities established by or under a Central or State Act, government-aided bodies, Government companies, Departments of Government, companies, bodies corporate, associations, firms, cooperative societies, trusts, agencies, and institutions.
key_definitions.inclusive_education: A system of education where transgender students learn with other students without fear of discrimination, neglect, harassment, or intimidation, with teaching and learning adapted to their needs.
key_definitions.transgender_person: A person whose gender does not match the gender assigned at birth, including trans-man, trans-woman (with or without SRS or hormone therapy), persons with intersex variations, genderqueer, and socio-cultural identities like kinner, hijra, aravani, and jogta.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appropriate Government', 'establishment', 'family', 'inclusive education', 'institution', 'local authority', 'National Council', 'notification', 'person with intersex variations', 'prescribed', and 'transgender person'.

Prohibits any person or establishment from discriminating against a transgender person on various grounds, including denial of education, unfair treatment in employment, denial of healthcare, denial of access to public goods/services, and denial of the right to reside or occupy property.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of identity of transgender person
main_sections.description: States that a transgender person has the right to be recognized as such and a right to self-perceived gender identity.
Allows a transgender person to apply to the District Magistrate for a certificate of identity as a transgender person. For minors, the application is made by a parent or guardian.

Details the process by which the District Magistrate issues a certificate of identity as a transgender person, which is to be recorded in all official documents and confers rights and proof of recognition.
Outlines the procedure for a transgender person to apply for a revised certificate after undergoing gender-affirming surgery, enabling changes in birth certificates and other official documents.

Mandates the appropriate Government to take steps for the full and effective participation and inclusion of transgender persons, formulate welfare schemes, provide rescue and rehabilitation, and promote participation in cultural and recreational activities.
Prohibits establishments from discriminating against transgender persons in any matter related to employment, including recruitment and promotion.
Requires every establishment to comply with the Act's provisions and provide prescribed facilities to transgender persons.
Stipulates that every establishment must designate a complaint officer to handle complaints regarding violations of the Act.

Ensures that children cannot be separated from their families due to being transgender except by court order, and grants transgender persons the right to reside in their parental household, not be excluded, and use facilities without discrimination. It also outlines provisions for placement in rehabilitation centers if parents are unable to care for them.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of educational institutions to provide inclusive education
main_sections.description: Requires educational institutions funded or recognized by the appropriate Government to provide inclusive education and opportunities for sports and recreation to transgender persons on an equal basis.
Directs the appropriate Government to formulate schemes for vocational training and self-employment to support the livelihood of transgender persons.

Mandates the appropriate Government to set up HIV surveillance centers, provide medical care including sex reassignment surgery and hormonal therapy, offer pre and post-surgery counseling, develop health manuals, review medical curricula, facilitate access to healthcare institutions, and provide comprehensive insurance coverage for medical expenses.

Details the constitution and composition of the National Council for Transgender Persons, which is to be established by the Central Government to exercise powers and perform functions assigned to it under the Act. The Council includes ex-officio members from various ministries and departments, representatives from State Governments and Union territories, and nominated transgender community representatives and experts.

important_rules: No person or establishment shall discriminate against a transgender person in education, employment, healthcare, access to public facilities, right of movement, right to reside or occupy property, or in government/private establishments.
A transgender person has the right to be recognized as such based on self-perceived gender identity.
District Magistrates are responsible for issuing certificates of identity to transgender persons and revised certificates after gender affirmation surgery.
Appropriate Governments must take steps for the welfare, inclusion, and rehabilitation of transgender persons, and formulate transgender-sensitive schemes.
Establishments must not discriminate in employment, comply with the Act, and provide a grievance redressal mechanism.
Transgender persons have a right to reside in their parental household and use its facilities without discrimination.
Educational institutions must provide inclusive education and equal opportunities.
Appropriate Governments must facilitate vocational training, self-employment, and comprehensive healthcare, including sex reassignment surgery and hormonal therapy, with insurance coverage.
A National Council for Transgender Persons is to be constituted to exercise powers and perform functions under the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Magistrate (for identity certificates), Appropriate Government (for welfare measures and ensuring compliance), Establishments (for non-discrimination and grievance redressal), National Council for Transgender Persons (for performing its functions).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of identity certificates, formulation of welfare schemes, establishment of grievance redressal mechanisms, and the establishment and functioning of the National Council for Transgender Persons. Penalties for offences are detailed in Chapter VIII (not fully provided).

rights: Right to be recognized as a transgender person.
Right to self-perceived gender identity.
Right to obtain a certificate of identity.
Right to change gender in official documents after surgery.
Right to inclusive education and participation in sports/recreation.
Right to livelihood through vocational training and self-employment.
Right to healthcare facilities, including sex reassignment surgery and hormonal therapy, with counseling and insurance coverage.
Right to reside in the household where parents or immediate family members reside.
Right not to be excluded from the household.
Right to enjoy and use household facilities in a non-discriminatory manner.
duties: Duty of every person and establishment not to discriminate against transgender persons.
Duty of the appropriate Government to take steps for welfare, inclusion, and rehabilitation of transgender persons.
Duty of educational institutions to provide inclusive education.
Duty of establishments to ensure compliance with the Act and provide facilities.
Duty of establishments to designate a complaint officer for grievance redressal.
obligations: Obligation of the appropriate Government to formulate transgender-sensitive welfare schemes.
Obligation of educational institutions to provide inclusive education and opportunities.
Obligation of establishments to comply with the Act and provide facilities.
Obligation of establishments to implement grievance redressal mechanisms.
Obligation of parents or immediate family members to not separate a child on the ground of being transgender, except by court order.

key_procedures: Application for a certificate of identity as a transgender person to the District Magistrate.
Application for a revised certificate of identity after gender-affirming surgery to the District Magistrate.
Establishment of a grievance redressal mechanism within each establishment.
Constitution and functioning of the National Council for Transgender Persons.
administration: Central Government (through Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for the National Council), State Governments, District Magistrates, and various ministries/departments as represented in the National Council.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of India.
The Act came into force on 10th January, 2020.
The definitions of 'establishment' and 'transgender person' are broad and inclusive.

Section 17 (Functions of Council), Section 18 (Offences and Penalties), Section 19 (Grants by Central Government), Section 20 (Act not in derogation of any other law), Section 21 (Protection of action taken in good faith), Section 22 (Power of appropriate Government to make rules), and Section 23 (Power to remove difficulties) are listed in the arrangement but their specific content is not detailed in the provided text.

title: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Merger of Union Territories) Act, 2019
purpose: To provide for the merger of the Union territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the Union territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. It concerns the formation of a new Union territory, amendments to the Constitution, representation in Parliament, High Court jurisdiction, assets and liabilities, and provisions for services.

key_definitions.appointed day: The day on which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint for the Act to come into force.
key_definitions.existing Union territories: The Union territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu as they existed immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.law: Includes any enactment, Ordinance, regulation, order, bye-law, rule, scheme, notification or other instrument having the force of law in the whole or any part of the existing Union territories immediately before the appointed day.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'existing Union territories', and 'law'.

main_sections.section_title: Formation of Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
main_sections.description: Declares the formation of a new Union territory named 'Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu' comprising the territories of the existing Union territories.
Amends article 240 of the Constitution to include the new Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of First Schedule to Constitution
main_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the name and extent of the new Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Allocation of seats in House of People
main_sections.description: Allocates two seats to the new Union territory in the House of the People and amends the Representation of the People Act, 1950 accordingly.
Deals with provisions for sitting members of the House of the People representing constituencies affected by the merger, ensuring their term of office remains unaltered.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of jurisdiction of High Court of Bombay
main_sections.description: Ensures that the jurisdiction of the High Court of Bombay continues to extend to the new Union territory.
States that all land and goods held by the existing Union territories shall vest in the new Union territory.
Merges the cash balances of the existing Union territories into the new Union territory.
Vests the right to recover arrears of tax or duty, including land revenue, in the new Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Right to recover loans and advances
main_sections.description: Transfers the right to recover loans and advances made by the existing Union territories to the new Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Assets and liabilities of Union territory undertakings
main_sections.description: States that assets and liabilities of commercial undertakings of the existing Union territories shall vest in the new Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Refund of taxes collected in excess
main_sections.description: Specifies that the liability to refund excess taxes collected rests with the new Union territory.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions relating to All India Services
main_sections.description: Deals with the cadre of members of All India Services borne on the existing Union territories cadre.

Covers provisions for persons employed in connection with the affairs of the existing Union territories, their provisional and final allotment to the new Union territory, and the establishment of Advisory Committees.
Ensures that all laws in force in the existing Union territories continue to be in force in their respective areas after the merger.
Grants courts, tribunals, or authorities the power to construe laws to facilitate their application in the new Union territory.
Empowers the Central Government to make adaptations and modifications to laws to facilitate their application in the new Union territory.
Provides for the substitution of the new Union territory in legal proceedings where the existing Union territories were a party.
Deals with the transfer of pending proceedings before courts, tribunals, authorities, or officers in the existing Union territories to their corresponding counterparts in the new Union territory.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).

Rule 2: Upon merger, the existing Union territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu cease to form part of the existing Union territories and instead form a new Union territory known as the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Section 3).
Rule 3: All land and goods held by the existing Union territories vest in the new Union territory (Section 9).
Rule 4: Cash balances of the existing Union territories are merged into the new Union territory (Section 10).

Rule 5: All persons employed in connection with the affairs of the existing Union territories shall continue to serve in the new Union territory and be deemed provisionally allotted, with final allotment to be determined by the Central Government (Section 16(1) & (2)).
Rule 6: Laws in force in the existing Union territories continue to be in force in their respective areas after the merger (Section 17).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Administrator of the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu are implicitly responsible for enforcement through various provisions like issuing notifications, orders, and adaptations of laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through notifications, orders, adaptations of laws, and the continuation and transfer of legal and administrative proceedings.

rights: Right to recover arrears of tax or duty (Section 11).
Right to recover loans and advances made by the existing Union territories (Section 12).
Right to receive refunds of taxes collected in excess (Section 14).
obligations: Obligation to continue serving in the new Union territory for persons employed in existing Union territories (Section 16(1)(a)).
Obligation to follow conditions of service as determined by the Central Government (Section 16(5)).

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Central Government appoints an 'appointed day' by notification in the Official Gazette for the Act to come into force (Section 1(2)).
Procedure 2: The Central Government may, by order, make adaptations and modifications to laws to facilitate their application in the new Union territory (Section 19).

Procedure 3: Pending proceedings before any court, tribunal, authority, or officer in the existing Union territories are transferred to the corresponding entity in the new Union territory (Section 21).
administration: The Central Government plays a significant role in the administration of this Act, including appointing the commencement date, making adaptations to laws, and determining the final allotment of service personnel. The Administrator of the Union territory is also mentioned in relation to determining corresponding courts/tribunals.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act effectively merges two existing Union territories into one, streamlining administration and governance.
Note 2: The Act ensures continuity of laws and services, with provisions for adaptation and integration to facilitate the smooth transition.
Note 3: Specific provisions are made for the representation of the new Union territory in the House of the People and the extension of the jurisdiction of the High Court of Bombay.

Note 4: The conditions of service for persons employed in the existing Union territories shall not be varied to their disadvantage except with the previous approval of the Central Government (Section 16(5) proviso).

title: The Repealing and Amending Act, 2019
purpose: To repeal certain enactments and to amend certain other enactments.
scope: This act applies to the enactments listed in the First and Second Schedules, which are central enactments of India. It repeals and amends various specific laws.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Repealing and Amending Act, 2019.
Specifies that the enactments listed in the First Schedule are hereby repealed.
States that the enactments specified in the Second Schedule are hereby amended to the extent and in the manner specified in the fourth column thereof.

Provides that the repeal of any enactment by this Act will not affect other enactments that incorporated or referred to the repealed enactment. It also clarifies that the Act does not affect anything already done or suffered, acquired rights, liabilities, remedies, or the validity of past acts. Furthermore, it preserves existing legal principles, jurisdictions, practices, and customs that may have been derived from the repealed enactments, and it does not revive any non-existent jurisdiction or matter.

important_rules: Rule 1: Enactments listed in the First Schedule are repealed (Section 2).
Rule 2: Enactments listed in the Second Schedule are amended as specified (Section 3).
Rule 3: The repeal of an enactment does not affect other enactments, past actions, liabilities, or existing legal principles and practices (Section 4).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, as the act is primarily about repealing and amending other acts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not applicable, as the act itself does not impose direct penalties or require enforcement in the typical sense; it modifies other legislation.

rights: Protection of rights, titles, obligations, and liabilities already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal of an enactment (Section 4).
duties: Protection of obligations and liabilities already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal of an enactment (Section 4).
obligations: Protection of obligations already acquired, accrued, or incurred before the repeal of an enactment (Section 4).

administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely falls under the purview of the Ministry of Law and Justice or the legislative department responsible for enacting laws.
important_notes: The act lists numerous specific enactments to be repealed, including acts related to public accountants, municipal taxation, government estates, terminal tax, legislative assembly validation, cotton transport, Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, dramatic performances, public employment, rent control, acquisition of undertakings, labour welfare cess and funds, tea, universities, road transport corporations, agricultural service co-operative societies, bank notes, motor vehicles, registration, institutes of technology, Dalmia Dadri Cement, central road fund, prevention of money-laundering, central industrial security force, civil defence, repatriation of prisoners, customs, national institutes of technology, governors' emoluments, telecom regulatory authority, merchant shipping, national capital territory of Delhi laws, public premises, insurance laws, mines and minerals, regional rural banks, warehousing corporations, election laws, high court and supreme court judges' salaries, central agricultural university, and taxation laws.
The act also specifies amendments to the Income-tax Act, 1961, and the Indian Institutes of Management Act, 2017.

title: THE CENTRAL SANSKRIT UNIVERSITIES ACT, 2020
purpose: To establish and incorporate Universities for teaching and research in Sanskrit, to develop all-inclusive Sanskrit promotional activities and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of three Central Sanskrit Universities: the Central Sanskrit University (formerly Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan, New Delhi), Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (formerly Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeeth, New Delhi), and the National Sanskrit University (formerly Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeeth, Tirupati). It covers teaching, research, and promotion of Sanskrit language and related traditional subjects, with provisions for integrated courses, innovations in teaching, and manpower development.

key_definitions.University: A University established and incorporated as a University under this Act.
key_definitions.Sanskrit: The Sanskrit language, in modern, classical or ancient form, and the knowledge available therein or related thereto, in addition to Sanskrit language.
key_definitions.Campus: Any unit established or constituted by the University at any place within or outside India for making arrangements for instruction, research, education and training in Sanskrit and includes an existing Campus established by the University prior to the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.distance education system: The system of imparting education through any means of communication, such as broadcasting, telecasting, internet, correspondence course, seminar, contact programme, non-formal pattern or a combination of any two or more such means, except the regular system of education.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, academic staff, Board of Studies, Campus, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, College, corresponding University, deemed to be University, Court, Department, Director, distance education system, employee, Executive Council, Faculty, Hall, Institution, Principal, Regulations, Sanskrit, Schedule, School, School of Studies, Society, Statutes, Ordinances, and teachers of the University.

Establishes three specific 'deemed to be Universities' as three separate Central Universities, outlining their names and headquarters, and constituting them as bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Details the consequences of the Act's commencement, including the dissolution of the previous societies, the transfer of properties, rights, and liabilities to the new Universities, the continuation of employment for existing staff under specified terms, and the deemed appointment of existing Vice-Chancellors.

Outlines the primary objectives of the Universities, focusing on disseminating and advancing knowledge in Sanskrit, providing integrated courses, promoting innovations in teaching-learning, and developing manpower for Sanskrit promotion and research.

Enumerates the powers of the Universities, including providing instruction in Sanskrit and related subjects, granting diplomas and degrees, organizing extramural studies, conferring honorary degrees, facilitating distance education, providing higher education in allied fields like Indian Philosophy and Ayurveda, and instituting academic positions.

important_rules: Rule: The Universities shall be established as bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (Section 3(2) & 3(3)).

Rule: On commencement of the Act, the formerly 'deemed to be Universities' shall stand dissolved, and their properties, rights, and liabilities shall be transferred to the corresponding new Universities (Section 4(a), 4(c), 4(d)).

Rule: Existing employees of the dissolved societies shall continue their employment in the new Universities with same tenure, remuneration, terms, and conditions unless altered, with provisions for termination and compensation (Section 4(e)).
Rule: The Universities' objects include disseminating and advancing knowledge, promoting Sanskrit, and providing integrated courses (Section 5).
Rule: Universities have powers to provide instruction, grant degrees, organize extension services, and offer education through distance learning (Section 6).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (through notifications for commencement and by extension, the Universities themselves for their internal governance)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations made thereunder. Enforcement of University rules would be through its internal administrative and academic bodies.

rights: Employees have rights to continue employment with same tenure, remuneration, and terms unless altered, with rights to compensation if termination occurs due to altered terms (Section 4(e)).
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases against students (Section 36).
duties: Universities have a duty to disseminate and advance knowledge in Sanskrit and related fields (Section 5).
Universities have a duty to make special provisions for integrated courses and promote innovations (Section 5).
Universities have a duty to educate and train manpower for the development, promotion, preservation, and research in Sanskrit (Section 5).
Universities must ensure to be open to all castes, creeds, races, or classes (Section 7 - implied as an objective or principle).
obligations: The Central Government has the obligation to appoint a commencement date via notification (Section 1(2)).
The Universities have an obligation to act as bodies corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal (Section 3(2) & 3(3)).
The Universities must ensure that their properties, rights, and liabilities are managed according to the Act (Section 4).

key_procedures: Establishment of Universities: The Act dissolves existing 'deemed to be Universities' and establishes them as new Central Universities (Section 3 & 4).

Appointment of Employees: Employees of dissolved societies continue their service in the new Universities under existing terms unless altered, with provisions for termination and compensation (Section 4(e)).

Granting Degrees and Diplomas: Universities can grant diplomas, certificates, degrees, and other academic distinctions based on examination, evaluation, or other testing methods, and can withdraw them for cause (Section 6(ii)).
Making Statutes and Ordinances: The Act outlines the power to make Statutes (Section 27) and Ordinances (Section 29), and how they are to be made (Section 28).
Publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations: These are to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament (Section 44).
administration: The Central Government is responsible for appointing the commencement date. The Universities themselves are administered through their respective authorities, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Executive Council, and Academic Council, as defined by the Act and governed by Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
important_notes: The Act converts three 'deemed to be Universities' into Central Universities, integrating their assets, liabilities, and staff (Section 4).
The Universities are mandated to be open to all castes, creeds, races, or classes (Section 7).
The Act provides for the establishment of various officers and authorities within the Universities to manage their affairs (Sections 9-26).

title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
purpose: To provide for the processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognizes both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process such personal data for lawful purposes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the processing of digital personal data within the territory of India, where the personal data is collected in digital form or in non-digital form and digitized subsequently. It also applies to the processing of digital personal data outside India if such processing is related to offering goods or services to Data Principals within India. It does not apply to personal data processed by an individual for personal or domestic purposes, or personal data made publicly available by the Data Principal or by any other person under an obligation to make it public.

key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: The Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal established under section 14 of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997.
key_definitions.automated: Any digital process capable of operating automatically in response to instructions given or otherwise for the purpose of processing data.
key_definitions.Board: The Data Protection Board of India established by the Central Government.
key_definitions.child: An individual who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.Consent Manager: A person registered with the Board, who acts as a single point of contact to enable a Data Principal to give, manage, review and withdraw her consent.
key_definitions.data: A representation of information, facts, concepts, opinions or instructions in a manner suitable for communication, interpretation or processing by human beings or by automated means.
key_definitions.Data Fiduciary: Any person who alone or in conjunction with other persons determines the purpose and means of processing of personal data.
key_definitions.Data Principal: The individual to whom the personal data relates, including parents/lawful guardians for children and persons with disability.
key_definitions.Data Processor: Any person who processes personal data on behalf of a Data Fiduciary.
key_definitions.gain: A gain in property or supply of services, or an opportunity to earn remuneration or financial advantage.
key_definitions.loss: A loss in property or interruption in supply of services, or a loss of opportunity to earn remuneration or financial advantage.
key_definitions.personal data: Any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data.
key_definitions.personal data breach: Unauthorized processing or accidental disclosure, acquisition, sharing, use, alteration, destruction or loss of access to personal data, compromising confidentiality, integrity or availability.
key_definitions.processing: A wholly or partly automated operation or set of operations performed on digital personal data, including collection, recording, organization, structuring, storage, adaptation, retrieval, use, alignment or combination, indexing, sharing, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, restriction, erasure or destruction.
key_definitions.Significant Data Fiduciary: Any Data Fiduciary or class of Data Fiduciaries notified by the Central Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and provides for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Appellate Tribunal', 'Board', 'child', 'Data Fiduciary', 'Data Principal', 'personal data', 'processing', etc.
Specifies the territorial and subject-matter scope of the Act, including its applicability to processing within and outside India, and exclusions.
Outlines the conditions under which personal data can be processed, primarily based on the consent of the Data Principal or for certain legitimate uses.
Mandates that Data Fiduciaries must provide a notice to Data Principals before requesting consent, informing them about the personal data, purpose of processing, and their rights.
Defines the requirements for valid consent, which must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action.
Details specific situations where personal data can be processed without consent.
Lays down the general responsibilities of Data Fiduciaries in processing personal data.

main_sections.description: Addresses specific provisions for processing the personal data of children.

main_sections.section_title: Additional obligations of Significant Data Fiduciary
main_sections.description: Imposes further obligations on Data Fiduciaries classified as 'Significant Data Fiduciaries'.

main_sections.section_title: Right to access information about personal data
main_sections.description: Grants Data Principals the right to access information about their personal data being processed.

main_sections.section_title: Right to correction and erasure of personal data
main_sections.description: Enables Data Principals to request correction and erasure of their personal data.
Provides Data Principals with the right to seek redressal for grievances related to their personal data.
Grants Data Principals the right to nominate a person to exercise their rights in the event of their death or incapacity.
Outlines the responsibilities and duties of Data Principals.

main_sections.section_title: Processing of personal data outside India
main_sections.description: Details the conditions and implications of processing personal data outside India.
Specifies circumstances and types of personal data that are exempt from the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the establishment of the Data Protection Board of India.

main_sections.description: Defines the composition and qualifications required for the Chairperson and members of the Board.

main_sections.description: Specifies the salary, allowances, and term of office for the Chairperson and members of the Board.

main_sections.description: Lists the grounds for disqualification for appointment and continuation as Chairperson and Members of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation by Members and filling of vacancy
main_sections.description: Covers the process of resignation by members and filling of any vacancies in the Board.
Outlines the procedures and conduct of proceedings by the Board.
Deals with the appointment and functioning of officers and employees of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Members and officers to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members and officers of the Board as public servants.
Details the specific powers vested in the Chairperson of the Board.
Enumerate the powers and functions of the Data Protection Board of India.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed by Board
main_sections.description: Describes the procedure that the Board must follow in its functioning and adjudication.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders of the Board to the Appellate Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Orders passed by Appellate Tribunal to be executable as decree
main_sections.description: Specifies that orders passed by the Appellate Tribunal are executable as a decree.
Introduces provisions for alternate dispute resolution mechanisms.
Allows for voluntary undertakings by parties in certain proceedings.
Specifies the penalties that may be imposed for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Crediting sums realised by way of penalties to Consolidated Fund of India
main_sections.description: Deals with the crediting of penalties collected to the Consolidated Fund of India.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Grants the power to call for information for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions for the implementation of the Act.
Ensures consistency of the Act with other existing laws.
Specifies limitations on the jurisdiction of civil courts in certain matters under the Act.
Confers the power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of rules and certain notification
main_sections.description: Provides for the laying of rules and certain notifications before Parliament.
Grants the power to amend the Schedule to the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Contains provisions for amendments to certain other Acts.

important_rules: Personal data can only be processed for a lawful purpose, either with the consent of the Data Principal or for certain legitimate uses.
Data Fiduciaries must provide a clear notice to Data Principals before requesting consent, detailing the data to be processed, the purpose, and the Principal's rights.
Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous, demonstrated by a clear affirmative action, and limited to the data necessary for the specified purpose.
Data Principals have the right to access, correct, and erase their personal data, and the right to grievance redressal.
Processing of personal data of children requires verifiable consent from parents or lawful guardians, with specific protections in place.
Significant Data Fiduciaries have additional obligations, including appointing a Data Protection Officer.
Personal data breaches must be reported to the Board and affected Data Principals under prescribed conditions.
Processing of personal data outside India is permitted under specific conditions, including if it relates to offering goods or services within India.
Certain personal data is exempt from the Act, including data processed for personal/domestic purposes or data made publicly available.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of provisions, with varying amounts depending on the nature and severity of the breach (detailed in Section 33 and the Schedule).
Specific penalties may apply for failure to take reasonable security safeguards, breach of duties by Data Fiduciary, breach of obligations by Data Processor, etc.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Data Protection Board of India and the Appellate Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigations, inquiries, adjudication proceedings by the Board, and appeals to the Appellate Tribunal. The Central Government can also issue directions.

rights: Right to access information about personal data.
Right to correction and erasure of personal data.
Right to grievance redressal.
Right to nominate.
Right to be informed of personal data breaches.
duties: Duties of the Data Principal include providing accurate information and not suppressing material information.
Duties of the Data Fiduciary include obtaining consent, providing notice, ensuring data accuracy, implementing reasonable security safeguards, reporting breaches, etc.
obligations: Obligations of Data Fiduciaries (general and significant).
Obligations of Data Processors.
Obligations related to processing of children's data.
Obligations to maintain records and provide information to the Board.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining consent from Data Principals, including providing notice and ensuring consent is free, specific, informed, and unambiguous.
Procedure for Data Principals to exercise their rights of access, correction, erasure, and grievance redressal.
Procedure for Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors to manage personal data and implement security safeguards.
Procedure for reporting and handling of personal data breaches.
Procedure for investigations, inquiries, and adjudication by the Data Protection Board of India.
Procedure for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal.
Procedure for alternate dispute resolution and voluntary undertakings.
administration: The Data Protection Board of India and the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act allows for different commencement dates for different provisions.
The definition of 'person' is broad and includes individuals, companies, firms, associations, the State, and artificial juristic persons.
The Act aims to balance the right to privacy with the need for data processing for lawful purposes.
The Act provides for the establishment of a dedicated Data Protection Board of India.

title: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation Act, 2023
purpose: To establish the Anusandhan National Research Foundation to provide high-level strategic direction for research, innovation, and entrepreneurship in natural sciences (including mathematical sciences), engineering and technology, environmental and earth sciences, health and agriculture, and the scientific and technological interfaces of humanities and social sciences, and to promote, monitor, and support such research.
scope: The Act applies to research, innovation, and entrepreneurship within India, specifically focusing on the specified scientific and technological fields. It aims to coordinate efforts across government, industry, and academic institutions.

key_definitions.appointed_date: The date appointed by the Central Government for the commencement of the Act.
key_definitions.Chief_Executive_Officer: The Chief Executive Officer of the Foundation.
key_definitions.Executive_Council: The council constituted under section 7 of the Act.
key_definitions.Foundation: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation established under section 3.
key_definitions.Governing_Board: The Governing Board of the Foundation constituted under section 5.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and outlines that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification, allowing for different dates for different provisions.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed date', 'Chief Executive Officer', 'Executive Council', 'Foundation', 'Funds', 'Governing Board', 'Member', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'regulations'.
Establishes the Anusandhan National Research Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowering it to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract.

Outlines the primary objective of the Foundation to provide strategic direction for research, innovation, and entrepreneurship. It further details specific initiatives such as preparing roadmaps, seeding research, funding grants, assisting in infrastructure development, increasing India's global participation, supporting translation of research, evolving coordinated programs for societal challenges, coordinating expenditure analysis, fostering international collaboration, encouraging investment from public and private sectors, and conducting annual surveys of research outcomes (excluding strategic areas).

Establishes the Governing Board to provide strategic direction and monitor the Foundation's objectives. It details the ex officio members (Prime Minister as President, Union Ministers of Science and Technology and Education as Vice-Presidents, NITI Aayog member, Secretaries from various science and technology related departments, and Principal Scientific Advisor as Member-Secretary) and other nominated members from science and innovation councils, industry, humanities, research institutions, and experts.
Specifies that the Governing Board will meet at times and places determined by regulations and that in the President's absence, a Vice-President will preside.

Details the constitution of the Executive Council, responsible for implementing the Act's provisions. It lists ex officio members (Principal Scientific Advisor as Chairperson, Secretaries from various science and technology departments, and the Chief Executive Officer as Member-Secretary) and nominated expert members.

Outlines that the Executive Council will meet as per regulations and that in the Chairperson's absence, another member will preside. The Chairperson also exercises powers delegated by the Governing Board.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of Governing Board or Executive Council
main_sections.description: States that vacancies or defects in the constitution or appointment of members of the Governing Board or Executive Council, or procedural irregularities not affecting the merits of a case, will not invalidate their proceedings.

Defines the functions of the Executive Council, which include implementing the Foundation's objectives based on the Governing Board's guidance. This includes considering grant applications, determining regulations for financial assistance (registration, reporting, extension, revocation), and facilitating intellectual property rights filings.

important_rules: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation Act, 2023, officially commenced on February 5, 2024.
The Governing Board, headed by the Prime Minister, provides strategic direction.
The Executive Council, chaired by the Principal Scientific Advisor, is responsible for implementing the Foundation's objectives and managing financial assistance.
The Foundation aims to foster research and innovation across a broad spectrum of scientific and technological fields.
The Act mandates the creation of a body corporate, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, with powers to manage property and contracts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement through the Governing Board and the Executive Council, supported by the Central Government and its relevant departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the implementation of the Act's objectives, the establishment and functioning of the Governing Board and Executive Council, and the making and adherence to rules and regulations.

rights: The right to receive financial assistance for research, subject to eligibility criteria and regulations.
The right to benefit from the infrastructure and environment conducive to scientific pursuit facilitated by the Foundation.
duties: The Foundation has a duty to prepare research roadmaps and facilitate research capacity building.
The Governing Board has a duty to provide high-level strategic direction.
The Executive Council has a duty to implement the Foundation's objectives and manage financial assistance.
Entities receiving financial assistance have duties related to reporting and compliance as per regulations.
obligations: The Central Government has the obligation to appoint commencement dates and publish notifications.
The Foundation is obligated to promote, monitor, and support research, innovation, and entrepreneurship.
The Foundation is obligated to coordinate efforts across various stakeholders.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation via Central Government notification.
Constitution of the Governing Board with specified ex officio and nominated members.
Constitution of the Executive Council with specified ex officio and nominated members.
The Executive Council considering applications for financial assistance and determining regulations for the same.
The Governing Board and Executive Council conducting meetings according to their respective rules of procedure.
administration: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation, administered through its Governing Board and Executive Council, with overall oversight from the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act was notified to come into force on the 5th day of February, 2024.
The survey of research outcomes conducted by the Foundation will exclude strategic research areas determined by the Governing Board.

Acts or proceedings of the Governing Board or Executive Council are not invalidated by vacancies, defects in constitution or appointment, or procedural irregularities that do not affect the merits of the case.

title: The National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Act, 2023
purpose: To provide for the regulation and maintenance of standards of education and services by nursing and midwifery professionals, assessment of institutions, maintenance of a National Register and State Registers, and creation of a system to improve access, research and development, and adoption of latest scientific advancements, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to nursing and midwifery education, services, professionals, institutions, and related matters across India. It establishes regulatory bodies at the national and state levels.

key_definitions.autonomous_board: Any of the Autonomous Boards constituted under section 11.
key_definitions.chairperson: The Chairperson of the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission appointed under section 4.
key_definitions.fund: The National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Fund referred to in section 38.
key_definitions.midwifery: Skilled, knowledgeable, and compassionate care for childbearing women, new-born infants, and families across the continuum from pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, birth, postpartum, and the early weeks of life. It includes preventive measures, promotion of normal birth, detection of complications, accessing medical care, appropriate referrals, and emergency measures as per the scope of practice.
key_definitions.midwifery_associate: A member of the health team who has acquired a recognized qualification and is licensed to practice as a midwifery associate by the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission. They assist doctors or nurse practitioners in midwifery and provide care during pregnancy, labor, and postpartum, instructing parents in baby care.
key_definitions.midwifery_professional: A person who has obtained a recognized basic or advanced qualification and is granted a license to practice by the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission.
key_definitions.national_commission: The National Nursing and Midwifery Commission constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.national_register: The Indian Nurses and Midwives' Register maintained by the Nursing and Midwifery Ethics and Registration Board under section 25.
key_definitions.nurse: A healthcare professional who has completed a formally recognized program of basic, generalized nursing education, acquired the requisite qualification, is licensed to practice nursing by the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission, and demonstrates competency in nursing practice.
key_definitions.nurse_practitioner: A licensed nurse who has completed a formally recognized advanced education and training program, acquired the requisite qualification, is licensed to practice by the National Commission, and demonstrates clinical competencies for the scope of practice, complex decision making, and has expert knowledge in the area of specialization.
key_definitions.nurse_practitioner_in_midwifery: A licensed nurse who has completed a formally recognized advanced education and training program, acquired the requisite qualification, is licensed to practice by the National Commission, and demonstrates clinical competency for the scope of practice, complex decision making, and has expert knowledge in the area of specialization.
key_definitions.nursing: The autonomous and collaborative care of individuals of all ages, families, groups, and communities, sick or well, including the promotion of health, prevention of illness, care of the physically ill, mentally ill, disabled, and dying people in all healthcare and other community settings. It involves healthcare teaching, participation as a healthcare team member, supervising and training auxiliaries, and other key roles.
key_definitions.nursing_and_midwifery_institution: An educational and training institution or a research institution in India, recognized under this Act, which grants diploma or undergraduate or postgraduate or any other post-degree diploma or certificate in nursing and midwifery, and includes affiliated colleges and deemed to be Universities.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Autonomous Board, Chairperson, Fund, Midwifery, Midwifery Associate, Midwifery Professional, National Commission, National Register, Nurse, Nurse Practitioner, Nurse Practitioner in Midwifery, Nursing, Nursing and Midwifery Institution, Nursing and Midwifery Assessment and Rating Board, Nursing and Midwifery Ethics and Registration Board, Nursing and Midwifery Undergraduate and Postgraduate Education Board, Nursing Associate, Nursing Professional, Prescribed, Qualification, Recognised nursing and midwifery qualification, Registered Professional, Regulations, State Commission, State Register, and University.

Establishes the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission, a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, to exercise powers and discharge duties laid down under the Act. Its head office is in New Delhi.
Details the composition of the National Commission, which includes a Chairperson, sixteen ex officio Members, and twelve other Members.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of National Commission
main_sections.description: Outlines the various powers and functions of the National Commission, which are extensive and cover regulation, standards, education, and professional conduct in nursing and midwifery.
Provides for the establishment of Autonomous Boards, which are constituent bodies of the National Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Nursing and Midwifery Undergraduate and Postgraduate Education Board
main_sections.description: Specifies the powers and functions of the board responsible for undergraduate and postgraduate education in nursing and midwifery.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Nursing and Midwifery Assessment and Rating Board
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the board responsible for assessing and rating nursing and midwifery institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Nursing and Midwifery Ethics and Registration Board
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the board responsible for ethics and registration of nursing and midwifery professionals.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of State Nursing and Midwifery Commission
main_sections.description: Deals with the constitution and composition of State Nursing and Midwifery Commissions.
Establishes the National Register and State Registers for nursing and midwifery professionals.
Specifies conditions under which practice of nursing and midwifery is barred.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of nursing and Midwifery qualifications granted by Universities or nursing and midwifery institutions in India
main_sections.description: Deals with the recognition of nursing and midwifery qualifications obtained from Indian institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of nursing and midwifery qualifications granted by nursing and midwifery institutions outside India
main_sections.description: Covers the recognition of nursing and midwifery qualifications from institutions outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Withdrawal of recognition granted to nursing and midwifery qualification granted by nursing and midwifery institutions in India
main_sections.description: Allows for the withdrawal of recognition for qualifications from Indian institutions.
Details the provision of grants by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Fund
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Fund.
Specifies how offences under the Act are to be taken cognizance of.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede National Commission
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to supersede the National Commission in certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules under the Act.
Empowers the National Commission to make regulations.
Deals with the repeal of existing provisions and saving clauses.

important_rules: Rule: Professionals must obtain a license to practice nursing and midwifery, granted by the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission (Section 26).
Rule: Nursing and midwifery institutions must be recognized under this Act to grant diplomas or certificates (Section 2(p)).
Rule: The National Commission is responsible for maintaining a National Register of nurses and midwives (Section 25).
Rule: The Central Government has the power to give directions to the National Commission, Autonomous Boards, and Nursing and Midwifery Advisory Council (Section 41).
Rule: Universities and nursing and midwifery institutions have an obligation to comply with the provisions of this Act (Section 45).

penalties: Specific penalties for offences are not detailed in the provided text but would likely be defined in later sections or through rules/regulations made under the Act. Section 49 discusses cognizance of offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Nursing and Midwifery Commission, Autonomous Boards, State Nursing and Midwifery Commissions, and relevant government authorities (Central and State) are responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves maintaining registers, assessing and rating institutions, granting licenses, regulating practice, and taking cognizance of offences.

rights: Right of registered professionals to practice nursing and midwifery (Section 26).
Right to have qualifications recognized if granted by eligible institutions (Sections 28, 29, 32).
duties: Duty of professionals to be enrolled in the National Register or State Register (Section 26).
Duty of Universities and nursing and midwifery institutions to comply with the Act (Section 45).
obligations: Obligations of registered professionals to adhere to the terms of their license and practice standards (implied by Section 26).
Obligations of institutions to seek recognition and maintain standards.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishment of new nursing or midwifery institutions, including obtaining permission (Section 21).
Procedure for assessment and approval or disapproval of proposals for new institutions (Section 22).
Procedure for registration of nursing and midwifery professionals in the National Register and State Registers (Section 25).
Procedure for recognition of nursing and midwifery qualifications, both domestic and international (Sections 28, 29, 32, 33).
administration: The Central Government, through the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, plays a significant role in establishing and directing the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission. The National Commission itself and the State Commissions administer various aspects of the Act.
important_notes: Note: Different provisions of the Act may come into force on different dates as notified by the Central Government.
Note: The Act establishes a hierarchical structure with the National Commission overseeing Autonomous Boards and State Commissions.
Note: The Act allows for the withdrawal of recognition of qualifications under specific circumstances.
Note: The Chairperson and Members of the National Commission and officers of the Commission and Autonomous Boards are deemed to be public servants (Section 47).
Note: The Central Government has the power to supersede the National Commission if it fails to discharge its functions or acts against public interest (Section 50).

title: THE INTER-SERVICES ORGANISATIONS (COMMAND, CONTROL AND DISCIPLINE) ACT, 2023
purpose: To empower the Commander-in-Chief or the Officer-in-Command of Inter-services Organisations in respect of service personnel subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950 and the Navy Act, 1957, serving under or attached to their command, for the maintenance of discipline and proper discharge of their duties, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to all persons subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950 and the Navy Act, 1957, and to persons of such other forces as the Central Government may specify, who are serving in or attached to an Inter-services Organisation. It also applies to Inter-services Organisations constituted by the Central Government.

key_definitions.Air Officer: An officer of the Air Force above the rank of Group Captain.
key_definitions.Chief of Defence Staff: An officer of the regular Army, Indian Navy, or Air Force appointed as such by the Central Government.
key_definitions.Commander-in-Chief: A General Officer of the regular Army, a Flag Officer of the Indian Navy, or an Air Officer of the Air Force appointed as Commander-in-Chief of a Joint Services Command, and in their absence, the officer on whom the command devolves.
key_definitions.Commanding Officer: The officer in actual command of the unit, ship or establishment and includes an officer appointed as such by the Commander-in-Chief or the Officer-in-Command of an Inter-services Organisation.
key_definitions.Flag Officer: An officer of the rank of Admiral of the Fleet, Admiral, Vice-Admiral or Rear-Admiral.
key_definitions.General Officer: An officer of the regular Army above the rank of Brigadier.
key_definitions.Inter-services Organisation: A body of troops including a Joint Services Command consisting of persons subject to any two or all of the Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950 and the Navy Act, 1957.
key_definitions.Officer-in-Command: A General Officer of the regular Army, a Flag Officer of the Indian Navy, or an Air Officer of the Air Force appointed as the Officer-in-Command of an Inter-services Organisation (other than a Joint Services Command), and in their absence, the officer on whom the command devolves.
key_definitions.Service Acts: The Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950, or the Navy Act, 1957, or any two or all of them.
key_definitions.service personnel: Persons who are subject to any of the Service Acts.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Inter-services Organisations (Command, Control and Discipline) Act, 2023, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

Specifies that the Act applies to personnel subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, Army Act, 1950, Navy Act, 1957, and other forces notified by the Central Government, who are serving in or attached to an Inter-services Organisation.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as Air Officer, Chief of Defence Staff, Commander-in-Chief, Commanding Officer, Inter-services Organisation, and Service Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision for certain forces under Central Government
