main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to specify forces to which all or any provisions of this Act shall apply, with or without modifications. It also vests disciplinary and administrative powers in the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command of the Inter-services Organisation for such forces.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Inter-services Organisation or Joint Services Command
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to constitute an Inter-services Organisation or Joint Services Command comprising personnel subject to the Service Acts. It also enables the Central Government to delegate powers of the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command to other officers.

main_sections.section_title: Existing Inter-services Organisations and Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command to continue
main_sections.description: Ensures that Inter-services Organisations and their Commanders-in-Chief or Officers-in-Command functioning before the commencement of the Act are deemed to have been constituted or appointed under this Act. It also validates actions taken prior to the Act's commencement.

Declares the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command as the head of the Inter-services Organisation and grants them command and control over personnel for discipline and duty maintenance. They are empowered to exercise disciplinary and administrative powers equivalent to those of various service command authorities.

Defines the role of the Commanding Officer in an Inter-services Organisation, including additional duties assigned by the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command, and the power to initiate disciplinary or administrative actions.
States that the Central Government has superintendence over Inter-services Organisations and can issue directions on matters of national security or general administration.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare persons to be on active service
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to declare, by notification, any service personnel or class of personnel to be on active service with reference to an Inter-services Organisation or this Act, notwithstanding anything in the Service Acts.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
States that the provisions of this Act have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law or instrument.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for any action taken or intended to be taken in good faith under this Act.

Authorizes the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, for a period of three years from its commencement. Orders made under this section must be laid before Parliament.
Mandates that every rule made by the Central Government under this Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specific period, allowing for modifications or annulment.

important_rules: Service personnel subject to Air Force Act, Army Act, or Navy Act, and serving in or attached to an Inter-services Organisation are under the command and control of the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command for discipline and duty maintenance.

The Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command of an Inter-services Organisation exercises disciplinary and administrative powers equivalent to those of higher authorities within their respective services.
The Central Government can specify other forces to which this Act applies and can delegate powers related to discipline and administration.
Existing Inter-services Organisations and their leadership are recognized under this Act.
The Central Government has the power to declare service personnel to be on active service in relation to Inter-services Organisations.
Rules made by the Central Government under this Act are subject to parliamentary scrutiny.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command of Inter-services Organisations, with superintendence by the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of disciplinary and administrative powers by the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command, and through rules made by the Central Government.

rights: Right to protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Service personnel retain rights as defined under their respective Service Acts unless overridden by this Act.
duties: Duty to maintain discipline and properly discharge duties within Inter-services Organisations.
Duty to comply with directions issued by the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command.
Duty to comply with rules made under the Act.
obligations: Obligation for personnel to be subject to the command and control of the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command.
Obligation for Inter-services Organisations to function under the superintendence of the Central Government.

key_procedures: Constitution of Inter-services Organisations or Joint Services Commands by Central Government notification.
Notification by Central Government to specify forces to which the Act applies.
Central Government may issue notifications to declare personnel on active service.
Central Government may make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions, which must be laid before Parliament.
administration: Central Government (specifically, the superintendence of Inter-services Organisations vests in the Central Government).
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on any inconsistent provisions in other laws.
No legal proceedings can be initiated against persons for actions taken in good faith under this Act.
The Central Government has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of three years, with parliamentary oversight.
The Act aims to harmonize command, control, and discipline across different service branches within joint organisations.

title: THE CHIEF ELECTION COMMISSIONER AND OTHER ELECTION COMMISSIONERS (APPOINTMENT, CONDITIONS OF SERVICE AND TERM OF OFFICE) ACT, 2023
purpose: To regulate the appointment, conditions of service and term of office of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, the procedure for transaction of business by the Election Commission and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the appointment, conditions of service, and term of office of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners in India. It also governs the procedure for the transaction of business by the Election Commission.

key_definitions.Chief Election Commissioner: The Chief Election Commissioner appointed under clause (2) of article 324 of the Constitution and in accordance with this Act.
key_definitions.Election Commission: The Election Commission referred to in clause (1) of article 324 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.Election Commissioner: Any other Election Commissioner appointed under clause (2) of article 324 of the Constitution and in accordance with this Act.
key_definitions.Search Committee: The Search Committee for preparation of panel of persons for consideration for appointment as Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
key_definitions.Selection Committee: The Selection Committee that recommends appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including Chief Election Commissioner, Election Commission, Election Commissioner, Search Committee, and Selection Committee.
States that the Election Commission shall consist of the Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may fix.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners shall be appointed by the President by warrant.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners
main_sections.description: Outlines the qualifications for appointment, requiring persons to hold or have held a post equivalent to the rank of Secretary to the Government of India, and to be persons of integrity with knowledge and experience in management and conduct of elections.

Establishes a Search Committee, headed by the Minister of Law and Justice and comprising two other members not below the rank of Secretary to the Government of India, to prepare a panel of five persons for consideration by the Selection Committee.

Constitutes the Selection Committee for recommending appointments, consisting of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of Opposition in the House of the People (Member), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister (Member). It also clarifies that vacancies or defects in the Selection Committee do not invalidate appointments.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Selection Committee to regulate its own procedure
main_sections.description: Grants the Selection Committee the power to regulate its own procedure in a transparent manner and allows it to consider persons not on the Search Committee's panel.

Specifies a term of office of six years or until the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier. Re-appointment is not permitted. If an Election Commissioner is appointed as Chief Election Commissioner, the aggregate term shall not exceed six years.

Determines that the salary of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners shall be equal to that of a Judge of the Supreme Court. It also covers provisions for disadvantageous variations in service conditions for those already in office, reduction in salary if a pension is drawn from previous service, dearness allowance, and encashment of earned leave.

Allows the Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner to resign by writing to the President. The Chief Election Commissioner can only be removed like a Supreme Court Judge, while other Election Commissioners can be removed on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Allows for leave to be granted according to rules applicable to the member's previous service, with the power to grant or refuse leave vesting in the President.
Deals with pension entitlements for those who were in government service before appointment, allowing them to opt for their previous pension and retirement benefits.

main_sections.section_title: Right to subscribe to General Provident Fund
main_sections.description: Confirms the right of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners to subscribe to the General Provident Fund.
Empowers the President to determine other conditions of service, such as travelling allowance, medical facilities, and conveyance facilities, through rules.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners
main_sections.description: Provides protection against civil or criminal proceedings for acts, things, or words committed or spoken in the discharge of official duty.
States that the business of the Election Commission shall be transacted in accordance with the Act's provisions.
Allows the Election Commission to regulate its business and allocation of work by unanimous decision. Matters of difference shall be decided by majority opinion.
Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions within five years of its commencement.
Requires all rules and orders made under the Act to be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modification or annulment.

Repeals the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991, and saves actions taken under the repealed Act, provided they are not inconsistent with the current Act.

important_rules: The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners shall hold office for a term of six years or till they attain the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.
The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners are not eligible for re-appointment.

The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners shall be appointed from among persons holding or having held a post equivalent to the rank of Secretary to the Government of India, who are of integrity and have experience in election management.
The Election Commission shall transact its business as far as possible by unanimous decision; in case of differences, the decision will be by majority.
No court shall entertain or continue civil or criminal proceedings against any person for any act done in the discharge of their official duty as Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Election Commission itself, with judicial oversight.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment process, term limits, removal procedures, and judicial protection granted to the Commissioners. The Central Government can also remove difficulties in implementation, and rules and orders are subject to parliamentary review.

rights: Right to salary and allowances equal to a Judge of the Supreme Court.
Right to dearness allowance.
Right to encashment of earned leave.
Right to subscribe to the General Provident Fund.
Right to medical facilities, leave travel concession, and conveyance facilities (as determined by rules).
Protection from civil and criminal proceedings for official acts.
duties: To conduct elections in accordance with the Constitution and the Act.
To transact business of the Election Commission.
To uphold integrity and knowledge in the conduct of elections.
obligations: To be appointed through a prescribed process involving a Search Committee and a Selection Committee.
To serve for the specified term and adhere to age limits.
To resign by writing to the President if seeking to demit office early.
To operate within the framework of unanimous or majority decisions in the Election Commission's business.

key_procedures: Appointment Procedure: A Search Committee prepares a panel of five persons. A Selection Committee (comprising PM, Leader of Opposition, and a Union Minister) recommends candidates to the President. The President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
Transaction of Business: The Election Commission transacts its business by unanimous decision where possible. In case of differences, the matter is decided by majority opinion.
Removal Procedure: Chief Election Commissioner removed like a Supreme Court Judge. Other Election Commissioners removed on recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Lay-out Procedure: Rules and orders made under the Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for review and potential modification or annulment.
administration: The Central Government is responsible for appointing the Election Commissioners and making rules related to their service conditions. The Election Commission is an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting elections.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991.
Anything done or action taken under the repealed Act is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act, if not inconsistent.
The Leader of Opposition definition includes the leader of the single largest party in opposition if the formal Leader of Opposition is not recognized.
The appointment shall not be invalid due to any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Selection Committee.

title: THE PRESS AND REGISTRATION OF PERIODICALS ACT, 2023
purpose: To provide for press, registration of periodicals and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to printing presses and periodicals published in India, including their owners, printers, publishers, and editors. It also covers facsimile editions of foreign periodicals printed in India.

key_definitions.facsimile_edition: An exact reproduction of the original edition of a foreign publication in English or an Indian language included in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.
key_definitions.journal: A periodical publication, other than a magazine, which primarily carries academic, scientific or technical content related to a particular discipline or profession.
key_definitions.keeper: A person who manages the day-to-day operations of a printing press, the owner of which is a non-individual entity.
key_definitions.newspaper: A periodical of loose-folded sheets usually printed on newsprint and brought out daily or at least once in a week, containing information on current events, public news or comments on public news.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Gazette of India or the Official Gazette of a State, as the case may be.
key_definitions.owner: An individual, firm or any such legal entity owning a periodical.
key_definitions.periodical: Any publication, including a newspaper, which is published and printed at regular intervals containing public news or comments on public news, but does not include a book, or a journal including a book or journal of scientific, technical and academic nature.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.press_registrar_general: The Press Registrar General of India, appointed by the Central Government.
key_definitions.printer: The owner or keeper of a printing press.
key_definitions.printing: Reproduction of a periodical through any technology involving mass production of copies, but does not include photocopying.
key_definitions.publication: Newspapers, magazines, journals or newsletters printed periodically and published in India, and shall include its reproduction in electronic form or any syndication, facsimile edition, for public distribution or access.
key_definitions.publish: The process of making a work available to the public by issuing or causing to be issued the copies thereof or in any other manner, whether for a price or free of charge.
key_definitions.publisher: A person responsible to publish any periodical.
key_definitions.register: The register of periodicals maintained under clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 5.
key_definitions.specified_authority: A District Magistrate or Collector or such other officer as the State Government or, as the case may be, Union territory Administration may, by notification, specify.
key_definitions.title: The name of a periodical as may be verified by the Press Registrar General, printed prominently and legibly as the masthead on the front page of that periodical by which it shall be known or be identified.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its extent (whole of India), and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as periodical, newspaper, journal, owner, printer, publisher, and Press Registrar General.
Mandates that every printer of a periodical must furnish an online intimation to the Press Registrar General and the specified authority within whose jurisdiction the printing press is located.

Establishes that any citizen of India or entity registered in India can bring out a periodical, with specific exclusions for individuals convicted of certain offences related to terrorism or the security of the State. It also requires specific details to be printed on every periodical and outlines conditions for printing facsimile editions of foreign periodicals.

main_sections.section_title: Press Registrar General and other officers
main_sections.description: Details the appointment of the Press Registrar General and other officers by the Central Government. It outlines the functions of the Press Registrar General, including issuing registration certificates, maintaining a register of periodicals, setting guidelines for titles, collecting fees, managing funds, and publishing annual reports.

Specifies the powers of the Press Registrar General, including obtaining annual statements, verifying circulation figures, revising, suspending, or cancelling registration, requisitioning services for verification, calling for records and information, and imposing penalties.

Lays down the procedure for obtaining a certificate of registration for a periodical. It requires an online application to the Press Registrar General and the specified authority, suggesting titles, and providing necessary documents and particulars. It also outlines the process for the specified authority's no-objection/comments, the Press Registrar General's satisfaction, issuance of the certificate, and conditions for commencement of publication.

main_sections.section_title: Revision of certificate of registration or title
main_sections.description: Allows a publisher to apply for revision of the certificate of registration or title, subject to satisfaction and issuance of a revised certificate by the Press Registrar General.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of ownership of a periodical
main_sections.description: Governs the transfer of ownership of a registered periodical. It requires an application to the Press Registrar General, provision of documents, and payment of fees. The Press Registrar General's satisfaction is necessary for permission, and any change in shareholding must be intimated.
Allows the owner of a periodical to discontinue it.
Provides for the suspension or cancellation of a periodical's registration under certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Annual statement to be furnished by periodical
main_sections.description: Requires periodicals to furnish an annual statement.
Mentions the preparation and publication of an annual report by the Press Registrar General.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Press Registrar General to impose penalty
main_sections.description: Grants the Press Registrar General the power to impose penalties.
Establishes a Press and Registration Appellate Board for appeals against decisions made under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions for the implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Press Registrar General and other officers to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Press Registrar General and other officers appointed under the Act as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith by individuals acting under the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rule
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties encountered in the implementation of the Act.
Requires rules and notifications made under the Act to be laid before Parliament.
Deals with the repeal of existing provisions and savings, indicating that this Act supersedes previous legislation on the subject.

important_rules: Every printer of a periodical must furnish an online intimation to the Press Registrar General and the specified authority.
Every periodical printed in India must legibly display the name of the printer, place of printing, name of editor, publisher, and place of publication.
A citizen of India or a registered entity in India may bring out a periodical, provided they have not been convicted of acts of terrorism or against the security of the State.
Facsimile editions of foreign periodicals may be printed in India only with the previous approval of the Central Government and require registration.
Publishers must obtain a certificate of registration from the Press Registrar General for any periodical intended for publication in India.
The title of a periodical must not be the same or similar to an existing title and must conform to guidelines issued by the Press Registrar General.
Publication of a periodical must commence within twelve months of receiving the registration certificate, failing which the registration may be cancelled.
Any transfer of ownership of a periodical requires an application and permission from the Press Registrar General.
Owners of periodicals must intimate any change in shareholding pattern within fifteen days of informing the Registrar of Companies.

penalties: The Press Registrar General has the power to impose penalties (details of specific penalties are not elaborated in the provided text but are indicated by Section 14).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Press Registrar General and other officers appointed under the Act, along with specified authorities (District Magistrates, Collectors, etc.).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through processes like intimation, registration, verification of circulation figures, revision, suspension, or cancellation of registration, and imposition of penalties. The Press Registrar General can also call for records and information and requisition services for verification.

rights: Any citizen of India or entity registered in India has the right to bring out a periodical (subject to certain conditions).
Publishers have the right to apply for registration, revision of certificates, and title changes.
Owners have the right to transfer ownership of a periodical.
Owners have the right to discontinue a periodical.
Individuals have the right to appeal against decisions to the Press and Registration Appellate Board.
duties: Printers have a duty to furnish intimation.
Publishers have a duty to obtain a certificate of registration.
Publishers and printers have a duty to ensure that periodicals contain specific printed information.
Owners have a duty to intimate changes in shareholding.
Periodicals have a duty to furnish annual statements.
Press Registrar General and other officers have a duty to act as public servants.
obligations: To comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
To ensure that publications do not contain content prohibited by law.
To follow prescribed procedures for registration, transfer of ownership, and discontinuation.

key_procedures: Furnishing intimation by printer: Printer to submit an online intimation to the Press Registrar General and the specified authority.

Registration of a periodical: Publisher to submit an online application to the Press Registrar General and specified authority, suggesting titles, providing particulars and documents, and paying fees. Specified authority to provide comments within 60 days. Press Registrar General to issue a certificate if satisfied.
Revision of certificate or title: Publisher to apply to the Press Registrar General for revision, providing necessary particulars.

Transfer of ownership: Owner to apply to the Press Registrar General with required documents and fees. Press Registrar General to permit transfer upon satisfaction. Publisher to obtain a revised certificate.
Discontinuation of a periodical: Owner to inform the Press Registrar General about the discontinuation.
Appeals: Appeals against decisions to be made to the Press and Registration Appellate Board.
administration: The Central Government, through the Press Registrar General of India and other appointed officers, is responsible for the administration of this Act. State Governments and Union territory Administrations, through specified authorities, also play a role in the process.
important_notes: The Act came into force on March 1, 2024.
The definition of 'publication' includes its reproduction in electronic form.
The Press Registrar General is empowered to verify circulation figures and may requisition services for this purpose.
The Central Government has the power to make rules and remove difficulties related to the Act.
Actions taken in good faith by individuals acting under the Act are protected.

title: The “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University Act, 2025
purpose: To establish the Institute of Rural Management Anand as a University named “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University, declare it an institution of national importance, and to impart technical and management education and training in the co-operative sector, promote co-operative research and development, and attain global standards of excellence to strengthen the co-operative movement in India.
scope: This Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University, which is to be headquartered in Anand, Gujarat. It also covers the Institute of Rural Management Anand School as one of the Schools of the University. The Act allows for the establishment of Schools or outlying campuses or affiliation of institutes within India and potentially outside India with prior Central Government approval. It also applies to co-operative societies registered under various Acts and their employees.

key_definitions.University: “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University established and incorporated under this Act.
key_definitions.Institute of Rural Management Anand: The Institute of Rural Management Anand established and incorporated under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, located in Anand, Gujarat.
key_definitions.Institute of Rural Management Anand Scho: One of the Schools of the “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University.
key_definitions.co-operative societies: All co-operative societies registered under the Co-operative Societies Acts of the respective States, Union territories with Legislature and without Legislature and the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002.
key_definitions.co-operative principles: The co-operative principles provided in the First Schedule of the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it will come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette. Different dates can be appointed for different provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University as institution of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares the “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University as an institution of national importance, based on its objectives.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including academic bodies, officers, co-operative related terms, and the University itself.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University
main_sections.description: Establishes the “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with its headquarters in Anand, Gujarat. It outlines the powers to acquire property and enter into contracts. It also specifies that the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and various councils constitute the University.

Details the consequences of the University's establishment, including the dissolution of the Institute of Rural Management Anand Society, the transfer of assets and liabilities, the continuation of the Institute of Rural Management Anand School's identity and autonomy, and the protection of employment terms for existing staff. It also declares the Institute of Rural Management Anand School as a 'Centre of Excellence' for Rural Management.

Outlines the primary objectives of the University, which include providing trained manpower for the co-operative sector, offering training and capacity building, acting as an apex body for coordinating academic and research activities, and standardizing course design and pedagogy in co-operative education.

important_rules: The Act must be officially commenced by a notification from the Central Government.
The “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University is declared an institution of national importance.
The Institute of Rural Management Anand is dissolved and becomes the “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University.
All property, rights, and liabilities of the Institute of Rural Management Anand are transferred to the University.
The Institute of Rural Management Anand School retains its identity and autonomy, with an Executive Board responsible for its autonomy and a Director for implementing its decisions.
The Institute of Rural Management Anand School is designated as a 'Centre of Excellence' for Rural Management, with greater autonomy and responsibility for developing and spreading best practices.
Employees of the Institute of Rural Management Anand will continue their employment with the University under the same terms and conditions, with protections for their tenure, rights, and privileges.
The University can deploy employees to any area, field, or location in India as it deems fit to further its objects.

The identity and autonomy of ongoing academic programs and courses of the Institute of Rural Management Anand School must be preserved, with modifications requiring concurrence from the School's Executive Board.

rights: Employees of the Institute of Rural Management Anand have the right to continue their employment with the University on the same terms and conditions, with protections for pension and gratuity.
The Institute of Rural Management Anand School has the right to administrative and academic autonomy as provided by the Statutes.
Post-retirement benefits of superannuated employees of the Institute of Rural Management Anand are to be borne by the University without disadvantage.
The University and Institute of Rural Management Anand School are public authorities under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (Section 46).
duties: The University has a duty to provide qualified and trained manpower for the co-operative sector.
The University has a duty to provide training, education, and capacity building for employees and board members of co-operative societies.
The University has a duty to integrate, coordinate, and standardize academic and research activities of affiliated co-operative institutes.
The Institute of Rural Management Anand School has a duty to develop and spread best practices in education, training, and research.
The Executive Board of the Institute of Rural Management Anand School is responsible for ensuring the identity and autonomy of the School.
obligations: The University must ensure that terms and conditions, rights, and privileges of employees are not varied to their disadvantage.
Modifications to ongoing academic programs and courses of the Institute of Rural Management Anand School require the concurrence of the Executive Board of the School.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Central Government appoints a date by notification in the Official Gazette.
Establishment of the University: The Central Government appoints a date for the establishment of the “Tribhuvan” Sahkari University.
Transfer of Assets and Liabilities: Upon commencement, all property, rights, and liabilities of the Institute of Rural Management Anand are automatically transferred to the University.
Employment Continuation: Persons employed in the Institute of Rural Management Anand immediately before commencement continue in the University under same terms and conditions.
Disciplinary Proceedings: Ongoing disciplinary proceedings against permanent employees continue under the Institute of Rural Management Anand Society Rules, 2004.
administration: The Central Government has a role in appointing commencement dates and approving outlying campuses outside India. The University itself is administered through various officers and authorities as detailed in Chapters III and IV.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect (Section 48).
Acts and proceedings of the University are not invalidated by vacancies in its authorities (Section 45).
The University and Institute of Rural Management Anand School are considered public authorities under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (Section 46).
Actions taken in good faith are protected (Section 47).
Transitional provisions exist to address matters not covered by the Act (Section 53).
The First Schedule provides co-operative principles from the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002.

title: The Bills of Lading Act, 2025
purpose: To make provisions for the transfer of rights of suit and all liabilities to the consignee named in a bill of lading and every endorsee of a bill of lading, to whom the property in the goods mentioned in the bill of lading shall pass, upon or by reason of a consignment or an endorsement, and for matters connected therewith or related thereto. It aims to ensure that rights in respect of the contract contained in the bill of lading pass with the property and that bills of lading in the hands of a bona fide holder are conclusive evidence of shipment.
scope: This Act applies to all bills of lading issued in India. It governs the rights and liabilities associated with the transfer of property in goods mentioned in a bill of lading through consignment or endorsement.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The Bills of Lading Act, 2025' and outlines that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Rights under bills of lading to vest in consignee or endorsee
main_sections.description: States that every consignee or endorsee of a bill of lading, to whom the property in the goods passes, shall have all rights of suit and be subject to the same liabilities as if the contract in the bill of lading had been made with them.

main_sections.section_title: Right of stoppage in transit or claims for freight not to be affected
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not prejudice the right of stoppage in transit, the right to claim freight against the original shipper or owner, or the liability of the consignee or endorsee by reason of their status or receipt of goods.

main_sections.section_title: Bill of lading in hands of consignee, etc., conclusive evidence of shipment as against master, etc.
main_sections.description: Declares that a bill of lading in the hands of a consignee or endorsee for valuable consideration, representing goods shipped, is conclusive evidence of shipment against the master or signer, unless the misrepresentation was due to the fraud of the shipper or holder, or the holder had actual notice that the goods were not shipped.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to give directions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue necessary directions for the implementation of the Act's provisions.

Repeals the Indian Bills of Lading Act, 1856, and includes provisions for the continuity of previous operations, rights, liabilities, proceedings, and references under the repealed Act, as well as the application of Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897.

important_rules: Rule 1: Consignees and endorsees of bills of lading, to whom property in goods passes, acquire all rights of suit and are subject to liabilities as if they were the original contracting parties.

Rule 2: A bill of lading held by a bona fide holder for value, stating goods have been shipped, is conclusive evidence of shipment against the master or signer, with exceptions for fraud or actual notice of non-shipment.
Rule 3: The right of stoppage in transit and the right to claim freight against the original shipper or owner remain unaffected by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directions issued by the Central Government and by recourse to legal proceedings under the Act.

rights: Right of suit transferred to consignee or endorsee.
Conclusive evidence of shipment for bona fide holders of bills of lading.
Right of stoppage in transit (not affected).
Right to claim freight against original shipper or owner (not affected).
duties: Subject to liabilities in respect of the goods as if the contract was made with the consignee or endorsee.
obligations: Obligations transfer to the consignee or endorsee upon property passing.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Transfer of rights and liabilities occurs automatically upon consignment or endorsement of a bill of lading where property in the goods passes to the consignee or endorsee.
Procedure 2: The Central Government may issue notifications to bring the Act into force.
Procedure 3: In case of disputes regarding shipment representation, the bill of lading is conclusive evidence unless fraud by the shipper or holder, or actual notice of non-shipment, is proven.
administration: Central Government
important_notes: The Act repeals the Indian Bills of Lading Act, 1856, but savings clauses ensure the continuity of past operations and rights.
The Act is intended to align with modern legislation, simplify understanding, and facilitate ease of use, while retaining the substance of the previous law.

title: The Repealing and Amending Act, 2025
purpose: To repeal certain enactments that have ceased to be in force, become obsolete, or are no longer necessary as separate Acts, and to amend certain other enactments to correct formal defects.
scope: This Act applies to various enactments listed in the First and Second Schedules. The repeal of an enactment does not affect other enactments where it has been applied, incorporated, or referred to, nor does it affect anything already done or suffered, or any rights, obligations, liabilities, or remedies already acquired or incurred. It also does not affect existing principles of law, jurisdictions, or procedures derived from repealed enactments, nor does it revive anything no longer in force. The amendments are specified in the Second Schedule and relate to specific provisions within the amended acts.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Repealing and Amending Act, 2025.
This section states that the enactments specified in the First Schedule are hereby repealed.
This section states that the enactments specified in the Second Schedule are hereby amended to the extent and in the manner mentioned in the fourth column thereof.

This section outlines the effects of the repeal and amendments made by the Act. It ensures that past actions, rights, and liabilities are preserved, and it clarifies that the Act does not revive any repealed jurisdictions or things not currently in force.

important_rules: Rule: Enactments listed in the First Schedule are repealed.
Rule: Enactments listed in the Second Schedule are amended as specified.
Rule: The repeal of an enactment does not affect other enactments that incorporate or refer to it.
Rule: The repeal does not invalidate anything already done or affect existing rights, obligations, liabilities, or remedies.
Rule: The repeal does not affect principles of law, jurisdictions, or procedures derived from repealed enactments.
Rule: The repeal does not revive anything not currently in force.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the authorities responsible for implementing the amended laws and ensuring compliance with the repealed ones.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the provisions of the amended enactments and the continued inapplicability of the repealed enactments.

rights: Preservation of rights acquired, accrued, or incurred before the enactment of this Act.
Preservation of remedies or proceedings in respect of anything already done or suffered.
duties: Compliance with the amended provisions of enactments listed in the Second Schedule.
obligations: Preservation of obligations acquired, accrued, or incurred before the enactment of this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: Identification and listing of enactments for repeal in the First Schedule.
Procedure: Identification and listing of enactments for amendment in the Second Schedule, including the specific amendments to be made.
Procedure: Application of the savings clause (Section 4) to ensure continuity and prevent unintended consequences.
administration: Not explicitly stated for this Act itself, as it is a repealing and amending act. Administration would fall under the purview of the respective government departments responsible for the enactments that are amended or were previously in force.
important_notes: The First Schedule lists enactments to be repealed, including Acts from 1886 to 2023.

The Second Schedule lists enactments to be amended, with specific changes detailed. For example, the General Clauses Act, 1897 is amended to replace 'registered post' with 'speed post with registration'. The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 has several amendments related to service of documents, replacing 'registered post, acknowledgement due' with 'speed post with registration and proof of delivery'. The Indian Succession Act, 1925 has sections related to probate and letters of administration omitted or modified. The Disaster Management Act, 2025 has a minor amendment to a clause in section 30.
The 'Statement of Objects and Reasons' indicates that this is a periodical measure for legislative cleanup.

title: The Revenue Recovery Act, 1890
purpose: To make better provision for recovering certain public demands.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. The Act applies to the recovery of arrears of land-revenue and sums recoverable as arrears of land-revenue, and other public demands.

key_definitions.collector: Means the chief officer in charge of the land-revenue administration of a district.
key_definitions.defaulter: Means a person from whom an arrear of land-revenue, or a sum recoverable as an arrear of land-revenue, is due, and includes a person who is responsible as surety for the payment of any such arrear or sum.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'district', 'Collector', and 'defaulter'.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of public demands by enforcement of processes in other districts than those in which they become payable
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for recovering land revenue arrears or sums recoverable as such from a defaulter in a different district through a certificate sent to the Collector of that other district.

main_sections.section_title: Remedy available to person denying liability to pay amount recovered under last foregoing section
main_sections.description: Provides a remedy for individuals who deny their liability to pay amounts recovered under Section 3, allowing them to institute a suit for repayment under protest.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery by Collectors of sums recoverable as arrears of revenue by other public officers or by local authorities
main_sections.description: Enables Collectors to recover sums due to other public officers or local authorities as if they were arrears of land-revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Property liable to sale under this Act
main_sections.description: Specifies that immovable property belonging to a defaulter can be subjected to a proclamation prohibiting its transfer or charging.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of local laws relating to revenue
main_sections.description: Saves existing local laws related to revenue recovery.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery in India of certain public demands arising beyond India
main_sections.description: Allows for the recovery in India of certain public demands that originated outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery in India of land revenues’ etc., accruing in Burma
main_sections.description: Specifically addresses the recovery in India of land revenues and other sums that accrued in Burma.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Collectors to remit moneys collected in certain cases
main_sections.description: Imposes a duty on Collectors to remit collected moneys in specific circumstances.

important_rules: When an arrear of land-revenue or a sum recoverable as such is payable by a defaulter in another district, the Collector can send a certificate to the Collector of that other district for recovery.
The certificate sent by the Collector is generally conclusive proof of the stated matters.
If a person denies liability and pays under protest, they can institute a suit for repayment.
Collectors can recover sums due to other public officers or local authorities as if they were arrears of land-revenue.
Collectors can issue a proclamation prohibiting the transfer or charging of a defaulter's immovable property.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collectors of districts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of certificates and the enforcement of processes for the recovery of arrears of land-revenue and other public demands.

rights: Right of a defaulter to institute a suit for repayment if liability is denied and payment is made under protest (Section 4).
duties: Duty of Collectors to send certificates for recovery in other districts (Section 3).
Duty of Collectors of other districts to proceed with recovery upon receiving a certificate (Section 3).
Duty of Collectors to remit moneys collected in certain cases (Section 10).

key_procedures: Procedure for recovering public demands from a defaulter in another district: A Collector sends a certificate detailing the defaulter, amount, and account to the Collector of the other district. The receiving Collector then proceeds to recover the amount as if it were an arrear of land-revenue in his own district.

Procedure for a person denying liability: If proceedings are taken against a person under Section 3, and they deny liability, they can pay the amount under protest and then institute a suit in a Civil Court for repayment.

Procedure for recovery by Collectors for other public officers/local authorities: A Collector of a district where the office of the other public officer or local authority is situated will, upon request, recover the sum as if it were an arrear of land-revenue, and can send a certificate to another district if needed.
administration: Collectors of districts are the primary administrative authority for enforcing this Act.
important_notes: The Act has been modified in its application to various regions and has state-specific amendments (e.g., Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Uttarakhand, Haryana).
The extent of the Act has been subject to adaptations, particularly concerning the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Section 4(4) extends the application of Section 4 to situations where proceedings are taken in Pakistan or Burma under similar acts.

title: THE INDIAN PARTNERSHIP ACT, 1932
purpose: To define and amend the law relating to partnership.
scope: Extends to the whole of India. Applies to partnerships, partners, firms, and firm names.

key_definitions.act_of_a_firm: Any act or omission by all the partners, or by any partner or agent of the firm which gives rise to a right enforceable by or against the firm.
key_definitions.business: Includes every trade, occupation and profession.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.third_party: Used in relation to a firm or to a partner therein, means any person who is not a partner in the firm.
key_definitions.partnership: The relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
key_definitions.partner: A person who has entered into a partnership with one another.
key_definitions.firm: Persons who have entered into partnership with one another, collectively.
key_definitions.firm_name: The name under which their business is carried on.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the dates on which its provisions come into force.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'act of a firm', 'business', 'prescribed', and 'third party'.

main_sections.section_title: Application of provisions of Act 9 of 1872
main_sections.description: States that the unrepealed provisions of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, will continue to apply to firms, unless inconsistent with this Act.
Defines the core concepts of partnership, partner, firm, and firm name.
Clarifies that the relation of partnership arises from contract and not from status.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of determining existence of partnership
main_sections.description: Outlines how to determine if a partnership exists, emphasizing the real relation between parties and providing explanations regarding profit sharing.
Defines a partnership at will as one where there's no provision for duration or determination.
Allows for a person to become a partner in specific adventures or undertakings.
Establishes the duties of partners to carry on the business for the greatest common advantage, be just and faithful, and render true accounts and information.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to indemnify for loss caused by fraud
main_sections.description: Requires each partner to indemnify the firm for any loss caused by their fraud in the conduct of the business.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of rights and duties of partners by contract between the partners. Agreements in restraint of trade
main_sections.description: Allows partners to determine their mutual rights and duties by contract, including agreements not to carry on other businesses while a partner.
Details the rights and duties related to the conduct of business, including the right to participate, the duty to attend diligently, decisions by majority on ordinary matters, and access to books.
Covers aspects like remuneration, sharing of profits and losses, interest on capital, advances, and indemnification for liabilities incurred in the conduct of business or in emergencies.
Defines what constitutes the property of the firm, including originally brought-in assets and those acquired for the business, as well as goodwill.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the property of the firm
main_sections.description: Stipulates that firm property must be held and used exclusively for the purposes of the business.
Addresses situations where a partner derives personal profits, subject to contractual agreements.
Deals with the dissolution of a firm, including dissolution by agreement, compulsory dissolution, dissolution by notice, and dissolution by the Court.

main_sections.section_title: Power to exempt from application of this Chapter
main_sections.description: Grants power to exempt certain entities from the application of Chapter VII concerning registration.
Provides for the appointment of Registrars of Firms.
Specifies the procedure for applying for the registration of a firm.
Details the consequences of a firm not being registered, particularly regarding its ability to sue third parties.
Prescribes penalties for providing false information during the registration process.
Contains provisions for savings and clarifies that nothing in the Act affects certain previous laws or transactions.

important_rules: Partners are bound to carry on the business for the greatest common advantage, be just and faithful to each other, and render true accounts and full information (Section 9).
Every partner shall indemnify the firm for any loss caused to it by his fraud in the conduct of the business (Section 10).
Subject to contract, partners have the right to take part in the conduct of the business and are bound to attend diligently to their duties (Section 12).
Subject to contract, partners share profits and losses equally and are entitled to share equally in the profits earned (Section 13).
Subject to contract, firm property must be held and used exclusively for the purposes of the business (Section 15).
Partners have specific rights and duties after a change in the firm, after the expiry of the term, and where additional undertakings are carried out (Section 17).
A partner can be sued for acts of the firm, and the firm is liable for wrongful acts and misapplications by a partner (Sections 25, 26, 27).
The registration of a firm is crucial for its ability to sue third parties (Section 69).
Firms must be registered by applying to the Registrar and providing specific particulars (Sections 58, 60, 62, 63).

penalties: Penalty for furnishing false particulars: A fine may be imposed for providing false information during registration (Section 70).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrars of Firms (appointed under Section 57) and potentially the Courts (as indicated by Section 65 for amendment of the Register by order of Court).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves registration of firms, maintenance of a Register of Firms, rectification of mistakes, and potential court orders. The Act also outlines the legal liabilities of partners and the firm for various acts.

rights: Right to take part in the conduct of the business (Section 12(a)).
Right to express an opinion before a decision is made on ordinary business matters (Section 12(c)).
Right to access, inspect, and copy the books of the firm (Section 12(d)).
Right to share equally in profits and contribute equally to losses (Section 13(b)).
Right to receive interest on capital subscribed if stipulated (Section 13(c)).
Right to interest on advances made beyond agreed capital (Section 13(d)).
Right to be indemnified for payments/liabilities incurred in ordinary conduct or emergencies (Section 13(e)).
Right to have business wound up after dissolution (Section 46).
Right to inspect the Register and filed documents (Section 66).
Right to obtain copies of documents from the Register (Section 67).
duties: Duty to carry on the business to the greatest common advantage (Section 9).
Duty to be just and faithful to each other (Section 9).
Duty to render true accounts and full information to partners (Section 9).
Duty to indemnify the firm for loss caused by fraud (Section 10).
Duty to attend diligently to duties in the conduct of the business (Section 12(b)).
Duty to contribute equally to losses sustained by the firm (Section 13(b)).
Duty to indemnify the firm for loss caused by wilful neglect (Section 13(f)).
Duty to hold and use firm property exclusively for business purposes (Section 15).
obligations: Obligation to carry on the business for the greatest common advantage.
Obligation to be faithful to other partners.
Obligation to provide accurate accounts and information.
Obligation to indemnify the firm for losses caused by fraud or wilful neglect.
Obligation to use firm property exclusively for business purposes.
Obligation to adhere to agreements regarding the duration and determination of the partnership.

key_procedures: Determining the existence of a partnership involves examining the real relation between parties considering all relevant facts (Section 6).
Partnership agreements, which can be expressed or implied, determine the mutual rights and duties of partners (Section 11).
Decisions on ordinary business matters are made by a majority of partners, but changes in the nature of the business require consent of all partners (Section 12(c)).
The settlement of accounts between partners upon dissolution involves paying firm debts and then distributing any surplus among partners, or requiring partners to contribute to deficits (Section 48).
Application for registration of a firm involves submitting a statement to the Registrar containing specific details about the firm and its partners (Section 58).
Recording of changes in the firm's name, place of business, branches, and partners' names and addresses is required with the Registrar (Sections 60, 61, 62, 63).
administration: The administration of the Act primarily involves the Registrars of Firms, appointed under Section 57, who maintain the Register of Firms and process registration applications and related changes. The Indian Contract Act, 1872, is also relevant where its provisions are not inconsistent with this Act.
important_notes: The Act allows for agreements in restraint of trade between partners, subject to specific conditions (Section 11(2), Section 36, Section 54, Section 55).
Minors can be admitted to the benefits of a partnership but not to its liabilities (Section 30).
The Act provides for the dissolution of a firm by agreement, compulsion, notice, or by a court order (Sections 40, 41, 42, 43, 44).
Registration of a firm is not compulsory, but non-registration has significant consequences, notably the inability to sue third parties (Section 69).

title: The Immigrants (Expulsion From Assam) Act, 1950
purpose: To provide the Central Government with the necessary powers to deal with the situation arising from the immigration of a large number of people into Assam, which is disturbing the economy and giving rise to law and order problems.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It specifically addresses the expulsion of certain immigrants from Assam.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Immigrants (Expulsion from Assam) Act, 1950, and that it extends to the whole of India.

main_sections.section_title: Power to order expulsion of certain immigrants
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to order the expulsion of any person or class of persons who have come into Assam from outside India, if their stay is deemed detrimental to the interests of the general public or any Scheduled Tribe in Assam. This includes directions for removal from India or Assam and other necessary directions. It provides an exception for persons displaced due to civil disturbances in areas now forming part of Pakistan.

Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers and duties under section 2 to subordinate officers or the Government of Assam, Meghalaya, or Nagaland, or officers subordinate to those governments, with specified conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Power to give effect to orders, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants authorities empowered under the Act the power to take necessary steps and use force, as deemed reasonably necessary, for the effective exercise of their powers.

Specifies penalties for contravening or abetting the contravention of orders made under section 2, failing to comply with directions, or harboring persons who have contravened such orders. Penalties include imprisonment up to three years and fine.

main_sections.section_title: Protection to persons acting under this Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection from suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act.
This section, related to Repeal and saving, has been repealed.

important_rules: If the Central Government is of the opinion that the stay of a person or class of persons in Assam is detrimental to public interest or to any Scheduled Tribe, it may order their removal from India or Assam.
The Central Government can delegate its expulsion powers to subordinate officers or state governments.
Authorities can use reasonable force to give effect to orders made under the Act.
Harboring individuals who have contravened expulsion orders is a punishable offense.

penalties: Imprisonment which may extend to three years.
Liability to fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government, and delegated authorities (subordinate officers or State Governments of Assam, Meghalaya, or Nagaland).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders for removal from India or Assam, further directions for removal, and the use of reasonable force where necessary. Enforcement includes penalizing contraventions, non-compliance, and harborment.

rights: Protection from legal proceedings for good faith actions under the Act.
duties: Immigrants ordered to expel must comply with removal directions.
Individuals must not harbor persons who have contravened expulsion orders.

key_procedures: Assessment by Central Government: The Central Government forms an opinion regarding the detrimental stay of immigrants in Assam.
Issuance of Order: If deemed detrimental, the Central Government issues an order for removal, specifying time and route.
Delegation of Power: Central Government may delegate this power via notification.
Execution of Orders: Empowered authorities can take steps and use force to ensure effective implementation of orders.
administration: Central Government, with powers delegable to State Governments (Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland) and their subordinate officers.
important_notes: The Act's scope includes the whole of India, but its primary focus is expulsion from Assam.
An exception exists for persons displaced from Pakistan due to civil disturbances.
Section 7, which dealt with Repeal and saving, has been repealed.

title: The Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950
purpose: To provide for the establishment and maintenance of the Contingency Fund of India, enabling the government to meet unforeseen expenditure pending parliamentary authorization.
scope: This act applies to the establishment, custody, and withdrawal of funds from the Contingency Fund of India. It is a central act of the Indian Parliament. The geographical scope is all of India. The subject matter scope is financial management for unforeseen expenditures.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called 'The Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of the Contingency Fund of India
main_sections.description: Establishes a Contingency Fund in the nature of an imprest, titled 'The Contingency Fund of India'. It specifies the initial and subsequent enhanced amounts to be paid into the fund from the Consolidated Fund of India.

main_sections.section_title: Custody of the Contingency Fund and withdrawals therefrom
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Fund shall be held on behalf of the President by a Secretary in the Ministry of Finance. It outlines that no advances can be made from the Fund except for meeting unforeseen expenditure, which must be subsequently authorized by Parliament.

Grants the Central Government the power to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, concerning the custody, payment into, and withdrawal from, the Contingency Fund of India. It also includes a provision for laying such rules before Parliament for modification or annulment.

important_rules: Withdrawals from the Contingency Fund are only permissible for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorization by Parliament.
Any advances made from the fund must be resumed or regularized by Parliament through supplementary appropriation acts or at the end of the financial year.
Rules made under Section 4 must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and are subject to modification or annulment by Parliament.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, specifically the Ministry of Finance, is responsible for administering the fund and making rules. Parliament has oversight and authorization powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the rules made by the Central Government and the parliamentary authorization process for withdrawals.

rights: The Government has the right to establish and utilize the Contingency Fund for unforeseen expenditure.
duties: The duty to maintain the Contingency Fund of India.
The duty to ensure that withdrawals are for unforeseen expenditure.
The duty to seek parliamentary authorization for all withdrawals.
The duty to lay rules made under the Act before Parliament.
obligations: Parliament has an obligation to authorize expenditure from the fund.
The Ministry of Finance has an obligation to hold the fund and manage withdrawals as per the Act and rules.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Fund: A sum is paid from the Consolidated Fund of India into the Contingency Fund of India.
Withdrawal of Funds: Advances can be made from the Fund to meet unforeseen expenditure.
Parliamentary Authorization: The unforeseen expenditure met from the Fund must be subsequently authorized by Parliament through appropriation acts.
Rule Making: The Central Government can make rules to govern the Fund, which are subject to parliamentary approval.
administration: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
important_notes: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Pondicherry.
The amount in the Contingency Fund has been enhanced multiple times since its inception through various amendments.
The Act is based on Articles 267(1) and 283(1) of the Constitution of India.
Rules made under the Act must be presented to Parliament and are subject to its approval or modification.

title: The Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950
purpose: To provide for the incorporation and regulation of Road Transport Corporations for the purpose of developing, coordinating, and improving road transport facilities, offering efficient and economical services for passengers and goods.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, with specific provisions for the Union territory of Delhi and Mizoram. It applies to Road Transport Corporations established under the Act.

key_definitions.ancillary_service: Any subsidiary service that provides amenities or facilities to persons using a Corporation's road transport service.
key_definitions.board: The Board of Directors of a Corporation.
key_definitions.corporation: A Road Transport Corporation established under section 3.
key_definitions.director: A member of the Board of Directors.
key_definitions.extended_area: Any area or route to which a Corporation's road transport service has been extended.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.road_transport_service: A service carrying passengers or goods or both by road in vehicles for hire or reward.
key_definitions.vehicle: Any mechanically propelled vehicle used or capable of being used for road transport, including tram-cars, trolley-vehicles, and trailers.

main_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act as 'The Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950', specifies its territorial extent across India (including specific extensions to Delhi and Mizoram), and its commencement.
Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'ancillary service', 'Board', 'Corporation', 'Director', 'extended area', 'prescribed', 'road transport service', and 'vehicle'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Road Transport Corporations in the States
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to establish Road Transport Corporations by notification, considering public advantages, coordination with other transport forms, and the need for efficient and economical road transport services.
States that every Corporation established under section 3 shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of suing and being sued in its corporate name.

main_sections.section_title: Management of Corporation and Board of Directors
main_sections.description: Details that the general superintendence, direction, and management of a Corporation's affairs vest in a Board of Directors, consisting of a Chairman and other Directors. It also outlines the appointment of a Vice-Chairman and provisions for representation of the Central and State Governments and shareholders on the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualifications for being chosen as, or for being, a Director of a Corporation
main_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which a person is disqualified from being a Director, including being of unsound mind, an undischarged insolvent, convicted of an offense involving moral turpitude, having direct interest in contracts with the Corporation (with exceptions), or having a financial interest in another road transport undertaking.
Outlines the primary responsibility of a Corporation to provide or cause to be provided an efficient, adequate, economical and properly coordinated system of road transport service.

Enumerates the extensive powers granted to a Corporation, including planning, operating, and extending road transport services, acquiring vehicles and property, entering into contracts, borrowing money, and carrying out ancillary services.
Mandates that Corporations maintain proper accounts and prepare annual statements of accounts, which are subject to audit by auditors appointed by the State Government.

Grants the State Government the power to make rules for various aspects of the Act, including the constitution of the Board, appointment of officers, and other matters necessary for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Corporation to make regulations, consistent with the Act and rules, for the transaction of its business, including meetings, committees, and the conduct of its employees.
Provides for penalties for any person who contravenes any rule made under the Act or any regulation made by the Corporation.

important_rules: The State Government may establish Road Transport Corporations for the development and improvement of road transport services (Section 3).
Corporations are managed by a Board of Directors with general superintendence and direction (Section 5).
Specific disqualifications exist for individuals to become or remain Directors (Section 6).
Corporations have a general duty to provide efficient, adequate, economical, and coordinated road transport services (Section 18).
Corporations possess broad powers to plan, operate, acquire assets, and manage their services (Section 19).
Corporations must adhere to principles of sound finance, including the provision for depreciation, reserves, and distribution of profits (Chapter IV).
State Governments can issue directions to Corporations, and in certain circumstances, supersede a Corporation (Sections 34, 38).

penalties: Penalty for breach of rules made under the Act (Section 46).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, through its appointed authorities and by making rules and regulations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the making and enforcement of rules and regulations, the power of direction and supersession of corporations, and by prescribing penalties for breaches.

rights: Right to sue and be sued in its corporate name (Section 4).
Right to appoint committees and delegate functions (Section 12).
Right to operate road transport services and ancillary services (Section 19).
duties: General duty to provide an efficient, adequate, economical, and coordinated system of road transport service (Section 18).
Duty to maintain proper accounts and prepare annual statements of accounts (Section 33).
Duty to adhere to directions issued by the State Government (Section 34).
Duty to comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to obtain approval of the Central Government in certain cases (Section 19B).
Obligation to pay interest and dividends as per financial provisions (Section 28).
Obligation to lay rules and regulations before the State Legislature (Section 45A).

key_procedures: Establishment of a Road Transport Corporation by the State Government via official gazette notification (Section 3).
Management of the Corporation by a Board of Directors, including appointment of Chairman and other Directors (Section 5).
Procedure for meetings of the Board, including quorum, voting, and presiding officers (Section 11).
Procedure for making rules by the State Government (Section 44).
Procedure for making regulations by the Corporation (Section 45).
Procedure for the liquidation of a Corporation (Section 39).
administration: State Government, with provisions for Central Government involvement in representation on Boards and in certain approvals.
important_notes: The Act underwent several amendments, including by the Road Transport Corporations (Amendment) Act, 1956, 1959, 1982, and laws concerning reorganization of states and Union territories like Delhi and Jammu and Kashmir.
Provisions exist for the establishment of subsidiary corporations (Chapter IIA).
Specific provisions apply to the Union territory of Delhi regarding prosecution and cognizance of offenses (Chapter VI).

title: The Khaddar (Protection of Name) Act, 1950
purpose: To regulate the use of the words “Khaddar” and “Khadi” when applied as a trade description of woven materials, and to prevent the sale of spurious Khadi as genuine Khadi.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. Initially excluded Jammu and Kashmir, but later made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

key_definitions.trade_description: The words “Khaddar” and “Khadi”, whether in Hindi or in any other Indian language or in English, when applied to any woven material, shall be deemed to be a trade description. This description indicates that the material is cloth woven on handlooms in India from cotton, silk or woolen yarn hand-spun in India or from a mixture of any two or all of such yarns.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its territorial extent.

main_sections.section_title: The words “Khaddar” and “Khadi” to be trade description
main_sections.description: Defines the words "Khaddar" and "Khadi" as trade descriptions and specifies the criteria for materials to qualify for this description.
This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1957.

important_rules: Rule 1: The words 'Khaddar' and 'Khadi' can only be used as a trade description for woven materials that meet specific criteria: woven on handlooms in India from cotton, silk or woolen yarn hand-spun in India or a mixture of these yarns.
Rule 2: The Act aims to prevent the improper use of the words 'Khaddar' and 'Khadi' and the sale of spurious Khadi.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The text mentions that the Act was enacted to prevent improper use and sale of spurious goods, implying enforcement through relevant trade and merchandise mark laws.

duties: Duty to use the terms 'Khaddar' and 'Khadi' only for materials conforming to the defined trade description.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but the context suggests oversight related to trade descriptions and merchandise marks.
important_notes: The Act was amended to include silk and woolen Khadi fabrics within its scope.
The Act's applicability was extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by a notification in 2019.

The original Khaddar (Name Protection) Act, 1934, was found to be ineffective in preventing the sale of spurious Khadi and did not cover silk and woolen Khadi fabrics, leading to the enactment of this Act.

title: The Companies (Donations to National Funds) Act, 1951
purpose: To enable companies to make donations to certain National Funds, specifically the Gandhi National Memorial Fund, the Sardar Vallabhbhai National Memorial Fund, or any other Fund established for a charitable purpose of national importance approved by the Central Government.
