duties: It is the duty of the Authority to promote the development of the marine products industry, with special reference to exports.
The Authority has a duty to carry out inspections to ensure the quality of marine products.
The Authority has a duty to collect and publish statistics relating to the marine products industry.
obligations: Owners of fishing vessels, processing plants, etc., have an obligation to register them.
Persons engaged in the marine products industry have an obligation to provide statistics when requested.
Employees of the Authority (Chairman, Director, Secretary, etc.) have an obligation not to undertake outside work without permission from the Central Government.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Authority: Central Government specifies a date by notification to establish the Authority, which is a body corporate.
Constitution of the Authority: Appointing a Chairman, ex-officio members, members of Parliament, ministry representatives, and other appointed members.
Registration of entities: Owners of fishing vessels, processing plants, etc., must apply for and obtain registration.
Making of Rules and Regulations: The Central Government has the power to make rules, and the Authority has the power to make regulations, subject to Central Government approval.
administration: The Central Government, with the establishment of the Marine Products Export Development Authority as the primary administrative body for the development and regulation of the marine products industry.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for the commencement of different provisions of the Act.
The Authority shall perform its functions in accordance with and subject to rules made by the Central Government.
The Central Government may delegate its powers under the Act.
No action taken in good faith under the Act will be deemed unlawful.
The Act does not bar the application of other laws.

title: The Diplomatic Relations (Vienna Convention) Act, 1972
purpose: To give effect to the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961 and to provide for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India. It specifically addresses the privileges and immunities of diplomatic missions and their members in India, in line with the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961.

key_definitions.head_of_the_mission: The person charged by the sending State with the duty of acting in that capacity.
key_definitions.members_of_the_mission: The head of the mission and the members of the staff of the mission.
key_definitions.members_of_the_staff_of_the_mission: The members of the diplomatic staff, of the administrative and technical staff and of the service staff of the mission.
key_definitions.members_of_the_diplomatic_staff: The members of the staff of the mission having diplomatic rank.
key_definitions.diplomatic_agent: The head of the mission or a member of the diplomatic staff of the mission.
key_definitions.members_of_the_administrative_and_techni: The members of the staff of the mission employed in the administrative and technical service of the mission.
key_definitions.members_of_the_service_staff: The members of the staff of the mission in the domestic service of the mission.
key_definitions.private_servant: A person who is in the domestic service of a member of the mission and who is not an employee of the sending State.
key_definitions.premises_of_the_mission: The buildings or parts of buildings and the land ancillary thereto, irrespective of ownership, used for the purpose of the mission including the residence of the head of the mission.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Diplomatic Relations (Vienna Convention) Act, 1972' and specifies that it extends to the whole of India.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations
main_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961, as set out in the Schedule to this Act, shall have the force of law in India. It also allows the Central Government to amend the Schedule in conformity with amendments to the Convention.

main_sections.section_title: Application of certain privileges and immunities to diplomatic missions and their members pursuant to international agreement
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to extend privileges and immunities, similar to those in the Schedule, to diplomatic missions and their members from states not party to the Vienna Convention, or to other special missions, based on international agreements.

Allows the Central Government to withdraw privileges and immunities from diplomatic missions of a State party to the Convention if that State breaches its obligations or if Indian missions in that State receive fewer privileges and immunities.
Specifies that for the purpose of article 32 of the Convention, a waiver by the head of the mission or the person performing their functions is considered a waiver by the sending State.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on certain exemptions from customs duty, etc.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that article 36 of the Convention does not grant unlimited rights to import goods free of customs duty for subsequent sale in India by diplomatic missions or their members.

main_sections.section_title: Privileges and immunities of citizens of India
main_sections.description: States that Indian citizens are entitled only to additional privileges and immunities beyond those in article 38 of the Convention, as granted by the Central Government through notification.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on entry into diplomatic premises
main_sections.description: Prohibits public servants or agents of government from entering diplomatic premises to serve legal process without the consent of the head of the mission, which can be obtained through the Ministry of External Affairs.

States that a certificate from the Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of External Affairs regarding a person's entitlement to privilege or immunity under the Act is conclusive evidence of that fact.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, to be published in the Official Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Notifications issued and rules made under this Act to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates that all notifications and rules made under the Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulment.

important_rules: The provisions of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961, as set out in the Schedule, have the force of law in India.
The Central Government can amend the Schedule to the Act to align with amendments to the Vienna Convention.
Privileges and immunities can be extended to missions of non-signatory states or special missions based on international agreements.
The Central Government can withdraw privileges and immunities if a State breaches its obligations under the Convention or reciprocally restricts Indian missions.
Waiver of immunity from jurisdiction by the head of a mission is considered a waiver by the sending State.
Exemptions from customs duty do not permit unrestricted resale of imported goods within India.
Indian citizens are only entitled to additional privileges and immunities as specifically notified by the Central Government.
Entry into diplomatic premises for serving legal process requires the consent of the head of the mission.
Certificates from the Ministry of External Affairs regarding privileges and immunities are conclusive evidence.
The Central Government can make rules to implement the Act.
All notifications and rules made under the Act are subject to parliamentary review and potential modification or annulment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (through various ministries, particularly the Ministry of External Affairs, and law enforcement agencies where applicable).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Vienna Convention provisions as having the force of law in India, by issuing notifications and rules, and by exercising powers to withdraw privileges and immunities.

rights: Diplomatic missions and their members have rights to inviolability of premises, archives, and communications.
Diplomatic agents have personal inviolability and immunity from criminal, civil, and administrative jurisdiction, with specified exceptions.
Diplomatic missions and their members are exempt from certain taxes and dues.
Diplomatic missions have the right to free communication for official purposes.
Diplomatic couriers are protected and enjoy personal inviolability.
Diplomatic agents' private residences enjoy inviolability and protection.
duties: The receiving State (India) has a duty to protect diplomatic premises from intrusion and disturbance.
The receiving State has a duty to treat diplomatic agents with due respect and prevent attacks on their person, freedom, or dignity.
The receiving State has a duty to permit and protect free communication for diplomatic missions.
The receiving State has a duty to protect diplomatic couriers in the performance of their functions.
obligations: Sending States have an obligation to respect the laws and regulations of the receiving State.
Sending States and their missions have an obligation to ensure that their activities do not interfere with the internal affairs of the receiving State.
Sending States are responsible for ensuring that their staff members adhere to the Convention's provisions.
Individuals enjoying immunity have an obligation to not abuse their privileges and immunities.

key_procedures: Granting of privileges and immunities to missions from states not party to the Vienna Convention: Central Government issues a notification specifying the application of the Schedule's provisions, possibly with modifications.
Withdrawal of privileges and immunities: Central Government issues a notification to withdraw specified privileges and immunities.
Obtaining consent for entry into diplomatic premises: Consent for serving legal process can be obtained through the Ministry of External Affairs.
Making rules: Central Government publishes rules in the Official Gazette.
Laying notifications and rules before Parliament: Notifications and rules are submitted to Parliament for review and potential modification or annulment.
administration: Central Government, specifically through the Ministry of External Affairs, is primarily responsible for the administration and implementation of this Act.
important_notes: The Act gives effect to the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961, meaning the Convention's provisions are legally binding in India.
Section 4 allows for reciprocal restrictions on privileges and immunities if India's missions are treated unfairly abroad.
Section 6 clarifies that customs duty exemptions do not allow for unrestricted resale of imported goods.
Section 7 limits additional privileges for Indian citizens to those explicitly granted by the Central Government.

The inclusion of the Vienna Convention's articles in the Schedule means that specific provisions regarding the definition of terms, inviolability of premises, archives, diplomatic bag, personal inviolability, immunity from jurisdiction, waiver of immunity, and exemptions from social security provisions are directly applicable in India.

title: The Chandigarh (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1987
purpose: To provide for the delegation of powers vested in the Administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Union territory of Chandigarh. It covers the delegation of powers, authority, jurisdiction, or duties vested in the Administrator under any law in force in Chandigarh.

key_definitions.Administrator: The administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Chandigarh (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1987, and states that it extends to the whole of the Union territory of Chandigarh.
Defines the term 'Administrator' as the administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Delegation of powers, etc., vested in Administrator
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government or the Administrator to delegate any power, authority, jurisdiction, or duty vested in the Administrator to any officer or other authority by notification. It also allows the Administrator to transfer pending appeals, revision applications, or other matters to a competent officer and to withdraw such matters for self-disposal.

Validates any exercise or discharge of powers, authority, jurisdiction, or duty by any officer or other authority before the commencement of the Act, provided it was done in accordance with the provisions that would have been in force had Section 3(1) been applicable at the material times. It also prevents legal proceedings on the grounds of such officer or authority not being competent.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any power, authority, jurisdiction, or duty of the Administrator can be exercised or discharged by an officer or authority specified by the Central Government or the Administrator via notification.
Rule 2: The Administrator can transfer pending appeals, revision applications, or other matters to a competent officer or authority for disposal.
Rule 3: The Administrator can withdraw any pending appeal, revision application, or other matter from an officer or authority and dispose of it himself.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government or the Administrator
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Official Gazette specifying officers or authorities to whom powers are delegated, and through the process of transferring or withdrawing cases for disposal.

rights: Right of the Administrator to delegate powers.
Right to transfer or withdraw cases.
Right to have actions validated retrospectively.
duties: Duty of the Administrator to exercise powers or discharge duties as per law.
Duty to appoint officers or authorities for delegation.
obligations: Obligation to follow procedures outlined in the Act for delegation and transfer of cases.
Obligation to comply with the provisions for validation of past actions.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: To delegate powers, the Central Government or the Administrator issues a notification in the Official Gazette specifying the officer or authority.
Procedure 2: To transfer a pending matter, the Administrator sends it to a competent officer/authority for disposal.
Procedure 3: To withdraw a pending matter, the Administrator takes it back for self-disposal.
Procedure 4: To validate past actions, the Act retrospectively deems them valid if they align with the delegation provisions.
administration: Administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh and the Central Government.
important_notes: The Act aims to address the practical difficulties faced by the Administrator in disposing of a large number of pending cases, particularly quasi-judicial functions.
Section 4 provides a retrospective validation for actions taken by officers and authorities before the Act's commencement, ensuring legal continuity and preventing challenges to past decisions.

title: The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act, 1987
purpose: To provide for the more effective prevention of the commission of sati and its glorification, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Comes into force in a State on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

key_definitions.code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.glorification: In relation to sati, includes the observance of any ceremony or procession, supporting or justifying sati, arranging functions to eulogize a person who committed sati, or creating trusts, collecting funds, or constructing temples or structures to perpetuate the honor or memory of a person who committed sati.
key_definitions.sati: The act of burning or burying alive of any widow with the body of her deceased husband or relative, or any woman with the body of any of her relatives, regardless of whether it's claimed to be voluntary.
key_definitions.special_court: A Special Court constituted under section 9 of the Act.
key_definitions.temple: Includes any building or structure, roofed or not, constructed or made to preserve the memory of a person in respect of whom sati has been committed, or used or intended to be used for worship or ceremonies related to such commission.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the procedure for its commencement in different states.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Code', 'glorification', 'sati', 'Special Court', and 'temple'.
Prescribes punishment for attempting to commit sati, taking into consideration various factors related to the attempt.
Defines and prescribes punishment for abetting the commission of sati, including specific acts deemed as abetment.
Specifies the punishment for any act of glorification of sati.
Grants the Collector or District Magistrate the power to prohibit acts related to the commission or glorification of sati.

main_sections.section_title: Power to remove certain temples or other structures
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government or Collector/District Magistrate to order the removal of temples or structures used for the glorification of sati.
Allows the Collector or District Magistrate to seize funds or property collected or acquired for the glorification of sati.

main_sections.section_title: Trial of offences under this Act
main_sections.description: Establishes Special Courts for the trial of offences under the Act and outlines their constitution and jurisdiction.
Provides for the appointment of Special Public Prosecutors for the Special Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of Special Courts
main_sections.description: Details the procedure and powers of Special Courts, which are similar to those of a Court of Session.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Special Court with respect to other offences
main_sections.description: Allows Special Courts to try other connected offences and convict for other offences committed under the Act or other laws during a trial.
Empowers Special Courts to declare forfeiture of seized funds or property to the State upon conviction of an offence under the Act.
Provides for the right of appeal from judgments, sentences, or orders of a Special Court to the High Court.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of existing laws related to the prevention of sati.

important_rules: Attempting to commit sati is punishable with imprisonment up to six months or fine or both.
Abetting the commission of sati is punishable with death or imprisonment for life and fine.
Abetting an attempt to commit sati is punishable with imprisonment for life and fine.

Glorifying sati is punishable with imprisonment for a term of not less than one year and not more than seven years, and a fine of not less than five thousand rupees and not more than thirty thousand rupees.

Contravention of orders issued by the Collector or District Magistrate to prohibit acts related to sati or its glorification is punishable with imprisonment for a term of not less than one year and not more than seven years, and a fine of not less than five thousand rupees and not more than thirty thousand rupees.

penalties: Attempt to commit sati: Imprisonment up to six months or fine or both.
Abetment of sati: Death or imprisonment for life and fine.
Abetment of attempt to commit sati: Imprisonment for life and fine.
Glorification of sati: Imprisonment of not less than one year but not more than seven years, and fine of not less than five thousand rupees but not more than thirty thousand rupees.

Contravention of prohibition orders (Section 6): Imprisonment of not less than one year but not more than seven years, and fine of not less than five thousand rupees but not more than thirty thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector or District Magistrate, State Government, Special Courts, Police Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Prohibition orders, removal of structures, seizure of property, trial by Special Courts, imposition of penalties as prescribed.

rights: Right to appeal against judgments, sentences, or orders of a Special Court to the High Court.
Right to have offences tried by a Special Court.
duties: Duty to report the commission of an offence under this Act to the authorities (Section 17).
Duty of the Central Government to appoint commencement dates for the Act in different states.
Duty of the State Government to constitute Special Courts and appoint Judges and Special Public Prosecutors.
Duty of the Collector or District Magistrate to prevent offences and take necessary actions.
obligations: Obligation to not commit, abet, or glorify sati.
Obligation to comply with orders issued by the Collector or District Magistrate.
Obligation to assist police in preventing the commission of sati.

key_procedures: Constitution of Special Courts by the State Government upon notification.
Appointment of a Judge for a Special Court by the State Government in concurrence with the Chief Justice of the High Court.
Appointment of Special Public Prosecutors by the State Government for each Special Court.
Special Courts taking cognizance of offences upon receiving a complaint or police report.
Trial of offences by Special Courts with the powers of a Court of Session.
Appeals from Special Court judgments to the High Court within 30 days.
Forfeiture of funds or property by the Special Court upon conviction.
administration: Central Government (for rules), State Government (for implementation, court constitution, and appointments), Collector or District Magistrate (for prevention and local enforcement).
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect over other laws.
The definition of 'glorification' is broad and includes various acts aimed at perpetuating the honor or memory of a person who committed sati.
The Act specifically addresses the glorification of sati, not just its commission.
Provisions are made for the speedy trial of offences.

title: The Special Protection Group Act, 1988
purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for providing proximate security to the Prime Minister of India and former Prime Ministers of India and members of their immediate families, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to members of the Special Protection Group (SPG) wherever they may be. It provides proximate security to the Prime Minister and members of their immediate families residing with them, and to former Prime Ministers and members of their immediate families residing with them for a period of five years from the date they cease to hold office. The Act also covers situations where proximate security may be declined or withdrawn, with provisions for continued security if threat levels warrant it.

key_definitions.active duty: Any duty as a member of the Group during the period when they are posted to physically protect the Prime Minister of India and the members of their immediate family, or a former Prime Minister and the members of their immediate family, wherever they may be.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of the Group appointed under sub-section (1) of section 5.
key_definitions.Group: The Special Protection Group constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.member of the Group: A person appointed to the Group by the prescribed authority, whether before or after the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.proximate security: Protection provided from close quarters, during journey by road, rail, aircraft, watercraft or on foot or any other means of transport, and includes protection at functions, engagements, residence or halt, and comprises ring round teams, isolation cordons, sterile zones, and access control to the person or members of their immediate family.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Special Protection Group Act, 1988' and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'active duty', 'Director', 'Group', 'member of the Group', 'members of immediate family', 'prescribed', and 'proximate security'. It also clarifies that words not defined in the Act but defined in the Indian Penal Code shall have their respective meanings.
Declares that every member of the Group is subject to the provisions of this Act, irrespective of their location.

Establishes the Special Protection Group as an armed force of the Union for providing proximate security to the Prime Minister and members of their immediate family residing with them, and to former Prime Ministers and their immediate family members residing with them for five years post-premiership. It allows for the declination of proximate security and details the manner of Group constitution and service terms.

Vests the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Group in the Central Government. The command and supervision are vested in a Director appointed by the Central Government, who is assisted by other officers.

main_sections.section_title: Liability for service in and outside India
main_sections.description: States that every member of the Group is liable to serve anywhere in India as well as outside India.

main_sections.section_title: Members of the Group always on active duty
main_sections.description: Specifies that members of the Group, when not on leave or under suspension, are considered to be on active duty at all times and can be deployed as required by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation and withdrawal from the post
main_sections.description: Prohibits members of the Group from resigning or withdrawing from their duties without the prior written permission of the prescribed authority.
States that every member of the Group holds office during the pleasure of the President.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions respecting right to form associations, freedom of speech, etc.
main_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on members of the Group regarding joining trade unions, political associations, or other organizations without prior sanction. It also restricts communication with the press and publication of certain documents, with exceptions for bona fide discharge of duties or purely literary/artistic/scientific content. Members are also restricted from participating in political meetings or demonstrations.
Empowers the prescribed authority to terminate the appointment of any member of the Group in the public interest. Such termination is considered a discharge simpliciter and not dismissal or removal.
Provides for an appeal process for members aggrieved by an order under section 11. Appeals are to be made to a Board constituted by the Central Government, whose decision is final.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties conferable on members of the Group
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to direct, by order, that members of the Group may exercise or discharge specific powers or duties to give effect to the Act's provisions.

Makes it a duty for all Ministries, Departments, administrations, Missions, local authorities, and civil or military authorities to assist the Director or any member of the Group when called upon to do so.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under this Act
main_sections.description: Grants protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for any act done in good faith in pursuance of the Act, its orders, or rules.

Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions, covering matters such as the constitution of the Group, terms of service, prescribed authorities, nature of communications, and purposes for which members may not participate in meetings or demonstrations.
Mandates that all orders issued under section 13 and rules made under section 16 must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulments.

main_sections.section_title: Provision as to existing Special Protection Group
main_sections.description: Deems the Special Protection Group existing at the commencement of the Act as the Group constituted under the Act, and its members as appointed under the Act. It also validates actions taken prior to the commencement.

important_rules: Members of the Group are subject to this Act at all times and in all places.
Members of the Group cannot resign or withdraw from duty without prior written permission.
Members of the Group are restricted from joining political associations or communicating with the press without prior sanction.
Members of the Group are considered always on active duty unless on leave or under suspension.
Any Ministry, Department, or Authority is obligated to assist the SPG when called upon to do so.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and the Director of the Group, assisted by other officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Director and other appointed officers, with the overall superintendence and control of the Central Government. Enforcement also involves the obligation of other governmental and civil/military authorities to provide assistance.

rights: Right to appeal an order of termination of service to a Board constituted by the Central Government.
Members of immediate family of a former Prime Minister may be provided security if threat levels warrant it, even if proximate security is withdrawn from the former Prime Minister.
duties: To provide proximate security to the Prime Minister and former Prime Ministers and their immediate families.
To be always on active duty when not on leave or under suspension.
To serve in any part of India and outside India.
To act in aid of the Director or any member of the Group when called upon to do so by any Ministry, Department, or Authority.
obligations: To maintain secrecy and refrain from unauthorized communication with the press or public.
To adhere to restrictions regarding membership in political associations or other organizations.
To comply with the terms and conditions of service as prescribed.

key_procedures: Appointment of members to the Group by the prescribed authority.
Procedure for resignation or withdrawal from duty (requires prior written permission).
Procedure for termination of service by the prescribed authority in the public interest.
Appeals against termination orders are to be submitted to a Board constituted by the Central Government within thirty days.
The Central Government can issue general or special orders to confer powers and duties on members of the Group.
Rules are to be made by the Central Government for carrying out the Act's provisions, and these rules are to be laid before Parliament.
administration: The Central Government (overall superintendence, direction, and control); The Director of the Group (command and supervision), assisted by Inspectors General, Deputy Inspectors General, Assistant Inspectors General, and other officers.
important_notes: The proximate security for a former Prime Minister can be declined by them or their immediate family members.
If proximate security is withdrawn from a former Prime Minister, it is also withdrawn from their immediate family, unless a specific threat assessment warrants continued security for family members.
All words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Indian Penal Code, 1860, have their meanings as assigned in that Code.
Orders and rules made under the Act are subject to parliamentary review and potential modification or annulment.

title: The Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988
purpose: To prohibit benami transactions and the right to recover property held benami, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to all transactions and arrangements that fall under the definition of 'benami transaction'.

key_definitions.benami_property: Any property which is the subject matter of a benami transaction and also includes the proceeds from such property.
key_definitions.benami_transaction: A transaction or arrangement where property is transferred to or held by a person, but the consideration is provided by another person, and the property is held for the benefit of the person who provided the consideration. Exceptions include certain family arrangements (HUF, spouse, children, siblings, lineal ascendants/descendants), fiduciary capacity holdings, and fictitious name transactions or where the owner denies knowledge of ownership, or the provider of consideration is untraceable or fictitious. It does not include transactions allowed under Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, under specific conditions like consideration paid by the possessor, stamp duty paid, and contract registration.
key_definitions.benamidar: A person or a fictitious person in whose name the benami property is transferred or held, and includes a person who lends their name.
key_definitions.beneficial_owner: A person, whether their identity is known or not, for whose benefit the benami property is held by a benamidar.
key_definitions.property: Assets of any kind, whether movable or immovable, tangible or intangible, corporeal or incorporeal, including rights, interests, legal documents, or instruments evidencing title or interest, and property in its converted form, as well as its proceeds.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and commencement dates for different provisions (sections 3, 5, and 8 came into force at once; others are deemed to have come into force on May 19, 1988).

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Adjudicating Authority, Administrator, Appellate Tribunal, Approving Authority, attachment, authority, banking company, benami property, benami transaction, benamidar, beneficial owner, Board, director, executor, fair market value, firm, High Court, Initiating Officer, Member, notification, partner, partnership, person, prescribed, property, public financial institution, Special Court, transfer, and trustee.
Prohibits the entering into of benami transactions.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of the right to recover property held benami
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from claiming ownership of property held benami, or from recovering property held benami.

main_sections.section_title: Property held benami liable to confiscation
main_sections.description: States that any property held benami is liable to be confiscated by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on re-transfer of property by benamidar
main_sections.description: Prohibits a benamidar from re-transferring the benami property.
Establishes the Adjudicating Authority for the purposes of the Act.
Deals with the appointment and jurisdiction of authorities under the Act.
Outlines the powers vested in the authorities appointed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Notice and attachment of property involved in benami transaction
main_sections.description: Empowers authorities to issue notices and attach property involved in a benami transaction.
Provides for the process of adjudication of benami property.

main_sections.section_title: Confiscation and vesting of benami property
main_sections.description: Details the process of confiscation and vesting of benami property in the Central Government.
Provides for the establishment of an Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals against orders passed under the Act.
Lays down the procedure for filing appeals to the Appellate Tribunal.
Provides for appeals from the Appellate Tribunal to the High Court.
Provides for the establishment of Special Courts for the trial of offences under the Act.
Prescribes penalties for engaging in benami transactions.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Repeals certain provisions of other Acts and provides for savings.

important_rules: No person shall enter into any benami transaction (Section 3(1)).
No person shall be allowed to recover any property held benami (Section 4(1)).
Any property held benami shall be liable to confiscation by the Central Government (Section 5(1)).
A benamidar shall not re-transfer the benami property to the beneficial owner (Section 6(1)).
Property attached under this Act shall not be transferred or otherwise dealt with by any arrangement or contract, except as allowed by the attachment order (Section 24(3)).

penalties: Penalty for benami transaction: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to twenty-five per cent of the value of the property (Section 53(1)).
Penalty for false information: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees (Section 54).

Penalty for failure to comply with notices or furnish information: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to fifty lakh rupees or with both (Section 54A).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Adjudicating Authority, Initiating Officers, Approving Authorities, and Special Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation, attachment and confiscation of benami property, imposition of penalties, and prosecution of offenders in Special Courts. The Act also establishes an Appellate Tribunal for appeals.

rights: Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against orders of confiscation.
Right to appeal to the High Court against orders of the Appellate Tribunal.
Right to representation before the Appellate Tribunal.
duties: Duty to not enter into benami transactions.
Duty to not claim ownership of benami property.
Duty to comply with notices issued by authorities.
Duty to furnish information as required by authorities.
obligations: Obligation to report benami transactions.
Obligation to cooperate with investigations.
Obligation to pay penalties and fines as prescribed.

key_procedures: Issuance of notice and attachment of property suspected to be benami by the Initiating Officer.
Adjudication by the Adjudicating Authority to determine if the property is benami.
Confiscation and vesting of benami property in the Central Government if so determined.
Appeal process to the Appellate Tribunal and then to the High Court.
Prosecution of offenders in Special Courts.
administration: The Central Government, through various authorities and bodies like the Board of Direct Taxes, oversees the administration and implementation of the Act.
important_notes: The Act underwent significant amendments in 2016.
Certain provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and other related laws are referenced for definitions and procedures.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions will prevail over other laws in case of inconsistency.

title: The Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1988
purpose: To provide for detention in certain cases for the purpose of preventing illicit traffic in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of India, excluding the State of Jammu and Kashmir prior to its reorganization, but now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh. The act targets persons engaged in illicit traffic of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.

key_definitions.appropriate Government: The Central Government for orders made by it or its officers, and the State Government for orders made by it or its officers.
key_definitions.detention order: An order made under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.illicit traffic: Includes cultivating coca or opium poppy or cannabis plants; production, manufacture, possession, sale, purchase, transportation, warehousing, concealment, use, consumption, import/export (inter-State and into/from India), transhipment of narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances; dealing in other related activities; handling premises for such activities; financing, abetting, conspiring in, or harbouring persons engaged in such activities, excluding those permitted under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (initially excluding Jammu and Kashmir, later extended), and its deemed commencement date (July 4, 1988).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appropriate Government', 'customs airport', 'detention order', 'foreigner', 'illicit traffic', 'Indian customs waters', and 'State Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government or State Government, or their specially empowered officers, the power to issue detention orders against individuals to prevent them from engaging in illicit traffic of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. It also outlines reporting requirements for State Government detention orders to the Central Government and the timeline for communicating grounds of detention.
States that detention orders can be executed anywhere in India in the manner provided for the execution of arrest warrants under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate place and conditions of detention
main_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to specify the place and conditions of detention, including maintenance, interviews, communication, discipline, and punishments. It also allows for removal of persons from one detention place to another, with consent from the receiving State Government if it's a transfer between states.

Provides that if a detention order is based on multiple grounds, it will not be invalidated if one or more grounds are vague, non-existent, irrelevant, not connected, or otherwise invalid. The detention will be considered valid based on the remaining valid grounds.

main_sections.section_title: Detention orders not to be invalid or inoperative on certain grounds
main_sections.description: Ensures that detention orders are not invalidated simply because the person to be detained or the place of detention is outside the territorial jurisdiction of the issuing authority.

main_sections.section_title: Powers in relation to absconding persons
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the appropriate Government if a detained person absconds or conceals themselves, including reporting to a Magistrate (triggering provisions of CrPC related to absconding persons and their property) and ordering the person to appear before an officer. Failure to comply without a valid excuse is punishable.

Establishes the role of Advisory Boards in reviewing detention orders. It outlines the constitution of these boards, the requirement for references to be made to them within specific timeframes, their procedure for considering cases (including hearing the detenu), and the consequences of their opinions (sufficient cause for detention leads to confirmation, insufficient cause leads to release).

main_sections.section_title: Cases in which and circumstances under which persons may be detained for periods longer than three months without obtaining the opinion of Advisory Board
main_sections.description: Allows for detention periods longer than three months (up to six months) without the Advisory Board's opinion for persons whose detention is aimed at preventing illicit traffic, under certain circumstances and for a specified period (originally until July 31, 1999).
Specifies the maximum period for which a person can be detained under the Act.
Deals with the revocation of detention orders.
Provides for the temporary release of persons under detention.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Grants protection to actions taken in good faith by the Government or its officers under the Act.
Addresses the repeal of any previous law and savings provisions.

important_rules: Persons can be detained if the appropriate Government is satisfied that it is necessary to prevent them from engaging in illicit traffic of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances (Section 3(1)).
Grounds of detention must be communicated to the detenu as soon as possible, ordinarily within five days, and in exceptional circumstances within fifteen days of detention (Section 3(3)).
Detention orders can be executed at any place in India (Section 4).
Detained persons are subject to specified places and conditions of detention, and can be moved between detention locations (Section 5).
If a detention order is based on multiple grounds, it remains valid if at least one ground is valid (Section 6).
Detention orders are not invalidated by territorial jurisdiction issues (Section 7).

Absconding or concealing persons are subject to specific legal actions, including provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure for absconding offenders and potential penalties for non-compliance with appearance orders (Section 8).
The case of a detained person must be referred to an Advisory Board within five weeks of detention, unless specific exceptions apply (Section 9(b)).
Advisory Boards must submit their report within eleven weeks of detention (Section 9(c)).
Detenus are not allowed legal representation before the Advisory Board, except for the opinion part of the report, which is confidential (Section 9(e)).
If the Advisory Board opines sufficient cause for detention, the Government may confirm it; if insufficient cause, the order must be revoked and the person released (Section 9(f)).
Under specific circumstances and for a limited period, detention can extend beyond three months without an Advisory Board opinion (Section 10).

penalties: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both, for failure to comply with an order to appear before an officer (Section 8(1)(b)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government and State Governments, along with their empowered officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through detention orders, execution of these orders, regulation of detention conditions, powers related to absconding persons, and review by Advisory Boards. Enforcement also relies on provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure for execution and related matters. Offences under Section 8(1)(b) are cognizable.

rights: Right to have grounds of detention communicated as soon as possible (Section 3(3)).
Right to have their case reviewed by an Advisory Board (Article 22 of the Constitution, as implemented by Section 9).
Right to be released if the Advisory Board finds insufficient cause for detention (Section 9(f)).
Right to temporary release under certain conditions (Section 13).
Protection of actions taken in good faith (Section 14).
duties: Duty to comply with detention orders.
Duty to appear before authorities when ordered, if absconding or concealing (Section 8(1)(b)).
obligations: Obligation for State Governments to report detention orders to the Central Government within ten days (Section 3(2)).
Obligation to refer cases to Advisory Boards within five weeks of detention (Section 9(b)).

key_procedures: Issuance of a detention order by the appropriate Government or empowered officer if satisfied that preventive detention is necessary (Section 3(1)).
Communication of grounds of detention to the detenu within stipulated timeframes (Section 3(3)).
Execution of the detention order (Section 4).
Regulation of place and conditions of detention (Section 5).
Reference of the detention case to an Advisory Board within five weeks (Section 9(b)).
The Advisory Board's review process, including considering materials, seeking further information, and potentially hearing the detenu (Section 9(c)).
The Advisory Board's report on whether sufficient cause for detention exists (Section 9(c), 9(f)).
Government's action based on the Advisory Board's report: confirmation of detention if sufficient cause is found, or revocation and release if insufficient cause is found (Section 9(f)).
Procedure for dealing with absconding persons, including reporting to magistrates and issuing appearance orders (Section 8).
administration: Administered by the Central Government and State Governments, with specific roles for empowered officers and Advisory Boards.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1990, 1993, 1996, and 2001. Section 10, concerning extended detention periods without Advisory Board opinion, was originally valid until July 31, 1999.
The Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are now covered by the Act.

The Act is supplemental to the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, which deals with the substantive offences related to drugs and psychotropic substances. This Act focuses on preventive detention for illicit traffic.

title: The Jamia Millia Islamia Act, 1988
purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching University in the Union territory of Delhi and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. It also aims to dissolve the Jamia Millia Islamia Society, Delhi, and transfer all its properties and rights to the newly established University.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Jamia Millia Islamia University, located in New Delhi. It covers all aspects of the University's operations, including its objects, powers, authorities, officers, employees, students, and financial matters. The University is intended to be open to all, irrespective of sex, race, creed, caste, or class.

key_definitions.academic_staff: Categories of staff designated as academic staff by the Ordinances.
key_definitions.Board of Studies: The Board of Studies of the University.
key_definitions.Department: A Department of Studies, and includes a Centre of Studies and Research.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University, including teachers and other staff.
key_definitions.Hall: A unit of residence or of corporate life for the students of the University.
key_definitions.Institution: An Academic Institution, established or maintained by the University.
key_definitions.Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council): The Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council) of the University.
key_definitions.Majlis-i-Talimi (Academic Council): The Majlis-i-Talimi (Academic Council) of the University.
key_definitions.Principal: The head of an Institution, School or Polytechnic.
key_definitions.Statutes: The Statutes of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.Ordinances: The Ordinances of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.Regulations: The Regulations of the University for the time being in force.
key_definitions.teachers of the University: Professors, Readers, Lecturers and other persons appointed for imparting instruction or conducting research in the University.
key_definitions.University: The educational institution known as Jamia Millia Islamia, founded in 1920, registered as Jamia Millia Islamia Society in 1939, and declared as an institution deemed to be a University in 1962, and incorporated as a University under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including academic staff, officers, authorities, and types of University publications (Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations).

Establishes the Jamia Millia Islamia University and states its headquarters will be in New Delhi. It also declares that the current officers and members of the governing bodies will form a body corporate named Jamia Millia Islamia with perpetual succession and a common seal.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of the Jamia Millia Islamia Society and transfer of all property to the University
main_sections.description: Details the dissolution of the Jamia Millia Islamia Society and the transfer of all its movable and immovable property, rights, powers, and privileges to the University. It also covers the transfer of debts, liabilities, and obligations, and how existing documents and employment conditions will be treated.

Outlines the primary objectives of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge through instruction, research, and extension facilities. It emphasizes promoting innovation in education, studies in various disciplines, inter-disciplinary studies, national integration, secularism, and international understanding.

Lists the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and research, promoting religious and cultural studies, granting degrees, organizing adult education, conferring honorary degrees, establishing and maintaining institutions, appointing staff, cooperating with other bodies, awarding scholarships, managing property, and ensuring discipline.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creed
main_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all individuals regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, and prohibits any religious tests for admission or holding office. It allows for reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, physically handicapped persons, and women.

Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University. It grants the Visitor the right to inspect and inquire into the University's administration, finances, and activities, with provisions for notice to the University and the right of the University to make representations.
Lists the various officers of the University.
Deals with the office of the Chancellor.
Deals with the office of the Vice-Chancellor.
Deals with the office of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
Deals with the office of the Registrar.
Deals with the Deans of Faculties.
Deals with the office of the Finance Officer.
Covers any other officers of the University not explicitly mentioned.
Lists the various authorities of the University.
Deals with the constitution and functions of the Anjuman (Court).
Deals with the constitution and functions of the Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council).
Deals with the constitution and functions of the Majlis-i-Talimi (Academic Council).
Deals with the Planning Board of the University.
Covers any other authorities of the University.
Grants the University the power to make Statutes.
Prescribes the procedure for making Statutes.
Grants the University the power to make Ordinances.
Grants the University the power to make Regulations.
Requires the University to prepare and submit an annual report.
Requires the University to prepare and submit annual accounts.
Governs the terms and conditions of service for University employees.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedures for appeals and arbitration in disciplinary cases involving students.
Deals with the right of appeal for individuals within the University.
Covers the establishment and management of provident and pension funds for employees.

main_sections.section_title: Disputes as to constitution of University authorities and bodies
main_sections.description: Provides for the resolution of disputes concerning the constitution of University authorities and bodies.
Deals with the formation of various committees within the University.
Specifies the procedure for filling casual vacancies in University offices and bodies.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings of University authorities or bodies not invalidated by vacancies
main_sections.description: States that vacancies in University authorities or bodies do not invalidate their proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith by individuals associated with the University.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of proof of University record
main_sections.description: Prescribes the method of proving University records.

main_sections.section_title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates the publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their laying before Parliament.
Grants power to the Central Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Contains provisions for the transition from the previous legal framework to this Act.

important_rules: University shall be open to persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class, without any religious tests for admission or holding office.
The President of India shall be the Visitor of the University and has the right to inspect and inquire into University affairs.
The University shall disseminate and advance knowledge, promote innovations in education, and foster national integration, secularism, and international understanding.
The University has powers to provide instruction, conduct research, grant degrees, organize extra-mural studies, confer honorary degrees, and establish and maintain institutions.
Employees employed before the commencement of the Act shall continue their employment with the University on the same terms and conditions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University itself, through its various authorities (e.g., Executive Council, Academic Council), and potentially the Visitor (President of India) in specific oversight capacities. The Central Government has powers to remove difficulties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations made by the University. Disciplinary measures can be taken against employees and students. The Visitor's oversight and inquiry powers also serve as an enforcement mechanism.

rights: Right of students and teachers to receive instruction, research, and extension facilities.
Right to appeal in disciplinary cases and other matters.
Right of the University to admit persons of any sex, race, creed, caste, or class.
Right of the University to confer degrees and academic distinctions.
Right of employees to continue employment on existing terms and conditions.
Right to make representations to the Visitor during inspections or inquiries.
duties: Duty of the University to provide instruction, research, and extension facilities.
Duty to promote innovation, national integration, secularism, and international understanding.
Duty to be open to all and not impose religious tests.
Duty to prepare and submit annual reports and accounts.
Duty to regulate and enforce discipline among employees and students.
Duty to provide for the health and general welfare of employees and students.
obligations: Obligation to dissolve the Jamia Millia Islamia Society and transfer all its assets and liabilities.
Obligation to apply transferred properties to the University's objects.
Obligation to discharge debts and liabilities of the former Society.
Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Obligation to ensure University remains open to all classes, castes, and creeds.

key_procedures: Appointment of officers and staff through relevant University authorities.
Making of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations according to prescribed procedures.
Conducting examinations, evaluations, and other testing methods for granting degrees and diplomas.
Process for inspection and inquiry by the Visitor, including the University's right to make representations.
Procedure for appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
Filling of casual vacancies in University authorities and bodies.
Publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and laying them before Parliament.
administration: The administration of the University is vested in its various authorities, including the Anjuman (Court), Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council), and Majlis-i-Talimi (Academic Council), as well as its officers like the Amir-i-Jamia (Chancellor), Shaikh-ul-Jamia (Vice-Chancellor), and Registrar. The Central Government oversees certain aspects, particularly through the Visitor and the power to remove difficulties.
important_notes: The Act incorporates the historical Jamia Millia Islamia, which was founded in 1920, registered as a Society in 1939, and deemed a University in 1962.
The Act provides for reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, physically handicapped persons, and women, notwithstanding the general principle of openness.
Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations made under the Act must be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.

title: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
purpose: To prevent the commission of offences of atrocities against the members of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, to provide for Special Courts and Exclusive Special Courts for the trial of such offences and for the relief and rehabilitation of the victims of such offences and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to offences committed against members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.dependent: The spouse, children, parents, brother and sister of the victim, who are dependent wholly or mainly on such victim for his support and maintenance.
key_definitions.economic_boycott: A refusal to deal with, work for hire or do business with other person; or to deny opportunities including access to services or contractual opportunities for rendering service for consideration; or to refuse to do anything on the terms on which things would be commonly done in the ordinary course of business; or to abstain from the professional or business relations that one would maintain with other person.
key_definitions.exclusive_special_court: The Exclusive Special Court established under sub-section (1) of section 14 exclusively to try the offences under this Act.
key_definitions.forest_rights: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007).
key_definitions.manual_scavenger: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (25 of 2013).
key_definitions.public_servant: A public servant as defined under section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), as well as any other person deemed to be a public servant under any other law for the time being in force and includes any person acting in his official capacity under the Central Government or the State Government, as the case may be.
key_definitions.scheduled_castes_and_scheduled_tribes: Shall have the meanings assigned to them respectively under clause (24) and clause (25) of article 366 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.special_court: A Court of Session specified as a Special Court in section 14.
key_definitions.special_public_prosecutor: A Public Prosecutor specified as a Special Public Prosecutor or an advocate referred to in section 15.
key_definitions.schedule: The Schedule appended to this Act.
key_definitions.social_boycott: A refusal to permit a person to render to other person or receive from him any customary service or to abstain from social relations that one would maintain with other person or to isolate him from others.
key_definitions.victim: Any individual who falls within the definition of the “Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes” under clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 2, and who has suffered or experienced physical, mental, psychological, emotional or monetary harm or harm to his property as a result of the commission of any offence under this Act and includes his relatives, legal guardian and legal heirs.
key_definitions.witness: Any person who is acquainted with the facts and circumstances, or is in possession of any information or has knowledge necessary for the purpose of investigation, inquiry or trial of any crime involving an offence under this Act, and who is or may be required to give information or make a statement or produce any document during investigation, inquiry or trial of such case and includes a victim of such offence.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the procedure for its commencement.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'atrocity', 'Code', 'dependent', 'economic boycott', 'Exclusive Special Court', 'forest rights', 'manual scavenger', 'public servant', 'Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes', 'Special Court', 'Special Public Prosecutor', 'schedule', 'social boycott', 'victim', and 'witness'.

Details the various offences constituting 'atrocities' and their corresponding punishments. This section lists a wide range of acts that are considered atrocities when committed against members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes.
Prescribes punishment for public servants who neglect their duties under the Act.
Provides for enhanced punishment in case of subsequent convictions for offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of certain provisions of the Indian Penal Code
main_sections.description: Specifies that certain provisions of the Indian Penal Code are applicable to offences under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Forfeiture of property of certain persons
main_sections.description: Allows for the forfeiture of property of persons convicted of certain offences under the Act.
Lays down presumptions that may be drawn in relation to offences committed under the Act.
Grants powers to the State Government to confer certain powers on police officers.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of person likely to commit offence
main_sections.description: Empowers authorities to take preventive action by ordering the removal of persons likely to commit offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure on failure of person to remove himself from area and enter thereon after removal
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure to be followed when a person fails to comply with an order of removal under section 10.

main_sections.section_title: Taking measurements and photographs, etc., of persons against whom order under section 10 is made
main_sections.description: Allows for the taking of measurements and photographs of persons against whom an order under section 10 is made.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for non-compliance of order under section 10
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for non-compliance with orders issued under section 10.

main_sections.section_title: Special Court and Exclusive Special Court
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and jurisdiction of Special Courts and Exclusive Special Courts for the trial of offences under this Act.
Deals with the provisions related to appeals against judgments or orders of Special Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Special Public Prosecutor and Exclusive Public Prosecutor
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Special Public Prosecutors and Exclusive Public Prosecutors for conducting cases under the Act.
Enshrines the rights of victims and witnesses of atrocities, including protection and support during and after the legal proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to impose collective fine
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to impose a collective fine on the inhabitants of an area where certain offences have been committed.

main_sections.section_title: Preventive action to be taken by the law and order machinery
main_sections.description: Mandates the law and order machinery to take preventive action to protect members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

main_sections.section_title: Section 438 of the Code not to apply to persons committing an offence under the Act
main_sections.description: Excludes the applicability of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (anticipatory bail) to persons accused of offences under this Act.
Specifies that no inquiry or approval is required for certain actions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Section 360 of the Code or the provisions of the Probation of Offenders Act not to apply to persons guilty of an offence under the Act
main_sections.description: Excludes the application of Section 360 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Probation of Offenders Act to persons convicted of offences under this Act.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Government to ensure effective implementation of the Act
main_sections.description: Places a duty on the Government to ensure the effective implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Whoever, not being a member of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe, commits any of the acts listed in Section 3 against a member of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe, shall be punishable.
Public servants who neglect their duties under the Act are liable for punishment.
Enhanced punishment is prescribed for subsequent convictions of offences under the Act.
Anticipatory bail (Section 438 of the Code) is not applicable to persons accused of offences under this Act.
The Act overrides other laws, meaning its provisions will prevail in case of inconsistency.
The Government has a duty to ensure the effective implementation of the Act.

penalties: Punishment for offences of atrocities (detailed in Section 3), which can include imprisonment and fine.
Punishment for neglect of duties by public servants (Section 4).
Enhanced punishment for subsequent convictions (Section 5).
Penalty for non-compliance of orders under section 10 (Section 13).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Law and order machinery, including police, and Special Courts/Exclusive Special Courts established under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation of offences, trial by Special Courts, imposition of penalties, preventive actions, and ensuring the rights of victims and witnesses.

rights: Right to be protected from atrocities.
Right to relief and rehabilitation for victims (as per Section 15A).
Rights of witnesses, including protection (as per Section 15A).
Right to access justice through Special Courts.
duties: Duty of the Government to ensure effective implementation of the Act (Section 21).
Duty of law and order machinery to take preventive action (Section 17).
obligations: Obligation of individuals not to commit atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Obligations of public servants to perform their duties diligently to prevent atrocities.

key_procedures: Investigation of offences of atrocities by the police.
Trial of offences by Special Courts or Exclusive Special Courts.
Taking of preventive action by law and order machinery (e.g., removal of persons likely to commit offences).
Appeals against judgments or orders of Special Courts.
Procedure for dealing with persons who fail to comply with orders of removal.
administration: While the Act is enacted by Parliament, its implementation involves State Governments, the Central Government (for making rules), and the judiciary (Special Courts and Exclusive Special Courts).
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2015 and 2018.
The application of the Act was extended to the whole of India after the omission of the exception for the State of Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.

The Act explicitly excludes the application of anticipatory bail (Section 438 of the Code) and provisions of the Probation of Offenders Act to persons guilty of offences under this Act, indicating the seriousness with which these offences are treated.

title: The Remittances of Foreign Exchange and Investment in Foreign Exchange Bonds (Immunities and Exemptions) Act, 1991
purpose: To provide certain immunities to persons receiving remittances in foreign exchange and to persons owning Foreign Exchange Bonds, and for certain exemptions from direct taxes in relation to such remittances and bonds, with the objective of attracting large inflows of foreign exchange due to a difficult balance of payments position.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to remittances made in foreign exchange from persons resident outside India to persons resident in India, and to investment in Foreign Exchange Bonds issued by the State Bank of India, made by non-resident Indians and overseas corporate bodies. The immunities and exemptions are primarily related to the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, Income-tax Act, 1961, Wealth-tax Act, 1957, and Gift-tax Act, 1958.

key_definitions.recipient: A person as defined in clause (31) of section 2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, who receives a remittance under Chapter II.
key_definitions.remittance: A remittance made in foreign exchange by a person resident outside India to a person resident in India, on or after the Act's commencement date but before the specified date. It can be in the form of draft, traveller's cheques, cheques drawn on banks outside India, telegraphic transfers, mail transfers, money orders, or by way of transfer from specific Non-resident accounts.
key_definitions.specified date: December 1, 1991, or such other later date as the Central Government may specify by notification.
key_definitions.Foreign Exchange Bonds: Bonds issued by the State Bank of India, wherein investment is made on or after the Act's commencement date but before the specified date, according to a scheme specified by the Reserve Bank of India.
key_definitions.non-resident Indian: An individual, being a citizen of India or a person of Indian origin, who is resident outside India.
key_definitions.overseas corporate body: An institution, association, or body, incorporated or not, established under the laws of a country outside India, wherein any non-resident Indian has an interest.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its territorial applicability, which is to the whole of India.
Defines terms specific to Chapter II concerning remittances of foreign exchange, including 'recipient', 'remittance', and 'specified date'.

Provides immunities to recipients of remittances, preventing disclosure of nature/source of remittance, barring inquiries/investigations on that ground, and making the fact of receiving a remittance inadmissible as evidence, with specific exceptions.

main_sections.section_title: Remittances not to be taken into account in certain cases (Chapter II)
main_sections.description: Clarifies that remittances received under Chapter II are not to be taken into account for proceedings under the Income-tax Act, 1961, and will not form part of assets for Wealth-tax Act, 1957, for assessment years before April 1, 1992.
Defines terms specific to Chapter III concerning investment in Foreign Exchange Bonds, including 'Foreign Exchange Bonds', 'non-resident Indian', 'overseas corporate body', and 'specified date'.

Provides immunities to owners of Foreign Exchange Bonds and recipients of gifts of such bonds, preventing disclosure of investment source/nature, barring inquiries/investigations, and making ownership inadmissible as evidence, with specific exceptions.

main_sections.section_title: Foreign Exchange Bonds not to be taken into account in certain cases (Chapter III)
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Income-tax Act, Wealth-tax Act, and Gift-tax Act provisions will not apply to interest accruing on Foreign Exchange Bonds, to the bonds themselves, or to gifts of such bonds under certain conditions.

important_rules: Rule 1: Recipients of foreign exchange remittances under this Act are granted immunity from disclosing the nature and source of such remittances for any purpose.
Rule 2: No inquiry or investigation shall be commenced against a recipient of a remittance under this Act on the ground that they received such remittance.
Rule 3: The fact of receiving a remittance under this Act shall not be admissible as evidence in any proceedings related to offences or penalties.
Rule 4: Foreign Exchange Bonds are exempt from the provisions of the Wealth-tax Act, 1957, and Gift-tax Act, 1958.
Rule 5: Interest accruing in relation to Foreign Exchange Bonds is exempt from the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated for the immunities and exemptions themselves, but the underlying laws for foreign exchange and direct taxes would be enforced by their respective authorities. The Reserve Bank of India is involved in specifying schemes for remittances and bonds.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The immunities and exemptions provided by this Act limit the scope of enforcement actions under other specified laws (e.g., Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, Income-tax Act, Wealth-tax Act) regarding the remittances and bonds covered by the Act.

rights: Right of recipients of remittances to claim immunity regarding the disclosure of the nature and source of such remittances.
Right of owners of Foreign Exchange Bonds to claim immunity regarding the disclosure of the nature and source of their investment in such bonds.
duties: Duty to comply with schemes notified by the Reserve Bank of India for receiving remittances and investing in Foreign Exchange Bonds.

Duty to ensure that any foreign exchange required to be brought into India under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, or Income-tax Act, 1961, is brought within the specified period, as immunities do not apply if this condition is not met.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: A scheme is to be notified by the Reserve Bank of India for the purposes of receiving remittances under Chapter II. Recipients must comply with this scheme to claim immunity.
