Procedure 2: A scheme is to be notified by the Reserve Bank of India for the issuance of Foreign Exchange Bonds by the State Bank of India under Chapter III. Investment must be made according to this scheme to benefit from immunities.
Procedure 3: Schemes notified by the Reserve Bank of India under Chapters II and III must be laid before each House of Parliament by the Central Government.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but the Reserve Bank of India plays a key role in notifying schemes. The Central Government is responsible for laying these schemes before Parliament.
important_notes: The immunities and exemptions provided by this Act do not apply to foreign exchange that was required to be brought into India under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, or the Income-tax Act, 1961, if the stipulated period for bringing it into India has not expired.

Prosecution for offences under specific chapters of the Indian Penal Code, the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987, or the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, are exceptions to the immunities granted.
Enforcement of civil liability is also an exception to the immunities.

The Income-tax Act, 1961, will still apply to any income that accrues or arises to the recipient from the amount of the remittance itself, even though the remittance itself is not taken into account for assessment.
The Act aims to attract foreign exchange inflow to address a difficult balance of payments position.

title: The Cess and Other Taxes on Minerals (Validation) Act, 1992
purpose: To validate the imposition and collection of cesses and certain other taxes on minerals under certain State laws, which had been struck down by courts.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It specifically validates cesses and taxes on minerals imposed under certain State laws listed in the Schedule. The validation applies to actions taken and things done under these laws, including rules made, notifications issued, and taxes realised, up to April 4, 1991.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and the date it is deemed to have come into force (February 15, 1992).

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain State laws and actions taken and things done thereunder
main_sections.description: This section validates specified State laws and all actions taken, things done, rules made, notifications issued, and taxes realised under those laws. It declares these as valid as if enacted by Parliament and remaining in force until April 4, 1991. It also bars suits for the refund of taxes realised under these laws, but allows claims for refunds of amounts paid in excess of the due amount.

This section repeals the Cess and Other Taxes on Minerals (Validation) Ordinance, 1992, and states that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: State laws listed in the Schedule, relating to cesses or other taxes on minerals, are deemed to have been validly enacted by Parliament and in force up to April 4, 1991.
All actions, rules, notifications, and tax collections under these State laws are deemed valid.
No suit or proceeding can be maintained for refund of taxes realised under these laws, except for amounts paid in excess of what was due.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The text does not explicitly name an enforcement authority. However, the validation of laws implies that actions under those laws would be governed by the respective State legal frameworks.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act validates past actions and collections, effectively preventing challenges to them in courts. The enforcement of the underlying State laws would continue as before, subject to this validation.

rights: Right to claim refund of any cess or tax paid in excess of the amount due under the validated State laws.

key_procedures: No specific new procedures are introduced. The Act's primary function is to validate existing State laws and actions.
The procedure for claiming a refund of excess tax paid is implicitly established by sub-section (3) of Section 2.
administration: The administration of the underlying State laws would fall under the respective State governments. The Act itself does not establish a new central administrative body.
important_notes: The Act retroactively validates State laws and actions concerning cesses and taxes on minerals.
The validation extends only up to April 4, 1991.
The Act aims to protect State revenues by preventing large-scale refunds of taxes already collected.
The Schedule lists specific State Acts that are covered by this validation.

title: The Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) Act, 1992
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Special Court for the trial of offences relating to transactions in securities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to offences relating to transactions in securities, specifically concerning persons involved in such transactions between April 1, 1991, and June 6, 1992. It establishes a Special Court with exclusive jurisdiction over these matters and the properties attached related to these transactions.

key_definitions.Code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.Custodian: A person appointed under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.securities: Includes shares, scrips, stocks, bonds, debentures, debenture stock, units of the Unit Trust of India or any other mutual fund or other marketable securities of a like nature in or of any incorporated company or other body corporate; Government securities; and rights or interests in securities.
key_definitions.Special Court: The Special Court established under sub-section (1) of section 5.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it is deemed to have come into force on June 6, 1992.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Code', 'Custodian', 'securities', and 'Special Court'.

Empowers the Central Government to appoint one or more Custodians. It outlines the Custodian's power to notify names of persons involved in securities transactions offences and the subsequent attachment of their property.

main_sections.section_title: Contracts entered into fraudulently may be cancelled
main_sections.description: Grants the Custodian the power to cancel fraudulent contracts or agreements related to the property of a notified person, after providing an opportunity to be heard. It also specifies the procedure for filing objections to the Custodian's actions with the Special Court.
Mandates the establishment of a Special Court by the Central Government and outlines its composition, consisting of one or more sitting Judges of the High Court nominated by the Chief Justice.

main_sections.section_title: Cognizance of cases by Special Court
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Special Court shall take cognizance of or try cases instituted before it or transferred to it.
Establishes the exclusive jurisdiction of the Special Court for prosecutions related to offences specified in sub-section (2) of section 3, and mandates the transfer of pending prosecutions to it.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of Special Court
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure to be followed by the Special Court during trials, which is generally that for warrant cases before a magistrate, and grants it the powers of a Court of Session. It also allows for adopting procedures consistent with natural justice for other matters.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction, powers, authority and procedure of Special Court in civil matters
main_sections.description: Grants the Special Court jurisdiction over matters and claims related to attached property or arising from securities transactions during the specified period. It also details the transfer of pending civil suits and specifies that the Special Court will be guided by principles of natural justice, not strictly bound by the Code of Civil Procedure.
Provides for appeals from judgments, decrees, sentences, or orders (not interlocutory) of the Special Court to the Supreme Court, both on facts and law, within a 30-day period.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws for the matters it deals with.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous enactment and savings provisions.

important_rules: Property of a person notified under section 3(2) shall stand attached simultaneously with the issue of the notification.

The Custodian may cancel any contract or agreement entered into fraudulently or to defeat the provisions of the Act, relating to the property of a notified person, after giving parties an opportunity to be heard.
Prosecutions for offences referred to in section 3(2) shall be instituted only in the Special Court and any pending prosecutions shall be transferred to it.
The Special Court shall follow the procedure prescribed by the Code of Criminal Procedure for the trial of warrant cases before a magistrate.
Appeals from the Special Court lie to the Supreme Court within 30 days of the judgment, sentence or order.

penalties: The Act empowers the Special Court to pass any sentence authorized by law for the punishment of the offence of which a person is convicted (Section 9(3)). Specific penalties are not detailed in the provided excerpt but are implied to be determined by the nature of the offences related to securities transactions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Special Court is the primary authority for the trial and enforcement of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of a Special Court with exclusive jurisdiction, the attachment and management of properties, and the trial of specified offences. The Custodian plays a key role in identifying and attaching properties. Appeals are heard by the Supreme Court.

rights: Parties to a contract or agreement cancelled by the Custodian have the right to a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
Any person aggrieved by a notification, cancellation, or order of the Custodian can file an objection with the Special Court.
An appellant has the right to appeal to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree, sentence or order (not interlocutory) of the Special Court, on facts and law.
duties: The Custodian has a duty to investigate and notify persons involved in securities transaction offences.
The Special Court has a duty to try cases instituted or transferred to it, and to deal with them according to law and principles of natural justice.
The Central Government has a duty to establish the Special Court.
obligations: Persons involved in offences relating to transactions in securities within the specified period are subject to the provisions of this Act, including potential attachment of property and trial by the Special Court.
Parties to contracts that are investigated for fraud must be given an opportunity to be heard before cancellation.

Parties involved in suits or legal proceedings before the commencement of the Amendment Act of 1994, that fall under the Special Court's jurisdiction, are obligated to have their cases transferred to the Special Court.

key_procedures: Notification of persons involved in securities transactions offences by the Custodian.
Attachment of property of notified persons.
Cancellation of fraudulent contracts or agreements by the Custodian after providing an opportunity to be heard.
Filing of objections to Custodian's actions with the Special Court within a specified period.
Trial of cases by the Special Court following procedures similar to warrant cases, with powers of a Court of Session.
Transfer of pending cases related to securities transactions offences to the Special Court.
Appeals from the Special Court to the Supreme Court within 30 days.
administration: The Central Government establishes and oversees the Special Court. The Custodian is appointed by the Central Government and acts under the direction of the Special Court.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on June 6, 1992.
The Special Court's jurisdiction in civil matters, established by the 1994 Amendment Act, has overriding effect, meaning no other court can exercise jurisdiction in such matters.
The Special Court is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but guided by principles of natural justice in civil matters.
The Supreme Court may entertain appeals after the expiry of the 30-day period if sufficient cause is shown.

title: The Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992
purpose: To provide for the regulation of production, supply and distribution of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles and infant foods with a view to the protection and promotion of breast-feeding and ensuring the proper use of infant foods and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to the production, supply, and distribution of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, and infant foods. It also governs related advertisements, educational materials, and practices within the health care system.

key_definitions.advertisement: Includes any notice, circular, label, wrapper or any other document or visible representation or announcement made by means of any light, sound, smoke or gas or by means of electronic transmission or by audio or visual transmission.
key_definitions.container: Means a box, bottle, casket, tin, can, barrel, case, tube, receptacle, sack, wrapper or other thing in which any infant milk substitute, feeding bottle or infant food is placed or packed for sale or distribution.
key_definitions.feeding bottle: Means any bottle or receptacle used for the purpose of feeding infant milk substitutes, and includes a teat and a valve attached or capable of being attached to such bottle or receptacle.
key_definitions.health care system: Means an institution or organisation engaged, either directly or indirectly, in health care for mothers, infants or pregnant women, and includes a health worker in private practice, a pharmacy, drug store and any association of health workers.
key_definitions.health worker: Means a person engaged in health care for mothers, infants or pregnant women.
key_definitions.infant food: Means any food (by whatever name called) being marketed or otherwise represented as a complement to mother’s milk to meet the growing nutritional needs of the infant after the age of six months and up to the age of two years.
key_definitions.infant milk substitute: Means any food being marketed or otherwise represented as a partial or total replacement for mother’s milk for infant up to the age of two years.
key_definitions.label: Means a display of written, marked, stamped, printed or graphic matter affixed to, or appearing upon, any container.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.promotion: Means to employ directly or indirectly any method of encouraging any person to purchase or use infant milk substitute, feeding bottle or infant food.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of India), and outlines the commencement provision which is dependent on a notification by the Central Government.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as advertisement, container, feeding bottle, health care system, health worker, infant food, infant milk substitute, label, prescribed, and promotion.

main_sections.section_title: Certain prohibitions in relation to infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles and infant foods
main_sections.description: Prohibits advertising or participating in the publication of advertisements for the distribution, sale, or supply of these products. It also forbids creating the impression that these substitutes are equivalent to or better than mother's milk, and prohibits promotion of these products.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of incentives for the use or sale of infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles or infant foods
main_sections.description: Prohibits the supply or distribution of samples, gifts of utensils or other articles, contacting pregnant women or mothers of infants, or offering any other inducement for the purpose of promoting the use or sale of these products.

main_sections.section_title: Donations of infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles or equipment or materials relating thereto
main_sections.description: Restricts the donation or distribution of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, or infant foods, except to orphanages. It also limits the donation of informational or educational material unless it's through the health care system under prescribed conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Information on containers and labels of infant milk substitutes or infant foods
main_sections.description: Mandates that containers and labels of infant milk substitutes or infant foods must clearly indicate specific particulars, including the superiority of mother's milk, the need for health worker advice, warnings against exclusive use, preparation instructions, ingredients, composition, storage conditions, batch number, and expiry date. It also prohibits certain imagery, words like 'humanised' or 'maternalised', and other phrases designed to increase saleability.

main_sections.section_title: Educational and other materials relating to feeding of infants to contain certain particulars
main_sections.description: Requires educational and promotional materials related to infant feeding to include information on the benefits of breastfeeding, its preparation and continuation, the harmful effects of bottle feeding, difficulties in reverting to breastfeeding, financial and social implications of using substitutes, and health hazards of improper use. It also mandates details like printing date and publisher's name. Crucially, such materials cannot be used to promote the use or sale of infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles.

Regulates the use of the health care system for promoting infant milk substitutes. It prohibits displaying placards or distributing promotional materials. It also prevents payments to health workers for promotion and restricts demonstrations of feeding with substitutes to mothers by non-health workers. Distribution to mothers unable to breastfeed or afford substitutes is permitted only by health care institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Inducement to health worker for promoting use of infant milk substitutes, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits offering or giving financial inducements or gifts to health workers or their families for promoting the use of infant milk substitutes. It also prohibits producers from contributing financially to health workers or their associations for various purposes like seminars, research, or sponsorships.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision relating to employees of person who produces, supplies, distributes or sells infant milk substitutes, etc.
main_sections.description: This section, though only partially provided in the text, likely deals with the responsibilities and conduct of employees of entities involved in the production, supply, distribution, or sale of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, and infant foods.

main_sections.section_title: Standards of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles or infant foods
main_sections.description: This section likely deals with establishing and enforcing standards for infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, and infant foods.
This section likely grants authorities the power to enter premises and conduct searches in relation to the enforcement of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to seize infant milk substitutes, etc., or containers thereof
main_sections.description: This section likely empowers authorities to seize prohibited items and their containers.
This section likely outlines the process and grounds for confiscation of seized items.

main_sections.section_title: Power to give option to pay cost in lieu of confiscation
main_sections.description: This section likely provides an option for owners to pay the cost of the seized items as an alternative to confiscation.

main_sections.section_title: Confiscation not to interfere with other punishments
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that confiscation does not preclude other forms of punishment under the Act.
This section likely details the process of adjudication in cases of violations of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Giving of opportunity to the owner of the seized infant milk substitute or feeding bottle or infant food or container thereof
main_sections.description: This section ensures that the owner of seized items is given an opportunity to be heard before any action is taken.
This section likely outlines the procedure for appealing decisions made under the Act.
This section specifies the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act.
This section likely deals with how offences under the Act are to be taken cognizance of by courts.
This section likely addresses the liability of companies for offences committed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable and bailable
main_sections.description: This section clarifies the nature of offences under the Act, specifically whether they are cognizable (arrestable without warrant) and bailable.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: This section provides protection against legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith in the execution of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act 37 of 1954 not barred
main_sections.description: This section likely clarifies that the provisions of another Act (likely related to food adulteration) are not superseded by this Act.
This section grants the government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall advertise, promote, or give an impression that infant milk substitutes and infant foods are equivalent to or better than mother's milk.
No person shall supply samples, gifts, or offer inducements to promote the use or sale of infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles.
Donations of infant milk substitutes or infant foods are restricted to orphanages, and informational material can only be distributed through the health care system under specified conditions.

Containers and labels of infant milk substitutes or infant foods must display 'important notice' and specific information including the superiority of mother's milk, the need for health worker advice, and warnings about health hazards.
Educational materials must highlight the benefits of breastfeeding and the harms of substitutes, and cannot be used to promote sales of such products.
The health care system cannot be used for displaying placards or distributing promotional materials for infant milk substitutes. Health workers cannot receive payments for promotion.
Producers or distributors shall not offer financial inducements or gifts to health workers or their families for promoting the use of infant milk substitutes.

penalties: The Act specifies penalties for contravening its provisions (detailed in Section 20, though the exact nature of penalties is not provided in the extract).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely Central Government agencies and designated authorities empowered under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, search, and seizure of prohibited items, adjudication of offences, and imposition of penalties.

rights: Mothers have a right to information about the benefits of breastfeeding and the hazards of substitutes.
Health workers have a right to receive scientific and factual information related to infant feeding.
duties: Producers, suppliers, and distributors have a duty to comply with all regulations regarding production, supply, distribution, labeling, and promotion.
Health workers have a duty to provide accurate information regarding infant feeding and to not be induced for promotional purposes.
Manufacturers have a duty to ensure containers and labels provide all mandated information and warnings.
Entities involved in producing or distributing these products have a duty to not offer inducements to health workers.
obligations: Obligation to clearly label infant milk substitutes and infant foods with specific warnings and instructions.
Obligation to ensure that all promotional and educational materials are factual and do not mislead regarding breastfeeding.
Obligation for producers and distributors to refrain from any form of incentivization for the promotion of their products.

key_procedures: Notification by the Central Government to bring the Act into force.
Prescribing of specific requirements for labels and containers.
Procedures for donation and distribution of infant milk substitutes and related materials.
Processes for carrying out entry, search, and seizure by authorized personnel.
Adjudication of offences and appeals against decisions.
Making of rules by the government to implement the Act.
administration: The administration of the Act is likely overseen by the Ministry of Women and Child Development and potentially other relevant ministries such as the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, along with enforcement by food safety and other authorized bodies.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 2003 by the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Food (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Amendment Act, 2003 (38 of 2003), and also impacted by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (34 of 2006).
Certain definitions and provisions have been substituted or inserted by these amending acts, indicating ongoing regulatory adjustments.
The Act aims to protect and promote breastfeeding, emphasizing that mother's milk is best for babies.

title: The Code on Wages, 2019
purpose: To amend and consolidate the laws relating to wages and bonus and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to various establishments and employees as defined within the Act.

key_definitions.employee: Any person employed on wages by an establishment to do any skilled, semi-skilled or unskilled, manual, operational, supervisory, managerial, administrative, technical or clerical work for hire or reward, excluding apprentices and members of the Armed Forces.
key_definitions.employer: A person who employs one or more employees in his establishment, including the occupier of a factory, the ultimate authority controlling an establishment, contractors, and legal representatives of a deceased employer.
key_definitions.wages: All remuneration expressed in terms of money, including basic pay, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance, payable to a person employed in respect of his employment or work done, but excluding certain components like bonus not forming part of remuneration, value of amenities, employer's contributions to pension/provident fund, conveyance allowance, special expense allowances, house rent allowance, remuneration under awards/settlements, overtime allowance, commission, gratuity, and retrenchment compensation.
key_definitions.appropriate_government: In relation to Central Government establishments (railways, mines, oil fields, major ports, etc.) or corporations established by a Central Act, it's the Central Government. For all other establishments, it's the State Government.
key_definitions.establishment: Any place where any industry, trade, business, manufacture or occupation is carried on, including Government establishments.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Code on Wages, 2019', states its extent as the whole of India, and outlines that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'accounting year', 'Advisory Board', 'appropriate Government', 'company', 'contractor', 'contract labour', 'employee', 'employer', 'establishment', 'wages', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of discrimination on ground of gender
main_sections.description: Prohibits discrimination in employment or conditions of employment on the basis of gender.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of minimum rate of wages
main_sections.description: Deals with the requirement to pay minimum rates of wages to employees.
Specifies provisions related to wages for employees who undertake overtime work.
Outlines the permissible methods for paying wages to employees.

main_sections.section_title: Deductions which may be made from wages
main_sections.description: Lists the specific types of deductions that can legally be made from an employee's wages.
Specifies the conditions and eligibility criteria for receiving bonus payments.

main_sections.section_title: Central Advisory Board and State Advisory Boards
main_sections.description: Establishes the Central Advisory Board and State Advisory Boards for advising on matters related to wages and bonus.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Inspector-cum-Facilitators and their powers
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Inspector-cum-Facilitators and outlines their powers and functions.
Details the penalties that can be imposed for various offences committed under the Code.
Deals with the repeal of certain existing laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Employees must be paid at least the minimum rate of wages fixed under the Act (Section 5).
Wages shall be paid in coin or currency or in legal tender of India, or by crediting to the bank account of the employee (Section 15).
Deductions from wages are permissible only under specific circumstances outlined in the Act (Section 18).
Employers are prohibited from discriminating against employees on the ground of gender in matters of employment or conditions of employment (Section 3).
The Act defines 'wages' to include basic pay, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance, but excludes certain other payments (Section 2(y)).
Specific provisions exist for the payment of overtime work and the eligibility and computation of bonus (Chapters II, III, and IV).

penalties: Penalties for offenses range from fines to imprisonment, depending on the nature and repetition of the offense (Section 54).
Penalties can be imposed on companies for offenses committed by them (Section 55).
Power of officers of the appropriate Government to impose penalties in certain cases (Section 53).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The 'appropriate Government' (Central Government or State Government, depending on the establishment) and 'Inspector-cum-Facilitators' appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, imposition of penalties for non-compliance, adjudication of claims, and legal proceedings as prescribed.

rights: Right to receive minimum wages.
Right to receive wages in the prescribed mode and within the stipulated time limits.
Right to receive bonus as per eligibility criteria.
Right to be free from discrimination on the ground of gender.
Right to approach for resolution of claims and disputes.
duties: Duty of employer to pay wages, minimum wages, and bonus as per the Act.
Duty of employer to maintain records and provide notices as required.
Duty of employer to comply with provisions related to deductions from wages.
Duty of employer to not discriminate on the ground of gender.
obligations: Employers have the obligation to ensure timely and correct payment of wages and bonus.
Employers are obligated to adhere to the rules regarding deductions from wages.
Establishments are obligated to comply with the provisions concerning working hours, overtime, and other employment conditions outlined in the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for fixation and revision of minimum wages (Section 8).
Procedure for claims under the Code and resolution of disputes (Sections 45 and 46).
Procedure for appeal against orders (Section 49).
administration: The 'appropriate Government' (Central or State Government) is responsible for the administration of the Act, with the Central Government having powers to make rules and give directions.
important_notes: The Act consolidates and amends existing laws related to wages and bonus, aiming to simplify and rationalize the legal framework.
The Act specifies that it extends to the whole of India, indicating a uniform application across the country.
The commencement of the Act is subject to notification by the Central Government, and different provisions may come into force at different times.
Specific exclusions from the definition of 'wages' and 'employee' are detailed, which are important for interpretation and application of the Act.

title: The Major Port Authorities Act, 2021
purpose: To provide for the regulation, operation, and planning of Major Ports in India and to vest the administration, control, and management of such ports upon the Boards of Major Port Authorities, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the Major Ports of Chennai, Cochin, Deendayal (Kandla), Jawaharlal Nehru (Nhava Sheva), Kolkata, Mormugao, Mumbai, New Mangalore, Paradip, V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin), and Visakhapatnam. It also applies to navigable rivers and channels leading to these ports where the Indian Ports Act is in force.

key_definitions.Adjudicatory Board: The Board constituted by the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 54.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Major Port Authority constituted by the Central Government in accordance with sub-section (1) of section 3 for each Major Port under this Act.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board appointed under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.Deputy Chairperson: The Deputy Chairperson of the Board appointed under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.dock: Includes all basins, locks, cuts, entrances, graving docks, graving blocks, inclined planes, slipways, gridirons, moorings, transit-sheds, warehouses, tramways, railways and other works and things appertaining to any dock, and also the portion of the sea enclosed or protected by the arms or groynes of a harbour.
key_definitions.goods: Includes livestock and every kind of movable property.
key_definitions.grave emergency: A condition as determined by the Central Government wherein the Board is unable to discharge its duties appropriately and includes acts of sedition, non-performance, unlawful and illegal actions, negligence and financial misappropriation.
key_definitions.immovable property: Includes wharfage-rights and all other rights exercisable on, over, or in respect of, any land, wharf, dock or pier.
key_definitions.Major Port: Means the Major Port as defined in clause (8) of section 3 of the Indian Ports Act.
key_definitions.port assets: Means any asset within the port limits including land, movable or immovable property or any other property, whether tangible or intangible, owned by or vested with the Board through the Central Government or the State Government, as the case may be.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes anything made for the conveyance, by water, of human beings or of goods.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, the date of commencement (to be appointed by the Central Government by notification), and specifies the Major Ports to which the Act applies.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as Adjudicatory Board, Board, Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson, dock, goods, grave emergency, immovable property, Major Port, port assets, and vessel. It also states that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Indian Ports Act shall have the same meanings as assigned in that Act.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of Board of Major Port Authority
main_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute a Board for each Major Port within ninety days of the Act's commencement. It specifies the composition of the Board, including a Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson, representatives from the concerned State Government, Ministries of Railways and Defence, Customs, Independent Members, an ex-officio Member, and employee representatives. It also states that existing Boards of Trustees will continue until the new Board is constituted.

main_sections.section_title: Qualifications of Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson and Members of Board
main_sections.description: Outlines the process and qualifications for appointing the Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson, which will be done by the Central Government based on the recommendation of a Selection Committee. It also specifies the qualifications and appointment process for other Members.

main_sections.section_title: Scale of rates for assets and services available at Major Port
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to determine the scale of rates for assets and services provided at the Major Port.
Deals with the accounts of the Major Port Authorities and their audit.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to take over management of Board
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to take over the management of a Board under certain circumstances.
Provides for the constitution of an Adjudicatory Board.

main_sections.section_title: General provision for punishment of offences
main_sections.description: Sets out general provisions for the punishment of offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make regulations for the administration and management of the Major Port.
Deals with the repeal of existing laws and savings.

important_rules: Rule related to the constitution and composition of the Board of Major Port Authority, ensuring representation from various governmental bodies and stakeholders.
Rules regarding the qualifications, appointment, disqualification, term of office, and removal of Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson, and Members of the Board.
Rules for the application of port assets and the determination of rates for services and assets available at the Major Port.
Rules concerning the financial powers of the Boards, including the power to raise loans and issue securities.
Rules for the supervision of the Central Government over the Boards, including powers to order surveys, take over management, and issue directions.
Rules for the constitution, powers, and functions of the Adjudicatory Board.
Rules for penalties and the punishment of offences.
Rules for the Central Government to make rules and for the Board to make regulations for the effective implementation of the Act.

penalties: General provision for punishment of offences: Details of specific penalties for various offences are likely to be found in Chapter VII and related sections.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board of Major Port Authority and potentially the Central Government, depending on the specific provisions and nature of the offense.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement mechanisms would include the imposition of penalties for offences, the Adjudicatory Board's jurisdiction over disputes, and supervisory powers of the Central Government.

rights: Right of the Board to acquire, hold, or dispose of property.
Right of the Board to contract and sue or be sued.
Right to determine the scale of rates for assets and services.
Right to raise loans and issue securities.
Right to apply for review and appeal of Adjudicatory Board decisions (subject to specified conditions).
Right to engage in Corporate Social Responsibility and infrastructure development.
Rights of individuals and entities interacting with the port, as governed by the Act and related regulations.
duties: Duty of the Board to regulate, operate, and plan Major Ports.
Duty of the Board to manage and administer the Major Port.
Duty to comply with directions issued by the Central Government.
Duty to maintain accounts and undergo audits.
Duty to ensure the safety and good governance of the Major Port.
Duty to implement Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives.
obligations: Obligations of the Board regarding the usage of port assets.
Obligations related to the imposition and recovery of rates and charges.
Obligations concerning financial management, including the establishment and application of sinking funds.
Obligations to obtain sanction from the Central Government before selling or alienating assets.
Obligations of employees of the Board or Adjudicatory Board to be public servants.

key_procedures: Procedure for the constitution and composition of the Board of Major Port Authority.
Procedure for the appointment and removal of Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson, and Members.
Procedure for the determination and imposition of rates for port assets and services.
Procedure for raising loans and issuing securities.
Procedure for the Central Government to order surveys or take over the management of a Board.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Adjudicatory Board, including review and appeal processes.
Procedure for the Central Government to make rules and for the Board to make regulations.
Procedure for the removal of difficulties and transitional provisions.
administration: The administration, control, and management of Major Ports are vested upon the Boards of Major Port Authorities, which are constituted by the Central Government. The Central Government also exercises supervision and has powers to issue directions and intervene in the management of the Boards.
important_notes: The Act requires the Central Government to appoint the commencement date by notification in the Official Gazette.
Existing Boards of Trustees under the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963, will cease to exist upon the constitution of the new Boards under this Act.
The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in certain matters related to the Adjudicatory Board.
The Act provides for the repeal of the Indian Ports Act, 1908, and the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963, with savings provisions.
The Central Government has the power to make rules, and the Board has the power to make regulations, for the effective implementation of the Act.

title: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021
purpose: To provide for the regulation and maintenance of standards of education and services by allied and healthcare professionals, assessment of institutions, maintenance of a Central Register and State Register, and creation of a system to improve access, research and development, and adoption of the latest scientific advancements.
scope: This Act applies to allied and healthcare professionals, allied and healthcare institutions, and the regulation of their education and services across India. It also establishes mechanisms for central and state-level registration and oversight.

key_definitions.advisory_council: The National Allied and Healthcare Advisory Council constituted under sub-section (1) of section 12.
key_definitions.allied_and_healthcare_institution: An educational or research institution which grants diploma or undergraduate, postgraduate or doctoral degree or any other post degree certification in any allied and healthcare professional under this Act.
key_definitions.allied_and_healthcare_professional: Any allied health professional or healthcare professional under this Act.
key_definitions.allied_health_professional: An associate, technician or technologist trained to perform technical and practical tasks to support diagnosis and treatment, and to support the implementation of any healthcare treatment and referral plan recommended by a medical, nursing or any other healthcare professional, having obtained a diploma or degree under this Act with a duration of not less than two thousand hours spread over two to four years.
key_definitions.allied_and_healthcare_qualification: A recognised diploma or degree possessed by an allied and healthcare professional through regular learning mode under this Act or any additional recognised course obtained thereafter.
key_definitions.central_register: The Central Allied and Healthcare Professionals' Register maintained by the Commission under section 13.
key_definitions.commission: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Profession constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.healthcare_professional: A scientist, therapist or other professional who studies, advises, researches, supervises or provides preventive, curative, rehabilitative, therapeutic or promotional health services, and has obtained a degree under this Act with a duration of not less than three thousand six hundred hours spread over three to six years.
key_definitions.state_register: The State Allied and Healthcare Professionals' Register maintained under section 32.
key_definitions.task_shifting: The process whereby specific tasks are moved, where appropriate to related allied and healthcare professionals specialised in those tasks, by reorganising the health workforce efficiently for improved healthcare.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and outlines the commencement provisions, allowing for different dates for different provisions.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'Advisory Council', 'allied and healthcare institution', 'allied and healthcare professional', 'allied health professional', 'allied and healthcare qualification', 'Central Register', 'Commission', 'healthcare professional', 'State Register', and 'Task shifting'.

Establishes the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Profession as a body corporate and details its composition, including the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, ex officio Members from various government departments and institutions, and Part-time Members.
Concerns the constitution of Professional Councils.
Outlines the various functions and duties of the National Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Central Allied and Healthcare Professionals' Register
main_sections.description: Deals with the maintenance of the Central Register for Allied and Healthcare Professionals.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of State Council
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and composition of State Allied and Healthcare Councils.
Details the functions and responsibilities of the State Councils.

main_sections.section_title: State Allied and Healthcare Professionals' Register
main_sections.description: Concerns the maintenance of the State Register for Allied and Healthcare Professionals.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition of allied and healthcare institutions and reciprocity
main_sections.description: Addresses the recognition of allied and healthcare institutions and the establishment of reciprocity.

main_sections.section_title: Permission for establishment of new allied and healthcare institution, new courses of study, etc.
main_sections.description: Governs the process for obtaining permission to establish new allied and healthcare institutions or introduce new courses.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be entered in Central Register and State Register
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for falsely claiming to be registered in the Central or State Register.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of Act
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for violating other provisions of the Act.
States that this Act has an overriding effect on other laws in certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules under the Act.
Grants the Commission the power to make regulations.

important_rules: Allied health professionals must possess a recognized diploma or degree with a specific minimum duration and credit hours.
Healthcare professionals must possess a recognized degree with a specific minimum duration and credit hours.
New allied and healthcare institutions and courses require prior permission.
The Act establishes a Central Register and State Registers for allied and healthcare professionals.
The Central Government has the power to make rules, and the Commission has the power to make regulations.
The Act has an overriding effect, implying its provisions take precedence over conflicting laws.

penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be entered in Central Register and State Register.
Penalty for misuse of titles.
Penalty for failure to surrender certificate of registration.
Penalty for contravention of provisions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Profession, State Councils, and potentially other designated authorities under the Central Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties for violations, maintenance of registers, recognition of institutions and qualifications, and the overarching legal framework established by the Act and rules/regulations made thereunder.

rights: Right to practice as an allied and healthcare professional upon registration.
Rights of persons enrolled on the Central Register regarding practice.
Privileges for enrollment on the Central Register.
duties: Duty to maintain standards of education and services.
Duty to adhere to regulations and rules set by the Commission and State Councils.
Duty of institutions to obtain necessary permissions and recognition.
Duty to surrender certificate of registration when required.
obligations: Obligation to register with the Central or State Register to practice.
Obligation for institutions to meet minimum essential standards.
Obligation to comply with provisions related to recognition and reciprocity.

key_procedures: Procedure for constitution and composition of the National Commission and State Councils.
Procedure for appointment of Chairperson and Members.
Procedure for registration of allied and healthcare professionals in the Central and State Registers.
Procedure for obtaining permission for establishing new allied and healthcare institutions or courses.
Procedure for recognition of allied and healthcare qualifications and institutions.
Procedure for withdrawal of recognition.
administration: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Profession (for central matters) and State Allied and Healthcare Councils (for state matters), overseen by the Central Government.
important_notes: Different commencement dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The Act emphasizes the importance of maintaining minimum essential standards by allied and healthcare institutions.
The Act aims to improve access to healthcare services through regulation and the adoption of scientific advancements.

title: The National Institutes of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management Act, 2021
purpose: To declare certain institutions of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management as institutions of national importance, and to provide for instruction and research in food technology, entrepreneurship and management, for the advancement of learning and dissemination of knowledge in such branches, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the National Institutes of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management, as mentioned in the Schedule. It establishes these institutes as bodies corporate for higher education and research in specified fields. The Act has national scope within India.

key_definitions.Board: The Board of Governors of an Institute, as referred to in section 11.
key_definitions.Chairperson: The Chairperson of the Board of an Institute.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of an Institute appointed under section 19.
key_definitions.Institute: The Institute mentioned in column (3) of the Schedule.
key_definitions.Registrar: The Registrar of an Institute appointed under section 20.
key_definitions.Schedule: The Schedule appended to the Act, which lists the existing and corresponding Institutes.
key_definitions.Society: An existing Institute registered as a Society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_definitions.Statutes and Ordinances: The Statutes and Ordinances of an Institute made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The National Institutes of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management Act, 2021' and outlines the process for its commencement through notification by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of certain Institutes as institutions of national importance
main_sections.description: Declares that the Institutes mentioned in the Schedule are institutions of national importance, based on their objects.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Board, Chairperson, Council, Director, Institute, Registrar, Schedule, Society, and Statutes and Ordinances.

States that on commencement of the Act, each Institute mentioned in the Schedule shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and common seal, with powers to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract, and to sue or be sued in its name.

Details the consequences of incorporation, including renaming of existing institutes in legal documents, transfer of properties, rights, and liabilities, continuation of employment for existing staff with provisions for altered terms, migration of students, and continuation of legal proceedings.

Outlines the powers and functions of each Institute, including providing instruction and research, granting degrees, establishing hostels, maintaining discipline, instituting academic posts, dealing with property, receiving gifts, collaborating with other institutions, and awarding fellowships and scholarships. It also requires Central Government approval for disposing of immovable property.

main_sections.section_title: Institutes to be open to all races, creed and classes
main_sections.description: Mandates that Institutes must be open to all irrespective of gender, race, creed, caste or class, without religious or professional tests for admission or appointment. It also prohibits acceptance of bequests with conflicting conditions and specifies that admission shall be merit-based, with provisions for special reservations for women, persons with disabilities, and socially/educationally backward classes, and recognizes them as Central Educational Institutions under the 2006 Act.

main_sections.section_title: Institutes to be not-for-profit legal entity
main_sections.description: Establishes each Institute as a not-for-profit legal entity, requiring any surplus revenue to be used solely for the Institute's growth, development, or research. Institutes are also required to strive for self-sufficiency and sustainability.
States that all teaching at the Institutes must be conducted in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances.
Lists the authorities of an Institute as the Board of Governors, the Senate, and any other authorities declared by the Statutes.

Defines the Board of Governors as the principal executive body of an Institute. It details the composition of the Board, including the Chairperson, ex officio members from various government departments and institutions, nominated members, faculty members, and the Registrar as Member-Secretary. It also allows the Chairperson to invite experts.
Outlines the powers and functions of the Board of Governors, which is the principal executive body of the Institute.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of, vacancies among, and allowances payable to, Members of Board
main_sections.description: Covers the tenure, filling of vacancies, and remuneration of Board members.
Details the procedure for filling casual vacancies in the Board.
Provides for the resignation of members of the Board.
Refers to the Senate of the Institute.
Describes the functions of the Senate.
Outlines the powers and functions of the Chairperson of the Board.
Refers to the Director of the Institute.
Refers to the Registrar of the Institute.
Mentions other authorities and officers that may be constituted as per the Statutes.
Deals with appointments to various positions within the Institute.
Refers to the Statutes of an Institute.
Explains the procedure for making Statutes.
Refers to the Ordinances of an Institute.
Explains the procedure for making Ordinances.
Mentions the establishment of a Tribunal of Arbitration.
Concerns the establishment of the Council.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of, vacancies among, and allowances payable to members of Council
main_sections.description: Details the tenure, vacancies, and allowances for Council members.
Outlines the functions of the Council.
Pertains to the meetings of the Council.
Deals with financial grants provided by the Central Government to the Institutes.
Explains the maintenance and management of the Fund of each Institute.
Covers the accounting procedures and auditing of the Institutes' finances.
Addresses matters related to pension, insurance, and provident funds for employees.

main_sections.section_title: Acts and proceedings not to be invalidated by vacancies, etc.
main_sections.description: Ensures that the validity of acts and proceedings is not affected by vacancies or technical defects.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to individuals acting in good faith under the Act.
Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules, Statutes and Ordinances to be published in Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: Mandates the publication of rules, Statutes, and Ordinances in the Official Gazette and their subsequent laying before Parliament.
Empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties encountered in giving effect to the Act.
Includes provisions for the transition from existing arrangements to the framework established by the Act.

important_rules: Institutes must be open to all individuals irrespective of gender, race, creed, caste, or class.
Admission to academic courses must be based on merit, with transparent and disclosed criteria.
Special provisions can be made for the employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, and socially/educationally backward classes, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Institutes are designated as Central Educational Institutions for the purposes of the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006.
Institutes must be not-for-profit legal entities, with any surplus revenue reinvested for the Institute's growth and development or research.
Institutes shall strive for self-sufficiency and sustainability.
Teaching at Institutes must be conducted in accordance with the Statutes and Ordinances.
Immovable property of an Institute cannot be disposed of without prior approval from the Central Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Central Government, and through the various authorities of the Institutes (Board of Governors, Director, Registrar, Council) as established by the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Central Government to make rules, issue notifications, and remove difficulties. The functioning of the Institutes is governed by their respective Statutes and Ordinances, and the overall framework of the Act. Enforcement also occurs through the provisions related to the powers and functions of the Institutes' authorities and through legal proceedings.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (subject to approval for immovable property).
Right to contract and sue or be sued.
Right to provide instruction and research.
Right to grant degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions.
Right to confer honorary degrees.
Right to fix, demand, and receive fees.
Right to establish and manage hostels.
Right to supervise and control discipline, and promote health and welfare.
Right to institute academic and other posts (except Director) and make appointments.
Right to receive gifts, grants, donations, bequests, and transfers of property.
Right to co-operate and collaborate with other institutions.
Right to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, exhibitions, prizes, and medals.
Rights of employees regarding tenure, remuneration, and terms and conditions of service (subject to alteration with compensation if not acceptable).
duties: Duty to serve the objects of the Institute.
Duty to be open to all races, creed, and classes.
Duty to ensure admission is merit-based.
Duty to strive for self-sufficiency and sustainability.
Duty to conduct teaching in accordance with Statutes and Ordinances.
Duty to maintain a Fund and adhere to accounting and audit procedures.
Duty of the Board to act as the principal executive body.
Duty of the Council to perform its functions.
Duty to publish rules, Statutes, and Ordinances in the Official Gazette and lay them before Parliament.
obligations: Obligation to seek Central Government approval for disposing of immovable property.
Obligation not to accept bequests with conditions opposed to the spirit of inclusivity.
Obligation to operate as a not-for-profit legal entity.
Obligation to reinvest surplus revenue for the Institute's growth, development, or research.
Obligation to adhere to Statutes and Ordinances for teaching and other matters.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Central Government appoints a date by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(2)).
Incorporation of Institutes: Institutes become bodies corporate on the date of commencement (Section 4).
Transfer of Assets and Liabilities: Existing institutes' properties, rights, and liabilities are transferred to the corresponding incorporated institutes (Section 5).
Appointment of Director: Appointment is made under section 19 (not detailed in extracted text).
Making of Statutes: Procedure outlined in Section 24 (not detailed in extracted text).
Making of Ordinances: Procedure outlined in Section 26 (not detailed in extracted text).
Establishment of Council: As per Section 28 (not detailed in extracted text).
Granting of Funds: Central Government provides grants (Section 32).
Financial Management: Maintenance of Fund, accounts, and audit (Sections 33-34).
Rule Making: Central Government power to make rules (Section 38).
Publication and Laying: Rules, Statutes, and Ordinances are published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament (Section 39).
administration: The Central Government, along with the governing bodies of the Institutes (Board of Governors, Council) and specific officers like the Director and Registrar.
important_notes: Different commencement dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The Board of Governors composition includes ex officio members from key government bodies and educational institutions, alongside nominated and elected faculty members.
The Act mandates a transparent and merit-based admission process, with exceptions for reservations for specific categories.
Institutes are required to raise funds for self-sufficiency and sustainability.

title: The Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021
purpose: To provide for the development, maintenance and management of aids to navigation in India; for training and certification of operators of aids to navigation, development of its historical, educational and cultural value; to ensure compliance with obligations under maritime treaties and international instruments to which India is a party, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India, including the maritime zones of India as specified in the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976. It applies to aids to navigation, vessel traffic services, marking of wrecks, and heritage lighthouses.

key_definitions.aid_to_navigation: A device, system or service, external to vessels, designed and operated to enhance safe and efficient navigation of individual vessels and vessel traffic, but shall not be construed to include a reference to vessel traffic services, unless otherwise specified.
key_definitions.vessel_traffic_service: A service implemented under this Act to improve the safety and efficiency of vessel traffic and to protect the environment.
key_definitions.general_aid_to_navigation: Any aid to navigation which the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare to be a general aid to navigation for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.local_aid_to_navigation: Any aid to navigation which is not a general aid to navigation.
key_definitions.heritage_lighthouse: An aid to navigation designated as such under section 23.
key_definitions.owner: The owner of a vessel including its registered owner, a person to whom a share in the vessel belongs, bareboat charterer, manager and operator of the vessel.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes every description of water craft used or capable of being used in the marine environment, such as ship, boat, sailing vessel, fishing vessel, submersible, semi-submersible, hydrofoils, non-displacement crafts, amphibious crafts, wing-in-ground crafts, pleasure crafts, barges, lighters, mobile offshore drilling units or mobile offshore units.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India including maritime zones), and the provision for commencement by notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'aid to navigation', 'vessel traffic service', 'general aid to navigation', 'local aid to navigation', 'heritage lighthouse', 'owner', and 'vessel'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to designate general aid to navigation
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to designate any aid to navigation as a general aid to navigation by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Director General, Deputy Director Generals and Directors
main_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Director General, Deputy Director Generals, and Directors for demarcated districts by the Central Government.
Outlines the duties of the Director General, including advising the Central Government on matters related to aids to navigation and performing other prescribed duties.

main_sections.section_title: Management of general aids to navigation
main_sections.description: States that the development, maintenance, and management of all general aids to navigation shall be vested in the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Levy and collection of marine aids to navigation dues
main_sections.description: Provides for the levy and collection of marine aids to navigation dues.

main_sections.section_title: Intentionally obstructing aids to navigation or vessel traffic services
main_sections.description: Defines the offense of intentionally obstructing aids to navigation or vessel traffic services.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of existing provisions and savings for actions taken under previous laws.

important_rules: The Central Government has the power to designate general aids to navigation by notification.
The development, maintenance, and management of general aids to navigation are vested in the Central Government.
The Central Government is responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of vessel traffic services.
Marine aids to navigation dues are to be levied and collected.
Rules can be made by the Central Government to carry out the provisions of the Act.

penalties: Intentionally obstructing aids to navigation or vessel traffic services.
Negligently obstructing aids to navigation or vessel traffic services.
Intentionally destroying or damaging aids to navigation or vessel traffic services.
Negligently destroying or damaging aids to navigation or vessel traffic services.
Causing damage to a heritage lighthouse.
Evading payment of marine aids to navigation dues.
Noncompliance with directions of a vessel traffic service provider.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for offenses and penalties, cognizance of offenses by courts, and the power of the Central Government to issue directions and make rules.

rights: The right of vessels to safe and efficient navigation through aids to navigation and vessel traffic services.
The right of the Central Government to establish, maintain, and manage aids to navigation and vessel traffic services.
The right to designate certain aids as heritage lighthouses.
duties: Duty to develop, maintain, and manage aids to navigation and vessel traffic services.
Duty to ensure compliance with maritime treaties and international instruments.
Duty to train and certify operators of aids to navigation and vessel traffic services.
Duty to consult the Central Advisory Committee on matters related to aids to navigation.
obligations: Obligation to pay marine aids to navigation dues.
Obligation to comply with directions given by vessel traffic service providers.
Obligation to avoid obstructing, destroying, or damaging aids to navigation or vessel traffic services.

key_procedures: Designation of general aids to navigation by the Central Government through notification.
Appointment of Director General, Deputy Director Generals, and Directors.
Consultation with the Central Advisory Committee on matters related to aids to navigation.
Establishment and management of vessel traffic services by the Central Government.
Levy and collection of marine aids to navigation dues.
