Duty of all agencies to assist statistics officers.
Duty to maintain the security of collected information.
Duty of researchers/institutions to use disclosed information solely for bona fide research or statistical purposes.
obligations: Obligation on informants to provide accurate and complete statistical information.
Obligation on agencies to cooperate with the statistical collection process.
Obligation on individuals and agencies involved in handling statistical data to ensure its security and confidentiality.

key_procedures: The appropriate Government may direct the collection of statistics via notification.
Statistics officers can be appointed to facilitate collection.
Statistics officers have the power to call for information from informants through notices, questions, or electronic modes.
Informants are required to furnish the requested information.
Information collected is subject to security and disclosure restrictions.
Procedures for adjudication and appeal are established for penalties.
administration: The administration of the Act involves the Central Government, State Governments, Union territory Administrations, and local governments, acting as 'appropriate Governments'. Statistics officers and designated agencies play a crucial role in the day-to-day collection and management of statistics.
important_notes: The extent of the Act was amended in 2017 to include the whole of India, with certain provisions omitted for Jammu and Kashmir and the Union Territory of Ladakh in 2020.
The Act came into force on June 11, 2010.
The Act provides for the appointment of a nodal officer to coordinate statistical activities.
Provisions exist for the disclosure of information for bona fide research or statistical purposes, with strict conditions on informant anonymity and data usage.
The Act includes a provision for the overriding effect of its provisions (Section 32), suggesting it may supersede other laws in certain respects related to statistics collection.

title: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024
purpose: To provide for regulation and control of the design, manufacture, maintenance, possession, use, operation, sale, export and import of aircraft and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Extends to the whole of India and applies to: citizens of India wherever they may be; aircraft, and persons on aircraft, registered in India wherever they may be; aircraft, and persons on aircraft, registered outside India but for the time being in or over India; and aircraft operated by a person not a citizen of India but with their principal place of business or permanent residence in India.

key_definitions.aerodrome: Any definite or limited ground or water area intended to be used, either wholly or in part, for the landing, departure and surface movement of aircraft, and includes all buildings, sheds, vessels, piers and other structures thereon or appertaining thereto.
key_definitions.aerodrome reference point: A designated point established in the horizontal plane at or near the geometric centre of that part of the aerodrome reserved for the departure or landing of aircraft.
key_definitions.aircraft: Any machine that can derive support in the atmosphere from reactions of the air, other than reactions of the air against the earth’s surface.
key_definitions.Aircraft Accidents Investigation Bureau: The Aircraft Accidents Investigation Bureau constituted under section 7.
key_definitions.Bureau of Civil Aviation Security: The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security constituted under section 5.
key_definitions.design: The set of data and information that defines the configuration of an aeronautical product type, its associated parts and appliances for the purpose of airworthiness determination.
key_definitions.Directorate General of Civil Aviation: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.maintenance: The performance of tasks on an aircraft, engine, propeller or associated part required to ensure the continuing airworthiness of an aircraft, engine, propeller or associated part including any one or combination of overhaul, inspection, replacement, defect rectification, and the embodiment of a modification or repair.
key_definitions.manufacture: The performance of tasks that involve assembly or production of aircraft, engine, propeller or associated parts and appliances in conformity with its applicable design including prototype.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application and commencement
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, the entities it applies to, and the mechanism for its commencement.
Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'aerodrome', 'aircraft', 'design', 'manufacture', etc.
Establishes the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), its head (Director General), its responsibilities for safety oversight and regulatory functions, and the power to delegate its authority.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Director General of Civil Aviation to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Director General of Civil Aviation (or an empowered officer) the authority to issue directions concerning various aspects of aircraft operations, aerodrome management, and air traffic control, for the security of India or safety of aircraft operations.
Establishes the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS), its head (Director General), its responsibilities for security and oversight functions, and the power to delegate its authority.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Director General of Bureau of Civil Aviation Security to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the Director General of the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (or an empowered officer) the authority to issue directions related to civil aviation security, safeguarding against unlawful interference, for the security of India or civil aviation operations.

Establishes the Aircraft Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB), its head (Director General), its responsibilities for investigating aircraft accidents or incidents, and the power to delegate its authority.
Vests the superintendence of the DGCA, BCAS, and AAIB in the Central Government, granting it the power to issue directions to these organizations in the public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to review orders passed under section 4 or section 6
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to review orders passed by the Director General of Civil Aviation or the Director General of Bureau of Civil Aviation Security and issue directions to rescind or modify those orders.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules regulating various aspects of aircraft, including design, manufacture, maintenance, use, sale, import, and export, for ensuring aircraft safety.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules on various aviation-related matters.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules for investigation of accidents
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules specifically for the investigation of aircraft accidents.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules for protecting public health
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for protecting public health in relation to aviation.

main_sections.section_title: Emergency powers of Central Government for protecting public health
main_sections.description: Confers emergency powers on the Central Government for the protection of public health.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make orders in emergency
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make orders during emergencies.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules for securing safe custody and re-delivery of unclaimed property
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for the safe custody and re-delivery of unclaimed property related to aircraft.

main_sections.section_title: Central Government to make rules to implement Convention
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules to implement any Convention relating to aviation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to prohibit or regulate construction of buildings, planting of trees, and the like
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to prohibit or regulate the construction of buildings, planting of trees, and similar activities that could pose a hazard to aircraft operations.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to restrict, suspend or cancel licence, certificate or approval
main_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to restrict, suspend, or cancel any licence, certificate, or approval related to aircraft.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to exempt certain aircraft
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to exempt certain aircraft from the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to delegate
main_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act to other authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Manner of determination and payment of compensation for loss or damage
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for determining and paying compensation for loss or damage.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal from award in respect of compensation
main_sections.description: Provides for appeals against awards made in respect of compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Arbitrator to have certain powers of civil courts
main_sections.description: Grants arbitrators certain powers similar to those of civil courts in matters of compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of rule made under this Act
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening rules made under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for flying so as to cause danger
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for flying an aircraft in a manner that causes danger.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to comply with directions issued under section 4 or section 6
main_sections.description: Defines penalties for failing to comply with directions issued by the Director General of Civil Aviation or the Director General of Bureau of Civil Aviation Security.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to comply with directions issued under section 18
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for failing to comply with directions issued by the Central Government under section 18 concerning construction and other activities.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for abetment of offences and attempted offences
main_sections.description: Covers penalties for abetting or attempting to commit offences under the Act.
Provides for the compounding of certain offences.
Deals with the cognizance that courts can take of offences under the Act.
Outlines the process for adjudicating penalties.
Provides for appeals against decisions made under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be made after publication
main_sections.description: Mandates that rules made by the Central Government must be published.
Requires that rules made under the Act be laid before Parliament.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Court to order forfeiture
main_sections.description: Grants courts the power to order the forfeiture of aircraft or other property.
Addresses matters related to aircraft wreck and salvage.

main_sections.section_title: Use of patented invention on aircraft not registered in India
main_sections.description: Deals with the use of patented inventions on aircraft not registered in India.
Prohibits certain types of suits.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Specifies savings related to the application of the Act.
Grants the Central Government power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of previous legislation and savings in relation to the repealed provisions.

important_rules: Rules regulating the design, manufacture, maintenance, possession, use, operation, sale, import, or export of aircraft (Section 10(1)).
Rules to ensure the safety of aircraft operations (Section 10(1)).
Rules for the regulation of air transport services and licensing (Section 10(2)(b)).
Rules for the economic regulation of civil aviation and air transport services, including tariff approval (Section 10(2)(c)).
Rules for protecting public health in relation to aviation (Section 13).
Rules for the safe custody and re-delivery of unclaimed property (Section 16).
Rules to implement Conventions relating to aviation (Section 17).

penalties: Penalty for contravention of rules made under the Act (Section 25).
Penalty for flying an aircraft so as to cause danger (Section 26).
Penalty for failure to comply with directions issued by DGCA or BCAS (Section 27).
Penalty for failure to comply with directions issued by Central Government regarding construction etc. (Section 28).
Penalty for abetment or attempt to commit offences (Section 29).
Power of Court to order forfeiture (Section 36).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS), Aircraft Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB), Central Government, and officers specially empowered.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of directions, imposition of penalties, adjudication of penalties, and court orders including forfeiture. Rules are made by the Central Government and must be complied with.

rights: Right to appeal against awards in respect of compensation (Section 23).
Right to appeal against decisions made under the Act (Section 33).
duties: Duty to comply with directions issued by DGCA or empowered officers (Section 4(2)).
Duty to comply with directions issued by BCAS or empowered officers (Section 6(2)).
Duty to comply with directions issued by the Central Government (implied in various sections related to rules and orders).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to regulations concerning the design, manufacture, maintenance, possession, use, operation, sale, export, and import of aircraft.
Obligation to ensure aircraft safety and prevent danger during flight.
Obligation to comply with rules and directions issued by relevant authorities.

key_procedures: Issuance of directions by DGCA or BCAS with compliance required (Sections 4 & 6).
Review of orders by the Central Government and issuance of directions (Section 9).
Determination and payment of compensation for loss or damage (Section 22).
Appeal process for compensation awards (Section 23).
Adjudication of penalties (Section 32).
Appeals against decisions (Section 33).
Removal of difficulties by the Central Government (Section 42).
administration: The Central Government, through the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS), and Aircraft Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB), is responsible for the administration of this Act.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government through notification in the Official Gazette (Section 1(3)).
The DGCA, BCAS, and AAIB constituted under the Aircraft Act, 1934, are deemed to have been constituted under this Act (Sections 3(1), 5(1), 7(1)).
The Central Government can delegate powers vested in the Directors General of DGCA, BCAS, and AAIB (Sections 3(4), 5(4), 7(4)).
The Central Government has emergency powers related to protecting public health (Section 14) and making orders in emergency situations (Section 15).

title: The Cattle-Trespass Act, 1871
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to trespasses by cattle.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States, and the presidency-towns and such local areas as the State Government may, by notification, exclude. The Act has various state amendments, notably in Maharashtra, extending its application to specific areas.

key_definitions.cattle: Includes elephants, camels, buffaloes, horses, mares, geldings, ponies, colts, fillies, mules, asses, pigs, rams, ewes, sheep, lambs, goats and kids.
key_definitions.local authority: Any body of persons invested by law with the control and administration of matters within a specified local area.
key_definitions.local fund: Any fund under the control or management of a local authority.

main_sections.description: Defines the short title of the Act and its territorial applicability, with provisions for exclusion by State Governments.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'officer of police', 'cattle', 'local authority', and 'local fund'.
Empowers the Magistrate of the District, under the general control of the State Government, to direct the establishment of pounds at specified places and to determine the villages they will serve.

main_sections.section_title: Control of pounds. Rates of charge for feeding impounded cattle.
main_sections.description: Places pounds under the control of the Magistrate of the District and authorizes the Magistrate to fix and alter rates for feeding and watering impounded cattle.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of pound-keepers. Pound-keepers may hold other offices. Pound-keepers to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Mandates the State Government to appoint a pound-keeper for each pound, allows pound-keepers to hold other government offices, and deems them public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

Allows cultivators, occupiers, or persons involved in crop cultivation to seize cattle trespassing on their land and causing damage, and send them to the pound. Police officers are mandated to aid such seizures.

main_sections.section_title: Cattle damaging public roads, canals and embankments
main_sections.description: Permits persons in charge of public roads, plantations, canals, embankments, etc., and police officers to seize cattle causing damage to these properties or found straying on them, and send them to the nearest pound.

States that pound-keepers shall levy fines for impounded cattle according to scales prescribed by the State Government. Fines are to be sent to the District Magistrate. A list of fines and feeding charges must be posted at each pound.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for forcibly opposing the seizure of cattle or rescuing the same.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who forcibly oppose the seizure of cattle or rescue impounded cattle.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of penalty for mischief committed by causing cattle to trespass.
main_sections.description: Details the recovery of penalties for the offense of mischief by causing cattle to trespass.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for damage caused to land or crops or public roads by pigs.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for damage caused to land, crops, or public roads by pigs.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on pound-keeper failing to perform duties.
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for pound-keepers who fail to perform their prescribed duties.

important_rules: Cattle found trespassing and causing damage to land, crops, public roads, canals, or embankments can be seized and sent to a pound.
Police officers must aid in preventing resistance to seizures and rescues of seized cattle.
Pound-keepers are responsible for taking charge of, feeding, and watering impounded cattle until they are disposed of.
A fine is levied for each head of cattle impounded, according to scales prescribed by the State Government.
A list of fines and feeding charges must be displayed at every pound.
Pound-keepers must maintain registers of seized cattle and provide copies of entries to the seizer.
If cattle are not claimed within a week, they may be sold.
Fines and expenses incurred from impounding and selling cattle are to be accounted for by the Magistrate.

penalties: Penalty for forcibly opposing seizure or rescuing cattle.
Penalty for mischief committed by causing cattle to trespass.
Penalty for damage caused by pigs to land, crops, or public roads.
Penalty for pound-keepers failing to perform their duties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate of the District, State Government, and officers of police.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through seizure of cattle, impoundment, levying of fines, sale of unclaimed cattle, and prosecution for offenses.

rights: Right of cultivators/occupiers to seize cattle trespassing and causing damage.
Right to claim impounded cattle by proving ownership and paying fines/charges.
Right to compensation for illegal seizure or detention of cattle.
Right to the surplus proceeds of sale of impounded cattle if any, after deducting fines and expenses.
duties: Duty of pound-keepers to maintain registers, take charge of cattle, feed and water them, and perform other directed duties.
Duty of police officers to aid in seizures and prevent rescues.
Duty of cattle owners to pay fines and charges for their impounded cattle.
Duty of the State Government to establish pounds, appoint pound-keepers, and prescribe fine scales.
obligations: Obligation to send seized cattle to the pound within twenty-four hours.
Obligation to deposit fines and charges for claiming impounded cattle.
Obligation not to oppose lawful seizures or rescue impounded cattle.

key_procedures: Seizure of trespassing cattle by authorized persons.
Delivery of seized cattle to the pound-keeper within twenty-four hours.
Registration of seized cattle by the pound-keeper, with a copy of the entry provided to the seizer.
Feeding and watering of impounded cattle by the pound-keeper.
Claiming impounded cattle by the owner upon payment of fines and charges.
Sale of unclaimed cattle after one week, with proceeds used to cover fines and expenses.
Disposal of fines, expenses, and surplus sale proceeds.
Procedure for complaints regarding illegal seizure or detention, including compensation and release of cattle.
administration: Magistrate of the District and the State Government.
important_notes: The Act has been subject to numerous local and state amendments, particularly concerning its application and specific provisions in different regions of India.
The definition of 'cattle' is extensive, including a wide range of animals.
Specific sections are repealed or amended by subsequent legislation, as indicated by the 'List of Amending Acts' and footnotes.
State Governments have the power to exclude specific local areas from the operation of the Act.
Certain provisions are to be read in conjunction with other laws, such as the Indian Penal Code and the Indian Forest Act.

title: The Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of certain banking companies to further control the heights of the economy, meet the needs of economic development, and promote public welfare, in line with Article 39(b) and (c) of the Constitution.
scope: This Act applies to specific banking companies as defined and listed in the First Schedule, with a threshold of total demand and time liabilities in India not less than two hundred crores as of March 14, 1980. It focuses on the acquisition and transfer of their undertakings to corresponding new banks.

key_definitions.banking company: Does not include a foreign company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.corresponding new bank: A body corporate specified in the First Schedule, established in relation to an existing bank.
key_definitions.Custodian: The person appointed as Custodian under section 7.
key_definitions.existing bank: A banking company listed in the First Schedule whose total demand and time liabilities in India as of March 14, 1980, were not less than two hundred crores.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it is deemed to have come into force on April 15, 1980.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'banking company', 'corresponding new bank', 'Custodian', and 'existing bank'. It also specifies that undefined terms will take their meaning from the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, or the Companies Act, 1956.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of corresponding new banks and business thereof
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of corresponding new banks and specifies their paid-up capital. It also outlines provisions for the authorized capital, increasing and reducing paid-up capital, and conditions for public issues and shareholding by the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Undertakings of existing banks to vest in corresponding new banks
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of undertakings of existing banks to their corresponding new banks.
Describes the general consequences of the vesting of undertakings.
Concerns the payment of amounts related to the acquisition.
Addresses the head office and management of the corresponding new banks.

main_sections.section_title: Corresponding new banks to be guided by the directions of the Central Government
main_sections.description: Stipulates that corresponding new banks shall follow the directions of the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make scheme
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to frame schemes related to the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Obligations as to fidelity and secrecy
main_sections.description: Outlines the duties of employees regarding fidelity and secrecy.
Confers the power to make regulations under the Act.
Provides for the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: Corresponding new banks must be guided by the directions of the Central Government (Section 8).
The Central Government has the power to make schemes for the efficient management and functioning of the corresponding new banks (Section 9).
All officers and employees of existing banks are to be transferred to the corresponding new banks with continuity of service and terms (implied by transfer of undertaking).
Shareholders of corresponding new banks (other than the Central Government) have voting rights limited to ten percent of the total voting rights (Section 3(2E)).
Restrictions are placed on foreign investment in shares of corresponding new banks (Section 3(2D)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government and Reserve Bank of India (implied through powers to guide, make schemes, and grant approvals).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the Central Government's power to issue directions, make schemes, and through regulatory oversight by the Reserve Bank of India.

rights: Right of shareholders (other than Central Government) to exercise voting rights, capped at 10% of total voting rights.
Right of preference shareholders to vote on resolutions directly affecting their rights.
Shareholders have the right to freely transfer shares not held by the Central Government.
duties: Duty of corresponding new banks to be guided by Central Government directions.
Duty of employees to maintain fidelity and secrecy.
Duty of corresponding new banks to keep a register of shareholders.
obligations: Obligation of the Central Government to hold at least fifty-one percent of equity shares.
Obligations related to the transfer of undertakings and payment of amounts.

key_procedures: Establishment of corresponding new banks.
Transfer of undertakings from existing banks to corresponding new banks.
Procedure for increasing or reducing the paid-up capital of corresponding new banks, including public issues and rights issues.
Procedure for the Central Government to make schemes.
Maintenance of a register of shareholders by corresponding new banks.
Regulation of voting rights for shareholders.
Restrictions on shareholding by entities outside India.
administration: The Central Government, in conjunction with the Reserve Bank of India, is responsible for the administration and oversight of this Act.
important_notes: The Act came into force retrospectively from April 15, 1980.
Various amendments have been made to the Act over time, as listed.
The Act defines 'banking company' to exclude foreign companies.
Specific thresholds for liabilities of existing banks (rupees two hundred crores) determine their inclusion.

title: The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021
purpose: To constitute National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board, State Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Boards and appoint appropriate authorities for the regulation of the practice and process of surrogacy and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the entire territory of India. It regulates surrogacy and surrogacy procedures, including the establishment and operation of surrogacy clinics, the rights and duties of surrogate mothers and intending parents, and the prohibition of commercial surrogacy.

key_definitions.abandoned child: A child born out of a surrogacy procedure who has been deserted by his intending parents or guardians and declared as abandoned by the appropriate authority after due enquiry.
key_definitions.altruistic surrogacy: Surrogacy where no charges, expenses, fees, remuneration, or monetary incentive of any nature, except medical and prescribed expenses and insurance coverage for the surrogate mother, are given to the surrogate mother or her dependents.
key_definitions.appropriate authority: The appropriate authority appointed under Section 35.
key_definitions.commercial surrogacy: Commercialisation of surrogacy services or procedures, including selling or buying human embryos or gametes, or trading in services of surrogate motherhood through payment, reward, benefit, fees, remuneration, or monetary incentive in cash or kind, except medical and prescribed expenses and insurance coverage for the surrogate mother.
key_definitions.couple: A legally married Indian man and woman above the age of 21 years and 18 years respectively.
key_definitions.embryo: A developing or developed organism after fertilization until the end of fifty-six days.
key_definitions.fertilisation: The penetration of the ovum by the spermatozoan and fusion of genetic materials resulting in the development of a zygote.
key_definitions.foetus: A human organism during its development from the fifty-seventh day following fertilization or creation until birth.
key_definitions.gynaecologist: Has the same meaning as assigned in the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994.
key_definitions.implantation: The attachment and subsequent penetration by the zona-free blastocyst, starting five to seven days following fertilization.
key_definitions.insurance: An arrangement by which a company, individual, or intending couple provides a guarantee of compensation for medical expenses, health issues, specified loss, damage, illness, or death of the surrogate mother during the surrogacy process.
key_definitions.intending couple: A couple who have a medical indication necessitating gestational surrogacy and intend to become parents through surrogacy.
key_definitions.intending woman: An Indian woman who is a widow or divorcee between the age of 35 to 45 years and intends to avail surrogacy.
key_definitions.oocyte: Naturally ovulating oocyte in the female genetic tract.
key_definitions.Paediatrician: A person with a post-graduate qualification in paediatrics recognized under the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered medical practitioner: A medical practitioner with a recognized medical qualification and whose name is entered in a State Medical Register.
key_definitions.regulation: Regulations made by the Board under this Act.
key_definitions.sex selection: Has the same meaning as assigned in the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994.
key_definitions.State Board: The State Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board constituted under section 26.
key_definitions.State Government: In relation to a Union territory with a Legislature, means the Administrator appointed by the President.
key_definitions.surrogacy: A practice whereby one woman bears and gives birth to a child for an intending couple with the intention of handing over such child to the intending couple after birth.
key_definitions.surrogacy clinic: Any clinic, centre, or laboratory conducting assisted reproductive technology services, in-vitro fertilization services, genetic counseling, genetic laboratory, Assisted Reproductive Technology Banks, or any clinical establishment conducting surrogacy procedures.
key_definitions.surrogacy procedures: All gynecological, obstetrical, or medical procedures, techniques, tests, practices, or services involving the handling of human gametes and human embryos in surrogacy.
key_definitions.surrogate mother: A woman who agrees to bear a child (genetically related to the intending couple or intending woman) through surrogacy from embryo implantation and fulfills specified conditions.
key_definitions.zygote: The fertilized oocyte prior to the first cell division.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its extent (entirety of India), and the commencement date which is appointed by the Central Government via notification.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'abandoned child', 'altruistic surrogacy', 'appropriate authority', 'commercial surrogacy', 'couple', 'egg', 'embryo', 'fertilisation', 'foetus', 'gamete', 'gynaecologist', 'implantation', 'insurance', 'intending couple', 'intending woman', 'oocyte', 'Paediatrician', 'prescribed', 'registered medical practitioner', 'regulation', 'sex selection', 'State Board', 'State Government', 'surrogacy', 'surrogacy clinic', 'surrogacy procedures', 'surrogate mother', and 'zygote'. It also states that terms defined in the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act shall have the same meaning.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition and regulation of surrogacy clinics
main_sections.description: This section outlines prohibitions and regulations for surrogacy clinics. It mandates registration for clinics, prohibits commercial surrogacy, specifies qualifications for employed personnel, restricts surrogacy procedures to registered places, prohibits advertising of surrogacy services (especially commercial ones), requires written consent for abortion during surrogacy (subject to MTP Act), prohibits storage of embryos/gametes for surrogacy (except for specified legal purposes), and prohibits sex selection for surrogacy.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of surrogacy and surrogacy procedures
main_sections.description: This section details the conditions under which surrogacy and surrogacy procedures can be conducted. It specifies that only places registered under the Act can be used and that surrogacy can only be conducted for specific purposes, primarily when an intending couple has a medical indication necessitating gestational surrogacy, and they must obtain a certificate of recommendation from the Board.
This section likely details specific prohibitions related to conducting surrogacy.

main_sections.section_title: Written informed consent of surrogate mother
main_sections.description: This section emphasizes the requirement for written informed consent from the surrogate mother.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition to abandon child born through surrogacy
main_sections.description: This section prohibits the abandonment of a child born through surrogacy.
This section outlines the rights that a child born through surrogacy is entitled to.

main_sections.section_title: Number of oocytes or human embryos to be implanted
main_sections.description: This section likely regulates the number of oocytes or human embryos that can be implanted during the surrogacy process.
This section prohibits abortion during the surrogacy process, likely with specific exceptions and conditions.
This section details the process and requirements for the registration of surrogacy clinics.
This section likely pertains to the issuance of the registration certificate for surrogacy clinics.
This section outlines the grounds and procedures for cancelling or suspending the registration of a surrogacy clinic.
This section likely provides a mechanism for appealing decisions related to registration or other actions taken under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Registry
main_sections.description: This section details the establishment of a national registry for assisted reproductive technology and surrogacy.

main_sections.section_title: Application of provisions of Assisted Reproductive Technology Act with respect to National Registry
main_sections.description: This section specifies how provisions of the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act apply to the National Registry.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board
main_sections.description: This section describes the formation and composition of the National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board.
This section outlines the various functions and responsibilities of the National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of State Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board
main_sections.description: This section details the establishment and formation of the State Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Boards.
This section deals with the appointment of appropriate authorities responsible for implementing the Act.
This section specifies the roles and functions of the appointed appropriate authorities.
This section outlines the powers vested in the appropriate authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of commercial surrogacy, exploitation of surrogate mothers and children born through surrogacy
main_sections.description: This section explicitly prohibits commercial surrogacy and the exploitation of surrogate mothers and children born through surrogacy.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for contravention of provisions of Act
main_sections.description: This section prescribes punishments for violations of the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for not following altruistic surrogacy
main_sections.description: This section likely details penalties for failing to adhere to the principles of altruistic surrogacy.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of Act or rules for which no specific punishment is provided
main_sections.description: This section covers penalties for contraventions of the Act or rules for which no specific punishment is otherwise defined.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption in the case of surrogacy
main_sections.description: This section likely deals with legal presumptions that may arise in cases related to surrogacy.

main_sections.section_title: Offence to be cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable
main_sections.description: This section classifies offenses under the Act as cognizable, non-bailable, and non-compoundable.
This section outlines the procedure for taking cognizance of offenses under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Certain provisions of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 not to apply
main_sections.description: This section specifies certain provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, that will not apply to proceedings under this Act.
This section mandates the maintenance of records by relevant parties involved in surrogacy.

main_sections.section_title: Power to search and seize records, etc.
main_sections.description: This section grants powers to search and seize records related to surrogacy.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: This section provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that the Act does not preclude the application of other relevant laws.
This section empowers the government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
This section empowers the Board to make regulations for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament
main_sections.description: This section mandates that rules and regulations made under the Act are to be presented before Parliament.
This section provides for transitional arrangements to facilitate the smooth implementation of the Act.
This section grants the government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: No surrogacy clinic shall conduct or associate with surrogacy or surrogacy procedures unless registered under the Act.
Commercial surrogacy in any form is prohibited.

Surrogacy can only be conducted for altruistic purposes, with the intending couple having a medical indication necessitating gestational surrogacy, and obtaining a certificate of recommendation from the Board.

A surrogate mother must be a close relative of the intending couple or intending woman and must be married with a child of her own. She must be medically and psychologically fit, and must provide written informed consent.
The child born through surrogacy has the same rights and is entitled to the same parental rights as a naturally born child.

Abortion during surrogacy is prohibited without the written consent of the surrogate mother and authorization from the appropriate authority, subject to the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971.
Sex selection for surrogacy is strictly prohibited.
Intending couples or intending women must be Indian citizens.
The child born through surrogacy must be handed over to the intending parents immediately after birth.
The National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board and State Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Boards are constituted to regulate and oversee surrogacy practices.

penalties: Punishment for contravention of provisions of the Act, with imprisonment and fines, which may vary depending on the specific offense.
Punishment for conducting commercial surrogacy, exploitation of surrogate mothers and children.
Penalties for failing to follow altruistic surrogacy principles.
Penalties for contraventions for which no specific punishment is provided.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Appropriate authorities appointed under Section 35, National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board, and State Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Boards.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appointment of appropriate authorities, registration of surrogacy clinics, investigation of complaints, imposition of penalties, and prosecution for offenses. Powers include search and seizure of records. Offenses are cognizable, non-bailable, and non-compoundable.

rights: Right of the surrogate child to have the same rights and parental rights as a naturally born child.
Right of intending couples/women to avail altruistic surrogacy under specific conditions.
Right to appeal decisions made by appropriate authorities or Boards.
Right to protection of action taken in good faith.
duties: Duty of surrogacy clinics to be registered and comply with all provisions of the Act.
Duty of medical practitioners and others involved to adhere to regulations.
Duty of intending parents not to abandon the child born through surrogacy.
Duty to obtain informed consent of the surrogate mother.
Duty to comply with the regulations regarding embryo and gamete handling and implantation.
obligations: Obligation to conduct only altruistic surrogacy.
Obligation to provide medical expenses, insurance coverage, and other prescribed expenses to the surrogate mother.
Obligation to maintain records as prescribed.
Obligation to hand over the child to the intending parents immediately after birth.

key_procedures: Registration of surrogacy clinics: Clinics must apply for and obtain registration from the appropriate authority.

Availing surrogacy: Intending couples or women must obtain a certificate of recommendation from the Board based on a prescribed application form, demonstrating a medical indication for gestational surrogacy.
Informed Consent: The surrogate mother must provide written informed consent for the procedure.
Reporting and Record Keeping: Surrogacy clinics and involved practitioners must maintain records as prescribed and make them available for inspection.
Appeals: Procedures for appealing decisions of the appropriate authority or Boards.
administration: National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board and State Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Boards, along with Appropriate Authorities appointed under the Act.
important_notes: The Act clearly distinguishes between altruistic and commercial surrogacy, with commercial surrogacy being strictly prohibited.
Only Indian citizens are permitted to avail surrogacy services.
The surrogate mother must be a close relative of the intending couple/woman, married, and have at least one child of her own.
The Act is to be read in conjunction with the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act, 2021, and the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994.
The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971, is relevant for abortion procedures during surrogacy.

title: The Disaster Management Act, 2005
purpose: To provide for the effective management of disasters and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to all aspects of disaster management, including prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery.

key_definitions.disaster: A catastrophe, mishap, calamity or grave occurrence in any area, arising from natural or man made causes, or by accident or negligence which results in substantial loss of life or human suffering or damage to, and destruction of, property, or damage to, or degradation of, environment, and is of such a nature or magnitude as to be beyond the coping capacity of the community of the affected area.
key_definitions.disaster management: A continuous and integrated process of planning, organising, coordinating and implementing measures necessary or expedient for prevention of danger or threat of any disaster; mitigation or reduction of risk of any disaster or its severity or consequences; capacity-building; preparedness to deal with any disaster; prompt response to any threatening disaster situation or disaster; assessing the severity or magnitude of effects of any disaster; evacuation, rescue and relief; rehabilitation, recovery and reconstruction.
key_definitions.affected area: An area or part of the country affected by a disaster.
key_definitions.capacity-building: Includes identification of existing resources and resources to be acquired or created; acquiring or creating resources; organisation and training of personnel and coordination of such training for effective management of disasters.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its extent (whole of India), and outlines the commencement provisions, allowing for different dates for different provisions and states.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'affected area', 'capacity-building', 'disaster', 'disaster management', 'National Authority', 'State Authority', 'District Authority', 'mitigation', 'preparedness', 'response', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of National Disaster Management Authority
main_sections.description: Establishes the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).
Deals with the preparation and contents of the National Disaster Management Plan.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of State Disaster Management Authority
main_sections.description: Establishes the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA).

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of District Disaster Management Authority
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMA).
Outlines the responsibilities and functions of local authorities in disaster management.
Provides for the establishment and functioning of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF).
Establishes the National Disaster Response Fund.
Specifies penalties for obstructing disaster management efforts.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in matters related to disaster management.

important_rules: Disaster management is a continuous and integrated process.

Measures for disaster management include prevention, mitigation, capacity-building, preparedness, prompt response, assessment, evacuation, rescue, relief, rehabilitation, recovery, and reconstruction.
The Central Government, State Governments, and District Authorities are responsible for taking measures for disaster management.
Local authorities have specific functions in disaster management within their areas.
A National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs), and District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs) are established to oversee disaster management.

penalties: Punishment for obstruction, false claims, misappropriation of funds/materials, and false warnings.
Penalties for failure of officers in duty or connivance at contraventions.
Penalty for contravention of orders regarding requisitioning.
Offences by companies.
Punishment for contravention of orders regarding nature of hazard.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforcement is carried out by various authorities established under the Act, including the National Authority, State Authorities, District Authorities, and potentially police and judicial bodies for penal provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of plans, directions, and orders issued by the respective authorities, and through legal prosecution for offences and penalties prescribed in Chapter X.

rights: Right to timely warnings and communication of disaster-related information.
Right to rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and recovery in the event of a disaster.
duties: Duty of Central Government to take measures for disaster management.
Duty of State Government to take measures for disaster management.
Duty of Ministries/Departments to prepare disaster management plans.
Duty of District Authority to prepare District Plan.
Duty of local authorities to perform functions related to disaster management.
Duty of individuals and communities to cooperate with authorities during disaster management efforts.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to and implement disaster management plans.
Obligation to comply with orders and directions issued by competent authorities.
Obligation to provide resources or services when requisitioned for disaster management.
Obligation to report or provide information relevant to disaster management when required.

key_procedures: Establishment and functioning of National, State, and District Disaster Management Authorities.
Preparation of National, State, and District Disaster Management Plans.
Constitution and functions of National and State Executive Committees.
Establishment and operation of National and State Disaster Response Forces.
Procedures for requisitioning resources for rescue operations.
Procedures for prosecution and cognizance of offences.
administration: The Ministry or Department of the Government of India having administrative control of disaster management (for the Central Government) and corresponding departments at the State level administer the Act.
important_notes: The Act provides for the establishment of funds such as the National Disaster Response Fund and National Disaster Mitigation Fund.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over any other law in matters of disaster management.
Immunity from legal process is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
The Central Government has powers to make rules and the National Authority has powers to make regulations under the Act.

title: THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide for protection of the interests of consumers and for the said purpose, to establish authorities for timely and effective administration and settlement of consumers' disputes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh). It applies to all goods and services unless otherwise expressly provided by the Central Government.

key_definitions.advertisement: Any audio or visual publicity, representation, endorsement or pronouncement made by means of light, sound, smoke, gas, print, electronic media, internet or website and includes any notice, circular, label, wrapper, invoice or such other documents.
key_definitions.appropriate_laboratory: A laboratory or an organisation recognised by the Central or State Government, or established by or under any law, and maintained, financed or aided by the Central or State Government for carrying out analysis or test of any goods to determine defects.
key_definitions.branch_office: Any office or place of work described as a branch by the establishment, or any establishment carrying on either the same or substantially the same activity as the head office.
key_definitions.central_authority: The Central Consumer Protection Authority established under section 10.
key_definitions.complainant: Includes a consumer, a voluntary consumer association, the Central or State Government, the Central Authority, one or more consumers with the same interest, legal heir/representative of a deceased consumer, or parent/legal guardian of a minor consumer.
key_definitions.complaint: An allegation in writing by a complainant for obtaining relief, alleging unfair trade practice, defects in goods, deficiency in services, overcharging, hazardous goods or services, or a claim for product liability action.
key_definitions.consumer: Any person who buys goods or hires/avails services for a consideration, and includes users of such goods/services with approval, but excludes those obtaining goods for resale or commercial purposes. 'Commercial purpose' excludes use for earning livelihood by self-employment. 'Buys any goods' and 'hires or avails any services' include offline or online transactions.
key_definitions.consumer_dispute: A dispute where the person against whom a complaint has been made, denies or disputes the allegations contained in the complaint.
key_definitions.consumer_rights: Includes the right to be protected against hazardous goods/services, to be informed about quality, quantity, price, etc., access to a variety of goods/services at competitive prices, to be heard, to seek redressal against unfair practices, and consumer awareness.
key_definitions.defect: Any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard of goods required by law, contract, or claimed by the trader.
key_definitions.deficiency: Any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance of services, including negligence, omission, commission causing loss or injury, or deliberate withholding of relevant information.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
main_sections.description: Specifies the title of the Act as the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, its extent to the whole of India (with an exception for Jammu and Kashmir which was later amended), commencement by notification by the Central Government, and application to all goods and services.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as advertisement, appropriate laboratory, branch office, Central Authority, complainant, complaint, consumer, consumer dispute, consumer rights, defect, and deficiency.
Establishes the Central Consumer Protection Council.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Central Consumer Protection Authority.
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Central Consumer Protection Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of Central Authority.
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Central Consumer Protection Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
Defines the jurisdiction of the District Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
Defines the jurisdiction of the State Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
Defines the jurisdiction of the National Commission.
Provides for the establishment of consumer mediation cells.
Deals with product liability actions.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for non-compliance of direction of Central Authority.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for not complying with the directions of the Central Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for false or misleading advertisement.
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for false or misleading advertisements.

main_sections.section_title: Measures to prevent unfair trade practices in e-commerce, direct selling, etc.
main_sections.description: Outlines measures to prevent unfair trade practices in e-commerce and direct selling.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules.
Deals with the repeal of previous laws and savings.

important_rules: Consumers have the right to be protected against marketing of hazardous goods, products or services.
Consumers have the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods, products or services to protect them against unfair trade practices.
Consumers have the right to access a variety of goods, products or services at competitive prices.
Consumers have the right to be heard and have their interests considered at appropriate fora.
Consumers have the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practice or restrictive trade practices or unscrupulous exploitation.
Consumers have the right to consumer awareness.
The Central Consumer Protection Authority can investigate unfair trade practices, misleading advertisements, and issues related to product safety.
Product liability action can be initiated against product manufacturers, service providers, and sellers.
Measures are prescribed to prevent unfair trade practices in e-commerce, direct selling, etc.

penalties: Penalty for non-compliance of direction of Central Authority (section 88).
Punishment for false or misleading advertisement (section 89).
Punishment for manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing, or importing products containing adulterants (section 90).
Punishment for manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing, or importing spurious goods (section 91).
Penalty for non-compliance of order of District Commission, State Commission, or National Commission (section 72).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Consumer Protection Authority (established under section 10), District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, and National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigations, issuance of directions, imposition of penalties, recalling of goods, search and seizure, and enforcement of orders by the respective consumer disputes redressal commissions. The Central Authority can also refer matters for investigation or to other regulators.

rights: Right to safety
Right to be informed
Right to choose
Right to be heard
Right to seek redressal
Right to consumer awareness
Right to approach consumer forums for dispute resolution.
duties: Traders and service providers have a duty to provide goods and services that meet specified standards and are not hazardous.
Traders and service providers have a duty to provide accurate information about goods and services.
Traders have a duty to display prices, and not charge more than the displayed or legally fixed price.
Product manufacturers, service providers, and sellers have duties related to product liability.
Mediators have a duty to disclose certain facts and maintain impartiality.
obligations: Obligation to provide safe goods and services.
Obligation to not engage in unfair trade practices or restrictive trade practices.
Obligation to provide accurate and complete information.
Obligation to adhere to price regulations and displayed prices.
Obligation to participate in mediation proceedings if referred.

key_procedures: Filing a complaint before the appropriate District, State, or National Commission based on pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction.
Mediation process established for a quicker resolution of disputes.
Investigation by the Central Authority, including search and seizure powers.
Filing of appeals against orders of subordinate commissions to higher commissions.
Procedure for hearings, evidence, and passing of orders by the consumer disputes redressal commissions.
Procedure for product liability actions.
administration: The Central Government and the Central Consumer Protection Authority.
important_notes: The Act specifies that it extends to the whole of India, with an initial exception for Jammu and Kashmir, which was later amended to include it as a Union Territory.
Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force.
The Act is not in derogation of any other law, meaning it is in addition to other existing laws.
The Central Government has the power to make rules, and the Central Authority and National Commission have the power to make regulations.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

title: THE AADHAAR (TARGETED DELIVERY OF FINANCIAL AND OTHER SUBSIDIES, BENEFITS AND SERVICES) ACT, 2016
purpose: To provide for, as a good governance, efficient, transparent, and targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services, the expenditure for which is incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India, or the Consolidated Fund of the State, to individuals residing in India through assigning of unique identity numbers to such individuals and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to any offence or contravention committed outside India by any person. It applies to individuals residing in India for obtaining unique identity numbers (Aadhaar numbers) for targeted delivery of financial and other subsidies, benefits, and services.

key_definitions.aadhaar_number: An identification number issued to an individual under sub-section (3) of section 3, and includes any alternative virtual identity generated under sub-section (4) of that section.
key_definitions.aadhaar_ecosystem: Includes enrolling agencies, Registrars, requesting entities, offline verification-seeking entities and any other entity or group of entities as may be specified by regulations.
key_definitions.aadhaar_number_holder: An individual who has been issued an Aadhaar number under this Act.
key_definitions.authentication: The process by which the Aadhaar number along with demographic information or biometric information of an individual is submitted to the Central Identities Data Repository for its verification and such Repository verifies the correctness, or the lack thereof, on the basis of information available with it.
key_definitions.biometric_information: Photograph, finger print, Iris scan, or such other biological attributes of an individual as may be specified by regulations.
key_definitions.demographic_information: Includes information relating to the name, date of birth, address and other relevant information of an individual, as may be specified by regulations for the purpose of issuing an Aadhaar number, but shall not include race, religion, caste, tribe, ethnicity, language, records of entitlement, income or medical history.
key_definitions.resident: An individual who has resided in India for a period or periods amounting in all to one hundred and eighty-two days or more in the twelve months immediately preceding the date of application for enrolment.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of India), and its commencement date (as appointed by the Central Government).
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Aadhaar number', 'authentication', 'biometric information', 'demographic information', 'resident', etc.

Establishes the entitlement of every resident to obtain an Aadhaar number by submitting demographic and biometric information. It also outlines what enrolling agencies must inform individuals during enrolment and how the Aadhaar number is issued and its format.

main_sections.section_title: Proof of Aadhaar number necessary for receipt of certain subsidies, benefits and services, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies that proof of Aadhaar number or the application for enrolment is necessary for receiving certain subsidies, benefits, and services.
Describes the Central Identities Data Repository as a centralized database containing Aadhaar numbers and associated demographic and biometric information.
Provides for the establishment of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI).
Outlines the general powers and functions of the Unique Identification Authority of India.
Mandates the security and confidentiality of information collected under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to comply with provisions of this Act, rules, regulations and directions
main_sections.description: Introduces civil penalties for non-compliance with the Act, rules, regulations, and directions.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for impersonation at time of enrolment
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for impersonation during the Aadhaar enrolment process.
Provides for a general penalty for offences and contraventions not specifically covered.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Authority to make regulations
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Proof of Aadhaar number is necessary for the receipt of certain subsidies, benefits, and services (Section 7).
Rule 2: Enrolling agencies must inform individuals about the use and sharing of their information and their right to access it during enrolment (Section 3(2)).
Rule 3: An Aadhaar number, once issued, cannot be reassigned to another individual (Section 4(1)).
Rule 4: An Aadhaar number shall be a random number and bear no relation to the attributes or identity of the Aadhaar number holder (Section 4(2)).
Rule 5: Voluntary use of Aadhaar number for authentication requires informed consent of the Aadhaar number holder (Section 4(3) Explanation).
Rule 6: Security and confidentiality of information collected under the Act must be maintained (Section 28).
Rule 7: Restrictions are placed on sharing information collected under the Act (Section 29).
Rule 8: Biometric information is deemed to be sensitive personal information (Section 30).

Rule 9: A child shall not be denied any subsidy, benefit or service if they fail to establish identity or furnish proof of Aadhaar number, or if they have not been assigned an Aadhaar number but have applied for enrolment (Section 3A(3)).

penalties: Civil penalties for failure to comply with provisions of the Act, rules, regulations, and directions (Section 33A).
Penalty for impersonation at the time of enrolment (Section 34).
Penalty for impersonating an Aadhaar number holder by changing demographic or biometric information (Section 35).
Penalty for impersonation (Section 36).
Penalty for disclosing identity information (Section 37).
Penalty for unauthorized access to the Central Identities Data Repository (Section 38).
Penalty for tampering with data in the Central Identities Data Repository (Section 39).
Penalty for unauthorized use by requesting entity or offline verification-seeking entity (Section 40).
Penalty for non-compliance with intimation requirements (Section 41).
General penalty for offences (Section 42).
Penalties for offences committed by companies (Section 43).
Penalties not to interfere with other punishments (Section 46).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) is the primary body for establishing and managing the Aadhaar system. Civil penalties are adjudicated by an Adjudicating Officer (Section 33B). Offences are investigated by specified officers (Section 45).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment of the Authority, appointment of officers, imposition of civil penalties and criminal offences with associated punishments, and the power to investigate and adjudicate matters.

rights: Right of a resident to obtain an Aadhaar number (Section 3(1)).
Right to access one's own information and records of requests for authentication (Section 32).
Right to have biometric information treated as sensitive personal information (Section 30).
A child's right to not be denied subsidies, benefits, or services due to issues with Aadhaar establishment (Section 3A(3)).
duties: Duty of enrolling agencies to inform individuals about information usage, sharing, and access rights (Section 3(2)).
Duty to maintain security and confidentiality of information (Section 28).
Duty to restrict sharing of information (Section 29).
Duty of the Authority to issue Aadhaar numbers after verification (Section 3(3)).
Duty of the Authority to cancel a child's Aadhaar number upon request after they attain 18 years of age (Section 3A(2)).
obligations: Obligation to use Aadhaar number for receipt of certain subsidies, benefits and services (Section 7).
Obligation to undergo enrolment process to obtain an Aadhaar number (Section 3(1)).
Obligation not to impersonate during enrolment or with Aadhaar number holder's details (Sections 34, 35, 36).
Obligation not to disclose identity information unlawfully (Section 37).
Obligation not to gain unauthorized access to the Central Identities Data Repository (Section 38).
Obligation not to tamper with data in the Central Identities Data Repository (Section 39).
Obligation for requesting entities and offline verification-seeking entities not to use Aadhaar information unauthorizedly (Section 40).

key_procedures: Enrolment Procedure: Residents submit demographic and biometric information to enrolling agencies, who then forward it to the Authority for verification and issuance of an Aadhaar number (Section 3).

Authentication Procedure: An individual submits their Aadhaar number and demographic/biometric information to a requesting entity, which then submits it to the Central Identities Data Repository for verification (Section 2(c)).
Offline Verification Procedure: A process specified by regulations for verifying Aadhaar number holder identity without authentication (Section 2(pa)).
Update of Information: Process for updating demographic or biometric information (Section 6).

Appeal Procedure: In case of civil penalties, there's a procedure for appeals to the Adjudicating Officer, then to the Appellate Tribunal, and finally to the Supreme Court of India (Sections 33B, 33C, 33E).
administration: The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) is established to administer the Act. The Central Government also plays a significant role in making rules and providing grants.
important_notes: The Aadhaar number is not evidence of citizenship or domicile (Section 9).
Different dates may be appointed for commencement of different provisions of the Act (Section 1(3)).
The Act was extended to the whole of India, with the exclusion of Jammu and Kashmir previously, which has now been omitted (Section 1(2)).
The Aadhaar number issued is a twelve-digit number. Virtual identities can also be generated (Section 3(4)).
Voluntary use of Aadhaar number requires informed consent of the Aadhaar number holder (Section 4(3) Explanation).
A child's Aadhaar number can be cancelled upon application within six months of attaining eighteen years of age (Section 3A(2)).

title: The Legal Metrology Act, 2009
purpose: To establish and enforce standards of weights and measures, regulate trade and commerce in weights, measures and other goods which are sold or distributed by weight, measure or number and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India. It applies to weights, measures, and goods sold or distributed by weight, measure, or number, and to related matters. It also covers the appointment of officials, their powers, verification and stamping of weights and measures, and offenses and penalties.

key_definitions.controller: The Controller of Legal Metrology appointed under section 14.
key_definitions.dealer: A person who carries on the business of buying, selling, supplying or distributing any weight or measure.
key_definitions.director: The Director of Legal Metrology appointed under section 13.
key_definitions.legal_metrology: That part of metrology which treats units of weighment and measurement, methods of weighment and measurement and weighing and measuring instruments, in relation to the mandatory technical and legal requirements which have the object of ensuring public guarantee from the point of view of security and accuracy of the weighments and measurements.
key_definitions.legal_metrology_officer: Additional Director, Additional Controller, Joint Director, Joint Controller, Deputy Director, Deputy Controller, Assistant Director, Assistant Controller and Inspector appointed under sections 13 and 14.
key_definitions.manufacturer: A person who manufactures or assembles weights or measures, or puts their own mark on them.
key_definitions.pre-packaged_commodity: A commodity which without the purchaser being present is placed in a package of whatever nature, whether sealed or not, so that the product contained therein has a pre-determined quantity.
key_definitions.repairer: A person who repairs a weight or measure and includes a person who adjusts, cleans, lubricates or paints any weight or measure or renders any other service to such weight or measure to ensure that such weight or measure conforms to the standards established by or under this Act.
key_definitions.sale: Transfer of property in any weight, measure or other goods by one person to another for cash or for deferred payment or for any other valuable consideration, including hire-purchase or instalment systems.
key_definitions.stamp: A mark made by impressing, casting, engraving, etching, branding, affixing pre-stressed paper seal or any other process in relation to, any weight or measure, certifying its conformity to standards or indicating obliteration of a previous conformity mark.
key_definitions.transaction: Any contract, assessment of royalty, toll, duty or other dues, or assessment of work done, wages due or services rendered.
key_definitions.verification: The process of comparing, checking, testing or adjusting a weight or measure to ensure it conforms to established standards, including re-verification and calibration.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Legal Metrology Act, 2009', states that it extends to the whole of India, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Controller', 'dealer', 'Director', 'Legal Metrology', 'legal metrology officer', 'manufacturer', 'pre-packaged commodity', 'repairer', 'sale', 'stamp', 'transaction', and 'verification'.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of this Act to override provisions of any other law
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act will have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law or instrument.

main_sections.section_title: Units of weights and measures to be based on metric system
main_sections.description: Mandates that all units of weight or measure must be in accordance with the metric system based on the international system of units.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Director, legal metrology officers and other employees
main_sections.description: Details the provisions for the appointment of the Director of Legal Metrology and other legal metrology officers and employees.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Controller, legal metrology officers and other employees
main_sections.description: Details the provisions for the appointment of the Controller of Legal Metrology and other legal metrology officers and employees.
Grants powers to the Director, Controller, and legal metrology officers to inspect, search, and seize articles or documents.

main_sections.section_title: Verification and stamping of weight or measure
main_sections.description: Deals with the process of verifying and stamping weights or measures to ensure they conform to standards.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for use of non-standard weight or measure
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for the use of weights or measures that do not conform to the established standards.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of the Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 and Standards of Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1985
main_sections.description: Repeals the previous Acts related to standards of weights and measures.

important_rules: Units of weights and measures must be based on the metric system (Section 4).
No weight, measure, or numeral other than the standard shall be used as a standard (Section 8(3)).
