Weights or measures cannot be manufactured or imported unless they conform to specified standards, with exceptions for export or scientific research (Section 8(4) & Proviso).
Reference, secondary, and working standards must be verified and stamped according to prescribed procedures and fees (Section 9).
Transactions, dealings, or contracts must be in terms of standard units of weight, measure, or numeration (Section 11).
Any custom or usage contrary to standard weights, measures, or numeration is void (Section 12).
Manufacturers, dealers, and repairers must obtain licenses for their activities (Sections 23, 45, 46).
Pre-packaged commodities must have specific declarations on their labels (Section 18).
Importers of weights or measures must be registered (Section 19).
Non-standard weights and measures cannot be imported (Section 20).
Models of weights or measures must be approved before manufacture or sale (Section 22).

penalties: Penalty for use of non-standard weight or measure (Section 25).
Penalty for alteration of weight and measure (Section 26).
Penalty for manufacture or sale of non-standard weight or measure (Section 27).
Penalty for making transactions, deals, or contracts in contravention of prescribed standards (Section 28).
Penalty for quoting or publishing non-standard units (Section 29).
Penalty for transactions in contravention of standard weight or measure (Section 30).
Penalty for non-production of documents (Section 31).
Penalty for failure to get model approved (Section 32).
Penalty for use of unverified weight or measure (Section 33).
Penalty for sale or delivery of commodities by non-standard weight or measure (Section 34).
Penalty for rendering services by non-standard weight, measure, or number (Section 35).
Penalty for selling non-standard packages (Section 36).
Penalty for contravention by Government approved Test Centre (Section 37).
Penalty for non-registration by importer of weight or measure (Section 38).
Penalty for import of non-standard weight or measure (Section 39).
Penalty for obstructing Director, Controller, or legal metrology officer (Section 40).
Penalty for giving false information or false return (Section 41).
Penalty for vexatious search (Section 42).
Penalty for verification in contravention of Act and rules (Section 43).
Penalty for counterfeiting of seals, etc. (Section 44).
Penalty for manufacture of weight and measure without licence (Section 45).
Penalty for repair, sale, etc., of weight and measure without licence (Section 46).
Penalty for tampering with licence (Section 47).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Director, Controller, and legal metrology officers appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of inspection, seizure, search, and prosecution for various offenses and penalties prescribed in the Act. Enforcement also involves verification and stamping of weights and measures, and registration of importers.

rights: Right to trade and commerce using standard weights and measures.
Right to be protected from inaccurate weighments and measurements, ensuring public guarantee from the point of view of security and accuracy.
duties: Manufacturers, dealers, and repairers have duties related to obtaining licenses, maintaining records, and ensuring their products conform to standards.
All persons involved in transactions must use standard weights and measures.
Importers have a duty to register and only import non-standard weights and measures.
Entities must comply with verification and stamping requirements for weights and measures.
Individuals must provide accurate information and documents when required by enforcement authorities.
Users of weights and measures have a duty to ensure they are verified and standard.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the metric system for all units of weight and measure.
Obligation to use standard weights, measures, and numerals in all transactions.
Obligation to ensure that weights and measures are verified and stamped.
Obligation to obtain necessary licenses and approvals.
Obligation to provide correct declarations on pre-packaged commodities.
Obligation not to obstruct or hinder legal metrology officers in their duties.

key_procedures: Appointment of Director and Controller of Legal Metrology and other officers (Sections 13, 14).
Inspection, search, and seizure of non-conforming items and documents by legal metrology officers (Section 15).
Verification and stamping of weights and measures to certify conformity to standards (Section 24).
Approval of models of weights or measures before manufacture or sale (Section 22).
Registration of importers of weights or measures (Section 19).
Compounding of offences by payment of a sum of money (Section 48).
Appeals against decisions made under the Act (Section 50).
administration: The Central Government and State Governments have powers to make rules, delegate powers, and administer the Act. The Director and Controller of Legal Metrology, along with legal metrology officers, are responsible for the day-to-day enforcement and administration.
important_notes: The Act explicitly states that its provisions override those of any other law that is inconsistent with it (Section 3).
The Act provides for the repeal of the Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 and the Standards of Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1985 (Section 57).
The Act clarifies that its provisions do not apply in certain cases (Section 55), though these specific cases are not detailed in the provided text excerpt.

title: The Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act
purpose: To provide for the better administration, supervision, regulation and development of waqf properties and institutions in India.
scope: Applies to all waqf properties and institutions in India, whether created before or after commencement, subject to specified exclusions.

key_definitions.waqf: Permanent dedication of movable or immovable property for purposes recognised by Muslim law as pious, religious or charitable.
key_definitions.mutawalli: Person appointed to manage or administer a waqf.
key_definitions.waqf_board: Statutory body established for supervision and administration of waqf properties.
key_definitions.encroacher: Any person or institution occupying waqf property without lawful authority.

main_sections.description: Provides short title, extent, commencement, application and key definitions under the Act.
Mandates survey, publication of list of auqaf and resolution of disputes by Tribunal.
Establishes Central Waqf Council and provides for its finance, accounts and rule-making powers.
Constitution, powers, duties and functioning of State Waqf Boards and their officers.
Provides for compulsory registration and maintenance of registers of waqf properties.
Regulates budgeting, audit, alienation, encroachment removal, appointment and removal of mutawallis.
Establishes Tribunals and bars civil court jurisdiction in waqf matters.

important_rules: Mandatory registration of waqf properties
Alienation of waqf property without Board sanction is void
Disputes to be decided by Waqf Tribunals

penalties: Penalty for unauthorised alienation of waqf property
Penalties for encroachment and misuse of waqf assets
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Waqf Boards and Waqf Tribunals
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, recovery proceedings, eviction orders and Tribunal adjudication

rights: Right of beneficiaries to proper use of waqf income
Right to approach Tribunal for dispute resolution
duties: Duty of mutawalli to manage waqf property prudently
Duty to submit accounts and comply with Board directions
obligations: Obligation to preserve waqf property and income for intended purposes

key_procedures: Survey and publication of auqaf list
Registration and maintenance of waqf records
Tribunal adjudication of disputes
administration: Administered by Central Waqf Council, State Waqf Boards and Waqf Tribunals.
important_notes: Amended by Waqf (Amendment) Acts, 2013 and 2025
Certain declarations of waqf in protected or scheduled areas are barred

title: The Indian Succession Act
purpose: To consolidate the law applicable to intestate and testamentary succession in India.
scope: Applies to succession, wills, probate and administration of estates, subject to personal law exceptions.

key_definitions.intestate: Person dying without making a valid will.
key_definitions.will: Legal declaration of intention of a testator regarding disposal of property after death.
key_definitions.executor: Person appointed to execute a will.
key_definitions.administrator: Person appointed by court to administer estate when no executor exists.

main_sections.description: Short title, definitions and power to exempt certain communities.
Rules governing distribution of property where no will exists.
Provisions relating to wills, codicils, construction and revocation.
Legal character and powers of executors and administrators.
Procedure for grant, revocation and administration of estates.

important_rules: Succession governed by domicile
Specific rules for intestate distribution
Formal execution and attestation of wills

penalties: Punishment for false statements in probate proceedings
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Civil Courts and District Judges
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through probate, administration and judicial proceedings

rights: Right of heirs to inherit as per law
Right to make a will subject to legal capacity
duties: Duty of executor or administrator to administer estate faithfully
obligations: Obligation to pay debts and distribute estate lawfully

key_procedures: Execution and revocation of wills
Grant of probate or letters of administration
Distribution of estate
administration: Administered through civil courts, primarily District Courts.
important_notes: Extensively amended over time
Personal law exceptions apply in certain cases

title: The Representation of the People Act
purpose: To provide for conduct of elections to Parliament and State Legislatures and related matters.
